name: In Nightmare
detailed_description: Enter A Chilling Dreamworld Of Whimsy and Horror Closing his heart to reality, our protagonist falls into a deep slumber and awakens in a nightmarish dreamworld. In Nightmare is a narrative-driven horror adventure game combining sneak action with diverse puzzles. It follows a young boy in search for the last hope of love who is working out his own salvation by navigating through his fear. Experiencing effects of a broken family, and the heartache it brings, a young child will escape reality into a dark, whimsical world created from his own memories. This sets him on his journey to uncover what truly lies within. Having suffered in reality, his past trauma turns into terrifying monsters that want to keep him in an eternal nightmare. With the help of his dream spirit, the boy will find ways to sneak past enemies, overcome intricate puzzles, embrace his fear, and uncover the truth so that he may be able to purify the monsters he has created, and finally wake up. Will you overcome what you fear or be caught in the nightmare? Hope Rests in your Dreams - Escape the dark whimsical dreamworld that has trapped you, search the realm for clues, and begin uncovering the truth of your reality. Puzzle Through Pain - Along your journey, you will encounter puzzles that will attempt to thwart your progress. Use your wits and your spirit guide to help you overcome anything that gets in your way. A Light in the Darkness - Control your dream spirit to assist you as a decoy, detect invisible pathways or items, and become keenly aware of threats that lie ahead. Nightmares Made Real - Your subconscious creates the monsters you truly fear. Don’t let them or the shadows lurking catch you and keep you in the eternal nightmare.

Now let me talk about my personal feeling. 1.The difficulty is gradual and easy to master, level setting is very sophisticated.2.The plot presented in the game shocked me, and made me think about myself quite a lot, which pushed the artistry of the game to a climax. In the story, Bill jumps over deep ravines, escape dangerous monsters and solve the puzzles in order to get out of his psychological shadow. 3.The whole game seems to perform a drama with a tight rhythm, leaving player enough space for thinking. _childDocuments_.review: I found this indie isometric horror game to be more frustrating than enjoyable. This is because it quickly turns into a hide from the monster game with no way to defend yourself and no manual save. You constantly keep getting caught by the monsters because they can easily detect you, even when crouched and hiding in the shadows. Your stamina meter also drops quickly, so you can't outrun them. There is also an annoying heartbeat sound that doesn't stop when monsters are near. Graphics are faded and washed out and I had to use Reshade to get the shading to look right. This game also suffers from typical Unity engine stuttery camera movement, even when the frame rate remains maxed. Overall, I did not enjoy my time spent with this game and I therefore cannot recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: In Nightmare is a pretty good horror adventure game, okay then the story. In a hospital a young man named Bill Thompson is in a deep sleep after suffering so much tragedy in his young life he finds himself unable to face the real world, now in a deep, deep coma he dreams, but his dreams are not pleasant ones as he is trapped in a nightmare world where he must confront his past and his trauma to wake up or else he shall sleep forever.Okay what are the likes, the story is good I like how it talks and handles the themes of child abuse and neglect and it doesn't go over the top with it for shock value, no it's handled much more sensitively, also talking about things like divorce and trauma. I also like the parts about forgiveness, facing your fears and overcoming trauma.The gameplay is good it's a mixture of exploration and puzzle solving while also running and hiding from monsters, it has a nice little nightmares kind of vibe to it, there are some frustrating parts. The puzzles were good a lot of them were fair with some decent amount of hints to tell you how to solve them, except for one puzzle though but I'll get to that in the dislikes.The graphics are good it has a great use and good balance of bright and somber dark colors giving it a sort of dreamy like quality, the designs are also quite good not just the world, but the characters and monsters too.The levels are good each one very creative and quite diverse that really implements and uses the whole dream aspects to each level, even the hub world is just breathtaking to look at. It's also interesting that each of the levels are thematically tied with the character, while also being warped and exaggerated to fit the nightmarish dream world. The monsters are good each one has their own unique looks and are very creepy, I also really like how each one really ties in with the themes of the story and our main character, it was quite creative especially after a second playthrough and reading all the notes.The characters are very good while there is officially only one character Billy he was well developed through his notes and diary entries, we can see him going from a sweet and sensitive young kid to someone who's really jaded and angry, even his parents like his father are quite three-dimensional even though we don't really see them besides in flashbacks they're actually portrayed as complicated people who both have their faults and while I do blame the dad for a lot of the crap in Billy's life and he is one of the key factors in his abuse, he written in the notes to not really be a bad man he was just not meant to be a single parent and later in a note he even admits to screwing up, the mom does too but I feel like the dad was had more to blame than the mom, but that's just me personally.The notes are really good it does a good job in expanding the characters and the story as a whole just like any good notes should do. The music was really good each haunting scores from the first level as you creep around this weird childish nursery/kid’sroom, to the almost mystical soundtrack to the forest level to even being chased by monsters, each score really fit the game was good.Now is this game scary not really, it's not going to make you jump or feel dread it's more tragic, it is a little disappointing to be honest, but I do think the story is good regardless of it not being scary as it could be.Okay what are the dislikes, there are some frustrating parts in the game like one part is the first puzzle in chapter 3 basically in order to complete this puzzle you have to go through doors turning them clockwise or counterclockwise a certain number of times, I felt that puzzle to be very vague and kind of cheap, there is a clue in the floor mural but I felt it too vague and really confusing compared to the other puzzles hits, while some of the other puzzles you can brute force your way your way through, you can’t brute forcing this puzzle and it can ultimately take you out of the game.The second frustrating part is the forearmed boss monster, the boss fight is really cheap because not only are you running from the monster you also have to be careful because in the boss arena there is columns of fire and if you get hit by the boss or by those columns of fire no matter how far in the boss fight you are, if you die you have to restart the whole fight again it was quite frustrating.Alright now with that all done with In Nightmare is a pretty good horror adventure game, it has a good story, good graphics and good monsters, now I do recommend this game if you're looking for a game that's not really scary, but has a very good story then I definitely recommend it.

name: Grindstone
detailed_description: A Puzzle Game where Epic Adventures are your 9-to-5. Grindstone Mountain is overrun with vicious Creeps! Part color-matching, part monster-slaying ridiculousness, in Grindstone it’s your job to mine grindstones from the Creeps that lurk on the mountain. Slay your way up the treacherous peak by completing over 250 levels of intricate puzzles and hazards, besting bosses and exploring a variety of weird and wonderful locations along the way. More Ways to Slay! As your tackle the challenges of Grindstone Mountain, you'll also discover long-lost blueprints to craft powerful new gear, unlock a challenging boss-rush mode, try your luck at the wheel of fortune in a creepy carnival, and have the chance to prove your prowess on the leaderboards of three daily modes. Award-Winning Original Soundtrack Your musical maestro throughout Grindstone is Sam Webster, composer of the game's widely-acclaimed original soundtrack. From Your Pals at CAPY! Grindstone is a game of sword-slashing puzzle battles from the award-winning creators of Superbrothers: Sword & Sworcery EP, Super Time Force Ultra, BELOW, Might & Magic: Clash of Heroes and Critter Crunch!

_childDocuments_.review: Chill, relatively easy but still challenging puzzle game. Amazing to play now and then when relaxing/watching something else on your second monitor. Good substitute for autobattlers/puzzlegames with quality written all over it. More positives than negatives, could use more tweaking and changes to some features. Pros:- Refreshing and unique puzzle elements- Amazing aesthetics and art style- Cool character designs and animations- Satisfying gameplay (long combos and figuring out better chains)- Adds new variables and mechanics to the core gameplay the further you get, making it harder and interesting- Easy and hard puzzles- Massive amounts of gameplay time (atm 19h and not even 50% done with the game)- Challenges- Dailies- A lot of different consumables, gear and items to make your own gameplay style different50/50 pro/con- Mobile UI elements (I personally like it because it's simplistic and snappy)- A lot of animations (can be frustrating for players like me who don't care about them anymore)- RNG placement of chests and slob kings (optional missions in puzzles) can sometimes be really weird, making it extremely easy or nearly impossible to get. This adds rng variable to the puzzles which is nice, but sometimes makes you replay the puzzle for easier spawns.- CalArts artstyle (I'm neutral about it but it's super basic and saturated at this point, animations and presentation makes it special)- Some costumes are locked behind a weekly quest gate. If you don't meet the requirements (eg. on launch you need 50 spike shield kills, and with my 19 hours of gameplay time I still haven't gotten it), I have no idea if you'll ever be able to get it again.Cons:- Clearly developed for mobile first as a f2p+p2w game, then changed to p2p model. This makes some mechanics and features "weird" for a pay to play game.- Resource dependant with consumables, special items and hp. If you suck at the game, you might need to grind the older levels for resources which ofc sucks butt because it's a husk feature from the p2w mobile game dev version. (No idea how bad it is because so far I haven't had to replay any puzzles for resources)- No fast mode, can get tedious to wait for the animations to finish- Some puzzles are so hard that you need special items to complete them. On paper this is not a bad feature, but because the items need resources to use them and if you get stuck/suck at the puzzle, you need to grind the resources back which ofc is horrible and tedious. Once again, mobile game version's husk feature.Tips:- Use the pickaxe to spawn more items on the map, which are neutral colored pickups. Makes combos easier and gives more room to move. Pickaxe refills after every puzzle aka you don't need resources to use it.- When you are in a position where you have to either take damage or use an item to get out of the situation, think about which is less expensive for your; taking 1 hit which costs 5 gems to heal OR getting out of the situation with an item which costs eg. 10 gems + other resources to refill/repair. Sometimes taking 1 hit is much better decision.- In the early game you can pick special resources from challenges to make new items/gear, but later on I highly recommend always picking up gems because you need them for hp and item refills/repair. You'll get plenty resources from other things in the game.- If the puzzle map is special with map hazards or multiple tough hp enemies, don't be afraid to quit the puzzle when you've checked it out at the start, change to appropriate items and trying again. This doesn't cost you anything as long as you've not lost any hp and/or used items which require resources.- Remember to use monster goo at Helgä's shop regularly to craft super items. Once the amount of goo hits the 6000 limit, you can't gather more until you've free'd up some space.Thanks for reading.Edit: Added more bullets points

_childDocuments_.review: First played Grindstone during the game demo Steam event. Was immediately hooked. After realizing it was made by Capybara Games, I felt compelled to pay full price on Steam for support. Even though the game was was on Apple Arcade for free. I figured, I loved a similar match three type game by CAPY; Critter Crunch. And the Steam features were something I felt had enough value to justify my support.However, I should have taken the feature on Apple Arcade as a hint of the target audience. The mobile game community has a reputation of endless games that don't really require skill or increase in difficulty. Designed to suck the user in with the insinuation that the levels keep progressing, and they are going somewhere.Grindstone starts strong with a hand drawn art style, and a video which leads you to believe there may be a story unfolding. But there really isn't a story. You simply  through areas, each with there own new element, and finish out with a boss. They have added this weapon and amor element to add to the rogue like feel of the game. It sounds interesting enough. And at the beginning it is pretty amusing.But the problem the problem is the game just doesn't change from the first moment you play. It gets boring and tiresome quickly. If there were a story it would help remove the repetition of doing the same thing over and over again. The difficulty never seems to ramp up unless RNG screws you. In which case you can just reload and the crisis is averted. And the weapons and armour are hardly clever. I actually stuck with the same gear for almost the entire game, even after getting the "elite" gear at the end.Honestly the only reason I finished was because I felt like I had already invested so much time, I wanted to see if anything changed or got harder. But in the end the game is the same almost the entire way through, with one level feeling slightly harder, and the next feeling like the very first level. The game is basically a classic match three game. Pointless, endless, and mindless. But the joke is on me for not seeing through the graphical polish to the empty core.

_childDocuments_.review: I played through Grindstone while it was a mobile game and I'm playing through it again now on PC. That's how good this game is.While it may look like your typical Match-3 puzzle game on the screenshots, it actually isn't one. The game uses rather unique mechanics to challenge the player.You play as Jorj, a family man and hard worker. Your job is to collect shiny gems, the titular Grindstones. To get these gems you need to slay monsters that live inside a big mountain cave. Basic gameplay revolves around drawing lines from Jorj through same-colored monsters to perform a combo. Jorj will move through once you end your round. if you get a combo of 10, a Grindstone will drop on a random tile. Moving through a gem allows Jorj to change from one color to any other color, making it possible to chain larger combos. Bigger combos give bigger gems which are worth more Grindstones. This acts as the currency of the game.After Jorj made his turn, enemies will make theiris. If Jorj moved nect to an aggroed creep, he will get attacked. Creeps will aggro randomly on each turn and will stay angry until they are killed or have attacked Jorj. There are also big baddies who have more health and you need to meet a target combo number before you can slay them but they work like gems and allow you to chain into another color of choice. Big baddies drop loot that Jorj can collect during his move.Each stage has a specific goal, most of the time you need to slay a specific amount of enmies, sometimes you need a set number of Grindstones. Later stages might have more complicated goals that you need to solve. Once you finished the goal, the exit gets opened but you don't have to leave right away. If you want, you can still grind the level for loot and gems. However, the longer Jorj sticks around, the faster enemies get angry and at some point you might get overwhelmed and won't find a single safe space anymore.There are also two sub goals on each stage, getting a treasure chest and killing the King creep. The king creep has 5 HP and needs to be killed in a specific color and does not allow you to change color, which makes it somewhat tricky to get him. If you get him, he will give you a crown that you need to open new sections of the game. The treasure chest on the other hand needs a key that one enemy on the map gets. If you kill that enemy, you can collect and open the chest with a combo of 5 or 10, depending on the rarity of the chest. The chest will contain some loot and sometimes a blueprint. All three objectives are marked on your map but you generally need only the main objective and a handful of crown objectives to get through the game. Getting all objectives however makes the game a lot easir in the long run.Early on you get introduced to equipment. Jorj can have three different items equipped and these can be used during a level. Items are divided into two types, one that recharges between level and one that needs to be replenished. The first one is generally weaker but can save currency, the second is more powerful but could be too expensive on the long run.There are different types of equipment like swords that allow Jorj to attack in specific patterns, shields that allow Jorj to block attacks and relese effects if he does so, arrows that can be shot at a single enemy to kill it and utility items that can have all types of effects. Jorj can mix these however he wants, if you want to take three swords to a level, the game won't stop you.Blueprints that you get from chests will allow Jorj to craft new items if he has the right materials. These materials are what you get from the enemies and sometimes obstacles that are on the field. You can also find blueprints for clothing. Clothes allow Jorj to have a passive effect and might interact with enemies or your equipment. Clothes never need to be repaired and just like equipment it can be switched between levels however you like.The game offers a lot of additional content besides the main levels. There are three types of daily challenges that you can do and compete on leaderboards with other players. There are also bonus stages that offer a lot of materials and gemstones, once you finish them and if you beat the entire bonus section, you get a blueprint for a random golden equipment. Golden equipment is a more powerful version of the same item that allows you to use that item six times during a stage. Gold is however very rare and the player has to actively grind for it to get enough for golden items.Overall the game is very fun, you can play this game very casually or you can try to compete with others players on the daily leaderboards. Mixing equipment and testing new strategies is mega fun and the game has so many levels that it will take you a long time to finish the game.The visuals are also very nice, the game uses a cartoony but rather gory art syle. Copmbined with the soundtrack you have a very pleasant gaming experience.If you like puzzle games, you totally should get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The main purpose of this review is to debunk some of the comments by a lot of other reviewers regarding the need to grind for additional resources. Having completed the game using the 'basic' equipment that does not need any repairs with resources (i.e. pick axe, basic shield and basic arrow) - except to gain the achievements related to the other equipment - I can safely say you do not need to repeat levels unless the equipment choices you make force you to do so.In terms of the game itself, it's well designed - the mechanics are solid and there are enough variations in level features, enemies and equipment that it has every chance to keep you engaged if you enjoy the central premise of 'chaining' through Creeps. There's certainly a lot of satisfaction to be had in building a long streak and taking out several of the more advanced enemies at the same time. The grind is real insofar as there are literally hundreds of levels to complete (some are not 'required' for achievement completion).Just on a comparison to other games you could get at the normal price point, I'd suggest waiting for a discount and it seems a bit much for a mobile port. For me, this was part of a Humble Bundle and I certainly got my money's worth.

_childDocuments_.review: is a tile-matching puzzle game with a fairly butch framing aesthetic for the genre; instead of gems or blocks, the protagonist must gorily slaughter his or her way through long lines of color-coded enemies, finessing the end position of the combo so that the enemies can't hit back between turns.The game originated as a mobile title, and it shows: it's optimized for touchscreen (although it also handles beautifully with the Steam Deck's joystick) and prioritizes quantity over quality of content.   has hundreds and hundreds of levels, few of which are particularly distinctive or well-differentiated, and the experience can get very samey if the player just tries to plow through the game in one go.  However, despite that emphasis on quantity, the baseline quality of  is quite high to begin with.  The core game loop of chaining huge combos is satisfying and the difficulty is fairly forgiving, with some occasional levels jumping up in complexity.  Rarely, it can take some very big-brain maneuvers to figure out a combo trajectory that won't end with the player being hurt, killed, or boxed into a corner at the end of it.The original soundtrack, by musician Sam Webster, is a brilliant match for the title: meditative, dreamy trip-hop, unobtrusive enough that it can just melt into long hours of gameplay without distraction but distinctive enough that I always feel like I'm going  when I start a level.  The art and animation style is probably going to be the most polarizing: it's modeled off of the contemporary Cartoon Network house style, often derisively referred to as "CalArts style," "Bean Mouth," "thin line art style," or occasionally as "the downfall of Western civilization" by the most terminally online people in the world.  Personally, I like this look a lot for the game: it reminds me of the later, more adult-oriented Pendleton Ward works like .The perfect way to consume  is at the cadence of the mobile game it was intended to be: it doesn't really hold up to a marathon session because of the aforementioned saminess between puzzles, but I've been playing a few levels a day to feel my brain get tickled in the same way that some people do their daily crossword or sudoku.  Together with the fantastic presentation, it's a great little hit of dopamine to start or end my day.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a super polished basic puzzle game, there is variety in terms of enemies, level hazards and equippable items, but for the most part the game is finding a massive chain, getting a grindstone out of it, then using it to make an even bigger chain next time.No time pressure, super easy mechanics and consistent game rules mean you can easily pick this up and play a few rounds whenever it fits into your day - during a boring zoom call, before bed, or while your girlfriend is trying to explain something to you.There is a TON of levels, im at 13 hours so far and I think maybe less than 25% in terms of total level count.

_childDocuments_.review: Game looks great and have a lot of content but is plague with RNG. The puzzle mechanic is fun and engaging. However RNG is  making some levels simply unbeatable. You will jump from impossible to super easy all the time.  I feel that there is very little strategy involved (Note that I 100% the game). Grindstone is simply too long for no reason and gets tedious and repetitive very fast because there is little to no varation to the content. Also, the game will prevent you from progressing further if you don't unlocked some specific objectives, like chest, which is fantasticaly BS and frustrating. Animations are cool but very long and unskipable, therefore after a few hours you will get tired of waiting all the time for it to finish to be able to play. Don't get me wrong it's still a very decent game to enjoy in short burst. Another great example that Valve should really implement the Mixed review rating.The new free update : Comsic Darkside is exactly in the same vein as the main content. Once again you'll pass from super easy to impossible levels without any variations in content whatsoever. On top of that, the new infection mechanic just makes everything worst and unfair because it snowball so fast that your only choice will be to restart over and over until you get lucky. Sure it's a hard mode but the speed of infection is completely disproportionate in later levels leaving you with only one option : Resign and restart again.

_childDocuments_.review: Grindstone is one of the funnest, most addicting, "just one more level" games I've played. I bought this on the ninendo switch several years ago and i've been VERY impressed by how much free expansion levels have been added by the dev team at no cost over the years. literally waves of hundreds of levels, doubling, and then tripling, and quadrupling the scope of content of the game over a few years.I've probably got hundreds of hours into this game on Switch and still wanted to purchase it again on Steam so I could play it from start to finish again and earn all of the achievements playing it on my ROG Ally X when traveling and whatnot.Couldn't recommend a casual game more than Grindstone. It's super simple, fun, and doesn't get boring.

_childDocuments_.review: One or two ollllld iOS games had the same main mechanic and I always all ways loved those. This game has fewer things to do than those games (so far) but is just as fun all the same nonetheless.Thr characters and art style are wacky and grotesque and garish and therefore somewhat unpleasant to look at most of the time—but serve their purpose, are well animated, and at least stand out from other games well.Music’s good too, but I haven’t heard it recently, since this quickly becomes a “distraction” game you mostly play while doing other things due to its simplicity. Not necessarily an insult, I often need games like that. The first example that comes to mind is Threes! But I also have fond memories of playing Rocket League that way. And surely several if not dozens of others. But I distract myself here again.Bejeweled series is another great point of reference in this regard, especially by way of its relative similarity to Grindstone.Also relatedly, plays well on Steam Deck, including at much lower framerates for the sake of battery life.Good game, wouldn’t spend more than $5 or mayyybr $10 on it though if I were you. Best in short bursts.

_childDocuments_.review: Could you imagine a puzzle game with lots of (candy) gore? Here it is! _childDocuments_.review: Grindstone is great. Makes me feel like a kid again, when I played Game House Collection stuff just to chill out. The game is made with love, and it's perfect for people who love puzzlers.The drawing and animation are top notch, the characters and mobs have heart and humor, the music and sound design are - *cheff kiss*. Chaining monsters feels super rewarding, and the risk-to-reward management is balanced just right (sometimes it's too easy, if I was to critique one thing). There is a story mode with boss levels, daily grind modes, dungeons introducing new gimmicks, and enough power ups and consumables to give the game a huge replay value.Overall, Grindstone is a gem, and I can't recommend it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this one. The art, music, and basic game-play are great, but it is very repetitive and has some odd, mobile-ish mechanics that feel very grindy and not worth your time.Repetition: I think the game would be quite a bit stronger if it was . The game is broken into sets of ~10 levels, which alternate between sets of general cave levels and sets of themed levels. The themed levels are generally interesting with gimmicks that range from making maps significantly easier to those that make things much more difficult (with no apparent progression from easy to difficult across the course of the game, oddly). The intermediate cave levels are fairly basic, sometimes with very minor gimmicks (and always end with the same, re-used boss). Most areas also have an optional set of 10 additional levels you can do, which mix general cave levels and themed ones. Each level takes about 5-20 minutes, and there are  non-optional levels. Cutting the optional levels and the cave levels entirely would make the game feel way less grindy.Odd mechanics: Many of the mechanics in the game feel really out-of-place in a $20 game. The game has quite a few set of sometimes quite powerful upgrades that you can craft, but nearly all of these break after a few uses and have to be repaired for a large amount of resources (in total, with each use repaired separately). To actually use your upgrades regularly, you will need to grind quite a lot. Since you also don't get uses back if you fail (or more likely back out of) a puzzle after using them. This makes since in a free-to-play mobile game context, where you could just pay for more uses as an alternative, but not in a $20 game. Mostly you can get away without using your costly upgrades (outside of a few randomly dispersed very hard maps), but it seems a shame to never use the vast majority of your kit.So yah, overall the game feels like it's in a weird place: the core game is very enjoyable but it is super repetitive and has additional grindy aspects that feel very out-of-place. Probably much better as a steam deck game where you can play 15 minutes while waiting to do something else, though!

_childDocuments_.review: theres like two core issues with the game that really hold it back an absurd amount1) the entire game, despite being a full title without MTX to begin with, is inherently designed like any other free to play match 3 game for mobile. all the trimmings are there, its got the same sort of level map, the same complete random chance "maybe you'll beat this level, maybe you wont" tier rng for spawns, limited use items that require resources to recharge, said resources being split apart into tens of different kinds for no reason whatsoever and basically everything requiring its usage, certain levels being next to impossible unless you have specific items available... it's just heinous. no matter how hard i try, i just cannot separate this from any other predatory match 3 game on phones because its designed exactly the same as them, just with the MTXs awkwardly removed and nothing done to really compensate properly for that.2) Other negative reviews mention how this game is pretty much the same from beginning to end with no real change and I regrettably have to join in that voicing. The core gameplay is just not engaging enough to have any true stickiness and the previously mentioned problem of its entire design only exacerbates that flaw. It's not that I hate match 3 games at all. Hell, slap me in front of Bejeweled 2's endless mode and I'll be happy. But in trying so hard to be innovative or different in the genre, it's carved itself into a small hole where it only has the one hat trick and it shows it to you immediately. There's a beauty in the simplicity of other similar puzzle games where the addictiveness comes from how easy it is to pick up and play and just zone out. But with Grindstone I just find myself exhaling deeply and growing increasingly tired and exhausted as I load up yet another level where I have to constantly pull off large chains just to get rid of enemies on screen yet again, and then going to the next level and doing exactly the same thing again. There's no consistency in this despite it being the same every time because of the way its designed and because of the RNG elements. If you don't magically get to unlock the next thing that lets you actually get through the level then you just have to endlessly repeat the previous levels. It's just tedious. And if you managed to make a game like this innately feel tedious then you've really messed up quite badly.

_childDocuments_.review: Grindstone is a mobile app that's been dumped on Steam as if it was a real PC game (it's not)... it's a cash grab from greedy mobile devs.  This mobile app is a really basic hybrid Candy-Crush/Bejewelled game meets simple pathing puzzle as you need to put your finger on your iPhone and trace a line through the matching gems (monsters, whatever) to eliminate as many as you can each turn.  There's a couple of other gimmicks but basically this is a crap mobile app and that's all PC gamers really should need to know. From a technical perspective, as a mobile app, this doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.The mobile app is comprised of somewhat mediocre hand drawn 2D illustrations instead of professional looking 3D game assets.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget to arrange someone who can create graphical assets properly, or lack of talent.  Regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is very low, beneath what PC gamers have come to expect in this era of cutting edge photorealistic 3D graphics.  At least it's not pixel "art", but if you're looking for contemporary, immersive visuals, this mobile app is a fail.There's no option to change the resolution and no useful graphics tweaks.  There's no way to ensure this is running at the native resolution of your display.  There's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.The controls can't be customised because the game has such a dumbed down, simplified interface that it's just iPhone screen tapping stuff.  The fact that the interface is this dumbed down might be seen as a problem in itself, however... this is a fairly shallow experience if you're the kind of gamer that likes to play games with deep, rich control schemes and interaction.  You'll get none of that here.Because this is a mobile app, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the iPhones that the mobile app was designed for.  These are unfortunate handicaps and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was an afterthought for the iPhone developers who are to blame for this.  The mobile app is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for mobile phones forces upon a game.  Once more, mobile devs have made gaming worse for everyone.  I didn't spend thousands on building a gaming rig just so I could pretend it's an iPhone.These technical defects push this mobile app below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.The mobile app never really caught on with the millions of gamers on Steam, with a very low peak player count close to launch, and then just a handful of players launching this mobile app every couple of days.  This is undoubtedly caused by factors such as those raised in this review.  It's always helpful with buying decisions to consider how popular and successful the product is, and unfortunately while this did accumulate a few participation trophy reviews, overall, people just aren't using it.So, should you buy this mobile app?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?Grindstone has the ridiculous, laughable price of $20 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the mobile app, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.  They seriously want TWENTY BUCKS FOR A MOBILE APP. Just who do they think we are?

_childDocuments_.review: I used a random steam game picker and hit Grindstone by accident. WOW... best wheel spin ever! I never would have found this gem but for luck, and I gotta tell ya it is INSANELY underrated. Like, this is more satisfying than hitmarkers, more comfy than minecraft, and more unique than any puzzle game I've seen in YEARS. It's such a good concept that it makes you wonder why it took so long for somebody to release a matching game that also involves tactical movement. Chaining combinations is just too good to pass up and I have to wonder if the game is designed to create more of them than it otherwise would at random. So far, the game seems to create opportunities often enough that I feel like I'm wining at a slot machine everytime I play this. Puzzle game of the freaking decade by my book!

_childDocuments_.review: Quick Description:-Grindstone is a blood soaked Match 3 puzzle game w/ a very unique art direction.  I really enjoyed my just under 9 hrs w/ Grindstone.  I have very fond memories of playing Tetris Attack for endless hrs back almost 30 years ago on the SNES.  This is probably the most interesting game in this genre that I've played since the good old days of Tetris Attack.  I enjoyed this quite a bit more than Shovel Knight Pocket Dungeon, which was really surprising to me.  Consensus:-Solid Game (Tier 3 and makes up 35% of my reviews).  I loved the art style, really enjoyed hunting down blueprints and unlocking cool new weapons, and loved seeing what kind of crazy combo I could string together.  Unfortunately, I did start to find the overall experience to be a bit repetitive by the 7th or 8th hr.  W/ it's most recent update, there are over 350 levels, which is insane value.  I picked this up for $5 and think that is a slam dunk recommendation at that price point.

_childDocuments_.review: Played this on Apple Arcade back in 2020/2021. I'm not a match 3 player, but this game also isn't exactly a match 3. It takes the best part of match 3 (trying to create chain's) and takes it up a couple notches. One of the most creative games in the past 5 years, and glad to see it not stuck on a dying platform. Also, the soundtrack is nuts for a match 3 game, so you should listen to that even if you have no interest in playing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: TDLR: Super addictive, charming puzzle game. Worth the money (even more worth if it's on sale).Grindstone is NOT a Bejeweled or 3 matcher type game. It's about creating paths between creeps of the same colour, and creating huge combos to complete objectives on the maps.I last played Grindstone a couple of years ago on Apple Arcade (20hrs+), and it's just as great as I remember. They've added a lot of new features (dailies, hats etc) since I last played.Yes It is a port of the mobile game to PC, but it doesn't have ANY mobile game BS (ads, micro transactions, etc), and the controls work great with mouse.Worth the $20, but should probably be cheaper ($10-$15 would be perfect). I got it on sale for $5, but I wouldn't have any regrets if I bought it at full price.The only thing I don't like is how potentially easy it is to click the "Erase save" button in the settings menu, it seems like that option should only be available on the "Choose a Save" screen when the game launches. The game speed (animations/scrolling) appears to be tied to the frame rate, so run it as high as possible (180fps in my case) for the smoothest experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun concept of a game, basically it is a logic game where you have to connect as much creeps in a line as you can using various bonuses and abilities. Very addictive and fun once you see the execution of your planning (moving down enemies with fervor and bloodlust). It gets really hard going into late levels, especially when you want to get all treasures and defeat special creeps.
_childDocuments_.name: Grindstone

_childDocuments_.review: Grindstone is exactly the game I wanted it to be. From the first time I saw the trailer, it caught my interest and I was instantly attracted to the game's theme. Having played many puzzle games in the past, it can be hard to find one that is different enough for one to dive back into those waters. Grindstone is a great puzzle game with a fantastically silly premise. This would be one of the only puzzle games I would recommend for my friends who normally turn their noses up at the genre. I know I was late to the party, but the game did not disappoint! Well recommended for a gamer who wants some light fun and enjoys dark humor in a fantasy setting.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty simple idea but quite addicting. I hope this game gets mobile port someday, I'm enjoying it a lot. The gameplay is pretty solid, with my main nitpicks being small things that definitely can be improved like small QoL and touches: the lack of bgm on the map/inn area (when you talk to npc it's lively, but when you try to back out the sudden silence is a bit jarring) and lack of quick restart button for those who wants to redo their level from a bad startThe art and animation is very charming and the character design is so good. I love it! The gameplay is very addictive and for the price it's quite a grab. Love it.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game.  I got it in the latest humble bundle.  It's a cute game with a sweet soundtrack.  The gameplay loop is addicting and seeing the creeps get crushed is satisfying.  I remote into my computer at home to play it during calls at work LOL.  It is a good way to pass the time.  One thing I dislike however is how RNG levels can be, sometimes the same level will be exponentially harder because of the placement/colors of the creeps.  Also, the "grind" (heh) for some one use items as well as the mandatory healing requiring grindstones which are hard to come by is rather annoying.  Worth a buy on sale for sure for hours of puzzling entertainment if you are into that sort of thing.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun spin on a match game. Sure, it's a mobile game first, but it's still fun and scratches an itch. The gear you earn in game makes past zones interesting by adding more to your arsenal to earn chests with mats to make more gear, and it never strayed too far into "too difficult" for my baby brain. I personally enjoy the animation style and think it's neat to look at.

_childDocuments_.name: Grindstone

_childDocuments_.review: CRIMINALLY UNDERRATED GEM! I mainly played this on Nintendo Switch and put like at least 20 hours into it on there. I need to play it more here on Steam too. I am not usually into puzzle games, but there is just something so satisfying and unique about Grinstone that it's a rare exception for me. I have heard people say it's like a more bizarre ultraviolent take on Bejeweled (never played Bejeweled) which honestly can't think of anything else quite like this game! This game has such quality and care put into it's art style and animations! The minute to minute game feel is EXCELLENT. Plus I love the Flying Lotus inspired soundtrack too since I am a big fan of Flylo (saw an interview where the composer said the music is inspired by Flying Lotus!)Oh and MAN can this game get challenging the deeper you delve into it's levels. I remember many times getting my ass properly kicked by the very intelligently designed challenging puzzles that feel borderline impossible at times, but eventually you pass the level that felt impossible and you feel awesome for it! Grindstone is a hidden gem that if I put an arbitrary number on the end, I think i'd give it a STRONG 9/10 review score! It's definitely a title I am trying to get my friends to take notice in because great games like this deserve to succeed! So yeah, just putting this review up here to help Grindstone gain more traction and exposure.

_childDocuments_.review: (Played on Steam Deck, which works to perfection) This is a great time-wasting game that makes the minutes go by with its satisfying take on the Match 3 concept. Instead, players can just match 1 - but the real joy is in making long chains that connect with materials (such as wood) and gems to make the strings even longer. It really is a simple concept, but such a satisfying pay off. I paid $9 during the Winter Sale and I already feel like even at full price this is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely addictive, with a fun and approachable charm. It's interesting to see such casual cartoon gore, portrayed in a way that isn't "candifying" it or making it seem like it could be passed for anything other than guts and gore. And yet it remains charming and fits within the aesthetic of the game!My brother regrets revealing this game's existence to me. He has found me playing this game for hours straight without eating or drinking or sleeping. He watches with horror as I continue to vanquish Creeps, slaughtering millions without mercy.Anyway the game's great and you should get it. Very fun puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: This has been my go to game when I had Apple Arcade but I they wouldn't let me buy the game outright on it, so I got it on Steam.  It's a fun puzzle where you play a father (or his mom) trying to gather funds for a vacation by going berserk and killing mostly harmless creatures of the same color and stealing their treasures (or mock them by breaking gems in front of their faces).  But it's okay because the CalArts design makes everything family friendly and even the blood are in pastel colors.But really it's fun to come back to this game from time-to-time, and for now the developers are still adding content.
_childDocuments_.name: Grindstone

_childDocuments_.review: I've come to the realization that this is my all-time favorite game. A friend said it's like candy crush on testosterone. There are some light rpg/strategy elements as you can equip different, craftable weapons. You get three slots at a time and you can use a vast combination of shields, swords, arrows, and potions. The Adventure Time-esque (aka CAL Arts) style and the high replay value, both keep me coming back for more. Heck, it's probably more the incredible soundtrack than anything. Either way, it's a great way to unwind each night. (I literally play every night before bed.) Most my play time is on other devices, so I'm like 200+ hours into this game. It's simple, but I can't stop and won't stop ever playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent variation on the matching mechanic. Packed with content, with new features, new enemies and power-ups dropping constantly. On the early levels, use the power-ups which recharge every level for free so you have plenty of resources for the later levels. _childDocuments_.review: The game has a demo which is pretty cool on the devs part.The art style is beautiful, the music is soothing and engaging, and the gameplay loop is surprisingly satisfying, and it doesn’t really get old; there’s a ton of different items to unlock and the game is chocked full of content, it’s also not grindy, which I was worried given this was a mobile game originally.The game has been adapted beautifully to pc and it can run on pretty much everything, the ui has been reworked for a much better keyboard and mouse control, and the game is fairly relaxing and doesn’t get too challenging unless you’re trying to get most collectibles and/or items.
_childDocuments_.name: Grindstone

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this game is great fun and well worth the modest asking price. Tons of levels and lots of variety, a great match 3 now that Puzzle Quest has gone to the horrible, at least for me, freemium model.The game is not without its issues though. The biggest issue is that the difficulty balance as you progress through the game is a bit off at times. I might get stuck for quite a while on one level that seems to depend mostly on luck, then I'll breeze through the next ten levels. Compounding this issue is that the resources you win, which are used to purchase abilities to help you clear levels, are also poorly balanced. I have tons of gems but lack many of the other much more useful resources. The abilities are extremely expensive to buy so making a mistake and buying something is is expensive that doesn't work out is always a risk. It is very difficult to grind for these rarer resources.Still a great game and highly reccomended.

name: MultiVersus

And as the roster expands, so does the spectacle — with new personalities and play styles turning up the heat in every battle.    MAPS Our maps turn legendary realms like the  Batman’s Bat Cave, Jake and Finn’s Treefort, Game of Thrones’ Throne Room into epic battle grounds. And the best part? We’re adding new maps regularly, so the party never stops! MODES Whether you’re seeking the intensity of 1v1, the frenzy of a 4-player mayhem, or team up for strategic 2v2 battles, we’ve got you covered. Plus, introducing an all new PvE mode, a thrilling realm of limitless combat possibilities designed for solo or co-op play. CROSS-PLATFORM MultiVersus has full cross-play and cross-progression support across all platforms. THAT’S NOT ALL FOLKS! Our brawlin’ Multiverse does not hit snooze — and neither should you! There’s always something new brewing in our evolving MultiVerse with regular content drops and on-going quality improvements.

_childDocuments_.review: - A heavy focus on team play. Abilities that help teammates. Perk stacking.- Roster with good variety. Everyone feels unique.- Lots of personality. (character animations, profile customization, etc.)- Controller settings that Smash Bros. desperately needs. (input buffer, platform drop, neutral buttons, etc.)- Very customizable interface settings.- Cross-platform matchmaking that can be toggled.- You can try every character in training. Something I wish Apex Legends would allow. You can even try their premium skins. Try before you buy.- The overall feel of the game just doesn't feel good to me. The aerial movement is floaty and snappy at the same time.- The online is horrible (or people are on Wi-Fi). Players are teleporting frequently. My moves don't hit when they visually do. I get hit randomly sometimes.- It's F2P and there's MTX (microtransactions). I didn't play long enough to know if it's done well or horribly.Overall, I can't recommend this game because of the 2 bad reasons I mentioned above. _childDocuments_.review: In don't post reviews often, but I believe PFG need to understand how badly they've messed up and if even one more review helps, I'll contribute.The game in beta was a great experience with only some bugs, glitches and exploit combos that needed to be fixed. Somehow PFG has un-optimized the game (possibly due to upgrading to UE5) and caused it to run badly on most platforms unless your specs far exceed the recommended reqs and your internet quality is perfect.Attack decay was added specifically to prevent spamming combos from occurring and was one of the best updates to the beta creating a fair playing environment.........and the decay feature was just removed, there is no possible reason this was a good decision. The games netcode is written by a child causing constant freezing on loading screens, lagging, desync an disconnects/crashes. Further, people are facing search timeouts after being disconnected! How this has been allowed for over a week with no acknowledgement from PFG is actually insane.The perk and currency system has been "improved", yet now requires players to max level 5-6 characters just to afford to unlock 1. The large selection of perks available in the beta have been reduced to a few options, most of which have little to no effect on the game. Previously, players cold earn gold from playing matches. Now what do i get from playing each game? A little experience? Progress on the battlepass? So how are players supposed to unlock new fighters? the obvious solution would be the micro-transactions.TLDR: Somehow PFG has nuked the potential this game had by making it worse than the beta, rolling back good beta updates, and showing their greed for micro-transactions. As someone that couldn't stop talking about this game; who was excitedly waiting for the re-release, this is a huge disappointment, and in its current state, this game will die within the month.

_childDocuments_.review: Played this quite extensively during the initial beta (Peaked in top 100 Shaggy players, hovered around 500 top) and I'm just confused why they decided to tone down the speed of the game to a snail's pace whilst including an intentional 30 frame delay on inputs. It makes the general flow of the game feel awful especially with how fights feel as though you're looking through a microscope rather than from the actual proper camera zoomed out at the stage. Move priority still isn't a thing for some reason, even though every other single platform fighter worth its weight has established that as a means for heavies to compete reasonably with lighter characters (that or super armor), but nope! People who know how to play Assassins can fish out a quick frame, no risk move that, if it connects, strings together an easy 60% combo that sets up a free ringout or leads in to juggle that leads to a ringout. Some moves have an insane linger  that you can't punish as a result, otherwise you get sucked in and chipped by them because good game design™. Only heavy character that has any reasonable chance against people who are competent right now is Iron Giant and that's because he has a guaranteed infinite grab chain by cancelling his taunt that can lead to a ringout.Hit boxes are trash and have been trash ever since the initial beta overhaul and there's an entire encyclopedia's worth of moves that just seem to hit whenever they feel like it which is asinine for any fighting game. You don't have to make them 1:1, no one is saying that, but if you have extensions (like Banana Guard's spear thrust) you need to at least attempt to make them match up to the extension. I don't know if this is a net code thing or if the servers are currently being put under heavy player load, but it felt this way prior to the initial release back during the initial beta as well and it's disappointing to see that this hasn't really been changed.New players can barely get to consider who they even want to play because the time you need to invest for a single character is unreasonable, there's four different currencies that players have to manage for some reason alongside that which makes ZERO sense and you can't even practice characters you haven't unlocked to at least get a feel for how those characters perform before considering a purchase for them. So then that leads to the greatest question: How can you recommend this to a player that wasn't around for the initial launch when getting characters was fairly easy (took a few hours, if even that, rather than...days) and even worse, how can you recommend a game like this when it's currently performing the way it is? You don't, that's what. And until Warner Brothers steps off and lets Player First Games try to actually make the game playable, it's going to remain that way until WBs either does the classic move they do where they shut down the game a year from now, or the player count dwindles to unsustainable numbers and the game gets closed down because it's not raking in enough profit for them. They do this with every game under their banner and it's going to be shame if Multiversus goes down the same road.

_childDocuments_.review: Out of all the "Smash-clones," this one has the potential to actually be better than Smash. Coming from someone who played Smash since Melee. The game is F2P. Grinding for new chars is pretty tedious. You'll have to play for 5 - 8 hours or so to get enough in-game currencies for a new char. Good thing is that there is a paid option to skip the grind entirely, which is buying the game for as low as $40. The $40 pack gives you 15 characters unlock, so you have access to the entire roster right away. Or you can use the tokens to unlock the chars that you want to play and slowly grind to unlock the rest, while saving the rest of the tokens for future DLC chars. Besides that, all purchases are for cosmetics that doesn't affect gameplay. The main competitive focus of the game is 2v2 instead of 1v1 unlike Smash, so the meta is very different. There's a new layer of team building and character synergy that isn't in Smash. The roster current already has a good mix from franchises, but will definitely get even more interesting in the future since WB owns a huge catalog of massively successful franchises that they could add to the game, including DC superheros, LOTR, Matrix, Mad Max, Harry Potter, LEGO, Adult Swim, Cartoon Network, Scooby-Doo, Space Jam, etc...It's free, so give it a try. If you liked the game, my suggestion is to buy the Founder's pack for $40 and not having to worry about the grind, since that's the worst aspect of the game by far, and I hope the devs address it when the game launches.

_childDocuments_.review: Unless you enjoy playing against bots while the game is pretending those are real players you won't have much fun.This game has no respect for you or your time. It is (or rather used to be) a decent platform fighter somewhat built around baiting you into purchasing characters and cosmetics like a mobile game. Now it's just that - a mobile-esque game with a WB theme.The full release was supposed to fix the glaring issues of the beta but as it turns out it broke/removed a lot of features. Promises of better netcode remain unfulfilled, with what feels like a 1 in 5 chance for the server to crash or drop at least one player. That is if you even get matched against real players - the matchmaking forces you to play against bots if you are playing with someone new to the game or if you are on a losing streak. These forced bot matches have an even higher chance of booting you back to the main menu (or even crashing the game altogether).They slowed down the game and nerfed mobility in what one might assume was an attempt to improve net play. The gameplay suffered greatly, and for nothing.It seems like the attack decay mechanic (a later addition I was not fond of) has been reworked but none of the characters have been thoroughly tested, a lot of them having easy setups for infinites and/or game breaking bugs. Removing a band-aid solution is great, not balancing characters accordingly is not so great.The perk system has been simplified. Perks have been reduced to almost a non-factor, removing interesting synergies and disincentivising strategy.Most new stages are gimmicky and full of stage hazards. I'm not saying every game should be an esport but this is definitely a complete 180 in direction from the beta. I'd rather get outplayed by my opponents in a fighting game, not by the stage itself.The new singleplayer 'content' is really uninspired, not much else to say about it. Perhaps I would be willing to try more of these rifts out if I wasn't already tired of playing against bots in regular matches.The game has like seven different 'reward tracks' or 'battle passes' running at the same time. These are all separate menus that you have to click through if you want to receive your rewards for playing the game. Now, I'm not one to care about any of that pointless fluff but it's so blatantly designed to bait you into spending money that I can't help but feel disgusted.With all these bugs, questionable design decisions, terrible progression systems, predatory monetisation scheme, mobile-esque UI, and core features missing this is truly more 'beta' than the previous beta.

_childDocuments_.review: After a good week of playing MultiVersus, here's my main thoughts:   The gameplay is great, but Jesus Christ, the Online, Live Service elements really bring it down. First of all, what kind of game has you BUY the roster separately, as opposed to unlocking them just by playing? The same goes for currency! Everything is WAY too expensive & unless you pay $20, you're stuck having to grind & log in daily for weeks, only to get a criminally low amount. This game is WAY too greedy with currency. What PlayerFirst Games SHOULD have done is make EVERY currency (including Gleamium) completely free & instead of making it exclusive to missions, limited time events & Battle Passes, you can earn a minimum of 1,000 of every currency just by PLAYING MATCHES, and you get an extra 1,000 for each by WINNING THE MATCHES.   Don't even get me started on XP for BP, Account, & Characters. My complaints with currency directly applies to XP! My solution would be the same one I have for currency, give 1,000 of EVERY XP for every match you play, and an extra 1,000 for winning!   Then there is the constant connection and server issues, what the flying fudge happened? I can't even play an online match for more than 30 seconds without getting disconnected, even though I have a strong internet connection. For example, I won an online 2v2 match and even got to the results/victory screen. Then, for literally no reason, I get disconnected, resulting in the game not even registering my progress on a "Win PvP games" mission, even though I CLEARLY WON. So I just straight-up got screwed over because of PlayerFirst Games' failure to maintain good servers. They seriously need to fix this before I do anything past logging in for the day.   This is what happens when you make your game "free" to play. You deal with EVERY bad thing that comes with making a game a Live Service game, you get ♥♥♥♥ all for just playing & enjoying the game, unless you pay more money than what a full-price copy of the game would actually cost. Whoever decided to make this game a "free"-to-play, live service game at Warner Bros. games, here's a big "SCREW YOU" for potentially ruining a game that is actually great without any Live Service elements.With that being said, MultiVersus a solid 8/10, B-!It is an absolutely wonderful game, with gorgeous styles, incredible character designs, impressive voice-work, & incredible gameplay. But before I recommend it to any of my friends, as well as any players in general, I believe it seriously needs a major overhaul that removes every single Live Service element in its design, as well as get their servers in check so players don't keep disconnecting every minute.

_childDocuments_.review: Multiversus is a platform fighter game like Super Smash Bros, but focuses on 2v2 instead of 1v1. It currently has characters from various Warner Brothers properties and will likely have plenty of characters added in the future. The gameplay itself is solid and each character plays quite differently from one another. However, there is not much content in the game. The arcade mode is fairly basic so far and there are about three other main game modes when fighting against other players or bots. It also takes a while to unlock new characters since you get around 15 to 20 gold per match. If you mainly play only several characters, this problem is not too bad.However, I cannot recommend the game due to how the game is seemingly designed to try to get you to play as long as possible. The xp rate for character leveling was halved and completing the battle pass takes longer this season. Furthermore, battle pass progress mainly comes from daily and weekly missions. You get little xp from completing a match. A recent event also took quite some time to get all of the free items. Personally, I did not like this and stopped playing the game since it felt like the game either wants to play a lot or start paying for characters or event progression. In the recent event, if you bought an event skin (only two were free), you would get a higher rate of event progression.Overall, I do not recommend playing Multiversus at this time. He asked that I use my chemistry knowledge to cook methamphetamine, which he would then sell using his connections in the drug world. Connections that he made through his career with the DEA. I was astounded, I always thought that Hank was a very moral man and I was thrown and confused, but I was also particularly vulnerable at the time, something he knew and took advantage of. I've been dealing with a cancer diagnosis that's poised to bankrupt my family. Hank took me on a ride along, and showed me just how much money even a small meth operation could make. And I was weak. I didn't want my family to go into financial ruin so I agreed. Every day, I think back at that moment with regret. I quickly realized that I was in way over my head, and Hank had a partner named Gus (50M) and essentially sold me into servitude to this man, and when I tried to quit, Gus threatened my family. I didn't know where to turn.Eventually, Hank and Gus had a falling out. From what I can gather, Hank was always pushing for a greater share of the business, to which Gus flatly refused to give him, and things escalated. Gus was able to arrange what you call it a "hit" on my brother-in-law, and failed, but Hank was seriously injured, and I wound up paying his medical bills which amounted to a little over $177,000. Upon recovery, Hank was bent on revenge and started working with a guy named Hector (70M) to plot to kill Gus, and the bomb that he used was built by me, and he gave me no option in it. I killed him. I have often contemplated suicide, but I wanted to go to the police, I was frightened, Hank had risen in the ranks to become the head of the local DEA, and about that time, to keep me in line, he took my children from me. _childDocuments_.review: VERY fun game. Every character is unique and feels good to play, save for the first few matches with them when you're figuring things out. When you're starting out at the game, it might feel noodly and overly-fluid in a way, but as you get more used to the mechanics, you learn to use the game's almost-slipperiness as a combo tool or an evasive aid, and it begins to feel satisfying as you master the game's movement and characters.A note for any Smash fans looking to play this game - the game's definitely similar, and having Smash experience will absolutely help with playing this game, but DON'T try to play this game like Smash. _childDocuments_.review: Edit: This review was written during the beta, and as such, it no longer accurately reflects the current state of the game or my opinion of it.Pros:- The gameplay is fantastic. Each character feels distinctly different and unique. The doubles gameplay, which the game advertises as its primary gameplay, is interesting and allows for great synergy between characters. The controls handle as tightly as the characters are supposed to, and I’ve had zero issues with mis-inputs that aren’t just because of my specific controller.- The personality is on full display in this game’s presentation. Every character has unique dialogue with every other character, both at the start of the match and when landing a knockout.- The roster for this game is fantastic, with everything from Looney Tunes to DC Comics to Game of Thrones. Additionally, the relative obscurity of some of these characters (like Stripe) makes it clear that the development team is foremost concerned with including characters with potential, alongside Warner Bros.’s flagship characters. And even when the team adds a character that’s clearly for marketing purposes (like Black Adam), they still base the character on the original source material, whether it be the comics, an animated series, or something else.- The movesets are a sight to see. Each one is distinctly different from all the others, even when characters use similar weapons (like Arya Stark and Wonder Woman). It’s also very much worth noting that no character feels like an amalgamation of references to the source material; every character feels like you’re playing how the character would fight if they were in an arena.Cons:- The pricing scheme is easily the biggest issue with the game, currently. Put simply, the Founder’s Pack is the only $10+ thing that’s worth the price. $5 for a character is fine, since it’s the price to pay if you don’t want to save up coins to unlock them. The issue comes with the skins and emotes. $5 for an emote is absurd, and that’s the lowest you’ll have to pay for an emote; some cost $10. And then… there’s the skins. During the Halloween event, there were two particular skins available for purchase: Black Lantern versions of Wonder Woman and Superman. These two skins were the highest tier of rarity, and the completely changed the characters’ appearances, voicelines, and post-match animations. They also cost $20 each. For reference, the Standard Edition Founder’s Pack costs $39.99. It allows you to unlock 15 characters and gives you 300 Gleamium. Buying both Black Lantern skins would cost you the same amount of money for far, far less reward.- The Season Pass. The dev team isn’t making the premium pass worth the price, especially for Season 2.- The grinding for gold can be a big turn-off for a lot of players. Personally, I’ve not been bothered much by it, but I acknowledge it’s an issue. Character unlock prices can range from 1,000 gold to 3,000 gold, with new characters mostly costing more. That gold can take a lot of playtime to build up, sometimes more than can realistically be accomplished between character releases. There’s a weekly rotation of free characters, but that can only take you so far.- Grinding character levels. To get all of a character’s gameplay-relevant level unlocks, you need to reach roughly level 10 on that character, 15 for all general character-specific unlocks. There are XP packs to speed up the process, but they’re almost nonexistent to acquire, so you’ll mostly gain character XP through gameplay. It takes several hours to reach level 10, and that was before the dev team increased the XP requirement. It definitely can discourage players from wanting to try new characters.Overall, the game is worth playing, but it has some major flaws that the dev team really needs to fix if they want the game to survive another few months.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - Player First Games should worry more about making a fun game, than how to bait players into spending money and time on boring, unrewarding content.  You'll spend less money buying Super Smash Bros, even if you have to buy the Switch too.Review - I wish steam had a neutral review, but they don't so sadly, this game gets a thumbs down.  I suppose that could change - but Player First Games has only made player last decisions for the duration of this game's existence.  I dropped $99 on a founder's pack in the beta, so clearly I felt like this game had potential.  The characters are cool, the move kits are fun, and it looks great.  But sadly, the development of the game has been a lesson in frustration.The game entered an open early access with no commentary on it being a limited time open beta.  But when things didn't go well for the game they suddenly announced the open beta was ending.  (This unfortunately will continue to be a theme with how the dev team fails to maintain transparency with their player base)  As sad as this was for the few fans left, most took it in stride and took it on good faith when the game returned in a year it would be polished and ready.  Sometimes having the guts (and funds) to take a game offline to really work on it is brave, right?It could have been.  Unfortunately after a year of closed doors development the game relaunched with less features than before, more bugs, and an extremely predatory mobile game monetization method.  True the dev team had rebuilt the game in unreal 5, and I'm sure that was no small feat in a year.  But sadly most gamers will miss that because after not playing the game for a year the differences would be hard to notice for most.  The net code was supposed to be better, and maybe it is, but it can be hard to tell as many gamers ran into strange disconnects and lag issues.  I for one never experienced any lag or disconnects in the beta but have frequently in the relaunch.  I'm sure that issue will get worked out in time, unfortunately the next issue probably wont.Where as the game had a pretty standard f2p model before (not far from a game like League of Legends), the relaunch had monetization method that looks less like f2p games and more like a mobile game.  The relaunch did inclued a single player mode, but it required the leveling of gems which is a slow, burdensome, and boring process.  If you guessed you could bypass this buy just paying to level your gems you'd be right.  The problem with this mode is the challenges often require a specific character and a specific character with a specific skin.  (In there defense many of these can be obtained eventually by watching for twitch giveaways or weekly challenges - the problem is it requires a watchdog eye on the game and still leaves gaps) Since I bought the $99 founders pass I already have every character unlocked, and there are still challenges I just can't do because I haven't purchased a $20 skin.  (They have softened this a patch requiring less completion in a rift and sometimes letting you 'borrow' a skin but it's too little too late imho) This single player mode will be more frustrating for anyone who's new to the game and has a handful of characters unlocked.  You can mitigate some of this pain by inviting a friend to do the single player mode with you, but you have to be at the same level of progress - this basically makes making friends online to play with almost worthless.  One or both of you will be doing challenges for no credit.As if that wasn't enough some of the challenges the devs clearly tweeked to be extra impossible hurdles to surmount.  You can have your gems double what the required gem level is and still run into a challenge that is stupidly impossible.  I even had a friend (also 2x gem level higher than require) try to help me with a challenge and we still couldn't pass it.The devs also dangle rewards for these single players rifts but then obscure what the path to unlock them is really like.  You can unlock Agent Smith for free.  You only have to defeat 20 single player bosses.  No big deal, right?  Each 'Rift' has 5 difficulty levels, and they've confirmed 8.  So if you thought to yourself - well, I'll just clear each rift on the 3 easiest difficulty levels and not worry about the stretch goals, and I'll have room to breathe, you'd be wrong.  Because inexplicably certain difficulties are unavailable on certain rifts.  Rift 1 might have 1-3 difficulties unlocked, but rift 2 won't have the 2nd difficulty unlocked.  All this is to basically say they removed random mid, or early, level difficulties to make the path to unlock rewards harder than it appears and to keep the work involved obscured until you're already invested.Did I mention repeating the exactly same content upwards of 5 times (on stupidly dumb difficulties levels even if you have grinded up your gems levels) is really really boring?To their credit the devs have softened some of these aspects as the community has complained, but in truth it probably has more to do with player count dropping than them working to make a game in community with their player base.There are daily quests to do, and you can make descent pace on things by just doing your dailies.  This works very well for the season pass, but less well for the single player rifts, which still require you to clear a bunch of challenges (repeating the same content 3-5 times over) even if your gems are very high, it's still a boring and tedius process.  Also the reddit community started memeing the challenges because they are often laughably specific.  Knock out a player on the left side of the map while wearing a shark hat on ToonVille Map.  I'm being a little hyperbolic, but that's not far from the truth.All of this is made extra salty because the dev studio is named Player First Games.  Yet sadly, since the open beta the game has consistently made choices that put players last.The sad thing is clearly a lot of time, thought, and planning went into how to bait and switch gamers with a new gatcha style fomo cash shop - too bad these resources didn't go into making a fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty damn fun and has a lot of heart and soul put into it by developers who obviously care. They were releasing a character every two weeks complete with a unique and finished moveset and professional voice acting done by the character's original voice actors (in many cases). However, until they fix the servers I cannot in good faith recommend this game. Every single gamemode and every single match is unplayable until they do. 2v2, 1v1, even Vs. Bots are all in states of decay, as rubberbanding characters and disconnected attacks plague every game I have played for the past few months. I keep thinking they'll fix the servers as the head developer said they would but I look back and realize he made that promise over five months ago and the servers only continue to get worse and I have to think they aren't really doing anything. I am not exaggerating when I say I have not played a match without horrendous lag since, like, November 2022. Maybe I'll come back and change my review when they fix the servers.P.S. revert the changes made to character leveling and the battle pass leveling both of them were fine and now both are needlessly grindy. _childDocuments_.review: It's actually one of the greatest ironic stories of all time. They release a more than good beta a year ago, and they finalized the game by making it slower and a grind-fest a year later. There's a multitude of people complaining everywhere you look on this game. The final game could have been what it was shown in the beta. For anyone getting into platform fighters, I do not recommend this one, because this is the slowest platform fighter in the history of all platform fighters. There is no platform fighter that is slower than this, bar none. Why would one think that making the game slower would make it fun? Here's my theory. What they did was follow Nintendo's footsteps with Brawl into making the game into a more casual, and broader experience for the non-fighting game player--but you will see in less than a year that this game's player base will be dead if the developers are NOT listening to the community because the core player base that expect a platform fighter to be fast will leave first.
