_childDocuments_.review: Open beta was insanely better.Here is why:- Gameplay feels too slow - This is one we are hearing a lot, putting it at the top of the list.- UI is hard to read and difficult to navigate- Input Buffer is long. Estimated 30 Frames- Battle Pass XP should be earned via Gameplay not just missions.- Camera Zoom is zoomed in too far.- Unable to Switch Characters between Rematches- Option to turn off Player Color Overlay is missing.- 1v1 (Bots) & 2v2 (Bots) is missing from Core Gameplay options- Unable to Select Servers- Rift Gems are difficult to level and feel very Pay 2 Win (Rift Feedback Thread)- Rifts requiring Multiplayer to 100% doesn't feel good for Solo Players.- Agent Smith Event is too grindy and impossible to complete at this point.- No Offline Mode - Game is always online.- Career Profiles are lackluster, displaying a lot less information than in the Beta with no ability to see full match details.- Characters should be able to be purchased with Tickets, Gleamium or Fighter Currency. Should always have the choice.- Xbox Graphical Fidelity & Framerate is low.- Fighter Currency feels cumbersome to earn when compared to Gold from the Beta Version.- Missing Ability to Swap neutral and side attack, as you could in the Beta Version.- Spectator Mode missing from Local PlayThe game is now way too slow, but that's not the worst part... There's also a 30 FRAMES delay between inputs now (Input buffer)... So that means if you press jump, you will jump after 30 frames have passed from the previous input. This used to be a setting. Not anymore. Default was estimated from 5-10. Now default is set at 30.For comparison, ultimate is 9 frames. and Rivals of Aether 6 frames.Now, they did switch to a new engine and implement a new netcode. Many of these things can be fixed, so I'm giving them a chance. But I will leave a review of the current state of the game, which is a Nope.

_childDocuments_.review: At a surface-level, MultiVersus combines Super Smash Bros. mechanics with a more hack-and-slash style of combat. Casual players and thrill-seekers are sure to welcome the fast-paced action with open arms - if that's you, this is your game! However, more methodical, hardcore players are likely to become frustrated by the low cooldown and start-up frames of most attacks, the unclear hitbox sizes, and the lack of hitstun, leading to a watered-down strategical gameplay experience.- Polished visuals- Polished sound design- Fun character gameplay designs - goofy moments galore- Character balanced, while still flawed in many ways, is overall very decent for a newly released fighter.- With the ability to customize your character taunts, out-of-bounds (death) animations, and loading screen flairs (think token system in LoL) via your account/character progress, you'll eventually have a wealth of customization options to choose from.- Continuing from the above point, the payment model is clearly more cosmetics-focused, which I categorize as a good thing.- For the time being, the time it takes to grind up gold to buy characters seems bit too slow, even for a free-to-play game. Gold-gain is much better paced toward buying perks.- Attack animations do not currently cleanly match their hitboxes. This makes for some very confusing character attack interactions.- The attack descriptions in the game, while good to have, do not provide enough information for more hardcore players to derive much meaningful info from them. (attack startup frames/cooldowns, hitboxes, hitbox frames, etc.)- See the section at the bottom of this review for thoughts from a long-time SSB competitor regarding strategy.- The "cave of life" in the Scooby's Haunted Mansion stage can lead to frustrating or funny moments, depending on your disposition toward stage hazards.- Currently there is no ranked mode, though there are matchmaking-rating leaderboards for the casual gameplay 1v1 and 2v2 modes. As indicated in the menu options, the devs clearly plan to launch a ranked mode at some point.- The perks system, while interesting in terms of the customization options available to augment any given strategy, adds a bit of a pay-to-win element to the game. Reason is - the perks cost gold to train, which is the same currency used to buy characters. If your goal is strictly to win, you need to have a variety of perks to match any given team, opponent, or stage set-up. However, if you want quicker access to characters to learn their ins and outs in PvP, you will be at a stat (perks) deficit compared to your opponents - Think runes in the early days of LoL.---I compiled a list of cons that affect me specifically from a strategical point of view, as a former SSB professional/semi-pro. Please note that the game is still in Beta and it's very possible that some or all of these will eventually be addressed by the game team. These are just my opinions.Neutral = game state in which no characters have been hit, and none are off-stageButton mashing, while still bad play from a strategical standpoint, unfortunately cannot be punished on reaction quite as frequently as one would expect. Aerials, airdodging, grounded attacks - The animations are so quick from start to end, that players are encouraged to use attacks even with the understanding that their attacks are likely to miss.This has the potential to dramatically slow down the pace of neutral if you plan on playing in a calm, collected, methodical manner - think SSBB Mr. Game & Watch upsmash and SSBB Metaknight forward-smash levels of cooldown frames on many, many attacks, both grounded and aerial.While character movement speed is indeed very fast, the pace of combat, before landing hits, can be quite tedious and slow as a result of the above. This leads to a very boring neutral unless you play mages (projectile users in MultiVersus).The character movement speed, while overall fast, fluid, and fun in its own right - when combined with the amount of movement, dodging, and directional airdodging options available - makes for a frustrating time chasing down opponents that choose not to interact. This makes it feel like being above an opponent or offstage is not as much of a disadvantage as it maybe should be.The movement options in the game are quick, but hitstun is very, very low and dodging options are plentiful (think Super Smash Bros Brawl levels of hitstun and dodging options, but on steroids). This shifts your focus while in advantaged states (after hitting someone) away from comboing as the advantaged player, and interacting as the disadvantaged player via knockback influence, more toward a rock-paper-scissors-style of guessing game about which option your opponent is going to choose to get out of what could be a nice, short combo.

_childDocuments_.review: What a travesty of a game.I had already hopped off of it for a while back when it first released due to really bad servers. It's insane.Putting the purchase issues and mismanagement of the servers, and losing any potential new players aside, even the core gameplay itself was broken. I definitely had fun at times with it, and the concept of a bunch of cartoon characters fighting was really awesome and there were good things about it, but they focused much more on making money than ever actually balancing the game. As a fighting game it was not good. As a fighting game it would have no place in EVO nor alongside the likes of super smash bros.My main purpose for writing this review is to warn any new players or even previous ones who didn't spend a dime on the game to keep it that way when it releases again. _childDocuments_.review: I remember buying this game for my sister a few years back. Didn't think much of it at the time, but I thought it would be a nice gift for her. I remember seeing her playing it from time to time, the message indicating that she'd started playing it popping up on the corner of my screen. There was always a certain small pride in seeing that, because to me it meant that she was enjoying my gift.Last September she committed suicide.After everything had more or less settled down from that, I sat down and booted up her computer. All that was on there was Chrome, Steam, Word, and a few games. One of them, of course, was Core keeper.She had played this game to pieces, clocking over 170 hours and owning practically everything the game had to offer. She had used every square inch to its maximum potential, and was making ridiculous amounts of loot. It was only then did I see just how much she loved my present. No other game she played quite captured her affection as much as this one. None of her friends really knew about it, however; it seems like she preferred to keep it to herself. Like it was her own little bit of heaven she could turn to whenever she wanted.And because of that, I can't help but smile whenever I play this game.I cannot recommend it enough; every bit of hard work the developer put into this masterpiece shows in every single aspect. The music is catchy and memorable (I'll often find myself humming certain tunes from it), the world feels lived-in and natural, and the gameplay is incredibly laid back and enjoyable. It's hard to stop once I get invested in the game; minutes can easily turn into several hours. And now, with the multiplayer beta, I play for even longer with my friends, each of us dedicated to our desired jobs. Most of all, however, we're all just happy to be together.

_childDocuments_.review: Can't recommend in it's current state, it left Beta and somehow came out in another Alpha a year later. An engine upgrade was not worth these changes. If you need know more than that, then read below. Before deep diving into a read, the game is free, so please play it yourself and come to your own conclusions, don't be like the social media hivemind that dismisses as it slow (which it is) when they go off and play equally as slow games (specifically smash ult) genuinely watch them side by side and you'll see what I mean.This is more of a gameplay deep dive review than addressing the anti-consumer-y stuff that's obviously going on.I'll preface this saying it's a different game now and I'm posting this on day 2. I don't expect anything to change really. My main discontentment is the game essentially caving to smash player's opinions on the Beta, and that being the likely leading reason why the game is a shadow of it's former self. Of all things I'm generally just most upset that the game lost it's Gameplay Identity, streamlining gameplay and focusing more on 1v1 changes. People wanted more visual clarity and a slower game so they got it.They fixed a lot of issues during the Beta and this feels like they spat in the face of all the dev time and work that went into delicately crafting it, scrapping most of that balance and starting over.It had issues with some pretty simple fixes that they simply didn't implement. The game being "too much to keep track of" and dodging out of moves being too safe was fixable with adjusting whiff recovery for instance. With the changes, dodging is now a gamble of a resource, and the movement has been severely neutered so it feels nowhere near as fun to move around in, and scrapping offstage is no longer frequent. This next point is attributed to all the people that complained about the game not having enough visual clarity or thinking that characters were too fast in the Beta. Generally the gameplay has been slowed down, not just in the framedata and hitstun but also in the way the game demands you play it now. Since dodges are very limited now, camping feels dominant, and camping with projectiles or disjoints until you get an opener feels like it's going to overtake the game. Even with the new "Stop camping" mechanic that burns your dodge meter, which, is very inconsistent and punishes the wrong players very often, it still does nothing because people would rather camp with projectiles and disjoints.This leads me to my next major gripe and major subtraction from the Beta, Attack Decay is gone.I think Attack Decay was an amazing mechanic that prevented spam of such mentioned above, it made gameplay much more dynamic and was a built-in balancing mechanism for forcing people to vary their moveset. It has been replaced by "move staling" (it got smashified) So now the meta will heavily center on people spamming and/or camping with their best moves much more, as well as all the inconsistencies that come with managing move staling. There is now only a tiny penalty for mindlessly spamming strong moves.Essentially the game got "smashified" ledge and disadvantage is a nightmare now, no one wants to take risks for openings or kills because the punishment is potentially incredibly severe for the low payoff. You're going to see way more ledgeguarding than offstage play now because of all of this.Downward spikes killpower feel nerfed hard as well, which is gonna make people wanna sit on the ledge instead of scrapping offstage Killpower generally is all over the place, some moves that feel like they shouldn't kill, do. It is incredibly inconsistent that I can kill someone at 40 off the top while not even that close to the blastzone, with a move that looks like it's made for damage racking and juggling, while I can't even spike someone near the bottom blastzone at the same or more damage and they still live. This is especially bad for 2v2, where team combos were and still are important, but now they flat out kill you when they happen. Hitboxes are also incredibly inconsistent across the board, especially on Wonder Woman, where I'll see her shield moves clip through me and not hit me but her sword moves be nowhere near my character and hit me. Iron Giant's downair can hit above his shoulder, and other crazy shenanigans.One of the worst changes is the 1-1 accurate hurtboxes for the characters, they now don't really have a cylinder, this means that if they go into hitstun animations they may just fall out of moves due to their hurtbox shifting, making combos and strings incredibly inconsistent from character to character. I don't know why they did this change because this isn't supposed to be an "immersive" game, it's a plat fighter, lol. More accurate hurtboxes is good but Gameplay is more important at times.Parries are wickedly unsatisfying because the window for punishment is huge, and I don't feel like I deserve to destroy somebody because I timed my one primary defensive option that I was, gonna hit anyway, at the right time. I think it's a fine mechanic but it's overtuned right now. This will get MUCH worse when custom buffer is added. What also sucks is that custom combos or anything that isn't a fully "true combo" now comes with the risk of you getting reversed and potentially dying at 20 off the top or something similar. I've done this to people and it doesn't feel right.Overall the movement in the Beta was full of player expression, and really just needed some fine tuning with things like whiff recovery.  Now it feels like no matter what character you play, you follow a limited flowchart, forced by unfortunately limited movement, and edging out your dodge meter as much as possible.Feels like the sauce and fun engaging movement is just all gone and they tried fixing something that wasn't broke. Better netcode and adding whiff recovery felt like the right path and for some reason they just swerved into a ditch.I can only imagine they made these changes to majorly streamline to a casual audience, which is fine but it came at a brutal cost of the game's identity and the player expression. To be honest I have a lot of fun playing it as a party game now. I hope people still enjoy the game cause I would really like it to succeed and hope the gameplay identity returns with it.

_childDocuments_.review: After about a week of normal play, my PvP now fails matchmaking 100% of the time. This has gone on for 5 days. Support gave me a Chat GPT answer of "this bug report probably covers it" (It didn't) and closed the ticket immediately.All suggested fixes have failed (verifying game files, turning off crossplay, reinstalling).Aside from the technical issues and abysmal customer support, the game has multiple currencies, including for unlocking fighter perks. After a week of play doing all challenges (including grinding all available characters to level 5 and taking advantage of an event that gave out fighter curency) I have managed to unlock all of two characters.The developers lock some content behind fighters being unlocked, so some branches of PvE content is locked unless you have a specific character or costume for a character.PvE has "missions" for each stage. One of these missions on every single stage is to play with another person.PvE progression is locked behind the average level of colored gems associated with a particular rift. These can only be leveled through crates. This means randomly. You get one crate per stage, then one crate per daily, which is usually about 5ish on one specific rift. Some of these dailies will choose stages locked behind characters or costumes.There are daily and weekly challenges, as well as event challenges. Like rifts, some of these are locked behind specific requirements that free players may not be able to fulfill. Additionally, some of these are also locked behind having the battle pass unlocked.These factors combine to create a situation where your'e driven to unlock specific characters with your extremely precious fighter points because of rift requirements or daily/weekly challenges if you have any hope to grind through the battle pass.The entire game is engineered to frustrate you into paying for their premium currency, which can be used to buy basically everything you'd be grinding for as a free player, including the battle pass, characters, costumes and account things like profile pics and the background behind your fighter.Due to the bugs, lack of customer support, and the design choices made to further the extreme monetization, I cannot recommend the game in its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: Just to get it out of the way, the Live Service, Battle Pass model is terrible especially for a platform fighting game. And with 4 separate currencies to keep track of it's already a bad look and clearly designed to keep a high player count as you try to earn 3 of the currencies; Fighter Currency, Perk Currency, and Prestige Currency. One of the worst elements of this game lies with the one thing designed to get you to play the game, the cast of characters from different big ips all owned by one corporation Warner Bros. Unlocking the characters is stupid. You are given 6 characters out of the 26 and the rest can only be unlocked by buying them with the Fighter Currency or the "Premium" Currency: Gleamium (aka real money). From all the fighting games I have played there is bound to be a DLC fighter or two that you have to buy with real money, all of which cost about 5ish dollars or lower. In MultiVersus, if you use Gleamium it will cost you over 10 dollars. That's over 200 dollars to have the full roster of characters, that number is only going to go up as they add more characters because "LiVe SeRvIce!".   Let's say you don't want to spend over 200 dollars, lets say you buckle down, play the game it's self and work hard and grind unlocking the full roster. Not only do they make it hard for you to earn the Fighter Currency so they can have that "High Player Count" they do it to eventually make you cave and purchase a character with that "Premium Currency" once or twice. So that no matter what they win and you THINK you win.  The game it's self plays horribly it's a clunky mess and the fighting it's self is lame, if you're used to Smash Bros or just any good platform fighter you know that if you stand still and hit the attack button 3 times you will attack 3 times and so get to do a three hit combo. This game wanted to be different. Standing still and attacking will have you do a charge attack (the equivalent of a smash/C stick attack) and feels weird, if you wanna to that 3 hit combo you have to walk forward and attack 3 times. This game is riddled with more strange attack inputs, making the game feel more clunky with it's already floaty physics.This game has so many things that aren't fun or just unnecessary like skills to unlock and "Reindog" if you want a fun and moneys worth platform fighter on steam play Rivals of Aether a game with fantastic movement, controls, 2 fair priced and fun 3rd party DLC characters; Shovel Knight from the game "Shovel Knight and Ori from "Ori and the Blind Forest". In addition it has built in mod support allowing you to play the characters in this game, as well as an infinite number of others from anywhere. Another great platform fighter is Smack Studio, while I feel the game it's self plays a little bit clunky at times (but plays thousands of miles better than MultiVersus) has a built in, easy to use character creator. They even have a playlist of tutorials if you don't know what your doing when creating your character.The Live Service model is terrible and designed solely to benefit the company who made the game. The only way to win is to not play which I have a feeling that not many will play this game for long.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially gave this game a thumbs up, but I cannot recommend it anymore, the honeymoon period is long gone. There is no reason this game should be pushing my RTX 4090 to it's limits, every time I boot the game the fan goes full throttle (this does not happen with theoretically more demanding games).--Season pass, daily quest and end of season ranked reward feel bad, FOMO is an issue like any live service game, it just feels wrong to grind/complete. --Game forces you to play characters or types of characters you don't like to get rewards and XP, and some missions force you to play a certain way in order to complete it. It feels like an unnecessary grind. It's sad, this game has true potential, will come back next year and see if it gets any better, I just hope it can retain the small player base it has.

_childDocuments_.review: My name is Walter Hartwell White. I live at 308 Negra Arroyo Lane, Albuquerque, New Mexico, 87104. This is my confession. If you're watching this tape, I'm probably dead, murdered by my brother-in-law Hank Schrader. Hank has been building a meth empire for over a year now and using me as his chemist. Shortly after my 50th birthday, Hank came to me with a rather, shocking proposition. He asked that I use my chemistry knowledge to cook methamphetamine, which he would then sell using his connections in the drug world. Connections that he made through his career with the DEA. I was... astounded, I... I always thought that Hank was a very moral man and I was... thrown, confused, but I was also particularly vulnerable at the time, something he knew and took advantage of. I was reeling from a cancer diagnosis that was poised to bankrupt my family. Hank took me on a ride along, and showed me just how much money even a small meth operation could make. And I was weak. I didn't want my family to go into financial ruin so I agreed. Every day, I think back at that moment with regret. I quickly realized that I was in way over my head, and Hank had a partner, a man named Gustavo Fring, a businessman. Hank essentially sold me into servitude to this man, and when I tried to quit, Fring threatened my family. I didn't know where to turn.Eventually, Hank and Fring had a falling out. From what I can gather, Hank was always pushing for a greater share of the business, to which Fring flatly refused to give him, and things escalated. Fring was able to arrange, uh I guess I guess you call it a "hit" on my brother-in-law, and failed, but Hank was seriously injured, and I wound up paying his medical bills which amounted to a little over $177,000. Upon recovery, Hank was bent on revenge, working with a man named Hector Salamanca, he plotted to kill Fring, and did so. In fact, the bomb that he used was built by me, and he gave me no option in it. I have often contemplated suicide, but I'm a coward. I wanted to go to the police, but I was frightened. Hank had risen in the ranks to become the head of the Albuquerque DEA, and about that time, to keep me in line, he took my children from me. For 3 months he kept them. My wife, who up until that point, had no idea of my criminal activities, was horrified to learn what I had done, why Hank had taken our children. We were scared. I was in Hell, I hated myself for what I had brought upon my family. Recently, I tried once again to quit, to end this nightmare, and in response, he gave me this. I can't take this anymore. I live in fear every day that Hank will kill me, or worse, hurt my family. I... All I could think to do was to make this video in hope that the world will finally see this man, for what he really is.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great entry into platform fighters if you've never played one before or played one seriously. Overall it's pretty fun, relatively easy to pick up, and a game you can jump in and play a few games without needing to invest hours in. For example, I'd often play a couple games if I have 15 minutes before going to the gym.One of my favorite things about the game is how faithful the characters are to their source material. The Powerpuff Girls will bring up their crossovers ads with Samurai Jack in the early 2000s, Iron Giant is a pacifist who just inadvertently hits you while he eats metal and plays with cars all game. And Nubia's animations straight up look like poses you'd find in a panel of a Wonder Woman comic.This game isn't without it's flaws. Personally I find the UI very cluttered and the in-game shop in particular has way too many things going on. There's also frequent events which is nice, but the events often have their own currency or sometimes multiple currencies in the shop. This is to allow flexibility to choose what cosmetics players want to get, but I could see it being very confusing for new players to understand what all the currencies are for, how to get them, and what to do with them.Also in terms of balancing, it's far from perfect and the devs are generally taking things in the right direction, but there's a lot of stumbling and questionable decisions on the way.Overall, I highly recommend Multiversus. I know the devs are really passionate about making their game the best it can be, and they're pretty open to feedback. It's also free and a relatively light install, so if you're thinking about it, give it a shot.One additional note: If you're new to platform fighters I'd definitely recommend looking up guides as there are a lot of mechanics not covered in the game's tutorial as well as new mechanics slowly being added. Multiversus' Youtube channel has guides on how to play some of their newer characters, and Nakat has great videos on what to think about as you're playing a game.

_childDocuments_.review: edit: the progression and difficulty scaling on the pve content is horrendous. with the worst mobile game monetization and the worst mobile game difficulty scaling, i cant give thumbs up, even if the core game play is fun.The monetization model is one of the most atrociously designed things i have got to experience. There are problems with it that should be obvious to anyone who understands either their game or the ftp landscape. The game wants you to spend 10€ per fighter as a baseline price. bad enough but it could work. what is worse, the game doesnt provide any incentive to get invested in the economy to get people to consider spending 10 bucks. Here are some problems the game creates for itself:- problem 1: you cant play a character you like, when youre trying the game out. basically every ftp game in the last 10 years offers a 5€ bundle thats like 3-5x the value of what 5€ would buy you usually. the game should sell at least 1 and 2/3 of a hero for 5€ once. i would expect a lot of people quit at this point already, trying to check out the game but no chance to pick a hero you like. this is to get people invested in your game in the first place.- problem 2: lets say youre invested. theres no cheap way to build a hero roster for you to have some variety for your play. 2 starter + 3 rotation is not enough. you should get at least 1/3 of the roster, better more, for a single cheap price. when lol was in beta you could buy all champions for like 30 bucks, when hots came out you could buy a class bundle with 20 champs for, i guess also 30 bucks. character based games usually offer you a one time way to build a pool of options. this is to get the invested people to stay. people need a reason to play without feeling fleeced, then you can upsell them to skins or whatever.- problem 3: you can unlock skins only for money, while also having your PvE events and quests require skins for characters (or even certain characters). this is so bad. you get to choose only one of these things for obvious reasons of how its going to be perceived.- problem 4: if you offer a free character make it sensible to attain this character. currently you can grind to unlock agent smith. the character will be priced at 10 bucks, so i bet the average unlock time calculated is gonna be around 20h because they dont think your time is worth more than 50c. people seem to agree that it is not onl too time consuming but also too too hard to unlock that guy. so. if you make an unlock track for a free guy, people will engage with it. if you make that unlock track disrespectfully hard to obtain, players will not be happy as to how _childDocuments_.review: I have been addicted to this game ever since the open beta came out.And now that the full game is released I will give you my review and tell you whether or not i reccomend this game.No, I don't think you should play this game. I love it to death, but its in the worst state ever, and it will take a ♥♥♥♥ ton of effort from WB and PFG to get this game back to an atleast playable state.Right now as it currently stands there are three main un-ignorable issues with the game aside from game balance and gameplay.1. Online only.2. Free to play, grind to win.3. you don't own anything you pay for in this game.In order to play the game (even the single player rifts or the local mode) you *must* connect to the multiversus servers. Not only does this cause issues with in person tournaments or just wanting to play the game with friends at a buddy's house, but this has one bigger overwhelming issue: what happens if the game dies completely. If the game dies completely, thats that, you will not be able to play the game ever again, ever.Whilst this game is free to play, with each new character that gets released they get stronger and stronger with the last character released at the time of writing (8/25/24) being beetlejuice. Right now BeetleJuice has an infinite combo with one of his signature perks, pretty much allowing him to kill any character off of one successful hit. But the only way to get the character for free is by grinding for fighter currency. I don't know how to accurately explain how difficult it is to grind up fighter currency for newly released characters, but ask anyone who plays this game and they will tell you that it is a very long, unfun, painful experience. And whilst I award WB for atleast making it so that you *can* grind to unlock the characters that release so that anyone can pick the free win character of the week, it might as well be pay to win with how painful it actually is.There have been two seperate occassions where a character has been straight up removed from the game. Mind you, not disabled for online play, not only available in "offline" modes, not disabled for challenges and ranked, I mean you literally could not play as the characters anywhere at all whatsoever because they were removed from the game entirely. Meaning if your favorite character you've sunken your time and money into gets removed for whatever reason, that means you won't be recieving any form of compensation whatsoever until the character gets added back into the game later, and thats only *if* the character gets added back into the game. Now, whilst the last time this has happened was after the first major patch with Jason and he was readded after a week, whose to say it won't happen again?This game is very fun, and I hate to say it, but until these three issues are explicitly addressed, this game is not worth your money, let alone your time.Update: whilst things have been slowly getting better over time, only the "free to play, grind to win" issue has been addressed so far. So has it gotten better? Yes and no, on one hand the battlepass for the game became much less grindy for many reasons. However, events for the became more grindy, whereas events have missions tied to characters or costumes that if you don't have that you must grind for, meaning you have to grind for the oppurtunity to grind certain events, which is worse.In addition to this: recently I've been inexplicably having issues with matchmaking recently. Either I get a "Matchmaking failed" error whenever i try to find an online match, or when i do get into a match all of my inputs get rolled back constantly. They released a patch and an update that should've fixed this today, and whilst it did improve the issue slightly allowing me a bit more control over my character, it didn't get rid of it outright and I'm still incapable of actually playing the game online right now, after 3 days of not being able to do so.I hate to say it, but things have gotten worse for multiversus, even though I really wish they hadn't.

_childDocuments_.review: it's like the developers have never played a platform fighter before. no effort was put into making the movement feel good, every character is floaty and weightless. attacks are slow and clunky with unsatisfying animations that completely fail to convey the weight of any impact. lack of genre knowledge is on full display in the character designs; instead of interacting with the core gameplay systems, most characters are gimmicky solitaire fighters playing a completely different game from everyone else. the oversimplified combat completely misses the nuance of better platform fighters, but the developers seem to think overloading the game with status effects, moves with cooldowns, autocombos, and many other mechanics that only serve to pollute the screen with even more particle effects makes up for this lack of depth.they did the bare minimum for making a platform fighter, loaded it up with gimmicks and mechanics that don't belong in the genre, and slapped a predatory monetization system on top of it. i know most of you are only here because the game is free, but this is such a poor example of what this genre has to offer. i urge you to instead play something made by a studio that's actually passionate about platform fighters.

_childDocuments_.review: Am I playing a video game or visiting the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ foreign exchange? Before the tutorial is even done, MultiVersus starts throwing its different currencies at you - the gems, the battle points, the diddly-doodlies, and then ♥♥♥♥♥ right off, not even bothering to teach you the controls properly. Mobile gaming and its consequences have been a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ disaster for the human race. MultiVersus is ostensibly a Smash clone making use of WB's many phagocytosed IPs, but in reality it's a front to sell you imaginary ♥♥♥♥ you don't need as hard as possible.This game is so utterly banal, so sterile, so bereft of personality, so devoid of character, that it sparks no joy at all. The monkey's paw curled, and I realized a huge crossover between all these characters was better left as a pipe dream. Any smidgen of a stimulus has been carefully scrubbed out, with the art style sitting cozily between corporate training video and GrubHub ad, while the music never dares to edge near the foreground. It took me a while to realize that they actually were using musical motifs appropriate to the stages and characters, just that the soundtrack was arranged to be as same-y and unexciting as possible lest the customer switch out of 'buy' mode.As for the gameplay... it's functional. There really isn't a lot to do, and the game feels very slow, and you spend more time looking at rewards screens screaming 'CLAIM CLAIM CLAIM CLAIM' than you do actually playing. Almost none of the characters are unlocked by default, to force you to either grind for or buy them - it actually kind of shows how diluted Superman's brand has become that he's unlocked by default in a game this greedy. Guess we should accept Batman is the DC mascot now?This is one of the most cynicism-inducing experiences I've ever had with a video game, and the second-fastest I've abandoned one. It's joever. _childDocuments_.review: I write this review as a result of the recent influence of my cohort Ricky. Multiversus is an online multiplayer video game which has cross-play and co-op, finding itself in the crossover fighting game genre. Multiversus has unique and intriguing graphics, an unrivalled roster of characters to chose from, and finally, spectacular gameplay. The artistic choices and liberties taken by Multiversus are nothing short of outstanding. I can't help but feel immersed within the game due to the high attention to detail, and the simplistic yet defined art style. I find it difficult to explain to someone unfamiliar with the game, that a charterer like Shaggy, and an action hero like batman can seem as though they were conceptualised within the same world. However Warner-Brothers have managed to make it a reality with their breathtaking work for the graphic design of this game.What sets this game apart from other games of similar nature, is their absolutely stunning character roster. Never in my most wildest dreams would I believe in a day where I could be playing Tom & Jerry as well as Wonder women in the same game. Even with that being said, I find myself infatuated with some of the original characters made for this game, specifically Reindog; A cute and fluffy dog, with consistent damage output, a unique move that can save allies, and a very satisfying spike attack. The movement and fighting mechanics are surprisingly intuitive, even for people not well versed with crossover fighting games. I was overjoyed with dismay when partaking in playing Multiversus, as I had strong expectations for it to be similar with its well known counterpart SSBU (Super Smash Bro's Ultimate). As with many online multiplayer games, it can be a daunting task to constantly win against your opponents on the first attempt. However Multiversus has come up with a ingenious solution to combat said issue, by implementing a rematch button.          I personally was drawn by the unique graphics, and the electrifying character selection. However stayed for the astounding game-play. Overall, I'm pleased with how Warner-Brothers demonstrated their prowess withing the video game industry, and I as well as many others are ecstatic thinking about what the Warner-Brothers come up with next!

_childDocuments_.review: Surprise of 2022 for me. Great cast and extremely solid combat. Smash Bros inspired without being a carbon copy. Easy to pick up new fighters and I get to fuel that nostalgia with my favorite WB characters. The F2P aspects actually aren't bad outside of some ridiculously priced skins (Batman Animated Series for $20?) and some ringout animations. Luckily, the grind for new characters isn't bad at all. It will of course be a real grind to get everyone, but almost every character is viable. (Tip: You can try out ANY character or skin in The Lab against bots to try out before purchasing them).My advice: If you find yourself loving the game after a couple sessions, grab the $40 Founders Pack which gives you 15 character tokens. 1 token = 1 character. Unlock the characters who cost the most gold to acquire and grind the cheaper characters you aren't so sure about to save those tokens up for future characters (Arya costs 3,000 gold to grind for while someone like Shaggy or LeBron is only 2,000). If you want to go the F2P route, group up with a friend for 30% XP bonuses and get your daily missions done. The dailies aren't difficult, and you get one free re-roll if you don't want to run a particular mission. If you are looking for an incredible attacker, pick up Shaggy ASAP. If you want someone who can do everything, pick up Velma. I believe both are only 2,000 gold and are viable at any level of play.Overall, the game is extremely fun. It's even more entertaining with a friend. The barrier of entry is free, so pick it up and tell your friends. You'll have a blast whether you get the Founder's Pack or not. By the time you hit mastery on one character, chances are you are ready or close to having enough gold to buy another for free.9/10. Could be a 10/10 if future characters are great and if they lower some of the MTX prices. Not all are bad, but some are pretty horrendous.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Pay Us First Games!A free to play title that is incredibly fun to play but the team came out swinging with the monetization. As a beta player who gave into the hype, got the $100 founders pack I can't be more disappointed where we ended. The game releases with less features and more scummy monetization.Pros:- The game play is fun, they rebuilt the game in UE5 and made positive changes to the way dodging works.- ^ That one. That's all.Cons:- The game play, although fun is a good bit slower. Not a big con, but a change I'm not sure many of us expected.- The monetization. They did away with the single currency they had and added 3 different ones just so they can make you feel like they're giving you things more often. Gold has turned into "Fighter Currency, Perk Currency, PvE Gems"If you're playing PvE and want to skip ahead, buy gem EXP! Or if you're on the hard mode and use all your lives, refill your lives for $10! (They've come out to say that "This is a bug" after a massive amount of backlash)- The game will give you dailies for characters you don't have, so you either buy them with the limited fighter currency / real money or just don't get to do those dailies (took away the "reroll" feature for dailies)- No longer able to play all characters in offline mode, farther locking things behind a paywall.- No more stat screens after each match to let you know how well or poor you did.- A year in the oven and still no ranked play since it went offline- Players missing rewards they bought with gold / earned in the beta getting no support or answers.I'm sure I could come up with more but most of you probably haven't even read this far in. If you just want a fun free-to-play game where you can jump in and beat people up, go ahead and hop in. But if care about companies coming up with some of the most predatory monetization practices and forcing out unfinished games with missing features, I'd skip on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: In mid 2022 Player First Games teamed up with Warner Bros. Games to release an open beta of a platform fighter similar to Super Smash Bros. Called, MultiVerse, Warner Bros. packed their game with characters from Adventure Time, Rick and Morty, DC Comics, Looney Toons, Scooby-Doo, and other lesser properties.I played with my two sons and we discovered a few features. This game makes combat more complicated. The mechanic, Attack Decay, makes each attack of the same type, inflict less damage and distance than the last. The player is forced to perform combos to win. Secondly, it seemed to be difficult to knock people off the map.The beta has ended, with a full release planned for 2024. We stopped playing long before the beta ended. Neither myself nor my children found it fun compared to the classic formula of Super Smash Bros.

_childDocuments_.review: You want to have fun with your (childhood) heroes? Want to escape the daily grind of (Home)work and commitments? Make a commitment with our season pass, WORK and GRIND for EVERY Character. And dare you take a day off.  You might not finish the SPECIAL, EPIC, SUPER, MEGA, event in time. Let's embrace FOMO together in "MULTIVERSUS" !!! An adults nightmare of a childhood dream coming true. Okay, but seriously:all the lightness I associate with the characters and IPs in this game is unfortunately ruined by the "Game as a Service"/"Free to Play" cash grab grind. This could have been such a well rounded game. I would have been happy to spend another €50+ on top of the €100 Beta Premium Edition to simply get a finished game WITHOUT an in-game store, three different currencies, daily challenges, stupid events and all that crap. I'm getting sick when I see this games menu with its questionable cash grab content.I bought the Premium Edition back then because I hoped that the developers or the publisher would go a different way this time if they got enough support. I could also have lived with payed DLC characters.I played the Beta back then and allready disliked the system. Last month I reinstalled the game to try the release version of the game. I played for another 1 hour, clicked through this mess of a menu with its store, challenges and events and uninstalled it afterwards. The gameplay, the music and the design of the characters are really well done and a joy to play. When the game was announced and I saw the first pictures, I could already imagine playing a round with my favorite Warner Bros. characters on a Saturday morning without thinking about money, tasks and obligations. Or just playing with friends on the couch in the evening. Basically just escaping the daily grind, which is already full enough with money, chores and obligations. Just like these IPs did in my childhood/teenage years. Combining these IP's with such a monitization system is a paradox that, for all my love, I don't understand and really makes me sick. My guess would be that the Inventors of Bugs Bunny, Batman and Wonder Woman would also find this concept appalling. The "Game as a Service" model took all the fun out of the selling Point of this game for me and I'm ashamed to have bought the €100 premium version. I don't think I'll ever play this game with my friends on the couch because I'm embarrassed to have spent money on this paradox of a Childhood Cashgrab game.R.I.P. Multiversus.

_childDocuments_.review: Re-reviewing this now that it's fully out. In terms of the gameplay, I still think it's fun. There aren't many 2v2 online platform fighters that you can play with friends, and they've continued to add exciting new characters with interesting kits. It's also quite easy to create custom lobbies and play 1v1 or 2v2 with friends - I've had a great time doing this and getting an experience that I previously would only have on the rare occasion that we are all physically in the same place and end up playing smash. I also enjoy that the game has progression, in terms of character mastery, account level, and with the events that they've been super consistent with so far. PvP is really fun, and I've found myself enjoying 1v1s more this time around.The new monetization system seems to be the main thing people are complaining about, and honestly I think people are being overly critical. Not allowing players to try character for free in training before purchasing them was undoubtedly a massive mistake, but that feature has been added. This is a platform fighter, not a MOBA. People typically have one or two characters that they main, and the game is 100% free to play. I actually feel that they've been quite generous - if you played in beta at all they give you the first battlepass for free (this means you get Jason for free). The battlepass also rewards enough premium currency to buy the next battlepass, do those who play a lot - or just do daily/weekly missions - could have every battlepass in the game's lifetime without paying. They also gave out the Banana Guard character for free to anyone who logged in twice. The skin prices are quite scummy, but at the end of the day, as a free to play game the elements that effect the actual gameplay - not cosmetics - are extremely fair IMO as they need to make money off this somehow.They added a PvE mode this time around, it's really mid. The easy difficulties are way too easy, and the hard difficulties aren't hard because the enemy AI is better, they're hard because the enemy AI takes no damage, but does a ton of damage, and any friendly AI is useless. I also don't like that certainly PvE missions require you to play specific characters, as it locks people who don't have said characters out of what should be the game's most accessible mode. My main criticisms are that some attack hitboxes need to be a little more in-line with the animation and my girl Velma needs a buff because she was gutted down to worst character in the game status (what's the point of a mage with no useful or aimable  ranged attacks?), Overall, this is still a really fun game that's a unique experience on PC, and very easy to pick-up and play for short periods of time as matches and match-making are both extremely quick. They certainly will need to keep it rolling with character releases, balance patches, fun events, and quality of life changes if they want to succeed, but what's here is good and promising.

_childDocuments_.review: As with every Smash clone, ultimately I just end up asking myself: Why am I not just playing Smash Bros. instead?Rollback is nice. Crossplay, having real online is great (even if the UI is an unintuitive mess). Free to play is great for maintaining a high player count. Unfortunately none of those things matter if there's not a solid game underneath it all.Every character feels floaty and slow, not fast and precise. Attacks have long windups and unsatisfying impacts, compounded by characters being so convoluted in design that you need to lab everything in the game before you can understand what's happening in a match. Everything looks plastic, the soundtrack all this bland, generic, sterile, corporate superhero orchestra, and the roster is such a mishmash of everything that it's hard to see this game forming a real community. Smash fans all have the fact that they play video games in common. What do MultiVersus players have? Their shared love of Warner Bros. Incorporated?If MV is to be a solid game, it needs to be tight and intuitive. Unfortunately I can use neither of these words to describe this game, and I don't see this changing by release. In all likelihood, MultiVersus will only ever be the strictly inferior knockoff version of Smash for kids who can't afford the real thing.

_childDocuments_.review: Multiversus is the first platform fighter that, in my opinion, has really come into it's own and does not just feel like another Smash clone. In fact, I do not think Multiversus can be called a Smash clone at all.While Nickelodeon opted to bring back the nostalgia and competitive scene of games like Melee, WB opted to go their own route and make a unique game with gameplay not based on nostalgia, but rather prioritize teamwork and 2v2 gameplay instead.Whether or not you liked the gameplay of the Nickelodeon themed brawler that came out last year, the reason Nickelodeon All-Star Brawl failed was their lack of a reason to play the game. Multiversus decided to add a battle pass system with daily missions as well as an ingame currency (Gold) you can use to unlock characters, which I think is great! I have a couple of criticisms with this system however, mostly being that once you do your dailies, battle pass EXP is slowed to a snail's pace and you practically cannot progress until the next day. This discourages grinding. My other gripe is that Gold gain is simply too slow and there is no way to speed it up; Not even through spending money. The only ways to get gold right now are: Battle pass, which is limited, Leveling a character up to 5, which is limited, leveling up, and playing matches. The latter two, of course, provide the least amount of Gold, and therefore are the only repeatable ones. This means grinding to unlock a character with a full battle pass will take you a long time. I have resorted to saving my Gold and only using it to unlock the free characters I have already gotten good at once they leave the rotation, which discourages experimentation. Oh right, did I mention that the characters are on a rotation?You start with one character; Wonder Woman (assuming you completed the tutorial), as well as four other characters that rotate out every week or so. The characters seem to be random, and do not include the three "Expert" characters currently in the game. While I think this is a good system, characters right now simply take too long to unlock (I have 19 hours in this game and a completed battle pass and I have about 4 additional characters unlocked permanently), and certain simple characters are now locked behind a rather large time sink. I think that there should be one additional free character, in addition to Shaggy being the free character acquired from the tutorial instead of Wonder Woman, seeing as he is the most basic character in the game.This sounds like a lot of whining and complaining, but the good thing is that these are not criticisms to the gameplay itself, but rather the battle pass and unlockables system. The actual gameplay is very nice!Every character has some kind of weird or crazy gimmick except for maybe Superman. If you're interested in learning more about the gameplay, watch a gameplay video or two! Or... just install the game and try it out, because I do recommend this game! I think the battle pass and unlockables system could use an overhaul, and try not to get persuaded by the ludicrously expensive cosmetics. (Some KO animations cost like, $15 USD. Why?)If anyone at WB is reading this, I love your game! I hope it thrives for a long time to come. But please make sure we get enough Gleamium from the premium battle pass to actually earn it back by the end. If you do, you'll have a happy customer.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit 3/14/24: YEEEAAAAYYYAAHHH!!! Original review is as follows with a couple, minor edits.Now, I know the question on everyone's mind. Can Smash Ultimate be the platform fighter to take down MultiVersus. I know, crazy. MultiVersus has rollback netcode that works with up to 4 players on screen at once. Along with it's dynamic cast and the ability to play the game without spending a dime. And while Smash Ultimate has online netplay that would feel criminal to charge anyone with a wired connection, it does have a dev team and cast built up over 5 different iterations of characters and experience, along with the power of Nintendo's influence to draw multiple fanbases towards it's franchise.All jokes aside, I wasn't sure how much I was going to be into MultiVersus when it first came out. I wanted to be able to play a platform fighter like the Smash Bros series again, but most attention on that genre has been largely aimed at Nintendo and to this day I'm still hearing about different titles that have been largely ignored. I might recommend the "platform fighter" tag be used more ubiquitously on Steam as it feels like a dis-service to the efforts of devs in general.MultiVersus is centered largely around the 2v2 format, which is a format I'm fond of. It's reminiscent of free-for-alls with friends and family, and does center more around spacing and a neutral game rather than exclusively combos, rushdown, and masher oriented styles. The game is floaty, probably more in line with a Smash Bros Brawl, but also has movement that is quite fast. This leads to a lot of interactions that can happen on all areas of the screen. High edge-guards, low recoveries, juggling, flanking, and all forms of shenanigans can occur. 1v1s tend to be less of that dynamic or the focus as a whole, but there does seem to be a lot of players gravitating towards that.The game does still cater well to casual players (which seems like a dirty word in any fighting game). But with how matchmaking works and how much new players may get absolutely destroyed by a team of tournament players, it can probably feel pretty rough for anyone's first time playing. There are other modes to play, even if it's just practice against bots or the newly introduced Arcade Mode, but they can be handy for learning new characters and probably a better place to start rather than immediately wanting to jump into matchmaking. I'm far from a top player and not into competitive gaming that much. But I also like trying new things in games like this, leading to me laughing at how stupid I am. But not being afraid to try new things can lead to some spectacular things in MultiVersus.The game has seen quite a few changes between new characters, balance patches, an entire hitbox and hurtbox rework, and various other tweaks. A lot of the style of the game early on seemed to lean towards a projectile heavy meta. At least at top level. This wasn't really something I noticed at whatever level I'm at. Mid-level? My Gizmo is top 1000 in 2v2s but I have no idea what that means besides a lower case w for me. Projectile and zoner characters have been nerfed a bit, and I still can't speak to that at top level. Personally I've never been a huge fan of that rushdown, combo oriented style, where you just approach while spamming your safest attack. But if that is your concern as well, there have been approaches to neutralize a more masher heavy style, adding more end lag to moves that whiff in order to make players space and calculate their approach. I have a few gripes with some characters and the direction of the game, but I'd probably be lying to myself if everything I wanted was unequivocally the best way for the game to go. In it's current state, I still feel the devs are taking all these things into account. I still don't like Batman or Shaggy and I feel bad for Tom & Jerry and Iron Giant (my two who haven't gotten through Hard Mode Arcade), but pretty sure that that's mostly a me thing.Comparing this game to Nick All-Stars, the netcode when I first played both games felt similar (I can say the netcode of MultiVersus has improved for myself). Hits have better feedback in MultiVersus, and the characters stand out better from things like the background (having outline features is very helpful). Compared to Brawlhalla, the characters are far more dynamic and unique. This isn't a knock on Brawlhalla as I totally understand the design, but I do enjoy the personality of games like MultiVersus. The movement of MultiVersus both feels floatier but also faster. I want to say the netcode for both games is on par, but your region and internet may affect that experience.Comparing to Smash Ultimate, the only thing I can really say is MultiVersus let's me play the game where as Ultimate is more worried about how shiny it is. Even when I was trying to get into Ultimate at the time, I kept trying to give myself things to do with it in order to get a grasp on it. Challenge runs, controller testing, Youtube and Twitch content (not trying to plug, it's just what I did), and even modding to help me understand the game better. But the more I dug into it, the less it felt like any of it was designed for me as a player. MultiVersus has just been fun. I haven't felt the need to save all my clips, which I kinda regret (Marvin shenanigans, amiright?). I didn't feel I needed to upload a bunch of stuff onto Youtube. I didn't feel the need to constantly do Ironmans or practice tech in training. I just enjoyed playing the game. I've been slowly working in spacing and neutral into my style again, where as Smash online felt like it was giving me brain damage to even attempt. By the time I was starting MultiVersus, I felt like I had to work out all my mashing habits that were ingrained into my muscle memory.Actually playing a platform fighter again with real people has been fun. Sure there's been some off days and bad matches and sometimes just way too much salt. But a lot of the worst days of MultiVersus are more comparable to the better days of Smash quickplay, and there hasn't been a lot of either.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely worth checking out!Personally I like the combat in this more than the latest Smash Bro games. The movement in MultiVersus feels more fluid to me. I didn't like Smash Brawl or Ultimate because the movement felt a bit more stiff than in previous games, like if you move a direction you're more committed to it, where in this it lets you turn and punch a bit faster. The characters are not that hard to unlock, it's like Apex where it's free to login and you get points to unlock the characters, which it's faster to unlock everything than Apex. The characters are awesome and I have a feeling they're gonna add a lot. I have a small fear they might add some ridiculous characters that almost don't make sense like a T-Rex or something from Jurassic Park. But that's kind of the name of the game.One of the only cons I have so far is that the menu's and vibe seem to be aimed at a younger audience yet if you mark your age under 18 you are blocked from online play. Given there's no text chat in the game they could probably lower that restriction to 13 like most other games. I'm not under 18 so it's not a problem for me but a lot of young folks are gonna have to learn how to show hidden files in Windows to access the .sav file in AppData to reset their age.The graphics aren't amazing, it's mainly just 2D animations, but the colors are nice and the animations are smooth. They suit the game play enough for it not to be bothersome.Overall I think this game has the potential to be one of the most popular games over the next few years

_childDocuments_.review: A game with a lot of love put into the original idea. Character animations are full of references and clever design, the skins are all faithful references, the maps each have their own playstyle that fits the theme of the IP, and the voice lines are all done by a lot of the original cast. Although the game is quite unbalanced, with certain characters or combos being awful to go against, that’s not the biggest issue.The biggest issue is the release. The devs decided to go as money hungry as possible with micro transactions for almost everything. Characters cost $10 each, one character will be locked behind every battle pass, earn-able account cosmetics were put into the shop, you can pay for lives and “gems” in singleplayer mode, and you get a seperate currency, “prestige,” which you can only obtain by purchasing things from the shop or buying the battle pass. This game is fun at its core, but since release the devs have removed every reason to keep players interest in place of micro transactions and battle passes.

_childDocuments_.review: LeBron Raymone James (/ləˈbrɒn/; born December 30, 1984) is an American professional basketball player for the Los Angeles Lakers of the National Basketball Association (NBA). Nicknamed "King James", he is widely considered one of the greatest players in NBA history and is often compared to Michael Jordan in debates over the greatest basketball player ever. James has won four NBA championships, four NBA MVP awards, four NBA Finals MVP awards, three All-Star MVP awards, and two Olympic gold medals. James has scored the most points in the playoffs, the second most career points, and has the seventh most career assists. He has been selected an NBA All-Star 18 times, to the All-NBA Team a record 17 times, and to the NBA All-Defensive First Team five times. He has competed in ten NBA Finals, the third most all time, including eight consecutively between 2011 and 2018. In 2021, James was selected to the NBA 75th Anniversary Team.James played basketball for St. Vincent–St. Mary High School in his hometown of Akron, Ohio, and was heavily touted by the national media as a future NBA superstar. A prep-to-pro, he was selected by the Cleveland Cavaliers with the first overall pick in the 2003 NBA draft. Named the 2004 NBA Rookie of the Year, he soon established himself as one of the league's premier players, winning the NBA MVP award in 2009 and 2010. After failing to win a championship with Cleveland, James left in 2010 as a free agent to join the Miami Heat; this was announced in the television special The Decision and is among the most controversial free-agent decisions in sports history.James won his first two NBA championships while playing for the Heat in 2012 and 2013; in both of these years, he also earned the league's MVP and Finals MVP awards. After his fourth season with the Heat in 2014, James opted out of his contract to re-sign with the Cavaliers. In 2016, he led the Cavaliers to victory over the Golden State Warriors in the Finals by coming back from a 3–1 deficit, delivering the team's first championship and ending the Cleveland sports curse. In 2018, James exercised his contract option to leave the Cavaliers and signed with the Lakers, where he won the 2020 NBA championship and his fourth Finals MVP. James is also the first player in NBA history to accumulate $1 billion in earnings as an active player.Off the court, James has accumulated more wealth and fame from numerous endorsement contracts. He has featured in books, documentaries (including winning two Sports Emmy Awards as an executive producer), and television commercials. He has won 19 ESPY Awards, hosted Saturday Night Live, and starred in the sports film Space Jam: A New Legacy (2021). James has been a part-owner of Liverpool F.C. since 2011 and leads the LeBron James Family Foundation, which has opened an elementary school, housing complex, retail plaza, and community center in Akron.

_childDocuments_.review: I love platform fighter and the unique direction each game pulls it into and I think Multiversus is like two steps forward and one step back. First off I love the amount of care that went into not only the character's moveset such as Shaggy's d-air being his running animation but with what you can change in the settings like the input buffering and finally the scoreboard placement which that is a huge step up that Rivals of Aether doesn't even allow. Now for something that I thought would be a standard for all games and question I should never ask myself; why does this game not let you pause in the middle of a match against BOTS? Why are matches against BOTS server side? Rivals of Aether and Smash Ultimate never have this problem because these games are developed with offline play in mind, I understand yes this is an open beta and I hope this is just a beta thing but why can't bot's be handled client-side you don't even have to make the game fully offline to do that. Also that battle pass system, I personally hate battle pass-like systems because why should I grind 50 levels in order to get one thing I really want out of that entire battle pass when you can just set it to an achievement like "Beat Classic Mode on max difficulty with Shaggy" to get a cool skin, that feels more intuitive and rewarding to earn than getting your ass kicked over and over until I just so happen to earn it.This leads into something I hope they really put into the full release of the game; Classic/Arcade mode, Adventure/Story mode, and an All-Star Mode, the inclusion of these modes are in my opinion dictates whether this game will survive or flop if you can't find a better alternative, please add some type of Single/Couch-Co-op player modes that will at least increase the game's longevity, because in terms of content Super Smash Bros. 64 has more replayability than the online mode, yeah sure you have more characters than the unmoded version of Smash 64 with more unlockables but, do you even have a Classic/Arcade mode? With at least 5 difficulty options and a congratulations screen that also lets you unlock the character if you beat it in a match?I'm recommending this because it's free and having soo much potential but comparing the current build to Smash Ultimate and Rivals of Aether this game has a lot of catching up to do, but I'd like to think there's another build of the game that's not accessible to us that has some work in progress modes. _childDocuments_.review: This is a good attempt at a smash like game, but like all of the others it comes with baggage. My #1 reason for not recommending the game is the monetization practices. The gameplay is also a bit janky, but overall I'd say I'm still having fun with the game nonetheless. ❌ - It is absolutely awful. You want that batman skin with a brighter yellow belt and chest logo? That will cost you 2000 gleamium. That's about $20 for a skin, and it's barely different than the normal one. Not all skins cost this much, but in most cases, the USD equivalent price you are paying for things makes no sense at all. When you buy the $40 standard edition of the game, you get a whopping 300 gleamium to spend. Don't blow it all in one place! For characters you can buy them with gold earned in game, but gold accrual is terribly slow. You get about 2k gold from one-time starter missions, after that I've earned about 2k additional gold in the 8.5 hours I've played, some of that was from bonuses I won't be able to get again (ie. character level bonuses) Since characters cost 1.5k-3k, it would take you a good while to unlock a whole lot through gameplay alone. ❌ - Perks are neat, but it messes up balance especially when you are starting out with a character. It would be nice if you could turn them off or if you had a serviceable starter set to use.  ❌  - They are no where near as refined as they are in smash. Sometimes it feels like you are fighting under water or in a dream depending on the characters or moves you use. Big sweeping hits often go right through other characters making it difficult to discern when or where hits will connect.  ❌ - There are limited defensive options. You can dodge in place or directionally dodge, but there is no block or grab. If someone is attacking you, you can either try to hit them first or dodge and hit, those are your options. There's no way to try catching yourself when you hit the ground or walls after an attack and there's no ledge grabbing. ❌  - Sometimes you forward attack to do a combo hit, sometimes it's neutral attack. Some characters' neutral aerial is quick and light, other times it's heavy and you want to use a forward aerial for a light attack. It seems pretty all over the place, so you really have to pay attention when learning characters. Smash does a great job at having a ton of move variety, while still following some familiar core patterns to ground you when switching characters.❌  - Don't allow extra people to wait in a queue (spectating would be nice) so if you want to play with more than 4 people, you just have to orchestrate a rotation manually leaving and joining the lobby. There's also no stock option for the FFA mode, which is odd because it's an option for 2v2.❌  - It's 100% fighting in one of three modes (1v1, 2v2, 4p FFA). You can use bots, so there is that.✅  - Love the 2v2 focused mechanics. I always liked team battles and think it's a fun way to play. It does make it tough I think for some of the support characters to be viable for 1v1, but time will tell for that.✅  The game looks great and has some fun characters, stages, voices, and music.✅  - Character perks can only be unlocked through game progression at the same rate no matter how much gleamium you have.✅  - All players can choose whether to rematch for a best of 3. All players can change characters after rematching (time to pull out your best!) You can give toast to other players which gives them 20 gold. Taunts are all pretty friendly (except superman, he's a real jerk) Cross play seems to be working as far as I can tell. I have seen a fair number of disconnection issues even in our custom lobbies, but it's quick to get back up and going. Hopefully they will clean that up.

_childDocuments_.review: Cool concept. More like Smash Bros 64, but unfortunately, its 2022. Building a "team-smash bros" is a cool concept with characters/weakness, but introduces a fundamental problem, other people are looking out for themselves, and you are unable to change your choice or leave after you sign up.Unless you start in teams WITH another player, throwing you into a random match with another random player is straight up a gamble on whether your characters will mesh right, and makes the self-sufficient characters shine better than they should be. This also doesn't help Player First Games save face from a flawed fundamental character design choice. They developed a game that HIGHLIGHTS specific characters that have weakness built into them with the excuse of them be more specialized. These characters will either get buffed into outer space, or fall into player oblivion with 1-2% pick rates.This is ESPECIALLY highlighted in 1v1. You can't build a game that is attempting to be competitive like this by "baking in" deficiencies and weaknesses from a character design point with the thought process of a teammate to shore them up for you, AND then make general "Good" character with NO weaknesses, that just do everything "Okay." The "Okay" characters will become "Great" because they aren't bad at ANYTHING. Either every character must have some kind of weakness, or make every character stand-up on their own.Each comes with it's own balancing issues, but Player First Games signed up for one hell of an active updating scheduling by designing like this. Unless they clean it up quickly, this game won't survive long, because eventually it all just boil down to "Fox/Falco" on "Final Destination."Except it'll be Bugs/Tom/Shaggy/Harley on Sky Platform.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game as much as I do enjoy it sometimes. I want to go over everything I like about the game first. Every character is made very well. They're fun, have unique gimmicks, and overall are the best part of this game by far. They're expertly crafted and make these iconic characters really come to life. This is the one thing this game does right. Characters are handled very well, have interactions, skins, and more. Play this game if you're interested in any of that. Now for all the bad parts.Balancing is a massive issue. Some characters are a pain in the ass to fight and I feel as if they do not get nerfed often. And on the same side of that, the characters who need buffs don't really get them. Jason is one of my favorite characters. He is a heavyweight with slow moves. Now, imagine Bowser in Smash Ultimate to compare. A lot of his attacks have priority or super armor. Even in this game Superman has this. Jason has none. All of his slow attacks can be interrupted. Second biggest hitbox in the game and he has no way of getting people off of him. The only thing he can use is his neutral special in order to get superarmor, although that has a cooldown and can only be done on the ground. I love the idea behind this, but Jason really cannot use any of his moves reliably without this. I have seen infinite combos on him, unwinnable scenarios set up by other characters, and honestly I am amazed that they seem to be avoiding him like the plague with the patches. Second massive issue: Grinding. I can't tell if this is personal or not but it feels cheap. Grinding for characters takes weeks to do, but that's not the part i'm upset about. The part I hate is that, aside from money, there is no consistent way to get characters. Missions have been slowly fixing this, so this may be a non issue by now, but there are so many ways to get Fighter Currency and none of them give you very much. On top of that, this game has 3 different currencies for you to buy things with. The most common one being Perk Currency. You will get more perk currency than you will ever use, as it pads you out for a real reward. I understand padding is needed but this is loony. You can play the game for a while and not make any real progress towards getting a new character. Its maddening The final major issue I have is that... there's nothing to do. With the few characters you get to actually play, lack of modes or a GOOD PvE, the game feels empty. The gameplay loop goes as such1: Boot up game2: Play Match3: Rematch or not4: Inevitably end up facing someone who plays this game for 8 hours a day since there STILL isn't any ranked mode5: Close game I could forgive this if they didn't have a year to do this. What were they working on for that long? I keep telling myself that the game is gonna get better, and I do genuinely enjoy the game at some points, but its painful. Boot up, play 2 matches, realize there's nothing to do and I don't get any enjoyment out of the characters I have right now, and get off. I want to change this review to positive in the future. _childDocuments_.review: As far as platform fighters go, it's one of the best. The developers are very attentive to the community, some could argue too much so. The balancing is a work in progress for sure but they aren't blind to it.Pros:- Very active devs who respond to the community- Great attention to detail and respect for licensed characters- Combat mechanics, graphics, etc.- It's really fun for those who like fighters- Very competitive- It's a fighting game where you grow and feel yourself get better- Focused around 2v2 so great to play with a friend- Lots of less competitive modes for those that don't want to stress- Great accessibility, allowing you to change things like input buffer frames- Cross progressionCons:- New players can have a hard time with the matchmaking- Some characters have wonky hit boxes- Some characters are still being balanced- The community gets unconventional characters nerfed to the ground (big sad for IG and Superman)

In super smash brothers you had a chance against pro players because the characters were perfectly balanced. Here, if someone master's a character you will become their punching bag. End of story.Maybe I'm just a noob, but the other HUGE problem which is probably causing the downfall of the game are the currencies and the leveling up system. 3 different currencies (what ?) and a lot of LOT OF grinding. I get it. I'ts a free game, you want players to pay some real cash in the shop...but THIS IS NOT FUN. Even if you win in the game you get a few points and you need thousands to unlock a character. Which means hundreds of matches and days of grinding to get a single fighter. This could be the next big hit, but the reward system absolutely destroys it. Fix that and I will be back. *Uninstalls the game*
