_childDocuments_.review: I've just completed this game and overall would recommend to casual/core gamers who love platformers. Disclaimer: I was given a review copy to test and create content via keymailer.Its starts off slow and very narrative driven. It seemed to explain a lot and I just wanted to play the game lol. For what was going on, I think things could have been explained quicker in the first hour or so. After the initial story and "how to-play" was over is when the part I love comes into play, the grind. Once I got the controls down and general ambiance of the game, I flew through it. I enjoyed the game and the story. It felt easy at first and then it really went from casual to core gamer difficulty which I loved. I just wish there was more cuz I beat it in 8 hours. I completed all the missions and all there is left is to do is go back and 100% it.Overall I enjoyed this game with the positives out weighing the negatives. If this is on your wish list and a fan of platformers, pull the trigger...right meow!The controls were a little off to me but you can remap them. I grew up a console gamer so having full controller support made me feel right at home with a platformer. The pirate theme was a plus in a cute chibi kinda way. I got Megaman legends vibes with the cute enemies and companions along the way. Its too bad Kao didn't have a gun.

_childDocuments_.review: Koa and the Five Pirates of Mara is a 3D Platform adventure game which will appeal to many gamers out there who are looking for a fun, casual adventure game to pass the time, You control the titular character (joined alongside her friend Napopo) as she travels across in search of items that will help her restore the island from the actions caused by the Five Pirates. This game certainly made me feel nostalgic of the classic platform days of yesteryear. Fans of Mario, Sonic, Donkey Kong Country, etc will find plenty to enjoy from this game.The game has a very colorful, cute art style that will be appealing to all ages. Great soundtrack as well. With platforming being the main aspect of the game, each level has their own unique feel and flair about it that keeps the player engaged throughout. Replayability is quite high as well, since players can go back to previous rounds and try to go for the fastest run time, collect all hidden items found around the level, or unlock other areas around the map for fun mini-games. A wide cast of characters with on-going relationships and back stories fill out through the entirety. I find it quite interesting that this game is third in a series of 'Mara' themed adventures, with the other two games featured with different genres of gameplay. Although, you do not need to have any prior knowledge of previous games to enjoy this one. I am curious to check out the other two games after having thoroughly enjoyed this one & look forward to the expanding 'Mara' universe with future adventures. Highly Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little platformer that doesn't take long to beat. Took me exactly 8 hours to finish my 100% playthrough. It's cute and fun but I have my issues. Maybe because I was constantly comparing it to A Hat in Time and Sonic, but the movement felt a little off. The roll move feels like it should both be it's own button but also should have momentum tied to it. Normally what happens when you roll is you jump, land, then press the run button right after landing to do a roll. And my problem partly comes from that the roll is the only way to break boxes. And feels clunky to jump into a roll just to break a box. Feels a little weird on small platforms. The other problem I have with the roll is that it doesn't matter if you're going up or down hill, doesn't matter how fast you're going, the roll always lasts the same amount of time. And it feels a bit off to be rolling down a hill just to uncurl because you can't continue your roll. It feels like you should be able to just hold the roll button down and keep it going until you either let the button go or lose your speed from keeping the roll on flat ground for a while.TL:DR, Game is great, it's just missing a few things that'd make it perfect for me personally.

_childDocuments_.review: Super reminiscent of Mario Sunshine or A Hat in Time. Koa takes the iconic formula of dive > well-timed-jump from the former two games and twists it into jump > well-timed-roll > jump to get around fast. This change makes it stand out just enough from the others while still having that insanely addicting risk-reward that makes you want to keep restarting a level until you perform your route perfectly.Visually, this is Chibig's best 3D work by far! It's amazing to see how much they've improved since Summer in Mara.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this one. It's a short and sweet 3D platformer that appears to take inspiration from both Super Mario 3D World and Wind Waker. It's great for beginners who are new to platformers or to video games in general. In the earlier levels, it can feel a little simplistic but it gradually picks up in difficulty. The final stage was very hard compared to the rest of the game, but it was no doubt my favorite level. I personally love challenging games with an ability to retry quickly, though it's also good that they offered an easy mode for those who are less experienced.The only real critique I have is the map screen. The fixed camera angle is a little awkward, and it's difficult to see where you are going especially if you're headed south. I feel that either a top-down view or a free rotating camera would have made it much better, but I'm sure it can be addressed in a future patch.If you're looking for a quick and easy platforming experience with a wholesome atmosphere, I highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Koa and the Five Pirates of Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Koa and the Five Pirates of Mara is a third person platformer which appeals to both the speed runners and to the explorers. Story: Basically the pirates have attacked the Island Qälis and pillaged it. Its up to Koa to confront them and restore harmony to the islands of Mara. A straight forward story, and if I know most platformers, they don't need a complex story to encourage them to take the challenge and complete some levels. Gameplay: If you played Hat in time, Crash, Mario, and Wind Waker than everything will seem familiar. You have a jump, dash, ground pound, and roll. There no lives and the only penalty to dying is a worst time score. Each level have 3 medals (Gold, silver, bronze), and you are awarded these by how fast you finish the level. Most levels will have 3 items to collect. These items unlock outfits/backpack for Koa to wear as well as items to restore Qälis. I often found that doing 2 runs was best. First run to explore and get all items. Second run to speed run for a gold medal. The levels are long enough to enjoy but short enough to not drag on. A happy medium.The first 3 Islands worth of levels are nothing too challenging, but I would say its around the 4th island when the difficulty start to climb. Nothing unfair or crazy, but it was around this point that I found out the game had an relaxed mode (it prompted me to switch to it because I kept dying).There are several other levels to break up the pace. The first are races where you compete against 3 other AI players to race to an end of a level. The other are diving levels to reach the bottom for an item.Finally the bosses are unique. None are repeated in terms of how you beat them.Final Thoughts: I would have probably missed Koa and the Five Pirates of Mara if the kickstarter page wasn't advertised to me. I backed it and got to say, it was worth it. Seeing as how it's $17 right now (a sale, usual price is $20 USD), its a nice game to pick up for those platformers.

name: Minabo - A walk through life
detailed_description: Minabo - A walk through life is a social simulation game where you walk the path of life while your turnip grows and thrives (or not) in its social relationships. Life starts when you sprout, time goes by with every step you take, and you can set your pace at any moment. You live and learn: surround yourself with other turnips and interact with them to forge your personality. Your acquired strengths and weaknesses will affect your future interactions. Build your social circle by maintaining and caring for the relationships that matter the most to you, and run away from the ones that don't. You can adopt many radish-pets and spend your life with them, start a family and breed little turnips or live fast and die young. There are thousands of ways to live and none is correct! Just live as you wish! (and assume the consequences of your decisions when you rot). Living and thriving in social relationships is not easy, so Minabo - A walk through life offers collectible hats that produce different effects when worn. Easily falling in love, making everyone hate you, getting an elegance plus or even changing your life expectancy... In Minabo - A walk through life , no two lives are the same and when they end, every one of them will generate a summary that you can share with your friends. What would you change from your past? What would life have been if you weren't rude to that one friend of your childhood? What if you spent more time with your family? Minabo - A walk through life will allow you to discover the answers if you decide to go back in time instead of starting a new life. Main features: 25 quests with dozens of goals to make every life a challenge. Free life mode: Each life and character is randomly generated. No two lives are the same! Explore interpersonal relationships and build your social circle. Realistic relationships counselled by psychologists! Surround yourself with other turnips and radish-pets! Appealing visuals for all audiences, charming characters with hundreds of animations and seasonal backgrounds. Share your life's summary with your friends. Start a new life or change your past. You can restart any life to change whatever you'd like (or at least try)

_childDocuments_.review: Minabo - a walk through life is a life sim that's as visually endearing as it is heart wrenching, and that you won't be forgetting. Raise your little turnip from crawl to casket, attempting to build relationships and take care of yourself along the way. Check out our video review on I Dream of Indie Games here: 💖 Deeply emotional game play mimicking life's progression💖 Cute turnip based art and world, including turnip pets!💖 Introspective messaging on life and growing up💖 A small but great example of games as art☠️ Messy controls when too many turnips on screen☠️ Just one song that's nice, but gets old quick☠️ An incest crown exists - why?!?!?Not everyone will connect to this game as much as I did, but I could not stop crying while playing. Specifically, as your life goes on and you get older, so do your parents. Watching my turnip parents age, weaken, and pass on was incredibly painful for me, and I kept comforting these fictional turnip parents while thinking about my own aging family. So if you're an emotional person as well... prepare to cry. In a good way. Minabo is a lovely reminder of what's most important in life.

I worked hard to make friends with the cats and dogs, and they were my best buds for like 60 seconds, then BOOM! slab of stone, friend gone. And what, you have a hat to make him live for another 60 seconds? Yay.. No thanks.Best depression simulator ever!

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? No, it is just an absolutely cute (and easy) 3D platform game originally released on Stadia Pro (RIP). We play Sigrid, a young girl who lives with her grandmother on a small island. On it is a large lighthouse, whose powerful light keeps the surrounding area free from the all-consuming black fog that has engulfed most of the rest of the world. Only a handful of other tiny islands rise out of the sea, and a few other people still live here. Despite this dystopian scenario, however, the world is colourful and actually quite nice, the inhabitants are friendly people and the buildings are intact. Of course, things can't stay that way, and one day a huge black cloud spills over the islands as well, only Sigrid is rescued from the sea by a mysterious being. She must now first free her grandmother and then travel to the other islands to fight the black mass that has covered everything. Sigrid has the ability to glide across the sea as fast as an arrow. She can also pull herself up in special places with her hook. In the air we can glide a short distance like a helicopter, we can also run fast or glide especially fast over the sea and jump out far. Of course, Sigrid also masters the double jump. The gameplay is relatively straightforward - we rescue people trapped by the black mass, bring them lost things (a few fetch quests), activate switched-off electrical devices, find a way up tall buildings, collect "sparks" (electrical energy) and thus uncover more and more of the map. There are a few additional collectibles, saving is automatic at certain save points. We can call up a map of the surroundings at any time.There are also enemies, but they are only a serious danger when we take a coffee break. Not even the final boss was really challenging. We hit low-tier enemies two times with our fishing net and have defeated them. Dying is hardly possible (we don't take any damage even if we jump down from a great height), and if we do manage to die, we are only set back a little and can continue playing immediately. The jumping passages are not particularly demanding either, but you do need a rudimentary sense of direction in a 3D environment. The playful challenge lies in exploring the world, finding and activating things, uncovering the background story. Sigrid, of course, has to look around carefully to find her way to the top of buildings - and that's where you often find the things you need to move forward. A compass shows us the direction to the next waypoint to advance the main story. The open tasks are permanently displayed, information found is automatically entered into Sigrid's notebook. There you will find notes about collectibles, about people we have met or about the history of the world. We can also read about the controls of the game here at any time. In a shop (no real money shop, you pay with currency found in the game) we can buy new outfits or hats for Sigrid or dye her hair a different colour.A not particularly difficult 3D platformer with a (relatively) child-friendly story about family and the destruction of our world. It is not necessarily baby's first jump and run, but also not a great challenge for experienced players, but a relaxing weekend activity that you can play through in a good six hours.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has not received a single patch since its Steam launch despite multiple glaring bugs that have been known to the developers for months now.Most importantly, this games renderer is capped at 1080p, so if you've got a 1440p screen or higher the game will look like a mess. Not having a single patch dropped since then however, which at the time of writing this is ) for the record, is simply unacceptable.Edit: Updating this well after a year and despite periodic promises there's still nox fix. Unbelievable.

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty good game that could have been *AMAZING* with a little more effort and variety. When I saw the trailer I got a Windwaker vibe, which is a game I loved, and it certainly delivered something like that with the story and aesthetics, especially the beautiful water and fun surfing mechanics. It's the gameplay that could use some work, though.At the beginning of the game, you're introduced to like 99% of the mechanics the game has to offer so nothing really evolves or complexifies as you play. Instead of dungeons there are towers. The towers might not be literal, they might be a series of buildings, a rock formation, a ship wreck, etc, but the point is you always have to climb something. To climb, you have double jump, elevators, grapple points and spring pads and that's it. Every tower in the game you use these handful of mechanics to climb in a samey fashion over and over. The combat has the same issue. Most of the enemy types are introduced right away with one special variety saved for the halfway point but you fight every single one the same way. You can ground pound for an AOE attack if there are a bunch of them or you can just rapidly hit the attack button to take them out one at a time. Nothing is ever introduced to spice up the combat.Sidequests? There really aren't any that are worthwhile except for the time trial challenges. Those are fun. The rest are all the same: you meet someone that's right on the path of a main objective, that person asks you to get something/someone, that something/someone is in the immediate area and also right on the path of the main objective, you return to the quest-giver and they give you a handful of currency. Every single one. Since nothing is out of the way, you aren't rewarded for exploring. It's just a minor bonus on the way to the main objective.It might sound like I'm complaining but, overall, the game is pretty fun, if a little repetitive. The surfing is especially good with some nice touches like a diving mechanic, a power jump and a little glow that lets you know when you're over water, along with the gorgeous water itself. That part was very well polished. It's just that with a little more effort and variety this game could have been truly *AMAZING*, like I said. It's a missed opportunity.

_childDocuments_.review: The Good:-really beautiful stylised water-fun surfing and traversal mechanics-very cute character design and art styleThe Middle:-music is good, but several times feels like it doesn't fit the theme of what's happening on screen-voice acting. Very hit and miss, some characters are flat and emotionless, while others feel like some effort was applied.-map menu and journal feels a bit wonky and weirdThe Bad:-combat. Too easy, becomes a chore, just not really engaging at all, feels almost tacked on-narrative. The environmental message is kinda blunt, but worse is the pacing. Slow but fitting at the beginning, then BAM! this is the end, have a little exposition, okay go on to the last fight and the credits. It all just felt so contrived.-side quests. Just fetch quests that reward you with currency that you pick up through the whole game anyway, to buy outfits for your character ~ mehI played and enjoyed the demo, which prompted me to buy the full game, as I thought there would be more "depth,"(hehe) but sadly that was not the case. This feels like a labour of love and I know that the studio went through all that stadia nonsense, but I just can't recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wavetale

_childDocuments_.review: Sigrid lost her mother when she was small and is now looked after by her grandmother.Their city was flooded when the Dirty Paws unleashed a fog like substance they call “The Gloom”, which submerged land for miles around, cutting them off from the outside world. Sigrid longs to explore and travel outside the realms of the fog, but it is a constant struggle just to keep the gloom at bay, only the Lighthouse beam charged with sparks can dissipate the fog, but it soon emerges again. One day, the Dirty Paws appear once more and threaten their very existence with a tidal wave of gloom that engulfs the inhabitants. Rescue the villagers, destroy the fog, and uncover information regarding your mother and The Dirty Paws, in this heartwarming, ecological, platforming narrative adventure.Wavetale had vibes of “Submerged”, navigating around a sunken city and exploring it through platforming elements. The city is quite fragmented though, with six main sections, marked on the map, and lots of archipelagos or small islands joining them up. There’s quite a lot of distance to cover to get around all the different areas.Each island is very small, so there’s not much opportunity to explore on land, but the compact designs are built to explore upwards rather than around the island. Sigrid can surf the waves on the sea, and at quite a pace too. I absolutely loved diving off high buildings, Assassins Creed style, and then watching her travelling under the water. If you time it right you can leap out of the water and then dive again. It felt very satisfying watching her do this, and she looked like she belonged in the water, almost swimming like a dolphin would. I found the travelling very relaxing, and the waves on the sea looked spectacular. Getting around the water sections didn’t feel laborious or a burden, even though there are large distances to travel sometimes.There is a compass on the screen, which also pinpoints things of relevant interest, and a map, which helps in navigation. I was glad to see that the map had way points which you can set, and Sigrid faces the way she is travelling on the map, which is very useful in a watery world to see which way you are going. On land, Sigrid can jump on to platforms, or use grappling methods to pull her up on to ledges, if available. Whilst in the air, she can hover as she descends, helping her travel long distances and reaching far away ledges. Navigation on land is a pleasure also, with many very tall buildings to ascend in a satisfying way, and then either leap off into the sea, or glide around looking for a place to land.Platforming is performed mostly on land, although there are some sections in the water, especially with Asta’s challenges, which are timed assault courses in essence, and quite difficult to complete in time.Story arcs and quests drive your need to climb buildings, and most of the time there is a similar game play loop. Turn on generators by finding and flicking switches, or look for sparks which power weaponry to repel the gloom. There are various iterations to this theme, but mostly you will be performing these tasks. Sigrid can jump on to platforms, activate pads which allow wind cannons to propel her higher, grapple on to certain ledges, or shoot through portals which send her travelling up or down chutes. Frequently, these mechanics are chained together in quick succession allowing for some exciting platforming. Operating any of these mechanics seems smooth and reactive and I hardly had any frustrating moments, even when platforming was manic. The only slight negative is that in these frenzied moments, the camera can feel a little disorientating sometimes, but really it is only a small ♥♥♥♥♥♥.There is nothing worse than lag or difficult controls whilst platforming, but Wavetale felt fluid, smooth and fun. Sometimes, the transition between surfing the waves to leaping out of the water and immediately starting platforming was awesome. The grapple function is excellent at wrenching you out of the sea, straight into the platforming sections, and the layout of the buildings are cleverly designed so that you can climb them quickly, or swing, glide, or leap between sections and feel great doing it.After the story element finishes, there is a free roam to pick up any achievements or finish quests. I would have liked Asta’s surf challenges to be marked more clearly on the map, as they are problematic to find as the areas are vast, and it’s not always obvious which ones you have already completed. The story was surprisingly good, and had an ecological feel about it. There were plenty of hints and suggestions that what Sigrid and the inhabitants of Strandville were going through, mirrored our own, and there were lots of interesting facets and nuances that were hidden under the surface. The cutscenes were very dramatic and the story had a nice pace to it, building gradually to a satisfying conclusion. The main characters are larger than life and excellently imagined, with some impressive artwork and great voice acting in the cut scenes. During normal conversation, there is no voice acting, but murmurs and noises mimicking voice. I really enjoyed the story. It felt heartwarming and immersive. There are also numerous quests which can be carried out, but they felt a little forced and not very interesting. They never managed to create any alternative stories to the main narrative, and I never felt these fringe characters were developed enough for me to care whether I managed to find someone’s engagement ring or lost dog. They basically acted as vehicles to reward you with tokens for purchasing outfits and hair colorings. I did manage to collect everything on offer but I was never compensated with an achievement or anything other than different looks for your character, so I wouldn’t bother unless that interests you.The game took me around five hours to complete, but this could be done in less time if you ignore the quests or Asta’s challenges. There are some combat sections where you fight gloom monsters on land, or sea monsters on the waves. For the majority of the time combat is embarrassingly easy, only feeling challenging towards the end when the main boss fight happens. Even then, respawning is very generous and there are plenty of checkpoints for it to become exciting but easy to complete.
_childDocuments_.name: Wavetale

_childDocuments_.review: Wavetale is family-friendly platformer with distinct art and simple gameplay. Once a Stadia exclusive, it has now finally made its way to PC and other platforms, to be enjoyed by all. Its major downfall is the excessively expensive price tag. Whilst I enjoyed the game, its small gameplay time and simplicity does little to justify such a cost, and I encourage those interested to keep this in mind.Wavetale’s story is that of the wholesome, family-friendly kind, focusing on memories of what once existed, family and reconciliation,  but also environmental devastation. The latter subject is what interested me the most, and whilst it is not heavily discussed, its theme is ever present, and encourages player reflection on our own ecological footprints. You play as Sigrid, a young girl in the decaying archipelago of her city, Strandville. The city and surrounds have sunken, there is little land and a black substance called gloom has taken over everything that once was. The gloom continues to spread, infecting everything that it touches, even encasing other characters. Sigrid can fight the gloom with her trusty spark-filled net, and alongside her cantankerous grandmother and other townsfolk, she is determined to make a difference to the slowly deteriorating world. With the help of an enigmatic shadow, Sigrid is able to walk, run and glide on the watery surfaces, allowing her to traverse the treacherous ocean with ease. As a side note for those interested, the game is very LGBTQ friendly, with many dialogue references around inclusive pronouns and features some non-heterosexual relationships. This is not a main element of the game by any means, but I found it refreshing that these choices were sprinkled casually into the game without it being a main focus or theme.Wavetale is a narrative-driven action-platformer that excels in gameplay fluidity. Effortlessly glide through the open sea, grappling to vantage points whilst being thrust into the air. Dive into the water, pick up speed and even compete in timed races. This core gameplay is fun, it is one of those games where you can almost switch your brain off and just sit back and enjoy. There are combat elements, but they mostly involve mashing the attack button. Do this, and the enemies cannot hit you. Even if they do, Sigrid has a large amount of health. I never died once, nor did I come close to it,  but the enemies are useful in breaking up the surfing gameplay and their simplicity matches well with the game as a whole.  There are no real puzzles, just levers to hit to unlock grappling areas, or to turn on machinery, and it is always very obvious to deduce what is required of you. Navigation is also effortless, there is a simple compass at the top of the screen that clearly portrays where to go and becoming lost would be near impossible.There are ample collectables to find scattered throughout the different areas. Interestingly, these collectables are not related to any of the achievements, making a 100% playthrough very simple. There are journal pages to discover, each providing a glimpse into the old world and how it once was. Furthermore, there are a handful of optional side quests which are all fetch quests of items typically found nearby, but it was a nice addition regardless. Lastly, there are the tokens to collect which represent the currency used to buy cosmetics. Now, these are absolutely everywhere and there was such an over-abundance of them that I had around 1000 upon finishing the game, and most cosmetics cost 5-20 pieces EACH. The cosmetics are nice, featuring hats, hair dye, accessories and outfits. However, I already had my preferred choice of style very early on, and there simply was not a sufficient variety to warrant the enormous amount of currency scattered everywhere, making it rather pointless to collect.Overall, the gameplay is reminiscent of the popular Indie game  Both revolve around flooded cities and small islands. Both are narrative driven platformers and majority of the game is spent on the open ocean. Whilst I must say that I preferred Submerged, if you enjoyed that game, you are more than likely going to enjoy your time with Wavetale.In terms of the gameplay, the camera was my biggest enemy. It locks onto targets, constantly pushing players in the “correct” direction, but this became frustrating, not helpful. The camera shakily jumps around as soon as you grapple onto a platform, immediately showing you where to go. I suppose the aim of this is to further increase the smooth movement and Sigrid’s speed. But many times this resulted in me being flung in the wrong direction, the camera becoming stuck inside a solid object, or was just plain disorientating. Whilst I believe I do understand the intent behind the camera choice, it was trying to hold my hand so much, that it had the opposite effect of being helpful. To speed up, RT is held, and A is held to charge up a jump. This combination is frequently used, but as a result, players cannot manually redirect the camera angle via the right toggle. Many times this also resulted in a disaster where I could not see, as the camera is jumping to points it thinks I wish to traverse to. Wavetale incorporates gorgeous pastel hues throughout almost every section of the game. The character art is rather distinct, almost cartoonish with characters eyes and eyebrows moving sharply in conversations. Admittedly, I did find their faces rather odd, but the environments themselves are simply stunning. A rather small nitpick, but I was disappointed to see that my custom outfit that I spent too long creating, is not shown in cutscenes. The backing soundtrack is just as relaxing as the visuals and the voice-acting is rather decent. Mixing in the dramatised voices of an elderly grandmother, pirates and more.  5 hours. I completed all quests and 100% achievements in this time (but I did miss some journal collectables & characters). Yes No, it is very easy to achieve all achievements on one playthrough and therefore I had little motivation to go back and find the remaining undiscovered journal entries.Wavetale is a charming and short action-platformer. Its visuals are gorgeous and distinct, whilst the story is heart-warming, but also features a bleak environmental theme throughout. The gameplay is extremely easy and smooth, making the water traversal and platforming elements the major highlight of the game. However, the automatic camera angles can be frustrating and disorientating, and the price tag is rather extreme. Whilst I greatly enjoyed my time in Wavetale, I heavily recommend this on a sale only, and to be well aware that the game is only around five hours long.

_childDocuments_.review: Dive into this beautifully crafted oceanic world filled with mystery and darkness. Traversing the seas with your surfing and swing ability is absolutely fun especially with the smooth responsive controls. The combat is very basic and never builds from it throughout the entire game as all your abilities are unlocked in the beginning. Dying is virtually impossible as the combat is easy, your life points regenerate and you take no fall damage. The platforming sections are fun especially when vertically climbing up large structures to activate switches or complete your objective. You collect electricity which can be traded in at the only one shop to unlock customization's for your character. Overall, this game is very relaxing and offers an enjoyable experience with a wonderful soundtrack, unique art style, and excellent movement controls in this 3D platformer. [8/10]

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this game. It felt like Wind Waker meets Jak and Daxter, with a dash of Gravity Rush and some of the most fluid gameplay I've ever enjoyed. It's hard not to compare this to Solar Ash, which I played earlier this year. Honestly, Solar Ash's presentation may be much stronger, but the gameplay and the one character at the heart of this wavebound tale resounded far more with me than those of Ash. The tone is dim but hopeful, and the environmentalist message isn't... exactly original or well-rendered, but it was somewhat charming.However, after beating the main story in one sitting, I can't fully recommend this game--not unless it's on sale for less thatn $20. I like short games. They're less of a commitment, so they're easier for relaxation. I think Wavetale could have been a masterpiece--a breakout hit of indie game development--if it was just more polished and there was anything to do in it.Imagine if Wind Waker:had only the main quest, with a couple of pointless fetch quests and races as side content,was a linear game instead of an open-world game,all of the items were unlocked at the beginning,and the dungeons all looked and felt the same,and worst of all, Grandma was not only extremely bossy, but she was your constant companion.That's more or less what we've got here, unfortunately.Maybe it's a little unfair to compare this to Wind Waker. I know it's an indie game. I gave it a lot of patience. I gave it my full attention for four straight hours. But after finishing it, I'm more than a little disappointed not in spite of its gameplay, but actually because of how ridiculously good this game could have been.There are side quests, but everything boils down to fetch quests. Even the main quests are ALL fetch quests. Go here. Do this thing. Gather three things while you're at it. I cannot stress this enough. If you can't stand 4+ straight hours of fetch quests, do not play this game. It starts to feel like an MMO at its worst. You don't gain or upgrade any abilities during the game. Money is just for cosmetic stuff.Kill a few enemies, and it soon becomes clear the combat is just not up to par. Contrary to the movement controls, the combat controls are too stiff and simplistic for this kind of game. Here, Solar Ash has it beat HARD, and it was simplistic itself. I would have gone for something like Gravity Rush's combat--maybe grabbing things out of the water and shooting them at enemies? Propelling yourself to bounce off enemies? Both would have fit so well in this game. Instead, you have two attacks and a grapple. Animation canceling doesn't seem to work with the normal attack. This is really only an issue in the final boss fight.Ugh, the final boss fight. It's hard to pinpoint exactly how it feels wrong... but something is really off. Swarmed by a wave of minions after each phase (which is only hinted at in the cutscenes, not visually shown at all). I don't mind the lack of health bars, I do mind the lack of visual clarification that I was nearing the end of the boss fight (no cracks on the "shell").Sigi really carries the story. She's a believable character and the perfect choice for a protagonist. If it weren't for her, the other characters would be grating. As it was, I was frustrated constantly getting an earful from Grandma. Her arc was good near the end, but it felt a bit rushed.The movement controls, while near-perfect, aren't without issue. I was three hours in before I realized I could dash or ground pound. The game gives you tutorials on a few buttons and that's it. With the exception of the ground pound, I just never needed to use those utility moves until the final hour. Sometimes the auto-aim gets a bit wonky or your momentum sends you flying past the location where you swear you grappled to a platform. What exacerbates this is the camera.I'm not sure what's wrong with the camera, but as I got further into the game I started having to actively fight against it just to finish the last hour. The section where you follow an airship was a real problem. The camera kept trying to look up at it. The FOV might be to blame, but increasing it did not make the game feel better.Sometimes the art design and character expressions can look a bit uncanny. At first, I found the hand-drawn style charming, but by the fourth hour I was just over it. It's similar to a low-poly Windwaker, but painted over like A Hat in Time. Oftentimes things just aren't quite visually clear enough. There's a lot of fog and effects in the game that detract from visual clarity.The environments feel manufactured, not lived in--despite their efforts at environmental storytelling. I was so disappointed in seeing this because the world and mysteries sounded interesting at first. However, I predicted most of the interesting story beats, including a "twist" that I think the developers realized wasn't much of a twist and smartly kept as a character's sad revelation instead.Grandma was absolutely annoying. She actively made the game worse even when she was off-screen, because she's still shutting down Siggi's attempts to get close (understandable but grating later in the story) and judging everyone you meet. If they had toned her down to an eighth of how important she was to the plot and made you see her once every hour I would not be so frustrated with her.The plot just... isn't there either. It's a linear story-driven game with a plot that is barely held up by a likable main character. I kept wondering if I should put the game down, then something happened and the plot picked up again and... oh wait, that's the end of the game. It's nothing groundbreaking or even great, just serviceable. If it weren't the main focus of the game despite the excellent traversal, that would not matter.There are some nice collectibles, but they weren't enough to keep me interested.For what it's worth, the traversal mechanics are amazing. I never fully got them down, and they seemed a little inconsistent, but it really, really feels good to build up speed, jump off the crest of a wave, dive under the water like a dolphin, chain a second jump into a grappling hook, slide through a grind-rail type booster, then do it all over again. You might get all of that enjoyment for free with the demo.Unfortunately, there's no reason to explore or go off on your own. I really wish there had been. I wish I felt like returning to Wavetale's world--but I don't.TLDR: try the demo, unfortunately everything is fetch quests and angry grandma chiding you

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Here's that video I mentioned making, sorry it took so long to get done I just got busy for awhile. The rest of this steam review has been left unchanged. The price tag for this game was going to determine a lot of what I said in this Steam review, I have a video I'm working on that talks about a lot more in depth of whats really going on behind the scenes with this one but let's get this out of the way because as much as I like certain aspects of this, 30 bucks is ridiculous.Why is that ridiculous you might ask? For starters, this game is not new. Wavetale actually fully released on the Google Stadia in November of 2021. The leadup to this steam relaunch unintentionally or not was making it seem as though this game was JUST coming out this year when that is entirely not true. The other massive problem is playtime. I am one of those people that doesn't usually care if a game is short as long as its quality all the way through. That is sadly not the case here. I will be sure to link the video once I finish it as its a lot easier to listen to than read a mile worth of my thoughts on this, but the composer, concept artist and narrative lead I think all got kinda left in the dust on this one by the devs. The framework of this game they got handed was great, and then the actual execution was really really mediocre. And again, this game is NOT brand new, they had a year from its release on Stadia to fix and polish and improve on the game and at the end of the day they still ended up with a mediocre game they're charging an absurd 30 bucks for. I have reviewed a good bit of Thunderful's publishing library before and a through line for the games they choose to publish for whatever reason is that they look and sound great but always fall short on the gameplay side and the games rarely last over like 4 hours. As far as specifics just so I'm not saying its bad without justification, lets start with the good before the bad. Surfing around in Wavetale is by far the most fun you'll have in the game. When the music kicks in and you're just zooming across the ocean its a lot of fun. The second the game takes you away from that (which is a lot) it goes downhill quick. The combat in this game consists of 3 moves. You have a basic attack which doesn't even have a 1-2-3 combo, its just slap, slap, slap forever, a spin move, and a ground pound. None of the enemies take more than a couple hits to die, and it took me 2/3 of the game to realize you can get hurt. Seriously, they are that non threatening that I didn't take damage until the very end of the game. Now as far as the platforming goes, theres a lot of movement options which is nice, except it allows you to kinda pull a Skyrim in that you can kinda climb any surface and very rarely need to go the "intended" way. There's also this fishing line that acts as a zip line of sorts. It locks onto certain points that shoots you to the point and then launches you in a direction like a jump pad. I think these maybe worked 50% of the time. The other 50% of the time it pulls you to the jump pad then you just kinda fall down and have to start it all over. This carries over into the final sequence of the game even when none of the jump pads were working on the final platforming section so I had to cheese my way into the final boss room rather than taking the very easy route they wanted me to because the normal route wasn't working properly. Also, the final boss is insanely anticlimactic. There's these robot sea snakes all through the game that are visually great but instead of fighting one of those you fight this weird ball thing in a tiny room, and for me the boss music cut out halfway through the fight so it was just combat noises. Super lame. I think the aesthetic and music of Wavetale deserve a lot of praise, but the actual execution of the game and implementation of that aesthetic and music are really lackluster.And again, this game is less than 4 hours of unpolished gameplay and is charging 30 bucks. I have all but 3 achievements that need you to do a speed course basically. The speed courses aren't hard, they just arent marked on the map and I didn't feel like hunting them down. Once I finish working on the video I'll update this review with a link so that you can see what I'm talking about, but there definitely seems to be a bit of weirdness going on behind the scenes here beyond trying to hide the fact that this is a Stadia refugee and not a new release. Initially when this released on Stadia, Zoink! Games were the developers, who have been under Thunderful for awhile, but not its "Thunderful Development" not Zoink! which is weird to me because Zoink! hasn't gone anywhere. They worked on Lost in Random among a few other games, and if there was any mention of Wavetale on their social media its gone now, but there are still tweets and even the IGN game preview from last year's launch say that Zoink! was the dev. Its entirely possible that I'm just reading into something I shouldn't be and that the Zoink team just got moved around a bit and renamed to Thunderful Development, but its still worth mentioning. Anyways, thanks for reading. Really was hoping this one would be good but no way to beat around the bush. As always, reviews are opinions and you may not agree with mine, thankfully there's a demo though so check it out yourself before you buy. Feel free to follow my steam curator page and I'll be sure to link the full video talking more about the weirdness with this game's launch and more specifics of what kind of game this actually is as soon as its finished.Last thing, I just wanna reiterate, the people that worked on concept art, music and narrative all have interviews linked on Wavetale's game page and Thunderful's Youtube. They really seem talented to me and I don't think anything they had to do with the game is whats wrong with it. Kinda a sad situation all around.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite being an ocean themed game, it is an ironically shallow experience. The full extent of platforming the game has to offer is shown in the first 20 minutes of gameplay and is simply repeated. Each mission objective is going to a place, whacking the same 2 enemy types, pulling a lever to activate a grapple spot, then grappling to the next area. The most fun you can have are four Sonic style speed challenges in between missions that actually requires you to go fast and be tactical about your grapples and rail grinds. The momentum physics are there but there were only a couple of instances that actually took advantage of it. The story is virtually devoid of pacing. There's approximately 3-4 central characters, each representing some sort of ideology.  An old woman stubborn in her ways refusing to adapt to new information, a quasi-dictator who pursues power at the cost of civil stability, and a kid who naively has hope for the world. The main problem is that none of these positions are truly fully developed because the game doesn't give any of these characters real screen time. Outside of being nagged by your grandma during quests, there aren't many meaningful conversations happening. Eventually there is a twist ending that is revealed to you in a single conversation and subsequently resolved in 10 minutes. It tries to end on some poignant philosophical note about entrusting the future of the world to the youth but it just feels hollow. Additionally, there are side quests but they are beyond optional to the point where they may as well not even exist. As some miscellaneous criticisms, there's no way of knowing when the game last saved. Both times I quit the game resulted in two separate quest tracking glitches, a permanent waymarked on the map for a quest I definitely did, and a main story mission displaying twice completing once and leaving the other. Additionally, the currency is grapple-able  which caused a couple of instances where I grabbed a coin instead of leashing onto a grapple point.Lastly, the game is woke is it gains +1 pity point.3/12

_childDocuments_.review: As some reviewers mentioned, the game does feel a bit short for its $30 price tag and the combat is very basic. But for me honestly, the movement feels excellent, the soundtrack is wonderful and the world is so beautiful that it just felt worth it. Beat it in about 4 hours skipping some side quests. If the price feels too much, just wait for it to go on sale I'd say.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so I played through the entirety of this game, haven't 100%'d it just yet, but I'm gonna give a quick run-down with a few of my nitpicks afterward!   Overall, it's a very enjoyable and peaceful game that's fun to travel around in. Not much to it, as I think it could be completed in two or so hours naturally - sooner if you're really running it and skipping scenes and such along with being experienced in such movement based platforming, but I do recommend it if you want to just enjoy free-roaming and a good story!Now, I do have a few gripes to address - nothing too egregious and nothing that'll upset the overall gameplay experience - just wee bits and pieces that are nigh irrelevant but things that bothered me nonetheless. This is relatively unimportant too as I've already written my main opinion above, I just feel like writing atm (So feel free to stop reading past this point)! Hope I don't put any more Gloom in this game than there already is, haha!   1.  Now, I've completed (most of) this game in one sitting, so I had no need for it. However when exiting, there's a "loss of progress" message which leads me to wonder where or when my progress is saved, especially since there's no dedicated Save Button. The game relies on checkpoints, but said checkpoints are, well, presumably only after completing quests and such. Game doesn't notify you about that either, but it's a fairly obvious guess. Nothing big, it's not hard to complete a side quest either, so it's not exactly much of a hassle unless someone had to suddenly leave in the middle of completing a quest. And even then, like already stated, it's not difficult so you'd only lose a little, easy-to-gain progress!  2.  There are a few things that the game doesn't directly tell you about or that I feel are unimportant or underutilized. That, or I somehow missed the guide window for it. This includes:   - Dashing, done with the "F" key, provides a little boost through the air, land, or sea. Also induces sliding on land. There's no tutorial or menu guide for this (as far as I'm aware), so I wasn't even aware of it before randomly finding it while heading towards the final area lol   - Wave-Jump Boosting, if you've ever noticed you're going a little faster than normal during certain jumps off the water, that's what I'm talking about! For me, it mostly triggers at the height of a wave (while sprinting) where the water's shining white, but there's no clear indicator and it doesn't always work.   - Aiming, done with the Right Click of your mouse, provides "Bullet Time", or a slowdown function. It's strange though, as not only does Sig not have anything acting as ranged weaponry or utility, most objects at distance have a magnet pull and no tight windows to use the feature, so you don't have to try to aim anyways. Perhaps it's for Controller Users? Not sure, but still. I did find it interesting that it can be used to make tight turns while waverunning! Useless, but fun!   - Water Fighting, although fun has absolutely no variety for it; there's only the Water Striders to deal with in this fashion. Plus you can Net Slam, Dash, all that jazz! I really wish this was used more!  - Enemy Variety, not exactly a control thing but while we're on the topic of variety, there's only three (land-based) types: Gloomling, Rush-Gloom, and Heavy-Gloom. I understand that this game is prioritizing exploration over combat, which is why I put this one last, but to me, who's played plenty of platformers over the years, the fight is just as important as the flight.  3,  There will be  when doing fetch quests, or if there is you're meant to catch it in the one line of dialogue (that you can't repeat). Quest Markers won't tell you anything, except the area of the quest. You're meant to search for it, after all. A lot of 'em are at least in the close area of the given quest, but there're some a bit  open for a comfortable experience,  Just wish there was a compass of sorts to help. But oh well, happy hunting!    That's mostly it control-wise. I hope that if there's a next time returning to this world and or movement system, that these things are put to more use! It'd be so much fun! Now, these are for the beats and other lore that I thought should either be clarified or just didn't ring as well. Again, just personal ticks, nothing major or world-breaking. Could be spoilers though! Be ready!  1.  All this talk about family and its had me wondering near the end:  Maybe I was just chuggin' too fast and didn't catch all the story beats through side-quests, but there ain't a water droplet of stuff about 'im as far as I've noticed. Sig doesn't talk about him, Granny doesn't, no evidence of him even existing either, but again, haven't 100%'d, so continuing to find out what else the world has to offer. He could just be that unimportant to the story, or maybe he's just the deadbeat noone wants to talk about, maybe he really doesn't exist and women can just be bestowed pregnancy like an Act of God, but whatever.  2.  Honestly, the Mayor, aside from the (imo) unwelcome touching and his stubbornness, wasn't really a bad dude whatsoever. He was doing what he believed was right and what he was likely taught what was right, doing what he considered good for his people. Seemed like someone a bit uppity and prideful, but someone that could at least be reasoned with in a calm manner and environment. I honestly thought he was gonna turn out straight up evil or something along that story beat. Nah, just got too focused on completing his mission and "protecting his people". , but whatever. 3.  I thought that the realization that, oh, wait, MAJOR SPOILERS - hold on:  4. (MAJOR-ER SPOILER)   4.  This one's my smallest nitpick, literally just writing fodder to me. Although I do find filler swears/words to be endearing at times, especially when built around the world, it's quite strange to have them be mainly the two major things in this world: Sparks and Gloom. I mean, Gloom I can get behind, bad thing = bad word, yada yada. Sparks, on the otherhand, well, it's like getting mad and yelling "MONEY!" at people, ha! No big deal though, it is what it is.   Don't let this (long list, dang) fool you, I had plenty of fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Wavetale is absolutely stunning to watch; gliding across the water gives the same euphoric feeling as watching Link sore through the ocean in Wind Waker, and in many ways, it's a more fluid mechanic. Sigrid's ability to jump, flip, dive, and even just walk across the seas of Strandville makes momentum a core mechanic of Wavetale, and with a smaller, more direct map, endless traversal is a problem avoided. Unfortunately, while the water itself may be deep, there's a shallowness to Wavetale's experience that just cannot be rectified when examining its core mechanics, making a game that is enjoyable to watch, a thrill at first to play, but ultimately more of a drag as its short runtime wears on.What does work for Wavetale is its story; I wouldn't call it "deep" as far as narratives go, but it's deeper than I might have expected, touching upon some post-apocalyptic topics, and sidequests that deal with pregnancy, dementia, grieving, and the like. This isn't a game with a complicated narrative - in actuality, it's remarkably straightforward - but it does, at times, touch upon something more meaningful under the surface. It's easy to get that feeling a lot with Wavetale, as there are so many times I brushed up against something satisfying while only getting a real skimming of the surface.I always am cognizant not to expect gigantic or immensely complex experiences from indie titles, knowing they just do not have the budget of modern AAA games, but I tend to expect a more euphoric, varied experience; modern gaming is so filled with bloat, so seeing it in an indie game to pad out length just feels disheartening. Wavetale has you constantly turning on generators, opening circuits, and pretty much any other activity done in realms of 3's. This would be more tolerable if the mechanics of the game evolved at all, but they never do - at all. There are no new abilities, power-ups, improvements, nada. The combat, which is simple swings and  a ground-pound, is the exact same throughout. It just didn't sit well with me that simple mechanics never went anywhere, and while the experience of movement is good, the movement through the repeated linearity of Wavetale didn't feel so great. The game runs well, and feels crisp, but shaking the feeling of repetition was hard.Wavetale isn't a long experience, with a completionist run being well short of a dozen hours; there are some collectibles to get, and they offer a robust amount of customization options, but when these don't even appear in cutscenes, it's easy to feel a bit bummed out. There are some minor time challenge quests, and a variety of sidequests amounting to collecting items, but that's it. I did enjoy my time with Wavetale in recognizing the limitations of what it professes, but I would have a hard time recommending this to anyone when there are much more diverse and stories indie experiences for cheaper.Wavetale's first few minutes of gliding across the water is one of those experiences that feels difficult to replicate in its august presentation, but ultimately, the experience never elevates beyond that moment. It's a shallow, shiny pool to wade in, and move on from.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I just can't recommend this game, far too much of its runtime is just tedious busywork. There are redeeming qualities like the art style and voice acting, but the game is just not fun to play. Mainly because of how insanely easy all of it is. Half of the platforming challenges are just grinding along pipes or latching to pre-defined points, essentially letting the game play itself. The combat is one-button spam with virtually no enemy variety throughout the entire game. Fortunately you can simply ignore the vast majority of combat encounters and just run right past them.The sad thing is that there are glimpses of a great platforming system underneath, there ware ways to preserve momentum and chain moves together in ways that are super satisfying, but it's never required and it even breaks what little challenge the game presents to you.On a technical level the game is hard capped at 60 fps and there's something weird going on with the resolution as well, like the game is only rendering at 3/4 of the resolution and displayed with no upscaling or smoothing. Graphics options are non-existant.

_childDocuments_.review: Full written version below but I made a video here if you prefer the format: I feel like Wavetale will get more “mixed” in the review consensus as people play it. Despite the asking price of $30 dollars, it’s only 4 hours with little to no replay value and the gameplay mechanics don’t stretch well since the game is quite simplistic. The ending also feels a bit unsatisfying.So why am I still recommending it?Well, it’s one of those games you can “relax to” because it’s got a really nice soundtrack, a great sense of momentum and the platforming is fun. It’s quite easy so there’s not a lot of challenge and since the mechanics you learn in the first hour don’t evolve or change, so you don’t have progression either. Variety is also lacking.It sucks because the story was actually kind of nice. It doesn’t shove cutscenes down your throat, it's paced fairly well, but the gameplay got repetitive. Out of nowhere, the game rushes to the final level. So while at least the gameplay didn’t get too repetitive in that it ends in 4 hours, the story suffered because up until that point it was fine and paced well. Rather than a bunch of things happening at once, you’re given snippets and pieces of the world and you can take in the atmosphere and silence after spoken dialogue with the quiet moments the game gives, this is helped by the soothing soundtrack. I felt that the game was on the right track to deliver something really interesting about the world or the characters but no, the writing never leads to any substantial revelation about the world or the characters like you’d think. The game isn’t fully voice-acted either which just hurts it further that it’s only 4 hours. And if you wanna do a 4 hour game at a high price, that’s fine, but the gameplay just isn’t very strong and neither is the writing for the ending.So in conclusion, you’re probably going to see a lot of mixed reviews for this one. Can I recommend it to 3D platformer fans? No, the mechanics are too barebones, and the variety and challenge aren't there. Can I recommend it to the story and narrative video game fans? No, because the ending isn’t great.But can I recommend it to people who want something more relaxing and a bit on the easy side that can still hold your attention? Yes, but only on sale!Thank you for reading. We have a Steam curator page with recommendations if you want to check that out:

_childDocuments_.review: A short and sweet game that I was glad to pick up in a sale but didn't feel was quite up to its full price. Wavetale's core gameplay consists of simple platforming, free skating across the sea, some collecting and exploration combined with easy combat. It tells a poignant but somewhat unoriginal tale of an earth destroyed by environmental destruction and a hopeful restoration along with some growing up and dealing with loss and relationships. On the whole I felt the simple tale provided a workable back drop to the game.In summary, it plays fairly nicely, entertained me for a few hours with good natured enjoyable gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: It is sad for me, really. It is sad for me that I have to say that I don't recommend Wavetale.I played the demo on the gamescom back in august and I loved it. It made so much fun and I was very excited for the release on 12th December 2022. I purchased it three minutes after it was released. During the first week after release, it has a 10 % discount - 27 Euro instead of 30 Euro.I won't judge the price. A lot of people say it is too high but I won't judge it because game development is a way more than most people see (I developed games by my own).What I can say is that the game has around 3 - 4 hours of gameplay.The time I played made a lot of fun. I had fun jumping around, explore the islands, read and collect everything and so on. The platforming made fun and the general art style is very charming for me.This fun was dulled a lot by the negative aspects that still need polishing or fixes from the developers. The game crashed every half an hour, I can't even finish it because the game just doesn't open anymore and if it does and I click on "Continue", it loads an eternity and won't continue.Besides the crashes, the gameplay makes a lot of fun but has a lot of fallbacks, for example that objects and shadows just pop in.The camera has weird behavior as well. For example when you walk upstairs and dash, the camera gets crazy and may stuck inside the stairs.I was excited a lot for Wavetale. I accepted the price because it was very funny for me. However, the final game is not what I expected and I would not recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: The story, art, and music contain depths in this otherwise very basic 3d platformer.I enjoyed both the environmentalist angle and the grandma-granddaughter emotional core. There were some surprisingly hard-hitting dialogue, bolstered by excellent voice acting.The combat is rudimentary, and smashing the weak attack button will get you through all battles except the final boss.The gameplay hook, which is doing parkour on the open ocean, is fine. Sort of an indie Spider-Man feeling. It doesn't develop very much, but when you start going fast it does feel quite nice. Special shout-out to the music, which is just gorgeous. I'd love to see what this could've looked like with a larger budget. It's definitely worth a look if you get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: "Wavetale" is a super sweet, short, and charming game, that I would gladly recommend! The game is very short, yes, and I encountered quite a number of bugs that soured my experience a little bit, but, the feeling you get when you've fully mastered the controls, and surfing the waters with the shade below, together with the music, the environment and everything else, is honestly kind of unmatched. The water movement is easily this games biggest highlight, and is worth buying for it alone. It's SOOOOO smooth and atmospheric, and I LOOOVED some of the conversations Sigrid had during those moments. Ever since I've played it, I still haven't found a game that gives me quite the same feeling just yet.The rest of the game though doesn't feel quite as polished though, sadly. As mentioned, I encountered quite a number of bugs (mostly minor though), and the pacing/story made it so that the game wasn't quite as satisfying to finish, nor leave a huge impact on me personally. Which is super sad because I feel like this game had SOOOOOO much potential to be a MASTERPIECE! The setting, the characters, the themes, the story, the music, the   g a m e p l a y  - it was all good! But it felt like it had the potential to be  with a  more time in the oven. But, either way, I really really enjoyed my time with it, and was bummed when the ride was over. This game has awoken a hunger within me for something similar to this vibe, that I haven't found a supplement for just yet, so I'm really eager to see what this team will do in the future! Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: A great 3D platformer with fluid, momentum-based movement that has you sliding around a fairly large world, fighting inky-black creatures with a rudimentary combat system, climbing on top of giant inky-black creatures, and trying to prevent the apocalypse. No, I'm not talking about Solar Ash. Sufficed to say, if you like Solar Ash then you'll probably like this too and vice versa. However, this game took half as long for me to beat as Solar Ash (a mere 5 hours vs 10) and is only $10 less. I try not to compare games TOO much, as games often take inspiration from the same sources and genres, but MAN these two games are SO INCREDIBLY SIMILAR (even down to them being released around the same time, AND being initially exclusive to another platform for a year) that it's hard for me to see this game as much more than just an inferior Solar Ash. It's still a fun game, don't get me wrong. But if you want to play a fun momentum-based 3D platformer with gorgeous visuals, then I'd recommend Solar Ash over this. Consider getting this game when it's on sale, though ($30 is kinda steep for a 5-hour game imo).

_childDocuments_.review: You can skip this first part if you want to, it's just me rambling. Video games are, for me, a way to immerse myself in a fantasy story, in a fictional place separated from reality. They give me the chance to incarnate another life, to get into the role of another person or even different creatures; they give me the opportunity to experience other worlds and colorful, unique universes. In Wavetale, I was given the chance to explore an aquatic planet, with wonderful oceanic environments and peculiar secrets. It is described as a story where we will have to unveil the mysteries of the past and help islanders; so I ventured in to learn about the world and why its surface is flooded by giant oceans, about the dark creatures that inhabit it, the terrifying mist that consumes everything, and, of course, its inhabitants. In this game we will play the role of a young islander named Sigrid, who lives with her grandma in a small corner of the vast sea. At the beginning, everything is going as usual between the protagonist and her granny, who receives a regular visitor that deilvers to them some objects to repair and some merchandise; until the mysterious mist looms on the horizon, darkening everything in its path. As we gain control of the character, we must then collect energy, in the form of bubble-like creatures called "sparks", in order to fuel our lightouse and keep the mist at bay. Following Granny's instructions, and with her catching net at hand, Sigrid readies for the task! However, when we finish our mission, we realize that the energy won't be enough this time, and the mist cannot be stopped. This of course is an alarming situation, as we are given to understand very quickly that nothing good comes out of going into the fog. No matter how much we want to oppose it, the brume advances abruptly and completely covers the small island; and, amidst the commotion, our protagonist ends up losing consciousness, thus falling into a light sleep. Upon waking up, a marvelous scene will unfold, a key moment in the plot that will completely change Sigrid's life; we will be introduced to a "shadow", a creature of humanoid appearance but totally dark (as the name implies), who will be in charge of helping our protagonist travel across the surface of the water. This will be the main mechanic of the game, and it opens the way to exploration and adventure; but, before that, we will have to rescue the grandma from the clutches of the mist, defeating the creatures that appeared with her on our way. After what I would call the prologue, we will begin our journey, with a reluctant grandma that does not quite trust our new friend, the shadow; and as we move from island to island, we will see what the future holds for us and those we meet along the way.I want to clarify that, although so far I have described a bit of its mysterious story, and some action and adventure, the vibe that the game gave me, more than anything else, was one of tranquility and peace; hella chill. It's a game that I found very relaxing, a really neat experience. Traveling through the sea, accompanied by our shadow under Sigrid's feet and the atmospheric soundtrack, created an ambience that I really enjoyed. Of course, it has its tonal changes, where I was able to experience more tense moments and other funny ones; and this kept it fresh and very entertaining!Let's start with the visual section, having an artistic style that I found very nice and reminded me of other games, such as, for example, Haven, A Hat in Time or Zelda: Breath of the Wild; but with its own unique and distinctive touch. The design of the protagonist, and the rest of the characters, is simple but very characteristic, and I think it fits very well with the type of videogame that Wavetale is, and I thought Sigrid's animations for her different movements were great and very eye-catching! It is worth noting that we will be able to customize the protagonist's outfit, hair color, and accessories; a small detail that I appreciate, as I really like customization. The environment is very striking, and the different locations have their own touches to separate them a little bit from each other. The waves and the tide in general are very well done, and simply very beautiful. I stood adrift in the middle of the ocean multiple times, just letting the waves rock Sigrid around as I took screenshots.The plot is wrapped in an air of adventure, somewhat mysterious, and slowly presents us the story of the world around us. The ocean, which now almost completely covers most buildings and homes, was not always so predominant; once, there were roads and cities beneath that deep tide. On top of that, a war was fought that ended up making things even worse; after all, the much-feared fog was a product of such a terrible event. Throughout the adventure we will unveil more details about the mist, Sigrid's family, and the "shadow" that accompanies us. Without going any further and spoiler-ish, I really enjoyed the story of Wavetale, a tale that is very well accompanied by its gameplay and soundtrack.While I'm on the subject of gameplay, I found this aspect to be quite appealing and it was what caught my attention the most in the trailer. Being an adventure platformer, it has the typical mechanics of this genre, such as double jumping, descending slowly by pressing the jump button, and shortening distances with a fast dash; among others that we can discover as we progress. When we are in the ocean, we will have these skills, but also adding some moves that can only be used in the water, such as surfing or diving for example. The controls are fluid both on land and at sea, but in my opinion they stand out much more in the latter, as it's where I found it more entertaining because of the surfing; particularly, my favorite part of Wavetale to no one's surprise. Moving beyond the movement system, we will also have combat moves to take down the creatures of the mist; nothing too overcomplicated, but appreciated, as I found it a very fun part of the game. In short, the freedom of movement offered by the title left me delighted. In terms of activities, we will have some side missions and challenges; a few little things to entertain us between main story missions, if we want to pursue them that is.The soundtrack seemed excellent to me, with several tracks of different styles and instruments, although generally very pleasant and calm. These melodies of course change depending on the situation, and I found them to be a very fitting and pleasant accompaniment for the different parts of the adventure. Wavetale also has voice actors for several of its characters, giving them a deeper and more unique character to each one of them; and, in my opinion, the voices were very well done, you can see the effort they put into their lines, and I really enjoyed it. Both visually and musically, it's just such a very nice game and it seemed to me that everything fit together so well.In conclusion, I thought it was a fantastic video game, and I enjoyed accompanying Sigrid throughout her adventure. I loved the freedom of movement and had a lot of fun because of it; it made me think that it really is very rare to find a game like this, and Thunderful made the most out of it's mechanics and setting! The answers I initially asked myself were mostly answered, and the various action, funny, and emotional moments, along with some plot twists, left me very satisfied with Wavetale; and, I have to say, I found the ending very nice, without going into any details. As a bonus, completing the game unlocks a free exploration mode, for those who want to finish some side quest or catch any elusive achievement, although they're not that hard to get. I highly recommend it to those looking for a chill adventure platformer, an entertaining story, and exciting gameplay!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm surprised at how much love this game seems to get in reviews. I like the art style and the water effects, but the gameplay is repetitive and boring.  There's absolutely zero challenge...no puzzles, no platforming, no enemy AI or variety.  The entire game is just jumping around similar looking environments and tapping 'A' next to any switch that glows.  There are only two types of enemies, both of which just run at you and can easily be swatted away with your weapon.  There's a passable story, but nothing special really.  There's zero character/meta progression, as every move and ability is unlocked from the beginning.If the game isn't meant to present any sort of challenge, and the main draw is supposed to be exploration, then there's a glaring flaw in its design.  There's no real reward for exploring!  At best you'll get a few extra $$$ for exploring yet another copy + pasted set of buildings, switches, and slides.  You also may unlock a few extra lines of dialogue for one of the many unmemorable characters, or another doodle with 2 or 3 lines of lore added to your journal.  Yay...  Not only that, but exploring side quests are the laziest, most boring thing imaginable!  They're basically "Hey, I lost 3 apples...help me find them."  Then you just run around the map looking for 3 apples, which aren't in an orchard or something clever...they're basically just placed randomly on rooftops or behind a house or something.  And what's the reward?  Just some more $$$...yawn*I was initially drawn to the promise of "surfing" around the ocean, skimming over waves and such.  Unfortunately, even that under-delivers.  Maybe I'm expecting too much, but I was hoping riding over waves would feel more dynamic...a bit more like Wave Race 64 (one of the launch titles on N64 back in 1996).  Granted, Wave Race 64 still has some of the best wave physics in game (imo), but you'd think Wavetale, a game focused on waves/water, would be able to do something similar 15 years later!I was excited to play this game...I really wanted to like it.  But after about 2 hours into it, I realized it wasn't going to get any better or complex.  I kept going because the whole thing only takes about 4 hours to beat, but it wasn't what I would call "fun."  I really don't understand all the praise for the game...

_childDocuments_.review: 6h 3/10 1 You don't need a guide for this gem No No No No No No No No difficulty option NoWow I'm blown away by this awesome game. Wavetale has such a great story, beautiful artwork, but the best of it all... how good and fun the game feels to play. I felt like a kid on a playground, speeding up, jumping around, and crashing back into the water.. it has been a while since I felt that in a game, and the last game that did that for me was , which also shares a bit of the theme with Wavetale. You play as Sigrid in a very dark and doomed (but still beautiful-looking) world, where there is not much hope for the future. You live together with your grandma on a small island till one day the bad guys attack and everything takes a turn for the worst. You two decide to fight back and do everything you can to save the world. What made this game so awesome to play where the movements, you move around with so much speed and can kinda do tricks while surfing to the next destination. And you never have to guess where to go as a marker will show you the way, which I prefer over being lost and having to find it for yourself. This game was all about the story and the experience this game is. The only downside I noticed is the saving system. Maybe it saved so quickly, but I never was sure when the game had saved and when it was safe to quit the game. There is no manual system and you might lose progress if you quit randomly. Maybe add a loading symbol and if it is there but just saves instantly.. maybe let the animation idle for like 5 seconds or so? I figured out that when reaching the new destination for the story and after the cutscene it had saved.. kinda before the cutscene but I happily go through that quickly again than losing my progress. One weird thing I noticed is that one time the game just had forgotten a sidequest I had before quitting the game, gladly I knew which one it was and I just hadn't completed it. About those side quests, they aren't required for the achievements, so you can ignore them totally if you want, but they give the characters a bit more depth, and most of the time the objective you have to find is very close by. Most of the achievements are for completing the main storyline. There are 4 achievements for 4 different races, those might be the most challenging ones in this game. Most of them were still very doable, I only had to retry the last one like 10 times because I just missed it, or made a wrong jump. Gladly the game has a very easy restart the race option, no hassle with going back to the start or waiting till the timer runs out. The last achievement is hearing all the jokes the shopkeeper makes, this just requires you to start a conversation with him about 10/15 times. I want to end this review with a message for the developers: This game is easily in my top 5 games of 2022, but maybe even in the top 3. There are 2 more contenders for 2022 that I'll try to play before the end of this year.
