_childDocuments_.review: The lenght comment about game lenght is at bottom of this review.Let me first express that I absolutely love the art-style. Its a mix of comics, adventure time and I'd say TLOZ:Wind Waker. Really lovely, expressive and very, should I say, scandinavic at times when it comes to architechture and small details like room deco. If you know, you know. Simplistic but works really well. No major flaws imo. Small details and quality-of-life, such as having character shadow shown directly under so you know where you are landing, are there. It has some easier and more lenient mechanics when it comes to platforming: Double jump, hovering for really long time, really - and I mean really - long "grappling hook" mechanic and "magnets" so you can hit the smaller things such as half-pipes.I would, personally, say that the game is meant for younger audiences and adults looking for chill and casual fun.The game presents a heartfelt message wrapped in unique visuals, making it feel like an animated series perfect for older kids. What I loved about the way story was told is that it had lot of "show, dont tell" moments. Some things are left to players and some are told later as reference to something you heard before. Story is set in "post-apocalypse" where water levels have raised, causing need to adapt and making people to live way above water. The main character has grown in these settings all her life - while the characters supporting character, her grandma, has seen pre-apocalypse and keeps remembering "good old days" which causes the main char some internal struggles of future outlook, annoyances but also intrigue. There is, as most post-apos have, a environmental message. "But" here its akin to a Ghibli movie—Could've use more depth. But before I go further I have to note that this is NOT a combat focused game so its not heavy minus.While the battles are fun and it never feels like a chore, they are a bit too simplistic at times. A bit more variety and complexity in the fighting mechanics would have made the experience even richer.Heck, 2 hours in the game gives me tutorial for "ground smash" attack - that shouldve been from get go. You could even use it before it? Also you never really need Dodge button, which the game somehow doesnt even mention or show in tutorial texts, because Basic attacks literally stunlock the enemies to the point I was never in any danger. But again, might be for younger audiances.Some cons and critique:* Aim is kinda useless, not sure why is it there. You have freeze time "aiming at something" but theres not actually any ranged attacks. I guess if you want to change camera middle of flight but dont have reaction speed?* Enemies too easy to stunlock :(* No tutorial of any kind for dodge or heavy attack?? Not that you need it but kinda odd.* Wave boost jumping should have tutorial its so cool! (let go of boost button in water if you are in the "sorta under water riding the shadow" instead of "surfing above water")* Maybe fast travel in free mode. Maybe.Its really up to you how much do you care about "dollar per hour". If you do, get it on sale.The game has pretty much no filler - cosmetic unlocks and sidequests are FULLY optional. Even from achievement standpoint you only need "the trial" ones for 100%Sure, adding features like a stamina meter, crafting, leveling, or talent systems might have doubled or triple the playtime, but I prefer not have those.

_childDocuments_.review: It is not fully polished for a game that cost 40AUD / 30USDI played the demo kinda late so I thought they would've fixed some of the weird things that they had there. They did not.I wouldn't recommend this game until they first fixed the issues.I am somewhat harsh because the visuals are very very beautiful and the animations are fun, esp the surfing on the water part. But everything else kind of sucks and made playing the game not as fun as I want it to be.First of all, the intro. It feels like they skipped some of the stories. I know they're supposed to sprinkle the stories here and there for mysteries, but you still have to explain some of them. like  Grandma keeps nagging about us asking too much but she doesn't explain anything and I would've like to know why, or at the very least,  like "oh no granma got turned into a blob" or "oh no the gloom turns people into a blob" before I whack grandma with my net because the enemies are all blobs, ya know?I only played for the first two hours so I don't know if they explained it later, but at least I would've liked them to tell me earlier in the intro. Because people being turned into blob monsters are kinda distressing and confusing, and it would be nice to have the distinction between people who got turned into blobs and the blob enemies spelled out with words instead of the player guessing and almost whacking an innocent person.The second part is the platforming. The game is not precise enough to have this many platforming. I'm not the best at platform games but it is so hard to gauge how you land or how far you jump on this game. I missed the platforms into the water more times than I'd like to. The aimed part are fun but that doesn't help that much.I ran into a bug where they ships just jumping up and down higher than it should be, and it persists throughout the game. The game crashed when it opened the shop the first time, and when I continue it, the ship still jumped up and down. Including the shop ship. During the shopping menu. I have a video to prove it. It was funny for a while but it get nauseating really fast.It is very laggy. My laptop is inteli7 with GTX 960M and 24GB RAM and its still lags as all hell. There's no windowed option either, so having a smaller resolution wouldn't mean much. And no option to turn down the frame rate either so its just permanently laggy. Ironically, it's less laggy on the ocean than it is on the land while jumping on platforms.They also don't have edge-grab, which is kinda important for a game that makes you jump to high places with extremely high risks of falling if you don't land precisely in the middle of the platforms.The game is very pretty and the UI are really nice looking. But aside that it's not that fun to play and really is not worth 30USD for permanent jumping ships and laggy platforms.

_childDocuments_.review: : The game is good. The story is well-written and heartfelt. The mechanics are decently polished. The music and art direction are wonderful. It has roughly 5 hours of very easy content, plus collectibles. It has a significant number of issues that I will describe below. I bought the game full price, but unfortunately, it's not worth it. Play the free demo and then buy on sale. Also, press F to dash.Wavetale has all the right pieces for an exceptional experience. The movement is fast, fluid, and fun, the art style is gorgeous, and enchanting adaptive music ties it all together. I played the demo, and, in spite of reviews, bought the game full price. I wanted believe it had more to offer, and I just couldn't wait for a sale. Simply put, it was a let down.First, gameplay. Wavetale's base is fantastic. When I played the demo, I was immediately drawn to how incredible it felt to just . Throughout the game, there are plenty of opportunities to engage with the movement, and Wavetale does a decent job of setting up fun sequences between story beats. However, the movement can be extremely inconsistent, and there are a number of times when the flow of movement is completely interrupted. For example, landing on ground almost always removes horizontal momentum. This would be fine, except for the fact that solid ground is often the only path forward between grapples, which greatly accelerate your movement. There is a button to dash [F], which becomes a slide on the ground, but this is not mentioned at any point in the game. I didn't discover it until I'd completed the story.About an 45 minutes in, jump pads are introduced that boost the player straight upwards. I'll be blunt; these are the worst objects in the game by far. The player snaps into place above them, which is again, fine, but as a result, all horizontal momentum is lost. You cannot bounce forward off of these, only up. They are frequently placed between grapple points, or after slides, and completely kill your speed when you're forced to use them. There is a similar issue with the moving platforms: you often have to wait for them to come down, and they provide very little in terms of gameplay other than a way up.Sometimes you will not be able to dive, even when the game tells you that you can (most notable in the demo). Grappling to launchers takes a variable amount of time that often breaks up your movement. Sometimes when you jump out of water, you are given a boost of speed, but the jump takes about a half second to activate. This is good for travel between locations, but it often occurred when I was coming up to an island, causing me to crash into it instead of jumping over/on it. It is also never explained, and I don't know how to activate it consistently.There are a few other minor things that interrupt movement.The other major problem with the gameplay is the combat. Let me preface this by saying the game is easy; I don't have an issue with that. What I don't understand is the inclusion of combat in the first place. Overall, the combat encounters are relatively insignificant. They are sprinkled throughout the game's objectives, but never prove to be more than a speed bump. Their difficulty does not increase, because every enemy can be stun locked by mashing attack. Again, the problem is not the difficulty, but that it is barely treated like a game mechanic. The game proves that it can do something more by adding a single water-based enemy, but the novelty wears off quickly due to the simplicity of the combat. The worst crime of the game's combat is that  This is when my heart sank, and when I ultimately decided to write a lengthy review.For a game set in the ocean, the setting is awfully shallow. Although the environments are well-decorated, the camera is a little too far from the player, making it difficult to appreciate the details. It also constantly jumps forward and backward when traversing through close quarters, causing me to generally avoid staying between buildings for too long. Out on the ocean, however, the camera hugs the player much too tightly, and as such it was almost impossible to fully appreciate the beauty of the waves. The camera pulls back a bit when you jump, but not as you speed up. There is no sea life to be found. That may be for story reasons, but in my opinion, it was a massive missed opportunity. I can only imagine how amazing it would be to leap out of the water with dolphins, swim with schools of fish, or just see a whale.There is a decent bit of environmental storytelling going on. Major locations are well fleshed out, but because of the above issues, it's difficult to appreciate the small details, and doubly so because of the pace of the gameplay. There is rarely an opportunity or reason to explore things at a smaller scale. The inclusion of journal entries helps some, (and I love the implementation!) but there aren't enough of them, and as far as I could tell, they generally weren't hidden in buildings or decorated sets. I would've loved to find some points of interest with little dialogue popups, giving small insights into the world or more information on the wealth of side characters.Speaking of side characters, it's quantity over quality. The vast majority of them are "I am X. Can you go find Y?" and nothing more. The main cast of characters are so well fleshed out, it seems like a disservice that the others get so little time to matter. Even the ones that are more involved with the main character (namely Blaine and Asta) barely get time in the spotlight. I want to know who these people are, how they live, and how they used to live. We only ever hear Doris' experiences, and although a key part of the story is , this development would hit harder if she had the opportunity to hear other people's perspectives, too. Finally, some less thought out gripes I have with the game overall.This game is suffocated by its length. That said, I would rather it exist the way it is than be stuck in development hell. It makes such a great first impression, and overall, the experience of simply playing it is nothing short of magical. Despite its flaws, I have to recommend Wavetale.

_childDocuments_.review: *Thanksgiving Grandma learns how to not do the no no speech*Wavetale doesn't do anything exceptionally, but the sum of its parts come together to create a pretty cohesive experience. There's little variation in the gameplay, but if played over a few instalments it doesn't get stale. There's enough to the land movement when you incorporate dashing and air dashing to create a pretty smooth and fluid platforming experience and I didn't get bored of it. Environments are repetitive, but it does have a wee bit of the Windwaker ocean charm to it. Whilst I don't think the dialogue is great, it gets across the analysis of a post-war world that it seems to intend, and though simplistic, it's fairly effective in delivery....even if it can be very hammy and blunt. The game's charming, and if you have a few hours and want a unique experience with a new world to run through then I'd absolutely recommend it. if the price is too steep then get it on a sale.And....admittedly the shadows are a damn cool idea, and a very unique way to thematically excuse water-walking.

_childDocuments_.review: In Wavetale, you are Sigrid, one of the last remaining survivors of the gloom.  Your goal is to save the world from the gloom.  You live in a world where plants and trees are no more and you are surrounded by water.  This is casual game for sure as dying is most likely not going to happen and if it does there are no penalties at all.  It is mostly a platforming game as you seek out specific items like sparks or other levers that turn on lifts and such to help you reach your destinations to move the story along.  There will be fights along the way, but again the game is casual and those fights are only meant as action scenes for the game to add a new layer of gameplay, not to make it difficult on the player.  Overall, this is a cute, child friendly game that is entertaining for the hours that it lasts.  It is short, but long enough to tell a good story and introduce you to unique characters within the game.The mechanics of the game are simple.  You can surf the water, with the help of a shadow creature who acts as your surf board.  You can double jump and if you hold the jump key/button then you will glide and slowly lose elevation as you go back to the water or the ground.  You have multiple fight moves, but the fights are basic and do not require much more than a few buttons mashed.  You have a compass at the top of the screen that constantly lets you know where things are and you have a to do list that appears on your HUD on the upper left to always let you know what your objectives are.The graphics are interesting.  While I played in 4k, the look of the graphics seemed much less than 4k.  The textures, especially of the faces are texture animations and not actual mesh animations.  It didn't look bad, in fact it looked unique and worked well, but again it seemed to take away from the high definition that I was playing in to make it look like it was at a much lower resolution.  The world around you is fairly drab in the sense that there aren't too many colors of the palette that are used due to the gloom around you and the lack of plants during the game definitely leaves a dreary look of the world that you are in.  This is ok though as that is the storyline that you are following, you are trying to save that world.The voice overs and sounds are decent, definitely not something to brag about, but I thought for an indie game that they did a good job of finding decent actors for the characters they voices.  Sigrid and her grandmother being the most important, I have to say they did a good job.  The background music is gentle, sets the mood and gets dark when it needs to.  It's dynamic depending on where you are in the world and plays well along with the rest of the story and the environment.The game is short, fun, and is a decent storyline to follow.  You can easily play this over the course of a weekend.  It's an experience worth having.  If you get the chance to pick it up, give it a shot.  I definitely recommend that you do.

_childDocuments_.review: wavetale was an instant purchase for me the moment i played the demo.pros: movement is fluid and super fun. game is well stylized and runs well. soundtrack is charming although it can be unfitting at times. voice acting is well done, and the story and world are greatcons: combat is lackluster, although it isn't necessarily the point of the game. in terms of content there's very little. you're set on a linear story path with a few collectibles. 4-10 hours of gameplay for the current price seems steep.this game has all the good and bad that comes along with a game that seems to be straight out of the ps2 era. overall a fun experience, grab it on sale. good job to the devs

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time playing , which met but did not exceed my expectations based on its trailer. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This game made me feel like I was watching Adventure Time. Some charming characters and a whole lot of wacky business going on and then BAM, deep lore that will scar the main character's image of others. The game's selling points (wave riding, open-world exploration, soundtrack) are its strongest points. My only gripe would be that the game is too easy. But, if you like what you see, you'll like what you get. What a special little indie title this was. So full of charm and magic, that I couldn't help but be enthralled by it all as I played. This game is so cozy and relaxing, yet still kept me in the action enough to stay interested, and I think this is the perfect little niche game for people who like to experiment and take a gamble on a game. The first thing we HAVE to talk about is the sea surfing mechanic. It is smooth. I mean buttery smooth. Besides awkward momentum transitions from ocean to shore (which were more fun and goofy than annoying) riding the waves in this game is just a blast all the way through. I see some reviews say that the mechanic didn't do enough, or that they got bored with it quickly, but it seems almost impossible for this to get boring for only 6 hours of gameplay. I had such a great time trying to time my jumps with the waves to get as high as I could, so maybe I'm just easily distracted.Yes, this game is only six hours long, but there's nothing wrong with that. For a game with so much charm and comfort, it's the perfect one sitting or weekend game for any casual gamer, especially with such a nice little story. It's very basic, and kind of predictable, but for me, I allow myself to get easily invested into stories, their lore, and their characters, so I enjoyed it through and through. The lore was very interesting too, I was a little surprised at how much there was to discover. And the characters? Great. Filled with so many fun little quirks. No God of War tier writing or acting, sure, but again, for a comfy and cozy game? Perfect. Kudos to the voice actors for their very convincing performance here. They keep it light and breezy, but man do they perfectly fit these roles. I loved Sigrid and the entire arc she went through. And I have to shout out this art direction too! Beautiful environments, with stellar, almost Doctor Seuss-like, architecture that dots the landscape and gives a fun, interesting map to explore. Different parts of the world have very distinct styles and atmospheres. It was very fun seeing this beautiful world, built up from the remnants of a sunken society.AND THE MUSIC OH! We just can't forget about the music. Composed by Joel Bille, (who I've heard before on the soundtrack of the Fe video game) it is such a gorgeous score, with different sounds that accompany all the feelings that could be felt during this game. A strong, sweeping sensation of the horns while you look to discover new islands. A sad, somber guitar, played one string at a time, and those strings are actually your heart strings. Or a loud and amped-up synth to get you in gear to fight some gross shadow creatures. If you get this game for at least two reasons, let them be the wave riding and this gorgeous soundtrack. I will certainly be listening to this album for days to come. Now, that I've done all my praising, there are some bad things I have to talk about, namely combat, and one weird glitch. Let's start with combat. Is it good? No. It's very barebones, but when I see people get upset over it, I wonder if they ever played the Crash Bandicoot games, where you just spin and jump. Or if they ever played Spyro, where you just spew some fire. Or Super Mario 64, where all you do is punch and kick. It's a platformer where you ride the waves. Honestly, for a platformer, it could be a lot worse. I don't know if this is an explicit game mechanic, or just how disconnected the combat is, but it seems to not let you button mash, so you have to time your hits properly to do consecutive attacks. That kept me engaged in the fights, but it's probably more of a testament to how broken it is. But all in all, it does indeed get the job done. And there was this one weird glitch where the game would just start stuttering its audio and gameplay. Everything just got stuck going back and forth for ten seconds at a time. This was very infrequent and happened near the end of the game, so it's nothing game-breaking, but it was annoying. I'd just pause the game until I heard everything go back to normal and went on with it. This shouldn't affect your decision in purchasing, because it's probably just my PC, but I thought I'd mention it anyway. My biggest gripe with the game though? It's easy. A bit too easy. Now, I know I said this was a cozy game earlier, and it is, but I felt like the combat was just too easy, which is probably why it seems so uninteresting. And even though they have really nice set pieces that let you do cool things, they're all planned-out spots, so there's not too much room for innovation, which isn't a good thing for this type of game.And let's not forget, this is an indie game after all, so there are some small, sorta goofy visual glitches going on now and then. There also feels to be a lack of cohesion between the game's main gameplay styles, and switching between them gets a bit wonky. However, it didn't bother me none, and it most likely won't bother you. So yeah, a solid little title that would be perfect for gamers like me who just want something to kick back and relax to. Since we as human beings are not confident in our ability to determine the thoughts of others into genuine advice or criticism, we like to quantify them into review scores and "should you play"s. However, I'm not gonna let some arbitrary number distract someone who this game would be perfect for. Put simply, if you like the vibe of this game, you'll most like the rest of it too.

_childDocuments_.review: While there are pieces of this game that work well, the overall package is thin and it overstays its welcome - to the point that I was barely able to make myself finish it. I got it on sale, and even at $10 it falls short of stronger titles. Definitely targeted to a younger audience.I'm not someone who enjoys mechanical difficulty, but fortunately there effectively isn't any to frustrate someone like me (it's easier than even something like Gris, which is itself easier than platformers where the challenge is the point.) The game's interest in platforming is about making , not asking the player to develop mastery, and this is very much in line with my own preferences - and yet it still fell flat for me. First, the environment design (i.e. jumping puzzles) are not tightly calibrated to the movement. My guess at the issue here is that in trying to be super forgiving with difficulty, they ended up designing situations where it's very easy to overshoot things if you execute the jump (or whatever) halfway decently.While the game is a platformer, the jumping parts don't really count as jump puzzles, as there's no challenge and nothing to "figure out" - you just execute them - mostly without trouble - and that's it. But that isn't really the game's core movement mechanic; the main feature is the "surfing." You can walk on water, but holding shift causes you to surf across it at high speed. The initial experience of this is fantastic, and that experience in the demo is what sold me on the game. Because of this, I feel the following is the most important criticism I can make of this title: for me, that thrill went away after about 15 minutes. I kept hoping for some kind of progression, some change, some Metroidvania-style unlock, but there's just nothing there. Nor any player skill development - there's nothing to execute that will make it feel better. On top of this situation: you have to do too much of it. While you go really fast, you also have to go really far. And neither the movement itself nor the environments you move through hold up to how much traveling there is. As a point of comparison, I played this game just after finishing The Pathless, which is another movement-focused game. The Pathless, however, has much more environmental variety, a bit more skill to develop in "moving properly," and a couple progression mechanics tied to movement - how fast you can sprint, how may "repeats" you get of the double jump, how fast you can glide, etc. Because of these additions, the first five minutes of movement in that game are different from the last five minutes of movement. Wavetale does not have this - movement is exactly the same from beginning to end. What made me very nearly not finish this game was simply how much of that same movement I had to do between story beats.[h3[Story[/h3]Despite the focus on the surfing mechanic, the story is really what got me to finish the game. The story isn't bad. It's extremely straightforward, with every twist seen coming from a mile away, and it delivers a cartoonishly straightforward political message in the bluntest way you can imagine. But it's not objectionable (okay it may be objectionable for people whose politics lean right of center.) Interestingly, while the overall arc of the plot was really dull, the actual dialog - the moment-to-moment lines - seemed quite strong to me. It's as though they hired talented writers, but told them they had to use their skills to deliver an extremely straightforward YA drama. It's a bit of a surprise to me that a game which bears so many of the traditional marks of indie titledom (focus on diversity and representation in its characters, strong visual style, lack of VA) comes up short on plot, and my best guess here is that it's because the game was originally developed for Google's failed Stadia console, which might have imagined having a younger-leaning audience, whereas most indie titles on PC (via Steam or itch.io) with those same political leanings tend to aim for an artsy, high-brow audience. In any case, it's not a bad story - as I said, it got me to finish the game even though I knew how it would turn out.Um... not great. The control scheme and graphics settings can't be changed, and that's almost enough for me to not recommend a game. The fact that the "advance/initiate dialog" key is 1 is the only time I've seen a game do that, and it makes 0 sense. Moreover, outside that context, similar "meta" buttons (i.e. keys not use for controlling movement) include F, E, G, M, right mouse, and left mouse. PC players complain about games developed for console dumbing down control schemes, but this game has the most extreme case of using way too many keys for no reason that I've ever seen in a game.There's no ability to manually save and no access to multiple autosaves, and the UI around the save function is straight up idiotic: it tells you you'll lose progress when you quit to menu, but the player has no ability to do anything else, and there's no indication of when the game is saving. Even now, I have no idea what was going on here. I ran into a handful of places where mistakes in level design (holes, basically) left me stuck, so I just had to hope that the save wasn't so recent I'd be stuck there, but not so far back that I'd lose a ton of progress. There are enemies in this game that, when defeated, result in a fairly strong forward boost. One of the combat sequences that involves them takes place in a narrow area where the "walls" act as kill zones. And three times in a row during this fight I got flung directly into the wall because of this design, having to restart the fight due to the uncontrollable boost. During the final minutes of the game, I couldn't figure out what buttons to press to continue (see above re: there being like 5 different buttons used for interaction.) I ended up having to pause the game and do an internet search for what button to use, only to watch a Vtuber .Not really why anyone should play this game, but they're nice enough. The colors are fantastic, though there's no variation here. By far the best feature here - and this was absolutely the best place for them to focus - is the water, which is really beautiful. The characters are also quite good, with their "costuming" being particularly great. The enemies, while having basically 0 diversity from a gameplay perspective and more or less all sharing the same design, work well thematically, and it's nice that they stand out from the environment.The environment design is decent, but I think the bar is really high for indie projects, and this game doesn't clear it for me. You can't throw a stick in the indie space without hitting a beautiful game, and this game really doesn't offer anything exceptional here. Even color-wise it's falling short of something like Firewatch. It's not as coherent or intriguing as Journey or The Pathless, not as poetic and beautiful as Gris or Sable, not as cute-but-sinister as What Remains of Edith Finch. The stylization doesn't support the game's tone or story as well as Disco Elysium. I could go on and on, but you get the point: the art direction here is fine, but I never noticed something it was doing while playing and had the thought that it was good or looked cool or was doing something interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: 1) Story: 4/5. It was a fresh narrative with a some basic tropes. The real intrigue of the story comes from the water shadow, but the game is short so you don't get too much of a deep dive (pun intended). For a game about riding the ocean the story isn't that deep (pun also intended), but it's tied up nicely and wholesome by the end.2) Characters: 3/5. There's a lot of unique NPCs, some with some charm, some with some...nothing really to them. Similar to the story, this game is a bit too short to really offer much depth to any of them. The only characters who get much depth and growth are the main characters.3) Setting: 4/5. This whole game is about exploring the ocean and seeing the havoc the dark fog has wrecked upon the seas. Each area isn't all that different from another since it's mostly just ocean, but with this short time is still does a good job of setting the scene here and there. However, down-side is there's no fast travel and just sometimes the ocean feels a little too big...4) Music: 4/5. It's a game about exploration and vibing on the ocean so the music helps with that vibe. Heck, there's even some combat to it and the music seamlessly shifts to a more energetic riff to match. When you're alone on the ocean just cruising, or at the sadder parts of the story, the music does a good job matching the mood.5) Gameplay: 5/5. For a game about riding the ocean you can bet the controls feel good as your surf and swing with your spark-net at break-neck speeds. The movement controls is honestly the biggest thing that kept me coming back. Like a Hat in Time, this game has some movetech to it in regards to diving. When you're jumping over the ocean, your character highlights pink indicating you can dive. When you dive you travel under the water at increased speed. At any point until you run out of breath you can release the dive early to launch far forward over the surface. If you time your launch well enough with a mid-air dash and double-jump, then your character highlights pink again allowing you to chain the dive movement. It does have a timing window though else you lose your pink highlight opportunity and the only way to reset it so to get on dry land. It feels good and rewarding to chain-dive to get around! All in all, that comes out to an 80%. I'd give it a B- and a definitely wait until it's on sale. Not really worth it for the current price, but would definitely recommend it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: For  you really shouldn't buy this.But in a good sale (like for 10 bucks), I'd say it's not terrible. Try the demo to know what to expect.It's a short 5h adventure with inoffensive combat, some fun traversal mechanics and good production value.I really liked the visual design, atmosphere, the animations as well as the music and sound design.The gameplay is pretty responsive and the basic "game feel" is good. Sadly, the traversal mechanics - while all fluid and responsive on their own - don't really lead into each other... It's so weird to get these Sonic-esque speedslides and boosters, and then just - drop down to the ocean in matter of a few meters & have to keep going with normal sprint speed. Big missed chance to give the player a bit more organic momentum and make the traversal both much more fun and the true core of the game. Mechanically, the story- and side quest are mostly just busy work fetch quests & "hit the switches in the predetermined order". There are no puzzles here.The writing itself is "solid", atleast for my palate and the voice-acting carries it very well.The buyable cosmetics aspect I really don't get tbh. Only 1 or 2 outfits really fit the character and none of the cosmetics are visible during cutscenes - it's always the default character model.Do yourself a favor and don't bother collecting any of the orange collectibles if they're out of your way - their only use is buying other hair colours and mostly ugly hats & outfits. You get plenty, just by doing the side quests and traversal routes, to buy the one or two outfit versions that don't look completely out of place.The visual design, animation work, music / voice-acting is what carried this game for me - enough to play through it in one sitting. If those don't do anything for you, there's probably nothing here for you.Sadly it's also a bit marred by light technical issues - it doesn't render right on 1440p, no matter what the settings say (drop it to 1080p, or it will look jaggy af!)Animations sometimes hitch if you get too rowdy during traversal, and the camera has trouble keeping up in some of the faster sections too, especially near the end. The final mission input is missing it's prompt (it's "1"), and side quest progress doesn't seem to save between sessions/area reloads unless you actually finish the quest. Not game-breaking bugginess, not even close - but still sad to see.The game badly deserves more than 350 Reviews and idk how it flew under the radar  badly.It's not exactly thrilling, but considering all the goofy asset flips that get pushed to the front, it's sad to see a game with this much geniune heart put into it fly so low.

_childDocuments_.review: The Dirty Paws are back and it is up to you, and the shadows below, to stop them and bring peace back to the decaying archipelago of Strandville. Wavetale is a story-driven adventure where, as Sigrid, you will skate across the waves and fight gloomy enemies. Using your net, you will traverse buildings, hookshot into pipes, blast yourself out of cannons, and more to make your way across the stretch of islands. You can customize Sigrid as well with different outfits and hats to really make her your own!Wavetale was something I really didn't expect myself to enjoy nearly as much as I did. The combat felt a bit lacking since you're just whacking enemies until they blow up, but I can't get over how much I love skating on the water. It feels awesome to hold down the jump button to eject yourself higher than normal and hooking onto a continuous stream of pipes and cannons to traverse long stretches of water. While I had a blast playing, I think we should look more into the Steam Deck experience.Due to this being an open game with a decent amount of buildings, I didn't expect performance to be up to 60 FPS. At max settings, I was getting an average 48 - 49 framerate with 22W battery drain and 85c temps. There were a couple moments this would dip closer to 40 with drain and temps would go higher as well. Luckily though, with a couple of tweaks, Wavetale can be much more playable!I went back and forth between whether I preferred battery life or a smoother framerate and, after playing for a bit, I had to go with smoother framerate. Gliding across the sea at a smoother pace was by far the more enjoyable choice. It did mean the battery would be draining faster (around 14W-16W in most spots), but the trade off was worth it for 40 FPS. I did notice some spots did drop to 38-39 at a TDP of 10, but these almost immediately bounced back so it didn't bother me in the slightest.I did also want to make a 30 FPS build that focused on battery and further refined stability. I was able to get a TDP limit of 6 comfortably while drain stuck around 9W - 12W for almost 4 hours of battery. It didn't feel as great to me as 40 did, but it was still very comfortable and playable.When testing the game, I tried a multitude of different options to get it to work right. While the game does have some accessibility options, there weren't any graphical ones apart from resolution (which only has 720p and 800p). I decided to try to force the resolution down through Steam, which I could then use to upscale to save on performance, but doing this caused a lot more stuttering, so keeping it at native was the only option. Otherwise, I didn't encounter any other issues in regards to performance.Wavetale is really an awesome game. I can't say enough how enjoyable it felt to surf the waters and hook across pipes and cannons that accelerated your movement. The combat may be lacking in depth, but the game makes up for it with the way you move and traverse across the world. And on the Steam Deck, this will be a wonderful action-adventure experience definitely worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: I actually played this game when it was on Stadia (remember that?). It was on Stadia Pro, which I got 3 months of for free with my Google Pixel 6.  Short summary: If there is only one word to describe this game, I would say "beautiful" - in emotion, art, and gameplay. This game is heartwarming, funny, atmospheric, and above all incredibly fun and smooth to play. Bonus: The ending actually made me cry - a rare thing for any media, let alone a videogame to do.Playing this game again has really made it age better and I am so glad that it is now available on Steam. Wavetale is the story of Sigrid, a young girl who lives with her granny in a beautiful, but almost post-apocalyptic aquatic world. There is a darkness that surrounds their world - "the Gloom" - and nobody dares go into The Gloom. Sigrid, through a series of cool events, finally gets a Shadow, which mirrors her exactly in the water... Allowing her to literally walk, surf, and glide over water. And this is just the beginning. Sigrid and Shadow must save their world from The Gloom and it's creatures, help any townfolk you find along the way, and learn more about what came to be of the World Before. Despite the premise, the game is action-packed, yet tranquil and chill. The story and gameplay provide enough challenge to drive you forward without giving too much trouble. Combat js simple, but it's not going to be a slog. The main elements of the game are platforming and travelling - both land and water travel are very fun, and Sigrid is very capable of jumping, surfing, and whacking things.The graphics are GORGEOUS. The art style really matches what they're going for. It is bright, colourful, and engrossing. It feels like a moving watercolour painting sometimes. I can only imagine how gorgeous it would be. The animations are really smooth too. If games are art, this I would put this as one of them. The story is engrossing and profound The quest for Sigrid to help others and save her world is beautiful. Sigrid is by no means a complex character, but she has depth and you can feel her develop and grow as the story does too. There are few side missions that flesh her out a little bit. You can also learn more about how their world came to be - there are glimpses of cities and towns under the water... And like I said, the ending made me break down in tears with how moving and beautiful it was. Other characters are also brilliant, including the grandma, the mayor, and others. Sound: The music is just as beautiful as the artwork. They put a lot of effort into that. The sounds of the water is also brilliant. I lived by the sea for a while and they really captured how water just works. The voice acting is superb too, everyone really did a good job.Conclusion: I highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a game rich in beauty - in art style, music, story, and gameplay.

Which wasn't explained at all.- You can also dash, which was never explained either. Unless it gets explained further into the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a short, beautiful, and enjoyable experience with a simplistic yet massively enjoyable game-play system.  Switching between surfing on the water and combat is seamless, and the momentum both figuratively and literally carries it swimmingly. The art style although feeling a bit old is beautiful at almost all times, if also at times feels a bit limiting on expressive moments and scenes, with emotions getting lost if not for the smooth voice acting. Along with an old but fresh-feeling art style is a small and diverse soundtrack, with smooth, calm tracks to lose yourself among the weaves and intense beats to defeat enemies and even some bosses. The main story although nothing new is still quite well written and stays simple and understandable, nothing gained but nothing lost. Customization is surprisingly wide with many options to choose from and collect if a tad bit shallow with not many options on what to customize, especially when customization does not carry over to cutscenes. Side missions are just enough to feel achievable without feeling like a second thought and range from the same simple story to quite uniquely written and interesting dynamics, across the game's sparingly diverse and interesting cast. Overall well worth the $30 price tag for the around 12-14 hour experience, especially if you enjoy the demo and if on sale. Story-5Game-play-6Style-7Pros-Stylish graphics -Strong performance-Unique concepts-Well-rounded gameplay -good soundtrack-Fair content to price balance Cons-confusing side mission directions-occasional janky feeling during intense moments -Not much repeatability

_childDocuments_.review: What I tremendously enjoyed here is the playful soundtrack and how great the voice performances were. I think they all outdid themselves, and it really helps elevate Wavetale's overall gameplay. Traversing also feels fantastic most of the time and while the mechanics are not that plentiful or deep, the short runtime managed to land my enjoyment safe and sound at the last minute before I would have gotten bored with it.The overarching story was serviceable, and the unexpected twists managed to surprise me.Sadly I have to, as many in the reviews already did, disagree with the price point.I wouldn't even mind the runtime that much, but the game is just not polished enough. There's a myriad of strange hiccups with the geometry and physics, loading from autosave deletes side quests for some reason and a lot of the cutscenes end with very weird camera swerves.Overall Wavetale is a wonderful little message about listening not only to your own people, but everyone, and even the environment's voice. Before it's too late.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for good combat this is not for you. However this game holds a special place in my heart. It is not a long game, and it makes me wish for more. The movement is fluid, quick, and snappy. The story is caught between cute and sad, and the characters are written so well. It's balanced between wanting to linger on the characters and to actually play the game. Its engaging, every area rewards you with exploring with the little sparks that you can just speed right by, since they hold no value towards the gameplay. They're just there if you'd want to get more cosmetics in the game and it's nice. For the first time playing i would say you should help around do all the side-quests just to feel the world. I can also see this game being a fun challenge to speedrun after your initial playthrough. TL/DR: 9/10, a great story and great gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: (Played on Steam Deck)I would recommend Wavetale, but look for it on a sale. The game is short (5 hours) but that´s not a problem. Short games are nice between your longer games. The story is neat, the voice acting is awesome and the art style is very charming. This game has a unique movement set that is really fun. I really enjoyed exploring the different isles and the sea, the puzzles are fun but not too hard. It is all in all a cozy game although the narrative can be a little bit dark at times (which I like).The only problem is that the game´s combat is - after the beginning of the game - not satisfying. There is no variety in the enemy design and you can´t learn any combos at all. The combat is the part where I always felt that the game isn´t finished and why I would buy it on a sale. There is stuff missing and that is why combat is boring after the first half of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever played fast-motion, fluid 3D platformers like The Pathless made by Giant Squid (devs for games like Abzu), then this game would definitely be up your alley. I played this on an Xbox Wireless Controller and it was a pretty smooth ride. Travelling around the sunken city barely feels like a burden, though the adaptive music can get confused sometimes when to close to an enemy's aggro range. While the facial animation most often doesn't entirely fit the character's emotions, the voice acting more than makes up for it. This game overall feels like a great combination of both the setting and thematic values of Man vs. Machine/Industry found in Abzu and the quick-time 3D platforming found in The Pathless. And sure there are plenty of rough edges and places for improvement, just like a hand-knit woolen sweater, it'll keep you with a warm and cozy feeling at the end.

_childDocuments_.review: this was much better than I expected to be, especially story and character wise.some dialogue hit really hard and is extremely relatable, both for the overarching plot and situation of their world, but also some family relationship and tension. there is genuine quality in the story of this game, also highlighted by excellent voice acting.the game looks pretty good and has a good art style and great color palette, the music is also fitting the mood of the particular scene or quest pretty well.as for the gameplay, it is mixed. by itself, it is almost entirely focused on smooth and unpunishing high speed movement flow. it is very fun to move around and explore in this game. platforming is also pretty fun because of the movement. however, the combat is very VERY basic, and from a gameplay perspective, once you've played an hour, you've seen everything the game has to offer in that regard. playing the middle parts of the game, where not much of the story is revealed yet and what you have to do is a collection of uninteresting fetch quests, can get a bit tedious because of the gameplay depth being unable to accomodate the game's length.however, when I started getting bored of going around, the story picked up immensely for a final act that was really interesting and rewarding.i would heavily recommend this game, however on sale as the full asking price is too much for the 5/6 hours this game has.

_childDocuments_.review: The Story was very well written and the combat was very simplistic, The game was great and all except for some major things like advanced attacks and dashing, water surfing also felt limited unless you're really good at dive dashing with the shadow and know how to combo at the height of the waves to catch enough speed to perform the shadow dive dash ability it honestly felt limiting to me, especially after realizing the boat speeds were far superior than anything else in the game, why are boats going like 4 times faster than the MC? (lol) also no new abilities to speak of and the shop literally only has cosmetics and most aren't that good (sorry) but it definitely would be nice to see if this story ever get's a chapter 2 in the future (most likely not) where new abilities might be learned instead of smacking bosses or mobs with auto attacks senselessly because lmao, there should be at least more to the combat aspect don't you think? anyway the tutorial never taught advanced movesets like groundslam, spin attack or dash, as fun as dash would've been to play around with i never used it until accidently finding the control for it at the very tail end of the game. the games not perfect either but it definitely could've had more to both the shadow and combat and water parts of the game and i give it a 7/10 overall.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR: Short and sweet, pretty solid story, art style and gameplay. However lacked final polish. Difficulty is VERY casual, something to sit back and relaxed to. A lot of small glitches here and there, like already rescued individuals and defeated monsters still showing up on compass (the game seemed to have trouble keeping track of progress flags); sometimes events will not trigger (like grandma's boat wouldn't move out, spark tank wouldn't power up etc) but fortunately the ones I encountered could be solved by reloading a previous save and not game-breaking.The rest are general UX problems, such as having the same button (X) for attack and skipping dialog, which caused me to accidentally skipping a lot of dialog when I "rescued" individuals. The funniest one is that at NO point was the dash move (B) tutorialized, or even mentioned in the journal, despite being an extremely helpful move both for combat and racing. Confirmed compatible with Steam Deck - the "text too small" on the current compatibility issue can be resolved by setting text size to "huge" in options. No other graphics settings though, which is a shame since the default drawing distance is quite short with a lot of "pop in" issues.Overall I hoped all these eventually could get fixed to give us the polish this game definitely deserves, unfortunately though there's been no updates for a while.

_childDocuments_.review: Voice acting is nice, but not all dialogue seems to be voiced in a rather short linear game.  Fighting is solid enough once you get into the grove. Story is good. Visuals are unique.Movement on water is very good and platforming is solid enough. Both can get very satisfying once you get it down. I encountered a lot of terrain bugs (somehow main protagonist feet just clip into the ground at points, etc.). Audio seemed to commit "perish" quite often. Camera would freak out out when entering a new zone and constant zone loading stutters. Game managed to crash 1 time and I lost some progress. Very jarring cutscene transitions the further you get into the game (start to get teleported to story start points).Oh and no saves. When the game saved? You may catch a glimpse of the save button or you may not! Good luck!I feel like this game could have used more time in the oven to be completely done. I have encountered free student games that ran smoother than this. I hope that this game gets remastered in the future as the base is very solid.I am only recommending the game on a steep discount. Not worth 30 euros at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Easy cozy platforming game, but I don't think I can recommend it unless on a deep sale. The good aspects are fluid chain platforming movements, pretty world/game art, but that's about it.The story is very mild and short if it wasn't for the long traveling required to go from region to region. I probably could complete it in 2-3 hours if I wasn't trying to platinum it. The twist is very predictable.The issues with games include the fact that the fast paced platforming doesn't match the slow cozy pace of story. The world is shallow for how large it is, so there is a lot of empty space and no fast travel. Usually, I think games have to many collectibles, but this game felt like it could use more to help populate and let player explore the world. However, it would need some mechanic to help identify nearby collectibles as it was a chore to explore the world if trying to collect everything since there was so many empty areas. Lastly, there is a lot of technical issues with game that devs haven't fixed since releasing it a couple years ago. First, the video/graphic settings are poor. It only gives you resolution and vsync option. The game locks you at a 60 fps rather than let you set the frame rate. The video quality get worse if you set the resolution higher than 1080p even tho there options to go up to your monitor's native resolution. I have a 2K monitor and game looked horrible and blocky in 2K which ruins one of the pluses of the game, the aesthetic. The save method of the game is horrible. It only auto-saves and doesn't allow player saves. Saves only occur at certain checkpoints in the main story. All the side quests and collectibles don't matter and won't be saved if you don't reach a check point.Happy to change my recommendation if devs address the issues with the game as there is potential.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes but:Beautiful game, good voice acting, nice music, amazing art.Sadly, controls are not super sharp and it doesn't always feel great to control. _childDocuments_.review: I want to start off by talking about the thing I love most about , and yes, it's the movement. It is such a unreal joy to dive, glide, surf and grapple your way through every space of this world dominated by waves. It enhances the experience beyond its otherwise relative simplicity because it's such a buzz to go from A to B, from point to point, quest to quest. But what are you doing with this momentous charge around this cozy corner of the world? Fetch quests and other basic activities. And that's really the unfortunate thing about it, in that, a movement system this enjoyable highlights a deeper issue with exploration and quest structure. What worth is an endless surf on a wide open ocean if the only reward for exploration is a basic climb and some sparks? I get that its to keep the player on the straight and narrow but I can't help but feel it was lost potential, albeit the scale of the game would've likely ballooned in the process. Even still, I cannot downplay the magic contained within flights to the heavens during battles with the colossal, celestial being that persists all throughout. Or even the rush of stringing from one shadow stalker to another beforehand. The combat might be pretty basic when you actually look at it, but it's enriched so much by surrounding elements.  Also, I thought this had a surprisingly evocative story for a game so short. Characters so real and expressive despite little dialogue and a plot with real tension, real conflict in a sub five-hour container. A lot of it comes down to having a fully voiced cast and stylised characters who are beautifully animated. It really enjoyed it. There's a lot of wonder, lots of curiosity to be had about Strandville and this world buried underneath an endless ocean. In the end, this is a little title with a lot of big ideas and lots of charm but lacks the additional layer of complexity to make it truly great. Doesn't stop it from being well worth the money though. And, in the end, I really wanted more.
_childDocuments_.name: Wavetale

_childDocuments_.review: This is another I would consider mixed.  I did enjoy it, but the full story is only around 5 hours, which even on sale was just under $14US plus tax is a bit low.  There isn't a lot of replayability in the game to warrant the higher cost.Art wise it's a low detail stylized 3D platformer, fairly smooth models but it has a low detail art style that makes it a little more timeless.  There aren't a great deal of added effects, but what's there looks nice.  Reflections and water effects are solid.  Music is pretty good and fitting for the mood of the game.Gameplay is pretty solid.  Sigrid has a good amount of moves and moving around generally feels good to execute.  All movement is available from the start, even before the game teaches it, so if you know the movement or take the time to look through the control mapping, you'll be ahead of the game.  You have a double jump, a run/water dash, an air dash (I don't remember this being taught), a normal and a strong attack, a ground slam attack, a grapple that works to specific targets (including certain monsters), and a dive into the water.  Most of these moves can be chained together and many of them build or preserve speed and momentum for some satisfying traversal.The story is about environmental destruction, with leanings into .  Many of the major characters aside from Sigrid are very unlikable, and I got frustrated doing their bidding.  This includes her grandmother, who is abrasive, dismissive to Sigrid's needs, and overall unpleasant to deal with .The problems include:* Camera issues during a major boss fight, this can cause you to miss jumps or grapples, and since the sequence is timed, makes it more likely to fail and have to start a cycle over again.* Camera is nightmarishly bad in the lead-up to the final section of the game, it's constantly shifting your camera away from the destination when using the provided grapple points.  In addition, the spawn points and movement of the monsters you have to fight leading up to this sequence also makes you very likely to end up in the death fog.* Two sidequests would not spawn their item, one about ⅓'d through the game, the other just before the ending sequence.  The first one I literally checked every island multiple times, even breaking out of the map once, but still never managed to find it.  The second I just didn't bother with as I just felt like finishing.* Pacing isn't too bad, but since there's no real progression of your movement or combat abilities it can feel like more of the same with each new area.  Each zone you move between these particular islands, do some jumping and movement puzzles, collect an item or two, and speak to some npc's then do it again.* Combat isn't super exciting, there are only 4 or 5 different types of normal monsters, a , and a final boss.* The cosmetics don't really have a lot of in-game support.  You only have to buy a cosmetic once in-game, from currency you find scattered around, but there's no in-game menu to change or equip it.  You instead need to change equipment within the shop again, It just feels a little tacked on, even though it's the sole purpose for the currency you gather.For accessibility, there is an FoV slider which is great.  The camera issues in some areas and the speed you can get with some movement may still cause motion sickness issues.  The camera shifting and locking definitely affected my vertigo.  There are a few other accessibility options which might help some people.Overall, I enjoyed it mostly.  I didn't think I got my money's worth, but it was a mostly enjoyable story with very fun movement.  It didn't overstay its welcome, it's just a bit expensive for what you get.  Ran perfectly on my Linux desktop, and I expect that it would perform really well on the SteamDeck too.
_childDocuments_.name: Wavetale

_childDocuments_.review: Before I get into anything, I must say that even from the trailer alone, I loved the concept of Wavetale. I am also a big fan of Zoink's "Lost in Random" and went into this game knowing that a few of them worked on it, that I would recognize some of the voices. With this in mind, it immediately made the game more enjoyable to me personally. But in spite of this, here is an honest review.The premise to the story is neat, but the plot is a little shallow. It didn't quite pack the emotional punch that it could have. I think this is mostly due to the games short playtime. The emphasis on specific scenes and story beats feels slightly misplaced — some pieces of dialogue deserved a cutscene, while some cutscenes could have passed as a quick dialogue. The characters' personalities and motivations are quite convincing however, and the voice actors did a fine job! (Overall, the story is not bad given how short it actually is.)The movement is fast and fluid, and the transitions from running, to gliding, to surfing, to grappling feels graceful and smooth. This fast-paced movement encourages exploration, and makes collecting more fun. Unfortunately, the objectives throughout the game lack variety, feeling a little monotonous after a while. The music was rather enjoyable! It fit the world and the atmosphere well, and really helped set the mood for the game. (And come on — adaptive music is always cool!)The combat is pretty straightforward and easy. I found it becomes slightly monotonous after a while, the various enemies posing no significant threat at any point in the game. If you're more of a casual player, this may not bother you. The challenge in Wavetale lies more in its platforming than its combat.[h5]Story: 2/5[/h5] Neat world and concept. Convincing character personalities! Had some good moments, but too short to tell a full story. Felt a little shallow.[h5]Art: 3/5[/h5] Beautiful graphics! The sights don't disappoint.[h5]Music: 3/5[/h5] Enjoyable! The adaptive soundtracks are quite fitting to the game's atmosphere. Set the mood well![h5]Gameplay: 3/5[/h5]Easily the highlight of the game! Fast-paced, fluid movement that encourages exploration.[h5]Combat: 1/5[/h5] Simple. Slightly monotonous, and not very challenging. (This may not bother some people. This was just my experience.)Encountered a semi-frequent bug where the audio and/or game would freeze for a few seconds. The game never crashed, however, so it didn't bother me too badly. Not sure if anyone else had this problem. Definitely not worth the asking price for most people, but worth snagging during a sale in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: ( full review with screenshots:  )Wavetale is something like Gravity Rush by way of a 2000s platformer. Its art style, story, setting, combat, and movement are all very similar to Gravity Rush in roughly descending order. The 2000s platformer comparison comes from its puzzles and boss fights, which will feel familiar if you've played Ratchet & Clank, Battle for Bikini Bottom, etc. If you haven't played Gravity Rush or any of those games, you're getting a cartoony post apocalyptic game about a girl with magic powers sliding and jumping around vaguely Victorian ruins and slamming into enemies to kill them. It's not very original, but it works. Wavetale isn't explicitly advertised as a kid's game, but I think it's best to go into it knowing that it easily could be one. The combat and platforming are incredibly easy and the story, while surprisingly well done, could easily work as a Saturday morning cartoon. I don't think there's anything here that will give more experienced players even a hint of trouble, so it'll have to be the story or movement that carries the game for you. The main criticism I've seen of it is that it's too short, which is hard to argue against for a game that takes 3.5 hours and costs $30. It's definitely at least twice as expensive as it should be, which unfortunately also really hurts its value as a kid's game. That said, I think the real flaw is the price rather than the length. As short as it is, the runtime feels almost perfect for what this game has to offer, and I don't think they could've extended it without a bunch of pointless padding. Sales will be your friend here. Provided you can get it for 50% or so off (I got it for $13.49) and don't mind a very low difficulty, this is a pretty easy recommendation. The optional content is not worth bothering with at all, so unless you're playing with very young kids, I don't think you can get much more than 3-4 hours out of it. If an afternoon or weekend's worth of lighthearted story and fun movement sounds good to you, give it a look.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Movement is super satisfying, the game is short but replayable, soundtrack is incredible and the vibe of the whole game is super chill, reminds me a lot of Sable. The customisation is basic but fun, although some more things to spend the abundance of sparklings you collect would have been nice.Cons: Writing is at best on the nose and at worst kind of cringey, the story was extremely predictable (not necessarily a bad thing but the game isn't going to challenge anyone's world view). The voice acting was also fairly hit/miss, some of it is great while sometimes it feels very forced. The game is also extremely linear aside from the occasional fetch quest, which makes the world feel very empty. Linear games are also fine, but you've got this incredible movement on the water and the platforming is very fluid, why not let us do more of it? Even if its just for some collectibles or something, there should have been so much more to do and explore. Also, combat is boiled down to spamming the attack button until monsters die. Combat against striders is much more interesting, however, and more sea based combat could have been a fun way to spice things up.Overall would give a 6.5 out of 10, it's a very satisfying game to play and the movement is some of the best in any game I've played, but because of how short the game is (finished in just over 4 hours), I would struggle to recommend buying at full price. I picked it up on sale and suggest others do the same. It's a chill way to spend an afternoon or two, but nothing more.

_childDocuments_.review: What is Wavetale? It's 3D-era Sonic the Hedgehog plopped in the setting of The Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker ... without  the sailing. And if that sounds like the most Xer description of a video game ever, you're welcome.The main attraction here, like any Sonic game, is the movement. Sigrid is massively overpowered. She glides like greased lightning across the water, jumps like she's strapped to solid rocket boosters, and hovers like an attack helicopter. Her attacks stagger enemies into helplessness, regardless of their power level, and she gets a grappling hook right our of the gate, immediately accessing all of the game's roller coaster troughs and speed inducing warp ... thingies. All of Sigrid's moves are available from the start, making this an ideal speedrunning festival of exploit obnoxiousness.And that's good, because there's only 5 hours of content to exploit here. Wavetale's story is exceedingly brief, but it is delivered with such grounded and relatable voice acting that it doesn't feel slight. The superb performances allowed the developers to imbue their aphoristic characters with more life, roundness, and motivation in this short window than Alloy received in all of 1164 hours of Horizon: Zero Dawn. The themes of generational divide, environmental recovery, and post-apocalyptic recovery resonate, even if the story gallops along with exposition dumps and hurried conclusions.It's worth putting up with Wavetail's repetitive, uninteresting objectives (go to the thing, hit the switch, kill weak enemies, repeat) to experience it's acting and bare-bones, yet effective, face texture animation. Give this team more resources for their next project, and we could see Great Things.

_childDocuments_.review: The art style is absolutely gorgeous and the soundtrack is also quite beautiful. Wavetale also tells a very nice story, and I enjoyed happening upon Journal Entries so I could see Sigrid's inner thoughts about the things she did. However, as a game, Wavetale is very lacking. While building up momentum is satisfying, the platforming is kind of dull otherwise. Sidequests give no hint as to where the needed item/person is, combat is boring and clearly an after thought: most of it is skippable and in the final fight, you can get stunlocked into oblivion when the boss summons a group of enemies. It's also one of those games where for some damn reason, the only way to save is through autosave checkpoints, but the game does not bother to tell you when the last save was.Just playing the story is very quickly done, though, so if you wanna experience it plus the music and artstyle, get it while it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A pleasant platformer with a lovely aesthetic but that's often underwhelming and maybe a touch too simple in many areas. Movement and whatnot feel excellent, yet nothing is done to stretch the potential of that promising system. While it's nice that you begin the game with a decent set of abilities, it's a shame that you end that game having never expanded upon that moveset. A lot of Wavetale consists of going to a place to flip a switch to activate another switch that also needs flipping. The old "backup generator" routine doesn't make for a compelling objective and is even more inauthentic when it's used ad nauseam. Combat is fairly standard and enemies can be ignored ninety percent of the time. Enemy variety is nothing to write home about either. Riding the waves is pretty stylish but it often amounts to little more than holding up and RT for a while. The collectible that you acquire is only used for cosmetics, which makes pursuing it feel rather hollow. Still, I found myself enjoying the time I spent with Wavetale. It's quite nice to play something that just lets you platform around while progressing a competent narrative amidst some appealing oceanic scenery and calming music. It would've been more fair to lower my 'game-y' expectations going into Wavetale. Instead, I've come to appreciate how Wavetale excels as a low-stakes, short-form, solid-fundmentals platformer.
_childDocuments_.name: Wavetale

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this is a game which knows exactly what story it’s trying to tell and goes that extra mile to present it in a visually satisfying way whilst making the voyage across it’s waves a satisfying one. _childDocuments_.review: Found this purely by chance, and ended up playing & finishing it in one sitting.I definitely recommend it for an afternoon's play, but I do feel there are some flaws:1) While Sigrid herself sounds great, some of the voice actors' delivery is incredibly phoned-in. The less significant the character is, the more their voice starts to sound like the VA won the role in a cereal box.2) Various bugs that shouldn't be in a $30 game, such as the ground-collision randomly screwing up and causing Sigrid to always stand like she's on a slope, side-quest descriptions being listed twice, and enemies respawning in midair but being inactive if you revisit a scripted area.3) The game overall feels too short, with not enough to do in terms of side-quests. It feels like a whole bunch of wasted areas that could've held more objectives and replay value.4) Sigrid's model having no toes in the MANY closeups of her feet, even though she clearly has them in the 2D artwork, gives me that "uncanny-valley" vibe. It's off-putting and weird, and even with the cartoony art style, this just feels incredibly lazy on the part of whoever did the 3D modelling.5) Various inconsistencies in character art, from skin tones being different between models to faces being drawn COMPLETELY differently, which you would think would've been more of a focus in a game that's going for a specific art aesthetic.6) Probably more of a cultural "we don't want to be ostracized in our career or friend circle so we'll just do what's currently-palatable" issue with how Sweden has been the last decade or so, but not a single mention of - or allusion to - Sigrid's father. Not even one. On top of that, the only two white male characters who aren't evil, stupid, cowardly or kids are either dead or have too much PTSD to be of any help. A little... weird, to say the least, given the "current climate".Overall, a good game, my recommendation is only marred by these easily-avoidable - and easily-fixable - issues. If they can fix some of these problems, I may update my review, but for now I'll leave it at "get it on sale and enjoy."

Voice acting was great, especially from the lead.The games a little unpolished and quite short for £25 but great fun nonetheless. I would've liked a little more put into the combat mechanically. _childDocuments_.review: I went looking for a game that gave e the same feels as Super Mario Sunshine; I think I found one. This is a beautifully visual and blessedly sonorous game. The music by itself is worth listening to over and over again; I cannot overstate how much I enjoy the music and the atmosphere it creates. I love the world and the free-roaming exploration. Really glad I bought and played this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wavetale

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet action platformer about the coming of age of our protagonist Siggy and a story about taking care of the world we live in.The combat and platforming are very easy and I personally would have liked to be a little more challenged, but i feel like it the platforming especially was focused more on momentum, with lots of points to grapple onto and shoot you forward.A very large part of the gameplay also consists of surfing across a wavy ocean akin to Windwaker.It's pretty fun to to get into a rythm of diving underwater to build up speed and then shoot out into the air with lots of speed only to dive back down to build up speed again.The simplicity of the gameplay doesn't overstay it's welcome since the game is beatable in around 5 hours.A big part of the appeal is also the gorgeous visuals, underlined by a surprisingly great soundtrack.If you enjoy a very laid back platformer with a nice story and beautiful presentation I highly recommend checking out Wavetale.
_childDocuments_.name: Wavetale

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. I love the story, the style, the charachters and the action. Surfing over the waves is quite thrilling, so is discovering all the islands. It's not a long game, but that's okay, because this way it's short enough to play it again. Negative point: at times the camera can get really annoying. But it didn't ruin the game for me.

_childDocuments_.review: wavetale is a very pleasant little game. the story is only a few hours long, you may consider it too expensive for the time if thats how you judge a video game, but i would gladly have paid full price for it, i picked it up during the summer sale. it has a couple bugs here and there but overall the game has a beautiful art style, and feels incredible to move around in. the combat is simplistic, but thats not really what the game is about and it gives you enough tools for it to not feel like a drag in the parts of the game where its necessary. 8/10 but incredibly memorable, and will probably be playing again multiple times. might learn how to speedrun it.
