_childDocuments_.review: One of those games that sucks because its too short, but before you buy it lets keep this in mind:Pros:* Art is fine. The real touch is the face expression. Its vivid and trembling with a lot of focus in the eyes. I'm pretty sure I've seen this style in old animations. French maybe? It does reminds me of Tin Tin drawing looks.* Core game mechanic makes you feel like you're in a water park. They really nailed the physics for "surfing".  Making the game truly enjoyable just by "surfing" around. And *.* * Using the slides + the camera really makes the motion incredible. Its like Tony Hawks Pro Skater on the water, but **.* The story isn't superb, but its alright and enjoyable. The face expressions and voice acting also adds to it. Its the usual adult tantrum trope. i.e. Kids cry when they want something or don't get said something. Adults destroy or harm others.* One thing I find superb is the wave mechanics. You really feel the ups and downs and they really nailed the transition from water to land when you have high/low tides. This is particularly true when you're surfing like nuts and you actually have to pay attention to hidden islands.* Free roam mode, but ***.Cons:* ** The camera can be wonky sometime. Auto-changing to some weird places like when you're close to the black fogs, etc.* *** Not much to do besides getting hiddens or doing the time attacks tracks.* Object collision isn't polished and can lead to some wonky stuff.* Game crashed near the end, but that only happened once.* Awfully short.* Combat is there, but is meh. Unless you dash-jump-glide-hit like a cyberpunk junkie.The game is worth just because of the wave-surfing physics. Never seen anything like it. Its not particularly challenging, but is extremely enjoyable play. And it does have potential to be something more. Maybe they will make a Wavetale II with Pro Skater like stuff, scoreboard/online content, etc. Also you're looking for 4ish hours of gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Wavetale

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to love this game, I really enjoy the story, music and artsyle, but wow is it rough around the edges.Camera is a little jank, the max speed is too slow for my taste and (most importantly) there's no re-center button, just an "Aim" button which I've found absolutely useless.There is no Anti-Aliasing it seems, so enjoy your steppy edges or force some through ReShade (if you could make the AA there work, I couldn't) or your GPU drivers. 21:9 was also not very well supported, the camera seems to handle it fine, but all the UI is cut off at the top and bottom, so you have to at minimum switch to 16:9 just to read some button prompts in menus.Collision can be a bit janky, I've gotten completely stuck once, forcing me to reload the save, and it felt like I almost got stuck a few times too.I've seen some complain that the combat is too plain, but I honestly don't mind it being not more than just mashing X at the enemy, although the only reason for the Y button/heavy attack to exists comes up quite late into the game, I never actually used it in combat because of all that recovery time.Having no dedicated use button can feel weird sometimes, you just attack everything .
_childDocuments_.name: Wavetale

_childDocuments_.review: Picked this up on a whim when it was on sale. Tbh honest i typically don't play games like this as i don't like how once you see the story, that's all there is to see. However this one will forever stand out as an exception to the rule. The story was well more than enough to make me come back for multiple runs, but between each i still find myself spending my time just surfing on the waters and admiring the gorgeous, extremely smooth movement, and memorable soundtrack. If you haven't played it yet, you should do it at least once. It'll warm your heart.
_childDocuments_.name: Wavetale

_childDocuments_.review: Wavetale is a vibes game. It nails the tone, the art, the MUSIC (it REALLY nails the music), and the feel. Running dashing and jumping all feel great and fluid and expressive and all that jazz. However, it's half baked. Not that what's here is bad or anything, I'm actually confident that everyone involved in the game was phenomenal, and contributed whole-heartedly. The care and quality show. It just didn't get the time it deserved. There are little threads that show just how much of this game was cut in development. Story threads that hardly get the time to set themselves up (much less resolve successfully), gameplay features that clearly got cut (left trigger makes you aim for some reason? Never used for anything), and a campaign that hurtles headlong into the finish line just minutes after building up intrigue.If this were an early access game with more updates planned to flesh it out, I would whole heartedly recommend it. In its current state, it just doesn't hold up to the $25 price tag. I hope Thunderful can come back to this project, because it is SO SO SO close to being up there as one of my favorite platformers of all time.

_childDocuments_.review: Very cozy, cute artstyle and the movement feels great. Zipping around the map makes you feel like a speedrunner, even though it's almost effortless. Some of the best voice acting I've heard in an indie game.Edit: Steam shows that I played <3 hours, but it actually took me a bit over 4 hours to finish the main story, though I skipped a few side quests.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely wonderful game!If I have to give an outta 10 rating, I'd give it a 10/10 due to how good the movement feels +  purely selfish reasons of being reminded of wonderful games like Rayman (gliding fun).Pros:- Really nice art style with beautiful locations- Really good music with really fluid switches when action starts or when you move between areas.- Movement is great with a great sense of momentum.- The locations are really fun to explore and jump around, besides being beautiful.- Very pleasant world building. You have a lil' sketchbook that shows some extra info about locations. Here's where I'll also mention picking up sketches doesn't throw you into a menu which is a definite plus.- The story is very good. Goes for the feels quite often but not in an overbearing way. Cursing, mostly from Grandma, is also funny rather than just stale.- Other jokes are also funny.- Length may be a con given the price tag, but none of the things you do are filler. Quests are usually just "Go and pick this up" but they're really an excuse for going into the various platforming sections, so I can allow it.Cons:- Quite a big price tag for the length, I waited until completing the story to write the review, and it took me about 4 hours (may say a bit more cuz I got it open to fact check the things I'm writing). Don't think I explored everything and as of posting I don't have all the achievements, so I imagine there may be half an hour more to this. Replayability varies. Again no filler so it's 4 hour-ish of just fun.- I feel some mechanics were underutilized at times. I don't think the dash mechanic even ever got its own tutorial bubble, which is a shame because it really is what makes the movement system complete. There's a few sections where you're kinda just pressing the "grapple" button to pull to predetermined points, it looks cool, but it's gotten a bit old with how many games use it. Those same sections can also be completed by just chaining jumps, glides and dashes, which the game also expects you to do in other places, and I think is way cooler. I wouldn't say this is that bad, cuz you have the option to do it the latter way.Doesn't really matter:- Combat isn't really a big focus and it's mostly wacking things with the net repeatedly. Enemies don't have a lotta health and you can just run right past them most of the time so it isn't an issue.- The music takes a while to start so sometimes you might stay in silence for a lil' while, don't go into audio settings just yet.- Replayabilty varies, the locations are still fun to jump around even if you've seen them, but there's no specific feature I'd say would MAKE you wanna replay it.

_childDocuments_.review: Smooth and fluid movement mechanics, a quaint yet wonderful soundtrack of adaptive music, and a simple yet heartfelt main story, this game is perfect for a relaxed/casual playthrough. Combat isn't particularly difficult, but personally I find it to be a side part to the gorgeous ocean environments and ruins with an artstyle akin to Wind Waker and old hand drawn comics. In regards to it's other aspects I would say it isn't perfect. Side quests are frequently found throughout the world but overall don't have much substance to them, and the only reward you seem to get is currency for cosmetics, which isn't a terrible award in and of itself given their nature, so I don't mind it too much. Despite the beautifully stylized environments and characters, functionally there are some places that need polishing, especially in regards to platforming, where you may sometimes clip through solid objects when attempting to get to an objective. Additionally the physics of the boat vessels could use some work seeming more natural. But these are minor nitpicks at best and don't take away from the overall experience too much. Assuming this was the game studio's first venture, they hit the nail in almost everywhere else in terms of quality.All in all, if you're looking for a quick and easy, yet entertaining and immersive open world-ish game, and don't mind the occasional minor bug here and there, Wavetale is for you! Keep your spark shining, surfers.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying, I understand everyone's qualms about the pricing, however you should definitely wishlist it to be notified when it has a bigger discount! The movement is very fun, going from gliding across the waves to launching onto an island a smacking the gloom is really satisfying! The artstyle is great and the music gets you into the vibe the whole game! Like people have said, it really is a short game depending on if you explore around and do the little fetch quests, it takes roughly 4-6hrs to complete. TLDR: Fun and satisfying movement, great visuals and music, takes around 4-6hrs to complete. Would definitely recommend getting it when it's on sale!

_childDocuments_.review: The visual design is great, the movement is fluid and satisfying, the story and lore are compelling, the voice acting and cutscene direction are great... but man, I wish there was more to it. The gameplay loop is pretty cool for about the first hour, until you realize... that is all there is. The platforming never meaningfully develops past what you do in the first leg of the game, the combat is bare bones and basically a space filler, there are some cool platforming setpieces throughout but between them is a lot of samey-looking islands with samey-looking buildings and samey-feeling platforming where you fight the same enemies over and over again... the game is not long but even then the gameplay feels a bit stretched thin at spots.There's also not much in the way of side-content - you can buy outfits, there are diary pages and quests to do (all of which reward you with money to buy outfits, the only thing you can buy), and there are some pretty cool races, but only, like, a few of them... the game's not very focused on exploration, either. Islands are littered with switches that only activate when the plot demands it, the large, open map is secretly just a linear tunnel that moves around in a lot of different directions, this is all inherently fine enough but it just leaves the game feeling very bare-bones, like, they had a good story, they had a good movement system, but the content to make the two meet just wasn't there. Pair that with a really basic, ugly menu screen with relatively minimal graphics options and it ends up feeling... weirdly unfinished, for a game that's technically been out for a year?And yeah, no, this game is beautiful to look at but it lacks both the polish and depth I'd expect out of a game at its price point.I like this game, I really do, but I wanted to love it, and even if I found the story compelling enough to follow through on it, I still come away from it a liiiittle disappointed it didn't have more to offer. Wait for a sale, it's worth playing, just... don't expect the next best game ever, either.

_childDocuments_.review:
Surf the waters of a submerged city! Unravel the past, save the islanders from mysterious sea monsters and discover secrets hidden under the surface.

Explore an open sea and the decaying archipelago of Strandville in Wavetale, a story-driven action-adventure game introducing you to fed-up fishermen, secretive hermits - and maybe a pirate or two. Traverse calm waters and surging waves as Sigrid, a young girl who befriends a mysterious shadow that provides her with the power to walk on water.

Speed through the waves, swing yourself from housetops with your net, and defeat an old nemesis to save the citizens of the islands. All with a bit of help from the shadows down below - and your cranky grandmother.

name: Chivalry 2
detailed_description: JOIN OUR DISCORD Steam Exclusive Offer Special Edition King's Edition About the Game Return to the ultimate medieval battlefield! Chivalry 2 is a multiplayer first person slasher inspired by epic medieval movie battles. Players are thrust into the action of every iconic moment of the era - from clashing swords, to storms of flaming arrows, to sprawling castle sieges and more. Dominate massive, 64-player battlefields. Catapults tear the earth apart as you lay siege to castles, set fire to villages and slaughter filthy peasants in the return of Team Objective maps. A fully featured mounted combat system makes you feel like you are fighting atop a thousand pound beast of war, including the ability to trample your foes, land devastating front or rear horse kicks, unhorse your opponent with a lance and engage in deep melee combat with grounded or mounted opponents. Rise to glory and expand your arsenal with a new subclass system that provides more variety than ever before. Four base classes expand to 10+ subclasses and over 30 unique weapons, each with multiple visual variants. New support items ranging from oil pots to barricades, supply crates and archer’s stakes add even more tactical options to the battlefield. Charge to battle alongside your friends with all-platform Crossplay and claim glory by your blade!

_childDocuments_.review: If I could partially recommend Chivalry 2, I would.  The meat of Chivalry 2 - it's combat - is unique and hard to find anywhere else. My victories are often glorious, and my defeats often earned. . . in fights, at least: the same could not be said of the team-based objectives. The game invites you to have a good time, not a consistent time. So long as you can stomach watching success crumbling away as your team ignores the objective or a single enemy claims it, you can have a great time.What we're in for is - as advertised - the cinematic medieval combat experience. Teams of warriors from shining knights to fearsome berserkers charging against each other to claim victory on a variety of maps with a wide variety of weapons. Whether you want to embody the fantasy of landing an arrow through a far-away eye slit in a helmet, or to lead a charge as your mighty hammer compacts some poor spearman.As someone who has always appreciated the more historically present polearms, hammers, and axes from medieval eras, I'm glad to say that Chivalry won't leave you wanting. The wide variety of weapons is a joy to unlock and experiment with, to the point that the meta can be safely ignored in favor of what feels the most fun for you, with no worry that a one-handed mace functions identically to a one-handed sword. A variety of different ways to avoid damage through artful dodges or expert ripostes makes defense just as engaging at the ways you can return damage through quick off-hand jabs, stabs, or just outright throwing your weapon.My primary issue with the game is that its design seems . . . confused, as-if a different team has worked on each update:A recent map has an objective of setting explosive black-powder charges against an enemy structure. The defending team can defuse these, preventing mindless suicide rushes. The other two incarnations of this objective type have no defuse option, meaning it's a case of keeping mindless drones from getting anywhere within six feet of a wide objective and instantly invalidating fighting for your life to hold-off three or five enemies at once.Siege weapons are also spread across different maps, though inconsistently. This results in narrow bridges with no way to utilize catapults or ballista to clear them. Other maps may have three ballista for defense against a moving caravan but no ballista for a stationary defense point, which leads a castle door that could be broken with slow, dangerous bombs . . . or the two catapults on the other side of the battlefield from the defenders which can be rebuilt (if destroyed) in under five seconds, resulting in a penultimate hold point which lasts only a few minutes as defenders can't hope to run across an entire battlefield to destroy one of two catapults, which can be rebuilt three times as fast as the defender can respawn.These above two issues often lead to the highly-skilled members of either team switching to the one with the best chances of winning, leading to predictable scoreboards where the best players on the opposite team may have levels ranging from one hundred to five hundred, while you were abandoned to fight along people with far less experience who only have a few dozen levels. Many of the classes have overlap in weapons which makes very little sense. The Footman with the polearm skill tree may cannot use the falchion sidearm that their subclass can use. The knight with a shield subclass can use a one-handed spear, but the footman's shield subclass cannot, despite the polearm footman having access to the two-handed spear.  The heavy knight and polearm vanguard can both use the two-handed hammer, but the polearm vanguard cannot use the poleaxe the knight gets, nor can the heavy vanguard use the heavy mace of the knight. The archer - the ranged class - gets a knife or other sidearm in case they are ambushed or caught out of position. The engineer - who is not a ranged class - is meant to be in melee, but does not get a sidearm: this means that they will be defending their buildings with weapons that deal bonus damage to buildings (their own included) without any back-up in case they lose their primary weapon: the only class in the entire game to have this issue.Finally is the release of cosmetic or map-based content. . . it's inconsistent. Many pieces of armor will not show your heraldry (a cool design you can get for your armor) at all, or put another design over it, or are painted with no complimentary armor set that has the same paint-scheme: meaning a bright-red checkerboard or bright-blue stripes on a helmet may have no way to make them consistent with the rest of the outfit. A third faction was added with between one or three sets of armor per class and no heraldry to set them apart from eachother, as opposed to the four or more sets of armor per class in the main two factions, and dozens of different identifying heraldries.

_childDocuments_.review: Game breaking glitches that will never be fixed, lets just add more broken maps and broken hit boxes. This game has everything else to make it so fun, but the glaring glitches and clipping issues on maps just makes it un-fun to play or can just make you tilt off the planet. I honestly worry for my mental health when I play this game, no other game makes me as upset as this one can, because of moments where my hit won't land, or somehow the enemy has timing advantage despite weapon speed, or i get caught on some badly clipped rock or stone that prevents my character from moving in any direction, or situations where my teammate is downed but because of some revive glitch I cannot lift him back up and just watch him die before my eyes.At least in other games when I get upset, it is at my opponent or maybe a weapon is overpowered and should be nerfed, or cheaters, etc. But with this game there have been too many times where I have actually felt CHEATED out of winning a duel or fight because of a glitch. Every dev diary is just mentioning new maps and new content, nothing about addressing issues like where the siege ramps don't properly fold out and cause players to get clipped at the top, etc. Honestly pretty disappointing when there are so many glaring issues with this game engine and how it interacts with the game. Like trying to throw a med kit to a teammate, the engine is so broken and the hitboxes are so messed up that if you accidentally misthrow even SLIGHTLY, your medkit will go flying in the total opposite direction or just bounce flying in some random direction if it hits a teammate with full health. How is something so basic like this still in the game? Why not just have the med kits deaden upon impact and fall to the ground and stay there? at least i could pick them back up and try throwing them again. Another situation that is similar is if a teammate blows their trumpet/horn to heal their teammates at the same time as you, thus negating the effect of your horn and only one of you gets points. There shouldn't be situations where you just waste your trumpet if no teammates can even be healed, it should at least come back half full if not a single person is healed, thus allowing you to get it faster, or something else that can balance this effect. Sometimes the refresh can be minutes on this, just making it that much more irritating when it happens.I could go on and on, but the point being that I'm sure many of these issues have been around since the start of the game and it doesn't feel like they ever plan on being addressed. I've honestly decided to uninstall this game and no longer play it until I hear about some progress being made on these glaring issues for the actual gameplay and balance between teams. If some progress is made on this, I would be more than happy to change this to a positive review! The gore is fun, the humor is dark, the voice acting is both amazing and terrible, mostly in good ways but maybe re-record some of them? they actually sound like they are recorded on different quality microphones for some of the base voices... (The voice acting itself is great, I'll miss being the Highlander!!!)

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of speaking this game is worth mostly 10 bucks. It is an early access, where developers seek to understand the balance of created game.If you are really into medieval war games, like War of Roses, I definitely suggest waiting for upcoming patches and discounts.As I am pretty disappointed with the value and cost balance of this game, I will describe full list of features that require updates to be able to enjoy the game without feeling that rage tickle in your head.1. To start with, you have no ability to customize gamestyle to your needs. There are no scalable abilities, weapons or runes, buffs. This game has raw medieval weapon slaughter playstyle, that either you hate it or love it. But here comes the sad part. The only weapon and class customization that the game provides are separated by levels. And to max out certain class or selected weapon, you have to play at least 30+ hours on the same class. This really sucks, since there is no different approach to provided weapons and you are continuously stuck with playing one weapon (trying to get that crispy 20 lvl. sword).2. Limited actions. In a game of war, where you need to get your head straight fighting skilled players, you are faced with action delay (healing, swinging, canceling). This one is simple, without spamming the needed key during the battle to activate your slow heal or cancel a swing/shot - developers have to implement queue actions (Swing -> Cancel -> Swing) with a delay in game, but not on players output end (we wanna to see the result playing the game, not to expect it to happen someday while spamming the required button).3. Balance issues. Probably the biggest flaw, that stops this game is ranged class. The game mechanics works pretty well, it handles easily. Despite that, the damage of the arrow or bolt does not compensate the time needed to aim, shoot and reload. It is realistic game, shooting enemies are as hard as it gets, but hitting them rewards you with nothing.Quick example: with most melees you can swing for 80+ damage most of the time per half a second, with ranged - you can hit 30 for a body shot and 80+ for a headshot in 2-3 seconds. Let me add, that all melee weapons have AoE, which means, they could swing thru 3 players with 100+ damage, whilst ranged unit will do ~35% damage of any other class during the whole match.4. Finally, the vision. During this release, game has 4 playable game modes and a selection of insanely developed maps. However, the game is repetitive, scoring system is based more on killing rather than doing actual quests, there are no possible ranked matches and lastly, as I mentioned before, after 5-10 hours you will get the hang of it and start choosing your main class. However, good luck grinding for last weapon in the class as it demans not a skill, but time - actual physical time.All in all, if you are looking for a 10 hour lifetime experience for 30+ dollars, give it a try - why not. At the end of the day, the game is unique and offers something we have not seen in decades. But I would definitely urge you to wait for game updates, fixes and balances.

_childDocuments_.review: Played this on the free weekend. This is a lot of fun! Combat is hard to master, and if I were to get serious I would probably remap the attack keys. Using the scroll wheel to attack is a bit ridiculous. In fact using a controller would be a very good idea to turn the right way to get the blows to hit faster.I couldn't complete the final stage of the tutorial where you have to turn quickly to hit faster. For some reason the attacks weren't chaining. Could be that this feature is more optimised for controller inputs than pc/mouse?Anyway, once you're in the battle being good at 1v1 combat is only half the battle - literally. There are different phases to an assault, overwatch style, and in some phases it is better to switch out to an archer and pick off enemies at range, or to pick a close range build and go in swinging. Battlefield awareness is also key, especially if your combat skills are not great. You can often help out someone else to 2v1 an unsuspecting enemy.The graphics are beautiful and the weapons and armour are very detailed. There's even a character editor with quite a few customisation options, even though your face is behind a helm most of the time.Other players are really nice. Lots of 'gg's after each match. There's a feature where you can commend someone who killed you, which is a nice touch when you get into a long 1v1 exchange and someone uses genuine skill to take you down, or an archer pulls off a long range snipe.The combat damage is gory and quite hilarious at times. One time my right arm got cut off, but I wasn't immediately killed so I wandered around the battlefield for a minute or so until I bled out! Overall a really fun experience :)

_childDocuments_.review: Hackers are running rampant in this game and the devs have no intention of doing anything about it. Their anti-cheat is straight garbage. Anybody can just load up Cheat Engine and use the speedhack even if its just slight. I've never seen people swing the heaviest weapons imaginable in the game like they are toothpicks so much in my life. It definitely doesn't help how people who are outright worse than you are doing the most trash talk and there's no easy way to report them. Not like they'll get punished for it anyway. I've encountered a severe amount of one shot hacks being used as well. I'm running around as a Knight - the tankier class - getting one shot by a knife, sword or insta dying to fire pots while I'm at full health and the fire damage comes up as "4 damage". Implying I only had 4 HP at full health. Let's not forget, if you try calling out cheaters, you signed your own death warrant with everybody because they will immediately dogpile on you in chat and votekick spam you. I've also encountered infinite health hacks being used by a lot of people as well as infinite stamina and infinite weapon durability. When you have one guy surrounded by 6 people wailing on them and not only are they not dying, but they're constantly blocking with their weapon, not even parrying or doing any kind of evading. Then they take a single swing start one shotting everybody.I've encountered teleportation hacks that allow people to appear wherever they want, whenever they want. I had this happen in an AI match no less to end off a night of doing 64 man team objective. The game loves to respawn you half way across the planet, so it's incredibly unrealistic to compete objectives in some portions of maps. Me and 2 others noticed another player on the other team teleport into existence, conveniently in the exact spot needed to compete taking over a bridge and proceeded to clear 7 of us on the point like it was nothing. One shot, infinite stamina and health. I've encountered countless people that run through several oil pots and never ignite or lose health and they will even stand in the fire and take no damage and proceed to one shot your 130+ health class with a 70 damage non-heavy attack while you're at full health. I've encountered more people that phase through my maul swings. I see my maul physically go through someone's torso. Completely missing them and that same person one shots me with a dagger or a polearm while I'm at full health. People are hitting me through my block. People are 360 auto-blocking. Just to list a couple severe issues that prevent you from playing the game.This is the second time in a row they took a game with huge potential and ruined it miserably with sheer neglect. It's absurd how little the devs care about this game. It's appalling. This game doesn't remotely deserve it's positive status. Steam reviews are a cancer. _childDocuments_.review: I entered this game expecting to feel like a brave knight, but I actually feel like a sack of potatoes with a sword. Health is basically a suggestion, and combat is a mix between dancing in armor and trying to open a door while blindfolded. this game is the most authentic medieval experience you can get, if what you’re looking for is a quick, painful death while your friends laugh at how you fell trying to jump over a fence.The first 10 minutes were just me trying to hit someone, miserably failing, and then falling to the ground. It’s like a workplace accident simulator, but with swords, though it becomes incredibly dynamic once you realize that all you need to do is run around like a maniac with no plan other than not losing your head (literally). But the worst part? The archers. There’s always one perched up high, with a radar that somehow locks directly onto my face, because they've decided I’m the perfect target. No matter how well you’re playing, there’s a 90% chance you’ll end the match with an arrow between your eyes, courtesy of some guy with way too much patience.

_childDocuments_.review: Chivalry 2 by far has been the most enjoyable and joyous game I’ve played in awhile. Through my life primarily playing first person shooters, Chivalry brings a new light into PvP rather than your typical “aim and shoot”. Close quarter combat with shields, two-handed axes and spears piercing through your opponents head. All while trying to perfecting your movement, range and timing of your attack balancing and honing your defensive and offensive skills is more satisfying than ever. In my case, the skill gap in Chivalry compared to your typical first person shooter is different is not only immersively different. But does an absolutely brilliant job capturing a true chaotic battlefield that romanticizing medieval times. Love slaying heads!10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Im not particularly good at writing reviews so ill keep this short and sweet while bringing attention to the traits that most other Medieval Slasher games struggle with. Where Chivalry greatly excels over Mordhau is maps and its onboarding for new players, while new players can still be mopped up by veterans, a veteran will use kicks, bashes, feints and dodges to beat a new player, while a Mordhau veteran can simply break the animations to excel or drag until your parry runs out. Did I enjoy Mordhau sales and absolutely cleaning up on the newbies? Of course I did but I think Chivalry has finally solved the "fights that look like real fights" issue and all it took was allowing players to hold a block.

_childDocuments_.review: After 45 hours of Team Objective and dueling (with a 50/50% split) these are the negatives i noticed, that ultimately made me not interested in the game anymore. Teammate indicators are tiny, easily blend in, and just disappear 5-10 meters away. That makes reading the battlefield unnecessary hard. 3rd person view helps but has a fixed narrow FOV that looks very bad. Big battles are rarely a line vs line, and more often dudes trying to run around and backstab as much as possible, or 2-3 players ganking on some dude that is separated from his team. This tactic or flow would be fine if it wasn't so much reinforced by movement mechanics and bad team indicators (1st point). Movement mechanics problems are: very fast top speed (it builds up when holding W), and very slow low speed (first steps forward, or walking sideways/back). The battles look like everybody is a cavalry unit: they hit & run through, circle around to hit unsuspecting enemies. If you're in melee range, its very hard to disengage to seek your team, and there's also a catch up mechanic that gives speed boost to chasers. The incoming enemies with top speed will make sure you're gangbanged thoroughly, and you're entirely dependent on teammates either helping you or running off. Unoptimized controls. Can't bind "dash" to separate key (its merged with "jump"). Why when i press "Slash attack" two times in a quick succession, it doesn't do a "Slash" -> "feint into Alt Slash"? It should at least be a toggle-able setting. Its inconsistent, because pressing "Slash" then "Overhead" makes you feint without the need for Alt Attack Modifier. Same thing with countering, if i'm doing "Counter->feint into Counter" with the same attack type, just make me press the same attack type again (why do i need to use "Alt Attack Modifier"). For countering, at least i found a fix for this: bind both "Alt Attack Modifier" and "Parry" to RMB - that way you do first counter (alt modifier on), release RMB and can do a second counter just by pressing attack. HUD: no mod support to change it. Health and stamina are bottom left, too far from center of attention. Slow, muddy and clunky feel of combat. The thing i most hate is the mouse sensitivity limiter during attack release. I understand why limiter is there, but its just a band-aid fix, and there are other ways to achieve good looking combat.Because of sensitivity limit, you kinda need a huge mousepad.When i see a very slow attack / drag, that hits like a truck, it immediately breaks immersion. Someone gently touches me with a hammer or axe, and i lose half of my health. Feels like going into parry isn't instant, and there's a delay after you drop a parry, where you cant do anything and can still get hit or kicked to guardbreak (maybe the game isn't meant to be enjoyable for 50+ ping). Attacker advantage in TO. All map stages except the last one, are almost guaranteed to be lost by defenders => feels lame to even try to defend them, feels so artificial, like a sightseeing tour. On the other hand, playing attack is more fun cause you have more chance to wipe the opposition and push through like a hero.Attacker team is often stacked by better players. Its obvious at first two stages when they will steamroll through the map.  No good training mode, bots are pointless, can't train certain mechanics or moves on your own. There's a tutorial, but it only serves as an introduction, weak one at that.To get good you're reliant on dueling servers, playing against veterans that aren't there to teach you, and you have no replay function to see your mistakes. This style of ridiculous, weird and cranky medieval setting, is just not for me. The objectives, the narrator, the voicelines are very silly. Attack animations vary in quality wildly, somehow they can be both hard to read and ugly looking (sometimes its just the veterans manipulating the system with accels/drags). 3rd person vs 1st person dilemma.In Team Battles, 3rd person view is way better, you get more results with it. But it also looks worse (FOV too narrow) and not as immersive (1st person animations are solid).In 1st person, considering bad team indicators, sensitivity limiter during attacks, the need to aim when parrying, losing sight of the enemies if i'm doing an accel - means i just don't see what the hell is going on.Someone in 3rd person just sees the battlefield much better, he can see what's happening behind the row of fighters in front of him, and directly to his sides - so all the mentioned problems in 1st person view have way less impact.Overall this game seems questionable to sink my time into, its a gamble whether or not higher skill will solve above issues. The game's style, design decisions and quality problems are reasons enough for me to drop it.If you want a good swordfighting game, try Vermintide 2 on sale, it has something for any skill level, great teamplay and a smooth progression.

_childDocuments_.review: Chivalry 2 is a first-person medieval action game developed by Torn Banner Studios. The game features large-scale multiplayer battles with up to 64 players, where players can choose to fight for either the Agatha Knights or the Mason Order. The game's combat system is one of its strongest features, allowing for a variety of attack and defense options, making each battle feel unique. The game's graphics and sound design are also top-notch, creating a believable medieval world that immerses the player.The game's multiplayer mode is the main focus, but Chivalry 2 also includes a single-player campaign that serves as a tutorial for the game's mechanics. The campaign is short, but it gives players a good understanding of the game's controls and mechanics, as well as its world and lore.One of the most notable aspects of Chivalry 2 is its brutal, visceral combat. The game's attention to detail, from the animations to the sound effects, makes each strike feel powerful and impactful. The game also allows players to use a variety of weapons, including swords, maces, and axes, each with its own strengths and weaknesses.One issue with Chivalry 2 is that it can become repetitive after playing for a while. The multiplayer battles, while intense, can feel similar after a few hours of play. Additionally, the game's matchmaking system can take a long time to find a match, leading to frustration for players.In conclusion, Chivalry 2 is a great game for players who enjoy first-person medieval combat. The game's combat system, graphics, and sound design are top-notch, and the multiplayer battles are intense and enjoyable. However, the game's repetition and slow matchmaking can be a drawback for some players. Overall, Chivalry 2 is a must-play for fans of the genre, and a solid recommendation for anyone looking for a fun multiplayer experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd describe the overall feel of this game to be Team Fortress 2-esque. There's quite a bit of room for character expression with lots of flavorful chat wheel voice lines. The armor variety might be described as lackluster but it's not confusing or out of place, yet. Between the excellent sound, ragdoll physics, and spectacular feedback response to player actions, it's extremely satisfying to play.This the most balanced PvP game I've ever played. The hitboxes are amazingly accurate, which allows for all sorts of amazing duel interactions past an infinite loop of block, swing, block, swing. And there's no dodge roll.  Halle-f*cking-lujah. If the sword hits your player model, it's a hit. If it just the tip just misses, it misses. Being able to count on the hitboxes really opens up a whole new avenue of advanced gameplay. It's not impossible to kill high skill players or defend yourself from more than one attacker. In the words of Ziggylata, you can face three enemies in front of you, but not a single one behind you.One thing I hate about this game is the horrid party system. I've read there's a party cap of three, and it can be quite frustrating trying to play with a friend. It's always  worked, but it's taken upwards of ten minutes of troubleshooting trying to get a party sorted. I'm going to guess that implementing crossplay into the game probably complicated the deployment of quite a few features you'd take for granted in a game like this. I have complete faith that they will fix this issue, and once you do get to playing with your buds it's a blast. Even with this issue I whole heartedly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR A game about cutting people to pieces and screaming, but with a surprisingly in depth combat system. The game doesn't take itself too seriously, but there are some serious moments during a fight that can really give the player a sense of being a real knight; like the time I threw a pig at an enemy before my team and I rushed him. It's silly, tight, casual and entertaining. I think it's worth a look.The gameplay is close quarters combat with some archery involved. The sword play is slower than, say, an action game or fighter, giving the player more room to actually see what the guy who just beat them did, as well as what your own movements look like and how they connect. The tutorial is helpful and  so you can get a run down on how the game plays, as well as pick up on the difference between a block and riposte, and what they do. No shame in replaying it to get a better understanding of the games mechanics.The game consists primarily of objective based game modes with an attacking and defending team. There is also team deathmatch, free for all, duels and some other modes that can be played on or offline. There are also player made servers that run specific game types, like strictly duels but in the form of a free for all so the matches can happen one at a time all within the same server, just be respectful and you're welcome! There is a beginners game mode that puts 6 players total on either team, and the rest are bots. It's a good balance between offline and real online battles. There is no level cap on that game mode, so there will sometimes be folks with super high levels joining a team. Please note that they can be ganged up on and beaten. Otherwise, it makes for a great introduction to the game and is good for training.  Offline, there are bots with a set skill level. You can play any of the game modes on any of the maps. I mention this because it's good training and also can be just plain fun.I want to mention this because it's part of the game and can get frustrating if it happens a lot, and it probably will. I will say I think it's part of the fun. Imagine running from your spawn, pressing "C" to scream, and then run right into a big group of people with your sword swinging. Whether you survive or get cut down, you literally ran in there screaming like a mad man with your team mates. It's fun, and optional. You can also just run around that group and get into a 1 on 1, or find their archers and take them on. There's a lot to do on the battlefield, it gives a lot of options for each life and role.There are four classes to choose from, with three total sub classes each that are unlocked through leveling up that class, all offering different weapon types and buffs. There are archers, the vanguard, pole arm men, and knights, all with varying health pools and strengths/weaknesses. Each class offers unique play styles and use on the battlefield. Want to hang back and offer long range support? A good archer can literally change the tide of battle. How about dealing crushing blows with heavy weapons? The vanguard exists for slow, powerful swings that take time to get used to, but hit hard. Want to keep enemies at a distance while fighting? The pole arms user has longer reach with their weapon to keep enemies at a distance. Maybe charging in and cracking some skulls is more your style? The knight has the largest health pool and ample buffs to keep you fighting for longer against those hordes of hostile knights (hordes will still win 9/10 times). The class system gives players more opportunity to play the role they feel most comfortable in, as well as adapt to a changing battlefield.In my 17 hours of playing this game (maybe 14 of those in full player lobbies), I actually enjoyed my time with the text chat (there is no in game voice chat). I asked a question about controls, and someone from the enemy team helped me. That's rare in my experience, and I think adds to the casual nature of the game. I rarely speak up in games like this, but I found myself joining in jokes (like how the pigs back side had an astonishing level of detail) and paying attention to the chat when my team mates needed some help on a point. It's an online game, there is salt, there is edge, it's unavoidable. That being said, I have seen far more "gg" than "go die" talk in these servers, and that makes an impact in my opinion. Again, community experience is subjective, and this could get more sweaty as I level up, but for a first time player with these impressionable interactions, I can actually say I'm enjoying myself.Pros:

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like it's in Early Access. There are glitches and jank everywhere. The combat in this game is awful, very sluggish and unresponsive. The inputs are frequently ignored, you need to spam "heal" or "change weapon" keys multiple times if you want to ensure the action is performed in the game. There is some very inconsistent behaviour, successfully performing a jab or a kick can stun the enemy or have almost no effect. Blocking is extremely inconsistent, someone could be directly in front of you and they will swing slightly off-centre of your screen and that will register as a hit, but you could be standing at your opponent's shoulder blade and they will be able to block your swings. Everything is pretty much a flip of a coin, you can not rely on any of the mechanics. The combat itself involves frantic flailing around of your weapon, and if any section of it touches the hit box of the enemy - that's a hit. Doesnt matter what part of the weapon or during which part of the animation, you get "touched" - that's a comprehensive hit. This is obviously intentional, as the game teaches you to "drag" your weapon, but it gets pretty ridiculous in some matches. The inept state of this game is epitomised in the cavalry combat, it is the most half-assed implementation I have come across in recent memory.

_childDocuments_.review: offers you an opportunity to experience all the grit and gore as if you were a medieval soldier caught up in battle centuries ago.  Players can select a few different modes to play, mounted, mixed or 1v1/3v3. In a normal mixed game, two teams of 32 players face off on a variety of different maps, each with its own goal list and introductions. Each map has unique goals that must be achieved by the end of a timer by the attackers. Combat is fun and exhilarating. You can choose between four classes of infantry, and weaponry for each class. Each selection will have different benefits to your combat. The stamina mechanic allows you to sustain quite a few attacks before you get mauled, which I found was a nice way to reflect real medieval fighting (ie. Exhaustion is the main weakness). After dying, the action is just a short distance away from your respawn, so you can jump back in – literally.  does not give in to the trope about medieval armor being really heavy and burdensome. In the game, you are able to sprint, jump, kick and dodge attacks, all off which requiring a small amount of stamina.The learning process is very simple and straight-forward. The tutorial is quick to complete, and you can see the controls again anytime by pressing F1. You will, however, be mashing a lot of keys, so a good gaming keyboard is recommended. Gameplay is very inviting and fun, and  does a good job at offering a realistic medieval fighting experience to players. I do, however, think the decision not to use more historically based factions and battles was a detracting factor, although minor. Real factions and battles would have made  stand out incredibly amongst its cohorts. There is lore but I have not dove deeply into it, it has no impact on the game, as there is no single-player story. Each map is paired with another to represent an ‘eye for an eye’ type of feeling. If the Masons attack Agatha in one map, the next map will have the Argathians getting their revenge. There are over 15 maps that you can play currently.You can create a party and play with your friends, but there is no in-game clan feature or way to add friends (without adding on Steam). Cross-play is available for those who want to play with friends using different platforms.Visually, the game looks spectacular and is very detailed. Buildings are especially well done, and for the most part historically accurate. Small details, such as fire animations and dust are also are very nice. Each little detail further adds to an immersive experience. Building destruction animations play out very smoothly and also look amazing. Although it would be nice if more things were destructible.I do not have any recommendations, apart from adding some more armor-coloring options.Every sound you would expect to hear on a medieval battlefield is present in . Each slash or block makes a different noise. Crackling fires and the screams of dying soldiers fill the air almost constantly, with catapults or ballistae adding to the symphony of war. Could be improved by adding more background screams from “peasants” and barking dogs/hissing cats. Also, if  had used real-life factions, different languages would have been a bonus. contains strong violence, decapitations, mutilations and gore, which make it mostly unsuitable for younger children or more sensitive people. It is aimed at people who are interested in the Medieval Era.System: Gigabyte G5 KD (11th Gen i5 11400H + RTX 3060 6GB 105W)I was able to play  with ‘Epic’ graphics settings at a maximum of 90FPS stably (I personally limit to 70FPS with PL1 40W, PL2 45W and Turbo 28W on my CPU to keep temps in 80s) at 1080x1920 resolution.I did not encounter many bugs, although I had the occasional crash. Every time I exit the game, the Unreal crash report comes up but it does not affect the game in any way. is quite demanding, but can be played on weaker systems as long as graphics and effects are set to a minimum. If you are using a gaming laptop, make sure it is elevated and cap the CPU wattage if temperatures are concerning.  is an excellent example of medieval warfare, and will keep you occupied for many hours. But this comes at a cost, as  is priced at 40USD. I would recommend waiting until the next 50% off sale. The developers are constantly updating the game and there is an active Discord community, so you do not need to worry about the game becoming inactive any time soon.

_childDocuments_.review: I am new to the sword fighting genre, and I have nothing but praise for the game mechanics, game modes, maps, and classes. The maps are stunning to battle in, and the voice acting and character creation allows you to fully immerse yourself into the world of the Agatha and Mason armies. The sword play is fluid, and has a high skill ceiling that with enough effort anyone can learn. The modes in combination with the maps are fantastic, though at times one-sided depending on the map. There is tons of polish and very few bugs. The gear is fairly well balanced, and fights are determined by skill, positioning, footwork, and tactics rather than an OP sword. I however cannot recommend this game. The game itself is fantastic, and if it were just that alone, it would probably be my favorite game of the year. However, the community is what ruins this game, and makes the experience utterly miserable.  Personally, I have never bothered much with it. Still, from viewing the chat, those with softer skin or more mainstream players new to the genre will immediately be put off by the constant racism, sexism, homophobic language, and general toxicity. In my 51 games, I have never been in a game that was not toxic. This kills the joy in the game, as matches that are meant to be 32v32 or 20v20 turn into x v x as players just argue in the chat. You do have the option to turn off the chat, but that comes with the cost of immersing yourself in the community. People shouting iconic lines from history, or ordering players into battalions, is really cool stuff. These are rare occurrences sadly. If you are only interested in the game, then I highly recommend this game to you, it's a blast and loads of fun. However, I strongly encourage turning off the text chat.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy passionately screaming while charging with your bastard sword into big groups of armored chads & possibly to your death, then this game is definitely for you.  Chivarly 2 is a medieval team-based grand battle PVP with epic cinematic sieges for up to 128 people per match (64 vs 64)! It belongs in the "easy to play hard to master" category, with slow & heavy combat, generous mechanics & massive maps with team objectives. To delve further: There are 4 factions which all share the same 4 classes. Each class has a pool of weapons to choose from, different setups& a couple of unique skills. Three of those are melee based and last are the archers.  Gameplay is polished & a step-up from the first one, with 3 attacks and combinations between those, feints, side steps, punches, kicks, dodges and comeback mechanics. Riposting after successful blocking can deflect all visible attacks while you wind up yours, making handicap takes viable. You can fight while horse riding in specific events or areas. You can use catapults for massive area damage or your surrounding items, that being either stones, feces or your opponents chopped head & distract or claim kills with those.You can also RP a bard *lute my beloved* Last but not least, the infamous "Balarina Spinning" exploit from Civ 1 is finally not-present! No more 10k DPI 720 360s' per second warriors to deal with. The maps are enormous with great variation on both landscapes and team objectives. Fight in open area deserts or narrow frozen paths, claim territories, steal supplies, raid villages, siege castles & kill the king, escort missions capture points and the list goes on & on.There is even a stage that the objective is to raid a village and steal pigs and peasants, oh my lord!Matches last from 15-40 minutes and I still haven't seen all maps, so chances are some may last even longer. Game's so enjoyable though that you probably won't even notice, time flies faster than my fast evolving negative KDA.  Finally there is a progression system for each class that let's unlock extra weapons, loadouts & costumes. Yes, there is customization alsoand it's plentiful, might take you hours just to take a look at what the game has to offer on that department! But it will take you much more, to see all available maps & content. All in all , Civarly 2 will surely please both veterans of the first one & newcomers alike. Playerbase is huge, queues are fast,and it'll stay that way judging from the predecessor's success and how well delivered this one is. I honestly can't praise how good it is at what it is.

The combat system is primitive and makes no sense in a meaning, as a HEMA practitioner, parry and feits of Mordhau are how in the result the combat irl works when you simplify it. Constant block in the result is almost nonexistent irl (to some degree it basically exists only around shields because they are wider than other weapons, and guess what, there is a constant block for shields in Mordhau, not for regular weapons). A lot of people argument that you can constantly hold the weapon in front of you irl, so why not in Mordhau, well, because irl you always block/parry in an active manner, because of various angles, so irl if you mess up the angle and so the timing, you virtually mess up the parry window and get hit and because of the various angles feints exist to make you mess up the angle/window, which is exactly how Mordhau simulates the result of this principle in a simplified way, AKA the parry system contains dealing with angles without actually having to deal with angles, because it would be a keyboard mess, I mean it might seem its just a short block, so it might seem it also makes no sense as the constant block, but as I said its about the result, its simplified in a right way, so when you interpret it right you realize Mordhau devs actually know how fencing combat should work, for the most parts atleast. Tho they actually tried to make a mechanic that somewhat gets you as close as possible to the manner of having to deal with atleast some angles and those are chambers, while chamgers are also a very smart way of how to balance feints (I mean dont get me wrong, balance is very important for a game to be competitively enjoyable, tho Mordhau makes it in immersively sensible way). Which gets me to what I also prefer on Mordhau is the direction of attacks determined by a slight mouse movement, I find so primitive to basically have only 3 angles of swing determined by ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ buttons/keys, it takes away the joy of feeling like you actually control the weapon, it makes you less happy when you successfully decapitate someone, because you didnt achive this angle. I understand Chivalry 2 devs tried to make the combat system more simple so more accessible, but Mordhau combat system is much more satisfying when you learn it, because you achieved something and still achieving it from there on every single time you kill someone, while it also creates very loyal playerbase that doesnt seem to want to die. Chivalry 2 aims on quantity over quality in its playerbase, but did it really work, I mean Google player count of both games and make your own opinion on this.2. The customization of characters is very restrictive, while the presets of gear are laughable mess, from goofy shaped kettle helmets, to brigandine with lamellar pauldrons, to weirdly chunky swords, to Mason's Men at Arms forced around round shields (which atleast would make more sense for Agatha as they are said in the lore to be a bit more wild and primitivistic, some of them being stylized around early to mid medieval gear). Also most of the preset gear looks like an armor put together by poor looters, each piece of the gear feels like it holds no identy together and its there just so there would be atleast something, like its with lazy intentions, its so random. I mean in Mordhau you see few people walking around naked with pans as a weapon, which is the direct result of almost unrestricted customizations, but a huge majority of people are actually making gears that both look good and make sense (not neccessary in a realistic way, but in an immersive way, in individually functional way with stylization), which to me is pretty ironic as Chivalry, through its lore, presents itself a bit more serious around roleplaying, while Mordhau is the mess... right? Well, now it feels mostly opposite. I tried to give it many chances but I felt little satisfaction or fun playing it.One of the only things Chivalry 2 does very good to me is the faction lore system, the sense of purpose of all the battles, the joy of having a favorite side and being a bit proud when it wins (and thats something I miss a lot in Mordhau and hope for it if we ever get Mordhau 2, as Mordhau now tends to be more nihilistic), its so good also because both sides are well thought through to be very relatable: one side wants people of iron, competent, skilled and inteligent society by any means necessary, a side that was frustrated being ruled by weaklings that almost doomed them, so they fight for taking the lead in their own superior vision, they fight for the greater good, while the other side fights for a wilder sense of freedom, honor, faith and solidarity (tho both forcing their ideology upon all others). Also map/objective design is very good in Chivalry 2 (thats something Mordhau could also improve on). And as a final thing for fellow archers, Chivalry 2 is a bit better for it, mainly because of the zoom and defensively functional layout of the maps, but everything else is goofy in a sad way, so much so Im disappointed of the very disappointment, I mean I was really excited about trying it even tho I knew there are some certain differences between Mordhau and Chivalry 2, but I wasnt ready for this. Anyway still I will continue to play it for some time, because I still want to give it a chance and I want to see what atleast 100 hours will do to me.

_childDocuments_.review: By the time you realize how bad this game is, you'll be cheated out of a refund.  DO NOT BUY THIS GAME.The progression system is specifically time-gated to prevent a refund before you figure out whether or not you like it.The good:Voice-lines are funny and the maps are beautiful.The bad:Customization sucks:- The men look like comical fools and the women look more masculine than the men, or downright butt-ugly.- Men get like, 15 voices to pick from.  Women get 2.- Armor is limited to the class you're playing and the team you're put on.  If you don't like a certain armor set... Well, sucks to be you, I guess.Classes suck:- You have four main classes, each getting three sub-classes.  Sounds great, but they're all mechanically the same aside from the archer, because the archer has you choosing between a fast high-damage bow, a crossbow with a long reload and the same damage as the bow, and a javelin that you can melee with (the dagger is more useful and in the time it takes a bad bowman to notice an enemy is running towards him he's either shot the enemy dead or already has his dagger out)- Basically, the only viable playstyle is the fourth class 'Knight' because every weapon is the same barring length, which doesn't account for much because there's no way to make a gap between you and your opponent.  There's a dodge that sends you backwards, but in the time it takes for you to recover from that action your opponent has already sprinted to close the gap.- If you play anything other than Knight, you're giving the enemy a free kill because they have more health than you and that is basically the only notable difference between classes.Combat sucks:- You have a lot of tools at your disposal.  Swing manipulation, feints, 'counters' (these do not counter) and stuff like that.  The only problem is that these tools are almost always a complete waste of stamina and only work against new players.You're either a casual that enjoys turning your brain off and swinging mindlessly or you're a tryhard that thinks minmaxing teeny tiny animation differences is fun.  Easily the worst combat system I've ever played.  Lots of fluff, no substance.- Hit detection also sucks.  I've had thrown weapons 'hit' enemies, only to teleport above them and glide past them with no damage dealt.Community (OCE) sucks:- Horrifically toxic.  This has been said before and I'll say it here again.  I can take some mean words and banter for sure, but this shows itself when vote-kicking (which should never be a thing in the first place, because it's always abused like this) appears.  If you're 'too good' in a game, someone can vote-kick you.  If you're 'too bad', someone can votekick you.  If you're just playing the game and someone decides they're offended by the emote you just used, they can vote-kick you.  It's less of a vote-kick and more of a instant-kick, because the community seems so transfixed on all vote-kicks being correct that not even 5 seconds will pass before the person being voted gets kicked.I've said it before and I'll say it again: Vote-kicking in ANY context aside from removing cheaters is infinitely more toxic than being "mean".Progression sucks:The progression system is SLOW.  VERY SLOW.  So slow, in fact, that it took me 7 hours to realize that every weapon played the same because it took me 7 hours to unlock half the gear for two classes (when I say "half the gear", I mean two extra weapons per class).  I asked another player that was much, much higher level than me (about 50 or so), and he affirmed my suspicions.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel that I've got enough time in this game to write a fair review so here's a super comprehensive review:TLDR- Good combat, good balance, good variety, super fun. Some small issues which need fixing, character customization could be more varied, objectives could be more interesting. 8/10, good game. Pros: The combat is very fun and satisfying. It feels smooth to swing weapons and weighty when dealing damage to other players. Slicing off limbs with a sword or bashing someones skull with a mace both have distinct feels to give the game some great variety in combat. The combat itself is solid in it's variety and gives a lot of room for different play styles. Learning the basics is easy for new players and simple enough to have fun even when matched with experienced players. You'll still die a lot at first but are still able to get kills and have fun while you improve. That being said, experience does clearly matter and the game rewards players who master the mechanics. The skill ceiling is not as high as other games (Mordhau being the obvious example) but there is a clear difference between new and veteran players. You can also use all sorts of wacky items as weapons: anvils, chickens, logs, barrels, boxes, rocks, shrubs, and even decapitated heads. Small addition but adds a ton of fun and meme potential which I love. Next I'm going to talk about balance. Since this is a new game, the meta is developing and likely will see some changes here and there. That being said, this is one of the most balanced multiplayer games I've played. You see plenty of "x is so OP" or "x sucks so bad" but in most cases it's just run of the mill complaining. There are three primary classes you can play and each has three subclass within it. Each primary class has different levels of health, speed and stamina. While no class will always win a fight against another, it's clear that some classes are made to counter others. It's a pretty solid rock, paper, scissors situation but skill does play a big role. From what I can tell, this is how the balance works: Vanguard counters the Knight which counter the Footman which counters the Vanguard. There is also an archer class which everyone hates but is actually pretty solid as well. Their job isn't to 1v1 but to provide support and thin out the numbers of enemies (basically like mosquitoes). All in all, great job with the balance.Cons: The majority of the cons are small things that just bug the hell out of me but are easy to fix. You have no manual re-spawn after death. This isn't something I realized was important but it's very annoying to be thrown into the match after death if I need to grab a drink or take a piss. Since you're automatically placed back into the match after death, people who are briefly AFK clog up the spawn and present an easy kill for the other team. I also like to browse the class menu at this time and hate being flung into the match as an archer while comparing bow damage. The next thing is the "deserting" function which is just a huge annoyance. There are always areas in games like this where you're not allowed to go and are killed for being there too long. It makes sense to do this at an enemy spawn or map boundaries but it forces all players into a very small area which blocks off everything else. The reason is to ensure the battles stays in a local area but it makes it so you very rarely engage in small scale fights. Giving players a wider range to run around in ensures not every fight is a huge scrum and allows for some fun 1v1's or 2v2's without a bunch of other players getting involved. It's just a little too strict and I find it takes away some potential fun. I know that one is arguable but there yah go. People also sometimes spawn under the map so yah know...fix that too.Objectives: Objectives are mostly meant to give players a reason to kill each other and not really the main point of the game. They're fine as is and I don't think they're bad but could be a little more interesting. Having some crazy stuff like making players blow themselves up to break a wall instead of just pressing E on a bomb. Maybe have spots where players can get temporary buffs like over the top unique weapons or temporary increased armor. Not really an issue but the game would benefit from some more silliness. Lastly, character customization could use some love. Making a unique warrior is the most fun part of these games and the variety is lacking pretty hard. I know more cosmetics will be added as the game goes on so this is a temp complaint but I'd like to see more than 2 armor sets that look good. I know this sounds like a personal gripe but you really do see 90% of players with the same type of armor. The higher level players get some cool armor which makes sense but a ton of armor at low to mid levels just looks plain dumb. Also, the ability to edit your colors and armor tint would be great. Red and Blue are the primary colors but let me unlock bronze, black or gold metal for my armor. You could also add in some other colors which clearly show what team your on but aren't just blue or red. A player with orange armor is clearly on the red team and a player with purple is clearly blue. I'd also like to change my cosmetics during a match as well. Lastly, you cant rotate your character in the customization menu. The back of your character is the only part you see during a match and you're unable to know what it's gonna look like until you've purchased the cosmetic and hop in a game. All in all, most cons are either minor or just things I personally don't like. I'm not saying these are all objectively bad but it's been my experience and it's my review so shut up.

_childDocuments_.review: To put this as clearly as possible. Top tier play is practicing blocking your allies strikes, and having awareness when one is near. Bad players don't know anything but getting wrecked, so they will not become frustrated and quit or they would have quit the game entirely in frustration at not ever being able to win. As such the slot on the losing team you will most likely be filling, is that of a average player who didn't want to deal with the friendly fire or wet toilet paper grade resistance of their team. The only thing you can do is mash the change team button to join all the other winners as you wait for six minutes of mashing the button to join the players who will at least also strike the enemy when they are busy hitting you and forcing themselves into the way. And when you finally get there, your on a team steam rolling the enemy. Every fight will be a 3-8 vs 1 in your favor. The reward for making it is to almost never having a interesting engagement.Game play is actually good. I just wish the arena scene was more alive so i could dodge the core rot at the centre of this games; or that they had had any plan at all for dealing with terrible players getting in the way and directly attacking you on purpose or by accident (if there is a FF ban system its simply not enough). _childDocuments_.review: Extremely buggy to the point of being gamebreaking, where to begin?Glitched weapons letting players attack with punches while retaining block/damage from a weaponOften attacks completely phase through other players doing nothingKicks/punches do not interrupt blocks/attacks quite oftenPlayers attacking through your blockPlayers blocking/attacking things that are directly behind themFalling through the mapAmong many other serious bugs and balancing issues.There are also some huge flaws including the ability to switch teams at any point, including after a loss to artificially inflate your W/L. No autobalancing to speak of means good players switch to the winning team, causing a snowball effect during gameplay. Certain weapons (highland sword, javelin) being objectively OP and restricted to high-level players compounds this and means higher level players have such an advantage over lower level ones they are practically unbeatable without luck. No wonder the active playerbase dropped from 10k to 2k in the space of a month, especially when you take into account how toxic every match is.This game is funny for a few minutes of gameplay, but very quickly you realise it's just another buggy cash grab mess of a game. It's not worth the $10 I paid for it, let alone the $40 it's listed for on steam. Might be good in 3-4 years if the developers pay any attention to the issues, but as the game was taken out of beta in this state, that seems very unlikely.

_childDocuments_.review: Chivalry 2 is a fantastic, if somewhat flawed, multiplayer experience. I've had the game since it launched on EGS last year and have only fallen more in love with it in the last 5 months. It scratches an itch that no other game I own can reach, one of chaotic, visceral medieval multiplayer combat. There's a high skill ceiling, but you can also have plenty of fun just running into the fray clicking LMB on repeat. With the option of 1st or 3rd person gameplay, there's no shortage of immersion here. The game looks great at high settings, and combined with 1st person can lead to some really intense, immersive moments. Being a part of a 32 v 32 frontline stalemate on a bridge with nowhere to go but forward as shields and armor smash into each other is just awesome, there's no other way to say it. The kills are satisfying and make you feel like a badass, even if you blundered into them.My only real knock on the game is that it has some (somewhat endearingly) annoying bugs that have persisted for a while now. Sometimes, a thrown weapon on a direct path to an opponents head will simply freeze in midair, inches from their face, hanging there useless. Sometimes you will respawn a few feet under the map, sending you into a freefall that eventually kills you again. Currently, choosing to go helmetless with your character will (most of the time) result in you spawning with a default, base-level helmet on instead.None of those bugs are game-breaking, but they can be a real buzz kill at times, and the fact that some of them have persisted through most of the game's life cycle so far is somewhat disheartening. Torn Banner is a small developer, though, so I give them some leeway in that department. The game has enough charm, with a big dose of visceral, skill-based combat and just a splash of light-hearted silliness, that you can very easily manage to overlook these small flaws.The game gets semi-regular updates adding maps, weapon skins, seasonal event playlists etc. and has a team that seemingly does its best to engage with and listen to the community. tl;dr This game delivers on its promise of large-scale, intense medieval combat. The fighting is fun, with room to be a casual swing-and-pray player or highly-skilled swordsman, and the maps are well designed. It has its bugs here and there, but I don't find them to ruin the experience. TB is a good dev that has lightning in a bottle here with a lot of potential for growth. If you're on the fence, I say pull the trigger, then come find me on the field; My axe is thirsty...

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointing Experience with Chivalry 2 and Torn Banner StudiosAs an avid player of Chivalry 2 with close to a thousand hours invested, I am deeply disheartened by the ongoing issues with the game, particularly for players in South Africa. Despite years of feedback and requests, the developer, Torn Banner Studios, has not addressed several critical concerns impacting the gaming experience in our region.One major issue is the instability of servers for RSA players, which often results in high latency and unplayable conditions due to persistent ping issues exceeding 160ms. This problem is exacerbated by the presence of bots in both training grounds and live servers, which detracts from the overall experience. Despite numerous appeals for dedicated server files or regional servers to mitigate these problems, no satisfactory solution has been provided.Moreover, the lack of support and transparency from Torn Banner Studios is troubling. The company appears to prioritize financial gain over addressing player concerns, and there is a troubling pattern of suppressing negative feedback outside of Steam reviews. This has led to a sense of frustration and disenfranchisement among the player base.Most concerning is the impact of these issues on individual players. Reports suggest that some players have faced severe consequences, including permanent bans that have significantly affected their livelihoods. Such actions, coupled with a lack of clear communication and resolution, have led to an overall negative perception of the studio's commitment to its community.In summary, while Chivalry 2 has the potential to be an excellent game, the ongoing issues and the studio's lack of responsiveness have left many players, particularly in South Africa, deeply dissatisfied. Until Torn Banner Studios addresses these concerns and takes meaningful steps to improve the situation, I cannot recommend the game to players in our region.
