_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game since the first installment because I was initially drawn to its lore and storyline. I've noticed that the content of this game draws inspiration from various aspects of world history that I'm particularly fond of, including the Crusades era and Arthurian legends. It's fascinating how the names Argon and Malric evoke a similar feeling to Arthur and Mordred, respectively. The lore in this world is incredibly intriguing, and the armor designs are stunningly beautiful - I truly love it.Thank you for creating such a game. In this second installment, the combat system is absolutely thrilling. The intensity of the battles, the weight of the weapons, and the satisfaction of landing a well-timed strike all contribute to an immersive medieval combat experience. The large-scale battles create a sense of being part of something epic, while the smaller skirmishes allow for more tactical play.I appreciate the attention to historical detail in the weaponry and fighting styles, while still maintaining a balance that makes the game fun and accessible. The variety of classes and subclasses adds depth to the gameplay, allowing players to find a style that suits them best.The environmental interactions and the ability to use various objects as impromptu weapons add an extra layer of unpredictability and humor to the fights. It's these little touches that make each battle feel unique and entertaining.Please continue to develop and expand this game. I'm excited to see what new maps, modes, and features you might add in the future. You have my full support, and I look forward to many more hours of medieval mayhem in Chivalry 2!

Combat is also easy to pick up, yet there is quite a lot to work on and an impressively large skill ceiling.Graphics are quite good, but most notably, the optimization is phenomenal. _childDocuments_.review: Chivalry 2 is a good game in which you play as 1 of 4 roles in a PvP environment focused around completing objectives.With that said, I'll point out that while I recommend the game to others, you should be warned that the game has some major issues with its customization menu and even if it was working properly, the amount of customization is really small overall. This is not a game where you change enough of your character to feel unique, but more where you change small details here and there for the sake of not looking like clones.The game allows you to play in either 1st person (extremely useful with ranged/thrown attacks) and 3rd person, which is a good thing in my opinion as the combat animation makes the camera, in 1st person, move all around and some people (or if you're just tired and want to have fun) might feel sick out of all the momentum. (Considering that you NEED to rotate your character/camera to adjust the position, rotation & speed of your weapon when you strike.)The game is relatively well balanced, with a few issues here and there. Even if you just start, you can still succeed in the combat by properly learn the controls and play with your team.At this moment, I would put a 6/10 for this game, but it should raise to 8 or 9 out of 10 once the multiple problem/bug/exploit are fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: Chivalry 2 is a huge improvement over Chivalry 1, which was a great game in of itself. The new iteration see's a marked improvement over the visuals, mechanics, and general atmosphere of the first game's. The feeling of charging the enemy line with 30 other's screaming at the top of their lungs pledging their loyalty to that guy they all like is a vibe to behold. There is a huge selection of weapons and variants, leading to a mix of game play! There are some things that could use improvement, though. The balancing could surely use an update, with a lot of games either being a pretty balanced or a sweep. I understand that some players have a preference for certain factions then overs, but this shouldn't come at the cost of the more experienced players all congregating on one team. While I also get pretty decent ping to the servers the games are hosted on, there should be a maximum ping a player can have before they are kicked out. I am tired of playing against people with 300+ ping in a game where reaction timing is essential to game play. I also personally don't like the whole crouching and looking up to dodge attacks, it just feels weird and inconsistent. There are also a sect of the community that are very toxic and get very salty or sweaty. It is a game, not a area for you to digitally peen measure against others. If you wanna be apart of that, there are plenty of servers hosted for 1v1's. Some of the maps also need to have a passover by the development team, they don't measure up to the quality of the others and the everyone knows it.All in all, Chivalry 2 is a great medieval action game with great visuals and satisfying game play. There is nothing as satisfying as diving into the enemy line or punching a man to death with a flaming chicken. The game balances serious mechanically-sound medical combat with silly shenanigans pretty well to combine into one of the most enjoyable and authentic medieval games I have experienced to date.

_childDocuments_.review: Soft recommend. This is one of those "Spawn, run for a minute to the deathball, die, go back to the deathball" games. It's more fun to play and experience than a lot of other medieval rock-paper-scissors fighting games. It is certainly better than For Honor in that you can pick up just about anything and use it successfully without learning a Street Fighter level of move lists. One major downside is that classes are locked behind extensive grind, and then subclasses behind even more. For example, if you want to unlock javelin thrower, you need to slowly grind out playing two other classes you might not even like or want before you can get to it. The classes also don't really matter outside of spawn kit. Even though they have perks listed they will almost never really matter in the big deathball. The game can have climactic moments where it feels like you're making a difference on the battlefield, but these are short lived and ultimately you're just there as a big part of a mass either steamrolling or getting steamrolled. There's little strategy involved in the fight. Pick the biggest, heaviest weapon you can and heavy swing it, team damage be damned. Eventually someone else will decapitate you with a heavier hammer, waddle back to the fight, do it again. It's certainly worth buying on sale, but if you find yourself easily tilted when getting insta-gibbed by things you can't control or see coming, this game is DEFINITELY not for you. I fail to understand why none of these medieval combat games ever orient themselves as a proper arena combat game. The advantage of something like that is that you don't necessarily need to spend so much time in between deaths just trudging back to the fight. These big set-piece objective games have their place certainly, but there's so much potential in *NOT* having to spend 10 seconds respawning, then another 45 seconds getting back into place and just dying again. There is a mode or two within this title that come close to that aspect, but unless you have serious game knowledge you aren't going to be competitive within them.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely HATE this game. 50% I hate this game. Also 50% I love this game. I have never loved a game as equally as I hate it.Let me explain.I hate the keybindings (PC) that suggest that arthritis or tendon mutations are needed. Why not use intuative double tap keys? The ridiculous Hollywood stupidity of how they think weapons are actually used in real combat grinds my nerves. No research has been done into even the most basic of attacks or defences with almost every single weapon. It's a clown-show that bears a semblance of swinging around a sack of potatoes rather than the true agility of a simple blade. Same is true of halberds, glaives and all the pole arms. Abysmal.  The maps are too limited and very repetative, although the new addition of cavalry make for extra chaos.But why then recommend it?Well I also have to admit that the silliness is an endearing factor. The fact that you can behead an enemy and the throw the severed head back at their respawn does lend itself to a few chuckles. Throwing cabbages, horse dung, turkeys, bells, stale bread, rocks and all manner of junk does have an appeal.There is no voice in what could be a very useful feature, but instead there are humorous wheel speeches that are ok, but not terribly useful.Some maps are absolutely biased to one side or the other - some are fun, some are infuriating. Definately better played with friends - but make no mistake - it's a game made to be a ♥♥♥♥ fight. and a ♥♥♥♥ fight ye shall have.

_childDocuments_.review: I logged in to Steam one day and saw that Chivalry 2 had finally been released on Steam, it was on sale for 21€ and I bought it almost immediately, It's the fastest purchase of a game I have ever done.Torn Banner took the success from the previous iterations of Chivalry and Chivalry: Deadliest Warrior and upgraded almost every aspect of it.I never played Mordhau but did play Chivalry 1 and I must say this feels like the first game only much much better. If you didn't like Chivalry 1 then don't bother with this game but if you liked it then this is an instant buy.Now this isn't to say that it doesn't have it's issues: The hitboxes could be better, there seems to be some server lag (although rare) and there is too much slash and block where fights sometimes seem too much M1/attack immediately followed by M2/block, but if you know how to kick or dodge you can stop this sequence to your advantage.But these issues seem small compared to what this game really is: fun. This game is fun, the crazy carnage the bloody clashes that are not too bloody and violent or too little, the voice lines, the abillity to pick up you enemy's head and limbs and throw it back at them and don't forget the interactability of the environment around you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 53.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for Chivalry 2, but the combat system has left me extremely disappointed. It's a complete mess that takes away all the fun and enjoyment from the game. Here are some of the major issues I faced:    Clunky and Unresponsive Controls: The controls feel incredibly clunky and unresponsive. Swinging your weapon feels more like a chore than a fluid motion, making combat frustratingly slow and cumbersome. The delay between pressing a button and your character actually performing the action is ridiculous.    Inconsistent Hit Detection: Hit detection is all over the place. Sometimes your weapon will pass right through enemies without registering a hit, while other times you'll get hit from what feels like a mile away. This inconsistency makes it impossible to predict the outcome of any encounter.    Overpowered Weapons and Classes: Balance is nonexistent. Certain weapons and classes are grossly overpowered, making the game feel unfair and frustrating. It's infuriating to be constantly outmatched simply because the game’s balance is so poorly implemented.    Spammy and Exploitative Tactics: The combat encourages spammy and exploitative tactics. Players can abuse certain moves and mechanics to gain an unfair advantage, ruining the experience for those who want to play the game as intended.    Lag and Performance Issues: On top of the combat system being broken, lag and performance issues plague the game. It's nearly impossible to have a smooth combat experience when the game stutters and lags during crucial moments.    Poorly Designed Maps: The maps are poorly designed and often force players into tight, chaotic spaces where the flawed combat system shines in the worst way possible. It becomes a frustrating mess rather than a strategic battle.In conclusion, Chivalry 2's combat system is a disaster. It's clunky, unbalanced, and encourages cheap tactics. Combined with performance issues and poorly designed maps, it completely ruins the game. Save your money and look elsewhere if you want a satisfying medieval combat experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most genuine, pure unfiltered FUN I've had in a video game for the longest time ever.Interactive environment, storytelling that occurs naturally from the gameplay, utterly inert of unfairness.The battlefield team-work really comes to life here in a variety of beautiful maps. The only downside stems from the greatness of the unorthodox gamemodes, usually being a thematic part of an event.The problem is that it is limited, and so the game has official, everstanding modes coupled with event-locked modes or simply modes that do not stay for ever.  These I find to be the highlight of the game, but also sieges.Sieges are what differentiates this game from the likes of Mordhau. That game is a wretched game inhabited by smelly tryhards. No, in this game you do have skill ceiling but the combat feels much more fun. Duels are perhaps the weakest point of Chivalry, in comparison to Mordhau perhaps, however do not let yourself believe that this game lacks any complexity at all. It is simply different, and equally mechanical. Grab a spear as a castle defender and stab people when they try to jump from a siege tower. Grab a knife stuck in your teammate and throw it at someone. This game is fun.

The cross platform party and friend invite feature also needs some work as one will often run into issues with players who are online not showing up or party invites sent not being received. UI may need more stability. Bot spawn and player respawn could use an update to avoid spawn killing. Really hope and wishing for additional bot features are added to counter the loss of online players joining in the foreseeable future. Would really like to see the game stay alive.

_childDocuments_.review: As I sprinted through the torrential downpour of arrows and falling rocks, my whole life plays on repeat in my mind. Growing up in our village, learning how to till the soil and work the Cattle with my grandfather and father. Baking bread with my mother. The warm summers spent tussling in the long grass with that summers' lover. All of that seems so distant now. To my left, Edmund, a mere boy of 17 stumbles aimlessly around looking for his dropped weapon, unaware of the fact that it lay still clutched in the hand of his arm that had been cleaved clean off 15 seconds prior.  Blood gushed from his open wounds, much in a similar fashion to the to the main artery of our forces, flowing up and up battlefield ever closer to Argon's traitorous throne.  For the first time since conscription, a momentary thought shot itself through my psyche - must this barbarism transpire all at the raising of a high born's hand? Just then to my right, a ceramic pot shattered and belched its sticky fire in every direction. In an instant, chainmail was melted to the flesh of my fellow soldiers and the screams of agony in unison roared like an ugly choir. I was pulled back into this hell on earth against my will, but I knew I must keep moving or I was next. I had yet to christen my steel with the lifeblood of a dirty argonian, and I was unsure if I was man enough to kill. I had heard the stories of battle many times before from the village blacksmith, Thorin. They were often grandiose stories of valor and bravery, stories of a forgone age from Thorin's foregone youth. The last piece of wisdom he departed on me before I left his shop with my freshly forged steel in hand struck me as callous and cold. "Keep your feet below you and your eyes forward" he had said with an icy glare I had never seen before. I hadn't understood what he had meant until the horn has been blown and the lines began advancing. All around me there was death, but I was determined to out-dance the devil. I continued on, the soldiers already burnt beyond recognition. As I rounded a corner to join up with the main forces, the glint of a narrow saber in my peripheral caught my eyes and I dropped to my knees, almost instinctualy. Before I even had the chance to understand what was happening, the blade was rapidly crashing down towards my face. I winced, and raised my own steel to attempt a last minute parry, fully ready to embrace the reaper. I closed my eyes and waited for the impact, but it never came. Instead, I heard the pounding of feet in the mud, and the violent warcry of another soldier clad in red cloth as his full weight crushed through the silent argonion who had almost taken my life. The two men slammed into the muddy earth, and as my savior rose to his feet and regained his composure, it was clear that the argonian who had broken much of the red soldiers fall, had lost all the air within his lungs. He clumsily made his way to his feet, and grabbed for his blade that had been thrown in the impact. With neither oxygen in his lungs nor a weapon in hand, I suddenly became very aware that this was my chance. I remembered what Thorin had told me once more, and rapidly altered my stance into one ready to kill. I swung my heavy blade with the power of 10,000 bulls and felt the razored edge glide through flesh like butter. With all my power depleted in one swing, I raised my brow, triumphantly until I realized that my opponent was not dead in the muck, but instead was still standing before me. I turned towards my teammate, who was now missing a head, and then I felt the cold sting of the saber pierced my abdomen. "sorry for tk" we all say in unison.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that I am absurdly happy I received a key for from the dev, because it is SO good that it's a feather in my hat as a content creator. I cannot begin to describe how fun the first few hours of this game were, it was like this unfettered joy because I could murder another man with a cabbage or bonk him in the head to death with a shield. The war cries, the ragdoll, the style, this is probably the best game you could play to blow off steam. I will mention that for people who play this game for thousands of hours, the cracks will show a bit in the combat, but for the vast majority of players you won't get to that point. It feels fair and fun for the most part. And honestly? What game doesn't show cracks after 1000 plus hours? Very few. The devs seem really committed to keeping this game going for a long time and once crossplay hits between Steam and Epic in the next update, the playerbase is gonna be massive. 40 bucks is a lot for a game, but honestly, I would have gladly paid for this had I not received it for free. Get this game, chop heads off, get your head chopped off, throw a sword into some dudes face then pull it out and chop his head off. Easily one of my favorite multiplayer games to date.

The classes and subclasses gives plenty of variation to strategy for players. The moment to moment combat is pretty great even if it still has some unfortunate quirks like drags/animation exploits. Besides that achilles heel, the weapons are balanced quite well around sidegrades, and the combat itself certainly remains fresh with feints, attack wind up canceling, riposte/counter/parry, kicks and jabs, the various projectiles and throwable weapons having their own arcs and physics, and so on. The maps are pretty compelling too for all the modes. So overall, worth the money, time, and effort.

_childDocuments_.review: If you appreciate good melee combat systems... you need to experience Chivalry 2. I've played everything, seen all the systems out there. This core combat system has the simplicity, control and depth that all other games should be looking to and learning from. As far as I'm concerned this is the ground floor gold standard moving forward. Every other melee combat system out there feels old and out dated by comparison. Oh ya... and the overall game itself is very addicting. I keep coming back to it and pouring in the hours like I would for the biggest RPGs out there, and yet Torn Banner is serving up here is very straight forward multiplayer brawling in a handful of game modes (albeit they are solid game modes).

_childDocuments_.review: Hello everyone,I've been playing the game for over 1000 hours, and my rank is at level 1000. The game is among the best in multiplayer medieval-themed games. Due to its multiplayer nature, it requires a good internet connection and low ping times. Unfortunately, even if your internet is good, the ping levels that are good in other games seem to be excessively high in this one. This results in a bit of lag compared to other players. Personally, I haven't been able to improve my ping in this game despite extensive research. After thorough investigation, I found that this issue is entirely related to the game servers. If you connect from a location close to the game servers and have good internet, you can achieve a ping value between 0 and 20. However, I believe this creates an unfair advantage against other players.I've listed the Chivalry 2 servers below:North America Servers:Use san jose01Use san jose02Use san jose03Use san jose04Use san jose05South America Servers:BR Sao Paulo01BR Sao Paulo02BR Sao Paulo03BR Sao Paulo04BR Sao Paulo05BR Sao Paulo06Europe Servers:NL Amsterdam01NL Amsterdam02NL Amsterdam03Asia Servers:JP Tokyo01JP Tokyo02JP Tokyo03JP Tokyo04JP Tokyo05JP Tokyo06KR Seoul01KR Seoul02KR Seoul03KR Seoul04KR Seoul05SG Singapore01SG Singapore02SG Singapore03SG Singapore04SG Singapore05If you are in a country corresponding to these servers or are close to them, and your internet is good, you can enter the game with low ping levels. For players in other countries, ping levels tend to be high. Having servers only in the Amsterdam region in the European region seems unfair to European players. The presence of servers, especially in Germany, Greece, France, and Turkey, could address this unfairness, but it seems the company is not responsive to the demands of users playing this game. I haven't been able to lower my ping below 52 in this game. In other games, my ping ranges between 8 and 12. In summary, ping levels can be frustrating, even if you are highly experienced in the game.Cheating is also present in this game, as in any other. Some players openly use cheats on Duel servers, and you can see high-ranking players using cheats as well. I don't know how effective reporting is. I stopped reporting when I saw players using the same cheats repeatedly.You may also notice differences in player accessories. If you buy the game on Epic, you may see different accessories compared to console players or those playing on Steam. Some accessories being exclusive to Epic seems nonsensical. If I'm paying for this game, all accessories should be available to everyone. Having a rank of 1000 doesn't bring much change to the game. Those reaching rank 1000 should have better accessories, but the options are limited. Besides all this, if your internet is good, and you enter the game with low ping levels, you'll enjoy it. I hope (though I doubt it) that Chivalry 2 provides a fair server distribution for all players.

_childDocuments_.review: The Winter War update released on 11/30/22 has ruined this game for my daughter and I. I recently bought the game on Steam for myself and my daughter both in the expectation that we could play together and enjoy the game. My steam account name is xxxxxxxxx, hers is xxxxxxxxx and I will be attempting to refund the game for both of us for the following reasons, which I will try to keep short and succinct for your sake.  Bugs: Chivalry 2 has been released for 18 months now on other platforms. There are bugs that have not been fixed since release that impact gameplay. I won't list them all but here are some examples: The game crashes 100% of the time when attempting to exit the game and has to be manually closed. Customization options randomly reset, requiring an excessive amount of time spent manually adjusting settings again and again. Hitboxes randomly don't work at times and there is proof of this on ZiggyLata's YouTube channel. The Winter War update released days ago has also introduced new bugs in addition to those unfixed for 18 months. Broken Features: Anti-cheat does not prevent cheaters. There are recent YouTube videos that prove this. Instead of preventing cheaters, it will kick you from the game if you do certain Team Objectives in Team Objective mode; i.e. you light explosives to blow up a trebuchet or a lighthouse, but if teammates are standing near the objective when it explodes, they die and the anti-cheat kicks you from the server for excessive team damage. This has gone unfixed for a long time. Also, the party system/crossplay system is broken. You cannot play with friends on a different platform as is advertised. Either you cannot join a party with them, or if you can join a party with them, it won't let you join the same server together, or if you do get on the same server together it will put you on opposite teams. This has been broken for a long time and gone unfixed despite releasing a recent update.Servers: The servers are already overburdened and not being upgraded, resulting in unacceptable lag in a multiplayer PvP game where it matters for gameplay enjoyment. I have an average ping of 4 to 40, yet input to response times feel like 400 to 4000. This is unacceptable in a game where millisecond reaction times are required to perform well at all. The new update and influx of new players has made this much, much worse in the past few days due to the update.Poor Optimization for PC: I have a powerful PC with an RTX 3080 GPU. I can play graphically challenging titles like Cyberpunk 2077 at 1440p at high framerates with settings nearly maxed out. Chivalry 2 gets far lower framerates even with several of the most impacting settings turned to low, and also results in higher GPU temps at the same time. This is in a game with much worse graphics than the average recently released game. The recent update has somehow made this worse, too, with the introduction of a new map.BattlePass: I did not purchase the BattlePass introduced with the update, but according to the community it does not grant XP toward the BattlePass as it is advertised to do. Also regular progression XP gained to unlock new customization options was greatly reduced, which was not in any patch notes and therefore a bug. Also there is no purchase confirmation, if you click on it, it buys it in one click. Gladiator Voice: The Winter War update includes a customization option for voice lines that are used by players in the game that other players nearby are forced to hear. This wasn't a problem before, but the new Gladiator voice lines are a modern American(in a medieval game) talking about TEABAGGING as if it were a good thing to do. This reinforces toxic behavior in game, as you cannot mute voice lines without muting all of the game's sound, which is necessary to be able to play the game competitively. I wanted to play the game with my 15 year old daughter, and bought it for her as well. I do not want my daughter to have to deal with toxic players spamming voice lines about TEABAGGING! It's completely unacceptable that we have to constantly hear about TEABAGGING in a video game if we want to play it and the Winter War update introduced this. Toxic Community: I know this isn't unique to Chivalry 2 but much of the community is toxic in a way that you can't avoid and isn't moderated. The in game chat is supposed to be moderated, yet relies on a votekick system to deal with players who intentionally grief teammates or say racist, homophobic, or very inappropriate things. The problem is that the community is toxic enough that most of the votekicks fail because they think it's funny, and I have never once seen a moderator do anything about it in the game. The new update has made this even worse that it was before. I was willing to deal with it before, but now it has increased to an unacceptable level.Conclusion: The Winter War update released days ago has completely ruined any enjoyment of this game for me and my daughter. I refuse to play it and I refuse to sit idly by and let a game company get away with this unacceptable behavior. The bugs that didn't get fixed yet more were introduced, the broken features with no fix in sight, the laggy servers, the poor optimization for PC, and the broken and buggy BattlePass that introduced TOXICITY AS A FEATURE OF THE GAME are unacceptable behavior. If you need any proof of my claims, all you need to do is look at the r/Chivalry 2 subreddit where I am far from alone in thinking that this is UNACCEPTABLE behavior from a game company. Torn Banner and Embracer should be ASHAMED at asking people to pay more money for an already broken game that they somehow managed to MAKE FAR WORSE WITH AN UPDATE.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. But I feel as if there was a lack of proper insight into what a fighting game should be. I won't draw comparisons to other games, but playing this I can't help but feel a lot of the combat was given severe oversight into how it should function. (I should note I have well over 1000+ hours in other slashers and melee-focused fighting games. Not that all games in the genre should be exactly the same nor play the same.)The blocking mechanics feel so clunky more than half the time and hits feel more like a game of chance rather that proper mechanical application, I'm not super fond of the generalized block based on  your viewmodel nor the very strange parry system, I almost feel reflexive blocking would have fared better than something that's a generalized hitbox. The movement is strange and feels strange, especially the dodging aspect of things.  For a melee slasher, it feels as if the melee side of things was not properly thought out or planned and they settled for something more simple rather than tuning it properly.Game was also only released because of Mordhau's bombing steam reviews, as if they'd somehow steal the playerbase from that small game to this (honestly) worse game than Mordhau. At least Mordhau has reflexive blocking and parrying that makes sense, this game has some of the worst combat logic and design I've seen in a game in a long time. I was excited for this game coming from other slasher prospects as I enjoyed the first all those years ago, but I can't quite recommend this one, it feels like it lacks a lot of love and a lot of proper critical thinking from a development point of view. The passion just isn't there, and for that reason, I can't quite recommend it to anyone who considers them self a fan of the genre as a whole.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is awesome - an absolute blast. I played 3 separate sessions on 3 days without issue, but now the game just won't launch due to memory leak issues. All other games in my library run perfectly fine and I haven't changed hardware or installed any other software since my last successful play session in Chiv2. It pains me to request a refund since this was my most anticipated game this year after all the failures in the AAA space. I'll revisit again in the future to see if the issues have been resolved. I suggest you look around to get a sense of the state of this problem before you purchase at any point in time.

_childDocuments_.review: If you live in the SEA region, DO NOT even consider buying this game. The SEA players are allocated to asia-east(low ping) and japan(high ping) servers but we get allocated into japan servers way more often that asia-east servers. This means that we need to keep on leaving and rejoining until an asia-east server appears. This is because this game, for some reason, does not have a region selector. Players have been asking for this for many years, but the devs don't give a damn about player experience. On top of this, the asia-east servers regularly break. For days, even weeks, some players can experience abnormally high ping in asia-east servers while their connection in the custom servers (HK, SG) still work well. This is happening to me currently for the second time, and it's the third day at this point. The last time it happened to me was about a month ago, which is why I quit the game for a while. A PvP-focused game like this having servers like this is an immense problem. The fact that the devs have been completely ignoring this problem doesn't bode well either. So please don't buy this terrible game that ignores players who can't play the game because of janky servers. They deserve no support. If you're in the NA or EU region where the game's servers are somewhat functional.....I still do not recommend this game. All the animations have way too much overswing.A longsword looks feels like it has the weight of a tire, and the combat is extremely gimmicky overall with a high skill curve relying exclusively on gimmicks that function like coin tosses thanks to the game's pathetic hit registration.This makes the combat feel extremely clunky and unsatisfying.Furthermore, the small yet old playerbase is full of people who played this game a tad bit too much for their own good. Since there is no skill based matchmaking (I don't think there should be one in this game since the playerbase is too small for it), noobs are placed amongst people who have put thousands of hours into this game. Combined with the gimmicky combat, the new player experience can be described as 'atrocious'. It is also quite evident that the developers of the game know very little about the weapons used during the medieval era, displayed by the presence of weapons such as:The DOUBLE HEADED AXES (no practical use, the few that were made were all for ornamental purposes)The heavy cavalry sword (way past medieval era)The Italian dueling rapier (also past the medieval era, should be changed to the sidesword or the estoc)Messers that aren't actually messers (seriously?) The two handed hammer (never even existed) And weapons that look extremely heavy because they have too much metal on them, whether it be ridiculous langettes or metal shafts. It is also disturbing to watch small weapons like daggers being able to easily 'block' large weapons with ease.Finally, the game should remove the team change feature. This causes massive imbalance in game lobbies and most of the matches I've been in were steamrolls. Since people like to play on the winning team, it often ends up with the very experienced players stacking on one team to curbstomp the noobs.Instead, they should add a 'preferred faction' option, so that a player can still play on the faction they want to play in while not being able to change team. Player-to-dev communication is absolute garbage in this game. Servers aren't being fixed, important QoL changes aren't being implemented, and I don't think this is going to get better anytime soon..For the past couple of weeks, I've been in contact with a game dev about the server issue. I've sent him lots of server performance reports, hoping that something could be done. The only solution I was given was to contact my internet provider.This doesn't make any sense. All my other games run with single digit ping, every other server except the asia-east servers have ping I would expect them to. Every second I spent in this game was a terrible waste of my time, and I am uninstalling this pathetic excuse for a live service game. DO NOT BUY THIS GARBAGE

_childDocuments_.review: Chivalry 2 is an incredible game that combines gorgeous graphics with fast-paced, strategic gameplay. The battles are intense and thrilling, and the game rewards both skill and teamwork. I love the variety of weapons and classes available – it adds a level of depth to the gameplay that keeps things fresh and exciting.One thing that sets Chivalry 2 apart from other games is the attention to detail in the combat mechanics. Each weapon feels distinct and requires a different strategy, and the game rewards players who take the time to learn these nuances. The sound effects and animations add to the immersion, making each battle feel like a cinematic experience.The multiplayer mode is where Chivalry 2 really shines – the team-based objectives make for some epic battles, and the community is friendly and welcoming. The game is challenging but not frustrating, and the progression system is well-balanced and rewarding.Overall, Chivalry 2 is an outstanding game that I would recommend to anyone who loves medieval combat or team-based multiplayer games. It's engaging, addictive, and offers endless hours of fun. If you're looking for a game that combines strategy, action, and teamwork in a beautiful package, Chivalry 2 is definitely worth a try.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game at launch for a while on console, but since the Steam release I've barely been able to put this game down.  After about 40 hours at the time of this review, I've spent a fair amount of time with multiple classes (mainly Footman, some Vanguard, and more recently dabbling in Archer).  One thing I almost always hear when people speak of this game is that it is "mindless fun".  While I agree that it can be that perfect fix whenever you need to just start slashing and forget about your real world troubles, I have to say that Chivalry 2 is also very rewarding for those who try to develop their skills.  If you put the time in, you can learn how to make your enemy pay by anticipating their attack and countering effectively.  Suddenly getting ganged up on by 3 players isn't that scary, and surviving such an incident feels really good.  There are dedicated Duel servers where almost every player (despite the occasional bored, chaotic troll) obeys the etiquette of fluorishing/bowing before a duel, and not interrupting an ensuing battle to the death.  This mode is excellent for honing skills that you can take back into team objective or deathmatch.  You also have the ability to choose 64- or 40-player modes, which will add another layer of strategy to your approach.New players shouldn't be turned off by the potential of getting insta-killed by a mob of skilled players, mind you.  There is a beginner server for you to practice against other new players mixed in with some AI bots.  For bonus content, there has been a handful of really good patches with new maps, objectives, and even mounted horse combat.  From the looks of it, the game is still growing and Torn Banner's roadmap suggests that there is a lot more content to come from Chivalry 2.I give it my wholehearted recommendation.  Hope this helps.  See you in the game!

_childDocuments_.review: The combat itself is fun and engaging,  the graphics are very nice.  There is a high degree of freedom in your combat style where you can mix things up to create your own style.  Blocks, kicks, counters, throws and a multitude of striking angles, accelerations etc makes it a very diverse combat system where you will bound to find something you like.  The game is however hindered by the following problems.1) MatchmakingFrom my experience with the game, very little thought seem to went into making both teams balanced during matchmaking.  Teams will have players in single digit levels all bunched up in a single team facing off against 5-10 stack level 300-900 players.  Teams also do not fill up evenly when new players join the game.  So you will have a team of 5 players vs 7 players but the new player will still go to the 7 player team.2) Attacker advantage Significant advantage in favor of attackers in most maps as most attack objectives can be accomplished with bum rushes or involves breaking or taking certain resources that does not flip the progress bar the other way once attack side gets progress.  Defense side requires extensive knowledge of choke points as well as teamwork.  Which isn't to say it cannot be done but with how much of a mess the matchmaking is, attack side requires so much less teamwork than defense.  Attackers are also given way too generous amount of time to complete objectives, and the game actively hampers defensive side with very far spawns and the deserting system, which we will get to later.3) Team swappingThe game allows swapping of teams throughout the game.  Which causes most players to pile onto attack side or whichever side is more favorable on the specific map.  Making the teams further imbalanced.  Which  makes defense side even harder to play when people straight out swaps off the team or just leaves.4) Auto-balancingThe game's answer to the problematic matchmaking comes in the form of their "Balancing" mechanic that only seems to trigger very late into the match in which it force swaps the best players in the winning team.  The player that contributed the most in their team throughout the whole game into the losing team.  This is very insulting and disrespects the hard work the player put into the match.  So many games where you will think you finally have a good match then players fro other team will drop out of the game and you will suddenly get swapped into the losing team in the last 1-2 minutes just to take a defeat.  Which is extremely frustrating.5) Deserter systemWhen objectives changes, you are given 20 seconds to move to the next objective zone or you will commit suicide once timer runs out.  And so many of these zones are sooo far apart especially when you are in the middle of an epic duel.  Some will have you run from the field all the way back up the walls while having 2-3 guys chasing you around.  This forces you to die and respawns if you catch the zone change mid fight.  The deserter zone also kills any ambush/backline assassination play styles.  While archers sits at the other side of the map sniping you with a warbow, you can't approach them without risking zone out if you run melee.Once again, the game is not a bad game.  Combat is solid, graphics are nice, and the 32vs32 skrimishes are epic, but the game is held back by some very fixable problems.  A dive into improving the matching making and a tweak here or there on objective timers/zones and I believe it will take off.  But until these problems are addressed, at the current state of the game, I cannot wholeheartedly recommend the game to my friends.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a good one insofar as I am concerned. _childDocuments_.review: I wanted to give it a solid try before posting a review. This pains me on so many levels to say no at the moment. The fantastic gameplay, character interactions and fight mechanics are solid! I think each person will have their own tastes on this, but it is quite fun. However, its the ankle biters that make the overall experience a bad one.First is the respawn mechanic. There rarely is a rhyme or reason to the timers and spawn positions. Nothing can be more frustrating to gamer and just sit in re-spawn timer hell while other teammates that died after you, spawn in a wave earlier then you. A few maps do not have the right atmosphere with those spawn points and timers;  leading to a incredibly  frustrating experience.The second, is the objectives. Each objective has goals for a team, either push a column, burn a tent, hold a flag point and etc. Some maps have back to back objectives that do not contribute to the enjoyment of a battefield experience. One in particular, is the map where you spawn as peasants..... twice.... while the other team is fully geared and ready to go. In my viewpoint, players are human and will react as so. Forcing a player to be a peasant twice in a row against a heavily armed foe is not a fun one. SUre, you might get a zinger kill and feel good for that one kill. But overall experience on the map, is not for fun.  Contrast it with the other map where all the peasants from both teams duke it out before respawning in normal gear. NOW THATS FUN! It adheres to both sides on an even playing field.Lastly, the topic of even playing fields. If you favor a map creation on just one side, it takes away some of the fun for the other team. While it's cool I can spawn in as a monk on last obj, how cool would it be if players on the opposing team could do the same but with their own niche as well. Then it makes the interactions a lot more fun.All in all, I think the game has initial fun fare, but lacks sustain and longevity of both content and gamer engagement.

_childDocuments_.review: It's good fun. Easy to learn, hard to master type of game. At this point in the games life cycle, you're going to get ♥♥♥♥ on a lot. That's just part of the learning curve, and it can be discouraging and frustrating at times, so be warned of that first. But if you like it enough to stick with it, you'll be fine.The game mechanics are forgiving enough that once you get the fundamentals down, you'll enjoy yourself. There's nothing game breaking that players can do that doesn't have a direct counter. If it can't be countered, then you made a mistake at some point, you should take it as a lesson to not fall for it again. The combat is fluid, catering to a wide range of playstyles and strategies. But not so technical and complicated that you have to spend hundreds of hours to wrap your head around before standing a chance. If you bought it right now, you'd probably have a pretty good idea of what you can expect to see moving forward after a few hours. Getting comfortable with what's available to you is a different story. Getting a feel for the game can take quite a while. So don't misunderstand, it is a time investment. Even out of combat, there's a bunch of silly shenanigans you can partake in with a bunch of intractable items around the maps and funny voice lines to have fun with other players. The game can genuinely be funny in that regard.  There's no other game quite like it, and it's the best melee slasher on the market currently imo. Support has ended at this point, so what you pay for is what you get, which is quite a bit. If you like the medieval setting, and melee games overall, you should definitely give it a shot. Especially if it goes on sale, which it does pretty often. You can get this game for like $5 sometimes, which is a steal. Final piece of advice: If you're new, you can probably steer clear of the training grounds mode. It can be fun, but players of any level can play it, so you might get stomped by a high level on a power trip in there. If you wanna play against bots to practice, just make a private match.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: This review was originally a positive one, but in lieu of recent events I can't find it in my heart to recommend the game. While it's fun, the devs are heartless, incompetent, petty sociopaths. If you're gonna buy this game, do so with CDKeys, as it's leagues cheaper and you'll be handing these guys less of your money.=============================================================Chiv 2 is a pretty solid sword-fighting PVP game, and one I could easily recommend over Mordhau: the community is far more active, far less toxic, the combat is far harder to cheese, and it's currently in its prime having been out for about a year now. The combat is the big thing here so let's talk about that: it's solid and surprisingly broad. You're able to swing from side to side, thrust forward, overhead attack, charge swings(you can do light attacks and heavy attacks), special attack (dependent on the weapon), kick to break blocks, interrupt enemy attacks, riposte, dodge, morph attacks, and feint attacks. And depending on your class you have additional moves as well: the footman can do massive damage with a charge attack, but it can be blocked or dodged, though blocking this attack will leave the player open to a normal attack. The knight tackles, which same deal, leave the person you hit open to attack if they block it, but if they don't they take minor damage and their ass is knocked to the dirt for a painful few seconds where you can get a free hit on them. And then finally there's a sprint attack for the vanguard which is a really powerful and quick leaping-slash that can often one shot people if it's done from behind. Your class, of which their are four to choose from (archer, vanguard, knight, and footman) also have three additional sub-classes which come with special perks that charge over time. These perks would be the horn, which is an AOE healing effect, flags, also an AOE healing effect though its far less effective but continuous until the flag is destroyed, medkits, which heal a lot for one person, firebombs,  which burn people, and fortifications and traps. The latter perks are often the least used. So, to summarize all of that real fast: you can do a lot already with just your weapon, but your weapon also has a special attack, YOU have a special running attack (unless you're an archer), and you get some sort of perk that charges over time which can often turn the tide of a fight. Not to mention just like in Mordhau you can accelerate and drag your sword swings by turning with your attack and practicing good footwork, and that is on top of already being able to charge your swings which would delay an attack already. Speaking of Mordhau, let's talk about that too: the combat in Chiv not as intricate as Mordhau's, but I honestly don't think this is a bad thing. It's far easier to grasp for noobs. As a level 20 I was steamrolling people in the triple digits. Granted playing Mordhau religiously probably gave me an edge here, I've had the same happen to me now that I'm level 100-something.  The combat is also far harder to abuse too: like in Mordhau people can still feint spam, but because you're no longer only able to parry and can effectively hold a block their animation manipulation isn't nearly as damning and generally punishes only themselves. That being said you do have a "block meter" which will gradually empty the longer you keep up a defensive stance and when you actually block an enemy's attack. The larger the weapon or the heavier the swing the larger portion of your meter will go down. If your meter goes down, you're disarmed, and if the actual swing of the weapon (the damage is increased) goes past your block meter threshold you take damage as well. That being said, feint spamming is pretty worthless because you'd only be wasting your own stamina, not your enemies. It's far more effective to just hit them with your weapon than to try and snake-eyes every millisecond, and that's just how I like it.The battles are cool, down right cinematic at times, there's events almost every week, and the chaos generated from the battles is just awesome. The only thing that I think is lackluster is the game modes: there's TDM 1v1, 3v3, 20v20, and 32v32. Respectively, there is also a death-match, which can also have 64 players max. Those are pretty insane. There is a gamemode where you can ride horses, which is alright I guess. The weekly events are neat: brawls, bar fights, and archer-only fights are welcome. There's no true PVE gamemode besides offline practice and the tutorial. Training grounds is a thing, but it's technically PVP/PVE cause there's 15 bots on each side, plus 10 players tossed in, five on each side respectively. I really don't have much to say about the game con wise. The fashion is lackibng, but what's there, most of it anyways, is really cool looking. Nothing is really pay to win, it's just cosmetic. Some armors can't even be paid for with real money which is pretty rare now-a-days.

_childDocuments_.review: Builds on what was good about Chivalry 1. An improvement in pretty much every way. The biggest improvement between the two games are the game objectives. A typical game will go through several phases of objectives. (I.e, - Besiege walls, hold the gatehouse and open the gates, burn the market in the town centre, besiege the keep, enter the keep and kill the king). This detail brings the game to life and makes it feel like an actual siege or battlefield compared to the first game. Pros:Game makes me laugh out loud and embraces sillyness Game objectives make it feel like an actual siegeCharacter customisation is improved over Chiv1Game gets regular updatesCavalry are in some game modes which is fun to play as AND fun to play againstCons:Takes a long time to level (I am level 23 at 23 hours played) and a lot of the items don't unlock until later levels. Expensive upgrade from Chiv1. (£36 at time of review, 2.5 years after release)

The competitive nature of the game rarely its shown outside of its community browser which is a pinch of the game with its duel servers.The Community of the game is decent, you will have to expect varied responses from players, this game after all has a varied learning curve. However the competitive dueling community is almost certain to give you toxic attacking if you denounce or call out players. Players can get frustrated if you teamkill or hurt them and even call out votekicks, these will succeeded as most players press the vote yes button without taking reason to the votekick.Fantastic Tutorial, teaches you about everything you need to know and throws you ready to a bot battle. The learning curve is naturally come about as you play the game, you pick one of the 4 classes and choose one of its subclasses, learning as you discover the weapons they use.There is Cheating, but on a miniscule scale i have never met a cheater but they have been a rampant problem in the games history. Be aware that higher players or duelists take advantage of weapon animations and abuse them to get an advantage over you, in these situations i'd suggest watching they're movements and patterns and determine how you can beat them or if they are not a legit player.The maps are great and so are some of the modes. 64 Players mode is the mode to go, there you'll find the most enjoyable and the most casual of players. However be aware that when modes such as Free for All and Team Deathmatch is enabled, you will have to expect that the small percentage of the community, the duelists will appear frequently throughout these matches, and making it into a competitive game. Do not expect any casual natures of the so called duel modes, use the Community Browser to find 64 player mode servers.While Chivarly 2 is great, it lacks the things that made the Competive game Mordhau great in its small percentage of Casual gameplay which included its swing disruption on objects and its customization which Chivarly 2 falls far from. It the next installment, i'd like see most of these features implemented in the game, but retain its casual gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Chivalry 2 is a fun game, one that may dethrone the monopoly previously held by Mordhau over the hack n' slash melee genre. The gameplay feels weighty and remarkably satisfying, foregoing omni-directional mouse-based attacking which can often lead to animation abuse in these sorts of games (ala Mordhau) in favor of a simplified combat system that is easy to learn but provides enough depth to keep skilled players coming back.Content is admittedly on the sparse side, with a handful of gamemodes across a handful of intricately detailed battlefields. Dev support seems good, with a large content update corresponding with the game's steam release, one year after being originally released exclusively on the Epic Games store.Microtransactions exist in the form of purchasable currencies, but this currency exists only to earn cosmetics without needing to be a certain level to unlock them for free. Currency is also given out fairly liberally for completing matches, scoring kills, playing the objectives, etc.Ultimately, I hope Chivalry 2 brings in new players and helps bolster the community around medieval slashers. As one such community veteran myself, I think this game may also teach future titles in this genre a valuable lesson; overly complex and multilayered combat does not a game make.Rating: 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Where to even start?Tenosian invasion adds nothing to the game, except a separate queue for a few more maps and some more voice acting.  Splitting an already small playerbase all the more.  Why not combine it with the normal 64 queue?  Simple.  FOMO.  You'll buy the DLC, thinking there's all sorts of new content and goodies behind it, get scammed, and the devs will accomplish their goal:  A quick DLC buck off mental manipulation tactics.Team swapping adds nothing but problems to the game, due to incompetent objective balance.  All attackers on all maps doubtlessly have a very, very high win rate, and for good reason:  Zerging and dying to make small progress on an objective is not only a legitimate tactic, but it works startlingly well.  The only defense mission you'll see defenders remotely win without a stack of their own is "defend X super unit" because the super unit can be healed.  Thusly all players with a few hours in the game will swap to attacking, stacking the teams.  And it's the nature of this type of game to make stacks oppressive.  Better players means more players on the field, means more 2v1 etc. fights, means massive snowball and easy victory.  No matter how good you are, there's a ton of ways to flat out lose 2v1s.  And if it goes up to a 3 or more versus 1 it's just plain over, there's no winning, only delaying the inevitable death as your stamina gets sapped away by constant hitboxes coming at you and blocking them or dodging them.  Not to mention your entire strategy goes poof the minute one of those players uses the block disabling kick on you, which thanks to having 1-2 other players spamming hitboxes beside them, can become a "you have to take this hit" situation, and thusly, guess you'll die!  Or, worse, one of them breaks off your front and runs around behind you.Hitboxes can be a mess.  You'll frequently find yourself wondering "wait how did that land..?" and there's genuinely no good answer, the hitbox was just strange.  Thrusting attacks are a good blatant example of this, your weapon must sneeze on every thrusting attack, because it hits a decent space in front of your weapon's animation, elongating the attack by differing and sometimes amusing amounts depending on your weapon.Killscreens are a mess.  Your cause of death window is often blatantly wrong to alarming degrees.  I'm sorry, but a knife slash attack didn't hit me for 100 damage.  And I'm pretty sure that I was killed by a mace, not a longsword.  And I'm 100% sure I was killed by my teammate, not the random guy just now running up to the fight and the only guy anywhere near my zip code using a polearm.  Though with the other dev incompetence in the game, I can almost believe it.  But it's also quite hard to tell and call anyone out on it, because, amusingly, you have no idea how much HP your character has, nor how much damage you're actually doing.  You're given an arbitrary amount of score whenever you land a hit, and this has no bearing on the actual damage you've done in my experience.  I'm sure some wiki somewhere has the info, but it should be provided in game, full stop.  Not doing so suggests the dev team has something to hide simply by the nature of suspicious omission.Downed state and losing an arm is a good frustration mechanic and not much else.  It's frustrating for the player, who has to sit and watch themselves take another hit after already losing a battle, and it's frustrating for the enemy, if that person got away you were just denied a rightful kill because whynot.  Losing an arm is just a coin toss, lost the shield arm, you can almost kinda play, lost your main arm, you should just tap F10-suicide button-and get it over with.  Why is it still in the game?  Player retention, even a bad player can get some kills off downed enemies randomly, making them think "oh yeah I totally killed somebody I rule" and keeps them playing.  A terrible mechanic, but it fulfills the dev's role for it nicely.Some of the advertisement material for the game stated ballerina antics are gone.  Join a server and watch how many people-especially those of middling to high level-crouch spam on every attack, on every dodge, or just utterly randomly.  No penalty for it, and it provides a benefit, as sometimes attacks will miss from it, so it rewards you just mashing the button randomly to mash the button.  A stamina loss on duck would fix this to it's intended use as a defensive OPTION, not mandate, but that's work for the devs that isn't more FOMO paid DLC so it won't see attention.Always open your scoreboard with tab when you join a server.  If your ping is 0 for more than 3 seconds, you've gotten a bug, and you will never spawn.  There is no way to fix this, you must exit that server and queue again.  Fun waste of time.Battlefields, and spawn points, are needlessly distant in some objectives and maps.  You'll die, wait to respawn on the wave respawn system, and then spend 20 seconds or more just holding W to run allllll the way back to a battlefield.  Punishing newer players all the more, as they'll spend a large amount of their time with the game running, not fighting and learning.New players having a bad experience and the long run to battle time is also compounded because, simply put, you are going to die sometimes and it's just not your fault.  An archer will snipe you while you're fighting someone else, and blocking may have been an impossibility at that time due to fight mechanics.  A ballista will one shot you with no counterplay possible from you.  A catapult will hit you from a mile away and one shot you with no counterplay possible from you.  Someone will run up behind you and hit you with a massive, near death or instakill weapon without you even knowing they're there and you will just flat out die.  All your teammates will die and 5 enemies will pile on you in an utterly unwinnable "guess I'll die :D!"  It's not your fault, you had no way to stop this from happening on your own, and it's just...gonna happen.  And you've, frankly, just gotta be amused by your funny ragdoll or be able to deal with it.It's the nature of this game type to reward skill and knowledge of the game, practice.  Which means the longer it is released, the more players will climb the skill ladder.  Inversely, nature of the beast style, this also means the later in this game's lifespan you join, the worse experience you will have.  High level, highly skilled players will dominate the battlefields, and as a new player, you're just going to get ganked with little idea as to why.  This isn't a failure on development, this is simply the nature of a game of this type.All in all, since this is a very niche genre, having, to my knowledge, very few contenders in the field, this will get you that melee medieval fighting fix and has good combat mechanics.  The combat has a lot of options to learn and some interesting and fun balance to it as a whole, and you will enjoy the combat, as it seems just about any strategy in the game has counterplay somewhere in it's mechanics.  But expect the many, many problems in the background to quietly nip and pester at you, weighing down the entire experience.  And definitely expect the devs to not really fix much of anything.  Also, do yourself a favor:  Turn off the chat, as this niche genre's community is A) Not policed by the dev teams in the slightest in any game in the genre, and thusly B) Is incredibly, undeniably toxic.  You can also expect several players to mock you on kills, addding to frustration, especially for a newer player. _childDocuments_.review: You stand with your back to the king, you are the last line of defense.  Four enemies rush at you, you block all their attacks by holding down the block button because you know timing is not important in this game.  You riposte and quickly swing your axe, none of your enemies appear to have their own blocks up.  Your axe passes noiselessly and with out resistance through all four player characters, which seems odd, you were expecting a crunch or metal sound.  Damage numbers pop up on the screen, you have done team damage and your score is reduced by 100 points.  You had a teammate standing 15 meters behind your enemies, he is the guy you hit.  Anxiety builds in your mind, why did this happen, what does it mean what are the rules of this game?Your character has died, you don't remember seeing it but some guy named DankCringeMeme420 hit you with a comically large highlander sword according to the kill ticker in the upper corner of your screen.  You think you would have remembered that. You wait for your character to respawn as frustration and confusion swirls around in your mind and suddenly find yourself at the main title screen.  The server has crashed. The pang of disappointment is slowly replaced by a feeling of tranquility as you realize...you're free now.I think the game they were trying to make was a kind-of Mordhau with training wheels, but because of the server issues it plays more like a dice rolling game.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that development has ended on Chiv 2, I thought it would be a good time to finally write a review. This is one of those games that is hard to encapsulate with a thumbs up/down or star rating, as what you get out of it is going to vary wildly from person to person. You could play nothing but Team Objective mode and have a really good time just hacking away in a huge amount of gorgeous maps while spamming funny emotes the whole time. If you're like me you might get mildly-extremely sweaty trying to master the mechanics of melee combat in duels. You could be a truly despicable human being and master ranged "combat". Either way you are going to get your moneys worth if any of that sounds good to you, though for just the casual experience, I'd say the price is borderline. I would definitely recommend it to anyone with a passing interest in the genre, fantasy/medieval fans, and anyone who likes mastering PvP combat.Personally I think melee first person games are the absolute best PvP experience, with the most chance for skill expression and hundreds of hours of mastering mechanics. FPS games definitely have their place, but at the end of the day, they all boil down to aim, dodge, and any novel mechanics a particular game might offer. Melee games by default involve timing, spacing, blocking, parry mechanics, counters, and that's just the basics. Every time one of these games comes out there's a lot of talk about esports etc. They tried with Mordhau but anyone with a passing knowledge of that game's playerbase and top players can imagine how that went (it was hilarious, recommend a YT search). Aside from Chiv 2 right now, Mordhau is really the only other option in the genre (I guess maybe For Honor). Mordhau really is off the table unless you want to spend your first 1000 hours in brutal pain being dominated by some chain-smoker in an Ex-Soviet bloc 360 animation canceling you. I genuinely like Mordhau combat, but sinking that much time into a dead/dying game is just stupid. So Chiv 2 is really the only choice in the genre for now. There's a few promising first person melee games in the pipeline, either led or consulted by top players who have excellent insights into what the genre needs. Mobius has a playtest you can try, but its rare to find anyone online yet, though the mechanics are promising.Some genre vets will ridicule Chiv 2's combat as simplistic or boring, but it really has depth they probably haven't reached in their gametime, or they just have a bias toward Mordhau. All you have to do is watch some good players duel. There's a lot going on. The held-parry system allows for longer, often more tedious fights at lower skill levels, but once you get past that skill-tier, you realize that holding block is extremely readable and you will be punished. At the higher level fights can often be drawn out just because both players are so good, but they are still really exciting to watch if you understand whats going on imo. Its almost like boxing or HEMA in that sense, as once I learned more about it, fights that seemed boring took on a whole different meaning.The main W for Chiv 2, is that its combat looks insanely better than other/previous first person melee games. There are some fighting styles that look wonky, but nothing extreme. Some people debate whether drags should be a mechanic in melee combat games, as they were originally an unintended discovery in Chiv 1 mechanics, and now have become an expected feature. They argue nobody would "slow down" a swing in a melee fight, but this just isn't true, as changing up your timing in any kind of melee combat is reliable way to throw somebody off. Whether a 20 lbs macehead hits you at a bit lower of a speed isn't going to make it suck any less, and dragging is really the only way I can think to simulate this timing changeup.Lastly, any history heads will get some enjoyment from nods to dark age/medieval/renaissance history. There's nothing authentic, or realistic here, but as someone with an interest in the era, I can appreciate the world they have created. There's some lore, but its threadbare, which is kind of cool in a minimalistic, get out there and pillage sort of way. I moreso just like the comedic tone, and material drawn from actual history. You will see a nice mix of fantasy and very real, well-researched weapons. You can tell the devs had a passion for the era, and the tone in general is a huge positive. Spamming VO's really is what makes this game endlessly playable.There are plenty of negatives, but I don't really care to get into the bulk of them, as they are unlikely to affect you until you're 100s hours deep and have already gotten your moneys worth. One bit I would warn anyone about is the server performance as of late. Its not as terrible as some would say, but I have noticed more jank than in the past, but hopefully this gets resolved. End of development isn't too huge of a deal, as there's enough content and people playing to hopefully keep the game alive until the next entry in the genre (plz God do not make me play Mordhau). Another negative, Torn Banner in general. They don't behave as poorly as a AAA studio, but they are kind of mid at best. They refuse to allow modding, and they had an (imo) ignorant opinion toward ranked modes. I personally was dying for ranked, and think it would give the game a huge post-EOL playerbase, but they seem content to completely ignore that possibility. After 700+ hours I only come back every couple weeks, but I still really enjoy myself when I do. Beyond that I can't really invest too much more time improving without some sort of ranking/competitive system. Overall, I still recommend this game, if only to get your foot in genre. I definitely am hooked, and felt I got my money's worth. FOR MALRIC!!!

_childDocuments_.review: A very tough review for me to write, but I'll say some things that I haven't seen others say and give my honest opinion.Just FYI, I'm a very competitive gamer with a decent level of skill, and I've also played over 600 hours of Chivalry 1, a lot of Mount & Blade, and love historical, fantasy, melee games etc.. I don't mind sweaty online e-sports games, but I also enjoy immersive games and casual fun games.Chivalry 2 is in a very weird spot at the moment. To sum it up and give a TL;DR - It's a lot of fun for awhile and it seems like they nailed the atmosphere and improved upon some of the exploits that ruined the first Chivalry, but after putting in a fair amount of hours, the flaws and bugs in the game really start to come out and the fun all but disappears (as it did for me and looks like is evident by the rapidly dropping player count).To expand on this, the first thing to understand is that Chivalry 1 was a gem for its time and had a great atmosphere and game mechanics, that is until the 5,000 hour no-lifers that enjoy exploiting every game they play discovered the mechanical exploits such as spinning 360 degrees instantly, hitting people with wonky backswings, dragging to glitch out your block, and other weird, unintentional exploits of the game engine. These exploits couldn't be countered and would destroy regular players, pretty much dooming the game and playerbase to the small core of die-hard fans that had to endure the exploiters that flew spinning slo-mo 360 degrees into battle like armored medieval ballerinas. It was a tragedy, and the devs seemed powerless (or uninterested) to fix it.I understand that making a "balanced" medieval combat game is very difficult, and at first glance, the Chiv 2 devs seemed to have a very solid foundation and have addressed many of the problems and exploits that destroyed Chiv 1. For example, swing speed and turn rate is limited, so no more 360-spinning or backswing idiocy. Blocking is also a lot easier, which takes some of the sting out what exploits the no-life exploiters have already discovered, such as certain weapons and attacks hitting much easier than they should due to wonky hitboxes or timings. The melee game is actually pretty solid, that is for now until the aforementioned no-life exploiting game-ruiners continue their relentless quest to find the exploits in the game in order to fill the sucking void that is their miserable life by "dominating" anonymous online gamers and eventually ruining the game entirely.The problem is that on top of the melee, there are archers, which are an entire argument on their own. Some enjoy them, most hate them, but they remain a strange thorn in the side of the great melee combat game. They constantly hit friendlies in the back, they have a hard time actually helping on objectives, shooting and throwing is much easier than it should be, and the list of issues goes on. This leads into another problem in the game that throwing is very strong and almost EVERYTHING can be thrown. Even things on the ground and in the level can be picked up and hurled, which is kind of cool and funny for awhile until you get randomly hit by a perfectly-thrown bottle or something else stupid and killed for the hundredth time.That's one of the biggest problems in the game: the combat and game modes are not refined AT ALL and always devolve into a giant gank-fest of absolute chaos where you WILL die endlessly to all kinds of crap you can't control and feels cheap, such as randomly spammed arrows and javelins, people throwing everything like shields, axes, swords, bottles, barrels, logs, pigs, even other people, siege weapons that are way too accurate, constantly spammed into friendlies, and instantly kill you, and other horribly cheap stuff like firepots and fire lanterns that are constantly being spammed.This is very funny for awhile, YMMV, but I guarantee you that almost everyone will get tired of this type of lol-so-randumb meme-fest gameplay after a few days or weeks. It's so random as to be very frustrating if you're trying to play the objective or do well in the game, and imo the game would really shine if it were much better streamlined and some of these random elements and contradictory gameplay designs were smoothed out and done better (like archers being in the game at all, playing an FPS while everyone else runs around with swords). That's the number one thing that has made me tire of this game much faster than I did of Chivalry 1--it's just random chaos probably 80% of the time. There are official duel modes that hardly anyone plays, and plenty of duel 1v1 servers, and these are fun if you like that style of play, but this gets tiring as well as most of these players are the super tryhards and exploiters that I mentioned earlier, and you HAVE to use these exploits if you want to beat these players. Some weapons are just OP compared to others, and many moves you have to use to win feel cheap, like kicking, ducking, and throwing crap at random. You will be having a great duel, both injured and down to no life, and your opponent will whip out a knife or bottle or something stupid and hit you with it perfectly, killing you. It's really extremely lame, and you almost can't blame the players--it's the devs fault for leaving all of this spammy, lame crap in the game and ruining an otherwise great and well-balanced melee system of guessing, timing, feints, footwork, and varying your attacks.There are other problems that everyone has noticed too, like the objectives in the objective mode being horribly unbalanced and almost unwinnable for one side, spawns being terrible making teams run across half the map, and lots, I repeat LOTS, of bugs like spawning below the map and falling to your death, getting stuck on the map, spawning with the wrong gear on, and endless bugs and glitches with the combat itself like hits not hitting when they should, blocks not blocking when they should, lots of lag and rubber-banding, etc.. This all adds to the endless frustration of everything I mentioned above and has made me give the thumbs down.The game does have promise, and I hope the devs read some of these and think about how to improve their game, but for now, I honestly wish I had bought Bannerlord instead.
