_childDocuments_.review: I hated the first one and the War of Roses back in the early 2010's. The scale of combat felt too small (felt like 5 people were fighting 5 people in a massive battlefield).The scale of combat in this game feels just right. Although there are only about 30 people on each side, the map design, sounds of swords clanging in the distance and overall chaos when fighting people makes it feel like you're fighting in a large scale battle similar to Mount and Blade. They really nailed the feeling of medieval combat (with added humour to boot).My only gripe about the game is that the only modes available at the moment are two sides fighting each other similar to a typical Battlefield match. It would be cool to have a story mode with this style of hack n slash combat. If not that, a horde mode would be interesting as well.They added battle passes in this game with the Winter update and I'm not sure what to make of it. In the past, you could either pay real money to buy in-game skins if you didn't want to go through the hassle of levelling up to the unlock level of the item. It was not a requirement, though. With the battle pass, you do have to pay for the items. They seem to be following suit to Halo Infinite in terms of battle passes: they will always be available to purchase long after that season's over. You can choose which one you want to level in the future.In terms of player numbers, a lot of people play this game. It's cross-platform, so Steam numbers aren't really accurate. Even if the game had 0 players, it could still be a fun experience with bots. In fact, I enjoy playing against bots & players as it has this League of Legends-type of feel. When you encounter another player, it is difficult to end them, but bots in high numbers can also be a threat. Individually, bots are easy to fight, though.I give the game a 10/10. Very few games like it on the market. Mount and Blade Bannerlord didn't really scratch the itch for me: that game had a lot of time-sink qualities to it. This game brings you straight into the action.

_childDocuments_.review: Chivalry 2 is arguably one of the greatest melee combat games out there. It's one of those games where it's easy to pick up, but hard to master, and when you get gud with it's mechanics and you routinely win 1v5s, you feel like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ warlord.Officially speaking, there will be no further content updates aside from bug fixes and server support to ensure the game remains playable. But what you have is a very dedicated playerbase that will always get you into a game. From whacking bots, to grand sieges and the infamous 1v1 duel servers.If I were to describe the game in simple terms it would "Just good enough." Where everything *just* fine, with the exception being this game's combat and humor. This is one of the only few games where you can go from duel of the fates, to slapstick comedy gold in the span of one match as you go from an intense 1v1 to getting domed in the face by a bell from another guy just around the corner.The only real complaints I have with this game is the "character creation" is fairly basic, and the UI is a bit clunky to navigate and there is no indication on what weapon is unlocked as your customizing it's skin. but those are minor issues. The game is well worth the money, and is definitely worth a buy if on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to recommend this game, but I can't. Let's start with the positive aspects: The gameplay is fantastic, it is a blast to play, having many classes and load-outs that will suit your fighting style, from archer to knight, having more stamina, less speed and the other way around. Moreover, you can grab almost any object from the floor or around the map and use it as a weapon, from horse poop to an egg, which is hilarious and gives room for a more relaxed gaming session.  The game looks and runs quite well, having a menu that doesn't do justice to the graphics. Lastly, as you unlock new weapons for each class, play rounds and kill enemies, you will earn points that will serve you to buy plenty of cosmetics, for both you and your weapons. However, the game lacks a balancing tool that makes some rounds unbearable. Veteran players will stack on the attacking side  (which has more chances to win the round, as they spawn faster, and closer to the objective). Therefore, if you play on the defense you will find yourself more often than not facing a team stacked with +600lvl, while yours is crammed with new players like yourself. As a consequence, the round will probably end in 10 min, with one side completely steam-rolling the other.

_childDocuments_.review: Chivalry 2 is a really fun game that I’ve played for three hours, and my buddy and I have had a great time with it. The game is full of exciting moments, with plenty of ups and downs that keep things interesting. It’s like a battle royale, but with swords and shields instead of guns, which makes it feel fresh and different. The combat is intense, and you need both skill and strategy to do well, especially in the chaotic big battles. Playing with friends adds to the fun, as teamwork is key. Overall, it’s a great time, and I definitely recommend it to anyone who enjoys a good multiplayer game.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: A solid gameplay loop with many unforgivable Game Design choices that cause frustration. Toxic Community.There's something to be said for a game that's been out so long and suffers from a lack of refinement of simple things.Starting with my first experiences, The tutorial is Great. It gives you a good basic understanding of the mechanics of the melee combat of the game. The core gameplay loop is fairly good, the maps have a flow and the random objects in a level to kill someone with is fun.However there are some glaring things that cause no end of frustration:The AI - its rubbish... take this back to the drawing board please. Its a frustrating mess of code - you have 2 AI on you? prepared to be hit as they attack one after the other repeatedly as you try to use the block mechanics to break out - only to die. They absolutely love stabbing you on the ground - but your ally AI will charge off and not revive you if there's an enemy several hundred feet away. Whomever made the absolutely BRILLIANT idea of giving the AI pathing preference - should be ashamed of that decision...they push the ally players off ledges or into traps, or block them into corners, or even worse - jam them in doors, or wedge their character model into glitched positions (Mainly in open open situations where there's tiny ledges you have to jump instead of step onto...)Moving away from AI - the game design choice of not allowing some form or "Last stand" when it comes to point or objective captures... it makes no sense whatsoever to end a game just because there's a time limit, 10 allys on the point and 3 enemies, and its being capture - but you lose because of time... Make an adjustment, make a "Final Push" for the defending or losing team - where they have a single life to challenge the point until its lost or something, because the current Design choice of it is terrible.Forced Cavalry - On the new maps - there's horses - I personally don't want to get on a horse a large majority of the time - but it will force you onto one anyway if you happen to be dead at the right time."Out of Bounds" areas - Make absolutely no sense - why can I not sneak into the enemy backline  and hijack a ballista to start killing the enemy team? why do I have that stupid instructor ytelling at me that I am fleeing the battlefield, where if it was an actual war - you'd probably get hailed a hero? Why can I not hold a chokepoint of an enemy assault into our own keep because its "Leaving the field of battle" yet they are bearing down on me... Utter tragedy this design choice.Progression - There really is not much here - you get weapons, you level them up, you unlock skins or other cosmetics via level. But that's it, there doesn't feel like there's any reason anyone should spend any more money on this game, just to make your sword look a bit flashy faster. You know how many times i've cared about a person's weapon? Never. They are just for you really. Whilst on that subject - you can choose and preview armour - but some armour previews reset your helmet to the default one for the class. Something small, but annoying nonetheless.The lack of an effective report feature, or anything other than turning off chat will see some 64 modes degrade into racist abuse. There's no moderation, there's nothing to report abuse to, and the community is very toxic. I don't recommend a new streamer, or many streamers other an those veterans who know the tricks of it, to stream.Awful AI, Buggy Code, Forced gameplay mechanics you may not want, Lack of meaningful progression and a Toxic community, just a few reasons why I cannot recommend the game to anyone, but excuse me as I go suffer some more of it…

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: They added a battle pass. That's a big no from me.Beautiful graphics when maxed and has tongue-in-cheek humor that many other games no longer consider "worth the resources" but which I love: pickable decapitated heads, chicken, and wooden chairs will go flying about during a melee in the midst of all the brutal gravity of blood, death, and gore. The world building, level design, objectives, cinematic intros, wealth of voice options, ease of obtaining in-game unlockables, and the attention to detail are noticeable and noteworthy for sure.I was worried about the complaints regarding team switching and stacking but after playing it I realized that I couldn't care less about that because win or lose, it's a very good game with satisfying mechanics all the way to the end of the match. It's also definitely more arcadey than Chivalry 1 and that's for the better in my opinion.Very well made game.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game featuring deep and yet fairly intuitive combat systems that is fairly easy to learn but hard to master. I feel like I'm never done improving my gameplay and discovering new advantages despite what looks to be on the surface a small amount of content. Every match feels different. This kind of game has difficulty attracting new players, and I think that's a shame, because although it may look daunting, there really is a lot you can do to improve your gameplay fairly easily (locking down basic mechanics + positioning).So yeah, definitely try this, you'll have a lot of fun. I wouldn't wholeheartedly sign off on playing it on Xbox One or PS4 though, only because you'll receive a lot less support from the developers and it'll run poorly. It also generally is just easier played on PC. Additionally the online community can be rather toxic in a very traditional "Call of Duty" or "Halo" kind of way. If you're a woman, part of the LGBTQ+ community, or non-white you might face ridicule, harassment, or votekicking should other players find out, so be warned.

_childDocuments_.review: simple multiplayer hack and slash, its not a game that requires you to git good to have fun. There is strong progression with every match something will level up unlocking new classes, weapons and cosmetics. Its got immersive 64 player castle siege maps based on the three factions with fun secret weapons to find and environmental kills. Keep reading if you want the bad and the ugly...The maps are linear and it gets crowded a lot so if your looking for 1v1s you have to play that mode. Getting ganked is very common unless you stick with the team. If playing archer some enemy players will die and respawn over and over to your team just to kill you and other archers to get easy kills.Progression slows way down once you hit level 10 on a class, short of being a chad who gets 30 kills every match it might take you three games to level up once with some of the best weapons requiring you to be a high level on that class. Compared to mordhau the combat is less advanced with movement tech and chambering stops instantly with no back and fourth. Its better for all players since then a noob can beat a pro every once in a while, but makes it harder for pros to dominate and show off their skill.Each class/subclass has specific weapons and stats with only the archer getting the bow while having the least health and normally equipped with the weakest shortest melee weapons, while the knight has the most health cannot use the highland sword or duel daggers that are exclusive to vanguard. You can find and take any weapon from the enemy but on respawn you will lose it.Customisation is good with the first two factions but the third has limited customisation. All classes have at least five weapons to choose from which is less then a quarter of all the weapons in the game, encouraging players to use all classes which some might not want to do when they have to be leveled each to unlock all weapons.In summary if you want a game with massive 64 player castle sieges that is immersive and fun for both new players and vets alike that you and your friends will enjoy then this is for you. If you want complete control over your weapons, armour, playstyle and open battlefield sized maps with a space skill ceiing, and don't mind sinking many hours into getting good that your friends probably not want to play then morhau is better for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I waited a long time for this game to release on Steam and now that it's here, I can't help but feel a tad bit disappointed and really wish I could just give a "neutral" review. I'll give my TL;DR of pros and consPros:*Fun maps*Excellent class balance*Sound design*Objectives are fun *Being able to take on more than one opponent is satisfying thanks to new mechanics*Models and textures are good*1st and 3rd person are coolCons:*Wayyyyy too easy to block/counter. This leads to fights that can last a ridiculously long time if both players have half a brain cell or played the tutorial. *Weapon balance is all over the place *Lack of voice chat leads to many moments where gameplay is negatively affected due to lack of cooperationHonestly, I try not to compare this game to Mordhau because they're two different games, but in many ways it's clearly better gameplay wise and I'd recommend you check that out first before you consider getting this if you're a veteran of medieval combat games. If you're new to this genre however, I'd watch some gameplay and give it a try if it seems interesting. This game has a lot of potential to be great, but Torn Banner has some work to do if they want to retain their growing playerbase. THIS IS NOT A BAD GAME, it just needs some polish.Edit: I'm editing this review quite a bit since some significant changes have been made. Also, they enabled Linux support which was a huge plus and a big win for Steam Deck players. My only major gripe now is the weapon balance and archers are absolutely horrible to play as. Genuinely one of the worst archer experiences in any game. Other than that, solid game 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely LOVE* Chivalry 2.  The gameplay is extremely enjoyable, the setpieces are beautiful, the combat mechanics are dynamic (not just "hit left-click") and actually give some strategy to a medieval melee fighting game, and there's a semi-serious tone that lets "fun" happen naturally outside the combat with emotes.However, I cannot in good faith suggest this game to anyone unless Torn Banner makes some MAJOR changes.  Namely, in regards to cheaters, server stability and griefing.Since the newest update (and when player population began to rise due to it), I have played in 108 separate lobbies.  There have been cheaters present in 59 of them; mathematically, this is 54.63% of my lobbies (17 were Team Objective, the other 91 were duels).  Some are speedhacks (swinging faster than you can see, moving faster than possible, etc), some are autoblocks/infinite stamina cheats (so they take no damage and never have to counter), some are the full suite of "fly around and spawn in map objects" (these ones aren't trying to ruin your gameplay experience at least, they usually just clown around in the background harmlessly, not fighting; still not permissible though, cheating is cheating) and the ones I've started seeing a lot more recently (mainly in duels servers) are a combination of all of these, but on top of it, they crash the server when someone initiates a kick against them so you can't do anything about it other than leave and hope the other servers are:  1.) not full of griefers/rdmers, 2.) not also housing cheaters and 3.) not full already with other people trying to avoid cheaters.  Yea I could "play the community servers," but what if I want to actually PROGRESS MY ACCOUNT?  You have to play official servers to do that.  This means the options are now "maybe have fun on a clan duel server (if they aren't housing closet cheaters and aren't awful people)" or "waste your time not enjoying anything because you're being griefed."  Both of these are a MASSIVE gamble, which like all other forms of gambling, usually doesn't come up in your favor.Of my remaining 49 lobbies, I have been force-disconnected from 13 of them (12%) via server instability on routing connections.  I did not have this problem before the most recent update, and nothing else in the network between me and Torn Banner has changed, which leads me to think Torn Banner's servers are somewhere between "on fire" and "made out of electrical tape, sandwich wrappers and a bit of chewing gum."Of my 108 total lobbies, I have been griefed in 91 of them (84.25%, all of my duel server time).  This comes from a few sources:  1.) new players that don't know the rules (and refuse to learn them once told), 2.) console players who can't read chat to know what's going on (why can't console at least READ chat, Torn Banner?  This is absurd), 3.) players who intentionally ignore the rules to "troll," and 4.) "rdmer known in the community that has done nothing but grief other players since the game released in 2021 who hasn't been banned ever" choosing to target you.  These are all things that ruin the experience for people who ACTUALLY WANT TO PLAY THE GAME, because you literally CANNOT PLAY THE GAMEMODE AS INTENDED if these people exist in the server.  Torn Banner has done nothing about any of these.  I get that you can't just ban new players, but some form of "here's the server rules" plainly visible so no argument can be had over them would go a LONG way.  Let console VIEW in-game chat.  ACTUALLY ACT ON IN-GAME REPORTS INSTEAD OF RELY ON PEOPLE SENDING DISCORD DMs TO YOUR DEV TEAM TO ISSUE BANS WITH VIDEO EVIDENCE; using a Discord server as your entire customer support form is extremely unprofessional.If Torn Banner cleans up and does SOMETHING about the current state of the game, I will recant my statement and suggest this game to everyone I can.  I really want to, but it has been so aggressively mismanaged and left to rot that I can't do that at present.7/22/2024 edit:  I said I would recant if things got better.  They got MUCH worse.  TB has, in their official communication, said they no longer monitor reports in regards to the "social" (duels for people who aren't playing clan politics) servers.  This includes reports of cheating, general harassment and actual crimes being committed (like doxxing or DDoSing).  TB effectively said "we give up, give us even more money for a worse experience" due to connection quality, forced downtime (that the "social" servers don't have) and being forced to play 3rd-party politicking with the varying degrees of clans that still inhabit this game (since that number decreases every day with the mismanagement by Torn Banner).I absolutely REFUSE to suggest anyone buy this game anymore.*past tense, because TB seems to have given up on retaining a playerbase via doing LESS THAN THE BARE MINIMUM.  I hope you're happy with your legacy of abandoned games, Torn Banner.

_childDocuments_.review: I just want to leave a review for this because I assume there are others like me. I tried the first Chivalry and Steam says I bounced off after only 12 hours. _childDocuments_.review: Title: A Triumph of Medieval Mayhem: Chivalry 2 ReviewChivalry 2 is an exhilarating journey back to the brutal and chaotic battlefields of medieval times. Developed by Torn Banner Studios, this long-awaited sequel successfully builds upon the foundations of its predecessor, delivering an immersive and visceral multiplayer experience that captures the essence of medieval warfare. With its impressive attention to detail, satisfying combat mechanics, and robust game modes, Chivalry 2 stands tall as a triumphant return to the age of chivalry.One of the standout aspects of Chivalry 2 is its dedication to authenticity. From the meticulously designed maps that recreate medieval towns, castles, and fields of war, to the detailed armor and weaponry, the game transports players to a bygone era with stunning accuracy. The visuals are not only impressive but also contribute to the overall immersion, creating an atmosphere that truly feels like a battlefield ripped from the pages of history.

_childDocuments_.review: Are you a racist, homophobe, or otherwise horrible human being? Do you enjoy flurries of sub-par, automated emails from a company that, despite charging to buy the base game and skins packs, apparently doesn't have a human in Customer Service? Boy, have you found the right game!Chivalry II itself is a 9/10. The combat mechanics are simple, but refined. Take the ragdoll physics for example. They're the perfect mix of realistic and cartoonish, adding a sense of gravity and lividity to the combat. However, this game only has a few single player modes, and while the AI is good, the mainstay of the game is the online experience. Chivalry II's online scene is more toxic than a 2008 Halo 3 online lobby. The Tenosians, a faction loosely based off of a Medieval Caliphate or Sultanate, are often referred in game as "Sand N******" in the in-game player chat. LGBTQIA folks are routinely discriminated against. Try to say something and you'll get booted by racist and/or homophobic players.In my last game, a player on my team initiated a votekick against another player. I asked the team chat why this votekick was happening. Another player responded "because your gay!" I responded "and?" because, if you're still reading dear reader, I don't care if a random online stranger calls me gay or not. Being LGBTQIA isn't an insult. This player then succesfuly initiated a votekick against me (which requires over half of your own team to vote in favor of). When trying to bring these concerns to Torn Banner, the automated emails really convinced me that a real, live, human being actually works at Torn Banner, let alone in the Customer Service department. Chivalry II is a great game ruined by a trash community and trash designers. Obviously Torn Banner can't control what players say or do in online game, but this lackluster response has convinced me Torn Banner is trash. Which I shouldn't be surprised by,One final note. Look up who Soter Dave was and how Torn Banner permanently banned him for mentioning their anti-cheat engine (which is a whole other controversy) in a Chivalry II April Fools Youtube video. At the writing of this post, it seems pretty conclusive that one of the contributing factors to Soter Dave's death by suicide was the permanent ban from Chiv II. If only Torn Banner was as committed to removing toxic players from the player base as they are apparently committed to bullying one of their (former) best public supporters.

_childDocuments_.review: My experience with this game pretty much sums up to: Why didn't anyone tell me this is better than Mordhau?I played the original Chivalry and it was fun for a bit at the time but some of the "degenerate gameplay" that started to appear as players got familiar with manipulating the game made it pretty tiring to play.  When Mordhau came out and included this vague promise of being like Chivalry but a more sophisticated physics-based combat and less 360 greatsword upside down blender gameplay, I was sold.  As it turns out the developers of Mordhau were not that great and the game sort of fizzled and the abuse of game mechanics that create obnoxious gameplay ended up existing anyway which made it just not very fun anymore.  When Chivalry 2 was announced I was skeptical but I tried it in the last free weekend and I was hooked.  The gameplay is much less complex than Mordhau but I think that's actually a good thing.  There's much less wild variation in what your opponent can do and it doesn't feel quite as rock-paper-scissors devolving into pure mind games the way that many fighting games do.  It's a very fun, casual, visually impressive, often funny type of game.  I wish they had more options for female characters but it's got more than most games so I'm at least satisfied with that.  A great game to pick up and play casually for a few hours a night for a while.  I expect to get around 100 hours out of this game but many people could get way more out of it than that.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this review to journal my experience with both Chiv 2 and Mordhau (apologys for the bad english)Chivarly 2 is a larger game and you won't have trouble finding a server, a added bonus is that most servers will be mostly full at all times.  The Graphics are great even for medium computer like mine (Looks terrible on low settings) and the core of the combat is wonderful, I really liked Mordhau's combat system but i find my self like the core and i specify core combat more appealing given its ease. I appreciate the level of detailing that went into the map design as every map has a sense of awe about it.This is all the positive things i can say for chiv 2 and here are the negatives (in my opinion)1: Customisation is lacking at best, Mordhau has an extensive array of armor to the point that everyone in a server looks different, you can change the colour, the material even the foot piece and gauntlets can be changed. Chiv is different there is very little in the way of significant changes to overall look and the majority of cosmetics are minor altercations to the armour you start with.2: The actual combat in chiv 2 except for dueling servers boils down to ganging up or being ganged up on by 6 other players. Also the hit boxes are atleast from my experience worse in chiv than Mordhau, so many times have i been killed despite looking at the direction of the attack and even more times i have been killed because despite attacking a while before the enemy the attack is negated and i die.3. Community is not as appealing, I mean this is just my opinion but i prefer the mordhau communityI would say if you want a "easier" learning experience play chivif you want better graphics play chivif you want epic castles play chivif you want a challenging learning curve play mordhauif you want more customization play mordhauIf you want more realism play mordhauif you like horde modes play mordhau

_childDocuments_.review: Update 2 - at the top I know, I'm sorry.They haven't updated the description yet or added the feature for cross play parties, but it does look like they updated the FAQ on their website and it now says the feature will be coming Summer 2022, and no longer June 2022. Also, for those still thinking "why the negative review" in the description of the game they "We acknowledge that our messaging around what Chivalry 2 ‘cross-play’ would and wouldn’t entail caused confusion." - direct quote from the website (I had to search for it), not on steam, I think is referencing the statement: "Charge to battle alongside your friends with all-platform Crossplay and claim glory by your blade!" - from the DESCRIPTION of the game.Original review:I honestly will enjoy this game. However including "Charge to battle alongside your friends with all-platform Crossplay and claim glory by your blade!" in the game description implies that the game has cross platform party support. According to the developers website the update for cross platform party support will be coming by end of Q2 aka this end of this month, but including it as a current feature of the game and not an upcoming feature seems intentionally misleading, as such I cannot recommend this game. Developers should set expectations straight and if it is a feature I sure as hell can't find a way to invite my friend from xbox to my party and there are no current guides that I can find online.The developer makes it seem like the game would have cross platform party support, but currently the game does not. I cannot and will not recommend a game that is missing features it claims to have. So until they add support for the feature or removed the highly subjective message from they game description I will not recommend this game.Update 1:A small update per some comments (also removed the tl;dr):Overall the game is fun, my friends and I used a work around in order to play together and we still enjoyed the game. The work around is you select the same server to play on, but it is a work around and not the feature the developers suggest in the description of the game. I had another issue where the graphics didn't look very appealing to me, but the game defaulted to some custom setting and I adjusted the game to "Epic" quality which the game then decided I wanted "Auto" quality, but it still looked better than the "custom" settings that it defaulted to. I do not recommend the game due to it lacking the so called ability to "Charge to battle alongside your friends with all-platform Crossplay and claim glory by your blade!" - my interpretation of that is that the game allows cross platform parties (it doesn't).If/when I do another update it will be when/if the developers add cross platform parties or when/if I notice them adjust the description of their game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you remember and loved Chivalry stay far away from Chivalry 2Chivalry 2 simply isn't Chivalry.  By that I mean it lost its identity and is now just another PvP game.  I immediately noticed the number of work arounds and counters tripled or more.  If memory serves me right in Chivalry 1 attacking drained your stamina not blocking this was switched and I would say for the worse.  Parrying is now an option and if you can parry you can near always win and this leaves your opponent disadvantaged constantly (I know I can't parry so this is a me issue) but it takes away the defenders stamina while keeping yours regenerated for parrying.  Parrying biases aside it doesn't matter if you're good at this game or not cause if you're in a duel usually 3 to 4 people will come over from either team and finish you for an easy kill.  Another work around that kills the fun of Chivalry's combat is it's whoever can get to the edge of your character first usually wins.  I'd bring up the archers but I'd rant instead of review. So what is Chivalry 2 honestly I'd have to call it Medieval Battlefield 4 no one really cares about the objective or winning.  I understand to some people that sounds awesome and I can understand that I really didn't have any gripes until my final 3 hours.  However that's not what I came for I came for Chivalry with improved graphics, new weapons, bigger and better maps, better customization.  I'd say I got everything except Chivalry 1 2.0. Side note if you war cry 8/10 times your characters voice cracks and I just don't enjoy playing as a prepubescent teenage boy.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just fantastic. The gameplay and scale, especially in 64-player modes, feels awesome. It's also very casual friendly and you can succeed well straight out of the tutorial without using much of the advanced techniques. Fairly low skill floor, but high skill ceiling make this good for both casual and competitive folks alike. Team modes especially have the old structured chaos vibe of TF2 back when Quickplay was a thing, or older Battlefield/CoD games. Just a good, fun time swinging sharp metal around and dressing up all fancy. The archery is also good, especially the arrow cam, if you enjoy shooting more than swinging.Despite my shining review of the game itself, I can't recommend it to everyone. If you're the type of person that doesn't mind playing with chat turned off, then by all means you'll have a good time. However, this type of game still has a portion of their playerbase that is very vocal about their hate for LGBTQ+ people. Playing since Steam release, I'd say a little over half the games I was in had folks throwing slurs at each other or talking about what should or should not be done to minorities. There is an in-game report function, but I'm not sure a week is a good enough timeframe to determine how effective it is. Will update if the situation ever changes.Edit: Months and 200 more hours later, the game's playerbase has only gotten worse. About 3/5 rounds the chat will be a stream of bigotry, players have found ways to sidestep the game's bare bones censoring system, and hateful people are so many they can often votekick normal players that ask them to stop. I keep seeing a lot of the same players doing this as well, despite numerous reports, so I'm forced to assume there is no moderation. Don't play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: "Easy to pick up, hard to master."I put in some healthy 400+ hours into Chivalry, Mordhau, and now Chivalry 2-- I play Team Objective because it's what I enjoy. Duel and FFA servers are not my flavor. I like my slashers goofy at times-- I think C2 and Mordhau allowed for that. I believe that people who clamor for removal of "for fun" game play items, should stick to the duel or modified community servers.Chivalry 2 has vastly improved the system in its predecessor Chivalry Medieval Warfare. Wide arc swings with polearms are viable but there are no more "helicopter attacks" while aiming at the sky and twirling like a figure skater. Comparing to Mordhau, the combat system is more simplified which is a genuine blessing. The frames in which you can block/parry are longer and combat in C2 relies more on positioning, strategy, and speed. I felt as though Mordhau suffered from LMB spamming with Executioners' Sword. To sum up C2 combat, you can:- Fast Attack- Swing, Overhead, or Thrust- Heavy Attack- Swing, Overhead, or Thrust- Alternate Swing (Change direction of swing)- Special Attack (Weapon Specific)- Sprint Attack- Kick- Jab- Attacks can be canceled for a feint.- Feints can be morphed into a different attack type.- Blocks can held but drain stamina. Kicks stagger blocking opponents.- A riposte is performed by attacking quickly after a successful block. This will create a 0.5 second autoparry window that blocks incoming attacks in front of the player while performing the attack. This allows players to fight multiple opponents if they can riposte or counter the first incoming attack. This does nothing for players who are surrounded-- positioning is key.- Counters can be performed by matching an incoming attack while blocking it. A counter negates stamina use of the block and also create a 0.5 second period of autoparry that negates stamina use (unlike the riposte). This 0.5 second period window can be extended by blocking any additional attacks and allow for consecutive counters. The follow-up attack after a counter is accelerated. It can also be feinted/morphed.Game runs with no performance loss on an RTX 3060. Some levels have a greater resource need. Update your drivers and/or turn down your settings.

_childDocuments_.review: Anyone who played the original Chivalry will recall it's fast and frantic nature and just how fun it was. A game that really did embrace the mantra of: 'easy to learn, difficult to master'. Chivalry 2 delivers that and adds a whole lot more.Firstly, the graphics are excellent and the environment just feels completely right. It's an event in of itself being able to storm a castle or raid a village and with all the sounds and feeling that this would invoke. This game captivates the player and puts you there in the action without question.But where the devs really put in good work is in the gameplay. Fans of the original Chivalry will know that it was sometimes quite unforgiving and could be challenging for the newer player because a portion of the 'expert' playerbase did all kinds of weird mouse dragging antics and they thus became virtually impossible to block. The devs have been more careful in their implementation of the weapons/fighting mechanics in this game and I think it results in more rewarding gameplay that doesn't seem as one-sided now. It is easier (or at least it feels so to me) to block effectively and the way attacks and hits are melded into the gameplay has been polished nicely. This means you don't see players doing daft ninja or Matrix moves in this and magically landing unstoppable attacks. It also means you can win fights by using cunning instead of relying on brute skill or button mashing.Even the AI is reasonable. A lot of seasoned players will view them as mere meat shields that get in the way but they can still overwhelm and kill a careless player who becomes surrounded. True, they are easier to kill and evade than human players but they are still able to take you down and of course other game modes are available where they are replaced by human players instead.There are one or two maps which are presently slightly borked because of their asymmetrical layout means the defenders have something of an advantage but in reality this means that team work is essential and players are obliged to work cooperatively to achieve the required goal.In terms of longevity there are just endless character customisation options now and an even bigger array of weapons and the like to try out. You could spend hundreds of hours alone learning how to best wield the newest weapon and trying your luck in the fighting arenas before ever setting foot in the bigger game scenarios which can be absolutely incredible due to the huge team sizes.The only thing I do miss from the original Chivalry is the horde mode where you could team up with some friends and try to survive waves of ever tougher AI enemies which unfortunately isn't a thing in Chivalry 2.

_childDocuments_.review: As a near 4 hour veteran of Frequent Death Simulator: Mi"die"val Edition, I am one happy customer!  At first, if I'm being honest, I wasn't sure this was for me.  Dying over and over again in a semi-pointless mosh pit of team damage and what looks like a silverware drawer explosion, just felt... well, empty.  Then I got into a yelling match with one of my teammates.  We yelled and ran and ran.... I watched him die.  I died too, shortly thereafter, but you know what?  There he was right next to me again!  Yelling!  We ran and ran.... anyway, this is Frequent Death Simulator not Yelling and Running like a Lunatic Simulator, which I'll wait until it goes on sale to try- (it's on my WIshlist for now).  Where was I?Running, yelling, yada yada, oh yes, you're probably like, hey man get to the point - DEATH SIMULATOR!  Do tell!Well, here's a smattering of the deaths my unique skill sets have allowed me to experience.  Beheading, throat jab, skull cleave, dismemberment, team-damage, ankle-death-punch, fire, large rock, explosion, arrows about the head-neck-chest-and-throat area, slip and fall, cannon fire, catapult, horse trample, spear stab, blunt spear, bastilla crush, axe cleave, glancing blow, fire, boot to the head, boot to the knee, boot to the fingertip, fallen rock tower, bleed out, near-death heal-celebrate and then random killing blow, chicken assault, chicken wing on fire and used as a hammer, more fire, team-damage, thrown hammer, thrown axe, thrown rock, thrown chicken, thrown spear, thrown pig (that's not true, I made that up)...  Guys I mean, the list goes on and on...  It's a frikin' Death Simulator, where do I get off?Sigh, okay.  There's some videos out there talking about skills like Reposte (pronounced - ree-"post" folks) and counters...  garbage.  Oh sure, you get a weapon, a few actually.  You can even hit people with them!  And *finger quotes* "armor".  Spoiler alert -It's only for show.  And there's a dressing room where those of us who can afford to dedicate our entire lives to dying can dress themselves in various dapper ways before doing so.  Yes, you can get fancy weapons to die with, take your pick.  Pointless....  You're not in there to turn the tides, hold that hill, seize the day, or see how many enemies you can slay, you're in there to die!  All that stuff is foo-foo in the way!  Get to it!In summary, for those who want Cliff's-notes.  This isn't some well-designed, buttery-smooth, thought out, highly entertaining Medieval 3rd person skill-based weapon-swinger in a time where there's Chivalry too.  It's Frequent Death Simulator: Mi"die"val Edition and rightfully so!

_childDocuments_.review: Between Mordhau and this game, this game is clearly better, and I commend them for that. Unfortunately, I still wouldn't recommend this game to new players coming in or to Chivalry 1 players.This is objectively a worse version of Chivalry 1 in every way. This was designed to be an "easy" version of the first game, in an effort to appeal to the widest net of console players possible. Here is exactly why:The mechanics are terrible compared to the first. No more drags or feints because there are no more timed parries, every weapon is a shield now. 360 degrees of movement for your character and weapon are now like maybe 60 degrees, probably less. Footwork is severely reduced, characters move slower until they run for 5 seconds uninterrupted then get a speed boost. Hitting different body parts all deals the same damage now. You can't stab someone in the side to get around their block anymore. Hitting or parrying someone behind you is removed, UNLESS you are laggy, which brings me to the next point.The net code and lag is worse. You will hit someone in the back and they will still magically parry it, some people have a total 360 degrees of parry range and it doesn't make any sense. If your attack is blocked you are supposed to get a "timing advantage" to attack back. Unless your opponent is very laggy with a quick weapon. The mechanics noticeably change based on lag. I see a good amount of people with "0 ping", which is obviously not physically possible. The servers very weirdly favor some people's connections over others. You hit first, they take no damage, but hit you right after.Class and weapon balance is worse. Man at arms are vanguards now and vice versa, bows deal more damage than giant swords and maces, small weapons do the same damage as large weapons, there is no logic to it whatsoever.Map design and looks are..... WORSE? Yeah, this game just looks worse than the first, and it has everything to do with the maps. The map design for the first game was outstanding, with super unique and beautiful maps and castles. Bad lighting and bad environments will make a game with supposed "better graphics" look worse, and this is a perfect example. Also the team objective maps just... aren't nearly as fun. They aren't even close to balanced between attackers and defenders either.The skill ceiling is laughable in this game, I mastered it in days and now constantly get top of the scoreboard every game. My best score is I think 106-15. That's not because I'm just so great, the game is just easy and mostly played by console noobs. This game, and Mordhau for that matter, have no competitive scene or players or clans whatsoever. Chivalry 1 had an awesome fan made competitive scene, with very well made mods that made the game more competitive. No mods here, not even any private servers!Edit: Developers have cut funding to the game completely, which shows most of all in the servers. The official servers are all dead, except one east coast server which is so unbelievably laggy that it is totally unplayable.

_childDocuments_.review: Chivalry 2 is a multiplayer first person slasher inspired by epic medieval movie battles. Players are thrust into the action of every iconic moment of the era - from the thunder of cavalry charges, to storms of flaming arrows, sprawling castle sieges and more. Catapults tear the earth apart as players lay siege to castles, set fire to villages and slaughter filthy peasants in the return of grand Team Objective maps. Ride to war on horseback and claim glory by your blade. Are ye a heroic warrior, or a blood-soaked murderer? Keep fighting and gurgling out battlecries even when wounded, bleeding out and missing limbs.  Enhanced player expression brings thousands of hilarious new voice-lines and deep character customization. A revamped, faster and more fluid combat system offers an expanded range of creative choices, allowing players to perfect their playstyle. Immersive sound and effects ensure every blow lands with the sickening thud of steel sinking into bone.

name: Tin Hearts
detailed_description: WISHLIST MEOW! 😻 Accolades About the Game Embark on a series of lemmings-like puzzles to relive the captivating and emotional story of a genius inventor, Albert J. Butterworth, whilst guiding a troop of tin soldiers to reach their goal. Critically acclaimed for its moving narrative, refined puzzle design, and immersive atmosphere, Tin Hearts is a narrative puzzle adventure where the ghosts of the past emerge to tell a resonating tale of family, love, and compromise. Spanning across four distinctive acts with 50+ puzzles masterfully woven throughout a grand Victorian home, steadily uncover a variety of whimsical inventions with unique abilities to provide a safe route of passage for the tin soldiers to travel. From the meticulous garden, where the soldiers can bounce, glide and soar to their goal, or the inventor’s basement filled with the heights of innovation and technology, each location has an abundance of treasured memories, whilst there are some that would rather be forgotten. In a tragic fable which will see Albert overwhelmed by sorrow and heartache, discover what brilliant minds do when the love for life, and the love for invention, are threatened by life itself. Set out on an immersive adventure through 50+ lemmings-like puzzles which constantly evolve as you progress. Uncover new routes to your destination each time you play, with multiple ways to solve the intricate puzzles. In a multi-layered and heartfelt narrative, told through treasured memories, photographs and hand-written letters, there is much to be uncovered in Tin Hearts. Witness the delicate balance of family with the persistence of work and the exploitative nature of the Guild of Toy Makers as you wander through Alberts life. Explore the world through the perspective of the independent and fully controllable Mr Soldier, a Tin Soldier who is able to break rank and scout out the best way to progress, whilst bringing with him an additional layer of discovery throughout the adventure. Unlock the power to control a variety of ground-breaking inventions steadily introduced throughout the game. Manoeuvre toy cannons, trampoline drums, and balloon inflating machines before taking on the electrifying vigour of the power glove, a visionary invention which is truly ahead of its time. Pause, fast-forward and rewind time to observe and change the outcome of your actions. With the offer of hints readily available, Tin Hearts provides an accessible and relaxing puzzle-solving experience to complement your journey. Take your time working through the relaxing puzzles whilst indulging in the poignant soundtrack from award-winning composer Matthew Chastney, whose credits include trailers for ‘JOKER’, 'Chernobyl', and 'Bridgerton'. Tin Hearts is brought to life by former members of the exceptionally talented Lionhead Studios development team, responsible for the critically acclaimed Fable series. Experience the VR version of the game, designed exclusively from the ground up for virtual reality platforms, where players can fully immerse themselves in the beautiful world of Tin Hearts. Directly control, touch and feel the game’s mechanics, or physically move closer to take a look at the stunning environments and charming toys.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? This is a passion project - but does this make it a good game? There once was Lemmings, a stroke of genius from 1991. You guided a stream of braindead Lemmings from the level entry to the exit, trying to save as many as you could. Your Lemmings were just running straight ahead, until they died when hitting one of the ubiquitous environmental dangers or turned around when hitting a wall. You could instruct Lemmings to do or build certain things, like using a parachute when falling down or constructing a springboard so that all your tribesmen would automatically jump (and avoid a danger). Tin Heart uses the same mechanic, with the main difference that the game is not in 2D but uses an isometric view (you look at everything from above) and your tin soldiers run around in a 3D environment. You also manipulate the environment directly (and not your soldiers) with your ghostly hand and guide your - braindead - tin soldiers through the levels.Does this make the game better? The pseudo 3D view of the game makes it far harder to see where everyone is at the moment, it makes it harder to place and manipulate certain objects. New games released today have to be in (a kind of) 3D, but I don't think that this always makes the game better. Sometimes less is more, and in this case I am not so happy when a soldier dies because I didn't see him in a remote edge of the map, when I struggle to place an object at the correct place (and in the correct orientation) fast enough, or if I don't understand a puzzle at all because the view simply makes it hard to really understand what is going on. This reminds me a bit of the later Lemmings games that switched to isometric view... and were by far not as successful as the first game.The game starts with your tin soldiers slowly entering the world and running straight ahead until the hit a wall that either redirects them in a different angle or lets them run back from where they came. Should they fall off the world they die. You see a table from above and can place various stuff like triangular blocks or other toys, or even little trains or cannons and so on to redirect your soldiers to the exit. The puzzles get more complex over time, you`ll soon have to change things under time pressure. Rotating objects in 3D may be far more complex than playing in 2D, but for me trying to find the correct orientation and then placing an object at the correct spot in 3D is more stress than fun. You might disagree. You can always pause the game to think about what to do next, you can speed up time and make your little lemmings (I mean tin soldiers) run around very fast, or you can (and this was not possible in the original Lemmings) rewind the time if something bad happens. While you guide the toy solders to the exit, you see past family memories presented in charming visuals. They are well made and somewhat melancholic, but at first you have no idea what these touching scenes have to do with playing with your toy soldiers. Lemmings was just pure fun, even if you nuked all your Lemmings after reaching a dead-end. Tin Heart on the other hand presents a touching story that may make you cry and that you generally find in narrative games and not puzzlers. You may also start to cry because the isometric view combined with time pressure and sometimes a stuttering camera. You have been warned. On the plus side, the challenges get more complex from level to level and new gameplay mechanics are introduced regularly, so it does not become repetitive too fast. The default language is Italian, which is... unusual. Cloud saves are not supported, which is weak. You play with mouse and keyboard with fixed keybindings (also weak), or with your gamepad. I'd recommend it for fans of puzzle games, but it might not be for everyone even if you enjoy the genre.A Lemmings-inspired puzzler in 3D using a suboptimal isometric view, combined with a touching story of a man remembering his past family and later professional life. Certainly a strange combination.

_childDocuments_.review: You can view my gameplay & early impressions here: This is a lovely game to play. It's a cozy Lemmings-type narrative-driven puzzle game. The game looks absolutely beautiful and is a joy to visit in VR. You can tell just from playing it that the developers had VR first and foremost in their hearts, even if they originally released the game without VR support.This game is perfect for those new to VR and casual / puzzle beginners. Honestly, you're almost sad to solve the puzzle and leave the toy maker's room that you want to play in with all the toys strewn about. You wish you could go toy eye-level and get to walk around and enjoy all the sights and toys available. The puzzles start off pretty easy and there is a slow but steady difficulty curve where you are taught new game mechanics.However, all is not perfect. This game has button turning instead of joystick turning (right joystick is default in most video games for a good reason). This is a really bad development decision. I hope the developers add right joystick turning and allow you to change the default button configuration. Let's talk about the elephant in the room now: Humanity VR. Yes, Humanity VR is probably the best VR puzzle game out there (it's definitely the best Lemmings type puzzle game ever for VR and non-VR). However, I think I prefer Tin Hearts. While the puzzles aren't as challenging or as have the ingenuity of Humanity, it's just cozier to play this game. The visuals and environmental story telling are much better here. The narrated cut scenes are way better. In the end, these are two very different games intended for two very different audiences. Humanity is perfect for puzzle veterans / pros, while Tin Hearts is perfect for casuals / cozy gamers.Tin Hearts is running on the Unity Engine. On my RTX 3080, I was getting a steady 72 fps. I did not experience any serious issues or bugs, however, I did have a bug where the left joystick stopped working with locomotion and where I temporarily could not pick up a puzzle piece (for a few seconds). You have teleportation and full locomotion available, along with smooth or snap turning. You can play comfortably seated as you a button elevation and magnet hands.

_childDocuments_.review: Tin Hearts is a heartwarming story told in Victorian times about a husband, wife and the daughter they have. All this unfolds whilst playing through a Lemmings-style puzzle game with cute little Tin Soldiers as you strive to get them into the magical fairy doors and hopefully leaving no soldier behind.I love the beautiful graphics, sound, music and story in this game. The developers are very passionate about their game and have an amazing attention to detail that really shows in every aspect of this game. I have been following the game since when I purchased the original VR-only prologue version in late 2019.I unreservedly recommend this game to all puzzle players, even if you're not a normal puzzle player the game starts you off very easily and has a gentle learning curve to help you through. The later Acts 3 and 4 get a real challenge, but by then you would have honed your puzzling skills enough.Though this version is currently a screen-only game. I can't wait to play this final version of the game in VR sometime later this year. As the developers have promised this update and I know they will deliver on it. So do yourself a big favour and get this beautiful masterpiece of a game. You won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a hidden gem, one of the best puzzle games I've played in the last few years.  I haven't finished it yet but so far it's great, developers put a lot of love and attention into it.  The sad story of the family who lived in the house and the excellent music bring an emotional element to the overall atmosphere.  The puzzles never never get too old or repetitive because the game introduces new mechanics at each 3 or 4 levels.If you like mechanical / physics based puzzles, don't hesitate to buy it, you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: So far so wonderful. One piece of advice, stay with it through the first Act, which is like a long tutorial. The whole game opens up in Act 2, the story starts to unfold, more machinery to manipulate and bigger environments. I'm only 3 hours in but I'm really warming to the characters. Just completed the Garden level and it was absolutely lovely. One of my soldiers got left behind so while I was solving puzzles over one side of the garden I could see him  desperately trying to catch up, so I created a little loop for the rest of the group and eventually he rejoined his buddies...aaaw.Update after about 6hrs: Blimey, this just keeps getting better and the attention to detail. I just completed a level where you have to push 4 things with the direct control soldier, each animation for the soldier was different, with the final one being a kind of roundhouse karate kick which almost made me laugh out loud, to then be brought down to earth with a lump in my throat at the cut scene between Albert and his wife, gulp.Update after completing the game. Holy moly, THAT. WAS. BRILLIANT. The puzzles get bigger but not crazy difficult, you can solve them in smallish chunks. And of course rewind time. The acting in the final cut scenes was top notch and that final uplifting song with the musical soldier and end credits rounded the whole thing off perfectly. I just let out an aaaah and smiled.

I was on a Quest 3 with a decent spec PC. It took multiple attempts to launch the game in various different methods to get it to work in VR. Then when I did it crashed a couple of times during play... but overall it was worth it. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Tin Hearts

_childDocuments_.review: Fun lemming's-like puzzle game that, unlike some other VR puzzle games, is of decent length. Graphics quality is outstanding, and the tin soldiers are so detailed and lifelike. You're bound to get sucked into the environment through the story, of which the ending is among the best I've experienced in any game.It's well worth the original $20 price that I paid for it, but right now it's part of the summer event listed as $12, which is a steal for this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Tin Hearts

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very well done puzzle game which is not an easy feat to pull off.  I think the difficulty curve is great and the hint system is very helpful if you get stuck.  This is something I wish more of these kinds of games implemented.  The game is a great price for what is here and I'd highly recommend.  It also runs perfectly on the Steam Deck too from the few levels I tried on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tin Hearts

_childDocuments_.review: There will be inevitable comparisons between Tin Hearts and Lemmings. Any such comparison will fail to capture how captivatingly beautiful and agonizingly tragic Tin Hearts is.It is a little like Lemmings, though.The story follows 19th century toymaker Albert Butterworth as forces outside of his control push him toward the modern age. It takes a while for the plot to really get rolling (the first few hours are mainly to establish Butterworth and his family), but it's worth sticking it out for a while.The central gameplay loop involves manipulating objects in each room to direct Butterworth's wind-up soldiers toward a goal. Some of the rooms can be very large, but the layout of the controllable objects usually suggests a solution. And while you're working out that solution, you'll have time to enjoy some character moments - which are woven into the puzzles - and the absolutely gorgeous graphics design.In sum: It's good if you like puzzle games and it's good if you like a good story, and if you like both? Don't stay your hand.
_childDocuments_.name: Tin Hearts

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game with cute graphics & interesting story. The levels are quite detailed & thought out. The world around you evolves and changes as the story goes on. Contrary to what I expected, the game is decently long.Having said that, a few issues:- camera can feel sluggish- some textures for big objects need more detail/resolution- wish I could disable/skip some forced camera movement upon completing a part of a puzzle- there should be an option to skip all story-related elements when replaying the levels you've already finishedOverall, a very well made game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tin Hearts

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:  Ignore the cliché story and work the puzzles and you will LOVE this game on multiple levels.Tin Hearts is a brilliant puzzle title that calls back to the days of Lemmings but adds so much to the genre (if we can claim that exists).  The 3D element alone would have been sufficient to laud this title and I am certain it is amazing in VR.But there is so much more as well!  The interface allows the player to have direct control over elements of the environment, which grows in complexity as the game progresses.  This is integral to the puzzles in many, sometimes subtle ways.  Though not always  ;)The player can not only act as themselves, they can often take direct control of a unit to perform unique actions critical to the solution of certain puzzles.The soundtrack, story, lore, and clues are beautifully interwoven into each scene.  And let me circle back to that soundtrack because it is absolutely beautiful and fitting.I cannot say enough good things about this game!  If you like environmental puzzle gaming, this is a great find!  Downsides (and it hurts me to share them):1. The introduction of story elements creates levels so large that in many cases the makers do not take advantage of them.  (The old Open World problem.  Very minor)2. Depth perception is a REAL problem and it ruins the platforming elements.  Fortunately, these are rare enough to be forgiven.3. Minor spoilers ahead.  Skip if you don't care about story and themes.*Mounts soapbox*I love a good story.  And I accept and even enjoy that a game like this, that has ZERO need for one, goes so far as to include a rich tale.  Sadly, to no direct fault of the makers, the game stumbles with the modern crutch of storytelling.  15 years ago this story would have been groundbreaking!  And if you are new to gaming/storytelling, I pray you get from it what I should have!  But this game came out in 2023,  The days of inserting negative themes just to avoid a "fairy tale ending" are gone. We needed them for a while and will again, surely.  But there is a middle-ground and...  we've been through some dark years (globally, not to take away from ANY who are still living it).   Death and denial are not the only sources of non-violent conflict.Loss is not the only motivator.Bittersweet is not the only flavour.Before the Cough of Death ever reared its face, this story had all the elements of Love, Ambition, and Need  in place to tell an amazing (and better) tale.*Dismounts soapbox*Still with me?  Good, cause...   BUY this game!   If you enjoy puzzlers, you will not be disappointed and anything negative I may have said should NOT be measured by paragraph size!  This is a brilliant game by game makers who are worthy of our support!  Loved it!
_childDocuments_.name: Tin Hearts

_childDocuments_.review: An Absolutely amazing title. Potentially one of my favorite games of 2023. The content the developers and publishers have delivered is unbelievable. I will be updating this review once I hit 50/60hrs gameplay - or when I complete the game on multiple formats. But for now - Thank you Rogue Sun and Wired Productions, this has been a pleasant, unexpected adventure - Everybody needs to walk this path.
_childDocuments_.name: Tin Hearts

_childDocuments_.review: Very chill Lemmings-style puzzle game with exquisite graphics and a cute theme. Mechanics expand over chapters and the difficulty ramps up near the end of the first act, but there's a hint system that's not too spoilery so you won't have to resort to a guide if you get stuck. Well worth your time and money if you're a fan of this genre. Plays smoothly on the Steam Deck as well!
_childDocuments_.name: Tin Hearts

_childDocuments_.review: After 16.3 hours of playing this game I have to say... boy was it challenging. Fun but challengingThere is no mixed review option but if I have to really sit on it and think on it. I would say: "Yes. But exercise caution" Tin Hearts is a lemmings type puzzle that pits you and your group of soldiers getting from point A to point B in elaborate and sometimes head scratching puzzles.The story is nothing to write home about as it's essentially: "A family man who gets engrossed with his work so much so that life events happened and he hides his grief behind his work until he realizes that his family is so important to him" type of story. There are some "feels" moments but overall it's nothing to write home about.The gameplay portion is what I want to focus on and why I exercise caution. The puzzles start out simple enough and then at some point the game takes a hard left turn and the puzzles become more extravagant and sometimes arrogant right up until the end. The basement levels are by far the worse This all basically boils down to: Intuitive design. Why can't I just teleport or walk faster? Why do I have to be so up close to the puzzle to even reach for it when using the zoom in function? Why are you giving me mechanics and obstacles that hopscotch in appearance per level? Keep it consistent and to the point. And the game sadly didn't do that.Overall if you are willing to methodically take your time with this game. Then I say go for it. But be aware of softlocks, and technical issues with the camera and stuff
_childDocuments_.name: Tin Hearts

_childDocuments_.review: This took me 14.7 hours to beat in VR, and I highly recommend it. It has very impressively detailed graphics, emotional music, and a major family story during and in between the levels. The puzzles are really good too. Some will really challenge you, but there are hints available. This has turned out to be one of my favorites.
_childDocuments_.name: Tin Hearts

_childDocuments_.review: After a delay of a couple of months, they fixed the bug in level 50, and it's possible to finish the game again.Tin Hearts is a puzzle game along the line of Lemmings. In each level, you guide a line of marching toy soldiers to the exit. You have to move various parts such as blocks and drums (which act as trampolines) around until they can reach their destination.There's also some light platforming. About midway through the game you gain the ability to possess one of the soldiers and control it directly. In puzzles where this is an option, you need to send this scout ahead to perform various actions that the regular soldiers won't do on their own. Usually this involves a bit of jumping and following paths that the regular soldiers won't.Each level is a Rube Goldberg machine, often with a number of ridiculous things happening. The early levels are very simple. For example, the blocks in the first few puzzles can only be placed on specific locations, which is very restrictive and makes the puzzles trivial. After a bit of that, though, you get blocks that can be placed pretty much anywhere, and that's the least of the things you end up doing. Eventually the game takes a decidedly steampunk bent, with all sorts of fantastic steam-powered machines and pneumatic tube systems to send the soldiers around the increasingly large and more complex puzzles.One of the abilities you get early is the ability to pause time or rewind it, which is essential to finishing the game since otherwise there's a lot of time sensitive actions. Usually you have a limited number of pieces, and you have to re-use pieces from earlier in the puzzle.Eventually the puzzles get difficult enough that most of them have some sort of "aha" moment where you find a way past something that initially looks impossible. The game has a hint system, but it foolishly penalizes you by forbidding achievements if you use it too much. It's like the designers *want* the player to look up YouTube videoes instead of staying in the game.It's really amazing looking in VR. The environments are complex and the art very well done with few exceptions. The soldiers in particular are really fantastic, with elaborate animations for everything they do, from climbing to jumping to riding balloons. The only weak point in the art is the humans, who look cartoonish at best, and sometimes downright creepy because of the eyes.Which brings me to the only part I didn't like about the game. The story. It's a rather banal, uninteresting story of pointless tragedy, and the cutscenes detailing this sometimes go on far, far too long. Particularly the epilogue after you finish the last, 3-part puzzle.Regardless, it's still an excellent game, particularly if you have a VR headset. I played using Index controllers, and I gather it works well enough with Quest controllers, but I don't know how well it plays with Vive wands. It felt like the joysticks were really essential.
_childDocuments_.name: Tin Hearts

_childDocuments_.review: only a few hours into the game and I am already loving it. The atmosphere is magical and relaxing, and the moment the puzzle 'clicks' and you get to watch the soldiers march away is very satisfying. I can tell the puzzles getting progressively more involved, without reaching bang head on wall levels. The music/sounds tie in perfectly with the vibes. The presentation of the story is very intriguing, with lots of nice little details sprinkled around in the rooms, and I'm looking forward to revealing more of it in the next days, so far really lives up to the great reviews I've seen.I saw a couple reviews mention issues with controls, but I’ve been playing with mouse and keyboard without any issues. The game does toggle you from first person to manipulating various objects in a sort of top down / strategy game mode, so maybe it's about that. The trick is to remember that you "are" the object in that moment (it does say you "possess" it).  Controlling things became second nature fairly quickly, soon after completing the prologue/tutorial. The "pause" time is on space bar so you can take as long as you need anyway to set stuff up, and even rewind and correct if you mess something up. That part is very cool actually, love how it affects the music.Can’t wait to see where it all goes next, the trailers looked like there’s much more to it. Might update the review when I get further.
_childDocuments_.name: Tin Hearts

_childDocuments_.review: From start to finish there is something happening; whether its a new interaction you can use, an important part of the story or a new piece of scenery there is always something to keep your attention.As far as puzzle games go, this ticks the boxes - everything you do fits the narrative and leads nicely into the story and/or the next part of the puzzle. With the freedom to have a nosey around you can really take your time and enjoy the surroundings, pictures on the wall, toys in the baskets and certificates on the walls. I was heavily reminded of an old time favourite, Lemmings.The story will take you on a journey full of emotion, and the ending delivers a true punch. The piano music throughout is a delight and very relaxing. The difficulty definitely increases as you progress but you are given the instructions seamlessly within the levels to help you along your journey.I would highly recommend this game to any gamer, whether you love a good story, a game with great music, puzzles, visually pleasant colours, or just a chill time to relax and immerse yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Tin Hearts

_childDocuments_.review: ** I'll leave my original review in place. I recommended it from my brief playthrough with some call outs of exceptions. BUT... regarding my "Exceptions":*** Please consider the Developer's response.**** I did not give this the time it may deserve, and their context may help you decide to give it a shot.Thanks!==== Original Review ====Recommended *if you are in the hunt for a PUZZLE game with small narrative rewards*Based on: Only 1 hour of gameplay.With limited research, heading into this: I will say I wasn't exactly sure what to expect from the trailer videos and preview videos. I liked how it certainly looks different and like something unique. And there seemed to be a depiction and suggestion of a compelling narrative woven into this title. This was supported by a few of the initial (albeit low volume) reviews coming in.>> One initial note (*the developer comments on this impression in a reply): If you got the impression that you directly control the toy-soldier type characters in this game that is not the case. You are in first-person control of someone in the room manipulating objects they run into. I just thought I'd call that out if you were someone less attentive like me that thought you might be latching yourself onto balloons and soaring through the air yourself and then solving puzzles as you walk about. Nope. Not NECESSARILY the developer's fault. Just my impulse reactions to visuals.1) If you love puzzle games, and that is your focus:- I think you'll love this. - I imagine many will find it novel how they are incorporating a story that briefly rewards you between puzzles.2) If you are looking to be immersed in some way:- After 1hr, I give it a "so-so". - The growing feature set of the puzzles is great, if you're looking for that.- The music is good, but repretitive. It sets a certain mood but Im not certain on the payoff without investing more time. Given the general mood many suggest from comments/reviews I'd suspect it will be fitting, albeit not anything that grabs you as you're worrying about puzzles.---- GRAPHICS ----- The visuals are decent. The character models and items you interact with particularly so. But you will find quite a few things with much lower resolution textures. I dont think they ruin the experience, but they certainly wont collectively give you the "wow" factor other modern releases might. 3) Narrative- As others have said: its not really leaning heavily on actual narration in the early stages of the game. Its more of a visual with a bit of mystery to what they're going to tell you. Its compelling in that way, but might be lacking for others.- Im being a bit judgey because I'm fresh off Bramble: The Mountain King, The Quarry, and Detroit: Become Human. Which isnt particularly a fair comparison. However if you've searched titles for unique story experiences where that is the main shining feature above most other elements.... this isnt the one for you I dont think. You have to be going in with a majority of your interest being the puzzles and then a reward of narrative with it.That's my take. I recommend it for the individuals I call out in the commentary, but I myself requested a refund since it wasn't what I was looking for.
_childDocuments_.name: Tin Hearts

_childDocuments_.review: Played through 1st chapter and one more level and really loved it thus far - great art, atmosphere and using various toys to guide your tin soldiers to exit is really nice mix-up on lemmings formula. Puzzles require some pondering - those aren't too easy.I will however hold back on other levels until VR mode is added.My only gripe right now is that there are some really low resolution textures on some props: moon emblems on doors in 1st chapter, red square carpet.And suggestion - advertisement banners or anything with text on it could have some game lore (higher res. textures so those could be read as is or text displayed in popup or audio playback when used).

_childDocuments_.review: Full Game: I played the game for 5 hours. I didn`t finished yet, but I passed half of the game. Is a nice game, with an emotional story. There are lots of puzzles and the levels are quite different so you won`t get bored. The music is great as well. The game is not really for grown up man, like, if you like this puzzles game, its a nice game to play. But I feel the game is more for kids around 10-15 years to teach critical thinking. I think is still worth playing in a nice chill sunday.So I finished the game in 13 hours. I got a good amount of achievements, and I manage to finish without hints. The story is emotional. In all this battle royal games, fast paced; this is a nice break from all that. Some bugs, especially at level 44; where you have to get the glove. It happened that the tin soldier would go outside the capsule and I would not be able to pass. Another bug is if you fast forward and go back more times and the spider is buging when catching the soldiers. I once got out of balance with a soldier. and sometimes some pipes where activated even if I didn`t do what I had to do to activate. Anyway with a simple restart of the level everything was fine. A bit annoying because I had to replay some levels but not a big deal since I knew what to do. To respond to developer question about how hard are the last levels; Is not that hard. Level 44 was a bit annoying because I didn`t know that I can destroy spiders with shocks but the difficulty I guess is fine. The only thing would be good if there would be a way to make a tutorial for the other machines, like glove, like the multiplication machine or others that are introduced first without you knowing what to do.
