_childDocuments_.review: This is a lot more fun than I expected- I was very much on the fence. I think Soulslite is bad marketing and it turned me off. I like good hard action games.For the first hour or two, I was unimpressed, but now I'm actually really enjoying myself. This certainly isn't as good as God of War, so play that first if you haven't, but it is quite fun and has a number of solid innovations that make it worth a playthrough. In particular, the XP multiplier is really fun- you build up a multiplier which is NOT time bound as you fight through enemies, based on skill/variety etc. You can cash it in at any time, but if you get hit, you lose your multiplier and just get the base experience. This makes farming a truly fun risk/reward game (not that farming is strictly necessary- it isn't on normal if you're decent- but if you want to get more skills and upgrades on Hard, it's fun!)I've heard tell that it's too short, but I'm still very early in the game after 6-7 hrs- so if you aren't playing on easy and breezing through the main quest, it feels like it has good run time (I could end up being wrong, but I've killed 0/5 BIG bosses so far)I don't like the main character, (brash in an annoying way) but she's not bad enough to ruin enjoyment of the game. The story is otherwise forgettable, but not in the way of the game.It's pretty good! Maybe get it on sale, but again- I was ready to return this one if it sucked, and I'm definitely enjoying my time with it.

As such, really feel like giving this more of a go than most typical fromsoft stamina locked attack trading that it feels like those turns into. Enki is goodest boi ^_^
_childDocuments_.name: Flintlock: The Siege of Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: A ways to go yet but it's a good example of the fun 7/10 type of game to me. Somewhere between God Of War and a Souls, bit harder than GoW but way faster and more fluid than Souls. Pretty significant emphasis on using the correct parry / dodge / interrupt and target priority, as well as some exploration.The world / lore seems cool, but it sounds like it's extremely unexplored in the game itself, outside of the first like hour of the game.I am unsure about the optimization complaints, it runs flawlessly for me and people I know so it might be issues with particular hardware or software, certainly much better optimized than like... _childDocuments_.review: Good graphics and Story so far. But terrible Souls game. _childDocuments_.review: Cool game with a cool setting who doesn't try to be 3 genre at once and doesn't make you wait 1 hour to jump straight to action (like God of The Last of War of Us). It's not a "try-hard" game with pattern-memorizing but it's not just button smashing, it's a good middle ground between the two and it does feel good to play something else rather than a From Software wannabe-game. Good linear level-design with visible connected area (just like Ashen), the small size of the areas is, again, a welcoming change in an oversaturated open-world market...It's not a AAAAAAAAA game, it does feel a little unpolished at times (the sound mixing is bad, some bugs with hitbox/ennemies getting stuck on things, etc) but it's still less buggy than the average overpriced, overpromised hundredfold A.Overall a good AA game, the kind of release between an indie-game (without being a rogue-lite/card game/survival game, in 2024, crazy !) and a budget ps4 game.

_childDocuments_.review: The character design for Nor, the player character, and Enki, your soon-to-be-companion for this adventure, along with their banter and conversations along the way is the highlight of Flintlock. There's story and emotion to be uncovered, and a few fun callbacks if you explore early and pay attention later. Their voice acting is wonderful, even if the direction sometimes falters a little and you have some tonal shifts, or recording volume switch-ups.During gameplay, Flintlock plays familiarly to many Souls-like games, with dodges, blocks, parries, and a multitude of attacks. Where Flintlock differs is by having many, many tools at your disposal, and by mostly taking away your ability to secure a stagger with a simple swing of your trusty axe. Throughout the game, you'll acquire grenades, several musket-style weapons, various pistols, Enki's help, and several axes that each have their strengths. The skill tree also unlocks new tactical options that will remain with you regardless of your choice of loadout - and in the case of charged attacks is even further altered by your specific choices of gun and axe.Unfortunately, despite the wide variety of options, as well as a double dodge and double jump, plus an air dash and some other movement options you can unlock along the way, Flintlock often ends up feeling stiff. This is mostly owed to the way Nor controls which feels like she is often sliding around during her animations. This is in contrast to some of the moves in the game where animation and movement are strongly tied together.What's even more disappointing, is that this stiffness also translates to Nor's air mobility, where you can use the double jump and air dash to change directions, but are otherwise completely locked into whatever direction you choose.Luckily, these issues of stiffness aren't a death knell for the game's satisfying fights, where coming through unscathed and with your combo intact can be truly exhilarating, and in an example of pure sublime design, the game's few fights against its biggest bosses are some of the most satisfying combat I've had in a long time, leaning on the power of spectacle and power fantasy, after a gruelling journey to get to them in the first place.I can easily recommend Flintlock, despite stiffness, simply to see Enki and Nor's relationship grow throughout their journey, and experience some truly wonderful boss fights.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly really enjoyed this game, it is very flawed and its gameplay is an odd mishmash of the recent god of wars and some souls elements, but, once you get through the rough beginning it comes into its stride and there's plenty of fun to be had, especially with the movement abilities, even if they feel oddly floaty. It's a very pretty game with some great views, performed well enough, great voice acting performances, particularly for the Nor and Enki, pretty solid story, with a really interesting world that we don't get to see enough of. The biggest problem was marketing it as a souls-lite, it certainly didn't do them any favors, builds the wrong expectations,  and frankly the game would have been better off just not having those elements in it anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: As not someone who likes insane difficulty, I was worried when I put this on "Normal" difficulty. But, all things considered, I'm glad I did. Fights could be challenging depending on how much attention I was paying, or how rushed I was at the moment. Traversal and movement was unique and different. The combat had some flavor to it, although the various main weapons (melee and ranged) didn't seem to have much actual impact on the way you played. The secondary ranged weapon was only really usable when you had the element of surprise, or managed to get a good interrupt in and some time to set it up. And then it was a little lackluster.The ending does feel unfinished. Kill a boss, a line or two of dialog, and then credits and a menu. No new game plus, no rewind and finish a few fights, and I never filled out all my trees or weapons, and no real feeling that it'd get a sequel or more story. it benefits from a play where you know what you want and you optimize for that. There were a lot of hidden things, but nothing that really made finding them worth it. A few weapons here or there, or some armor that needed a bit more variety. And the vanity shirt/pants weren't worth it.Still, despite all its flaws, the voice acting was good, there was plenty of various humor elements, the plot, while predictable for a souls light, felt like someone who cared wrote it, and it wasn't difficult to follow. I will happily be looking for DLC for the game, just continue on the story and see if there's any hint at what happens next.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a really good game and I recommend it even to the non-souls-lite fans: there is a lot of content for the buck and will keep you busy for a good 25-30 hours. I've only played on normal difficulty and in the beginning there are a few moments where the game seems harsh and unforgiving but roughly half-way through you will just cross the threshold with your character development and even bosses will only make you sweat a bit. You do not even need to farm (unless you're wasting reputation on a lot of cosmetics) so it does not get boring or repetitive and you can focus on the storyline all the way.The graphics, animations are good, maybe even great but do not quite reach the limits of the new Unreal engine (do not expect Senua's Saga-like visuals) but it is a solid work. Voice acting is good, there are not many great dialogs that you would remember years later, but they are well-written, witty, sometimes even funny. The story is good overall, even though there are no major surprises or plot-twists that would blow your mind but the world it paints is interesting, lively and colorful.The music is dynamic and atmospheric (altough not remarkable) and the sound effects are also good.Some tips including spoilers: I bought the game on Steam, only later realizing that it is included with the XBox Game Pass, so if you are subscribed, you don't need to spend on acquiring it.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game from these devs. Wonderful world design, excellent sound and VO work and the combat is pretty on point. The "jump" mechanic is rather floaty but it is what it is. Don't use it much unless I'm traversing tbh.  It's almost insane just how MUCH there is to explore in each area. MULTIPLE ways to approach a situation. See gunmen in the near distance. Circle around them and get them from behind. Don't want to do that? Use your "sniping" rifle to take em from a distance and get close to do melee with melee combatants. Story seems really interesting so far and am curious to see where it leads. The VO work for BAZ (character you will meet) is done by Elias Toufexis. The same guy that did the VO work for the newer Deus Ex games, FF VII Rebirth, Fortnite, Starfield as well as lots of others. The VO for the main character (NOR) is done by Olive Gray. She was in the Halo series if you watched. My point being that the VO work is stellar so far. Graphics are done really well also. Although NOT a AAA game release (the price point reflects that) I believe that A44 studio has done a great job of doing what they could. There are some muddy textures here and there, nothing immersion breaking. Like I said before, the jump mechanic is rather "floaty" as well. Still, there's a LOT to like here. It's a Souls-LITE. You WILL need to be on point and use the mechanics the game gives you to accomplish battles. However, the game is NOT Stamina based so swing to your heart's content. All in all, unless I encounter serious issues, bug or crashes, this game is pretty awesome tbh. I've noticed ZERO misconnects, ZERO hit box misses or anything odd or weird. Having a blast.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy this game a decent amount. It took a while through the first major open zone for it to click with me and I don't think the combat is well balanced at the onset (with a lot of enemies that you don't have direct answers for and enemies do unblockables as much or more than regular attacks). But once you get some abilities to deal with armor and shields it evens out.This gameplay, exploration, and art are all very good and gel together to create a fun and well paced experience. The lore is good. The story telling, voice acting, sound mixing, and writing are all sub par which really hurts the story telling.The simplest comparison is to say this game's combat and exploration feel like god of war, while the level design and leveling/respawn mechanics are souls like. That is to say, it combines strong elements from two amazing styles of games and I think it's a good value at the price point.As for DEI. I don't like feeling preached to in my games and if it's too on the nose it will knock me right out of it. This game may have sweet baby involvement, but IMO, it didn't harm the overall game as it really just affected character designs at a superficial level and it doesn't feel preachy in any way. If you can't support games with Sweet Baby, I get it. but if you just want to know if it's had a huge negative impact, it has not in my opinion.I really love when the AA market makes games at this quality level so I'm happy this one turned out so well and I hope word of mouth helps it pick up some sales as the months go on. This is a quality game that punches above the budget price.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's release got straight out poisoned by the association with the SBI cancer. Having played over ten hours other than some aesthetics I've yet to strike any overt DEI moralising. You'll cop more in five minutes of Starfield than anything I've seen so far. For those that can get past playing a black female, you'll find the character Nor is a decent and likeable protagonist. She and the sidekick Enki are well voiced and fit their characters. The bad: There are some apparent bugs which should have been picked up before release. Fullscreen is effectively borked without any way to change resolution. The workaround is set your desktop resolution to whatever you want and use a borderless window. I had a crash bug where at the first lodestone it would lockup at a select the inventory dialog. After a couple of attempts I got past this by selecting another menu item first. The lockon mechanic could use some work. Sometime you lock onto unintended background items. If you have no target in view it would help if it locked to the nearest target. Nor's running animation is a bit weird. I think it relates to the character model. The legs run but her backside and hips stay almost still. Sometimes when existing from the setting menu you repeatedly get stuck in a loop with a dialog pop-up to save your settings despite already acknowledging the dialog. The good: I've had no CTD events. The graphics are very attractive and the game runs really well. There is a tiny amount of shader complie stutter but considering it doesn't precompile it's excellent. There is also a small amount of the typical UE pop-up but minor. If only EA could manage to make games that run this well. Maybe I didn't 'get gud' enough for Dark Souls but I'm finding the combat challenging. Similar broad mechanic's, you get Lodestones in place of camp fires (you actually get campfires too). Enemies respawn after resting. Yadder, yadder. I've seen comments about there being no dodge but there certainly is. I love the character design for Enki with the coat of iridescent feathers and the animation is spot on. Hopefully the bugs get fixed and more people give the game a fair go, I don't condone the SBI agenda but as far as Flintlock goes it is really overblown. Overall really enjoying the game.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all this game is not a soulslike, its much closer to God of War (2018) than any FromSoft game. Which is absolutely fine and despite rather cold critical reception it turned out to be a lot of fun to play. Its a solid 7/10 game, with interesting setting, good graphics and engaging gameplay. The story is kinda meh, despite interesting setting and premise. There is some banter between main character and her companions, but its rather insubstantial. It doesn't feel like there is a specific goal to accomplish in each location, I was just making progress for the gameplay's sake, but once I beaten the first big boss I wasn't even sure who it was and why it needed to die. It was mentioned before, but it wasn't fleshed out or justified enough.I am not here for the story though and on the gameplay front this game delivers in spades. Though I admit at first movement felt a bit floaty and I needed a moment to get a hang of it. Once I started to unlock new moves on the skill trees and game opened up a bit it really clicked. Moving around feels great, your character zips around with double jumps and air dodges, platforming is satisfying and there is not a hint of yellow paint to be found anywhere. Its not an open world game, more of a hub based adventure with three different biomes. They are quite distinct from one another and an interesting mix of themes. You will unlock these purple portals to use as shortcuts or to access secret areas. There is actually a little bit of depth to using these portals. If you time your inputs right you can keep this nice flow between portal jumps and you can also jump out of the portal in three different ways: rolling down, dash forward or high jump. These are actually fun to use in some platforming sections.Combat is just as strong in Flintlock. Since your character is a bit squishy at first (even on Normal difficulty), you need to utilize every tool in your arsenal to succeed. Thankfully there is a lot to choose from. You have your right hand melee weapon which comes in a few variations, my favorite being this fiery axe that causes explosions on charge attack. In left hand you have a gun, which is the most varied and useful tool you have, as it functions like your regular ranged weapon with lock-on, but its also a parry button AND is used to interrupt enemy actions. There is a lot of depth in the use of your gun and its always satisfying to pull off a perfect parry followed up by gunshot to the enemy face.Outside of your main tools, you can also pull out the secondary guns, which are slow to reload and serve more of a utility purpose, like crowd control or sniping enemy shooters. They even implemented a Sniper Elite-like bullet camera for the sniper headshots (its a bit janky, but hilarious). If the 'big guns' are not enough for you, there is a variety of grenades to use, they aren't a big damage dealers and are used to apply status effects like burning, shock etc.Enemy variety is pretty good and well designed, each biome has a different cast of baddies. We encounter medieval knights, pirates, zombies, ostriches (what?), the works. There aren't that many bosses, just a few main ones and some mini bosses, that are just a variant of standard enemies. Nothing to write home about thus far, but they do the job and can be quite challenging (bloody Sealed Lord).Performance wise its pretty smooth, stable 60 FPS at 1440p with everything maxed out on RTX3070. I had one crash in 15 hours of gameplay and one part of Writ city caused a bit of a slowdown. Good performance is a rare thing these days (looking at you Jedi Survivor) and A44 Games deserve a praise for delivering such a good looking game in a well optimized state.Overall Flintlock: The Siege of Dawn is solid AA game, that won't wow you with its story, but provides a fun, smooth and engaging gameplay in an interesting, original setting. Making a new IP is not an easy task and I commend the devs for going for it and actually delivering a solid result. I wasn't a big fan of their previous game - Ashen, but I think they found their stride with Flintlock. I really hope this game finds its audience, despite so-so critical reception. I think we'll have a Darksiders 3 situation here, which also got a mediocre scores at launch, but was considered an underrated gem after some time. Also, screw SkillUp for giving this 'not recommended' score, what an a$$, poses as an indie/AA games advocate only to burn them when someone tries something new.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially approached this game with an open mind, despite the considerable noise and criticism surrounding it. However, I regret not heeding the warnings. To start, the game crashed multiple times, a glaring issue that should have been addressed before release.Once I managed to get past the crashes, I found the gameplay to be exceedingly disappointing. This is perhaps the most generic and uninspired attempt at a Dark Souls clone I have ever encountered. The game world is dull, devoid of meaningful content, and utterly unengaging. The difficulty level is egregiously unbalanced, making it a frustrating and unrewarding experience. For reference, I completed Elden Ring and found it thoroughly enjoyable, but this game felt more like a tedious chore rather than an having fun.Adding to the dismal experience is the overt agenda-pushing by the developers. The inclusion of certain characters, particularly a black female protagonist, felt forced and disingenuous, clearly a result of pandering to DEI mandates rather than genuine storytelling. This misplaced focus detracts from the game and alienates players. Moreover, the involvement of SBI in the game's development has predictably led to another failure. The pattern is clear: their influence consistently results in subpar products, and this game is no exception.From a technical standpoint, the game feels incomplete and poorly optimized. Charging $40 for such an unfinished product is not just unreasonable; it's exploitative. I wouldn't be surprised if the player base dwindles to single digits within a month, forcing the game to go to free-to-play model out of sheer necessity.In summary, this game is a prime example of how not to develop and market a video game. It is uninteresting, unenjoyable, and grossly overpriced. The negative reviews are justified, and I strongly advise against purchasing this game. Save your money and your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty solid game. I'll start with the cons:Sound mixing is weird. Things play at a mostly appropriate volume, but with zero indications of direction, and I swear, the last boss is just mumbling. Thankfully, I have subtitles on, and I think that boss is supposed to be speaking another language anyway. It's "close enough" for the most part, and I wouldn't be surprised if it got patched.And a conversation takes place at the 9th of 8 health+ shrines involving a character who is, at that point, dead. It would have made a LOT of sense to have the conversation pop up on #8, and the achievement for getting them all at #9.That concludes the "why didn't they fix that?" issues. I did struggle against the wildlife as it's hard to tell what's an attack and what's normal movement. But I suspect that's a "me" thing, and there's a good deal of wind-up in most of the animations to identify what's about to happen. Most attacks are not BS... excepting one shield guy's no-windup bash, but it also doesn't do much damage.Now the awesome:Mild-spoiler-- There is an optional fight rather early on. Stone guardian, it makes it clear he's there to test you. The fight is extremely rough, as he can two-shot you, and your best option is parrying. The reward is a weapon that gains damage bonus equal to your current XP modifier, and gets a nice red sheen as the bonus goes up. Which resets when you get hit or bank the XP. (nice mechanism when I'd remember it) And it requires zero upgrade materials beyond XP. Which makes it feel a LOT like it's an optional bonus thing. Which you only get... if you prove that you can play well enough for it to be useful. And when you beat the guardian, he congratulates you as he crumbles away. This is a series of good design choices and had my expectations running high throughout.The skill tree is solid. Every entry is a new move or substantial upgrade to an existing mechanic. They all contribute to a modest damage bonus to either melee, magic, or firearm damage... and that's the only minor anything.The best skill for my money was one that tweaked the armor sets. There's only 3 slots, and you only need 2 to activate a set bonus. The skill makes the 3rd one have its own set bonus active. 's 5 different sets, that's a lot of interesting builds you can make right there. I'm only just now realizing I could have made one boss encounter so much easier if I'd changed out one thing. XD Hindsight. ^^;I managed to complete the whole thing, got all the sidequests, all the important loot... although I did cheat regarding XP. It's a single player game, I'm here to explore and have fun, not make a job of it. Optional bosses aside, this is not a particularly hard game. I played on normal.I quite liked it. Feels about the right length for the story they wanted to tell.

_childDocuments_.review: First things first: While Flintlock definitely has some soulslike trappings, mainly in the way it handles death, it is really just a fairly competent riff on God of War 2019 -- if Kratos had a double jump and an air dash. Yes, there's a parry and a dodge roll but there's no stamina bar you have to nurse and you can actually pause the game ;) While the combat doesn't feel especially good, the graphics aren't anything to write home about (except when they sometimes are) and the story is flimsy at best, this game just offers so many mechanics and they all tie together rather elegantly. Shooting, stabbing, throwing grenades, and magic are just a few ways you can dispatch enemies -- and the game actively encourages you to switch it up by upping your score multiplier, almost like it's Devil May Cry. So yes, the game is good. Some great loot, beautiful music and chill vistas -- for less than 30 bucks I paid it's more than worth it.Now, I know, the question that's been burning on everyone's mind: is the game woke? Just kidding, I don't know. But you know what's certainly not woke? Touching grass.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Flintlock is a really solid single player campaign with zero microtransactions or predatory content. The campaign is relatively short and focused with an almost linear path albeit set in one giant open world type map with unlockable interconnecting shortcuts as you would expect from any game that takes its cues from the souls genre.This is very much a souls-lite and its marketed as such. I don't tend to enjoy the souls genre as i find the demand too frustrating. This game has certainly presented me with a number of intimidating foes and difficult encounters that i've had to attempt several times but it's never had the level of frustration and i never felt like i was wasting my time.The story and pacing keeps you moving forward the whole time and while there are minor deviations such as a few side quests or places to explore they almost always reward you with an upgrade or something that will improve your ability to face more challenging enemies. Tonally i love the game. It's got a fairly somber vibe. The voice acting of the central character carries the same cadence and tone as the central characters in Hades and it fits the game world perfectly. Some repeated voice lines get a little tedious ever time you pick up resources but its a minor complaint to an overall fantastically well voiced game.The story is really good. I enjoyed the theme, the character development and some of the more thought provoking and philosophical conversations between your character and Enki as you wonder around.The music is fantastic throughout. Its never intrusive and always builds on the atmosphere and theme. There are moments when i swear that the music reached a much more intense level as i crested a rooftop or hill almost like it was under-scoring the magnificent view i had uncovered.Combat and movement is good once you get to grips with it. I'm playing on Mouse and Keyboard which isn't recomended by the game but works just fine. Once you start to uncover some elemental weapons and unlock some beter skills combat gets really satisfying. The enemy animation and signaling of attacks is very well done and for someone like me who struggles with Souls games i found things really easy to get to grips with. The challenge on the middle setting felt decent enough never being too easy to get dull and never getting too difficult to become a frustration.Traversal is really nice as well with a wonderfully fun way to travel through shortcuts you can unlock as well as the blackpowder abilities which while pretty generic (double jump and double dodge) are presented very nicely and thematically in-line with the game and character and serve their purpoe well.It took me a little while to get into the groove with this game but once things clicked i could not put it down and now i feel that the end is close i really don't want it to be over which is always the sign of a well paced game.Would love to see additional story content for this game as DLC down the road.

_childDocuments_.review: Flintlock: The Siege of Dawn - A Captivating Souls-Lite JourneyFlintlock: The Siege of Dawn is an ambitious entry into the action role-playing genre, carving its own niche as a 'Souls-Lite' game. Developed with Unreal Engine 4, it promises an experience that balances challenge with accessibility, making it an ideal gateway for newcomers to the Souls-like genre. Flintlock brilliantly manages to ease players into the typically unforgiving world of Souls-like games. The gameplay mechanics are intuitive, challenging, and rewarding as you get more precise. The world it's set in offers a satisfying blend of combat and exploration. The game introduces players to its demanding style gradually, ensuring that newcomers aren't overwhelmed right out of the gate.One standout feature is the photo mode editor, a unique touch that allows players to capture the game’s breathtaking moments. It’s a delightful addition that adds a layer of personalization and creativity to the gaming experience.The game’s charm is further elevated by Enki, a fox-like demon companion who quickly becomes an endearing part of your adventure. Enki’s presence isn't just for show; his abilities are integral to your survival and success. Honestly, this little spirit demon deserves his own line of plushies!Flintlock’s visual presentation is nothing short of breathtaking. Built on Unreal Engine 4, the game delivers intense and immersive graphics that keep you on the edge of your seat. Characters are uniquely designed, each one contributing to the game’s vibrant and often eerie atmosphere.The audio quality complements the visual splendor perfectly. The soundtrack and sound effects enhance the overall immersion, pulling you deeper into the game's world. Whether it's the clashing of swords or the subtle sounds of the environment, every audio detail is meticulously crafted.Flintlock: The Siege of Dawn is a visually stunning and engaging 'Souls-Lite' game that serves as a perfect entry point for those new to the genre. Its combination of accessible gameplay, beautiful graphics, and compelling audio creates a memorable gaming experience. And with features like the photo mode editor and the adorable Enki, it offers unique elements that set it apart from its peers.Whether you’re a seasoned veteran of Souls-like games or a curious newcomer, Flintlock promises a captivating and rewarding adventure. BTW, can you defeat the first boss you're introduced to? I'm told the closest someone has gotten is 50% health! Ready to take on that challenge? Oh and careful around the evil chocobo's . wink

_childDocuments_.review: If you're playing Flintlock as part of Gamergate 2.0 to get mad and throw a fit, there's plenty for you to find.  If you're just a normal person here to enjoy a smaller game, I think it's an easy recommend if a little pricey.    (I played on normal difficulty on a controller)     Story and Characters: Easily the weakest part of the game.  Only the main pair have any real character to them, and while they're fun to listen to throughout, they remain pretty static.  The stakes and scale of the story do a lot for making the boss fights feel important and your actions consequential.  I found the design of the world and the enemies to be gorgeous throughout.      Gameplay: Once I fixed up the controls, I found the combat and movement incredibly fluid and fun-- like a quicker God of War with a Bloodborne feel.  The game encourages you to take control of the battlefield with your tools and movement.  If you play it like Elden Ring, you're not going to have fun.  The guns feel weighty and fun, the armor is unique and encourages different kinds of play, and the main melee weapons are reliable if limited.  I found it challenging in places (less challenging than other games in the genre) but fairer than other games in the genre.  Exploration is always rewarded one way or another.  I never experienced any glitches during combat other than non-obtrusive visual bugs.        Side Content: This game's side content is how side content should be.  90% of collectables outside of a weird flag quest yield unique dialogue and lore.  The side quests are succinct, build on the characters and world, and give proper rewards.  The upgrade and reputation system was a little annoying, but I had no trouble completing late tier content with unleveled gear.  Flintlock respects your time without 30+ hours of filler content like other open world games.  What is here is good, mostly polished, and not required for progression.  There are no arbitrary level requirements or anything.  If you are struggling, the game's side content is there to help.      Length: I finished the main story and much of the side stuff in around 14 hrs.  The game is compact, but it doesn't waste your time on meaningless side content.  I really appreciated this and hope the trend of shorter titles sticks around.       Glitches: My system isn't in the best state, but I never experienced more than very scattered lag spikes and an annoying glitch where my death XP disappeared twice in the same room.  Not a single crash, though, which I wasn't expecting at all from a brand new game from a smaller studio.

_childDocuments_.review: Flintlock is not a bad game.  I can understand people being wary of buying it seeing the SBI involvement and rightfully so as SBI has a track record of any game they are involved in being pretty awful, and I went in expecting to hear all about colonizers and the poor struggling main character who had it tough and happily got none of that (though more of her later).  I played on the hardest difficulty (possessed) and the beginning was quite challenging when I had no combat options and I would die in a few hits, but as the game went on it became more balanced.  Gameplay would be most similar to 2018 God of War; you have your standard melee attacks, block, dodge and parry.  Enki your stand in Atreus has his stun attacks and his large rune attack.  You have the titular flintlock which is used much like the firearms in Bloodborne for interrupting attacks, and grenades of various types for extra flavor though difficult to get to in the middle of combat since it occupies the healing flask slot.  You have three armor slots (Head, Shoulder, Hand) and five different armor sets.  The armor provides no statistical benefit (no extra HP, no extra attack power), but changes the way the characters plays (extra distance on melee attacks, slow down time if you dodge last second, etc.).  The leveling system is three interlinked trees (Firearms, Melee, Magic) and each node gives a new skill or enhancement to existing skills with each node in a tree giving a small boost to the damage from that tree to a maximum of 140%.The game takes a while for the combat to really show itself and I would say I started to appreciate it around when I got my first piece of armor which I believe was a few hours into the game.  From then on things felt balanced where I could clear towns without dying, but if I was lazy I could be killed easily (this may vary depending on the difficulty you play on).The characters are mostly enjoyable though the main character seems to start off as annoying and headstrong but fairly quickly matures.  Enki was great though having him constantly tell me I am a natural after 20 hours (days/weeks? in game time) of going through the slip gates got old.  The rest of the sapper crew were a mixed bunch, but by the end I enjoyed them for what they were, old man father figure, stoic guy, other guy, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ chick that respects you.The story was enjoyable but I swear this game was meant to be another 25% longer or so as some plot points (betrayals) are immediately glossed over in cut-scenes; e.g. character A betrays character B's trust, in the immediate cut-scene another character says they've been talking among themselves and when you get back to gameplay it's all good.  It's very jarring having these moments that feel important suddenly get shuffled off with no time to digest.  The world is interesting, the enemies are fine (some better than others and the later ones better than the early ones), the music was enjoyable.There are bugs and I have doubts they will be fixed, they don't stop you from completing the game but they are real annoying.  One bug is that a horde (large group of normal enemies you can clear for extra exp/money) could not be completed as the final enemy would not count toward the total group health and so when all of the enemies were killed the encounter never ended.  The second bug I ran into was that on the enemy turn in the Sebo mini-game if you open and close the special piece menu while hovering over a special piece you will constantly remove turns from the enemy even giving the enemy negative turns meaning as soon as they make their first move they lose the game (I hated Sebo so once I realized this was still a thing I abused it).  The third bug I encountered was that after winning a game of Sebo the game stopped asking if I wanted to keep playing Sebo and just assumed I did, I could not escape the mini-game even if I forfeit the match and so had to alt f4 out of the game (though winning the match had been saved).  I had one crash on the final boss during a cutscene in between phases which made me start the whole fight over, but did not set my health or resources to pre-fight conditions, but that was my one game crash.  I had quite a few bad stutters while playing which did sometimes lead to me dying (less than ten more than five).Overall Flintlock isn't going to revolutionize anything, but if you are looking for a not quite open world (again like GoW 2018) with a decent combat system and ok world, some decent characters, for a decent price then you could do worse than this.

_childDocuments_.review: Can only play as a woman... in a game about using brute force to defeat opponents.Stupidly immersion breaking when every fight is followed up with "yeah, right" when you smack an opponent across the room.  Especially when they are at least double your size.And that's in addition to the fact that for some reason you only get 3 shots with your flintlock pistol (that you don't actually reload), but is your primary source of interrupts and damage.  Confusing mechanics choice there by the developers.  So you're stuck using your axe for most of the damage which... as I mentioned is pathetically unbelievable when you're a tiny woman.The levels all seem to be linear and basically disguised rooms with mobs waiting for you to fight them.There's some kind of mechanic where you're basically gambling with your "reputation" which is garnered by killing mobs, but it disappears if you don't cash it in and get hit...   again, kind of amusingly poor choice by the developers.The usual tropes are there.. Red attacks means unblockable.There's a block/parry skill just like every other game lately that only seems to work when it wants to.The sprint key is rebound to CTRL for some reason and shift is your dodge instead of sprint.. no idea why.  Massive stuttering if you have a current-gen video card.  You'll need to look up some articles on how to fix it and what to disable.Oh, and... this whole adventure happens because you shot a gun at a forcefield... and broke it.... during a war... when people are shooting guns constantly.Yeah, so much of this is garbage.

_childDocuments_.review: Flintlock is a good game that falls short of being great, its a bit rough starting off pushing alot of buttons and mechanics on you for combat some with very tight timing windows but after i while and you learn to control the chaos it ends up being quite fun with brutal animations for critical attacks and explosions knocking enemies around.The reputation system is this games twist on souls where you can stack a combo for a bonus but it never really felt good, its very hard to track in combat and considering its a souls like i'm probably going to get hit at least once or twice in a fight or the game would be too easy, unless your perfect it feels like its just punishing you for doing nothing but playing the game.Progression in this game felt fine but never really stretched beyond that with only 4 sets of gear each having unique effects and set bonuses and around 20 weapons its a good variety but never gets enough to flesh out build crafting and variety, the game has 2 main areas with a 3rd being a walk up to the finally and one small one for a side area so progression is very fast as its not a huge game but i never had enough currency to upgrade lesser equipment like grenades and rifles so i would normally shelf them and favour my already upgraded melee weapon.If you are looking for a shorter rpg i would recommend picking this up its a good experience for the duration i just wish it had a bit more in it.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun RPG souls-"lite" with strong God-of-War influences.I enjoyed the mechanics of Enki, the double jump and jump-dodge. Story is pretty normal and straightforward, but that's not a bad thing - a refreshing change coming off a bunch of FromSoft games.The counters, the move breaks, axe/pistol executions and the movement fit together in a really nice flow once you get a few upgrades going and the game does a great job of making you feel _awesome_. The whole reputation multiplier mechanic is a nice bit of innovation, and (minor spoilers) there's a weapon you can get that gets more powerful the higher your multiplier, which really encourages you to stay in the flow and risk-it-for-the-biscuit for even more damage and reputation. The portal travel is also good fun.Big shout-out to the general aesthetic as well, refreshing change.It's not totally perfect, the dodge could be a teeny bit longer, the graphics could do with a minor upgrade, and I think given how powerful the game makes you feel, it would really benefit from giving you more enemies to plow through by upping the density and aggression slightly, enemies, especially the dead are a bit sparse, which is a pity, because of how much fun they are to fight through.Overall, fun game. Always here for small/medium studios doing some new stuff, nothings perfect, but this definitely earned it's price, and as I said, always keen to see fresh new stuff like this from studios.Overall, 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Is this a good game? No. It's clunky, it's janky, animations don't flow, the sound balancing is way off, combat is full of weird balancing issues caused by the inability to cancel, and it puts a bad foot forward.That said: once the game gets rolling, and you have a few of the key skills unlocked, it really comes into its own, and the entertaining flow of combat becomes less an occasional glimpse of a better game, and the constant reality of Flintlock's combat. When it's working properly, it's FUN. The give and take between your various tools and powers to solve various problems gives encounters an enjoyable right key for the right lock feel, and though it started to get frustrating again toward the end, there's a lot of good meat through the middle. The price is right, I think.What genuinely surprised me though was the writing. The bones of the plot are nothing special, but the world and the character dialogue are both extremely strong, and the arcs of the two central characters, as well as the quality voice acting and the consistently-strong exchanges between them, left me surprised and impressed.This isn't a great game, strictly speaking from a technical standpoint, but I had a lot of fun, I finished it, and I'm glad it exists.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I really liked this game. It's a clever play on the souls-like gameplay that makes it generally much, much more accessible and casual (without ever feeling braindead or overly easy).The gameplay overall is very good throughout (with only a few misses in gameplay, or bugs/issues), the game is pretty enough that I'd actively look at the scenery (though never truly breathtaking), and the story is surprisingly solid despite it's rough start (Enki quickly becomes rather endearing). There's some minor gripes throughout (mantling often clips through objects, you can sometimes get stuck on objects and unable to move, a couple of times enemies spawned inside terrain) but overall none of these impacted the experience in any significant manner.The only major thing I'd state for people to be aware of is that the game's rather short, I 100%'d the game in just over 16 hours (not quite, but in terms of meaningful content definitely), and that was with me frequently only playing it for 5 minute intervals (thus losing a lot of time to re-orienting myself and figuring out what I was doing). If you blast through the story and ignore everything else, I'd be surprised if you didn't finish the game in less than half that. To me, this was a good thing. I generally prefer short, high quality games and Flintlock absolutely delivers. But if you're looking for a game to play for 40+ hours this isn't it.Overall, definitely would recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a neat little action adventure with soulslike elements. You've got your estus flask and bonfire equivalents, however the actual combat and camera placement are more akin to the recent God of War games. The traversal is also very Jedi Survivor-like - you got double jump, air dash, sliding down a slope, phasing through portals etc. So yeah, it's a bit of a mishmash but it works for the most part. The audio mix could use some work (everything is either overly compressed and earsplittingly loud or barely audible) and the controller vibration is very bare bones -> they could have done much more here, like adding rumble effect for sliding, parrying and air dash. The story feels like another take on the God of War formula, what with the whole killing gods theme. It's set in this alternate fantasy land that combines Medieval, 17th century and WW1-era Europe, but also ancient Egypt and Aztec Mexico because why not. Your companion is a little fox-like god called Enki that functions in a similar manner to Atreus in GoW. He assists you in combat but can also be upgraded to perform large magical attacks.7.5/10 It doesn't exactly reinvent the wheel + technical issues, however for a small AA release it's pretty impressive.
_childDocuments_.name: Flintlock: The Siege of Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting combat system. Pretty good combat mechanics, range of weapons and styles. Good to play but not sure if it's worth at full price. Overall completion is easy, only 1 really hard achievement. Multiplier system is extremely cool and definitely motivated me to play around more.Storytelling could have been longer honestly. This is one of the reasons why it's not worth at full price because so much of the story feels rushed. Anyone other than the main character and maybe 1 or 2 side characters get a proper buildup and even then its generous. Even after spending hours on that 1 really hard achievement mentioned above (and farming maybe 1-2 hours?) I only took 25 hours. Probably only took me 19 hours to finish the game honestly. Even shorter if you don't go for 100%. If you're playing this for the souls-like difficulty, I suggest picking the hardest difficulty. Easy doesn't net achievements and normal gets really easy really fast once you get used to the mechanics. It was basically a cakewalk once I got used to the whole game.Some negatives are the Mantle ability; you know the ledge grab thing. If you double jump up against a wall, your character will be forced to face the side, which means you can't mantle... then fall to your death.If the Devs ever read this, I suggest expanding on the range of enemies to help extend the story because that can really help push this all the way to AAA quality other than some annoying bugs and stuff like the mantling issue.TLDR: Get on discount, it's quite a good game but not worth at full price right now.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy souls-likes to a limited extent, but am not always down with the difficulty (I have dexterity problems due to severe arthritis). This has a lot of the good parts of souls-likes: Challenging combat, death penalties, and careful planning against bosses.It also has freakin' difficulty settings!I spend most of my time on Normal, but while I was sick dealing with medication reactions I wanted to play.. But didn't have even my barely functional reaction times, so I dropped the difficulty down to story for the day, and was able to have fun.Anyway, it's a fun game. The story is interesting and the world itself is fascinating.. And Enki, your sidekick? Really well written. His little bits of dialog while you explore the world are great.Only real gripe I have is the audio has no spatial processing.. So once you're in "hearing" range, the sound is just as loud as if they were right next to you, which gets annoying (here's hoping they fix that in a patch).It's not AAA - it's a AA title, for sure - but it's also priced just right and is a good fun game.Here's hoping we see some good updates. The team is receptive to community feedback from what I've seen; Crossing my fingers for transmog and NG+. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Overall Flintlock was an overall shorter and more straight forward game with fun hack and slack combat and an interesting narrative. Nothing felt particularly new for the game, but if you a fan of action/RPGs, Hack&slash, or souls like getting this game at price or on sale I think it is worth the experience. Some negatives for me would be the World design and specific narrative beats. (no spoilers). Certain vendors, mini-game NPC, and item locations felt randomly thrown around to try and flesh out the world and make it feel larger than it is. Across the game you have about 2 regions and about 3 distinct locations (once you combine smaller segments). The game's mini-game Sebo has random NPC thrown around, while some locations such as hamlets make since on more than one occasion I would find a Sebo player in the middle of an undead invested region being left alone to enjoy their game. I always found this odd. The narrative, while interesting to me, is a plot about the people of the world rising up in a 10 year war against the undead and their gods. I had a lot of questions about the overall world and how certain pieces connected I never felt were properly answers or even fleshed out by the team, Some of the timeline that the protagonist and her companion mention don't exactly line up and there was mentions of certain event before the start of the game I think are owed further exploration to fully make sense of what cause the war to start and who was really winning from it. There's also a few bugs I ran into across my 24 hours playing the game. Enemies would get stuck as if their AI could not switch between states allowing me to freely attack them. Some of the purple flying points would not unlock because enemies were on the other side of a wall (that I could not access from my location). I also feel some balancing with the game's economy is due, the main currency reputation (think souls) issued to upgrade all your weapons and armor, unlock new skills, and purchase new cosmetic clothes from vendors. By the end of the game I’d done all side missions, freed all helmets, gotten all health upgraded, beaten all revenants and kills the random enemies across the world 2 or 3 times over and only managed to unlock half the total skill tree, fully upgrade 1 weapons (with everything else being upgraded half way) and still needed about 2 or 3 times the total reputation I had amassed so far to fully unlock everything. I feel like lowering costs or increasing gain would help with allowing me to get more. There isn’t to much in the way of enemies to farm to get a lot of Rep. and with no NG+ I don’t really have a chance or incentive to unlock everything. (which I usually prefer doing)Taking all of this into account, from a new and fairly unique world, and a promising but mostly undercooked narrative, a few bugs and balancing issues I think the game would sit somewhere at a 5 or 6 out of 10. You probably want to wait for a sale, but I managed to get the game for $30 and at that price I would say it’s worth the 20-30 hours to play through casually.

_childDocuments_.review: For starters, I really enjoyed this game from start to finish, despite the short length and breakneck pacing. I think it actually is a service to the game oddly enough. Yet I find the complaints to still be fair since the game progresses at a breakneck pace.I would like to highlight the way this game describes itself; A "Souls-lite" while this is a 'fitting' genre name from a distance, it really feels sorta misplaced and even wrong? The game "is a souls-lite" through some mechanics like bonfires and respawning enemies, plus other things that are in the genres DNA.Those feel like vague influences to a degree though, I don't mean that as an insult - I loved seeing those influences.It's just that there are flashy abilities and the game rewards you for mixing up combos and throwing in fresh moves. There's upgrade trees that give you passives and unique abilities and even unique special abilities. Calling it a hack n slash feels MUCH more fitting for the style of game it truly is. I do not mean to bash on the game in anyway by doing this. I just think that due to the genre, it may be hitting the wrong audience? Maybe I'm just thinking too hard about things. I would gladly call this a hack n slash instead.Anyway, Flintlock as a whole is a pretty enjoyable game from start to finish. It may have some lacking qualities but it excels in some places while faltering in some others. The narrative is surprisingly well decent and forwardly presented, you will hear the world talked about by Nora and Enki, you will watch them develop a friendship and grow together. The narrative, to a degree, is designed around them and they comment on every side-quest, sometimes they comment on small areas that are off the beaten path, they will share thoughts on things and have regular conversation.As you continue through the games narrative, you will find companions that were part of the games intro scattered around the world as you progressive the narrative, they have their own dedicated side quests and are a little one-note? I didn't really mind given the games length, though with the focus on story in mind, it felt a little strange. The side quests added some nice development to the characters though!Which leads me to say that the voice acting is pretty alright but the production is kind of all over the place. Some characters sound too close to the microphone, while others are at a good distance and some characters sound a little overproduced and muffled, some even sound distant. Production on voices is a real toss-up.I find the lore and world to be quite interesting, It is not nearly as deeply written as one might want, but its serviceable and has its own factions, rules, bounds and other such things you would expect, as mentioned above- The world is a regular topic and is talked about by Nora and Enki, almost as much as the core narrative. Not much to say, I find the world to be kind of neat.Music is pretty decent for boss-fights, it takes a different tone than I would expect, going for suspenseful and sort of ambient in places. Then jumping to being explosive and almost like the musical pieces itself are trying to be a spectacle, the music shares some issues with VA production though unfortunately. Its always a little too loud and the mixing is kind of off? Some instrumentation kind of falls way or overpowers other pieces. Kind of upsetting, overall I did not mind the soundtrack.I sorta covered some pieces of gameplay when I unnecessarily ranted about the game genre, but its got its ups and downs. Enemy variety is nothing too special and can feel a bit bland, some designs are downright frustrating? Their animations don't quite work properly or their attacks come out just a tad too fast. Sometimes unblockable attacks come out pretty fast, to the point where it interrupts your pistol shot. Maybe that's a skill issue though.The armor systems are kinda the best part of the game regarding build variety and the changes to gameplay. I found a pauldron that slowed down time when I perfectly dodged and I found another set that spread curses and made those curses explode. Extremely fun and I loved it, your build lives off of your armor choices and to a degree- Your weapon choices.The weapon choices in the game are pretty entertaining to be completely honest, although I didn't use over half of what I found, the things I stuck to where genuinely super fun and I loved using them and mixing it up between my mainstay weapons. Although the melee weapon variety was a little disappointing, choosing between a sword and axe (which really only have minor speed changes and minor animation changes.) to a hammer (slower, and heavier.) was a bit of a let-down. It's a great thing that the skill system is robust. Briefly covering that, the skill system has 3 different options; Ranged - Magic - Melee.They have dedicated abilities and passives to each tree, but they also have some that bleed over and offer passives for both. Its unique and refreshing to see in a game like this, I can see a few different build options that someone might do, it may be small but I can see a lot of fun being had with some of them- I personally ran a curse oriented build with melee and magic thrown in.Let's cover those core combat mechanics that I have been mentioning such as curses.Curses are a another system that let you apply various status effects (though the list is small) and they are somewhat vital to the gameplay loop? At least the Prime status effect is- It enables critical attacks (Akin to backstabs and ripostes) and allows you to remove enemy armor and shields.Some weapons apply those status effects too! Quite early you can find an axe that applies Burn and I later found weapons that applied other status effects as well.I mentioned enemy armor and shields, enemy armor is displayed by overlaying the standard health bar but the damage you to do armor also applies to health. The enemies with armor just have some level of damage resistance. Armor can be removed!The game also features grenades which can, believe it or not. Apply status effects, they tend to also disrupt enemies, damage armor, or act as enemy wave clearShields do what they typically do. Shields can get ripped away from enemies (through parries!) which acts like a mini-stun and allows you to get some damage in.Parries are here as usual! Some skills effect them though and enable different choices for attacks after a parry.Briefly touching on Enki- He is a core part of the gameplay systems and is one of the few ways you can apply status effects. You get a couple upgrades for Enki within the skill tree and he enables some of your abilities, so paying attention to his charges is fairly important. He also allows for special abilities to be activated through his withering gauge, I honestly didn't pay attention to filling it much, but I had it up fairly consistently. Enki is a nice little addition to a flashy combat system and a great companion.Almost forgot about exploration-Flintlock is a strange game with its world. It features some open ended design with areas that are off the beaten path, yet not part of side quests or the main story progression. Finding the areas is easy enough and exploring them is more often than not met with some kind of reward other than currency, I would often find weapons, armor, upgrade materials or even upgrades to my grenades. You will also find health upgrades and upgrades for Enki as well.I find the levels to be fairly linear and have some mechanics to them that are sorta forgettable and borderline unnecessary and while the world design isn't much to write home about, its at least fun to go through with Rifts enabling quick movement and backtracking.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not super far into it, but nine hours in, it makes for a pretty fun low key budget souls type experience (positive connotation); it ain't got the absurd polish of a from soft joint, or the clout and sanded off sheen of a big publisher clone like jedi, but the budget it did have feels like it went to where it's needed; whilst the enemy pathing and agro + some animation blending can look a bit silly on occasion,  the core game feel is good and makes for a really nice low stress variation of this gameplay type with enough unique mechanics to keep things interestingIt's also seemingly devoid of bugs (in my playthrough at least), which is a damn rarity nowadaysfor the most part though, I kinda just like that it has an identity that isn't just 'knock off dark souls.'up till now, the surge was kinda the only souls lite that managed to achieve that without being stapled onto another ip, but even then it was still chasing the vibe and atmosphere of souls, So to have this do something that feels wholly different is honestly kinda satisfying, even if it's dragged the game into modern day culture war nonsenseAlas we can't have nice things it seems; apparently the internet has decided to punish this for the crime of not giving us yet another entry in the long line of boring custom characters and stale white twink protagonists.It's kind of a shame to tell you the truth, cause I think the game is honestly better for itanywhoI think if you like souls clones and you are really done with AAA output and want to see what the budget side of the market can give you as an alternative, this has plenty to offerit also has a cute lil fops companion who runs alongside you and does cute little fops pounces and that means the world to me, I want more fops games

_childDocuments_.review: Flintlock is so much fun ! It's an action Souls-Lite akin to God of War but with its own twist. The graphics and voice acting are all quite good but the story is a bit hit or miss, the combat is the games strong suit and the Devs knows it so conversations are short. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun game. Movement is very enjoyable and paired with wide linear level design with a lot of verticality it is the best part of the game. Just running around, exploring and looking at a pretty visuals is fun. Combat is alright, the core of it feels pretty good, i had a bit of a problem with "flow" at first, felt like enemies just cheated me out of dodging and kept turning after me etc., which made me play a lot more defensive, and that's boring. But then it just started clicking and everything got a lot more fluid and enjoyable. The problem is variety - there's very little of it. Enemies are pretty much all very similar and different weapons don't offer much difference in how they play, only different stats. There's too little rpg and weapon variety for souls game, and too little depth for a proper character action game. But the enemies aren't very difficult on normal and there isn't a ton of them so you don't have to constantly fight and progress through the game feels pretty fast even though i think i did most of the side content available.

_childDocuments_.review: For a budget AA game its a yes for me but there are issues some players will dislike more than others.UPDATE: 11 hours in I can properly add some issues I have and some of my likes as well. The staggering is great and visual appealing but I notice when fighting against a group you are vulnerable after finishing the special attack which in harder difficulty can get you killed. Nor's movement took a bit of time to get use to. She feel "slippery" but the options when moving is fair trade off IMO. Combat is a starts slow however once you start unlocking abilities is gets really fun. The hardest difficulty option didn't allow many mistakes which forces you to get it right or perish in some encounters. I'm enjoying the groups and size of the battlegrounds in the game. Sometimes your space is large and some are very small. Being able to switch from defensive to aggressive without thinking took me awhile to understand. Once you find your flow the combat is a blast. I'll go over my thoughts on exploration later

name: Neptunia x SENRAN KAGURA: Ninja Wars
detailed_description: Neptunia and SENRAN KAGURA join forces in this hack 'n slash RPG! Pair up 10 playable characters to slice through enemy hordes, channel the elements, and perform special character attacks. Then find your center with the Peaches & Cream Meditation minigame before taking on the post-game challenges of Yomi-Training! Key Features When 2 Become 1 The two warring nations from the Neptunia and SENRAN KAGURA series have now joined forces in one action-packed RPG! Choose from 10 possible characters, including two new characters: Yuuki and Goh, and pick two characters to set forth on your adventure. Swiftly switch between your two chosen characters in battle! This version also includes a new difficulty setting option! The Art of the Ninja Each character possess a unique set of skills, known as Ninja Art Skills. Chain your Ninja Art Skills to leave your enemies in the dust. Ninjas and shinobi are also equipped with projectiles that can inflict physical damage or temporary status ailments to slow down foes. Stay Stylin’ with Spirit Gems Collect Spirit Gems for helpful stat boosts! Legend says arranging them in certain combinations can add even bigger boosts... Are You a True Ninja Warrior? Find your center with the Peaches & Cream Meditation mini-game to get extra stat boosts in battle. Plus, test your might with the post-game content, Yomi-Training! Expert ninjas and shinobi can play through 8 different trials, each set with difficult restrictions! Story Gamninjustri – a place where all manner of ninjas gather. As the struggle for control increased between the Daimyos of the nations, tensions rose between the two great nations, each of which was home to one of the major schools of martial arts. The Compa Style which has mastered the Ninja Arts based on the Command Technique. The Honeypa Style which has mastered the Ninja Arts rooted in the Action Technique. The two camps were stuck in a ruthless competition of skill in order to achieve hegemony, but as they fought on, a mysterious army of mechanical ninjas made their assault. The mechanical ninja army overran the smaller nations in an instant, and the Steeme Legion leader, Yoh Gamer, made an announcement to the world: The Super NINJA War to decide the world's strongest school is about to begin!

_childDocuments_.review: - This is primarily a Hyperdimension Neptunia game, so don't expect it to be similar to Senran Kagura titles.- As with all Neptunia side games, this one has no story connection whatsoever. Not knowing any of the main games will just result in some meta-jokes falling flat.- This review is to be considered .Once again a new Neptunia spin-off game and again, as is custom, with a vastly different genre than the main games. Probably following the success of the old Hack-n-Slay title "Hyperdimension Neptunia U: Action Unleashed" we get another game in that direction - and what better marketing move than to collaborate with another huge and well-known Beat-em-Up franchise like Senran Kagura?So far, on paper, that sounds great. Personally, I enjoyed both the Senran Kagura games as well as Neptunia U. Turning your brain mostly off while mindlessly chopping through hordes of enemies with sick looking combos and skills is a great way to spend your afternoon. And Neptunia - Ninja Wars does deliver a few nice elements: Having (after unlocking them in the story) 10 unique characters to play with, each with a unique moveset, strengths and weaknesses, as well as 6 different Ninja Arts of which you can equip and combo chain up to 4 of at a time, plus ultimate skill and manual limit breaking with 4 different types of buffs, is a good setup to start with. After getting used to it - which is further supported by abilities being gradually unlocked and explained via text tutorials - it does make fun to play.But, as previously mentioned,  Neptunia - Ninja Wars is an Idea Factory/Compile Heart game and hence fundamentally different from Senran Kagura, and going in with similar expectations will turn out a bad decision. The game is even notably different in how it feels compared to Neptunia U - because while you might recognize the mechanic where you select two playable characters at a time and can switch between them in the missions, gameplay differs in one crucial key area: Speed. First off, the amount of enemies on the map at a time is very small - only in the later end- and post-game missions will you see 10+ at a time. To compensate that, the range of your attacks sometimes feels like a joke, otherwise you would breeze through them at the speed of light.Speaking of which, I highly recommend playing on the hard difficulty so that those few enemies are actually a challenge, having damage-sponge levels of HP while killing you in a couple of hits. After switching to normal difficulty in the post-game because the grind became absolutely fun-killing it felt like I turned on the one-hit mode gimmick from Neptunia U.Second, frame cancling is non-existent or at the very least heavily inconsistent. That results in some attacks getting you heavily punished if not even killed while you are waiting several seconds for the fade-out transition of your last move to end before you can block or dodge again. This greatly reduces the speed of gameplay, as you are (on hard difficulty at least) forced into a defensive playstyle where you learn to parry, or at least block, dozens of attacks from all sides before using a small opening to get a couple normal hits, maybe even a single Ninja Art, in. Speaking of parrying, all it does is letting you take no damage at all and refills your stamina, which is used to dodge, run or use Ninja Arts. Nothing more, no counters no nothing.Furthermore, due to that using the two different throwable ranged weapons you have - which can get pretty overpowered in the endgame, especially with the right "Infinite throwables for x seconds" skill - can become the way more comfortable alternative to endangering yourself in order to see cool moves.In general it takes around 10-15h to complete the story. During that time you can spend another 5-ish hours doing side quests, letting you run through the same dungeons killing the same enemies over and over again. Finally you can then spend 10+ hours in the post-game for that additional grind to top off your week's workload. At least, when doing the side quests when they come up you are never underleveled. During all that time you will clearly see the charm of IF/Compa games again as you are fighting the same, like, 8 enemy types in three differently colored, "stronger" variants as well as the same bosses several times over.There is the P&C minigame, which you may want to do with every character once and once on hard (when unlocked) for the achievement, and then skip with items you can buy ever after. It's a nice idea for a minigame, though nothing you'd want to do over and over again, and no comparison to the fanservice Senran Kagura players are used to. There isn't even clothing breaking like in all the previous games or transformations. You can also collect and upgrade "Sprit Orbs" that you can arrange in a 5x5 grid to get passive buffs, though getting that stuff just happens while playing normally, and specifically grinding for those isn't worth it.The game has a gallery where you can look at all the event CGs, watch the opening and ending movies again, listen to all the BGM tracks and view all the story and side dialogue events again. The frequent crashes during those 2D VN scenes have been patched by now, but the sprites are still lazy. Changing only once per scene, random blinking and a constant mouth open-and-close loop during voiceline playback. Furthermore, our marvelous guests have their mouths placed at very weird looking positions half of the time.At least the characters themselves, personalities, background stories and all, are on-spot and the typical Neptunia meta-jokes, references and 4th wall breaking manage to entertain throughout the game.Hardly. Looking at the full price of the game, you could get any Senran Kagura game and enjoy way better Hack-n-Slay gameplay. You could get Hyperdimension Neptunia U: Action Unleashed for a third of the price, if you want the genre-predecessor Neptunia Hack-n-Slay game. You could get any other Neptunia game for way less too, if you want some NepNep humor while fighting "copy'n'paste - the enemy".Though if you desperately want to see the crossover between your two favorite franchises, or want to see the few good elements of this modern Hack-n-Slay, wait for a sale. A big one. I'm sure there will be one, one day.
