_childDocuments_.review: So, this new Neptunia and Senran Kagura crossover... I was mainly looking forward to this game, because I thought it was going to be the first Senran Kagura game with series-staple gameplay mechanics in years. After hearing some news about the game and increasingly becoming disinterested in it (AKA: hype dying down), here comes the Switch and PC releases. I want to preface this by saying that I helped test the game for bugs, and to give port related feedback, hence the "Received Product for Free" tag that I added. That said, I'm going to refrain from further details about the testing, as I don't want to accidentally violate an NDA agreement or something.The game itself exceeded my initial impressions based on the pre-release PR and promotional materials, and the PC port is mostly serviceable this time around (Outside of some quirks that I'm going to get into later that haven't been addressed yet, Tamsoft did this PC port in-house, and it really shows in the quality and lack of issues/bugs compared to any PC port that Ghostlight or PreApp Partners have touched). Despite some of the weirdness in some story elements that people correlate with a lack of budget (A certain scene involving rivers comes to mind), this release is really damn polished. Tamsoft also figured out how to add mipmapping to their engine, which fixes one of my biggest issues with their ports for a while (Which makes anti-aliasing or supersampling redundant due to the shimmering textures). So I guess God of War, this game, and Glover are the only good PC ports that have released this year. A really well deserved break from constant buggy game releases.The gameplay doesn't feel like a Senran Kagura game, and the level design and general boss AI design feels more like a Devil May Cry game in structure, and get's progressively more difficult as it continues (No pacer test memes here, sir). The bosses, even at normal difficulty, aren't going down without a fight. That said, it lacks a good chunk of the experimentation and tools that those games offer, as you are ultimately left to two attack buttons, a pallette of four stronger attacks, a special attack (that uses a gauge), and transformations (Which give extra status effects), and the ability to hoard healing items to use in the middle of the level takes away a lot of the punishment that the Devil May Cry games have when you mess up an attack streak. The enemy placement doesn't feel like a musou/beat-em-up game (like the previous Senran Kagura games), and are generally stronger this time around. Hence why I think it feels less like a Senran Kagura game, and it's going to be different than most people are going to come in expecting. Pretty fun during the bosses, but there's some gameplay flaws in some areas.This game mostly hones in on a few Senran Kagura characters, a new character (Yuuki), a guest character, and four Neptunia characters, and while it gives some room for polish, certain characters (specifically the Senran Kagura ones) feel notably downgraded in comparison to their versions in Estival Versus (the peak of that series). I wish they added more Senran Kagura characters, Iffy and Compa, and maybe the CPU candidates. It is also a bit of a shame that the clothes tearing feature that was one of the bigger gimmicks of those games is nowhere to be seen in the Switch or PC releases (despite advertising a new hard difficulty that isn't present on PS4), and the mouse movement (While feeling smooth), clamps past a certain point, making it feel less good.The story seems like a Neptunia game, in all senses of the word. One of the new characters, Yuuki seems more like she belongs in a Taimanin game. Not that I dislike her character design, and I’m not gonna whine about it like any Twitter user yelling at the clouds over Xenoblade 2, just that it’s out of left field.I can only really level a few criticisms toward the PC port, and at least it’s serviceable (I say this coming from the DERQ2, Virtual Stars, and MS2 ports) and fixes some of the longstanding issues with the Senran Kagura ports. It's absolutely fantastic to see a Senran Kagura game (and an IdeaFactory published PC port) that supports uncapped framerates (mostly) out of the box during gameplay. It also runs like butter on my RTX 3070 at 1440p and maxed settings (My GPU can easily push 650FPS when VSync is disabled). For those wondering whether or not the game runs in Proton, it works out of the box for me (And probably won't have issues running on the Steam Deck either). The primary issues are hardcoded resolution options (Only goes up to 4K, and if you want to use a hex editor to force, say 3440x1440, the game will (for some reason) force an output of 3440x1935), a 60FPS framelimiter outside of gameplay that has rounding issues (So it caps out at 57-58FPS, you can however use Special K to force a sleepless render thread), and a 60FPS cap that occurs outside of gameplay and during special attacks that looks extremely jarring when it occurs. That, and maybThe most that I can really say could be improved in an update is a better implemented framelimiter (Sleep is well known to have rounding issues), uncapped framerate through the entire game (A framerate cap that isn't in control by the user is horrible for framepacing, especially if you don't have a FreeSync/GSync monitor, which is a lot of non-60Hz monitors until recently), and supporting whatever display resolutions are available from the display (including centering the UI on non-16:9 aspect ratios).Like if you want better ports from IF, and more Senran Kagura games, I’d suggest to vote with your wallet. They really should consider having Compile Heart do their PC ports in-house (Hopefully, since Nep SisVsSis and CH's hiring page goes to show that they're moving to Unity, which is probably easier for multiplatform support than say Orochi 4, and so they actually go about addressing technical issues with their games, even on consoles), or outsource to better porting houses (I.E: not the Persona 4 Golden port developer's C team). The quality of this port says a lot about the value of not outsourcing your ports to porting houses that constantly make excuses for pulling the same stuff each release (I.E: offering a 4K option, and still hardcoding post-processing to 1080p, thus making such an option redundant), and I can also recommend this game with some of the asterisks that I mentioned earlier in mind.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're expecting a Senran Kagura game with Neptunia characters in it -- THIS IS NOT THAT GAME.This is an action Neptunia game. If you're familiar with the Neptunia games you'll know they're incredibly jank and particularly the action Neptunia games (like 4 Goddess Online) have very bad combat. This game is improves from the previous Neptunia action games but not by much. They've made a lot of absolutely horrible design decisions in the way they've implemented combat in this game.First: Invulnerability frames, enemy hitbox sizes and timings are all out of wack. You will often be hit when you could swear you shouldn't be. You can't rely on dodging or perfect blocking. This is not in and of itself too bad. Obviously it is better to have good hitboxes, but low invul frames isn't necessarily a bad choice for a game. It does however push you in a more defensive direction for a game series I expect to very aggressive and fast paced. The major issue with this point is that it exacerbates the following points.Second: Every single special attack you do has 0 invulnerability frames and very long wind ups and wind downs. Most enemies have lots of super-armor and bosses have infinite super armor until you "Break" them. This means you cannot play this game aggressively. You have to play defensively and be very sure you're either far away enough to not get hit, or you perfect dodge/block everything. Chip damage through block is very high, but still ends up being the most reliable way to progress.While you CAN flinch normal mobs, there is often very little indication of whether they're being flinched or not (no animation) unless they are being knocked down. However enemies all over the map will be shooting you with pellets/arrows which deal 30-50% of your HP damage and you won't be able to flinch them, since you're not hitting them, and the down-times in your animations will lock you into getting hit, so even if you see the projectiles coming you're screwed. While there are lots of animations that can be cancelled in certain specific ways (but not always the same way, it's confusing) there are lots that can't, or at least can't be cancelled in an evasive way, or not without using a special attack.Third: The bosses have insanely high HP and defence and cannot be effectively damaged unless you completely destroy their 'break' bar. HOWEVER their break bar regenerates at lightning fast speed if you stop attacking them for a few seconds so if you don't stay super aggressive you will not be able to break them. Therefore you cannot play this game defensively EITHER.You cannot play aggressively, and you cannot play defensively, you need to do both simultaneously. Can you do that? No, you can't. When you're being defensive you're defensive, when you're being aggressive you're being aggressive and you get punished for doing BOTH. There is no perfect dodge/guard that gives you a counter attack, there is no way to damage the break bar while being defensive, and there is little to no way to close long distances while being defensive while pressured (no shunpo on perfect dodge, no attacks that do large tracking lunges or anything like that), there are no guard points or invul frames in any attack animation.So essentially you have a really janky animation locked system where even the most basic slime enemy has lots of super armor that is designed for you to be both incredibly defensive but ALSO incredibly offensive but simultaneously punishes you for doing either. The one saving grace of the combat system is that you can use items instantly and at any point during any animation so it seems that the intended gameplay is to just get owned all the time, which is very unfun and unlike what I expect from a high energy game like this, and then just spam healing items.In the end it makes for an incredibly frustrating game to play. It is very clear by how awkward and bad the combat system is that this is a Neptunia game and not a Senran Kagura game. Not to say Senran Kagura has never been janky, but they improved a lot over time and the core gameplay still made sense. Here the core gameplay is at odds with itself.If you care about it, this game is Neptunia and NOT Senran Kagura in other ways too: no clothes breaking, I have not come across a posing/diorama room yet, very small roster of characters, small amount of outfits so far, no accessories very few CGs.For these reasons I cannot recommend the game. I don't think Neptunia fans are going to get what they want out of this game and Senran Kagura fans certainly aren't getting what they want out of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Neptunia x Senran Kagura is a hack and slash game that features both Neptunia characters (more preferably the main CPU characters) and Senran Kagura characters (mainly the leader of each school), in addition to two new characters. Here you are basically trying to save Gam*nin*justri (not Gamindustri) from the forces of the Steele Legion. You battle familiar mobs from the Neptunia series such as dogoos, mushrooms, neko mobs and others, in addition to Steele Legion exclusive mobs. You can slash, or use throwable weapons that can be recharged over time, or use your ninja skills against them, which requires the usage of your stamina meter. When you have a full Shinobi meter, you can unleash the Shinobi Extreme, which is basically a super skill. You also have access to the Fuurinzan Drive, which is basically this game version of Drive mode. You will infuse yourself with specific element, granting certain bonuses to attack, defense or even getting HP regen, though this mode can only be used 5 times in a single battle. If things get too hot, you can tag out for your partner.Voice acting is top notch, along with the music. All the JP VAs who voiced the Senran Kagura and Neptunia characters make a return here, in addition to VAs to the new playable characters and NPCs. Shout out to particularly Chiwa Saito, who voices an NPC that uses a LOT of Engrish. If I remembered she uses an Engrish word or phrase in almost every line she speaks. Visually, the characters look pretty good as well, in comparison to old Senran Kagura and Neptunia games. I really liked the shared XP between all your characters, regardless of them being used in combat or not, since I don't have to grind XP for a particular character if I want to use her.Unfortunately, the gameplay is quite a mess. You only have one melee attack string, and its only guard cancellable at certain points. The guard itself doesn't guarantee damage negation, since you will take chip damage, though if timed right, it will allow you to fully negate an attack, while replenishing your stamina meter. Sounds great, except parrying does not stop an enemy's attack string, nor can it negate damage from another source appearing at the same time. So in an event where an enemy is attacking continuously, all you can do if parry everything, or if not possible, block them, which can still inflict a huge amount of damage regardless. In terms of gearing up, all you need to change are your throwable weapons. That's it. No bangle, no armor, no melee weapon, nothing. Instead you get this gem system, where equipping gems boost you stats, and you need few gems to start gaining some bonuses. You can craft higher level gems, but usually people will just wait to complete the story, since the best gems are only available in a mode that is unlocked after the story is completed. The gameplay is also very repetitive as well, though there are some missions where you need to collect stuffs only, which is slightly different from the "clear all enemies and boss" objectives.If you think modes like Re;birth 1 Colosseum mode was bad, the post story mode content is terribly designed. There's 9 levels, with each levels consisting of 3 rounds. Every round rewards a gem for your effort, and at the end, there's a boss you need to defeat to complete it. However, the catch is that each round bars the usage of a specific stuff. For example, one level does not allow you to tag in your character. Some of it becomes extremely hard if you were playing a particular style (e.g. parry and use Ninja skill) and not knowing about how stupidly good the throwable weapons are, in addition to the time limit imposed in most of them. To add salt into wound, you cannot quit halfway, since if you do, you need to start the whole level again. Scratch that, you need to start the whole level again even if you fully cleared the level OR lost a single round. What's with this ridiculous need for a grind? Let's not forget, the bosses here can easily wipe you, if you get caught in a single barrage (I am looking at you Guardian Yoh Gamer) or handled wrongly (yes, you, Affimojas, with your ridiculous attacks).Also, why is the throwable weapons so good? There's some levels where it was almost impossible to play via melee style (or if you have to resort to only auto attacks), and the throwable weapons just blows it out of the water completely. If you do finish all the levels, you will get the best throwable weapons in the game, which is even more stupidly good. Its so stupidly good, you don't even need to consider using ninja skills or Shinobi Extreme anymore. Just parry and throw them, everything will just get KOed instantly. Playing the previous Neptunia games, I was extremely disappointed with the character sprites. Its just a loop of them blinking and opening and closing their mouth in a uniform cycle. No variation in mouth movement, nor timing in mouth movement at all. Oh if you are expecting customization for the characters, there's pretty much none. You can change the colour of the CPU outfits, or use the casual outfits for the Senran Kagura girls, but that's about it. No customization hairstyle, armor, clothing nothing. No clothes ripping too, which is pretty much a trademark from Senran Kagura series.Overall, if you really, really want to see ninja Neptune and gang, or you just want to experience the crossover, you can try this game. However, I would really recommend playing other games from their respective universe instead (e.g. Neptunia Unleashed for the Neptunia series and Shinovi or Estival Versus for the Senran Kagura series).

_childDocuments_.review: It’s important to set expectations here. This may be a crossover, but this is ultimately just another Neptunia spin-off and it brings pretty much all the usuals associated with that label. The gameplay that has a good base, but some flaws on top of it, the story that takes up around 75% of the game’s play time, and the overall “not really taking itself seriously”-kind of attitude. This doesn’t make it a bad game though – just a Neptunia game.Ninja Wars is a full-blown action-based combo brawler that is kind of reminiscent of the Ys games. You have your one basic attack string per character, but then a handful of character abilities that can be comboed together in different ways. The core to the combat here is fine – there’s a good amount of feedback and it’s not as weightless as it appears.That said, the flow can be a bit iffy. The basic strings feel great to use and the character abilities too, but I was not a fan of how the game is effectively paused when you’re selecting which ability to use. That and I also did not like the fact that these abilities cannot be canceled mid-animation.I guess it’s a way of balancing difficulty, but most of them have so much ending lag that it’s like the game is actively encouraging you not to combo them together. The entire combo system is effectively useless against bosses anyways since they do not stagger like regular enemies and you only ever have enough time to really get off one ability before the boss starts attacking again.And on the topic of those bosses – they’re actually pretty good. Multiple unique attacks, cool designs, and some surprisingly high difficulty. I won’t deny, some of the bosses took me multiple attempts, but it never reached the point of outright frustration. What started off as a relatively easy game became less so as it went on – granted, I also was a bit of a pro gamer taking on dungeons that were higher level than my characters.The dungeons are just okay. It is a Neptunia game, so I can’t say I was expecting much, but it’s pretty much just the usual long hallways, bigger rooms to accommodate enemy fights, and only a couple branching paths along the way. The loot you find is mostly healing items and the occasional weapon upgrade – beyond that the exploration is extremely limited.This can be seen in the overall game loop as well. You basically: enter level, watch cutscene, kill some enemies, take on a mid-boss, kill some more enemies, take on dungeon boss, and then watch another cutscene. Repeat this for about ten hours and you’ve completed Neptunia x Senran Kagura: Ninja Wars. It’s a fairly barebones overall package and the extra stuff on top of that isn’t really all that exciting either.You can’t change character appearance and the only customization you gave is with your two equipped ranged weapons and your two charms per character – basically passive upgrades. The most advanced it gets is with the spirit gem feature, which allows you to align spirit gems on a board, each providing some passive buff that is only increased depending on how you lay them out on the spirit board. It’s a nice feature to have, but again, nothing too major here. At least the main story is fine. I wouldn’t say it’s… great, but if you like the usual Neptunia comedy-adventure duo, that is on full display here – just with the Senran Kagura girls as a bonus. The setting is this neat mix of Japanese history, but with that classic Neptunia sci-fi/video game twist and it kinda reminded me of Cyberdimension Neptunia. Par for the series – the story does not take itself seriously and you will get the usual bad guys turning good and other predictable plot developments.According to the publisher the only two changes made to the PC and Switch versions from the PS4 version is the addition of a new easy mode, hard mode, and some alternate character costumes. That last one is basically useless, but the hard mode is a nice change. The game was already a little bit challenging, so that extra edge can definitely add to the experience for some.Otherwise - it’s the same game. They actually gave us a pretty good port though and with a handful of nice graphical settings too. Higher resolution support, uncapped FPS, borderless window, anti-aliasing, background quality, shadow quality, depth of field, bloom - I feel like this is more than we usually get with these Compile Heart ports and I am happy they seem to be stepping up their game.I played at 1440p 144fps and the game ran flawlessly outside of one crash that happened during the first opening dialogue scene - no idea how that happened, but have yet to have another one. I also played exclusively using keyboard and mouse and that actually did not feel terrible. It’s still not ideal and I did have to change around a few of the keys (thankfully fully rebindable), but better than I was expecting.I actually didn’t have to change any settings at all to get the game running on the Deck. It worked right out of the box, controls, visuals, and all and I did not have any issues running it at a constant 60 fps. In fact, I might actually prefer playing it this way over keyboard and mouse. Ninja Wars takes elements that make both series great and combines them into something just… okay. The combat is pretty involved as far as those two series go, but it doesn’t flow all that well. The boss fights are cool, but the aren’t enough of them and the game is over in just 10 hours – of which roughly only 2-3 were actual gameplay. The story, which makes up the rest of those hours, is also nothing special beyond the typical Neptunia fare. It’s not bad, just average.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: I like both Neptunia and Senran Kagura, so for me this is like the biggest crossover event since The Avengers but better! Story-wise this is a full-on Neptunia game with a couple Senran Kagura cameos, which is fine by me. You either really like or really hate Neptunia games and it's stories, though I was a bit disappointed with the Visual Novel cutscenes. Even the ReBirth games for the PSVita had character models that moved and reacted with lots of expressions, here it's really just a couple jpegs with many lengthy transitions between them.Combat wise it was fine. Funnily enough this is not the first Neptunia game with Senran Kagura like combat. They already did that with Neptunia U Action Unleashed but there the combat was terrible imo. Here it's competent and actually fun to play. Because here they made a new combat system from the ground up instead of trying to fit RPG elements into existing Senran Kagura combat like in Neptunia U. This sadly also means that pretty much all of the fan-service stuff from the SK games are missing here. No clothes ripping, no questionable camera angles, nothing. This might actually be the most prudent game of both franchises to date!The game is not that hard, not that deep and not that long but I like it when games know when to call it quits and not overstay it's welcome. This is a 2/5 3/5 game for most people but because I'm insane it gets the Neptune bonus to 4/5.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR, its a good game and I definitely recommend.The GOODIt took me around 15 hours to finish the game but if you don't do any of the extra missions you could probably finish it in 10 hours or so. I think that is a perfect length for a game like this. The story was pretty good if you like hyperbolic anime trope humor.  Every line from Neptune was basically pure gold.  The fighting system was pretty solid and it never got boring mowing through waves of enemies.  Each character was pretty unique which made it really fun to try out different combinations of characters. Expecially Yumi, since she has a ice slide move that she can use to get around the levels (every other character just sprints).The NOT SO GOODThere was a whole lot of mechanics that ended up being kind of useless. For instance the peach balancing training was pointless. I also did not really notice much of a difference with the spirit gems I had equipped. I just basically used to auto-equip for attack the entire game.  To be fair, you can level up spirit gems which might have made a bigger difference but you probably won't have any trouble until the end of the game. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a mixed bag to be honest, and I consider this more of a neutral review.It is a low quality, low effort spin off title, but I had fun playing it. I'd recommend this game only if it's really cheap and you're a big fan of both Neptunia and Senran Kagura characters. It's all about the characters and the funny dialogues, game/anime references and interactions. DO NOT buy this game for the gameplay.The story is pretty much non existent and is as generic as it can get, but Yuuki's plot is really big in this game and I suggest you pay extra attention to that because it's an integral and essential part of the game and this might be the reason you're buying this game some day lolThe artwork and the character designs are pretty good. The VN sections take over 80% of the gameplay time. It's very short and can be completed in about 8 hours. It is fully voiced, which is very nice. My only complaint about the VN part is the static image of the characters with the odd mouth movement animation that looks really bad and is a big downgrade over the Live2D used in previous games.The battles are pretty bad though. Combat is very clunky, the dungeons look uninspired, monster designs are simple and not interesting. It's nowhere near Senran Kagura's combat system.Most of the dungeons can be completed really quickly in less than 5 minutes until you reach another VN dialogue section.The PC port is pretty good. It runs perfectly at 4K 60fps max settings on a RTX2060 Super, and I didn't encounter any issues during my entire playthrough.Unfortunately both Neptunia and Senran Kagura series took a big hit because of Sony's censorship policies back in 2018, and both series have yet to deliver a full high quality sequel to Neptunia VII and Estival Versus. Ever since these games released, all we got were low budget spinoff titles.It's a funny thing seeing both of these franchises suffering from a similar situation getting a crossover title like this, but I still hope we get a proper main line game sequel for both franchises one day.

_childDocuments_.review: Was excited for this game but glad I didn't get too far into the game as it felt clunky with it's combat mechanics. It's a hack and slash game where it should feel nice and fluid right? Well that's the kicker, it's not. You're attacks are extremely stiff and there's no real combo system. Using a skill leaves you stuck in place as there's no way of canceling these moves so you have to wait the full length of the skill to do anything. The only "fluid" moveset is to do your basic combo 3 times, Kunai, then dash if you need more distance, but even after all that it just doesn't feel fluid at all. And the so called "Hard" difficulty just increases health, defense, and attack. That's it, You get hit 2-3 times and your character is done. Which by the way remember how I mentioned you're stuck in your skill animation when you use a skill? Well you take the full damage when you're stuck doing your dumb skill so you'll rarely have an opening to do so. It took 10 mins for me personally to take down the 2nd boss you face not because it's hard, but because you have to play around his kit since blocking pointless, using skills will leave you open to his attacks so unless your skill animation is short DON'T USE SKILLS, and you're only saving grace is that you get your ultimate which can break half of his guard. You're really only buying this because it's a Neptunia game, if you were here looking for a hack and slash, just get the Senran Kagura series.

_childDocuments_.review: - The 10 characters, each with unique abilities and movesets, are fun to play as.- Combat is simple and can be satisfying when you learn to chain attacks and special attacks.- The bosses are fun to fight, though 1 of them has the worst attack in the entire game.- The gem system offers a nice variety of character build for certain playstyle.- The CG cutscenes while look high quality, the presentation is lazy.- The characters of both franchises while have a lot interactions, very few of those moments stand out.- There isn't any fanservice and the minigame is way too tame to be called fanservice.- The map designs are mostly flat land, making exploration boring.- A severe lack of character customization.- Hard difficulty makes the game longer and more tedious as all enemies turn into complete damage sponges.- The game somewhat lacks enemies type, you will see a lot of recolored enemies barely half way into the game.- The game has 14 boss fights but 3 of which are recolored bosses and 2 are the same bosses with stronger attacks.- Combat can take a while to get used to because of the delay animations for all characters and you can't cancel attacks mid-animation.- The lock-on camera is a clunky mess to deal with.- Despite the name, the game is through and through a Neptunia game only with senran kagura characters. I don't recommend this to any fan of Senran Kagura or anyone expecting a good crossover. But if you are a Neptunia fan and looking for a fun time-waster then i say try this game out on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay:You explore a large world map consisting of different locations with enemies and treasure chests.You have 10 characters available: 4 original Neptunia girls + 4 original Senran Kagura girls + 2 new girls Yuuki and Goh.You can take any two characters into the current mission and use them in turn. One character appears on the screen, you can control it, and the second restores health. You can switch between them at any time.Each girl has a main attack (you can make combo chains), a special unique set of Ninja Art skills (uses stamina) and a super move.You can use the main weapon and equip a throwing weapon.After clearing the main story, you have access to Yomi-Training (eight additional challenge missions).+ 10 playable characters (4 Neptunia girls + 4 Senran Kagura girls + 2 new girls Yuuki and Goh).+ Beautiful art, models and textures.+ Excellent music and sounds.+ High-quality Japanese voice acting.+ Simple, dynamic, exciting gameplay.+ Humor in the spirit of Neptunia games.+ Interesting Ninja Art skill system.+ Spirit Gems (increase character stats).+ Peaches & Cream Meditation mini-game (provides temporary buffs).+ Main and side quests.+ Post-game content Yomi-Training (8 additional challenges)+ Achievements and collectible cards.

_childDocuments_.review: Senran Kagura only in name and closer to Neptunia Action U. If you like Senran Kagura games then skip this.That was the short of it, but now let's get to the real problem. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR is at the bottom for anyone who just wants a fast verdict.This was very disappointing as a Nep fan and an SK fan, but definitely more disappointing for the latter. This game lacks most of the iconic aspects of both series and it unfortunately was clearly made with the Sony censorship policies first and foremost. A better result would have been to develop a more true vision with the previous entries on switch and pc, then port to playstation but they didn't bother, so we get a mediocre game with none of the fun ecchi aspects.SK fans will miss the ecchi and darker storyline but honestly even Nep fans will miss the ecchi, this is by far the tamest entry in both franchises. You can't even move the camera up at all or zoom in to look at the (admittedly well done) character models or animations; this is how far toned down this game is to remove ecchi. There's no interesting story or darker motivations here; the story amounts to "Nep squad fights Senrans, new threat, team up, story ends." There really isn't much crossover in terms of how the characters act even - you could remove the SK cast and replace them with Nep OCs and it really wouldn't change much of anything.Music was fine but nothing stood out to me - subjective of course, but I feel both series have had far better soundtracks than what is available here. Voice acting was fine but there is no dub so if you like that, or were hoping to hear the senrans with a dub voice, it won't happen here. Most scenes are voiced but with how short the game is and how little story is actually here it doesn't amount to much.The presentation is frankly poor - I am aware both series are low budget games but it is astonishingly cheap here. There are no 3D cutscenes to speak of, very few CGs and awkward and cheap looking animated portraits for the senrans. They don't even have transformations here, which both series have. There's very few levels and you will be seeing similar ones and repeating the same ones frequently to do quests to stay leveled. The girls all look lovely and the new ninja designs for the Goddesses look great, but you won't ever even get a good look at any of them with how restrictive the camera is. I will give a note to say I really liked the design of Yuuki, it is such a shame she is stuck in this mediocre game and will likely never see an appearance again.Gameplay is very disappointing; there's no hordes of enemies to take down, no territorial control as seen in other musou games, piss poor AI and equipment systems that are bare bones. The duo system isn't even cool like SK Deep Crimson with unique quotes or animations with pairs, which feels incredibly disappointing as there's only ten characters anyway. Combat will boil down to a system of spam ranged attacks and then use special skills in the order that they give buffs/debuffs. A serious lack of enemy variety doesn't help as at least in the SK games, you usually finish off a level fighting another senran which will have unique moves and helps the game flow.The game feels so rushed and half assed. Even if we remove the Sony censorship (that we all know happened,) the game has so little to enjoy for a fan of either series. It isn't a bad game - it doesn't really have bugs and I never experienced any issues with the performance; nothing about it stands out as bad per se. But it is a wholly mediocre title, with very little to redeem it. TLDR - Mediocre Nep game and a poor SK game - you won't find the fun ecchi stuff here and the gameplay is disappointing if you want a easy and fun musou game. Only recommended on a deep sale if you really want to see a mangled collaboration of two loved IPs.

_childDocuments_.review: Another year and another neptunia game and a spin-off as well. To start off I did complete the game under 10 hours 100%/Platnium however, this is the second time i've played this game originally owning it day one on PS4 which tells the game is at least quality to be replayed. Before I start I will like to mention that the port although crashing on me twice is super solid and the game is supported by a impressible auto-save feature so it has your back no matter what bug might take you down. (its a miracle).Fairly simple story has a mix of Nep story telling and Senran story telling although was obvious that the writers in Idea had the most controls with it mainly being focused on the land of Gaminjitsu (that pun alone takes a whole point i'm sorry) as a ninja war is brewing and its up to the heroes of Neptunia and Senran to set aside their differences and save the day. It works for a fun adventure for the groups and overall I liked it but also not super engaging but works for a spin-off.I think this is where most people get split and I understand why. For a neptunia game especially one thats a Muso its easily the best. The gameplay is fast, fluid and responsive there is dead time here and there but they're mostly are combo enders or response of not using your stamina meter properly and getting punished for it. Characters are all for the most part different being used for many reasons but overall blending together which isn't the best when you're about unique characters with their own combos but still uniquely flashy to tell them apart.The 4 style systems are very cool all interacting with apart of the combat: Healing/Status Nullify, Easy Block, More damage but worse defence and fast stamina recharge. Most characters have their advantages but you mainly use it for how your play style and skill level is which is very nice.And every character gets a shuriken and kunai to change and change for more stronger but less or faster but weaker.Finally, with the PC release they've added a difficulty slider and trying both I can say how I feel about them both. Easy is pathetic you get meter way to fast and almost every enemy kneels without as much as sneezing on them. Normal is the OG base game and a perfect difficulty. Hard however is a little silly. Instead of adding more deadly attack or maybe making them be far more aggressive they merely have more health and deal game ending damage to you which is one of the worst ways to do difficulty and with no bonus rewards there is almost zero point worrying about it unless you hate yourself.But for a Senran fan or someone trying because of it being senran related they'd be rather disappointed the game is quite watered down for the Nep audience they isn't super flash combos, Aerials are not in this game sadly except for a smash type attack and the level of combos is relegated to one button which for most fans will disappoint them which is fine its a massive step down but I feel like with the more tougher boss design Senran fans will find some fun fighting the closest thing to Nep Souls we'll ever have.Overall, Fun gameplay for a Neptunia game easily a step up from how weak the U Unleashed and Mega Tagmension were and hopefully will be a start of a new era for good Nep spin-offs.I know little of Senran so I won't talk of them in great length except for they seem to be portrayed with some justice however the character sprites looks a little off and them only being stationary except with empty blinks and lips flaps someone worse then 4kids dubs I will say they were done dirty somewhat. but overall the Nep characters were done justice with some hiccups there but overall their design are very pretty and I like them alot.Very solid soundtrack but I wished there was more unique themes for the characters when they go into a drive then being 3/4 tracks overall since the main focus is going into drives and mowing down waves the same songs kinda drone on the ears after sometime. But its still a nice background music for this game but not really bangers.For a Neptunia game this is a very solid title which is a nice streak since the last new spin-offs and ports have been very lacking this game is incredibly short and somewhat repetitive which brings its score down overall but knowing its just a fun muso game it does what it strives to be very well. However, if you're a Senran fan you won't find much here its a very basic and standard muso game with blandish combos and more repetitive the massive combos are almost non existent and overall I recommend maybe giving it a pass. Although I did rag on it in the perspective of a Senran Fan its just the truth of how most Senran Fans see this game which isn't a bad thing but shows that at least to most of them its obvious which franchise it was pandering to.

_childDocuments_.review: If you have played a Senran Kagura game, the gameplay should be recognizable. While you can button mash to some extent, the bosses can be unforgiving, and the side quests give almost a necessary boost in some regards. As the title implies, it brings the Neptunia characters into the world, with their own flair.The graphics are crisp, and design wise pleasant to look at. The gameplay runs fairly smooth, though it should be noted I observed slight dips in Frame Rate as monsters would spawn in a room (by design).With that noted, the story/side quests are scripted and can feel redundant. Monster variety is limited to varying colors and strengths, but not by design. Side quests are just monster variations on the same maps that you will encounter during the campaign. In addition, it is important to understand that the dialogue is engaged before most missions, and involves long conversations between characters. This is consistent with prior experiences in both series (Senran and Neptunia) but for someone with no prior experience it may be jarring. The combat is satisfying, with a combination of attacks, skills, stances, and items that allow you engage opponents. In regards to Fan Service, there isn't as much as one might expect from a Senran game, so take that for what it is. The variety of characters and costumes are a bit disappointing as well. A lot of characters are brought over for the crossover, but only 10 total are playable, with limited variations. While the stances chance the colors of the clothing, that is about the extent of variation.I bought this at a discount, and I would advise the same. Depending on your expectations, the full price could be justifiable, but nothing extremely notable in comparison to either series past games.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of both Neptunia and Senran Kagura games. And I can safely say that, this game is just okay.I've been playing a lot of this game on the Switch and have played the game almost to the end of the main story. _childDocuments_.review: Updated Neptunia x Senran Kagura Ninja Wars Review - A Fun But Flawed CrossoverIntroduction:Neptunia x Senran Kagura Ninja Wars brings together two beloved franchises in a crossover game that promises an exciting experience for fans. While the game manages to deliver enjoyable gameplay and entertaining moments, it initially suffered from some drawbacks. However, with later updates addressing stability issues, it has improved the overall gaming experience.Story Length:One of the primary drawbacks of Neptunia x Senran Kagura Ninja Wars is its disappointingly short story. Fans were eagerly anticipating a deep and engaging narrative that would fully explore the potential of this crossover. Unfortunately, the game fails to deliver on this aspect, leaving players wanting more substance to the story.2D Facials:The visual aspect of the game, especially the 2D facials, has been a topic of concern among players. In comparison to previous games from both franchises, the 2D facials appear to be poorly made, lacking the attention to detail fans have come to expect. This oversight detracts from the overall immersive experience and may leave players feeling a bit let down.Missing Playable Characters:One of the most significant letdowns for fans is the absence of beloved characters, such as Compa and Iffy, from the roster of playable characters. These iconic characters have been an integral part of the Neptunia series, and their exclusion is bound to disappoint long-time fans.Stability Issues - Fixed in Later Updates:The game's earlier versions suffered from stability issues, with several players experiencing crashes during cutscenes. However, it is worth noting that the developers have actively addressed these issues with later updates, resulting in a more stable gaming experience. This improvement is a positive step that shows the developers' commitment to enhancing the overall quality of the game.Conclusion:Neptunia x Senran Kagura Ninja Wars is undeniably a good time-killing game, and fans of both franchises will still find enjoyment in this crossover. While it initially faced issues with stability and lacked in certain aspects like story length and 2D facials, the developers' efforts to fix stability issues are commendable. With these improvements, the game has the potential to become even more enjoyable for players. Considering these factors, I would give it a 7.5/10, acknowledging its entertaining elements and the steps taken to address the stability concerns.

_childDocuments_.review: "You can't always get what you wantYou can't always get what you wantYou can't always get what you wantBut if you try sometimes, well, you might findYou get what you need!"~The Rolling StonesAfter unwinding at Peace-Beach-Splash island you thought you were gonna get your big break in the ninja-biz! The 7th yokai purge-a-thon lined up nicely after your graduation ceremony and as a "chosen one" you would be slaying monsters alongside all time greats like Ryu Hayabusa! (Yes,that Ryu Hayabusa!) Alas,there were a lot of lay offs last minute and you were one of them. It really was humbling and brought you back down to earth. I mean you were going places. Your name carried prestige. You had actual fans! Where exactly did it all go wrong? News finally reaches your ears that the Safety-Bubble-Board with their consortium of community managers brought up inappropriate work attire and foreign tourists getting offended as reasons for the lay-offs as well as the cancellations. Oh,and those same tourists began rallying for yokai rights! Granted they got eaten by those same yokai moments later but the damage had already been done. You were out of work and needed to pay your rent!Then Nep calls you on the phone. Your best childhood friend before you had been spirited away to become a kunoichi. You remember how you'd spend lazy summer days playing a lot of video games and scavenging in the Akibara strip for fun collectibles. Her family is setting up a local faire with carnival rides to bring in some much needed revenue to help repair a neighborhood monument and to set up a day care center for the local children. Best of all,you don't have to deal with any bureaucratic red tape out in the sticks! Yokai are to be slain on sight,if you got it you can flaunt it,and a few of your college sorority sisters have already been hired to help along with the festivities and to be security!Sure,it's not the glorious 7th yokai purge-a-thon you had hoped for but gosh darn it, it's easy honest paying work!What I enjoyed+Fun combat with a lot of potential when it comes to slowing down time and stringing together combos!+Tag-team hi-jinks. (Like wrestling but with cute ninja waifus!) + 4th wall breaking humor that's not complete cringe. (If you are a weeb. If you are not a weeb then yeah,it's still cringe!)  +Jet (Goh) and Yuuki are perfection! (You'll see what I mean!)+The elemental switch-up system along with using spirit gems that offer buffs/perks when socket-ed into each heroine's chakra grid adds much needed complexity to the game's overall mechanics.+Plenty of shrine side-quests (Mostly enemy-hunting horde modes and item scavenger hunts) for completionists and gamers that want to add longevity to their experience. +While you are limited to a stamina gauge it recovers very quickly.+A few musical compositions catchy enough to play in the background as you do your chores or whatever!What could be potentially off-putting for others-No dress up wardrobe options  -No air-dash-Maps tend to be very small whilst they loop back in on themselves. -The one mini game present was shoe-horned in and does not add much of anything to the proceedings.-Excessive dialogue that meanders. (Though you do have the option to skip it.)-If you have played and enjoyed mainline entries of Senran Kagura the character roster here may seem disappointing by comparison.-No destructible clothing or additional fan service. That is Senran Kagura's big selling point for many fans and even Hyperdimension Neptunia games have had decent cake before. I'm just glad the base character designs are still attractive. While a few customization options and features were subtracted noone got beaten with an ugly stick. In "current year" I'm grateful  for even the smallest of victories!For you if...You need a fun romp on the cheap to deal with that boring and lonely Summer-time-sadness! This isn't a genre redefining title or graphical power-house but it does not have to be. As an rpg lite hack n slasher it does a competent job. I would still suggest Shinovi versus,Burst Renewal,and Estival versus over Ninja-Wars but that does not make Ninja Wars "bad". It still has good art assets,appealing character designs,and satisfying side content for those willing to dig a little deeper. This is strictly a feel good pop-corn-and-county-faire tier affair. Aka,it may not be like going to Disney-Land during the 80's and 90's but it is close to being a Six Flags or a Carowinds! I got it just to show my support for Senran Kagura as a franchise which deserves much more love and care than it has gotten lately. That and Fairy Fencer F Advent Dark Force was the bomb so I figured I'd support those peeps as well!       Not for you ifIf you are expecting to be completely amazed or want Ninja Wars to be Senran Kagura in all but name then you'll be let down. You could say because of certain real-life developments with certain big name corpos  this was the death bell for Senran Kagura as we knew it in the past. While the combat is enjoyable it does not have many of the same deeper mechanics from Burst Renewal or Estival Versus. That's because its' foundation pillars also include parts from the Hyperdimension Neptunia games as well. Additionally the story is more campy humor and referential "gaming meta" than it is an attempt at deep lore or an epic high stakes "final battle". Likewise if you would prefer something grittier and darker with slightly more sophisticated and gorier combat I would suggest looking into the Ninja Gaiden collection,Oneechanbara Origin,or Bloody Spell!

_childDocuments_.review: The worst part about this game is that I played it for too long before realizing how bad it is so I can't refund it. It's really bad. It's terrible. No guard-cancelling to interrupt your own attack combos in order to avoid being struck, so if you're starting a 5-hit combo, you're committed to it and will take whatever damage. _childDocuments_.review: If someone asked me to describe this game I'd tell them it is like one of those older IP games from the 2k years: Technically, it does nothing wrong but fails to have any unique features that would be recognizable as exactly this one game. And it's always a step behind what could have been possible.The game runs really smooth. I specifically installed it on my 9 years old secondary rig with a native 4k display monitor to test the optimization and NxSK works flawlessly at 60. Unlike other IF games in the past this one has no problems adjusting to resolution changes and does not require any 3rd party solutions. There is also free button mapping. Easy transition from similar games thanks to it.The graphics on the other hand are not that great. The stages are pretty offensive to the eye of modern gamers, but ofc this helps with making the game really low requirenment to run. The characters look acceptable, however there is a lack of consistency between the Neptunia and original characters on one side, and the Senran Kagura characters on the other side. The latter looks significantly worse in all regards because they had no real costume overhaul to speak of and it does not blend in well with the other characters. The visual discreparency here continues on dialogue scenes where SK characters just don't have the same drawing style as the rest of the cast.It's a really bad mixture of Senran Kagura, Fate Extella and Neptunia Spinoffs. You can't button combo between X and Y because Y is throwing weapons. You can lock on enemies but most of the time you're better off just running in their direction and activating a skill. Skills come from a seperate 4 choices action window. They got the same annoying delay where retreating enemy types are not being hit due to the animation timer just like in Senran Kagura. At the same time unlike SK, Fate or Koei Musou games you are not untangible while performing the skill animation and thus lose HP if the enemy also attacks. There is a reason why all these other games make you invincible during skill animations - because it's just so bad otherwise. Decades of experience have gone into this concept but IF still doesn't understand.The way enemies act is... well, they stand around and perform their attack pattern on a pre determined interval. So basically you wait until they are done, dash out of the way or block or simply walk out of range of said attack, and then perform a skill on them. Or whatever number you'll be able to squeeze in before the attack pattern is being activated again. Now, this is pretty boring but easy enough, the problem is it feels lame and at the same time creates this bizzare scenario where as soon as there are enough opponents around you, you can't really do anything since they just pile up with their patterns - often enough off camera. It's a really weak combat feeling all around.The stages are pretty much small corridors with clearings in between the paths and an occasional crossroad. If you've ever played Toukiden 1 it's like that but on an even smaller scale. Obviously map design requires manpower and lots of money, both of which IF does not have. So it's forgivable. But you're really just trampling down the same pre-determined path every time.I've had this game day one and a week later I'm still sitting at just three hours. Because whenever I played this game I got bored after half an hour. There is just nothing to draw me in: The gameplay is lame and annoying. The game already gave me 32% of all achievements in under three hours - classic case of  but I didn't really do anything. _childDocuments_.review: I like Neptunia and I like Senran Kagura - but I do not like this game. It feels like Neptunia Unleashed - which while a fun little way to kill a few minutes when it was a Vita game, is not a great way to go about doing a big full price collaboration game between two popular franchises that is being released on nearly every major platform. Walk down narrow ugly PS2 looking ass hallways while taking out small groups of enemies, battle occasional bosses, visual novel style story bits scattered about liberally. It all just feels so, so cheap and halfhearted and done a million times.Combat is slow, clunky, and clearly designed without much in mind other than the barebones basics. There is an insane pause between each attack sequence, blocking is slow and unreliable when attacking, lock on is useless, and in general everything just feels very poor. You're playing as super fast and powerful ninja girls but everything feels like you're in syrup. Virtually any Senran Kagura game has better combat, and most of the more recent Neptunia games with action combat have felt better as well.Story is ho hum, the usual asinine nonsense which is perfectly fine - basically just a conveyor belt for humorous character interactions. I found the humor to be adequate but unexceptional given the pedigree of both series being known for good humor centered on current pop culture; but to be fair I won't be completing this game, so maybe the humor gets better later in the game. The visual novel esque dialogue moments in these games are beginning to wear on me, it no longer feels stylistic or crafty and instead just feels like a way to be cheap. There is no reason this game couldn't just have had basic in engine cutscenes where the characters interact, I mean come on. Extra cheap still is a lack of English voice acting which is baffling given the tiny cast of characters compared to most of the standalone franchise entries.It could have been so much more, a fresh and inventive and less cheap feeling path for both franchises to move forward with, but instead this feels a step backwards in time, like a decade old Vita game with slightly nicer character models. Honestly, Action Unleashed was literally funner. It's time we expect better games and more consistency from IF and Compile - they are charging full price for budget games and are starting to get incredibly brazen about it.Just go buy Estival Versus.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying that this is a game by Idea Factory, and it's Neptunia x Senran Kagura. It's not by Tamsoft, not by Marvelous, not Senran x Neptunia.So, if you're expecting a Senran Kagura with Neptunia characters and not the other way around, you're off and it's really your fault for setting expectations for yourself with no basis.Combat is basic and okay at best. You have a ground combo spamming X, a divekick attack, a kunai/shuriken throw and no way to cancel the combo with dashes or jumps to make it more fun. Then you have the core of your damage, the special attacks you do holding L1 and pressing one of the face buttons. You can cancel your basic attacks into these aaaand that's it.These special attacks have some properties like "add poison", "boost attack" and stuff based on where in the combos you do them, but this really only matters in the first few stages since you'll just end up being overleveled after a bit and oneshot everything, bosses included.There's also a "ultimate attack" called Shinobi Extreme you charge by hitting enemies but it's just more damage and that's it.Combat is basic, game is pretty easy since you can overlevel so easily and even then using one of the buffs to just deal tons of damage makes it so you can fight enemies way above you with ease (and earn tons of exp in the process, making your characters even more overleveled).There's some endgame content which is pretty hard and okay overall, so at least there's that.Story is just your regular Neptunia spin-off story. Save a princess, defeat the baddie, find out the baddie is not a real baddie, everyone is happy. This time with more boobs.Characters are locked into their stereotypes and never come out of them. Nep just says silly stuff (even while being Purple Heart), Noire is the serious one that gets mocked by everyone else, Vert only talks about little sisters and boobs, and the few times Blanc speaks it's just another "i'm flat" joke. Senran characters are just plain boring, they never really stand out, making the new OC more interesting than them. Asuka only has some funny moments and that's it.Fanservice is... uhhh... there but not really there? Like, the dialogue arts are a booba fest and there's a few bath CGs, but really it's more a fanservice that is hinted on like it's there but not really, making this a pretty tame game after all, pretty funny considering it's a crossover with Senran Kagura.So. Combat is not great, story is bad, fanservice is bad.Why a thumbs up then?I don't really even know why, the game is bad but it still had enough charm to keep me hooked on it and beat it in two days. I rarely play more than an hour per sitting so that's saying something.But then again, this might be the way I'd describe Neptunia series as a whole: bad games overall, but charming enough to earn your love.Get this on a discount if you're a fan of the Neptunia series. Get it at an even deeper discount if you're a fan of the Senran series since it's a very different game.Don't buy it if you're looking for the next Devil May Cry.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: I do not recommend the game, even though I had fun playing it. The game has little content - especially for this price. It is a mix of two genres Visual Novel and Action/Slasher. The story part is not bad, although the plot is also somehow not particularly interesting. The length of the plot is acceptable considering the genre in general. The biggest drawback of the game, however, is the action part. The part is empty, and the product seems to be severely lacking because of this. Monster models are few, the rest are repetitive recolors. The locations are ugly, small and empty. Animations are sometimes wooden. Great evidence of this is the fact that the pictures and videos on the product page show almost everything the game offers in this regard. It's sad that free MMO games very often give more of this type of content for free. The game also puts a strong emphasis on fan service in the form of large breasts or suggestive animations - neither a disadvantage nor an advantage for me. The ability to make tactical decisions in the context of the build is there, but its importance on gameplay is marginal, the game seems to offer such things only to give us the impression of control and sense of those repetitive boring fights. The game doesn't offer any way to quickly test all the characters and all their available attacks, making it necessary to start training several times to explore the subject. The mini-game with meditation on the peach might as well not exist, it is mainly for fan service.

The combat in this game can certainly feel a bit stiff and clunky at times, but is still enjoyable and flashy enough to keep coming back for. Legend says arranging them in certain combinations can add even bigger boosts...Are You a True Ninja Warrior?Find your center with the Peaches & Cream Meditation mini-game to get extra stat boosts in battle. Plus, test your might with the post-game content, Yomi-Training! Expert ninjas and shinobi can play through 8 different trials, each set with difficult restrictions!StoryGamninjustri – a place where all manner of ninjas gather.As the struggle for control increased between the Daimyos of the nations, tensions rose between the two great nations, each of which was home to one of the major schools of martial arts.The Compa Style which has mastered the Ninja Arts based on the Command Technique.The Honeypa Style which has mastered the Ninja Arts rooted in the Action Technique.The two camps were stuck in a ruthless competition of skill in order to achieve hegemony, but as they fought on, a mysterious army of mechanical ninjas made their assault.The mechanical ninja army overran the smaller nations in an instant, and the Steeme Legion leader, Yoh Gamer, made an announcement to the world:The Super NINJA War to decide the world's strongest school is about to begin!

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game for 85+ hours on switch, which is why I haven't played much on here yet. That said, I absolutely LOVE this game and it's one of my favorite Senran games! While it is a crossover with the Neptunia series it plays very similar to Burst Re: Newal (as far as combat) with light RPG elements. Between missions you can change equiptment, equip gems for different buffs, and even change a character's ninja arts. There are also plenty of sidequests which can get repetitive but I didn't mind as it gave me more opportunities to try different abilities and characters. The story is nothing "spectacular" and is typical of the Neptunia series- if you've played those games or even just watched the anime you will have an idea. The soundtrack is great! It's hard to explain but it takes the styles of both series and they mesh very well. As far as fanservice, it's been toned down quite a bit, probably due to it being a crossover more than outright censorship. Honestly, it's not that big of a deal, the game is really good without all of the nonsense. There are still plenty of jokes and funny moments through dialogue. And that brings me to my only gripe with this game: dialogue. It's well wriiten and witty BUT there is just SO MUCH of it between missions! Say a mission takes 30 minutes. After that, you will be reading for another 30 (or more) minutes before you can save! That said, you can skip scenes and watch them later if you need to get off the game. Overall, Neptunia x Senran Kagura is a great game and I would reccommend it to fans of both series as they blend together very well :)

_childDocuments_.review: I won't explain this game in great details, instead I will give a simple rundown of the combat system and why I ended up not enjoying the gameplay.The overall controls scheme is extremely simple, you have one button for melee attacks, one button for throwing kunai projectiles, one button for blocking and one for jumping. You can also dodge with R2. R1 will bring out a wheel with four special skills that you can use but I will explain this in greater details later, as it is the roots of my main issue with the combat.Do no expect any fancy combos for melee, there's basically only one combo string per character. Kunais also aren't very useful, you can use them during a combo but you don't get any real benefits for doing so other than hitting an enemy from afar which is rarely ever useful. A downward jumping attack exist but is rather pointless in my experience and I ended up rarely ever using it. You can also parry attacks by blocking at the last second, the parry window is very generous but besides gaining back some action points and avoid damage, it's not very useful or required.The real issue for me is the skills system. Holding R1 will slow down time and give you the opportunity to use one of your skills which is relegated to one of the face button. It usually results in a long flashy combo attack that does big damage to your enemies. The problem however is that you cannot cancel out of these moves, not by dodging nor by blocking, so you are committed to the animation once it starts, some of them can be really long and drawn out. There are no invincibility frames window or reduced damage so it leaves you totally opened to getting attacked. These moves also do not stun bosses. So I found that the best way to play this game is to stick to the normal combo string which also cannot be cancelled out of but can quickly be interrupted by simply stopping mid combo, then you can block or dodge as necessary. It ends up being a very repetitive and shallow combat system. The rest of the package is also not interesting enough to keep you playing this for long, there are no interesting unlockables or fan service that would make you keep playing through this average action game.If you want to play a fun hack-n-slash set in the Neptunia universe, I would recommend playing Hyperdimension Neptunia U: Action Unleashed instead.Final score: 5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a positive review is more of a mixed review, just leaving it positive as I support the SK franchiseTL;DR Lazily made, not smooth combat, only played for the SK crumbs, if you liked 4 goddess online you prob like this one too.The game really had the potential to be better than what it is, with the concept of ninja and hack slash, sadly the hack slash experience feels really interrupted, almost every special attack animation locks you on the animation until it ends or you input another special attack, and this makes the flow of the combat feel choppy and not really smooth. Played on hard difficulty where this really means something as enemies hit harder (make yourself a favor and play on normal or easy) this also meant that I had to spent some time figuring out which characters use as to find whose had the lowest downtime after an special attack otherwise on that downtime you would be punished very hard as you are unable to react to enemy attacks.Also the game feels really lazily, as is very short, and most of the side missions are also very copy paste on nature reusing the same stages or parts of the main story stages. There are other lazily things as the cut scenes are just static images and a textbox, the "animation" for when a character speaks is just a loop of the mouth being open and close without any sync. there are like 9 flavors of normal enemies and a bunch of re-skins, skill icons are re-used just re-colored as well.The most variety of side content is on the end-game where Yomi training is unlocked as you need to fulfill a stage with a gimmick like not being able to use items or swap between your 2 characters but it's also feels underwhelming as again there's not much variety of objectives/enemies.For the story is just what expect from a spin off nep game, doesn't really matter is just there mostly for the interaction of the main characters. When I finished everything about the game didn't feel the need to play to use all the other characters and such felt sad as I was mostly playing it for the crumbs of more SK content.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like a sequel and better version of Cyberdimension Neptunia 4 Goddeses Online, it's fun, addictive and a nice addition to the franchise. I love how the dungeons look, i am happy that they worked on the art so hard that this is probably the most beautiful episode in the series. My problem with this is that the story is kind of wacky, i love the puns but i kinda just rushed with the story since this game is more like a visual novel. The game barely let's you walk 5 meters than a new event occur, and i don't mind dungeon crawler games, cause the Neptunia franchise is literally that but this time with Real Time battle system (just like in U, Cyberdimension) but this game is not hard, nor challenging (perhaps this is why they added difficulty selection first time in the series). It's a short game for 40 euros but you can get like 40 hours of playtime if you complete everything. The peach meditation is a new and unique way to get buffs, and i do like the equipment management too. Overall this could've been the strongest Real Time Nep game but in terms of animation quality, story, and style it's kind of boring. I still can recommend it cause i don't see anything that players would straight up dislike except the mouth animation and that waterfall jump scene (my god that was so bad, why did they even implement it) it's a 7.5 out of 10 for me, the half point is for the missing dub, i know it's reasons but still I can't forget about that.

_childDocuments_.review: Didn't think I'd enjoy this game as much as I did honestly, specially when considering Neptunia's track record with real time combat entries. Game doesn't really resemble Senran in any way aside from having Senran characters so if you were expecting it to be nearer to Senran Kagura than Neptunia I advise against this game.Action combat with skills assigned to RB + Button. There's rewards for chaining multiple skills after each other like buffs or debuffs if a skill is the in a certain part of a chain. I dig it, super nice incentive to get good with planning out your skills and doing more than just spamming your basic attack. You can also throw shuriken or kunai which can debuff or stagger enemies as well as dash.Combat overall feels decently smooth though the enemy AIs are kinda weird and enemies don't have any super well telegraphed attacks and some enemies being kinda ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ (looking at you gatling gun douchebags) though this doesn't pose much issues in the main game (mostly in the postgame dungeon). There's also a relatively alright equipment system where you just select 2 different accessories + the kunai/shuriken you're bringing with you on x character. Each character also has an orb grid that you can add passives to and there are patterns that boost the effectiveness of these as well.Neptunia style lighthearted lots of jokes. Story isn't super serious or takes itself seriously. Not a bad thing overall but it leans heavily into Neptunia's current mostly joke stories rather than Senran's usually more serious story.VN style cutscenes, decent graphics though textures are eh. Combat is just really fun to look at though.Aside from the postgame content it's relatively easy overall. Roughly 10 hours for main story content, it's a really short game which sucks.So in the postgame you gain access to a bunch of challenge levels called Trials of Yomi or whatever and some of them are just utter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Like extremely annoying to do, the defense trial which gives you the best defense gems in the game is just complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, hard to survive against hordes of enemies when you're just not allowed to heal or use skills. Otherwise, you can do an insane amount of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ past that cuz after you clear it you get basically the best kunai and shuriken in the game. You can combine this with Goh and basically have a machinegun that destroys everything ever thanks to her infinite tool use buff. Aside from that there's not much side content aside from side quests.Unique equipment are pretty much entirely one time drops, this means that you can never have the same setup on multiple characters and end up favoring gearing up a single character instead which sucks cuz each character plays different enough to be mostly unique and have fun playstyles overall.Good game but not worth the price, wait for a sale

_childDocuments_.review: For the people glossing over reviews: Its a fun beat 'em up with jiggly waifus. Enough said. (Also Nep humor. <3)Now I'll explain a bit more. If you've come here looking for the classic Senran Kagura gameplay then you won't find it here. The ladies are still jiggly but theres no clothing ripping and theres barely any fanservice scenes outside of CG. However whats missing there is made up in gameplay. In Senran Kagura you mash skills until you win. Here your skills are limited slightly which forces other tools, the girls are also slower moving making dodging and blocking more useful. It is a really short game. (100% Achievements in 20 hrs.) There is postgame content in the form of high difficulty dungeons but thats pretty much it.To sum it up, If you like the Senran Kagura games but wanted less spammy gameplay, buy this. _childDocuments_.review: Disappointing overall.They could have done so much with this crossover, with both series having an enormous amount of characters to play as, but this game only has 10. 4 of the main Neptunia roster, 4 of the main SK representatives, and 2 original game creations.Combat is absolutely atrocious. Every enemy you fight is a brick wall and cannot be staggered at all. Taking any hit in general will stunlock you in an animation while you get ganked by enemies, so you have to guard every single hit. Because there is no animation cancelling, the attack animations all require you to wait for the characters to pose before taking any other action, and characters like Homura has skills where it will lock your controls for a good 2-3 seconds, causing you to take huge amounts of damage. A lot of the skills also has zero I-frames, so when using them you still take damage. Side Missions/Requests are extremely repetitive, all of them requiring you to kill all enemies on the map and picking items up, which is very dull. Some missions even making you run to one part of the map to activate something, to then run back all the way to the start of the map for a door/wall that opens.The enemy and map designs are also reused in every single way, with the same 4-6 enemies just re-coloured and their name-changed. There are also only like 4-6 different maps so you will see the same maps all the time, and side missions also reusing the same maps.The story is very generic and boring. Having to hear the same "Noire has no friends/Noire is a tsundere" and "Blanc is flat" jokes for 7 years now since the first Hyperdimension Neptunia game is extremely unfunny and just really old at this point.If you skipped all the filler scenes in the story the game will not last you a day.The most annoying part of this game is the constant crashing, especially during cutscenes. If you crashed in the middle of a cutscene that takes place after a map mission, you will have to replay the entire map and skip the cutscene to the point where you crashed, and even on skip dialogue mode you still have to watch all the PNGs move around.The only funny thing about the game was saying that Yuuki fell down a waterfall and the devs showed it by dragging her still PNG down a waterfall, lmao.This game is not worth anything more than 15 bucks. Selling this game for over 30 bucks is just daylight robbery.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat immediately reminded me of cyberdimension which had my favourite combat style up until this point. However, I do wish the campaign was a bit longer but that's really my only complaint. Also enjoyed the character design and the soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Neptunia x SENRAN KAGURA: Ninja Wars

_childDocuments_.review: FIRST AND FOREMOST: THIS IS NOT A SENRAN KAGURA GAME, IT IS A NEPTUNIA GAME. This game contains barely, if not zero, gameplay elements/features that you would find in a Senran Kagura game. The four Senran Kagura characters are just guest characters.I would only recommend this game if you're a Neptunia fan. If you are familiar with Neptunia games and Compile Heart's game design, you should know how this game is going to be with all it's jankness. I think this game's first impression is that it isn't a very good game and there are quite a few problems that lead to that. This game's combat is very sluggish on appearance, animation canceling is very limited and most Ninja Art as a lot of end lag but the upside is that you can cancel the end lag into another Ninja Art. Ninja arts are fun and flashy to use but unfortunately the enemy aren't designed around them. Most enemy will just eat you up while you're in attack animation. Most bosses doesn't give you a long enough opening for you to use the ninja arts freely so you have to pick your moment all the time. The break system is back for bosses imo on a casual play through I probably only broke 1 boss due to the break bar regenerating if you don't keep attacking it. Majority of these problems get somewhat mitigated as you progress further in the game with an equip making ninja arts cheaper in cost and stamina regenerating orbs so you can spam arts quite often.I didn't change character very often due to there is only one screen where you can change your character so it is quite a hassle. I stuck to two characters for the entire game. I also only this the town stage theme is the only good music track in the game.If you're familiar with Senran Kagura, they have most of their animations from their games. Otherwise I think they're out of place in this game. They're are in their own art style, including in the CGs so the art style clashes. Since the entire game is design with a ninja theme, they stick out even more because Senran Kagura character design doesn't really give off the impression that they're ninjas.I think this game is not good, but despite the loads of problem I do think this game is fun. I probably would consider it the best Neptunia action game currently. Unfortunately you have to stick with the game till end game with the resources to make it enjoyable. This game is also on the shorter side, about less than 15 hours for all the achievements.  I would recommend this game only if you're a Neptunia fan, otherwise you probably should skip this.

_childDocuments_.review: This is ok standard for a Action Neptunia game.
