_childDocuments_.review: If you like Neptnia series, if you like Senran Kagura, if you like hack and slash then you should enjoy this game for what it has to offer. Combat is decent, but there are no heavy attacks like in Senran Kagura. They were added as special skills that use stamina in combat, which isn't necessarily bad, but I would like if they weren't treated like special attacks, but more like combo finishers, which they can technicaly be used as, but they are a bit too powerful for that.I like how they handled elemental buff forms for each character, which depending on what element you use, a different buff will happen, like one gives you an attack buff while lowering your deffence, another buffs deffence wile also making blocks completely nullify damage(which normaly blocks only block most damage, not all of it)Difficulty is also suprisingly more sattisfying then I was expecting while starting the game. _childDocuments_.review: Neptunia  Ninja action adventure game this time the 4 goddesses of Gamindustri find themselves in a world ruled only by NINJA !!! Neptunia x Senran Kagura: Ninja War is not a mainline Neptunia but a spin-off crossover game featuring four characters from the Senran Kagura games as new partners to the goddesses if your a fan of either series or most likely both you won't want to pass this one up. It is a hack-and-slash fighting game that should be familiar to players who have played either series in the past just do not expect the Senran Kagura gameplay here, think of it more of another Spin Off Action Neptunia game like Neptunia Virtual Stars or Cyberdimension Neptunia: 4 Goddesses Online. _childDocuments_.review: Way better than Virtual stars!So far I am enjoying it, the jokes are actually funny like the old Nep games. At least with Tamsoft involved Idea factory/ Compile heart had less room to mess it up. Both these game serieses (if that's a real word) are known for having some fan service and while nothing extreme has happened, they have had some.Neptunia characters seem to be back to their old selves after that mess that was Virtual Stars. I haven't played too much Senran Kagura so I can't speak to that.Story so far is pretty standard Neptunia stuff, so if you're a Nep fan you'll enjoy it. I'm mostly here for Neptunes fourth wall breaks, I do enjoy a good wall breaking.Music is ninjaish, standard anime ninja stuff.2d Art is sharp on nep characters as always but it sort of clashes with the Senran character art, not bad just weird.3d Models look good.Gameplay, I saved it for last as most people will be split on this. It's not fast paced like Senran Kagura, it reminded me more of Ninja Gaiden 1 to be honest (That's probably cause the ninja aesthetic), though some people say DMC. Overall, it does work but you can't just rush enemies, the biggest problem as others have mentioned is the skills leave you open against bosses. You're only able to use one skill on a boss at a time (without getting hit) and only right after they attack. Enemies do hit harder in this game than in other Neptunia or Senran Kagura games but it still isn't that hard, your average gamer should do just fine.Overall, more a game for Neptunia fans than Senran Kagura fans, I will say it crashed once thus far and at one point when I went to quit it got stuck on the title screen and I had to do a full shutdown,Update!Finished the game and like many others didn't get The Greatest Shinobi achievement or whatever it's called, it's the only one I need fore full completion.The game did also crash a second time after the update and for some reason the characters, Noire in particular will stop moving completely from time to time, leaving me open to attack.Lastly I'll say that this is a game for Neptunia fans, sorry Senran Kagura fans but if you don't like jokes and fourth wall breaks, you probably won't like this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really do like this game. The gameplay is significantly better than the last game, Virtual Stars. The performance is a hell of a lot better, too. The graphics are gorgeous, sharp, and colorful. The music is pretty great. The combat is snappy and satisfying. Everything is pretty awesome!I also have a public service announcement on how to significantly improve your enjoyment of the combat system. Just hold the block button all the time! Blocking interrupts the end lag of your dash and drastically increases the speed of your movement. See the comparison below; at first I dodge normally, then I dodge while holding the block button.There is definitely some bad stuff though, as is usual for the series. For one, the story is quite underwhelming, even for a Neptunia spinoff. I'm also disappointed that there's no English dub yet again. I hope Sisters V Sisters will get one, because I miss the English cast a lot. There's also a general lack of content.Also, this is NOT a Senran Kagura game with Neptunia characters in it, it is a Neptunia game with Senran Kagura characters in it. The gameplay is NOTHING like Shinovi/Estival VS, it is more like 4 Goddesses Online. The spotlight also focuses more on the 4 Goddesses than it does on the 4 girls from SK. All in all I was satisfied with this game as a big Neptunia fan, but I think if you're coming here as a Senran Kagura fan you might be dissapointed. Take this into consideration before purchasing.

name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees
detailed_description: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees is a hand-drawn adventure following a lost gibbon as they embark on a dangerous journey into unknown lands. Race to freedom in liberation mode, or play through an hour-long narrative that captures the real struggle of living creatures around the world. Master the gibbon’s art of brachiation (swinging from branch to branch) at high speed, building momentum, pulling off spectacular somersaults, and launching yourself higher and further into the air with the help of your fellow Gibbons, feeling the thrill and exhilaration of life in an untamed jungle. Features: Experience free-flowing dynamic movement based on brachiation, the way real gibbons swing through the trees. Master acrobatic moves, including launching from another gibbon’s hands in mid air A touching adventure of a family of gibbons trying to survive amid an encroaching human threat. Play through an hourlong adventure in story mode, or race to freedom through a procedurally generated jungle in liberation mode. Compete in the leaderboards and see how far you can swing, backflip and slide in Daily Run mode. Stunning 2D hand painted visuals that breathe life into a rapidly vanishing world. Explore varied environments, from the wild jungles of Southeast Asia to the hectic human world beyond. Collect all encyclopedia entries and find out more about gibbons and their habitat. Gibbon: Beyond the Trees deals with challenging but acute environmental topics, including deforestation, poaching and climate change

_childDocuments_.review: I was hesitant to spend money on this game because I knew I'd probably be too clumsy to have much fun with it and I knew a bunch about apes and their situation already. I'm still glad I got to check it out after the devs generously provided me with a review copy. They asked people for a Steam Award nomination for outstanding visual style, and for good reason. It's very pleasant looking, and the wilderness scenes are stunning. Sound design succeeds in giving off a jungle feeling too, and the ape calls reflecting their mood was a nice detail. Gameplay is quite a bit like platforming mechanically, except that it was actually fun when I managed to do well enough for a bit. Which didn't happen a lot because I absolutely suck at platforming and everything related. My fingers got sweaty real quick and I messed up and died A LOT of times. I fell down gorges, got shot, run over by cars, and I have a whole series of screenshots of my poor ape turning into a fireball which I found oddly hilarious (sorry, buddy). It's pretty forgiving in that you'll just have to repeat a small stretch and (iirc) will sometimes be placed in a better starting position. Story-wise, it's about the situation of an endangered species so it's quite obviously sad at least some of the time. I'm glad I read some spoilers before playing (about ) so I was (kind of) prepared. Still, it was only really joyful during the first chapters (apparently you'll get more out of it if you're better with the controls though).For those who don't suck at being a gibbon or want to train their frustration tolerance, there's both a story-less longer run where you liberate other animals and a "daily run". Now I'm considering making a donation to one of those organisations working for real Gibbons' protection, which was probably one of the points of this game. Well played, devs. * * * If you like chill and story-driven games, check out my curator . You're also welcome to join the .

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Very fun and relaxing experience swinging- The story tells a great message to the player on the reality on not just Gibbons, but also other endangered animal species around the world.- Mostly calm and and relaxing music to listen to, as the music compensates the themes on the backgrounds as well as the story.- "Liberation" being an endless mode to rescue other animals is a pretty cool and unique game mode while swinging fast.- Art style with the 2D shaders on the animal and human models blending in with a paint brush style background just makes this game feel very refreshing to look at.Cons:- For the games pricing, I think it does not justify considering on how short the story actually is (about an hour to and hour and a half worth of story game play).- Liberation being a cool "endless runner" type of mode does get boring if the only objective is to rescue other animals.- Movement switching system based on a key pressing queue system on what move would be followed up is pretty slow and janky (((ESPECIALLY TRYING TO PERFORM A MOVE RIGHT AFTER BACKFLIPPING))) (it's kinda painful).- In the city regions along side the apartments, it's too difficult to elevate, especially with the movement queue system being too slow to register on what height the gibbon should be swinging.- In Liberation there are too many region sequences of lacking trees or elevation, forcing the player to mostly run most of the time. I get the point that it's the cause of deforestation as well as the effects of the palm tree industry, but it's literally unnecessary amounts of those regions being randomised.I love the game overall, noticed a few bugs and I do believe the movement queue can be improved. It would be cool if they had added more elements to Liberation like ground predators or poachers that would try to stop you or add a chase sequence within some of the regions in liberation to spice it up.Overall good game. Most of the cons I had mentioned don't kill the game entirely, just things I've picked up on the 7 hours worth of swinging (or trying to swing).

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game!I got it after watching David Rosen's video, so the animation is obviously a highlight.I really loved the visual style, especially the stark use of colors, which really carry the emotional impact of the various scenes.The swinging is a bit tricky to get the hang of (sorry), but it feels great when you do. The main game is very very short, but you're encouraged to keep playing to basically get collectibles (freeing the animals and encyclopedia pages), or go for daily runs. While I would generally consider this to be a rather cheap way out, I think it works really well, here - the reason being that, gameplay-wise, this is a very slow-burner. It's about spending some relaxing time and building up the intuition of when to grab a branch, when to let you, and so on.It's not a game that you really play with a set goal, but rather something you casually zone out to, go with the flow.It's rather situational, but I think it works.Finally, the story was quite well told, despite its simplicity, and it has a good message.Overall, I love how unique it is. It's rather unassuming, it doesn't try to do much, but what it does, no other game does, and it also does it brilliantly. That alone makes it worth playing, in my book. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees is a beautiful game. The art is gorgeous, the animations both look and feel good and the production values have a lot of care put into them. It's also a good game, with fun runner-esque mechanics that feel tailored to you playing as a gibbon ape. It's clear that a lot of care was put into the way that the mechanics interact with the subject matter as well, where different areas are presented different to make a point about the game's environmental politics, something that is not bad in of itself.This is a decent game, and I generally liked it. I just want to point that out as a preface to what I'm about to write.While individual parts of this game are fine, ranging from average to great, I feel like they fail to fit together in a way that makes sense. There are two parts to this game; the narrative story section, which is about 1½ hours long, and the collectathon afterwards. The narrative part is supposed to give you a contrast between the freedom of the forest and the restriction of other areas, to communicate the point of human expansion and its effect on wildlife. However, the jungle in this game is so lush, with so much to grab onto, that it feels really awkward when you're just getting started – the flow just isn't there, since you're not used to the mechanics yet. So the game starts by feeling stiff and awkward, and moves on to becoming even more restrictive as the game goes on. This muddles the emotions that you're supposed to have with frustration; I feel like the game could have been helped by making the forest easier to traverse. The game is quite forceful when it wants you down at the ground as well, without being clear about what it was doing, which was confusing and distracting as I wondered what went wrong.This brings me to the collectathon, which very few people seem to have actually played. It's a shame too, because there is a lot of good in there; you get to interact more with the game and become better at swinging, there are some fancy animations and it's pretty gratifying to get to the end. However, I still understand it, because those same story environments that are designed to be difficult and restrictive to traverse? They are still there in the collectathon and they are a chore. By the end I genuinely threw myself off cliffs or into fire to reset from those areas and hope for a different pattern, because they were just boring to play through.I could go on, but those are my main issues with the game. I still think that it's worth playing through, and I applaud the effort and the thought that went into it. I would just recommend to temper your expectations, because there are some abrasive elements here. If you're prepared for that, then I'll think that you'll have a good time with Gibbon: Beyond the Trees.

_childDocuments_.review: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees, at its core, is a zen side-scrolling adventure with a powerful humanitarian story to tell. The main game takes almost exactly one hour to complete, and afterwards you can continue, with a procedurally generated endless environment called "liberation mode". I'll be considering the main story and liberation mode separately in this review.The main story is fantastic. As you begin this game, you swing through the trees without a care in the world. The swinging is nearly effortless (though the tutorial is slightly longer than it should be) and you love life. The story progresses and along come emotions, as you realize even monkeys experience deep hardships. Within an hour, the story is over and you are definitely left wanting more. The game provides this in the form of "liberation mode," an endless version of the game, without the story behind it.Liberation mode is where this game unfortunately falls off in my opinion. This mode is where 19 of the 21 achievements can be gotten, and these achievements showcase the game's weak points. You're tasked with  liberating 10 of each kind of 10 different animals. These animals are often on the ground, which forces you to stop your zen swinging motions to walk on the ground, before having to work your way back up into the trees to begin your zen again. Other animals are up in the air, which showcases how difficult the game makes it to be precise in your jumps. One separate achievement requires you to reach the top of a tall crane in a town, which only shows up randomly every 30 minutes or so and you only get a legitimate chance at reaching the top randomly every 2-3 hours or so. When you get a chance and mess up, it's frustrating and punishing because you have no way to go back or retry without just hoping for another shot. I have not gotten this achievement and don't plan to continue playing this game to hunt for it.Overall, I highly recommend Gibbon: Beyond the Trees to anyone looking for a short, sweet story. I do not, however, recommend this game as it exists today, if you plan to hunt for 100% achievements in the endless "liberation mode".

_childDocuments_.review: In the verdant canopies of the ancient Asian rainforests, where the symphony of nature hums a tune of untouched wilderness, the gibbons reigned with a grace unmatched by their primate cousins. This story, woven from the whispers of leaves and the songs of the forest, tells why the gibbons are regarded as the best of apes.Gibbons, the acrobats of the arboreal world, swing with an elegance that turns the dense forest into a grand theater of aerial performance. Their mode of locomotion, called brachiation, allows them to sail through the trees with such speed and precision, they seem to be composing a poem with their long, outstretched arms. Unlike their ground-dwelling relatives, gibbons choose the loftiest paths, ensuring the forest floor's secrets remain undisturbed, its carpet of life untrampled.Their morning calls, as melodic as the most intricate compositions, serve not just as territorial claims, but also as the forest's wake-up call, a natural alarm clock that speaks of the day's bright beginning. These operatic serenades echo through the trees, a testament to their complex social structures and communication skills, which rival even the most sophisticated of their simian brethren.The gibbon’s fidelity is another trait that sets them apart. They form monogamous pairs, a rarity in the primate world, showcasing a level of commitment that underpins their social harmony. Family groups are tight-knit, with parents teaching their offspring the ways of the canopy, from finding food to mastering the art of brachiation.Their slender frames and expressive faces are like a mirror reflecting the very essence of the forest. With fewer threats from predators up high, gibbons live a life that is both peaceful and poised. They are the custodians of the treetops, maintaining a delicate balance in the ecosystem by dispersing seeds and pollinating flowers, ensuring the forest’s health and its future.And so, in this tale of the treetops, the gibbons are not just seen as the best apes; they are the guardians of the green throne, where the earth touches the sky. With a spirit as free as the wind and a bond with nature as deep as the roots of the ancient trees, gibbons are indeed the true aristocrats of the ape world.

_childDocuments_.review: I love my gibbon friend Monti and monkeys in general as my profile shows. Thank you guys for making a very lovely memory and message for us to enjoy. _childDocuments_.review: The game is way too short.The unusual control should be the reason for this game to be new and refreshing.Instead control is buggy and inconsistent: sometimes you press the grab button and it works, sometimes it doesn't and you fall. Some other times you grab on objects you would not expect you can swing from then you fall because often you can't tell apart in-game objects from background.Sometimes if you release the button you get extra speed and sometimes you will just fall down and lose speed. Movement is kind of scripted and not physical based as you would expect.If you want a game in which you can swing around, I would recommend Webbed instead.

_childDocuments_.review: The swinging mechanic is great, and you can tell the developers really cared for the product and message.Unfortunately, movement/traversal felt mostly frustrating to me.+ Great swinging mechanic+ Branching traversal routes (always left to right, but branching and joining vertically)+ Mostly great graphics, rich level design and background world* Although it becomes a bit ridiculous story-wise, well executed message and (in the middle) atmosphere- Frustrating after the initial jungle area (I died many times in fire) with slow and way-back gameplay resets- Tutorial felt stiffling, with repeated interruptionsIt's not a  product, but I can't  it.
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to preface this review by saying that the main story mode took me 75 minutes to finish. While I do wish they prolonged it and added a few more scenes to the game with more difficult zones, at its core this game is meant to depict real environmental issues surrounding Gibbons and deforestations, and so the scenery and events that happen can't be too fantastical . They definitely portrayed quite a lot of lower-end neighbourhoods in the few final chapters of the game though, and while I understand that's because Gibbons are prominent in Southeast Asia and a lot of third-world countries are among them, I wish there was one more zone that portrayed a metropolitan (or a more modernized city of sorts) for our Gibbon to traverse through.With that criticism being said, this game is absolutely beautiful. It's not just the stunning art you see on the trailer or how smooth the animations are, but the music also really gave a lot of emotion to the game. For such a cheap price it is most definitely a steal, although if you care a lot about money-to-playtime ratio, you probably are having a few concerns that this game is too short. Don't worry, because it does have an endless mode, employing randomized zone ordering with some neat achievements to hunt and some objectives to complete.Gameplay-wise, it looks deceptively simple, but doing fluid movements or even a "no-death-story-mode" requires some mastery and trial-and-error to get right. Basically you have a run button and a swing button and holding them down continuously does the movement. You can jump by letting go of either buttons after holding them down. You also have a backflip button for when you want to do a long jump and get a speed boost upon landing, but if you backflip on a gap that's too short, you won't be facing the right way up to actually land, often resulting in a major slowdown and/or death. Also, you can't move backwards at all or slow down manually like you would expect. Everything depends on your momentum which is build entirely by either running, swinging, and letting go of either. So you can't reposition yourself and walk backwards to re-try climbing an upward branch you failed to land on. Combine all of this and it actually becomes a rather tricky game of reflex and timing if you want to fluidly move about and avoid the occasional environmental hazard. The story itself is rather simple since it's a short game without any dialogue or portrayal of Gibbon thoughts whatsoever. While I would like to say a lot of this game could be compared to Gris, I fail to find any meaningful symbolism in the events that happen here. Again, it's meant to be a game that brings awareness to real issues Gibbons face, so I can't complain too much about it.I definitely would recommend this game to anyone. It's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: I play a lot of chill indie games but this really misses the mark, I think that their priority was more the messaging before making a good game. The swinging is just straight up slow and it doesn't really let you build up momentum very much. There's a few cool mechanics but at the end of the day you would be far better off playing a decent endless runner such as the Alto games. While I liked the art overall, the Gibbon 3d models are very clearly low poly and it sticks out from the otherwise beautiful game. (I finished the main campaign but my hours are really low because I played while offline and steam doesn't always want to count that for some reason)
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: I thought about this one for a while and in the end I believe I feel a tiny bit more negative thatn positive. The story was really touching but I didn't enjoy playing so much, it quickly became repetitive. Plus the main story is really short. I got the game in a discount but if I bought it for a full price I would feel like it wasn't worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: I'm recommending this on principle for the incredibly important message it represents, but I gotta say I personally kind of hate the way this game plays. It's fine for what it is, but I strongly feel like this concept would have been better realized as more of an exploratory platformer, along the lines of Webbed or the Ori series. Locking player movement to one direction seems counter-intuitive to the game's themes of freedom for wildlife. That said, I genuinely hope this title does well enough to justify a sequel. There's an insane amount of potential here.
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: Story mode is short (under 100 minutes... yeah, minutes), yet I still played it over 18 hours. Why? Partly because I wanted to get all the achievements, but mostly because the game is bugged after liberating all the monkeys and birds. If you don't find all the Encyclopedia pages before finishing the liberation mode, some parts of the biomes with Encyclopedia pages might never spawn.The game is relatively simple and laid back with a couple of challenging parts in each biome. It's like a rhythm game where your visual cues, which button to press/release are part of the environment - too early/late and you lose forward-moving momentum, which you need to gain again by doing backflips or falling from a great height.In addition to the short story and liberation mode, there are also daily runs with a high score table, where you can try to beat the score of other people each day.
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little game for two hours of fun. Artstyle is absolutely cute and so are monkeys with their funny  moves and noises, but core of the game is movement, traversing between trees and through  powerlines, rooftops, climbing, jumping and sliding. It can feel satisfying for a while, but unfortunately I think it  gets boring too fast because of simplicity, there is definitely not enough variety of moves in a game that revolve around it, hence two hours are probably all fun youll get out of this game, and truth be told, it feels targeted for younger audience. I recommend to get it on sale especially if you have young siblings.
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: Great message, fantastic art style and direction.The movement feels great when you're successfully landing backflips for speed boosts and timing of swings and on vines. I enjoyed the story and the daily runs give the game a slight bit of replayability.However, the games core mechanics sadly are frustrating, too clunky and inconsistent.These are problems that might be unique to me, but it happened enough for me to mention.Input of grabs on branches (grabbing them initially or even on release at the end of a branch) or backflips commonly not working immediately (with some weird input delay) or sometimes not working at all.Random backflips when I didn't press the inputs for them which consistently caused deaths.Randomly coming to a full stop for no reason when swinging. (NOT the holding too long threshold)Quite often when barely making it onto a vine or cable that saves you from falling to your death, the character model hitbox goes through a bottom of the map threshold even if you made the swing and sadly it counts it as a death anyway. The actual story of the game is quite short (which is fine for the price), you can beat the game in about 90 minutes provided you don't get consistently reset back because of the rng of the map generation.For the price it isn't bad, I bought it when it was half price. What I got was a very frustrating, very inconsistent albeit beautiful game that resulted in many roasted/drowned/smooshed gibbons that felt like MOSTLY not my fault but entirely the game punishing me for no reason and made it less enjoyable than it should have been.
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: Looks nice, but otherwise it's boring and pedantic. The gameplay novelty wears off after 10 minutes and 30 minutes later you wonder why you're still playing. This is one of those titles that pretends to be a game until people realize that its gameplay is literally less dynamic than Pong, at which point it becomes an "experience" instead. It's the kind of experience in which the dev team feels compelled to inform us before we've even started playing that their trite and shallow observations on deforestation have been sanctified by woke fiat. It soothes the mind and soul knowing that while I press CCCCCCXXCCCCXXCCCCCCXCC I can do so knowing that the devs are out there bashing the fash, fronting for NGOs, and definitely not writing code on laptops that were snapped and screwed together by child laborers.The game is organized into "chapters", which is an exceedingly generous descriptor for sections of a story which could be told in its entirety using a few hieroglyphs on a cave wall.The core mechanic ("momentum") sounds fun and satisfying, and normally it probably would be, but the flow is interrupted constantly and it is irritating immediately. You know the uncomfortable, unresolved feeling you get when something is just barely out of place? Like the floating, bouncing screensaver graphic that ALMOST fits evenly into the corner of the screen, but instead it barely misses and bounces away, leaving everyone feeling annoyed and unsatisfied? That's the game. You're paying for that feeling.
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: Just let me know when it's a mobile game, regardless of the message.When you're constantly interrupted on how to play the game, it doesn't make the game any fun.  You have to confirm that you can't press the L or R triggers exactly how they'd like it.  I like Gibbons.  Change the constant interruptions with the "You know you're not doing it how I like it, right?"  2 button game play?  The graphics are cool, but I'm sure this is just as great on the ipad as anything.I gave it 11 minutes before requesting a refund.  Misleading description.  It's literally 2 buttons you use to play the game.  I thought it was going to be more advanced and free.  Instead, you just use 2 BUTTONS.  for $13.
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: This is an informative game about the effects of humans on the habitat of one of the most endangered animals on Earth. The controls take some getting used to, and sometimes it's a little difficult to recover if you miss swings or jumps, but overall this is a game that more people need to experience. It only lasts about an hour (but there is post-game stuff as well). I like learning about animals, and this was very enlightening about gibbons and their status as a species. The developers also include helpful places to donate and resources for more information, which I thought was cool! If you can spare an hour and the few dollars this game costs, I'd recommend checking it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is very simple and honestly got a little dull in the last two chapters, but the artstyle and sound design is simply amazing. The game looks very beautiful and is pretty relaxing to play. I wish they focused a little more on the momentum aspect of the game and how you can possibly increase it - the price tag of 12,99€ might also be a little steep for 2 hours of solid gameplay but I got it for a couple bucks in a bundle so I can't complain. (8/10)
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: A short but very informative game about the human impact on wildlife (in this case, Gibbons). The main story is pretty short but I enjoyed every bit of it. There is a liberation mode and daily run if you want to continue playing past the initial story which I've really been enjoying. The game is really forgiving if you end up missing an animal or jump. Yes it "resets" you but it doesn't limit you on finding or getting past areas. Just try again.
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: In Gibbon you play as a gibbon, guided by another gibbon. After you save a gibbon, another part of the game opens up and you can save more gibbons.The main gameplay is keeping momentum through swinging and it feels pretty good when you get the hang of it.Nice visuals and sound. And it made me donate towards saving gibbons.
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: Apes together strong. I have really enjoyed playing this game. I adore the art style, the music, how it plays (for the most part) and the genuine good nature that comes from trying to educate people about nature and how it's at risk. While perhaps not being the only game in this sort that conveys the message, it's still a powerful message done in one of the most artistic ways possible. As long time nature, and specifically monkey enthusiast, it was fantastic seeing facts covered so well. The campaign is fun, emotional, and actually at times, very cinematic.  The daily run mode is also pretty fun and offers a nice challenge with the simplistic controls. And this is where I have to get into the only negative thing I have to say about this game. Liberation Mode is a mode where you specifically have to run into target areas to free an animal or pick up a page for your encyclopedia. Normally, this type of mode would be amazing. To a point, it still is because of all the nice detail with all the animal friends you can pick up on the way. The controls being as simple are they are, are VERY highlighted here. With no way of moving back, no real way of seeing ahead, no real quick action, it becomes very irritating missing these things and then having to swing for another three - five minutes until they appear again.Unless you're like me and want to perfect this game, because I do adore it so much, this won't be an issue.  If you do care about perfecting these games? Prepare for a challenge.All of that said, I hope we see more games about nature from this dev team. They clearly have a passion for what they're speaking about, and their artistic design can not be wasted.
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

But having the story be transmitted with the change of scenery -which affects the gameplay's difficulty, is so unique and makes this game stand out. And there's also daily runs/challenges! _childDocuments_.review: I’ve watched this on YouTube sometime in the past. Bought during the winter sale to finally play. The tutorial straddles you for 10 solid minutes like you’re a 2 year old who’s never played a video game before, pausing the gameplay every 5 seconds to repeat the same few messages on how to use the (TWO!) buttons that this game uses. And there is no way to turn it off in the settings.Even after it seemed like the tutorial was over, I missed a branch by holding R2 too long and it paused the game to let me know how I’d failed. It reminded me of when I was taking a driving lesson nearly 10 years ago and the instructor wouldn’t take his foot off the extra breaks he had on the passenger side. You can’t succeed when you’re held back like this. I recommend this game because it has a beautiful purpose and message, but boy does it need to loosen up on the tutorial. Still deciding on if I want to open it up again after the 12 minutes I played last night to see if it will let me actually play the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: There's little I can say that hasn't already been said about this amazing game. The gameplay is active without distracting too much from the story, and the artwork & animation are wonderfully breathtaking. The message of conservation and protection of our wild spaces is crystal clear, and Gibbon is an excellent educator in putting the player right in the shoes (well, gibbons don't really wear shoes, but you know what I mean) of the creatures impacted the most by the many threats that rainforests face in our modern age.
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an excellent exploration platformer with beautiful artwork and supporting an important ecological cause. The simple and elegant movement mechanic and beautiful artwork with surprisingly enjoyable peaceful music makes this game a joy to play. It's base price is a bit expansive, but it does help finance legitimate NGO dedicated to the protection and rehabilitation of captive Gibbons. You can almost certainly find it on sale during Earth day or similar events too. I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: This is a work of art and the first time I've seen games be utilised for activism. I absolutely adore it and I honestly think thatv everyone should play this. it's an excellent educational tool and I'd love to see it used by somebody to teach kids of the importance of environmental protection. Cheers!
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. It’s short, but it’s oozing with passion for the topic it’s covering. Very simple controls allow you to enjoy swinging through the trees with ease, and leaves plenty of room for you to think about why the game was made in the first place. You can tell a lot of love and care went into making this game! I bought and played the game again on Steam (after playing it on Apple Arcade) because it’s a game that’s well worth supporting. Indie games like this are what we like to see!You can watch my full review here:
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very short but really really well made.It's a strongly art-oriented game but not just in the sense of looking pretty. It really manages to create an atmosphere, and actually not just one but several atmospheres which serve the story: sometimes you're very relaxed, sometimes you're tense, sometimes you're happily swinging (with a pleasant gameplay) and sometimes you're sad, and you have changes of pace. You can feel these emotions quite strongly. At the same time it does contain a bit of challenge. It's probably not a game for the hardcore minmaxing players, but it's difficult enough to make you die from time to time and retry from the last checkpoint. That's sometimes necessary to give you some feeling of tension, and it allows to keep you involved and active in the story, so that it doesn't boil down to watching a film.But it terribly hurts your fingers on the X and C keys XDAnother limitation: I think the part in the middle of a noisy crowd in the market (right before the end of Pink's adventure) could have been better. You were probably supposed to feel a bit overwhelmed in this specific part of the story, I did not.
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay might be simple, but thanks to the fun and fluid movement, it feels great to play. The story is also very simple, but effective at what it does. It's definitely an emotional ride. Also, the environments look fantastic, so it's worth playing for that as well. Music was wonderful too, and the message is powerful, so I recommend it for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: This is amazing creation. I and my girl friend shed tears playing it. This is a real candidate for Persuasive game that we really feel for the animal without some pedantic from PETA forcing us to.The developer built our connection too good to the gibbon on screen that we can feel everything they've been through. _childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: I always loved seeing gibbons in the zoo as a child, how they ran arround, swung arround and their calls, so hauntingly bittersweet. As with most monkeys, they are endangered in part because their land is being taken over by plantations, cut for lumber or they themselves target by poachers for using their offspring in the tourist industry.all of this is front and center as you control a gibbon as it swings through the forest and the concrete jungle. the gibbon is fast as hell and you don't get a moment's rest which is something I did have to get used to. Part of me wished for a moment's rest or time to look at the layout of the trees to figure where to go or to appreciate the art and scenery which is gorgeous, but no such luck, you have to adapt to the gibbon way of life or quit the game. Despite this push to keep going I quickly got into the rythem fo the game and given that the game sponsors genuine organisations dedicated to keep this beautiful precious creatures in the wild, it is worth the price and your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: The game is gorgeous looking and it plays nice and smooth. Great music and audio design. The gameplay is simple (in the best possible way)  and relaxing. With only three inputs we control the Gibbons and make them flow through the trees in a very satisfying way. The story is very compelling. Once you finish the campaign there is an endless mode and a daily run. Beautiful work Broken Rules! Congratulations!
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: First things first: I am not good at this game. I'm not a fantastic adventure gamer, I am not great at platforming, and I spent more time than I should have on the ground rather than enjoying the fantastic views that were put into this game.That having been said, I love this game so much that I don't know how to write a good enough review. It's gorgeous, it's fun, it's motivating, and I'll play it another ten times. Didn't want to stop playing for a second and, again, I died far more than the average player. If you cry easily, good luck.

_childDocuments_.review: very fun swinging monkey game. be aware that this is pretty much a two button runner (like mario mobile), at first i was put off by it, but it works really well. fun nature story. also this is a very short experience (i havent beaten it yet, but like around 1,2 hrs. still great presentation, great flow and nice monkey sounds.
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: Such a beautiful and emotional game. As an animal and nature lover I was drawn to the theme of this game. This doesn't seem to be mentioned here but this game brings awareness of gibbon conservation, because they are currently threatened by development. Despite the seriousness and heartfelt message, the game is also incredibly... FUN! You only need two buttons it seems to swing from limb to vine to another gibbon, and it is thrilling to see the main character, a gibbon, traverse incredible distances at what feels like a natural but incredibly quick speed. Along with the movement theme of the game, its story brings attention to human threats. There's pretty much everything in the world going for this game, and with everything mentioned there, I implore you to acknowledge the value of this one.Here is a gameplay video I made for a showcase with my friends at the Indie Game Collective.
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: The game is super fun and beautiful, very simplistic and has a story with a nice message, but it's super short and the content that you get out of it is mainly achievement hunting after the story mode. The price does seem to be a bit high for the content you can get out of it, but for me it was worth it. In the end it's not trying to reinvent the wheel or anything, but I love it nonetheless.
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely short game dedicated to my favourite animal, what's not to like?Gameplay wise, the free flowing movement is excellent and allows you to get great speed if you master it, which shouldn't take much time.Story wise, it's been a long time since I've become so attached to characters that don't talk at all.Excellent, short game, easy recommend if you love gibbons or you like games with great horizontal movement.

_childDocuments_.review:
Gibbon: Beyond the Trees is a hand-drawn adventure following a lost gibbon as they embark on a dangerous journey into unknown lands. Race to freedom in liberation mode, or play through an hour-long narrative that captures the real struggle of living creatures around the world.

Master the gibbon's art of brachiation (swinging from branch to branch) at high speed, building momentum, pulling off spectacular somersaults, and launching yourself higher and further into the air with the help of your fellow Gibbons, feeling the thrill and exhilaration of life in an untamed jungle.
_childDocuments_.name: Gibbon: Beyond the Trees

name: RPG Time: The Legend of Wright
detailed_description: It's time for an adventure! Once classes are over, RPG Time begins! Game master Kenta's notebook holds a handwritten RPG made just for you. Every turn of the page brings thrills, heroics, and a whole lot of fun! After school, the classroom transforms into the world of 'The Legend of Wright,' an RPG designed by young aspiring game maker Kenta. As you make your way through the game, crafted by Kenta from drawings and cardboard and stationery, you'll see that it's so much more than 'just' an RPG. Despite the name, RPG Time also features everything from action to adventure to bullet hell to turn-based battles! It's a treasure chest stuffed full of fun, and there's no telling what Kenta will pull out next. Nostalgic yet modern, this game is sure to shake up your after-school routine! _childDocuments_.review: I am shocked this game is not on more cozy/wholesome game lists. It is vastly underrated & super fun! I had a blast with this game. You're in school & your classmate asks you to play his game. You agree & it ends up being a RPG that he has made in his notebook with all homemade props. There is even an entire sidequest section. Just know if you're here for a hardcore RPG strat game this isn't it. This is relaxing, fun, cozy and adorable.
_childDocuments_.name: RPG Time: The Legend of Wright

_childDocuments_.review: Very charming and creative game. The homemade aesthetic of it is incredibly cute and the idea of your friend hand crafting a game for you to play after school is so fun. Game play is incredibly simple, mostly point and click, but the jokes and world are endearing and keep you interested. A short game, definitely worth buying, especially on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: RPG Time: The Legend of Wright

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine when you were little and were not allowed any handheld device in school. This is how we (Gen X ) play games with our friends, with pencils and drawing books.This game is a point-and-click puzzle with a little bit of action-adventure and a lot of narrative and storytelling. The story is so cute, especially how they are represented in the game. The puzzle level is easy (of course!). You can not find challenging experiences in this game. It was meant for storytelling and enjoying visual art mainly. Some chapters may be spooky for children under 8. However, it is pretty safe for children at any age. I finished the game with nearly all collectibles within 11 hours. The only downside is that once you finish the game, you can not retry a specific chapter that you miss the collectible. You have to replay from the start.It is recommended for artists, those who enjoy playing point-and-click games and doodle art, and all children.
_childDocuments_.name: RPG Time: The Legend of Wright

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super cute and worth the play through.  The art style is great.  The idea behind the game looking like a game a kid could put together from things they had laying around home is really masterful.  However, it does have some frustrations that are really aggravating.It takes four hours to get to a settings menu.  Four.  Hours.  That is entirely unacceptable in this day and age.  I had to adjust my computer sound settings specifically for this program because the music and sound was absolutely blasting.  Settings menus should be available immediately to make adjustments.  Needing to play through an entire act before you can get to one is a failure of the developer.There's no way to leave the game.  In order to close it, you have to alt+F4.  I had to google just to find out how to quit.  Again, utterly unacceptable in a game these days.The inputs are really slow.  It takes several button presses either with the spacebar or mouse click to advance the dialogue to the next scene, even after all of the dialogue has generated in the bubble.  I had to take breaks from the game just because moving through it was so mindnumbing as it took so long to get to the next piece.That said, it is a really enchanting game with a very unique take on showcasing the world of the game, so if you get get over the frustrations with the interface (like I said, I had to take breaks from it), it's worth playing through once.
_childDocuments_.name: RPG Time: The Legend of Wright

_childDocuments_.review: I spent most of this game grinning ear to ear, for the meta narrative of this game is so charming! This is an 8 year old who spent SO MUCH TIME crafting this amazing world. Every item and animation had excited, seeing what would be introduced next. Minigames, a little party game introduced when you relaunch the game, all sorts of cute gags! As dumb as it sounds, I kept feeling myself feeling proud for Kenta, even though I logically know this was a team of adults. but honestly...that somehow just makes it better, they've clung on to the excitement of making up games with a friend so well! Then again, with this apparently thought up 16 years prior to release by a person who spent thier childhood making games from cardbord and such, I suppose I am still so proud of a child's idea. even if it took until adulthood to quite finish.There's only one issue, and granted it is an annoying one. You can't quit. I don't mean that like "oh it's so addicting", I mean the menu screen is something you unlock in chapter 2. And even then there's no save and quit option. It autosaves constantly so I never lost any progress, but it still felt weird having to shut down the game from the system like that. But there are far worse porting issues to have, I still enjoyed it immensely.
_childDocuments_.name: RPG Time: The Legend of Wright

_childDocuments_.review: Cute and fun.  My only complaint is it should have a "take a break" button to end the game from the inside.  You literally have to kill the program to exit it.  10-12 hours of playtime.  Just a straight up RPG set up as if it was run by a preteen dungeon master, all making it seem to be a real childhood friend you are playing with.
_childDocuments_.name: RPG Time: The Legend of Wright

_childDocuments_.review: The game is magnificent, but terrible in some aspectCannot get menu option until half through the gameCannot even quit the game properlyWeird and inconsistent movement control Too many unnecessary narrative through out the gameYou miss an achievement? too bad, now you must delete the save file and try again from the start
_childDocuments_.name: RPG Time: The Legend of Wright

_childDocuments_.review: This is an extremely creative game and has some of the best presentation I've ever seen in the medium. The concept is you're a kid in school playing a D&D style tabletop RPG that your friend made and the visuals are made up of cardboard structures, paper-mache, and drawings in a notebook. In addition to being stylistically striking, the game also features some surprisingly charming and funny writing. In terms of gameplay, RPG Time switches between a wide variety of genres that ensures it never gets boring, but the quality of these varies wildly. If you're okay with some inconsistent gameplay that feaures very high highs and very low lows as well as a baffling lack of settings (including a way to exit the game without using ALT + F4), this is definitely worth playing. With a little bit of refinement I think this developer can make something really special.7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: RPG Time: The Legend of Wright

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most creative games I have played in years. The story is fun, I enjoyed the commentary of the in-game game master, the gameplay is just varied enough, and the game doesn't overstay its welcome; it's exactly the length I wanted it to be.Yes, the choice to put the options menu behind progression is a little weird, but I just adjusted the sound with the volume mixer, and yes, the lack of an in-game quit button is weird, but alt-f4 works. If this game wasn't as well polished as it is in every other respect, I wouldn't be as willing to overlook these two weird choices, but because the game is so well made in every other respect, I am willing to overlook these choices as quirks. Ultimately, they did not detract from my experience beyond causing me to raise an eyebrow quizzically as I discovered them.Overall, I enjoyed this game thoroughly. It transported me to simpler times, and let me see the world with a childlike wonder I haven't experienced since I was, well, a child. I wholeheartedly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: RPG Time: The Legend of Wright

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game. I genuinely wanted to play this game, however there were a couple things that made this game unplayable for me. There's no quit button, so you're made to force close the game every time you're done playing.Secondly, after playing for over an hour I still hadn't unlocked the Options menu... you know... the thing you usually configure first before starting any game.Thirdly, (and perhaps this is hidden in the Options menu) there was no way I could find to delete your save. I missed a few items in the beginning and wanted to restart before getting too far into the game but that doesn't seem to be an option... or maybe just something I have to unlock later in the game but that just seems like poor design.
_childDocuments_.name: RPG Time: The Legend of Wright

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really good. When we were children, we tried to fill 3-4 pages of a notebook to do something similar in theory but much more smaller in scale and imagination. It was so fun to play with our cousins. Seeing this game feels like a  dream come true when I remember those days. It's beautiful and brilliant. But, the game master is very annoying. I had to mute the game to stop hearing his music. Also, there is no Escape button in the first 30 minutes. I had to Alt+F4. I mean, it's not perfect. Yet, I totally loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: RPG Time: The Legend of Wright

_childDocuments_.review: You either like it or hate it. It took me quite some time to adapt to the style and pace of the game. If you are looking for thrilling rpg gameplay, i wont recommend this game at all.Also how can a game not a have a quit function, the optimization of this game is equally bad.Kids may find joy in this game, but unfortunately not me.
_childDocuments_.name: RPG Time: The Legend of Wright

_childDocuments_.review: This game was an amazing experience! a great and funny RPG to play from start to finish. My only issue is there's no level select mode, so if you forgot to do anything before the final boss then too bad. You'll have to reset the game and lose all your progress. Personally I'd just prefer the option to go back to any point in the game to re experience my favorite parts rather than start all over again and lose all my collectibles. If that could be fixed then it's a 10 out of 10
_childDocuments_.name: RPG Time: The Legend of Wright

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super charming and creative, capturing the essence of childhood beautifully. When I first saw the trailer and read "RPG TIME," I was expecting a turn-based RPG, but it's more of a point-and-click adventure with some boss battles. But hey, there's still plenty of RPG here. You have this boy that narrates a story to you, it's kind of like playing D&D with a friend.
_childDocuments_.name: RPG Time: The Legend of Wright

_childDocuments_.review: The level of detail and polish in this is pretty insane. This is like a first party Nintendo experience. (the good Nintendo). It was not what I was expecting because its definitely not an RPG. Its more of a RPN: Role Playing Narrative Experience. I would have liked it to be more of a game, but the amount of heart put into this game and the quality of the narrative and artwork was so good I have to give this experience props.
_childDocuments_.name: RPG Time: The Legend of Wright

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Jester me all you want, everything I said is true, and people on the discussion board occasionally comment on my post there confirming that the inability to exit the game via normal means STILL hasn't been addressed months later.  15 people found my review helpful, 3 gave me free steam points.---About a month ago I bought this, played for a while, thought it was okay (very cute, but not that fun)... but I also discovered that they forgot to put any way in the game to quit.  ESC doesn't do it, and there's no buttons or menus in the UI that have an option to close the game.  I made a discussion board post and wrote an email to the contact address, but never heard back.  As far as I can tell, this issue was never addressed.Other people on the board came to the same conclusion that there's no way to properly quit the game, besides tabbing out of it and closing it via the taskbar (alt-f4 might work, too.. forgot to try it).  Strange that this has such a high review score when the developers forgot something so basic, and refuse to even look at the discussion board posts, or respond to emails.It seems way overpriced, and mostly relies on it's charm, not gameplay.. And it's hard to look over the fact that when they decided to port this from whatever Tablet or Console this was originally on they did a mostly good job, but forgot one very important thing that every PC game is supposed to have!  Okay for adults like me who play a wide variety of stuff, but this one's probably better suited for kids.  Maybe buy it for them on sale, otherwise don't bother.TL;DR: Game's cute, but not that fun, and pricey.  Port's okay except they forgot a 'quit' button.
_childDocuments_.name: RPG Time: The Legend of Wright

_childDocuments_.review: It's really unfortunate that I started the game, enjoyed it, and then when I put it down for a few months and came back and wanted to start over becaise I had forgotten the story and wanted to show it to some friends, there is literally no way to reset the game's progress it seems where I am at. A lone online post references a pencil sharpener to click that doesn't exist. I can't find any information on how to delete the save data either. Overall, the game is cute, but now I have zero motivation to play it bc I didn't want to pick up where I left off.
_childDocuments_.name: RPG Time: The Legend of Wright

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly can't remember the last time I played a game that was so creative, so downright joyous, and clearly so well-loved by its own creator. The level of detail that was put into every chapter and each "page" was staggering, to the same degree of perusing some of those I-Spy books us Olds might remember. This is a clear love-letter to the RPG and tabletop genres, absolutely worth your time! The only gripe I had was the bizarre lack of game settings and accessibility options (heck, you don't even "unlock" the settings menu until an hour or so into the game) and the complete lack of a "quit to desktop" function.
_childDocuments_.name: RPG Time: The Legend of Wright

_childDocuments_.review: I like how the game literally bullies Wright every time I do sth stupid - like: Go for it. What could possible go wrong. I dare you.Fun game, had to laugh way to hard in several situations but the gameplay and fights could have been more challenging.AND I'M NOT SORRY FOR EATING ALL OF THE SHARDS OF LIGHT.Also the self portrait did me dirty. xD
_childDocuments_.name: RPG Time: The Legend of Wright

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game! Love the art style and I feel like I'm back in class playing RPG during recess. There seems to be a bug though - I'm playing on Steam Deck, on the level where Double Jump was first given and Wright had to jump over the gap, if you fall into the gap the game freezes and must be restarted.
_childDocuments_.name: RPG Time: The Legend of Wright

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most quirky and innovative game I have seen or played ALL YEAR. I cannot extol its virtues enough. From the beautiful sketch book graphics to the quirky controls and the well written story and interaction with the narrator in the tutorial ( Which I highly recommend you play first) The controls are smooth even though the visual control is very different to anything I have used before. The turn based combat is both funny, eccentric and well structured. I could honestly believe a kiddy had spent every waking hour on this notebook game to impress his friend. I felt as though he had put his heart and soul into its creation and the game was immersive. I was totally blown away by it, so BUY IT! If I was to give it a star rating it would be 15/10 its that good.It reminded me very much of how I felt when I first played Little Big Planet on the PS3 many years ago. There is only 1 issue I came across and that was the apparent lack of a way to quit the game. I had to use task manager in the end to get out of it but in the grand scheme of things its a small error in what is essentially a gorgeous and entertaining game
_childDocuments_.name: RPG Time: The Legend of Wright

_childDocuments_.review:
It's time for adventure! When school's out, it's RPG time!

Let's play an RPG that's hand-drawn by a game-loving boy named Kenta, who drew it all on his notebook. Fun and exciting gimmicks and tricks appear every time you turn the page!

While the game's title contains the term "RPG," players will soon find themselves playing games other than the hand-drawn RPG on a notebook: a world made from cardboard and stationary strewn across a desk will also have players play action, adventure, side-scrolling shooters, and command battle games! The game is absolutely chock full of Kenta's playful imagination!

Taking fifteen years to conceive and 9 years to develop, "RPG Time: The Legend of Wright" is packed with its creators' ideas and entertaining flourishes.
_childDocuments_.name: RPG Time: The Legend of Wright

name: Dakar Desert Rally
detailed_description: Dakar Desert Rally is the biggest and most epic off-road rally racing adventure ever developed. Dakar Desert Rally captures the genuine speed and excitement of Amaury Sport Organisation’s largest rally race on the planet, featuring a wide variety of licensed vehicles from the world’s top makers, including motorcycles, cars, trucks, quads and SSVs. The game offers unique challenges for off-road simulation diehards and casual racing fans alike. Compete in fierce online multiplayer races or navigate the vast wilds in single-player offline. Deluxe Edition The Deluxe Edition of Dakar Desert Rally includes the base game and the Dakar Desert Rally - Season Pass. The Dakar Desert Rally - Season Pass includes 2 immediate day one vehicle unlocks - The DAF Truck Turbo-Twin and the Peugeot 405 Turbo 16 as well as 5 future DLC packs with new vehicles, a new map, and 2 new Rally Events all at a discounted rate. Authentic Dakar Rally Experience Over 30 stages of full rally racing from the official 2020, 2021 and 2022 Dakar Rally races with officially licensed vehicles, teams and pilots across multiplayer and single-player modes. All across an immense open world that doesn’t limit you to tracks and roads. The game also supports a wide array of steering wheels for the ultimate driving experience. Seasons and Dynamic Weather Featuring all four seasons and a full day-night cycle. Whether facing billowing sandstorms, blazing desert sunlight, grueling rain and snow, or deep mud, you’ll need to overcome the elements and your competition to win. Single-Player And Online Multiplayer Evolve your Rally Raid career in single-player or compete in online multiplayer events with your friends.

_childDocuments_.review: The biggest problem with this game is that the developers completely and utterly failed to identify the demographic who was likeliest to buy and play this game. It doesn't exactly take a rocket scientist to realize that rally sim fans coming from the Dirt Rally and WRC games would be the main audience. After that, truck simmers coming from Snowrunner, ATS and ETS2. Lastly, sim racers seeking a change of pace. Unfortunately, the developers deluded themselves into thinking they were going to poach a large number of Forza fans here, and tailored this game mainly to them instead.Honestly, I'm about one or two good patches away from flipping this review around to "RECOMMENDED" because there is a lot to like here, and good reason to be hopeful for the future. Patch 1.4 resolved most peoples' performance issues and helped a good bit with wheel support, but there is still work to do. Graphics are absolutely outstanding (by far the best-looking bad weather I've seen in a game), this game fills a racing niche that nobody else even comes close to, and the devs are very open and responsive to constructive criticism, so I feel it is still worth supporting this project. There is plenty of fun to be found in this game already, but I had to throw out the big red thumbs-down for now because like most games nowadays, it just wasn't finished and playtested correctly before launch. While unfinished games seem to be the norm industry-wide these days, it feels to me that us loyal racing fans have particularly received poor treatment in recent years and I am sick of it. We aren't your beta-testers, we are paying customers buying what should be finished products, and we want our time and money to be respected a little bit more.Support for steering wheels and other peripherals is absolutely abysmal. Last time I saw a game launch with such poor wheel support.... was Snowrunner, by this very same company. I was one of the lucky few whose wheel (G29) was supposedly supported from day one, but the game can't make use of my h-pattern shifter, my handbrake, or my button box. It took strange and counterintuitive settings to make the wheel work somewhat right, but even after two hours of fiddling I couldn't get my wheel to match 1:1 with the on-screen wheel, there's always significant lag between what the wheel in my hands is doing and when the wheel in the game catches up to it. The linearity slider appears to be flipped around without anyone in QA catching that before release, and going into negative numbers makes your wheel MORE linear, and higher numbers less linear. Basically, think of it as the non-linearity slider a la SCS truck sims. For a G29 user such as myself, 50% saturation is essential to make the wheel usable, which is a really strange and unusual setting I've never had to resort to in any other racing game.  I play on a 32:9 super ultrawide monitor, which is only about half-supported. I can not play the game in fullscreen because even though the correct resolution is listed in the settings, in fullscreen it can only show a 16:9 image stretched to fit. In borderless, the aspect ratio is correct, but all the performance benefits of running in fullscreen are lost, and unfortunately this game is so poorly optimized that even on a beastly PC this game needs all the performance help it can get. There are a variety of other issues as well. I will keep tacking more and more points to this list as I come across them.- There is no FOV adjustment, which especially stinks for widescreen users since the image stretches wildly on the edges. - Only some of the controls can be rebinded to your preference, and several important things such as pausing simply can not be assigned to other buttons so you just need to live with what the devs decided for you. For example, in literally every other racing/driving game I play, I bind the 'switch camera' control to precisely the same button, but in this game that button halts your race and runs repairs and can not be reassigned. - Gear boxes are quite simply all wrong (just like Snowrunner) and playing with manual transmission feels really odd; you always seem to be about two gears up on what an actual motor vehicle would call for in any given situation- The often wildy incorrect navigator's voice is laughably bad, like they made no attempt whatsoever to match up the tone of his voice to make him sound able to speak in full sentences, giving it an irritating robotic quality.- FFB is improperly scaled not just between different classes, but also between vehicles within the same class. You can't just "set it and forget it" and move comfortably between different cars and classes. For example, if you make the Praga truck feel pleasant to drive and then switch over to the DAF, the FFB is suddenly far too stiff and chunky and violent, and not in any realistic sort of way. They need to either scale the FFBs far better or allow for adjusting the gain on each vehicle individually.- While the damage model has its moments, it also is rife with bugs such as getting tapped lightly on your rear bumper resulting in your windshield shattering for no easily explainable reason.- And of course, locking players out of playing the Dakar Rally for the first ten to twenty hours of play is just unforgivable and absurd, considering this is the official Dakar Rally game.All in all this is a decent and pretty promising Early-Access-quality game that was rushed to release in a very unfinished state. There is still a fair bit of potential here, but if the devs don't acknowledge who their main audience actually is and pivot toward a slightly more simulation style ASAP, this game is doomed. If you are considering buying this, throw it on your wishlist and hope there's a sale come Christmastime, because it definitely isn't worth full price as it stands right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Just a quick update. I've completed all five classes on a few more Sport Mode events, gaining some new reward vehicles, and completed more Pro Mode events. I've also finished my first Simulation Mode event, the Dakar Experience 2020, which took 2H 13M(!) but was amazing. And I've posted a new Steam Guide, I have been posting some bug reports to Saber. The most annoying ones are stages which can't be completed because the AI vehicles back up at the time stamp points and then all get stuck. I think Saber is pretty much already aware of these but it never hurts to open a trouble ticket just to make them understand that it's not an isolated incident. I've run a rally in Simulation mode in an SxS but have two issues. The first is that the car, truck and SxS classes have speed limits which are very difficult to avoid exceeding repeatedly during stages that can last up to an hour. While in real life a professional driver can probably avoid the limit, it is just too brutal for a game player with a controller or even pedals. I've suggested to Saber that they have an option to allow an automatic limiter.My second issue is that when I placed lower than eighth during the second stage of a Simulation rally, I was given a choice to either repeat the stage or withdraw. While for Sport mode and (maybe) Professional mode this might be acceptable, in Simulation mode where this particular stage took fifty-nine minutes of real time to complete it is just too brutal to accept as a hard requirement. I have suggested to Saber that this requirement for repeating the stage if placing lower than eighth be either option or just dropped.None of the three items above are game breakers, but the bugs need to be fixed and I hope both my suggestions accepted. Just a quick update to say that I've reached level 25, so I've unlocked Simulation Mode, or as I called it, Masochist Mode ;)I'm not sure if folks are going to come back to this review, but I thought I'd post a few more impressions just in case. I've reached level 22 in the game.First, I've tweaked the game settings for my X360 controller a bit and with a little tweaking of the quad set ups, I'm doing very nicely racing the quads now. In fact I'm now winning events in the Sport mode so I can collect those reward vehicles. Racing the quad needs finesse on the controls but if a sixty-nine year old(!) can figure out how to do it, other folks can too.Second, I've done more events in the Professional mode. There are issues with the navigator shouting out the wrong instructions or repeatedly telling me I'm on the wrong CAP, but I just ignore those. Between the roadbook, the kilometer counter and the CAP, and looking for other competitors or the camera helos I've managed to do pretty well, in fact today I finished first in the Tabuk 2021 event with the Audi e-tron. Overall time was fifty-four minutes and it was quite an experience. I did have to restart a few times when I just got flustered at the beginning, but overall it was a lot of fun. Just wanted to add this update as I've spent more time playing in Professional mode (Pro mode). This is not going to be easy for folks who haven't played rally games with navigation before and even if you have, expect to make a lot of mistakes till you get used to the system used by this game. Because the length of the stages have been compressed in the game, to make them more manageable for players of different skills, you'll often be hitting new waypoints just tens of seconds apart. And because the game only flags you as you pass certain waypoints, you'll have to manually advance your roadbook to keep up. And that's while driving, checking mileage, heading and looking out for boulders, etc. Not to say that this is bad, just as a heads up for those who might just want to jump directly into Pro mode. You really ought to check out Sport mode first for awhile just to get a feel for the game. I've got in just over eight hours on the game. I've done a number of rallies in Sport mode and three in Pro mode. People have been talking about Sport mode as be the "arcade" or "easy" mode but it's not. The navigation is assisted but the stages are pretty tough. Admittedly they aren't what you would see in a real Dakar Rally stage, what with the snowstorms and everything, but they are fun and challenging. Of course the stages start with all class competitors leaving at the same time so it's a bit like NASCAR in the desert, but again fun and challenging.Pro mode is more like Dakar 18, you need to use the road book and pay more attention to navigation. The rally stages I saw were more like the actually Dakar stages and with less "arcade" like elements. If you enjoyed the stages in Dakar 18 you'll find Pro mode to your liking.The graphics are excellent. I'm running an RTX 3080, i9-10850K and 32GB RAM with Windows 10. I'm running at 2560x1440 without any stutter at 60 fps. And I'm only using an X360 controller for the bikes, all others I'm using a G920 wheel/pedal. The controller doesn't work well for me with the quads, but the wheel does. For the G920 the only change I made in the game settings is to turn force feedback down from 60% to 40%. Make *sure* you run the in-game calibration routine.The game world for the stages of the rallies is outstanding. Kudos to the devs for stepping up to making a full open world rather than canned stages. And also more kudos with taking liberties with the real Saudi Arabian peninsula by adding ship wrecks on shore, airplanes you can jump off and other fun elements. Again, not truly realistic but it makes the rallies more fun. And a bit more kudos for the blizzards and lightning storms.The servicing of the vehicles is more simplified than some rally games, but it doesn't really take away from the enjoyment of the game. For those who remember DiRT 4 with its many upgrades for parts, that was a game in itself but would be overkill in this game. You do pay a penalty in Dakar Points (one of the two "currencies" in the game) if you bang up you vehicle but it isn't too burdensome.The five vehicle classes are very nicely differentiated from each other in terms of handling. The bikes handle better than in Dakar 18, although I still haven't found the sweet spot for the settings on the controller menu for it. Everything else I drive with the G920 and it feels really good. The giant trucks feel like giant ungainly trucks, the SxS are nimble, the cars are fast and easy to overdrive if you don't pay attention. The quads still give me trouble, but watching the coverage of the real Dakar you know that they give their riders a hard time as well.In eight hours I've had only one crash which didn't repeat. Navigation of the menus is straightforward and there are lots of settings to tweak. You can change the key bindings on the keyboard, controller and wheel/pedal which is good. There are plenty of graphics options to play around with. I play with music off and the engine and environment sounds are good.It is a disappointment that some features that were supposed to be available on initial release are now to be released downstream, but there is enough good content in the game right now for me. I'm hoping that the devs don't get too discouraged with the flurry of early negative reviews, I think that too many people just put in too little time and rushed to judgement. Dakar Desert Rally has lived up to my expectations, assuming the roadmap items get released in a timely manner.
