_childDocuments_.review: This game is getting a lot of stick... No doubt some deserved. The updates are coming slow, the road-map is changed but not publicly, there are bugs, some ppl seem to get lots, I haven't had any major issues outside the need for AI tweaking etc. But to see this game trashed by people who returned it after two hours is sad... I'm not saying they should have kept it, if your not feeling it, return it but to claim you've given it every chance when you've not. 2 hours into playing this I hadn't seen anything of it's best bits. Sports mode is not representative and one vehicle you can really suck with and another it's night and day. Many need tweaking to get the best out of it. I have 54 hours played on Steam and another 45 on PS, I still play it everyday. I don't play rally games. I mainly play iRacing but the Dakar is special and this game... captures a lot of that. I can drive for 55 mins in a simulation stage only to roll my truck... and you can't resolve this. Simulation is brutal. You can have a perfect run going and smash your vehicle and have 30 mins of repairs and staying under the speed limits in some of the simulation vehicles takes practice. I think things like this will ruin some peoples experience if you don't wan't the brutality of Dakar. I kinda dig it... Doing 12 stages of simulation Dakar is painful, your navigator isn't perfect so you need to stay on top of your own navigation lots.The driving is fun, theres definite feedback to work with whether on paths or dunes your getting information that feels right, it's not perfect and I think some ppl aren't happy with it, there's tweaking in the settings required. The cars and trucks etc have different feels, strengths etc. There is a lot of stuff to do. Sports mode is just racing others with easy way-points. Professional is a step up, longer stages and proper navigation which comes thick and fast, it's actually not as bad in simulation as the way-points are further apart mostly. There is a treasure hunting mode coming very soon too for something different.Unlocking simulation is held off... you have to get to level 25 and it takes a bit of time. This is being patched i believe in the next update but I can't promise that. I think it will though, I've did it on PlayStation and then PC so it's not undo-able but I agree it's overly long for those keen to play Dakar like Dakar really is (or as close to in a game.) Dakar sim has 3 Dakar Experience stages... long stages but 3-6 stages i think depending. These are good to ease you in. Dakar 2020, 2021 and 2022 are replicated. Not the long 4 to 7 hours plus stages of RL but these around 40m to 1h15m depending so kinda 10 percent of the real thing. That if you don't get lost ofc!  Anyway, it's a weird game, it's not a simulation race game, but it's got strong simulation navigation with sim-cade-ish controls and that works well. Pure Sim Dakar might have a very limited customer base. I'd buy it... but i'll take this in the meantime.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was disappointed mostly due to the difficult control of all the vehicles. They all had the tendency to over steer in curves and lose control on straight lines for no clear reason. Also, the Sport mode was really not my thing – I don’t like bumping against other competitors, be pushed out of the track by them or even, roll over motorbike driver bodies...When Patch 1.4 came out, I started playing in Professional Mode. The Patch 1.4 has radically improved the cars control and with that, my opinion about the game. Secondly, the Professional Mode introduces a new dimension with the roadbook navigation. It is true that the copilot says wrong indications from time to time but mastering reading the roadbook is really satisfactory. This is when the game shows all its potential and purpose – it’s finally about rally raid and navigation.After reaching Level 25, I played the 12 stages of Dakar 2020 in Simulation Mode. Adding the (real) 170kph maximum speed limit to the roadbook navigation effort makes it a real coordination challenge for the brain. The duration of the stages nearing one hour, without any possibility to restart to the last waypoint is realistic and increases the difficulty/realism. I love it! One could say that the game is quite forgiving with the player mistakes but that’s OK to me. Yes it must be challenging but not frustrating either - I'm happy that my car can make a roll (-: and still I can win the stage ;-)Now I started playing with quads and motorbikes… and the oversteering problem is very present – really difficult to control! That’s a disappointment…As someone who lives in Saudi Arabia and has driven for thousands of kilometer in the desert, I can confirm the landscapes are beautiful and representative of Saudi Arabia. However, the stages do not really look like the actual legs. I’ve been personally on several stages of the Dakar in Saudi Arabia and some aspects such as the wadis are missing - and clearly no stage is like the actual one. All in all, I like the game and recommend it. For the record, I had bought Dakar 18 and returned it within 1 hour. This new edition is much better – cars finally behave like cars.Things to be improved:

_childDocuments_.review: After almost a year, I finally LOVE this game. Why so long? Because when I bought and downloaded it on day 1, the framerate was terrible and there were micro-delays taking me out of the enjoyment. I played a few times throughout the year, never really caring if I played it again. But yesterday, as of this writing, I played one more time hoping that perhaps I was wrong and Nope, not wrong. Didn't like playing it again. Laggy and just not fun. : (In my frustration and disappointment, I decided to move all my Graphics from Medium to EPIC. I wanted to see just how slow this thing could go (morbid curiosity). HOLY CRAP - this changed the game completely. The frame rate IMPROVED after setting the graphics higher?? I am using an RTX 3060 so I thought I had already maxed it out. But for some reason, this game runs worse on lower graphics settings. It's like the optimization has been reversed and it only has good frame rates on higher graphic settings. Now, I LOVE this game. It's smooth. It's so detailed and expansive. The graphics and effects are amazing. The vehicles feel right. The physics are  beautiful. I'm using a Thrustmaster TX-SW and the force feedback is phenomenal - I can feel everything, the small bumps, the pull on the tires, even the railroad tracks that try to grab the wheel from you. It is pure joy driving now, all because I decided to push the graphics to the limit. I had to dial them back just a little bit in one or two settings to get a good balance, but like I said, it's now a different game. Don't get me wrong, there are still flaws: -The co-driver can sometimes be a detriment because he's late or wrong (calling out the wrong CAP (direction) that don't match the book). I just turn off his calls and do much better. -You sometimes have to be super spot on with some of the markers otherwise you'll be lost. A few degrees off your course can make a huge difference. Challenging but also, that's part of the challenge too. Still, eventually you are helped to get back on track. -The AI can be true bastards sometimes. You're doing well and one decides to come up behind you and pit-maneuver you into a 360. What did I do to you? I had one guy on a motorcycle pull in front of my car and slow down... I wasted him but I wasn't trying to. Then, he caught up and did it again! Right in front of my car! So, the AI Needs work. There's a ton to like about this game and quite a bit to piss you off (had it crash on me tonight - will send error message to devs), but now instead of having no desire to play like I used to, I can't wait to get back to it because everything runs so much smoother after updating my graphics settings. It's the kind of fun and challenge I was hoping it would be on day 1. The game has been lambasted in the reviews, which is too bad because now I want to play others online and there's no one around. I really, really hope people get back into this title so the game doesn't fade away. It's an impressive achievement.

_childDocuments_.review: I can recommend Dakar Desert Rally but if you are not sure after reading reviews, whishlist it and wait a couple of months for features like freeroam, livery editor and track editor release.I waited to unlock simulation mode before I wrote a review so I can experience most of what the game has to offer. Firstly, it feels like 3 diferent games in one package and it is best to look at it that way. All gamemodes have mostly separate progression and you can exclusively play one of the gamemodes, not touch any other and still have fun. I think it might be better if these gamemodes are even more separated with separate garages and leveling. And Simulation mode should be unlocked from the start. is pure arcade fun. I was listening to a motorstorm soundtrack and enjoing jumps over dunes and pretty detailed crashes and suprisingly good rider ragdolls. Tracks are a mix of fantasy and real tracks. offers the similar tracks as Sport mode, but with more "realistic" type of racing taking place on them. Most of the stages are longer than in Sport mode. It is similar to Simulation mode but without general speed limits present in Dakar Rally which results in some pretty hard and unrealistic races where AI just blasts through bumps and dunes without any care for their vehicle. I takes around 30 minutes to complete one whole event. is in my opinion the best Dakar experience this game has to offer. Tracks in sim mode are recreations of the Dakar Rally from 2020 to 2022. Stages are longer than in sport and pro mode. It takes aroun 40 minutes per stage and around 2 hours for the whole event. There are general speed limits in place which prevent just blasting through everything. AI behaves more realistic than in pro and sport mode. All this combined makes sim mode the most fun (at least for me).It is important to note that I was mostly driving trucks! feels good. It is responsive and vehicles behave resonably. It is not as realistic as Dirt Rally or RBR but is good enough. It definately feels better than Dakar 18. Different surfaces affect the vehicle differently. For example sand dunes are much harder to climb than typical soil. Wheels slip and struggle for grip while the open differential just makes things worse. are great. Suspension works nicely, tires deform on the wheels and numerous bits and bobs on cars behave mostly physicaly accurate. Sometime it buggs out but it is mostly stable. model is more in depth than I expected with damage being modeled for things like the engine but also parts like the clutch and batteries. Damaged parts affect the vehicles handling. It is just unfortunate it does not affect gameplay in a big way because it is to easy to fix a vehicle before each stage or rally. Repairs should take time at least in sim and pro mode. You can choose which part to repair (clutch, transmission, lights, battery, engine, etc.) but the game does not encurage that when you can fix the whole vehicle with a press of a button for lik 60 DC.There are a lot of vehicles in the game. From bikes and quads to cars and sxs and of course trucks. Also there are classic vehicles like citroen cv2 and peugeot 205. The only thing i dont like about the vehicles is that classic vehicles are mixed with contemporary vehicles when raced. I think they should be in their own category. Especially for multiplayer.One thing i miss from Dakar 18 is being able to leave your vehicle and dig yourself out.All in all the game has its problems but I definatley recommend it as there is no better rally raid game on the market.PS if you can't find out how to turn off in race music make sure you lower the "playlist" volume.

_childDocuments_.review: In nearly 20 years on Steam this is THE ONLY GAME I have ever refunded.It's THAT miserable.I wanted to like this so bad, but sadly, just like nearly every other Saber Interactive product, this game is absolutely bleeding 'minimal viable product' out of every orifice.A relatively niche genre like this can't be expected to have a hundred million dollar budget, and could be worth buying if the game fundamentals are functioning okay. This is not the case.The biggest problems boil down to the driving physics being fundamentally unenjoyable, the world being bland, ugly and uninteresting (a massive empty desert is awesome, repetitive ugly canyons are not), the professional racing directions are a mess, the AI is infuriating and the game performance kills any shred of joy someone could have with it.A more inclusive list of all the problems I encountered in no particular order:-Excluding only the dunes environment and the car models, the game generally has subpar visuals and is almost completely outdated graphically (ps3 era graphics just in high resolution) while terribly optimized with stutters, pop in, low fps and crashes. Especially rocks, mountains and foliage look terrible.-Countless visual glitches and low effort production value, you can be driving through a canyon and the entire sunlight and shadows just flicker on and off, road markers and grass always pop in 20 ft in front of your vehicle on maxed settings. I've seen AI quads ghost driving around without a driver npc seated. Some vehicles have completely non functioning head or tail lights. Bugs will be a recurring theme. This is an extremely buggy game.-When you start Freeroam you can see your car falling out of the sky when spawning in like you're playing in some kind of editor and half the world and car model have yet to load in while gameplay has started (on a 7gb/s nvme drive)-While sand displacement is okay, the tire tracks disappear 20 ft behind your car-Certain vehicles GAIN traction and speed instead of losing traction and speed when you climb steep hills IN REVERSE. Normally-unclimbable 50 degree slopes can be powered up 100km/h in reverse no problem. I mean you can't make this ♥♥♥♥ up.-You can see clear abrupt hard cuts in terrain changes where the developers just used terrain brushes to draw the world as quickly as possible, absolutely everywhere.There is no handcrafted personality, no immersion, no realism nor videogamey fun to anything about this world. Way older massive open world low budget games like Just Cause 1 and FUEL, while also using copy paste scenery, have much, much higher world quality in a much larger setting than this game.-This extends beyond visual mediocrity, I've had my truck clip through the ground of the world in the first hour of gameplay, and I got stuck on and behind scenery while exploring in freeroam multiple times in the 90 minutes I played. You can see the cracks in the world geometry everywhere when you go off the beaten path for just a second and you can go out of bounds everywhere.-A large part of the vehicles just feel like floating stiff boxes on rough ice. They are generally neither realistic nor fun to drive.-Physics overall are GARBAGE and extremely jank. Jumping and landing feels really bad, vehicles drive unnaturally, they are stiff yet finicky, the weight of the vehicles feels awful. -A whole bunch of vehicles do not sound like their real life versions at all and instead sound like electric mobility scooters-Codriver has such a monotonous artificial robot voice it's giving me a headache hearing him spout way too much text with way too little good info NON STOP, sounds like they used Microsoft Sam levels of AI speech generation.-Professional mode codriver notes are rushed, not checked properly and not written with due diligence. Notes can come way too late, long after you've passed the note's objective because the codriver was too busy talking about pointless landmarks from last checkpoint, sometimes codriver will completely SKIP compass readouts or crucial direction changes when there IS time, where there are new coordinates present on the physical map in the corner but the driver simply never calls them out, and sometimes the codriver will contradict itself in the same sentence ('leave tracks keep left' when tracks ARE the route going left.....) and the codriver will even flatout lie calling for changes in course that are simply nonexistant when following the route perfectly. I've had cap readouts that when followed actively drove me straight AWAY from the next checkpoint.-Damage balance is jank. You can drive a perfect 30 minute race and be on world record pace, then finish last because you had to change two flats and a radiator because of a 20 mph bump into rocks while 95% of the AI drivers magically do not need a single repair ever. Then at the same time you can do a deathroll 8 times over and drive off perfectly fine.-Distance scaling is awful. 1km in this game is like 50 yards. It ruins immersion and completely screws your mind when you have to follow notes that callout '2km' that in reality mean 'in 100 meters'.-Tried one 'sports' race against AI, they just ram straight into your vehicle at full speed non stop, the AI in Wreckfest is less aggressive and I'm not even kidding. You can be fighting for first place in a massive endurance race, then AI just becomes an unstoppable force and freighttrains into you, you instantly lose your entire engine, wheels, need to repair to even drive again bam rip your 20 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minutes because with that time penalty you instantly lost the entire 3 race event while AI drives on without a problem har dee har.-Extremely unnatural and ugly lighting, everything in the world except your own car and dune sand looks silvery and washed out, ps3 era levels of bloom-Atrocious performance on a high end system (constant microstutter on a system with a 7gb/s nvme)-And to top the ♥♥♥♥ sundae it crashed with Unreal Engine 4 Fatal error (like countless other people have encountered) OVER A YEAR AFTER IT'S LAUNCH THIS STILL HAPPENS TO EVERYONEThe only positives this game has going for it are the vehicles themselves, the selection is 'okay' even if half of them are reskins of identical vehicles and there's only one quad, the models are pretty good with decent detail, moving parts, wind blowing in the tarps, good visual damage, some of the sound design has good detail with interior camera's having shaking parts, the tires making a good sound and the sound is directional if the camera swings around. The motorcycle and quad rider animations are good, the bike wobble and animations for climbing rocks are great. The camera options are also good with multiple interior views allowing free lookaround and a heli chase cam. And finally I have to give props for at least having some small destructible objects in the world like fences and props like chairs and barrels having basic physics.There are the tiniest sparks of what could have been absolute brilliance when you're driving around in free roam, cruising the endless dunes. But still you are pulled out of the immersion every second by something. Visual glitches, the sun literally turning on and off constantly, pop in, janky physics, floaty jumps and wonky landings, un-fun driving, brushwork rushwork terrain, and all I can do is just be sad and hope that this license goes to a better publisher as soon as possible, or the management is replaced allowing people to work properly on their games before and after launch. There is SOME talented work here. But it's wasted in the rushed end product and lack of post launch support.I buy and enjoy a lot of games with a mixed reception as I can usually find at least some fun in them. If even ONE aspect of DDR was at least decent I could accept that somewhat for a low price, but this game delivers on absolutely nothing of any value. It's core mechanics are fundamentally unfun.

_childDocuments_.review: This genre (rally raid) doesn't have many games, so any entry is to be recommended... I really like the length of the stages, and how the vehicles feel driving on sand (it actually feels like a deep layer of sand, not just a sandy texture you're "floating over"). What I dislike is the inconsistent AI. When they're too far away to be seen, they are simulated. Only when they get close to you, do physics apply to them. They seem to consistently have more horsepower to get up dunes than the player, and they never have to slow down to navigate or think where the next waypoint is. They really are machines, treating every stage like they know the route by heart (because they do). They only make dumb mistakes when they're near you - when they're offscreen, their performance is flawless (they even arrive at the finish without a single speck of dust on their car) but they get random repair penalties (even though they never stopped). For the player, there's a repair mechanic between stages, but it doesn't cost time so no thought goes into this - just press "repair all".I could go on for hours... there's a lot they could improve in this game, but it's still pretty enjoyable as it is.

_childDocuments_.review: Looks like I finally stumbled upon a racing game that will pull me from my Forza addiction, at least for a while. I wasn’t sure I want to check this one out, but I’m glad I did.I never played any Dakar game before, so I don’t have any comparison in that regard, but I played quite a few racing games in general. What I found here is a decent rally title which I would place almost in the same league as DiRT Rally 2.0. Maybe not as  as Forza, but with graphics and handling model both better than latest WRC efforts (for me at least). Also, much cheaper than said Forza when it comes to Polish regional pricing set for this title – finally, a sensible publisher.No game-breaking bugs on premiere day. No other bugs, really, besides occasional stutter and frame drops during a race, and this is, frankly, a bit inconvenient at times. I hope this will be ironed out shortly, or perhaps new drivers will take care of it.Dakar setting looks very eye-catching. Racing especially over those huge dunes in the sunset stood out for me the most so far. Real-life locations and dynamic weather system provide variety in the scenery, too. There are bikes and quads available. I’ve never used a bike in a racing game, so I mostly race on bikes and quads now.AI needs a bit of tweaking, which is already acknowledged by the devs. At the beginning of a race, or at any point really, it can happily ram into you as of now, so you must put some work to try and actively avoid your competitors. Also, you mostly race in the sand, so be prepared for abrupt changes in your driving line, should you — more or less consciously – decide to implement the  rule. This game is not about that, and thankfully. Don’t worry if you crash once or twice – given the number of stages in an event, you’ll still have many occasions to be faster elsewhere and take the overall win.Lots of controller mapping settings, graphics options – a proper PC game I’d say. The accompanying background soundtrack has a potential to not irritate after five hours. What  irritate is that you need to spend at least 15 to 20 hours to unlock the  mode. I like progressive nature of gaming, but some may be impatient here. Oh, and no photo mode yet – is allegedly promised in a future update.Still, I recommend this game to DiRT Rally and WRC fans. Maybe a bit less to Forza followers, but those with open minds will find many good things here as well. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Dakar Desert Rally

_childDocuments_.review: [Quick update: Patch 1.4 update seems to have made a genuine improvement to AI overtaking behaviours and has smoothed out some twitchiness in bike handling. I'm yet to test the handling in much depth, but it at least seems like a step in the right direction and shows the developers are responding well to community feedback. I believe it's also fixed the checkpoint glitch mentioned towards the end of my review, though I've not confirmed this yet.]A few performance hitches, semi-homicidal AI and occasionally twitchy handling haven't stopped me from having a blast flying through the desert in Dakar: Desert Rally. On the visual front the desert environments are varied, beautiful, and epic in scale. The vehicles are fully destructible and look great in all conditions with excellent attention to detail, right down to the way the cloth atop racing trucks ripples through the air, compressing and billowing with every rise and fall. Riders on bikes and quads likewise look great as they dynamically shift their weight around to compensate for bumps, jumps and turns (there's even a setting to control this directly, though I've not been adventurous enough to try it... yet).The various weather effects add further variety and are nothing short of stunning; there was something so cool about looking over my shoulder to check on my rivals, only to see them swallowed up by a rapidly encroaching wall of sand as the first dust storm I'd seen swept in from behind... Or blitzing along the coastline at night when a massive storm hit and lightning began crashing down in all directions, offering brief flashes of improved visibility amidst the downpour.The soundtrack may be my favourite original racing game OST since the days of pre-EA Burnout. I accept that orchestra-backed hard rock isn't going to be everyone's cup of tea, but I couldn't be happier with the choice. Car audio is also great. The navigator lines can come off feeling a little robotic, very American, and are sometimes ambiguous, not always seeming to line up perfectly with the roadbook - but for the most part they still serve their purpose well enough. I've primarily been piloting bikes anyhow, where there's no room for a navigator onboard so it's left up to me to decipher the arcane scribblings of the roadbook in (relative) silence.Difficulty settings are locked to three different preset modes; Sport, Professional, and Simulation. Whilst the former two are unlocked from the start, the Sim mode requires around 15-30 hours of progress made in the other modes before it unlocks. I understand hardcore Dakar/sim-racing enthusiasts' frustration at having to grind through less-realistic modes to get to the content they care about, and I sincerely hope this is something that can be addressed in a future patch. As a total newcomer to the world of Dakar myself, I'm very grateful for the inclusion of various features which make the experience more accessible up front. I only hope that future updates can bring more flexibility to allow players to tailor the difficulty to their own preferences instead of being shoehorned into one of the three categories; all the more because each mode currently contains unique routes which are coupled to those distinct settings. It'd be fun to try different combinations, like racing against harder AI with simplified navigation on the Professional routes, or trying Simulation's realistic navigation across long endurance routes with less punishing penalties for doing repairs after I inevitably crash into rocks because I was focusing a little too hard on the roadbook. PC performance was rough in the early hours, with a lot of hitching which seemed to exacerbate some of the issues with twitchy handling (more on that shortly). Fortunately things have improved a great deal as I've put more hours into the game. That leads me to believe that shader compilation may have been the main culprit, with hitching being at its worst when first driving through new areas with unique props and materials. Either way, on an RTX 3080 I'm now hitting a mostly steady 60fps at 4k with balanced DLSS and all graphics settings either maxed out or at their second-highest option. It looks and feels great.For the most part I think the vehicle handling hits a fairly ideal "simcade" sweetspot. It's not as brutally detailed as something like Dirt Rally, but it still feels distinctly physical and grounded in reality. The catch is that oversteer currently feels off; the moment a vehicle begins to oversteer by even the slightest margin, a spin-out is all but inevitable. Different vehicle types will be prone to this by differing degrees, with quads behaving worst and trucks generally being more manageable, but it's present across the board. I've gradually learned to play in a way which mitigates it, but there's no denying that not being able to reliably drift in a rally game feels distinctly wrong. Fortunately this has been flagged as a known issue by the developers, so I look forward to seeing improvements in future patches.Whilst my experience has otherwise been mostly bug-free, there is one issue worth noting; late in the career is an event which currently appears to be impassable for the majority of players due to erroneous disqualification at a checkpoint, near the end of an hour-long race. I've been holding off on attempting the event myself until I see it fixed. It's undeniably a bit of a bummer - and understandably very frustrating for any who encounter it - but in the meantime I'm still finding fun to be had in improving my times and trying other vehicles on previous events.All in all I've found a lot to like about Dakar Desert Rally, even with a few rough edges. With a little extra polish and the addition of various features promised in the roadmap I genuinely believe this could become an offroad racing masterpiece. Until then there's still a beautiful, wonderfully unique racing experience on offer for those who can look past its flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel since the last game: something has been lost. Sure, the previous game wasn't exactly a masterpiece either but at times it would at least give you  of the sensation that you were taking part in one of the most interesting events on the motorsport calendar.Long stages under the desert sun. Sand, dunes, isolation. All of that good stuff.Granted, the handling was a bit shonky and the co-driver was, at best, grating - but there was something there... That feeling of Dakar, however fleeting.Whatever has happened in the interim has ruined what little enjoyment there was for me in the previous game.To articulate this feeling of Dakar is a difficult thing but this time around I find myself feeling something else which is much easier to quantify: frustration and disappointment.The landscapes you'll find yourself driving through can, at times, be pretty stunning. Some of the weather effects are down right awesome and when the two are combined, at their best, it is a rather fantastic experience. However, these moments feel very fleeting as something else in the game will pull you out of your brief reverie, and back to the fact that this just isn't a very good game.The selection of vehicles is excellent. The roster of the last three years is more or less intact, the main players are all included anyway. The method of unlocking the classic vehicles however, is not so excellent. Complete each short rally in each different class? Who honestly thought that was a good idea?And that is more or less all I can find that I like about this game. I could spend a VERY long time reeling off a whole list of issues with the game at the time of writing but at this point it just feels pretty pointless.What I will describe however is my sense of frustration and disappointment mentioned earlier. Dakar, for all its history, good and bad: there is a lot to say about it. You could have discussions about it that last almost as long as the race itself. There is none of that here. This game (with my admittedly low playtime (so far)) feels very empty. Not in a content-sense, but in a, again, much harder to quantify way. It feels like the game is lacking soul, character, love, something, anything. It feels like shovelware - a game made to fulfil a contract - and that makes me very sad. When you think of all that a Dakar game could be, this game is not it.If you're looking for a title that will scratch the Dakar itch, whilst we wait on updates here (or a miracle) - I would suggest checking out the previous game. It does have a lot of the same problems that others have mentioned (handling, dodgy co-driver and the like) but it at least felt more like Dakar and will most likely be a bit cheaper.I'm going to continue holding out hope that this game will someday reach it's potential, but right now that feels as fruitless as trying to dig a 10 ton truck out of a dune with a teaspoon.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still building more detail, but I want to say immediately, the game is good, and the Saudi Map Extension DLC is the sole cause of all the crashes I experienced. I was able to install all the DLC without issue, except the Saudi Map DLC. Once I installed the Map Extension, the game was unplayable with constant crashes.Dakar Desert Rally is perfect for those of us that are tired of Dirt Rally 2.0 crap. When I fired up Dakar, I was locking my screen, pulling the internet cable, and doing all sorts of things to INTENTIONALLY crash this game, and I could not. This game can launch offline, save, and I had no issues with cloud saves or anything. This was the exact answer to all my Dirt Rally complaints.IT WAS ONLY AFTER INSTALLING THE SAUDI MAP EXTENSION DLC THAT I HAD ANY ISSUES AT ALL.Full transparency, I did get errors as the game closed without that DLC, but nothing disrupted gameplay or my save file. This is a lot better than I expected, and I think that Map DLC is the only problem at this time. If you are looking for something to scratch the Dirt Rally itch, I think this game is genuinely better. It is much more streamlined and doesn't feel unnecessarily flashy, for example, you get from game launch, to the race, with less menu ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. The game is very well optimized on my i5-12600 and 3080 with maxed out settings at 4K with DLSS quality.The roadbook has a legend so you can learn 100+ symbols and review them constantly and I open it and just keep skimming them and slowly I'm learning the language of Dakar, just like I was learning the language of Rally a few years ago.Just like Dirt Rally, I'm learning the copilot lingo as well. At the start, it is just constant nonsense, but then I learned slowly what the copilot is trying to tell me and that process of learning and discovery is just as fun as when I was learning Dirt.I LOVE that it's open world and there is NO MAP. It takes skill to not get lost.  The game does not penalize me for being slow. I take my time to find all the waypoints and cross the finish line, and that has been tons of fun. I'm learning how to read the roadbook, because it has at least 100 symbols and words to represent things as specific as "water inside concrete" because you would want to know that, actually, because THERE IS NO MAP and I love that. It's all roadbook and exploration and the roadbook is awesome. Even when I'm slow as heck, I found myself turning onto a track with 5 different vehicles close together and it was just like I'm in a freaking game trailer overtaking them as I finished the race. Bobbing and weaving like that Motorstorm trailer for PS3 and as I passed the biker next to a car I was thinking in my head "huh, it only took like 20 years for that PS3 trailer to be real!"This game is fun as heck and if you like Dirt Rally or Dirt Rally 2.0, buy this and go straight to Professional, skip easy mode. It's good. Don't install the Saudi Map Extension. If the game is crashing for you, refund. I was actively trying the crash and refund, but the game wouldn't crash. I thank Steam for letting me form my own informed opinions.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, this is nowhere near realistic or Dakar rally simulation for multiple reasons: 1. Controls feel too like arcade. I say this because I was easily able to handle my vehicle from 3rd person (in fact, it was even easier than from the cocpit view). I get that devs wanted to make this game accessible, but even Forza Horizon 5 is more complex.  2. AI. I'm not talking about the sport mode, I'm talking about proffesional, which is supposed to, at least partially, simulate real Dakar. 4 times out of 5 I reach a huge pile of vehicles on 30th km or so, which causes 2 things: FPS drops for no reason (my GPU should be able to handle an increased amount of vehicles) and unrealistic crashes, because the AI is very dumb, at least right now. 3. AI (again). I have already played a few racing games (from wreckfest to Dirt Rally 2.0). i have never seen such an aggressive AI, not even in wreckfest. Here, it will take every opportunity to screw you, ramming you if you drive anywhere near it. Seriously, this is not how racing works. I thought Dakar is more about helping others when they get stuck, not sending them into sand and rocks whenever possible. A huge disappointment here. 4. Physics and terrain. If you look at real Dakar, you will see vehicles getting stuck, drivers going around big sand dunes, because it's an extremely unpredictable terrain. None of that is in the game, or at least I haven't encountered it in my gameplay. You can just drive wherever you want. Trucks are big and should tip over when drifting at a wrong time (I get that they are adapted, but here you can pull a handbrake in 140 kph in what is supposed to be a deep sand and all that happens is you spinning around, losing speed).Conclusion: Do you want an offroad extreme weather racing wih mutiple vehicle classes? Buy this game. Graphics is good and racing is pretty fun (when the game works). You don't even need a wheel to enjoy it. But if you're looking for an offroad racing sim, avoid this game. You will be disappointed.Oh, and did i mention that out of 16 competitors, you have to place 8th or higher in order to proceed to the next stage? Didn't know this was a thing in Dakar rally

_childDocuments_.review: I stand by my Dakar 18 review. If you want a more authentic Dakar rally raid experience - play that. This game is more like an arcade approximation of Dakar. The stages are shrunk and 'spectacle'fied. There's pumping orchestral rock 'epic' music everywhere. They were going for a vibe that they kind of missed. The physics are a little improved over Dakar 18, especially on the bikes - which are raceable now. But they're still not very great. I wouldn't recommend this over 18 or Baja Edge of Control HD for anyone who's seriously into rally raid. While you can shut off the markers from the start for 'professional' mode, the actual 'sim' mode is locked behind a level grind and even then it's pointless since the stages are so spectaclefied you can make out landmarks easily. Which is a small mercy, since the robot man reading the notes is awful. Tbh I'll probably just stay in sport mode and enjoy the casual experience and go back to 18 or Baja for a more sim one. The graphics presentation is excellent and the damage model is borderline incredible but it's head back by a terrible lack of speed sense and the less than ideal physics. Overall if you want a rally raid game that's more focused than Dirt 5 but less involved than Baja or 18, this is worth a try and maybe even a buy - on sale -

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this 2 months after release. Using fanatec base/pedals/handbrake and th8a shifter. The FFB is absolutely fine - not iracing level, but I can not call it bad by any means - it is very decent. Playing on a regular controller was great too.Physics are a lot better than the previous game. It is still a little arcady in some cases, e.g. the gravity and centrifugal forces work in your favor sometimes, but you definitely have to worry about stability all the time, you flip over rather easily and it feels immersive.Other stuff: there are minor visual bugs, e.g. when you finish a race and the game shows top 3 vehicles - everyone but you are new and shiny, not even dusty or destroyed in any way. AI can be a little dumb, but I cannot recall another racing game with decent AI to be honest. The graphics are great, except for an odd amount of graininess I've found while in the first person camera. Not game-breaking, likely to get patched, or perhaps I can fix it with tweaking the settings - didn't spend time on that yet.It is worth noting that the main meat of the game (at least for me and many others) is professional/simulation mode on trucks. Everything else feels like it was added to boost the sales a little bit - which is fair. Though it must be a tad unclear for a new player what the game is really about. It is mostly about navigation and reading the racebook on the go. This is not forza - you don't race against 15 opponents at the same time. Very unique gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: (I feel pity for the wave of negative reviews the devs got so I will rate this as a "recommended" because well........I do recommend it actually.........but there is also flaws in the game and other personal things I didn't quite like about it. I still recommend it though !)I opened the game, played through it, and had a blast to be honest ! But.......after looking at the reviews of what other people think, it helped me wash away my thoughts which were greatly radicalised by my excitement of a new Dakar game coming out. It's not a "sim", which I expected and although I havent tried it on a wheel yet, people are telling me not to, which is quite disappointing. The camera options are also great especially for a wheel.....whenever that will work properly lolAnd all the repairs and stuff is very cool too.Another thing I dont really like, which also makes the game feel arcadey, is that the cars start the stage together rather than having to start individually with a minute game in between. _childDocuments_.review: This game isn't without it's issues. In the early (shorter) stages you"ll be frustrated by the navigator costing you a lot of time. But don't give up. In the longer stages, he will still cost you time, but this is when you start to realize it's just part of Dakar. Everyone loses time because they get lost. The AI loses time because they miss waypoints too!This isn't  sport where you're just trying to be a faster driver, you're also trying to be the best at finding out where you need to go. And it's really good at doing that. The navigator does make strange mistakes (eg telling you "left", and giving you a compass point that very much takes you "right"), but it matters less when the stage itself is at least 20 minutes (and not 2 minutes for the early ones)sometimes damage is weird, and repairs take the player A LOT longer than the AI seems to get.but then you drive through a sandstorm (try the Extreme Rally!), and getting to the finish just feels like accomplishment.it's not the best racing game out there, but it's definitely the best Dakar game.

It runs really smoother and more stable now, most of the bugs were fixed, I have not encountered any major issues playing it through. It has still some general flaws with its game mechanics though, mainly not realistic physics of some vehicles and mandatory speed limits in simulation mode without any speed limiters available onboard like the real dakar cars have. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely a brilliant game that managed to scratch the itch of a proper game that is similar to Forza's rally raid but they managed to replicate as much of the sport as possible. Enjoyed it so far and please fix the bugs. Positives: + Absolutely a delight to play. Can't really say the same for a lot of newer racing games while Dakar respects the sport decently. It is not sim like AC but it is one very very very enjoyable game on gamepad+ It is nice to see a licensed series game that have cars from several years in one game plus vintage cars.+ Driving handling is quite good for the most part on gamepad. + You do need to see where you drive, as landing wrongly over a sand dune will wreck your car+ There is an element of endurance too despite fairly short races where you have to live with damages. Broke one head lights 25% into a race? Have to live with one headlight in the dark. + The cars and bikes has decent handling characteristics+ Reasonable accessible, it feels like a long lost cousin of Grid 1 or Dirt 2 to me+ No party atmosphere that plagues many modern racing games from Forza to Grid Legends. All you get in Dakar is humans vs nature+ The track variety are fantastic that ranges from jumping over sand dunes, speeding through mountainous terrain or even crossing towns. Very good sense of journey. + Love that you see other classes on the rally where even if you drive a car, you'll still see some bikes, quads or trucks racing ahead+ The AI is decent, they do make mistakes when they are driving through dangerous environments but it is occuring too often. No catchup or AI running on god mode physics which is nice and suited for the spirit of Dakar. Unlike Forza ridiculous AI in raid mode. Negative: - Performance isnt the best, with occasional stutter to low 20 fps- I have been getting fatal error crash to desktop- The occasional weird snapping behaviour with the physics is annoying. Often happens when you corner the car+ Environment is beautiful with good variety- The unlock system is absolutely rubbish to get the vintage cars, you need to win the rally with all 5 classes to unlock the vintage car. - The unlock system for modern cars is also rubbish, you need to buy each car with each livery separately. Cash gain is slow but no IAP- AI is not perfect, they are crashing too often now. Especially the trucks.

_childDocuments_.review: The number one thing I look for in a driving game is the driving feel and force feedback. Unfortunately Dakar Desert Rally feels terrible. However much you fiddle with the force feedback sliders the only thing that comes through the wheel is rather violent bumps and and a pull if you're completely spinning out. Forza Horizon has better feel and that's pretty arcade like. If you're expecting anything resembling a simulation you'll be sorely disappointed. The driving feel seems to be designed for Sport mode but this replaces the roadbook navigation with arcade beacon checkpoints.The USP of this game is the rally raid roadbook and navigating through an open and hostile environment. That element is good: the vast landscapes are constantly varying, diverse and look impressive... if you have the latest graphics card. With a GTX 1060 6GB @ 1080p on medium graphics settings (level 2/5) the frame rate can barely be maintained at 60fps and often drops to 45fps. Switching to low makes it look 10 years old. This is pretty poor for the most popular graphics card on Steam.Another annoyance is the unlockable vehicles require you to win the same race in every vehicle class including motorcycles which don't work well with a wheel so require a controller but even then they seem quite unresponsive in comparison to cars. Why not unlock cars with car races and motorcycles with bike races?Overall this game is trying to be too many different things and fails to excel in any of them. If you want open world racing directly against others (like the Sport mode) you're probably better off with Forza Horizon. If you want simulation rallying against the clock (that Professional & Simulation is attempting) you'll have a lot more fun in Dirt Rally 2.0. If you're a diehard rally raid fan I hope they bring some major improvements to the driving experience.

_childDocuments_.review: When it works, it can be very fun, and I enjoyed the half an hour it worked properly. The other half of it was crashes, stutters, suicidal AI, a music slider that does not work, physics that will not allow you to catch a slide or catapult you on the smallest boulder, and the most nitpicky of them all but still annoying, the distance counter going up at a much faster rate than the speed of the vehicle. The game pumps up kilometers as if you're going 900km/h when the speedometer says 150km/h.I wanted it to be good, and I hope with future updates it gets there, there is a lot of potential underneath. But in it's current state I can not recommend it I'm afraid, sorry.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, I would certainly recommend this game. Yes, it does have some issues and it certainly could do with some optimisation. In fact, whilst I'm moaning, I can't use my G29's h-shifter, because the Reverse gear simply does not work. Oh, and multiplayer is a bit sparse, but 'hopefully' this review may help that. If you get past the negatives, this game as so much potential. It manages to satisfy the casual and the sim fanatic alike. The handling model is a bit arcadey compared to the old version, but overall, it is more fun to drive. The format of the career and the unlockables seem to be reasonably laid out. It's a bit frustrating that you have to complete each stage, with every type of vehicle, mainly because I use a wheel. However, the unlockable vehicles are worthy classics to chase. The events themselves are, so far, very well detailed and laid out. It's like playing a classic arcade racer, like Sega Rally, with the chaos of Motorstorm, all wrapped up as the Dakar rally. I don't know if the tracks are official or if they actually drive through ship wrecks and tropical wetland. I kinda guess not. However, it makes for a fun race throughout. It is a bit odd that you encounter other vehicles when you're miles out in front, that treat you like it's Mad Max, but that all seems to add to the fun.Dakar 18 had the 'official sim' thing down. It was just rough around the edges. Dakar Desert Rally rekindles the arcade fun of old, wrapped up it a reasonable sim (esq). It should make for some mad multiplayer, but alas, so far I have met noone :( Someone play with me!?

_childDocuments_.review: Update after playing free roam: The free roam, full region wide open plains and hill country is just amazing, it is a totally different experience from sport and pro mode. Before you write a review I recommend to do a 314 km free roam section and take in the view, then write review (if not you miss out on the game's biggest offering). Well we asked for simulation, this is (free roam) Dakar 18 without the shovels but for all other aspect it is amazing and is just better than anything I have seen. Following Patch, update to review below: I think they fixed the game, AI makes a good effort avoiding crashing into each other or into the player, if accidents happen those types possibly play out similar way in real life (or close to it), all in all, the races are much more enjoyable, much more relaxing (but still keep your attention from start to finish), and even they feel more actual simulation like. I have seen no crashes or lost saves anymore either so far. For that I have decided the game is worth my time again, cars are very nicely modeled, driving physics are much more enjoyable (a bit more relaxing), I think this is mostly what most negative reviews asked for. If you were waiting for an update I think the latest patch made it happen.Update as of 50 hours of game play: the game made me reset my account today (Oct 9) by instructing me at start up to accept an Audi DLC (which I already had for the entire 50 hours) with a comment that my progress will be lost. There was no option to back out, not to accept, anything. I have accepted it and now I am back to level 1 from level 25 (at 50 hours I have just passed level 25 and started my first route in simulation mode). As of now I am starting over. Instead, I am playing Dakar 18, which is actually might be the better game after all. The open country truly simulation like, I think distances 1:1, car physics are fine in my opinion. I am using a brand new XBox controller with a relatively new gaming PC. I think lot of the audience of Dakar 18 expected cars drive on rails, when in reality vehicles are not that stable at speed driving over lose terrain. Dakar Desert Rally (the new release) while can be very pretty, the cars are nice to look at, all in all and extended arcade experience, with a monetarily discover-able simulation bits here and there. If you want the actual simulation, I am sorry to say, you have to go back to Dakar 18 (vast and drivable open country lays out in front of you for hundreds of miles, which is pretty awesome and unique, definitely supports the simulation feel). By the way, Dakar 18's copilot (guide who yells out driving directions) is very accurate, spot on, which is also impressive given how large distances you have to drive through. Update: the Quads are fine, the reason they are hard to ride (easily spins out if throttle is floored in corners) is because they are all rear wheel drive. If you ever drove a BMW on snow you know what this looks like (compared to a Subaru or any other all wheel drive vehicle)Super fun...the only issue I have encountered so far is that the music cannot be turned off. Driving is awesome, far better than Dakar 18 (which I have already liked). Just drive with some common sense, use the brakes, position yourself, etc. Do not blast through everything (if you do you will end up hitting all kinds of things). Just buy it if you are on the fence, the game is pure fun with the sense of discovery and realism. This is the only game in my library that I just cannot stop playing, all others were fine but none of them were so much fun for me. I must admit I do have a relatively new gaming PC, a Logitech G920 wheel (which works very well), but perhaps the most fun is driving with WASD and use mouse for camera around the car or bike while you are driving or riding. Super fast paced action, AI is flying by you or you fly by them, they crash with you, around you, or do their best to make the whole thing just a spectacle every time you get on a course. Damage is modeled very well also, you will see parts of your car flying off, remaining parts on the car will show visible damage (seem to be with large variation), driving will be impacted with excessive damage also (which you can fix on the trail to an extent with time penalty). And yes, suspension is fine, it works fine and it visibly articulates fine. I love the way the dust is kicked  up (again use the mouse to move the camera around the dust when possible and do not drive directly behind a large truck kicking up must of the dust). Guys there is no other racing game that is this much fun, I just tried ACC, I had to refund it for lack of entertainment, while the cars and physics were good, driving around the same course doing laps is just not for me. But this game is soooo much different. I think this is my only interest from my entire gaming library of over 200 games. I cannot wait for new content, however there is plenty to do already (currently level 17, looking forward to unlock simulation mode at level 25).Bugs: The game crashed on me a few times. That is it. I have no other bugs to report. Also, if you find that the navigator is not always right (I have not tested this fully but it seems ok to me, road book is also seems good not sure what the complaint is) but still; Do you think real human beings working as coopilots never make a mistake?? If we run into a coopilot here who is confused, guess what, this just adds to realism in my book.Advice: do not always push for first place, at least not in the earlier part of the races. Let the lead cars "lead the way" and crash if they have to, play defensive driving in the first half, then carefully try to move up, if you managed not to crash too many times you will have plenty of chances to take the lead cars over and finish first (in sport mode). Tip: large trucks drive very well with WASD and mouse for camera, especially from 3rd person mode (outside view). Same is true for motorcycles and cars. I advise you not to bother with quads (ATVs), they are impossible to drive due to unpredictable loss of traction (they had the same issue in Dakar 18).

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game. Unfortunately, as with many macrostudio releases in the past few years, it seems Saber put the horse before the cart.I didn't make it through the intro sequence before experiencing my first fatal CtD. Whenever you change game functions (Garage to bivouac, bivouac to stage, stage to next bivouac), there is a good chance that you will experience a crash.Additionally, there are several elements missing that should be considered base content for a game of this type: unique character models, a livery editor, replays, photo mode, etc. I would likely forgive this if this was marketed as early access, but Saber acts as though this is the end commercial product. The roadmap on the game's website also raises eyebrows. The aformentioned bells and whistles like custom paint and replay mode have been placed after a couple of DLC releases. Even then, none of the roadmap items specify a month, only that they will be (allegedly) released this year.GPU-bound aspects of the game are unpolished and unoptimized. I have i nvested over 1500 USD into my computer, and even on medium settings the game regularly drops to about 20 FPS. The game also stutters repeatedly during driving, which really harms your immersion and rhythm.I do hope that Saber actually gives DDR some much-needed love. If the constant crashes, poor framerate, and missing features do get sorted out later this year, I would happily recommend it. But right now, it just simply isn't worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's a list of reasons you should not buy this game (especially if you played Dakar 18)- No getting out of the car to use your shovel, rope and recovery boards or to ask for assistance.- Navigator is significantly worse than Dakar 18. He sounds like something from a D-List action movie. Also he told me I was going the wrong direction for 8 km only for me to make it to the next waypoint without issue. If I didn't know how to read a roadbook, I'd be completely lost.- AI is insufferably bad. I couldn't enter the checkpoint due to a pile up at the finish boards and it ruined the whole event.- Literally the only thing I enjoyed in this game was being able to play as Ari Vatanen in a Peugeot but I could already do that in Dakar 18.Some of these things can be fixed but it is going to take a while. _childDocuments_.review: When I pre-ordered this, my friends really wondered what I was thinking. What I was thinking was, I really enjoyed Dakar 18, even rough around the edges as it was, and I was intrigued what a new, serious rally raid experience would feel like. There's no competition for it, and it has room to be something completely different.Shame, then, that the result is a game of compromises, terrified to do anything interesting out of fear it will disrupt a casual audience it will not receive.The map is compressed. Obviously. I didn't expect them to include a 1/1 entire country. But it's compressed very oddly, with kilometers themselves  and thus all co-driver calls being excessively bizarrely short, as "in one kilometer" means "within the next three seconds". Trying to read the roadbook on higher difficulties when you are already there nearly every time you look at it is just brain-pretzeling baffling, and unlike many of my favorite driving games, having any actual experience with the sport being replicated will not help you with this strange gamified version.The vehicle roster is impressive, boasting three different years of competition, and lots of classic vehicles from Dakar history to boot. I think having many of the classics be unlockables is exciting and interesting. I think having them be locked behind redoing the stages with all classes is annoying, and locking them behind the  difficulty  is nonsensical. (Also let's be real, I was gonna be mad about SnowRunner stuff getting in instead of more actual rally raid cars, but they're actually very fun and funny, if deeply suboptimal.)Which by the way, the Easy difficulty plays nothing at all like Dakar 18 or like a rally raid in general, putting everybody on the track at the same time. The spirit and sportsmanship of the deadly race where you must cooperate to survive are completely absent as these jerkbags will t-bone and tackle you at any opportunity. When you spin out, you spin out. There is no saving yourself from a slide. Any loss of traction in anything but Trucks is a death sentence to your stage time, which has the side effect of making Trucks a lot more appealing than they usually would be.  Trucks are fun. I'll say this, trucks are fun.The weather effects are absolutely mystifying and gorgeous. Other Dakar games had the benefit of vast and varied locations, but this is mostly stuck with the desert; when it's getting lashed with sandstorms, thunderstorms, and snowstorms, though, it's gorgeous beyond a level of compare.However, where the rubber meets the road (or the traces, at least) is where it falls apart. You can't just run the Dakar. The tremendous long stages that made Dakar 18 so singular are gone unless you grind to unlock them. You aren't even allowed to have Simulation settings on at all because they are counted as a difficulty and must be unlocked. You  to slog through tiny stages and an utterly irrelevant wheel-to-wheel demo derby to get the  to be allowed to run the thing you probably bought the game for. Which begs the question, who is this for? It seems to, instead of letting you customize and put together the game you want to play, be insistent on forcing you to do every different variant of it like you're doing it wrong if you don't. It's too niche for a casual audience, and it punishes the niche audience by forcing them to play casually. It is a slog. It had potential to be something completely unmatched and uncontested and then just sort of got overwritten by a bevy of truly baffling design decisions and awful performance. It does not run well.I have been waiting for like eight months for it to finally click and be the game I was waiting for, because it still has no peers or opponents in this field, and it is not getting there. I feel for the devs stuck on a roadmap that's now months and months late for a tie-in game to an event that ended a long time ago. They're doing their best. I just think somebody somewhere in charge instituted some really baffling calls that drag this down, and I don't think there's gonna be much of an option to just patch those things out.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so I have played many of rally games in my 41 years, and this one for what it offers is the best.Now its a new game, so yeah its got some bugs, but I played a solid 4hrs+ without any problems.Some people have complained about stability, and how the AI will wreck you in which are all true.At the same time rubbing is racing, and you are going at high rates of speed through the desertin blizzards, sandstorms, monsoons, and whatever else you can think of.Also pro tip for offroading in general is if you want stability/traction let some air out of the tires.Now keep in mind this is at the cost of acceleration by a smidge, so 5 to 6lbs tops.Hammer Down Peeps ;)

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: Forget Dakar 18, this is a whole other experience that is more enjoyable, polished, and compelling.  18' felt like you were just wandering aimlessly while someone yelled at you.  This is not like that at all. (thank god)If you are looking for an awesome long-form racing/off-road experience then this is the game for you.  Some of the rally stages are an hour long (once you reach Simulation difficulty at level 25), yet do not get boring.  If you have a lot of time to invest, this game is totally worth it.  The quick races on Sport difficulty are fun as well, but not nearly as challenging and entertaining as Simulation or Professional modes. IMO, other than SnowRunner, this is the best off-road experience out there. EDIT:  I have been remiss to not have mentioned the graphics - they are amazing and the game is very pretty.  It's a perk, not the sole reason to play this, but damn is it easy on the eyes.NOTE: After acquiring a logitech g920 wheel+pedals I have to say that the game is way better with them.  It's  fun with a controller but it's a blast with a wheel.  The feedback is great and it's easier to stay under the speed limit with pedals.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is a total let down 😞 Everyone had big hopes for it and unfortunately for some reason developers failed to provide a good sequel to Dakar 18. Of course there are many improvements and changes but those turned game into Forza Horizon clone what is not good in case of rally raid game.First of all game is boring. With simplified physics and navigation even in simulation mode I was bored very quickly as most stages are full throttle for most of time. There is no need to care much about how you drive and ride because off track elements like rocks bushes or branches are just visual objects - they do not interact with vehicle. So in the end you go full speed through rough terrain where you need to watch out only for bumps and trees. As for physics it is more arcade than simulation: traction loss was removed, no matter if you choose car or bike you have full traction even on steep sandy dune. You can not get stuck in sand what we had in previous game. Bikes is the worst and easiest class in game. They are glued to srface, they brake immidiately, hardly lift up on bumps amd can land from building high dune wothout crashing. Once they loose grip, vehicle ends in uncontrollable spin. If you are a car class fan, you may find some fun because it is the class that has the best physics, and what is a major improvement comparing to previous game. Features: many of features advertised before release did not arrive… yet. No roadbook editor, no livery editor, no photo mode, no replays, no multiplayer co-driving. All those are supposed to be added later as for some reason, after few DLCs developers decided to drop the schedule and instead of releasing DLCs consecutively, they will release one big update during summer.Biggest let down, next to physics is immersion. Dakar 18 had many flaws but player was able to leave car, repair it, tow, feel the surrounding world thanks to fantastic environmental sounds. Penalties were not only by the added time but also time of day changed. Here if you crash, you get time added to final result - you do not feel the time flow needed for repairs because there is no such thing.You will not experience time of day change despite its there - even longest stages feel like they are 30 minutes in game time because time sun movement is too slow. Stages are indeed bigger but so are speeds. Meters pass like miliseconds and navigation points are sometimes so close that it reminds driving through waypoints nather than navigating through dunes. Night racing is something you will experience very rarely and even if you get lost riding around night is too bright to be a serious challange. Developers even removed high beam lights…like they knew you will not even make it to ride at night. Devs tried to make game more realistic with series of patches what was a good try. Navigation was made closer to reality, FOV adjustment was added, crashes were made more punishing. It was a good change towards more interesting experience, but sadly the development of improvements atopped and developers announced they will only add roadmap features some time in 2023. As I speak of navigation. It is also boring. In Dakar 18, player had to watch closely what danger was described in the notes. In DDR you can ignore everything apart from Danger 3 and direction notes. The positive side is Sport mode where you just race against other opponents validating waypoints. Unfortunately AI is so unbalanced that you never know if you will win or loose even if you make the stage without any error. Yet the physics make bike class extremely boring as you do not need to care about grip loss or maintaining traction.Multiplayer became dead quickly due to lack of interesting features and lobbies limited to 4 players. Some may argue that DDR is focused on single player experience , but even if, the multiplayer is as boring as single player.As a conclusion. Many people had high hopes for Dakar 18 sequel which will fix things that were bad in previous game and that requested features will be added. Developers however had their own vision and wanted to meet wider audience by creating game more like Forza Horizon. This was achieved by removing unique features and dumbed down physics. As a result we got a game boring and unrealistic. Even if player can choose from different levels of difficulty, physics still are the same - quite far from realistic. Wide variety of vehicles, big Saudi Arabia map or good graphics do not compensate lack of immersion and thrill of taking part in Dakar Rally.Buy the game on sale, it is not that bad to give negative review but also not worth recommending if you look for realism and entertaining title.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has had some updates and is now a GREAT game!  My review below was written before the updates which have fixed many of the game's issues.  The game really changes when you go from sport to professional and simulation modes.  It is more of the traditional rally experience but with the uniqueness of a rally raid which includes navigation.  It is a very unique experience and I am loving it.  I cannot wait  for future updates and DLC.This is a GOOD game, do not let all the negative reviews make your decision.  It DOES SUPPORT RACING WHEELS because it works with my G923 which WAS LISTED as a supported wheel from pre-release.   Those that were not listed will probably be patched in later, such as the Fanatec wheels.  ALSO you will need a good pc with a good graphics card to enjoy this game properly as it will glitch graphically if you use a lower end pc.   This is a sim-cade racer with lots of over the top action and excitement.  I love Dirt Rally 2.0 and Assetto Corsa Competizione and this game is not like those.  Those are simulations with realistic handling and physics while this game can be unrealistic and more arcade style.  However, this game is great at what it is.  It is a really fun game and I cant stop playing it lately.  It has some crazy action and the AI can be crazy but most of the time it just makes the race more intense.  Though I would like to see the AI tweaked to make it drive better and not get caught in big pile ups which can ruin a race.  The driving is exciting and all the vehicles handle differently with different physics and the driving is just plain fun.  The fact that it is not as demanding as a full simulation is what I expected and wanted.  If you are looking for a simulation this is NOT your game but if you are looking for an action packed sim-cade racer than this IS your game.  There are some rough edges that need to be patched so this game is not yet at its full potential and has a few issues here and there that hopefully get fixed in future patches.  Overall, it is a blast to play and is a very unique experience but keep in mind that it is not a simulation and there are some issues that need to be fixed.  However, none of them have been game breaking and this game will get better with time.  Which is exciting because this game has a lot of potential.

_childDocuments_.review: Crucially, and I don't know where this assumption has come from, this is NOT A SIMULATOR. Its made painfully evident from the fact this game has casual modes that it isn't aimed at the hardcore audience. It's comfortably a simcade title, nothing more nothing less.This game is a massive improvement on Dakar 18, which had the right formula, but was let down but every other aspect. Desert Rally is very enjoyable, and brings with it a nice difficulty curve in professional mode and beyond. Every vehicle feels different, and with 3 years of Dakar (plus retro) to choose from there's plenty of options. The stages are impressive and dynamic weather adds real challenge-especially severe storms where you can't see more than a few metres in front of you. Graphics are good, not seeing the same performance issues as others report, although there are minor glitches-in particular on cockpit displays which is easy to resolve. Damage model is also very in depth-something that is very important for an endurance off-road game. The crash physics can go a bit wild, had a few issues with the can-am doing loops and exponentially increasing the amount of damage sustained. It's a rare bug, and seems to just happen if you take a massive nosedive off a dune, but is a pain when you're mid stage. Roll over physics aren't too bad and happen at the right time, but they are quite dramatic and does add real consequence to being too confident behind the wheel. I'm not a fan of the sponsor wheel stuff (think super wheelspins in Horizon) as I'd rather progress into new vehicles using currency as opposed to luck, but I can overlook it considering you're by no means forced to keep them. The AI have already been noted by the developer as an area to be patched, so I won't bother repeating the same things others have mentioned.All in all, a very solid start point for a Dakar game, and its future looks positive. The bugs/glitches I've noted are all I've really seen in my 5 or so hours, which is pretty impressive considering the scale of this title.

_childDocuments_.review: I got Paris Dakar Rally as a kid. Which I kind of liked, but I can remember dreaming of a better Dakar Rally game, this is that game. I've reached level 20 and only played the professional mode, my honest review goes as follow: Dakar Dessert Rally is a racing game out of the ordinary. Don't go into this game expecting a great experience without knowing what the essence of Dakar Rally is. It's a hard game which forces you to work with your co-driver. You should be prepared for the frustration of getting lost, or not understanding where the hell your co-driver wants you to go. BUT when you get into the flow and start nailing the pace notes you'll feel like the king of the dessert, even if you get lost a couple of times. I must admit that there's some rough edges that needs to be polished, but so far it seems like a decent game with a respectable amount of fun. Looking forward to see how the game and title develops.I'd give the game a solid 7/10, after 8 hours that is.If you're looking for easy fun, no.If you're looking for a challenge, yes.
