_childDocuments_.review: Dakar Desert Rally (Dakar here on) is a successor to Dakar 18, and proves that developers, when given a proper budget, can put it to good use, when given the right IP to play with. Dakar is a rally game that lets' you compete in no less than FIVE different classes of vehicles: car, quad, motorcross, large truck, and buggy. Car, buggy, and truck have multi-men crew who will act as co-driver to give you verbal navigational pointers as per the roadbook. You do get icons on screen as prompt as well, if you have time to read them. The rally raid is not the same as rally in WRC or such. Instead, it is both a racing AND a navigation exercise. The roadbook contains all of the navigation instructions, such as follow road, or follow trace (path on ground), and when you get close enough to the nav point, you will get a notification that you've validated your waypoint, and can continue to the next one. If not... You clearly read the instructions wrong and have to reorient yourself! In sport mode (read: easy) there are "augmented reality" overlays to let you see the nav "beacon" but you don't get that in higher levels of difficulty. Keep in mind even if you know where the nav point is, you often cannot approach it directly due to valleys, rocks, hills, and such. While the game does let you drive offroad, let's just say, going 100+km and hit a rock will NOT do your vehicle any favors. And when you *can* approach it directly, you may NOT want to due to the need to turn for the next waypoint, or you need to climb a large hill and jump, and so on. The vehicles do behave quite differently. Buggies are relatively light, but with powerful engines they can accelerate very quickly, but they aren't very sturdy. Cars are sturdier, but obviously weigh more and less maneuverable. Trucks are ponderous and turning them at speed is a gamble. Quads don't really want to turn unless you slow down, while motorcross bikes are known for flying... if you land them right. Each event is composed of multiple stages, which involves driving through dozens of waypoints as described above, in various weather, that can range from sunny day to heavy fog, to snowstorm to heavy rain to sandstorm and more. The terrain varies from mountainous pass to sand dunes, from swampy land to desert towns, from plane wreckage to small bits of oasis, there are a LOT of variety in both terrain and weather. The three difficult levels also makes things interesting. Starters should use "sport" mode, which has all the vehicles starting together in a grid, with visible "beacons" for navpoints, and generally it should not be hard to win the overall race, even if you don't win individual stages. Professional mode removes most of the cheats, while the truly authenticity seekers will want to try the "simulation" mode. The career basically gives you enough starting money to buy one vehicle, and take it racing. As you race, you gain both XP (experience) and DP (Dakar points) which is currency to buy other vehicles. As you gain XP and "level up", you unlock additional rallies across the entire Arabian map. If you win or podium one of the rallies you get a chance to spin the "sponsorship wheel", which lets you choose among three "rewards", generally a fixed amount of DP, or 2 vehicles. However, to keep the vehicle, you need to win the specified race for that vehicle (it could be a multi-stage rally, or it could be as simple as the single-stage "Dakar Qualifier").  On the other hand, the vehicles *can* be rather expensive, as some of the past Dakar winners costs THOUSANDS of DPs, and you only win just over 100 DP per stage win (and less if you did not win!) The game lets you keep about 6 vehicles active (presumably, 1 vehicle per class, and 1 "new" vehicle you are trying out). Any additional vehicles can be moved to the warehouse, and moved back as needed. The game is also very friendly to you switching between classes. You can have each of the vehicles participating in a race, and it will say "in play" so you can go back in and resume the event. The vehicles *do* take damage in the race, esp. from collisions with objects or other vehicles (in sport mode)  and bad driving will result in high repair bills, or even "retired" (due to damage). And bad sportsmanship (intentionally crashing into other vehicles) will result in disqualification. And they do get dirtier as they race. You also have controls to lights, wipers, and so on (mainly for simulation). You will need to repair the vehicle in the bivouac area between events, as well as tune the vehicle to your driving style. The only thing I miss is a replay system, and according to the FAQ, it may be issued as a patch later. There are talks of certain vehicular rewards for certain races, but there is no detail on how that's done. I suspect its for winning or podium in all five classes of vehicles. Graphics are gorgeous as this is powered by Unreal Engine, and I have an RTX, so graphics are great at 1080p. Sound is also quite good, even if it's just stereo headphones. There is a bit of stability issue though, but it could be due to my system. I had to quit the game after running 2 stages, and sometimes exiting the game after that results in an UE4 error (no big deal). However, I've also experience weird freezes, like during the event startup, or right as I ended the race (!!!). I recommend race only 2 stages at most, then quit the game, reboot, and get back in, so you ahve a smooth experience. There are, of course, additional modes such as free roam, and the addition of Snowrunner vehicles into the game was a bit of fun. There are more DLCs coming (and you will get them if you bought the season pass). All in all, Dakar is a good improvement over its predecessor, in terms of both graphics and handling. While it's questionable how many vehicles will you try and how many races can you do, before you get bored, it is certain a LOT of variety.

_childDocuments_.review: A huge step up from Dakar 18, driving and physics feels great when going straight/light turns or doing jumps, but it's still  got ways to go when compared to the likes of WRC or Dirt Rally. All vehicle classes feel very prone to snap oversteer, the quads being particularly bad. The feeling of weight and momentum during turns/slides it's still not quite there.However, this game does a lot of things that no other games do. Doing a 20 minute stage with only your road book to guide you is an immensly rewarding experience and is where this game shines. Just you and the desert(and the copilot that a lot of times is more of a hindrance than help). Another great feature is the damage model and repair mechanics during stages, combined with the long stages and an AI that also makes a lot of mistakes it really incentivizes you to repair the car and not just restart the stage, because the win on the event will still be very much possible.The more arcade sport mode can be fun in short bursts but because in this this mode all your focus goes to the driving instead of the navigation the driving physics shortcomings just become more frustating, I would find it hard to recommend this game if this mode is all you're interested in.Some WTFs that they need to patch:-Level 25 to unlock simulation mode: it was one of the modes that I was more interested in and 12 hours in and I still can't play it. apparently it can take over 20h........-Only sport mode has rewards cars... there's nothing to unlock in professional mode...-U need play same event with ALL 5 classes to unlock said cars : not only are u forcing me to play Sport Mode, u're forcing to play each event FIVE TIMES, one of those times with THE QUADS...- You're disqualified of an event if u finish lower than P8 in a stage....... just why? goes against the concept of an endurance race, incentivizes the restart of a stage on every small mistake instead of engaging with the great repair mechanics you've implemented...In conclusion, i have a lot of problems with the game. But there are no other games like it. So yeah, hope they can give this one the final polish it deserves in the coming months.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is unplayable in the more realistic modes. _childDocuments_.review: Fun game, a few issues that hopefully will get patched but if you are a fan of Dakar and rally raid navigation its well worth it in my opinion.Running mostly 60FPS on max settings with Auto DLSS (RTX2080, i9 7th gen). Only drops slightly to low 50's when a lot of vehicles in front and a lot of particles on screen, but for me its running quite well for the most part.A few tips:1 if you go for Professional mode (Sport can be fun but the value for me its in Professional and Simulation) you have to keep referencing\looking at the Roadbook yourself, do not rely solely on the navigator call outs or you will get lost very often. 2 White roadbook notes that are not "validateable" Waypoints do not progress on their own on your roadbook, you have to do it manually as you pass them (the game does not tell you this which can lead to a lot of confusion). On a controller its the right bumper to move it forward, left for backward.3 Learn your roadbook symbols! These can help you a lot when navigating. For example HP = offroad, which means follow a specific Cap in as straight a line as possible, P = Follow Road, CX = Rocks, etc.4 When on P (road), PP (main road) or Follow Traces (lines in dirt\sand\soil), the CAP is a reference point taken at the intersection, so mostly useless. When following any track you have to reference the Tulip picture to see if there are intersections and which path to take. By keeping a close look at the roadbook tulip and symbols you can see when going from following track to offroad (HP) Cap headings5 Go slow at first if you are just getting used to navigating using the roadbook. Once you get used to it you can speed things up. Its pretty fun once you get used to it!Edit after patch 1.04:Now white roadbook notes also advance automatically (tip 2) as long as you go through the radius so you no longer have to worry about doing it manually unless you go through a different route or stray too far from the route path

_childDocuments_.review: Game is very fun. Realistic, pretty, challenging. List is subject to change.However, there are many glaring issues:No PS Button guides. Support, no guide. -Game is incredibly difficult to control on M&KBefore races start, you have to press square (x) to edit your settings, which is weird, given that the OPTIONS button isn't used for anything else there.Driver's head occasionally bugs into frame in first person.Jittering in race starts, cars stopping awkwardly, objects freezing.Cannot test drive owned vehicles straight from the garage, you have to go into the catalog first, which causes some vehicles to be impossible to test drive as not all are in the catalog.The Race Title sequence is a tad long, and unskippable. An alternative race start scene before the start line, like you're already in the vehicle, just waiting on the countdown, would be neat.On night maps, the exposure will lowers when a vehicle with its lights on is directly behind you, making it difficult to see where you're going.Quality of Life:In Free Roam, the ability to view the map instead of just the mini map would be nice.The ability to honk your horn.Repositioning in Free Roam should get some more polishing.While finding treasures is good motivation for playing free roam, there should be some other activities to flesh it out a bit more.You should be able to go straight into races by driving to their locations on the map, driving to them should let you select if you want to race, or to hide race markers, or similar. Their icons should appear on the minimap.8/10 Really good, needs improvement.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Almost perfect Dakar/Off-road game, needs WAY much more polishing and fixingI played this game using Logitech G29 and I literally spent more than an hour to make it barely playable. Steering wheel controls are horrible in default. 5% deadzone as default? WHY?!?. This is the first time I'm seeing default deadzone setting, and considering you can't turn steering wheel more than -40°/40°, 5% makes a massive difference over 900°. Default force feedback is extremely sharp, making you almost lose control in every jump. After fixing and tinkering around controls, the gameplay is almost perfect with minor problems with realicity of AI. They race like veterans, taking every turn flawless and following WP's without missing any of them. Also motorcycle AI is suicidal, they need therapy. They absolutely love jumping in front of trucks going +150 km/h. Handling is realistic, car performance is almost on par, and co-pilot is actually very helpful. There are not many bugs, excluding graphical ones. Some textures in vehicles have z-fighting. Snowy stages are impossible to navigate due to foliage rendering glitches. If Steam had neutral review, I would give that but currently it is not worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: Refunded very shortly after original launch day due to wheel setup issues. Patch in April featured the notes... "Improved Steering Wheel Wizard’s compatibility for brands without official support."... and I can confirm it's true.  Simucube OSW base, Bodnar based buttons on my wheel, Bodnar based pedal set, Thrustmaster TH8A in analong hand brake mode... it's all working, and it all feels really good.  I'm really enjoying this now.Co-driver in professional mode could be better, find the call outs too late (no option to adjust)... but if you use him as an assistant and check-in a little more on the visual road book you can do just fine navigating. Also thank you for getting rid of the "must finish top half" requirement in pro mode stages; now finish the stage and move on, how it should had been day one. And sport mode and free roam modes are really nice for a slightly more casual experience, even though AI can be bit chaotic and unpredictable.It's too bad it took 7 months after release (9 months for me to rebuy it, on sale of course), but I'm really glad I gave this a second chance... but I think it'll be a hard recovery for the devs after the rocky start, but I appreciate any future updates and may consider buying DLC too.

_childDocuments_.review: Another potentially good racing game ruined by Unreal Engine 4 physics. 4WD vehicles snap oversteer like an old Porsche driving on wet roads, grazing the edge of a small gently sloped rock is the same as smacking into a giant concrete cube, vehicles will rotate 90 degrees onto their side in midair if you take a jump even slightly off. I get that there's always some measure of unpredictability when offroad racing, but I have no confidence that any of the vehicles on offer will behave consistently from one moment to the next simply because UE4 has never been that good for racing games in general, let alone ones that take place away from paved surfaces.More my own fault for not doing the research beforehand to see what game engine this was using, I guess.

_childDocuments_.review: It seems like this game doesn't know what it wants to be.Simulation mode is locked from the start, you can't play it until you level 25. I reached lvl 8 in 1.7 hrs.From the start you can play "Sport" mode or "Pro" mode. In short words, "Sport" mode is arcade mode with bots and navigational arrows (NFS, Forza-like). "Pro" is a race with time, where you need to navigate the road, but your co-pilot will help you to do it.So, the problem here - why learn to navigate the desert, when you can play "sport" mode, learn the tracks, and then drive "pro" and "sim" by memory? I thought tracks will be randomized, so that you will have to find your way through the desert on your own each time. Pointless.Driving physics and controls are ok, but it's too arcady for me. Cars can't stuck in the sand, they ride all types of terrain in the same way, maybe a little slower. Boring.And the sad point here, it is not a competitive game. You compete against bots. Not real players. I thought we will have seasons for specific race zones, and you will have to compete with time of other players.In the end, I can't imagine why I should want to play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I have Played for over 5 Hours now -  From Career to PVP Here's what i got so far.In Career you will most likely start with a quad or a Bike because of DP points (money) that you need to buy vehicles from. And the Bikes are pretty crap..  They over steer so quickly and you end up becoming last in the race. Yes you can adjust the tyre pressure and yes it helps a little but not enough. So if you LOVE bikes Like i do - Forget it its crap  ( i currently ride CRF450 and a Kawasaki Z900 )The bikes are supposed to be able to go over some obstacles right? -  Nope, you hit the slightest rock and you crash and then sometimes you hit a wall and the bikes goes over. I get the feeling whoever made this game have no idea how bikes work.and to Top it off , no matter what bike you have in the game even if its the fastest one you will always lose 2-4 spots once the race begins. The rolling starts are Crap and your bike will never be as fast as the other bikes in career mode. My second biggest issue is the A.I. In career mode they will drive behind you and literally hit you like they dont see or care. Yes they drive straight at you and if this was CARMAGHEDDON it would have been fun but its not. Its suppose to be realistic, its the Dakar.Then once you have enough DP points (money) to buy a better vehicle / truck its gets slightly better.  The open world map that they bragged about isn't really open world as you still have to meet waypoints every few Miles/Kilos so that's null and void.Then there's online PVP.Once you start doing this it also gets slightly better , no more A.I. trying to kill you and you end up losing cause of them. But now you race against players. Who so far cant even find some of the waypoints and you end up spectating more than racing because there is no minimap. I even had to watch a player drive in second gear for halve the track because they didnt know how to fix / repair their car. And if that sounds funny waiting for other players to finish so you can carry on and collect your points for 15 minutes isnt Fun. Getting lost or missing a waypoint is real!Whats nice about the game?The tracks are really beautiful and i love how you can spectate as a helicopter once you finished in PVP mode waiting for the other players to finish. (the Helicopter needs a little camera handling adjustment though but not to bad)Its really not a easy game and it will put most players off. They will probabbly end up playing need for speed.So why the thumbs up?  Well im hoping they would fix the crappy A.I. and Bike handling as well as the rolling starts and that players will learn or get used to the PVP and not quit the game half way though. Once that happens this could be a great game. And even though the rolling starts are crap, the bikes are crap, the few races i did win with my Truck did feel pretty nice and i did enjoy it.  Regards - Solo Zero Gaming

_childDocuments_.review: Finally a game that does the Dakar justice!! If you have any interest in the Dakar Rally, you'll like this game!I am really enjoying this game so far! It is definitely the best Dakar simulation I have come across. I had Dakar 2018 and could never really get into it, but this is much better and I hope will continue to improve further! The detail of the map is unbelievable! Graphics are pretty good! There is some stuttering here and there that I have noticed, but it doesn't affect gameplay too much. Definitely feel like I am in the middle of nowhere in Saudi Arabia!I am a diehard sim racer and like my driving experience to be as real as possible. I am using a Fanatec Podium series wheelbase in compatibility mode (i heard Fanatec support is coming to the game soon) and it feels pretty decent. I keep dialing in the FFB settings every time I play and they are feeling pretty good. Have not tried the bikes or quads yet as a wheel is not really suitable for them. Overall I would call the physics simcade (Don't expect Dirt Rally 2.0), but still enjoyable to someone who likes things as real as possible in racing sims. The damage model is very cool!! Love the shedding body panels and broken windscreens! I do wish the vehicles took damage a bit easier though! I mean you can jump off a massive sand dune and fall hundreds of feet and the car is fine. Only rollovers and really massive shunts cause big damage. Little too on the arcade side for me there and it takes away some of the finesse and the challenge of choosing the correct line over an obstacle that the real Dakar drivers experience.The challenge of navigating is very fun! I think it is great that there is 3 levels of difficulty! I have learned a lot about the Dakar roadbook and the GPS system that will help me understand it better when I watch the real race on TV. The co-driver can use some improvements I feel. He usually warns you about danger as you hit it and by then it is too late. Same thing with turns in the road. Usually the call to "turn left" comes as you cross the intersection. I wish there was a way to adjust how early or late the calls are as in other rally titles. Wish the English co-driver had a bit less annoying voice. It isn't terrible, but he kind of sounds like a 12 year old kid sometimes. The co-driver I use in Dirt Rally 2.0 kind of reminds me of Brian Johnson from AC/DC. That's the voice I want guiding me through Dakar!! But if you rely on the roadbook and use the co-driver passively, it works well enough.As for the vehicle selection, it is awesome! Just about every vehicle from the past 3 Dakar's is in here! Plus the historic pack DLC includes tons of Dakar legends of the past. I do wish i didn't have to win the same race 5 times (once in each vehicle class) in order to unlock them though. That's frustrating especially if you dont have a gamepad handy for the bikes. But overall I'm happy.Graphics: 8/10Handling/Physics: 8/10Sounds: 9/10Realism: 7/10Vehicle Selection: 10/10Atmosphere: 9/10Co-driver: 3/10Overall: 8.5/10 and hopefully only getting better!

_childDocuments_.review: The short version, absolutely brilliant game with stunning graphics, amazing attention to detail and incredible sound mixing. -a must haveThis game is lots of fun to play, easy to setup and get into races whether your using a wheel or controller.  The Sabre team have surpassed what i expected this game to be by a long shot... the physics are a very good mix of sim and arcade.  A lot of people wouldn't last 2 seconds driving in these conditions with full simulation physics, so i'm glad they chose the path they chose.Visually this game has to be the best usage of the Unreal 4 engine that i've seen.. its a game where the more you look, the more you see, like how the motors in each vehicle are all different, and actually mounted like real motors, notable by the way they move under acceleration and deceleration.The FFB is detailed enough to give you a good sense of the harsh bumps, vibrations etc you'd expect on these tracks and trails, with plenty of options to fine tune it to your liking.The map size, MASSIVE... Course designs are very well done with a great flow and mix of terrians, tight stuff and long flowing.The AI can use a little work, but the devs have already stated thats going to happen in the next patch for the game, so thats not a concern at all.Honestly, this game blows Dakar 18 (not the same devs) out of the water.. far more fun to play, better looking and more likely to keep your attention.The roadmap for this game is also packed with huge amounts of content coming in the future, that being said, i personally recommend getting the Deluxe edition so you get it all at the best price.8/10 for me and im pretty picky.. Ignore the nonsense reviews on here giving thumbs down with fake reasons for it, this game is fantastic and very much worth your time, effort and hard earned cash.you can watch the full stream review here

_childDocuments_.review: So where to begin?  The review is a positive one because of the overall concept and the clear roadmap the developers have in place to add some of the advertised features that are missing at the moment.  It's a little disappointing to not be able to use my steering wheel as yet, but it's a minor inconvenience.Starting with the gripes on things that are conscious decisions by the developers rather than simply things we don't have yet, having to reach level 25 to unlock the hardcore sim mode is a pain.  That's what I bought the game for, and now I need to grind through game modes that don't interest me in order to get to it.While I appreciate the effort that went into the dynamic weather, I can't think of a world region that requires it less than the Middle East.  It's dry and dusty all the time, why am I always driving through thunderstorms and rain?The navigator needs some work.  It's often not clear what exactly you should be doing, leaving you to assume much of the time.  Normally I get through this OK, but a recent night stage (again why?) I ended up getting lost four times then DQd at a time control.  I'm still not sure precisely why.  I was able to get around pretty well in Dakar 18.I haven't come even remotely close to getting stuck yet.  This is a common occurrence in the real Dakar, I hope the simulation mode, once unlocked, is more realistic.  I also haven't seen anything to suggest you can exit your car, dig yourself out or assist competitors either which will be disappointing if it's absent from the game.  The trailers also suggested the player would encounter other classes out on the stage, have never seen anything other than my own class.Now onto the good stuff.  The physics, as far as I can tell through my controller, feel pretty good.  The open world will be brilliant once it's properly implemented.  The vehicle choice is great.  The graphics and sounds are awesome.  The fundamentals are all there, it just needs a little tidying up.One feature I would like to see is regarding the classic content.  Rather than sending Vatanen's 405 in there with Sainz and Al Attiyah, give us the real classic category they run today.  Regularity/navigation style, speed doesn't matter.  Would be cool to have that option which would almost be another game mode.It's pretty on the fence review I'll admit, but the test is am I enjoying it?  I am.  So it gets the thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: I think it's pretty fun so far. It definitely needs more polish but I can see the potential. The AI is really aggressive in a mostly good way. It's really cool to come around a corner and see an overturned rally truck and have to dodge it. The graphics are pretty good and it runs mostly well for me, I've had a few lag spikes so far that basically make me have to restart the race.The AI can also be pretty frustrating with their aggression, sometimes they'll gun right for you and cause you to crash. Which is fine, it's a trade off that I'll deal with in order to see them crash on their own like I do sometimes. The only problem I have is restarting the races. It could just be my own impatience, but I hate that I have to go to the leaderboard again, then go through the intro cutscene/wait until the skip button works, then I can restart the race. With the amount of times I've crashed due to overly aggressive AI right at the beginning of the race makes me wish that this process was faster.Overall I like the physics so far and it's incredibly scary to be riding my motorcycle and then catch up to the rally trucks. The dust is realistic and makes it hard to see, combined with the weather it makes it pretty enjoyably intense. The navigation is also pretty cool once you get used to reading it.I'm excited to see what they do when it's a finished product and it's fully polished. I hope that I can do the full Dakar in the future rather than various rallies. There are a lot of negative reviews surrounding direct drive wheels, I don't use one. I prefer arcade racers and found this to be pretty satisfying using a controller. I also have a wheel so I understand others frustration but to those that don't have one, the game is still plenty fun and playable.

_childDocuments_.review: I figured that 6 months after release this game would have ironed out whatever made it have mixed reviews. I was VERY wrong. The handling is likely the worst I've ever experienced. It truly feels like trying to ice skate in clown shoes with a cake on your head. Though that would likely be more enjoyable.The AI is playing a different genre of game entirely and are on a mission to make each race into a demolition derby, when in proximity to you they will more often then not attempt to ram you with their vehicle.Adding insult to injury the call outs are downright obnoxious, they sound as though each line is being read off by a free text to voice reader and there is very little to no reprieve from its monotony. If you're looking for a fun car game, I suggest you look literally anywhere else.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a lot of problems. The game was also according to the roadmap at release far from ready, a pity for the stressed release. You should have done better!What bothers me the most are the following things:- Keyboard control is a disaster! Feels like every click on the key has a 5000% impact.- Unlocking the Dakar Rally, I bought a Dakar Game, I wanted to play the Dakar, i can't! Why you want to educate me here is beyond me. We are in 2022, unlocks just do not fit anymore. To play the Dakar it takes many hours to unlock it. Too bad- No context, no depth. You just drive stage by stage and get to the finish after that the race is over, finished. I don't need a story either, but a little more depth wouldn't hurt, that's completely missing here.- Multiplayer doesn't give XP or Credits. I played most of the time only online with a colleague. That was all for nothing, as I unlocked nothing, no rallies, no credits, no XP really nothing. If you're going to make the leveling game important and deprive people of content, at least do it right. The game in the public lobby is as good as dead- Multiplayer Rally, in the service zone no damage to the vehicle can be repaired, although the vehicle can break down during the stage and this can/must be repaired in each case only in the stage. Also there are no tables or stage information visible in the service zone. Also you can't see how many stages you have to drive etc. No possibility to save the game etc. This again hurts the depth of the game. Also online it is no more than driving and that's it.- Landscape design, I must admit I have never been to the Saudi desert, however the tracks look very scripted and in my opinion seem quite arcade heavy in very many places. The driving between the canyons etc. Also it feels very repetitive even if you drive a different rally.As I said the game feels quite unemotional and doesn't really have a long term effect for me. Too bad about that. It would have been much more doable.If you are wondering if you should buy the game now, I recommend you wait and get it in the sale. It's not worth the money. Maybe at a later time. Let's see.

_childDocuments_.review: I was already pissed off the first time I opened the game.  I had just spent 42 dollars buying the deluxe edition, only to find out It doesnt even come with the new audi e tron dlc pack that was locked away behind a pre order bonus.  So regardless of how much money you pay, you're not getting the complete game.  Its a really crappy feeling to just spend extra money on a season pass, and find out you are STILL missing content,  that they are punishing you for not pre buying the game and waiting for a slight discount or reviews.  If they want to offer an extra dlc goodie for pre orders I dont care,  but like with mortal kombat X they should GIVE YOU THE ABILITY TO BUY IT, and include it with the 30 freaking dollar season pass!  Not just lock it away to oblivion.  (Edit) Oh boy they finally remembered about the pack and made it available to download after 2 years of locking it away, that just changes everything 10/10 game of the year 2069!1!1!!  Now for the reason I'm refunding,  the game is BROKEN!  It crashed on me multiple times during start up, and the tutorial.  Half the time when I click play the launcher begins, it shows dakar in my task manager.. yet it just never opens.  When I do finally get the game to freaking open and run, it stutters and lags like crazy while constantly dropping below 20fps.  I am well within recommended specs,  I by no means have a nasa rich boi computer, but its got an rtx 2070 max Q, i7 10750, and 16gb of ram.  My computer runs games like assetto corsa competizioine, total war warhammer 3, and elden ring at mostly ultra settings 60fps, maybe bump msaa down to 4x just to keep the laptop from getting too hot.  I had hoped the games patch 1.4 fixed the performance issues so I decided to buy the game.  I REALLY want to support these devs,  I want them to succeed!  I love off road racing games, and am desperate for a rally raid/multi class off road racing game that is good!  But this game is basically unplayable in its current state.  There is nothing more frustrating than crashing into a boulder and ruining a race due to a stutter that threw you off balance mid corner, its so damn distracting.  I tried lowering every setting in the game to its lowest possible, to where it basically looked like a ps2 game.  And it STILL stuttered constantly and couldnt keep a half steady frame rate.  Something is severely wrong with either the engine, or the optimization of this game.  Even if all this was fixed, the core gameplay and driving mechanics feels horrible.  The cars all have a tendancy to snap oversteer and spin around, like your gliding on ice with no traction.  There is no "feel" to the driving, Even just driving straight on an open road, the slightest turn will cause the car to flip around.  The motorcycles on the other hand feel sluggish and not maneuverable or agile at all, almost like the steering fork is broken and jammed to only allow 5 degrees of rotation or something.  It just feels horrible to drive.  The trucks felt.. ok i guess, no real complaints, at least they didnt pit maneuver themselves constantly like the cars/buggies.    In summary it pains me to write this review,  I really wanted to like this game and was super excited at the concept.  However if the game is fundamentally broken then that is unacceptable.  I'll be refunding the game, and would recommend ANY of you, regardless of whatever sale prices this game drops to in the future, make SURE they patched out these bugs/glitches and performance issues.  I would be refunding this game even if I payed 10 dollars for it, but for 40 bucks this is straight up egregious.  It's disgusting how broken this game is, yet they still have no problem selling it out to people.  I'm getting my money back and buying a game like spider man remastered or ghostwire tokyo.

_childDocuments_.review: It is terribly difficult to write a review for this. It's unfinished. It's bugged. It's unpolished. The physics are nothing special, the optimization is horrible, the codriver sometimes gets so lost you basically have to look at the roadbook yourself all the time. The difficulty scaling is odd etc. And yet... heavens, this is a unique experience. Just did a stage that lasted 50 minutes (without getting lost). The navigation is truly a great challenge, unlike any racing game I've ever experienced. It's so satisfying when you get it right. So difficult and yet so rewarding. The stages are extremely long and yet they never get boring. When I had a 10 minute stage in a regular rally game like Dirt 2.0 or RBR, I'd get bored. Here, after a stage lasting 40-50 minutes I want to do more! So I am going to make an assumption. I will give this a recommendation hoping that they will fix the bugs. If they don't I will change the review to not recommend it. Be warned this game is unfinished, but amazing.EDIT Instead of fixing bugs, they added a patch that created more bugs - now in the garage the game lags like crazy. Plus you can now more frequently catch up vehicles on a stage. Which would be a good thing if it wasn't so totally random. How the hell am I catching trucks with my bike, if trucks start the stages AFTER the bikes!? So yeah, with a heavy heart, I'm changing my review to a negative oneEDIT2 They fixed the garage lag in the next patch so that's a plus

_childDocuments_.review: I was waiting to review this game until after I had unlocked simulation mode, so that I could review it based on everything it had to offer rather than my initial impressions. I am unsure why certain members of the community are comparing this game to the likes of Assetto Corsa or other similar simracing games, as it sits much closer to Forza than it does Euro-truck sim.I recommend this game. I've been having a lot of fun with it once I figured out the niche which it occupies and changed my approach to suit. The game is about racing and driving fast, yes, but the navigational aspect of it is also a massive part of the experience. I think it's wrong to review simply the driving physics, or AI racing in isolation because it's not a traditional racer in that sense.The three different game modes are quite separated, although professional and simulation are closer to each other in terms of their offering. Sport mode is the easiest option, which feels very much like it's been included to cater to the casual or younger player, where you drive between big highlighted way points side by side with your opponents. I had a bit of fun with this, but it is quite easy in honestly, especially as you can bee-line to the next way point and ignore the terrain features.Professional mode is where I think the game is at its best. Traditional rally time trial where your start is staggered so you don't have to race wheel to wheel, there is no visible way point markers and you must find your way between way points using the navigational tools you are given, whilst driving quickly and not crashing. Stages are between 10-15 minutes, and you need to navigate and drive carefully to not lose lots of time on repairs and retracing your steps. Simulation mode really extends the stage length, and stages can take upwards of 40 minutes to complete. While this is a fun challenge, it can be quite a time commitment to a single stage of 40 continuous minutes of driving if that isn't your thing.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: All the issues below have been addressed. It is a shame they did not just postpone launch by a month, as a lot of bad reviews could have been avoided that way.This game has a lot of potential. Unfortunately potential is not really playable. It was already delayed, and I think it would have been wise to delay the release again, as currently my Fanatec CSW 2.5 does not work (even though it used to say on the website that Fanatec was supported - that has since changed to "Coming soon"), and even worse, it does not allow mapping my steering axis to the actual steering in-game. And no, not being supported and straight up not working are two different things - plenty of games from before this wheel was released, like rFactor, work fine. Luckily the steering axis problem can be resolved by manually editing the game's steering wheel configuration JSON files. FFB still does not work though, but surely that will be fixed at some point. Once you spent the hours to get the game to work, it is time to play. For a game that also aims to be a simulator (or at least simcade), some odd choices were made. Most notably:- Simulation mode unlocks at level 25- In order to progress from a stage you need to finish at least 8th- Stages require a certain level to unlockI can somewhat understand this for a career mode, but this also affects the game in online mode, and a "quick play" mode is not available yet. Whereas in Dakar 18 you could start any stage with any vehicle from the get-go, here that is all locked away. I have not come across many simulators (Assetto Corsa, rFactor, Raceroom, even Project CARS 2, etc.) where this is the case.

_childDocuments_.review: I was long waiting for this update of Dakar Desert rally, until this day.So far I will share my experience with you:These are my current hardware:Fanatec Clubsport CSW V2.5Heusinkveld Sprint PedalsHuesinkveld Sequential ShifterHeusinkveld HandbrakeBased on this combo, it has been really a huge hassle for me to map all the buttons for a single working configuration, even after the new Wheel configuration wizard it did not work properly.Changing the inverted axis does not work consistently.The pedal and steering wheel are mapped as one with continuous input from pedals making driving impossible.My experience in the game so far has been based on keyboard or gamepad, which is far from ideal for someone passionate about Dakar Rally racing.There is a lot of work needs to be done regarding hardware mapping in the game, and at this stage I think it is a major priority before releasing any new content or DLC.If you have any of these combination of hardware above, I do not recommend buying the game in its current state until further updates are made to solve this major issue.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge Dakar and offroad racing fan, so when I saw this game, I was excited. My buddy and I bought it together with the intention of sort of racing the Dakar against eachother. And while the graphics and terrain look pretty good, the driving physics are awful. Even the most minute sterring input while driving, turns your multi-million dollar dessert race machine into a drift car, sending you careening off into the rocks in a hopeless spin. Its really bad and not fun. And if a racing games racing is no good, then neither is the game, in my opinion. Fortunately, we were both able to get refunds.

_childDocuments_.review: Dakar Desert Rally feels like a proper game release now.While it still doesn't run great, the huge stutters seem to be gone and driving the vehicles on a gamepad has greatly improved.I hope Saber keeps improving the game's optimization and, personally, I also hope they allow for even faster steering response in the next updates since it's still a bit on the slow side.On the topic of controls, the countersteering has improved on all vehicles, but it can still be a bit unreliable at points, likely due to it still being a touch slow.Otherwise the driving feels absolutely stellar. The grip makes sense, even if a bit high, the vehicles react well to jumps, you can feel the weight shift, and in general the bikes feel like bikes and the cars and trucks feel like cars and trucks.All in all, it's an amazing offroading experience with a huge playground to mess around in.The issues with wheel support have been fixed too, I can plug in my wheel and configure it without any trouble now.Some weird design choices are still there. When playing on the Sport mode that allows you to play the game like Sega Rally, when a vehicle gets ahead of you it's impossible to see due to the dust.If the point of the Sport mode is to make the game more accessible to a more casual audience, you should be able to see better when behind another vehicle in this mode, like in other arcade rally games.You can now start a quick race without going through the online lobby system, like any other game.Pick a vehicle, pick a location, and just have fun.They've also added the ability to pause the game midrace (because it's not online anymore) and it's possible to skip a part of the race start sequence.Sadly it's still an AI that launches your vehicle, you cannot rev it up yourself and launch it the way you want. This goes for all of the 3 difficulty modes. and it's nice to see that Saber cared and even after the tons of negative (and many times not constructive) criticism they delivered something great.While the game still isn't perfect, if this patch is a sign of things to come, for me this game will go down in history as one of the best racing games from this generation that makes the garbage AAA studios are putting out look even worse.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this one. And part of me still does, deep down. Somebody tried very hard to make this a fun experience, there's a huge amount of content here and a lot of it is surprisingly polished. But a racing game lives or dies by its racing, and that's the one place Dakar Desert Rally falls down. I don't hate it, but in a crowded off-road arcade racer market it wouldn't be the game I recommend. DDR's steering physics are perplexing. I'm unsure whether by bug or feature, but the gamepad steering is really heavy but also really vague. I was able to find a comfy place by adjusting sense and linearity, but it was still sluggish. The cornering physics are just weird, if the rear steps out my steering inputs had no effect. It was like... I don't know. I was taught to catch a sliding car by gently applying the brakes and counter-steering. And that the last thing you want to do is release the throttle as this shifts the weight forward and unloads the rear axle. Around you go. That latter scenario is what slides in DDR feel like, and I couldn't for the life of me find a way to counteract that. I played with gamepad settings and tried different techniques for an hour, nada. And that for me, unfortunately, is gamebreaking. It feels like a bug rather than a feature so I think I'll wait 6 months and come back.

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics are very good as is the sound. The AI can be frustrating when AI opponents purposely runs into you like a missile but the AI makes normal mistakes as well. I've read reviews that the game doesn't support 32 X 9 and it doesn't. It stretches the picture like many games and DLSS also does work with 32 X 9 monitors but that's not an issue with the game but the technology. I can run all settings on EPIC at 2560 X 1440 ( stretched to 5120 X 1440 ) and keep a frame rate above 60 with my desktop RYZEN 3800x & NVIDIA RTX2080 TI and 32 gigs of RAM. 0n my laptop with a RYZEN 9 5940 and NVIDIA RTX 3070 and 8 gigs of RAM at 2560 X 1440 at the same settings frame rate will occasionally drop to about 58 but mostly stay above 60. With DLSS the laptop stays above 75 FPS.Some people complain about the handling, that the cars feel like driving on greasy roads. I'm a big fan of sim racing ( RACEROOM ), I personally think the vehicle handling is pretty good. Remember your on dirt, rocks, sand, ice, snow, if you can't handle the vehicle your driving your probably driving to fast, slower is sometimes faster. That was my number 1 issue in the first few hours, driving too fast too often, not letting off the gas when the car takes to the air or getting too much air because I was going to fast.The game to me feels more simulation than arcade like Dirt Rally 2 (sim) Vs V-Rally 4 (arcade). Dirt Rally requires you to drive more like you would in the real world and V-Rally is much easier to jump in and just play and drive recklessly and get away with it unlike the real world.I've played with an XBOX One controller and a Thrustmaster TS-PC wheel and pedal, both work great for me. The game is far from perfect but if you put the time in and learn to drive with patience you'll find yourself competitive at least and enjoying the game rather than being frustrated by it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a bit... came back to see if things changed.First race my car didn't move during the "start cut scene" so I got rear ended... why is there a cut scene for a rolling start?FPS bounces between 60fps and 30fps out of no where.I braked to make a sharp left, AI doesn't lift and just wipes me out into a rock.I came over a jump and there was a truck sitting there, rear ended it... no idea why it wasn't moving on the other side of a blind jump... our cars got stuck together. It started moving though but I was basically a trailer for 10 seconds... finally break free, we both make a right into a canyon... truck spazs out and slams into a rock and rolls even though I had backed off because I didn't want to get stuck again.Game is still terrible. Uninstalling I'll be back in a year.I’m leaving my original review below because I think it shows my emotional descent with this game.This is one of the worst racing games of all time. It has good graphics and the pleasure of being one of the few off road racing games that exist. The progression system isn’t bad. After that everything about the actual races falls apart.The AI is terrible. Comically terrible. They will run you off the road, slam into a rock and cause a 5 car pile up, randomly brake, randomly accelerate past you on an uphill.The controls are terrible. You can check reddit, people are throwing together guides on how to make vehicles “drivable” but if you have to custom modify the race suspension just to make it drivable that is a bad design. There is no counter steering, you can not slide a vehicle. The e brake is a death sentence and will just cause you to spin like a top. There is no steering wheel support at this time, don’t let people tell you otherwise they got it “kind of working” that isn’t functional.The game stutters and you lose control of the vehicle while it stutters. On more than one occasion the game stuttered and I ended up in a rock. Look below for my PC specs, I don’t feel like I should be stuttering.This is like every other low budget developer that got a hold of the Unreal Engine. They dumped all their money and time into making a good looking world and never considered someone may want to actually play a game in it. If I could return this steaming pile I would.Bleh. Where to start.I have a i9-9900k with a 3080ti and 32GB RAM with it installed on a SSD.The first time I play through a section it stutters, almost like the level is still loading while playing. The second time I replayed the same level no stuttering. It is something you can work around but it is really jaring.Okay... so I have a G920 and getting the settings functional has been... well stupid. You either have a very loose steering wheel or it jitters the whole time. At this point I would caution anyone from buying the game, that being said I'm not returning it. I'll spend more time tweeking my settings and worse case I can play with a controller.UPDATE:I'm not returning the game against better judgment. As of this posting do not bother with a steering wheel. The Dev's say a fix is coming but we'll see if they'll patch at the rate Monster Hunter World did (fixed all major issues in 2 weeks) or at the rate of CP2077 (which took a year?).On to controller with ATVs. I'm pretty sure the dev's have never ridden an ATV in the desert before. I did enduro racing on ATV, they are not nearly as squirrely as this game leads you to think. Any little bump, rock, whoop, and the ATV spins around like a top. The AI is terrible... like broken terrible. The AI come in two types.Type 1: Drives fast and perfect, good luck catching them.Type 2: (Ironically the worst of the two) Drives like a kamikaze, super fast then wrecks, or wrecks into you. You pass them because they wrecked, they take off again super fast then plow into you from behind, rinse and repeat. Once in awhile you'll manage to avoid them only for the AI to brake check you as soon as they pass you.There isn't a lot of off road racing games out there. Unless you are a die hard Dakar want to play a racing game I would pass, anyone on the "fence" will hate this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Just buy Dakar 18 instead.  Most of the issues this game has aren't a problem in that one, and the stages are more fun too IMO.Buggy, unstable, wheel support is hilariously bad, strange use of speed limits but without the real world's speed limiters (you have to constantly watch your speed, that's NOT realistic for Dakar), co-driver is a mess, easy and pro difficulties are a joke because you can't even run Dakar until you unlock sim difficulty, bike handling is hilariously bad (ever spun out like a car while on a bike before? yeah, me neither), and framerate absolutely tanks in many places where it just shouldn't. _childDocuments_.review: It was released quite suddenly as a diamond in the rough. But the core gameplay is very solid, it captures the Dakar endurance experience like no other game building massively on the earlier installment and most of the hickups (like buggy steering wheel support) can and hopefully will be patched out. I will be sticking with it.EDIT January: So there is good and bad news. The developers are behind on promised features (I am really waiting to create my own team) and haven't communicated much about it. I'd hold of on buying the Season Pass for now. But my steering wheel (G27) got patched in quite quickly and works solidly now after adjusting some settings. Also I just unlocked the "Expert" Mode with longer stages and the full Dakar Race, which is weid that I had to grind for it, however, it was also way worth it. The pace overall is remarkably better, co-driver calls are more dependable and the feelings of progression and achievement are multiplied manifold. tl.dr: The solid base is evolving and improving the more I time passes and the further I play, but not as quickly as could be hoped.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended : ♥♥♥♥ no, even on sale.Yes, the game looks gorgeous. But it's riddled with more problems and annoyances than my old dog has fleas.First off, you get thrown into a race even before you can configure your graphics or controls. Then, the game struggles to keep a steady framerate set to something appropriate for my rig (and I'm a tech savy guy, I know my ♥♥♥♥ around a rig). You chose you career and then you're stuck with it.I've quickly realised that the handling for the car I had picked was TERRIBLE. I mean, really, really terrible. So hey, I bought a new one. It was stored "in the warehouse" and I was stuck with the first one. Switching to trucks ? Impossible.Allright then, I'm fine with trying stuff in free ride to see what happens, and it's not just that car that is terrible, it's EVERYTHING. Well, to be fair, trucks handle pretty nicely, even though they seem to be unrealisticaly stable.Cars ? Forget brakes, brakes are for losers. Since you're a winner, your team decided not to fit any on your car. The downside is that if you see a tree or a rock just ahead, you WILL crash into it. So, to take a corner, you can't count on brakes, but handbrake, right ? Nope, it either does nothing at all, or sends you into a mad spin. But honestly, you get thrown into a mad spin for pretty much no reason at all, all the time, so maybe it has nothing to do with the handbrake. There are times when driving straight on a mostly even ground is impossible. Times when you know you ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up, and expect to tumble, and just get into a spin. The driving model is absolutely terrible. Need For Speed had more accurate models in the late 1990's.Allright, quads then ? Nope. Could not drive straight for more than a few tens of meters, then got into a spin, tried to counter it, did nothing. Halt, try to start again, spin again before even gaining speed.Bikes ? Cancer.Buggy ? Basically the same as cars, but slower, and tumbles when you'd expect a spin. Figures.I really wanted to love this game. There aren't many rally raid games (read basically none), but this one's execution is FUBAR. The driving model is so busted that there is no enjoyment to be found here.[EDIT] Tried again after deleting my save (not from within the game, it's impossible) so that I could get to race with a truck instead of a car. Things were going slightly better, until I hit an invisible rock and got stuck blocking the track. Visually, there was enough room between me and the rock wall to easily fit a bike, but apparently that's close enough to stop a several tons truck dead in its track and spin it 90°.If anyone has a decent rally raid game to recommend, I'll happy take suggestions in the comments.

_childDocuments_.review: Game with a potential but with huge flawsI am a very demanding player and I know that, I have been ever since. I also feel the potential and the work the developers put into this game, however even if I am sorry, I just can't recommend the game, at least not in it's current state. I'll start with pros and finish with things that are really bad in my opinion.Pros: Licence (obviously) - A lot of vehicles to choose fromReally nice car models - the vehicle models are really well done and the stickers of the sponsors are perfect and real. It's really nice just to look around and admire the vehicles.Good engine sounds - the vehicles sound really good (at least the ones that I have driven), from all angles.Maps look nice, though some locations don't feel natural.Cons: Vehicle handling - besides the handling is too arcady to my liking, vehicles tend to oversteer in every single turn. Even the trucks to some extent. It just feels like if the power was 80% RWD and 20% FWD, not 4WD/AWD. And don't get me started on the quads and bikes. Unplayable is not an exaggeration if you like your mental health as you'll loose control in any sharper turn or on any dune. Not only it's utterly unrealistic, it's also very frustrating. There's no punishment for going offtrack because neither grass nor water does really slow you down and bushes have no colision model. I must admit tho, you can feel the weels are dipping in the snad when you are on the desert. But that's about all the good things. I just wish we could choose - arcade model and simulation model. It wouldn't be too hard, games like Mafia II from 2010 have it.Damage - well, basically you can just hold the pedal from start to finish. You can fly dozens and dozens of meters over dunes and the vehicle will be intact, not even a slight loss of control over the vehicle when you land from 30 meters jump. As I already said, bushes have literally no colision model so the only way to damage your car is to crash into trees, rocks or rarely on a jump, but you won't usually even notice it. Or crashing into the AI, but that's my next point. On the other hand, when you smash into something, the car damage is visually quite nice.AI - self-preservation instinct is nonexistent, literally. I wanted to try sports mode but I had to turn it off after like 2 or 3 minutes of playing, my car was wrecked, the AI was wrecked and it was just horrible experience. Unfortunately professional is not much better because the AI still will fly on jumps like if they want to land on the Moon. They'll fly over the ideal landing spot by miles and crash intro objects that are behind the jump, usually when there's a turn after the jump. That also leads to them getting out of the ideal racing line and it takes a lot of effort for them to rejoin. Not only it looks bad, it also makes the game easy because it takes them forever to finish. I haven't felt pressure of finishing late the whole time.Overdramatic soundtrack - The first thing I did was to turn off the racing playlist. I am not saying it's a bad thing, just I don't like it. However before every start there is still too dramatic music to my liking. Yes, I get it, Dakar is a dangerous sport but Jesus Christ, too much is too much. Cinematic start - My God, who thought this would be a good idea? I want to focus on the start, I want to start manually, why would you make a cinematic start? That's a huge let down for me. Small things matter and I consider this a very very important small thing. Not to mention the unskipable part before the start is too long too.Stages - too short, too much waypoints.Level 25 - Another not so good decision. I understand that there has to be a sense of progression in games, but why would you restrict the players from one of the main reasons buy the game? Seems to me just like a lazy game design or the developers themselves knew that the players can't achieve it under 2 play hours so that they can't refund it after they can try the *real* mode. The navigator - I understand that this might be one of the more expensive parts of the game, however I still think that they could've hired a better voiceactor for the navigator. He sounds robotic, without emotions. Not to mention there literally are mistakes in his notes and sometimes he misleads you on a bad way (and no, I went throught the stage carefully multiple times and it wasn't my fault).Half finished procut released as a full game - there's more to come in the future updates and these things sound really interesting to be fair, however if it was in the launch I think the reception would be also much better. Unfortunately it seems like it's normal in this day and age.Conclusion - I think the game, even through the undeniably hard work of the developers, is underaverage car game that happens to have the license. If it was not for the license, I think this game wouldn't be really talked about, because with all honesty there is not much to talk about appart from the licence and the detailed models. I am curious how the developers will continue to improve the game and as I know myself, I'll be tempted to give it a go in the future. I just hope the devs won't get disheartened from the negative reviews, including mine, and work on the improvements instead. As I said, the game has potential, unfortunately it's mostly unused

_childDocuments_.review: So far the game is decent, a lot better than Dakar18.It has a lot it can improve on, but if they stick with it, which they have shown with Snowrunner, this could be a great game imo.It plays a lot more arcade than I expected, but it is still that weighty arcade racer, kind of like Baja Edge of Control. _childDocuments_.review: I have to admit, I wanted so badly to like this game. I'm a huge fan of the Dakar rally. Jumping in the game the physics fall short immediately, with the cars repeatedly tank slapping with seemingly no way to recover. No matter though, the other vehicles are so much more fun. Let's hop into the campaign, trucks were my first choice and holy wow they handle nice... just a shame the guy giving you directions is clearly on AN APPOSING TEAM. Directions are given early, late, incorrectly, unclear, and every combination of the above. Add to this the fact that when you think you're finally flying in the right direction... suddenly "you're on the wrong track"... THEN TELL ME WHERE TO GO. Only 1km later does he FINALLY tell you where you should be going. Extremely frustrating, and frankly it's ruined the game for me. The idea is there, but the approach has fallen short in a few key aspects.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated review after v1.4:The basic gameplay, navigation and stages are great. There are lots of vehicles that genuinely drive differently from each other, and with the Saudi-Arabia DLC you get the full Dakar events with very long stages. That being said, the game still has its share of bugs. Performance is okay but I needed to drop the graphics settings a lot to get smooth performance. The co-driver frequently gets confused even when you were just following in a fixed CAP direction. The 5-fold compression of the map makes the stages quite hectic and there are not enough obstacles (loose rocks etc.) to make driving at full speed feel dangerous. The FFB is not good especially in cars and wheel support is sporadic (please provide a general system to support any wheel instead of one model at a time).A refreshingly unique driving game that hovers somewhere between a freeroam arcade racer and a hardcore rally sim.

I probably understands the reasons behind it, because creating a unique color scheme and stickers will be adding another layer of complexity to damage model and everything, but on the other hand other games can do it, so it's nothing impossible.Generally I am very happy with the game. It would be a blast to have VR, but even without it it is a nice offroad truck racing game which has a lot to offer. Do not expect only sand and rocks, you will be driving through mud, rain, water and even snow

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a fun and easy to pick up multi-class offroad racing game then this is an absolute buy. If you're one of the weird people who were into Dakar 18 and were looking for an upgrade, maybe put off until Saber Porto finishes a few more features they've promised on the roadmap. After just under 30 hours and finishing first place in every event on professional mode several times I've finally unlocked simulation mode. The stages are about 3x the length and the speed limits adds a layer of complexity and authenticity that I felt was lacking in sport and pro modes, but the game still feels too much like it provides the Dakar spectacle rather than the Dakar experience. Maybe once they add more terrain variance, the ability to disembark from your vehicle to dig yourself out, use recovery boards, and tow straps, ask for help and help other drivers, ect. it will feel more in the spirit of the actual rally. Do I regret buying the game? Not yet. I remain cautiously optimistic that Saber Porto will be able to deliver on promises and make an already decent game great.

_childDocuments_.review: I am stunned at how unique of a rally racer this is!I was unsure about it because of the mixed reviews, but damn I'm glad I jumped in!First, there was some stuttering going on in the beginning but I lowered my graphics to high and they smoothed out over time.But this game is really something to not miss out on. I never heard of a Dakar Rally before and jumping in to this was shocking at how ALIVE the world is.Usually rally racing games have events strung along with time trial after trial looking only at leaderboards to see others. But this is like a mix of time trial and racing against others live on the map.Time is beyond a valuable resource as your timed position finish carries over into the next race. The best part is you can catch up to the ai way ahead that's currently simulating their time. And with penalties in place, you could finish 8th but the ai ahead messes up with repairs and such so you jump into first because you had a flawless run! So unique and it's way cool to see other car types racing too as if more is going on. Gameplay feels like Forza and Dirt together with a good usage of light yet effective tuning to make something feeling crappy to drive snappy. The next thing that blew me away was navigating and getting used to it without waypoints. Play sport mode first only to get used to the tuning and physics, then bring your cars into Professional mode as soon as you can. This is where you really start getting a sample of the true depth this game has to offer.Learning to read the road map, getting lost, being careful of 90 km limit areas, and doing all this while it's pitch black or in a storm is an unforgettable experience! Plus it's SO NICE to play something that doesn't surround a track with walls 24/7.Can't wait for all the planned updates!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic, and for anyone who just wants a solid racing game as a package, this is worth it IMO, I would say its more about the experience, as you go through these luxurious landscapes, starting off the beaten track, and a sandstorm impairs your vision, and then going into the water, through a cave, just to notice there is a drop at the end of a waterfall that you need to pass through.I dont think ill be able to experience moments like this in any other racing game, so its worth it for that.Whilst i only play on sport mode (The more arcadey setting, point to point races) it feels authentic, understanding the weight of the vehicle is one thing where as knowing how terrain plays out is another, the map has just as much of an effect on how you play as do your simplified settings menu does, also there are some options for controls that you can fine tune to give yourself a better personal experience if the handling isnt what you expect, I feel its well rounded, but this is no simulation, and personally, I dont want a simulation game so this is fine for me.On that note though the options are available for a more realistic dakar experience with the rather intuitive way to read the map and flick through notes.

_childDocuments_.review: Very Disappointed in this game. First off, I dont understand why the game is launching my Viveport app and forcing open VR when the game has no VR capabilities. closing the steamVR app results in Dakar closing; by far the most absurd bug ive heard of. Day 1 review, about the only thing i cant complain about it the graphics. The game is visually amazing, the environment is beautiful and the water and other elements really make the graphics that much better. when there isnt horrible frame skipping. the initial cutscene and 'tutorial' put you through a series of vehicles, showing off different environments and racing styles. Being the first scene anyone will see opening this game, i would expect it to be completely polished without any kind of lag or delay or skips between movements. something like that really set the precedence for what else the game has to offer if the first scene is extremely choppy and all over the place. after the initial tutorial 'race' you will select your first vehicle and begin your first Dakar Qualification race. right off the bat you are at a disadvantage. all of the ai are just slightly faster than you, even if you select the vehicle with the highest top speed which is odd. possibly they have vehicle 'upgrades' and are faster, and maybe you arent expected to win in the qualifying race anyway, but i actually couldnt finish the race before giving up even after restarting several times.(and im not one to give up grinding something out i hate just to complete it. i.e Dark souls)the steering starts at a neutral 50%, and that is already extremely sensitive. turning down to 20% you can still barely keep control of the vehicle. even when making very minor flicks on the analog stick, it is near impossible to avoid a back-and-forth fishtail. there isnt much correction in the steering, it is just an immediate response that sends you back and forth to be quickly spun out. graphically this game is all i want it to be, but i cant turn down the steering responsiveness down to the point to where im not spinning out. the concept of this game is amazing, but compared to one of the only other games in this Genre being Baja: Edge of control, you can best believe i have sent a refund to go back and play a game from 2009. the only important aspect in driving games is how the car controls, and in a game like this where you can literally spend 20+ hours in a race, i cant see myself going past a 5 minute race in its current stage.my first review, and only to show my disappointment and to hopefully steer other away until they have resolved some of the very key components that even make this game worth playing to begin with. this game has the potential to be amazing, but for now, for me its a no

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give this a mixed review so I'm just going to say this here, this is a MIXED review, not strictly positive or negative. I use a G29 Log wheel with T LCM load pedals (sim pedals) with no real issues so take that with a grain of salt since they still have not added the update for all types which is in my opinion, unacceptable since you can download free programs that would do so for you. Not only that, all buttons on my G29 are not properly recognized either and you cannot change the pause or repair buttons which is stupid.The driving isn't a SIM but it functions mostly well. Where it fails at is not allowing you to change your differential. In a game like this where you need to modulate your accelerations and deceleration this is god awful. If you are using a truck who cares? It's a tub or lard and likely won't oversteer anyway. If you are using a car, on the other hand, you will likely be oversteering off the track every single time you release off the throttle. It's really awful and should be adjustable. But other than that I don't really have any gripes with how the cars handle.The next thing that needs to be fixed, is the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ navigator. The issue? If you drive slow, no issues whatsoever. But once you start averaging speed of over 160 KPH this thing starts becoming useless. He will literally tell you to start turning when you've already reached or passed the corner rather than 3-5 seconds earlier like he should have. It leads you to constantly getting lost if you actually are listening to what he is saying. The roadmap isn't much better either since it doesn't scroll up as you go until you pass a CP forcing YOU to do it manually, while you are going 160 KPH. Really?Overall the experience is a 7.5 out of 10. If you learn a track it's pretty good. If it's your first time, expect to struggle a lot and get lost 24/7 because the nav is completely busted at points. Just go watch any streamer and you can easily confirm this. The physics are good, they are nice to the players when it comes to damages, the AI provide just the right amount of challenge to get started for more experienced drivers, etc. But while the issues I mentioned above aren't game breaking, they are abhorrently bad and should have been fixed before this game was ever released.I changed my mind, the physics in this game are god awful. How the grip works doesn't make sense. The differential doesn't make sense. I set up my car with full rear brake bias and it still brakes completely in a straight line. Did they even test this game?!?!?

_childDocuments_.review: I got this after watching Dakar Rally 2023 on TV. I've never been a rally game fan, spending most time on F1 games and more recently, Assetto Corsa. Like those, driving these cars is still a skill, and it takes time and track awareness to avoid flying off at every corner. I've seen many complaints about the game's stability and also the vehicle physics, but I did not have any of these issues (using mid-Jan 2023 version) on my Core i9 with RTX 3070 at QHD on epic graphics settings. I spent the most time in SxS, and although traction was often challenging, I found it OK by using small steering inputs and careful braking, just like holding an F1 car on track at low speed. Although I've never driven any of these vehicles in real life, the physics did not seem especially bad compared to what I expected. Most of all, the scenery was spectacular and the competitive driving was just really fun. I think this is an exceptional genre-defining game and would thoroughly recommend it to anyone who is new to rally games. I also appreciated the simple progression and unlock system, no crazy micro-transactions or hundreds of DLC to acquire, or weird partial unlocks that take forever to add up to anything. For a reasonable price, you get a complete game with tonnes of content, similar in architecture to Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit (albeit without the cops!). Pick any event from a map, build up a collection of cars, and race through stunning courses. This is one of few games that I would genuinely rate 5-stars (in any genre).

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not having the issues that some others have experienced. After playing 73 hours so far the game has only crashed a couple of times. That said if I play the game on my gaming laptop with RTX 2070 GPU I do get the frame rate drop. Part of the problem I suspect is the game is constantly auto saving and if your internet connection is a bit slow it makes the game stutter. I also played Dakar 18 and much prefer Dakar Desert Rally and I'm really enjoying it. One thing you learn early on is not to trust the navigator. He'll often say "keep" left when in fact you should keep right. You need to be constant keeping an eye on the roadbook. Hopefully this is something that will get addressed in a patch.The other annoying thing in simulation mode is the 170 km/h speed limit. It's very easy to exceed this and receive a time penalty. My solution is to lower the tyre pressures and drive in manual mode and don't go into top gear. There really needs to be a speed limiter built in. _childDocuments_.review: The graphics of the game are absolutely outstanding, and they give a wonderful realistic impression of Saudi Arabia, where I used to live for a while. Maybe this could be the best open world game around atm. 1. 'Sport Mode' ist not a rally, but a race.2. Car controls are not really precise, and it is very difficult to tweak them good enough for the trucks. For the faster vehicles it is more or less impossible to make them handle realistically.3. the game obviously has been designed for more or less professional and enthusiastic young gamers with expensive equipment like steering wheels and pedals and shifters etc. A poor old man with just wasd in automatic mode has no real chance in professional mode to finish rank 8 or even better to qualify for the next stage. I might be giving up now at level 24, because sometimes I need more than 7 attempts to finish one single stage. And trying it again and again and again ist no fun and frustrating.4. the navigator is a complete idiot, in real live I would have fired him after the second stage. He is talking too much, and often not precise enough. And why does he not keep an eye on the tripmaster in order to pick the exact right moment to announce a speed limit zone or bends and obstacles ? Once you get lost, he has no clue where to go and needs minutes to sort it out. And where is the map in addition to the roadbook which typically belongs on every navigator's desk ? Also, there is no navigator with german language, which makes it sometimes even more difficult, and the way he is reading the road book is not what I remember out of my time as an active rally driver, certainly on smaller events than the Dakar Rally. That navigator has to be configurable somehow, he does not have to say unimportant things twice and important things at the wrong time.5. All together: what a pity that such a potential has been wasted on a game which completely discriminates hobby gamers. Sure I did see some really great youtube clips of really excellent and fast drivers finishing stages in a brilliant way, but I guess even those guys would be having a real hard time with my hardware.*. I really would love to take my old Misubishi Pajero Evolution or Manta 400 out of the garage, paint it black and yellow and start in the 'historical class' as an amateur, enjoying the beautiful landscape, the roadbooks, and the whole setup around, without having to compete against Sebastian Loeb. Certainly I would be happy with rank 45 or even 450 on a list leaded by Eduard Nikolajew.I did spend at least 10000 kilometers on desert tracks in my live, with standard cars, and with two marston mats, two shovels and a little winch ready to be applied when it really comes to desert business. Maybe this game is not meant to be played by occasional gamers - so is it the right one for you ?
