_childDocuments_.review: So far, I have been enjoying this game as much as I can, and find this game to be a lot of fun, when not taking into account the performance issues that I've been having. For what I've got, I can get moments where the game runs at a solid 60 fps, but more often than not, there are times where the game seriously chugs and goes to like 20 fps, or even 15 fps, from my cpu being under very heavy loads while running the game. However what really gets me is trying to figure out why I'm having such performance hits, cause when I look at the minimum and recommended specs for both this game and Dakar 18, this game's prequel, there are some things that I'd expect, but then also some things that don't make sense to me.The way I define what 'minimum requirements' means is the minimum specs needed to be able to run the game at its intended frame rate with the graphics set as low as possible and have very little stuttering or slow down, with 'recommended requirements' being the minimum specs to run the game at its intended frame rate, but with graphics set as high as they can go and minimum stuttering if any could be present. But when I go to look up the different requirements for both games, minimum and recommended, some things don't add up to me.The Intel cpu that is put for the minimum requirements is an i5-2300, which has a base speed of 2.8 GHz. The Intel cpu listed for the minimum for Dakar 18 is an i5-2400s, which has a base speed of 2.5 GHz. This is understandable, this newer game requires a cpu with a higher base speed than an older game. The recommended Intel cpus for both games are an i5-4690k for Dakar 18, which has a base speed of 3.5 GHz, and an i5-4790k for this game, which has a base speed of 4 GHz. And again, this makes sense given which game came first. However, note how I only put the base speeds. All of the Intel cpus that were put for the requirements for both games have turbo modes. For this game, the max turbo speeds for the recommended Intel cpus for both games are 4 GHz for the i5-4690k for Dakar 18 and 4.4 GHz for the i5-4790k for this game, and still, everything appears normal, the newer game recommends a cpu with more power at the top end than the older game. But now, here's where the pattern breaks. For the Intel cpus listed as the minimums for both games, the i5-2300 set as the minimum for this game has a max turbo speed of 3.1 GHz, but the i5-2400s set as the minimum for the prequel, Dakar 18, has a max turbo speed of 3.3 GHz. The older game requires a cpu with a higher turbo speed than the newer game.Now I'm gonna compare these speeds to the cpu inside my PC. My PC has an i7-8750h inside, which has a base speed of 2.2 GHz, so at the low end, my cpu is the weakest of the 5 cpus mentioned here. However, like the other 4 cpus listed above, mine also has a turbo mode. The max turbo speed of my cpu is 4.1 GHz, which is well higher than the max turbo speeds of the minimum cpus for both games, as well as the recommended cpu for Dakar 18, and within the range of speeds for the recommended cpu for this game. Even though when I've tested my performance for the game by having task manager open along side it, and my cpu peaks at around 3.9 GHz when running the game, that's still within the range of the recommended cpu for the prequel game, and I can run that game flawlessly, whereas here I get heavy slow downs 50-70% of the time.Though this wouldn't be that big of an issue, at least for me, if the in-game clock timing your run of each stage accounted for when you're having slow downs and performance hits, but it doesn't. When experiencing slow downs, the actually gameplay speed takes a hit equal in strength as the hit the performance gets, meaning you actually do move slower when the game is running slower, but the stage timer does not slow down. The timer matches real-time speed, instead of in-game speed. So if you are having slow down such that your frame rate is at 20 fps, and your vehicle is moving on screen at an equal speed ratio compared to when running at the full 60 fps, the clock doesn't count a second as every 60 in-game frames computed, but instead every real second gets counted as a second for the stage time, meaning at 20 fps, one rendered second equals 3 real seconds counted on the stage clock.Even though almost all of what I've said has been talking about the cons of the game, I still find the game itself a lot of fun to play, cause I love watching the Dakar Rally on TV, and being able to experience myself in a video game format I think is really amazing. That and I love long racing games, so having the Dakar Rally be made into a game, along with many other endurance rallies, I find to be very fascinating, and I do recommend this game for those that like racing games and like rally races.

_childDocuments_.review: 5/10Somewhat improved over Dakar 18 but that's not saying much.Handling and physics are still terrible, no weight to the cars, no wheelspin control to speak of, as if they wanted the game to be approachable, meanwhile Dirt Rally and WRC games with their brutal difficulty sell like hotcakes and people come back for more.Even a physics and handling model 1/4 as good as DR 2.0 would've been enough, instead you get a "simulation mode" with Crazy Taxi physics and brutally difficult navigation.What did you want the game to be? Another "what if" disappointment? Nailed it.- Arcade mode is fun but the races are too short.- Pro mode has unlimited speed but AI is too easy and races are too short- Simulation mode has decent AI and long stages but every single mile is speed limited. It's fine for realism sake and an interesting challenge, but applying it to an entire game mode instead of specific events is a baffling decision that ultimately cuts the game's legs right off because......- .....the addition of classic cars like Citroen DS or Peugeot 405 T16 is fantastic..........but because every single mile of every single race is speed limited, you will never have a simulation race to enjoy them on. If you want to let them fly, you go back to the pedestrian game modes and enjoy bad AI and 6 minute stages. yaaaaySo essentially : Go buy some DLC cars and have fun driving them at half throttle for 60 hours. A total joke.So everywhere you turn, every game mode has a glaring flaw, there is no place in this game that has it all or a game mode where you feel like "THAT'S IT". Every aspect of this game is another opportunity where they dropped the ball.I hoped the USA expansion would have some new simulation races at full speed but no, it's some more Arcade/Pro mode races and that's it, so I won't be wasting money on that either.And the big announcements are over, the roadmap is done THERE WILL BE NO MORE CONTENT, so enjoy your speed limits and thanks for playing.All you get when playing this game is the nagging feeling of what it could've been all over again.Don't buy this.

name: Terminator: Dark Fate - Defiance
detailed_description: Terminator: Dark Fate – Defiance is a real-time strategy game based on the Terminator: Dark Fate universe that follows the war between humanity and Legion's synthetic intelligent machine network. In the single-player campaign , you take the role of a commander in the Founders, a force made up of the remnants of the US military and guide your army in an attempt to foil Legion's plan to exterminate the last remnants of humanity. In skirmish and multiplayer modes, play as three very diverse factions: Founders, Movement and Legion. Take control of an army carried over from mission to mission on a series of large strategic maps. Make decisions about unit placement, battle tactics and abilities so that you don’t just survive but can become the leader of the resistance against the machines. Hone your skills and military expertise by replaying and achieving the best possible outcomes. Dynamic battlefields: realistic tactics and consequences Engage in complex, realistic battles where your tactical decisions are vital to your survival and ultimate victory. Use a variety of military equipment, vehicles and ammunition types in your battles against the enemy. Recruit and train new units, assign new skills and acquire new weapons and equipment to continue the resistance. Encounter tense battles. Your battlefield tactics and choices have deep consequences that will impact through the campaign, with other factions and characters either joining you or fighting against you, and with certain missions being available or not depending on your actions. Your resources are limited and you must protect your army. Weapons of war receive damage through a modular component damage system where armour characteristics, component malfunctions and hull structure all affect if your troops survive. Lead the survival of mankind Recruit others to your cause and grow your army . Mix and match the composition of your troops to fit your preferred battle tactics. Use infantry units, heavy armoured military vehicles, plasma cannon technology, drones and other flying units and even human skirmishers to achieve victory. Use the battlefield to your advantage! Physics-based building demolition lets you generate a realistic set of tactical consequences, especially in urban areas. Multiplayer Mayhem: Skirmish and Online Battles The excitement amplifies in skirmish and multiplayer modes , where you can play as three distinct factions : Founders, Movement, and Legion. Engage in epic battles across vast strategic landscapes, testing your skills and military expertise. Every decision matters, impacting alliances, missions, and the overall survival of mankind. Challenge your skills in skirmish and online multiplayer matches, facing off against AI or real-life human opponents in intense 1v1 and 2v2 battles.

_childDocuments_.review: After many hours playing this game i would have to give it a big thumbs down.Pathfinding is just as broken as it was on release day.Save scumming is a real game mechanic not sure why they went this route but it looks like it is here to stay thanks to insisting on rng and lack of intuitive missions.Did i mention pathfinding because this is the real deal breaker units will get stuck on everything including each other and it happens regularly throughout the entire game and the developers have made no clear intentions on fixing this.Visuals leave alot to be desired for a 2024 game made in ue5The audio effects are adequate but the soundtrack get really old really fast.The campaign mechanics on the other hand are what kept me playing,though you really arent given alot of choice concerning your army composition due to supply constraints.You can be a force of militia type units via movement or old usa units via the founders in much smaller nembers as for the integrators it is possible to aquire their units also but the supply costs are so high that it would lead to game over.I think this could be a great game if the devs stop trying to bring in a better camera or some skirmish maps that noone will play instead of resolving gamebreaking bugs and the awful pathfinding.

_childDocuments_.review: Where to start???I rarely write reviews in all honesty but this game made me! The premise of this game is really great in terms of its micromanagement of your forces, supplies and Goodwill points. It's RTS style is pretty decent, offering various types of squads to counteract enemy troops and lots of opportunities to re-supply and restore your troops. The cover system, whether laying on floor or set up in a building, is absolutely vital to keeping your squads alive as without it, your squad will perish.However!This game becomes increasingly frustrating as the enemy troops, whether be it machines or Cartel, are incredibly over powered against your own squads. Especially when you can only choose a select amount from your army first. Like i said previously if your squads aren't in cover you perish pretty easily, this makes it even harder to assault enemy buildings when exiting vehicles near the building or sprinting as both vehicles and troops just get mowed down. Troops seem to die way to easily on this game for my liking, making it almost impossible to complete.I've played a lot of RTS' in my day but none quite annoyingly fun, frustrating, unique and difficult to play. I started on hard difficulty first, quickly found myself moving to moderate then eventually playing on easy to keep the 'fun' still in the game but i do strongly believe the enemies are way too strong, which i guess is the point in this but for me completely ruins it for me. Other than those few points, it is a good game but enemies need toning down a bit lol

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: After further playtime, I honestly can't recommend this game to anyone unless they're interested in intense frustration. There's a lot of good framework behind this game that just never quite works out, and more often than not the game feels like it's punishing you for no discernible reason. The mechanics feel nonsensical at times or only work when the game feels like they should. This will be one of the few games I will not return to after hitting a breaking point with frustration.Decently fun but flawed. The lack of precise commands or positioning options when giving orders to a squad leads to some wholly frustrating experiences in an otherwise alright game. Gameplay reminds me of a cross between Gates of Hell: Ostfront and Company of Heroes, with all the flaws of both games and a few additional ones. There is no infantry cover mechanic outside of garrisoning buildings, which they do allow you to adjust the general focus of the garrison from one side of a building or another with a specific command. This leads to situations where an assault on a hostile position is necessary, but you lack any useful tools to commit that short of a limited use of smoke grenades. The squad's AI is also a bit cumbersome, requiring orders to even go prone under fire rather than stand up and take it to the face.Following that, the AI will freely position its units in intelligent defensive patterns. Which is a good thing, by and large, but massively frustrating when you need to deal with artillery guarded by a defensive line with machine guns to prevent infantry rushing and anti-tank to prevent vehicle rushing to deal with it. Artillery present also doesn't stop the squad AI from deciding that those Rangers you just sent into a building clearly need to be on the rooftop, exposed, where the garrison command now offers zero benefit for protection from overhead barrage. Cover is a direct obstruction- as the building takes damage, it goes away visually, and being shot from an angle that isn't covered by a wall means that cover doesn't provide benefit. Again, reasonable and realistic, but the lack of fine control to manage your troops' position makes it more frustrating than it needs to be, with squads regularly losing members while in cover because the AI won't reposition them into a spot that actually helps them. In a game all about resource management, including finite personnel for replacements, losing a single infantryman has impact. Again, all the more frustrating by how little control you actually have over their movements.Vehicles feel weak, with damage quickly accumulating even to small arms fire unless it's rated as a drivable by a Tank Crew, not a Vehicle Crew. Vehicles like a Stryker, which have decent armor for protection against small arms, can be damaged by 5.56mm rounds. Very often the first through-armor hit, which doesn't take long to happen, will immediately hamper the vehicle in some way. From my experience with the game so far, it's almost always been engine damage, slowing the vehicle down until it can be repaired. Thankfully that's possible to do in the field to some extent, but the armor doesn't come back. Just the functionality. Considering some things can be armored with Junk Armor and it's clearly made of scrap laying around like sheet metal and wooden barrels, that feels a bit off.Resource management is a good attempt but again feels off. All resources - food, ammo, fuel - are calculated as a single abstract resource for ease, but the calculations for what everything consumes in a day feel strange. A squad of 7 Infantry consume more resources daily than a squad of 8 Militia for whatever reason, and daily consumption is calculated separately from resupplying ammo. Vehicles also have a daily consumption, which again makes some sense for fuel while moving and maintenance, but things like a trailer have nearly as much daily consumption as the vehicle that carries it. I can make an argument both for and against the way it's handled, but I end up going back to my original statement here that it just feels off. TL;DR, the game is decently fun if you like the genre and I do recommend it if so. Just be prepared for frustration when your units decide that those bullets flying their way would make a great consumable and eat them instead of avoiding them.EDIT: After further playtime, I honestly can't recommend this game to anyone unless they're interested in intense frustration. There's a lot of good framework behind this game that just never quite works out, and more often than not the game feels like it's punishing you for no discernible reason. The mechanics feel nonsensical at times or only work when the game feels like they should. This will be one of the few games I will not return to after hitting a breaking point with frustration.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly one of the most enjoyable RTS games I have ever played, my only wish was that the campaign was longer or they added some sort of dynamic campaign that allowed continuation past the end of the game.  It was punishingly difficult at time, but I honestly never really felt cheated out of win (though I had a lot of reloads).  There are a few situations where there is a right answer so to speak, and I get that some will not like that, however it was fun to learn the differing routes for success even if I wanted to pull my hair out a few times.Additionally, I played through the campaign in parallel with one of my good buddies, sharing strategies, experiences, frustrations ect.  Based on our compared experiences there really is a lot of variance in how everything is handled on a mission by mission basis.I would for sure recommend this game if you have an enjoyment for semi realistic difficult RTS games.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has alot of potential and cool ideas. However, there are some core gameplay designs leave alot to be desired. The Campaign itself has an okay story and it has more choices than I expected it to have. However, it falls short in mission design and some of the core gameplay design really shows its flaws when you get down to it. Let me explain the really big flaws I found while playing:- Cover and Camoflauge/Stealth is very inconsistent and hard to figure out if it works. - Pathfinding can seem cool at first but it gets really frustrating later on with vehicles randomly deciding to take the roads with the most enemy, infantry squad mates getting stuck at terrain, infantry not knowing how to position themselves at buildings, and shots going through terrain or for some reason not seeing the enemy through terrain even if they are clearly visible.- Guided rockets being inconsistent with damage and lock-on accuracy.- For some reason the devs made it so you cannot grind for manpower, supplies, or equipment outside of story missions. Meaning you may need to restart an entire Campaign if you screw up a mission or just lack the materials to go on.- Frustrating mission designs (Spawns all over for enemy, lots of ground to realistically cover with what you have, objectives being placed near enemy spawns, list goes on....)So would I recommend this game? Hard no. Only can recommend it if your a fan of really hard RTS or Terminator games.Alot of changes need to happen for this game to reach its full potential.

_childDocuments_.review: My experience after (some of, and only) the campaign is: a very tentative yes. There's a lot of things this game does right but it seems to hit a wall after a certain point. I think a lot of things need to be re-balanced. It becomes so much of a slug-fest that you find yourself losing interest. I imagine they're attempting to make you feel desperate, but... it's a game... and not much fun when you're going against concrete bunkers w/ MG emplacements/minefields/artillery support towards the end of a mission and you're out of supply and on a 15 minute time limit. Units move way too slow for that - even mounted (assuming they have fuel). The campaign is on a rail and I feel like I was on it until the final Cartel side mission.I can't speak for Skirmishes because I haven't tried any, but judging from the very small list of maps/scenarios available - it's not something they're going to concentrate on, which is what I was hoping for. It's really disappointing and didn't even seem appealing enough for me to try.I think it's worth it but barely - as it is. I like to spend 1-2USD/per hour of enjoyment. I'm feeling shorted right now but patches may change that.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great!! I was skeptical at first. Even after watching some gameplay. But after buying it and playing for a few hours last night, I finally say the beauty in it. It’s like Men of War and Jagged alliance had a baby. It’s not the war feeling of Men of War but a bit more personal like you would be with Jagged Alliance. It’s got a map inbetween missions that you can choose where to go next, and it’s not linear. You can choose what troops you will bring with you, what troops will be in what vehicles, what weapons and armor to mount to vehicles, and you can repair vehicles you find during the battle and if you keep them alive and are able to escape the mission with them, they become part of your army. You can hire infantry (many different types), vehicles, and supplies. There is a lot of cool micro management in the game, both on the map and in the battle. And the story is not bland, it’s open ended and give the feel of being in war and being in the Terminator world. 9/10I recommend downloading a few mods. And it could use a few more that I havnt seen yet but sure they will come. Definitely get all troop have drivers licenses. That mod is essential.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to enjoy this title. I really, really do. It really scratches that Tiberian Sun itch. And let me tell you there are fewer things more satisfying than taking out a specific target with precision ATGM placement. There are some great parts to this game. But there are absolutely some glaring issues.Pathfinding is... well, let me give some specific examples:You will regularly see your own vehicles clip through each other, or collide and block each other.Don't bother group selecting your vehicles to move, the predefined destination spaces are good only if you want all of your vehicles to get oneshot by literally any AT or artillery or any of the other brutal ranged AoE that exists in the game.The pathfinding will regularly ♥♥♥♥ the bed and send your units the exact opposite way you intend, often times directly into the patrol you're trying to avoid, or insisting to use a road which obviously is mined.Want to move your three units from one building to another? Make sure you don't individually select them and click the building, because they will literally run into each other, stop at the doorways and get mowed down by the enemy while pathing into each other. Apparently the "correct" way is to select the whole building, and tell the BUILDING to deploy into ANOTHER building. Of course!Got a lot of units in a single building? Good luck getting any AT shots off, those units will be ping-ponging from wall to wall and never complete their AT deployment progress bar to fire their missile (all the while being shot to ♥♥♥♥ by the enemy). You practically have to put an AT unit in it's own building for it to behave with any effectiveness.A simple suite of integration and unit tests would have prevented all of these problems. It's frankly embarrassing and unacceptable for a title in 2024 to have worse pathfinding than games I played 30 years ago.Some other issues:Music is generic and boring. Started out kind of interesting, but I found myself just tabbing to Spotify and loading up my favorite sci-fi OSTs after about 3-5 hours of listening to this. It all sounds pretty derivative of T2 and nothing stood out.Regularly experience graphic bugs related to the debris system. After a tank of mine blew up an abandoned trailer all of the confetti pieces exploded, one of those pieces then enlarged about 500x and filled the entire screen. Apparently this issue SURVIVED A SAVE / LOAD ?! I'm not even sure how the hell that's possible.The unit leveling system is absolutely a Flex Tape last minute addition. There is no reason to pick the obvious options like stealth for snipers or rate of fire for most other units. Choosing anything else just nerfs the unit vs a unit that had rate of fire or stealth upgrade, so this system is basically pointless and only serves to give the player the illusion they are directing their unit's progression.I shouldn't have to squint and nitpick so much about making sure my units are picking up fallen weaponry, and it should be readily obvious which weaponry is an upgrade / downgrade for the unit.I shouldn't have to unpause the game for the indicators of fallen weapons to become highlightable by my selected unit.I should have way more control over a unit's equipment and levelups DURING the mission, not just after it.If you swap a unit's weapon between missions that weapon comes empty and you have to pay to resupply. Switch weapons back? Resupply. Switch weapons a third time? Yup, you're just dumping ammunition every time! WHY?!Complete lack of anything online about the game. No wiki, no unit information, no guides, nothing.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most in depth RTS games I have played. I have played C&C, Halo wars 1 and 2, Company of Heroes and many others and this game is very fun to play. Although the one thing I will say is even on normal I find myself restarting a bunch of times with the NPC enemy being very difficult. The learning curve is steep and there is not much of a tutorial but once you get past the first couple of missions things start to fall together. If you enjoy a challenge in RTS this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Terminator: Dark Fate - Defiance

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, not only is RTS back in a big way, but also evolving in all the right directions in Terminator: Dark Fate - Defiance. This game is tough, you have to think and try new strategies, and you've got to balance conserving your forces and resources whilst trying to achieve multiple stretch goals. I love it, it's like I've gone back to the golden days of RTS. Is the game perfect? No, it could do with a few patches and a little more polish and maybe isn't everyone's cup of tea, but I think it's an absolute gem of a game.I for one am not going to take potshots at this labour of love, but rather say a big thanks for seeing something like this being developed in modern gaming, where sadly there is a deluge of money grabs and poor quality games - something this is not. Goodbye life stretch goals, hello defiance.

_childDocuments_.review: So I just beat the campaign for the first time. All I can say is wow. Literally one of the best RTS campaigns I've ever played. There is a lot of awesomeness packed into this game and I love the lore. I have some recommendations for a few gameplay optimizations that would make it even more amazing than it already is.Please make tanks not expend precious tank rounds on individual soldiers. They're smart enough to select ammo types for the job, but please make them more discerning with tank (particularly plasma tank rounds).Some missions took an entire day to beat lol, perhaps shift all the difficulty levels up one and create a "regular mode". If you are just starting out be sure to start in Story Mode.I have a decent gaming rig that plays all current AAA titles at 75-144 FPS. The last mission was chugging along at about 20fps the whole mission. Ouch. Perhaps some performance optimizations for that level? I suspect it was the water animation. Maybe I saved too many of my units from previous missions and my army was too big.There were some odd bugs where I would save from resource management screen and when I load, the campaign would react differently. For example I helped the integrators get the storm technology and at the resource screen they didn't offer me to trade supplies. I saved and reloaded and they paid me a large sum and opened up trade. This was an welcome twist, however if I hadn't saved and reloaded the game I would have been in a tough spot.Your ability to progress effectively in the game feels almost solely related to your ability to hit F5 and F8. I had to reload my game probably 150 times over the course of the campaign.Some additional sorting functionality in the resource screen would be very helpful when upgrading/retrofitting. For example sort by "has available training slots", sort by damage.Some quantitative stats on the units like available HP meter, and how certain range and armor upgrades impact each unit. I found myself guessing at times despite the helpful descriptions.Please make units make somewhat of a better attempt to make line of site before firing. I think its cool to see the occasional fence post or swing set get obliterated by a tank round but when the enemy is on the other side of a strong building, there's no reason to start firing yet. Keep some of the line of margin of error because it adds to the experience but maybe turn down a bit on obvious obstructions?Don't take this as anything negative, definitely get the game it's worth it and I enjoyed it.

_childDocuments_.review: Terminator: Dark Fate - Defiance is "Terminator: Dark Fate – Defiance is not just a game; it's an adrenaline-fueled journey where your strategic prowess decides the fate of mankind against the machines". Well lets be honest... Its not really adrenaline fueled but it does have some really good strategic elements to it. In this review we will break down the mechanics of the game and hopefully help others make a more informed decision on their purchases.I had a faily lengthy review written out detailing and breaking down all the different aspects of the game. Sadly I was way over the character limitations of the review. So we are going to do this more simply.PROS:The details of the buildings is great and the environment on the city maps is just perfect for the story.The music and sounds of the game are great as well.The concept of the game is great and its a really loved franchise.Partially asymmetrical factions.CONS:The non city maps look dull, boring, and just outright out of place.The RTS aspects of the game are constantly interrupted by conversations, sometimes it stops the gameplay sometimes it doesnt but it seems to constantly be happening the entire mission.This game follows a failing RTS model in which you cannot produce units on the battlefield, have very limited resources, fighting a much superior enemy that completely lacks balance.The game boasts complex parts as in a truck as the chasis, engine, wheels, etc etc. Yet on the mechs units dont focus on what they can take out but merely attack the unit. This could be amazing if say snipers focused on the optics\targeting, heavy weapons focused on mobility parts, and rockets focused on the core. Sadly this doesnt appear to be the case at all. Medium and Large units are best taken out by long range rockets and small units by gunners and thats about it. Should nearly anything get up close and personal with your units there is a very good chance they are already dead.Balancing is an issue through and through. Straight out gunfights, entrenched warfare, etc just doesnt feel very solid. A group of actual soldiers cant take out a squad of militia in a building without a huge firefight let alone terminators in a building. Either way you will blow through most your ammo or lose most of your squads trying to do it. Even just watching the AI try and fight itself (The Movement vs Terminators) the losses are ridiculous for the Movement.Ally AI will steal your vehicles at every chance, even when you are just making repairs or if the vehicle has caught fire and your crew is forced to get out.There doesnt appear to really be a defensive bonus that is noticed visually, gameplay wise, etc for holding a building over being in the prone position fighting enemies. You cant take defensive positions behind walls.Setting formations even for a single unit to be effective in combat is a joke.Terminators will attack through building, vehicles, etc to directly damage units that cant seem to fire back because they dont have line of sight.The post up in a particular direction in a building is a joke. Say you want everyone guarding the north side of a building. you can give the order but for the next few min everyone in the building is just running around not firing like they dont know which way is north. Even once they get in position as soon as the first soldier dies in the building they all start running around again. Units feel overpriced and under valued in the battlefield - A player will spend a lot of credits upgrading a unit, given the limited line of sight and harsh damage output of the Terminators, that they will often just die nearly instantly if they are facing a unit that counters them in any way. ATG vs RPG combat is a joke. You have to constantly micromanage these units to make sure they dont waste ammo on units that can easily be taken out by riflemen. MEH:The strategic map concept feels half baked. Its either linear or its not and a game like this is a fight for survival and when you wipe all the enemy out of an area there should be something great for that but this game doesnt reward fighting back like that. Its linear and there isnt always some great benefit to wiping the map, aside from maybe scavenging a few vehicles. I could break down a lot more of this game as I did in the initially written review. Overall this game takes a great concept and introduces it with all the current failing ideas in the RTS genre. Players like building bases in an RTS, or at least being able to call in more units. Players like being able to have recon over an area to know whats coming so they can react accordingly. Players like coop play on more than 5 maps. Players like a story driven rts where the story doesnt constantly interrupt their gameplay. Players like having the ability to make their own maps. Players like being able to play as more than one faction. Players like a UI that is smooth and easy to use. Players like gameply that rewards great strategic choices rather than the fastest clickers. Players like being able to reinforce their units to replenish loses like Company of Heroes did. Sadly all the aspects that has made the most popular RTS games the most popular. This game lacks. Its relying mostly on the story telling, the franchise, and the broken model of many failed RTS games. And for me personally I dont like having to fight my allies for vehicles I brought to the battlefield. The game does have a huge potential to become a staple in the industry. Balancing, reinforcing units, better recon abilities, and better AI are going to be the key to whether or not this game can make that top 10 on the steam charts. Until there are some solid updates I have to recommend avoiding this game to see how it progresses. Hopefully the developers will look at what they have vs what has been massively successful and why those titles have been so successful and make a few changes to round out the gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun but challenging RTS game. Plays very differently to others in the genre, more similar to syrian warfare than something like starcraft. It's a game that challenges the player and can feel absolutely impossible at times especially prior to the balance changes that were recently made. The game has persistent units from mission to mission which really makes you connect with and appreciate the value of your individual units (and of course adds to the frustration of losing them). Unfortunately this game seems to punish you for not knowing things you'd normally have no way of knowing without first experiencing them and having to reload which doesn't feel great at the best of times. Luckily the game is still incredibly fun and I can easily see an RTS veteran (or a masochist) thoroughly enjoying their time with this game. Big props to the developers for engaging with the community so much and listening to feedback. They are constantly improving the game and it shows in the latest patch notes.TL;DRA fun but very challenging and unorthodox RTS that is having its issues regularly addressed by the developers.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard game to recommend. If I were to score it an arbitrary value, I would give it a 6/10. Maybe 6.5, but that is pushing it. Be warned, if you get this game, you should consider save scumming a lot. I will detail why below, and I will be starting with the bad, and ending with a bit of good.My issues with the game stem from a bunch of small design decisions that add up to create a horribly frustrating experience. Stuff like pathing for all units being wonky as all hell, infantry always getting stuck in terrain, vehicles (both friendly and enemy) and each other, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ like having enemy 50 cal. emplacements knock out tank crew with said emplacement firing at the front of the tank. The problem is that these issues are consistent throughout the game and are infuriating to deal with because they lead to you losing squad members for no good reason, and the more squad members of any squad die, the less effective they become (even worse for tank crews, since as soon as 2 out of the 4 are dead, that tank may as well be worthless since it will never fire it's main gun after that point, and the only solution is to save scum to a previous point and hope this does not happen). This means that you're getting penalized by RNG and, quite frankly, bad game design that only ever affects you, the player, because the AI has unlimited resources to throw at you.You need to keep winning, but the enemy only needs to win once. And so, save scumming is a must (at least in my opinion).There are also bigger issues to consider: the player units, even when at maximum rank, do not feel like they are better than lower rank units at all. The game says that squads at higher ranks deal more damage and are more accurate, but there is quite literally no difference between a max rank sniper squad and a minimum rank one, nor is there any appreciable difference between maximum and minimum ranks for rifle squads, rockets, or tank commanders. The only upgrade that ever matters exists on only "Founder" type units, called "Survivalist", with the rest falling between absolutely worthless, like damage, HP and attack speed upgrades (this is because of the above issue with the ranks, if the squad is no better at a higher rank than a lower one, then what is the point of ranking up? Also, most "upgrades" are 10% increases in something, meaning that it ultimately doesn't matter for the bigger picture), or somewhat useful (Like Chameleon or Powerlifter, because they actually provide some sort of appreciable change to your units).The cover system does not feel good to engage with at all, it is not properly explained that buildings eventually lose walls and ceilings, thus making your infantry vulnerable even if they are technically still considered to be inside a "building", when in reality there are no more walls to separate the inside from the outside. What this does is make your infantry just stand in the open to get shot at, meaning that a lot of the time they'd be better off outside and prone on the ground.Another big problem is that units are supposed to be able to pick up special weapons off the ground to arm themselves with, but in practice this system is implemented in such an ass-backwards way that it's baffling. The reason why is because certain units need to have a slot for a weapon type, like a sniper rifle, light machine gun, rocket launcher, etc. In theory, this lets you upgrade your squad to be better in general, and it's supposed to be useful while fighting, so you can loot what your enemy has to be better at fighting in the moment. But for some reason, if you have a squad that has multiple slots open for the same weapon type, like snipers or rocket squads, and you want to pick up weapons for everyone in the squad that can carry them, the game does not let you - instead only one person is allowed to carry that gun, and that one person will go out to every single weapon you try to pick up, meaning that you can never fully upgrade any squad with multiple slots open slots for the same weapon types.Why is this a problem? Because other than the sniper squads, every single other squad can be upgraded to have the entire squad switch to a different primary weapon by switching out one weapon. One. Yet to do so for specialist squads, you need to play by these moronic rules that only serve to frustrate for no good reason.The last issue is with how the supply system works. For some reason, instead of just having "you have supplies for X number of days" and using a system where each supply has a charge that is consumed while travelling, the supplies are numbered in the hundreds of thousands... to do exactly what I just described. The money you get to buy supplies, weapons and other upgrades is similar in its stupidity, especially because if you want to use up all of your money to get as many supplies as possible, you can't, because you need to work with a slider that doesn't allow for precise number inputs for whatever reason.Another issue with the supply system is that rearming your units is needlessly tedious: you get access to supply vehicles that hold either ammunition or fuel, but while on the map screen, you can't draw from them, no matter how full they are, to resupply your army. Instead, you are forced to always draw from your incredibly precious general supplies that are used for travelling instead. Couple this with the fact that every new infantry squad and vehicle that joins your army adds to the drain of supplies, and you suddenly have an exponential explosion of supply consumption and the only way to get rid of that is to sell them off.DO NOT DISBAND. NEVER DISBAND. Disbanding does not reduce supply consumption! It only removes that troop from your active list so that it can be used later to replace losses! The only way to reduce consumption is by selling off whatever you do not need! Couple that with the fact that the only equipment you get to keep after a fight are only the vehicles you get our with, and NONE of the weapons lying on the ground, it means that at the start, there can be few opportunities to make more money, while later the game keeps showering you with extra manpower reserves that will forever eat away at your supplies because you can never get rid of them.So the supply system is incredibly ♥♥♥♥♥♥. My experience of playing on the Medium difficulty was of scrounging for every single enemy vehicle I could get my grubby hands on to immediately sell so I could by as many supplies as possible, only for those to be near immediately consumed. I would use up all of my money after pretty much every single mission. It is not fun to stress over not even being able to continue the campaign because of how ♥♥♥♥♥♥ this system is.So, what about the good? Well, this is only an RTS in the most basic definition of controlling units in real time. What this game actually resembles in practice is a real-time RPG where you get a bunch of units to control. And when (more importantly, if) it clicks, it feels good! Actually, if you've played Call to Arms: Gates of Hell, this game is similar to that, for both good and ill, but with a lot more pausing to issue emergency orders as you look at the ominous shells suspended in the air, hoping that they're not going to instantly wipe out squads when time is resumed. It requires a lot of scouting out, some planning, some occasional hail marry ideas, and it feels great to pull off. The unit variety is good too, even if the units themselves are horrible to control half the time. And you often have a lot more options in quite a few missions than you realize at first, so exploration of each map is paramount, though be warned that from the very start, missions can (and will) take multiple hours to complete. But honestly, other than the fact that you can pull off some mighty impressive heists and make off like a bandit in the amount of loot you can steal, that's about it for the good.

_childDocuments_.review: I was in the beta for this game and as such have had a decent amount of experience with it, and I can recommend it wholeheartedly. It fits a fun niche since it works as both an rts and as a Terminator game. The story is plenty compelling even if it operates int he Dark Fate timeline, you hit the story beats that one would expect from the future war. Mechanics wise there is a learning curve, the game is not easy and will punish you for your choices. That being said it adds to the experience because you are playing the plucky human resistance against eh ultimate AI enemy. The atmosphere is great, the campaign is expansive and has varied missions with enough paths and choices that you can get a good amount of replay-ability. The bad that does exist is the currently limited multiplayer, where there are only a few maps and modes as of right now (though the devs are looking to expand on this very soon). You can run into a problem where your tactics worked but the method results in loss several hours later, this is the learning curve, make sure you explore and pick your battles carefully. As for bugs, its a mixed bag,  I had bugs that couldn't be replicated or runs without bugs, or game breakers. A lot have been addressed and in the release version I have not had anything happen that wasnt fixed by reloading a checkpoint.The game is fun, but its not for everyone since it fits niche part of RTS, if you liked Syrian warfare you'll like this. If you like terminator you'll probable like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly a refreshing RTS experience at a reasonable price.Challenging even on normal difficulty, I recommend opting for Story or Normal mode even if you are experienced with RTS, anything higher demands near perfect tactics and game knowledge. Certain units are essentially irreplaceable and losing them can be very painful, so methodical play is a requirement.Campaign mode is the main attraction here. The story is okay, nothing truly memorable but it is intriguing enough to keep you listening in cut scenes. Game breaking bugs are present but relatively rare and as of this review a beta patch resolves many of them, the developer appears to be fairly engaged with the community in this regard and I personally have not encountered any in my play-through.Its biggest problems are QoL related and how poorly many aspects of game info are communicated to the player. _childDocuments_.review: If I could give this a neutral review it is what I would give this game. It doesn't deserve the thumbs down but it doesn't deserve a thumbs up either.I would like to start by saying I want to love this game, but as it is, I can only like its vision. There is genuine passion behind the development of this game, and it shows. Interesting characters, a multitude of units and equipment to use, and the sheer variety of options presented to you make this game something that should be highly replayable and enjoyable for hundreds of hours. But what I am about to present below is what destroys its potential in this regard.1. There is an utterly insane level of focus on micromanagement that genuinely makes my head hurt after just one or two missions. Resources and supplies are counted in the tens of thousands, and your army will be consuming at least 30k supplies a day after the third mission, assuming you managed to salvage as many vehicles as possible from that mission.2. Leaning off the above point, there is a stupid amount of work you need to do to keep units alive in this game. The game will throw multiple objectives at you, and to even get a passing grade that doesn't cripple you down the road requires Grand Master levels of micro on the players' part. Anyone less will require either cheesing the situation or sheer brute force to overcome.3. Continuing as another tangent of point #1, there is an incredibly accurate counter for all ammunition used by all units in your current mission, including allied units and (I am assuming) enemy units as well. So what's the problem? That is *every single unit on the map.* I admit I am playing on a very old PC, but I expect even newer hardware to suffer under the load of this game in the late game. There is simply too much to handle.4. Like most wargame-types before it, there is a certain level of RNG involved as to whether shots land or miss, and there is an impressive amount of extra variables that can contribute to success or failure. But again, this demands even more out of your PC and it makes certain hero missions fustrating to deal with without numerous reloads. Gods forbid if you bring your heroes (since they are just as squishy as any other unit you have) into regular missions without putting them into the heaviest armor you have--and that might not save them still. Unless you are utterly confident in your micro skills, save yourself the hassle.5. Leaning on quicksaves. Oh good heavens, I am a S.T.A.L.K.E.R. player and this game has beaten how often I hit F5 and F9 to quicksave/quickload. Because of the RNG system mentioned above sometimes you are just one bad roll away from getting utterly sodomized by the enemy, no matter how well you play your cards. The game would be far more enjoyable if you didn't end up staring at the loading screen so consistently just so you don't break your odds of success down the road.In closing, if the devs are reading this, I need to state this right now: your focus on detail is f*cking awesome but it is overkill for how many units you have to manage at the same time while pursuing multiple objectives. However, this hardcore attention to "realism" is crippling this game for the casual observer and the folks trying to enjoy their time outside of work, as well as their poor rigs that weren't built to NASA standards.I am still going to try to complete this game but I am unsure if I can fully complete this game without burning either myself or my PC to the ground in the process.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an amazing story driven RTS. It follows the early days of the resistance against "Legion" (skynet). The game is meant to provide "realistic" combat. If you dont make sure your troops are in cover then of course the game is going to be hard. If you just throw troops at the enemy and hope for the best then of course it is hard. You have to use the buildings, the land, your equipment, and your wits to win. Control the important parts of the map and ou wont get flanked. Raid into enemy territory to crush enemy arty and then pull back. Different tactics are needed for different missions. Do not be put off by the reviews talking about difficulty, it isnt that bad (for people saying "its hard when you play on hard" what did you expect? ITS HARD DIFFICULTY OF COURSE IT IS GOING TO BE HARD)If you are looking for a solid story driven RTS then you cannot go wrong with this (the minor RPG elements are a very nice touch)

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game.  Really challenging and janky though, but it's got a surprising amount of detail for whats basically a tie-in movie game.   Solid 7/10 for me.  Really love how you build up your army and they carry over to the next mission.  Making sure to keep your more important units alive.   Reminds me of Homeworld a bit.  Minus the unit-construction.   Really like how your army looks like a Mad Max military force by the end. Resource management is a challenge.  Too challenging actually.  I feel like they need to tweak it a bit.Gameplay is Real-Time Tactics.  Think Men of War, Call to Arms, or Syrian Warfare (both are running on the same engine).  DO NOT play this like a traditional RTS or you're in for a bad time.  Unit position is key.  Do not leave your infantry alone, support them with arty or vehicles as much as you can, if not, garrison them to give them better defenses.  Pay attention to what your units can do, it will help in the long run. Also, Artillery is king in this game.   Just be careful because as there is friendly-fire from artillery. Not a lot of content outside the campaign.  Skirmish mode it just four maps I think.  One of them being a defense/offense mode on a fortified underground base.  They'll either have to release more maps or release a map editor. Would love to see some sort of Dynamic free campaign mode.  The overworld maps just screams it. Game is set in the Dark Fate timeline instead of Skynet T1-T3, which is sort of a let down.  However, I would say this sorta gives them a lot more creative freedom.   I would've still preferred it set in the classic timeline.   Still, you get your classic Terminators to fight against.  All walking menacingly as they fire mini-guns or plasma guns at your forces.  Who knows, maybe it'll be a DLC.  Ending basically set up the creation of the Resistance.Oh yeah, you don't play as the Resistance, they haven't formed yet.  You actually don't just fight Legion, you fight other human groups.  From bandits to gangs and scavengers.   Kinda wish they toned that down, fighting other humans.  Was having more fun fighting against the Machines.  Most of the time, it actually feels like you're in the world of classic Terminator, especially once you get most of your forces using Plasma weaponry.  Until they mention "Legion" that you remember Skynet doesn't exist and this is a different timeline.  Still.  Like I mentioned before, it ain't that bad, you're still fighting robots.  Hope they plan on releasing campaign DLCs for this.   A Legion campaign is an obvious choice, but after seeing the ending, I hope we get a Resistance DLC.This game MUST have mod support.  Please.  There is so much potential here.  I never though I'd see a Real time tactics game set in Terminator, and here we are.

_childDocuments_.review: So the concept of this game is cool but there are some glaring issues that the devs NEED to address. Just to name a few, if you change your graphical settings the game crashes to desktop (every time) and will not save the settings you wanted. The game will crash at random intervals entirely of it's own accord (primarily in cut scenes), just played a 30 minute mission meticulously managing your forces' attack/defense strategy? Too bad, crash to desktop and restart the mission. This has happened three times now within three hours of playing. The audio in multiple cut scenes is either non-existent or plays sporadically cutting in and out leaving you feeling "un-immersed" and often times with questions as to what is happening and what you need to do going forward. Last point is that several missions leave out mission critical information that could lead to the success of said mission. One instance is a base defense mission where you need ammo, fuel, and drivers to supply those resources to the front line, (this is called logistics for people who don't know). Need an ammo truck? No indication as to where it is other than "hurry up and grab a resupply vehicle!" Need fuel? No indication as to where it is other than "hurry up and grab a fuel vehicle!" Need drivers to ferry the fuel and ammo back and forth? No indication where these drivers are at other than "we're sending you reinforcements!" It's not a matter of hand holding so much as it is just poor game design. I shouldn't have to drop everything I'm doing (and leave my soldiers undefended/wounded/dying) just to go on a "where's Waldo" adventure to find this driver to move supplies. As of the typing of this review, I'm currently trying to start a new mission where I need to select a "scouting squad" to commandeer a village/town and after selecting all of my forces the game literally will not let me advance beyond that screen, thus preventing me from playing the game. I'm assuming this is because I have wide screen monitor but it's 2024, all of these problems listed should be a non-issue, these are incredibly trivial problems to be having, get it fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super fun. Especially if you're into games like Men of War or any super tactical rts game. However, I can't recommend at this time because of the supply mechanic. After 50 hours, I am literally stuck in the campaign and can't advance any further because I don't have enough supplies to get to the next mission. Even if I disband all my forces, the settlement only sells 3 days of supplies, and the next destination requires 6 days. So, I am going to have to start the campaign over. Imagine going from having fun with sweet realistic battles with robots to having to start over because of logistics. It's just a huge let down in the middle of a fun game. So, until they come out with cheats, or the devs fix the supplies, I can't recommend. Which is a real shame.Edit: I've been meaning to come back to this for a while. It was really nice for the devs to respond with a solution to the issue I encountered, and it did solve the problem. So, hats off to them. HOWEVER, that solution came in the form of an update that was released the same day I posted my review. Before that, it was 100% possible to get stuck in the game and have to either hope you had a decent save from before the issue occurred or start over. The game was out for a month at that point and tons of people, even including streamers who had devs in their chats encountered the problem. The way the supplies was originally set up was a huge draw back to the game and restricted players to play the campaign in a certain way. That completely defeats the purpose of giving the player the choice of where they go next. In my opinion, they should have launched with a way to adjust supply consumption or cut it out of the game. Finally, to address the people dropping the stupid clown emoji on my review, grow up. Constructive feedback is essential for game design and in this case, it's clear that there was an actual problem that was not based solely on the skill of the players. Otherwise, they would have just said "get gud" instead of spending money and man hours to fix it.

_childDocuments_.review: Terminator: Dark Fate – Defiance (TDFD) is a much better game than I expected. The game is a semi-realistic war RTS with micromanagement and army management, including upgrading weapons, unit upkeep, and carrying over units from mission to mission similar to Panzer General. TDFD reminds me the most of Men of War (MoW) – if you liked MoW, you should definitely check out TDFD.The game contains a surprising amount of choices and narrative which is sometimes a bit too much in a short time, but overall better than expected. There are also various factions that you will interact with during the campaign. What is really great about this game is the mission design: no mission is like another. I also like that you often start missions with smaller units and have more reserves available later on in a mission. This way, even weaker units still have a purpose later in the game (e.g. Humvees) and you have to adapt your play style to the available units.The army management is important for the entire campaign because you have to supply your existing troops. You will start with some small units and probably finish the game with a large army. However, the more troops, the higher the upkeep. There are some units that are better than others, but these also cost more upkeep. I like the overall balancing of the different unit types and that there is no dominating uber-unit or uber-weapon. Regarding micromanagement, each unit has special abilities and different weapon ranges, as well as a limited number of soldiers, ammo, and fuel similar to Men of War but faaar less fiddly because in TDFD the smallest controllable unit is a squad. For me, this level of micromanagement is just right! Moreover, the game can be paused at any time to issue commands.The enemy AI is okay. It is mostly rather passive. The difficulty level is still quite high since you should avoid losses because unit reserves are finite. TDFD might not be for commanders who enjoy frontal attacks ala Command & Conquer. Though, avoiding losses may lead to many save/load sessions – I personally like playing this way, but it’s certainly not for everyone. Interestingly, the enemy’s field of vision and weapon ranges cannot be displayed. Rather unusual nowadays, but I liked it because I have to play the game more intuitively.I have only a few negative points: The lack of information in the GUI (e.g., no comparison of weapons you can pick up during a mission and that only the squad leader can pick up weapons) and the army administration screen between missions (e.g., fiddly when switching drivers for vehicles). The final mission was a bit lackluster. Finally, a few more different (graphical) environments as well as different units for the Terminator faction might be nice (for more variety).

_childDocuments_.review: I have finally managed to complete the campaign... in what was Story Mode.... as well as played around with the skirmish features so time for a review.I'll do a Pros and Cons, as that is usually the best way to do things and I'll start with Cons;CONS -1). The depth of the games story feels a bit shallow... more on this later.2). AI can on occasion have your guys running all over the shop/or at least on paths you wouldn't have chosen.3). Panning in and out feels restrictive and this game could definitely be improved with a tactical view mode such as Total War.4). Choices or paths you can take aren't always clear or just aren't offered. e.g. Nueva Tortuga... if you know, you know. Shout out to Costin Gaming for that one.5). Skirmish needs fleshing out. It seems to be going for the Steel Division - Capture the points kind of play, but this doesn't appear to influence the points you get in order to mount the pressure beyond most points captured wins. The maps are small 1v1's it needs to be up to 4v4 minimum with larger maps and different modes such as a destruction mode were it is based off points from the units you destroy on the enemy team. There is one 1v1 "Invasion Map", it's not great and gets stale as quickly as it sounds. These are the reason the Online Multiplayer is essentially none existent.6). No bunker warfare, no dogs, no skin walkers... I remember the original. So much map not explored.7). I had to turn the difficulty down, that made me feel less accomplished. Sneak to ambush people doesn't always work the best either... you are unlikely to bomb that passing tank.8). I want an original Terminator Time Line for this one.9). This game would also rock from being an RTS with base building. I know it's not meant to be.- Yeah, I'll stop here. I'm really scraping the bottom of the barrel with these last three.PROS -1). This game is SO immersive. From the beginning it really takes you on a journey, whether you like where that story takes you... well there are variations on the ending so far as I can tell. You will most likely save scum and I hate that, but for this, yeah I pressed on and it was enjoyable, like changing the past.2). Good graphics, not Warno - "that guy has a moustache" graphics, but they are good and probably better than is needed for your level of involvement. You do get to shoot at an Arial Hunter Kill from a Technical while it drives through the decimated streets.3). On that note, I LOVE the vehicles, especially The Movement stuff. The trailers... brilliant. 4). It left me wanting more. I want to know more about the factions, I want to see more of the rest of the world, I wanted to continue fighting until Skynet (I mean Legion) was smashed.5). Controls and UI are very nice, smooth, easy to take in the information and that is important when you are dealing with a hundred things at once.6). The music, needs more original sound track sure, but again amazing and draws you into that immersion. 7). Voice acting is on point. The dialogue can be both great and cheesy. It doesn't take itself too seriously. An Original Terminator story arc should though and it should make me cry.8). IT IS HARD and much like so many of the Great Games you enjoy losing despite how frustrating it can be. 9). Even the Campaign has replayabilty, how much I have to get back to you on. I haven't had a chance to play another "bad guy" campaign yet. 10). If you are looking for a HARD CORE challenge you will love the hardest difficulty. It is what fighting the Terminators would really be like. 11). Vehicle scrounging - You will pick the battlefield clean, probably spending more time on that than on mission. It gets really involved as does the trade and upgrading. My answer... If in doubt, ARTILLERY! 12). Coming back to pathing. This game is a tactical, meaning that micro management of your forces is key. The terrain effects the movement speed of some vehicles and vehicles will favour roads to move at their fastest as can be seen on their speedometer (yes, speedometer). If you aren't doing this, they will path through the way of least resistance rather than the directest route, which can be straight into the path of a Terminator Tank.Summary - This game is awesome. It is an RTT, you our limited in your numbers both by mechanics and through availability. Yes there are improvements that could be made, as with all games, and there is nothing to say that Slitherine won't be adding more features, vehicles, maps, new campaigns from the view point of other factions, new factions, updating skirmish and multiplayer... this game only released last month. Look at Stellaris, that's not even the same game that was originally released. I think the real question is, does this need doing straight away? Is it otherwise a broken game? NO, not at all. I just hope Slitherine put as much effort into this as they have say the development of Distant Worlds 2 (Or 1 would be a fair example).I don't often write a review so be sure that if things get worse, there is no development, I will be back and the thumbs up can just as easily become a thumbs down. Firm, firm but fair.

However it ain't gonna scratch a actual terminator but a 50. cal or anything thats an autocannon could put them in there place. Vehicles is pretty much no brainer, Does the autocannon damage? > yes > lawn mower them, Does the autocannon penetrate them? > no > use anything related to HEAT (High Explosive Anti-Tank) shells.There are 3 factions to choose from with there own play styles. Legion being a slow but sturdy robot faction, The Movement being mobile but squishy humans, and The Founders being humans with actual body armor, familiar military equipment, and vehicles.If new to the game and you're starting off the game into skirmish believe me you will get swiss cheesed cause many mechanic are reviled to you in the story campaign (which so far I like). I was one of those people that play skirmish first then play story later to get the feel of the game.Is this a good game? YESIs it bugging out? Haven"t found one yet so farIs it worth the price? I would say well worth*Future road map ideas*Would love to see maps with bigger team size and new factions or units.

_childDocuments_.review: What I like so far: The realistic mechanics governing combat. -Large caliber weapons have long ranges(compared to C&C where tanks shoot 30 yards)-Line of sightInfantry use smoke or environmental objects for cover.Infantry hiding in buildings can remain undetected to new units when they hold their fire, entering Ambush mode-Infantry get it doneVehicles are great support tools, but an equipped squad using cover will destroy most medium to light armor. (Remember Russia's early invasion of Ukraine? Sending a tank without Infantry support is a bad idea)-Vehicle mechanics/field repairsIf a vehicle, i.e Humvee takes an RPG hit to the side, odds are its going to blow out the tires and compromise the armor on the side it was hit. This is stuff you have to deal with in combat.-Call of Duty, Not Medal of HonorInfantry, tank crews, snipers, etc all work in teams and their effectivness lessens with caualties(duh!). No hero/commando/OP unit.-RPG elementsYou make choices in the story and on the field, that alter the gameplay for good or bad. Your crews level up. Tank crew, Rangers, mercenaries, etc. They gain experience and gain perks the more exp they get. You can rename them, and they stay with you forever(unless they die.)Your army can be upgraded with better weapons, vehicle mods, or armor if you can afford or trade for it.-ScavengingWhen you kill enemies in combat, if your crew has proficiency they can take abandoned enemy vehicles. If you kill a group of terminators, they will drop their plasma rifles on the ground and you can loot the weapons. Either equip them or sell them.-Finite resources(Logistics)*this is a mixed bag for most people* Nothing is infinite. Your Bradley can run out of TOWs, fuel, spare parts(repairs). Squads can deplete their 5.56mm, LAW, grenades, whatever. Setup resupply points for combat. Rotate troops and equipment.-Sound The sound effects are decent enough, but I REALLY appreciate the developer used the original plasma gunfire effects from Terminator 2.What I don't like:-You fight Legion, not Skynet-Unforgiving combatIt's pretty brutal at times in terms of difficulty.-Mission SuppliesNeeding supplies to make it to your next mission map destination. The concept is cool, but when it's just for the sake of a map screen, then it's tiresome and adds unnecessary extra steps of having to scavenge for stuff just click a point in the map.-Graphical Effects Envirmental detail is excellent. Units and models look great, but explosions and gunfire effects are just OK. If World in Conflict's effects are a solid 10, this game would be at a 5. Noting WiC came out in 2008.Plasma weapon effects don't look that great, and there's an issue where a Terminator will fire its weapon but the plasma bolts fire from 10 yards ahead of it. -Story/scriptIm only half-way through however the story isnt that compelling. The voice acting reminds me of Ace Combat, but flatter and more forced. We dont really have any emotional investment in the main character or his allies. I feel more loss for my Ranger squad that survived 5 missions, only to die in an ambush I could have avoided. Overall, Its fun enough for $35.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely one of the most unique RTS games I have played in a long time. There is a strong focus on RPG elements during some of the missions with exploration and dialogue, as well as branching mission choices that let you do missions in different ways. I really liked that aspect of the campaign.All of the vehicle and unit models are great, and there is a large variety of choices for different units you can make. Want to keep some classic US military hardware like the Abrams and Bradley with a bunch of US Rangers? You can do that. Want to Terminator 2 it up and just have a bunch of technicals and vans with guns on them with some hard pressed militia? You can do that too.The supply management and army management are really fun to mess around with. Prior to the latest beta patch supply consumption was extremely harsh, but they changed it to be a little more reasonable. I also went 1/3rd of the campaign realizing I could trade good will points for supplies, and trade my vehicles in for good will points. I was just scrapping vehicles I couldn't afford and that's a big mistake.The game's horrible RNG is one downside, and it does require a lot of quick saving to get through unless you just want to lose all of your troops every mission. Considering you need to have veteran troops to even stand a chance against the terminators, you'll need to do your utmost to keep your core units alive each mission. When infantry are down to a few squad members, retreat them out of the line of battle and hide them.The closest game I can compare this to is Syrian Warfare, and I think the devs for that worked on this initially before it was taken over by Slitherine in house. It's definitely a more unique RTS, and it may not be for everyone, but I did fully enjoy both the RTS game play and the mechanics in it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has great ideas and potential, just not executed well and need some number adjustments.There's too much rng in the combat, sometimes long reloading anti tank homing missiles just randomly miss without smoke cover, it can literally be life or death of the unit.I had 2 sniper squads shooting each other across rooftops till they ran out of ammo, and did zero dmg and took zero dmg.The defence missions are fun but the offense missions are usually not, especially when you gotta tackle an entrenched position with enemies of every weapon type and artillery in a hard to reach position, feels like you're sending troops into a meat grinder and pray to rng god that they don't randomly die in a smoke.The campaign supply mechanic is frustrating, having to scrap or sell off 1/3 of your army after every mission just feels really bad.Wait for some balance changesEdit: finished the campaign after the supply mechanic nerf, felt much better being able to have multiple tanks and bradleys. But the campaign story feels rushed and unfinished, character motivations are questionable, people hating on you for no reason, and people go 180 on their character out of nowhere. The final mission doesn't feel like anything was concluded, its like the dev just ran out of time or money and says oh well this is the last mission. The last mission map was clearly pushing the game engine to the limits, Im running 4080 rtx i7-12700K   3.61 GHz and the entire mission was running around 10fps. The third mission in the campaign, Haven base defense was the probably the best mission, if the game sticked to smaller scale base defenses, this game would've been amazing. But as it stands, the multiplayer/skirmish is barebones with 4 maps, majority of the campaign missions were mediocre with few fun missions inbetween.

_childDocuments_.review: When I played the demo for this game, I was hooked. I was hooked so much that the moment the demo ended I immediately bought Syrian Warfare just to scratch the itch that waiting for this game made me feel. The fact that the demo cuts off immediately after giving you a taste of the persistent unit mechanics was absolutely genius marketing.Unfortunately, reality doesn't mix well with expectations, and it was a sobering experience.First thing's first: For the price point the game is good. It is not very well polished, units get stuck on terrain, mission scripting can go insane at times, but it's unique and topical enough with good enough mechanics that I am satisfied with my purchase. You get what's on the tin: An RTS game set in the Terminator universe, complete with online skirmish modes and a whole single-player campaign. The rest of this is just going to be nit-picks of things that I found particularly jarring so other people can know what it is they'll be getting into:Dynamic campaign: The game features a "free-form" campaign where you make decisions during missions that affect the outcome of character arcs and stories. This is great because it adds a role-playing element to things, and characters that survive in missions will remain active as the story progresses. All of your units level up, they remain consistent as the game goes forward (assuming they survive) and you can equip them with different weapons, and upgrade your vehicles with various modules. It's very cool.The issue however is the resource mechanic: Supplies and "Goodwill Points." Goodwill points act as your currency, and they're what you use to buy upgrades, supplies, and more men for your army. Supplies on the other hand are what you use to navigate the world map, and are by-far the most frustrating aspect of the game's campaign. You get supplies by doing missions, and these missions only ever give you enough supplies to go to the next mission location. This is frustrating simply because of the amount of locations there are to go and the ways you can interact with them. You can purchase supplies for Goodwill points, but the amount of supplies you get per point spent barely covers the cost of one day's trip in most cases, and that's after spending the maximum amount of supplies. Also, the size of your army and the vehicles in it play into the draw on your available supplies, so you are expected to maintain a small army at most times in order to keep from burning through your supplies. There are very few ways to organically earn supplies and goodwill points outside of the missions, none of which are randomly generated, and all follow a determined canonical path. It's frustrating at best, and very cumbersome at worst.Gameplay: If you've played Syrian Warfare, then you know what to expect: The game is a "realistic" RTS where firefights result in high amounts of casualties extremely quickly, and there is no way to reinforce lost squad members to a unit while it is still in the mission. The main issue I had with Syrian Warfare is that the game's UI simply did not compliment the speed at which the game happened, which meant that I was constantly slapping space-bar ever second or so just so I could make sure that every squad I had was doing exactly what I needed it to do at any given moment, and what was worse was the fact that the game did not even have a unit quick-select bar like Company of Heroes. Fortunately, not only does Terminator: Dark Fate - Defiance keep the active pause mechanic, but it also added a unit hot-bar, so managing your soldiers during high-lethality situations is a lot less frustrating, but not entirely curbed.Mission Design: I give the mission design props for being incredibly ballsy, most of the time they play out more like a session from a tabletop campaign than a typical RTS mission (please for the love of god I want RTS games to add more tools to turn them into tabletop role-playing modules I'm begging you), with various decisions you can make, optional objectives that can help or hinder you in one way or the other, and even faction politics that you can juggle around before the mission ends. The execution of these missions can range from inspiring to absolutely mind-meltingly confusing, the most notable example being the first mission you do against "The Cartel," where you infiltrate one of their main settlements in order to start a slave uprising. An entire portion of this mission is dedicated to save-scumming until you can RNG the outcome of a pitched battle between one of your squads and an enemy's squad, of which you don't get to control your squad, and if your squad dies then it's a game over. It's ludicrous, and my squad died 5 out of 6 attempts on Normal mode, and that was with all the possible weapon upgrades I could've gotten for them before the fight; I can't imagine how many attempts it'd take on the harder difficulties.
