_childDocuments_.review: Ever played a  game where all the mechanics are unfairly rigged against the player and in favor of the bots? Unfortunately that is the case for this game where you are punished for everything you do in this game because the balancing is rigged against you as the player.Want to do the next mission? Sorry but it appears when you went to the store, you did not realize you were not given enough supplies to make it to the next location. Looks like you need to reload the game to an earlier save because you were suppose to spend your resources on supplies.Want to save people or salvage vehicles?Every person you save is going to cost you a fortune to keep in reserve, and salvaging doesn't remotely repay you for the cost of traveling with the vehicle. Don't worry though, those supplies are just thrown out the window since it's not spent on refueling, arming, or healing you at all.Want to fight the enemy?Well since you are the attacker, all enemies are invisible by default by the "hidden" mechanic so you won't see unmoving enemies until you are already being shot at or right in their face.I heard you like fog of war, so we added fog of war to every enemy unit on top of your standard fog of war.Want to enjoy the game?No, this is a RTS where you play how they want you to play the game. All missions tell you what units you're allowed to bring, limit how many you can bring, or deny certain units for arbitrary reasons to make the game more difficult for you.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people are comparing this to C&C or COH, but it's not even close except that it's a RTS.  To be fair  to those who are thinking of buying this game it is not even close to COC or COH because there is not base building.  This falls more in line with Commandos in that you have limited resources at every mission.  You can't just throw all your infantry into the melee like a modern day Russian assault on Ukraine because unlike Russia you actually need your troops.  I DO like the graphics, the sound, the carrying over of experienced units, but it's hard for me because I hate pausing the game to plan out my attack and hope it works then restart after I just played the map for an hour and try again.  Just not my thing, but some of you may like it.

Then again smash them into the HQ where they have a unholy amount of artillery that somehow can see me when I cant see them without the enemy having eyes on me. _childDocuments_.review: Make sure to do a bit of research before jumping straight into the game, because this game might very well not be what you might expect from the first glance. Instead of a RTS in the style of Command & Conquer Generals, it is closer to WW2 games like Close Combat in terms of mechanics. The mission design on the other hand is very narrative driven with branching missions and tons of optional objectives and paths to victory, at least in the first half of the game I'Ve played thus far.  While I do consider these traits to mostly good, it is nevertheless quite rough around the edges. While it might still need some finetuning, I most certainly can admire how the devs did not play it safe.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very frustrating game, playing on Realistic difficulty is "tear your hair out" experience. But playing it other than "realistic" does not sit well with me.A game that requires you to save and re-load a save every few minutes. Make a micro gains, quick save and repeat.Weapons here are very deadly and It's very easy to lose your entire force in 2-3 minutes. So rush does not help. Units consume ammo. Infantry can not be reinforced during missions. Enemy AI love fighting from buildings so every urban area is you doing some careful maneuvering and taking building by building. Urban maps are Bakhmut like experience. Overall it's a pretty great "hardcore" RTS set in Terminator universe.- At the time of writing this, all content of the game is in Campaign, a very long one. - Only 4 skirmish maps, which you can play vs AI. Skirmish is just plain old control the flags (Domination).- Campaign has a proper story, voice acting, missions and overall a dark approach to settings. It's pretty good and immersive. A map has a main mission with side missions, side missions give you additional units. So it's worth completing them. Some maps have mini choices that just a bit affect your story, but it's light and nothing critical. Still cool.- Map design is excellent and overall game's visuals are very good. - Music, voices, weapon sounds are very good.   - Between missions you have to manage your units and resources. Overall your army needs supplies to move between locations on global map. The same supplies are also used to buy fuel, ammo, repair. So you have to balance them. Without enough supplies you can't progress on Global Map (reach next mission). - Units can be bought and sold, better weapons and armor can be equipped.- At the end of each mission you are free to take all empty vehicles if you have enough crew. These vehicles can be later sold on the market for money.- No base building, just pool of units you can call in, so reduce your loses or you gonna be stuck in further missions.Problems:- Line of Sight is bugged, your units will sometime not see the enemy, until that enemy starts shooting and enemy is very accurate. One-shot your vehicles and units all the time. There is no way to recon. So you are left with: Quick save, send units forward, lose your units, see where enemy is, quick load and act accordingly.- Supplies issue, you don't get enough of them and when you are forced to sell good chunk of your forces in order to save on your supplies gives a dull experience. Collecting all those cool and better units, only to be forced to sell them because you don't have enough supplies to reach the next mission. - Only 4 skirmish maps, but devs mentioned about adding more in future. Remains to be seen.- Legion instead of Skynet. Devs should have stayed with original Terminator universe/timeline. If you played and liked Syrian Warfare then it's basically the same gameplay here. Just with much better visuals.  I like it, even though after playing it for 31 hours I still haven't finished the campaign. The missions are loong. Losing more than 2 hours on completing just one mission is a norm. Probably on easier difficulties it's much faster. But yeah i like and hate it at the same time.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Very very buggy. game breaking buggy. Current state is a 5.5 out of 10 with a potential for 8/10BUGS- Pathing:   * units get stuck in building and environment which is game breaking because you need to      extract everyone at the end of every mission.  * maybe not a bug but very frustrating is that you need to issue move commands in small increments and babysit your troops as they move because they tend to follow random paths and the supply trucks and some other units usually separate from their escorts and get themselves killed for anything more than a screen size length of movement in a single command.- Units refuse to move. at all. as if the game was paused. (reloading helped)- Mission Triggers don't work:    # get the truck to the location. what truck, what location? (read fix below)   # here are more reinforcements. what reinforcements ?These are just the ones that I experienced. I could not finish the game because of the bugs above. which was especially frustrating as the bug that got to me was at the very end of the game (I think it was the end)(EDIT: I did finish the game since I wrote the review originally. Just take every supply truck you have to the <?> marker and one of them will trigger the endgame cutscene)PERFORMANCEumm.. 15-20 FPS on low settings on a 3070 M15 laptop while only using 30% of the GPU means this game is very unoptimised.[EDIT]: my 4090 PC cand pull 60-100 fps but again, only uses 20% GPU and 5% CPU.I heard the game is single CPU core and it may bottleneck the GPU. Expect terrible performance when you bring your entire force on the map. Somehow it feels like more than that (or I just got used to it) but the FPS counter doeasn't lie.GOOD - specialised infantry: rangers, snipers, atgm squads, light and heavy infantry, mercenaries, etc - logistics, both on map with ammo management and supply and fuel trucks and off map between missions- inventory for every unit and tank, you can customise every squad's loadout between missions and to a limited degree during missions.- skills that transform units completely, keep your people alive and they will become very powerful- stealth, - modular health on tanks, guns, engine, etc have their own health pools.etc.BAD- artillery is useless and SO expensive. also bugged. the HIMARS decided to move across the map to get line of sight and got itself killed while I was microing another battle. regular artillery DOES NOT DO SPLASH DMG. it can land next to you and you'll be just fine. - small platforms are useless. (large non artillery platforms are OK for defence)- planes/heli are extra useless and cannot be repaired- supply needs balancing. Personally, I'd probably remove the map supply entirely and just use it for rearming between missions.- AI allies steal your vehicles if you leave them unmanned. there are a lot of reasons why you would leave vehicles unmanned and you wouldn't want the AI to steal all your plasma technicals or your atgm hummers while you scout ahead..- armour plates seem pointless. they add some initial HP but cannot be restored..- five multiplayer maps.- short campaign. ADVICE (as in, please add this to the game)- Dynamic campaign. DEVS, please check out Ostfront Conquest Mode on how to do more with less.- Game needs coop. yes coop. Give some of your forces to a friend and work together. Fun factor x3000- more content. Legion/Skynet campaigns. Longer founders campaign.- more units. - some common sense changes such as    * dont allow units to waste ATGM in smoke    * pop smoke if you get incoming ATGMs, Enemy AI drops smoke the instant the ATGM      fires, and I think friendly AI should do the same, especially when you're microing on the      other side of the map.   * allow weapon collecting instead of swapping. for example when one of your snipers die      they drop their rifle and you cannot pick it up, you can only swap it with another rifle. It      discourages you from equiping your soldiers with the best gear..Good luck!

_childDocuments_.review: The game has its fun points, and has potential, but there is some significant tweaks needed to the supply system. Any improvement in your units rapidly drives up the supply cost... and higher supply cost forces you to have fewer units. In fact, the game will force you to give up hard-won units, just to make it to the next area. Its obvious the developer wants it to feel like you're constantly scraping by and having to scrounge desperately to keep some semblance of an army going... but the current implementation of the supply mechanic... something which punishes you for making progress... just isn't fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I gotta say I love it. I have not been so engrossed into the subtleties of a tactical game since the Close Combat era. It combines successfully (in my opinion) the small unit tactics of Company of Heroes, the theme I absolutely love, the realistic engagement scale and setting of CC4 - what a treat! The factions play very differently, each with their strengths and drawback, the resource system (at least in skirmish/mp) is really cool, allowing for timed pushes without detracting from the combat part and allowing you to preplan properly, the pace is great. It's hard to keep track of multiple fronts engagements, esp vs the AI who is able to evaluate and act on all of them at once, but the units left to their own are pretty smart about how to engage and you can always pull back a bit into cover on one front and focus on progressing on the otehr. The pace being relatively slow, it requires preplanning and does not rely on micromanaging units (thankful for that since my apm is no longer holding up if it ever has) - so you choose a plan and try to stick with it, if you want to win, switching strategies mid battle it pretty hard, esp on 20 min skirmishes. As a con, I found the solo campaign a bit tedious, with some sloppy mission trigger work (although I understand that it's for realism's sake, in some cases) and I didnt' progress to far through it so far, but really enjoying the skirmishes and looking forward to some actual pvp once my friends start picking it up. All in all worth a buy! Thanks Slitherine !

I get major framedrop and unstable image. This is due to the fact that the game AMAZINGLY in 2024 used only 1 CPU core. Yes! ... _childDocuments_.review: Edited Final: After finishing the game, its about 40 hours of fun and pain, let me explain. The fun aspect to it is that the game does add a bit of challenge to it, even on its easiest mode. Controls feel smooth and do enjoy the different mechanics they have with needing the correct skills to use certain vehicles, if a squad member is dead then your squad is unable to use whatever weapon the dead member was assigned, and the realism of needing to manage supplies ammo and fuel. The not so fun side to it now. The game as mentioned is rather challenging and could be a real turn away from newer players to the RTS genres, even on its easiest mode, I too found myself needing to restart due to a vital error in the start of the mission. whether that be the loss of a squad or just not bringing the correct troops. (the game does not let you know if you have messed up, it kinda lets you figure that out when you're near the end and you cant make a final push because you don't have ammo or all your men with the skills you need are dead from a previous mission). The game does need some optimizing as well. found myself playing a powerpoint as some parts through the game due to how choppy the frames were getting, maybe its just my computer ill never know since i finished the game and probably wont touch this game again. And with that it brings me to my final point, The game lacks replay-ability, once your done thats kinda just it, there is no multiplayer (there is, its just dead) and the skirmish modes are... bland to say the least. Is the game fun, yes. Do I feel this is worth the buy... Yes, but barely. at the end of the day, I got almost 40 hours of entertainment for $40... I'd give it a 6/10 Maybe this may just be me, but i do miss the base building RTS games like before and really wish they went with that style, but none the less I did enjoy the game

The core game play loop rewards fighting hard to keep units around, so why do I hold the highway to Albuquerque then all of a sudden have to live off of two squads and a ragtag force? plot reasons, why did I have to pay to bring my whole army? Don't know yet, PLEASE less staged things, let me use the force that told me to give you a positive review. _childDocuments_.review: Yes. Mostly. Maybe. But not for full price. on Normal difficulty.* Related controversy: * Publisher doesn't inform who the real developer is. However, the game's end credits show this: The most severe gripe with the game, is that . And this will bottleneck the frame rate severely, and create atrocious loading times. On my system it uses 1 single core at 100% all the time – meaning it’s only using 1/12 of available CPU resources. As a result, I have 30-40 fps on my RTX 4070 SUPER.- Good ol' fashioned instant RTS action. It reminds me a lot of Ground Control (2000).- No base building, just your units and the enemy.- Good variation in unit types, with lots of upgrades and weapons for each type- Maps are mostly well designed, and fairly large.- Maps, landscapes, and units have pretty decent 3D models, but it doesn’t really matter because you cannot zoom far enough in to notice.- Decent voice actors (but horrible acting, tbh)- It’s a lot of fun to watch enemies being hammered by your Bradley’s plasma miniguns, while 155mm airbursts rain down over enemy positions. And watching the TOW missiles creep along the landscape while closing in on their target never gets old.- The story/dialogue is extremely tedious, with a lot of poorly timed dialogue interruptions (suddenly pauses the gameplay). In the end you just want it all to go away, so you start pressing ESC immediately whenever something pops up.- The story dialogue and plot is so dumb and naïve, it might have been written by one of the developers’ kids, I guess. And it goes on foreeeeeeever… jeez.- Super annoying generic soundtrack consisting of techno-pop with fuzzy guitars.- Sound controls only have… 10 steps on each slider. Yup. So you end up on 1st step, and then having to reduce volume in Windows because the devs don’t understand that volume controls need to be logarithmic – and need finer control than 10 steps lol.- Very poor “AI” - it’s literally non-existent. Both for your units and the enemy. Everything simply walks in a straight line into deadly fire.- Very poor unit pathfinding. Sometimes the vehicles will follow roads. But not always. Or when they do follow it, they drive juuuust outside the road surface, making it drive super slowly.- Units do not take cover behind structures, or in the landscape. I’m sure the game tutorial says they actually do, but I’m fairly confident they do not. The 3D models never move when taking fire, and simply stand there. Some units (snipers) will go prone when taking fire, and that’s it.- Army configuration screen… Oh dear. It’s so bad it’s infuriating at times. Scrolling up and down and up and down in the list of units, trying to find that single maxed out squad you so desperately want to use as drivers on a vehicle… Sigh.- Army configuration screen… Good luck clicking that 1 pixel wide scroll bar when you want to actually use it.- No control over formations when grouping units together. And if you move a group of vehicles together by simply clicking in the landscape, they all retain their relative position, with units sometimes ending up in ridiculous places – like at the map edge where you can’t see them.- Extremely poor performance due to game only using a single thread/core. See above.The list of cons could go on forever, tbh. It’s not a great game.But it’s fun for some casual RTS action.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome setting,Some military realism,And plenty of micro management for my taste.If you liked the Men of War games, you will most likely like this too.I love micro management games and this is no exception. You are constantly looking into the little world of each unit or squad and trying to squeeze as much performance out of them as you can. So many other are RTS games are just about maximizing resource output and defeating your enemy with brute force and/or attrition. But Terminator: Dark Fate is more about guerilla tactics, like setting up an ambush, or luring troops from a battle and then stealing (or recovering) equipment.It also has some military realism, in the sense that you need to think about the logistics of a battle, like setting up FOBs to supply troops that retreated, or thinking about what types of ammunition to use and what to save for certain engagements, for example there are HEAT rounds and AP rounds. And then, not every rifle in the game uses "rifle ammo" but uses 7.62 or .308,Also, just like Aliens: Dark Descent, I only vaguely remember the movies because I saw them as a kid. But Aliens and Terminator were both made into solid RTS games, that can easily hold up on their own without needing to see the movies.
_childDocuments_.name: Terminator: Dark Fate - Defiance

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the campaign 30-40 minutes ago. It was a tough bout'. Won't spoil anyone for the story and what happens, but it definitely has an open ending and has a "cliffhanger" so to speak.All of the missions were largely solid, though a few stand out as very problematic:-> Cartel Mission (Infiltration). Very tedious and a lot of downtime & back and forth. You can cheese it immensely with C4 charges but I'm not sure this was the intended way to beat it by the devs. Suggest reducing the downtime by simply giving a faster vehicle and give more rebel reinforcements.-> Integrator Side/Bonus Mission. Again, won't spoil anything BUT please reduce the amount of Legion spawns in that mission. It's way too much and the only way to adequately beat it is with cheese. Also some of the story make up of that mission doesn't make sense. Also please remove the mines or provide a way to adequate -detect- and -remove- mines.Those are the only two missions I've had the biggest issues with due to the mechanics not being fleshed out. Now for some genuine feedback:1) Campaign is awesome. I love the setup and I love the liberties you guys have taken with it. It's really suiting the style and the universe. The mission variety is solid and fun. I half-expected the campaign to end in the Oklahoma mission. Real good stakes and setup.2) The music is superb (albeit in some cases repetitive).3) The atmosphere is solid and the traversal on the campaign map is solid. Takes a bit of thought. You don't really need to have a massive army, but a specialised one with veterans. Keeping people alive with veterancy has proven much more useful than more units.4) The combat is solid, however while I'm aware of the RNG aspects for accuracy, there isn't a lot of information present in the game. How much damage is being done by what weapons and so forth. No need for numbers, just 'low/medium/heavy' and subsequent references to armor. A lot of the stuff is basic knowledge if you have army knowledge and gun knowledge IRL, but it should still be properly descriptive for everyone.5) Actual game mechanics are legit awesome. The ammo/fuel/specific damage and repair is superb. The ability to scavenge the map before leaving is amazing.7) Allow to gather dropped weapons either by Supply Truck or by Technicians. I've missed so many upgrades just because of the rudimentary mechanic of not having the right unit to actually pick up the weapon.8) Add more bonus areas and missions in the Campaign map. That could be something to be done with future DLC but having more additions there as areas for you to explore and grind some resources/fight the machines, would be awesome.9) To have an option that shows all range indicators for weapons constantly (not on the minimap but in the actual game). I know when you however over a weapon-type you can see them even in the open world, but they are vague and you have to hover on the weapon.10) Introduce a Supremacy mode similar to Battlesector. It's going to help for the longevity of the game.11) Expand on the factions and make some playable. (Skirmish) Integrators as one. Also please introduce more integrator vehicles as they are barely touched and used if you don't snipe/flame up the crew/vehicle.12) This obviously goes to the above but add more maps and more modes.13) Map editing and potential mod support will help greatly with the longevity of the game.Those are the main points that I wanted to share with both the Devs and the other folks that bought and are still playing the game.The game overall is very solid and I found it really enjoyable. Will take a bit of a break to play something else (Pacific Drive :>), but I am definitely planning on getting back to it with a higher difficulty campaign, in the coming weeks. It's really a hidden gem and a really well done RTS in the Terminator universe.Has a similar vibe akin to Terminator: Resistance, which is a big plus. Overall, I'd give it a 8/10. Some improvements need to be made and some additions, but what's there really works and it's really awesome.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a hard call, imagine trying to impress your spouse with a romantic dinner following a Gordon Ramsey recipe, but all the ingredients are from a dollar store.  THAT is Terminator: Dark Fate. It's got good ideas, but they are half baked into the game.For example:1- Units can pick up weapon types assigned to them, but have no access to an inventory system during battle. Which means if someone in said unit dies, you lose the weapon. Someone can 'technically' replace him and use the weapon, but this isn't viable to sniper squads or any squads where almost everyone has a unique weapon type. Also in battle, you can't pick up and store any guns, which makes purchasing them somewhat pointless unless you constantly save scum for a deathless run.2- The building cover system is great in some aspects in that it has physics based damage, but thats about it. Infantry don't try to avoid exposed areas on their own, the building still indicates itself as a 'strong' building even though all of its wall parts are blown off, and infantry pathing in the building is a serious pain. You see, when infantry enter buildings they take forever to run to a designated spot to shoot from. This is especially true for big buildings, and all the while they are running slowly to get in position the enemy can blast away at the building. Another issue with this is when you tell in infantry squad to 'assault' a building, which is to go inside and melee any enemy to death. Yes, MELEE, while the enemy inside shoots your guys with their guns. This can be extremely annoying on buildings with open interiors like the prison.3- The terrible spawns. So many missions where your units literally spawn right in front of enemies, or enemies being to close to friendly spawn areas. This enforces save scumming, and even trying to figure out script timings so you can take out enemy units by making use of some of the wonky script timings for events and mission objectives.4- Lack of cover. Infantry can only be inside a building for protection. Outside, you can either lie down or pop smoke grenades but still take big casualties. I don't know why they didn't think of buildable foxholes or trenches/sandbags. This also applies for buildings too. They should have added an option to patch gaps and holes in buildings with furniture or something. At least that way, buidlings can be reusable to some extent. Theres heavy emphasis on vehicle use, but infantry plays a big role in battles. But they are severely limited do to being overly squishy and exposed.5- Infantry weapon loadout is unaccesible in battle. Other than checking their ammo, it won't have a convenient indicator on what weapon your units are using in battle. Also, if a unit uses 2 of the same weapon types, for example the sniper or rpg units, they will only pick up 1 weapon instead of 2. So even if you have a empty slot for a unit, they wont pick it up for the guy thats lacking the weapon. But instead swap it with the guy that already has something instead. The lack of weapon control for infantry during battle is a huge pain, especially since you can buy/sell guns.As i said before, they had the formula for something amazing. But most features weren't utilized to its fullest potential and instead has the feeling of  being slapped on at the last minute.

_childDocuments_.review: On a mission where i need to get npc trucks from point A  to point B then back to point A. During this mission you defend point B while survivors trickle out of the building. The game makes a point of not telling you how many will come out or when this will come out. (Something a long the lines of "we don't know how many are in there or how long it will take them to come out,") After a while I send my soldiers to defend the trucks while they get back to point A. The game tells me i took too long and its game over, mission failed. Keep in mind the game didn't stress the fact the trucks need to get there quickly or you will fail. It does not give you a timer or any indication you need to hurry, it just randomly ends the mission and tells you mission  failed. OK whatever, a LOT of this game is having to reload saves because you failed an objective the game didn't warn you about or you cant prepare for unless you've reloaded and know whats coming. I go back 30 minutes and do everything to make sure i send the trucks back the second they are done their objective so i don't run out the invisible clock and fail again. Every thing goes quick and smoothly but the game fails me again. Invisible clock ran out apparently. So i reload from an hour ago and do everything i can to make sure no time is wasted. I'm there the second the objective is available and gone the second its done. After basically redoing the mission perfectly the game still fails me as im about to finish since the invisible clock ran out. Do i want to waste another hour and redo the mission again just to risk the invisible clock auto failing me? Does it even matter if the actual game is good or bad when these awful decisions from the Devs stop me from progressing? Who though putting an invisible timer to fail the mission that dosn't have any correlation to the story was a good idea? Did they think that was fun? "Oh you failed the hour and a half long mission because of something you had no way of knowing about, and that will fail you again randomly during your next try. Aren't you glad you get to possibly waste another hour and a half redoing the mission? The cherry on the top is during the beginning of the mission you have to help protect some kids from legion. During my first attempt i failed because they just died within 4 seconds right in front of me the moment the event started. So i had to restart the mission with a team who had smokes, pre-smoke the area they will spawn in before the event starts so they don't just get melted and the game hard fails me. Perfect example of the game making it literally impossible to progress without having to restart with knowledge you can only get from the game failing you and making you restart. In my 21 hours of gameplay probably 10 of them are actual progress while the other 11 are just restarting the same missions since the game failed you due to things out of your control, or you had no knowledge to properly prepare for. The balance, controls, units all that stuff is decent but the devs did a VERY good job of making sure you wont enjoy your time playing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent strategy game! Honestly I was expecting a passable product merely cashing in on the Terminator name, but I was completely blown away.Top praise must go to the immense detail - buildings have interiors (not just "garrisoned vs. not garrisoned", projectiles are fully modelled, the environment takes damage (so a building with one side bombed out will be unsafe... from that one side), squads have multiple soldiers with different weapons, you can tell gunners to pop in and out of the hatch... It's just an endless realm of possibility.The rest of the game is good too - absolutely top-notch graphics, fun music, simple but capable storyline, solid voice acting (lots of highly situational voice lines for different units!).It's true, some aspects of the game need polish - it doesn't always explain things, and some missions pull surprises that aren't really fair. Nonetheless, this is the most enjoyable strategy game I've played in a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game's engine shines as the best RTS game engine to date IMO. Guided missiles look and track like a guided missile and not arrow like in other RTS games. Units storm and occupy buildings in realistic ways and buildings have various stages of integrity. The game's difficulty is increased by having to manage resources like ammo, gas, and spare parts to repair your vehicles. The campaign is decent length, pretty well written, challenging and engaging. Highly recommend this to all RTS fans. Bonus if you're a fan of the Terminator series.
_childDocuments_.name: Terminator: Dark Fate - Defiance

_childDocuments_.review: A challenging if not a little buggy RTS that I very much enjoyed. I really hope that Slitherine gives it the Battlestar Galactica: Deadlock treatment and does a few expansions and QoL passes. Personally I would like: a Roguelike/lite mode where it is semi-endless, New equipment (Legion plasma artillery cannon that can be mounted on Founder/Movement Artillery) New units (If the Terminators get more advanced Rev models and the Humans get a prototype of the cyber augments)also I saw people complaining about it being set in the Dark Fate timeline and they clearly don't remember Salvation or Genisys lmao there was far worse films it could have been based off of.
_childDocuments_.name: Terminator: Dark Fate - Defiance

_childDocuments_.review: Great game that sits alongside the greats like Men of War while improving upon them. Yes it will be difficult, and yes it is janky at times, but it will scratch that itch. You know the one.  This game is all about positioning and vision.  Have spotters up the front to let your machine guns and tanks fire from out of view. Have artillery support your frontal push. The terminators are powerful but short range and you need to use that to your advantage. Amazing singleplayer campaign where your strategy matters long term - you keep troops between fights. Losing a tank can be a huge loss, so do you sacrifice a humvee and a squad of infantry to help it escape? Choices like that I love.
_childDocuments_.name: Terminator: Dark Fate - Defiance

_childDocuments_.review: I don't do a lot of reviews, but this game deserves your attention. For any kid who grew up watching T1/T2 and wanted to see more of the 'future war' scenes with Reese and John Connor leading the Resistance, here it is - and you're in control. So far, totally impressed. I've played C&C, CoH, SC, Warner, and this RTS is more engaging then anything I've played. There's a true sense of survival and wanting to protect your troops. They persist (or don't) from mission to mission, so you're constantly evaluating risk/reward choices on your tactics. Replay factor is already off the chart as I've restarted several missions to try and get better results. Active pause is pretty cool. When things get hectic you can pause to queue up move orders etc. to respond to the dynamic battle.By the way, while set in the Dark Fate universe (which I despise, Terminator ended with T2), this really feels like the 'future war' that Reese told about. Loving it so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Terminator: Dark Fate - Defiance

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying that I actually really like this game, however I cannot recommend it in the current state.I love many of the game concepts surrounding building and supplying your own squad, including salvaging abandoned vehicles (some of which I forced the crew to run away because I set it on fire) but it is quite disheartening to see it immediately explode in the next mission from literally nowhere.You could order your vehicle into an open field approximately 10 k's from the nearest building and see it destroyed by a 100% accurate recoiless or ATGM shot from someone you can't even see, probably while you were trying to micro your soldiers who are too dumb to prone when the first two members of their squad got killed by, one again, 100% accuracy single guy with an AK.I like that it's hard. I enjoy challenging. However what I can't stand is a game that relies on constant save scumming to avoid catastrophic casualties that are game ending.Case in point, there is a mission 7 or 8 against human enemies where my small squad, upon entering the mission, lost 1/3rd of their members including a recoiless fully armored van and the two hero snipers next to it because the devs saw fit to place a humvee with a gatling and a rocket armed infantry squad right in front of them. So the mission starts, I pause, and have a lovely view of the explosion and my hero squad bleeding to death.Reload. Might assault that ATGM squad with my rangers in tha building over there, ATGM kills my whole ranger squad in hand to hand combat. Reload. Might put some snipers in the building opposite and shoot the ATGM, Artillery from half the map away destroys the building before I can get my snipers out of it. Reload.Reload. Reload. Reload. Reload. Reload. Reload. Reload.
_childDocuments_.name: Terminator: Dark Fate - Defiance

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth it. It had potential but the game came out untested , half implemented ideas (and that after delaying the launch date from december to february ) - if you have a widescreen it's absolutely unplayable, the "fix"that they tried its just a bad joke. The game has random crashes, so make sure you save or you might find your self at the end of a mission only for the game to crash when you are extracting your units from the map. The campaign is linear so forget about roaming the map going your own way , that doesnt exist you move from mission to mission and you can't even go back and revisit places you ve been ( unless the campaign takes you back there for some reason) . The pathfinding is just horrible you will either micromanage every unit or risk loosing them all. Most multiplayer games will resolve around using artillery and the maps ( only 4 of them - whaaaat? ) are fairly small, which means you can use them to fire from one side to the other as long as you have some scouts properly placed. All this being said i would hold of on purchasing the game until and if they start fixing it and adding more content and options.
_childDocuments_.name: Terminator: Dark Fate - Defiance

_childDocuments_.name: Terminator: Dark Fate - Defiance

_childDocuments_.review: terminator dark fate has come a long way to becoming a good rts game. the campaign is fun and challenging and encourages you to make use of various mechanics. _childDocuments_.name: Terminator: Dark Fate - Defiance

_childDocuments_.review: I have only played the campaign so far, so I am not rating its skirmish yet, and as far at the campaign goes this is awesome!. _childDocuments_.name: Terminator: Dark Fate - Defiance

_childDocuments_.review: Hi, Mostly good storytelling, with good actors and characters that you really like. I bonded with Big Bob and Mason. Very nice graphics and sound. Energy weapons, destruction and explosions and sounds are perfect.When fighting unfolds the way you plan it feels so efficient. Taking out the prison on the road to Santa fe, by storming it with your founder squads and just smashing the looters and rabble inside is great. The more so, if you already bought the plasma rifles from the first integrator base. Really loved having my combat group and collecting stuff for it. (Don't really see the need for booth goodwill points and supply though. Only supplies would do for trade)What can be improved.Units loS is strange. Units firing their missiles, artillery or cannons through sky scrapers where there are allies. Artillery should warn you if there is a building blocking their barrel.Also my infantry love to shift postilions. You set up the perfect ambush only to have your TOW team or rifleman decide to change floors, and get annihilated. Missions soon become too gimmicky and unfair. The infinite spawns from every angle is not very fun. Let me know a large force have arrived on the battlefield so that i can deal with it.(preferably not from the same direction i arrived.) Spawning in random spiders and tanks from everywhere just makes for stress, and chaos. My fort worth mission bugged out upon exit. And when i realized i felt relief and not a sense of completion upon exit, i decided to skip the last two missions. And i did not wanna redo the mission and risk another broken  save. And watching the final one on ThreatX stream of the entire campaign. I have no regrets. Cool boss fight, but mostly unfair if not played a number of times. A mission that is easy the third time but nigh impossible the first. I feel like learning enemy spawn timings and mission structure is not really strategy. Being blasted by artillery and hoping they do not annihilate your most precious units is just RNG. This happens too much. Sometimes you get hit and carry on, sometimes your units drop like flies. Isn't really up to your care or handling. Just luck. Many have spoken of sandbox campaign. And This could be fun. Although sandbox campaign missions can't just be random skirmish maps. They should feel semi realistic, and military justifiable. There is nothing wrong with attacking and seizing a well entrenched enemy position and then also maybe defend against their counter attack. Take out a radar, destroy a production line conquer railroad junctions. Free a village to gain their support. You could also flesh out the campaign with missions like this. I was so eager to go explore the map, but it did not really unfold as i thought it would. These are my biggest negatives. And my experience with the game was stable, i only had the one crash. I really enjoyed this game, especially all the missions up to fort worth. I applaud the developers for mixing sci-fi with a realistic approach to combat.
_childDocuments_.name: Terminator: Dark Fate - Defiance

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with good old game vibes from late 2000's (in a very good way) and complex RTS (in fact it's an RTT title) with great graphics and design. In my opinion if you like the genre just buy it, because we really need more of these.P.S. As I've seen in other reviews, a lot of people are comparing it to Men of War. Of course, I can also compare it call to arms...but going way back in time in 2006 there was a title JOINT TASK FORCE - this title it's way to similar in some ways with that title, you can find it on steam, I almost finished it again last year (except for finishing it back in 2006)....

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Oh man, I sure love this game. The campaign has branching decisions and several of the setpiece missions can be played in different ways which leads to different outcomes in later missions and completely different dialogue in some cases. There's perma-death for hero units and some villains, and the game tracks that and adjusts the story accordingly. This is my sleeper-hit game of the year for 2024. It's fun, kinda hectic, and I'm pretty bad at it so far. Made it about four missions in and I'm pretty sure I let a hero get killed because I just forgot he existed during the general confusion. Biggest downside is that this can be a little mico-heavy, and there are a LOT of units and logistics to juggle. Graphics are good, music is excellent, voice acting is great (so far), there's a discernible story, and it's set in the Terminator franchise branch that actually pushed the story forward. Who gives a ♥♥♥♥ about the Connors?  This is a pleasantly small installation for a brand new game.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, where do I start?Of course, with the big negative:The game is not just hard. It can be unfair sometimes. You will reload. You will probably even savescum. At least the game provides you with reasonable autosaves in most - not all - missions.You essentially need some tactical and weapon literacy. The game does not give you much to go on to determine which weapon is how effective against what. However, most things behave quite realistically. You can get a long way by applying out-of-game knowledge to it. If you don't have it though, you will be back at the previous point. Lots of frustration. Lots of reloading.Alright, that out of the way, why do I recommend this?Can't speak much about combat without losing myself in praise. To cut it short: Things feel right. House to house fighting is brutal. Human and machine enemies are very different in how you have to approach them. Units do what I expect them to do. Equipment has its niche. Ammunition comes at a premium. Combat shifts between fast-paced and drawn out. Just like it should in my opinion.The Campaign is awesome. You have to manage your army well. You cannot afford to take everyone with you. You cannot afford to just put every last vehicle you find into service. And still, you want to scavenge every last darn piece of metal you can find on the map. Why? Its your currency. You can buy upgrades and equipment with it. You can bolster your numbers if required. Your choices matter. Sometimes you get allies. Sometimes equipment. Sometimes people will return a favour one or two missions down the line.In regards to my own game:I played a pretty goody-two-shoes. Helping everyone (except Integrators - they are slavers) and getting myself into trouble for it on occasion. I could definitely have sustained a lot more casualties in retrospect. I was reloading far too often to save one or two squads. Vehicles too. Especially early on, you should only reload for your Founders and heavy armour IMO. Saves you time and avoids some of the bloat in resources and manpower. Also, I ended up letting go of many people to save supplies.As per other reviews, particularly negative: The game can frustrate you incredibly easily. A lot of the frustration goes away in retrospect when you realize how things work, take a measured approach to missions and laugh at yourself for worrying so much about losses. For me, the payoff of understanding and solving the game was great. I cannot guarantee that it will be the same for you.

_childDocuments_.name: Terminator: Dark Fate - Defiance

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really want to love this game. The mechanics of unit veterancy, customization, and the semi realistic style of combat are things I've wanted in persistent RTS games like this for years. It's so close to greatness almost all of the time, but just can't quite reach it. The main problem for me is how levels are designed in the first place. It feels like the game expects you to play as if you already know what, where, and how you're about to fight at any given time. The prime example in my mind is in the Legion convoy mission, where several Rev-6's and homunculi (terminators for those uninformed) just spawn in where you entered the map from, gunning down any vulnerable unit you dared leave behind in the starting area. Your only warning of this? The "We're getting slaughtered here!" callout for losing a unit, *after* they die.Another thing is the time to kill. In the right circumstances, say, shooting down a Legion aircraft, which falls out of the sky and into your troops, turning your 7 man infantry squad into 2 dudes; you loose entire units in seconds. That honestly isn't bad by itself, I actually like it. The problem is there is no way to reinforce dead squad members. Who, again, will die in seconds.TLDR; Fun game, great concepts, questionable execution. Get it if you enjoy cheese
_childDocuments_.name: Terminator: Dark Fate - Defiance

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun, challenging and addictive.I love the campaign with resource managment and being able to "build" your task force. Each unit is valuable, some are more valuable than others it is nice to see how amateurs are turned into pros and obviously it hurts when you see them perish during missions. _childDocuments_.review: Game is just quick save quick load simulator, the line of sight system is completely opaque and the AI seem to abuse it heavily because they know every angle they can get a shot from and position their units perfectly for it while your units run around back and forth trying to get line of sight of an enemy units that's shooting direct line of fire weapons. Enemy units will be invisible to you until they start firing or you get right up on them, then you'll watch your units shoot the building for 10 minutes before they die, meanwhile your own infantry in buildings will get torn to shreds in seconds. The terminator enemies have been largely manageable for me but the Cartel missions are entirely miserable affairs that aren't difficult in so much as they require you to save scum constantly to see what the enemy has where. In the end the enemy can lose all it's units because the next mission it will just have more but if you lose more than a couple units it's game over. The game also strangles you with an awful supply system that restricts how many units you can have but then some missions it will give you a dozen extra units in mission and in other missions they give you one or two squads and that's it. The game wants you to use infantry to screen for tanks but the camouflage and line of sight systems makes any advance with infantry into an open space entirely suicidal, you'll lose enough men that your squad will be useless the rest of the mission and not worth risking and thus become unable to actually then complete the objective as some missions will spam egregious numbers of AT troops, minefields and artillery that will shred your vehicles if you try to move them up in either support or as a spearhead. For some reason the Cartel ATGM squads also have a sniper too so countering them with infantry basically guarantees losing multiple squad members crossing the distance as smoke seems entirely RNG about if it has any real effect.The game has a lot of potential, I like the actual concept and the gameplay a lot, but the mission design is appalling and the RNG elements just do not work well with a consistent force between missions. Sometimes you'll watch your troops CONSTANTLY miss enemies standing stationary in the open and they will then just turn around and 100% accuracy snipe your units and wipe an entire squad in seconds who are supposed to be getting a cover bonus from being in buildings. That's not a skill issue, that's just RNG screwing you over, time to reload your save again. You move infantry through a town piece by piece and wipe out infantry you find and the second you move a vehicle forwards surprise there was an RPG squad in a building somewhere that you never saw and they pop up and your vehicle is instantly dead. Reload. Oh, you completed an objective, now the game spawns a handful of armoured vehicles in this one place that attack and objective and you have a limited amount of time to stop it. Reload. Move a unit to the other side of the map, you have 15 minutes. Oh, and there's an entire enemy base in between surrounded by mines and filled with ATGM troops, snipers and artillery. Hope you enjoy spending the next 2 hours reloading saves as you try and decipher what exact action the game devs are trying to force you to take.In the end, whatever fun there is to be had is buried beneath not a difficult, but instead a frustrating pile of bad mechanics/

_childDocuments_.review: I like Terminator, and I'm an OK-ish RTS player. I am by no means a hardcore RTS player. Love the setting, and overall I like the game play. It's a little frustrating for me in the sense that I really have no clue what's going on situational from map to map in the campaign. Maybe that's a shortcoming on my part, or maybe I just need to "git gud". I would have like a little bit of intel on each mission that at least hints at what's coming (and from where). I had to figure out a lot through trial and error (and some save scumming). It sounds like I'm griping hard on this game, but it really is a lot of fun (and tense). The persistence of your units, veterancy, and upgrading them hits the spot. There's no base building, but there is a satisfying strategic view where all that training and upgrades take place. And the setting works and sells the Future War vibe even though its Legion and not Skynet. Overall, I recommend the game if you're into the franchise and like a challenging RTS.

_childDocuments_.review: Rough around the edges but it a genre of RTS that is very rare. Mixing realism, the vehicles and ammo count are very true to the real thing, with scifi feels really good. The campaign is serviceable, half of the missions are fun the other half not so much. The missions that focus on fighting the machine are great. There is one mission were you have to navigate a cartel city which involve talking to a lot of NPCs and loosing control of your troops for crucial fights, this one is terrible.  The game would have been better if it focused more on scrapping by and choosing where to hit the machine guerilla style with a more interactive map.The unit leveling and progression of your units is nice, and also keeping your best unit for the whole run feels great. But losing them is devastating. The game is more akin to a tactical rogue like. You will reload a lot because the slightest mistake is unrecoverable, The time to kill is too short for human units, a slight misstep and you will lose your best units.The graphic are not the best and the engine is outdated(performance, they are working on it), sometimes you get really cinematic fights.Conclusion, for an old ass gamer like it scrached that "Soldier of anarchy" itch that I had for so long.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the best games from the Terminator franchise - in years. There's very little to complain about, and, while some might complain about the difficulty? That's part of the game.You won't keep every unit. The machines don't need to recklessly leave their vehicles to man roof-mounted guns, unlike your men. An Abrams commander might be picked off at a distance, because they're manning the machine gun. The same can be said for a Humvee or any manner of technical aside.They don't need to dismount for repairs. Unlike your men, they have repair drones for most, if not all vehicles that allow the crew to remain safe. If it even has a crew, and isn't just an unmanned platform. The only thing you'll get close to that, is a Stryker the CROW system. Hardly comparable; all but worthless against plasma when it just eats through your hull.They're outright superior to you, exemplified by the first mission of the game, which takes place in one of the last redoubts of your initial character's area. Highly skilled infantry, of which you'll have plenty at the start, are an incredible thing in comparison to the militia groups. Something you'll have to use as fodder later to save your own men time and again.The only hope is quick thinking on your end. For just as easily as your men die? One smart act can delay, if not entirely halt the advance of Legion's forces in any given mission. Landmines, helicopter support, artillery, etc. You're not defenceless, even though it'll feel like that at first. Especially with what I've described above, where you're at a continual disadvantage.Don't want to suffer that, however, and would much prefer to inflict it all upon others?Play Multiplayer. It's a pretty cathartic experience, watching someone try to rush you, only to counter their entire play with a singular suicide drone. A drone you put into place twenty minutes before and forgot about, at that.In any case, if it couldn't be determined from the above? I very much enjoy this game. It feels like a labour of love from a studio that I've never heard of before(for development, not publishing), on an engine that's even more archaic than the series its depicting.I'd suggest it to friends in the future and have already done so.You should give it a chance. The worst that can happen in your case, is that you'll request a refund. Though i highly doubt that.I suggest playing on Realistic for your first playthrough. It cranks the difficulty to obscene levels, but that's how it's intended to be played IMO. Hell, you could even just play Normal on the world map, and swap to Realistic in the RTS portion of the game if that's easier for you. But Realistic adds to the experience - don't skip it if you can stomach the difficulty hike.

_childDocuments_.review: Cannot recommend sadly, and please do take note I only have under 3 hours of gameplay. This doesn't count the time I spent with the demo which encompassed the first three missions of the game, in which I did skip when playing the fully game. From what I've seen, they've not changed much if at all so I don't believe it matters too much.The main game itself is the issue. I really did wanna like this game. It had a lot I really wanna see more of. Unit customisation, an open world to dig through, those big open missions that feel more like an RPG are fantastic and I loved the one I got to play (first mission post opener.) But man the game just doesn't know what it wants to be...It has a really low Time To Kill but also expects you to take care of your squads since losing one is permanent. It also gives you 30+ squads after mission 2 then throws everything you have into the start of mission 3. Along with that it does try to reward you for keeping squads alive with experience, training and custom equipment, but you're just throwing bodies at a problem until you run out essentially. Considering how low the TTK is and the fact you can't replenish squads mid mission which means losing one or two soldiers can bring a squad to the verge of permanent death. Making them unusable for the mission if you actually care for your squads.I'm well aware the game is supposed to be hard, but it's more trial and error pain until you get everything right sadly... I was playing on normal and enemies could one shot most things I had before my own soldiers started firing. A lot of things seem just oddly broken as well. Like how garrisoned units are a pain to fight since your units actually have to have a clear sight line to them to actually damage them, but they'll shoot the building even if they can't do damage and waste ammo on them. Along with that I've had an experience where an enemy shot through a building wall and one shot one of my vehicles as I was trying to line it up to actually hit him in the first place.From what I learned post refund, there's apparently a storm building option for certain squads? The game doesn't tell you this to until mission 4 btw. Despite missions 1 & 3 having plenty of house fighting in them.A lot of my thoughts can be pretty easily summed up by watching Rimmy Downunder's experience with the game tbh. I agree with all the problems he brings up about it because I've experienced them myself. The game was close to being great, but mission design was probably the main killer.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this a good multiplayer or skirmish game? Yes.Is this a good game then? Eehhh...It's trying to be Company of Heroes and Men of War, but not really melding the two genres together. It has a cover mechanic like Men of War but it's more to the simplistic side and not really well explained or visualised. Infantry in the middle of the road will be taken down easily, but the issue come with any other cover. Does this grassland provide any cover beside concealment? I don't know. Does having my squad around these trees/rocky terrain provide more cover from enemy fire? I don't know. How much better is a strong cover building compared to a medium one, cause my men seem to get shredded either way. I don't know. It wants to dumb down the Men of war cover system but doesn't provide any explanation or visualisation of this cover mechanic besides buildings. The gameplay is an interesting mixed bag. It wants you to play intelligently but when you do try to play intelligently you aren't rewarded, but more or less punished. In one mission, I have to take two bridges before the cartel destroys them. After you capture the first bridge you're informed that there is a command unit boosting cartel fighting ability on peninsula of the island you crossed over to with the first bridge. Easy pickings. Except it wasn't as the house before the command unit is occupied by 1 sniper team, 2 infantry squads, some AT squads and a grenade launcher just to shut down any sort of assault even advancing with smoke cover. Okay, so lets play intelligently. I can shoot the command unit from the bank across the river without engaging the main blocking force. So I move a sniper in stealthily, identify the command unit, blow their vehicle up with an ATGM team and get ready to snipe the command unit (yes, even if you completely destroy the vehicle the crew can still jump out of a molten pile of slag). Turns out the command unit is a sniper team or something because I couldn't see them. Artillery. A lot of bad situations can be dealt with by employing artillery. which means I can't really play intelligently, but the game wants me to play intelligently. And some units are just hard counters to all, like the mercenaries. Anti-infantry and armour with good health and movement. The game is good in skirmish and probably multiplayer(haven't tried it yet), the real let down to me at least is the campaign. I thought it would be an open world RTS/RPG from the gameplay and trailers, it's not, you go from one mission place to another with just enough supplies to get you there. And you're rewarded with the decision of either currency or supplies and you'll take the supplies because you don't have any left and would need to buy more if you take the currency. You can't go to a town and get a side quest that send you to another town with a side quest that leads to a massive reward, it's just the main missions which is disappointing.I thought it would be like Company of Heroes 3 or Wargame where you can move freely around the map. I just became very tired of attempting to figure this game out and how to approach it strategically and coming up with half baked mechanics taken from other games. And that's what this game is really. It's a bit like when you were a kid and maybe made some food concoction with a variety of different tasty ingredients, it ended up being meh or bad and this game is like that, it takes elements and mechanics from other successful games and tried to blend it together, but to me, it just turned out meh.

_childDocuments_.review: In its current the state the game is just a save-n-load simulator that forces you to play each map EXACTLY the way the devs want. You may have different squad types but you NEED to go first to point A from there to B and then to C, to D, to E, yaddayaddayadda. And if you dare to go to point D or E before you simply won´t make it till the end of the map or even worse find out next map that you didn´t save the right squad or collected enough resources so you load the old map again and play the map once again exactly as the developers intended.Your own units are incredibly weak. A squad of enemies easily damage or kill your own squads. It helps to lay down but you simply can´t play the whole game with units sticking their noses in the gras. Additionally the own units have horribly bad aim which means that due to being made out of wet paper plus horrible aim one need at least a 3-1 ratio to kill an enemy squad.In addition, the game shines again and again through absolute chaos: the game presents several POIs at the same time, simultaneously with a mass of dialogues and your own troops under attack from several directions with camera jumping back and forth as cherry on top.And then there's the fact that some mechanics simply don't work: for example, the radius for EMPs is less than the radius for automatic attacks even in passive/defence mode. This means that the units start firing just before you actually want to trigger the emp, which of course alerts the enemy and wipes out your own unit in no time at all (so you have to load an old savegame over and over again trying to make it work).So you only have the option of playing 10, 20, at most half an hour into the future and then reloading the game to start again from the beginning in the hope of mastering the critical situations better this time.I know there are a lot of players out there who like this kind of game, but for me it's just not for me because I find this kind of gameplay frustrating in the long run. You can make a game hard and use mechanics that give the player a chance to complete the game without having to save and reload a dozen times on every map.I can well imagine that it will be reworked better in the future. For now, at any rate, I wish I hadn't spent my money on this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I changed my review from negative to positive because I did put in 70h of game into this so I figured it WAS worth the buy despite the amount of frustration and the love-hate relationship I built with it.I figured now after finishing the campaign I would add more bullet points on top of the original ones:- Do yourself a favor and play this campaign on "NORMAL" (easy) difficulty because issues listed below (bottom).- Campaign story wasn't bad, it actually was interesting and kept me wanting to play more despite being set on rails and not having much player agency over it.- Each campaign mission was pretty well done both in story and in map design. Some missions, especially in the first half of the campaign, do rush you with timers which I personally really dislike but the "do this before..." stops in the second half.- I really love the way the campaign makes you feel like there's actual continuity for your characters and your army. You don't just "appear" into a mission and then "disappear" at the end. You have to "enter" a mission, progressively, via particular entry points, then the mission "unfolds" in front of you, in steps, progressively, then at the end you have to "exit" the mission, again at specific points, and in accordance to the mission. This is something I haven't seen in any other RTS game and I just love it.- I also really love the fact that you get to keep your units and vehicles and your army really feels like something that belongs to you and that you manage and care for throughout the campaign. Though this aspect of the game is being negatively impacted by the poorly designed/balanced supply system and the game's higher difficulty levels.- I love the in-between missions aspect of the game. Moving around the map (wish there was an actual open world aspect, not a railed experience). The economy of units, supplies (if only they were properly balanced), unit experience and level ups, equipment management (if only it wasn't so quirky and frustrating to micro-manage), vehicle upgrades (again frustrating because of availability coupled with inability to freely move around the map). Yeah, again, mixed bag, lots of great features that are not so well implemented, or kick each other in the nuts instead of harmonizing...- I started playing this game in hard, then I switched to moderate, then I ultimately switched to easy (normal) after Oklahoma because I was just soft-stuck due to lack of supplies. In the end, I reached 2 conclusions:       -- If you play the game on EASY, the challenge doesn't really exist and you just mainly follow the story around.       -- If you play the game ABOVE easy, then you end up saving and loading over and over again to the point you sped more time in the load screen than playing (IF you care about your units and don't want to loose them) THEN you have to delete/sell MOST of your units because of lack of supplies.       -- Because of 2 issues mentioned above, the game doesn't have a "golden" spot where you can have both a challenge and enjoy playing the way you want to. It's either too easy or extremely frustrating and unpleasant/unplayable by design.I think I could talk around in circles about this game for hours but I can't quite put my finger on exact single issues that I could name which could be "fixed" to clearly improve the game. So in the end I think the best way to describe this is "mixed bag" of things, some really good, others bad, others not really bad but not really mixing well with the others.----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Original review (mostly negatives) below:This game is GREAT but it's NOT a release-ready version, more like an improperly QA-ed beta that suffers from game-breaking bugs and performance issues. So:1. The performance is horrid.2. Some campaign missions just bug out and you can't complete them (their mission script gets stuck), especially when loading often.3. The game has an "open world" campaign map and then instantly proceeds to put you on solid rails so that you have little to no control over where you go and what you do next.4. Game forces ridiculous upkeep costs upon the player and (because of stuff mentioned above) makes it very hard for you to properly manage your resources. Expect MANY situations where you do your best to play the mission carefully and save your vehicles and troops only to be FORCED to simply DELETE most of them after.In fewer words, they released the game too soon (again, lack of QA mentioned above) and they didn't do a proper job balancing out this supply mechanic.

Sure, this game has the aspect of using the environment for a strategic advantage, but there's something lacking in this game's world building, immersion, and perhaps even the game-play design. It sucks me right out. And i feel like i'm playing a soul dead licensed game.  In my opinion, you can't make a RTS Terminator game without the TERMINATOR FLARE. Without being up close and personal, to see the enemy face to face.  Like Xcom 2, which is a Turn based strategy game. So we can be immersed in the Terminator world.  Maybe this game would've been better as a Simulation RTS Terminator game. Almost like Total War, with a free roam camera. And replays. Maybe even a theatre mode, to watch battles after you play them. _childDocuments_.review: I did enjoy the demo so I was looking forward to playing the game. The first three missions (that you play through in the demo) are legitimately quite good, surviving against a dangerous army of robotic killing machines and escaping missions beat up but still barely hanging in there to continue raging against the machines feels SO right for the setting. The first few four or so missions and skirmish matches (though I haven't had much time to dabble in them) showcase the game at its best and it is a legitimately solid RTS, especially if you're a fan of games like Syrian Conflict.Unfortunately, the game drops the ball pretty hard after its solid start. To start with the campaign's strategic layer, each mission leads into the next, remembering your decisions and keeping your army in the state it was in last battle. If you lose a soldier in a squad, that squad will be down a member until you find a replacement, and a squad or vehicle being blown up is dead for good (including named hero units! RIP big bob). Units take up supply and you need to manage the size of your army to make sure you can keep up with their demand.This sounds like a great idea on paper, but in execution, this leads to losses being punishing in a game with very high lethality. Battles are large, its hard to keep track of everyone, and that's troublesome when every lost vehicle or squad screws over your future prospects. An ATGM or plasma cannon from across the map obliterating your Bradley in a single hit or Rev 9 terminators eviscerating a ranger squad with pinpoint precision would be fine if units where more expendable or battles where smaller/easier to micro. Neither of these conditions are true, so good luck trying to control upwards of 30 units when trying to minimise losses for the next battle. Thankfully, the developers do provide a mid battle pause function to help, though pausing every 10 seconds to check three seperate battles and make sure my units in buildings aren't staring at walls instead of shooting through windows isn't exactly my idea of an engaging RTS. In battles, vehicles feel responsive and fun to control, they're probably the most enjoyable part of combat. Tanks feel like their namesake, technicals are appropriately potent for supporting infantry with machine gun fire and the various battle-trailers and weapons platforms the Movement trucks and dozers can pull are very thematic and fun to use. Sometimes pathing can get weird though, especially when shift clicking to queue up multiple orders (I find the game doesn't like shift click very much in general). You don't get a ton of vehicles, and they're limited by harsh supply requirements, but they're impactful and fun to use, right up until half your vehicles get obliterated from across the map by ATGMs and force you to reset.. Infantry, are, well, a mess. Like in similar games, they're able to garrison buildings and are somewhat fragile when outside of cover, so you'd hope buildings would work, but they're incredibly inconsistent. Infantry will sprint across floors to get to a window on the opposite side of where the enemy is coming from, then dash back to where they started, then go to stare at a wall and then go to some random window, which is hopefully one they can shoot the enemy from. If a building connects to another, like a prison complex being split into blocks, then don't even expect them to do anything to their enemy neighbours other than run around in circles and get their heads popped by snipers. Sometimes it works perfectly and my infantry conduct a good ambush while other times it makes me question if they aren't terminators in disguise trying to screw me over. So lets say you lose most of your rangers to rockets because they where too busy admiring the fine interior design of the gas station. They still killed the enemies in the end so you can just heal them up and send them back in, no need to worry about it. Except you do have to actually worry about it because you can't heal squads in the middle of combat. If the anti tank specialist gets his head popped like a watermelon by a laser sniper rifle provided directly from monolith HQ, that squad is ineffective for the rest of the battle against 80% of the legion roster, hope you're cool with your elites suddenly being a liability, where the best thing you can do is hide them in a corner somewhere so the squad doesn't get wiped.The campaign just, doesn't fit together to form the vision of what its going for. Infantry are fragile but also most are too valuable to be used as cannon fodder, yet they can't be replenished once injured in battle. The various enemy factions are dangerous and lethal, and you're usually always on the back foot, but missions expect you to fight against superior numbers and superior technology and not only survive but win. Your supplies limit the ability to bring a huge force and instead encourage a smaller more elite warband, yet every battle expects you to be bringing the entire founders military in the opening and a full horde of movement rebels in reinforcements. The game had a great start and if the mechanics weren't actively fighting themselves, this could be a damn good RTS, not unlike something I'd play in my childhood, but at current, I cannot recommend the game. Slitherine do have a good track record with other RTS titles, so its even more surprisingly seeing how badly the strategic layer of the campaign meshes with the large scale battles. And what really sucks is the mission design is really good, each mission has an interesting premise and cool and unique mechanics to manage, and they would be great fun if you weren't worrying about the state of your army and if you'll have enough troops left alive for the next mission. The individual parts of the game are all individually good but everything goes up in flames once they're connected to the chassis of the game.
