_childDocuments_.review: I was skeptical about this game, since it's a Slitherine product (champions of Paradox-like pricing schemes and dubious quality) and... well, based on the Dark Fate universe. Still, screenshots looked fine and Terminator (strictly only 1-2) was a defining period of my childhood. Decided to risk a purchase and did I regret it? Eeeeeeh... dunna. This game is a big fat meh, definitely not for purchase now.Don't take me wrong, Dark Fate gets many things right. Combat really feels overwhelming to the advantage of the machines, it's easy (even on normal) to get your troops mowed down, including armored vehicles of yours. It really captures that desperate, tooth to nail fight against a seemingly endless waves of terminators. It also has unit customization and unit micromanagement and me likey those a lot.So why the negative review? To be honest, nothing is broken in it's core, it can be patched without a hickup. But this game is simply half-baked, not playtested properly and has an insane amount of issues, quality of life and otherwise. Let me give you a few examples. This game is absolutely (or at least pretty close to) zero loss and conserving your resources (troops, etc). That's fine. But even if you have the perfect plan, executed sharply, random ♥♥♥♥ will ♥♥♥♥ you up. Namely:- Unit pathfinding is abysmal. Vehicles will crash into each other and push them around, happily, delaying vital maneouvers and/or exposing themselves.- Game is just overcomplicated. I lost vital units, till I figured out basic things. Like how to dismount/abandon resource points and such. Many mechanics are not explained, simply trial and error. Many elements are either hidden behind submenus, resulting in redundant clicking or just simply hard to get a grasp on. E.g. on the third map I found a .50cal machine gun, tooltip said that move a unit there to pick it up. I did it. Couldn't pick it up. Why? No idea. Tried different units to no avail. Desperately needed it, but ♥♥♥♥ it, I gave up trying after a few minutes.- Game is super heavily scripted with triggers left and right, some of them super broken or simply not prepared for certain scenarios. Like second mission, escort a few soldiers back to base. Did it, but it just didn't complete the step, couldn't proceed. Game has to be reloaded. Or third map, my army had to hide at one of certain places. However, one hiding spot (the primary one) didn't have enough slots for my soldiers, I was one person shot. Didn't have time to get to the other one, so mission failed. Also, still third map, I thought I am performing an optional mission (well, the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mission description was marked as optional), yet, it triggered the final event. While I still wanted to go around and explore.Maybe it will be patched, maybe not, but it's pretty annoying to fumble not because I messed up something, but because of bugs/♥♥♥♥♥♥ gameplay system/lack of explanation. Either way, happy to change that review to positive later, but Slihetherin really has to get it's ♥♥♥♥ together for that.UPDATE: To be frank, after spending 10+ hours with the game, it can be pretty entertaining, assuming that you accept it's shortcomings. And learn the combat system, which is totally not explained at all. Since I didn't really see any tips and hints regarding to the game, here are some. Don't expect to be exhaustive, I only got through the first few maps.Some of these may be patched, but that's how they work at the moment.- If you switch stance with a squad (prone/standing), it will immediately stop movement. It may be patched in the future, now it works like this for me. Pay attention, so they won't be exposed.- Entering and leaving a building takes time, depending on the building's size, as your units will actually go through the interior. Also, if you want some units to select and leave the building, square selection (hold left click) won't work. Shift+left click, select them individually.- If you give attack order for units in a building, they will absolutely NOT attack if they have no clear line of sight and most of the time won't even reposition for an attack position. You have to micromanage, that's especially painful with anti-armor units.- There is no shame in save scumming, especially that if you end up with losing complete units (vehicles), I highly doubt that you can get through the campaign. Also, you may unintentionally trigger events, which you really didn't want.- Although everyone can drive basic vehicles, their effectiveness won't be the same (especially with uprades). So only drivers should drive, as a general rule.- Just because a vehicles gets hit badly, starts to burn and units exit, doesn't mean that it's unusable. Wait until fire dies down, enter the vehicle and if there are spare parts, you can repair it to a pristine state even.- Resource points / units have mobile and deployed (supply) position. Units can only exit (enter) in mobile position, but resource is only distributed in deployed/supply mode. But switching between them takes time. Factor it in your plans, as some units can stuck there for many seconds, without the ability of being able to exit. Also, every unit can man a resource point/unit.- Almost all vehicles (except ones like tanks) can carry one or more units around. House your vulnerable ones, like drivers. Also a good idea to have spare drivers, since ->- Make sure to canvass the whole map (if you have a chance) and try to complete all of the side-quests. E.g. there is an abandoned humvee at the exit point of the second map, and at the third map you can get two military vehicles. Without the latter ones, I can't imagine how can one complete the third map. To continue this chain of thought ->- Make sure to pick up/collect ALL of the vehicles (technicals), towable turrets, etc on the map and exit with them. Don't leave anything on the battleground, driveable/towable units WON'T be visible, unless one or more units of yours actually see them.- BEFORE exiting the mission, make sure to round up all your units and gather the available supply trailers/oil trailers and resupply all units with ammo and oil. Even if you leave the map with a truckload of ammo (oil), resupplying between missions costs supply points, regardless of how much goodies you have in your trailers. Those only work during missions. Stupid? Yes. But that's how it works.- After finishing a mission, DON'T go anywhere. Moving costs supply points and chances are, that you have lots of stuff which you may want (need), but you won't have supply for it. So moving in a bloated state will drain your supply excessively. Instead of it browse the salvaged vehicles and units which joined. You have two options, disband them and get some supplies or "sell" them at settlements (drag them to the vendor inventory at the hiring window) for goodwill credits. It's a good idea to get rid of supply hog vehicles and units before moving. However, regardless of disbanding or selling a unit, make sure to check it's inventory. They may have improved weapons and equipment, remove it before getting rid of them.- Be VERY cautious when you change/upgrade weapons between missions. If you have a gun equipped with fully stocked ammo and you replace it with another one, you have to purchase ammo for it again. If you install the original gun back, you have to purchase ammo for it AGAIN. Fiddling around can drain your resources pretty quickly, e.g. fully restocking a high caliber gun's ammo can cost 1200 supply units (equivalent of a humvee and an infantry's daily consumption). Stupid system? Absolutely, hope it gets patched.

_childDocuments_.review: ---------------------------------------What is Terminator: Dark Fate Defiance?---------------------------------------T:DF Defiance is a Command and Conquer-style, real time strategy Game. You command a rag-tag group of ex-US soldiers fighting Legion, this games version of Skynet.You have to fight, not just the Machines (Legion), but Cartel, criminal gangs and Scavenger groups that litter this brave new world.You play the role of Lt. Church, a member of 'the Founders' a Faction composed of what's left of the US Military. You are thrown into the deep end as you uncover a dark conspiracy; the Machines are abducting Humans for unknown reasons.I will not spoil the plot of the game further, the rest is up to you to uncover.The game comprises of you growing your numbers and gaining battle experience of your troops unlocking new abilities, classes to make your soldiers more versatile as you befriend Factions that are fighting the Machines as well.You command troops, tanks, carriers and carrier vehicles that you can upgrade at any settlement. There is a resource element to the game, you need to balance as travelling from location to location costs men, supplies and goodwill (The games currency) You can also grab tanks, Humvees and other abandoned military/repurposed civilian vehicles on the battlefield which you can keep or trade for supplies, if you have squad members with the driver trait or driving units, you can use them to confiscate these vehicles and add them to your squad. ----------Game Types----------Choose between the Campaign, which is the Story Mode.Multiplayer Skirmish mode where you can play as Legion.----------Story Mode----------You play as Lt. Church and his second in command Lt. Mason as you travel across the Western US fighting Legion and other hostile Human Factions trying to survive. The game is broken down into 2 modes. -----------------------Mode 1: The Battlefield-----------------------Here, you command your troops and vehicles (point and click) to fight the enemy in a Rock, Paper, Scissors style fire fight, you need to use the right units/weapons for the job, utilize buildings for cover (Buildings are destructible) to keep your units alive and strategically push forward and make best use of your units special abilities. (Which T:DF Defiance does amazingly!!). For me it was a real slog to push forward in certain missions, the enemy was hunkered down and in certain areas.. There was no cover to push forward which lead to risky advances that caused many necessary casualties. Every mission has a checklist of mission tasks you must fulfil, some optional that could reward you if you complete it, or make the main mission easier, others that might slightly alter the storyline etc.Battles tend to start in 2 ways.- Infiltration/Recon Missions, you send a small recon unit to gather information, you talk to the locals, find contacts in neutral/hostile territory that can help you gain the advantage on the enemy in the Main Battle. By performing missions and trying to advance the storyline, certain rewards become available if you successfully complete the tasks. Once you've completed most the tasks in infiltration missions, it always lead to the Main Battle.- Main Battle, In full battle mode you gain access to reinforcements.. Before you engage in the Main Battle, or you start infiltration mode? You have to choose what units you will send into the battlefield. Infiltration/recon missions only allow for a light vehicle or 2 and a tiny handful of units; whereas big battles? You choose larger numbers with the potential to unlock reinforcements if certain tasks are met; a reinforcement button appears in the left side of the screen.Littered across the battlefield are abandoned vehicles that you can capture and repurpose.Vehicles suffer damage on the battlefield, a repair button appears where you can stop and repair the damage, but this leaves you vulnerable to attack, so find a safe spot behind a building to enact repairs. Repairs require spare parts, you run out? You can't repair it.Also of great importance is the use of supply/fuel trucks, some are pulled by a lorry, others are storage vehicles that you can drive to a battle and set up to refuel/rearm your vehicles and soldiers. Remember, units can run out of ammunition, vehicles can run out of fuel, so make sure you have arms/fuel trucks on standby to keep your units armed and fuelled for the fight or they will be mincemeat for Legion's grinder.Once the mission is complete, an evacuation point appears, leave the scene with all your vehicles to end the mission.Most occasions when you complete the main mission? You can freely comb the region for any abandoned vehicles/ you can repurpose or dropped weapons that your soldiers can pick up before you leave the warzone. Other times you can't hang around, Legion is hot on your tail, you need to flee or you will be overrun. -------------------------Mode 2: The Map Interface -------------------------Which you go to after every battle. Here you.. - Buy/sell your units.- Buy upgrades for your troops, better weapons and add-ons for your vehicles.- Rearm, refuel and heal your units.- Accept optional/mandatory missions.This requires having the 3 following currencies in order to advance your campaign.- Manpower points to replace fallen soldiers and purchase supplies.- Goodwill points to purchase vehicles, weapons, upgrades and supplies.- Supplies to keep your troops fed, to refuel your vehicles and to rearm your troops and vehicles.Supplies are VERY IMPORTANT as travelling from place to place consumes supplies.You have to be wise and ensure you don't run out of supplies, if you find yourself short? You can exchange Goodwill and Manpower for supplies, you can also sell units too which will reduce your consumption at the cost of less units on the battlefield; you have to make those hard decisions in order to advance. There is also missions that will activate on the campaign map that will (If accepted/declined) alter the storyline, so be smart as to what you can manage for rewards.. Refusing to aid certain Factions? Could weaken you or strengthen your campaign; again, you have to make these tough decisions.----------CONCLUSION----------Terminator: Dark Fate Defiance is a truly splendid game, made by Slytherin Ltd. I've played another of their games similar to this, 'Starship Troopers: Terran Command'.They are really good at making tactical real-time strategy games like this.Although there is no base building elements to this game, as you are constantly on the move, fighting machines that are constantly hunting you. The amount of time I had to pour into arming, supplying and preparing for the next operation had me engaged a good while. Advancing on the battlefield is extremely difficult, you may at first have them running with their tails between their legs, before you know it? They will unleash heavier tank units or you encounter a battle ground lacking defences while being pounded by artillery shells that have your troops fleeing for their lives to the nearest building for cover; you can easily get pinned down which forces you to change tactics to break their counter attack.This game is constantly forcing you to alter your tactics as it adapts and lures you into a false sense of security.The music is fantastic and immerses you in the fight.The character development is entertaining and had me immersed in the story, for example.. Lt. Church and Lt. Mason are constantly at each others throats, but, as you progress through the game?.. Mason softens up and starts to respect Church's command.The storyline is brilliant and had me captivated through out. The other characters, good and bad? Their character were all well written.All in all, I've played allot of these type of strategy games over 30 years and this one has interesting fresh ideas, Give it a try,

You can utilize buildings, cool, but you can't really hide behind rocks or downed trees. Infantry units can't take the high ground such as mountains or whatever, they can mostly travel on flat land or hills. Vehicle repairs were almost instantenous. Throwing off immersion. I couldn't tell what health my squads had, they'd almost instantly heal themselves to full strength. Giving up on the campaign, I moved to skimrish. You earn 6,000 income per (x) amount of seconds. Eventually in the battle you can call in stronger units. But overall, it becomes a cluttered mess with all the unit spam. I gave this game a chance, seeing how slitherine would perform in a RTS like this. Their games are usually hexagonal turn by turn games, designed for old gamers. They're usually deep and sophisticated, but not very fun. So I was a bit eager to see what Slitherine could bring to the table. Needless to say, I'm just disappointed. Another buggy unfinished game on the market. Really feels like RTS is dying out? I am so tired of these developers pushing gimmicky crap onto the market all to make an easy dollar. I guess I'm going back to gates of hell and other RTS games that feel sophisticated, engaging, and fun to play. If you're new to RTS, a big fan of the terminator series, and want a very casual arcade like RTS - this game might be up your alley.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty amazing RTS, and Terminator inspired to boot. If you love playing slow paced, tactical strategy games this is one to get for sure. _childDocuments_.review: I might be wrong but I believe this game is from the same people who stood behind Syrian Warfare. I love them.As I disliked most Terminator movies, I was always fascinated by post-apocalyptic world of AI annihilation. This masterpiece hits the right spot. All alone against the world in a grim but fascinating story. Pick your cards and play your game to the very end. Last time I played RTS campaign with such important story-making decisions was probably in early 2000's Battle Realms. Beware of what dialogue options you pick, units you sacrifice and bullets you waste. The world you are trying to survive in is pretty unforgiving.For the most important part of the game - battles. They are hell, they are chaotic, they are punishing, they are hardcore. Prepare atleast 1-1.5 hours for each map. In the beginning, you get small vanguard to explore the map. Then you may call waves of reinforcements that help you to complete the objectives. The problem of post-apo world is that the equipment you have is the equipment you salvage. Every unit has different specialisation - some may be good for spec-ops, some are good for destroying enemy armors, some may be just bunch of armed survivors. Some may be able to fly helicopters, drive tanks and operate artillery and some may be just meat for the grinder you transport around to fill the gaps. The combat is only about how you learn to recognize opportunities and utilize them. Units and factions are very diverse most of them may use any vehicle and equipment they see if they meet the prerequisites. Every unit has limited amount of ammo it can replenish from ammo truck - but ammo trucks also have limited amount of ammo. The combat is kind of fast paced and liquid, you will need to pause and micromanage regularly. Did your guerrilas destroy enemy patrol? They send light vehicles. Did you send in armored vehicle with HE cannon? They send tank. Did you send in guys with AP rockets? They send artillery barrage and kill of you.9/10, you will often ragequit but it's worth it.Downsides:- Poor campaign map where you basically just click towns and watch dot to move, can't move anywhere else than your mission. Full strategic map like in Steel Division or Warno would be nice.- Multiplayer is dead, probably poor marketing but this game needs more people

_childDocuments_.review: does the game have one of the dumbest-ass stories ever written, and engage in a huge amount of copsucking and otherwise deepthroating the boot of American Authority through its representatives: Good, Hard, Men in coyote plate carriers? yes. did anyone ask for a Terminator: Dark Fate videogame? no. do I even know what Terminator: Dark Fate is? also no!but the game is pretty good! it's like a mix of a Company of Heroes and, perhaps, a Wargame: Red Dragon. It's incredibly systems-rich. You manage and shape your army through persistent units, which can suffer persistent deaths, across missions - and they WILL suffer persistent deaths, because (playing on Hard, at least), the game is DIFFICULT. Not to the point of complete failure, but to the point where (even using frequent quickloads and quicksaves), you WILL take casualties unless you're some sort of perfect brain genius RTS god. I think that's a very fine line of balance to walk, and it's really impressive to see it walked here. Missions are large, long, girthy, etc, and objectives typically evolve several times over the course of one. If you played Last Train Home recently and were disappointed at that game's simplicity and easiness, this is a good one for you.I am left with only one, probably unanswerable question; why is it Terminator: Dark Fate branded? There was obviously a huge amount of work, and even passion, that went into this game. Does Terminator: Dark Fate still have shooters? Are the devs all diehard Terminator: Dark Fate fans? Did they achieve some sort of monetary reward for branding their game after a 2019 movie with 6.2/10 on imdb that I literally did not know existed until five seconds ago, when I finally googled it to see what it was?Actually, probably that last one.Anyway, the game's pretty good.

_childDocuments_.review: After beating the campaign on the hardest difficulty (with a ton of save scumming and few scrapped runs) I would give this game a tentative recommend. I love the combat and management aspects, having decide if the extra Abrams is worth the supplies and stealing every vehicle on the map after a battle to sell it off to robo-bros for a couple plasma cannons is great. I both love/hate how every unit matters so much, and the mission design ranges from nail biting hold out to trucking around Mexico rolling the dice on a dumb duel. I love how missions have so many ways to accomplish them with story branches that actually matter and change the layout of future missions. Heck, I don't even mind the extreme difficult on some missions. Having to send snipers and rangers in to scout out houses before rolling tanks through, use artillery to soft targets knowing every shell cost precious supplies, EMPing an enemy tank and hacking it mid battle. I found myself pushed out of my usual RTS comfort zone to master this game. But then in ends. After 12 missions (some optional) it just, ends. The skirmish isn't even worth much a mention, I wanted more army management darn it. Look, its a hard game that rewards you for taking your time, scouting, preparing, and carefully managing your resources. Even so it will still punch your teeth in and cause you to reload 20 times in the same mission. I enjoyed it obviously, but its that annoying spot where it was so close to being one of my favorite modern/sci-fi military games of all time, but right now its good bordering on fine. I got my money out of it, I hope we get more missions and more support cause the base here is excellent. Also the stories fine, feels like an 80s action movie plot, so that is fitting.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to recommend this game, but I can't. It's a terminator game in the ambiance of a different timeline I'm not used to, but that isn't the issue here. The issue is that the first four missions are a struggle (was playing on hard), but I felt there was something more I could do and just do it better. The fifth mission, the cartel mission, is damn near unplayable. It has infinite spawns for the enemies so you can't wait them out. Half the mission is based on RNG randomness, but you can stomach through it. But in the last part of that mission, it is almost impossible. I've been checking the discussions to see the strategies people use, but in this strategy game, there is only one way to tackle the 40-60 minute mission that has to be followed perfectly. Worse, even if you follow it perfectly, you can lose an essential squad in two seconds and the mission becomes unplayable and you have to reload. I've reloaded the same save about 10-15 times trying to push through it, going so far as to drop the difficutly.The point of this rant is that until this gets fixed, I can't recommend the game. It has so much potential and some difficult but rewarding mechanics. But that mission.... it breaks the flow, makes me hate the game, and I can't play it until it gets balanced. I'll delete my review if/when they fix it, but damn, I am broken and frustrated with this game that I was fervently waiting for._____________________________________________________________________Addendum, they did fix the issues I presented above, I opted to add an edited review and change my recommendation from no to yes to demonstrate that the Devs made the fixes and I can recommend the game. It still has some save issues, but now that level no longer feels like a stonewall that breaks the flow.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of bad reviews of this game are based around this: Save Scumming: Yes, this game is incredibly hard. The units are boneheaded, the missions are unfair, and the enemy seems to know where you are at every turn and will kill your troops incredibly easy. There are some people that will say "ew a true xcom player plays with no saves" but this is not the case in this game. You will lose your ass incredibly fast and the missions will become unwinnable in a span of seconds. However there is a ton of fun here. There is a crazy level of detail and unit customization that will make any military aficionado giggle. You can take of a 50 cal off an Abrams and put a Tow Launcher on top, and can customize the weapon load out of infantry squads, switch out armor plating, purchase skills, and buy and sell all kinds of different units. The house cover mechanic is extremely cool as units will move from room to room to get to windows and other fighting points. Vehicle combat is fun but is also extremely risky as unarmored vehicles will get messed up at the drop of a hat. If an ATGM hits your Humvee, its gone.  There is also a very in depth supply management system. Units require ammo, fuel, and repair parts. This can be very annoying, especially when you get really cool units that you want to keep but you don't have the supplies to get them forward. My advice is to always pick supply options when you get rewards and conserve as much as possible, especially when you get tanks. All in all, I really do enjoy this rts. I know its getting a lot of hate, but honestly I really love Men of War Assault Squad: Terminator edition.

_childDocuments_.review: Surprising amount of depth for a game based on the Terminator franchise. Mechanically, it's somewhere between Men of War, Company of Heroes, Wargame, Jagged Alliance 2, Ground Control, World In Conflict and Act of War. Probably closest towards Men of War in terms of scale.All your units have ammo for their weapons, with vehicles having directional armour and components, as well as fuel, spare parts for field repairs, and an ammo pool for infantry to rearm from. Infantry squads also have ammo, and can equip a variety of support weapons. All of which persists between missions, from the very beginning; Ammo, fuel and spare parts  are replenished from a limited supply; you need to actually acquire special weapons to save them. Infantry casualties must be replaced between missions from the civilians you rescue during them or from disbanding other squads - with additional squads and new vehicles being awarded for completing side objectives or just found in the missions. Vehicles must be crewed by troops trained to do so - who you can freely dismount at-will if you need to crew another vehicle or avoid making one a target; many can carry passengers with a specific number of seats rather than squad slots. In the same way, buildings are garrisonable and have decent destruction. Projectiles are physical and must actually connect with their target to do damage. Armoured vehicles are very resistant, if not impervious to small arms.The game certainly has its flaws; it's a little unpolished on the interface/controls/responsivity side of things. There are balance and pacing issues, with the 3rd mission being a huge difficulty spike - and pulling your attention six different ways at once. Make sure to get that Bradley going the second you have control over it, and, and start pulling your squads back to the central bunker and other defensive positions within the base before the game prompts you to; use engineers to set up mines in every choke-point behind the initial frontline. Get your armour crews to the southeast corner as soon as you can afford to give up the repair bay/supply depot area. In general, the more squads you manage to pull out, the better off you'll be for the rest of the campaign.Most weapons are purely lethal to infantry, and it's hard to go through any given mission without losing a few from each squad. Vehicles can die just as quickly, and armour facing doesn't seem to account for much on the scale of things. The maps consist mostly of a lot of open ground which even the machines' most basic armoured vehicle will dominate - you're pretty much forced to crawl anywhere there's an enemy presence, to get in range before engaging and to do so safely. Unless your name's Sun Tzu I'd recommend against playing on the hardest difficulty. Most special weapons types can only be used by specific squad types, when the majority of them are something that - while they might not be proficient with, they could probably figure out and put to use if it came down to it.There's only 2 infantry formations - tactical blob, and line - and wider-spaced variants of each. There's been a few situations where a staggered column or wedge wouldn't have gone amiss - but more than anything else, I wish it had a more CoH or MoW-style cover system, where troops conform to the terrain features at least as much as their formations.Skirmish mode is very undercooked with only 4(?) maps, with a couple having versions for both modes. The domination mode ends the instant one team or the other controls all the points, which are themselves captured just as quickly with a unit standing on it.What I like most is that past the first 3 missions, you get a lot of choices to make - speaking to characters to get quests within the mission, and multiple ways to complete the main objectives - with side objectives being meaningful and consequential. Voice acting ranges from decent to hammy, but never offensively so. Unit barks are good and convincing, as well as informative - and you can even overhear conversations between troops like in CoH. The game has a decent notification system for when a squad runs out of a given ammo type, takes a casualty or is wiped; ditto with vehicles being immobilised or having their weapon knocked out.If you like the Terminator franchise or just the idea of real-time-tactics with a metagame against a robotic enemy, it's a pretty easy recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Mediocore game that does not use its potential Great setting, graphics and sounds Worst gameplay I have ever experienced in an RTSFar, far, far to much dialogs. (50% of a mission is not playing, it is listening to annoying dialogs like in an RPG)Worst mission design in an RTS ever (go from location A to B talk to C, go entire way back to A talk to D to return to location B)Missions are boring and take way to longControls are bad and way to complicated (why cant every unit drive a vehicle, why does not every plate fit on any type of vehcile)Game shows a every few minutes tutorial screens with long texts (every thing is so detailed that it is far to complicated to remember)GUI is ok, but could be better. I waited for sooo long for this game and was really sad, when its release was delayed. Could't wait to play it. Maybe I had something wrong in mind (more like a c&c type of rts), but what in the hell is this? I like the setting, I like the graphics and audios, but for someone like me, who almost played (and beat) most rts-games, this is really overwhelming. The game has far, far, far to much (confusing) micro management. Do not get me wrong. I specific level of micro is good for a RTS and and a must have, but here every few minutes a popup-screen appears with very long texts to understand how to manage every detail like loading ammunition, refueling a.m.m.In my opinion no one needs this level of detail in a RTS. Additionally there is far to much talking and the game does not really tell you clearly what to do in a mission (which are also way to long) This could be the RTS of the year, if you make a lot of improvements:Have you ever experiencen an RTS? UI, Gameplay Macro- and Micromanagement must be perfect.Your missions are a katastrophe. Why this much talking from boring characters?Why do I need a special button to leave builings? (Do it with right click)Get rid of placing the units on a specific side of a building. Stuff like this should work autmatically in a RTS.Why can't every unit drive vehicles? While in combat the player has no time to check which unit can drive cars.The most silliest part is that the ammunition and the fuel of units is limited and must be refilled. Remember Battle Isle 2 from the 90s? Everybody hated it because of exactly this mechanic and it was turn based. In an RTS this is just annoying and takes away the gameflow. It took me way to long to understand how this details of buying, selling and suppling ammo, units etc is meant to be.All in all I hope there will be many improvements in the near future. I really want to give a chance to this game, but right now it just does not make any fun, because of the aspects (and some more) mentioned above.

_childDocuments_.review: Initial impressions and thought:- camera controls are unintuitive. too far to get to controls, need to reach all across keyboard or let go of mouse - poor design. I'v reassigned the turn-right/turn-left controls to Q and E, like how pretty much any RTS does it.- game should take note of UI options of other successful RTS games: Starcraft 2, Fallout: Tactics- player should be able to designate movement waypoints & unit path should be displayed or toggleable- speed of world time progression should be adjustable. ie. x0.5, x.75, x1, x1.25, x1.5, x1.75, x2- text and subtitle size and color should be adjustable- mouse scroll wheel sensitivity should be adjustable. Too much scrolling to completely zoom in or out.- gamma and brightness should be adjustable- game should have more graphics and VFX options.- game should have depth-of-field and fog of war options - see Starcraft for war of fog example.- game should take advantage of DLSS and texture sharpening.- game should have keyboard profile for Logitech G915 keyboard with pre-set actions/commands for macro keys- should be able to save the game without needing to type anything. game should auto-name saves if player doesn't enter custom names. Saves frequently end up as useless names like "a" "b" "aa" "as" "asd," etc. that tell the player nothing, just so the player can save the game.- the unit AI can be somewhat dumb sometimes- player should be able to play game without using keyboard; mouse-only.- game should have subtitle and accessibility options- game feels uncompleted/not fully tested, like the players are being used as guinea-pigs to test out the gameplay and UI, and I'm offended I was made to pay $40 for it like a dumb sucker to help out doing the Devs job for them.PS I definitely have NOT played the game for 2.8 hours, and am currently considering requesting a refund. _childDocuments_.review: TERMINATOR: DARK FATE - DEFIANCE grabbed my attention and has kept it since booting it up. Very detailed gameplay with stats, damage models. If you lose a team member specialized in a skill your squad won't be able to use that skill or weapon anymore. You can do battlefield repairs on the spot but takes time so best to do it away from enemy fire or with a friendly unit covering your back. You can position your squad members to individual different locations when you enter a building putting a missile guy in a front window and a guy with pistol or assault rifle by a back window etc. You can play as the Terminators in single player skirmish mode. Not sure about multiplayer though since i only do singleplayer.Loading screens are gorgeous to look at with great artwork along with the eerie despair and desolation of the beutifully animated main menu screen.Audio and music are fantastic fitting the apocalyptic doomsday character of the game world. Weapons and other sound effects are top notch bringing the fear as plasma fire goes flying at your units shredding them into mincemeat. Voice acting is fabulously done as your force screams in unbelievable eye bulging horror that they need back up or that they are taking anything from light to heavy damage where an engine or wheel gets knocked out needing repair. Great story and dialogue. Incredible user interface with a perfect pop up box explaining what ui icons do when hovering over them. Ammo is limited but you can control its use by telling your units not to use certain weapons at certain times by clicking on the appropriate icon in the ui.Environment is totally destructible with many ways to destroy them from weapons fire shredding shacks into tiny wood fibers to tanks smashing thru walls because WHO NEEDS ROADS!!! Phenomenal tactical pause system which pretty much transforms the game into a turn based futuristic tabletop war game of UNIMAGINABLE DEVASTATION!!! where you can order your units to move one by one or do things like vehicle repair and restocking up on ammo from transports before getting out of tactical pause mode and seeing everything play out with the ability to pause again to change your plans on the fly when the unexpected happens or things turn out nasty.Cons- Unresponsive controls when telling units to go to an area or attack an enemy or structure. Unit movement seems odd with only one man moving with the rest of unit standing still. Might be an issue with certain maps or pathing as i just ran into this on one of skirmish maps. Also graphics are not looking too great on anything less than 1440p resolution with 1080p looking really jaggy as if there is something wrong with the antialias.TERMINATOR: DARK FATE - DEFIANCE, Buy it! Play it! Feel the nightmare pull of the infinite timelines as the machines crash into your reality beyond reasoning, beyond stopping! With one sole intent to TERMINATE.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll admit, I actually bought the game and returned it but something told me I didn't give it enough time to see everything it had to offer.I'm actually happy I bought it again, because the game is pretty awesome! The campaign seems like its going to be a really long game, because the campaign map itself is HUGE! Make no mistake, this game is insanely hard. I'm playing on Hard difficulty and so far I think they nailed down the "Humans fighting for survival" aspect, because you're severely outnumbered, outgunned, and have to use your units and position them smartly. The game plays similar to wargame, so you have a variety of units that can do various things. You can upgrade the units, and train them during the campaign map inbetween missions to give them better equipment. I like how you can upgrade humvee's or any vehicle and give them better armor, and weapons.A few things I would like to see improved are, directions on where enemies may be coming from. Sometimes I positioned my units thinking the enemy was going to come from that direction, but they came entirely on the opposite side. Maybe it gets better in different parts of the campaign. Another thing I would like to see improved is the supplies. Everything costs supplies, so you have to pick and choose what units to keep and what units to disband, because the upkeep will make or break you. There's ways to alleviate it by trading, and such, but you don't really know how many units to keep, or what is in store for you going further into the campaign, so you may disband too many units and not have enough to beat the next mission. Possibly anyway, but I can see that happening. I think the upkeep is too high for the units, and should be adjusted a bit.Overall the game is fun and I hope they keep expanding it, because I could see it becoming pretty popular.

_childDocuments_.review: "Terminator: Dark Fate" presents itself as a decent entry for enthusiasts of the franchise, capturing the essence of the storied universe that has captivated audiences for decades. As a fan, the game initially resonates with me, offering an immersive dive into the dystopian realms that have defined the series. However, my early impressions, formed within the first few minutes of gameplay, hold back from casting a definitive judgment on the title's overall quality. My respect goes to the developers, no question. But in my opinion, much more could have been made of the game and the story. One notable omission that tempers my enjoyment is the lack of base-building or capturing elements. The strategic depth and personalization afforded by constructing one's stronghold, developing unique Terminators, and wielding the apocalyptic might of nuclear armaments would elevate the gameplay experience to new heights. The prospect of steering the game towards this direction tantalizes the imagination, hinting at a dream scenario for fans like myself, keen on intertwining strategy with the raw, mechanical lore of the Terminator universe.Graphically, the game stands out with appealing visuals. Although my Samsung Odyssey G9 remains unused due to my main rig being under maintenance, the anticipation of an upcoming update to accommodate wider screen ratios should add a layer of excitement for the visual experience to come.In sum, "Terminator: Dark Fate" lays a solid foundation with its graphics and mechanics, aligning well with the franchise's aesthetic and thematic expectations. Yet, it harbors untapped potential that could significantly enhance its appeal, particularly with the integration of base-building features. Such an addition would not only cater to fans' aspirations but also enrich the strategic dimension of the game, presenting a much-welcomed evolution in its development trajectory.

_childDocuments_.review: There are things I liked about the game, and other things I didn't. To get the worst of it out of the way, if you're new to RTS style games, this is not the game for you. Second, if you don't have a Saint's patience this isn't the game for you. This game is very unbalanced in favor of Legion (Basically Skynet), even on its easy mode, and you'll find yourself save scumming just to scrape by so often its basically a feature baked into the game. As others pointed out, in a series that bases itself on time travel, this makes an ironic sort of sense. This wouldn't be so bad if the loading screens didn't take such a long time. Its ending is also anticlimactic in my opinion and, despite the length of the campaign, it felt like we were only halfway through the story before it ended. All that being said, this is an interesting, challenging game that, with some balance tweaking, fixes, and more content, could become something I can find myself losing hours in, and not just because of the loading screens. A continuation of the story and skirmish modes would be something I can find myself getting invested in if its flaws could be ironed out.  Do I recommend this game for most at the moment? No. Once the developers or modders give it some finishing touches, maybe. For people who really like hard RTS games? I'd say give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: No fate but what you make.I was first made aware of this game from a youtuber called Rimmy, who while he liked some things, gave the game an overall negative review. While watching I understood his frustration, but had to try it myself as I was intrigued and im glad to say, that it was well worth the price. Defiance is an interesting game with a lot of ideas, the execution is flawed, but not nearly as bad as some make it out to be. Lets talk about it shall we.Difficulty: This is the elephant in the room for this game, its soul crushing difficulty, and people who complain about this dont just have to "git gud" it really is difficult to the point of absurdity. The biggest mistake you can make with this game, is choosing a difficulty mode higher than medium. While it might damage your pride, I highly recommend storymode. Its a decent challenge that I would call medium to hard on other RTS games. The beginning starts off fairly easy but the difficulty increases quite drastically. The only "cheat" or "exploit" you get for this difficulty, is that mission critical squads do not "die" when killed, but eventually revive. This addresses the main complain most people have with the game.Gameplay: This is why the game is so interesting and why I highly recommend it. The game is split into two main phases, the over strategy layer which is a map where you direct your force to different towns, talk to characters via portraits when in towns, and you also have the ability to assist in side objectives that cost either supplies or manpower such as clearing a road for local forces of debris. This over layer plays an important role, as your force uses supplies when moving, and the amount of supplies is dependent on the size of and composition of your force. Its entirely possibly to lose the game, by running out of supplies while traversing this layer. So keep in mind the balance of your force and its supply consumption. While an entire army of bradley's and multiple abrams and helicopters will absolutely wreck your enemies, youre going to run out of bombs, beans, bullets, and gas in the middle of nowhere and all die terribly. Further in this mode you can modify your troops. Everything is persistent, from your troops armaments, to their perks, experience, what vehicles theyre driving, how many men are in the squad, their ammo, their fuel. This layer is also where you will purchase upgrades from trading post/towns, hire new recruits, refill squads with new bodies, and purchase fuel.The second layer, is the tactical gameplay, IE the actual boots on the ground fighting/missions. This layer does a lot of interesting things going on. Unlike most RTS games ammo and fuel matter, you will need to have fuel and ammo trucks available for your units to resupply. All squads and their armaments are persistent, while you can buy new weaponry from post, you can also find it on the map and this is always a cost benefit situation. Do you really want to take on those REV6 Terminators with their plasma miniguns? If you do and win, well you have 6 plasma miniguns now, but it might be too costly to do so. One of the really interesting things, is how the game wants you to think, and explore. Its entirely possible to get several bradley/strykers an abrams, and a 155mm self propelled gun, if youre smart, and keep as many troops alive as possible, by the 3rd mission. For example, I found a gun carriage towed by a blown up mac truck, the gun carriage had a 105mm artillery gun on it, but no way to move it. Well i explored the map, and found a bulldozer. Crewing that bulldozer with a team of snipers, allowed me to attach the carriage to it, and walk away with 105mm artillery piece early game which made several levels MUCH easier even on story mode difficulty, Further, I was able to find a plasma cannon for my abrams, taking its heavy cannon off, I was able to place it on the gun carriage, and turned it into a 155mm artillery platform. Making the end of a certain hard mission "Cough Tortuga cough" much easier, as instead of fighting house to house, I simply leveled the town. The game encourages a post apocalyptic scavenging mindset and its really fun playing as smart as possible, trying to crew kill enemy vehicles to steal, pick up better weapons and equip your squads.The Army: The biggest draw of this game, is your army and how you build and manage it. You start with several "Founders" troops, these guys are a US Military remnant, which effectively, makes them irreplaceable. If they take losses you can refill the ranks, but if you lose a squad, that its they're gone. To balance that, you can recruit local militia forces. You might be tempted to utilize militia forces only, but a militia squad, fully upgraded with the best perks and weapons, will only just reach the level of a Ranger team in effectiveness while still being easier to kill. At the end of the day, youre going to be trading lives for time and resources. In a situation where you can either have 2 ranger squads and an ATGM team engage a Terminator tank, or 6 militia RPG teams engage it, its better to send in the militia RPG teams even if they all die, then risk those 3 Founders units. Who if its still alive can easily mop it up. One thing to keep in mind, is that all projectiles are physical objects in the game world, a missile that misses one of your tanks, is still a missile, its still going to explode, and its still moving. Further this also makes terrain destruction quite cool, with things like the 20mm chaingun shreading buildings with sweeps of fire. Damage is also calculated via projectile type, armor rating, speed, distance, and other modifiers. You will need high grade AT to take down Terminator tanks, while technicals can be destroyed by rifle fire, however with the upgrade system, you could make a technical with high grade steel armor plates and a plasma gun making the technical a very deadly unit for its initial cost investment that will require plasma or AT weaponry to take out.The Missions and story: The missions themselves are long, youre going to spend at minimum an hour on most, most likely much longer, and this is on storymode difficulty. There are TONS of side objectives, some that pop up, some that are hidden. The missions are fairly well designed though dont expect handholding, overall the missions are fun, and challenging. The story is quite good and id say very well told. Further the game takes so much into account, that the story constantly changes based on your actions and how you approach your interactions with other factions. While the game is an RTS its not an unfair remark to say that it borrows heavily from CRPGs with branching storylines, dialogue choices with consequences.Round up: Overall the game is a hidden gem, with its main detraction being its difficulty curve. The mechanics are there, they're great. The story is legitimately good and the choices you make do have an effect in game. The breadth of hidden objectives and cool things you can accomplish really makes each mission fun to play. I recommend this game for anyone who likes RTS games, just as I said, do yourself a favor, and try it out on storymode first, if youd like, bump it up to medium. But god help you if you go higher, because its not going to be a good time. Use a guide for Nuevo Tortuga mission for the love of god.

_childDocuments_.review: Im impressed, i always loved the base building in the RTS universe. At first this game seams just ok, but once u get passed 7 missions and unlock squad abilities and weapon attachments - then u get the idea what the Devs are trying to do here. Every unit matters, its not about the quantity of units, its rather about the capability of units. U dont want to end up with a lot of mouths to feed in this RTS universe. U rather want to build a capable mercenary force with best capable units, this will take time and effort. When u lose a unit that took u a while to train and bring up ( it blows ) This is where this RTS differs from other RTS games - each unit has a personality in a way - when u lose a special unit, there is a real sense of loss on ur behalf. This is where the problem arrives - people will constantly save and repeat in order not to lose units. The missions are somewhat confusing at times - so saving and repeating is a must. This turns this game in to a frustrating loop of save and repeat. If u rush u will lose units, its a very slow pace RTS game, with much planning on how to approach each situation. This is why active pause is included with this game ( by hitting spacebar ) It takes time to think sometimes, so u do not keep saving and repeating ur self. This type of RTS game only shines in story mode, as it takes time to build and train units ( equipping them how u chose to ) The problem with this is - The skirmish mode is not that fun, as u dont have the time to attach ur self mentally to ur units as u do while playing the story mode. I dont think this was ever done in a traditional style RTS before, what i mean by that is - the new style of RTS game such as The Broken Arrow has the capability to zoom all the way out and see the map in its entirety. A lot of players including my self dont like that - as it takes away visually - the immersion of graphics and units. Many players prefer the traditional zoom RTS where details are still visible and the view is panned around with W,S,A,D.So as i was saying, this was never done before on a traditional RTS game, where its very story driven, units have character - are very customizable and are built up during the story line. Each map has broken equipment and hidden weapons, it is up to u to find it, fix it up and take it on the road ( keep in mind u cant feed a large army in a post nuclear war ) The attention to this type of detail in an traditional RTS game is unherd of. RTS  games are usually not to scale, meaning units are larger than buildings, things dont look right. Unless u play WARNO or Broken Arrow where things are to scale. But those games do not follow the traditional RTS zoom rules - its why i dislike those games. It almost becomes a game of chess on screen - where u are just looking at on screen red and blue emblems most the time. Its very nice that this game implements old school RTS rules of zoom and pan, but introduces this emotional attachment between the player and his units on the front line. U lose a tank - u most likely wont find it in a long time - not the way u had it anyway ( skill, crew, and weapons, armor ) I have to say i like it ! But this type of RTS story driven game - only works offline - thats where it shines. The skirmish mode is pointless and has a time limit on it. Maybe this will be changed with future updates - U dont get attached to ur units in a skirmish online match up. This is where base building RTS games shine - Skirmish mode is always better on a base building RTS driven game. Skirmish mode for Terminator Dark Fate .D. will have to be changed - where its on a larger map that u have to travel about - find equipment, fix things up, recruit prisoners from Legion outposts for recruitment. The skirmish mode is an open sand box survival on a large open world map with many outposts of Legion exist. The main Skynet base has to be traveled to over many hours of game play. Terminator Dark Fate .D. on skirmish mode has to be an RTS survival game in some way. Otherwise it wont work the way its intended in my opinion. The unit build up - with finding resources just doesnt work on a short fast pace skirmish mode for this type of RTS. Over all the story mode with its unique upgrade and travel system is second to none so far. This game is ment to be played offline as it is right now. Its where it shines - until a more open world skirmish mode is implemented. Where the player almost has to exist on the map and take down Legion main base over many hours of gameplay. Building up the units as they live on the map and search for scrap. There was never an RTS game with all these features that kept it so original. For that alone i give this game a solid 8/10 - The skirmish mode needs to be reimagined for this type of RTS.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't believe the hate. If you like Terminator, and you like the RTS games of old like command and conquer or AoE, you'll like this game. The campaign is way more thought out story wise than it has any right to be for a franchise game. It is well and thoroughly voice acted with characters that are likeable and easy to get attached to. Especially since in the campaign your troops role from one missions to the next. So whoever you lose or what whatever you scavenge from the map, you carry that into the next missions. Each mission does provide you with fresh troops so that you're not totally screwed if you lose a bunch of men. There are definitely some bugs that I ran into that I hope they get fixed, but nothing game breaking for me so far.I never watched Terminator Dark Fate, because I heard it wasn't good, but that doesn't really have any affect on the enjoyability of the game for me. You could easily just change the name legion out for Skynet. It feels just like the guerilla warfare that was shown in the very first Terminator movie. Unlike a lot of other RTS games where you can see any units that are in your line of sight, this game has a stealth system that allows you or the AI to hide units for an ambush. This adds a lot of tactics you can use against the enemy to lure them into a trap. Each unit has a camo stat that affects how long they have to be somewhere before they are hidden and some units are trash at ambush.I was expecting a simple game where you just throw units at the other team until someone wins, but this is way more in depth than that. The campaign is thoroughly enjoyable and a huge challenge with choices that can seriously affect things that happen later. At the moment the game is mostly just the campaign. The skirmish and multiplayer aren't yet fully fleshed out. They still leave a lot to be desired. But whatever brings you to this game, you'll stay for the campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: So I have been waiting for this game for a long while. A new RTS and one styled in the terminator universe sounded awesome. I saw it released, instantly bought it and now we're here. Where I can't really recommend this to RTS fans. Before buying this game, I was hoping it would be more Command and Conquer, Age of Empires, Red Alert 3 beat. However this game is more Men of War, Wargame, CoH2(kinda) in terms of gameplay. As a disclaimer, I am the type to not really care about a campaign. I jump straight into skirmish or multiplayer. I did the same with AOE4, EE2, CNC and many more. So the only experience I have is with the skirmish, where there are 𝐨𝐧𝐥𝐲 𝟒 𝐦𝐚𝐩𝐬 𝐨𝐧 𝐫𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐬𝐞. 4 maps is crazy low especially for a 1.0 release. There is no base building, the game uses a reserve system like Men of War/Wargame. Except here there is an entirely different menu pop up. If you've played men of war/wargame, you can still see whats happening on your screen. Here there is an entirely different UI that takes your whole screen to display 𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐲 𝐭𝐫𝐨𝐨𝐩. Going off of the troops, I was very happy with the unit variety. One of the most important parts of any RTS. I only played the movement and the founders. Each felt unique and definitely had their own units. The graphics are great and so are the effects. But when you're in the game trying to issue orders, it feels like walking through sludge. The game is incredibly slow paced. Slow movement combines with the UI mentioned earlier to make the game feel like an eternity when replacing units. You gain these reserve points over time, but I found myself overflowing so often that I was just repetitively clicking units just to get them out there. For the squad based infantry; I would try to get them behind cover like I would in COH2, or in Men of War, or even Endwar, but the only forms of cover in the game are lying down and getting in a building. Where an incredibly long gunfight will occur.The game feels clunky. The camera is limiting, I'm doing pop up simulator with the reserves. There are other reviews that have talked about the pathfinding far more than I have so I don't need to go into that. It does not feel like a 1.0 release, it feels more like a beta or even a late alpha. This is my longest review for any game I have played. I think it is because I do want this to succeed because this is a pretty awesome idea. But when I played, I felt like I was trying to get myself to like the game. I realized that isn't how its supposed to be, and I unfortunately plan on refunding it.

_childDocuments_.review: Use third party for a steam key, $40 was too steep for me, however $20 was perfect for it, using ♥♥♥ key. It is an exceptional game, with its mechanics, setting, unit design, and rogue-like/RPG approach to RTS. Linear campaign that gives you choices to skip missions or not, help factions or not (just one really). I played through entirely once so far, working on my 2nd full playthrough. I restarted once. I suggest turning down supply upkeep to 20-30% (60% being normal), as well as damage received to just above normal, at 20%, and enable "more enemies". These are the settings that will reduce the use of save/reload that's talked about often. It isn't fun for me to do that, it's a chore, to hell with "challenge", I'm 28, not 12, I play games still to have fun. There is nothing like this that I have played, if there is, someone please let me know (Men at War is similar but not the same as far as campaign and the units you save/upgrade stay in your roster to the next mission). Which is why as soon as I finished the campaign, I started a new game. I took a path that removes the use of tanks through most of the campaign, instead focusing on the roster of the more mobile albeit squishy faction of the Movement. There is only one mission where you can bring in your entire force, and that is the 2nd mission after the intro/tutorial missions, called Sante Fe. Afterwards you either shrink your force and focus on the ones you have, or trade units out in missions, as in use recruit level units over the ones you have with higher veterancy. There is no singular way to play this game, which is very appealing. There are videos out there "best start 101" etc. that try to min-max everything and use save/reload all the time. Play how you want to play. Mass infantry assaults covered by artillery,? It's an option. Vehicle assaults towing weapon platforms, armored troop carriers with more weapons mounted on them and out-maneuver your enemy? It's an option. Set up a fighting position garrisoning buildings, setting down weapon platforms in strategic locations, with artillery behind a "U" of units/platforms, with a small strike force to send to mission objectives? It's an option. As said, there are many ways to play, you don't have to be a one-trick pony, and you don't have to play it on a setting that basically requires save/reload, dragging out missions to 2-3 hours each. It's worth the time played. Multiplayer capable, and skirmish mode (currently 2 maps for attack/defense mode among typical capture points for resource generation to bring in more units maps). Play as the machines, former U.S army, or civilian-militia faction. There is also a machine focused campaign DLC in the works. I will say that the few times I've gone to play multiplayer, no one was playing, unfortunately. All in all, this is a very niche approach to the genre, and a niche setting. Sound design is spectacular, unit design is spectacular, most missions are really dang cool (more than halfway through, the level design gets a little lackluster).You don't have to play this on the unforgiving settings, not at first. Go through it once without too much save/reload, read along a steam guide, for optimal results of obtaining extra stuff/units. If you haven't had enough of it, turn up the damage received and start anew. Even "normal" setting is a bit difficult, use Custom setting.

_childDocuments_.review: This game certainly has its issues, but I had a lot of fun with it during the 24 hours it took me to finish the campaign once, and I'm rearing to start a second run tomorrow. Let's do a quick rundown of the pros and cons.Pros:+ Great graphics with an awesome level of detail and a well-crafted, depressing  atmosphere+ Intricate gameplay with lots of depth+ Wildly varied campaign missions with tons of cool ideas and few repetitions+ Mildly branching story paths in the campaign provide replayability+ Lots of content for its asking price+ Solid voice acting+ Decent soundtrackNeutral:+/- Tough as nails and utterly unforgiving even on Easy difficulty. Some people like this, others don't. If you're looking for an RTS to relax with, this one sure ain't it.+/- Dark Fate timeline. Oldschool  fans will probably recoil in disgust upon reading this, but it's not as bad as it sounds. That terrible movie and its characters and plot play no role here whatsoever. The DF timeline is simply used as an excuse to fight Terminators with modern-day military equipment, and to give Budget Skynet some new toys to play with that OG Skynet didn't have.+/- Performance probably could be better. As a gamer from the 90s I'm used to 30 FPS, so I wasn't bothered for most of the campaign except for some serious lag in the final mission, but I know that younger gamers have this weird obsession with 60 or even 144 FPS, so be warned that you're unlikely to get this kind of performance from this game no matter what hardware you're rocking.Cons:- Confusing and/or incomplete tutorials. Most gameplay mechanics are only superficially explained, and many missions feature unique gimmicks that sometimes get no actual explanation at all, leaving the player to figure things out on their own. It kinda seems to me that the devs expect their players to already be familiar with their previous games that run on this engine. Either way, your second playthrough will be much more enjoyable than the first, simply because you'll have learned how to actually play the game properly by then.- Shockingly bad English localization. The voice-acted dialogue is completely fine, but the tutorial texts and most unit ability descriptions are rife with bad grammar and questionable wording. I might've overlooked it if English wasn't the devs' first language, but Slitherine are apparently Brits and thus have absolutely no excuse for this travesty. Did you even proofread any this stuff before you shipped it, mates?- There were some more issues I had with the game, but these have been fixed over a couple of updates, so props to the devs for this.No opinion:Multiplayer. Never cared about that, never will.Verdict:After giving an initial 7 out of 10, I'm giving the game an 8.5 out of 10 now that most of my major complaints have been adressed. This is a rock-solid realistic tactical RTS with many things to love and enjoy, so if you're a masochist and find the thought of shooting Terminators in the face with 20mm Vulcan cannons appealing, look no further.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, its pretty obvious by now, that these devs had created a game engine, and just keep making new (same) games in a different setting.Terminator is pretty much a Warfare (2008) but with a better graphics and, well, terminators...I am a huge fun of this game series (Warfare, Syrian warfare, Terminator etc...) and if you feel the same, then this game is a MUST!In case you are unfamiliar with this game engine, make sure to read the manual (comes with the game), to understand all of the game mechanics, controls and tricks you can do.This game is "Old school", so it will not hold your hand, and will punish you for ignorance.Otherwise, this is a very satisfying and fun tactical game, that can be played on ironmode (apparently dev's made sure its playable that way). Also, this game, will entice you into savescumming, and, consequently, getting very frustrating. Save-loading often can "Break" the game, and make the whole experience even more infuriating.The trick is - don't savescumTreat this game as a roguelike and you will truly enjoy this game.Even if you loose some good units, or fail a side objective - just keep playing.The game is designed in such a way, that, most likely, you will still prevail and find some alternative ways to move forward. _childDocuments_.review: Terminator Defiance is an RTS and a pretty good one. There are a lot of units divided between infantry and vehicles (Bradley, Humvee, Abrams, HIMARS, etc.).The story is based on Terminator: Dark Fate. It’s not complex and is quite linear, but it does a better job than the movie. You fight against the machines as the commander of a U.S. Army unit that survived the nuclear holocaust.A positive note is that the developers included many choices in each mission, and these choices have consequences later in the campaign (choose wisely).The controls aren’t complex, but the game is quite difficult. The units you can use in a mission are the survivors from the previous level. The high difficulty is both a pro and a con because it forces you to play tactically. However, it can turn the gameplay loop into “fast save -> fast reload -> repeat until you win without too many casualties,” which can become frustrating. Additionally, if too many important units die or supplies are insufficient, you risk soft-locking your campaign (it’s difficult but can still happen if you are not careful).I didn’t notice any significant bugs. The game is still supported by the developers, who continue to release patches and new content. Unfortunately, the online community is pretty dead apart from 2 or 3 lobbies. Luckily the skirmish mode against the AI is still a viable solution.The game requires a lot of micromanagement and offers extensive unit customization. For example, you can change your infantry’s weapons from M416 to plasma rifles to counter machines instead of scavengers. Or you can mount a new anti-tank missile launcher on your M2 Bradley (it’s OP, do it) instead of a smoke grenade launcher.The graphics are well-made and allow for many cinematic moments and crazy situations (like entire buildings exploding into debris as artillery hits them).In conclusion, this game is a hidden gem for all RTS players and a great Terminator game that offers references and new additions to the story that will please any Terminator fan. Even if you are not a veteran RTS player, I would still advise you to play it. It can be frustrating at times, but each victory brings a lot of gratification and learning potential for future matches. Over time, you will notice improvements in your tactics and learn where and when to use certain units to turn the tide of battle.Verdict: Let’s go bust some wireheads!!!

_childDocuments_.review: So after ages of waiting for this game, and very little said about it, it has amazing potential to be an absolutely STELLA!!! RTS tactical game. However as it stands currently its an unbalanced and unfinished mess, troops behave erratically sometimes just flat out refusing to shoot at things in direct line of sight and within range (not helped by the lack of a LOS tool),  as well as just walking in circles sometimes. Buildings when occupied by enemies seem to be almost invincible, then when using specified shock troops to dislodge them you will take 80% casualties rendering that unit useless for the remainder of the mission, basically meaning even basic troops can hold against incredibly advanced and upgraded troops. flip the coin however and even your most dug in soldiers in a entrenched building will seemingly get one shot out of nowhere an incredibly frustrating experience when you have spent 5 missions levelling up a sniper unit with good gear only to have it in stealth mode get deleted by an enemy you cant see. these are just a few of the gripes I have with just the mechanics of the RTS portionStep outside of this and to the main campaign map and you have a poorly thought through and half finished game, half the sites are un-visitable or you never get any side-quests to go there. you have to Guess how much supplies you need before moving to a new sector meaning you can literally have a campaign end because you dont know your next missions distance away from you. the unit variety and upgrade potential is lacking to say the least for a asymmetrical tactical RTS The game play loop seems to priorities and promote careful and methodical game play but then punishes this on the large map by forcing you to disband or sell the troops you've carefully accrued just to get to the next mission... All in all if your looking to pick this up maybe wait 6-9 months when the devs or community have released some patches or mods to either balance the gameplay or introduce QOL improvements. I fail to believe anyone has completed this game on the realistic mode without having to either reload or play though the missions before hand on a easier difficulty so they know whats in store. as playing through this blind on realistic is literally impossible.

Much of it comes from reviewers playing on the hardest setting and then whinging about the game being too hard. My advice - don't feel like you have to play on realistic. If you're one of these people that's insecure about your credibility as a gamer, I'm here to tell you that you are a meaningless speck of dust occupying an insignificant blip in time and space. You don't matter, and neither does your difficulty setting. With that said, if you're a masochist who hates themselves, and prefers to spend Friday and Saturday nights crying violently, then crank that sucker to realistic and live your best life, king.This game is inevitable.

_childDocuments_.review: I fell in love with this game. It is hard, it is punishing, but it also has a compelling storyline and once in while when a plan comes together it is just amazing. Units can level up, they can get physical upgrades as well and nursing my first tank through a whole campaign and watch the crew become veterans is quite satisfiying. I really enjoy the atmosphere, you are struggling for survival, surplies are sparse and you often have to make tough decisions, whether you keep a unit or sell it because you don't have the supplies to keep going otherwise. Force management is important, you need to cut the fat away, I can pour over my forces during missions for hours, trying to optimize my task force. You can still have quite a powerful task force, I have 4 Abrams, 4 Bradleys, 2 wheeled tanks, 6 artillery pieces and enough AFVs to get my well equipped Infantry into combat and have them supported by their rides, tbf I might be 2 missions away from the ending. I tried helicopters, but they seem too fragile.If they'd add DLC campaigns I would absolutely buy them. I absolutely love their storytelling. The world map is great and I want to go to all the places, so a bit more open world would be nice.It is not perfect, but it doesn't have to be, for me it is a lot fun. A solid 9/10 from me.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an Old School Strategy Game, for those that like a challenge, persistence and planning.This game expects you to BE A COMMANDER! It gives you all the tools but expects you discover their nuances through fire.... glorious mechanical fire.It wants you to plan, plan, plan..... then react when it all goes out the window on first contact. Players who can react and have contingencies in place will find the game VERY SATISFYING.Possibly the closest you can get to RTS X-COMMost of the negative reviews will point out the supply system and the fragility of units as the major flaw. Major losses forcing gamers with less patience to rage and save scum, these are not unwarranted. I've played RTS for 20 years, so this game was like an old friend.Combat is Realistic, men will die if exposed. cover, concealment and elevation all apply, though its not obvious.Infantry have longer line of sight than vehicles and should be used to spot. (ambush stance, prone)Smoke is critical, move infantry only when supported. When played correctly infantry are your greatest asset.Every mission is a tactical operation and should be treated as such, no one should do anything alone or without support.Teams need to be assembled, and task delegated. (minelaying, Sector Security, Convoy Escorts) You have to plan your army in advance, build a core and add supporting units to it as supplies allow.if you are riding absolute bare minimum supply between trips, your army is too big! Your aspiration is larger than your fuel tank. When you start to receive proper military tech (abrams, strykers) keep in mind that their efficiency can replace MANY civilian vehicles... They also reduce micro burden.High Tech and Military Vehicles are intentionally expensive to support, to reflect their rarity and power and also their difficulty to maintain in the field (ie. LEGION tech costs 10k per day)Collect as many vehicles to sell as you can... keep the best troops and weapons and sell the rest, You are a scout force with fast strike capability.... not an army!75k per day should be your absolute maximum budgetmy post OKLAHOMA army consists of3 Abrams3 Bradleys3 Strykers2 HIMARS2 supply HEMTT1 Fuel HEMTT6 infantry squads3 Sharpshooters3 ATGMS squads3 Engineers+ Assorted crew and support squads as needed for vehicle recovery and other operationsI played the campaign Twice both times on HARD

_childDocuments_.review: Look I love a good terminator game but if I'm being honest setting it in the Dark fate timeline is so stupid but thats something I can look past, but what really annoys me is:When using trailers for the truck's instead of doing a turn the truck will instead reverse into the trailer and they'll both slide along the road.AI path finding is ♥♥♥♥, I had a single guy running headlong into a wall because he simply did not understand that his squad had gone into the door 4 feet away, not to mention that units will collide and run against each other instead of simply avoiding each other.Some Positives:I like the branching options in some levels, like I can help this guy and anger another guy, save this guy or do this objective for some extra troops or weaponry.The Fact you need to rearm and repair your stuff between missions and have the choices to attach weaponry and extra armour to vehicles. Now do I think this game has potential? Yes.Would I waste $50AUD if I knew about these issues? Depends, I do like Terminators and Real-Time Strategy Games but at the same time this game only recently came out so I could only hope it gets better over time.
