_childDocuments_.review: This is the most frustrating and tedious POS I've ever played! I've spent more time trying to manage my army between missions and reloading saves than actually playing the missions because of bullsh*t RNG, I loved the army and resource management for the first 2 hours of it but after that it has become nothing but a nuisance!Game has two types of missions, smaller scale RPG like missions where you do quests for NPCs which then culminate into a larger battle and then you have missions which are more traditional RTS missions, huge maps with simple go here kill enemy objectives and some side objectives. All of these large missions lag like f*ck!The devs could have added a single recurring map or randomly generated maps where you could search for supplies to keep your army supplied, could've had increasing Legion presence until it becomes overwhelming and you risk your scavver force being obliterated because god forbid if you want to have more than 1 Abrams and 1 Bradley in your army good luck having enough supplies to move to the next mission!Friendly AI will also jump into your empty trailers you're towing and steal them from you so you have to pay for additional squads to idle in your rearm, fuel, and turret trailers.Could've given us entirely optional side missions with their own separate locations on the world map, they could've even been as simple as go destroy a Legion outpost or something.I was also hoping for some sort of sandbox type mode where you'd have to survive against Legion map location after map location while managing your dwindling army as you barely survive.The most fun missions are the tutorial missions because they're mostly on rails and you don't really have to manage this garbage supply system and why the h*ll do we spend a third of the campaign fighting humans?!If I want to fight human enemies in an RTS game I can go play Men of War or Company of Heroes 2, I'm here to kill robots that want to wipe us out!Multiplayer is literally a skeleton, I haven't even touched it after a brief look at it.

_childDocuments_.review: The Slitherine team did a fantastic job on this game. I have played a lot of RTS Games and I can easily say this one had a fantastic story line, a few plot twists, dynamic objectives. The character development was actually present in a way I don't think I've seen since CoH 1. That all said I am very excited for the future content and hope that you find my feedback valuable.Pros:1. The story and campaign was dynamic and extremely well done. I can't emphasize that enough. I've played a great deal of RTS games and this has been one of the most enjoyable campaigns I've played. Story, Dynamic Objectives, Optional Objectives, Meaningful Decisions with consequences, faction variety, and diversity; It was all done extremely well.2. Units were fun and interesting to use.3. Missions were challenging, dynamic, and interesting.Suggestions:1. More customization with weapons and equipment like being able to give rangers a LMG, infantry a grenade launcher, upgrading the ATGM or grenade launcher, being able to train more units to drive trucks. Basically adding more customization to the founder units. Instead of a "ATGM" squad letting them operate more like the heavy weapons squad and carry ATGMs. Having infantry chose between a SMAW and and Sniper or LMG or grenade launcher etc. Again nothing game breaking just a thought.My experience in the game was that basic infantry became pretty useless when I got access to Mercs because they can't drive and they require a van at the least to transport them. Honestly the Mercs really beat out every other type of infantry in the game. Largely due to their weapon selection and being able to drive. Please don't nerf the Mercs just provide more options to other units to make them more versatile. I also didn't get to use Church and Mason as much as I would have liked to.2. While Legion didn't use many air units Stinger teams could be useful if you decide to make Legion air more frequent.3. Vehicles were pretty decent in customization. I don't have many suggestions. I will say that being able to replace superior armor with inferior armor maybe should not be an option (yep i made that mistake). The Mortar HUMVEE can't be upgraded at all, the HEMMIT can not be equipped with a basic turret, and no upgrades for Helicopters.4. Lastly I mentioned this in the discussion thread in the one year road map section but  Sandbox campaign mode would be perfect for this game. To the hard working people at Slitherine I hope you were able to take the time to read this. I Really think you did a fantastic job. _childDocuments_.review: One for the people who loved Command and Conquer and the early PC RTS era generally, an old school keep-that-perimeter-secure fest which captures the just after Judgement Day conflict of the Terminator series well.Very scripted missions, but not totally predictable so still a lot of fun to fight. Persistence of forces battle to battle adds attrition, experience (Battle Isle, back in the day...) and upgradable units as a continuous factor, though the associated resource aspect is undercooked and feels like a bit of an artificial difficulty barrier on upper skill levels, but does add difficult choices as to who gets reinforced and who doesn't, and whether you can REALLY afford the upkeep on that extra Abrams.Script, character, voice and story are kept to a minimum and clearly not a big part of the budget, but these just passed my budget sci-fi muster.Save scums absolutely required, and the highlight was bolting sheet metal and heavy machine guns to bulldozers and big rigs.Plenty of money's worth at 80 hours (with the inevitable tactical pauses) to complete the campaign, and bugs were minimal. Gets my future support.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I want to say this game is fun and a very welcome surprise to the genre, however there are some glaring issue that I hope get fixed and it actually hurts a bit to give this a negative review. Here are some of my gripes as well as some potential ways to make things better if at all possible:-Supply: I'll start with this just because it's been beaten to death. Individual unit upkeep costs WAY too much, and you can't travel without making a ton of sacrifices. I understand the premise is to keep your team light and mobile, but the upkeep is way too oppressive and seems to force me to keep my army weak. A compromise could be to make the upkeep lower, but increase the cost of rearming units after a mission.-Buildings: I have a lot to say on this one. Fighting infantry in buildings as well as garrisoning your troops is very hit or miss. For enemies, i'll watch my army dump mag after mag, launch a salvo of 20mm grenades direct impacting windows and people, and sometimes even take tank rounds and barely make a dent to the enemies there all while wasting precious ammo. In a worst case scenario, I had two squads breach a building and there was just one cartel soldier prone in a corner and my squads just didn't seem to kill him despite orders to attack and this one guy wiped out both squads. For my own guys garrisoning a building, sometimes they would hang out in a spot that contributed nothing or I watch as my ATGM unit bounced from window to window failing to set up what should be a clear shot on spiders and tanks barreling towards the building. The mechanic of infantry moving through buildings is a neat concept, but at this point i'd rather having the buildings act like other RTS games and your troops just pop into them and teleport from window to window wherever the fighting is thickest and the buildings themselves just act like a form of armor.-Cover: Outside of buildings, I wish you could order your troops to get cover behind certain objects (which still seem to block bullets), but no such mechanic exists. This would be a good way to organize troops in better defensive positions instead of always relying on buildings, being prone, or just happen to be in a good spot behind cover anyway.-Pathfinding: Sometimes units would get stuck on objects and cause you to have to micro them to get them out. If you're not paying attention, you might accidentally leave some people behind. Should be a theoretically simple bug fix.-Missions: Some people might chalk this up as "skill issue", and you're probably right and this one is definitely me just whining. I get you're supposed to the underdog fighting outnumbered, out gunned, and always uphill struggling, but throw us a bone every once in a while. It feels like after most missions there's always the thought of "I couldn't keep that up much longer" and kinda makes you dread what the next mission is gonna pull out of pocket and throw at you, and if you even have the right units and upgrades to carry you through. Having some missions sprinkled in where you are top-dog (at least for the moment) and gives you a little cool down period especially after some of the more cancerous mission like Chihuahua (god I hated Chihuahua).

_childDocuments_.review: Terminator: Dark Fate – Defiance:~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~The highly advanced A.I. “Legion” scared its creators to the point they were about to pull the plug on it! But the A.I. algorithm beat them to it, and the Earth was suddenly sent back to centuries past. And that was only the start. Legion began the human genocide by launching Nukes on its citizens, then erecting a massive army of machines to finish them off. Soldiers from what was left of the American army fought the machines bravely but had to pull back. And here you are in Atlanta with a fragment of your troops, one month after Judgement Day! It will be brutal and relentless in Terminator: Dark Fate – Defiance. Terminator: Dark Fate - Defiance is a real-time strategy game developed and self-published by Slitherine Ltd. on February 22, 2024, on the Steam platform.The game consists of a campaign, skirmish and multiplayer modes. The last two modes, which I haven’t tried yet, will give the game longevity and replayability; I was more interested to see how the campaign mode would hold up. After 20 hours of gameplay, I am astonished at how excellent this game is – it’s brutal, and that’s playing on the medium difficulty level, the second out of four difficulty levels. The opening narrative is well done and leads to an excellent tutorial or first mission in command (in Atlanta), where you are familiarised with the interface and will probably start to realise how tough this game will become. The game is heavily focused on ammunition, fuel supply and keeping your units in good shape so you can upgrade them with new perks and weapons as you move through the levels. However, keeping them healthy will become more complex and challenging as the mission progresses, and some will vanish due to your lack of tactical expertise, or from overwhelming enemy attacks. The trick is to keep one member alive per infantry unit until the end of the mission, where you can not only resupply them with ammunition and better weapons, but also restore the unit with new blood and implement upgrades to give them more chance in the next mission. The vehicle units are similar but can sustain more damage, and the infantry units operating them can jump out of the vehicle to repair it. However,  if the same Humvee, tank or truck is continually hit after having been repaired a few times, it will become unusable. Be careful with the tanks, with Humvee equipped with rocket launchers, and also with large wirehead units equipped with plasma cannons, because one hit can be enough to destroy vehicle units. And that is fighting against other human factions. Some wirehead units are cool – they’re strong and deliver tremendous firing powers. I find them deadlier to infantry than vehicles. Before starting a mission, you’ll have to select your units, which can vary in quantity from one mission to the next. You can also resupply all your units with ammunition, refuel vehicles and repair damaged ones, all of which will cost you supply resources. If infantry units reach the needed experience points, you can upgrade them with new perks. You need goodwill points to purchase new weapons and armour for vehicle units. Goodwill points can be converted into supply and manpower resources. Yes, you must have available manpower points to restore infantry units. So, if three of your infantry units have lost three men each, you’ll need a minimum of nine manpower points to fix all three units. You’ll receive goodwill and supply points after each mission, depending on how many objectives (especially second objectives) you successfully completed.  One thing you must do regarding vehicle units and turrets is to dedicate an infantry unit to operate them, such as technicians, RPG, heavy weapons and sharpshooter squads (units between two and four members).  These units can be allocated to vehicles, whereas militia units of eight members cannot. When all is ready, you can launch the next mission.Some missions will be about securing multiple objectives one after the other. Others will include specific positions to discover new factions and characters that unfold the story. Yes, you’ll be fighting at some point within these missions, but it might not be straight away, and depending on what second objectives you can complete, the battle might be different. It’s good stuff, I must say! I really like the fact that the game autosaves when you reach significant points within each mission. However, I strongly recommend saving at your leisure, especially if you make a tactical breakthrough. Again, try to keep as many of your units alive as possible, you’ll thank me later on. All structures in-game can receive extensive damage and that you can post infantry units within them for cover or to ambush enemies, which is great. If you see any supply or fuel trucks near your units, try to secure them and take them out of enemy range. To resupply all units, these trucks must be deployed, which means they must be operated by one of your infantry units at any given time and, if possible, out of the range of enemy units, which can be difficult. It is vital to master the fuel and ammunition supplies in this game, otherwise you’ll be stuffed. It can be frustrating at times. Try to get any other vehicles too, such as tanks, humvees, vans with turrets or large mobile turrets with powerful weapons laid on the map, and ensure you have enough firepower to cover the units you send to them.  You can use EMP grenades on larger wirehead units and then hack them to take control. The sharpshooter units are the experts for that kind of attack but are not as well equipped in terms of protection. One tactic is to throw smoke grenades all around those wireheads' large units and try to get close to them. Then use the EMP grenade and hack their system. Don’t expect to be successful all the time, and make sure to keep your sharpshooter units alive. Remember, you want one member left per unit (infantry) at the end of the mission so you can upgrade and restore them. It is so easy in theory but super hard in practice. Positives:~~~~~~~ +	Great graphics, voice-overs and sound effects+	Campaign, skirmish and multiplayer modes+	Several different factions with their own units+	Four levels of difficulty+	Easy to play but hard to master+	Good mission variation+	AchievementsNegatives:~~~~~~~~ -	Needs to balance some units-	Issues ordering units to leave buildings here and there-	No trading cards as yetTerminator: Dark Fate—Defiance surprised me! This title is in the running for the best RTS of 2024. You’ll be back for more!8/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: Upon stumbling across this game on YouTube, I was immediately drawn in by its attention to detail and real-time strategy (RTS) mechanics reminiscent of Company of Heroes 2. Regrettably, despite my initial excitement, after investing approximately 30 hours into the game, I found myself losing interest. Here's a breakdown of my experience, highlighting both its strengths and weaknesses:Pros:Immersive Narrative: The storyline is gripping, immersing players in the dystopian world of the Terminator universe. The narrative unfolds seamlessly, casting players as resistance fighters battling against Skynet's forces. The atmosphere and soundtrack effectively capture the essence of the Terminator franchise, enhancing the overall experience.Strategic Gameplay: Managing supplies and equipping your army before each mission adds depth to the gameplay. The mechanics force players to make strategic decisions, ensuring each mission presents a unique challenge. The concept of limited supplies and scarce shops creates a sense of urgency, reinforcing the post-apocalyptic setting.Visuals: The game boasts visually captivating environments, featuring detailed landscapes, realistic character models, and impressive special effects. The attention to detail truly brings the world of Terminator to life.Cons:Tactical Execution: Despite the strategic depth, tactical execution often feels frustrating. Units sometimes fail to follow orders or exhibit inconsistent behavior, detracting from the real-time experience. The AI's accuracy and advantages in combat situations, whilst being disproved by the Devs, can feel unfair, leading to frequent reloads and diminished enjoyment.Shortcomings in AI: The AI occasionally exhibits behaviors that defy logic, such as pinpoint accuracy from long distances or detecting units with unrealistic precision. These inconsistencies detract from the overall immersion and challenge of the gameplay.Limited Replayability: While the game offers an engaging storyline, decisions where you can or can't supply or level up units is rather puzzling (ex. Chihuahua, those that played know). Some players found the overall length of the game to be lacking. Additionally, the frustrations encountered during gameplay may deter continued exploration of the game's content. Whilst I would really like to see DLCs for this game, I really hope Dev do not have in mind creating multiple DLC that will have the price of a full game to compensate.It was truly disheartening to discover the inability to freely explore locations while still engaging with the main quest line. Different pointers suggesting location that you will visit were rather misleading. The absence of explorable areas severely curtailed the game's potential, leaving a sense of missed opportunity and unfulfilled exploration.Despite its flaws, Terminator Dark Fate Defiance offers moments of enjoyment and immersion. However, the shortcomings in tactical execution and AI behavior ultimately detract from its overall appeal. I remain hopeful that future updates may address these issues, potentially reigniting my interest in revisiting the game down the line. Additionally, the discrepancies in unit accuracy, such as enemy unit's exhibiting unrealistic precision like shooting through the walls or nearly faultless missile precision while the player's elite units struggling to even accurately hit targets right in front of them, further contribute to the frustrations encountered during gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: "Terminator: Dark Fate Defiance" is a very well-crafted strategy game. Each move must be carefully planned as your troops are difficult to replenish. _childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game against all odds, now that I played the game I realize the Terminator setting was a good fit for... "post-apocalyptic survival tactics"... after all. Anyway, this team have taken the lemon that is this rather unpopular Dark Fate franchise, and they have made absolutely  lemonade with it. I mean, they have made super-lemonade, they have made Gatorade, they have made Monster energy drink.Very tactical, post-apocalyptical, survivalist and scrappy: if you like the idea of  taking over a map while eliminating 500 enemy infantry and 70 vehicles with your "army" of ... 40? then, this is for you... hours upon hours of neverending joy. If you call that a horrible slugfest (yes it is), this may not be for you... hours upon hours of grinding.The game modes:- Ground-control , like the Dawn of War games, or... well, Ground Control. Surprisingly fun, and short (default duration is 20 minutes). Not much action online, despite ~2000-ish players.By the way: Terminator models are actually pretty damn strong.- Very long, post-apocalyptic and scrappy : careful not to run out of fuel, repair the hell out of your vehicles, careful not to lose tanks (big tanks especially), careful not to lose people (specialized people, especially)."Optional" objectives that you really should do, but nobody forces you to. I skipped some, and managed to push ahead despite lacking key advantages, but I absolutely don't recommend it.Mostly about fighting the machines: if you think this is about Mexico, you haven't seen 20% of the campaign.Now on the surface, this game is a very hard sell: the graphics are a bit 2010's, the music is OK, but just OK, the multiplayer features are basic, and the lobbies themselves are quite empty. It took me 30 minutes to find a single game across the three regions, and that was during the first week, when the game was still relatively "trending".Otherwise an easy buy for many, myself included. Slitherine overdelivered with the very long demo, and now they have overdelivered with the full game.I have not lost troops due to frame drops, I have lost troops due to spectacularly bad throws of the dice, like "your driver was killed" after the first bullet, and things like that.If we consider , the game is very playable: In my hardware, in a normal skirmish game, I am getting average 70 FPS with a dip down to 37 FPS in the 1% low, and then down to 17 FPS in the 0.1% low, so 17 is about worst frame drop I get.Yes, CPU usage is clearly single-threaded, but this performance is quite decent, I have seen a bunch of Unity games and Unreal games drop to 1 FPS and stay in 1 or 2 as soon as there are more than 5 tanks on screen... this game never gets that bad.I am happy to see the game getting some traction, despite the Dark Fate timeline, despite the RTS tag, despite the lack of base-building, despite the cartel missions. Against all odds, like the game's theme: "Defiance"!

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this game is a wild ride! It doesn't pull any punches, I don't think I've played anything this difficult before. I did enjoy this take on a more "realistic" RTS, where things like fuel, ammo, cover and physics matter and heavy armour can't be defeated without anti tank weaponry. Only thing I really missed is cover indicators outside of buildings (like the ones from the Dawn of War games) and that I am somewhat too slow for this level of micro-management in an RTS; higher difficulty levels are likely impossible to beat without frequent and proper use of smokescreens, mine laying and the other various special abilities. Be prepared to save and load a lot, this game will either make you go berserk or teach you a zen level of self-control; I think I need a prolonged holiday from existence after my first playthrough...

_childDocuments_.review: To quote a famous philosopher: I'm sorry, I wasn't familiar with your game. I am now able to understand and appreciate the subtleties and nuances of this game. It's very much hands-off, which is good. Learn from the game itself. The mechanics of it are quite fun, once you get used to it. The veterancy could use some tweaks and I do recommend some of the mods for additional fun. But this game adopts one of the best mechanics from an old RTS (Lord of Rings) about keeping an army. The damage, fuel consumption, armour, specific weapons and their effects is better than anything else I've played. I loved their Starship Trooper games and I very much recommend this game. I would love a campaign that is double or triple the length. BUY THIS GAME!My original review: I've been thinking about this game for a bit. I've put in a lot of hours and there are some great elements that bring in innovation to the RPS genre. But there's optimisation, performance, writing and AI that need work.I think this would benefit from a Total War campaign. It definitely needs more missions with the ability to incorporate more RPG elements; Army and unit customisation/tactics, making alliances (including dealing with the unsavoury elements of Founders) and the ability to do side missions similar to X-Com to gather resources, set-back enemy progress, recruit allies/units/defectors, counter-intelligence, etc. The tactical gameplay feels more like spamming attacks. The physics and modular damage are very innovative but the AI can be so frustrating. I like certain gameplay mechanics like ammunition and fuel resupply but would like for a medic/mechanic healing function (infantry heal with stationary and Legion can use drones to heal). No spoilers but that last mission is just awful. The gameplay and story just kill the soul. But the potential for this game is visible.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent example of real time tactics that deserves more recognition than its getting I feel. - And a RARE Terminator franchise game that captures the essence of the setting.Other reviews are a testament to the fact that it is being received rather well by the community and that's a good thing considering how venomous RTT and large scale tactics fans can be if it doesn't meet their very specific requirements to fit into that niche.There are a lot of influences here and it shows in a good way. Troops have real value, their loss can and will sting if you value how important experience becomes later on. The story has multiple branching paths and decisions that impact how other survivors will deal with you, and the world around you will shift and change based on prior choices that may seem irrelevant.Be prepared. Save often, save like its a sierra game if you're new. The tutorial will NOT hand you all the answers in one go, and read your tooltips if this is your first dip into the RTT pool. Be prepared to lose all the friends you make- and yes, their survival is indeed on you, most every character and named hero can die and their loss won't end the campaigns, but their survival can save a mission later in ways you'd not expect. Salvage everything you can, a weapon or vehicle left behind cant be traded to other survivors or factions and can't be used in the fight against the machines either.Remember. - The future's not set. There's no fate but what we make for ourselves. - RESIST

_childDocuments_.review: A more complex RTS game with a good use of film license.  The game looks and sounds good. There is so much that can be done in a classical post-apocalyptic settings, so its mostly showing various kinds of deserts and city ruins. Units look good, but they will be viewed from distance anyway. Effects are functional and do not impact readability of the battlefield.  Mechanically the game is an RTS without base building. Men, vehicles and materiel are limited resources that must be managed both on tactical (mission) and strategic level (campaign map). Ammunition for each weapon is tracked separately, as are charges for smoke launchers, etc. Fuel and spare parts for vehicles are also limited. Some of these can be replenished in mission by logistic support vehicles. There is a full bulding occupation and clearing mechanic, which can be assisted by direct sorties from IFVs. Empty vehicles can be captured and used as well.  Soldiers are handled as squads, with each squaddie being a separately tracked unit (can be killed, change weapon, ...). Squads gain expirience and new skills a in simple RPG mechanic. Vehicles have more complex damage model with subsystems and directional amour, in some cases even active defense systems. They can be upgraded with added armour, new weapons or modified engines.  Campaign was fairly interesting, with well designed and challenging missions. There is a degree of non-linearity in chosing side-objectives or side missions and gaining or losing support of some factions. The story takes place in alternate Terminator universe (Dark Fate) in early stages of war against AI, so there are still multiple human factions and titular Terminators are very rare. The story was OK, but a bit weaker towards the end.

_childDocuments_.review: I, personally, have had fun with this game at times, however I don't think many other people will. The game throws lots of very good units at you very quickly, and has a very very fast time to kill in engagements. It gives you a very big toolkit, some easy logistics, and a persistent army that you can tailor to your playstyle (in theory) BUT in the campaign you are kind of railroaded into choosing very safe options to safeguard your units, and will still lose a lot of them as you play and the game just feels very at odds with itself. Like the low time to kill combined with an inability to replace downed squad members in mission just feels like it's conspiring to bleed you dry of all good combat capability in the first third of a mission and leaves you kind of scrambling to try and work around not losing your damaged squads for the rest of the mission while still completing all of your objectives with a dwindling supply of men and vehicles. It's just not cohesive. I'm still going to finish it, because I AM having some fun with it, it's just not as much fun as you could be having with say, Homeworld or one of the old Total War games.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has Issues. Ignoring all the bugs and performance issues let me talk about the game-play.-THE GAME-PLAY-The game's first tutorial hint is how to quick-save This is meant to show just how "Hard and Unfair" its meant to feel/play. It also warns the player that can read between lines that despite the devs claim that this is an RTS the quick-save/load and an in game pause feature makes the game play like a TBS, or on some (most) missions it plays like a power point slide show.I'll say that again here : This "RTS" Plays like a power point presentation.Between reloading due to bad 'RNG'  or finding out that you didn't move that one unit 10 seconds before you did and the bots spawning from out of the map spawns a tank, spider, 2 wolf-packs, and/or suicide drones and gets to kill your unit and now half your army is out of position and flanked and shortly going to die or you lose a vehicle you cannot win without (Tank/Bradley), A player will be replaying the same 1 to 2 minutes over and over again pausing every 5 seconds to make sure they issued all orders this time only to be screwed over by 'RNG'.The 'RNG' in this game is what makes it hard. Not good counter attacks from the AI or poor planning on the player's part, just 'RNG'.  'RNG' in this game can make it so that in a 1v1, tank vs tank, a tank can miss its first 5 shots or blow up the other tank in one shot. You can reload the same 1v1 and rarely get the same outcome a second time. This leads to plans falling apart not because of poor planning but because the player having two tanks and 4 bradlys with ATGMs vs a single bot tank not doing enough damage to kill it but the bot tank can still kill something important of the player's.These Issues and others like it are big reason why I can't recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Below is a copy paste of a post I made about the game being too hard:I just got this game and want to say it's too hard also, and that it's mostly a puzzle game too.I think the biggest reason is the vision in the game and the range of units. Everyone has short vision but can shoot very long range. And the heavy hitters (tanks and such) have some of the longest range. Because of this, unless you know exactly where everything is in the game beforehand, you can't plan or react much. So the game plays like everyone is blind, but then you end up bumping into the enemy and everyone shoots their load. And because of this, you don't have the ability beforehand to reposition everything in the best way to win the fight. The extreme high damage doesn't help either. The tank you just aggro'd is now one shotting your rides at high fire rate. Many good RTS, you can see father than anyone can shoot.So the game devs don't want high vision, lower damage? Ok., so they want you to lose tons of troops repeatedly. Some RTS are like that, but many of them have production abilities. You tank gets blown up, just hold out for enough credits to buy another one. You have to grind your way out. But this game doesn't have reenforcement mechanics. So it's RNG, bump into someone and game over.How you know this game isn't skill based?1. If this game was really not too hard but skill based, you would see many "Iron man" let plays on youtube with no pause. I only see one iron man and it's pausing repeatedly2. You would also see speedruns of this game. I don't see any of those either.3. You would atleast see self challenge runs. Something like light vehicles only or infantry only runs. I see nothing like that eitherThose are the things skillful players to show how good they are. Seems those players are avoiding this game for a reason. And the people who claim to be good, are not doing these feats for a reason.my 2 cents

_childDocuments_.review: This game, despite it's INCREDIBLE frustrations at times, is SO FUN. This is a masterclass in story, character development (even if they are a tad cheesy) and fun gameplay mechanics. First off: THE BAD- This game is really really unforgiving, especially at first. I am admittedly playing it on hard, but you blink for a second and sometimes a vital squad or asset is toast. Honestly though, the unforgiving nature of it is also slightly a plus in my book. I'm an Army infantry / Afghanistan vet and this really does bring a level of realism that some people might find unpalatable. Regardless, quicksave will fast become a welcome friend in this game. On to the good: The combat is incredibly satisfying. This game gives you tons of opportunities to plan assaults and defenses under pressure. There are only a few annoying missions where you have to escort convoys, but those aside, the tactical nuance is actually surprising. This game REALLY brings to heart the fact that you're a resistance fighter in a beleaguered human resistance force. You don't have unlimited ammo, fuel or resources. You have to consider these things. It also forces you to constantly consider who you're sending forward on an assault or recon, and who you're leaving behind to defend supply assets. You have to pull half-strength units off from the front line consistently and replace them with fresh troops. The fighting is intense and satisfying. Be in against the machines (Legion) or various criminal human elements, the weapons systems feel organic and realistic. Damage to vehicles is in varying levels- sometimes you'll damage a tanks reloading system, sometimes you'll destroy it's engine, and if you're lucky, sometimes you'll get a catastrophic kill.  Again, this all fuels the sense of realism. In between each mission you have an opportunity to upgrade troops and vehicles and purchase more with "Goodwill Points" - but you have to balance this all with the fact that humans need to be fed and vehicles / weapons need maintenance, ammo and fuel. This is reflected in a "supply points" system that is somewhat unforgiving, if not realistic. Keep in mind, SUPPLY POINTS OVER EVERYTHING ELSE, and you'll be fine.I'm a HUGE Terminator franchise fan, and this feels great in that world. As aformentioned, the characters are a touch one sided, but there are a lot of fun surprising moments in the story arch, and I really enjoyed it overall.This game rules. If you like challenging RTS games and like Terminator, you're gonna love this.

I would also like some deeper level of cover, not just lay down in the open or jump into houses.There is also a ton of gameplay mechanic stuff they don't really tell you, like if you extract from Haven with just one driver guy (like I did), you only have one tiny squad of drivers with smgs in the next mission. Which is basically impossible.But after a sloooow boring start it opened up and you get to manage your army, rename groups and watch them get more experience. Very satisfying.Graphics are great, there is some level of building destruction, effects look great.It's cool to watch your men reposition inside the building they are taking cover inside.It's kinda like Men of War light, but you keep your army between missions so you 'get to know them' and feel for them if they die, which I really like. About the same difficulty as MoW as well.

_childDocuments_.review: A super fun game, Worth the buy in my opinion. A few shortcomings though, the game can feel like it forces you to save scum in certain scenarios. For instance, the enemy ai can rocket you from the fog of war without any way of predicting or preventing it besides reloading and being more careful. So the ai clearly have that typical advantage of not actually being blinded by fog of war so your just playing at their mercy. I started the game on realistic but holy hell dont do that. The aforementioned issue is exacerbated tenfold as any and all of your units become made of paper. and the ai become literal Terminators (lol) with that i mean they become insanely more tanky by a large margin, and will wipe out anything you send at them. Only my Abrams and the founders rocket unit with the javelin can stand a chance, Forget using any of your other units, especially your infantry which will die immediately in any gun fight since the enemy infantry are dialed up to eleven. But that was on realism difficulty, story mode if far more forgiving and beatable without losing your entire army in a single skirmish.The story is not terrible, we could of got a lot worse, but instead we got a return to a style of story i haven't really seen since i was younger. Just a story to be told with fun and challenging missions and a narrative to keep the pace going. Nothing too serious. I love all the optional objectives, makes the missions feel a lot more fun and getting some useful units or gear is always nice. Not sure how we are suppose to move around the map with limited supplies. I guess we are suppose to keep our army pretty small if we want to back track or go out of the way? No matter what i did i couldn't get enough supplies to do any of the objectives on the travel map. Much less travel to, say the integrator camp for the best upgrades. That was literally impossible. Idk maybe i didnt fully understand the system, i just keep selling extra vehicles for goodwill and the mission rewards would give me enough to move forward but any type of excursion out of the main path was not going to happen when you have 3 days of supplies and the main objective is 3 days supplies travel but that juicy integrator camp is also 3 days travel the OTHER way, what, do i have to sell my entire army off just to visit some out of the way side task? All in all its a fun game with potential, I hope they will add workshop to the game, it would be really great to see what kind of mods this game could inspire. I think it could really benefit it and mods offer longevity.

_childDocuments_.review: after killing machines, saving people, managing my forces, establishing allys, trying to do the best I could do to save the world.. and reloading a billion saves to accomplish the best possible out come at every step, I finally completed the main story, I wont spoil anything but Ill start with what I didnt like, the supply system was a cool concept and i loved it (at first) but i quickly learned that it takes away from the game play and my personal play style in strategy games and quickly seemed to be.. unforgiving and pointless, the second thing I didnt like is that by the end of it, I expected more I didnt think it was going to end where it did, and it felt like there should be more and was going to be more but got cut (i could be wrong though), I am left desiring a lot more out side of the main story the main story seemed shorter than I thought it would be, which is bitter sweet, it was challenging, fun, frustrating, and impressively for a rts game it actually had me immersed and i loved how it made me feel so immersed like i write my own story and save the world my way or let the world burn my own way, and the way you build your forces and deploy them in battle added to that, it felt perfect it was a interesting new take on it yet also familiar, I could not stop playing for days, and I simply just wish there was "more" especially in the skirmish section.. just 4 maps with adequate but good replay-ability will only hold over my need for this game in my life for so long.. so to sum it up I would absolutely recommend this game and I would pay full price for it, its worth every cent.. but I hope that they make more content for it, and add to it, and make many games just like this in the future! and also get rid of the supply system or atleast make it forgiving.. i understand what they wanted to do with it but it did isolate my play style.. and took away from the possibilities to try and play the campaign over and over again in different ways, also i do hope if they make another game like this they add a way to "create" squads.. my goal in the game was to build up a large uniform force and i just simply couldnt do it with how they designed it.. which now that I know that theres little to no reason for me to reply the story persoanlly because in the end i wont be able to play how i personally like to and im sure im not the only gamer who will feel forced to change how they usually play strategy games due to some of the mechanics and lack there of, having said that this game is a instant classic standing tall in my head along with many other classic strategy games in the RTS hall of fame.to the devs Thank You for what you've accomplished here with this masterpiece, dont sell out, what you have here is what other devs wish they had and what certain publishers wish they could bleed dry for their greed, not naming any names but im sure yall know who im talking about

_childDocuments_.review: Terminator: Dark Fate – Defiance offers an exhilarating experience that goes beyond just playing a game—it's about immersing yourself in a battle for humanity's survival. The attention to detail in depicting the US Army's tactics and equipment in their relentless fight against the terminators adds a layer of realism and strategic depth that is rarely seen in games of this genre. It's not just about the action; it's about making smart, tactical decisions that could either save or doom mankind. A must-play for anyone who appreciates well-thought-out military strategies and the Terminator universe. 5/5 stars for delivering an adrenaline-pumping, strategic masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: As a lover of RTS games and having an extensive amount in my library i give this game a solid 8/10 rating and i urge people to give it a try.Ill say here though the game is touch and go, you will either love it or hate it. It has some indepth mechanics not seen in other RTS games make simple but impactful such as resource management, equipment and vehicle looting, persistent armies and decision that have impactful meaning in later missions. Do i push the main mission or slip away for a side mission, it will cost more resources but it will give me access to unique weapons and opportunities for later missions?My few gripes on the games come as like many other peoples gripes, the game is hard and unforgiving, People are a resource so losing them hurts save scumming is a common tie in alot of the campaign missions because of the cost of units and the fear of losing a unit that could be useful later in the campaign. Line of sight benefiting the AI over you. Campaign missions with ambiguous of unclear objectives and progression.For the above id like to suggest some fixes or additions to the game. Support units: Medics and ambulances to heal troops and save troopers to mitigate the heavy cost of losing people in a mission. Mechanines/Repair vehicles, to mitigate running out of spare parts for vehicles a and can help repair armour mid mission. Recon units to help extend Line of Sight so the playing field can be equalled to mitigate the effect of losing troops to being sniped from the fog of war.What i would like to see going forward:A persistent rougelike mission game mode similar to Call to arms/Gates of hell ( As this is the best example for similarites to the game i can make) where we can progress of a psuedo war campaign against random generated enemies forces and can work down the tech trees of different factions to help win the fights.Different campaign perspectives lets see more of the movement and their war, lets see the integrators trying to become united, lets play as legion to control the world etc. their is so much story potential and i hope it gets explored.Lets see more factions and groups. Lets go global and see international forces rebel militaries, indepenent human factions. the shells of former goverment, warlords... and with these groups some expanded unit and troop rosters.Lastly more maps, for skirmish and the Campaign, this game is great and i want more content and more customisation.TLDR: Games is great to play, has some shortfalls and is unforgiving, Very unique as far as RTS Games go.

_childDocuments_.review: Good tactical game with almost-RPG-like campaign. Not without it quirks but a pleasant addition for a strategy fan.First tutorial missions are a bit slow and mostly about defense. Controls are fine and pretty responsive. If you played RTSs before you'll feel at home. Units have different sets of weapons and ammo types, that they competently enough use against correct targets asking little micro from the player. Your job mostly in positioning analyzing covers and assessing lines of sights (that should've come with some kind of visibility tool, but I had no issues). Fights are pretty and intense with that bit of modern combat realism to ground SciFi a bit.After big base defense you'll start the actual campaign. Big overworld map is in fact a resource management game with mission selector. You need supplies to travel between locations and you need to get to locations to play a mission and get more supplies. You should (and game gives you time to do it) to scavenge as much vehicles (mostly) and stuff to sell it in the overworld to rearm and upgrade your units of choice with new weapons, skills and modifications like additional armor and HMG-nests.Surprisingly there is some factions between humans and from the start you will mix your sci-fi-army with post-apoc survivors units. It's an interesting worldbuilding but wrapping your head around different MadMax-cars and a lot of similar infantry squads is a bit confusing at start. The whole scavenging aspect is fun enough but time consuming and can feel like a chore. At first I spend almost an hour trying to figure what I want to sell and what I want to keep ans supply just to understand that I screwed up a little and it will be wiser to reload a save and do it again,That's actually what you should do a lot. Savescumming is your friend, especially if you are new to this. Setting aside confusing you math in supply screen or losing bunch of your vehicles due poor decisions in combat, you should save a lot just to be ready for some story twists mid missions.First "real" mission asks you to visit a bunch of NPCs on a big map to make some moral choices before big robot attack. And it's not entirely clear what means what until you see it. So its smart to save a lot, see what game has for you (and where you should place your units beforehand). And yeah, losing units suck, so F5 is your friend in any case. Don't overdo it, though, you can afford some losses. Maybe even more than you and I think.I do have some reservations about complexity of the mission structures. I'm two "real" missions in and it feels like they both were "end-game" level of complexity. Multiple primary and secondary objectives, time pressure, hidden events, attacks from multiple directions and "gifting" me new units mid-combat that I don't know what to do in the heat of the fight. And non-stop radio-chatter with new mission info.I do despise tactical pauses in RTS-games but here I can't play without it - assessing map, commanding new units, checking on old units, checking side objectives, reading new dialogues etc.It is a lot. So take it easy and save a lot, play a bit more careful. It will click.I've finished second "real" mission with only one restart after my units mistakenly drove into territory on a neutral faction and failed to leave in time, provoking them.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great mid-budget title that came out of nowhere for me and really shocked me by how competent it is. Slitherine tends to publish a lot of hidden gems and this one is no exception.As a game, this is somewhat like a mix between Company of Heroes by Relic, and Eugene systems games like Wargame and WARNO. You maintain your army between missions, customize soldiers, upgrade your tanks with new armor and mods, and then you lead them in battle. Like in CoH, units can take cover in buildings, have special abilities that can be activated (like smoke grenades, AT mines, or EMP grenades), and you control your squads and vehicles fairly close up; tank guns have ranges of around 100-150 meters, rather than 1-2 kilometers like in Eugene systems games.Like those Eugene systems games, however, units have limited ammo, vehicles have fuel and repair supplies, and these things need to be resupplied in the field. Supply trucks can bring in lots of supplies, while smaller vehicles like Hummves and Strykers carry spare ammunition for individual squads. Most missions will have you start with a limited part of your force, and then slowly ramp up the intensity as you call in the reserves. Unit variety is somewhat lacking in one sense, but actually quite good in another. While you only get one true tank, for example (the M1 Abrams), the tank has two weapon slots. You can have a tank with a plasma main gun and a minigun, or a tank with a 30mm vulcan cannon and a TOW launcher, for example. Looting vehicles off the battlefield is a large part of this game: you can sell the looted vehicles for credits between missions, and you can strip them off any mounted weapons to transfer to the other parts of your force.The gameplay stresses combined arms warfare in pretty interesting ways. Obviously, different squads are good at different things (snipers are good for scouting and picking off unsupported units at long range, AT squads carry two RPGs), but light vehicles such as hummvees can both transport squads around the map and provide decent fire support at range. This can be suprisingly deep and engaging in practice: one way to deal with low force limit missions is to have good anti-infantry squads like Rangers or Mercenaries move around the battlefield in TOW hummvees: if armor appears, the mounted weapon can take them out, while the squad can dismount for anti-infantry work. All in all, the gameplay is very, very solid. There's a few smaller issues (AI for moving around buildings is pretty annoying, losing weapons on squad member deaths and picking them up again can be quite annoying as well), but none of them really mar the final picture. The game is VERY difficult to start, because unsupported infantry will die very quickly, and it takes a while to understand when and how to take engagements properly. The amount of units you'll have to manage in bigger missions can also be overwhelming at first. Once you get the hang of the game and the matchups, and learn to pair infantry with vehicles for support and transport - whether APCs, Strykers, Hummvees or Bradleys -  it gets easier, and the end result is really fun to play.Voice acting is very good for a game like this, both for units and characters. It's not on the level of Company of Heroes, but it is solidly above the genre average when it comes to contextual voice lines. As more than half of infantry units can drive light vehicles (anything less heavy than a Bradley), they will change their voice lines depending on what vehicle they're driving. The female sniper team thus has specific voicelines for when you place them in a mobile artillery platform, a tractor, an ammo carrier, and so on. There are also several "hero" units with unique voice lines, and these are mostly really fun and with lots of personality ("Big Bob ready to blow ♥♥♥♥ up!"). All in all, this game is a solid 8.5 out of 10, at least. If you enjoy games like Company of Heroes or Warno and want something in the middle between those games, this is a strong recommend. It's quite hard at first - you *definitely* want to start on Normal until you're more comfortable with the systems - but it is a rewarding game to master. Blowing up terminators with HIMARS rockets never gets old, and watching as your tiny recon force slowly grows into this massive juggernaut is very rewarding as well.

_childDocuments_.review: - - - - - Intro :Disclaimer, I was in the Beta which is how I got this review out so quick. Gonna keep it short and stay light on spoilers here because I think the story is something you should get to experience yourself.I’ll address the elephant in the room first, yes this game is set in the Dark Fate Timeline, but i don’t think you should let that affect your judgement of it. This is a very Authentic Terminator Experience, as far as atmosphere goes you really feel like an underdog in a post apocalyptic war with all of the odds against you and the Characters are quite likeable with their own personalities. With the Persistent Army, general atmosphere, the closest game I could compare this too would be Homeworld 1, which being one of my favourite games is big praise for me. This is a great RTS and a good Story based game, with your choices throughout actually affecting the story in various ways both in gameplay and dialogue. - - - - -  Tactical Gameplay - [] :Cover and positioning is key here, placing infantry into buildings or vehicles, but also using the terrain to your advantage. The game won’t give you little shield pips that show you were covered like in say Company of Heroes, so you have to actually look at the terrain and think for yourself ‘is this cover? Will this protect my squad?’  The second mission shows this off a little bit Like in Homeworld, you can be pretty sly, capturing enemy vehicles and weapons will give you a great advantage, not only providing you with more firepower but you can sell them off to settlements and bases providing you with more money to either buy new infantry squads or to upgrade or provide new skills for your existing units. This also makes you consider how you approach enemy units, do you use an ATGM to take out an enemy tank, or do you take it on with less powerful weapons hoping to disable the vehicle so you can capture it for your own forces, putting your squads at greater risk in the process.- - - - -  Strategic Gameplay - [] :Your army is persistent, it sticks with you throughout the entire game. Your units level up and you can give them various upgrades, from new weapons to different upgrades for your vehicles like improved engines, armour or new features such as a Missile Launcher for your Bradly being added on top of its already existing weapons. You have two main resources to consider during the campaign, Goodwill Credits [money] and Supplies. Your Army takes supplies to move from location to location, so you need to balance how many units you have with how many supplies you have, do you bring a bunch of Technicals or a Tank for example? This is imo the most difficult aspect of the game, though there is a skill that can mitigate a units Supply Cost [Survivalist]. The coolest part of the strategic layer imo is customising your units, giving them upgrades, new weapons and so on. - - - - - Units :  Your main units in this are Infantry and Ground Vehicles, though each major faction has an aircraft of their own [Huey for the Movement, Blackhawk for the Founders and a HK Aerial for the Legion] Units generally stay pretty useful throughout the Campaign, though the different factions have different uses / playstyles for their vehicles and infantry. This means that Humvee you got in Mission 3 can stick with you right until the end and still be effective right up to the end.Units have Skills that can increase their effectiveness too, which makes the game feel kind of like an RPG at points. Each unit levels up as they gain experience, incentivising you to keep them alive. You can spend your Good Will Credits at certain Settlements and Bases to Train your units, gaining skills that can improve them in various ways. The game has Hero Units, but they don’t work like you might expect. They are quite powerful, but only if used right, they can die just as easily as anyone else and unlike in other RTS they won’t respawn or revive if killed, they’re just dead. Keeping them alive can affect the story and mission objectives, so you have to balance using powerful ‘hero’ units or not risking them. - - - - - Story :  The Story is very good imo, the characters are generally pretty likeable and the fact you can affect how the story progresses. I want to avoid spoilers here, but you should think about what you do and how you do it as things can affect the story and your objectives in ways you might not think.  With my favourite character being a hero unit you unlock in mission 4 called ‘Kondo’.  There is an in game encyclopaedia which gives info on units, both gameplay stuff and lore info which is brilliant. I love when games have this kind of feature. I do wish there was info on Weapons and Upgrades lore wise but we get plenty of lore as is. - - - - - How can the game improve :The biggest way I think the game could be improved is just to add more of what we have, more upgrades, more units, more missions and so on.The second biggest and perhaps more important than the first is a map editor, this was game changing for Starship Troopers: Terran Command and would be great here, allowing the community to keep making maps and missions to keep the game alive even after players have finished the main campaign.  Cosmetic Customisation for units, this is pretty low priority but being able to choose the paint colour of our units would be nice or adding decals / flags and such.

_childDocuments_.review: I was very excited to see a real-time Terminator game. Unfortunately, many disappointing Terminator games have been added to the list over the years. The best one played was The Terminator: Future Shock back in 1995. Firstly, the storyline does not align with the Terminator franchise, including Legion. Humans fought humans at first in the chaos after the nukes dropped. The machines slowly enslaved humans to build their factories in exchange for food and shelter. Then, the exterminations started wiping out pockets of residents. This game is too complicated for a decent real-time strategy game. I enjoyed the first couple of missions, but having to do this and that and having the entire base slaughtered without knowing what was happening. I gave up and added this to the list of disappointing Terminator games. I agree with a few other fans' comments saying they should have stayed with the original Skynet timeline. Create a DLC for the various timelines... I'll push on trying to play this game and force myself to like it, but even playing a skirmish sucks! Paying the Introductory Offer with a 10% discount would help the developers because I want to support my favourite game franchises. But, I regret not waiting for future 50%+ discount sales for such a poor outcome.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm recommending this, with some caveats. You absolutely are going to want to save often, there's a couple of traps that can make the rest of your campaign super painful. For example, leaving haven base without all of your troops + the humvee at the end is going to cripple you. On the plus side, if that happens you can skip the tutorial and start with a default army, so hey, whatever. I'd recommend doing it until you get it down properly, however. You're going to want to scan each map for vehicles before you leave, you can dismantle them for some supplies even if you don't want to travel with them. You're going to want to double and triple check your commands and where your people are going. Sometimes you'll click behind your unit and they'll want to drive off down the street towards the enemy to pull a u turn rather than just reversing (luckily there's a command for that). Each mission is going to take you a couple of hours and they can play out differently, depending on what you do and how fast you do it. For example, in the final cartel mission, its entirely possible to have legion show up. I won't say how, but my friends did not encounter this, whereas I did on my first playthrough and didn't on my second when I had the game kinda mastered. You'll fight the UI a lot. It's really frustrating trying to get units to behave properly or deploy properly. The ATGM/TOW rng is really, really annoying. Sometimes you'll fire and hit straight away. You might reload later on, take the exact same shot and they'll miss three times. That being said, hitting a building with smoke, pulling up in a bradley, having units exit + sweep and clear it so you can use it to set up a strongpoint to safely rally around is wildly satisfying and I couldn't stop coming back to the game until I had completed it. I also kept having to alt f4 and walk away from it occasionally. But it has something that kept me coming back.

_childDocuments_.review: It is not really often that a game hooks me anymore, It needs to have a certain level of complicated mechanics mixed with a decent challenge. This has done a good job drawing me in for the past few weeks, eating away daylight and evenings alike.This game demands a lot out of the player, there's a lot of RNG mechanics which come into play if not respected and mitigated through playstyle choices. The player controls a lot of the diff. through strat and tactical alternatives, including choices regarding how you tackle each missions list of objectives.For example - a troop running along runs the danger of a surprise machine gun ambush mowing the team down in moments , a tank moving without knowledge of surrondings can get tapped apart by RPG fire from nearby buildings, etc.As a player you can opt to devestate entire regions to watch the fireworks or slowly creep forward to salvage loot for gains, capturing as many vehicles as possible to sell them off after fights.The main complaint I have is that the terrain can act a little to wonky, making it seem like you've set up a perfect ambush but a vehicle needs to be moved to a whole other position to actually be parked on a flat surface to increase it's accuracy. Beware the little bumps blocking firing lines, etc, but as one plays these terrain oddities become more apparent.

_childDocuments_.review: Game has great potential but it has some flaws. To be honest, I was very excited about the first 5 episodes. Game mechanics were very nice. Story plotline seems good too. I can't say I am too fond of dialogues. Map designs are beyond great.Then what is the problem you may ask. Well here it goes;- Building to building combat are the worst. Your troops die very fast whilst enemies don't. A few enemy troops in a single building can destroy tanks and a few regiments by themselves. You can try to snipe them out but some of them out-range snipers. Also, howitzers don't solve the problem(especially light ones). This should be somehow balanced.- I play on the "normal" difficulty, which feels around hardest. Since vision is limited, you could be easily hit by a missile or so. Don't get me wrong, I adore realism but, this is just overwhelming micro(I don't consider myself young but i did play SC-Coh series a lot). Controlling whole map, whilist looking out for every possible threat is too much. So I found myself taking autosaves around every 3-4 mins to reload. Btw, game's original autosave periods are bad. I mean really BAD.- Weapon drops seems unnecessary, since you often have better equipment.- Game needs some kind of a cover system like in the MoW or CoH series. Proning is a nice touch but not enough.- Optimisation has some issues. Game drops around 20-30 fps in big maps(episode 5-7)But overall, game is fun when you are not exhausted by loosing precious units. Intensity of combat feels nice. Side missions are worth to give a try. Haven't been able to try multiplayer yet, but story mod itself, would be suffice. A solid 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Before the review, I had never seen any Terminator movies, but played around with one terminator game. As one should see, this game uses the same engine and gameplay mechanics as Syrian Warfare, which is nice since few RTS games exist that use this style (for now).This game is not for everyone just like Syrian warfare was not for everyone either, even if you consider yourself a “alpha RTS gamer”. You can play straight away on hard difficulty and do well. You can miss securing the tank on the first mission (as well as the Bradley), and still do well in the next missions with the more “unconventional” forces at your disposal as you fight legion’s hordes. So, even when trophy equipment is missed out during the early missions, a good enough or lucky enough player, can in fact reach the later mission with acceptable losses, for example 128 troops lost, 7 vehicles, for 586 enemy troops, 48 vehicles. But that means you (the player) have massive casualties to replenish, and not enough resources nor manpower. Unlike Syrian warfare, the player isn’t given troops over time to pick and choose from, instead on the tactical map, different locations have either movement forces, integrator camps, or surviving human settlements, some can give troops and equipment, others will only give training to your troops, all will give resources for travel. Legion is the main threat to humanity, but like Syrian warfare, humans somehow have time to fight and kill each other for their own reasons and agendas.  To be honest, reviewers who say that AI has sheer randomness of unit’s accuracy and lethality, is true, especially considering some of the obvious weapons being used. For example, the javelin shouldn’t miss unless the target has electronic countermeasures or hide in a good spot at the last minute, so the atgm team will miss a spider out in the open at least once, then suddenly hit it when it tries moving out of range of the atgm. but at the same time, who knows how actually effective it can be when 10 years of unclear maintenance programs goes on for western hardware.Anyway, there is also the fact that on a certain mission later in the campaign, the “duels”, are completely random, which kind of works, but at the same time is literally up to chance, because the troops given are already elite rank, but supposedly have no “training perks”, so they can still die, and the mission automatically fails. The story is passable, if you just don’t care for terminator lore, the characters also passable, if you just don’t care and simply use them for what they are for, tank crews and free upgrade loot. The game itself is fun, especially if you like the gameplay mechanics of Syrian warfare, one obvious challenge is working with western style equipment and vehicles, but it’s possible and rewarding with the right tactics. Plus, the ability to upgrade troops and vehicles with armors, weapons, an engine upgrades is a wonderful feature that hopefully is used in the future for “Syrian Warfare like” games. In summary, since my personal experience with the game so far is alright, I would still recommend the game since it will get better, eventually. There are error issues and game freezes, for now I only saw game freezes at times when a artillery round is about to hit the ground, or a tank explodes on occasion as well. So yes, the game has issues. I would not recommend the game to gamers who are not comfortable with the different mechanics to experience from rts games like command and conquer, StarCraft, company of heroes, or the upcoming touhou empires, because the gameplay mechanics are going to be significantly different, from all those games, the only one similar enough would be COH and Men of War of course.Edit after completing campaign: Whelp, I still can recommend this only if the developers bring in patches, add factions to Skirmish/multiplayer, and fix those awful bugs and issues, just trying to play the game. Its also overpriced considering the content given (30 bucks max should be the price), so in summary, if you have 35 to 40 bucks to burn, try ti out, if not, don't even wait for a sale, just check out the game in a year or two, then see for yourself i you actually want to play this. If neither options are appealing, just buy Syrian Warfare, its well made, fun, has steam workshop mod content, and is based on real events (for those that want to satisfy the Historical RTS itch)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this with the understanding ive only played about 10 hours of the game.at the time of writing i have only completed the first campaign mission to some level of satisfactory outcome where i didnt lose any units that i felt were critical. this took me about 6-7 attempts to do and 2 attempts to understand the most efficient way of doing it.this game is extremely difficult, even on the medium setting. as many others write, its extremely punishing. i havent even save scummed to the extent that others are, merely restart the entire mission and hope that somehow it goes better this time.my biggest issue is how harsh the game can punish you for simply engaging a tank and how inconsistent damage feels. sometimes my tank can tank a beating head on. other times it gets demolished after 3 hits where everything is hitting the turret. on the second mission there is an additional group in the center of the map. after somehow managing to barely get my tank to survive and the final wave being sent. i had a perfect plan with most of my units being in decent shape. it fell apart in less than a minute. my bradley blew up and due to pathing i "tread on" this additional factions territory, which made them hostile and caused them to wipe out everything i had moving over to ambush the final wave. there is a circle, a big circle that the game shows you, which isnt even consistent with the actual area that they begin to threaten you, nor does it even give me an inkling of an idea of where "we're going to attack you" even starts.i can't recommend it as im having such an internal fight between loving this game as an RTS and hating it for how punishing it is on medium difficulty.also, if anyone decided to read my cobbled together review. thank you. i know this was as painful to read as it was to write.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very hard game to review, or even recommend. I just finished the campaign and I basically enjoyed it and dont regret buying it, but there are some serious issues which can completely ruin your experience. So:+ terminator setting (although not the typical one from movies which most of people expected)+ very enjoyable sounds of guns, vehicles, etc. You feel like you are in there with the units.+ enjoyable battles, where every decision and unit matters+ lot of units/factions to choose from+ many upgrades for your units, both infantry and vehicles (both skills and items like better weapons, armour, etc)+ missions are varied enough , with many side objectives and some hard decisions as well- despite being graphically very mediocre, it has atrocious, and I mean ATROCIOUS performance/optimisation in city maps. My rig is not the best, but definitely can handle todays games on high settings (Cyberpunk 70 FPS + on high for example). This game drops to even 20 FPS in city maps in heavy fights, which is bordering the unplayable, or at least frustrating experience... Devs acknowledged  this  and are working on better optimisation, but also stated that the problem is that engine uses only one CPU core, so I don't hope for any major improvement in this area. To be honest this is one of the most horribly optimised/performing game I played  in my 30+ years of gaming and I really wonder why build such a good game on such horrendous engine (money?). Lowering any graphics details in the game, which there are very few btw (texture quality, shadows, grass..) doesn't improve anything.. its obviously  an issue of bad game engine. Galveston  mission is just a 10-12 FPS nightmare..- VERY micro-managing heavy. You need to pause a lot during fights, micromanage every unit (if you don't want to loose them, which is BIG part of this game, units carry over), use cover, plan your approach . Its definitely not the game to select all your best units and just send them to attack the other end of the map.. you will get slaughtered. Personally I don't mind such games, I even enjoy them, but this can be biggest problem for people expecting normal strategy game like CnC, which I expected this game to be.- many missions can be very hard because "you dont see the future objectives" and some of them are just very hard to do if they appear from nowhere. When you know what to expect when replaying mission, its getting much easier and less frustrating.  (good example is the mission when you are holding off many legion waves, if you know what comes and from where, its much more manageable).  Yes, you can still finish the  missions on first try, but you will probably suffer many more losses, which will  hurt you in long run. I feel like this game is build around replaying missions or at least heavy save-scumming, which I personal dont like.- there has been many posts about supply issue on strategic map, meaning you really have to know what you are doing otherwise your campaign will be very short.. New patch solves this by lowering supply cost of all units by 40 percent, if you play on lowest diff... Many people find themselves hardlocked by supply issues and need to restart the campaign, even several times. Me personally I didn't have much issues before the patch, but I guess it was because I read forums and some suggestions from devs themselves how to approach the supply stuff.So, still recommending the game despite some heavy issues, but just be prepared that this game is not the usual strategy game like CnC. Its a mix between games like Man of War and, lets say, Command and Conquer, with some strategic layer as well. Its probably closest to games like Regiments, Warno, Red dragon, etc.  I am glad devs risked this approach, such games are getting rarer and rarer.

_childDocuments_.review: I recently completed the game and found it to be a truly enjoyable experience, particularly due to its unique RPG elements. Despite encountering several bugs throughout my playthrough, none were significant enough to crash the game, allowing for uninterrupted enjoyment. The gameplay itself can be described as hectic, requiring players to manage multiple tasks simultaneously. The combination of high enemy spawns from various directions, coupled with the high lethality of combat and the significance of each unit, often led to instances of save scumming. However, these challenges did not detract from the overall enjoyment of the game.Suggestions for Improvement:Scouting Abilities and Stealth Mechanisms:Implementing scouting abilities and stealth mechanics could greatly enhance the gameplay. For example, granting snipers the ability to shoot without being easily detected would increase their utility.Additionally, providing increased sight range for units positioned on high buildings would add strategic depth to the game.Ability to Withdraw Units and Resupply:Introducing the ability to withdraw units from the map would offer players greater control over their squad management, particularly in situations where only a few units remain.Allowing supply trucks to automatically return for refilling when their supplies are depleted would streamline gameplay and reduce micromanagement.Direction of Attack and Retreat:Implementing a designated direction of attack and retreat, with enemy spawns limited to one or two directions (except when dictated by the story), would enhance strategic planning.Providing players with a mapped-out exit point at the beginning of missions would facilitate the establishment of defensive positions and improve overall gameplay experience.Heli Drops as a Perk:Making heli drops a perk for units would significantly impact gameplay, especially if scouting mechanics are introduced.This feature would enable players to strategically deploy units, such as stealthy sniper scouts, to unknown areas, alleviating the challenge of landing helicopters in difficult terrain.UI Improvements:Enhancing the user interface to isolate units when selecting tabs, such as light vehicles, would improve clarity and ease of army management.Implementing features like selecting eligible drivers directly from vehicle slots would streamline gameplay and reduce time spent on micromanagement tasks.over all very fun. looking forward to dlc.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, mostly offline play.Story is unique, has unexpected turns and is engaging with impactful branching.  The real star IMO is the game design.The army system reminds me in a lot of ways of old school mech commander where you collect, buy and carry units with you.  But even beyond that, there is the element of unit experience leading to skill picks and inventory load outs - per unit.  Some might complain about the micro aspects but personally I think this is exactly the kind of mature RTS that the market has been lacking for a while and is desperately needed in a world of "lowest common denominator" game design.Graphics were decent, world and level design was solid, control scheme was reasonable and performance was fine even on a mid level laptop.Only real con IMO is the lack of reasonable modding which I hope gets addressed with further titles cause this always adds life to a game.I am not usually one to endorse a game at full price but I think it's fair in this case.Dear Slitherine - lean into this mindset of game design.  Add add easy access to game rules / files for modding.
