_childDocuments_.review: I am giving the game an overall good rating as I enjoyed it, even though I was heavily frustrated and annoyed at times. It is hard to figure things out throughout the campaign unless your save and redo the missions many times over or someone tells on you about these things. I had to look up a few parts because I could not figure it out. The supply situation was horrendous, but after an update it is much better. Still annoying though to manage. The gameplay is fun with cool units an mechanics, as it definitely hooks you. There are pathing issues and for some reason when you select units to move as group they down really stay in that group. They will go at different speeds and even take different routes unless you micromanage each move point. The story I thought was pretty good, although basic. I do wish the ending wasn't so abrupt at the end, as the mission completed and then cut to credits. No little talk or cutscenes to close out with. Now, the main thing that I think needs a whole new rework is skirmsish. Way to basic and kind of boring. I tried it out and didn't feel the need or want to continue playing any skirmish. For one, there is only four maps, three with the same game mode, and the last is pretty much just replaying haven base mission. Also only three factions available. No cartel or integrators. You also only have preset number of units and times you can call them in. It is also only 1v1, so no allies or multiple enemy factions. Honestly, they need to do something similiar to command and conquer or other similiar games where you buiild a base, or have a prebuilt base to recruit units and go from there. To me the current state of the game just has no replayability. A lot of potential though. I do hope they continue update the game. Skirmish I think is a dud though, unless it gets a major rework.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this game. This game is hard, but it's not because of the terminators and Legion. The game is hard because it is buggy and you're fighting the game controls more than Legion itself.Controls are super clunky and unresponsive. This takes away the fun of some missions and you spend more time micromanaging units than tactics and strategy. There are also glitches and bugs that'll get your units killed needlessly. Command and Conquer: Tiberium Dawn, a game released in 1995 has better unit control and responsiveness than this game in 2024. Shocking.Supply and resource management is a constant pain point especially on harder difficulties. Some strategy genre fans love the supply management simulation but it doesn't make the game fun. Supply is there to limit your fighting units becoming a doom stack and force you to scavenge for supplies in the field. But this could have been simplified with a unit and supply cap instead of all of the unnecessary logistics and micromanagement. Legion also cheats as it is not limited by the same rules, and can throw infinite amount of units at you without restrictions. Upgrades to units are easily missed because you don't have the right unit to pick up the upgrade on the ground. It could be simplified to allow any units on the ground to pick up weapon upgrades in the field and then send it to a pool at the end of the mission. This way units can be resupplied for the next mission.Infantry takes forever occupying buildings. I don't want or need to see them run 24 flights of stairs to the top of the building? Just animate them to fortify the building like in Red Alert 3? The terminators are hard enough to deal with, I don't want to see them fortify a building in real time. Vehicles suffer from the worst path finding on some maps. Tanks have trouble getting through some maps and take the shortest path to get to their destination - even if it means driving through a Legion stronghold. Queuing multiple orders don't seem to work. Vehicles will at least try to move as a convoy but forget about trying to get them to use formations or a battle line. You'll need to pause and move each unit individually.Vehicle groups will also move at the speed of the slowest unit. So it's generally not a good idea to attach faster attack vehicles to the main battle groups if speed is a factor in the skirmish. I don't really get the decision to separate vehicle cabins between crew (tank crew and pilots) and fighters. I don't think this has been very well thought out. Its a clunky mess when organising your troops in the tactical world map. It also needs to be explained better in game. The annoying thing is that tank crews and pilots count as fighters on the deployment screen. This restricts your actual fighting force on reconnaissance missions for no reason other than to be annoying. Tank crews and pilots should be hidden from the deployment screen, so that infantry slots are only filled with your fighting force you plan to deploy for the mission. If a vehicle is destroyed, then you've got pilots and tank crew which are liabilities, not an asset, on the front lines.All the micro management issues above aside, the story campaign is immersive. Some missions are more annoying and frustrating than others. I like that there are multiple factions involved in the campaign and different factions have their own agendas.

_childDocuments_.review: Apart from being guilty of having a rather messy name Terminator: Dark Fate - Defiance is a solid RTS/RPG hybrid.I haven't tested Skirmish or Multiplayer yet, so I can't comment on those. But the Campaign is a lot of fun,  if misleading. The Campaign is not a straight forward RTS, you don't build a base/units and try and sweep the enemy from the map. instead it plays a lot more like Jagged Alliance with a touch of Fallout: Tactics. Your "Army" is made up of units/vehicles you scavenge from the field or trade for from friendly settlements each unit levels up and can be further specialised with unique abilities and equipment load outs. Your supplies are finite and need to be carefully managed, it maybe awesome to have that M1 Abrams with a plasma cannon, but it's also going to cost a fortune in supplies to keep it battle ready. What this results in is you needing to make difficult decisions about the composition of your army,. You also can't do everything in every map, your choices will matter (at least they have so far) so you need to choose your objectives carefully and learn to live with the consequences.You are a guerrilla force facing off against a far superior enemy with almost limitless resources. You don't get the luxury of being able to take everything for every situation, you need to be focus on modifying/enhancing the strengths of your army.To that end the game gives the player a lot of freedom in just what that army's strengths are. There are many options with many different ways of customising them. You could have a very small but powerful force of high-tech modern units that cost a fortune to maintain and are hard to replace, but can hit like a sledgehammer and are too stubborn to die easily. Alternatively, you could create a highly mobile force of cheap/disposable vehicles that are specialised in ambushing and hit-and-run strikes or a Mad-Max style army of modified Semi-Trucks and trailers all heavily modified with scrap armour and as many guns as you can modify the chassis to fit.Overall, Terminator: Dark Fate - Defiance will most likely appeal to those who enjoy games like Jagged Alliance or strategy games that include a focus on Logistics and Strategic Army Management. If you are looking for a Starcraft style RTS with endless amounts of units smashing against one another, you will be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm happy to see a game in Terminator universe (depsite how complicated it is). It's a blend of RTS with some RPG style management, a bit of skills and equipment for your units. The game starts pretty slowly allowing you to get a grip, however, tutorials could have been more thorough. I like the aspect of managing supplies, especially early-midgame it adds to the "on the run" feeling of humanity losing to machines. There is a lot of micromanaging available and some missions rely on that. Some missons are a typical RTS: bnring more than they have and eff them up. Some are much more focused on storytelling, micromanaging and choosing your path. For me it's a breath of a fresh air in the genre. I really do like how different the missions felt. Oh, BTW, missions are usually long 1-1,5h to be exact. End game felt rushed both in storytelling and in missions. It's not as polished as early and midgame. The final is very unsatyasfying as game cuts before any possible fallout of your actions can be observed. Another weak spect is the characters. They are flat as a pizza stone. Completely linear, predictable and frankly boring. I wish they spend more time developing them, because there was a huge potential for storytelling and character arcs in a setting like this. Overall: had fun, won't replay the game.6/10 got my money worthPros:Nice blend of RTS and RPGMix of smaller story-driven missions and big battlesMany possible playstylesInteresting setting...Cons:...which wasn't utulised enoughPerformance: game likes to crash and runs like assBoring charactersUnsatysfying ending

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to give the game a good review. But some rather unpleasant parts hit hard. Tactical map Econ is broken, you need to pay supplies daily to keep troops good to go, that's fine; makes sense. Then costs show up, your random civilian dudes with cheap single shot assault rifles cost around 800 a day. Modern dayish infantry squad 1100, A technical truck with terminator auto guns jury rigged to back costs 10,000. Your reward for winning that last mission 180,000 supplies. I had nearly 50k upkeep a day. You have 4+ days of travel ahead to next mission. Its hard to build up a force to fight robot menace because of these costs, so disband and throw the men and vehicles in recycle can and inch by with the scraps remaining. After third mission you can travel north to visit tech cultists to trade. Depending on how many guys you still have left your campaign can softlock here as you won't have enough resources to bring the army back the way you came. Fourth mission defend against convoy went smooth enough. Annoyingly I couldn't get my snipers or rpg teams to pick up better gear. They only switch out first gun of two for other stuff you find preventing them in mission from upgrading guns. Also started to notice just how fast everyone and thing died.I came here to fight terminators. First few missions are this thankfully. Now game decides time to fight Mexican criminals instead of race ending robots.. Cool.. What came after was 10 hours of terrible game play. Infiltration mission alright, you interact with certain areas/npc squads, your mission critical unit gets in a arena fight which you can't control your squad and is pure rng if they just straight up die in ensuing fight. Forcing you to start over. Literally set game difficulty to story mode, went to this arena, watched trained soldiers get stomped by drunks from the bar.. Save reload several times before the duels were won, continued infiltrating mission. Get to moment when things get loud. Alright your now surrounded and outnumbered by enemy soldiers with a timer. Alright won that part your backup is here.. They spawn in kill box of enemy forces at the gate. Okay through skin of your teeth you did that. Now its time to go through entire city house to house combat. Your enemies are thugs who have better skill then your crack commandos. Out range you using exact same guns, better accuracy and you can't spot them until they start shooting. Literally had sniper looking down a open road, saw nothing, vehicle moved up, surprise anti vehicle missile team was waiting 10 feet from squad guess your Humvee is scrap now. Another block away oops happens again but this time your Apc and its squad got wrecked. Another block, turn corner hey HMG team was waiting militia squad mulched. Halfway through time to rush prison they executing people. No your snipers can't pick them off from side, geography has LoS blockers there. On a flat plain to front gates. Find out later you can go to a certain unmarked area, force fire npc squad, enter a building and rescue some allies, with no knowledge as to their existence prior. One of them is a commando squad who can plant bombs. Then you can exploit Ai to rig entire map to explode with c4. Aggro the enemy and just insta gib everything present. Now you just need to deal with spawning enemies swarming from the either. Alright slaughter is almost done just pack up and leave through exit point. woops mission loss because you sent your critical squad out first. Reload send everyone else out first, woops mission critical squad last guy out piloting your tank despawns, losing your tank. But you won mission.  My experience alone in this mission is enough to force review to be bad from good. Regardless of rest of game. Not here to fight people. I want to fight the robots like Conner intended.Now you would look at the big ole tactical map and think must be a lot of missions and fighting to be had.. around 12 battles. Alright bet skirmish and multiplayer is pretty decent. There are 4 maps. Content is rather light. Although they intend to bring DLC to add on to game.. Probably best to wait until game is on sale at some future point and potential they have patched/modified existing game.

The game is really old school in difficulty , and , having played alot of them in ye olden days , it has , just like those games of yonder quite a few frustrations to deal with. What i mean by that is : the loss of salvage you've had your eye on, trying the last half hour to carefully preserve only to have it blasted by stray friendly fire from your units. Oh boy, does that happen a lot. Damage to vehicles and loss of troops is completely up to the rng gods so reloads are often because of these. You can't really afford to lose anything that's upgraded. But you know, you could make the case that it makes a lot of sense in the terminator universe more than save scumming. Which you'll do ... A LOT ! Did i say that allready? on the other hand ,when will there ever be another terminator rts? another ten years at least?maybe twenty, pretty niche this. Older gamers will know what I'm talking about. Pathfinding is janky as f***, infantry can get stuck on literally anything,a barrel,a corner of this or that building. Reading up on the missions with guides is certainly advised because of all the surprise moments the devs spring on you, usually after conversations on the battlefield . The graphics are a bit meh for today. Still, if it'd be anything more i bet my rig would grind to a screeching halt , what with the large scale battlefields and a lot of shooting that happens at the same time all over the place. to lose oversight is common. Units do verbally tell you when shots are fired  but it's not that clear who is getting shot so save often. I might have mentioned that in here somewhere.  anyways ,don't let this stop you from playing and enjoying terminator defiance. For all the aformentioned shortcomings ,the storytelling is very good and the atmosphere is nailed down .Action is aplenty and I'm salivating for the next chapter that let's me play with legion.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of potential, but feels unfinished in its current form. It has amazing detail, with ammo, fuel, and spare parts all taken into account--but detail doesn't equal fun. There are only four skirmish maps, with no ability to adjust things like army pop cap, types of units available, or win conditions--stuff that was common in RTS's decades ago. The gameplay is rather odd, with reinforcement 'rounds' where each round gives you an apparently random assortment of options to choose from. One round you may be able to buy tanks, the next round tanks are not available, then the next they are again. For a game that emphasizes logistics, it is remarkably stingy with giving you the option to buy logistics vehicles. I think that with some more time to flesh out the game design, or some mods, this could be great. I'd wait for a sale, and check up on it later.

_childDocuments_.review: Please listen to the people saying this game has big issues! I did not and have suffered for it.Cons:•conflicting, "buggy," under-explained, or confusing triggered events•extremely restrictive fog of war-Why does vision end so far in front of gun range? The gameplay loop involves continuously baiting out enemies who should be clearly visible to your troops.•high-end conventional small arms do next to nothing, even against human enemies-The game seems very 50 BMG-centric.•your units are extremely (and unrealistically) inaccurate at times-Example: a stationary autocannon on high ground struggles to land a single hit against a lone crawling soldier on an opposite hillside. Shots miss by 15 to 20 feet. (Note: not all weapon types fire on all enemies as default. In this case autocannons are set to fire on infantry by the game itself. I think it's appropriate given the resilience of machine infantry. Similar lack of accuracy occurs with small arms as well as mounted automatics.)-This inaccuracy is well showcased in the store page GIFs. It looks so cool at least!•the combat is extremely building centric-This is of course realistic however the buildings seem largely invulnerable even to absurd firepower. Buildings should degrade.-The player is at the mercy of building entrance locations -- be careful -- commanding your troops to occupy a building might mean they run around the entire thing to the front door while under fire! (This makes sense at times or can be absurd given there should be secondary entrances and windows for your troops to leverage.) Also, some multi-unit complexes have odd behaviour or unknowns as to whether the infantry can stay within the building or must exit to go the next section. I'd think busting through some drywall to the next apartment instead of running around on the streets would be the realistic approach here ..?)•strong buildings seem to benefit the AI way more-For instance, I once had 3x 50cal, 2x rotary cannon, and a plasma cannon all firing at a single enemy three-man squad who were holed up in a strong building. They just wouldn't die! Meanwhile precious ammo is being used up. Friendlies have no trigger control or sense of ammo conservation. There should be an intermediate ammo conservation mode between the on/off options presented -A single enemy 50cal in a competing strong building will  drop your most experienced and levelled marines even if they occupy a strong building from behind and even if other friendlies are already shooting on target.-Must we use sniper rifles versus buildings as Inforiel suggests? Acceptable, of course, but this edges the game as many of the issues do away from creative solutions to playing rigid rock/paper/scissors. Is there one correct way to play the game? Laser-sniper equipped rangers are super fun but the battles would take even longer, especially given the fog of war issues, if a specifically sniper-squad centric approach were to be pursued. I'm willing to try it but am uncertain it solves the issues of the game. Fielding more fragile units accentuates the issues around line of sight, fog of war, and formation.•the line of sight system seems to be deeply flawed-Your forces will dump shots into a large building even if the target they are trying to hit is running around the middle of the roof. They can't hit him until he comes to the edge but fire none the less. (Don't get me started on troops running laps in the big buildings..!)-Enemies and friendlies alike treat intervening buildings and cover as shoot-through-able.This is extremely cool when, for instance, a rotary cannon blasts over fences (or shoots "through" tiny buildings) and totally silly when tanks shoot at each other with no line of sight or chance to hit all the while wasting ammo. -This comes to a head in that you'll need to micro your anti-tank units or they'll just shoot fences even if a better angle is only a few feet away and they moved 90% of the way there on their own from an attack command.•there's no stressed or pinned mechanic (for human friendlies or enemies) to reduce damage output•there's no proper cover mechanic to make use of small intervening terrain or variation-Although there are hills and buildings, the game is effectively limited to 2D play.-That said, your units do indeed accidentally hit hills and other terrain when firing on-target. (There seems to be some trouble with unit accuracy when engaging at hill/cliff edges.)•the group formation option (hold RMB, thanks Inforiel) is too simple to be useful-The per-squad formation option seems fairly good, however.•there's no stacking/queuing unit commands or actions nor is there or on-screen path visualization-It feels archaic not to be able to all at once once choose the path my vehicle will take while supplying my back lines and moving around troops. This matters given land mines, AI patrols, and map control. The automatic path finding near edge of map can be problematic as can pathfinding on narrow cliffside roads.•I've yet to come to terms with the extreme effectiveness of smokes-Guided rockets veer off course without fail and armoured combat slows to a crawl.-Is the dev-proposed approach to buildings smoking them to assault with infantry in CQC -- ? This is a bit counter-intuitive given the firepower at your disposal; the animations show literal hand to hand combat when assaulting buildings. Getting close enough to do this is no small feat.•more an oddity than anything else, but I swear unoccupied vehicles take extra damage from incidental/accidental fireThe game is also missing options for quality of life and accessibility such as HUD size + preferences, in-game notifications, gamma, etc.Pros:•great graphics, I mean seriously, the game looks awesome •cool setting•very fun army customization•mission design such that you don't neatly tie things up but instead are caught in ever-increasingly complex and dynamic situations•the game runs totally fine at max on my i7 8700 and 3060ti at 1440pConclusion:I wrote this review because from my perspective the pros just don't outweigh the cons. I found that the store page and game price combined do indeed make some implicit claims. In reality the quality and features fall short. I document this here for the reader's benefit. Gameplay wise this game has more in common with the original Command & Conquer than Company of Heroes (or DOW2). It also starts quite slowly: I didn't feel like I had a good grasp of what was on offer until about five hours in. By that point, Steam rejected my refund request. Finally, I should note that I actually bought this game because I was looking for a difficult game. This game -is- difficult. Note that I do not criticize the high difficulty at all. I'm just looking for an internally consistent "simulation" with logical rules. The noted issues continuously pull me out of that RTS flow state we're all seeking.I really wish the devs would reconsider some of their choices. This game is super fun when it works. Unfortunately most of the time the player is fighting with issues. The game doesn't train your tactical mind, it bends you to its arbitrary patterns. Dark Fate Defiance really could be an all-time best RTS. I just can't understand why proper terrain cover and interaction isn't a must-include in a game very much presenting as "tactical."

_childDocuments_.review: OK so I have beaten the campaign and these are my overall thoughts. 1. The game is the type of game that requires a lot of trial and error, it is very difficult and very frustrating but when you do start to figure out how to play the game good, the game gets quite fun and enjoyable. 2. The difficulty is too much where it becomes no longer fun. I can see a lot of rts fans not having the patience to learn the mechanics of this game and to sit for hours on end perfecting it. I did because I love terminator as a franchise but many won't. 3. The game looks great, the devs really nailed the future war atmostphere and look, design of the units is cool and you do have immersion. The music and audio is also very good. 4. The story is not the best and it is not the story driven campaign with cutscenes I expected from a Terminator game. 5. The game put you in a position where you will always be out numbered, out gunned and have no reinforcements against an AI that has unlimited resources-this is quite annoying. 6. One particular mission (Cartel) is one of the most annoying rts missions I have ever played. Play it if you dare lol. 7. Despite the terminator faction looking great and seeing some of our favourite models from the franchise, it is missing things like Time Travel, Sarah Connor and T-800 despite them being in the Dark Fate Movie. Also no reference to the cyborg units like Grace in the movie. The Rev-9's are in the game but are quite dissapointing and just and ordinary unit. 8. The ending was quite dissapointing and the final mission one of the worst in the game but I don't want to be too harsh. Overall though, I did enjoy it for what it is and I would recommend it to most RTS players, there is a lot of cool stuff here and I am hopeful that the game grows from here and we get more games and content in the future. 7/10 score.

_childDocuments_.review: Halfway through 2024 and still THE best game I've played this year.Some personal highlights:- Old school RTS where missions can take hours to complete.- Tactical gameplay that emphasizes positioning and cover. High APM or doomstacks will not win you the game.- Ballistic simulation where tank shots/missiles can miss and hit things that are far behind what they were firing at. - Every single weapon has ammo that can run out. This forces the player to think more about how to handle each engagement.- Going back to the more tactical aspect of the game, any unit lost is permanent, along with the experience and weapons the unit was carrying.- An engaging soundtrack that fits the mood of the game.Between this and Starship Troopers: Terran Command, we have some great and innovative RTS games that are pushing the genre forward, and we need more of that in the gaming world today.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to spend a few hours playing the game before giving a review because I was a bit conflicted.The game is decent, I would say—5/10. Here’s why:Pros:- The game is quite immersive in the Terminator world. The weapons, scenarios, maps, and vehicles—all of the graphics—are impressive.- Some campaign mechanics are well-designed, especially the systems for managing supplies, morale, and your own battalions.Playing as Legion is pretty fun.- The developers have listened to the community; the game is no longer impossibly difficult!- The music is amazing!Cons:- The AI is terrible. Pathfinding is a complete disaster, with the AI glitching 8/10 times. It often cannot find a proper path, requiring you to guide it manually. Sometimes units get stuck, and you can’t unstuck them.- Animations and sounds for some units are subpar. Helicopters circle around aimlessly, getting shot while firing, and they make no sounds. Trucks and helicopters also lack sound effects, though Terminator tanks are somewhat better. The game definitely needs a revamp in this area.- The damage and destruction mechanics need improvement. An helicopter firing 500 rockets should cause a building to collapse and kill any units inside, but this isn’t the case here. Rockets feel more like confetti, while a single shot from a rifle can severely damage a helicopter.- The game most of the time really feels like it's on rails- Nobody is playing multiplayer, dead serversAt the moment I would not reccomand for the price, they still need to change stuff for me to reccomand this game

_childDocuments_.review:
Terminator: Dark Fate - Defiance is a real-time strategy game based on the Terminator: Dark Fate universe that follows the war between humanity and Legion's synthetic intelligent machine network. In the single-player campaign, you take the role of a commander in the Founders, a force made up of the remnants of the US military and guide your army in an attempt to foil Legion's plan to exterminate the last remnants of humanity. In skirmish and multiplayer modes, play as three very diverse factions: Founders, Resistance and Legion.

Take control of an army carried over from mission to mission on a series of large strategic maps. Make decisions about unit placement, battle tactics and abilities so that you just don't survive but become the leader of the resistance against the machines. Hone your skills and military expertise by replaying and achieving the best possible outcomes.

name: Homeworld 3
detailed_description: Editions The Homeworld 3: Fleet Command edition includes the Base Game, Year One Pass, Multiplayer Customization Set, & Digital Soundtrack. The Year One Pass includes three DLC drops that expand the co-op War Games mode with new playable factions and artifacts. About the Game Tactical, beautiful, and wholly unique, the GOTY-winning sci-fi RTS returns with Homeworld 3. Assume control and battle through fleet combat in dazzling, fully 3D space while the award-winning story unfolds on a galactic scale. Strategic freedom is yours. Hulking space derelicts called megaliths bring 3D terrain into the classic Homeworld battlespace. Use the crumbling remains of an ancient civilization to funnel foes into a brilliant ambush or hide your fleet from powerful enemies. Fortresses teem with menacing turrets and invite your strike craft into dangerous trench runs deep behind enemy lines. But not everything is in your control. Dangerous space phenomena like particle storms and asteroid fields will test even senior commanders. Attack head-on, with a clever flank, or even from above and below your foes. Homeworld 3’s fully simulated ballistics make line of sight and cover critical strategic considerations. Your fleet persists from mission to mission. Scars on your ships linger. Strike craft pilots and capital ship captains pass along critical information through battlefield chatter. Homeworld’s timeless art style evolves with modern technology, offering an incredible sense of scale, destruction, and wonder. Strike craft fly in formation between hulking Battlecruisers against a backdrop of stars and nebulae. Iconic ships cast silhouettes over the remains of ancient civilizations. Explosions ripple and erupt across hulls as one fleet stakes its victory over another. Homeworld’s game-of-the-year winning story continues. Since the end of Homeworld 2, the galaxy enjoyed an age of abundance thanks to the Hyperspace Gate Network. Cycles of plenty and war have come and gone. Now the gates themselves are catastrophically failing and Karan, who has passed into myth and religious idolatry, is the key to the mystery threatening a galaxy’s future. War Games, the all-new three player co-op mode extends your game beyond the campaign. Fusing Homeworld’s RTS gameplay with roguelike inspiration, commanders take on a randomized series of fleet combat challenges. Claim powerful Artifacts that augment your ships with more power, speed, and, of course, weapons. Based on your results, you’ll unlock new fleets to shake up your strategy. Your ultimate test of tactical skill comes in battle against human opponents. Sharpen your instincts in AI skirmish matches, before squaring off with human opponents in 1v1, free-for-all, or team battles. Mods allow players to craft their own content for Homeworld 3 and share it with players around the world. From rebuilding maps with megaliths, to augmenting ships, the Unreal game editor is at your fingertips. If direct creation isn’t your thing, enjoy the creativity of the community by downloading mods hassle-free through in-game mod.io integration.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is infuriating because it's like someone told someone else what Homeworld was like. And they ignored them and made this. _childDocuments_.review: They Add nothing new to Homeworld except of the wrecks you fly around. Great music and voice acting. But It is soulless. There is no real strategy no risks and the story is not great. The campaign is "fun" and the war-games are interesting but fall into the same trap as rest of the game, lacking layers and depth. This is a 30$ game that would fit in well with games that came out 20 years ago. I have "fun" but it is a disappointment for the Homeworld series. Just buy the remastered collection and Deserts of Kharak they are both better in almost every-way and cheaper.My more in depth review is the game lacks that what made the prior games so good and that is the sci-fi mythos and deep layered tactical and strategical choices you had to make in combat as well as but less so the verticality. The games story takes no risks, makes no statements, and does nothing interesting besides pass the the Bachdel test, which for this games quality, is honestly a surprise. It lacks any of the in depth systems the first game featured 20 years ago and has no real soul or passion. Its graphics are good and the voice acting and internal games coms are amazing but the cutscenes and story are almost painful to watch. I could have gone entirely without the cutscenes and just animated scenes from the original games which were simple and form fitting. The story is messy lacks any soul and fails to stay interesting. the whole arc feels like they wrote in the last year not the last five. It has so many chances and really good ideas but it makes use of almost none of them which is a shame as said earlier the voice acting is maybe the best I have heard in the last decade. I have many specific gripes some of the missions and how it lacks the feeling of fighting the enemy they are describing in the story. While missions are not bad but they do not take advantage of things they were bragging about in the fig campaign or promotional material and its because those things are not their in the way that makes the game fun or a Homeworld game. Its legally all there but not spiritually. They use none of the amazing mythos and layered strategy systems BBI them-selves built 20 years ago and it shows. The skirmish is just a throw units at each other and watch them fight in box "game", with almost no strategy other than click to gather resources and click to attack. On that note the AI lacks polish and or any actual character and is only impressive compared to the systems from 20 years ago. This game has many bugs that don't belong in a finished product. They say there will be adding significant modding support but they also made all kinds of those promises during the campaign to produce this game and have of time of writing this yet to fulfil. I am also highly suspicious of the road map as it seems to be promising tons of content at fast rate which I honeslty do not expect them to keep or fullfil. I would also like the point out the mobile they made about 2 years appears to have more content than this game. The skirmish and wargames also lack any of the strategy or much verticality even though it could fairly easy to introduce with very simple fixes like spawns above and below the space hulks and making fighter craft able to dodge. I would love to say all the other things I have issues with individually but I feel that list would be too long and would miss the point of why this game is bad. What I am trying to say is those whom were/are responsible for details aren't at fault its the decisions makers who seem to have simply made poor decisions that made this game the way it is.This game is something not becoming of BBI's prior games or work and is soulless at its heart.Many of these issues regarding gameplay were pointed out in the demo and it would appear they did not listen or at-least take seriously this feedback and one the quickest way to anger a community is not listen and show you are not listening. As someone who has bought the game I am warning who ever might be thinking of buying this game be prepared for that to be a truth of this game rather than a temporary setback.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game after only about 15 hours while taking everything slow so the campaign isn't super long. Its a very beautiful game and it plays fairly well for as intensive as it can get with the amount of ships you can build and control. Once you've completed the campaign (or before) you have 2 other game modes to play with. 1. being the Skirmish mode where you battle AIs or other players. Skirmish can be fun but its not for everyone. The 2nd game mode is War Games which is honestly great fun especially if you have a few friends playing with you. The difficulty scales with players and rounds defeated so you can always have a more difficult mission. Great fun for after the campaign as it gives some more story here and there. I've been playing homeworld for years now and while I will agree its not quite up to standard with the previous games its still an amazing time playing. The people complaining about ship size probably don't realize NLIPs is enabled by default to help people select the tiny little fighters in the sea of frigates and capitol ships. If you want a game to play that will give you a cinematic experience and a fairly close knit community then its for you. Be aware some aspects of the game require micromanaging so if you don't like games like Starcraft then this game isn't for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Homeworld 3

_childDocuments_.review: After playing through the campaign, I am thoroughly impressed. I have been playing Homeworld since the original release back in the late 90s and Homeworld 3 is a worthy successor to those games. It has been updated for a modern audience which may frustrate some old school fans but at its core Homeworld 3 is everything Homeworld should be. To me Homeworld is about a few things.... The Art, The Music and the Story.   Homeworld 3 hits all of this marks well. Game play is on point as well even if it lacks some of the nuance of the older games. Yes, the game play derives down to a lot of Rock, Paper, Scissors, but you have tactical choices and with full freedom to move the game is as unique as ever. Its been a long wait but I think that Homeworld 3 delivers a “Modern” Homeworld game with beautiful graphics and a story that adds to the existing lore. For my old school Homeworld fans nostalgia is a powerful drug and sometimes expecting everything new to be just like you remember will lead to disappointment. Give the game a shot the campaign is worth it and the other game modes look impressive as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Homeworld 3

_childDocuments_.review: Im going to leave an honest review as a homeworld vet, having played them all for countless hours (cataclysm ftw!)Having played and completed the campaign on hard, here's my thoughts. Story: Doesn't make sense. Tons of plot holes and discontinuity. Animations look super bad. Small scale and RUSHED missions. No time to collect yourself or your resources, no time to regroup, no time to reorganize. You just make a ball of units and yeet them into the enemy's ball and pray. It's basically GO GO GO. Doesn't hold up to hw1/2 standards. AUTO HYPERSPACE?? Come on. Structures get in the way, the whole concept of "send fighters into the tubes of the megastructure" literally doesn't work. Lots of missions are kind of gimmick-y as well, like the ice fiend and asteroid missions.Game play: "Its the DOW 3 of home world." AI unit pathing is really poor, units want to be on the same horizontal plane to shoot as the enemies in a 3d space game? Formations are useless, they break most of the time anyway and the ships collide into eachother constantly and just go braindead. I never even used battleships because they're so slow and never fire anyway. Torpedo frigates are the strongest unit in the game somehow? Audio: 10/10 fantastic jobGraphics: 9.5/10. Suffers from performance issues now and then but looks goodI really want to believe they'll fix the game play issues because i want to enjoy this game the way it should be. Alot of features from the old HW games are missing here and the AI falls way short from what we were given in the past. Currently i can NOT recommend this game in its current state unless you're a devoted HW fan....and it pains me to say that...

The way motherships explode like Star Wars VII, the dream sequences look like the cover of Three Body Problem, characters quote "Aliens" movies, etc.Very challenging to control ships with default settings. _childDocuments_.review: Look...After going through the idea of refunding the game before I even installed it (due to mixed comments) I decided to give it a try.  What can I say, I love it.I like the fact that there are callbacks to all of the previous games including Deserts of Kharak. Even Kiith Somtaaw gets a shout out if you play the tutorial.Love the graphics.  Ran this on RTX 4070 ti Super and it did not disappoint.  Hats off to the design team.Music is on point as usual.  Paul Ruskay is the man.Ironically, I have also enjoyed the story.  As cliche as it may seem I finished the campaign during a weekend and this is probably as close to an animated Homeworld movie as we got, and I enjoyed it.  Cut scenes were not at all as annoying to me as they were to other people.Of course, I do wish the campaign was longer, units had veterancy and capital ships to have subsystems.  Neat thing about Homeworld 2 was the ability to customise a carrier for a specific purpose (fire control tower), or disable enemy engines and production facilities.  None of those however change the fact that I enjoyed the experience.Looking forward to seeing what War Games bring to the table, once again thanks to the dev team for delivering the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Played 1 and 2, etc.  HW3 is good. Idk about full AAA price good, if that's your main concern, but i like it. Music is a vibe, the battles are a vibe, and wargames is a cool framework.  They have some bugs to squash, and hopefully they can move quickly, but overall I give HW3 a solid 7 of 10.  With patches, and more mods, and more content, could bump that to a strong 8.   Imo, too many people are chasing nostalgia/moments that they think a new title will somehow perfectly land as they did when they were younger.  Sure good/great sequels should be the ask, but expecting any title to match the nostalgia, imo, is setting an unrealistic expectation. It's one thing to ask for a complete, polished game. It's one thing to ask for bug free, or rapid patching support to handle immersion breaking bugs, that's fine. But what i see currently among the discussions, are something else to see people asking for a game in 2024 to equal the "remembered nostalgia" of a game from nearly 20 years ago.Hopefully things move forward, but thought i'd share my piece. I'm happy with my Physical CE, and am happy to play this alot into the future.Graphics - 9/10Music - 7/10         (i think the Vaygr had cooler bad guy themes)Gameplay/Strategy  7.5/10   Playability  7/10       (wargames phase 3 sync drop to 1/4th time sometimes) SP and Skirm is fine.Campaign Length - ~13missions,  ...up the difficulty and actually challenge yourself if it's too 'short'. Narrative was ok,  some interesting choices,  but to me, it's still Homeworld. Coulda used ~10 more missions imo. The game is technically gorgeous, and they could have kept playing with that to tell a longer story.Mods being available day 1 is a definite buffer to complaints imo, and i'm excited to see that grow.May the burden remain.
_childDocuments_.name: Homeworld 3

_childDocuments_.review: The game is generally mid, and the story atrocious. However, it has significant potential. If the developers patch well, HW3 has the core ingredients to surpass its predecessors. The mechanical aspects of the game have improved greatly. The controls  including camera movement and unit selection and movement are more intuitive. But, the newfound intuitive controls come at the cost of any sort of reliable AI. The ships spend too much time trying to get into formation and make confounding choices when engaging enemy units. Often times, it looks like ships forgot your orders, or don't know what to do. Other times, you can't quite right click the correct ship or the cursor changes to a different category even though you are hovering over the ship. Capital ships are WAYYY too slow, and there are too many structures that really don't add any depth to the game. The structures could be there or be completely removed and it wouldn't change really what's happening. The idea has potential to add depth, but without more sound ship movement AI the idea is dead in the water.There is too little variety, almost assuredly to promote DLC. It feels a bit cheap to have that kind of business plan but I get it, you have to make money somehow. Mods at the outset is great, and a lot of the gripes could be fixed by player mods.    Overall, I'm saddened by the limited scope of the game and some of the downgrades from previous installations, but I'm hopeful that the game can be transformed into something worthwhile with the right future changes. A lot of them are not giant asks. HW1->HW3 feels a lot similar to AOE2->AOE4. Some of what made the game incredible has been stripped away, but the core part of the game has survived, and could be the basis of a future fantastic iteration.
_childDocuments_.name: Homeworld 3

_childDocuments_.review: The TLDR version: The CE edition is worth it alone for the physical goodies, but the game itself is lackluster.And the formation control is what I can't stand and makes me not recommend this.The story is... serviceable at best, but the lack of ability to control my ships the way I want makes this a "not recommended" from me.There's a lot of little things that are just... gone from previous titles, and things that drive me nuts:- Support frigates are back!- Visual style/Art/music is god tier as usual.- You can swap the mothership's horiz/vert orientation now! Banana however you want to.- People like to complain about the camera or whatever, but there's many many interface options that make it behave much like older games if you want. Camera control is good and customizable.- Everything is auto-forced into a formation on move/attack. And I mean .Select a bunch of bombers and send them to attack and now you'll have two big delta wings going at it... no game./.. I didn't put any of them in a formation, leave them alone!So I cancel the formation except.... this aborts the attack order too.Basically, I have to pause the game, issue attack orders  to achieve what I want and it's just.... no.And not just strike craft. Tell a bunch of resource collectors to guard the mothership and they are auto placed into a 'custom' formation which just means they basically keep their current exact positioning as a formation. It's stupid and annoying.This whole thing just makes moving units  such a chore. A chore that didn't exist in any previous HW game.- Formation sizes are also automatic and outside of your control.You can't make one big formation of 20 frigates, because no matter what you want, the game will force that into three separate formations. There's no way around this retartedness, you just have to 'deal with it'.-  This is  still there. You issue attack  move orders, and the ships  obey. Depends on the ship and whether or not the formations will play nicely.- You are forced to jump out at the end of a campaign level. You don't have time to collect resources, so you best ignore the nagging fleet intelligence telling you what to do and go collect resources  you do the objectives, since you won't have time later.The worst part? .I honestly wouldn't mind it so much if not for that loss of resources issue. Not even the HW2 force-jump system was that bad.- You don't see existing unit move lines. What I mean is, in previous titles, if you issued a move order, go elsewhere then come back, and then clicked on a unit, you'd see the move line and destination again.This info is now gone, and you don't know where the unit is moving to anymore, so I hope you have a good memory of where you told it to go.Edit: Apparently this works  but  if you manage to click on the formation lead unit. The rest are just... nothing.- The Hiigarans have  corvette type. Yes, that's right, one single corvette type. So much for unit variety.I want my multi-gun corvettes back. :(- Finished the game, the campaign story is.... bad. There's basically only three/four people in the game. Gone is the overarching view of fleet command and intelligence and such. Now we just see the individual. In previous games you got the sense that intel was a group of people on a bridge working together. Hell, in Cata clicking on the main ship would even play audio where you hear "Bridge".But intell in this case is ONLY ONE PERSON. EVER. In a room by himself. You never see him interact with anyone not through a monitor.There's no connection to anything else. You just follow the plight of these few people and the overarching situation is ignored.The worst part is hyperspace has devolved into Disney space magic.In HW1 fleet command was a woman whom connected herself to the mothership to solve a data problem. They needed a way to coordinate all the massive amount of data coming in from everywhere and the neural connection was the solution.Now this apparently gives you super powers akin to the force, but with control over hyperspace. WTF. They are "navigators" now.There's a point early on where the 'enemy' hypers into an asteroid, solid matter, and just erases the part it hypers into. They shouldn't be able to do that, and it's a plot point of the story.Except the only time it comes up later is when  so this exact thing, and how/why is never explained. It's just Disney magic.There's a big plot point brought up where the enemy can just hyper into wherever they want and they don't need to use gates or have cores on their ships. (Because they are being sent from a location making hyperspace tunnels or something.)Except there's a mission where you are near a gate and instead of the enemy hypering in around you... they all stupidly ONLY use the gate which is stupid for two reasons:- It's heavily guarded (by you( and they have the ability to just jump past it. It's tactically stupid.- There's a SECOND gate on the map, which is completely ignored the whole mission. There's never an attempt to use it, you never have to guard more than one point.That mission is basically tower defense but with only one route. There were plenty of opportunities for curve-balls to be thrown at you, but nothing ever happens. The enemy just doubles down on stupid tactics.- It's short. I finished the campaign in about 12 hours. (Probably less given I leave the game running when doing other things.)- No more subsystems. This feels like a step backwards, but it's a design choice I can deal with.- I love the model that came with my CE edition, though I wish there was a silent option. Minor, but a nitpick none-the-less.- The addition of huge (and I mean ) progenitor wrecks on every map is great for gameplay/cover, but cheapens them as a whole. They aren't rare super massive structures anymore.I've loved the HW games since I was 10 and played HW1 so much as a kid. I cannot express how much I love the series/universe, but this addition to it is.... there's a lot that I love (mostly the visual style) but so much that is frustrating to deal with when playing.

_childDocuments_.review: This gets a thumbs up from me, barely, for feeling like a Homeworld game in graphics, design and music. However, what is here is bare bones with limited unit rosters and questionable design choices (camera issues, harvesters are heavily automated, research encourages zerging than tech rush, production is separate for each ship type encouraging spam, Wargames is limited to carrier only removing heavy ship classes from player use, etc.) which are incentivizing limited play styles especially when resources are set in the map center. I was never going to touch the story (Cataclysm was the last good entry) , so what is here is a new Wargames mode which I was excited about and traditional skirmish, AI and humans. As I said, Wargames doesn't give you access to big ships so your goal is to spam smaller ships, zerg quickly, and escape. It's fun but sadly in a limited way which frustrated me until I figured out the system. Tellingly, I've beaten the hard AI (no humans yet) simply by spamming and zerging without building anything heavier than a destroyer, only one which saw no action. (Edit: Just tried to tech up and not only is it a bad play but the AI pathing for caps appears brain dead) The original Homeworlds gave you a lot more flexibility in your designs and composition that I was surprised at how quickly I understood HW3s limited systems. All told, what is here is fine but there is not enough and BBI clearly needs to put out some FLC, not DLC, to win back the fanbase. There is a solid foundation but we need so much content than what is being offered out of the box.Update: Hate to do this but I'm changing to a downvote. Haven't really felt the urge to revisit this game and nothing in the patches indicated this game was moving in the right direction. Then the first DLC drops and its an overpriced modest add on that does nothing to address the games issues. This is exactly the Suicide Squad esque direction I was worried the game would take and not were it should be headed. Look at what WH3 appears to be doing for an example of working to fix issues although it needed stuff like this to get there too. I feel I need to join the majority and voice my disapproval here.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I want to like this game, I can't. As with almost every other review, the story is poor, there are clearly missing features (hyperspaceing, reasearch, etc.), and the game does not feel polished. A very big disappointment for someone who pre-ordered the game and has been a fan of the series since the first game was released in the 90s.Bad: Targeting is bad, unit formations are not consistent with previous titles, and unit intelligence is not there. On many occasions throughout the main game, units would just do their own thing even after being given commands multiple times. Additionally, enemy ships will kite, or attach user ships without them responding or firing back. This causes a great deal of frustration to the end user as you have to micromanage more than should be necessary, and while micromanaging you notice that the units are still not responding to your commands. Missions: The missions are a mix of not too difficult and broken enemy waves of capture corvettes overwhelming your fleet if you do not immediately do what "intelligence" is telling you to. There are a total of 13 missions and even taking your time you can expect to clear through them in 10 hrs or less. I played through on medium difficulty, and only had to restart 2 of the last 3 missions because of the broken waves. In my opinion, this is not value for the price I paid on the game. $20 at most is what this game is worth in its current form.Scaling and Unit Development: Playing through and assessing each of the individual unit types makes it seem like the development team did not really think through unit characteristics. Unit speeds, sizes, stats and firepower do not seem to be differentiated enough between ship classes. I watched interceptors move at the same speed as bombers and railgun corvettes, or assault and ion frigates do as much or more damage than the battlecruiser next to them. The mother ship does appear to be the fastest ship in the fleet, lol. If you look closely while playing the game, some things just don't add up.  Overall HW 1, Cataclysm, and HW 2 all felt way more thought-through, planned out, and better polished when released than HW 3. Hopefully the unit targeting, formation holding, and command following issues can be fixed through patching, but I don't have my hopes up. Of note, when I completed my play through, the first two patches had already been released and installed. The story line will be what it is, terrible, just hold space-bar.

_childDocuments_.review: [Edit] Changed review to "Recommend". TL;DR;Story is not what HW fans want. Is a character drama which doesn't leave room for player to imagine being part of as with most other titles in the series. Bad antogonist, long cutscenes and story is very boring. Good news is that the campaign is 10x better just by skipping the FMV cutscenes. Gameplay is really good, graphics are awesome even on older hardware. Sound and music is very good. AI for units does some smart stuff automatically. ----- original review -----I am a longtime HW fan. I have all the HW games for PC, and have played through them multiple times. I was decent at online multiplayer in a couple of them back in the day.HW3 is by definitely the best looking, has great ship designs, sounds awesome, plays well (which is very hard to do and groundbreaking for this game!), and has the most visually striking maps. Wargames is fun and replayable. I have yet to try multiplayer, but I see some potential there.The single player campaign is... complicated. It has mostly excellent mission design and execution. Gameplay was interrupted for scripted events more than I'd like but the missions were fun. The story, however, was not written for the HW audience. HW stories were always hand-drawn and focused on the journey of the whole fleet and gave us a big picture of what was going on. HW3 has full motion video cutscenes that are purely a character story about a super-capable young woman whose only real limitation is herself, which she overcomes over the course of the game. By mission 4, I wanted to start skipping the cutscenes. I just couldn't care less about Imogen's journey, the cartoon villain, and Alex who was supposed to be Imogen's foil I guess. The plot introduced only questions and no answers to the general HW story. It's too bad, because clearly a lot of effort and cost went into building and animating the video sequences. Voice acting was sorta fine, not great.BBI, please look at your audience and give them what they want from a HW game, never let your writing team think that they somehow know better. There are a number of negative reviews, and it pains me to be one of them. I expect a good story from HW, first and foremost. That needed to be your priority. You know your audience, so cater to it.

_childDocuments_.review: Homeworld 3 is a solid entry in the franchise. While the past four games are undoubtedly better, there is still a lot to appreciate here. 3D space combat is as delightful as it has ever been, and the new rogue-lite war games mode has been fairly addicting. BBI did an excellent job replicating the visual feel and the sound design of the franchise. Likewise, Paul Ruskay’s soundtrack is stunning as usual.The campaign does have a noticeably poor-quality story, but I would refrain from buzzwords like “Netflix crap” or incoherent culture war babble. The most disappointing part of the story is the shift from the hand-drawn cinematics of old to the new CGI scenes. Homeworld’s old cinematics had a great deal of subtlety, gravitas, and mystery to them, while the new scenes are noticeably more repetitive and melodramatic. There is some typical sci-fi schlock here, and the short length of the campaign can amplify this. Despite this, the story is still passable. The strong atmosphere and the actual gameplay of the missions greatly compensate for these faults.If this is your first foray into the franchise, you would be better off starting with the remastered collection. However, with the gameplay being as fun as it is, the new war games mode adding replay-ability, entertaining skirmish matches, and great atmosphere, this entry shouldn't be skipped. Consider waiting for a sale if the mediocre story and short campaign length is holding you back, but I would still recommend buying Homeworld 3.

_childDocuments_.review: As a longtime Homeworld fan, and one who holds the series near and dear, I was pleasantly surprised with this entry. Twenty years is a long time to wait between mainline releases, and while it certainly isn't perfect, I find it endearingly flawed. I can only hope BBI is afforded time to continue working on the series.The story is alright—it's a cut above Homeworld 2—but the cutscenes are a little disappointing. They range from serviceable at best to awkward at worst. While everything else is stunning to look at, the facial animations leave much to be desired. There are many strange moments where Isaac is talking to an eyes-closed Imogen, who strains her face while speaking. There was a lot more potential for a protagonist-driven Homeworld story that wasn't realized, I feel, but it was a solid step into new territory. I enjoyed Imogen and the Incarnate Queen; I only wish that the campaign was longer, as you can get through it rather quickly. I completed the 13-mission roster in a little under four hours.The gameplay lacks complexity, and the Hiigaran unit roster is pretty sparse. Still, the battles are spectacular to behold. Combined with the solid sound direction and voice acting, these elements help keep you engaged. They went above and beyond in that department. War Games is a fun addition that I'm excited to see further developed and tuned. It still includes the classic skirmish mode if you want to slam toys together. All things considered, I think this is a solid release that could appeal to both newcomers to the series and the genre. Even if you're a longtime fan, I think its safe to give it a chance. You may find yourself enjoying it despite some of its flaws.Edit: Tactical pause is being implemented in the june 1.1 patch for both offline wargames and skirmish, thankfully. Welcomed and much needed addition.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried to convince myself I was having fun with this. It's Homeworld after all; the series has always been a little janky, but that's what gave it it's scrappy charm. But no. This is big money entertainment trying to pass off a half-baked product, hoping the nostalgia value attached will catapult it into profitability. I'm a latecomer to the Homeworld series, having started with DoK back when it first released, and then playing the first two games after that (still haven't been able to get my hands on Cataclysm). I mention this, because a lot of reviews I'm seeing focus on how much of a disappointment this game is after waiting for so long. Well, I'm here to say that it's disappointing even without the context of 21 years of waiting. The first thing I'll touch on is unit AI. I know that's a strange place to start, but it genuinely mars so much of the experience that I feel I need to cover it at the top. The unit AI is bad. No mincing words: its . They've gone for smaller maps cluttered with megastructures, which is a sound idea in theory. It provides some potential for interesting tactical maneuvers. Two problems with that. Firstly, your unit AI can hardly seem to navigate its way out of a paper bag. Units get stuck on level geometry, make no attempts at evasive actions (even when a giant asteroid is bearing down on them), and frequently refuse to follow orders, obstinately sticking to stance and formation settings, even when being given a direct move order. The second problem with wanting to make tactical use of the new level design is that the enemy AI is, frankly, stupid. More often than not, they will rush towards your units in a big, unorganized blob, necessitating no greater strategic response than "get out of the way and shoot them in the backside". However, as discussed, this is often proves too tall an order for your braindead Hiigaran pilots, who would rather sit around comparing notes on how many eyeballs they all have than listen to a single thing you tell them to do. There's one mission in particular that I feel exemplifies how little strategic thought is required to beat this game. The Mothership is docked at a station for repairs, and you're told to establish a defensive perimeter while the repairs get underway. You're also given, out of nowhere, a number of turret ships and mine-layer frigates to do this with. So of course, you set up mines absolutely everywhere, and deploy as many turrets as you can around the gateway out of which, you are told, the enemy will begin pouring momentarily. About two dozen enemy ships arrive over the course of the mission, and you are able to sideline your entire existing fleet, while these new ships and defenses that you recieved  absolutely dumpster everything in their path with virtually no resistance. This is just one mission of the 12 available in the campaign, but they all exist on this level. As long as you're pumping out fodder ships and throwing them at the enemy, you're going to win; often with very few casualties. There's a lot of hey made in the story about how the new Fleet Command, Imogen S'jet, feels guilty for the losses sustained under her command. However, the constant navel gazing rings somewhat hollow when, at most, I'll lose a probe and maybe a few interceptors during a mission. I won't touch too much on the story, since other's have covered it, and frankly, it didn't hold my interest enough to keep my attention for long. Something about a cult using hyperspace as a weapon, Karan is the only one who knows how to stop them, yadda yadda. The only saving grace for this game is its visual presentation. It looks incredible. The units are all super detailed, the art direction on a lot of the ships feels right out of HW 1 and 2, and the design of the main antagonist is genuinely incredibly striking. But man cannot subsist on tasty visuals alone, and by every other metric, Homeworld 3 falls short. Do not buy.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR : It's nice, but it's not the best. Atmosphere nailed, lacking depth.Game is good overall, the campaign have a much more pronounced narration and is very generous with beautiful cutscene and dialogues. The game is really beautiful and really nail the Homeworld atmosphere. The gameplay also does match Homeworld perfectly in its essence. With the usual campaign and skirmish mode they went out of their way to create a nice Roguelike mode that can be seriously fun to go through. Now for the less nice part : the campaign feels a bit short, as only the 2 last missions are really hairy (but hairy they are !). It's actually not much shorter in term of quantity of missions than the 2 first game but because the difficulty is lesser, it does take less time to finish. I'd add that if there is nice addition like some special skill on ships, it does come with a cost : more micromanagement is necessary as the game is balanced with those skills, not using them make your fleet much less a threat. There is also less ship variety (only one corvette type for hiigaran) and the hiigaran battle cruiser is quite frankly bad as it is right now, with very tame damage and a skill that prevent it from making any damage at all. There is also no more modules system, which make your cruiser feels even less of a threat.Finally no more hyperspace system, none that you can trigger, which also take a way some depth.So overall, i think the game is enjoyable and is a good Homeworld game. But it doesn't feel the best as there is a lack of content on some aspect that take away some of the tactic depth of the second game.

_childDocuments_.review: I was going to hold off on my review until my upgraded PC arrives, but I just can’t wait any longer!I’ve been a fan of Homeworld since HW1, and I can honestly say I love HW3. I’ve played all the releases, and no, HW3 isn’t exactly like the others. But honestly, that’s part of the charm. Each Homeworld game has its own unique feel, while still fitting into the overarching story arc. With every new instalment, there are always some improvements and some steps back – it’s all part of the journey.The dev team has built something special here. Yes, the game needed some work at release, but with the latest updates, they’re addressing a lot of the concerns the community has raised. And it sounds like they’re committed to continuing to make improvements based on our feedback.I know some folks aren’t thrilled with the campaign story, but personally, I enjoyed it. I didn’t expect it to look or feel exactly like it did 20 years ago. Times have changed, and the story is good in its own right. I’m hopeful they’ll continue to build on it with new campaigns and add-ons.Now, some “old-timers” have said that Homeworld is all about the campaign. I have to disagree a bit. Don’t get me wrong, the story and campaign are a huge part of the experience, but HW has always been more than just that. Over the past 20 years, HW2 and DoK have been my go-to games – like old friends you can cosy up with, settle down, and lose hours in a comp stomp, trying out different strategies and attack patterns.I truly love this game, and it’s definitely worth buying! Give it a shot and see what you think.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't get the vitriol for this game.  I'm having a lot of fun with the campaign.  It does feel a little different than the original, but that's OK. But I honestly think they're a little shocked at the feedback and hopefully this encourages them to not abandon it. I also don't get the complaints about the story?  To me it has the same feel as the original.  Granted I haven't finished it, but I don't mind the cutscenes.  However, there are too many of them, and many things that should have been show through gameplay are just relegated to a cutscene.  Another  issue is that the game does feel less tactical than the original.  I found myself just grouping things together and throwing them at the enemy instead of creating strike groups and carefully picking targets.  The developers need to work on this - examine the combat of the originals and make some changes.  As someone that has played Homeworld 1 and 2, this was worth a purchase.  It doesn't fully deserve a positive review, but I'm crossing my fingers the developers will make this a truly worthy successor instead of just a good game in the Homeworld universe.

_childDocuments_.review: To be frank, I didn't know it was possible to continue this title. The team has blown up many of my negative presumptions (extensive marketing, pricing, staff firings, delays...).Perhaps Cunningham was overly worried about remaining faithful? It's definitely a hard comparison when you look at HW1/2, which is a shame because the QA, Devs, and art team did a fantastic job!Play Recommendations:Go hard. I am not the best RTS player out there, but this level strikes a good balance between being challenging and not too punishing.Alt + Right Click a unit to scuttle or retire it. There are no buttons nor key for this, at least in my playthrough, and it wasn't explained in the tutorials either.Use the P key! If you're slow like me, play at 50% speed haha.It should take around 15 hours to finish the campaign.To the Devs, and mostly to Cunningham:The DLC and addons are where I think this game could really shine. You've built solid mechanics, there are no crashes or glitches with a ton of units! But so were Homeworld 1 and 2. So what sets this game apart?I personally find the cutscenes and punchlines corny at best... We're in our mid-20s, if not 30s or 40s by now, right? Think of titles like Skyrim and Half-Life... Do you really need to invest so much in the cutscenes to make the game great? The story was just passable; it felt more like "finishing a job started from HW2" than trying to stand on its own. You need to pivot the story around the player, not the new navigator. You can't assume we care about her—it's the player's adventure! Yes, writing a good story is hard, but it's even harder to watch all the effort go into almost a half-hour long monologue about a world I wasn't a part of. WHY should I help her? WHY should I care about the Hiigara? Let us connect with the character through gameplay, not by watching a movie. Your homework assignment is to read The Odyssey, The Lord of the Rings, and The Ultimate Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy... You start with nothing, you build up, and watch your actions shape the world.A lot of the magic of Homeworld is in the big battles and the sandbox. I think the campaign had only one or two missions that were large enough for strategic play. Yes, there are some unique ideas! But I think that the game was cut a bit short... There is no way you guys made the entire corvette menu only to have one class available... And is there a real reason why players cannot capture carriers and battlecruisers? They look shiny, and I paid to have fun here, not to follow some "vision of balance" of yours so that "the end game could be challenging enough." We are highly functional RTS players; we don't need your rules telling us what we can't do, especially from something we were used to in HW1/2...Multiplayer is kind of middling in general. In skirmish, I am right next to other motherships (map size issue). I lost interest after the first time I played the roamer mode... too simple, too reliant on actions per minute, where everybody builds torpedo frigates and anything else barely works...I wish you luck in pulling in some form of profit and survive. it sounds like I had a lot of negatives but there just isn't any new and exciting space RTS out there right now ... and I really wanted HW3 to hit just right. Your team did a fantastic job in a lot of the stuff.. just not the story and playstyle. I still don't think is too late to pivot towards mechanics that can make something more meaningful. Because here we are with a game that probably won't satisfy the general audience, even though I think you've really tried. And, though I am very thankful as a HW fan, I think the original Homeworlers will notice the dullness of HW3. It's a game with a phenomenal backend but somewhat untouched potential. I will stay tuned for the DLCs.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Need more maps and better pathfinding but game is overall fun in Skirmish and WarGames. Campaign was entertaining and fun to play on hard mode, but dont expect to get any replay-ability on that (not like you had that on HW1 or HW2 either).Campaign Update: Now that I have finished the campaign on Hard, I was very happy with it. I probably wont replay it any time soon but I also never replayed the HW1 or HW2 campaigns either except to maybe revisit every few years. I think people have rose tinted glasses on a 20 year old HW1 campaign and get mad when people try new things to move things forward. Yea this focuses more on the crew, but you still feel like your crew is on a life or death mission trying to stop a apocalyptic threat that would wipe the galaxy out. If you play the campaign, do it on Hard Mode and thank me later as it actually feels like you have to do more than throw ships at problems.But with that said, I usually only care about Cooperative Multiplayer via Skirmish and now War Games, I am overall Happy with this entry and have had a lot of fun with my brother working together to win battles. The only few things I can think of that truly annoys me a little bit is:1. 6 Skirmish Maps, and only one of these supports 6 players. 3 are 1v1 and 2 are 2v2. This needs to be expanded upon especially on the larger end. I would like to see maps scaled for 8-10 players even if the player cap is still 6 based on current map size.2. No Hyperspace Ability, but right now this is not usefull except for maybe the one 3v3 map. I think they should bring this back to skirmish mode to add an extra layer of strategy.3. Path-finding - While its usually pretty good, if an object with collision enabled is close to a larger ship sometimes you have to do some of the thinking and manually navigate through an open area rather than let the auto-pathing do it. 4. War Games - No Un-lockable in game cosmetics (that I can see) and also appears to be a low map count as well. Although each mission has felt different due to different orders and such.The Skirmish maps will likely be fixed with the mod tools once released, as the devs have already announced that is going to be the main thing people will be able to make. I imagine this will carry over into War Games as well. I am happy they are experimenting and trying to add modes that bring replay-ability because who wants to play a campaign mission over and over. With further iterations and content additions, I believe War Games will be a great mode.
