_childDocuments_.review: This has been a tricky review to write. I've been a fan of the series since, well the beginning, and it is great to see it back after so many years. Deserts of Kharak was fun, Blackbird did a good job with it, but it just wasn't the same thing as the original Homeworld games.That said, this game has issues, and is a prime example that you can't develop something in a bubble these days without player feedback. It isn't all bad, but there are some fundamental issues which make it impossible to give this a full hearted recommendation, I'd say it is a 3/5 for me. Wait for it to be more on sale, but if you're familiar with the series or 'classic' rts games, I think it is still worth a play through even though it has lost some of what made Homeworld so unique.I'll start with the good: - The game itself is gorgeous, exactly what I'd hoped for a modern Homeworld. The giant structures are so cool to see as actual obstacles in game and not just painted into the background. And it absolutely scratches the itch for more glorious space battles. This to me is what just barely keeps it in the recommend level, I think mods could do some really neat things to make up for other issues. - War Games are also a neat addition, I have played some and really enjoyed it, but focused on the campaign first. As much as I might like them however I would never purchase dlc specifically for this mode.The average: - I took my time, and the campaign lasted about 14 hours for me on Medium difficulty. That's a far cry from all the hours I spent in the campaigns for prior titles (I have 48 hours in the remaster) and even a little shorter than Deserts of Kharak was.- I'm still more partial to the ships in the older games, these are lackluster for some reason, also I don't know if they're saving content for the dlc/pass or what but it feels like it is missing things. Units also just still feel squishy despite some balancing mentioned in the patch notes, I can't sit back and enjoy the space explosions because everything dies so fast.- The controls are improved from the demo, but still feel off, I ended up playing with a blend of classic and modern with a handful of commands re-bound.The not so good: - Units sometimes have a mind of their own, taking off in random directions or just forgetting commands and sitting there. Further aggravating this, there's so many in-game cutscenes that will deselect units and sometimes also cancel commands.  Worst issue of all here though, it makes is so hard to actually use the terrain cover system since my units will often just ignore and take off into enemy fire.- The game also overall feels light on the strategy part. Perhaps because of the frustration in issuing commands, it often just turns into sending all units to attack, they seem to actually do better when given less instruction. - Last, the campaign just isn't a great story and this we'll obviously be stuck with. The individual missions themselves are ok, they just do a poor job setting things up, like there's something we completely missed as a precursor. Going back to the shortness of the game, could have easily added a few missions to the beginning to learn more, catch people up on the history. Also the rendered cutscenes to me added zero value. I don't really feel like we needed all this forced face time with the characters which were not a primary focus of past games, a couple would have been ok to help frame the story but this was just too much.Specific issues for the devs as a big fan of the prior games:- Where are the corvettes? Aside from there being only 1 to build, you jump to Frigates so fast I barely even used them.- The research menu needs to come back, having them muddled into the build menu is poor design.- I was really hoping for proper ship upgrades/modules, something to add a little more strategy to the game than just temp abilities.- Why in the world do the missions end automatically? That was one of the greatest, most unique strategic aspects of prior Homeworld games that you could take time to regroup and rebuild before setting off to the next one (and also just explore and admire the zones). Also, am I even getting all the resources left on the map? It was near impossible to tell. I think you'd already perfected this in Homeworld 2.- I'm torn on the resource controllers, I kinda like that they're independent, but that was another strategy aspect lost now, having to protect the harvesting routes (or just move the mothership/carrier).

_childDocuments_.review: Homeworld 3 Review: A Disappointing Return for the SeriesAfter a long wait, Homeworld 3 has finally arrived, bringing with it high expectations from myself. Yet unfortunately, this latest installment falls short of those expectations in several key areas, leaving myself feeling massively underwhelmed.One of the most noticeable shortcomings is the graphics. Contrary to what might be expected from a modern installment of a well-regarded series, the visuals appear quite basic and lacking in detail. This lack of polish suggests that perhaps not enough effort was put into pushing the graphical capabilities to match current standards. The ship designs and backdrops, which should evoke the vastness and isolation of space, instead feel uninspired and do not contribute to the immersive experience that the series is known for.Gameplay mechanics, particularly the scale of combat zones, also leave much to be desired. These areas are surprisingly confined, significantly limiting strategic options and undermining what has historically been a cornerstone of Homeworld's gameplay. Its like being limited to playing on a football pitch, but in 3D, instead of being an open vastness of space. This is particularly evident in solo play modes, where players often find themselves overwhelmed by enemy forces without adequate means to respond, due to restrictive fleet caps and rapid enemy spawns.For example, early levels for me were fraustrating as being restricted to managing small fleets of about 30 interceptors along with a few bombers and frigates, in the face of continuous waves of enemy destroyers (7 at one point, which are EXTREMLEY well armoured). The disparity in fleet capabilities and the rate at which enemies spawn create a balance issue that shifts the game from challenging to exasperating, detracting from the satisfaction that should come from strategic planning and execution.Furthermore, the small scale of the ship representations makes selecting specific units or groups during the heat of battle cumbersome. This issue is compounded by a hectic pace that often forced me to slow down the game speed significantly to maintain control, especially during frequent and constant enemy engagements. I appreciate that the idea is to think on the fly and adapt to what is coming, but when the enemy can spawn a series of destroyers, against your capped 30 and somewhat under-powered frigates, there is just no match for power, and inevitably, despite your best tactics, getting wiped out. This need for constant adjustment disrupts the game play flow and can be taxing rather than engaging.The AI (if you can call it that) in solo play does little to add depth or compensate for the tactical limitations imposed by the gameplay structure. It feels like navigating through a challenging scenario with inadequate tools, missing the strategic depth and engagement that fans expect.The cinematic aspects of the game, which portray massive and intense space battles, set a dramatic stage that the gameplay itself fails to live up to. The reality of the in-game experience is a far cry from these cinematic promises, resulting in a game that feels more akin to a typical mobile game rather than a major PC release.In conclusion, Homeworld 3 for me, does not live up to the legacy of its predecessors. With basic graphics, constrained gameplay, and a lack of strategic depth, it might provide some level of entertainment for newcomers or casual players, but longtime fans and those seeking a compelling strategic experience will likely find it disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: Look how they massacred my [game]...As someone who has grown up with the Homeworld series, my journey with these games started with the original demo disc. The memory of discovering Kharak in a firestorm and making sure I grabbed all six hypersleep cores before moving on still gives me chills. Moments like Adagio for Strings playing, the Bentusi arriving to sell new tech, and the breathtaking nebula scenes were defining moments of my PC gaming life.Cataclysm (later renamed) introduced us to The Beast, a story where you transition from a simple mining vessel to a battleship, ready to take on one of the most unique enemies in gaming. It was a phenomenal addition to the series.Homeworld 2, started to show some cracks. The decision to give human characters to the voices took away some of the series' mystery, which I felt was unnecessary. Mystery is good; it keeps the allure alive. Explaining everything ruined some of the magic.Deserts of Kharak attempted to capture the same essence as Homeworld, but on land. While it fell short of the original's impact, it still provided epic moments, like the land ship emerging from the bay with the sun setting in the desert. Truly amazing.Now, we have Homeworld 3. The game's graphics are stunning, with amazing backgrounds and lighting that bring back the epic feel of the original. However, the cutscenes are a huge letdown. They are so disappointing that they make me want to cry. After 20 years, it feels like the lore of Homeworld has been reduced to a dumpster fire. The narrative direction is a massive disappointment, leaving me unsure if I want to continue playing. It's a sad feeling for a long-time fan.If you're a long-time Homeworld fan like me, you'll inevitably buy this game for the battles, which are still worth experiencing. However, be prepared for disappointment in the story.Wasted opportunity unfortunately.

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks and feels like good old Homeworld. Gameplay, visuals, and sound design are all evolutionary and modern while maintaining the essence of the classic games. I had a few issues and minor bugs but nothing that really was a show stopper. Some audio mixups, like when I took out enemy capital ships fleet command would say that I lost a capital ship, that kinda thing. The worst is sometimes guard orders wouldn't stick, but this was more annoying than anything. These are all things that almost certainly can be fixed with patches.The campaign is shorter than I would have liked. The missions were all interesting, very good layout of different objectives. It was def faster paced, but not frantic. I do wish  that you had a chance at the end of some missions to organize and gather resources, or at least auto harvest and dock, or just make it clear if its auto harvesting. I don't want to go back to mission trigger manipulation to try and max out resources. That being said, they do practically throw RUs at you, so I was never even close to running out.I only played a bit of wargames, but I think it could have promise. It's probably a lot better with friends than solo, though. I did not play any multiplayer.The most controversial thing will probably be the story. This was always going to be a really tough job to follow up on the old games. They went in a new direction with the story telling and style, and it won't be for everyone but I do not think it's bad. As a side note, I wonder if I played HW 1 now and not as a 12 year old like I did for the first time if I would be more critical. Pop sci-fi has always been derivative and melodramatic, I think how much you like it depends on how you feel about what it was largely derived from. The first game borrowed from things I generally really liked and kept within that theme. This one is more influenced by more recent sci-fi, which I am less a fan of. Overall, its a Homeworld game - but it is its own game, not just a rehash. If you are a fan of HW or would be interested in playing the most recent iteration of one of the only truly 3D RTS franchises, I think it's worth giving a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: Homeworld fans will enjoy some aspects of the game but be incredibly frustrated by other issues that are glaringly obvious. Most of the frustrations can be patched, but the trope-filled story is the games biggest failing. If you just want to see spaceships explode spectacularly and play a fun roguelike MP mode then you'll be happy. - The game looks gorgeous, with some of the latter missions being particularly unique. - The usual amazing work on pilot comms, voices, weapons sounds etc is all here. Everything sounds like something from the Homeworld universe - It feels like Homeworld. A Homeworld more akin to HW2 than HW1, and some people will enjoy that. They're wrong, but that's okay as long as they don't ask for squadrons to be brought back. - You can salvage destroyers with a single resource controller. They aren't great ships, but they're free!The controls are almost great. The defaults have some frustrating foibles and the 'helpful' things like band-box selection assist needs to be toned down on the mothership/carrier as you end up selecting it when it is nowhere near the box. Multi-monitor users will get frustrated as the edge of your extended monitor will sometimes not scroll but sometimes it will. - It's neat to see ships on neutral/passive actually hug terrain and probes take novel routes to distant targets around large structures. It's not perfect, large formations going through tunnels just causes temporary chaos, but it's generally okay. Unless it's the mothership, which likes to just hit large structures and stop dead instead of attempt to move around them. - The soundtrack reminds me of the generic, dull soundtracks infesting many action films these days. As in it reminds me of nothing. Previous games had great soundtracks, from Imperial Battle to The Planet Killers. Music that set the tone of the mission, gave you goosebumps or made you worked as just a great theme whilst you micromanaged your way to victory. Homeworld 3 has nothing of note, no tracks that sound like I'm involved in  a battle or building up to a confrontation. - Ships don't respect them, and only some formations seem to work reliably. Wall formation is just pointless as you end up with separate mini walls. - For certain targets, ships will seemingly prioritise them over everything else. No matter the ship type. So you get stupid behaviour like long range torpedo ships breaking off an engagement because a corvette is attacking them, and ion cannon frigates rolling around trying to hit ships passing them and ignoring the destroyer you're desperately trying to kill before it gets too close.Also everything seems to have a fetish for turrets. Presumably because turrets have a huge engagement range (outside of their actual weapon range) so your ships respond to the attempt to attack them by flying up to them. Whereby they get engaged by many more turrets and ultimately wiped out. Final mission I'm looking at you with disappointment on my face. Even the mothership will do this which is infuriating. And the final mission sets all ships to aggressive stance with 200+ turrets to wade through, so if you don't catch that quickly oh boy you're in for some fun. - Passive is basically suicide mode, Neutral is mostly okay and Aggressive is herding cats mode. - Large ships are dense. They can't fly in formation, they move around like someone else is giving them move orders and if you aren't micromanaging large groups of frigates they will do the stupidest thing possible and then double down as soon as you look away. - I played with classic controls, and found that the UI would happily let you issue a move order to a nearby location but when you rotate your view you can actually see the green move objective line is miles away. It's almost like the game decides where you click is an arbitrary value with an infinite possible distance, and the furthest away the better. - Ships feel small. You don't really get a sense of scale because corvettes, frigates, destroyers, and everything not a mothership is just all in the same size range. - The incarnate ships are actually half decent designs, harking back to HW2 designs. The Hiigaran ships are incredibly bland looking. - I never want to see another one of these ever again. We didn’t need the entire campaign based around every map having them, and 90% of them look identical thanks to them having the same textures or design aesthetic. Neat concept but utterly overused. - I loved the huge maps of HW1, the slow build up to a major engagement and the few missions that had a much more intense close-in action kept it interesting and helped sell that you were getting to the final showdown. HW2 flipped that on its head and had way more up close and personal fights with wave after wave of enemies which wasn’t as fun, especially with them coming in from sources off the map you can't affect. In HW3, every mission is in a small enclosed space, with huge numbers of ships being thrown at you constantly. Whilst you can destroy hangars or carriers to reduce production of enemy ships, the AI is cheating and ships do hyperspace in on some maps. Because of this, you don't get any prep time or space to breathe, so you need to be constantly multi-tasking, pausing and rebuilding losses. It lost the Homeworld feel pretty early on and other than one mission where you're sneaking for a small portion of it, the entire campaign is made worse because of the unending engagements. Even when there is a point in the story where you would expect to get a breather, you're dumped into a fight immediately.The campaign maps also suffer from turretitis, curable with 15 torpedo frigates with their special activated. The final mission is obnoxious for this, but easy with torpedo frigates.Yeah those CGI cutscenes are pretty awful and have a real uncanny valley feel to them, with bad lip-sync also not helping. Imogen is in a blender for some reason, too. Fleet Intel redeems it ever so slightly through a great performance by the actor and actually having his eyes open, but he still manages to produce a creepy grin every now and then. The editing and set pieces get worse and worse, and by the final scenes I actually rolled my eyes at just how bad it was. Overall it's just a really amateurish telling of a resolution from multiple other franchises. All of which did it significantly better, and it just doesn’t feel like anything is earned. Imogen is a Mary Sue character if you read the backstory, and the whole focus on S'Jet and 'Lady Karen' feels like someone skimmed Wikipedia and wrote the story without actually playing the first two games. - The HW2 story retconned the award winning HW1 story to create a treasure hunt style story and HW3 doubles down on the retcons but also contradicts the mess HW2 made of the lore to give us a story that I've already forgotten.

_childDocuments_.review: HW1 and HW2 were amazing games. A third was hopeful of being more innovative than the first two, but this was not. Modes of skill need rework, for example, EASY mode should be EASY, to train players to challenge themselves with increased difficulty later on, but EASY mode is too difficult for even veteran players. I think the game was play-tested poorly. Also, why do the women in this game have to be trans-ugly in games these days? They look like ugly trans, not women.

_childDocuments_.review: Less unit variety, horrible story, dislikeable characters, broken mechanics. The one new addition, Wargames, are 3 short missions that are simple and quite boring. You need to grind to unlock new fleets, but there’s no incentive as the mode is just not very fun.Save your money and wait for a sale, even then I’d hesitate to recommend.I love the franchise, and I was so stoked when it was announced the IP was brought and HW3 was now in production.I brought the fleet addition and booked the 13th, 14th and 15th off work so I could get a full 6 days of nerding out on my favourite game series.This is a hard review to write, as I’m so bitterly disappointed… Homeworld 3 is a  game.The full campaign is only 13 missions long, and can be completed in about 3-5 hours if you skip all the cutscenes (and there’s a lot).The cutscenes are poorly done and animated, and voice acting isn’t the best. No more concept art cutscenes that became a staple of the series.The story itself is a mess, full of plot holes and completely forgettable. The characters unlikable and the main antagonist a joke.The game doesn’t feel like previous titles.Gone is the calm, professional monotone of the fleet, and in it’s place is the unprofessional emotional chatter and arguments you’d expect to see in a school project, and not in a military fleet of highly skilled and trained professionals. Where Karen Sjet was the focused heart of the Fleet Command, Imogen is an emotional woman trying to find herself and her grandmother. It feels less like the epic space opera of the previous series and more like a badly written fanfic.Honestly, it feels like what Disney has done to Star Wars. They’ve last Jedi’d HW3.I don’t know how, but HW3 is a downgrade in every way on previous titles.There’s almost no unit variety in HW3. For example, in Homeworld 1.Strike craft – Scout, interceptor, Cloaked fighter, defender, bomber.Corvettes – Light corvette, heavy corvette, repair corvette, salvage corvette, multigun corvette, minelayer corvette.Frigates – Assault frigate, drone frigate, ion cannon frigate, support frigate.Capitals – Carrier, destroyer, missile destroyer, heavy cruiser.Support – Research ship, sensors array, proximity sensor, probe, resource collector, resource controller.That’s 25 ships, which you would need to research and / or salvage to unlock, from a game almost a 25 years old.In Homeworld 3.Strike craft – Recon, interceptor, bomber.Corvette – Rail corvette (yes, only 1 corvette)Frigates – Assault frigate, ion cannon frigate, support frigate, minelayer frigate, suppression frigate, torpedo frigateSupport – probe, resource controllerCapitals – Carrier, destroyer, battlecruiser That’s 15 ships, and the destroyer and battlecruiser are of limited use as they don’t appear to be working correctly and do almost no damage. A battlegroup of a 6 destroyers, which would be a formidable force in previous games, will loose to a grip of frigates. Despite the lack of unit variety, the way these ships are acquired are just given to the player throughout missions and require no gameplay to unlock, just a small cost of resources.Upgrades are done similarly, and are very sparse.Modules have been removed from the game, no more attacking production modules, ships or weapon emplacements on capital ships. It’s a struggle to get ships to obey orders and attack the correct targets, capitals don’t fulfil their role of anti-frigate / capital ships and get out performed by strike craft or frigates. Formations are broken and require constant micromanaging.The one new addition to the game, space terrain (wrecks, super structures, asteroids, etc) adds little but frustration as your fleet gets stuck attempting to path around these objects.Multiplayer maps are tiny, in 1v1 you basically spawn on top of each other and have no real option to manoeuvrer. Bigger player maps are not quite as restrictive, but still very small compared to previous titles.Boring and horrible.3 short missions, and you only have a carrier. You can unlock more fleets and artifacts, but it’s a grind and there’s no incentive, as the missions are simple and offer no reward for completion. Obviously, there’s no mods released yet, but I honestly don’t see many people working on mods. HW3 adds nothing over HW2 (apart from an intrusive DRM), which already has a thriving modding scene.In ending… at least we’ll always have HW1, 2 Cata and the remastered editions. Homeworld died with Relic.

_childDocuments_.review: Homeworld 1 is one of the greatest games of all time and I tell you this with a heavy heart; Skip every cutscene in this game and you will enjoy 3 a lot more.Unfortunately the devs have abandoned the game after the reception was terrible and my favorite scifi, one that came to define my life in many ways, is dead. Every day I check the forum just to try and ease my heartbreak, but the daily pang of pain is very real and constant. I've never been depressed, Homeworld was about pushing forward despite even the most grim situations, but Homeworld series' fate is something that I would say is very depressing. I hope in time I come to forgive Blackbird, however unlikely, but I don't think I will can ever forgive Gearbox for how they've massacred something with so much potential, for no real reason at all. 20+ years of fandom and this was the best they could do, designing a product that pleases absolutely no one and causes so much damage to the property that it would have been better to just not release it at all.All I know is, the people involved collected their pay and went onto the next project, never to think about Homeworld again. But I think about Homeworld every day. It's criminal.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game so far, but I only played about three quarters of the campaign.Its a good Homeworld game, but in terms of storytelling it does not reach the heights of HW1 and HW Cataclysm.A bit more fine tuning will help this game a lot I suppose.+ The Missions are very diverse+ Map design is awesome+ Graphics are really stunning+ Sound is great and immersive+ Every ship has special abilities that make a differenceSome topics had a rough start, but I think that can be sorted out quite soon:- Ships look and feel too similar to each other.- Frigates and Destroyers seem to be lost in space. There is not enough perception left of what sizes the ships are. In my opinion, Homeworld 1 and Cataclysm did a better job on that.- Tech trees are too simple, no extra Research development is needed- Building queues are non-existent. You can build whatever ship you want simultaneously with most other ships- The overview of the building queue is not very good.- In the interface it is hard to distinguish which ship has been researched yet.- Balancing is not final - because you can build so much its too easy to spam- Storyline is quite flat. Simply slower pacing could make a difference to get into it- Missions are not ended by the player but automatically end, even though there are resources left to gather- Pacing again: In some cases, new ships are made available in the midst of a battle, and the story progresses while players have all hands full and not time to get into it.- I'm missing the siege cannon :DI'll continue with the campaign and look forward to the already planned updates.For skirmish, Hyperdrive jumps will be brought back, which I definitely welcome :)

_childDocuments_.review: This just doesn't feel like Homeworld, and I'm not enjoying the game.   -The camera controls are clunky, you've got to constantly try to find a unit, then focus on that to get the camera to the POV you want to issue orders. The camera often ends up inside debris and turns your whole screen blue.  Exiting the sensor map throws your camera POV to a random part of the map.   I've been using the default camera controls, I may try classic camera controls.-The unit path finding is inexcusably bad.   Units just don't get to where you ask them to go.-Unit AI/decision making/order following is the most egregious shortcoming with the game.   The units just ignore your orders: If you assign frigates to a battle group with a support in the mix to keep them alive.. good luck.  They've split into 3 cross formations and left the support frigate alone somewhere behind.    You sent your interceptors back to the carrier or mother ship to dock for repairs?  Nah, they won't do that.  They'd rather hangout at some random waypoint, and die one by one.  You switched some ships to neutral or passive and sent them to a point away form the giant enemy formation coming in?  Nah, that one frigate would rather charge fullsteam ahead into the enemy destroyer group.-WarGames:  This just isn't fun!  The enemy AI has a massive numerical and ship class advantage that closes in from multiple spawn points.  The artifacts you have to fight to collect that are supposed to upgrade your fleet, often makes your ships weaker!  Each artifact you collect lets you unlock 1 of 3 artifact "upgrade" options.  Most, maybe all, artifacts seem to have a positive and a negative attribute, and often the negatives outweigh the positives.  You have to select one of those three before you can view the next artifact you collected.  Blackbird, WTH?!?! FIX this!

_childDocuments_.review: Like a lot of people, I was disappointed in the campaign. You offhand hear about worlds being attacked, and run into some evidence of it, but you never really feel the danger unlike the other Homeworld games. There are great moments revolving around your immediate fleet and it being in danger, but it doesn't really feel like there's any galactic level threat this time around. The villains motivations aren't super compelling and it's a little confusing who they even are. They just do things because they feel like it. They just sort of waved their hand and created a new-ish faction out of the dregs of the previous enemies, it's all pretty muddy. The campaign is also about half as long as you'd expect. Basically every map has super structures and because of that, they're all pretty hemmed in and don't have the scale other homeworld games have.The cutscenes are barely serviceable. I liked some of the personal stories, but we never really pull back to see whats going on outside of 3-4 people. If you're going to have a 3D character floating in water...I get not giving her realistic hair physics but have the hair geo do SOMETHING. It was super distracting. I really would have rather they stayed with the storyboard/motion comic style the originals had over half-baked 3D.Functionally, I like how a lot of the systems are streamlined. Build and research are now in the same menu, which I think is great. The number of units has been streamlined as well, which I think is another good thing. I always stuck to my favorites in each class of ship and they're all of the ones that are represented. The unit caps are lower, which I think is to get you to play more proactively vs building a massive fleet and killing everything with a blob, which I can appreciate. Pathfinding is awful - to highlight that, they put you in a mission with environmental hazards you have to navigate. I kid you not, I'd tell some ships to go one place, and a portion of them went in the other direction and flew right into the hazards. I also had a lovely bug just now that captured ships were aggressive towards everyone if they didn't have direct commands to attack someone. It was like they were designated ally to my ships, but would fire on the enemy, my ships and each other. If you're going to have the gameplay and map design focus so much on cover you HAVE to have a good pathing system. As it is now, it's incredibly frustrating to deal with - especially on the more high stakes missions where it's highlighted.I've only played a few of the multiplayer/ai maps and they're all frustratingly close range. Some other reviews have said it, but it basically turns into who can spam harassment units as you upgrade your skill tree wins. There's not really any surprises as to what you opponent is or isn't going to research and you don't have any breathing room since everyone's almost right on top of each other, even on the largest maps.Its hard to give this game a pass/fail rating when I'm incredibly neutral about it. I'm playing through it again on hard difficulty, but that highlights some of the issues I have with it. I do find myself wanting to pick it back up though (after quitting because of frustrating bugs a few times). I'm neutral on this game. I want the series to continue, but I want it to be more polished than this.

_childDocuments_.review: If you, like me, are a huge fan of the original Homeworld then I expect you'll like this game - I loved it.  It felt like a return-to-form, a worthy successor, to the original game in a way Homeworld 2 never did.  There are still things about it I didn't like as much - the lengthy, interrupting, and no-longer-black-and-white-stylized cutscenes, the lack of corvette diversity, the conversely large diversity of frigates, and the relatively few missions for a not-as-long-as-I'd-have-liked-and-technically-open-ended story to name a few.  But with all of that said: the missions we do get are interesting and varied, the combat is solid as are the units, the cutscenes are beautiful and the story's interesting (even if disruptive at times), but most of all there's a je ne sais quoi about how all the disparate elements of the game come together, from combat to the unit types/specialties to the map screen to the level designs to the story itself which strongly evoke, but without replicating, the feel of original.I loved this game, and if you liked the original then you'll at minimum like, if not love like I did, this latest addition to the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big Homeworld fan, played all the games and I would like to love the game. But after 16 hours, I am not really sure about it...The good:+ The campaign is entertaining and has interesting missions (although the story telling is very bad, see below). + Music is like in all other HW games fabulous+ Graphics and presentation (i.e. level design) are amazing, the Homeworld feeling is back!+ The performance is generally good (except when you have a huge number of ships on screen) and I had no crashes during my play through!The bad:- The campaign from a story-telling perspective is shallow and cheesy. I would have expected something with more depth like in the other HW games.- The campaign feels too fast-paced (no cool-down at the end of a mission to prepare your fleet or collect resources). - The balancing is not feeling right at the moment (it feels like the enemy has always the twice as many ships as you), some ships die too fast- War games are not very fun in solo mode, the enemy is always super aggressive, even on the easiest difficulty.- I don't like the behavior of my ship AI during attacks, the AI should take more intelligent decisions instead of having me to micro-manage everything.- Elements like ship subsystems or hyperspace jump are missing which made the HW games more strategic and interesting (but why?!)Conclusion:> For a Homeworld fan it is a must-play, for everyone else it depends! > The game needs better balancing, the ship AI must be improved and the difficulty of solo war games needs to be adjusted.> I give a positive review for the overall feeling of the game (a 6/10), but I really hope, many things get fixed in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is gorgeous. Despite being an simpler experience to HW2, it does honour the franchise and its roots.HOWEVER. The game is rather thin at times. There are no WTF moments. No "Karak is Burning" or "Cut us loose!" I was waiting for that holy sh%T moment, but it never came.  Also, I will admit I'm a little let down that HW3 is the shortest of all of them, including DOK and Cataclysm. At only 13 main campaign missions, at medium difficulty, I had the game wrapped in under 9 hours, and that includes the last mission, which I had to restart as it was the only one that really offered a challenge. I mean it's a good game. I guess I was wanting more. It has a singular plot point where the previous ones had you going off in different directions with different subplots. The cinematics were amazing, but they were also long...very long, and I wonder if they spent more time on missions, we could have had a longer, more satisfying experience. The previous games got by with animated paintings--did we really need near-photorealistic characters talking to each other for five minutes between missions?

_childDocuments_.review: Oh dear, I really wanted to love this game having been a massive fan of the previous titles in the series but I am not sure what on earth this hot mess is supposed to be. My play time is low out of pure frustration and I'll probably come back to this game and attempt to finish at some point but that will purely out of love for the previous titles in the series. I will say visually this is a lovely looking game and once again the music and sound design is brilliant however...The game play is terrible and seems riddled with bugs, there was a big song and dance about adding "terrain" in the form of space based mega structures which I confess on paper seems very cool. What actually happens is you ships repeatedly fly in to them bouncing gently off only to do same over and over again. Ships will drop orders and just sit still, take the longest possible route to fly around said space terrain before they get bored of fighting and just fly in the terrain again. All of the previous ship AI seems to be gone, dedicated anti fighter ships insist of shooting at enemy capital ships while ignoring bombers, corvettes refuse to strafe or orbit targets like they used to. There is a tactical pause option where you can remedy this by individually picking targets for each of your hundreds of ships but they tend to forget these orders and fly in to the nearest piece of terrain straight away so its not much help. It does mean you can watch your recently captured enemy ships forget that they have been captured and continue trying to shoot you other ships before they too get bored and go back to flying in to the nearest wall. The campaign so far seems to be from a totally different series, there are hints of the older games in there but thus far its just dull. Gone is the space opera of the old games, no tear jerking burning of Kharak, no Bentusi, no Kadesh, just strange women on acid trips arguing in poor cut scenes. I may change my mind on this point as I play more but it seems highly unlikely. Still, there is always the odd rogue like wargames section to play which I am sure will have new and interesting things. No, wait, its just the same as the normal game but with yawn inducing buff cards to pick from for each short play through. No idea why this made it in to the game or who was actually asking for it but it seems like a bizzare addition. All in all if it wasn't abundantly clear already I am highly disappointed by this game, even more so since it doesn't look like I am the only one so this may well be the last gasp of one of the finest RTS series going. What a shame.Edit- Finished the campaign. Wish I hadn't bothered...Edit Edit- Now they want £6.49 for a wargames faction that proudly consists of ships from the other factions.... If it was funny I'd say it was a joke

_childDocuments_.review: Been waiting for this game for 18 years since Homeworld 2 came out.So here it goes.I am very disappointed in the game. In total there are twelve or thirteen missions, with five of them taking under five minutes to complete. Homeworld two had around twenty five missions. The story overall graphics wise is great, but I still don't know whether the incarnate queen was actually a woman, or a bloke pretending to be. The dialogue was cringey, such as when she started humming randomly and the console listened to her and stuff, I was like howay... Overall though, I thought the story was daft.Ships and scale:The ships were rather bland, blocky, and a little bit boring, it sort of felt like when you played Supreme Commander Forged alliance, where units had metallic textures, and better splines, but then Supreme Commander 2 came along and all the units were blocky with plain coloured textures, sort of like Homeworld 3.I love the mega-structures in this game, but they are rather useless, I had thoughts about deploying my mothership and carriers in them, but they don't go through, in fact, the path finding is rather horrible.Unfortunately, the sense of scale is felt with the mega-structures, but not with the ships, the mothership for example feels like a frigate, and the rest of the fleet feel like tugboats. The mothership doesn't have any sort of metallic sheen to it to make it look like it is made of metal, and the same goes for everything else.Spamming units over and over WargamesWargames is fun, but a little bland, I know they are releasing dlc sometime in the future, but meh. One of my biggest gripes with wargames is when you become level 15 and unlock the platform build, but this build is completely useless, because a single destroyer can wipe out all 10 capital turrets, and sustain only a quarter of the hull lost.SkirmishSkirmish is boring, all motherships practically drop on top of each other in a 2v2 1v4 map.Things I do like about the game are the mega structures, the graphics of the structures, the atmosphere, and I thought the music could be a bit more diverse, like it was in Homeworld 2.I like the fact they included a sort of artistic book to the game, but they should have included population counts with the ship specs.While I really wanted to review this game, that I had been waiting for for nearly two decades, I just can't give it the rating I wanted. It feels like Homeworld, but it feels dumbed down, minimalistic, and overall the game needs more ships, they really should have included a shipyard, multiple types of frigates, and I am not happy that they used unreal engine, they should have built their own engine.PS: I nearly bought the collectors edition of the game for £235 since it was sold out everywhere, best thing ever was the bank cancelling my debit card, because they thought the purchase was made by an unsavoury fellow using  instead of amazon.co.ukPPS: TYVM for the points :D

_childDocuments_.review: Homeworld 3 review so far:POSITIVE ASPECTS AND OVERALL REVIEW: If you go to the remastered Homeworld, you'll find me expressing in detail how it's my favourite game in the review. So far, Homeworld 3 lives up to some of the expectations. It maintains the essence of what made the first two games were on a basic level while introducing new features. For example, in Homeworld 1 and 2, once turrets were deployed, they couldn't be moved. However, in Homeworld 3, this limitation is addressed with an 'un-deploy' option (but it does have a massive flaw I do not like which I discuss later on). Moreover, while the campaigns in Homeworld 1 and 2 adjusted difficulty based on your fleet power, Homeworld 3 offers customisable difficulty settings, allowing players to tailor their experience from incredibly challenging to a story mode with invulnerable fleets and unlimited resources. It's truly a game that you can personalise to suit your preferences in a campaign sense. Additionally, the inclusion of the 'War-games' mode is interesting. Some may enjoy it while others find it to be a weak attempt at replayability. Overall, Homeworld 3 is a mediocre game. The reason I'm not putting recommended (and it does hurt to do this to my favourite IP) is because the game is simply not worth the price tag. NEGATIVE ASPECT: One aspect that I find disappointing is the fact that coloured ship engine 'tails' seem to be locked behind a paywall, at least as far as I know. This feature was standard in previous Homeworld games, and it's unfortunate that it was seemingly removed to encourage more purchases. Despite this, the game remains enjoyable.THINGS THAT CAN BE IMPROVED: Things I believe can be improved with time and thought. Much of my review is tailored to my experience (which is a skirmish/offline mode type of homeworld). In-Game Pausing: So far there is no form of in-game pausing for skirmish or war-games modes. I understand for the sake of playing online why that is the case but I play exclusively offline and this feature is vital to having a more casual experience! Why not just add in the option for offline and remove it when online? Surely that's not much to ask for. To pause the game you still can press ‘esc’ and it will bring up the menu and the game will pause in the background but there is no way to in-game pause so that you can survey the battlefield or take your time in queuing orders which I thought would be fundamental. Idea: why not have pausing in online mode come up as a vote?No save for skirmish or wargame: Again another flaw because it was designed purely to prioritise an online experience. I play offline and would like to come back to my skirmish later on. Why not allow saving of these games for offline mode? Turrets no turret: First, I want to make it clear that the ability to deploy turrets to surfaces is sick af. However… WHY WOULD YOU MAKE IT SO THAT THE ONLY WAY TO DEPLOY A TURRET IS EXCLUSIVE TO SURFACES! Let me set up a turret in open space please!Ship tails colour defaulting: There seems to be a bug with the colour of the ships engine ‘tails’ that (even though it came in a separately paid dlc) the ship tail colours seem to default to blue with certain ships. Unit abilities: This is… interesting? I mean it feels really forced and even unnecessary. I understand there are downsides to using them. For instance, you can have a temporary attack boost at the expense of a weaker hull. Yet, why have it all? I mean its ships in space not a diablo game, which means beyond attack boost and maybe speed boost what else can you actually boost with abilities before you realise… it's  a space strategy game. Not rogue-like. No minelayer in skirmish or war-games mode?: So we’re just going to completely rid some spacecraft from certain modes of the game? Why are minelayers exclusive to campaign? Aggressiveness scalability: Please implement a scale option for the aggressiveness of AI. The skirmish and wargames feel simply way too fast paced. For people who prefer a slower-paced strategy game this does not compliment their tastes the way the original homeworlds did.  More map options with larger varieties: Why are there not more options for maps in skirmish mode? And lager options in general. These maps feel so tight and claustrophobic which again, does not help in the pacing of these games.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to give this game a cautious thumbs up due to the hate it's getting for the story. I've changed my mind.I am a massive fan, started playing the series with HW2 and have since played every game in the franchise with the exception of the mobile game. I played the mods, FX and Complex to death. Homeworld 2 is, to me, one of the greatest games made simply by virtue of its cinematic potential. Fights were absolutely out of this world way back when the game released and still are nowadays.Now why am I giving HW3 a thumbs down?I don't care about the state of the story, or the skirmish balance or the roguelike mode. The biggest, gameplay destroying issue with this game is the fact that your units have the self preservation instincts of a sloth about to be crushed by a tractor and the attention span of your average ticktock user.I am at the final mission, I cleared the first core and am moving towards the second. My battlecruisers are moving ahead. Zone clear. There's a anti aircraft turret plinking at one of my battlecruisers hull. The battlecruiser group is set to aggressive and they are just standing there taking hits, targeting objects that are way out of their ranges.Ion frigates are amazing, I love them. Please attack this other frigate group, you're all on aggressive. they fire a salvo and then start turning away. Why? the enemy is still alive I need you to kill it not the other thing that's being engaged by destroyers.Units move on their own, they hyperfocus on doing one task at a time, if you're not constantly telling them what to engage they lose focus and get into a semi idle mode that seems to react one in a blue moon. The game is frustrating to play, I lost 20 minutes of the last mission because the Kar-sajuuk started charging the enemy formation, my cruisers are deciding what angle they should come in, the rest of the fleet is engaging a turret on one of the top platforms that wasn't even attacking anything and my ion frigates are having trouble doing anything because the AI is programmed to hit center mass and this target is moving.It's frustrating, they made this game for a younger audience that likes fast things and units with skills. That's cool but at least fix these basic AI issues before shipping.I'll give this review another go once there's an update.

_childDocuments_.review: is there fun to be had here? yes maybe get it on sale. is it worthy of being called homeworld? not really.as of the 1.2 update ai us better and ship combat feels like it;s almost in a good spot. There are still a lot of instances where ships will ignore incoming fire or refuse to move when ordered. ships are still pretty bad at staying in formation and moving as a group to one spot. The superstructures and tunnels are not really utilized at all and feel like a hinderance more than anything.  there is a decent variety of missions here but in the back half it feels like you are swimming upstream against a constant stream of enemy ships. 1every ship has a boring activated ability that just makes them shoot harder. there isn't really any strategic nuance here, just keep pumping out ships and you'll be fine (i never came close to running out of resources).the story is an unsalvagable mess. Tt is never really adequately  explained what the big bad is doing and why it is bad, why you are doing what you are doing and why any of this matters. Things just sort of happen and take you to the next place where the enemy just happens to already be waiting. like most modern writing, it is overly wordy and constantly drawing attention and taking control from the player to say nothing of particular value.  its kind of cool how it flows from one mission to the next without load screen like previous games but that's really my only compliment.The campaign has cool missions but i doubt i'd ever play it again.War games is kind of a neat idea but it was a bad idea for them to place all their bets on. all upcoming dlc is focused on this mode which feels like a big mistake and nobody will really care what they do with it. mod tools are supposed to be coming, maybe modding in fleets from past games or remaking their campaigns could make this game worthwhile.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is beautiful. I like the way “terrain” has been integrated - hearing about it months ago and seeing it in practice, it makes sense, and it’s an interesting strategic mechanic. Same thing with the “modern controls” - I absolutely hated them until it clicked, and they’re pretty good. The story kinda sucks - I haven't gotten all the way through it, but it feels like something targeted at high schoolers, the characters are annoying (having an option to reduce VO, like in XCOM would be amazing), skip cutscenes, etc. not automatically ending the mission once the objectives are met would be cool too - please give me back my “hyperspace” button, let me harvest resources, repair and replace ships, look at the background, etc. And weirdly, subsystems are gone, which I know not everyone will care about, but I was expecting to see them. I personally like the way they influenced gameplay.As other reviewers have pointed out, ship behavior is "dodgy" and inconsistent. AI, balance, and behavior seems to vary considerably between the campaign and wargames, which is bizarre. The decision to omit on-map hyperspacing from wargames and skirmish is surprising, and not in a good way. It's like they developed two games with common assets and a lot of surface level consistencies, and then joined them via a launcher disguised as a main menu. All in all, I wanted to like this game, I wish I could recommend it. But for being so many years in the making, priced at $100 American (probably something like ten billion kangaroo pelts for my Aussie friends, poor blokes gday innit) for the "fleet command" edition...this is a misfire in my opinion. I think I have finally learned my lesson, not to pre-order games anymore. If you want something that is unequivocally worth your time and money, pick up the Homeworld Remastered Collection. In the meantime, I'm going to hope that wargames turns out to be great one day, and that some custom campaigns and mods come along to salvage the core SP experience. Devs: definitely add workshop if you're reading this.

_childDocuments_.review: Played all HW games, they are all on my "Never uninstall" list on my PC and have a dedicated list in Steam for them.Sigh.  Here we go:Art and sound are solid.Everything else is lacking, especially the story.  Not a big deal for most RTSs, but it's always been a mainstay of the Homeworld series, so here in this case it's really important.  Story feels very tacked on and focus of the story has shifted from "the struggles of the people" to "the struggles of the person" and it does not fit well with how every other HW game has functioned.  This is not a bad thing by itself, but unfortunately the delivery as well was significantly subpar.  Youtube will show you what I mean, I'm not going to go into it too much here, just know that this option is only for the morbidly curious.Gameplay is mostly okay but there are significant things that feel like they are missing.  Features that past games had that are missing here but without anything else to replace them and ship behaviors that are very strange.Each HW title brought something to the table that other games maybe did not have at all, or iterated on:HW1 had fuel, individual strike craft, and very strong capital ships that you could keep through an entire campaign.  HW:Emergence had much different fleet mechanics, varied unit types, and support units (SUs - think "Supply" from Starcraft).  HW2 added subsystems and a combat model more flexible than very strict Rock-Paper-Scissors.  HW:DoK had unit veterancy and brought back a very strict rock-paper-scissors fleet balance but with it also brought in excellent LOS and directional damage mechanics to still make it feel meaningful and reward good tactics. HW3 does not have fuel, no subsystems, returned to very strict rock-paper-scissors mechanics, very minimal tactical rewards, no veterancy, weak capital ships, limited unit types, etc.And speaking of veterancy; fleet continuity is all-but-gone.  You have no attachment to your units as you have no time to rebuild between missions and most units die fairly quickly.  This is all despite the art team doing a phenomenal job and designing a persistent battle damage system that will keep a ship with the same battle damage effects on it from mission 1 to the end of the campaign.  If even the big capital ships die so fast, why boast about persistent battle damage effects?The developer has put out a roadmap for updates and fixes but alot of the issues are things that the (Very long-time dedicated(20+ years??)) community pointed out consistently along the development pipeline.Multiplayer suffers from severe balance and gameplay issues.  The War Games mode they introduced, while a good starting point, has connectivity issues and limited replayability due to a lack of significant "roguelite" elements that most other games like that have.  For example, most other roguelites have a method built in to be able to shape your build and allows you to plan your way through the match/game.  HW3 has none of that and you are completely at the whim of chance when you retrieve a relic.  Oh your first 3 artifacts sort of pushed you into building into assault frigates?  Well the next 4 artifacts have nothing for assault frigates, I hope you enjoy trying to turn your carrier into a battle-carrier.  (The Battle-Carrier is not good.)We will see how this pans out, but for now - I would recommend waiting for a good sale and significant patches.

_childDocuments_.review: Homeworld 3 is fun. It  like Homeworld, it  like Homeworld, and it overall feels like Homeworld. There are some issues with pathing and utilizing larger formation sizes but overall it just kinda has the vibe of Homeworld. It isn't bad, its about as much of a downgrade that was between Homeworld 1 and Homeworld 2. The War Games mode is hella good fun and the multiplayer overall provides a better Homeworld experience than the single player, even if that's also where the map design (an S-rank feature of this game) shines as bright as LED headlights.I still think strikecraft auto-returning to carriers is necessary as well as them having fuel and munitions - this may be "skill issue" of me but some sort of feature to auto-reinforce groups based on unit production type would also make it just a more enjoyable game. I LOVE strikecraft but I feel like every game since Homeworld 1 has done them dirty and wrong. Ships smaller than capital-class feels wafer thin in singleplayer, some of them (like railgun corvettes) not worth caring about at all.The lack of locational/system damage is really sorely needed and makes larger ships feel either arbitrarily squishy or arbitrarily spongy. But the ballistics are fun and feel impactful, it's just a lot of the more complicated bits that need work. I am hoping that BBI gets that in time and I genuinely believe they will, given the scope of future updates.Additionally, the visual design is perfect. Some ships - frigates especially - are a little samey but they're still gorgeous. The comm chatter and voice acting overall is fantastic and exactly what you would expect following Deserts of Kharak.Now where the game falls apart is its story. Homeworld was a grand-scale story and that's more or less what its always banked on and remembered for, no matter what the gameplay junkies say. That's why Deserts of Kharak was good, that's why Homeworld: Cataclysm was so sorely missed in the Remastered collection. Homeworld 1 is a masterclass in 'less is more' storytelling. Homeworld 3 is 'kitchen sink' storytelling.Idiotic (but beautiful!) cutscenes involving random giant people in the hyperspace mind palace is just an awful idea. It doesn't work, Homeworld had this sweet spot of science fiction and it did not include psychic mind palaces or hyperspace wizards. The animatics of Deserts of Kharak were wonderful and memorable and in their place are a very sterile obsession with AAA-style presentation. I'm sure it works for someone but it doesn't work for me. It doesn't even work for the game. Remembering the villains of Deserts of Kharak, we were robbed of some genuinely cool people and in their place is some one-note idiot who at least is nicely sent off in the only part of the story that I like: the end.The story fails on multiple levels but the general gist of it is that it tries to be a grand-scale story and interpersonal drama at the same time. Imogen S'jet is not especially annoying or even written poorly in comparison to others but she is just exceptionally , which is something I really do not want out of a navigator and I think it makes the story lesser because she emotes too much, acts too much like a 'call to adventure' fantasy protagonist instead of a pilot or scientist. I think if the protagonist was Intel it would have been a better game and I think that every Homeworld story shackling itself to a S'jet is an active detriment to how far Homeworld can grow and go - look at the Somtaaw from Homeworld: Cataclysm and the supporting cast of Deserts of Kharak - we do not need only one Kiith getting all the glory. It just comes off as pedestrian.If story is important to you I cannot recommend it, but I will say the ending does "reset" a lot of what was wrong in Homeworld 3, giving me some hope for the future. However if you like Homeworld games, space games, or multiplayer offerings then you could do worse. I do not regret my purchase but I hope that BBI learns from the major missteps of the story here and adjusts accordingly now that they've really pissed a good amount of their goodwill away.It isn't a bad game, though, not by a long shot. Its just not a great Homeworld game. Just good with the potential for a lot more.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has only the very faintest traces of the DNA of the Homeworld franchise.The game feels very unfinished/rushed. The big new feature of terrain is essentially unused.Gearbox continues on its path of exploiting nostalgia for as much money as possible. Homeworld 3 is a sequel in title only; the story is not only by far the worst in the series, but feels totally out of character compared with previous titles. The gameplay attempts to be reminiscent of Homeworld 1, but due to a deluge of bugs and foolhardy or unfinished mechanics, feels awful. This is saying nothing about the wild unit balancing, and the totally broken fleet scaling that can be found in the campaign.As someone who never donated to any type of kickstarter in my life, being a Fig backer for this half finished, cash grab of a product is embarrassing.The kick in the teeth is the lack of communication from either BBI or Gearbox since the release of this game, with no official statement given on the state of its mechanics, the buggy UI, whatever happened to the story. The prevailing feeling is that BBI had a timeline and vision which Gearbox probably squashed into an earlier release than expected.What this means for the franchise as a whole is unclear; having this happen after the previous letdown of Remastered Collection is truly demoralising.At the least, the game is pretty to look at, although I can't say I'm impressed at all with the art direction when compared with Homeworld 1, or even with 2 and other titles like DoK. The enemy ships are particularly same-same looking, and no ship in this game struck me as iconic or stunning. The set-pieces are quite grand, and I think this is the only strong aspect of the visual design of Homeworld 3.

_childDocuments_.review: I am disappointed in the story, but I am not disappointed in the game. I still enjoyed playing through the campaign and continue enjoying skirmish pvp + warmode, even if the character-focused story I don't think fits HW and I also think the story is overall bad because I think the enemy faction/antagonist motivations is not well written. The Blizzard-style approach to character-focused RTS does not fit HW and its style of RTS hereIn other HW games, you care about the fleet/hiigarans, and their survival. In HW3 the story is focused on 3-4 characters, which is badly written and what the game wants you to focus/care about - although the progenitor stuff from HW2 is the backdrop here in HW3 too, it takes a back seat to the awful antagonist/faction and their motivations, and there is no time even to explore this, as the campaign is way too short to even to do that for a character-focused story. It would need to be an epic 30 hour or so campaign like Warcraft 3 RoK and TFT. In general, I don't think the format suits this style of RTS, and the previous games (including prequel Deserts of Kharak, not even set in space) understood this, and why HW always had its own style to a story campaign for a RTS.I recommend the game, because I still enjoyed my time playing through the campaign, and I enjoy the rest of the game, as well as the PvP skirmishes, and warmode. The pros outside of the story:I feel like maps for skirmish are too small, so getting future and larger (and completely open-space) maps will be a plus, even player-created ones. No hyperspacing in skirmish maps i also don't like, i hope they bring that back for skirmish/pvpSo yeah, I recommend it, because the rest of the game outside of story is good. I am still playing warmode and pvp skirmishes even though I didn't like the story. So I cannot give a thumbs down. I hope they make an expansion that tells a new story and they learn from the feedback.

_childDocuments_.review: What a disappointment. For old Homeworld hands, the story is such a bummer - some character driven "I'm special and unique" nonesense. Homeworld is supposed to be about humanity's struggle against galactic odds, not the dialogue between the forgettable good guy and the forgettable bad guy. They serious overplayed the character-driven narrative, which has no place in Homeworld universe where 1000s of people are on each ship. For new Homeworld / RTS fans - I don't know what to tell you. Sure it's got interesting 3d mechanics, but Homeworld 2 did as well. OK, it's got refined controls that make it a little more accessible and modern, but so what? There's nothing really *there*. The terrain stuff makes the maps feel claustrophobic where before travel and placement were somehow *more* important, though I do appreciate a new mechanic as much as the next guy. The ship design is anemic, boring samey ships with no depth, and somehow after literally 25 years nobody figured out a better way of saying "Select these types of ships in this area".  Even Deserts of Kharak took gambles on fighter squadron deployments that and subsystem / upgrade / veterancy systems that *paid off*! What if they had brought those lessons to this game? It'd be much better. It just feels like the magic is gone, so if you're at all curious, try Deserts of Kharak and the Homeworld remastered series. Leave this one behind.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing the homeworld series since I was quite young and could play them with my own money! I must say I loved the ENTIRE series. HW2 and Deserts of Kharak were masterful in their gameplay, story and PVP! Not to mention FUN!HW3 is... Almost none of these. The gameplay COULD be fun, but it feels overburdened and deep without being WIDE (Like the analogy about being a wide yet shallow puddle, this is the opposite.) HW3 is a deep yet size less puddle. (and i'm not really talking about the campaign here)War games are a seriously missed opportunity! The missions are somewhat challenging, but there's not enough... You only get a small taste of the full game and EVERY MISSION IS THE SAME! You don't get a full fleet, and the missions tend to get very redundant and repetitive. The massive structures are negligible and get in your way more than anything. The game has depth that feels unexploited and updates to war games just adds different fleets that don't inspire me to play because the game ends up not having enough or feels shallow in other areas. The balance of fun, interesting ideas are completely against each other here.I cannot recommend this without a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: In retrospect, Desert of Kharak betrayed me. Because it tricked me into believing that the same studio could be trusted to make another Homeworld game. The obvious points that have been made are about game mechanics but I'll list them again: Units behaving badly, terrain getting in the way, time to kill, even on larger unit is ridiculously short. If you hated yourself for succumbing to the siren's call of capital ships blob in 1 and 2 because you didn't know what you were doing  (as I was) 3 is going to absolve you of your guilt: Because with shoddy pathfinding and unresponsive units the only way to reliably get some damage on the board is to group every gun you have and slowboat them toward the enemy fleet. At least that how it was with the campaign maybe one of the other gamemode that nobody coming from Homeworld wanted to be the focus of the game ("yes, give me a multiplayer PvE roguelite for my space opera RTS" Statement dreamed up by the utterly deranged) fares better. The campaign itself managed to drag all the narrative issue of homeworld 2: That is overt reliance on mystical mcguffins and mistaking not contextualizing your story with giving itself an air of mistery. it was bad enough in 2 but for 3 not only is The End Near(tm) again but it gets drowned in the more personal story of Imogene S'jet the new fleet command searching for Karan the 400 years old Hiigaran equivalent of Moses and David put together. To be fair it is interesting to see a less emotionally detached fleet command. The audio call-outs in game when she announces the destruction of a ship get the point across of her being uneasy about her responsability in its crew's death. The main problem is that the whole narrative revolves around trust. About how the main antagonist of the game was distrusted and resented people around them for it and therefore think they could bring imogene to their side because she is in a similar situation. The problem is that the back and forth between Imogene and isaac (Fleet Intel) does nothing to indicate that at any point they could not trust each other. Karan herself is most likely akin to a religious figure considering the events of Homeworld 1 and 2. This shtick about navigators (If I was the guy that came up with Unbounds in Cataclysm I'd be suing about this btw) being outcasts and therefore, maybe sensitive to the antagonist's shtick doesn't f***ing work because there is nothing across the whole franchise that indicated anything about that and there isn't even an element in their own story that could maybe make Imogene consider her options. And I kinda see what happened (for one thing extensive rewrites over the course of the game's developpement) For the antagonist to make sense either Imogene or Isaac had to be somewhat of a bad person in a few cinematics but since the whold thing had been sandpappered by a dozen different writers over the course of several scripts and that I can't even be sure that Karan didn't have a very different role in an earlier version of the story (I was convinced, at first, that Imogene's synthetic cores were gonna be the material manifestation of a struggle against progenitor tech that Karan would find herself defending to dramatic extremes) All that remains (appart from The Burden(tm), JFC) is the two main characters being good friends and trusting each other from pretty much the begining making the antagonist promises fall completely flat. The whole Incarnate fleet that you fight the whole game are functionally Star Trek borgs exept the ship design are somehow less stricking than a dark cube. I don't think there is anything wrong with wanting to tell a more personal story in Homeworld, if anything Rachel's quest for her missing brother merged nicely with the overarching plot in DoK. But if you wan't character conflict you have to commit, if you want ideological conflict you need ideologies. And also you need to go back to the semi-rothoscopic cinematic of DoK because even on mute without the dialogue this stuff looks strange and I'm being polite.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I'm glad I got the game and am patiently hoping work is done to make the game great and I believe it can be.Campaign gave me the nostalgia I was looking for in parts, but definitely felt a bit too easy at the end on the normal difficulty. I struggled to beat the old homeworld games, but maybe I've learned a bit since those first days.Characters get annoying and story isn't really fun at the end. Started strong though. Some of the disastrous things that are only alluded to during the campaign would have really made this feel much more like a complete homeworld campaign.Music is great.Multiplayer skirmish AI is not fun at all to play against. They just rush out to get resources and keep throwing themselves in a fight over resources until they all run out of resources and sit in their spawn spot doing nothing. _childDocuments_.review: Foundations very solid, but implementation extremely buggy.Mechanics and graphics are good, optimisation is actually not bad, notwithstanding that particular map that lagged extremely badly.This game has great modding potential, so we can look forward to playing anything but the main game at least.However, plenty of things simply have not gone through play testing,missile behaviour is absolute ass, they can't hit the broadside of a barn, and will miss stationary targets.Lack of unit stats beyond HP makes understanding damage impossible, even when staring at it for minutes on end.Wargames balance is terrible, artefact stats are all over the place, and have buggy interactions(e.g. when you reduce your range a lot).It's an absolute broken grindfest, in terms of enemy HP, your units simply don't do damage.It does NOT have the fun difficulty of a rougelike, it's just a giant swarm of HP pool.Case in point, the enemy destroyer has 200k hp, your reinforcement destroyer has 63k.So basically to artificially inflate difficulty, they multiplied the health pools by 3.I've literally sat there with a popcapped fleet, blasting away at a single enemy destroyer stopping me from capping,and it didn't die until the next wave came. (I had 8 ions, it wasn't a unit counter problem)Unit AI/pathfinding is terrible, and it's not about "claustrophobic" vs "open" maps,long range units simply don't work, as they just float behind cover and start turning around to not face the enemy.They'll move into cover for no reason, but NEVER EXIT cover in order to shoot, even when you order them to.The unit drift is super annoying, your units will constantly move away from where you want them to be,while strike craft will stay still and act like frigate unless you manually micro them.Formations mostly don't make sense, they mostly serve to block your own units, and reduce responsiveness.(e.g. whole wing of 10 fighters turning very slowly while getting shot at, extremely large turning radius compared to HW2)Not to mention units start automatically forming formations that you didn't tell them to, and break up/change existing ones that you did; the same goes for stances.I feel like these can be fixed, and the team is clearly talented, so come back in 3-6 months.

_childDocuments_.review: "Oh you want to research the new ship that just unlocked, too bad because you have no resources because the game auto ends missions because we don't want you to have fun. Go replay the last two missions, including the stupid suicide mission that is not fun." At least Homeworld 2 auto-collected resources at the end of a mission when it forced you to leave.There are too many gameplay interruptions in the campaign. It takes control from you every few minutes. Can I not just play the damn game? Homeworld has always had interruptions in its campaign, but the sheer number of them in this one is frustrating. The camera controls are a confusing mess. "Sure you can use the old style orbit camera, but we won't let you zoom out using it." Why? "We want you to use the new camera." Unit control is unfathomable. I expect strike-craft to maneuver in a fight, but the lone corvette class ship we are given, just stops dead in space and allows capital ships to shoot non moving targets because *reasons*. I got tired of it and just sent them away so they didn't die, and they kept turning around and re-engaging despite not completing their move order. EVEN UNDER PASSIVE TACTICS. Why even bother if the units refuse to follow orders? How are you supposed to coordinate an entire battle-space if movement is so broken you have to babysit units to not die on their own?Imogen could have been a cool character, but the writing team decided that the protege to the most important person History would learn nothing from her mentor. At. All. How is she a protege if Karan never taught her about the hazards of being a navigator? The overwhelming nature of being one with an entire fleet of ships? How to lead? We don't even get a throwaway line of  "Karan had told me what it was like, but to actually experience it was something I couldn't comprehend before." Writing team did her dirty.The wargame mode is okay. I only played one playthrough on it, and it's really fast paced. It still suffers from the game's overall problems, but if those were fixed, I'd love to play co-op with my friends using it.I'm going to finish the campaign, but like, I'm not having fun man. I'm incredibly frustrated controlling my fleet, things don't listen, and the controls are really clunky. The right-click drop down of HMW1 felt easier to use than this setup. I think I've spent more time in menus trying to get the game to cooperate with me than I've ever spent in ui and controls before. A lot of things have me questioning scale in the Homeworld universe now. In the first mission you see freighters bigger than the mothership. The largest combat ships are absolutely dwarfed by these things. The largest fleet you can build could comfortably fit inside one of these cargo ships. Why is there a facility bigger than the entire mothership just hanging randomly in space just so it can hold the mothership's production facility? This warehouse is so big you could build entire fleets out of it instead. How does the entire facility open up like that? What's powering it? What idiot decided resources should be used building this...thing, instead of ships for the fleet?Some of the game is excellent though. The gatecamp fight is so much fun, and so stressful. The mothership's first jump through a gate is really memorable too. It's not all bad, there was some real potential for a fun game in here.Edit after finishing the campaign: I'm sorry, but how can you expect me to feel bad for the bad guy when our first introduction to them is an act of genocide? We are supposed to empathize with Space Hitler? Forgive them for treating anyone below them as a lesser being unworthy of making their own decisions? Nah. Miss me with that.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a blast on release weekend with my friends, we played maybe 20 hours worth of co-op in the wargames mode. I got around to the campaign and it is possibly the worst narrative sci-fi experiences I've had since the Star Wars Sequel Trilogy.They pulled the narrative back to interpersonal drama as opposed to what one might expect out of Homeworld. It was novel, but doesn't work. The antagonist is limp, the protagonist is a wet blanket. They bring Karan back and I felt nothing. The campaign scenarios feel uninspired and I was powering through to see what kind of neat ships I get to command. It really was not worth it.The gameplay in co-op felt somewhat tactical, considering the fleet limitations. Gameplay in campaign (medium) felt like I turned my brain off, spamming ships until I hit the category limit.The presentation is also boring, brow furrowing, headache inducing, and uncanny. I was skeptical of the critical reception of the narrative and went in cautious, but they really did miss the mark on what made Homeworld compelling.  A good majority of the cutscenes is the protagonist floating around in a chamber with her eyes and mouth closed and maybe talking to one of the officers. Sometimes she's on a screen depicted floating around. The rest of the cutscenes are in some contrived navigator mindscape having the worst character drama I've seen in awhile with a horrible villain with boring conceits.The best part of the campaign was the credits because I got to listen to some decent music and looked at some cool art. I wish they stuck to the legacy presentation via their iconic art.Had I not enjoyed several hours with my friends, I would ask for a refund. Game is NOT worth the asking price if you're in it for the campaign. I'm going to spend the rest of my evening lamenting my afternoon.
