_childDocuments_.review: Let's start off with Homeworld III isn't a standard RTS. It has many of the core mechanics.. ie resource capture etc, but isn't a quick drop game. Of course there are the pros and cons.. so in standard form let's start with that.Ambush tacticsLimited army count(Yes this is a pro)MultiplayerArt&SoundControl PrecisionPathfinding IssuesLimited map to playstyle choicesControlled Ship Counts.The ability to hide your strike craft inside crevices and pop out behind someone with the damage being increased if you attack from behind is so satisfying.Due to the limited amount of resources on the skirmish maps this rarely comes into play but when one person manages to max out ship count those that find themselves behind still stand a chance with good tactics.This means the game will stick around for awhile.. as everyone that plays RTSs knows this is what matters in RTS games.The game is just beautiful.. I think this one has been beat by other reviewers. The mechanics in the game are very reliant on precise controls but the ability to do this just isn't there. (Why cant you land turrets on any surface other than player owned ships?)The auto move of ships.. but really the fading into walls will at some point lead to someone figuring out a way to drop their mothership inside the terrain and thus making it very difficult to destroy.This is just a lack of open maps, I understand the reason but having even 1 would be nice. (Yes, the reason is two of the major mechanics would be rendered moot)This restricts the fleet makeup.. and has always bothered me with homeworld. There is a reason most RTSs just use a 'point' system to determine army counts.TL:DR It's a great game, but not perfect :)

_childDocuments_.review: I wish i could recommend this. So hard. I wish I loved it, and that i could say BBI made another HW classic. But it they did not. This is a barely passable "ok" Homeworld game, and worse at every turn than the first two games (as much as HW2 was hated compared to 1) and MUCH worse in terms of story and mechanics than Deserts of Kharak. Another great game gimped by developers too afraid to make a new, complex, space RTS game. Babied down and simplified to a sad mobile game. Kindly ♥♥♥♥ off BBI. BBI had the chance to make another magnificent, epic space game. Whom ever wrote this games story line, I understand wanting to make it more personal and about the characters, but you simply failed on the first task, this game is NOT about the S'jet or Karan or any Hiigaran. Its "Homeworld". Its about an epic space journey to reclaim their Homeworld (HW1), about saving it from a power mad warlord that nearly destroyed it(HW2), or in this case, about... yet another warlord that slept for thousands of years and wants to take over the galaxy? This is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Star Wars sequels levels of bad in terms of writing. Writing should have kept the distance from the player and characters, and stick to an epic space opera instead of some weird soap opera storyline.So the story is ♥♥♥♥, they decided to stick to some low res animated shorts for a reason, instead of the cool schematic style - war room shorts of ALL previous games, and making it more cringe in the process. Deserts of Kharak had it so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ right, I don't know how you guys ♥♥♥♥♥♥ this one up. Movement is dumb as ♥♥♥♥, and everything is AGAIN simplified as ♥♥♥♥. Less ship types, LESS player management overall (collectors are basically automatic?) and no research ships. Fleet management is about as dumb as point and click. And yeah the new controls SUCK. I can't believe this is the same team that delivered the last entry. The mothership in the Skirmish is just a fat target capable of NOTHING. Unlike carriers in DoK, where you could decide to make your carrier a powerhouse, this here is just a production house. Also there is no Queue, just somehow all ships are in production all the time, there are no upgrades for the mothership in skirmish mode or ANY meaningful interaction with it other than building ♥♥♥♥, moving it or blowing it up. The graphics, sounds design and ship design are top ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ notch, but everything else is a massive let down. What happened? Is this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ PC game or a Mobile game? The formations are okay but UNIT behaviors are ♥♥♥♥. We don't even get a hold position mode? WHAT the ♥♥♥♥. Its either don't shoot, or chase into blind fire. Units love to wander by themselves everywhere. Ranges of engagements are poorly understood visually and mechanics wise. Sigh... at least the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ turrets are functional unlike HW2. Also I'm sure some units are bugged as they just refuse to shoot sometimes. Even things like the cores clipping through ships during the last campaign mission tick me off. WHY? WHY was there not enough attention to detail if this was delayed so much? You could have done better BBI. Deserts of Kharak was a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love letter to all of us the long time fans, and gave me faith in you. But the titular sequel? You missed the mark. Big ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ time. Doesn't mean I don't want a Homeworld 4 game, but this is a bit sad. Things they got right? Sound design, UI, ship design, Map design (even if they are 12 by 12 inch shoeboxes), the idea of a quick and easy coop mode, the campaign levels are fun too. here is sadly, less to like and plenty more to dislike.Please fix this. Make the mothership a useful thing, like carriers in DoK. Give us better unit behaviors, or at least a HOLD POSITION and SHOOT ALL ♥♥♥♥ mode. The campaign is GONE, you certainly can't go back and fix that mess, but the voice acting did everything it could to save it. The auto cover and interesting maps are certainly a win too. Wish we had some more claustrophobic maps. And to all fans, if you simply want a better game, go look at Nebulous: Fleet Command.

_childDocuments_.review: I was introduced to the Homeworld series in 2004 with Homeworld 2. It became one of my favorite strategy games ever. I had been so excited for Homeworld 3. So excited!And then I started playing it. A visual spectacle, I was back to feeling like my old high school self. And then the story began to unfold, and I was unsettled. Without spoilers, Homeworld 3's campaign is abysmal and an insult to this game's universe and playerbase. It's by far one of the worst stories ever told and focuses down the trials of entire civilizations to merely 3-4 characters. These characters are poorly written and have the worst dialogue and acting. Do not get me started on the hyperspace interactions. I ended up skipping most of the cutscenes because they were *that* bad.So, campaign aside, the War Games looked fun at least to somewhat salvage this travesty. My first-ever game, I am bugged from success. Salvage parts: sounds easy. Nope! Carrier won't accept the parts and one of the salvage parts is off the map and unobtainable. I am angry that I spent money on this game. Do yourself a favor, and don't.

_childDocuments_.review: Was really excited for this release, but sadly it doesn't even hold up to the most basic requirements.Gameplay:The interface, while relatively simple doesn't show enough information. Having to fight with a Ressource Unit that's next to about 10k RUs but refuses to harvest is the opposite of fun, especially as you're being brigaded by enemies,The much hyped use of terrain is completely useless when your units refuse to use the cover or get stuck in it.Some units are just TOO good, working well against everything, kinda making the other units worthless.Story: The story, it's just not good. _childDocuments_.review: As always there are different opinions. Some people might find the story boring, some enjoy the story. I've read articles of different gaming magazines and while some praise the same aspects of the game they have opposite perspectives on other.I enjoy the modern look of the game, detailed ship models, great effects, wonderful backgrounds and interactive superstructures. Of course you will find some smashie textures, some artifacts and maybe some aspects of the graphics you do not like. I haven't seen a game like this in the past years. The graphics are lovely and full of passion.Same for the sound. You get the goosebumps from the old Homeworld, the intense feeling when Hiigara burns, the "crying" of the choir and sadness of the voice of the mothershop S'Jet. It is not the same but similar with new nuances. The sound quite often is in the background, supporting the level. Many many tracks for each part of the story and stage you're in.Gameplay. You can play it the old way if you want, or a modern outline of controlling the battle or just mix it. It wanted to give the new controls a try, it works. I am sure there are people not happy and their criticism might be valid, I don't really have something I would critisize at the moment. The amount of units is totally fine at the moment. More only means more to balance (an issue in past Homeworld games) and less overall units to play with.The story is the heart of the game. I've read from magazines they were done within 8 hours, others stated 15 hours. I will see how long I will take and more important, if I want to play a second time through the game. The start was intense, well explained and interesting. The mothershop taking off the planets surface....whow. The many little story snippets during the fight are to help understand the development, Imogen S'Jet, the head of the mothership and though during the course of the story you might see some flaws and issues in the telling, some think it is boring, it keeps me waiting to see the end. Isn't that the goal? When I think of many movies and how many flaws you can find in the story.... I think this is very subjective in the end though some stuff could have been presented differently. Too much to pay? This is what I read from some recensations. Well it is not a cheap game. You're paying quite some money to play 15 to 20 hours (or more if you enjoy the modes or less if you don't like the game at all but that has probably nothing to do with the amount of time you could spend with the game).I have played Homeworld 1, Cataclysm, 2, the remastered versions and Deserts of Kharak. I want to say: I know Homeworld. But it doesn't matter if you are a fan of the old Homeworld or start this game as someone never playing anything like that before. It is not the same people (I guess) creating the game nor can we expect to get the same more than 20 years later. You will also not get "Star Trek The Next Generation" back or any other 20 or more year old production because people and their priorities change, the demand changes. Expecting a Homeworld 3 that is basically a homage of Homeworld 1 is not what people do nowadays. As time changes, games are and demands. Initially the release date was withdrawn after the feedback of the Demo. What game/publishers do this nowadays? Listen to feedback to improve the game? I remember many games being released with tons of bugs or in Early Access state. This game is polished.If you're looking for Homeworld 1, play remastered or the many mods. If you want a new Homeworld, with its many additions, new game mechanics and wonderful presentation. There is of course more potential in the game. Therefore I am eager to see what future brings. Mothership....

_childDocuments_.review: Edit - One big thing I've noticed is the religious symbolism is no longer quite as pervasive as it was in the previous two games.  It's still there, just takes a bit longer to notice.First off.  Fleet Command ain't bald.  Cardinal sin right there.  Secondly, Fleet Command is unprepared, abruptly thrust into an unexpected position and situation.  I think that explains people's complaints about her sounding unprofessional, immature... human.  Her compatriots helping manage the ship call her on this in the intro, as well.  Everything points to a leader far out of her comfort zone despite being both hand-picked and the best qualified for the role.  She does have a bit of an unfortunate chin, but maybe that's why she went into the space program.  Not everyone needs to be a supermodel and it is really nice to see the team showcase the new graphics.  Probably why she's got hair.  They wanted it to look cool.  The voice acting is quite well done.  They clearly spent time putting personality into it.  Why not?  If they didn't may as well use AI and save a buck.  I was pleased to see a variety of many different voices for different things.  New storage capacity of modern hardware compared to the first game on a single CD (I bought the disc version three times and played it enough to wear it out twice as many times).  Everything from the menues to the game itself are littered with nostalgic tidbits.  Visual artifacts on the edges of the launch screen strongly reminiscent of the first Homeworld.  Expands upon the lore of the previous games quite a bit.  Some changes with what keybinds do what compared to the previous games and the salvager and resource collectors have been integrated into the resource controller which is a nice change.  Managing all of those ships could get quite tedious with how large your fleet of combat ships can get.P.S. As an added bonus they got the Temu Jordan Howlett to be your proverbial co-pilot for the journey.  The "rerun" missions also seem different enough to me to still pose a challenge and have some deviations to keep them spicy.

_childDocuments_.review: So I didn't want to review this game until I had at least completed the campaign, but after six hours its...physically difficult to make myself continue. Playing this game is, for anyone who loved the old Homeworld games, depressing.I'll also start by mentioning that I am a big fan of the other Homeworld games, I backed both the HW Remastered collection and this game and I have the little mothership statuettes sitting on my desk as I type. Although I may have to turn them away so they don't see what I'm about to type...Lets start with the good;The graphics look great, if a little too shiny. Ships are awesome, the maps look cool, and in general it has a good level of visual polish. I find the ship designs a little lacking, there is a lack of connection to the older Higaaran designs that I don't quite like, but overall ok.Gameplay is nice, they've addressed a lot of the problems with the older games and brought back some nice features from Homeworld one. Being able to fly through tunnels inside structures is cool, although a bit situational, and the rock/paper/scissors elements are strong enough that it does feel nessasary to bring suitable counters for different ship types. The ship selection is somewhat limited, and some ships are a bit unbalanced compared to others, but thats fixable.Ok, now for EVERYTHING ELSE!The story is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and the characters empty. Old homeworld games had really powerful storytelling, that was only enhanced by the facelessness of the characters. We didn't know who Fleet Command was, we didn't know their face, only their voice. Sure, we need Karan's name, but even then the game was never framed as "Karan S'Jet vs the Taidan/Vaygr". It was the people of Hiigara fighting to reclaim their homeworld, and then fighting to save it. The narrative had weight behind it, it made you care about the stakes. Heck, it HAD stakes. You see Kushan burn, you see the Vaygr blasting Hiigara from orbit.This game tho, has none of that. Firstly, giving the characters explicit faces and names was a terrible choice. It separates them from the player, makes them individuals. Not very likeable ones either. The villains too have faces and names and it just makes them dull. The threat they pose is never demonstrated, never shown to us; we are simply told that bad things will happen, and expected to believe it. The dialogue is some of the worst I've ever heard in a game; whenever a cutscene started, I found myself smashing every button I could to try and skip it, and when that failed I just turned off my speakers until the cutscene ended. There is no storytelling here, just a bunch of cut-and-paste characters narrating a childrens book.This also ties in to their abandonment of some of the most iconic aspects of previous Homeworld games, the cutscenes. The use of still, often black and white images during cutscenes added so much impact and gravity. It allowed the game to show vistas and structures in a different light to how they appeared during gameplay, showing off things that we couldn't see from our top-down view. It was awsome and epic and it hurts SO much that this piece of tripe abandoned that in favour of soulless, uninspired motion capture cut scenes.The mission design is just fine, never exceptional. The only vaguely interesting mission I played involved avoiding asteroids, and it was only interesting because it at least looked cool; in the end, it was pretty simple. The only difficult mission I encountered was a short section at the start of one, where you recieve a token fleet and have to destroy two objectives. It was only difficult because the ships you are given are not suited to the job at hand. Theres also a mission where the game tells you to set up a choke point, and just hands you a massive pile of turrets and minelayers. Things that, until that mission, you could not build, and that you probably will never build again.For a particularly cynical take, the entire game feels soulless and empty, and like it was designed for season passes and microtransactions. Honestly, when the game made me sign multiple EULAs to even start playing, that was a pretty bad sign. To summarise, this game has one final good point; it will make the previous games seem even better by comparison. I don't think I've ever been more disappointed in something, something that could have been a glorious continuation of a fantastic series of games. As is, I cannot recommend this game to anyone. Even if the price dropped to nothing, you'd still be better off buying HW Remastered or the original games instead.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR : It's okay, but it needs more work. I do recommend for now because it's great fun, but I might change it to a thumbs down if the updates are lackluster or if the modding scene doesn't take off much...I'm on mission 12, played a few rounds of Wargames and a few skirmishes, and it's pretty nice for now...Gameplay is responsive and dynamic, though there are a few oddities like the camera and some of the controls that take a bit of getting used to. Thankfully, these are highly customizable (lesson taken from the demo), so it's fine.Apart from that, it sticks to the general formula of Homeworld, but with a few twists and changes that make the experience fresh, like "Space terrain", more dynamic formations and parallel build queues.I was worried about the pathfinding, the demo had issues on that front, but I haven't had any problem with it for now... It does need a bit of handholding to get it to use a tunnel sometimes, first directing the squadron to the start of the tunnel and then to the end, else they might just go around it, but I haven't seen anything that seemingly didn't work mostly as it's supposed to...Formations sometimes have a bit of a hard time entering a tunnel, mostly if the formation is too large to fit as-is, they'll shuffle around a bit before deciding to, ♥♥♥♥ it, stop holding the formation for the length of the tunnel...Story seems okay for now, it's a lot more character-focused than previous HW games (following the changes made by HW2 and DOK on that front), and they switched from the usual style of painterly cinematics to animated CG (low quality animated CG, though it has its moments, it's also not great on average), the dialogue is a bit stiff in cinematics (outside of cataclysm, it was never really HW's forte), but it does the trick and the comms chatter and mission dialogue is really great... Music is Homeworld, so it's pretty good, though I haven't heard anything really memorable yet bar one or two tracks, it's a bit too *ambient*, and rarely strays outside the *generic middle eastern* vibe too much...Graphics are really great, ship detail is at an all time high, with damage decals, small animations like sliding turrets and VLS doors, RCS and coolant venting, models are nicely detailed, with great textures serving pretty good designs. Only thing I'd note about the designs is that they look a bit too same-y inside a faction's roster, and might have benefited from a tad more variety, especially with the notably reduced number of designs we get.Environments have a bit of repetition too, but nothing too jarring, and the vistas are really cool, though I think it lacks a bit of the mood of the previous games by having less fancy HDRIs that go for a more photoreal look, and are mostly obscured by fog most of the time anyway... The "Space Sunset" mood that was common in earlier games is mostly replaced by a "Space Mist" mood with colors varying between brown and blue.Outside of the Campaign, Wargames mode is kinda neat, I'm not really into roguelikes usually, but I could see myself going back to this, especially if they add more scenarios.Skirmish seems to be mostly unchanged, though the fact that you can parallelize build and research queues means it mostly ends up being a ressource race and a big brawl in 2 minutes more than a really strategic fight, since you can build multiple units at the same time, there's a lot less management on that front. Map selection is very lackluster too, with only 6 maps, the largest of which are still quite small. Hopefully this will be corrected as the game recieves updates.Performance is okay, I'm running on a very beefy rig, in 3440*1440p, and i'm getting stable 70fps on most missions without using any DLSS and with everything maxxed up. It can dip under 60 during very large fights, and there's a quite bunch of stuttering, especially in maps with lots of volumetric fog and nebulae, which is especially noticeable on the camera movement.All in all, very decent first impression, and I don't feel like I didn't get my money's worth (still need to recieve the collector itself though), but for Homeworld 3 to be on par with its predecessors, it is gonna need a lot more work.

WHERE IS TACTICAL HYPERSPACE JUMPS IN THIS GAME? They did really remove it from Multiplayer? Now that is just...The game can lag even in the lowest settings, especially true in Wargames mode, which really kills all joy playing it (hopefully it will get fixed). This poor optimalization on the Server part is an extremely bad start for a new game...So yeah, I am conflicted, a new player may trash this game for the right reasons, as a fan however I more like sad about it. I know it is salvagable, but WILL the Company make it right? Time will tell, for the time being I give a Positive, in hopes of many issues will be fixed and that will make it very enjoyable with tons of new unique content.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very torn with this game.I played the originals on CD - Actually I think I still have them in my closet here in their original cases. I loved the remasters even if people still loathe the non-projectile based combat. IT felt like a passion of love and seemed to capture everything well enough to present it to a modern audience. Also, I was personally quite fond of DoK and it's campaign.. I played a little MP with friends but it didn't have enough popular appeal to keep me coming back. Needless to say, I'm a long time fan, backed them on FIG, etc.As for HW3:I love the visuals, the audio, the stylized UI. The fact they listened to the community after the demo and modified the feel of the controls!- I love the megaliths, but hate the interactions with them -- The interactions with random 'terrain' objects makes movement in 3D space awkward.. you go to click something in the foreground and end up sending your units off into another area..- The Story felt very forced, you don't care about the characters, it's very personal without any feeling.. The animations don't do it much help. -- they're not 'bad' they just dont 'fit'. Which is what makes people think they're bad. -- They're almost jarring with how expressive and uncanny they are.. I would have preferred the stylized art with many of the audio bits. Also more masked and non-human characters. Something was missed here in the presentation of the narrative and the usage of a personal story that just doesn't gel the experience well. If I close my eyes and listed to the banter it's sometimes decent, so I think it was just a missed landing in the art direction of the visual and the story telling.- Why remove core elements of the game for story sake? No hyperspacing? Few corvettes? - Where did my 'hive' like swarming go on my attack craft? They seem to not create enough space, and sometimes awkwardly nuzzle or refuse to shoot at their designated targets. This often costs me important kills/objectives due to awkwardness in their handling.- Many of the campaign missions have REALLY cool designs that want to make use of the new features, some of it is done well. Others are an utter slog that feel artificially sluggish to increase the length of the campaign time..There are probably good bones here. But first impressions are really important nowadays. We live in a different world of gaming with a different landscape to navigate through.. and this was maybe stuck in development hell for too long, and seems to have lost some of it's direction somewhere in the making.. -- All in all, it's a shame.I'll recommend it on the basis that I'm hoping to see it fleshed out in the future -- and there are some really cool visually impressive pieces, soundscapes, and of the ships that do exist they are really nice looking.. but the choice to keep them so similar in design renders it repetitive. Also, please, please support the multiplayer and balance it.. Make the fighting space larger!Also -- whatever happened to railgun frigates? That was a whole thing in development.. just vanished? FLC/DLC?Edit - 07.13.2024:After 2 months since my previous review -- I'm just disappointed. The mod tools were thrown in our laps and a small additional 'siege' unit which is a slightly modded stat craft. OK. -- I'm expecting something from the road map to drop, some news, some open communication about the disappointing launch.. something. Are we expecting this to just die a year our with little support like DoW3?

_childDocuments_.review: I am happy to see this franchise continue and it is a long awaited delight. Homeworld has a rich lore and atmosphere to draw from and BBI have kept to the spirit which made it popular. If you are a fan of and enjoyed Homeworld 1 and Homeworld 2 then you will enjoy Homeworld 3. Recommended for sci-fi and strategy fans. I really do hope to see more in the series and potential spin offs. ProsTo me this feels like a return to Homeworld 1 play style which is refreshing. Similar pacing in gameplay with some quality of life uplifts such as mission endings being faster - though it would be nice if they still made it a player controlled choice in more missions and communicated which resources were collected. The campaign felt satisfying enough and further immersed into the characters of the series. There was a decent story arc and it ends on a clear note. Constructive Feedback - some minor potential spoilersDifficulty and TacticsThe campaign gameplay felt a bit too easy (Medium - don't get much time these days) and by the end did not require too much tactical thought. I can see potential for exploring this further in the hardest difficulty setting and recommend going in on hard if you want more gameplay challenge. Though towards the end it becomes overwhelming juggling massive fleets. The utilisation of the Pause and Time slow may help juggle this aspect, however in Medium it became the approach to just hit F4 (Select all military ships) and roll around the map in an aggro ball. However this has been similar in all the series and is more a personal reflection on wanting more engagement in the gameplay loop. I think the missed opportunity here was the evolution of the Sensors Manager / Strategic View.  It felt like this mode was missing a little love. Originally it was invented to offset the limitations of the 1990's graphics engine view distance and it was a beautiful take on things. In the modern era it is hard to see what purpose this really serves anymore which is sad because it is core to the formula and atmosphere. I found I rarely needed to drop into that mode as I could see just about everything anyway. I honestly thought they could of explored adding something more to this view mode to entice usage - something like a hexagonal grid to manage larger fleet movements, multi-zone areas / maps to jump around too, or consider adding a layer above for navigating around the galaxy. Maybe they experimented internally and it didn't feel right - just felt like this could of been uplifted a bit.Story and CinematicsI can appreciate the modern desire for fleshing out characters to make it personal and I enjoyed the cutscenes more or less. However I would say part of the charm of the original Homeworld was the overall atmosphere and feeling of disconnect which was overcome through voice narration, comms chatter, and cinematic framing to emote the personality of the ships. You never really see a face in the original - and you slowly came to appreciate the feeling of isolation as fleet command. Then Mission 03 hit you with the Adagio of Strings / Lamb of God - and drew out one of the most emotional scenes in a video game without a character on screen. There was one mission which stretched for this but I thought fell a little short. The cinematics were decent, there just lacked some emotional punch in the story. Even looking back at Homeworld Cataclysm / Emergence when the SOMTAAW confronted the Bentusi on running from the beast - that was a more engaging moment than any offered in this story arc. They could of played that angle way more with this Queen's seeming thoughtless minions - but that question was never answered. It honestly feels like this may have originally been a story which could fit the beast story arc but was changed in development. Maybe not, but there seems like a few unresolved story triggers and questions. CharactersThe Queen character felt rushed and two dimensional. One of the difficulties in trying to create immersive characters through cutscenes is there is not enough time. I think they could of built more menace and mystery through a lower key approach and not showing her face. For someone insinuated to be millenia old, she comes across as a teenage brat. I think it would of been better served leaving it up to the imagination of the player. Something like how the Bentusi were built up. Why the idea of the "Unbound" was not explored and this Queen's perversion of that seemed like another missed opportunity. Space Zombines 2.0 or something.With the exception of the Intel guy, I do not understand this modern character design for the three women either - 5 minutes in an Unreal Character creator would make a better job on the three women fleet navigators. Karen looked like a prune, Imogen looked like some 90's era CGI, and the Queen seemed like a cheap Disney villain... This is a widespread industry problem so I don't know what's going on there but it is just... bad. DLC RoadmapLooks okay but I am disappointed there seems to be no mention of additional campaign / story missions. The campaign was a bit on the short side.ConclusionDecent sci-fi strategy game campaign and recommend. The co-op warzone mode looks promising but this review is purely on the campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: What follows is a long list of incredibly amateur bugs, baffling UI decisions, and step backwards in gameplay and game design:UI, Stability, and Lobby Issues- The "Remove Player" button is non-functional in lobbies, so if someone is AFK, it kills the lobby.- While typing in the chat box in a lobby, if someone else joins or types, it interrupts your typing input, requiring you to click into the box again to resume typing.- Unlike almost every other online game in the past 30 years, when you press ENTER in game, to bring up the chat box, rather than being front and centre in the screen, it’s tucked away at the bottom. And UNLIKE EVERY OTHER GAME IN THE PAST 30 YEARS, pressing Enter to send your text through doesnt automatically close the dialogue box, it remains open, out of view, and you need to press ESC to close it- When someone joins the lobby, the map resets to the default 1v1 map, somewhat breaking the lobby as it prevents others from joining until the map resets. Due to the poor UI design, the host might not notice this issue. - The UI in general feels like it was developed from a Duplo Drag & Drop software designed to teach teens how to program.- Under many of the UI elements are programming text leftover from the Duplo Build-a-UI, that made it into the full release - The UI design philosophy seems to "Dementia Clock" and if so, it 100% accomplishes this vision.- The game frequently runs out of memory and crashes when other applications (browser, Discord, Slack, etc.) are open. It also redlines my 3080.- The universal upgrade for strikecraft is tucked away and easily overlooked on the build menu.- Quick Match often places players either in games by themselves that end abruptly or in broken lobbies attempting to accommodate three players in a 1v1.- Joining a lobby has about a 40% success rate. Most time out or simply can't connect.- The absence of team chat in a pvp is baffling.- The decision to have the text in the lobby chat bar flash every 3 seconds is nonsensical and disruptive.Gameplay and Balance- There really is no strategy here. Resource income is so fast, that games devolve to spamming units, and then trying to win an APM race as blobs fly around one another as seen in this clip - The inclusion of terrain means that maps are SIGNIFICANTLY smaller. The biggest 3v3 map is smaller than Deserts of Kharaks 1v1 maps- Terrain also gets in the way of Homeworlds full 3d gameplay. Because there is now a top, bottom, left and right in the map there is SIGNIFICANTLY less room to move around, and it’s now just like any other top-down RTS.- Maps that have a lot of terrain end up blocking views. In the zoomed out tactical view, you cannot select units if they are behind terrain, even though in this view, terrain is see through and you can see the unit. You will need to maneuver the camera around the busy maps to select your unit.- Hiigarian bombers melt resource collectors, no unit on the Incarnate side can do this.- The tech tree is linear, offering no strategic choices for either faction. Every match consists of waddling your mothership to the opponent and spamming units.- There are no upgrades or modules for your Mothership like in previous editions. In DoK, focusing on your carrier upgrades was a path you could take in a game. Now all your mothership does is spit out dinky low damage PDCs - Wargames is an incredibly boring mode. What if you could play homeworld with less units, a much lower pop, and more braindead AI that spawn out of thin-air at points specifically pointed out on the map?I have never played a game that has made ask, outloud, to my empty decrepit hovel  “What is going on at this studio?” more than this game.The highlight of the game is the soundtrack, which aboslutely rules, and the fact that Paul Ruskay did not make the soundtrack for nu-Dune shows how cursed this world is.

_childDocuments_.review: Homeworld 1 was a grand space opera with a focus on the survival of the Kushan people journeying to their Homeworld. Cataclysm was a more personal story of a raise of a single clan. Homeworld 2 went quasi religious and dove into the past history of the galaxy. Deserts of Karak filled in the back story of the Kushan. Now Homeworld 3 goes back to being the personal story similar to Cataclysm, where it focuses on pretty much just 4 characters. The new fleet command character Imogen, her intelligence officer, the big bad, and an old familiar face. We get a lot of time with our new big bad compared to HW 1&2, but I do not think that this new villain is quite as intimidating as Maakan from HW2 or the Taiidan Emperor. There was a mystique and looming presence for these characters that is just not here in the 3rd installment. I think its because we see a little too much of this new villain. On the other hand, I loved Imogen and her relationship with the intelligence officer. You can feel more of a bond between these two than in the other games. Voice acting was stellar across the board, and while the new cutscenes are a dramatic departure of style for this series I did not mind them and they carry the overall story well.Overall, the story I find to be one of weaker parts of this game, which is a bit of a shame.It was a bit short though...The campaign was fantastic, we have almost a greatest hits of missions from previous entries. We got the asteroid level, assaulting a base, a stealth mission, a defence mission, all things that we've seen before in this series but set in levels that now have all kinds of massive pieces of terrain which I think add a new level of strategy that ends up being required. Sometimes these terrain pieces do make navigating a bit more difficult, but the controls still handle it and AI appears to be able to navigate sufficiently. Missions do end automatically, and do not allow you to linger and collect resources or perform research. This is a big nitpick from Homeworld 2, and its sad to see that it returns in force in this entry. What I did notice though is that between missions you'll end up seeing quite a few more units that may have been producing when the last mission ended just available for use. I suppose its a decent trade, but I wish I could choose when to leave.I played through the campaign on normal/medium difficulty and found it to be rather easy, if you make use of support frigates you will not experience much losses. Overall, I always have enough resources to replace any losses almost immediately. I suspect that Hard campaign will alleviate my concerns on this front so I don't fault it. My first run through was enjoyable. UPDATE after finishing hard campaign, it was as I suspected. Hard mode caused me to have to engage more with mechanics and actually capture things to keep up with growing fleets being thrown at me.I am currently running a Geforce RTX 3070 laptop edition, and i'm able to use DLSS and run everything maxed out sans RTX, and no motion blurr. Its absolutely playable, and even in the last few campaign missions when things get nutty there is a hitch here and there that I suspect I wouldn't have if I lowered graphics. I refuse to do this and still hover around 60 FPS with DLSS putting in work downscaling when needed. In cutscenes during missions there is a split second where textures must load in, but otherwise I'd say performance is just fine.NOTE: YOU NEED TO UPDATE YOUR DIVERS FOR NVIDIA. PRIOR TO THIS UPDATE IT RAN LIKE DOO DOO.On the gameplay side of things, this is what I wanted to see in a sequel. I am a big fan of how ships behave from Homeworld 1, and hate how things are in Homeworld 2, this feels like a balance between those two. Gone are squads and we see the return of producing individual units, gone is building subsystems on every single ship and we see a merging of research from the first game and special abilities and upgrades from the second game. Now, you must first research a unit before you can produce it, but its on the same tab as where you build it and once research is done you click the same button to build it. Under the unit itself in the build menu are special abilities you can unlock and then use with a hotkey for each unit. I like this new system quite a bit, it reduces the bloat from 2 but keeps what matters.Shipyards from Homeworld 2 are also gone and the focus is back on The Mothership and Carriers as the only producing units. You are also able to build all ships at once, with every single ship having its own 'queue' so you can pump out units just like in Homeworld 1. I mentioned it a bit in Campaign, but Terrain plays a much larger role in this game. Turrets are produced like they were in Homeworld 2, but now must be placed on terrain pieces instead of directly in space. When having units in certain behavior stances (neutral or passive) ships will automatically path behind nearby cover on approach which I think is pretty neat and seems to work well.Unit AI I do think needs some work though, larger capital ships like the Battlecruiser do not effectively bring their hardpoints to bear, units sometimes seem to forget guard orders and do not follow the target they should be protecting. Formations sometimes fall apart or break into smaller formations for some reason when you have too many entities. All of this I think is patchable, either by the community or hopefully by BBI. Overall, I think this FEELS like a Homeworld game which is a big win in my book. I never played the demo, but I do not feel a lot of the complaints from that time is valid anymore. The few months they took to polish I think shows. The remaining issues I believe are patchable.A new mode added to Homeworld 3 which is a 'roguelike' mode where you are given a carrier and a small selected fleet. You and a few mates pop into this mode, and are given time to harvest resources before a random objective will spawn and once completed you'll be given the chance to remain as long as you like (with enemies still spawning) until moving onto the next mission. Each 'wargame' consists of 3 missions where you carry what you end each little mission with into the next mission.Random modifiers are earned throughout these 3 missions which allow you to specialize your fleet, like buffing your torpedo frigates, your fighters, or carrier. When you complete a wargame session you're given experience and level up. At each level you receive awards like new artifact bonuses which will appear in future sessions, a new fleet to start with, or portraits. The mode is a little bit sparse on content at the moment, but the bones are here for something really special. The DLC roadmap appears to be adding quite a lot to wargames and i'm excited to see where they take it. Having played a few matches so far with randoms, it was a good time and decently challenging. Speaking of challenges, there are optional modifiers which you can add to make things more difficult too. I don't think im too qualified to speak about this too much. It seems to have all the features you'd expect. The few skirmishes i've played have been fun, although the AI is aggresive at the start and then tends to fall off. I think we can see some tweaks by the dev if needed in this area. I'm excited to see the new factions that they will add.I'm a bit sad to say here, but I don't think the music is really doing anything super special here. It fits the theme of the game, but there are no standout tracks like there were in Homeworld 1 and 2. I think its awesome they brought back Paul Ruskay and I think he did a good job.

_childDocuments_.review: It's always exciting to see a new entry in the RTS genre, especially in as storied a franchise as Homeworld.However, Homeworld 3 is by and large a disappointment. Some its flaws are forgivable, but baffling. Like recommending "modern" controls, but then having the modern controls mess up important hotkeys without informing the player anywhere. Or having a deploy mulitple turrets UI-functionality which stops working in the "active pause" mode, where the game slows to a crawl, but you can still assign orders.Other stuff is kinda overblown, in my view. The story telling has received a lot of criticism, but I found it to be engaging enough, and not badly told.However, all of this is overshadowed by the fact that the gameplay itself is a muddled mess. Battles quickly devolve into giant meat grinders into which both sides simply throw in as many units as possible and rebuild constantly to replace lost units. It's entirely unclear what other options there are, and units react to orders so sluggishly, that it often seems like trying to give orders in combat becomes detrimental to your forces in the fight. Units will also often ignore orders to go to a specific location in favour of hanging out in the general area you specified, which is sometimes fine but occasionally a real pain. Especially with large control groups, the ships tend to just sort of do whatever they please.The campaign missions frequently try to force you into playing strategically, using cover and precise movement to bypass enemy turrets and asteroid hazards and the like. This is the exact right way to design a campaign - force the players to engage with the mechanics so they learn how to do it, and add new techniques to their toolbox. However, the aforementioned sloppy controls undermines this at every turn. In one case, you need to capture a control point, but it's surrounded by powerful turrets. But you can approach through a tunnel, and come up on the control point from an angle where the turrets can't see you. Clever! However, the moment you start capturing the control point, enemy ships come in and in the ensuing dogfight, all of your own ships inevitably fly out in front of the turrets to do battle anyway, leaving the whole exercise completely pointless.In another one, you have to move your mothership through an fast moving asteroid field, sheltering it behind large, stationary asteroids in a sort of Frogger situation. Your ships can break up asteroids with their weapons, but they don't always target the right ones. Easy, target the ones that are headed for the mothership manually, right? Wrong! The moment you do, all the smaller ships break formation from the mothership and start floating around doing whatever, as the AI is wont to do, leaving loads of them to float randomly into the path of asteroids regardless of how many times you order them to group up on the mothership or get into formation. Most people I've seen discussing on forums how to beat it say to completely ignore the instructions and actually dock the smaller ships inside the mothership, as the asteroids don't do enough damage to threaten the mothership anyway, rendering the whole mission tame and pointless. Another example of how the awful unresponsiveness of ships undercuts the level design.I doubt I'll finish the campaign. Controlling your space navy is like being a temp teacher in a class of really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ kids - your commands are taken as vague suggestions and mostly nobody seems to listen.

Those giant nebulae and structures in those beautiful backgrounds, especially in HW2, I always wondered what it would be like to fly my ships around them, see their scale up close. Homeworld 3 realizes that dream! Its gorgeous, varied, and I'm absolutely loving it. Yea, the writing isn't great so far, and maybe it will become SO bad that I'll really hate how the story ends. But even with that...I'm gonna play War Games with my dad, way cooler than what we did with just regular multiplayer 20 years ago. I'm gonna be greatful that 20 years after the last mainline sequel, this franchise still has enough diehards that love it that we got another game. _childDocuments_.review: This was the only game I was looking forward to in 2024.In short, it's . , but it's not very good. It looks nice, but it certainly  in my opinion.Let me start with what I like: - It looks good but then again what doesn't these days? It still has that weird bluriness that games have noways. - The music is good. It deviates from the classic style a bit but it's still good. - The 3D real-time strategy is still there. The feeling of "thinking on your toes" is still there. - Some campaign moments are neat. - The tunnels and terrain add some nice tactical options. - I love that there's a command to rotate the Mothership to the  orientation. - Ship designs are neat, if a little samey. - The difficulty isn't brutal.Things that can be fixed: - The unit AI is weird. There are some pathfinding issues and sometimes they just sit and watch the action instead of doing something. - Selecting single units, especially smaller ones, can be difficult because their selection box seems to be tied to the 3D model and is therefore really tiny in many cases. In older games you can easily select such units by clicking on the icon and not a small 3D model. - Resource controller automatic collection should be on by default, and they should stop searching beyond a certain radius so they don't go straight into enemy territory. - Radio chatter frequency is annoying sometimes, so an option to reduce it would be great.The bad: - The story, characters, cutscenes, dialogue, and voice acting just don't feel like Homeworld. - The cold, dry, matter-of-fact, and professional atmosphere that I loved so much about Homeworld (especially 2) is gone. - Something I hated about Deserts of Kharak was the excessive "military-sounding" verbose radio chatter. This game took that further. - The dialogue is just annoying most of the time. So much unnecessary made-up jargon being thrown around when they could be so much more brief! - Aside from that, I don't like the sound design, there's less unit variety, no capital ship subsystems, and other little annoyances.The only way to salvage this game is to make a redux, director's cut, or something like that.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could put a maybe, that would be my score. It's a beautiful game and the Homeworld feel is present with a lot of things lacking. HW1 and HW2 was a long journey with many intense battles mixed with serene and calm moments. Even Deserts of Kharak was able to capture that unique feel. HW3 threw a lot out and kept the intensity very high. Once you start your journey, you're basically in a non-stop fight for survival from start to finish. The Single Player of HW3 is REALLY short and that's my biggest critic about it. It's not bad but compared to Deserts of Karak, it is very very weak. Imogen is not exactly interesting and the antagonist is rough to watch... Like who the hell would even bother following her. Any veteran Homeworld player will flow through the campaign in 5-7 hours without a problem. HW1 and HW2 were easily 15-20 hours long even for pro players. War Games is nice and I really hope that we get to see this mode evolve through the years. _childDocuments_.review: Given that I am only a few years older than Homeworld 2, I am part of the group that never played the first games. So I can't be relied on if you're looking for a review from the perspective of a franchise player.   The game has great graphics and was fairly easy to navigate the 3-D environment, however, since most maps are destroyed locations with scattered debris, my camera would often get caught in terrain. Ships and their weaponry are very similar in designs, making it hard to identify what ship is what.    There are very few QoL improvements as well which makes it very frustrating to play at times. For example, you cannot shift-click plant multiple turrets, can't box-drag salvage or auto capture, can't auto-put new ships in a control-group, a severe lack of ability auto-casting on short CD abilities, and so on.   Game AI is not very good, especially on skirmishes, and ship AI is also really bad at times. I've had bombers turn corners and fly right past enemies without bombing, snipers going behind walls while firing at enemies, ships just... forgetting orders when an enemy shoots them, and other poor decision making that made combat control weak.   I have no clue what the plot of the story is. Even after reading the game's history pamphlet, I was still lost. I was not really wowed by the story or the levels. In fact, I grew quite frustrated with certain levels, particularly the asteroid evading one. The pacing felt really off, and the "threat" of the major threat felt inconsistent. I was left with too many questions to really remember the story, but at least I got to make a big-ass fleet. The biggest one I could ever make in the game.   Skirmish is Skirmish. There isn't really anything unique about it that can't also just be summed up in just explaining the gameplay. I also don't really play PvP, but the bots in those mode are atrocious, just hap-haphazardly vomiting a stream of uncoordinated units until they run out of resources.   War Games is the big mode of this game. It has the most content currently and on the road-map. You get a small set of ships and a pre-set list of what you can build and must go through 3 levels, completing objectives and getting artifacts that can alter ship parameters. If you are gonna get the game, this mode should hold the biggest weight of it. While I don't hate it, it's very lacking.     The mode is quite short, consisting of only 3 levels, of which you can only get upgrades on the first 2. By the time builds are actually starting to develop, the mode is over. You are also hard set to the lower levels of units, which are strikecraft to frigates. You don't get to find or use the larger capital units like destroyers or battlecruisers.   Difficulty is increased by adding modifiers to make the game harder. You cannot pick and choose the mods, they come in a static lift. Some increase enemy count and frequency, but others just make the mode less fun. For example: mod 4: allies carriers stay dead between levels, is redundant if you're playing single player since losing the carrier loses the mode, and just means if you're carrier gets snipped in multiplayer you might as well just leave the lobby as you are now a spectator. Mods 7 and 9 reduce the number of artifacts and the choices you get from each one. Mods 2 and 8 reduce usable resources.   By increasing difficulty, the game mode ends up killing its own roguelite nature, as apposed to other roguelites which increase rewards alongside difficulty. by giving less resources, you have less diverse fleet setups, and by giving less buff options and buffs overall, you have less impactful builds.    This game mode has a lot of potential, but I think the devs need to go back and analyze both what makes a roguelite enjoyable and what makes people want to push into higher difficulties in those games. If they keep this current method of progression both in-game and in difficulty, then even with new content if won't be very satisfying to play and beat compared to other roguelites.   Even with my negative review, I'll still keep playing it, because there just aren't many roguelite fleet battle games. If that concept sounds cool to you, then you'll at least find this passable. But there's a lot that could have been done that they simply didn't do, and it felt like it was made with only a surface level understanding of roguelites.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a long-time fan of the Homeworld series, and backed this game on Fig (RIP) when the funding campaign was announced. Overall I enjoyed the game, a solid B. The visuals are excellent, with interesting environments and effects. Soundtrack is wonderful as they have been in previous games. The strategic depth of HW3 is somewhat less than its predecessors, and left me wishing for the modular ship design of HW2. Unlike in previous games,resources in HM3 are plentiful and when playing on medium I never found myself wanting. I found the UI to be well designed and intuitive for the most part, however given the sheer number of units under the player's control, I found it difficult (even with the ability to group units) to quickly select the units that I wanted in a given moment of action - especially as you lose units and need to reinforce existing groups. Regarding the pot and characters, HW3 is not the strongest of the franchise, especially when compared with HW1 and Deserts of Kharak. A criticism I have of lots of sequels is that writers seem to feel the need to up the ante with a existential crisis bigger than the last - and HW3 falls into that trap - complete with a unintentionally comical, melodramatic villain who was difficult to take seriously. The cooperative Wargames mode adds much needed replayability to a game that would otherwise be very short, which is good, because I don't see myself re-playing the campaign anytime soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Perhaps I am getting to old, but I miss the days when you could get a solid single player game. Yes, it has a campaign, but it is short, largely because of the forced stress by constantly making the player push forward. Sure, much of my dissapointment comes from playing the games as a kid, but I do feel that the slow gamepace that could be chosen at that time is no longer possible. The player is constantly forced on the offensive, perhaps to appeal players that enjoy competitive gameplay, but perhaps being naive i was expecting some laid back gameplay as that was what was offered from the previous series. (not in all missions, but you would always be given some respite after an intense mission) As for the story, i feel it has moved towards the C&C or red alert series of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ dialouges, whatever happened with having 20 seconds of solid artwork and direct monologues? As far as the story goes, I find it lacking, perhaps in part by the forced tempo of the rest of the game. The wargames is surely something that could appeal the multiplayer masses. But perhaps a game that had its roots in solid single player gaming should have focused on the single player campaign first hand and added upon the multiplayer experience after release. Perhaps they forgot that the games originated from a single player game originally and that the multiplayer community and modding arose from the fact that there was no sequel for a substantial period of time. The artifacts idea and fleet progression sounds good, but why could this not have been part of a single player experience? Atleast offer some sort of veterancy to the units, but then again, given the constant spewing of forces from nowhere in some mission, the veterancy would have been redundant. I appreciate shareholder expectations and the whole push from executives to monetize to any degree, but perhaps the producers should have studied eve online rather than fortnite or some other ♥♥♥♥♥ made for kids withour impulse control before deciding on whatever they thought this would become. so in short: This game does not live up to its previous namesakes. Much of the problem lies in the game design, where the developers seem to think that we are all in need of constant challenges and input, and that having a few seconds of peace would be detrimental to our overall welfare. It also seems the producers where to focused on creating some kind of multiplayer experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I really hope one day I can change this review. Was very excited to get back into the HW series after playing since the release of HW1. This is a step back from HW2/Remastered collection. No ship feels truly useful, and subsystems seem to be going, battles turn into spam, spam spam and little more. There is no thought to plan, no aspect of strategy, and no long investment of planning to out think your enemies. With being able to research and build everything at once they leave no room to have to plan your R&D to win, its again spam, spam spam.Outside the gutted mechanics, the scale is truly disappointing....previous HW titles the maps felt vast, you had to invest time to recon, to spy, and plan the best routes to defeat your foes. This is absent, even what are presented as the largest maps in skirmish seem to place you right next to each other to begin the...spam, spam, spam with little delay. In addition to the maps lacking the scale and awe of previous titles, the ships themselves lack it. Battlecrusiers or any other capital ship seem to be in only the most minor way larger and more noticeable than frigates. Nothing seems like it is a battle tide turning behemoth.As disappointed as i am I will end on the positive. HW3 compared to many of the titles that jokingly call themselves RTS in recent years is a step towards a positive and solid title. It just isn't a title to bring back the love, the awe, and feel of the HW series.

_childDocuments_.review: tldr: Even if Homeworld 3 is not as good as Homeworld 1, Cataclysm or 2, it still is a good RTS game. You can have plenty of fun with the Campaign, the kinda rogue like War Game mode (Solo or Coop) or the classic Skirmish.Presentation:Homeworld 3 simply looks awesome. The Ship models and Maps are beautiful. The cutscenes look good and the UI is awesome. But the graphics come at a cost of very low FPS in big fights. Story:Quite the point of contention if you read other comments. But I find it alright. I find the comparison to Homeworld 1&2 funny. I replayed both for the release of Homeworld 3. I think many just talk from nostalgia. The story of Homeworld 1 is so short it could be explained in 5 sentences. The same with the story of Homeworld 2, just with a little more fluff here and there (like captain Soban). Don't get me wrong, Homeworld 1&2 Campaigns are amazing. But more because of the missions and atmosphere. That is maybe the main weakpoint of Homeworld 3. The atmosphere is just not as good as Homeworld 1&2. Sound:Short and simple. VFX sound is amazing. Voice and combat chatter is good. Music is alright but sometimes forgettable. Gameplay:This is maybe the biggest flaw for the game and I agree with many others. It’s just too fast for a Homeworld game. The small maps also contribute to that. Everything is right on top of you. Production is also too fast, you can build everything in parallel. The combat itself looks and sounds awesome. It’s just so fast that you can never even take a look :(You also don't have to think much. You can and should counter the units, but the most important thing is just to keep ALL the unit queues filled so you have enough replacements for all the losses. Money is rarely a problem.Campaign:The missions are great, I think. As varied as in Homeworld 1&2. The obligatory “Asteroid mission” is the best version yet :DYou have to be careful again not to finish the mission too early or you lose out on many RU’s. I like this more than in the Remake where it auto collects everything after a mission. I simply stopped gathering RU’s in Homeworld 1&2 mission’s and lived from my stockpile. I would get everything anyway after the mission so there was no point for me.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of this writing, 46% of the steam reviews for this game are positive. I purchased this game from Fanatical and got all of the Fleet Edition content for $68. I always value games that I consider worth the money at 1$/per hour of game play. I beat the campaign on Medium in about 10 hours. The campaign serves mostly as solid tutorial on how to play the game. Judging by the offical road map that was published for this game, it appears that the War Games mode is where your attention should be focused. I haven't had the opportunity to play co-op or pvp and have spent most of my time after the campaign playing the War Games mode solo. Currently with 19(EDIT: 45 hours on record), I feel like the war games are ment to be grinded to the top level. The graphics are amazing as can be expected from an Unreal Engine 4 title. The fact that the game running isn't Unreal Engine 5.3 is kind of a let down, but I bought this game for the gameplay, not the tech behind it. In war games, I haven't yet been able to finish the entire mission yet even though I have maxed out my fleet population caps. I feel like this is potentially a balance issue, but it may be that I need to grind to a higher level to survive longer. Not sure, but there seems to be an underlying balance problem. I'm leaving a positive review but I might change it if I decide there isn't enough content to justify the price. So far I feel this will turn out to really be worth the money though. It's fun and the campaign story is kind of stupid, but it's just a tutorial.

_childDocuments_.review: Longtime HW fan since HW 1. I'm having a pretty good time with the wargames, so this review will mostly be on those. I'll play the campaign eventually. Positive:-Megastructures are amazing, hiding behind them to avoid destroyers is pretty neat.-The "roguelike" mechanics of wargames is really fun to try out builds and then you accidentally overspecialize your assault frigates so they have basically 0 range lmao-A few different builds, different options.-Multiple different "preselected" fleets that tend to specialize or have a couple things different about them from the other fleets (except one is just a reskin so you can use the HW1 Kushan carrier).-Tough but not too tough, only tried up to difficulty 5 for right now. You can really feel yourself get better as you learn how to use the ships and combos. I tend to lose more than I win right now unless I can pull off a good build.-Claw formation! Wall formation! Sphere formation where your ships surround their guard or attack target!-They already hotfixed it so that's pretty indicative that they seem to actually care so far.-Custom fleet colors/ship engine trails.Negatives-The game is a little... bleached out or something? I messed with the graphics and can't seem to fix it. Is it supposed to be fog or something?-I don't know what to call it, maybe pathfinding? But that's not really it. My fighters/frigates obsessively try to get back into formation. This results in them sometimes stopping their shooting and turning around when the other squadmate is backing up. You can work around a bit by yourself obsessively setting the squad to "no formation" and sometimes it seems like if you just click one at a time they act like you think they should.-To follow up, ships like the torpedo frigate act really weird. They are already limited from using their massive range (with toggled ability) with the cover system from the megastructures. So why do they have to be in exactly their optimal range or they refuse to shoot? They just keep moving to get in some exact sweet spot. So basically I don't use torpedo frigates at all. They are almost entirely useless except on the wargame mission to kill the titan. That said, the one time I used the shrapnel upgrades with missile frigates and they obliterated a strike craft/corvette wave was really awesome.-Denuvo.-No offline mode, even if the games says there is. You are required to be online to play "offline" mode. My internet was interrupted for about an hour on launch day so I simply couldn't play. It wasn't a big deal, but what happens when the server go down in however many years? You need to change this to true offline.Neutral-A lot of the negatives can be worked around if you take it as a learning opportunity. Because of the way the obsessive repositioning works, turreted frigates (especially the ones with ion beams) are incredible if you get an upgrade or two on them. They are continually moving anyway, so take advantage of it. It's still frustrating when you're fighting a timer before your carrier gets caught by enemies and dies. Torpedo frigates with a huge wide open space can snipe stuff from nearly across the map.-Wargames seems to be about 90% designed for singleplayer, with 10% multiplayer. What I mean by this is that one of the difficulty levels removes the ability to respawn carriers. I could definitely see that wargames would be a ton easier if you played mulitplayer and had respawnable carriers. The objectives sometimes scale to more players, so in some missions it's roughly easier solo and some they're easier in MP.-RTS devs need yet another reminder that nobody plays multiplayer on RTS games. Wargames is where they seem to have made their "big thing" / sellingpoint happen so I appreciate that it is enjoyable for the singleplayer experience, even if parts of it seem to be designed for multiplayer.Overall, I recommend this game. No crashes, only seen one bug where a tutorial popup wouldn't go away, high framerate on medium settings with my medium spec computer.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm someone who played the original Homeworld back in the day. The song that Yes wrote for the game is on regular playlist rotation.I loved the cosmic horror of Cataclysm (now called 'Emergence' thanks to Blizzard). I've sunk countless hours into HW3 and, eventually, the endless combination of mods that eventually became available. I was never great at RTS games, let alone strategy games, but there was something about Homeworld's enigmatic , combined with its breathtaking music (which predated Battlestar Galactica by many years) and jaw-dropping visuals that simply transported my younger self into the game's heart-tugging odyssey. I was along for the ride, following the Kushan's journey across the stars, in search of Hiigara, 'home.' As the band Yes sang, it 'was a question of origin.'So this moment has been a long time in the making. That's what makes this moment especially weird, and, sadly, a little disappointing.Like so many other players have been sharing in their reviews, I have mixed feelings after playing through Homeworld 3's campaign. Maybe it was the dramatic tonal shift between the game's trailers, which looked and sounded like what we've come to expect from a Homeworld game, and what we got in the finished game. Compared to the artful direction in the game trailers, the finished game's cuts-scenes look and feel rushed. The characters and script feel boilerplate. By the end of the short campaign (altogether 12 levels), I found myself nearly tempted to hit the space bar and skip the dialogue altogether.Don't get me wrong. HW1 was lightning in a bottle. There was no reason to expect the developers to match it in the sequel, and from what I recall,  game's campaign wasn't very memorable, either. After all these years, and knowing that some of the original creators were behind the new game, perhaps I was expecting too much from HW3's campaign. Then again, I wasn't expecting so little.There are moments, especially early on in HW3's campaign, that glimmer with the feeling and tone of the original games. "May the burden remain" comes to mind. Those moments are especially heartfelt, and you can tell that  love and care for the franchise went into the story, with a few callbacks and nods here and there for longtime fans. The plot, however, is so uninspired and vague (especially its villain) that it makes these glimmering moments hard to appreciate. The campaign's game play is fun enough to enjoy. The maps are clever, and the ancient derelict super-structures are a lot of fun to work into your fleet strategies. I've already found myself requeuing for War Games and Skirmishes to experiment with different ways to utilize these structures (although I share the opinion that deep space maps are sorely missing from the game and just not Homeworld without them).I don't share a lot of the vocal concerns about the game's lack of features. Those, I'm sure, are coming with patches and updates. So what can I say? I'm left, sadly, with a similar opinion of Homeworld that I held before the release of this newest game.If you're looking for a fantastic space opera story, Homeworld and Homeworld: Cataclysm remain unmatched. Homeworld 3 is much like Homeworld 2 in that it's campaign is somewhat forgettable.If you're looking to get this game and hoping for a good story, I'm sorry to say that this title falls drastically short. I'm reminded of Noah Gervais' excellent video essay, 'A Thorough Look at Homeworld,' where he described HW2's story as 'maddeningly bland... devastating to player investment.' Noah's analysis of HW2 is entirely, disappointingly dead-on accurate for HW3.If you're looking to enjoy epic and colorful space battles, wait a few months for the patches to start rolling out. Think about grabbing it on sale.Fortunately and from the looks of it, the game's developers seem to be pretty responsive, and I'm imagining they'll be scrambling to start patching the game and winning back the Homeworld community's trust (developers, you've heard the fans: give us those deep space maps).It's clear that the developers were betting on the success of multiplayer and modding for HW3's longevity. So while Homeworld 3's short campaign may be unfixable, I think it's safe to say that the game's features and elements will keep improving and expanding.Who knows, maybe they will even release  story content that listens to what the fans have been calling for. After seeing The Templin Institute's video essay which explored many of Hiigara's factions, it's hard to deny that the Homeworld universe is sitting on a wealth of intriguing stories that rival any of the great space operas of science fiction. Here's hoping they tap some good writers and tell new stories, capture the imagination of a new generation.

_childDocuments_.review: It's just bad.  I was hoping it would be good, I kept playing it hoping it would GET good, but it just doesn't.The things that made the Homeworld series shine were the engaging story, the freedom of space combat, and the minimalistic yet beautiful art style.The story is a completely generic "Save the universe from (threat)" with the same stereotypical whiny, insecure protagonist we've seen a hundred times before (Get in the Mothership, Shinji!)The space combat is bad, in a game that is entirely space combat.  Unit formations are cumbersome, the AI is brain-dead, and variety is severely lacking.  Even more baffling, in a series that was revolutionary for allowing you freedom of movement to control your units in three dimensions, now EVERY. SINGLE. MAP. is cluttered with giant megastructures that were supposed to "enhance tactical gameplay" or some nonsense... while the pathfinding is so bad that you'll constantly watch your ships spend half a fight trying to find their way around a wall with their face.  And this was considered a MAJOR SELLING POINT.Finally, the charming, classic style and story-board presentation has been replaced with downright goofy cutscenes that look like they came out of the mid-2000s, and not in a good way.  Long story short, this isn't a Homeworld game.  It's a Battle Pass wearing Homeworld's corpse like a hat.

_childDocuments_.review: PLEASE NOTE I RECEVED A CODE FOR FREE DUE TO THIRD PARTY DELAYS IN MY FLEET COMMAND EDITIONHomeworld 3: A Nostalgic Journey with a few new TwistsAfter putting around 15 hours into the game, I can easily recommend it, albeit with some caveats.The GoodThe graphics and graphic design are great. The 2D backdrops of the original games are  dynamic set pieces, creating dynamic battlefields. Ships, structures, and views that offer visually captivating experiences.The Gameplay is solid, very similar to Deserts of KharakThe sound design is immersive, with that trademark unit under pressure chatter which adds to the atmosphere. The Performance scales well, although intense battles may strain even high-end gear. i sometimes suffered some choppyness on a 2070 STRIX but overall was brief Now the The BadThe pathfinding is not great. While I mentioned the ability to take cover, it can be a coin toss as to whether or not units will use any thats there. As a result units can get stuck,attack a different unit altogether. missle frigates can also seem to change their firing distance, which can be very frustrating at times.Now the story is also pretty mediocre, especially if you are going to compare to HW1 and DoK. The narrative follows a much more personal tale this time and has the trope of the new seeking/finding the old generation and taking over, which appears to be a step down from the "The Journey" themes often explored in the previous games. The CGI cutscenes, which i will admit i am neutral one but personally I much preferred the semi rotascoped style, and tone of the cutscenes in DoK, although this is my opinion, so others may feel differentlly. The game can also be completed in anything from 6-12 hours (i beat it on hard). I had a great time in the missions that I played, so I was really hoping for more, which is a shame.The Skirmish/wargames AI is overly aggressive and unbalanced, this could be  due to issues with production speed, making  rushes common. Difficulty however seems to be  ineffective however this could be a bug.overallFor Homeworld fans; its a easy choice. yes The game has some flaws, but there is good here for you to recognise and enjoy. For newcomers, PLEASE go pick up Deserts of Kharak and the Remastered Collection first. They can be found for substantially cheap on steam and GOG (and sometimes for free on EGS) it'll give you a good idea of what to expect in this game. However if you are still unsure you can either wait for the mandalore review OR wait for a sale to pick it upDespite its imperfections, Homeworld 3 has been a rewarding experience, and I look forward to revisiting it as the roadmap progresses.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge Homeworld fan. I've played the first one, the second, the noncanonical one. This is supposed to be successor. The next chapter in the series. This isn't it. It says its strategic, but the easiest strategy is to build up forces and then swarm the enemy with sheer numbers. There is no strategy. The story isn't compelling, its like the gameplay; totally linear and transparent. It practically drags you, forces you along the path to victory; there is only one path and the campaign leaves you with only one option to win. The music and graphics, the sound design are amazing... but everything else isn't.Then there are the DLCs. Promises of extra content, new enemies, etc. Those are things that honestly should have been in this game to begin with. Because the campaign is pretty short, all things considered. And the replay value is low, due to how campaign is structured, linear paths to win against a frankly dumb AI. It's pretty clear the game was designed with multiplayer in mind, not the singleplayer campaigns that Homeworld was best known for.
