_childDocuments_.review: This game is in a weird spot for me. There is a lot to like about this game. The visuals are great, the sound design is amazing, two of the biggest parts of the Homeworld formula are hit just dead on. Wonderful, no notes.The AI of the units, however, is lacking, and that is a rather large issue to have. Homeworld 3 adds in "terrain" to the formula, in the form of  asteroids or the large structures you would always see in the background of Homeworld 1 and 2. It's not uncommon to have your units get snagged on the terrain, or go way around a way that was not shown to you with the little move conformation lines.Additionally, units will often just ignore orders, like not guarding units they were ordered to. Two of my favorites with this are will the Support and Torpedo frigates. With the Supports, if you order a group of the to guard a group of ships, they won't, and will just pick a ship at random. Additionally, they will automatically assign themselves the Delta formation. When they assign themselves this formation, only the lead Support frigate will use its healing ability, so you have to tell the group of them that they have no formation at all, and that will mostly kinda help them go and heal stuff as a group. With the Torpedo frigates, they have an ability that lets them trade a lot of speed for a lot of range. When you have them set to aggressive stance, in which they attack anything in range, and they have this range buff on, they will not attack anything that is outside of their normal range without you telling them to. So, the range they search is not updated when you buff them.Lastly, story. Not great. Honestly, I can see that they tried, but I think they missed the mark. Homeworld is a science fiction setting, with some space religion elements sprinkled in there. I feel Homeworld 3 strayed into science fantasy, which while not bad in and of itself, I don't feel like this story hit the mark, and felt a little too fantasy then science.There is a solid foundation here, and so I think this could be a good game with some more love. I would say check back in 6-12 months, or after a few patches.

_childDocuments_.review: The feeling of Homeworld 3 is similar to when you anticipated SW ep. 7/8/9 in hopes they'll somehow redeem for SW ep. 1/2/3 but then they're so bad that suddenly ep. 1/2/3 seem good, combined with that sinking realization that you have when you start watching new exciting SF/EF series because you want to see setting, technology and some freakin' SPACESHIPS and SPACE only to realize that it's going to be one of those melodramas bordering on reality show where they focus on characters 90% of screen time justified by "pEoPlE lOvE fOcUs on ChaRaCtErS" (reality - no one cares about drama or relationships or even the characters, it's just way cheaper to make) also known as "Oh, so it's another BSG/Expanse/WD/GoT all over again".Homeworld series was always pretty much 95% just Homeworld 1 all along, with a beautiful completed story, that was unique in that for a positive change it didn't like everything else revolve around characters melodrama but went so far in the opposite direction that no character was ever shown. In fact, the very appeal of the narrative was that it didn't necessarily even have to be humans but whatever you imagine (ok, few short silhouettes in two cinematic scenes gave away they're probably some kind of humanoids but that's it). The point is that it WASN'T about protagonists but about the bigger picture - leading the only remaining 500 000 people (unofficial 600 000 because no fan worth his salt allowed that 6th cryo-tray to be destroyed) to their mystical home after the planet they considered their home (and figured out was just their sanctuary 4000 years ago until they regressed back to pre-industrial and forgot about it) was destroyed by the very same empire that exiled them in the first place. The precious few characters all communicated via radio and were the very epitome of what they should represent - professional above all, goal-focused, talking only about relevant points such as objectives (not opinions and emotions except in few masterfully subtle hints and undertones).The investment in story was complete - you'd be conveyed such a sense of duty that you'd feel like you'll have no sleep or food until you get Kushan home! Campaign was breathtaking. Ending was everything that you could've hoped for. Perfect complete story.Cataclysm (renamed Emergence) being a spin-off didn't really fit the narrative and scale of all that and had an awkward "Franchise:SpinoffAdventures!" feel about it but it was at least appreciated for the few things it was trying to do gameplay-wise - some rudimentary 1st-person view from ships, attempts of improving the map with a "fence" (wireframe), modular mothership, multi-purpose collectors. Not all of that was actually successful but you could see that someone was trying to improve something and you could appreciate that. It had that promise of maybe leading to something better.Then HW2 came and did pretty aggressive and vulgar retcon with those super-special hyperspace cores (which was beginning of the end for the story), new not-a-space-mongols enemy and the whole cranking up the "greater destiny" gauge. But again it was kinda "allowed" by the fans on the fact that it brought many new gameplay concepts.Deserts of Kharak prequel was strangely a step in the right direction with one of the best executed prequels that I've seen in respecting the material so far, paying close attention not to retcon almost anything and somehow squeeze an entire new story literally within the frame of two sentences of the original HW1 intro: "100 years ago, a satellite detected an object under the sands of the great desert. An expedition was sent." and then tell a story about that expedition. Even more impressive was the fact that they managed to repurpose a different homeworld-inspired game (google the story about Hardware:Shipbreakers) into a bonafide Homeworld game and not f it up.And now we have.................................................. this.......................travesty.It's like someone wrote the worst possible fan-fiction of Homeworld without knowing about it, just having someone superficial third-hand knowledge and said: "Hey, I know what this was missing all along. A DEEP PERSONAL STORY WITH A FOCUS ON CHARACTERS!". So the obvious previous story developed so far about the Anomaly and planets missing of the map was quickly re-adapted into "find your grandma" along with some ideas obviously belonging to the third or maybe even fourth draft, I don't know it's impossible to follow all of these chopped plot points, they're contradictory to one another, with the established setting, with the retcon on the scale of RPG Game Master with ADHD watching Lost. In effect, story is so bad that there is no story.And the characters they put so much focus on are spending 90% of their screen time pondering their doubts, fears and emotional states, consistent with today's cringe "emotions are everything" style of writing, complete with Netflix-level of shoving 150 proverbs, sayings and cryptic one-liners to everyone in order to convey character depth. Best example is the main antagonist's general, the Warsage - dude literally didn't communicate anything except PR one-liners to the point of starting to appear like this: "is this guy like............. a cousin of BBEG or something? He seems incapable of thinking, let alone leading the army. It's like he's reading from a pamphlet.... Boy, bad side sure has some nepotism goin' on in their ranks, oh well that's why they are bad guys I guess...". But you then get to the point of your own side reaching the tactical brilliance of "You'll just have to trust me" and realize - oh, ok so everyone's completely incompetent in this part of the space, ok.In summary - this is not a Homeworld. This is a malicious cash-grab, with a quality of off-brand low-budget adaptation.But it does weirdly one thing good - it puts things into an excellent perspective. It is so bad that you now clearly realize Homeworld 1 never needed a sequel because the story was complete but you somehow put up with it because you desired more. It makes you realize that occasional faithful remaster of HW1 every 10y or so with the latest engine is everything that you need.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a wonder to behold, evoking the whole series with its mix of old and new ship designs, lore callbacks and spectacular audio design. The gameplay walks a fine line between complexity and streamlining, mostly taking cues from HW1. New terrain mechanics make battles feel tactical and claustrophobic, the new reflections and lighting system is top of the class. While unit rosters suffered a noticable cut since Cataclysm, it will probably make life more managable for newcomers to the series.It is, therefore, incredibly sad that the plot presentation has been butchered. Decisions that, on paper, seemed humanising to the story protagonists, backfire spectacularly. The full 3D cutscenes leave no room to the imagination and lack any of the character that both the B&W and rotoscoped stills from previous entries had, and the character animations are woefully undercooked, with botched lipsynching, blurry textures and blatant asset recycling. The story itself, keeping an intimate (or rather, emotionally blatant and cheap) approach to it's protagonists, fails to capture the broader Kushan society in the centre of conflict - something that the series always prided itself upon. It does, however, have it's moments, especially for people who waited for the sequel since 2004.The recommendation, while bitter, is still fairly easy. Homeworld has never been copied, imitated or even properly homaged. It is a unique experience that, while sadly failing to recapture ligtning into the bottle, will not be topped in the forseeable future.The landing on Hiigara is a turbulent one, but by the Hand of Sajuuk we have landed.
_childDocuments_.name: Homeworld 3

_childDocuments_.review: After 20 bloody years (!!!) you shouldn't expect any sequel to *truly* live up to expectations. It will probably be more of a reboot. It'll have gameplay changes to align with modern standards (and I'm sure many people will disagree that this is a good thing). It will, inevitably, feel more streamlined. I went into the game knowing all this. Yet I can't help but feel that while this game is pretty good, it is a little underbaked - in terms of content, especially.The game gets a lot of the fundamentals right - moment-to-moment gameplay is fun, presentation is amazing, and the game controls much better than it did during the demo (but it's still flawed, more on that later). Formations and stances do matter and simulated ballistics make a return (notably missing in the Remastered Collection until its last few patches). If you find yourself struggling with disobedient AI, try playing around with formations and stances.However, the new gameplay mechanics do change things up pretty massively. Maps have been shrunk and littered with cover, which means that you and your enemies will have an easier time finding each other, even unintentionally. This makes units feel more fragile, as it becomes much harder to remediate bad positioning. I don't think any adjustment of HP will change this basic fact. Capital ships, anecdotally, seem to have an easier time dealing with strikecraft. Combined, this means that your strikecraft will melt if they find themselves unsupported or caught in a bad position.These sound good in a vacuum. But these can make the gameplay frustrating because of the game's biggest addition: cover in the form of megastructures. The new cover system forces you to move your camera around a lot, far more than the previous games. Neither of the default control schemes are good, in my opinion. And even after some tweaking, you will struggle for a bit. Until you get used to it, expect units to die, die, die, as you simply can't get to them fast enough. Skill issue? Yes, maybe. But the idea of this happening because the controls have a steeper than needed learning curve does irritate me a little.There are also some smaller issues that worsen this feeling of clunkiness. Unit selection can sometimes fail to work. AI pathing can get weird sometimes, so you may need to babysit your ships by queuing commands, especially if you want them to take a certain course around cover. Ships don't always act as you're expecting when they're in formation - I've seen assault frigates charge destroyers, even when not ordered to. Units need better target prioritization. If I highlight a group of enemies for my interceptors, I don't expect them to do strafing runs on capital ships. At least not until the escorting fighters are dead.Okay, let's finally talk about my main disappointment - the content. Honestly, it's not the quality that gets me, it's the quantity.The campaign is pretty short. It has 13 missions of varying length. Even if you're a bad player like me, expect to complete the campaign in 8-10 hours. The missions are, individually, pretty fun. However, they don't give you much room to breathe and maneuver. Missions feel more heavily scripted, especially as the maps are far smaller. Beyond playing a harder difficulty, don't expect much replayability.Now, the story - uhhh. It's different. It focuses more on characters instead of fleets and civilizations. It is more like a hero's journey or a coming-of-age story. This is, unfortunately, a swing and a miss. The campaign is far too short to allow for meaningful character development in the way this game does it - through cutscenes at the beginning and end of missions.  It feels poorly paced, with Fleet Command going from nervous to self-assured within the first few missions. Her back-and-forth with Intel - and the antagonist - helps, but it's not enough. It's like they tried to go for the same minimalist storytelling the previous games were known for, just with individuals instead of fleets. Then tried doing that with half the campaign size.Now, to discuss other gameplay modes before I finish this off.I've only played a couple of skirmish matches, and they're okay. The maps are small and resources are finite, so expect short matches. The AI is incredibly aggressive as a result - if you slack in production or disruption you will get destroyed in short order. I wish there more maps, and bigger maps at that. I have only played a single match on war games (and watched other people play), so I can't really say much on that. I do like the idea, but it's clearly intended for co-op as enemies get too difficult if you don't complete the mission fast enough. Objectives tend to be split and located in locations far from each other.Overall: Don't buy this game just yet. It has a good base -  -  but it needs more content, especially for the price tag.  Having some sort of endless multiplayer game mode shouldn't be an excuse to neglect the single-player game modes. It's not a buggy mess, thank goodness, but I hope the devs sort out the pathing, controls, and other bugs I probably was too blind to spot. I also suggest waiting to see how the devs approach patches and new content. Plus, it gives the community time to test how robust the game's mod support is, especially compared to its prequels.

_childDocuments_.review: Perfectly good.There was good effort and development in making each campaign environment somewhat dynamic as well as flowing seamlessly from story point to mission and back again. This was well done. And the story was acceptable. The characters a bit.....bland.For all this, each campaign map felt cramped. Encroached on. Caged in. Gone is the strategic wonder of establishing a supply base and exploring a sector of cold, dark space. And the game lost something for it. Each step prompted. Each step practically scripted. Free to seek resources or be creative in how you maneuver, but the vast depths of space were successfully reduced to the size and feel of a desert canyon on Kharak.There was one mission where about 5 times in very short succession it interrupted the start of gameplay just to toss some mission video or conversation in. THAT was annoying. Just let me play. Let me explore. Let me figure it out instead of handing me the guides of where / when to go in the case of asteroids in motion. And why must each sector be so colorfully backlit? Space is BLACK with a few pinpricks of light.The hot-swap to tactical view was interesting. Just not effective. Just allow us to zoom far enough out on the map in general and you can ditch that view altogether.This is all me being nit-picky. The game was still fun to play. Kind of quick to burn through on Medium for a veteran. I'll go back to select missions in the future perhaps. Hoping for more scenario gameplay options. OH! And having just two factions and relatively slim depth of ship models / upgrades.... meh.

_childDocuments_.review: True 3D space combat returns after over twenty years! I'm a veteran of Homeworld 1, 2 and Desserts of Kharak. I loved Homeworld 1, it was just about the perfect space RTS except it was missing the ability to use structures for cover. Homeworld 2 had a confusing and, frankly, underwhelming story and lost some of the squadron combat fun from HW 1, but made up for those losses with general improvements in combat and the neat cap ship subsystem targetting system. Desserts had a nice capital ship subsystems feature and a good story, but I didn't like how the game transitioned away from true 3D combat (sure sure, you could take the high ground, but it missed that true 3D freedom of being in space). Now...finally, we're back in space with HW 3. Let me break it down for you: The Good: - Graphics- Audio & music (welcome back, Paul Ruskay!)- Gameplay, specifically we can FINALLY utilize megastructures in combat; THIS IS HUGE! - Controls & UI: The Devs listened to feedback from the demo, and we have a LOT of control over the UI and controls...more then I've seen from other modern RTS games. - Multiplayer: Wargames is clearly this game's break and butter and, thankfully it's fun! Homeworld meets rogue-light gameplay with a progression system focused around securing artifacts...which fits the general Homeworld vibe just fine. The meh: - The story: It's fine....lots of people hate it, but it's a run of the mill character driven piece of sci fi. The Higgarans are in a position of power, so the story naturally won't revolve around them finding their homeworld, and the story of a young S'Jen finding the confidence to take command is compelling. Don't hate the story because it's not Homeworld 1....move on.- System requirments: It's definitly a demanding game, but it scales well enough to be playable on the Steam Deck, so a wide range of systems should have no problem at least playing the game. The Ugly: - Fan-base: I hate to say this, but the almost venamous hatred of this game seems to come from Homeworld die-hards, like myself, but.....these die-hards refuse to like anything that isn't a carbon copy of Homeworld 1 or 2. Move on...it's 2024, the Khushan don't need to find their homeworld anymore, and the story and tone of the game should (and do) bring the game into the modern world. SO, should you buy HW 3? Yes, IF you like a complex true 3D real time strategy game with great visuals and a great soundtrack. IF you just want Homeworld 1 & 2, then go play those games. There's enough of the original Homeworld feel here to call this a worthy sequel, so please don't complain that the game isn't a carbon copy of a twenty year old game.In the meantime, the Mothership is back on-line and I am here for it!

_childDocuments_.review: Steam really needs a neutral option for its reviews. This is a three-point-five star game, to use the GoG system, but... oh well, up or down it is, so...The first question anybody is going to ask about HW3 is whether or not it lives up to HW1 or Cataclysm. The answer to that question is "no"- but let's face it, nothing else in this franchise has lived up to HW1 or Cata. This series peaked with its first two entries, and it's time we all faced the fact that nothing following those high highs is ever going to blow us away like the Mothership launching or the Beast infecting the Kuun-Lan's lower decks did.And... I'd be lying if I said there aren't a raft of other shortcomings with this game. It doesn't meet the standard set by HW1 and Cata, and it doesn't even rise to the level of HW2. But I'm still going to recommend it, for one simple reason: the field of fully-3D RTS games is still a shockingly empty one, and that dearth of competition alone makes Homeworld 3 the best of its kind to be seen in years. If that's the itch you're looking to scratch, this is pretty much the best you're going to get. If that sounds like damning with faint praise... well, yeah. But that's the whole point, isn't it? Is HW3's lack of ambition- its failure to carve out an identity of its own, beyond the title it inherited- any real surprise, when the glorious heritage it rests on has seen no real challenge in almost two human generations?Even a quarter of a century later, the list of even passably decent RTS games with 3-dimensional gameplay (as opposed to just 3D graphics) is a pathetically short one... and most of the games on that list are titled "Homeworld." Even if not all of the promises were delivered on, and even if this game is a mere echo of the greatness this series achieved with its first two entries, it's still head and shoulders above the rest of the genre, which has dared only the most timid ventures into the third dimension in the two and a half decades since Homeworld fans issued their first vertical move command to their first formation of Scouts in Kharak orbit, just to marvel at the fact that we could, all those years ago. And, in the end, the tragic failure of the rest of the genre to follow in Homeworld's footsteps is far more of a disappointment than Homeworld 3 failing to fill its own progenitors' shoes. So... fans of 3D strategy games with actual 3D gameplay should play Homeworld 3, even if it's more than a little bit of a letdown to fans of the series. They'll likely have little else to sate their appetite until the next Homeworld comes around.

_childDocuments_.review: The good:-Mothership / Carriers have decent point defense weapons now.-Hiigara's ship design is clearly continuing to evolve, and this shows across the entire fleet.-Parallel construction across fabricators - just like HW1. I missed this so much.-Graphics are incredible. -Soundscape is both very satisfying & informative.-A strong emphasis on tactical combat vs massive blobbing tactics.-Less micro with resourcing - controllers handle salvaging, resourcing, and stealing enemy ships. A change from HW:C that continues to be used to this day, though we have Support Frigates for healing now, and Incarnate use controllers for repairs.-Assault frigates are the tanks they were destined to be, with an active ability to make them even tankier.Outstanding OST. -Battle chatter is even more immersive.-Unreal Engine is best in class for modding - very excited to see what the community produces over the coming months.-War Games is a great coop experience with a ton of replay-ability.The bad:-No tactical hyperspacing - supercaps have to crawl around the map (all game modes)-Only two factions, again. Homeworld: Remastered spoiled me here. Would've been nice to have more options, but maybe we'll get them in mods.-Few Multiplayer maps, with most of the release ones being far too small for my taste. Resourcing hotspots will become hotly contested within minutes of a round starting.-Railgun corvettes. A terrible corvette and Hiigara's only option? I don't get why Incarnate gets anti-fighter, anti-capital, and crowd control corvettes. _childDocuments_.review: Homeworld 3 is an example of what happens when a publisher refuses to allow a developer control over its own game. On the things that BBI had control over, it performed very well. This includes art style, optimization, sound, and music. Everything else? Everything else ranges from serviceable to completely and utterly bad. The gameplay is serviceable in that BBI still has a chance as of writing to a) add features it promised in the Fig Campaign, and b) bring the gameplay up to HW2/HW1 standard in terms of content/functionality. As for the single player campaign, we must divide it into 2 parts: The mission design and the story. The mission design varies in quality, but for the most part it is passable. The first 6 missions are well structured. The asteroid mission in particular is quite challenging is a nice change of pace. We can see, however, that the end of the game was derailed by malicious entities at Gearbox; the final two missions of the game do not feel like the rest. The final missions of HW1 and HW2 were, as one would expect, were brutal, massive fleet actions. M12 and M13 of HW3 are not. They are unsatisfying, particularly M13, and this is likely because at time of writing unit pathing is still a huge issue. M13 is also a failure of a final mission because of the narrative. The story of Homeworld 3 is a catastrophe of a narrative. It has unnecessary inconsistencies, the worst dialogue I have seen in a game in years, an antagonist that is for all intents and purposes a petulant child, character development that is undone in two cutscenes, and a conclusion that leaves the player unimaginably unsatisfied. I've never finished a videogame story feeling like I was cheated out of the victory that the player should have obtained, but Homeworld 3 somehow accomplishes that. If there is any takeaway I obtained from the Homeworld 3 campaign, it is that no gamer should ever play a game with a story written by Gearbox. When the mod tools for HW3 are released, I imagine some great mods will be made that will improve the game dramatically. For the moment though, Homeworld 3 is just one more game in a long list of titles ruined by publishers that think far too highly of themselves.

_childDocuments_.review: As a game, it is serviceable. As an entry to the Homeworld franchise, it is abysmal. It's sad to think that this may just be the last Homeworld game ever made, officially at any rate. The fleet roster feels extremely lacking. Only one corvette? Only the 3 basic strike craft? Why did all the ideas go into the frigates only for the campaign to limit you to a total of 50? The ships look beautiful, like most things in this game, their sound is great and most feel nice to field. It could just use more ship types and fewer restrictions on number in certain instances. By the time I got torp frigates, I couldn't build more than 3, and I'm not sure if this is player error or what but there doesn't seem to be an ability to retire ships. The story. Sajuuk save us. What is the story of Homeworld? It's a war story following a displaced people defending their right to exist and to reclaim their lost homeworld from the empire which doomed them all for their forgotten ancestors' sins. It does not focus on character or development, it focuses on the big picture, of guiding and protecting a group of people. Its characters are professionals whose performances help guide the emotional journey of the story.HW1 set this up for the series flawlessly. When Kharak burned, we didn't get a cutscene of Karan and Intel crying in each other's arms. We got Adagio for Strings and choked devastation in the delivery of briefings. We didn't get clubbed over the head to understand Karan's selflessness, we learned it after seeing her entombed within the mothership and after she chose to be the last person to set foot on the world they fought to reclaim.Cataclysm did this perfectly as well at a smaller scale. It told a story of protecting the homeworld from an ancient terror as a group of outsiders, unloved and uncelebrated by all. We didn't get animated cutscenes of The Beast taking over peoples' bodies. We got these professionals screaming in agony and terror, we got the ancient, powerful Bentusi panicking to leave the galaxy and preserve themselves against the terror. HW2 derailed to a certain degree. It muddled the warstory of protecting the homeworld from a threatening barbarian warlord into an ancient prophesy to uncover an ancient ship turned mythical god. It told the story well and in keeping with Homeworld's style. The characters are still not the focus, but the campaign. The war to uncover the truth and outpace the enemy took center-stage. Deserts of Kharak, a prequel made by the same studio, developed wonderfully on the formula while staying faithful. The character drama is present but in the background. The main story is the hunt for an anomalous artifact against fanatical resistance, to save your world from encroaching climate disaster and death. What did we get in HW3? We got bludgeoned repeatedly by childish, unprofessional characters. They squabble and fight and act with more angst than a midwest emo group. The setup is interesting, a space anomaly eating the galaxy from hyperspace which no one knows how to defeat. To protect your homeworld you must stop the spread of the anomaly. But when we got angsty lonely space hitler destroying planets to spite us for convoluted reasons, it really left any pretense of following Homeworld's style. The art style of cutscenes is completely different. The 3D animation on its own does look nice. But when you have a series known for its storyboard style animations, focusing on space ships, stellar phenomena and megastructures, the character-driven animations simply don't fit. Character drama and development is not what this series is about, it's about the protection of your people and your home. To basically abandon that home at the end spits in the face of the series. There's more to say about the game. Why does every map have to be approximately 20 square meters hovering 30cm over a megastructure? Why no expansive space maps with asteroids, the bread and butter of the homeworld franchise? I'll leave this here, however. I wanted this game to be good, I love this series. In its current state, I just can't, and the work required to fix it would basically turn it into a whole new game. Someone messed this game up, the love for the setting and series can still be felt in some places. Hopefully we can get something of a spiritual successor made by someone who loves this style of storytelling and gameplay without some corporate exec breathing down their throat to turn it into something it shouldn't be.

_childDocuments_.review: I really, *really* wanted to like this.  Like "I waited for 22 years" wanted to like it.In its current state, I don't.  I enjoy the RTS aspects of it, and the environmental stuff that was teased for HW2 in 2001 has taken its damn time, so that's nice to see.  However, environments are difficult to navigate with ships often choosing to go around as it's an easier route than a tunnel.  The "NOW YOU CAN CHOOSE YOUR BANANA'S ORIENTATION" mechanic appears in the final parts of the final mission and is entirely restricted to one specific action above three stationary locations.  I'm not talking navigating environmental puzzles here,, I'm talking "we have to move above this thing and drop something which can only be dropped when we're horizontal".  It's appalling.The single player campaign is VA'd extremely poorly, the cutscenes genuinely look like an AI filter, the script is honestly cringeworthy, the stakes aren't communicated.  It's extremely poorly directed, with some bizarre story beats that don't make any sense.  Any real exposition is hidden behind "ThE aNoMaLy"... like... what IS the anomaly?  What MAKES it an anomaly?Why are we ordered to stop communicating with Hiigara?  Never explained.  Why doesn't the Hyperspace Wizard simply melt our ships like they did with entire ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ planets?  Never explained.  How did Karan S'Jet end up a popsicle?  Never explained.  Where did all her crew go?  Never explained.  How did she survive TWENTY YEARS alone and plugged in to a frozen ship?  Never explained.  Why is her ship more powerful than one twenty years younger?  Never explained.  Why is the mothership the fastest ship in the game?  You guessed it.  Who, and I mean this in the most sympathetic way, the ♥♥♥♥ is Imogen S'Jet and why do we care?Gameplay isn't entirely bad, but is still bad.  It takes a little getting used to, having research and building in the same menu, but it kind of works.  Resourcing operations are now entirely automated and never placed where you'd need to defend them.  Select all, tap H, ignore them for the rest of the mission, profit.Upgrades to ships are entirely linear, extremely basic, and feel like they have very little overall effect on the gameplay (with the exception of the ludicrous speed upgrade for the mothership).  It's the familiar rock-paper-scissors of any RTS game, but zerg-rushing with an ample unit cap and more resources at your disposal than Elon ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Musk means that there is very little challenge to the game.  Ships are fragile and you can lose a lot with only a couple of dumb decisions, especially with fighters near poorly-telegraphed AoE explosions, but those decisions come from boredom and just wanting to progress to the next mission more than anything else.  Worse, you can ignore main objectives to clear maps (such as the final mission) entirely before absolutely walking the actual mission.I might enjoy skirmish and war games, but I am frankly dreading more voice acting that I, as someone who has never voiced anything in my life, could do better.Overall, it's painfully disappointing.  This is not worth 22 years of your time, £50 of your money, or whatever Gearbox paid to acquire the IP.

_childDocuments_.review: tl:dr: DON'T BUY FULL PRICE, WAIT FOR SALE. The admiral that flies the ship, looks/reminds me of the "Come here, come closer" guy for food hacks on pizza from social media.I don't usually write reviews but I'm feeling pretty ripped off for getting the Fleet Command Edition and the constant let down of new game released the last 5 years especially. It seems it's just better to wait for games to release before buying these days instead of pre-ordering because you love the game series/company/franchise. Homeworld 3 is unfortunately no exception to that, you definitely can't trust company marketing anymore these days. Homeworld 3 is unfortunately, a big let down and disappointment for me. I had a lot of expectations and the team seems like it delivered based on their trailers and showcasing of the game. However I can now confirm, they failed hard on delivering. It's NOTHING like Homeworld 1 and 2. The game doesn't allow for large scale warfare, there's such a small cap on units that it feels like you only ever have a small battalion for an army. I think the unit cap is 80 or 85?, it's super disappointing. Pros: The sound and cinematics team for Homeworld 3 did a PHENOMENAL job. The experience for campaign was stellar. However, the story turned out to be super mediocre, bland, and the campaign was so short. The landscape in the game/mega structures/environment/lighting looks amazing. Graphics i'd say is pretty good, design of ships are cool too. The big pro of this game I'd say is mods, modding is definitely going to be the redeeming factor of this game I'd say so just wait a little bit for players to start work and release mods for this game.Cons: Combat was very difficult because unit pathing makes NO SENSE. I find that often times, my units will not do as I've commanded/ordered them to which leads to MANY headaches especially during crucial moments in combat. Formation is also frustrating and found that formations helped next to none because my units were always trying to create/maintain formation and would be more focused on formation than combat so I found that turning off formation worked out better.Homeworld 3 feels like yet, another incomplete game with horrible decisions that don't make sense and seem counter intuitive to the RTS genre. It's sad to see this consistent restriction of keeping unit caps low in MANY RTS games or going squad based/MOBA direction. The skirmish is god awful as well, you're placed so close to one another and the biggest team is only a 3v3. This makes NO SENSE to me, why not go up to 8v8 for example? Not a lot of selection of maps or options for skirmish as well. The small unit cap count makes it hard to like this game as much as I wantd to love it.I really wanted to like Homeworld 3 but I find myself learning more on negative than positive. It pains me to say this, but if you like sci-fi, space, and large scale warfare, you're probably better off waiting for Sins of a Solar Empire 2 that's releasing later 2024.

_childDocuments_.review: If anyone at BBI sees this I want you to know how much it hurts to give this game a negative review. 20 years waiting for a sequel to HW2 and we get this? HW3's story makes HW2's look like a masterpiece instead of just being mid. I could actually somewhat forgive (but not really because it just doesn't make sense) things like the simplified gameplay and wonky unit ai if the story for HW3 wasn't so unbelievably terrible and just cringey af lol. Main villain? Laughably bad, literal space hitler who is lonely gets essentially forgiven for killing millions just like that? Karan now is apparently incompetent? You're seriously telling me the person who led the exiles from the near extinction of their race against the Taiidan empire AND the near annihilation of Hiigara from the Vaygr invasion just...loses? Just like that? To the Incarnate? The most lame enemies of any of the HW games? Yeah right LOL. GTFO of here with that nonsense. Where did Sajuuk go? Synthetic hyperspace cores, bruh...really? tf? I thought the cores were supposed to be these highly coveted and deeply significant objects? They sure were before in HW1 and HW2. In HW1 the core the exiles secreted from the Taiidan was what allowed them to even stand a chance at reaching Hiigara. HW2's main plot point revolved around the 3 cores lol. Now they can just make hyperspace cores? I guess they just aren't that important or special anymore.Whatever, the story is an unsalvageable travesty, fine ok let's move on to gameplay stuff since at least that has a chance to improve. First, what was the reason to remove features and simplify gameplay elements from 20 years ago, like for example subsystems from HW2, which ok yeah only HW2 really had (I know in HWC the command ship had modules but they weren't targetable your ships just hit them if they fired in their direction) but why remove that feature? Why combine build and research? Doesn't make any sense to me, it just comes off as unnecessary.Again though I could somewhat forgive there being things like that if the rest of the game functioned well but it just doesn't. Unit balancing is wack, who in tf balanced this game? Drunk people? I'd have to be to think any of the following is a good idea.1. Mothership is on super speed upgrades why? In campaign in OUTRUNS STRIKE CRAFT LOL. It's just...dumb.2 .Fighters and corvettes are slow af in general. Turn speed slow af, max speed is slow af (except recons using speed upgrade I guess). Also why do Hiigarans have only ONE CORVETTE? Incarnate have only ONE FIGHTER? It's just bad...bad, bad, BAD.3. Capital ships are just pathetic. Slower than the mothership (again, just...why is it so fast lol), have like, what? 2km weapon range? Barely do any damage, really bad combat unit ai in general. Really accurate against strike craft though lol, which btw is BAD. They should not be very good vs strike craft unless its something like the missile destroyer of HW1. Imagine HW2 hiigaran bc sniping fighers with its ion cannons lol. Yeah there's a reason it wasn't able to do that it's called game balance.4. Just resource controllers now, seriously? WHY? Utterly unnecessary and removes even more of the strategic depth that this game barely has as it is! Just like combining build and research because research barely exists!5. Oh right research, that thing that barely exists for a boring and EXTREMELY LINEAR AND REALLY BORING TECH TREE. If you can even call it a "tech tree"...wait you can't because its not a tree at all it's a singular pathway LOL. Just why?6. To continue with the lame research "tree". Unit abilities! EVERY. SINGLE. UNIT. IN. THE. GAME. Holy crap why?! Who are you trying to appeal to with this? I mean at least it's not as bad now as it was in the wargames demo (because dear god, those horrendous braindead APM spam abilities were pure pain). Actually I'd be ok with all these abilities on units if the abilities they have are mostly cool and/or creative like in previous games (HWC and DoK, especially in HWC though) but they aren't so...yeah it's just bad!7. The unit AI is just infuriating! PLEASE FIX! Units (especially units in formation) can have their pathing get hung up or just seem to get confused by the "terrain". Terrain which too many maps have too much of, seriously it is a cool feature but way overused, this is still a game set in space you know? Also units in formation, well frigates and larger ships anyway, just...don't work very well in formation at all lol.8. Speaking of formations can we PLEASE for the love of all things holy REMOVE the unit behavior that causes everything you select not in a formation to automatically enter into delta formations?! It is beyond seriously annoying! You can then tell them to LEAVE FORMATION and they will just immediately give you the finger and go right back into delta LOL. Why is this a thing? It needs to be removed ASAP.Alright I could go on but that's enough for now. With mod tools available (which relies on there being somebody with the time and will to dedicate to that) and possible official updates, though at this point in time I must doubt much will come from them, (please prove me wrong BBI I beg you) there is maybe, hopefully, some shred of hope for this game to at least be as good as HW2. Surely that isn't asking too much? I could be asking for it to be as good as HW1 or HWC but, well we all know that is pretty much impossible. Though again I would love to be proved wrong about that!I know it seems I just hate this game completely but that's not true.1. Music is overall quite good, just not many pieces that stand out from the rest save a few such as the Adagio for Strings remix.2. Art style is faithful to Homeworld. Well ingame at least, cutscenes not so much, makes me wonder what happened to the DoK looking cutscene art style we saw a couple years ago? It looked a lot better then :/3. Ship designs are good I just wish there was more variety. Some also look a bit too similar to others but whatever I can deal with that.4. Sound effects and graphics are all very good but as always good graphics alone don't make a good game.Anyway time to look forward and hope Sins of Solar Empire 2 is good to help alleviate the pain of HW3.

_childDocuments_.review: I got the Collectors Edition, I actually preordered it on the day it was announced 30 August 2019.I can't say if the game is recommendable or not on its release. There are some issues gameplay quality-wise that I have. I do enjoy the level design and map feel, I can see what the design team wanted from the beginning back in 2003. Now that the technology has caught up, unfortunately the timelessness hasn't. Homeworld 3 is content inferior to Homeworld 2, Soundtrack is merged between Homeworld 1, 2, and DoK with some unique tracks. I do think some bug-fixes are needed. I also think this game can be made extremely great due to Mod Support and the innate power of Unreal 4. But I will recommend this game because when the Mod Tools release it will be like opening Pandora's Box. Although I will remark that the storyline could have been done better, not as simple as Homeworld 1 and not nearly has Epic as Homeworld 2. The idea of the incarnate while novel, the idea of the Incarnate Queen and how she is portrayed is nothing compared to the terror of Khad-Sajuuk, Riesstiu, the Beast and lastly Makaan (who I think was the scariest of all). Although what I can see is that they tried merging the four adversaries into one, but they didn't do it right, It came out more psychopathic Beast lady who throws a tantrum the whole time, than anything else. Wargames is fun, Skirmish is Skirmish, Campaign has amazing level design, but terrible story telling, and we really only fight the Incarnate, with Kalan Raiders being some sort of tutorial opponent, they could have at least added 2 more factions to fight and expanded the mission count to 17 or 18 even with a epilogue mission. They can adjust Ship sizes though, some ships are too small, others too big. DLC Campaigns with Characters with real hateful or loving depth would make the difference. I enjoyed it but didn't feel ultimately satisfied like Homeworld 1 or 2 with the Campaign ending.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a pure gem and is just what I expected from Homeworld saga. Superb story! Had a blast playing campaign from start to finish on Hard Difficulty. Brought me a lot of challenge and 35 hours of game play just to do campaign. Really hope there will be more to the story! To relive something again 20 years back - feels nice, good old child memories. Really recommend playing this game on Hard, it's very enjoyable and challenging!Graphics are stunning. Everything looks beautiful in game. The scenery of space, ships and of course the looks of your Mothership just makes me melt.Combat is amazing! Offers huge space battles that makes my pc go vroom. Ships have their specials abilities to use against an enemy. There is a way to play it full assault or sneaky peaky like and strike an enemy from behind in different ways. I love it!War Games one of the best modes that could happen to Homeworld franchise. It's very fun, battle intense and addictive, but for a very short time as it needs a lot more content to it. Right now it's bit too short, needs more objectives, more play styles and way more maps. The major downside I have on this game is it's a bit very high CPU intensive game or maybe just badly optimized, because you might run into low performance issues while fighting in huge battles, but once you get used to it - you won't notice a thing.Is it worth the money? Suit yourself! Because for me it for sure was worth it! Would love to see more content for Homeworld 3 in the future.Fleet Commander signing out. Peace!

_childDocuments_.review: My biggest issue with this game was trying to keep track of my own ships.  The environment had a lot going on and the ships are not visually distinctive.While I do appreciate their attempt to shift away from the the grand adventure of a people to make a more human story, it felt somewhat disjointed. It actually felt like there were scenes missing.I dont get the value of the "cover mechanic."  You can send you fighters into tunnels to keep them safe from the enemy only to have them pop out the other side just to get obliterated by anti fighter turrets. So what was the point of the trench run? The game never really rewarded me for doing anything clever.  If I figured out a choke point the enemy would just not go that way.

_childDocuments_.review: As a Homeworld 1, 2 and Kharak fan, I felt Homeworld 3 was very disappointing and very hard to see how they could justify the price point and the fact they have a battle pass.I cannot think of anything new this game brought to the franchise, like nothing stood out to me. Low ship variety of familiar ship classes, tactics seem to be simplified to zerging and blobbing.Then there was the story. I loved Homeworld for its dynamic storytelling that comes through the battle chatter and the occasional cutscenes you'd get. A formula set through all the previous games. The stories were grounded in relatively believable consistency of the Homeworld Universe. Homeworld 3's story seems to deviate from that. Infact the story seems to have taken centre stage over the game itself at times and the vibe set by the previous Homeworld games. It felt as if to me that making Homeworld 3 was the only way that the person behind the story could make their own low budge scifi film or TV show. The story of Homeworld 3 are all the crappy bits of the 2004 Battlestar Galactica run.Is the story bad? Is it what has killed Homeworld 3? No. Its an uninspired sequel to a great franchise that tries to deviate from previous games with a grandiose SyFi channel plot. Its an OK game but cannot recommend at full price, I would have refunded by I mistakenly passed the three hour mark in an attempt to give the game a chance.

The game isn’t too demanding to run, I found it running quite well on my 1080GPU with all settings on except Ray Tracing and at 1080p however I got a constant 60fps (Limit due to my TV Herts) Homeworld 3 is a solid game, a game I enjoyed, and I would recommend it for Homeworld fans, RTS fans and Sci-Fi fans, but expect a short Campaign. _childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game, so much of it I love from the previous homeworlds, including Deserts of Kharak... but the game is empty. The story is half-told and doesn't make sense, the WarGames Coop is just button mashing to get as many ships out the door as possible (for the moment), and Skirmish is... fine, but has 6 maps and no real tech/research trees. I've played 11 hours, beat the campaign, a couple skirmishes, and a couple wargames... and I'm done for now. I even have the ship models from my Collector's Edition, and I'm sure I'll come back and play some more down the line... but for now, this game doesn't deliver what we all hoped it would.I hope they come back and fix a lot of these things, though realistically it would require a remake. I'm worried about the future of the series, because I love this series and want more Homeworld, but in their hope to make HW3 seemingly more of an E-sport vs keeping it in tune with what it always was (a slower, methodical, tactical game), it feels as if they lost their way. I'm putting this as a 'recommend' because I'm finding it difficult to actually hit 'no', but this game is not what I was hoping it would be.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot comfortably recommend this game in its current state.When it comes to HW games this does not feel like a true HW game if anything its trying to be one to hard. I would say an attempt was made at best.Cons:-Story line has to much focus on characters and to much in game chatter between them. Does not have the kind of epic feel the past HW installments had.-Unit designs feel like copy and paste and unique abilities are a micro manage nightmare... Do they look cool? sure seems more fire animations and such but they are no different from past HW units and the capital ships can handle fighters/bombers with ease which creates an imbalance. The capital ships also have no weak-points and no armor strong/weak areas now. The units build for fighters is single units which is like the old HW and not like the HW2 fighter squads which was so much better.-HUD/Interface made a little too complex than should be. Could of used the interface system used from HW1/2 and would of been fine and kept the hotkeys from that but they re-did the whole system...-Resource units have to be micro-managed and will not go off and find more resources near by that's rather off-putting. Turret platforms seem to only be mounted to astroid or still platforms not like old turret platforms from HW2Pros:-Resource controllers make and hive manage resource collectors so less moving parts-Mother ship turret system feels more reliable than past games-History of HW at menu-Graphics are rather good for the game-Same composer from last games-different game mode and a co-op systemOverall the game just feels its lacking in design of the actual game-play and went a step back than forward. When designing a successor game need to look at what people liked in the previous games and what to add or make better not take away and not dumb it down. This does not feel like its better or more fun than the previous installments of the series and feels lack luster.

_childDocuments_.review: This has nothing to do with previous homeworlds, and is a step back in every aspect, and i mean it.Tutorial is disjointed from the whole campaign unlike HW1/2.compare how strikecrafts fly in Hw1/2 and 3 - properly splitting into wingman pairs, flanking targets vs roughly being arranged in formation and flying on flat plane in space.Pathfinding is atrocious - how can you mess up pathfinding in mostly empty space!Superstructures are neat idea, but super clunky to actually use. Sometimes you try to send your recons through the structure only to get 2 out of 5 of them fly on the outside. They are extremly clunky to use, and serve similar purpose as nebulae.No customization of mothership - previously you had to decide - what types of fabrication capabilities will i have on my ships, now it's just all in one.Upgrades are gimmick abilities that are 'press to deal more daamge' tier. doesn't change how you play at all.Story, i have no words how they messed it up - homeworld was always a story about nations, groups and journey. characters never had faces nor identities except one: Karan S'Jet, who was less human and more machine. Now we have basically marvel tier writing that's also inconsistent to hell, with a "journey" that's forced for logical reason.Game starts with Mothership launching on the Planet(!) surface - which is already pointless, why would you give atmospheric flight capabilities to such ship? - and hyperspacing out. in atmosphere. through matter(air).Then they have a plot point about enemy using hyperspace through matter - which Hiigarans did in first mission.The more i play it, the less i want to. I'll keep the game and see what moders can cook, because my time would be better spent on HW1 and HW2. Because HW3 is worse in every aspect than those games - art style, atmosphere, gameplay, and plot.

_childDocuments_.review: To put it mildly. I am very disappointed at the outcome of this game. It wears the name and look of Homeworld, but lacks all of its depth and nuance. It looks amazing and sounds fantastic, but under the hood is a oversimplified game that is  missing almost every game mechanic that makes Homeworld unique.-small ships are slow and sluggish, while the large ships are too fast and nimble. Almost no ship moves the way they should based on their size. The mothership is the fastest ship in the game, at least in single player. Let that sink in.-strikecraft don't act right In formations, they just cluster around a central point and fly as a giant swarm. They don't engage multiple enemies at once, even if there is more than one. They don't evade, split up, or anything.-strike craft have no staying power, since they're built one at a time. Battlecruisers counter everything.-no directional damage as far as I can tell. This renders the 3D combat almost meaningless. Not that it matters, because ships turn so fast, you can't flank them anyway.-no moving-while-engaging. Capitals ships will stop and turn around if you tell them to move while they're engaged, instead of kiting enemies like they did in both previous games. This makes capital ship combat pointless. Clearly its in the game, because enemies do it sometimes, but for some reason mine never do.-no subsystems or modules from HW2. We're back to the HW1 system now. This means a carrier can do pretty much what a mothership can do, short of building battlecruisers. No longer can i choose what my carrier can do, or place hyperspace modules on my battlecruisers.-since there are no sub systems, large ships can't have their engines disabled by smaller ships, leading to boring "fly-foward-and-shoot" type gameplay.-no tactical jumps from HW2. For a game about hyperspace, I can't hyperspace. Not that it matters too much since the maps are tiny, most of which are just straight lines.-tiny maps, made even small by the giant megaliths. For a space game, there is a lack of space in this game. Every map is filled with a giant structure that takes up most of the map. I know this is a selling point, but honestly does it need to be in every map?And all of this sacrificed for a overblown CG cinematic that takes up 1/3 of the ~7 hour playtime, with a lot of unskippable dialogue in-mission that bloats the length even more. There are already many mentions of how bad the story and characters are, so I won't beat that dead horse. To put it simply, it lacks the relatable epic of HW1, it lacks the sense of awe and discovery in HW2, and lacks the stylized painted cinematics of Deserts of Kharak. A step down in every sense.Was it worth waiting for 8 years? No. Is it worth the 60 dollar price tag? Absolutely not. Is it even a Homeworld game? maybe only on the surface.

_childDocuments_.review: It's very bad.I tried to give this game a chance... but no.  Its just very disappointing.  The last time I felt like this was when Dawn of War 3 came out.   I'd refund if I could, even tried multiple times, but was rejected due to my play-time (17 hours).  I really REALLY tried to give it a chance, but no.I waited for a long time for a new Homeworld game.  Deserts of Kharak was good, but that was just a side-game and prequel.  I wanted a follow-up to Homeworld 2.This ain't it.  This ain't it at all.  The only parts they got right are surface-level stuff.  Art-style, graphics, and sounds are good.  Thats it.  Camera is a little busted, but you can get used to it.  I used modern-controls but changed the camera to legacy. I really hate how enclosed the maps are.  It's a space game WHERE'S THE SPACE!This had the side-effect of just forcing you to blob your forces.  There's little to no tactical and strategic planning like in previous games.   Pathfinding is also atrocious as a result.  I get they wanted to show-off the megalith and terrain, but I'm playing a space game, not deserts of kharak but with zero-gravity.  It's just a neat-gimmick that looks great on paper, but the implementation of it and how over-reliant this game is on the terrain is very bad.  The story is downright atrocious and doesn't make sense.  You know how people say HW2 has the weakest story of all the Homeworld games back then?  This makes HW2's story look like a master-piece.   There's also ugly cutscenes.   Gone are those beautiful motion-painting style cutscenes that previous games had.  They replaced them with uncanny valley horror CG.  Also, why do they keep bringing the camera so close to the character's ugly mug?  Stop that.  I don't want to see Imogen making bizarre facial twitches up close or the Incarnate-Queen making a smirk that makes her look like Donkey from Shrek.  I get the feeling these shots worked well if it was done in the style like Deserts of Kharak, but it doesn't work here.  Who the hell animated these?  I hope for a mod to just replace these, or hell, an official update the replaces them with classic style cutscenes.  It has to be sitting somewhere in their offices because back in 2021 reveal trailer, they did have plans on using old-style cutscenes but dropped it some time around 2023!Skirmish is the worst.  Only six maps SIX MAPS.  wtf! I don't think Deserts of Kharak was this bad on it's release.  The main meat is obviously the Wargames mode, since their year 1 roadmap is centered around it.  But its unbelievably short!  after 3 or 4 maps, its done, you're booted back into the menu.   Its also built around co-op since the balancing for Wargames is very bad if you're trying to play solo.  You just get swarmed by capital ships that you can't even build yourself.   Well they better change that in the future because very soon there won't be a lot of people playing this game.  Hell its only been less than a month and the player-base is almost dead already. For a $60 game, it is severely lacking in content DO NOT BUY IT AT FULL PRICE.  Wait for a sale.  Judging from how bad of a flop this game is, that shouldn't be too far away.Homeworld just got the Dawn of War 3 treatment.  Now it remains to be seen if they plan on abandoning it.update:  Well it's almost the end of July, yep they're abandoning it.   Just treat this game like C&C4.

_childDocuments_.review: Voting this down was hard for me, because I really love Homeworld since I was a teenanger. This is not on Blackbird Interactive. They proved that they can deliver a Homeworld game with Deserts of Kharak. Gearbox and its creative meddling since 2022 is solely to blame for ruining Homeworld 3's story.Graphics are great. Soundtrack is good. Gameplay a little dumbed down compared to HW1, Cataclysm and HW2 but it is not bad. I had a lot of fun playing the missions (even thouhg there are not that many and those are rather short) and stuff so it is not a bad RTS at all. It still has a glimmer of a great Homeworld 3 which BBI wanted to create so to say.The story is derailed and awful. The lore established by previous games is not respected at all. The problem can be summed up as this: My impression is that previous Homeworld games' stories were about a people - the Kushan or Hiigarans respectively - and their journey, strife and overcoming against all odds while HW3's story is about three people. The focus on three people and their personal feelings is just not Homeworld, and the CGI cutscenes while being of good quality are really not suited for telling a Homeworld story. HW3 is not that epic space opera previous HW games were - it feels rather small and narrow.The biggest issue in the story presented to me is the antagonist - the incarnte queen. She is the worst antagonist you could think of. The queen feels forcibly inserted into the story, her capabilities and motives make no sense and I still do not know what her ultimate goal even was. This character is uninspired, irritating, annoying and after all her atrocities the ending is not handling this character in a proper way at all. She also has way too much screentime and her ramblings and nagging is a constant theme of the story after the first third to half of the game.Since we'll probably never know what the actual Homeworld 3 story should have been as BBI imagined it I'd like to give my idea on how this existing mess could have been fleshed out in a more lore-friendly, less irritating way.[Very mild and vague spoilers (the mysterious faction who have ancient progenitor lvl tech(!) who built the planet killers from HW2)-make the incarnate not just moronic zealots but abducted people controlled/heavily influenced by the T-Mat-instead of the incarnate queen the T-Mat turn out to be an ancient, conscious Progenitor AI which was tasked originally with maintaining and managing the Gate Network but went insane and turned against its creators, shut down the Gate Network, enslaved people somehow (mind alteration/control via brain implants or something) waged war against and destroyed Progenitor civilization and plunged the galaxy into the dark ages (would make more sense why the Progenitors hid Sajuuk in the center of the galaxy, scattered/hid the Great Hyperspace Cores and created the Keepers to protect their remaining stuff they still had control of)-T-Mat/AI has not been fully active throughout the eons and was slumbering -when Karan S'Jet finds the Eye of Aarran & reactives the Gate Network in the epilogue of HW2 the T-Mat AI notices of course and becomes fully awake again-(maybe since being somehow tapped into hyperspace the usage of hyperspace via the gates causes it "AI-migraine", because making an AI into some form of Unbound has this effect?) idk about this one but it could be an interesting motive why it went insane in the first place-since thousands of years have passed and much of progenitor tech it once took control of is in ruins, it has only control of a relatively small Incarnate force it maintained in "sleep mode" and starts to build up again -it taps into the gate network by taking control of a gate, corrupting it and gaining some control over hyperspace-starts taking over/corrupting connected gates (the more gates it has and corrupts the stronger its ability to control hyperspace becomes)-proceeds to abduct crews of ships unfortunate enough to travel through gates it controls to build up it's forces-the T-Mat's goal is to shut down/destroy the gate network and end spacefaring civilization of the galaxy for good this time by all means neccesary and weaponizes hyperspace (would also explain the antagonists insane control and abilities with hyperspace since it being an ancient AI which was created to do just that)-(maybe the AI becomes more insane and erratic the more it expands its control of hyperspace/the network)-Karan S'Jet in command of the Khar-Sajuuk gets sent out to investigate-Homeworld 3's story starts 20 years later with Imogen and Isaac and the Khar-Kushan-story unfolds similarly with the player finding out the above slowly after mission 4-meet other factions of the galaxy (a Bentusi trade ship would have been nice giving insight about what is going on. Maybe help evacuate a planet of the Taiidan Republic, etc. something along those lines); (Maybe have the Keepers battle the Incarnate alongside us since T'Mat/AI being their ancient enemy in a mission or two)-no blabla cutscenes with the incarnate queen but manipulative, tormenting flashes sent by the T-Mat -similarly to HW1 actual conversation with antagonist happens very late in the game, before that the player must piece together clues and does not know what really is going on-during last mission reveal the name of the AI (don't even have to change the queen's name) which then explains why everyone called that faction "T-Mat"-AI gets destroyed or shut down/put to rest in the end with help of Karan S'jet and the progenitor cores (maybe more like ending the AI's tormented existence, like an act of mercy)-Incarnate no longer under AI mind control-Gate Network gets repaired/reconfigured how it should be by Karan S'Jet taking the AI's place in ancient Progentior control HUB => the true Age of S'Jet beginsI'm no writer by any means. _childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying any criticism you've heard about this game is wrong. The game is in fact even worse than you have heard. I knew things would be bad when I heard they had a "roguelike" mode for Homeworld. TLDR: Do not buy this game.Allow me to list just a handful of the many, many, many problems with this broken and unfinished game: If you skip a cutscene then the "focus" command is immediately bugged and will focus instead on the relative position of ships during that cutscene rather than where they actually are.Skipping cutscenes (which you will want to do, because they are awful) will regularly soft lock your game. As missions begin and end (and have multiple cutscenes in between, again, you would not believe how much they are trying to force the so called story down your throat) with these cutscenes, you will regularly find yourself having to replay missions. I began saving constantly because otherwise there was no way to avoid this. However, save game functionality is only functional sometimes. Sometimes you just cannot save the game, and the "save game" button just does nothing when you click it. Other times you will click save game, and nothing will happen, and when you go to load games to check, there are no new save files, but then you check back later and the save file IS there. Totally inconsistent. Pretty sure we had "save your game" technology down in the 1980s but these guys can't make it work. Captured enemy vessels seem to be bugged to not fire, or if they do it is very infrequent. So you can capture them and they will take up population but don't actually shoot their weapons, making them useless. So that entire game mechanic is just pointless essentially. The camera itself is really janky, although admittedly you can customize it to a decent extent, but I never found a "comfortable" setting. The original release in 1999 had a better setup. If fighters/attack craft are not in Sphere formation, then half the time they will not be firing. There is no reason to ever use any other formation. As an example, 10 recon units in a sphere can easily take out a capital ship just because they are that much more efficient in a sphere formation. There really is no reason to ever do anything else. Annoyingly, there is no way to "lock" formation, and you will regularly come back to find that your fighters/attack craft now have a "?" "mixed" formation, even though you didn't change anything, so you will be constantly forcing them back into a sphere because anything else is just woefully inefficient by comparison. Also sometimes units will just select a random formation which is worse than the default one. You will genuinely spend much of your time trying to force your fighters back into the right formation, and it is so annoying. Something I could not believe was happening until I went and triple checked was that resource collectors will (admittedly not always but sometimes), usually after saving/loading the game, stop collecting resources. You have to go back and tell them to harvest resources or they will sit there just doing nothing. Also, resource collectors have an automatic "harvest" button. However, you can put them right next to a resource, click it, and they will sometimes just not harvest the resource until you manually tell them to.Pathfinding is (somehow) totally broken in a game where most things are literally just empty space. However the second you encounter "terrain", good luck. You have to manually control your ships to have any chance of getting them to do what you want. It's absolutely pathetic. Again, Homeworld 1 did not have this problem in 1999. To add to this they had the genius idea to force your ships to go through "tunnels". How cool and quirky! Shame it does not work at all. Half your ships will just fly for miles around the tunnel instead. When some missions require you to do this, that means you will be manually piloting individual ships for frustration-inducing amounts of time just to overcome the totally broken pathfinding through brute force. This also means (get ready for this) some vessels will get STUCK. Which means you will send some ships to a location, come back to find some missing, and then zoom out to realise they got stuck on a piece of terrain ages ago and are on the other side of the map still. Utterly bewildering how they thought this was ready to release. The worst culprit is resource collectors trying to put stuff inside the mothership. They will occasionally get stuck on it and, because they lack even the most basic pathfinding, will just fly directly into the mothership non stop for hours until you force them to drop what they're carrying, MOVE THE MOTHERSHIP, and let them try again. In one mission you are told to "hide" the mothership in a nebula, so enemies can't find it. When enemies show up, they make a bee line straight for the mothership. They know its there. So that game mechanic just... doesn't work?You regularly have to use Resource Collectors to capture enemy ships or objects. However, the resource collector deploys drones to do this, while it itself stays behind. That means if you capture an enemy ship on the other side of the map, the drones will take it all the way back to the mothership while the resource collector stays where it was... miles away. If it dies, the drones die, and the ship is now free. If you MOVE the resource collector WHILE the drones are capturing something, the drones will RELEASE IT IMMEDIATELY and it will be free. How did you guys manage to mess up a mechanic which has worked perfectly since the first game in 1999? This is awful. In order to successfully capture something, you will have to send more than one resource collector. Enemies will just destroy them too quickly so you have to overwhelm them, and their pathfinding is so bad they will "Overshoot" targets. However this means you won't know which resource collector is doing the capturing, because there is no way to tell. So you have to leave all of your resource collectors bunched together in the middle of nowhere while capturing something because if you order the wrong one to move, the prisoner gets released. Let me know if you can see why that might be a problem. Deselecting/selecting units is extremely janky. I regularly had to pause the game just to fight the game to select the units I actually wanted to select, which totally kills the pacing. Perhaps for this reason, and pathfinding reasons, this game commits the ultimate cardinal sin of having a dedicated 1-A button. Ctrl + Capslock will auto select all military units, because they knew deep down people would eventually just resort to using a death ball. It's so sad to see them program this into the game itself. It's just such an obvious sign of "we give up". You will find yourself using the "Guard" command often. Not for tactical reasons, but because it means you have to fight with the controls a lot less. Using the Guard command you can send fighters/etc to guard a friendly unit, moving to it directly and staying with it when it moves. Oddly, this command does not work like previous titles and let you guard other objects, which would have made it much more useful. However, another issue with this is that pathfinding seems bugged for guard units. You will usually use fighters/corvettes to guard slower vessels. However, despite fighters being "faster", they will lag behind further and further as friendly slower ships move, until your big heavy ship has somehow left its escorts miles behind trying to catch up despite being 3x faster than it. Build queue's now have two build timers. One for the overall "order" and one for the next ship to complete. For some reason, the "overall" timer takes up 90% of the UI space, and there is a tiny bar at the bottom for individual ships. There is no obvious sign of which is which at a glance, so if you are in a hurry you will mistake how soon that next ship is coming.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start this way:I am one of the few enthusiasts, that waited over 21 years for this game with lots of love for HomeWorld 1, Cataclysm and ofc the diamond in the sky: HomeWorld 2 ().And it hurts in my soul to write this bad review, just after less than 8h gameplay and a recommendation: Dont buy it. And theres a couple of reasons.But first, lets start with the short, but good things:GOOD- The graphics and damage-models are beautiful.- The choice between hybrit, classic and modern controls are good- Music and animations of the cutscenes are very nice (I talk from a technical point of view, NOT content)- The overview and UI help alot to keep control of the environment, like in all good rts gamesNEUTRAL- There is alot of things happening during the gameplay and because of the negative things below, it happens alot to completly get desoriented.- It sometimes feels more like Star Wars battles than Battlestar Galactica (from a feeling point of view, that can be good, can be bad, depends what you expect from the game).THE BAD (oh boy...)- Gameplay and Balance is an absolute MESS. Rock-Paper-Scissor principle is just a marketing gag. Its simply not existant in this game- All situations lead to mass-production and unit-spam to win-  (example RV per Unit: StarCraft / example RA: Supreme Commander) was never reviewed by any developer. There is no way in hell, if a proper QA-test had been done, that this obvious flaw did make it into the final game. This is the main reason, why the game-balance is simply not there and why the core gameplay feels hollow. To put it simply: there is no strategy in this "Strategy-game".This however can be fixed by a patch, but the developer knows exactly, if he does this, he has to rewrite the entire Campaign-scripts, otherwise and because of obvious reasons, the CPU WILL crush you into oblivion on every difficulty.- The campaign lengh is a joke. 7h is simply admitting, that the campaign is only there because there needed to be one.- Where is the map hyperdrivejump?- Why are the maps so small? ( )- Unit pathfinding ()- SubSystems attacking? Where? What happend?THE REAL BAD- The story. And lets be clear: To compare the story of HomeWorld 3 between 1 and 2 would not be fair, since you would compare a Van Gogh with a 5 years old kids drawing of a car and the kid only gets compliments from its over protective mother, while the rest of the class is laughing at the drawing.- That my sound harsh, but: That story has nowhere near the depth of HW 1 and 2. While 1 and 2 had a very clear focus ON THE ENTIRE RACE of the Kushans, 3 makes a skyfall all the way down to a single character. And even that character has no personal development during the entire story, she doesnt need help from others, she knows everything, she can do everything ... in movies you call that the "Mary Sue principle". You can compare Imogen to Rey from Star Wars (and ofc this is one of the many reasons, why these films failed). HW 1 and 2 did make you feel, that you realy fought for your survival and loosing a single ship did realy hurt you.- And dont let me get on the villain...but lets say just this: . Or take the Beast from Cataclysm: now THAT was a fear-worthy opponent.- - Lots of plotholes (too many of them. One example: - Summary: Just realy realy bad writing and somewhat lack of imagination. Whoever wrote that story needs to be fired. Plain and simple from a company-perspective.After the HW3 campaign and some games vs the CPU I switched back to HomeWorld 2 for proper comparrison: It felt like a huuuuuuge upgrade to the new HW3. And its is still, after 21 years, so much enjoyable, so much depth and refined gameplay, that I simply cant imagine, what happend during the development of HomeWorld 3.
