_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I think the amount of negative reviews is quite misleading.I played Homeworld 1 and 2 and honestly theres some changes to subsystem targetting and some other smaller changes but I don't think its so different from 1 or 2. Homeworld 3 was NEVER going to live up to Homeworld 1 or even 2 because those games are classics and were genre defining. Homeworld 3 didn't do anything revolutionary but what can they do when the fans want Homeworld 1 and 2 again. Theres not much to revolutionize. I don't think the story is trash. It's not the best story but it was still interesting at times and the missions were fun. They were put together well and all were pretty memorable. Not to mention the world and atmosphere of each level was stunning. The graphics of this game are amazing and I found myself taking a ton of screenshots. I haven't noticed any bugs or issues really apart from one thats pretty big but solvable. Support frigate pathing feels terrible. They'll get stuck on things from time to time and just wont repair ships in the vicinity until you move them yourself. Thats a specific pathing issue ive noticed however one overall pathing issue is when youre ships are grouped together in formations they sometimes just move weird. I guess to stay in formation the ships at the back wait for the front ships to move and sometimes it makes it where the back ships take several seconds before moving. This is especially noticeable in missions where things explode and you have to get out of the explosion radius.  I don't have an issue with it being $60 since that's just the normal price for games and I feel that its worth it. Not to mention day one mod support is nice and I can't wait to see some epic mods come out like Halo, Star Wars, or maybe a WH40K mod would be awesome to see. Paid DLC is kind of a bummer but as long as they aren't like $20 just for a new faction or artifacts then I don't have a huge issue with it. I'm sure if DLC and microtransactions are too expensive the community will complain the devs will probably change it.  Overall, if you haven't played Homeworld in awhile or you're new to series I would say you'll like it. I don't know whats wrong with the old heads but they all seem to hate it. Comparison is the thief of joy and even then its not comparisons ruining the reviews its the nostalgia everyone has for the first two Homeworlds. Well I hate to break it to you guys but no game will live up to nostalgia. I enjoyed it and its probably 7.5/10 at the state its in.

_childDocuments_.review: Terrible story... like real bad. Could have been forgivable if the gameplay or level design was fun, but no. Homeworld 3 is not deserving of the Homeworld name. I played the originals back in 1999-2001 when I was in elementary school. Played the remastered when those came out. I've probably played through a dozen times. Do not buy this game, just go play the originals and pretend like this one never existed.In HW1 and 2, the ships and the fleet were the characters. This was a pro not a con. HW3's characters are whinny and sound utterly incompetent. In HW 1 and 2, the voice overs were calm and professional fitting for the leaders of a massive interstellar fleet. There was something very impactful of the calm but urgent announcement of an incoming hyperspace signature detected when you knew your fleet wasn't ready to engage. In HW3, Imogen and Intel freak out and are screaming like their hair is on fire at every turn.  Imogen cries over every fighter lost, and what the hell is with the "Sands and Sinners" thing. It seems so forced. Stop trying to make fetch happen.....One of the most memorable artistic aspects of HW1 and 2 are those glorious 2D moving art shots. They effectively gave a great sense of atmosphere and scale. I think that style was implemented very effectively  Deserts of Kharak, with a roto scope liveaction footage. HW3? None of that, not even close. Zero stylistic relation to any of prior entries of the series.  Instead we just get bad CG shots of Imogen with her eyes closed making weird faces for most of the cut scenes. All cut scenes felt like a weird low budget Starcraft 1 knockoff with respect to artistic style (Starcraft's style is good for Starcraft... not Homeworld)Every level felt claustrophobic, none of the vast epic levels of the old games. I don't think I ever even really needed to use the sensor manager screen. I could never use the aggressive stance because everything was so close that my units would immediately see and go chasing the primary enemy targets. The terrain was interesting but mostly just got in the way.  Unit control felt broken, units just flat out wouldn't engage or move at times. Units refusing to follow orders, never moving correctly. Felt super sluggish. So many things wrong with this game... really left a bad taste in my mouth.  I think I'm going to hang my hat up on the HW series. I'll remember the originals fondly. Any new entry is going have to do a lot to convince me to come back.

When you do have to move the Mothership (or really any ship) it's very awkward to do so because it's so difficult to get the camera to do what you want it to do. In the previous games, the story really shines with a "less is more" approach. The bits and pieces the games would give you were really impactful and effective. HW3 tries to enrich the lore of the universe and introduce more details about the characters, however this actually does the game a disservice. "Intel" and Imogen are bland and predicable characters. In the other Homeworld games, the characters you'd actually see would be literal cutscenes of cool drawings/art, whereas HW3 uses somewhat flimsy animation to try and give the characters more life. _childDocuments_.review: Can't recommend due to bugs, poor story, and mundane mission design. Hoping at least the bugs can be fixed but I can't see anything fixing the campaign. Bugs (Campaign and War Games)1. Ships are either missing weapons or won't fire them      Example: anti-fighter frigate will only fire in one direction which means they spend most of their time spinning around trying to track fighters2. Formations don't seem to work     Example: In HW1 you would want to select a balanced group of ships (anti-fighter, anti-frigate, around a capital ship) and then choose a formation so they would move together. That doesn't work in HW3, ships will blob together and maneuver off on their own instead of sticking together.     Also, strike craft will lose their formation after docking. So your bomber group set up in X or Claw will revert back to delta after docking.3. Stances are poorly set up     Example: Aggressive stance is the only stance where your ships will move and react to enemies before they're damaged. But they'll also chase all over the map. Neutral stance ships won't fire until fired upon and won't move or chase. So for interceptors you can either try to micromanage them as they continually try to chase down ships on the other side of the map or they'll sit still and get hit by any weapon. Neutral stance should have ships react to enemies within range and maneuver but instead of chasing they'll return to formation, this is how it worked in previous Homeworld games. 4. Pathfinding breaks    The big new addition to HW3 are the giant structures (megaliths) on the map which could be used for cover and hiding. But units have trouble maneuvering around structures and can get hung up on them and slowly have to get unstuck. And the megaliths are on almost every map.5. Resource Gathering (probably not a bug)In HW2 all resources on the map were gathered automatically at the end of a mission. This saves the player a lot of time compared to HW1 where you had to manually harvest resources and then finish the mission which took a lot of time. In HW3, missions finish automatically and no resources are automatically gathered so you get the worst of both games.StoryThe story is also pretty poorly done. It's very derivative of existing sci-fi stories and games with plot points that feel directly lifted from other stories. The animation of characters is oddly overdone, probably because having a character with their eyes closed who doesn't open their mouth limits expression to lots of furrowed eyebrows and wincing. At one point a realistically rendered character emotes like they're from a Pixar or Disney movie while trying to be menacing.It's especially disappointing because the opening half hour is actually pretty good with interplay between various crew and high command. There are stakes introduced and I thought that the complaints about story were overblown.But then you're cut off from communicating with high command (for no explained reason) and dialogue narrows down to almost entirely to exposition between Fleet Command and the villain.  The voice actors do manage to do a good job with what they're given, they just don't have much to work with. It almost feels like they were able to finish three missions to a high level of quality and then were unable to devote any time to the rest of the campaign.Mission DesignThere aren't a lot of missions but most are a variation of 'capture a point, move mothership forward'. There's one mission which is basically a stealth mission where you have to move the mothership from shadow to shadow. And some 'defend until the timer counts down'. These could be fun if the writing supported them but by the last half of the campaign dialogue is basically 'You need to capture this point' and 'We're under attack, hold out'.

_childDocuments_.review: Personally I think the gameplay is quite solid, the visuals are stunning, and the controls are about as good as could be asked for in a 3D RTS, but I can already tell that this game, at least in it's current state, is not worth a full $60. I should note that I have not played the other games in the series, so I can't quite compare it directly with it's predecessors like many other people have, but even without unfavorable comparisons to it's prior installments, I mainly just find the game lacking content-wise for a full $60 game.With only 2 factions that play marginally different from each other, (one of which you can only play in skirmish) limited unit roster, (which is made even more limited by certain ships only being allowed in certain gamemodes) and only 6 skirmish maps, (all of which are fairly tiny and most of which are limited to 1v1's) there is very little longevity to be had here. Even the units themselves are fairly basic, with few tricks up their sleeves or clever ways to use them. Cover and such is a thing they can take advantage of, but almost all of their (singular) abilities more or less devolve into "Temporarily gains x at the cost of y," with x and y being some combination of speed, damage, durability, or some other generic stat. There is really no ability that can turn an engagement around with a single well-timed proc, instead it's more just sacrificing one part of your fleet to gain more in another part, for what usually amounts to a near-even trade, making you wonder why you even really bothered using it.Outside of that, combat basically devolves into having a fleet composition that either is just better than, or at least counters, your opponent's fleet, or else you lose. From what I can tell flanking and clever positioning don't really have a super big impact on battles, and formations can actually be a hindrance more than a benefit in some cases. Accounting for hardpoint placement on enemy ships is about the biggest technical challenge you will face when it comes to fighting, where angle of attack and flanking *may* come into some account. Though considering the wide range of coverage on most ships, and their ability to simply turn and face you with little issue, it's of limited use at best. From what I can tell there is no damage bonus for hitting the sides or back of a ship, for example, or any important modules that can be destroyed.Resource gathering... exists, but it's about as simple as you can get. On the plus side, you don't need to spend a whole lot of time micro-ing your non-combat units to make sure they are being productive, but on the other hand, it does mean that there is really no deeper mechanics to speak of other than the already shallow combat.The campaign by all accounts is fun, but only the first time around, and is also pretty short at only ~9 hours, and the cinematics and dialogue are bad. Quite a shame considering that a solid, replayable campaign would pretty much be the only reason to dive in this early IMO.War games is a "love it or hate it" kind of thing, and in any case requires a co-op partner to get the most out of it. I assume most people will find it a novel idea that is impaired significantly by basically being a more limited skirmish with a gimmick.All told you could easily see all of what this game has to offer in less than 30 hours, (probably more like 20 if you know what you are doing) after which the only real appeal would be doing PvP skirmish, if that's your thing. I hope they add more factions, ships, maps, another campaign, or at least lower the price a bit, because as it stands now I don't really foresee anyone but the most die-hard fans of being able to sit down and enjoy this game for more than a week or two, at most.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original Homeworld in primary school and at the time and it quickly became legendary for it's aesthetic and story; but before I heard all the praise my first impression was that the black and white slideshow was a little bit cheap. From the point of view of most people in fact, the series was too difficult to get into and was even panned by some publications for being gimmicky. They wondered what the point of space battles in 3D really was, as the camera and positioning controls were hard to get a hang of, and inherently 3D didn't seem to offer any game play benefits to offset the loss of interesting terrain and land/air/sea units that 2D RTS games had.Fast forward to 2024, Homeworld 3 is a beautiful, cinematic new take on the franchise that makes it easier to get into, more digestible, and there is some strategy in there too, but they did their best to make the game not overwhelming and introduce a more accessible mechanic. I think that's a great thing, because if more people got into Homeworld we wouldn't have to wait decades between instalments. As it stands, I think they did a remarkable job of blending old and new visual elements with old and new characters and stories. For those that just have to have a clone of the 'classic' game... well, the originals were remastered, so just play the remasters again, and let this game be itself!In summary: I played through the campaign in 8 hours and very much enjoyed all of it, didn't have any problems adapting to the game and I think the developers did a wonderful job bringing this game to the masses and breathing some new life into it. I am looking forward to new missions in the future.

As such I unlike many other reviews will simply say:IF you fancy playing an RTS game, or a space sci fi opera game, this is a game worth playing when compared to releases in those genres which are thin on the ground recently.IT is not a patch on the first 3 games in the series, and even is outshone by Deserts of Kharak,  but before we all forget Deserts came out in 2016. 8 years ago. Conclusion:Could have, should have been so much better, but if you want to play a new game in this genre don't let negative reviews put you off.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is what I was hopeful for, but it was apparently guided by what I can only assume as an off handed comment to make the ships and characters more impactful, which ended up being mixed up during the restructure and layoffs to a degree that it became the singular guiding through line.Characters were always an embodiment of something, not the petty dramas of people written to be children with power over the folding of space resulting in the deaths of billions.Karan was the hope of Kharak, we and them were this shared curiousity, something greater than ourselves.Imogen is a "genius" wonder baby, daughter of the space president mentored by lady Karan herself and yet can't put 2-2 together to read a room.It led to a problem that undermined the effects of giving a ♥♥♥♥ about ship losses, I was actively put off by the quaver in Imogens voice any time I heard the fatal announcement of a ships loss, because it further emphasised a young unsteeled individual wielding the top of the line resources of a great peoples, the respect and lives under them and at no point deserved them.I don't like losing ships because of imaginery space peoples pilot them, Imogen actively burned away that care into an eye roll.I don't want a journey of a young woman discovering herself, Life is strange is right there for that.I was rather hoping for a story that challenged the perceived birthright of Hiigara, the unfortunate position they were thrust into in HW1-2 and the near destruction of the galaxy at the hands of the beast through Hiigaran political scheming now laid bare before the other factions of the universe demanding them to answer the question of whether the survival and return of Hiigara was morally right?If there is a follow up, I hope it comes with the determination that the past is the past, but the Unbound were arguably responsible for the catastrophic destabilisation of the galaxy at every turn, they should not be trusted and the only righteous freedom is to leave them to their pompous madness dressed as wisdom.The only burden that remains is on whoever owns this IP to try salvage it before the money runs out again, I hope so.I doubt it.

_childDocuments_.review: 1) The story is so boring... The characters are dead, and it's too short. I felt nothing for the main hero. I used to play the prior 3 games and then rewatch all missions and cutscenes on YouTube dozens of times, just to revisit the stories. Whoever wrote this game definitely rushed it or didn't care at all.2) The cutscenes are so bland. It's a huge improvement from Homeworld 2, but for me, it's more interesting to watch ships move than the characters in this game. The graphics for a cinematic cutscene in 2024 are not the best. Character design is also disappointing. I've seen the same levels of cinematic in Starcraft 2, and that was a while ago.3) They removed module targeting, which I think is a big mistake. Why take anything out of a legendary game? You know that people already love the existing product - add new stuff, improve on the existing game.4) The ability to stay in the mission after the victory to make sure you collect everything has been removed... Like this is the weirdest decision from the devs so far. You can't take time to collect all the remaining resources and rebuild the fleet. Instead of using this to hide secret points of interest in the mission or even hidden side missions - the game just goes "NOPE. YOU'RE DONE HERE, BYE!"1) Graphics are really good. It's really atmospheric!2) The new approach to level design is amazing too! But I do feel that the campaign could use at least a couple of missions in empty, open space. I don't write bad reviews for games on Steam a lot. If I don't like a game - I either refund it and move on or just keep it in my library. But Homeworld is my favorite game, and it's a shame that the game has been delivered in the state that it is right now. I don't have a good feeling about a potential 4th installment after seeing what Homeworld 3 is... and this scares me because it would be a shame to lose this franchise, its amazing lore, and world.Can you fix this? Most likely! Will they fix it? I don't know. Currently, it doesn't look good. Feels like Gearbox didn't do much to generate buzz around this project, and the current numbers are not pretty. Will these devs care enough to continue working on it? It's not in Early Access...

_childDocuments_.review: ** will update and adjust as I play more **Findings after campaign completion:Short version: Campaign feels a little short (even in hard mode) - I was expecting a bit more to do, but felt like an abrupt end.Not sure what to make of the ending of the story - villain was not particularly villainous. Story lacks a bit of gravitas. Lore kinda got scuffed and the story really really lets this game down.Definitely missed a trick by not including the summary before the game starts as a part of the campaign info. It really helps to settle into the universe. Should really rethink that move considering state of story.Game balance: Medium is way too easy - (a sign of the times perhaps?). I restarted campaign after a few missions because medium was a walkover. Hard mode feels good for vets and older HW players.Gameplay is fun, but simplified. Some mechanics like salvaging are a little fiddly - not being able to box scrap. Scrap being unselectable at times for reasons unknown. (Bug?)Not terrible. Just feels like while upgrading some features were missing. The torpedo frigates are cool - an expansion of campaign would be welcome for reasonable price considering the upfront cost of the game.I would get it, but wait for sale. Its not a terrible game - just feels like they skimped on a few key areas while upgrading the engine, its a real shame they butchered the lore and the story - I don't think the way was lots of multiplayer DLC/skins and doing weird story campaigns.Namely story, fleet lineup and game balance could do with improvement. It feels like the decision was made to cut a bunch of content/mechanics/ships due to time to publish - for the most part, it is well polished engine wise.Occasionally units wont follow orders, and the priority selection of some boxing modes such as harvesting / repair don't quite work/respond.New camera isn't bad, takes some getting used to - I prefer it but I do miss the hotkeys without having to use a modifier.Yet to try other modes - hopefully they are worth it. But we come for the story, that was 50/50 so hoping the rest lives up to it.If I was a teacher - solid start, could do much better. Wait for sale.Initial findings:An expansion on the original HW1 forumla. I miss the subsystem targeting at times - but this doesn't take away from the gameplay at all. Hence it feels like a re-imagining HW1.I would recommend if you like epic space battles (just add hard mode).I'm mixed on the new cutscene style - but I like progress and experimentation. But perhaps thats looking at them through nostalgia vision - but overall not impressed with the story. Feels watered down and non-impactful. It doesnt make sense. Its a shame as the game works well considering scale and objects in space.Definitely wants me to keep playing it for now - just not for the story, some slight changes of mechanics. Battles are great, love the space terrain, it really adds a great dynamic from the open void when required. Story has really dampened my love for this game.Story is definitely a continuation but not in a good way. Its smooth, well optimised.I would say though, play it on hard mode, because for a veteran medium difficulty is super easy so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to Homeworld, Homeworld: Cataclysm, and Homeworld 2, this game feels like a joke. While the graphics are good and the controls are more modern, the campaign is poorly designed. The missions seem like an afterthought, with content that lacks depth. The strategy in all missions boils down to building as many ships as possible.The variety of available ships is limited compared to Homeworld 2, and some, like the battlecruisers, are practically useless. Although the graphics are decent, the cutscenes suffer from poor quality, weak storytelling, and inadequate setup. The strategic elements of the game are virtually nonexistent, which is disappointing.Overall, Homeworld 2 Remastered is a far better game in every aspect. Given these shortcomings, this game is not recommendable at its current price.

_childDocuments_.review: A sad day for the Homeworld franchise. Let's start with the single player. Now Homeworld never really had that much of a story, it was more of a broad setting but it was sold really well by the Narrator. Now here we have a more personal CGI cuscenes that take too long and don't contain anything noteworthy, we have a weak villain and an ending that that makes me wish i never started the campaign. On top of that it's around 6 hours long with 1 hour of that probably being the cutscenes. The only good thing about it are the mission themselves, little as they were.So with the weak single player I at least have hope for the War Games or Skirmish. Well abandon all hope ye who enter here. War Games is just 3 missions played back to back with the same 5 or 6 maps every time and the last map seems to be the same EVERY time. Artefacts are just passives and usually you will focus on at best 2 types to strenghten the specific units you have access to. Finally Skirmish, here you will feel the last stab, the kidney shot. You will play a few games and you will release it - the strategy is gone. All you are doing is sending a never ending flow of units down a lane like a moba and someone eventually runs out of resources. The reason for this is simple there are no hard counters or any game changing abilities. Even hyperscape jump is gone. Apart from this the game suffers from some very basic problems, mostly related to AI. For instance the game is focused on monolith type maps with geography and cover, yet units are completely incapable of using it. A few examples:During the campaing you are constantly reminded about cover where you have exposed areas covered by turrets and safe areas bypassing them in cover. Guess what happens when you order a squad to move on one side of cover - half of them are there the other half decides to get shredded by turrets.Or when you order units to go at a lower or higher elevation and part of the unit formation starts to get stuck on the walls while they descend/ascend.Then you have units that simply do whatever they want - fighters flying back and forth 3-4 times before they remember they were in combat and supposed to fire at someone.Capital ships that simply refuse to move close to enemies or even fire at them. Or my favorite - the torpedo frigates that seem to religiously need to be at exactly the right range and if their target moves too close they simply turn around and start to run and you can't tell them to just fire another volley and finish the target.Then you have the barely functional multiplayer browser that takes ages to refresh and at best 10 available games to join as it seems the game is either already dead or something doesn't work right and you don't see too many games.The only thing the game has going for it are the graphics and soundtrack. The game is not worth it at the asking price, especially if you look at the remastered versions of the older games.
_childDocuments_.name: Homeworld 3

_childDocuments_.review: HW1 and HW2 vet, played them both on release. I dig Homeworld bigly. I backed this on Fig (remember that place? I don't) as soon as I saw it was being made. Also played DoK but it wasn't my jam. This game largely feels like DoK but somehow more of a let down because I had expectations.So good stuff first;The game looks good and if you mish-mash the control between OG and new style then you get pretty good and easy control of things - though a number of orders are hidden in an alt-menu the game doesn't really tell you about.Soundscape, similarly good. Lots of battle chatter though perhaps it's a little too 'clean'. Just not quite enough fuzz for my tastes.It's live service. Looks like it's going to be supported for a long time.Wargames are pretty neat.Now the rub. (in no particular order but most egregious is last)So it's a live service games. This means it *always* needs a net connection. No net, no game. Boo.Unit cap seems low. Given this, while a pretty game, is not going to be breaking any records for visuals it seems odd to have such a low unit cap. That said I found it a little finicky to workout how to sensibly control my units. Happy to accept that might just be me. Pathfinding just sucks. Oh lord pathfinding is awful. Which is curious given space is mostly empty (though they manage to fill it bloody well).No squadrons. Yup, they binned them in favour of single strike craft and corvettes. Gods only know why. So you have these enormous strike craft, which move really quite slowly and have essentially point blank weapons bumping into each other. No more wide swooping arcs...just bumpage. It's like Eve-Online all over again. And corvettes? Hope you didn't like have a choice because there is exactly 1 type of corvette and you'll replace it possibly faster than you do your interceptors and bombers as it just sits there and gets mangled by anything that can hit a barn at 10 paces. Strike craft are universally weak -which is to be expected- but not being in squadrons means that when you have your 35 interceptors and 25 bombers and near similar number of frigates...the scale is a bit out there especially as they seem to take disproportionate casualties. Just leave then on a massive queue on your mothership and carriers so you never need to think about replacing them.Ion Cannon frigates seem to be point-blank knife fighters now rather than artillery. Torpedo frigates are the future and just super good. Assault frigates make very pretty battlefields but I'm not 100% convinced of their efficacy other than eating enemy fire. Support frigates are critical for fleet maintenance and look like strike craft should be able to dock on them but don't. Minelayer frigates which, as expected, outside of the purpose built mission for them where you get given five, they are utterly hopelessly useless. Honestly, a mine which detonates after x minutes is useless unless you can guarantee enemy traffic. Oy. Suppression Frigates...I built these because it seemed like a good idea at the time. No idea if they were worth the RU's.Destroyers and Battcruisers are slower than the Mothership (which is surprisingly fast!) but seem to have about as much firepower as an interceptor. These things are just bigger assault frigates but without the fireworks.Turrets are handy and useful except, despite them being deployable, you don't carry them between missions for some insane reason. Which makes it difficult to justify their use outside three times in the campaign. Why spend RU's on something that can't come with you over spending on a fleet you can.Oh and don't expect *any* time to gather resources, rebuild your fleet or simply reorganise yourself after a mission. As soon as you complete that final objective you are whisked away. Total pain in the ass and there is no sensible reason for it mechanically and little excuse plot wise.All units have special abilities..which I guess is ok if you like micro but most seem pretty useless. That said I used cloak on the bombers a lot (though it was a 50/50 whether it actually worked or not) and the range boost on the torp frigates. Most everything else was pretty useless, fiddly, or I simply forgot it was there. Why can't a ship just be a ship. Why does everything need toggle powers or cooldowns or whatever.Maps are very small and very compressed by 'terrain' in the form of floating hunks of someone elses space station. Every fight is a totally disorderly knife fight where ranged combat is for loosers and organization can go hang. There is a single strategy - throw as much metal as the enemy as possible as fast as possible. Pretensions to alternative strategy are false; outside of the most rudimentary tacticts, there is little to do.Cutscenes. Endless middlingly rendered cutscenes. No more awesome (mostly) static pictures like in HW1 and HW2 and even DoK. They just get rammed in between missions (and elsewhere) and just eat time with badly written dialogue, visuals which...are just not up to scratch really alas and also don't really provide much. Oh and during cutscenes in missions, everything keeps going on in the background so if you are desperately trying to micro your ships to save something...yeah they're gonna die.Oh boy oh boy the plot. It's hot garbage, genuinely awful. I think it's fair to say that HW1 and HW2 while having characters you were pretty distant from them - Karan S'Jet (AKA Fleet Command), Fleet Intelligence, the Bentusi etc. You never really see any of these people (entities?) and you were taken in by the scale of the situation rather than individual quibbles. Well throw out all that good space opera stuff because now we're getting stuck in the dome of a lassie who things giving your troops a rousing speech is lying to them. Imogen S'Jet is just..whiny and uninteresting. Karan was comfortably detached which I suspect would be the result of plugging your brain into a poorly understood extra-dimensional jet engine which can also make you functionally immortal and give you all sorts of other weird powers. Also, who the hell are the incarnate, other than a poor mans Vagyr? There's little sense or purpose or scale other than 'this crazy lady wants my engines' and Fleet Intelligence and Imogen bickering. What is the anomaly? Why is it a big thing? Why is it so poorly explained? I was sure paying attention but...urgh. By being so 'zoomed in' to the characters it definitely doesn't feel like a homeworld story. In HW1 and HW2 I didn't have any interest in Karan S'Jet beyond the mothership because she *was* the mothership. I actively saw her story, her travels, her struggles through the pitting on her hull and the works of her production bays. By contrast I have no desire to know and am indeed repelled by Imogen S'Jet. She appears to be utterly unchanged by the astonishing power of the mothership and her responsibilities. Maybe its her synthetic cores she made, maybe they are just as bland and uninteresting as she is.The campaign was short, you were constantly rushed but it never seemed sensible as to why, it's pretty and sounds good but it ain't homeworld. At best it's 'meh' but I'm quite a fan of the grand space opera scale of HW1 and HW2 and this is just a very *very* poor rehash of HW2 but with none of the grandeur.EDIT:As a late addition, they love taking control away from you. Some missions it feels you are barely in control of the game as you get control taken from you by Fleet Intelligence repeatedly -sometimes mere seconds apart- just to tell you something you already know. He also loves bugging the hell out of you every two minutes for objectives you are fighting hard to obtain.The game is also frankly a rip off and had I not jumped in years ago on Fig for it I wouldn't pay £50 for it now and certainly wouldn't pay £73(!!!!)

_childDocuments_.review: Like some others really wanted to like this game and almost waited literal decades for it to happen. Homeworld has been a classic from my childhood and an all time favorite series of mine. Even Cataclysm for what it was, was at least fun. There are just so many things wrong with HW3 though, that it's almost impossible to list. The pros aren't just overwhelmed by the negatives, it's straight defiled, burned, buried, dug up, and beaten to death again before being tossed in a ditch to rot. Here goes.-Pros- (what few there are)Graphic fidelity - Ships are more detailed than they need to be but, it makes focusing on a craft during an engagement great. The weapons and engine trails are the classic high visibility HW style that are fun to watch.Sound effects and music - This is like listening to HW1 and 2 all over again. The space chatter, ambient music and sound effects are still just as cool as 1 and 2. My only gripe and not something big enough for this not to be a pro is that fleet command tells you that every ship that blows up is yours, enemy or otherwise. Just kill a destroyer and "Fleet Command: Friendly destroyer lost."........ sure fleet command, sure.Ambient visuals - The background visuals are great. God rays coming though a nebula, gas clouds and debris, and the giant remains of ancient ships are all just as great as the originals.And on to the cons........MILD SPOILER ALERT FOR THOSE IT CONCERNS-Cons- (literally everything else but I'll name the most egregious)THE STORY - The story writing and dialogue is just bad. All around bad. Villian being a villian just to be a villain because being bad makes people get gud? Really?! THAT'S THE FREAKING VILLAINS PURPOSE?! Everything else about the previous homeworld games are abandoned and burned. None or barely any mention of the other ancient races, factions, allies from the past, THE PROGENITORS. NOTHING! Now its all about a know it all perfect goody goody fleet command and an uppity intel commander and the worst Sunday morning cartoon villain imaginable. What little there is makes literally no sense and has nothing to do with all the setup from 1 and 2. In the end they killed the story and any connection it had to the previous games. The story of Homeworld without a full reboot is effectively DEAD. The only other path is to do to HW3 what was done with Cataclysm and do it over again.Unit pathing and AI - This game is one of the WORST for pathing and AI. Seriously it almost makes the final mission impossible because your mother ship just wants to Tokyo drift around the map completely ignoring your commands. Your biggest opponent in the game is the unit pathing. Ships all cluster together all the time, ignore your commands, don't avoid incoming fire regardless of formation or behavior settings and just randomly drift around the map at their own will. Never thought I'd say this but ion frigates can OBLITERATE fighter formations. The only way to keep ships in one spot is to force the sphere formation and tell them to go guard something. Every other setting and formation is functionally useless 90% of the time.Maps and combat - This game is no longer an epic space strategy game. It's a poorly planned skirmish game where the faster you spam the big stuff the faster you win. Once frigates are spammable you can just never make another fighter again..... yes, I'm being serious and worst of all you just spam two specific frigates and......PROFIT! Maps are now really, really small. Roughly half a dozen probes and the entire map is revealed to you so fog of war is pointless too on maps this tiny. There's no travel time to be had and your mothership can travel the entire map in about a minute because the only thing faster than your mothership are fighter craft. What? You thought this game made sense?!Cutscense, characters, and animations - This game looks like they tried to make a Disney cartoon in cut scenes. No I'm not joking. They should have stuck with 2D animated slides. Not because they were better but, it gave the game a unique and deep story like feel, like you're listening to a historical document, and the original narration of the original 2 was just leagues ahead of the team that made......this. Also the characters are always way too expressive and emotional. Seriously, cartoon levels of emotional and expressive. It was honestly cringe worthy to have to watch some these cut scenes. The character designs themselves also for the style of animation they went with just look meh. All the 2D artwork they made and showed off for this game makes the 3D designs that we got look like child's play. In the end the skills for whoever worked on this part of the game aren't trash, they just don't belong here. This game was not their calling.Wargames - Ah wargames. Where to start. Rogue like? partially. Intuitive, fun, and engaging? Nope, none of the above. The game mode doesn't have intuitive objectives or goals. Just spam whatever the strongest thing you can spam is until the game throws literally 2 dozen destroyers or even a single battle cruiser at you when the only thing you can build is frigates and fighters..... yep..... fun and engaging. The objectives are capture based and if even a single enemy rolls in on your whole little entourage then the capture stops and did I mention hordes of destroyers before? yeah the make those objectives almost impossible to achieve. The best is the battle cruiser objective. Kill the enemy battle cruiser you say? You're sending heavy reinforcements to help you say? Maybe some bombers, a group of ion frigates, or destroyer(S), yes multiples? PERCHANSE?! ALL I GET IS A SINGLE FREAKING DESTROYER SPAWNED ALL THE WAY ACROSS THE MAP THAT WON'T ARRIVE IN TIME YOU SAY?! Best part is a battle cruisers can run down your carrier and once it starts its game over. You can't distract it, it won't stop, and it will win. Some of the fleet load outs can kill it but, unless you have a heavy anti capital focused fleet you're screwed, period.DLC - They're trying to sell you on the broke a** wargames they can't shut up about. All they're doing is adding new factions and maps. Hope they plan on putting what little resources they'll have left into improving pathing, AI, and enemy unit spawns cause oh boi is this gonna die in a fire something quick. That's it, rant over. There's way more to say but I just can't. Not worth it and I don't think Gearbox or the Devs give a crap about what happens to the HW series now.  I'm gonna try and test a few more things in wargames but I will NEVER play the campaign again, ever. Go play Helldivers 2 or V Rising. They're new games and leagues more fun than this and don't cost nearly as much. Oh and if you want a true scifi rogue like slap stick never ending fun game go play Risk of Rain 1 or 2 or Everspace.

_childDocuments_.review: I had to sit and mull over my opinion on this game. I so wanted it to be good. It was beautiful, and while the Hiigaran ship designs aren't the best or most diverse in the series, I still liked them. The music was great, and the sound design was great. I followed many of the updates on forums, whenever they released info about the game. I eventually even caved and pre-ordered. I wasn't even mad when that order was screwed up and I missed the 72 Hours pre-release forcing me to wait a week and dodge spoilers until I could finally play it. Ok, I was a little mad, but still excited!I mean, I've loved Homeworld since I was a kid and I got the first game for Christmas after begging my parents for over a year to get it, and at the time we didn't even have a computer that could run it, so I just read and re-read the Historical and Technical briefing over and over. I never got to play Cataclysm when it came out, but I played Homeworld 2 and DoK and loved them both. The Hiigaran Battlecruiser from HW2 - now that's great ship design! Heck, I loved the Remaster for all its initial faults. All this is to say, I loved this series.But....this...wasn't Homeworld. The gameplay was just...build up to unit cap, set queues to keep rebuilding, spam F4, and direct the death ball at objectives. Research wasn't research, it was just...something else to spend RUs on, and maybe a slight delay on a linear path up. And that story.... I know everyone's talked about how the shift from a epic space opera about a fleet/people to what is effectively a character coming-of-age story was jarring, how the main villain was annoying and inconsistent, heck, how most of the characters were annoying and inconsistent, or how the cutscenes just looked...wrong, but what gets me is how empty and unsatisfied I was after beating it. Like, there were great set pieces, some of the environments were gorgeous (and as annoying as terrain was, following ships flying through a tunnel was really cool), there were homages to the original games with some of the mission types, and some missions had unique mechanics (namely the bombing-run one). It should have been good, but the story was so bad and such a distraction I couldn't enjoy it. Like, why was the Mothership launched in an incomplete state? Why was a vital component of the ship stored in the middle of nowhere without protection? Why were pirates randomly there and still a threat?!? We're told planets are destroyed, but we never see it first hand, it's so distant and meaningless you don't really care - which when paired with a B-plot where an unlikable character tries to rescue Karan S'Jet by jumping to random conclusions and getting stupid-lucky coincidences (a plot which should have been strong motivation, but....wasn't because of the contrivances) make it unenjoyable. I was playing it not because it was fun or engaging, but to beat missions and to check off boxes. OH, and that ending - what the hell was that?!?! I just...couldn't process what I had seen during the campaign.I literally sat and thought it over for an hour after beating it, thinking about how empty it left me feeling. Then I jumped into a few Skirmish games (of which most the Remastered settings are gone and there are only 6 maps?!?) to see if maybe that would be better, to find out it was more of the same. Less options, still no capital hyperspace, and all the same problems as the campaign. I mean, I still need to try wargames at time of writing, but I am not really into that...plus, it just feels like it was made for micro-transactions down the line.I just... I can't recommend this game. Like, for RTS fans, this feel like when Supreme Commander 2 came out after Forged Alliance - but so much worse, because you can still see the bones of that good, beautiful game underneath...buried in the mediocrity. Maybe they will fix it in time, but right now, I don't recommend this. Also, one last piece of frustration, the Soundtrack is missing the new version of Adagio for Strings/Tears of Karan - literally, the best song used in one of the best moments. It's just...come on.

_childDocuments_.review: As a stalwart 25+ year HW fan, yes, I would recommend this game just because it's Homeworld and I love the franchise. I'd also urge other fans to seek out the parts they enjoy. The Homeworld feel that we all know and love is there. The soundtrack and battle chatter do the usual wonders. Contrary to some other opinions I do feel the story is mostly robust, though the villains are a little cardboard-cut. Don't like the CGI cutscenes as much as the static art-style from the previous games, but hey, that's subjective. The overall feel and design of the megaliths, asteroid fields and ships are just simply outstanding. However, the gameplay is a far cry from what the old games achieved which itself seems an achievement given the potential of HW3 and what they were trying to achieve. I have been playing (and will continue to play) the game with it's new fancy camera, as it was meant to be played, but do find this approach rather jarring. The classic controls feel a lot easier to use for me (unsurprisingly as I am used to them), but I also think they would be easier for new players. So far I don't see how the new camera would provide an advantage in navigating the megaliths, as they are sufficiently compact that I keep clipping into them anyway and need to make much more use of the tactical pause while i reorient myself like a boomer. Maybe this will change in multiplayer. The AI is lackluster. Does not seem to take advantage of the breathtaking megaliths. In Neutral or Passive stances the units find the most non-logical place to hug the wall and sometimes this works totally against you. Whether this is a 'bug' or just a lack of intelligent AI manoeuvring, I dunno... Similar gripes across the board for how units behave. Overall positive, but with some pretty big setbacks for such a long development time. The art, sound and level design is incredible, and deserves only the best praise and reception. The gameplay is mediocre at best, which is a huge shame.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving it a thumbs up because of a promise I made to my 14-year-old self after playing Homeworld 2; however, this is not a positive review.Where do I even begin with Homeworld, a series that has defined my gaming life since 1999? No game with this emotional pedigree can live up to expectations—not a single one. But this one manages to do something spectacular: it messes up every single element that made Homeworld great. I'll start with the least offensive bits.First of all, the graphics. At first glance, they're a feast for the eyes: beautiful backgrounds and settings, beautiful effects. But then you zoom in on a ship and realize the textures up close are worse than Homeworld 2. The original. From 2003."Okay, but the ships themselves look fine, right? Right?" Padme asked anxiously while Anakin smiled maliciously. No, they don't. Apart from the Interceptor, Carrier, and Khar-Kushan, the design is sterile, and there's little variation. Unit variety is laughable. The ships lack any semblance of scale, a staple of the Homeworld series. Everything is small, and the blurry textures don't help. The Incarnate look like someone ran the Vaygr and Progenitor ships through Midjourney and called it a day.And all of that would be forgiven if the gameplay were any good. Here, I take a small pause and look at the media scores—80 to 100. What are those guys smoking? Because I want some of that if it makes me like this barely controllable mess. Either that, or the birthdates on the reviewers' ID cards read well after September 28, 1999.The battles are chaotic, and not in a good way. You feel barely in control. The unit AI is so brain-dead that you have to micromanage. The fleet size required to progress makes it a chore, and in other words, much worse than the 25-year-old Homeworld. At one point, I gave up, selected all units, pressed F4, and tossed them into the fray. This worked in Homeworld 2 and made for some of the best visual battles seen to this day. Not the case here. The units start bumping into one another like Top Gear presenters on a special. They maneuver idiotically, and it looks ugly as hell. The pathfinding is idiotic. None of the beautiful maneuvering by the interceptors to avoid capital ships while engaging other strike craft dodging between the flak fire glory of Homeworld 2; just utter ugly chaos.The terrain is cool at first sight, overused at second, and horrendously executed at third. Every single mission had it. There isn't one cool open space battle. Everything feels flat and on one plane. This is impressive, considering Deserts of Kharak always felt like a Homeworld game; this one doesn't.And now the crown jewel in this cake of excrement: the story! Oh my God, the story. Please, guys, just come out and say you ran this through ChatGPT. Please save some face. I cannot believe human beings signed off on this and thought it was okay. So here's a quick recap. Imogen S'jet creates synthetic hyperspace cores by reverse engineering the Progenitor core (so basically what the Kushan did 220 years ago before you retconned it, right?). She's looking to find Karan, who still has the original three cores. Cool, I can work with that. Who will try to stop us? The Vaygrgenitors and their bad mama. Where did she come from? Not explained. What did she want other than Sunday cartoon villain "I'm bad"? Not explained. What happened to the actual ship Sajuuk? Not explained. The story direction is also atrocious. There's no stake, nothing happens to make it matter. In Homeworld 1, you see your planet burning. In Homeworld 2, wherever you go, the Vaygr burn everything in your wake, and Makaan declares his ultimatum in the second mission. There are high stakes. Even in Deserts of Kharak, there was more cohesion. What do we have here? We show you a cutscene video that depicts Starkiller Base dunking on the peaceful galactic population, and you're supposed to feel angry and motivated. It doesn't work like that. The only bit I actually liked was when one inconsequential pirate captain said, "Where Hiigarans go, death follows," which could have been an amazing introspective story beat given the history of the Hiigaran and Kushan people, but alas, that goes absolutely nowhere immediately following said captain's violent disassembly.The Historic and Technical Manual is also miles apart from previous Homeworld titles. In the almost 300 pages of lore for Homeworld, Homeworld: Cataclysm/Emergence, and Homeworld 2, the word "human" is used zero times. In Homeworld 3's Technical Manual, which is 80 pages but could have easily fit into 10, the word "human" is used three times. It's almost as if you guys don't know or care about your own lore.Wait, what is that I feel? I remember now—oh God, a repressed memory is awakened. The nightmare fuel that are the "artistic" CGIs. Computer-generated imagery so bad it wouldn't have been passable at the release of Homeworld 2, let alone 21 years later. Dear lord. The facial animations are from the 90s; motion capture hasn't been invented yet. The horrors I saw and experienced. I have no mouth, and I must scream. Comparing the opening of Homeworld 2 to the opening of Homeworld 3 is like comparing Villeneuve's Dune to Battlefield Earth (if you remember that Scientological masterpiece). Bloody hell, who needed this? Who saw it and thought it was okay? Damned be the traditions of 2D black-and-white minimal animation; this is just NOT okay by itself. Why did you feel the need to put a face and expression (however badly animated) to the story of Homeworld? Your crowning achievement was making players cry staring at a planet and a ship in a scene containing fewer polygons than a single of HW3's interceptors. Why did you think you needed more? You didn't, we didn't, nobody did.But alas, at least we can put Homeworld to its grave. Seeing the reviews, sales figures, and what's happening with the owner of the IP, I'm confident there won't be another one. And maybe that's a good thing. Seriously, if you are a Homeworld fan, whether new or one of the original ones, don't do this to yourself. Let the game you love live without this stain in your mind. You are better off for it. Keep away so you don't have to experience the things that make you write this.Yeah, I gave it a thumbs up, but that was a promise to myself that if I lived to see Homeworld 3, it would be my favorite game ever. It isn't, and I'm not that kid, and Homeworld isn't Homeworld. No one's left... Everything's gone... Homeworld is burning...

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR at the bottom.A new homeworld, after all this time. i couldn't have pre-ordered fast enough. even after what gearbox did to 2 remastered. i just want any and all homeworld content. do I regret paying full price? no. should i have paid full price? no. Campaign has none of the emotional investment, the world building, the sorrow and righteous vengence that usually accompanies kushan and hiigaran tales. it is short and borrows heavily from 1 and 2s mission designs, almost clones in some examples. the game is beautiful, the weapon effects and ballistic trajectories are beautiful. the motherships moving while tracking point defense guns...beautiful. the ship design, again. beautiful. unbalanced as hell as usual for a gearbox HW piece. the unit size scaling also seems really really off. fighters are essentially worthless except for high alpha damage for the first pass and then a lazy non evasive strafing run after strafing run. count on keeping fighter production ques maxed out in perpetuity.no more subsystems, no more short jump hyperspace, no more cloak/gravity generators. they just picked and chose some features from all the games and mashed them all together. multiplayer map count and design is ABYSMAL. 6 maps to start, all knife fight in a closet type maps. where the only objective is to out produce the other and when the resources run out whoever has the most resources in the bank wins.too much focus is put into the war-games/co-op mode. don't get me wrong, i love the co-op option out side of team skirmishes but it looks like all the updates coming will be solely focused on that. is it a homeworld game? yes, is it underwhelming? yes. do i have probably 7000 hours in all the homeworld games including pre-steam? yes. should you wait until its on sale? yes. will modders save this game? absolutely.TL;DR: wait till its on sale and modders save the game. also please donate to modders that make good content. they literally keep some games alive.Update: Big mods abandoned. The scaffold has been destroyed. All orbital facilities destroyed. Significant debris ring in low Kharak orbit. Receiving no communication from anywhere in the system... not even beacons.There's nothing left for us here. lets go.

LET THE SHIPS TAKE ADVANTAGE OF THIS FACT!-units are too expensive for how little resources are on each map-the terrain gets in the camera's way half of the time, making it quite difficult to maneuver if you're a Homeworld veteran.-easily the shortest campaign in the series-the background interaction between Imogen and the villain is completely unnecessary-the cutscenes are fully animated videos, which is NOT a Homeworld trait-the villain is animated and written like it's from mid-2010s Disney (some of her body language is also completely incorrect for what she's trying to convey-the Incarnate ship design is nothing but "hey, you know the Sajuuk ship from 2, right? _childDocuments_.review: EDIT: My review has changed now that ive completed the storyNote - This review will still update over time as it is patched.Pros - - That classic Homeworld Gameplay - frantic and frenetic. Feels very much like previous games though not without its issues (see cons)- Beautiful in game visuals- Great voice cast- Option to mix and match controls if you prefer how it handled in previous games- Surprisingly, for a modern game, very few bugs on releaseCons - -There isn't much else to like about it in its current state- The new camera controls where it acts like a free-cam and goes where you point in any direction isn't for me. Thankfully you can switch it to the old style where it locks to the plain and you can control height with controls- Cutscene FMVs have weirdly poor visuals in places. some feel like they are from 20+ years ago and can be jarring. in particular, so far at least Imogens scenes seem to be the worst offenders. They should never of strayed from the classic monochromatic storyboards the previous games were well known for- Ship variety seems low compared to previous games. Roles are clumped together. So for example Destroyers and Battleships are the be all and end all. Previously that was never the case and they still needed smaller escorts to support them. There is literally 1 corvette class. Upgrades feel ineffectual and ship scale feels wonky. - The story is poor, the antagonist is weak, you never feel any sense of being threatened. it feels like the first draft of a much bigger story that was never developed fully.- Story maps all feel smallI had really hoped things improved as i played but if anything they got worse so i can no longer recommend this game as is.I haven't messed with the skirmish mode much but given the lack of ships i dont think i will enjoy it as much as HW2. _childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed Homeworld 3.  If you are a fan of classic hard sci-fi, the story explores some interesting themes of transcendance (do transcendant beings get lonely?  What do they do if nobody else transcends with them?).  There are a couple big logical leaps that I feel could have been set up more, but I forgave it.I also enjoyed the tactical gameplay.  Unit balancing is a bit off and leaves openings for players to optimize the fun out of the game (such as just building a big ball of torpedo frigates, or capturing 9001 destroyers).  If you hold yourself back from those fun-destroying pitfalls, you'll be fine until a balance patch comes out.The game is VERY well polished in terms of bugs.  This is no buggy nightmare like so many other recent releases.  Really, just a few unit behaviour and balance issues that need a light pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, this is the first time I'm ever going to NOT recommend a Homeworld title to new people. There are far too many horrible decisions made with this game that completely backpedal on the amazing mechanics, atmosphere, and universe of HW.Cons:-The gameplay is boiled hot dog water compared to prior titles. There is no unique feeling to each individual class of vessel, nor is there any nuance for strategy. Honestly this is reflected perfectly with how the Skirmish AI acts. There is only one strategy: SPAM and SWARM. You have no choice in the matter, if you decide to focus heavily into strikecraft, frigates, capitals, doesn't matter. Only numbers matter. Extremely linear progression in technology, fleet formations and compositions have zero impact on the outcome, all that matters is how big is your number compared to the enemy? Disappointing.-Story is... wow. Not gonna touch that campaign button again. Horrid. Awful. I won't even explain myself fully on how efficiently the story detracts from the universe of Homeworld. An entirely worthless plot that devolves into the 'predetermined destiny' of a chosen few. Sound familiar? The main protagonist is an emotional child, and somehow the main antagonist is the exact same way, but worse and also intolerably nihilistic and prone to outbursts of rage because she didn't get her way.  Karan S'jet? How to slaughter a previously beloved established character 101. Horrible campaign, one of the worst plot-lines I've seen in a while, and I've watched the entire Star Wars Sequel trilogy.Pros:-Soundtrack and Sound design are phenomenal! Nailed that one, 10/10 Sounds like Homeworld. -Visuals are also fantastic, love the effects and explosions. The Hiigaran ship designs are amazing, always have been a sucker for angular hulls with lethal edges. Incarnate look good too, however I wish they would've gone a bit more wild on their designs. They just look kinda like the Vaygr 2.0. Their Mothership class however, looks excellent. 10/10 Visual design.-Overall? Shiny game with all the bells and whistles. Looks and sounds pretty, however it's hollow. Horribly hollow. Look just under the newly painted battleplate and what do you see? An empty cavern. 3/10, and those 3 points are just because it looks and sounds good. Everything else is awful, go back to the drawing board and make something actually substantial.

_childDocuments_.review: Many games out there easily qualify for the $60 purchase, and then achieve a huge amount of value even beyond that. I think this is a case of just barely being worth $60, and only to fans of the Homeworld series or the RTS genre of games. However this opinion could easily being changed given the live-service model this game has adopted.@BBI Fix bugs, optimize performance, and make unit abilities/selection/docking more intuitive. Once that's done, it would be easy to recommend this game to .This is especially frustrating when micro-managing strike craft. Imagine you have a carrier with a control group of 15 interceptors. The enemy attacks with 10 interceptors of their own. The most efficient way to deal with them is to continually dock damaged interceptors with the carrier so that you don't lose any. After the damaged interceptors are re-launched from the carrier, they need to be reissued the attack order (unless they are on aggressive stance and the enemies are near enough) which is unintuitive; they should do whatever the control group is doing. Let's say you have 5 interceptors going in docking with the carrier and 10 more enemy interceptors show up. You issue an attack command with your control group, and now those 5 interceptors decide to go back out into combat, resulting in their deaths. I think the only thing that should cancel a dock command is the stop command. This would also solve the stop-and-go movement that craft experience whenever you send repeated dock commands.

_childDocuments_.review: Where to start?......EDIT 7/20/24: Cautiously changed my view from Not Recommended to Recommended, but i would Wait Until HW3 Goes On Sale, and to edit for more clarity.I have been a Homeworld fan since the first classic game was introduced in 1999. I was very active in the HW modding community. I used to be called The Stress Puppy back then. I Contributed to the Sacrifice of Angels mod for HW1. I am still a Modeler, and Texture artist for the Star Trek: Chronicles mod for HWRM.Classic Homeworld was awe inspiring. A story based on discovering that your people are exiles from your original home planet, and the fight against all odds to reclaim your Homeworld from the Taiidan Empire. Homeworld also was the first game to introduce 3D RTS Mechanics, and physics based projectiles. Each unit had function, and purpose. To this day Homeworld: Classic is still considered to be the best in the series.Homeworld: Cataclysm (Now Emergence) was just as inspiring. Basically becoming a Hero from Zero story about Kith Somtaaw, and the Kith's heroic stand against a plague that threatens the entire galaxy that they themselves accidentally unleashed. Game play basically added on to what was already good about Classic Homeworld. I consider this game equal to HW1Homeworld 2. While 2nd in series IMO game play, and story wise. It is still pretty compelling, and retcon delved into the origin of the three Projenitor Hyperspace cores, and the fight between Higaraa, and the Vaygr to control them. Then the opening of the Projenitor Hyperspace gate network. Game Play replaced the physics based projectile system with random die role hit/miss system, and subsystems were added, but overall still played similar to Classic Homeworld.Deserts of Kharak. Basically the origin story of the Kushan. We already know what is going to happen to them. DOK just tells us how it happened. The Game itself is not bad. Homeworld 2D RTS. Not much else to say about DOK.Now after 20+ years of waiting we finally get Homeworld 3.I will start with the Good first.The Artwork, The Ship Models, The Environment are as good as it gets. I salute the art department. You captured the look, and feel of Homeworld as it should. Since BBI was founded by the former artist from Relic that created Classic Homeworld.The Game Play (in the SP Campaign) while a bit wonky it is still satisfying. There are some path finding, and units abandoning orders issues that future patches should be able to iron out, but overall it plays like a Homeworld game.The Soundtrack is spot on.Now for the BAD:While HW3 was advertised as bringing back what made Homeworld great. Not very much of it was delivered. HW3 uses the random die role hit/miss system when it was said that the physics based system would return. I now know it is a mix of both Physics, and RNG. The main issues are as said above. Units Abandon Orders, and at times just Freeze In Place. This is a leftover path finding issue from HW: Remastered. Which tells me the same, or similar code was used. Units most of the time wont fire until they are on the same level/plane as enemy units. As if the game is set in 2D. Units get stuck trying to figure out what to shoot at. HWRM had the very same issues, and they were eventually fixed (Through a mod). The same could be done with HW3.The units themselves are not near as fleshed out as in previous HW games. The Incarnate have far better unit variety, and purpose than the Higaraans do. Higaraan Destroyers, and Battlecruisers serve pretty much the same purpose, and once Battlecruisers are fielded you don't need Destroyers any more. Frigates are only two types. Short, and Long range. The Anti Fighter Suppression Frigate does not target Fighters, or Corvettes. Goes after other frigates instead. Despite being ordered otherwise. Destroyers and Battlecruisers just do their own thing. Despite orders. Fighters/Bombers have a bad habit of freezing, and forgetting orders. Especially guard orders.The Mothership is the fastest unit in game....The Environment, and Maps. While the maps look awesome they contribute to the unit path finding issues, and at times units get "stuck on terrain" clipped into a wall. Overall play area is about 1/3rd the map size. So the sense of scale is still just an illusion. I get what BBI wanted to do with the environments. Huge megaliths that can be used, and exploited, It is the execution that is problematic.SP Campaign is Way Too Short. All but a few missions strategy is spam units.No Collisions, or Kamakazi like in HW1/2, No Hyperspace on skirmish maps. Only 6 skirmish maps. Skirmish, and War Games plays just like Starcraft. Basically hurry up, harvest, and build what you can, Zerg rush it, and hope for the best. No strategy. No thought. Just spam units, and button mash ability's until you run out of resources, or die... Whichever comes first.The Story:Seriously Gearbox?!! You took creative control away from BBI, and gave us THIS?! The STORY is really what made all of the previous Homeworld games so GREAT. The STORY is what made us all come back for MORE, but HW3's story Makes An Absolute Mockery Of All Of The Previous HW Titles. While the story started off good enough. It went on a downward spiral from there. The Higaraans want to end their reliance on Projenitor Tech that they still do not understand. I can understand that. Yet they still rely on that same Progenitor Tech to repair the Motherships synthetic cores. We didn't learn anything new about the Projenitors. There is no empathy for the Higaraans, because there is no real threat to them, or sense of impending doom in the HW3 SP Campaign, because most of the story's important plot points are forgotten about right after seeing them just one time. Leaving Plot Holes so Big that an Entire Planet can fit through them. The story really needed A Lot More Exposition to understand what is going on. Like how were the hyperspace portals used as a weapon? We only saw this once, and no explanation was given as to how, or why it happened. How do the Incarnate hyperspace with no long jump hyperspace cores? No explanation. How ships can materialize inside solid objects? I even had a flashback of Rise of Skywalker's "They can fly now?!". "They shouldn't be able to do that!" Then second to last mission YOU DO JUST THAT... No Explanation Given. Where the hell is SAJUUK? (not the Khar-Sajuuk). The story is told from the point of view of 4 individuals. Not as a race in general fighting for its survival. Using CGI rendered cut scene's that are borderline "Pixar-ish". HW3 would have been better served with the old school Story Board/Narration animations of HW1, and HW2, or even DoK style cut scene's. The Villain is a laughable over the top monolog spilling villain. Who's motivations, and methods were unclear. Basically she did everything she did, "Because she can". Then all of her atrocity's were forgotten about. The protagonists seem to have forgotten all about what they were fighting for by the end game. I don't care what race, ethnicity, or gender the characters are. This is just a VERY BADLY written and/or edited story. The story is indeed the worst part of HW3. It is as if written by people that have never played any of the previous HW games, or even looked up the lore. We have nods to the previous games, and that is about it for continuity. Well we now have an answer... Gearbox.As for the game itself. It is good if you can ignore the story. The game art itself is top notch. There is hope for HW3. Many of the current path finding, and freeze issues are indeed Fixable. Units can be re-balanced. More units can be added. More "open" maps can be added.The game looks like it can be a very good platform for mods. I really hope BBI keeps its word, and fixes the issues, and continues to update the game. If not i will write HW3 off as non-canon. Just like Relic did with HW:Cat. We will always have HW1, Cat, and HW2

_childDocuments_.review: I wrote a long ass review, but steam didn't submit it for some dumb reason... so here's a highly condensed version. Campaign: 8/10 - Decent campaign that most will be satisfied with. Some missions are really cool. Gameplay: 8/10 - Good foundation, but I hope they make adjustments and other elements. Sounds: 8/10 - Pretty good. Atmosphere: 10/10 Fantastic. Graphics: 10/10 - Fantastic. Controls: 8/10 - The basic controls are good, but some specific controls have poor key binds that are inconvenient and silly. Multiplayer: 6/10 - Skirmish maps are way too small, and fighting starts within 1 minute and never ends. Very poorly implemented. Performance 7/10 - I run on the recommended settings for my hardware, but the game lags at 20-30 FPS when in large fights. Acceptable performance, but could be better. Overall: 8/10 - A decent game that I think most will like. May have very limited replayability, because multiplayer doesn't seem to currently be implemented well, but I think it can reasonably be fixed. Overall, I would recommend this to someone who like space or RTS games.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd be trending more towards neutral than good, but there's still no option for that. This all pertains to the single player campaign, I haven't played the war games mode (maybe later) or multiplayer (probably never) modes.Let's start with the good:- The in game art direction is stellar. Both the ships as well as the surroundings look like Homeworld... which is all you could as for.- Soundtrack is great. Same guy, same great music.- Sound design is spot on. Everything from the environmental / ambient, to the guns and other ship sounds, the the battle chatter... absolutely no complaints.- Most missions are fun. The fights in and around mega structures is a somewhat fresh spin. I would've liked so see a bit more open space though.- The campaign length is comparable to HW1/2/Cataclysm (screw you Blizzard!)/DoK... no, taking an hour to mine every last asteroid in HW1 shouldn't count towards the completion time, just like staring at the main menu doesn't. .P- Mod support will hopefully deliver more content over the coming years/months and fix some of the streamlining issues.Then the eh... really?- Adagio for Strings is missing from the soundtrack. Why? How?- Concept art style and in engine cut-scenes > whatever they've tried here. What a waste of budget and render cycles. Some of the in engine stuff is once again a please to look at btw.- There's a bit too much oversimplification in the game play mechanics. No subsystem targeting, no harvester management, and even the unit experience from DoK didn't make it over as well. It feels like a over-correction to please the attention deficit crowd.And the bad:- Why can't I stay in mission and salvage materials / rebuild my fleet when a mission is done? I get it when you're under pressure / fleeing, but otherwise there's no reason to just warp off asap.- The story is forgettable, nothing new, and terribly presented. "Sands and Sinners"? Once would've been fine... but hearing it every third cinematic really dials up the cringe. Doesn't matter if it's the same writer as for HW1 - getting the same person sadly isn't a guarantee for quality. Just remember George and the prequel trilogy? If it was a book, I'd ban it off my shelve to make space for something better. And no, I'm not expecting or hoping for Banks, Le Guin, or [fill in your favorite SciFi author] level writing but I've read fan fiction better and more original than this.Overall this absolutely isn't what it could've been and/or players of the originals hoped for, but it isn't the affront to gaming and worst game ever (until they find the next title to complain about) some people make it out to be. But nuance is dead... so that's that. tl;dr: 6.5-7.5/10, unless you need to play it right now maybe wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The good:Campaign is "good." The mission chatter and cutscenes are solid, space vistas are beautiful, and the soundtrack hits on all the right notes.The bad:Everything else.Only 1 type of fighter, bomber, corvette, and destroyer. The observant may notice that that means the only unit type with variety is the frigate class. Coincidentally, anything smaller than a frigate is nearly irrelevant. Corvettes evaporate under any kind of fire, strikecraft can't kill anything except strikecraft and other fighters, bombers get hit by anti-capital weaponry regularly, and frigates can pretty much cover their jobs.War games feels like a roguelike made by someone who has no idea what FUN is. The player is restricted to ships sized Frigate and below, and not all of them are available at all times - for example the starting fleet composition doesn't even get the Assault Frigate. This means that the player only has 7 unit types to deploy. 7. That is PATHETIC. The artifacts are 50% utter dogwater, 30% useless, and 20% interesting choices.Destroyer spam by the AI is a complete slog, with over 150k hp each they take forever to kill and the AI will regularly deathball 8 of them together. Whether they can be killed or not isn't an issue, they just take FOREVER even with dedicated anticap weapons.The destroyer issue goes further. They are effective against everything from bombers to other capital ships. One size fits all. And the player can't even build them.Haven't touched pvp, probably won't. The game's unit sandbox is fundamentally boring, unbalanced, and will not keep me coming back.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not angry Blackbird, I'm just disappointed.Now, Homeworld 3 is a... decent game. It honestly has a lot going for it. War Games is a fantastic addition, 3D stellar terrain is wonderful, but why'd you have to remove so much to get us there?The problem is that while it's a decent game, it's a bad Homeworld game. So much has been stripped out from the previous entries that it just doesn't feel like Homeworld anymore. There's no subsystems to target on enemy capital ships or protect on your own, likewise there's no building specific structures on different Carriers to gain access to different ships, each ship type only has one upgrade which gives them a MOBA-style activatable ability, the maps are TINY compared to Homeworld 1 and 2, the Shipyard is gone, I could go on and on and on.Furthermore, Homeworld has never been a micro-intensive series in terms of combat. It has always been the thinking man's RTS, where fleet compositions, 3D angles of attack, time-to-target, reconnaissance and intelligence, special subsystems such as Hyperspace Jumps or Cloaking, all of them combine together to allow a clever player to win each battle before it begins by using actual strategy and tactics.Homeworld 3 is an APM clickfest where if you're not cycling through your ships and using their activatable abilities as quickly as the other guy, you are going to lose. Strategy is dead, it's all about the tactics here, with the vaunted body-blocking (which was already in previous Homeworld titles, by the way) and 3D terrain being the second actual deciding factor in battles.Don't get me wrong, I do like this game. I'm going to keep playing it. And if it had been called anything except Homeworld 3 this review would be positively glowing.But I didn't want to like this game, I wanted to love it. I wanted it to be not just a decent game, but a great Homeworld game, and it sadly isn't. And at this point I don't think Blackbird or Gearbox can save it. They've removed too much and it would be too much work to put it back in.On top of all this, it uses Denuvo, which is a well-known datamining system that gathers and sells your personal data.And that's why, despite its upsides, this game makes me sad.
