_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is..... passable at best. The poor pathing and tracking of ships can get on your nerves at key moments. Your ships will be bumping into each-other constantly, and missing targets because of it. This is especially true of ion cannon frigates. The map design forces close quarters battles that turn into a visual mess you have to pause to navigate and command.Next is ship design. At first you think it's good, until you zoom out and see that everything just kinda gets muddled together in an indistinguishable blob when the fighting starts. This is especially true for enemy ships. There isn't much that separates them from each-other until you zoom in on them. It's like you are looking at the same ship at different sizes.The story... oh god the story. I knew it would be bad when I saw the first cutscene was cg and not the drawn style of the previous games. I am only on the ninth mission and I can easily predict how it will all play out. When the antagonist showed up as a giant and started stomping around while monologuing about her evil plan I lost all motivation to finish this. This is a poor skinsuit of a Homeworld game. Someone had their own idea of what Homeworld SHOULD be like, and this is what they spat out. Oh well. Another franchise ruined by people who care more about fulfilling their own generic vision than continuing with what made the previous games beloved.I would refund it if i could.

_childDocuments_.review: I will start this out with I am not new to the Homeworld games, I have played the Remaster and Deserts of Kharak. Going from the prior mentions to this new installment I am very much underwhelmed by it.I get this game is new but with how much time they had it cooking in the oven this doesn't feel like a well made game. I have personally experienced connection loss at several points on the main menu screen when going to start either a Wargame or a Skirmish match whether it was hosted by me or searching for either or Despite the fact I am connected to my internet via ethernet cable. I have also experienced losing connection in the middle of matches and at the very beginning of them and when going to load up a replay.Gameplay wise it still feels unfinished, as several units either do not engage until they are literally nose to nose with the target or there is a delay from actively engaging it. Now the cut-scenes, I do not care for the cut-scenes, they look poorly done and there are so many of them, not to mention how many pop up in the middle of a mission when you are trying to give orders are not ideal. _childDocuments_.review: To start I have played HW1, H2W2, HWC, HWDOK all when they originally came out and their remastered edition.THE GOOD The game itself is BEAUTIFUL. Seeing the ship’s point defense turrets slide up and down the hull to engage threats is stunning. It runs smoothly and I haven’t had any crashes. Playing maps and missions on the giant mega structures that were in the background of previous titles is nice and does give it a nice change.THE OKAY/Can be fixed with updates.Combat feels okay, formations and tactics feel like they don’t stick when you reinforce a strike group so every time, I add a ship I have to change formation and change tactics. As battles progress formations seem to dissolve. Maybe I’m doing something wrong or using the wrong formation. Combat is complex if you use it. You can place turrets on the wreckage of super structures and in counter you can fly around the structures and use them as cover. Seems good in practice but I could also fly out the middle of space and just avoid the turrets all together. I see what they were trying to do but maybe it can be improved.Only having 6 skirmish maps on launch is lame.THE BAD It pains me to say this, but the story is terrible. HW1 and HWC had really great stories HW2 felt okay. DoK was nice I guess just didn’t love it. HW3 just feels like a giant retcon. They ignore a lot of the story telling at the end of all previous titles. There is no "bring Sajuuk to bear" moment, there is no "our Homeworld is burning" moment. The story feels soulless. Having back this on Fig in 2019 and having it come out. kind of feel like a kick in the pants. The mid mission CGI looks good and bad at the same time. There is graphical blurring with people’s mouths that I can’t tell if its intentional or not and either way for it to make it into the final product feels bad. HW1/2/C had simple cinematics and they could have saved a lot of money if they would have kept doing that.The missions feel incredible short. Short missions with a short story. That took me approximately 10ish hours to beat the campaign on medium difficulty.TLDR; Game very pretty, campaign missions not enough and too short, skirmish mode lacks depth. combat is okay to good and can be improved. story telling is garbage.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm recommending this because the gameplay remains excellent. It is everything you want from Homeworld gameplay and more. War Games mode is an absolutely brilliant idea that can provide hours and hours of fun and always keep you returning for more.The thing is tho, what i loved about the Homeworld series is the Space Opera stories it had and the way it told them and this game completely fails to live up to that.Homeworld 3's story is a best a rehash of Homeworld 2's and at worst just really really lame. Certainly it's lacking the powerful emotional heart that Homeworld 1 or 2 had, it's a story that i just couldn't connect with at all on any level, and i think that's cause the core three characters involved aren't that interesting. Imogen's ok but i didn't really connect to her at all and her journey feels a bit forced. Karen's played utterly lifelessly. And the villainess comes off more as an annoying brat than the heart of a galaxy spanning threat.TL;DR - Ultimately i recommend this game for it's gameplay. Cause it's fun. Play Skirmish and War Games and you'll have a great time!BUT: If you're coming here because you want a fantastic Space Opera story like you got in Homeworld 1, Cataclysm and 2 then don't play this, cause you'll be very disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Campaign is a different style of story telling from Homeworld 1 and 2. Campaign missions themselves are fun for the most part. There are 13 Campaign missions and I completed them all in approximately 7 hours. Game does need some balance work, but I'm sure that will come within the first few weeks or months. There are some features from the previous games that are not in the game, such as sub-systems. Game is beautiful and performs as described in their performance breakdown guide. Mechanics are a bit complicated for an entry level RTS player, and even an experienced Homeworld player can still make mistakes when moving in the completely open planes of movement.Haven't tried the multiplayer, skirmish, or war games modes yet. I'm not big in multiplayer for RTS, unless I'm doing a co-op comp stomp, so I think I might enjoy the War Games mode (if they improved the balance from the demo) Overall get it if you're a fan of Homeworld or Space RTS games.
_childDocuments_.name: Homeworld 3

_childDocuments_.review: So. *Long deep breath* I'm writing this of a fan of every Homeworld game. Unfortunately not this one.Is this a Homeworld game? No. Not by a hyperspace jump.Let's start with the big part, the core soul of the game. The story.The story isn't Homeworld. It's got a Homeworld skin on it, but it isn't. In the deep, rich yet open, story they could have pulled from any of the previous titles, they decided to go with. *Checks notes* Hyperspace wizards and witches somehow have power over hyperspace jump portals. So some long living Progenitor takes control of hyperspace though.... means. Okay…how? There is no ‘how’ other than BBEG has the ‘power and technology’. Not some new lore or new expansion to the existing lore? Anything?! No reason for BBEG being the BBEG other than “I want that thing cause I’m powerful”. I seriously got more excited thinking Karen went mad, or taken over by some lost Progenitor AI or even some version of the Beast.That didn't happen, we have typical villain model #230, and a "let's pull from all the interesting missions from past games" to make missions format. The campaign has only one direction and it's so, so boring. Nothing exciting, nothing unexpected. Hell I didn't even feel like this was a huge galactic threat when all we see of the 'galactic ending' events happening is in cutscenes. Where's the Hiigarin fleet you're fighting with getting atomized by a Hyperspace beam? Where's a notable planet like maybe one of the Taidani Republic worlds getting hit with the stuff from the cutscenes? No you don't feel or see any of it in game, and it's such a huge blow to the series. There was nothing in the game that felt like it was just more than just a threat from the local pirate lord who found a nice big toy.Every Homeworld story had some sort of punch to it.I wish I could find anything good about this story, but I can't. Shallow characters, the cutscenes. Ugh they sucked. The simplicity of the previous game's cutscenes had such a charm. There's so many plot holes "That's not possible to jump through solid objects" Literally have proof of it happening in the first game in the timeline! Then you do it without any clear explanation on how in the second to last mission? Come on guys.  Gameplay.It's not homeworld. You blob assault frigates in front of everything and just ram your whole fleet into theirs. There's no strategy. So many ship classes including all of the strike craft are just useless combat wise, and started being just fodder for my capture ships to get in. Stopped using them after like mission 4-5?  The 'space cover' and ruins you fly though are a very weak gimmick. That's it. It harms the game so bad it's not worth it. It limits the sizes of the maps and instead of a very wide and open you know...space? The nebula clouds in the other games did a 10x better job of effecting the map than the physical masses. You feel like your in a box with a bunch of loose cardboard floating in it.The AI pathing with the new objects in space. Oh my god they can't handle it. Just no, fly 10k above anything and hope your units don't blob on the scenery. Not to mention any fleet engagement doesn't separate out like the other games did. It's all one, uncontrollable blob of units.Edit: Forgot to mention. There's no fleet building or breathing room. Kill the last enemy and your fleet is in tatters? OH WELL next mission. There's no breathing room, no time to re-arrange your fleet for the next mission. No time to go "Oh I don't need these units anymore, time to decom them." It's gone, not a single point do you get to breath in this game and fix your fleet!Side tangent: Deserts of Kharak made our main mothership/carrier a beast. You could bring it into combat and It could be useful. A big tank to soak up damage, powerhouse with weapons to eat away the enemy, front line repair unit. You made it what you wanted using a heat system. It had such a good change in pace for the lead unit I thought for sure they'd bring those elements in to make the new mothership a powerhouse and not just a backline factory worker. Nope, wasted mechanic option that was one of highlights of a past game.The controls are such a freaking mess. We need a total rebound option. It's just near unplayable if you want to actually strategize with 3D space. But if you do that you lose any sensible control over using the new gimmicks.I have no idea how multiplayer is, cause I was so fed up with the controls I stopped playing after one round.I'm sorry guys, this isn't the Homeworld 3 we were expecting. I can't recommend this to anyone. It's clear now you rushed your dev teams, rushed your writers, and rushed yet another game. This pattern happening to our beloved franchises is really, really getting sand cursed old.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving a positive review because I see that there is quality and effort invested in this game, it has fun moments, nice visuals and there was a clear roadmap on where they were planning to go with it (war games). So the short answer, , but very limited for me. Take it as a generous positive review in hopes that the project continues and the game evolves, because it has potential and already scratches an old itch, but this review should be mixed instead.Having said this, as someone who had realistic expectations and a backstory with the franchise from Homeworld 1, 2 while also enjoying modding (complex), I must say that . This feels like testing Dawn of War 3 all over again, the game was created with War Games in mind, clearly, and the way it was implemented, the skirmishes and the campaign feel awfully out of place and annoying to play due to this (can't say for PVP as I don't play it, but it's likely hell on space there too).I hope the game improves overall. War Games are fun, I'm digging it, but right now  they are costing the soul of the franchise and I'm pretty sure they burn fast.

_childDocuments_.review: So, for me Homeworld was always about the story, the music, the visuals and the unique atmosphere. So despite the (maybe justified) gameplay critique I was quite on board with the game for 7 or so missions on Story difficulty. Visuals, art, music and even the premise were very-very endearing and engaging. I was even kinda ok with the very serious tonal shift in cutscenes and narrative in general. And with very cheap facial animations.Then the game pulled a several Mary Sue plot-points out of S'jets literal ass, forgot the entire premise and started the space-magic fluff strtaigh out of worst parts of Destiny 2 lore. So yeah, I've just raged-deleted the whole thing. Too bad I can't really refund it cuz it was a gift from a good mate.What's wrong with you, BBI? It's almost that you've lost all the style, the simple elegance and mystery and replaced minimalistic and moody Homeworld tone with some Amazon show episodes created by a bunch of nobodies. Deserts of Kharak was a terrific prequel that lined-up stylistically and narratively with 1 and 2 perfecty.Homeworld 3? It's a checklist of modern narrative sins wrapped up in a neatly looking package. Without spoilers I will say that this is, sadly, the lowest point for the series if you really love the universe, the story and the vibe.It pains me dearly to say it, but: hard pass. Play the first two, too bad they've never made a third installment.

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't write reviews often but this game I feel needs one.I really really was so excited to have another Homeworld game to play, however despite the efforts to make this a grand affair this really feels like a let down.The loss of subsystems on larger ships as a game mechanic was a huge blow in my opinion, this allowed for personalisation of your fleet, along with a vastly cut down choice of ships from HW 2 the game feels like your playing checkers when you should be playing in a chess tournament.Oh i grant you the single player campaign was very impressive visually, however this was a glaring gap in the game, it feels like there is little to no soul injected into this.13 missions and its all done, far too short and this is with me saying that i took over 2 hours on the final mission. I miss my old HW2 battle-cruisers, I miss the punch they administered when you owned one, in HW3 the capital ships feel like bricks to just absorb damage.If you haven't played yet, frigates frigates & more frigates. Assault Frigates are the absolute workhorse of the game. A maxed out population of 15 will pay for themselves 10x over against anything smaller than themselves, Support Frigates keep everyone alive in the game so protect them like they are gold. Ion Frigates, meh they are ok but as soon as you get Torpedo Frigates don't lament their loss. Torpedo Frigates are just death, pure unadulterated death to anything frigate and above.Suppression Frigates are a sub par version of the Assault Frigates, great if you need extra anti strike craft.Carriers are something i wish i had paid more attention to earlier in the game, get all 3 ASAP. the improved production ability for a short period is just too good to ignore.Fleet Bombers, these are great for a hit and run with the cloaking ability to get you to the target. However they are eaten up by everything far too quickly, don't get attached to the pilots.The StoryThis was a pale shadow of the plots from HW and HW 2, at times i was finding it very dull and uninteresting.  These games had a sweeping story on an epic scale involving worlds and vast distances, it seems like a drive to a cornershop scuffle in comparison.There was some great potential with the changes to the hyperspace mechanism the opposition used but it was shown once as a brief plot point and then basically forgotten about.In summary this feels like half a game with barely enough plot to get your teeth into before your shoved forward to gawk at the next pretty map they made.If I could pull HW 2 into this new engine and boot out the HW3 stuff i would

_childDocuments_.review: you say! Based on everyone's input you see around, but allow me a moment of your time to explain.Experience level: Played Homeworld since it came out in 1999, Homeworld 2. Was waiting for this forever.First, the good:Without giving spoilers, this version of Homeworld thrusts you immediately into peril. You are outgunned, out numbered.Your crew is green, you are not ready. As the fighting happens, you discover a means that works best for you to stay alive. Both Intel/Command paint the path forward to stave off devastation.Veterans (or perhaps just me cause I'm weird) have wanted to explore the map more. We're in a 3D environment, why can't I explore that massive wreck over there?  Not only do you get close to it, but you can fly through the debris; you can hid in the debris, you can use it as an advantage to attack. But guess what? .The universe is more alive, enemies aren't just straight...well, going straight at you. Now, you never know what direction they'll come from. You need to play cautious, else your unguarded mothership sitting next to an open port may suddenly find itself being swarmed by the enemy fleet.Intel tells you to approach a task a certain way; do you follow orders, or go it your own way? Exampe: early on there is some frigs that pose a massive threat to your mission - but you're most likely a Homeworld vet like myself. Why destroy them? Make them your own through grand theft spacecraft. Steal your way to victory!The storytelling through individual experiences, emotion, passion, certainly is a different approach that, in my opinion, a welcome change. It isn't another "hey do this thing" as it's an exploration of the individual. Makes things feel more fleshed out, more "Alive" within the universe.I can't go into details, but man. What an ending. It leaves you with a sense of closure, happiness and yet sadness.It's an emotional ride.The AI isn't as aggressive as I would hope; you can turtle your way through the map to get everything done with minimal losses. In the end that's a waste, as I had 80K+ resources but meh. I do love my Homeworld turtle.The AI I've seen get stuck behind walls and unable to move. Path finding can be horrible for your fleet balls as ships will stonewall each other from advancing. Hopefully though, they are working to fix this (We have to remain hopeful).The ships come down to simply balling together and pushing forward. Assault/Ion frigs and eventually destroyers, followed by support healers, will roll through anything coming at you.I hadn't tested out the fight/corvette combos as my playstyle took over; a ball of 35 Bombers would decimate enemy emplacements, which therein runs back to the earlier issue of AI. You can stealth bomb/retreat bombers essentially forever against capital ships as the enemy wont pursue - effectively making their death a slow, but eventual, death.

_childDocuments_.review: Night of reviews here. A couple of things that get an instant negative review:1. Day-one release with DLC. Extra content that they chose not to give you and want you to pay extra for? Why not just not make that and just give us the game early? Or just, you know... give it to us free as part of the game?2. Pay extra to get the game 3-7 days early. This game has been in development for years. The "pay more for early access" gets you an instant negative on principle. Sure, one or two days now is fine, but 10 years from now? What, only the wealthy get to play new games? No thanks.Game:I was so looking forward to this game. Loved Homeworld one, but there are some problems here:1. Pacing. What the hell, guys? Give me some time to save. There should be a semi-cutscene or pause between missions.2. On-the-fly research. What new research? Grab. What does it do? No idea, but it came up so I know I have to get it. Also, part of problem one: you need to make research a choice so people have to read it and understand what they're choosing.3. Poor campaign development. Yeah, let's be honest here. Asteroids are stupid.

_childDocuments_.review: Huge respects to the studio and developers for picking up the series and giving us a Homeworld 3. This is a passion project and it shows. While there is definitively weaknessess, it largely is a worthy successor.Is it better than Homeworld 1 and 2? Hard no from me. It is a good game regardless and I do hope that there will be improvements and some reworks down the line. If you are just looking for "more Homeworld" and have palyed both 1 and 2, then you should get it - at least on a discount. For people who are new to the series, you may want to start with the Remastered Originals first. If you are looking for a modern multiplayer RTS with active community, HW3 is also a legitimate option.Now about the features... Are the new features worth the ones that were cut? While I like many, if not most, of the additions, I do miss old features like capital ship compartments. The new features and control sets don't completely make up for things like that. The change to single snub units instead of squadrons is a return to HW1 and I like it overall. I do feel a hybrid between HW1 and HW2 squads could have been possible though and it would have appeased those who prefered it the other way. The ship compartments also did not yet exist in HW1, but were one of the great additions of HW2 and I will miss them a lot.I am a big fan of the terrain options, which shake up the gameplay quite a bit and give HW3 it's own spot of uniqueness in the series. It's certainly a nice addition - though I would have liked some more larger maps with a varied mix of open space and megastructures,There is also some technical weaknesses in combat, with pathfinding and some combat mechanics being far from what they could have been. Especially the lack of attack move options is a problem for me. Snub fights also seem inorganic and not as interesting as in the older games (although pathfinding and stupid pilot decisions were always annoying me the series). A lot of the homeworld potential was apparently cut short in favor simplicity in general. While simplicity often makes for better RTS games, some of ths cuts have taken away some quirks of Homeworld that make it more interesting, organic and athmospheric. It's not like these features were unituitive - attack moves were incredibly rewarding once mastered for example.The Story so far (I am near completion) is far less memorable than it's predecessors and the Homeworld athmosphere is a bit lackluster. The same was once said about HW2 in comparison to the first game and I take that HW3 is suffering from the sequel burdon (may it remain). Coming up with a worthy story is hard and I can see that they tried coming up with something compelling. The result is not that great, but I wouldn't say it is as bad either as some of the reviews make it out.Sound design and music are superb and even the disappointed folks agree on this. To me this is a big part of why this is a real homeworld game. It adds to the athmosphere and creates a true sense of Homeworld nostalgia and immersive space combat.The campaign animations, while not atrocious, could have been better. Most of the ones involving Imogen look clumsy and older than they are. Depictions of Intel and other characters are usually fine.I do sympathise with the disappointment of old fans of the series, the "great return"-hype has lead to high expectations, which even a "good" game couldn't match. Still, I don't think the devs have missed the mark by a long shot and I do wish great success to this release, so that it may lead to more Homeworld and the lasting continuation of the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Homeworld 3

_childDocuments_.review: So this game has been in "development" for years.The problems:The CGI cut scenes are incredibly bad and dated. Like legit feels like the scenes were rendered before the game announcement was made back in 2018Ship AI/Pathing needs improving/reworking (Harvesters, Support Frigates don't really behave as they should)The story (so far, only 7 missions in) just doesn't really make sense and is very disjointed and it is just bad story telling.This game for some odd reason makes a 4080 sweat, so there's some optimization issues going onShip selecting can be odd at timesSomehow lost my cursor a few times, so had to reload from last save/checkpoint.Some missions don't really make sense at times outside of demonstrating some kind of "feature" or ship and again just feels off "Oh here's a problem" and instantly "Here, research the ship to help with that"Compared to HW1, the pacing as well of the story is far too accelerated/feels too forcedThere's no other factions/races or interaction with the universe so to speak.The music or lack of variation, HW1 had some beautiful scores. Whereas HW3... there's Adagio for Strings and then there's Adagio for Strings and some more Adagio for String... No atmosphere, no feeling or emotion reallyThe OkThe interface is much better compared to the demo a few months backYeah... nothing really "ok" with this gameThe goodCamera control isn't too badIt is a pretty (but again, don't get why it's so intense on the GPU)Honestly for been so long, so much time, I feels the did nothing for the first 2-3 years and then started doing the development in a rush.... Not exactly expecting a new BG3 GOTY ordeal, but this game is just disappointing and is it let down.They should have dropped the nonsense CGI scenes, stuck with the simple and yet nicely drawn stills with light animations like in HW1, keep it clean, build it up gradually and build up the universe so to speak gradually. They shouldn't haven bothered wasting time, money and effort with the travesty of their mobile game.The foundations is there, but just seems cobbled together in a hurry with little care for the dialog/story/plot, same with the music, same with the universe.5/10 - as a standalone game, it is ok, nothing great and nothing terrible3/10 - as a sequel, just lacking in all areas....

_childDocuments_.review: As a veteran who got into the series by playing HW: Raider Retreat, I will leave my impression here, of the notable things I have found so far in game:Overall so far is quite a nice HW game, 7.5/10, which surprises me how a lot of people are reacting negatively to it.Honestly, feels like all over again when HW2 came out: It was overhyped, so when it finally came out, fans tore it down, between the rushed plot, the insane dynamic difficulty, the Bentusi going extinct, and the game being so demanding, that for a while, it was like a graphic benchmark for PCs of the era.Give it time, and people will warm to it. Definitely, I can attest it isn't "unfinished" nor "a wreck of a plot".

_childDocuments_.review: Having only completed the campaign so far on hard, this game is a solid 9/10.- Visually stunning. Soundtrack and sound effects are fantastic.- Control scheme & Interfaces are some of the best I've seen. - Maintains and improves upon the 'Homeworld' feel - Capital ships are incredibly satisfying to use- Time controls are a fantastic addition- Astonishingly quick load times? Criticisms (which are honestly pretty minor).The asteroid mission is pure cancer. Actually, this criticism is not minor. - Story is... Good? But odd. I'd honestly prefer if there were no cut scenes. Just do exposition & voice lines in the main game. - Campaign is a little short, but well worth it.- Strike craft & corvettes die way to quick, and there is no way any of them are staying alive in a fight. They do pack a punch though.- Player controlled ships seem to never do what they are told. Good luck keeping formations, or engaging an enemy with an actual fleet. _childDocuments_.review: The core, graphics, new terrain system and the return of ballistic physics is good.The issue lies in the fact that they oversimplified many systems. I could live with some of the changes but the biggest issue is that they made all the maps extremely small where combat starts in 2 minutes and is just a endless stream of enemy fighters.There is no depth to resource collection anymore and there is no need to really defend them.Small maps remove the whole "strategic" aspect that they wanted terrain feature to have because there is no point in creating choke points or awesome defensive position because currently the only viable strategy is to ZERG rush the opponent because you have insane amount of resources and the parallel production speed is insane.Campaign and warmode is nice but MP is complete garbage because of the changes, which means the game has no longetivity so it is not worth the money they are asking for.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all. SBI was involved. DO NOT support it.Update:They roll back the production system back to HM1&2, which you can only produce/research one item each time, changing from parallel production for each ship category. This is a absolute mistake! Here is your problem, the map size and combat scenario were very small, they were for fast and rapid conflicts. Ofc ppl won't like it if they are too familiar with previous HW games, but it was OK, just different, not bad. Now what do you have? A freak hybrid. Small map, close contact, fast and convenient income system, but with slow productions. What do you want? Fast game or slow game? Oh btw, it is really hard to find lobby now. _childDocuments_.review: Pros: Engine is smooth, no crashes, and they've got the Homeworld aesthetics nailed down.Negatives...Homeworld Cataclysm did take some liberties with how it shifted the Homeworld story in making it more horror themed. I've seen some argue whether it can be considered canon or not, but it doesn't change that its story was gripping, scary, and left one eager for more.Homeworld 3 on the other hand feels like being swept into some strange alternate version of the universe where the scifi portions are replaced with some metaphysical, badly explained, story about a trio of witches arguing with one another, one being a grandmother constantly cooing in the background, one which is a ranting loon, and a third which goes from crying about how difficult everything is to mastering hyperspace in the span of two hours.The story basically begins by breaking all set rules in the universe, weaponizing hyperspace in the process, and hurling entire planets around as if they were playthings. The main characters argue how this is impossible, can't believe their eyes, then... by mission 7 in the game, starts doing the very same impossible thing without even mentioning how or why.The ending is equally, maddeningly crazy, contains ghosts, and a lot of facial expressions which one moment seem happy in a 'i'm about to eat you' way, before suddenly becoming resentful. The missions in the game are short and hectic. Stuff like tunnels come across as worthless gimmicks and charging straight in works a lot better.You'll find yourself constantly struggling against the UI, and locating units is a constant chore. Destroyers and Battlecruisers behave as if broken. The camera tends to be wonky.I can't recommend this latest iteration of Homeworld, and this is most likely the end of the franchise as I can see no way to repair the damage to the narrative or overall storyline.Addendum: The main storyline has about 6,5 hours of content and the wargames have little appeal after going through it.TLDR: This is a modern fantasy half-broken trope story with a lot of patting yourself on the back that has been wrapped in Homeworld aestethics. Beware.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a long time fan of the series, you won't find the compelling narrative that you adored in Homeworld in this game. Without spoiling too much, it starts with the intriguing premise of the missing Karan S'jet who departed with a new mothership from Higaara to investigate why a region of the Hyper Gate network that opened all across the galaxy in Homeworld 2 has shut down. As it turns out, a new antagonist is the cause for this and it is now up to the player to stop this. Sadly, the story doesn't really reach the emotional highs and lows of the original game.The game features new ships, new environments, and new control schemes to play with. However, combat felt shallow and finicky especially during the Campaign. It's essentially a numbers game where you just keep pumping out units and moving your blob of ships against the enemy until one side prevails. Certain units have problems with pathfinding and don't even engage in combat when grouped with other ships (looking at you destroyers and battle cruisers). It feels like the game is an iterative step from Homeworld 1 but loses the changes introduced by Homeworld 2 in the form of squadrons, tactics, and ship components.Bought this at full price because I want to support the series. I sincerely hope the developers keep improving the multiplayer aspect and deliver content to make the season pass worth it.So is this worth a buy? Not yet. Let's see what the developers will do for now. If you're looking to buy this anyway, buy it at a discount during a Steam sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played the original HW1 and HW2 on release, but it's hard to believe, and deeply frustrating, that after so much love, care, and thought, this was the final product.A beautiful game without a soul:- Camera control is confusing and buggy, and some default keybindings are shared with unit actions, which prevents you from using them.- Fighting mechanics are nonsense: all units damage others equally. A few ion frigates can burn through a battlecruiser like it's nothing, and a battlecruiser can quickly kill fighters.- Unit progression is lame and uneventful; you just "get them," and most don't give any immediate benefit on their missions.- Carriers are useless; you can't even tell specific units to dock on specific carriers, which is something you could do in previous games.- Special abilities are interesting but poorly implemented; you can't, for example, select multiple targets when triggering them from a group. Either the entire group uses the ability on one target, or you must manually select individual units and targets.- Missions end abruptly, and you never have enough time to gather resources. I had to delay completing objectives to give my collectors time to gather everything properly.- Using terrain hardly gives any real advantage since units struggle to find a path around it. I rarely used terrain for anything during the campaign, and it was always frustrating when I did. It feels like a feature they really, really wanted to implement but, at the same time, is one that makes no sense since most, if not all, space battles won't ever have terrain close by.- But worst of all, the story... The Kushan should have a top-notch fleet powered by ancient tech after the events of HW2, but what we get is basically HW1 with new skin. Instead of making enemies stronger, we have the same old boring units doing the same thing as before... that was very, very disappointing. And, to top it all, we get a kids cartoon villain that shows their tantrums because they can't get what they want... I feel sad about this game because it promised so much. Still, maybe modders can rescue it from oblivion.

_childDocuments_.review: **Homeworld 3: A Disappointing Descent into Mediocrity***1/5 Stars*As a long-time fan of the *Homeworld* series, I had high hopes for *Homeworld 3*. Unfortunately, the game is plagued with issues that make it a frustrating experience, from clunky AI to a storyline that feels more like a forced social commentary than an engaging space epic. Here are the main problems:### 1. **AI on Ships is Broken**The ship AI is one of the most disappointing aspects of the game. Units simply don’t hold formations properly, often breaking away and acting independently, even after precise orders. This makes fleet coordination a nightmare, and when you're trying to execute strategic maneuvers, this AI malfunction ruins the flow of combat. In a game that revolves around commanding a fleet in space, having your ships disobey or fail to carry out orders makes the experience infuriating. ### 2. **Storyline Overloaded with DEI and Woke Themes**The storyline feels like it’s more focused on pushing diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) narratives than telling an engaging story. I get that modern games try to be inclusive, but here, it feels shoehorned and detracts from the core plot. It’s distracting and completely unnecessary, especially when you're supposed to be commanding an interstellar fleet in the heat of battle. Instead of focusing on the tactical aspects of warfare and leadership, the game constantly pulls you out of the immersion with emotionally charged dialogues that simply don't fit the tone.### 3. **Emotional Sob Stories in the Middle of Battle**This is where the game truly loses touch with its premise. As a fleet commander, you're expected to make tough decisions and deal with losses. However, *Homeworld 3* takes it to an absurd level by having key characters like Fleet Intel and Imogen break down in the middle of battle. The constant emotional outbursts and "grieving" over every casualty feel incredibly out of place. It’s as if the developers have no idea what it means to be in command, where staying composed and making hard choices is paramount. Instead, we get characters falling apart, disrupting the flow of the story and combat. ### 4. **Poorly Written Plot**The plot of *Homeworld 3* feels hastily thrown together, with poorly developed characters and a storyline that lacks the depth and complexity we’ve seen in previous entries of the series. It’s as if the writing team was more focused on inserting modern social commentaries than crafting a compelling space narrative. Honestly, I've seen better storylines written by a 12-year-old fanfic writer. The pacing is awkward, the plot twists are predictable, and the characters are either flat or unbearably emotional in situations where that should be the last thing on their mind.### Conclusion*Homeworld 3* is a massive letdown. The broken AI, misplaced emotional beats, and a storyline cluttered with unnecessary woke elements make it a frustrating experience. As a commander, you’re expected to lead with a clear head, but this game constantly drags you into forced emotional turmoil and unrealistic character reactions. The developers clearly missed the mark on what *Homeworld* fans were looking for—an engaging, tactical space strategy game with a strong narrative. Instead, we got this mess. **Avoid this game if you're a fan of the original series or if you prefer your space strategy games with competent AI and focused storytelling.**

_childDocuments_.review: Played for 33 hours at time of review.Most of that due to either reloading, sitting idle, or just staring at the wall.It pains me to add to the hate bandwagon, as much as I love Homeworld, don't buy this game.I was so excited for another entry, but with this the franchise is dead. Stick to the previous entries.I'm sure the developers tried, and I'm sure they were under a lot of pressure. But the result is disappointing.Like many of the other reviews, the voice acting wasn't bad, but the story is underwhelming.I won't go into a rant over the lore issues or that they've taken away what made homeworld great.The fate of the galaxy, now hyperspace is weaponised... But it loses that impending doom. It's just... Bad.The other reviews sum up everything wrong with the story. And touch on a lot of problems with the game. You can read those to get a better idea. Mini rant over. Ignoring the previous entries, onto the game itself.Not recommended. Why?Progression bugs. And on the first level no less. The fix I found was DO NOT skip in mission cinematics.Mission 11. Carriers and Units spawned INTO THE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ GLACIER and got stuck. Why?- Campaign completes in around 10 hours. Just 10 hours if you're slow.- The story sucks. Completely underwhelming.- Maps are 1/3 the size of previous entries. With even smaller play area.- Forced map progression missing resources, but fine because resources are practically redundant.- The Mothership is the fastest unit.- Unit scales are off.- No unit progression. Minimal upgrades. Linear. Boring- Unit variety sucks. Steal everything meaning the only thing you build are fighters.- Units move point blank range to fire. Then get stuck.- Units pass target, take forever to turn, then target half way across map.- Unit speed, firepower, logic are all unbalanced.- Clipping issues and trajectory.- No strategy, brute force your way through everything. Why?- Structure cover and sneaking is poorly implemented. Why?- BECAUSE PATH FINDING IS ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ AWFUL. Units likely to get stuck figuring out how to go round a wall.- Bad game logic, unit logic, flight logic, targeting logic.- Ignored commands, attack orders, move orders, repair orders, formation orders.Why 10 Utility units when I can only have 5? Why aren't there more Corvettes? Why aren't there more levels? Most are wasted time that do barely anything to the story. Which is bad enough as it is.Why are my units so stupid? Spin in circles trying to target something, then move past them. Cool.Okay, I'm sure there's lots more I could say. But honestly, what they wanted to do with this game is NOT what they produced with this game. I know others have had better experiences, but this is just frustrating.I can't recommend this. I want to. But I can't. It feels broken. I'm sorry Devs, but you just killed any hopes I had at a decent Homeworld game. There's just too many issues, with lackluster progression, and a poorly implemented strategy.I'm giving it a generous 6/10 as the voice acting and graphics are decent, and the ambience and backgrounds were good.

_childDocuments_.review: ... There might be some minor spoilers below ...Full disclosure: I have never played Homeworld 1 and 2 or Remastered. I have Deserts of Kharak in my Steam library but have not even played a full hour of it. I have always heard about the other games and how much the fanbase loves them but I have no personal experience to reference from. HW 3 is my very first Homeworld game that I have actually played and my review is from the viewpoint of a fresh newcomer to the series.I was immediately drawn to HW3 as soon as I saw the first trailer and the visual style of the gameplay. It all looked very interesting to me. Right up my alley. I really enjoy RTS games in general (Starcraft, Supreme Commander, Command and Conquer, Sins of a Solar Empire, Age of Empires, and Spellforce being among my favorites) but HW3 was really my first RTS that added the 3rd dimension to the field of play. Being attacked from any direction in 3D space is rather new for me.Having said all that, I will give this game a reluctant positive review but I fully acknowledge it's really not for everyone and it will never be popular.What I liked:- I like the gameplay for the most part. Note: the battles can be very frantic.- Great graphics and visual effects.- The space maps are not just wide open emptiness but they have these large ancient megastructures that add some complexity. It's not always a straight line from point A to B.- Campaign had some great missions.- Soundtrack was great.- Really dig the spaceship designs.- I liked the cinematic cutscenes. (I'm not a fan of the drawing style 2D cinematics that apparently the previous games had. Just a matter of personal taste I suppose.)- Wargames can be a great game mode but it's not well realized yet.What I did not like:- Campaign felt very short to me. I cannot believe it was over in 13 missions.- The story itself is probably the weakest point. No surprises, no twists, no turns. The whole story quite literally revolves around just 3 characters. Really no other characters of note at all.- I was hoping for some kind of epic space opera. The story was simply "small", for lack of a better word.- Only 6 skirmish maps at launch? This seems so inadequate.- War Games needed more factions, more fleets, more artifacts, more maps at launch. Only variety can add replayability to this mode.- Unit responsiveness seems poor. _childDocuments_.review: Homeworld 3 is a moderately OK game. Homeworld 3 is also a very poor Homeworld game.Homeworld as a series has a storied history, with most of the games relying on excellent storytelling to stay in their player's minds. The only exception was Homeworld 2, which had the weakest story of all 4 pre-Homeworld 3 games, but that game had the best modding scene. The game was so mod-able that the remaster from 2014 re-used the Homeworld 2 engine, and even to this date, work continues on the complex and Homeworld.fx mods, the latter of which even implements a sandbox RPG mode to the game.Homeworld 3 has yet to foster a community of modders to work on the game, and I have doubts that such a scene will ever grow with the lackluster response to this game (of which I am a part of, I know). Primarily however, I take issue with the game's story, the main reason anyone plays a Homeworld game. The game drops the slightly detached briefing-style story delivery from all prior games, instead turning it into a character drama that focuses on Imogen S'jet and her intelligence officer, creating friction and useless chatter half of the time between the two characters. Where Homeworld 1 would have us receive a briefing about our next mission alongside the importance of the target to our war effort, Homeworld 3 gives us a scene with Karen forcibly singing a lullabye to Imogen in some hyperspace-flashback. They try to make the characters endearing, but it almost makes the rest of the galaxy seem lame in comparison.Karen S'jet was the self-insert protagonist of the first game. The expansion to the game, Cataclysm/Emergence focused mostly on other Kith (Families) of the Hiigarans now going on to do their own great things, and making the galaxy feel alive with more people than just the S'jet Kith. Gearbox instead doubles down on putting Karen and her Kith on a pedestal, practically elevating them to godhood and making the entire story revolve around her disappearance. It ruins the Homeworld universe by implying that anything of importance must happen nearby a S'jet otherwise it's basically yesterday's news. There can be good stories in the Homeworld universe, but gearbox tacitly refuses to acknowledge it, instead preferring to turn Karen, Rachael, and Imogen into Mary Sues. This can be partially blamed on the state of the galaxy/cannon after Homeworld 2, where the hyperspace cores are required for any long-distance journey throughout the galaxy not relying on the gates, and the gates obviously will create high-traffic areas which distinctly won't have that feeling of exploration anymore. But Homeworld 3 tantalizingly has a solution introduced in the opening cutscene - Imogen S'jet has created synthetic hyperspace cores! Too bad the only person who is capable of using them is herself, another S'jet. The gameplay itself is fun, like most Homeworld games, and there are a few touching moments in the campaign (where fighter pilots are intentionally sacrificed for the mothership's continued mission). Salvaging is possible, but very difficult to pull off as only resource controllers can actually capture enemy ships, and there's a hard-cap of 5 controllers. I personally manage to make it through most of the campaign by simply creating a battle-blob of assault frigates and having 10 support frigates follow them around like a pocket medic, which works until the last 2 missions, making it mostly boring. I also run into issues controlling units, where the pathfinding which is trying to account for geometry, decides my units must run to an arbitrary waypoint before they can engage enemies.I hesitate to include the previous 2 sentences in this review, as balance and pathfinding issues are easy challenges for the developers to solve in a future patch, but the story itself is integral to this game's continued success, alongside being significantly more difficult to solve. I pray they release a "Director's Cut" in the future which leaves the overarching cannon in a more serviceable state.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to not recommend this game as someone who genuinely enjoys and had fun with it, but I can't in good conscience recommend this game both to homeworld fans and non-homeworld fans.So, lets start with the good. Graphically, the game is beautiful, the gameplay is enjoyable, wargames is very fun when playing with friends, and the new faction introduced in this game (the Incarnate) are pleasing on an aesthetic and gameplay level.Okay, now to the bad. The story is atrocious. I've heard a lot of good things about Homeworld 2 but I feel like what I've seen from Homeworld 2 story wise had a large hand in what was wrong with Homeworld 3. I'll leave you to come up with your own conjectures about what I mean by that, but I'll just say I think cataclysm was a better sequel. With that out of the way, the story in this game once again follows the S'Jet Kiith (through the eyes of the granddaughter of Karen S'Jet, Imogen) trying to enter a zone known as the "anomaly", a zone where Karen S'Jet and the Khar-Sajuuk went missing. Going there, you deal with this new force known as the Incarnate. Thats as far as I'm going to go into, because that is as interesting as it gets in my opinion. It's all downhill from there. And seeing as how most of us are probably here for the story of Homeworld, the fact the the story is shafted for Wargames is trash, especially since Wargames isn't really that great in the first place. Is it fun? yes. But matches are too short, usually being 3 missions long rather than proper campaigns all their own. Said Wargames missions, in my opinion, feel extremely disjointed as well. "Why are we here?"Would I recommend the game? No. Not at full price. The story is abysmal and the mode they want you to focus on is halfbaked. If it's on a pretty good sale? Go out and buy it! It's a fun game, and I hate to ♥♥♥♥ on it as much as I have been, but like...it's just not good as a Homeworld game.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing the Homeworld series since 1999. I had the compendium book, read all the lore, and I loved it. This game helped me personally manage my ADD as it taught me the benefits patience, multi-tasking, and long-term rewards. To say this game series is close to me is an understatement. It pains me greatly to not recommend this game. Retrospectively the only reason I would buy it is for nostalgia. On to the problems...Story: 2/5 stars. Much of what I love about the Homeworld universe is the story telling. The mix of the middle eastern inspired culture that was woven into the campaign. The single player mode only had the slightest whisper of that same feeling. The animated cut scenes were an unnecessary "update" to something that game Homeworld its distinct feel. There were a few callbacks that I appreciated such as the reference to the Turanic raiders cut scene from Homeworld 1. The story misses nearly every mark except for the core of searching for Karan S'jet. That being said the objectives and mission play itself was enjoyable. I found hard mode to be challenging and still fun (the achievement is bugged and does not show my completion). Which leads to the gameplay...Gameplay: 3/5 stars.  Homeworld 1, 2, cataclysm, and Deserts of Kharak all had their distinct play styles. Homeworld 2 had some additions I enjoyed and some I did not. Kharak was a prequel that i begrudgingly played and was glad I did. Overall the thing most RTS fans enjoy is some degree of diversity in effective strategies, some sort of complexity within reason, and a few ace-in-the hole mechanics; for homeworld that is the use of hyperspace jumping. As many have said, centeralizing larger unit production to motherships was a good move. I personally also enjoy the single unit production as well. It forces me to keep carriers actually close to the action. What I do not enjoy is the lack of ability to cripple carriers and other units by targeting subsystems. I at least expected to blast engines again. The inability to jump with hyperspace in skirmish is incredibly disappointing and I hope is a feature that will be added. There are also many balance issues with units that still have yet to be addressed and the AI for moving through structures and around debris still needs a lot of work. Overall the gameplay seems like an even more dumbed down version of Homeworld 1. The single thing I thought was great was the integration of resource controllers and collectors. I would have liked to see similar integrated unit types such as drone frigates placed into the game as well. War games was initially intriguing but has been very glitchy, many games result in a connection loss and often objectives are unable to be completed due to bugs. I would have liked to see a skill/research tree instead of randomized artifact cards that sometimes set up a player for failure or at best a bad time. Customization of fleets and carriers would draw me to invest more time. This model could even be presented as a more immersive search for the 5th fleet and stranded Hiigarran citizens through the galaxy and allow the fans to do what we have been dreaming of. Allowing people to play with friends, customize carriers and fleets, and explore the Homeworld galaxy together. TL:DR- Homeworld 3 misses the mark and brings shame upon Sajuuk. It lacks a compelling story, tries to fix things that aren't broken, such as moving away from the old cut scene style. Gameplay is overall average and presents very little innovation in the RTS world. It plays like a simpler Homeworld 1 and that's bad. The rogue-like war games are glitchy and the artifacts are inconsistent. I hope that this game gets more development in the future. P.S- If Blackbird and gearbox want to actually save this game here is what can be done:-Give us back hyperspace in skirmish-Build a better war games mode (carrier customization, replace artifacts with a research tree, and allow players to select areas to go to in the galaxy)-Give us things like a Taiidan republic fleet to use, Kedeshi, etc..- Within reason a similar model to helldivers II universe. Don't squeeze us for money, allow players to both buy and use found in-game currency to get new content.

_childDocuments_.review: It took me a while to really word why this game doesn't meet the mark. But really, what this game lacks is . Graphically, it looks amazing. The music is great, though it's not quite as good as the previous entries. The sound design is all there. It definitely  like Homeworld, until you get to the actual  part. First off, what in the world happened with the controls? They feel as if I'm making  and the camera just wakes up and decides whether or not it wants to be a camera for that frame or not. I mean, I get it, this game is a workout for both the CPU and the GPU, but that's really no excuse for how bad the controls respond to input; the Unreal engine is  of doing better. That's not even taking into account how lazy, lethargic, and randomly the ships respond to orders and go off doing their own space cowboy thing, though I'm aware of the irony. I really don't want to micromanage everything  have terrible controls to do it with. Then there's the story/campaign. I think I made it about 3/4ths of the way through it before realizing how bored I actually was. It's just not very compelling, and lacks a lot of the ancient, epic, and mysterious elements that the previous entries were filled with. Instead, the story is very generic and leans heavily on dramatic interpersonal interactions. Honestly, I really don't understand why modern science fiction writers are so insistent of copying Star Wars when ; I'm still very adamant that one of the (many) reasons Halo died, was that they stopped ripping  and went after Star Wars instead. Either way, here's another case of trying to make one franchise check all the boxes of another. I also didn't like the decision to go with full CGI cinematics; the hand-drawn greyscale cinematics were a signature Homeworld trait and added to the mystery and were dramatic in a way that didn't need overwritten dialog. I would have even taken the Deserts of Kharak style cinematics, which added in color and more elaborate animations in a way that paid homage to the previous entries.I really don't have much to say about the rest of the game; Live service games are not my thing, and I just don't have the time or patience for multiplayer. Tl;dr: All flash, no substance. Go play Homeworld Remastered, Deserts of Kharak, and Cataclysm/Emergence instead. There are also other great space games out there that deserve your attention (including Star Wars!).

_childDocuments_.review: It's really hard to have to do this to one of my favorite IP's of all time, but if you're looking for a game that matches the feeling you got playing other entries in this universe, and in particular the first Homeworld, this leaves a lot to be desired. The big miss to me is the story and characters. It's fairly rife with plot holes, especially towards the end, and honestly it just feels like it's geared towards a young audience. It's like Disney acquired the IP then turned it into a scifi show for teens, where everyone is redeemable no matter how genocidal they may have been, and relationship development is basically just forced emotional moments that don't feel well placed, while a regurgitated variation of Adagio for Strings plays in the background. Homeworld 1, for me anyways, created this really intriguing setting that had an interesting underlying story about a lost people re-discovering their history while trying to survive, and exploring the state of the universe under the rule of the Taiidan Empire. Homeworld 3 was like "what's a setting? Here's some tropey characters!"Another thing that's story-ish related is that there are hardly any other factions. There's basically a pirate faction, which I will not spoil, that really only gets touched on then never mentioned again after their last mission. There was some explanation, but honestly it felt like there should have been more to them than what was covered. Past that, there aren't other factions. No friendlies, like a Captain Soban from Homeworld 2, and no neutral/mysterious factions like the Bentusi (I know they're gone, but something like that).Aside from story, I do have some gameplay gripes:-Why did the devs feel the need to keep the unskippable cutscenes mid-game? Come on, that's the one thing I would have been happy to see go away from previous entries.-This game is extremely easy. I played on Medium, partially because it's been a while since I played a Homeworld game, but also because I remember the challenge that was Homeworld 2 scaling, but it was way too easy. Definitely go for a harder setting if you've played Homeworld at all.-Battle cruisers just slowed the game down way too much. I know they're supposed to be cumbersome, but they seem really bad at moving under some circumstances, in some cases coming to a dead stop with orders issued. Honestly, I wanted to just ditch them and replace them with destroyers by the end of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the campaign and to be honest, I am beyond disappointed. None of the mystery, impending doom and sense of vastness that the previous games' stories had. Super shallow plot. The deliberate absence of faces and characters on screen in previous games made you care about the people as a whole, without delving into their individuality, which has never been the focus, aside from maybe Karan a little. And all we got before was her voice, enacted so well, it was all we needed. There's nothing of that here. The antagonist was ridiculous and laughable. The protagonists weren't far off that. The pirates came and went, and left no lasting impression. There was no Bentusi (yeah, I know, I mean it conceptually), there's no other kiithid, no sense of loss, no strong uniting cause, nothing. DoK had more gripping story than this...The cutscenes look like they've been made in 2010. Crappy models, crappy animation, ugly designs, mesh clipping in plain sight(?!?)... This does not feel at all like something we all waited 20 years for. On the contrary - it looks extremely cheap and half-assed. I'd much rather prefer the hand drawn mostly static cutscenes and narrator we had before.The gameplay is awesome, ingame ships, ingame animations, FX, etc. But it somehow feels like it was all in the name of modes like Wargames. Almost like the whole game was centered around the competitive multiplayer side of it, and the campaign was just made as an excuse.This is fine. But is not what made HW, what it is. It's the story that got us all hooked and made us play it over and over again, and spend countless hours in skirmishes and multiplayer after.There's none of that here. I am not seeing it.And just as the credits rolled I realized that it felt just like the Matrix 4 felt. With all its stupid reasons for existing.And I don't think there's much more to say, after that. Hence why this review is negative.Edit: It turns out the gameplay stuff is done by BBI (original creators of the HW franchise, under Relic), but the story is written by a Gearbox pink-haired wokie, that had no clue what this game is about. This explains a lot. Keep in mind this little fact was kept away from the potential buyers pre-release. This review will remain negative, until the whole campaign is rewritten and updated by the original developers. Which will never happen, so consider it indefinite. That's a prime example of how you ruin a franchise. Thanks for nothing, Gearbox.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a redact to my original comment when I said HW3 is great.  Just to put it into perspective - I'm 42 and I played the original HW1 on a Packard Bell 133Mhz CPU PC, catalyst expansion, HW2, complex mod (on of my favs), deserts of Kharak, remastered versions - I played and own them all.  On CDs and even some duplicates for ez of install on steam.  Now that I've spent 4 hours with HW3, I honestly am baffled by all the negative comments from people.  Controls are awkward - fine, "D" doesn't mean dock anymore but transpose right.  Switch to non modern scheme.  S is stop, D is dock.  Easily fixed.  Love the support frigate auto-heal function tho and when those capital class explode - the screen shake is just awesome!  Thank you for that.  Anyway, no point in writing a bad review because you can't manage the controls (albeit BBI did mess this one up, it's not a show stopper).  The most important part is BBI/GB retained the atmosphere, the music is amazing, the experience is awe.  People complain of a short campaign - fine, when was it ever long enough?   I honestly give it close to 100.  I don't usually write reviews at all - bad or good, but I feel this game deserves my time to write one.  This game franchise is a pioneer with RTS - any time people mention price in their reviews, you know they don't have experience nor time to contribute.  Price at this point will not matter for anyone who played original HW 25 years ago.  You either didn't like it or did and you became a fan.  For perspective, HW3 deluxe is the first game I ever purchased retail price pre-release - wish I went collectors edition tho, my buddy loves the physical models and other trinkets he got.  It's not about the price-value, although I would argue for any RTS lover, this price is just - I support the development and I will go see Pink Floyd if David and Roger plays again - it's not about the price, it's about the experience. Same with this game - you either like it or hate it.  If HW3 is your introduction to HW franchise, I suggest you stop and play the HW1 and HW2 first, but those that have waited 20+ years for a sequel, won't be disappointed.  This game is for us - 42 year olds - I feel new generation's metric on reviewing the game is along the Karen lines.  This game is not just great, it's amazing.  I love every aspect of it (aside from minor bugs that will eventually be ironed out).  One thing I really don't like is how hot my PC gets when I turn on all the settings to EPIC, but I love the view on my 49in curved monitor has never been so breathtaking.  Yes, this game fully supports UWM and no, you don't need a beast of a PC to enjoy this.  I think this is just how AMD hardware works - runs hot all the time.

_childDocuments_.review: Having fallen in love with the OG Homeworld and its sequel over 20 years ago, as well as really enjoying the remastered collection and being pleasantly surprised by Deserts of Kharak, despite it not being set in space, suffice to say Homeworld 3 has a lot riding on it to deliver, especially after the somewhat wonky demo a few months.  But I'm pleased to say I'm really enjoying this game, the campaign has a great variety of mission types and layouts.  Mastering the new space terrain/debris takes some time particularly when trying to deploy ships or turrets to the correct surface, but when you watch your wing of bombers literally fly under the enemy's radar and emerge from a massive derelict station to take out an enemy carrier it's all worth it.The maps and ships are beautiful, particularly the nebula and lighting effects. I would say I miss the old artstyle for the cutscenes, which are fully voiced and animated now, maybe they could have stuck to the Deserts of Kharak animated/blended artwork and voiceover style, but that's just my preference.The war games/roguelite runs a lot smoother than the demo (you can actually finish a match this time!).  Even playing this CPU intensive game on the steam deck on medium and low settings works relatively well.Recommend this game both for fans of the series and newcomers looking for a Space RTS that lets you research, build and hurl fleets of ships at your enemies and watching space (not Kharak) burn.

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth at full price, I'm not sure that even 50% discount would make this worthwhile. Just get Homeworld Remastered and Homeworld Emergence instead.The game doesn't seem to do anything better than the previous games (excluding graphics). The gameplay is gutted. The game removes several important gameplay features present in previous games and doesn't execute the remaining ones as well as the previous games did. The only new addition is terrain in space which, in my opinion, is more of a detriment. It is by far the weakest game in the franchise (excluding mobile and VR games, never played them) in all respects save for obviously graphics.The game looks excellent, if you have the hardware for it. The models are nice, the effects are great (in particular large ship explosions and their wrecks). The ships and sound effects sound great. There is a lot of banter between units (almost too much sometimes and you can't isolate anything useful out of it), I only wish it was more relevant to what is happening from gameplay perspective (e.g. "we're under fire from enemy corvette/frigate/destroyer etc.).Except prerendered cutscenes, they just look bad. The best way to describe the cutscenes is outdated and out of place. Previous games had 2D art with some small amount of animation and they looked and set the tone brilliantly. Not sure why BBI decided to (presumably) spend more money on something that looks and works worse than the (presumably) cheaper and easier solution. That's just the visual part of the cutscenes, their content is actualy far, far worse.One thing that surprises me, is that even though the music is composed by Paul Ruskay (who also made the OSTs for previous games) there are no standout music tracks. The biggest difference to me was a lot more drums with lot of bass, but they are mostly background ambience with no noticeable melody to them. The only memorable tracks were those few that borrowed/replayed themes from the previous games. We also get one more iteration of Adagio for strings.You can't really specialize and the best strategy is just to get as many resource collectors as possible, spam all available units which you research almost immediately. Then, gather them up and toss them at the enemy. Your mothership can be producing multiple craft simultaneously. Not spamming all ships leaves you at a disadvantage.The strikecraft have 0 dogfighting behaviour. They stick to one formation like a school of fish fighting other school of fish and never break formation to engage multiple targets. No evasive manoeuvres, no jinking, It really looks terrible compared to previous games, in particular to Homeworld 1. Gone are the stances that changed how units behave in dogfight (evasive, neutral, aggressive). The stances available just decide the distance at which they will try to find targets to shoot at.Collisions/ramming as a mechanic is absent, so is fuel. Tactics are of no impact, spamming and force concentration are king.The unit AI seems unfinished at best and downright broken at worst. They often refuse to fire on hostiles within weapon range until you give them a direct attack order. This is a frequent occurrence, units are within firing range and their set stance should have them fire on the enemy, but they just ignore each other. The AI and pathfinding become another issue due to a new feature introduced in this game, namely terrain. Much too often they go where you don't them to go. They also refuse to sit still and fire their weapons on a target within range, they constantly wander off. This makes frigates and capital ships incredibly frustrating and underwhelming to use.Terrain in space. Its impressive the developer took the risk, but at its current execution it only detracts from the gameplay. First of all, the terrain (megastructures, space rocks) are way too large and the maps are way too small, heavily restricting the space in which you play. I don't think there is a single map that would just be the void of space with some small rocks to harvest for resources, like it was in the previous games. It feels like you're diving in underground caves and not flying in space.Second of all, the AI sometimes has weird interactions with it. It is competent enough to not cause traffic jams when you order a lot of ships to move in tight spaces, however if you order a lot of ships to move behind a rock, some will end up on the side you don't want them to be. Also using terrain isn't really necessary and doesn't give any significant advantage.I don't think it really adds anything interesting to the game at this point. The vision, weapon ranges and ship speed aren't balanced to work well with this terrain. What does it matter that an enemy is behind a wreck of some megaship if I wouldn't be able to see nor fire on them anyway, had there been no wreck in the way?With the presence of directional damage (ships take more damage from behind etc.) we should have more controls over the pitch, yaw, roll and direction of our ships. Yet all we have is a simple move and attack order with no fine control which direction the ship is facing. This also isn't necessary. TTK is extremely low.All subsystems were removed from the game. This is just a straight downgrade for no dis reason. Same goes for utility modules, such as cloaking, hyperspace, hyperspace inhibitors, research modules, attack/defense modules. Hyperspace as an ability/movement option is completely gone. There are no buildable hyperspace gates. It is present in story and cutscenes, but is removed entirely from gameplay. This is a big deal. It might be correlated to the maps being so small, but I'm not sure which came first in that case. I am really baffled by removal of this option as it is such an integral part of the universe and gameplay.The game feels really dumbed down with all those features absent, like a bad knockoff and not a sequel.My complaints with the story can be narrowed down to bad presentation and execution, different approach to the way the story is told and awful writing. There is a character limit here so I will post my thoughts elsewhere, but in short:Hiigarans are utterly incompetent fools who are struggling against a saturday morning cartoon villain. The antagonist has powers that break existing rules of the universe with no explanation. To allow the plot to happen both suffer from sudden onset of amnesia and forget about both existing tech from previous games and the new abilities they are shown to possess in this game. The antagonist apparently just forgets they could kill our fleets in an instance.The presentation is poor due to the prerendered cutscenes. The models look bad, there is plenty of clipping during closeups (cables and Imogen's hair), Isaac's jersey having some weird artifacts on his back. Further the facial animations are also, at best, outdated. Up close they just do not look good for prerendered cutscenes. Imogen looks like she is doing her best to hold it in and failing. The lip sync is off, it seems the characters were animated by hand with no mocap (which is impressive), but also makes them extremely emotive, almost like cartoon characters. the Antagonist is the worst offender in this, at one cutscene I thought I was watching a Pixar animation due to how she moved her arms and head.The ending also felt off, instead of having a conventional victory there is a sacrifice/reconciliation theme going on which I don’t find to have been explained adequately as the only viable/best solution. The focus on personal drama was not done particularly well and doesn’t fit the setting.The campaign is also very short, but given how terrible the story is that's actually a benefit.

name: Headquarters: World War II
detailed_description: Headquarters: World War II is a fast paced turn-based strategy covering the Battle of Normandy in the three plot-driven campaigns and a number of skirmishes. Choose your side, form your force, assign heroes, level up your units, and use Headquarters skills to overcome the enemy. Face a real tactical challenge The game's combat system is based on an easy to learn - hard to master approach . Deceptively easy at a first glance, it offers lots of possibilities: Units have front/side/back/top armor and their positioning matters a lot Fences and other obstacles offer a directional cover that depends on the angle of attack Different terrain types offer various bonuses and affect Line of Sight Destroyed vehicles and other large objects affect the battlefield and provide cover High Ground mechanics allow multiple levels of terrain elevation that affect Line of Sight and combat effectiveness Destructible buildings with different stages of demolition create unique challenges Enjoy the striking visuals All units and scenery are created with the finest attention to detail using Unreal Engine 4 to achieve a very realistic visual style: Realistic unit models with proper physics in place Visceral elements of devastation - burning tank hulks, ruined houses, shell craters, smoke, death, and destruction. You will witness this and many other horrors of the war Varied surroundings - your troops will come across war-torn battlefields as well as peaceful villages with cattle and fields of grain. Mind your tanks - this quaint beauty is quite fragile Go through numerous battles See all sides of the story by completing 3 campaigns with 9 operations in each. The game features United States, United Kingdom, and German campaigns all set in the Normandy landings period of the war. _childDocuments_.review: Imagine, PanzerGeneral/PanzerCorps style rules, with a 3D map/Units with little movie cut scenes of actions.  This game is fun!  If you like WWII turn based strategy, you should enjoy this.  Game has unit management, promotions, level ups, heroes, purchasing and carrying over your core units to the next battles, etc.  Unlike PG/PzC, unit facing is important, and when you suffer losses to a unit, it degrades in performance.  (Losing a driver, impacts the units ability to move)3 Factions currently, each with about 10 missions.  Looks like they could easily add more scenarios and hopefully grand campaigns in the future.  No bugs encountered yet.  Graphics are sufficient.  There is no built in multi-monitor support, which is a bit irritating in this day and age, but you can work around it.  Sound is pretty good.If you're into WWII TBS Strategy games, you will enjoy this!

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and "just one more turn" addictive game.  Once you get the hang of knowing how to spot the enemy, and see their weapon ranges, it is pretty manageable on normal difficulty.  Two artillery for the win so far on every mission!  Very little counter artillery fire.. so far.. 3-4 missions in on each the British, American and German campaigns..and we have managed to kill any artillery we come across before they get a chance to do any damage and they seem like they do not prioritize your own arty as targets.  AI could be more aggressive, but they have key points to protect, so it's understandable that they keep close to the defensive points, but it makes them predictable.  PvP on this game would be totally different. Have not tried that yet.  Thumbs up and worth a buy at any discount (I personally only purchase games when there is a discount.)  I can see where once you have done all the scenarios the game would be less interesting unless you are a completest and want to win them all on the harder difficulties.  Custom scenarios will give this game a few more legs at least for a while particularly if you want to play against a friend.   Worth a buy!Update: Since May 28th patch (1.00.06) a bug was introduced that will not let you complete some campaigns due to an Unreal Engine crash.  I do not recommend playing until after patch 1.00.07 comes out if you want to play the campaigns.  Can't finish the USA campaign so far.  Again.. I concur with others to wait for a discount before purchasing.  Solid fun game outside of the crash issue.  Pretty easy on normal difficulty.  Wish the core units had perma-death and they could use more unit upgrade features.  For instance the ability to upgrade past 3 stars or choose more options if you get enough upgrade points to go back and select more unit upgrade features even if already at 3 stars.
