_childDocuments_.review: it's a good time and in some ways better than the normal version of the game, but it has too many issues that can't be overlooked. Just to name a few: -it's a 50/50 whether or not you crash as soon as you join a game -nobody ever joins your games if they aren't at least half full-no party system, so good luck trying to queue up for a public match with friends when the game tries to fill up the half full lobbies as quick as possible-ghosts can open doors which is visible to living players, giving them a method of communication with the living -only 1 mapIt's odd to charge double the price for arguably less content and more bugs. I understand it's a VR upgrade, but if we ignore that novelty, this is just among us with less content and proximity chat.
_childDocuments_.name: Among Us VR

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun, I love it but I have a number of complaints that stop me from recommending it to others.- There is no party mode so good luck getting into public matches with friends (you need at least 5 people if you want a chance of your lobby being picked up by the elusive 'quick match' function)- There is a 50/50 chance of just not being able to connect to a new lobby and/or losing connection to a lobby after a game concludes- Sometimes the voice chat just stops working completely (only fix for me is a restart)- Don't unfocus the game in windows or you won't be able to press anything (this shouldn't happen in a VR game)- An age bracket selection of some kind would be fantastic, not only to protect kids but to protect my eardrumsBesides that I'm amazed by how well this game ports into VR. Can't wait until some/all of these issues are fixed :)Edit:Since writing this I've learnt that the private-to-public lobby function does indeed work however there is a 5-10 minute wait until it is picked up by the quick match list.Another thing worth mentioning is that I'm acutely aware that this is a kids game but my point regarding age bracket selection still stands.I do enjoy this game wholeheartedly so please assume that everything I *haven't* mentioned in this list works very well.

_childDocuments_.review: You can view my review & gameplay here: This is a solid VR port, if a bit underwhelming, of the formerly popular Among US. Honestly, this VR port may have arrived a year too late, but what's here is a good deal for only $10 USD. This VR port is the definitive experience for Among US, even if it is missing several features of the non-VR version.Among Us VR is a lot more fun than Among Us (non-VR). Not only does everyone have proximity voice chat available now (although you can turn option off in both settings & also in creating a lobby), but now you will have to watch your six while completing simple VR tasks such as pumping a handle, playing whack-a-mole, or guiding a ship with a wheel to its destination. The gameplay is simple, but effective in creating a sense of tension. Who can you trust? Or, if you're an impostor, how do you get away with it?The social deduction viral hit just works better in VR. Beware though: a large segment of the playerbase consists of young kids, not just under 18, but also under 13. Yes, all the moms and dads out there that let their bratty kids play VR unsupervised ...  and most adults will probably find that annoying. There is no way to stop this other than being host and manually kicking out anybody that sounds under-aged. Also, if you know the Steam playerbase like I do, you know it's a cesspool for racial slurs, misogyny, & homophobia. This game is definitely better if you just happen to have 9 VR friends with good internet connections in a region near you.Game is running on the Unity Engine. I did have frame rate drops, but it wasn't too bad. You do have comfort options, full locomotion, smooth & snap turning, along with speed of turns. You also have several text or voice options. The VR interactions are basically either point & click, or highlight & hold and push / pull or turn. The mini-game tasks aren't interesting, but it is still interesting enough, especially when you have someone right behind you looking sus.Overall, I had fun, but your fun will vary depending on the public group randoms you get. Keep in mind, you can choose a private lobby and that is recommended. Also, there is only one map in this VR port.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally had bought this game on the meta quest PC app but a few months after I bought it, they stopped supporting it. I shrugged it off thinking "There are way too many kids in this game for it to be fun" and at the time that was very true.I heard that this was less of an issue today, so seeing that the game was on sale, I decided to spend $7 on it, I do not recommend this game as it is still infested with kids, also people tend to get very inpatient when waiting for people to join the game.If I had to rate it out of 10 it would be a 2 it is only fun if you can get a good lobby (which almost never happens) It is an interesting take on among us, but feels like a different game. I wish that Innersloth would actually develop their VR game instead of outsourcing it. There are also some behaviors in this game that differ from regular among us.  - You can only have 3 engineers (everyone can be engineer in base game)  - you can only have 10 player lobbies (15 player lobbies in base game) - there are only 2 maps (compared to the 5 in the base game) - when the host leaves, everyone gets disconnected (in the base game when the host disconnects, host is transferred to someone else)  - Host cannot kick/ban players from public lobbies (in base game the host has way more power over their lobby)  - vote kicking does not show the amount of votes (the base game will show a progress bar on how many more votes are needed to kick someone) There are at least 10 more things that I could come up with, but I will not list them here. This game could easily be a 10/10 from me but it isn't because of how the developers are making the game for money, not to make a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: In the vast history of the human race, a few key events seem to emerge in the forethought of an individual’s mind. The invention of the wheel. The conception of electricity. The origination of the great country we call the United States. Though paramount in their time, these events all dull in comparison to what we, the human race, are privileged to experience in the present era; Among Us VR. A miracle, some might say, has been constructed before our very eyes. Though rudimentary, the Among Us VR experience is thoroughly promising and presents ideas that haven’t been fabricated thus far. Unique and confident in its design, Among Us VR boasts a stylized and quite agreeable aesthetic that predecessors, such as Among Us VRChat, have yet to achieve. The bold, dark lines surrounding the characters, as well as the saturated and caricature-like environment, merge into a seemingly perfect habitat for the creative and daring gamer. All things considered, the creators of this experience strive not to manufacture realism, but to produce something unseen. Departing from the artistic aspect to the conventional, what can be said other than brilliant. The minimalistic controls and facile tasks serve to uplift Among Us VR from good to great. It is quite rare to find an electronic game with as much grace and simplicity, one not even needing a tutorial to begin playing. Though one must understand the rules of the original Among Us, most individuals who choose to purchase this commodity will already hold such knowledge. Though it is advisable for some to swap the A and B buttons, as this correlates directly to VRChat controls, it is not necessary and cannot be recommended to most persons. All that being said, I, Lunkiee, deem this game a well-founded 9/10. The troupe who put their time and effort into this astounding creation were obviously highly motivated and involved, and it shows in the brilliance of this media.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I just want to preface this review by saying the game is in fact really fun. Yes, the matchmaking is horrendous. Yes, I feel content such as security cams, more tasks, or settings should have been implemented. Still, the game at its core is a joy when you are with the right people. Therefore, I do definitively recommend this game to other people. That being said-Edit v2 the sequel: I believe they have somewhat fixed matches made by you hosting, it takes around 10 minutes for players to join in a public lobby you have created but it does in fact work nowOriginal Review: As a beta tester, this game was fantastic. Now that it's been released, I cannot recommend anyone to buy this unless they are looking for purely random lobbies or have a group of enough friends to fill a lobby.The matchmaking is atrocious, with no server browser. If you get into a game, it is almost entirely guaranteed that you are either the 9 or 10th person in, with the game about to start. This means that, with us attempting for almost an hour, I could not at any point get into a game with just one friend of mine. On top of this, when we created our own lobby, not a single soul joined into it through quick matching. The random games themselves weren't the greatest, as I only twice managed to find like 2 people above the age of 10. Screaming children rampant, it wasn't so much a game of social deduction as much as trying to reason with others about something terribly obvious while the children decide to vote you because... well, they are children. On top of all of this, there is a consistent bug where upon trying to quickmatch into a game it sends me to a lobby of just myself, and when I leave it says "Server Connection Timed Out." Keep in mind my wifi is really good and I was in fact using airlink to connect to Steam VR, proving a good connection. This error happened at one point four times in a row.The game itself is fun, so if you want Among Us in VR you're getting exactly that. I just wish I could hang out with a friend. If they ever fix matchmaking, it is 100% a recommendation from me. Even with the children, just messing around with my pal could've made it a blast. I hope they improve this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely write reviews this extensively but, holy hell this was disappointing. Most of the very positive reviews also just seem like they're joking around, so don't let the store page fool you.I had this game gifted to me by a friend, and it was probably the worst Among Us experience we've ever had. I hate to say that, because I was really looking forward to playing this, and it would have given me and excuse to use my VR headset more often. Here's just a small-ish list of issues I've had with the game so far:- Controls already feel wonkyMost of it is fine, but the turning is a major put-off (and before you ask, yes I have tried both styles)I also have no idea how to input my own damn name, would have been nice to know without looking like a fool asking someone else ingame.- Matchmaking is a hassleCreating a lobby feels like it doesn't do anything. Me and two friends waited in our own public lobby for what had to have been roughly 20 minutes for nothing to happen. Major waste of time to make a room with friends if you can't even fill the rest of the room up with randoms. We've had to resort to just all going to quick play and praying we all get in a match together.- Not much contentVR is a big leap, I get that. However, base Among Us has everything you already expect it to have. I was expecting some more content other than the things we've seen from the trailer, but nah. You get just the first basic 12 colors, only 9 hats (with a hat DLC on launch by the way), and the ONLY map you can play on is Skeld. Not very exciting, especially for the wait.There's probably some other bugs/features/fixes that I may not have pointed out, but honestly I've wasted enough time already, and I'd rather not re-purchase this game. SAVE YOUR MONEY (At least when there's more things to see). If you want to have a good time playing Among Us in VR with friends, just head over to VRC instead. Trust me, you'll have a way better time.--edit--After looking at some other footage/gameplay from other people, I've come to give out a couple extra details I might have missed. I won't go into much detail here, since I'm just writing a review, not a whole damn essay:- Microphone quality tends to fluctuate sometimes (In some instances not work at all)- Some of the cell shading on the crewmates look a little iffy, but honestly aren't too bad- No room settings to tweak how you wanna play the game is pretty disappointing...- I've recalled some instances where you can't see people's hands while ingame (Excluding meetings)- There are some things I still DO like! The general setting of Skeld looks great in VR, and doing the tasks feels fun and enjoyable!I don't want to be completely negative, but I only spew out my distaste for this game because I WANT it to be a fun and enjoyable experience. As of right now though, my point still stands. TL:DRDon't let positive meme reviews deter you, the game is very barebones right now. We've waited MONTHS to only have one map, 12 colors, and nine hats (With a DLC that costs roughly half of the base game). Matchmaking is just atrocious, and is missing a lot of things that PC Among Us already offered everyone. Very disappointing.If you want to play Among Us reliably with friends, just play it on PC. If you REALLY wanna do it in VR, just go on Jar's world on VRChat, it's not hard to miss.

_childDocuments_.review: A good concept executed poorly. Among Us VR is a faithful recreation of the original game designed for virtual reality play, and does a fine job with its basic concept. However, the game lacks variety, and in my opinion, does not have enough content to warrant the 10 dollar price tag. On top of the lack of contents such as maps, tasks, and the crewmate roles that the standard game holds, the game is also highly dependent on online play, which fails immensely by it being a VR only title of a game that already has dwindling player numbers. Among Us VR features no cross-play with the base game, so any servers one would join are more than likely to be entirely empty, rendering the game practically unplayable. Many people can not afford virtual reality, and even more find little value in playing a watered down 3D port of a much better game that can be played cheaper- in all regards. As such, Among Us VR fails in finding an audience that truly finds any value in it.3/10Decent concept, horrendous execution, with little chance of recovery, and the issues of the game being mostly unplayable.

_childDocuments_.review: (Old review is below)This game still has a lot of issues after launch, the worst being the servers. I'm lucky to get through one game without a disconnect. As of right now I cannot recommend the game, it has too many issues that make it extremely annoying to play. The game has potential but I'm not seeing any improvements to the game from the dev team, so it's hard to imagine the game reaching its full potential. ____________Weird bug where you can't hear other players, and they can't hear you. Heads are not tracked, your player model is set in the center of your playspace, so your hands could be floating 2 feet away from your body. Game runs fine just isn't polished, also had a few issues with disconnecting. Overall these bugs will be ironed out, game is fun can't wait for cams to be added. I also think wires needs to be added too ngl. Maybe make a way to type in chat too, the voice chat is unhinged so you might as well let the text chat type what they want too. TLDR: good start, hope it continues to get better through updates and stuff. (UPDATE: game still has many issues after launch, and server traffic has made it very hard to play in general. I don't recommend the game right now in general, let alone for $10)

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong, the game IS fun!  I've had a good time playing it.  However, in terms of value for money I feel like the developers have rushed this out way too soon.Problems Encountered:- Right out of the starting gate, the game would not accept my date of birth.  Why?  Because despite it prompting for MM/DD/YYYY, it turned out to actually be accepting DD/MM/YYYY.- Single map, which is less feature complete than the original, such as the cameras- No rule customisation.  2 impostors were too much for most of our lobbies with a few disconnects- Extremely limited character customisation- Matchmaking needs improving, ESPECIALLY in regards to age.  Nothing will scare teens / adults off the game more than a lobby full of screaming kids!- I personally only had one disconnect, but noticed it frequently happening to other players- Start of each round was mostly being locked in the cafeteria, due to sabotages being immediately available- Very jarring default settings, such as the tunnel vision and snap turning.  I think this should be a preference question on first run.Announcing a road map is all well and good, but first impressions are the most important, and many people will not be as willing to come back and try again later in development.

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to recommend this, but not in its current state. This game needs some serious fixing. It has connection problems, glitches that make it impossible to play normally and a really low amount of content. There's only one map and a lot of the tasks that you're used to from the 2d topdown game aren't even here. On top of that from what i could tell you can't even change any of the game rules when hosting (Which is a problem in a game where you sometimes get people who will tryhard and follow you around to watch you complete tasks and see if the taskbar actually goes up). In terms of glitches i had sessions where i couldn't see certain people (one where i couldn't see the entire lobby), bodies that got reported through out the same match would always be the same color or even have people share the same color and just have the tag "player name". I also highly highly recommend to the devs to add the ability to do quicksearch with certain requisites. Especially an 18+ only filter since there's been way too many times where i've ran into small children. Like not even Teens but actually single diggit age sounding children. As an Adult player it feels incredibly awkward to get put in a lobby only to find everyone else is a minor. It feels like Chris Hansen is gonna join the lobby any second and ask me to sit down and answer a few questions for him. I know it's pretty easy to just lie about your age but i think or atleast hope that the actual small children who've probably asked their parents to set the game up for them to begin with, will not do that (Seriously people do a better job at parenting, don't just put your preteen kids infront of a game and call it a day). Also having other filters might be a good idea later down the line, like "Only Default Settings", "Only modified Settings" and "Fine with either Settings" for when we actually are able to change the game rules with presumably one of the upcoming updates. Unless you're going into this with an allready decently sized friend group or something this game is really not worth getting right now. PS. for the devs: If you guys want this to actually take off and have a higher player count it would be in your best interest to look into adding a desktop mode. So far none of the tasks require you to use both hands so you'd just have figure out how to map one hand to the mouse which in terms of buttons would be as easy as pressing right mousebutton makes you point and pressing right and left together makes a fist. It's just gonna be kinda awkward to change depth and rotation via buttons but i'm sure there is some kind of workaround given how many people i know that played vr chat without a vr-headset.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not that bad. The tasks are well integrated and the map is pretty well done. However this game is definitely not complete and needed at least another few months of development. There is only one map as of now, which would be fine if it was large enough and provided enough content to last till another map comes out. However there are multiple parts of the map that are unpolished/not done. For example the cameras in security are non functional and when you vent you can just stand a little taller and it allows you to see the whole map and where people are. Also you cannot edit how many impostors/tasks/etc are present in the game. This would have released great as a pre alpha or a play test to show what the devs have been up to but it definitely not a done game that is worthy of your money as of now. Also there is a HUGE problem with children in this game. There are no filters on the VOIP so anything can be said to these kids. While i realize not much can be done about this it is still very annoying and quite concerning.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine the most bare bones beta version of Amogus and put it in VR. Actually maybe alpha because this lacks basic features that flatscreen Amogus had at launch like lobby settings, camera room, etc. The voice chat sounds terrible, the game is full of jank and bugs, and lobbies almost never work.For some reason voice chat seems to have everyone at the same insanely high volume and you can hear people from pretty far away. _childDocuments_.review: Okay, let's be real. Playing Among Us in 2022 is cringe af. But you know how the VR elitists are, always needing their fix, so I'd be lying, if I said this game wasn't fun. They ported the tasks pretty nicely into VR, lurking in the vents feels pretty cool as well. Best part about this version is the proximity voice chat outside of meetings though, honestly to me personally this was something that always felt off about the original.I enjoy these social deduction games and this one somehow tickles all the right parts of my monkey brain. After I've grown kinda tired of Pavlov TTT, this is quite the nice alternative and since it's made for the Quest, this will likely run on a potato, too. If there was a way to not have toddlers scream into your ear, I wouldn't have anything negative to say about this game, but muting them is a valid option, I guess. For eight bucks it's slightly overpriced in its current state, but show me any new game release that's complete nowadays lul.I'll definitely be checking out the next updates, for now the one map's unfortunately gotta do it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's missing important features from the original game. You can't change game rules and there's no server browser. If you have a small group of friends with VR like me, you probably won't be able to get a game going with your friends and some randoms. We tried waiting a while for randoms to join our public 3/10 full room, but nobody ever joined. Then we tried using quickplay (because there's no server browser) to get a mostly empty room that we could fill the slots of, but none of us were able to join a game with more than 2 free slots. It seems the quickplay system prioritizes mostly full games, which probably explains why we never got anyone in our own room.Aside from that, the game seems fine, you just need a large group of friends with VR (probably unlikely?) and/or be willing to just play with randoms all the time.

Somehow I was deemed innocent, and the vote was between Orange and Green, which ended up with my fellow imposter Green being voted out. Following this Me, Orange, and Red grouped up and as we walked through engines Green locked us in, my time had arrived. Red saw me coming and started screaming, but it was too late. _childDocuments_.review: A beta release missing major features.There are some user experience issues that make me think they didnt ask rnadom people ot test their game.  Things like the game suddenly snapping you to objectives instead of letting you maneuver to them.  Forced movement in VR is never acceptable.Basic implementations seem completely missing:1) No visual tasks anymore that I can see2) Cameras don't exist3) No server settings.  This is the big one, because you can't adjust server settings you can't do things like adjust movement speeds, light range, kill timers, things like that so a server is a server is a server.4)  Apparently the idea is to microtransaction their income.  A pack of 6-7 hats is a $4 DLC on the store at this time.  So you pay for basically no features...and then pay for hats.  Right.In short, its a good first start but they left too much out to say this is an acceptable version of the game.  I have refunded at this time.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like Among Us VR. It's incredibly well made - more so than the standard game I would say - but it's genuinely impossible to get into games that aren't filled with Quest kids that aren't actually old enough to use their headsets according to Meta's TOS.I understand the irony in saying that Among Us of all games isn't good in VR because of the amount of children, but I can't overstate how impossible it is to get into a game that isn't majority children. I desperately wish there was a way to play with just adults. Among Us VR is not fun at all unless you can gather a group of older people interested in playing. It's also very difficult to seriously play this version as impostor. Because of proximity chat, if you chase someone they can just scream out your colour as they're running, and players are more likely to group up than in the original game. It's also harder to know who's looking since you can't see around you at all times.On top of all of this, Among Us VR doesn't include the new colours added to the original game, and there aren't many cosmetics in the game at all. The cosmetics they do have are sold as part of cosmetic packs instead of being included in free cosmicubes like in the original. I hope more maps and more free cosmetics are added in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore the reviews that complain about lobbies being filled with children. The game is just plain bad.There is one map. You can't customize any lobby settings. The tasks are somehow even more boring and uncreative than in the normal game. Opening a private lobby to the public just doesn't work, so you can't play with friends unless you have enough to fill the lobby. The game is incredibly buggy and crashes often. _childDocuments_.review: It's the usual among us affair, but, with proximity chat and being able to show more expressions with hand gestures makes this game way more interesting, in a way that made me prefer the VR version over the normal version. This game is definitely worth the price, but I'd recommend that you and your friends gather up for some rounds.
_childDocuments_.name: Among Us VR

_childDocuments_.review: Movement can be laggy, there's no settings for the lobby host, while some tasks transition well into vr most if not all of them have been simplified to the point where you can do it with your eyes closed or just flail your hands at it until you finish. To make matters worse, there's no server browser so if you don't have more than at least 5 people willing to start up a server with you its almost impossible for two people to get into the same lobby as each other. While I've had fun with this game it should be considered early access on steam because it feels like playing an alpha build of the game instead of a finished product. While there are a lot of problems with the game, it is still a fun time with friends and I'd gladly change this to positive if fixes start to come out sometime soon.

I would guess the servers are being overloaded since it is day one, it probably will be better later.Other than server issues, the game is missing some kind of push to talk function. I'm not always alone in the room I play, and sometimes I want to talk to family members but not in the game.Smooth turning speed could also be faster. IMO it's not quite fast enough even at maximum speed.Good start, but I guess it needs a couple more updates.

_childDocuments_.review: I recently had the opportunity to play Among Us in virtual reality (VR), and it was an absolutely fantastic experience. Among Us was already an engaging and popular game, but the transition to VR takes it to a whole new level. Here are some of the reasons why I thoroughly enjoyed playing Among Us in VR:Immersive Gameplay: Among Us VR truly immerses you in the game's world. You're not just controlling a character on a screen; you become a crewmember aboard a spaceship. The feeling of being physically present in the game's environment adds an exciting layer of immersion.Social Interaction: Among Us has always been a social game that's best enjoyed with friends, and VR amplifies this aspect. You can see and interact with your fellow players as if you were in the same room, making it feel like a true social experience.Realistic Tasks: Completing tasks in VR is surprisingly satisfying. Whether you're fixing wires, swiping a card, or emptying trash, the physicality of the tasks enhances the gameplay and makes them more enjoyable.Impostor Experience: Being an impostor in Among Us VR is an adrenaline rush. Sneaking around the spaceship, sabotaging systems, and trying to deceive your friends feels even more exhilarating when you can see their reactions up close.Stunning Environments: The VR version of Among Us features detailed 3D environments that look great in virtual reality. It's a pleasure to explore the ship's various rooms, and the added depth adds to the feeling of being on a real spaceship.

_childDocuments_.review: At the day of launch (Nov. 10), this game is very clearly incomplete. Movement is buggy and unintuitive, even when switched to head-based movement. There are no lobby settings like in the base game. There is only one map, the original from the base game, and it is very barebones. Key mechanics such as the surveillance camera system have been removed, even though the room they were in remains. Tasks will auto-adjust your camera/view, but more often than not will face you away from what you are looking at, requiring you to then manually adjust yourself. Matchmaking is incredibly buggy, sometimes you will get a match, and other times you will get a black screen of nothing, but with audible footsteps as if there were players in the lobby you couldn't see, only to be booted back to the main menu after about a minute. Cosmetic items that were free in the original game are now paid DLC. Many reviewers will also cite the game's clearly very young playerbase in their negative reviews, but I feel that was truly unavoidable and was present in the original, it's just way more apparent and annoying now that their is proximity voice-chat (no push to talk option though). Given that this is launch day, I imagine that a lot of the technical/QOL issues will be ironed out soon, but as it stands right now this is an incomplete product that definitely would have benefited from more time in the oven.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game! With friends or in a random lobby!Before I go on with reasons why here is my overall rating, 8.8/10Essentially the game is the same as regular Among Us ( Wow what a surprise ) but with VR mechanics! My personal big downside with the original Among Us is that it was WAY too easy for the type of game it was going for being. Adding VR to the mix really brings out the hard thinking moments in people to try and figure out exactly who the impstor(s) is, not only does VR make the game harder for crewmates but for the impostors too!As of typing this review out ( 2 hours after release ) there is only 1 map which I'm aware of so the amount of "content" in the game is definitely not as filled as the original game which has 4 maps I believe which I'm certain this VR adaptation will get more maps as time goes on.The UI is very nice to move around in and feels decently smooth, as an impostor it can be difficult to close doors/sabotage as the buttons will at some points glitch and you have to keep pressing until you get it. And more difficult tasks, be it simon says, the card swipe, or any thing like that could be practiced. In Among Us VR there is no practice mode, you can only learn the map and the tasks while in the full game. This is particullary problematic with some of the new tasks, like the new engine room one, that are hard to do and you can't really practice them as you are either killed or some sort of sabotage is going on preventing you learning.2 ) Lack of options. _childDocuments_.review: Decent VR game to come this year but needs A LOT of work with simple matchmaking and reporting functions. Before getting into the real issues of this game you will have to wait over 5 minutes to get into a lobby and then, possibly, longer than that for the match to start. There are lot of trolls that'll get host and simply not start the match or play some game to kick people they don't want before they start. The servers are not on the West coast which has resulted in connection issues: kicked mid match, can't connect at all, jumbling of movement and audio. But the real issues of Among Us VR is the lack of community moderation and report functions. People have, obviously, noticed and taken advantage of the anonymity the game gives them. The most racist, sexist, and homophobic statements I've heard in my 20+ years of gaming I have heard within my nearly 7 hours of playing this game. It is truly disgusting that the developers would make this game knowing a large portion of the people playing it would be children and not implement ANY report function or way to trace people back to their Steam, Facebook, whatever, account. I've heard seemly very young kids told they're going to be decapitated, their moms would be sexually assaulted, insanely racist things I'm not going to type out, if you can imagine the most vile thing you could say to inflict harm on a younger person it was probably said. All this to say: FIX YOUR GAME. The game can be fun and in the rare instance I got into a normal lobby and had people that wanted to play the game, I had a good time. But, that was so rare I wouldn't actually say that is what people are getting when deciding to buy and play this. If you're a parent deciding to buy your kid this: pay attention to what is happening in the game and moderate your child. I would just not recommend this to anyone that is looking for a positive gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: If you really like the VR chat version and want an upgrade, or just want among us in VR, this is a surprisingly good game. It does, however, like most modern games feel incomplete. Why's this?Well to start, there's only one map, skeld. But it translates very well to VR, and feels much larger than I would think it to be comparing it to the original. The lighting and art style for this game is overall very fitting and brings a better and more real feeling tone to among us(somehow). Honestly though, I do wish they included one other map to add some variety.The settings for each round are also non-existent, unless its changing the lobby from private to public and the other way around. There's no changing the kill cooldown(which is 40+ seconds btw), no discussion or voting time adjustments, nothing. There's also none of those special roles like medic, engineer, and shapeshifter. Even more sickening are the variety of hats, there's barely any! This is the bare-bones of among us in virtual reality. Which is not a a bad thing for the most part, it's still very fun, but also incomplete.I have not yet played a public lobby, as of writing this, last night I played some private lobbies with my friends and this may actually be the most fun I've had on a VR game since I first played BONEWORKS awhile ago. There's proximity voice chat in this game, and it's a ton of fun. Crossplay is a thing for this game, I obviously played this one PC while most of friend were on quest 2 and everything except the VC worked pretty fine, some bugs here and there but not exactly game-breaking. I assume that because it's also on quest 2, you're gonna unfortunately get a lot of young children in public lobbies(honestly I'm too scared to find out for myself), but you can mute individual players or turn off VC entirely. There is also a text chat feature so if you don't got a mic or don't want to use yours, you should be good, though I don't know how functional it is cause I've never used it.Overall, if you wanna play it and have the cash to do so, go ahead. And if you don't like it, just remember there's a refund option if you've played it for less than 3 hours within the timespan of 2 weeks.

_childDocuments_.review: This is literally like the dumbest possible implementation of a really simple concept. So first off, the game is turning the guardian grid of the Index off. Like, you can never be sure if you are about to punch or run into a wall if you move physically. Why does the game do that? No idea.Than the movement in the game is so dumb it is not even funny. It is the standard push the thumbstick forward to walk into the direction your left hand is pointing at. What we used  to call Onward controls. But that unlike every other VR game (well, any VR game on PC or Quest) the game only uses the controller direction once when you start to move but isn't updating it once you are moving. So to walk a curve you literally need to stop, turn and then start to move again. Again, no idea why the game is doing that.And while the game has so little hardware demand that it runs easily at even 144hz with super high numbers of super sampling (no ingame option...) as evident by the frame time meter of Steam VR and the general smoothness of hand motions etc, when moving to objects like the button terminals those stutter. Doesn't matter if I run 144, 120 or 90hz and it isn't reprojecting. It just seems like some weird stutter of the camera while moving around. Not super noticeable but still.

_childDocuments_.review: A new way to be Sus, seriously VR refreshes everything about Among Us typical gameplay loop, in a brilliant manner, the new tasks are challenging enough to be anxiety inducing (like Face Scan, or Motor's levers), the way you can point and blame your fellow crewmates with proximity voice chat is amazing, and above all, the first person point of view gives a wicked twist to the game, it's free paranoia. A very nice VR game, simple yet effective.Right now I only have 2 real issues with this game, one is that the lobby system is extremely simplistic, no server browser or friend system (if they add one you should call it "Crewmate list", it has to be), just Quick Play, Host, and Direct Join (with lobby code), so you can't really choose what kind of lobby do you want to join (+18 for example) and you have to rely on Discord to coordinate games, the other is that there's a lack of content compared to flat screen Among Us, I'm sure it'll get updated eventually, but right now, you only have 1 map, and a few hats, and that's it, no pets, no roles, no body accessories.It's worth the price at it's current state? Yeah, it feels like a complete game nonetheless, and hopefully they'll implement all of the OG Among Us content back in the future, so, You want to lie to other people in space? Then buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Good review because i Hit the griddy and people didnt vote me out because of itThe game is exactly what you expect, but less. Don't get me wrong i enjoy the game, and the proximity chat for a game as simple as VR among us is worth the low price, BUT its more expensive than the original, with a smaller player community, ONE map, and the removed the tasks that would be MOST fun for VR like asteroids and the ability to watch Cameras, its incredibly simple and for that reason it feels plain.. additionally no one expected the 13+ age requirement would do anything, but its completely filled with 7 year olds at best, now sometimes that creates funny moments but children and proximity chat is just absolute chaos with no end, again while sometimes funny, i do wish among us VR would add an age preference on lobbies so it wasn't blatantly a day care. Among us has come so far in so few years but this game feels like the first stage of among us on mobile, you currently cannot search servers, you cannot do many tasks, customization has less options, server settings DO NOT exist, you just press quick play and that's it. its very buggy (which is honestly fine) but all of this together makes me leave this review that you are not buying among us VR, you are buying an early access game that in not listed as such.

_childDocuments_.review: If the host leaves, the game ends. So kill the host and your turn as imposter is over, and its back to searching for a new lobby.You cannot easily group with friends.  This involves joining many lobbies hoping for space, hoping you give your friend the code in time before it fills or starts, hoping the host doesnt just leave, and hoping that no game bugs are stopping you.  Sometimes the quick match puts you into your own lobby, and I've never had anyone else join.Among Us, and by extension Among Us VR are very good games in theory. There just needs to be some work to make it more consistently enjoyable.Would like to see:The host switch to someone else when the current host leaves. (the fact that this doesn't happen is the main reason why I do not recommend this game.)The option to avoid joining a solo lobby, even if that means waiting a bit longer.The option to join groups and then queue together.aspects of the non vr game, such as 15 players, shapeshifters, engineers, custom settings such as kill cd, quantity of tasks, etc (preferrably not movement speed)

_childDocuments_.review: Disregarding public lobbies and fanbases (as most games can have this used against them generically), this game is REALLY good.If you have a VR headset and an hour to spare a whole 10 bucks for, this is worth it!As someone who heavily enjoyed the original Among Us, I'm surprised at the effort and detail put into this.What's that? Has one map? Shut up! Be greatful that we got a small great game instead of a huge soulless game.Seriously, roam around the ship and check out places like the storage room's ceiling. (after you've done tasks)Issues:- My Rift S's input breaks if I screw around with my buttons (even by accident) outside of lobbies or games. (I had rebooted my game THREE TIMES to initially play) The solution? Boot up the game in Oculus mode. This severely limits the bug's sudden appearance for me.- Hands are a little wonky and sometimes don't look correct to other people, or just feel unresponsive. It's mostly visual.- Names are getting cut off in the game for players without names hidden.- Sometimes I'm thrown back into a game with indefinite loading screens just to be thrown to the menus 2 minutes later. One solution is to just join a new lobby every time. Seems less common.- VC seems to have some odd effect on alive crewmembers despite me also being alive. (Reminds me of Fruity Flanger from FL Studio) The only time this doesn't happen is when you and the person you're talking to are both dead.- Vents are unresponsive and feel a little.... underdeveloped. I can't describe it, but it isn't fluid enough to feel like it wasn't thrown together by ForteBass (or whoever) in 3 minutes with a black screen. What i'd recommend for vent swapping is to have the player's camera crawl back a little during the fade and play a small vent crawling sound. Same for the vent you enter but in the opposite order. It'd make it feel more responsive, but have it happen in less than 2.5 seconds.- The quick chat menu is very unclear or unaccessible for people who need it. I wasn't aware it was there until I had opened the map and realized a chat button was there well into over an hour and a half of the game. Perhaps make a preview of quick chat appear somewhere in the meetings near or next to the screen. Alternatively, have a button appear above the meeting button you can press to open up right to it.- Ghosts can't pass through walls, kind of defeating the point for me. I will give credit where it's due, though. You might give someone a seizure with the polygons being thrown through the headset, so maybe just make door locks transparent so you can walk to them at the bare minimum.

_childDocuments_.review: Among us VR is the best adaptation for the original 2d game so far. There are many cheaper alternatives to among us vr, but this is the one that has the most optimal and confortable vr experience. Unfortunatly, this game does not yet have anywhere near the amount of customisability as the original game. You cannot change anything about game mechanics, and have very limited customisation options compared to the original game. In addition to this, some of the stratagy of the original game has been removed, as at this point in time, there are no cameras. Dispite this, I still consider this game worth the money, provided it gets future content updates.

_childDocuments_.review: Whereas Among Us provides a top down view, Among Us VR provides a fully immersive first person experience. It is full of chaotic goodness, trying to eliminate the crewmates and ejecting the impostors. Of course, there is a lot of finger pointing going on (literally), so make sure to choose your friends carefully. Who knows who's standing behind you while you do your tasks after all.I have thoroughly enjoyed the games that I've played so far. It is to be expected, but the game carries a lot of younger players. So if you'd still like to play with others but not the youngsters, then I recommend you look for some friends that have VR and get together for a custom match. The task minigames are all interactive, and therefore highly enjoyable, just like the killing of crewmates.So if you like chaotic screaming at each other, pointing fingers and snapping necks. This game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I actually enjoyed my time with this game. With that being said, you can pretty much experience everything this game has to offer within the first hour of play. My main issue at the moment is the lack of content in comparison to the base Among Us game and lacking fundamental features, such as the account system. This is a game I would recommended wish listing for now and wait for a few more updates to not only iron out the bugs present at launch but to dig your teeth into more content.
_childDocuments_.name: Among Us VR

_childDocuments_.review: The game code feels like it's held together by duct tape and hot glue. Filling the taskbar doesn't let the crewmates win, the host keeps disconnecting, walking up to any task causes you to clip into the nearest wall which resets your playspace 90 times a second giving you a seizure, some trivial things are completely missing from the game (like comms and security), default settings are designed by someone who has never played a VR game in their life, reporting a dead body takes 30 seconds for it to even register, tabbing out causes your controls to stop working, anything that isn't an Oculus controller is barely supported, and the very first word I heard in the very first round I played happened to be one that starts with an N and rhymes with TiggerOverall 10/10 experience those were the funniest 87 minutes of my life

_childDocuments_.review: Got motion sickness and merk'd by squeakers - but when you find a group of adults the game is fun10/10On a serious note-Those who are leaving negative reviews expect video games to be perfect at launch. Yes this game is a little rough at the moment lobby wise, but it is still fun nevertheless. I am sure these features will be implemented eventually, but the game needs the following:-Custom match selection + match names (I want to pick my lobby, not join children)-Custom game settings (killer cool down, how many impostors, etc)-Kicking option/report option for toxic players saying slurs-mic only matches, no chat. Force everyone to have mics-Cameras don't work and some tasks are missing-1 map only-limited dlc hats (why can't we have pets yet too? :(   (my hamster)-Teleport movement option for my VR motion sickness homies like me ((you are valid, ilysm))-Chat option is bugged and players text don't show up but the msg bubbles do-I have been disconnected and forced to be a host when I try joining someone elses game which is annoying. Rather be taken straight to the game menu instead-The simon says task in reactor breaks if someone else completes it-I want my hands to show in game FFS - I keep head patting people who can't see my HANDS while the match is going on-Option to toggle player visibility if they're in your personal space. Sometimes I wan't someone to dab me up without them vanishing for being too close-I am sure there is more but I am too tiredOverall the game is more playable/enjoyable than Cyberpunks launch, it's just missing some features I believe Devs will add eventually because it is so new and the gaming industry sucks. Love ya devs!

_childDocuments_.review: Best version of Among Us. Tasks in VR just feel great, and proximity chat is a welcoming addition. Very fun with friends, pubs are okay if you don't mind the annoyances of the children (depends on how you feel, could be either laughable or infuriating). It's also only ten bucks.The only issue with this game is its lack of content so far, none of the 5 other colors and only the Skeld so far, so it's basically an early access game. Nevertheless, I'm sure it'll get better overtime.

_childDocuments_.review: Actually a good game. One of the games I played involved me (as the impostor) and 4 other people. Someone "heard a dead body" that didn't exist, and after another dude walked by I made one and accidentally self reported. The entire rest of the game was spent with an argument between the "heard a dead body" guy and the dude who walked past me. I'm talking hysterical arguments where they both said the other was the impostor. They never suspected it was me even in their final moments. This game recaptured that special magic Among Us had when I originally played it. If you don't have this game you're not even real anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 27.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ing minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

_childDocuments_.review: Among Us VR – Betrayal, Teamwork, and Virtual Shenanigans 🚀👾So you think you can trust your friends in space? Think again! Among Us VR takes all the backstabbing, betrayal, and frantic task-completion of the classic 2D version and adds a whole new level of chaos—literally, since now you’re inside the spaceship. 🛸Let’s be real: it’s not quite as smooth as the 2D original or the VRChat version, but that doesn’t stop it from being a ridiculously fun time. The level of deception you can pull off in VR is mind-blowing! You can literally pretend to be fixing wires while you’re silently plotting someone’s demise, and no one will know until it’s too late. Plus, walking around and pretending to be the innocent crewmate, all while being a cold-hearted impostor, is far more satisfying when you can look your victims in the eye—well, virtually. 👀🔪The best part? It’s a blast with friends. There’s nothing quite like hearing your friend’s voice crack as they try to explain why they weren’t near the body, all while you watch them fumble through their VR hand movements trying to cover up their tracks. It's chaotic, it's funny, and sometimes, it’s a little too real when you’re the one being ejected into space. 😆🪐While it might not dethrone the 2D classic or VRChat’s version of space betrayal, Among Us VR still delivers an amazing experience. It’s perfect for laughs, chaos, and a healthy amount of distrust among your friends. Will you survive, or will you be the next to be tossed out the airlock? Find out and prepare for some hilarious moments in space! 🚀💀Created with <3

_childDocuments_.review: Take the following into consideration. TL;DR at the bottom. The game is functional, but barely so. The animated graphics are so fun and the ambiance is great, but the game-play is just the same as regular Among Us. On top of that, Among Us (North American servers) is filled mostly with 6 to 9 year-old children, the occasional inappropriate weeaboo (and potentially dangerous people now that I think about it-), and internet pranksters. You have a grand total of 12 color options for your character and maybe 10 options for hats. No pets, no login, no cosmetics for that $10 price tag. The tasks have been revamped beautifully to work in VR, each one being almost completely different, but there are 0 options that you can customize for your lobby, is limited to 10 people, and the only map that exists is the Skeld. Reminder, this is a $10 version of an originally free game. Basically the only thing that you're paying for is just the ability walk around 3D models. Proximity voice chat also exists, but you can get it for regular Among Us for free, but they can pose a danger to young children; the majority of the ones who play the game. TL;DR: No, unless you only enjoy the bare bones version of Among Us and don't hate children.

It's extremely frustrating after playing for 30 to 60 minutes, getting the Impostor role, just to see a server error.Also, don't get to comfortable with the people you play with, the game lobby could collapse any minute and you will never see them again... There's also a bug where you don't hear anybody talking, voice is not being transmitted and I can hear nothing. It fixes itself when I leave the lobby and join a totally different game...The only playable map, Skeld, is currently not finished and (imho) vital elements of the map like the camera room are unfinished and not functioning as expected. I hope more will be done, and more maps will be added someday, maybe next year?All in all, this is an "ok" game for die-hard Among Us fans who like proximity chat with many loud children, most of them without critical thinking skills.I won't refund this game, but I do not see myself playing this again anytime soon. I wish it was different, but I can't enjoy the game in its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: Among Us is already a fairly simple game technically, but that simplicity is translated to VR really well. _childDocuments_.review: Among Us is a 2018 online multiplayer social deduction game developed and published by American game studio Innersloth. The game was inspired by the party game Mafia and the science fiction horror film The Thing. The game allows for cross-platform play, first released on iOS and Android devices in June 2018 and on Windows later that year in November. The game was then ported to the Nintendo Switch in December 2020, and on the PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox One and Xbox Series X/S in December 2021. While the game was initially released in 2018 to little mainstream attention, it received a massive influx of popularity in 2020 due to many well-known Twitch streamers and YouTubers playing it. A separate VR version of the game, Among Us VR, was released in November 2022Among Us takes place in space-themed settings where players are colorful armless cartoon astronauts; Each player takes on one of two roles: most are Crewmates, but a small number play Impostors, which appear identical to Crewmates. The goal of the Crewmates is to either identify and vote out the Impostors, or to complete all the tasks around the map; the goal of the Impostors is to covertly sabotage the mission either by killing the Crewmates before they complete all their tasks or by triggering a disaster that is not resolved in time.

_childDocuments_.review: Hilarity in Space: A Side-Splitting Saga of SuspicionRating: ★★★★★ (5/5)Prepare yourself for a rollercoaster of laughter and deceit in the cosmos with Among Us, the game that turns friendships into funny frenemies! If you're looking for a dose of laughter-induced stomach cramps, this game is the ultimate prescription. Here's why Among Us will leave you clutching your sides in mirth:Space Detective Academy:Among Us turns ordinary crewmates into interstellar Sherlock Holmes wannabes, piecing together evidence with all the grace of a herd of clumsy penguins. Watching players bumble around trying to solve murders is like witnessing a troupe of comedians auditioning for a slapstick routine. Who needs a magnifying glass when you have a crewmate mistaking a vent for a portal to Narnia?The Art of Accusations:If you thought politicians were masters of deception, wait until you see your friends try to defend their innocence in Among Us. It's a symphony of excuses, alibis, and finger-pointing that would put even the most skilled lawyers to shame. Accusing someone of venting feels like presenting evidence in court, except here it's more like a wild improv session where truth takes a backseat and hilarity takes the wheel.Double Trouble:Ah, the joys of being an imposter! Sneaking around, sabotaging tasks, and trying to blend in while your heart pounds like a drum set on steroids. The imposter's struggles are as entertaining as watching a monkey try to solve a Rubik's Cube. Their attempts at mimicking innocent tasks end up being as subtle as a bull in a china shop. It's pure comedy gold when they accidentally vent right in front of an unsuspecting crewmate, sending everyone into fits of laughter.Emergency Meetings Gone Wild:Among Us transforms simple meetings into full-blown comedy sketches. Picture a group of friends trying to establish democracy in space, but instead, they create a circus of chaos and confusion. Emergency meetings turn into a whirlwind of accusations, wild theories, and accidental self-incrimination that would make even the Three Stooges proud.Cosmic Fashion Faux Pas:The game allows players to dress up their characters in all sorts of outrageous outfits. From unicorn hats to traffic cones on heads, it's like a fashion show hosted by aliens with questionable taste. Watching these oddly attired beings run around, desperately trying to complete tasks, is a visual feast that adds an extra layer of absurdity to the already hilarious gameplay.Conclusion:Among Us is a game that serves up more laughs than a stand-up comedy marathon. Its combination of comical gameplay mechanics, wacky accusations, and cosmic shenanigans make it an absolute riot. Just remember, if you find yourself clutching your stomach in fits of laughter, don't blame the game—blame your friends for being hilarious suspects. Grab your spacesuit, gather your friends, and get ready for the laughter-filled adventure of a lifetime!Thank you for all your hard workWith love,Addilyn Bazeele

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun! It's a new way to play Among Us and it's interesting enough to be worth the super low 8€ asking price. However, the fact that it's in VR is really not as game changing as the developers want it to be. The biggest change from the original Among Us game is the proximity chat and that could have been achieved in the original game with a simple patch. It couldn't have been that difficult to implement as there are already mods that support proximity chat in the original game. That being said, I will admit that the meetings are a bit more interesting with voice chat and VR gestures and having new VR based tasks does add a bit of variety, but that new variety goes away literally after you've done each task once and the voice chat based meetings are not THAT different from just joining an Among Us Discord server and playing the game with voice chat.I did run into one bug, where a dead body stayed in electrical and anyone was able to report it in all the games in that same lobby, but that could have been a fluke. If it was 25€, forget about it, but for 8€, it's a steal. Also I feel like the game will be alive for a long time, because the game supports crossplay with Meta headsets and for them, this is one of the best games they can get, as their puny systems don't support Alyx without a gaming PC and they cannot mod Beat Saber to get custom songs and stop that game from being painfully mundane.It's still a positive rating though, because of the incredibly low price and the effort that went into this game, which despite some crucial missing options in the lobby settings, seems pretty well optimized and balanced.

_childDocuments_.review: Played a good bit this last weekend, the game translates to VR surprisingly well.The base game of course is amazing, that's why it became a phenomenon, the VR version is slightly simplified (4 buttons for Simon Says, bicycle pump for leaves, etc).     This is probably due to how awkward it can be to do things in a seated VR environment.The tradeoff is great though.    Running through hallways in the dark isn't a circle of "blind past this point", it's a dropoff of light where you can see silhouettes off a good ways but ID'ing is hard till you're close.    There's a lot more viceral "who's behind me!?" that you don't have in the regular game, and you hear voices the whole time with distance dropoff, including kills behind closed doors.   Very well done.

Not many players seem to be active on this game either despite it being on all platforms which is disappointing, but I mean afterall what do you expect, it is literally just Among Us but on VR. that game hasn't been doing well for a while now so I don't see why this would either unless the game suddenly becomes trending again, but I don't know if that will happen as this is on VR and there are still a lot of people out there that see VR as a gimmick or not worth it.Keep in mind, this game has been in development for a year and it's a shame how lacking this port is. Overtime I'm hoping Innersloth will pump out more updates if this game actually does well and will have all the features it's Non-VR counterpart does. For it being almost half the price as the original and only has half the features, it isn't worth it right now and should have a price cut because of that and also because buying a VR or/and PC to play VR on is already expensive enough.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know if this just affected me, but the controls were virtually unplayable. My controller would get stuck vibrating permanently whenever I'd interact with some task or another and I'd have to open and close the settings to fix it. Whenever I walk into the circle of a task, the game flips me around and away from it, and the directional controls become really weird if you turn using your actual body, so disorienting... Sometimes, the footstep sounds would get stuck, and sometimes they wouldn't play at all.I'm a long-term VR player and these controls feel very amateurish, I hope they'll look into these issues and fix them in the future.Edit: A developer asked me to provide more details in a bug report, I've now done so and hope they can fix these issues!

_childDocuments_.review: It will only show 14 minutes of playtime for the Steam version of this game but I played a few more rounds on the Quest 2 and decided to give a review not to sway anyone or change opinions but instead just give my own opinion on it. First I believe a review should not tell you to not buy or purchase the game but form your own opinion by your own individual experience. The game itself is FAR better than the VRchat version, While only released, it showed that it was more immersive with tasks and following people around while dead. I won't continue to compare this one to the VRchat version but I will say those are the two things that stood out to me. It's nice to have the Wardrobe option in this version as well so we can all have our uniqueness but it lack clothes for the body which I hope will be in a future update.  The menu UI is easy to navigate as well as the map when looking for tasks. Everything about this version sucked me back into the constant arguments, fighting, and screaming, "IT WASN'T ME". I love this version but I'll let you decide for yourself :)

_childDocuments_.review: Never played amogus in my life -- here's my first impressions.TL;DR -- Minimal 'bugs' and slightly-bad imposter implementations. Loud, screaming, migraine-inducing lobbies. Add an 18+ queue with vote-kick capabilities. Overall opinion: very fun and social game with infinite repeatability, and the ability to form friendships and ruin them at the same time - 100% worth $10, especially for VR.Simple, fun, and it works. However, a bit clunky as of now. Game doesn't work if the window is not focused on your PC, doing tasks snap-turns you according to your IRL direction (can be very disorienting), and playing as imposter can be just plain-obvious due to its implementation. Only these few issues, and they're easy to fix!The biggest 'issue' for me? Imposter. Being an imposter can be very, very difficult to hide; unintentionally. When doing fake tasks, if you don't automatically 'snap-turn' like everyone else then you've already given yourself away. Or when you're trying to sabotage, standing still and having to click on your mini-map can't be any more obvious - why? Because nobody but imposters have to click their mini-map for anything.The 'fix' for these issues? Well, first off, don't force users to snap-turn and teleport into tasks when performing them. And to sabotage? Maybe put them near tasks to create the 'illusion' of you performing something useful!Additions? 18+ lobbies and vote-kick options for them. I'm not one to complain about age-groups in VR, but in this game you might as well say goodbye to your eardrums. Screaming, squeaking, music, footsteps - all the ingredients to a migraine and loss-of-hearing. 18+ lobbies are a necessity for this game; especially after reading countless reviews about it myself. And how do we enforce it? Add the ability to vote-kick users that may have faked their age to enter an '18+ queue'.Just my own personal nit-picking and user-friendly fixes; but the game is fun. Put up with these very minimal issues, and you have a simple, social, fun game of deception.

_childDocuments_.review: Among US VR is one of the best social deduction games because it allows players to directly interact with one another in a virtual space. This allows for a more immersive experience that can help players become more invested in the game. Additionally, the game features a number of mechanics that encourage social interaction, such as the need to discuss suspicions and the ability to accused other players of being the impostor. The spatial audio during game play  also furthers the feeling of presence and immersiveness. However,  some players may find the game to be too intense or anxiety-inducing due to the constant need to be aware of one's surroundings and the possibility of being accused or attacked by other players. Overall,  Among US VR is a great social deduction game that offers a unique and immersive experience.

name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY
detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition This product is a Digital Deluxe Edition, a bundle that contains the game and the TRIANGLE STRATEGY Mini-Artbook (digital download). (The TRIANGLE STRATEGY Mini-Artbook (digital download) is an abridged version of TRIANGLE STRATEGY Design Works THE ART OF TRIANGLE 2018-2022. It comprises 20 pages, including character sketches of the eight members of the Wolffort house and a collection of pixel art.) 『TRIANGLE STRATEGY DIGITAL DELUXE EDITION』+『VARIOUS DAYLIFE』Bundle To commemorate the release of TRIANGLE STRATEGY and VARIOUS DAYLIFE, the two games are now available as a bundle! ■Bundle content ・TRIANGLE STRATEGY DIGITAL DELUXE EDITION: (Includes TRIANGLE STRATEGY game software & TRIANGLE STRATEGY mini-artbook (digital download)) ・VARIOUS DAYLIFE game software About the Game Three mighty powers have long waged war on the great continent of Norzelia. This land bears a long and scarred history that includes the Saltiron War, a war that erupted over control of salt and iron resources. A balance of power has been achieved between the Holy State of Hyzante, which controls the salt, the Grand Dutchy of Aesfrost, a land of iron clad in frost and snow, and the forested Kingdom of Glenbook, which lies nestled between the other two powers. However, a certain incident shakes the balance between these three powers, which then begins to crumble away... The player's sense of justice will be tested in the face of convictions. Various actions and choices within the game will build up to form your conviction, based on three sets of values - Utility, Morality, and Liberty. This will affect your path through the story and which allied units will join your cause. Voting Important decisions that will decide the fate of the protagonist and his allies will be determined through a vote using the Scales of Conviction. For the player to assert their own opinion, they must convince their allies. Choices with a profound impact on the destinies of the group will likewise have a major impact on the story. Highly strategic battles It will be crucial to use the terrain and differences in elevation to position yourself advantageously. Enjoy satisfying and challenging battles and strategy with great depth: with the ability to select from characters with uniquely different traits in your party formation, and gameplay systems that allow flanking the enemy to perform follow-up attacks or using your allies' abilities to coordinate attacks. Converse with and strengthen your allies in the Encampment In the Encampment, you can speak with allied characters and purchase goods from shops. You can also strengthen your characters and weapons at the Sundry Shop and the Smithy. Additionally, once you've strengthened your characters, you can put their strength to the test at the Tavern by taking part in Mental Mock Battles. These battles range from standard combat to those with somewhat unique victory conditions, allowing you to enjoy Triangle Strategy's combat on an even deeper level.

_childDocuments_.review: The game might be good, but it is not intended to be played with a mouse or keyboard and requires a beefier machine than it's graphics would suggest. - When navigating menus that would normally have a dropdown (e.g., resolution), menu items need to be moused-over and then selected with arrow keys. Left clicking exits the menu with a confirmation to save and right clicking exits the menu without saving. - The overworld map is navigated using a targeting reticle chases the true mouse cursor at a fixed speed. The true mouse cursor is not visible, and is also not constrained to the window and so can pass onto your second monitor in borderless fullscreen mode. - The has minor frame drops on mid-range (10th gen Intel CPU/2060 Nvidia card) hardware. Edit: Having now finished the game, here are my extended thoughts.For the right person, the game is good and is worth the $30 (sale) asking price and your time. Character customization is limited, but this is fine because the cast of characters is large and every character is unique. The tactical gameplay is fun, but not groundbreaking -- extremely similar to Final Fantasy Tactics or Tactics Ogre, but with fewer skills, higher hit rates, and minimal friendly fire. The writing is good, but 60-70% of the game is spent in cutscenes. My guess is that the majority of people who do not enjoy this game did not enjoy it for this reason. The player gets to make meaningful and non-obvious choices throughout the course of a playthrough. That being said, the set of decisions that are required for the "true" ending are not hinted at in any way, and my guess is that the majority of players who want the good ending do it on a subsequent playthrough with a guide. The animations in the cutscenes take too long and adversely affect the pacing. For instance, there is a "..." animation that plays above a character's head during some cutscenes that takes 7-8 seconds to finish. Unnecessary animations that could be completely removed without damaging the game extend the length of cutscenes by 10-15%. Voice acting is mostly good, with a few jarring exceptions. I have been told that the Japanese voice acting is better than the English voice acting, but I prefer to hear voice acting in a language that I can understand so YMMV. There is some mandatory exploration which involves hunting for hidden items and talking to all of the NPCs which I did not enjoy. All of the exploration scenes together constitute maybe 60-80 minutes of gameplay in a roughly 30 hour campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of FFT, so I came in wanting to scratch that old, insatiable itch. Honestly though, its just sooooo much story and exposition. Easily over 50% of the game is dialog, cutscenes and reading. And not particularly interesting at that. I'm not kidding when I say it's more of a visual novel than a tactics game. So far there has been at least like 3 or 4 drawn-out cutscenes and an exploration phase (which involves a lot of talking with NPCs) in-between each actual fight. I will continue playing for now just to give it a chance but I feel like these devs have never heard of the phrase "show, don't tell"
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: Listen. This game has a LOOOOT of dialogue, cutscenes, exposition, etc. A lot of the bad reviews point this out, I don't think this aspect of the game is inherently bad by any means, it just isn't for everybody. If you really enjoy RPGs, especially strategy based ones like Fire Emblem or Final Fantasy Tactics, and you don't mind spending lots of time immersing yourself in a world and learning about its characters, you will LOVE this game. It is not a game for everyone but it is otherwise an EXCELLENT experience if it is indeed up your alley.Just do yourself a favor and use the Japanese voices. Serenoa's English voice actor must not have been given context or something, he sounds out of place in most of his lines and it really does hurt the experience. Everyone else sounds really good in English, so I wonder what happened there?
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: Played and beat this on the Nintendo switch so most of my experience with the game play and story is from that version.Triangle Strategy is the story of Serenoa the son of one of the 3 major nobles who has to navigate dangerous politics were everyone has an agenda and everyone lies; while also dealing with uphill battles against increasing high stakes odds.The game features many branching paths which follow the themes of morality, liberty and pragmatism as well as NG+ which allows for different playthroughs with different routes, decisions and endings.The battle system in game terms is roughly like the battles systems from Final Fantasy Tactics and Tactics Ogre so grid based with a turn order which is displayed at the bottom of the screen which allows for further planning of actions.The characters are all set characters so no generic characters like in Final Fantasy Tactics but each character has a unique set of skills along with a 3 tier upgrade system which is reminiscent of Vandal Hearts and Shining Force.PC options are pretty basic and if you play it is probably better played with a controller as the PC layout is very cumbersome and demands of you to use the keyboard mostly instead of the mouse for everything so be forewarned.After playing this I am proud to say that we finally have another strategy game that can sit among the big boys of Final Fantasy Tactics and Tactics Ogre (Which is also coming to PC this year) so if you like those games then definitely think about picking this one up.
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY
