_childDocuments_.review: So ill be honest, i didnt complete the game. i'm assuming i got near the end based on where the story was going. Id assume i had maybe 2 or 3 more missions to go. couldnt have been far off from the end anyway. But i just couldnt finish the game because for me too many of its late game missions are far too "puzzley" for my taste. Where youre kind of forced into doing battles in a very specific way in order to not lose. And im not a fan of having to save scum in games in general or having to otherwise reload saves multiple times over as well as replaying missions a million times until i finally get it right.For example the last mission i was one was a stealth mission. And if i didnt get to a certain point with all my units on the map with out alerting the guards and hold it (which felt impossible to do. i couldnt figure out how to not eventually alert the guards) a bunch of enemy units spawn in random places and it becomes nearly impossible to win at that point because just about every unit is elite. I will 100% still give this game a recommend though to anyone who likes turn based tactics rpg's like fire emblem or final fantasy tactics from back in the day or other games along those lines. The story is pretty solid and enjoyable in my opinion. Albeit kind of predictable in a lot of areas as it kind of plays out like a game of thrones kind of story. Still has some suprises though here and there even with that being said. The combat is slightly janky if youre using a mouse and keyboard so if you have a controller id recommend that over m+kb but it does still work if you do use mouse and keyboard. Its too bad it didnt hold my attention all the way through because i was really enjoying the game for the first 15 or 20 hours or so but just those puzzley missions that make you save scum and re load saves over and over and over until you finally get it right really loses my attention. And if you also dont like that in games then id say tactics ogre reborn is the better way to go over this game and its roughly the same price.But if my few gripes dont bother you at all then id 100% recommend this game if you are already a fan of turn based tactics games or even if youre new to this genre this would be a great start. Also, i guess i should warn people that if you dont like stories in games and would rather skip every piece of dialogue, dont buy this game. Because you have to pay attention to the story in this game for a certain game mechanic and the first 8 hours or so is far more story focused than battle focused so if you just blast past dialogue in games id say this one isnt for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine Triangle Strategy to be a fusion of epic medieval saga in the style of The Song of Ice and Fire and anime/manga influences. Sounds weird? I thought so too but it actually works. Despite several shortcomings and rather dull and slow start, Triangle Strategy turned out to be a compelling drama with intriguing twists and turns in the story and a decent level of tactical battles. I would definitely recommend the fans of the TRPG genre to give it a chance and try to stick with it to the end - it's worth it.Also, if you have a Steam Deck, this game plays amazing on it.* Story is well thought out and brings a rather unique perspective on war on resources (I won't spoil more).* Some characters have a good depth and their dialogues delve well into the philosophical layer of morality, free will and following up on one's convictions, so the side story scenes don't always feel superficial or like a typical "anime fluff". * The game provides satisfactory closure at the end (the hidden true ending) but also leaves enough doors open for a potential sequel. * Battles are interesting with enough tactical layer to engage even veterans of the genre but not too complex to dissuade newbies.* Even though the ratio of story scenes and battles are about 50-50, the optional Mental Mock Battles are mostly fun and engaging, and can be done at any time.* There is some grind involved but it's not an overwhelming amount, and the XP system is designed well enough so that even under-levelled characters are able to catch up quickly with little amount of XP-grind.* The 2D-HD graphical rendition in Unreal Engine looks * Towards the end, the story likes to take some logical shortcuts that may leave a more keen player scratching their head a bit.* Not all character dialogues have the above mentioned depth and some characters are very shallow and uni-dimensional.* RPG elements and character development are rather limited. Stat boost and new abilities often feel pretty underwhelming.* I disliked the NG+ approach - the game doesn't give you any indication about your Morality, Liberty and Utility scores until you finish it at least once and then start a New Game plus. Meaning that lots of the content gets locked behind the requirement of multiple playthroughs. I would appreciate a more flexible approach, where after finishing the game I may simply return to a previous story junction, and choose one of the unexplored paths, instead of having to play * On Steam Deck with 60 FPS the game drains the battery pretty fast.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm 57 hours into this game.  I've been playing tactical RPGs my entire life.  The story on this one is pretty corny and honestly none of the characters have me hooked.  It's okay but not great.  The characters having unique classes is definitely a unique take on the genre.  Learning what combinations of characters to use in each battle is engaging and practicing in the encampment means all characters have a place.My greatest frustration is the uneccesary difficulty.  I'm 57 hours in and it feels like a slog.  I'm battling in the encampment constantly just to struggle in the story battles getting one shot by these crazy powerful enemies.  I am at Chapter 16 at the battle in the mines and I'm trying not to give up on this game.  Finally I realize I need to go tone down the difficulty.  So I sleep on it and return the next day.  I boot up the game and go to battle options.  I look at the difficulty.  It says Hard?What the hell?  Why would I have done that to myself?  Who invites that level of pain?  So I bump it down to Normal and play the next battle, a battle I played the night before and struggled.  Yep, smoked em.  I honestly feel a weight has been lifted.  I may yet enjoy the rest of the game... To be continued.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall really enjoyed it and would recommend with some caveats.PRO- Engaging storylines with meaningful decisions- Likeable protagonists with a strong amount of moral ambiguity- Replayability bc of the 1st point- Art style / character sprites- Preset difficulty options (this isn't standard in every TRPG)- UI that makes navigating the battlefield and potential outcomes well outlined CON- Length of battles- Lack of diversity in the way enemy AI approach you- Story content is great, there's just too much of itTo explain the Cons just a bit: I've decided I generally like TRPGs that deploy 5-6 units per side so the battle doesn't last 45-60 mins. I'd even prefer having to redo a battle 2-3x because there's much less margin for error with a smaller party (no deadweight, your mistakes can be more punishing etc) than just slugging through extremely long fights one after another.The length of battle is compounded even further by SE deciding to use the same strategy again and again in major battles to increase difficulty and it just gets predictable + really only serves to extend the fight. I would have preferred instead of always programming the same event, if they'd scaled how often enemy AI applies statuses (poison, taunt, sleep, stun, blind, charm) it could have presented a much more varied approach. As it stands I ended up feeling like I knew exactly what was about to happen by endgame, it was just a matter of time before I won.SE wrote the story and class masteries in a way that encourages, if not outright demands, a 2nd playthrough. I'm just wrapping up my 1st game and I'm around 48-50 hours. My appetite was really filled up around 35 hours so I'm just slogging through the end game. I'll eventually play a 2nd time after a decent break, I just think the way the story could have been slimmed down and some battles consist of only 5-6 characters for infiltration style missions.All in all good game if you can live w those critiques.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, a successor to FF Tactics it is not. - The plot wants to be political, and it even had potential, but unfortunately ends up resulting childish as it is constantly failed by *terrible* writing, with characters acting with very shallow motivations and/or making illogical decisions, paper villains that seem to be evil for no reason, and no character depth to be found anywhere, and everyone repeating the same thing as if they are spoon-feeding you every little piece of information that you already knew. It really feels written for 12 year olds.- The battle system is ok, but very straightforward, it feels limited. It gets ridicolously easy very quickly even on max difficulty, which had bored me, though later on I gave the game another chance and it does actually become challenging again later on. Unfortunately, it mostly feels hard by virtue of enemy being numerically stronger rather than interesting tactical challenges for the most part. You also probably need to grind mock battles a bit to get any decent amount of components to buy weapon upgrades, which isn't particularly fun.- There is very little actual customization that matters or is interesting. The most impact, if any, is choosing who to promote since for most of the game you will have limited promotion items (but even then, you just promote, you higher level/favourite chars, and do *not* get any choice upon promotion such as different classes in Fire Embles style). Most stat upgrades matter very little, except weapon upgrades and the very few ability upgrades/new abilities that there are.- The voting system is a neat gimmick but definitely not enough to matter, and also at times disappointing. It is generally easy to decide what you want to do since you usually only really need to persuade 1 out of 4. Sometimes, you will want to use straightforward logical arguments, yet you won't even be presented with such options. In one case, I actually got so annoyed that the game wasn't letting me state the obvious reason for doing A, that I ended up going for B just because the possible motivations I was given to explain myself were sounder for that decision.- Exploration sequences are SO limited and pointless (even more than Octopath's already minuscule dungeons) that you wonder why they are even there in the first place, rather than just cut them alltogether like it was in FF:T.All in all, a let down.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like Triangle Strategy. The gameplay and graphics are nice, but the flaws kept getting in the way, and now I have no desire to finish it.There are way too many characters joining your army, and not nearly enough enemy types. If you can only take ten characters into battle, then there’s no reason to have 20+ characters in your roster, especially if you have to spread resources among all of them. And fighting the same enemy types for one map after another is truly a cursed game design. It should be flipped, with only a handful of characters in your army, but all of them take an active role in the story. They could have easily made some of the character types into enemy units, especially since they have no real depth. The witchy weather girl is a perfect example, just make her an enemy. Same for the flying shield guy, he’s eerily similar to the shield guy we started with, except he can fly. And why would they have a warrior who goes into battle only with a shield??? That’s aesthetically lame and just a gameplay gimmick rather than a real character. Really, they fumbled the ball on character stories in general. And no, Jens telling me about his dead buddy every time I want to upgrade my weapons doesn’t count as story.I was drawn into the narrative at first, because of course I wanted to see how the intrigue between the nations would be handled. Unfortunately the characters themselves have no depth, so eventually I stopped caring about what happened to any of the nations! Was there ever any character development??? There was one instance when a female character temporarily left my party, and another one really cozied up to the main character. Then the first female returned… ruh roh! I thought there would be some real drama there, like a love triangle type situation. But no, nothing! Maybe the situation was resolved later on, and I just quit too early, but that’s storytelling - you have to keep the audience hooked.One funny thing is that Triangle Strategy unintentionally proves that democracy svcks. The voting system during plot branches seemed interesting, but eventually it becomes obvious that some routes aren’t meant to be unlocked on the first playthrough. At least, not unless you’ve said the correct responses to random townsfolk. I was often barred from making the most interesting decisions, and I came to resent my own teammates for voting against me, which is pretty much modern democracy in a nutshell. A game should be BETTER than reality, and give you opportunities to do things that you can’t do in real life. I like beating up bad guys in games because if you do that in real life, you go to prison. It’s the same with player choice, you have no control over real life, so in the game they should just make you head of the house with top-down authority. You make the decisions, and everyone else has to deal with it. If you want to play a game where nobody does what you want them to do, then just give up on video games and live a real life. Real life is full of people who don’t care about your opinion on anything, just like your teammates in this game!To wrap up this longwinded review, I think it’s safe to say that Vandal Hearts is still the uncontested king of tactics games. In fact, I think I’ve had it UP TO HERE with Square tactics games where they load you down with a roster of fifty thousand characters and character types. It’s like, okay my man, I can only take a few characters into battle, what are the rest of these jokers going to do? Are they kickin’ back, relaxing in the rear with the gear??? This all comes from Square’s employees focusing their creativity on cool looking heroes they can use for promo material, rather than thinking “Okay, what the heck are we going to do with eight hundred protagonists???”Sorry for going off!

_childDocuments_.review: I genuinely love everything about this game. The characters, the gameplay mechanics, the STORY!! Everything about this game felt like it was hand-crafted with utmost care. The English voice acting is... a little rough, but by the end of the game it felt somehow endearing instead of irksome. I've only finished a single playthrough but even as I was finishing up the last levels I was thinking ahead to what other paths I wanted to explore in my next. Not one chapter had me bored to tears—I watched every single side-story, every character interlude, everything that the game gave me the option to experience I did, and eagerly too!I know for a fact I missed a lot of things in my first playthrough, it's just the nature of the game. I'm probably going to miss a lot in my second playthrough too, and for once that doesn't bother my completionist self at all. If anything it's an incentive to play this game over and over again to see just what differs based on what path I take.The fact that there was no "right" path was very refreshing. It's not a story about good VS. evil, it's a story about ambitions and values clashing against each other: the human sins of greed, pride, envy, etc. influencing the minds of Norzelia's best and brightest to create a powder keg primed to explode. I read through the notes, the information blurbs, ran around speaking to every NPC that would let me talk to them, and explored to my heart's content in the world they created for us. It's like JRPG Game of Thrones: you can't walk three steps without bumping into something potentially significant.I'll say that the game has a bunch of characters but I only really used about half of them. Once I had a set party that I was comfortable with/leveled up to my heart's content there wasn't really a need for me to level up others whose abilities weren't really my speed. (Sorry Jens.) Some of the members in my roster never saw battle even once. I don't even remember some of their names. Something to try in a different playthrough perhaps.TL;DR: I LOVED this game! If you like long, branching narratives that give weight to each choice you make + turn based RPG where no two characters in your roster have the same abilities, you'll have a great time.If you don't like reading... maybe this one isn't for you. There's a LOT of story/cutscenes in this one.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT again: A MASTERPIECE.  Great story, writing, RPG, combat mechanics and great quality of life features.  Very few flaws.  A timeless classic.  I rarely play a campaign game a second time, but I am now as I write this playing NG+, and it is a great experience.  This game is a classic that will be respected for many, many years to come.EDIT: As I have gotten much further into this game, I want to add that it's a GREAT STORY.  A gripping drama, with lots of twists and turns, and characters that act in character and develop over the game.  It has some of the consistently BEST WRITING I have ever seen in a video game.  One recent example I just read as I write this. Roland upon learning of deaths in his kingdom "How many people will I fail? Bear it I must -- else I become doomed to repeat it. [Serenoa offers words of consolation]  Where you offer comfort, I see only excuses."[Initial Review begins] Although 'pixel graphics' the HD-2D graphics are very colorful and very pretty.  The animators get surprisingly good emotions out of small pixel characters.  There's a lot of story, fortunately there's a wonderful QoL feature, auto text advance, so you don't have to press a key after every text bubble to advance to the next.  Yes, it's a bit like an animated movie, except you take over for many parts.  All the story provides context and immersion in the world.  I like it. The opposite would be one tactical battle after another, with little context or character development.If you're looking for a hack n slash or fighter or FPS game, this is not it, though even you might like some variety in your game repertoire such as this to complement those games.  Another nice QoL features is there is a Depth of Field toggle to easily turn off the depth of field blur that some people find excessive.  The tactical battles, with a wide variety of units, will absorb your full attention. It's a low stress game, in the sense that you can take your time through all parts of it, there's no time pressure to stress you.  Another nice QoL feature is if you lose a battle, all your heroes keep the experience gained, and none are permanently dead (i.e., no permadeath, at least on Normal difficulty).  This is a wonderful game design innovation and I hope other game developers include it at least as an option for those who prefer it (like me!). In my most recent battle, at Normal difficulty, first playthrough, I won with just two units left alive.  A thrilling finish.  Great game design and polish to facilitate an exciting finish like that.  In sum, is it enjoyable?  Yes.  Though some people adversely react to the thought of "too much story", I find the story enhances the immersion and makes the other components of the game that much richer.

_childDocuments_.review: When I play a "tactics"-type game I expect two things:- A riveting, dramatic, engrossing story- Engaging tactical gameplayTriangle Strategy is mediocre in both aspects.The story suffers from severe issues with pacing, exposition, and gravitas. It is VERY slow to get going, spending the first quarter of the game in an idyllic realm with zero tension, and there's multiple points where the drama seems to simmer down when it should be ramping up. I physically yelled at the game several times to "get on with it."Worse, any time the story sets up a dramatic plot point, it spoils it immediately beforehand by handing you Omniscient Narrator Glasses and showing a cutscene where a villain has an internal monologue all but explaining exactly what they're about to do and then laughing maniacally to themselves. It's infuriatingly cliche, obnoxious, and deflating. If there's one piece of advice I could give to anyone who would play this game, it would be to skip the green "Side Story" markers as they don't feature any battles and are always detrimental to the story.But even without having the story threads spoiled, it simply lacks impactful plot twists. There's no clever subversion of expectations, or even moments where you're like "I saw THAT coming" followed immediately by "but not THAT." Here's an "anti-spoiler" detailing plot twists you will NOT experience: Other issues I had with the story were the extremely black-and-white morality of most of the antagonists and the lack of truly diverging storylines. Supposedly, the impact of your choices is the defining gimmick of this game, but the story always converges back on the same path regardless of what you choose. There are only three endings, plus a "True Ending" which of course depends on you choosing the "correct" options. It's not enough.As for the actual battles, I have to say they're rather standard. In fact it feels a bit slow and lacks mechanics that really give me the ability to feel clever and effective on the battlefield. Each battle is just both sides slowly whittling each other down.If you're dying for a tactics game and EXTREMELY patient with the story, then it can be worth your time, but for me it was not. I finished my run almost out of spite; I figured if I was going to write a negative review I might as well do so fully informed of what the game has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend playing the game. I'll talk about things I feel are unique about this game. Play the game blind. Don't go for the "golden ending." Do that on the second play through if you want.The Scales of Conviction:It's a fancy way to say choices. There are 3 "flavors" of choices: Morality, Utility, and Liberty. When you make a choice or play a certain way you get points to one of those 3 options.It's fun because you feel like you get to influence the branching paths, characters you use, missions you play.When they pull the titular scale out. Characters will vote, and you have an opportunity to pursued them to your cause.The only bad thing is the game requires certain amount of points in an option to convince characters of a choice. So you might spam all the dialogue options but always fail and the game doesn't tell you it's because you lack points in Morality, Utility, or Liberty.The StrategyPriority: The game has a priority list. Unlike Fire Emblem or Valkyria Chronicles, your speed and certain actions determine your individual units turn. This is fun. You are sometimes trying to manipulate the priority list to move units away from others, or to strategize who you should focus on.Position: This game has elevation. Like the old star wars meme "I have the high ground!" At first it's intimidating, but you get the hang of it really quickly. Another unique thing about the game is "backwards" attack. The direction your unit faces is important. If someone hits behind you, they get an automatic crit on you. Lastly, I want to talk about "pincer" attacks. If two units sandwhich another, the second unit gets a weaker additional hit. These concepts sound hard, but you get the hang of all them after a few maps.Unit Uniqueness: I'm a fan of characters being unique. I hate reclassing because characters lose their identity. Every unit in this game is unique. They have unique mechanics that cost tech points. This does wonders for replay-ability. You can use ice magic mages or a unit that is all utility who uses items. It's so fun to play with different units.The art:I'll be honest. I originally didn't want to play the game because I thought the art wasn't appealing. It's sprites on a 3d-ish cube. I don't mind it in old GBA games, but I want to see characters. I want to see emotions. I don't want to see the same sprite art when units talk. In older games, they had an excuse, but here I feel like it's an easy way to not focus on animating models.After a few hours though. The art grew on me. I find it charming now. Part of me wished characters were more expressive but there are scenes in the game where I do feel the impact.The Story:It's good. It gives you context on why you are fighting and keeps you interested. One downside is that there are a lot of cutscenes. Like a lot. I love it, but I can see people being turned off if they aren't interested in the story.Overall I give the game like a 9/10. It's a really fun game. I recommend it. If you are looking for other strategy games, I recommend Valkyria Chronicles 4 (It's a sequel, but a stand alone game). It's different from this but if you like story heavy strategy games, you'll probably love that game too.

_childDocuments_.review: Triangle Strategy is a tactical role-playing game developed by Artdink and Square Enix, and produced by Tomoya Asano, who also produced Bravely Default, and Octopath Traveler, the latter of which especially influencing Triangle Strategy's ethos as a title. With a variety of controllable character units with distinctive combat niches, and set in a medieval setting, Triangle Strategy stands as a story-heavy campaign where player choice takes front seat, filling a similar genre niche to Final Fantasy Tactics, and Fire Emblem: Three Houses.Triangle Strategy centers said player choice by interweaving a tripartite field of ethical ideologies, specifically Morality, Liberty, and Utilitarianism, that Serenoa, the protagonist, may align himself to. Each ideology changes the means with which the story unfolds and concludes, and is the main means in which player choice is expressed through gameplay.Serenoa's ideological alignment may be determined simply by choosing certain conversation topics in cutscenes, to waging war certain ways; using strategies in battle can boost any of your ideological convictions dependent on condition. For instance, using an ends justify the means sense of ethics as your solution to win a fight might make said fight easier, but will also compromise your sense of Morality, and bring Serenoa more in line with a rugged Utilitarian approach. On top of this, some characters are locked dependent on Serenoa's ideological conviction. Lastly, in certain points of the game, there exist elections wherein the 7 members of your core party vote to decide upcoming levels as war council decisions, each voting unit able to be persuaded to whichever side you prefer based on Serenoa's ideological conviction.The variety of units that can be controlled give additional depth to combat outside of the ideology system; some units may allow you to change terrain access by building ladders, setting traps to damage enemy forces, provide temporary stat bonuses, or use items on other party members. Each character brings their own unique spice to the game's combat, and makes for party compositions that always give new characters a chance to shine, and change the pace and means with which battles are fought. For instance, terrain advantages might make certain units more viable than others due to the tactical niches with which they inhabit. Despite its similarities to Fire Emblem, there is no permadeath, even as an option, though a New Game Plus option is present.In general, I'd recommend Triangle Strategy to people already familiar and amicable to story-driven tactical RPGs. If you liked Three Houses, you're probably going to find Triangle Strategy a bit of fresh air, though prepare for another dialogue-heavy story. Also, this game's a port from the Switch, runs smoothly at 60 frames given your respective specs, can account for for Xbox One Controllers in its in visual interface, and brings a stunning mix of HD-2D diorama art that you might recognize from Octopath Traveler.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - 8/10, fantastic graphics and fun combat, pacing can be slow between fights, not quite as deep in terms of character customization as FFTI played about 20 hours of this on switch, but when I saw it was coming to PC I put it down to wait for what I assumed would be a superior version. That ended up being the right call because wow does it look and play better on beefier hardware. Animations and effects look ultra smooth, and the camera flows around with no jerkiness whatsoever.As for the game itself, I'm enjoying it a lot. I'd probably list Final Fantasy Tactics in my top 5 games of all time, so much so that I've sunk dozens of hours into modding it (shoutout . This game doesn't have nearly as much depth in its class system from what I've seen, but it does have a satisfying depth to the combat mechanics themselves. Attacks from behind enemy units, or high ground, or when an ally is present on the opposite side of the enemy, all do more damage. This makes it much more interesting than just "walk up to the nearest thing and hit them". And I personally enjoy the action points system a lot (it replaces MP as a consumable resource for special abilities) since it replenishes each round and leads to opportunities to regroup briefly before launching coordinated attacks. Bravely Default and Octopath Traveler had a version of this that was more geared towards multiple actions in a single turn, as opposed to something you spend on more powerful attacks, but a lot of the same strategies apply.Graphics are beautiful, but I'm a real sucker for this HD-2D trend we're seeing. Particle effects on attacks look nice, and the sound design is satisfying. I don't notice the music too much while I'm playing, probably because there's so many voiced lines playing during each combat turn.Pacing can be an issue if you want tactics games to drop you on a map and let you go nuts until you walk up to the next story marker. Random battles here are replaced with repeatable (but not randomized) mock battles that unlock as you progress through the story. This also seems to be your main avenue for making money and grinding upgrade materials, so you'll likely be seeing each of these fights a lot. That lack of variety is a bummer, but I feel like FFT is the only game I can think of that actually went so far as to randomize the random battles, so that may be too high a standard to apply here. That being said, you can end up sitting through A LOT of exposition between fights, so if the story doesn't grab you then that might be too much to suffer through. It's not quite up to FFT's level of depth and maturity, but it definitely isn't basic either.The pacing and fight variety may open up after the point in the game where I stopped on the switch, but from what I've seen in the first 7 chapters in the game (out of 19 according to google), I can recommend it to fans of SRPGs. Maybe watch a let's play of the first bit of story and combat encounter to see if the general vibe of the game feels right to you.

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely one of those times where I wish I could give a neutral rating rather than a positive one. However, I've played the game for a decent length of time, and will almost certainly finish it, so it can lean positive in this case.As a tactics game, the basic gameplay is quite good. Each unit is unique, with a special set of skills, and there are some fun synergies to be had. Some really stand out above the rest, like the assassin Anna, but generally each character is useful for something, and while I have my favorites, I can see how each would be useful in their own way. Clever tactics are definitely rewarded, and unlike say Fire Emblem, there's no character permadeath, so you can afford to make desperate gambits in a pinch. The combat really shines in the mock battles you can grind in the encampment because usually you can utilize whatever best suits you, and you're on somewhat fair footing.Not so in the story missions. I'm playing on Hard mode, and god is it frustrating at times. It's not even a matter of winning and losing, since I can reliably win. The issue is that winning often doesn't feel very fun or rewarding because I have no choice but to use pretty passive tactics. Enemies are numerous, have more health than you, and do LOADS more damage. Like double your damage. So any aggressive play will be absolutely demolished. And this isn't a matter of equipment or levels, either. I have been over the recommended level for each story mission, and it is still like this. I suppose on Normal this will be less the case, but it's disappointing since the game would be so much more fun if you could play a bit more aggressively, if you and your foes were roughly equivalent in strength, and they simply had a numbers advantage over you. Instead, they get both numbers, and massive boosts to strength as well, so even though I rarely have to restart a story mission, I still don't enjoy them as much as I might otherwise.I've spent the bulk of my time talking about the gameplay because, full disclosure, I have chosen to skip the dialogue and story sequences entirely. Sure, I started out listening to the scenes, waiting patiently for the next battle to begin. But these things just go on and on and on and on and ON! Dear god, it's like they were trying to cram three novels' worth of text into this game. And if it was all gripping, engaging writing from start to finish, that could at least take the edge off. But it's not. Dialogue is banal and long-winded, the characters aren't awful, but rarely stand out, and while the plot seems like it has a few interesting movements that I glimpse as I skip through the scenes, nothing made me sit up and really want to pay attention in the first 2 hours, so I decided to just stick to the parts I actually enjoyed. And for reference, even if you are like me and skip every single cut scene and dialogue sequence, it can still take nearly 10 minutes (!) just to get through all the skipping and back to the actual gameplay. You have been warned.I'd give this something like a 6 or a 7 out of 10. Not amazing, but rubs my tactics liking brain enough that I can just mindlessly play it while listening to a podcast or something on the side. Will probably never play or think about it again once I beat it, but don't hate it either.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a turn based Strategy (J)RPG with graphics similar to Octopath Traveler (2D-3D mix with retro style). It draws inspiration from the TV show Game of Thrones, royal houses scheming over power and resources. The world map also looks like the opening from that TV show. It is heavily story driven and depending on your play-style and decisions throughout the game the story progresses into different directions. Excellent game. I recommend it to all strategy fans (except the ones who hate reading).Graphics: Very nice drawings and environments with lovely details. Music: Amazing orchestral soundtrack befitting a war scenario.Gameplay: Excellent gameplay similar to FFT or Fire Emblem with a lot of dept. Controls: This is best played with a controller. Good responsive and logical controls overall. Story: Fantastic deep story with great characters and subplots. Difficulty: You can choose one of 4 difficulties. The highest difficulty is very challenging. Probably Normal is what you wanna go for unless you are a hardcore strategy game player then you can try difficult.Replay Value: Since the game has several paths to walk it can be interesting to play it again. It also has a NewGame+ mode after you win.German translation: This game has a really high quality German translation. Someone with a really high level of knowledge of the German language translated this. It reads like a good book. I did find a handfull of typos though ;-) But thumbs up for the translator!Some critic: - the world map could have been better, it tried to resemble GoT but it is just ok.- the difficulty is balanced by "illusionary training battles" where you can level up infinitely in your tent in between battles. On the highest difficulty I'm sure these are absolutely necessary, although you keep your XP from failed tries of mainstory battles too, which I found odd because failing missions makes it easier to beat them. - The game is very text heavy and starts slow with lots of text to read. The beginning can be tiresome but keep going because it gets very interesting once the struggles start.- I found it a bit weird how some of the soldiers you recruit are: a very young girl (child), an old grandma who is super strong and fast, And then the strongest knight & general of one of the kingdoms is a woman. It just seems random sometimes. However most of the time it is fine.- There are some side stories to recruit new characters that can be accessed in between missions. However the timing of those side stories often does not fit the situation of the main story. Like you cannot escape from a current place but the side story shows you walking somewhere freely and people visiting you in your tent.- i found it disappointing that the outcome of the tournament does not depend on your performance. It will always end the same way. A missed opportunity to have the player influence something by playing the strategy part well.

_childDocuments_.review: Triangle Strategy is a decent game that's worth a play through. The game's story is its greatest strength while its combat and characters (especially the optional recruits) leave something to be desired. I would give this game a 6/10 and value it at around $30 or less. Triangle Strategy has a strong, overarching story filled with political intrigue. Alliances are forged and broken while betrayals are had on all sides. What's especially great is that both enemies and allies alike have clear motives, whether that be wealth, power, or even values. But as the game progresses, difficult decisions must be made. Values can be noble, but can they be justified when survival is at stake?This ties nicely into the voting mechanic. Throughout the game, your council will have to the vote on the most pressing of matters, with the majority deciding on your group's fate. Each member of your council has their own opinions and beliefs and its up to you to understand their viewpoints, then sway their opinion if you prefer a certain decision. While some characters will remain steadfast to their opinions no matter what you say, others may be indifferent to certain topics. I found this to be a terrific mechanic as it ties into the theme of no person ever rising to power on their own, but only through the support of those gathered around them do they succeed.Characters that appear regularly in the story have enough screen time such that they feel decently fleshed out. The same cannot be said for the optional recruits that join your team throughout the game. These characters often feel shallow as each you only get a handful of cut scenes for each of them, all of which consist of few lines of dialogue at most. As a result, these characters end up becoming little more than caricatures and its difficult to get invested into their meager story lines. The game is already lacking in substantial side content, so a few additional missions here and there would have helped to round out their stories.This brings us to combat. The combat is serviceable, being standard tactical RPG affair with melee attacks, range attacks, and AoE magic attacks. However, the largest problems are balance (or lack thereof) and map design. Often times, enemies will greatly outnumber you. While you can do your best to funnel enemies into choke points to circumvent their numbers, the sheer number of enemy troops will usually lead to them overwhelming you at some point and despite playing on normal difficulty, I found myself struggling at times.As a result, you will either have to go back and grind previous missions or mock battles to level up, which isn't particularly fun (again, the game has a lack of real side content, so this is the only way you'll be able to level up), or searching for cheese on the more difficult maps, which is unsatisfying. As an example of bad map design, certain maps will have a ladder leading to a ledge with no other way up. As long as you place an archer at the top of the ladder, melee units cannot reach your archer and you're free to pick enemy units off one by one as their AI is too dumb to leave your bow's range.Overall, I enjoyed my time with Triangle Strategy, but not enough to go back and play through all the other scenarios I missed out on. I made sure to get the true ending on my first play through and if you're like me, who rarely replays a game / doesn't care for New Game+, I recommend looking up how to achieve the  before starting the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Simple and short, this game intends to be one thing but is in fact not what is advertise.Triangle Strategy is really the bare bones of what you expect a tactile rpg to play as. Battles are set up to make one think there is suppose to be a level of complex and depth though these amount to just being a last man standing type of affair. Seldom you will have different mission objects that are different from just wiping out your opponent but in playing 17 hours, as of this review, I have only encountered two instances where this occurs. Credit is due for the terrain design, from an artistic standpoint, but again it is very simple and plain compared to other prior trpgs like FF Tactics, Tactics Ogre, etc. Most of these amount to just having environmental aspects where it causes rough terrain and setting things on fire.As to the character design, it is a mix bag. From a story narrative the key characters of your party, villains and NPCs are fleshed out into a generally interesting story from a plot perspective. The issue however is that while you can have a multitude of recruits there is nothing more to them than just a quick animated scene to explain why they are in your party. So they are just mainly hirelings. Where the game falls short is in the design of character mechanics. Many fall into stereotypical tropes, which while not a bad thing per say, are very basic in terms of abilities. The game does give you a sub-system of options that can be purchased and used but these amount to just rehashed abilities someone in your party already has and requires a resource mechanic that takes much time to acquire with little payoff and mostly are just a one or two time use per battle. Another sub-system amounts to character upgrades which are done by promotions at certain levels. However, beyond just raising stats they only other noticeable difference is unlocking more action points to do things on a turn. Upgrades to equipment are non-existent as you only have ring slots which offer basic upgrades to stats or to a resistance of some type. What upgrades that are present require an extensive collection of resources that don't really increase anything beyond a minor benefit which makes no noticeable difference in battle. Also there is very little in terms of world exploration or world building as your play areas are repeated places you been to before.The two things however that I really dislike was the intensive grinding for resources and leveling up characters. What is the kicker on this aspect is the main story battles are few in instances. In order to level up or obtain dropped loot such as resources, cash, etc. you have to constantly grind "mock" battles. So you will be repeating the same "mock" battles constantly which just makes the game boring. An option is included as well to repeat story battles though these are limited to the level they commence at and despite what later levels you acquire these will be restricted to the level of the specific story battle. The only reason to repeat these is if you are really after a specific loot items which at some point can be bought later. The other thing that was a let down is the supposed Triangle choice system. The game props itself up as implying that choices made by you as the main character have dramatic consequences down the line for the overall story. But this is not what the reality of the system is. There is very little player agency with regards to choice as you are shoehorned into story events based upon which one of the three decision stats (liberty, morality, utility) is the highest. These stats, which are hidden from you, do not provide story options of choice but are used only to influence the 7 key NPCs into making a decision you want them to and even at that there is no guarantee they will do it. So key story elements are decided by NPC committee. You have no final say in the matter. That was the huge let down as several instances I made choices only to be overruled by others into doing the things I didn't want to do, which is ironic considering you are suppose to be a Lord...In all the game was a let down for me and I wouldn't recommend this even if on sale. For a 60 dollar game, this feels like a very bare bones trpg game with little to no content, unnecessary amounts of level grinding, and a "specially advertise" system which amounts to nothing.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is - despite some vexing flaws - my favourite new RPG I've played in 2023. I'm going to simplify this by dividing my review into what I like and don't like:WHAT I LIKE:- The tactical combat system. It's am absolute blast and arguably my favourite turn based system of any RPG I've ever played. The different strengths and weaknesses of the main party members are really well balanced with each other and combined with the various methods for flanking/rear attacking enemy and the ways in which terrain can be exploited make for a system I'm finding totally engrossing. Some people have complained that the battles are too long but I disagree because the strategic and tactical planning they require have got me enjoying every second of them. I much prefer this to the mind numbing tedium that quickly ensues with the random encounters approach that a lot of non tactical RPGs use. - The overall story arc. Whilst arguably a tad predictable so far - as well as stumbling a bit in execution due to some issues I'll discuss later - I actually like the the Games of Thrones-like approach of the overall story arc.  - The world building. Although maybe a bit naive in places, I think the identities and differences between the three main factions are quite well fleshed out, certainly much deeper than in many JRPGs and I'd love to see more games in this genre that take a similar approach. - Choices actually seem to matter. Although I'll have to do at least another play-through to really get a handle on how true this is, it really feels like the outcomes of the votes with the scales are having real impacts on the direction of the story, [spoiler[ Roland being given up and the Aesfrost sabotaging the Wolfort's attempts at cooperation with Lord Landroi seem like a example in my playthrough so far[/spoiler]- The HD-2D and pixel art look great as a whole.WHAT I DON'T LIKE OR WHAT I FIND TO BE MERELY AVERAGE:- The voice acting. Whilst I am finding there to be some exceptions like Archduke Gustadolph, for the most part I agree with all the other reviewers that have criticized the voice acting in this game overall. A lot of it just plan isn't good and feels really forced. It also doesn't sit well with the next issue which is:- The dialogue and structure of the storytelling. Simply put, as other reviewers have noted the dialogue really isn't great for the most part. When it isn't trying and failing to sound a lot more profound than it actually is, it's repeating the same details over and over again. There are entire segments of narrator dialogue on the world map that could've simply been cut from the game altogether because they just repeated what you'd already been told several times and just make the pacing feel less smooth.On that note, there are times where the game exits a scene to go out onto the world map but the only scene you can choose to play next is in the exact same time and place meaning that the flow of the game just ends up being interrupted for no good reason. This might not matter to some people at all but to me it just feels like obviously flawed and unpolished design. This along with the voice acting might not be such a big deal except that there is a looooooooooot of dialogue in this game, particular in the first two hours or so which can actually make those kinda torturous to get through. I really do think that being a bit more ruthless with the editing to make some of these scenes more succinct could've helped here.  One more issue on this front is I'm finding that the game occasionally bungles the execution of the story telling in ways that might not bother some people at all but to me are quite obvious and that someone should've probably pointed out during development. An early example of this is  Had I just been given a little more context beforehand then I wouldn't have reacted the way I did to this line and I can't help but think that the narrative designers executed this one back to front. To sum it up, I honestly think if the execution of the voice acting and dialogue had been a little more succinct and just better written then this game would definitely be on very positive rather than mostly positive. - So far I'm not really warming to the less important characters that you can recruit through stories. I've only added the tavern owner and the little girl who can create a decoy of herself and neither of them do anything for me as characters. Even most of the main characters are a little bland if I'm honest although they seem to be improving as the game gets going. I'd rather they'd just cut these extra characters out and put that time and energy into improving other things in the game. - The game seems to sometimes make use of the 'idiot trope' where someone  does something stupid or doesn't do something they obviously should all because the plot needs it to happen that way. An example of this is ALL IN ALL:I have to say that despite some really glaring flaws I think I have to (almost reluctantly) conclude that Triangle Strategy is my favourite RPG I've picked up in 2023. I'm just loving the gameplay so much and can't wait to play more of it. It's just a bit tragic that a lot of the big flaws were probably quite avoidable if they'd just thought things through a little more. I really recommend getting this one and just slogging it through the first two hours. I'm definitely going to do a playthrough on hard difficulty when I beat the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't remember the last time I played a game for 70hrs+ without any other obligation behind it. I surprised myself with this one. Overall 7/10! I recommend :)Despite its simple political landscape, it maximises the moral and political complexities of each situation colouring each faction and choice you can make with nuance and intrigue.Albeit, because of the complexities of that story it can be hard to predict the details of each outcome of your decision. Which sometimes gives the feeling of being a bit too lucky - which momentarily reveal's the author's hand. On top of this, the knowledge that each choice weaves back into the story eventually makes it feel the story is still on rails though, I doubt the story could keep its complexities and still give that detail and nuance without increase the scope of the game massively. That being said each decision was fun to ponder over, regardless.The dialogue is often lambasted at boring and bland. And while I see this point, it fits the time period and aids in deepening the subtext and inferences of each conversation. This may have work better a non-pixel art style, but I found the voice acting good enough to carry give it character.The OST was done by the same composer as FMA: Brotherhood, so it had a wonderful range from bombastic, to playful, to sombre. The art is also wonderful. Even if the pixel art animations are quite simple.The gameplay is another hightlight of a simple yet fun system that once you get your hands on, allows you to use each character in different situations and maps that they work best.The difficulty on normal felt very well balanced with the only noticeable difficulty spikes being when I chose a more risky choice to keep my moral purity. That being said, playing the game through had me wishing I had hit the true golden ending on the first time by accident as all other endings are purposely made to be not fully satisfying. Ultimately, replaying games often dull emotions and cause the first experience to fade. Leaving you with a more muted opinion on it then you initially had. It ruins the organic feeling of the story as it pulls back the curtain to reveal the author entirely.Which is not ideal for a more story driven game such as this. This is why I may never my favourite games of recent memory again. Its an interesting conundrum.

_childDocuments_.review: Triangle Strategy has been one of my favorite gaming experiences of 2024. I initially ignored the game on release as I thought it was simply a spiritual successor to Octopath Traveler, which I had yet to finish, due to the similar art styles. Having just finished both games back to back, I could not have been more wrong. Octopath was a very beautiful (more so than Triangle Strategy imo) and very tedious game that felt like it had very little to offer in terms of storytelling and player agency. Triangle Strategy has a lot more in common with Fire Emblem (Specifically Fates and Three Houses). It hits pretty much all the positive elements of FE that I love that were missing or lackluster in the latest game Engage. There is more of an emphasis on story. About 40% of the game feels like its dialogue which is fantastic if you love in-depth world building but would feel tedious if you are just playing the game for the strategy component. The games combat is tactic based (which I personally find more engaging), there is a greater emphasis on the story, and there are multiple endings and side characters to unlock that encourage multiple play throughs. The game feels complete in the sense that nothing feels like it was cut from the game, and it has many small details that did not need to be included. The entire game did not need to be voice acted, but they did (not including exploration segments but that is such a small portion of the game that it feels unnecessary). They did not need to include fail state epilogue cutscenes, but they did. They did not need to give all the side characters unique voice lines right before they attack the final boss, but they did. They did not need to include an optional epilogue once you beat the game for a more satisfying conclusion, but they did. They did not need to include sprite animations that are only used once or twice in the entire game, but they did. They did not need to update the character’s profile with an up-to-date status of their role to the plot immediately after a big status changing event, but they do. All these little details showcase the passion behind this game. The world building and lore can be a little dense when first starting the game, but it does pay off in the end. Both my brother and I were glad that we did not skip any of the optional cutscenes as they did a great job at sucking us deeper into the world and characters. The story itself is great. All the decisions feel impactful and define how your character thinks as a leader. Do you place more of an emphasis on morality and honor or are you more practical and care more about survival and tactical advantages? Every decision does a good job of feeling more and more important and impactful at defining your character and beliefs as time goes on. Based on your decisions you will also attract new characters to join your cause. Using them will unlock short and simple side stories that explores their motivations. Gameplay wise, the only story element that this is lacking compared to Fire Emblem is the permanent unit death at harder difficulties. I don’t really feel incentivized to beat every mission perfectly as a result. Then again, this combat is a little more difficult than FE on normal and it can be harder to try and achieve a flawless victory. Maybe the devs wanted to prevent frustration from setting in, I don’t know.The Combat overall is satisfying and there are a lot of unique characters with interesting builds. Though some of them are far more useful than others. The blacksmith in particular is a weak glass cannon with utility skills that are not effective enough to justify using him even on maps where he should thrive. He has a ladder which sounds very useful in theory to reposition units, but its only like one block tall which many characters can jump naturally. Meanwhile, you have Anna, a spy who is so versatile that she can single handedly hold off and solo one of the games final bosses (provided she has enough healing items) while the rest of the under leveled units work together on killing off the weaker enemies. The elemental magic system is also quite interesting. Each element will interact with terrain and other elements in various ways. You can set some terrain (or throwable oil barrels) on fire for constant damage or zone control. You can use wind to spread the fire and turn around enemies. You can freeze the ground debuffing movement speed. Then you can melt Ice with fire to make puddles. You can Zap puddles with lightning damaging units over a massive area. The few characters that can control time also have very interesting mechanics that are difficult to master or wrap your head around but feel very satisfying when pulled off well. My only critique with the magic system is that spells don’t do friendly fire damage unless the unit is standing on a tile that can be affected by that element. It just feels wrong to thoughtlessly throw a massive fireball into a group of allies and enemies and your allies coming out unharmed. I feel it does devalue strategizing forward unit placement. The 3D world can be a little jank and confusing to navigate in some spots at the exploration phase, but that is such a small portion with no stakes, so I don’t consider that a big deal. It works just fine in the turn based combat.I played this game at two different extremes. I played a lot of the early game on the LCD Steam Deck and most of the mid to late game on a 4K 32in OLED. On the Steam Deck, I was not really a fan of all the visual post processing effects. It made the pixel art look very soft. You can turn a lot of the effects off which does help somewhat, but the design of the sprites do have gradients and blending techniques that just make the art feel a little soft at that scale. The art is fine, but does not fit my personal tastes. Octopath’s simpler art sprite style looked slightly better and sharper to my tastes on the Deck and the post processing and macro lens effect just looked better in general than what is present in this game. I will also note that by default, the steam deck controls are a little over sensitive for my liking and the snapping at specific viewing angles feels a little jarring as a result. I would recommend tweaking the joysticks to be less sensitive and turning off the snapping feature. On the 4K 32in OLED, the graphics were a different story. The pixel art remained sharp and crisp even with all the post processing effects cranked out. Using an Xbox controller felt better tuned than the Steam Deck in terms of sensitivity. The Mouse and Keyboard controls feel intuitive to use (and not an after thought like in Octopath) if you want to use that method of control. I do love all the sketchy art style of all the character profiles and the end screen. I love the vibes of the illustrations and how you can tell the personalities of all the characters at a glance based on their caricatures. My only critique is that sometimes the voice actor does not necessarily feel like it matches the illustration, though that issue is not very prevalent. Overall this game is great! I can’t believe I had been sleeping on it this long. This game feels feature complete and respects the players wallet and time. There is no DLC or tedious grinding. Just fun combat and an interesting story.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. Combat is always engaging and exciting and the ending brought tears to my eyes. Took me 44 hours to beat it once and I think everyone should play it, BUT...This game has a terrible flaw that might frustrate some and infuriate others: its pacing. It's not just terrible, it's abysmal. At first, I thought I was dealing with some Kojima level of never-ending cutscenes bullsh*t, but it got much, MUCH worse.On many different occasions, I had just one hour of free time to play it, and in those one-hour periods, I played ZERO turns of tactical RPG combat.Probably about 70% of those 44 hours were spent outside of combat. Even if the cutscenes were twice shorter, it would still be too much. And that sucks because the game's story is awesome. Too bad it is told in such a sluggish and obnoxious way. And every true RPG fan knows that fast forwarding the story is NOT an option.

_childDocuments_.review: Our son was only 14 when he was diagnosed with Lukemia. The journey was long, filled with treatments, surgeries, and countless nights where we watched him battle not just the disease, but the overwhelming fear and loneliness that came with it.But there was one thing that brought him back to life in those dark moments: Triangle Strategy.He found it during one of his hospital stays, and at first, it was just something to pass the time. But soon, it became more. As he played, he would tell us about his missions—how his squad worked together, how they fought back against impossible odds. We saw him light up with excitement, a spark of joy we hadn’t seen in a long time. The game gave him a sense of purpose, a chance to be a hero, even when he couldn’t be one in his own life. For hours, he’d immerse himself in that world, and for a while, the pain seemed to fade.Sadly, he lost his battle. But those moments, those hours spent with Triangle Strategy, were some of the happiest of his final months. We know that, for him, it wasn’t just a game. It was a source of strength. A way to feel like he was in control when so much of his life had been taken from him.To the creators of Triangle Strategy: Thank you. You gave our son a little piece of light when everything else felt so heavy. You gave him a way to feel like he could fight back, and for that, we are forever grateful.

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics, if you can appreciate that they chose this style deliberately, I give it 10/10. I can appreciate the aim, and I think, for what it's worth, they did the best they could. Consider it FFT upgraded, without going FULL 3D models. Some of us like the pixelated 2D stuff. I'm neither here nor there on it, but I can appreciate it for what it is, if I did prefer this style. The sound, much to be desired. The score, compared to masterpieces like FFT, is wanting. You can't produce something like that and give us this. Is is bad? I wouldnt say that. Is is good....eehhh....it could use some love. 7/10Gameplay now, this is obviously where the game shines. Synergy, in ways I wont spoil. Could use some more variety, but I can see theyre trying to give us the FFT experience, without completely copying it. I will give them credit for trying something new. I had my gripes with it at first, but now that Im on my second playthrough, I can appreciate how much effort they put in the multiple routes of the story, and still give you a unique experience even during New Game +. This I believe they did well, than any other game. New Game + feels brand new if you choose another path, while still giving you a challenging gameplay you dont have to artificially get to you. 9.5/10. They can improve on this. give us more magic and skills. It feels limited, but again, first edition.The story now.....the story is VERY stressful. They could have pulled this story off without trying so hard to be like Game of Thrones. And if you're paying attention, it has ALOT of similarities. Betrayal is a HUGE part of this game, if you get your feelings involved, it's gonna be a bumpy ride I'm telling you now. This game is very good at pulling you in, getting you attached, and ripping it away from you. And there is NO SOLACE from this. even after you beat the game, you dont really feel like the people that need to get got, really get the justice served to them as deserved. I feel there is ZERO satisfaction in beating the game, the bad guys dont get what they deserve, and the main character is too soft to even think of it. Very unsatisfying story. There are no feelings of accomplishment when it comes to the story. honestly, 1/10. I dont ever want to see a story like this ever again. No where near enough satisfaction for the betrayal at every single turn in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Great Story but a little long in the tooth at points that might turn some folks off.World building is top notch although some folks are evil for evils sake which could have been done a bit better.Progression and choices seem to actually matter in this one so that is great.Due to that choices replay-ability is high is you don't mind the amount of time the story takes. Not massively grindy, in fact you can almost ignore it completely and just lose a fight a couple times. By the third go your level is usually high enough to overcome as you keep levels gained on a loss. You might need to grind mock battles for cash time to time though.I have two big negatives and they sit heavy on me1st. Equipment system absolutely sucks, as you only get two ring/amulet/whatever slots. I much prefer the old FF Tactics full armor/weapon/accessory system. It sucks never being able to get new gear. This is especially true when you have so much customization if you pull something legendary to try different builds. 2nd. Sprites don't change for your character portraits as folk rank up. This is the same for character models in cut scenes. Becoming Veteran and Elite make your models look much cooler in battle I really wish they had updated portraits and non battle sprites to go along with it. This is something I consider a big detail oversight. This game isn't perfect but it's about the closest thing I've ever seen come to FF tactics. It also reminds me of Crono Trigger for some reason which is my all time favorite.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, the game feel empty in the gameplay, story is rich, Tactical features are really good but grinding feel boring, here my Pros and Cons about it.-Pros:1- Pretty music and art style like Octopath Traveler2- Lot of unique characters with stories, you can adapt any situation, some have really interesting mechanics that are barely seen in tactical games3- Lot of special skills in skill tree to unlock 4- Rich story with a lot of forks/choices5- Tactical use of the land, weather and pincer attacks that are useful or can't be ignored.5- Playing on Hard is actually hard and need real strategy-Cons1- Barely being able to explore maps, to enjoy its layouts, except at some keypoint of the storyline.2- Barely no personnalisation for characters... you can equip 2 accessories, that's all. Most of them barely improve stats. Also, you need to accomodate with the characters you have, there is no class change or recruitement.3- Skills are purchased to be unlock and at some point with ressources barely available with the stoyline. If you made wrong choices, you can be stuck in the storyline with undereffective characters (you need to focus on a few at the begining/middle)... i play on hard, i really need to do micromanagement, not i'm against it, but you can be trapped.4- Nearly to much cinematics and chapters, sometime it feel you read more that actually play. Also, forks choices are taken from Tactics Ogre (just to say).5- Bug for add effect of targeting spells or items (burn, freeze, electrocution) that have often a misplaced trigger and area of effect, that can result in not doing what you intended (like not triggering electrocution in a water area for example).6- Grinding is hard and boring. You need to pickup drops/loot on the map (no loot if you don't), enemies can take it before you, and you need a lot of it, but it's random for quality (normal, blue or gold) or to even drop. XP is leveled based of the level of the map, you barely XP if you're the lvl or above of the map.7- To grind, you HAVE TO do the same maps in available in the camp (unlocked with progress in storyline), but it's leveled, so only the highest one is the best (so you come back doing and doing the same too often, even it's painful to you best characters setting)...8- CAUSE  in this game (there is only the main story and camp), .9- Character dying are not permanent (only some missions say to specific character to survive)The gameplay and story are good, but the lack of personnalisation, freedom, rewardless/boring grinding and the bugged target for aditional effects... make the game a bit tiresome.I love to grind to fill gaps of power in tactical game, but here in Hard Mode, it's not possible and you can't even count on accessories items to fill the gap too, you need to often sacrifice some characters (i don't like it, but no consequences having a character dying feels empty).It's more a story game, tactial aspect is really fun and have interesting mechanics... but the game does not of much, the game isn't bad, but i've played other stuff i enjoyed more, and Tactics Ogre (soon available on steam with a "Reborn" at the end) was more interesting 12 years ago on PSP... So i'll play while waitting for Tactics Ogre Reborn.

_childDocuments_.review: Easy 9/10Triangle Strategy might have one of the silliest names of all time, but it is a masterclass at telling a branching story with multiple vastly different outcomes and story beats along the way depending on your choices, or how good you are at influencing the choices of others.The story is thought provoking, and at times brutal in it's depiction of consequence and ambition. It wears its Game of Thrones influences on its sleeve.On top of that the combat is extremely well done, with each encounter being thoroughly thought out, with a ton of different units and strategies that can be used for each stage. It is also quite challenging at times.One thing that really stood out was how unique each unit felt in terms of game-play mechanics. Each unit feels truly their own in how they operate within your team, and it is a lot of fun mixing your roster up during encounters.I knew I would like this game, but I didn't expect it would be one of the best games of 2022.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a review only for people aiming to play the game on a PC using keyboard and mouse.The game starts out a bit frustrating in terms of selecting tiles, both to attack and to move to.  Often, the game picks a different tile.  Usually, you can see in time and back out with a right click -- but I lost some character turns due to resulting misfires.The real problem kicks in when you get to maps where the battle centers on controlling the rooftops and similar much higher ground.  In this case, I found it totally impossible, either to move my (hawk-flying) unit to tiles, which were colored to indicate that they were legal moves.  Rooftop tiles simply would not highlight, no matter what angle or zoom the camera was at.  Even then, I thought I would try to plow through by staying low and targeting the rooftops -- only to find that enemy units on rooftops, could also not be targeted by my archer, although colored as legitimate targets.  Again, it was impossible to highlight the tiles in question, at all.Thus, for me, the game is unplayable.This is a shame.  The tactical battles are very interesting, and the story is quite a bit better than the average video game.  (It can also be fast forwarded easily, if you prefer.)  But tactical battles where you cannot use or target high ground -- that simply doesn't work.

_childDocuments_.review: So, this game was disappointing, but I still do recommend it but there are a lot of things to know before buying it.  I will run through my positives and negatives for the game, but I give it a 6.5/10.  I enjoyed overall the game, but man was I expecting much better.Positives:- Combat: I really enjoyed the actual gameplay of Triangle Strategy a lot.  Now, I found the game to be rather easy once you learn more about how combat works and the roster expands, but I found the actual positioning and abilities to be rather fun and actual need some thought behind your actions.  There are two issues involving combat, but I will mention those later as they are not actual issues with the mechanics of gameplay. 8.5/10- Story (barely):  I will mention my biggest issue with this game (the start) in the negatives, but once the beginning got done with, I found myself pretty interested in the story.  Sadly, my enjoyment went down once the story went on a bit too long, and the ending chapters to be sort of disappointing (at least for the route I went).  But, this is a war and politics story based game.  It does not dive really deep into either one which would have been more interesting, but this story comes out above average to me.  I did like that the ending I got (not true ending) wasn't just a perfect ending, felt a bit more real. 6.5/10- Characters:  They are average to above average.  No one is revolutionizing the JRPG or RPG formula, but I did not hate any of the main members.  The side characters barely have any characterization to them, so they are whatever.  Gustadolph did disappoint me though. 8/10Negatives:- The start of the game.  It is way too slow and meandering for this to be the start of this game.  I have no issue with slow, world-building games (I enjoy Trails a lot), but this game had me bored out of mind for the first few hours.  This is such a bad impression, and I see why a lot of people would drop this game.  One fight for the first couple hours, who came up with that.  - Voice Acting: I really have never been such a huge guy on voice acting breaking a game.  But, it is so clear that the voice acting for a lot of characters (especially main characters) is just not up to par.  Hurts the story and the scenes when the characters are just not performing well.- Number of Battles: In a normal run (which you will do your first playthrough unless you purposely go for the true ending), is 20 chapters which translates to 20 battles.  20 battles in your long, TRPG.  There are some mind battles which is your place to train and earn rewards, but those are not even close to a real battle that shapes the story.  I did not expect this game to be overflowing with battles, but this feels like a VN with some battles along the way (especially in the beginning).- Port: It is not terrible.  I had no crashes or lag.  But the controls are where the PC port falls a part when in combat.  The camera mixed with keyboard and mouse controls just does not work sometimes.  I would click on a space and it would not allow me, even though it should.  Did not hamper my experience that much, but I get this was made with controller in mind.A lot of negatives, but I maybe went into this with slightly different expectations then what I actually played.  Maybe one day I will replay it to get the true ending, but I wish the game just had some more gameplay to it and that the story went a bit further into the intrigue of war and politics.
