_childDocuments_.review: Triangle Strategy is an excellent SRPG lumbered with an extraordinarily boring name. As bland and uninspired as the title makes it sound, Triangle Strategy is a unique and creative experience that kept me engaged right the way through to the end.Combat in Triangle Strategy is turn-based on a per-unit level, meaning each unit's speed stat determines the order in which they move. Positioning is everything in this game, with units on opposite sides of an enemy able to inflict follow-up attacks and units taking critical hits from behind. This combines with a dynamic movement system with lots of character abilities revolving around changing how friendly or enemy units move across the map to create complex and enjoyable battles.Units themselves are entirely unique; there is no class changing and everyone brings something of their own to the table. While this could take away from replayability for some, I really appreciated how every unit had a unique identity that gave me a reason to use them all. There are no "dead weight" characters and the game's branching paths do result in some different roster additions.I decided to play the game on Hard difficulty, considering myself quite familiar with strategy games, and found it satisfying. Aside from a handful of notable spikes the level of challenge was fairly consistent. Enemy AI is smart, exploiting any poor positioning on your part and retreating to healers in the backlines when injured or inflicted with status effects.One strength of Triangle Strategy that I really didn't expect going in was the story. It's a big part of the game and large stretches of time will be spent in cutscenes and dialogue (which is something that should be noted going in). What I expected to be a standard tale of good VS. evil ended up as a plot with a lot of twists, turns and interesting dilemmas. There were some plot beats that felt a little weak to me, particularly in the game's middle section, and a couple of revelations fell flat, but the overarching narrative rooted in believable conflicts and an interesting central cast kept it going.At many pivotal moments in the game's story your party will vote on an action to take next. As the protagonist, Serenoa, you interestingly do not get a vote of your own, but instead can persuade his allies to vote one way or the other to pursue your desired outcome. This comes with a supposed risk that you will fail to win over enough characters and end up being sent down whichever alternate path the majority decides, although I found that the voting system was lenient enough that this never happened to me. I can understand this, as making it too easy to go against the player's own choices could have made the voting irritating. As a way to flesh out the supporting characters and add some flavour to the branching choices, it works.The problems that Serenoa's party end up voting on are generally of major importance to the plot, determining what you will be doing for the next couple of chapters. What I really enjoyed is that the solutions are never clear-cut, with each choice having merits and each character having their own personal convictions. A couple of votes had me putting the game down for the evening because I just couldn't bring myself to make a decision, and in one instance I made no attempt to persuade any characters and let the chips fall on their own to take the weight off of my shoulders. There are no world-shattering choices that will branch you away for half the game, but the choices that do appear are present often enough that it does feel like you get to shape the narrative yourself in a way that ends up feeling very satisfying.I haven't touched on the visuals yet, which uses a similar "HD-2D" style to the one seen in the Octopath Traveller games, albeit without a fixed camera. I like it here in Triangle Strategy, although for whatever reason the brightness is increased compared to the Octopath games which resulted in a few environments looking a bit washed out. The game's soundtrack is catchy and suits the atmosphere well but got a bit repetitive at points, particularly with the battle tracks that get reused often.Overall, I wholeheartedly recommend Triangle Strategy to fans of the SRPG genre. There's a lot to like here, from the engaging combat to the thought-provoking story that all comes together in a charming package. It's not perfect, but it gets enough right that I've already started exploring different choices in New Game+ and I would be very interested in a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing on hard mode is some of the most challenging and fun out of any of the turn-based tactics games I've played. Clearly inspired by the Song of Ice and Fire (Game of Thrones) books, although without quite as deep characters. I still found myself caring for them anyway, though.Just make sure to use a controller -- keyboard/mouse controls aren't great.

_childDocuments_.review: I had heard some not so great things about this game, but had hoped that my love for the original FFT would be enough to allow me to push through.I was wrong.Combat forces you into an overly defensive playstyle otherwise you'll just get completely murdered.  I understand that this is a strategy/tactics game and as such you're expected to be strategic and/or tactical...but there's nothing really strategic or tactical about being forced to turtle because of how easy it is for anyone too far forward to just get surrounded and wrecked in a single turn.  So you hold back and wait for the enemy to come to you, but they don't want to come to you because they also know how easy it is for you to just surround them and destroy them.  So both sides just sit there mean-mugging each other for the first couple rounds until an enemy sets foot within your attack range.  Can't go in then, however, because that's just the bait.Attacks from behind are guaranteed crits, so your incentivised to just stick to the walls so you don't leave an opening.  Attacking someone while an ally is on the opposite side of them allows that ally to just take a free attack, and if that ally is behind them then the guaranteed crit comes into play.  These mechanics work for the enemy as well, and this is why you're forced into a defensive playstyle.  If you try to actually engage the enemy, this is what will happen:-Move to engage the enemy and attack.-Enemy 1 circles around behind and gets a free crit.-Enemy 2 walks up in front, smacking you.  This prompts the enemy behind you to get another free crit.-Your character is now dead.I can appreciate a good challenge in a strategy game that requires forethought and planning, and maybe I just suck, but personally I found that this game just isn't fun.  Like in the first battle a guy shows up to help out.  I can only imagine that his purpose in this fight is to show you how completely screwed you are if you get surrounded.  He starts out behind the enemy line, so they just turn around and murder him after his first turn.  Doesn't help that the controls for this PC port are horrendously implemented.Can't even refund it because 90% of the opening is cutscenes.  Played for 3.5 hours and made it to the 2nd fight before I said ♥♥♥♥ this ♥♥♥♥, I'm out.

_childDocuments_.review: A tactical turn-based game that deserves a place on the podium alongside Final Fantasy Tactics and XCOM2!This game is perfect whether you are new to the genre or a seasoned veteran of tactical turn-based games.The graphical style has the nostalgic feel of Final Fantasy Tactics and the gameplay is almost identical. There are also different stories and allies to unlock depending on choices you make throughout the story, which makes for great replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is fun, but much too few and far between.  The storyline is... ok.  Compelling in its overall arches, but poorly written in detail.  The world is small and isolated and entire kingdoms are conveniently caught off-guard my their arch enemies just because.  And I'm not that far in.As for the combat being few and far between, I've just completed my fourth battle.  And the battles aren't that long.Oh, and controls are a bit wonky, oddly trying to use both sides of the keyboard AND the mouse at the same time.Still, if you're aching for some TRPG combat, this one fills the need nicely, with some unique mechanics that freshen it up.
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: Good story so far. Enjoying the tactics style play. The lack of permadeath is really nice. Would hate to see some of these characters disappear. Plenty of story, side stories, and character stories. Which also means there is a lot of reading/listening if you want to do that, which can be a bit much some times when you all you want is some action. Music is amazing. One annoying thing is that ever ellipsis (...) is dragged on by three distinct notes to signify that it is a ... Really annoying and drags out scenes. I would understand if it was meant for some emphasis, but every time isn't emphasis.
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: 20 hours in and I liking this a lot.Hard mode is pretty challengingSprite and skills look greatStory is goodbut the first 5 hours or so of the game is a visual novel pretty much. You are thrown so many names of people, houses and stuff and it initially is hard to follow long and maybe sometimes care. But the story ramps up around chapter 5 or so and currently I'm loving it. Playing alongside a friend and his story is pretty different from what I got going on so the replayability is definitely there. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first playthrough on normal that took about 52 hours, and I had an absolute blast!Pros:- The story is excellent!  The political intrigue, treachery, and interpersonal dialogue between the factions and the characters is very well done.  Think of the story as "Game of Thrones Lite" with 3 main factions, a few smaller factions, and lots of violence.- The voice acting is outstanding.- There's a high level of replayability in this game!  After 1 playthrough, I can confidently say that with only 36/108 achievements unlocked, there's at least 2-3 more playthroughs of content for you to enjoy.- New Game + , resolve features, and additional unlocks become available after the first completion.- Combat and tactics are fast, clean, and fun.- The upgrade system is straightforward.  You can focus on building stats, unlock new abilities, or unlock existing ability modifies.  Each character has 3 tiers of classes and 3 tiers of weapons they can upgrade to.Cons:- Some people didn't like the story because the first 1/3 of the game seems like a slow burn.  (For me personally, I chalk this up to patient world building that pays off in the middle and the end.)- Grinding for materials takes time.  You have to not only play practice scenario and mental matches, you have to be mindful of always picking up all enemy and map drops to optimize your party.  It can be difficult to tell which practice will yield which materials sometimes.- The weapon and class upgrade resources from the first playthrough are definitely finite.  You can't "Full grind to max" all of your characters attributes.  (Personally, I like putting in the extra grind to overpower the end-game, but was bummed you couldn't do it.)Overall:  8.5 out of 10  (Great job, Devs!)- I'll be playing this game more at a later date.  I'm very interested in seeing the alternative story paths.- I got the game on sale for $24.99 and totally got my money's worth.  "If" I had paid full price, I would still personally feel like my purchase was worth it having experienced the game in its entirety.- If a sequel happens, I would buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: I must admit i should have done more research before my purchase. This game is nothing more then a animated novel where you control the battles. If you want a good story then it's alright but not worth even close to the 60 bucks they ask for. There is no customization to the characters, only equipment you choose is 2 rings. For the most part the game is 2 hours of cutscences fallowed by a small exploration map, by small i mean tiny, 2 minutes to search it, then some vote scene, and a battle, repeat over and over again. Their are some training missions you can do when you choose for xp, items, and money, but other then that its more or less just a novel.
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very story-heavy, but I thoroughly enjoyed both the story AND the battles! On hard I'd often have to retry fights and develop my tactics, which is, you know, a lot of fun in a tactics-based game. Reading the reviews, I believe the focus on its story to be hit or miss, but as I said, I really enjoyed it!Something random I feel like noting is that I find it really impressive just how many memorable and distinct characters there are in a fantasy world such as this (where I'd normally tend to mix people up or forget names/faces), particularly with how early you meet most of them... and, at least for me, some of these characters really had a larger than life presence and I'd get so hyped when they'd become playable.Overall, I just find the game extremely impressive and really hope there's some continuation of the world in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: Story is mundane better to skip it entirely.Really put off early on when the decision to flee after reaching the "goal" so to speak. Felt like what I did accomplished nothing. Further decisions I didn't want to do were forced with the companion system. Figured if i couldn't convince them i'd just let them decide the next one anyway. Turned into a split decision where i had to decide the course regardless. Battle is interesting I actually enjoyed the positioning aspect and combos. Magic is meh, with the field system making or breaking it. The leveling system is crap, zero character customization. Everyone has a fixed class with linear class ups like swordsman > swordmaster. With limited upgrade materials you have to choose certain characters that have a class you like. Wish there was some variation in either class upg. or abilities you can customize. I'd like to bring a character you want, that might not fit your battle style. Having branching classes to change my parties make-up vs just swapping members out, that i might not even have access too. It seems like a missed opportunity.
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: Not very far into the game but far enough to feel this is a decent, not, it is a decent, not a really good game.Basically, classical Japanese STRATEGY Role Playing Game that people back in the late 90s and early 2000s enjoy. With cleaner presentations and voice overs.Bought it during sales, wouldn't recommend it for a full price purchase. Well it is up to you, I like the game. NOTE: Like not LOVE, decent not GOOD.
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say I've quite enjoyed Triangle Strategy so far. I have not finished my first run of the game yet, and I understand that it takes at least 4 runs to 100% the game, but I currently plan on doing such. The gameplay is solid, and the upgrade system, while a bit slow in my opinion so far, is enough to keep me invested in the grind.One thing that I haven't seen mentioned in other reviews that I'd like to throw out there is that when I first started the game I was not having a terribly good time. It felt like it took forever to get to any of the tactical part of the game, and the writing in the early game leaves a bit to be desired, as they try to present too much information at once leading to clunky lines clearly devised to advance the plot. HOWEVER, I found a simple fix that immediately made this game much more tolerable to me. I turned the voice volume down to zero. This is not a slight against the voice acting - I did enjoy a good amount of it. The problem is that leaving the voices on made each cutscene drag on for far too long, and admittedly there are a few characters that did not have the cleanest acting. Turning the voices off really brought out that old school Final Fantasy Tactics vibe that made the game much more tolerable, with the upside of getting to battles all the quicker. If you are struggling with the early game, I would recommend trying this and I would bet for a decent amount of others this will improve the overall experience. It's just one of those "too much of a good thing" scenarios where there is so much dialogue in between battles that waiting for the lines to be read to you is just a bit too time consuming, and rather than cutting off the voice acting as I read ahead I just turned it into a souped-up GBA game.
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: A good strategy RPG along the lines of the old Shining Force games or Final Fantasy Tactics with a few modern additions. The weakest part is the story, not for its content but for how it's told: mainly through overly-long strings of cut scenes and without much at the start to endear you to the characters or the struggle. Still a good game overall is you like the genre and far better than what we've had for quite some time.
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: I love the gameplay which is reminiscent of tactics ogre. I love the rpg mechanics and how the characters are all unique, interesting and, worth using depending on the situation. I however can't recommend this game because for some reason it crashes constantly. It's really discouraging to make your way through most of a tough fight only to have this game inexplicably crash and cost you half an hour of hard won progress. FIX IT PLS.
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: Great SRPG. Imo underrated.The game has branching story paths and a "morality" system where your choices affect on what missions you go and how the story evolves. Combat is a little different since there is no class system per se but all the unique characters have their own bunch of skills which you can upgrade etc.Pros:*Combat*Story (Geopolitical story with characters arcs)*Gfx (Similar to Octopath)*Difficulty (if payed on hardmode some missions are a real challenge and you can fiese your way around hardships)*Branching story paths/levels(bosses even change according to your choices)which adds replayability*Dialouge/story heavy (might not be your cup of tea)Cons:*if you go in blind it's really a matter of huge luck to be able to get the best ending so you'd need to do at least a NG+If not for my huge backlog, work and youtube(you can watch all the endings there) this would be one of the few games i'd come back to just to see the other paths.All in all a huge surprise of a game for me.8,5/10
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: ::1 hour into the game:: Okay, this is kind of boring...::10 hours into the game:: FOR HOUSE WOLFFORT!Game starts slow, but once it gets going... you're in for a good story. VERY story and dialogue focused which I don't mind because the story is great. Battles are of moderate difficulty but very fun. Each character brings something unique to the table so there's lots of customization for battling. Recommend this game for people that don't mind sitting through lots of dialogue and enjoys a political story. Side note: graphics in this game are gorgeous.
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: First of all this game has mostly interesting dialogue - it can drag on at some pointsThe visuals are great.My opinion would change if the game received a balance patch or had modding support to fix the poor difficulty curve.My complaint is the the difficulty is poorly tuned. I love hard games but the end game battles in the path i choose all combats devolved into the enemy zerging my front line with their superior numbers and 2 shotting my units. I ended up winning every battle by kitting the boss around with the units i kept alive and cycling them out after they get hit once. The only way not to get zerged is to rely on RNG debuffs.the final mission on my route requires you to guide uncontrollable units along a path guarded by archers that will ignore your units unless they can kill them. these archers 2 shot almost every unit on a non crit. you can imagine how fun it is to restart because you used your healer to keep whats left of your front line alive while the Ai unit literally decides to kill themselves by standing on a tile where they can be ranged.Mages require heavy investment to make workable considering you can attack twice until you get TP generation, but enemy mages are absolute monsters. Mild spoilers but Hyzante mages will be the bane of your existence, they will sit behind the zerg ball and will cast the most ridiculously powerful spell. Not only will your unit have a chance to get stunned but they will take so much damage they are pretty much guaranteed to die because the mages generally only cast if the AI knows it can kill someone.If you wanna win I highly recommend you build around Ana and Archers (you get one for most of the game however on my route) because Archers are broken. they trigger counter attacks from range and it's the easiest way to burst down the enemy zerg ball when they start bringing multiple healers. I find bringing only 1 or 2 mages is best because there's not enough damage boosting items to make their AOE attacks worthwhile when the enemy can just spam refresh 2 in the end game.Also I recommend levelling up the blacksmith, there's a couple of missions you can trivialise with spring traps.The economy is way too end game heavy. I had barely any money for most of the game, then as soon as end game hit I was so rich I had more consumables then I'd ever need.

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend the game; I think it's good enough to warrant a look for fans of the genre. It's enjoyable and has some difficult battles. But at 60€? No.The game has a lot of story sequences and non-battle exploration sequences, so be aware of that. These make up about half of the playtime, depending on difficulty.The overall story is interesting. It's sort of realistic-feeling three-way political power struggle. Unfortunately, where it fails is the conveyance of the story. I don't know if it's because of the translation or what, but the writing often feels too childish for the seriousness of the overall plot, the characters too caricatured and clichéd. You've got the always reasonable, right and just lord, the good-but-vengeful prince, the helpless-turned-not-so-helpless princess, you even have the obligatory "Luke you're my son"-moment. Evil characters will laugh evilly and so on. When do we get away from that crap, who knows.Also, the English voice-overs are unreasonably bad. I turned them to Japanese after two lines, so of course don't know how the later characters sound, but in any case I think the dialogue is easier to stomach in a language you're not familiar with.You occasionally have to make some decisions, and these are interesting thematically. The game utilizes a system where, in theory, you don't directly get to decide which choice you make, but rather your allies vote on it. However, you can affect their votes by persuasion and it is so easy to do that in practise you always get to do what you want. Great idea, but pointless execution.Battles are the move-and-do-action variety. The game utilizes the speed-based ATB-style battle system, which every game should have instead of the the usual "everyone goes once per round". Status effects are very powerful.There are four difficulty levels, the easiest being brains-off and hardest being quite hard, though the first half of the game is pretty easy on hard as well. It picks up significantly, though. You can change difficulty at any time.There is very limited character customization. The point of the game is that you have more characters than can be taken into battle, and each character has their own skills and stats, so you choose the best combination for the situation. It's a very simplistic approach, but works well in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: I love SRPG's.  Played them a lot ever since FFT back in the 90's.  I have never played Triangle Strategy on anything but hard and was blown away that the difficulty was just about perfect.  It's not too easy or too hard.  Though I would lose a lot in my first play through (first battle took a few attempts...), it was extremely rewarding working out more and more creative strategies to finally win a battle that seemed balanced towards the enemy's advantage.  And I bet there are a bunch of ways to win hard battles.  Which is the strength of Triangle Strategy; the game encourages the player to be creative and think outside of the box.  Best new game+ system imo too (tho CT still might be king), lots of replay value.
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: Put simply, if you like games like tactical RPGs, then this game is a must buy. Because of the lack of permadeath, the game can introduce a certain extra level of difficulty into its combat, making it much more engaging than the one-shot nature of a game like Fire Emblem Three Houses. No permadeath also allows for a breadth of tactical options, sacking a character is a valid tactic here. I'd recommend playing the game on the hard difficulty, as the combat really comes alive with the extra damage and health in the mix.In terms of the story, i'd say it is a 7 or 8/10, with my only complaints coming near the very end. The world is great, and feels well fleshed out, plot hooks laid out in the early stages of the game are satisfactorily delivered upon, and the the Scales of Conviction serve as an interesting mechanism by which you, the player, can make decisions. Music is banging, not too much to say there, but yeah. Its damn good. Visuals are phenomenal, but anyone can tell that from looking at the steam page haha.Uhh yea. excellent game, a beautiful entry into the tactical RPG genre. 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: Has its flaws, none of which are a deal breaker, but overall a good game with plenty to keep you engaged.Graphics: 8/10Charming HD-2D style, the perfect blend of pixel art and flashy spell and skill animations. Nitpick: why isn't there a sitting animation? So many thrones to sit on and desks to sit behind looking authoritative but there's no sitting animation. It's frustrating.Sound & Music: 8/10It's exactly what you'd expect from a Square Enix game. There's only a handful of catchy tunes that stand out, but most of the game is of the atmospheric/background type that fits in well with a strategy game where you're probably going to be listening to the same song for 15~20 minutes at a time during battle.Gameplay: 7.5/10Flashy animations and lots of character variety and tactical mechanics keeps you engaged, but some battles feel a bit dragged out due to how spread out units can be. Enemy AI can be a bit lacking but nothing gamebreaking (an archer unit that attacks, but then moves closer to melee range for some reason or a healer unit that runs far from the battle and is never able to get close enough to heal when it's needed). New Game+ exists, since gathering enough materials for all your units is impossible in one play-though (luckily there's multiple endings). Honestly, the game is more focused on the story.Story & Dialogue: 10/10This is the meat of the game, so expect there to be pauses in gameplay where you watch the story unfold. There's enough plot twists to put M. Night Shyamalan to shame and enough political maneuvering and backstabbing to make Game of Thrones look like two toddlers arguing over a toy. Some games claim that dialogue choices matter: in Triangle Strategy this is a very real part of the game. Your dialogue choices can change the course of the game along multiple branching paths, and the convictions & scales system is fascinating, ensuring that you actually need to know what each character's desires and motives are in order to persuade them to follow the path you want. There's a ton of gray areas in the dialogue, and there's no way of truly knowing (until New Game+) what way dialogue choices will go until the votes come in.

_childDocuments_.review: Much like my review of Octopath Traveler... Triangle Strategy was worth buying TWICE! I sunk 200+ hours in on Switch, and I'm starting fresh on Hard mode here on Steam for a challenging trophy hunt. Steam wants to pass the buck to SquareEnix, and Square to Steam - leaving we consumers out in the cold and condescended to.Back to a positive review, after Square (finally) applied a fix for the achievement bug in version 1.1.0.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about the game in general, but overall, I’d say it was enjoyable to play as a throwback to FFT style mechanics. Story/characterization is flat & predictable. I’d give the game 3/5 stars so just barely a positive review.Pros:+The graphics are a nice throwback to old sprites with a modern twist. If you've played Octopath Traveler, you'll recognize the atmosphere. A lot of work and detail went into the graphics and it's fun to watch all the character animations. Aesthetics change whenever you upgrade a weapon or promote a character to a more advanced level--all nice touches.+The music is really nice. It's not quite as epic as a typical Final Fantasy, but it isn't boring to listen to. I've even found myself humming a few of the tunes every so often.+The game is almost fully voice acted, which is a really nice touch. You can switch between languages--a feature that I always applaud.+The gameplay itself is quite fun. There are a variety of different characters with all sorts of abilities that allow for creativity in combinations. The battle system allows for a lot of fun interactions without being overly complicated or cumbersome.+I think it's great that they give you multiple story pathways to explore. It gives you a very real sense that you can control the outcome of what happens in the world.Cons:-If you're looking for something on par with a story out of Ivalice, this isn't it. It should be noted that Yasumi Matsuno, the creator of FFT, Tactics Ogre, FF12, etc. originally went to school studying foreign policy, which is a form of political science. He also had a background reporting on economics before he went into video game design. That said, you can see why his stories were more grounded and intricate when it came to political world building than other games on the market. By contrast, Triangle presents an overly simplistic and binary political structure. You have evil autocrats on one end and idealistic heroes on the other. There aren't many shades of gray and you don't really get a feel for what it's like to be an average citizen in any of the three countries. You'll get some average stump dialogue from town NPCs that either praises the government/main party or condemns them. I wish we could get a better look at average life in each country, but your view is limited to the top. All of the main party are characters that either come from aristocracy or are deeply affiliated with them such as retainers, advisors, etc. The economy is also rather nonsensical. As players, we're always reminded of a hefty tax on salt, but you don't really get to see either end of it. Who's paying for it, how, and where's the money really going? The whole premise really relies on the idea that “tax = evil” without showing any real repercussions or economic debate. There's supposedly a black market, but there's not enough information about it except it's "illegal" and the guy cooking the books is making a killing off it. We don't get to meet many average citizens to learn how they're making their money, how their expenses are split, and what government policies are in place to offset the salt tax burden. We're told that the Consortium exists to help mediate and regulate tax and trade, but it seems to be doing a really bad job. There's only one character from the Consortium and you barely ever get to interact with him. He’s presented as a wicked opportunist at first (and his portrait looks pretty sinister) but somehow at the end of one or two story arcs he suddenly turns into a fervent loyalist and supporter of the main party with no real explanation as to his motivations. We don't even see where all the tax money is really going. You can assume it's going towards the R&D of some stuff that's happening in Hyzante, but without more to go on, all you can do is speculate. If you don't care much for political world building, then this probably won't bother you. The simplicity might actually be a selling point. It's your typical good vs. evil story with a noble, good-hearted youth that topples two irredeemable governments. This isn’t really something I personally want to see in a game that’s being pushed as a spiritual successor to FFT, however.-Characterization is kind of flat. There isn’t much growth that’s shown. You get the sense that the two main protagonists started as righteous and then end as righteous as well. Trials and tribulations are sometimes implied, but not overly fleshed out. The principal main character is a bit of an overpowered, overly righteous idealist that keeps getting more titles added to his very young and untested name. Despite the titles, however, you rarely see him coping with responsibilities or political machinations that would often accompany these roles.Characterization for some of the other roster also lacks substance. Aside from your main party, when you reach certain milestones or make certain path decisions, you'll recruit new people to your army. Here you'll get one recruitment scene and then two little story scenes giving you a snippet of their lives and small personal arcs. Emphasis on the word "small". The characters in this game feel mostly tossed together. You don't get any deep ties and I personally didn't find myself getting any emotional attachment to most of them. A lot of the characters are pretty paper-thin and you don't get a sense of struggle or growth beyond a few of them. For a game that focuses so much on story rather than gameplay, I was hoping for more investment in characterization.-The English voice acting can be jarring at times. It falls a little flat in some places and some actors really don't sound right for their roles. I think most of the main characters have good or decent performances, but side characters get the short end of the stick in some places. It can get kind of cringey. In the rare instance that an NPC is voiced—usually a generic soldier of some sort—the acting is so bad that you can’t even really call it acting. It’s as if someone stuck an unpaid intern in front of a mic and said: “Here, read this.” A good actor can convey a character’s whole world in just one line.-The localization isn't the greatest. You can tell it's trying hard to be like FF12's. But whereas FF12 comes across as lyrical and Shakespearean, Triangle can come off as overly verbose, complicated, and sometimes awkward. There are rarely good lines, but they get buried under the mountains of superfluous text. I commend the localization's attempt to give the dialogue personality, but I wish it was punchier and more memorable. It ultimately falls pretty flat and unremarkable. Combined with the simple plot and convoluted, boring speech, I found myself skipping through a lot of dialogue because I just couldn't be bothered to care.-A lot of others have already commented on this, but the game is very story-heavy (even if the story is simplistic and mundane). There's a lot of exposition before you get to the battles, and those battles aren't all that many. If you love the gameplay a lot, you'll probably do what I've done and spend a lot of time at the Encampment where you can play Mental Mock Battles. I was really hoping for more map battles like you'd get in FFT, but sadly not. All story battles are scripted and there's no free roam on the map. Mock battles have no variation or randomness, either. You’ll always fight the same enemies in each designated battle. I always liked getting surprised when I got into battles in FFT, never knowing what kind of enemies would show up.If they ever make a sequel, I'd like more world building, tons more character exposition, and writing that flows better. I want to feel more emotionally invested in the characters and their world, and I'd like for the antagonists to be more than just one-dimensional liars, schemers, and murderers.
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: I feel this game does not get enough praise it deserves. Maybe the audience playing it is too young and have not experienced the two decades where we had a huge gap, lacking any decent Tactical JRPG games (especially on PC). The graphics are good. Main characters can grow on you. Story wise I have really enjoyed Triangle Strategy with it's plot twists. Lengthy dialogues (which some people may dislike) are well made although some side characters and their lines could have been made better with slightly more depth. Game-play wise it is also a winner that offers a decent challenge. There might be a bit of grinding required but I did not struggle with any story missions in particular, usually doing them 1-2 level below recommended one. The grinding itself is not painful but could have been made much better/accessible as you are basically repeating same missions to keep your team more or less up with the story difficulty. It kinda feel as a cheap trick to use mock training battles to fill in 20% of the game content - but like I said, it is not mandatory, and it doesn't kill the general positive reception of this title. I love the fact that there is a good replay value in TS for multiple walk-throughs to discover all the possible stories, characters and endings. Definitely a game that I will come back to after a year or so. Just make sure to play it with pad rather than keyboard and mouse.
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: Strong points of this game:1. Artstyle2. Graphical effects3. Relative originality to other videogames...But the one glaring thing wrong is the CONSTANT interruption and input bugs. The mouse is constantly getting stuck on menu items, causing misclicks. The player has no sense of when a cutscene is going to end, and some parts are not quickly skippable. You cannot go back to a previous cutscene so the cutscenes and dialogue become a constant tarpit. Most of what people say in the game is either tropey or useless in application. Side missions in the game are tutorials which pull you out of the game, some of the classes completely suck or overlap too much and the game has extra grind in it.I give this game a 7.5/10, there are too many hitches in the user experience and the game's concept is a bit rough. The player can't give a crap about the story because it's always interrupting the gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: Very pleasantly surprised by this one, going by the title and the one trailer I saw when it was released, I figured this one would be a dry, mechanics heavy, SRPG, almost like a Tactics Ogre with any of the ambition with a political story. What I got instead was a tightly designed strategy game that spends equal time with its story as well its combat mechanics. It's not that open ended in terms of character building, but the limited resources and character slots gives weight to your choices.They really should have gone with another name though.
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: This is a temporary review and I will come back to it with more time in.This was a Christmas present to myself and from the start, well...it is definitely a square enix game. The cut scenes are long and as it stands of nearly 2 and a half hours in I have been able to do 1 battle while the rest has been spent watching cut scenes. This so far is my only gripe as I have caught myself daydreaming or zoning out as the story line so far is...boring? I mean its no final fantasy but maybe I need more time in, but 2 hours to get through essentially a days time and explain the houses is a bit much. Lets move on to the game play and graphics. I have zero complaints about the art style and graphics, reminds me a lot of octopath traveler and I absolutely love this style. Feels like a Tabletop RPG come to life in pixel form...if they redid final fantasy 6 in this style or 7 even I would 100% buy them. Combat so far from the one battle I did do against the brigands I can see a mix of FF tactics in it with their own spin. I do however dislike the fact that characters get free moves if they surround you or you do the same...pretty cheesy in my opinion but its part of it so I will overlook it. all in all its a solid 7/10 for me so far and I don't regret the purchase, but as stated this is a temporary review and once I get through at least half the game or finish I will return to redo this. I just hope...that I get more action to cutscene ratio as so far its not looking good.
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: Triangle Strategy is a mixed bag. The on-map gameplay is satisfying, and the maps and character designs are aesthetically pleasing. Unfortunately, the story is presented terribly, with some of the worst voice direction I've seen in a video game. A line delivered with real emotion is a needle in a haystack. The characters just standing with minimal emoting spouting out text box after text box doesn't help, either. I can't honestly be sure if the writing was passable or not because the presentation just left everything feeling utterly droll. As for the main gimmick of the game, that being making choices, I still can't accept the fact that mere soldiers and retainers have a vote in how the lord proceeds each time. I don't care how trusted their opinions are. Overall, I can recommend the game to TRPG diehards, but most everyone else will likely quit after a few chapters out of boredom.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be fooled by the confusingly terrible name: this is your proper Final Fantasy Tactics sequel. Made by the same team within Square Enix that put together the unparalleled old school Final Fantasy spiritual sequel, Octopath Traveler, it delivers superb pixel graphics, an excellent branching story, and exceedingly well thought out gameplay.Yes, it is too narrative heavy at the start, and if you really want to skip over the Game of Thrones style world building, you easily can at the push of a button, but you'd be missing out on a fantastic story that does contain magic, but few other fantastical elements, being much more grounded in human interaction and societal questions.Yes, you can't change classes, but in doing so, each of the many recruitable characters ends up playing uniquely and has a lot more personality in battle, with different ones providing strong advantages in different types of maps.The game isn't overly drawn out for each playthrough, and respects your time by doing things like clearly pointing out different paths that you could have taken and allowing you to keep the experience that you gained even after losing a battle. Individual fights are all hand crafted and usually challenging, but with no character permadeath, they never get overly frustrating or demotivating. There are no random battles, but there are many interesting and varied selectable side missions that you can play whenever you want to gain experience and upgrade items. You can save pretty much any time, with even the story blurbs being cut up into sections of no more than five minutes.There's actually even a good variety to the game flow as you jump between story sequences, character dialogue blurbs, primary and optional battles, unit upgrading, a detective style town exploration hunting for items and information, and a series of moral quandries wherein you try to choose the correct arguments to convince the eight main characters (again, made by Octopath people) which direction your band should take.It's all a blast and it warrants its premium price. Play it.
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is fun but the game is bogged down by endless cutscenes and "choices" that you don't actually get to make. Often you will be shoved into lopsided battles that require grinding, being very good or heavy luck. Unfortunately while these should be avoidable by choosing another route you find that the game tends to lock you into routes and your choices don't really matter. Overall there are some decent points but the frustrations of never-ending dialogue, lack of your choices having an impact and the terribly unbalanced combat made this game a dissapointment.
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy. This game is a tactical JRPG masterpiece. An absolute must play. After sinking almost 40 hours into it, I've moved on to other games, though I can absolutely see myself returning to this game as I did not achieve the best ending nor many of the characters, many of the story arcs and a ton of achievements.Yes, as you might have heard, the pacing for this game is fairly slow. There's a lot of story. However...it's absolutely fantastic. The game does a phenomenal job with character development and the overall story. You become invested in the characters and their plights. You end up making decisions that have consequences for the outcome of the story. It's an absolute blast to watch how things develop through the story of this game and there is a ton of replay value as well.And the tactics gameplay itself...there is still a ton of it, and it's a lot of fun. The tactical system in the game is incredible and there are a lot of fun and challenging battles. Personally, I think the game balances story and battles extremely well. There's a lot of both...they're both incredible, and this game leaves you constantly wanting to come back for more. The game was definitely right up there in quality with Octopath Traveler for me, so any JRPG fans should definitely consider picking this one up.

_childDocuments_.review: About 7 hours into the game, maybe 4 combats, and 6 "one of three vaguely identical conversation options" events, each of which lead to the response of "I see, how interesting." Astonishingly uninteresting game. Tons of combat elements introduced, with no real combat opportunities that justify them. After the initial tutorial combat, waited through about an hour of conversation where every "plot point" was repeated three times, get to the combat at the tourney (knowing from my fantasy RPG knowledge that "tourney" means tutorial, despite already having had the tutorial combat an hour ago), and it is just both sides one movement range away from each other with no terrain features. Astonishingly uninteresting. Maybe it'll get better. As it stands, I boot up the game when I can muster the constitution required to accede the expectations that I'll have an hour to waste clicking through boring repetitive dialogue, and maybe eventually a dull, uninspired and tutorial-twinged combat will happen. It's a rare experience that I will yell at a game out of bored exasperation. That has occurred for me with this game during each game session over 7 cumulative hours. Maybe after 30 hours it will get better.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a bit like a Final Fantasy Tactics, but with a Game of Thrones like flair (the good seasons anyway). Each character has very unique mechanics, so the way you approach battles really does change depending on who you bring with you. It follows a consistent formula throughout - first you experience story cutscenes, then you're given "exploration" scenes where you talk to people and find hidden items, you then either enter a fight, or you convene a vote to decide which branching path you will take.I played on normal, and that provides a decent challenge. At no point did I feel like it was a brainless chore, nor did I ever feel overwhelmingly challenged. I've only beaten it once thus far, and have only just started on my new game plus run, so I don't know for certain how much the events vary based on your choices, but I get the impression that at least a few key points will have a dramatic impact on how the rest of the game plays out.At the very least, it seemed fairly obvious that your final choice WILL result in different endings. The graphics, aesthetics, UIn and sounds were all satisfactory to me. The game is complete. There are no annoying microtransactions, ads for other content, or obviously carved out content for DLC. I don't even think DLC exists for the game. The campaign is decently long as well. It took me around 60 hours to complete, and that was going at a relaxed pace - I didn't rush through, nor did I spend too much time grinding. I generally just kept my level at pace with or slightly under the recommendations for each combat.Overall, I'd say it's an excellent game. Unlike with some of the Fire Emblem games, where I find the last few levels to be a little TOO much of a slog for me, this game did a good job presenting higher challenges in the last levels without going overboard with the number of enemies (though there were more than usual). The final level in the path I chose was also extremely different than the rest - it was an escort quest that actually was enjoyable (I didn't think that was possible). I just had to make very smart use of my tanks.
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: Story and the choices you make are interesting. The battles are challenging, but fair. Even if you lose or quit, you still retain all the exp you gained, so it doesn't feel like a waste of time. The customization comes mostly from choosing which units to use, but there is still a bit of strategy when it comes to choosing which weapon and job upgrades to prioritize. The story:battle ratio balances out over time, as story battles can take a long time to complete. This is especially true if you play all the mock battles as they unlock.

_childDocuments_.review: Lets talk about the elephant in the room first. The first 2 hours. Felt disappointed and like refunding this game, because we didnt pay for a super nintendo visual novel right? Just 1 (fun) fight in there and lots of blablabla that makes no sense about a treaty between characters from 3 countries, all with grim looking portraits, plus weird tutorials.Then somehow, after that, and as the narrative evolves, it turns into one of the most engrossing tactical RPGs ever.In depth analysis:Possitives+ Final Fantasy Tactics battle system with all its intrincacies+ Multiple paths in the story for supperb replay value. The game always ask Serenoa, the main character, what he thinks, and builds a morality system according to the decisions he makes; from crucial political decisions to small questions like what do you think of the Rosalians (a race of pink haired humans treated as sub humans in this world)+ the story is actually nice. Every major character from the 3 countries has a scheme and having to make the decisions for the main character is mentally taxing sometimes. Crazy that salt is so important in this world.+ The world feels like an Ivalice lite+ Lots of Mage units that unlock as you play the game in the form of "characters stories". Love wizard units in tactical games. But also archers, buffers, warriors, etc.+ customization in the form of spending resources, money, materials, to level up characters, and making decisions on which characters to level up and how. Example, I focused all my resources on mages and buffers cause I like that style+ mental mob battles and replay of story battles for rewards in the camp keep this game from being too visual novelish+ hard mode from the start. I played 100% in hard mode and without spoilers, there is a lot of depth and every decision could be crucial in the tactical battles. Checkmate situations happen. I managed to overcome a battle with 2 units agaisnt like 8 units thanks to the terrain advantages (and Hughette flying), for example.Negatives- graphics are not quite on Octopath Traveler 2 level despite being a similar style- no dual classes or a compelling job system for units means not as much customization as old Final Fantasy tactics games- No monsters or humanoids. Only soldier units from the 3 countries and boss characters- The first two hours dont represent the overall quality of the game- Too visual novelish sometimes- the soundtrack, while trying to be Hitoshi Sakimoto, fails to be memorable save for 1 or 2 songs. It fits the narrative and Ivalice lite world well however.- some grinding required if in hard mode sometimes but only for really hard battles- no water bodies like swamps or rivers from Final Fantasy tactics- not sure how Serenoa "convictions" change with each decision. It is there but the game dont tell you in form of quantitative data.- The exploring parts feel like a gameboy gameFair score overall, 7.5 to 8/10 (the first two hours are a 6/10). If into tactical rpgs like me, 9 to 9.5/10. Never thought I would like a visual novelish game so much (Final Fantasy XII is my favorite jrpg ever btw). Hopefully the next one improves all the negatives. Worth it 100% at the $30 price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: What a unique and great game!People complain about 2 things: the game is too story driven and too grindy. Both are just wrong!The game is not story driven it is a big awesome political plot and the strategy combat part are just to round it up. If you don't like fascinating stories and just come for the strategy and fights, than this game is not for you.You get the option to just do some training combats where you earn exp and materials but that is not meant to grind to oblivion and you don't need to.Do the fight get harder? _childDocuments_.review: Triangle Strategy, for me, was a little too bland. It felt like the developers really wanted to make a grand Game of Thrones-ish storyline filled with twists and turns, but also were afraid of making complex characters. The characters and overall story didn’t really engage me, and the twists and turns that you go through during the game just sort of fell flat for me. The tactics gameplay kept me going through to see one of the four endings, but I had no desire to see the other three.The flow of the game is a little strange. The general outline is that you have a bunch of cutscenes, some of which are optional to view, and then you eventually get to a small map to explore where you run around picking up items and talking to characters, and then sometimes you go through a voting phase with your party where you make decisions about what to do, and then you have a story battle. In between those story beats, you can visit your party encampment where you can grind on what are called “mental mock battles” or do some upgrading for your party.I really enjoy tactics gameplay, so that basically kept me going through to the end, but I really had to force my way through the last few chapters. I wouldn’t call this an explicitly bad game, but I wouldn’t call this a great game either. If you really dig tactical games, maybe pick it up, but be ready to sit through a lot of dialogue you might not really care about and experience some twists that feel a little forced.I can't really hit a thumbs down on this game because it wasn't a terrible game by any means, just sort of boring near the end.

_childDocuments_.review: So far this game looks excellent! The artwork and style remind me of the original Final Fantasy Tactics on PS1! I am enjoying that this is a very story-heavy tactical RPG. Most of the time, the beginning will be exposion-filled and peppered here and there with battles. Later on though the TRPGs I have played in the past usually allowed for more frequent action if not infinite battle time to farm and level up or do side quests after the bulk of the story was played through. I don't know yet, but I do hope this one does that too! Square-Enix usually doesn't disappoint me! They're always good to me as a fan of many Final Fantasy games and movies and more!

_childDocuments_.review: So this game is getting a bad rap so here is my recommendation.tldr The game is good. If you like world building, narrative and Turn based tactics its a great game.It has a huge narrative and world building aspect where much like final fantasy tactics it builds this huge story to ground you in the world,politics and choices. You get notes and written narrative much like final fantasy tactics where you learn a lot of information between events/cut scenes that is none essential/essential but lovely to read none the less.All major cut scenes and events are fully voice acted with exploration phases being written dialogue. Even in the English   the majority of the characters are nice to listen to, engaging and emotional.Exploration phases you basically are able to freely move around a map to explore chat with people, make choices and learn about the world the mc lives in. You can also find "hidden treasures" on most exploration phase's.The first 2 hours or so are basically introductions to the numerous system's, story and people in this world. You chat with people get information only to use that information to make choices/convince followers to go where you want to go. Basically you need to explore talk and learn information about the world so you can make important choices. Introductions to combat.They could of added a couple more practice battles between this narrative portion but it does change around the 2 hour mark.The game isn't for everyone but it is for me. Much like final fantasy tactics it is drawing me into a different world where I feel a abit more grounded compared to other fantasy games.
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: The game is cool, reminds me of tactics ogre and final fantasy tactics (both of which I loved), but... it has a lot of shortfalls.I should preface by saying I really like difficult games and try to make them more difficult for myself (hardest difficulty settings, personal custom rules, etc.).  The reason is I really like to engage with the strategy of the game and sometimes taste defeat and feel rewarded for my tactics.  Triangle Strategy did not do that for me.  It's not that there is no strategy, but the inability to prevent enemies from just waltzing by your front line and instead rely on disables (multiple that are based on random luck) means that RNG and AI stupidity will be the major determining factors of the outcome.I should also mention the characters have cool interactions with each other, are unique, and overall quite enjoyable.  I like the characters in this game.  Some are kinda silly but I just chose not to use them.The UI is also gorgeous, and the maps are very well done.  However, for some reason I found using the UI cumbersome and clunky.  Not totally sure why, but I still quite enjoy the visuals in the game.However, neither the poor AI or UI are the biggest faults of the game.  The biggest one is the plot and time spent on it.  The game will FORCE you to talk about issues ad nauseam.  You will go in and out of cut scenes watching the game say "saving" just to enter a scene about a guy saying that he wants to talk about an issue.  It seems minor but it actually kinda ruined the game for me.  I'd spend over an hour just walking around feeling forced to talk to random villagers about whether they like salt or not.  Then watch a 5 minute cut scene about the main character saying "maybe we should think more about salt".  Then another 5 minute cut scene about him talking to his advisor saying "My lord! Let's talk about salt".  Then another 5 minutes for another stupid cut scene.  I feel like more than HALF of the entire game is just watching scenes and watching scenes load, maybe 30% of it is actually battles (this sentence I do NOT feel is an exaggeration).   I kind of knew this getting in, but I thought it was only the beginning.  So I pushed myself to learn the plot, all the characters, etc. and read through the beginning plot (and it was not fun but kinda OK plot)...  I was thinking that afterwards it would be more about battle and strategy and the plot would get good.  I was wrong, it was still so many seemingly arbitrary and useless scenes and dialogues.  I started skipping them all (which I really did not want to do) and then I realized it was still taking over half the game... Unfortunately, I did not finish this game, and I don't think I will.

_childDocuments_.review: Well made game. This is 50% tactics game and 50% cut-scenes. The voice acting is great and the cut-scenes really get you into the lore and politics. This not explained in the game and is hidden in your first play through.If you only have time to play this game once, there are multiple endings and I would recommend a guide to help figure out how to get the "golden route" ending.

_childDocuments_.review: Triangle Story is a graphically beautiful game, but the combat and mechanics are a disappointment. In comparison to other strategy games there are very few battles to the actual main story-line of the game. The one positive of this is there are no filler battles in the story-line, but it feels like the game is mostly small cut-scenes. There are a glut of characters you receive over the course of the game and in a normal strategy game there would be enough content to fully explore each of these, but in TS if you want to "taste" all the different ways to play you will have to do the mental battles over and over and over and over. I wish there was more to chew on. I would avoid buying this game. Do yourself a favor and purchase Tactics Ogre: Reborn. Far superior game.

_childDocuments_.review: 100% a worthy spiritual successor to Tactics Ogre and Final Fantasy Tactics. Each party member feels unique in their style of gameplay and battles are appropriately balanced. The story deals with heavy topics with very few missteps. It's very clear that there's a lot of love from the dev team for FF Tactics and Tactics Ogre, but Triangle Strategy firmly establishes its own identity and stands on its own merits. Hell, it's even pretty clear that the writers did their research on actual historical wars.If you have any love for the Ogre Battle series or for the Ivalice setting in Final Fantasy, this is well worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: very fun well designed standard stock jrpg with grid turn based combat. Some fun extras that add to combat like height/surround/elemental/terrain/AP mechanics which all feel relatively good to play around with. Love how fluid combat feels in general in this game, and you learn what sorts of mistakes you can make wrt positioning fast in this game. One con is the poorly balanced characters (although this game is better than most srpgs), My interpretation was that mages healers OP, tanks meh, mounted characters generally pretty good. end game isn't super fun, skill/weapon progression unsatisfying and non-transformative can feel silly to upgrade (ATK +1) in circumstances. This is a pretty difficult issue for turn based games in general I feel but this game definitely doesn't manage to solve it. most maps are pretty fun to play, takes a few tries on hard mode but intuitive and not frustrating to solve aka good degree of difficulty that requires user to use at least a bit of their brain. I would say that the strength of this game is definitely the map design, many maps feel super unique and I would still remember them weeks later if prompted. Overall the weaknesses are that story is too long, characters are kinda dumbasses and unlikeable but that's also a pro for the story in a way, cinematics/explore mode are clunky for a game that is so story focused, it should not be so difficult to go through the story. Generically the lore is simple, easy to keep up with, and generally interesting which is exactly what I'd want from a game. I enjoyed keeping up with the story even though it dragged. recommend for any modern SRPG gamers.
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: After 150hrs and reaching 100% of the game 6 months ago, I can definitely say this was one of the best turn based tactical rpg in recent years. The HD-2D artstyle is beautiful and is complimented by an amazing soundtrack and branching story with 4 different endings. While the combat may not be as complex as ogre reborn it still offers a reasonable challenge with a vast roster of characters to play around with.
_childDocuments_.name: TRIANGLE STRATEGY

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is awesome, however there is too much dialogue in this game. Characters will go on and on about their views and ideas for literal hours. There are multiple sections in the game where you have to sit through an hour of cutscene dialogue just to be able to land in a battle to play the game. The story although well-thought out, has very long-winded dialogue that could be written more concisely. There are moments where you understand a character's motive and you want them to move on, only for them to simply keep ranting circularly about their ideals. Honestly an easy fix for the dialogue could have been how they did it in past Tactics games, such as FF: Tactics, FF: Tactics Advance, Valkyria Chronicles, which all have dialogue play out seamlessly throughout combat. Had they gone down this route, they could have added in more gameplay while being able to divulge the plot at a steady pace. Instead we get 1 hour of dialogue -> 30 minutes of combat -> 1 hour of dialogue -> 30 minutes of combat. This format gets a bit grueling after a while especially when you've just had an amazing time playing a combat sequence only for that emotional high to be stopped by boring long-winded dialogue that lasts an hour. Because of this I could not play this game in long-sittings. Knowing I had to sit through long dialogue just after a battle really was a huge turn-off. The characters are not one-dimensional but they are also not the best. Some characters also betray their entire character arcs in order to create alternative choices players have to make in the game. I was not the most pleased by this. There are several characters who have distinct ideologies and moral compasses throughout the story that are supposedly unwavering. There are instances where they will almost jump to opposite conclusions just to create conflict, which I personally attribute to just bad writing. This happens a few times but having said this it isn't a deal breaker. The gameplay itself is amazing, and I wish there was more of it. In a nutshell it is basically extremely similar to FF: Tactics, but with some added strategic elements. If you're a fan of turn-based strategy RPG's you will love the combat system. My only gripe with it is, I feel like things were only starting to get challenging before the game ended abruptly. The story really picks up in the 2nd to last chapter, and gets super interesting. I wish they had gone further with those concepts presented near the final chapter and perhaps they will decide to make a sequel following that. Overall the game is worth getting if you like these type of games. If you want to play for the story however, it isn't amazing or anything. It will carry you enough to the end of the game with exception of the last 2 chapters. Gameplay: 10/10Story: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I enjoyed the game. There were a few cons that I feel you should be aware of.1.you aren't actually in control of the choices you get to make. There is a hidden rating system that consist of 3 values, that the game doesn't show you and if your rating doesn't meet the requirement for a choice that you wanted (the game doesn't tell you the requirement for the choice you want) then you cant get the choice no matter what dialogue option you chose. These 3 values are gained based on dialogue choices and other weird things that shouldn't even count. For example killing units, looting, buying and selling stuff increase one of the 3 values when they shouldn't play a role in the story decisions I want to make. There is no sense of consequence to choices as if you didn't get the option you want its always oh my rating doesn't line up not, oh I made this choice early thats why I can only do this choice.2. Mouse keyboard controls are terrible. Not terrible in the sense that the binding is bad but more so that it is unresponsive and clunky. You can play the game on either mouse or keyboard so when you try to use both inputs at once the game has trouble registering your commands.3. they went the lazy route for difficulty level. Higher difficulty is just enemies have more stats when they should have added more units/change enemy unit placement to make the battle harder.4. Your companions get exp by doing damage/buffing/using items. You don't get any exp at the end of an encounter nor from any quest. Meaning when your ally dies early in the fight they miss out on a good amount of exp. Which doesn't incentives you to take risk in battle. This also means there is no point in swapping out companions as the ones you don't bring into battle will always be underdeveloped.

_childDocuments_.review: I have put 180 hours into the Switch version and was very excited for the Steam version to be announced. This has become my most favorite tactics RPG of all time and one of my favorite games overall. Gameplay - 10/10The most appealing aspect of this game for me is the battle system and character progression. Each character has their own skill tree to upgrade their specific kit - this means every upgrade you get for a character is relevant to them and rarely feels wasted. The battle system has been masterfully designed to contain a lot of depth and complexity hidden by its overt simplicity. Winning a difficult battle feels satisfying and rewarding. The game rewards you even for losing a battle by allowing you to keep XP earned but forgets about any items used. This makes the game less of a grind. For those like me who enjoy Hard mode, throwing yourself at a battle over and over is much less frustrating when your squad is getting incrementally better each time. There are 30 characters in the game and each is completely unique with real applications, almost no characters feel like filler or unusable. Experienced players are rewarded after beating the game, as New Game+ offers a huge list of quality of life improvements for the rest of your playthroughs on that save, and probably one of the most exciting and rewarding New Game+ experiences of any game I have played due to the branching paths.Story - 7.5/10The story is quite deep and interesting. Each choice you make puts you into a different scenario, which means that even on my 3rd playthrough I was still seeing cutscenes and playing battles that I had not yet done. Yes, as noted in other reviews, the story can be quite dense at times. I personally enjoy a rich story in my games, and the Game of Thrones-esque drama in Triangle Strategy is very fulfilling and your patience with the story is paid out by the different endings. On subsequent playthroughs, you can easily skip or fast forward through every cutscene and get straight to the good stuff if you want.Graphics - 9/10The HD-2D graphics in this game are beautiful, and the graphical performance really shines on the Steam port. Playing the game at 60 FPS makes all the difference as the effects of the environment and overworld are allowed to breathe. The game still is such that those with laptops or other computers that might struggle with some AAA games should be able to play it on most devices, though I have not personally tested this.Sound - 8/10The soundtrack of this game includes some absolute bangers that will get stuck in your head for days at a time. The voice acting is inconsistent at times as mentioned by other reviewers but it was never bad enough to break my immersion too badly. I have heard that turning on Japanese voices helps some with their voice acting complaints, though I have never felt a need to do this.Steam Port - 10/10As far as differences between Switch and PC, I will share my early experiences: as I mentioned the FPS difference is very noticeable. I was able to run this game on Steam Deck with no issues, however for some reason I had to launch it once from the desktop side before it would launch in SteamOS. Note this was moments after the game released on Steam so your experience may vary but give this a try if you are having issues. Having 108 achievements at release was also very exciting: this game feels like a completionism challenge for me and the achievements illustrate the work needed to "100%" the game very well. The mouse and keyboard controls will take some getting used to for me as I have spent 180 hours playing with a controller, however I do like how fluid the game feels with a mouse at first glance. I did connect a controller right away for PC play anyway.Overall - 9.5/10If you are a fan of tactics RPGs I highly suggest you give this game a try. There is a demo on Switch that includes the first 3 chapters if you are unsure. I am excited to see if Square Enix gives us a sequel or DLC in this universe as this game has completely hooked me.

_childDocuments_.review: I've managed to play this game on most of its difficulty settings and see almost all that it has to offer. With that being said - this is an incredibly well-designed tactical RPG that you should seriously consider.The story elements are above average for this genre. Keep in mind - that I generally despise the writing in these strategy RPGs. However, the story has good twists and turns and the branching paths you can take are actually interesting. The "Voting" mechanics are not difficult to manipulate as a player and you can guide the story wherever you want without trouble.The number of time wasters in the game are lower than average - but still need some call outs here. First of all, there is an "Exploration" mechanic before most battles where you get to run your character over the battlefield before the fight begins. This is interesting for getting a tactile feel of the landscape, but kind of unnecessary. During your exploration, you can talk to individuals, find items, ETC . . . some may favor this, but I felt it was a waste of time.Similarly - the story sequences can take a bit longer than you may like. They are all very skipable, but there is a decent bit of story here. Once you play through the game once and can confidently skip the story bits, the pacing of the game improves .Pacing during fights is actually quite good so long as you hold the fast-forward key. This is nice, because if you do want to watch things play out slowly - you can do that - and the fast-forward key allows you to move through enemy turns very quickly. With the sheer volume of units on the field, you need this speed, and the pacing is good to allow you to move through a fairly large engagement at a reasonable pace.This is the bread-and-butter of the game, and it delivers in a great way. The combat is absolutely fantastic. Working synergies between your units and working through the enemy is very satisfying in the game. I won't say overly much here other than the combat is extremely enjoyable and the tactical options you have are vast due to the number of characters available to you and the very well-designed maps. Elevation is well done and positioning options are varied and interesting. There are a variety of ways to position and attack.The difficulty settings demand a special mention as I would highly recommend you play the game on "Normal" difficulty. It is very well-balanced at this difficulty and an experienced RPG fan should find this to be a sufficient challenge.The "Hard" difficulty is for masochists. I played through most of the game on hard difficulty on my first play through and it is doable - but you have to min-max and abuse every micro-advantage you can to move forward. "Hard" difficulty is most enjoyable when you've fully accessed every unit in the game, have maxed their statistics, and you want to push the limits of what the game has to offer.There are a TON of characters in this game. Your ability to customize them is fairly limited, mostly through 2 accessories and through what abilities you choose to upgrade first - but I like this quite a bit. Instead of building a character to a certain archetype, you have pre-built archetypes that you choose from to try to fit into the right situation. After playing a lot with all of the characters - I genuinely believe they are all quite viable and interesting. Some are more niche, some are better at higher levels than lower levels, but all of them are very interesting and fun to try to use. This system is extremely well-designed and deserves to be recognized.The only negative is that you will unlock a large number of characters toward the end of the game - making it feel a bit odd if you just want to play through the game once. This game regrettably is infinitely more enjoyable on your second play-through than your first - which is probably the worst thing I can say about the game.Overall - I highly recommend this game because its favorables massively outweigh its unfavorables. I was very impressed.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is way worth the money, if you like strategy games with turn based combat, it is a must play. You feel the choices you have to make... and the consequences. However in my opinion the game has three downsides (nothing is perfect after all). 1. The summary between every chapter part from the narrator is quite annoying, even if you can skip it. It just tells you again what you just experienced through dialogues in the story.2. The difference between normal and Hard Mode. While in normal Mode the combats where no big challenge the hard mode seems almost impossible (at least for my level of skill). This difference is a liitle odd since normal mode was almost too boring and Hard mode impossible.3. Character development. To level all characters (which is under certain circumstances neccessary) you need not only to grind levels but also the smithing materials. Unless you play in easy or very easy it is definitely necessary to grind quite a bit. Doing the same level a few times gets boring very quick, despite the different character palystyles.That said, In my opinion the pros outweigh the cons. Since you can replay the game for the different endings and choosing other routes throughout the story set you partially on a complete different path than before with new story dialogues and new battles. So that you can even replay it at least once and it feels like playing another part of a game series.

Sure, the world and its history is laid out really well, but it's also pretty generic medieval power struggle we've seen many times over. Soundtrack also struggles to produce even a single memorable track, which is all the more tragic given the HD-2D predecessor. Even the art design barely takes advantage of all the graphical tools available.You're just as likely to enjoy the game as you are to forget about it afterwards.7.3/10
