_childDocuments_.review: Triangle Strategy (Overall Game Play)I have been playing Triangle Strategy for quite some time now, a total of 303 hours to be exact which is equivalent to 12 and a half days. This game has been a great discovery for me and I consider it the Game of the Year for 2023. Although I discovered it a little late as my attention was focused on Crystal Project in 2022. The overall game play is amazing, the story line is captivating, and the character growth throughout each game play is impressive. I particularly love the fact that you can acquire different characters, each with their own strengths and weaknesses, but when combined as a team, they are unbeatable. This game is definitely challenging and is recommended for those who enjoy role-playing or tactical games.(Recommendation)I highly recommend playing Triangle Strategy, especially if you're a fan of tactical games. As someone who loved playing games like Final Fantasy Tactics growing up, I always hoped for a sequel. Although we never got one, Triangle Strategy is an excellent substitute. While it might not surpass the level of Final Fantasy Tactics, it's definitely on par with it.The only downside to Triangle Strategy is that you have to play through it multiple times to unlock all the characters. Even after beating it without a guide, I still missed some characters. I had to replay it a few times to get them all, and even then, I had to use a guide. Despite this inconvenience, I still think the game is excellent. If there was a way to unlock everything in one play through, that would be ideal. However, even with this issue, I would still recommend playing it. While it's not perfect, it's pretty close to it. I would give it a 10 out of 10 rating.*Rating*10/10

_childDocuments_.review: So glad this came to PC.  I loved this game on Switch as I put well over 100 hours into it.  I was on the fence about it and almost didn't buy it and by the end of the year it was my favorite game of the year and all the ones I was hyped for felt like letdowns. The combat is a true strategy RPG which is the strongest point.  Between the ability to make ladders and walls etc it actually made every other SRPG I've played feel like it was made for small infants with no actual thought or build variety.  The lack of jobs was a bummer at first but after a few run throughs you realize the kits are so specialized and balanced it wouldn't be possible to do any other way as stacking some stuff would have broken the game.  The choices you make actually lead to different missions and not just a different one liner as a reply and I could go on and on but at the end of the day I highly recommend this game.  I do wish some special stages weren't only really seen once in like one ending and there were more mock battles but my hope with it being on PC is that maybe one day fans can add more content and improve the graphics beyond the point where the final product was left as unlikely as that seems to ever happen.  The game does pick up in pace and you learn to appreciate the dialogue I do admit it was a lot at first but the ability to skip scenes and in new game plus runs the fact enemies scale and you recruit more allies as you go through different routes gives you a lot of bang for your buck.

_childDocuments_.review: No, really, the writers of this game believe that your IQ is negative. It is obvious from the story that they wanted to tell a tale of political intrigue, of politics and backstabbing, of philosophy and the darker side of human nature. They wanted this to be Game of Thrones. And to their credit, the actual plot of the game is exactly that - political scheming and backstabbing and people changing sides while vying for power.However, it feels like a studio executive looked at the script and said "dumb this down so children can easily understand it" and now you have Triangle Strategy. The characters stop and recap to each other every conversation, just in case the player is too dumb to understand the very basic info that was just stated. The characters themselves are also portrayed as very oblivious in this manner, so other characters have to point out the obvious to them and keep the player up to date.The characters are one dimensional and have zero nuance. Most of the main cast of playable characters fit nicely into a stereotype and that is ok; where it really fails is the villains. The villains are just evil because they can be. Rude to everyone for no reason, laughing at their own evil schemes. Pretty sure they all go out for drinks after hours and look for puppies on the sidewalk to kick just to make children cry. Meanwhile the hero is a perfect boy scout at all times. It's extremely black and white, with no depth to either side.The reason I focus so hard on the story in this review is due to just how much story there is, with numerous, long cutscenes in every chapter. I only played three battles in the first six hours of play time; the rest was cutscenes and wandering around town talking to NPCs and making decisions. When a game features so much story, that story should be better written than this. There is also the voice acting, which is soulless and emotionless from the protagonist and his fiance.This is doubled down on by the fact that the characters frequently come together to vote on the next course of action, which can have major story implications and/or choose which level to go to next. If you have skipped through the dialogue, you may miss critical clues, and then be unable to convince your followers to agree with you. I was actually outvoted once in my playthrough and not allowed to visit the area I wanted to go to. So you can't even skip the dreary dialogue, otherwise you may be penalized or get a bad ending.For the actual gameplay, it's surprisingly good. I know I just tore the acting and characters apart, but the battles do make up for it. Snappy turns and movement, creative skills, lots of playable characters, pleasing visuals, and fun mechanics. The battles are very fun and kept me playing to the end. The only downside is customization - there isn't any. You can't change classes, or weapons or armor, or anything. You get two slots for accessories and there are very few accessories in the game to pick from, so putting together your own custom 'builds' isn't really possible here. The customization instead relies on experimenting with different party member combinations, since every character brings completely separate skill sets to the field.I have seen a few people mentioning in their reviews that this game is too easy; that may be true on normal settings but if you want a challenge you can put it on Hard. This game will absolutely and ruthlessly destroy you right out the gate with no mercy on Hard. It's not exactly balanced though, as every enemy has mountains of HP and hits much harder than you, so you have to play perfectly and/or cheese every encounter. But if you really want a challenge, that option is there.Overall I recommend the game for its strategic fun, but I caution anyone who was looking for a deep or compelling story and memorable characters to pass on this. Go play Tactics Ogre: Reborn instead if you are looking for a SRPG with actual characters and storytelling.Characters are dumb and forgettable, and many have painfully bad voice actingPlot of story is okCombat is good, very funMany characters and strategiesNo customization, your characters come in a boxPrepare to sit through very long cutscenes

_childDocuments_.review: Triangle Strategy is a fun game, but I think the biggest flaw of why i cannot recommend is that the story telling side and the combat side clash with each other making the experience jarring. One moment you will be stuck in 30-60 minutes (depending on if you listen to the voice acting) of exposition and storytelling, and then next you will be in a slow paced tactics combat for the next hour. Of course, at all the climatic moments of the story tend to culminate in a battle. As soon as i start to get into the story the put you into a cliffhanger situation as you are forced to fight. If the combat didn't take so long and there was more battles spread between (which i can understanding be difficult from a story telling perspective) it wouldn't be as annoying. Honestly the story is somewhat simple - i didn't feel inspired by any of the characters, they all feel very superficial, but the scale and events are interesting enough to have a few interesting moments. The voting gimmick felt dumb since you could generally sway the votes the way you wanted very easily. The JP voice acting is really good, but i somewhat wish i just read the text since the story sections were so long. Combat was okay - generally the best tactic is to ball up and auto-attack. The difficulty on normal didn't really force me to use any of the tactic buffs so it felt like a waste of time to spend the extra 5-10 minutes of combat to play tactically when i could generally just play recklessly. I love playing spell casters but they felt horrible to play since they could only cast using 2 energy meaning they could only act every other turn.Overall, decent tactics game, but i would not recommend if you are not a hardcore fan of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: This might be my new favorite game, wow. I'm mostly writing this because I just need to process my thoughts on it. I spent my evenings for basically a whole week on voice chat with friends while playing this and spending the rest of the day working on stuff and thinking "oh man, I'm gonna be able to play more Triangle Strategy!". Even though I noticed some flaws, I was having such a great time that I really didn't care about any of those problems.It's not for everybody, since it is very, VERY dialogue heavy and it has a very slow start. After the first battle is probably about 2 hours of exposition (then again I was taking my sweet ass time), but once the ball gets rolling there is not a single dull moment. It also tends to overexplain things and repeat them a lot, but honestly I know that was helpful for me to understand the plot, I might have been lost otherwise. The choices they have you make are actually difficult and interesting choices, not like the old mid 2000's "Be a good person or be selfish and mean and evil". They're very compelling and every single one saw me completely stop in my tracks from anywhere between a few minutes to half an hour (maybe longer, I wasn't really keeping track) just so I can make a decision about what I want. And it's not as simple as clicking a dialogue box either, since you have to persuade your allies to your side. I really like this because you need to use what you know about the characters and try to respond with what they would find most convincing, which is not always the objectively smartest thing to say.Speaking of characters, some of them can come off as sort of dull to same, and to an extent I agree, but a lot of them have enough subtle intricacies once you dig into them that they can stay interesting. I still got very invested in them, and I got really emotional and nearly cried at the ending I got. I'm also weird, and a lot of games that make others emotional don't do anything for me, so who knows.The combat system is easy to understand and has a lot of flexibility, with every single attack able to take advantage of a number of factors like height advantages, back attacks, paired follow-up attacks, things of this nature that you will try to take advantage of whenever possible. Every character is so distinct from one another, so even though there is not much character customization, there doesn't need to be, it's more about finding which character you need for which task. This all comes with some great level design that will constant throw new things at you. And to top it all off, if you get a game over you still keep all the experience you got while still getting your items back, so even though you can grind on skirmish maps, you don't have to at all. I played on normal and I found the perfect level of difficulty for me was just starting just a tiny bit underneath the recommended level. And you'll almost certainly stay in that range since underlevelled characters will catch up absurdly fast and overlevelled characters will slow down a lot so they don't outpace the rest of the army. The balance is absurdly well tuned.I'm a sucker for the 2D sprites in the 3D environments, blend together so seamlessly that barely even remember that's what they were doing. The soundtrack is also full of bangers. The voice acting is hit or miss though, some of the actors were incredible and others are just wooden. The main character is fairly monotone most of the time, but the actor has some real standout moments, so I suspect this was more of a directing issue than an acting one.I think I've run out of thoughts for now, but wow I really love this game. If you're interested and the flaws I described aren't deal breakers for you, give it a shot. Some say that it shouldn't be worth 60 bucks, but for a 40 hour RPG I think that's fair. Feel free to wait for a sale regardless, though, that's always worth it. I will absolutely jump back in at some point to try out the choices I didn't go with in a new run, the only thing keeping me from doing so immediately is because FE Engage comes out in a week and I don't want to get too deep into something so close to it. But even though I'm a huge Fire Emblem fan, it's gonna take a lot for this new game to beat this one out.

_childDocuments_.review: A game with a half baked name like "Triangle Strategy" ends up as a half baked experience.The new tactic these days is to lure people in with nostalgia and charge premium prices on games that are only side projects, and sadly as you can see based on the "very positive" reviews, it works.So you got the story with is stretched thin to hide the fact that there really isn't as much there, but then you have the extra layer of laziness of the combat being obnoxiously simple and having very little depth.  Normal difficulty is too easy, and Hard difficulty is artificially inflated to stretch out those gameplay hours even more, but because the game is really deep as a puddle the investment to progress is higher than the actual quality of the experience you get back.  So then normal is generally the better way to play or you'll be replaying battles way more than you should, but then normal just becomes "get through it" mode, so fights are boring and monotonous, to then get boring and monotonous story.Not to mention the voice acting is actually so poor that it makes the experience truly a chore to play through.  Absolutely no passion was given in any of the performances to the point where it has a huge damper on the story.I try playing for 1 hour and I just get so bored I want to gouge my eyeballs out.  Then I boot up FF12 or basically any other good game and 5 hours go by like nothing even happened.  Do yourself a favor and skip this game, and maybe skip every nostalgically fueled marketed JRPG from Squareenix from now on, as none of these games have any real reason to play them, unless you're just that desperate to relive your childhood and can't see a genuinely bad game even when its staring you in the face.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're considering buying Triangle Strategy, you should. There simply aren't enough tactics games to be picky, and this one is worth your time.With that out of the way, let's dive into the details. The game is good, but falls short of being truly great in a few places. The music is excellent, and the pixel art is good. The combat balance is quite good. Characters' abilities are distinct, but their growth is completely linear. I was also disappointed by the lack of a job system. While there are many unique characters to choose from, the lack of customization harms replayability.The game features a Very Important Choice System, but it doesn't truly have diverging paths. Each choice impacts only 1-2 missions before you return to the main path. Some details will be remembered and can be used later, but this reduces the sense of weight for the earlier choices.The writing is a major focus; it varies in quality over the course of the game, but is strong overall. It started to feel like tropey Fire Emblem writing in the middle, but the character writing in the late game evoked powerful emotions. In spite of having an average run-time, its emotional moments were foreshadowed and felt well-earned.This brings us to the game's strongest element: its theme. Triangle Strategy's story is about making the best of a bad situation, and the dangers of hubris. That may sound pretty artsy for a video game, but the writers demonstrate these themes in the minute-to-minute dialogue & events until a broader picture is painted. Seranoa is not on a typical hero's journey. He's just a man with a little power trying to get by in a world where the strong thoughtlessly trample the weak. I can't go into more detail without spoilers but, for me, the consistency of this theme made the game very impactful.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna be straight up right off the bat, don't buy this game if you aren't prepared for a lot of unfair combat and a fair amount of frustration. This is a modern re-release of a game that comes from the era of old school trial by fire. It doesn't care about being fair, and it doesn't care how many times you lose. If you want to know more, read on.The biggest issue that this game has is unfair enemy behavior. You'll often find yourself spamming punches and kicks, that in any other game would be part of an unbreakable combo chain, but in this game, enemies will nonchalantly start hitting you right through whatever combo you're in the middle of. This is the most common occurrence of the game, and defines most of the combat experience here. What's worse is that all the enemies in the game are tanks, requiring more damage than what feels reasonable to take even just one of them down. You're going to be frequently outnumbered, taking tons of unfair damage, which is going to compel most players to start playing in an exploitative fashion. You do have infinite lives, but not every checkpoint is forgiving, so if you aren't ready to deal with that, this isn't for you.You play as all four River City characters in this game, swapping them out on the fly, which should have been cool, but it kinda isn't. I say that because although you can swap them all out on the fly, they each have their own individual health bars, which sounds okay, until you discover that if one of them dies, they all die. The game basically makes you flirt with death, swapping out characters before they die, which essentially equals the player having less health. This could have been a reasonable gameplay mechanic if all four of the characters offered a different playstyle from one another, but they don't. The boys play identically to one another; the girls play identically to one another; and the boys and girls differ ever so slightly from one another. In theory, this means you actually would have been better off just playing as a single character with an extended health bar, equal to all four.Am I being way too harsh here? Kinda. This is a really old game, and the standards were different back then. If I'm being honest with myself, if I had this game as a kid, I actually think I would have loved it. It's an unfair game, no doubt, but if you grew up in the 90's, that's nothing new, and being unfair certainly didn't stop these kinds of games from being a good time (not always). The combat is still fun enough, the environments are interesting, and the game has a decent amount of pre-fight dialogue before boss encounters, giving every fight context and purpose (which wasn't very common for beat'em'up games in the era this was made in). Co-op is probably not a bad time with this one either, though I haven't tried that to speak too much on it, so I won't.Given that this is 2022 though, some folks might be compelled to judge this game off the backs of more recent games like the original River City Girls, Mother Russia Bleeds, and Streets of Rage 4. Does this have anywhere near the same modern day sensibilities that those games have? No. Duh, right? But still, just as a fair warning to anyone born after the year 2000, I know that your first experience with River City games is likely 2019's River City Girls. Just know that this is a vastly different beast from that game. Don't expect ANY of the humor of that game here, nor a catchy soundtrack that will make you want to own the songs (aside from the awesome intro song which was added in just for this release), nor any of the RPG elements. THIS-IS-DIFFERENT. The game does include a tailored intro that features the girls in their modern day forms, and it's pretty cool, but that's about all that this game has in connection with the previous one. The playable portion of this will punish you, as most of the games from its time did.P.S. This game dawns the name River City Girls, but that's just for brand recognition due to the popularity and success of the 2019 game. This is more about Kunio and Rikki than it is about the girls.

_childDocuments_.review: A modern day re-release of the last entry for the Nekketsu Koha series in the Kunio-kun franchise placed into the River City Girls spinoff series. This release was a split project between WayForward who handled all of the translations & newly added visuals wrapped around the game with Limited Run Games handling the original game itself. WayForward chose to take this project on as a way to serve as an origin story for Misako & Kyoko's playable debuts in the franchise with many of the events & characters in this game to be referenced in the upcoming River City Girls 2.Without any source code being available for the project, emulation was used on the Carbon engine which was originally made for Shantae GBC's re-release on the Switch. Nothing was changed about the original game apart from being available in other languages so any issues from then remain present here. The emulator runs fine, though backing in & out of a game may sometimes cause game audio to cut out entirely or other similar issues at the time of writing.From the gameplay side of things this plays well enough and should feel pretty familiar to those who've played the original arcade game or Technos' other franchise Double Dragon. Playing this present day the controls can feel stiff compared to the Downtown Nekketsu beat em' up games seen on the NES and especially to those who might be coming straight out of River City Girls' modern approach. You're using your punch & kicks throughout with the boys being able to perform grabs and the girls being able to move & attack faster. The game is played in a stage-by-stage linear fashion and certainly doesn't overstay it's welcome in the total length with you being able to clear the whole thing in a couple of hours dependant on how many times you die throughout.What I'd say to be the real meat & potatoes would have to be the story. The Koha series of Kunio games were all made with relatively darker & serious themes in mind in comparison to the others and this is no exception. WayForward provides two options for the script with those either being the original 1994 script or a flavoured version edited to sound more like the characters' River City Girls counterparts. Both scripts provide a good experience throughout!The biggest flaw the PC version has is that there's no sort of settings menu at all. Your volume, window size, full screen, or keyboard controls cannot be changed at all or must be manually done. If all of this is not an issue or you're playing on a controller then in it's current state I can suggest the PC version. If any of these are an issue but you'd still like to purchase a copy of the game instead of resorting to playing the old fan translation then I'd recommend any of the console releases. The game itself is more than fine but the PC version in specific needs some more work done.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really recommend this game in its current state, since there isn't really much for it to offer than the two script options.As for the game itself...The translation creates a false dichotomy where the game makes you choose between two English options.  You have English (Original) and English (RCG).  In plain terms, one is an actual attempt at localization and the other is a cynical phone in that is truer to the premise of the original game but EXTREMELY cynical.  If you know any Japanese, then you know that English (Original) is deliberately translated in a way where someone decided that people who might possibly not want a game that is rewritten to the extent that it fails to really, gasp, translate what the original game was about while also keeping it from sounding wooden and awkward.There is an exchange in the original between Misako and Kunio where "English (Original)" chooses to translate [くにお。。。?!　あんたホントにくにおなの？]  "Kunio... are you really, Kunio?!"You could seriously just translate this as "Is that really you?"  And that's what I mean when I say there is a false dichotomy between the two scripts where the only way you can get something that doesn't read stiff and literal is to choose the script that also inserts jokes and makes attempts at changing the original tone of the game to match River City Girls.This is NOT a choice between "Literal" and "Localized", this is a choice between a cynical, phoned in "translation" that is barely better than the fan translation patch that was released for this game or writing that is more about making an obscure Japanese game fit the tone of River City Girls.Shin Nekketsu Kouha Kunio-Kun: Kunio-tachi no Banka is NOT a particularly light hearted game.  It's a mostly earnest teen drama in tone.  I think there would be ways to update the script without necessarily making it more akin to the Downtown Nekketsu/River City Ransom series of games, which are PARODIES of "Nekketsu Kouha Kunio-Kun"/Hot-Blooded Renegade Kunio.I know enough Japanese to tell that there is something extremely condescending about the English (Original) script, that it was done by someone who is clearly insulting you in plain sight like you won't notice, and ultimately I think that it's just a marketing scam that doesn't even do justice to the game it's bringing over.  I won't say Kunio-tachi no Banka is a particularly perfect game, it's extremely esoteric, relying on action game exploits and timing to stay ahead on life and not die between chapters.  The game itself is probably about an hour or two in total if you aren't taking a lot of deaths. What is interesting about it as a game is that it was deliberately trying to deliver a story before anything else.  If you can't really represent what that story was in a way that isn't horribly cynical and "brand focused", I think it's really depressing to experience.  Because you can only really think of what could be relative to a game that doesn't really understand what it's working in the tradition of in the first place.  Anyway, this isn't just sour grapes, I mean that as of when I'm writing this you can't even cleanly select between the two scripts.  The game has a bug where it defaults to English (RCG) which is the half localized/half rewritten Wayforward script.  The game doesn't really function properly, one of the Japanese negative reviews for this game gave a thumbs down saying it would change this if the Japanese language option is changed to work properly.So in terms of what this game is seeking to do, I can't really recommend it.  And as far as a game where the basic settings act as selected... well that doesn't happen either.  Poor translation and a buggy emulation front end.  Get the Switch version  or wait for a patch!

_childDocuments_.review: First off: There are 2 possible translations possible in English. An original adaptation to make it flow better with river city girls 1 and a new one which is a close translation to the Japanese. The devs listened to feedback and provided extra options which is to be commended. What is this game? This is a very old school brawler. This was a "graphical update" from the nes sprites of the original and I the only game in the "kunio" or "river city ransom" series that seems to use these sprites. There are also no rpg elements in this one. You can't pop in a shop to eat, buy skill books or anything like that. It's pure action. True to form, the Japanese only uses hiragana and kana for text and it is hard to read due to the low resolution.The story is a bigger deal and a bit the beginning is a bit darker than the typical kunio game. The title is also a bit misleading since the girls are playable, but the main stars are kunio and riki. The Japanese title makes that a bit more clear. You eventually have 4 characters, which can be shared with another player (regardless if they own the game or not) or you can use all 4 for yourself and switch them out. In single player at least, if anyone of them get knocked out, you lose. You need to switch before they get KOed. What is a bit unusual for this game is that the enemies have more combo priority than you do. Most brawlers or fighting games have a kind of hit stun after you hit someone or invincibility frames. You don't get that here; your combos will be broken by the guy you are wailing on, if they feel like it. That doesn't work both ways though, you can't really break out of a combo yourself. Think of it this way: in case of a tie, the player loses. In modern games it is the opposite. This is the source of the perceived difficulty of the game. Therefore, I found that the best way to fight is to knock them down with one hit. The good ol jump kick them to death technique from back in the day is back. Some reviews commented that all 4 characters are essentially the same and just a lifebar. This is incorrect and it only seems that way at the beginning: the special moves are different and the girls slap instead of punch which seems slightly easier to finish combos with than punches. I am not sure on damage numbers but according to a guide a steam, not all attacks do the same amount of damage.The remastering of this game adds a link to the newest river city girl through an intro comic and opening. I like how the song sounds slightly distorted like it was recorded in the 80s. You can also add some filters but I didn't see a huge difference other than the CRT filter. Another addition is the use of saving. The old game used a password system. You input a password and it brings you to that stage. You can use either. This allows you to skip parts of the game if you like. The game isn't terribly long but you may prefer some stages over others when replaying. For more Japanese games on pc check out

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could rate this as a "meh". The main game itself isn't that bad, it's a tough as balls SNES game where the CPU has a total advantage over you most of the time so you have to cheese them, which works with everyone except the bosses. The story's actually pretty okay, the River City Girls localization isn't an issue at all.The big issue is with the frontend itself; no way to remap controls, a really weird savegame system where you have to save and quit (instead of just saving), over 4 GB of extra intro / ending videos that aren't needed, a crash bug that happens after beating the game if you have a certain option selected (bug was never fixed), lots of leftover Japanese signage and text in the game itself that wasn't touched - including the game's end credits and original manual - and a rare but easy to reproduce bug that completely kills the SNES audio. And unfinished menu text if you choose an European language.There was an attempt, but this game could've used another month of QA. But WayForward doesn't do QA, especially when it comes to languages.I'm happy I only paid a few bucks for this through a Humble Bundle, because it's not worth the full list price, let alone the Limited Run extortion cost for a physical copy.

_childDocuments_.review: The translation is good, the new cutscenes and extras are good. But I kind of expect a bit more from Wayforward remakes. For example, the Wonder Boy series was an amazing, super-responsive remake with original and updated graphics. If you didn't go out of your way to switch to retro music and graphics, you wouldn't even know the game was as old as it was. That remake polished an old classic and showed how great the source material was. But look at this trash.I mean, this is the same company that makes the Shantae games. Why did they release a game that wasn't fun and use the excuse of being true to the original? Where are the portraits when talking? The smoothed animations and effects? Why stop at just recreating MODE 7 effects? Why stick solely to the password system and not implement game saves? Why not redo the art and stages and take advantage of better resolution and widescreen? Why not make ways to speed up the atrociously slow dialogue?, or clean up the fonts? Why not properly use all the extra buttons?This literally feels like playing a translated rom on a SNES emulator. Yeah, there's cutscenes and music changes. But the moves are spongy, the hitboxes unclear, movement is sluggish, and the graphics are pulled straight from the SNES. The original was for hardcore fans who wanted to play all the series, and because of that, the original devs didn't bother to make fun gameplay. It played generic-AF, but was particularly cheap about solid gameplay. A faithful port with cutscenes is lipstick on a pig. I'd rather watch someone else play this than play it myself.Honestly, with both Wayforward and Arc System Works, who both understand 2D and fighting games, I would have expected them to at least tweak the input and game engine for a smooth, fun play game - with an *option* to use the sub-par original gameplay. Kunio games have a ton of potential if devs look to iterate and improve. If you're making a direct port with box/concept art extras, you don't provide any additional value in a market full of emulators. That's why the PS2-era classic game re-releases were so forgettable.I honestly stopped playing after a half-hour. I expected much better from all parties involved. Guess I've got another game to ignore.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the reason this never got ported to other regions is because they realized it is a very bad game.  Do not go into this expecting it to be an improvement on River City Ransom, it is a step backwards in every conceivable way.  Gone is the buttery smooth combat of the NES version.  Movement and attacks are jerky, unresponsive and — worst of all — unreliable.  You will lose count of how many times you try to do a particular move and the game does something else.  One of the worst offenders is the stomp attack.  If you are using Kunio or Riki, this move is extremely unreliable.  The game constantly confuses the stomp attack (down+kick) with the command to straddle the enemy (down).  Since every time you straddle, you almost immediately get throw off and lose some health, you really don't want to use the straddle move at all, the stomp is by far the better move in my opinion.  Yet due to the unreliable controls, even if you are very careful to hit both buttons at the same time every time, you're lucky if the game does one stomp before straddling the enemy.  The problem is the same to a lesser extent for every special attack.  In order to activate the special, instead of holding R and hitting punch, kick, or jump, you have to hit R first and then wait and hit the other button after a delay.  Even if you do this very carefully, at least half the time it simply doesn't work.  Even if you are able to pull it off, since the specials seem to lack the appropriate "safe" frames, most of the time you get knocked out of the attack before you are able to execute it.  There are a lot of other issues with the game, none of which are as big of an issue as the unreliable controls, but bear mentioning all the same.  There is very little variation in enemies and you will fight the same ones over and over.  They didn't even bother to make different faces for them, all enemies of a certain type look completely identical except for color.  The enemies are tanks and their attacks are able to break out of any of your attacks, even combos that would paralyze the enemy in any other fighting game.  Essentially the enemies don't fight fair which leads you to stop trying to fight them with regular moves and then the entire game becomes a tedious repetition of knock-down-ground-stomp-repeat.  And while the port overall seems to be good, with a convenient save-anywhere save-state system, the music skips and distorts constantly and generally just sound really bad.  I bought this game at full price because I love "Kunio-kun" games and I want to support and encourage more of them being released on Steam but in this case, I can't recommend this in any way.

_childDocuments_.review: I love retro games but this game is AWFUL, just play River City Girls 1 & 2 and please skip this one... unless you're a masochist, in that case go ahead.It has it all:-  - I've lost how many times I've punched/kicked through an enemy (by the graphics' look) but it didn't register any hit.-  - You'll question if your controller is broken.-  - They either stare motionless at you or performs like 3 combos at turbo speed faster than your own kick! I've got tired of cheesing the same technique because after middle game you can't battle the AI normally anymore... zero fun to play that way.-  - Thankfully it doesn't happen during gameplay (I think!) but if you select END at the Continue screen you can't get out of the password screen, if you "Save & Quit" you'll have to fully delete your savegame and start a brand new game. At least you can re-input the password to get your progress back.-  - Minor complain I know, 4,97GB for a game isn't much nowadays but consider that the SNES ROM is only 2MB, that's like over 2400x size increase... Yikes! Yeah sure, there's very few extra content like Intro & Outro videos and a bunch of static images in the gallery, yet I can't see where all that wasted space comes from, River City Girls 1 takes a bit less space and has significantly a lot more content, Ooof.-  - It's fine that the original SNES ROM can't rebind the keys because you're playing with your SNES controller, but the remaster made in 2022 don't allow any video configurations or any rebind either, what gives!?!? Pfff... _childDocuments_.review: A decently alright, if frustratingly difficult Super Famicom beat-em-up wrapped up in one of the WORST emulators I have ever experienced. Or at least, I think it's the emulator, this could just be a bad port issue but it is still an awful experience because of these technical issues.The game itself is a great idea, bringing forward an official translated version of the game that pretty much inspired the River City Girls games to get made. The story bookends uses River City Girl's manga style cut-scenes with RCG's more lighthearted writing. Which is stronger than usual due how RCG's heroines are playing a game of their first adventure that may or may not have actually happened in their timeline. This even leans into the main game itself, where it has two English translations, a more faithful adaptation to the script, and one that goes more into River City Girl's style of writing, the more lighthearted and 4th wall breaking way.Onto the game itself, it is a 1994 beat-em-up, so of course it's going to have the issues of that genre of games in that era, but it has spikes of difficulty that can get way too frustrating at times. This becomes incredibly noticeable against the bosses who can get a crazy amount of damage out and can take a while to put down. The final boss is so high in difficulty I had to basically do a cheesy strategy where even with it, one or two mistakes is a restart.  Fortunately you can pick an Easy difficulty, which I recommend if you're not used to the brutal difficulty this era of gaming brings or simply don't want to bother....That is, until the technical issues pop up, and they pop up fast. Audio desync, which can lead to glitchy audio that not only starts slowing the game down, falls so far behind the gameplay that it becomes an unplayable, headache inducing,  laggy mess. Restarting the game fixes it but it is only temporary, this is a very consistent issue you are guaranteed to run into. I thought this static audio and slowdown was just exclusive to the emulator, but I also got it briefly during the final manga cutscene. Which makes me question if it is a bad emulator, a bad port or even both.I can't recommend playing this in the state it is in, you are honestly much better off either watching a playthrough or the cut-scenes, or playing the game through a better emulator. I enjoy the first RCG and will probably enjoy the 2nd game, but this version of 0 is just terrible.

_childDocuments_.review: If any release exemplified Wayforward's tendency to attach to an existing franchise and deliver a halfassed product, it is this release right here.To start with, this is NOT a "River City Girls" game, so those of you who don't know a thing about the franchise's origins and are expecting another romp similar to that title are going to be hugely disappointed. This game is nothing more than a simple translation patch for an ancient Super Nintendo game, and I'm not at all making that part up -- the actual ROM is right there in the game's installation directory, and you can replace it with a different ROM (including the superior preexisting fan translation patch of the same game) to make this sloppy release play that instead of the intended game.You are essentially paying a huge premium on what is maaaaybe around 3 minutes of the same manga-style cutscenes that RSG used, one prior to the game showing the girls hooking up an old SNES to play this, and another at the end after they finish playing. That, and some scans of the original Japanese manual, are the only extra effort they put into this game.Actually, I lied. They also did a short opening animation set to cringetastic grrrrl power lyrics, and a closing looped animation for the ending credits. When I say "ending credits", I mean Wayforward's team in the end credits taking a victory lap for something they barely touched, which is doubly insulting after they did not even bother translating the original game's ending credits to give proper due to the team who actually put it together way back in the day.As if all of this isn't bad enough, these dingdongs didn't even do a very good job of emulating the ROM, resulting in crackles and pops in the audio, weird input lag, and even outright choppy cancellations of input which will frequently result in short jumps and you standing there with your mouth hanging open to get wrecked because your intended inputs randomly cut off. That last bit is all the more annoying because this is a rough game with cheap AI, making those control failures extremely punishing in some situations.Do yourself a favor and just go find the intro and outro segments on Youtube if you really want to see the whopping ~3 minutes of RCG content, or maybe even watch a Let's Play for the actual game content if you want to see the source for the references in the RCG games.Whatever you do, don't buy this. At all, really. I probably paid $3 for it as part of some bundle or another in my forgotten past, but even that is too much for a game I finished with full cheevo completion in 3 hours recorded playtime despite having gone AFK for at least 60 minutes during that time.

_childDocuments_.review: My impressions video: This is an interesting 16-bit curiosity. It's the first Kunio-Kun (River City) title that involved Misako and Kyoko, the protagonists from WayForward excellent River City Girls that came out before. It's a SNES title that was originally never released outside of Japan, but which has been given a fresh localisation by WayForward, as well as comic cutscenes that humourously tie this into the series in an almost reverse retcon, plus a couple of awesome new Megan McDuffee songs to boot.You will eventually unlock four playable characters, which you can switch between on the fly and all of whom have different moves. However, if any one of them dies, it's game over, so you have to manage that. Local co-op is also available, which I imagine makes things easier. The original game uses a password system for "saves", which you can use here, though you can use more traditional save states as well.The package uses the Limited Run Games Carbon Engine, which is supposed to be focused on putting retro games on modern system, but this offers only the bare minimum of ways to tune the visuals and gameplay experience, far less than other retro re-releases, including ones not on a purpose-built engine. It has a lot of SNES slowdown and the ability to smooth that out through dynamic overclocking of the ROM would have been very nice.The game itself is...fine I guess. Kunio-Kun got a lot more entries in Japan than it did in North America, but I'm just not the biggest fan of this one. The gameplay is slow, cheap and often frustrating, requiring you to do really awkward and unresponsive platforming, or fight powerful bosses in tight spaces where you basically have to cheese them to win. Once you've beaten the story once, there's no New Game Plus or additional modes and the achievements are all tied to story progression so there's really no reason to go back to it.This is a neat curiosity, but isn't the best package, nor the best brawler and it's expensive for just one game. I do recommend it because it is an entry in this series that wasn't easily accessible to the west before, but it's only for hardcore Kunio-Kun fans.

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable retro beat-em-up from the 16 bit era.This is a remake of sort of an old game released only in Japan. It has been translated and updated I believe with new scenes and animations.The overall gameplay is as expected: go through levels, beat whatever moves. The gameplay is more nuanced that usual Final Fight and similar games from the late 90s; as you have more than just one attack button and one jump button; as you can buy upgraded moves to perfomr, and you don't lose health for perfoming your "special" move. It is moderately difficult, but nothing too crazy if you used to play old games on Sega or Nintendo console; it is not Cuphead so don't worry about that; but a couple of levels have quite a spike in terms of difficulty, and not necessarily because they are hard, but because controls and dodge mechanics seems to be off at times.There is no animation cancel, so when you perform a move and try to dodge, there is a period of time for either the dodge or parry, when you need to wait for the end of the animation; so that means if you don't time correctly the attacks and dodge/parry, you get hit. Maybe this is OK for you but I find this annoying, as I like that parry and dodge should cancel whatever attack animation you are performing.Other than that, music is fun, you unlock characters as you go, and the story is so old school and nonsensical that you won't even pay attention to it. Fun for few hours and to play with friends. 7 out of 10 for me

_childDocuments_.review: There are two main reasons to play this game: an interest in game preservation or a sincere love for the River City series. RCGZ does faithfully bring back 2D Brawler action of the 90s, complete with clunky movement and graphics of the time period. The music is fantastic and the dialogue is fun, whether it is 90s camp or leaning hard on the fourth wall. This said, the difficulty and clunkiness of controls do not make it a great time to play. The difficulty can be mitigated through a save state function built into the game. The addition of save states does make the game more playable and helps with frustration but also make me wonder why I am not playing a better balanced game instead. The game is also short, most players are likely clear it within 3-5 hours. RCGZ made me truly appreciate modern games like River City Girls and Streets of Rage 4, but does not have me wanting to go back to it ever again. Play if you are a mega fan of the series or want to see how far games have come in the past 28 years, otherwise give it a hard pass.

_childDocuments_.review: The charm of the presentation and little gimmicks here and there can't mask what was fundamentally a shallow, generic retro beat 'em up. I liked River City Girls a lot and I like a lot of 90s beat 'em fare like Streets of Rage and Final Fight, and if you're familiar with the heights of the genre it's impossible to ignore that from a pure gameplay perspective this is extremely lackluster. I'm really not familiar with the classic Kunio-kun games at all but I thought they generally had more exploration / rpg elements, things like shops etc. - you don't get that here at all, just tiny areas, occasional gimmick levels and guys with the same attacks over and over followed by a boss who maybe has one special attack but takes a million years to die (only to come back later sometimes, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Shinji and his tatsumaki). If you still think this might be for you I'd recommend you check out some video footage before you commit -  the price tag is well above what you should be paying for something like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Beat it in about 3 hours, could probably do it in 2 hours on easy for that "100% discount". Use that info for what you will.Also warning, on normal at least, game becomes a pain halfway through. we're talking take 50% of your life in one hit levels of pain. final boss can either hit you for 20% life or 80% life, since you can switch chars that gives you a max of 2 mistakes.Anyway...Game has an opening and ending comic with the River City Girls version of Kyoko and Misako finding this game about their past adventures as a way to forcibly retcon the plot into their universe. The voice acting is great on these, as it was for River City Girls.However, knowing the story line of -that- game, I have decided to use the "classic" translation rather than the default RCG, which is the one that alters dialogue to better fit with their new personalities, and "Fit in better". I find that a bunch of hogwash, but definitely appreciate the option to choose it or not, and wish more games took that approach if they were going to make alterations.Other positives unique to this release include containing the original Japanese manual, as well as other images in the gallery. There's a new opening and credits sequence (which appears AFTER the ingame credits...) that are animated, but you can find that on your video viewer of choice, so it's not necessary if you own, or "own" the original.This is the simpler of the two Kunio beatemups I know of on SNES, or Super Famicom. The other one is more meaty in it's design while this one is a totally linear beatemup. The unique advantage this game has, however, is that it's actually quite stunning in spots. There were moments where they actually did some wonderful things with shadows, backgrounds are lively in general, and there's a dance club section with what appears to be 3D rotating spotlights. I don't care for how the art style looks, but those levels are eye candy.At it's current price point, it's way too much. maybe between 5-10 US dollars is the optimal amount, but I feel like most of cost players are paying for is just going what amounts to a prettified rom emulator. Meanwhile, you can play genesis games for a couple bucks each, making this a hard sell.As a side note, since it's relevant to the point above, they make a claim in-universe that people would not want to play this game without having the additional cutscenes or opening, which I personally find untrue. Either way, it's nice to have another... Nekketsu?... Kunio-kun?... Game ported to the PC. I would like to see them all eventually, even if it's not likely to happen. Well, know what you're getting into, and tread carefully. Maybe play the -ahem- Free trial and see if it's a game you like, and then purchase this to show your support. You might not be supporting Technos, but you will be supporting the series going forward. Wayforward... Heh.

name: God of Rock
detailed_description: The mysterious God of Rock has revived the souls of the universe’s greatest musicians to clash for his entertainment. Revitalized with new bodies and new powers, each musician will become a contestant in his game, battling it out with each other for musical supremacy on a global stage. God of Rock blends rhythm-based gameplay with fighting game mechanics in tense 1v1 matches. Choose from a dozen unique fighters, each with their own design, mechanics, and harmonic attacks. Soften up your opponent by executing normal moves and building meter by hitting notes to the beat of the song, then spend your meter to unleash EX and special moves do damage and add complexity to their tracks. Finally, finish them off with a devastating Super attack! As the battle progresses, the music track will continue to grow in complexity and difficulty until only one fighter is left standing! Key Features Battle to the Beat – Engage in over-the-top musical battles in this competitive rhythm-based fighter. Limitless Skill Ceiling – Tracks will continue to scale in difficulty until only one fighter remains. Over 40 Original Songs – Each with their own unique and challenging tracks to master. The Universe is Your Stage – Control 12 wildly different characters each with their own playstyle across 8 dynamic stages set across the universe. Game Modes Story Mode – Follow your favorite character through a branching story mode, battling against other musicians to become the last one standing. Training Mode – Master the most challenging segments each song and practice executing special moves to the beat. Track Editor – Put your own spin on your favorite tracks by adding and removing notes to your liking. Local & Ranked Online Multiplayer – Go head-to-head against players at home or around the globe in casual and ranked multiplayer.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so first off I'll lead this review by saying that it is a good game, the charting is excellent and it's insanely fun to play for what it is. However there are two glaring issues, one has a work around, one doesn't. The horizontal note lane is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ atrocious for reading notes, especially if you come from any other rhythm game ever made. There's a reason with Taiko no Tatsujin and Muse Dash limit the game to just two note types, because horizontally the notes become overwhelming to read. This can be fixed by flipping your monitor into portrait mode through Windows however, though you're stuck with mirrored notes if you need downscroll. The second issue is that the health bar is just too far away from the rest of the information, this is a rhythm game so your eyes are glued to a certain part of the screen at all times, and they designed the ultra and EX meters well enough with this in mind, however, the health is on the complete opposite end of the screen making it pretty much a no go to look at unless you're on a simple part of the song and your opponent isn't completely ruining you with garbage. It's a fun game but it needs some sort of UI customization, which is something that many people were asking for in the discussions and it seemed like the creators of this game refused to listen to them. As is I can't fully recommend this game since you have to physically flip your screen or with a setting to be able to play it well.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore the low playtime; I spent a long time with the press demo before release and meant to get this out earlier. I purchased the full game to confirm criticisms were still applicable to the final product.God of Rock is a visually frustrating game that fails to adequately represent either of the genres it's mashing together, but could easily be a mainstay in the genre if the UI was overhauled and the control scheme revisited.For fighting game players thinking this could be a good addition to your local, you'll be disappointed by a lack of button binding at character select and the bindings themselves being confusing. On a traditional stick you're missing out on a second hand's worth of rhythm buttons, which are crucial for jacks in higher difficulty songs. On a leverless controller, you have to rebind your Dpad to joystick inputs - except the inputs are labelled, for some bizarre reason, as "Up/Down" and "Up/Down (2)". Which one is 'up'? Why are there two of these? Does it matter? Why can you bind two buttons for each of the directions? The obvious intended method of playing this is on a pad like a DS4, but those aren't always available - and I'll bet most people at locals don't want to switch to a regular controller just to play this.The motion inputs are, speaking as a fighting game player, unnecessary for this game. I get the difficulty stems from pulling off 360s and QCFs while not dropping your rhythm combo, but it's just a needless layer of complexity. Pairing a non-rhythmic mechanical task with a rhythmic one is just... jarring. It's like typing a review with one hand and pulling off the TTFAF guitar solo with the other. I can't believe I'm saying this, but one-button specials would be tremendously helpful here.The actual mechanics of fighting are simple enough; you have a health bar, and specials from yourself and your opponent will manipulate that health bar. Doing a higher level special move than your opponent at the same time they do will cancel theirs out, and this can chain up until the highest level, meaning you can't just mindlessly churn them out. Succeeding at the rhythm game gives you meter to perform these specials; the core loop is to score high combos, use the meter you build to go on the attack, and to make sure you're never starved for specials to counter their offense. Characters vary from the self-healing Hilda to the stance-focused Kosaku, and they're genuinely interesting. If this was a game that was easy to bring to locals and to get people set up, it'd be a fun side game.While we're on that point, let's talk about the characters. The designs are fun! Many of the characters are obvious homages to rock legends, like Ziggy the Starman paying tribute to David Bowie's stage persona Ziggy Stardust or the obvious Elvis recreation King. Champ's just a buff shirtless Freddie Mercury and I'm extremely here for it. The cast is diverse, and hot-shot VAs like Kira Buckland (Hilde) and Jeff Williams (King) bring them to life. I genuinely want to see more of them! Edith's grayscale color palette is a nice bit of visual flair, and the God of Rock looks straight out of a guitar hero game. These characters would kick ass in a traditional fighting game, and there's already a nice foundation - heck, they even beat each other up on screen with each hit note. They're excellent, and easily one of the best parts of the game.The game's visual flair is excellent, too, outside of the gameplay portions. I love the graffiti-esque stylings of the menus, the way portraits at character select look like they were spray-painted onto a wall. Song select is framed like you're picking out a single from an album. It wants an aesthetic, and it hits it. The game's a visual treat when you're not playing it.Rhythm game players, I'm so sorry - it's a four-button horizontal-scroller. There's a reason most rhythm games are vertical scrollers, and that's to provide an easy analogue for which button is which note; notes fall onto your buttons. The vertical layout of the note icons/judgement line is confusing, and while it's learnable, it's annoying that there's no option to rotate it. I found myself craning my head 90 degrees to simulate a downscroll, and left my play sessions with neck pain. The chart itself takes up a tiny portion of the screen, and while most of the relevant information is clustered there - your special gauges and your EX meter, for instance - your health is for whatever reason all the way in the top corners. Having to dart your vision between the chart and the opposite side of the screen is disorienting, which makes it difficult to judge the state of the match. What's your life lead? Should you cash in and try to take out the last scrap of their health bar? The nature of rhythm games discourages you from looking away from the chart, but the HUD almost forces you to. This is especially pronounced when playing a character like Hilde, who self-heals; did your hard-earned 15 heal stacks actually just do anything? Drop your combo and find out, idiot.The soundtrack is good, though. It won't be to everyone's tastes, but I like it. 'Embers' is a particular favorite.Most of the screen seems to be dedicated toward showcasing the characters; they clash in the center as you and your opponent duke it out. The animation is good, the designs are good, but good god the VFX is overwhelming. If you're both doing well, then each blocked strike from the on-screen avatars sends out a blur and a flash of light. Consider that this means every hit note means there's a bright flash from off of the chart. Most rhythm games have some option or another to dim or disable non-chart elements for focus's sake, but God of Rock doesn't offer that. The visual flair for spectators seems to be prioritized over the experience of the players. Considering the giant wheel in the bottom-center of the screen showing what specials are being used, I can't imagine why it wouldn't be an option.I experienced more than a few charts that weren't synced, but that could've been a calibration problem. YMMV.God of Rock has a solid foundation. I really, really want this game to be good - we need more experimental games like this, and it knows what it's trying to do. I'm just not sure God of Rock knows how to do it. The team at Modus Games seems to really adore the project, so I'm 100% sure they'll bring it around within a year or so, but as-is on launch day I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's talk about motion inputs.The basic concept of a motion input in a fighting game is to define a move's use case. A quater-circle forward or a Dragon Punch motion requires you to push your control stick forward, making the move a risk to use in close quarters. A charge input can be performed by blocking or crouching, allowing a character to turn defensive pressure into offensive rewards. 360's require you to press jump, meaning that the move often needs to be buffered - and consequently makes opponents fear those buffered options. It's all in service of adding to the mindgames, encouraging play patterns that translate into a complex loop of offense and defense where you’re constantly predicting and reacting to each other, finding openings and punishing mistakes.So clearly we need to slap unrelated joystick inputs into a genre that doesn't require any of these things, loudly interrupting its own gameplay loop to demand that you memorize complex and often nonsensical input patterns for the sole purpose of making the game needlessly complicated, while also throwing full-difficulty rhtyhm game charts that require all of your focus to maintain.It's a shame. I loved the concept when I first heard about it. But you managed to skip everything that makes each genre good and wound up with the worst of both worlds. How do you screw up such an interesting pitch so badly?

_childDocuments_.review: DISCLAIMER: I know my hours are low currently, but I put a lot offline over the weekend at Combo Breaker where this game had local setups, as well as on another steam account that has the game shared from this one.This game does not deserve the mixed reviews it has received. God of Rock does exactly what it sets out to do in combining fighting game elements into a competitive rhythm gaming experience. Many of the criticisms listed in the negative reviews for this game can honestly simply be reduced to skill issues. The game has a bit of a learning curve to it, as getting used to a horizontally scrolling note highway can be jarring to people who have played other rhythm games in the past, but it is nothing that's impossible to adapt to. I come from a background in StepMania, osu!Mania, and other 4-key rhythm games, and was able to perfect combo through some of the harder songs within a few hours of play time. The gameplay actually feels extraordinarily satisfying. The charts are wonderfully made, the sound design is excellent, and each character feels unique in the uses of their special moves. The special move inputs can be somewhat frustrating at times, as sometimes you drop your inputs when trying to keep track of the notes, but again, this is something that will just take time to get used to, as is with learning any game. After speaking with the team that represented the game at Combo Breaker, they seemed very passionate about the game and said that they are actively working to fix the issues that many users have expressed. If you currently do not feel compelled to try this game (which I strongly suggest you to give it a try, it really is a great time), I would say to at least keep an eye on its future, since patches have been implemented regularly since release. This is a mix of genres that I've been wanting to see for a very long time, and it really is the first of its kind. I sincerely hope that one day this game receives the attention it deserves, or that someone sees the game and makes something similar. I would love to see this game get more players, so if you have any questions about the game, please feel free to reach out to me with questions about it.

_childDocuments_.review: While I haven't played fighting games past a casual level, I am a huge rhythm game nerd and am having a blast playing this game.I see a lot of reviews complaining about the lack of a vertical scrolling option, and I honestly do not think it should be added SOLELY on the basis of convenience. Hear me out.I can play some of the hardest charts of Museca, Jubeat, Chunithm, Guitar Hero, Groove Coaster, Taiko, Crossbeats, Muse Dash, Osu!, and Osu!mania. I greatly enjoy but suck at Pop'n, SDVX, and PIU doubles. Why did I bother listing those? If you look them up, almost all of them have a different take on how a player hits notes. Some of them are super intuitive and can be learned quickly (for me, Jubeat), but some of them can take extra practice to learn even if you have an extensive rhythm gaming background (Taiko and SDVX). Different people pick up different games faster, even some of the "hard" games can be easy for some folks to learn.In the same way, some fighting games are pretty intuitive in their controls (smash), while other games require a lot of learning and practice before you even remotely begin to feel like you're experiencing the intended gameplay (skullgirls).I think it is entirely okay for God of Rock to come out with a new take on rhythm games in the form of a difficult 4-key horizontal lane. It just means you probably can't hit the ground running and be a pro. You actually have to take time to learn the controls, figure out what keybinds work for you, and above all else practice if you want to be decent. Just like a lot of the harder rhythm AND fighting games.I generally think the game is challenging. If you're not used to reading streams and patterns, ESPECIALLY in a horizontal format like Taiko, this game will be really, really hard.If it's purely an ACCESSIBILITY issue, as in no matter how much a person practices they can't physically read the notes coming in sideways, then yes by all means please add a vertical option if possible. Make the game accessible. But if it's just for the sake of convenience? I'm okay with this game taking me extra time to feel comfortable. The game doesn't need to be convenient and easy to learn, but it will limit the number of people willing to play (just look at other reviews lol). So I guess it's up to the devs to decide which matters more, a small audience of players willing to improve to be able to play, or a wider audience. I was looking for a challenging rhythm game, and that's exactly what I got, so I overall recommend it if you're looking for that.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who enjoys both Fighting Games and Rhythm Games, this game lacks a lot of the QoL options many modern iterations of those games have.As a fighting game player, this game lacks a lot of quality of life features, especially an inability to change the controls upon character select, but also the tutorial seems broken in that the special button does not work properly in mirrored CPU mode so you can't practice special inputs with characters and especially you can't practice charge characters properly. The health is also so far from the chart that it feels impossible to tell who is in the lead until the chart starts flashing red.From the rhythm game sides of things, the only note speed options are in training mode for some reason. There is no way to change offset between different controllers to potentially account for different input delays, especially between wired and wireless controllers, which usually wouldn't be an issue for fighting games, but given there is the timing aspect of rhythm games giving you different strengths it feels like a strange oversight. The area that the chart is on is so small for the amount of notes you have that reading can get really hard that it feels like really dumb levels of memorisation. The organisation of charts for each map feels bizarre as it doesn't sort by difficulty for some reason. In fact there aren't really any way to sort charts to begin with.Also there isn't a mode that lets you play the game like a normal rhythm game which feels like it leads to the charts ending up rather unmemorable. Like, it's ONLY focused on the fighting game 1v1 aspect when it really feels like so much more could have been done with this game.This game is honestly a massive disappointment to what could have been such a great and novel experience.

The mysterious God of Rock has revived the souls of the universe's greatest musicians to clash for his entertainment. Revitalized with new bodies and new powers, each musician will become a contestant in his game, battling it out with each other for musical supremacy on a global stage.

God of Rock blends rhythm-based gameplay with fighting game mechanics in tense 1v1 matches.

Choose from a dozen unique fighters, each with their own design, mechanics, and harmonic attacks. Soften up your opponent by executing normal moves and building meter by hitting notes to the beat of the song, then spend your meter to unleash EX and special moves do damage and add complexity to their tracks. Finally, finish them off with a devastating Super attack!

As the battle progresses, the music track will continue to grow in complexity and difficulty until only one fighter is left standing!

name: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure
detailed_description: Explore the roots of the Disgaea series with the strategy RPG Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure ! Play as a young girl named Cornet who has the power to communicate with puppets, and join her to fulfill her dream of meeting her “prince charming”. But all isn’t well in the kingdom with the evil Marjorly around! Rhapsody features many original songs and interludes throughout the game. Colorfully illustrated anime characters and backgrounds as well as an intuitive, isometric battle system and multiple difficulty levels offer something for new players and veteran role-play gamers alike. Dive in and discover the love and music! Gain the advantage in combat with features such as Cornet’s horn, which allows you to enhance your puppets while bestowing Appreciation Points. Once a puppet earns enough Appreciation Points, they’ll gain access to special Rewards that have a variety of powerful effects! Additionally, each character (and enemy) has an elemental affinity which grants them a unique set of spells. Use these spells in combination with other characters' elemental abilities to exploit your enemies' vulnerabilities. But remember, every element has its own weakness!

_childDocuments_.review: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure is a profound example of the saying "You shouldn't Judge a Book by it's cover".This game is basically NIS's Mother 3. It had the misfortune of being initially released during a period where JRPG's and 'girly' games were not socially acceptable in the West, and as a result was a western financial disaster. Rhapsody is a very VERY early PS1 RPG; and is definitely a hidden gem of it's time... With unforgettable music numbers, surprising depth and dark subject matter despite it's cutesy outward appearance.Most people judge this game for it's long prologue(that goes until the prince is kidnapped- before the plot actually starts). As well as how 'girly' it appears, and how easy it is. If you can forgive those aspects about it.. You will quickly find this game has more to it than it seems. Below it's cutesy exterior.... It is a game that openly judges your morality. The primary theme of this game is exploring what love really means; Both romantically, platonically and familial. But the game isn't afraid to openly criticize Cornets(Or the players) shallow pursuit of the Prince for personal gain- if that is what the player chooses. There are also themes of suicide, death, murder, hopelessness, domestic abuse and neglect in this game. Nothing is as it seems: and there are definitely points where this game gets quite unexpectedly dark and leaves you feeling like you completely failed to make other characters happy.It is one of the only games that has made me openly conflicted about a choice I've made. And the unsettling thing about it... is that you almost never know the gravity or impact of what you've done until it's too late. And while these choices have no impact on the ending.. The game makes SURE that you never forget the impact of what you've done.What are you willing to do, or who will you sacrifice in the pursuit of love? What does 'Love' really mean? These are questions Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure poses to it's players.-----For these reasons, it is my favourite JRPG EVER made. Like others have said, it's musical numbers(despite being cheesy sounding in English) make the game something that sticks in your mind even 20 years after you've played it. I catch myself humming or searching the soundtrack online every so often. The intangible feeling this game leaves with you after it's finished, is indicative of a masterpiece despite it's flaws. And I wish more people knew about this game and actually gave it a chance.I would also like to clarify that this is the ATLUS translation of the game; not NIS's translation. Meaning, the pop culture references and cringey translations or censorship is not NIS's fault.10/10 and looking forward to the sequels coming out soon(this summer). Support the game. Buy it. BUY ITTT NOWWWW!

_childDocuments_.review: A forgotten tactical RPG classic from the PlayStation era has finally returned for another musical tour. Being a proud owner of Rhapsody for the original PS1, DS, and now the physical limited/digital deluxe edition bundled with NIS Classics Vol. 3, I can honestly say that the Steam/Switch port is actually pretty good. However, I do have some minor nitpicks worth mentioning:The Good:- It's the original with tactical elements and monster recruits (Not the turn-based DS version)- Video filters (CRT is recommended)- The load times are gone.- No more slowdown during Cornet's "Sugar Candy" reward.- Keyboard and gamepad configuration- You can now go back to the main menu by selecting "Give Up" on the options menu, though the reset code still works in this version.The Bad:- BGMs do not sound accurate like it's original counterpart.- The audio suddenly goes mute for a few seconds at random during battle scenes. (Steam)- Video resolution is not properly adjusted, thus the sprites and backgrounds appear stretched.- No 4:3 resolution option? I really can't stand the black borders.- The vocal tracks cut off abruptly for a couple of musicals when it ends.Do I recommend this port? Yes. As much as I prefer the PS1 version the most, this port is a good start for those who's never played Rhapsody before. I also highly recommend anyone who's not familiar with the Marl Kingdom/Rhapsody series. It's an excellent series that deserves more recognition. Hopefully after this release, NIS America will finally shed some light about both Cornet and Ferdinand's future once we're given the two sequels we've been patiently waiting for.

_childDocuments_.review: This here is some JRPG jank.  None of the gameplay elements work.  The game is super easy.  There are basically two dungeon tilesets and they weren't good the first time you went through them, let alone the sixth.  You can actually recruit a bunch of monsters by having Cornet beat them to death with her horn but they all start at level 1, meanwhile you already have a dozen or so puppet companions that for some reason also start at level 1 no matter how deep into the game you are when they join the team.  Why do we have so many different potential allies when you spend so little time fighting and the fights are so easy?   This is compounded by the game being about 10-12 hours long.  Why are we fighting on a grid?  Items and equipment feel nearly pointless.  There are multiple annoying flag triggers.  None of this make sense.All that said, the game is super charming.  Character interactions, npc dialogue and inspection points are consistently fun.  The game will probably make you smile.  There are even a number of musical bits throughout the game, though even here they goofed up a bit, as one of the few songs where there's actual some level of choreography only plays if you idle on the tile screen a bit when it should've played when starting a new game. The game is also surprisingly open-ended in the second half which would be cool if the gameplay worked at all.Rhapsody is a good example where the enjoyment level is greater than the sum of the parts.  Also, just looked the store page trailer for the first time and that's probably a pretty good barometer for whether you'll like the game or not.  Do you want some cheesy musical bits interspersed into your b-movie tier jrpg?  If so, you're at the right place.

_childDocuments_.review: There was a meme on Twitter a while back among indie game people that the best games are 7/10.  Games like Rhapsody are why.  It's a low budget RPG that sometimes feels like it's struggling against its limitations (like dungeons are all just a handful of one screen backgrounds that get reused over and over, sometimes giving you the novelty of tinting them a new color), they didn't get combat balance right (it's too easy except for a few bosses who might almost immediately take someone out if you're unlucky), and I feel like some people are going to be unhappy that you can easily finish it in under 10 hours.  But this is filled to the brim with charm.  The character writing is mostly great, and the writers knew how to mix up silliness with an exploration of grief as well as a good Dragon Quest game.  I think this game is going to stick with me much longer than "better" games.  Highly recommended if you can stand some jank.
