_childDocuments_.review: New player here, I bought the game after a random recommendation, hearing that a Steam release will be soon. At the glance, the game would be a pass from me - and boy, I would miss out.It's remarkable how this game has so much character despite being so simple and short. The main story is really cute and well written, there are multiple Easter eggs to find in the world, and the game manages to get both a laugh and a tear out of me. It's a shame that combat is pretty easy and bit repetitive, but it doesn't need to be exceptional in order to really enjoy this small gem of a game. What's most important, Rhapsody stays FUN throughout. A huge recommend, even if it's not a game for everyone. The only thing I would like to see changed is the option to have Japanese musical alongside English subtitles - I think original Japanese vocals make experience more natural and fit the tone better, but the musical itself is a big part of a story, forcing me to look for the external subtitles to go with the Japanese setting.Note for future buyers: as suggested in other reviews, make sure to turn on the CRT filter in settings, makes the game look much better on modern displays!

_childDocuments_.review: I must admit, I was expecting Buffy the Vampire Slayer's  Once More With Feeling with such a title for a game, but I was misled.This one is quite an old Nippon Ichi SRPG, featuring a girl called Cornet, who plays the cornet and makes puppets come to life. Cornet is obsessed with a prince, and so the game (or at least the start of the game) is concerned with trying to meet this prince.Along the way, you'll meet strange cats, jellies, pirates and skeletons, some of whom will want to join your party and these will help you out in the random tactical battles, where each character will take their turn to move, attack or use magic.And that's largely it. There's none of the flashiness of attack animations you get in the more modern Disgaea games, and the story is of its time - but it's an interesting glance into one of NIS's earlier titles, which seems to have been ported pretty well to PC.Overall, this one gets 7 Maria von Trapps out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Talk about tickling my nostalgia itch, Rhapsody is probably my first JRPG I have experienced with the PS1.I still remember not even beating the tutorial like a game urinalist, but at least I have a valid excuse. I was 6-9 years old, literal skill issue on my part and coming back to it now in 2023. The game is really cutesy simple and feels too easy with my IQ upgrade.The music is probably the best part and my main reason to purchasing this game. It is like hearing an old lullaby your mother use to sing, to help you fall asleep. The main song is unforgettable and the animations look the same as I remembered. I can't be sure if the official localisation has changed or censored anything as it feels similar or the same as the PS1 walkthroughs you can find online.The art style is very distinct from anime back in the late 90s, reminds me of Sailor Moon which use to be on TV every morning before school starts. It is jarring to look at since modern anime styles have been refined but you will get use to it, like moving from a 4K display to a 720p one. Speaking of pixels, as crazy as it sounds. The CRT option is the best way to play the game, the other two filters look way too blocky for my liking and the CRT filter smooths out the sprites quite well.My only gripe with Rhapsody is the two decade old game design. You know your objective to get the story going, but you don't know where to find it. It is trial and error, memory or if you give up, look for a walkthrough online. However, back then only the lucky had internet or you wait for a guide from a game magazine. For the authentic experience, try and finish the game with not guide if you get lost. The maps are small with the process of elimination, you will find where you will need to go eventually.There are probably other modern pixel art JRPGs worth while to buy at the same price than this re-release. However, Rhapsody is a hidden gem in the PS1 era, which did not got global localisation for the sequels due to poor sales.I recommend buying this for the nostalgia or experience what JRPGs were like during the hay days of final fantasy.If the first game is to your liking, buy the sequels as you don't need to learn Japanese to experience the dizty journey of our beloved puppet princess.
_childDocuments_.name: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to start off by saying I really loved my time with Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure and it is the definition of a hidden gem. I would very highly recommend it! 8.5 out of 10 experience.The art is beautiful and thanks to this amazing port it has never looked better! Make sure to use the CTR filter, it looks really great! The dialogue is very charming and is genuinely funny at times, the musical songs sound wonderful in both Japanese and English. They are infused with this whimsical energy that is present throughout the majority of the game that left me smiling a lot. Even now I have the soundtrack playing while I write this very review! Though my love for cheesy English voice acting in JRPGS may be clouding my judgement.The characters where all very lovable with Kururu and Etolie Rosenqueen being my personal favorites. I can't say enough good things about the villains. Marjoly and her minions where so much fun and I'd honestly love and game just about them. Cornet was a great protagonist and her relationship/dynamic with Kururu and especially Etonlie along with her singing and musical numbers which always capture her feeling a motivations perfectly made me root for her. The prince charming stuff was a bit silly, but the story and characters acknowledge this and has fun with it. I felt the ending though a bit predicable was heartwarming and left on a note that left me with a big stupid smile on my face.In terms of gameplay even on the hardest mode it's very simple and offers very little in the way of true challenge. For those familiar with other TRPGS from NIS such as the series Disgaea or Phantom Brave, Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure is babies first TRPG. Its battle maps are always a single static area/image with very little strategy or movement being necessary. There are quite a few abilities that just straight up wipe the entire map in a single move making battles almost comically short. Bosses don't provide much in the way of challenge either. I can't express how funny it is to encounter a character who looks super badass, and story-wise has caused me so much trouble only for me to beat them in one turn. Needless to say I never saw the game over screen in the eight hours it took me to complete the main story. The difficulty and length didn't bother me. I really appreciate brief relaxed games sometimes you know? A sweet little easy experience that's over before you know it.Next I'd like to talk about three areas that did bother me a bit, though. First off I can't say I love how cryptic what you are suppose to do next to progress the main story is at times. I had to check a walkthrough a couple of times which I really like to avoid if possible.Second is the dungeon variety was majorly lacking. Every once in awhile you had you unique locations such as a ghost ship or a restaurant! But more often than not it will be the same cave or generic castle. I'm sorry, but it will never be cool to be climbing up to a volcano and once you go inside it's the same cave as last time but with a red color filter. Thankfully most dungeons are over before you know it and the game isn't long enough for it to truly bother me.Third is focused on the sinister fellow who decided what the achievements for this game were going to be and is less about the quality of the game. I'd just recommend playing the game on the hardest difficulty and enjoying the amazing main story and don't worry about 100% completing the game. A lot of the achievements amplify what I consider to be the games weak spots and feel like busy work and completely worthless. A few examples include.An Illustrious Achievement - All of the illustrations and beyond what you can even collect within dungeons are available right at the start of the game in the main menu. Though I'd recommend beating the game first as the galley contains some spoilers.Omega-Level Caster - This game is very easy and you'll have more than enough puppets just going through the main story to beat it. Collecting them all and completing their quest is truly optional as what you are missing out on is like a few lines of dialogue and a lot of puppets you won't need to use because the game is already pretty much over when you track all of them down. If your like me you had like three favorites that you leveled you throughout the game. But this achievement adds something to do with them after you beat the game!... Pain. To let you know how long this achievement would take to get, it took me the entire game to level up the STARTING PUPPET high enough to get her omega ability. And not every puppet has an omega ability so you have to pick specific ones and not the puppets you find fun to use or cool. Some of the puppets with omega abilities can only be obtained near the end of the game which means you will be grinding a lot to make these already over powered puppets mega strong for what you might ask? Nothing since there is no end game content that would require them to be that powerful.Aliment Connoisseur - This is the worst achievement on this list by far. To put it simply it's asks you to seek out specific enemies that cast specific abilities such as sleep, poison, paralyze, turtle, and these specific enemies are in specific dungeons and it is completely random what monsters will show up in each battle and the higher your level the less likely you are to get hit by them and the enemies have a set amount of MP and if they use it all you have to find new monsters and try it all over again. Now do this with every status effect in the game... Absolute insanity.Harder Happily Ever After - Getting this achievement doesn't automatically give you the normal/easy mode version and that's just cruel.To summarize I really loved my time with Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure and I highly recommend it to anyone look for a sweet little game with a fun whimsical story filled with colorful characters, wonderful musical numbers, and a more relaxed and simple combat system! This is a game I'll be returning to for years to come. Just maybe don't go achievement hunting...

_childDocuments_.review: To preface, this is not my first time playing the game. I bought a copy of the DS port on release so most of my experience comes from that. Right off the bat, I've noticed some key differences between that and this PSX version. For starters, the sprite art for the characters is a bit more refined than its DS counterpart. The game also features English singing that was pulled from the DS port. I'm a weeb so I keep it in Japanese though. The excuse was that it was necessary to add extra scenarios... which we never got. The biggest difference however is definitely the combat system.  Instead of your typical turn-based FF-esque combat, you fight on an isometric field where you need to move your character and then select an action akin to Disgaea or other SRPG titles. I love this as it makes it feel more engaging than if it just had you choose an action every turn. The DS port understandably had to change to accommodate the smaller screen. Main characters are well written with Cornet and Kururu having a big-sister little-sister dynamic. Kururu offers Cornet guidance and snippets of wisdom. Cornet dreams of finding love(same here), loves dolls, and is great at the trumpet and singing. They both go really well together and offer some nice comedic and touching moments. This game offers its own spice when you line it up with the other RPGs of its time. The musical numbers are a joy and not something I recall seeing elsewhere in the genre. Cornet being a female protagonist with the mission to rescue her prince is still uncommon. I wish they could have fleshed it out more as this is only a 10-hour game and they don't interact all that much.  If you like musicals, colourful settings, cute dolls, a little spice to your combat, and appreciate a funny RPG that doesn't take itself too seriously, you'll love this one. While not by the same company, another game I'd love to see get a PC port someday is Tail Concerto.

_childDocuments_.review: Visuals: the best part about the game, great monster and character designs, cute sprites, charming animations and decent backgrounds (although they overuse the cave and dungeon ones).Music: definitely not the composer's best work, not bad by any means but overall bland / too safe. The musical numbers are cool though.Story: some funny dialogue here and there, it doesn't take itself too seriously and has some good serious moments, but it ends up feeling underdeveloped, the characters don't do enough to carry the shallow plot.Gameplay: extremely easy (even on hard difficulty) and repetitive, zero strategy involved. All dungeons consist of single screen labyrinths with random encounters and it has a few moments where progression is blocked by some weird triggers (like speaking to some overly specific npc or going back to an area with little or no hints).Personally I enjoyed the game, I like cheesy musicals and it's short enough that the bad parts didn't drag on too long. But I still don't recommend it, unless you really know what you're getting into and want to turn off your brain for a bit to enjoy the presentation.

_childDocuments_.review: A really charming and funny JRPG. But I dropped it because of the old-school game design. Yes, it is an old game, but dungeons are so easy to get lost in because every room looks the same. It isn't always obvious where to go either, usually, you had to go to a random place or talk to a random NPC. On the positive side again, it had really beautiful sprite work and animations. The voice acting/singing was good too, at least to my untrained ears. The random encounter rate was also really fair, not too many at all. The combat is fun, it's like a baby version of Trails/Kiseki and was very engaging, but the fights were so easy and over fast, so I'm not sure who the demographic of the game actually is. Still, I can see it's a good game, but not for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: Writing a review for Rhapsody is hard.There is the charm of the characters...watching the first minutes alone is fun. Seeing the main character playing her horn...and of course the musical part. I played both parts only to hear the english and the japanese singing...well if you like the unnatural high singing.All those parts are screaming: Buy me.But we should also talk about the shadow side of this game. You see there is actual only very little interacting between the characters and only a few songs in the whole game.Most of the game you are running around in dungeons.Not bad if you consider that this is an RPG.If (and that's an big IF) the designers only put a little more variety into this game.Most of the time you see the same picture...corridors with walls. Most screens you can walk through with few steps and than the same picture welcomes you.I played with normal difficult and there was no problem with winning the fights (even boss fights were done in seconds).Early on you have all the puppets from the game.Now, I've missed some achievements but playing the same game again...sorry but there is just not enough meat on this bone. Oh, and the long playtime is only because for some of the achievements you must grind different characters till they reach a certain level.So can I recommend this game?I would say....if you get it on sale it is OK. If you like an easy game with funny characters...buy it.But don't expect anything close to an real RPG.
_childDocuments_.name: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: I never had a chance to play this on the PS1 back in elementary  days but now that it got ported to PC, I can finally say that this game is pretty fun. The dungeon design leaves alot to be desired since it plays mostly like a dungeon crawler with maze like maps and dead ends. And it is clear that the budget for this game wasn't big due to how overused certain backgrounds are used and reused across the game. The game is also pretty damn easy even on the hardest difficulty as I pretty much auto battled all the time and won without too much thinking. But these, I feel, are entirely forgivable due to the charm of its story and characters. It can be funny at times and can be pretty dark at some points too. Believe it or not, there is even a psychological aspect to this game too when it comes to making decisions that could impact the way the world views Cornet. The kind of stuff that makes you question if you are playing as a good or bad guy kinda stuff. I was legitimately surprised at the amount of themes this game tackles onto its story such as what it means to love, what a person would do for it, tragedy, suicide, and other stuff. It is not all fun and games. The songs in the game are pretty good and I enjoyed the cutscenes where the characters are singing and stuff. It was my first time experiencing a musical JRPG and honestly, I wish there were more of these kinds of games. It is a relatively short game but I would still recommend for people to play this hidden gem of the PS1 days. Rhapsody 2 and 3 are also getting localized on Steam in Summer 2023 so this was a great chance for me to get prepared for the other games I had no idea even existed. Play this game people!
_childDocuments_.name: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely easy, extremely cute, and good insight into NIS's tactical RPG roots.  Note:  There are definitely some problematic parts--some sexism and one random homophobic frog NPC comment--but mostly it's a cute jaunt.  Would love to see more of Cornet and friends in non-Rhapsody titles instead of just Marjoly!
_childDocuments_.name: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe this is something I could enjoy with some more time into it but as a grown ass adult man it's just not for me. It really feels like this was made with "teenage girls first JRPG" in mind, and hey good for them and good for you if it's your thing, but I can't sit through the song that plays in the demo on the main menu without wincing in pain, and I grew up doing musical theater. The story and characters are clearly meant to invoke Mew Mew Power or Magical Do-Re-Mi tiers of "I want to find my prince, fall in love, and be a good house wife", and it doesn't help that it looks like ATLUS decided to play script doctor. Aye, aye, Captain Crunch indeed.The combat is at least interesting, it's a very watered down Trails in the Sky and seems like there's some sort of pokemon esq monster collecting later which sounds neat, sadly I ended up falling down into an ancient dungeon of identical rooms and getting lost for 30 minutes before I realized I didn't even need to be there and it just gave me some money at best. I suppose that's partly my fault, but this does come from the era of RPGs where keeping the player up to date on what they're doing is asking a bit too much if you missed it the first time.TL;DR great if you want magical girl falls in love and finds her prince type story with a basic but decent JRPG, not for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: The Japanese dub for the singing is better than the English dub by a lot, so you want to play it listening to the singing in Japanese. THOUGH, for some reason, the team that brought this to Steam made it so the subtitles for the Japanese singing is romaji letters spelling out the actual Japanese being sung; making the songs impossible to understand if you don't speak Japanese. There is no option for English subtitles translating the Japanese singing, so you HAVE to play the game in English if you want to understand the Musical parts of the game. One part with the Evil Queen NEEDS to be in English if you want to understand her singing her motivations; meaning if you play in Japanese, you are literally missing out on important story bits.Do yourself a favor and avoid this game. It's very much a nostalgia bait port for people that played it as a kid. It's a subpar badly aged RPG with a generic early 2000's shoujo story. Definitely not worth the price tag. Especially because 90% of the game is just reused assets and dungeons that are created to all look the same with a labyrinth design that doesn't do anything but elongate your time getting into random battles going through rooms that all look the same, without a single puzzle or anything unique between dungeons. This game is 90% dungeons, 5% cutscenes, 4% towns, and 1% musicals. For "A Musical Adventure", there were like 5 total unique songs (and only one good song).
_childDocuments_.name: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: The story has a few funny moments, the japanese singing voices aren't that bad and the CRT filter brings back some good memories. However, everything else just feels very underwhelming.The lack of animations, sound effect variety and challenging combat makes the game worse than it has to be.100% requires 2 playthroughs, in which you'll need to open pretty much every treasure chest, finish every sidequest (including a missable one) and grind levels so that you can see every spell. It's not difficult, but can be very time consuming if you're unlucky.

_childDocuments_.name: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: I can just barely recommend this one. The pixel art is great, the music is nice, and the story is low-stakes but entertaining and humorous. I really liked all the characters too. However, this game really fumbles the bag when it comes to the gameplay. First of all, the dungeon-crawling sucks. The dungeons only come in two designs, ugly caverns and generic stone temples. They reuse the exact same screens in all of these dungeons and just make them long, boring mazes for the sake of dragging out playtime. These dungeons will drive you mad unless you just use a guide. Second, the combat sucks. There is almost zero challenge even on hard mode, and the only time you will die is when you accidentally go into an area with enemies that are too high a level for your party. In fact, the scariest enemies in the games are the ones that can confuse your party members, because your own party members hit way harder than any of the enemies in this game could even dream of. The battles take place on weird SRPG-esque isometric grids, and I can't figure out why. It doesn't add any strategy to the game, it just drags out battles by having to needlessly move your party members towards the enemies. And these battle screens are often so cramped that you will typically have only 3 of your party members involved in the fight while your 4th party member is sucking his thumb in a corner because your party members have already surrounded the enemy. You can recruit lots of other party members, but it's absolutely pointless. They all start at level 1, which means not only will they be a liability while you're sitting there fighting level 20 enemies, but it takes so long to level them that it's pointless. And if you choose to level-up a monster instead of a puppet, once they die, they're gone for good! How about just don't bother? Yeah, I mean the game is so easy you can win all battles with the first few puppets that join your party, so why not just keep the same party and ignore everyone else? It reminds me a lot of Ni no Kuni and the system is just as annoying here as it is there.The game length is also pathetic, it's something like 15 hours and that's if you're going slow and really taking your time, you could probably beat it in 10 hours if you're focused. And this runtime only exists because the dungeons are mazes. But the maze design also extends to the overworld. Often you just won't have a clue where you're supposed to go next. You should honestly play this game with a walkthrough. If you don't, all you're doing is wasting your time, there is no joy to be had in having to traverse the dungeons or figure out where to go next by talking to every NPC in the game every time you finish a dungeon.There are other minor issues like typos, and one particularly annoying glitch where if you save and then exit out of the save menu too quick, a dialog box will get stuck on the screen. These are not really that bad in the grand scheme of things, but this is what, the game's 3rd release? I mean damn, tons of classic JRPGs don't even get that kind of love. The least they could do is fix some of these issues.When you think of classic PS1 JRPGs, what comes to mind? Maybe FF7, Grandia, Xenogears. Rhapsody never comes up, and for a good reason. The sad thing here is that the game sabotaged itself by being lazy in its game design when a few simple changes could have elevated this game to classic status. The world here was definitely designed with care and attention, and the graphics and music reminds me a lot of one of my favorite RPGs, Super Mario RPG. Unfortunately you spend way too much time dungeon crawling for such poorly implemented gameplay. But at the end of the day, it's a competently executed PS1-era JRPG and if that's all you're looking for, this will definitely do. Would I play the sequels? Probably not. But I don't regret my time with this one. 6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very simple and easy tactics JRPG that has a very basic 'save the prince from evil' story. The reason this game is interesting is because it's a musical. I only recommend this if you like musicals, as the 9 or so tracks are paced fairly well throughout the relatively short playtime and feel like they are straight out of a Disney princess movie. It's a concept I'm surprised I haven't seen more often.Note: Steam doesn't sync offline steam deck play so playtime of review is inaccurate.
_childDocuments_.name: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10Rhapsody is a surprisingly fun short story that subverts a few of the classic tropes and also manages to touch mature themes now and then. 9/10It is called a musical adventure, so this rating was to be expected. 8/10Very charming, and still manage to work today. The only bad thing is how repetitive dungeons look which makes them a hassle.  7/10To be honest it is pretty simplistic, and if you want 100% everything it will be tedious since you need to lvl-up several puppets for their side quests and you just don’t need that to beat the game. The dungeons are very repetitive and horrible to navigate; but in general terms it is a short and simple story without too many complications in terms of gameplay. 8.5/10It is a nice story about a girl who is in love, and in a change of pace, must save the prince from the evil witch. It has a surprising amount of sidequests that tackle some delicate themes. I would say that for the most part, it is a great story if you want to introduce your children to videogames while having a laugh.
_childDocuments_.name: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game on a whim as I though it would be better to play it this way then through emulation, and I like supporting NIS anyway.This game was a cute little RPG, I beat it in about 16 hours, and I know I goofed around a little.The music was great, especial they little musical numbers, they had that "1990s English dub" vib to them.The graphics where wonderful, game was colorful and bright, monsters and characters where detailed, and I had this Siren in my party that would just flash her boobs every time we wont a fight... good times.The game is a good bit on the easy side, I never really had any problems at any point, and only grinded in a few spots when I was trying to get a certain monster in my party.I loved everything from the story to the gameplay, and I look forward to finding out what happens next in the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game.Story:Cornet heads out on a journey to save the Prince. And along the way, she faces her trials, and comes into the reality of how her mother died. Eventually, this playing into how it ends. A puppet who has their wish granted will pass on and reincarnate, this is one of the main things in the story. While it is funny, it is also sad, and the songs reflect this.System:It is a simple turn based game. where Cornet empowers her puppets, but also has some actions based on how many times she uses her horn in battle.Music:Amazing.Art Style:Great.Overall:I recommend giving this game a go.
_childDocuments_.name: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: You don't play this game for a challenge, you play it for the silly antics, the plot, the "bad" guys giving your character life lessons, and the strong characters who are going to show initiative (or insult their old hag of a boss for hitting on younger men.)Play that horn and make all the dreams come true~ I originally played this on DS, so i'm enjoying finding all the original bits not included like monster recruitment and tactics combat which makes ranged puppets actually....you know ranged.
_childDocuments_.name: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: I had always wanted to play this around the time it originally released but missed it for whatever reason. It's a light and breezy RPG that is firmly from the PS1 era for better and worse. It's absurdly easy for anyone who has played another other RPG, but for me that didn't matter too much; I enjoyed it as a romp through a classic game with a fun localization. The battle system is pretty simplistic, but does have a nice sprinkling of tactics elements in there to keep it interesting. At roughly 8-10 hours the game does not overstay its welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: A very easy Disney-esque RPG that earns a recommendation off charm alone.  The gameplay is simplistic to a fault - a seasoned player will probably be bored by it but it's perfect for first timers or even younger children to play with parents.  The songs are silly and a little basic in composition but still deliver in their hilarity and heart.  Heavily reminiscent of 90s cartoons where despite (likely) being for kids there are plenty of jokes and innuendos for adults as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: ♫Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure, is a (as the title suggests) musical RPG with tons of unique characters, and world to explore![Before I get into this review, it might be a bit biased for one reason, that being I played this game when I was very little, and absolutely loved this game, I had sort of forgotten all about it until quite recently when I saw it on the steam store, I asked myself "why not give it a shot?"and I am glad I did, because this reignited my love for this hidden gem I'd call a masterpiece, especially for it's time]The artstyle is charming, and cute, the visuals are very good, especially for it's time, and the story is very engaging!If you give the time to sit down and really explore this game, and take it all in, reading the dialogue, paying attention, replaying the game even, I'm sure you'll come to realize my obsession with the game, it's a very lighthearted, innocent, adorable, cute game that really allows you to sit back and enjoy a relaxing game again, at least for me, I don't usually have a relaxing, and calming time with games like I do with games like Rhapsody.The combat is fun, it's your run of the mill late 90s turn based combat, but it's really well made, not issues so far in terms of combat, if you're familiar with JRPG's and their combat systems, you'll fair well in this game.The music is really well composed, fits the visuals, and story of the game perfectly, and goes hand in hand with the games overall tone, it actually enhances and establishes the tone more firmly, a lighthearted RPG with some really good songs worthy of an encore!The story is more engaging than anything in this game, the cute, witty, humorous, and sometimes corny banter that takes place between the characters, draws the player to want more dialogue, and it's just enough dialogue where it isn't over saturated with useless text boxes, that draw out the length of the game, but just enough where you really get a sense that these characters hold meaning and value into the world you are in.As I am sure you can tell, I am not really good at writing reviews, considering this as being my first ever time, trying to write a review for a game I adore, I'd say it's an alright review.Well for a quick conclusion as I don't want to drag this out, it's a masterpiece, a hidden gem, and I am sure the other 2 games will do it justice! 10/10.🎶
_childDocuments_.name: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: This is a charming little jrpg.The premise is a simple fairytale. Defeat the evil witch and rescue the prince. Each village you pass on the way has it's own little side-plot, and sometimes they are surprisingly tragic. The characters are likable and have some depth to them. They are also quite funny.The gameplay is simple but still fun. It has a strategy rpg-style combat system but it's a bit too easy, even on hard mode. I went through the game just basic attacking normal enemies and using magic on bosses or large groups. I never had to use items and I didn't even bother grinding for the most powerful 'omega' spells.Dungeon design is poor. Lots of identical single screens with one or more exits and lots of dead ends. My short-term memory isn't very good, so these got frustrating to navigate in the late game. Maps exist on gamefaqs though.Overall it's still worth playing and will only take you 10-15 hours.EDIT: I forgot to add that there is a monster capturing system, but the monsters are weaker than your normal puppets so it's better to just ignore it
_childDocuments_.name: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: i never played this game before nor am i the target demo and this game is easy even on hard but you know what this is still a good/funny game and a great first rpg title cornet is a funny the songs are catchy in either language i think the only reasons people would hate this is it being an old ps1 title or to easy but if you got young kids or are just brand new to this genre give this a go but seriously play it on hard if you want most things die in 1 hit i can;'t even migine how much easier the other modes are
_childDocuments_.name: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: Not a very hard srpg, its strenght comes from the charm of the characters and the feeling of watching an old shojo show. You can't help but feel a very warm feeling of nostalgia with each song, though I would've liked if nippon ichi actually made subs for them and not only a romanji adaptation (I'm playing with the jp voices). _childDocuments_.name: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: The story alone is worth the play. The price I feel is worth it. The game has a lot of cute detail and funny dialogue. The adding of music into the game in the form of song's is a nice touch to a RPG style game. Not to mention the interesting attacks from the main character. Sure to give you a bit of a chuckle. _childDocuments_.name: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: Really good jrpg, solid story, music + dialogue. Just overall super fun to play.Gripes include hard mode being way too easy, a lot of unnecessary grind backloaded into achievements, and beating the game on hardmode not unlocking the achieve for normal mode, necessitating a 2nd playthrough.Took about 15 hours to get to the end of hard mode + the status effect achieve.Then another 5hrs of grind in the  to get all my dudes leveled for the puppet quests & omega skills. I think the main game could be completed in ~8h if ignoring those achieves w/ compounded rng grind. I have 34h bc I left the game running overnight.The game was easily clearable w/o that grind and even like monsters you'd find in the alt endgame dungeon were rare but pointless - leveling them adds nothing to your overall power level since there's no postgame and the final boss is killable late 30s. I went from lvl 44 up to lvl 78 completing the omega skills / puppet quest achieve.Because of how agility makes you dodge monster attacks (and you have more agi the more you level up...) the slightest amount of grind makes you outlevel monsters and their status effects, which need to be inflicted on Cornet (and also use monster mp), so even if you find the right monster and they use their skill, there's like a 10% chance it'll actually effect you, and a greater chance they'll just run out of mp to use the skill = need to encounter them again. The achieve to get 7 status effects requires hard farming + skipping turns for hours on end waiting for the mobs to use the skills as a result. This further exacerbates the issue as you soak up large amounts of xp while farming status effects. The items that remove status effects are largely worthless since you'll never get inflicted by them unless horribly unlucky and even then they clear after a battle. I didn't need any healing items outside of the  boss, to heal the 3 stooges who were lvl ~12 after the raid aoe  Since level scaling trivializes all encounters I ended up 1-2 shotting most things including bosses. Autobattle encourages muscle mages up until lvl 31 where you can just spam (w/ holy charm for 1/2 mp) aoe skills since you regen full mp on level up and Omega-x skills (e.g. Meteor) can 1-tap full-screen without movement.Also don't understand why monsters, given penalty of permadeath and no puppet buff, even exist since they're not comparably strong even when leveled. Puppets basically do everything better, so why bother with the monster system outside of needing one mister golem for the achieve.
_childDocuments_.name: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: I remember playing this when I was around 11 years old, and the story absolutely sucked me in. It lasted as one of my absolute favorite games throughout my life, and I was so excited to see it come to Steam. It it so heartwarming, with moments that will make you sit and think, decisions that will break your heart, and music that you can't help but sing along to. An absolute gem that has lasted through the years.
_childDocuments_.name: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: A charming RPG with great story, characters and is enjoyable to look at and listen to.This game has dungeon crawling with copy-paste room layouts, so if you don't like getting lost, you may need to find some maps online.A huge positive for me is that you can recruit most of the monster classes through battle. So if you want to change up your party, you can add some monsters. (You can also store characters in a shop if you run out of room in your party.)The music in this game is so good and you have the option to have either English or Japanese audio for the singing sections. As other reviews mention, I suggest turning on the CRT filter in the options.Also exclusive to this version, they replaced some of the contents of chests with hidden artwork you can collect.
_childDocuments_.name: Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly a blast from my childhood, for years I have been wanting to play this game remastered on my PC and it looks like a finally got my wish. This is an earlier NIS title that was originally released on the PS1 so don't be expecting Disgaea or La Pucelle type of game here. Combat is fairly steady with 4 party member at a time, sadly if a member isn't in active combat it doesn't level up so you will have lots of puppets on the side lines that aren't gaining EXP.This game is very story line driven and the music in it is very well done for it's time. If you are okay with older style games and enjoy a solid JRPG then look no further and be prepared for singing occasionally as this is a musical ;)

A remake of the PlayStation original, Rhapsody: A Musical Adventure for Nintendo DS delivers high-resolution 2D sprites, innovative music-based RPG gameplay, and more features than ever before. name: WrestleQuest
detailed_description: Powerbomb and piledrive your way through a massive pixel art universe where professional wrestling and RPG fantasy collide. Take a hero’s journey... in tights! Upgrade from aspiring rookie to world champ by training, learning, glamming, and SLAMMING to the top of the pro wrestling food chain. Draw inspiration from wrestling icons like Jake the Snake Roberts, 'Macho Man' Randy Savage, and even André the Giant. Explore worlds based on their lofty careers. Classic RPG combat meet wrestling moves, match styles, and gimmicks galore. Wild realms, exotic monsters, action figure fighters, and spandexed allies await as this fantasy goes beyond the ring. Choose your moves, style, taunts, and even your entrance as you learn what it takes to be the cream of the crop in the pro wrestling world of your dreams.

_childDocuments_.review: You know they say that all games are created equal, but you look at me and you look at WWE 2K23 and you can see that statement is not true. See, normally if you go one on one with another wrestling game, you got a 50/50 chance of winning. But I'm a genetic freak and I'm not normal! So you got a 25%, AT BEST, at beat me. Then you add AEW Fight Forever to the mix, your chances of winning drastic go down. See the 3 way on Steam, you got a 33 1/3 chance of winning, but I, I got a 66 and 2/3 chance of winning, because AEW Fight Forever KNOWS he can't beat me and he's not even gonna try!So WWE 2K23, you take your 33 1/3 chance, minus my 25% chance and you got an 8 1/3 chance of winning on Steam. But then you take my 75% chance of winning, if we was to go one on one, and then add 66 2/3 per cents, I got 141 2/3 chance of winning on Steam. See WWE, the numbers don't lie, and they spell disaster for you on Steam.
_childDocuments_.name: WrestleQuest

_childDocuments_.review: I dont understand what went wrong. I was really looking forward to this game. It should have been an easy home run, or 3 count as the case may be. They literally took two things I love, Wrestling and RPGs, put them together and somehow made me hate it.It has turn based combat. In my mind that is an almost impossible thing to screw up, in its simplicity rather than anything else, and yet they did with near constant QTEs.Almost every attack has at least 1 QTE, maybe more, including basic attacks, and even the ones that dont need the little characters to do their little song and dance every single time which eventually, and by that I mean almost immediately, becomes tedious. None of the moves can be skipped or sped up, presumably because of the QTEs.Also adding a PINNING MINIGAME, something that the WWE 2k games tried and everyone hated. It boggles the mind.To add to list of things that move far too slowly, outside of combat you character is pretty sluggish too, with the ever so useful 'Run' button allowing you to move at what feels like 1.0000001 times faster.The music is very good, when there is music. Some over world areas have music and some do not. Hopefully that is a technical issue and not a choice. A  highlight of this game is that when you enter a battle in one of the aforementioned 'over world areas with music' the music flows from the over world music to the battle music literally seamlessly.The art is fun and colourful. The main characters have style to them. I felt like the choice to have the setting be a toy box and all the characters toys was a bad one, that detracted and distracted from the game rather than adding to it, this could easily be a taste issue and regardless is far from the worst thing about it.I was looking forward to this for a long time and am disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: WrestleQuest

_childDocuments_.review: I received a copy of this game through Dare Drop, and I was really excited to give it a playthrough.I want to start by saying that I really wanted to like this game. Heck, part of me still does! It is an extremely charming idea: wrestling toys trying to save the world of wrestling within the toy room. It's a great little idea, but sadly the game gets in its own way time and time again. I'll start with what I liked, and then I'll list my issues- The art work is wonderful. Real love went into every sprite, background, and effect.- The music is fantastic. Really matches the scenes, and vibe of the game as a whole.- A lot of enjoyable (if somewhat shallow) characters to interact with. You can tell who's a face and who's a heel and it just works.- The writing, when you actually get to it, is pretty well done. It's marching out a lot of game and wrestling tropes, and there's nothing wrong with that because this is basically one protracted wrestling season. It makes sense.- The battle mechanics are on flavour. Whilst I think they are far too drawn out for their own good, I think the core mechanics of the battles are really cute. It's in a ring; everyone's doing wrestling moves; you have to pin your enemy; etc.- I enjoyed the various plotlines and hopping between them, and how they eventually came together. Mostly.- I legitimately enjoyed the inclusion of the wrestling statues that gave me (a non-wrestling fan) some interesting history that helped build the world. I also liked that those wrestlers were actually in game, and you could get them as managers, summons, and the givers of legendary equipment. That was a really fun touch.At it's core, I think there's the bones of a good game here, I really honestly do. Sadly WrestleQuest is extremely disrespectful of the players time, and I'll outline why:- The QTEs in battle extend battle time too much. Yes you can now auto-win them (which i recommend) due to recent updates. Also enabling the auto-win does not work for plot-based combat scenarios, which means even though it's an accessibility option, you are still forced to do them for certain fights. That defeats the purpose.- The walking and running speed is too slow. Yes they've made adjustments, no they're not good enough.- The walking speed issue is exacerbated by the fact that you have to traverse large world map areas that have almost nothing to do in them. Each area has a couple points of interest, and you have to run a marathon to almost all of them- This is even further compounded by the fact that every sidequest effectively requires you to region-hop to do them, and there is no reasonable method of quick travel. Yes, there are 2 sort of methods of quick travel  and  but they are at best point to point, and some quests require you to hop across multiple regions- If the above wasn't enough, there is also the fact that many dungeons are choke-points for travel. There is no way to bypass a dungeon if you're just trying to get to the other side, regardless if you've actually defeated that dungeon before. I walked through one dungeon six times just for some cutscenes. Six. Times.- A great example of the game disrespecting you takes place late in the game in - There are many, many instances where the game will put you in a cutscene and say "okay lets go to {some location}" and then hands control back to you to walk to  to trigger the next cutscene. Why? Just make a longer cutscene and include what you need to include. So many instances of this.- You cannot run from any battle once engaged. You can attempt to avoid fighting a unit entirely, but when that (often) fails, you are forced into combat. No exceptions are made even if you dramatically out-level your opponents.- The mini-games included in WrestleQuest are all half-baked and not enjoyable at all. They all feel bolted-on and clunky. They are supposed to be adding the ability to skip them, which leads me to the thought of "why have them at all if so many people want to skip them?" If your mini-game is not legitimately adding anything to the players enjoyment, don't add it.- The plot drags on. I know it's a wrestling game and you need the twists and whatnot, but there is a lot of "well I guess that happened" in the game wherein you're just doing stuff because the game said so, and it's not really contributing to the overall narrative.- You are introduced to gimmicks through the game (dramatic moments, tag team matches, cage match) that are neat and almost never re-used.- - You never get to fight - The ending of this game is an absolute travesty, and I'm going to go into why.It may be the worst ending to any piece of media I have consumed, and I don't say that lightly.  It honestly feels like the writers, the developers, or the accountants ran out of resources and they just had to throw something together.What bugs me most about the ending is that if the whole point is that  My point here is that there were so many different ways you could have brought in previous mechanics or plot beats to make it a meaningful ending, and instead you give us... what you gave us.I feel robbed of my 60 hours of playtime.In the end, WrestleQuest is an amazing example of people saying "hey what if we added X" and everyone else in the room saying "yeah! and what if we also added X" over and over until the vision board was filled up. Then literally no one came in with a red pen (or garden sheers) to cut away anything. This game desperately needed an editor: someone to say "no" once in awhile.I truly believe that you could trim out half of this game and throw in some QoL changes, and end up with a really tight, enjoyable 25 hour game. Instead we have this drawn-out, meandering storyline with a bunch of filler cruft, topped off with an absolute lame-duck ending.

_childDocuments_.review: *PSA* This is free on the Netflix mobile app if you're subscribed.Just played around 5 hours, so I don't consider this a real review by my own criteria. WrestleQuest is actually a traditional turn-based RPG like the old Final Fantasy games, but with strong WWF wrestling trappings... complete with famous wrestlers from the 80's and 90's that you'll see, even "summon" (not seen that yet), but don't play as. What I didn't expect is that this is in a toy world and that all the wrestlers are action figures. In fact, all the characters are toys from one kind or another. I had to get used to that look, but it turns out that, in fact, it permits the game to be more imaginative and varied. Other than that, the graphics made me initially think of something made with RPG Maker (not a compliment), but that was an unfair assessment. They're pretty, they're detailed and they grew on me. The animations are well done and there's lots of little incidental stuff in the world.There's all the typical retro RPG tropes, but they're very well integrated into the wrestling/Toy Story theme, surprinsingly so.  You have levelling, exploring towns, talking to people there, walking on the overland map, equiping better gear and turn-based battles with gimmicks (think magic). There's also trash talking before certain matches (think Monkey Island insult swordfighting), managers with different bonuses, designing your own entrance, karma level (good or evil by your dialog choices), silly mini-games and hyping the crowd which are nice touches. All of that, except the hype meter, has been introduced but little used up to now. However, most of the time will eventually be spent wandering around "dungeons" with battles that are not really wrestling matches (no extras) but easy fights with flunkies until you get to the big boss. Not that noticeable up to now, but I do see the battles getting strategic with the special moves and status effects. I was afraid the lack of enemy variety might get tiresome, but the "dungeons" seem to end roughly at the right time (up to now). I actually like the QTE (quick-time events) but would have liked less frequency and more variety beyond pressing one of the four gamepad buttons. The option to slow them down doesn't seem to do much of anything, but I'm sure that will be fixed, and an option to win them automatically is forthcoming. In fact, there are toggles to make the game as easy as you want it to be.The characters you meet are fun, the cornier the better, although there's a lot of model recycling, which is to be expected in that type of RPG. I like the story and I like that you alternate between two parties. I wish some party members had more personality (looking at you Barbae and Toy Box Jimmy). It feels like I've barely scratched the surface of the game considering how many famous wrestlers I haven't seen yet, so there's tons of content. It's a love letter to an era of wrestling, but it's definitely *not* a wrestling action game, and I also think it can appeal to fans of retro RPGs who'd like a change from the typical fantasy setting.  This is like the Final Fantasy/Mario RPG/WWF Wrestling/Toy Story hybrid I never thought I'd see or wanted. I'm rather pleased up to now, and I just hope it doesn't get too tedious as I advance.

_childDocuments_.review: I have felt for many years that the tumultuous backstage world of professional wrestling would make an excellent RPG. All wrestling fans have heard the stories of events like Hulk Hogan pulling his creative control clause to refuse to lose to somebody the promotion wants to put over. Ultimate Warrior famously got fired after trying to hold up Vince McMahon for a ton of money the night of a pay-per-view. The entire real life rivalry between Bret Hart and Shawn Michaels. In many ways, the stuff going on behind the scenes is more interesting than what happens on our television sets.So when WrestleQuest was announced, and the concept of an up and comer in the business's journey through the political mess of the wrestling business was on the table to say I was excited for it would be an understatement. On paper this game is practically tailor made for me. An easy 10/10 GOTY. However, in practice, it became one of the most disappointing and frustrating titles I've played in a long time.The story primarily sticks out as a down point. A video game in a genre primarily focused on storytelling, about a industry that is entirely about telling a story in the ring. The eternal struggle of heel and face. Good vs Evil. On paper this story should be an easy tale to tell. Unfortunately what WrestleQuest gives the player is a story that probably could have been told in 10 hours, and pads it out for damn near 40+. Every time it feels like the plot is going somewhere you are immediately without fail yanked in a completely opposite direction. Sometimes story arcs don't even complete before you're bouncing multiple times between different parties doing completely different things. Characters just do things with the most trivial and barely developed motivations possible.The game has a karma system where you can choose responses to make yourself a face, or a heel. For the most part this does absolutely nothing. The game doesn't even have any indication of if a choice is a heel choice or a face choice. Even a green border versus a red border or something would be sufficient. And yes sometimes the dialog is semi obvious as your choices will be something like "donate money to the orphans" and "literally burn a child alive for no reason" but there are plenty of them where it's a slightly differently worded insult and you're still insulting somebody so neither feels like a clearly marked face option.Side quests also continue this trend of being padded out. You'll get a side mission, and you won't even be able to access the area you need to go for 10+ real time gameplay hours. Instead you'll go there as a different party ensuring that by the time the person who has to go there actually arrives, you will be so massively overleveled for this side quest you got so long ago you don't even remember the story context for it existing that you'll one shot everything immediately. Some side quests throw a bunch of dialog choices at you, and if you answer any one of them wrong ONCE it completely ends the side quest with no way of trying it again, locking you out of summons, gear, and content. Half the time it's not even clear where you're meant to be getting the information that is asked of you and if you don't know the question is coming and haven't saved in a while whelp your choices are to simply miss the content or redo hours of gameplay to get back to where you were. This is straight up poor game design. If I'm trying to stop a kidnapping and I fail to persuade an NPC to believe a lie, why does the game not offer alternative methods of completing the quest? Maybe I could break into the base and defeat everybody and save them directly, where as persuading the NPC skips a bunch of optional battles. Maybe you allow the player to have a mulligan where they can get the option wrong once. An auto save when you leave or exit a screen would be sufficient. I would even accept letting me go all the way back to where you get the quest and having to do the whole thing over again rather than the current method of "whoops, did you misclick? That's it mate".These things could be waved away if the game play is solid. And to a degree it is. However, the over reliance on certain mechanics combined with just how long and padded out the game is very clearly makes fun battles become tedious. Every move you do has a QTE, as the game attempts to do something akin to Super Mario RPG. You hit the QTEs for higher damage, or better defending. However the timing for these QTEs varies in speed, and which button you have to push. Every. Single. Time. You have zero chance of developing any sort of muscle memory. This has been noted as a problem so often that the devs added a slow QTEs accessibility option (with no indication on if turning it on or not will void achievements), and they've also announced they're gonna just add a no QTE option.This also carries into the pinfall mechanic. Some enemies you can't fully defeat until you pin for a three count. This is represented via a bar that slides right to left. You line a cursor over a green square and click three times. The game implies it gets easier every time somebody kicks out on follow up pin attempts but honestly I never noticed a difference. like the QTE timing the timing for this is also very erratic. The devs have also announced an auto pin is coming, as again, the mini game gets tedious very quickly. The other big mechanic is hype, and hype types. Hype Types are sort of like special modifiers you can apply to a character to determine what the fans like about them. So when they do specific actions they'll get a hype bar benefit. Reaching certain points on the hype bar unlocks big buffs (and if you go into negatives debuffs).However, this has two major issues. The first is every hype type has massive negatives listed, such as you take double damage and the like. So when the hype types are first introduced somebody is gonna take one look at that and figure using no hype type will likely be better, to avoid taking massive damage for what they won't understand is a MASSIVE buff. The other, more critical problem is when the game puts dramatic moments in front of you. Dramatic Moments are special boss fight events where you have to do certain objectives to complete a story line, akin to a real wrestling match. Sometimes these are skip able, and you merely get a bonus item drop. Sometimes, however, these are completely mandatory - and hype type can break things completely. In one boss fight you are tasked with continuously getting negative hype. You cannot complete the boss fight until you accomplish this. However, while I had the hype type active for my character I was intentionally just doing basic attacks and putting the controller down and intentionally missing every QTE to try build up as little hype as possible so that when the boss did his moves his negative hype would get me there. Unfortunately even failing to do things garnered so much hype that I was always in the positives.And all of this is before the bugs. Achievements not unlocking even though you have hit the points where they should have. Moments where the literal entire ring background simply doesn't load and any attempt to do any special move causes the game to endlessly softlock the characters can't move into position. An entire town that randomly might teleport you to the wrong area entirely and render you unable to leave. Janky mini games where your car won't even be on camera but still taking damage when you have no way of seeing what you're driving into. And that is just the stuff I've personally seen, or personally seen people mentioning.This game has so much potential. An amazing concept. But the devs did almost nothing with it. I want to like it. I want to love it. But nothing short of completely re-writing the game is gonna fix all the padding issues. So at this point I'll just settle for being able to play it, without it just feeling like a slog at all times.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to preface this review by saying this isn't a bad game. I don't recommend it, it has many issues, but it's perfectly acceptable. But I'm disappointed enough with it and feel the issues I have with it are numerous enough that the only honest review I can give it is a negative one. I'm a lapsed wrestling fan and I have very fond memories of playing various wrestling games, and I quite enjoy turn based RPGs. So when this game was announced I immediately wishlisted it. The idea of an indie RPG about pro wrestling, which has the actual Macho Man and other famous wrestlers in it, sounded right up my alley.So I'll start with what I like about the game. The combat is pretty excellent. It's simple but engaging turn based rpg combat, every character has unique skills, the various moves and status effects all have a strategic use, there's fun synergy between various abilities, characters and status ailments. It's not super complex and some of it feels half-baked but it works. You can even pin people, good stuff.The pixel art is also great. It's gorgeously animated, every cameo is recognizable, and the grapples are mostly readable despite the chibi style.The music is also quite good. It sticks in your mind and has a lot of energy.There was also a storyline in the middle of the game featuring a luchador having to choose between being a good family man and his career that I thought was quite well done. Unfortunately, that's the end of my positive feelings about this game.The first and foremost complaint I have about the game is in its writing. In a word, it's bad. To start with, the dialogue constantly feels stilted and unnatural. Run-on sentences, inconsistent speech patterns, awkward turns of phrase, lifeless punctuation, samey voice for every character, inelegant exposition dumps, bad grammar.Even when specific celebrity cameos come into the game, the simple way their dialogue is written out creates an uncanny feeling that it's not really them talking. This game's story is almost entirely delivered through text, so this is a big problems.You also get really tired of hearing the canned audio lines each character has. They're too long and elaborate to be as frequent as they are, and distract from the text. You wouldn't know it from the advertising, but this game is about toys. Every character is a toy, every city is a playset, there's constant jokes and references to plastic and bootlegs and toy-ness. This is weird and makes the world and story feel a bit incoherent. I'm not meeting Macho Man, I'm meeting a Macho Man toy. There's so much emphasis placed on the toy stuff that it detracts from the wrestling stuff.I also hate how this game incorporates real world cameos. There are hundreds of them, but you're never given context for who they are, and most of them don't really fit into the story. I'll see an npc with an oddly realistic character portrait who'll say something that seems to be a catchphrase. Clearly I'm supposed to know who this is, but I don't. And it happens constantly. Most of them are podcasters or retired wrestlers, and I'm lucky I recognized half of them.Who the hell is going to know who Konnan is just from the name and one text box obliquely namedropping his podcast? I watched him in his prime and I barely remembered him. Is this game only meant for extremely online wrestling podcast nerds? A casual or non wrestling fan will get absolutely nothing from these cameos. But will those huge wrestling nerds need to constantly get wikipedia summaries of the real wrestlers who are featured as summons and quest NPCs?The story and characters are also just kind of boring. Really one dimensional stuff, peppered with unfunny jokes and dumb references. Oh, the canadian wrestler is a moose. He talks about maple syrup. The mexican one talks about hot peppers. Street Fighter would call this stuff tired and stereotypical. And they have no depth to get attached to them as people, either.The world isn't fleshed out and you don't understand the relationship between any of the wrestling organizations and characters enough to care about the stakes. At one point I was in the land of giants. Apparently giants exist in this world! No one else ever mentions giants and once you do a single quest there you never hear of them again. There's techno cities but also post apocalyptic wastelands but also horror themed regions. It's justified as being toy stuff but it just feels like bad improv.The story constantly gets distracted from the main quest to engage in dumb toy related sidetracks. If the story is supposed to be climbing the ranks of pro wrestling and defeating rival organizations, why am I dungeon delving into playsets to get macguffins? Every random encounter is just random 'wild' toys or wrestler toys just kind of deciding to fight you for no reason.The game also treats wrestling as a scripted show but also constantly has real fights between wrestlers. Which means you can't get interested in either version of the story because the other version constantly undercuts it. And the main character seems unaware that wrestling is fake, which stops being funny the 11th time it comes up.It seems very easy to write a rags to riches wrestling story or a story about an evil wrestling empire muscling out all the smaller federations, but this game totally bungles it.There's also an annoying and pointless framing device where podcasters recount the events of the story and comment on them between chapters. These sections add nothing and are totally lifeless, which I assume is a bad representation of the real life podcast.The dungeons are also boring as hell. Most of them are straight lines with samey combat encounters, sometimes if you're lucky you'll get a bad switch puzzle or a Simon Says section. The game also keeps switching the story perspective and playable party on you without warning you, which is kind of annoying and disorienting. You wanted to do a sidequest after this boss? Too bad, you're playing as other people on the other side of the world for the next half hour. It's also annoying in the sense that you can go from level 12 to level 3 between chapter transitions without warning.Traversal sucks. You eventually, very late in the game, get to use teleporters from a teleport hub to revisit locations, but for dozens of hours you'll just be walking across large empty maps, forced to re-traverse dungeons blocking your way to revisit cities during sidequests or to shop. And you also have to take slow boats to reach different continents. At no point do you ever get a chocobo or airship equivalent.There's some very undercooked mechanics. You can choose an entrance theme, fireworks, & taunts, and you unlock options as you progress in the story, but all any of them do is give you a tiny hype bonus before a fight. You also get to use it so rarely that it feels pointless to even have the mechanic at all.There are Paper Mario style button prompts in combat, but the game pauses and shows a timer every time, which makes missing them nearly impossible and greatly slows down combat. Even worse, the game is balanced around the idea you'll miss some of them, since they nullify some enemy attacks completely and give you crazy damage bonuses. The fact you're guaranteed to hit almost every one makes combat completely trivial.Theres some jank here, too. Sometimes animations play wrong. You can switch party members around but most cutscenes won't play if the main character isn't in the lead. I picked up a move meant for one character with another and it just kind of vanished into thin air. I also got trapped in a wall once and if I hadn't been rotating saves I would've been completely unable to progress.Bottom line, this game is completely lacking in charm, heavy in tedium and I don't know who it's for. It almost feels like the creators wanted to make a toy RPG but thought the online wrestling nerd would be easier to market to.

_childDocuments_.review: It's cute, it's funny, it's cool... and it's got a lot of heart. The devs are working hard to fix bugs that pop up and there's this weird feeling I get when playing as Muchacho Man that even though I know he's tough as nails, I also feel he's so sweet and adorkable that I don't want him to get hurt....is what my first review said. Now that I have more hours into the game, a lot of problems have come up that made me change my thumb from up to down. First off, all the things I said at the start still stand: I love the characters, the pixel art is cute and gorgeous... but the gameplay is bad. Really bad. The fights take forever to finish even if you turn auto-QTE on, because all enemies are bullet sponges, they start every fight by buffing their armor or evasion and then using long animations to deal chip damage. Whenever a fight starts, I groan, because I know it'll be several minutes to finish an encounter... and there are A LOT of encounters. At first it was okay when the fights were fast and I only had to pin the occasional enemy, but then I ended up in the military zone with the B-party, and for some reason I had to pin EVERY. SINGLE. ENEMY. And that was after chipping them down with scratch damage as there are no vendors or ways to improve my characters outside of finding loot chests. All of that would be okay if the gameplay was fluid, but the fight animations all take AGES to finish. They're soooo slooooow. Every enemy attack takes 5-10 seconds to finish. And you have to watch all of them over and over again while you wait for your turn to chip away at the enemy. If you try to finish fights faster with Gimmicks (spells) you run out of AP in one combat and then have to grind through battles on autoattack. And the areas are huuuuuuuuge. Like you think a dungeon is a coherent little dungeon? Nope. These areas are massive, on the level of most games' final dungeons, except they're mostly empty except for the same five assets copypasted over and over again.  And the music is AWFUL! All the music apart from the Title screen music are bland 15 second loops that play over and over and over and over and over and over and over and over...But then there's the worst part: instability. This game is, well, to put it nicely, badly coded. The game gets stuck or crashes right out of the blue. There's no quicksave, so if you don't manually save every minute, you'll be pushed back a long way if you die/crash/get stuck. I've gotten stuck on terrain several times. I've had the game crash when I was trying to read a tutorial during combat. And worst of all, I've gotten into solving a puzzle or fighting some enemies and forgotten to save, and BAM. 15 minutes, 30 minutes of gameplay lost. I came to write this when I'd been solving a puzzle dungeon where I had to split my party of three into one-man groups (yes, all of them had to fight against twin mobs over and over while the mobs healed each other and buffed up their defenses) until finally one of those battles dropped my character to 0hp. In every single battle before that, the enemy has tried to pin me and I've had to mash buttons to get up and continue, but for some reason, this time I just got a game over. And when I loaded my previous save? I was at the start of the dungeon. 30 minutes lost. Why there isn't a quicksave or autosave option, I don't understand. Even loading games is buggy, because when you re-start your game (can't load games inside the game, only from the title menu) and press continue, it loads the topmost savegame from your three slots instead of your most recent one, so then you alt-f4 (no way to quit the game inside the game), re-launch it, then pick load game.And for some reason I can't dash diagonally up and left. I can walk and dash in every other direction. I can walk in that direction, but I can't dash. I desperately want to like this game because it's got so much heart, but the execution is so very bad. In its current state, I can't suggest it to anyone. And this is doubly hurtful because a dev answered my original review and was happy about it, so I feel twice as awful for changing my review and writing something like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: + A wrestling RPG is something I never thought I wanted. It's such a good idea.+ Graphics. Game looks awesome.+ Combat is accessible. Cons:- The thing I was most disappointed about was the story. As it's a wrestling RPG that at first seems to be an homage to (mainly) 80's wrestling I expected a lot of focus on the story. The story is just not interesting at all. It's bland, it's cookie cutter and worst of all it doesn't really feel like a wrestling world after a few hours. - Combat is way too easy and repetitive. There are some interesting parts but they should have been fleshed out. For instance, you can taunt to gain hype, this gives certain boosts... But the taunt is weak and completely unnecessary. Either:+- I was suprised that this takes place in a toy world. Basically you're playing as an action figure. Personally I'm not a fan of this but it's not really a dealbreaker as I could ignore it most of the time.+- Fantasy: There are "human" (toys) characters and there are animal characters. Again, not a big fan as I'd rather have this set in a more or less realistic universe. This is something you can't ignore though as half the characters are animals.I'm giving this a thumbs up as I wouldn't feel good giving it a negative. But honestly I'm disappointed. Some games rely mostly on their story and some on their combat. But this despite this games initial promise it offers neither. The story is negligible and the combat is way too easy and repetitive.

_childDocuments_.review: On one hand, there are numerous deep and clever references that a wrestle-fan would appreciate. A story with characters that is crafted with care that clearly comes from a place of love for the sport. Combat that makes sense in terms of what a Wrestling role-playing game would actually look like. So, a traditional turn based pro wrestling themed RPG that understands the source material AND has Macho Man as a benevolent deity sounds like what I would have used my third genie wish to make. Sadly... it just doesn't come together. Things get repetitive pretty quick, especially with the combat system. Having heard this as feedback, the devs added a 'Skip QTE' option as well as the ability to run around the map faster. I get the idea behind QTEs during battles to help simulate the tug of war that is a real match, but it's just not fun so you can skip it altogether. Doing that breaks things a bit because some moves essentially turbo mash your way to easy fights. The toy box feel is clever since most fans grew up playing with action figures of their favorite wrestler. It's cool to go through each mission collecting all these 'figures' that you can use to battle all the heels in this world. Great in concept, but you rarely get the full stable together so you can pick who you want in your team. Instead, it is constantly switching the roster around depending on what’s happening in the story. Everything is building up to a confrontation/team-up of the two protagonists to form the mega powers, but it just takes too long for that to happen. The game would of benefited greatly from an overworld map and fast travel that arrives sooner than in the last hour of a 40+ hour play through. I struggled to finish this, only doing so based out of love for the concept of what they were going for. My wishlist for a sequel would be to fix the above items and to remove the minigames since they are more frustrating than fun. Even though I can’t recommend this for non fans of the business, I am hoping it still does well enough to make a follow-up that would fine tune the whole experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so awesome that I had to convince my older (much more Pro-Wrestling Savvy) brother that it was real. Wrestle Quest is basically a SNES-era JRPG that's part Super Mario RPG, Part Final Fantasy 6, Part Toy Story, that's Pro-Wrestling at it's core. The devs have also clearly done their homework, so if you're familiar with Pro-Wrestling of all types (or even 80s/90s Pop Culture) you'll appreciate the references. The fact they're also doing constant QoL updates is also excellent Customer Service... Especially the Running Speed issue.My only problem with the game is that I felt it was too easy, even without any of the Insta-Success features activated. Hopefully there's a Super-Boss or two planned for future updates.
