_childDocuments_.review: I was very much having a fun time with this game, as were my viewers. Its a hilarious story about toys that look up to real world wrestlers and in turn, want to be wrestlers. They have their own league and everything, it's great. So, so far everything was going good and then I hit a GAME BREAKING BUG!!! That's right, this game has been out for how long and I hit a game breaking bug. Shortly after completing the Junkyard mission and meeting Slimy the alligator. The game cuts to the second main character, Logan. Seems Logan and his sister have to go meet with the WWA (weather wrestling association, they handle weather control in the Toy Box). Well, we leave home to go get Stag and that's where it all goes wrong. I CAN NOT ENTER ANY PLACE!! I am locked on the world map, I shut the game down, restated it three times, even restarted my whole PC, rebooted the game up, and it's still there. SO, I have put almost 4 hours into this game, only to have my progress completely halted by this glitch. So, until this is  addressed or fixed, I can't not rightfully suggest this game. PLEASE developers take note!!!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: WrestleQuest

_childDocuments_.review: If there were a ton of good modern wrestling games, I don't know that I would recommend WrestleQuest. However, in a world in which there is little to no choice for high quality wrestling related games, I'm having a blast so far. It's a vanilla JRPG in a world that makes very little sense. It has QTEs for every attack which can be quite annoying if you're someone who often checks their phone/other monitor during JRPG attack animations (you'd be surprised how much you do that), and I hope that the developers listen to players and add an option to remove QTEs or at least remove them for all but the most powerful of moves. The story isn't entirely coherent, either. Even though these glaring issues should keep me from enjoying the game they're not. The world makes no sense but it's bright and colorful and fun to be in. The QTEs in combat suck but it's still TURN BASED WRESTLING. If you simply want more wrestling games in your life and think the idea of a turn based wrestler sounds intriguing, I think you'll enjoy this.
_childDocuments_.name: WrestleQuest

_childDocuments_.review: I seriously like this game. Yeah, QTEs suck, but it's the direction they took with this. I wasn't expecting AAA work here, nor should you. If you are an old school wrestling fan, there's enough in here for you to crack a smile at the nostalgia. If you like RPGs, there's enough in here to keep you entertained. Is this Final Fantasy level RPG? No. I like that it's an original concept that gives me just enough of the superhero-esque wrestling that I needed. I'm constantly waiting to see the next wrestling superstar cameo. Lots of little Easter eggs of sayings and likenesses as well. I'm enjoying this. Give it a shot.. If it's not your squared circle, then get that refund. Just enjoy your time as "Muchacho Man" Randy Santos! "¡Oh Si!"
_childDocuments_.name: WrestleQuest

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game that's a great game if you're into wrestling. It has a lot of references, allusions, and great style. The game could use some polish. That's mostly fine though since you can change options, like turning off the qte's after they've stopped being interesting and become tedious, continuing the game, get an airship to bypass a lot of annoying travel (though I think too late in the story), and the devs have put out a quality of life update. It's possible that everything that rubs me the wrong way about the game will be resolved over time. There's more positives than negatives. The story, characters, art, references, style, ect. Wrestlequest is a good jrpg that's an easy recommend to people the game was clearly made for. I'd say to remember this game if that's not you. Work your way through your backlog and come to this game later if this isn't in your strike zone.
_childDocuments_.name: WrestleQuest

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed playing the game! I haven't finished the storyline yet but I will definitely continue playing because i'm interested in how the story pans out in the end.Things I liked:1. The cute 2D art style: I also liked the animations around the environment and I would sometimes stop and watch them play out. 2. The unique timing based mechanic: This is the first time I have encountered it in a turn based game and I liked how it makes the player engaged. 3. The variety of characters: The wrestlers, the NPCs all have a personality to them. It makes the story more interesting.Things that needs some more polishing:1. Interaction with the objects: There was one instance where I was on this junkyard stage and I couldn't break the barrel or open the treasure because I got hit by the fire while breaking one barrel. It was a minor bug that got fixed when I saved the game and reloaded it. I also find it hard to distinguish which objects can be interacted on unless I really moved closer to the edges of the object to see if they will get highlighted. 2. The huge banner that covers the screen: It's this banner that pops out when you completed the quest or you are on the world map. I just find it annoying that I cannot see my character due to it being on display for some seconds. Overall the game is still enjoyable and fun to play even as a non-wrestling fan. I recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: WrestleQuest

_childDocuments_.review: My experience with this game was really a Love/Hate relationship. I wish I was able to give this a "maybe"/mix recommendation, but because STEAM doesn't allow that option I'm forced to choose Not Recommend based on my reasonings below. Again this is from my experience.Let's start with the GOOD, because there is a lot of good to this game. - pixel graphics - music - wrestling lore {homework well done}- wrestling summons and managers - homage to wrestlers- easy gameplayHere what I found to be bad- repetitive battles- ridiculous mini games/battles {the battleship segment almost made me quit this}- constant party switching - NO ITEM SHARING BETWEEN PARTIES- the story is very "meh" for me- the gameplay?- how wide/sluggish the wrestlers are when moving in certain areas- open world?Let me elaborate on the questionable gameplay and open world. I understand the battle system is inspired by Paper Mario and Legend of the Dragoon, but why not make this an Action RPG as opposed to a turned based RPG? I also didn't understand how some enemies you HAD to pin, were other enemies you just had to beat {although I do appreciate the KO and submission options}. After a while the gameplay got tedious with the quick time actions. However it is simple gameplay for new comers to the genre. Now I didn't finish this game, because I WASN'T ABLE to finish this due to a section in the Tower with: Barbre, Rad Cod, and Vendetta. Apparently I am required to have a Double Table Spot Token in order to proceed a path that is blocked. Well much earlier in the game when I had Brink and Stag Logan I actually visited the Tower and looted the majority of the blue treasure chests. So I didn't realize until that point in the game that Brink Logan has the Double Table Spot Token I needed to continue. WHY IS THAT POSSIBLE!? WHY IS ITEM SHARING NOT A THING!? WHY DO YOU SWITCH PARTIES SO OFTEN!? WHY AM I ABLE TO EXPLORE AREAS IN THE GAME THAT AREN'T RESTRICTED!? There are sections in the game the wrestlers will state "I'm not supposed to be here", and are unable to proceed. Why wasn't the Tower section one of them!? After 32 hours logged into this game I cannot complete it because something so ridiculous that the developers could have prevented. My experience with this game is ruined because of that. How was I supposed to know that I shouldn't explore in an area I had access too? That's what open world is! That's what most RPGs allow you to do! WTF!?!?Obviously I'm frustrated, but I am much more disappointed because I cannot get the time back on this game. I'm not even sure if I want to revisit this. So for anyone reading do not make the same mistake that I did. Just go where you are supposed to go, and enjoy your railroad experience to WrestleQuest. Unlike me who crashed...

_childDocuments_.review: Great graphics, cool story line. _REALLY_ good combat system.Works with PS5 and Xbox controllers.Unfortunately it's hampered by bugs such as :  Sudden closes, unable to break objects or open chests after being hit by environmental dmg, unable to speak with NPC, going "out of bounds" on maps, unable to trigger certain events. _childDocuments_.review: Crashed twice within 7 minutes, never a good start. I went in to this trying not to spoil things at first, only having seen one trailer video, but from the first occurrence of something in the game, I thought I better go and look it up quickly... And unfortunately, my worst fears are realised. The game absolutely destroys the mix of two of my favourite things of all time (RPGs and Wrestling), by making 90% of the combat about timing button presses. This is fine in one type of video game, and that's anything musical. And if you're a fan of that, fair enough. But I'm not, and my disappointment is massive, because it may have been one of the worst design decisions that could have been made. All I can do instead is watch someone else play this on Youtube or Twitch or something, so maybe at least I can experience what seems like a very cool aesthetic, fun story, decentish audio etc, without having to deal with the awfulness of timed button pressing 20 times a battle, and very little other gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: There's bugs, but it's also a small dev and a recent release. Like, there's a puzzle near the end of the game where you gotta push statues onto a conveyor belt, but also the conveyor belts move faster to thwart their fix to running speed being too slow. I managed to solve that one through clever use of the reset button, though.There's also lots of backtracking mid-game that I feel shouldn't happen, especially if you gotta walk through an area full of enemies each time. Once in a video I made I had a mission critical item just...not work until I loaded the save.But it made me laugh in several parts. The Hype bar and conditional boss battles is a nice change to the RPG formula. Factual information about many big wrestlers, and not just the WWF ones we all heard about. They really showed they know and love what they're talking about.Really most of the flubs are just game maker things, and I kinda wish the game got more attention after it's rocky start in August. _childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a game that is going to make you rethink what a modern RPG is, you will walk away disappointed. If you are looking for a solid game that will 100% make you feel like a kid again though, look no further.This game IS however a love letter to all things 80s and 90s, from the wrestler cameos to the Mario RPG style combat, pop culture toy nods and beyond and it does it pretty well. The only things that would make this game better is if it handed me a box of cereal with a prize in it and some bagel bites....or maybe just a few less QTE's.Combat in the game is standard turn based RPG flavor, but it's some of the absolutely hilarious animations for your gimmick skills that really sell it. The graphics are solid and fit nicely with the retro vibe of the whole game. Story can be kind of goofy at times but considering the characters are toys it 100% fits the vibe of this might just be a storyline any 80s child would've made up in their head sitting in the living room with a pile of action figures on a Saturday morning waiting for WWF to come on after a morning filled with cartoons.Overall I'm giving this game a 8.5/10 so far with special emphasis on the fact that "Spice so Nice" has become a catchphrase for literally every dumb thing said on my streams the past few days.

_childDocuments_.review: Wrestle Quest is an absolute delight for both fans of classic CRPGs and pixel art. This game takes the best elements of both genres and fuses them into seamless and incredibly enjoyable experience that had me hooked from the moment I started playing.The first thing that struck me about Wrestle Quest was its stunning pixel art. The attention to detail in every character sprite, environment, and animation is simply outstanding. It's evident that the developers poured their heart and soul into creating a visually appealing world that feels both nostalgic and fresh at the same time. The retro-inspired aesthetics transported me back to the golden age of gaming while still offering a modern twist.Gameplay-wise, Wrestle Quest truly shines. The blend of turn-based combat and traditional CRPG mechanics is executed flawlessly. Building and customizing your team of wrestling heroes is a joy, with a diverse roster of characters to choose from, each with their own unique abilities and personalities. The tactical depth of the combat system kept me engaged throughout, and the learning curve was just right – challenging but not overly punishing.The story in Wrestle Quest is surprisingly compelling. It's a humorous and imaginative tale that weaves a wrestling-themed narrative into the CRPG structure seamlessly. The quirky characters and their interactions had me chuckling more than once, and the dialogue choices added a layer of immersion that drew me deeper into the game world.One of the standout features of Wrestle Quest is the sheer amount of content it offers. The game is packed with side quests, hidden treasures, and a variety of challenges that kept me exploring. This is a game that truly rewards curiosity and exploration, and I found myself constantly stumbling upon delightful surprises.The soundtrack deserves a special mention as well. The catchy tunes perfectly complement the game's atmosphere, adding an extra layer of nostalgia and charm.In conclusion, Wrestle Quest is a fantastic addition to the world of CRPGs and a testament to the enduring appeal of pixel art. It successfully captures the essence of classic RPGs while offering a fresh and entertaining take on the genre. Whether you're a long-time fan of CRPGs or simply appreciate well-crafted pixel art, Wrestle Quest is an absolute must-play. It's a delightful journey filled with humor, strategy, and unforgettable moments that will keep you coming back for more. Don't miss out on this gem of a game!
_childDocuments_.name: WrestleQuest

_childDocuments_.review: The problem with this game is that it's so close to amazing that it makes the shortcomings a bit glaring.  The biggest I think is the story itself somewhat overstays its welcome.  The swerves, betrayals and reunions are appropriate for the subject matter, but at some point it just felt like it was padding and not really moving the story along.Now for some decisions that were frustrating.  One I hit last night is what made me decide to write.  There's a swap in location right after a cut scene followed by a must win to continue battle and no chance to save after the cut scene.  In this day and age, that's super annoying especially when one of the opponents in the battle has an instant KO attack.  There are several segments when various team members are separated (by story, not the split party function) and if it doesn't feature one of the main characters, you're often completely lacking any money and if you hadn't thought to heal before the separation, it could be a bad situation.  in my case, ended up replaying fortunately no more than about 15 minutes to fix things before the split.  It could have been worse if I didn't save as often as I do.  I also would like some indication when taking on a quest how long it would be expected to take.  Not a huge deal, but some things turned out to be way bigger deals than I expected while others I expected to be an ordeal were nothing of note.The biggest control issue was as an analog controller user, the fragile ground, circling cows and moving sidewalks are frustrating using the analog.  A couple I switch to keyboard arrow keys.It's a good game, it could be great.

_childDocuments_.review: (INITIAL REVIEW WILL UPDATE ONCE I FINISH THE GAME)To start things off, WrestleQuest is an homage not only to classic retro JRPG enthusiasts but also to wrestling enthusiasts as well. The developers really knew what they were doing when they mixed the wrestling and JRPG mechanics into this game. Specifically the turn-based charm that classic JRPG games had added by the high-flying, cinematic, hype-inducing and grandeur wrestling moves we all loved as kids back then when we watched WWE which they nailed really well and integrated well into the combat system of the game.Story-wise (Which is the bread and butter of JRPGs), I can tell that im only into the introductory stage of the narrative (Clocking about 7 hours in) and I can already tell that things will get much more interesting later on (fingers-crossed it does not bite me back after finishing the game). The story focuses on two main protagonists one who is a dream-filled, passion-induced, Randy Santos, Muchacho Man, loves to bring spice and authenticity into it's gimmick and the other is Brink Logan, the do-it all family man even at the cost of his own career. This being said, it is obvious that they are 2 sides of the same coin and will intersect into the later to mid part of the story. Reinforcing them are various side-characters with fleshed out attitudes and personality which makes the player think that they are not merely background characters that follow the main protagonists during their quest. _childDocuments_.review: Title: A Nostalgic Journey into Wrestling with WrestleQuestRating: ★★★★☆ (4/5)If you're looking for a nostalgic throwback to the days of 32-bit gaming, WrestleQuest on Steam might be just what you need. This game offers a unique blend of turn-based gameplay, an engaging storyline, and a laid-back atmosphere that's perfect for unwinding.Graphics-wise, WrestleQuest provides an old-school charm with its 32-bit aesthetics. While not groundbreaking, the visuals capture the essence of retro gaming, which adds to its overall appeal. The pixel art and character designs are reminiscent of classic titles, invoking a sense of nostalgia for those who grew up with these games.The story in WrestleQuest is both a strength and a weakness. On one hand, it adds depth to the game and immerses you in the wrestling world. On the other, the need to press "skip story" multiple times can be slightly frustrating, especially if you're more interested in the gameplay. However, it's worth noting that the story itself is well-crafted and enjoyable, even if it occasionally feels a bit excessive.Gameplay revolves around turn-based wrestling, where strategy is key. You'll find yourself pondering your moves, and the level of challenge is just right for a relaxing gaming experience. If you're looking for more excitement, an increased difficulty option would be a welcome addition to cater to a broader audience.WrestleQuest's overall charm lies in its ability to take you on a journey back to a simpler era of gaming. It's a title that offers a chill and relaxed atmosphere, making it an excellent choice for unwinding and passing the time. If you have fond memories of classic 32-bit games and appreciate turn-based gameplay with a wrestling twist, WrestleQuest is a game that's sure to hit the right notes. So, if you're in the mood for a laid-back gaming experience, give WrestleQuest a shot and step into the wrestling ring for a dose of nostalgia.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT 8/23/23Developer replied to my review and they had this to say regarding the Licensing, and the pricing:"About the wrestlers featured, have no fear! Everyone that is featured in the game is licensed. Going through the due diligence with them and figuring out who wasn't blocked for their likeness rights was one of the wildest parts of development. But, since the game is one big love letter to these wrestlers, we were extra sure we were clear before we could put them on the pedestal (statue) they deserve."This makes me happier than it needs to, but it makes me happy, I want them boys to get paid, and I'm glad they did their due diligence! "Regarding the game's pricing, we based it partially on how much total content we offer. The main story clocks in at 40 hours, and there is plenty more to do with all the side content. Overall it is around a 50-60 hour game, and felt the price was appropriate for how long it can keep players slamming. I'm still glad you took a chance with our game and gave it a shot to entertain you." This is a canned response, and I get it, but the reasoning doesn't work for me. This game is a $25 game, I know the distinction is going to vary by person, but to ME, you're still asking too much, and I still recommend grabbing it on sale. It will definitely be on sale, like FOR sure.ORIGINAL REVIEW!This is pretty fun, right away there's a bunch of stuff that's warm and comfortable. The OST is good, they did a good job on it and it reminds me of Hotline Miami almost.  The menus and the color choices in general are pleasing to the eye and good. So right away before even playing i was like oh sh*t!- Dope music- I like the menu's right awayGameplay- 1. I was a little disappointed that there's no Character creator, and you kind of jump around through a whole bunch of character stories, so it's hard to get attached because right away, BAM you're off in another thing? But like you don't play RPGs and go "f*ck, i couldn't make my own guy, i have to be link" or whatever2.Characters are over the top and fun, the allusions to real life stuff are pretty fun as well. Obviously it's a love letter to the 80s.3. game design choices remind me of Mario RPG for the Super Nintendo, like REALLY hard. It has the same kind of QTE mechanic, only it's more forgiving, and it has an overworld and "levels" the same kind of way.  4. The buttons are decent, they thought of things like managers having moves, it's f*ckin cool man!I haven't gotten very far yet, but I'm having a good time. I do think the game is a perfect like $24.99 sort of title, and the devs charging $30 for it might be a little arrogant, especially given all the terrible reviews they're getting? I don't think the reviews are fair per se, and I like the game so "game journelism" can definitely f*ck off, but it feels a tad overpriced. Finally there's a ethical question I don't know the answer to- did these famous people sign off on this? Some of them are dead, did their estates sign off on this? My main worry here, is that like is DDP getting paid for this? He's in it? And if not, that's really not cool, and grounds for a No review from me, but for now, since i'm not sure, and I'm having fun, it's a yes. Get it on sale if you can, it's good, but not worth $30. Something tells me it will be on heavy sale rotation by Xmas, too.

_childDocuments_.review: WrestleQuest: A Slam That Misses or Connects?WrestleQuest throws together two seemingly odd genres: wrestling and RPGs. Does it deliver a championship match, or end up disqualified?  This review will dive into the ring to find out.Body Slam StoryWrestleQuest's narrative is a bit of a mixed bag. On one hand, it boasts a unique premise and a love letter's worth of wrestling references. You'll encounter quirky characters and stories that range from hilarious to heartfelt.  On the other hand, the juggling of multiple storylines can feel scattered, and the humor might miss sometimes.Sharpshooter GameplayThe core gameplay is a turn-based RPG battle system with a wrestling twist.  There's a fun "hype" meter that builds momentum for powerful moves, and  quick-time events add a layer of interactivity to matches.  However, some repetitive battles and a lack of fast-forward options can slow things down.Visually StunningWrestleQuest shines in the presentation department.  The vibrant, comic book-style art and the over-the-top animations bring the wrestling world to life.Worth the Entrance Fee?WrestleQuest offers a unique experience for RPG and wrestling fans alike.  While the story and pacing have some shortcomings, the core gameplay and presentation are solid. If you're looking for a quirky homage to wrestling with RPG flair, WrestleQuest might be your next champion.  But for those expecting a knockout narrative or deep RPG mechanics, be prepared for a few pinfalls.Final Verdict:WrestleQuest delivers a fun and flashy experience, but uneven storytelling and repetitive battles hold it back from a perfect ten count.

_childDocuments_.review: It may not look like the RPGs of today, but it's good and it knows it's good.  But only good, I think.I like most of what the game offers. The pixel art is fantastic, and the wrestling heroes are well-represented alongside some of their lore and stories. There are plenty of cross-references to other RPGs and video games.  The combat feels a lot like Super Mario RPG and has plenty of accessibility options if timing-based gameplay isn't really your thing.  The soundtrack is good, but if you've been spoiled with your indie game choices as far as OSTs go lately (Tunic, Celeste, Chicory, heck even Holocure), it's not quite up to those levels. I've gotten through most of the game without really using the tag or triple-tag abilities, to say nothing of the summons.  They're kind of hidden away on the menu and I'm pretty overpowered without them.  When you DO use them though, they look fantastic!But the rough spots are really, REALLY rough. There's no running in wrestling, so there is no running from combat in this game. You can't take a countout loss, so if you end up in battle, you've gotta win it. This would be less of a problem if many fights didn't require the pinfall mechanic. This would be less of a problem if there was a soft-reset to try stealthing around an enemy again. If you want to start over a special fight to try for the optional dramatic moments again, you have to Alt-F4. You are often punished for hitting your promos and building up your hype meter before a fight by immediately being asked to let your opponent generate hype.Because of this, backtracking or repeating an area for any reason is absolutely agonizing. There is no quick travel, not even "Chrono Cross" style quick-travel where you can just walk *over* somethign on the world map if you've cleared it before. Doing a sidequest with a backtrack often means being stuck in a handful of meaningless battles with minimum XP reward and drops you outleveled hours ago. Brutal.This would all suck a little bit less if you were a little more free to explore and rewarded for doing so, but the game is fairly linear.  This is not a bad thing, not every game has to be open-world like Tears of the Kingdom, but if you're the check-every-nook-and-cranny type of gamer, you're not going to find a lot of crumbs to keep you going here. Even the hidden chests are not well-hidden and outside of one drop that is definitely overpowered by ACCIDENT, you don't really need the hidden items.If you're both a wrestling an an RPG fan, there's a lot to like here, but it's not as polished as other RPGs so don't come in expecting "EarthBound/Undertale/<insert your favorite indie RPG here> in Wrestling Tights." The side content is fun but it's up to you how much backtracking you want to suffer through to see it all.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a unique game experience. Never in my years would I thought I'd see a Wrestling + JRPG mashup but here we are. Wrestle Quest has it's own unique charm. The artstyle and sound design are it's strong points. I love the almost uncanny looking portraits and the VFX work is superb for a pixel art game.Haven't experienced much of the story so far, but it seems promising. _childDocuments_.review: This game is so much fun! I had high hopes, but became a little worried about some of the early reviews. Turns out, I vehemently disagreed with almost all of the criticisms that were repeatedly popping up. The developers have also done a very prompt job of fixing the issues that those players had in the first place.There is clearly a lot of care that went into this, given the variety of moves, all with correct wrestling terminology. It fits with the traditional grand scale of a JRPG, with the campiness of professional wrestling. The writing style is very apt for this incredibly specific subgenre, as is the aesthetic of the world you're in.A few small nits that I have to pick:-I wish you could use a licensed wrestlers move earlier into the game. It wasn't until 2-3 hours in until I could use the ability of real-life wrestlers. Given the era of people playing games for an hour or two before they decide if they want to return it, getting them hooked by using the advertised wrestlers would keep people engaged early on.-Double team moves seem to be excessively expensive when they do only a little more damage than a solo special move, which is half the energy cost. Overall, I'm incredibly happy this game is as fun as I had hoped it would be. I'm excited to keep playing and see what the rest of the story has to offer!

_childDocuments_.review: Not Enough of What Makes WrestleQuest SpecialThis game is a thumbs down from me, but a reluctant one.  I make my reasoning as succinct as I can below, but to be clear, it's still being updated by their development team and I'd like to give it another shot down the line.To be clear, I like the idea of the game.  As someone who enjoys indie gaming and classic wrestling, this game has a lot going for it: childhood characters, an interesting button prompt battle system akin to the days of Super Mario RPG, and lots of characters to add to your stable.  The idea of tag team moves is also fun -- as you unlock them, you get to see your characters interact in fun and different ways.I rather enjoy the idea of finding customizable entrance themes.  However, experiencing some of what makes this game special is too much repetition in between.  I like the idea of "dramatic events," meaning you have to work with your opponent to fulfill certain objectives, as actual wrestlers do.  But, those moments are literally hours apart between themselves.  In between the dramatic events, you're you're wandering in an empty, non-interactable world map filled with imaginative toybox decor -- that you can't do anything with.  You're fighting the same enemies who pretty much all do the same thing. Some of the maps seem like they had plenty of attention to detail, while others feel like afterthoughts.  Exploration in many cases goes unrewarded, which is a bummer for an RPG of this type.After 10 hours of repetition, I felt like it wasn't worth continuing in this state.  While the game itself plays fine, I'd like to see a bit more fleshed out.  Maybe with a bit more of the customization that makes wrestling games special.  And a bit less of Toybox Jimmy telling me about HOW WE DO IT IN BOXWOOD.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to preface by saying that I absolutely love turn-based RPGs and wrestling, and it's clear that the devs do too. I was unimaginably excited for Wrestlequest, and while there is a clear passion for both of these pinnacles of human art in this game, they just don't combine together here in a way that is enjoyable.I really wanted to love WQ, but the combat struggles to keep my attention and even though I love wrestling, I feel very little drive to move forward. I dunno it feels weird, like they took the simplest parts of old school RPGs and made it gorgeous, but it lacks something inherent in the creativity of games created in those formative years. When Super Mario RPG was new, the QTEs were original and they felt *good*. Nowadays we are numb to them, and they quickly become a chore if they aren't implemented thoughtfully. Some games have you time a button press along with a hit or a block right at the moment of impact, and this can be fun because then the press feels like it's relevant to the move-- it creates the sensation of you executing the action. But when the press is just trying to hit a button before a timer runs out, you lose that. And being forced to do it frequently feels like a task.There are other omissions that hurt the experience as well; character progression for example. You don't choose what to learn, and there are no trees or points besides basic XP. You can't even see what abilities your character will learn or at what levels. I understand that this is out of a desire to make it feel old-school, but this is a staple nowadays because it makes grinding for XP fun, and makes it feel like you're customizing your party members. You also cannot make a character even though it's an RPG, about wrestling, where you play as toys. The menus and icons all have a modern pop aesthetic instead of matching the pixel art style of the rest of the game. There is no map.So while WQ might have quite a few hours of gameplay, it feels very light, and combined with the menus and map, I actually get casual mobile game vibes from it.And ya wanna know somethin' BROTHER? If this was like 15 bucks I'd probably not write this review. But it's 30 dollars and nowadays that demands more than QTEs covered in beautiful wrestling pixel art, which is what this game is at its core. I may revisit WQ someday because the devs clearly love this game and are proud of it, and I know it is difficult to make a game, so I don't want to be disrespectful. It's also clear that they're working on ways to improve it, which is awesome. In addition, I'm only about 90 minutes in because 2 hours is the cutoff for a refund, so there might be things that change or that I've missed and the devs can correct me if that's the case. But right now WQ is unable to command my attention, although I definitely hope that changes someday.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard one, because I don't think this is a bad game, but I do think it needs work.  I recently saw there was an update  announcement and it seems the developers are really working on the game but in it's current state, I just couldn't find myself enjoying the game at the stage I was at.So what the game does well.  I really like the world and the graphics.  It's a very fun pixel world, there's a lot of neat vibrant backgrounds and scenes.  I like that it's set in a toy world and that ties everything up well.  Honestly, I was enjoying all of this.  I grew up with professional wrestling. I never really followed it super well, but I recognize a lot of the big names and it's really entertaining how it's all integrated.  Honestly, I'm all for the world that the game exists in.The combat system that is pretty reminiscent to super mario RPG and was overall fun.  You have a basic attack where you can hit an input to do added damage.  You also have specials that often have inputs related to them that can boost the damage or chance of special effects.  I also liked the system of tag team attacks.  Certain enemy types after you reduce their HP, you also have to pin them to finish them off (wrestling trope).   I didn't mind the pin system, but I think it felt more appropriate for boss type battles than for enemies in random encounters.  So with that said, I will talk about what I didn't like and why I ultimately had to stop playing at the moment.  During one segment you go to an area called Camp Diet.  Camp Diet didn't have an actual rest area (or area to pay to recovery HP/SP).  There was an item shop, but health recovery items are expensive and I'd honestly lose money in the process to get enough to recovery myself fully.  At one point, I tried to avoid combat and traverse through two whole areas to return to the previous zone just to heal up before I continued.  And that amount of backtracking just to recovery was not fun.  The game will refill your HP/SP when you level up, but I don't want to rely on that to be able to top off my team before I head into another area.  The other difficult point of this particular area ( maybe other later areas as well, as yet to be determined) is we got a new party member, and they started at level 1.  So they were several levels lower than my team.  And one segment not far in requires you to split your team up into 3 and this low level character is on his own unless you leveled him up some by grinding in a previous area.  In this section, I ended up having the low level character often get knocked out and would have to restart.  At one point the autosave had them going into another fight very soon after, and my last save was quite a while before that.  I don't think it would be as much an issue if you could leave these areas from the entrance.  But it seems like once the group is split up, you are locked int that instance.  My only other issue was during boss battles, if you are trying to follow the script for the bonus items, I had one fight where I had to just taunt for like 10 minutes straight because they were never doing enough damage to knock out one of my characters out right.  Like, I get the nostalgia and the nod to wrestling, but in practice it can be unfulfilling.  As I said, the next update may help with some of these issues, but I just feel there are a lot of qualify of life features that need to be implemented.

_childDocuments_.review: WrestleQuest is a Wrestling JRPG based on the old 80s wrestlers. I really wish Steam had a So-So in-between for reviews, cause I don't think it's a bad game, it just over stays it's welcome. The over-arcing story line isn't that special; little guys vs. the big bad corpo. What is cool, is the story (at first) is splits into two different perspectives: the Fanatic Fan who became a wrestler, and the One Born into the Legacy. You were given a clear goal to get to the big match and win it. And this is where the game losses me, I finish the goal start from the beginning of the game 24 hours later thinking it was done, only  to be told there's about 9 more hours left of the story. Even before this, when they started having you play as the sidekicks as the main characters in their own story 14 hours in, the characters I didn't even bother to level up cause their side characters that I didn't think would show back up. So the sidekicks side was hard cause of being underleveled, and some of the boss fights for the main characters were hard cause they were overleveled and had a hard time being forced to LOSE during matches. I really wanted to finish the game, but after winning the big match stated from the beginning, it couldn't hold my interest anymore. Also it very telling when you get a 3.6% rare achievement for completing a story boss. I think the game at the very least should have been 14 to maybe 20 hours long, not 35+. I liked recommend the first 12 hours of the game....

_childDocuments_.review: After a long period of watching streams, I finally got my hands on Wrestlequest, and I can confidently say that it's simply amazing. I love how the developers skillfully merged the mechanics of classic JRPGs with the world of professional wrestling. If you're a fan of retro aesthetics, Wrestlequest is definitely up your alley.From the very first moments of the game, the sense of immersion in this world becomes increasingly vivid. The intriguing storyline and dialogues, crafted with a deep understanding of the subject matter, add extra depth to the game.Visually, the game is also quite appealing. I spent the first 15 minutes just admiring the details in the locations that the developers meticulously created.The soundtrack is one of Wrestlequest's strong suits. It greatly contributes to the immersion and perfectly captures the atmosphere of each location.The battles in the game are engaging and captivating. Any initial skepticism about how the turn-based combat fits with wrestling quickly dissipates, and you discover how well they complement each other. The combat system is thoroughly developed, and you eagerly anticipate leveling up to unlock new abilities.In the end, Wrestlequest is definitely a game where I'm more than willing to invest 50+ hours of my life.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun but NOT FINISHED. The first 30 hours were a blast, and that's why I hit recommend; 30 hours is definite value. That said, after that point it becomes very clear that the game is simply not where it needs to be, and if it is, that's a major fault to the developer. Characters that you get later on are simply not optimized for the enemies, the minigames that help pad out the length become tedious, and there's no sense in several fights the game gives you. There's a section near the end which is interesting but superfluous, and by this point in the game, I honestly just wanted it to be done. The game is basically ending starting at the 30 hour mark and going for 20 more hours.That said, the JRPG + QTE thing is actually fun, though I've seen lots of griping about it. I think more could be done with it; maybe the time on combat QTEs could be lengthened just a hair, and then a Hard Mode could be added where you are rated on how fast you get the QTE; if that's how it works now, it's not apparent. The premise is not my favorite but it does provide for interesting levels and enemies. There's definite creativity in the whole idea of playing with toys and how different types of figures get roped in to whatever your playing, so Stone Cold has to fight a lego man, stuff like that.Fun game but it totally falls apart near the end. It may get some patches etc. to clean that stuff up.EDIT: I still have not finished but I had to change my review to Not Recommended. This game refuses to end, it has been in ending mode for 20+ hours, and in that time it has become one of the worst things I have ever played.  It is so tedious, the story refuses to end, it keeps giving you mandatory fights with your worst characters, this sucks so much. I still stand by my appraisal in that if you are just playing for the first 30 hours it's fun, but once Brink starts doing heel stuff, you should stop playing. Everything after that is an absolute chore. No matter how I felt about the opening I can't recommend a game like this.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a very busy person, so I know only 30 minutes of a game isn't enough to state it's good or bad, but I grew up with a lot of wrestle mania games, and while the graphic aesthetics of this game piqued my interest, I couldn't stand the slow, repetitive and janky game play. For me, the frame rate was not great, and the over world was off putting because the world was so large and you were so itty bitty. While the beautiful pixel graphics and music were excellent, the game play was tedious. I have a friend who is REALLY into wrestling and even she was turned off by this game, mainly because it is turn-based and not free movement. That is not to suggest that the game play was so bad that it was not salvageable. The game's difficulties for me was that while moving about and interacting with cut scenes/dialogue, the game would stall out and you would have to wait a few moments for the game to allow controller input to actually move, which killed the pacing. I assumed it wouldn't be a turn-based wrestling game, which wasn't even that interesting. The same monotonous conflicts played out over and over with little variation. I would have much loved the opportunity to simply play a wrestling game with complete control.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Old-school wrestling nostalgia is amazing. Great theme if you are or were a wrestling fan back in the day- Story is over the top - which is perfect for old school wrestling.- Action figure jokes are great- Soundtrack is incredible.- Variety of combat moves is goodCons:- Combat. There's no indicators or numbers to calculate damage. Fights feel like combining abilities until you win a fight. While that is fun, and dealing damage is fun. It should be basic game information.-Its not explained anywhere outside of Sargeant Slaughter's ability what enemies are weak to what. That should also be basic game information. Put it in the charater's ability menu. Even if its a "X power move" and the damage ranges are hidden. That's the solution pokemon uses, and that's fine.- Combat is too easy. I'm not sure whether this is just my experience w/ games in the genre or whether the combat is genuinely too easy. I think that a higher difficulty mode would be good - if the above issues with combat clarity were fixed. Enemy abilities aren't always clear on what they can do. I'm not sure if this is in the beastiary or not. Edit: No no it is not.- Voice Acting is just catch phrases as opposed to real V/O. You could have no audio on characters speaking and it would be an improvement.- Minimap. The minimap is atrocious. You have to interact with billboards (that don't tell you where you are on them) in order to see an overview of an area. However, this does not update the minimap (it should). Alternatively, just update your map when you go to new places and remove Fog of War or something. Having indicators to where you go next is nice though. Areas where this would be particularly good are the jungle biomes and military biomes where the map segments are very similar - and it is easy to get lost. This is not fun when you're hunting for collectibles.- Item system is quite basic. Stat boosts and elemental effects. Again, when its not apparent what elemental effects are good against what - its sort of difficult to determine why you would pick one over another.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. It's a good feel from the 90s in both the look and content. It feels like a classic turnbased RPG based on Wrestling from that time era. Story is absolutely amazing.For this next section, please, don't think I hated the game, as I'm going to rip into it a little, but I did want to list a couple of things I think could have been better. As much as I love the game, though, there's some really big flaws that I saw.The controls are VERY janky at times. Most of the time this is fine, but there were a few missions where I had to activate switches, and while they glowed, I could not activate them. I absolutely LOATHed a couple of the movement puzzles. While simple looking, with the controls the way they were, they were awful and almost made me rage quit. This was the worst of if for me.I write this next bit hesitantly as I just hit end game, and a few of my characters are lower leveled, so that could be the issue. I really feel like the characters are very unbalanced. In most of these games, everyone has their favorites of course. I've found some of them just unusable due to how worthless they are. I'm hoping that they're just undergeared/underleveled, but some of them I've been struggling to find gear for a while, but then I have another character that can go through and clear everything by themselves.There is no map. There is a compass that shows directions, but that's it. Whether you're in an area or the overworld, there's nothing other than a little compass that shows you stores, hospitals, and SOME quest. I've been looking into trying to find a map or guide or something to help with any missables, and there haven't been any finished. A map would have made it a lot easier with finding things or even getting your bearings sometimes.The way it saves is a little confusing as well. When you load, sometimes it loads your save. Sometimes it goes back a couple of saves (even if you've saved over them somehow), and you have to go back to the main menu and load the save you needed.All that being said, I would love to see a lot more fixes and updates with content. It sounded like they got support from a couple of the wrestlers they have featured in the game, and it shows. Even though I have my issues, I REALLY am enjoying this game.

_childDocuments_.review: That sounds like an exciting and unique combination of pro wrestling and RPG fantasy! WrestleQuest appears to offer a creative blend of two popular genres, providing players with the opportunity to experience the thrill of professional wrestling while incorporating elements of classic role-playing games.The incorporation of iconic wrestling personalities like "Macho Man" Randy Savage adds a nostalgic touch and could enhance the overall appeal for fans of the sport. The comparison to Pokemon and Final Fantasy suggests a captivating gameplay experience with strategic elements, character development, and perhaps even a storyline that unfolds as players progress.The pixel-powered adventure style adds a classic and visually appealing aspect to the game. It's always interesting when games draw inspiration from multiple genres, as it can lead to a fresh and engaging gaming experience.If you enjoy both pro wrestling and RPGs, it seems like WrestleQuest has the potential to deliver a unique and entertaining gaming experience. Exploring the world of wrestling while navigating through a fantasy RPG setting could offer a novel and enjoyable adventure for players.Rating: ★★★★☆ (4/5)
_childDocuments_.name: WrestleQuest

_childDocuments_.review: Wrestling games have always been a niche in the gaming world, primarily appealing to dedicated fans of the sport. However, WrestleQuest manages to break that barrier, captivating even non-wrestling fans like me with its breathtaking graphics and captivating storyline.Graphics (5/5):From the moment you launch WrestleQuest, you'll be spellbound by its stunning visuals. The character models are incredibly detailed, showcasing the painstaking effort put into their design. The animations are smooth and realistic, enhancing the overall experience. The arenas are a sight to behold, and the crowd reactions are so convincing that you can't help but feel like you're part of a real wrestling event. Even if you've never been interested in wrestling before, the visual splendor of this game will leave you in awe.Gameplay (4/5):WrestleQuest manages to strike a balance between accessibility and depth, making it easy for newcomers to get the hang of the gameplay. The controls are intuitive, and you don't need to be well-versed in wrestling moves to execute them. Performing signature moves and executing high-flying stunts feels incredibly satisfying. The pacing of the matches keeps you engaged, and you never feel like the bouts are dragging on.Storyline (5/5):Even if you have no prior interest in wrestling, the game's narrative will draw you in. You'll find yourself genuinely invested in the struggles and triumphs of your in-game character. The game masterfully blends drama, humor, and action, keeping you hooked throughout your journey.Variety (4/5):The game boasts a diverse roster of wrestlers, each with their own unique personalities and fighting styles. The different match types and venues inject variety into the gameplay, and the game's progression system provides motivation to unlock new content.In summary, this is a game that beckons not just wrestling enthusiasts, but also those who have never considered themselves fans of the sport. Its remarkable graphics, engaging storyline, and approachable gameplay make it a hidden gem for wrestling novices.

_childDocuments_.review: From the moment you dive into this game, you'll be hit with a wave of nostalgia as Randy Savage's larger-than-life persona takes center stage. The developers have paid the utmost attention to detail, capturing the essence of Randy's charisma, flamboyance, and in-ring prowess. It's almost as if the Macho Man himself has been resurrected in digital form, ready to step back into the squared circle.But it's not just about reliving the glory days of wrestling; this game has a modern plot and characters that are as captivating as they are relatable. The storyline weaves a web of drama, suspense, and emotion that keeps you invested from start to finish. You'll find yourself emotionally connected to the characters, cheering them on as they battle their way through the world of professional wrestling.The gameplay is a delightful fusion of retro charm and modern mechanics. The turn-based RPG elements are seamlessly integrated with the wrestling action, offering a unique and engaging experience. Every grapple, every suplex, and every finishing move feels authentic and satisfying, just like the classics we grew up watching.Although here are the things I wish can be improved:- Mini-maps should have outlines or guidelines.- I am using an Xbox controller, and when presented with choices (hype type) that I need to choose, it automatically moves through all the choices. Is it really a part of the system? It makes it hard to choose and read.- Hopping between Randy's storyline and the Logan brothers' storyline is sometimes a bit confusing. I was engaged in Randy's storyline, and the momentum kind of got broken when I switched to the Logan Brothers. Can dramatic moments not be skipped? Please add an option to skip.Nevertheless, WrestleQuest is definitely a masterpiece that is truly worth the penny.
_childDocuments_.name: WrestleQuest

_childDocuments_.review: Hidden behind the silly premise of wrestling toys is a charming story about *several* heroes' journeys. Some characters discover themselves, others rediscover themselves, and others confront their dreams and their failures. The title is very apt: this is very much a quest.The wrestling mechanics are *really* good, too. There's some limited button mashing to keep old-fashioned beat'em up fans like yours truly entertained but not too much to turn this into a brawl. Actually, most of the fight is focused on tactics and balancing resources. It requires brains more than quick fingers.And it totally captures the essence of the wrestling world. The quests, the dialogs, the story are infused with blitzy, showmanship-focused, over-the-top flashiness, and the ever-present feeling that sometimes you just gotta act the part. It's full of tropes but they're not tired.The story does feel a little unwieldy at times, maybe because there's so much *actual* wrestling mechanics to it that some of it feels off when it's applied to, you know, wrestling plush toys and the like. But I think I just need to play it some more :-D. It also takes some time to work out the right way to channel things like public hype, so the game feels a little unfair at first. But it's really just a matter of learning to play it right, it's otherwise a great game altogether!

The crowd roars, the music pumps, and every suplex and slam feels impactful.Wrestle Quest is not just a game, it's a trip back in time. _childDocuments_.review: Inspired by classic JRPG's, WrestleQuest is a Turn-Based RPG that takes the traditional formula while adding elements from Wrestling (Pinning, Taunting, Tag Teams etc.).  Some initial impressions- Pixel Art looks great- Music sounds awesome and fits with the game- Game play is simple and easy to get a grasp on - A good amount of Wrestling references for the Wrestling fansAlthough it takes awhile before the story gets on a much better pace, the game for the most part, was fun and engaging both game play and story wise.This game is recommend for wrestling fans, for retro turn-based fans, and especially the niche overlap of those two fan-bases. There are several areas in which the game can still improve upon such as some adjustments to the speed of combat and the over-world walk speed, otherwise it was pretty good effort for what it wanted to achieve!
_childDocuments_.name: WrestleQuest

_childDocuments_.review: I've been enjoying my time with the game so far! The gameplay reminds me of some of the old Mario RPGs I've played where it features turn-based battles that have some active elements to it. In WrestleQuest's case, they use quick time events, which some people may or may not like but I got used to them. WrestleQuest also shakes up the traditional RPG system by adapting it towards its wrestling theme, like the name changes for stats and party roles. The battles also introduce mechanical quirks like hype meter management and pinning as the win condition which freshens up the experience as well! Not to mention that the set-design of the places you visit look really good and feels packed with personality. I find the story to be quite campy and fun which might not be for everyone, but I'm enjoying it so far even as someone who's not that big of a fan of wrestling. This has overall been a neat experience so far and will probably be a game that I take my time with!
_childDocuments_.name: WrestleQuest

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a handful of JRPG Turn-Based Combat Games and decided to give this a try because why not, right? The controls took a bit of time to get used to but once you get the hang of it, it really is easy. I like the combat system with its added QTE System which highlights combo-ish move abilities. The story starts a bit slow but it gets more interesting as it progresses which is one of the main driving force of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've recently had the pleasure of diving headfirst into the world of "WrestleQuest," and let me tell you, it's been a fantastic ride. Combining the adrenaline-pumping action of professional wrestling with the strategic depth of role-playing games, it delivers an engaging and entertaining experience.Matches are fast-paced and tactical, requiring a mix of well-timed button presses and strategic decision-making. The mechanic for striking and countering adds depth to the combat system, and mastering it is immensely satisfying.What sets WrestleQuest apart is its storytelling. The game cleverly weaves a captivating narrative into the wrestling world, complete with rivalries, backstage drama, and unexpected plot twists. The writing is sharp and humorous making it a joy to follow your character's journey from underdog to champion.The graphics are pixel-crisp, featuring vibrant arenas and finely-animated wrestlers. The attention to detail is exceptional, offering a wide array of interactive elements that continually breathe fresh life into the game.In conclusion, WrestleQuest is a delightful fusion of wrestling and RPG elements that offers hours of entertainment. Its engaging gameplay, and well-crafted storytelling make it a must-try for fans of either genre. I highly recommend trying the game yourself!

_childDocuments_.review: Wrestle Quest is a game I really like because I am fond of JRPGs. It does build upon the genre with a few creative and unique ideas. Firstly, it is not common that in a battle scene, the playable characters are from the right, in more traditional games, the usual orientation is the playable characters are from the left going to the right. Secondly, QTEs are added as a form of a dynamic battle experience compared to a static one where the player would just press menu buttons. It is not anything new with the old Mario RPG games having implemented them already but I do not observe any other games emulating that implementation. I think it is a great way to use QTEs and not the other cases where it’s done only against the last boss. Thirdly, I think the tag teams are a great way to make the fight more dynamic as a whole because some characters have built-in kits that are way more offensive while some have supportive and defensive kits. It reflects the different classes of traditional games; knight, rogue, magician, and healer. In those cases, bringing a healer can impact your team’s total damage and you might want to opt them out in certain situations. In the case of Wrestle Quest, it has tag team and triple tag team mechanics that involve your healer/support to deal damage or even inflict status effects on enemies. Finally, the hype meter is a unique mechanic that I have never experienced before in any other game, it is essentially a team-wide buff and debuff mechanic depending on if the audience’s hype is on you or the enemy. It incentivizes the players to execute actions to put it in their favor but at a cost that balances out the buffs of the hype meter. Really interesting mechanics and features that are implemented into the game.I only have a few gripes about the game, I really like the recent trend of JRPGs where the players could impact the start of the encounter by attacking the enemies first in the overworld. Unfortunately, the game lacks that feature, I think it adds another layer of player agency in an otherwise lack of player agency the genre is known for. Moreover, the cost of doing a tag team and triple tag team moves is quite high. Although the hype meter introduces an AP regen mechanic if it is high enough, the fact that the initiation requires 10 AP and the executor requires 20+ AP to just execute one tag team or triple tag team move is high. Overall, I would give the game a solid 8/10. It did well with the attempts to modify the JRPG format and I think the game is charming and unique. The music is also really good, I had a few times where I stopped playing just to listen and vibe to the soundtrack for a little bit.

_childDocuments_.review: WrestleQuest stands as a testament to the fusion of classic 2D pixel art aesthetics and an engaging RPG narrative. This is not a mere game; it's an experience that manages to strike a harmonious balance between its strengths and shortcomings.Pros:🎨 Pixel Art Mastery: The game's pixel graphics are a work of art. Every frame is carefully crafted, and the Toy Room world is a marvel of design. It's a testament to the developer's attention to detail.😂 Clever Humor: Amidst the intense action, WrestleQuest cleverly interweaves humor into its dialogue. It's a welcome relief and adds depth to the characters.🎵 Auditory Excellence: The music and sound effects are perfectly synchronized with the game's atmosphere. They enhance the immersion and elevate the gaming experience.However, let's address the game's imperfections:Cons:⏱️ QTE Complexities: WrestleQuest's reliance on Quick Time Events (QTEs) may not resonate with everyone. The timing can be unforgiving, especially in some gimmicks with rapid QTE sequences. Improvement in the timing and execution is needed.🚶 Sluggish Movement: Navigating the overworld maps can feel sluggish, which detracts from the overall pacing. A smoother movement system would greatly enhance the gameplay.🙈 Interaction Quirks: At times, interactions with objects can be cumbersome, disrupting the flow of the game. Though not a major issue, it's worth noting.In summary, WrestleQuest is an intriguing blend of wrestling, pixel art, and RPG elements. It's a game that demands appreciation for its dedication to its craft. If you're a fan of any of these genres, WrestleQuest is a commendable addition to your gaming library. The positives undoubtedly overshadow the negatives, making it a worthwhile journey for the discerning gamer. Dive into the Toy Room world and uncover the charm of WrestleQuest.

_childDocuments_.review: When my friend asked me if I liked wrestling, I totally thought they were asking me to watch old Wrestlemania videos. Never thought they'd slap me in the face with the love child of old RPGs we used to play on our GBAs and WWE but here we are. WrestleQuest is a love-letter for wrestling enthusiasts everywhere, make no mistake about it. It may not be the wrestling game you've imagined but it's what we deserve and more.Pros:- The music is sick. Like, I can just spend my time listening to the tracks. Is there going to be an OST Bundle?- The banter between the wrestlers are great, while I do keep failing to pick the right hype message (I acknowledge I'm very bad at this) they're entertaining enough that I don't mind the lower hype.- The Hype System's a nice touch to a Turn-based RPG. It kind of stops me from just picking attack all night long, which is cool since it keeps the combat from growing repetitive or stale.- Appreciated the setting for slower QTE's, we're not big on our reflexes so it sort of helped ease us through the combat system that relied on it a lot.- Stag Logan. No, really, he's the PRO in all of this. Stag Logan, love that guy. I'd play this entire game just for Stag.Cons:1. Not a big fan of the QTE's being almost everywhere. Works nicely in action games but in a Turn-Based RPG it was a little bit too much. Maybe if it was just in the Gimmicks since that totally makes sense especially if hitting the right button hypes up the crowd a bit more!Nice to have:- OST Bundle?- Auto Run Setting. Would be nice if there was a toggle in the menu for it so I don't have to press down on the button all the time.- PS Controller Buttons. Right now I think when you hook up a controller it'd default to just seeing the XBOX buttons for the QTEs. It kind of confused me for a hot second while doing the QTE so would be nice if the game recognized the type of controller we have so it can display the right button for it.Now excuse us as we try to drag one of our friends to a pool to try Muchacho Man's moves.

_childDocuments_.review: I was intrigued with the concept of mixing wrestling with RPG elements, and the first hour of the game hooked me! Seeing wrestling presented as a turn-based RPG caught my attention, as it breaks the mold of being a fighting game. I also love the underdog story as it is easily relatable -- however, it was a missed opportunity to customize the main character after the introduction time skip. I also find the QTEs unsatisfying at times, breaking the flow of combat. Some fights in WrestleQuest also have "conditions" wherein if you accomplished specific actions, you gain more rewards, which reflects the "scriptedness" of the world of wrestling, and I like how it was implemented.Despite my dismay of the QTEs, my initial impression of the game is positive and I see a lot of potential where the story can go. Overall, I recommend this game if youre looking for a fun and quirky turn-based RPG.

_childDocuments_.review: Love it! Love love love it! Captures the delirious thrills and bombast of professional wrasslin' and delivers it in such an affectionate, nostalgia-prodding way. Surprised at how substantial the game is, was expecting a few-hours-and-done indie title, but this is closer to a classic Final Fantasy or a Mario & Luigi RPG game, with a large cast of characters and a fun, perfectly serviceable story that, at more than just a few times, makes me a bit giddy.. Any substantial complaints I had are being addressed in an upcoming patch. I'm especially appreciative of the increase in running-speed, feeling that to be an absolute must for some of the larger areas.The only issue that remains is that the game doesn't take place entirely in San Sebastián del Encordado, Wrestlequest's lucha libre themed realm. I adore that setting and am pooling together the funds to move there permanently.Viva! Viva los Loachadores!

_childDocuments_.review: More Oh Yeah than Oh noMost of the issues I've came across so far are just quality of life issues that hopefully can be patched in, but even if not, this still could be a classic that I come back to every year or so.Pros/Cons:-Music: 9/10, Freaking Great, we're not talking Final Fantasy, but I didn't ever want to turn it off for sure.-Graphics: 7.5/10, Not Octopath Traveller but one of the best pixel art style JRPG's I've played.-Writing: 9/10, Didn't feel the 4th wall moments with YouTube personalities (in the way they were used, toss em on the podcast at least vs in the wild) - but otherwise, just the right amount of cream without cringe-Combat: 8/10, I love the throwback of active-active time battles like Mario RPG, and the overworld map/tag team combo's remind me of Chrono Trigger, I do find that the timing of the buttons for somethings (Pinning specifically) seems to have some latency issues though.-UI/UX: 5/10, This is the biggest issue for me in the game (Which, thankfully most of isn't where I'm spending a lot of time.) - How to Fix the UI/UX issues,1) Let me re-map every button/command and let it be easier.2) The current run speed should replace the walk speed, and the current run speed should be around 3.5x faster.3) Let me hit up to go-to the bottom of my menu if I'm at the top currently.4) There's an accessability menu for options to make the game easier, but there's no tool tips/alt text on the options to tell me what some of them do. (Auto-Pin/QTE Slow are obvious, the others, not so much) - Add more options as I see some other complaints, but most importantly - tell me what they do without me having to experiment.5) Setting to Controller, seems to reset to Mouse/Keyboard whenever I re-launch the game. (but it also doesn't seem to matter/change anything as the controller still functions the same...?)Overall: 7/10, but with some more QOL updates could surely hit 8/10 at least - this is a game mashup for childhood me for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm re-reviewing after reaching what I presume to be the first boss. My original review was from a much angrier and unhinged perspective of a tired, new father. I hope this one is a lot less caustic and much more productive to the devs and the players.So, I've been playing for a little bit on the Steam Deck and it's been a good experience thus far. As stated in my now-deleted angry review, the presentation is great. The pixel art is crisp and detailed, while the music is catchy and energetic. The animation quality is a moot point given there isn't much to work with when using sprites.As far as the story goes - it's a mixed bag. There's quite obviously an underlying "Fed Bad" theme in the story. Jabs at writers, scripts, and other big WWE TV nuances are largely prevalent early in. This, for some reason, annoyed me in my first foray into Wrestlequest but is not actually a big deal. It's cute, it's funny, and it's not coming from a place of maliciousness but instead comes from a place of love for the core aspects of the wrestling business.My favorite thing about Wrestlequest so far is the battle system. Generally, battles in RPGs and JRPGs can be a slog to get through, but Mega Cat turns that on its head and introduces a few gameplay mechanics that perfectly coincide with the overarching theme of pro wrestling. The stand-outs here are the Tag-Team and Pin mechanics.Framerate has been stabilized and works flawlessly on Steam Deck. Occasionally I'll get a hiccup in controls, but I'm unsure why. I'll randomly be unable to make my character go north as the up button on the D-Pad and going up with the analog and touch pad just stops working. A simple restart fixes it, so the ability to save anywhere really helps mitigate the frustration.I would love to see this get an official Steam Deck Verified tag in the future and look forward to playing more very soon.I apologize to Mega Cat, wholeheartedly, for the bizarrely offensive review I left upon release. I don't really know why I attacked this game so harshly over innocuous things like Conrad Thompson being involved. Nobody deserved that.Thank you for loving the wrestling business enough to make a pioneering genre combination like this. I hope to see more in the future.

name: Solar Ash
detailed_description: From the creators of the award-winning Hyper Light Drifter comes the high-speed and gravity-bending world of Solar Ash. Set amidst a surreal dreamscape filled with long-abandoned ruins of great civilizations past, you play as Rei, a Voidrunner determined to stop at nothing to save her planet from falling prey to the Ultravoid’s path of eternal hunger. Fight through mobs of grotesque creatures, grind rails with sheer delight, grapple to wild heights, take down enormous bosses, and surf the ashen clouds of shattered, bygone worlds swallowed by the void. In this highly stylized action adventure unlike no other, will Rei persevere and make her way through the deadly encounters of this ravenous void in order to save her home? Will she learn the truth about these massive beasts that roam this strange land and uncover the mysteries of the Starseed and Echo? The answer to these questions, and more, awaits you in the Ultravoid.

_childDocuments_.review: If there is one thing I dont like, its the dialog. Your character, Rei, loves to talk. its never so much to be overbearing but about 80% of anything she said felt unnecessary. unlock a shortcut? "that should help me get back here faster" find some object or log you can inspect in the world? Rei's got a quip or comment on it. I dont mind playing as a character outside of myself but I dont like being told how to think about a thing, how to feel about a situation, or that this shortcut is, indeed, a shortcut.WITH THAT SAID, other aspects of the game are great, movement feels good, art is beautiful, music is fitting and wonderful. but everything stays fairly stagnate, no real meaningful upgrades to get or push in combat past new enemy types, though combat isnt the focus.each area follows a pretty systematic approach. there are non-annoying gimmicks and mechanics in each ares to keep engagement but if the game went on much longer it would have needed more spice.id say check it out on sale and be excited for hyper light breaker. the team no doubt learned a lot about making a 3d game from this. 3/5, pretty good

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favorite game. It replaced Hyper Light Drifter, which was my favorite before it. I explain it to friends as 'shadow of the colossus but with rocket boots and a grapple hook'. It takes about 6 hours to play, even to 100%. I've beat the game 4 times now, twice hardcore mode (first in Epic then again once it moved to Steam so I could get the achievements.) No one I know has even heard of this game until I bring it up, which is criminal. The story is dark and beautiful, the voice acting is so good that I would still tear up a little on my third play through,  and it just feels good to play. A game about mobility HAS to feel good to run around in, and with this you're gliding on skates across smooth clouds, hooking onto grapple points mid air, zipping by enemies, darting between objectives and monsters. It all just feels great. The music is a vibe, the colors are a dream, it's the best game I've ever played and I still need to learn how to speed run it so that I can just keep playing it over and over. You don't need a guide to get 100% of the collectibles, of which there is a very streamlined amount. Some NPC storylines, and some loot caches that I really think you have to get if you want the game's full story and effect. Everything is telegraphed clearly, but just obscured enough to make discovering one feel like you hunted for it. The quests and the caches are the only collectibles, aside from a series of little NPC notes that you don't have to collect to 100% the game, but you can collect for an achievement. It feels so intentional, not bloated, a whole rich story and world packed into 6 hours of a good, fun game with a unique atmosphere that is always fluctuating between high energy zip lining, and melancholic, quiet beauty- even ranging into a little body horror with the monsters and their black oozy eyes. Definitely hits a vibe I just wish I had more of. Bright and beautiful but also gloomy and quiet. Characters are authentic and you really feel for them. Plus, their designs are stellar. I also like that you can see pieces of the levels from different vantage points across the entire map, it really makes the world feel like you are this hyper-mobile cyberpunk skater who can explore every inch of the map, and it's compact enough that it isn't an overwhelming feeling. Heart Machine has made 2 games and is my favorite developer because they're just so unique and excellent.Oh and you CAN toggle the skate button between holding the trigger down, or toggling on and off, which is a nice setting if you don't want to squeeze a trigger for 6 hours straight.

_childDocuments_.review: ABOUT STUTTER CONCERNS:Contrary to a certain review, the game does NOT suffer from shader compilation stutter. It does have minor loading stutters occasionally, but I have confirmed that it is free of shader compilation stutters or otherwise incessant stutters using a frametime graph.ABOUT STEAM DECK:Unfortunately, the game performs quite poorly on deck, has minor graphical glitches, and does stutter seemingly due to a compatibility layer bottleneck of some kind. I cannot recommend it on the deck at the moment.FINAL THOUGHTS:While Hyper Light Drifter is my favorite game of all time, this game is entirely unlike it. I'm leaving my review as positive because for me, the game was perfectly functional and I am returning it for personal reasons.
