_childDocuments_.review: Solar Ash is a game with great ideas and themes that get a bit muddied down with their executions. The game gets close, but not all the way there.If you're a fan of Heart Machine games and want to support this developer's work, I would recommend buying at the full $40 USD price tag. If not, that price point can seem a bit steep - with the amount of content this game gives you, I'm not sure if it fully measures up to that chunk of change for a lot of people.It took me about 12 hours total to 100% this game (all Voidrunner caches/suits, side content). I don't necessarily consider my money wasted - it's a very rare occurence that I 100% a game (ever), so in a way I was glad that I was able to do that so easily, however at the end I was left wanting so much more than what I ended up getting.If you're not a diehard fan of this developer, $40 isn't quite right for the amount of content on display here. I'm not going to pretend I know how expensive making a game is nowadays (I'm a developer, just not a game developer). If I had forgotten how much I paid for this game, I would have guessed the price would sit at a nice $25 or even $30 for the amount of stuff there is to do.Another point to add is there are many people who won't care to 100% this game, in which case they'll finish it off around the 6-8 hour mark - making the $40 price tag a bit too steep for those people.Considering Hyper Light Drifter (Heart Machine's previous title) sits at $20 USD, and I got 18 hours out of that rather than the 12 I got here, I feel I got a much better deal with HLD.Maybe wait for a sale, unless you want to support Heart Machine, in which case, godspeed.This game takes a good amount of inspiration from HLD - you're an agile warrior that has sword-like attacks, and you can dash and run. You only have ONE main attack in this game (slash combo, 3 parts). You can also use your "grappling hook" to hit and latch onto enemies as well, something I didn't learn until much later in the game than I should have.There are only about 4/5 main enemy types (excluding the "big bads" at the end of every zone) - each enemy type can basically be killed by hitting them a lot. Most of them don't require special tactics to take down, just spam melee at them. There was no progression of the combat systems as you progress the game. What you have in the opening section is what you'll use the entire rest of your playthrough.Movement feels great here as you skirt and skate on and around these environments - it definitely feels what this game wanted to nail down the most was movement and the environment design to complement that, and I think the developer did a great job there. Each zone feels different enough to move around in that I never really got bored of traversing this world. You've got rails/vines to skate on that really make you feel like a badass, and skating on the many "clouds" in the game feels fluid, just as it should.I definitely would have liked to see more "safeguards" around movement here though, as some times it feels a bit floaty and it's easy to miss your intended direction as you jump/dash. There are times when it feels your momentum isn't preserved enough (as you tend to suddenly switch directions when dashing in a direction that isn't completely straight ahead), and there are also time when it feels your momentum is preserved too much. I think some fine tuning would have been great in this department.Overall, I think the story did the job it needed to - but for a $40 title, I expected a bit more than I got. Definitely not as much depth to the characters as I wanted - there were plenty of moments where I was left wanting for more interaction, but did not find it.A note on the main character - her voice actress does a great job portraying her character's feelings of desperation, despair, and grief - absolutely necessary when the character's animations during story moments are basically non-existent.Speaking of exposition - along your journey, you'll find Voidrunner Caches in the zones you explore. These are leftover voice recordings from your "teammates" you came to this place with in order to stop a devastating event from happening.Unfortunately, you have to stop dead in your tracks, unable to move while you listen to them - and sometimes they . Some recordings go on for over a minute, while you're left unable to move, or do anything, really. This ended up being one of my biggest pet peeves in this game - with the game being focused around fluid, fast movement, it seems counterintuitive to make the player completely stop moving when they come across a Cache, being basically stuck in a pause screen while the audio plays. I really wish this was eventually changed, but wasn't, and most likely will never be.Overall, I wouldn't buy this game for its story at all - it had great ideas, it just didn't flesh those ideas out enough for me to consider this a good buy for story alone.Graphically, Solar Ash is stunning to look at, with each zone being visually distinct from the last but remaining just as awe-inspiring all the way through. This game certaintly has its "wow" moments - in certain areas, the game is pre-programmed to pan the camera out and reveal a much more "top-down" view of the zone you're about to explore. This is one of those "every moment is a screenshot" games that never pulls its punches on its visual delivery.The game is highly stylized in many aspects - one of which being its beautiful color palette.Solar Ash was Heart Machine's first foray into 3D worlds and I believe this developer  nailed it on the head. Lots of missed marks in terms of story/presentation, character development, and combat depth and progression. However, many other marks were hit right on the head: movement, overall gameplay loop, visual/sound/musical presentation, and just being a fun video game.I really liked what I played here - I just wish there was more of it - I wish there was more stuff to do, more places to go, and more enemies to fight.I'd recommend to diehard Heart Machine fans and people who love the "space skater" schtick - if neither of those labels speak to you, I'd wait for a sale to try this one out.

_childDocuments_.review: Solar Ash clearly has its own focus in mind, and executes its vision mostly pretty well. I do not think it has any fatal flaws. It is slow in the very beginning, but grows the player's interest without falter to the very end. The game may not be for you if you don't like wanting to actively seek out bits of narrative development in the form of voice logs (yes, you can listen to all of them instead of having to read them, they are all voice-acted), which aren't necessary to beat the game. This game is certainly worth the money, unarguably even more so if you are a fan of fast-paced 3D platformers. The game truly shines when the player gets to keep moving in one long, unforgiving, single motion of slashing and grappling, which that opportunity is given many, many times. Heart Machine's second game, Solar Ash, is a fantastic game.My following criticisms of the game may feel heavy-handed at first, so just hear me out.I have three prominent issues with the game:Firstly, in the first zone/area, despite its vibrant coloring (which the game keeps up consistently), was only lightly interesting. I cannot put my finger on exactly what it was that made the beginning feel bland, but I suppose it is that the level design and boss is too safe and formulaic as an introduction to the game's mechanics. I think that I am pretty good at video games, platformers especially, so this may be because I found it too easy (mind that I played through this game on the hard difficulty, the most difficult mode available for a first playthrough). That is especially a problem because it is the player's first impression of the game.Secondly, I think the narrative for the game is a little weak, by that I mean all the other characters. I think the primary narrative of 'finding out what happened' gets better the more voice logs you look at or listen to; but even still, not everyone will want to seek out voice logs of your other Voidrunner crew-mateswhich is the primary drive of how interested I was in the primary narrative. Secondary narratives (includes all other characters) feel like they lack any sort of importance. You are expected to care about your other Voidrunner crew-mates while having no prior introduction to them and . As for the other side character's storylines, they aren't compelling enough and feel like set-dressing more than anything else even though most of the time you have to actively seek out their many different locations of interaction to progress their stories if you want their full story. I think the logs are only interesting for finding out what happened to the other world(s) which was/were swallowed by the Ultravoid, and not as much for who was documenting it. As for the other characters, I wouldn't have cared as much to find out all of their storylines if it wasn't for the fact that the game has a nice 100% completion reward (which is: spoiler: ) Lastly (), Despite all of what was previously stated, I really do like and recommend this game. The art direction is stunning and vibrant. The cutscenes are beautiful. Despite being able to very rapidly traverse the ever-bending warped-gravity surfaces of the game, the camera functions impressively well as it can alternate from free-cam to a fixed perspective fluidly and comfortably, it has a few customization options too -- it is rarely awkward. The music is best appreciated when it gets to blare through the satisfying sound design of sprint-boosting and slashing enemies. I absolutely loved being able to tackle the monstrously-large bosses, sprinting across their surfaces like an ant with the unrelenting flow and force of a great, rushing river.I recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: From the developers of Hyper Light Drifter comes a new game that tells a story about regret and moving on. Solar Ash is a third person roller-skating game. As Voidrunner Rei, players need to skate through ruins on the Ultravoid to prevent your planet from being destroyed by said void. Activate the Starseed and everything can be saved, only things might not be this straightforward as you continue down the path. I like this game. Not only because it's made by Heart Machine, but also it's great to see the dev team improve and evolve outside of their comfort zone. The game does have various issues regarding gameplay, but I still recommend Solar Ash for those who likes smooth skating and some time-racing.Basically the Risk Of Rain 2 treatment. I am glad the dev steps out their comfort zone and make their second game a 3D game. It is a wonderful transition. They manage to recreate the style of Hyper Light Drifter into a smooth 3D world, with its own aesthetic and without losing the same personality.Skating is the main feature of the game. It is also the best thing about Solar Ash. Skating through the cloud ocean all the while weaving in and out of ruins never feels this good. The animation is smooth and fluent. The control feels responsive, making boosted-jumping through gaps, across buildings, and between rails easy to achieve. I especially adore moments which the camera will zoom out during long skating session and let you take in the beautiful yet crumbled world ahead of you.→Boss Fights is speed-up Shadow Of Colossus with timed-racing.→Bold usage of colors.→: Story itself is quite simple and effective.→: What I don't like about the story is that the turns and twists should happen sooner. The opposite voice should appear at the middle point of the game and become clearer at late game. Currently the opposite voice only appears at the last area. Thus, in my opinion, it is quite hard to set up a dilemma at the end of the game without forcing a confrontation.I am quite confused at these design choices. Every time you meet Echo, she will always destroy one shield of Rei permanently until you fix it, which the latter is really easy to do considering plasma is quite abundant in each area. Other than metaphorical meanings, I fail to see logic behind such design. Another issue I have about it is how irrelevant the shield system against boss fight. If you fail the speed test, you will take damage and will be sent back to the checkpoint. Why it couldn't just let me fall down the Remnant so I can get back up and try again immediately is beyond me.The fun of skating can only last so long considering you can only press two buttons for it - one to skate forever and one to boost yourself for a short distance. I wish the game can offer more abilities to make skating more than just changing direction. Things like creating jump pads and rails at will, charged boost, integrating attacks with mobility, etc could easily help elevate the game to higher levels.→Camera angle during certain skating session feels really janky and even won't allow you yo move.→I wish all the area are inter-connected so our parkour/skating skill can shine even brighter while exploring.中文小簡評→光明行者製作團隊跳出舒適圈做出來的新作。→能夠將光明行者的畫風完美詮釋於3D建模。→競速型汪達與巨象。→角色動畫操作流暢，無論在雲海中溜冰、在失落文明間跳躍穿梭、或者在極長的軌道眺望整個世界都是那麼令人興奮。→故事起承轉合簡單分明，但是「轉」的部分太晚出現且不足，以至於無法體現結尾的兩難。→護盾及其修補機制覺得雞肋。→如果有更多技能跑酷溜冰技能就好了。→王的攻擊方式及慾望要再多點。→鏡頭在某些地方溜冰時容易亂跑。

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous graphics, fun gameplay and unique art style.The talented people at Heart Machine created an incredible world brimming with atmosphere and the otherworldly bosses you will encounter are kinda reminiscent of Lovercraft.Solar Ash also deliver a really cool and fluid movement system and it play perfectly fine with mouse and keyboard despite the game clearly telling you it's best played with a controller.You know a game is good when you can have fun just wandering around doing nothing but exploring and enjoying the movement system.I'm having a great time so far, would easily recommend if you enjoy fast paced 3D platformer and exploration.Warframe and Super Cloudbuilt being two of my favorites when it comes to fast paced movements platformers I can say I'm right at home here with Solar Ash.However the combat seems somehow limited and kinda clunky in Solar Ash so probably not the game strongest part.There's few problems with the camera during some bosses phases but nothing too dramatic.Also have to say there are minor frame drops issues but the game runs smoothly most of the times.Just sad we had to wait a whole year to finally play it on PC though.Take your time, have fun exploring the world, read and listen to the logs to expand the lore and you will enjoy this game even more.The sheer amount of creativity on display here is outstanding and it's quite sad to see people still buying their generic recycled crap games every years but end up ignoring games like Solar Ash which deliver unique experiences.This is a really good game which I highly recommend if you enjoy 3D platformers and exploration.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm afraid I don't recommend Solar Ash. It's by the Hyper Light Drifter people (Zelda/Souls mix) but this time it's Shadow of the Colossus meets a Platformer(tm) by way of Jet Set Radio.Now you can do pretty much everything on one save file and get both endings, which is a plus. However, the game isn't very long and has only 3 side "missions" - which usually involve walking to some places and interacting with a person or object to get some lore. They're not really "missions." The collectibles are the same way. There are 5 suit parts per area and 6 areas in the game. Each suit part comes with an audiolog and each completed suit has special abilities. However, these are the only collectibles in the game and the final suit part has the ability to.. find collectibles, which is useless if you already have the other suits. There is also an issue in that one suit in particular (the instant dash suit) is basically the objectively best suit in the game.Ultimately, the game felt lacking. The game tries to put a spin on shadow of the colossus but its bosses never attack you while you are on them; you will only die or take damage due to falling off or running out of time. The timed aspect is also pretty irritating as it just forces you to respawn and retry. Health feels pretty meaningless as it's not really used in boss fights or during the eye sections you do around the map to unlock the boss. There are some cool things like the rail grinding that aren't really developed in any meaningful way. By the end of the game I was invested in the plot (despite a couple inconsistencies in writing), but just felt tired. I had short bursts of fun but it was very off and on. The irritation from the bosses and eyes never really went away and the whole time I was just thinking about other games that have done the concepts better. For $40, this is kind of terrible value for money; now I paid half that personally and at that it's alright, but it was a fairly middling experience and I feel like I should have just played a different platformer instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Played through it. Got what the game calls 100% completion. Didn't have fun. The end.In more detail: Everything in the game feels low stakes / impactless; it's sort of surprising they left non-boss combat in it at all, since it doesn't feel elegant, doesn't have much room for skill expression, doesn't have important outcomes, and doesn't feel like it ties into the plot. You platform around environments that are more linear than they look, you occasionally perform a timed movement segment with a woefully squishy-feeling movement system where you're fighting either the camera, questionable geometry, or the controls, and then you keep doing that for several hours. If you fail a segment, you just start back at that segment again. 'Puzzles', if they can be called that, are extraordinarily rudimentary. You can find secret things but none of them really matter. You can do sidequests; they're done not when they come to a meaningful resolution, but when you exhaust whatever amount of arbitrary writing they have.The game tries to tell an emotionally heavy story revolving around planetary-scale disaster and sacrifice and refusal to accept reality and the ways in which suffering can be inflicted despite good intentions, and then undercuts any ability to take it seriously with plot elements like the cartoonish deaths of background characters (e.g. one group is shown to have died by ) and non sequitur references to famous poems by one Tarragon Danderpaws. There are stories into which such elements can fit, but here they make it hard to envision the game-world as a place where the main character can be driven by the life-and-death pressures that underlie their characterization.Maybe this game is a victim of its predecessor's success. Maybe I was foolish for seeing the game's visual callbacks to HLD (e.g. blade-wielding pink-cape-wearing main character with its distinctive color scheme) and assuming this game would have any similarity to HLD, with its tight controls, skill-heavy gameplay, and thoughtfully-designed challenges. But apart from this game's reasonably high production-value with its varying and visually-appealing environments and its technically cool playing around with the directionality of gravity, there was nothing really engaging about the rote and drawn-out gameplay.$40 for a game with a 10-hour play-time is a relatively high price in this market. This game doesn't deliver the kind of experience that would justify it. It's probably unfair to expect this developer to capture lightning in a bottle twice after selecting such a radically different medium for this game, but that doesn't reduce the feeling of disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really disappointing platformer and I did 100% completion of it on standard difficulty so you don't have to (and I will never play it again). I really wanted to love it because I love Hyper Light Drifter (I have over 150 hours in HLD)Pros:10/10 Art style. Fantastic presentation10/10 Music. Can't go wrong with DisasterpieceCons:3/10 Narrative. Overall concept of story is good, but the presentation of it was really bad. The worlds felt very empty and the things you can see in them and interact with don't do a good job telling the story. An example is when you come across five dead bodies, and you interact with them and are told that some were senators and some citizens. But they all had the same model, same clothing, so you wouldn't know from just looking at them. The most you'll learn is from the logs, which is just exposition. If you liked the way you can learn the lore in Hyper Light Drifter by paying attention to the environment, you won't find that here.2/10 Gameplay. The fighting is terrible, it's just run up jump and click X to win. Avoiding attacks for the most part just requires jumping, positioning you character correctly or timely is not important at all. There are only 5 enemies in the game, with virtually no increasing difficulty as you progress. The boss fights are all the same timed platforming challenges with a janky camera and gravity. The grapple range is inconsistent, and it isn't clearly explained that the grapple range is increased with timeshifting. The gameplay lacks variability and gets boring really fast. Also the health system was completely pointless, the only time it makes a difference is if you get hit by an enemy, which you almost never will because they're so easy. But whether you are killed or hurt by something in the environment, like lava, you get restarted at your last checkpoint, so the penalty is the same. The final boss removes the healthbar, and honestly the whole game should have done that if it were gonna be this easy. Ideally, the pink goo points could have been used on new weapons, which would help fight enemies that are actually challenging. If the enemies were harder, keep the healthbar, and have you just upgrade it once per slot (rather than losing an upgrade every time you beat a boss). Quests are uninteresting there really isn't much you learn from them with regards to lore, Arrhic's is probably the most interesting but you can figure out what it's implying from just talking to one Umbral elder.I would recommend other platformers more like the Ori series if you want a challenge, Spyro remakes (make sure to install a mod to change the FOV) if you want something relaxing.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Please note: while I recommend this game, it is more of a "meh." It's inoffensive but nothing special. A sight to behold with a story I'd rather not told.This is a traversal exploration game similar to The Pathless and is made by the team behind Hyper Light Drifter. You skate around, solving some environmental puzzles, finding some not-so-secret secrets, and defeating some bosses via a skating version of Shadow of the Colossus.The movement is fun enough, if a bit flawed. It had some side-to-side weight to it which makes control never feel quite right. It can be easy to over or under steer your character when skating around, not unlike being on ice. None of the traversal puzzles are all that complicated, though there are plenty of things that interfere with your movement. It feels more broken up than I feel it should, whether it be from climbing things, stopping to activate Hub points, stopping to because the speed throws you into geometry, or something else, which unfortunately detracts from the movement system that could have shined more than it does.There is combat, which is admittedly rather simple. It's not unlike the run-n-gun equivalent of the likes of Contra. It's not a focal point. It's more like something that mainly seems to exist to add some level of danger and to not have you just skating around the whole time. Something to keep your brain stimulated just enough to keep you playing. Nothing about it is too complex, even with the bosses, though I've heard from other reviewers that issues with perspective and in-game depth perception can make bosses more challenging for some. You can fairly easily ignore most enemy encounters, except for ones where you're either climbing or would continue to be in the line-of-sight of the sniper enemies.Solar Ash is quite a pretty game that has no dedicated photo mode, which is sad because that's it's greatest strength, in my opinion. They even have integrated scenic view spots where they take control of the camera from you to show you the environment, similar to the sections in Hades before you start the next zones. This definitely is a title hurting for a photo mode and I would spend plenty more hours in the game just to take photos where the character and HUD are removed. If there's one thing I think people can appreciate from this game, it's the art direction and the beautiful, screen-filling vistas it enables.The story is the biggest let down. It tries to add intrigue. It tries being clever with hints to a story that you can piece together parts of way before the credits roll. It tries being big-brained but feels more like it just pulled the story out of it's rear by the time credits roll, and that's with the good ending. At most, it has a good message, but that's about it. It left a sour taste in my mouth because I like brainy stories. This just seemed to think itself more brainy than it is, not unlike when movies undeservedly pull a "it was all a dream" twist.Anyway, at the end of the day, there are many more titles that deserve your time and this was a waste of mine, but it's at least a competent, inoffensive game that can please some people looking for a chill time in a beautiful world. If I had to give this a number, I'd rate this a 6.5. It was good enough to not have me hate it, but only just and that's why I would still recommend it. Get it on sale though, if at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Solar Ash is a movement-based platformer game with some great world building, voice acting, and accompanying sound design. The world consists of various levels that seem to be made in their signature neon-colored cyberpunk art style, which lends a great look to the world and feels like a lot of fun to look at and explore. However, as all the levels/worlds sit in these foggy blue clouds, some parts of the world can feel a bit empty and boring. But one can mostly just ignore these side areas to enjoy the main parts of the levels.When playing Solar Ash, there's one thing I constantly wished for, and that was a higher difficulty for the game's platforming – whether that be tighter jumps, less sticky grinding, or less automatic hitboxes for targets to grab onto. I played this game on normal difficulty and had a look at hard, but sadly, the hard mode seems to just increase damage taken and some enemy spawns, and doesn't influence the gameplay much in my opinion. Enemies are/feel like mostly ignoreable filler in the game, just there to hinder you ever so slightly once in a while.Overall, if you're looking for a nice short story game, this fits that role. But if you're looking for something more challenging, I'd suggest looking elsewhere. Sadly at its current price point i can't recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty good game. Moving around is not overly challenging and I never quite felt the sensation of momentum I was really hoping for, but still enjoyed exploring the environments and solving the challenges. It can be tough keeping track of where you are when traversing a big enemy, adding some frustration when you just look the wrong way and run out of time.The story was what kept me through. It's not overly complex, but finding all the hidden caches and doing the extra side quests really fleshed things out and put some important context to the main storyline. And the main story itself is well done.Glad I got it on sale though. $40 is a bit steep for 7 hours, though it is visually a wonderful game to look at, and the voice acting is top notch.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Basically Super mario Galaxy + Tony Hawk's Pro Skater + Shadow of the Colossus, super fun, smooth and quick movement. The scenery looks absolutely incredible from a distance which is greatly enhanced by the fact there's no loading screens, just one gigantic map.Big rec when on sale, can't say I'd get it full price tho.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: It's like the Pathless but sci-fi instead of ancient ruins/guardian spirits .EDIT: OH, and btw, you know shadow of the colossus? Well in this game you'll be pathless-ing on top of huge colossi at the end of each zone.EDIT 2: It's a shame not everyone will see it but in the last section of the game, it truly looks unlike anythink else you've ever seen. Incredible. Bug free game
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Great gameplay, fluid movement, rewarding exploration. Story's a bit hit or miss, but its worth seeing through to the end. Plays like Shadow of the Colossus with Jet Set Radio and Mario Galaxy sprinkled in. This is one of those "every frame a wallpaper" kind of games, some of the scenes are absolutely beautiful. I spent a good while just looking around at the vistas. If you're on an ultrawide monitor, there's a hex edit to enable ultrawide resolutions, but the HUD is misaligned (Targets, quest markers, etc.). A stupid issue, but totally playable.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: FOR DECK USERS:This game still runs verrrry poorly on the Steam Deck - which sucks, because I specifically asked for this game as a gift since I really like the IDEA of this game. Mature and creative 3D platformers are a rarer breed, and I thought this was going to be the game that scratched that run-and-jump itch for me. Unfortunately, it runs terribly on Deck, and seeing as my Deck is my only competent Steam gaming device, it's what I'm stuck with. Until something about the optimization of this game is changed, it will be gathering dust on my digital shelf."Steam Deck Playable" is a large overstatement - otherwise I wouldn't be giving a negative rating. Expect unstable 30fps on the lowest settings, and from what I'm told of future areas of the game the performance only gets worse. I cannot grant the patience for this game on Deck as is.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: I ended up refunding this - while it is definitely not a bad game, its a pretty weird one that I couldn't see myself enjoying.  I went into this as a self confessed Hyper Light Drifter fanatic, and while i knew going into Solar Ash that it was going to be  different, I guess i didn't appreciate just how different it was actually going to be. Solar Ash at its core is a mash up of a platform/puzzle game with almost like a skateboarding sim or Jet Set Radio.  Combat is pretty much an after thought (a few button pushes here and there) and the majority of the game is environmental puzzles, including the boss fights.  Skating down a giant space beasties, pinging weird syringe like switches and hitting stuff with your space grappling hook until it dies, and I didn't find it challanging or engaging.  I understand that maybe that's the point and that this was just supposed to be a chill exploration/platform game.Music was great, as always from disasterpeace, and i liked the art direction (although i was getting quite a juttery performance from such a lo-fi game).  Camera and controls felt a bit sticky, although I the animations were quite nice.Anyways like I said before this is not a bad game in any way but it really is a strange one and not one that I could get into.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: This game is wonderful and it is downright criminal that it's as niche as it is. It expands on the art style and aesthetic of Hyper Light Drifter, adds speed and interesting platforming to the base ideas of Shadow of the Colossus, and becomes something unique and glorious. It has perhaps the best movement mechanics I've ever had the pleasure of using. It manages to be high speed and momentum based, while also perfectly balancing precise movement with the appropriate level of slip and flow that skating requires.The enemies are fun to work around, the bosses are challenging while still being fair and having a good level of escalation, the puzzles are intriguing and satisfying to complete. The world that is built is incredibly fascinating, and the conclusion has a beautiful message that many will need to hear.Solar Ash is as close to perfect as a game can be and you'd be doing yourself a disservice by not playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, wow. I might need to come back to this later, but that was terrible.What if somebody took a colorful, trance-like space adventure, turned into an empty open world, and then turned the bosses into some of the most repetitive and janky 3D Sonic stages of all time?The health system is useless. Whenever you are either accessing a key to the boss or fighting the boss itself, you'll be doing a short section where you slash or grapple onto some blue pegs until you stab an eye at the end of the sequence (This, by the way, other than the open world sections of gliding around on some weird blue stuff, is the entire game play loop of the game). Whenever you fail at these timed sections, you will lose a hitpoint and be teleported back to a nearby checkpoint, or otherwise die. These checkpoints save you *as your current health stands*, so unless there are healing items directly nearby you may as well have one health.The bosses, if you can really call them that, are glitchy setpieces which will see you dying repeatedly to unseen geometry and parts of the setpiece not working as intended, hurling you into the lava. I've seen a few people say that the bosses have the same feel as Shadow of The Colossus, but since you can only hold onto them for upwards of 3 seconds before they turn into an instant death blob, there's absolutely no utility in holding onto them. You repeat the same stage ad nauseam, hitting arbitrary points of interest in a select order, while under a strict time limit, until you eventually win. There isn't anything else. Platforming in the open world sections serves no purpose other than to get lost in, and not in the sense that the surroundings are gorgeous- which given other reviews, one might think the game is going for. The game just isn't that visually interesting. You run on some unidentified blue stuff and grind on rails (also like Sonic, interestingly enough) around some empty locations. I get that you're literally inside a black hole, but it isn't empty in the sense that you're inside the Idea of the End of the Universe. It's empty insofar as it is plain.There appear to be some strange textural glitches sprinkled on top just as a bonus? The shortcut doors just turn into white blocks when you open them, so you can't see through them unless you turn the camera. Sometimes you'll die on a boss or key area for no reason whatsoever, and the notification that you have in fact been killed will stay in the middle of the screen for a while during your next attempt.Of course, I didn't beat the game- so maybe it gets better, maybe the story gets interesting, maybe the characters start having anything to say about where they are. But this was a mess.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: It's not terrible, just very, very average and hard to actually recommend. The art direction looked cool, but you kinda see all of it in the trailer. Imagine that stretched into 8 hours with mostly empty landscapes, repetitive traversal and really flaky combat. The boss battles were probably the the most fun it got, but there's lots of games that do that part better as well. The story is bland and predictable, but could've worked better if it was a much shorter experience with less filler.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: I'm upset this game doesn't have more attention. I picked it up in anticipation of Hyper Light Breaker but I was left just wanting more like this. The game is truly beautiful with gorgeous visuals and many wallpaper worthy moments and just wonderful to control and skate around.I'll also be thinking about the story for a while I think.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely stunning 3D platformer. The gameplay is simple but effective, and very stylish. Exploring the world is incredible, and the bosses are amazing; they're up there with some of my favorites. A bit pricey for it's length but this is probably one of the most quality-packed shorter games out there, especially for 3D platformers. It felt a bit awkward at first, and some of the boss segments are a bit annoying because of the camera and awkwardness, but the good points of the game heavily outweigh anything negative I could say. As someone who really loved Sonic Frontiers, this scratches a similar itch. The music during bosses isn't quite on the same level, and it's different since it doesn't have all of the Sonic gimmicks, but it shines on its own. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: A really beautiful game that suffers from some serious problems - i feel like it needed another few months in the oven before its release. I am not recommending this game due to its high price point of 53 Dollars CAD, ontop of some glaring gameplay and writing issues. The art style and music are spectacular, i feel that Solar Ash is just short of being amazing. I found my playthrough rife with little things that caused significant points of frustration; like finicky grind rails and buggy platforms on bosses, which shouldnt be issues that exist in a speed based precision 3D platformer. The writing could have been much more nuanced to make the end reveal more impactful - as it doesn't take long to figure out what's actually going on.  I really wish that the story wasn't spoonfed to you and was something you discover slowly through the environment or hinted to, with a large buildup to the end. I genuinely love Heart Machine's games for their art style and music, Solar Ash is worth playing for that experience - however not for 50 dollars in its current state. Definitely buy on sale if you are interested.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: I loved how Hyper Light Drifter managed to convey the story without words, and thus I was concerned about a voiced main protagonist. To my surprise I found the main VA quite fitting.Some of the other cast is a hit or miss.The game is greatly carried by the atmosphere, which is formed by excellent visuals and music and which greatly reminds me of the first game.The writing is solid and gameplay is enjoyable even if a tad bit on the easy side (playing on the hardest difficulty which is available on first playthrough, I never really felt like I was about to die in the game).Not sure if worth of 39€, but certainly a rather enjoyable experience. As many other reviews have pointed out, as of now some of the achievements seem to be bugged.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Despite some of the negative reviews, I decided to give this game a try anyway, given how much I enjoyed Hyper Light Drifter. This one takes place in the same universe but is far from the World of Light, so the story and the characters within it seem to be unrelated at this time. That aside, the story is fantastic, whose overarching theme seems to center around . Nearly everything is voice acted and you can tell it was well-produced.Some said that the game's "lack" of tutorial made it too hard for them to understand what to do, but I found it extremely simple to get the hang of. The basic controls are straightforward - you can skate, attack, latch onto things, and slow time to latch onto things. Everything else is revealed in due time. Solar Ash has been likened to a sci-fi Shadow of the Colossus, and I would concur. I would describe the gameplay as moderately challenging at times, but it remains smooth and enjoyable throughout.If you are going to play this game, complete it. Get all of the Voidrunner caches - they're not required to beat the game, but they're essential if you want the unabridged story. Finding them can be a little difficult at first; just keep an eye out for .Throughout the game I only encountered two glitches. Both were fixable by quitting and reloading the game, which is easy enough and only impedes your gameplay by a minute or two. One was straightforward, "oh, I'm stuck" - the other wasn't. If you're in the orange zone and you warp to Cyd after the boss initially activates, nothing you do will let you reach the boss during the fight. Reload the game  This may be fixed in a future patch.Anyway, the bottom line is that if you aren't a critic or you have an IQ greater than that of a potato, you will probably enjoy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: I expected great things from Heart Machine. Hyper Light Drifter was cool, highly stylized, and different, and the combat and exploration were enough to make up for the lack of an expressible story.Solar Ash is not that. There are elements of Hyper Light Drifter in its design, but the gameplay falls short of being interesting. Movement feels slow, esp. since there's so little of interest in between your main goals. You end up skating/boosting to point a, do the miniboss clear "dance", then skate to point b, rinse and repeat. The story started out interesting, but having to unlock story elements by hunting down secret paths in this too-sparse world just made me lose interest.What's missing is the sense of skill progression or leveling up. In Hyper Light Drifter you could unlock upgrades to your weapons and movement. In Solar Ash, you are actively punished after defeating each boss, by having your health reduced. Your main moveset/attack capabilities are the same at the end of the game as at the beginning.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game was rad!!!Beautiful visuals, a nice and fluid gameplay and an interesting story !The only trouble I've more or less had is with the camera but the slowing down time feature makes up for it ^^We can clearly see the wonderful style of Heart Machine in this game and I live for it (being a hyper light drifter fan, Solar Ash really took me back with this amazing style)Loved it ^^
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Solar Ash is another great game by Heart Machine, albeit lesser known than Hyper Light Drifter. Half of the game is skating around in interesting environments, and the other half is fast paced giant monster slaying action. I feel that once again, Heart Machine takes the difficulty in hardcore just a little too far for the games' mechanics, but overall getting good at it is quite satisfying. If anything the only real downside is the price, which is a little steep for a game that is beatable in about 6 hours, and easily less than 2 hours if you know what you're doing.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just okay, and that's a bit disappointing since I absolutely loved Hyper Light Drifter. It's mechanically solid - the movement is just about the only thing in the game and it's fluid and enjoyable. But the bosses and objectives throughout the levels rarely make good use of it. I played on the harder difficulty and it just felt finicky and frustrating, not especially challenging or satisfying. Also quite inconsistent. Combat feels like an annoyance.My other beef with this game is the tone and the story-telling. The punk, comic book style does absolutely nothing for me and the story felt like melodramatic, soft sci-fi nonsense. Clearly this is a matter of taste. But it feels like such a change from HLD that I hope it's really what the developers wanted to make, and not a case of publisher meddling.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: This game is kinda just a really uninteresting speed game.  You get this boring open world to go around in that has a bunch of weird speed challenges sprinkled in, ranging from REALLY REALLY easy to a rather normal difficulty.  The mechanics of the game are rather uninteresting, you just get a run button and a boost button essentially, and you move at a moderately quick pace.  Alot of the game is just slowly gliding over to where the next interesting thing is, getting blocked by bad puzzles or platforming challenges.  It starts giving you "puzzles" that are essentially just "look for the thing you need idiot."The story is trying to be this weird like kinda cryptic story about what's happening with this world, but it's pretty uninspired.  The main character is very whatever and keeps randomly giving marvel tier quips when you do certain things.  It trys to give this message about letting the past go, but it's pretty heavy handed and annoying about it imo.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Frontiers + Shadow of the Colossus+ Creative/Unique worldbuilding+ Predictable but satisfying campaign+ Compelling subplots+ Beautiful design- Your greatest enemy is the camera- Tracing weak points is a trial and error systemUnfortunately the bones of this game are just too weak and underdeveloped to support the meat on top of it. If just either one of the flaws were fixed, this game could have been twice as enjoyable and immersion wouldn’t break so much. Completing 100% and Hardcore sub 3hrs was not worth it. Only buy this game on an extreme sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: I passed on this game, like a fool, for years because it was given a "7" in a review. I couldn't stand to feel disappointed to the successor of Hyper Light Drifter.I was so wrong.There is a lot here to cover. The story telling connects by veiling themes of anxiety, grief, and the general emotional self destructive inability to let go with hyperlight drifter style sci-fi urgency and abstraction. It paints it over with Shadow of the Furi Hawk Colossus and packs an emotive punch all the way in the end game.Please buy this game. It doesn't insult your intelligence; it has legitimate beauty in every frame, and made me feel absolutely destroyed when I was complete with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: I've been enjoying Hyper Light Drifter, so decided to give Solar Ash a go too. Both games have the perfect sci-fi aesthetic a fantasy loving space nerd could hope for.It's a real shame I didn't record my first run, because there aren't many games out there that have got so much random reactions out of me. The video would've been probably called a compilation of surprised yelps upon falling into the void or horrified cursing upon noticing something enormous swimming in the clouds beneath me.The only "downside" I can come up with is being somehow... left thirsty for more. Although the length of the game and pace of the story were good and didn't feel rushed, I could've gladly spent another 10 hours or more with this. The other voidrunners seemed very interesting characters and finding stashes was one of my favorite things. Would've been nice to see some flashbacks or interactions between them, before everything turned to s**t. Also, will we get Steam backgrounds and emojis ever? The game is full of so pretty landscapes. Would be shame if... one couldn't use them as a gaming profile wallpaper.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: When you start the game, it throws you in the middle of a plot, and you eventually piece together whats supposed to be going on. The game play boils down to skate everywhere, climb black goop, run an obstacle course where you can't always see the next marker (so you need to re run the course because it times out), do those things several times, run an obstacle course on the boss, do all of that in a new area again and again until the game is over. Besides not always being able to see the next marker, the controls are not tight enough for the game play, leading to frustration more than fun. Another problem is that the grapple mechanism FEELS like there is no consistency to the distance at which it grapples. It might actually be the same every time, but it didn't feel like it. There are 3 side quests, which i skipped because by the time I got to the first one, I realized story was not this game's strong suit. Nor is game play... or controls... or graphics.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+crazy good art, worth the price alone just to see it+creative and cool environments, always felt surprised by a new area, never felt like you could predict what was next, and no area dragged on too long+fun boss designs, reminiscent of Shadow of the Colossus, but with grip mechanics replaced with timed checkpoints. Bosses never felt stale or underwhelming+wonderful movement, walk, slide, grapple, boost, and rail grind, feels a wall run or trick system away from a movement game+characters were simple without being grating, and never overstayed their welcome either+fantastic pacing, never dragged yet gave enough time to explore every area+despite having secrets, collectibles, and side quests, none felt annoyingly or unfairly hidden. Side quests are even tracked on the map which helped a lot when coming back after a day or two. And the hidden caches' zones are marked with a specific sign when in the area to help players hone-in on where they could beMehs (not cons, just mediocre)*Combat is just ok, enemies are varied and end of the game had some very fun gauntlets, but overall a lot of fights  (with grunts, not bosses) feel just ok*music was often well synced up with the tone, fit the environments, and didn't get in the way or grate. But also was often quite forgettable due to that*somewhat shorter game, took roughly 8 hours for me to beat, and while I think that time is perfectly fitting, mileage may varyCons: (both are rather minimal but I wanted to be fair)-running out of health leaves the player with only 1 HP, which in some areas means they may find themselves going through a gauntlet over and over again, dying repeatedly. Thankfully, enemies stay dead and this annoying loop only happened once and for maybe 2 minutes of my 8 hour playtime-bosses have an instakill during last phases that feels more an annoyance than a threat. Would have rather been damaged by it than have to repeat a whole sectionOverall the game was a wonderful time, highly recommended to anyone looking for a solid 7-10 hour 3D platformer or some great art.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: this game doesn't come as a high recommend, but its good enough by the end. combat is horrible, traversal isn't as fluid as you'd like, and the enemy variety is lame - what carries this game is the world and the lore around it, and the meaning behind the ending. if you like platformers with minimal challenge, this is an ok 5-6 hours of gameplay. i dont think i saw a single character in the game wearing jeans which is also a knock against it, so consider that before purchasing.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: I don't even know what to say, this was such an experience, there is no way to summarize this game that fully does it justice. I was on the edge on my seat through the entire ending, I was so anxious and excited to see what was going to happen next.The gameplay is so incredibly unique I've never played anything quite like it before, I had tons of fun exploring these environments and unveiling their secrets. The characters are such a great addition to the environments and the stories they told as well, I highly enjoyed interacting with them and watching their lives unfold bit by bit.Rei herself is such a fantastic character as well, she has so much depth to her, my feelings about her shifted as I played through the game, I loved her then I hated her, but by the end everything came together and I was able to understand and empathize with her.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: As many who bought this game, I came here after Hyper Light Drifter entered my favorite games of all time list.Solar Ash isn't bad on its own. But nowadays, so many games are just that so it ends up being forgettable.I think that while a lot of the same elements are back, the very cohesion of it all that made HLD blew my mind isn't there on this project. Because the game is different, the same formula actually misses its target. For example I think Disasterpeace fits completely with the mystery and cryptic narration of HLD but after one playthrough there was no moment in SA that I remember his music to have hit me. Maybe the fact that there are dialogues? very defined visual elements in a 3D world as opposed to pixel-art?Hard to tell.Once again, it's still enjoyable so if you want to play it, then play it because you will probably enjoy something in it. But if you're expecting to buy a masterpiece, it's not.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Review so far: I've seen a lot of people complain of stuttering issues, which made me nervous. In my 4.5 hours of playtime right now, I have not once experienced stuttering. If you thoroughly enjoyed "The Pathless" you will love this game. The mechanics and setup of this game are very similar. I picked up this game because I haven't been disappointed by the handful of games I've played that Annapurna has published. Secondly, I wanted to play this game because I found the art style breath taking, and that too has been astonishing. I highly recommend this game to anyone who played and enjoyed "The Pathless", "Outer Wilds" and or "Journey". This game so far has made my Top 5 list of the best relaxing and adventuring games I've played.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Solar Ash was an interesting experience, if there was one word to describe the game, it would be "minimal." You traverse through a vast world that is split into different areas by skating around while you do some light platforming and in certain areas some minor environmental puzzles. The movement of the game feels very nice and fluid and the controls are tight and responsive. There are side quest and these catches that you can collect that unlock suits for you to use with different abilities and lore of the game. I enjoyed the design of the different suits a lot and just overall the design of this game as a whole. The world you're in is very beautiful to look at and at times I would just stand for a bit to take it all in, the graphics are definitely a highlight of this game. Oftentimes the game felt relaxing while I skated and explored as the atmosphere and the soundtrack complimented the game very well.There is very minimal combat, it does happen but it is not the focus of the game. However, every area has a boss. The bosses you fight are what can only be described as Shadow of the Colossus-esq type fights and to me was my main drive to complete this game and see what I had waiting for me in the next area. These were the most enjoyable part of the game for me.I do have some issues with it, such as I wish the skating was just automatic instead of having to hold down a button the whole time, you will be spending the whole game holding down the skate button as there are no reasons not to. The currency was a bit pointless since you only use it to gain extra hitpoints, which you lose one every time you clear an area, so you would have to rebuy it, you do get a lot of it and there's plenty to go around even after beating the game but I would of liked to have seen it been used in other ways.  The side quest were also a bit underwhelming but they are optional and do extend the playtime. The world map was also not that great and it would of been nice to see details of the areas you were in, I had to complete a side quest by visiting the npc in a certain spot and I had no idea where it was because the map does not show anything besides just the names of the main areas you unlocked and how they connect.Its a neat game, I think its a very nice and relaxing experience and if you are into Fast Traversal Platforming Narrative-Driven games with Shadow of the Colossus type bosses, then this is the game for you. Its not very long, it took me 8 hours to 100% but that is no issue for me. However, it might be for you, so if anything pick it up on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is beautiful and Disasterpeace's music is nice to hear again after so long, although it sounds more environmental and subdued rather than having strong melodies like in the previous game which worries me a bit.The performance is bad even on a 4090 in 1440p. I don't know why it struggles so much during boss fights, going below 40 sometimes with several hitches. I don't know why, it doesn't look like a taxxing game.I also don't like how the story is conveyed so far. Hyper Light Drifter was pretty much silent, no one talked in that game. In a way, it felt even more puzzling than Dark Souls and Outer Wilds, perhaps too much even, but the approach they've seem to have taken here is not at all to my tastes.The protagonists makes remarks to herself about what is going on and what she should be doing like Alloy in Horizon. "Wow that's a big monster", "I can't use this yet", "I bet I could use this ability to get past this", "I wonder whats behind this".It's annoying, it doesn't respect my intelligence, like I'm spoonfed what I should care about and what I should do. _childDocuments_.review: A visually stunning game with fluid movement and a beautifully desolate setting. The game has an intriguing and self-contained plot that is fun to gradually piece together. The scale is grandiose and overwhelming, and does the boundless void of cosmos justice. You feel as small and lonely as you think you would when entire planets are on the line.The controls are smooth, and moving Rei feels great! Like, you could ignore the main objective and still have a blast just screwing around because the game is so darn fun to play. Combat takes a back seat, which works in the game's favour, in my opinion. Despite that, the boss battles are grandiose and exciting, and feel like a combination of parkour and Shadow of the Colossus.While relatively straightforward in progression, the game has collectibles to find and characters to help, making for a great diversion from the main goal as you dash off the beaten track. Finding the Voidrunner Stashes and getting suit upgrades, as well as gradually learning about the rest of Rei's crew felt rewarding. You also find diary pages scattered in the wildest places, feeding the player bits of lore. The game is close to perfect as is. I only wish there was a way to keep track of found and missing diary pages.If you love space, stories about overcoming trauma, and prefer fast movement and exploration to deep combat mechanics, this game should be on your radar! Pros:- Fantastic visuals, a sheer joy to take in the sights- A spectacular scale that invokes feelings of cosmic isolation and loneliness- Controls are butter smooth- Fast and simple combat- A wonderful soundtrack- Interesting plot that doesn't step outside its boundaries- Lots of secrets to find- Best girl Rei <3Cons (not really)- No way to track found and missing diary pages

_childDocuments_.review: This game is mediocre at its best moments, and most of the time it is not at its best. Hyper Light Drifter is one of my favorite games of all time, and it baffles me that this mess was made by the same people. It seems that with the success of their first game, Heart Machine wanted to shoot for "bigger and better", but sometimes less is more.Instead of HLD's understated environmental storytelling, this game's story is told via dialogue trees composed almost entirely of forced exposition and bad jokes delivered by terrible voice actors. On top of that, Rei is constantly talking to herself as a thinly veiled means of tutorializing, which is one of my biggest pet peeves in gaming.Instead of focusing on combat like HLD, the gameplay is mainly focused on platforming. This would be fine, except for two things:1. There is still combat in this game, and it is atrocious. Rei's moveset is extremely limited, and the way she moves does not gel with the way the enemies move. Combat encounters generally felt like minor annoyances rather than engaging battles.2. The movement is almost as clunky as the combat. The arc of Rei's jump is fixed and she retains a significant amount of momentum from running, which  often made me overshoot platforms and rails. In general the levels and bosses seem to require a level of precision that the mechanics simply don't afford you, which made me feel like I was fighting the controls moreso than the monsters.It's a shame because I really like the core gameplay loop in concept: You start the level by platforming around to find black goo, destroy the black goo to awaken the boss, and then grapple onto the boss and strike at its weak points Shadow-of-the-Colossus-style. But the aforementioned lack of precision coupled with the strict time limits between weak points just broke the experience for me.In the end, the only strengths that carried over from HLD to this game are the visual aesthetic and the music. But neon colors and grimy synths can only carry the game so far. Everything else the game has to offer is done leagues better by other games. If you're looking for a good platformer, just play A Hat in Time instead. If you're enticed by the giant monster boss fights, just play Shadow of the Colossus instead. Don't waste your time with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Not everyone is gonna absorb a game's atmosphere the same as you, especially if you're not able to fully immerse yourself within one's fictional world. Thankfully  had no difficulty setting the mood for its world and environments, establishing the massive scale of all five locations within the Ultravoid. You're able to see previous and upcoming areas, along with the Starseed, from wherever you're standing.  previous game,  multilayered music tracks return, scaling progression off of how far you've traversed a level, or what phase you're fighting a boss on. Exploring open environments with a movement system that is fast and fluid is akin to the early 3D Mario games, while the gravity-bending planets and quiet atmosphere just screams  Taking on the gigantic Remnant boss fights after completing an area's gameplay loop is also reminiscent of This game delivers on so many levels and tells an extremely important message about letting go of the past and moving forward, while dealing with themes of loss, loneliness, and desperation among others. But it also manages to hit the mark on a personal level. Not many games manage to give me full-body goosebumps on multiple occasions, or to even make me shed a tear, but this definitely accomplishes that.  feels like a vivid idea I dreamt up as a culmination of specific sources of media from my childhood, and manages to deliver one of the best original 3D platformers I've ever played. (and yeah I may have enjoyed it more than HLD, but  still BANGS)

_childDocuments_.review: i think this game rewired my brain. the colors are very bright and in your face but in the best way that creates incredibly beautiful and alien scenes; the artstyle and aesthetic is incredibly unique to the point that it feels like you're playing through a surreal painting; the world is immersive and intriguing; the controls are fine tuned to give an incredibly satisfying sense of gliding through the game. the only agruably lackluster aspect of the game is the story (though i still found it enjoyable), but i feel like the game revolves more around offering an immersive dreamlike world to experience (on which it very much delivers) than telling an impactful story, so i didn't have a problem with it.the game's challenge lies more in maximizing efficiency and speed as opposed to learning and mastering a complex combat system. this drove me away from it for a while, as it's a bit of an unfamiliar playstyle to me (and i'm sure i'm not the only one), but i can say with confidence that when i finally mustered the courage to give it a chance, i fell in absolute love. it's certainly not for everyone, but it's definitely in my top games, and i'd absolutely recommend giving it a chance.oh, and if you can, play with a controller! it makes all the difference.EDIT i take back everything i said about the story this game's story is perfect and flawless for me specifically

_childDocuments_.review: This is a painful thumbs down and refund request after Hyper Light Drifter (HLD), I really wanted to support Heart Machine. I will summarise at least the first hour of this game as "sparse" (1st area and boss + some of second area). Most people seem to like it, but after I got bored and went to read reviews, it doesn't look like much changes. I was going to write a longer review, but I cut most of it to try and keep it brief.I say "sparse" because there wasn't much to do except collect orbs to top up your 5 hit points (which get depleted after each boss). Sometimes you encounter bits of story in the game world that suggest post-apocalypse, but don't say anything different to other games with this theme, it's just people the player doesn't know doing stuff I didn't care about - it didn't hook me. Despite the bold art style, for the first hour there wasn't much compelling about the visuals. Unlike the melting titans of HLD and their decayed remains in the game world, there wasn't much visual interest in the very abstract world design of buildings sitting on a big cloud area. Orientation in the game world felt frustrating because nothing casts clear shadows and cel shading makes it kind of flat. Also, the camera is entirely manual, which makes you realise most games subtly direct it at enemies or points of interest - there is no lock on to help with this. This is important because you need to do precision jumping to beat bosses (which is, for the first boss, a timed platforming skill check sequence, not a combat encounter) but you can't always tell where you are in the game space and the camera doesn't point down to show the platforms you need to see, meaning I died because I couldn't always tell where I'd land.If all that sounds fine to you, please enjoy. Otherwise, hold out for their next game and hope it's closer to the majesty of HLD.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a combination of both The Pathless and Shadow of the Colossus and whilst the latter parts are fantastic, the The Pathless parts, just like in said game, suck. Or at least I didn't like them, what do I know.Game works like this: it has a fantastic opening, it looks seriously good and the sound design is solid. You are introduced to the first giant and after you beat it, you feel like a god.Then the next area opens up, and you have to "summon" the next giant by destroying these sort of eyes scattered throughout the map. It's a big map so you have to navigate it surfing through the waves, defeating enemies and doing some very very light puzzles. Okay cool, you do that, next colossus shows up, the fight feels really good and then... new section with the same gameplay loop.And that gameplay loop I just described isn't good. It's simple and tedious and the gameplay is not always super tight and you end up falling through large areas or getting killed by a monster just because the controls aren't doing what you're telling them to do. For me, all the parts except the giants were extremely boring. In fact, I got stuck trying to decipher how to get through a certain section and when I looked at a walkthrough video and saw that I was still on hour one out of four I let out a big sigh.It's a shame 'cause the game has a lot of potential and it is in fact much better than The Pathless but I feel like every Shadow of the Colossus clone that I play is trying to innovate the formula in a way that just doesn't do it (I'm looking at you Praey for the Gods). I appreciate developers trying new stuff, but I don't think this is the way. I wasn't having any fun in the traversal parts and the gameplay loop was extremely repetitive.3/5 - Meh

_childDocuments_.review: It's good, that's for sure. But... I'm never going to experience another masterpiece like Hyper Light Drifter, nothing will ever come close again, and I'll be chasing my dreams of 2016 forever. I had a feeling it would be like that, but the direction of Heart Machine confirms it for me, that the spirit of this studio is axiomatically different from where it started, and 99.99% of people who enjoy the same things as me enjoy them for fundamentally different reasons to the point where I don't have much if any hope for being passionate about anything new that comes out. Even if it's in the spirit of, or by the creators of my favourite things.If you're part of that 00.01% like me, the one in ten thousand who cares *differently*, then I share that dreamy sorrow with you, this game is not going to capture your heart much after all. If you're everyone else, you will think this game is pretty cool and enjoy it just fine, get it. If you think I'm being edgy or melodramatic, it's not like we could communicate much anyway so you should probably listen to someone else. I'm open for (some) discussion if anyone wants to. Discussion, not debate. My opinions are pretty well formed and firm. I'm reaching out a hand to you 00.01% for your taste.

_childDocuments_.review: The enemy I found myself fighting the most in this game is the one you can't defeat:  the camera.  I gave up trying to wrestle with my view during the boss fight against the Withered Eye, which takes place on a very small moon (reminiscent of a boss fight from Super Mario Galaxy but without the charm).  Unfortunately, the camera can't decide where the horizon is supposed to be so it's constantly pointing up into the sky when I need to see where I'm skating, either on the ground or when scaling the boss.  What should have been a 15 minute dash from weak point to weak point to kill point ended up being dash to weak point, camera points skyward, touch molten lava part of boss, die and respawn ad nauseum.  The only balm to this tedium is that other than wasting time, there is no real penalty.  I was free to keep trying the last stage of any failed boss fight for a theoretical eternity, banging my head against the wall of broken camera the whole time.For a game that is so dependent on platforming and ridiculous timing it needs either better active camera control, or a passive camera controlled entirely by the player.  What it has now is exactly the worst combination of neither.[edit]I should point out that the soundtrack is outstanding.  Definitely worth buying on its own.[/edit]

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal game that I took way too long to pick up. It's short, ~7 hours to 100%. The story had me guessing what was happening till about 80% through the game, and I was fully engaged trying to piece together what exactly is the Ultravoid. The finale was amazing, satisfied everything I could want from a Heart Machine story. The gameplay didn't change at all throughout the game, but it didn't bother me once. The movement is fluid and engaging, and the game isn't long enough for anything to get too repetitive. The story was what kept me engaged, the in-between did its job at firing the dopamine receptors. The game is a platformer, combat only exists to be a small obstacle. Each area added new depth to platforming, so job done in my book. The world was beautiful, and awesome to explore. Real mastery of level design. Every secret is naturally found, hints along the way. I always got that "Aha" moment finding the last few logs in an area, but never was frustrated.  The side quests are perfect in difficulty, I usually get annoyed in story heavy games like this, but each one helped me piece together what the ending was going to be like. I also loved the voice acting. I saw some negative reviews that the quips took away from the experience, but I honestly believe it wouldn't be the same without the personification of Rei. The story wouldn't work without Rei being her own person, and her not being vocal about her surroundings leads to her just being another self-insert. It showed Rei's light-hearted personality in the face of death (and adds impact to the emotional moments, where that facade cracks when she finds each runner). Overall, easily one of my favorites of all time. Seriously had me drop everything and play through it for 7 hours straight. I haven't done that since the release of Hollow Knight.

_childDocuments_.review: Solar Ash totally nails its mesmerizing visuals, sweeping electronic soundtrack, and dancer-like movement. Skating your way through floating islands never stops looking like trailer fuel. The twists and turns of the landscapes flow naturally with the simple yet precise fluidity of chaining jumps, dashes, slashes, and grinds. Even so, the game’s well-designed core is held back by the absence of meaningful mechanical growth to accompany the player’s skill and mirror the environmental diversity that’s seen throughout the journey.Put simply, the introductory moveset stays the same and the environment hardly demands much more than what it expects from you at the beginning. I just wish that the platforming, and combat, had taken the opportunity to evolve impactfully throughout the course of the game. Nothing too complicated, just a new core mechanic or two sprinkled in to complement the allure of possibility held within exploring each beautiful location. Even the game’s massive bosses could use a little spice to emphasize the player’s progress as well as to help conceptually differentiate them from each other.Oh, and perhaps there should’ve been a few tweaks to UI or landmarks in order to make navigating in some areas more intuitive. I didn’t mind missing tall jumps or a bit of clueless backtracking since I still enjoyed controlling Rei, I just would’ve preferred to have not been unintentionally off-task for longer than I expected.Despite not being as meaty of a game as you'd expect, Solar Ash is constantly captivating. Maybe it's the sort of game you want to replay on occasion simply because of how natural it feels to move around in this gorgeous world. Heart Machine's transition from 2D to 3D here is impressive. Watching the developers bring their outstanding pixel art into a 3D setting is odd yet appealing. Solar Ash was great and it easily has me excited to see how Hyper Light Breaker will play out.

_childDocuments_.review: I've now beaten the game, all I have left are the two achievements for <3 hour completion and hardcore completion. And I've got to say, it's a good game. It's certainly a shorter game as you can see by my playtime, but its a good few hours. The movement is extremely fluid throughout all the tricks, and as you go through the areas more environmental obstacles and enemies are introduced, keeping things interesting as you play. I found the story and lore to be not exactly engaging, but fun to read. There's the plain story of how the Ultravoid and Starseed and all of that work and the ending of the game, but there's more information if you keep looking. There's a series of journals around the map that tell the tale of an adventurer, there's caches stashed everywhere that tell the tale of fellow Voidrunners, and there's even 3 character-based sidequests that tell you about the tragedies of the Ultravoid. Overall, it'd say its a good game, and rate it maybe an 8/10, but definitely wait for a sale as I don't think its worth the $40 price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful, fluid 3D platformer by the developers of Hyper Light Drifter (one of my favorite games ever). Skating around the Ultravoid is a joy, but the lack of any unlockable abilities or additional powers is somewhat disappointing. It's also surprisingly linear for a game with no mechanical progression: the world is split into distinct areas (with non-linear objectives), and you must complete each area in a set order. It doesn't detract much from the experience, and it does allow for a much tighter difficulty curve, but I did find myself missing the free-form exploration found in HLD. Nevertheless, the world design is absolutely incredible both to look at and navigate through. There are quite a few other games similar to this one in many ways (The Pathless, Sonic Frontiers, Wavetale), but this one probably has them all beat when it comes to world design. Can't wait for Hyper Light Breaker!

_childDocuments_.review: Solar Ash is truly special. It's extremely rare I'll play a game through in one sitting, but everything about it, from the genuinely awe-inspiring audio and visual design, to the world it takes place in, to the affecting and sincere story, are crafted with such verve, care and imagination.If Hyper Light Drifter was an ambitious first game for Heart Machine, Solar Ash feels like their moonshot artistic statement. It is without doubt one of the greatest games I have ever played, and it's a genuine shame Annapurna let it linger the Epic Store for a whole year.

_childDocuments_.review: Solar Ash marks a significant departure from Hyper Light Drifter, and I have mixed feelings about it.Judging the game on its own merits, it is undeniably fun with a serviceable story and brilliant mechanics. However, compared to Hyper Light Drifter, several notable changes stand out:Story:I have mixed feelings about the story. Unlike Hyper Light Drifter, which hinted at a greater narrative without fully explaining it, Solar Ash is more straightforward. This shift may or may not appeal to you, depending on your preference for storytelling.Transition from 2D to 3D:The move from 2D to 3D is another mixed bag. The developers have done an excellent job translating the mechanics, and the main character is a joy to control. However, the addition of a third dimension introduces complexity. Navigating to certain areas can be tedious at times, though the overall experience remains enjoyable.Secrets:The approach to secrets is also different. In Solar Ash, secrets are fewer and harder to miss but are crucial for understanding the full story. This contrasts with Hyper Light Drifter, which had numerous, well-hidden secrets that felt more rewarding to discover. Again, this depends on your personal preference.Overall, Solar Ash is a fun game with its own unique strengths, but it inevitably draws comparisons to Hyper Light Drifter. Whether you'll enjoy these changes depends on what you value more in a gaming experience.I think Solar Ash won't stick in my mind as much as Hyper Light Drifter did (for whatever that is worth)

_childDocuments_.review: Like other Annapurna published games, this game was a lovely story experience that can be beaten in a couple sittings. It is about 8-10 hours to beat depending on how much exploring you do for collectibles, so you may want to wait for a sale if $40 seems too steep for that.
