_childDocuments_.review: The game has fantastic visuals, the story is interesting, but I'll never know how it concludes since the optimization is inexcusably poor. It's as if it was ported to PC with zero thought or care. I was getting massive frame rate drops that made it unplayable after I defeated the first boss. It has potential, but the developers need to get off their butts and patch it. It's unbelievable that it's been left in this state for unsuspecting players to find. I am beyond disappointed. I got far enough in to be interested to see where it went and then this happens and it's unplayable out of nowhere. Thankfully it stopped working before I couldn't send it back. Pure, flaming garbage. Try it on another platform MAYBE. No one cares when a game comes to PC. Massive let down. Thanks for nothing.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: With some fast-paced gameplay and stellar graphics, Solar Ash invokes the feeling of games such as Shadow of the Colossus with the sprawling anomalies you're tasked with destroying. The combat, while simple, feels instantly gratifying which only gets better with the different unlockable suits. It's not a long game by any means, with my all-storylines playthrough taking a total of 7 hours my first time (on PS5), but it's still absolutely worth it for the experience alone.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: It's alright. The movement feels nice but is also very simple and doesn't have much nuance to it but the areas are super well designed and fun to navigate. The story, exists, I guess? I didn't care much for the characters and most of the dialogue didn't feel like it had much to say. The music is nice but not super noticable, and visually the game is really cool looking, especially Mirrorsea and the Broken Capital. BIG WARNING THOUGH, I'm not sure what's up with the game's optimization, and maybe this is my fault, but the stats on the steam page are super inaccurate for the minimum specs. I tried playing this on a gaming laptop that far exceeded even the recommended specs, and the game lagged REALLY badly. It was only after building a proper desktop pc that I was actually able to finish the game. Overall its a pretty fun experience, but it's not super incredible, and at full price it's not really worth it, but if the game ever goes on sale and it looks fun, it's pretty worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the visuals, and when the game opened up, it really had a great feel of speeding around. However, the camera angles and enough imprecision or frustration was apparent, especially the camera at times, that it felt like the game kept getting in it's own way. The story elements were fine, but didn't really add to the experience too deeply, which is a shame. I think there was a 10/10 potential in this game, but I really have to give it a conditional recommendation: if you want a highly stylistic, brightly colored game that lets you zip around and fight colossi, and don't mind a little jank, then this is worth it. If you really want another taste of Hyper Light Drifter (like I did), it's ultimately worth it. I guess I'm saying this game is fine, and the most frustrating thing (other than the camera), is that you can tell it could have been great.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Went into this game expecting a fun, fast-paced parkour type of game and left crying. The environments are SO beautiful, the combat is a lot of fun, and I really enjoyed solving the puzzles. The worlds never felt overwhelming to me, they actually left me excited to keep exploring after I 100%ed it!I do wish the game had an FOV slider as it made me a bit motion sick at times. I also hope they optimize the game for the Steam Deck because it would be the PERFECT handheld game, but it runs a bit choppy on there.Truly a beautiful experience, and a game I was honored to play at least once in my life.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Stylish and pretty platformer game. If you played Hyper Light Drifter, you'll recognize the haunting music and post-apocalyptic artstyle, but unfortunately combat is a much lower priority for this game. No enemy takes more than a handful of hits and bosses are more platforming challenges now, illustrating the game's quick and agile movement. If the boss fights and pixel artwork was the main draw for HLD, you might be disappointed. But the exploration and world are still strong here, and so for those players, this is a solid recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game of smooth and seamless movement, very slick animations, and amazing vistas. The art direction in is gorgeous, the chatty mc is fun (though I miss the silent contemplation of HLD) and the gameplay is consistently fun and smooth. Gameplay itself is like a significantly more open and modernized version of your favorite 3D platformers from the 90s and 00s. I literally have nothing bad to say about this game other than I wish it was expanded out to a 20 hours game, but if it was I probably would not have played it in the first place. At 7 hours of playtime I think this game has hit the perfect length to feature set balance. There aren't many abilities, and there aren't really upgrades (though there are suit side-grades) but that arguably helps sell the playability of the game. Its <10 hours, you deserve to play and <10 hour game over the weekend.This game gives me confidence that whatever Heart Machine puts out next will be even better, this is clearly only as good as it is due to being their first 3D game, and we saw what they could do with HLD.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVED IT! It has a great story, voice acting is amazing. It is a very fluidly fun game to play. I would say it isn't that difficult, but the experience was still absolutely worth it. The game play didn't change much, but what the game play WAS was amazing. If you do try it, and liked how the beginning felt, you will end up loving the rest. Yes, the mechanics don't change, but the way in which you use the mechanics does, in a very cool way. The world is super fun to get lost in. It is a bit big, but not too big. Overall, highly recommend this, especially on sale. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Machine Heart always seems to the best experiences when it comes to games. I'd argue with both Solar Ash and Hyper Light Drift, its more of an experience than a game and for that only I can't recommend this game enough to anyone. It has its flaws such as camera movement and some glitches but that doesn't diminish the experience
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that has a surprisingly calming effect to it. Highly appreciate the movement tech, you smoothly traverse the map with great speed and flow- grinding on rails is a good time too. The story telling is short and sweet-cutscenes and collecting the collectibles help expand on the story. Boss fights are similar to each other throughout, but it never  repetitive. All in all, gg.Also a great game to speedrun as well!
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: like The Pathless but good.but seriously, this game is awesome. it's like how i wish breath of the wild had been (or the pathless, or any number of others), and how i wish more open world games would be designed. vibrant art, satisfying controls and a world worth exploring. never felt like a waste of time or a chore, even the times it frustrated me.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Great story with certain characteristics that I'm a sucker for. Environments are well crafted and exploration is encouraged. For the most part the feel is smooth and fun, though occasionally I got frustrated by the nature of speed vs precision 3D. Very much looking forward to playing Hyper Light Breaker next.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely incredible. I do have a few notes, though.For starters, if you are susceptible to motion sickness when playing games, this game may not be for you. Due to the way the world is designed, the camera can often move in strange ways in order to keep up with the player as they move through the world and experience the changes in gravity, similarly to Super Mario Galaxy, though on a more open scale rather than clusters of small planetoids. That said, if you can get past the motion sickness, this game is very much worth playing. Aside from the incredible story, the game controls incredibly smoothly and the combat and movement both feel incredibly fluid. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: ...Neat. This one had a hard time before it could grow on me. But give Solar Ash a chance. The game's world is split into areas, and by the third or fourth area the game designers and artists start to show off seriously impressive vistas and level designs. The way later levels focus on vertical *and* gravity bending platforming are nothing to scoff at. Although... something I will scoff at are the "black goo" challenges.Black goo can be climbed and will slow you down when on foot. Challenges make clever use of quickly scaffolding or avoiding the black goo to hit checkmarks in time based challenges that progress each area. These were oddly frustrating to me and I almost dropped the game at some of these. Of course, they're not THAT bad but sheesh they're completely at odds with the kind of momentum based gameplay that shines through the rest of the game. SEGA should hire Heart Machine to design the next 3D Sonic game because they could probably nail the kind of speed based platforming Sonic requires.The game is at it's peak with each area's boss fight. You're scaffolding giant bosses and skating across their backs while carefully managing your momentum to avoid gaps. There are similar speed/momentum challenges in each level's regular gameplay, too. It's super fun to skate around as Rei and thwack bad guys at top speed. All in all, this is a solid 3D platformer with superb visuals. If you have a beefy PC and a pretty screen then you've gotta pick this one up.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, not a bad game. It is quite short but the boss fights in general are very satisfying. The movement can be a little wonky from time to time but for the most part is pretty smooth. The art is beautiful throughout the game and each place in the game feels very unique despite there not being many different mechanics between them. Will definitely go back and complete all the achievements. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: I played it and finished it on my Xbox through Game pass and I have one word for it.. Beautiful.I love the game and I recommend it, however if you seek an experience with good combat then maybe not get the game as its more into movement and story. Although I enjoy the simple combat and fun bosses in the game. I think 7 or 8/10 is a good placement.Highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun platformer; story takes some inspiration from Bastion and gameplay from Sonic the Hedgehog. I enjoyed the platforming, art, and story which were all very engaging. The music is subdued, intentionally I'm sure, but doesn't leave much impression as a result. Took me around 11 hours to complete with collecting all the suits, and completing all the sidequests, but the main game can be beat in under 3 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: A stunningly beautiful game in more both story and artstyle. I didn't know much about the game going into it, but by the end, my heart was aching from the storytelling. The gameplay is fast and fluid, but not too punishing. If you're a fan of Jet Set Radio and Bomb Rush Cyberfunk, you'll be in for a treat here. Story-wise, they're very different, but the movement feels similar.This game doesn't receive enough attention in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic story, fantastic game play, fantastic setting, fantastic visuals. This honestly just makes me even more hyped for hyper light breaker. If you liked hyper light drifter, you will love this. Same Heart Machine vibes, soundtrack is amazing of course, and they again nail the hyper pop, neon aesthetic. Wonderful concise experience. However, screw the black goo, that is all.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game. I get to go zoom zoom and vroom vroom across an incredibly beautiful and surreal landscape, and the gravity is so deliciously malleable. The feeling I get when I finish a platforming section only to realize that the game has turned completely upside-down is something I've yet to experience in any other game. The puzzles can get a bit dull, but the landscape changes succeed at inspiring awe at every turn. If you like platformers, you'll probably love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Mario Galaxy like gravity in a high-contrast neon, glow-infused skater platformer.Beautiful visuals with nearly every area and vista perfect for screenshots accompanied by ambient and sweeping synthetic scores to highlight the danger and beauty of each biome.The skating of the game has very good momentum and grinding along ruins or beams of curved light has an a-plus camera to correct as you slide and see more of what the levels have to offer.Costumes for varied styled of gameplay to be collected while you complete each areas hidden lore and nice finisher cinematic for each boss area.The story is gleaned mostly through log entries and the occasional check-in with an cybernetic companion that assists you as you play through the game. While I didn't find it too engaging, there's enough to keep momentum as you play.While I would not classify this as a long game, it is a beautiful platforming starscape of cosmic visuals.Strongly consider purchasing if it is for sale, or if you are a fan of physics and skate controls in a neon drenched cosmic environment that Heart Machine is so VERY well known for.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like gliding like you got permanent skates on?Do you like riding giant monsters while slicing them like that one Shadow of Colossus game?Did you love Hyper Light Drifter and didn't realize this is the same developer? Oh, you already knew that?But you didn't play it as it's just sitting in your backlog?!!!Ok I'm not finishing this review until you realize what you've missing out on.Solar Ash is basically just drifting across a diverse planet with simple combat that might be too easy and casual for me but the style and unique boss fights help carry it as we haven't seen since something evolve upon the formula since 2005. Actually a   did come out around the same time that is rather close, tough to decide which one to get? Why not both.When you spend 20 hours to make a video and decide not release it. I'll put it here so I don't regret the time wasted.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful adventure that defies space and gravity, and even time itselfA must playMovement is fluid and satisfying with a few odd moments. Combat is simple and a little barren, however you don't need to rely to much on it, only pay attention on the timing between your attacks because that affects the flow of some bosses.Visually impressive, making you imerse yourself in that world and the music adds so much to that feeling. The shadow of the colossus boss battles are fun and manage to have a little variety (while being in essence the same thing).The story is interesting but not enough to grab your attention and make you care about what is happening. For a game about feeling and movement it is packed with text that can harm the flow of the experience. Less is more
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: I can't say I've 100%'d many games, I can count them on one hand - but this is one of them. If you enjoy flow state games with an emphasis on movement and traversal, this is for you.If you like a nice little story, one that doesn't make you think too hard but still offers a few twists and turns that keep you engaged, this is for you.If you need engaging combat, this game is not for you - the combat is a little dull, it's there in case you want to engage in it but it's the same basic 3 hit combo the whole game through, the traversal, movement, story, and unique art style are what sets this game apart - not it's combat system.

The music and fragmented 3D world are absolutely stellar. Personally I enjoy experiencing events without being told what is happening in HyperLight style. _childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot get enough of this game, first session and couldn't put the controller down, 14+h later i realised i spent the whole day on this game hahaThe flow of the movement feels natural and has a really good flow, just needs a bit getting to used to. Now I cant really finish my review without also mentioning how freaking beautiful this game is. Everywhere you look you will probably see something jaw dropping. My screenshot folder has tons of desktop worthy views. The fighting is where i have a slight problem with but this might just be skill issue. the camera feels too Janky during battles, especially during boss fights. Idk how many times I've had to retry some of the sections because i couldn't see where the next target was. The boss battles themselves absolutely made me feel like a badass ninjaOverall this game has absolutely exceeded my every expectations. I knew it was going to be an amazing game because it was made all the amazing people that are Heart Machine9.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: The game is absolutely gorgeous and controls really well. The best way I can describe how it feels to play this game is Shadow of the Colossus on Ice, and it's amazing. The soundtrack is gorgeous and really adds to the game's sense of scale. It leaves you feeling small and in awe of the beauty of it's world while you desperately try to find a way to destroy it. The narrative left some room to be desired. Its plot was predictable, albeit still enjoyable and effective. The voice acting didn't quite land for me at times, and some of the side characters got on my nerves. A part of me wishes Heart Machine would have opted for an entirely visual method of storytelling like they did in Hyper Light Drifter, but giving the characters voices really did help drive home the game's themes, so I forgive the decision.The only problem is the price. Last I checked, this goes for $40 normally, and I can't recommend it in good faith at that price point. If you see it for somewhere closer to $25 or less it is 100% worth the pickup.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: I believe I'm nearing the end of Solar Ash and I must say I love nearly everything about this game.It oozes style and an identity all it's own. The story is interesting and asks you to think about what is going on. The game play is fun, simple, yet keeps you engaged. It reminds me a lot of The Pathless and that as well was a great game. I recommend you experience this game. I'm not even done and I know I want more.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth the price. It's short (5-6 hours), low replayability value, a bit janky and the initial charm starts to wear off by the last 2 hours, especially with the gameplay, it felt repetitive by the second half of the game ( there's not enough there to fully grasp the player). For me, most of the game's value comes from it's artistic presentation. The sceneries, the style, the design, it's all great, at least whatever is in the game. I wish the environments could be richer however, even though i'm aware of it's stylistic choices, and the narrative's context behind them. I still believe they could've pushed it further. I still recommend the game if can buy it 50% off or more, Asking almost 40 euros (43 usd) is insane for the product they're offering.

_childDocuments_.review: Only about an hour of playtime as of this review, but I feel like I have a good grasp of what the game has to offer already.This game was made by the creators of Hyper Light Drifter, a game that I like a lot but have yet to finish. The people at this game studio seem to know how to make good, fun games without stretching themselves too far and ending up with an unpolished product like many other developers.I really like the controls and the mechanics of the 'skating' with the Voidrunner that you play as - Rei. You traverse through a strange world. You collect other Voidrunner suits that grant you different capabilities that alter how you play a little bit. There is also a resource called Plasma that is typically placed in line patterns that you can skate through to collect, but you can also destroy certain boxes to collect them.Throughout the game, I've met and talked to other NPCs as well as inspected various things in the game that give the world a bit of lore. I can't remember every single detail, but Rei entered a black hole in an attempt to save it with something called a Starseed. So far it looks like whatever the Starseed was supposed to do to "undo" the black hole hasn't worked. Rei is trying to figure out how to fix it, which is what I think the plot of the game is? My memory is terrible.The art style reminds me a bit of other platformers from when I was younger, like the Jak and Daxter games. Solar Ash's color palette though is a bit more 'sci-fi', though. I really dig it, and it seems like Heart Machine is doing a similar style for their next game Hyper Like Breaker which I'm really looking forward to.Anyways, everything works very simple with great polish, which makes it a great game to just turn off your brain after work. Give it a go!
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Every detail, from the twisting worlds and the slimy beasts that haunt them, from the way Rei's relationship expands with Cyd to the bob in her step when back to the mission... every detail stuck with me. It led me to an ending where I could not stop crying. I don't think Solar Ash will ever leave my mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: A nice little game to sit back and relax with while listening to a podcast or chatting with a friend on an off-day or weekend. It's mostly chill and atmospheric with short sections of adrenaline, especially during the boss fights. They're always really satisfying to complete and give you a big dopamine rush. There's some occasional jank here and there but the overall experience is mostly polished and endearing with a heartfelt message at the end.Do consider giving it a shot if you're looking for something short and sweet to kill time with. 100%ing (in-game not achievements) only took me about 9 hours in total; it's really not a huge commitment. Though I'd say the price seems a bit high to me for a game of this little length and depth, so I recommend you pick it up on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game for people who love smooth movement, platforming and explorationThe artstyle of the game is beautiful, the designs are all great, it managed to really pull me inYou explore big open levels, find your way around them, collect semi-hidden collectibles for new suits, battle some Shadow of the Colossus type bosses.It's simple, but extremely satisfying and polished.I don't have a problem with short games, but i beat the game 100% in 6 hours. _childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: It's rather hard to give a concrete picture of Solar Ash, as it's a very peculiar game. It's controls are much stiffer than those of other platformers, yet many of the game's best moments are heavily based on flow and smooth movement at high speeds. Its art style blends a polygonal, cell-shaded look with highly contrasting colors in a way that I struggle to compare to any other games that I have played. The story is generally meant to take a backseat to gameplay, yet story scenes were some of the most engaging parts of the game. This game feels an enigma. None of these elements should work together.But they do.When this game is firing on all cylinders, all of its elements combine to create a truly one-of-a-kind experience, one that occasionally even exceeds the enjoyment found in games with far more budget and resources. This is not a poor man's Sonic Frontiers, often exceeding its closest competitor on a surprisingly frequent occasion. Unfortunately, however, it does suffer from the inevitable dilemma of any high speed platforming game. It's hard to have engaging platforming while going fast, and it's hard to go fast while platforming. Nonetheless, this game is still quite enjoyable, and if you have even a passing interest in 3D platformers, I recommend giving it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. It has been a pleasure from beginning to the end to skate through the levels, being amazed by the views and transported by the musics.The story is a bit hard to understand, especially in the first part, but it doesn't impact the pleasure to explore the environments and discover the secrets of the game.Probably in my top 3 this year.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Solar Ash was an interesting mix of Sonic the Hedgehog and Shadow of the Colossus.  Their traversal focused on quick movement and simple puzzle solving, and most of their combat was pretty bare bones, both of which I feel were good choices for the game they made.  The best parts of the game were the fights against the remnants - The Shadow of the colossus-style large enemy fights - As they provided challenge and large-scale spectacle that just isn't seen in most games.  I enjoyed the game overall, but I will say it got repetitive pretty quickly.  I also feel like some of their timers could have been tuned to be more generous.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing visuals and it feels great to skate around the broken void. _childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: A quite short yet wonderful experience. It's a shame that the heavy price has held me off of this game for so long, and I am glad that I bought it on sale.The Steam page screenshots don't entirely do the game's artstyle justice, it's stunning. It looks like Heart Machine have successfully transcended Hyper Light Drifter's visuals into 3D space. Even the skyboxes are impressive.The performance was perfect on even my raggedy old machine; My NVIDIA GeForce GTX 960 and 8GB of RAM handled this perfectly. No crashes, no lags.The combat is fun, consisting of skating, dashing, grappling and 3-hit combo melee combat, but maybe a tad too forgiving; Losing health means respawning, and "Dying" means the same thing except prolonged by a few secondsAlso I want ranged combat.The story is mind-blowing, dialogue and visuals convey a metaphore of moving on from tragedy and inner conflict or something, but even 100%-ing the game leaves a few questions open, such as;     If you understood any more of the story than I did, feel free to enlighten me.The soundtrack is great. Each area and scenario gets represented well by its accompanying music but I agree that it doesn't sound as cohesive as that of many other indie classics, which really isn't a huge issue.Summing up, definitely buy this but buy it on sale. While I root for Heart Machine and somewhat know what their founder goes through, I know you can't change your wallet's opinion with even the most tragic life story.

_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere of Solar Ash resembles an old PS2 collectathon platformer, from the minimalist shapes and textures to the distinct art styles of the zones and wacky characters. In the latter half of the game especially Solar Ash is at its strongest when you're skating at gravity-defying mach speed across beautifully desolate landscapes, searching for clues to escape the void and solving short, tight platforming gauntlets.Unfortunately this strength rarely makes an appearance. The earlier zones are uninspired compared to later ones, as well as NPCs and voice acting in general. The game takes so long to get up to speed that I almost dropped it halfway through because it seemed like they had run out of ideas already. Pacing-wise the introduction and expansion of new mechanics is too slow and too sparse and the first few levels barely have you doing anything that you hadn't already learned in the tutorial sections. World-building is similarly shallow, as if there is some deeper underlying context happening alongside the story it is neither compelling nor does it express itself well through the NPCs, clues and inspectable objects scattered throughout the game's areas. A couple of NPCs have such irritating voices and the writing is so boringly vague (in a style that people now love to attribute to Dark Souls), that I eventually decided to skip half of the dialogue and text for the rest of the game and allow the environments to do the storytelling which did actually improve the experience somewhat.Performance and optimisation is notoriously poor and I could barely hit a smooth 60fps on low settings, but this did not make it unplayable.The platforming gauntlets that serve as the game's main combat and progression have a wildly inconsistent difficulty level. The game is overall not excessively difficult, but some sections are a breeze on the first try and others seemingly leave you with milliseconds to complete tight jumps - spikes in difficulty that don't correspond with your progression through the game or specific zone as you'd expect. Their design is also often confusing, leaving me baffled when I have to make a split-second decision on which direction to dash to the next needle point. In this case the unique selling point of gravity-defying platforming comes at the cost of visibility where the indicator of where to go next is impossible to perceive because of depth-perception.Sound design is good where it exists, but several cutscenes and moments feel awkwardly silent in an oddly similar way to Kingdom Hearts, where you can forgive the latter because it's such a bizarre and uncanny game already. After Hyper Light Drifter the bar for another awesome soundscape was set high, but Solar Ash fails to deliver. Most of the tracks are forgettable, and the game is lacking enough grand musical flourishes that accented the vistas and setpieces of HLD. Issues with the soundtrack can be attributed to the departure of the original composer Disasterpiece during development due to issues out of either party's control, so hopefully Hyper Light Breaker will be back to full strength music-wise.Despite these criticisms the second half of the game has some banger levels, and the game overall has plenty of good moments that make it worth playing, but the whole time I felt like it could have been done better. I remain optimistic for Hyper Light Breaker and still believe that Heart Machine can once again strike gold.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Solar Ash is a perfectly fine game...and that kinda irks me. This is the latest from the people who made Hyper Light Drifter, and published by the group responsible for Stray, Outer Wilds, and The Pathless, and yet this one feels...off. Let me explain.GAMEFEEL: The game feels good to play, no doubt about it. While the movement can be punishing, especially during the bosses, it feels fluid and smooth, though it often demands a precision that is difficult at the speeds that you tend to move. The combat is VERY barebones, and you don't have any sort of upgrades, alternate weapons, or combos to allow it to be anything more than spamming two buttons. This would benefit greatly from some sort of enemy or weapon scaling, so the challenge is more than simply platforming-based, though that is by no means a fault. STORY: The story of Solar Ash is abstract, and that on its own is not a bad thing. HLD is famous for having a story that is incredibly vague (bird cult? death dog? Kwolok?), and upon starting the game, I expected much of the same: an opening cutscene, and little else. However, as I played, I was excited when that turned out to not be the case. It's the execution that annoys me. The other characters are interesting enough, but the fact that their fates are incredibly obvious takes away any sort of attachment. A prologue stage where you can see Rei interact with the other Voidrunners would make the dataentries you find far more interesting, and allow an emotional core to be more present. That way it would be 'what happened to the raccoon guy?' instead of 'who tf is Verse?' The story that is there is equally infuriating to me, with a main antagonist(?) who does nothing, and who you learn nothing about until the very end of the story. While the twist-barrage is interesting enough, you never feel like you're unraveling a story, instead of having the beats spelled out for you. When The Pathless had a story tacked onto an adventure, I was annoyed it was there, but when Solar Ash has it, I'm just mad.ART: The Game looks great. and the art style manages to do several things at once and somehow nails all of them. Even though the game is marketed as something entirely different, the gravity-bending and explorative nature reminded me a lot of Mario Galaxy, which is a great thing. The music, however,  The OST was made by like 4 different people, and thus feels just as disjointed, as well as being a lot less memorable than HLD. Disasterpiece did contribute, but the dissociative quality of a lot of their work simply isn't present here. OVERALL: 7/10, a great time if you don't think about it too much.

_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Been interested in this one since playing Hyper Light Drifter a while back as it's by the same devs.Functionally, it's a movement platformer that's easily compared to shadow of the colossus, but with an additional focus on exploration and story.While the core gameplay elements are fairly simple, the game's star of the show is the environment design and scenery - gravity itself is all over the place and you'll frequently find yourself upside-down or on what you thought was a wall. This is also one of those "if you can see it you can go there" games which I adore, especially paired with the level of exploration and stylised art design.I ended up getting 100% completion in my first playthrough, which was definitely worth it but felt natural enough that I didn't have to backtrack much or look anything up.In short, if you're a fan of Hyper Light Drifter's art and score, or looking for something in between a 3D sonic game and shadow of the colossus, you'll enjoy this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: The game really was an amazing experience. I was reluctant to play it as HLD is one of my favourite games and Solar Ash is very different from what I expected. Nonetheless I had a lot of fun and loved the story. My favourite bit has always been exploration and the game did not disappoint in that aspect. All in all, I am glad I finally gave it a go and happy to recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10: Solar Ash is a stylish puzzle platformer mixing together fluid skating, jumping, climbing, and grinding with an apocalyptic story and some big bosses that need their weak spots stabbed if you want to progress. Clear out the Remnants so you can activate the Starseed and save your planet! Coming from Heart Machine, the studio that created Hyper Light Drifter, Solar Ash adapts the studios style and color palette of magenta, cyan, black, and white to a 3D platformer experience. Although not combat focused compared to Hyper Light Drifter, Solar Ash does have some light combat against minor enemies you encounter on your way between collectibles and points of interest. Most of the games progress involves solving movement and platforming puzzles to reach specific points within certain time limits, resulting in you clearing up the dark goo that covers parts of the levels. Do this enough times and the local boss called a Remnant gets aggravated and comes down to give you a stern talking to. Even the boss fights are movement challenges involving quick maneuvering to weak points on their bodies, resulting in an overall feel like if Shadow of the Colossus were mixed with Super Mario and Tony Hawk.The story follows Rei, one of a team of Voidrunners sent to the black hole called the Ultravoid in order to keep it from destroying their planet by activating the Starseed, the games ultimate macguffin. After waking up alone it's on you to figure out what happened to your teammates and how to activate the Starseed. As you traverse the levels and clear up the the goo more of the story is revealed through a combination of your friendly AI CYD, the handful of locals that provide side quests, and the very reasonable duo of collectible items scattered about:  Voidrunner stashes and the notebook pages of Tarragon Danderpaws. The Voidrunner stashes are especially valuable as they provide not only recordings of the other Voidrunner members but suit portions as well, which are the main way to add new abilities to Rei such as doubling Plasma collection rates or improving the dash recharge rate.  The economy of Solar Ash is basic, with a single currency called Plasma that goes directly into increasing Rei's total shields. The solidified crystals give you large amounts of Plasma at once if you destroy them, but it is easy enough to restore broken shields through regular play that you won't need to go out of your way to get more Plasma. Just restore your existing capacity of shields by breaking the blue boxes found around the levels and you'll stay pretty safe. Even if you lose all your life though, the last respawn or checkpoint is rarely more than 5-10 minutes ago. Solar Ash is a great puzzle platformer about exploring the inner workings of a black hole and the motivations of Rei. Pairing a contrasting colors style with the darker, melancholy story of trying to save a doomed world, Solar Ash is good for 5-10 hours of low-pressure fun. If you're really looking for a challenge, pair up the two toughest achievements and try to finish the game in less than 3 hours on hardcore mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: tldr: 84/100 - A great speedy, action game with Shadow of the Colossus type bosses, a killer world to explore, and with deep and profound themes.Solar Ash is what would happen if a modern, 3D Sonic game was combined with an exploration game as well as Shadow of the Colossus...and it works really, really well! The action is fun and fast, it feels really good to get a grove on with your movement, and the action only occasionally veers into frustration, but in the best possible way. It is fun to overcome the bosses and the challenges which annoy you. The game, overall, is very forgiving, and if you make a mistake it doesn't send you too far back. The NPCs and the world are really cool and the setting for the game is AMAZING and super unique. The themes in the game are surprisingly deep and mature. I had not even heard of this game but was searching for good exploration games with cool worlds on a random YouTube video and found this game listed. The game is only 7 hours long (and that's with 100% completion), so you may want to wait for a sale as $40 is a bit much...but the game is high, high quality. Give them game a whirl if you love exploring strange worlds and cool, sci-fi stories! You won't regret it!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: I enjoyed Solar Ash due to its beautiful graphics, expansive world, and raw skill-based gameplay. Exploring the game's areas while skating around on hover boots is a blast, and collecting pink plasma caches is optional but rewarding. The protagonist, Rei, is endearing and well-voiced. The puzzles and boss battles were enjoyable, but the side quests felt unnecessary. Overall, the game is fun to explore and offers a good story for those who enjoy skating and solving puzzles. Rating: 8.2/10-I only gave Solar Ash a chance because Annapurna Interactive, the publisher, puts out some seriously top-notch games. Solar Ash joined my Steam library family after I got a nice discount from the Summer Sale and some gameplay footage from a few YouTube videos.I didn't understand the game's plot when I first started playing. The story escaped my attention completely. Usually, I don't pay attention to the stories in video games, but if I do, I know I'll have to play it again or watch the cutscenes or recordings again because they're so good! One of those games is this.After you finish the game, is there a reason to play it again? In my opinion, no. It's a one-and-done kind of game for me. The game's world is so expansive, though, that exploring it is a blast! Collecting the pink plasma found throughout the areas is a clever mechanic used in the game to encourage exploration. It is also very rewarding, so you can bet that you'll be doing it constantly. The best part, in my opinion, is that it is also optional. Another aspect of the game is that while you aren't required to find these "caches," as they are known, they greatly assist in making the game easier for you once you do find them all. You aren't required to find them, though, if you don't want to. I continued to collect them because they were helpful to me; however, if I had preferred to complete the game without collecting any, I could have done so.In essence, the entire game involves solving puzzles while skating around on what I believe to be hover boots on clouds and using platforms to ascend to higher clouds. The danger increases when the clouds vanish in other places. Have you ever played or heard of Praey for the Gods or Shadow of the Colossus? Yes, you will be scaling and skating atop enormous bosses of each area after solving the puzzles. The game's graphics are absolutely stunning, and riding a giant around just makes them look even cooler.What does the game look like? Beautiful. I adore how it looks. When you're exploring every area, it feels like you're in a planet, galaxy, or space. Some places even take on a sort of "you're in the sky" vibe. To put it mildly, each area has its own vibe, but mostly from what I sensed, it felt more like space and the universe to me.Rei, the protagonist, is a very endearing person. She initially didn't appeal to me because, well, who is she, right? However, as you take on her character, you can see what sort of person she is, and based on what I saw, I like characters like her. I think more people ought to aspire to be like her, lol. When Rei touches something she doesn't like, she'll often say, "Ugh," or "Ew," in disgust. This is one of the funnier things I like about her. She does find some moments where she laughs and giggles as she is riding rails while exploring the areas, despite the fact that the story and what she is going through is generally sad and distressing. The character was effectively brought to life by Rei's voice.This game's strength is what I like to refer to as how "raw" it is. The majority of it is skill. To proceed, you don't need to gather anything. Because you didn't "unlock" a special ability or power, you can proceed to the next area without returning to one that you have already cleared. Basically, just keep going and solve the puzzles until the boss shows up to play. It's really, really cool when you solve the game's puzzles but fail before you do so because, once you finally master the controls, it feels awesome to complete the skating, jumping, dodging enemies, and reaching the puzzle's core. It makes me want to go out and buy some skates and skate in the park.I played the game longer than the average amount of time recommended by the website How Long to Beat, which said it would take me 5.5 hours to complete. Given that I finished the game with a 93% completion rate, to me that indicates that I took my time. Considering how much fun this game was and how many other games I still needed to play, I searched for every cache and even maxed out my plasma at the end.In all honesty, this game is fun to explore. Sitting back and looking out over the lovely areas while ascending some buildings is really lovely. When you master the controls for this game, it's very calming and makes you feel cool.The side quests, last but not least, were something I didn't like or care for. I didn't see a reason to finish them. I'm not sure if they give you a reward or if you wanted to learn more about the side story from the main one, but I didn't need to finish them to feel like I "finished" the game. I found the main plot to be satisfying enough, but unlike gathering the plasma or finding the caches, there didn't seem to be a "reward" for finishing the side quests. I would have done them if they had added a special ability for aiding the other characters. Maybe one day, but not today, I'll achieve 100%.In the end, Solar Ash is a really good game that you should play at least once if you like skating around while looking cool and solving puzzles with a good story.-8/10 Fun - Great fun with occasional minor issues.8/10 Gameplay - Skating, grappling, and boss fights are excellent, but side quests weren't appealing.8/10 Length - Engaging but might be too long for some.8/10 Characters - Rei is likable, but others didn't stand out.9/10 Character Design - Impressive, except for one minor flaw.8/10 Voice Acting - Mostly well-done, except for one character I didn't like, Cyd's left arm with the two hands.9/10 Animations - Beautiful, with some minor glitches.7/10 Music - Not much remembered about the music.9/10 Graphics - Stunning visuals with attractive colors.8/10 Story - I paid more attention later and appreciated the ending.Overall: 41/50-Rating Meanings:0/10 - Completely Flawed / Empty1/10 - The Worst / Hated2/10 - Terrible / Really Disliked3/10 - Bad / Disliked4/10 - Insufficient / Not Okay5/10 - Indifferent / Half6/10 - Acceptable / Okay7/10 - Good / Liked8/10 - Great / Really Liked9/10 - The Best / Loved10/10 - Perfect / Full

_childDocuments_.review: Solar Ash is an interesting follow up to the incredible Hyper Light Drifter (HLD). It feels less tight as an experience than HLD (which I consider to be an almost perfect game) but is also more accessible. The bosses and world were fun to traverse. I found the momentum of the movement system very fun, similar to skateboarding or rollerblading games. At points I found some bosses a bit clunky, but never irritating. The story was also more straightforward than HLD with voiced characters and a more thoroughly explained setting, which could be a pro or a con depending on your preferences.The aesthetic was also super badass in terms of character designs and colour palettes with many throwbacks to HLD. I did find that the performance was a bit unstable for what was on display, but in general it did not detract from gameplay.Overall I really enjoyed Solar Ash, its always nice to see developers follow up a very successful game with something different, instead of an iteration of the prior success.

_childDocuments_.review: Really good, gives me huge Gravity Rush (1) vibes for some reason. The free form area based exploration with weird gravity on top of the boss designs all just feels like it took a lot of the great parts of GR and condensed it down. On that note, the story is pretty good and I like the interactions between Rei and Echo throughout the game, although Rei is a little thick headed. One problem I have is that while the 3 quest givers are pretty fleshed out, lobter man being the least, even if you ignore them, the game still acts like you know what's up with them in the ending cutscene which is a tiny bit dumb but isn't a plot hole per say. Lastly the game is a little easy and the only real challenge are the bosses, on hardcore, otherwise you can breeze through the rest of the game and chill, not bad but don't go in expecting like... something difficult??

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best games I've played recently. I don't play many single player games anymore but this piqued my interest.With a gameplay that feels like a mix of Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Sonic, it wraps it all up with the style and charm of Outer Wilds, Sky, or Journey.The story is fantastic, I'm comparing this to Outer Wilds because it deserves to be compared with my favorite game of all time. The story is more in-depth and is able to explore deeper topics while simultaneously keeping you never really feeling left out of the loop. Every corner of this game has purpose and allows you to develop a deeper understanding of the world you find yourself in, and how unassumingly tragic the game is, like Outer Wilds.The music is phenomenal but purely atmospheric. There weren't any memorable tracks but the music and art style is what made this game rise to my favorites in such a short time. I definitely will be checking out the OST and will use it for background music while studying/working.Conclusion:In my opinion games are a form of artwork and this is one of my favorite pieces. Sure, the gameplay could always be more exciting, however, the intrigue of the story, the secrets behind every corner, the fast-paced movement, and the gorgeous art style kept my attention and continuously provided a memorable and enjoyable experience of a lifetime.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the coolest looking video games I've ever seen, along with being one of the best controlling 3D platformers I've ever played.Solar Ash is an open world 3D platformer. It's very similar to that of Sonic Frontiers. Finish all the challenges in an area, fight the big boss. It just has FAR more style and polish than Sonic did. The art style blends with the unique sci-fi story and aesthetic beautifully. The game almost feels similar to Journey or Abzu. Playing on normal mode, it's not a particularly difficult game, but a more relaxed experience that remains satisfying through really fun and fluid movement.Normally I'm very wary of the story in games like this as I feel they're often overly pretentious, but to my surprise it was actually fairly simple and easy to understand. It doesn't beat you over the head with words you don't know or references to past events that you don't see happen. It acts as a very simple backdrop to what you're doing, exactly how I like video game stories to be, while also having fairly strong emotional themes.I don't really have any complaints. I could get into some, but I feel they would be mostly personal nitpicks.I don't think it's worth $40. I was able to 100% the game outside of maybe 5 achievements in just under 10 hours. I bought it on sale and would personally say I got my $20 worth, as I do wish to revisit this game eventually.This game is small, but solid. Really solid. It's quickly become another one of my favorite indies. It's by the devs who made Hyper Light Drifter, which is a game I've heard of but is now actually on my radar.If you enjoy incredible art design and fluid, fast, action platformers then this is a must buy experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: The style of Solar Ash has many similarities with Heart Machine's predecessor hyper light drifter: bright and rich color schemes, a lost and desolate world, and a lonely protagonist. I really like its art style, and the boss battle experience is hearty. However, the protagonist has too many lines, the gameplay seems not too innovative, and the plot is too fragmented (maybe this is not a shortcoming). Looking forward to the upcoming work of Heart Machine, hyper light breaker!
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+ Movement is fast-paced and fun.+ Platforming challenges are almost always very satisfying to beat. The best parts of the game are getting to the top of an area and opening a passageway to where you came from. It makes you feel like you really accomplished something, like any semi-open world platformer should.+ Exploration is tied in with platforming seamlessly. Sometimes you'll just want to see what's around the corner but end up completing a challenge, just like that.+ I like the art style. It feels halfway between cartoonist and realistic.Cons:- I never felt engaged with the story or lore.- Bosses feel samey, their platforming challenges interchangeable. None of them has a unique personality that truly changes the way the challenge plays out. It feels like a missed opportunity.- It's pretty easy to 100% the game in only one playthrough, this giving it very little replay value.Overall, I give this game a lukewarm recommendation, but not for the full price. $40 is way overpriced for this game. But if you can get it on sale, then it's worth it (I got it for a much more appropriate $24).
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Games are art. Ever since i've played SOMA, Outer Wilds and Ori i've known this. But between all the AAA garbage and the heaps of indie jank this trait sometimes gets lost. However if you dig deep enough you can find gold again. Solar ash is exactly that, a hidden indie gem that barely gets the recognition it deserves. It's not nearly as popular as Heart machine's debut title HLD, which i didn't play but did watch, and in my opinion solar ash is even better. Allow me to elaborate.Almost every frame in solar ash is a work of art, be that due to its gorgeous visuals, brilliant levels, unique character designs or its smooth animations. I found myself constantly in awe as i skated through the clouds of solar ash's world. Everything felt so deliberate, like an artists' brush strokes, there seemed to be thought put into every minute detail. Not only aesthetically but also gameplay wise. Not only in the movement mechanics themselves, but also the environments wherein you put them to use.Each 'time trial challenge' used the same solid core movement set in a different way. And while the overal structure of clearing X amount of trials to unlock the boss which you then defeat to move to the next area to do it all over again felt very formulaic and a little bit repetitive, actually doing each and every one of them felt unique in its own way. This is because each area has its own identity, adding something new ontop of everything else you encountered thus far.After scouring an area to tackle all its challenges, which is rewarding in and off itself thanks to great level design, you get treated to a boss fight challenge that kicks everything into the next gear. The sheer scale of them, as well as their designs and the way they move as you scale them, tackling weak point after weak point is just insane. It's hard to put into words how cool this feels but dear lord when the final phase's synths kick in, right as you're blasting from weakpoint to weakpoint... Literal chills.The story is also great and despite being an indie title, is fully voice acted. The voice acting as well as the writing comes together to make a gripping story about some pretty heavy themes such as denial and letting go. The game moved me in a way that only good art can do, and that alone is reason enought to recommend it. It is quite pricey at base price but on sale it's an easy score that's unlike any other game i've played. Solar ash easily deserves it's place among my libraries favorites as well as getting to live rent free in my head for the next couple of weeks.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: After 100 percent on the achievements, I can adequately say that this game is worth your time. The game has great controls that feel smooth and make running around the world an enjoyable experience in itself. The combat is simple but offers a great combination of adding just enough difficulty that it doesn’t become obnoxious whilst keeping it fresh between doing the puzzles and boss fights. Also, the side quests are compelling and fun to interact with, but they don’t serve any purpose for the gameplay and instead just add lore. Which I think is great because it offers a break from the gameplay to bring the player closer on the past of this world and what the implications could be. The game is also kinda short with one being able to beat it in 2-3 hours if you skip all the story and speed run, but I think it's worth spending the 40 because the mixture of Shadow of the Colossus and the Battle of Bikini Bottom makes it feel like a new experience. 10/10, would play again.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite 3D platformers ever. The movement has a great flow that makes simple running around and exploring feel awesome, not to mention the platforming challenges and boss fights which, while not particularly difficult, have plenty of exciting moments to offer. The graphics are some of the coolest 3D art I've seen in my life, and the story and voice acting also surprised me with how much I enjoyed them. I have some nitpicks, particularly with the timed platforming challenges which I often found visually hard to follow, but overall this is a beautiful game that I highly recommend. It's also not very long (but still long enough to explore its ideas to a satisfying degree), which is a big selling point if you ask me.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: The ebb and flow of this game is amazing. Striding around on skates across clouds while trying to stop the inevitable end of your homeworld is such a fun fantasy! There's plenty of reason to explore for either new suits or side quests, and collecting the red blobby "plasma" currency reminds me of retro platformers like Banjo-Kazooie!When you get to a new area, I heavily recommend focusing on your flow instead of trying to dip into corners looking for secrets. You can go back for secrets later; but experiencing an area with the real flow the game was intended to be played with? It's like a fun 3d sonic!
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game! The skating aspect works and is enjoyable. The time sequences are fun and challenging enough to feel cool when completing them. Combat is a bit boring usually except from some cases where it becomes kind of a puzzle. Side-quests are interesting stories, mostly there to add to the lore of the world. The world building is great, I love the scifi setting and cosmic horror/psychological undertones. Graphics could have been a bit more detailed but they work. Overall a great game, kind of unique in its genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: It's a short, bright, boss-rush-y sort of game interspersed with scenic vistas, lore, and very satisfying movement. If I had any complaints it's that some of the clambering on bosses is a -little- finicky and that none of them feel particularly dangerous besides going too fast and missing a jump, but otherwise it's a great bit of spectacle
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun movement, bosses are cool but pretty simple on normal, they're way more precise on hardcore though. The levels are beautiful and sometimes a bit trippy. I really enjoyed exploring the whole map and finding all of the notes/suits. The game is pretty short, but I didn't feel like it needed to be longer for the story it told. The combat is very basic but this isn't really a combat game like hyperlight drifter was, I don't think I died once to normal enemies.Overall I loved this game, my biggest complaint is that there isn't really much progression. The resource you collect can only be used to increase your max health, which I had maxed by the third zone. You can get minor upgrades through finding different suits, which are nice, but not a huge game changer.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. But the reality is, it has strange performance problems. My machine is more than sufficient (RTX 3090) and I couldn't maintain a locked 60FPS at 1440p, even with all settings on Low. To be clear, the average frame rate was high, but there are regular frame drops and stutters throughout various levels. These wore me down and I gave up on the game. Would be happy to retry if it eventually gets another optimization pass.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Jesus this game is beautiful. This game creates emotional scenes and well crafted characters through hints via the surrounding world and audio logs through caches and it is executed very well and it lets you know the path all of these characters took to their final moment. Heart machine has this tendency of making outstanding mystical soundtracks and this does not fail to show that. ending animations to boss fights are also extremely creative. Something i will be thinking about for the rest of my life.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game. Had me fully captivated for a solid 8 hours. Had I not needed to sleep, I would have (and wish I had) finished it in one session. I felt that the world created, the mysterious fragments of past civilisations, was so alluring and well crafted, that I followed the side stories without the thought of ignoring them. And that's not even mentioning the boss battles, which were absolutely spectacular. My only wish is that I could fight them for the first time again.Something to note.  I cannot imagine playing without one, and the game explicitly says that it  playing with one.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Heart Machine has done well with another beautifully-crafted story on the heels of their debut, Hyper Light Drifter. The game is a visually-beautiful, uniquely-styled 3D adventure through various worlds in a race against time to save the homeworld of the protagonist Voidrunner, Rei. Using an innovative skating feature to move through the world, the game tells a story about planetary ecological collapse and the roles played leading up to it. While the controls are innovative, the game does languish somewhat with repetitive tasks, but makes up for it in beauty, story and style. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Played through this game over the course of a couple months, and I had a good time with it. While the movement and platforming are fun, I feel the setting and atmosphere are the highlights of this game. The environments and views of this game are a feast for the eyes, with everything draped in this wonderful neon cell shading which really sells the feeling of otherworldliness to the setting. It'll even burst into these explosions of color when completing something substantial, and it really adds impact and emotion to the experience.The story was also pretty engaging. A lot of the optional content in this game is story focused, and I enjoyed learning about the stories of different people who lived in this area. Sometimes I enjoyed this side content even more than the main content, and it felt satisfying completing the stories of some of these side characters. However when it came to the actual gameplay, I honestly felt a bit underwhelmed. To it's core, it's a game about momentum platforming with light puzzle aspects. There is combat, but it's surface level to the point where enemies feel not dissimilar to the variety of environmental hazards. The movement is pretty fun though, you can hold a button to initiate a skate and press another for a quick boost. Everything from the main objectives and bosses are essentially movement puzzles, where you have to complete mini platforming time trials to progress. There is some variety to these, but personally they weren't too engaging. For the most part they felt pretty easy, and I was playing on hard. The biggest issue for me was it's use in the bosses. While the bosses had super cool designs and all looked very unique, actually fighting the bosses felt very samey. They "attack", give you the opportunity to hop on, complete a time trial, rinse and repeat x3. I felt that the only difference between them was how you actually got onto the bosses, but it was always super apparent and quite easy to do so. I found myself fighting the bosses less because I enjoyed it and morseso to simply unlock the next area.All things considered, I had a good time. It took me about 10 hours to complete this game, and I achieved 100%, so it'd probably take an hour or so less if you weren't going for that. While I had my gripes about the core gameplay loop, actually playing the game every couple of weeks was quite relaxing, and the ending was shockingly awesome. I recommend the game if you can get it at a decent discount.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game with 1 enormous caveat.To start, this game is gorgeous, as I'm sure you can see from the trailers and screenshots. If you're a fan of Heart Machine's first game, Hyper Light Drifter, you'll no doubt enjoy the aesthetic of this one. The score makes a lot of call backs to HLD's music as well with the satisfying synth chords and ambiance. Controls feel tight, but only after getting used to them for a while. There's definitely a pretty big learning curve to controlling Rei, the player character, efficiently. Once you do, though, gliding across the different landscapes in this game is immensely satisfying, akin to the likes of Super Mario Galaxy. You'll know what I mean after a couple hours in.Now we get to the biggest glaring issue that I had with this game: the camera.During gameplay, the camera shifts itself after hitting certain nodes during a boss fight or puzzle in order to direct you towards the next one. There are times when moving from point to point slashing nodes feels fluid and intuitive. However, there are other times when the camera simply doesn't know what on earth it wants to do, and in some cases actively works against you. It cannot be understated just how frustrating this can be. The final boss fight was a  because of it. Perhaps navigating the camera has a learning curve of its own and I simply never managed to master it, but I honestly don't think that's the case.Another smaller issue I had was with how the game handles gravity shifting. During the final battle, if you fail, you get respawned outside the playable area and have to skate back into it. Upon skating and falling into the playable area, the gravity would suddenly shift sideways halfway down and send me orbiting around that area for a few seconds... every single time. On one occasion, I orbited the boss area for so long that the game gave me an achievement for staying in the air for 10 seconds lol. This issue was entirely localized to the final boss fight, though. I didn't run into it anywhere else in the game.Having said that, I would still highly recommend this game to anyone thinking about it. You just have to be willing to look past the fact that the camera is going to screw you over multiple times without warning. To anyone who did the no-hit hardcore runs of this game, y'all are masochists.Also, this game does not support ultrawide resolutions. There is a fix you can do by editing the game's executable via a hex editor, but it isn't perfect. Button prompts on screen appear off-center from where they should be and some UI elements actually get cut off. Quite a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: Solar Ash can never live up to the expectations set by Hyper Light Drifter. Despite that, I would still recommend it. The gameplay is fun enough, and the visuals are striking. I really want to like it.One thing I think about regularly is that Pat on the podcast Castle Super Beast once said that the name Solar Ash Kingdom established a solid naming convention. Two one syllable words followed by a two syllable word. Then the name was changed to just Solar Ash. This game does not feel like a follow up to HLD, and the naming convention being lost was a major red flag. It feels much more rushed than its predecessor, like a sequel churned out for no other reason than to hit a deadline. Its got slick 3D graphics and excellent voice acting, but I don't feel as much heart.Even before the name change, the transition from 2D to 3D was a dead giveaway. Almost nothing of the gameplay of HLD was preserved, and the setting was completely different. I was crushed when it was revealed there would be voice acting. Very little of what the characters have to say is worth saying, which is such a tragedy because the performance the voice actors gave was excellent. HLD told its story almost exclusively through visual and environmental storytelling. It gave minimal detail leaving your imagination to fill in the rest, whereas Solar Ash is much more direct. The Ultra Void is a black hole. One race was decimated by clockwork horrors before their planet was sucked into the Ultravoid. Yes, those guys really did crush themselves with their own ship like looney tunes characters and Zapp Brannigan over here is pretending they died heroically.The Ultra Void feels more empty, less realized than the land from HLD. Sparse elements from each consumed planet are held together with cloud matter to form video game platforming challenges. Contrast with trekking through the post-apocalyptic landscape of HLD where we see the ruins and survivors of full civilizations. If anything, they didn't go hard enough with the platforming. If anything they should have fully leaned into the video game feel. Planetoids with their own gravity like in Super Mario Galaxy would have meshed seamlessly to the skating gameplay.Progression is needlessly linear. Instead of three distinct locations to fight through before unlocking the fourth, you have several levels unlocked in order with challenges scattered around. I would posit that it wouldn't have been difficult to have all three of the Strangers' story lines available from the start instead of arbitrarily locking them behind each other. This would give some agency to the player, and the levels containing the second half of each story line could have been locked behind the first.Clearing a level is enjoyable enough. Rei must navigate the zone, clearing up black goop by doing a short platforming challenge. Once you've finished cleaning up Isle Delphino, a lovecraftian horror who has been standing around aimlessly decides it's had enough of your crap. Honestly I wish the anomalies would have been more active. Instead of hanging out in the skybox, they should have been meandering around the level providing another obstacle to avoid. Enemies feel like speed bumps at best. They are easily overcome or avoided rather than competent foes defending their territory that must be skillfully dispatched.Bosses are equally unchallenging and bland. Missing are the unique aesthetic matching their location, different attack patterns, and the story that can be inferred from their appearance. A cool blob of black ink and white bone shows up, do a few short platforming challenges, and you're on to the next level. Their designs are all good, I love the style. They just feel alien to the world, which is already extremely alien to begin with. One of the reasons Shadow of the Colossus worked so well was that the Colossi are alien to the mostly grounded world. Without contrast, the anomalies aren't as striking.On to minor nitpicks, I wish the game had more collectibles. The different armors are a nice start, but Hyper Light Drifter had multiple guns to collect and moves to unlock. Skating in this game feels fun, but I want to be able to do tricks off of ramps like in Mario Kart and the hyper dash from HLD is sorely missed. The game feels incomplete. Rei can't even sit down and take in the scenery. She has no idle animation whatsoever. What's there works, but everything just feels so bare bones.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had a weird relationship with Heart Machine's games, Hyper Light Drifter got stuck for me halfway through unfortunately, however I've had the same feeling through both of these, I've felt weird playing these games, I'm not sure how to describe it. Solar Ash is a very simple-mechanic game, it isn't focused on combat or a complex movement system, just a run, a small boost, some slashes here and there, etc. You get Suits that change your focus of play (along with 1 for completing 100% on one save that affects your entire profile, so you always have access), some pages, and 3 sidequests,  The artstyle is godly as the game before it, . There's giant spectacle bosses with some substance of traversal, and a bit of Mario Galaxy type areas where you circle around masses of clouds. It's a very simple straightforward game but things change for 100% playthroughs.The 2 other playthroughs were enjoyable challenges, Speedrun & Hardcore, The 3 hour time limit gives quite a bit of room for success if you're playing on novice & Hardcore will put your timing to the test, I have only 1 piece of advice for Hardcore:Update for Game Awards: Still good7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Another phenomenal unique title from Heart Machine, Solar Ash is a brilliant action-platformer that controls with fluid skating and grappling mechanisms, within non-traditional gravity and platforming settings. The game wraps these one-of-a-kind set of controls with a vibrant and astonishing world, delightful and charming characters, and great bite-sized story to go along with it. The game lacks an advanced combat system as it focuses in on the player movement, and thus the difficulty comes mostly from speed and perspective challenges, but due to the enjoyable fast controls and overall short playtime, the lack of a difficult obstacle does not dull the experience at all.

Wish there was more to do, but its a quality succinct game that rewards exploration in lore and narrative. Depending on how into similar concepts you are, there's some things you can predict, but it doesn't detract from the overall experience IMO. _childDocuments_.review: Such a fun game, with such a good, if sad and simple, story. The art style is cool, the music has a hint of 80s sci-fi, and the fast paced zooming-about is such a joy. The dark themes and messages around saving your people from the inevitable feel at place with the times we live in. Though I loved the story, it's not easy to consider the consequences of being too late. But that might just be me, I find it hard to always untangle (post-) apocalyptic stories from our own climate crisis.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DRPROS:-Does fast flowy 3d platforming well.  Its fun to move in the world-Giant bosses you run on-Beautiful worldCONS:-Very little in the way of player progression or new abilities.  Solar ash plays like a cross between a competently made Sonic game and Shadow of the Colossus.It does the rare feat of doing fast, flowing platforming in a 3d space well.  Each level peaks in a boss fight where you run around the boss itself.The world is gorgeous, and I think its style will age well.My one criticism is that I wish there were unlockable ways to increase movement options.  An air dash would have been fantastic.  A way to run up vertical surfaces to make some of the early stuff trivial, or a glide, would also have worked.  The game is about moving around, but in an effort to be fast and streamlined, limits how I can move. I'm excited to see what Heart Machine's next game is like.  I know its also full 3d.  I'd love to see a lot of the core of this game, but with more character progression and a larger, more customizable move set like with HLD.

_childDocuments_.review: Solar Ash is a satisfying action-platformer seasoned with obnoxious dialogue and some half-baked systems, but it's a testament to the quality of its movement mechanics that the game is still enjoyable from start to finish in spite of those issues.dialogue is hollow and ham-fisted.there's a distinct lack of upgrades to your combat and movement options, which limits the effects of the game's optional Suits, and the game's skill ceiling.atmosphere, visuals, sounds, and music are all very solid. the content here feels smaller in scope than Hyper Light Drifter, and far less replayable. i think $40 is a bit much, but if you can get it for ~$20 or less, i'd say it's worth it.
