_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. I was so excited for it. Even waited an extra year for it to come to Steam. While it's definitely not a bad game, it was mostly disappointing for me. As a huge fan of Hyper Light Drifter, I had pretty high expectations. This game is very different from HLD. Almost antithetical to it in some ways. I get that this game should be able to be its own thing and not necessarily live in its predecessor's shadow, but I can't help but compare them (in part because they take place in the same universe).There are a few things this game does very well. The fluidity of the movement and controlling Rei in general is a lot of fun. It's fun just to dash, skate, rail grind, and jump around even if you aren't doing anything. The world and atmosphere are also wonderful. It feels like a great 3D interpretation of the environments and colors we saw in HLD. The general atmosphere is lonesome and eerie, yet beautiful. This is aided by a decent soundtrack (again, still not as good at HLD ost).My problems... well, firstly the exposition is exhausting. Rei never shuts the hell up. There is so much information in speech, text, logs, unskippable cutscenes. HLD told a compelling story AND explained the game's mechanics without using a SINGLE WORD. It's environmental storytelling was top notch, and also left pretty much the whole game open for interpretation. In comparison, Solar Ash dumps a tremendous amount of information on you. Towards the beginning of the game I was trying to absorb all of the logs and extra details and by the end I couldn't have been bothered. Which is a shame because the premise of the plot contains a pretty dire situation yet it just gets boring. Less is more.I found the voice acting in general to be pretty mediocre (sometimes downright cringe). Rei simply does not at all look like how you would imagine her to sound. It’s jarring and annoying. In fact, aside from Cyd, maybe Echo, and MAYBE a couple of other forgettable NPCs, most of the voice cast do NOT sound like how you think their character would sound. If I ever replay this game I will 100% play it with the voice sound turned off. Again, I feel like if there was no voice acting but also much less text, the game would have been much better off.The platforming challenges completely range from fairly exciting to downright frustrating. A big part of the frustration for me is the camera. I found a lot of my mistakes were due to a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ fixed camera angle. Furthermore, the primary gameplay loop gets quite repetitive. Go to a new area, unlock 5 eyes or whatever through light puzzle solving and platforming challenges, kill the boss, repeat. This is further exacerbated by a very dumbed down combat system. You’ll get to a point in the game, especially when backtracking, that it’s more fun and practical to just skip enemy encounters.On top of all that some design decisions weren’t terrible but sort of just bewildering. Why does Echo permanently take a notch of my health every time I beat a boss? To make me continue to collect pointless currency to get it back? Why are the suit upgrades locked behind hidden logs? I don’t know, man.Overall, it's not that bad. Just really not what I wanted. 5 or 6 / 10. This game makes me even more excited and also more nervous for Hyper Light Breaker.

_childDocuments_.review: I got interested in Heart Machine as a dev the first time I played Hyper Light Drifter (and left it unfinished). When Solar Ash was revealed and launched, I slept on it due to its exclusivity on a competing PC games store.After finishing Hyper Light Drifter I got a much better appreciation for the artistry to come from Heart Machine, so I used Solar Ash's Steam release and the Steam Winter sale to finally dive in, and I am very glad I did.Let's get the grievances out of the way. The world is pretty empty. The narrative somewhat tries to justify this but It would have been better to have seen some of the "lore spots" come from actual NPCs and not just tablets or observations from the protagonist. While movement and combat are fast, fluid, and fun, they are overly simple, and some players may find that boring. While each area plays around with shifting between linearity and exploration, the gameplay loop is literally exactly the same in every area. Skate around, find the needles, destroy the needles in a time limit, fight the boss which also revolves around destroying the needles in a time limit... For some players, that can also get very boring, very quickly.For me though? The repetitiveness was put aside, because I was just in awe of the visual design of the world. Vibrant colors everywhere, eerily beautiful atmosphere, an incredible ambient soundtrack, one of my favorite VGM tracks of all time in the boss theme, awesome gravity sections that literally turn entire worlds upside-down... It's awesome.It very much reminds me of another Annapurna-published game, The Pathless. And while I love this game's world design and artistry so much, The Pathless is better. If you desperately are looking for "protagonist glides around the world and hunts for things the game published by Annapurna" and Solar Ash and The Pathless are your only two choices, go with The Pathless. This game also falls short of the artistic highs set by its predecessor Hyper Light Drifter, but to its credit, Hyper Light Drifter is a high artistic bar to jump over.Still, all things considered, Solar Ash is a wonderful experience. My favorite? Far from it. But if an amazing visual style is something that you value in a game, and you're looking for a game where you can just run around in the world... This will serve you pretty well.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful, atmospheric, momentum based movement platformer that’s unfortunately weighed down by weird design decisions on both a story/character level and gameplay level. Ultimately, the game is short enough that none of the downsides bothered me all too much, but I could see others going into it feeling unsatisfied. My biggest gripe gameplay wise was the weird auto forward movement when skates are equipped, or the fact that there’s a toggle at ALL. It makes more precise stuff a little easier, but I really don’t think that would’ve ever been an issue if the skates just. Didn’t automatically move you forward. Jet set radio and future didn’t have a toggle, and I rarely felt like the precision movement with skates was too hard. It adds another layer of switching between skates/no skates that I didn’t really find necessary. Sure, you can have the skates as a hold rather than toggle, but that leads to you holding down one button for a very long period of time. The grapple is a great idea but the required timestop with janky controls to move around the targeted area to use the grapple BUT only for certain situations (on enemies/if you’re far away?) is also really strange. Other than that, I had a great time. The bosses were great, although I think the game held your hand a little too much on the first 2-3 areas (they are pretty easy) and most of my enjoyment was from the last 2 areas and the bosses. The story… is fine? The character designs are all great, but the dialogue often feels uncanny and weird for the dire situation Rei is in. I think the dialogueless story in HLD is definitely one of it’s strongest assets, and it’s pretty obvious heartmachine is still getting accustomed to writing characters. It’s a very, very straightforward story. Due to length, I am fine with this but again I could see others not getting much out of it. Despite these flaws, it’s definitely a game worth checking out if it’s on sale and you’re a speedy platformer lover.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, took 11 hours to 100% it. Optimization issues are a thing, and my frames dropped a lot, but I still played through it because the game was really good :D I played using mouse and keyboard, but there is full controller support.I like the characters, they served as side quests, and they weren't as simple as go kill x a certain amount of times or anything, they all had their own little story that felt important, and interesting.Visuals are amazing, story is good, Combat is fairly simple, but not in a bad way. The bosses still had me struggling a lot, and they were super cool to fight. Honestly I wish there was an air dash because it would've made things much less punishing, but seeing as the game is 39.99, I'd wait for a sale to buy this just because it took me 11 hours, which doesn't warrant such a high price.

_childDocuments_.review: A damn fine movement focused platformer that explores some interesting ideas. I like how combat was kept simple to focus on making movement and exploration the core of the experience. Art and sound was great, characters were worth learning more about and the NPCs made my heart ache for the worlds lost. Absolutely worth the sale price of $25, I really enjoyed my 8 hours with it.The only negative I have to put forward is a few nauseating instances of camera movement and one or two boss moments where the camera betrayed me. They were few and far between though.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Sonic Frontiers, or fast paced platformers in general, Id give this a shot. One thing that doesn't make sense is the performance. I played this on both my 5600X / 2060 machine and the Steam Deck. I'm not a developer, but I do have eyes. This game looks rather simple, right? Why does it run so strangely? Steam Deck can barely get 40 at 15 watts and my PC dips below 60 at Low. It feels like a crime to play such a nicely animated game without a smooth framerate and the nice effects. Though, at the end of the day, games still fun as heck and really impressive for an indie effort!Fix the framerate, add a hud size toggle. Makes a great game all the better!
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: This has become my favorite game over night. The movement feels smooth. The fighting is clean. The puzzles feel fantastic. The story and themes perfectly fit with the game play. The atmosphere has a pinch of anxiety while it isn't clear, giving optimal tension and suspense. After you clear an area, it feels serene and tranquil. The collectibles where a great excuse to check out an area after clearing it, and just move around. If this game gets a sequel, I'll be buying it without hesitation.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: As a 3D platformer, Solar Ash is probably one of my favorites - the movement mechanics are simple, and the environments are well-designed. I would recommend doing a completionist playthrough your first time around - it doesn't take much extra effort, gives you some useful items, and basically all of the interesting parts of the world are buried in the out-of-the-way stuff. There's some replay value, with higher difficulties and its great potential as a speedgame, but for a more casual playthrough, it might not bring a ton. Definitely recommend getting if you're into the movement, but with the short length and the price it's at, I'd say to wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: While this game is quite a departure from Hyper Light Drifter, I really liked it. The atmosphere and style are gorgeous and unique, the soundtrack from disasterpeace matches them perfectly, and in general the game emanates good vibes. The gameplay is quite different to HLD, and the combat is much simpler, but I feel like they're a good match to the overall style. Not a huge fan of the voice acting, although the themes of the story are compelling and powerful, something about the abundant speech, noises and such took me out of the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a really interesting game, and if you liked Hyperlight Drifter you're going to get a kick out of the style and gameplay here. Overall it's a pretty chill game to play, skating around the environments, discovering new areas and hidden things. Combat is pretty straightforward, with light Shadow of the Colossus type bosses that require some reasonable timing in order to dispatch. There's nothing punishing here, and the experience is very unique.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Just two hours in, I am already loving what this 3D platformer has to offer. The art style is gorgeous and the story's mystery unravels at just the right pace. However, this game really needs to be played with a controller and NOT a mouse and keyboard. The game warns you of this right away, but I believe it needs restating.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: The game is such a joy to play, with fast and fluid, yet demanding movement. The visuals are impeccable, with the store screenshots completely failing to do it justice. The story is entrancing all on its own, with an ending twist that completely recontextualizes the entire experience.The only negative I have is the price. I waited for a sale, which is probably the right thing to do
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: I made a long review to post here but I accidentally deleted it... so take 2. I might update this review later with more thoughts.Before I say anything, I want to make something very clear. This is not Hyper Light Drifter 2. Don't go in expecting Hyper Light Drifter 2. HLD and Solar Ash are two completely different types of games. HLD is a 2D dungeon crawler hack-and-slash. Solar Ash is if a good physics based Sonic game was mixed with Mario Galaxy's gravity and then was adopted by Shadow of the Colossus. This is also the studio's first attempt at a 3D video game, and its development was much longer than expected, and had a good amount of challenges in regards to making the game work the way they wanted to.There are also a few things people should be aware of before playing this game. First of all, Solar Ash has some cutscenes with lots of flashing lights. These only happen, if my memory serves me correct, in the opening cutscene and after boss fights. If you are prone to seizures, please be careful.Also, this game deals with themes regarding trauma, grief, life, and death. It may make some people uncomfortable simply because these are uncomfortable themes. If you want a platformer to relax to, I would say to go probably play something more like A Hat in Time. Enemy and boss designs can be really creepy. The 3rd and 4th boss are especially creepy. I can only describe my emotions in regards to their designs as "Thanks I hate it." I actually enjoyed the horror inspired designs, but I acknowledge that they can be uncomfortable for some.This game is also quite short for its asking price of $40. I beat it with 100% completion in about 13 hours and 40 minutes. Most beat it in less. If you want to make sure you "get your moneys worth" than get this game on sale. I got it for around $25.With all that being said, I proudly say that Solar Ash is one of my favorite video games.It's movement is fast, fluid, and fun. I got lots of joy from figuring out the rail grinding mechanics. I also enjoyed the game's unique gravity. It subtly reminds that you are in fact, in an anomalous black hole and not just some weird fantasy land. The combat exists. You run up to enemies and hit X a bit. You can grapple to enemies by using your cool slow-down-time powers, but I honestly forgot this was a mechanic. Might have just been a me thing though. Some enemies fire lasers and you have to run to avoid them. Some you have to doge their fast attacks. Enemies exist to add some danger and challenge to the world. It's perfectly fine. Solar Ash is about cool and fast movement, and not combat.Secrets are fun to find. They aren't obnoxiously hard, but aren't stupidly easy either. You will need to actively explore around and think to get to them, but you won't be spending hours looking for a single audio log. I would also recommend getting what the game considers 100% completion, as it gives more context to the story. Speaking of the story, I have seen many people criticize the story for being forgettable or poorly delivered. I strongly disagree with this sentiment. Throughout my entire play through, of which I did over a few weeks, I was constantly theorizing about the world and the characters. It also handles plot twists very well. They still surprise you and change the plot, but they also make sense. You can look through previous dialogue and understand how it foreshadows any plot twists. The game's good ending is especially memorable. I struggle to find the words to properly convey my strong emotions regarding it. This game has given me some of my favorite quotes. At the end of the game, I was left wanting more. Not because there was something wrong or some untied plot threads, but simply because I wanted to see more of the characters and this world. Solar Ash is a story wrapped up nicely with a bow, and I crave a squeal. I have seen some people complain about how much the protagonist talks. I personally did not mind how much dialogue there was, and most of the time found it quite endearing. I can understand the annoyance however. TLDR: R.I.P. my feelings. This game could use a seizure warning. I'm sick of people comparing this game to HLD when they are completely different genres. 10/10 one of my top favorite games, and I beat Hollow Knight,
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: 100% the game, would definitely recommend it. The combat is fairly simple with just a three-hit combo for your attack, but I feel like that's reasonable considering the majority of action in the game is moreso oriented around the parkour aspect of the game. You don't fight bosses or complete puzzles in the sense of slash and dash, you conquer them through maneuvering around and getting your movement to be incredible. The story is pretty interesting, and while it was a bit predictable for its twists, it was still lively and fun with well-written dialogue. It's honestly probably the first time I've ever let the voicelines play out for the whole game rather than just reading and skipping, the voice actors were great and they did a great job at keeping you wrapped in this story. Best part of the game by far is the visuals and the world overall, they just leave you in awe. The trails of light when you move, the Mario Galaxy-esque areas of gravity-bending terrains, practically every area and object in this game looks just incredible. The only bad part about the game I see is the fact that it took so long to get onto Steam.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game. If you are a fan of speed, parkour, and exploration this is the game you should play. I have had a good amount of fun when I boot the game up, playing as Rei to speed boost across platforms, rails, or clouds just to get further to other platforms is both relaxing and self fulfilling in game wise. I have not run into a lot of issues. The only things I have gotten to in terms of problems would be one moment accidentally placing Rei into a constant fall animation within a crevice which in all honesty, i shouldn't even be there so that only happened through brute force. One thing for certain it has a short learning curve which it mostly boils down to: Be fast and play the game the floor is lava.The story of this game is still something I am exploring and I don't want to spoil it, but basically you are part a group called the Voidrunners trying to stop a black hole from destroying your home, where people are still stuck there, you guys built a tool to do just that but it isn't operating and you cant contact your crew. That is as much as i wan't to tell without giving too much away as I really think you should give this game a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: platformer shadow of the colossus, an amazing combo. Im not a big fan of platformers but the artstyle was enough to pull me in. I loved how fluid the movement was. skating around and spamming the boost button off every hill for max speed made traveling around the map fun on its own without any platforming. Toward the end of the game it starts to drag from a repetitive design of...-travel to subquest -defeat miniboss-repeat till all of them in an area are complete-boss fightFor a non fan of the genre it was a shame but i think anyone who IS a big fan of this kind of game wont notice and appreciate the variety of the challenges even if the mechanical depth stays the same. All the game gives you to complete these challenges is easier challenges to help you get good at the game. ONE COMPLAINT The markers for where youre supposed to go hurt more than it helped. I felt like they showed me where to go in a way that confused me more than if they werent there at all. Sometimes heading to a marker is the wrong way to go. Sometimes a hole on the other side of the map is the real way to go but the game never tells you that. I think the experience wouldve been better for me if there was a better waypoint system or none at all focusing more on level design that leads you to the goal instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: A calm and still interesting journey, having tense moments as well as brief exploration with charming landscaped, fantastic visuals, an awesome score and a story never experienced before. You receive little information about what is going on, so you can figure it out yourself. I could write a lot more here, but I keep it simple.If it would've come out before the Game Awards, I would be outraged not seeing it there.P.S: My 8 year old toaster PC can run this with solid FPS so yeah I don't see any performance issues.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: fun skating, good platforming, incredible art, pretty good story, good VA, about 6 hours long and well worth it, I look forward to replaying this in a few months.my only suggestion would be some type of map to better understand where I'm at in each zone, and some type of NG+ to enjoy my collectables with a harder game mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: If you have a lot of experience in video games, play it on "challenging". I played it on "challenging" and did not regret my decision, otherwise I would've probably found it too easy.The team created great movement options and built a world around those.The visuals are stellar, while the gameplay can be a bit repetitive.If you like going fast like Sonic but without the jank, this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Cute aesthetic, but the controls are not beginner friendly on easy difficulties. The tutorial does a bad job of familiarising the controls, and the game almost immediately tossed you into situations where a higher understanding of general game design and mechanics are a prerequisite to playing. Having a tutorial you can skip over for experienced players that introduces new players to the mechanics before demanding timed coordination of those things is such a low bar to jump over in game design, and there's no pretence of wanting accessibility here.There's also a huge lack of accessibility settings, such as removing flashing effects or a colourblind mode. I would anticipate this being a bad game to play if you have epilepsy or any light or noise sensitivity whatsoever. The flashing lights mean I cannot play this game for more than a few minutes at a time, breaking up the story and gameplay in a way that would have still flowed with sections otherwise, especially if you are dying to the timing of mechanics. I'll be happy to change this review if the devs decide to take their time to learn some basic accessibility skills. The game doesn't need to lack difficulty in order to be accessible, but having an introduction for new players and having accessibility settings is a must and I cannot recommend this for people who may want or need those things, or who have player bases who may want or need those things.I'm looking forward to finishing this, in at least triple the amount of time the average player might take, due to the necessary breaks I might need to add to prevent symptom flare ups.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Solid 7/10, no motive for replaying the game thoughMusic and Art are 10/10 highly stylized and very cool, I liked it in Hyperlight Drifter and I like it here. Moving around the clouds with these desecrated areas feels very cool, and the atmospheric and sparse music adds to that effect.  Gameplay gets a 5/10 for me, mainly because the movement is like an 8, and the combat is like a 2. Moving around feels really good, and while you cannot get too creative with moving around, it still feels great to schmoove around and Railgrinding and grappling are very good. I had a lot of fun skating around the map and exploring the beautiful worlds. The combat is basically non existent, you have a 3 hit chain on your attack button and nothing else the enemies honestly don't even need to be in the game, and my review wouldn't change. The bossfights, aren't really bossfights, they're more of an extension of the platforming challenges that you need to do to progress anyway, and that was a little dissapointing as they weren't very difficult to begin with, i would've preferred more traditional colossal bossfights, with climbing the boss only being 1 part of the fight, instead of the entire fight. Another thing I would've liked would be real progression, as the game's currency can only be used to upgrade your health, and nothing else. There aren't any new skills to gain from sidequests like an airboost, or grappling to rails and so on. you start and finish with the same moveset. The Story is fine, It gets a 6/10, a little predictable, and a little confusing, but it works for the game, Unlike hyperlight drifter, the characters don't speak slideshow, so thats cool. The game is pretty short, I got an 100% save file on my first and only playthrough. And The only thing that made it 10 hours was that i spent half the game looking for the bonus collectibles. You could easily tear through this game is 5 or even 3 hours if you didn't care for the story. I'd say buy it when it goes on sale, it's pretty short and the experience isn't as cool as other games i've played at a cheaper price tag, but it's a solid platformer experience. Hopefully heart machine uses the year of feedback from this game and fix issues with their transition to 3d in hyperlight breaker
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and satisfying game, but rather short and without much replayability unless you really have a hankering to try to speed run it. The art and music is amazing, the controls and movement are satisfying, the boss fights and designs are really cool and overall it is a good game to relax with. Only issue I have with it, is that I don't think it is worth $60.00 (NZD) for a 10 ± 5 hour game. I even got in on sale for $40 and that is still pushing it for me. I do recommend the game if you really want to play it, but heavily consider if you actually think the price will be worth it for you first or pick it up when it is on a significant sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game! Shadow of the Colossus meets Journey/Jet Set Radio. Flowy glidy movement with fantastic responsiveness used to navigate a colorful and varied world. Easy to learn fun to master reflexive skating around wonderful landmarks of bygone civilizations. You move around awakening colossi with incredibly interesting platforming puzzles followed by a boss battle that feels epic in scale and satisfying to defeat.The colossi design is also incredibly cool, and the civilizations all hint at deeper lore that you're welcome to explore with interesting platforming and puzzles. New mechanics are introduced at a steady clip but never overstay their welcome. A great game for some fun pseudo nostalgic platform colossus slaying!
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking to have fun running around REALLY fast with GORGEOUS art and design and skatebording around with AMAZING atmospheric music, just vibing, this is just perfect. I'm in love with this world and all of the beautiful landscapes that there is to explore, it became really fast one of my favorite games of all-time.It is a short journey that is really worth taking, I completed 100% with 9 hours of gameplay but the experience of playing is just worth it.The story and the worldbuilding really got to me, I was caught immediately interested in what was going on, the NPCs quest lines were really cool too, my favorite being the Fungus Guy (forgot his name).
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Solar Ash is a okay game, but not one I would recommend unless you can get it for a good deal. The story is bland, the music is mediocre, the movement is fun, but the combat is boring. Bosses also lack depth. Once you defeat the first boss, you know how to defeat the rest of them. If you're looking for something casual to kill time, this might be a good choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: This is my second time buying this game, and I do not regret it.You'll see a meme floating around calling this "Jet Set Mario Galaxy of the Colossus Evangelion". And while they're not wrong (even the devs agree), it does this game a disservice. This game is wonderful, beautiful, and just so much fun to play. Skating on clouds and around derelict cityscapes, all the while your planet above your head getting closer and closer like a doomsday clock. It's atmospheric as hell. Combat is fast and fun, zipping around your foes and cutting them to pieces hasn't felt this satisfying in a long time. And the story is just...I can't in good conscious say anything about spoilers, but just trust me on this FIND ALL THE VOID LOGS BEFORE YOU FINISH THE GAME. It brings you to new lows only to lift you up in the most unexpected way. When I first played this game on PS5, I was both smiling and trying to hold back tears. The message this game holds is powerful, and I cannot recommend it enough.Now if you'll excuse me I'm going to buy a copy for all my friends. AND YOU SHOULD TOO!
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Stylish and fun, with a gentle difficulty curve that meant I never got frustrated. Might be too easy for some: combat with normal enemies is very simple.The game has a great sense of scale and speed, and the movement is fluid. Gameplay reminds me of the Shadow levels in Sonic Adventure 2, but with well-behaved grindrails and rewarding exploration.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Having Hyper Light Drifter as one of my favorite games, what about Solar Ash?A game with very fun and fluid gameplay, very responsive controls, a world full of color, mystery and something that arouses curiosity.Solar Ash brings a totally different art direction, the Heart Machine studio decides here to experiment with a three-dimensional world and does so with a lot of freedom, which brings even more depth to the world.In short, imagine a fusion of HLD + Shadow of the Colossus + Evangelion, that's Solar Ash!Game time hits the average of most of Indie games and worth every moment! 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't plan on spending my entire day off playing this game, but I got so drawn into it that I ended up 100%ing it in one sitting. That said, this is not a long/difficult game. It is, however, jam-packed with action and one of the best-written stories I've seen done. It feels like a rogue-like Super Mario Galaxy, and I'm in awe of how well that concept was accomplished.Pros:- Extremely, extremely beautiful art style. I had my initial reservations about them making the jump from pixel art to 3D graphics, but they NAILED it.- Absolutely amazing characters/story.- Very fun platforming that never got uninteresting.Cons:- Compared to Hyper Light Drifter, the player doesn't get upgrades or movement/attack styles. If the game was longer, it would be a real drag having no change in movement or combat for the whole game.- Not a whole lot of secret content. The player just isn't as rewarded for exploration, as there just aren't a lot of pickups and those pickups are all story-based (i.e. don't lead to upgrades).- No, I don't know how they could have implemented multi-dashing in this game, but they needed to find a way anyways. This isn't real criticism; I just really wanted multi-dashing.Overall, while this game isn't perfect, I'm confident to say this is one of my favorite games I've ever played. A definite 9.5/10. It really makes me excited for Hyper Light Breaker next year.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Movement is this game's biggest strength. It's a puzzle platformer with momentum + skate physics. It's fun to move around and make jumps. Combat is very shallow, however, and I do see why some people can get bored with the gameplay loop. It's repetitive, at least from what I've experienced so far (go to an area, activate the point things, boss wakes up, beat the boss). I feel like this is the kinda game you wanna play in short bursts. Music is nice and atmospheric, fits the game's vibe really well. Graphics are pretty to look at, at least if you can appreciate the lo-fi look. Although maybe the foliage could've been more detailed, and maybe given more animation to make the game look more lively. I'd get it on sale if you enjoy platformers (especially ones that emphasize momentum).I'd probably give it a 7/10. Steam should really have a star rating system or something instead of a binary recommend/don't recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: An entertaining experience but not one I can recommend for everyone. This is a very fast free running/skating platformer similar to jet set radio, set in a humongous world where the center of gravity changes to allow the player freedom of motion up and around structures that can go nearly any direction. The forward dash and forward skating movement system feel VERY powerful, but at the cost of making the game feel a little easy and imprecise. You can get going so fast that many of the boss challenges and "obstacle courses" seem tailor made to avoid asking the player to make too many adjustments or turns. There will NEVER be any expectation that the player control their speed to make a turn or to avoid overshooting a jump. Many times during these boss segments leaping before you look is perfectly fine, because if a turn coming up looks too sharp to be made, the "checkpoint" at that turn is an auto-brake/reset which brings you to a full stop and angles the camera behind you.This is a shame because these boss challenges are on giant, moving creatures with breaking platforms on them. It looks awesome, but doesn't feel like it required me to really do anything as a player. I don't think I ever experienced a game over while playing a boss on standard difficulty. There are higher difficulty modes, but these don't feel better tuned in terms of turning and careful platforming, they just lower the time allowed to the player in the challenges. For scenery, this game is a 10/10. Beautiful, unique, extremely cool. For exploration likewise the world felt unique and interesting to explore, on account of all the locations that bent gravity and allow you to fly through space like a rocket ninja. I just wish the balance were a little tighter, however unrealistic that might be out of an indie team.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Not what I expected from the trailers but still a pretty good game. At first I thought the game would be extremely movement focused and it is at first but you don't really get any new movement abilities at least not many of them. The gameplay stays pretty much the same throughout except for the enemies and environments which do change it up a bit. But you have basically the same 1 attack and few mobility tools all the way through the game which is fine because the game is not very long. The thing I was pleasantly surprised by is the focus on story. I really enjoyed the story of this game but if you're not looking for a story focused game you can blast through the story pretty fast. There are 3 side quests and multiple logs that tell you more about what happened but you can basically ignore them if you don't care about the story. The logs do have upgrades locked behind them but none of them are substantial enough for them to be your only reason for collecting the logs. If you do like story focused games then I do recommend trying to complete the side quests and collect the logs as they all have a pretty interesting story around them. My one complaint about these sidequests is it can be pretty hard to find the locations you're supposed to go to to complete them. I don't think I completed any of them without looking up a guide to one of the steps.TLDR: Good game, gameplay begins to get stale eventually but the game is pretty short anyways, story is surprisingly good and can be sped through if you don't care.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Every aspect of  contributes to its stylistic masterpiece. The gorgeous vistas set in a soft, yet striking, color palette whisk you away to a world unlike any other. The deep synthetic tones of the unrivaled score bear down with tension or accentuate your drift through the weightless clouds. The movement and combat system has you effortlessly dancing through this cosmic painting as you strike down titans and colossi alike. The otherworldly denizens you meet give context to your surroundings and motivation to your goals with their tragic tales. Every frame of  is a visual wonder and every moment you spend with it is breathtaking. Do yourself a favor, and dance across creation in this stellar experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty cool 3D platformer. Skating around on clouds and grinding on rails feels very nice. The game's aesthetic looks great, and so does the gravity-defying scenery. I couldn't help but be reminded of Mario Galaxy a bit, though in Solar Ash the irregular gravity is mostly just used to create cool set pieces, and doesn't change the gameplay too much.The game has you running around more or less open levels to solve timed platforming challenges in order to unlock boss battles that take the form of more timed platforming challenges. It's always pretty fun.Besides all the cool dashing, skating, climbing and jumping, the game also features combat! And it's... a bit dry. You have your basic 1-2-3 combo, as well as a button to slow-down time and aim a dash attack at an enemy. It does the same damage as your basic hits so it's mostly just a gap closer. Combat is never mandatory to progress but many enemy types can hit you with ranged attacks or dashes from a large distance if you don't deal with them and they're often placed in the middle of platforming sections were you can't escape from them fast enough if you haven't dealt with them first.The health system is also bothersome, many sources of damage will send you straight back to a checkpoint regardless of whether you died (on hardcore, all damage results in being sent back), only difference being you have to go through a game over screen on death. Furthermore, you health goes down by one for every boss beaten, forcing you to buy more. Often on bosses I found myself running to the nearest health pickup between every attempt (they respawn all the time) so I didn't have to sit through the game over animation. I genuinely feel like the game would have been better if you just instantly respawned every time without worrying about health, so I could jump back into the game quicker.Performance-wise the game ran well for me, I didn't get any of the shader compilation stutters I heard about in other reviews. I didn't notice many bugs either, and never anything game-breaking.The story was nice, and I'm not sure how much I can talk about it without spoiling it so I'll just stop at that.The soundtrack, sound effects and voice work were also of good quality.Overall Solar Ash is pretty easy to recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: ...with a review! I love this game. In fact, it's one of my all time favorites! The story is mysterious and tragic, the visuals are beautiful and the mechanics are BEYOND satisfying. The movement is fluid, the combat is fun, and the bossfights make YOU feel like a boss! I've never felt like a titan slayer before, and I have to say...it's a great feeling. I recommend this game with every inch of my body.I love it so much that I bought it TWO TIMES! Once on Epic Store like a year ago, and now again! And I loved the experience as much as I did back then, if not even more! Play this game! Play it!...
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Very pretty visuals, just like HLD, except its 3D now and man does it look great. This game is short but fun, a tad bit overpriced for the amount of hours you get out of it.Otherwise, I love the HLD-esc music coming back, the mechanics are interesting and work surprisingly well, also extremely satisfying grinding on rails and zooming by while slashing enemies to bits. 100% would recommend when on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just stupid fun. It hits so many points in games I love, you get to zoom around super fast covering crazy ground uncovering secrets and lots of other fun thinks along the way. The music is super good as well, it fits the atmosphere super well and I'll definitely come back to get all the achievements sooner rather than later.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely fantastic. I didn't have very many graphical issues like some have been having (and at this time, I have a... Let's say toaster of a laptop to play this on).Granted, I feel there were some very minor gameplay issues, specifically fighting some bosses that like to roam a lot faster than others. When they like to make a sharp turn, sometimes it was very poor timing and I instantly die cause I touch a no touchy zone.Other than that though, the gameplay other than that is fantastic. It's hyper light drifter, but the movement is on steroids. There was lot more simple on the exploration (it's 10x easier to 100% this game than HLD, that's for sure, but you can see the main focus was on platforming challenges more than finding secrets for the most part.The story was a tiny bit hit and miss. I liked the voice acting for the most part, it was probably needed from how complicated the story got towards the end, but after the "show don't tell" of Hyper light drifter it caught me off guard. The story through and through is definitely great, and I'd highly recommend this game to anyone who loves fast paced platformers with a little hint of collectathon in it. (I mainly loved it cause of how fast I could go, though I felt that a mid air dash would make movement a lot better, but maybe too similar to another... blue blurred franchise.)If this is the basis on what Hyper Light Breaker is going to be, then I'm all the more excited and hype to see what's to come.

_childDocuments_.review: i love this game! please buy itthat being said, there are some bugs, over sights, and a few other minor issues. nothing that ruins the experience for me, but i remembered how they made me feel the first time playing the game. i wish they wouldve given this title a bit more love, and time in the oven. i also wish that it wasnt an EGS exclusive for the first year of release, because it totally killed the game's publicity and was essentially dead on arrival for PC players. i bought the game on all 3 platforms its currently available on, and i have to say it runs poorly on a standard PS4. i suggest playing the PS5 version bc the achievements are broken on steam and it runs flawlessly. if this is your only option, just dont expect proper achievements to be a part of the gameplay experience for you
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, this game rules.The gameplay is super fast and fluid, and while the combat may not be super difficult, some of the platforming challenges certainly make up the difference, especially on the higher difficulties. It feels almost like a neon Jet Set Radio, with how you build speed and skate around.The art is gorgeous, and despite no longer being pixel based, still has that signature Heart Machine "neon in a ruined world" flair. The music is a similarly high level of gorgeous and it perfectly compliments the world and certain gameplay moments.The story is pretty simple on the surface but some of the finer details about certain plot elements have more depth than you would expect and it's pretty cool. Nothing mindblowing but also nothing to scoff at. The voice acting is a little jarring if you're coming to this from Hyper Light Drifter, but you get used to it pretty quick.The one gripe I have with the game is that it's a little short (My first time 100% playthrough clocked in at just under 6 hours), but if you're an achievement completionist you need to do three total playthroughs, which is more enjoyable than you would think seeing as how both hardcore mode and beating it in less than 3 hours require you to play differently from how you would otherwise.Another banger game from Heart Machine, can't wait for Hyper Light Breaker!
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: What an experience. Some of the best, most fluid 3D platforming, some of the most beautiful visuals and environments, and a compelling narrative with some pretty cool twists tying it all together, all in a compact 10 hour experience that feels just the right length for what it is. Like, I could nitpick about minor camera issues or rough optimization, or how the game is not... "hard" (I don't think I "died" proper a single time?) but they'd be nitpicks at most.The boss fights in particular may be the best in any 3D platformer ever, because they use the inherent mechanics of the game so beautifully while also being fantastic spectacles. The level design is varied, most every environment feels wholly unique both visually and structurally (though Ironroot Basin is a little... weak on this aspect) and the game just. Feels good to play, man. Maybe hard to recommend at its full $40 price but the game itself is so good I'd still vouch for it anyways.
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy the worlds heart machine makes, especially their gameplay. What'll find is fun movement mechanics, with some some nice shadow of the colossus vibes, sometimes things are clunky, but that is usually the case when it comes to gravity-defying platforming. The story is linear and simple, but how it's told is a fresh perspective with a little twist. finding the secrets and finishing the quests lead for an 8 hour experience that was entertaining, and a solid hour of it was just skating around.To sum up the game: Space acupuncturists tries to save planet with big bomb
_childDocuments_.name: Solar Ash

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only about halfway through the game from the looks of it and I am already wholeheartedly recommending this game.Though it's worth noting there are some performance issues in some locations which shouldn't really be happening on my hardware, but they are rare and don't happen during sections where precision is required. Just sort of breaks the immersion when it happens especially because the majority of the game is so smooth.UPDATE: Just beat the game. Loved every minute of it, start to finish. Looking forward to Hyper Light Breaker if this game is any indication of what that is going to be!

_childDocuments_.review: My favourite aspect of it though being its detached and ungrounded sci-fi aesthetic. The mysterious existentialist story and the world building all done silently and piece meal where you had a lot left to the imagination.  It's a problem because it seemingly  that approach and goes the other way of doing a lot of telling, but not as much showing. Which is a real shame, as the story and world building feel lesser because of the game's insistence in explaining every detail with simplistic exposition, with almost nothing left to the imagination. Not to mention the inclusion of voice acting leaves the story feeling all too grounded in an attempt to be more relatable to a casual audience  - which as bizarre as it may seem, lessens the cosmic nature of the atmosphere and setting the narrative is in. This left me feeling pulled out of the crafted alien and sci-fi setting at times to be reminded that this could be Earth.Compounding that is the characters themselves are also fairly cliche, you have the witless A.I. who doesn't understand human sentiment and word humour, the gruff simple minded veteran who somehow has a dog despite being part of a non Earth alien race, the irritable tech genius, the reverent religious fanatic etc. The main character for all her determination and multitude of lines interacting with these characters still feels more like a bland shell compared to the silent protagonist from Hyper Light Drifter. As for the game itself - it plays well, though camera sometimes can be a problem especially on default settings. The difficulty and learning curve of Hyper Light Drifter seem absent though as the game is extremely forgiving and there doesn't seem to be much of a skill ceiling to the action pieces and platforming. Secrets are generally far more telegraphed or obvious though exploration is still fun especially because of the nature of the excellent movement and the unconventional level design. That said, do not expect to tackle areas in a free form fashion as the game's campaign is quite a linear one.The visuals are nice, stylised yet simple though perhaps not quite as standout gorgeous as the pixel art of Hyper Light Drifter. The colours do pop and there is enough variety in the different biomes you go through. Sound design is excellent and the soundtrack is as minimalist and drone like ambient in the same vein as Hyper Light Drifter.Overall, as a followup to one of my favourite games, it's just okay. Enjoyable, but I'm not left wondering about the story or its fantastic sci-fi setting as much. Which is a shame because .

_childDocuments_.review: I am a Hyper Light Drifter fanatic, but this was a very different game with its own unique aesthetic. It is a solid game with traversal, platforming, rhythm, exploration, and light combat elements. The level design and boss battles were an absolute blast, and voice acting was done very well. I thought the wall climbing sections felt a little out of place and slowed the pace of the game a little too much, but I did find myself enjoying the exploration of each area for the journals, caches, and side quests the game features. Overall it’s worth a purchase, and makes me look forward to Heart Machine’s next title!

name: DAVE THE DIVER
detailed_description: V 1.0 Out Now! DISCORD About the Game ・An adventure, RPG, management hybrid Explore and unravel the mysteries in the depths of the Blue Hole by day and run a successful exotic sushi restaurant by night. It’s easy to get hooked on the satisfying gameplay loop! ・Casual combat and gathering gameplay with rogue-like elements Dive into the ever-changing Blue Hole and use a harpoon and other weapons to catch fish and various creatures. Upgrade and forge equipment with collected resources and sushi restaurant profits to prepare for the dangers that lurk in the unknown. Running out of oxygen means leaving collected items and fish behind! ・Eccentric characters with a lighthearted narrative Quirky but lovable characters and a story full of in-jokes, spoofs, and other humorous scenes provide an approachable and enjoyable gameplay experience. ・A beautiful sea environment with attractive 2D/3D Art A combination of pixel and 3D graphics provides a stunning art style that showcases breathtaking underwater scenery. This oceanic adventure is set in the real marine environment of a Blue Hole filled with over 200 kinds of sea creatures. ・Ample additional content to complement the main gameplay loop Minigames, side quests, and multiple storylines provide many hours of entertainment and varied gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute effing gem of a game. It changes the gameplay up constantly, which is like a fun, wholesome, satisfying blanket wrapped around my ADHD. Every time I got sad that I thought it was coming to an end, some brand new zone/minigame/weird NPC popped up and was so happy I was able to continue! The humor is wonderful, and the game is never boring for a second, including the credits themselves. I wish I could erase these 47 hours from my memory and play it again for the first time. So damn good.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Dave the Diver is a great adventure RPG, restaurant management, farming game. The story is very interesting and kept me interested through end game. I 100% this in around 50 hours (some idle time). Loved the different characters from the story and even the employees; I had a small connection with the ones I used in my restaurant. The pixel graphics are incredible, some cutscenes are absolutely gorgeous, some cutscenes are hilarious, it is a real testament to the animation crew on this game; really fantastic. The game loop of diving twice and then serving at the restaurant was pretty fun for most of the game but eventually diving became tedious and not fun. Luckily the boss fights were pretty epic, challenging, and fun. If you die, they make it easier next try. Also boss fights are not required for story progress (good for more casual players). Let’s go over some negatives for this game; as I just said, the diving / fishing part of the game became stale after I was able to dive up to 90 minutes each time. Also in mid game there are a lot of new features thrown at you very quickly and can be confusing and overwhelming. Also some of the quests of mid game were a little… boring, but I completed them all nonetheless. I also felt there was one weapon which was better than the rest, due to its long range so balance was a little off there. Should you get it? Yes, I certainly enjoyed the time I played Dave the Diver. There was a free DLC released as well which I only scratched the surface of, but I think at 60 hours I’ve done what I wanted. I got it on a slight sale at $16 and feel it was well spent. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE DAVE THE DIVERThe indie game scene has been thriving for a good few years now, and modern gaming is all the better for it. While we see a number of really good games we see still see only a handful of games like DAVE THE DIVER. The game isn't overly complicated, it doesn't take itself too seriously, yet it delivers on the core aspect. It is FUN to play. It reminds me of when I first picked up Stardew Valley on a whim. I wasn't expecting it to be as great as it was, but WHAM it hits you. With DAVE THE DIVER, the more you play, the more you are rewarded with expanding content, an actual story (that quite frankly didn't need to be as good as it is), and some seriously hilarious gags, that made me burst out with laughter, along the way. There are clear undertones of environmental activism laced within, but it is never 'preachy', and very on the nose. In fact, the devs even hide (in plain sight) some tongue and cheek humour, poking fun at phony activism (a.k.a., virtue signaling), which I will just leave at that.As a disclaimer, I have not completed the game, but feel that I already have gotten enough out of the game to recommend it to literally anybody. Notwithstanding, the fact that this game could probably be played on almost any piece of hardware, as it is not computationally demanding at all. I find myself switching between my main PC and my steam deck (made simple due to cloud saves), all the time and having just as much fun. I will say, at least in my experience playing on the steam deck, some of the textures, and text can be a little hard to see/read, as they suffer from the lower pixel counts. It would be nice to see a minor tweak of the UI for the Steam Deck, to make the text elements bigger and some of the sprites less blurry. I admit this is sort of nitpicking, as it doesn't detract far from the PC experience.Thank you to the devs for crafting such a gem of a game. It has brought me much joy to play.12/10 would get destroyed by sharks again.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: This game is simply a gem. I've been playing this game slowly, taking my time and not rushing the story at all. I'm 50h in and I still get new mechanics and I'm still discovering new stuff. I cannot recommend this game enough to anyone that just wants to have some pure, chill and unadulterated fun. Do yourself a favour and get this game.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, and the first maybe third or half of it, where you're fishing and cooking is really fun. Unfortunately, the game keeps throwing more and more new mechanics at you until they drown out the fun core game loop of the beginning. Tedious minigames, tedious fishing at deeper depths, and the combat. The combat is so bad in this game, and the second half of the game focuses on it almost entirely. It just isn't fair, the aiming is miserable, you move way too slow, hitboxes are impossible, enemies are unflinching and move too fast, you will get stuck under them taking damage multiple times. The game just slowly gets more frustrating and less fun as you progress.My hours are from playing the beginning multiple times and bouncing off it as it becomes more combat focused.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: You may think this game is just diving, catching fish and running a sushi restaurant but its not. Its so much more than that. Its an EXPERIENCE with surprises around every corner. This game combines different elements that somehow seamlessly fit and makes sense. Its management, fun storytelling, satisfying & addictive gameplay, boss battles, collecting, mini-games, upgrading, exploration, relaxing & sometimes terrifying combat. Not to mention the stunning combination of 2D & 3D pixel art.An absolute GEM made with immaculate detail & love.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some of the worst boss fight experiences I've ever had in a video game.Most bosses are huge in size and fast and smooth in movement like a high-speed truck that can track your moves coming at you; in comparison, Dave is small and slow, and can easily get killed if he moves too close to the boss, but it is oftentimes necessary to move close to the boss in order to attack. It usually takes two to three shots for the boss to kill you, and the attacks often feel impossible to dodge due to the aforesaid differences in size and movement. Your stamina is basically your health, and the only way to restore it takes a few seconds, which exposes you to the boss. Even after winning, I feel no sense of achievements (there are neither in-game achievements), but only fortuitous.And the stories about different bosses are mostly bs, but I won't mention examples here since I don't want to spoil.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I have played maybe half an hour of this game and have never encountered a game that tries to juggle multiple full scale mechanics in one experience this well. everything is so fleshed out and it feels so fun to play, even on my macbook for school. So lovely, promises anyone a good time. This better win the bafta.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Dave is my spirit animal. This may very well be one of the best games I have ever had the pleasure of playing. Talk about a vibe...this game is almost chill to the max. It's great to just pick up and enjoy yourself while you explore the ocean, catch some fish, slay some sharks and serve up some sushi and drinks. The cut scenes are simple and epic at the same time. Creating or enhancing a dish feels like you're watching a hero's evolution in anime. Highly recommend, very cowabunga! 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Dave the Diver is one of those games that you can pick up and put down as you please, the story progression feels smooth and the gameplay is stunning. I am not too far into the game at present, but I have enjoyed every minute so far. I am really hopeful of this games future and would love to see more content being added to this wonderful hidden gem.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Dave the Diver is an amazing game!There is tons of stuff you can do and the story is super fun and goofy.Here is what I enjoyed about the game:1. Diving of course!2. Collecting fish, cooking ingredients, cat food, and a huge variety of items that help you improve your gear and stuff you need for quests3. Late at night, you start to work at the sushi bar which is the territory of the legendary sushi chef Bancho, and your task is to help him select and prepare the dishes4. You hire staff to work at the bar and sign them up for training, while they obtain useful skills to make serving and cooking more effective5. There are several interesting customers and VIP's who request special dishes, all while events are hosted regulary, to which you have to gather the right ingredients in time for them to be happy6. Decorating the bar is also a welcome option and sometimes you earn decorations through quests 7. There is a lot to discover in the blue hole...Like really, a lot! (*cough*seafolk *cough* and sharks, god do I love sharks in this game)8. Mini games! Dave owns a smartphone with all the useful information, and mini games, contacts and much more9. Farming is a thing in this game and it is perfectly done in my opinion!10. The most important thing! Dave is an absolute sweetheart who helps everyone out(even though he does have questionable people around him)There is so much more that I could mention, but those are the things that stood out to me, and I am still not finished with the game so I imagine there is a lot more on the way that I will enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game with a bunch of mini games stuck in. The main gameplay is exploring the vast blue hole and catching fish with weapons and your speargun, but along that there is a mystery and story to unravel. While during the night, you manage the restaurant and play a mini food serving game. Alongside all that, there is card/fish collection for those collectathon, dream sequence rhythm mini game, and more. It's not just the gameplay is that amazing either, a lot of budget went into the cutscenes, music perfectly fits each environment you're in, and overall story is interesting as well.It's hard to make a new game that hasn't already been done before, but with the amount of content in Dave the Diver, I feel like no matter who you are, there is something for everyone in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most entertaining games I have recently played. The pixel art is perfect. The gameplay loop finely balanced and there is little to no grind. The story is engaging and there is a multitude of side content to keep you coming for more.  Finished the main quest along with all side quests in 24hours.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I think my favorite thing in this game is that the NPC's run the show. Dave is always getting roped in to their quests and egos. Such a great game in general. I am super picky about gameplay and everything here is  fine-tuned to be fun and relatively intuitive. If you put in the effort to maximize your day, it feels worth it, but you can also just ... go dive and not worry about it. Great that you can really find rewards doing either.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Dave the Diver has been such a beautiful underwater experience. The exploration of sea life has been tense but oh-so mesmerizing. You may think, “Oh, it’s just a chill fishing game with some restaurant management.” Initially, it may seem like that, but once you dive deeper, you’re in for a ride. This game is such a unique one in its roguelike genre. It piggybacked little ideas from other games and was incorporated into the game very well. The storyline of the game is simple to follow. There are plenty of quests to keep you occupied while exploring the ocean. After you’ve done a few quests/fishing rounds, you’ll be earning some cash to make the restaurant better and upgrade your diving gear and farm. You’ll encounter many characters like VIP guests, scientists, pirates and that will appear as you progress throughout the game. The overall gaming mechanics can be quite tricky to get a hang of at first, but once you play around with it for a bit, it will be addicting. The game also references plenty of memes, so keep a lookout for those. ;) So far the developers have released 2 free DLCs since its launch, Dredge and the Godzilla content pack being the most recent. I’m looking forward to more content in the future! Overall Dave the Diver is such a gem of a game and I highly recommend you to play it.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Dave The Diver is a wild game.I love fishing games and also these kind of "number go up" games in terms of upgrading your stuff. Dave The Diver was surely enjoyable but it was a bit much at times. It throws 50 different mechanics and game mods in. There's a rhythm game in this. A tamagochi. You manage a subbranch. You need to do cooking minigames and stuff. Plus, it drags on a bit too much, but that's maybe because I 100% it. Even though the dragging started before the main story completed.Overall, I recommend it but don't try to go for everything.What I really love about Dave The Diver though is Dave. He's great. He's, at least from my point of view, the first positive fat gaming protagonist. Not once did his weight come up. He's just naturally friendshaped and that does not impair his ability at all.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: A very enjoyable, often times relaxing game. You  dive beneath a special area called "The Blue Hole",  the layout of which slightly changes every time you go into it. You explore and catch fish, which are used in your sushi restaurant at night. As the game progresses, you upgrade both your diving gear and the restaurant, unlock other areas such as a small farm and a fish raising area to raise fish you have caught. There are also many mini-games along the way as you play through a very enjoyable campaign. If I had to compare this to another game, it would probably be Stardew Valley. The game play tends to have that same relaxing feel. I will be surprised if another indy game can top this game in this year's releases. At least for me.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Tutorial flow was bugged for me; got locked out of being able to do anything at all. No clicks would register anywhere. Escape menu wouldn't even let me exit the game, had to force close it.Was disappointed in the play up to that point. Very slow going and wasn't grabbing me. And running into an unrecoverable bug so soon into gameplay makes me not want to invest any more time into it.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game and very addicting. At first it appears very simplistic Just Dive, Catch fish, serve Sushi, but the farther you get in the game the more new things it gives you to do even if it's just a one time minigame event. Haven't finished the story, but it's decent so far, nothing revolutionary but has a lot of charm mainly due to the characters. A warning that mid-late game you go from the five-ten minute dives of early game to fifteen-twenty minute dives full upgrades could probably let's you continue for around thirty if you are smart about it so if you have trouble with: "Just one more." Syndrome it can sneak up on you how much time you are using without realizing it.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: The kind of game that keeps me playing games. Every so often a game comes along that seems to get everything right. Dave the Diver is a game like this. I had no idea I wanted a diving / restaurant management sim so much until playing this. Simply amazing! I'll update more as I get further in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Dave the Diver keeps throwing new things to do at you so that things never become stale. The core gameplay is fun, engaging and broken up exceptionally well so that nothing overstays its welcome.  A lot of the time games that go for this sort of relaxed, casual feeling end up just being dull to play, this certainly is not one of those games. This is something that I can easily recommend to anyone that has the slightest interest in video games and be pretty confident that they will like it.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: The game is overrated, it's not that great in my experience. Unless you love minigames of the quick time event type (timed keystrokes) because those are everywhere. I personnally find them annoying. Cutscenes with lenghty dialogs are also constant. I read them at first but grew tired of it. At least you can skip your way through. I find the game to be stressful and difficult at times rather than casual. The amount of content is overhelming and is thrown at you too fast, they should have paced it down. Maybe I got my hopes too high because of the reviews but it's not the casual and atmospheric game I was hoping for.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: As a diver myself, I wish the game would take a critical look at the what actual ramifications the actions of the player would have on an eco system. Collecting starfish, shells and killing sharks, manta, squids and anything living in these numbers would cause irreversible damage to any reef.Not only does the game not address this selfish, unsustainable exploitation, it also portraits the group of ecologists and the enemy.Eventually I had to put the game down
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: All these great reviews, I'll gonna write a bad one! This game is terrible! Black Tiger on Ps4 was better! Superman on N64 was better! ... I'M JUST KIDDING! This game is really fun, and very relaxing (most of the time), but, much like the sushi Dave serves at night, it's best enjoyed in bites. Do a dive or two, then a night at the restaurant, then take a break. This is not one of those binge at night and before you know it it's morning games.

_childDocuments_.review: Starts off as a very fun game but at some point it randomly decides to become a visual novel, replacing the enjoyable gameplay with an endless array of cutscenes followed by brief 2 minute segments of trivial puzzles and quick-time events; the interesting exploration and cool boss fights of the first half simply disappear, replaced by a linear series of corridors for you to trudge through, every new room complete with a relatively simple puzzle that the game nonetheless pauses and explains to you. It is is also joylessly stretched out by forcing you to return to town and get a mcguffin every few puzzles, so you don't blow through it all in one go. For some reason, around this time you also start unlocking a lot of random mini-games and activities to do. If only they had maintained their focus on what drew players in the first place, this could have been an excellent game. Instead I find myself struggling to finish it, hoping to find its original charm somewhere hidden amongst what it's become.

_childDocuments_.review: Dave the Diver is a wonderful working sim/management/adventure hybrid. To be honest, I didn't really expect much of DtD going in, but now that I'm 40 hours in and STILL finding stuff to do I am beyond impressed with it.The story is a perfect balance of intriguing and hilarious. It’s all held together with charming and lovable characters including the titular Dave himself being the quintessential "straight man" trope character, helplessly entangled in the lives/ambitions of countless absurd inhabitants of the Blue Hole after his sketchy-yet-reliable friend Cobra sets him up with a "gravy" job gathering fish for the stoic and taciturn sushi chef Bancho. (personal favorite character of mine is your weapons supplier, Duff, an Otaku who is hopelessly obsessed with some idol-mecha anime/game.)The core gameplay loop never gets boring, and the sheer amount of content and things to do is staggering; Fishing, scavenging, Managing a Restaurant, taking wildlife photos, fighting giant boss monsters, farming both fish and vegetables for making complex dishes for said restaurant... I don't want to spoil too much, and if i wanted to I think I'd take all day going over all the stuff you'd do in this game. You're drip-fed a steady amount of tasks and mechanics so its never overwhelming either, which I appreciate. I hate having a long, unwieldy list of things to do in a game. I love the art style and graphical choice of the game, the environments and fish are wonderfully detailed (Entries for them in the bestiary of the game has neat real life facts about them too!), and the 3D and 2D sprite work is clean and beautiful. The soundtrack is very nice, sets the mood perfectly for each scene and level you encounter. Dave the Diver is a chill and relaxing game when you get stuck in a routine, but it has its fill of exciting encounters that will liven things up, keeping things fresh and new each time you play. Dave the Diver earned a special place in my heart, wish it got more recognition as well, I 100% recommend it! One of my favorites from 2023.

_childDocuments_.review: Dave the Diver heavily exceeded my expectations and had me thoroughly enjoying every moment of gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: Rating: 7/10Dave the Diver captivated me with its vibrant underwater world and intuitive gameplay mechanics. Exploring the depths, discovering items, and encountering exotic sea creatures provided a sense of wonder and excitement. However, the repetitive nature of the tasks and lack of significant variation made the experience feel stale rather quickly. None of it's core mechanics are deep enough to further dive into, leaving me wishing for more complexity and depth to the gameplay. Despite this, I found myself drawn to complete the game and unlock all the achievements, driven by a desire to fully immerse myself in Dave's underwater journey. While Dave the Diver didn't offer the depth and lasting appeal I had hoped for, it still managed to provide enough enjoyment to warrant seeing it through to the end.

_childDocuments_.review: This game shows that a developer can create a fun and funny game while also having no idea how to make a game. _childDocuments_.review: amazing game! amazing story! i love it all. 10/10. i dearly hope development will continue at a steady pace. i can see this game becoming something i come back to for many years, if done well. this is a game i would even buy dlc content for after its finished, thats how much i love it!the gameplay loops are constantly engaging and seeing your progress is satisfying. my only complaints is that i want more! i want bigger ocean maps and deeper depths to explore! im a huge fan of the layering of mechanics, maybe its a little too busy for some people, but perfect for me! theres  theres a lot going on but i think its done really well and wouldn't mind even a few more things to do! ive watched a few letsplayers try this game and they seem a little lost sometimes. people skip dialogue they need fairly often in this game and a dedicated mechanics explanation somewhere you can access at any time would be helpful for those kinds of players. also,  also!! for some reason this game takes really long to launch for me? im not sure why and its not that important but i got very worried the first few times i launched the game and it wouldnt open!i have played the game for about 19 hours in early access and have finished the main quest with only 2 remaining quests to finish out. i payed 20$ for this and would say the experience is     worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the perfect 'I don't want to think much' game but if you DO want to put thought into things, you can really get into running the restaurant as well. Backtracking a bit, fishing can be stressful at times, so I'm not sure I would count this as a stress-free cozy game. It is pretty mellow once you're fully upgraded and your weapons are higher powered, which results in a great time sink of a game. There's just enough to do that if you want a mission or need more 'goals,' the game has you covered.The only thing I wish was a little different are the forced cut scenes. I don't want to follow the octopus right now, please let me hunt. With the dolphins, I could ignore that and the mission reset the next day. The octopus was a much less involved 'event' and yet I was forced into it. I'm not sure how they pick and choose, but in my opinion, with the exception of boss fights and plot development, they should all work like the dolphins.Truly, that's such a minor nitpick as I try to objectively rate the game. It's a charming, mostly relaxing experience. I thought I wouldn't enjoy the restaurant aspect, but it turns out 'Murica capitalism runs in my blood and I'm totally into it. It can be a little challenging to consistently start turning a profit, and even longer to turn HUGE profits, but it's so worth it to hit those milestones and see your stats begin to improve. This is a great game for anyone who wants to relax while still feeling like they're accomplishing something during game play. It's especially great for people who can only play a game for a limited time. The fishing cycle can be as long as you need once you learn how to navigate for oxygen, which helps make gameplay as short or as long as you want.Definitely see myself sinking a lot of hours into this before I move on to something else.
