_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - You'll spend more time reading text than playing. And the little amount of gameplay there is (which is interrupted every 2 seconds) isn't fun enough to make up for the otherwise boring story.I feel like this is one of those cases where a game has been grossly over-hyped...I really wanted to like the game, but 8 hours into it (I feel like I've given it a fair shot), here are my thoughts:The gameplay loop is not particularly fun. It's novel the first couple times, but it gets old very quickly. You dive in, go as deep as possible as fast as possible, catch the highest tier fish you can, then get out.The story is just annoying. It's not particularly funny. Most of the jokes fall flat. And the gameplay is interrupted every 2 seconds for some cut-scene or call or boat arriving or new mechanic etc etc etc..... I just want to play the game.I'm willing to admit that I might be completely missing the point, that maybe this really is a masterpiece, and that I'm just not seeing it. But my honest opinion is that this game kind of sucks. The cut-scenes/interruptions feel like ads in a mobile game that I was desperate to have an option to pay so that I wouldn't have to deal with them anymore. If you buy this, I hope you enjoy it. I didn't.

_childDocuments_.review: Dive twice a day to catch fish to sell at your sushi restaurant at night. Then you serve your customers. It's like Half Super Nintendo Mario Style fish Diver and Half Restaurant manager. There is a lot of variety in fish. Different sizes, HP, some attack you, some don't. There are boss battles too. You need to upgrade your harpoon to catch fish easier, Upgrade your Oxygen to dive longer and go deeper, Hire staff to keep up with the demand in your restaurant, etc and so forth you always have something to upgrade and work towards. You have a cell phone with a bunch of apps that do different things. There is a lot to this game and it's actually very deep. They do an excellent job of slowly introducing new things to you one by one so it doesn't overwhelm you off the bat. It is pretty addictive but it does get kind of tedious the longer you play. Definitely worth the $20 and it's very unique there is nothing out there like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately the game crashes for me every 3 to 5 dives on “Unity 3D render” errors (the higher the resolution the more frequent). Whatever I have collected so far gets lost, making longer dives (10min+) too risky. Even though those issues are reported since more than half a year, you get the “sorry, we hear you” canned reaction, the studio doesn’t seem to address them given how little their inquiries structure responses.Many a game-mechanic is unclear and remains unexplained: Why shouldn’t I set dishes to auto-supply (any influence on meal-prepraration time?)? What are the wages for staff? Why would I engage with in-game social media?Controls are laggy at crucial moments. I frequently find myself using the knife instead of the gun or harpoon because a fast right-click didn’t register. Or L-shift remained without effect. The option to replace slamming keys in mini-games (“QTE”) by keeping them down doesn’t seem to have had a change.The cutscenes are nice, once or twice, but way too repetitive they interrupt the flow.

_childDocuments_.review: Dave the Diver has so many cool ideas and fun gameplay loops! Unfortunately, the pacing of the game is ALL over the place and is really inconsistent, making it feel excited at times, and a chore at others. There are a lot of basic systems and pieces of content that get locked away for 20+ hours because it's tied to story progression for no real reason, making some of the sushi restaurant elements feel even more detached from the rest of the game/story than it already kinda is.But man, that early game where you are first exploring the first few areas of the sea, unlocking new weapons and tools, and getting new restaurant unlocks to make more money? It's fantastic and it really hooked me. It's once you meet the sea people, the game starts to really slow down significantly and become a lot more tedious. The final couple of areas, while visually rad and have great music, require so much backtracking and gating for what ultimately ends up being pretty small and unexciting zones. Overall the game is really neat, and I'm glad I played it! There's just a lot of missed potential on both halves of the game to really shine sadly.

Lots of humour, good storyline, has end game "do whatever you want mode"...Fantastic game for its price, 10/10.- That said, I believe this game is sold as a "relaxing" game. I found it quite the opposite, as there are so many things to do and so much to explore. - Yes, you can do it bit by bit and there is no time limit in the game, but I have limited gaming time in real life- Needing to chase fish, run away from fish, fight fish, watching my oxygen, trying to find oxygen, etc does not make me relaxed. _childDocuments_.review: Dave the Diver doesn’t have a clear focus, which is simultaneously its biggest weakness and greatest selling point. No one mechanic ever feels fully fleshed out, but they come and go so rapidly that it doesn’t really matter. The day-to-day loop of diving for fish then managing a sushi restaurant gets abandoned pretty fast. While the game initially appears to be an “upgrade” style tycoon game, it starts mixing in new experiences and minigames really quickly. You start going on rescue missions, collecting pokemon, taking safari pictures, feeding cats, farming, raising chickens, meeting ancient underwater civilizations, fighting neolithic era monsters, playing rhythm games, raising tamagotchis, playing a mini-version of Dredge, and even going on spy missions. While this kept the experience fresh, it never felt like it had any depth to it. The moment a mechanic approaches satisfying complexity, it gets swapped out for a new one. Recommended at a discount to make a fun couple weekends. It makes for a poor tycoon game, but still a strong overall game if you can embrace the absurdity.

_childDocuments_.review: Couldn't expect less than a perfect game after being recommended by lots of friends and reviewers, this game is so good it makes you question the gaming industry as why is it that hard for the AAA games to deliver even 50% of what this one did.It's purely 10/10, engaging story with a good plot and perfect gameplay, especially the special cooking competitions (I honestly wish they add more of this if they make a DLC or another game).
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a game that combines the thrill of exploration with the unpredictability of comedy, then look no further! It's like Finding Nemo met Monty Python underwater.Dave, our intrepid hero, is not your typical diver. He's got the grave of a sea cucumber and the speed of a particularly lazy manatee, but that's what makes him so endearing. The controls are as smooth as a dolphins back, even if Dave moves like he's got an octopus stuck to his face.The graphics are vibrant and colorful, making the underwater world feel alive and inviting. The soundtrack is a bubbly mix of tunes that will have you humming along as Dave belly flops onto unsuspecting sea creatures.In conclusion, Dave the Diver is a hilarious adventure that will keep you entertained for hours. It proves that no all heroes wear capes - some wear flippers and diving gear.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so many different things that you can do from diving, catching fish, battling bosses, to questing. Then you get some mini games as well. This game is so much fun and I highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys Stardew Valley, farming sims, or slice of life. This game is very well rounded on what you get to do with your time and there are always new things to discover. I would highly recommend this to anyone looking to try and new game.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Game seems simple.Dive in water, harpoon fishy, make fish sushi, sell sushi for money, upgrade dive gear, repeat.And then of course there's the quests, stuff for the main story, basic fetch quests, collect x items and turn in.Plenty of cool little puzzles and whatnot throughout the missions.There's the boss fights every once and a while and the legendary sushi that sells for a whole lot.And then there's also the farming so you can get rice and vegetables and eggs, and also underwater farming for kelp and seaweed.Oh and then don't forget the sea horse racing minigame, rythym minigame, tamagotchi minigame, tea pouring minigame, employee management system, weapon upgrade trees, consumables and melee weapons, recipe enhancement, night fishing, mining, secret areas, Metal Gear Solid stealth mission, One Punch Grandma, Prehistoric creatures of the deep, Pirates, Poachers, Dragonkin Soldier of Nokstella, Crocodile Dentist minigame, Water Boy and Lava Girl puzzle, Giant Truck Crab, platformer minigame, photography minigame, card collections, trinkets and artifacts, obligatory escort missions, and The Kraken.Yeah to be honest I'm not so sure this is just a diving game.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute masterpiece. The core loop is so satisfying that I plan to keep on playing after seeing the credits, and I still can't understand how it keeps introducing mechanics and systems the whole game with an absurdly high frequency until the very end. This game feels like a polished amalgam of several video game developers' theses and I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I love dave the diver....I wrote a poem...In the ocean's depth, where mysteries reside,Lives a diver named Dave, with a heart so wide.With glee and passion, he dives into the blue,To hunt and gather, his livelihood anew.In Dave the Diver's world, he co-owns with pride,A sushi restaurant where dreams collide.With net in hand and fins upon his feet,He serves customers with a smile so sweet.Amidst coral reefs and swaying kelp strands,Dave hunts for treasures with precise hands.From colorful schools to elusive eels,His sushi dreams are what this tale reveals.Though the sea might test him, and currents may clash,Dave's resilience shines with every splash.He helps his staff and treats them with great care,In his heart, compassion is always there.In his sushi restaurant, where laughter resounds,Dave's warmth and charm make it hallowed grounds.His sushi creations, a work of art,Bring joy to diners and fill every heart.A jovial soul, he wears his heart on his sleeve,With kindness and love, he'll never deceive.His laughter echoes through the salty air,As customers indulge in flavors so rare.Dave's passion for the ocean knows no end,His love for its creatures, his heart does defend.Through every dive and every catch he takes,He cherishes the life that the sea awakes.So here's to Dave, the diver with a heart so true,In his underwater world, he's someone you'll pursue.With kindness, humor, and a spirit that's alive,He's a beloved friend, a hero to strive.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a great game. _childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Remember when video games used to be about fun? When hacks like Neil Druckmann who "wAnTeD tO tElL aN eMoTiOnAl StOrY" were laughed at? Where the concern of the developers was not raking in millions from horse armor or lootboxes, but making an enjoyable game? Before the repetitive battle royales, before the needlessly large and empty ""open worlds""? Just so you know- of all the AAA games released this year, only one, Hi-Fi rush, was actually new IP? Everything else is either a "sequel" (despite being almost exactly the same game) or a "remaster" (that upscale to 1080p and downgrade of textures? 70$ please!). The games industry has been in the gutter for years, and it's at its worst point in a long time today. Once legendary studios like Nintendo, Square Enix and Activision have done nothing but make the same games they made years ago over and over again, somehow making it worse each time despite barely breaking from the same formula each time. But games like Dave the Diver give me hope that video gaming still has some life in it.This game is a strong reminder of what the games industry should be doing, and is a possible GOTY contender. It is a great game to play, and nothing less. You go diving to collect fish and explore underseas ruins, and then run your sushi restauraunt afterwards. It's a very engaging, enjoyable experience where it feels like the developers had a genuine passion for making the game, and invested their body, mind, and soul into making this game as great as it is. For only 20 USD, this game is a steal. Absolutely incredible, this is a VIDEO GAME.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fell in love with this game. I recently got a Steam Deck and was looking into good games to play on it. Repeatedly, I saw comments raving over this game. The gameplay remains fresh through the entire experience, and it scratches the "completionist" itch within me. Fantastic experience that I cannot recommend enough. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible. I always thought I'd seen it all and then it throws another curveball at me! _childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a ton of great ideas but it is a massive killjoy in my opinion and leaves me asking "do I enjoy this game or do I slog through the game to get the things I enjoy?". The pacing of this game is pretty bad. I am constantly inundated with forced tutorials that I really don't need, forced into or out of the ocean when I had other plans for progression, or weirdly held back from upgrading things because I haven't waded through said forced content. DAVE THE DIVER, as the title insists, has very limited game mechanics. This isn't even a bad thing really, I think it says a lot that the game is so popular and enjoyable with such limited mechanics. That is not to say that there is not much to do, just that the core gameplay is effectively just a handful of the same actions in different flavors. So it is a good game to chill out wi.....................except whoops you died so whatever you just did was meaningless. I could use an autosave every once in a while in the ocean especially in this ADHD format. I really like the restaurant stuff, in fact I would love to run the restaurant and use the diving to fuel it for the most part. Instead the restaurant comes and goes with the haste of an underpaid escort while you are thrust back into the ocean to do the same few things again for the billionth time. Oh god why am I already tired of diving in a game about diving?The game is obviously well done but I just find myself being more unhappy than happy so I don't need to force myself through the remainder. If you choose to buy this game I hope you enjoy it, but I just feel annoyed more than anything else.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game mostly because I was bored and looking for something different.  Boy was I surprised by how different this game is.  It has the sea exploration somewhat like Subnautica but it's also very much running a shop.  You upgrade your gear to continue to get deeper and find newer stuff.  You can upgrade your shop recipes as you continue to get more stuff.  You can change the shop decoration as well as higher and level up staff of your choosing.  There is a book to fill with all the different fish you find so you can complete that too.  So far I'm very impressed and happy with this game.  Definitely found a gem!
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly relaxing roguelike-esque game about diving, fishing and sushi-restauranteuring. Absolutely worth it for the price, but there are still plenty of improvements to be made, especially in the settings.The aim-and-fire control scheme is not that intuitive to me but there is no control remapping. As others have mentioned, there is also plenty of button-mashing without accessibility options, though it might be subject to change. There is also a chromatic abberation and depth of focus effect around the edges of the screen that makes me slightly dizzy and can't be disabled.Perhaps my biggest gripe, though, is the lack of controller deadzone. My old wired xbox 360 controller makes pouring beverages impossible, and I've had to work around it using Steam controller layouts available in the community. A setting would be preferable. All in all though, a solid purchase and a really fun experience so far!

_childDocuments_.review: Dave the Diver might seem like a cutesy and less-than-serious game, and in many great ways it is just that, but don't be fooled either, there are plenty of mature elements to it as well. There is gear to level up and mod, recipes to unlock and improve, the Deep Blue can be a challenge at times, but not frustratingly so and the quest system works as it should. Plus you are equal parts diver, server, farmer, collector, and hero, I don't play many games that can have the main character so successfully play so many roles and execute each role well. The presentation is "old school" but with modern polish and the in game music is wonderful! Best thing I can say about Dave the Diver is I went into it with decently high expectations from it's recent popularity and the game was able to exceed those expectations, something that almost no game, big or small, can do anymore. Kudos to the developers on a one-of-a-kind achievement!Now Back to the Deep!!

_childDocuments_.review: I appreciate a bit of sillyness, the story is quite okay but not particularly interesting (although the game makes sure you get it shoved down your throat with MANY slow, unskippable cutscenes...). _childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a "maybe" recommendation.Dave The Diver is a charming game with a lot of soul and effort put into it, and you will enjoy first 10 hours, while remaining time gets bogged down by repetitive mechanics and tedious management. Furthermore lack of coherence and unnecessary padding makes the game fall apart in later chapters.Light early game mechanics spoilers below.Pros:- Fantastic art direction, glorious cutscenes that made me laugh and good soundtrack- The beginning cycle of dive-catch-cook-sell is really addictive and will get you hooked(hehe) on the game- Restaurant staff and diving tool upgrades match the natural flow of the game, making it more fluid and reduce the tedium- I found variety of mini games and interactive story cutscenes charming, some made me genuinely chuckleNeutral:- Story is interesting and easy to follow, yet sometimes blocked by lack of a particular diving suit upgrade which you will have to grind for- Tons of fish to find, catch and collect, with a handy reference guide on where are the missing fish located. However, your effort to 100% it or catch all fish ★★★ is not rewarded at all- Additional sub-missions that reward underwater collection are disproportionately demanding compared to the reward you getCons:- No coherence in sushi menus, there is literally no point in upgrading early dishes while dishes from fish caught later are almost always better even unupgraded.- Pointless "tasty" food mechanic that only serves to block your rank up to next restaurant level and nothing else- More and more gameplay layers are added that don't match the energy, excitement and polish of sea exploration, such as fish farm and vegetable farm, and are a chore to do every in-game day- Minigames when catching a single fish are tedious (there is accessibility option to make repeated presses easier, but nothing about wiggling or rotating the stick)- Enemies do way too much damage and are too fast for Dave to circle around. Sometimes you get chunked for more than half health because you get hit once and then the enemy's hit box lingers in Dave's hit box, leading to more hits- Puzzle solving is constantly interrupted by Dave telling you the answer to the puzzle- If you want to be fast and snappy with your management mechanics prepare to be staring at 10-15s loading screens every interaction (Steam Deck at least)

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I recommend this game. 8/10- some spoilers below -The central gameplay loop is satisfying:Dive - collect, hunt, exploreRestaurant - make a menu, manage ingredients, staff, profitManage - spend gold on upgrades, farm, grow fishThere is enough diversity between all of these different phases to make my 30 hours very enjoyable. The combat is casual and fun, the story missions were always fun and varied. The overall pacing of Dave the Diver was excellent, as you break from the core loop for unique mini-games all the time (notable examples would include Cooking Mama-esque cooking mini-games to participating in a rhythm game at a K-Pop concert)The variety of gameplay elements is very good. However, the very final act felt a bit weak and did detract from the overall score. Throughout the story the Sea People tell you of their history of their King Long and the evil Bio-Engineer whose conflict sent their people into a 1000 year decline. Despite their significance to the Sea People's history, they have no bearing on the modern day conflict that is destroying their sacred tree. When you are in the final act, there is no mention of these important figures except for a monster that the Bio-Engineer left behind! A mindless monster which did not have any real emotional impact to defeating. There was no foreshadowing of this monster. There easily was narrative space to have the Sea People's story be more active in how they saved themselves, not just lifting a heavy thing at the end. They could have given us access to magic, or come to help us actually fight the Bio-Engineer who'd lived this entire time under the glacier plotting his revenge. Missed opportunity.The game also began to require a grind to achieve better taste scores to promote the restaurant which was not ideal.Overall, game was good, glad I played it. Would recommend at this price point ($25.99 CAD)
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Game is friggen phenomenal. 50hrs in and it's still surprising me with plotlines, and characters. The jokes are witty and the story is intriguing. Plus the style and animations are so unique and clean compared to anything I've played in awhile, especially for a pixel game. My favourite thing is probably just how many other games they managed to fit in this title. From cooking mama to a farming sim you're getting like 10 games in one. Truly a beyond stellar experience that I can't get enough of. Wholeheartedly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this game kind of came out of nowhere to end up as one of my favorites of 2023. It instantly hooked me in the same way as games like Stardew Valley and Terraria, although admittedly it doesn't have the same infinite re-playability of those. The gameplay loop alternates between the diving and restaurant portions, with story, events, and mini games sprinkled all over, making it feel extremely varied and giving you plenty of things to get lost in. The pixel cut-scenes aren't like anything I've seen before and are easily one of the most charming aspects of the game. I really hope the developers go for a sequel with more potential in the endgame; that was honestly the only thing I found lacking in this one.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not going to spoil anything in this game, but I don't see many reviews actually talking about how much game there is in this single project. I honestly thought I'd be buying into a game where the core gameplay loop was going to be, fish during day, serve sushi during night, buy upgrades with the money earned, rinse repeat.Absolutely not the case. While the core gameplay loop is super solid and could entertain you for a good while, it is also supported by a surprising amount of side mechanics that not only are well thought out on their own, but directly feed back into the core gameplay loop. I cannot stress how great it feels to interact with almost every part of this game.There is so much love and time poured into this project. Combined with a passionate and skillful team, this is one of those gems that will be placed among the greats along with the likes of terraria, stardew valley, and others. A game that will be used as inspiration for other projects in the future no doubt. Do yourself a favor and buy this game. Even at full price, there is so much value here that the 20 dollars will seem like a steal.

_childDocuments_.review: Neat adventure that goes all out to try and make it as pleasant and fun as possible (right until it doesn't)Visuals and music are nice, and basic mechanics are both polished and accessible. . Restaurant part, for example, might look daunting at first, but then you hire some help, and it always stays manageable — you can't go out of business, there are no penalties.That goes for about 10 to 20 hours, and again, diving, catching fish and selling sushi is polished. But then game tries to compensate its shallowness by providing as many sorts of (even more shallow) activities as possible, and finally goes overboard with it.Hey, here's some fish ponds so you don't haev to go and catch fish in a game of fish catching. And now there's farming with my most hated part of Stardew Valley — the watering can that you have to refill. Oh, and here's tamagochi minigame — because I clearly have extra free time to spend NOT playing the actual game.Another huge annoyance are unskippable content and cutscenes (not animated movies, but gameplay ones) . In some places game insists on grabbing your hand and forcing you through sidequest without option to say "maybe later please". Yes, I know what to do with that giant mirror and ray of light, that is not the first time I've seen that contraption in other games! No, I don't want to go and check on kaiju in a dark cave just now, I had other plans for this dive!

_childDocuments_.review: Well what an interesting idea for a game. Even in early access this game contains alot of content, after 12ish hours I've completed the story that is currently available and I think the majority of the side content as well. Where this game shines is the core gameplay loop, each day is split into 3, 2 dives during the day and a session in your restaurant. When diving you have multiple ways to catch fish including the harpoon several types of gun and even melee weapons. Along the way you will find many types of fish not only different species but with entirely different behavour, most will run from you but some will attack you others will flat out ignore you. Theres alot more involved in exploring the sea including hidden locations and gameplay elements but i will leave that for you to discover. When you finish diving for the day you get to run your sushi restaurant. Theres a heap in running it, you not only have to manage your menu which is tied to the fish you catch but you also have to worry about staffing including training and skills, decor and even special requests from customers. Once your restaurant takes off and you have a large number of menu items it gets very busy on a night between pouring tea (which makes customers tip more) ensuring your wasabi supplies are full (or else you cant even make anything) and cleaning up. This is a surprisingly complete game for something that is in early access. In my play I only encountered one bug which was a result of activating something out of sync. Overall I give this an 6/7 well worth the money
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Dave the Diver is a mix of a diving adventure, with some light simulation elements, and a restaurant manager in form of a Sushi bar, garnished with a lovely story and wrapped up in beautiful 2d pixel graphics. And you can feed cats :3   The general gameplay can be loosely sorted into 3 categories. Diving and collecting loot and fish for the restaurant, doing main and/or side story missions and working and managing the restaurant. Your day starts on your trusty boat in the morning (each day is divided into morning/afternoon/evening) and you set out to dive into the Blue Hole to collect fish / materials and other things for yourself and for your restaurant, or follow other various activities, the same happens in the afternoon and in the evening, you work in the restaurant. And while this may sound like a repetitive and boring – it is far from that.The Blue Hole is generated randomly to a degree. So while you might find certain fishes in the same depth regions, there is always some variation to the landscape and loot. Three times a week you can also put in an extra dive in the evening which allows you to hunt different fishes which only come out at night, but be careful, it’s dangerous! When you work for the restaurant, your job is to set up the menu, upgrade dishes and serve customers. With time you can hire new stuff and level them up to help you with the service or send them out on missions to collect certain ingredients. There are also some more unlocks later, but I don’t want to spoil anything here.  The money you make is used in various ways. To upgrade Dave’s gear, so he can dive for longer, carry more or dive deeper. Buy vanity items for the restaurant and other crafting efforts. Also later in the game, you unlock various side activities, which I won’t mention here.  -The graphics, Dave the Diver is certainly one of the most beautiful pixel art style games ever released, every part of the game is filled with lovely details, vibrant colors and lovely animations that often just put a big smile on your face. -You can feed and pat cats!-Beside the fantastic general gameplay, there are also a lot of side activities later in the game, which are just there to be enjoyed and nothing else. -The main story, but also the side stories are so much fun to play through-Characters/npcs – so many interesting personalities’, each with their own funny quirks and goals -Did I mention that you can pet cats?-Exploration: the Blue hole is vast, deep and filled with things to uncover -It’s fun to work the restaurant and see how it improves with time. Dave the Diver works so well as a game, all aspects of it go hand in hand together, from the gathering and upgrading to the restaurant management and Story, it all combines to an amazing and enjoyable adventure which I can only recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I am writing this review as soon as I got all the achievements available so far and I am sure I will not come back to this game until new contents are added. Dave the Diver is definitely one of the best games I've played recently. I am personally a big fan of oceanic games. This game certainly is one of the better ones when it comes to designing oceanic maps and creatures. I admire the amount of contents in this game --- especially different vibes for different levels and fishes. I also appreciate the difficulty of the main quest being very chill. A few times I thought I'd stuck for a bit, but it did not take me long to break through. The art style is very attractive and I assure you it only gets better. Many of the cut scene are so thoughtfully made I still watch them after countless number of times. The dishes was also so attractive that I straight up had sushi for dinner for a week. I may sound crazy but I'm pretty sure some of those fish were not supposed to be captured or killed or eaten, I think it would be a better idea if instead of dishes they can be donated to some sort of facilities that does legal research on those species while maintaining their financial value. I was surprised by how many contents are offered in this game, even beyond the basic diving. The mini games and different features you get as you progress the game felt endless in the first dozens of hours. This is such a rare trait in nowadays game. You get bored so quickly because their contents are so easily exhaustible. This is not to say the game is truly endless. In fact, after all the features are revealed, you get bored very quickly as diving no longer offers you the excitement of explorations, you only do because you want certain materials or ingredients to sustain your restaurant. But the end game of restaurants are so exponentially expensive that you won't last till you finish them. To chase the last few achievements I was so ready to get it over with and move on. The fact that no achievements for full collection etc also discouraged me from continuing. Though at this point it is almost a relief that I don't have to do more. There are also a lot of criticism towards the second half of the game, in which you get along with sea people and discovers a new area. The fact that randomness basically disappeared for newer regions is definitely somewhat disappointing. Although I really like the art style of the map and fishes, it basically became a routine near end game for me to get ingredient. A random terrain generator would definitely make this much much better. All and all, I would still recommend this game because the first 50 ish hours was fantastic experience. I mean, how many single player game offers you this many hours of joy?
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Dave the Diver is a fantastic casual game because it gives you so much to do. One day you might hunt for a specific fish that your sushi chef needs to impress a food critic. The next day you might gather driftwood and metals from the sea to craft a new gun. Then the next day a scientist commissions you to find a cave with relics of an ancient underwater race. You can farm veggies, work as a waiter in the sushi bar, fight bosses like giant sharks or krakens, race snails, collect pokemon cards, etc, etc, etc. Most aspects of the game are not very deep but the variety keeps you going for a really long time. Following the main story constantly unlocks new areas to visit with different fish, and new characters. New mechanics are slowly unlocked throughout the game, and there are tonnes of upgrades for everything.I also absolutely adored the pixel animations sprinkled throughout the game, I was surprised how many there were considering how long and high quality they were. They really add a lot of life and personality to a simple 2D game.Solid 8/10 for me, I did eventually get kinda tired of the main fishing game but £17 for 50 hours is pretty good value.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so refreshing in multiple ways. It's a product that feels very much cared for, both in the game design and art departments. It's got so much content, but the pace at which they give it to you doesn't feel overwhelming or confusing, and it remains surprising and engaging. I would compare this level of care to something like , another great game which handles character dialogue, progression and repetitive gameplay loops well in my opinion.I've played over half-way through the story so far while writing this review, and as someone who really enjoys these types of indie games, it already has made a spot in my top.This game is making a big  with its 1.0 release, and it deserves the attention!(Edit 21/07/23)So after beating the game and getting all of the achievements (which is something I rarely do) I can still recommend this game! I will say, it feels nice all the way until the end, though I do think that the post-game content is its weakest part, the gameplay is familiar and can get tiring after about 20-30 hours of beating the main game, so by all means, if you only do the main story and then never pick it up again, it's a great experience. I chose to continue, and I don't regret it, but I did feel like certain achievements became a chore.That's all for now, if they decide to update it with more content in the future, I will gladly play through it!

_childDocuments_.review: This game lies to you to think that it is a low budget indie game, until you start playing to realize that it's a 3D stylized masterpiece with tons of random content, full-fledged RPG story that keeps rolling out and spanning over more than 30 hours of playtime. Even so it maintains its intensity triggering all sorts of story moments and events that I find the development dedication unbelievable.Sound design that matches that "fake" retro pixel graphics are top notch, character "voices" are incredibly designed with a unique tone and demeanor for each character. You don't even need to look to know who's talking even though it's retro RPG sounding voices.If you're tired of generic games that are all around the same format, this is the game for you. It extracts various gameplay elements from the 2D game genres and presents them uniquely at different points of the game. It's fresh, it's really eye-opening, beautifully crafted, beautifully orchestrated, and really tons of little stupid content that needn't need to be in the game but exist.

_childDocuments_.review: What a perfect little gem of a game. Most writers of todays AAA-Games could take a long hard look on how to write characters probably even though it isn't the core of the game.You play as Dave the Diver (what a suprise I know!) and go down into the Deep Blue to catch fish by the day, and sometimes even at night, to sell them as Sushi in the evening. With the bucks earned you upgrade your diving gear to go even deeper and catch bigger targets while polishing the Sushi restaurant to satisfy your growing number of customers.But of course you got a nice little story with all its hurdles, humor, puzzles and Mini-Games to keep you company. The charming cutszenes with a huge variety of tributes to other things, memes etc. are just great and the music is absolutely glorious.There isn't really anything I disliked about the game, though I would say that a certain village you will encounter was a bit unutilized in my opinion and if you want to 100% the game you might find yourself just skipping through at the end to get it done. But none of those things take away from the ones which make this game so great. Even the credits aren't just music and names running down your screen but a Mini-Game as well!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game with a few annoyances. The highlight of the game is the diving and sushi restaurant mechanics. The first 10 hours felt like a "cozy" game, and I really enjoyed it. The later parts of the game end up being a ton of fetch quests that are pretty annoying and distract from the overall game. Nevertheless, I completed the game in about 46 hours with main story + all side quests completed. I didn't collect all fish or 100% all the available recipes which is a ton.The best way I can describe the game is if you took ALOT of flash mini games from mid 2000s and put them all into a game. This game has so many different mini games that I cannot give a count. The puzzles are not that hard in the game either. Replayability?: I probably wouldn't want to go through the whole story again, but I think I'll still hope on my current file and keep diving from time to time and earning money from restaurant. But there's not a lot of additional post ending replayability. By the time you beat the game, you should be earning so much money that you have nothing to spend it on. Hopefully devs had more post end content + things to spend $100,000s to spend on.

_childDocuments_.review: In "Dave the Diver" you play as Dave, who is not just a diver but also a manager/server at a restaurant, and a farmer of both plants and fish.  The core game play loop is Dave diving to collect fish and managing your restaurants menu.  Within the game you'll also explore the depths of the (as of current two) ocean maps, complete various quests given to you by a host of unique and fun characters, manage your restaurant by hiring/training staff, and overseeing your fish/rice farm.  The game starts you exploring a small portion of a what it calls a constant changing pocket of the ocean (again only two maps as of now) wherein after learning the controls you'll become a server in the restaurant slowly opening up more game play as you progress.Things done well in my opinion:- The core game play loop is enjoyable- There's a lot to do in the game- The NPS are silly, entertaining, and the dialog is fairly well written- Animations are over the top and a joy to watch (skippable after repeated viewings)- The oxygen as health bar mechanic adds a nice level of tension to the gameWhat needs work in my opinion:- There's a delay in trying to rapid fire your speargun that's annoying and makes fighting fast moving fish annoying- It has the "Mario" mechanic where simply touching an enemy damages you, when fighting larger fish this can be very annoying as the tail or fins will destroy you in close combat- Fish can get inside your hit box wherein you're unable to repel them.  If you're heavy this can outright kill you as you're unable to escape- It would be nice to be able to change the music around and "Set" it to different locations.  As it is now, you can listen to any of the music you unlocked in the game on your phone but that's all you can do with it.Overall "Dave the Diver" is quite a fun game and I would recommend it to others.

_childDocuments_.review: Dave the diver is a lovely game! _childDocuments_.review: I must admit, Dave The Diver took me by surprise. _childDocuments_.review: A collage of all kinds of addictive game doesn't make it a good game. It feels very bloated and tiring rather than layered. Even the graphics is not consistent with so many different styles like pixel, watercolor, cartoon, etc etc... Seems a bit desperate already.Didn't see much criticism on the design of characters and plots in the comment but thought it was the worst part. There are so many stereotypes presented not in a fun way e.g. Duff the weapon specialist has some lines that are full of male gaze (I don't get the importance of an otaku character in this game?? It feels super abrupt and shows no consideration for female players); The ancient civilization sea people too serve no use for the game and are designed as brainless and selfish creature. Super patriarchal, too: when dave refused to rescue the sea people one female character said "but I am a wounded woman"... The developers also somehow have an underlying hostility towards the environmentalists, calling them creepy at the first encounter and designed them as extremely hypocritical who received bribes from big corps. The battles against this environmentalist group are also full of unnecessary sarcasm. If you are looking for a fun game, this is at least fun to play; but it's not a good game and definitely overhyped imo. And make sure that you know some plots are very annoying before diving into it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a solid experience at the start but then it kinda starts to drag due to getting busy work and because your time in the ocean scales a ton while the management side gets left behind pretty quickly.The issue is that later enemies get really annoying with their movesets and you don't really get a good answer to them.  This leads to long drawn out battles with frustrating intermissions if you dare to encouter a trash mob while fighting them.The issue with imbalance between gameplay is probably even larger, you can stay under water for like 20-60 minutes later on, while the entire above-ocean part never really goes past 5-10 minutes. The game is called Dave the Diver, not the restaurant owner, so that seems like a weird complaint, however there is no real payoff for staying underwater so long. Due to massive costs you get progress gated hunting the same fish over and over again accumulating wealth and building up more stockpiles which get invalidated every once in a while anyway. It's gotten to the point where I'm honestly thinking about just skipping through days to make money and stop fishing all together.Finally, the mission design. This is probably the main issue, a lot of them just feel like really pointless busywork. Get 10 of this material, dive to that location and take a picture, go back to the surface and come back tomorrow, etc. When you reach the village it gets really bad, be prepared for multiple hours of mmorpg-side-quest-tier quests.All in all, it's a good 7/10 experience that kind of loses its charm halfway through but still gives you enough systems to ineract with to keep you somewhat hooked.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is wild. So I'll keep it short and as spoiler free as possible. Do you like capitalism and running your own business? Do you like large sandboxes/slightly open-world exploration that's semi-rogue-like? Do you like games that teeter the fine line between parody and copyright infringement? Then this is your game. You play as a diver named (Spoiler!) Dave who's coerced into catching fish during the day and serving them to patrons at a sushi restaurant during the evening. Game progression is simple: you catch fish, you sell fish, you use money for upgrades. As Dave continues to forego his right to decline favors, you unlock more activities, areas, and tools that'll help you on your quest to become the pushover you were always meant to be. There's so much content despite being a $20 game. So if you're ready to "dive" in with Dave, I guarantee it'll definitely be worth your while; unless you dislike all of the aforementioned things above.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a relaxing, wholesome, fun, and in some cases grindy game with a lot of different content. Main idea is to catch fish in the mornings and afternoons and make them into sushis in the evenings. But there is way too much different content to simplify the game into this sentence. There are different quests involving "sea people" a lot of collectibles, godzilla, so many different and fleshed-out characters, different tools, farming, harvesting, feeding the cat, improving dishes, even making the dishes, catching fishes in the vortices, killing bosses, so many different side missions, even like destroying asteroids, and playing tamagotchi on your phone inside of the game. There are so many more different content that is unlocked as you play and there is always something to do. It's one of those, "one more round" games and it is not like a grind-fest but it is filled with funny little cutscenes and fun story. Again, it's a relaxing wholesome game that I am glad I played. Easy recommendation

_childDocuments_.review: Played a few hours on the Steam Deck OLED.What I liked:- The game looks really good! The style and animations. The mix of pixel art and 3D is really well executed- The soundtrack- How the game manages to blend diving, fishing, deep sea exploration and sushi restaurant management- Dave and his big smile. I love his attitude and positivism- The main cast of 3. I even managed to notice character development from the ChefWhat I didn't like- The game started to overwhelm me with too many new features very early on, like new apps, events and tasks- Enhancing sushi with epic animations were fun the first time, but they could've been just very short animation clips- Upgrading my diving equipment was underwhelming- The attitude of most side characters. Why is everyone so rude towards Dave?- The Weapons Specialist being a stereotypical otaku was weird- You're always dropped in the same location in Blue Hole- Loading times when transitioning between locations took a little while to load up (even on Steam Deck OLED M.2)- Some minor game design decisions-  Not wholesomeThe game wasn't quite what I wanted it to be.The sushi restaurant management gameplay with time limits and things to do, paired with multiple tasks and events going on at the same time were a little too stressful for me to enjoy.As my experience wasn't quite what I was expecting, I refunded the game.The game is casual, but not relaxing.Either way, just because of the uniqueness of the game, I'd recommend anyone to try it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most strongly compelled I have ever felt to review a game, and even if at 40k+ reviews as of writing it kind of feels like adding water to the ocean (ha), I still need to share my thoughts on this game.I honestly do not remember when this ended up on my wishlist. I do not remember what exactly, in the midst of this years-long (sometimes somewhat tiresome) "post-Stardew Valley sim boom" we currently find ourselves in, drew me to this game among so many others. Maybe that's just the insane gravity of Dave's charisma.I think I got this game in the first week of official launch and haven't looked back. I have annoyed friends, family, and Discord servers in my quest to beg everyone to play this game. I might have even looked into learning to free dive, if I lived in a more agreeable climate. This is all for you, Dave.My personal problem with a lot of farm/resource/restaurant sim type games is how quickly the core gameplay loop seems to grow stale. Dave the Diver sidesteps this entirely by combining several different gameplay loops into each in-game day, all of which also being just short enough to keep the loop feeling fun and varied, while also providing constant clean breaks to save and quit for the day. I have a full-time office job and plenty of home responsibilities (all of which I have neglected in some way to squeeze in more diving hours) so being able to pick this up just for one or two loops at times is very appealing to me. Even after finishing the story, I still feel the pull to keep leveling my equipment, sushi, and inventory.It's kind of weird to have to say this, but I can't remember the last time I played a game like this that felt so "complete" and well-rounded in its presentation. This game was clearly made with love in every aspect. Every facet of the gameplay and design feels as equally deliberate and polished as every other, even if some make very brief appearances. The story is fun and compelling without getting too heavy, and never drags. The character writing is effortlessly funny and charming without being in-your-face about certain characteristics that ABSOLUTELY would have been driven right into the dirt in most other games. Basically nothing overstays its welcome. So much so that when the OBLIGATORY farming mechanic made its appearance, I was actually super excited to see how this would expand my restaurant menu, instead of groaning at what could have felt like a gamedev checkbox.This is so so so so SO lame to say but all in all I would say Dave The Diver is like a serving of high-end sushi: it is complete, it is deliberate in all its choices, and satisfies while leaving you wanting for just a little more. A+ game, I want Dave to be my best friend.

_childDocuments_.review: Decided to revise my review after reaching the Glacier Area.Pros:1. Animations during upgrades/enhancements are pretty interesting. I especially like the Bancho ones.2. The atmosphere is great when diving. You really feel like you are diving. And when you see sharks, whales etc, you get the feels.3. Sushi Restaurant is fun.4. Lack of time limits means you can mostly take your time doing stuff.5. Catching fish is fun and going up against bigger predators are kinda exciting.Cons:1. A lot of stuff is not explained and they just throw you in the deep end. For example, the cooking competitions ( I especially hate the part where they ask you to dip the fish in the batter), and the sparkly stuff that is displayed when you kill sharks. Poison harpoon that need circular motion, it doesn't state how big a circle you need to create. I play with keyboard and mouse and it is really annoying.2. QTEs that require you to mash buttons to do certain actions in order to get harpoon tips to work render some harpoon weapon types useless if you don't have fast enough reflex or understand how it works.3. Useless melee weapon types. After you upgrade your melee weapon, imagine picking up a golf ball or something that renders the mining ability useless and you are not allowed to drop the weapon after you pick it up.4. Guns require higher ammo slots. 3 shots is stupid especially for the low range guns, 5. I want a mini map function. Yes I know the map changes each time. _childDocuments_.review: This game is like 5 games in one. It uses a scatter-gun approach to appeal to every type of player, which is the major issue. I liked the diving aspect of the game but putting that on pause to do chores was very annoying in the long run and made me quit the game. The game gives you timed objectives and it provides unnecessary pressure to do things optimally instead of playing and trying things as you go. It is an okay casual game for its price, but after a while, the progression slows down a lot and you are grinding for things you don't care about. The best part about the game imo is the presentation and style, but the other negatives overpower it after a while.Still a solid 15-20 hr experience, maybe more if you like the scatter-gun approach.

The game mechanic becomes longer and longer so the fun decreases a lot. Despite new mechanics like a fish farm it gets very monotone. Some dialog cant be skipped... There should be some sort of advice what to serve for the customer and not this simple mechanic of i serve the most expensive stuff as much as possible. _childDocuments_.review: Update22h later I "finished" the game (main story), there is still more to explore and enjoy.This game kept surprising and entertaining me the whole ride. There are tons of activities and minigames, loveable characters and funny, cheesy montages stretched over the whole game. The one thing I didn't get: bored.It's outstanding game throughout, diving (pun intended) through the history of videogames with countless minigame homages while keeping a unique very upbeat game world of its own. FUN is priority number one and the Korean team delivered a master piece.It's noteworthy, that I didn't encounter a single bug or crash through my playthrough, something equally uncommon in this day and age of day-1-patches and "high-end" engine crashes (UE5 :/ )YOU CALL YOURSELF A GAMER? GET THIS GAME!---------------------------------------Awesome adventure/management game focusing on fun, humour and excellent, varied gameplay. Controls with gamepad are great and responsive (haven't tried mouse & keyboard yet).I played 5 hours straight, something I cannot tell about many recent AAA games, no matter how well received.The gameplay is fun and captivating. Capable diver at day, fishing and exploring for new ingredients to help the local sushi bar's master chef. Restaurant manager and short-breathed waiter at night. You hire service workers, improve the bar's interior and renomée to turn the restaurant into a gold mine by time, luring in foodies and gourmets from all over the world.At day you try to improve your gear with the hard-earned money, and indulge yourself in side missions and local mysteries. Dodgy researchers, militant eco warriors, rumors of seafolk, trading card collectors, an eccentric weapon maker etc. spice up your day and night activities.The game is well worth its money. After 5 hours, I got about a third of the achievements, so I expect at least another 10 glorious and fun hours.Most positive surprise of the year, to me. Give it a shot!

_childDocuments_.review: I felt that I had to rewrite my review. Before I just wrote that it was a great game but I feel that it deserves a bit more than that, so here I go:This is a great game that is clearly made with love. The basic gameplay loop is simple: Dive, get some fish and go back up. Do this twice and then at evening you'll serve sushi and drinks to earn money which you use to upgrade gear to dive deeper or carry more fish. Simple right? But what makes this game so good is just everything about it. The music is very fitting for the locations, the cutscenes are funny and well made. For me the game never really feel tedious either which is a great plus.While the basic gameplay loop is simple, you'll get introduced to new things constantly but it never becomes overwhelming and it just make the game better. Dave the Diver has a lot of minigames but they are very rarely used more than once so it always feel fresh from start to finish. At this moment I have played the game for around 69 hours and I still have some things that I need to do, and I will gladly do it.All in all, I cannot recommend this game enough and strongly hope that everyone that are thinking of buying Dave the Diver, do so for a relaxing fun experience!!

_childDocuments_.review: All in all, a pretty good game. I was drawn in by pretty graphics and running the restaurant is fun. The diving mechanics are fun and can punish you for being caviler with your oxygen. This game unfortunately tries to do far too many things at once however. Running/stocking the restaurant is busy, but then they throw a whole farm and fishery at you which don't quite replace manually getting ingredients and feels like a ton of busywork. By the time the branch game around I was so mentally checked out that I didn't bother. Your character is entirely 1 dimensional which is okay, but the dialogue gets so bad and repetitive mid to late game. Your character has to stop the game and comment on every small thing he sees, literally tells you how to complete every puzzle and treats you like a 3 year old. Another issue is that it claims to be a different generated dive each type, which really just cycles between 2-3 presets and gets incredibly stale. There is a lot of over-explanation for simple things (like the puzzles) and no explanation for the vague things like how the fishery actually works. This is a bit of a rant, but this game was so close to being great that I'm sad what it becomes after the initial few days. I wish they had just focused on refining fewer mechanics rather than slapping in as many as they could, but to each their own.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I had a positive experience. It kept me playing through when AAA titles like Hogwarts, Horizon, AC, GOW RE etc all fail to keep me playing for more than 30 min.The game runs and plays well on my M3 Macbook Air, as well as gaming PC. A xbox controller is recommended.The diving/exploration got one-dimensional and repetitive quickly. It's visually appealing and engaging but despite not having a map/navigation system, the ocean feels more like an aquarium or a swimming pool as you quickly reach the limits of the map. But even then, some of the key locations require repeated visit & special tools to progress the story and it can be a chore to get to them every time.I enjoy the restaurant sim, and I'd say that's the most fun bit to me. Once you build up a good ingredient inventory and hire some helpers, it's very fun to set the menu, see customers pour in as you attend to them, and run the restaurant.The short animations that sometimes play when you upgrade/enhance something or when cook something special, is very stylized and creative. I like these bits and how they can be skipped after first viewing.The main story arc is where I have mixed feelings with. One the one hand it's pretty... imaginative, and also adds mystery to the dives, and helps push Dave's arc forward. However most of the time I just want to get back to diving, catching exotic fish, explore the world, etc. I wish I could be left alone with all the plot development, or choose to progress at my own pace.I got WeMod and it works with this game very well, despite WeMod showing a warning message. I set movement speed to 2x for Dave and it helps with the diving pacing a lot. Also can adjust resources so don't have to grind. (I'm not affiliated with or paid by WeMod or anything...) I do think the game would feel more rewarding if I did not use any mods.Anyway I have no regret with this purchase, and no regret spending time in this game world. I hope the dev can continue to create more content, a sequel, or release more games that are varied and interesting like this one.Some suggestions though on this game: It would be awesome if there's more undersea locations, or make it bigger but can be charted/mapped, with custom marking function to notate spawn spots of certain species. Also better fish management by type, kind, etc, maybe a search function. Also the game would be a lot more respectable if there's more actual scientific/biological facts about some of the fish in the game, so that I might learn a thing or two about my catches.Anyways cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: It’s so nice to finally be able to play as a fat character in a video game. Dave do be divin’ straight into our heart.My wife’s boyfriend loved this one. It’s like a mash up of every genre he likes plus his favorite food type.This game brings me great joy. Not just fun, but joy. As my wife always says about making love, "I only wish it was longer".Dave the Diver is something totally different to me and I really loved it. I have a stressful job and this time of the year is really especially exhausting, but playing this on the weekend and evenings really gets me out of my head. It’s fun to discover new things and animals in the water, the sea people are hilarious, the restaurant is thrilling to me, and I love discovering new dishes. I really enjoyed the story and characters. Something really resonates with me about being a fat guy who is unappreciated by the people who depend on him. His main motivation is to eat delicious food and live a comfortable life, yet gets dragged along into other people's adventures. Dave isn't a hero, he is a guy who is certified to do a technically complex thing that nobody else in the area seems to be able to do. A little bit like me in real life. It’s just so delightful to me.Basically it's two games in one, sushi management game with exploring the ocean/getting supplies for the resturant. It seems initially simple but hides a lot of complexity in the mechanics but it's also very forgiving, can be played for ten mins or two hours at a time, lots of different mechanics that gradually unlock, lots of different activities you can choose to focus on (or completely ignore if it's not your thing), great art style, funny characters and a good story that you just want to explore. The loop is essentially you get two dives per day, and each dive stops when either you decide to finish early, or you run out of oxygen. In each dive, you can catch fish, which you then bring back to the restaurant which runs at night, and you play a hectic 5 or so minutes where you try to get everyone their food and drinks. You then earn some money for the night, which you can then spend the next day on improvements to your diving gear (e.g. oxygen tank capacity and fish carrying capacity) or on the restaurant (e.g. hiring and training staff). The loop itself is great, but what sets it apart from other games to me is how nearly every day you'll get an NPC calling you/driving a boat to you and starting you on a side quest which leads to new equipment/abilities/game features. There's even a whole side story about an Atlantis-type region with mermaids.Oh, and the pixel art cutscenes. So many beautiful pixel art cutscenes, for even the most trivial of things (e.g. asking someone to upgrade your weapon). Aside from the epic cutscenes and beautiful presentation, the gameplay loop has enough variety to keep it fresh while avoiding being tedious and boring. As you progress, you get access to diffrent interfaces and information. So at first you are just having fun exploring but as you continue you have the tools to be more meticilious about your planning. There is some real love in this game, for nerd culture and for the ocean and it drips from every dramatic scene we get.I think my favorite part overall is how seriously casual it is. As far as I know, you have absolutely no reason to do anything you don't want to do. You can't really "miss" anything and there's no specific reward for doing things the "right" way. After you unlock a couple of things, you can actually stay down in the water as long as you want because you can refill your O2 indefinitely. Or conversely, you don't actually have to dive in the water except for some very early stuff where the game forces you to.You can't 'die' in Dave the Diver. If you run out of oxygen, you get rescued and you just don't get anything from that particular dive. If you don't deliver something at the restaurant fast enough, you just... don't make as much money. But there's no 'you lose' state for Dave the Diver. There's just faster or slower progression. There are so few games that are both fun and engaging while also being so casual and flexible. It's refreshing.I think if you try to put the game into a neat category you'll struggle with it. I wouldn't see it as "a fishing game" or "a restaurant manager" or "farming game" or something like this. If you see the game as a collection of minigames with an overall exploration and underwater-hunting-game as the thing that ties all together, its great fun and you won't go into it with wrong expectations.Overall the game is super charming and keeps things fresh by introducing new mechanics at a very regular pace. There’s a great balance in that you always feel like there's something "extra" to be working on in addition to the loop of fishing and restaurant management.  But it also doesn't overload you with sidequests. It plays around with way more ideas than a little indie game feels like it should be able to, but everything it adds is always very simple so it never feels overwhelming. I highly recommend it.It’s a 10/10 for me, but I’ll make it a 20/10 if they make it so you can see Oceangate at the bottom in an update or something.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really good and deserves a positive review score. But Overwhelmingly Positive is a stretch imo.I give a thumbs down to balance the review score out and hopefully devs read negative comments for feedback.Apart all the good things you can read in other comments the game has some severe issues in pacing and balancing.--SPOILERS---- Pacing --You get thrown a lot of events and cut scenes and stuff day after day and do not have any time to adjust. Way too many missions are time sensitive and you progress way too fast at the beginning which results in being stuck in a terrible state in late-mid game. Your quest tab is filled almost every day in the game. I unlocked almost platinum and am on the way to diamond (last level of sushi bar) but did not even manage to unlock the smithy in the fish village. And this is not because of me not trying. Now I need to catch way too many fish for the night and 20 of my 30 +7 lvl recipes do not bring in enough money to keep me in the plus because I unlocked fish farm too late?I managed to get the "cucumber festival" BEFORE I even unlocked the farm to harvest cucumbers in the game? When I had unlocked the farm at the end the event was 1 day away and I could not even plant anything. Practically "failing" the festival. I am pretty sure that the game wants you to chill because the festivals and events probably reappear on a loop like they do in stardew valley calender style. I am also sure that there are many players who just relax and ignore quests but power players or completionists/perfectionists like me try to do everything as efficient as possible. In that case the game hustles you a lot and punishes you for following through and doing a lot. ?!?The game needs to spread out the events way more than it does at the moment. It needs more roadblocks to block you from progressing too fast and needs to check some parameters before unlocking events/quests. Basically only unlocking them when you are actually ready to take them on. Compared to other games of the same category the pacing is not good.-- Bosses --I've got the "klaus the white shark" boss event twice now , which is apparently meant to be beaten as the last boss because I cannot beat it in my current upgrade state and fail the mission and have to wait for another stormy weather. And I have a 0.5% rarity achievement for upgrading a gun 3 times so it cannot be my equipment or oxygen levels. You cannot restart days so once you decided to go in your equipment choices are locked and you either win or ♥♥♥♥ up the boss fights. In fact the boss fights and how they are handled is one of the most common critiques you can read in the internet.I hope the developers do balance the boss fights a little to get closer to "casual and chill" experience. Because at the moment the shark feels like I am trying to beat smoug and ornstein with a broken sword in dark souls. And if it supposed to be the very last hardcore boss of the game why do you throw it at me in mid-game? Twice? You dive to fish for night's shift to fulfill a request. As you dive suddenly: Cutscene! Even the main story itself became very irritating at certain points, PARTICULARLY BOSS FIGHTS. Based on how much effort was put into the best parts of the game, I'm surprised at how abysmal the boss design is. Thankfully this is not what the majority of the game is spent on. Dave the Diver feels like an amazing early access game, but it isn't early access. I have enjoyed most of my time playing, but large parts of it outside of the main gameplay loop simply feel unfinished or tacked-on. _childDocuments_.review: Dave the Diver is a frenetic arcade of mini-games and quick-time events that provide a compelling gameplay & story experience, while simultaneously being the kind of game you can use to unwind at the end of the day or kill a few hours on a road trip.What I find intriguing about Dave the Diver is that it’s core gameplay is so uninteresting and repetitive, yet it’s used as a foundation for such a variety of minigames and side quest-like content that can truly captivate you for the entire ~30 hour runtime. Thirty hours, from a game whose central gameplay wouldn’t be fun by itself. Diving down & harpooning fish can get repetitive and monotonous, and the relaxing, slow-paced nature of the activity doesn’t present much opportunity for mechanical challenge or mastery. Instead, Dave the Diver shines in overwhelming you with characters who will either task you to do something fun & different while diving – go find this specific cave, catch this funny looking fish, take a picture of this thing – or reward you with a new between-dive gameplay mechanic for serving them their favourite dish. You will get quests from so many different sources so rapidly and in such quantities that you can’t keep track of them all, let alone complete them in a single dive, which gives you something to go back for the next time, and the next, and the next. While you’re playing through higher production quality missions, there’s also a plethora of collect-athon type content to explore: finding certain colour seashells in ridiculous quantities, catching a large number of a certain fish, collecting materials for weapon upgrades, the list goes on. This really helps Blue Hole come alive as you need to pay attention to every environmental detail, as you may spot something that’ll progress one of these medium-term goals while you’re on your way to a specific area to progress the story. All of these things to do and collect then feed back into the myriad of upgrade options or things you want to buy. There’s a huge variety here too – upgrades for your diving gear, restaurant, weapons, and other facilities you unlock as you progress through the game.Speaking of detail, the care and attention put into the art in this game is phenomenal. The 2D pixel art is easy on the eyes despite holding a good level of detail, the animated cutscenes are full of personality, and the occasional 3D cooking minigame or water creature gives the game flexibility to use more fluid animations, without creating distracting visual noise from all the aliasing. Keeping the textures of 3D models as pixel art keeps them grounded within the game’s art style so they never feel out of place or jarring. One quick thing to note though is that battery life on a handheld console like the Steam Deck might not be what you would expect of a simple 2D pixel art game, as the ocean you’re diving in is rendered in 3D, requiring more power to do so. The game doesn’t struggle for performance by any means, but you’re not going to get pure-2D game battery life here.To touch more on the game’s cast, they’re all vibrant people bursting with personality. They all have unique mumbles for their dialogue, but where they really come alive is in the animated cutscenes. You need only to encounter Duff for the first time and ask him to make a weapon to see what I mean. Dave the Diver isn’t afraid to poke at stereotypes and stretch them into absurdity; this isn’t a serious game, and the cutscenes are designed to make you laugh. They do an outstanding job of breathing life into the characters, and even those that don’t get a little cinematic are written with a clear personality and/or accent in mind that keeps everyone feeling unique.The full version of my review is on my website as it exceeds Steam's character limit:

_childDocuments_.review: ON A GAMEPLAY NOTE:So, generally, i dont like writing reviews. its a hassle. But... I want to love this game. I really do. So why is it, the one thing the game is good at, it seems to... not want you to do? the loop of fishing, and running the sushi place, generally feels good enough that i wanna ignore everything else, but instead im stuck in chapter 4s boring plot.Have fun, every other day, getting dragged along into some boring side quest for a 1 note character, that ends in you swimming some place youve passed and never interacted with before 20 times before. and then. having to end the game to be spoon fed an item to solve this "puzzle". _childDocuments_.review: TLDR; This game has a lot of charm. I feel as though there are flaws to the diving experience that make it difficult to enjoy at times, so I can't say that I recommend it at its current state.--- The restaurant aspect is quite fun; I wish it were more central to the gameplay! The process of growing your business is addictive, and I think this is where it shines. The animations for special guests, interactive food serving mechanics (like serving various drinks!); the only issue I have is that I wish it could be longer. Granted, I'm only two chapters in, and I understand that this game is meant to focus on the diving part.Unfortunately, to say that the restaurant part outshines the diving part is telling of the latter's flaws. I have a growing list of issues in my diving experience that is making it difficult to enjoy.- Scripted diving moments feel too disruptive. I might go down to focus on catching all kinds of fish as well as finishing up a fetch quest for a customer only to end up fighting a boss I did not expect. The rude interruptions of my expeditions (where after certain quests are complete, I'm forced to go back up to the boat and wait for the next day to fish again) is not fun. There was a countdown toward an event where I had to prepare a bunch of menu items of a specific kind (jellyfish), and when the day came, a quest regarding the sea people forced me to miss the opening of the restaurant. I thought I had missed the event as well and was upset. Fortunately, it did push to the next day, but this felt like a bug to me.  - There should be an ability to reference other info besides quests while diving. I get that having a smartphone underwater is not realistic, but I feel like it's necessary to be able to access info on what fish you need to get (for certain menu items, for achievements). Or even like, where I could find certain fish? All of this is available on your phone and the restaurant, but not while you're diving? Just something to think about.- Diving controls feel really muddy to me. This issue is glaring especially during combat events; it just isn't fun to struggle because aiming is limited and you can't turn as quickly to avoid wide attacks. I wish that moving around felt more responsive, but it's too slow and limiting at its current state. I know that charms exist to boost certain stats, but in my opinion the difference is negligible. I am sure that time will either prove that the developers can create a more cohesive, enjoyable experience, or that this game is simply not for me. I really want to like this game, so my fingers are crossed.

_childDocuments_.review: I was never a fan of RPGs until l traded swords and spells for sushi and scuba in the whimsical .I was never much into the sword and sorcery genre. My first exposure to  was  on Intellivision, which is more of a proto- than a dice-rolling campaign. My tastes leaned more towards He-Man than Conan, less Middle Earth than . ? . And so forth.Imagine my surprise when by sheer curiosity I played an RPG where instead of leveling up the stats on a rogue mage, I swam calmly through a magical reef filled with marine life from every ocean, catching a few rare fish to serve in the beachfront sushi place I share with my shady equipment supplier buddy and an enigmatic samurai chef.This description barely scratches the surface of what  brings to the table. It's challenging without being frustrating. Whimsical without being pretentious. Casual, addictive, and above all, relaxing.Even more impressive is the fact that developer MINTROCKET and publisher Nexon Korea frequently publish new content and updates that keep you coming back to the Giant Blue Hole. is the closest thing a graphic adventure game has ever come to being ASMR. The highest of compliments for a casual game.
