_childDocuments_.review: is an enjoyable and challenging adventure game made by . Players take control of Dave, a deep-sea diver, and explore the beauty of the designed and made ocean in search of the treasure and secrets it holds. This game was really fun to open every day just to relax, waste good hours diving, exploring, and doing a lot of side content it has to offer. One of the things that makes Dave the Diver so enjoyable is its unique gameplay. You get to explore a big underwater world, and hunt for some fish to sell in your Sushi Restaurant ( YES! This game also features a fun and challenging Sushi Restaurant minigame where you can take a break from diving ). This game also has a lot of different varieties of fish you can catch some are small and friendly, others are deadly and huge.+ Very addictive gameplay loop that is both relaxing and challenging and never gets boring as it constantly introduces new mechanics as you play.+ Lot of content here from diving and catching fish to exploring the big ocean to running a Sushi restaurant to Farming to Fish breeding games to Taking photographs to Racing Seahorses. YEAH! There is a lot of content here.+ Well-written Story with well-written and interesting characters you meet along the way and plenty of good humor that will surely make you laugh for smile.+ Well-made cutscenes and a very Beautiful art direction with a lot of pleasing scenery.+ Incredible Soundtrack that definitely had me jammed and I will surely keep on listening to it on Spotify or Youtube.+ Boss Battles might be irritating and challenging at times BUT they were well-designed and presented unique challenges and required different strategies to overcome.+ If you are a fan of collecting stuff, this game also offers that. You can collect over 100+ cards in Dave the Diver by exploring, opening treasures, and hunting for fishes- There were a few bugs I faced during my playthrough which is not a major negative of this game but still wanted to mention them.- Dave the Diver can sometimes struggle with pacing also which I didn’t like. A good example is at one point in the game, you are focused on doing the main story mission objective when suddenly you get a call to get stuff for a VIP who has visited your restaurant so you need to switch focus on completing that cause it is time-limited and then you also need to do other side missions along the way which also are time-limited… Of course, they are not necessary to do, but if you get hooked on the game, you get the urge to do them, and hence the momentum you had going while following main story missions is gone.

_childDocuments_.review: It was hard to decide where to fall on the thumb direction front here.  Dave the Diver is an attractive game, with a fun story.  The varied mechanics of exploration, fishing, management, etc. keep you engaged with the grind without it becoming boring and they do a really good job of slowly opening up new complexity as the story progresses.But.The game heavily relies on QTE mechanics for most of the fishing.  This seems original at first, but becomes old fast.  Eventually you'll see it at best as a way to slowly break your controller, at worst as a shocking absence of accessibility.  Some of the motions, on the wider grip of the Steam Deck, can even become painful.  They also don't work very well when performance dips.  The interface also struggles when you have multiple options - it offers button prompts that won't react because you are either moving, not in perfect pixel position for their trigger, or there is another overlapping prompt that causes you to do something unexpected.Performance was initially good on the Steam Deck, but over the course of patching (or potentially game progress) it has gone into the (fish) tank.  This makes a lot of the game difficult to achieve when it requires good timing, and it's unpleasant to play.Many of the boss fights are just not fun to play.  There's a trick to each one, and once you find it that's fine, but often it's very easy to think you've done the right thing but the game doesn't register it because their alignment of action to graphics seems off.  Sometimes they seem just downright un-fun - because your health and oxygen and therefore dashing are all linked, you can get yourself into a position where you might as well give up and reset the fight as you literally don't have the resources to do it.  It's like a bad puzzle that also relies on janky AI and badly tuned models.I think overall I've got to thumb the game down.  As usual, a game ruined by a lack of testing and reviews that are too busy fawning over prettiness to actually consider the real issues with the game.

Many hours of fun to be had and well worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: If there were a "neutral" review, I'd use it. As-is, I have to go with a negative review. This game has a great concept bogged down by a lot of little mechanics that don't really do anything. This game feels extremely unfocused, like the developers just kept adding features with no regard for consistent tone or coherent gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very good game and I will continue playing. Thumbs down to get attention from devs as there are many important details that still makes this overrated and overpriced:- No procedural dives, what you get is always the same with more parts of the same map being available with each update.- Too many events, there are things happening constantly and the game holds you tight by the hand, never giving options or letting go. You follow tasks, millions of cutscenes, after a while feels incredibly forced.- Punishment is too cruel. A fish charges at you in a second and you press up or down a little too late? 99% of inventory gone along with half the day, which might make you lose a time constrained mission. Better to do ctrl+alt+delete instantly. - You have 30 degrees of shooting while fish charges you from any angle. - If you pick up a gun, the old one is gone forever.- The crates have so little possibilities, nothing surprises after only couple of hours of playing.- To check what missions you have is a pain. Along with new creatures and eco missions. You just play with a lot of guessing.- You constantly have to sacrifice fish to gain better meals. And those better meals can't be done anymore because you used the fish to upgrade. Horrible trade-off each time I'm at the restaurant.- The restaurant is also insanely simple. You go right, you go left. You have 3 optional minigames which are also too simple. No control, no fun, bad bad game design. I can hardly call that a game.- Crafting is extremely boring and what you get is basically a gun which you can find below in a second anyway. Played 5 hours, no ultra special guns.Guys, let's be realistic. This is not overwhelmingly positive. This is a nice little korean game, with very cool pixel art and amazing music. I would be a very happy buyer if this was 5 EUR but not 20... If the devs are hardworking though, I can see how it can be one of my all time favs. Just not right now.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the best $20 I've spent on entertainment since Cultist Simulator. Loads of fun, perfect progression, tons of variety of stuff to do to keep things engaging.My one complaint ~~is~~ was that some of the relevant data is hidden. It's impossible to see how many customers you have or project each night, how much your employees get paid, and some other little things that would make it a little easier to manage the restaurant aspect.But after playing it some more, I don't know that it's really a problem. I've never been short on money and not having that system means that I can focus on the fun parts instead of looking too closely at optimizing things.Still, the game is very chill, and I've never had to worry about balancing things too closely. If you don't like the restaurant part, it's easy to hire employees, train them, and have them do all the work. If you enjoy it yourself, you don't have to hire the help. Pretty clever system.Overall it's a great casual ... I want to say roguelike, but that's not quite right. It's like Spelunky in that the level changes every run, but you never play a different character. There's a great variety of equipment and things to discover, though, and it perfectly scratches an itch I have for something relaxing and fun.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great but unpolished.Things that feel lacking:Content: You finish the main quest chain 25-40 days of playing, and from there you get a branch option but quests and boss fights more or less come to a total stop. Once the branch is up and running basically you can buy everything within a week after the branch  opens if you didn't already have it. There inst much left to do other than grind out about 20-30 recipes. Time: I don't think they need to use a 365 day 12 month calendar, I made it to mid November, I have no major purchases left to make and I sitting on 6 figures worth of gold, I have all of the achievements except the one to feed the cat 20 times and the phone game achievements. There doesn't seem like anything really to do, I think having four seasons of 28 days like they do in Stardew Valley would make more sense. I would dive for Threshers, tuna, marlins, sailfish, hammerheads, crabs, and then head to the glacial  areas for the three sharks, and whatever else I could fill up on, the average dive time gets closer to 25-30 minutes unless I am looking for all available resources or looking for a tranq harpoon. Needless to say you could almost make every dive last a hour if you wanted to look at everything, making every day two hours long. Seasonal fish over random spawns would be preferable. I once went 10 days without seeing the cave with the sea grapes, and I also went almost as many days without seeing a Bonito spawn, the only curry fish that sells worth a ♥♥♥♥ and missed it altogether for the Curry party.It doesn't seem like there is enough to do at the sushi restaurant, the fact every thing is simply a vanity item for decoration and doesn't do anything to impact sells or bring in customers is a bit upsetting. I wish you could expand your restaurant or maybe compete against other restaurants. Once you beat the main quest line and events come to a trickle it just gets to be a grind for what?The mermaid city is too big, I get you can hire the Whale to move faster, but it is needlessly too big of an area for what is offered there. the Casino should have items to buy, or a way to sell seahorses. They probably should have a fish market of some sort too. I wish the other two nodes at the fish farm you could custom put single species of fish into. The eco terrorists aren't ever really dealt with either, seems like a loose end.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know what to say about this game. I'm 6 hours in with 12/15 achievements. I'm not sure how much more there is to this game, but from what I've played this game is not worth full price or the overwhelmingly positive review it holds. Is it fun? It's okay. The diving is alright but fish quickly become redundant when you upgrade your gear and can catch fish worth way more. The restaurant aspect quickly becomes pretty much automated when you hire a few employees, leaving you to clean up the same way and not tend to the unique orders. When I saw the reviews and the art style I thought it would be a relaxing game like Stardew Valley, but this game is not that. Diving you're forced into encounters with enemies that require slight timing/pressing the correct button to avoid and button mashing. The restaurant sim requires you run up and down either filling orders or cleaning up/filling drinks. This game puts you on rails and forces you into an unavoidable loop, meaning you don't have the choice to just dive or just run the restaurant. All in all the game is fine. It's not unfun. But I just strongly feel that the reviews don't paint an accurate picture. If you want a better overwhelmingly positive game for $10 less play Stardew, you'll have more fun and have way more content. I'd only buy this game knowing that the gameplay loop in the first few hours is seemingly all there is to it. If you can see yourself sinking endless hours into that loop then pick it up. If not, I'd look to request a refund. TL:DR: the game is fine but not worth the price. Reviews imo are misleading. Better "casual" games for less money. Game is not relaxing if that's what you're looking for.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Dave the Diver is a relaxed game where you dive into a ocean world collecting ingredients by day which you then use in a sushi restaurant to make money at night.While the simplicity of the game makes it accessible for pretty much anyone to play I think this is also where it's downfall is. Even though you'll discover new areas and get more possibilities to do things other than diving and selling sushi (such as breeding fish or farming) the gameplay loop stays the same and I think that gameplay loop just became boring for me once I've played it for a while. After this realization I tried playing the game more in hopes anything would change but it stayed the same. For that reason I wouldn't recommend the game to anyone, unless they are okay with spending the money on but a few hours of actual enjoyment.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot of content to the game and layered progression system.  Some content is unlocked via the story line while other content is unlocked by improvement of your restaurant.  The game can be finished in 20 hours or you can min max to unlock everything and upgrade everything from weapons to dishes for a lot more hours in gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Dave The Diver should be an amazing game, but the pacing brings this game down so much that it's impossible to ignore. The game is beautifully crafted, the art style is great, the music is fitting and catchy, and the sushi restaurant is a fun change of pace. Unfortunately, after an hour and a half or so of diving, you get to experience the restaurant for maybe 5 minutes before the night is over and it's time to dive again. This loop becomes boring really quickly, as you have to keep catching new fish out in the wild. In the late game this problem is solved with the fish farm, but the fish farm and vegetable farms come into play far too late. The game was still drip feeding content to me multiple hours after the end credits rolled, and it made it really hard to care about any new features that were coming my way. That being said, the pacing got better towards the end of the game because you were able to focus on missions and let the fish and vegetable farms do the most boring aspects of the game, if that content was accessible 30 hours earlier, the overall experience would have been much better. This is not a bad game, and it is worth checking out, but the pacing does make it hard to recommend at full price. If you do grab this one, get it while it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly one of the funnest games I've played in a while.There's so many different ways to play the game, you can follow the quest storyline, you can focus on fishing, you can focus on managing the restaurant, but every aspect is super enjoyable and feels interactive.The game has a lot of detail and depth, whether it is the terminology (I've worked for 5 years as a sushi chef and the vocabulary is pretty accurate) or the different "apps" and it still doesn't feel overwhelming when you play, which is very impressive. The graphics are quite unique with the combination of 3D and pixel art that works super well together.Really looking forward to the direction of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Dave the Diver is full of personality. It's charming, packed to the gills with colourful characters (and fish) and more! Every time you think there's no more to unlock, something new pops up.Fish by day, sushi by night, yet there's also so much more. I won't spoil it; you'll have to keep on playing to find out. I'm looking forward to continuing the story and exploring the deeper areas. I had to stop playing to give this one a well-deserved thumbs up!
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: The best mixed genre management game available out there.It's a metroidvania rougelite underwater exploration game when Dave is diving under the sea. It's a restaurant management game when Dave works at the Sushi bar at night. It's also a farming game where Dave grows rice, carrots, eggplants etc and raises chickens & fishes in Ottos farm. It's a visual novel when it shows Brancho's backstory. It's a cooking game when Brancho is in competition. It felt like a stealth spy game at some point. It blends many more genres and it keeps introducing new mechanics of the game even after 30 hours of playtime.Also, it's a great story-rich game that is both serious and goofy at times, with a lot of character references from other games/movies/shows like Pokemon (fat ash), King of Fighters, Skyrim, Salt Bae, The Matrix, Bioshock, Tomb Raider, Half-Life, One Piece, and so on. This game also features crafting, boss fights, and a variety of other activities. It's a combination of almost everything we know in gaming.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing, I have completed Dave the Diver.A casual and relaxing game about managing a sushi bar and catching the fish required. Story is lighthearted with beautiful moments of emotion sprinkled on. The game-play loop is simple, but enjoyable enough to have kept me for 40 hours. The most smooth and fluid pixel animation I've ever seen. Only gripe I have is that harpooning stronger fish will send you into a QTE minigame that is in desperate need of accessibility options. Though the developers have said they are working on implementing them. If you fail the QTE minigame, you can attempt it again with each following attempt being easier. So if you have some sort of disability that makes very rapid button pressing or stick spinning difficult, the game will be only slightly harder. You can always upgrade your harpoon gun or shoot the fish with something else prior. Overall, fantastic experience. Made me sad when I beat it, cuz I wanted to find more!8/10
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I love the exploring, fishing and collecting part. 9.5 out of 10. That's why I played so much.Everything else is annoying and frustrating for me:- Unskippable 10min grafic novels about the background of side characters. Who cares?- Stupid mini games/quests- UI and UX is abysmal- When fishing or in minigames, you must for example dodge or hold something down. The game tells you not to press "Down", it tells you to press "S". And instead of shake "Left" and "Right", it tells you to press press "A", then "D". This subtle difference not only is harder to apply, it also kills the immersive experience!- But the reason why I rage uninstalled it, was this:When I had to control two characters at the same time. At one point I had to press RightShift + DownArrow + Mouse4 + "S". This is literally not possible unless you have 3 hands or lift the mouse over the keyboard.So I reset my custom key bindings, but it didnt apply. I continued with holding my mouse over my keyboad and pressing buttons, but at one point I lost it. I was done. It was the straw that broke the camel's back.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: You owe it to yourself (8.5/10) to play this, in my humble opinion. There is a certain freedom, and ease to this game (depending on your upgrades). Go into it for the causal experience. Learn "level layouts"..they change whether you decide to farm or complete story objectives - (more freedom in your choice pacing I think is a +) depending on the day of the week, as well as some minor weather & day/night cycle changing what is or isnt available. The Dredge DLC offers a nice burst of money when it counts, and offers not a whole lot more than a spooky theme, music, and fish art style. But can break up what you may feel as monotonous, grindy or repetitive. OR, aSoothing and an "at your own pace" game, depending on your perspective. It feels good to % through the in game progression trackers."Mini games" essentially make up the game play loop with a story that can be entertaining depending on your level of inner calm, or inebriation. That is: diving / min maxing hauls, managing restaurants, character objectives, cooking challenges, story objectives, and bosses.Micromanaging property, upgrades and staff above and below the water line I found enjoyable.Its not necessarily "no stress" but a casual game you play for the single player days of your week.I think every character introduced has a very pronounced art style, and personality. Nothing bland and its definitely on purpose lol. You get all the archetypes for a compelling, light hearted, sometimes frustrating interactive story, both for the base game and subsequent DLC.Character cut scenes are enjoyable the 1st, or 100th time, though i found myself skipping once i'd seen them all. They're enjoyable and well done. The music loop depending on depth level you dive at I also find extremely satisfying. You'll definitely have a favorite. There are sub areas within certain depths and are worth revisiting at least once or twice to 100%.Blind play through best play through.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Great visuals and super fun. Could be improved with a more diverse soundtrack while playing as it gets a bit old but the story keeps you guessing and has lots of fun puzzles randomly dispersed throughout so you never get too bored doing the same thing. Wish that there was more content in the sushi restaurant or that the evenings could be extended because it goes by so quickly, but 10/10 game overall.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: It's a gem of a single-player RPG adventure that combines underwater exploration and restaurant management to perfection. Dive into the mysterious depths of the Blue Hole to fish and discover treasure by day, then don your chef's hat to run a bustling sushi restaurant by night. With its eccentric characters and captivating gameplay, it offers a unique and relaxed experience that will appeal to all lovers of adventure and management. A must-have adventure that will keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish!
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the incredible variety of gameplay mechanics in Dave the Diver. I appreciate novelty, and can get bored if a game lasts a while with just more of the same. In the first few hours, the variety felt overwhelming, as the game threw more at me to learn. However, it all came together in my head soon enough, and the game continued to surprise me again and again (I'm glad I didn't know much about it before I played). Combined with the amusing graphics, characters and story, this game was entertaining from start to finish. In fact, it might be the most pure fun I've ever had playing a game!
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Half aquatic shoot-and-loot, half restaurant manager, and full of fun. It has some pacing and UI issues that make the latter third of the game a little tedious as you have to wait days for NPCs to do their thing without any new content to explore, but that's a fairly small complaint. The light-hearted, self-conscious, neo-retro vibes that seep through the whole game combine well with the very forgiving game play for a relaxing (but occasionally tense!) experience.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most addicting games of my life, combines open world exploration and story-telling, with an amazingly in-depth restaurant management sim. Can get lost exploring the depths of the ocean just as easy as you can get caught up maximizing profits at Bancho's! Cutscenes and 8-bit style give it a unique one of a kind feel that will leave every player with a sense of genuine entertainment, something harder and harder to find in today's AAA-saturated gaming marketplace.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: At a very fundamental level, this is Stardew Valley under the sea. More accurately, it's a task-focused management game that has you splitting your time between diving for fish (and other things) and running a sushi restaurant. Even more accurately, it's a smorgasbord of mini-games with just enough focus that it doesn't feel 'messy'. The characters are interesting, the over-the-top cutscenes are brilliant, and you'll likely have quite a few laugh-out-loud moments. It's a really pleasant time, marred only by a few boss fights, where the gameplay changed direction and difficulty spiked.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I only bought this game because I personally do love diving (certified rebreather/trimix). Honestly I assumed this would be another <2 hour steam return.I was wrong. You should buy this game even if you don't like diving.I don't know how such a small studio manages to pull off a game that is.. actually fun? It's sad to say that in 2024 a game that is actually fun, smart, and clever with appealing characters and great art to boot is so rare.Dave The Diver is super fun, varied, and the right balance of engaging but not so hard that you have to min-max. You can play the game how you want and have a good time... You know, like a game is supposed to be played.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

The music in this game calms me down and hypes me up at exactly the right moment. The sound effects on weapons and in the restaurant are exactly what I need in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an incredible version of what it is, a farming/job simulator with progression elements, but set around the sea and a sushi restaurant and with a banger sound track. It's so much more charming, funny, and relaxing than any of those other games in the same genre. It has the perfect mix of relaxed game play while still allowing you to obsessively do all the tasks and maximize your time per day.Other than the awesome music, the biggest positive for me with a game like this is the passage of time, the day is broken up into morning, afternoon, and night. Time passes when you leave or enter your boat. Realistically you could be in the water for as long as you can pick up oxygen (there are tanks under water to grab) and only once you return to your boat would time have passed to the next stage in the day. This alone makes the game so much better than a game like Stardew Valley which makes it seem like you can play it in a relaxed way, but the clock is always ticking and you always feel the need to spend every day doing something productive. In Dave the diver you don't necessarily feel that same stress but they still have a way to work in weekly events or special orders for the restaurant that are on a timer.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics are some good-looking pixel art and the theme has a nice humor but there are as well as issues with the game: - the default controls don't match keyboard keys (not a the biggest of deal except that it's a keyboard game) ;- the gameplay is based around task repetition and key smashing.For me it's definitely not worth near close the price it is at right now.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot stress enough how much I believe that this is Game of the Year 2023.Everything from the art, the story, the gameplay, and progression is fantastic. Even in Early Access, there's a sizeable amount of content. (Now that it's out of Early Access, there's SO MUCH more content)If you love the look of the game but you're put off by the restaurant management part of the game, don't be. It's not overly stressful, and gets significantly easier as you progress. It's a great way to feel like you're making progress when you see how much money you're earning compared to previous days.The dev team are awesome at listening to ideas and communicating with players on their Discord server.I have seen a significant amount of people mention that they don't typically play singleplayer games (including myself) who were totally captured by this game. I don't know what it is about the game that appeals to people like us so strongly, but it's there.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't like cozy games, usually the lack of risk and the "grindy" nature make them boring. Dave the Diver fixes this by not only having a risk factor, where you can lose your items on a dive, but by throwing enough curveballs at you to break the grind. It's pretty dynamic, one minute you are harpooning fish and the next you are in a neckbeard's dream cheering on this world's equivalent to Miku. The restaurant running aspect is strangely addictive, i was so absorbed that I currently have physical irl notes on what i need to plan for and what ingredients I need to farm. Maybe I have a secret fantasy of running a sushi bar, but the fact that a mundane thing is something i look forward to as a reward for my efforts of battling sharks all day speaks volumes. The characters are witty, varied, and fun despite the common trend to take advantage of Dave and the silly story arc feels rewarding. Unfortunately the downside of this game is also one of it's main attractions, the many curveballs and minigames it throws at you tend to clutter the core game, I think I would have gotten more enjoyment if I did not feel like I had to change gears so often. Despite this, I would recommend picking this game up as I cannot say that this game is not fun, I had a blast.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: For someone who like a little bit of everything, this game really does offer you that. I've still got a lot more to go and surprised that I'm finding new mechanics to help keep this game interesting! The pacing feels great and does not feel like I'm obviously grinding. For a casual gamer who likes the occasional twist thrown at them, this is perfect!

_childDocuments_.review: I have played this game NONSTOP since purchasing. I have nothing but praise for it. _childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Dave the Diver is a game I really wanted to like and give a thumbs up review because it feels like the devs deserve it. The entire game definitely had some though put into it.The visuals are the best part. The cutscenes, the environment, the animations, everything looks great. Sound effects and music are also done well. The concept of the game is good too: a mixture of RPG and sim elements with some minigames sprinkled in that feels very much reminiscent of classic flash games like "Learn to Fly". All that sounds great, so what went wrong?Unfortunately, the gameplay just fails to deliver the premise. The first few hours were very fun but soon after, the game just moves away from what was the "core gameplay" before. More and more minigames are introduced, more apps you need to check, more NPCs, more everything. To progress the story, you now have to perform boring fetch quests, watch endless cutscenes, and tutorials for more and more special cases. I just wish I could play the game for a bit as it introduced itself to me: Collect fish and then sell them at my restaurant. But the more I progress, the more I find myself loathing in the grind of badly designed tasks just to get back to the fun part at some point.Unless it gets much worse, I'll probably still finish the game. But looking back I would have liked to spend my time and money on something else on my wishlist.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Instead of "just one more turn", this game features "just one more dive". And it may even be more addicting. At first it is just a chill and relaxing diving game, with some hectic sushi bar serving during the evening, but the more you play, the more it opens up. Never getting too complex, it introduces more and more game mechanics, that I didn't expect from this game at all. The only con are some of the quick action mechanics, that disturb the chill diving.- great (and surprising) story and storytelling- relaxing dives in a beautiful 2D pixel word- hilarious characters- lots of sushi- quite a lot of boss fights with different mechanics (some are also a bit hard, needed 2-3 tries on at least 2 bosses)- more gameplay than you might expect (38h in, not finished with the story and still soooo much stuff to do)- some of the quick action button mashing doesn't fit too well with the otherwise relaxing game- the theme is a bit hard when you know that sharks aren't as evil and aggressive as they are shown here and fishing in general is a complicated story (mini spoiler:

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game 9/10. It is an excellent chill business grinding game like Recettear or Stardew Valley. Each has management element and an action element and Dave the Diver's action element blows those legendary games out of the water. All while having a similarly charming and fun management element on par with Rec and Stardew. My only gripes are little nitpicks about the way that the management element fails to automate tedious tasks and is more complicated than necessary.=Everything below this point is the little things that I think make the overall game fall short of perfection=FARMINGThe normal farm is expensive to scale up. I beat the final boss on day 33 and didn't manage to get the land farm producing at a volume that would make leveling recipes practical.The sea people farm is great but comes at the minor cost that you must carry all of the grown food for the day that you pick it up. Potentially losing the entire harvest if you get killed by a shark on your run. We know they can swim to the surface. It would be an improvement if they could ship it to you.The Fish Farm SUCKS! At the beginning of every day you need to visit a series of menus to sell or harvest all your excess fish. They bind an entire button to selling or harvesting everything when the button everyone needs is harvest all BUT the two highest star of each fish. When you use the harvest all button it even warns you that you are screwing yourself. So fish farming is taking a boat to a room where you interact with 7 spreadsheets where you adjust the numbers on every cell one at a time. The menu even has unique key binds to master for performing the operation quickly. It still isn't game play. I loved collecting two 3* of every fish. I hated not knowing what Roe if any I was collecting or knowing what rate fish were growing or if expanding early produced more fish than leaving it at 99%.THE SUSHI RESTAURANTPlatinum rank secretly adds $2000 to your daily operating costs! Diamond rank secretly increases this cost to $5000! Ranking to Bronze, Silver, and Gold are all beneficial and should be gotten as fast as possible. You should sandbag on upgrading to platinum as long as you can. Normally low level workers have poor performance but low wages making for an even incline where you can afford to sell crappy low level fish and grow as you want. Once you hit platinum it creates a floor where every fish you sell needs to be worth $290 per piece to make the extra customers from platinum break even. MOST of the recipes in the entire game even at rank 10 do not generate $290 per unit. The optimal strategy is to spam your best recipe endlessly every night. This is a problem by itself. Platinum and later diamond force that strategy even if you weren't done with messing around with your menu. Reaching platinum makes night diving more costly as it is $2000 every night even if you spent a third of it under water.Picking the correct employees requires referencing a guide or making incredibly expensive trial an error. Money you need good employees to get.FISHING GUNSThe weapon crafting and upgrade system is hamstrung by unnecessary gold costs and too many overlapping options. The entire game can and should be played with a Level 1 Tranq Rifle for most of the run through. Live caught fish and their secret roe are more than THREE TIMES more valuable than dead ones. This makes most of the guns and their elemental variants useless and expensive ways to fail.Upgrading weapons requires a bunch of gathered resources that are fun to collect. Unfortunately because weapon upgrades also come with a hefty price tag they create an unnecessary opportunity cost. The stats of weapons are secret unless you expensively explore the tree and the end result is one minor variation on 18 ways to ruin fish. Fish should be weak to and stunned by a different element making live capture possible with more than just Tranq.Because you have no control of your Melee weapon or your Harpoon your gun MUST cover a universal role further narrowing the options to just sticking with the Tranq rifle. Leveling up guns in your inventory doesn't make them more powerful when found underwater so there is zero benefit to expanding your arsenal especially because gold costs rob the other game systems of growth. The game is great with a Tranq rifle I just wish the other options were less costly and more viable.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing, and the price is a good selling point. It takes up very little space on your device, and it is a very visually appealing art style. _childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very cute, addictive, and stylish game with a lot of potential. My only complaint is that progression in this game seemed too quick for a restaurant management game. With the gameplay loop being as satisfying as it is, I think the game would benefit from slower progression, allowing the players to just relax, explore, and enjoy their time working towards the growth of their restaurant. Slowing the progression of the game down, coupled with enhancements to the procedural generation of the game so that it feels more varied on each dive, I would very much like to see. Overall, this game has a lot of potential. I fell in love with the gameplay, design, music, and style. I just wish that progression was slower so that I could spend more time just diving, cooking, and managing my business.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Dave has dived right into my heart. This game is probably one of the best I’ve ever played, despite it’s “just” a 2D side scroller where you swim in water.It started with getting some fishes for your new sushi restaurant and quickly evolves into a great story with a lot of interesting characters. What I like the most is the pace, which you can choose on your own. You can either embark on your missions and kill big bosses, or just chill going fishing for the restaurant.Definitely a must-play.

_childDocuments_.review: Live Review: Game still good.Early Access Review:This game has about 15 hours of content as of the time of this review, but you can keep grinding past that. Although the build is only in 0.6, it feels like it is VERY polished. The game reminds me of Recettear, where you spend chunks of your day underwater and one chunk of your day doing a restaurant management minigame.The underwater segment feels almost identical to the original Subnautica in a way, except that it is 2D. It is very comfy.The restaurant portion is interesting and goes by pretty quickly.While I enjoy the game a lot, there isn't a TON of depth to any of the activities and there are many minigames that pop up as you progress.It's definitely worth $20 if you like this style of game. I love it and I can't wait to see what they add.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Everything you want in an Indie game. Great art and scenery. Fun characters, with 10/10 cut-scenes that are a pleasure to watch. One of the cleanest gameplay loops I have seen. You start your day fishing and exploring, then get a dopamine hit from making money by selling what you caught at the Sushi restaurant at night. You use those funds to invest in more gear/staff for the restaurant/ more  goodies. As you get better gear, you can explore deeper into the Blue Hole, opening up more fishing and ingredients. The game keeps you coming back for more. One more dive, one more night at Bancho's. I am amazed this game is in early access, I put a solid 35 hours in, and I still have not finished up all the quests. I look forward to full release, they have really struck gold on this one.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: This is just overflowing with actual passion from the developers. It's been years since I saw a game that had this level of polish and fun, even where it's completely not even needed; They did it anyways.I'm suspicious when I see anything reviewed with "Overwhelmingly Positive" but this is well earned and deserved.Is Dave the Diver perfect? Not exactly, it has small flaws and discomforts, probably not great for your controller at times with some of the mini-games but the amount of effort they put into this game is clear and most importantly: Its FUN.If you like a resource management + restaurant manager this will easily scratch that itch. Might not be for anyone, but a short 5 min gameplay video will help give you the gist of if it's for you or not.... and if it is there's more than you'll expect and it's a pleasant and often funny surprise.Plus they have a guy called DR BACON. They know what they are doing.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I have not had that much fun with a single player game in a while. It's so entertaining and kind of addicting even. There's so much to do. The game has a story, which progresses and special customers to deal with. There's fetching, collecting, quests and encounters throughout the depths of the sea. It's not frustrating and while mysterious, it's not scary like some other underwater games (looking at you Subnautica). Oh and the art is also amazing and hilarious. I highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Dave the Diver is a pleasant blend of hunting, farming, and restaurant sim with a very chill and humorous atmosphere. The game is completely saturated with minigames, some that occur only a few times or less, from rhythm games, cooking games, to even a virtual pet game. The bulk of gameplay, however, is mainly constituted by exploring sections of ocean, capturing fish, and cooking/serving dishes by night in a full day cycle. The story lasts a good while and has an organic way of proceeding, with logical barriers slowly leaking out different types of content to avoid being overwhelmed from the start.  Once the story is over and you enter the epilogue, the game continues, albeit I would argue that many crafting recipes (that are not so much necessary) require rare components that would only come about with luck or grind. It also felt like some systems such as the land farming/fish farming were unnecessary for the main campaign. If I were to call it perfect I would want the game's difficult recipes to correspond to additional content that beckoned for it or otherwise make those recipes easier to complete throughout the story (there is no great reason to fully upgrade a gun and some guns seemed to serve little purpose).My absolute favorite parts of the game was managing the sushi restaurant with hilarious staff, fun minigames, and interesting dishes. This and of course the numerous over-the-top cut scenes any time you have an upgrade or research new recipes.If you enjoy sea exploration or restaurant sim, I highly recommend. If "laid back" were a game this would be it!
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: When it first came out, I added it to my wishlist but didn't think much of it, thought it was a diving/sushi management game and that was all there was to it (and management games give me anxiety so I wasn't entirely on board!!) but when I finally got around to playing it I could not be more wrong. The art, the content, mini games on Dave's phone (raising your own tamagotchi!), the characters, the writing, etc- It's easy to see why this game became so popular.If you're on the fence about playing this game, bite the bullet and buy it, you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

Game play is very satisfying and Bancho is the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ goat.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Dave The Diver is an incredibly enjoyable experience. For 20$ you can enjoy catching fish, exploring a changing ocean, and serving sushi at your restaurant.This game has a surprising amount of depth to it, besides the 3 main selling points this game also has an encyclopedia, a passive story, customization for your sushi bar, upgrades for your divers gear and weapons, genuinely fun combat, and much more.If you enjoy the indie game charm and have 20 bucks to spare, absolutely pick this game up. It is worth your time. The developers clearly have put a lot of love into this game and deserve some recognition.I had no idea the game was early access until I was about 5 hours in, best "early access" game I've ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game more than I initially thought I would.It has a good relaxing ambiance (except when a shark is blocking an oxygen point -_-)The game at times does overload you with different quests or mechanics that get unlocked, but on the flip side, there are enough mechanics and gameplay to keep you busy for quite a while. This is not a game that you will be finishing in a couple of hours, it took me around 35 hours for completion of the storymode. So money well worth.7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: to sum up the review: the game is extremely charming but plays slow and clunky, i would recommend it to nearly anyone who's not menow the particulars! i get the feeling that were i able to skip past all the cutscenes and special events and not get shoved into 4 different quests i have no interest in all the time I'd really quite enjoy the game, and my bias should be noted: my favorite games these past few years have been hollow knight, ultrakill, and sekiro on the higher pace side and a short hike and dredge on the slower more relaxed end of things.I've found dave the diver to be too relaxing and slow paced to appeal to the high octane parts of my preference but far too demanding with dialogue and minigames and unskippable cutscenes to appeal to my need for a fully chill game.as it stands it feels like every ten minutes of gameplay will feature an unskippable, unavoidable, bit of smashing space to skip through irrelevant dialogue.The combat, the most high stakes part of the game is also often very inconsitent, dave moves so slowly, there seems to be no way to avoid many attacks and when you are made to heal the process leaves you completely vulnerable, allowing failure to stack up quickly.To be frank i think this game could be fixed for me if a skip or "do this later" option were added into the scripted events, then i'd be more willing to look past its slow awkward pace.i keep questioning whether or not i like this game, that doubt alone serves as enough evidence that i don't fully enjoy it, and given steam's binary review system I can't fully recommend it
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Overrated, only buy with significant discount.All too often the satisfying gameplay loop is split up by irritating fetch quests or semi-broken puzzles.However, when you do get the chance to simply gather fish for your sushi restaurant, it becomes clear how shallow the game actually is. You will spend 25 hours in the same relatively small area catching mostly the same fish with mostly the same tools.You will either be frustrated that you cannot go fishing, or bored of fishing.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: A pleasant and chill game with a simple but funny backstory. Two different gameplay : the day you’re a diver seeking for fish to catchthe night you handle a sushi bar, the dishes you’ll propose to the clients are made with the fish you’ve caught earlier. Simple, yet incredible, a lot of new things are coming and some more gameplay element will be added during the game, animations are beautiful and you never want to skip them even if you see them billions of times.The graphics are impressive and the mood keeps you under for hours and hours (missed my bedtime, went to bed at 4am without knowing it was actually 4am)
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: When i heard from this game and saw the crazy positive rating on Steam, i was interested. I watched a few trailers and a small bit of gameplay but was not quite sold, mostly because of the pixel style. Togehter with a buddy i bought this game to check it out, since 20€ is easily affordable.We started the game and after only 15 minutes of play, we were addicted. The pixely graphics style is not a problem in the least, its rather that it elevates the game. The funny little "cutscenes" which show up when you upgrade or craft things are so well made and always make me smile, i never skip those even after having seen them over 4 times. A few pop culture references for those that notice them are like a cherry on the cake. The diving and sushi restaurant mechanics are working together perfectly. After 8 hours of play there are still getting things unlocked that improve the game further. AND ITS NOT EVEN OUT OF EARLY ACCESS! Its almost criminal that this game is ONLY 20€. You will not regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: All style, very little substance.The cooking/management section is very fun, I enjoyed it immensely. The diving was just okay, combat is incredibly clunky and can lead to cheap early game deaths before many upgrades.I got to about Chapter 3 and then I just couldn't take it anymore. The story content in this game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ abysmal. The dialogue just isn't good, and there are sections where the game wrongly assumes that is it's strong suit and subjects you to 10 minute long cutscenes that truly do not matter at all.Chapter 3 is "Filler content, The Chapter". I was actually getting into the groove of the game, then it decided that to progress I should do 6-8 fetch quests that mainly have nothing to do with the cooking/management or diving section of the game.There's way too many great games that aren't full of boring ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ filler to waste your time on this. This is yet another game where people love the style so much it gets a complete pass on some incredibly mediocre gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't ready for how much this game has to offer. Not only is the main gameplay loop pretty fun, but there is additional content that given to you in such a well paced manner. The world has so much character. The characters themselves all have great personalities, especially the titular Dave who at times can tell when someone is BS'ing him. The animations that take place when unlocking/upgrading a recipe are hilarious. And the story, imo, is well written. This game is absolutely worth full price, and if you get on a sale? All the better. Enjoy this silly, fun, chill game.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish I could recommend this game. It's good in the first few hours, but over time it's not what it seems. It introduces so many new mechanics in a short time. Every time you come back to the boat, somebody wants something from you. The game gets constantly interrupted by side missions and NPCs just talking and talking. After some time, it turns into a minigame nightmare. The game pushes so many minigames at you, it's crazy, and they are not fun at all.The bosses are not fun at all either. The most fun I had was with the sushi bar, but after some time, you do the sushi bar less and less. It feels like the devs didn't know what the player likes about the game and just added a bunch of minigames for the sake of it.This game is not what it seems. If you think it's something like Stardew Valley or similar games, and you want that, don't buy this game. It is NOT that!
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: The core gameplay is fun. Too bad the game insists on pulling you away from it. Endless dialogue, endless interjections, random cutscenes causing the time to skip, and tedious fetch quests galore. This game has a ton of promise, but by Chapter 3, the tedious distractions are too much to be called fun. My breaking point was the pointless 30 min unskippable cutscene about the chef's backstory. Let me fish and run my damn restaurant in peace.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I came, I saw, I conquered, scuba dives and sold out sushi concerts!What an amazing, charming little game this is.Part roguelite, part farm sim, part stealth game and more.It took a little while to click, as more systems kept being introduced and a few things could have been explained a lot better (which cost me hours to make up for at the end in completing achievements), but this is a nice relaxing game that gives you bang for buck.Catch sushi in the day, serve sushi in the night, whilst trying to catch them all and progress an overarching plot.Only real criticism is that it can feel like there are too many mechanics and some key things could have been explained a lot lot better. 8.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly believe that Dave the Diver will become a video game classic.It is an absolute must-play. A game that can be succinctly boiled down to one word: .Dave the Diver is simply fun.I implore you to buy this game. If you're thinking about it, if you even have the faintest notion of it, buy the game.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: The vast majority of my time in this game was spent in the demo. At first glance this game is a Recettear-like; something I've been dying for. I love the initial gameplay loop of diving, catching fish/gathering ingredients and running the restaurant. Its fun, calming and engaging. A great time waster. The collection side-quests in the background are just a little bonus. Then the full game released and the actual plot happened. It went from a fun, chill capitalism sim to a confusing wanna-be RPG with major illusion of choice issues. I'm too busy faffing about for the Sea People to do the fun parts anymore. And there are a ton of small genre jumps in the form of mini-games that are either poorly explained or tied to characters I give no craps about because most of the characters in this game are utter jerks. Seriously, I think the cat is the only character in this game who never insults Dave. Its not funny. I wish I could go back to the demo. I just wanna play restaurant supplier.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most relaxing game I've played in recent years. Dave the Diver has a lot of different gameplay elements ranging from managing a restaurant and fishing to farming and playing rhythm games. The soundtrack is amazing, though a bit repetitive and the art style is great. I was especially impressed by the cinematics and all the effort that went into making them so detailed. I think the story is too short relative to the amount of side content there is. By the time I was done with the main game, I didn't have much of a reason to continue upgrading my gear or do anything else for that matter. All in all, it's an amazing game and I recommend you buy it at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Decent chillax game. Quirky as they get. It drags on a bit too long imo and I lost interest in it towards the end. I'd have preferred more story around Bancho than what actually happens in the game. Definitely get a copy on sale if you're worried about enjoying it or not, but this one is worth full price.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: This has something in common with one of my all-time top 5 games, Steamworld Dig 2: An incredibly addicting game loop. Fish the depths by day, run a sushi restaurant by night - it just clicks so well. This game surprises and delights with nonstop introductions of new systems, mini games, and surprises, which make it feel fresh all the way through. But, you can also play this an infinite amount of in-game days and optimize your restaurant into a money-making machine if you so wish!I loved playing this game. And if nothing else about it catches your attention, then at least look up the cutscenes - they're incredible, funny, and probably the best part of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like restaurant simulators but wish you could have a hand in where the ingredients come from?  Well this is your game!  You dive to catch fish during the day, and run a sushi restaurant at night!  Besides the simulator part, it has a full on story and an indefinite duration of restauranteering!  I think the catching and restaurant part can last forever, but I think it would be real useful if you are trying to 100% the game.  Overall, I recommend this game! It is a charming game that goes whimsical places.  You end up doing and seeing many things pertinent to the ocean and life within it that you didn't anticipate, it is multiple games in one. The art style is great and the humor is top notch.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: This game is nice, long and satisfying in visual effects, collectability, and new features laid out slowly. But the boss fights are not for the faint of heart. I was able to complete them without too much trial and error. But there are some areas of effects from attacks that can get frustrating. And of course working for over an hour and failing a run just because you went for that one more item and ran out of your escape item. And so many times I would get into a boss fight with my net gun or dart gun and not be prepared.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: This is a charming and surprisingly refreshing indie gem that blends adventure, exploration, and management with an underwater twist. The game excels in its dual game play mechanics. The diving segments are both relaxing and thrilling, featuring beautiful underwater environments teeming with colorful marine life and hidden secrets. Back on land, managing your sushi restaurant is equally engaging. If you’re looking for a game that combines relaxing exploration with engaging management, Dave’s underwater adventures are well worth diving into.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little game that mixes a few different kinds of games.  Makes me really feel good while playing it.  The art style is bright and colorful, the story and characters are endearing, and the gameplay loop is fun. If I'm feeling depressed or a little down and play Dave the Diver, it ends up pulling me out of that funk and I come out the other side of my game play session feeling good.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: When watching the trailer for this game, I was overwhelmed with the amount of things you could possibly do in this game and was worried this would be all shoved in. However, this game has been an absolute treat! It's not overwhelming and I've enjoyed each aspect of this game, from diving and discovering new areas and fish; to playing minigames and figuring out puzzles. My favourite part is the sushi restaurant and managing the staff and what food goes out :)The pixel art is stunning and I love the amount of work and love the devs clearly put in this game. it's definitely worth the price and experience.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Off the hop Dave the Diver is a cute, relatively chill game with a neat style and concept; however the further you get in to the game the more it adds. One or two things would have been fine, but the longer it goes on the more it feels like you're needing to grind multiple things at once, most of which are distracting from the story and the simple beginnings that made it fun. To be fair, for some people, that's great. They love it, and all the power to them. I haven't, and likely won't ever actually finish the game. If all you wanted was a fishing game, this ain't it. It reminds me more of a bunch of single player mini-games sewn together.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: This game blowsmost other games i've played out of the water. Dave is a 10 across the board. The gaming renaissance is here.If you have a refined palate for games and are tired of complete garbage, play this game and have your faith in indie titles restored until something else comes along and ruins it.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Dave the Diver is one of the extremely few games where there is so much more gameplay and polish than it seems. Everytime I think "hey maybe this is it", nope, more content. A stark contrast between most the games on Steam that look like they have content and polish, but are completely crap the bed on both.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I cant believe i forgot to review this damn. What a cute game! It's perfect for chilling out before bed. Very simple game play loop has you deep diving to fulfill Bancho's high-end sushi joints by night (If you aren't night diving that is.) ** My advice to new players is to be absolutely certain your ready to open up a branch because obtaining artisan's flame gets harder from that point on. (you'll only get 4 flame per day unless your skills are excellent). Also make sure to upgrade your tranq gun to add jelly fish to your tank.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first session and I have to write a review. This game is beyond relaxing, and I love every moment of it.It has character and the art is beautiful. The game play loop is very subnautica-esq where you are limited by gear which you upgrade and go deeper and explore more. Put this on the top of the fact the area you explore changes every day and you got yourself a super satisfying Fishing by day Managing a restaurant by night game on your hands.Really the trailers and pictures can't do justice and honestly neither can words. I hope this spurs more games of it's kind as I love mixed genre's. Simulation + Exploration is a classic, and this feels like it uses the best of both worlds to leave you mesmerized and always saying "just one more day and ill be done."

_childDocuments_.review: Dave the Diver is a simple funny game, occasionally evoking thoughts of a vertically-oriented Stardew Valley. However, the majority of the gameplay leans towards a 2D Ubisoft-style open world, lacking the depth and charm of its inspirations.  Dave the Diver's humor and quirky gameplay make it a lighthearted choice for casual gamers but it falls short of delivering a truly captivating experience.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Normally I don't write reviews, so here goes.  Dave the Diver scratches some part of my ADHD brain in a way that keeps me entertained and playing.  I've been balancing this game by playing maybe one to three in game days per real-life days and I still get entertained.   At first it may seem slow when you're serving the customer's by yourself but once you add and train your staff it gets easier in that department (In my case by Chapter 2).  But the cut-scenes are hilarious and well animated, "death" isn't meaningless as if you die during normal day to day stuff you can retrieve ONE item when you're rescued; Also If you fail a Boss fight you don't go back to the boat but can restart the boss fight).  If you're a fan of storytelling the Lore in this game is also very well thought out and goes into some backstories of different characters and some twists that I can not say otherwise spoilers.  All in all very balanced and thought out and honestly deserves its Overwhelmingly positive reviews. And if your dissuaded by some of the negative reviews, let me add on some things.  YES there are quite a few mini-games throughout the game, BUT IMO they break the monotony that some games can develop aside from the cut-scenes.  Another thing is that Yes the fishing/diving is NOT realistic, but lets get some things straight.  A Blue Hole where species found oceans apart and living in different climates and water types and usually not considered edible or practical isn't realistic; I don't think that's the point of this game.  It's supposed to be fun, and entertaining, and NOT to be taken too serious.  This isn't Dark Souls, or COD, or Fallout.  And FYI if you're expecting realistic, than sea people/mer-people don't exist.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Dave the Diver brings a lot creativity and fun - you can fish, collect, upgrade your diving suit, farm fish, prepare sushi, prep menus for your restaurant. There is so much stuff in this game and it's doing it without overwhelming you. Yeah, there are ways to maximize profit, to streamline and get the best fish, but you can also do want you want and don't have the feeling that you are missing out. Sometimes it's like a book with different PoV's: at the end of one person's chapter, you are disappointed about switching to the next character - that's how I felt after completing a dive and going on with the evening at the restaurant. Sometimes I wished to just focus on thing or the other, but with the day/night cycle that's not possible. Great game with a fresh concept that works very good.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: So much fun!  You can absolutely cruise through the storyline pretty quick if you want, but this game makes you want to do all all the side quests, it just doesn't get boring. The artwork is top-notch, the characters are lovable and even the credits are fun. I enjoyed every minute. I really hope they expand this game or make a sequel! Thank you to the developers, you did a wonderful job. :)
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Very good chill game with a hell lot of different minigames. The artstyle and animations are extremely well done and while one becomes used to them, of course, the first time seeing them is an absolute treat. When it comes to sound and music, they're excellent too. The game does not have voice over but it doesn't take anything away tbh. All the sound effects are good and the music is wonderful. The gameplay is pretty varied but basically it's one part gathering resources (fish) and one part management game with other stuff on top. Each element by itself is less complex and detailed than in dedicated games, e.g. Stardew Valley beats Dave's farming easily, but the sheer number of them is enough to provide you with good time. I would say, though, that sometimes the number of elements and minigames can be a bit too much and seem just a tiny bit excessive. For instance, at some point you can boost your stats, such as move speed, with consumables. I've never found any usage for it and it was a kinda useless mechanic which did not really add anything to my playthrough. It was just there and that's it. The game does have a plot and a lot of the mechanics are hidden behind plot progression. I found it OK since I alternated between farming/management and moving plot forward. The plot itself is pretty nice, nothing special, but cute and easy to follow. The characters are really fun, especially when coupled with the aforementioned amazing animations. In conclusion, it's nice game with plenty of content, though none of the elements are particularly deep on its own. It felt grindy it times but the cutscenes, the characters, and the setting in general made it a very cozy experience.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: it's a great game with great pexel art, I loved the short scenes it's very funny with unexpected actions. the lore looks very much like the one piece lore. this game has a chilling vibes. I recommend it for you if you need to chill for a while.but as you move forward into the game play you may get bored a little bit
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I can't find it within myself to recommend this game even though I have already beat it. The game starts off with a good concept of trying to get fish for your sushi restaurant, while gradually introducing some pretty interesting characters you will be interacting with on a pretty regular basis. However, I would safe around the halfway mark, the game loses its main focus on what it was. It practically becomes an ADHD-fueled nightmare by adding in so many unnecessary aspects in order to get the player engaged.One moment, I'm just trying to catch a shark and having to do a repetitive button mashing mini-game (Which is tolerable for the most part), to then having to try and take of a Great Value brand Tamagotchi. On top of that, I'm now having to do multiple missions in several different regions of the ocean, interact with sea people and their issues, try to collect fish like Pokemon, take care of a Tamagotchi, catch fish for a sushi bar, run the sushi bar, grow underwater crops for the sushi bar, deal with multiple interruptions in the game from missions, and many more issues. "But you don't have to grow crops or run the sushi bar, you can just keep catching fish if you want!" No, I can't, because that's the only way to generate money to afford the upgrades for your equipment, so that I can spend more than 3 minutes underwater without losing air.I genuinely enjoyed playing the game and tolerated a new addition here or there because the game (at the beginning) was different, funny, and interesting. Towards the end, I found myself just wanting the game to hurry up and finish, then I immediately uninstalled it regardless of the fact that new DLC was eventually coming out.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I wish i could say i liked this game but i dont. Due to a variety of mostly game play/design reasons.boss fights are not well designed and there is a controls are clunky, dave already moves slowly, so the fact that there are no simultaneous inputs (eg. shift -> space/rmb) is genuinely detrimental to the experience (furthermore, trying to quickly get a shot off by shooting as soon as you aim will often not shoot where you are aiming, but rather where you aimed last). Breath of the wild game out in 2016, we have to be able to move while picking up items/performing actions, hammering the space key while staring down the space button prompt all for nothing to happen is awkward and disincentivizes  core gameplay aspects of diving (the fun part of the game). Imagine if you had to pick up every single minecraft/terraria/stardew item drop with a janky button press.Also, camera work is often unreliable, bosses are way out of frame until they enter a range where they can potentially get a quick attack on you. Hostile enemies also rotate on their central axis, instead of closer to their head, so large/lengthy enemies will very often damage you by barely brushing up against you due to suddenly rotating 90+ degrees (all the while, design wise it's abundantly clear the devs wanted you to have a grace zone by having enemies wait before they telegraph, which displays incompetency in design.)this, paired with Dave's inability to aim past certain vertical points means that trying to engage enemies above or below is a genuine gamble since enemy turn speed paired with fast, wide attacks means more often than not you can still get hit while travelling at speeds thought to be making safe distance.I sincerely believe that this game does not deserves it's accolades. Given it's budget of just under 10 million dollars, I think any group of spirited developers and artists could create the admittedly beautiful and varied creature collectathon of which dave the diver definitely purports to be.however the sloppy gameplay and underachieving narratives are unsatisfying. One could call the multitudes of diverse minigames as homage or replicas, but in my eyes... it's nothing more than throwing sh*t at the wall and seeing what sticks.and now i've played a good portion of the game? I must say, not a lot of it does.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly fun and adorable game. The storyline is engaging in a way that doesn't get in the way of gameplay, progression isn't strictly linear, but it does ramp you up in a way where you aren't just boring slogging through the next thing. _childDocuments_.review: Playing this game to chapter 5, restarting just to finish the game is something ive only done in a handful of games. I am not the type to look up "things i wish i knew before playing" i wanna experience what the game wanted me to, and then adjust. if you are fetch questy, this is for you. the sushi part is something that you could get very micromanaged in if you wanted to expand the entire recipe menu. i did not get everything but felt that i really got the full experience of what this had to offer. Lastly, and i saved it on purpose. There is something in some games that just feel sooooo good. The way the ball hit a player in super dodge ball. the feel and bounce on a goomba in mario one. the super punch in super punch out. and the way the harpoon feels in this game. one of a kind.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: This game cannot get out of its own way. Why take the time and spend the energy to create a fun, inventive game only to hamstring it at every possible opportunity. At heart, this game is fun. You should get it, try it and play it for as long as you are able to enjoy it. Sooner or later some horrible design is gonna make you froth at the mouth. But I like this game. Or at least enough pieces of it. Even if I don't like the whole.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I can't remember the last time I left a review on a game. Typically, I just quietly play video games during my downtime and keep to myself. But, something about Dave the Diver has me wanting to spend all my free time diving into the Blue Hole and seeing what mysteries, beautiful scenery, or delicious fish I can run into next. The 8-bit graphic style fits this game so perfectly. There are so many moments where I'm blown away by how unique, yet fluid the animated characters and scenery can feel while keeping the style intact throughout cut-scenes, normal gameplay, and menu interactions. Also, I feel like I have ONLY scratched the surface, and there is so much more depth (pun intended) that I have yet to uncover. The moment I feel like I've started raking in money at the sushi bar, I've gotten enough gear to travel into the deepest parts of the Blue Hole, or I've unlocked enough to breeze through the rest of the game is the exact moment I realize there's a whole new chunk of content I just gained access to. The pacing, the art style, the characters, and just the overall experience is some of the best I've ever encountered out of any game. You can tell that the developers poured their passion into this, yet the game never takes itself too seriously. Every moment is more pleasant than the next. And, although there should be some repetitiveness to the process of catching fish, I have yet to find myself not wanting to gear up for my next dive. I'm sure I've got another 40 hours at least before I've decided that MAYBE I can try out another game other than Dave the Diver.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Worth the price just for the ridiculous little cutscenes. There's a hecking load of passion and humour that went into this game. Feels great to play, not too stressful, difficulty feels right for me, music is cool, writing's on point, graphics are just right. Bit grindy at times and some of the QTE-styled stuff feels a little weird, though since it doesn't seem to be core gameplay so much as QTE for bonus/convenience it's entirely forgivable. It's just well-designed really, and you feel it.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: [x] core gameplay loop as addictive as vampire survivors[x] it never really felt like I was wasting time at any point-----[x] memes, memes everywhere[x] lots of stuff to do, and ways to automate it when you get bored[] anything involving swirling the mouse (in lieu of swirling a thumbstick) is janky[] one of the bosses was a massive difficulty spike due to its size[] perhaps too addictive (I dunno I'm actually running short on stuff here)-----This is made by Nexon, the Korean publisher you might know of from a bunch of pay2win games that occasionally make it across the sea.  The devs here have decided to take all the addictive mechanics that keep people in their regular f2p games and dial it back down to "let the player have fun".  The game itself is made of a mass of minigames and other titles that are somehow neatly merged together, from roguelites to metal gear solid to stardew valley to pokemon snap, and the non-core ones only go for a couple minutes at any time.  At no point was I stuck in some dumb minigame hell the dev should have cut out.  Additionally there is nothing pushing you that hard in the main storyline/gameplay loop besides making enough sales to pay off the staff and gradually upgrade your gear, and even that's trivial once you start using enough tools and realise one captured good quality shark will make up nearly the entire day's menu on its own.  Once the day is paid off you can adventure around the watery universe at your heart's content, or manage things via the fish farm, or even waste time on minigames while waiting for the next night's cooking to startTLDR BELIEVE THE HYPE
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best put together games I have seen for quite some time. It just works. The art style and games remind me of some of the old Sierra titles back in the day like Hero's Quest, Police Quest, etc. The story and cutscenes are fantastic, just a really fun way to spend 15 minutes or a couple of hours at a time. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the best game indie game I have ever played, hands down. The amount of love and care that the team puts into the game is really clear and it's just insanely fun. Really taking my time as I refuse to let it end. Loads of content under the sea, bosses, and the restaurant sim management is incredible although I do wish it was a little bit more expanded upon (potential dlc please). props to the whole team for creating an unforgettable game.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER
