_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: NOT WHAT IT IS ADVERTISED.  If you're drawn to it primarily for the oceanic aesthetic, run away; its tagged as "casual" and "relaxing" and somehow even won a "Sit Back and Relax" Steam award, but its actually Super Motherload + Diner Dash with a seaside skin.  If I wanted to manage various kinds of timer-based systems and be given a bunch of arbitrary requests to fill, I'd do that irl and get paid actual money to do it, it's called having a job, and its not relaxing.  Also, this won a Bafta for Design?  For the hour i played it all it did was bark orders and rules at me and gave me a bunch of fetch quests. Bought it as one of 5 different games during a sale, ironically it was the highest-rated and the only one I'm returning.  I'm sure the game has many redeeming qualities but do NOT purchase this if you're looking for "a relaxing end to a long day", as one of it's awards suggested.  I literally felt like I had unwittingly signed up for a part time job.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I never knew I needed a game this much until I bought it. If i could i would download this right into my brain. I love the art style, the story, the characters and the fun energetic dialog. My one and only problem is your allowed (and encouraged to by the prices it sells by) to kill sharks. But other than that this is a underappreciated master piece.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: It took me a while to give a go as i was sceptical that I could enjoy it nearly as much as any other casual management game that i have played but whoa!! I am thoroughly enjoying Dave the Diver and haven't had a been able to have a break from it for the 4 hrs since starting today... So enjoyable and relaxing, loving the controls, the graphics, the story line and all the relatable personalities of the characters, the cut-scenes when enhancing and other story based snippets are so entertaining to watch, A tonne of love, fun and heck tonnes of effort must have been put into this game, highly recommend <3

_childDocuments_.review: Once again proof of how good an indie game can be. Dave the Diver has kept me playing for a long time and is one of the few games where I wanted to unlock all the archives. _childDocuments_.review: i'm starting to see a trend of games that i like that include (un)ethical ways to ruin an ecosystem. i wonder if that says something about myself.i love this game. it's calming and often puts me to sleep mid-session, but it can also keep me awake overnight. it's fun and imo easy to learn. i also like the ocean a lot.this will be a little long. my pros: - i love fishing games. a lot. in this one, you get to pull an england and stab fish or sharks to death if you want. or the american way with a rifle. you can do the ethical way and use a harpoon, too, but that's way less fun.- you're able to upgrade o2, dive depth, harpoon dmg, etc. at reasonable prices starting, but also price gouges later. some upgrades are necessary to advance! two or three you obtain later in the game, like crab boxes.- there are SO many smaller minigames. you unlock phone games, a farm with THREE different things to manage, a fish farm with a population problem (if you hoard sharks), an underwater farm, crab pots, marinca (pokemon but for fish), a branch for the restaurant, etc.- it has boss fights. you heard me right, you can fight a f-cking mantis shrimp who will beat you to death. or you can fight john watson. the bosses drop sushi ingredients that are one-time use only.- there is dredge (another superb fishing game) and godzilla DLC. while the godzilla dlc is good, i LOVE that they've added aspects of dredge into dave the diver. you get foggy nights to fish for aberrants, you sell them to the hooded people, and the rest you sell to the travelling merchant, making you a quick buck. HOWEVER, in my experience, the fog is relatively uncommon.- the game is PRETTY. the animations are smooth for pixels.- i also happen to like sushi a lot. the entire menu makes me hungry.

_childDocuments_.review: There was some debacle a while back about whether or not Dave the Diver is an indie game. I find that argument interesting now, because a few hours with the game is all it takes to make it clear how non-indie the game is. And I'm not just saying that because of the big AAA publisher parading its name all over the title screen.The game starts with a fun, innocent premise: Here's Dave, he's a diver, and he loves sushi; he's been invited to the mysterious Blue Hole where all kinds of fish gather. Get out there and catch some exotic fish to make exotic sushi! Sell those sushi, make a name for the restaurant, gather more and more customers, and eventually get rich, upgrade the restaurant, your equipment, the sushi; dive deeper, explore more of the ocean, catch even rarer fish, make even more sushi, get even richer! The blue hole hides many mysteries, which you can unravel slowly through bits and pieces of lore that you find on your journey to the Apex Sushi.Sounds like an awesome gameplay loop and a fun light-hearted plot, right? If only the devs agreed.Yes, unfortunately the devs had...grander ideas. I won't spoil too much, but let's just say it involves undead sea people and ancient amphibious parasites. The sushi restaurant element was only there to lure you over the edge and pull you deeper into a grandiose plot. It isn't that long until the whole sushi side of the story becomes exactly that: the side of the story. No longer are you diving to explore and find fish; you're diving to get to the next objective marker and progress the plot. The plot that has nothing to do with your sushi venture.Oh sure, you  money to upgrade your gear so you can stand a chance against Liam Eelson the Titanic Eel Monster that's guarding the next objective marker, but that's it, isn't it? It doesn't take that much money to upgrade your gear, and even if you don't have enough, just do some restaurant-ing for a day or two and you're gold--you probably have enough fish anyways, from your rampant hunting during your daily story-progressing; because why wouldn't you fill your pockets while you're down there in the sea? The fish are free. Beyond that, the only thing that restaurant upgrades serve is making the restaurant side easier and less engaging--namely by upgrading employee levels and how much each dish sells for. Usually a business management story like this would involve competing against rival businesses or something involving the success of your business, but there isn't really anything like that here; even the restaurant side quests revolve around gathering a specific set of ingredients before a set date, and if you have the ingredients by the deadline, you win; your restaurant quality or success doesn't matter.Shallow; that's what it is. Ironic, I know. The overarching plot was so disconnected from the premise of the game that it feels surreal to even experience, and the actual sushi premise that lured me in became an afterthought.Speaking of shallows, remember how I said the game is very clearly not indie? You wanna know how I came to that conclusion? Well first it started out with a lengthy tutorial on diving, followed by a lengthy tutorial on restaurant management, and then it introduced a weapon crafting mechanic with its own tutorial, and along your adventure you're given these minigames and micro-puzzles where you weld along a line or move rocks around--with their own tutorials. Something's missing; what is it? More minigames? Well here's a tamagotchi app for your phone. Golly gee, we've been having a lot of plot lately haven't we? How about a little refresher? Your weaponsmith friend is having a rhythm game dream and you NEED to play this rhythm game to proceed. Are you having fun yet? No? Man, what does it take to please people these days? Memory-matching? Pop-up Pirates? Seahorse racing? C'mon, one of these things should catch your attention! What's that? The story? The restaurant? B-but we have so many minigames to play! Look, your tamagotchi just evolved into a blobfish! Fun!It all screams of something desperately trying to capture as big an audience as possible, casting its net so wide it doesn't realise how thin it is.I'm not even sure why I kept playing until the end. Is it Dave? I think it's Dave. Dave's a cool guy! Friendly, competent, not afraid to speak his mind about the absurd behaviours of his friends; but he too has his passions, particularly about fish and sushi. Alas, even Dave is victim to the thinnening; as the story goes on, his writing devolves from an expression of a fun character to "I NEED to clear this blockade to continue the story!"It's a damned shame, really. Underneath all this fluff I see a potential Game of the Year, about a fun guy exploring a vast and mysterious underwater world, finding secrets of the deep as he pursues his one true love of exotic sushi. Maybe the mysteries will be solved, but the ultimate goal is that of sushi. But then for some reason they covered that GotY with the cement that is side material, and then more, and more, and more, until eventually that brightly-shining core became but a small unseen remnant of a fantastic idea, in the giant ball of dull grey cement.I feel kinda sad now. I don't even have the drive anymore to talk about how the procedural generation of the underwater world means almost nothing because all of the points of interest are always in the same direction and distance from the entry point so you're basically treading the exact same routes for 30 hours. I'm gonna go play...I'unno, Subnautica or something.

Feels like the game keeps throwing new tasks & mini games at you to distract you from the laborious grind of fishing for 2 hours each day to get to the restaurant to make sushi for 2 minutes.If this game would have been more snappy, like for example 'Cook, serve, Delicious!' Why do you need to use mirror -loading- go to house -loading- buy dumpling -triggered cut scene- to then exit the house -loading screen- to use mirror again or exit through door -loading screen- just to get a 8% movement speed increase? just put a stall or something instead? its madness when you are actually trying to 100% the game & make things any faster.There are no permanent movement speed upgrades. Why can you upgrade everything else but not this?The game doesn't let you catch 3 star fish until the end of the game, so there is more grinding each time you dive to search every single weapon box to get the tranq tip for the gun, so you could get more meat to make things take less which end up taking more if you dont find the tip which you are looking for... Why cant you just unlock these & keep them..?I dont even mind all of the Gyao raising, the Fishmon or all of the DLC content that much, but the base game is just SO ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slow. _childDocuments_.review: is a fun, beautiful, slightly educational game of dive fishing by day, and sushi serving by night.  Along the way, there is a storyline as deep and as complicated as the ocean, with many secrets to discover.You are the titular Dave, a professional diver who is oddly plump for someone who swims all day, more fat walrus than sleek dolphin.  Your slightly shady friend Cobra ropes you into helping him start and run a sushi restaurant.  The chef is the very temperamental (more "I am an ARTISTE!!!" than raging Gordon Ramsey) sushi chef named Bancho.The game has a basic rhythm of two dives per day, morning and afternoon, then running the restaurant in the evening.  Later, you get the option of a nighttime dive, but that cuts the night's hours for the restaurant by about a third.You fish by attacking the fishies swimming about and collecting their bodies.  You get a small marine knife for melee action and a harpoon gun and various guns for ranged attacks.  Annoyingly but realistically, you can only have two ranged weapons at a time:  the harpoon gun and one other.  You can switch guns at the dive box on your boat before a dive.  You will need the guns eventually, as there are sharks swimming about.And bosses to fight.You won't be finding just fishies, though.  You'll be able to harvest seaweed to be used in dishes and eventually pick up sea urchins and catch crabs and lobster.There are also weirder finds.  Salt, soy sauce, and other such ingredients can be found in big red cooking pots on the ocean floor.Gun cases contain different guns.  Drop the gun you have and bring up a new type of gun, and a friendly NPC will gain blueprints to craft a gun.  You don't keep the guns you find in the ocean, but any crafted guns become a permanent part of your arsenal.You'll also find some debris to pick up, which will be used to craft guns.Yellow marine chests will contain helpful items, but you won't be able to keep them with you past that dive, just like the guns.Cobra will eventually open a shop on his boat open only during the day.  Each day, he sells three random helpful items, such as a bomb to damage fish or a net trap to capture all but the largest fish.  Once bought, the items are good for just that dive.  It's just a small annoyance, since the items are all pretty cheap.  He'll also buy any non-food items you find.Dave has some limits to his dives.  You get a cargo box to carry your finds in.  Go over the weight limit and you'll be burdened and swim slower.Your oxygen tank doubles as your HP meter.  Hits from aggressive sharks will damage you.  You can dash a bit to avoid them or speed up, but this drains your O2 more.Run out of HP/air, and you'll have to be rescued, but at the loss of your finds on the dive.  In a move that slightly eases frustrations, you do get to keep one chosen item.  (Sometimes a dive is specifically for one thing, so this feature does help at times.)But one of the things you find on the ocean floor are spare O2 tanks, either as items to use or to take.There are also spots to call in a rescue pod.  You'll have to hold down a button for a few seconds to call it in, but it rewards you with a cutscene of Dave decompressing.Meanwhile, the sushi restaurant asks you to set up the menu based on the ingredients you've acquired. Bancho also will need to research most recipes, but this is done instantly.  He can also instantly and permanently enhance a dish to boost its price and taste value.  This spends a few dishes' worth of ingredients.You will have to prepare with a bit of care, as you cannot reclaim any ingredients you lay out for the night.  (Most sushi is raw, after all.)  You will never run completely out of dishes to serve, as there is a very cheap seaweed sushi dish to fall back on once you run out of ingredients.Later, you gain the ability to serve various drinks.  This is done with a quick and simple minigame at the customer.Bancho automatically makes the ordered dishes.  All Dave has to do is serve the food, pour drinks, and refill the wasabi.  He can also clean up after a customer for a little extra cash.You soon gain the ability to advertise for and hire some help.  These staff can then be trained up to improve their performance.  They can be assigned to help prepare food or serve it.  But no one but Dave grinds the wasabi.Staff can also be sent out to procure a little extra ingredients, which takes about a day.  How much they come back with is based on their level and stats.You are fishing in a place called the Giant Blue Hole, a strange nexus of the world's oceans where any fish found anywhere in the ocean might show up, albeit at the approximate depth and temperature of their usual home.This weird place is said to change its terrain each time you enter it.  It's a nice in-universe way of explaining why the game refreshes each time you enter the water.  You can never overfish the place.While this explanation makes it seem as if you'll encounter a procedurally generated area each time, this is NOT quite the case.  The terrain is hand-crafted, and only the shallows alternate forms.  Below a certain depth, you get the same layout each time.What DOES change is what spawns where and when.  Everything feels like a 50-50 or one-third chance of spawning.  This makes hunting for some specific creature not terribly frustrating.The game does a wonderful job of slowly introducing various features, and usually with a good tutorial walking you through using them.  You can take photos at certain spots, farm rice and yummy veggies, raise chickens, and raise fish, among many other things to do.Most of these are unlocked as you encounter new NPC friends, most of whom must be won over with a new specific dish with some new fish that the game unlocks access to.One huge potential source of frustration is the game's reliance on lots of QTEs and button combos.To simulate fighting with fish, you're often asked to do some quick button tapping.  Most of this can be cut back with a simple toggle in Settings.  Other times, time slows down and you are prompted to hit a specific button.Harpooning a fish requires you to hold down one button to aim and hit another to fire.Bancho gets roped into a series of low-rent cooking competitions, and preparing the meal is done through following along a series of QTE prompts.  Your performance there seems linked to his final score, but I never failed enough to lose.The devs also found a clever way to squeeze in a rhythm game.HOWEVER, anything game-critical I was asked to do, I managed to master enough to pass within minutes.This includes the boss battles.  All the bosses have unique moves and different ways to fight them.  Failure restarts the battle, allowing you to plunge back in, and with refreshed O2.  The game gives you just enough O2 items and ammo boxes to last, and often offers a gun case that might contain a good weapon.Certain long sequences of chases and puzzles also have automatic checkpoints that keep you from having to redo long stretches of game.This game is GORGEOUS to look at.  Fish seem to behave and swim realistically.  Underwater plants sway in currents.  Dishes are represented in pixel graphics yet still manage to look artful and delicious.Information and features are cleverly rounded up into apps on an in-game phone.  This includes Cooksta, an Instagram for chefs and foodies, where each dish you serve gets a loving photo from a customer the first time you serve it.The devs threw a whole lot of ideas and game styles into this one game, and yet it comes out as a delicious, perfect  (French fish stew).  Everything flows together well into a coherent whole and makes sense when they appear.And I haven't even spoiled the Giant Blue Hole's biggest secrets!
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: When I bought this game, I was expecting an actual casual adventure-management game.Emphasis on *casual*.It was advertised as such, and hyped up by so many reviews as such.I did not really watch any Lets Plays, My bad. After starting to play the game, watchingthe Lets Plays did not help much (many were older or heavily edited).It's not a bad game- if you love button smashing and really clunky controls.The controls- both kb/m and controller are awful, IMHO.The game is full of QTEs. TONS of them.There is a QTE override option in the settings, but it isn't well-implemented. It is marginally helpful when diving and harpooning fish.In the sushi restaurant- there is nothing to help with getting dishes, serving tea and trying to run back and forth while Dave gets exhausted every 3 seconds. Unlocking the ability to hire staff and train them takes forever- you need to get Gold status on COOKSTA, but you can't get followers and upvotes on the phone app if you are overwhelmed with customers that you can't get to fast enough to serve. The amount of time you have to get to them before they get mad is way too short, the controls above ground are awful (and only slightly better underwater). The first few days are "easy", then you get slammed.The economy is bad too- everything is expensive, but you make only pennies after selling food and drink in the sushi shop or selling off excess ingredients (fish) after deducting the daily cost of operation. You get punished, *hard* f you skip the sushi shop because your hands just can't deal with the button smashing and really awkward controls (even key rebinding did not help- if you could use the arrow keys *and* the movement and action keys at the same time while in the sushi shop- it would be much better. But you *can't*. You won't be using your mouse in the sushi shop- making it so you could move with the mouse and pick-up food and serve it would also be better.And OMG the number of unskippable cutscenes- so many unskippable cutscenes.So so so many unskippable cutscenes. That don't give you any useful information- they just "show off" the pixel art and add flavor. Flavor that isn't needed over and over and over and over.  Once is enough- thanks! I don;t want or need to see the same cutscene dozens of times.Not great.The settings menu only gives you the option of the "click and hold" QTE overrride and a "dedicated mouse cursor" which is a giant hand instead of a tiny Windows arrow cursor.The pixel art is beautiful if you are into it, but for folks with certain forms of colorblindness- it's going to be bad.If your hands are older, arthritic or you have tendinitis- the game is very difficult to play and is likely to be painful.(You can play short sessions, but there are quests and locations you cannot save & exit from- meaning you either finish it, or lose the progress and have to do it over again.)The text size is *tiny*, even on a 2560 x 1440 34" monitor. The font used is difficult to read (it took me a long time to figure out that the thing that looked like an upsidedown battery was actually the letter "Q".A good bit of stuff underwater is greyed out or very similar in color and saturation to the background it is on. Between that and the obnoxiously small text and HUD (that throws a big black window up on the screen, often blocking what you are trying to fight or shoot with your gun or harpoon gun)- this game is going to be bad for folks with low vision or some other vision conditions. Really near-sighted? You might be okay. Far-sighted? You are screwed.Probably *okay* for *some* Deaf and HoH players- the music is okay but I didn't miss it when I turned it off. But some audio cues will be missing, making the game a bot more difficult, since you won't hear hits with the gun, or sounds of approaching danger or damage to Dave.The controls are the worst part, though. The controls are awful for slow reflexes or tired hands.The game also throws you into situations with little or no explanation of what you have to do or expect- and the tiny text in the HUD and UI, and how little time the game gives you to try to read it means- yeah. You are going to  miss a lot and have to retry a lot of things. Probably not a terrible game for some folks (mostly younger, with perfect vision, perfect reflexes, able to jitter, can read tiny tiny tiny text, don't mid replaying various quests, don't mind getting punished like a thieving gollum if you die or fail to complete an interaction in the short time the game gives you...)I can't recommend the game, Soe people may really like it, and to be fair- diving and catching fish and exploring the map is fun. Dealing with the sushi shop and the painfully sow unlock of upgrades due to the horrible economy balance- not so fun.And a game advertised and often reviewed as "casual" should be fun, and able to be played by everyone. And this game is just not that. It isn't what all of the online advertisements said it was, what a good number of reviews said it was, what the carefully edited Lets Play videos said it was, and the devs and publishers trying to act like they are a small indie company is blatantly false.You are a masochist? Great! You'll love this game.You want a casual game about diving, avoid. It's not that.I will likely keep playing in short sessions, only because i am a Completionist and want to get as many achievements as possible. I will likely regret that urge many times over.(quick edit to correct some serious typos)

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, after playing more of the game, I'm remaking my review, with a tentative recommendation instead of the opposite. The issues I had still apply; there are some poorly-explained mechanics, some clunky combat (oddly, usually clunkier with 'wild' enemies rather than bosses) some unnecessary, annoying and tedious minigames, and the translation, while generally understandable, is still pretty bad.That said, if one can get past those issues, the core gameplay is entertaining, the story and cutscenes are wonderfully over-the-top, and the game seems to have a lot of heart.So overall, I'd recommend it...but only if you have a high tolerance for nonsense, positive and negative.

_childDocuments_.review: Saw this game a few times; wasn't really interested.  Finally gave it a chance...  First bit of playing, I loved the diving; hated the sushi restaurant; I mean LOATHED it.  Not my style of game.  Pushed through it until I got helpers/workers in the sushi place.  Was nice, but was still irritated I had to pour drinks.  Figured out you could train the workers... WHAT!?  Gave it a shot, found one that would pour drinks.  THANK YOU.OK so now that the rant is over...   It's a good game; just painful to get past certain things and definitely not the best at explaining things.  Heck it took me a bit to figure out how to do night time diving; thought I could do it AFTER doing the sushi bit; nope, gotta do it first AND the game punishes you for losing time at the sushi place giving you 1/3 less time to make money.  Meh...  Could have been balanced better on that part.I think after figuring out how to train the employees, the game started to shine and grow on me.  I still have to "deal" with the sushi restaurant which I'd rather not.  Lots of hidden gems, some fun games.  Only one bad  "boss" fight so far, and the problem is the lack of good information in this game can cause you some stress.  When you run into a bump or issue, go look it up.  Someone else has already figured it out and posted about it.  Wish the Devs would take note and make it more accessible in game vs needing to go external.

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty satisfying to play but that's all it is for me - just a sort of mindless distraction, so not worth spending more time on. The game absolutely refuses to just let things happen and let me notice them. It doesn't want me to explore, it wants to tell me exactly where to go and what to do. It loves spending 30 seconds on a cutscene that says everything it needs to in the first 5 seconds.Here's an example: A dolphin motions for me to follow it. I understand that it's a dolphin and that it's motioning for me to follow it after a few seconds, but the cutscene goes on for another 20 seconds, and then a dialogue box pops up and Dave says to himself incredibly obvious observations that are already apparent because this is a VISUAL MEDIUM - "Wow a dolphin!" "Wow I think it wants me to follow it!"I'm also not a fan of the small forced minigames (spamming buttons to catch bigger fish, or the stupid cutting game). It just gives me mobile game vibes - it adds nothing but extra time and fake engagement. Wasn't it exciting to catch the big fish because you had to press A 80 times? No. It's not challenging, it's just annoying, and it doesn't make engage more in the simulation of fishing because the abstraction is so simplistic that it's meaningless.Should I expect it to be an immersive exploration game like, for example, Abzu? Maybe not, but even if it just wants to be a mindless guided experience then it shouldn't constantly interrupt me with pointless minigames and long cutscenes. Just let me play the mindless game then.

_childDocuments_.review: Dave The Diver is a beautiful masterpiece of a game. I do not often buy / play early access games as sometimes they can be janky, full of bugs, or just not at the stage where there's enough story to play it. However, this game is an exception. I've had my eye on this game since it came out and since someone I watch on YouTube (CallMeKevin - funny Irish man) played it last year. I've been debating buying it purely because of the price being £16.99 and as a student I lack money to buy games regularly. However, I got paid and just decided - screw it. I bought the game and do not regret it, AT ALL. It's so simple and laid back. I like all the mechanics - although some seem a little daunting at first I will admit. This game is stunning, and i mean it literally. The graphics are gorgeous, and all the little cut-scenes when you enhance your sushi or make a new weapon (an so on) are just so unique and quirky. I always giggle a little when seeing them - and I never expect them to be as good as they are. Did I say the graphics are gorgeous already? I love how the game is so pixelated and then.. there are just 3D boats that come driving into the screen. For crying out loud, one of them drives a literal fish boat.The music is cute. I love how you can also just go into the phone and into the "music" app and listen to the soundtrack the devs have made. I've played many games but I don't think I've ever really seen that in any game, besides like stardew valley. I think it would be really cool if the soundtrack was added to spotify, I think I'd listen to it a lot. I strongly recommend this game if you are looking for something to play. Even though it is in early access as of right now, I believe full release is June 2023 (so I have heard). The game is only an in-game month when it comes to the story, but you can play beyond it and just run the sushi restaurant. I expect I'll play for a good 20/30 hours before leaving it and waiting for full release. Support the devs and buy the game - if you were on the fence like myself then I say just do it. Play it for an hour and if it's not for you then refund it ;)

_childDocuments_.review: Someone somewhere wasted their wish upon a star for a mobile game that wasn’t pay to win gatcha trash. And Dave the Diver was born.Or maybe the developer saw the mobile game landscape and wanted to challenge themselves, who knows? What I can tell you, is that Dave the Diver takes super simple could-work-on-a-touchscreen mechanics across a Smorgasboard of familiar genres and smashes it all together into a surprisingly lengthy and worthwhile adventure.It’s got bits of warioware, mobile farm sims, burger time resturant-ing, pokemans, and steamworld dig-esque loop. It works better than you’d expect, and no one element stays longer than It should. Wrap it all up with truly Humorous characters and scenarios, and this little would-be mobile game that lasts upwards of 20 hours until the end never gets stale. There’s even plenty of endgame grind for folks that wanna stick around a bit longer, and all without a single gatcha or request for your credit card information.It’s a very fine game.

_childDocuments_.review: In a sea of action-adventure-roguelike-shop-management games, Dave the Diver manages to stand out (pun intended) with it's pixelated charm and se gameplay mechanics. You play as Dave (duh), a diver (double duh) helping his friend run a new sushi bar. Your job is to gather ingredients throughout the day which are then sold at the restaurant during the night, the proceeds from which helps you buy higher gear so you can gather more ingredients faster. For a game that is supposed to feel grindy beyond comprehension from it's description, it's insane how fresh it feels everytime you pick it up. The sliver of a storyline that does exist isn't the most unique, but it's executed extremely well. Aside from it's base gameplay, Dave the Diver features a potpourri of a minigames, making every minute un-repetitive in some capacity, and I might even go a step further to say it has successfully crammed every conceivable mini-game that you can think of. 10/10 would drop my fat behind into the Blue Hole again.

_childDocuments_.review: A mastercraft of a game and unassuming too!For those who don't like any *potential* spoilers: Recommended 100%, great for casual gameplay and mixes lots of types of games togetherFor those who might want to risk any potential spoilers:Incredible mix of genres, there is diving aspect which is akin to that of a platformer, the sushi place mangement (in staff, menu and performance), there are puzzles to solve, a really cool and sweet story, there are also a bunch of different mini-games and button-prompt-action parts too,There are smile-humour moments throughout which make it very light-hearted, and the game also seems to keep unlocking parts slowly in a way which keeps the game fresh and interesting.The combat/balance is perfect, and the penalty for death is fair - The challenge is still there, but you can still play it casually while laying down, it is full controller compatible and has kept me occupied for hours so far,It is low-tax on the PC/Laptop and for the price is an absolute steal - 100% Recommend this to anyone with an ear to listen :)

_childDocuments_.review: I ignored this game during the Steam Summer sale. I thought, "Meh, I've already played Stardew Valley. I don't think I can fit myself into this game." I was really, really wrong. Dave the Diver is instantly addicting. I've owned the game for two days and already have 12 hours on board. It's really fun. I'm not sure what the total playtime is, but if it was 13 hours or 300 hours, I would have felt as if it was the right amount, because you're rewarded the whole way through the game.This game is incredible at helping you master its mechanics. Each mechanic is segmented so you aren't overloaded with things to do and feel like you can't manage everything at once. As each new mechanic was introduced, I thought, "OK, this is the part where I don't understand things" or "I'm going to start falling behind now," and it never happened. I kept up the whole time and felt like the last bit made the whole even better.Now for the downsides: Controller default mapping isn't exactly intuitive. I've screwed up several things because I was pressing the wrong buttons, because I felt another button mapping was more natural.

_childDocuments_.review: Game does a great job at allowing you to learn each mechanic by itself for a bit then adds another. Then as you learn this and get to place where it makes sense the game says well what if we added a farm, a fish keeping area, another restaurant, etc. Some guy said this is "predatory" but as a avid gamer, this is just good game design. This is EXACTLY how other games should work. You add to the game 1 mechanic at a time so that by the time you are at the end you can balance everything without starting out lost. In my mind this game is the exact opposite of Astroneer which just says ♥♥♥♥ you learn the entire game at once without any slow drip of content. Game devs take note, this is how you can make a game that has like 30 different mechanics without making it stressful to learn/start.

_childDocuments_.review: If you’re into games that let you chill but still keep things interesting, Dave the Diver is a total win. You dive into the ocean to catch fish, turn them into sushi, serve them at your restaurant, and use the money to upgrade your gear—it’s such a satisfying loop. The game hits this perfect balance between peaceful moments, like exploring the cove, and bursts of action, like dodging sharks or landing that tricky harpoon shot. Plus, there’s so much to do: farming, fishing, boss battles, mechs, and even naming chickens! The animations are super charming, the characters are funny, and the gameplay keeps you hooked for hours. If you want something unique that’s relaxing but never boring, this is it!

_childDocuments_.review: A game that scratches many itches.The basic premise of the game is that you're a diver catching fish for your growing sushi restaurant. So, of course there will be a restaurant management component to the game. However, that's not all there is.You get different weapons in the game that you could use to catch fish. Depending on the element that you use, a different mini-game will pop up that will determine whether you get the fish or not (don't worry, you'll have another try or two if you fail the first one).On top of that, there's also the collecting component which not only entices you to catch all the fish, but to catch them at their highest grade (3 stars). This isn't forced upon you, but it's certainly a nice goal for those of us who are collectors at heart.Then there's the restaurant proper in which every dish you serve can be upgraded to a max of level 10. Oh, and did I mention you can hire people? Yeah, you also train those guys to a max of level 20 -- each one with a pair of skills that help in certain roles more than others. Then there's all the other mini-games you encounter that highlight both the silliness and the creativity of the game. I don't want to spoil it all, but this game is honestly full of content. It can be overwhelming for those who choose to rush through it all, but the good news is you can take your time with the story and objectives.Then there's the story, which clearly doesn't take itself too seriously. Couple that with the humourous cutscenes and you're in for a good time. All in all, an amazing game and well worth the full price to show support for a game that clearly has a lot of heart put into it. Definitely grab it on a sale if you're on the fence.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely fun and moreish core gameplay loop, with endearing and quirky characters. Fish species, also, are brilliantly varied, but with predictable enough behaviour that you can adjust to hostile fish attacking you, yet enough variety that you can be caught off guard sometimes.The game often feels bloated, particularly in the late game, with far too many aspects to the gameplay - all quite different to each other: across farming, fishing, restaurant work, boss fights, minigames, etc. However, this is far from detrimental to the game, mostly just becoming evident when going for full completion.

_childDocuments_.review: Dave the Diver is a relentlessly enjoyable experience. When I played the demo months ago, I could tell that it was something unique and fun, but I had no idea that the final product would be packed with so much content while also remaining cohesive and endearing throughout. Then, to top it all off, it has some of the most hilarious and well-made pixel art cutscenes I have ever encountered. You can stop here and just play it, but if you need more convincing, continue below. Abbreviated Review:  The innocuous beginning of Dave the Diver makes it seem like you’re in for a run-of-the-mill management sim and side-scrolling ‘shooter’ of some sort. Your protagonist Dave is a seemingly mild-mannered and friendly guy who takes on any task presented to him with a smile. So, in addition to be-ing the sole diver hunting fish in the occasionally hostile environment of an island-encompassed blue hole, you’ll also be managing the menu, financials, décor, and being the primary server in the restaurant. The only thing you won’t be doing (mostly) is crafting the sushi itself – which is left to your mysterious hardnosed Chef Bancho. Bancho, like many of the noteworthy characters in the game, has a small story that you get to explore within the gameplay. Character exploration is part of the larger narrative in what ultimately becomes a fairly expansive story with a lot of mysteries and discoveries within it. Like the blue hole itself, the adventure seems basic on the surface but is actually deep and full of secrets. While initially your goals are only stocking and running a restaurant, various characters will wander out to meet you on the dive platform of your small boat to request your assistance in several unique and iterative quest chains. Some of these chains weave into the core of the story while others are just extra tasks that can provide rewards and keep the game rich. The money that you earn as a reward from some of these quests adds to your primary source of income – the restaurant. This money can be used for many tasks and resources including augmenting the restaurant as well as upgrading your gear to dive deeper, longer, and with better tools to keep you alive. The deeper you go, the more threats you’ll face, but you’ll also encounter rarer sea creatures that can be diced into more profitable dishes at the restaurant. However, that’s only a small portion of what you’ll find in the depths. One interesting aspect of the journey through Dave the Diver is the process of unlocking the things you need to make it into new environments. You’ll, of course, need more air available as it’s not only for breathing but also functions as your health bar. Any time you’re stung by a jellyfish or snapped at by a shark, you’ll lose air – while also steadily losing it as you breathe. You can find barrels of that life-retaining substance randomly on the sea floor along with chests full of one-time-use resources like underwater scooters and temporary oxygen boosts. You’ll also find chests with new spear tips, guns, and melee weapons you’ll need to fend off and take down larger predators and prey. Part of the unique challenge any time you dive into the ocean is that you have a sort of roguelike experience where you need to obtain stronger spears and weapons and the environment is slightly different. The undersea environment isn’t procedurally generated, so you will see the same map over several dives, but there are at least a handful of maps to navigate that change with the time of day. However, with the random nature of the items you obtain each time and the progressively more challenging creatures that appear as the story moves forward, it feels a lot more diverse than it is. The chapter-based campaign is blocked out by the main quest line that uses key items to limit your overall progression. While you can upgrade your oxygen and suit to go deeper as well as your harpoon and weapons to fish more efficiently, even your first steps into deeper water require you to complete a quest for a headlamp. You can sit around avoiding the main quest to fish endlessly and run the restaurant, but the game is built around the excellent pacing that has you balancing that aspect with exploration and mystery quite well. Of the 25 hours it took me to finish the main part of the game, I made only a handful of dives that weren’t connected in some way toward progression.   Dave the Diver’s pacing works so well because it always gives you something new to do. The number of minigames and evolving mechanics is astounding. From the simplest tasks like having a different minigame for reeling in a big fish using each different spear tip to an immersive rhythm-based music challenge you can revisit at any time, you will never be complacent. It was almost overwhelming at times with how any given moment you could be using a mechanic you have never seen before to accomplish your next task. There are entire moments crafted in the game using controls and functionality that happen a single time, which almost seems wasteful if it wasn’t also fun as hell. Between the minigames, boss fights, ever-expanding roles of spearfishing and restaurant management, and the hilarious cutscenes sprinkled throughout the game, I was blown away by everything presented. For a mere $20, this game provided one of the best experiences I’ve had in an indie game in a long time, and I am hoping that this isn’t the end of the adventure for Dave. The ongoing nature of serving new dishes in the restaurant and the potential to unlock more secret caves or deeper adventures leaves plenty of room for more content. However, even if somehow the developers don’t seize that opportunity, this game is well worth picking up and diving into.

_childDocuments_.review: Dave the Diver is a casual game that takes you on an underwater adventure, where you explore the ocean, catch fish during the day, and turn them into profitable dishes at night. It offers a mix of action side-scrolling, light restaurant management, and mini-games.One of the great things about the game is that each dive usually lasts under 20 minutes, striking a perfect balance where diving never feels drawn-out or monotonous.As you juggle around dealing with fish that get progressively dangerous and the increasing cost of your gear, every day in Dave the Diver is played to the fullest.The map is dynamic and changes its layout from time to time, which keeps things fresh and adds to the excitement.The music creates a relaxing atmosphere that complements the breathtaking scenery of the ocean.The combat is pretty bare-bones, which is fine since combat isn't the primary focus.Bosses are generally pretty cool and easy to deal with, you can get away with not having good weapons with you all the time and just pick up a decent weapon in the arena.The animations are really nice, and I love how every ingredient in the game has its own cute little illustration. It's clear that the devs put a lot of effort into these details.I had a blast playing this game, that is until I encountered the fish people.If you're interested in my description of the game, you should turn back and give it a try. Trust me, Dave the Diver is enjoyable before it takes a nosedive. Also, I'll be spoiling pretty much everything, so this is your last chance to experience the game firsthand.Dave the Diver is an amalgamation of creatively bankrupt mini games that are stitched together to create an illusion of exploration and novelty to stall the game as long as possible.Beneath the surface of casual and cozy indie game lies a soulless grinding QTE fest that has daddy Nexon behind its back.I would give Dave the Diver a seven out of ten. The entire game peaked at the Blue Hole Shallow, fitting for a game that has no depth.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: 30 hours of fun, but there are some issues. 4/5.+ The graphics are beautiful, the music is great, and the story line is quite interesting.+ The game is very calming and addicting. A good example for a simulation game to get lost in.+ Bancho's cooking cut-scenes. Superb.+ The exploring and fishing part is very very fun.- The few first hours of the game can get a bit repetitive, because most of the content is mid-game. At first, i wasn't able to play for hours and hours, and a 45 min session was all i could do. it gets better in time.- There are many weapons to use in the game,  but the upgrading menu can be quite confusing. Not only that, but i ended up using one weapon cause i didn't need anything else. One level upgrade was enough, even for the endgame. The Devs should put a bit more attention to weapons, upgrading them, and farming for materials (especially ores) to upgrade them.- I wish there were some difficulties to the game, make it harder fishing\having more sharks etc.- I wish there was some more emphasis on growing plants, making it a bit more fun. At the moment it feels like a very boring side mission, a tedious task. -
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: The diving part of the game is really fun. The sushi serving, tea pouring, farming, other farming, seahorse racing, fetch questing, beer pouring, menu managing, staff managing, fish farm managing, card matching, shipwreck cutting, gambling, quick time eventing and random the anime DDR game put me off.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I was genuinely impressed with the game. The initial gameplay was thrilling and highly enjoyable, drawing me in with its immersive world and engaging mechanics. However, as I progressed, the excitement quickly wore off. The game becomes increasingly tedious and repetitive. What began as a promising adventure turned into a monotonous grind that drained my enthusiasm.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best games I've ever played. The mechanics translate well to controller vs keyboard, and the tutorial is wonderful. It's the perfect blend of casual and--OH GOD A SHARK. I spent way too long in chapter 1 because I didn't want to advance the questline yet. Beautifully illustrated, hilarious dialogue, and finally, a relatable protagonist. I'm nearing the end of the game, which makes me a bit sad, but I know this game will be fun to play again and again.Tl;dr is buy this game. No tags fit the gameplay because it's incredibly unique. And to the devs, well done and please give us a second Dave the Diver or even more DLC ily
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: The game never gets dull with the variety of minigames and new features spread throughout your time playing. Even near the end of the game I was still unlocking new content but none of it ever felt like a wasted opportunity. You're never rushed into doing anything so it's very easy to play at your own pace.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: This game really was something special, quite the treat. I bought this on sale on a whim, I'm not a big indie gamer but I was looking for a new game that I could just jump in, play a bit, jump off; and Dave the Diver is very much that type of game! That said, I found myself fully engrossed in every little bit of the game and couldn't put it down! What I also loved about the game is that it kept giving you new, fun stuff to do up until the very end of the game, so it never got stale or boring through my entire play-though. There wasn't a thing about this game I didn't love. The writing, the easter egg references, the soundtrack, the hilarious yet stylistic cutscenes that never got old, the gameplay + mini games, everything. I don't think I've been this surprised and thoroughly, this game really blew me away and it's abundantly clear the development team put a whole lot of love into it.Buy this, play this, love this - that's not a recommendation, that's a guarantee
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: 3 times over worth the price, packed with content, tons of nods and pop culture references. just finished the game but i am looking forward to play more. graphics are adoable 7/10 and animations are surprisingly complex and cute 9/10. game play 9/10. Music 7/10 (10/10 looking at the track hot pepper tuna). best credit sequence in a long while. amazing how they managed to balance punishment for greed with rewards for progression. beating the main story boss was SUPER gratifying and left me wanting to play the past credits content even more. I have not played the full game before the big patch (only demo) but in this state the game is incredibly good.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I have almost spent 100 hours in this game, the achievement that is difficult for me to achieve is collecting ice weaponsThe storyline can be completed in about 3 hours. After the story is finished, you can relax by planting plants, cultivating fish, raising gyao fish, and many more things you can enjoy in this game.please give me a gift so I can be more enthusiastic about playing dave the diver for up to 1000 hours XD
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: It feels surreal to be able to play an indie game of this quality in a year where we have had so many great games already! Dave The Diver is a unique experience that will stick with you. Whether it's the amazing pixel art style, soundtrack or hilarious characters, this game will surprise you in many different ways.In a year where we have had so many amazing games, my backlog has only grown even more. However, I decided to make some time for this game and it ended up being one of the best decisions I made all year!DTD blew my mind when it came to how much the game had to offer. Everytime, I assumed I had experienced everything the game had to offer, it would suddenly introduce something completely new. The developers managed to create a game that offers a variety of gameplay, fun story, hilarious characters and plenty of stuff to grind for! If you are looking for a relaxing pixel art game, look no further, this is the game for you!Story: DTD is about a fat guy that gets scammed into coming out of retirement, only to end up as a diver/waiter/cook/manager/farmer/researcher. You are tasked to explore a mysterious "Blue Hole" that has a different environment each day! The further you descent the more you discover about the mysteries the "Blue Hole" has to offer. I won't spoil anything about the story, but it's pretty entertaining imo!Gameplay Mechanics:DTD revolves primarily around 2 gameplay mechanics. The first mechanic is being the diver, exploring the "Blue Hole" and collecting fish to supply your restaurant. The second mechanic revolves around managing your restaurant. Both are very fun and as you progress through the game, you unlock more things to do. Graphics:I am going to be honest, I am a sucker for pixel art games. DTD is no exception to this rule. The way the game implements pixel art and manages to utilize it is honestly incredible. I WISH MORE GAMES LOOKED LIKE THIS!Difficulty Level:There are no difficulty options in the game and tbh it doesn't really need it. The further you progress in the game, the harder it gets. Like I mentioned earlier, it's mostly a relaxing game that tends to offer challenging situations in smaller doses. Anyone should be able to start and finish this game without any trouble.Performance:I played this game on a 2080ti and a 5800X3D, no issues at all. Runs very smoothly and in my total 60 hours playtime I think I only crashed once or twice.Dave The Diver is a game that has definitely left its impact in 2023. I look forward to whatever MINTROCKET brings us next! 9/10Things I Would Love To See In The Future:- More upgrades for your diving knife (and that it evolves similar to the harpoon gun).- DLC? I fully completed the game, but I still want more!- Allow us to hire someone to manage the fish farm.- More decorations for the restaurant!
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I find it hard to simply recommend or not recommend this game, but since the current reviews are overwhelmingly positive I want to emphasize the flaws and hopefully things can be improved in the future. This game was very fun at the beginning - exploring the ocean, fishing and cooking, all the cool cut scene animations and new features...I would rate 10/10 if the whole game experience can maintain that level. However, as the story proceed, the diving parts become painful - no map, often have to swim long distance with a slow speed, boring tasks and super boring puzzles & hard and sudden battles...some boss fights and chasing fights are absolutely terrible. The last region, particularly, feels very empty, and exploring it with little direction was not rewarding at all, only to find I should return later to proceed story.In short - this game has many enjoyable contents, but I feel that because they are trying to pack as many as possible in the game, they didn't have time to balance/test every part very well, resulting in some bad game experience especially later in the game. Given the price I have to say I'm a bit disappointed, so if you really want to give it a try, I would suggest wait for a good discount.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Quite possibly the best indie game I have played in awhile. Basic description is its an exploration, combat, and restaurant management game, which seems odd on paper, but it actually works out pretty well and is super fun. The game also has lots of personality, not only in the characters but the art and environments as well. I'm a sucker for pixel art, so I may be biased, but it all just works so well.Psudo-game reviewer description over, 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Mixes different game genres, and pulls its off beautifully!The game progressively adds mini games / new features! which keeps the game refreshing and fun, this game keeps on giving.The art Is refreshing and very well done, story and side quest are perfectly paced and un-rushed allowing for ample time to explore if desired.10/10!
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly fun game that gets carried by it's charming characters and vibe.Pro:-big cast of various colourful good, fun characters and dialogue reminiscent of good old games such as FF7-relaxed, light hearted mood-easy to get into-interesting gameplay loop of exploring and gathering during the day and running a restraurant at night. reminded me a bit of games such as Recettear, although this game is more well rounded with less edges to get stuck on-charming graphics. some of the cutscene animations have no right to be this good-various mini games-decent, light hearted story-surprisingly long (took me 34 hours to complete main story)-fair priceCon:-controls can be a bit wonky at times, especially during fights-weird difficulty balance: deaths in exploring loses you everything you had, meanwhile scripted bossfights etc are strewn with checkpoints like a lot of modern games. overall the difficulty is best described as "challenging but casual friendly", similar to most modern nintendo games perhaps-way too grindy and upgrade gated. a lot of things are necessary or important to make progress and cost money, you have to choose between things that progress your main story or benefit your restaurant and sales, and you often have to score the same old regions to not miss limited edition fish that are in season. all of this contributes to a gameloop thats 2-3x more grindy and tiring as it needs to be-sometimes overwhelming amount of things to do: main story goals, secondary mission goals, collection goals, VIP menues, seasonal fish parties, taking care of your weapon upgrades, taking care of your equipment upgrades, taking care of your farm, taking care of your fish farm... while it always remains managable, the sheer amount of things to pay attention to at the same time can be tiring-weapon upgrades are mostly useless: some weapons have situational uses, but most scripted boss fights provide you with the means to win regardless of your weapon upgrades-fusion of restaurant gameplay and story gameplay is not ideal: you can easily finish the main story without reaching the end of the restaurants capabilities. less grindiness in the diving adventures, and more focus on main stories related to the restaurant so you get to experience the restaurant in the end game in all its glory by the time youre done with the main story wouldve been nice
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Before I get negative, . However, to me this is a great example of a good game that gets kneecapped by its execution. The core gameplay loop of gather fish and run the restaurant is fantastic and fun, yet it feels like the creators had no confidence in this being enough, leaving a lot of it feeling thin/abandoned in favour of other aspects.As a result, there are tons of events/minigames. Most of which are obligatory. Explained in a window that only appears the first time you start. That will stop the fun gameplay loop in its tracks. Constantly. Without spoiling, you will be forced to skip days without warning, locked into timed minigames that cannot be skipped or exited, boss fights in the middle of the otherwise chill game experience, and sudden walls of dialogue to either over-explain a plot point or awkwardly explain a new tacked-on game feature.Combined with the delay for entering and exiting all areas/UI elements and gotcha aspects designed to punish you for not remembering one of the many random tasks that are scattered across said areas/UI makes for a great game that actively tries to prevent you from playing the core game.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Creative. Ambitious. Exciting. Relaxing. Original. Promising.A lot of words come to mind while playing Dave the Diver and none of them are negative. Support the developers.

_childDocuments_.review: Dave The Diver is an incredibly difficult game, surpassing the likes of Dark Souls and Elden Ring. You are playing as Dave, a middle-aged man who intends to hunt down every species of fish in the ocean and the sea people. With the help of evildoers such as Cobra and Duff, you swore to wipe out dolphins, sharks and whales. Luckily, John Watson and his Sea Blue organisation, is here to stop you from committing such heinous crimes. Sea Blue organisation strives to protect the environment and every time I played as Dave, I realized how much I have sinned and my cruelty of hunting such fishes. May John Watson bring victory to the oceans and defend it from intruders like Dave the tyranny.

_childDocuments_.review: So I finished Dave The Diver and the game is technically awesome and the game play / story brilliant.Morally its a whole conversation... If you are an actual diver or someone who loves marine-life you might want to read this first.. In short - it feels like two groups of very different people were involved....Group one (original idea) is the devs who came up with a basic concept - "retro style diver game where diver dives and kills everything in order to help run a sushi restaurant + uses cool weapons and tactics". They probably developed the original game which looked good and then realised "hey, we need some sort of narrative". Then they realized it would be good to get input from someone with actual knowledge of marine life / diving.So group two arrived who were probably actual divers / people who knows marine life (hence forth Actual Divers or AD) and this is how it went:AD: "wow, cool looking game and we can add so many details and educational things to the story, like factoids on all the marine life "Devs: "and then we kill it all right?ADP: "uuuhm, maybe not all of it, there needs to be some element of education and some environmental elements, for example we will save the dolphins and not kill mammals"Devs: "is a narwhal a dolphin?ADP: "uuh, kinda yes. why?Devs: "no reason (scribbles note 'kill narwhals, dont tell greenies')ADP: "so cool, we can add a Sea Sheppard character modeled on Paul Watson to help carry this story"Devs: (says nothing, makes note - 'sea Sheppard style bad guys + Paul Watson aka John Watson = main moron and bad guy)ADP: "what are you writing there"devs: "nothing, keep going...."ADP: "cool, we will help you add some visual details to make the scenery look awesome and we can even feature super newly discovered animals like the Barreleye Fish"Devs: "perfect and dont you worry, we will make it look real Coool and pretty" (makes a note - barrel eye fish sushi, sounds delicious. kill it)By the end of this you have this weird mix of a game with some hit and miss environmental elements (save whales and *most* dolphins but slay everything else that moves. Oh and its a very weird trend where they start you off small (harpoon some clownfish) until you get in the habit of hunting every imaginable species of shark which stems from a culture very rooted in Asian cuisine and tradition (note that global shark populations have been decimated because if it), but then towards the end of the game they ramp it up to where So yeah, it was a very mixed and bizarre game and not something I would feel proud to tell my diver friends to play. Did I enjoy the game? Yes. Did I feel very dirty and hypocritical each time I played it. VERY

_childDocuments_.review: This game is FANTASTIC. I am a huge fan of calm sit-down games and have never found one that I truly loved since Stardew Valley. However, Dave The Diver wildly exceeded my expectations. This game is a master class in what development teams should strive for. Every detail of this game is masterfully created, from the artwork to the fight sequences, the puzzles, the characters, and the cut scenes. When I thought there couldn't be any more things they had to offer, they added a new mechanic, boss, gun, etc. It is one of the most fun and creative games I have played. This is one game that I will likely never put down and will continue to play even with the story being completed. 10/10!

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, it's hard to put into words exactly how I feel about this game. _childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: A great sea adventure with the added benefit of managing a restaurant on your own.It earned the "Sit back and relax 2023" award and that tells you a lot about the game. It's a not so challenging and laid back game that let's you enjoy the great pixel artwork and atmosphere of the ocean.You also get a free Dredge DLC which is always a nice bonus!
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome. I went into it thinking I was going to catch fish and run a sushi restaurant, yes I did that, but I did SO MUCH MORE. There is so much content in this game, for it's price it feels like a steal. I have intense thalassophobia and I thought this game would trigger this for me. And some bits at first, it did, but this game is so charming that it's hard to feel any fear. There are sharks. They suck, but they never come at you as a surprise and they're all very deal-with-able. There are zero spooky surprises. Some of the boss fights have creepy intros, but the fights themselves feel like something you'd expect in like a metroidvania. The soundtrack is amazing. I ADORE the boss fight music and Duff's music. The cutscenes and art were all awesome. This game has an awesome sense of humor.Highly recommend this game.Edit as of Nov 22, 2023, I still highly recommend this game. It got even better.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: While the overall implementation is fairly polished, I can't play this game very long. The gameplay is very repetitive and simple. There's really not much to managing your restaurant either. It may as well be an idle game, all it really requires is button mashing which just hurts my hand. It would be better if it didn't have so many pointless pauses and cutscenes and annoyingly long dialog. Why does it take me back to the boat when I skip time at the restaurant? It's annoying and I just have to wait for two extra loading screens! (which are really long for such a simple game btw).The pixel art is good and I do appreciate the quality but I can't stand it keeps popping up with these cutscenes especially in the restaurant. Probably to distract you from how little actual gameplay there is. Sometimes you can skip but you still have to hold the button down constantly and tap it like 50 times to skip all the dialog. If you're not going to record actual dialog how about just don't put it in the game. No one cares.Long story short, don't buy this game if you like games with actual depth. If you only care about it looking cute and clicking buttons over and over again maybe you'll be happy with this. Game should cost about $5 for what it is.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER
