_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a "Meh" option, but I've played too many, FAR worse games, to not give this a thumbs up.This is less one game and more a collection of fishing-themed minigames, most of which are references to other games. I wish they had spent less time on the minigames and more time polishing the core fishing loop, because I found it frustrating far more than I found it fun.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: It starts off very fun and explorative, first hours of the game I thought - this is awesome! But very soon, as you'll see other negative reviews point out, it becomes an absolute drag as it floods the game with tonnes of mechanics, management minigames and fetch quests. The loop that used to be so fun at first, quickly becomes dull and a chore to do. It's sad, cause I really loved the game at the start - the graphics, the funs, the atmosphere and the loop. But the game tries to be everything all at once to its own demise.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely cracked. More game than game in a game. I'm still unlocking things to do, the majority of them have an impact on your business and progression too. Though it's not necessarily needed for completion the compulsion to keep doing everything you can is powerful and I could definitely see it being overwhelming for some. The overall game is mostly relaxing and has a fun vibe ingrained into everything. Mechanics hold up and gain depth as you progress. Tons of customisation options, though I must admit the soundtrack feels a bit staid and placid in a lot of places. Might fit the vibe for some but I'd love more of a change up to be a feature. You can't fault the value for money though.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: A solid game. Excellent art style with a wide cast of fun characters. Music matches every location very well and the gameplay loop is satisfying. Try not to get caught up in trying to catch a perfect version of every fish as soon as possible since most them only spawn after certain events that occur as you progress through the calendar and story. My only gripe are the boss fights. They feel out of place at times and can occur way too frequently.Just 100%'d the game and I must say, still a good time. Except Gyao. That achievement would take way too long during normal gameplay. Made a separate save just to get it to not affect my main game. Apparently, nothing happens when you go deep into debt by continuously passing time.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastically fun game for all levels of gamers. It can be very challenging at times, but the most challenging missions are optional. The story is great fun, with a touch of fantasy to it. You really get to know the characters, and you can extend game play for quite some time, losing yourself in daily fish hunting and running the restaurant. It also takes elements from a ton of popular and iconic games and play styles, adding their own spin. It's a little bit Stardew Valley. A little Guitar Hero. Plenty of a restaurant simulator. A dash of Splinter Cell and Mechwarrior. And of course, entirely it's own imaginative story and game. This is now one of my favorite games. Cannot recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Good game!So far 4 hours in, not a thought in my mind like "oh no I exceeded the maximum refund time".Smooth gameplay, barely any loadtimes, I quite like the art style and the smoothness of everything.Fun gameplay, you fish in the morning, fish in the afternoon and service a restaurant in the evening.There's events, both in the water as well as the restaurant, progression into some sort of activities.Though to say the game has a story behind it may be a stretch.Discover mysteries as you go deeper and farther, fighting vast sea beasts and the occasional human.Uncover the forgotten pasts and have fun all the way while doing it.Definitely worth the money on my account.I rule that if I can get 1 hour of absolute fun playtime for each $ spent, it's been worth it.And though im barely 20% in of the time vs price, im sure ill reach well beyond it and still have fun!Quality game!
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Most games scratch a particular itch, maybe two, and I would never complain about that. DotA2 is my go-to for high-intensity team action. Portal is a quintessential puzzle experience. Animal Crossing makes me feel safe and happy in my little island with an enticing casual game loop. Dave the Diver, however, has the balls to cram 4 or 5 game types into a relatively small space while making it feel truly expansive. I got the game on a lark and couldn't put it down for several days. My family was not prepared for what this game did to me.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: i love this game <3the Artwort, the Characters, the Gameplayall those little minigamesit all fits in perfectlyjust like Banchos cooking!i dont write a lot of reviews, because it takes a lot to impress me..but this... this is Art!i can only recommend anyone to play this game!thank you Devs, you did a very great Job!
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I beat the game and really enjoyed the fishing and sushi bar mechanic/gameplay but my god the mini games are so awful. Everytime you unlock a new section of the map or plan to go on a big fishing expedition you are blue balled every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ time by some new annoying character that forces you to do a quest or a mini game all the way until you've beaten the game. I felt so vindicated when first introduced to the "optional" boss fights I intentionally ignored them initially to cuck fake ash ketchum. I would've recommended this game full price but the trail the cat mini game made me kill 6 cats in the process.Buy on deep discount $5
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly.... Unexpectedly AMAZINGI read the reviews, saw the numbers, but purely ignored them. I doubted them, surely a game like this can't be THAT good. I hate those restaurant management styles of games, the rush, serving customers, making a menu to please people. Its just not fun.And then diving into water to find food and ♥♥♥♥? Again, sounded boring and a waste of time, but it had good reviews somehow?Gave it a shot, and man my mouth was salivating at every single sushi, the craft, the complex designs, the beers and green tea, the fishes, MURDERING the sea. The game grabbed two things i hated and made a perfect game, The restaurant turned into being a fun little mini game and a mental break from the core component of fishing and diving. The diving provided endless fishies, but also a mysterious story that intrigues you more and makes you want to keep diving further and further. Genuinely, give this game a try, even if you hate the genres. Trust me, you'll love it
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Dave the Diver is a perfect game.At first all you see if a fishing game but with limitless exploration, main quests and side quests, farming, photography, boss fights and more it is hard to get bored of this game.The art style of this game along with its soundtrack make it extremely fun to play through and continue playing once the main story is complete. The game never feels boring or repetitive as it allows players to completely customise the way you play and the things you do in each day of Dave the Diver's life.I love 100% completing games and sometimes the achievement gathering can feel necessarily long and time consuming but not with this game, the achievement hunting adds another level and challenge and fun to an already fun game.I would recommend Dave the Diver to those who want a feel-good easy to play game which mixes all good things from other games currently on the market.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - game has TOO much and it becomes tedious/a chore to manage everything.This game is beautiful, quirky, and varied. I was super excited for the game since it combined two things I really love: management and exploring... But this is one of the very few games where . I loved the cycle of just wake up, fish, serve sushi. But the game constantly adds new mechanics/things where it ends up just feeling like a long laundry list of to-do's. My biggest gripe is that the new mechanics/things didn't really  the game but felt tedious since they lacked a bigger purpose to the game.Wanted to love the game, but all the pointless management drained a lot of the fun from playing. Finished the game but it felt like a chore.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I'm usually the kind of person who only watches other people play the games they love, but I just had to play Dave after watching one of my favorite youtubers play. This game is perfect, and has something everyone loves about video games. I genuinely think it would be impossible not to have at least a little fun playing this game!! It's silly, it's challenging, it's got fishing (AND gambling),  and an awesome story line with a fun cast of characters.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game, base content is already so enjoyable, and it just keeps getting bigger. Relaxing and chill, but also with a lot of depth and some intense moments as well. The game has a great sense of humor, and amazing art and music. There has never been a game in which I have smiled more often while playing through it.Main story took me ~34 hours, and there is still a lot that I haven't done. This is a rare, charming game that deserves all the attention it has gotten so far, and so much more.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I was wary at first since some management games can be tedious, however, this game is so fun. The pacing of introducing new features and areas in the game is perfect, not overwhelming and not drawn out. The story is cute and funny, and the characters are unique. The game play is fun and I never felt frustrated by the controls or annoyed, it felt like anytime I started to wish there was a certain mechanic, they would introduce it. I fell in love with this game and hope other game developers take notes.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was expecting a calm, almost ordinary pixelated RPG game but nothing could prepare me for what I was about to experience. This game literally has everything that I enjoy, its got fun visuals, designs, and lovable characters. Lets not forget that the two DLCs it has are absolutely free and packed with even more adventure. I highly recommend this game to anyone who wants to immerse themselves into a unique world with many wonderful moments. I simply cannot stop playing it, also, an extra 100 points for adding a Ghostbusters PKE meter Easter egg!
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: The game continually adds on new activities or and mini games but they just are not that fun. Most of the boss fights boil down to just trying to dodge their attacks and shoot but that is frustrating when Dave apparently can only look up or down so far. I can only assume this is because he has the same neck mobility as an end of career Peyton Manning.I did not find myself enjoying any of the story or "humor" that the game has. This came out around the same time as Dredge which although are not directly similar, they have some basic management of fishing that I find to be an overall better experience in Dredge. Towards the end of the game I found myself just trying to critical path to the end so that it would be over.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I didn’t have this game for a week yet and I have almost 10 hours into the game. I like how different the game is from other crafting games. The mini games and the story is just so 🥰🥰. The art is also very pretty and I love the sushi restaurant aspect of it as well. This is one of those games that I would want my daughter to play when she gets older
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: the sushi chef is ,the protagonist is a fat guy that can swim and achieve a lot,has a weeb character to normalize mediocrity,one of the waiters is a mexican luchador,10/10anyway, no spoilers,lets start with the bad,when you right click your harpoon while a previous animation is going, it doesn't register for the game and you end up panicking and clicking that mouse button like a maniac because the shark is eating your face.the shark/big fish body counts as a damage dealer/feels like it? so you die after dodging sometimes because there's a wall behind you.and that's pretty much all the bad.i'm about 60~70% done with the game but decided to write a review before i forget all the fun i had while playing,i knew the game was good, but honestly never expected all of this from it, the stories, the cat, the short HD pixel animations,every time i think i've seen it all, something new happens, a new event, a new npc, a new story, a new side activity, a new stupid dumb shark that makes me wanna quit after 8 hours of playing, an annoying fish with a mohawk and a bad attitude that chose violent in a small cave.i went in only knowing one thing, it's a management game with fishing and extremely good reviews, never understood how or why someone would spend 20~60 hours playing this till i tried it myself, and i'd recommend you do the same, don't look up gameplay or anything, just buy it and have fun exploring on your own.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: DO  you really think the mini-games you designed are very interesting?NO,the answer is NO.They're rubbish,cumbersome,disgusting.Even if all the content of these mini-games is deleted,the rare interesting parts of this game are not missing at all,just like if you have impotence ,your wife will not care,because she didn't feel it anyway.  Boring main line,boring weapon,boring process,and silly game details.If the experience of the first three days is 10,all the later is -10.  I JUST WANT CATCH FISH, SELL FISH, BREED FISH.  Don't do so much rubbish if you are rubbish.  I play games to relax,never to be disgusted by gold-leafed poop.Is it because of cults？If the life of  a  sacrifices is normal,maybe gold-leafed poop is indeed acceptable,but it is recommended not to give others.You can eat and enjoy it yourself.Thank you,
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: ... my love for Helm knows no bounds.  Or depths, in this case.Now if only she could appear in this game as a playable diver, the circle will be complete.If you've been enjoying the Dave crossover in Nikke so far, consider this game the main course than the healthy appetizer it is over there.  Again, if Dave's devs could bring us DLC that introduced the Aegis Squad proper here, instead of teasing us with a humble boat skin, something tells me said DLC would fly off the shelf faster than Bancho could cook it!
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game that seems very simple at the beginning and grows and grows. I'm not even halfway done with it and while I assume this rating could change, I highly doubt it. I'm loving everything and nothing is a chore. I love Dave as a protagonist. The jokes are really good and the cutscenes are the best. And the boss fight with the Wolf Eel was genuinely scary! Gave me nightmare flashbacks to that eel in Mario '64.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. Has a lot of love in it evidently. Easy to pop in and out of the game if you're busy. The story is nice, the characters are charming. Collecting all the fish can be a little tough since you can't check your in-game phone while underwater, but otherwise it's pretty seamless. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game is magnificent. Artwork, Characters, Music, Fun little mini-game aspects for various tools, weapons, etc. It's just flat out fun, and the vibe is fantastic, and obviously doesn't take itself too seriously. So far, it hasn't felt tedious or frustrating in any way. Even my 'failures' in the game seem like sufficient learning tools, and only minor setbacks that help me to avoid or do better the next go around. How the devs/designers pulled that off, I would love to know. Play this game. You won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Peak micromanagement with a lot of amusing memey diversions on the side... They were fun as a change in pace, but it could have definitely used a lot less backseating, using a mechanic for only a few minutes meant the unique sections ended up being 80% tutorial.The optimizer in me ended up making each dive take half an hour because there are just so. many. FISH.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: really nice game with multiple gameplays and minigames. It is possible to have quite short sessions as you can stop after each dive (so it's nice if you have limited amount of time). Game is quite forgiving (you don't really die) but can be challenging if you head on quite quickly with the main quest.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutley incredible and unique, its good to see games still have a soul, it might be a basic game with basic features but everything feels incredibly paced nothing stays too little or too short, it is a phenomenal game, I highly recommend to anyone looking for a  fun relaxed and funny experienced, can't remember the last time I laughed out loud at a game.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games to play when you're taking breaks, especially during heavy exam study periods or assignments. I just go diving and catch fish while waiting for my teammates to finish this assignment parts, or run my sushi store while I'm on a study break. It's just nice to take a break from the FPS genre and from LIFE!.Highly RECOMMENDED!
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Im a little over 10 hours of game time and the sheer variety of well made content is astounding. The game excels in nearly everything it does. It almost feels overwhelming the amount of content that is available to player at just a dozen hours in. And i don't think the game is out of tricks yet. My only complaint thus far is the default keyboard controls for player movement are a little finicky in situations that demand both precision and speed but it isn't frustrating enough to be mad about it.For 20 dollars usd and currently on sale for 18, picking this up is a no brainer.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. Been surfing around steam for ages feeling uninspired but this one popped up and it delivers on so many levels, first and foremost, the gameplay and content. The only slight downside is the fast clicking and button mashing required for some fish as my old bones can't take that much abuse these days, but besides that this game is perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like guys named Dave? Do you like diving? This game has both and more.I've watched a playthrough before purchasing, so I definitely didn't go in blind. That being said, this game, while having a story, is mostly about that gameplay, and the studio nailed this. It's fun to dive, it's fun to fight the fish, and its fun to manage your sushi restaurant. If you've seen any gameplay and thought "wow, that looks fun", you'll probably enjoy this. The main gameplay loops are also encountered within the refund time, so you'll have time to figure out whether or not you like the game before you commit your money.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: How is this overwhelmingly positive?Tedious gameplay loop, matched with paternalistic handholding, while still being unclear about limitations of characters and consequences for your actions.There is a charm to this game, but it's not all that good. I did notice that the majority of positive reviews are under 30 hours. Maybe I'll give the game another try, but I don't see this game standing alongside many of the other games that have the same rating.Feedback by others is welcome on my impression. Comments open.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: ⚙️ Gameplay: (10/10)DTD is well balanced with an incredible amount of content, all of which feels fresh and unique, and is introduced periodically throughout the game so it never feels overwhelming. And as long as you're the type of player that likes to explore then the grind is pretty much non-existent (maybe a few hours towards the end if you're hunting for all trophies).🎨 Graphics: (9/10)Glorious pixel art crafted from vibrant colour palette. Loses 1 mark for a v-sync issue (which I found easily ignorable).🔊 Sound: (10/10)Very cosy, especially under water. Maybe repetitive in places, but never annoying. Hot Pepper Tuna slaps 🔥🚀 Innovation: (9/10)Clearly takes inspiration from many other games out there, but the way it's been put together in this single package makes stand out in it's own right🌐 Multiplayer: (10/10)Literally non-existent. Perfect.📖 Storyline: (8/10)The characters are interesting and well written, but I wasn't always engaged with it. I found myself skipping some of the dialog, more so towards the mid/end game.🌍 World Design: (8/10)Traversing the world is more enjoyable that I thought it might have been thanks to how well the game is balanced and various QOL unlockables as the game progresses. There's a few places where you might get lost and be doubling back and yourself, but those are far and few between.🕹️ Controls: (9/10)Plays great on KBM and controller. I can see why they're releasing a patch for the button mashing mechanic, but personally, I didn't mind it.🔁 Replayability: (10/10)
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely game , love it to the core :) After 40 hours , I feel raped by content in this game , everytime when I was like : Damn, thats a lot of stuff game was like , nah , here , have some new mechanic , guns , areas .. but this kind of stuff repeat it self every few hours :D here have some fish farm and you know what grow your own vegetables.... Cool ... Bored ? Here heve new area , new guns and you know what ? here have another restaurant too ♥♥♥♥♥. :D Lots and lots of fun , no bugs very smooth experience. This year 10/10 :) Try it !!!!
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: The importance of a roguelite having an engaging campaign. Would be fairly bland if it was just the diving but every in-game day is met with fresh plotlines and mechanics. Then there’s the restaurant management expanding on staff, ingredients and recipes. Unique visual style, especially in the cinematics. Some endgame content although gold soon becomes pointless.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: It would be silly of me to give this a thumbs down after I played it for 20 hours and mostly enjoyed my time, but the game isn't as good as the reviews would suggest. There are a variety of systems in the game that are gradually revealed. The novelty factor this brings is what keeps you playing. But these systems aren't all that interesting, and many I didn't want to engage with at all since they were just tedious. I can't help thinking that the game would be better if more work went into the core gameplay of diving and exploring since actually the world is quite small and by the end you've seen everything many times over.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game! I really enjoyed playing it, either the gameplay itself, or the music, the art style and more.The character buildings (animation+personality exaggeration) are crazy, kinda reminds me a bit of the Ace Attorney series, which brought me a lot of fun.Overall I love this game, and if have to pick one point that can be improved on, I'll go with the under water palace scene, bc I really don't like swimming across the lateral ocean again and again just to help the villagers fix their problems sry :P
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I play a lot of pixel art games. I can say without a doubt, the art found in this game is some of the best pixel art I've ever seen. The mini cutscenes just ooze personality. The gameplay itself is addicting and feels incredibly varied thanks to the split between fishing and running the sushi bar.While calling this an indie might be a bit of a stretch due to the backing and budget it received, I still think all the praise it's been given is deserved.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: This has quickly become my favorite game, and it's still in early access?! The right amount of chill, the right amount of thrill, and just the right amount of time split between diving and sushi-ing to keep my ADD brain interested and satisfied. The sushi restaurant down the road appreciates this game as well, since it has me craving and ordering from them more than ever. Delish!
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: 40 hours, just finished the story of the game, but well worth the money.It's like Stardew Valley and Yakuza 0 had a kid and Dave the Diver is the result.  You have the main game (diving, managing a restaurant), but there are several different activities in the game that keeps it from getting stale.  Add a perfect soundtrack, humorous cut scenes, and a few challenging fights and you get a game that makes you want to 100% it.  Even after finishing the main story the game goes on afterwards, so you can relax and do what you want and skip everything else without feeling rushed.  If there is a gem in the rough of games of 2023, this is it.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Really got into this! Mixes pixel graphics / 3D ocean exploration / fish and item collecting / crafting / then at the end of the day you manage a restaurant which includes a whole other layer... / menu prep / decorating / staff hiring / then diner dashin through the actual meal time. It hooked me good and I hit the early access story cap and I want more...
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderfully made game.The exploration/fishing is great, the managing of the Sushi bar is unique and great fun and the story makes for a great silly time. Even the harvesting mechanics (which have become common in modern games and I'm not a fan of) are kept light enough, and automated enough, that it doesn't detract from the entire package.I re-installed to play the 2 free DLCs expecting to be done in an hour, but to my delight I spent 4 hours and still didn't finish everything - they're amazingly done with new fish, weapons, mechanics and great cut-scenes.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I somehow realized i got something for these diving/water games like Dredge and Dave the diver, they give off the same energy as most cozy games do, but with a little bit of action attached to them. The main aspect of the game which is catching fish and making them into sushi is, obviously, a repetitive task, although it get's switched up by catching/seeing new fish. Now in the 25 hours i've played this game to the end the repetition got the better of me once, that was when i needed to farm gold to progress. If you correctly "abuse" the event's that come up in the game though you wouldn't need to do that.The graphics in this game are what gives it this nice and cozy feeling while still maintaining a very pleasent atmosphere all together, unless you despise pixel graphics which some people do.The combat needs a bit of getting used to, little fatty dave doesn't have the best mobility underwater and some stuff straight up feels undodgeable, or at least i felt that way, probably just a skill issue after all.A lot of things you do in this game have special animations that get played when you do them, and these add so much flavor to this game it's insane, from comical stuff to boss animations, there is a bit of everything. They're also, at least i think so, very well made.In general the game isn't hard, when you encounter puzzles i think even a 6 year old would be able to solve them just by fooling around. The quests are pretty linear and well explained, there really isn't too much of a chance of not getting what they want to do.The story is fun and pretty easy to understand, it was a very nice game to play for the amount it costs.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: I am not sure why this is the best game ever, but it really is. The depth (ha.), animations, plethora of minigames, mixture of doable and near-impossible goals...its just very fun. There are certainly monotonous aspects, like having to go certain places daily, but the payoff is pretty immediate too. Anyway, check it out. v fun.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to 'DAVE THE DIVER', a marine adventure set in the mysterious Blue Hole. Explore the sea with Dave by day, and run a sushi restaurant at night. Uncover the secrets of the Blue Hole, and unwrap this deep sea mystery involving 3 friends, each with distinct personalities. New adventures await.
_childDocuments_.name: DAVE THE DIVER

name: The Knight Witch
detailed_description: Shoot 'Em Up Spellcasting Sorcery! Encounter evil foes and choose whether you wield your magic or use your weapons and wits to take them down. With their flight capabilities, superior fighting strength and reality-bending magic, The Knight Witches absolutely control the battlefield! Body and Mind: The Knight Witch Duality Shooting or Spell Cards? Why not both? Customize your own unique playstyle, upgrading your Knight abilities for a more fast-paced shmup experience, or strengthen your Witch magic and explore tons of different deckbuilding strategies with over 30 unique spell cards to choose from. Build Trust & Make Lasting Bonds As you journey across Dungeonidas, your heroic deeds and efforts will be seen and discussed by the citizenry. Knight Witches become stronger with gratitude and trust and they can earn it in many different ways, however, not all methods are sincere. Will you do anything to gain popularity, or will you try and stay honest? The choice is in your hands. Forward-Thinking Accessibility The Knight Witch has been lovingly designed as a Metroidvania without barriers; with an intuitive on/off 'auto-aim' system, world-altering 'cheats' and a focused main story navigation system - you will never get lost and you can tailor the game to your level of play. Super Mega Team The Knight Witch is brought to you by a veteran team of developers, with working experience on titles such as RiME, Moonlighter, and Plants VS Zombies.

Cast devastating card-based spells, forge close bonds, and make moral choices all in your quest to save your home and discover who's behind the War Golem invasion.

_childDocuments_.review: This games tries to do way too many things and ends up doing none of them very well. The"Metroidvania" element is incredible basic. Areas are very linear with an occasional hidden side area. The map only shows locked/blocked doors, and there are no custom markers of any kind, so don't forget where that villager was when you get the power you need. You character also moves at a snails pace, so backtracking with no markers is incredibly tedious.The "shmup" aspect does not feel very good. Your character moves and shoots very slowly, and the damage of your normal attack falls off very quickly. By the second  "dungeon", I was shooting enemies 15+ times before they die. Combat often takes place in small cramped hallways or rooms with annoying gimmicks to make ambushes harder than they need to be. Visual Clarity is a huge issue in this game with your character and enemies often disappearing behind something in the foreground, or enemies will start shooting before they even appear on screen, so hope you have good reaction time.Since your basic attack does no damage, you have to use cards to actually kill things. Whoever thought RNG deck building was a good addition to a bullet hell game was very mistaken. Trying to dodge a screen filled with projectiles while also trying to manage a random assortment of cards is dumb.  The underwater submarine levels are an absolute trash fire. Why did I have to wait 90+ minutes to unlock the dash just to have it taken away by this awful trash can???TLDR:Visuals: 8/10Visual Clarity: 4/10Music: 6/10Level Design: 2/10 Movement Speed: -2/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I've ever gone from liking a game so much to hating it so much in 3 hours.The developers have managed to make basically every mistake in the design book.I thought this was a fantastic combination of genres - there's so much potential and ideas to take from each type of game and all you need to do is make a tight package. Well, at least this game will hopefully inspire someone to do this meshup properly.- The enemies are bullet sponges, even when you get a tiny bit stronger, the new enemies have more health..- Weapon powerups are - get this - 8 seconds long. Yep. SO MUCH FUN!! They are also rare and you normally have a crappy peashooter that does no damage.- The cards mechanic is absurd. Isn't it fun to get powerups in random order so you need to look away during the heat of combat to know what the hell you got and decide what's useful while dodging 20 bullets with either no dash, or the shortest dash known to man.- I have no idea how the developers thought it was a good idea to start you off without a dash in a game like this. It feels so bad and there are times when you literally cannot evade damage.- The map is bad and boring.- The enemies are repetitive and lame.- The stores are useless! Buy armor (1 extra temp health) with infinite currency because it's so unnecessary.- The "upgrades" come way too slowly and are the usual boring type - 10% more damage every hour, wow.So sad this idea and beautiful art and atmosphere got wasted on some of the worst design choices I've seen in games. There's no excuse in 2023.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: I almost didn't buy this game after reading some of the other reviews, but after 100%ing it, my conclusion is that many of those complaining didn't really read the label. It's a bullet hell metroidvania, a.k.a. shmuptroidvania, and if you don't like shmups, that part isn't going to be as satisfying as the platforming you might be more used to. I'm not a big shmup player, but still enjoyed it a lot. Certainly has some rough edges here and there, but makes it pretty high on my overall rankings. Great art, a wonderful story that's actually much better-developed than the myriad souls-like-with-environmental-storytelling games out there, performant on my relatively low-end machine, and engaging enough to sink 20 hours into. I did end up looking up a video for how to unlock the puppy, and late-game cleanup is a bit tedious in terms of movement, but the core mechanics are solid, and while the deckbuilding aspect isn't super strong, it's there enough that you can have very different playstyles and still make good decks, and there are combo mechanics to be had.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: The first part of this review is going to be about the game, the second part is going to b**** about the quality of reviews, both steam and otherwise. You've been warned. Yes, I am using this review as my soapbox. Deal with it. First part: This game is great. In fact, it's fantastic. If you like Metroidvanias you will like this game. Frankly, I think it deserves to be mentioned with the same kind hallowed tone as Ori and Hollow Knight. I am not even really a fan of bullet hell games, but this one isn't unfair and that's my usually gripe about bullet hells. I found many of the bosses and ambushes to be quite challenging, but also extremely satisfying. The artwork and music are wonderful.  If you are a connoisseur of game music, go add "Mirror Lake" to your Spotify playlist. The story also has its ups and downs, and while I am usually the first to predict how a story will go by the time the introduction is finished, this one had me guessing. Several characters go through story arcs that have important themes like the burden of celebrity and what it means to have a hero complex. There is even a sort of morality mechanic that will determine how quickly you can level up your skills and demonstrates the dangers of propaganda. Metroidvanias live or die by their exploration and skill mechanics and I think this game really shines in that arena. Because your character flies, and thereby can inherently access a lot of the screen real estate to begin with, there aren't as many skills to acquire throughout the game, but personally I think this prevents a lot of unnecessary backtracking. To keep it spicy there is a spell system, which adds just a little bit of deckbuilding. The spells in your deck are randomly selected and applied to three slots so certain bosses may require a little bit of frequency analysis-type thinking. I really love this aspect. I love that there is a little bit of chaos to contend with as you run out of mana whilst hoping the spell you need pops up soon. When your heavy hitting spell pops up and you have the mana to use it and you slam that boss with the final hit, it's very satisfying. This is a solidly executed game. Buy it. Second part: I generally like what Team 17 publishes. I love Metroidvanias. I followed and wishlisted this game before it was released. Why did it take me two years to finally follow through and buy it? The word "Mixed". Mixed reviews. It seems like small Indie studios have the worst luck when it comes to game reviews because everyone is so eager to be edgy about their opinion. But if you actually go through and read some of the "mixed" reviews, you'll find most of them actually say the game is excellent but they had gripes about either tiny polishing details or that certain spells didn't feel like they had enough oomph. But otherwise they are saying the game is great. A lot of these reviews even incorporate their own rating system, like "4/5" in their reviews but then select "not recommended". It's insanity. Yes, Steam binary yes/no review system is awful. In my opinion, the only reason you should say a game is not recommended is for bugs, bad development, or unforgiveably bad gameplay. If it's a well executed game but you just, personally didn't like the story, for the love of God just click the thumbs up and explain. I find this problem extends to critic reviews as well. The Metacritic score is unbearable low. One critic said it has "too many mechanics" and the only thing I can conclude from that is that this person is a moron. Some reviews said the game is "excellent" and then gave it a score of 70. Clearly these people got C-'s in high school and felt contritely that their work was actually excellent. So dear reader, don't be like me, Buy the games you are excited about and refund it under two hours if you see it going downhill right away. Don't be like me and miss out on a great game for two years because people are idiots.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: A bullet hell, Metroidvania, card battler, where the result is a disservice to each genre.As a bullet hell, there is not enough contrast on the screen between the background and foreground objects. This is coupled with the fact that the player attacks overlay on top of or in conjunction with explosions when enemies are defeated. The dash is frustratingly limited. For the first 2/3rds of the game, you can get away with using cover and dashing (once acquired) to avoid attacks. However, in the last 1/3rd, there is almost no cover afforded to the player, which is frustrating as by that point there are several enemies which have attacks that can follow the player and cannot be evaded short of using defensive cards (see below for further discussion on that). I'm sure that's intentional, but with limited evasive options, and a difficulty spike on the final boss that is downright sadistic (, I can say that there are other bullet hell/shmups which are challenging yet fairer to the player. One additional note: screw the submarine section(s), which come at about 1/3 of the way into the game. The game is just starting to get into its groove and you have good command of the controls, evasion, etc. Now we're going to limit you to only firing laterally, while everything else in the game remains capable of 360 degree movement. It becomes a slog and rather than an interesting change of pace, it turns into a nightmare.As a Metroidvania - my favorite game genre - it barely checks the marks, and even if you did want to go back and explore, by the endgame you either a.) will have no need to or b.) won't care enough to because you want the game to be over. Exploration never feels organic. Comparing this to , , or , the levels are very simple but the traversal is slow, with no fast travel option. When you realize it will be a crawl to get to one of the other zones to go back and get a collectible or other item you now have access to, it isn't worth the investment considering the item won't yield any meaningful improvement to the player. Yes, it could be another card, or another upgrade to your mana link, but by the halfway point of the game, you have most of the spells you will need (or want) and will have figured out which are trash (at least half).As a card battler, the RNG itself isn't so bad. However, the issue lies with where the cards are located on the screen since this is also a bullet hell: random cards in the bottom right corner are very hard to identify in the heat of dodging thousands of projectiles. Not really sure how this could be improved; admittedly, i don't really play deck building games. Others might be able to speak to this more than I. In terms of the card powers, there is one card which is the absolute cheese (you'll need it to beat the final boss, though). I found some of the best cards were actually the ones acquired fairly early on. There are many defensive cards that feel useless, or comparatively so when looking at the offensive options. For awhile I tried to use the defensive cards to make up for the increasingly sparse cover as the game progressed. In the end, it seemed like a better strategy to just load up on nearly all offensive cards and wipe out as many enemies on the screen rather than trying to successfully dodge and evade from enemy projectiles. I'd say that isn't intentional, but might require balancing since there are a number of defensive cards that - in theory - sound like they would be very helpful.Some other general criticisms:

_childDocuments_.review: So, the good: The art is charmingly rich, warm, varied, and has an identity identity to itself - I'm not fluent in the language of visual art by any means, but for sure I never got tired of looking at this game in the way I did, say, Skyrim.Meanwhile the writing holds together, it knows what it wants to say and, while it's a bit kiddy/cozy about it all it's also not toothless by any means. The basic concept is that magitech society got The Industrialisations bad enough to threaten ecological collapse, and a fringe group, the Children of Gaia, escalated to the point of open war to save the planet. Their trump card against armies of magitech automatons were the Knight Witches, champions superpowered quite literally by the power of friendship - one of the core conceits of the setting is 'Link', a kind of mystic chain where putting your trust in a Knight Witch makes them mystically stronger. At the final battle, they triumphed over the regime, but not before the power unleashed literally broke the sky, forcing everybody to flee underground into the ruins of an older civilisation.It's actually not hardcore About Climate Change, although it's definitely not shy about where it stands on the issue, which I respect. If anything it's more about celebrity culture and personal integrity, playing with the pitfalls of being empowered by other people's trust, how much you'll listen to your PR manager in a crisis. It's not spectacularly profound or anything, but it's decent fare. Competent, hits the beats it wants to, knows how it wants to go out.The bad...Okay so, mechanically it's a fusion of metroidvania exploration, bullet hell combat, and deck builder advancement/customisation; flying around the levels, weaving between projectiles, exploring for goodies and using your custom deck of spell cards as special moves, paid for with a mana pool recharged by drops from enemies.The problem is that these elements don't cohere with each other and, in fact, get in each other's way;Because the combat draws from bullet hell traditions, the exploration is necessarily limited; there's not much room for mobility upgrades, and less for puzzles, when your basic mode of movement is unrestricted, inertialess flight.Because the levels are designed as areas to traverse and explore, your avatar has a bulkier model than the usual pixel core of a true Danmaku game, and enemies bob around only semi-predictably, so combat feels sloppy.And because combat is real-time and expected to absorb your attention, the spell card system has to be punchy enough to matter while unobtrusive enough not to distract you from trying to avoid the latest shotgun blast of death orbs, a balancing act that sees it looking distinctly wobbly.The compromise the devs hit on is that, rather than accessing all of your picked deck at once, you have three hotkey slots to choose from, each of which cycles through your chosen cards more or less at random; cast one, another slots in.It... I mean it works, insofar as it's quick and simple enough to make spell cards practical to use in combat (mostly), but it's ruinous to a player's ability to actually make something of the spell card system. Without control over what cards you have available, you can't really build synergies until very late in the game, and you're left picking cards based on their general-purpose profile, although bosses can warrant specific tailoring.You do, eventually, get enough breadth of options to have things like some cards you can cycle through freely to increase the frequency of using specifics cards, but it takes a prohibitively long time, and a lot of the time the best option is weapon cards, long-duration powerups that change your basic attack into something beefier, precisely because they're a low-fuss option that doesn't leave you in a tight spot fishing for a one-and-done spell that's suited to your problem.On top of that, this is a game where enemies respawn when you save, that expects you to backtrack for pickups when you get the new door-key upgrades, and has rudimentary fast travel at best. There's no warping between save points, and of the game's 9 levels, you can only even fast travel between 5 of them. Hell, you don't get a dash until the close of area 3.When it starts out it's all new and shiny, the combat is brisk and without reason to backtrack the mobility problems haven't reared their head yet. Between about the 30%-90% marks the problems make themselves known and it gets more of a slog, with some pronounced low points like an underwater section that has you in a minisub with fixed shooting angles, forcing you to rely more on spell attacks and the problems therein. Then the last 10% feeds you a couple of overpowered capstone tools and lets you trample over what came before, which is admittedly cathartic.Overall, while I think the mechanical combo of metroidvania/danmaku/deckbuilder has potential, it'll need another pass before someone can make it sing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: A visual feast that is fun overall but has issues.Difficulty-wise, the game starts easy, becomes annoyingly hard, then gets easy again near the end. The beginning of the game is balanced well-enough around the player not having many abilities. The middle of the game has enemies that take too long to kill with the basic shot, but you still probably won't have good-enough spells to compensate. Plus the game starts introducing downright annoying gimmicks like the infamous submarine (look at any other review) and sniper towers that damage you if you stand around for too long. Near the end, you finally start collecting powerful spells, some perhaps even TOO powerful. You're gonna need these spells, though, because the true final boss is VERY hard, so hard that you're given the option of skipping it entirely (but you get a bad ending). Overall, the game was frustrating at points, but it didn't ruin the game for me. Difficulty is, of course, extremely subjective, so you may or may not have an easier or harder time than me depending on your skill level.What is less subjective, however, is to odd inclusion of a "deckbuilding" system in a fast-paced bullet-hell. These two genres just fundamentally do not work well together. The game demands that you pay attention to three things at once: the ocean of bullets you need to avoid, the enemies you need to aim at, and the cards that you have available at any given time. There is no clear indication near the player character telling you what spells you have or how much mana you have to cast them: everything is grouped together in the bottom-right corner of the screen, far away from the action. It is LITERALLY impossible to pay attention to both things at once. You end up mostly focusing on the action so you don't take damage, but eventually you need to look down to check what you have, which distracts you from the bullet that's about to hit you. It doesn't help that the buttons you need to press for each spell constantly change as you cycle through your spells, so you can't even be sure what your buttons do without looking at the bottom-right of the screen. The deckbuilding really does not add much to the experience (it feels like a phoned-in attempt at chasing trends), and the way its executed causes more problems than it solves. Even with the questionable difficulty and level gimmicks, this is my biggest complain with the game because it is a fundamental design flaw that would take more than a balance patch to fix.Other problems exist as well, such as the slow movement speed and lack of fast-travel points that make backtracking a chore. The story is awkward: there isn't enough time spent building the world up, resulting in a lot of the game's setting and history feeling incomplete. There are frequent opportunities for the player to make "moral decisions" that suggest making the good choice will hamper your progress, but then you can just throw money at a machine to make up for it, making the decisions feel meaningless. Despite all of this, the game is still fun and gorgeous to look at (the music is pretty great, too) so I still recommend it. Just be aware that not every part of this game is as enjoyable as it probably should be.

_childDocuments_.review: Could have been a really good game, but it just has too many half-baked ideas.Good-Art is beautiful-Music is amazing - so many bangers-Story is mostly good-Controls are solidBad-Visually confusing. Too many bullets with too many different colors get lost in the vibrant artwork. Explosions cover bullets. Green shards that are good fly at you, some bullets are also green and fly at you.-Card system just doesn't work for me. Defensive options are no good because of the random nature of the cards. 1-cost cards are just filler to spam in order to cycle back to the good cards. So many cards are just not worth even using at all. Combos don't work because you can't guarantee you'll get the right cards and so few cards even have any combo potential anyway.-Upgrades are mostly useless and end up being glorified gate keys instead of weapons with any real utility.-Location of action is in the center of the screen, location of your most important abilities is in the bottom right. You have to look away from the action to see the randomly chosen cards.-Splash screen when starting the game is significantly louder than the in-game volume.-Traversal is very tedious-Several achievements did not unlock-Final boss is so bad there is an option to give up and get an alternate ending
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game where I wish I could give it a more neutral ranking. I actually quite enjoyed my time with it but I think many people may want to steer clear. I'll list some pros and cons and I think the reasoning will become clear.Pros:-Great art and a strong visual identity. This game looks great if you dig 2d.-An interesting plot that kept me hooked. And I was surprised how dark it got at times.-Huge degree of gameplay customization. You level up throughout the game and each time you can choose an upgrade along either the Knight or the Witch path with the former tending to buff you physically or power your basic attacks. The latter buffs your spell cards. Throughout the game you will collect a wide variety of these spell cards and these are made available 3 at a time drawn from your. You can customize your deck freely to suit your play style. There are upgrade items you collect which you can either give yourself more health or more MP (though these do cap and there's enough to max both). Lastly, there is an in-game cheat system which I always like to see, and you can use this to make your game harder or easier in various ways.-I do like that it gives you the option to skip the final boss with a full-on "Can't someone else do it?" choice for an alternate ending.Cons:-This game is HARD and very poorly balanced. This isn't always a con - I'm a huge dork for From Software's games - but this game is frequently just cheap. The very first boss you fight is ridiculously overtuned. By the time you get there you're playing basically un-upgraded (there's one HP/MP upgrade you can get and you better hope you picked HP) and don't even have the dash. I was hoping they'd balance this better after the demo but nope... it's exactly the same. I'd be willing to bet this fight alone made some people bounce off this game. I will openly admit that I made use of the cheats to get through some of the worst offenders in this game. Like the final boss, which is ridiculous.-This game desperately needed a fast travel system.So yeah, there it is. There's a lot to like, but it's hard to love.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: The game has promise, but everything bad about a bullet hell game can be found here.Cheap frustrating situations. Graphical effects that hide enemy bullets getting you hit. Off-screen projectiles that move at laser speed. The FOV is set specifically for each encounter and some of the fights are shrunk for maximum cheapness.Bad hit boxes.The spell card system could be a really fun and interesting system, but even that is plagued by bad design. Your spells are randomized out of a list of selected options. So you can pick multiple spells that are very situation and randomness decides if you get it or not. This is further compounded by bad design to have them displayed in the corner of the screen so good luck dodging attacks, aiming your weapon AND figuring out which random spell you have available to use. They also put the cost of the spell above it so you'll be easily tricked into pressing the number for that spells COST and not the spell slot it was placed it.Your resource management is poorly designed as well as the mana drops are inconsistent and spawn right next to the enemy to ensure you can't use it without getting hit or after you have won the battle. I feel a less random system would have fit the game much better.Still with all these flaws I'd still be interested in seeing where the series goes from here, but without improvements it will be a easy skip for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Visuals: The game is quite nice.It has a cute hand drawn style, and the aesthetics of a Knight that is a witch are in on point.But as a bullet hell, it is too visually busy.It can be very hard to keep track of everything, and sometimes you'll take damage and have no idea why.Combat:Combat is not great.You main weapon does basically no damage and has a pathetic rate of fire.You are supposed to make up for this using spell cards.But the cards you find are semi random, the cards you can actively use are random and whether you have the resources to use them when you need them is also random. Which means that in encounters where you NEED spell cards to progress (which is most of them late game) because your main weapon sucks, you only have two options:1) Smash your face against it repeatedly until all three layers of RNG line up and let you progress.2) Use cheats, which at this point, only feel like they are in the game because they knew the RNG sucks.It also doesn't help that Combat usually takes place in small cramped arenas, with at least one annoying gimmick preventing you from using the full range of your powers.Exploration:There... isn't any... well none tied to progression.... well...For some reason this is being billed as a metroidvania.And like... it just kind of... isn't.Well... it kind of is, but only in the lightest possible way.Each area has a very narrow linear path that you have to follow because the other paths are blocked by obstacles. Then you get to the end of the linear path and get a permanent upgrade (Sometimes, other times its a horrible submarine), then you use this upgrade to get past the obstacles and follow another linear path and finish the area... So... technically you do back track to open paths... KIND OF. Backtracking and exploration are reserved exclusively for secrets.Music:Really not something I pay attention to tbh.Nothing stands out as super annoying so it's probably good.Story:It's Fine.Pretty Generic, but I like the characters.Conclusion:It's not a very good game.3 or 4 out of 10 tops.If this is the developers first game, then I think it shows a lot of promise.It's not a bad idea to mash these concepts together, but I think maybe they didn't get enough outside feedback and got stuck in the weeds, design wise. I think 3 or 4 months of play testing and feedback from an outside perspective could have done this game a lot of good. As it stands the nicest thing I can say is that I am excited to see what the developers do next.Because if they improve upon what they have hear the next game could be fantastic.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:1. Respawn SystemThese beacons act as save points, respawn points, shops (when you unlock that feature), and healing spots. When you die, you respawn at the last beacon that you unlocked or rested at. This creates a challenge for the player to stay alive while mapping out the area, completing objectives, and looking for secrets. And when you die, you get to keep all the shards and other collectibles you had gotten prior to your death, so dying isn't too frustrating. The only progress you'll lose is just respawning at your last beacon and needing to travel again.2. Boss FightsWith the exception of the true final boss and the second fight against Robyn, I enjoyed the boss fights.First, the boss room is always near a beacon and a shop. So when you die, you will just respawn nearby. Then, you can quickly buy armor from the shop again and quickly go back to fighting the boss again.Second, most of the bosses have some fun gimmicks and challenge the player well.Hexkari Ancient Sentinel is a stationary boss that tests out your new dash ability. The Robyn fights were cool boss fights that mirror Rayne's attacksThe Kalypso and Graff tag team boss fight was a nice way of combining Kalypso's more traditional bullet attacks from regular enemies and Graff's attacks from his previous boss fightAnd the crazy boss fights against the castle's machine and the chains was neat. They don't do anything, so they spawn enemies to fight for them.3. The Cheat SystemI just find the Cheat System as a good way for new players or people who are bad at bullet hell to still play the game without dying too many times. It helps that you can toggle the cheats on or off after unlocking them.Cons: 1. The Second Robyn FightWhile most of the fight wasn't too bad, the real problem is one particular attack of Robyn. During Robyn's second phase, she can do some sort of fiery explosion attack that will hit the ENTIRE ROOM. As far as I can tell, it is impossible to dodge it. So you need to rely on a specific spell card that will protect you from the attack. If you don't have it in your hand by the time the attack arrives, you are guaranteed to lose a life. This is unfair because this game is a Bullet Hell battle, which definitely applies to Robyn's attack. This is especially bad because this attack will always come after Robyn's spiral bullet hell attack, which will most likely hit you unless you are very skilled at dodging.2. True Final Boss FightThe true final boss is IMPOSSIBLE to beat without using a Cheat. This boss has three phases.People would usually be exhausted by the third phase. And then the third phase had to unload so many enemies that can shoot out bullet patterns that are difficult to dodge.What the game should have done is just kept the boss fight in two phases, and the phases need to be more careful of how hard they are. This may be a bullet hell game, but it still needs to balance the difficulty even for a final boss.Recommendations(This is for the possibility that you will make a sequel for this game)1. Fast Travel SystemA common complaint I see for this game is the lack of fast travel for backtracting. While I don't find the backtracting too bad, I can definitely understand the feeling. Some areas like the Giga Tree aren't bad in backtracking because of the map's layout and the doors that you can unlock for quicker backtracking. But other levels like the Hall of Giants are a pain to backtrack because of how big the maps are and the lack of means to traverse faster.So, my suggestion is to have the beacons also act as a fast travel point. You can have the player fast travel between the the beacons that they have unlocked. You already had the beacon at as a means to fast travel back at the castle, so it makes sense to also have them fast travel you between other unlocked beacons.If the fast travel gets in the way for certain plot points, you can temporarily lock the fast travel system for certain areas until the player progresses the story further.2. Quests/Side StoriesExcluding the most important ones, I honestly don't remember much of the side characters that I rescued from their prison. A good way to fix that is to give quests or side stories to the side characters.These quests/side stories should be used to better understand and learn about the side characters and maybe even the main characters too. So, you need to be careful that the quests/side story is fleshed out story-wise, even if they are missable.3. StoryThe story isn't bad. But it did run into some bumps near the end.First starters, I think Gaia and the Hex civilization should have been more fleshed out. I didn't understand who Gaia or the Hex civilization are until near the end of the game.Tip 1: When you have important terms, events, or people, have the game give out information about them throughout the game. Don't give all the information at once, and don't give out that information near the end of the game.We should have had small events about them, one at a time, as we progress the story. Like in the Giga Tree level, we could have learnt from Lalashi about the Hex civilization bit by bit as we slowly explore the level.Second, we should have explored more about the creation of the Knight Witches. It's not a good idea to reveal the truth behind the Knight Witches' creation through hidden diary entries scattered throughout the game.Tip 2: Don't go putting important lore or plot points inside notes that are scattered or hidden around the game.It should have been used as part of the main story, being slowly revealed as you progress through the game. We could have learnt about them through the other Knight Witches, through Rayne overhearing the Venerable and En talking in secret, and through rumors from the civilians.Third, the Hooded Skull seemed like an out-of-place character. You hear about him from the Underbaker and bits about his backstory, but the Hooded Skull doesn't serve any main story purpose.His only purpose is to remove the skeletons and Underbaker from the game.Tip 3: If you are going to include someone that sounds important in the game, he should be more important than just screwing with the player. Have them be part of the main story or part of a great side story.If he is not going to be important in the main story, then give him importance in a side story at least. Maybe, after giving the Hooded Skull the card and making all the skeletons & Underbaker disappear, have Rayne track down the Hooded Skull (with some hints/directions on where to go) and have Rayne fight the Hooded Skull in an optional boss fight to save the skeletons and Underbaker.Fourth, Lalashi's betrayal and attempt of justification isn't well done.Tip 4: When you have a villain in the game, they should be explored and understood.You could have Rayne be partnered up with Lalashi throughout the game, with Lalashi acting as Rayne's guide through wireless communication. This will allow Rayne and Lalashi to interact more. This is allow the two to clash at times, as well as understand the both of them throughout the story.This will allow us to understand better on why Lalashi went through great lengths to cause so much trouble just for science and future advancement in technology.Fifth, the ending sequence could have been better.You could have had the end of the game allow Rayne to explore a bit of the new world she created and let her talk to all the people she saved and the people like Lalashi, the Venerable, and En.The joy for the ending is a bit damped because we didn't see the reaction of people after everything is over and we didn't see if Lalashi, the Venerable, and En ever reconsidered their previous beliefs on technology, politics, or the Knight Witches.Tip 5: Don't just abruptly end the game/story. Make sure to give some proper closure to it. No major loose ends left. And no cliffhanger endings.Final RemarksThe game is good, but it can be improved.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: It was a fun game overall, but there are definite issues with the gameplay and quality of life while playing1) Movement Speed: You move MAD slow. This wasn't an issue for me until you begin backtracking2) Fast Travel: There is no Fast Travel. Only World Portals. So when you couple the slow movement speed with the lack of fast travel, it ends up being a SLOG going from place to place. Every fountain should be a fast travel point. This was the case in Ori 2 and it was the case in Ender Lilies, (2 of the best Metroidvanias out there). It takes HOURS off your time just traversing the map heading for the spots that have secrets. Not this game. If you want to 100% the map (which I tend to do with Metroidvanias before fighting the final boss) you have spend all this time just moving through the map. At the endgame when you're trying to just 100% the map before taking on the final boss, you try to avoid enemies and just get to the location so you can find the secret. It's a PAIN to have to traverse the entire world to find the secret then traverse ALL THE WAY BACK to the world portal. I can't stress enough how much of a big deal it is for me to say "It's gonna be too much of a pain to 100% this game."3) Knight/Witch: It became apparent in the mid/end game that it is a mistake to ever go the path of the knight. By the end, it becomes far too much of a pain to use anything that isn't a spell or another weapon. While the damage has massive dropoff by the end, the bigger issue is that, unless you're using a piercing weapon (mostly Hand Cannon or Boomerang), killing the hordes of enemies will be unbearable. Hordes of bats and then there are enemies that spawn a school of fish to fly at you while spawning a ring of those fish around itself to protect it. Without a piercing weapon or spell like the axe, these are a NIGHTMARE to deal with. It's clear from this game that it WANTS you to choose the Witch path4) Difficulty: Yeah, the game is hard. Unforgivingly hard. I'm down for difficulty, but it was apparent that the game would become too annoying to play without cheats. There was only 1 cheat I used, and it was in the endgame: Enemies sometimes drop HP. The only cheat I used made the game infinitely more fun and manageable. I don't know why there isn't a way to heal outside of fountains and heart boxes. Add a spell that heals you a heart for like 5 mana or something, or a vampirism mechanic that heals you after you kill so many enemies or use so many spells. For bosses, maybe drop a heart or 2 at the halfway point or phase change or SOMETHING. Like, I know bullet hells are supposed to be difficult but this isn't supposed to be JUST a bullet hellVisuals: The game is visually stunning. That much I will give high praise forMusic: The OST for this game is also fantasticSo overall, it's a fun game. It really is. It's just that they definitely need to tweak the traversal aspects (AKA make every fountain a fast travel point), give the Knight path a MASSIVE buff, and add in some form of healing (or just use the Drop HP cheat). Outside of those things, I don't really have any complaints.I say it's worth the price for $20. It'll be fun, but you'll likely just want to beat it (100% or not) uninstall and then never touch again
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong, I had fun playing this game for the 10 hours or so it took to beat it.However, at the end of the day, it doesn't really capture the fun of Bullet hell games, or the fun of Metroidvanias.On the shmup side, most enemies just fire aimed sprays of bullets at you, which can become difficult to dodge due to the tight spaces and enemies swarming you. Since most bullets are blocked by the environment, it becomes a game of seeking cover from bullets, rather than dodging. Dodging is further discouraged by an unlockable mini-teleport and bullet clearing cards. If you still ever feel like actually dodging anything more complicated than the ever-present aimed bullets, you'll probably get punished for it, since the player hurtbox is big enough to throw you off. The detailed environments meant that foreground elements sometimes didn't stick out, and I sometimes ended up getting stuck on the complicated level geometry. The card system is a distraction from the dodging, since you have to look at the UI to figure out which cards are currently available.The card system itself is not great, with most abilities being situational or useless. Even worse, you are forced to fill your max deck size, and this is tied to mana upgrades, making these upgrades detrimental if you want a slim deck with only good cards.Despite all these shortcomings, the game is relatively easy. The player is not really punished for dying, which is probably good, since card RNG and mana management makes the difficulty somewhat volatile.The story is alright, but interrupts the gameplay too much, especially during the early game.The map doesn't have enough secrets for a worthwhile metroidvania, but it gets the job done. It'd be nice if the player character moved a bit faster: there is one movement speed, which is a bit slow for map traversal, and too fast for precision dodging.To summarize, it's not a terrible way to kill 10 hours, but the game has enough fundamental problems that it's hard to recommend it over any other way to kill time.If I had to compare it to another game, it'd be Aquaria.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Overall it's decent, but design choices hurt this title A LOT  4.5/10Many complaints talk about movement speed and the base weapon being weak the entire game. Both of these are true but not a reason for a thumbs down. The story is decent. The upgrades are well placed. Boss fights are a decent challenge. The problems start here. Combat is very hit and miss. You will be asking "What hit me?" quite often. A combination of poor bullet/background visuals and things shooting off screen get old fast. Add in that many fights happen in cramped areas. Spell cards is a good but rickety system. Sometimes you have what you need and it's cool other times you'll be wasting mana cycling to a card you need only to be out of mana to cast it. The card that let's you discard an draw shouldn't have a downside. Also, the player should be able to control the size of their deck and not have it be part of a mana upgrade.Ambushes, and the BS tied to them, are a down. The sword, with it's horribly short range, should do crazy damage in a shooter game.Submarine.......enough said.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable blend of the shoot-them-up and metroidvania genres.The game has a very solid gameplay core that offers a decent challenge, with really nice visuals. If you're a fan of both genres, I recommend playing the game and expect you'll get about a dozen hours of good fun.There are however a number of quality-of-life problems in the game that almost guarantee I will never go back to it.The story also felt like a patchwork, except a much less successful one. It wants to be feminist, it wants to be ecologist, it wants to be a deconstruction of the superhero genre and more, as if the devs had attempted to cram 10 years of binging TV shows into a little indie-game shell. That would have required far superior writing skills than were displayed here. Not that the narrative matters too much in such a game, but I could have done without the cringe.Overall, everything that isn't about dodging and shooting bullets felt slightly janky at best... but was also secondary when it comes to the gaming experience. Because at least, the dodging and the shooting was really fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever felt like it would be a great idea to mesh together metroidvania gameplay with fast-paced shoot 'em up combat? Well wonder no longer! The Knight Witch takes you on adventure to save your home and figuring out the cause behind the war golem invasion. As Rayne, a once rejected Knight Witch, you will fly through gorgeous hand-drawn environments and save as many people as possible, generating trust and forging bonds as you go. Utilizing spell cards and your magic bullets, you will overpower your enemies with combinations of unique skills and upgraded abilities in the hopes that you will discover who is behind this scheme.In my time with The Knight Witch, I have been enjoying it immensely. Not only is the pacing fantastic, but it feels fluid and enjoyable to play. It doesn't reinvent the wheel in terms of gameplay, but the execution is fantastic. I especially love the spell card system and its ability to change my playstyle right off the cuff. One of the types of cards you get will change how your basic attack works which can alter how I react to enemies pretty heavily. Overall, I am loving the game, but of course, we are here to talk about Steam Deck performance. The Knight Witch is not an intensive game and generally doesn't overuse resources, therefore, it runs like a charm on the Steam Deck! For the most part, the battery draw will stick under 10-11W with 3.5 - 4 hours of battery, but big areas and fights could go up to 14W. All in all, you will be getting around 3.5 hours of battery with silky smooth 60 FPS without changing a thing! Due to that, and full controller support, this is easily a Best on Deck title!There have been a couple times when trying to load into the game that it will just stick at an endless loading screen. This happened to be twice in a row with the third time working fine. I first thought this was due to having a TDP limit, so I turned it off, but it stuck the 2nd time too. The 3rd time, I quickly went into my save game and it worked, so it might be something that you need to quickly just go into your save. Luckily, I don't see a reason to linger on the main menu and since this didn't break the game after you are in, I would still recommend checking it out. This seems to only be in the main menu as loading once already in-game has no issues.The Knight Witch is a wonderful amalgamation of metroidvania exploring with shoot 'em up combat. Pair this with the beautiful art and enjoyable gameplay loop and you will find yourself having a great time with a great game. On the Steam Deck, the game performs perfectly without any changes needed to the settings or quick access menu. Even with the loading issue, I would still say this is a worthwhile investment!
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: The issue I find in The Knight Witch is the very combination of it's gameplay styles.Bullet-Hell and deck builder.In the Bullet Hell side you need to constantly scan the screen to see all the bullets you need to dodge.A deck builder is all about pruning and maintaining your deck so that you are more likely to get the cards you want.In The Knight Witch, your deck is your available spells. Every time you use a spell you get a new random spell card, each spell doing a different attack or gaining a boon.So there's the big problem, you have to look away from the bullet hell to see what spells you have... every time you get a new spell... which is many times during any encounter.While I applaud the idea of the push forward combat(you need to kill enemies in order to get Mana for your spells) the HUD is far too small and far away to be useful during a fight. This is also a Metroid-like, meaning you get new powers that will help you traverse the world.The problem is that one of the upgrades is a Submarine that: moves slower, only shoots in one direction, and removes your ability to dodge... while giving you absolutely no benefits.Which is where I'm stuck, I can't progress because of one encounter.There's a lot of charm and some decent fun to be had, but at's it's core The Knight Witch just doesn't come together.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of great things going for it; colorful, hand drawn art style with some fun, quirky characters and an elaborate story with some twists. The problem is that the developers could not decide on what type of game they wanted and created a hybrid "bullet-hell/metroidvania" that is more frustrating than fun. This game is HEAVY "bullet-hell" and LITE "metroidvania." So if you went into this game for the "metroidvania" aspect, you will be let down. All that aside, the main frustration comes from the spell card deck. You receive several interesting and fun spells to use as a powerful secondary attack (a must) and make a personalized deck.
