The mind blowing part is that these selected cards from your personalized deck are MIXED and RANDOMLY selected for you to use and show up in the  right bottom corner. Therefore, while you fly around in a SEA OF BULLETS you have to look down to the bottom right corner to see what card is coming up and if its something that would be beneficial. Why did the developers choose to randomize the players selection?!?! It becomes a race in just mashing buttons because the cards are random and maybe the player can use one and not the other. It dismantles the whole purpose of personalizing a deck. Frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: I played The Knight Witch to its completion and I've seen many reviews focusing on the metroidvania, bullethell & deckbuilding parts of the game, but I don't think this sort of categorisation makes much sense on this game. Yes there are a lot of bullets on screen sometimes. No, you cannot dodge at the beginning (hey, it's a cool upgrade). Yes there are hard sections (but there is a cheat system to help you with that if you get blocked and you're encouraged to use it in these cases). No, the submarine doesn't suck (or maybe yes, but maybe that's the point? think how much better you're gonna fight afterwards, as you're forced to use the cards better).You see, this is a different game, and as it happens with new things it's not easy to fit it into a box that we've already opened before. It's a new mix, and personally I think it works. And it works well.If you're hesitant whether to give it a go, I'd say go for it: every part of the game is way more thought and deeply connected that it may seem at first sight.However if what you're looking for is a experience that doesn't surprise you and that plays as any other games that you've already played, maybe this is not for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Metroidvania x Bullet hellWould not have thought that those genres could mesh, but they work well here. However. Your hitbox is a bit larger than your character, or at least it feels that way, maybe its tight, but i would still say its too large for a true bullet hell experience. The metroidvania aspects are fine, but I cant believe the devs have played a bullethell before. And to add insult to injury, when told the game is too hard (which i would argue is due to the hitbox issue), apparently the devs point to the cheat menu as a solution. The answer to "my hitbox needs to be tighter to my character" is not "invulnerability"
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: It took me about 2 months of playing off and on (around 11 hours) to 100% the game. Do I recommend it? Yes. Was it what was I expecting? Not really. Bullet hell metroidvania sounds incredibly promising, and while the game is good it tends towards frustration. I would perhaps blame that on mana for cards getting funneled into powerful weapon cards and there not being a lot of unlockable metroidvania features. Some people with a better brain than me might make interesting decks, I made one that allowed me to use the most powerful weapon card in the game as much as possible (and I probably didn't do that very well either.)That being said there's no long-term missables, the story/art/music are good, and it drew me in enough to want to actually 100% the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good concept, held down by annoying mechanics.This game has a very interesting mix of mechanics, from smup, to card battler and metroidvania, for the most part everything works together, which is a great feat, however, a couple of other mechanics hold back the game a lot.The card battler part kinda messes up the whole muscle memory thing that smups usually have, since cards are random and you buttons constantly change which spell they cast. this by itself is not so bad, if it wasn't by the fact that those cards are confined to the bottom right corner of your screen, forcing you to constantly look in that direction and leaving you unable to dodge the barrage of bullets usually fill the screen. I see many old comments in the community about this, which makes me think this game doesn't receive updates anymore.Exploration and movement are also cumbersome, since movement is very slow and you have to constantly spam the dodge button to go faster, when it could easy have a dash mechanic for traversing that wouldn't break the combat (making it so you couldn't attack during it).All in all, it's a fun game, but there's always going to be a point where it gets super frustrating having an challenge room completely filled with bullets, being forced to look down instead of having your cards hover your character so you can focus on the action at the same time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: A bit sad to give this a negative review, as this game had a lot of cool ideas. Huge downsides are : - A lot of ambushes are ULTRA annoying. Especially every single one in the water level, or the ones with the towers in the Forge.- Many Boss fights are either completely trivial or completely overtuned. Especially the very last boss fight that got me completely disgusted from the game. - A lot of visual clutter and serious performance issues. I had huge FPS drops in the final fight, when using the strongest witch spell. I have not had similar FPS drops in any other game, EVER.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a bullet hell genre that has some elements of Metroidvania, and it's a bad Metroidvania too. I liked it for a while, but soon it went downhill. I'm calling it a bad Metroidvania because the level design of some area makes backtracking an awful chore! I was just too tired/bored to backtrack to find secrets. The game story is all over the place, it's built on solid ideas but executed in a terrible way! It's like someone came up with a great concept then it was taken from them and given to incompetent people to decide what to do with it!The spell cards system is not polished, this is a tight bullet hell game, you need to glue your eyes to the screen so you don't get shot, but to use your spells you need to check the bottom of the screen to see what RANDOM spells the game chose for you now to use! I can't shoot and dodge while checking what are my current spells now.Pros:- Good visuals- Movement and shooting is funCons:- Story is all over the place, without spoilers: The villain doesn't have a real or relatable motive, character interactions are weird, the plot twists don't make any sense! Also the ending is awful - The characters are awful- The game is difficult in a bad way, enemies are bullet sponges, and you can't heal, when you die you have to cross a long way caved with enemies to reach the boss.- No fast travel, and areas sometimes are difficult to cross, so backtracking is a terrible experience, and that's a bad thing if you're developing a Metroidvania game!- The spell cards system is not polished- Sometimes it gets confusing which are your bullets and which are the enemies
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a number of issues, such as cards being incentivised due to their significantly higher damage while being a distraction in combat where you have to look down to check what cards you currently have. In its current form, it really doesn't work as a mechanic and would be much better if each button consistently did a single thing. It's quite telling when the most useful cards are the ones that make your normal bullets more powerful rather than the actual spells. Additionally, there are multiple "boss" encounters where the devs appear to have completely given up on making actually difficult enemies and have instead decided to cover the screen in enemies that spawn far faster than you can kill them.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Pretty artworkGood music Story has had some interesting moments so far.The basic gameplay is decent and the card system is a neat addition.Cons: Annoyingly unforgiving health system. Low hearts, full hearts of damage, enemies can't drop health pickups.Cheap deaths, mostly to trash. Somewhat slow movement and combat that grows old after a while makes those deaths even worse.Going the Knight route makes the game a lot more repetitive. Letting enemies drop alt weapons might help with this.Was pretty buggy at first, seems mostly better now but just a heads up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: I tried very hard to give this game a chance, but ultimately the negative review comes down to the disappointment, and the general response from the devs to feedback.This isn't a game for shmup players. This is a Metroidvania first with shmup elements added in. If you spend a lot of time playing shmups this will be frustrating due to how it breaks the rules of classic shmup design constantly. Even as a Metroidvania it seems bare bones and lacking. The maps are small, don't allow for much exploration, and offer very little value for revisiting them besides trying to find secrets later on.I was leaving my official stance as neutral, but the lack of a patch for the game-breaking issues over a week in and poor response from devs to feedback on the offcial forum leaves me without confidence that this will wind up being addressed in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? Yes, absolutely. Very beautiful visuals, fluid gameplay, an interesting and well-paced story, challenging (boss-)fights. As long as you enjoy metroidvanias, aren't afraid of (little) bullet hell games and don't hate card decks... this game is a joy to play (as long as it doesn't get stuck on the loading screen again...).After a worldwide war where the Knight Witches defeated a billionaire who devasted the earth, the rest of humanity (including you and your husband) were forced to live in an underground village. 14 peaceful years later suddenly an army of orcs (or in this case golems) invade the underground city and capture your friends. You are not a Knight Witch (yet), but you once trained to become one and so you can already fight and fly. You fly around and shoot your enemies using twin-stick controls. Or you do not use the right stick at all, and you will fire by instinct. Your shots will all be on target that way, but they are weaker than aimed shots. This is not the only unusual feature of the game. You can also craft a spell card deck in one of the beacons you find every few rooms. Collect many new spell cards during the game, there are more than three dozens. The spells are all quite different and help you during combat. Hit enemies with your regular shots to gain mana which you need to cast the spells. The really unusual thing is that you always have three spells available, randomly selected from your pre-constructed card deck, randomly assigned to three gamepad buttons. So you need to know how each spell works and how its icon looks like to make good use of it during combat. There is nothing more embrassing than intending to cast a long range attack spell and casting a melee sword attack instead.Combat is a bit like a bullet hell shooter, you evade a large number of enemy bullets, hide behind walls, circle your foes while shooting with your auto-aiming gun (or trying to aim yourself for even more powerful shots), and you use your spells for additional damage. Evading is more important than attacking. The game is divided into rooms, like in a roguelike. Kill all enemies to open the exits. Quite a few rooms do not contain enemies, but only stuff to collect or interact.  Collect green shards to buy armor from the baker skeletons (merchants). Collect Yupi cards to buy new spells. Collect various upgrades to become permanently stonger. An automap shows the current region. You can develop close bonds to inhabitants and gain support from them. You give press conferences and tell the population how the war is going... or lie to them. You gain followers on social networks to become stronger. Bosses leave mighty weapons behind that you can use in the future. When you die, you are transported back to the last beacon.The visual presentation is absolutely gorgeous and every room looks different, there are little things to find, different enemies and hazards, large areas with multiple rooms. Gamepad worked fine. Team 17 is on a run, they have become my favorite indie publisher. Hell Let Loose, Blashphemous, Bravery and Greed, Ship of Fools, Neon Abyss, Greak, Crown Trick, Batora, Tymesia, Narita Boy and Monster Sanctuary just to name some my recent favorites, and now The Knight Witch as well. One of the best looking metroidvanias of the year, fusing metroidvania mechanics with bullet-hell battles and an interersting (although slightly annoying with its RNG) spell system.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: TBH I'm just a sucker for thoughtful and loving game design. The writing is smart and encouraging (+inclusive without being exclusive), the art is spectacular, the game idea is bold, and it is not afraid to be challenging. Pretty much 100% the game. Backtracking was okay but there could have been more teleport spots or another option for faster travelling outside of combat!I hope they do more with this world. :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: A bullet hell will never work when you have to glance away from the barrage of bullets every few seconds to play card game at the bottom right of your hud.I couldn't find a difficulty setting to compensate either but there were cheats for Invulnerability which made this game pointless and extremely dull.I guess chalk this waste of money up to experience along with the heaving stacks of other deadwood in my Steam library.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: A metroidvania and bullet-hell game that fails on both.The paths are super linear, which isn't what metroidvanias are known for. There's backtracking, but good luck trying to reach those areas because there's no fast travel and your character's movement speed is slow. Late-game area is so terrible because to get to the teleporter, you have to go through many map changing scenes, which means many loading screens. I didn't bother trying to get 100% for this game because this game does not respect my time.The combat for this game fails in delivering a good bullet-hell experience. There are 3 things you have to keep an eye on during combat: the enemy bullet paths, your mana, and your card in hand. The last 2 requires you to glance at the bottom right of your screen, which goes against focusing on enemy bullet paths. Mana drops are RNG, and the nature of card deck RNG makes this even worser. It doesn't help that your basic bullets does close to no damage to late-game enemies, so you're forced to rely onto your cards to do damage.Enemy encounters that you face gets worse as you go through the game. At first, the enemy shoots red bullets, then green, then yellow, and many other forms. It's quite easy to get certain things mixed up with enemy bullets; currency drops are green-coloured, so you'll know what happens when the enemy also shoots green bullets. Enemies that spawns small minions swarming at you become common in late-game, and on top of that they also have a protective barrier that regenerates over time. You're forced to use piercing bullets to deal with them, but given the deck RNG, it gets frustrating trying to find the right card for the job.When these issues are addressed, maybe I will revisit this game again, but I doubt they'll ever improve, because the devs response to some people saying things are too difficult is to use cheats. Absolutely no dignity at all.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: The Knight Witch is a super underrated indie gem. The graphics, the story, the sound, and the gameplay are all fantastic. After playing the demo, I was obsessed. I could not put this game down until I had not only finished the game, but got 100% of the achievements.Highly recommended. If this catches your interest at all, you gotta give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: The Knight Witch is a 2d Bullethell Aquarivania about being chained down by societal pressures.  PewPewPew'd my way through it in 16.2 hours.  Difficulty is hard.  Beat it using a game controller.  I got this game on a humble bundle.Gameplay: Reminiscent of the games 'Aquaria' and 'Song of the Deep', you flyfloat around - sometimes submarine around - the map shooting at random adversaries in one of eight areas.  There are cards you collect that give you special abilities such as better spellfire, shields, explodybits, or some that amplify other cards.  You can swap out and fine tune the cards you want to use in the save beacons.  Story: Easy to follow, has twists, short, sometimes deep.  Has likeable, cute characters in it.Controls: The cards are set to X, Y, and B on the xbox controller.  A is for talking, R is for shooting, dash (when you get it) is L, and there are LT and RT abilities you get on the way.  'Start' selects the menu, and Left on the D-pad opens the map. Music: It's great with a Celtic flair about it.  Feels like a violin, flute, and lute made friends and go on an adventure together.  Recommend owning it.  Graphics: Also great and polished.  I love the look of Rayne.  Everything is smooth, it's easy to tell levels apart, all the npcs are easy to tell apart.  Only quip is the differing color of the enemy bullets can make it hard to tell what's friendly and not friendly fire in the thick of things.Dog: You can pet the dog.Difficulty: It spikes weirdly.  Really weirdly.  If there was one thing I wish the developers would fine tune, it'd be either how many/fast the bullets from some enemies are or the ambushes.  The ambushes can be daaang hard sometimes.  Way harder than the bosses, who seem straight-forward in comparison.  Except for Hextinction, who is impossibly far too hard for normal gamers.  If you have trouble, there is an option on the menu for various cheats you can toggle on and off (need to look at the community guides for the cheat codes to unlock each one, which is weird to me.)  Endings: There are 3.  Bad, Good, and True.  I've gotten good and true, and have no interest in getting bad because I don't think Rayne deserves it.  Backtracking:  Other reviews say there isn't any backtracking, but I backtracked the crap out of this game.  Really wish the game introduced an easier way to get around far sooner than it does.** Epilepsy Warning **: I wouldn't.  Lots of flashies and bullets.  None of the flashies I came across were terrible outside of Hextinction, but I have a feeling it'd sneak up on you in unfun ways. Thoughts: I'm a pretty good 2d 'Metroidvania' gamer.  I've beaten HellTemple on HardMode in LaMulana.  I had trouble on The Knight Witch until I Got Gud, and even after getting gud, I couldn't beat the final boss without cheating.  The difficulty spikes are weird, unlike other bullethell games the enemy fire can be unpredictable.  Lots of people had issues sorting out the cards and using them because you have to look up at the corner of the screen to see which cards are out, but it didn't hinder me too badly.  In fact, I enjoyed the crap out of this game until the end, when I got stuck in a death loop with the slog known as Hextinction for 3+ hours trying to beat the game without cheating until it became royally unfun. That is the least rewarding boss I've come across in a while and it seriously needs to be neutered on difficulty.  Weirdly I liked the normal ending and freaking Hated the true ending, which didn't seem to have much thought put into it.  Tips for playing:- Level up your strength before your magic early on.  - It is easier to hold down R for endless shooting and letting it auto aim than manually aiming with the joystick. On the flip side, if you're chased by monsters and trying to get out of a room, manually aim at the doorway to open it because auto aiming wont help you there. - Roughly 1/3rd of ambush areas lead to optional things like powerups, trapped people, and cards.  If the ambush comes across as unfun or too hard, look for other areas to go.  On the way you'll gradually get better with spells/shooting/farming mana or you'll find easier-to-attain spell cards and the ambush raid might not seem so hard next time.  The same goes for 'puzzle' areas that seem impossible or too hard.  - Focus on Rayne and dodging in heavier bullet moments and let auto-shoot and random spells do the rest.  - I used the cheats 'endless mana' and 'slower bullets' to beat Hextinction while keeping it fair.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: No neutral option, so going with not recommend. The difficulty spikes aren't necessarily the problem, the annoyance is when you have bullets approximately the same color as collectibles, making it hard to tell if you are receiving loot or if a bullet is coming after you.Some of the challenges can be frustrating simply due to how large the area is with hidden spawns and almost forced weapon changes (Especially frustrating if you are running a deck that revolves around mana recovery and weapons). Certain puzzles can be very frustrating because they feel very random with what will work (I've definitely had to solve a few puzzles in a likely unintended manner).Lots of pointless backtracking because there is no teleport to beacon. You do get a teleport from beacon later in the game, but it has very limited use outside of leaving an area faster. There is no dash option. You can spam the dodge button for faster movement, but there is no hold down dodge to move faster.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, probably one of the most fun Metroidvania and Bullet hell game i had in a while.I had a ton of fun exploring and building a deck to beat the enemies i faced later on, especially the boss fights. The Ambushes, Boss Battles, and even the normal fighting, it's all very challenging yet fun to take a jab at.Also, the music and Art is so beautiful in contrast to the setting and situation. I will say though the difficulty is a bit hard so players who are new to Bullet hell experiences will have a surprise; And the story is pretty well written for a Metroidvania game.Overall, this game is amazing and worth the price and time to pay/play 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: The Knight Witch is a bullet hell metroidvania with almost no backtracking. The graphics are amazing and I loved the story and characters.The deck customization is a nice touch, and I felt stronger the more I progressed through the game.It's a hard game, but even the bosses can be beaten after a few tries. There are no unfair challenges, but the true final boss is insanely hard. Luckily, there's a cheat menu to help with that one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game 100% and these are my impressions:In Short: When you are a Fan of the Metroidvania Genre, give it a go. But maybe wait for a discount!Longer explanation:First of all, The Knight Witch is a Metroidvania Shoot 'em up attempt and manages to blend these 2 Formulas quite well. We have the exploration and a lot of optional questlines and fast-paced bullethell action. So far, so good.However, some design decisions stick out and sadly not in a good way! For example, you dont get an option to dodge until like 30% of the game. Another example are collectibles (namely Frost Moon and Radiant suns), which you can collect, but don't get a real explanation, how to get them and what they do.These are just some examples, but there are many more.Story-wise, we have some decent story with one or two turns, but nothing blockbuster worthy.The cast is pretty forgettable and the world built around it is interesting in itself, but doesn't get all the possibilities to shine.Performance of the game is pretty good and fluid, no complaints here. Graphics are quite nice and feel vibrant with lots of details. Sadly these details don't add much more to it. You see it and that's it. It doesn't invite you to explore. But that's personal taste, i guess.The biggest minus in my opinion is the combat. I felt like, the further i got into the game, the more the combat felt like a chore. Enemies just get more health and you get more of them for each fight. I felt like you get thrown at with more and more bulletsponges but no new innovative enemies.All in all, it was a decent game, which does many things right but not exceptional and misses opportunities.Fans of the genre can give it a go, but maybe should wait for a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: To be quite honest, I don't *want* to say "I don't recommend this game", because I did have some good fun in parts of the game.Parts.The Knight Witch is hard. It is aggressive, demanding of perfection, and will punish failure with a long run back to where you failed.I stopped at the submarine section, where I cannot fire up or down anymore and only left or right, while being bombarded with attacks from enemies below and to the left, where you cannot fire. And the checkpoint for the section is 5 screens back, with shortcuts only cutting out *some* of the worst parts.The map design is more akin to a Rage Game with how stingy the checkpoints are. If I had the option to respawn on the same screen I died on, I would definitely be singing a different tune, but after running a gauntlet 30 times just to get the ability to shoot boomerangs at the end of a hard coridor... I can only conclude this game is built for people who do not mind being forced to rerun the same section over and over until they do it damageless. I am not that person, so I have to not recommend the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: The Knight Witch is a weak metroidvania and a mediocre bullet hell shooter, with a bizarrely spiky difficulty curve. The story broaches some interesting themes, but doesn't take them far enough for that to make the game worth playing. As somebody who loves bullet hell games AND metroidvania, I thought the game was *okay*, but the only people I can recommend this game to are people like me - people who were willing to completely ignore the mixed reviews, and buy the game based on a promising demo, hoping the full game got better. (And it... does, sometimes? But sometimes the difficulty just spikes, to a degree that feels awful due to Rayne's way-too-big hitbox and the game's unreasonable backtracking times.)
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: The demo really was fun and I enjoyed myself. Then as more and more enemies appear later in the game, it really does live up to bullet hell standards, however, I found there were a lot of frustrating aspects such as enemy types, bullet speed, different types of bullets, lack of space to dodge said bullets, movement speed etc. There are cheats that you can unlock to make the game easier and make sections of the game manageable. However I felt these cheats made very challenging boss fights almost too easy. For example, take a boss fight, you have 3-4 health points, thats enough for 3-4 hits to die from. There are generally no healing in boss fights. If you cant manage that, the next best cheat is total invincibility. Nothing to maybe half the damager you take or something similar. Heck, it'd be cool to add a difficulty setting. Essentially what I'm saying is that there was a feeling of a lack of inbetween. If you cant get past a boss fight, your next option was to absolutely demolish the boss with little to no difficulty. The characters are made with love and the connection between the main character and her husband is cute. Animation is cute as well. i like the spell card loadout aspect, though the mana felt a bit difficult to obtain. Cant remember if theres a cheat code for that other than "infinite mana".I really liked the idea of the game and look forward to what other games this company might make, but this game wasnt it for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: What a stupid game design to keep giving the player the dash ability then taking it away from them, literally making the game needlessly frustrating!! Good gameplay, interesting idea, great soundtrack, ruined by a VERY stupid and illogical decision. Adds superficial difficulty (because with all the bullet hell happening, you have ZERO maneuverability, even your normal movement is slow), and makes the game 100 times less enjoyable. Also, some levels have only 2 beacons that are too far apart, when there are more, you can't fast travel between them unfortunately.So, having put up with this frustrating sh*t, I get to the part of the portal at the last bit of the game, and I died before going, so now it bugged!!Awful, absolute bad experience, if I could give it two thumps down, I would.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: This game rules and is definitely a good addition to both the metroidvania and bullet hell genres. I'm only about an hour in, but the gameplay is solid and the weapon system is very fun. Honestly, with games like this, the moment-to-moment gameplay almost feels more important than anything else and this game nails it. I'm definitely interested in seeing how it develops further, but the gameplay base is very solid and enjoyable!
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Didn't enjoy it.Has some cool ideas, I like the card system, I do not like the seemingly random order they come out at and the fact I have to take my eyes off my character (who is usually being shot at) to check which card is on which button, and sometimes while doing this I would lose track of where my character was entirely.Some difficulties with visual clarity, I got a boomerang weapon that looks very similar to the enemy boomerangs, bullets that leave me going "what was I hit by?" and many other fun questions.I think the most annoying thing is that all enemy bullets stay on screen even after the enemy is dead, leading to a lot of hits taken while trying to deal with new targets.Can't comment on the story as it didn't grip me soon enough and I just wanted to play.Overall, with some tweaks it could be really fun! It's just not very fun at the moment.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;Dr It's a short, fun and enjoyable experience for the majority of the game.  I'd say 7/10I "finished" it after roughly 13 hours, I didn't beat the true final boss because it's insanely hard, it's so much harder than the other bosses that it makes the base game feel like you're on easy modeNegatives:- There is a water level which is unnecessarily hard for no reason, basically you have a dash and you can aim your bullet normally, but when you're in water, you lose both of that, which is just stupid. Meaning you can't aim up or diagonally while underwater- Bosses are challenging but never feel impossible, except for the final final boss, which is just too hard, it's almost impossible to beat without cheats
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: The good:Pretty graphics, 2D eyecandyThe overall plotThe link concept.The Bad:The plotholes and the characters, oh god the characters.Most of the spells are junk.The difficulty is quite high, and not in a good way - enemies are bullet sponges - tedium reigns supreme.Only 5 main areas, which you will be forced to traverse again and again, without fast travel.Dashing is the only thing that makes this bearable, you won't have it for the first half or so of the game.As soon as you get the dash ability, you'll have to get to the underwater level, which sadly fits the cliché.Enemies don't drop health and very rarely drop mana, so you'll be relying on those bullets for a majority of the game, making this The Ugly:The UI is an absolute failure. Bullet hell + randomly changing spells shown in the bottom right corner = you die due to the UI and have to repeat ambushes or bosses again and again.The UI positioning cannot be adjusted to bring these closer to the player character, which is where you want your attention at, normally.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a generally unpleasant experience. It is neither a good bullet hell nor a good metroidvania. (Review Written with 100% Completion)The Combat:  The largest problem is how painfully unfair the combat is, the majority of rooms in the game place mobs of enemies in the same spot and as far as I can tell their patterns are more or less random, even enemies that appear to have predictable patterns sometimes fire in an arbitrary direction. The result is an endless cacophony of scenarios where you may not actually have a possibility of dodging quickly decimating your 3 max health. Lastly, the hurtbox appears to be slightly larger than the player sprite so you can be hit by things you are narrowly missed by. It would probably have been far less frustrating if the hurtbox was at least a little bit tinier like in a traditional bullet hell.The Cards:The primary method of combat is card spam for as long as you can afford it. This would be fine with a better implementation but as it stands it was rather finicky. Firstly, the card UI is locked to the bottom right of the screen and the order your 9 spell cards appear in is totally random. As the game is a bullet hell you need to have your focus locked on your character but you constantly have to take quick glances to the corner to see what you have queued up. Ideally I'd prefer a system like One Step From Eden, which has the same deck system but in addition to having your deck in the corner, there is also a preview placed above your character allowing you to focus on evasion and offense. Secondly, there were tons of times where a card loaded in my deck but upon using it was actually a different card entirely. Apparently when using cards too quickly or using cards with timers the wrong card art can load leading to misfires. Collectibles - Ambushes:Ambushes are obnoxious enough to warrant their own short summary. For 100% completion there are 27 Ambushes across the game, each of which require being done hitless (fine) but also in 30 seconds. This is a flat 30 second timer that applies to every single ambush in the game regardless of enemy type, enemy density, room size, stage hazards, and number of waves. For some rooms this was extremely is simple consisting of two waves of normal enemies. However, there were also rooms so large that even if you kill the enemies instantly with spell cards, traveling around the room to reach enemies ate up so much time it was near impossible. Additionally, the enemies take several seconds to spawn in so if the room has 5 waves there is a set amount of time you lose from the time it takes the enemies to spawn, maybe giving you a handful of seconds to actually do combat while the rest is waiting for things to spawn and getting close enough you can actually attack them. Once I was getting into the late game I was so annoyed I turned on all the cheats in the game just to get through them as the challenges were far to constrained to be fun. Map Size, Back Tracking, and Fast Travel:A short point but the map is fairly large and also fairly liner. There are many collectibles strewn throughout the world, some of which are only available after certain conditions have been met. The amount of back tracking both for story, objectives, side quests, and collectibles caused me to travel the same long hallways at a slightly less than moderate pace dozens of times. To make matters worse, there's no real fast travel. There is a very late game side quest that allows you to travel to the start of maps but not to any beacons within them. Half the time spent in this game was probably just retreading everything to finish collecting. Story:It was okay, it raised some points about propaganda and worship culture but mostly fell flat, especially when the choices have no impact on the story and you can make up any missing levels by buying likes. The coolest aspect is only revealed in hidden notes around the painfully slow to navigate map.2.5/12
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Way better than I expected and a pretty good mix of the bullet hell and action adventurer genres, despite its flaws. The music is quite good, the art, environments and animations are absolutely gorgeous, the story and characters are simple and tongue in cheek but pretty good (and with clear political messages) and the combat is, imo, great. It's fluid, responsive and (until very close to the end) quite hard (I got 24 Radiant Suns and Frost Moons before I had the last link powers and best spellcards and I gotta say, some of those were mad hard. But everything became trivial after the last link powers and the Ghost Gun). The game does have some noticeable problems though.The major one was. to me, that you take a while to unlock some fundamental powers. You don't start with the dodge (unlocked only after the second map, which I considered a crime against humanity), many of the spellcards in the first half are complete trash and all the other powers that will aid you in your exploration are very slow to come by, which means you're in for quite a bit of late game backtracking. Which leads us to the slow speed of map traversal. Seriously, Rayne should fly faster when out of combat or be able to continuously dash, especially if you consider how expansive some of the maps are (e.g. the zone between the Forge Fields and Factory is a huuuge dead zone that takes forever to traverse) and we should be able to teleport between beacons to alleviate all the backtracking. That would make some sections of the game feel less like a chore. And, last but not least, the random nature of the spellcard casting can be extremely annoying. I get what they were going for but it's frustrating to be within a hard ambush challenge and get all your spells in the worst possible order, making you fail time and time again until RNG decides to smile upon you (the last Witch link power makes this irrelevant because you'll finally start to regen your mana... but you'll probably only get that at the very end of the game). It's not the end of the world and you can play around it but, damn, it didn't need to be such a pain.How seriously these flaws end up impacting the player's experience will vary from person to person. Personally, even with all that, I still had a lot of fun throughout the game, even during it's worst/slower parts. That's because I really vibed with it, so its faults ended up feeling minor to me. The combat felt engaging throughout, the music kept my mood up and the fluid animation never ceased to amaze me (plus, Rayne's character design is super cute).All in all, this one was a pretty good surprise that ended up being worth every penny.PS.: The dog is named Pistola... kudos to the genius who chose that name. Pistola in brazilian portuguese can mean either gun, penis or very angry. Everytime I saw that dog I chuckled.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: I love challenging games but this one is not well balanced at all. When your main gimmick is powerful spell cards why would you make it difficult to refill the mana it costs to use said cards, ESPECIALLY when the average enemy is a bullet sponge. Cool idea, decent story, terribly un-fun execution. I could probably finish this game but the days of torturing myself for self acknowledged "gamer cred" are far over. There's just way too many other well polished games fighting for attention.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fabulous, and I highly recommend it for search action fans. Maybe it doesn't perfect the shmup genre, and maybe the spellcards inject some element of luck into your play, but I still found the systems fun and engaging all the way through.I also really appreciated that the story was so upbeat, with many likable and empathizable characters. It's a rare treat to get a story where I wind up fond of everyone.These are what I consider the downsides. Please accept this critique.* The difficulty curve has a couple of spikes, including the very final boss. This wasn't a problem for me, but I could see some people being drawn in by the relative ease of most of the game and getting frustrated by a couple of parts. Fortunately, the menu suggests that you can use some cheats, though the game doesn't tell you how to do this.* The method by which one finishes off the final boss is not explained or telegraphed to the player. I had to look up a video.* The lack of a fast travel system -- barring the half-hearted implementation that you unlock  -- was a drag. Repeated backtracking isn't fun, because your normal movement is fairly slow, and using the dash requires tapping a button repeatedly. Why not let us warp around? I know that narratively, that's problematic at a couple of points, but you could have figured out a way to let us do it most of the time.* Enemy bullets, your own bullets, and the green gem pickups all blend together, visually. None of them have distinctive colors all their own, especially if you pull out a late-game, bullet spam spell that sends orange bullets everywhere. I'd have liked more distinctiveness. Visual noise is a problem for some of us. It's a lot easier to deal with games that keep things understandable at a glance.* It seems that the secret pages were not , or at least I never found the last few. I don't know whether this was intentional. Since they're secrets, maybe that's not so bad, but I expected they would be marked.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: What is it with beautiful games with interesting, blended concepts,   fail so much?The feelings, expectations and energy from the trailers in the  Steam Store Page are false. The game-play is not that. I would recommend this only if you like paying for games with nice drawn graphics or want to learn about what videogames shouldn't do. I just searched the nice ending online because how frustrating the experience was. There were some very, very very few moments  in which the game-play and concepts were nice. Overall, no. • The game is not hard. It is atrociously aggressive against the player.  ad hit-reg. The game does not trigger spells correctly. Incorrect color for enemy projectile. All the game a pickup is green; then  the game has  an enemy group that shoots the same Tie Fighter green exactly as the resource you are supposed to pick. • As other reviews say, the difficulty spikes nonsensically. Rather than being a balanced shoot'em up, the game goes  as a bullet hell in which you cannot move accordingly the situation. I just spammed that dodge button and left RNG allow me to survive. • It is not a metroidvania. Has some aspects of it, but wrongly implemented. It is ok some areas are linear. The game becomes tedious. • The game does not respect the mechanics it teaches as the premise. Enemy units just shoot through cover without any spells. Enemies are not affected by the traps you are. 0• You won't feel like a magical floating Jedi, Master Chief or Doom Slayer.  It is frustrating to flying around wondering how unfair the next area is going to be due to my attacks and movements being so bad. • The economics of the magic system are just so wrong. I didn't find a spell for health. There is 1 for armor, but is very  magically expensive. • The deck building aspect is horrible. It is about luck, not about deck building. There is no point of mixing cards because there is not enough mana. • It is a bullet hell shoot'em up, but having to move the sight to see what spell cards are available is a horrible design mistake. With other games as analogy:•I t is like playing Doom 2016 or Eternal, without ammo. The demons have all the weapons. Your bullets disappear after a few paces but the enemies' bullets have a much superior muzzle speed, never disappear. shoot through walls Also you don't run, just walk slowly. Melee animation kills do not throw armor or bullets. • It is like playing Helldivers, but  stratagems need mana. The stratagems are not efficient.  To get the mana you have to frustratingly  kill enemies with the melee or something that feels useless.  You don't have medkits.Not all kills give mana.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: The game has some absurd difficulty spikes, but trying (a lot) you eventually overcome them. The last boss though... I felt insulted. It isn't just too difficult, but the behaviours are so random between tries that I didn't feel I could actually learn and improve. Each try was a dice throw, and after 10+ tries I grew tired of it. Also, what about all the times I decided to make the witch be honest na dgain less Link at the expense of not lying to the people? I got NOTHING for doing that. Only the handicap of reaching the final boss with way less passive abilities... And narratively speaking, given that the Witch has all the time in the world to prepare before the last fight, how come she can't ask for more link to the people? How come she even can't access a damn shop to buy more armor????All in all, it has been a decent bullet hell game, with beautiful graphics and sound. But I can't just accept this last boss. If someone reads this and wants to try the game do yourself a favour: lie in all the interviews the witch has, in order to gain the most Link possible.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: This game needs a number of changes : remove the crazy difficulty spikes ( most of the game is fairly straightforward except for these super spikes ), make enemies less spongy, make backtracking less unpleasant , remove the very unwieldy puzzles with bombs ( I almost entirely gave up because of one of them)   improve the ergonomics ( the minute you look at your spells you die because they’re in a very inconvenient place)I lost interest two thirds into the game, turned on cheats, and still didn’t manage to finish it ( somehow I don’t understand how to kill the super end boss ) !
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: It is a fun game when it's not making your experience as painful as the devs could make it, creating hard games is easy. Making things enjoyable while still being difficult, well the game designers may need more practice on that one. Now if you like being constantly frustrated and angry at your game, then you should try this game. But, if you are not one of the players that like to play games like that, pass and spend waste your money or time.I wonder if Devs even playtest games anymore to gauge difficulty anymore.The deck-building thing just needs to be removed, cool idea but focusing on what random cards I got this time while avoiding the “Bullet Hell” aspect of the game is a bad combo. That and matching it with a mana system made it more unusable, especially during boss fights. Maybe have me select cards that work on a cooldown system, Gives the player occasional power boosts without drawing too much attention easily from the bullet hell.Heat-seeking bullets are great… in small quantities. So many boggs down the game especially with the deck-building mana-based cards being the only way to deal with them. If you want to saturate the player with them they have to eventually stop heat-seeking or explode after a delay.Bullet sponge enemies in a bullet hell game, are not bad but if they have something that protects them or they shoot heat-seeking bullets, tanky they do not need to be. Not much to this point that just seems like basic design.That's it, sorry I didn't like the game for those of you who think its fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: To be brief, I was not a huge fan. Minor spoilers ahead.Pros:- Story, solid story I followed from start to finish and it had some cool twists and turns.- Card System, sort of like slay the spire. Very cool and kept the combat fresh.- 2D Vertical Movement, was very interesting to me. The level design did not pop out, but being able to explore the full 2D plane made every room feel fresh. Cons:- Difficult Spikes, super irregular difficulty on enemy and boss fights. Took me about 7 or 8 tries on boss 4 but then I nearly first tried the boss after. Nothing compared to an enemy room in the second stage for me though.- (Most) Bosses, are either repeated or generally weak. I like a few fights but the final and  were both a huge let down for me.- Overall Gameplay, does not feel fluid. There is a lot of backtracking, and not for getting loot, to get to new levels by running through rooms you have already seen several times. On top of that, the hitbox for your character feels "large," making dodging clunky at times. I will note the hitbox thing was not as a big of an issue for me as it sounded like it was for others, I had a couple attacks hit me that felt very far away but overall it was solid.I think the game is overall okay, but I don't think I could recommend it to anyone. The combat, which is the main focus of the game, is only interesting cause of the card system and even that falls short at times. A lot of your deaths will feel unfair as they were caused by some random enemy shooting a bullet that was off your screen or blocked by the other 15 enemies on your screen. With there being so many new metroidvanias dropping this year (2024), I would suggest you save your time and look elsewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Great as an experiment, not as great as a game.This game is a mixed bag: on one hand you have awesome artstyle, good movement system and some cool concepts here and there. On other hand - this is quite a limited piece with lack of exploration, economy, precision and so on and so forth. I like the brave mix in the first place - free fly bullet hell metroidvania? Yes, please! Sounds fantastic. In reality you quickly tend to realize that the whole game is a one huge underwater level from any other game, so to say. Remember Aquaria? That kind of stuff. Not a bad thing tho. Next comes the core of the game - the combat. It's... fair? Yes, I assume. Not sure. At point - generic enemy fights (Ambushes) are more challenging than actual boss fights, like many folks stated in reviews. Then you realize what's so difficult about it - the controls and navigation, avoiding walls & spikes - that's the 80% of difficulty in this game.  And I state again - the movement system is well done in this game, except for, probably, dodge/dash - it's weird. The cards are... eh.. ok? Basically cards act like abiilities/weapons and require to be equipped (limited slots) and cast (with mana). They are indefinite, so once it's cast it goes to discard and shuffled back in to your active slots once those are depleted. I bet you won't use 70% of those cards, but it's a nice experiment and a smart system. By this point I would still recommend the game, yet couple following points ruin the whole experience for me: Level design in general. What are you expecting of a good metroidvania? Huge map with dozen of biomes, varied enemies and such? Forget it here - just a pinch of locations that are fantasy town, fantasy town, lava thing, factory thing and caves under fantasy town. Well, that suits well to tell a small localized story, sure. But it's so small and it ends so quick. I mean, after you played Afterimage, Bloodstained and other similar games would it be Time Spinners or Hollow Knight - you expect an adventure, right? Here you have a whole roller-coaster park which is closing in 15, so your smiling guide runs your through the attractions, nervously looking at the clock.   Sure, it's still somewhat fun, but gives you that feel like you're in a hurry. You want to see everything for yourself, explore this world for a little bit, but 'xcuse me, this pavilion is limited with just these 4 rooms, so please enjoy yourself while you can". Second problem is supporting systems, I would say. The game has some currency dropped by the enemies and it's a classic (by now) mistake of the new devs so far: you have the currency, but why would the player want to collect it? Why should the player bother killing enemies? To be able to pass through the room - that's right. But it's a metroidvania game - so there are lots of back and forth, why would player want to hunt the monsters on the way back? No reason. What I'm trying to say - the currency (little green crystals) can be used for several purposes: buying temp boosts (armor, shrines), duplicating cards and obtaining XP (limited). And that's all. You would say: but, hey, that's the perfect reasoning, no? No! After 6 hours of playing my witch has something like 50.000 of that currency that I literally have nowhere to spend for a reason, which screams "poor economy" to me. Spice it up with the strange "Link/XP" system, that gives you XP points only when you talk to other characters (saving them or moving plot further). I literally had no vision of when/where/how I am going to level up in this game. Would I become stronger by killing this boss? Nope! I got a card, so... yeah? I don't know. Why not adding things that just work: xp rewards from enemies, shops where upgrades could be bought from dropped currency? No idea. A great example where experiment for the sake of experiment won't be as fruitful as expected. Same goes for other game aspects such as Knight/Witch upgrades: so this game gives you an opportunity to build either a "combat heavy" character, or "spell mastery" type. There are choices when you level up your link between two parameters and there are "mystical fruits" that let you upgrade either health or mana points. Fruits are limited, of course. And guess what? If you, like me, were: "ooh, I'll go full hardcore tank thing! Spells are overrated gimme all the health!" - surprise! You can't. D: Up to a certain point you can add to your "knight" parameter (6 hearts) just to see the message of "Your health max limit reached", forcing you to invest to mana. Why? No idea. 6 hears in certain fights is like 20 seconds of gameplay attempt. Why not allowing to push further? I guess poor balance and realization somewhere late in development can basically softlock your progression by ruining the build? I don't know :)Anyways: a game that looks fine, feels fine in the short run and may appeal to some. _childDocuments_.review: This game feels like it's on the cusp of being great, but many design decisions hinder its potential.The biggest issue is the game gets boring quick because of simplicity. Gameplay, most of the time, still boils down to basic moving and shooting. Having a card system for your spells to rotate through them makes it a bit more interesting, but this ultimately doesn't matter when you barely get to use them. You get energy by hitting enemies, but the energy spawns near them. Meanwhile, the core gameplay encourages you to be away from enemies, dodging their projectiles. The gameplay would have been a lot more interesting if you automatically regained energy by fighting rather than needing to pick them up. This would have made the combat a lot more active, rather than having downtimes when your energy is depleted. Your energy is actually depleted most of the time too, so it starts feeling unreliable. There are sections in the game where there are floating stones that automatically replenish your energy. These sections really show how much more fun the combat is if you can continuously use spells. This contrast just made my experience with the game much more miserable, and I was already bored within the first hour.Along with the issue of the spells, the combat here feels very disjointed. Gameplay feels like you need to focus on one thing at a time. At one moment, I'm focusing on my aim, then I need to focus on dodging enemy projectiles, and then I need to focus on how I can use my spells to great effect. None of these aspects felt they came together to have fun unified combat.This could have been easily fixed if players had more options in combat, like being able to dodge or parry bullets.I know you actually get a dash later in the game, but I just don't understand why you don't have it from the very start. Some spells can parry or nullify bullets too, but as I said, your energy is depleted most of the time anyway, so you can't rely on them. The choice of locking mechanics early in made the start of the game feel very slow.Having a melee attack would have made the combat a lot more dynamic too. There are moments when the game wants you to square up face-to-face with enemies, but it doesn't actually give you the proper abilities for it. Easily could have been fixed if you had a guard button or some kind of rush attack that gives you invulnerability when hitting enemies.The story actually felt like it had some cool ideas too, but I ultimately couldn't care about it and just skipped most of the dialogue. They should have delivered the story more through gameplay/environment rather than boring dialogue. Show, don't tell.Ultimately, I don't disagree with the game's current rating. It can still be enjoyable if you're looking for something simple. But I found it disappointing as it actually has great elements and just needed the extra work to tie it all together.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish the review system was more than just yes or no. There's a decent game here, but it's not for me and I can't even really recommend it, maybe wait for a sale. _childDocuments_.review: (To give more context: I played an extra 45 minutes on the demo)I chose "Recommend", but I don't fully like or enjoy this game. It has enough glaring flaws to deserve a "Not Recommend", but at the same time it's still decent and competent, so it could be a great fun game for some specific players.This game is a twin-stick bullet hell (danmaku) shooter, mixed with deckbuilding elements. First I have to give my own gaming background: I played 250 hours of Slay the Spire, and I played 400+ hours of bullet hell/ damnaku.I can say that in the Knight witch, the merging of the deckbuilding elements doesn't fit with the gameplay at all.I) The game is fast paced and challenging. Getting hit once is a big deal (as you only get 3~5-ish HP at a time before dying).II) You need to be very mindful of your hitbox as there are many bullets at once on the screen, and some patterns can be complicated, so you need your full attention on simply not getting hit.III) It's also a twin-stick shooter where you base weapon has a mid-screen range and the bullet velocity is not so high: it means you need to AIM at your opponent.Both of these elements are already very challenging, and could work well, Enter The Gungeon has similar gameplay.But then the third element: deckbuilding breaks everything. In order to cast a spell, you need to look at your bottom right corner to see: 1) What spells are available, 2) To which button is the spell attached 3) Do you have enough mana to cast it?So how can you take care of I) II) and III), while at the same time NOT looking at the screen?You could attribute some of your death to the fact your TRIED to use a spell. And usually the spells aren't totally game changing, AND you spend your mana which needs to be collected near the body of the enemies (which is to say where you are most likely to take damage). You'd probably have better chance of survival solely focusing on dodging, aiming, and using the spells randomly.Here's how the game could have been fixed:1) Not having the deckbuilding system in the first, maybe go "Wizards of legend" route where you choose a spell that you bind to a specific button.2) Have the game be slowed down a lot more so that taking your eyes off your character isn't a death sentence3) Make the spells be used less frequently, but more impactful4) Somehow show the spells on the ingame sprite of your character, so atleast you can see more easily what cards you have in hands.Also the visual effects on the game is really confusing. Your bullets are just as brights as the enemies bullet, so it's very difficult to quickly process what are the bullets you should dodge (and remember, you are only a few mistakes away from dying.)This game could have been so great, but it was too ambitious and ultimately muddied it's game design.

_childDocuments_.review: I FUNKED THAT GREEN CHAIN SH!T UP! My poor fingers.This game is a little delightful treasure. The art is unique, cute, and memorable. The story is simple but effective, and it isn't purely linear, but sprinkled with twists, turns, and allegory. The music is catchy and enjoyable. Some of the music and sound effects were eerie which delicately piqued my horror-novelty fixation. The first time encountering the final boss, my stomach dropped. WHICH IS GREAT. REARRANGE MY VISCERA PLS.The controls are addictive and spammable. I thought I'd never be able to master shooting, dodging, and processing card priority/activation all simultaneously within a matter of seconds, but that was just silly doubt. Everything has a learning curve; believe in yourself! At first the card system wasn't very complex or interesting. The options to build combos were very limited, but that's to be expected. As the game progresses, better combinations are viable which becomes very satisfying. It's not big-brain complexity, but it still requires thoughtful consideration that makes the journey tailored to your preferences and enhances personalization.The hardest boss for me was the final boss, which probably would have been easier had I maxed out some upgrades...But I digress. When I finally conquered, I was elated. My biggest plot gripe which left me ambivalent was Robyn's metaphorical-depression arc. I don't like the implication that depressed people aren't solvable, but I suppose the interpretation is a point-of-no-return via destructive choices. People are still accountable for their actions. Yet, her despair engulfed me.Overall, I like the game very much because it's a happy-medium between tryhard and cozy. It challenges you beyond your perceived limits without stretching you thin. Albeit, there were grueling moments of frustration, but they were fleeting.+kitty n doggoWould purchase a sequel!

_childDocuments_.review: The Knight Witch is a shoot-’em-up Metroidvania. I’m usually not great at shmups, but I managed to fumble my way to the end and it was pretty enjoyable.What I really want to talk about is the story, though. It’s an environmentalist climate change narrative. It does a surprisingly good job of this up until the end, where you (of course) solve climate change by punching it in the face. I think this merits some discussion.The story beings by telling us that greedy capitalists drained the planet’s resources and devastated the environment, just like in real life. But in this story, magic is real, and believing in people makes them stronger. This allows for the creation of the titular Knight Witches, heroes who have godlike power due to the faith everyone has in them. They ultimately kill the CEO in a massive battle that reveals a massive cave system that was conveniently developed into an underground city by an ancient civilization. Everyone flees the now-uninhabited surface for the safety of the underground.The plot begins 14 years later, following a failed Knight Witch named Rayne. We learn the underground city only remains habitable due to powerful technology built by the precursors, and as you can probably guess, it’s eventually revealed it runs on evil fossil fuels that are killing the planet, so you have to destroy it. Along the way, we also learn that the narrative around the Knight Witches was largely manufactured and whitewashed to give them more power, and a major mechanic is choosing whether to be honest with the public or to feed them comforting lies for greater power. (I was worried this was leading to a reveal that actually the capitalists were the good guys, but fortunately no.) Tying into this is a racial subplot where it’s revealed the Knight Witches killed a lot of a particular ethnic group who served the capitalists during the war, but this was erased in favor of a narrative that they only fought robots. Rayne also discovers that her empathic power is a double-edged sword, as the Knight Witches feel everyone’s fear and anxiety as well as their love, which inevitably drives them insane from stress.So, yeah, that’s a . I think the first stumbling block is that the story tried to do too many things at once. It’s a climate change allegory  a critique of institutional corruption  racial commentary  a deconstruction of “clap your hands if you believe”  a psychological examination of heroes. That’s a lot of topics to cover in a 15-20 hour game! They’re related topics, so it does make sense to tackle them all at once, but there’s just not enough time or space to do them all justice. Most topics are only able to be touched briefly, and are rarely set up cleanly. In particular, I felt like the racial stuff came out of nowhere, despite there being plenty of opportunities to lay groundwork for it earlier. I would have appreciated if early NPC dialogue could have given us more worldbuilding about the current social structure, instead of being entirely focused on Rayne personally.Most of these topics are still handled well, or at least not actively badly (we are working with a very low bar here, after all), but I think they also muddy the climate change allegory. The Knight Witches, the Link, and the propaganda campaign surrounding them were all very interesting ideas, but they don’t make a lot of sense when applied to the allegory. Climate activism isn’t a movement that relies a few heroic public figures; it’s a necessarily amorphous movement that relies on collective action. And by that I mean  action, not passively believing in the cause. I don’t think the writers  to say the solution to climate change is for slacktivists to send good vibes to Greta Thunberg and do nothing else, but it’s hard to see how else the Link is supposed to be applicable to climate change. I think the Link would make more sense for a traditional war narrative, which does have a strong separation between combatants and civilians that limits what the latter can do for the former. (That’s also a situation that’s more invested in the concept of heroism.)The climate change narrative itself is also muddied by effectively splitting itself into two separate but unrelated environmentalist narratives that are handled very differently from one another. The first, the planetwide disaster we see in the prologue, was the one I thought was done much better. The evil CEO is a pretty blatant allegory for Elon Musk and similar technofuturists who believe the solution to climate change is to do it all again on another planet, and though the heroes defeat him, the planet is still ruined, because killing the Big Bad doesn’t magically undo the harm they caused.Unless you’re Rayne, in which case it does. She punches out the Climate Change Monster, literally becomes God, and then uses her god powers to fix the environment.Is this an intractable problem of telling a climate change allegory through the medium of a video game? Maybe. I think fundamentally, a big part of why climate change is so hard to fight is because it not only can’t be fought through traditional means, but those means actually make it worse. The power fantasy that video games indulge, of constantly becoming bigger and better so you can destroy every obstacle in your way without concern for inconveniences like finite resources and collateral damage, is the same fantasy that is creating climate change in the first place. Capitalism’s desire for infinite growth is what got us into this mess; you can’t get us out by cleaving to the same principles.The unfortunate truth is that reversing climate change at this point is going to be very, very painful. Even if the obstacles to doing so were removed, shutting down the Machine is going to have consequences. It’s going to require us to give up most of our modern comforts — 24/7 electricity and internet, cheap plastics, cheap meat, international shipping, year-round access to produce. And for some people, those aren’t comforts but necessities — hospital patients need 24/7 electricity and many disability aids require plastic. If you smash the Machine, you smash those people too. Do you have an alternative source of care lined up to catch those people?  ignores this question. No one asks how everyone will survive without the Machine, least of all Rayne. You destroy the thing everyone needs to survive but it’s fine because a literal deus ex machina comes in to fix it.I believe for a video game to be an accurate allegory for climate change, it needs to be a fantasy of  rather than gain, of weakness rather than power. It should make us understand the fact that a sustainable future requires us to sacrifice things we take for granted. (And if it absolutely must have a Climate Change Monster, make it a puzzle boss that can’t be defeated through traditional combat, because you can’t put out a fire with gasoline.) A video game could, in fact, convey these things better than any other medium! But of course, such mechanics would by their very nature run contrary to the appeal of most video games, so we’re unlikely to see such a thing outside of the ghetto of weird art games played by like five people.I don’t want to fault the game too much, because this  really hard. I think it genuinely tried, and losing your powers in the final stretch (combined with forcing you to give up power if you want to do the right thing) is at least gesturing in the right direction. It does better than most of its contemporaries and does draw attention to some important issues. But our games really need to step up their game if they want to send a serious message about climate change.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a lot more fun than I thought it would be initially. I love roguelikes and metroidvanias, so I gave this one a shot. Many reviews say that there is a difficulty spike in the middle that is unfun or unfair, but I don't share that opinion. It's a bullet hell, and you can use your cunning to figure out the best way through it. Regarding bugs or game crashes, I had no issues at all.Cute music, art and story. The gameplay was surprisingly more engaging than I expected, and had me on the edge of my seat through a few of those fights. Would recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun game. The combination of metroidvania and bullet-hell shooter is a winner!Story isn't terribly original, but it works and the main character is great. I enjoyed the deck-building aspect much more than I expected to, and the in-game unlockable cheats made the 100% clean-up much more manageable than it would have been otherwise.On the other hand, the maps (and the game as a whole) are a bit too linear, with a limited fast-travel system. Also there's a looooot of dialogue to get through. A lot of it is either charming or funny, but it's still a bit too much.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Straight up, this game has enough good and great qualities for me to highly recommend to others. The artistic style is cute and the backgrounds are nicely detailed. The music is fitting for each moment throughout the game and never got on my nerves. The difficulty curve never reaches a point where the game was rage inducing which is saying a lot given the genre of bullet hell. At one point I planned on not achieving some specific achievements to avoid frustration but nothing was too difficult to achieve. I rate the game at a low/medium difficulty level.The bullet hell + metroidvania aspects of the game were well done making the gameplay and challenge factor fit into a sweet spot of fun without frustration. The game map isn't huge which prevents it from feeling cumbersome when backtracking but still has lots of things to discover and places to explore. They added all the right quality of life features to allow to game to flow nicely without the need for external help including indicators to let you know if you have found everything in a certain room and access to a board that will tell you how many of certain things there are left to locate.The story wasn't a masterful work of art but was absolutely perfect for the game setting and message it was trying to portray. It wasn't childish or cloying and instead focuses on some very relevant perceptive issues especially when dealing with blissful ignorance, blind leadership, and extreme hero worship. The main character is a perfect balance of positivity and emotional strength. The character wasn't over complicated and by the end of the game I actually became quite fond of her personality. I ended the game very satisfied with everything involved.Speaking of the ending, you will find you high level of difficulty towards the end but the game but it will not punish you for winning the game on your own terms. I will not elaborate. It was this fact alone that boosted my opinion and made me rate this game as a 10/10 on my scale of games. How do you accurately rate a game? Do you nitpick small details within a masterpiece or do you rate it in terms of enjoyability? This game is enjoyable for a wide demographic, hits a lot of the right notes, and leaves you feeling satisfied without remorse. That to me is a masterpiece of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: This game wasn't quite what I expected at first, but the concept grew on me and now it's one of my favorite recent games. It's a metroidvania and a shoot 'em up combined. This combination takes some getting used to, but I think they pulled it off! Be aware that you start out very week, but don't despair, after a short while you'll get plenty of opportunities to upgrade. You'll be a Knight Witch in no time!

_childDocuments_.review: Picked up Knight Witch on sale recently, and had a blast 100%'ing it. Is this game flawless? No, there could be some QoL updates like a faster traversal move speed, but after almost not getting it due to some reviews about difficulty or issues, I don't get what people are so negative about. Absolutely beautiful art and music, fun but challenging combat (picks up more later into the game when you have mana upgrades for using spells) and likeable characters, I would for sure recommend Knight Witch to any fans of the genre!
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Bangai-O in a Wizard HatVery challenging and novel combo of bullet hell and metrovania. Random spell cards create a core gameplay loop of juggling spell use and combat, and keeps the game from simply disintegrating into finding an overpowered combo and grinding out every boss fight. Various mechanics in the game encourage a sort of cyclic style of combat, such as having to get near enemies to pick up mana. The biggest problem is visibility of enemy bullets, as weapons like machine guns can blot out incoming fire, leading to damage feeling somewhat random. All and all a fun challenge and an interesting twist on a familiar genre.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice little game. It has great graphics, a neat story, and good gameplay. I greatly enjoyed it and have spent most of the last two days doing nothing but playing it. There are two issues that might mar your enjoyment however. The first is that spells are tied to cards which are played from a pool randomly. You get three at a time, and the way they show up kind of whenever is not really conducive to planning. The devs have stated that they did this to force you to adapt, but frankly the action is too frantic for me. I mostly spent my time dodging bullets and shooting with my main gun. With only the occasional use of spells when I recognized a good card.The second issue is the submarine level. It moves and shoot differently than the main character does in the rest of the game. In the normal parts this is not bad. They use the constraints to make some interesting puzzles in how to defeat the enemies and clear a room. But there are two arena battles with very tight quarters that were quite frustrating. The devs recomend using cheats if the difficulty needs adjustment. And you know what. It works. I played most of the game without cheats, but for the places where I died again and again I enabled them. And personally I found it greatly increased my enjoyment of the entire game to just not need to bang my head against a wall for hours. Now maybe the devs could have balanced the game better, and maybe they could have called them difficulty options instead of cheats, but on the whole I think they do actually make the game better. It would have been sad if I had been put off the entire game just because of a few fights that were too much.So yeah I enjoyed the game. It was fun with and had me searching out all the secrets and hidden tidbits of lore. I wouldn't recommend it to a hardcore bullet hell player. But for someone looking for a more casual game that is just fun to blast around in it's pretty good.

_childDocuments_.review: Giving a positive review because the game is undoubtedly well made. That said, it's also a game where your mileage may vary. Maybe some sort of a 'reimagined' edition?
