_childDocuments_.review: Got told about this in July, added it to my wishlist on the trailer alone, then bought it once it released at the end of November. Easily one of my better purchases of the year - a mix of  search-action and twin-stick bullet-hell shooters makes for a solid game, that could use a bit more polish on the technical side to  shine against the crowd![The Good]• Solid Art-styleColourful hand-drawn graphics all over the place gives the game a fun identity, and a good edge over a fair number of its pixel-art kin. And given how much I tend to laud games with solid pixel-art styles, I hope that gets across how good it looks. Characters and enemies are generally rather unique in how they're portrayed; made more amusing with how some enemies are using existing behaviour types, but get a living counterpart to the robotic or vice-versa.• Dynamic MusicFor a mix of genres in gameplay, a mix of genres in music makes sense - mostly folksy music with traditional instruments sit shoulder-to-shoulder with the occasional active-techno tune in a way that doesn't feel too out-of-place in the game setting. There's a good use of leitmotifs, and overall it aids the setting quite well.• GameplayBeing a Knight Witch sounds like you'd have a fair arsenal on-hand, and whilst that's true in the later game to account for the standard search-action fare of tools that expand exploration possibilities, to begin with you play purely as a caster. Permanent flight means progress is barred in more direct manners - a dash that lets you through thin walls, a hefty sword that lets you smack switches, and a cat that conducts electricity, or later on just some good ol' fashioned locked doors that require keys to open. Ignoring the standard keys, the tools have their uses in combat too - the dash gives invuln frames and can be spammed to give the idea that you're dodging well (though you CAN still get blindsided), the sword can deal hefty damage and destroys bullets, whilst the kitty acts as a focal point for most of your character's spells, allowing for a bit of strategy when dealing with tougher encounters. The spell-cards on offer can either affect your shot-type (allowing for multi-shot, rapid-fire, or hand-cannon with piercing but low fire-rate), help clear the arena of bullets or enemies, summon familiars or shields to aid in offence or defence, or can aid in further casting (shuffling cards, extra MP and so on)On the other side of the field, enemies are generally quite varied, and have a good number of methods of filling the screen with bullets to dodge. Whilst they're not so rude as to let off lasers of any type at the player, patterned shots, homing bullets and phase rounds are the order of the day for filling the field with fire.• Coherent StoryHaving generally not followed the game until the release (which I could say is an anti-hype measure, but is really more of "busy life distracts me"), I wasn't wholly sure what to get from the story from the outset. So I was fairly surprised to find out that things took an eco-friendly bent that highlights the horrors of war, the pitfalls of creating super-soldiers, the troubles inherent in fighting existing powers, and how the  enemy of a planet's well-being isn't humanity as a WHOLE, but rather  people trying to maintain status quo via politics and good PR. Though this over-arching plot doesn't stop the game from having its goofier moments that can come off as a bit cheesy, but help in keeping the tension down and having moments of calm or levity.[The Bad]• Loading TimesAs a game built in Unity, this game has its fair share of loading times to deal with. Usually not too noticeable unless you're rapidly flicking between regions searching for things. The gates between areas are spread out enough that in  gameplay it won't be a major bugbear, but might annoy if you're aiming to backtrack.• Technical WoesWhilst the music is good, the dynamic usage means that some tracks can fail to end or start properly. This can leave some scenes with the wrong tune, or in sullen silence; or it can have other tracks overlap each other in a way that can be rather grating. Achievements also seem to not be unlocking at times; the devs are aware of these issues, and the hope is that they can be patched out.  A patch dropped on 22/12/2022 that's fixed the achievement-unlocking issue. Music didn't seem to glitch out any more either; I'm going to keep the above here for the sake of posterity, but these two glitches can be considered fixed for the time being!• Fast-TravelMost search-action games will eventually have means of travelling quickly between zones, and have their own ways of doing so. The Knight Witch  have such a feature, though with the main hub connecting five major zones already, it takes its time in giving the player access to the ability. And unlike the Link that the game establishes as two-way quite often in the setting, this functionality is one-way - use a checkpoint to warp back to one of the five main hub points. This  help with map-clearance if you aim for 100%, but the delay in unlocking it feels like a downside in my mind.[The Muddled]• DifficultyThis one seems to be a major point for some people; either the Instinct "auto-aim" makes the game too easy (possibly a hyperbolic comment), or the balancing of some encounters is off, making some encounters far tougher than expected. Given my experience lies more in controlling a gravity-bound guy instead of a flying fella, I definitely felt the sting of some of the side-encounters. But most of the toughest encounters were off the beaten path, and either counted towards levelling the character, or boosting her HP/MP. Most of the encounters on the "main" path are generally quite manageable with the tools afforded to the player. However, 100% relies on clearing "ambushes" in a set time, or without taking damage. These can be troublesome, but aren't  with the right spells.[Closing]As a mix of two genres, if you're a fan of both you might find this game is right up your alley. Fans of one or the other might well be put off by the opposite genre, but with a free demo available it's easy to at least try the game to see if it's to your tastes.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a bullet hell Metroidvania by a Dev that only had one game before this, a puzzle bullet hell game in 2017.I saw it via a tweet and it looked cool so I dove into it. The gameplay is very fun and tight. You have your regular gun as a weapon and then also a spellcard deck.In this spellcard deck you can put differe tweapons that you can equip for a limited time or spells you can use in combat. You have a starter deck of cards but the cards you collect during your gameplay are obviously a lot better, but I still used some of the early ones until way late into the game.The story is fairly good, had a twist or two in the story that I actually didn't anticipate. The concept is that the Knight Witches get stronger by having a better "Link" to the townspeople, so by finding and rescuing them in the map you gain link and level up. There you can either make your gun or your spells better.A spellcard has a mana cost, if you use it the card gets discarded and a new one gets drawn from your deck. Most cards you can have two copies of them, except the Boss spells you get.The artwork is pretty cute and very fluid. There is a dog in it, and you can pet it. For an indie metroidvania like this it's actually longer than most, but I had quite a lot of fun. The last boss was actually quite challenging.Time spent: 12 hoursVerdict: 8.4/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: The Knight Witch is a very good bullet hell with medtroidvia style map exploration elements mixed in.Lets start with the good, overall presentation and art style is consistent and clean. You can look at the screen shots to determine if you will enjoy that aspect. Music is also really good and appropriate to the game play.On a technical level I never encountered any bugs and load times were minimal, however, despite exceeding the system spec but a fair margin there was considerable slow down when the number of projectiles on the screen was ridiculously high. This only happened in a few areas, this issue did not occur 99% of the time. Gameplay wise, The Knight Witch is going to appeal to bullet hell enthusiasts rather than metroidvania fans. You will be flying around the map shooting projectiles while dodging various attack pattern from enemies, the biggest addition to the bullet hell formula is the random spellcard system which is interesting and frustrating in equal measure. You will create a deck of spellcards with various effects, these cards are randomly draw and assigned to 3 buttons (I used a controller) the frustrating part is the random assignment, meaning you can't rely on muscle memory when using spellcards and getting the right one can mean the difference between a battle being a cake walk or a nightmare. Difficulty wise The Knight Witch would probably rate medium to hard with a few difficulty spikes along the way, changing up your card deck can drasticly alter the difficulty. There are plenty of upgrades along the way which make gameplay fairly dynamic and interesting.Story wise...... Your mileage may vary on this one, there are themes of environmentalism vs industrialisation and the effect of social media on society within a framework of a magical adventure. My personal opinion is that it was delivered in a fairly blunt fashion and did not do much to enhance my enjoyment of the game but this is one of those things that will differ with each player.Minor gripes that annoyed me but may not annoy others - The randomness of the spellcards will vastly affect the difficulty of the game, get the right card and even the final boss is pretty easy. Having to take my eye off my character to see what cards I have available got pretty frustrating at times. Additionally the spell effects are huge and the screen can get crowded very quickly, with enemy projectiles also being a variety of colours it can be difficult to see whats going on sometimes.- Ambushes - which are combat encounters which serve as difficulty spikes, they can be pretty challenging when first encountered and if you can finish them quickly and without taking damage then you will get a token, unfortunately you need 25 / 27 tokens to get the reward and you can only retry the ambushes once you have completed most of the game, this means you will be returning to the ambushes with completely overpowered spellcards in order to get 2 spells that you may not even use for the final boss fight.- Lacks a fast travel system between checkpoints, which meas a lot of back tracking and padded playtime.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is fine , the control is snappy and responsive , the art style is great , the soundtrack is amazing. it's tend to go bullet hell with a lot's of flashy things everywhere which often make it's easy to lose track of what's going on.it's not the visual hell of Beat hazard but it's still give you a very busy screens.the story is about a band of world saviour witch knights fighting some guy who built a whole army of robots , their confrontation end with everyone escaping in the last surviving city of the planet somewhere underground.you will be playing the role of Rayne , one of the witch knight that actually never took part in the war.Helping peoples around to make your magical link with them stronger as you fight your way around to uncover who is behind the new treath that has broken out after so many years of peace.you can collect cards to launch abilities , collect different powerup to have more life and mana on top of getting stronger via the link system.while the story is good both ending of the games kind of feel weird and lacking something to make the whole experience feel complete , maybe it's just me nitpicking but yeah , both endings kind of feel weak naratively speaking. Actually the ''bad'' ending make more sense in some way with the overall tone and theme of the game which is also weird.the other special thing about witch knight is that it's got cheats with very easy to figure out cheats code , even without looking online you can easily just take your mouse and try out all of the possible symbols combination rather quickly. this is an Interesting feature if you ever get completly stuck somewhere down the line or just want a casual experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially had this game on my list ready to play at launch. I was very intrigued by the idea of a shoot 'em up (I'll refer to this as shmup) metroidvania that also includes cards to sling from. From the trailer, and gameplay I would actually compare it to a mix of the binding of isaac AND one step from eden smashed into a metroidvania. Calling it a shmup is kind of generous unless you are willing to call the binding of isaac a shmup. It is definitely a bullet hell similar to how isaac can be a bullet hell. A lot of negative reviews say that the bullet hell element and enemies are hard to dodge which is just false if you have any 2-3 digit hours put into the binding of isaac. Any negative review that also says that they can't manage the card system and the bullet hell is also incorrect. One step from eden has a similar system and it is not an issue for that game which also has quick dodging sequences. The game is not that hard. A very, very, very new player in these two games MAY struggle, but the game also gives you a dash that also destroys projectiles at the end of the dash.If you are looking for more of a challenge, get 100% of achievements. I believe it is not (or maybe never) bugged anymore due to a recent patch and there are some difficult sections. (If it is still an issue, restart the game and load the most recent save, it will update the achievements.) One "challenge" had me beating my face into the screen for a couple of hours.One other note is the water level. I do not care about it at all. It is very easy and VERY cheesable so I don't understand the issue people have with that. You can only shoot right or left BUT your rate of fire is HEAVILY increased. I am also surprised there aren't more complaints about the area after the water level which can be seen as very long and difficult for the power level you are at. Now with the "disclaimer" out of the way I can get into the actual review.-Pros-Fantastic artworkFantastic musicStory is good and intriguingControl and in-combat movement feel really responsiveGood cards feel really good to useDeck can be constructed in multiple ways even though some are favorable over others.One for all difficulty encourages hard and easier sections to vary the pace of the game.-Cons-out-of-combat movement can be slow.Fast travel isn't unlocked until later into the game and it COULD be better.Final bosses are not too difficult with max upgradesmana upgrades include max deck size upgrades which can be controversal (I don't mind at all though I get to use more unique cards and redundancy LOL)LVL 19 and 20 upgrades are Clearly OP take it as you will but some cards become S tier to D tier or D to S because of these (specifically looking at the witch upgrade).This game is a fantastic short play of a story of the little engine that could. I love the characters and the in game choices that you must make to determine if more people trust you or not. It is a short play (about 9ish hours for non 100% and 11-13ish for 100%). I would highly reccommend if like deckbuilders and the binding of isaac/one step from eden. If you haven't played those two games before, I would recommend NOT playing this unless you are used to dodging in those two games. Just play hallow knight instead unless you don't like a long playthrough. 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a simple cute metroidvania + bullet hell and it's well enough integrated and fun. Even if you are not very good in bullet hells, this genre mix makes it decently accessible (though more intense than other genre mixes like Undertale, keep in mind). Just know the final boss for the best ending is such a difficulty escalation that you are probably going to give up frustrated and stick with a disappointing bad ending, if you ignore that it's a good time. It's pretty also, the story is kinda eh and its themes and choices are very clumsily handled, but it's cute enough to keep you around enough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: The Knight Witch is an awesome game. Great art and visuals. Super tight gameplay. The level design is original, interesting and full of really well thought environmental puzzles and navigation challenges. The story is super cute and interesting and it has some very unique and smart moments (like the press conference), I also love the way the narrative is connected to the gameplay, the dialogues are funny with a light humor tone and slightly meta. The sound design and music are excellent.The game is super well-finished, with high production values, and very much polished, haven't found any bugs myself. The difficulty and balancing are really on point. The way the magic cards work is pretty challenging to the player, as you have to be looking at which card is loaded on which button and strategize, I often press the wrong button. Some of the optional Ambushes are quite the challenge but it is always fair.I'm enjoying the game a lot and this is definitely one of the best indies of 2022 for me. Congratulations to the team at Super Mega Team. They did a truly amazing job.

_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable game.  Nice story/art/gameplay.  The card mechanic can be a bit hectic while dodging bullets, but made easier with upgrades and building a cohesive deck. One nasty difficulty spike several hours in where you are restricted and too many enemies in a cramped area.  After that spot, reasonable amount of difficulty for light bullet hell game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Pro: Graphics. Easily the high point in a game infested with lows.Cons: No custom map markers so backtracking to collect missed things becomes a huge chore.Health powerups are incredibly scarce.Your character moves at an aybsmal pace, once you unlock your dash ability you'll be mashing L1 just to get around faster.Bosses are extremely unforgiving, many of them cross the threshold from "challenging yet fair" to "this is outrageously unfair, the developers are punishing me for trying to have fun, I'm googling a cheese strategy." There's one boss in particular who has an ability that FILLS the screen with bullets, and you're getting hit by it, deal with it. Said boss spams it. (Skill issue incoming.)RNG powerup system. You assign powerups to a deck which shuffles as you use abilities. RNG can literally decide the outcome of your bullet-hell boss battles.Many of the powerups are hopelessly anemic and may as well not exist.Pass on this game unless the developers balance some of the boss encounters and address weak powerups.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimately, this game isn't bad, but it just didn't click with me.The art is great, the plot at least tries to be unique-ish, and the gameplay isn't bad.But... there are some slow-downs when too many bullets are on the screen, but you can't adjust the graphics settings to try to mitigate them. The deck building aspect did nothing for me (useless choices, not enough mana to use everything, etc.) Sometimes it feels like the enemy balance is off (simultaneously too hard and too easy, you can ignore all the enemies bullets for a bunch of rooms, until you can't). I'd either want it easier (so it feels like less of a time sink) or harder (so it feels like an actual bullet hell shmup). It even manages to have the obligatory terrible water level.I got to the end of the campaign and decided I didn't need to go back through to 100% all the challenges.It's not that it's a bad game, but if I were to tell someone to sink 20 hours into a metroidvania, this isn't the one I'd recommend. Play Hollow Knight or Ori first and then swing back here if you really can't do without yet another pretty metroidvania.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, it's got some decent attempt at stuff, but didn't know just what it wanted to be and focus enough on that, so the gameplay is kinda shoddy in areas, key areas, for the type of game it is normally something you expect very tight controls and visuals/feedback for, wich it lacks... and the story is... well not great, not bad, had potential. Execution could have been better.World exploration, ok on very first time to a room, but never great, and backtracking is absolute hell and miserable in this thing. And that's required for a good ending, or a lot of the useful stuff.Overall, multiple points I felt like I just wanted to stop playing, only pushed through because I'm a completionist and at least want to finish a game once I start it, even if not 100% when I don't like it much, and then the ending I got really ticked me off in the worst way. I really should have just quit while I was ahead...Core combat is more iffy and finicky to aim a shooter than most metroidvanias. It's like a twin stick shooter, but with spellcards, things that randomly are drawn you must look away from combat to know what is what on what buttons currently to properly use.Makes for finicky feeling combat where you never get into the flow enough, always stopping to look what you have, while hopefully not dying during that time.Also collisions are iffy, as a witch my feet don't seem to trigger most projectiles, but as a sub they hit me when still a few pixels away from my model. When you make a bullet hell you need to have clear rules on the player collisoin to see just how they must move, and where they can fit between. Give us a single pixel in the very center, or accurate to per pixel visual collisions, not whatever they heck they have here...Enemy projectiles, being a bullet hell, should stand out. As should your own character and any obstacles... shame that's far too often not the case. Sometimes enemy projectiles are things like little bubbles, barely visible from all the other glowing stuff, bubbles, or spare particle effects coming off of your own spells or the enviornment. Enviornmental art is also not great, it looks nice sure, but far to many cases I find a background item, that looks almost identical in shading or saturation to a foreground element... like in the underwater ice areas especially, so much I will bump into and not move not sure why I'm stuck here taking damage in a fight, then realize what my mind fazed out as background ice, after going past several similarly shaded art pieces before... was here a foreground one with collision.Overall, it just feels like they focused more on visual ideas first, and gameplay second, but for a tight bullet hell/twin stick shooter combo... you need good reliable and readable combat.Some bosses have moves like being able to teleport around before launching attacks, this unfortunately includes teleporting right on top of you... where you take damage. If you had just dodged another attack they left on the field, you can't try dodge the instant they teleport and you just get auto hit from what feels like RNG. Some clearly non satisfying moments in some designs like this. Can probably learn exact delays between boss actions to figure out when they would possibly do this, and thus when I need to avoid dodging in preperation from this... but with no visual tell from them beforehand counting down to it over many seconds, that's a lot extra to track in mind for a new boss fight, while already handling what feels like rather poorly refined combat drawing your attention to far to many different things like your random spellcards instead of just dodging or aiming at the enemy as it is.Or a boss where, upon dropping their health it locks out your controls, and after some dialogue the enemy has a phase change and moves to the center bottom of the arena... while you still aren't able to move your own character... he can damage you on overlapping you while doing this...The spell deck system is terribly designed. Once you add cards, you can't just remove them from slots, so no setting up only 2 cards total or anything, once you add all cards, you always must have that number. You also can't select a slot, and just swap its card for another slots card, and you can't unequip, so you must replace one slots card with a card not currently used, then go back to the one you wanted it in, swap it in there, then go back to the first, and add the one you just removed... all very slow and annoying, and limits options in how you can play.A level where you must dodge every few seconds of take auto damage, audio queue to remind you isn't audible over busier fights, the visuals you can't see as is often the case over your own or enemy spells, and the part it's bugged so sometimes when leaving a room, you'll just auto take a point of damage even if you just dodged right before entering the doorway... a very disliked level. that one.Exploration of the world is slow, and very boring, basic movement isn't fun or particularly engaging. So moving long distances to side objectives is... really slow and not fun. Teleporting between respawn points would be greatly appreciated at least for the later part of the game. It just wastes so much time... and unlike in some games, that time moving through the world isn't really enjoyable at all after maybe the first time into a new map tile.Ending, pretty damn ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Probably a better version, but with the world exploration being so boring and slow... and how bad it was to search for hidden bits, I didn't do enough to find the last bits of whatever was needed for the better ending even after wasting too many hours of my life just trying for that, and then it locks you into one that seems pretty crappy, like not just a bad ending, an unsatisfying one for the player.Also crashed and wouldn't close once when I tried to exit the game. Still, was for the most part ok performance and reliabiltiy wise... Once crash taht I could task manager force kill out of isn't too bad for that many hours these days.

_childDocuments_.review: It was initially hard for me to tell if this game was poorly balanced, or if I was just bad at it. Over time, frustration grew: the character has little mobility early-game, and the bullet hell elements are there right from the beginning. The deck element is certainly an interesting idea, and it mostly worked, but you can also easily back yourself into a corner with it, and outside of specific arenas/boss battles, it's typically less frustrating to just load your best weapon and some low-cost utility spells. With no way to discard cards (other than special cards later, which take up one of your card slots anyways and have downsides), you can easily be locked into 3 cards you can't use until you gather enough mana to fire one off unless you limit your high cost cards. If you find a combo that works for you, it's deeply satisfying to clear out enemies, but oftentimes FINDING that combo was a core, and hit-or-miss whether I'd be able to actually execute it. Hint: prioritize the weapons that can shoot through walls.The metroidvania elements were fun to me, even (especially, for me) the backtracking. Brought back memories playing Metroid: Zero Mission, zigzagging around the map and  powerbombing every room to find everything. However, if you're used to multiple warps, you're going to be disappointed: eventually, you can warp back to the start from any save room, but you always warp into the start. I spent almost the entire game waiting for an upgrade that let me go into the water without the sub, and it never came: the sub sections are by far the most frustrating and tedious part of the game to me. At least the sub shoots and moves faster, but it doesn't make up for the lack of aiming or dash.The level up mechanic revolves around building links (exp) to raise your Link Level, with a choice of one of two rewards every level. You're not locked out of rewards, provided you level enough; there are 20 levels and 20 rewards, so this gives a bit of flexibility of build while not missing out on anything. There are press releases let you lie to raise your link substantially but sow distrust later on, or tell the truth to raise it little to none and frighten people now, but garner trust in the long run. I have the same problem with this that I did for the system in Fable 3 - there's practically no downside to doing the "good" thing, since you can immediately pay money to garner both rewards, and money is incredibly abundant. There is no practical reason to lie. I really wish games with this sort of choice would make the good option meaningfully harder, since otherwise there's no reason to be evil other than window dressing. The only thing that is meaningfully harder if you lie is the end gauntlet before the boss, which I appreciate but again wish they went farther.The art is beautiful, consistent, and doesn't distract from the gameplay - overlapping bullets nonwithstanding, that's sorta just a staple of the shmup/bullet hell genre, unfortunately.I actually liked the story and writing quite a bit. It can be boiled down to "corporations exploit the public via media and it's harmful for everyone" with a heaping helping of "friendship is literally magic." It's a bit heavy-handed, but not in a condescending way, just in the "we only have text and 1-4 facial expressions to get this concept across" way. I appreciated that much of the make certain characters more sympathetic without excusing their actions, except for [SPOILERS]. ♥♥♥♥ that guy, actually. I also appreciate that no matter what, the main character is allowed to stick to her morals of not killing anyone.The two endings both being hopeful is also nice. No matter your choices or actions, people pull together to try to keep going. The choices are essentially .During the press release segments, the PR agent has very obvious goals in getting you to lie, and your character has pretty strong reasons of her own not to, but can be convinced - either choice feels in-character and it's really down to your personal playstyle and/or morals. I appreciate that it's not "give free candy to everyone, or kick a puppy." There are pretty compelling reasons to lie, both for personal profit and to prevent panic, and a few times in my first playthough I went "hmmm there are kids watching these mid-day press releases, we REALLY shouldn't be talking about this on-air" and chose to lie.The cheats are fun, and they don't lock out achievements! They really should be unlocked from the start and called what they really are, tho: accessibility options. In particular, slowing down the bullets and/or making enemies drop health stopped me from quitting and never coming back - the early game is  in its difficulty swings.I'm aware that this is personal, and also very petty, but if this were rated on a 10 star system, I would take off a solid 2 stars for the unskippable, un-fast-forward-able credits that pause if you alt-tab out. Horrendous. Also, there's lyrics to the main theme over the credits, but sung very indistinctly and there's no captions, so I couldn't tell what they said other than the chorus of "here she comes( ??? maybe) our Knight Witch."

_childDocuments_.review: To the point===========================A cute, bubbly and strange game with some truly awful balancing issuesGood Stuff==========================- I appreciate the less explore gameplay types and this is one of them. It's a psuedo exploration/ psuedo bullet-hell game and I've never quite played anything like it before. I'd look forward to seeing alot of the bad stuff refined in a sequel.- Shockingly, the story is pretty good for this game. It's simple, but there's a good amount of twists to keep it fresh for the short runtime of the game (5-10 hours)- The general controls are fine one you unlock dashing and there is both an auto-aim and manual aim feature to fit your preferred playstyle.Bad Stuff============================- The biggest issue with this one is the balance. The game does a poor job and your character shoots too slowly and does too little damage for the raw amount of enemies and bullets they are throwing out at you. Even with an end game spell deck normal enemies take forever to kill making the fights extremely unenjoyable.- The spell deck is a cool idea but simply doesn't work well. I'm sure there are 1 or 2 combos that are great but mostly it's "buff your normal shot" because the special abilities are really pathetic with some truly awful damage output.- This game so desperately wants to be a bullet hell game but the thing about those games is your hitbox is like one pixel and you are encouraged to dodge between bullets. Your hitbox is this game is like 2 refridgerators wide and you take a lot of cheap shots you should be able to dodge through.- You can only heal at save points or using specific health crates. This makes long fights and certain bosses needlessly difficult.- The ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ last boss, my god he's the balance and health problem rolled into 1. You do microscopic damage while he throws ever bullet under the sun at you. All while you can take roughly 6 hits from him. I was able to get to his THIRD health bar before I called it quits. Way way WAY overtuned.- This game is sold as a metroidvania. It is not. It's a series of levels that you teleport to with minimal exploration.- You only level up during very specific events like freeing prisoners you find in the map which makes the process annoying when you're trying to increase your level.-There's a minigame where you can tell the truth for a little experience or lie for a ton of experience. The EXP you lose for telling the truth can be bought with in game currency and it doesn't seem to effect anything so why even bother telling the truth and save some money?

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun idea that blends bullet-hell with metroid-like. It looks cute, the art is clean, and the game plays well.One of the best things I liked was that it leaned more on the metroid side of things: exploration, movement, and discovery-based progression were the focus, with each room feeling unique. I much prefer that over the vania: focus on grinding, combat, levels, grinding, random item drops, grinding, cut-and-paste rooms, grinding. Oh, and did I mention the grinding? Yeah, I hate that. And unfortunately for me, many, MANY metroidvanias love to focus on the vania and think that players' time is well spent by moving back and forth between a few rooms, repeatedly beating on some poor sap a couple hundred times for exp and item drops. Thankfully, The Knight Witch doesn't focus on that aspect! All your "levels" and upgrades are gained by finding things. And you'll likely have more than enough game currency to buy anything you need without intentional grind.I felt in full control of the character while playing, which shouldn't be a thing I should have to praise a game for, but unfortunately many metroidvanias out there like to have stiff controls and horrible animation locks. The Knight Witch, however, is quite friendly with animation cancelling and freedom of movement/action. This feels wonderful as a player, and it also helps to remind you that if you messed up, it was completely on you. No blaming the bad controls like you can on other games!Now onto some gripes. The story was very predictable and many of the characters act bafflingly dense. The message was fine, but I would have preferred not to have been talked down to so much, or for the characters to be so frustratingly oblivious, just to get the point across.Gameplay-wise, my biggest issue was how useless the Knight levels/upgrades were. The game seems designed to make full use of the Witch aspect, and definitely requires that you use the spell cards to do anything as you progress later in the game. The Knight upgrades sound good on paper, but in practice simply can't keep up with the enemies and so they feel like a complete waste.Overall, I had a good time and wouldn't mind more of this style of game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gunna stsrt this off by saying this is not a metroidvania game. It doesn't feel or play like one. It's a purely bullet hell game with abilities, and the only way the game makes that difficult is by making fight areas laughbly small and enimies bullet sponges. There is no creativity in the game mechanics at all. Armor is a one off item you have to buy(and instantly use). And hardly helps with the games mechanics. You're better off equpiing the defense spells you get, theyre fsr more worth it due to being able to use it when you want(if the card is available).I don't know who's idea it was to give me a dodge mechanic in the game only to not allow me to use it in the next level along with taking away the 360 firing range for most of the level.With all that said, the game looks neat. _childDocuments_.review: Obligatory "I don't usually review games but..."This is a great little game for people like myself who enjoy both the typical metroidvania formula and the gameplay offered by typical twin-stick shooter/bullet hell games. I'm not leaving this review because it's one of the best games I've ever played, but because I think most of the negative reviews are pretty unfair, with most commenting on some combination of the randomized spell-card system or the "overall execution" of many different concepts. Anyone who gives a genuine gripe about the spell card system is insane and should not be taken seriously. You have available slots for cards you can cast chosen from a "deck" that you can customize with unlocked cards - though this will usually just boil down to jamming a bunch of blanks/bullet cleansers that you'll be holding onto while your other slots will let you comfortably cycle through whatever the strongest damaging spells or bullet augments are that you have available at the time. A lot of people really overthink this concept because most bullet hell games only give you 1-2 blanks/spells and that's it, and while giving the player a lot more variety can get somewhat confusing, you're playing this game because you like twin stick shooter/bullet hell gameplay. Literally just jam your deck full of blanks/bullet augment spells and I cannot see how this aspect is a genuine complaint.Many of the negative reviews commenting on the execution are also either overly-critical or borderline insane. This is a pretty simple and honest game all things considered - if you like bullet hells and metroidvanias you will most likely enjoy this game. If you don't, then the game makes its direction pretty clear within the first hour so if by that time you find that it isn't for you then take the justified refund. If you don't enjoy an imperfect indie game made for a niche audience, that doesn't really indicate anything about the game's execution - and if you aren't in the target audience then you may be even less qualified to comment on how well or unwell the game achieved the presented concept with its execution....As for any reviews negatively mentioning the underwater/submarine area, those are pretty justified. My favorite thing about The Knight Witch has been how fluid the movement feels, and this area heavily restricts both your movement and your ability to even interact with the enemies around you by confining the angles at which you can shoot. Relative to the rest of the game this area won't take up a lot of your time, and for me once I'd finally finished this section it was what made me genuinely appreciate how great the default moving and shooting feels even while having to often navigate the tight corners and corridors of the game's metroidvania half.If you're a fan of these genres I would heavily recommend giving this game a try. The characters are pretty great and the story is fairly solid with some wonderful moments. It's not a perfect game by any means but it definitely delivers on what it offers and I believe does so very well, especially for those who thoroughly enjoy both metroidvania and bullet hell genres.

_childDocuments_.review: It's OK. Overall the design of the 'game' part of the game is lacking.  Enemies will shoot at you from offscreen, while your own projectiles have laughably short range. _childDocuments_.review: The Knight Witch doesn't blow me away, but I don't think it's bad. It certainly deserves better than the negative reviews it's getting, which is why I'm giving the thumbs up. At the time of review, I've played 19 hours and unlocked all achievements. Main points:1. Art: The art is beautiful and the main theme music is great. 2. Gameplay: Gameplay tries to mash together deckbuilder and bullet hell genres, and it does so competently. It fails to feel compelling or exhilarating, but it's more than functional.3. Fast travel: There is no fast travel except for a limited method in late game. Worth mentioning since it's an immediate turn-off for some players. Retreading ground can feel a bit monotonous, but it's not a long game and dashing through saves enough time.4. Story/writing/characters: The writing is boring and feels like it's pulling punches. There are plot points, characters, and moments all set up with plenty of impact potential, but the delivery fails every time. It makes sense if the game was targeting a very young audience, but the difficulty doesn't align too well for such a young demographic. That said...Addressing some common points in other reviews:1. RE: Difficulty: It's not hard. I'm baffled by the reviews that talk about how hard it is / the intense difficulty curve. Those reviews almost put me off from buying the game. With those reviews in mind, I was carefully paying attention from the moment I started the game to notice the "difficulty spike." It never came, and I eventually wrote it off. 2: RE: Genre blending: I see a lot of complaints about the card HUD being unwieldy considering attention needs to stay on your character in a bullet hell game. Again, I prepared myself for the struggle... and found none. Your deck ranges from 5-9 (or so) cards over the course of the game. Your deck likely has duplicates if you have a basic knowledge of deckbuilding. The art design of the cards is distinct and easily recognizable from other card art, except in a few fringe cases. Even then, once you find your favorite cards, you'll know easily at a glance which is witch (sorry). Yes, it's smart to pick your moments to glance carefully, but that ties in character positioning and tactics. This isn't Ikaruga, you can safely blink.There are other pros and cons, and more disagreements I have with some negative reviews, but they're minor and varied. If you've read this far and you're still not sure, give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: From unskippable and uninspiring story segments to gameplay mechanics that feel disjointed, this game struggles to find its audience.The most glaring issue is the inundation of constant cutscenes and dialogue-heavy interactions that interrupt gameplay flow. Every character, including the protagonist who seems to converse with themselves frequently, contributes to a narrative that may appeal more to a younger, patient audience rather than those seeking more action-oriented gameplay.The primary attack auto-aims and constantly fires when a button is held down, a feature that feels unnecessary given the context of modern gaming where automatic actions could activate upon enemy proximity. Alternatively, the player can manually aim for extra damage. Additionally, when encountering doors and obstacles that require multiple hits to destroy introduces annoying delays and disrupts exploration.Spell cards, touted as a unique gameplay feature, fail to justify their inclusion. These cards, used to build a deck and perform special actions such as stunning enemies or deploying shields, often prove irrelevant or impractical due to high mana costs or situational appropriateness. This system adds unnecessary complexity without adding significant value compared to traditional spellcasting mechanics.Visually, "The Knight Witch" opts for a cutesy, child-like art style characterized by rounded, bubbly designs. While there's nothing inherently wrong with this aesthetic choice, it may not resonate with all players, particularly those seeking more mature or diverse character designs.Furthermore, the world feels disproportionately large compared to the protagonist's slow movement speed, exacerbating the sense of tedium during exploration segments.In conclusion, "The Knight Witch" struggles to find its footing amidst a myriad of design flaws and thematic missteps. While its colorful world and magical premise may attract a specific demographic, the game's inability to streamline its narrative pacing, gameplay mechanics, and visual style limits its appeal to a broader audience.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a shmup metroidvania with card combat which fails at all three of those things.The core combat is incredibly rough due to a hitbox the size of the moon and too many things on screen, the exploration is boring because of the slow movement speed and uninspiring rewards, and the card combat falls apart by having to focus on cards while navigating the shmup combat. Most of the cards are really bad too!The dialogue is dreadful, most of the characters are incredibly annoying, the checkpoints are bad, the difficulty frequently spikes, but the submarine bit is not as bad as everyone else seems to think.It's a real shame because it feels like it's  close to being good. _childDocuments_.review: This game is very pretty, the story is an interesting inversion of the usual damsel in distress story, and the beat-by-beat gameplay is fun.However, it's infuriatingly difficult.  I made it through Elden Ring just fine, I finished Dungeons of Dredmor in hardcore mode, but this game turns from a shooter into a bullet hell halfway through.  Worse, it does so without giving you the benefit of a tiny little hitbox like other games in that genre.  You also don't get any reliable defensive tools.  Your main defense is positioning, and everything else is card-based.  You only get to use cards by spending mana, which you earn irregularly by defeating foes, so cards become a "win more" mechanic that won't stop you from getting steamrolled.For me this is just too difficult to recommend to others.  I had fun with the early portion of the game, but was overwhelmed with frustration and went on to play other things before I could see how the story ended.

Some of the Narrative elements also feels strange.... there are various points in the story where you are interviewed  and you can lie to gain more link and get more powerful more quickly or you can tell the truth and gain no link and no real benefit.... while story line wise it's nice to have the option, as far as I can tell there is no penalty for lying to everyone and getting more link, as you link gets taken away near the end of the game regardless of which path you chose. There is also an option to boost the save points to also grant you armor, and again for storyline reasons you later learn that this is actually doing more harm than good and you have the option to cleanse the save points removing the armor buff, but again as far as I can tell there is no real benefit for doing so other that being the good guy in the story, said armor also doesn't add to the max total of armor you can get by the way, and if a shop upgrade would normally grant you 3 armor, it brings your total up to 3 essentially rendering the process pretty pointless to begin with. _childDocuments_.review: I usually don't leave reviews before I finish a game but The Knight Witch just came out yesterday and I wanted to help it stand out in some way by leaving a positive review. I only have about 3 hours in it thus far but the passion on display has already shone through. The game is incredibly atmospheric, the vibrant level designs paired with a beautiful soundtrack. The game may be somewhat difficult for those who aren't seasoned in bullet hells yet (e.g. Myself), but it falls into that "tough-but-fair" range where you may struggle at first but can also feel yourself improve as you adapt to the combat system. For those who have played Neon Abyss, another excellent title published by Team17, the combat feels very reminiscent of Neon Abyss with the flight mechanic you obtain from certain power-ups active throughout the game's entire duration. It's both familiar and new to me in multiple ways, and I am enjoying myself immensely.The only complaint I have is that I do wish there was a slider to turn down the mouse sensitivity, the default mouse sensitivity makes the cursor somewhat slippery and it's fairly easy to hit the edge of the screen mid-combat which is a bit of an annoyance. That aside though The Knight Witch thus far is a very strong labor of love from an indie studio that deserves recognition for what they've made here. The combat is refreshing, the game looks, sounds and runs beautifully, a lot of the characters are charming, the outlook on this one is incredibly good overall. I'm loving it so far and I hope you will too.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like shoot-em-ups?  Do you like Metroidvanias?  If so, this game is definitely worth your time.  It combines the two genres surprisingly well and also adds in some deckbuilding elements for good measure.  If you're  a fan of both genres, it's a bit more iffy, but it's still worth a look just to appreciate the creativity involved here.- The graphics are absolutely gorgeous; every screenshot is a painting.  Despite the lush graphics, it's also designed well enough that it's easy to track enemies and their bullets separately from your bullets and the background.- The music's beautiful, too.  I've still got a few tunes stuck in my head.- It's tough!  It knows it's a shmup, and there are some battles that probably took me ten or more tries to beat when I first encountered them.- The story is surprisingly interesting and well-told, too; on its surface it seems like it's the very embodiment of "technology bad, nature good" tropes, but without spoiling anything, there's a lot more depth to it than that, and it's  a commentary on the power of propaganda and how it can shape our view of history.- The deck-building elements add a lot of unnecessary randomness, and in difficult fights, sometimes it feels like you lost just because you got unlucky rather than you were lacking in skill.  This is less of an issue later in the game when you have enough cards that you can fine-tune your deck to reduce RNG and eliminate bad cards, but early on, it's frustrating.- Metroidvania elements are really rather light; areas are all separate from each other and self-contained, each of them has a relatively linear path through them with a few side paths to explore, and there's no fast travel (at least, nothing that is functionally useful for the majority of the game).- The submarine.  There are a few segments where you have to pilot a "submarine" that is basically identical to your character except lacking multiple abilities you previously had.  This just isn't fun.  These segments are really a pretty small part of the game overall, but they come early enough that they'll be a stumbling block for some people.

_childDocuments_.review: Would give a 'Mixed Review' if I could. Bought at 80% off and still ended up requesting a refund- normally I wouldn't considering the $5 I paid for it and its serviceable but in this economy even $5 is tight.This game is a strange mix. On one hand, the environments and art design are top-notch; the creators clearly have a very talented design team with a ton of passion, and art direction just exudes this (especially the environment). At the same time though, they use the wonky Dragonbone-style animation for their sprites that ends up looking really goofy and making this otherwise charming character art look like a cheap mobile game just from the animation alone. It's honestly a real damn shame.Gameplay is similarly a mixed bag. The initial concept here seems like a banger- Metroidvania Twin-Stick shooter? Sign me up. Unfortunately the execution here feels like it could have used some more polish. Character movement feels a tad too slow, especially when you start dealing with the mass of bullets you're dealing with. Thankfully your standard attack is auto aiming so you can concentrate a bit more on your placement than attacking back, though it takes a bit out of the engagements. The addition of a slight RNG-based 'spell deck' you use for special attacks seems innovative at first, but ends up feeling like more of an annoyance (at least, it does early on). I'm not sure if the issue with movement is solved later on admittedly, since I only played about an hour before getting tired of the game and trying to see past its issues. Continuing with issues: I'm not sure who this game was for- I think that might be the crux of it. I'm a Schmup and Metroidvania fan, but the developer didn't really capture what makes either genre magical- at least in my opinion. The bright presentation and cartoon aesthetic, combined with some very sugary-sweet writing, makes the game feel like it was directed towards a younger audience, yet the difficulty actually feels like this would be too hard for most kids (but maybe that's just my old and frail millenial senses failing me). I don't want to focus too hard on the story and presentation with this review, but the introduction to the core themes at the start definitely felt heavy-handed and about as subtle as a brick to the face. I usually have a high tolerance to this sort of story telling but I found myself groaning and skimming the dialogue a lot.Overall, I do think Super Mega Team has something on their hands here- their team clearly has an immense amount of talent and they should be proud of the work they've done here, I just think that there could have been some more work put into polishing the gameplay experience and storytelling (and maybe some hand-drawn animation wouldn't hurt?). I'll keep an eye on this team for their next game to see if they improve on their future projects, and if you're the type of person who prefers a slower and more methodical schmup experience you might just enjoy it, but personally, I'll pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably my own fault, but when I bought this I expected more or less normal metroidvania.Turns out, this is a mashup of genres - its a bit of a bullet-hell shootem up + metroidvania, with an interesting dash of card decks added: your cards are your spells, and you set yourself up with a tiny deck (out of all cards you own), from which you then draw cards to cast your spells.Difficulty ramps up pretty fast, which is surprising but not unwanted - it feels nice once you realize its not necessarily your movement and shooting skills that are the cause of your downfall, but the way you set up and use your spells.If there's one thing I'd dislike, its sometimes too much of a dialogue. Its not game's fault, its me - there's lore in there, but in a game like this, I just want to go around and shoot things, I don't care necessarily WHY am I shooting at them.All in all - highly recommended. _childDocuments_.review: I really really enjoyed the knight witch. Very good game if you like bullet-hells. The game wants you to feel outmatched in brute strength but capable with wit. There is also talk about unfair situations when in combat (no way of dodging an attack due to sheer amount of bullets on screen). I felt that most of the time that occurred was because it was my fault as a player. There were, of course, moments where you would look at the screen and say that the game hates you for how much is coming your way. I feel as though moments like that are inevitable in bullet-hells. The only times I felt immensely was unfair was Mirror Lake due to its unique combat scheme. The uniqueness was cool; however, it created moments inescapable attacks. That or I could just be bad at the game. Overall, I enjoyed the knight witch enough to 100% in game. I highly recommend you pick this up if you like artistic games and unforgiving bullet-hells

_childDocuments_.review: A great, challenging game with a few questionable game design decisions that can easily frustrate players who were expecting a more casual experience.I loved the game and got every achievement, but my gripes are like everyone else’s:1. Spell cards are cool but their system doesn’t work. Light randomization can keep things interesting, but glancing down costs fractions of a second that can mean death in a bullet hell.2. Difficulty spikes are large and early. Stage 2 ends up being a more arduous journey than 3 or 4. 3. Essential mechanics are hidden from the player. For instance, you CAN in fact see collectibles on the map, but you have to collect/spend a certain amount of the main collectible currency before this is unlocked. As another example, two other collectible types are never defined or seen until you receive one, so it’s theoretically possible to reach the end of the game without knowing they exist.4. The final boss is difficult in a way that punishes you for not obtaining 100% completion in the game. Once you’re there, you can’t go back to gain more upgrades without getting the “okay” ending first. I was personally worried that I’d have to start the game over if I did that, so I managed the boss with the one 6-mana spell I had (which drops the game’s fps to single digits when placed next to the final boss). HOWEVER, after you beat the game, you can load the file and it will put you right before the final sequence, which is nice. But I wish I would’ve been told that earlier!

_childDocuments_.review: The good: -Different that your average metroidvania, the fusion between bullet hell and metroidvania works well.-No performance issues.-Interesting graphical design.-Easy to play, hard to master.-You can collect different cards, each one with a different ability. You can equip several of them , but they will be "shuffled" each time, so you won't get the cards you want in the order you want them(when you spend one, you get the next , and so on). SInce you can use them as many times as you want, I think this mecanic is pretty interesting to balance things out so you don't get your most powerful weapons every time.-There's several secondary characters and although most of them are basic, some of them are actually interesting, like the knight witches or the main character's husband.The bad:-The plot, although starts interesting ends up being pretty generic by the end.-You are supposed to take certain decissions that imrpove(or not) your power, depending if you choose to tell the truth or not. The mecanic seems interesting unitl you realize that you can gain favor back  by spending shards...so it's basically useless.-The difficulty , although easier that most bullet hells , might be difficult for someone used to you classic 2d action adventure metroidvania.-I've missed a melee attack. There's one but it's not that useful.-It could use more fast travel points.-Since the way you move is by flying, there's no platorming . The game tries to compensatee this by having you move through paths with obstacles, but there's not that many of them and they are not the best: it's clear that this was not the focus of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Although not necessarily a standout in the genre, I feel like The Knight Witch brings enough to the table to be remembered, and thats already a feat considering how crowded the 2d platformer / metroidvania genre is, and the fact that this game doesn't even feel like neither of the two. Bullet hell based combat feels very nice to play. The design decisions made to make auto-aim and manual aim work together are outstanding, and that already makes it a good game pretty much, given thats it's main thing.The card system feels more gimmicky than anything, but still plays out fine. They could've just gone for a skill selector but instead put some time into balancing a card system, and I appreciate that, even if the result is average.Level design is also average, some rooms play out really nicely, while others feels too crammed or too large. Backtracking is pretty minimal inside each zone, but there's enough of "you clearly don't have the skill/item to get here yet" to be considered a metroidvania; anyone complaining about this, is just too much of a purist imo. Lastly, the artstyle, characters, and overally vibe of the game is waaaay above average for the genre. Characters are charming and likeable, dialogues are great, and the game just looks nice. Add that to an also pretty great plot, and even if the gameplay and core mechanics are not incredible, I still feel like its a winning combination.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Good game with nice art. I really enjoyed the story and most of the game play. I found the story to be pretty unique overall and while it has some common tropes I've never seen them done in this way before and was pretty refreshing. I very much liked the relationship between the main character and her husband and it felt like real love and a happy couple which was nice compared to how other games can portray it. Definitely has some flaws but nothing that caused too much frustration. The biggest issue is your spells in your deck are randomly assigned to 1 of 3 buttons as they get pulled. This owuldnt be a big deal if this wasnt a bullet hell, where glancing at your spells can cause you to get hit. I also would have appreciated a fast travel system around the end of a game for easier clean up of 100%. Most of the fights felt overall fair though there were a few spikes in diffculty here and there. The devs included easy to access cheats you can turn on and off if you're having difficulty. I wound up using the infinite mana cheat at the very end of the game due to your mana not replenishing after retrying challenge rooms and not wanting to constantly go back to a save to refresh.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: A hybrid of a Metroidvania that I did not expect to come across and honestly not bad for a first.  Some improvements can definitely be made to the combat, but overall, I'm very satisfied with what's given. It was somewhat of a challenge to get used to and fun to test my limits.Now others have claimed the story to be bland.  While I sort of disagree with them, I do find that the atmosphere and the mood did not match at all, it felt nothing like I imagined it should at any given point in the game, at least until I started marching into endgame.  I'd say I have more good points than ehh points.  But I can't say I have any nope points for this game.  The music totally smashes my dishes.   I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting blend of the shmup and metroidvania genres. The art style is very charming, and the story takes some interesting turns when discussing concepts like propaganda and media narratives. The bullet hell-dodging gameplay is generally strong, too, although it can get extremely difficult by the end. Some parts are kind of awkward, like how your attention needs to be split between multiple parts of the screen for the (very small) ammo indicator and to see what spell cards you have access to, making dodging even more frantic. But I do still recommend it, even if you end up needing to use one of the cheat codes to finish the final boss.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing it, I'm kinda baffled by the reviews most people seem to leave. This was a really nice game, and it does exactly what it says on the tin: Metroidvania with bullet hell mechanics. The free-flight movement somewhat gave me the same feeling as old classic indie game Aquaria, and the difficulty wasn't too crazy even for someone with medium-low experience with shmups.I really liked the water level, surprisingly. I thought it added a very interesting twist on the mechanics. The big weak point though, as others have said, was the backtracking. 90% of it is optional so I think if you just want to get through the game you won't notice it much, but if you care about completion/exploration, you will definitely feel it. I was waiting for a movement speed upgrade, but that never came. My advice is, only go for optional stuff once you have all abilities (one for each trigger/shoulder button) and you'll have a much smoother experience.Thoroughly recommend it for people who want a metroidvania with a different flavour still!
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun game, flying around blasting things is great. It's an excellent combination of shmup and metroid, with lots to find and some cool areas. I wish the basic gun was stronger early on to not make some of the enemies feel like such sponges, but by the time you've explored and gotten some upgrades it's fine.The story feels wasted, it has some cool concepts like the idea of literally growing stronger via media presence. But then it feels like it has very little to actually say about its ideas and it doesn't end in a satisfying note. The boss is great, but the emotion isn't there.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game but not easy, the most difficult parts are mostly in the optional sections though that's also where the good gear is to make the game easier. Personally I felt like the game play was great, really unique spin on the genre though definitely had moments where I needed to take a break. There's so much variety in the different spells and mechanics that I never got bored of exploring and looking for secrets. Story was also really nice, it's follows some tropes but spices them up enough that it still feels unique. The twists might be somewhat easy to guess but I still enjoyed them. Easily one of the best parts of the story was the main character, it's hard to put into words but its really refreshing to have a good guy protagonist that doesn't let others push them around or will actually call out people when they're being bad. I think the worst part of the game was how difficult it would get. Sometimes it really felt like pure luck, though I'm not a bullet hell player so it might be a skill issue. Eventually I got my hands on a certain card that made the game a lot easier but that was way later in the game.It seems to go on sale but either way it's definitely worth a try if you like Metroidvanias
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of fun, went with a full magic build to start and was later forced to get some gun/health upgrades which made the game easier. Overall the idea of cards and bullet hell is a bit frenetic, almost too hard to play the cards while dodging, one sub ambush took me like 4 hours to beat. The rest of the ambushes however have taken no more than an hour at the worst and most often less than 30.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: A twin-stick shooter that is also a metroidvania is not something that you see every day so this game is worth playing on that premise alone. However, there are a few areas that could use significant improvement.Your spells are essential to success but your spells come from a deck of cards so there is a medium RNG component. The biggest problem is that any of your 3 card slots can roll any type of card (offense / defense / misc). You often don't have time to see what card you just drew because you are currently navigating a bullethell. This system would be way better for the player if each card slot was dedicated to a specific type of card (e.g. "x" hotkey will always be an offense card / "y" hotkey will always be a defense card).The story of this game is an analogue of the kids TV show  with a few modifications. I put spoiler tags because the name of the show would spoil 70% of the story of this game. Names and places sound like they were made up on the spot with 20 seconds of thought put into each one (ex: Dungeonidas).A character at some point tells you they aren't a bad person because they haven't actually killed anyone. However, if you watch the background in one of the earliest game areas, you can see a train fall off its tracks plummeting into oblivion while you hear a faint screamtrack playing in the background. Somebody in the art department didn't keep pace with the person in the story-telling department or vice-versa lol.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: An occasionally tricky bullet hell metroidvania with lovely visuals and a story more complicated than the original premise suggests. Veterans of bullet hells probably won't be too challenged and for everyone else you can overcome the difficulty with intelligent spell selection and other enhancements. Definitely more of a combat focused game, but the 6 or so main areas were fun to explore and offered a bunch of unique environments that each complicated the business of exploding robots.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: I would call this game a Action Adventure Bullet-hell Metroidvania, is that a bad thing? Well I thought it was at first, but man was I wrong. This game is amazing.The dialogue is really cheesy but also funny, I had so much fun with all the dialogues in this game that I stopped and "rested" just to see if I could get a new response.I also find it really nice to see the lovey dovey dynamic with the protagonist and her husband, was a nice touch, you don't really see that in games.My only nitpick is that it feels so much better to go "Knight" instead of "Witch" bullets are just so much more solid. but it would be fun to try a new run and try a full witch build, since i definitely can see it being fun and working, but not as good.But I don't see myself playing the game again to be honest, the game feels like a one time experience and you're done.To sum it up.Fun game straight from start to end. Extremely charming.

_childDocuments_.review: ✦ Summary ✦= Multi-genre game (twin-stick bullet hell, Metroidvania, spellcard deck building)= Story about environmental issues intertwined with influencer culture+ Gameplay aspects connect well, with a variety of foes, environments, spell cards, and upgrades- Slightly rough around the edges--- Occasional difficulty spikes--- Some backtracking issues--- Makes up for this with unlocks to track and collect things--- Other minor issue: Game mutes on alt-tab (fixable with Special K)+ Natural, dynamic worldbuilding and characters+ Well-detailed, atmospheric art style+ Fun music that fits every environment+ Highly recommended for its effective arrangement of themes and gameplay✦ Detail ✦	The Knight Witch is a multi-genre game that combines twin-stick bullet hell, Metroidvania, and spell card deck building. It tells a story about a world damaged by environmental issues, intertwined with one about the Knight Witches themselves, heroes who are powered by Link - manifested trust from those that they help. 	I found each aspect of gameplay to connect well with each other. Numerous different foes and environments make the world fun to explore and the action exciting, combined with a variety of spell cards and upgrades to choose from for a fun tactics aspect.	The game is slightly rough around the edges. Some of the biggest issues are occasional difficulty spikes (mostly with one or two bosses that require substantial strategizing and learning) and some backtracking issues (compounded without an overall world map or the ability to teleport *to* individual save points). However, the game makes up for this with unlocks that can help to track and collect everything in each area. I'll spare the full details on the minor issues, but I ultimately simply enjoyed the experience of navigating and adapting with each encounter.	I also enjoyed the game's art style and music. The worldbuilding itself and the characters all felt very natural and dynamic. Likewise, the art has a lot of detail and delivers the atmosphere perfectly. The music is also fun to listen to, and it's excellent for the atmosphere of each and every environment. (The regular boss music, Giga Tree, and Mirror Lake are probably among my personal favorites.)	In summary, I can highly recommend The Knight Witch for its effective arrangement of different themes and gameplay aspects, presented in a coherent story and its own identity fitting to the name. If you enjoy hybrid themes, gameplay, and storytelling, you'll most likely enjoy The Knight Witch as well!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall cute game, nice little story. I liked the interactions between the MC and her husband throughout the game. _childDocuments_.review: I'm rating this positive, but consider it a soft thumbs up because the second half of the game has major issues.Welcome to a deck-building metroidvania/bullet-hell hybrid. A bulletvania if you will.This takes place in a fantastical world where the legendary Knight Witch Robyn defeated an evil emperor who was killing the planet with his machine empire. Unfortunately, Robyn was not able to defeat his lifestream-sucking giant robot fast enough and the surface became a barren wasteland scarred by solar radiation. As luck would have it, when the doom-mecha blew up, it revealed an underground city build by an extinct race of giants were everyone went to live in peace and harmony. Until decades later when the emperor's son stages an attack on the overground city to reclaim his right to rule and the Knight Witches must spring back into action. Or not, because the Witch Knights seem to be MIA. So you take on the role of Rayne, a Knight Witch cadet who didn't see battle due to being benched for sucking. But now, it's finally her time to shine in this moment of crisis. Armed with her spell cards, a randomized set of super-moves you can use in addition to your standard magic bullets, you will fly through the various zones of the kingdom as you unravel the mystery behind the invasion, dodging bullets as you dog-fight enemy fliers while navigating the maze-like areas. I would have given this game an unreserved thumbs up based just on the first few hours. The first half of the game is really good. It has fun and challenging combat, a decent storyline, and top-notch visuals. The biomes of the underground kingdom are visually stunning, like something out of a picture book. A real treat for the eyes. Unfortunately, the game doesn't stick the landing. There is a huge difficulty spike at the start of the second half (the area under the lake) that completely unbalances the experience. As many reviewers have already stated, the enemies get ridiculously spongy, the arenas get tighter so there is less room to maneuver, and they introduce new enemy projectiles that are green instead of the bright orange they've always been. Enemies drop green gems when they explode so it's easy to confuse a bullet for a power-up in the heat of battle and fly right into it. Combat never really recovers it's fun factor after this point. Since encounters took to long and just seemed to increase my chances of taking damage, I started just skirting through the trash mobs unless I was forced to fight them. I never seemed to power up enough to ever feel like I was on equal-footing with the enemies. They got stronger and I always seemed like I was a step or two behind. This game really could have benefited from adjustable difficulty levels, but they put in cheats instead. No, I don't want to finish the game on God-Mode. I just want a reasonable difficulty curve. Maybe if you are really into bullet-hell shooters, you might enjoy the second half more than I did.
