_childDocuments_.review: I wish that Steam had an option to recommend but with some asterics. Should you play this game? Maybe! If you like shoot em ups and like very light metroidvania elements, this could be fun. There are some major downsides I need to discuss however, first is that theres no fast travel in this game. The starting fly speed is your max speed, and though you do eventually get a dodge, its not much faster. Secondly, you're going to need to rely on spells for the majority of your damage, which would be fine if it wasn't for the fact the game has a rather bizarre way of handling magic. You have three slots for spells, and they're pulled randomly from a deck you make. The three spells can manifest any card from your deck any number of times and where it manifests is dependent on the last card you used. This has the odd downside of forcing you to split your attention from all of the chaos on screen to constantly checking both your mana and your spells. Its.. Frankly obnoxious. Its even worse when you can have multiple of the same card pop up even though you only have one in your deck.  As for the metroidvania side of things, theres very very very little you unlock. You get two skills to help open different levers and the dodge. Thats pretty much it. Everything else is tied to your spells and they're fairly simplistic.Overall, I do recommend it, after all I've 100%'d it, but do be aware of the flaws the game has.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Play the demo, if you like the demo you'll like the game, if you don't like the demo, you won't like the game.The Knight Witch is a SHMUP with some Metroidvania elements. While far from perfect, it has been a positive experience for me. It took me about 15 hours to finish, with around 85% completion rate.It's very colorful and the backgrounds are beautifully hand drawn. In general it looks fantastic and each setting is unique and interesting to look at. The enemy variety is huge considering it's a fairly short game, new types of enemies constantly show up with different patterns to learn and master. The game is tough but for the most part fair towards the player. In general, I think it's a solid game. The story is engaging and has a bunch of twists, and I found myself thinking "ok, so this will be the final boss" many times during my playthrough, just for my certainties to be overturned by a plot twist. The characters are fun to interact with, for the most part, and there are some nice ideas in terms of game design, such as the spell cards or other spoiler-ish stuff.Now for the bad things.The biggest problem this game has, in my opinion, is visual clarity. In a barrage of bullets coming your way, you have little time to think and if you struggle to distinguish the enemies' bullets from your own, or from elements of the scenery, or VFX of your spells, well... it's a problem. And it happens multiple times in this game.Fast travel basically does not exist: you travel through the same areas multiple times, and you have to fly through them, one dash after the other, for absolutely zero reasons.As others have said, having to look in a corner of your screen to see what spells you have available, while trying to avoid a sea of bullets, is not a very smart idea; but I found this thing problematic only in very specific instances: for the vast majority of the game, you have enough time to comfortably look at the spells.Challenge rooms: the ideas of these rooms is to cram all the space available with enemies, giving you little to no space to move around and figure it out by yourself. I think these rooms are unfair and badly designed.The  is completely useless.The final boss: without spoiling anything, let's just say that there is a thin line between insanely hard and unfair, and even if there was the thickest of lines, it wouldn't matter, because this boss is absolutely ridiculous in terms of balancement. I assume the devs wanted you to use cheats to beat it? Honestly I don't know, but I beat it legit and to take it down it requires a ton of concentration, a lot of time, patience and tries, deck building, and, unfortunately, LUCK. If you have a bad spell rotation, good luck doing anything.The settings. There are next to no graphics settings, why?The audio is very forgettable. Music included.Hitboxes. This one is not necessarily a problem but rather a question I've asked myself while playing. In most bullet hell games, your hitbox is a small sphere at the center of your character. In this case though, the whole character can be hit. It is a peculiar and questionable choice, that I don't necessarily apprecciate, but whatever. Also I don't quite understand why the character moves slower when hugging walls. Sometimes you get stuck in a corner while trying to move around. I don't know how valid of a choice this is.In conclusion, I want to stress the fact that this game is very fun, but a rough gem that could be further polished. I think the demo offers a very solid overview of what the game is.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Good artstyle and beautiful areas- Interesting concept of deckbuilding/bullet hellCons:- Having to look at your cards mid-fight makes it hard to dodge bullets- Short game- Backtracking is a pain as there is no fast travel and your only movement is a dash- Contrary to a dev statement armour does not help for no-hit challenges -> For me personally all the small inconveniences add up to make this game feel unenjoyable and tedious. _childDocuments_.review: Something a lot of the negative reviews for this miss is that this is a deck building game at it's core. The final boss is entirely beatable without cheats if you build a deck of cards geared specifically to fight it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: The Knight Witch has some issues with balancing it's difficulty and could certainly use some QoL improvements, but I think the reviews are overall much too harsh on this game.I really did enjoy my time playing (the underwater level notwithstanding)What first drew me into it definitely was it's gorgeous and colorful art style, both in terms of character design, as well as in it's background art. The music as well has some really comfy tracks I may keep coming back to even after having finished the game.The game starts off pretty good, giving you a short look at the abilities you will gain over the course of the game and starting you off with a strong arsenal of spells.After the short intro we meet our actual protagonist, Rayne, who starts off with a much weaker collection of weapons and spells to ease you into the gameplay now.Speaking of, the Knight Witch plays like a mix between an omnidirectional shmup/bullet hell and a metroidvania.You have two ways of attacking enemies.First, you can simply shoot enemies with a fast gun-like weapon, which you can either aim yourself or have autoaim at nearby enemies for a small damage penalty.I really like this, as it lets you concentrate more on the dodging when enemy bullets start filling the screen.You other main ability is your spell deck, which consists of a minimum of 5 spells of your choosing.You always have three cards drawn, each of which you can fire off with a specific button press, at which point a new card will be drawn in it's slot.These spells deal a lot more damage than your normal attack, but require mana to use.Mana, in turn, you generate by shooting at enemies with your normal attack!I really enjoyed this interplay between your attacks.However, roughly 3-4 hours in you will likely come across the infamous underwater level.I'm unsure how some of the combat encounters in this area managed to get through development without anyone saying: "Hey guys, don't you think this is a little too hard?"It's a mixture of your normal abilities being limited underwater, arenas that are too small for the amount of enemies and bullets on screen and the fact that you're likely not going to have very much HP at this point of the game, so you also die really quickly.This however is an extreme outlier.In the following levels you will gain more and more abilities and spells and you should have found some HP and mana upgrades at this point.With those new spells you will also be able to build better spell decks, especially if you look for synergies between cards, which will make controlling combat a whole lot more manageable.The Knight Witch really starts too shine within it's latter half as you get more options in combat.Sadly, that does require having to get over the bump in the road that is the underwater level.I understand anyone that is frustrated by this area (as was I), but I am glad I stuck around long enough to get to enjoy the rest of the game.I do thoroughly recommend the Knight Witch, but be warned of the game having one very frustrating to deal with area relatively early in the game and being a little rough around the edges in terms of QoL and some UI elements.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly this game reminds me of Dust: An Elysian Tail by it's artstyle.The background artstyle looks awesome and detailed, character design looks cute but main character looks absolutely adorable, also spirit cat :3This game can get hectic in a second with bullets and projectiles flying every direction when fighting the monsters and golems so if your playstyle isn't suited for this "bullet hell" type of game then please do reconsider of your purchase, but if you're up for a challenge then don't let me or anyone else be in your way and start blasting those monsters.The story is easy to follow and interesting enough to get into, altho I would have wanted to see animated cutscenes to easy up the amount of text.The  fml moment in the whole game is the non-existent teleportation inside level map, like you cannot teleport between Arcane Beacons which would have made the traveling bit more easier and not so cumbersome.In-game Cheats are fun but not necessary to complete the game. Pros:+ amazing artstyle and cute character design+ Interesting story+ Easier with controller (auto aim)+ Challenging enough  Cons:- No teleportation in levels, cumbersome traveling- No animated cutscenes- In some fights you cannot see where you're flying, so you end up taking dmg or in worst case dieNow I don't know how likely this could be, but I would like to see a sequel for this game. It wouldn't have to be Rayne (the main character) but e.g. it could be Rayne's and Akai's offspring as the mc fighting whatever there is or solving problems. Either way I would give this game 8/10, can recommend if you like this type of games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game looked interesting but I hadn't heard much about it. I was glad I decided to jump in and try it. I love metroidvania games and new takes on that sort of genre. This game turns it into a twin-stick bullet hell game in a way that is incredibly awesome, and also incredibly challenging. I would highly recommend this game if you can take a real bullet hell challenge. Enemies, especially nearing the end of the game will fill rooms with bullets going everywhere and it's important to use every tool at your disposal to keep alive to clear the room. The bosses in general posed far less difficulty than some of the ambush rooms where you are locked inside until you clear increasingly difficult waves. That being said, the game feels fantastic to play. Controls are tight and responsive, the battles are fast and frantic, and the story has been pretty fun and interesting. A bit of a reflection on how the world actually works, versus how it is presented through public media and influencers. It's a type of story I haven't seen the game go through before but it's cool to see how it changes your character as the game goes on, and the way it can affect your ability to grow in the game if you choose to be honest and real, or play up your heroism through stretching the truth, or sometimes outright lying.

_childDocuments_.review: Cons type I - Spell cards are forced into the main mechanic:- Players are discouraged from using different cards because of bad reliability or high power level requirement, which means 90~95% of spell cards will never be used by the player who wants to finish the game- The randomness on spell cards keeps distracting player from being able to avoid enemy projectiles, this means random "**** you"s are thrown at the player from time to timesRecommended fixes on making spell cards to be the main mechanic: Downgrade bullet dodging mechanics or difficulty, add more card slots, add a minor aiming assist on mouse-keyboard controlRecommended fixes on making bullet dodging to be the main mechanic: Instead of 3 dynamic and random spell card slots, make them static, the player only gets to use 3 cards at maximum, delete some of the filler & fluff cards, decrease player hit-box and bullet hit-boxRecommended fixes on double mechanics: make the bullet dodging to be the main combat mechanic of the game, and spell cards as the main puzzle mechanic for clearing some rooms, but this would mean re-development as this game does not have proper puzzle rooms, the closest one being the dash challenge in giga treeCons type II - Forced longer game sessions- Lack of a fast travel / faster moving ability- Very difficult to find side quest objectives, since the game only tracks main quest- The difficulty jolts up in middle on the game by introducing bullet sponges and more are added in late game levels, the game-play becomes boring and annoyingRecommended fixes: add a "map cleared" percentage, or change the map color per room if it was fully explored (like the ambushes being cleared), add a fast travel or upgrades that could permanently make longer dashes, reduce late game enemy HP

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This game is basically babies first bullet hell mixed with Metroidvania and Deckbuilding aspects and I'm all here for it!Some more detailed thoughts:Pros:Very satisfying exploration, lots of secrets with extra challenge rooms that feel rewarding, especially finding secret spell cardsDeckbuilding is fun, making your own personal spelldeck tailored to your needs and how much you cast works pretty well for the most partControls are smooth and responsive, the fact that you can let go of your aim and still hit things is great for more hectic situationsMids:There's some nitpicks I can agree with from other reviews likeThe spellcards being hard to look at during more hectic fights cause they're in the corner of the screenSome projectiles being hard to see sometimes (really isn't THAT bad though considering the plenty spells letting you get rid of bullets on screen and lots of checkpoints)Mana drops can be hard to get sometimes and probably should slowly float towards your character no matter the distance instead of dropping downAnd some of my own critiques:One of the imo best spellcards is locked behind the collectible coins and a random draw I think some spellcards need a price adjustment, especially some of the guns are too expensive for what they do  Cons:The storywriting is atrocious, the main character is frustratingly stupid and a lot of the story beats feel needlessly preachy, this whole script needs a proper writer to tear through and rewrite half of it,you wouldn't even need to change much on the game's storybeats, just change nearly everything Rayne says (how is this woman 35?)No difficulty sliders? At least I haven't seen any. I probably got lucky that the difficulty falls exactly in a sorta comfortable zone for me, considering a lot of the negative reviews seem to struggle with the game All in all I had a VERY good time with this game as long as I didn't pay too much attention to what characters say

_childDocuments_.review: I'll try to keep this short since so many of the other reviews have already covered pretty much all the points. Like others have said they tried to pull in many genres but ended up not the being able to excel at any of them and leaving you (at least me) feeling lukewarm about the whole experience. The stand outs for me was having the spells locked in the corner as this did nothing but create frustration at times. Was this a design choice an oversight or was it meant to cheaply increase the difficulty of the game? _childDocuments_.review: Preface this with me not really being huge on the metroidvania style games, and not being particuarly good at the bullet hell side of things either.  That aside, this game was a blast. Got a little frustrating at times, but still really fun.  One hint i would have for new players is this: Once you spend 350 coins at Yupi (7 cards), he gives you a secret scanner. He probably tells you in game, but i kind of just glossed over it. It shows up as a grid of dots on the map when you have an incomplete secret in that room. Pros:-Large maps with lots of little details-Fun story with cute/funny interactions-fun gameplay that rewards "gitting gud'-Lots of powerful cards to help you build your ideal setup. -If you want more or less challenge, you can activate some of the various cheat modsCons-She moves a little on the slow side- Gets a little tedious to backtrack... which there will likely be a lot of-Some fights get a little hectic really fast- Easy to get overwhelmed at various parts of the game-Decent chunk of the cards are borderline useless... even stated so by one of the NPCs-The aforementioned cheat mods are kind of annoying to unlock in the tedious sense. No real hints to them as far as i could tell. That said, its optional. If you care you can either look the codes up or just muscle your way through the combinations like i did. If there was a game that played like this set in the Touhou universe, it would feel right at home.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 Great game. I was apprehensive because I'm not into shooters, but I'm so glad I made the leap. Solid gameplay, great visuals, great music, fun exploration/re-exploration mechanics. I loved the story, commentary, and characters, too.Knight Witch can be challenging, which I enjoy, but I'm glad there are cheat options to make the game more accessible. Also, losing battles is definitely part of the process, and the game makes it easy to retry as you develop the skills and strategy you need to win.Note: Knight Witch looks like a metroidvania-shooter hybrid, but if you ignore the fact that you're visually looking at things from the side, the game plays like a top-down. So it's more akin to an OG Zelda-like + shooter. That's fine by me but it's good to know what you're getting into.

_childDocuments_.review: The Knight Witch is a fine metroidvania. The bullet hell perspective is a unique one, but when it comes down to it, maybe there's a reason more metroidvanias aren't bullet hells. There are plenty of "unfair" feeling fights in this game, because of how many enemy combinations have their bullet patterns overlap, and the screen quickly becomes a jumbled mess of your bullets and theirs. In my opinion, the generous "cheats" menu really saves it. It's more like an accessibility menu, like Celeste, with some simple toggles changing the game enough to feel right, and it's always there, doesn't disable achievements, and doesn't shame you for using them. Everything else about the game is great though, art, music, and a story that avoids some cliches. Good game, just don't expect a real, fair bullet hell.

_childDocuments_.review: Twin-stick 2d shooter meets Metroidvania is very compelling.  Art style is friggin' sweet, as are the character designs (visually and narratively).  There are some irritating difficulty spikes here and there, but if that's the only thing that'll stop you, there are built-in cheats that can give you various levels of advantage.I don't normally like a lot of bullet-hell in my shoot-em-up experience, but this game doesn't go overboard with it so it's well within my tolerance so far (one or two bosses excepted).The main challenge for me is needing to see things in three locations on the screen at the same time (Where is the thing I'm trying to shoot?  Where are the bullets I'm trying to dodge?  Which spells are available on which buttons right now?).  This makes using defensive abilities in particular pretty awkward.  The "auto-aim" functionality is nice as it can sometimes take one of those three things out of the equation, but during more difficult ambushes the auto-aim can betray you by targeting lesser threats when you really need to burn something else down.Anyway, pick it up!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty good for the most part. There's a decent amount of customization options for whether you want to use weapons or magic, but while I haven't gotten to do a magic build play through it seems like several of the spells are next to useless. I can't see them being very effective. I also have no idea how you'd beat the final boss with just magic, which brings me to my complaints. The difficulty for the game is pretty well balanced, a lot of the challenges can be revisited later on but with some perseverance and a bit of luck you can get through them when you encounter them. The game really makes you learn in stages, first by customizing your builds for different encounter and then finally with the final boss, resetting its HP 4 or 5 times and running away to hide for however long while it fills the screen with bullets. Also, getting through its final bar of hp only to not realize you have to do some more stuff or else it regenerates AGAIN is ♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ after the sometimes 10 minute fight you already survived. Other than that, the warning screen that pops up for every Ambush encounter and boss lasts wayyyy too long. It should be like half of what it is, or give an option to skip it.

_childDocuments_.review: A very careful positive / recommendation.The game is fun, but the difficulty can be very un-even at times. Even for someone good at bullet-hell games, at least one encounter near the end had me stuck for a good 15-20 minutes and I could not beat the final boss without enabling cheats after trying for upwards of an hour, as it commits the biggest sin in boss design: you can't damage it until it allows you to. In addition to other BS in that fight.The metroidvania elements are quite shallow, the areas have a few hidden nooks and crannies but the maps aren't fleshed out nearly as much as other games in the genre.I loved the idea of the moral choice system being tied to in-game rewards, but in the end it did not seem like my choices effected anything, so choosing the "bad" option for vastly more XP would have been better, I suppose.The game and its mechanics have potential, if the developers ever want to explore a sequel in the same setting and improve on it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: The Knight Witch is a great opportunity at exploring a mash-up of many common genres with a beautiful visual and sound design. I greatly appreciate them making a believable female protagonist that is mischievous, but is cute in her pursuit to carry through with her mission.Gameplay-wise, there are several elements I really thought worked well such as auto-targeting at the expense of some damage, but allowing you to take the reigns for full damage aiming manually when there's less chaos on the screen or you're feeling cheeky. The card system, like many card systems makes it somewhat reliable, putting a lot of cognitive load to focus more on the bullet-hell to learn to recognize what is good and bad on screen. It's great when you want to be able to plan certain ambushes once you learn the spawn orders to learn to hold your big guns for when you need them. I would have appreciated being able to choose a smaller deck to decrease the randomness, but you gain the ability to copy cards to increase your chances for good pulls.Story-wise, I think it does a great job telling a story and doesn't overly lock you into decisions by giving you an alternative way to not sacrifice power. There are some mini-side quests and collectables that you can look for to work towards 100% and leaves a bit of wiggle room in case some of them are tedious by not requiring all 100% of them to explore the character interactions. It's definitely not a true moral system like many RPGs, so making decisions should be done for how you want to play with minimal risk of losing out except for possibly 1 or 2 side quests. I really liked all the characters and the parts they played to move the story along an enjoyable experience that wouldn't be quite as deep as other metroidvanias like Hollow Knight or Ori & the Blind Forest, but was it's own take on a world past its prime.Overall, I'd definitely give this game a try for the price point because once some of the systems become familiar and comfortable, you'll be dashing around bullets doing all the witch things. If things get tough, there's a very obvious "Cheats" menu in the start menu you can use in order to progress the story and worry less about the gameplay and enjoy the really beautiful music, environments, and love the studio put into this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: An uncommon genre mashup that hits  of its targets.As the store page describes, your main task is exploring and upgrading around an interconnected map, but instead of running and jumping you'll be freely dodging and shooting, "twin-stick" style. With a bit of practice moving and attacking felt solid (for the record, I used an X360 controller); while the game encourages you to aim your bullets manually for the greatest effect, you also have the option to auto-target enemies and play more defensively if you desire. The traversal and combat augments you obtain are modest in number, but generally shake up the formula more than enough to keep things interesting through the game's running time.There's also just a touch of "deckbuilding" to tool around with here, as your special abilities come in the form of cards that are found or earned along your way. You can equip a limited "deck" of them at save points, of which a random selection of three will be available for use at a time; spend some MP to activate one and it goes back into the "draw pile", with another automatically taking its place up front. As such, while you won't always have access to  the ability you were banking on, a bit of trial and error (helped along by the option to freely experiment with your cards whilst saving) will allow you to stack the odds in your favor for whatever particular challenge you're up against.Speaking of which, challenge-wise the game felt  about right in my book; your HP remains fairly limited and healing opportunities between save points are somewhat sparse, so you're certainly not in for a cake walk and probably will need to retry certain segments a few times, not to mention more carefully plan your card loadout and overall approach as things heat up, but biting the dust  doesn't send you back  far (do note, however, that while most areas don't take an overly long time to pass through, there's no true fast travel ability available), so the necessary persistance on the player's part isn't overly demanding. That being said I would have appreciated some way to directly observe your character's hit area and gauge invincibility windows, even if only while "training", just to have a clearer idea of just how much leeway you have when dodging attacks.Of course, the first thing you likely noticed when you stumbled upon the store page were the game's visuals; as far as the sights on offer are concerned, I'm inclined to describe them as most akin to a lavishly-illustrated storybook, boasting distinctive character and environment designs, vibrant colors, and lots of little details to take in if you spare the time to notice them. Several enemy types across the different biomes are essentially upgraded/reskinned versions of each other, but this bit of corner-cutting does little to detract from an otherwise lovely presentation; my only truly notable complaint on this front - apart from the lack of an in-game gallery - is that foreground elements and pyrotechnics can sometimes obscure enemy attacks and lead to cheap hits.In terms of sound, I must say the game kind of snuck up on me in this regard; at first the music stayed mostly in the background, but as I progressed the track selection gradually started to stir in more varied and intense notes, and played a greater role in keeping me engaged. Voices are sparse outside of occasional -esque exclamations from the heroine, but I personally didn't mind, as keeping the dialogue text-based allowed the pace to remain, for the most part, appropriately brisk.One final strong point that I personally wasn't expecting was the story; when it comes to most action-oriented games I tend to all but assume that the plot elements will end up slowing things down more than they're worth, but I found myself surprisingly eager to keep apace with the goings-on of The Knight Witch's world and characters. Nearly all of the latter, by the by, are granted unique names, portraits and personalities, and thus make a much more memorable impression than the usual generic townies; just as importantly, the developers are rightly confident enough in the little fantasy civilization they've built to let its diverse, intermingling nature and surrounding themes stand entirely on their own and speak for themselves, without ever resorting to eyeroll-worthy "hey, make sure to notice (and praise) " overtures. Even your playable heroine, so frequently saddled with "blank slate" or "archetype" status, is not only earnest and determined but possesses a gently grounded, easygoing sense of humor which keeps her from ever becoming one-note or overbearing; this additional effort on the writers' and localizers' part is  much appreciated.In the end, of course, this review is inevitably a bit vestigial in nature since there's a demo you can try and get a feel for things with yourself, but in any event I wound up finishing with about 95% completion and 15-20 hours on the clock, so I can't claim to have experienced quite everything on offer (I should note that, unlike some of my fellow reviewers, I didn't experience any technical issues during my playthrough), but despite some misgivings here and there I had myself a good time, and very much intend to keep an eye out for the team's next release.
_childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game.It's gorgeous and the game play is tight.It is a metroidvania but you fly as in a 2D shooter.  You move with the left stick, aim with the right stick or auto aim without aiming the right stick.  The disadvantage in auto aiming is that your shots are weaker.You only have one main attack that upgrades but it can be changed using spellcards temporarily.The game is jumping between positive to mixed reviews but I bet if they just added souls-like in their description, it will stay "positive", lol.I didn't find it difficult even the submarine areas, just use your cards, slow down and back away and find cracks between bullets.Story-wise, it is lighthearted and dark at the same time.I like the characters too, the main character is refreshing, she is *minor spoilers* a 35 year old married woman.  And his husband is no beta either, the game explicitly says he's a bad ass.Overall a refreshing experience, I only went for 1 ending, I don't regret it.I hope they make more games with this art direction.*Spoilers*Suggestions for the developers:-Spellcards are a good concept but it would be good if the game had some sort of equipment system where you can change your main attack permanently instead of just a buff.-Game shows what you missed but is a little too cryptic.  I'm all for secrets but for a game with a smaller community, guides won't be readily available online.  I would have played with the game a little more but I don't want to spend it just trying to find stuff, unfortunately, adult life leaves me with limited time to play.(I don't have a clue how to reactivate ambushes/Good boi Pistola's fighting spirit is missing, etc)-Marketing-wise, I think the concept of bullet-hell metroidvania is really refreshing and excellent, I like it.But metroidvania in itself are either "souls-like" or not as difficult sidescroller and that's what people will be imagining when those keywords are mentioned.The difficulty can be adjusted by adding heals or potions OR keep the difficulty but market it as a "bullet-hell souls-like metroidvania", the latter would have made sense since after death, the game respawns you to a save point rather than an instant retry.Right now it's 70% Bullet Hell/30% Metroidvania.  Allowing equipment, consumables, etc. will make it more 50/50 if that's a direction the developers would like to consider if they are making another game.  If they want to lean more into bullet-hell, then the hit box should be smaller.Of course, that would mean it will require more resources on their end to create.I really like what the developers did here and I want them to be successful, that's why I am putting up my suggestions here.  I like the game mainly for its aesthetic and balance between being dark and light hearted.

_childDocuments_.review: So I enjoyed the game for the first few hours. Its colorful, has a pretty solid narrative, the characters have been pretty great, and the combat is unique. You have alot of freedom being able to fly and fire in any direction.That being said, at a certain point, something shifts in the gameplay after a few hours. Once you get the the dreaded water level, two things happen. First, the level becomes walled off and prevents you from returning to the Hub world (and subsequent upgrades). This means that if you are having a hard time, you will continue to have a hard time. This persists into the next level as well. Second, most of the level requires you to use a mechanic that restricts your movement (you can dash or leave a designated area) and forces you to shoot in only straight lines. Again, if you're struggling, this makes it hard to pull ahead and you'll find yourself hating playing the game. Would i recommend buying this? Yes, if you aren't repulsed by brutal combat and trying until you get it. Otherwise, don't be deceived, this is in no way an easy game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really interesting combination of platformer, bullet hell, deckbuilder, and arpg elements in a way that feels really enjoyable to play. No single element shines on its own, but the combination is unique and they meld well together.Platformer - weird claim because you’re flying, right? But there are several areas where you have to manage a series of precise movements in tight spaces with moving obstacles that can alter your movement. These are primarily side paths at least in the early game, but the mechanics are interesting  enough to be fair but require some execution.Bullet Hell - this should be self explanatory. The demo and videos showcase it reasonably well. You need to predict attack patterns and what can penetrate barriers to avoid damage effectively.The deckbuilder/arpg combination really makes encounters interesting. The reason they call it “deckbuilder” is because you have a selection of powers with shared energy and only 3 cards are available from your pool of powers to use at any given time. This forces you to vary your approach and use your tools creatively and reactively without leaning too hard on any single ability while still allowing you to structure how you want to play. The reason I’m comparing it to an APRG is because your abilities provide a good mix of defensive options, counters, powerups to your primary attacks, and different AOE attacks at close range or in different directions.I’m not finished with this game. I’m only a few hours in and am not sure where I am in terms of total content, but regardless of length it’s worth experiencing for the really well designed unique gameplay that merges several concepts together really well.

_childDocuments_.review: Bullet Hell Bill and Metroidvania Marge had a baby and made Slay the Spire the godfather (a somewhat absent one but still). Big fan.Of course, I'm a sucker for bullet hell games and metroidvanias so I'm probably smack in the middle of the target audience. Other than the core gameplay, though, the art is cute, I vibed with the BGM (kinda reminded me of The Bastion at some points), and the card system adds good flavor without taking over the game. Bonus points because you can break the crap out of it late game and breeze through earlier challenges.Some side notes* It's not a long game; I've hit 100% in ~11 hours which includes going over the entire map 3 times to find the last hidden achievement.* You don't get the dodge until the first new biome. Bit of a bummer. Not a huge deal though; the initial enemies are pretty straightforward.* There's a water biome which frequently puts you in a submarine. That submarine is the biggest bummer in this game. Fortunately it doesn't last that long.* Some of the "ambushes" (challenges with waves of enemies) are really hard for where they're at in the game. Those ones are also entirely optional. If it sucks, that probably means you can just leave and come back later.* You'll get the ability to repeat the ambushes later so don't sweat themSome responses to negative reviews / forum comments* Yes, the submarine is a pain. We know. The devs know. The devs even joke about it in by making an achievement homage to Ocarina of Time. It's like half of 1 level in the game and then never comes back.* Like I said, this game isn't always easy. A lot of those encounters are skippable and there are cheats to make it easier and you can always turn them off once you're done with a hard bit. If you want the game to be easy but tell you that it's on hard mode then you should probably miss this one.* Slow move speed? I guess but not  much slower than other games in it's class. The bullets are equally slow. A twitchy-reflex game this is not.

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't perfect, has some weird issues that could have been improved, like certain areas aren't reached by fast travel which makes backtracking to them a chore, the dodge mechanic isn't there by default and instead you have to get it in a fight, aside from the main quest there are no quest markers so sidequests can sometimes be confusing to do and as of now, some achivements aren't popping despite doing the requirements.Despite all this, the game is fun enough, it took me 16 hours-ish to complete, and its enjoyable enough. If you have the money and find it interesting, try it out. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: There's no doubt that Knight Witch can be difficult, but it's in no way insurmountable thanks to the magic system which lets you carve chunks out of enemy forces. It may not be the best Metroidvania from an exploration perspective but it's combat is deeply satisfying to get right. _childDocuments_.name: The Knight Witch

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+ Nice Soundtrack+ Clean visuals+ Main weapon and spells both effective, though only 3 or 4 of the main weapon variants are actually nice to use+ Decent story - starts off a little weak, but picks up later onCons:- Lack of fast travel- One obscure quest for an important completionist item - an extra hint of dialogue on what to do would probably be good to addTo anyone who says the main weapon isn't effective, I cleared the whole game using 0 spells, only main weapon upgrades. I have no clue why anyone would say they're not effective. To anyone who doesn't like the RNG card system, stack yourself some low cost cards to cycle through unwanted cards quickly.Other than those comments, overall I'm still quite pleased with the game. I won't 100% it since I don't want to go through the game a full second time for various achievements (when they work again), but I still greatly enjoyed the time I did spend on the game.Post Dec-22 Patch Edit: Achievements are fixed, so removed that from the con list.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying the game about 2/3 of the way through. I'm usually more into turn-based strategy, but the game's art caught my eye. I played through the demo a while ago and was excited about trying the rest of the game. So far I'm really impressed with the variety of challenges, and the story is a lot more complex and interesting that I would have guessed from the intro. It's quite difficult, but the "cheat" system has helped me get through a couple of things that would have been too frustrating otherwise. Happily the "cheats" don't disable achievements either. (There were some bugs in the achievement system, but they've been fixed.)A few words of caution: The deckbuilding spell system is divisive. I quite like it, but it's too random for some people. I also would like more of a fast travel system at this point in the game. It's annoying to deal with stuff multiple times when I'm revisiting old areas to find secrets.

name: Fracked
detailed_description: The award-winning action adventure, now on PC VR! From the creators of the ground-breaking Phantom: Covert Ops, Fracked seamlessly collides relentless “run and cover” gunfights with free and fluid skiing and climbing, in trailblazing fashion. Uncompromised, audacious, and unashamedly stylish, Fracked grabs your VR headset by the motion controllers and delivers an ass kicking game that has been made from the ground up for virtual reality platforms. Playable on Valve Index, HTC Vive, Meta Rift S, and Meta Quest and Quest 2 via Oculus Link. BE THE ACTION HERO Grab your gun, cock it, and take aim as a maverick war hero thrown back into the fight. Experience innovative VR gunplay that ingeniously blends improvised run and gun combat with a 1:1 grabbable cover system. Move freely around the battlefield to outflank, outsmart, and outgun an escalating threat with your arsenal of deadly, fully interactive weapons. FEEL THE ADVENTURE Venture through a harsh and dangerous mountain locale by seamlessly transitioning between a host of first-person free movement methods. Physically lean into the bends on your skis to master the slopes at high speed. Reach out and hold on for your life as you climb and zipline far above the ground or perform audacious base-jumps to elude your foes. No rails. No limits. No mercy. SAVE THE PLANET The corporation dug too deep unleashing the ‘Fracked’ from the depths below. Across one day, take on an interdimensional army that combines hive mind mentality and gun-wielding supremacy - the perfect targets to unload round upon round into. Fracked is in-your-face action with a cutting commentary on corporate greed and the climate change emergency. Save the day, to save the world. DESIGNED FOR VIRTUAL REALITY Created from the ground up for VR devices, Fracked pulls the action-adventure genre to revolutionary new heights through intuitive 1:1 VR gameplay. Interactions, locomotion and gunfights seamlessly combine in a single, pioneering VR game.

_childDocuments_.review: Borked controls and feels like a bad port.Gun angle is off.  Head steering only.  There is a another movement option called "Controller" which means you push Y button to move forward.  Again, steering is head only.You have to click in your thumbstick to run, and keep it down.  I haven't seen a game do this since 2016.This game has all the hallmarks of a lazy port.  Even the controls menu brings up the steam vr controller remapper.RESPONSE TO DEV:  My point is Thumbstick movement is always locked to head steering.  Locking my forward movement to where I'm looking is an old idea, but it helps with vr noobs and transitioning from flat screen gamingI should be able to walk forward while scanning my environment left and right.  It should not induce zigzag serpentine movement forcing me to fight the stick and transition constantly between forward and left/right strafing.  Please take a moment to check out controller based movement in other PCVR FPS games.  Here are some examples:Contractors,OnwardPavlov,HL Alyx,BoneworksSaints and Sinners,Arizona Sunshine,Population One,Skyrim VR,Zero CaliberAfter the FallEspire 1From other Sons, LarcenautsStar Wars Tales from the Galaxy's EdgeAsguards WrathMedal of HonorPath of the WarriorSeeking DawnWandererResident Evil 4[1st Response to Developer]Your response suggests thumbstick movement and headsteering are separate features or control methods.  No.  Thumbstick movement is lateral movement using the controller's stick.  What determines the "Forward" can be based on head position, or controller position."Controller" based movement as named by nDreams, appears to be a movement mode which, when pressing Y on the touch controller, lets me move forward.  Y?  Why y?  What happened here?  Is this a left over input from the PSVR port?Also, please have the sprint a click once feature to turn on.  The player can run until he releases forward on the stick.  Holding down click to run is the best way to break thumbsticks or at the very least makes the player tense up and  long gaming sessions become uncomfortable.Adjust weapon angle while in hand would be a nice touch.[2nd Response to Developer]No.  I did NOT clock a lot of time, but YES I DID get to play on my feet (as opposed to skiis).I'm not suggesting Controller thumbstick movement is not available. it IS available.  We are agreed on that.BUT YOU DON'T SEEM TO UNDERSTAND WHAT HEADSTEERING VS CONTROLLER STREERING MEANS.Most games offer the FORWARD as either relative to the HMD head position or the controller position.  You do not offer both options.  Only relative to head position.DO. NOT. CONFUSE. THE. TWO. This is my second attempt and explaining.If I have not made myself clear, it is likely that I am frustrated with you.  Seek some clarification elsewhere.  Maybe your team needs some training or VR gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Fracked on PCVR after having a long reputation for being one of the best PSVR games, I have to admit this does spark a bit of curiosity for die hard PCVR gamers doesn't it?Watch my first session in Fracked here: Fracked starts off quite relaxed in which you have to follow a helicopter as you ski down a mountain to avoid an incoming avalanche, which ultimately makes for a pretty tense moment.Controlling the skiing is not that difficult and you do it with the help of tilting your head (the headset) in the direction you want to point yourself in the game.After that you get a quick and clear tutorial of how all functions work and you are all set!In addition to skiing and hiking, there are many other resources that will help you move forward such as the ability to climb and even the use of many ziplines that are placed that allow you to quickly get to lower ground.You can also use your pistols to defend yourself from enemies while using these zip lines or even while skiing.You will have to be smart about using the weapons as reloading requires a lot of steps, nothing extreme of course but always keep in mind the extra seconds you need,you will often do this while hiding from incoming bullets,and while you are hiding behind some object you also have the option to grab something with one hand so that you can gently pull yourself up to fire calmly at the enemy, and drop down quickly when needed, a matter of saving those leg muscles, the AI ​​in the game can shoot quite well, so you will often have to bend over.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not PCVR, this is a really low-poly PSVR game with very low-res textures. That said, there are many nice scenic views, and the very low-end graphics can look nice from a distance. If only the gameplay was awesome, graphics may have meant less, but this really feels like a low-IQ and mediocre shooter. Levels are simple, opponents behave like they have an IQ of 50 - and you're just wandering through simple boring levels shooting much the same simple boring opponents. Not even the shooting feels like fun, weapons feel kinda clunkly. I think a game like Medal of Honor: Above & Beyond is like 10 times better than Fracked. But again, Fracked looks like a mobile game made for the Quest hmds, while Medal of Honor: A & B - even with its shortcomings - is a fullblooded PCVR experience. Devs did nothing to make Fracked shine on PCVR, we just got a 1:1 low-end PSVR port. Feels like an easy attempt to grab some cash. Like in Quest games, there are no graphics settings in Fracked, and the game could surely use some settings for antialiasing. There are no dynamic shadows in the game - but many baked shadows.  I'm using Index and a RTX 3090, i9 10900K (10 cores / 20 threads - 5.3GHz), 32GB ram and with res 500% in 90 Hz I mostly got 90 fps - but in a few scenes I dipped below 90 fps. So I reduced res to 400% (36 mill pixels per frame combining both eyes) - which still is totally overkill and shows this game does not need much gpu power. I bet you can play this game just fine using a GTX 970 or GTX 1060. I do love shooters, Alyx is my favorite VR game of all, but Fracked simply did not impress me, neither for the gameplay or especially the low-end graphics. To me this game would not be worth more than $15 - also the game is rather short and rated at about 4 hours. I'll refund, this game does not represent the quality of a great PCVR game - it's not even close, sadly. My rating 5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun arcade shooter. If you are looking for something colorful to throw on and run and gun, not think too much, it's perfect for that. It's not too deep, and you can pretty much predict the waves, but that's not always a bad thing. The duck/cover is really cool using your non-dominant hand (it does work left and right handed). The climbing is some of the funnest I've had. I came in with the right expectations, and I wasn't disappointed. It's kind of like a "B Action Movie", if you know what to expect you can have a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: Cool art style and a nice low poly aesthetic, but unfortunately first impressions aren't good beyond that. The game starts you off by doing a bit of downhill skiing where you steer by leaning your head side to side. If you're like me, it glitched as you loaded in, so you were perpetually spinning in circles while going down the side of the mountain. After making it past the skiing section (and almost losing my lunch), I noticed that the look joystick wasn't working. This was the result of the game unlocking controls incrementally as you progress through the second stage. Because this wasn't stated, I spent an hour and a half trying to customize and troubleshoot the frankly convoluted controller binds. After realizing that I needed to continue to unlock the ability to look, I found a gun. Unfortunately, said gun didn't hold in my hand quite right, so I had to awkwardly tilt my wrist down to shoot straight. All of these issues could probably be fixed with some mods and a bit of tinkering, but the out the box experience is not a solid one.

_childDocuments_.review: I only played for up to 30 minutes and am returning due to motion sickness inducing scenes, so take my review with a grain of salt. Game mechanics for shooting are smooth. I really like the holding onto cover system and the firefights are intense. The opening by skiing down a slope caused me to feel heavy motion sickness due to the ability to change direction too quickly, so I felt forced to ski in a boring straight line. Lastly, the graphics and textures are a bit too low resolution by today's standards, to the point where it is distracting and takes away from the game. It is a fun game, but I think too many things are holding it back from being even better.

_childDocuments_.review: some facts first. 1. i paid full price ($30) 2. it took me 2 hours to finished. 3. i played on a valve index.TLDR: It was fun, i liked playing it but there's no way its worth full price, $20-15 maybe.its was fun only because there are so few story driven campaign's in VR and i was really itching for onestory is fine, serviceable.Gun play is meh, they made a couple decisions i find odd. why make ammo limited but place so much of it everywhere? isn't the point of limited ammo to add a level of tension and resource management? ammo being littered everywhere defeats that doesn't it? there are 3 "power up guns" but they're everywhere, why not just give us the guns and make ammo for them scarce? guns feel weak, like pea shooters, there decent recoil and the enemy's react to being shot but Nerf guns sound more punchy then these dollar store throw away's enemy variety is a little lacking, but not that big of a deal. it is a 2 hour game after allthere's generic bad guy 1# he runs around and shoots at you, sometimes he taking cover, sometimes he flanks, sometimes he stares at the wall and ponder's the meaning of his lifethere's kamikaze guy hes loud and bright cant miss himand then there's big with big gun, he as a backpack you shoot at.i would of liked to see one maybe two more.some sort melee unit with a big fracking wrench maybe an animal unit too.the whole skiing thing is pretty cool my favorite parts  i had a nightmare of a time trying to grab the charging handle for the smg with my index controllers, finally i just rebound left grip to left trigger.might just be because my index is a couple years old

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, but a bit short, took me ~2.5hrs to finish the game on Normal difficulty (on easy you get lasers for your weapons, on hard you only have 1 life) And while its short and sweet, it has a few things to fix.As far as i could tell the game never tells you to try to "face forward" whenever possible, and this is an issue with like skying, where if you are looking not forward, its a pain to control your motions.With the vive wands, the aiming is a bit off, index controllers are way better... Except they ask you to click the right thumb to calibrate and the left one to sprint, there are no ingame options for that, you are sent to steamvr controller settings and as of right now there isnt a better remap, i would have definitively tried it, because click stick is a no-no. Also why doesnt anyone use the touchpads?There are only 2 weapons that i could find, pistol and smg, with a shotgun, revolver with laser sight, and a granade launcher as special weapons with limited ammo. Reloading is semi manual, and fits the game, bc its all fast paced, but at the same time if you drop a magazine you lose the bullets in it, but you still need to ♥♥♥♥ the weapon again after popping a new mag in when there should be a bullet in the chamber and "save" you the recocking of the weapon..Also there are also basically only 2 maybe 3 enemies. One that has like pistol, smg or shotgun, and its slightly spongier version, and a big robot that you can only harm by shooting at his backpack... I liked they go and take cover and dont beeline to you, and the animations when being shot, those where nice, but really they are zombies with weapons. and not very varied. There are no big boss fights, the final boss has a unique model but its basically the same enemy but moves faster than usual.The climbing sections where actually pretty entertaining but i wish they where more... active, like i can only remember 1 time i had to shoot while climbing a ladder, And the parts where you have to hang on while you are "crashing down" where EXCELLENT, and i wish they where more sections of that.There where also a lack of Slow-Mo moments i feel there are only a couple at the start? and then nothing... like i expected at least a couple (if not ALL) the sliding down the wire parts to have it, maybe i activated that while sliding down, that and i also kinda expected slowmo with very low health. Some levels had that WOAH cinematic moment!, not so much at the very end, So that was a bit underwhelming...I loved the graphics and the performance, The story is fine, nothing to complicated its easy to follow and it fits the game perfectly, the voice acting was pretty good, I dont think ill be replaying it, while it has cool sections i dont feel like replaying the whole wave parts to reach them, and there where little/no rewards for exploration except for some coins that i still have no idea what they do.Overall the game was action packed, fast paced, with some great ideas, a bit on the short side for the full price, but i liked the gunplay and while it had a simple and linear levels they where pretty enjoyable.Recommended, but maybe wait for a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: I appreciate the hard work that went into the game, and I absolutely love the visuals for this. I understand the developers aren't going for realism but there's too many restrictions, and immersion breaking things for me on this game. For example having invisible walls on low to the ground staircases is silly. I love nDreams and have liked or loved just about everything they've put out. But this just isn't one. I think this game would do wonders on the Quest 2 platform, but I'm not sure that's what the devs want. Unfortunately with some of the choices this feels old and stiff. The gunplay doesn't have the punch I was looking for, and in 43 minutes I beat 2 sections and met the first boss. Also in that same 43 minutes I got stuck in geometry twice and had to restart to keep going before I officially made it to the first boss. I've got my VR legs firmly planted but the skiing sections were disorienting, and if someone said they got sick from those sections - I'd believe them. I didn't get sick but its a super frustrating method of control that I would've loved to be able to look around more with. When the 2nd skiing sections goes down there are towers and enemies trying to get you. Those moments should've been epic like it was intended, but it just wasn't with those head only controls. I really wanted to love this game, I sincerely did, but I've refunded it.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty decent shooter with a unique Cel Shaded (XIII style) visuals, fun gunplay, decent music, and a great cover mechanic.  The gameplay could use a little mixing up from time to time, as the combat starts to get a bit repetitive by the ending where you've seen the same 3 or 4 enemy types for the entire game.  But the game is only around 3 hours to complete so doesn't overstay its welcome.  My only recommendations for new players are: - Play around with the visual settings as by default this game had the classic PSVR "screen smothered with vaseline" look - but you can improve the sharpness a lot without losing frames per sec.  - Sounds like a lot of people struggle with the skiing sections - bear in mind PSVR games were designed to play seated.  To steer left or right you just need to tilt your neck left or right.  So you can still technically look and shoot in all directions, but try not to tilt your neck L/R unless you're intending to turn.

_childDocuments_.review: Refunded.I was initially impressed with the skiing and tutorial phase of the game, but later on, I found the overall gameplay to be lacking.Firstly, the free locomotion direction cannot be changed, despite the setting being available in the gameplay menu. It does not work and the locomotion freezes completely when you resume the game. So it seems the only option available for free locomotion is head-oriented locomotion.Secondly, the audio is too low, even when I increase the volume to the maximum on both my headset and in the game settings. The sound design is lacking, which is particularly frustrating during intense combat. Attackers can sneak up from behind, but you won't hear them until you turn around. This is my biggest complaint about the game.If these issues don't seem too bad to you, the visual style, the environment and the progress within the story/dialogue can be intriguing and somewhat fun to try.

_childDocuments_.review: Reason I’m giving this a thumbs down is because in order the steer while skiing down a cliff you have to tilt your head side to side to steer. Dumbest mechanic in vr I’ve ever seen. They should let you steer with the thumb stick or hand controls. Steering by tilting your head makes it impossible to shoot enemies without crashing into a tree. I found the only way to shoot enemies while skiing was to blindly shoot to the side in hopes I’d hit them so I could keep my head straight. Steering with your head is not only uncomfortable but will cause vr newbies to get motion sickness. On a positive note I liked that you could physically grab cover to move around it while shooting. But the whole skiing part frustrated me enough that I turned the game off and returned it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fracked

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a very fun, simple and straight-forward action-adventure/shooter. It features a pistol, MP5K and 3 (if I recall correctly) "Power Weapons": Revolver, Shotgun and Grenade Launcher. There are 2-3 separate sequences where you get to ride on skis and the rest of the areas are varied with shooting while using cover and moving around the levels and also implementing the use of zip-lines, which is fun, although I wish the zip-lines moved faster! haha. The action is great, engaging and keeps your heart racing. there's only a few types of enemies, but there are also mini-bosses and of course an ending boss. The game can be completed on Medium difficulty in 2.5 hours. The graphics and visuals are very cool. It's like a cross between comic book art and cell shading, which was popularized in games like "XIII". This is the same studio that brought us games like "Shooty Fruity", "Phantom: Covert Ops" and also their newest title, "Synapse", which is currently an PSVR 2 exclusive title (But we hope it comes to Steam and PCVR!!). Overall, this game is great fun and has some exciting set-piece James Bond 007 style action moments! I snagged it on a sale for 50% off and I think that's a very fair price. There are a few small negatives, like during the skiing sequences you can only steer with your head, by looking left or right, which does not feel very natural and can lead to frustration while trying to ski over the ammo boxes to try and pick them up or while trying to avoid hitting a tree, etc, but thankfully the game is very generous with ammo, so you never have to really worry about running out. Btw, (and I'm not sure if this is true or not), but I have heard and read that this version of the game is a port from the PSVR, which if true may help to explain a little bit of the buggy nature. But, bugs aside, it's still very fun for an action-packed afternoon and I would definitely play it again. I never got tired of quickly reloading the MP5K in the frantic heat of battle. I would love to see even more gun types available in a future game. The story unfolds through audio voice overs and radio communication with your helicopter pilot, which is fun and makes you feel like a special agent. The story ends with a cliffhanger (no pun intended) and I hope that maybe someday we get to see a "Fracked 2" with even more features and maybe twice the campaign length. Kudos to the developers and keep up the good work. I'd recommend it!p.s. -- I can't believe I almost forgot to mention that there are awesome climbing sequences featured throughout the campaign which are very fun and tense! It reminds me of games like Uncharted and Tomb Raider. Very cool. I've always loved when Climbing is featured in VR games and this game does it well!

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed playing this game. There are however some downsides but the pros outweigh the cons in my opnion. The shooting is really nice and the cover system is also pretty original. the game has an original look to it which i kinda like. Also like the theme of some levels. The ski segments although very cool needs some time to getting used to. Some more weapon variety would have been nice. You only have 2 weapons equipped and can pick up some other weapons with limited ammo (upon which they will disappear when used). Also the game does not track were you are in relation to the game. So if you start in the center and walk around in the room you will be outside you're character. The game is also pretty short I finished the game in less then 4 hours. You can replay the game and see if you can find all the collectibles although this will not unlock anything as far i know. A short but really nice shooter that is definitely worth you're time if the game is at a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a neutral recommendation. Giving it a thumbs up because it feels like the game has unfairly low steam rating right now - 57%, and it is definitely not that bad.Fracked is a fast paced VR cover shooter with some ski action sprinkled around. The gameplay is solid and fun, cartoony visuals look nice despite lacking any noticeable graphic improvement for PC release, but the content is very limited. About 2 hours of campaign with only 2-5 weapons, 3 enemy types and very bland bossfight.Ski sections are very hit or miss: it is intuitive and exciting, but drifting during sharp turns can be problematic for people suffering from VR motion sickness. Gunplay is satisfying, and unique cover mechanics with ability to position yourself around by grabbing cover edges is much better accessibility option then "push button to crouch". The combat is well paced and rather difficult, but lacks variety, which would have been a problem if the game was not so short :)Climbing is ok, although some forced camera movement during it feel weird.Visual style is really nice, but the game clearly does not utilize PC VR capabilities. The environments are quite beautiful and interconnected, but backgrounds and skyboxes are very small and blurry, a lot of textures lack detail and there are no Graphic options to improve it other than cranking up Steam VR supersampling. Which I easily raised to 200% on Reverb G2 and RX 6800 XT, so at least the performance is good.The story is generic, but the voice acting is good.All and all, very mixed bag, but I still appreciate PSVR games releasing on PC, even when they are not masterpieces like Moss or Tetris Effect.

_childDocuments_.review: As stated by others, this game is very short, I finished the game in just under two hours.There are no complex mechanics, and no physics based interactions, however this was likely outside of the scope of a psvr title. The game feels like playing through an action movie, the cover system aids greatly with this as you can easily manoeuvre  and fire with no effort. the heavy tracers on all shots allow (and encourage) you to do silly things like blind firing and shooting the guns sideways like a true action hero! The real stand out are the skiing sections of the game, where with very little practice you can look in one direction and fire while still skiing straight. Feels like the snowmobile section from MW2 in vr at times.Unfortunately there are only two main weapons, with all others relegated to single use "power weapons"For full price I feel the game could have used more meat on it's bones, but if you're particularly starved for a good vr shooter, this can be a fantastic one sitting game.
_childDocuments_.name: Fracked

_childDocuments_.review: This is basically a cheesy B-grade action/sci-fi movie in VR form. I mean that in a good way. Most of the game revolves around arcadey cover-based shooting. You grab onto cover with one hand, then pull yourself around to lean out to shoot. It works really well for the most part. The skiing sequences were the best part for me. They had a great sense of speed and spectacle - it was awesome to go off a big jump and see everything go into slow motion. The climbing sequences were also cool.It could do with a bit more variety, but it's excusable for a fairly small production like this.Overall, a solid experience that I enjoyed.
_childDocuments_.name: Fracked

_childDocuments_.review:
Fracked is a PlayStation VR shooter that seamlessly combines relentless 'run-and-cover' gunfights with free and fluid skiing and climbing.

Stranded in a remote mountain facility, you play as a reluctant hero forced into a final stand between the planet and a legion of interdimensional enemies. 

Created by nDreams (Phantom: Covert Ops) for PS VR and PlayStation Move controllers, an innovative cover system will have you peeking out from behind environmental objects and outflanking enemies to gain the advantage.

About the Game Max Caulfield, photographer-in-residence at the prestigious Caledon University, discovers her closest new friend, Safi, dead in the snow. Murdered. Max realizes the killer will soon strike again – in both versions of reality. With her new power to Shift between two timelines – can Max solve and prevent the same murder? ORDINARY GIRL, EXTRAORDINARY POWER Max is thrust into a thrilling supernatural murder mystery – more dangerous than ever before! name: Shredders
detailed_description: You and your pal are making goofball snowboarding videos at the Frozen Wood resort when brand ambassador Lisa makes an offer for a couple of sponsored videos. She gives you a glimpse of a whole new world of snowboarding, professional riders, snowmobiles, and epic features to shred. An invitational has attracted a whole bunch of pro-riders to the area, and with Lisa’s help you have a chance to meet some of them, learn a bunch of their moves, and possibly even get a chance to join them in the kick ass invitational! A love letter to snowboarding, Shredders takes inspiration from a whole bunch of awesome snowboarding films, the Amped games from back in the day, and the snowboarding heroes on Instagram. Features Huge unlockable OPEN WORLD : The horizon is full of amazing lines, features, and gorgeous scenery, and the snow is always fresh! Shred with a top selection of PRO RIDERS: With their real voices and stories, this is as real snowboarding as it gets. Master DIVERSE LOCATIONS: Shredders is for powder fanatics and park rats, for urban street snowboarders and backcountry explorers. All areas are inspired by snowboarding movies and optimized for maximum fun. Ride with your unique STYLE: No snowboarding game has ever been created with this level of control. Every move feels amazing from gorgeous spins with Jamie Anderson, to lawn darts with Sebbe De Buck, and knuckle huck tricks with Marcus Kleveland. STORY MODE: With the help of your pal Scotty you’ll meet pros, learn their moves and shine! Play online and SHRED TOGETHER with friends: With multiplayer built into its core, you’ll be hitting the top spots with your buddies. Let’s drop! LIFELIKE ANIMATIONS inspired by pro boarders: Snowboarding has never been this fluid. Feel the flow! Stacks of snowboarding brands and REAL EQUIPMENT: Fresh real-world gear has been carefully digitized and prepped for you in Shredders. You’re guaranteed to look good.

name: Potionomics
detailed_description: Deluxe Edition About the Game After the untimely death of her uncle, a penniless witch named Sylvia finds herself thrust into the role of potion proprietor. It's all up to her to carry on her uncle's legacy and keep his potion shop afloat. Thankfully, she won't have to go it alone. With help from some new friends, Sylvia must hone her negotiation skills, outsell her craftiest competitors, and make her shop THE number-one potion destination in Rafta. It’s all about mastering the finer points of Potionomics! Key Features Wheel and Deal Negotiations can be tense when every coin counts, but you'll manage Sylvia’s stress with ease by playing your cards right. Develop friendships with adventurers and other shopkeepers on Rafta to learn even more advanced negotiation tactics. Recipe for Success Choose the best ingredients to make even basic potions extraordinary, perfecting the taste and aroma to please your pickiest customers. But beware—if you aren’t careful, you'll get some pretty gross results! Fantastic Friends and Foes Rafta, home to some of the world's most potent magic, is packed with big RPG personalities, each seeking a leg up in their adventures. Befriend and recruit them to help you level up your own potion game, but don't expect everyone to be friendly… Your Shop, Your Rules Make your shop really pop with customizable decor. Style points aren't the only perk; decorating your shop just right can improve your prices, make better quality potions, and more!
