_childDocuments_.review: This game needs a new game+! I binged through the whole game and my immediate thoughts are that cards being tied to character relationship is both neat and terrible. Especially when you fall in love with a characters aesthetics and then their cards guide you too a play style that is antithetical to what you want to play. Also a post game/free-play where you can just run your shop without competitions. I am realizing this is going from review to suggestion but i do recommend this game immensely and between amazing characters and a pretty good gameplay loop its a solid 7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty good, the animations are gorgeous, the negotiation mini game is pretty fun. BUT, it is not a casual shop management sim. The slice of life sim part is also pretty good, the only thing that i can think of for improving it is if it was actually voice acted.Finally the game ends on the 50th day, there is nothing after that fact, which is disappointing. _childDocuments_.review: After getting through the fourth competition, I'd say the biggest issue with this game is its "hit the ground running" mentality. One of the things that I liked the most about it was the fact that it looked like a good cute game that I could relax to, but instead, the first 50 days are filled with massive amounts of stress you're under to produce very high level potions for the competitions, as well as managing to make enough money to pay for the ingredients, equipment, and upgrades that you'll need to do that. I really was hoping to be able to ease into the game first before jumping straight into a nightmarish marathon of scrambling around to not end up as a literal slave.All that said, I have loved this game the entire time, stress aside. Since that's something a little too subjective, I won't hold it against the game, as some people love that stress. What is great about it is basically everything else. The characters are very fun, almost all of them are completely believable, the world they've built, the little details sprinkled in about history and current events. I especially love the animation. It's not like it's the most amazing animation ever, but that isn't the point. The emotion that the characters show is so good, and the interactions between characters is pretty funny. Also, while the variety of romanceable characters is a little small, what they do with it is great. I was very happy to have that aspect there as something to do between days of selling. As for what happens once you max out your love interest, so far, it hasn't done anything for the one I chose beyond the final date, and now it seems like nothing fun happens with it. I would like to see some kind of system for going on interesting dates, or activities you can do together, maybe some kind of minigame or way to gain extra items. I on't know if that's there and I just haven't gotten to it yet, but if it isn't, I really hope that they either make DLC, or make another game with those kinds of options available.Also, and this is just me, so don't count it against the game if you don't care about this, I would have liked there to be voice acting. For the price of this game, I imagine the way they kept the game from being more expensive was to not have to pay VA's to come in and record a ton of lines. I just like voices in my games these days, but it's not exactly a deal breaker. Besides, it does allow for streamers to put in their own voices while playing, so that is a bonus for them.Overall, an 8.5 out of 10, possibly 9 depending on how things end.Edit 1: Oh, I did forget to mention one GLARING flaw that I will call the devs out on, and that is the piss poor "random" chance of pulling stress cards based on the percentage likelihood After all, when I have an 8% chance of pulling a damn stress card and I get 2 stress cards in my first hand, I am legitimately a bit angry about that. It makes it near impossible to actually enjoy a session of selling sometimes when it pulls crap like that. If I have an 8% chance to pull a card, I should get MAYBE 1 card for that hand, not f***ing two.Amended score= 8/10, maybe 8.5 if the ending is good.Edit 2- So I just finished the game... and it just ends. No continuing on to see how much you can make, no fun dates with your romantic choice... nothing. And as for the romantic choice, the thing I was pretty excited about, you get one series of sort-of dates, one scene when you max out your relationship... and then not even any real acknowledgement that you even did it after that. This game is literally trash after completing it and realizing the devs didn't even let you continue playing after beating it and finish maxing out your relationships with the other people in the game to earn all their haggling tips, or learn interesting things about them, just, "Oh, so you beat our overly stressful and super short game? Here, go play it again knowing there's no real payoff. We're very glad you handed over your hard-earned money for our half-ass excuse for a game."Final score= 5/10. Good mechanics, amazing animation for a game, decent plotline, absolute garbage ending that doesn't even give you a celebration scene with your love interest after winning the final competition, and no continuation to keep running your shop without the stress after the competition is over. DO NOT PAY FULL PRICE. Get this on a deep discount and it'd be worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: The word that kept coming to mind while I played Potionomics was 'crystalized'. It is such a well executed formation of time based, card building, social and crafting mechanics along with a gorgeously animated presentation, witty writing and the soundtrack is god tier. It hits every note as clear as a bell.I wholly recommend this game for anyone who loves Recettearlikes, animation, card building and social/dating games. I have one caveat. however. Do not be fooled by the presentation, the hypnotically charming soundtrack and fun writing. This game is no slouch, your ass needs to be selling potions or you will lose. I've seen a lot people now who looked at the character art and dating mechanics and thought, "" and were gravely mistaken. It's not hard by any means and once you get into the rhythm of the game and diversify the tasks you do per a day, you'll find a deeply engaging recettearlike (that's what we're calling these now).On the side of the spectrum, you have people who love these types of games and wish it was even more difficulty. The fact that its able to engage both these demographics is I think a strength. Lots of games are either chill dating sims or time based bullet hells but you don't often find many games that slot nicely in between those two and still come out engaging for both parties. One thing I do want, and this is my pitch to the developers, New Game+ mode. I want it harder, I want to use all the mechanics I have access to by the end of the game (including my fully furnished shop) and I want to go through the dating mechanics again but without having to go through the whole shebang of introductions. Hell, I even want to see whatever New Game+ jokes the writing would have in store for me. That is my one criticism that I know I'm going to absolutely dominate this game, no challenge, in the next run because even by the end of my first run there was an entire mechanic (tied to a marketing moth girl) that I didn't even utilise. So I would, at the very least, extra difficulty options.Also I want to sleep with Muktuk.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: This game is everything I've wanted since discovering that alchemy was a mechanic in games. It takes inspiration from Recettear and does so much more with it. Everything is perfect. PERFECT. The potion-making is detailed and requires planning, but never gets frustrating. The haggling is dynamic, interesting, and involves the friendship growth aspect of the game so well that it feels seemless. And the characters?!? C'mon. I love them. Unapologetically. (Muktuk is the icing on the cake, that big artistic himbo.)When I finished the game, I legit teared up. I've been working on a game that, mechanically, looks very similar to this one. And it's amazing to see what that kind of game can look like with fantastic development, writing, and animation. Stunning. Buy this game and support this jaw-dropping studio. And thanks to the creators for letting us play this gem.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR, the game's extremely fun but a bit short-lived. I'm not gonna lie, this game made balancing numbers with ratios fun for me.Making potions is fun, interacting with characters is fun (which all of the characters are great in personality and design, too), the card game aspect is REALLY fun, and overall I was invested in this silly little world.It's super simple, but that kind of adds to the charm. Even with the simple premise, there's a lot of complexity trying to use certain ingredients to get the desired potions you want. It's just a bit of a shame that it's so short lived. _childDocuments_.review: 4/5When I got this game I quickly became addicted, The haggling, resource collection and social links made this game feel like persona with more depth. The time crunch and weekly deadlines seemed worrying but most of that worry was gone when I realised the game has an auto save for each day on top of your usual 20 save files. So getting stuck on a contest isn't heavily punishing for those who use their saves sparingly.My only two complaints are bug related, and that involved one of Xid's animations where she lifts her guitar constantly looping, it would be more bearable if not for the constant clanging sound the animation made every 2 seconds. _childDocuments_.review: Overall I liked it a lot. The game mainly revolves around this cycle of making potions, befriending characters and getting better cards that you use when you sell those potions.Making potions can seem both like the hardest and the easiest thing in the same time until you find your way of doing things. There can be a lot of unplanned events that occur when it comes to making and selling potions, and it can feel great when your stars align or your strategy proves successful.Each character is quirky in their own way and has their own blend of charisma, especially if you like over-the-top or dramatic characters.There still are things that feel rough around the edges. Things can depend a bit too much on RNG at the beginning of the game, when you can't afford many ingredients, so you have to make do with what you discover. The haggle card game has reasonable depth, there are many strategies that you can develop while combining the cards you get from each character, but after a while it can get pretty repetitive and formulaic.

_childDocuments_.review: I very much like this game. But I have some serious critiques. 1. This is a rogue-like. If thats your thing, cool.2. You work so hard to meet the deadlines that are required, and if you fail, you get to restart. Either wherever you saved, or at the beginning or whatever you prefer. I did restart a few times to try and sort things out better. 3. You work so damn hard to get it all done, to succeed with the requirements in the game, and then its over. Its done. Finito.There is no chance to get to know the characters better once the pressure is off, or to find better ingredients, or to expand your shop to see how big it can get and how good you can get. Its just done. I've worked very hard so far on this game, restarted from various spots, including the beginning, to basically min max my way to winning, and I've discovered that there is no honeymoon period. Theres no extra. Just the competition. That is incredibly saddening and has now made my stance be that until this is fixed, I will not play it. Pros:Characters are great. Potion mixing can be frustrating but is overall a great brain workout. Its incredibly satisfying to work threw making better potions and making things work. Its really wholesome. Cons: I lost sleep over how I could be doing things better. It can be quite tough if your ingredients arent working, if you cant haggle well, or your stress gets you. There is no endgame honeymoon period. Everything feels rushed. You only have so long to finish certain requirements, and within those times, you are ENTIRELY focused on how to get better haggling tips, making the potions, and getting your shop able to handle a better volume of customers and products. ANYTHING to get an edge over opponents that get progressively harder. Yes I realise thats a game concept in of itself, but theres no chance after all that to enjoy who you are working with, or go explore the vast island that you are working on. I feel like there should be more to this game. I recommend it, because it is fun, but be aware of what it does and does not do.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game to almost anyone, but not quite everyone. The game has 4 interconnected parts:1. Buying stuff. Decisions between long-term investments and short-term gain are interesting and challenging. You'll need ingredients for...2. Mixing potions. It's a math mini-game, and the only part of the game I'd say use a guide if you don't like math. You'll need the potions for...3. Selling stuff. The most fun part of the game in my opinion, it's a deck-builder card game to get the best value for your potion. And to get new cards, you need to...4. Role play. It's not super in-depth (you only have a choice of 2 dialogue options), but the character personalities, backstories, and humor is top-notch.As long as you like at least 3 of the 4 of these parts, you'll love this game, because there's a way to avoid spending a lot of time on the one you don't like. Well, except figuring out what to buy. If you don't like figuring out ratios, use a guide. If you don't like the haggling mini-game/deck builders, you get a vending machine that will do the work (the disadvantage is it's only a 15% mark-up instead of the 50% you could get from haggling). And if you don't like stories, well, you're weird, but I guess you can click through the dialogue.Challenge level is adequate, but not stressful. It's nice that the 4 parts of the game interact, so you can lean into the part you're good at. Who cares if your potions smell bad if you can consistently haggle them to a 50% mark up? If you like being a perfectionist with your optimization problems, you'll get rewarded. But if you fail to optimize, it's not back-breaking.The main criticism of the game is due to lack of automation, the late game can feel like a slog. Well, I feel you can still get your money's worth and avoid playing the last 10 days, but I'll see how I feel when I get to that point.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could rate this more than 'thumbs up', 'thumbs down'.  I rated thumbs up because I like the game but it has major QOL issues.  While the player can sort the shops ingredient inventory, they can't rearrange the ingredients.  If you want ingredients sorted by most used too bad can't do it. Want to place them by magimims highest to lowest, nope out of luck.  Additionally the ingredient vendor has no sort ability at all. Want to see only the A magimims that Quinn sells, so sorry Charlie, can't happen.  My biggest complaint is that the mouse cursor is teeny tiny.  So I hope you are not a middle aged gamer, like me, or you have eagle sight because it's really hard to see the cursor.  I've tried changing display ratios and resolutions, neither of which had an affect on cursor size.So, with complaints out of the way, what is the game? It's a shop management game with dating sim aspects that incorporates card battler mechanics into the haggling system.The main character inherits a potion shop after her uncle Oswald dies, unfortunately she also inherits her uncle's crippling debt.  The game sees the main character enter into a potion making tournament, whose cash prizes will enable her to pay off her sizable debt.  The tournament is split into 5 phases. Each phase takes 10 in game days with the last day being the day of the competition.  Along the way the player will buy ingredients, upgrade their shop, and have opportunities to build in game relationships. If romance is your thing you can choose any character to pursue.  Higher friendship levels with the characters reward the player with different cards for haggling and at certain levels discount coupons for goods and services.Half of the first phase is taken up with the tutorial.  So 5 in game days at the beginning are all tutorial which made the beginning feel rather hectic to me. As other people have noted there is no free play mode which is unfortunate.  The player will always be faced with time constraints and how best to manage their time per day as well as the days before the competition.Each competition phase has 3 different potions which must be brewed to complete the phase.  Each phase also has different quality requirements for the potions.All and all a good game.  It could be made better with some quality of life improvements as well as some display stability.  I found that if something happened with the steam client, update, achievement unlock, someone messaging me, etc., the game would reset to a default display forcing me to set the display back to my preferences.  Sometimes this was annoying and sometimes it made the game unplayable.  As for game play, the game uses a daily autosave feature.  I highly recommend taking full advantage of this and reloading less than productive days.  The late game is a little lack luster, but the story beats are cutesy and entertaining.

_childDocuments_.review: This is overall a great game and I really enjoyed it. (I have only played 4 hours so far) I will focus on game design as I am a designer myself.In terms of game design, what I really like about the game is the relationship progression. As the game goes on, you can build relationships with the characters in the game. Each of these characters can provide services that you need such as ingredients, upgrades, adventures and so on. Having better relationships will grant you coupons so that you can receive business benefits from these relationships. These characters are designed to have their own personalities, so knowing them will allow you to know them better and unlock dialogues. (Not sure if we can unlock stories as well?) With excellent animations, well designed characters really make you care about these characters. Moreover, building relationships can unlock new negotiation cards from each of the character. The most brilliant design is that the function of cards matches the personalities of each character, and it makes sense. This boosts the immersion of game. However, these characters can also become your customers as well. But right now I don’t need how relationship building can affect their behaviours as customers.Comparing to relationship progression, I do think running potion brewing is a little bland. Potion brewing is all about adding a combinations of ingredients to a cauldron according to the recipe. There are traits to the ingredients which adds trade-off to what ingredients you should use. You can upgrade the cauldron to enhance the capacity and number of ingredients you can put in. These designs are all great because it makes the system to have more depth. But it seems bland because all you interact with in this process is selecting ingredients. Sometimes dragging and dropping ingredients can be tiresome. Also there is less exploration in the potion brewing which makes it less exciting. You can certainly improvise, but combining the facts that brewing takes time, ingredients have cost, and the pacing of the game drives you to achieve high efficiency, all of them discourage the improvisation.

_childDocuments_.review: This type of game is right up my alley, so I'm enjoying it. It has deck building, resource management, math - but there are multiple solutions to the same problem, funny dialogue and interesting characters. Plus, there are deadlines and challenges that keep it interesting. You unlock more resources and potion options as you progress, constantly meeting new characters and improving your deck. My only gripes (so far): I have a beastly computer and somehow this game manages to dip into single digits FPS from time to time, regardless of the visual settings. It "auto-detects" all of my graphics as "epic" in 4K but not sure what that means because I can't notice any differences in visuals from "low" to "epic" at all. Not sure why there are performance issues in this game because it's basically a point and click game with static character models but it manages to max out my graphics card occasionally. And there are WAY too many loading screens. As mentioned, this games graphical style is simplistic AF. What is taking so long to load? Why does it need to reload the environment every time you change areas? Was this their solution to optimization to fix the performance issues? Because if so, it sucks and it didn't work.I have rage quit playing this game more than once because it is just soooooooo poorly optimized. I can play Minecraft in 4k with max render distance and shaders with no lag. How is this point and click game eating more RAM than that? Luckily the core gameplay loop is still fun enough to keep me coming back.

_childDocuments_.review: Endlessly clever, funny, and charming. There's so much love and talent put into every crevice of this game it's hard to zero in on any one thing. The art and animation are immediately eye catching, but behind the flash is an array of characters so entertaining it's hard not to play without just smiling constantly.Behind this is a rather deep collection of gameplay systems involving - you guessed it - making and selling potions. Overall this works remarkably well considering how many different systems are in play. It's deeply satisfying brewing, aging, marketing, pitching, and finally securing a big potion sell. However this also happens to be one of the game's biggest weaknesses. You see, understanding how all these layers interact with each other takes time and even though the game tries to ease the player into it, it's hard to really get your bearings before the first potion competition, which if you fail, you lose the game (keep multiple saves!). However even after you understand the systems it's still possible to get overwhelmed with the sheer amount of planning and moving parts involved, some of which the game, admittedly, does a poor job of displaying at any given time. Despite these minor frustrations I can only recommend Potionomics. The delicate balancing act of managing a potion shop is overall very gratifying and any faults are completely eclipsed by the sheer charm and entertainment of it all. It's probably my #1 game of 2022!

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Masterwork Edition-Potionomics is an amazing game for a couple reasons. The polish and love in this game is evident as over time feedback has been taken and operated on. Beyond that the fact that years after release it was updated to have fully voiced dialogue in the interaction scenes (though certain out of dialogue text isn't voice acted reminiscent of games like persona.) The attention to certain requests like an endless mode and difficulty changing, as well as a polyamorous mode are all appreciated as it is from community feedback. Beyond that the historical listening to concerns about difficulty and menu's are also worth shouting out.Now all that being said, this game does have minor quirks I am well willing to lookover that others may not respond to as kindly. I've beaten the game on original difficulty and now almost completely replayed on cozy mode. Cozy mode is extremely easy if you know what you're doing, I never appreciated how much travel time factored into difficulty, and I don't know if they tuned pricing in some ways but I absolutely crushed the bank in cozy. Another consideration is how even with the menu updates and such making potion ingredients and other things more parsable, there isn't quite the robust menu system that I would like. At times the menu is still a pain to navigate especially at later game, when trying to find exactly what's needed and flipping through pages can be cumbersome. Lastly the minor delays in animation and action in buffering can get annoying especially in two places, going up and to basement, and traveling between areas. All of these little things add up but I can recognize how minor they are when in-spite of it all I just respect the game and love so many aspects about it. All-in-all, this is one of the perfectly me games, like Battle-Chef Brigade and other games in that vein, I worry people will not give it the love and respect it deserves. I mean it has so much love and care and has such a great team I just desperately want to see it iterated on and improved. The batter mechanic mixed with the potion brewing and everything make it a joy for me, and though it's not perfect it does a great job. At it's price point and over the time they dedicated to it I would firmly recommend this to people who are willing to give it a try. Original Reviews:Game is excellent but the negative reviews are right about certain things. The game needs a certain level of polish it doesn't have. The game should be completely playable on controller but doesn't have that integrated into it. Beyond that the game really needs ingredient sorting, recipe saving and some other little things that honestly add up.However, I love this game, it's a sort of game I've been wanting for YEARS. It's great and really fun it just needs more polish. I think it's easily worth price of entry personally.Edit: Now having 15 more hours in this game, I have some changed opinions. I think the game does have a difficulty problem, not the one towards the beginning people seem to think it does, towards the end however I think it does. Most of it manufactured behind unintuitive game design.  Towards the beginning the game is masterful with not much to manage, and tight inventory. But as the games scope expands, its tools to help automate and manage don't expand with it. As most of these games go usually as the scope grows, you get resources and tools to make it more manageable. But the game lacks key features such as good inventory management, good automation systems and passive income generation among other things. I think if the game updates to work on these miss qualities it will be masterful but at this point it's marred by a less than stellar late game. I really hope they work on it.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played a ton of deck-building games before but if you a fan of Business Tycoon style games and Deck Building games... then I got to say this is the one to play. Never before have I seen such a charming game in terms of its character's interactions and art style that makes the gameplay so straight forward but the strategy and combinations in the deck-building section are extensive and in a single word "beautiful"My only complaint and I say this after completing the game over 6 times and mixing different character's cards to make a truly amusing and unique "Haggling Strategy" that is the game is very much worth every penny that I paid for it. If they ever make a DLC or sequel or even a prequel where we learn more about the main character's Uncle and how he gets into the mess that leads his niece to take over his shop, I can assure you I would buy it one day of release. So just to wrap up this review, if you're not only a fan of deck-building games but also enjoy Story driven games and "Feeling like you're interacting in a graphic novel" then I suggest you buy this game and see for yourself exactly what I mean.Gameplay 8/10 "Simple and feels like I'm reading a truly epic graphic novel and ever-changing with each time you play it again and again. My only complaint from this is I wish there was a hard mode as during the contests you can just outright win without playing a single card."Art Style 10/10 "It's cute and feels like you're reading a graphic novel but you're the one writing it as each action can change how you chose to play the game. Smooth transitions and overall some of the art you see during more intense or romantic moments is very well portrayed by the character's movements and expressions even though the game is not voiced"Story 10/10 "From a standpoint of some random girl running a failing potion shop and learning her uncle is dead only to get settled with his debt(Without a choice I might add!) to a successful young witch working hard to survive and succeed with every other person in the potion business out to run you out of business. The friends you make along the way and the stories they share are truly heartwarming. The relationships you form and the skills you develop through friendship in this heartwarming story are something I would encourage you to see and experience for yourself. Overall for the price point of $30 Canadian in my case, this is something I would say to try and I hope you get as wonderful an experience from this game as I did from my 30 hours of playing in the past 2 weeks alone. This game is truly a triple-A title if I could label one as such. I encourage and congratulate Voracious Games and I can only see more big things from them if this game is anything to predict what kinds of titles they will be giving us in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: "And that's not all, buy my potions now and get absolutely nothing for free!"Visual novels are an acquired taste and most people will bounce off them, often deeming them 'not even games'. Potionomics strives to stand out in that crowd, with the game blurring the line between a visual novel, a deck-building card game, a time management, potion brewing and shopkeeping simulator, all in one tidy package wrapped in stylish artwork and, quite frankly, far too many pretty characters! It's just not fair, they can't ALL look that good!But alas, they very much do. Character art, animation and emoting are all top notch and Potionomics is a delight to play just to see the exaggerated animations and expressions will come up as Sylvia charms her way to another sale.Sylvia is, as one might have guessed from the above, a maker of potions. Having inherited her late uncle's potion shop on a remote magical island, she finds herself also having inherited a debilitating load of debt and a curious talking owl that suggests she partake in a series of potion making contests to win enough prize money to clear her debt and free her to pursue her dreams.The core gameplay revolves around a loop of crafting potions by balancing six types of ingredients, along with a host of special features like strong smell or pleasant looking bubbles that alter the value of potions brewed. Once Sylvia has her potions, she can let in the customers and initiate a haggling card game in which the player must balance the stress of sales work with suitable combinations of cards to push up the price of her potions and securing a sale before the customer's patience runs out. The money earned can then be put towards more varied and better ingredients, allowing more advanced potions to be crafted for greater income. Each part of this gameplay loop clicks into its place almost immediately.The result is simply a fun experience, though the looming contest deadlines that demand the player's finest potions are always there to direct focus.To tie all the gameplay mechanics together Potionomics provides a cast of colourful characters to engage with. Sylvia can meet and forge relationships with various folks on the island, who then provide her with services such as rare ingredients, fuel for potion brewing or improved equipment and furniture. Some adventuring type characters can also accept potions to fuel their adventures, returning with loot from the various regions of the island that Sylvia can then use in her craft. Some basic dialogue options are provided to allow the player to fine-tune conversations to better friendships and perhaps even lead to a passionate love story to form (yes, of course I dated the walrus-man, he was objectively the best pick!). To motivate the player to pay attention, in addition to the snappy dialogue and animation, is the reward of new cards for use in the haggling minigame, which are unlocked whenever a new level of friendship is reached with a character.All in all I found Potionomics a blast to play and an easy recommend! Just keep in mind that having multiple save files is a good idea, as the game is not going to give you mercy if you find yourself missing a contest deadline!Playtime: 20+ hours (A single playthrough)Ratings (1-10)Visual: 9Audio: 6Story: 7Gameplay: 7Overall: 8

_childDocuments_.review: LOVE this game but rating a 7/10 ~ game has a HUGE DoWNfaLL taking away that chunk of 3 points...but..I really love this game.. the storyline, characters, graphics and idea of it ~ but there is ONE thing that is very frustrating and will probably keep me from continuing on.  The TIME that you are given to accomplish various tasks BEFORE competition day is HiNDeRiNg.  Time is not a typical clock counting down in minutes (but large blocks of time), and these 'blocks' disappear w each single task you do.  There are not enough 'blocks' to ~ make potions, make money, evolve friendships, travel, find new ingredients (by way of character friendship explorations), to have certain said 'found' ingredients be available to purchase (usually next day).. etc.. but when this block of time disappears, it makes the 'day' just go by WAY too fast to complete anything that needs to be done.Maybe i'm missing something because others have seemed to get through it fine.  Maybe I could look on YouTube and see how things are being accomplished in such a short amount of given time..  but I'd really love to figure it out on my own and feel this is a type of game that should be simple enough to do so. Traveling can take the whole morning segment.. (and usually there is more than one 'friend' you need to visit and level up).. Aside from this issue with time , everything else about the game is perfect.  It's humorous, endering, sweet, heartfelt.. maybe one day i'll try again (for the 4th or 5th time) i've lost count.. but until I see an 'update' where time is somewhat fixed.. _childDocuments_.review: Kudos to the designers, artists and writers for Potionomics. They've managed to break the pretty tired mould of the genre and deliver something that is cute, engaging and a pure joy to experience.However, it is let down dramatically by the difficulty tuning. You can not be doing anything that is not min-maxing your shop output or else you'll end up in an unfixable failure state and have to seriously consider restarting the story from the beginning. After sitting through all of the dialogue two or more times, and working out that actually spending time with the characters is an act of self-sabotage, whatever joy was there is ruined.Wait for balance patches before considering this title, and not just minor ones. The balance of the game needs a completely overhaul or you'll more than likely fail to even succeed at the first "easy" tournament, and failure is the end of your game with no room for compromise.

The characters are a joy to get to know, and it's very easy to root for the MC.There are quite a few QoL issues that will hopefully be resolved, and the difficulty is definitely front loaded. That's pretty typical for 'build up from nothing' games, though. A first play through may be kind of rough as you get used to the various systems, but once everything clicks a fresh start will be an enjoyable cake walk.My main complaint about the game is that there is very little replayability once you have a good run under your belt. The only differences between good runs would be who you romance, and maybe making alternate (and suboptimal) dialogue choices when chatting to the cast.Still, it's a great game for the price and I'd be excited to see more in this series!
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: So I will say right away that I absolutely loved this game at the time of this review (14 hours). The story has a really good sense of humour, the characters have lovely design, the game is colourful & nicely designed artistically wise.. BUT it is a game that I found extremely grindy, the mechanics are SOOO intertwined that you have to think DAYS in advance for what you are planning ahead to do and to sell to maximise your profits. I really wanted to like this game to the fullest and even restarted a playthrough after going for 13 in-game days but to no avail. It was going to be basically the same. It might be a personal issue and my smol smooth brain that it cannot handle all these decisions to make in a cute game that I mainly wanted to play for the dating sim aspect of it without expect the game to be so brutal with my choices when it comes to potion making and the likes. I still highly recommend it cause it is a very interesting and unique game but do be prepared to be challenge through and through, to have to think really really ahead and to maybe put the dating sim side of the game on hold until you have enough breathing room. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: I'm always down for games like this, crafting with a side of romance and a whole lot of money to be made. The art and characters look amazing and all of them are very fun to interact with.My biggest con to the game though is time. It's a time slot system where you have to decide what you're doing throughout the day, this isn't a new concept to games and seems fairly simple as things are labelled in how many time slots they'll use. The problem is that you have 10 days per competition and it feels like you can't access part of the game because of how careful you have to be. I passed the first week fairly easy but the second week has a decent jump and you have to use multiple slots to visit people, get ingredients, brew potions, make money and of course sell potions (2 slots to open shop or just use vendor which is no slots). The game also pushes new characters to meet and utilize but there were so many by the second week I found I just couldn't interact with most of them, they all cost gold which you need for farming ingredients and upgrading.As much as this list sounds, I believe it's doable but while also trying to do conversations with people which also costs time slots I found myself missing out trying to micro manage so much. I failed my second week which I was ok with since I figured it would just push back the challenge but it makes you go through the challenge and fail sending you back to the main menu. My last saved slot being just before the challenge so I have to start a new game so I can focus more on getting my upgrades in.I still recommend the game as it is really fun and it does have a lot but I recommend to any new players to pace yourself and focus on getting the potions up before doing too much side things. Upgrading is a must have so save what gold you can for that while also farming for ingredients. Cheers!
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one giant optimization puzzle with a level of graphic and musical quality that rivals triple-A. I personally LOVE the optimization aspect, I understand that's not everyone's thing but the sheer amount of effort that went into the characters, the writing, the models, everything; it's seriously worth a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loving this game! There are definitely some quality of life updates that could be made and it would benefit from a new game + feature or an endless mode, but overall it is an incredible game. I love being a bisexual flirt who is bad at math and fumbles their way to success. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: First 20-30 hours are brilliant. After that, if you are playing optimally, the game drags a bit. Recommended for casual gamers.Audio and animation here are fantastic and wonderful to behold. Characters are all wholesome with some light chuckles of comedy. Card game is well designed and the initial potion making is fun. However late game potion making becomes incredibly cumbersome, which can slow you down and ruin the games pacing (which is perfect during chapter 1-3). The second half of the game needs quality of life improvements. Firstly a way for you to save decks so you can swap and experiment easier. Secondly (and most importantly) a way to speed up the process of creating potions to reduce the amount of work required to make potions. As the game progresses, and you get more cauldrons, with higher capacity and more ingredients it can be a really draining part on the game flow.Overall its a great game if played casually. Enjoy the wonderful animation, audio and characters but don't let yourself get bogged down making the perfect potion each time.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid game with close to no replayability will nonetheless grab you with it's simple plot, great soundtrack, interesting mechanics and amazing characters! The ways of how to play the game can differ a lot based on your personal playstyle and finding those ways to improve is great! Would love to have the infinite mode after the end of the game to maybe experience a full shop sim, but it is still a great game and I highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely fun, and super charming! But I do agree with some of the negative reviews about it being just a tad too difficult.EDIT: They released a balance patch! The difficulty was decreased <3EDIT 2: Updating my review after the big update- the game was already amazing and worth its price before but now it's an absolute MUST BUY! I really cannot recommend this game enough!EDIT 3: Please implement something like a gallery of recollections because I'd love to go back and see some conversations of the love interests as well as the kissies or hugs!
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Very captivating, it's easy to get lost in the grind of making potions to see that line go up while rushing to get the right ingredients to make that perfect potion.- Fun characters each with their own unique stories, personalities and bartering styles.- Good power leveling (with the right RNG, see below), everything except for the last week felt like a genuine challenge.- Very pretty visuals- Great musicCons:- A couple of bugs ranging from game breaking (You can duplicate high tier cauldrons by placing them in one of the shop slots (I forget which one) after unlocking all 6 cauldron slots, this saves you lots of money and makes your potion crafting OP) to just minor annoyances which break immersion (Owl does not reappear properly in week 4, which means that his commentary and model are missing from cut-scenes and the end of day screen) -- however I hope these are being patched.- There is no endless game mode and the game forcefully ends after day 50, so if you were hoping to keep playing and building your shop after the competitions or maybe finish building your relationship ranks (like I was) tough luck. Really this is my biggest gripe with the game.- Heavily RNG based. If you don't get the right ingredients in week one good luck in week 2 with less money to build off, and this compounds into weeks 3-5, so the game can either be mind numbingly easy if you get good drops in weeks 1-2 or horribly difficult if you don't. This leads to plenty of restarts which the game's visual novel style storytelling just isn't ideal for (good luck trying to remember who you hung out with and how you leveled them up etc)- If you have a better potion than your competitor on day 50 you'll enter barter mode and then immediately win without actually bartering, which is annoying.- Characters give us conflicting information about what happened with the island's history which creates frustrating plot holes.- You don't actually get to craft the final potion Sylvia just produces it for a cutscene.- Very little replayability since pretty much everything is the same in cutscenes (except who you date, but that takes a long time and you can only go through the same cutscenese over and over so many times) and you will almost certainly be forced to replay parts due to above mentioned RNG.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: With Only a handful of hours spent in-game I by personal proxy think the game has a complex concept using a strategy and time-based haggling system whilst creating a manner of various potion types.I further agree with other reviews that a sandbox mode would utterly benefit the game as the game itself is a great way to blow off a few hours without batting an eye.Current rating 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: This game is cute as hell. addicting and there is one character that really screams the "Mommy?...sorry...Mommy?.....sorry" vibe. I adore this game and hope you  will too. Best blind purchase I have made in a long time. Buy it. You wont regret it.Ok quick aside....Gameplay is fun but stressful, Any time/day limit style game will be like that. Making potions is surprisingly fun and well thought out. Resource generation for potions and the like takes a bit getting use to and some risk/reward tactics. easy to understand a bit harder to master.8/10 and I will be buy a sequel if there is one and checking out more from this dev.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant and one of this year's best. Potionomics have you juggling deadlines, time, relationships, finances, and cards all the while making and selling potions. Initially it can be intimidating and overwhelming to get a grasp on the mechanics, but once you familiarize yourself with Potionomics's insanely addicting gameplay loop you'll be playing the economy and your competitors like a fiddle while admiring its animations and soundtrack.My only issues are with the UI that would've benefited from having more QoL added to it. A collect all potions and ingredients options would've been convenient. The characters also exude so much charm and personality that sometimes I wished the game would've included some VA.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super cute on all accounts. The art is what initially won me over, but the game that is underneath is also really fun. And I don't generally go for management sims so that's saying something. It's basically a deck builder, management sim, and visual novel all blended into one. It's no without some flaws, The UI could be improved in a few aspects to make thing a little more user friendly. Namely buying ingredients can get tedious as there doesn't seem to be any way to mass buy them. But that's something that could easily be patched. And I still really enjoyed the game despite a few minor issues like that.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: The game is incredibly charming and made with love. As for gameplay and difficulty-wise, the time management as well as card game aspect can be very intimidating and hard during the first few weeks. However, with good time management skills, it does get significantly easier after the third week. The haggling minigame actually has a deck that can completely break the game while the gardening aspect can help you snowball to the point of beating competitions without haggling. Tip: Captivate your customers.That said, there are still some bugs and glitches that might make for a less enjoyable experience but with the amount of love put into this game, I have faith that they will be patched out eventually. There are also some QoL that is very needed like checking custom orders while outside your shop, sorting ingredients while buying, gifting or even sorting potions by price, type. Edit: They did update the QoL and added bug fixes to where it mattered.As for the visual novel aspects, despite some complaints about there being not enough time in the day to hangout, it is actually possible to 100% all relationships with time to spare just by giving them gifts you grew with your garden.Probably the most fun I've had in a while with a more linear management game. Do wish that it has a sandbox or endless mode though.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Wow i am genuinely impressed how well made this game is.The graphical side is truly something to remember: the styles and the way they are used ingame are just majestic and they build the world and interactions like no other game does.The many different gameplay types ranging from cards through the dating-sim and finally the potion making itself provide a very large size of things to do altho i admit the time limit in one day is a little small to gain full aprecieation from the many things you can do.The plot is quite nice but a tad predictable in parts but thats not really an issue for me.TLDR: the game is worth your money and you will not be dissapointed
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: From game play to dialogue Potionomics is nothing but charming.A deeply passionate game that wears its heart on it's sleeve,  dual-part life management sim, and deck-builder/card game Potionomics perfectly balances a lovely story and entertaining game play all while making each character equally interesting and filled with depth a feat that feels lacking in similar styled games. All of which would make a great game on it's own, yet Potionomics has an ace up it's sleeve, even though it's hand is already loaded, the visual presence is nothing less than stunning with immaculate animations and art style and direction, from icons to UI the entire package is beautiful. The only negative I can conceive for this game, while not to sound cliche is that it ends. (this part pending until/if an endless mode is added for the post game)
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: This is a broadly OK game. It's a very polished and well thought out (mechanically) Deck Building/Potion Business sim. However, there are severe pacing and resource management issues. The current pace of the game does not allow for full use of the mechanics and discovery of the story/romance elements. The time and methods of the ingredient gathering conflict with the core game play of selling and crafting potions. Forcing you into poor choices, running for efficiency, lacking the time/materials to utilize other features (Looking at you custom orders). These issues make the game somewhat frustrating to play overall. I'm 9 hours in, and it's mostly me being stubborn about getting my value out of the purchase.I'll update in the future if my views change.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: You come in expecting another potion crafting game, and yes it is, but there is so much to it. Stunning art, characters, and the best part is the gameplay mechanic haggling prices. One of the best executions I have ever witnessed and I would recommend this game to anyone who likes a casual game. And yes, I managed to complete this game in a single session in 18h. All I can say, I got hooked!10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to edit this into a proper review once I've played much more, but just for the sake of clarity: Any negative reviews about the difficulty, about time management being stringent and no option to change that, etc., those reviews are now defunt; the game, on the 22nd of October, got a HUGE update that added a plethora of QoL options including very cozy difficulty settings! Game's in a great state now!
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, it's like if disney/pixar made a alchemy video game. Pro's:fantastic artperfect music great characterslighthearted and charming settingstory is wholesome but lite in many spotsCons:no new game plusmenu can be clunky at times, with some load speed issuesstory needed more events & interactions outside of dating sim.changing or upgrading items is a pain and has too many extra steps in menu.can be hard starting out, then difficulty drops off completely after second boss.could use a random/mini-boss event to help change up shop loop.           Rating: 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: so, would I recommend this game. yes, it is cute in appearance, with a neat game cycle.The only complaint is that it ends. Though really, the game being a crafting game I was entirely expecting the game to continue after paying off the debt, similar to Recettear, But no, it ends and auto saves before the last face off. that aside it is nice.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent, well-made game with absolutely incredible character design and vibes. I had a lot of fun playing it and seeing what happened. The storyline is cute and fun, and the mood of the game is lighthearted and frivolous.The gameplay is in complete contrast. As has been said by many other reviews, especially negative ones, this is not a fun, chill game. I play a lot of intense, grindy games but hits you hard with the micromanaging. You absolutely do not have to play optimally to beat this game. However, the game throws so many things at you and it's impossible to determine what to prioritize. Do you upgrade you cauldrons first? Your decks? Your heroes for better Magimin gathering? Why am I always out of money? Why am I always out of time?I could never play this game for more than a day or two at a time due to the stress build up from trying to manage a million different things at once. I liked that, but it was definitely not what I expected coming in. I would still recommend this game, but with the caveat that you're playing something more akin to Slay the Spire than Stardew Valley.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and absolutely love the characters, the design, and the card and brewing game play is solid. However, The RNG aspects of getting the best for the ingredients is my only major issue, especially trying to make the right potions for the competitions. I'm also a bit disappointed that the competitions are the main part of the game and after day 50 its over. Hopefully there will be a game mode just to play without the competitions being the main goals and have a more chill game experience and paying off the loans by potion selling rather than the competition check points. Also keeping track of queued brews, gardens, and adventurers can be a bit difficult, would have liked a panel of active queued work.Despite those issues i Find the game great and super fun and hope the devs have more in plan for the future also Xid best gal :)
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: I was really happy to get it when it came out and I got through the first 1 in 2 tries but had med stuff happen. I go in now to play the rest and it's all changed. instead of 1 position giving 3, it now gives only 1. it takes all day to make it no matter how many items are in the position. like it use to be. I was not able to make money to keep me afloat. I couldn't make 2 positions for the 2cd contest and lost. it was not fun anymore it was hard work
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Went through 2 playthoughs, It was really nice and charming while it lasted. Hoping for some additional post game content. Felt like I went through a fiery hot relationship that ended ice cold with how abruptly the game throws you into the main menu with no New Game + option after beating the last boss.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Like many said: The first competition after ten days is a bit rough but THEN you can easily enjoy the many funny, heartwarming and even the political-critical stories and dialogues while brewing some potions in between. The animation and art work is wonderful, the writing is excellent and the difficulty is really smoothing itself out a bit after you got to grips with the gameplay a bit.Minor spoiler tip: You really should become at least a bit friendly with Saffron in order to ace the future competitions haggling parts.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: The art style and animations are amazingly vibrant. The way the game immerses you as you play and interact with the other characters is great. But, this isn’t the casual potion making game that I was expecting. If you are going in blind, you very much can fail the first competition.You play through the days sending Mint out for new ingredients, brewing new potions, and getting to know the other characters better. But, then you wasted too much of your time playing around. You didn’t acquire better cards, equipment, or didn’t invest money into maximize the chance of getting better ingredients. Then you got to start from the very beginning because you didn’t set up your play through properly. Otherwise, you save scum to get the better rolls for ingredients, potions, or card draws. I think this game can be improved if there was a game mode without the competition. You just got to play and explore around. A mode where aren’t required to min/max or look up guides. If your looking for a casual alchemist sim game. Potionomics isn’t it.If your looking for a dating sim with randomness and punishments for poor planning. Potionomics is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this one. A fun card puzzle game with some enjoyable potion-making mechanics. I wish there was voice acting, but it still works. Story isn't super complicated or unexpected, but I think the character design and writing is really strong. It would also be nice if there was some post-game stuff where you don't have a required competition and can just build up your potion business.It's a game where if you take any of the individual parts they're not super unique but they're done really effectively and it comes together so well. If you like these types of games you'll like this one, I think.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: A relatively straight forward game all about enconomics and playing the market. The difficulty massively drops in the later game, but realistically that is because you are more knowledgeable and can game the system.The haggle system is interesting, there are a few playstyles you can go for, but none if it is particularly difficult to understand.Every 10 days you have to face off in a literal haggling battle with a rival. I enjoyed most of them, though I guessed the twist for the final boss pretty early on.  Sometimes if you have a good enough potion, you can outright win the battles without haggling, which I find hilarious.If you like potion crafting, time management, and dating sims, this one is for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely writing and characters. Loved seeing the depth and stories they all had.UI/UX was kinda lacking when I played at launch, but looks like recent patches are fixing that up? Even if not, still worth a play, just remember not to be too much of a perfectionist with potion ratios like me I guess, aha, especially later in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game! i love the design of the characters and overall world. The animation is pretty good and the facial expression are really good. My only complain is the time gated gameplay. I wish they don't have the timer that ticks down and will cause Game Over if not focused your time completing task which also is gated in terms of what ingredients you have.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Is a good game! there's some flaws here and there and it does get a little repetitive now and then, or require a bit of save scumming if you ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up some things before the competition, (like leaving your potions in the store). One thing i would like to see is a post-game, i hadn't maxed my characters out yet, and i wanted to play around with some more deck concepts and now i have to restart the game in order to do that.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Game has good art like most others have mentioned and most of gameplay is pretty well put together. The first "boss" challenge is more difficult than it should be. It relies heavily on luck and how quickly you realize exactly what you need to do to be able to actually meet the minimum requirements within the time limit, which is not going to be immediately obvious to the average person. If you don't get that luck and/or realization, you will restart a couple hours worth of gameplay, probably more than once. Many reviewers have stated various things to the effect of "get gud" over the difficulty of the first 10 days but that's not really helpful to anyone. Getting better, in and of itself, should be what the first portion of gameplay is designed around, but instead it's entirely "trial by fire" in that you either figure it out or you fail and restart. wash, rinse, repeat. The game leads you to believe that making money is the main point of the game but in reality you have to basically all but ignore making any money except what is absolutely necessary to keep your adventurer filled with potions and hitting as many friendship and shop upgrades you can as quickly as possible. The game does not give you any even vague attempts to help you past the barebones tutorial and you are entirely dependent on luck to meet a challenge that, despite what those who have passed it claim, is way harder than it should be for the early game. No, reloading saves generally will not help you as some have implied unless you are already close. If you're not on the correct path from the very beginning, you will restart the entire game, otherwise you will just waste time trying to meet the deadline by jumping only a couple days back without the foundation to even make it possible. Good luck.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Take my recommendation with a grain of salt. This game has some tasty treats awaiting inside, but full to the brim with quality of life issues that just drive me insane and mechanics that are both over and under explained. Its definitely not for everyone, and you need to know what you are getting into. I have not yet completed a full run of this game.The Pros:-Amazing characters and animations that are a delight to sit through and watch.-A store management game that I haven't seen the likes of anywhere else.-Clear dialogue trees with NPCS so you know exactly what kind of interaction you will have with them (as a romance/visual novel veteran, PRAISE)-A story that has me invested in the world and it's people.-Potion making is satisfying and always fun.The cons:-Timers. Timers everywhere. Timers to get your brews done, timers to get your relationships going, and the pressure will get to you. Save scumming is all but required. While that's expected from the store management aspect it really messes with the other major game mechanic of socializing and ranking up your confidants. I think the social aspect and selling mechanics are what makes this game shine, and the timer puts me in the mindset of "screw these people, I need money now".-Ingredient gathering is entirely rng. Its impossible to tell what area might net you what you need. Yes, there is some value to discovering each areas unique qualities, but when you have to brew increasingly advanced potions just to get anywhere later on, it would be nice to get a general idea of what areas get you what. I can't tell you how many times I wished for a bestiary or just a list of "What items come from x area" based on ingredients I've already gathered.One of these days I'll likely make a guide on how best to tackle this game without being overwhelmed or a full list of ingredients because I do love it. But if you are here just for the romance (Baptiste my beloved) you will not have a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic game with a lot of charm, the characters are lovable the mechanics are simple but fun and for the price it's worth it. its a stress free game that is nice to just relax and play.Two small problems though.1. the filter function isn't good as it organises them by when you got them not how much they offer so sorting through the shop and my inventory was kind of a hassle especially later in the game.2. no endless mode. i was so convinced that there would be an endless, on the last day i made longer brews planning for missing the entire next day, i was thinking that the first 3 adventures would get a difficulty boost to be on par with the final because i felt like i was missing ingredients and i'd be able to max out my rankings with all the characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable game, the writing is fun, the characters are enjoyable, and I liked the balance between making the potions, selling them, and going around hanging out with the townsfolk.I do think the game is a bit too long, and it gets quite tedious near the end. After day 30 or so, the interactions between Sylvia and the boss of the week really seems to drop off, and this ends up negatively being combined by you having a lot of cauldrons, slimes, and other things to balance, and they all take so much time. Early on, you might be able to get through a day in 5-10 minutes, by day 35, you will be spending 20-30 minutes just trying to get all of your potion slots moving because everything has to be done manually, there are a lot of extra clicks involved in doing basic tasks, and the game just grinds to a halt. It really feels like it was balance and playtested for the first half and then it's like they gave up a bit.Again, it's a recommendation, but I'm a bit disappointed that with the release of the Masterwork Edition (which provides absolutely phenomenal voicework I will say), that they didn't add in quality-of-life enhancements like not having to click the equipment tab EVERY SINGLE BREW to select a new pot. Or having a fast way to sort ingredients with only 1 type (if you want to see ingredients with only A, that's gonna be 8 clicks minimum).
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like Potionomics, I really do. It has a lot of good ideas. But it has too  many of them. And it doesn't do a good job of guiding you in the first part of the game. So I ended up barely making it through the first competition and was unable to make it past the second. And unfortunately the only way to fix my mistakes is to restart the game entirely at this point.There is so much to do in the game, that it's unclear what to prioritize. I tried to balance how I spent my time and that ended up being a huge mistake. You really need to just go hard at ingredient collecting and getting them available at Quinn's shop at first, despite all the other things you "can" do or you're going to fail.In some ways, this game reminds me of Recettear, which I absolutely adore. It's what led me to pick up Potiononmics in the first place. But overall, I just feel like the developers dumped too many ideas into the game and didn't give players enough time to figure out how to manage it all, making for a frustrating experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: The characters in this game are wonderful. This game has everything I love, all in one, and it doesn't skimp on ANY of it! Recent update improved your ability to filter through the many ingredients you will have by the end of the game, and it's so helpful. This game came out of nowhere for me, but it's now one of my favorite games ever. I've already told like 10 of my friends to buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game with beautiful art. Rather than being like all the other store management games where you have an action adventure game tied to store management you get a deck of cards to negotiate sales with customers. You stay in the town and hire people to go out adventuring for you.It could have been "Stardew but..." and instead it's its own new thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Great in concept but I got more than 10 hours in before I learned (from a guide!) there is really only one way to play this game.  The choices are an illusion and you can't pick a lot of them.  I have two kids in real life so do I start over or try to warn others?  Why the heck would you make a game that looks casual but punishes you for playing it casually?  Only the devs can know.38 hour edit:  I went back because it was a game the kids can watch.  I beat it and it was fun enough but has no replayability due to the tutorial being the first part of the game and just... really slowing you down so you can learn it.  It works but then you would need to slog through it every playthrough.  Needs some SERIOUS quality of life fixes:-Limited times you can see your inventory.  Why?  Is it terrible that I might buy an ingredient from the vendors?  You even lose the ability to see your inventory in the brewing menu if all cauldrons are currently full.  WHAT?  Double why?-Can only save in home shop.  Why should this matter?  You lose a time slot of the day to return to the shop but what if you need to run for some reason?  May as well quit back to the auto save of that day (I guess I WILL give props for the daily autosaves.  That is a GOOD FEATURE)-Other reviews mentioned the recipes get heavy near the end.  I think being able to save your recipes to reuse them would be a great help with this.  I just stopped brewing anything the last 3 days because it was a massive boring timesink at that point.Overall, still a good game, tried to do a lot, just... a lot of bizarre design decisions that have already been covered by 40 years of game development.  If you manage to play through it, it was probably for you.

_childDocuments_.review: You're a broke small business owner so you make it your business to rip off everyone you encounter. _childDocuments_.review: After waiting for a game like recettear to come around that I enjoyed just as much, this hit the spot perfectly. The main features of the game are crafting potions, and then selling them, which are both executed amazingly. The simplicity of the crafting system, with a wide array of potions to craft and ingredients to use. Trying to get the ratios of ingredients just right, while using as many ingredients with positive modifiers as possible, is a satisfying process that stretches your mathematical muscles, and the game rewards you for the optimisation of your recipe. However at the same time, if you want to just throw ingredients that have the right magimins and effects into the pot, the game doesn't punish you and you can still succeed.The characters in the game are also an extremely strong part of the game. You build your friendship with them to acquire discounts and understand their backstories, and romancing them is an option if you're interested in that. The cast itself is expressive and diverse, including LGBTQIA+ members. The character animations in the game are also amazing and are very expressive of the character's emotions and personalities.However with all the good the game has, there are a few issues.The two main low points of the game for me are; the lack of quality of life features, and the lack of any endless/relaxed game mode.Although the systems in the game work well, there are a lack of supporting QoL features that are desperately needed; - The shop has no sort feature, and is filled in a partially random order that is different in any playthrough, and there's no filter so you can isolate and purchase certain types of ingredients.- It's not obvious that you actually have an inventory you can look at to see all your current potions/ingredients/fuel from anywhere in the world. Only on my third playthrough did I find this option.- The game menus are sluggish, and often hang on speech bubbles that have a pre-determined display time. Additionally there is some subtle mouse lag and my fans ramp up in some menus, especially the brewing menu when you unlock larger cauldrons.- Duplicate cosmetics for your shop do not stack, and clog up your inventory, even though you can only use each cosmetic once. Making the menu hard to navigate.As for my other downside. Currently, the only game option is a time-limited mode that forces you to optimise your game plan, and play the game a certain way. You spend the majority of time trying to brew up potions for a competition that has no real reward other than more complexity in the game. Winning a competition isn't really satisfying, and often causes more stress as you now have to think about the next round.Additionally, as you get further in the game, you have to manage multiple cauldrons, barrels and gardening. This can get overwhelming quite quickly and slows down the game immensely.With the goods and bads taken into account I have a few things I'd like to see in future updates or DLCs:- More QoL features, Filters and sorting in the shops. - "dispensers" or something similar that allow you to take the burden of managing so many cauldrons, allowing you to dispense a limited number of pre-filled ingredients into a cauldron automatically after you have emptied it.- And endless / relaxed game mode, I'd love to see a game mode without the time pressure of impending game-over. Optional competitions that you can enter when you're ready to expand your potion license, and the option to re-enter competitions from a lower level to make some extra money. (randomised opponents here with a pay-to enter system would be really compelling and require you to be prepared.) - A personal suggestion, I'd love to see are a wider variety of shop cosmetics that have an impact on the customers (patience, perhaps).Although the game has its faults, it promises to be an engaging experience while it lasts, well worth the price they are charging for it.A unique and character-filled experience that I loved and can't help but recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: You can't even sort your bags . (A tedious workaround exists: new items always go into the bag at the end of the list. If you have a small enough stack of items, you could shuffle them to the end of the bag by placing them in the cauldron/store and then putting them back in your bag.)I love it anyway, though; I'm a sucker for good characters, and these ones are adorable, both in graphics and in personality. And there are CAT PIRATES, and their background music is the bomb. You haggle with customers via a card game; you get better cards by improving your friendship with the other characters. Friendship can improve just by interacting with their shops/services, but it improves more significantly if you spend chunks of time on them.Time management is in the vein of ; there are six time-chunks in an active day, and two passive overnight chunks that are NOT represented on the clock but contribute to your potion-brewing and your heroes' travels. Opening your shop takes two time-chunks; ranking-up a friend takes one; going into town takes at least one (but potentially many more, since that's where you have the chance to encounter friends). Gift-giving, purchasing, and swapping between shopkeepers while in town are free; hanging out and ranking up are not.There's no freeplay at the end of the 50-day competition window, alas; you win and that's the end. I don't  object to re-playing the competition arc to get to know the world and the characters better, but the game mechanics are otherwise so similar to  that I didn't expect it. I neglected deepening friendships to prioritize saving my soul from the debt collector, thinking there would be plenty of time to get to know them later, but, no. (I got to about Rank 4-6 on most of the characters, in that timeframe; good enough that I didn't have trouble with card acquisition, but narratively, I was getting to a point in each relationship where I wanted to know more about them and what they were going to do next, and that opportunity was cut off by... winning the game, I guess.
