_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Technically I like this game, I've played nearly 100 hours and I intend to keep going to the end. I'm putting my review as a would not recommend because the game desperately needs some Quality of Life updates so it stops being a frustrating slog. I'm a ways into the game, and I find that its starting to take up to 6 hours real time just to complete a single in-game day because of all of them. The fact I've played 100 hours in the game and are still on my first play-through says a lot to that fact.Despite that I keep playing because it's charming, funny, well done models and expressions, interesting story (for a management sim game), and the general gameplay loop is actually rewarding and fun when it's not fighting against you with the missing QoL issues. I would honestly say this would be my favorite management game ever and I would recommend it to everyone I know, if they addressed these issues. Since my original review, the studio has released updates to add in quality of life improvements for the biggest offenders for the problems I had previously, and the flow of the game is more enjoyable in the later stages of the game. The remaining issues I have don't come up nearly as often and are not as frustrating, just would be a bit nicer.Now that I've finished the game though and much more enjoyed the flow in the later stages, the thing I'd want most honestly is some improved replayability with some difficulty sliders, some additional randomness or variation, or maybe a shorter game mode with sort of daily-run feel or much steeper scaling to "see how long you can go".5) On the Shop page there's no way to Buy All, or one-click-buy ingredients. So if I want to buy out 10 copies of an ingredient, I need to click it, move the mouse, click the + icon 10 times, move the mouse, click buy. Later in the game when you have 50k to spend on ingredients, having to spend 10 seconds or so per ingredient can be a HUGE time sync as you want to buy possibly 100 different ingredients for the night, it can take like half an hour to do for something that could take 5 minutes or less if we could just right-click the item to buy all or something6) On the gardening page you can't select more than one copy of an ingredient at a time when feeding. At the same time you need to provide up to 1000 megamins worth of ingredients to get high-yields. This means you'll have to drag and drop THE SAME ingredient possibly dozens of times, instead of just being able to click, type a value, then drop, or even just being able to click-click-click a dozen times and only drag once.7) Certain aspects of the game are unnecessarily gated behind the Customization menu. For example if I am brewing potions, and I find that I don't need as many megamins for a potion as I thought, so I could use a cheaper cauldron and possibly be free to upgrade my better one this day. Well you have to go through 3 loading screens to swap it out and come back, instead of just being able to select it from the brew menu! In a similar vein, when you go out travelling, you can't be using your shelves since you're not selling anything, so why do you have to go into the customization menu and remove them BEFORE you head out if you want to upgrade them? Did you forget? Sorry you now have to either not upgrade it, or waste a time unit heading back to your shop to swap them out.8) There's no way to check what Marketing, or Investment you've chosen AFTER you did it. Took a break for lunch in the middle of your game, now you can't remember what you chose, so you don't know what potions to make? too bad!
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: I was torn on whether to recommend this game or not. I really wanted to say I loved it and that you should play it.But ultimately, looking back on it, I feel like I lost most of the time I spent on it and emerged disappointed.The positive first: Potionomics is an adorable game with a really nice setting and interesting characters. So many things are so cute. The gameplay manages to evolve at first and it's pretty nice to optimise your potions recipe and haggling technique.I really got lost in the game, enjoying redoing the same things all day but trying to adapt to the ingredients I still had, or those I had just acquired, balancing the money I had, and all characters you can befriend are really cool and I genuinely like them. I ended up going to bed way after midnight on the day I bought it, having no notion of the time I had spent.So, one of the things I must note: if you're vulnerable to timesink à la "Just One More Turn", please be careful. I have ADHD and I couldn't let the game go until I accidentally optimised it out of fun.At some point, I just... managed to generate way more money than I needed. I already had all the cards to haggle. My potions were too powerful and I one hit ko-ed the last three competitions due to that before the match even started.The problem with Potionomics comes with its fixed pacing. Either you don't optimise enough and you struggle, or you optimise in a way that you've already won and just... go through the motions or skip to the end. If you get some cauldrons and upgrade them, you can sell potions for so much more than you need. Prior to that, I was struggling, earning approximately as much as I was spending getting some upgrades and buying ingredients.Another problem in terms of pacing is that while the start of the game introduces new mechanics fairly regularly, there is a drought around the third week, which introduces the last character and mechanic (the slime) on day 22 (out of 50). After that, apart from a few visits by the weekly competitor, there really isn't anything new. While Finn is memorable and interacts with you a bit, Anubia has no real character and is barely seen.The last week only has one area to explore and no new potion to craft, which means I started it with the potions I needed to win. No curveball during the last days like the previous characters did.It genuinely feels like the game should have been shorter. I might have spent too much time in the beginning trying to get everything right, but since the game kinda... stops introducing anything new at the middle point and the last parts are not that filled out, you repeat the same thing. Except you already optimised it by then.Again, the game is really cute and nice, I loved its characters and had genuine fun at the beginning. I wish it had been shorter and denser, either with shorter weeks or cutting the fourth week out. Or a different pacing, one that maybe wouldn't be so fixed.But in the end, I feel like I fell into a cycle of gaming that I didn't enjoy and couldn't walk away from due to how easy it is to just want to play for longer, and longer. And this is why I don't feel like I can recommend this game, even though I really wanted to.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: 7/10Art style and animations are great; accompanied with solid game play in crafting and negotiation card game. The down side would be the timer mechanic that rushes players to complete certain tasks or game over. I wish there was a relax mode, so I can focus on parts of the game I enjoyed. Sadly, it a cycle of countdowns that forced player to search for ingredients to make a good enough potion to present at the end of the countdown. It turns this potential great relaxing game into a somewhat stressful min-max management game. If you like min maxing gameplay, it great, but I prefer at your own pace for these genres of games.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: After 30 hours, completing the game and getting all achievements I can say I thoroughly enjoyed the experience! Game is far from perfect and it can get repetitive around 30+ day mark, but that did not stopped me from playing. What was the most appealing at first – potion making – started to become tedious, mainly due to UI and lack of proper filtering. I’d say that is my biggest gripe with the title: it looks like a phone port. If they only implement some UI scaling, more filters for ingredients, maybe recipe-saver that could save some time I would like this game a lot more. Luckily, if you play your card right you can swim in dough during mid to late game and I felt absolutely no pressure to sell potions at all, focusing mainly on interactions.Some people say that time limit is a deal breaker for them (you can play only 50 days, then story ends). I don’t want to undermine their opinion, though I believe that it is not as rough as it sounds. When I jumped into play I was not trying to play optimally, and I still managed to ace the game with almost a 6 days to spare.To sum it up, this game is very enjoyable – characters are nicely albeit cheesily written, gameplay loop is interesting and music enhances the experience. That being said, the game needs to be updated with some quality of life features, such as more filtering options, recipe saving and so on.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game and I'd definitely recommend it, only thing thats kinda disappointing is the lack of a New game+, or even just the option of continuing your save after beating the story. _childDocuments_.review: Edit: I've now finished it after forcing myself to save scum for 20 hours. It gets easier in the second half, but the ending and resulting storylines from the characters and the plot in general are half baked and fall flat. The story didn't even turn out to be worth the hassle. And I found a load more bugs.---Don't get this if you'd looking for a casual, cute sim game with dating options. There's better options out there. I wanted to like this game so badly, especially because it was a gift so somebody else wasted their money instead. First things first: It's TIMED. Your "run" has 50 days, and then the game ends. It is a time-oriented experience with 5 deadlines or "competitions" that you must pass or the game is over and you fail. I played up to 20 days, and a mistake I had done in my second day ruined my whole run, and I didn't know until it was too late and 6 hours in. Because it's really hard. People are praising it as a game you can "turn your brain off" and play and that it's a nice "challenge" - but it is very min-max. You can't waste time often in this game, largely due to the looming deadlines. It was punishing to go to the shop, forget what I needed and have to go back to my house only to go back out again. It is not a game you can play with something on in the background or a drink. You need to pay attention, and save often. You'll probably lose your first run, unless you have good RNG on what hands you're given - and then you'll probably sit there going "what, people actually struggled with this game!?" which yes, some people do. It's not the dark souls of potion making games, but there's less room for error than I would like when I just want to kick back with a cider and not think much. And this is largely due to the fact it's RNG what ingredients you unlock each run, which is great for variation but terrible when you never unlock a certain ingredient colour you need for a potion, and then fail - you're literally at the mercy of the rng, and I think it's too much for how long the time between competitions actually is.And that leads onto my biggest problem: This game is a buggy mess. You're "soft-locked" into the first day tutorial if you press "new game" after playing previously, and cannot progress time or do anything - UNTIL YOU GO INTO YOUR GAME FILES AND DELETE ALL YOUR SAVES. That's mad weird, and I don't understand how a game with such a common, game breaking bug has very positive reviews over 2 months into launch. Not to mention, the game hates you alt-tabbing, and will seemingly crash for no reason. And if it crashes when you press new game? You've gotta delete those save files again.And it's such a shame, because there's a lot of good stuff here. I enjoyed my time with it. I liked the puzzles, I liked the mechanics, heck I even liked the characters which is something I don't often find in dating sim games. There were cute moments that left me screenshotting so much, and laughing to myself. It was enjoyable. But the issues are too glaring, with weirdly easy fixes that the devs just haven't bothered with. For example: Difficulty choices. Add a casual difficulty for people struggling, and add an "endless" mode for people after the 50 days for anybody who wants to vibe and just clean up their achievements or experience the full game without the pressure. Fix the game-breaking bugs. And for the love of god, give an option to skip the tutorial nonsense. I can't imagine going to play a 2nd or 3rd run to complete achievements of this game after 80+ hours and being forced to replay that long and condescending tutorial literally every time I wanted to replay it - especially when it can bug and break and lock you into it near the end of the tutorial. The game options are far too bare-bones and it feels like the only people having fun with this game are getting lucky with their RNG or aren't really bothered about replaying it and wooing everyone or seeing absolutely everything the game has to offer, and I just feel like the Devs could do so much more with it. Hell, keep the competitions. Keep the game breaking bug that softlocks you into the first day. Keep the horrid tutorials. But add a casual mode with slightly raised potion prices and cheaper ingredients, and add the dang endless mode. You are actively losing a massive portion of players that are deterred from this game for that reason.

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly fun, but by the end it bogs down quite a bit. The game-play loop of chatting up characters for ingredients, brewing up potions, and selling them with a card combat mechanism is pretty fun. Eventually you just have a lot of do each cycle so it takes a long time. I played it with my 4 and 7 year olds and read out the text to them and let them make decisions.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: The game is ruined by the unavoidable timed competitions. Even the simple addition of being able to choose WHEN to tackle the competitions, rather than being forced into battle every ten days, would improve things greatly. It would still gate progress to better potions and upgrades, while removing the stifling need to concentrate on one goal.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Potionomics is pretty neat! I finally beat the game. I don't typically do like whole reviews but I added it in at the bottom.Early Impressions: I like all of the characters even the random shoppers have personality and flair and some challenges to overcome when making a sale. The Main cast is also great and the sales cards they unlock actually make me want to switch up my deck. Also the 2 methods for getting new ingredients as well as the shop that restocks that you can expand is neat. Just won my first competition and I'm looking forward to the others!Update: The Big QOL Filters and Sorts options has made gift giving and brewing much easier! I am in what I believe is the final week now.BEAT THE GAME REVIEW!Graphics: 10/10     - Everyone and everything is so vibrant, and wonderfully animated. Even the shopping NPCs. Gameplay: 8/10     - This game was painful at launch since it was missing big quality of life sorting and filtering options. Thankfully they fixed that. As for playing I hope you understand math and ratios, because balancing the 5 colors and brewing potions is the main meat of the game. You sell those potions to get money which you use to get material. How do you get the materials for brewing though? That's where commissions from the Baptiste and the Heroes Guild comes in and you can also personally send out the hero friends you make along the way with potions you brewed to get them through zones. Additionally any materials can be given to Quinn who will then stock and resale some to you each day. Quinn’s prices are affected by how much over hunting on zones you do so you need to spread those heroes out or take it easy on some of Baptiste’s daily commissions. You can also befriend many NPCs unlocking new cards to help you sell better and win in the big contests, as well as discounts. Additionally there are other marketing tools you unlock later. Value: 8/10    - It was a wonderful game but I do not think I would replay it. I do not regret buying it at launch though. The only thing you could really change is who you decide to date. Which will affect their dialog and the last few character events.Overall: 7/10    - If you like math, colorful characters, and management shop sim games I recommend it highly.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent game that I highly recommend! The cute style and well-written character interactions never fail to make me smile. The haggling card game is simply but fun, and the potionmaking is complex but satisfying.But be aware that this game is fairly difficult if you don't manage your time well. Make sure you have multiple different saves throughout each week, or you may find yourself at one of the competitions completely unable to win. If you manage your time well, though, the game gets pretty easy as time goes on; early effort pays off.Really my one complaint is that there's no freeplay after beating the final competition. Once you finish day 50, that's the end. So if you were thinking of putting off maxing out friendships with the NPCs until after the final competition, think again. Everything has to be done within the 45-day time limit (5 days are devoted to the competitions). Still, I think this game is fantastic, and I'd love to see more games in the same setting. Rafta's a really cool place!
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: So let's cut to the chase:I've been seeing people give this game a bad rep for the time constriction but here's the thing;You don't need to do EVERYTHING to win, you can chose what tactics you wanna stick to in order to get to victory lane!  This game has so much replayability, there is a variety of different ways you can play in order to get the same result. The key is to limit yourself to the NPC's you find of most value that way you can also boost your relationships with them. I personally stick into Quinn, Saffron, and Muktuk because ingredient discounts and store upgrades have really been the most efficient route. Having multiple cauldrons leads to an endless supply of potions that I don't even know what to do with! I was so worried I wasn't going to like this game because of the time constrictions but now I'm glad to know it didn't impact me as greatly as I was lead to believe. 10/10 honestly the price tag on this game doesn't do the game-play/art justice and it should have been a $35 game imo
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah it's a little rough around the edges in terms of organization but so is the main character. Nothing inexcusable to the charming and wonderful personalities, world building, and animations that encompass this game's playability. Strong GOTY contender from me.My one wish was that it didn't end so I could just hang out in Rafta a bit longer.Edit: Lol they fixed that too! Damn! So much new added in recently:- Voice Acting is charming and hokey (and completely optional for picky listeners)- Added actual sort function. Extremely good. Very helpful from its change at release- Endless mode lets you just keep developing newer and newer card strategies.- Too Easy? More difficult mode available. Too Hard? Easier mode available. (I do wish these were more toggleable as individual features but it's still a step in the right direction)- Smooch all the homies now. If you want. Up to you really.This is just a wonderful, massive update that was free for the folks who had it already. A true labor of love. Can't wait to see what they make next.

_childDocuments_.review: If the stellar presentation isn't enough to get you, how about a diverse cast of lovely characters, a neatly condensed fusion of Recettear and the Atelier series, and very cute and wholesome LGBT-oriented romances? Also, the music, much like the visuals, is super cute and evocative. I have been looking forward to this experience for some time and so far, it has been absolutely worth it. I expect that I'll spend a lot of time losing myself in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Much preferred the demos pacing compared to this complicated grind of a release. Deckbuilding and shop management seem arbitrary now that the competitions are the one make or break factor. Vendors are RNG so you'll often find yourself one ingredient short of any given requirement. The characters are all charming and bursting with life but hanging out with them is just an inefficient use of time. Desperately in need of a difficulty overhaul because it's in steep contrast with how it's being advertised and players are feeling mis-sold. Make the owl give worthwhile hints at the very least.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Great animations, great music. People are complaining about the short days but that makes the game challenging. This is not a relaxing simulator like Stardew Valley but a great time management sim. The haggling mini game and deck building is fun, minmaxing potions are engaging and there is always new things thrown into the game to make it interesting. If you like me and love a great managing game where you have to think ahead and plan everything out, but love when all the things come together and enjoy success of your plan I would definitely recommend this game to you! If you just want to turn your brain off and relax this is not the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Every scene feels like I'm flipping through an art book. The characters have such vivid expressions in their movements, bodies, and faces. The music is great, extremely fitting and brings the atmosphere to life from peppy mornings to relaxing nights. The plot is perfect for progressively exploring more of the world while maintaining a steady pace, keeping players from immediately becoming overwhelmed. The characters are absolutely phenomenal, each have unique and strong personalities that I am genuinely interested in. I'm surprised by how much I'm enjoying this game. So much is keeping me engaged, from brewing and negotiating to the story and character interactions. One thing I will be critical about is filtering through ingredients. There are many ingredients (even early game) and the filter system only allows you to search for ingredients containing the component(s) that you have highlighted. It does not let you filter out ingredients consisting of components that you do not want, nor does it let you differentiate between AND/OR filtering. For example, if I want to look for ingredients with only A, then I have to select A and search for an ingredient with only A in a page full of ingredients with varying combinations of A and other components. It can become frustrating rather quickly when brewing multiple times a day, and even more so as you unlock more ingredients and cauldrons.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: This game is adorable and worth every penny. The characters are all fun, well written, adorably animated, and the little story concocted here is a treat from start to finish. The actual potion-making is a lot of fun to play around with, the deck building is unobtrusive and not overly complicated while still being engaging, the business management is equally well-designed, and the dating-sim aspect is cute, believable, and doesn't feel forced or cringey. Sleeper hit of 2022 - truly a joy to play. I hope we see more of Sylvia and the gang in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: It is very charming and well made. It is way more difficult then you assume from the visual style. For once a shop sim that tells you times are hard and actually means it. So far highly recommend it if you want something that can be wholesome one moment and then stress you over deadlines the next moment.Also Roxanne mommies milkers.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Game mechanics:-The potion crafting is mostly a numbers balancing puzzle with some additional element management.  Not very complex, but not so simple as to be boring.  A quick-recipe option would be nice (might be in later game?)-Negotiation deck-building is simple but fun, like a super-distilled Slay the Spire, weighing value vs turn number.-Material, gear, ship upgrades all weigh into a cost-benefit puzzle that feels fun to work through.-Shop upgrades are simply drag-and-drop to their element, no large-scale redesign like in a crafting game (I very much prefer this)Theme:-Art is excellent.-Characters are fun, well-defined, not too cliche.-Relationship/dating(?) aspect is nice enough, not burdensome, but not what I came here for.Overall, 8/10.  It's very much what I want in a game about running a potion shop.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: I was waffling on buying this game, but after buying it and playing it through one time I can say it was worth every penny. I was a huge fan of Recettear, and this game certainly inherited the soul of that game.Pros: Amazing animation and art direction. The characters come to life with personality with fluid motion and movement. Wonderful writing. From each character scene down to the delightful descriptions of each and every item. Great   characterization. Enjoyable gameplay. Time management at its finest. The deck building was genuinely fun. Cons: No post game - this was super disappointing. I was looking forward to harder challenges after unlocking week 5 cauldrons and shelves, only to find it was almost a waste of time. Information clutter - gets bad in weeks 3-5 and Quinn's inventory and slime bulb selection gets too crowded.I can honestly say that if you haven't tried the game and liked Recettear or games similar to it, you should stop and buy this game right away. My life will be poorer if a sequel isn't made.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: I super liked this game and all the characters, animation, concepts, story, all the building blocks are so fantastic! I don't have much to complain about outside the nitty gritty of the mechanics.There are some things, like positive and negative traits, that don't feel super necessary? Certain parts, especially in the beginning, can be sort of a grind. I'm also sad about the lack of end game content! It makes it hard to want to replay to see about building relationships with other characters or toying with more powerful potions during competitions if you have to build all of it up again. Something like new game + where maybe you had access to ingredients and cauldrons to make it easier to progress through the parts you've already played might be nice but I know not every game can accomplish that or maybe even really needs it. On the note of relationships, it feels super underwhelming there's not like, one last scene with your romance interest. Unless I missed it on my playthrough. I expected maybe something in the final competition where my LI helps out or one last scene in the epilogue about what they're up to. You have the final rank 10 scene with them and then basically don't hear from them again. It makes the romance feel almost tacked on as it has no bearing on the main story, none of the dialogue is any different to include their presence in your life, and there's no real closing note with your relationship with them. Even just a final piece of art with Sylvia, her LI, and Owl would do a lot to make it feel like your LI is part of the actual story and not just a side road. All in all I had a fantastic time, and the fact that I'm disappointed there isn't more after I've already finished speaks to how much I enjoyed it! So maybe my critiques are me selfishly wanting to continue lol highly recommend! I'm hoping the devs add more content and fix some of the bugs
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: This was pretty enjoyable. Its vision is very well-realized and the gameplay more engaging than I expected, leaving me so intent on brewing the perfect potions and negotiating that a lot more time would pass than I expected while playing. I was also not expecting to be doing a fair bit of math. The slice of a modern magical world that's presented here is both interesting and charming, and the cast of supporting characters (each with a solid design) are very well written, with particular praise to the snappy dialog. The main story is fine, more of a premise than anything and predictable in all of it notes, but it sets the stage well for seeing the characters interact and grow.There could be a few quality of life additions, like switching ingredients between cauldrons, better sorting, and the ability to check various things like relationship levels (and progress to the next level) at any time. It also takes more time to load than I would think. Things did start getting repetitive toward the end, and for the last ten days I basically focused on relationships over potions (you better maximize your gift-giving if you want to max out lots of relationships, by the way) but overall, this was a great idea and a solid game.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Despite what the top rated sub-4h playtime negative review says (almost every single point made in there is just factually wrong, but I'm not here to debunk it), this game is: - chill- not too difficult - enjoyable - entirely 100%able in a single first playthrough. The only reason I didn't 100% it is because two achievments are bugged right now (A character can't get past relationship rank 9, and an event leads to an automatic failure), but the devs have been informed, and are looking into it. The dev team is really quick to answer, present and they dropped a patch on day 2 that simplified the eaerly game for everyone (which was a very convoluted part, a lot of people had trouble with it). Plus, you're a redhead merchant, what's not to love? 9.5/10 would recommend it to my grandma
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: I do, in fact, recommend this game.HOWEVER:This game is too much luck based at it's current state, you can hard-lock yourself from winning competitions if you don't min-max and get good relationships with everyone as fast as possible.You need a lot of money, you need a lot of ingredients and you need a lot of luck. This is not a relaxing time spender, this is a highly demanding time management game, for someone that isn't used to playing this type of games with harsh challenges, you will NOT enjoy the game AT ALL.I'm at the third week, third challenge, my potions met the requirements, I can compete just fine, but I got hard-locked out of winning the competition because of the abusive system of the stress cards.I cannot stress this enough - at 20% stress you get two to SEVEN stress cards, with a boss that gives you 10% STRESS DEBUFF plus debuff that DOUBLES your stress receiving level.YOU CAN HARD-LOCK YOURSELF OUT OF THE GAME WITH TOO MUCH EASE, EVEN DOING THE PROPER POTIONS WITH PERFECT REQUIREMENTS!I can't stress this part ENOUGH.If you are a easily stressed person or get distressed with ease, do not, I repeat, do not play this game until they fix the balancing issues.At the current state, this game is too stressful for normal people.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very charming game with a lot of fun mechanics mashed together. Part resource management, part relationship simulator, part deck building card game. Great art, characters, and things to keep you busy.Personally, it starts to drag around the midway point, ~12 hours in. After unlocking all of the main game mechanics, the core gameplay loop started to lose a lot of interest. You find yourself doing the same things you were doing a few hours ago, just with "more" of everything -- higher value ingredients, potions, cards, etc. with aren't that different from what you've already been doing. For some people this might not be an issue, and I definitely got my money's worth from this even if I don't finish the game, so it gets a solid recommendation from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: The main game has a heavy time crunch aspect that the Next Fest Demo did not tutorialize or even imply, and the store page does not hint at those either. I would not have purchased the game if it was upfront about the game being a strict time-crunch. The game has other problems but to be honest I don't care about those. If the game adds a mode to remove the time limit or at least make it significantly less strict then I'll repurchase and try again. As-is, I refunded it so I could buy something else.

Very addicting gameplay loop, and the character writing and design is just fan-freakin-tastic. This would make for a fantastic stream game! _childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolutely wonderful game :)I was really sceptical at first, since card game mechanics really aren't my thing but I shot a message to the devs and they told me that they tried to make it as player-friendly as possible - and they did, I had a lot of fun!The characters are all so lovely, the designs so well done, the romantic scenes are darling and I really enjoyed them~I love the little details too: How each potion matches their maker, how characters greet you differently, depending on how well you know each other, actual lighting changes throughout the day for the cutscenes as well etc.And my god, the music! This is one of the games where I never had something running in the background to listen to because the music is just so good. The changes in tracks for each time of the day are very cool as well.I do have some gripes with the game though: There are just SO many ingredients. At a certain point it gets so overwhelming with all their stats and some are downright unusable - using them in potions just disrupts the whole balance which is a real bummer.The rng for finding certain items, for example for upgrading cauldrons and shelves was abyssmal on my first run too. It wasn't until my last in-game week that I finally found the necessary items to at least be able to upgrade SOME of them.I also would've loved some more time in general. I get that a deadline brings some pressure into the game to do your best and as fast as possible but if you have bad luck with expedition loot and low money, you are just floundering, hanging in mid air for something, anything good material-wise to come your way.I actually had to restart 3 times because it seems I could not master the mechanics fast enough, or had bad luck. Call me slow but the beginning was really not gentle on me. For a short time I was thinking of just abandoning this game, I was really frustrated.More time would also be nice to just, exist and decorate your shop. Maybe that's a fault on my end but I hardly ever got any interior design pieces until my last in-game week - and even then it seems I'm missing a ton. (I also have not once bought any display shelves or used services by either Luna or Roxanne). Everything feels so rushed.  Would be nice to have an endless After-Game-Mode where you can just collect all the things, buy all upgrades etc.Overall, still a fun experience and if you don't mind time pressure, I cannot reccomend this game enough :)
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: I can only recommend this game. The marriage of game genres, the writing of the characters, the art style, the animations (except for one glitched one for Xid), the music (Boss Finn's theme, babyyy), everything is in place, everything works in tandem and it is a great ride from start to finish. You want to have a good time dragging a potionshop out of a seemingly bottomless debt? Take this game for a spin.If you are turned off by it being a "dating sim", fear not - you do not need to romance anyone. I only made friends, but those friendships felt meaningful and interesting because of the characters involved. No ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ surface-level virtue-signaling "DiVeRsItY", this cast brings about the kind that actually matters - . There is bound to be at least one character who speaks to you on some level, and that is a true and rare treasure in today's media. And hey, if one of them really is to your liking, the romance option is always there. (Man, I just wish Finn joined the team....)The card game part is easy to understand even for a complete noob like me who never had interest in that genre. There are some crazy good builds you can put together, or you can fumble around (again, like me), but still have a great time.10/10, would face Boss Finn again.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: There have been significant changes in "sorting" and information available regarding ingredients and magimins since I posted this review. I will update when I have had a chance to figure out the extent of the changes.Potionomics is a streamlined Recettear. Assemble potions from components containing "Magimins" (of which there are five types: A, B, C, D, and E) of varying composition (e.g. 0-0-8-16-8) to win contests at the end of every 10 days, equip adventurers to get more components, make money to invest in improvements in the shop/equipment and adventuring expeditions, and make friend. Time is the most important part of this, and you have 6 (8 including the "sleep" period, which counts for all things that you are not actively participating in, e.g. adventuring and brewing).Some issues: QOL: 1) You cannot load from the general menu, and you CANNOT save from anywhere but your house (this becomes immensely frustrating when you make small mis-clicks, like accidentally ending the day early - something I have done innumerable times, trying to quit or go back to the title screen to reload a save after a previous misclick)  (2) You DO NOT KNOW what is going on in the other 'areas' with other 'tasks.' So, if you leave your house to talk to the adventurer, and then realize they're still on an adventure, you're screwed - and (3) There are limited information provided and NO sorting abilities in the stores, the component maker gives you numbers of components you have on a 1x1 basis [e.g. if you click on "Marshberry" it will tell you how many "Marshberries" you have] but does not allow you to sort by "magimin" groups, or "magimin" amounts. (Note: There has been a patch that allowed some sorting in brewing and I have not had a chance to double check this).These become very irritating, VERY fast. Hopefully they can be patched in at a later date.All in all, despite these irritating flaws, the writing is snappy and fun, the characters are likeable with beautiful 3D and high res "pixel-esque" graphics. The gameplay loop is engaging, and I suggest you pick it up.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: Tried for two hours and decided to refund. Too stressful.There is way too little time to gather ingredients and upgrade your shop before the first battle. If you lose the first battle then it's game over according the internet. Also the speech bubbles cannot be speed up and you just have to wait for them to pass with their own time. This just feels dumb to me, why not give the option to "finish" them sooner?One more thing: everything, and I mean everything is done via a menu you can choose for example traveling, brewing, selling and other stuff. So you use the menu a lot. I got so sick of looking at the black loading screen already in these few hours I was playing. It takes about 3-5 seconds for the wanted view to load, but like I said, you need to use the menu a lot and the loading screen is there always. Would not bother if you used it rarely.So many frustrations.

_childDocuments_.review: this game would have been good if it didn't stress you so much to get potions ready for the competion.i felt extemly overwhelmed and stressed when playing.trying to win compitions is hard too, i had all 3 potions, all were on great and two had 4 stars while the other had 3. yet the chances of winning when being stressed by the one you are trying to win aginst helps nothing.if you get stressed or overwhelmed by feeling pressure of needing to get stuff done then this game is probably now for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: The only time being stressed, straddled with debt, and failing a work-life balance has ever felt engrossing!The game's incredibly charming art direction belies a very complex and fulfilling juggling act. It's challenging, but rewards persistence and attentiveness.  I've never had literal nightmares about resource management before, so I think it's safe to say this game has punch.Perhaps the only issue is that with the rigors of keeping up with the difficulty, and the fact that you have their cards, services, and personalities to consider, you may not feel as attached to as many of the characters as you'd hope. In that sense, the friendship/dating elements may fall a little flat if you're too sweaty about the whole not-going-bankrupt thing.

_childDocuments_.review: This had the potential to be a really fun card-based dating sim game, but it really REALLY got old when you found yourself obsessively saving in new slots just so you could repeat every single thing a little bit differently before the upcoming competition should you happen to not brew the correct potions in time.
_childDocuments_.name: Potionomics

_childDocuments_.review: I managed to discover this game only recently and AFTER it was updated to be fully voice acted! What an incredibly charming and uplifting experience ♥ I started the game on the recommended difficulty, but swapped to 'cozy/easy' mode during the second chapter, because I couldn't be bothered to focus on my time management while on vacation haha, I imagine the hardest difficulty can be very challenging for those interested!I can go on-and-on about the incredible art style and assortment of illustrations throughout the entire game, the card art ESPECIALLY was so fun to collect and enjoy, even if I didn't use the cards in my simple deck :)But the real star of the show, was the writing (and the voice acting that highlighted it!). _childDocuments_.review: Interesting time management game with some deck building on the side.   Potionomics is a game about making the most of your time: you only have so many days to prepare your best potions before the next competition. If you're the type who likes to min-max the limited time they have in order to see everything the game has to offer in one playthrough, this game lets you do that quite comfortably. The issue arises when you've done everything there is to do with plenty of time left, there's no reason not to just skip to the final challenge. there's no incentive to earn more, to explore more, or to further deepen relationships. Potionomics would benefit greatly from an endless mode or challenge mode to incentivise more creative deck-building or potion brewing.   I myself saw everything there is to see in one playthrough without a guide, and had seven days afterward with which I had nothing to do but end the day and speed along to the last confrontation in order to see the ending. I feel like the latter half of the game is unfortunately easy compared to the first half, where the finance crunch is something that you really feel day after day.  Once you unlock the ability to sell your potions without interacting with the deck building aspect at all is where the game becomes frighteningly repetitive. Every day simply becomes:   Collect potions from your cauldrons.Collect ingredients from your garden.Place excess potions in the vending machine.Brew potions to be collected tomorrow morning.Place new ingredients in the garden to be collected tomorrow morning.Spend the entire day's time deepening your bonds with your business partners, buying ingredients, and sending your adventurers on expeditions.   Repetition in time management games isn't necessarily a bad thing, and I recognize I may be part of the problem by boiling the game down to it's optimal formula. I would argue the game directly incentivises such behavior, however, as the tools provided to perform the 'optimal' method are provided soon after the second boss.   The biggest shame by far is just that this method doesn't interact with the haggling system at all, which is the most fun part of the game in my opinion. Deepening your bonds gets you new cards, which in turn lets you haggle the prices of your potions higher. But why would I spend my precious time selling potions at an 80% markup myself when I can comfortably beat the game selling for a simple 15% markup with the vending machine?   Despite the game balance issues in the second half, Potionomics was gripping. The characters are entertaining, and it did get a few good laughs out of me with the writing. I played and beat the game in less than a week, and it was certainly time well spent. The replay value isn't quite there, but for a one-and-done, give this one a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, with some UX issues.This game is very fun. As a fan of crafting and shop sims, I'm spending hours straight just minmaxing and optimizing my crafts and chores and dragging out each ingame day as long a possible.A lot of care has been put into the game's visuals, and the core gameplay loop is very addictive. I'm having fun with the game. As someone with hand issues, I greatly enjoy that this game is mouse only and can be played entirely on my drawing tablet, which is much more ergonomic to me than any mouse or controller.I have a number of minor gripes with some of the clunkiness in the game's UX, and I'd love it if any one of them was addressed:- If you want to buy items in bulk from NPC vendors, you need to manually click on the plus button for every item you want to buy. So if you want to buy 10 of an ingredient, you need to click plus nine times. You cannot hold down the plus button to make it count up on its own, and you cannot press minus to instantly set it to the max.- If you've put a dozen ingredients into a potion brew, and decide you want to start over from scratch, you need to drag and drop every single ingredient out of the brew back into your inventory.- The only menu where you can actually get an overview of the potions you're holding, as well as sort them according to type, is the shop display menu. Having a general "view inventory" menu would be very helpful for example when you're figuring out what potions to brew and want to check if you're low on any particular sort of potion.- Every time a customer walks up to buy a potion, you have to click through two (2) textboxes of flavor text. There's a skip button yes, but you have to mouse over to click the skip button every time a new one walks in. You might sometimes get as much as a dozen customers or more per shop open session, which you can initiate multiple times a day, so this gets old very fast.- Before you leave an NPC vendor in town to go to a different one or return to your shop, you need to wait for them to throw out a dialogue box and wait a couple of seconds before the loading screen and transition initiates. This isn't a big deal in isolation, but when you're checking every single NPC every time you go into town, and often have to check back and forth between them multiple times because maybe you realized you need to buy an item off of one of them to gift to another one, or you finished your main shopping from one NPC and have money leftover that you want to spend on a different NPC's store, this delay adds up and gets grating.- If you want to change out the equipment in your store, you need to first enter the brewing menu, watch a loading screen, bottle any potions that have finished crafting, leave the brewing menu, watch a loading screen, click on the customization menu, change equipment, watch a loading screen for entering basement customization if you need to go there, change equipment, then leave the customization menu. It's very clunky and even on an SSD that makes every loading screen barely a second long it feels like a chore.- This one isn't really an issue so much as a personal aesthetic gripe, but it bothers me personally that Brewing and Gardening, the two tasks you might want to check in on and update every time block that you spend in your shop, are spread apart in the menu. I think it would also be helpful if these icons on the home menu had little number boxes indicating the amount of active brews and growths (and maybe if they're finished?) so you don't need to enter the menus themselves to double triple check before advancing your time slots with a different task.- You cannot check daily events while in an Adventuring menu, so if you want to double check what the daily bonus and overtaxed locations are while selecting location, you need to exit out of the Adventuring menu to look and then go back in. This all looks like a big list of complaints as if I hated the game, but I'm enjoying it a lot and stayed up until 5am last night playing it. I'm just hoping a dev might see this review and consider making some tweaks to the UX which would improve my experience even more. One of these small issues in isolation is absolutely not a deal breaker, it's just because there are multiple of them that they stand out to me in my playing.The core gameplay of this game is already very good. I'd love it if the systems and menus surrounding it were cleaned up in a future patch or sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: So I was absolutely excited to start playing this. The characters themselves is what first grabbed me, followed by potion crafting and running a business. It's an interesting world filled with a lot of amazing people and places. I really love this and want more people to experience this. HOWEVER: the time management is bad... very bad. So as most people have said, the first part of the game when you compete in the first competition is honestly stressful. I managed to scrape by. But it wasn't due to poor time management on my part. Surprisingly...I tried to send out for more supplies as much as possible, and giving all new ingredients to Quinn as soon as I get them. I'd stock up when prices were good and paid attention to what was selling and not selling. Upgraded when I could and I still stressed so bad to prepare for the first competition. I feel that the time management is not where it should be. Especially while trying to run a business and send out ventures AND PREPARE FOR A CONTEST.... it's a lot. Of course you get some sort of rhythm but it still feels like a crunch for time. Now aside from trying to get ready for the competition. You have all these wonderful and interesting characters to interact with and get to know. With the time limit and quickly the game is over, that's it. Can't go back to finish getting to know the characters. I feel like it's really taking away time for the player to really soak up the content in this game. You have this whole world, all these characters, fun writing and art, and it feels like I cannot enjoy it because of the time constraint. I would have happily go out and try to forage myself if that means I don't have to do this constant back and forth losing so much time in the day. Or at least not have traveling and opening up my shop to sell a few items take up a huge time slot.TLDR Please fix the time management. If you really want people to enjoy the hard work you and your team have put into this game. Let us actually have time to do so and not feel like we are constantly rushed.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game has a very fun mix of mechanics, between the store management and deck building, and how building your relationship with the different people in town feed back into the 2 main elements. My problem with the game comes from the dissonance of the chill potion brewing and characters, and the immense time pressure the game puts on you, both the daily 6 time slots, and short time periods between rounds of the potion brewing tournament. This game probably just isn't for me but I wanted to have more time to explore and play with the mechanics of the game than I felt I was given. Due to the loop of selling, talking with the townspeople, and brewing you have IMO too limited resources to adequately explore all of the aspects fully as I felt you needed to do too much optimization of your time/money in order to succeed. Unfortunately due to that optimization pressure it killed my enjoyment of the game and I quit part way through, which is a shame because I enjoyed the characters, and the mechanics of the game. Just not enough to make me want to keep play.

_childDocuments_.review: Potionomics is filled with amazing characters and a ton of mechanics. It is a genuinely fun game to play with so much to do!That said, that is also it's biggest flaw. The story is broken up between the days running and improving your shop, and competition days. You must prepare the required potions to win each competition, otherwise you will default on your debt without the prize money and it's game over. Thus, you're running on a time limit each time. Most of the time I had plenty of time, but having a timer looming over my head always added that extra layer of stress and worry about doing everything I wanted to. Honestly, there were some mechanics that I never took the time to learn because I was either in a vicious cycle of earning money then immediately spending it all on necessities, or I simply felt I didn't have the time and energy to spare.This, of course, would have been okay if there was a free-play mode, either as a separate mode, or as a post-game reward, allowing you to play and do everything you like without the countdown of the competitions looming over your head. Or maybe even a New Game+. Unfortunately, this game doesn't have anything like that, which is REALLY disappointing, as it's the perfect sort of game for that. Ultimately, I'd say it's worthwhile to play, just keep in mind that anything you haven't done before the last competition won't be getting done.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the hardest thumbs-down I've ever had to give. I was waiting for this game for years, as the animation and premise looked absolutely incredible. And for the first 6 hours or so, I was in love with the game, thinking it might even be my game of the year. The first chapter was a blast. The second one started to be a bit of a slog... and by halfway through the third chapter I just couldn't do it anymore. The art, the music, the atmosphere, the characters, the writing, everything is extremely high quality... but the gameplay loop just drives me insane. The time management is insanely tight, and once you've got several cauldrons, shelves, and adventurers, each of which you have to manage manually, several times a day, every day, for 10 days every chapter... throw in a surprising amount of RNG, and it just turns Potionomics into one of the most tedious experiences I've had in a long time. In the end I just can't recommend this game unless you have a ton of patience and enough time on your hands to really micromanage everything to the extent the game requires of you in order to conform to its time constraints.

_childDocuments_.review: I came from seeing busty witches, I stayed for a nice story.Potionomics starts off with a young college graduate saddled with a new found debt, go figure. You've gotta help Sylvia make potions to win contests and pay it off, or you will be cursed. The curse being working a cubicle for the rest of your life, but yeah. Game provides you plenty of nice characters, with background conflicts and stories for each one. You can romance most of the people in this game, just note, only one. Choose your poison, because you've got: Rude busty conwoman, A Pacific Islander Walrus man, Punk Rocker chick, Tomboy Warrior Gal, Non-Binary sleep-deprived sales person, Son of a Duke running the Adventurer's Hall, Forest Gal(She has horns and a wooden arm, don't get splinters,) All Natural Vegan Adventurer guy, and a quirky office working Moth Girl. Do not try and seduce the cats please. You talk to these people day in and day out while working on better and better potions, amassing cards to use, as well as Ingredients for your potions. These cards you use are to wager your potions for higher prices. Plenty of ways to play, so you could play through a couple of times.

_childDocuments_.review: After spending my entire week on it and beating the game, here's what I have to say!If only for the gorgeous artstyle, animation, graphics, UI, music and writing, the game is absolutely worth it. You can feel the amount of care and love poured into every aspect of the game, and it's a wonderful experience through and through. It's just absolute visual and musical candy!The mashing of different gameplays is ambitious, but I think Potionomics manages it well. However, the game is more challenging than it appears to be. It demands a good deal of strategy and punishes you if you fumble. You need to craft a battle plan and play your cards efficiently to get through each roadblock. The first 10 days are especially difficult, because you're learning the ropes of the game, and figuring out how the many moving parts interact with each other - but when you do, the game becomes a ton of fun. By the end of the game, I even had most of my time to spare to increase friendship with the characters, and way more cash than I needed (enjoy those ramen, Sylvia!)The game could use some quality of life improvements, minor balances and postgame content, but given how reactive they are, I'm certain the devs are planning on it. But despite these little flaws, I'm hooked on those potions and this loveable cast of characters, and given the chance I'm sure you can too.

_childDocuments_.review: I regret buying the game yet the game is close to a perfect game.The problem is the game is designed for a single play (poor replayability) through AND the crazy amount of mouse clicking it takes to get stuff done mid end game.   , I REALLY WISH the devs would add a few interface, quality of life, features that would make the game replayable. The interface could be improved to reduce the mouse clicking.For example, mid game an onward you need to buy lots of ingredients.  The only way to buy ingredients is 1 click at a time, so if you want 200 ingredients from an expedition, you get to click 200 times.  No shortcut keys or hotkeys like holding down shift while clicking exist.Another example, you can't save a recipe you figured out with specific ingredients.  So you have to write them down which gets messy fast.  I want to be able to record the perfect ingredient combos that I find through an in game interface.  (there are hundreds of ingredients and no easy way to find or sort through them).  The sorting interface is limited, could be much more effective with minor interface adjustments.I spent alot of time trying to remember and find the ingredient amounts I had already discovered.Don't get me wrong, I would put hundreds of hours more in this game if it's interface didn't waste so much of my time.  It is fun to see how fast I can make money and to hunt for new ingredients. I really like the idea of the game.  I love the polished feel of the sounds and expressions.  I feel bad about leaving a bad review but I'm to angry that this game was so close to perfect but it's interface makes it painfully slow to get things done!!   So much clicking :(The interface is so bad I declare that the developers don't play this game for fun themselves.  It almost feels like politically correct creative rich kids got together, wrote the story, drew great pictures, and payed some developers to make the game without actually playing the game themselves all the way to the end without cheating dev tools enabled.   Otherwise they would have realized the interface robs the game of replayability and joy.I really am angry, I am constantly on the hunt to great games and this game could be one if the interface was refined a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: I just rolled credits on this game, just a hair over 20 hours. Ultimately, I love this game. The art style is beautiful, both your protagonist and the NPCs you can form relationships with are fantastically designed with lots of character. The haggling aspect of the game is pretty fun, especially once you start getting more cards for your deck from the NPCs and you can really craft a deck that suits your playstyle. One thing I'm seeing listed as a con is that, at least at first, particularly if you're doing a blind playthrough, it can be fairly stressful trying to get the ingredients and equipment you need to make the potions you need for competition,  and that's fairly true. The game hits the ground running and you only 9 in game days between each competition to make any necessary upgrades, discover new ingredients you may need, and finish the potions for the next competition, all while selling potions in your shop to keep the money flowing. That said, once you get a feel for the game, and especially if you're used to playing management sims that require you to plan and budget your time, you'll be fine. I didn't hit a failure on competition day until the very end of the game, and going to a save from a few in game days ago and making a few changes to my use of time and my deck led me to beating the final competition with ease. I would say that I wished the game had something in the way of a post game or endless mode after you beat the story, just to mess around in. But that's a pretty minor complaint, as there's currently not THAT much reason to do so unless you, like I said, just want to mess around, finish off some relationships and max out your shop. The characters in this game are fantastic and I loved watching them interact. Sylvia, your character, is absolutely adorable, and all her potential friends and suitors bring some widely varied personalities to the table that are fun to develop a relationship with. The dating sim aspect is pretty light, you can easily form a relationship with whichever character you like simply by spending a little time with them regularly and throwing gifts their way. Things don't get any kind of steamy, and honestly that's a good thing, as I feel that it would clash with the game's overall feel and tone if they did. All in all, if you enjoy deckbuilders and management style games, you would be cheating yourself by sleeping on this game. It's an absolute delight from start to finish. Now if you'll excuse me, I'm going to start a second playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: The hours played aren't accurate - I have a bad habit of letting games run all day.Okay, so, I'm an Atelier/Recettear vet, and I really wanted to like this game - when it was gifted to me, I jumped right on it.  After entering the week of the second in-game competition and getting myself screwed by the brutal time limit after trying my best to make careful moves, however, I'm here writing a not recommended review.The game is absolutely gorgeous, and it's a genre that I love, but holy hell it's so stressful I can't stand it. The game has you constantly scrambling in the absolute worst way. There's so much to do and see and I WANT to do and see it all, but I can barely manage to keep the business afloat! Everything you do costs time, and there's barely enough of it to accomplish the basic goals, let alone get to know any characters! I'm technically doing all right, I guess, but it feels like drowning - managing tiny gasps of air while the time limit and your chronically-low funds press in on you from all sides, wanting to pull you under. As good as the character designs/animations, music, and general  are, this game is just such an unpleasant chore to play... to say I'm disappointed is an understatement. I was following the game on Twitter!That said, I just can't keep playing this - at least, not until they add an easier difficulty mode or double the time between competitions, or  to make it more manageable. I'm an old fart with a lot of real life stressors, and I certainly don't need that same time-focused stress when playing a video game.  Games are supposed to be FUN, and for me, at least, this just isn't.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: The rush the contest puts you under REALLY sucks but the game play is fun.All the characters that I've run into so far are quirky, interesting, and I've love to have more time to get to know them.I'd love nothing more than to slowly pay off my debt at the end of the week by selling potions and making friends in the town.SAVE OFTEN. USE ALL THE SAVE SLOTS. SAVE AT THE BEGINNING OF EACH WEEK. Or you'll have to restart your entire play through and that sucks.----------------I very much enjoy the game play mechanics, the potion making is thankfully easy to grasp and the deck building isn't too complicated. I was worried about that aspect when I bought the game as I don't have a great track record with deck builders. My favorite part is all the characters are quirky and full of personality! I want to meet them all and hang out with them but the why you're rushed by the ever looming "contest" really puts a damper on it for me. I don't particularly like feeling rushed and honestly that's all I felt while playing this. You don't have enough time in the day to juggle everything and I guess that's the point but honestly I'd LOVE for there to be a way to play the game where I can enjoy the world the developers crafted without having to be rushed by a 9 day timer. My first play through I couldn't make it past the second contestant because I just couldn't get good enough ingredients and no amount of haggling was going to make up for that fact.

_childDocuments_.review: Admittedly, after losing the first competition and being forced to go through the tutorial again (including two different haggling tutorials) I almost gave up and wrote a negative review, but I persevered and finished the game, and I'm glad I did, because the game is amazing. It took me about 60 hours in total to complete the game, and even though the replayability seems very low because the game is linear, I really enjoyed the time that I spent playing it. I would love to see the game turned into a roguelite (or maybe a roguelike), because the mechanics are really fun, and there's definitely an opportunity for replayability with some adjustments. Overall, I highly recommend it and I'm looking forward to seeing more games from this developer.

name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance
detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition About the Game The Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance Digital Deluxe Edition includes: • Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance Base Game • Mitama Dance of Wealth - Increases the drop rate of items that can be sold for Macca. • Mitama Dance of EXP - Increases drop rate of items that give the protagonist EXP and ally demons EXP. • Mitama Dance of Miracles - Increases drop rate of items that give Glory points needed to learn new bonus effects. • Demon Subquest - Sakura Cinders of the East - Additional subquest that allows players to recruit the demon “Konohana Sakuya” if they defeat her. • Demon Subquest - Holy Will and Profane Dissent - Additional subquest that allows players to recruit the demon “Dagda” if they defeat him. Experience two complete story paths in Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance, both filled with conflicting and tragic choices, forcing you to confront which ideologies you are willing to fight for. As order and chaos crumble around you, forge your own path to dictate the fate of humanity. 'Canon of Vengeance' – a dramatic tale of revenge by the fallen, centered around new characters and an enigmatic cohort of demons, the Qadištu, who plot their own dark designs apart from the war of those who fight to maintain order and those who seek to defy it. 'Canon of Creation' – an eternal conflict between angels and demons, in which the protagonist fights for the world’s fate. Battle through a decimated Tokyo, reduced to an expansive wasteland and overrun by mythical demons. Roam across wide, open areas and explore new locations for life-saving items or encounter a multitude of demons to battle or befriend as allies, including dozens of newly added demons to this game. Fully evolved with stunning visuals for modern consoles, the dark lore, unnerving atmosphere, and beautiful and monstrous demons are back and better than ever. Massively expanded with new areas, demons, and music, Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance features more accessible gameplay, an improved battle system, new demon experiences, and greater field exploration. Embark on this definitive version of the critically acclaimed Shin Megami Tensei V, massively expanded with a brand-new storyline featuring new locations, demons, and choices to make that will dictate the fate of all existence. • Intense, Turn-Based Combat System • Over 270 Demons to Recruit and Command • Explore a New Post-Apocalyptic Tokyo • Make New Allies Along Your Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Mechanically satisfying and visually stunning, SMT V: Vengeance unleashes the game's hidden potential.The Canon of Vengeance campaign is significantly better than the original's Canon of Creation, adding fleshed-out alignment reps that actually give the player a reason to consider their actions. It still isn't perfect, however, as the final zone of the game was too similar to the original to feel completely fixed.SMT's turn-based combat is still probably the most fun JRPG system out there. On hard difficulty, being underleveled for a boss means you're in for a bit of a challenge, but never doomed. Not once did I ever feel the need to grind, except for post-game bosses. You have so many tools at your disposal and finding out what works for each challenge is part of the fun.Even if you have the slightest interest, I highly recommend trying it out. It's just so fun.

_childDocuments_.review: SMTVV has the most fun gameplay out of any Atlus game I've played. When you get in your flow of traversing through Da'at, finding miman, fighting demons, fusing demons etc., it feels rly good. The game also gives you all the tools you need to fuse the best demon you want with essences, incenses, reverse fusion, and more.Although SMTVV improves on the original in many ways (better traversal, playable party members, unique skills, demon haunts, new content), it still falls short in some areas similar to the original. Although the new story is a bit better, I still feel it's lacking. They made an effort to put more emphasis on the characters but in the later part of the story I feel like the progression kind of falls off. Additionally, the new dungeon, Shakan, like the other dungeons is pretty linear. I hope in future SMT games they will implement dungeons with more mechanics/puzzles similar to older titles like Nocturne and Digital Devil Saga.Rly good game. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Where do I even begin with this one...After playing the original SMTV back in 2021, hearing about how there were some hidden button icons in the release back then, everyone kinda felt like a rerelease was inevitable, ala SMTIV:A. While we didn't get a full-on sequel, what we did get was a clearly passionate re-release of a game that had a troubled development. I mean, look. The whole original story is here, along with a NEW ONE?? That's wild.A lot of things ended up changing from then to now. The biggest one for me, was the combat balancing. While I loved the original's system to bits, I had to admit it felt a bit awkward how much levels mattered, in regards to combat in general. It was pretty strict, so to hear that this version of the game changed it, and that it was allowing you to be lower leveled again for hard encounters? That was AWESOME to me. A big part of SMT is the strategy before battles. What your party setup is before taking on a challenge. To have to be within a certain level range felt a little insulting to how it used to be, but now, it's more or less back to how it was. Be prepped for an encounter, and you can take on whatever you feel like you think you can.The other thing is, now that this game is on Steam especially, the game looks prettier than it ever did before. The game's stylized graphics, even without the most absolute highest polygons, shines through immensely. From colors popping, to shines, glares, and even winds in the air being so much more noticeable and less muddied. Like, so much so that this game not having a photo mode feels like a crime. Seriously, if you play this game, try to take in the environments you're in. The presentation is absolutely beautiful, despite any of the game's tones.Speaking of tones, everyone also knows the original story, named "Canon of Creation" in this release, has been infamously labelled as not the best in this series, and for good reason, honestly. A lot of ideas felt lost or not really put together in the best way they could be. The new "Canon of Vengeance" aims to correct this, and for the most part, it succeeds. The characters you get introduced to early in the game play a much more thorough, major role in the story. Characters once forgettable or sidelined shine much brighter, enough to the point where they're much more memorable parts of the game.And, if we wanna talk about memorable, Vengeance's wide array of additional music tracks for (mini) bosses and a couple new areas introduced is just spectacular. Ryota Kozuka did an amazing job with the new songs added, to the point where it feels like the two different Canons just have entirely different OSTs (outside of shared areas and boss fights between the routes, of course). Many of these additions are serious headbangers, or nice, atmospheric vibes that keep you calm. They'll seriously stick to your mind for a while.The only gripe I can personally mention here, are things basically at the end of the game, where it feels like the story direction still had some missed opportunities.Regardless of all this, if you like SMT or have an interest, especially now after the releases of Persona 3 Reload and Metaphor: ReFantazio, give this game the shot it deserves. Vengeance is one of the best SMTs, in freedom of its mechanics, soundtrack, overworld exploration and presentation. It even runs near flawlessly on Steam Deck, if that's what you choose to play on (which this game is perfectly designed for, now that you can also save anywhere in the overworld)!

_childDocuments_.review: If you're previously familiar with mainline SMT games, you will not be disappointed with this newest installment. You get a lot more tools than you generally did in previous games to build your team how you like, and can keep demons viable for a lot longer than before. On normal, you may find the challenge a bit lacking if you know what you're doing.If you liked persona 3-5 but have not played any mainline SMT games, think about what you liked most about Persona. Is it the story, characters, and slice of life aspect? Skip this. If you preferred the combat, get this ASAP.If you're brand new to the series as a whole, including Persona, but have played other JRPGs, understand that the demon summoning and fusion format may come across as a bit odd to get used to. Imagine Dragon Quest Monsters with lesser focus on selective breeding and a greater focus on tactical turn based combat. Your party composition frequently changes, and you're expected to have a decently sized pool of demons to work with, without getting too attached to any particular demon throughout the game. The series has come far from its classic Wizardry inspired roots, however. If you're up for a challenge and want a good place to jump in to one of the longest running rpg series, this is your place to do it.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game when it launched on Switch and thought it was okay if not underwhelming and never got that far. This version's QOL features actually brought me around to liking it a lot more. Despite rolling my eyes at all the "omfg 60 FPS" reviews here while it was downloading it really did make an impactful difference.As for the actual game, first and foremost the best quality of it is that you can spend so much time exploring and building your team at you leisure, discovering new parts of the map without any guidance and getting into fights with enemies you're not strong enough for yet. I think there was like 3 times in 25 hours where I ran into an invisible barrier that fades to black and turns you around, which is a massive improvement over other JRPGs of this type. The one thing SMT veterans complain about a lack of choice in the story, but the amount of decisions you make in a moment to moment basis more than makes it up for me.My criticisms are very minor, they literally copied Koroks from Breath of the Wild with two unnecessary fade to blacks that get irritating very quickly. However, there are "only" 200 of them. The beginning of the game is very handholdy and slow, but only lasts like one or two hours and like I said the interruptions are extremely minimal. My smallest nitpick are the demon negotiations, which have been tweaked in a way where they feel a lot more random, but give you ways to brute force them. I feel like I have less agency in this part of the game compared to prior ones.As an SMT sequel, the changes they made compared to the previous games were weird at first but make a lot of sense and retain a huge sense of freedom while still being challenging. The magutsuhi meter is probably the best new mechanic because of the way if increases your options and influences your strategies. Even keeping it full and not spending it has its advantages. And for the love of god, they made it easy to find the second demon you want to fuse again. Overall it's another amazing entry in this series, and I'm glad that this, Nocturne, and SMTIV are all wholly unique and enjoyable games in their own ways.
