_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, but in the end I was just disappointed.Let's get the pros out of the way first.  The combat is the best evolution of the Press Turn system I've played.  Essenses, elemental affinities and Magatsuhi moves (basically limit breaks) are all nice additions.The more open map layout is nice, and I like the verticality, but there are only four areas in the entire game.  And they are all too similar.  Ruined city with sand, ruined city in the dark, ruined city in the snow... Vengeance replaces one area, but it's just another ruined city.  In the original scenario the plot is just kinda missing.  They did an alright job of setting up a plot and then the game just skips to the ending(s).  Each ending gives maybe 5-10 minutes of new cutscenes and a different boss fight or two.  The plot of Vengeance is better, but that's not saying much.  It adds a new enemy faction, the Qadistu (sp?) with cool designs and quirks.  You fight them in a group battle.  When you win, they literally say "No, you lost", beat the crap out of you in a cutscene and accomplish their goal anyway.  Then they disappear from the game and are never heard from again.  Then the game more or less reverts back to the original plot until the last 30 minutes.To me, the improvements don't make up for the pieces that are still obviously missing.  The Vengeance storyline makes up for some of the game's weaknesses but not nearly enough.  It needed to be a completely new scenario set in unique areas.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played the original on Switch and being a long time SMT fan, this port is a God send (pun intended). No longer will you have to put up with sub 30 FPS, distant moving objects slowed to a crawl, and just the general bad performance the OG had on the glorified Android phone Nintendo calls a console. Not only that, but this Vengeance version comes chock full of extra content. New demons, new skills, and a demon dialog side area that is a fun distraction (Seriously, the demon negotiation writing was some of the best stuff in the original, so these extra conversations are highly entertaining). But the best additions so far is undoubtedly the work they did on the narrative. The story was the weakest part of the original release, sadly. I have only made it to the second area of the Nether realm, but choosing the "Vengeance Canon" at the beginning was a noticeable departure. To see Atlus put in the work and really flesh out the muddy areas and add a TON of characterization to the cast is a testament to their effort to make SMT V the crown jewel in the series. If you are a fan of JRPGs, challenging turn based combat, or are simply curious why everyone keeps talking about this "Meegamy Tensee" or "Purse Owner", Buy this immediately.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10: HD FMVs for Cadaver's Hollow and World of Shadow introduction Pls! Perfect Otherwise. _childDocuments_.review: Okay, so about 15 hours in, and I can already say I love this version way better than the original. The short answer is because SMT VV actually feels like it has an identity of its own. Vanilla SMT V felt like it wanted to be almost like another Nocturne, making a lot of parallels to it without really doing anything to stand out from all the references. Vengeance, while still drawing clear inspiration from Nocturne still, actually has a story to keep you interested (without getting into spoilers, the brand new story actually seems to have more going on in the short time I've played, versus the drawn out plot points of the original).Traversing the Netherworld is much more easy now, between some magatsu rails, and being able to save anywhere. Letline Fount were fairly plentiful, but there are still times you don't have access to one. So, it's nice to still be able to save when you want/need to. Besides, you still need to go to founts for fusions, shopping, etc. Speaking of fount functions, the demon haunt, while a little undercooked imo, is still a nice addition. It's nice to see your demons actually become more loyal to you as you talk to them, and fight alongside them. Plus, chatting with Aogami is always a good time, and provides you additional stat boosts. However, and this where I say it's undercooked, none of the demons will show complex personalities. I guess that goes with there being so many, but a few notable ones probably could have more going on.As a small point, the music slaps as hard in Vengeance as it did in the vanilla game. If you liked what V was doing sound wise, you'll like Vengeance too.Lastly, the gameplay is still really solid. I liked a lot of changes the original game made to shake things up, and it seems like they just tweaked most of it here. Bosses no longer feel like massive damage sponges, and demons now seem to have some innate skill attached to them, making party composition only more fun.That said, my only real gripe at this point would be the implementation of the Magatsuhi skills. It's not that they're all bad, but they pretty much get overshadowed by you starting with the guaranteed critical one. Basically, when you activate the critical skill, all of your attacks are guaranteed to be critical hits, making getting extra turns a breeze. For those not familiar, mainline SMT games, starting from 3 have used what's called the press turn system. If you crit, or hit an enemy's weakness, you get an extra turn. Since you can have a party of 4 demons, you can essentially get 8 turns total. To me, it just seems like a no brainer to activate critical when your magatsuhi gauge is full, since you don't have to work as hard to get extra turns at that point. I dunno, I just wish they fixed this by not giving you such a good skill at the beginning of the game.Overall, SMT V Vengeance is worth your time, when you're able to get it.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply one of the best JRPG I've ever played. I'm having way more fun here than I did in Persona 5 Royal gameplay wise.The combat is engaging due to the challenge it offers which can be punishing if you're not prepared and get complacent. High level of customisability of each of your party members allows you to beat the game fairly easily if you take your time to learn what your demons can do and what your opponents throw at you and come up with a way to beat each battles. Level scaling is also no longer as strong as it was in the original, making low level runs possible as long as you know what you're doing and what you're up against so you can anticipate and counter what's coming at you properly.The soundtrack is stellar. May not be everyone's cup of tea however, especially if you're coming from Persona 5 and expect something similar here. For me personally the music in this game left a strong impression. You will not hear this kind of music in Nier, Persona, Fire Emblem, Scarlet Nexus etc. The soundtrack is unique and diverse, giving the game its own identity. Shin megami tensei IV is the only game I know that sounds similar given the soundtrack of it is composed by the same person.The newly added story content feels a lot more coherent than the original story. We get to see more of the characters, find out their motives and their worldview. They have proper characterisation this time around, most of the characters are no longer mere devices to drive the plot forward although one particular character is still handled as badly as he was in the original. And I can't take one the of the new characters seriously as the things she says is sometimes are just ridiculous and/or extreme. The Qadistu are an interesting villain, but some have fewer screen time than the other, which is a shame. I just wish they appeared more in general.The only downside to this game is that if you strive to complete every content there is in the game, you may want to purchase the Mitama dlc to help with grinding. If you're not a streamer or a content creator, don't waste hours, days of your life grinding a video game especially if you have lots of better things to do. And don't listen to any of those who say you're basically cheating and that your run is invalid just because you use the dlc. At the end of the day, it is about self control. _childDocuments_.review: Excellent JRPG combat, but this game is not for everyone, nor is it perfect. Personally, it is one of my favorite games of all time. The combat, music, and atmosphere are the most standout parts of the game, while the narrative and exploration can stand a lot to gain.The gameplay is tight and centers around constantly redefining and rebuilding your team, slowly getting stronger and stronger as you burn through an ascent to godhood over the course of the game. You unlock more demons, more skills, and more abilities every step of the way which widens your arsenal as enemies and bosses can do more and more. Battles get more and more complex as the game furthers, and some of the endgame bosses and superbosses do an excellent job of challenging your understanding of the combat and the fusion system.The music is very unique and features a lot of unconventional and unorthodox sounds, but it sounds great and really helps set the mood of the game. Ambient tracks have a certain sense of melancholy to them, while combat tracks stand over a wide range from rock to metal to groovy in all sorts of ways. It's a great blend of sounding both modern and "spiritual", which helps sell the visuals and atmosphere of the game.The character designs of both the actual characters as well as the demons in this game are great. Many demons from older Atlus games are here, but the demons new to SMTV have great designs between Fionn, Hayatarou, Nuwa, Loup Garou, and so on. The new designs in Vengeance such as Anansi, Onyankapon, the Qadistu, etc. are great as well. It's nice to see more representation from cultures and time periods that haven't had much space in this series so far.The overworld exploration of the game is not great. The game primarily takes place across a few big areas, but the areas really lack in gameplay difference and don't make themselves stand out between each other. The game tells you where everything is on the map so you just wander around following the places where you know there are things, collecting items and fighting demons, and it stays this way the whole game. Knowing where everything is and this repetitive format can seriously wear you down by the end of the combat.Normal combat and the lack of any proper attrition while traversing can cause issues, too. Regular encounters are swing-y, but you can also save anywhere, so there is no danger. However in the original SMTV you could not save anywhere, which just make regular encounters really annoying because if you died far from a savepoint you would be forced to waste your time redoing arbitrary tasks like collecting items, which is just padding time for the sake of padding time. A middleground would be better; I think not letting you save anywhere but just booting you back to a checkpoint with maybe a money run like a souls-like may honestly be a better outcome for this kind of game.The story in both canons features a lot of flaws. A lot of characterization and the way the narrative is presented can be very lacking. While some characters are strong even with limited screentime, this is one of the worse Megami Tensei games when it comes to story, in my opinion. I think there's still a lot of value in it, though. Surprisingly, I think this game's story is better on a thematic level than it is a narrative one. The meaning of what goes on behind the scenes and how the writers are using the demons to tell a story about contemporary issues can feel really surprisingly nuanced about the subject matter, coming from Atlus.The game is really good, to re-iterate. If you're looking for tight, well-made JRPG combat, a uniquely amazing soundtrack and atmosphere, and hundreds of lovely creature designs, this game is for you. If you're looking for a super well-crafted narrative or want to engage in a drawn-out dungeon crawl of attrition, you might be better off looking elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: 100%'d the original on Switch, and this version have run super well for being a Switch port. Though most of cutscenes coming from original are very obviously up-scaled from Switch.To summarize the Shin Megami Tensei series or SMT for short: It's basically Pokemon, if the Pokemon are talking demons and will brutally murder you if you fail your dialogue checks.Persona 5's "new" mechanics where you can talk to the demons was originally from this series, and similarly you need to learn the demon's quirks and offers them stuff in order to let the conversations going smoothly.Comparatively.... honestly SMT V doesn't offer anything new. It is pretty much almost the same type of deal with SMT 3 Nocturne, where you as the protagonist gets thrown into a world of demons and you might or might not be able to return things to how they were... or maybe you'll become a new god instead.The story is very heavy with imagery of gods and demons, which is a tradition in this franchise.So for better or worse, it is the similar kind of vibes to Nocturne. Although Nocturne was very specifically more about the demons of Goetia, this one not so much. And this time around you also get humans as party members, what i find interesting with the humans is that they tend to have different sources of power that kinda references other SMT games.And a WARNING to the Persona fans: This is not a Persona game.SMT V is more of a classic JRPG where most of your time will be spent on running around the maps, fighting enemies, collecting items, and doing small side quests.Outside of chatting a demon up to join your party, "Socialization" exists but not to the extent you get with Persona 3, 4, or 5. You basically have a pocket dimension where you can chat with or give gifts to the demons/humans you've recruited to make them stronger, and also with the "Aogami" you've fused with to make *yourself* stronger.To conclude:If i have to give it a score it would be a solid 8/10 as i get everything i wanted out of it as big fan of SMT 3 Nocturne. But honestly the Persona series will offer much more in terms of story, characters, and systems. SMT V is mostly better in terms of combat and party management.Get this game if you want a traditional and straightforward JRPG adventure where the main focus is to recruit monsters as your party member.==========================================================================p.s. Currently as i wrote this review on late September 2024, the game is being review bombed by a group of Chinese players who are angry that the game had a 30% sales 3 months after Steam release. Look at the negative review spikes on the chart, around September 14th and 20th.That's why the current review score dropped to mostly positive... While a few of them are legit complains about the game, most of the reviews have very little to do with what they think about the game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's totally, entirely reasonable to feel burned and ripped off by the original release, which was just objectively an incomplete game. I don't blame anyone for swearing off Vengeance, especially at full damn price again. However, I do personally think it's worth it. Vengeance is, finally, an absolutely lovely game top to bottom. It has some of the deepest, most satisfying, customizable, unique, and well-designed turn based combat to have ever existed. It has gorgeous art style and music, even if it's not the most graphically powerful game. The sense of humor and whimsy in the characterization of the demons and the strange world they live in is lovely, and it doesn't ever undermine the haunting, otherworldly, ethereal feeling that hangs over your time exploring the world of Vengeance. There is a strange feeling at times that the game is... almost an apology for the original version? But it's still an excellent game for newcomers and series veterans alike. It's incredibly accessible compared to its predecessors, yet has an uncompromising demand for you to try your hardest and smartest to succeed. It has an absolutely unique system of progression where grinding almost doesn't matter and you instead gain power by exploration and discovery. You're encouraged to not brute-force your way through combat like traditional turn based RPGs and instead treat everything as a puzzle, that can be solved through tactics or developing a team in the World of Shadows.I can't recommend this game enough. Buy it and absolutely SAVOR it. Stand on a dune overlooking the wastelands of the Netherworld, basking in the alien ambient music, watching the bizarre ecosystems of demons.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're coming to this as a fan of the Persona series and love its style, story, and interesting characters, this game may look appealing at first. It's made by the same studio, and it has many of the same demons/shadows as Persona, and a similar combat system to boot.While the Persona games can have some odd story choices, they usually feel somewhat grounded in reality. Characters' motivations may be extreme, but ultimately you could see how someone could be driven to the choices that they make. SMT5 has none of that nuance. The new Canon of Vengeance storyline is a definite level-up to the original Canon of Creation storyline, but compared to a Persona game, it's still a mere shadow writing-wise.If you're new to SMT5, the Canon of Creation storyline is pure JRPG nonsense from the get-go. The characters are shallow caricatures of people, and there's really no redeeming value to this original storyline except to serve as context for Canon of Vengeance. The combat is pretty good, but it still feels like a step down from Persona 5, which had a better story, too.Canon of Vengeance, the new addition, constantly references Canon of Creation and mostly serves to "surprise" you if you had played the original. The writing is leagues better than Canon of Creation, and the main cast (Yoko, Atsuta, Tao, and Dazai) all feel like they have some legitimate motivations and personalities. You only see it very briefly, as they spend -very- little time establishing the characters before either killing them off or turning them into Saturday Morning Cartoon villains.If you just want more Persona-esque combat and that's what draws you to the series, go for it. If you want a compelling story, play something else.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a long-time SMT fan who played the original release on Switch. The original release was not great, I wont be referencing every difference made, but I am unavoidably writing this with the original release in mind. Selling improved versions of games for full price a couple years later is a really terrible trend from Atlus, that being said, this is an extremely good release and giving it anything but a very positive review would be disingenuous.Every aspect of the game has been improved; narrative, character arcs, demon fusion, map traversal, the list can go on and on, with an absolutely killer new soundtrack, not to mention fantastic PC performance. My current playtime consists of a full run of the new Canon of Vengeance story on Hard difficulty, all sidequests, max% compendium.The new Canon of Vengeance narrative gives way more time to the cast and lets each character have breathing room to develop and have an actual arc, something the original sorely lacked. Characters who were previously completely flat and one-dimensional now frequently interact with the plot and feel much more directly linked to the overarching story. The alignment reps have much more evident motivation for their actions (yes even Dazai, though to a lesser extent than the others) Tao and Yuzuru in particular I thought were huge improvements. The new character Yoko is also a great addition; the reason for her inclusion isn't immediately apparent but she is far less of a mary-sue than other Atlus re-release heroines haha, and her dynamic with a certain other major character is very well done.The gameplay and mechanics have been vastly improved over the original in a variety of ways. The most prominent is the drastic reduction in level scaling damage numbers. While it still exists, its a far reduced amount, and a correctly built team can have a far more enjoyable time fighting enemies 10+ levels above them (way less gargantuan damage sponge walls in low level runs, huge positive). The new 'innate skills' is a really clever way to add some uniqueness to demons that would otherwise be overlooked, with some really cool effects too, I felt encouraged to build around innate skills rather than just strictly fuse the usual nulls/debilitate/luster candy etc. I'm a fusion addict and I love this feature.The music of SMT games has always been standout, and this is no exception. Ryota Kozuka has been killing it ever since SMT IV, and I genuinely believe he's composed some of his best tracks here. The sheer volume too, 89 new tracks!! and so many are unique and used in only one quest, one dialogue, one boss fight. It really feels like a labour of love. 'beast of bloodshed' and 'primordial goddess' are my favourite tracks, but this soundtrack truly is full of bangers back to back, it doesn't miss.With all that being said, the game is not perfect. Dampeners still exist and are unchanged from the original, they can still trivialise the early to mid game until enemies start getting pierce skills (of which there seem to be significantly more of in the later game, to its credit). I can only suggest to not use them, as the early game is quite a fun and balanced experience if you pretend they don't exist.Omagatoki: Critical is still just as strong as the original. I definitely felt far more incentivized to use other Magatsuhi skills and I certainly did throughout my playthrough, but it still feels weird having one of the strongest combat tools straight out of the gate. The story, while VASTLY improved over the original, does have quite a lull around the level 50-70 mark when you reach the Taito region. Its still like a 7.5/10 story compared to the 2/10 story of the original though, cant detract too much from that.As I'm yet to play through the original Canon of Creation, I cant comment on any improvements made directly to the narrative or encounters of this route, but the new Canon of Vengeance alone is reason enough to recommend this game. I love this series and I want to see it get the love it deserves for a great release like this. I can only hope an SMT IV port happens at some point, though the difficulties of a 3ds port are pretty apparent. Thanks for reading, see you next year for Soul Hackers 2: GOLD EDITION V5.1

_childDocuments_.review: Shin Megami Tensei V is a standout entry in the Megaten series, delivering the demon collecting and fusing you’d expect but at its peak.The game is set in a Tokyo caught between realities. You start as a student at Jouin High School and quickly find yourself entangled in the eternal struggle between heaven and hell, order and chaos. After encountering an ancient power, you become the Nahobino, a fusion of human and demon with godlike abilities. While the story is intriguing, it's unfortunately one of the weaker aspects of the game. There's a branching narrative that influences the ending, but I found the choices unclear, particularly at a pivotal moment near the end (no spoilers), where it felt like the game steered you along a predetermined path rather than letting you choose freely. The overall story is weak, with forgettable, shallow characters—especially disappointing given the studio's connection to Persona.Despite the story’s shortcomings, the gameplay shines. The power progression and monster collecting loop are top-tier and incredibly satisfying. As the Nahobino, you’re a blank slate, allowing you to swap and redefine skills as you progress. Customizing your skill set and affinities to exploit boss weaknesses and absorb their attacks is crucial, using demon essences, a finite resource gained through exploration and leveling. This mechanic encourages exploration and demon collection, as new areas introduce new demons with unique skills. The fusion system is another highlight, letting you combine lower-level demons into powerful new ones. With 276 demons and countless combinations, each with its own unique feel, skillset, animations, and dialogue, it’s an absolute blast.The game’s artistic design is fantastic. Demon designs are the best in the series, with stunning details that emphasize their distinctness and mythological origins. The open-world levels are varied and beautiful, featuring everything from wasteland deserts to 90s vaporwave aesthetics. The soundtrack is equally impressive, blending metal tracks with orchestral scores, synth jazz, and vaporwave—experimental yet perfectly suited to the game.The SMTV: Vengeance edition adds a wealth of new features and quality-of-life improvements, including enhanced visuals, a save-anywhere feature, a new story route, demon haunts, new dungeons, sidequests, and more. It feels like a new game compared to the original Nintendo Switch release, though it's disappointing that there’s no ultrawide resolution support.There are a few downsides. The lack of interaction with the world is a missed opportunity. The silent protagonist rarely impacts the events around them, and the branching narrative feels awkward and confusing. The absence of social hubs or towns can make the game feel lonely at times, with your only companions being demons who mostly offer flavor text, though it can be funny. Unfortunately, the story and characters fall flat, which is particularly disappointing given the series' connection to Persona.Overall, I enjoyed my time with SMTV, thanks to its exceptional gameplay, fantastic artistic design, and great soundtrack, but the weak narrative prevents it from being an all-time great.

_childDocuments_.review: Another absolute banger escapes the Nintendo Switch gulag. This is a dramatically expanded and improved version of an already magnificent game, so if you haven't had the chance to play it yet, there's no reason to keep waiting. Even if you did experience it in its original format, there is easily enough new content here to warrant a double dip. I'd already completed the original release two years ago, so this time I played through the all new Canon of Vengeance route. Overall it is an improvement on the original game's story, with a few caveats. A lot of work has been done to make the narrative more character driven, with new girl Yoko Hiromine along with Tao Isonokami being firmly center stage. Both girls accompany you for the majority of the journey, join your party as controllable guest characters, and represent the new story's two alignments, order and chaos. Yoko is a bit of a mixed bag as a character, but overall she was a good addition, bringing a more cynical and realist perspective to many of the game's ethical dilemmas The supporting cast have been fleshed out a bit more as well, with one particular cringelord antagonist being given a slightly better arc this time around. A lot of work was put in here to make me actually care about the human characters in this story, which is a shame, because the endgame really fails to deliver a suitable payoff. Instead of allowing your relationships with these characters and their actions to dictate how things play out, the story once again reverts to prioritizing alignment over everything else in the final act. This was a problem for me, because I ended up agreeing philosophically with a particular character for most of the game, only to have them later reveal a hidden agenda I had absolutely no desire to help them with. It was too late, however, and the alignment system basically forced me to support them. Having the other characters scold me for this like I just peed on the rug was icing on the cake. Overall it didn't stick the landing for me, but it's still a large improvement over Canon of Creation, the game's original story which is also included.In terms of gameplay additions there's a fair amount to talk about as well. The most significant of these is an entirely new area to explore in Canon of Vengeance that replaces the original game's third region. The new area integrates very well with the rest of the campaign and for me was easily the most fun region to explore. New demons, quests, navigators, and skills have also been liberally sprinkled throughout the journey. New difficulty options and an ability to increase the level cap have also been added to make new game plus more interesting should you so choose as well. Easily the greatest improvement though is the ability to save anywhere at anytime, with there even being a convenient hotkey that takes you straight to the menu. The game's difficulty definitely feels a bit more merciful with this addition. If I had to choose one standout aspect of this game to praise, it would be how 'snappy' the entire experience feels. Many JRPGs love to waste your time like they're being paid by the hour, but the SMT V experience is expertly designed to never sandbag the player or get in the way of your forward momentum. All cutscenes are skippable, battle animations can be fast-forwarded, and the majority of random encounters can be completed about 10 seconds if you know what you're doing. Grinding is definitely a part of the experience, but there is so much loot to collect, quests to complete, and upgrades to manage that I found myself naturally gaining all the experience I needed without having to hang around in one place for too long. It took me about 80 hours to fully complete the campaign and at no point did it feel tedious. If you didn't have the chance to experience this one on the switch, don't hesitate to pick this one up. If you've already experienced it once before, the new content and story are more than worth the asking price. Overall, if you're even remotely interested, I unconditionally recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: as i'm closing in on 100% achievements, having beaten all super bosses (sans ) with only godborn and virtual trainer left, i think it's about the right time for a proper review.smt5 is not only the latest entry to the mainline games, but it's also part of my personal project to play -most- of the smt games, old and new. i played this back on the switch for a little bit, but the performance left a lot to be desired, and as atlus announced this updated release, i decided to wait for its release. and by gods it was worth the wait.vengeance is what smt5 should've been back on its 2021 launch. everything looks crispier, it actually runs on 60fps, some demons that were suspiciously missing are added back in, you can save anywhere, and they got rid of the obnoxious level scaling! (the performance it can be even better if you download a mod called smtv fix, that also provides proper ultrawide support for the people who use it.)if you aren't new to the franchise, you'd almost certainly notice that this game is very, very similar to  that also features a boy being turned into a half-human, half-demon being by circumstances. of course, atlus knew that 3 was the most popular smt entry by far, but they also tried to make the plot work... but oh boy, the plot. let's get it out of the way, canon of creation is a product of a rushed development. i can't even say that it's serviceable because it just isn't. character development that goes nowhere (or goes too quickly). expositions and lore dumps for certain after every major area. the most randomest addition of lore because they suddenly remembered that not-joker was a character. they wrote zayin from smt2 again except if you completely misunderstood what made zayin so great. the complete nothing burger that is the chaos and neutral rep. the nonsense that was the true neutral ending.it's a whole mess. to the point that while the stakes were extremely high - i would even say that higher than 3's - it didn't feel like it at any point.canon of vengeance was their attempt at fixing the plot and... they did. obviously it's still no masterpiece, but now there's actually a flow to the plot. characters are introduced properly when they needed to. you actually get to hang out with them to understand their point of view and how they have their own conflicts that leads to growth. the fact that your choices in dialogue now actually matter and will lead to whichever ending you're aligned with, instead of Choose One. (sure you can argue being able to choose one is qol... but i'd prefer meaningful choices myself.)weirdly enough, though i really hated coc, in the end i was glad that i played it first prior to cov. cov was presented in a way that it kind of assumed that you've played coc and knows the context of some events that were ultimately left unexplained in cov. which is to say, i actually recommend the order of creation (true neutral) to vengeance (either ending), if you're willing to play this game more than once and sees both as a complete story rather than two (trust me it will make sense once you get to .)canon of creation: canon of vengeance: atlus got something going when they introduced the press turn system back in 3, and it's back with even more ways to strategize (literally too, omagatoki: strategize is very hilarious if you know how to work it). in addition to their abilities, every demon now comes with an innate ability that is independent from the rest of their kit. for example, the pixie now comes with , which potentially allows a demon to forgive you should a negotiation fail. with the addition of innate abilities, comes a new layer of teambuilding as some demons that used to be overshadowed are now getting their own spotlight.don't have much else to say in regard to the gameplay. it's just THE turn-based system for me. it's just fun to play through and mess around with builds, with essences being so accessible it's like atlus is begging you to try builds out. good stuff, good stuff.this one's for the achievement chasers. if you want to get all of them, you'd need to play at least 6 playthrough on the same save file, each with a different ending. this is because there are route-only demons and the final boss fights are just slightly different enough that they have different entries in the virtual trainer. it sucks, i know, but at least for some of the playthroughs you can just blow through them in a few hours in ng+ (and you should, for creation chaos, law and neutral).on top of that, you also need to take note of route-only superbosses. coc for  and cov for . it goes without saying i really like this game, but here's the thing... the 2021 release clearly wasn't a finished product and though this rerelease manages to 'fix the game, it's a separate purchase. atlus can make good games but my god are they ever so greedy when it comes to the monetization of their games. (soul hackers 2 dlc anyone?)vengeance should've been the 'base' form of the game. imagine a smt5 where they didn't have to scramble to make cov work in the frameworks of coc. hopefully the cursed development of smt5 taught them a lesson of finishing a product before releasing it. and a final, personal gripe. i certainly pray that the trend of devs forcing a paimon-like traveling companion on you, even if the story doesn't call for one (we already have aogami? the whole ass demon haunt?? why do we need a paimon???) ends sooner rather than later, because it's almost enough for me to dock a whole point just because of amanazako alone. atlus certainly agreed that she doesn't do anything for the plot, as her involvement in vengeance is next to practically nothing.  this is also not a spoiler because she truly does so little for the game that removing her changed literally nothing. at least her innate ability is good, lmao.ultimately, an annoying companion isn't enough to make this a bad game. 9.4/10. this is peak JRPG. though maybe not at $70... definitely worth it if it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Shin Megami Tensei V Vengeance is some of the most fun that I have ever had with a videogame. I played the original game on the Nintendo Switch back in 2022 and I loved it a lot, I found the art style, music, atmosphere, and demon designs so cool and awesome. With Vengeance, it enhances the original game by adding a lot of things that the original didn't have, one major example being a new campaign that has a new story and gives new lore to the original game. I do have to admit, the original story wasn't the best, but it I mainly forgave for having such cool concepts and lore. The new story is a definite improvement to the original campaign, especially with the Qadistu as the main bad guys. My best comparison to them would be  the Divine Powers from 4 Apocalypse, where they don't really align with Law, Chaos, or Neutral characters that you partner with, but instead they are their own individual group that have their own goals and will do anything to get them. You get a good chunk of the game with them, although I do wish that there was more content from them. The protagonist Nahobino gets a new form in this game and it has its own unique animations and new moves and all of them are very good to use, they range from "Ok I can work with this," to "This is OP!" One thing that I was pretty surprised about this game when I found out about it is that you could choose which story you want to play, you have a new campaign, but if you'd like to play the original you definitely can, I thought ATLUS would pull a Shin Megami Tensei Strange Journey Redux or Persona 5 Royal and slap the new stuff with the old stuff and it mixes in a way that feels out of place and is barely anything new. However the fact that the devs listened to criticism and reworked the whole thing into a separate story and gave you the ability to play the og is really awesome. The new map in the new campaign that replaces the 3rd area of the original is absolutely beautiful, a blast to go through, and the music is outstanding. It was a little disappointing that maps 2 and 4 didn't get reworked that much but I don't mind that much because I still had fun going through them. (I didn't say the first map because I think that is a great intro map) Overall this game lived up to my hype and I'd even say it is one of my favorite games, also it has Naamah and Dagda, so that is going to be hard to beat that. I give this game a 9/10, would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I played vanilla SMT5 on Switch and thought it was fun, but not up to snuff with Nocturne and 4.  After finishing the first area in Vengeance. I can safely say the game feels a lot more polished.  If you liked Nocturne, you can just buy this game now.  If you liked Persona combat and fusions, but want less talking and more fighting, you can stop reading and buy it now.  For anyone that didn't like the gameplay of Vanilla SMT5, here's a quick list of all the QOL changes I've noticed so far:-You can save ANYWHERE on the field.  Save points still exist for all other services, though.  -Protagonist gets a lot more stat points to spend.  You can crank his offense a lot higher now.  -The penalty for being leveled lower than  bosses has been toned down significantly.  You're not going to miss attacks just for being one or two levels below the boss. -Many shortcuts have been added to the field, cutting out a lot of time spent running through empty plains.-Every demon now has a passive ability that doesn't cut into their skill slots.  They're often niche, but It's free and it could spice up your boss battles. -New heroine has excellent magic stats, can use items, and can take one of your demon party slots. Your demon fusions don't need to juggle as much because the heroine can pick up the slack.-Money is generally easier to get.  Shortcuts make it easier to reach resource points and some demons make them restock faster.  Also, there are more options to negotiate with demons while saving money.  -During negotiations, demons will sometimes replace the entire process with an easy "Who's That Pokemon" quiz.  If you identify the Demon being outlined, the quizzer joins you automatically.  No Q&A RNG, no bartering, no stat checks, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: Three years ago when this game released, I remember playing this on the Nintendo Switch. It was one of the best looking games on that system of all time and from that moment, I knew that this game would not be constrained to inferior hardware. The beauty was there... The high definition, frame rates, and so much more fidelity.Base SMT 5 before Vengeance just felt so incomplete in some areas, there were places that would just be such a pain in the ass to navigate around just for a Miman or another collectable, the balancing of the enemies were out of wack and I swear they were able to dodge every attack if I was even a level lower...I'm glad to say that in Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance, every single problem I've ever had with the base Switch release of the game has been improved upon in spades. Not only in gameplay, graphics, and sound, but in story as well with the inclusion of the "Canon of Vengeance" path. - The Protagonist gains additional status points with the inclusion of the Demon Haunt, a rest area where you may talk with your Demons, along with Aogami to gain boosts to your stats, gain bonus items after bonding with them, or have those demons gain a boost of stats that can go up to +8 of a random stat!! So if they got something to say, hear them out!! - SHORTCUTS!! Oh I loooove shortcuts!! Magatsu Rails have been added to cut the time of moving all over a single area for the sake of your convenience! No more having to go around the entirety of Tokyo Tower to miss a single Miman and travel all the way back...Now when you actually find that Magatsu Rail and use it, you've permanently unlocked that shortcut for the rest of your playthrough! Happy Miman Hunting! - Over 40 new demons added to the large roster with the addition of Group Skills!! Too many Demons to count and you want your favorite hee-ho's to team up for a super special attack? Vengeance has fixed this issue with this new addition to make your favorite demons viable! However, with just a bit of grinding (and by that I mean a lot), ANY demon would be able to fight with you at the endgame... But nobody would be THAT dedicated, right? - Innate Skills are unique passive skills added to Vengeance, making every demon unique in their own way. For instance, Jack Frost's innate ability is "Fickle Personalty," and when activating an Omagatoki effect, the user's attacks with a + in that specific Skill Potential that strikes the enemy's weakness will be a critical hit! That's more Press Turns AND more damage! Imagine fighting a superboss with a Beast Omagatoki, Adversity, active! Imagine the critical potential!! - Along with many of these quality of life features, there have been a lot of other additional features added to the Vengeance port! Guest characters, under certain conditions a powerful foe may be finally able to join your party, Consecutive Encounters to chain enemies for bigger bonuses of Macca and EXP, new demon conversation variations of quizzes or giving them an item to instantly join your team, Auto-Battling now has an Auto Skill function, Aogami-type Essences have their own unique Husks on the overworld, and so much more!!This is probably the PERFECT JRPG that I've played in a long time. Why are you still reading this?! Get to it and buy the game already if you're convinced! You're missing out on some of the best gameplay, music and story!! I can't stress enough how amazing this is.

_childDocuments_.review: V:Vengeance is basically a what-if of what would have happened if, on release, SMTV was a game that was actually complete, and had a plot and characters and content and good area design. As it turns out, the result is that it's peak. New players should immediately plunge into the Canon of Vengeance storyline, because that's where all the meat is, frankly. Canon of Creation might as well be a bonus to let you see what the game used to be like, and the difference in quality between both plotlines is incredibly stark.Very highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: The original monster collector. Absolutely legendary game right here. TWO campaigns all the DLC from the previous switch version. Absolutely addicting, some demons can look like a straight up ♥♥♥♥, but that being said there are some AMAZING demons designs mixed in there. The BEST turn based combat out there and its not even close. Bosses have you at the edge of your seat, some are soul crushingly hard at times but in turn make the rush of winning all that more deserved. Replaying this game with all your demons and maxed out levels makes you feel like a GOD but there are secret endings that push your levels and stats even FURTHER to prepare you for even harder content. not to mention ALL the upgrades you got from the last play-through STACK with your current.The only aspect of the game that prevents it being a 10/10 is the story. the characters are very much one dimensional and the story overall is pretty simple. Cannon of Vengeance tries to add some interesting aspects to the story. Its definitely better than Cannon of Creation route from the first release but its still not as amazing as I wanted it to be. I was kinda bummed that it couldn't match SMT IV's ground breaking story but that's just how amazing that game is.Overall easily a 9/10 this is the best bang for your buck. You can't look at other turn based games the same and will easily be itching to go back after the credits roll. Damn near IMPOSSIBLE to play Pokemon knowing this thing exists.

_childDocuments_.review: The original Shin Megami Tensei V was already the best playing JRPG, and the Vengeance version manages to improve on it. ATLUS is taking advantage of their decades of JRPG experience to make the most mechanically dense take on "simple" turn based combat, while other franchises like Final Fantasy feel the need to make things fresh by changing their systems with every new release. SMT3 was genre defining, and ATLUS took the opportunities they had to expand on it's systems with SMT4 and SMT4A, while also learning from their mistakes (smirk). Thus SMT5V is the closest we have ever gotten to what I would consider perfect JRPG combat.Of course there are still small hiccups in balancing, like dampeners being super affordable. It's like they knew how powerful dampeners were when they decided to limit how many you can carry to 3, but you can still just buy them at any leyline fount for pocket change. And once again magatsuhi skills are too niche. It being a frequently used base mechanic means you must give the player access to a good one from the start. But it just ends up overshadowing the rest. You even get access to a situationally better one when you become purplebino. There are rarely moments where you would pick a race's magatsuhi skill over party-wide guaranteed critical hits or repeating the nahobino's action four times. Same goes for the new demon exclusive magatsuhi skills, I didn't even use them to try them out, because they don't even sound good on paper. The non-nahobino magatsuhi skills just end up as glorified signature skills, they just do stuff that you can already do but at a slightly elevated level, while consuming the resource you could've used for crits.Other parts of the gameplay are also extremely strong and especially fun, like the progression. With the amount of gospels, incenses and more that drop it is clear that the developers really want to make the player feel powerful. This game really makes you feel like a nahobino. While the other games in the series mostly just make you fell like some dude, sure you're still super powerful and reshaping the world, but the demi-fiend is just a guy in shorts, and the other 3 protagonists are guys wearing cosplay. But I must admit the long hair on bluehobino looks pretty ugly in game, purplebino is way cooler.And while the exploring is fun and rewarding, it's not really exploring. You're not really finding anything, more like following maps icons and obviously telegraphed paths. While the rest of the art direction is incredibly strong in this game, all the areas still feel the same, even with the awful Chiyoda replaced with Shinjuku. SMT 1, 2 and 4 truly feel like worlds that are alive, while 3's world feels completely desolate, these games nail what they are going for. But this game feels like some weird in-between of a thought out populated world and a lonely wasteland. You're thrown into an undeveloped world with a bunch of soulless ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, exploring to find loot for you character, not to learn anything. The sidequests rarely do anything to expand on the world. I'm fighting the archangel Michael, why? Because the chaos guy told me to. And then that leads to nothing. All of the "exploring" and side content is fun and leads to amazing gameplay, but it should be used to expand on the world and tell stories that go further than dealing with two demon's holding a grudge.The vengeance plot I know this review was mostly critical, but this is still one of the best games I have ever played. All the pros listed in other reviews massively outweigh the cons.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is for people who want the power-fantasy of reaching higher and higher power-levels while building up a team of critters. In other words, a pokemon-style RPG-experience with a better battle-system. (Not unusual for a switch-port). It also has one of the worst stories I've seen in a game in years. The strength of the gameplay is in it's semi-open world-exploration. Instead of dungeon-crawling, per-se, the game gives you huge open levels that are just large enough to explore. The design of the environments is pretty unique, although your movement- and interaction-options are kind of limited. The most of what you'll be doing is looking for collectables, items and gimmick-encounters. If you've played an open-world game in the last decade or so, it will feel pretty familiar. The game is also largely story-driven, and its writing is embarrassingly awful. The other reviews have claimed that the new "Vengeance"-storyline puts more emphasis on the story, but that doesn't mean that they actually put in enough effort to make the story compelling. The basic problem is, just that the game doesn't do a good job of communicating anything with it's writing, whether it's characters, themes or the story-events. Characters aren't introduced properly, they don't act like people, the plot is way too slow to set up proper stakes, and the game constantly makes awful decisions on how it should set up events. It feels exactly as if every scene was created off the first draft, only to communicate the rough outline of what it's supposed to tell the player at that moment. That's why it's baffling that this is their second run through of it. For the main story, this script could have been disappointing in the PS1-era.So, a large part of this experience is kind of embarrassingly bad, especially for a major release. If you only play it for the combat, teambuilding, and the demons, the game can be fun enough to hold your attention. If you go in expecting a masterpiece, you'll be dissapointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is generally amazing with some minor nitpicks, like the new dungeon still being kinda meh. Otherwise i loved every second I spend killing various gods and demons.The new story for Vengeance is a big step up from the original SMT V's story, although it still has some of the same issues. Dazai's "development" hasn't gotten much better, Yuzuru also pretty much stays the same and Miyazu... well at least she has a bit more dialouge. In contrast Tao, Aogami, Yakumo and Koshimizu's characters are very much expanded upon in Vengeance along with Yoko being mostly well written imo. To my surprise she did not feel shoehorned in whatsoever and had a nice dynamic with Tao most of the time. It's not on the same level as SMT IV or Strange Journey when it comes to characters or story, but It's still pretty good.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big sucker for this franchise, and not having a switch to play the original on made me hyped beyond belief to finally get my hands on the game, especially when it came with new and revamped content at the same time. I'm still critical of some things, or when it comes to Atlus in general.-One of he biggest selling points of the game was the breaking away from the switch's shackles, finally obtaining the fabled 60 fps mark is a great joy. The Artstyle in itself was great, the designs of the demons themselves are iconic, and the newcomers are also well made (there are exceptions). I wouldn't say the game looks pherentical when it comes to graphical fidelity, there are times when I noticed blurry or low quality textures here and there, the way things just pop in when coming into view, and also the LoD being bad in great distances is also annoying, but obviously not a deal breaker. The presentation is amazing here, varied enviroments, cityscapes, and mystical areas beyond human comprehension are all great and give a nice flair to it all. Character designs is also spot on, everyone looks great like the aforementioned demons. Also, when the budget is low (for like quests and whatnot) it can be yakuza substory levels of goofy low quality cutscene moments. When given the chance to choose between high graphical fidelity and artstyle, I always choose artstyle, so it gets an 8.-Nothing to be said, the original was amazing and this one delivers the same rate of quality, Atlus never misses when it comes to doing unorthodox osts, having lots of alien droning, ethereal themes, bunch of metal/thrash music to offset it, and so on.-Now this is the meat and potatoes of this franchise, even if the stories bang the gameplay carries the experience, and I have to say, they made this as addictive as the rest of the franchise so it passes. Other than a few balancing issues, pacing and other formalities that are easily messed up, it's fun as hell, from collecting demons, fusing them, using apotheosis to fine-tune your build and so much more, it really is fun. My main issue comes with the exploration, it's not that it's bad per say, but it gets old, and sometimes that makes it a chore. The essences can be a hassle to grind for, so can finding Mitamas and the Miiman, and glory and a lot more. Also the dungeons are complete ass: a series this well known for their ball-busting dungeons having this low quality experiences is just debilitating (heh), honestly those might just be the worse parts of the game. Also no puzzles, basically none at all, again this is just bad because of how infamous some of those used to be . Side quests are fun, sometimes kinda useless, but there are enough incentives to do them. Demon Haunts are genuinely one of the best additions into megaten, hope to see this feature back in the future. Basically: the gameplay is fun, the exploration and other gameplay loops are kinda underbaked.-This game is fun, addicting and sometimes thought provoking, which balances out some of the shortcomings of the story and the pacing. I would recommend this game if you like jrpgs or megaten, but wouldn't recommend if you don't enjoy this genre at all, or are new into it, it's not as hard as is said by others, but it can be ball-busting at times. Also the price is ass, but the game is good so it stays.Now here are some ramblings of a man who played way too many games from this series:

_childDocuments_.review: The short version of this review is simple: If you love JRPGs, experimental soundtracks and think religious themes are interesting, buy this game. SMTV Vengeance (VV) is the definitive version of SMTV, improved in pretty much every way over the original. There are some problems with the story, but the gameplay is top notch, and this is a wonderful starting point for anyone to get into SMT. For a more in depth review continue reading. Slight spoilers ahead, but I tried to avoid anything major. MegaTen has been known as the experimental and more adult branch in the trinity of JRPGs, with usually more mature story telling and radically different gameplay than either DQ or FF. That is not to say any of the series' are bad, just that the audience is not the same. Good portions of SMT is aimed at either teenagers or young adults, and in this game this is no exception. Sacred prostitution, giant penis demons, characters getting murdered, hypocrisy of those in power, and power structures crumbling are standard fair in VV. VV contains massive references to various foundational myths, and before you play the game, I would recommend you are at least familiar with the stories of Amaterasu, Susanoo, Tsukuyomi (and the history of these deities and how they have changed). The slaying of Yamata-no-orochi, and where Murakumo/Kusanagi have come from are important as well. On the Judeo-Christian side, reading the first few chapters of Genesis will help immensely. So will Exodus, Nehemiah, Hosea, Job and 1 Kings. Furthermore, Paradise Lost and William Blake's woodcuts are helpful. Enuma Elish is a core part of the Canon of Vengeance and I'd recommend reading at least the first half of it. Familiarity with various bull cults, the Egyptian pantheon (especially Amun/Ammon), and the various horned serpents in Native American religions are also important. Some of these I picked up only after a playthrough or two, and the more I learned the more I appreciated. The game is a sequel to SMT III: Nocturne. Though if it is a spiritual sequel or a direct sequel is unknown. I would argue that it is a direct sequel, but there are some lines that suggest otherwise; though with the problems I have noticed in the translation, the intent might have been more ambiguous, or possibly only the Canon of Vengeance is the direct sequel. Either way, the game is filled with a myriad of easter eggs and characters, and you even get to talk to *THE* Lucifer from Nocturne. The battle system is the standard pressturn system, just refined. Battles are symmetric, and the bosses have the same limitations the player does (for the most part). Pressturn is better experienced than talked about, so I recommend looking up gameplay to really understand the system. The majority of the gameplay consists of experimenting and mastering the system. To truly explain pressturn fully would be to spoil the game in its entirety, though for those who have played other games with pressturn you will be pleasantly surprised at the new additions. Magatsuhi skills are one such additions that radically change the system, and they are some of the most varied and powerful skills in the game. They range from buffing everyone to max, to reducing all damage by 90%, to making every hit a critical (including magic), inflicting specific ailments, curing all ailments, and causing massive damage (AOE and ST). These charge up every few turns, and builds are regularly centered around these skills.The rest of the game you are running around an open world, doing sidequests and exploring the various areas. Exploration is regularly rewarded with different forms of currency, shortcuts or essences to customize the MC or your demons. Collecting demons, fusing them, building them, and preparing for the next boss is the vast majority of the game. This is so integral to the game that if you don't like it, you won't like the game. The music is top notch, and if you have played any SMT game before you know the quality of the music. Some sidequests have their own themes, and most major battles have their own themes. Leitmotifs and their use are common, with even a few being important to certain roles in the story. To get a general feel of the soundtrack, listen to a few songs listed below:Battle -primordial goddess-Battle -destruction-Battle -dancing crazy murder-Battle -the adversary- Battle -Beelzebub-Battle -Qadištu- Da'at: shinjuku 3rd block Da'at: uenoFinally we come to the main story. You have two campaigns for the story, one is called the Canon of Creation (CoC), the other the Canon of Vengeance (CoV). Choosing between these two is literally the first thing you do in the game, this is before you even set your name. I'd recommend to start with the Canon of Vengeance, though to truly understand the story you need to play through both campaigns. Both have information that helps the other, and both are needed to understand various roles they serve. There are a total of six endings, with two being in CoV, and four in CoC. Personally my favorite boss wise was CoV Law, but CoV Chaos is my "true ending". This leads to the biggest negative in my opinion. To open up all VR training missions, you have to play through every ending at least once, on the same save, resulting in playing through it in totality six times. Unless you are going for all achievements, don’t bother. Most of the differences in the ending is a 2 minute cutscene and the shuffling of boss order. The story is layered with so much symbolism I doubt anyone will be able to discover all of it within the next 10 years. This might be the game with the most levels of symbolism, motifs and themes ever created, and I don't say that lightly. Most people on the english speaking internet do not understand or discuss these themes, so discussion is centered instead around the execution, which at times is fumbled. Significant plot points are ruined because of translation errors, with the most egregious error being when Atsuta tells the MC about Koshimizu significantly earlier than we are supposed to know. Futhermore Dazai, and Tao both have problems in their execution, Dazai didn't have enough build up and Tao is so naive she comes off as stupid. It is best to view them by their role in the story, more than how they are actually portrayed in the story. The law representative in CoC comes off unhinged, and acts chaotic. The chaos rep acts cool and collected, the neutral rep, which is meant to be the middle ground, is the most proactive person in the story and is by far the most extreme. This is to show how God’s order and the natural state of things is in flux. To contrast this, in CoV Yoko regularly has her heart in the right place, but her ideals and execution seem a little extreme, and Tao barely pushes back against them; however as the story continues Tao's conviction is stronger and Yoko starts to waiver, softening significantly overtime. This is a natural development and all of this comes to a head during the final confrontation with the Qadištu. Why Yoko and Tao act the way they do is further elaborated upon at the end of the game, and I find the explanation perfectly satisfactory, but this is of secondary importance to the symbolism.Most symbolism seems to serve the underlying exploration of the Chaoskampf. It is easy to state who the various characters are, and what they represent, but I have never seen any piece of media do what VV has done. They took the Japanese Chaoskampf, and the one from Paradise Lost and put them together, with the serpent being the overlap between the two. A fusion not unlike the Nahobino. Unfortunately the story at times gets bogged down with highschool drama. Execution at times sucks, but I can understand what they are going for, and given the troubles they had during development, I am hopeful for the next iteration. Too bad that will probably take another ten years. Overall, enjoy the themes, ignore the teenage drama.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're new to Shin Megami Tensei, then basically it's a turn-based JRPG series with some dungeon crawler elements about demons, deities and humans fighting each other in post-apocalyptic Tokyo while you, a silent protagonist, use your devil summoner program to collect and even fuse them, just like in Pokemon, except all the demons and deities are based on real-life mythology (MegaTen was created way before Pokemon, however). If you're familiar with SMT series then you know what to expect. This version in particular is an enchanced re-release of SMT:V that previously was released exclusively for Nintendo Switch in 2021. It adds a new storyline while and many QOL features in general, so it's the original SMT:V with even more additional content (before Atlus did separate releases of original and enchanced editions of their games).As it's been mentioned, this game series is about collecting and fusing demons and deities, you can upgrade them and make them learn new skills, and there is ton of demons and deities in SMTV:Vengeance, "catching them all" alone can consume you for hundreds of hours, Demonic Compendium has everything you really need to help you (an archive of every demon fused, evolved, and recruited throughout the game). You recruit your demons through negotiations mechanics that can be very unpredictable and quite funny. You fight other demons and deities with your team of your own that you encounter in an open world-like dungeons, the game uses unique press-turn battle mechanics that force you to strategize your battles, especially with bosses (there are weaknesses, critical hits that gives you or your enemy an additional turn, you and your enemies can miss, repel or drain particular skills that may result in turn loss). You and your party can level up and as a result can learn new skills or gain more stat points, you can also collect, consume, buy and sell various items. Unlike previous entries, SMTV:Vengeance has a lot of QOL features on top of polished gameplay that's based on SMTIV:Apocalypse that was released exclusively for Nintendo 3DS, though in general the game itself is heavily inspired by SMT:III Nocturne Maniax (hence Atlus ). Gameplay and Demonic Compendium are the strongest points of this game and are nearly perfect among other games in the mainline series and especially among spin-offs (looking at you, Persona games).SMTV:Vengeance has two storylines, "Canon of Creation" and "Canon of Vengeance" with the former being original game storyline and the latter came with Vengeance edition. Many say that the story is weak in this game, however, to fully experience it you shoud do as many quests as possible and always talk to habitants of Tokyo because this time around the devs wanted to focus on the game world. The main plot isn't as strong as in SMT:I, II and IV as a result, I guess. Alignment mechanic was watered-down as well compared to SMT:IV. Still, you can also read lore of all the demons in the game. In this game you play as your typical Japanese high school student that ends up in apocalyptic Tokyo and becomes a god-like creature called nahobino.Now, one of the biggest reasons why many people didn't like this game as much is due to the fact that it was released, as I mentioned before, on Nintendo Switch that impacted game's performance in a negative way. The game experienced constant FPS drops and didn't look great either despite being an exclusive title for the platform. However, with Vengeance release we've finally got the definitive version of SMT:V. Not only the game looks gorgeous it's also very optimized (despite having Denuvo) and very mod friendly (the game was made with Unreal Engine 4 after all). There is a native support for Sony controllers with Dualshock 4 and Dualsense buttons (however, they ruined native support for DS at least with the latest patch, use Steam settings until they fix it) and there are plenty of settings you can fiddle with (there is higher than 60 FPS support, 4k resolution support, FOV settings), although they could add more PC-related settings (especially AA-related settings, but people fixed that problem with mods). Atlus also released a pretty good and big update that added a new demon and new navigators (the demons that follow the protagonist around and discover search points that contains items or can lead to the enemy battles). Hopefully they'll give us more content in the future, DLC included, because it seems Vengeance re-release was a big success because, well, it's a great game and one of a few great modern high budget video games.SMT:V Vengeance is one of the best modern JRPGs and maybe even one of the best video games released in general despite some of its flaws, it's a game that people bought their Nintendo Switch for, and now it's finally available on PC. Even older or weak hardware can run it with no issues, it's extremely rare that something like this happens nowadays. Not only that, it's a great game because it's actually a video game not some kind of a movie or a walking sim, it has very deep gameplay, it has quite rich lore and good story, it has great atmosphere and it will consume you for hunded of hours (despite performance issues I replayed the game on Switch countless times). It's worth it even for its price with no discount, SMT:VV is simply a must-have for the people who love video games, if you will.P.S.: Atlus, please bring us SMT:IV and Apocalypse, better even if you also give us enchanced (or PS1 versions) SMT:I and II re-releases as well. We need all mainline games on PC .
