_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: Played through the original on Switch, this is a definitive version with proper frame rate and fast paced battles.  You can tell in certain cutscenes where they're reusing their Switch assets (cutscenes primarily) but everything is sharper, faster and cleaner. Plus a whole other route to give anyone an excuse to jump in.
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: After finding IV, IV:A, and the original release of V to all be pretty alright but not stellar, I kinda figured that the mainline SMT games wouldn't come close to the heights of Nocturne again, and Vengeance proved me wrong. I do wish that there were some more formal dungeon zones instead of just the Da'at regions and the two (3 in Canon of Vengeance) actual (but very simple) dungeons, but this is the tightest that the SMT gameplay formula has ever been.
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: It's like Persona 5 but without the social/romance sim. The game is probably like 90% combat/action and 10% everything else, so if you enjoyed Persona 5 but wished you could stay in the palaces for longer or do more of them, this is your game. This game also focuses way more on the demons themselves, giving them more lore through unique dialogue with each demon as well as some demons even having their own questlines. The story itself is entirely based on the demons and mythology in general, and if you're familiar with any mythology you'll find yourself recognizing a lot of figures either by appearance or by name. Regardless this is a phenomenal JRPG that I really enjoyed my time with. The character/demon designs are fantastic, the music beats out Persona 5 in my opinion, with Persona 5 having a more jazz-focused soundtrack, whereas SMT V has a more ambient, atmospheric, and even futuristic sounding soundtrack with bits of EDM and rock sprinkled throughout some tracks. 100% recommend if you enjoyed the Persona series or even just enjoy JRPGs in general.
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: With Vengeance, it feels like Atlus has finally been able to make the version of the game that they wanted to make. On top of the basic improvements of finally running on hardware that works and showcases the gorgeous art direction, there's countless quality of life improvements and additions to the gameplay. Demons now have innate abilities that can greatly change the dynamic of your team, and you can even have chats with the little buggers! I didn't finish the original story, so I am going through that first, but I am excited to see how the new story works as a response to what people feel didn't work about the first iteration. All in all, this is a fantastic update to a game that makes it as wonderful as it deserved to be, and I would highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: This remaster/port of Shin Megami Tensei 5 is great. I played the original SMT 5 in 2021 on the Nintendo Switch, and I felt like it was hugely compromised by the console it was exclusive to, but now we're in 2024 with a PC port of the game and it's absolutely incredible. Extremely good graphics which are a massive upgrade from the Switch, high framerates which is another massive upgrade from the Switch, and an entire 2nd campaign as a bonus. Possibly the best JRPG I've played in a while
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely don't recommend for players who've played the original on switch already. I'm an avid gamer but rarely have felt this absolutely miserable playing a game.Accidentally saved over my save file before the final choice of the game in the COC route and even though I had completed all of the pre requisite quests for true ending I couldn't get it because my party was full after completing the Fionn quest so he didn't get added to my party or compendium.This alongside unskipable dialogue sequences that take too long (especially reading them for the 6th time), having random unclear quest completion requirements, nerfing iduns healing and the damage scaling making endgame Tama farming more time consuming, absolute terrible level design and a mediocre plot for a massive pricetag.The new content could have been DLC, not a full AAA price for a AA game that I've already played + payed full price for.
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: They fixed pretty much everything I have criticized about the game when it was on switch, Including map layouts, Story, And so much more, This game is way better now, Its an amaaaaziing game, Atlus always impresses Not to mention runs sooo freaking smooth compared to on switch, Its just perfection, Playing vengeance as someone who had beaten the game on switch, Blows my mind, So much had been change, This is an entirely different game than smt v on switch, To the point that got delisted. So give this game a shot, This game is amazing, And so much soul had been put onto it.Unrelated but uhh, Play metaphor refantazio once it releases on october 11, And Hopefully one day atlus remakes smt IV along with IVA.Yeah amazing game, What else can say, Shin megami tensei is one of the biggest and most greatest jrpg franchise out there, And I can't express it enough, Give it a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original release of Shin Megami Tensei V back in 2021 and I really enjoyed it. My favorite aspect was the challenging turn based combat, but I thought the story felt unfinished. I also found it annoying that the game would frequently dip below its 30 FPS framerate target, even in menus.Fortunately, Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance fixes my two biggest criticisms of the game. The new Canon of Vengeance storyline gives some much needed focus on characters that were got very little attention in the original storyline (called Canon of Creation in this version) and generally feels more complete. It does retread a lot of old ground from the original story up until the halfway point, but it's different enough to justify playing this version if you've played the original.Playing this on PC is far in away a better experience than playing the original was on the Switch. While it's still very clearly looks like a Switch game, it runs at a consistent 60 FPS.
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: 30 hours in so my thoughts cant accurately represent the game past the first two main areas, however, I personally think if the original SMTV was an 80/100 this would be a 95/100 based on my current experience, things like new negotiation options kept me on my toes, unique side quests, being able to actually interact with your friends and demons is a game changer, and a story that I can actually be engaged with too?? Amazing. The only gripe I have is that I wish your friends actually had more interaction with each other on screen maybe through use of the Demon Haunts?
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: I played the vanilla version on the switch and it is an amazing combat experience. It is challenging but enjoyable when you get the right demons and learn the new weakness mechanics. Bosses are challenging and you have to prepare and set a good plan when you face them in the lower levels. After you get powerful demons it's not that punishing.Graphics are pretty and they even added new details for most of the demons. The story is not its best selling point but if you love fighting bosses and collecting/fusion demons you will have a lot of fun.This is my third run playing the vanilla story and I am discovering the new stuff as I go. So many quality of life improvements. If you already played this on the switch you wont be disappointed getting Vengeance.
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10SMTV:V has the best combat (imo) in the series so far and probably the best combat I've ever played in an RPG. RPGs are often valued based on the freedom they afford the player, whether that be influencing the plot or the effectiveness of open exploration. SMTV has elements of both, but the true masterclass aspect is the insane level of player choice involved in every single combat encounter.I'll update this review with thoughts on plot after I finish the game but at 63 hours this game is unbelievably goated and definite GOTY material. I'm about halfway thru the game's new storyline and so far it's a tremendous improvement over base SMTV storyline.P.S. the soundtrack kicks ass
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the best gameplay Megaten has to offer with a new story that is pretty good. Includes the original route too as well in case you want to play through it. And to be honest, both are different enough story wise to warrant at least two play throughs. Each canon also has its own exclusive zone, dungeon, bosses, and super bosses. All and all I say its well worth it
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe how much better than the original Vengeance is, and I loved the original. OG SMTV brought me into SMT from persona and its been great. This game is just better in every way from the original release, more demons, more gameplay systems, a whole other story that is completely different from the start, a whole other soundtrack. Doesn't get much better than this.
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: Having played the original release on Switch, this is truly a wonderful experience. Performance is top notch, though it doesn't run in 16:10 even with scaling set on steam deck. All of the original dlc such as Mephisto and Cleopatra are included in the base purchase. Highly recommend if you enjoy any dark rpgs, japanese or otherwise.
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: The Shin Megami Tensei series is so brilliant in regards to the combat system and exploration, as well as its completionist side. Although I played but never finished the original release of SMTV, this rerelease far surpasses it. I love these games and wish Atlus would remaster/remake the DS/3DS games for modern platforms as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: First time Atlus player, picked Hard, I recommend others do the same. I really like how this game makes me actually think, plan, strategize. I feel a great joy, my brain buzzing in a game which is a glorified statistics sheet.You will die, but there's always a way forward. This is the greatest RPG system I have yet experienced.I can also assemble a harem of demon babes and then set them aside for little goober gremlims, hee-hello!
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolute upgrade over vanilla SMT V back on the Switch in 2021. Pretty much all the gripes I had with the game have been fixed in this new version such as the story, and some minor adjustments to the turn based combat system and not to mention the improved frame rate and resolution make the game look it's best on the new hardware. The new stuff is really good, everyone got more screen time and development story wise and I really liked Yoko's inclusion. She feels like she should have been there all along, the new foes are a welcome addition as well without going into spoilers. The new music is going to go down in megaten history as some of the best in the series, like I'm serious. Overall had a blast while getting my teeth kicked in by the games difficulty, but I never gave up and kept trying which is something I wish more games would do or achieve for people, if you like turn based JRPG's this is a must play IMO and I would recommend it to anyone who is interested in giving it a shot. Atlus cooked once again
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: What pokemon wishes it was. No, it's more than that. This game is a whole other beast, it stands alone on a pristine mountaintop in all shining glory while pokemon wallows in it's own excrement in a fetid swamp.The depth of monster collection and customization is already extremely apparent only a few hours in. You also get to customize and battle with your own main character along with four of your favorite monsters. From picking your abilities to the coolness factor, I see myself playing this game for dozens perhaps more than a hundred hours more. I simply cannot recommend this game more. Get it at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. If you are expecting a game exactly like Persona, this isn't it. Sure it is another JRPG with similar enemies and a turn based combat system, but they are very different games. Persona focuses very heavily on story and characters, this game is much less story focused and more combat and environment focused. However I have been extremely pleasantly surprised at the depth of the characters and story.The difficulty is harder than Persona. The combat flows dofferently, where press turns are stocked rather than an lmmediate bonus. There are no all out attacks or knockdown. It feels a bit more tactical and a bit less flashy.The art and music are amazing 10/10 enemies 10/10 music 8/10 environmental graphicsThis looks oozing with style in 4k/60fps, absolute night and day from the Switch experience that lost so much of the presentation.Even early game story feels better.Highly recommended, as long as that all sounds good to you.I want to be pissed about Denuvo and a re release at full price but the game is too good to pass up. Definitely has the production values of a Persona game.
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: A strong turn-based JRPG. The world is fascinating, eerie, and gorgeous. Mechanics are pretty standard fare for the genre with a few fun twists to keep it interesting. The story is a bit lacking so far. There's a lot more premise than plot. The premise is great, but the main character seems to be more of an observer to what happens than a participant.
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: While some new story changes definitely make the plot more interesting, it also for some reason includes most of the plot points from the og smt v that have no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ business being there, other then just to make the game 40hrs long. Some things literally take place behind the scenes, and I guess players are kinda expected to have already played the og plot to know what the ♥♥♥♥ actually happened there. Whats worse, the last 1/4 of the game is pretty much the same as the original, and there's maybe like 1 hour of new main story content, and when that new content ends, the game immediately returns to the ending of the base game. _childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: It's peak! Play Canon of Vengeance first and don't worry about which ending you get (they are both great). This game makes replays in new game plus very fun so getting every ending, unlocking every demon fusion, and fighting every boss (which many you can't fight until new game plus or ng++) is very very very very fun
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: A very substantial upgrade from the original. Most of its contentious issues are more or less solved, or at the very least mitigated significantly. The characters and story hold far more water than they ever did even if they aren't perfect. Simply just giving the characters screentime made me care a lot more about them than in the original where you hardly got to see much of them. Plus the horrible level scaling garbage that was in the original is entirely gone. Not only this, but there are so many new side quests and demons at times it feels like a totally different game. And in some ways, it kind of is. Especially when there's an entirely new story with multiple new areas while not invalidating the original story. It's not exactly perfect, like the endgame meta is the exact same as the original which is quite boring, and the "Protagonist death = game over" still sucks, but I have been playing these games for a long time that I am just used to the new SMT games having this feature. Doesn't mean I like it, though. All in all, though, I think that this is an amazing experience and only reinforces my opinion of the Shin Megami Tensei series being some of the best modern RPG experiences you can have.
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favourite JRPGS brought to modern platforms with tons of QOL Improvements, Finally free from 20FPS hell, If you want a JRPG with the super engaging, difficult but FAIR combat this is the game for you, The exploration is unmatched and you feel like your team is constantly getting stronger and stronger, its a addicting gameloop, I cant say much for the story content (as I'm only 15 hours in) but with two different campaigns theres so much game here, I already thought the original SMTV was good enough to be one of my all time favourite games but now with all this added content and improvements its such an easy reccomend
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: Fine apocalyptic action rpg. Gripe for the completionist: to get 100% of the achievements, it is required to weather six virtually identical playthroughs, pretty much only differing in dialogue choices and the occasional boss fight. An option to at least skip the extensive tutorial content would have been nice.
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: I have two saves for this game, one for playing alone whenever I want, and one for playing with my girlfriend whenever we hang out. I have to play through every event twice in the same day because of this. In any other game, I would be miserable. But SMTV:V is so amazing that I'm honestly excited to play through every section for a second time. It's that good. The original SMTV was already a near masterpiece with a few sizable blemishes that kept it from its full potential, but the changes in Vengeance have fixed all my issues and more, to the point that I can't bring myself to go back to the original anymore. 10/10. Congrats, Atlus, you knocked it out of the park.
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: After playing every Pokemon game on switch with dlc (yes I still like the Pokemon games despite their abysmal performance), this feels like a breath of fresh air for the creature collector/turn based battler game. Obviously it was on the switch, but now it has so much better performance and runs at 60 on steam deck plus all the extra DLC (Mitama ones making the game so much easier fyi). It isn't exactly the same gameplay as Pokemon, but similar in the fact of turn based moves with weaknesses and collecting (through fusions) creatures. Think of this as a more hardcore, darker, demon collecting game with a more mature and complex story and much more mature creatures to collect, as some would say adult pokemon. Plus there is no need to worry about min/maxing the base stats with IV breeding as the fusion system you can manipulate the stats to be the most beneficial for you build. Overall, I would recommend this game as I have had lots of fun playing it with a extremely high difficulty compared to pokemon which I wipe the floor with every trainer and gym leader (besides Cynthia in bdsp and surprisingly the last Kiernan fight in the dlc), and the fact there is a whole system about creating demons by combining your old ones, feels really in depth so far and can't wait to get to end game builds.I also know this is related to the persona franchise but I have only played an hour into persona 4 on the vita so I am not really familiar so I cannot comment based on that. I have heard less social stuff and more of a hardcore dungeon crawling experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: Long time Megaten/Persona fan. Mixed feeling about the game, but ultimately, I do not recommend. I did not play the Switch version.Runs lovely on the deck, game looks great. The core combat/demon mechanics not only feel good, they might be my favourite implementation of the Megaten formula. Freeform ability to set which skills migrate to a new fusion can be too powerful, but is tempered by affinities that make fire persona deal more damage with fire spells and less with ice. Japanese voices are excellent as expected, though can only be changed from the title, not in game. Great sense of mystery, world building so far.Look, let's be real, this is a pay to win mess. Enemies appear in the world and engaging them is mostly a waste of time, aside from demon negotiations. Enemies drop almost zero exp/macca. Except wait, there are mitama spawns in the world, which grant HUGE bonuses in comparison. Kushi mitama drop a book that guarantees levelling up the main character, and saki mitama drop thousands of macca. I hit the first boss ~ten levels higher than I should have been, and could probably hit max level before the first boss in a few hours if I tried (unless there's a balance mechanic). So ordinary mobs have been made useless and you farm mitama instead. And the DLC causes mitama to spawn every 2-3 demon packs. There is no gameplay sense from previous Megaten titles of slowly building up from weakness to strength in a harsh world. This is a very temporary thing, but cool, I see you have a lot of game systems SMTVV, but ripping control away from me a dozen times or more in the first area to explain one to me is getting annoying. I know this will go away so it's only a temporary thing, but let me explore more naturally in my own way. Unlike SMT3 (or even Eiyuden which I just came off), combat feels quite floaty. Physical attacks don't feel like they connect, there's poor feedback. This seems a bit better with spells. Other feedback in combat is a little off - multi hit abilities aren't super clear which damage is going to what mob etc, though this is a minor annoyance only.Look, it's a theme park. Without difficulty there's no strategy, and it's trivial to power game anything here. A great combat system rendered mostly redundant by P2W.Jump in, go kill god, have a blast. Could have been a visual novel.
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: I have just completed one of the two stories in SMT5.  This game is beyond compare.  I have not completed a single player game in years, nor a JRPG in decades, and this game is great enough to bring me back to the genre.amazing, just amazing.  two complete storylines, 6 endings, 200+ demons, all dripping with soul.  get this game.  you will not regret it, and it will not stay unplayed in your library.   get it at full price even, its worth every cent.
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: SMT5 Vengeance perfects the turn-based JRPG formula with its refined press turn system. The game runs super smoothly on PC, with Switch graphics scaling beautifully and the art direction holding up fantastically. Plus, the soundtrack is top-notch, continuing the series' tradition of excellence. A must-play!
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: I played SMT 5 back when it came out on switch a few years ago and while i enjoyed it, it didn't grab me as much as the older games did. Part of it I felt was because some of the characters got underdeveloped which i found out happened because of some really rough development. For instance the new character Yoko was supposed to be in the base game but they couldn't fit her in the game in time.This release on the other hand felt like they finally got the story they wanted to tell. The vengeance story is up there with one of my favourite Megaten stories and it gives context for the cannon of creation plot that was really needed. They put a ton of work into visual imagery and symbolism too which I was really absorbed into and the game play adjustments are so good its some of the best game play in the series.Genuinely love this game here's hoping Atlus ports SMT 4 and other 3ds games to PC
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: Already finished the original game on the switch way back before this version was even announced. It's a great game, it has excellent battles and music. The new music is really great. The original story is severely lacking and you can tell that it's a rushed product with content cut out to try and get as much of the narrative to work as possible. This version has more maps and more content, more demons, more gameplay features, and an update story that adds a lot more life to the game which it was lacking before. I don't jive with the game starting you at level 3 as opposed to level 1 like the original game, while also still keeping your introductory stats all at 5. It's so weird to me to start out in an SMT game of all games at level 3, especially a mainline game. This version feels easier than the original in some way I am not sure exactly how though. Disregarding mitama which I didn't even have the DLC on the original game until I got to the endgame. Mitama are negligible anyway and you don't have to use the items they drop. Nor do you have to keep their appearance cranked up. Anyway it's a good game. Turn based rpgs are some of my favorite games when the battle system is done in an excellent way like the press turn system. Something that actually rewards and punishes you for using it correctly or making mistakes or even just having the enemy dodge you is great. Plus having the enemy be able to do all the same things is good, I dislike when you're the only one that has access to the mechanics of the battle system. It would also be broken if only you had access to the things this battle system provides you.
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: One of the better collect-em-all's out there with adult themes. No longer bound to the Switch with atrocious frame rates.  Vengeance is similar to the Royal treatment that Persona 5 recieved, with the addition of new story, new sidequests, and several really great QoL features. With a variety of difficulty levels, you'll never feel frustrated while figuring out exactly what this game is, and how to maximize it's systems.  I highly recommend starting with the Canon of Vengeance story as the new human characters significantly reduce some of the initial difficulty (that's not to say some of the new boss's throw some surprises). Every new addition is brilliant, the new "haunt" system adds a tiny dose of socializing, and provides some interesting opportunities to enhance demons you enjoy the company of, and your main character sees a LOT of additional stat points to burn.Also the MItami DLCs? Enable/disable as needed, the enhanced appearance rate can be pretty spammy, but it's great when you want to quickly stack up some glory/cash/grimoires when you need them, and you can disable it to reduce the appearance rate when you don't.
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever played Persona and thought to yourself, man, I wish I could play the dang game and not have to do a million social links just to progress the story at a snail's pace? Have you ever wondered what it is like if every slot on the team can be entirely customized with affinities and movesets? Have you ever wondered what it would be like to be in a post-apocalyptic nightmare of mythological proportions? Then Shin Megami Tensei V Vengeance is your answer! Don't even bother playing other games, this will keep you plenty hooked with all the new changes which make this game even feel like a deck-builder at times. You can make teams designed around cheese strategies and actually be rewarded for it. You can build your own character however you want too. The sky's the limit when it comes to team synergies and strategies so go crazy if you'd like. Overall, just have fun with it, and remake or destroy the world.
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: Great music, fun combat, interesting story and amazing art. I don't know what's not to like. Don't go into this thinking it's The Witcher 3 with a huge open world with in depth dialogue and branching side quests, that's not the aim of the game.  It's not Persona either, god is dead, the world is over, you don't have time for friends. You won't win every fight on the first try, know your enemy, its strengths and its weaknesses, and forge your character and your team accordingly. Once you understand that this game is about strategizing and not grinding for hours until you're overleveled, you'll have much more fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

I didnt touch it again on switch for years, was worth waiting. Can still tell its a switch port from the backgrounds sometimes but overall it looks way better but the performance is so much better. _childDocuments_.review: Bought this game originally on switch and don't think I've ever been more disappointed in a release I was so excited for. I had even bought the Collectors Edition. I ended up selling it off because it looked like ♥♥♥♥ and played like ♥♥♥♥ on the switch. Reluctantly I bought this again on Steam and it is like an entirely new game. _childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: First, the good stuff: smt5 had very nice combat already, and with the Vengeance update we get more demons, more events, more bosses. The new story path has much much better writing, and you actually get human companions like in the older games. Also, a whole new area to explore with the accompanying dungeon. Of course, you still get fantastic areas to explore, great soundtrack (Ueno❤️), gorgeous demon models (which you can hang out with, with optional photo sessions).Now the not-so-great stuff. You still have three out of four areas from the original story line (albeit with some tweaks and route-specific events/quests). To complete the game, you'll have to do six full playthroughs from start to finish (one normal for each path, and four story critical paths). Unfortunately, there's not much new content on the last four runs, so it's a drag. ALSO, out of 3/5 hours (depending on the route) you'll spend  half an hour each time skipping all the tutorials, item explanations, etc . It really is a death by a thousand paper cuts.Anyway, you'll also have to do partial 7th run for the virtual battle completion. _childDocuments_.review: . Most encounters can ultimately be avoided due to a few exploits, and EXP/macca farming is even more broken now due to a combination of features now present. That seems good in execution logic, but fails in design IMO. If you're intended to explore the entire map looking for items or interactions while battling enemies, but players are looking for a way to avoid most bad engagements then it means they arent gonna pay much attention to exploring other than possibly money grinds.-  this might be as you're entering the 3rd map on both versions. If a player gives up by map 2 i feel like it explains how rough the experience is on Hard and Normal because you don't really do meaningful damage having to heavily rely on block skills or dampners. Its also possible vitality messes with the damage value quite a lot too.-  Where as in the original stories the NPCs truly felt worthless and just side characters that would appear for like 2 seconds before having to get a milk carton at the milk store. Then 30 hours into the experience the actual story kicks in and conveniently it turns out many NPCs went to the same milk store 50 million km away and conveniently shows up to your alignment lock door step theres a clear problem and this is aside from the garbled mess the random demon chats would spew contradicting nearly most points of the plot. Like the father who finally returned with that milk carton, SMT V Vengeance takes an already vaguely interesting premise like dad going out for milk and recreates the milk into a tres leches cake. If you're lactose intolerant or not, well the story is either pretty ok or diarrhea. The story is incredibly corny, borderline shonen manga stuff, and at one time I was like "holy, is that ffxiv reference?" I joked around up until I saw the SMT V Vengeance equivalent of the bahamut super saiyan jesus punch cutscene and i started laughing. I wish it was a joke, unfortunately i am not. While now, finally you feel some sort of attachment to the characters and admittedly a moment or two get an emotional response the original scenes from the original game mesh VERY oddly with the new story elements which recreates the forgettable aspect of the original story just like that joke earlier in the review about the unicorn entering a tesco. To further develop some plot points we have the introduction of Demon Haunts which admittedly introduces some funny dialogues, but rather comes off like a cheap method to put more intermittent dialogue throughout the game between most major plot points. The big flaw with these are dialogue is when the Aogami and Tsukuyomi are expected to speak with you, or speak for you in quests if you hold out on stuff, it messes with the progression aspect for these characters and quests? it seems like a strange complaint but if you just like hold off on some stuff and return to it, you will see some dialogue just seems off or wonk.- . In Atlus defense, this would likely be the next turn for SMT as a series though personally it seems to not work in conjunction with the wonk damage values. Its likely because of these new features, Atlus nerfed old strats and builds and reworked damage overall that was relevant to the original, some builds doing 1/4 or 1/2 of what is normally expected. Likely because you have to put these new features into play. In addition, some new bosses have HP bloat and it does not feel good at all on hard mode. Some of these issues maybe corrected in Godborn a new difficulty that unlocks after meeting certain requirements. This is because godborn axes the incense and grimoire grind at the expense of money grinding now. I enjoy grinding games as much as the next guy I personally like Monhon Dos (Gen 2 overall) and SMT Imagine, but when the only solution to some of the problems is "just beat the superbosses and unlock this harder difficulty dude lmao" by hour 352 I reckon most people simply won't care. But i guess neither does atlus since the alternative is to shell out the dosh, buy the dlc, and cheese the levels and stat crap for those unwilling to deal with tedious grinds. This isn't new though Etrian Odyssey exists.Unfortunately I don't, I just think SMT V as a whole is very bland and I would have preferred they pushed for 6 and hopefully redeem themselves. Honestly, I am one of the idiots willing to buy the game twice simply because I hope Atlus ports SMT 1,2, SJ, and 4 to PC at some point because theyre up there in my most favorite games of all time. That is not including some spinoffs too that I want ported that are pretty great or can use some polishing like Maken X. But all I can really say is, Atlus would likely need to polish some of the design elements in SMT V as whole to give the market an incentive to want and buy the new one. SMT V even in this form feels very confused, and adding complexity to already confused game that isn't sure what it wants to be will only further alienate a market that was at least curious to buying and trying it. Unfortunately, I am unable to recommend it because in its execution its just not very great. Its like pretty ok and thats about it. The music and visuals are pretty much carrying it, and the gameplay + story isn't really that great even now. For people unfamiliar with the series, some of these elements may never bother you, but as a long time edger of sorts this game is like alright.SMT overall is a good series and at least for me nothing really comes close to it, but if I had to say you had money to buy SMT V Vengeance or something else on steam? I would say probably something else. Anyways look forward to Shoji Meguro's new game Guns Undarkness or a weird RPG like Path of The Abyss (its like 7 bucks and I made a guide there, pretty fun game even though its hard). Atlus hopefully you port the other SMT games because idk if ima waste another $120 on SMT 6 and SMT 6 Final Vengeance Royal. Atlus fell Off + Atlus hates money + this game is still pretty mid

_childDocuments_.review: Shin Megami Tensei is so back! ATLUS once again makes me a FOOL for buying the base version of their game only to release the Royal/Imperial/Re-remake/VVengeance version X months later.Big improvement over an already great game in a lot of ways (save anywhere, magatsuhi rails for quicker navigation, sped up auto battle and skill-using auto battle -- and most importantly, fixed the level scaling so that being slightly underleveled isn't necessarily a death sentence), with a second story to play through (much of it is very similar but there are a couple of entirely distinct regions, as well as entirely new endings) and a host of new well-designed demons to summon (and talk to at the new Demon Haunt). Looks great, some great battle and zone themes, fun bossfights, etc. If you like the monster-collecting/press-turn combat/traditional turn-based combat where the enemies play by the same rulebook you do, you can't go wrong with this.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed Nocturne when it first came out, but even that was somewhat bare-bones other than the setting and some mechanics that were new to me at the time.Combat is fun at first, but fails to stay fresh even against late game bosses and dlc. I like having to defend against potential instakills, but far too many enemies are just sponges. You can have all four members of your team hitting weaknesses all fight long and it can still take 10 minutes to down an unimportant unintroduced boss thrown in to pad the game out.The world feels very empty, bland, and somehow the maps feel very small and way to large at the same time. Movement is slow and monotonous. It probably wouldn't have been so bad if I wasn't compelled to do every side quest and collect everything I could in an attempt to find anything compelling. Spoiler alert, there isn't anything compelling or interesting to stumble across. Every bombed out building is just collapsed walls, sand piles, and bare empty flat floors. Every street is filled with sand piles and the same handful of wrecked cars. Honestly, they could have made the world black and white or 2d and would have lost nothing. It becomes apparent very early on that the sand everywhere is just to 'sand' down the rough edges everywhere. Harder see how devoid of interesting designs, props, or anything if sand piles are blocking the view almost everywhere especially early on.The lowest point is the story and the characters. Characters are all one-note and I quickly started skipping dialog whenever possible which isn't something I do in many games. Characters will repeatedly natter on providing nothing new long after a player has already gotten the point they made initially. Most of this isn't voiced, which is fine, but the game will insert random phrases over the text. More often than not it does not fit the text and is just annoying. 'young man' 'young man' 'young man' 'young man' 'young man'.The MC is a blank slate. Some games do this well, this one does not. There are very few dialog choices and almost none of them do anything different. If someone says 'Take my hand', nodding and taking their hand or taking their hand while nodding is *not* a choice. It doesn't help that you could sum up this game's entire story in a single page without being overly reductive. This review is already longer than whatever story board they used. I guess, I'll download the easiest difficulty and plow through the other endings and achievements just so there's never any reason for me to revisit this game. Kudos if you like this game, hard pass from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me tell you something—Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance is straight-up peak gaming. A flawless 10/10, no contest. But before I dive into how epic this game is, I need to call out someone. You know who you are, Gooby.Gooby, you suck at video games, and it’s time the world knew. This guy can’t even beat the first boss in a tutorial, let alone tackle the glorious challenge that is SMTV: Vengeance. And what’s worse? He hates good games like this! I mean, who even does that? _childDocuments_.review: Elevator pitch: a monster collection JRPG with a focus on gameplay challenge over attachments to individual monsters (demons per the local nomenclature). You have great control over you party's characteristics, and the game fully expects you to use it to deal with whatever the bosses throw at you. Recruitment is done through the radical process of destructively fusing together your existing demons or the even more radical process of talking to random encounters instead of fighting them. Aesthetics are unapologetically drawn from mythologies around the world with a sprinkle of creative interpretation (there is a legitimate reason why Mara looks like a penis in a chariot, I swear), the Abrahamic representatives in particular playing the major roles.Downside up front: If you don't want the story to be really bad, take the girl's hand at the start. If you want the story to be really great, this game isn't for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely stellar RPG. I've been binging the new Canon of Vengeance route for the past week and I just cannot put it down. It builds on the original release in awesome ways, while still containing the original unaltered storyline for just a metric ton of content.The turn-based battles are as great as they've ever been, and the amount of customization you have for your team still astounds. Story has gotten a massive upgrade in the COV route as well, in my opinion making the original completely redundant aside from certain demons and skills locked to other route's endings, as well as some additional content for Canon of Creation unlocked through specific actions in a COV playthrough. Characters, being a big criticism of the original, are now far more fleshed out. You see a lot of them throughout them game now, and they even join your team for certain stretches of it, allowing much more engagement between them and the story. Honestly, if you're not a completionist, I'd personally recommend just playing the new route, and at best watching a playthrough of the original to see the neat parallels between the storylines. Knowledge of the original is not at all necessary however.Overall this is an amazing sendup of the original game, and perhaps it's too early to say this only being about 1/2-2/3 of the way through the game, but it definitely feels like a step back in the right direction for the Shin Megami Tensei series after the lackluster original release of V (story-wise, at least).

_childDocuments_.review: Before this, I have played the original release of SMT V. I had fun with it but I wanted a little more interaction when it came to the demons that I had in my party because, unlike the Persona series, my demons are my companions. They're the ones who I have in my party for most of my playthrough. So, imagine my delight when I realised that this version let's you have even more interactivity with them. Aside from that, having another character be involved in the story that adds two more endings and having the original casts be more involved in the main story and side quest fights in order to have them be more proactive within the world was such a welcome change. This version really feels like what the developers wanted it to be from the beginning. On top of that, as of this review, they seem to be updating the amount of over-world demon navigators that will accompany you as well as adding in more demons for you to summon. And all of that FOR FREE. So, yeah. I would definitely recommend this game. P.S. Amanozako is cute.

_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: SMT5 has some of the best game mechanics in the series to date. It's only real problem was the kind of nothing burger story. Luckily, the Vengeance remake has given us a side of fries and a shake to turn this into a proper meal. The story is nothing revolutionary but it is much more entertaining than the original. Having said that, I feel there is a special joy in having played the original Canon of Creation (original game story) and now playing the Canon of Vengeance (new story) in that it is a heck of a feeling when we build up to events that match the original timeline suddenly to swerve into something completely different and unexpected and that "WAIT WHAT!?" moment.If you have the patience to play through the game twice in a row, it can be fun to do Creation first and then Vengeance just to get that reaction. Though Vengeance also adds some freaking tough new bosses (which I love) so new game+ing into it might cheapen having to learn to deal with them stratgetically.Also if it wasn't obvious yet from my tone, the game comes with both the original version (but with updated QoL) called Canon of Creation, and the new story called Canon of Vengeance that you choose which to play through at the start of the game.The game is really fun overall. I enjoy the fact that you can really make any demon feasible for end game play thanks to the ability to use demon essences to transfer over skills. I have a level 99 Cait Sith with no weaknesses, immunity to physical attacks and endgame spells/abilities. XDGame is harder than your average mon game starting out, but as you get used to the logic of the game you can build hideously broken demons to battle with. It's actually funny, if you're new to SMT you're probably going to struggle more with the first boss than the last. But don't worry, there are plenty of challenging bosses to fight with that even with a level 99 optimized team will still put up a real fight. So that's fun.So yeah, game is a ton of fun, with decent challenge without being unfair (except a certain cameo optional super boss) and it huge improvement over the original SMT5. Two paws up!
_childDocuments_.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still not done with my first Vengeance playthrough but I have played through the original Shin Megami Tensei 5 on the Switch and I have to say, Vengeance fixes so many issues with the original that it is almost like a completely different game. Being able to play at a constant 60 FPS with some gorgeous visuals makes this easily the best way to play Shin Megami Tensei 5 and makes for an excellent entry into the series for anyone coming from Persona, or anyone who has never touched SMT or its spin-offs. The only negatives I can think of is that, personally, while the Vengeance storyline has far, far stronger characterization than the Creation (vanilla) storyline, I still feel like it is not the strongest. However, I do not see this as a massive negative because the bread-butter-and-tasty-meat of Shin Megami Tensei has been the gameplay, and Shin Megami Tensei 5 was already pure excellence and Vengeance only made it even better. If you are not a fan of high difficulty there are also options for those wanting an easier, laid-back experience, although I do personally recommend playing on at least Normal so you are inclined to play around the press-turn system.Vengeance comes with the DLCs of the original game which includes the, in my opinion excellent, DLC "Return of the True Demon" which includes a ton of new boss fights (all of which can be fused after defeat) as well as a brand new superboss. Vengeance goes even further to add more on top of this as well. It also comes with the original DLC demons, Artemis and Mephisto, both of which are quite fun to use although Artemis sometimes trivializes the difficulty so be warned. The new DLC demons for Vengeance are also quite good, both of which feeling a bit fan-servicey since both can be seen as coming from previous games in the SMT franchise. They are also quite strong and worth giving a try. Overall, Shin Megami Tensei 5: Vengeance is the de facto way to enjoy Shin Megami Tensei 5 and makes for a perfect intro to the series, whether you are coming from Persona (or other SMT spin-offs) or are just a fan of JRPGs in general. The graphics are gorgeous and it's a real treat to see your favorite demons looking so good, and the soundtrack is absolutely rockin' (especially battle music). The gameplay is fantastic and only got fantastic-er with Vengeance as well. The only possibly negative is that the story is not the greatest, but Vengeance has done a LOT to smooth over and provide greater context that even re-frames a lot from the original story. For those curious, one can play both the original story (Canon of Creation) or the new Vengeance story (Canon of Vengeance) and both have content very unique to each other. For those brand new to Shin Megami Tensei 5, I recommend starting with Canon of Creation, but for those who played SMT 5 on the Switch already I recommend Canon of Vengeance.

_childDocuments_.review: One playthrough for the Canon of Vengeance on Hard difficulty took me around 135 hours. It's the first SMT or Persona game that I've ever finished. I really liked it, but I would like to preface my praise with the biggest negatives first.-The overworld exploration is simple. You have a map, packs of demons, points of interest and a quest marker to navigate towards. The PoIs are worth reaching, finding Mimans, a collectable monster of sorts, is rather necessary for upgrades. Knowing where which monsters are is good for your own power gain. Being able to go straight for a fight that will give you extra passive upgrade options when you are having trouble with fights is good to have. However, it is by no means anything special. I enjoyed it for being a relaxing side activity that I could lazily do to progress.-The overworld zones are all variations of sand and city ruins. The various zones have different color palettes and the smaller dungeons have their own thematic look, but it will make you feel like you are trudging through the same thing for your whole playthrough. -The story is a simple JRPG narrative. You get story cutscenes with relevant characters, you have some smaller dialogues with the denizens of the world, you have smaller discussions between your party that influence the ending you get. As a whole, the game is straight forward in its presentation. -The game can get grindy and repetitive. The meat and potatoes of the game is collecting a team of your own so you can pass a tough fight and move to the next area. If the basic game loop of walking around an overworld to collect demons and items to fight a turn based battle doesn't fundamentally appeal to you, you will not enjoy SMTV.However, I think the positives far outshine the aforementioned negatives.Collecting demons to make a team to your own liking, to counter various enemy strengths feels great. It's not that complex, where you wouldn't be able to figure out how your ideal team composition for a fight should look like. Putting it together still feels like you are clever for figuring out a solution.You have various ways to up your power and alter both the MC and the demons under your control. You can unlock passive abilities that will empower the MC both generally and to be stronger with affinities that you find preferable. Some abilities are generally stronger, or more useful, but even having a sub-optimal set up is good enough for most of the game. Having a cadre of demons that you can mix and match feels nice from an optimization side. You have a lot of options while not being strained to optimize to the utmost just to keep going. Having a compendium of demons unlocked for mixing and matching at higher levels gives you a small dopamine rush when you unlock them, not unlike checking a TO-DO list.The story, while being straightforward, is thematically interesting. The setting is apocalyptical and the discussion is framed around order and chaos. While bits are predictable, it does not feel banal or childish. It has its darker aspects, but its a satisfying to experience. It has some notes that made me think about the fundamental nature of our human experience, and I appreciate it for it.The designs are varied. Between goofy creatures, grotesque monsters, cute fairies, strong looking demons, heavenly angels, handsome men and sexy ladies, you have the option to pick your favorites. I appreciate it all being tied to human mythology and I loved seeing the artists' interpretation of various creatures. Almost everything that you fight or encounter in the game can become a part of your team.The music is great. A few tamer or more boring tracks are in the mix, but most of the songs enhance the weirdness of the world you are in and are generally great to listen to.QRD, if you can stomach the negatives, SMT V Vengeance is a great game that I liked a lot more than I expected I would.

_childDocuments_.review: In short: The original story I felt had tons of potential despite turning out mediocre. If I had to quantify it, there's maybe an added 25% depth for most (not all) of the original characters, with the story feeling aimless after the 2nd area as it did in the original. Vengeance made the confusing choice to focus on the worst re-release characters ATLUS has ever created, while giving sprinkles of characterization to the original cast, before tossing them (and the new characters, for that matter) into the abyss. If you played the original SMTV and wanted to see the potential of the characters fully realized, you never will. If you just want more SMT combat and don't care about the story, then you'll have a good time, though the game is simple and easy.--Mainly writing this for those who played the original. If you are intending to play this and your main interest is in the new story, Canon of Vengeance, heavily temper your expectations. This is not a "definitive version" of SMTV, as what had seemed to be implied when it was announced; rather, it is an abridged version of the same story with quite literally the worst new added characters ATLUS has put into one of their re-releases. Yes, there are human party members for periods of time of Vengeance, and yes, there is more dialogue between them to actually give the game a pulse, but the near complete vanishing of the narrative and meaningful interactions still occurs after the 2nd area as it does in Canon of Creation. I also feel that most of the returning characters are outright shafted and just deemed irrelevant to the story once their ""development"" is rushed through. I don't think there's any intrigue whatsoever in the story of Vengeance, as while there is now a more definable big bad entity, there is legitimately not a single thing interesting about it. I cannot stress enough how bad the new characters are. The Qadistu are F-tier villians with cool designs. They are not interesting whatsoever and it boggles the mind as to why they were decided as the focal point of the game instead of fleshing out the other characters. Every ATLUS re-release has the "new girl", and Yoko is the most unnecessary yet. She serves as a mouthpiece for her alignment and does absolutely nothing for the story, does nothing to justify her existence.  I do not know why she was not instead a completely neutral character to sort of help develop the other existing characters. I respect them for not going the amnesiac route at least.As for combat, it is unchanged as far as I can tell. I do think the next SMT or even Persona 6 desperately needs to evolve this system, if they're going to make it so easy to build whatever you want. You can save everywhere now, so there is essentially no more tension, especially as the game is laughably easy on normal if you are familiar with SMT mechanics.I know some will see this and say "lol go play persona", but if a game has characters that speak and have their own motivations, I'd at least like to care about SOME of them. I did not care about any. I was never moved or swayed by anything they said. Maybe that never was the point? So if you just wanted an excuse to have more of the same combat, well you'll have it, otherwise do not expect much else other than your hopes of a compelling narrative being dashed after the first 1/3 of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I get that a lot of people love this but it wasn't for me.I didn't like the level design. It wasn't in any way immersive or even interesting to traverse. Wandering enemies strewn haphazardly throughout a level with only clear reasoning for a few of them is a very early 2000s design.The quests felt like busywork that you'd find in a terrible open world RPG.Progression was incredibly slow. This game is very grindy. With all of the things holding it back I had no desire to grind. I just wanted to quit.Character design was good = ).Combat was excellent.Difficulty was not good. There are plenty of gacha one-shot enemies due to weaknesses on your main character. Some bosses are easier than regular enemies. It was very much all over the place.Story was ... very bad.. lol... I didn't care about any of the characters. I didn't care about the plot. I just wanted to skip the cutscenes to be honest so that I could get back to running from checkpoint to checkpoint and question why I'm doing any of this.I really don't know why people enjoyed this. It seemed like kind of a jumbled terrible mess to me. Then again I haven't liked an ATLUS game since Disgaea 1. Maybe I don't get it. Maybe I'm very much not the target audience. In any case, to me, this game has very few redeeming qualities.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is for people who have never played the series:Shin Megami Tensai is a hard series to recommend. Persona? Sure, I can recommend that to anyone, but I think most people who play video games in the west will pick up something like SMTV, play it for two seconds, think it's the most nonsensical thing on the planet and give it up. They will be like "Hey, this isn't about high school life and eating hamburgers for stat gains! Also, where is my romance options?!"Imagine, if you will, Persona but instead of a life simulator and cute high school antics, you got a far more difficult dungeon crawler with the most nonsensical mumbo jumbo story about demons trying to blow up Tokyo for the 1000th time that has writing that makes that hobos on the street that scream about the Apocalypse seem far more lucid then the script here. Instead of cute mini-games and romance, you are listening to some old man scream about Tokyo mythology to you while Cleopatra keeps blasting you with charm debuffs. Playing as the titular NAHOBEEHO, you kinda go around and just bully demons over and over until you either save Tokyo or blow it up. If you are looking for a persona style game, skip it. If you want a difficult dungeon crawler (Oddly enough, still easier then 99% of most SMT games) and more stat sperging, pick it up.

_childDocuments_.review: You are playing as a common student in Tokyo who, by happenstance, stumbles into the Netherworld, a ruined version of the city in constant struggle between various factions of angels and demons alike. While being almost killed right in that moment, the protagonist is rescued by Aogami, who fuses with the main character to become the Nahobino, a demi-god with the potential to reshape the world. SMT:V has previously often been criticized for having a fairly weak story, or vice versa, SMT being in general weaker in writing when compared to its spin-off series Persona. In SMT:V’s case, I kind of disagree with both sentiments. While the writing varies in quality, SMT has always been a franchise that is more focused on thematic presentation and worldbuilding than raw exposure to a narrative. It does help if players have previously played Shin Megami Tensei III: Nocturne, as SMT:V is effectively a direct sequel to the events of that game. Furthermore, SMT:V does a fairly poor job at explaining some key terminology of the series, which can exasperate this issue.That being said, SMT:V, after its Vengeance update, includes two routes the player can go through: The original Canon of Creation, which in many ways once again mimics the structure of SMT:III Nocturne, as the player is primarily focused on the ideal of how the world should be rebuilt after its destruction, and the newly added titular Canon of Vengeance, which in some ways feels like a callback to earlier SMT entries due to the stronger focus on Alignment Representatives and genuine character development. This alignment focus is core to SMT at large, and SMT:V is no exception—effectively, the game features two factions in Law and Chaos, which are represented by characters in their respective routes and which steer the player towards the various endings. As an apocalypse story, SMT:V takes heavy inspiration from the Garden of Eden narrative in the books of Genesis, and as such, the iconography of the “Knowledge”, and “Life” of Eden, as well as biblical narrative, underlines most of the game’s story. It is difficult to say whether the differences in each route warrant them being separated, and therefore also whether SMT:V would be worth playing for the story alone, but I do think it features perfectly reasonable writing for how complex the setting is in which it takes place. The greatest appeal remains in seeing a myriad of mythological, biblical, and literary characters represented in wildly unique designs interact in an equally unique world that still manages to remain coherent.SMT:V is a turn-based creature collector. More specifically, the game features what is referred to as Press-Turn combat. A Press-Turn is a token that determines the number of actions either the enemy or the player, and their team of up to three additional demons, can take before the opposing side is up. However, players can manipulate these tokens, for example, by scoring critical hits or weaknesses with elemental attacks, which then grant them additional tokens. Much of combat revolves around this resource economy of trying to maximize your turns while suppressing the enemies’, in addition to the usual JRPG mechanics of mana management, buffs, debuffs, etc.Consequently, team building is the second major part of SMT:V. Players gain demons by either recruiting them out in the world or by fusing multiple demons they already own into a new one. The game heavily incentivizes this through the ability to inherit skills down to the next fused demon to eventually create extremely powerful and synergetic parties. SMT:V in particular has added a lot of quality-of-life systems to Demon Fusions, such as a new Reverse Fusion, which lists all possible combinations of demons that you have already discovered, as well as new items with which you can comfortably increase the stats and attack potency of demons. Effectively, this enables players to actually use any demon they may like and not just rely on the currently highest-level character they can fuse or find.The greatest departure from previous entries is that SMT:V has firmly moved away from being a dungeon crawler and instead features four maps per route, which are largely open and filled with sidequests, collectibles, and the usual fluff you would expect. Broadly speaking, I think overworld exploration is done fairly well but also relies heavily on verticality, which can be occasionally frustrating to navigate. One big focus of the game is not just the mere progression through either route but also an emphasis on NG+ exclusive unlocks, such as further demon summons or extraordinarily challenging superbosses. This is a fantastic direction for the series due to this newfound freedom in designing your party and therefore offers amazing replay value, even for someone like myself who tends to only really play RPGs for a single run.Graphically, SMT:V is a bit of a mixed bag. On the one hand, it is very much the most impressive entry in its series by a wide margin and excels at presentation—both in the general visuals of the different areas, but especially during the fairly frequent cutscenes, which do a great job of showcasing the grand scale of the setting.It is a little disappointing that SMT:V has barely changed many of the established demon models, which by now can very much show their age and which become even more apparent when compared to new characters. A very strong point is the constant use of high-contrast particle effects and lighting, which also helps to mask some of these older character models.Furthermore, most demons that are at all relevant to the story or feature prominent sidequests also come with unique skills of their own, which often have visually impressive effects accompanying them, and it goes a long way toward further supporting the very combat-heavy gameplay loop the series is known for.The soundtrack is even stronger, and it is a very difficult thing to get right in a setting such as Shin Megami Tensei; however, SMT:V manages to have the most consistently fantastic OST in the series, in my opinion, both by ambient music as well as character-specific themes, with the only real competition probably being Strange Journey. It features a wide array of genres, from raw and energetic thrash metal tracks like  to more jazzy Persona-esque music like . The game remains impressively flexible with its soundscape.SMT:V ran perfectly fine across my initial playthrough and is now well into my second run. I have not experienced any crashes, stutters, glitches, or bugs of any kind on the below system:Z790UD AXi7-13700KGeForce RTX 407032 GB DDR5 I am firmly convinced that Shin Megami Tensei: V stands as one of the best entries in its series, right next to Strange Journey, which may yet be preferable due to its stronger writing, or the Devil Survivor games. It expertly builds on Nocturne without relying on it for its own story too much, excels in presentation and playing up the sheer uniqueness of its world, and ultimately has mastered the combat system that has made the previous entries so engrossing.

_childDocuments_.review: SMT V: Vengeance follows ATLUS' trend of creating "definitive" versions of their games, and for once I'd say this was well and truly needed. SMT V on the switch, was a mess. Story was awful, characters were unremarkable, forgettable and forced; the environment absolutely devoid of anything interesting, and full of meaningless sidequests that, when combined with the god-awful framerate, really was a chore to finish. SMT V: Vengeance changed everything. For context, I have only played the new route in this game, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is it a joy to play. There's actually a fully fleshed out storyline, characters are actually likeable and do things, and the new boss battles are a joy to behold. In the first ~20 hours of the first game you're given only 2 boss battles: one of which isn't even a real boss. Here, you're greeted with 4 (or 3). I really love the new emphasis on ailments and status effects, which makes you  have to completely rethink how you form your party and trying to minmax each bossfight by changing you and your party's affinities and skills was so much fun. The demon haunt is a very nice touch as well, really immerses you into the world and its many demons. The framerate, it goes without saying, is amazing, which made me wonder why SMT V was released as a switch exclusive in the first place. The only qualm that remains really for me is the environment. It's still very bland and devoid of anything, which I get is the main design choice of the game, but they could've done so much better, following the footsteps of SMT III with its many dungeon mechanics, or SMT IV with their many NPC sidequests and storylines. The magatsuhi rail is a nice change, but it still doesn't change the fact that each area just feels so empty and samey. Still, thats a personal bias, and you can just shrug it off by saying I'm critiquing the fact that SMT V is not SMT III. Overall though, this is a much MUCH better game than the original, and I highly recommend it to both new and returning players of the franchise. It has its flaws, but it lives up to the 5th title of Shin Megami Tensei. I'd give it a strong 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, SMTV is the most enjoyable SMT game. Its easy enough to introduce new players, but still gives enough of a challenge to set expectations for the rest of the series. It is an absolute tragedy this game released exclusively on Nintendo switch. While I enjoyed my time playing the Switch version of the game, my few problems with the game mostly came from performance issues caused by the fact it was on Nintendo Switch. SMTV is beautiful, and im glad people can experience the definitive version of this amazing game. Some things to note, the story is not the best when compared to other megami tensei games, that being said I still believe the story to be enjoyable enough that I became invested in the characters and world while playing. Some of the animations can be a little funky, especially with characters who float or levitate, and they end up looking very stiff (This is more of a personal issue but still). For returning smt fans, this game might not be too difficult. This was technically my first megami tensei, so I found it very difficult (coming from someone who had only really played Pokemon games before this) but I know that people coming from SMT3 and 4 found this game to not be very hard. To finish this off, I ask anyone who has had any interest in megami tensei at all to give it a chance. It is a damn shame more people haven't played this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the Vanilla SMT V on the Switch. I only played through the Chaos route and didn't bother with most of the side quests. I loved the game, it was beautiful and had great music. But story wise? It was hard to be invested in it. It took me a whole year to go through that one playthrough as I played it on and off. I felt nothing for when any of the characters in it died or whatnot. However, I was very intrigued be Vengeance from the early trailers and concept alone. _childDocuments_.review: It's surprising that I was ever wary of Shin Megami Tensei V, because it's become one of my favorite RPGs. This was back when the title was a Switch exclusive too. The original version of this game didn't run terribly well (a problem that can be blamed solely on the hardware) and had a reputation for having a mediocre story. At least, that's what I kept hearing. I put off playing it for a while, but wound up being very pleasantly surprised when I dug into it. It's a great game! Running around ruined Tokyo feels amazing, and the world is smartly designed. I even loved the story, although I do agree there was something... clinical about it. It was more interesting and fascinating than emotionally engaging, I'd say. Vengeance revisits SMTV and brings new areas to explore, demons to collect, and a new storyline that imbues the cast and narrative with a lot of melancholy and heart. I loved the new campaign, I think that it's better than the original. I still think that original campaign should be experienced first though, the new story reevaluates and confronts ideas from the original, and certain characters get shafted outright. (Abdiel was my favorite, and she's barely in the new storyline at all. Every character beat for her happens off screen! I imagine a first time player might be confused by her sudden drastic change.) I haven't even fully beat Vengeance. This game is huge! I want to get all the endings, so I know I'll return to this one again in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary:+ Phenomenal turn-based combat+ Flexible fusion system allows for huge variety in team compositions+ Interesting lore and world which combines mythologies from all over the world past and present+ Solid, varied OST+ Creative visuals- Story lacks substance- Dungeons feel too empty for their sizeIf you're willing to play through the game at least twice, I would suggest playing the Canon of Creation (CoC) path first and the Canon of Vengeance (CoV) path second. If you only plan to play one path then just play CoV which is the better standalone path. You choose the path at the very start of the game: taking the girl's hand is CoV while not taking it is CoC. Also, for NG+ you can choose to carry over everything which will make the playthrough much shorter than the first even if you take the time to explore the new areas.The combat system in this game is one of my favorites out of any turn-based JRPG I've played. The flexibility provided by fusion system combined with punishing battles makes for constantly shifting team setups and strategies. There are also multiple superbosses and multi-phase battles to really push your strategies to their limits.In regards to the story I will make a food comparison. The story has tons of awesome ingredients (lore, world, mythological characters, etc.) and fantastic presentation (visuals, OST). However, the final meal does not feel filling. I think part of it is that the game really emphasizes gameplay (where it shines) and has only minimal story moments. The result is that some character motivations and events feel jarring instead of being naturally built up to or at least matching their introduction. The CoV path is a little better about this issue than the original CoC path since it devotes more time to interactions between the human characters. Nevertheless, even that does not feel like nearly enough, and it has its own sudden shifts as well. In short: it has its cool moments and does its job of tying everything together, but don't go in expecting a riveting story.The majority of the game takes place over the span of multiple huge open maps with tons of optional side content and areas to explore. There are also two comparatively shorter dungeons (technically three since one of them differs depending on your chosen story path). These play more like puzzle dungeons filled with mobs, scattered miscellaneous items, and not much else. I don't personally mind puzzle dungeons but going from these massive open areas filled with random goodies and optional content to these hollow dungeons felt off. Luckily they are not overly long, but I do wish they had more in them given that I thought their designs and gimmicks were actually neat. As is, it really feels like they overstay their welcome.Given their shared roots, I'll make the inevitable comparison to Persona. If Persona is 75% story 25% gameplay, I would say SMTV:V is 85% gameplay and 15% story. Do not expect anything like Persona story-wise, but the combat system, while sharing a similar base, is much more flexible and immersive.
