_childDocuments_.review: With a demo now available that lets you transfer your saves to the full game, I highly recommend giving this game a try for anyone who enjoys, or has enjoyed JRPGs, or monster catching games like Pokemon, or similar titles. It should provide a decent challenge for most, even if you're relatively familiar with JRPGs. The combat mechanics are fun, and making full use of them feels rewarding, Not to mention collecting and fusing demons to create your dream team can be very addicting.The game is relatively light on story, but has nice atmosphere with a great soundtrack. The vanilla Canon of Creation route especially has little story and the characters aren't very fleshed out. The new Canon of Vengeance improves on that a lot, but can still leave you a bit wanting, if you're looking for a story rich experience. Personally I found the story to be serviceable enough. While you'll probably appreciate CoV slightly more if you've played CoC first, CoV is not a sequel, and will be perfectly enjoyable, even if you haven't played the vanilla route first.Personally I find the game to be at its best on the Hard difficulty, but your mileage may vary depending how familiar you are with games of this type. However, since you can't switch to the hard difficulty after starting a game on normal, I recommend at least starting the game on hard, and then lowering it to normal, if you find it needlessly frustrating, or if you're simply not having fun. As with most games by Atlus, the beginning of the game tends to be the most difficult part of it, with the game getting easier as more options open up to handle encounters, until you reach the superbosses. Regardless of chosen difficulty, every encounter is fair and beatable with a decently built party and making proper use of the game's mechanics, without ever needing to resort to grinding, excluding the optional superbosses. The game doesn't stop you from grinding though, if you prefer to brute force through the encounters. If you don't want to become over leveled, I recommend saving any level-up items the game frequently hands out for the endgame, this also helps to minimize the amount of grinding needed, if you want to take on the superbosses at the end. Similarly, I do not recommend buying/using the mitama DLCs, at least not outside of endgame, unless you are specifically looking to make yourself ridiculously overpowered, and wish to steam roll through everything.Overall, this is one of my favorite games of the past few years.

_childDocuments_.review: A DECENT change of pace. As my first SMT title, despite being a PERSONA fan, this is not bad at all!-A LOT of game-play differences from persona, but a welcome one. Imagine fighting Shadows, but instead of human team-mates you use DEMONS instead! (until... well, find out for yourself!)-CHUNKY. It has TONS of game-play to be had, plenty of fusion combinations that are viable! Mix and match and create the perfect demons!-Canon of Vengeance vs Canon of Creation. Cannon of Vengeance lets you see/play the game through another lens! It features different zones, different approach to defeating unique enemies, and more. Canon of Creation, lets you revisit the ORIGINAL plot of the game (for those that are curious and want to see what the original plot was like on a new game plus, this is a nice touch!)-New Features and included DLC. This includes MOST of the DLC that SMT V had in the OG version of the game. Demons now have "Innate" or Passive skills, which add more strategy and fluidity to game-play. New areas to explore, new miracles to earn, new demons to recruit and fuse, and it seems like they've upped the spawn rates on "certain" rare enemies! All in all, this is a SUPERIOR JRPG, with MINIMUM 40-60 Hrs of game-play, not to mention a SIZE-ABLE amount of extras to pursue for a WHOPPING over 100+ HR game. (YES THERE IS ALSO NEW GAME PLUS!)A great use of funds if you are looking for a BEEFY turn-based JRPG. Look no further!

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I bought the original on the Nintendo Switch so here's my current update on the state of the game compared to the original. I will progressively update this review as I go through the game so if you're in the verge of deciding for or against buying this game, I hope I can help.Playtime ~1 hour:Graphics are good, I have a 4080 and there's absolutely 0 stuttering or framrate drops so far.Soundtrack is divine as always in any SMT game and we got a new sick intro.My main gripe with the original was it's very limited story aspect - it seems this has been acknowledged by the developers, there's now 2 main stories you can decide on playing. At the very beginning of the game you have the option to choose between the original story or the "vengance" story. I took the second option since I already played the original. Playtime ~10 hours:Voiceacting is top notch, the vengance story is already very different to the original. They put a lot more emphasis on cutscenes in this installment. I do not know whether the famous choice-aspect of the smt series will make a comback in a way that my first playthrough truly differs from yours or if it will be like in the main game where you basically got to choose your ending right before it happened via one choice. Added soundtrack is awesome.They also added a lot to the main game. New demons, new little areas to explore and new quests. I spent double the amount of time in the first area compared to my first playthrough and I'm not even fully done with the area yet. If you're a completionist, they bumped up your grind a lot - which is a good thing in my eyes - more content is always appreciated.Playtime ~16 hours:Still waiting for more than 1 important decision to make throughout the game's story.Multiple QoL improvements. Demon negotiations were worked on as well. Was shown the silhouette of a demon and had to guess the name correctly. Big plus for silly games like these.Playtime ~46 hours:Look, the story has been taken way more serious than the original game. I also like the optional content a lot and the new areas in the game a fun to traverse.But I've yet to see a glimpse of what made the SMT Franchise so special.I haven't seen any mention of the alignment system so far and I'm pretty far into the story - I'm currently in Taito. And while things like these have been teased so far, the only time I even read about it is in the Demon Compendium. In SMT 4 and SMT 4 Apocalypse your entire story could be influenced by the choices. I'm afraid they'll handle it like in the main game where you just choose your alignment shortly before the final boss. I hope I'll be proven wrong.80 hours: Satisfied on all accounts

_childDocuments_.review: Base game SMT V is a great game, but SMT V: Vengeance went ahead and fixed pretty much all of the performance issues that it had on switch. This thing runs incredibly smoothly on the steam deck, and any delay that was once present when opening menus or when selecting commands in battle is now non-existent. The gameplay of the original SMT V was, in my opinion, some of the best in the JRPG genre. In Vengeance, the gameplay maintains the same high standard, and the addition of innate skills to each demon adds even more strategy to an already strategic system.Anyone who has played the original SMT V to completion knows that the story was the weakest aspect of the game. While I am not particularly far along in the game, the brand new Canon of Vengeance route so far seems to add some much needed plot to help string things along. My opinion of Yoko Hiromine, this game's Atlus re-release girl™, is already much higher than that of the main cast in the original SMT V mainly due to the fact that we actually get to spend time with her and learn about her personality. One more thing, the music is, to the surprise of no one, absolutely orgasmic. Ryota Kozuka once again knocks it out of the park with the soundtrack, and I cannot wait to see what other tracks are lying in wait.The original SMT V is a game that I hold dear, but in my 5.8 hours of play (at the time of writing this), Vengeance has improved on pretty much all of my gripes that held the original from being a truly phenomenal game. I hope that this level of quality is maintained throughout the whole experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this on switch knowing Atlus was going to eventually release a definitive edition sometime later, that being said, there are so many quality of life improvements that makes this all the more worth it.- Higher and more stable framerate both in gameplay and cutscenes.-The ability to save anywhere.-A way better map (I don't know how to explain it but the mini seems different, like more detailed)-Old demons have new skills based on race.-New demons-A place called the demon haunt you can visit that you can have some downtime with Aogami and your demons and each demon has its own personality And those are just general changes that apply for both games while also having an entirely new story.That being said they're some changes that do stick out while not being a make it or break thing, are noticeable.-The sand doesn't shimmer like on the switch but it does during cutscenes-Some Ui are stuck at a lower framerate than the game so you can't change that-There some chopping during gameplay like the frame drops everyone in a while. From what I can gather it might be a shader cache thing, don't quote on that.As for steam deck performance it works out of the box 50 fps with the battery lasting 4ish hours.All in all, Atlus did it again, making a great game even better.

_childDocuments_.review: Glorified Yap Sesh Incoming: I was already a big fan of the original SMT V. With it being my introduction to the SMT series, it instantly got me hooked on its gameplay mechanics and its variety. With that, I can say that the gameplay in the original is near perfect in my opinion; everything else was subpar though. The story felt flat all throughout, which is to be expected in mainline SMT, you're not going to expect a super enthralling story from start to end, but even by the end I was wanting a LOT more than what I got. I also thought since it was on the Nintendo Switch, the performance was held back, with frame rate drops and pop-ins being all too prevalent. Although I put so much time into the game and replayed it several times, I knew this game could be a lot better if there was an enhanced version similar to how the Persona games are handled like with P4G or P5R. Luckily this game has improved nearly everything I thought faltered. The game looks amazing now, even better considering that I was surprised the game looked decent on the Switch to begin with. Every demon looks amazing and the overworld is much more fun to explore when it isn't stuttering so often. I also like the additions to the story with the new villians and especially the new character on your side, Yoko, adding a new dynamic to the main cast. Also, if you're wondering the new story mode is still very similar only until the end, from what I have played so far, there is still a lot of new stuff in this new 80 hour journey, with new or tweeked boss fights and how they affect story after completing them. The QOL features are also great, (personally, saving anywhere is a GODSEND when I don't feeling backtracking after missing an attack and getting crit and hit for weakness by a bunch of weaker enemies) and the new gameplay features like innate abilities make combat much more fun and makes each a demon a bit more unique. This is probably gonna be my GOTY like it was when it came out in 2021, and I highly recommend to any RPGhead out there or anyone interesting in the SMT series. Sorry for the long yap sesh, felt bored after coming home from work so decided to write all this out.(BTW, dont fight the Naamah boss fight with cutscenes on in front of your parents, that's a player's tip for ya.)

_childDocuments_.review: Shin Megami Tensei is such a fantastic series, and as per usual Atlus fashion, SMTV also continues it's trend of being a fantastic game! You basically have a more dark and gritty and adult version of Pokemon (yes I'm aware SMT came before Pokemon, but this review is for people that DON'T know that), where instead of cute Pocket Monsters you capture and use to fight, you use Dieties/Angels/Demons/Cryptids from Mythology and Folklore. With each demon you recruit to your team, you'll be tempted to read their mini-bios to learn a bit about them and a bit about the mythological culture of the real world we live in. I've always loved the designs Megaten does for these mythological and religious figures, and this game really provides some cool designs. With this newer version of SMTV:Vengaence, you get a lot of good DLC to help make the grind the original was a whole lot easier imo. You also get a brand new story mode added to the original story that you can choose by starting a new game and making the choice in the beginning. So not only is this a great game for people getting into the SMT series, but also a fantastic addition for those of us who already bought SMTV for the Nintendo Switch, but also wanted to get the game on PC with the additional content!ATLUS and From Software are two gaming companies that have a loyal fan from me. They've always released fantastic quality games and never sacrificed quality for anything else. They guarantee a sale from me every single time they make another game, and I look forward to SMTVI whenever that happens. I just hope I get to live to see a day when ATLUS makes a SMT game where I can make my own character. I miss SMT: Imagine.

_childDocuments_.review: Vanilla Shin Megami Tensei V honestly disappointed me. Its not because it was a bad game, far from it, SMTV had some of the best turn based gameplay of this generation. But in the places it was lacking, it really lacked. This goes for mainly the story. The game pays a lot of attention to it but does little to nothing with it. Character arcs and motivations are thin, if they even exist at all. The demons were great but I wish there was more with them. This isn’t to say that theres nothing interesting about the story, theres a lot of missed potential here that I really wish they did something with.Shin Megami Tensei V Vengeance uses that potential. Firstly, characters that had little to no attention in the original have been expanded upon, the conversations and interactions are super interesting. The plot over all is super interesting, having me constantly engaged. Concepts from the original story have been used to twist the story in really interesting ways. The new demons are really awesome. Overall everything was improved, to the point where the original story now has an added context to make it better.The gameplay was also heavily improved. There are these grind rails that either take you to a secret area with new demons and essences, or work as a short cut back to a checkpoint. You can now look at your position from above just in case you don’t know how to get to a certain area. You can save anywhere, which wasn’t a necessary addition but is a nice one. Nahobino unique abilities (which were originally a one and done essence) are now re-obtainable, thanks to them being rebuilt to “aogami husks”, which recharge after a certain amount of time. Many new miracles have been added for QOL or just for the sake of your advantage. An auto battle feature has been added. And even more beyond that.This is one of the few times where I really appreciate atlus coming back to this game and rereleasing it. Its one of my favorite games of this year and one of my favorite games in the SMT series. Get it when you can or on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Minor issues like no restart fight option are the only thing that hold this back. The variety of ways available to play this game are really neat. The main thing being that bosses are 'usually' not immune to any status effects like seal and charm, meaning you can actually use status effects in a JRPG. There are some exceptions like late game main story bosses but 90% of the encounters are free for you to enjoy whatever build you want. Not to mention 'pierce' skills which bypass resistances, which allows your optimised elemental demons to still be used in fights where their element would usually be detrimental to you.The 'Essence' system also allows for easy building since you can apply them to both your MC and demons to trade any skills you want onto any demon.Demon variety is also done excellently with unique skills and elemental affinities on individual demons. It's better to slap support skills on demons like Idun or Cleopatra due to their high support affinity and powerful support unique skills. Better to invest in Cu Chulainn as a wind demon due to his high wind affinity and unique wind skill. I could keep going.But on top of that, it's also totally viable to play this like Pokemon and keep certain demons with you throughout the whole game, due to special items that level up demons and increase their stats (as well as importing skills from Essences like I already mentioned). Idun is a level ~40 demon and I kept her up until level 90 because I just shoved Grimoires and Incenses into her to keep her stats high enough to keep up. Now she's an insane support machine, able to keep my entire team buffed and the entire enemy team debuffed.But the final piece that makes the combat feel so good is the Nahobino himself. The main character. He can be built however you so please. There are Nahobino unique skills you can find from special Essences, you can manually allocate 1/3 of his stat points every level to focus on a particular area and change resistances whenever you want by using copying them from Essences. By the end of the game, I was a physical critical damage build. Able to deal 4000+ damage per hit with a resistance to every damage type.No random encounters. Standard ambush system you'll recognise from Persona 3 and 4.You can save WHENEVER YOU WANT. No more running around in a panic to the next save point so you don't die and lose your progress after a difficult fight.Walking around allows you to interact with spots which can give you anything from weak consumables to permanent stat increases.Magastsu Rail shortcuts make it so your never too far away from your last heal station to refill on health and mana.Chests scattered around the map along with collectable 'Mimon' dudes you can find to get rewards.I wish the movement speed was like 10-15% faster but it's not too slow getting around.The last few dungeon areas had some annoying puzzle segments. One involving flipping the room around and another with stopping time to avoid enemies. I disliked both of these but I dislike puzzles in general so maybe that's just a me thing.It also ran very well on my mid-tier system at 100+ fps, but since this was a Nintendo Switch exclusive until recently, that's not a surprise.Overall a typical overworld exploration system. Nothing special about it really, but no downsides either and it was fun to explore. Especially the big Da'at maps which constantly surprised me with how big they were. I missed the entire northern half of one of them for hours since I was so pre-occupied with the southern side.It's an Atlus game.Demon visual design is great with a good mix of cool badass looking dudes like Dominion, Seth and Asura. Cute demons like Jack Frost (Nahobeeho especially), Idun and Demeter. Also the horny ones like Cleopatra, Cybele, Ishtar and all 4 members of the Qadistu (yes that's them on the cover art and yes there's an uncomfortable amount of jiggle physics).Overall a pleasant UI. It's not Persona level of stylised, but it's nice to look at and feels smooth.You shouldn't be surprised that the music is a masterpiece (mostly). The way that the music builds and refuses to start before your first move in combat sounded great the whole game. And god I love the Primordial Goddess theme. It really feels like it's the end of the world during this fight mostly due to the music. The Taito exploration theme too is so calming to hear as your last open area before the final dungeon.Only 'bad' song was the Shinjuku 3rd Block exploration theme. Mostly because I was so lost on how to climb up the buildings to get the chests on top of them. I had this song loop like 4-5 times while trying to get up and that guy mumbling + the piano really got repetitive.This is a 50 hour long game and I beat it in 4 days. SMT 6 when?9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Shin Megami Tensei V Vengeance is one of the dread “updated rerelease” that Atlus is infamously known for with other examples such as Strange Journey Redux, Devil Survivor Overclocked, Persona 5 Royal and Persona 3 FES. It’s weird how Persona 4 didn’t get one as it’s only release was in 2008 and nowhere else. But since a lot of people didn’t get the chance to play the original release on the Switch back in 2021, this is the perfect opportunity to hop in, as the game is packed with new things, better performance and the typical bells and whistles when coming to a higher end platform, and more QOL features than you can place in your skill slots.Vengeance starts you off with the choice of 2 routes, the canon of creation, which is the original campaign from 2021, and the canon of Vengeance, which contains the new story. I have not played the Canon of Creation since my last play through in 2021, so I can’t tell you what changes have occurred for new and returning players, but I’d say that the Vengeance campaign is definitely expanded and has significant differences from the original story (If you honestly can count it as one.) Once again, you play as a high school student living your life in good ole Tokyo. You’ve got a host of...I guess acquaintances? The intro is quite early reminiscent to another SMT game, one that I even reviewed previously. Maybe it’s intentional? Since I want to leave this largely spoiler free, some of the information of the beginning will be revealed to you so I’ll just speed it up a bit. One thing leads to another, and you are transported to a huge wasteland in what appears to be the ruins of Tokyo. This desert wasteland is crawling with strange hostile creatures called demons. Right before a pack of daemons rip you apart, a mysterious man appears before you, urging you to take his hand if you want to live. Clearly wanting to do so, you grab his hand and then you become one (Get your mind out of the gutter). You have become a being known as a Nahobino, giving you supernatural strength and prowess. With your new found powers, you are able to defend yourself from the onslaught of demons. Why did he Tokyo you knew become like this? Just what is a Nahobino, and are there others like you? If you want answers, a long road of demon corpses and sand shoes await you.SMTVV is a pseudo open world with rather than the crazy dungeons the series is known for, the entire over world is it own dungeon, with a host of demons, platforming, and maneuverings puzzles for you to keep it you on your toes. There is loads of things to find, such as items to help you survive the demonic wasteland, Miman, strange creatures that litter the various parts of Daat, which Gustave, the shopkeeper of the game reward you if you find enough, different cube like chest that contain money, items, and more important demon essences which allow you to take demon skills for yourself or to equip your own demons.Speaking of which, I should probably talk about the major aspect of the game, demon hunting and recruiting. Demons are the primary denizens of Daat, and nearly all of them wan to see you undead. Demons are murderous. They are fickle. They will maim you for saying the wrong thing or for just keeping something they want for them. But your time surviving will certainly be easier with help. Demons usually have a weakness that you or our own demonic allies can exploit which allows you to gain turns. Known as the press turns system, exploiting a demon’s weakness and protecting your own is the primary way you’ll be able to survive. Remember, demons are tools, so if a tool isn’t cut out for it’s next job, you get a new tool if you don’t want your “Magatsuhi” to be free flowing if you know what I mean. The game has a variety of skills you can use, and also a large number of demons for you to recruit, fuse, and fight. There are also a large number of side quest that, yea largely involve fighting, but the choices you make do a good job in determining your alignment (Something I’ll let the game explain to you later.)What you see is what you get regarding the gameplay, so don’t expect significant changes and if the time you spend during the first Daat does’t seem that appealing, then I suggest returning the game if you can since it won’t really change significantly. The game isn’t what I would call open ended as all the paths that players go through will meet sooner rather than later, but it’s definitely more open ended compared to something like Persona or other similiar JRPGs.Performance was really great, and although unfortunately it has denuvo, I didn’t really sense much hindrances although on very small occasions there were performance loss and CTD but so rare that it’s not worth mentioning. Course I am playing this on a PC that’s not super strong, but definitely more than enough for this game, so I am unsure how other platforms or even the Steam Deck would run. I keep my reviews spoiler free, at most telling you what happens in the first 10 minutes- 1 hour in a game. Basically nothing but the premise, and I will keep it that way. The original Canon of Creation in the 2021 release was barely a story at all and I would not recommend that especially if you were primarily concerned about story (yes, I know some people argue story in SMT doesn’t matter but that’s far from the truth. Devil Survivor, Strange Journey, and SMT4 before the alignment lock is some damn good readin). I can’t tell you if there are significant changes to it in Vengeance as I’m not going to play through this very long game twice at the very least not anytime soon, but I think you should keep that in mind. The new Canon of vengeance introduces the “New Girl” by the name of Yoko Hiromine, a staple of heroines in Atlus rereleases. Now Yoko is so obviously Chaos it hurts but the game takes a more nuanced approach than what you’ d expect. I would say this game is unique in that rather than one-off altercations that build (Some games more quickly than others) off each other, you will see characters have to defend their beliefs in mundane (Well, as far as SMT is concerned) circumstances. I think Vengeance was a steep more enjoyable than the original release, but what was a shame that it is not a complete retool which I think it might have needed. Now it might be unreasonable to expect them to overhaul a 3 year old game and put that effort in a new title, but it’s a shame that a good many of plot beats are carried over from the original game. The new Daat present in Vengeance though was definitely one of the better designed ones and I hope if they plan to expand more on SMTV’s game play in future titles that they use it as a reference.Difficulty is definitely more cut throat if you’re coming from Persona so you can easily be wiped (Hell it’s possible to lose the very first battle that way). But there are a variety of difficulty levels for those who want to focus more on the exploration and story. Can’t tell you how it’s balanced as I played on the hardest difficulty, but I found it very appealing. Late game eased up though, but that’s usually the case for most games anyway so I can’t really hold it against it. All in all, a really solid game and if you haven’t had the chance to play SMTV then Vengeance is your best (Some would say only, some of those people include me) shot.

_childDocuments_.review: I've put about 80 hours into this game and got all the achievements. I liked this game a lot, but I can still see the flaws. Allow me to write my thoughts so that it can be ignored.Having played the original SMT 5 on switch, this offering was very highly anticipated for me personally. The original was my first experience into the SMT/Persona series (I've since played SMT 3, SMT 4A, Persona 5 Royal, Persona 3 Reload), and while I loved the combat, there were some clear indicators the original was rushed. Did this entry fix things?? I hear you saying "this guy has 80 hours, obviously it must have" well it did, but still you might be slightly surprised! Spoilers ahead.The good:- The story is a significant improvement over the original. Don't get me wrong, it ain't Shakespeare, but they took the time to develop the main cast a lot more than the original. Mastema is a good addition, he's a more interesting villain than uhhhh... Abdiel, I guess was the original villain? I'd say the storytelling went from a D- to a B.- The OST has been re-worked and a number of really good new songs were added. One of the things I didn't care for in the original was how generic the music was in the original. The new tracks feel more like they have an "identity" and are fun to listen to and not some generic electric guitar over chanting/droning.- The gameplay is just as good as the original, which to me personally is top tier. The changes to demons innate abilities and the new limit breaks (not gonna use the real term here) allow you to approach battles in new and interesting ways. They also fixed some gaps in the ultimate skills of the main character so that a physical build isn't the only OP endgame build.- The new areas are IMO unquestionably better than the originals. I know this because part of the achievements require you to play the original areas at least 4 times, which is cruel to do to another human being.- Guest characters are fun and interesting. I like the guys who summon demons via their phone, it's like an evil pokemon thing. The series should do more of that.- Beezelbub killing the dumb ugly boring snake guy boss was really good, and his theme is cool. Wish there were more twists like this.The questionable:- The original, aka Canon of Creation, sucks. Sorry, it just does especially when it's side by side with the improved new content. I know it's a cultural thing in Japan you can't say something is bad, you have to say it's "interesting" or say "wa chotto" which is like saying "oh yea, the original game, uhhh.. a little... yeaaa..." and trail off. The story is inferior, the original third area map is ugly, hard to navigate, and is just unfun. The fan dungeon is ugly, hard to navigate, and is just unfun. I mention this because it plays in to some of the questionable things in the new content such as...- If you didn't play the original, I think it's clear some story beats won't make any sense. Some examples that come to mind are Zeus and Odin being mad at you (or, their existence in the story at all), the stuff going on in the original third area that gets referenced (the "demon king" who was just some fat guy and not Lucifer for some reason).- Dazai, the only character with any kind of arc in the original, has a more nebulous villainous turn,which is rough since it was pretty unclear in the original too! Though it is funny they made his battle portrait look like Donald Trump's mugshot.- The Qadistu kinda just disappear from the story in what I think is an unsatisfying way. You finally have a confrontation with all four of them midgame, you win, they have a cutscene where they kill you anyway, then that's it. I guess they get absorbed into Yoko or whatever, but it feels kinda like they got dropped.- I wonder how many of these missteps were because of dedicating time to ensure the original story "worked" with the new/altered content, or if they had to maintain some level of respect for the garbage original story rather than just do an SMT 4 Apocalypse style "what-if" alternative scenario. Ah well.- The second dungeon is untouched. I guess their grand vision for it was always "long, empty hallways where enemies run at you in a straight line and we copy/paste the evil horse to block doorways". Ok.- Why is there an achievement to fight the witch lady's projection twice? It's pretty clear after the first time how the mechanic works and I would assume the game doesn't want you to fight her projection 4 million times, so why make it an achievement? It's like an achievement for failing to jump over a goomba twice in Mario. This was actually the last achievement I got in the game because I didn't look at the list until I was doing the god-awful Canon of Creation playthroughs.At any rate, I'm glad this game exists and they released it on other platforms. They took a very flawed masterpiece in SMT 5 and created a not-quite-as-flawed masterpiece in SMT 5 Vengeance.

_childDocuments_.review: Like many folks, my first introduction to the Shin Megami Tensei franchise was through Persona. When SMT 3 HD released and people gawked at the price, I got turned off. Then when SMT 5 released only for the Switch, I got turned off again.So the enhanced Vengeance port was the perfect excuse for me to dive in, and I'm glad I did, with some caveats.The general "vibe" of SMT 5 is like no other game I have played before. Yes, the setting is "insert post apocalyptic world here" (in this case Tokyo), but everything about this game screams "humorous dread". Your demons in your party joke about how they would eat you or kill you. There are little humans to be seen. The demons in the world actually enjoy that the world is all wrecked up. You get a sense that this world is exactly how most of its inhabitants want it to be.For those who have played both SMT and Persona, there's a general consensus that Persona's combat gameplay is just "a dumbed down version of SMT" and after playing through SMT 5, I absolutely agree. In addition to standard weaknesses, each demon has innate buffs or debuffs to their attacks of a certain element. So you can't just throw an Agi fire skill onto a Jack Frost for coverage because his fire attack power is inherently debuffed. Then add the sheer number of available demons on top of that, with each demon having its own race, and certain special Magatsuhi skills only being usable by demons of a certain race, or a certain group of demons, you get it.And that's not even considering the Press Turn system, which is absolutely visceral in its application. SMT 5 rewards very risky combat, in fact, the more conservative you are, the more likely you will be to die in any particular combat encounter. It's tense, it's exciting... And now I will never think Persona's combat is better.For the story, I went straight for the Vengeance route, of which the consensus was that it was a better route than the original SMT 5, now called Creation.Unfortunately, the narrative starts out incredibly strong, but ends up incredibly, and suddenly, dull - same with the character progression. You initially team up with a few human characters and gradually progress your way through each open world zone, with interesting boss fights along the way. There's a lot of moral ambiguity throughout, and this is communicated through the contrasting viewpoints of two of the three lead characters. It all comes to a head about two-thirds of the way through the game in an amazing sequence......and then completely falls on its face. The rest of the game after this moment is dull, grindy, and bland. It's as if the scenario writers either gave up or were given the directive to stop midway through. The last open area and the last dungeon are so bland in their execution that they make Soul Hackers 2 look good. It got to the point where I was desperately hunting for level up items to reduce the grind and the time I spend in the last area. And even worse still, figuring out new and interesting endgame fusion combinations ended up being more fulfilling than actually progressing to the game's finale.Thankfully, the final sequence does redeem itself a bit, with several possible endings you can get depending on your dialogue choices throughout the game. It returned the game to the pace and stakes it had established earlier on.Overall, I don't regret the time I spent playing it at all, but it just dragged to the end after starting off strong. My playthrough lasted approximately 67 hours, including the main story on the Vengeance route, the majority (but not all) of the available sidequests, just under 100 Miman found, and about a 60% completion of the demon compendium.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original version of Switch back when it came out and this is basically a more complete package with much better performance (than the Switch original) and a lot of added elemts (including a more story-heavy campaign). It runs butter-smooth on PC and looks very polished (if you are okay with the aesthetics you can see in the trailer/screenshots).FOR PEOPLE WHO LIKE TURN-BASED GAMES this is a VERY solid RPG that combines an atmosphere akin to Dark Souls games (more grim/hostile world) with lighter elements (funny demon companions/narrative choices). The best way you can describe the battle system would be something like "darker Pokemon for adults" although it has to be noted that most demons and creatures in this game are inspired by international folklore/myths/legends which will ramp up significantly (want to battle Odin with Alice from Alice in Wonderland? You'll get that chance here). The difficulty (even on Normal) is nothing to scoff at either. It's an almost perfect curve for those who are used to turn-based RPGs without getting frustrated. FOR PEOPLE WHO LIKE PERSONA GAMES note that this is no Persona game! The emphasis in Shin Megami games is fighting and - in the case of this game - map exploration. While I appriciate the different focus and go well with its different emphasis, you might not so be aware that social links and a narrative-driven experience are not part of this product. While they clearly ramped up the story in the new Vegance plot, it still doesn't come close to games like P4 or P5. On the upside you'll get into the action much faster and much more often.Overall this might be one of THE best turn-based RPGs you can play on PC right now.

_childDocuments_.review: You can't really go wrong with a SMT title if you like thoughtful battles and fighting strong bosses in RPGs.My first playthrough took 150 hours; I would say 50% is from fusing demons and 25% is from fighting bosses. Good stuff. Gameplay was the star of the show as always, as in most SMT titles, battles in this game have your typical press turn system where you get more turns as you hit enemy weaknesses or you got crits; which motivates and rewards you to play efficiently. But let's say you hit the enemy's strengths instead, for example hitting a flame demon with fire, then you lose turns. You can't really choose a random attack and expect to win every time. Story was pretty bare bones in the original route, but in the new route for Vengeance has remedied this somewhat. However in that route, you will have party members giving comments on whatever decisions you make on most side quests so I guess it's up to you to decide that's a plus or not.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played the original on the Nintendo Switch upon release and getting over 300 hours in it I completely recommend this to any fans of JRPGs. I did a full playthrough of this version on the Nintendo Switch as well, but I wanted to experience this game in all of its glory. This game is super easy to run and I am getting whatever framerate I set in the options menu. It runs perfectly on Linux out of the box (I run Pop_OS with and Nvidia card). As for gameplay it is my favorite SMT game. The press turn battle system creates a lot of thought and strategy in more difficult fights and even regular encounters can push you. The quality of life updates, such as saving anywhere, really improve the flow. You can save right before boss battles getting rid of some of the running back you'd have to do in the original. The unique traits and abilities really amp up your team building as well. Storywise, it's okay. I was one of the few people that thought the story of the original was fine, it's based more on themes than actual story beats. The new Canon of Vengeance goes a lot more in depth with certain characters and the story provides some new context for the old story.Overall, great game. If you like turn-based games than I don't think you can go wrong with this.

_childDocuments_.review: History of the book that gave rise to Shin megami Tensei: Akemi Nakajima, of the school's gifted class and a computer genius, is assaulted by Hiroyuki Kondo of the normal class under the orders of Kyoko Takamizawa, who had been angered by Nakajima rejecting her romantic advances. Kyoko had told Kondo that Nakajima had been flirting with her rather than the other way around, prompting the attack.The normal students were rarely punished for their actions against other students out of fear and pity on the part of faculty. Battered and bloody, Nakajima comes home and decides to finish his Demon Summoning Program, a work in progress of his, to exact revenge. He discovers that his computer is not powerful enough to use the program, so he must use the school's Computer Aided Instruction (CAI) room's host computer.Sneaking into the school at night, Nakajima draws a pentagram in the computer room and attempts to run the program, but is found by Professor Iida. Nakajima has a tense conversation with the professor, who becomes afraid of him, but he is able to run the program regardless. Nakajima commands the program to kill Kondo and Kyoko, which causes a tremor in the school but otherwise appears to not work.A week later while Professor Iida is teaching a computer class in the CAI room with Nakajima and Kyoko present. Suddenly a voice resounds from the host computer. A demon, Loki, trapped inside the host computer, uses the monitors in the CAI room to hypnotize the entire class except Nakajima, Kyoko and Professor Iida. The demon follows Nakajima's request and commands the hypnotized students to kill Kyoko. They then lure Hiroyuki Kondo, into the room and kill him as well. Professor Iida is also killed in the chaos, which upsets Nakajima somewhat: Loki had followed the program's command, but Nakajima had not specified any restrictions.Drunk with power, Nakajima at first begins to comply with Loki's request for female sacrifices, offering him his female professor, Ohara, who proceeds to be metaphysically assaulted by Loki through the use of a helmet-like contraption connected to the summoning program. Permanently damaged by the encounter, Ohara eventually becomes Loki's loyal servant and helps Loki assume physical form in the human world through Nakajima's program as well as her own connection to the demon.Nakajima meets Yumiko Shirasagi during this time, a newly-transferred student with whom he feels a strange connection to. Unbeknownst to him, she had witnessed the bizarre encounter with Ohara and Loki, but had dismissed it as illusion and trickery. Eventually, the demon demands that Nakajima offer him Yumiko, which Nakajima refuses to do. He then advises Yumiko to stay away from the school in an attempt to save her. That night, Yumiko ignores Nakajima's advice and returns to the school, prompting the attention of Loki. Nakajima attempts to regain control of Loki, but the demon mocks Nakajima's attempts to command him.Loki summons himself into the physical world through the CAI room computer and goes on a killing spree, free from Nakajima's control. Jealous of Yumiko, Ohara attacks and wounds her. Nakajima summons a benign, loyal demon, Cerberus, to help him battle Loki, to no avail. During the battle, Yumiko is possessed by Izanami, of whom Yumiko is a reincarnation, and burns Loki with her powers. In addition to dealing with Cerberus, Loki is distracted enough so that Yumiko and Nakajima can escape through a dimensional warp to Asuka created by Izanami, although Loki succeeds in fatally wounding Yumiko as she flees.Still influenced by Izanami, Yumiko tells Nakajima that she will die, but could be revived if her body is brought to Izanami's tomb. Yumiko dies, but with the help of Cerberus, Nakajima complies with her dying request and travels to the Shirasagi Mount, where he meets Yomotsu-Shikome, a loyal servant of Izanami's.Yomotsu-Shikome provides Nakajima with two mystical spheres, and guides him onward. With Ohara's help, Loki is able to follow them to Asuka and Shirasagi Mount, where he kills Yomotsu-Shikome. Izanami meets Nakajima and Yumiko in the tomb, but she is attacked by Loki before the resurrection can take place. Nakajima summons Cerberus to help, but his companion is also no match for Loki, and is defeated. Desperate, Nakajima uses the two spheres that Yomotu-Shikome gave him, which ignite the pomade-covered floor of the tomb, summoning Hinokagutsuchi, who in turn transforms into a powerful, mystical fire sword, with which Nakajima is at last able to kill Loki. Izanami succeeds in reviving Yumiko, but keeps her with her, stating that Yumiko has great hidden powers within her with which they could battle evil.Meanwhile, Ohara, impregnated by Loki, attempts to communicate with him, not knowing that he has perished. This makes her accidentally contact the demon Seth.

_childDocuments_.review: The original release of SMT V was a failure in terms of its narrative. The story told in the AU campaign of this game improves on it drastically by having the important characters play a more involved role in the plot. The law and chaos characters travel with you and they will make regular comments on the events of the game. Having more insight on the thoughts and perspectives of the major characters went a long way in making me actually care about the decisions I made and the outcome of the story. That being said, there are still issues originating from SMT V that prevented this game from being as good as it could have been. Da'at is still an underwritten setting. Many of the major characters in the original campaign have nothing to do and their appearances are contrived/unnecessary. The entirety of the final area is also mostly carried over and it kills the momentum of the plot in an even worse way than it did in the original campaign. This is far from peak SMT, but it is the best new game since SMT IV. This has restored my faith that the people who are currently making these games know what made past SMT games so special. thank you shatlus

_childDocuments_.review: Not flawless by any means but 95% positive is fair. Party customization was fun at first but can become tedious after the first map. But I didn't really need to do those. After getting used to the mechanics it's quite easy to decide what is needed for each major fight. RNG-based stat growth sucks but that's a must have for JRPG at this point.Story though, is great. At least for the new Canon of Vengeance.For example, early onI really love the fact that this Canon has multiple endings but it's not a single choice you take that decides the outcome. Multiple important decisions (which you'll know it's not normal dialogue choices) contributes to what the story will be. And as someone who managed to dodge most spoilers the choices I liked ended up with the ending I prefer is a big plus.Many quests have good story to them too, though a lot of them is still "go there, then go over there". But enough of them is interesting enough for me to bother trying.Not without major flaws however. Two mandatory maps out of 6 you'll spend your time in are classified as "Dungeons" area. And are designed to just waste your time and absolutely nothing else. Other maps have quests to do, things to collect, reasons to explore in general. But these Dungeons are just mazes that force you to walk as long distance as possible with the least effort for the map makers to make them. In Vengeance Canon the "Shakan" map took me 2 hours of nothing but suffering to the point that had it been the start of the game I'd have refund it.Another really bad point is battle musics. Most of them are just plain bad. The specific feeling I can think of is, they were made to be the primary sound you pay attention to. But in a battle they were just distracting. Which is weird since ambient musics are really good and some battle musics are fine. And the lack of music setting beyond on or off for everything isn't helpful. Especially the mob-enemies battle music in the area right after Shakan area I just sufferred. It is really confusingly bad and distracting especially compared to ambient and boss musics of the very same map. Not that it's a bad as music in general but this one seems to be designed for visual-focused cutscenes and it could be good there if I only hear it once.Another minor but annoying thing they could improve but chose not to is not allowing the player to leave boss fights. Losing a fight in this game is game over and put you in title screen and you need to reload the save which is OK. But why didn't they give an option to just go to title screen or reload the save mid fight anyway? Certainly not difficult programming-wise. Thankfully quitting the game isn't bad since it load quite fast.

_childDocuments_.review: I am the target audience for this game, or I should be. Have been a fan of the SMT series from the beginning. This one was a game I was looking forward to. SMT in 3D. However, it was poorly done. The narrative. The combat was simple SMT so I won't complain about that. Narrativly though this fell far from SMT IV and very far from SMT Record breaker 1 and 2. It kept similar themes and endings, but none of it means anything. I'll go with record breaker. In SMT Record Breaker you start the game as a silent protagonist. You choose a butler as your guide, no sane person wants the bunny girl nagging at them, you go through the game and meet a cast of NPCs. You have your friends and you have your strangers.  Through YOUR choices you can deepen those friendships. Through Optional quests you learn more about each faction. By the end of the game you have already locked yourself into a certain path. You have picked sides and the people you didn't help and the people you didn't become friends with it all effects the outcome.In SMT V here....what do you get? You get some woman archangel for some reason leading the charge. She's never represented as good or decent. No one makes an argument for order, and the one person who decides her path is the sane one is a fella who is completely useless, and clings to her simply...because the plot needs someone to. He has no faith in God, doesn't even care about what "His" plan is or what "He" wants. He just wants to give responsibility for his life away to someone else...except he doesn't. You can see what they're "trying" to do, but fail at. For the Chaos outcome you have the myriad gods all doing their own thing. This also comes a bit out of left field. No one argues for it. No one is trying to explain it to you. It's just thrown at you as something you should have been considering the whole time. Then the "humanity" option is exactly the same.It tries to do everything IV and record breaker does, but falls flat. Because you don't have to make a choice on who to spend time with. You don't have people who will die if you don't save them. There are no stakes and no connections being made at all throughout the game.Things get worse with Vengeance. In Vengeance you are given this woman companion who tries to be the protagonist. Because the protagonist is silent she always feels entitled to speak for him. The story is also too much the same in the beginning at least. After the first level I was tired of it. The character you were stuck with was annoying, and with the lack of important choices to make I could not force myself to go through the game again even though I really enjoyed every single playthrough of record breaker. It also helped that you had to earn NG+ features with each playthough which was enjoyable in itself.So. If you like Record Breaker and IV Don't bother with this game, just watch the endings or playthroughs online. I am thoroughly disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance is a huge step up from the original game. First and foremost, the game just looks better on PC and it also is way smoother in every sense. Constant frame rate and the menus are butter smooth, almost instantaneous navigation. Zero load times (could because of my SSD), and no blurry backgrounds (even though, pretty some textures are still low res) No performance issues at all. Only gripe is that there are no Performance Settings. The new story route/version of the game is what the game should've been as the original game. It just feels more complete. The original game story wasn't bad, it was just lacking- Like something was missing, likely due to being rushed. Things weren't explain clearly or if, at all. About 75 hours to finish one route (starting on Hard) and there's 6(?) endings and i'm still missing side quests. The story here feels more complete, like characters actually have a purpose for being around in the Vengeance route. It doesn't feel like random cut scenes with the bare minimum amount of story. The characters actually talk and explain their motives and you even get to see action behind those motives.The small addition of the new "passive skills" steps up the combat for you and enemies (especially bosses). It makes you want to build different types of parties for wacky combos. Wish there were 36 or 48 demon slots for this reason. Too great additions to list here but the best are; more late game stuff, QoL changes, WAY better story, and upgraded combat.If you go by $1 = 1hr, it is more than worth the value.Great Game, worth the price. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Fun combat centric jrpg, and an odd mix of old and modern ideas.While some things like the minimalist storytelling in the Canon of Creation and the overall art style are like Nocturne, this plays a lot more like IV but with the side content and open areas taken to an extreme. Apart from four or five very trivial dungeons, this game is played almost entirely on a series of large overworld maps, and instead of traditional dungeon crawling the game is structured around optional side quests and huge amounts of boss fights. There's still plenty of exploration but since you can save anywhere and are never far from a recovery point it doesn't have the same kind of plodding, faintly stressful meta-game of managing your party and MP that older SMT games and heavy dungeon crawling jrpgs have. The challenge is all mainly in fighting.The story is split into two possible paths at the very beginning. The Canon of Creation is the typical SMT law/neutral/chaos faction rivalry told with very sparse plot and characterization, like I and III. Apparently Atlus wasn't fully satisfied with this so they added the Canon of Vengeance, which has storytelling with complexity and plot developments more on the level of an average jrpg. I kind of appreciate the understated style of CoC; like in III, sometimes simple storytelling can avoid muddying the lofty themes about creation and the apocalypse with mundane plot twists. That aside, if you really want to be told a story, Vengeance has the better one.The music is awesome, to the point I hopped on a proxy so I could spend 7500 yen on a download copy of the 9-disc combined soundtrack. If I have one complaint it's that you spend so much time on the overworld that you hear a lot of the same tracks without appreciating many of the better songs that only come by a couple times. But even then, I have Da'at: ueno playing in the background as I'm writing this.If there's one thing that resoundingly sucks about SMTV, it's the evident lack of an art budget throughout so much of the game. The overworld areas in CoC use the exact same assets with obvious recoloring and different lighting. It's absolutely just the same exact desert and ruined buildings in four different colors. CoV replaces one of them with a slightly more varied district, but the rest are entirely the same. The few dungeons in the game are visually distinct from each other but they're all obviously based on simple cube-based mesh libraries. Every dungeon environment is built from square, equally sized, and repetitive parts, and lack any real set pieces or visually apparent purpose. It's not exaggerating to say that Nocturne's indoor environments were much more interesting to navigate and look at. Everyone knows mainline SMT is no longer Atlus's golden child and this series never had high production values, but I feel they've done the series wrong with how recycled the environment art sometimes comes off.Anyhow, fun game regardless, and Nahobino is cute.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first SMT game; though I already played this on the Switch prior to steam - the remaster is actually quite decent, and very well optimized! - Aside from a few graphical glitches (splotchy UI elements). SMTV is a somewhat unique turn-based JRPG that incorporates light social gameplay elements, and a "press" turn battle system. Unlike other SMTs, this one has more 'free' movement within the world, with some aspects of platforming. There is a hefty amount of different recruitable demons, all of which now come with their own unique passive skills over the original version.The difficulty has been dialed back a little bit compared to the original due to some of these new changes; (more forgiving?), and including but not limited to  It could also be that I am experienced with this style of RPG already. Whichever your skill level is, you can be rest assured that there is an easy mode. Though the common sentiment among these games is that the early game can be rough, so save often.The platforming in this game feels a LOT less miserable with the new addition of Magatsu Rails - grind rails that allow you to quickly traverse areas with less backtracking. Sometimes the platforming still feels a bit clunky though, the massive sandbox areas are recreations of a destroyed Tokyo; much of the landscape is comprised of rubble and broken glass. The  I can say about the platforming is that I sometimes can get caught on the disjointed collision of the terrain - and that the only places you can actually grapple ledges are those  red-colored blocks, but this is a more of a nitpick than anything; to my knowledge Atlus doesn't normally design RPGs with platforming in mind.I think some tend to say that SMT is like Pokemon but with demons but this is incorrect, this style of RPG plays more similarly to Digimon. (4 active party members, 10+ party members in stock) The major difference is that fusion is a lot more prevalent in SMT as opposed to Digimon as a way of acquiring new and different party members - and it's deceptively intricate. I'd argue it's much better than Persona 5's.Lastly, the soundtrack is GODLIKE,  which isn't a surprise if you've played this series before, SMT has absolute bangers and in between has nice atmospheric pieces.My major criticism aside from the platforming, is the practice of Day 1 DLC we have been seeing from Atlus for their games lately. Though I didn't really purchase the deluxe edition for the bonus content; but for the Mitamas. For somebody like me who hyperfixates on creating my own special team, it cuts down on the countless of hours I would otherwise spend grinding without them.Been playing for about two weeks now, I'd say it was worth the buy 100% - there is a ♥♥♥♥ ton of content. SMT might be niche compared to how much traction Persona garners in the west, but SMT overall is getting more attention than it used to which is pretty nice - can't wait to see what the community does with modding this game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've only known Persona, you might look at some of the things in this game and go "wait isn't this just Persona??" but the truth is, Persona has always just been a spinoff of the Shin Megami Tensei mainline series. Other spinoffs of SMT include Soul Hackers, Digital Devil Saga, and Devil Survivors. This right here is the grandaddy of Persona and all those other series, the real deal, the big kahuna. Unlike Persona, which takes hours and hours of exposition before you can do anything fun, SMTV drops you right into the action within 30 minutes and says "good luck."There is no time limit or dating sim aspects like Persona, it's all action. If you specifically enjoy the COMBAT of Persona, fusing stronger and stronger gods and other folklore figures to do even more combat, and getting bodied by an enemy targeting the protagonist's weakness 5 times in a row before you even get a chance to attack, then you'll love this game. The game also treads a perfect middleground between open world and linear progression, there's plenty of exploration and secrets to find, but not an overwhelming amount, and you can comfortably and confidently full clear areas in a reasonable amount of time. SMTV was originally a Switch exclusive, but this new expanded Vengeance rerelease adds a TON of new content while also unshackling it from the confines of the Switch. You owe it to yourself to give this game a try -- like I said earlier, you get dropped into the action FAST so you can get a pretty solid taste of the game before the refund window expires, unlike other games that pack way too much exposition at the start.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tentative write-up, since this is a lengthy game and I'm barely grazing the surface of everything this new release has to offer, but I wanted to share my thoughts on some aspects of it.Firstly, the performance on Valve's Steam Deck is superb. The game runs native resolution at all times, as far as I can tell. It'll hit 90fps most of the time and 60fps almost 100% of the time, depending on where you decide to cap it, making it a wildly superior portable offering compared to the Nintendo Switch original (which I loved, but the chugging was difficult to stomach at times).Secondly, if you bounced off the original because of the level scaling issues or the game's apparent inability to do anything interesting with its cast, I also can't recommend this re-release highly enough. Combat feels much more like classic SMT now, where smart team composition is more important than what level you are. And on the Vengeance route, the game is doing a pretty fantastic job of integrating its cast into the story. Even early on, the difference can be pretty dramatic.This is probably Atlus' most extensive re-release to date. They effectively re-made the game with the Vengeance route. A lot of the content and story beats will feel similar, but there's enough new content constantly peppered throughout that it still feels fresh to me.Finally, it's worth mentioning that the story DLC from the original game is included in this release by default.This is possibly Atlus' best PC conversion to date, and one I'd wholeheartedly recommend to anyone who enjoys dark fantasy, gameplay-centered game design, monster-collecting games like Pokemon, or deep and challenging turn-based combat. Easily the game to beat in 2024 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a turn-based game, and it embraces all the positives of the genre. Not only that, it has a "pokedex" collection feature for all your Demons, so if you grew up with Pokemon main titles, and wanted a more difficult adult take, then this is it. Hard difficulty is incredibly daunting, and Godborn mode brings a fresh experience for those wading into newgame+.There are insurmountable optional challenges that will test you at your very best, and destroy you despite hours of preparation. However, once you're geared up for the optional superbosses, the story bosses might feel a bit easy even on hard difficulty.11/10 Gameplay, best of the genre, the only issue is how much Mora you actually waste on fusing demons, and buying items on Godborn. There's a fatal flaw in this game, it's vitality, the stat is too strong when you single-mindlessly invest into it. Strength and Magic each boosts the skills damage by 40% at 100 stat increments (kind of weak), so it should be buffed to at least 100%. Level differences matter more than all stats weights sans vitality, as it seems there's a lot of hidden weights on level differences between you and the enemy.9/10 Optimization, works on day 1 on most pcs without many performance issues, a rarity these days. Even P5R still has some PCs that can't run without lagging.8/10 "Grimdark tone" story, this game leans more into artistic direction for its characters and set pieces than actually trying to tell a grounded story, which I don't mind. It's not going to make you caree about the characters, and not going to wow you like Persona games. This is the kind of game where gameplay is king.Beating the game on one route, defeating all the superbosses, and completing all the missions took 35 hours, but I knew what I was doing. However, this game has six endings in total (four on Creation and two on Vengeance), so to get a perfect save file you might spend upwards of 100 hours, skipping cutscenes and whatnot.I started with Canon of Vengeance, and then I discovered that one of the superbosses is locked behind Canon of Creation. So, to get all fusible demons, you might have to complete multiple newgame+ attempts.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: gameplay/soundtrack/aesthetics are all absolute perfection, story is utter garbage. If that's fine with you and you like JRPGs, then definitely give this a shot.I played P4G/P5R/P3FES/P3R and loved them all, so I then decided to give SMT a shot. I did some basic research, and decided to just wait a bit for this to release and then play it, since most people seemed to agree that SMTV was the best in the series and this seemed like it was going to be an improvement on top of that (plus, coming to PC of course). I'm very glad I did so.There's a lot I could talk about, but ultimately, I think it all just boils down to the gameplay being fantastic. Game runs nice and smooth, and all the mechanics are super fun: the press-turn system is a blast to master, demon negotiation is always fun (even when it goes wrong), essences make experimenting so accessible and exciting, the demon haunt is cool and allows for some interesting interactions, ... there's a lot to love here.It also helps that the game actually looks really good. There are some technical limitations (it was originally designed for the Switch), but aesthetically, I find it gorgeous. The designs of demons are super inspiring and neat, there's an amazing visual/auditory feedback to actions, places on the map look interesting, etc. Ah, and the soundtrack is equally amazing.My biggest criticism is that the story . Now, don't get me wrong, the worldbuilding and the lore are extremely interesting and had me engaged, but the actual events happening, the characters themselves, the choices you can make, ... it's very bland, at best. The new storyline (Canon of Vengeance) plays around with the events of the "main" storyline (Canon of Creation), and there are some improvements, but even then, it's not particularly brilliant. Still, if you can tolerate the subpar narrative, this is very easy to recommend. I had a blast.Two final notes: one for the DLC, and another for the endings/NG+ (some small spoilers).Regarding the DLC:- The Dance of Mitamas kinda throw a wrench at the difficulty of the game. The Mitama Dance of Miracles I think is worth it, so you can get more Glory and attain Miracles that you otherwise probably wouldn't be able to get, but the other two (Dance of EXP, Dance of Wealth) I think make things too easy in an unsatisfying way. If you're struggling, I think it would be better to just lower the difficulty instead of using this. - "Holy Will and Profane Dissent" gives you Dagda. He's good, and has some strong skills in his essence, but nothing game-breaking, especially because you will probably only get him when you're already close to the endgame. Take it or leave it, it's fine. - "Sakura Cinders of the East" gives you Konohana Sakuya. Boy, is she busted. Idun was previously an absolute game-changing demon already, and KS is basically Idun-but-better, especially when you combo her with other particular demons (endgame spoiler: ). I highly recommend getting this one if you plan on fighting the super-bosses and don't want to grind a lot, she can absolutely help with that. Regarding the endings/NG+: A "full" playthrough (doing all quests, not skipping cutscenes, etc.) takes between 50 to 60 hours, and then NG+ runs skipping everything and keeping the power from the previous run can take as little as 3 to 4 hours.Any order that you choose to play is fine, honestly. Only "strong" recommendation I would have is to play the Canon of Creation first, and the Canon of Vengeance second. But if you want an "optimized order" (light spoilers): Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: It's decent, when you're not mashing through kingdom hearts-esque dialogue from schoolchildren. Missing a lot of what made the previous mainline games so great making it feel like any other generic JRPG. Plot is bland and predictable, especially this many "cycles" into the series and the flow of the game is constantly broken by unnecessary cutscenes so annoying archetypal anime children can explain the obvious to you or whine about their feelings.Visually it's fine, Kazuma Kaneko's iconic style struggles to be as effective in 3D and environments are very repetitive and simplistic but it was originally intended for the switch so it gets a pass. Music is pretty good, but never reaching the highs of IV's absolute bangers.Level curve/difficulty is actually an improvement over previous games in my opinion, I found myself struggling on more bosses but less severely.Roster is pretty poor, a seemingly exclusive emphasis on humanoids for whatever reason, I miss my boy Nidhoggr.Not a fan of removing equipped gear that affects your stats, but AM a fan of the essence system until I had to do some bizarre convoluted save/load rng farm for a 2nd Metatron. More build potential overall but still feels like a very finnicky system and a kind of sidegrade in terms of grind.Despite all these negatives I still enjoyed it enough as an SMT fan to recommend it to other fans but ultimately all playing this game did was make me want to replay IV or SJ.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I already played the original game on the Switch back in 2021, I decided to give the original Canon of Creation another try, this time going for the True Ending. And oh boi, what a ride.It's hooked me more than Elden Ring, I've done 100% of quests and enjoyed it much more than if I'd just skipped through. I think the side quests here DO add to the overall experience. Maybe they don't have the same significance as in Nier Automata, for example, but they certainly aren't there for filler.If there's one thing I LOVE about Shin Megami Tensei V, it's . Ominous, heavenly, . It's not just that the visuals are AWESOME, with vast landscapes and a multitude of levels, but the soundtrack enhances these sensations even more. Of course, here they cooked a lot.And what to say about the already classic Press Turn, it's simply addictive. Exploiting the weaknesses of the enemies to get stronger and end up being a GOD with almighty abilities is simply a game curve that I really enjoy. Plus, this added to the demon fusions, I can spend HOURS just watching demon A join demon B to form another. This scratches that part of my brain that gave me pleasure when I played Pokemon in my childhood, which was the collection of monsters, but in a more complex and interesting way.And what can I say, it seems to me a more rounded experience at the cost of sacrificing several central secondary characters of the original experience. Yoko behaves like a real teenager, rebellious and putting up a fuss about everything, and it is to be appreciated in a JRPG of this caliber where everyone has a clear moral compass from the beginning and everyone has a very strong sense of duty.I think that between that and the quadistu taking a little baton in the rhythm of the adventure from early on, it brings a much more solid set than just demonis doing demonis things without much more background as often happened in the scenes that are replaced in Vengeance.Besides, the fact that they physically accompany you in the battles even brings a little more cohesion and makes you get closer (even though I completed it after a True Ending run of 100% of the Canon of Creation, which was already at level 99 and... they didn't contribute much, but it's appreciated).In short, I am VERY happy that Shin Megami Tensei V has appeared outside the Switch and I find it the best version to play, without any doubt.Unfortunately,  (at least, the last 20ish hours). I did it because I love Shin Megami Tensei V and I wanted to see every nook and cranny of the story, but unfortunately, the changes are minimal and don't add much (specially in Canon of Creation).It's not just having to complete the game six times just to get the Virtual Trainer scenarios in one save data, but those virtual fights are already more than seen because you've gone through the game SIX times to get them. It's repetition, on top of repetition. And not just once, no, TWO rounds of each scenario to get both achievements.I'm really sorry, but I don't think it's something that can add to the experience or motivate you to expand the gameplay itself. Are they challenging? Yes, especially depending on what difficulty you play it on, but I would have even preferred if they had put an achievement of having to beat the game on Hard instead.Be that as it may, I love Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance and to anyone who wants to do 100%, I recommend that you do the Virtual Trainer as you get them.
