_childDocuments_.review: Just to give my background on the game before going into it, I've been playing Atlus JRPG's for over a decade now. I've completed all versions of Persona 3, Persona 4 and Persona 5. Beaten Shin Megami Tensei III: Nocturne and the original release of Shin Megami Tensei V and I've currently got a playthrough of SMT IV and Persona 2 Innocent Sin going on. I'll give the short answer first: If you love this style of game or are the type of player who will play anything, then buy it and play it. It's fantastic.Now to the long answer: This is a turn based JRPG with a set of combat rules that have existed in SMT games for their history, and if you don't like turn based strategy combat, this is not for you. Otherwise you should 100% give this game a shot. SMT games have a "Press Turn" mechanic in combat where you get 1 action for each party member, however you can get more or less actions based on what you do. If you hit a weakness or get a critical hit you get an additional action (with 4 party members you get a max of up to 8 unless something specific were to give you more). However if you use a skill of a damage type that the enemy demon blocks or they dodge your attack, then you lose one of your actions that turn. Furthermore, if you use an affinity that is either reflected back or absorbed (which heals the enemy) then you lose all remaining actions. Even moreso, all these rules applies to the opponents as well. This means for combat, especially boss fights, you need to have a somewhat of a plan (later bosses you will need a concrete plan) otherwise you will lose. These games are known for being unforgiving if you aren't prepared. If you go in blind it will take trial and error. These games will frustrate new players and this is no exception. And i absolutely love it. This game felt much harder than the base SMT V game that came out for the switch a few years ago. It definitely brought back the difficulty i felt with SMT III and i've been feeling with SMT IV that i didn't see in SMT V, and there were moments i wanted to yell, but i persevered and kept going. Now would be a good time to mention that i have 100% completed this game, getting all the achievements and beating all Super bosses. Let's start with talking about the story. The base SMT V story is still represented here in Canon of Creation. I think Canon of Creation does a fine job with telling it's story. It's weaker than the Canon of Vengeance, but it tells what it needs to. When going for 100% it can be a little daunting that the weaker of the 2 stories has 4 endings while the better story has only 2, but other than the CoC neutral ending, they all feel satisfying to finish. Like in other SMT games, it's the end of the world, and you need to travel around a desolated Tokyo to complete the game. You meet a cast of characters, with each ending being represented by another potential candidate that wants to remake the new world with their own view, ya know like the other SMT games. In this game however, the form of the person recreating the world is taken by what is called a Nahobino, which your character assumes the role of. The base plot is god sealed away the knowledge of other members of mythology in the garden of eden, and when humanity ate of the fruit, we became infused with their knowledge. These entities (Such as Odin or Zeus) are reffered to as demons and they cannot attain their true form without their knowledge. Fusions of person and demon are the Nahobino and they have similar powers to God to be able to recreate the world how they see fit.  You do quests, chase around and beat powerful demons, pick which ending you want then that's the world you would recreate. It's a fine example of SMT. I like the True Neutral ending path because they put a little more into it and the requirements to see it make you see some very challenging fights in the game that are worth seeing.Canon of Vengeance adds the Atlus classic new Female character in a "definitive edition." For this, Yoko(new girl) and Tao travel with you for a large segment of the game, and the choices you make in dialogue options will decide which of the 2 paths you will be on at the end of the game. One ending sides with Yoko and the other with Tao, play for yourself to see what each path gets you. It also adds a new evil faction to the game called the Qadistu, who's goal is to gain enough power to summon their patron god Tiamat. Your character dealing with this group instead of following the story from the base game, takes you to a brand new area exclusive to Canon of Vengeance as well, I gotta be honest, Canon of Vengeance is a breath of fresh air. I said earlier that Canon of Creation was a fine example of SMT games, but Vengeance is just so fun. The story is much more engaging, especially with your choices actually deciding your outcome versus one question near the end of the game. The Qadistu being an antagonist for a good chunk of the game is something this game needed too. In the Creation path, each area feels like it has it's own subplot for you to conquer before you just get thrown into the end game of "hey go here to beat the game." The Qadistu are relevant and causing trouble in almost every area you go, and you're working towards dealing with something they did even if they aren't in that area you happen to be in. The endings in this also feel much more thought and with more love put into them.Next I'll talk a little about gameplay. I've already talked about the main feature for these games earlier, with discussing the combat. To summarize combat, it is difficult, but satisfying. If you like to strategist and plan, then you will love the combat. My only advice is you cannot go into this like you would a game like pokemon. going into it thinking "oh i'll just have all offensive moves, and a variety of elements" is not going to win you the harder battles. Yes you need the weaknesses, but stat buffing and debuffing is a necessity in these games, especially the end game and super bosses. Other gameplay elements. Movement is really slick. This is among the best of these games for movement in my mind. I love how they designed this game as far as the Netherworld you travel in. The controls don't feel clunky in any way, and they work as intended.Design next. The netherworld is nice to navigate around. I mean it is similar to other SMT games with how the netherworld works, but it's a modern game and Atlus does a great job with details and ambiance. There are areas that seem barren and bland, but i believe that's by design. Some areas are meant to look boring so that the areas that are beautiful look even better. The new area that was added for Vengeance is absolutely gorgeous. Aesthetically the game is fantastic. Demon designs are, just like other games in the series (and Persona) are great too. Some classic designs are updated for the modern systems well, and the new designs look good as well. One of my favorite late game demons looks the best he's looked in the series. Overall good design.I'm running low on space so let me summarize my last few points really quick. Replaying the game for all endings and all achievements is miserably long. There are things they could have done to reduce the time, but they did not and it really drags on.MUSIC IS AMAZING. I listen to some of it outside of the game because it's genuinely some of the best a game has provided. But Atlus always does great with music. Final verdict: Fantastic game to play, terribly annoying to 100%

_childDocuments_.review: An exceptional JRPG that nonetheless disappoints in comparison to its potential and predecessors. There's a lot to love about SMT V, and it's important to note that my thoughts herein are strictly related to the Canon of Creation, and not the new Vengeance route. Even so, there are portions of my critique that carry through to the game's core mechanics, so it is at least my view that they are still applicable. As in prior games, the soundtrack is singularly exceptional, and a particular highlight for me throughout the game were the demon designs; they are near universally spectacular, and broad in assortment, ranging from sexy women to demonic monstrosities to abstract, alien, yet strangely familiar mimicries. The core press turn combat system is, as always, rock solid, and the first half of the game was rife with tension and satisfaction in overcoming difficulty. However, the second half of SMT V is where everything started to fall apart to me. Where Nocturne builds a constant atmosphere of dread with tinges of a strangely punk style of irreverence, V feels very unfocused in this regard, with its aim seeming to sway from one arc to the next. By the time Nocturne ultimately ceded to the genre's near-universal staples of self-actualization in its theming, it had build a world you felt well and truly accomplished for having mastering; by contrast, the additions made to V's combat left it feeling much easier in comparison, and thus both less memorable and less effective in its narrative weight. I got through all but two of the fights in the game- both superbosses- by relying on the default auto-crit Magatsuhi ability and a high-Phys build. My tactics never needed to change, and as such, I was bored far more often than not, especially near the end. There are character arcs delicately built in the background that reach abrupt ends without catharsis. What, at first, seems a net of relationships devolves into nothing at all by the midway point. You can make decisions that radically affect a character's fate, and ought to affect those around them, yet never a comment is made, as though they were forgotten about entirely. It makes an already disintegrating strength feel slipshod and lucky during the few times where it manages to hit. I say all this, but I wish to stress that I most definitely enjoy this game, and feel it was worth every penny put in. However, there are simply too many stumbles for me to say that it realizes its own possibility, and, especially in comparison to Nocturne, it's sadly simply inferior.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought the game again since I already experienced the vanilla game back in 2021 on the switch and playing it is like night and day.So far I have gotten done with area 1 of Vengeance and I can say the story shift up is very insane. The characters feels much more fleshed out compared to how they were written in the vanilla, the writing as well outside of the characters also feels very well done this time around.The additions with Yoko and the Qadistu is also good and I love how they play so far in the story. With new music arrangements, I can say I’m extremely pleased how they are ingame when you battle. The reguler battle theme getting a total new remix is so nice.For the gameplay itself, it’s also extremely engaging where you have to think what demons you need to bring, trials and errors up against bosses and so much more. The addition as well with unique magatsuki skills from different demon races is also a welcome addition that spices up the strategizing how one can approach for the tune-based gameplay.For Quality of life improvements, there were quite a lot that peeked my curiosity and that I was very happy about.The addition to bring back demons from their starting level in the compendium is super good addition, it helps out players to lower the cost of macca they would have to spend and they can rather use grimoires to get back said demon to level to get all the skills again. Love it so much.The sky view I also enjoy, but I also have some issues about it in which I will talk about later below.The magatsuhi rails is a welcome addition to speed up going to different areas again where players can go.More new demon navigators is also a nice addition rather than having to use Amanozako all the time in the vanilla game.Saving whenever you want is such a welcome addition, so this time you don’t have to go back to a leyline fount in order to save.Now, over about what I do not like about the game of what I’ve played and seen so far.For the QoL as I mentioned above of the sky view — while I like it, it also ruins the purpose of the abscess in the game in which they served a purpose in the vanilla game to be cleared out to reveal the rest of the map. This added a sense of exploration for players to find it to clear it out as soon as possible, but as well to get new miracles. Now their only purpose is serving for people to get it done over with to obtain said miracles, but loses out that they don’t cover the map anymore which sucks.That aside I don’t think there’s much that I dislike about the game.For those who wants tldr then here it is;- Good story and characters are more fleshed out- Very engaging gameplay- QoL is very good and saving anywhere is so GOOD- New music arrangements are extremely well doneCons- Sky view makes abscess lose their whole purpose- If you don’t like turn-based gameplay or to think out strategies, then the game isn’t for you.- You will die a lot (Might be a con if one doesn’t like that, but trial and errors is also part of its charm)Overall a solid 9/10 to me in my own personal opinion. Would highly recommend it for those who loves JRPGs.There might be some stuff I missed while writing my personal review, but so far I enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm nowhere close to being done with this game, but I think I've got a good idea of what I think of it.I was never willing to continue the original release of this game on Switch, mainly due to that I knew that the horrendous Switch hardware was holding the game back. When I heard that it would be getting an enhanced version that would be coming to other consoles, including to Steam, I was extremely excited. So far, it hasn't disappointed. SMT V is a very fun game. It feels like it takes just about every problem that I have with Nocturne and addresses them. The QoL changes that they made are especially great, such as being able to save wherever you want instead of exclusively at Leyline Founts. It saves so much time and doesn't leave you with the fear of losing literal hours of progress because you ran into a battle that you weren't properly equipped for (Nocturne). The game's also decently challenging without most of what made Nocturne so unfun to play. And this is my impression from most of my time being spent in the original story path, I've barely even started on the Vengeance one. It also goes without saying, but the game looks great and it's extremely satisfying to see it on a platform that can properly show it.Of course, it's not flawless. There are some issues, namely story, characters, some of the voice acting feels a little off, etc. But to be honest, I usually prioritize gameplay first when it comes to what I'm looking for in a game. Plus, not many SMT games do a very good job with story or characters anyway.And the best part, it's not tainted by Atlus's insistence of P5'ing just about everything they're working on nowadays. With all of Atlus's screw ups in the previous few years (lackluster Nocturne remaster, botched P3P port, failure to move on from Persona 5, ruining Persona 3's identity with Reload) I don't see myself enjoying an Atlus game this much for a long while. So I'm going to enjoy it while I can.

Me dying to random demons is actually quite common like wtf. First thing first I have no idea if there's any major changes in Canon of Creation(CoC) side of story. _childDocuments_.review: My Final Review of SMTV:Gameplay:Shin Megami Tensei V shines with its large Creature/Demon Database and Fusion system.All Demons have a very detailed Art style and with some you can form a great relationship (Jack Frost being one of my favorites).The Turn based Battle system is stasifying and allows variety, however lacks depth at later stages.The Story of SMTV is mid at best and doesn't reinvent anything, the human characters featured have different personality traits which will show especially at later stages of the game. Some characters can be lovely and others are straight up annoying. (Dazai being the absolute clown.)Often the game will throw choices at you that you have to make, however this is just the illusion of making decision and having choices but the outcome is linear scripted.Audio:The Soundtrack and general audio in the game is a mixed bag.IMO the best tunes are featured in Shinjuku and afterwards, especially the Boss or Elite battles have a "get pumped up" tune.On the other side you have total nosense of a soundtrack when you encounter a Mitama Blop.Dialogues in the Game dont feature a proper voice over and you just get short hints of the characters overall mood.Only the Cutscenes which are very nice to look at feature a full voice over.Level Design:The Level Design is the biggest upset of this whole game and one of the major reasons i downvote SMTV.After around 15 hours i was already tired of walking through the endless deserts, the Landscape looks bland and boring, the "Fairy Village" being the most detailed and prettiest area of the whole game that i've encountered.It also doesn't get any better later on in the game, you are thrown into dungeon after dungeon with similar assets and make your way through a maze. This happens 3 times in the Game.It feels like the game designers ran out of ideas which is a absolute shame and leaves lots of potential on the table.Overall the Level Design poor, somewhat better as in  "Digimon Cyber Sleuth".Summary:The Game pulled me in with its large Demon database and fusion system but that was the only gameplay aspect that kept me hooked until the end of my playthrough.The Cutscenes were nice too look at and some of the battles were quite nice.Overall i can not recommend this game for its story, graphics or level design.Personally would have wished for more QoL improvements since this game was originally released on N-switch.Original Review:I've been playing SMT V for a week now. Around 40 hours into the game and encountered the Quadistus, keep dying there cause I run out of Chakra drops.Now iam forced to farm Chakra to continue with the story and I can't even buy those at the merchant.The games Story is very mid, soundtrack is OK and mostly shines in shinjuku.Annoying that dialogues don't feature full voice over, only cutscenes have voice over.The navigator in game can't be muted "hee ho hee ho" what is funny at first can give you a headache later on when traveling through the bland, empty looking landscape which I was already tired of after 15 hours.Overall my experience has been quite disappointing, I like the battles and fusion part and the amount of demons the game features but that's the only aspect they nailed, although combat could be more in depth.Every other aspect of this game seems to be low standard. This was not my first J-RPG, I had a great time with "Yakuza like a dragon" and "Jade Cocoon" back on PSX which was also a monster/creature taming game.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely adored the original and Vengeance has added so much more to the game, not only with quests and demons but added quality of life features like Uncapped FPS and new overworld elements. Also you have the option of playing the original which is not what I was expecting. Really cool to see. For you JRPG fans who haven't played a MegaTen game. The turn based combat is addicting thanks to the Press Turn System. the combinations of new party members you can gain through Demon fusion will keep you slamming those monstrosities together time and time again.Even the overworld traversal is fun, thanks to the in built ice skates the protagonist has. _childDocuments_.review: The game is great, I'm a big fan of megaten games, and I did appreciate the original for the nintendo switch despite some of his flaws. Honestly this game is a must have if you're a fan of megaten games, and it's a fantastic game even if you're not into them. I'm not gonna comment on the artstyle or music, because they are incredible. I have no negative comment on this game except for(Rant ahead, be careful)The localization. The italian localization is heinous. I would not care if there was a direct and immediate option to change language, but there isn't and I was forced to use it. Now what could be wrong with it?First of all is full of typos. It's ok to have some typos in your localization, but this is FULL of typos. Dialogue with a random NPC? Typos. Touching cutscene? Typos.ONE OF THE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ IMPORTANT  STORY CHOICES GOT A TYPO. You know, the few, very important choices, the one your ending depends on? The one floating in the air? They got a typo even there. And the best part, is I'm fairly sure they translated from a translated localization. In said choices, when you hover on the other one, you can see the unselected dialogue, float. Well, in this case, the unselected dialogue is in ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ French. I think they directly just translated very poorly the french edition and called it done, but they forgot to change the text of the important choices. If this is not enough, we also have untraslated items and, my favourite, the magnificent string modifcator character left in the dialogue. Yes there is a character in the italian localization who says something like "%d %d /n" and the dialogue is all bugged and pops out of the regular textbox. Also, something that made me really mad and confirms this half assed work, was Mastema's passive skill translation. For those who don't know, in English is called "Crime and Punishment". Even stones know that, "Crime and Punishment" is a Dostoevskij's book, probably his most famous too. In italian it's alwyas has been translated as "Delitto and Castigo", in the game, obviously, was traslated as "Crimine e Castigo" which is the translation of the english title and completely misses the reference. Honestly this is not a problem of the game itself, but I have never seen a worse localization in my life, and I have seen tons of bad localizated games. I wish I could just switch to a different language, but you can't choose it neither in the options or when you start a new game. I know people like when a new game has a localization in their language, but if it's something done so poorly, with errors everywhere, forgotten untranslated text in multiple different languages, misses references, I would prefer not have it at all.

_childDocuments_.review: im pretty big on this series. tbh it would be much quicker to name all the mainline games i haven't played than those i have (bc there's literally only smt nine left lol)tl;dr i can't recommend this game enough. if you wanna get into mainline smt, this is the game to do it. just make sure you take the girl's hand at the start to do the new campaign (Canon of Vengeance) and avoid the old, worse one (Canon of Creation)when i first played smtv on release, i thought "man, the gameplay was great, but my god was that story bad", so when i learned about smtvv having a new campaign, i was cautiously optimistic that they'd actually listen to feedback and make some improvements. did that happen? overall, absolutely. i still have some nitpicks and a few issues with how things played out (namely, quite a few story moments feel as if they're saying "hey, look, we changed this thing, aren't you shocked??" in a way that clearly makes it seem that they're pandering to old fans while making newer fans just be like "why is this scene structured like this?"). however, the new story is definitely how this game should have been in the first place.there are two new endings to this game, and like nearly every other game in the series, the game slots you into either law or chaos based on your actions throughout the game (there's no neutral, but to my knowledge, if you ARE neutral aligned, you are given a choice between the two, like in SMT2 and Strange Journey. dont quote me on that, i was too far aligned on one side for this choice to show up).i ended up chaos aligned, and i'm overall pretty content with my ending. law and chaos feel much different in this game than the usual. usually, if you side with law, you're just upholding god's rule, and if you're chaos, you're siding with demon supremacy. this time around, law represents , whereas chaos represents .basically, both endings seem actually pretty decent, although tbh the law end has me a bit put off (i guess that's why the game figured i should go chaos lol). i hate to bring up persona in an smt review, but it actually makes sense here; the new law ending really feels like : . the new chaos gives me a more hopeful feeling with it brimming with possibility despite the fact that to get that ending, you generally need to make more pessimistic choices.as for characters, they do a really good job expanding on the base cast (and with the new character yoko). yuzuru is an actual person now and has lots of presence, dazai's weird edgy character arc isn't his focus anymore (at least until the very end), tao is now the law heroine and thus acts as a deutoragonist along with yoko (the chaos heroine), aogami feels like a bigger presence and ally instead of just hanging around saying "young man, we share a soul, so i think you're cool", yakumo gets much more expansion (as he should, people now get to understand how based he is, considering the original story leaves his ideology mostly implicit and not overt. somehow people think he's some supremacist fascist with no care for humanity, when his whole ideology is based around helping people grow), and koshimizu feels like such a bro all throughout (even without considering ).this game also really benefits from having a main antagonist. the original felt disconnected in its storytelling, but now, the qadistu actually provide a coherent threat that keeps the whole story connected. no more just being told by bethel "go do this", now, the MC-tao-yoko squad are basically the "qadistu execution squad", so what you do in the story actually feels natural.gameplay was also massively improved. i was surprised with how much the new additions benefited the game. i always thought the base game was nearly flawless from a gameplay standpoint, but with all the new stuff here, i can never imagine myself going back (not like there even would be a reason to lol).anyways, great game, goty 2024.

name: I Am Your Beast
detailed_description: More Strange Scaffold About the Game I Am Your Beast is a shortform covert revenge thriller FPS about getting hunted across the North American wilderness by the military-industrial complex — and turning the tables. You are secret agent Alphonse Harding. Retired for six years, you've been asked to complete ‘one last job’, one too many times. Declining your latest mission sets in motion a furious guerilla war between you and the Covert Operations Initiative (COI) that litters the forest with bodies and bullet casings. Break your opponents. Use their own equipment against them. Duck into your tunnel network before enemy forces zero in on your location. Repeat. Features Lightning-fast 'he's-in-the-walls' player fantasy, complete with superhuman tree climbing and head explosions. Fully voiced story campaign with 20+ levels. Lush comic book-inspired art style. Chase side objectives while getting the fastest times possible in replayable micro-sandboxes. Wield pistols, sniper rifles, bear traps, and more. Heart-slamming soundtrack from award-winning composer RJ Lake (Space Warlord Organ Trading Simulator, Unbeatable, El Paso, Elsewhere). Innovative 'kinetic typography' cutscene system.

_childDocuments_.review: This is for you low-skill gamers out there.Do you look at difficult games like this and say Elden Ring or even something like Blasphemous and go "I wish they made those for me..."   This one.... kinda is almost like a high-skill game for low-skill gamers.   Why?Everything makes you FEEL like a badass.  The fact that the levels are so quick you spend so much more time failing than you do succeeding but...your brain like forgets all of your failure. You just keep going. Everything feels so smooth and so fun and you just keep ripping through bad guys. It makes failure fun in a way because you just get another crack at the bad guys you want to keep killing.  It makes us low-skill gamers feel like we're doing really tough maneuvers when in reality its all about quickness and steady progress via repetition.  Theres no procedural or rogue-like development here you just are what you are, shaving off seconds from a hand crafted level built to perfection. The way gaming used to be.  But with all the cool visuals, tactile responsiveness, and music you want from a hot new title.TLDR: Theres lots of indy action titles that come out every year but theres been a handful last decade or so that stood out: Hades, Ultrakill, Risk of Rain 1 and 2, etc... this belongs with that conversation.  A++

_childDocuments_.review: (GOTY 2024. Original "pre-review" kept for posterity, detailed pros and cons at the bottom.)Dear Diary...I have a huge backlog. As a result, I don't usually buy games that aren't on sale or are over a tenner unless they're a Doom or Command & Conquer game, or a spiritual successor by the same developers. To get me to buy your game, you usually have to convince me that it won't sit in my backlog for 5+ years or be so cheap that it might as well be free. However, I bought this game more or less blind, not knowing what it really was other than an FPS with a cool art style with interestingly low system requirements. I've only played I Am Your Beast for 20 minutes and I'm terrible but I can tell that I'll get better and that it will turn out to be an incredibly special game for me.That intro and first couple of levels were exactly what I needed from a psychological, nay, an *emotional* perspective at this brief juncture in my personal life. It was worth the money just for that. The game has already done its job for me. I will play it to 100% completion and edit this review accordingly, but for now, it's time to go and be The Beast in the real world.I get that this isn't a real review and isn't the most helpful for potential "customers", but I want to thank the developers for that wonderful demonstration of the value of games as an art form. My first impression "review": it's essentially first-person Hotline Miami with a health bar that takes place in wide open areas, but holy **** these developers know how to do an introduction.Update on my personal bollocks if you care: Mission accomplished irl. I did what needed to be done months ago, or at least got the ball rolling. Happy Halloween. Thank you dev! "I am your ♥♥♥♥. You should be ashamed of what you have eaten." ROCK N ROLL... Positives:- The music is ace, 10/10.- I enjoy the progression, although some may not. The game demands that the player improves as they make their way through the game, so you are sometimes expected to go back to previous levels to achieve higher scores or complete bonus objectives before the next level and/or cutscene unlocks. The reason I enjoy this is that it forces the player to play levels that they previously found difficult, only for it to be shown to them how much they've improved by getting the satisfaction of utterly wrecking a level that used to be a hurdle. I wouldn't have got a single S-rank if this wasn't here, and it felt amazing.- From about a third of the way through the story, you begin to have options on how to approach combat scenarios. These options never include stealth, but direction of approach, combat style or even often (but not always) running straight past enemies.- The story is engaging and compliments the gameplay, which is one big power trip but with an artistic purpose to said power trip. If you have a thing for government conspiracy theories, this one's for you.Neutral:- Lots of adrenaline. I can only play this sorta thing for an hour or so at a time, but 10 years ago back when I still had a soul I would've lapped it up.- Main story missions will take around 4h but it really tests your FPS skill. I'd say that I'm a slightly above average FPS player, so make of that what you will. So kinda short, but honestly it's quality over quantity here and there is ZERO padding. There's plenty of postgame content, including challenges, which look like it could take a completionist around 20h. Beating only the main story will unlock all but two achievements. Negatives:- The AI is terrible when it's not scripted. Terrible to the point where it's so bad that they don't do what you'd expect if you've played other games with mid AI. The AI genuinely surprises you with how bad it is. I don't think it's programmed to try and hunt you down when left to its own devices, and if it is then it's very bad at it. This is obviously one of the reasons for the incredibly low system requirements, and having done some research on the dev and their other games, I think those requirements were a challenge that they set for themselves.- Collision is a bit janky sometimes. I've fallen through the floor once and got stuck on a climbable cliff. I've been stuck on geometry (such as between rocks) 3-4 times.Final thoughts:10/10 from an artistic perspective, 7/10 for gameplay mainly due to what happens to the AI once they're free from their scripted actions. But 10/10 overall because I'm INFJ as hell. I Am Your Beast is my GOTY 2024, partly because it symbolises my personal experience of 2024 perfectly. My heart thanks these devs.

_childDocuments_.review: I watched the 10 minute demo gameplay by ABG, and as soon as I saw the tutorial, I was hooked. I played the demo, finished it, immediately wishlisted. Release date came, and I ran through the story like a madman, and replayed it 3 times more only to stream it to all my friends (and flaunt some of my skill  while I was at that). Hoped to write a review after getting platinum, but the mission failed spectacularly. It’s just  not to write a review as soon as possible.It is a disgustingly beautiful, jaw-dropping endless kill spree, and damn, it feels so cathartic. The military machine grinded your soul to the pulp and now asks for another bite? Why not break its jaw while you blast and stomp through your former colleagues. Well, .But that’s not all to I AM YOUR BEAST. This game is a masterclass in how less makes so, so much more. Its brevity and snappines shows how restrictions make room for creativity and uniqueness. And the depth this game achieves in so many of its aspects and systems is way more than many AAA projects aspire to get with all their details and vastness.Visuals is what gets you first. Typical comic style with heavy stylisation: saturated blood, angular muzzle flashes, red crosses to mark a landed hit. Limited color palette, sharp shadows, thin lines. The artstyle sets everything happening in place, gives actions and objects priority, accentuating elements meticulously and setting its own rhythm. It stimulates, and it eases your eyes, never letting you tire of an endless bloodbath.How can you possibly tire of it, when the core loop is so addictive in its feverish speed? . The devil lies in the details: the enemy is overwhelming, but the player character is so much more savvy and skilled, yet not invincible. The controls are snappy and so smooth. It feels amazing to quick-press them in succession. Fling a branch towards an enemy, stomp their head while grabbing their gun on the fly, then land several headshots while running for your life. It seems the enemy agents too just can’t get enough of Harding’s skill, sometimes all they can do is shout in awe and disbelief: Every level is ranked, and the rank depends on your speed and style. The snappier and faster you play and the closer the seconds spend on the level to none, the higher the rank you get. Due to the brevity of every hand-crafted level, you don’t seem to notice failure. The learning curve is so smooth, you feel inclined to polish every level before you move on to the next. You just do it again, and again, and again, all the while experimenting with your approach. Just to shave off some of the seconds on the timer, even if the S-rank has already been reached 2, 3 or 4 hours ago. It is the most addicting thing, and I just can’t get enough of it.And it is hard to notice that you’ve been beating your own record for hours non-stop. And it is increasingly hard, when the soundtrack is so adrenaline-pumping and keeps progressing with every try, keeps escalating, and escalating. Until you become one with it and the game becomes a rhythm-shooter, and the S-rank is underway, and you’ve beat your own record for 0,24 seconds, then 1,76, then whole 3,41 past last rank.The soundtrack is hard to describe. It’s nostalgic and modern in a way, as if a beatmaker sampled old arcades on a track, and then a rave DJ splashed some tecnomantic experimental scratching into the mix. It is stylish, it is ideal for chaotic combat, and very clever in its progression. Every track puts you into combat flow immediately, but stays in your memory for long.The soundtrack accompanies not only the combat levels, but also the hard-hitting intermissions. Every story level is split up by radio banter. Nothing extra: no portraits, no animated scenes. Only plain background and bold text appearing word by word in rhythm with the voiced lines. And the voice acting is magnificent, one of the best in action game history to date.The writing itself is matching the voice acting. Everything most delicious, witty and sharp from the thriller genre is compressed into every line spoken. It’s down to earth, but highly quotable. And extremely soulful. You feel for Harding. His humor is dry and deadpan. Its delivery is spontaneous and sudden, but very welcome. And while his boss may talk like your stereotypical thriller antagonist, with the monologues about “honor” and “duty” and whatnot, the confrontation with him doesn’t feel like it. No, it feels more personal. As if you’re talking to your ass-of-a-superior, who wants you to work on your sick leave without pay. “We went fishing together!” or “You’ve held my son” and other types of gaslighting, guilttripping and gatekeeping (no girlbossing though) you into working overtime so that he can earn a dime more for your hard work.The strength of the narrative is not only in the confrontations. Every scene and story beat just hit the right mark in their brevity and cleanliness. Be it a sudden contact with a promising ally, who’s yet to become your mole in the ranks of the agency, or the scene of Harding painfully hitting rock bottom (quite literally). Not only that, every dialogue feels fresh and surprising.The context is just barely enough. The small details and tidbits are sparse and always in their place. We are plunged into the scene fast, and abruptly taken out with just enough new information to keep yearning for more. Nothing extra is given, so when some detail slips from characters’ tongues, you feel as if you’ve just experienced a new and exiting twist. And all of that happens in two-or-three brief lines. You can’t even feel that most of the characters don't subvert their tropes. And that doesn’t matter, because when the only subversion turns into a twist, it feels like a slap on the face. Well, the good kind of a slap.Because it’s gut-wrenching, heart-stopping and so full of life. It’s nervous, it’s filled with sudden realization, then helplessness, then hope, then denial… And relief. You don’t even know what to do, when the hardest hitting line comes to the screen:And it’s genius in how long it might fill your screen. Just long enough for you to feel the need to act, and then stay confused that if you do, then… the only course of action is… something you cannot fathom to do, something… Might this work? Oh.And the whole arc of revenge culminates spectacularly. As cathartically, as it felt throughout the whole gameplay.And only with the aftertaste the realization comes, in how witty and clever the story is in what is left unsaid, unnoticed at first. How the metaphor of a Beast gradually becomes so much more to only be fitting the conventions of the thriller genre. So much fuller, so much deeper, so much more close to your heart than it is comfortable. So much more than the addictive gameplay and killer of a story. So much more than the characters that are so typical yet so alive.It will come off as cheesy, but…

_childDocuments_.review: I love games like I Am Your Beast. I'm a big fan of speedrun modes or time attack, i'm a fan of well made mechanics and i'm a fan of very good voice acting. For one exception in gameplay, this here has it all. The "cutscenes", albeit just voice clips, are so well made and feel very natural to listen to, while the gameplay offers you little sandbox levels to experiment and maximize your time bonus, your path and your used equipment.Enemies act predictably, albeit stupid if they can't find a weapon in a level, which makes them stand in the level doing literally nothing. But for a game like this, it's what you want. The hazards, which can be turned against either side, are clearly visible and it all feels deterministic. Some challenges are stupid, but a nice time killer. The auto-aim makes running through a level and headshotting people so enjoyable, but which also makes the "ADS", which really is just canted aiming, pretty useles aside from the sniper rifle.The story is pretty over the top, while, as i said, the story cutscenes inbetween were really enjoyable, kudos to the actors.I only have two issues that i kept facing: In a fast-paced moment picking up the right item or using the right mission objective can be hard, even when directly looking at it and barrels that are visibly partially obstructed can't be shot at, even if you have a clear line of fire.Other than that, i can wholeheartedly recommend it, even if it has a lil jank in it. You will have a nice time.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: 9.5/10. Amazing game, cheap, underrated af, go get it.Today I 100%'d , a game by . I've never had played a game from them before but let me tell you, they did a fine first impression. The game reminds me of the frantic pace of  mixed with the gameplay from , with a little bit of : Go fast, kill everyone as stylishly as you can and reach the goal. The game will give you an A, and show you how close you are to getting an S rank. You feel like you can do better, because you know you can, so you try again. This time, the game proposes a challenge. It's usually a hint on how to do the mission faster and... well, better. Sometimes it's just something fun. You do it, and get a new perspective. You retry and do better. You play again. And again. Until you get that S rank. Yet you know you can do better...The story is better than I expected. I just didn't expect much. Without going into spoilers, you play as Alphonse Harding, ex-COI. You're done ending lives, many times innocent lives, just so some 1% can fill their already filled pockets with some more cash. Five one-last-jobs later, your ex-General Burkin asks you once again for your skills. You decide enough is enough and defend your dignity and humanity by the skin of your teeth. Whatever it takes. The story feels like it's a cliché, but I feel as if it's meant to be like that. You're supposed to feel like a character such as Rambo, and the game does a good job at that. I know I'm not the best shot. I'd say I'm very subpar when it comes to skill  but the game helps a lot by having some auto-aim, enabling most people to run and gun effortlessly, as the lore-accurate Harding would. It's a choice I feel some people won't agree with, but for the sake of immersion and fun, I'm all for it. I digress. It's easy to feel empathy with the presented characters, and while the game has some acid humor, it's not the main point.The art style reminds me a lot of . The snowy landscapes, the cyan, orange, magenta gradient skies, hand-painted textures... Both games made to feel like a comic book, and while  takes this art style and gives it a more somber, cozy, lonesome, dare I say realistic direction,  simply won't allow the cozyness to settle in. You've got a huge, snow white canvas waiting to be painted red. The sound design is very good. The gunshots sound amazing and satisfying and while they play a HUGE part in a first person shooter, I have to give kudos to the voice acting and the music. The VAs did a great job in this game: , the creative director AND Harding's voice actor does an amazing job at making the character feel natural, and while he whispers a lot, as a lone character talking to himself would, the lines are delivered quite clearly. I personally love the little whispers of "Yeah...", "Alright..." when you complete an objective. It's a neat way of notifying the player diegetically that the objective was completed. The soundtrack, by , is top notch. It fits the general style of the game very well, it's stylish all throughout, it's beautifully calm when it needs to be, and it's very energetic when the game demands, with a neat little addition of a simple dynamic BGM system. The overall art direction fits the game very well.Give this game a shot. It's not that expensive and you'll get a lot of replayability from this one. It's very well made, and the genre of movement shooter is right up my alley, so if you like action packed games, movement shooters, first person shooters, this is a must buy. If you don't enjoy FPSs that much or you're not too fond of movement shooters, I would still recommend you give this one a try. The game never forces you to play at peak performance, it's a satifying experience.My only serious complaints about the game would need to be the climbing/parkour mechanic, as a game dev I understand it's hard to make something like that as smooth as possible, but in a game with such tight control and gameplay, it's a shame I sometimes get stuck in a climbable ledge, or fall through a rope. That and the fact the fact that the weapon and item pick up button is the same as the interact button. Finishing a level just to be denied of actually ending it just for me to realize I picked up a herb or a weapon instead of interacting with a laptop is something that happened more than once, and while I'd usually say it's a skill issue from me (I'm not denying that though), objective laptops are usually filled with armor, health and weapons around, so it's easy to pick them up by accident instead of doing the objective.I 100% the game in 11 hours and 30 minutes of gameplay, but I basically ate the levels. I'm not that good, so if you're a pro gamer, you can probably 100% it in around 9 hours or less. Though I don't think I'm fully done...
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: An instantly enjoyable, extremely well scoped blend of fast paced gameplay that just feels fantastic to blaze through, especially if you enjoy a good FPS challenge with no bloat,If you have enjoyed Neon White and/or Hotline Miami, I Am Your Beast will absolutely scratch this itch in a refreshing format. The game features a highly surprising amount of (bangin') music, and really well executed voice acted scenes that absolutely set the scene without overstaying their welcome.As a game developer myself - I Am Your Beast did, probably more than any other game this year, made me remind myself that we need to make more smaller games with an extremely tight game loop, as this is a brilliant example of one such experience.Don't miss it!
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal storytelling, game flow, movement, and iconography, in this narrative arcade-y FPS. Mix the comic book stylings of XIII, the gun-fu of John Wick, improv weapon play of Hotline Miami, and critical commentary on the American military industrial complex like of Rambo, and then you have I AM YOUR BEAST. Each gun or weapon feels good to play with or chuck at your red eye goggled soldiers. Alphonse Harding's quest to live a life of bird-watching and whittling as he refuses to be called in for one last job at the behest of the American government to destabilise an impoverised developing nation is particularly satisfying. Delivered through bold screen-filling text with a forest-y background, colours denoting the mood and characters, with fantastic voice acting by Xalavier Nelson Jr (also game director) and voice direction by RJ Lake. Brandon Jenkins as Byron is also particularly good and the twists and turns between Alphonse and Byron's relationship is again quite satisfying. Jim Brown and Kevin Ribeiro's level design sings in the more open areas where they're effectively playgrounds, as you zoom past various weapons and tools to deliver stylish kills. There are 26 levels and most are a couple minutes long, but they're highly replayable for bonus objectives and getting higher ranks. There are also challenge levels if you're particularly great at S-ranks, of which I'm not! Not a fan of rank-gating some of the campaign levels, particularly the last few levels require you to get an S rank on a level (I'd recommend level 7). Another gripe I almost had was the aerial takedowns were hard to nail but then you can just press the disarm or attack button to home in on the enemies' heads. Otherwise, it's a great stylish romp through the American pacific northwest, and one of the best games of the year.
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: By far the best John Wick Simulator money can buy for 20 bucks. There is so much fun to be had here.Easily one of the best games I've played in a long time. You will find it impossible not to feel incredibly stylish while you dance through these levels backed by an infectious soundtrack from RJ LakeStory-wise, there are amazing performances from a small cast. Guffaw worthy dialogue from the main characters as well as the soldiers you encounter, not to mention the hilarious stunts you can pull while clearing out enemies. Whether you're barreling through a ravine of dudes with music blasting or taking in one of the audio cut-scenes between levels, you will be enthralled by this game's undeniable charm.If you like tight, frenetic gunplay with an emphasis on movement and style in a well-priced package, look no further than Strange Scaffold's I AM YOUR BEAST. Plenty of replay value with the bonus objectives and challenges that are unlocked as you complete the main story missions. The devs have promised free new levels, among other things, with the road map, so there's already more coming soon!
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece 1: The are style of the game kinda reminds of Neon White, while also adding in it's own twist to it.2: The game play feels incredible smooth once you get the hang of it.3: I personally love a good story, and this game has one of the coolest and most fascinating stories I've ever heard.4: Plus there are so many different paths you can take to playing a level that it adds so much replayability to each level.One thing I would love to see added to this game would be a level designer, and even a level designer can't be added I will replay this game till the day I die.Overall I would 100% recommend this game to everyone I know, it's worth however much I spent on it (I bought this game without looking at the price tbh)edit: Now having a hundred percented the game I now realize how perfectly crafted every level is to give you that feeling that you are truly a one man army. But I don't like how some of the bonus level you get are extremely linear not really giving you that feeling of you figured out the optimal way of doing the level. Honestly though that is just a small gripe I have with some of these levels.
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: This gameeeee is excellent. The "game soup" of it is 50% Hotline Miami 50% Neon White, which makes for a frenetic and challenging soup which champions quick decisions, spacial awareness, and y'know... doing dope ♥♥♥♥. I Am Your Beast is very TIGHT, it has a lot of verbs and they all connect to each other in fun and dynamic ways. While there aren't Leaderboards for now (the devs said maybe if everyone buys this game which they should hehe) with some levels being locked behind S ranks there's plenty of built-in reasons to put in the planning and attempts required to hit reach an S rank.Surprisingly for this genre, less surprising if you know Strange Scaffold, the story is excellent (and again, very tight). Charming, a little bit serious but also small enough in scope to not be *too* serious, and well acted, when its moments come together they hit and work as framing for why each level is the way it is.All that to say, if this looks like a game you'd like, you'll like it. It's what it looks like, it does it extremely well, and there's plenty to justify the price (especially if we get leaderboards down the line).

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played 30 minutes so far, and the only complaint is that I wish there was a next level button after beating a level. I understand the point is to replay a level until you master it, but personally, I like to finish levels, and then come back to 100% the level.After another ~20 minutes of gameplay, I realize the game is set on making you master a level as soon as you unlock it, as progression becomes locked behind getting a low enough time on levels, so far it appears you're not forced to perfect specific levels, but whether that continues remains to be seen.I have finished the story mode and gotten most levels up to at least A-tier, and for the love of god, Strange Scaffold, let me buy the soundtrack PLEASE. I am BEGGING.While I'm going to keep editing this review to share my concerns, this is not a game I plan on refunding at all, the weapons feel really good, and replayability is literally built into the design of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people are comparing this game to Neon White. They shouldn't be.Yes, this game has you kill a set number of enemies with an emphasis on speed, but other than that, it is nothing like Neon White. While Neon White is more like a first-person puzzle game/platformer, I Am Your Beast is a first-person shooter without any ambiguity.Now that that's out of the way, let's talk about the game! I Am Your Beast is a pretty good game with solid gunplay and GREAT music! The voice acting is also top notch, both in-game and during cutscenes. Though the cutscenes are quite minimal in presentation, the performances alone make up for it.Let's talk about the bad, now. The story, while interesting, feels like it finishes much too early. It's disappointing because it is quite interesting and has some likable characters. For the gameplay, you will VERY often times find yourself looking for the last enemy. The mini-map mediates this problem to a certain extent, but it's not a perfect solution. Additionally, when you get kills, the game has impact shakes that stop the game for half a second. While they do add to the dopamine rush you get from clicking heads, they sometimes break the flow and leave you overcorrecting.All in all, I Am Your Beast is a good game that could do with some further polishing in both story and gameplay and a way for me to inject the soundtrack directly into my veins.
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: If the premise of I Am Your Beast is to make the player feel like a beast, then it succeeds on all marks. While it may not be clear from the tutorial, once you find your rhythm and understand the playground of tools at your disposal to chain together the most outrageous combination swapping between equipment and weapons to chain a fluid and smooth series of kills all while spinting, jumping, and climbing your way around the level with ease. It's incredibly addicting to get S tier on every level through trial and error and through sheer determination. If you liked Neon White this game is going to be your GOTY

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down the best action game I've played in *years*.I've enjoyed El Paso, Elsewhere from Strange Scaffold greatly in the past, but this game is on a whole 'nother level.The difficulty is masterfully tuned and strikes a perfect balance between the extremes of too boring and too frustrating - it is neither, it is simply very, very fun, and presents a decent challenge with a good variety of level goals and restrictions, a decently sized arsenal of weapons and a good selection of enemy types to shoot with those guns.My heart's feeling things I thought were never to be felt again after I beat Hotline Miami for the first time.The sound design and the music are a standout, the visuals are gorgeously stylish - this game has everything.And it's only 2-3 GBs of storage space to boot!!!!Don't read anything else, just go and buy it already.

_childDocuments_.review: I Am Your Beast is a very fun first person shooter about revenge and survival. You play as Harding, a retired secret services agent, who has been summoned by Berkins. But you refuse. What follows is Burkins trying to kill you in the forest you call your home. The voice acting in this game is immaculate, the story itself is great and has nice thriller elements to it, and the gameplay feels smooth and responsive. The comic book-like art style fits the vibes of the game very well. The only semi-negative thing I have to note as someone who’s bad at FPS games is that story progression is locked behind performance in the levels (e.g. you need an A-rank in at least 3 levels to proceed) but the game is forgiving enough that achieving it was not too hard. I like the (non-canon) challenge levels, at least the ones I have unlocked so far, and overall this is a very well-polished game. I am very glad I played this game in February’s Steam Next Fest. Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I came for the voice acting, and I instantly  the game. I finished story mode in one evening, then decided to return later to try for some S Ranks, and have  it ever since. As a fast-paced FPS, it's a good game, but it truly shines as a , where you must find ways to optimize your deadly path through each level, creating a truly cinematic experience in process.I'd like to applaud the developers for requiring some A Ranks and one S Rank to progress the story — players really should be forced to experience the game's true depth at least a bit. It might have earned you a negative review, but hey, there are always unavoidable casualties.I still need to get a couple of S Ranks in the story levels and look forward to tackling the untouched challenge levels. So much fun in such a small game!Huge thanks to the developers for addressing my very peculiar bug.I promised to comment on the recent video recording feature, and it works as intended: it records the video of a run and saves it. Personally, I'd prefer mp4 over webm as the video container, but if there are reasons to stick with webm, so be it.Oh, and yes, the voice acting and writing are fantastic — like, AAA-grade, like, Hades-grade — like, -grade :). _childDocuments_.review: So there I was, thinking I could sneak through the woods and set a few bear traps like some kind of secret agent MacGyver. Next thing I know, everything’s on fire, enemies are swarming from every direction, and I’ve thrown all my grenades into a tree.This game isn’t just chaos—it’s controlled chaos, which is basically the polite way of saying “You’re going to panic, but it’s fine because so is everyone else.”The story? You’re an angry ex-spy out for revenge. Classic. Simple. Except now every decision you make is basically one long episode of What Could Possibly Go Wrong? Spoiler: everything. But when it works, oh man, it’s glorious. Luring an enemy into a trap while sprinting through a forest like you're auditioning for Die Hard? Chef’s kiss.Also, let’s talk about the S ranking system. I thought I was doing okay with my C rank, and the game just laughs like “Oh, sweet summer child, you tried.” Now I’m trapped in an endless loop of “one more run,” trying to be the speed demon I was never meant to be.In conclusion, I Am Your Beast is the ultimate test of how fast you can panic and still somehow succeed. 10/10. Would absolutely lay a bear trap in the wrong place again.
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: This ♥♥♥♥ slaps hardLet me clarify:- The audio work on this is insanely polished and clearly a lot of time went into the audio, music and VA. I think the last time I heard VA this good was like, Half Life 2. The music is fantastic and the last level's track instilled a level of confidence I didn't have in myself since I was like 11- The gameplay is great to the point where I think I redid the final mission around 6 times now. I S-ranked it, then played it 5 more times just because of how badass it made me feel. There are various quirks that keep the gameplay fresh and moving as you play it and get better at it- The story is great. I have a low bar for stories in indie games because I know how hard it is to craft a good one. However, this one is exceptional. The gameplay complements the story in such a way that it feels appropriate: as you get better at the game, the dialogue amps up. It's simple, but sometimes that's all you need. I think the devs may have been influenced by the graphic novel series Polar, but I can't speak for them- The runtime is only 3-4 hours, excluding challenge maps that I haven't unlocked yet. That part sucks. However I don't play games for runtime, I play them for how good of an experience they are, and this one is worth the price point- The raw adrenaline you get from this is comparable to the best moments of Doom, Hotline Miami, or Ultrakill. Think somewhere less than Ultrakill but more than Hotline Miami.- Graphics are fine. They are stylized but it doesn't really detract from the experience; it is clear they have had many rounds of playtesting to get the silhouettes, colours, and shapes in the environment very readable. Overall, get this game when you can. Polished as hell and sets a bar for indie games.

_childDocuments_.review: I Am Your Beast is a FPS Playground. Strange Scaffold lays out each ingredient like it's some episode of Chopped and asks you to cook up your own Sunday sauce. The level design is insane (which is an understatement, I just don't have the vocabulary to describe it) and has a final level that will have you grinning from ear to ear. Combat feels c r u n c h y, with every shot, every kick packing a punch. Top all of this off with a protagonist and voice acting that leaves the game oozing with cool. I'm chasing S-Ranks and Challenge levels now. The combos continue to evolve into these high-octane stunts. I heard this game described as an "adrenaline shooter" and I couldn't agree more.Easiest $20 I've spent for "one last job."

_childDocuments_.review: Short and snappy are the words that best sum up this brilliant game. tl;dr This is a fan-freaking-tastic lovechild of FEAR's enemy callout system, Hotline Miami's rapid repayable level system, and Doom Eternal's 'the battle is a symphony' combat feel, topped off with a great soundtrack and a simple but satisfying story.It's short, incredibly so. As of writing this review, I had spent about 2.4 hours in the game and finished the main story, even replayed a few levels to ensure I could unlock later story levels. If you were to base it on that alone, it'd not be worth the asking price. Instead, what you get for this asking price is a perfectionist's wet dream. Constant new challenges are the reward for completing previous ones. Finished the level? Great, now do that level again but using only melee attacks. Oh, you've done that too? Okay, this time, here's a bunch of activatable laptops that are in more obscure areas that force you to engage with enemies in a way you'd not usually need to in this level. You got a few S ranks? Wow! Incredible! Here's some  challenge levels for you to cut your teeth on. I've not unlocked the majority of those yet. I only have two S ranks. I intend to get more. The game is making me want to get them all.I haven't talked about the other attractions. A hard hitting satisfying gameplay loop, with a soundscape that applauds you for every kill, and pushes you to feel the rush of the speed that the game encourages both for score and survival purposes. The soundtrack? Ballistic, ecstatic, an electronic symphony with the kind of brutality you'd expect from the guy you're playing as. There is but one nitpick for me. I wish that the enemy callouts not only said what you were doing, but were more precise about *where* you were doing it. Yes, I am using headshots, but I want to hear them yell out "He's ran into the tunnels in the west!", or see enemies working together. When you're so close to emulating the brilliance of Fear's enemy callout system, it cannot help but be compared. And that's the thing; that's the only nitpick I've got!It sets out to do a job, and does it near-perfectly. It may as well be perfect when the nitpick is as ridiculous as 'I want to hear more of the voice acting.'Do yourself a favour:If you like FPS shooters - Play thisIf you like Hotline Miami - Play thisIf you like FEAR's callout system - Play thisIf you like games that push you to perfectionism - Play this If you want bang for your buck with a game you can replay again and again just to get better and better -

_childDocuments_.review: A cathartic, empowering, FPS gem. Playing this ♥♥♥♥ gets me hype beyond belief. Everything about this game is so simple, but so satisfying. It's just the right amount of challenge without getting too frustrating. Usually, speed-based, race the clock games don't get me hooked. But, this one sunk its talons right in and didn't let go until I 100%'d. Story rocks, music slaps, gameplay slays, graphics are stylin'. 100% recommendation. They just keep pumping out BANGERS.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing Space Marine 2 and being semi-disappointed by the feel of the controls only to have this release the next day and blow me the ♥♥♥♥ away with some of the smoothest gunplay I've seen was a true breath of fresh air. Xalavier and his team are some of the most interesting voices in the industry right now, and I'm thrilled to see such a triumph of a release with I Am Your Beast. If you have any love for stylish action backed by a slick story, you owe it to yourself to pick this up.
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I Am Your Beast is short, but oh so sweet. It's an amazingly fast paced, adrenaline filled FPS game. The term "The 3D Hotline Miami" has been labelled on a few games but both mechanics and general "feel" wise, this game is pretty damn close. The soundtrack probably gave me hearing loss but it's simply amazing, the gameplay is fast and doesn't slow down too badly if you die a ton, and the story and setting feel like a bunch of good twists on existing formulas. I'm probably a definitive Strange Scaffold fan after this game alone, and they plan on adding in some goodies down the road to make up for its admittedly short main story length. Challenges are already in their for those of us that need more pulse pounding action, and the rating system seems fair in my book. Great game!

_childDocuments_.review: I Am Your Beast blends the fast-paced, tactical action of Superhot with the precision puzzle solving of Neon White, wrapped up in an aesthetic reminiscent of The Long Dark. The game's short campaign is packed with adrenaline-fueled moments, and the gameplay loop had me coming back for more as I chased better scores and completed bonus objectives.The voice acting is top-notch, making every mission feel immersive, even though I found myself wishing the narrative lasted longer. Still, for the price, it's an absolute steal with plenty of replayability, leaving me hoping for more of this intense world in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: is an excellent fast-paced shooter with an engaging improvisational hook that has you flying through level after level using whatever you can get your hands on to ferociously dispatch foes--handguns, combat knives, bear traps, tree branches, and more. The combat feels mighty brutal and can put you into some really satisfying flow states like other arcadey shooters, while well-acted dialogue scenes in between levels break up the action without being too obtrusive. It took me around 3 hours to complete the full run of story missions, but there are many challenge levels to unlock by achieving S-ranks in the story levels and completing optional objectives. There's definitely a focus on precision and speedrunning here and some of the later levels might require you to perform better on previous levels before accessing them, but you won't necessarily need to sweat it out  too much to at least see the full story through. Of course, that will depend largely on how confident you are with fast shooters, so experience may vary.Oh, and the game's soundtrack is .

_childDocuments_.review: I highly,  recommend this game.I had high hopes. Knowing this was from the developers of "El Paso: Elsewhere," I set high expectations, and I'm glad to say those expectations were passed by leaps and bounds. Finished the game in basically one sitting, and though the price felt a little high. I can imagine the planned content additions will justify it even more. The music and combat felt perfect together. The story was engaging yet minimal enough to give more focus on game play. Allowing you the opportunity to truly step into Harding's shoes and feel like a real badass. The flow of the levels was stellar, you could tackle them in any way you see fit as long as you had the skill to do so. The wide aim of guns supports rash-"run and gun" type play. You don't have to maintain pin point accuracy. The game play mechanics added in further story levels add a nice touch to make sure the game play doesn't stagnate as player skill or knowledge increases, while also tying into the story further. Again, I highly recommend this for anyone who is even remotely interested in this title. Trust me, it is worth every penny. Amazing job, Strange Scaffold. You deserve praise for this. ♡

_childDocuments_.review: Updated Review after hitting 100% on story as well as challenge levels:The game is still a recommend in my book, the game-play feels amazing most of the time with blood pumping moments and very punchy gun play, the layouts are diverse and while not usually giving too many options (Not if you're looking for an optimal way to get a high rating) they are good at keeping interest from start to finish without giving much room to get bored of them. The soundtrack I have mixed feelings on as while some tracks are great others get very tiring with blaring music constantly assaulting your ears whenever you're replaying a level for that high rating, which resulted in me muting the music for some level, the final story level track tho? Golden.The story is fairly basic but elevated by the voice acting that really gives a perspective on who the characters are and their emotions without ever giving them a face.There have been a couple of bugs and caveats here or there, clipping through the ground at certain spots, getting stuck on a wall and the sort, but they have been fairly rare. Certain levels are made more annoying by the presence of helicopter raining bullets on you, which by itself is not the issue but it can friendly fire their own mercs which can ruin your score/time. All in all the pros still out-weight the cons, and the game time has been fairly decent for the price, 12 hours in total to get 100% on both Challenges and Story but I expect people who are better at these types of games to be faster.
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Dear Diary - turns out this game is every bit as good as the trailers looked.Chaining environmental hazards, grabbing items, flinging enemy munitions back at them and parkour all combine in a silky smooth dance that feels half test of reflexes, half puzzle box - and the combat feels GREAT -  figuring out each of the levels 'flows' is so damn satisfying.The story is light but not in a bad way, instead there is NO fat - no unnecessary exposition (and I say this as someone that loves Kojima games). The presentation of it? So stylish, the text cards, the environments and the Voice acting / Foley and Music are so good and give it a tense action thriller vibe that has had me fully engrossed by these characters, their backstories and how they react as the stakes raise in a way that you just wouldn't expect from a game that is front and centre segmented time trials. Its masterful.And the soundtrack - bloody hell the soundtrack. Play it at my wedding, play it at my funeral. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Today, I stumbled across a game that feels oddly familiar, like an old buddy showing up unannounced. Just like dodging bullets from my past while leaping through the forest. The game nails my gritty, style-sharp and to-the-point. Did I mention it features me?Between my coffee breaks, I get to relive my days atop piles of boards I mangled together to run I am Your Beast. Talk about dual citizenship. The cut-scenes? Pure gold. (Eat your heart out, COI.) I broke a few rules along the way, but what's life without a little rebellion? The game seems to agree with me.If you want something that'll put you into my scuffed shoes, (I'll steal new ones later.) I am Your Beast is the one. No going back, just moving forward, one entry at a time.

_childDocuments_.review: I Am Your Beast is a perfect game. What I mean by this, is that it simply accomplishes everything it sets out to do, and does this well. Of course this may seem easy given it's relatively small scope, however the quality of it's accomplishments are not something to be understated.IAYB is a bite-sized, hectic, time-trial style FPS that wants you to be fast. It wants you to keep retrying it's meticulously crafted paths of trenches, industrial pipelines and climbable trees until you can flow through them like the wind itself. It wants you to learn the time-saving difference between putting one between a goon's eyes, or throwing him into the ground and stomping his face in (it's 0.3 secs more when you stomp kill). And it wants you to feel the beautiful release that is seeing that "S" pop-up. I mean this when I say it: You owe it to this game to S-score everything. From the buttery smooth gameplay, to the feedback of killing someone, it's a beautiful rush.The story is told here through text, and colored backgrounds. This might sound lacklustrer for a game, but I guarantee you, it somehow manages to still be one of the most enrapturing stories in an indie game. This is greatly owed to some of the most stellar voicework I've heard. It barely feels acted out, every voice's got a good tinge of "reality" to it that's hard to really detail out, it's something you gotta hear to understand. As for the story, it takes from John Wick's premise of "the legendary, stone-cold killer returning to life" type deal, except instead of a legend brought back for revenge, you just REALLY want to quit your job and live in the woods. Relatable.Last, but CERTAINLY, ABSOLUTELY not the least: The soundtrack.RJ Lake is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ legend. I'm talking some Mick Gordon, Andrew Hushult, Simon Viklund level hype-sorcery here. This soundtrack doesn't just bang, it ♥♥♥♥♥. High-octane synths and beats in so many different styles accentuate your swift bloodshed with excellence. There is simply no outlier in the soundtrack, every single battle track can be placed side by side, if not above the ranks of bangers like BFG Division. And even the tracks used to accompany the aforementioned cutscenes, go hard. Alternating between lo-fi & mellow tracks in more calming conversation, to agressive & angry tones when ♥♥♥♥ gets messy. And it all sounds so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good, man. It's rare to see an OST so loaded even in the AAA scene. RJ Lake deserves to get a prize for this, if not every single prize he can. Good God, what a sick ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ OST.Like I said at the very beginning, this is a bite-sized game, so you'd imagine it'd be pretty easy to hit the marks of making a good game, given it's scope. But Strange Scaffolds went above and oh-so-beyond by crafting the ultimate speedrunner/action badass fan/adrenaline junkie's wet dream, all rolled up into one. It's small, but it accomplishes a lot more than many games thrice it's size. I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love this game so much.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't quite know where to start.I guess I'll start by saying I love this game.The gameplay/feel, the music, hell, even the voice acting is phenominal. The. entire. time.I'll go through each one:- The gameplay/feel just feels so responsive and every headshot or explosive kill feels so satisfying. The parkour aspect of the game also feels incredibly fluent and you are always in control of where you are going.- The music pulls the whole thing together and really makes you feel like a badass. There are times where you will even get a chance to sync up your shots with the music, and although there is no bonus for that, it feels rewarding either way.-The voice acting is honestly possibly my favourite part of this game. First there are the little quirks of dialogue during each level where the enemy soldiers give callouts to eachother depending on what weapon youre currently holding, or they'll scream at eachother in fear if you blow someones head off.Then there's the cutscenes. wow. I don't know how to explain it, but these conversations, moments of self reflection, all of it, just feels so real. and if you've played the game, I'm going to leave one word hinting at my favorite part of dialogue, but if you havent played it, this wont spoil it.Mercy.I genuienly watched that cutscene 3 times because I was just wowed by how real and intimate that moment felt.This game gets a 10/10 from me.Every second is so enjoyable, and if you have any interest in this game, please try it. You will love it.

_childDocuments_.review: I AM YOUR BEAST prioritizes everything that matters to a speedrunning FPS. The visuals are readable at speed without sacrificing style. No one weapon or tool in your arsenal overshadows any other. Generous aim assist? Rack up headshots without slowing down, cowboy. Most levels are open, giving you multiple routes to success.Completing every optional objective, and gunning for (almost) every S-Rank, was integral to my experience. You certainly could just move on after your first clear. But the best appreciation for this game comes from improving your times, learning the shortcuts and sneaky angles of approach, and drilling out combos. Relying on just one weapon or technique the whole game would kill the fun, so I'm glad the optional objectives are there to push exploration of the physical space and the variety of the sandbox.Dialogue hits with the same pace and punch as the action. The inter-mission exchanges provide a compelling drama in very few lines, and the enemy barks and pre-mission chatter are hilarious. The core conflict is well-summarized by the title. Harding refuses to be the CIO's hound on a leash, but if they don't stop coming after him, he'll have to become their living nightmare; their bete-noire.I'll be going back again to finish the Challenge missions and enjoy the post-launch update. Strange Scaffold and every other hand that worked on this game also deserve praise for their sustainable dev practices, at a time when the industry is undergoing contractions and mass layoffs.
