_childDocuments_.review: Ever wanted a Rambo: First Blood game that has the pace of Hotline Miami? Well then I have tha game for you! I Am Your Beast is a new high for Strange Scaffold, topping last year’s El Paso, Elsewhere for me as my favorite of their games. It may not be the fastest twitch shooter, or the smoothest parkour game out there, but it’s a very stylish, unique, and well executed blend of the two that’s short, but offers a lot of replayability.You play as an ex-special agent who is absolutely  coming out of retirement to go on one last mission, and your commander is pretty pissed about it. As he sends in squad after squad against you, you will be shooting, stabbing, drop kicking, and throwing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bear traps at them at breakneck speeds. It’s not just the core gameplay loop, but the way it’s presented that makes this game so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool. You don’t aim down your sights, even when holding a sniper rifle, you hold it sideways and your crosshairs will follow the angle of the gun. Enemies will call out what weapons you pick up to kill them with and where you are, which ends up being pretty useful when you’re swapping weapons while sprinting through a pile of guns and bodies towards your next target. There are plenty of opportunities to use the environment to your advantage and rack up your combos to get that S rank on levels, as well as bonus challenges. On top of being just good ways to make you think about how to approach the level in different ways, it will also unlock bonus challenge levels to play. Oh, and the soundtrack is once again a banger.This game does skimp out on its story bits though. It’s almost entirely told through text boxes on a screen in between most levels, and there aren’t any interesting characters or twists to it. It is the barest bones to string together the gameplay, and I’m okay with that because it doesn’t really interfere with it. What does interfere with the game is the fact that you have to exit out of every level and go back to a menu in order to select the next one you want to play instead of being able to play them back to back. You will also run into roadblocks that will force you to go back and get a certain number of A or S ranks, or complete a certain number of bonus challenges that only unlock after beating a level in order to unlock the next story mission. If this were a longer game, this would be a lot more frustrating.This is exactly the kind of game I want to see more of; short, but extremely engaging. I ended up blasting through this game in just over 2 hours, but I already feel the urge to jump back in and try to S rank every mission and unlock the rest of the challenge maps.

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing game for speed runners, FPS players, and puzzle solvers alike! I Am Your Beast does an amazing job at putting together short puzzles in the form of time trials where the player gets to feel like a badass over and over and over again. You get a rewarding feeling the first time you beat a level, and then again after completing its challenges, and once more when you finally get that S-rank that's sometimes just milliseconds away. This game has such a satisfying feel when playing it because of all the elements working together in harmony. The sounds and visuals of taking down an enemy, the fluid movement, the weapon variety, and the banging soundtrack (which is honestly so good it's worth buying the game just for it) all play a role in making I Am Your Beast a gratifying experience.If you are a completionist, a speed runner, an FPS player, or just enjoy feeling like a BAMF then this game is definitely for you!

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic story, well-told and through a really impactful way imo. The gameplay is incredibly tight, feels like Hotline Miami in first-person but in a way that makes sense. I encountered 0 bugs during my time with it aside from a couple jumps where I'm ~pretty~ sure I should've climbed something but didn't. The in-moment replayability is reminiscent of Neon White where you replay simply to do better, go faster, really nail down your routing.Each level has 2 bonus objectives and a letter grade so you're able to rerun them as needed or wanted, and quite a handful of challenge missions completed by doing so.Honestly I haven't played a game with such satisfying movement since Titanfall 2, the team absolutely knocked it out of the park. Enthusiastically recommended

_childDocuments_.review: I don't do serious reviews at all, half of my reviews are stupid ♥♥♥♥ like "No Sex" or something like that, but I feel like this is a very much appropriate exception. I hadn't heard much about this game when I decided to buy it, I only knew it was the same people who made Clickholding. A Fast-Paced Run N Gun guarantees a good time, but this game blew my expectations out of proportion. This game's scenery while using older graphics fits so perfectly, the levels mesh so well with the graphics that it's honestly amazing, and the game runs buttery smooth with little to no issues. The game manages to be so hard yet so rewarding, and getting S-ranks is an arduous task to do, but it yields such a dopamine rush (I have started my attempt to get them recently so I'll see how it goes). But by far my favorite part of this game is the character of Alphonse Harding. He serves as the commonly used, but rarely done right, character type of the "Edgey Killing Machine" but for me, he's a perfect example of how to do it right. The dialogue he has shifts from obvious tom-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to being downright cold and haunting, all be it some lines are a LITTLE cringy but it makes the interactions feel actually real. Kudos to the devs for how they wrote Harding, they give such a clear view of such a complex psyche. If any of you are on the fence about buying this game, then BUY IT PLEASE, it so well coded and written to the point where even if you're not big on FPS Shooters then you are gonna still really enjoy the story alone (And Vice-Verca). But let's say you dislike EVERYTHING I said, at the very least you should experience the final level. The cutscene before it, the song, the overwhelming yet manageable waves, your gonna be piss-poor if you missed out on that.

_childDocuments_.review: RJ Lake’s distorted bass grinds like gears of a rancid machine screeching to a halt. Xalavier Nelson Jr.’s lower-register fry, half-apathetic fully exhausted. A burnout Jason Bourne, a Michael Mann protagonist covered in layers of detachment and irony. A gun is just an extension of a hand. A knife, a tree branch, your feet and fists. Gotta kill faster, cleaner. Learn the route, learn the time, learn what to pick up and what to discard until you become exactly what they made you. A game about striving toward a perfection of violence employed directly contradictory to its systemic thesis.They removed your humanity to craft a perfect beast but never could have imagined you'd get so good you'd transcend time itself.
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: This game will make you feel like an unstoppable force of nature, your enemies are not killed by a man but by an unfortunate accident. There was nothing anyone could do.Edit: I forgot that I already wrote a review, went to write one, and then saw this. I can do better. This game is a high octane explosion of skill. What starts feeling complicated and daunting ramps up in complexity in such a way that the progression from shooting a few guys in the woods turns into slaughtering dozens in a perfectly orchestrated obstacle course, all to save a few hundredths of a second. The music overwhelms your senses in the best way possible, all melting into you and accenting your rampage. Much like in El Paso, Elsewhere, Xalavier Nelson Jr.'s subdued performance as the protagonist (Alphonse Harding, in this case) feels intimate and inspired. There are few vocal performances in games or otherwise that feel so authentic and real. I especially appreciated the player insert character Alan, who much like me was unable to abandon his duty, even just to relieve himself. We need to piss, Alan. Just... after this run.

_childDocuments_.review: Ten hours of very fast-paced action fun. Never a dull moment. Doing combos like exploding a barrel, throwing a flying kick at an enemy then firing off an RPG and a few pistol headshots never gets old.Story is there. It's fine. Has a nice ending. Challenge missions are actually very challenging to get S ranks at but not in an annoying way, it was very fun perfecting my runs with the quick restart function. Highly recommended to everyone.Only issue I had was that sometimes after entering a level I wouldn't be able to move or rotate the camera by any means, requiring a game restart. Besides that, the game runs great though the clip saving function does decrease performance a lot, so probably just use your GPU software for that. And a minor gripe: If you quit the game after watching a cutscene, you'll have to re-watch that cutscene again when you want to continue! It only saves progress on level completions.

_childDocuments_.review: Byron, you are the goat, I love you Babe.Quick and concise though, this game is great, combat is hectic (though sometimes enemies feel a bit braindead), weapons feel satisfying, movement is surprisingly smooth and feels great (beta tree climbing was rough, the full release feels smooth and snappy) and surprisingly an awesome narrative tagged to it as well.  What's awesome is that the narrative is spread through dialogue "cut scenes" that lack visuals, it's all text, but surprisingly, due to the style, and the great voice acting, feels far more enthralling for something that can best be described as audio logs in other games.  Though I finished it in 2 hours, I can see myself digging more time into it to S rank all missions, and to play challenges.  Hell I want to stream the game, just to mess with the Twitch Integration they added to it.  Genuinely a great game, if ya can't afford it at the cost it's at, wait for a sale later, but the cost ain't bad for the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I have 1.5 hours (As of writing), I can't have completed the game, right? Well, the story is about that long, including the progression gates the game has that locks the ability to advance further without replaying your previously completed levels.  you ask? Well, the game actually doesn't unlock the first side objective until you complete it normally, then it allows you to do them. Why does this matter, exactly? Well, I feel like it's to prevent someone from simply refunding the game early, as the actual content of the game is rather lacking in quantity. Don't get me wrong, what's there is absolute gold, I just wish there was MORE there. Yes, there's challenge missions, but those require you to at least play each regular mission  to unlock them all. I'm still itching to play more instead of starting to just perfect my runs.This game could be thought of similarly to Ultrakill by New Blood, however, the content there is not only greater than the developers genuinely had to go, but also got you to a point where you felt satisfied with the amount and could then push yourself to go back and redo some levels for higher rankings. If this game had more unique levels inside the campaign instead of relying on you replaying them to extend the runtime, I'd call this my new favorite game, hands down. I love the story, characters, and style, it just needs more meat. Randomly generated or player created missions, an endless mode where you have to keep moving/killing to survive, anything! This game feels and plays great, it just needs something to justify that price-tag.If this game sold with no additional updates or features for $10, I'd say it's perfect. $15-20 depends solely if achieving absolute perfection on repeated playthroughs of each level sounds good to you. If  kind of additional content gets added, I personally promise here to the developer that I will immediately fold and change this to the glowing review this game deserves. Hell, if it's a good amount of additional content, I even promise to buy someone an extra copy.

_childDocuments_.review: From the team that brought us the excellent El Paso Elsewhere from last year comes I Am Your Beast; a thrilling first person shooter with an emphasis on speedrunning through levels at a breakneck pace and blasting mercs in the face (ooh, I rhymed, maybe I’m on my way to being a rap artist like in the game).In the spirit of El Paso, the writing and story is surprisingly funny and poignant and delivers strong characters with minimal production values. The dialog and voice acting are PHENOMENAL and honestly master class for a video game at least. I genuinely wanted to get to the next level just to hear the next piece of radio chatter between the characters.The gameplay is stellar and accomplishes being a fast, white knuckle shooter about sprinting through a forest and killing mercenaries sent to assassinate you. The game is only about two and a half hours though, but there are tons of unlockable challenges and missions for S ranking story missions and BOY are those S ranks hard to get!The game also runs phenomenally on the steam deck. The one issue you may have is that in order to reach the final level you do have to obtain at least 1 S rank in any previous mission and to do that you need near perfect accuracy which can be hard with a controller. Other than that though, stellar port.So yeah, if you like well crafted action games that give a ♥♥♥♥ about telling a decent story with solid performances, definitely pick this one up.
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. The process of thinking of, and testing the best way to 100% each level feels extremely rewarding. It feels impossible at first but absolutely doable. _childDocuments_.review: There's a certain completeness that I AM YOUR BEAST presents players with that makes everything feel bigger than it is.  Is it weird to say that the menus are really good? _childDocuments_.review: FAIR WARNING: While a great experience, this can be a one-sitting game. It took me about 2 hours to beat the story, even while I was replaying almost all of the levels 2 or 3 times and trying a handful of the challenge missions here and there.That being said, there's some impressive level variation and the story, while simple in presentation and delivery, is satisfying with some solid voice acting. In short, it's a story-based FPS that emphasizes speed and stylish performance in it's levels, most of which are under a minute long (*foreshadowing*). The art is unique and it runs well, with not too much in the way of indie jank... but it is there and you will eventually start to notice some cracks. The soundtrack (called "I AM YOUR BEATS" lol) also really does it for me for a fast-paced game like this. If you're bad at aiming like me, there's some pretty generous headshot detection and the movement leaves little to be desired. Whipping through levels in this game can feel like a dream, but... with all the praise I can give it, there's really just the one glaring issue: just when you're starting to love the game, it's over, and there's next to nothing left to do.Don't get me wrong, I love games like this and Katana Zero that can be blazed through in under an hour without the story beats. The issue is that a full IAYB speedrun could be around 20 minutes (and that's for real time, not the "time" the game gives you that includes time reduced from kills). KZ also had it's length pointed out as it's biggest issue, and a "Gold" speedrun that game takes twice the amount of time as an "S" run of this game. This is just way too short for me, even before the $20 price tag. Even outside the gameplay, the story suffers because there's not enough time to formulate any questions about the plot or establish much of a relationship with the characters. Other games like KZ and Hotline Miami mitigate this by having story beats all over the place, but outside of the pre-mission talks (which don't always happen before every mission) there's none of that in IAYB. There's a stack of unlockable challenge missions that have no canon story involvement, and why those weren't thrown into the campaign and given some plot relevance is beyond me. You also get nothing for doing those or the optional story mission challenges, outside of an achievement for the former. No customization options, no additional story beats, no online leaderboards to compete in... nothing.I will 100% support any future content for this game, and certainly keep an eye on what these developers do next if it has something to do with this game or not. I'm somewhat conflicted, right now I have to leave it at a 4 out of 5. If they had leaned into the plot and given it some more time (especially during gameplay) all while working in just a little more mission objective and enemy variety, it would be an easy 5 out of 5. It just feels so criminal that we get to spend so little time with the main character and his struggle, as the quality of the game is way above average but the quantity you're getting is almost unacceptable. Almost.As of now, I would wait for at least a 25% off sale, 50% if you're not sure. In under 10 hours I have only one challenge mission that's not 100% and "S" rank. Other than that it feels like I'm done with IAYB already, and that kinda makes me sad.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has one of the most addictive combat loops I've ever seen and is probably THE most addicting "speedrun" type game I've ever played. This game is now at the peak of the games I've played like Neon White, Lovely Planet, Spring Dash, etc. where the goal isn't to just beat the level, but to come back and beat it as fast as you can for a better score. I played through every level and made sure to get the S rank and do both side objectives before moving on, and I found perfecting each level to be supremely entertaining. Beyond the level of fun I usually have with games like this, or even in games with "better" core shooting where the combat is more longform and improvisational. Something about the combination of the routing and the small adjustments you have to make when you mess up in a small way just makes this game work well for me. It took me about 5 hours to do all of that, but I've still got to complete all of the challenge missions. I just couldn't wait to leave as positive a review as I can.This game has the same amazing narration that 'El Paso, Elsewhere' had, but I would like to say that the story in this game is a lot more light compared to that game, but that is not to its detriment at all considering the dialogue works perfectly to break up the pace between missions and anything more would probably just bog the game down.Amazing game, 4/5, between this and Echo Point Nova this year has been great for shooters

_childDocuments_.review: I Am Your Beast is a butt ton of fun, and challenging in all the right ways. In addition, each level has a rank to beat, and the time and points system for the rank is very readable and understandable. You will have to get at least some of the challenges and S ranks done to unlock all of the story, and even more to unlock all the challenge levels, but I'd say that 100%ing this game is definitely worth it anyway. _childDocuments_.review: There a lot of games that I've played that i wish i had bought on sale. This is one of the few games I wish I paid full price.The art style is fantastically made without becoming a distraction, The characters are all incredibly likeable, The game play is so incredibly tight and fluid. I assume bullets are the size of logs because i never struggled to get a head-shot from hip-fire if i wanted; I thought this was incredibly weird at first before i realised the devs don't care if you scrim aim labs, they reward you for doing far more interesting and risky stuff. Oh and then there's the musicI have no idea how you did what you did, but not only are the tracks thrilling to listen to, but somehow so cleverly designed so that the enemy call outs are so clear they sound like they are part of the song. I think it's $20 well spent and something I could see myself revisiting in sporadic bursts for a while.  If you're all about speedrunning and optimizing routes through levels though, you'll get even more value out of this than I did as an already-satisfied customer.   The game prods you lightly at points to explore some of the replayability and bonus objectives throughout the campaign, but mostly leaves you to your own devices. But ultimately the chief appeal here is that it's nailed that quality you can't fake where all the action is deeply moreish thanks to an inspired combination of UX, graphic stylization, and sound design.

_childDocuments_.review: “I am your beast” quick review.Hey team Steam Deck. Absolutely loving this game. The premise is simple. You are a special agent/former special forces in retirement living it large in the woods when one of your former handlers gets in touch to get you to do “one last job”. You politely decline so the guy send a bunch of goons to get you to change your mind. What follows is what on the surface looks like a short story consisting of 27 quick levels. Each one is a run to get from A to B in the quickest way possible while disposing of your enemies in the most strategic way. A number of basic attacks such as punch and kick are mixed in with a selection of weapons that you pick up from the fallen enemies on the fly. These can be used as intended or thrown at enemies (be it a knife or an empty/not empty gun) to knock them out for a follow up finish.The first impression is that the game is on the easy side and you may be flying through each level. Upon completion of each run you have an option to move the story along or repeat the level with and added objective (2 extra per level for a suggested 3 runs minimum) which could be “head shots only” or “x number of bear trap kills” and the like. Even with these you may feel like the initial progress is fast.What I feel makes this game sing however is the tier system from C to S that encourages you to improve your score for each run. To be honest this is not something I usually have the patience for but in this game I truly believe this is THE feature that significantly elevates not only the quality of game play but also the length of the game as a whole. Rarely had I felt the satisfaction in a game of mapping out the run in my head and going for an A or an S rank.It is these ranks that quickly highlight the flow aspect of this game. Do you go from A to B down an intended route blowing everything in your path or could you save a few seconds by skidding past a goon with a shotgun blow to the nuts before picking off a hornets nest in the distance that gets you a few extra kills (and valuable seconds) on that side end of the level before dashing for the exit in the  opposite direction knocking the last enemy by throwing the empty barrel in their face + a stomp etc.The fact that each level is short and the graphics are somewhat simple makes the reload of each level (should you die or want to get a better start) instantaneous. This keeps you in the flow so you never lose momentum. It’s a testament to this game that after an hour my left thump was getting that familiar sore feeling you get when the game asks you to stay focused on sudden changes in direction of movement and aim. Each kill or destruction removes second to milliseconds from your total time. Just when you think you can’t possibly do this level in less 10 seconds (adjusted time) to get an S rank you find a new path at 7.32, surely this is the absolute limit….the 6.59. It just works. This combined with additional challenge mode added alongside the story makes the game very replayable and very much worth the price of admission.The art direction of this game is great. The graphics while somewhat simple add to the vibe of the game. The voice acting is superb and the soundtrack is absolutely banging, literally fuelling you as you accelerate your progress through each run.The game does a great job of introducing you to the new mechanics via the story progression. Simple at first but by level 5 your environments start to fill up with a variety of potentially useful items and features that also countered by new enemies and challenges.So while the story is short and you could blitz through the hole game in a few hours it’s all about repeating the runs to streamline the progress. You could easily get hooked for 30 minutes to an hour building on the flow on one level alone. Again I don’t usually bother with this as prefer to move on with the story and combat but found this aspect extremely satisfying and yet to finish the game because of this.One negative I found so far is that you get an occasional enemy wistfully staring into the distance seemingly forgetting you have just disposed of half of the team. But you are way  too much in the flow to pay that any attention, so a quick kick to the chest and an extra few milliseconds off your time as you fly by will remind him not to sleep on the job when you make another round in a few moments.In the world of 50-70 games it is always great to find a lower budget gem of such high polish and emphasis on fun. So, yes, a highly recommended game for those looking for a blast of a game with an easy pick up and play mechanic and autonomy to push their progress without being held back from progressing the story.In short an absolute blast.

_childDocuments_.review: Strange Scaffold is one of the most consistently exciting game studios producing right now. This game has some of the most satisfying PvE I've ever experienced. The drive to get a better "grade" on each level wasn't exhausting, it was invigorating. It feels like a horrible power trip.Horrible because you're murdering people, and are constantly reminded of that fact. Which is to say, it's intentional. The story here is certainly secondary to the unbelievably honed gameplay, but that didn't stop it from keeping a vice-tight grip on my throat throughout. I don't think the blindingly-fast-paced levels would be as manageable without the story breaks in between, and I'm sure this story wouldn't be as impactful if I wasn't witnessing (committing) the insane acts of terror that drive the story with their escalation.The joint effort of these two elements is the driving force of this game, and it's done near-perfectly. And it doesn't overdo itself. Some people might want more content. Honestly, I think if the game was much longer I would get fatigued. The gameplay is too powerful. It burns a hole in me. It took me a month to finish this game because I just couldn't keep up with it. I'm a firm believer that a too-short game is better than a too-long one, but luckily I don't think this one is either. It's a short experience that had an incredible amount of effort put into it and it shows.

_childDocuments_.review: It has been a very long time since I have played a game with gameplay and game-feel this good. There are many ways that I could describe this game, “ultrakill with speed running elements”, “John wick simulator”,  “3d hotline Miami”, “Mach 3 dark messiah with guns”, but I feel like that would be doing the incredible design that went into it a disservice, not because similar games are bad, or because there are no similar games, but because this game is such an overt passion project that it deserves better than to be judged by its peers when it is so completely capable standing and being enjoyed on its own.At its core the game is a level-based combat sandbox game focused on high mobility and a style-system. Missions have a ranking and points are awarded for completing optional challenges and achieving higher ranks, with bonus missions used as a reward to incentivize engaging with those extra challenges. Combat is simplistic, but has enormous Intrinsic depth and opportunity for player expression through numerous environmental hazards, and excellent overall level design and engagement is incentivized through the ranking system that awards points based on speed and creativity. Objectives are varied throughout the campaigns runtime, the most common being to eliminate enemies, interact with/destroy targets, or run through a gauntlet of enemies and hazards to escape. The game frequently adds modifiers to these like invincible “over watch” enemies that must be avoided or blood loss that makes your health constantly tick down.The combat and level design are closely intertwined, both are geared towards keeping the player moving, both because your health is low and you need to stay mobile to avoid damage and heal using spread out health pick-ups, and because limited ammunition encourages you to use environmental objects to your advantage, such as head stomping enemies by jumping on them.Speaking of limited ammunition, I was momentarily confused when I went to rebind my controls and saw that there was no reloading, this seemed odd for a game with a “realistic” setting, but it quickly made sense as a way of encouraging players to change tactics constantly. While fighting, you’re constantly dropping guns, throwing them at people, changing between different types with different advantages and always thinking about how to get the most bang for your buck with every shot. Ammo is plentiful because guns are plentiful, but you might not always have the kind you want which encourages creativity in how you use what you have.It should be noted that the campaign is fairly short, if that is something that matters to you. My first completion took about 3 hours, but the core gameplay is strong enough that I expect to be playing for a good while longer S ranking all of the missions and completing optional objectives. Frankly I think the game deserves better than to be judged on scope or play-time, it’s all killer and no filler and I expect that I’ll be replaying it regularly for that reason as well.Story wise the narrative is simplistic but incredibly heartfelt. You wouldn’t consider brutal guerrilla warfare to work well with wholesome gay romance and self-improvement but it does phenomenally well and adds a lot to your and the protagonist’s rampages because you get a better idea of what he is fighting for and to escape. There is also some hilarious dry-humor mixed in and overall the tone is a positive one.Graphically the game is very stylized, the setting is “realistic” in that it is about a rouge black-ops soldier, but by he violence is very cartoony and the art design is excellent, it’s a great art style because it is pleasant to look at but also because it lets you tell at a glance what you are looking at in the heat of combat, for example enemies have glowing pink eyes that in-universe are night vision goggles but also let you line up headshots while moving at high speed. The music is a mix of heart-pumping electronic music and calming country tones in-between.Overall I could not recommend this game enough, it’s hands down one of the most polished and well-designed single player experiences I’ve had in years and it feels like robbery that I only paid 20 dollars for such a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: There were a lot of people left disappointed after the second Hotline Miami game changed up the formula, adding much larger maps and focusing more on build variety. Open areas littered with enemies often implied a type of verticality not actually possible with the top-down perspective. I Am Your Beast takes a lot of the ideas present in HM2 and iterates on them with finesse. The voice acting and story are fantastic. The first-person gun-play is cathartic and the movement is as fluid Mirror's Edge. I Am Your Beast ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ owns!
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: A short indie game worth your money. Took me just under 3 hours to complete the story, getting almost every side objective and getting S ranks on the levels that weren't too hard. The game isn't difficult if you just want completion, but I'm excited to get back and S rank all levels since a lot of levels have different routes you can take to clear them. The story was fantastic, and the gameplay is very satisfying. There are challenge levels after the main story you unlock through side objectives and S ranks, so I haven't even finished all the content yet. The music is amazing and I think this is the type of game I will think about for a while.
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: When I bought this game, all I had seen were a few brief snippets of gameplay. This led me to believe that I would be getting into a fun, mindless action game that blends elements of SUPERHOT and Hotline Miami; that may be true, yet I was unexpectedly drawn into the protagonist's story and the world that the game presents to the player. I Am Your Beast really proves that long, bloated, "cinematic" games, while they can be great, are becoming a restrictive format for AAA devs, when this few hour experience (that I will certainly return to in the future) has left me satisfied and passionate enough to write this review. Give I Am Your Beast a shot, it rules.

_childDocuments_.review: Great voice acting, great story, amazing gameplay. The game makes you feel like the monster you are with fluid movement and responsive aiming, not to mention the mild bullet magnetism making aiming easier, it puts emphasis on your ability to pick apart each level like a puzzle instead of having perfect aim. You might want to mess with your settings a bit to deal with screenshake from explosions and just landing on the ground, but I can't fault a single issue for how well the rest of the game handles. From taking out enemies from above and knocking weapons out of their hands to use against them its just perfect mechanic wise. The game was short but enjoyable there are still a lot of challenge levels and missions I am going to go back and either complete or reach a higher rank in. My only complaint is that some of the story levels require you to get a higher grade to progress such as one requiring you to S rank any level, but I mean it when is say that is my only complaint.This game is a must play for anyone who enjoys fast pace action games or games with amazing character writing and world building. _childDocuments_.review: Fun fast paced first person shooter. Most of the levels are open enough to give you some room to interpret a problem while still having a well designed flow that feels good to move through. Just running through a course and reacting to and shooting the bad guys as they appear is a ton of fun as well!S-Ranks all feel very achievable, and the two optional objectives can incentivize you to explore the level a little more deeply or to try to play the game in ways that aren't your usual. The only downside for me are the scored arena missions. The very last one is okay, but S-ranking these levels requires intentionally gathering lots of enemies together for high scoring environmental deaths which doesn't feel as good in the gameplay systems available. No hesitation in reccomending despite that! Buy at full price and enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: I had a fantastic time with I Am Your Beast. It's a pretty short game, about two hours long if you're just bee-lining the main story, but potentially several hours longer if you're doing the challenges and trying to S-rank all the stages. At it's heart it's a speedrunning game, and while it's not really my type of genre, what made me truly enjoy I Am Your Beast (outside of pretty great stage design and satisfying headshots) is it's story. It's nothing complicated, but the personality of the protagonist and the very enjoyable voice acting made me finish it in one go.I only really have two minor complaints, which is that melee (unarmed) feels pretty unsatisfying. Not so much kicking as punching, with weak sound effects being my core issue. Outside of that, I disliked that sometimes, to unlock new story missions, you had to go back to old levels and replay them to complete challenges. Still, overall, very solid 9/10 for what it's trying to be.
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I'm typically one to play through a game all the way through to the end, and then if I really like it, go back through and get all the collectables or go for any kind of 'true completion'. I haven't beaten this game yet, because each level is so fire, that I get that 'true completion' itch after every one. Gotta get those S ranks!
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I Am Your Beast is a fast-paced, run-and-gun first-person shooter that feels like a mix of Hotline Miami in the world of Superhot played by John Wick with some Mirrors Edge free running thrown in. All of these combined bring an adrenaline-filled and addicting gameplay loop that would rival most current AAA FPS gamesIf you want to scratch that itch most of these modern FPS games can’t seem to scratch, I Am Your Beast might be what you’re looking for.
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome high score based speedrunning FPS. The gameplay is crisp with each kill giving a satisfying pop. Each level is fun to master - there's a number of different weapons, attacks and environmental hazards so that you can get a little bit creative to chain together an S tier run. The game is pretty fair and you can learn how to get an S tier on most levels within a dozen tries.The story is told through dialogue only. The writing can get edgy at times and the vocal fry voice work is not my favorite, but it's entertaining nonetheless.Overall great for a pickup and play arcade style FPS.
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: If you're like me, Neon White may have permanently altered your brain chemistry and given you a desire for speed with style. Well friends, look no further than I Am Your Beast. Rock solid controls and tight, varied level design give way to a brutal dance of sticks, fists, knives and bullets in order to finish your mission as fast as possible. If you love violent and stylish indies such as Hotline Miami, the aforementioned Neon White, or Sifu, prepare for your new favorite indie of 2024.
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: It is funny to me that all negative reviews have under 2 hours and complain about the lack of content. Before I moved onto the next level, I would complete both bonus challenges, and work towards an S Tier run. Some levels I would become obsessed with shaving off every last second that I could. For me, the game had the perfect amount of content for the price, and incredibly enjoyable the entire time. Be the Agent Harding that the developers believe that you can be, and you will love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I am being 100% honest in saying that this is one of the best games of 2024, and in my opinion one of the tightest, most entertaining, most compelling games I have ever played. Undoubtedly my personal game of the year, not just among indie titles. Voice acting is perfect, the soundtrack is back to back banger tracks, the gameplay borders on addictive, and the story is truly touching with its core message and characters. I wish I could buy it again, which I already did once after seeing a friend had it wish listed. This game is worth your money and time.
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: This game, once you find your flow, makes you feel like a legitimate badass. You are NOT invincible, by any means. Until later on in the game, if you don't take out the guys in front of you as fast as humanly possible, they're likely to swarm you and take you out. They balance this out by giving you optional armor pickups, and points where strategic shots will take out a group of enemies that will allow you to ease off and pick off the rest as you please. However, you're on a timer. At all times. This makes you feel like you need to go faster... and faster... until you hit that sweet sweet S rank. The music carries the flow of the combat in a way similar to that of Severed Steel and Neon White, and each song fits the feel of the situation perfectly.  There's a ??love interest??, there's a backstory that unfolds as you play, all the carnage is initiated in a John-Wick style of story that initially felt like a "oh, we're doin Wick again" moment, but actually feeling the hate Alphonse has and festers within him throughout the game gives the player a much more personal attachment to the reasoning behind his actions. This is a ~2-3 hour game that gives and takes, all within a complete, fulfilling narrative. Buy this game, babe.

_childDocuments_.review: I AM YOUR BEAST is, quite possibly, my Game of the Year 2024. I've taken the time to 100% it- and I can say, without a doubt, that this is not a game to miss. Do yourself a favor, pick this up, and don't put it down until you're satisfied.THE STORY- You are Alphonse Harding, and you live in the woods. A former agent of the Covert Operations Initiative (COI), you were the best in the business- and when you're the best, they won't ever let you go. However, one fateful winter morning, you come across some COI agents encroaching on your territory- and they kill a small, red bird. With years of resentment and hatred for what you once were and who you worked for built up, this is the straw that broke the camel's back- beginning a one-man campaign of vengeance, gunfire, and also yaoi that might just burn your woods- or maybe the COI itself- to the ground.THE GAMEPLAY- Fast paced and frenetic, IAYB is a speedrunner's dream. Your main goal is to clear the level as fast as you can, with the maximum rank of S. Depending on how you take down enemies, time is subracted from your score at the end of each run- requiring a balance of speed and death to get those high scores. Fans of Hotline Miami and Neon White take note.THE SOUNDTRACK- High energy electronic, with dynamic energy- there are two versions of every song, and the calm version is overrun by the loud version when you are first spotted by an enemy. There's even a whole original rap song written for one of the levels. (NO SPOILERS)MY REVIEW- This game is 10/10. It is a complete and highly polished experience that, once I picked it up, I could NOT put down. Replay value is extremely high- going for personal high scores and finding skips is a lot of fun. It has a great story, great sound, and the tightest gameplay that I've possibly EVER seen. Please. Play this game. Then buy it for your friends and make THEM play it. You won't regret it.Also yes I did say that there is yaoi and that isn't a lie that's just actually in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This ♥♥♥♥ magnificent.I have to say first: The soundtrack goes crazy. To get them, you REALLY need to understand the ins and outs of the game and be mechanically accurate in your movements. In other words, the game is easy to get into, but hard to master. _childDocuments_.review: I really love this game and I am currently following the speedrunning community for this game, and although it is small, I do recommend giving this game a try as It is one of the most fun speedrun/super hot style games I've played in a very long time. My buddy gifted me the game and I've put 10 hours into into in 2 days and plan to put more as I'll be attempting the Full game speedrun soon.Graphics: 8/10, If you're looking for realism, you wont find it here. But if you are looking for something kind of reminiscent of overkill or superhot, then this is it.Gameplay: 9/10, The gameplay is very smooth, and can be adjusted to your preferences. I love the feel of most of the guns, and the knives and bear traps are very, very fun to use. Exploding barrels, health and armor pick ups, throw a weapon using "Q" to knock them down and stomp them, its very fluid and goes together very well. I don't find myself using the slide mechanic too much because it slows you down a lot, and in speedruns, it waste so much time.Sound Design: 10/10, I love the music, sound of the guns, kill effects, and even the chatter on the radios at the beginning and during the levels, and the radios will get cut off when you kill someone while they are speaking, its very funny sometimes and has thrown me off while attempting to S rank some levels. Its nice though.Difficulty: 7/10, Now, it's not hard by any means, if you have experience playing games like Call Of Duty, CS:GO, or even Apex Legends and other First Person Shooters, Aiming shouldn't be too much of an Issue. The aim assist is very strong when it comes to aiming at someone with your gun, the bullet kind of feels like it will track them sometimes, and when throwing a bear trap or knife, I've literally had the bear trap turn into the briefcase chasing the guy on the jetski in Hitman. I'll say, its very challenging to get S rank on everything, and some of the Bonuses are difficult, but they're fun, not unforgiving.Overall: 8/10. I would strongly agree to try it and If you don't like it, you can always return it, obviously, but I love this game. _childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: Great game, it's speed-run parkour John Wick. Approx. 8-10hrs to S-rank story mode, + a few more hrs for challenges.If you enjoy flow-state parkour, first-person shooting, and speed-run challenges, this is the game for you. You speed-run parkour through winter forest levels, kicking, shooting, disarming, and throwing weapons at enemies, while constantly discarding and picking up weapons with limited ammo/use, in a race against the clock to complete objectives and leave the level. The player movement and level design are fantastic and manage to achieve a satisfying flow-state while speed-running through the levels. Weapons (shot and thrown) have a good amount of aim-assist that makes it less cumbersome to balance both running & gun, while still requiring a degree of skill to pull off shots/throws while maintaining speed; it feels great to shoot and throw weapons. Kicking is also a mechanic, which topples enemies over, giving the player an opportunity to curb stomp them, pickup their weapon, or run past. It all feels great.Everything else is also great. The art, voice acting, sound, music, story, technical game performance & stability... it's a polished gem of a game. It comes across as blend of Metal Gear Solid and 1960s aesthetics, and it all works for me. I had zero performance or stability issues on a RTX 3080 + 5900X.I have zero negatives to say about this game. I absolutely do want more, but for the price and the level of polish, the scope & value of the game is great, so I'm not even criticising that. I'm really looking forward to checking out future titles from Strange Scaffold.

_childDocuments_.review: After 4 hours of shooting agents, stomping agents, throwing weapons at agents, dying to agents, and replaying levels striving for that coveted S-rank 'til the very end, I can say that I Am Your Beast was a really good surprise of 2024.This game is dripping with style at every aspect. From the UI, cutscenes, set pieces, environment, music, gunplay, etc. everything about the game feels tailored into making you the biggest badass in this comic book about dismantling an entire PMC operation in a small pocket of Wild America. The voice acting and dialogue especially hooks you further into the game, making you want to fight for the next part of Harding's story.The gameplay is all about maximizing your efficiency in killing people, completing objectives, and extracting. Killing people in different ways gives you different time bonuses depending on how stylish the game considers the kill to be. Because of this, you're spending most of your time replaying the same parts of the level to optimize when, where, and how you kill. Well, that's how you need to play if you want the S-rank because these time cutoffs get rough. You don't need to put that much effort at all if you want to just hit A or B rank or you just want a relaxed experience. Your main tools of the trade boil down to stealing, stomping, throwing, sliding, and punching, the last of which is the only awful feeling thing in the entire game and discouraged to do at all times. Normally, playing 26 straight standard levels with these controls would get pretty repetitive and boring, but these aren't 26 standard levels.Each level is so tightly designed and readable at the same time. Trees to climb, barrels to shoot, and ♥♥♥♥ to throw at people are placed meticulously and purposefully throughout. It's just well designed. The first time you play through a level and look at your score, a colossal challenge opposes you as you ask the question, "How the hell is anyone supposed to S-rank this?" So you give it another shot, figuring out what seems to be a good traversal route. "This is doable," you say to yourself. There's ups where you optimize your killing, clean up your movement, and downs where you cross the i's and dot the t's. You even find a hidden trick along the way, cutting 5 seconds off. The score inches closer and closer. Then, you're right there where everything has clicked, all you need to do is execute it. You hit the exit, but you didn't get a good glimpse of the time. And when the bar tallies up and hits above S-rank, there's no greater feeling.You should absolutely give this game a shot. I haven't even touched the plentiful amount of challenge levels or targeted the bonus objectives for each level and I still feels like I got my money's worth in just 4 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is something special. From someone who bought it because "oh it looks kinda like ULTRAKILL, Trepang, Neon White, Ghostrunner, etc." This game was more than just that. If you want a nice little bundle to scratch that "boomer shooter" itch this will more than do that. This game felt like four and a half hours of pure bliss. It's important to say that this game doesn't reinvent the wheel. Because it never needed to. It took all the incredible parts of a linear boomer shooter and cranked them to the best of their abilities. The gunplay is smooth and polished while still feeling unique and full of style. The movement being smooth and snappy but not so full of crazy tech keeps it grounded and exciting. Not to mention that you really just feel like a bad ass running through the forest. The enemies are a little silly. Both in the purposeful way with their dialogue and quips, but as well as with their coding. It might be a bug but if you deprive an enemy of a weapon in a certain radius. They just sit there twiddling their thumbs while waiting for you to come kill them. They really managed to balance the overwhelming numbers feeling of being one man hunted by a whole militia, with the one man army power trip without either feeling underplayed. You never feel like you came into the fight with the upper hand but you still cleave your way through the level.What I really think is outstanding here is the story. Without getting into spoilers, it is incredible. Most games of this genre make a simple yet effective story (no shade but think Ghostrunner and Trepang.) But not here. The story is conveyed solely through gameplay and audio logs in between most missions. From the tutorial you can feel the life that oozes out of the story and characters. I want to give a huge round of applause to the VA for Harding. All the VA's do amazing but Harding, as the protagonist, does something so special. The story's bones follows the simple effective formula. But the acting, the tidbits, the characters all of it is screaming that the writers and actors were excited to be here.  TLDR: S+++ boomer shooter with incredible gameplay and an even more incredible story. Short and sweet and worth the 20$

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is the closest we'll ever get to a first-person Hotline Miami, and that alone is worth the price tag. The gameplay of I Am Your Beast is so close to perfection its maddening. Every pull of the trigger, every powerslide, every time I throw a bear trap or claymore mine into some schmuck's face like I'm the baseball pitcher from Hell, is a little jolt of dopamine to the gray matter that I deeply appreciate. It's challenging without being unreasonable; you can score a headshot, knock down a hornet's nest, or tag an enemy sniper with a pistol, without ripping your hair out. Getting an S-rank on a level will take some planning and persistence, but if I, a guy who is not good at first-person shooters, can S-rank all the story missions, I can guarantee that you can too. It feels Very Good. Before I continue, I feel like I should reiterate a point because it may be missed. You can throw a bear trap at peoples' faces. It will take their heads off. In fact, many things take peoples' heads off. You decapitate more people than the French Revolution did. It's great. The music is also a major plus. From the little "SOS" motif that plays in some of the later levels, to the gunshot background noise that I am almost certain is a Friday the 13th homage that plays in other levels, makes you feel like you aren't just Alphonse Harding, Sworn Enemy of the Human Head, but makes you feel like an out-and-out monster who is desperately (and violently) trying to be anything else. The story is fairly decent as well. While I question the judgment of the primary antagonist--why are you trying to capture a guy and force him to work for you when he's very good at not doing that, man, it's not gonna end well--the voice acting and general likability of the player character manages to mostly win me over. The graphics are fine. They're decently well-stylized, but honestly during the middle of running and gunning, it's rather hard to care to much about how the game looks, beyond its ability to not confuse me during a high-intensity murder spree. I have only two complaints. The first is that sometimes you get hung up on the level geometry when trying to jump over things. This was particularly noticeable during one of the challenge missions. You can absolutely jump onto the top of a truck, but if you get too close to the trailer of said truck, jumping becomes impossible. Having to course-correct so you can get another shot at jumping into something ruins the power fantasy ever so slightly.  Maybe a future update will handle that. The second complaint is incredibly quibbling, but occasionally the enemy chatter feels a little awkward. Sometimes it's endearing; the voice actress who introduces the RPGs sounds like she's having the best day of her life, and it almost makes one feel guilty about jumping directly onto the top of her head like a homicidal Mario. Other times, however, it takes me out of things. "Harding's using headshots" just feels like a bizarre thing to say, even for an action-movie mook who just watched Harding put a bullet into his buddy's corpus callosum. That being said, these complaints are completely and utterly outweighed by the utter triumph that is the rest of the game. Absolutely worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: In the dictionary under Flow State, it says: See this.If you like visceral, fast-paced rampage games like Hotline Miami or Superhot, just stop here and buy this! Strange Scaffold strikes again with yet another rapid release that's not only in a different genre, but genre defining in many ways. If you only play this to just get to the end of the story, it only takes about two hours, but there are challenges and ranks in each level, plus a whole list of separate challenge levels to boot.The story is short and only told through voiced slideshows, but it says a lot without needing a ton of words to do it. Like the levels themselves, everything is small but tightly packed and laser focused. Amazing to me that the Creative Director of both this and El Paso, Elsewhere is the principal voice actor in both and he absolutely nails it.The combat is some of the most precise feeling that I've played in a first-person shooter in a long time and I can only imagine the amount of tuning it went through. Everything is incredibly fast and when you get into the flow of combat, it feels like everything is happening in one slick, precise motion. There is also no loading time between level restarts, which helps keep you in that state if you need or want to try again. You never want to stop and the controls and systems ensure you never have to. Most of the levels have a number of different ways you can approach them, with various different weapons, melee objects and ways you can use each. You are scored based on both time and style and are encouraged to make the best of both, but you have a fairly generous amount to finish the levels is. If you want to unlock all the content, you will be replaying levels to get better scores, but if you're not a high-level player of this genre, it will accommodate you as well.An online leaderboard and/or replay system would have been cool because top-tier runs of this game will be a sight to behold, but I understand those aren't the simplest things to implement. Few games can land the kind of flow needed to evoke the feelings this one does and for it to come from such a small team, that's even more impressive.This is definitely going to be among my top games of 2024. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Bite sized adrenaline shots of retributive rampages that harken to the room clearing, weapon juggling flow of Hotline Miami (or more recently released 3d contemporary Anger Foot) with a light focus of parkour movement and stylish flair for high grade ranks almost like Neon White. Story is a breezy 2 hours of missions interrupted with radio conversations for light story dressing but RJ Lake's voice direction (following their great work in El Paso Elsewhere) gives the action an effective pathos. The meat of the game is its replayability for refining efficient battle plans between 25 story missions and 15 additional unique challenge levels which almost beg for you to knock the dominoes of action set pieces down again this time tighter. A fast combat loop, a stylish timing score system, and a soundtrack to play loud all combine to make this albeit succinct game worthy of a seat amongst its influences.

_childDocuments_.review: Historically, this studio makes really engaging and interesting games that lack polish. Don't get me wrong, I'm a certified fan. I've played just about everything they've made and I've reviewed them all positively. That said, if El Paso, Elsewhere had the exact same gameplay and none of the story or aesthetics, I wouldn't have thought twice about it. That's why I'm happy to say that I Am Your Beast is exactly as engaging conceptually as Strange Scaffold's previous projects, with incredibly tight gameplay. It's Neon White with big maps, Superhot gun grabbing, XIII style cell shading, and a Jason Bourne-style super spy government betrayal plot where different kinds of kills take time off of your total, making negative times possible. It feels just incredible to play, and the soundtrack is wonderful (sidenote, I'm very glad they changed how climbing worked from the demo). It's just such a blast to play and the story is a good time, too.Once in a while you run into a technical hiccup (like just very rarely you will get caught on geometry) and yeah that's somewhat annoying to run into if the run is going well, but it's so uncommon and the game is so otherwise tight it doesn't matter. Plus it was built in like 9 months. That said, I do think it's annoying when I still have to do all the challenge levels, but I beat the story and it's just such a fun game. Any gripes I have are nitpicks, and if you're craving more Neon White (which I was) I recommend it wholeheartedly.

_childDocuments_.review: This is going to have a short and long section.The short: If you're debating on getting the game, get it. The devs deserve every single cent. You don't need to be good at shooters to be good at this, the game does a good job of "helping things along" and is quite forgiving. That being said, trying to get max rank is quite challenging.The Long: It's a fast paced narrative shooter, with a 9/10 possibly even a 10/10 sound track and voice acting. The story while it isn't necessary original I would genuinely be invested in it if it were to become a book series. The humor is witty and light-hearted. I found myself immediately invested in the main character, and all the side characters along the way. I found myself caring for them, and while it might not initially seem like it fits, it compliments the story so well. This game may have found it's way onto my Mount Rushmore. It's just so enjoyable. Truly a lightning in a bottle game. The only criticism I can give it is that it's short. It's well worth the money, even at full price, but it's short. Overall if I had to give a 1-10 this game lands firmly at a 9.7/10 for me, phenomenal job. In summary : If you like good stories, with a terrifying protagonist that you somehow still can empathize with, you'll enjoy this. All around, this is a winner. Congratulations Strange Scaffold, you've made a fan out of me. Now give me more of this magic.

_childDocuments_.review: Cannot rave enough. An absolutely beautiful game. The format is very similar to Portal--a relatively short story with a few challenge levels in addition. Each of the levels are designed to be speed-ran, with the S-ranks being relatively difficult to get. It only takes a few hours to complete the campaign, but getting all the S's takes around 10 hours. The graphics are amazing, runs very smooth. Shooting feels amazing, and picking up/shooting the guns is nearly instantaneous. The level design is very good. Most levels require a decent amount of thought put into both the route and your mechanics. There is interesting usage of movement mechanics, and a very wide variety of ways to kill enemies.The story is IMO the highlight of the game. The voice acting is absurdly good--far better than I expect from indie games, and better than most AAA. It takes a classic formula (Special operative gets one last job) but somehow feels very different. The story doesn't insist upon itself, but the themes and implications of what you are forced(?) to do makes it very interesting.EDIT: Took about 20 hours to get every achievement in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I Am Your Beast is a game that is really hard to compare to other games, it has the level structure and rank system of a game like Ultrakill, it has the somewhat improvisational nature of using the environment against your enemies, and the feeling of mastery over a level coming essentially knowing where everything is of the Hitman games, it has amazing music, the cutscenes are admittedly pretty forgettable overall but that story really is just the perfect cherry on top. Harding is an interesting character and hearing the way he talks about wanting to be left to the forest is honestly extremely nice. Most of the levels are extremely well made with the only real exception to my taste being the final level that kind of just throws every item in the game at you in abundance and tells you to have fun. while it is quite fun its a little underwhelming in terms of difficulty.Overall the game has this extremely gratifying process of getting S rank on all the levels while you build a route and try to perfect it as best you can, its always extremely rewarding finding little off paths to save time or shortcuts that get you between objectives faster. Its similar in feeling to that of P - ranking Ultrakill in that feeling of gaining mastery of a level and with it a deeper understanding of the games mechanics as a wholeRaw mechanically I do think that I am your Beast is honestly one of the most unique games ive ever played. its system of scavenging weapons between enemies with limited ammo, going for more interesting kills or making decisions on the fly to save a little time. I am your Beast feels like a game made for speedrunning and that feeling of small improvements is absolutely tremendous. If I could only ask for one thing i really would like to have the ability to beat the times set by the authors of the levels themselves kind of like track-mania in a way, i think it could be a very interesting challenge for those wanting to grind a little harder.Other than that, the enemy AI is equivalent to that of a toaster but it ultimately doesn't matter, the music is some of the best in a game Ive ever heard, PLEASE GOD DONT MAKE ME STOP SPRINTING AFTER KICKING ITS SO SLUGGISH FEELING AND INTERRUPTS THE ENTIRE FEELING OF FLOW THE GAME IS BUILT ON EITHER MAKE IT NOT STOP MY SPRINT AT ALL OR MAKE IT SO THAT REPRESSING THE KEY WILL ALSO MAKE IT INSTANTLY START AGAIN PLEASE.Other than that the game really is amazing and one of a kind, fast paced while also being grounded, it can require quick thinking and reflexes but sometimes you can use your head a bit more and discover new routes and paths possible. Replay-ability and skill expression at its best
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Criminally short, but equally well worth buying. 1 and a half hours to beat the campaign, but absolutely no regrets. Amazingly satisfying combat, outstanding sound track, and a shockingly good story delivered with impeccable voice acting. Everything about this game hits. Strange Scaffold, it seems, just doesn't miss. The combat is fast, snappy, punchy, and satisfying. The speed is just right. The maps are well designed and objectives well thought out. Levels will push you in just the right way to get better every time you play. I won't say the game is necessarily "highly" replayable, but it's certainly got some value in mastering levels. Getting S rank on some missions is honestly absurdly difficult. Some seem way easier than others. Almost laughably easy on some, then impossibly hard on others. My only gripe about the game is how you need to get S rank on certain missions to unlock the bonus stages. I love replaying levels and getting better at them, but when I'm down to finishing a level in 9 seconds with only headshots and taking no damage at all, then only getting an A rank...I really don't feel that urge to keep trying. Feeling a necessity to search how to get an S rank on a mission you're blitzing through like a god feels...bad. It drains the fun out because it feels like I'm doing the best I could possibly do, yet it's not only not enough, but isn't telling me what I'm missing. It's not time, and it's not quick or efficient kills. The level unlock system is just a bit offputting, especially given it's mainly for the bonus levels. Some unlock in other ways, but it's a system I think the game would just be better without. That is seriously my only complaint. I absolutely adored my time with this game. I didn't expect the side story to be endearing, nor did I expect a delightful twist that is simple, but satisfying. The VA is just as stellar as it was in El Paso, Everywhere, and it is absolutely delightful to hear. This game is just an absolute riot. I wish there was more, but I'm glad they didn't drag it out to the point of tedium. This is, simply put, an absolute delight to play. It also doesn't arrogantly call itself a "John Wick Simulator". There is a shocking number of trashy indie games that do that, then end up sucking. The fact this game not only embodies that simple, normally outright incorrect, description well is a simple thing, but a notable one. You feel strong, but not invincible. It's a lot of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I Am Your Best is a fast, punchy and stylish shooter that feels a bit like Neon White got the John Wick license. It's very focused and slick, a lot of its basic verbs are designed to make you feel cool - one button to throw a gun, big THUNK feedback when things explode or get shot, instantly clambering up trees or sliding through the snow. It's good fun and really compactly designed.

_childDocuments_.review: I love hitstop, I love hitstop, I love histop.Writing this after completing the campaign. I really, really enjoyed the game. The action is frenetic, quick, and finely tuned, and you end up feeling invincible once you're able to map out the best path and execute it. The music is so perfect, and I'm excited for whenever it releases. The voice acting is incredible too. I kept saying "wow this is so cool" during the whole campaign. _childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic so far. First of all, Linux people, it runs beautifully with Proton 9. I didn't have to do any fooling around with it, and I have no gameplay, visual, or audio issues.Beyond that there isn't much to say that hasn't already been said, but I'll give it a shot. The animation and art style is fantastic. I couldn't ask for a more visually pleasing game. I don't play FPS games much, and I've never played anything this fast paced, but even for my newbie self it is not too hard once you get into the swing of it. the physics are super fun and relatively easy to wrap your mind around. The difficulty ramps up pretty naturally as well, I have yet to feel like I've hit a massive wall so to speak and I am a pretty good ways in. The sound track is fantastic, and matches the vibe of the game incredibly well (looking forward to that being released separately.All in all, I have no complaints and am having a grand old time. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: === the good:- presentation is fantastic- maps are (mostly) not confusing and very hard to get lost in- optional challenges are great- game feels well paced when played linearly (except when it asks you to redo levels)- controls are great- game has a good sense of "flow" with picking up weapons and moving around- 90% sure at least one bisexual character- levels are all distinct, never really a boring tired environment- no bugs or glitches in the game that i saw or was able to notice, besides maybe 1 with ai spawning.- game never stutters or drops framerate- great cracking tunes (music)=== the bad:- this game forces you to replay levels, sometimes tens of times if you arent a "pro gamer" like the developers expect- the game (as of september 15th) still lacks a "no timers" mode, which is slightly annoying. this is planned for post launch content, i might edit this once its in.- several times where explosions were larger or smaller than one would think, and a certain projectile weapon doesnt shoot projectiles out of where you'd think it would visually- ai feels lacking and groups up, and other times you can visually watch them spawn.- game has no uncapped framerate mode, instead has the options of vsync (limit to your monitor's refresh rate) or a custom frame limiter option up to 120 fps. i would PREFER an option to do DOUBLE my refresh ratefor 17.99 definitely a steal.
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve never written a review on Steam, but what a phenomenal game! _childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: This game is extremely fun...most of the time. When all the controls are working properly (which is unfortunately an issue with this game), you feel like an unstoppable force of nature running through these levels and trying to beat your previous times. Unfortunately, the controls not working properly plagued the majority of my playthrough. Sprinting doesn't seem to work at times and really needs to be fixed. The amount of runs I had to restart because the sprinting decided to stop working was egregious. Item pick ups are often prioritized over objective interaction ( even when you're looking directly at an objective) which is also a design choice that feels like it should be addressed. I even had some drops in input when trying to do actions simultaneously which is again something that shouldn't be present in a game the requires precision with your inputs. Weapon accuracy felt all over the place at times too. It feels like there's an auto-aim aspect to the game that isn't consistent. It feels like it can really mess up your shots if you're say trying to shoot a barrel next to an enemy and the shots aren't going where you feel like you're aiming. Hitboxes on explosive barrels and tripwire devices are pretty rough in places too.This game is at it's best when it embraces simplicity in it's level design and doesn't try to go overly complicated with item and enemy placement. The story levels are well done although the bonus objectives can be a bit silly and the game should unlock them if I happened to do them before they unlock after beating a level. The narrative is simple, but fun and is voice acted quite well.The challenge levels are much more miss than hit for me especially if you're attempting to S-Rank them. I wasn't a fan of how the actual levels were designed for a lot of those and it soured my experience a bit. At times, they require a level of precision that the game doesn't really allow for and it felt like the only challenge from them came from fighting how the game controlled more than anything else. One other random issue I had is that when killing enemies, their weapons do not drop consistently and will sometimes either fall through the map or just go flying in a way that makes it impossible to grab them which can kill a run. I also really feel like some of the challenge level S-Ranks could be lowered a bit.Overall, outside of a few issues, it's a fun game that I couldn't put down until I mastered every level.
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most unique games in terms of style, energy and overall vibe. The gameplay is incredible (kinda plays like Neon White but more combat focused rather than parkour, even if there is parkour here), the story is surprisingly good and the voice acting might be one of the best I've heard. Oh yea and the ost ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slaps so hard
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: There's an elegance to a game that is simple, but compelling far beyond the last level. Burnout. Doom. Ace Combat. I Am Your Beast is an addition to that list. This is an incredibly simple game in terms of what you actually do. Shoot enemies, run to the finish, repeat. It's the context of how you're shooting enemies (blowing up barrels, dropping bees on them, throwing bear traps into their faces while running across a tightrope) and how it feels to do it (awesome) that makes the game stand out. IAYB is short, with interesting visuals and a narrative with valuable lessons about taking no for an answer. It's only 2-3 hours to "finish", but if you're like me and crave the almighty S-Rank, you'll spend many more hours than that running the levels again. Faster. Deadlier. Faster still. Crucially, you won't get tired of it.
_childDocuments_.name: I Am Your Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like a mash between Neon White, Hotline Miami, and Superhot. Gameplay is very satisfying, levels generally well designed, music is nice, voice acting is surprisingly good, story is not what we're here for, but it gets you between levels. I played this as a palate cleanser and recommend it as such!
