_childDocuments_.review: is a really unique game, and one of my favorite 2024 releases thus far. It plays like an old school dungeon crawler mixed with a 2000s JRPG and . You control a party of four, each member of the party has a word for you to solve. You fight enemies in real time, or turn-based combat (the choice is yours), and type out your character's abilities to make them act. Upon defeating enemies you can choose a letter from their name to take. Your chosen letter is then revealed for all of your living party members. If you think you know one of the words you can type it out at any time- aside from combat- and unlock new skills for your party if you guess successfully. Generally,  does a great job of making use of its word based mechanics in different ways. For example, you're also able to reveal letters from catching fish, and some skills are case dependent such as "do 2 damage for each 'N' in the enemy's name". Certain enemies will also forbid the use of certain letters, or go stronger when particular words are typed. These distinctions create a purpose for variety within combat scenarios, and encourage you to make full use of your abilities. While the premise is great, it's backed up by an interesting world filled with wacky characters. There are hilarious NPC interactions, and quite a few funny moments throughout the game, many of which showcase the developers understanding of gaming tropes, and sometimes poke fun at them in a Deadpool-lite manner. While hard to describe perfectly,  is easy to understand once you're playing. It's honestly a great entry point for newer gamers; I completed the game playing with a non-gamer friend who's super into word games, and they loved it. I would like to throw out a few criticisms though, the first being the strict specifications on the utility of each character. It feels like nearly all of the heal/revive skills are on one character, so if that character dies while your others are alive, you might as well backtrack to a checkpoint. Especially because once characters die new letters you claim won't be revealed in their words, so in a sense you're losing potential progress by not healing, and it doesn't feel great knowing that happened because the RNG decided to randomly repeatedly target your healer in that encounter. My only other complaint involved the souls; killing enemies, and catching fish and bugs rewards souls. Using any of your characters skills, outside of the four they start the game with, costs souls. At times my friend was struggling with the combat, ran out of souls, and ended up killing our party trying to use abilities that they don't have enough souls to use (even if they were only trying to heal out of combat). In general, I find this system is more likely to punish people who are having a harder time with the game, while being completely trivial for those who aren't, so what's the point? Plus it can encourage grinding, which isn't great. That being said, I absolutely love when smaller developers get creative, and  is easily one of the most inventive games I've played in recent years. I absolutely loved it and highly recommend it. For less experienced gamers, switching to turn-based mode if you're struggling will create a much more approachable experience.  is one of a kind, and of superb quality.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR:I've beaten the game at this point and it really was a breath of fresh air. A fun, puzzle-typing game that was maybe a little too easy on the combat overall, but provided the best range of difficulty in terms of in world puzzles and riddles. From super easy, to takes a few minutes, to the community is working together to solve them. The art style and presentation are both cool and unsettling, the voice acting is amazing, and the writing is pretty witty and fun. 9/10.Pros:+ Story:The story is interesting from the jump. A group of ragtag and raggedy adventurer corpses being resurrected by what clearly seems like a nefarious entity is a fun concept. Pretty sure what I'm about to do isn't good, but I'm here for it.+ Voice Acting:The voice acting is really good. Talked to the likes of the Cryptmaster, some rats, a couple doors, a toad king, etc. All the voices are pretty spot on. The Cryptmaster is deep and suspicious, the rats are jolly good chaps, the doors are booming and authoritative, and the toad king is... sexy???+ WritingThe writing is fun and witty without feeling forced. The Cryptmaster is kinda an a-hole, but in a lovable and I'm going to tolerate this disrespect because he did bring me back to life, kind of way. The save points are altars where you have to actively disrespect the goddess it's dedicated to and she seems genuinely flustered and upset at what you have to do to save. The game has a clear sense of humor and it makes you smile. Also, the devs covered a LOT of bases in interactions. At times you can see where the limitations arise, but you can type some pretty wild stuff and get a new interaction.+ Puzzles:Oh man the puzzles here so far are simple yet fun. Basically a guessing game. The Cryptmaster hanging out with you will open chests and boxes and you have a certain amount of guesses to get what's in it. You can request certain things like look, touch, remember, etc to help you figure it out. Some are super easy and some have you take a pause for a minute. Another puzzle is just lying to characters who ask you questions. You can tell the truth, but not everyone wants to hear the truth. Then there are skull piles that tell more general or well known riddles. Then there are other puzzles like the crypticisms. Those are real sneaky and require either lots of exploration or paying close attention from the start.+ Gameplay:The gameplay is super simple, but in a good way. It feels like exploring an old school 2D text adventure game, but in 3D. Arrow keys to move, grid layout for movement, and typing nonsense to make your way through the game.Mixed:+/- MapThere doesn't really seem to be an in game map you can pull up. There is a map option, but it seems to just show you warp points. You can use that to jump to the major or relevant rooms in an area. You also have a constant mini map at the top of the screen that shows you the full layout of the room. These things are great, but I do wish there was a more detailed map that showed how the areas connect. It's neither easy nor hard to get lost, but a map you can check out would make navigation easier.Cons:- ReadabilityWhile I really dig the art style and presentation of this game, it is kinda difficult to figure out exactly what you're looking at sometimes. It's not a huge detriment as important things are both marked on your map and stand out pretty well, but looking at the environment can sometimes make you go cross-eyed.- Mouse CursorCan confirm this has been fixed!- Camera SpeedThere is an option to move the camera to look around, but most of the time you'll just turn in the direction you want to look. Because it's a grid system you're turning 90 degrees at a time. The speed the camera moves combined with the art style can be disorienting at times.-DifficultyThe game could stand to maybe be a bit more difficult in terms of combat. The difficulty increases as you remember more words and actions and try to manage your soul resource (using skills outside of the most basic one requires soul points), but unless you just blank on what to type or completely mismanage your resources it's not the most challenging experience out there.Review:The game is real good. Even though you're a bunch of old and stinky corpses coming out of a crypt, the game is a breath of fresh air. It's easy to start up and play and is fairly low commitment. I thought the typing might be House of the Dead style and require speed and precision, but it really doesn't. The game is more about strategy and memorization rather than just typing a bunch of words as fast as you can. Characters have cooldowns so even if you speed through words it doesn't just mean you win. I was looking for some smaller games to play while waiting for the Elden Ring expansion and I have to say this was a good find. It's made me smile multiple times in the first hour just at the sheer unique feel and solid writing. None of the issues I have with the game make it a deal breaker and they are all more nitpicks than anything else.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Cryptmaster has a simple concept, is highly stylized, and a ton of fun. The gameplay mechanic ties in neatly with the narrative, and it doesn't take itself too seriously. The mini game Whatever is addictive and has a good enough mix of RNG and strategy that has me going back for rematches until I beat an opponent. However, it would also greatly benefit from having a world map or at least a visual representation of where players are apart from the minimap, which doesn't anchor to North. Many a times I've found myself going around in circles looking for quest items just because there is simply no way to track which rooms I've been in. This doesn't make the game unplayable though as each area is generally small and rooms look distinct enough (mostly).I will also say that the opening of chests becomes a tad mechanical after a while, as you default on a few key phrases to help you decipher the items.Still, I adore this very solid game and think you will sink more hours into it than you expect.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely not perfect but I had a lot of fun with it and I loved the concept. In this day and age, it's really hard to do anything unique and the Wordle element was implemented differently than I'd seen anywhere else.The story is a lot of fun, as are the characters and the fact that you can type in anything and get a response. Occasionally you'll get some repeated things when the game doesn't know what to do but the amount of things you can type in and get real responses for is impressive. The voices are fun and there are some good moments throughout. The writing is pretty humorous at times. I also LOVED the art and sound design for this game. Top notch. Puts most AAA games to shame.As for gripes, my biggest one is that the game is very grindy if you're looking to unlock all of the character memories and skills. It also generally got grindy for me on act 3 since the enemies were so hard and I was running low on souls constantly. Sometimes enemies, fish and bugs weren't spawning in areas and I either had to wait or reload the game to try to get more letters to level up with. Enemies also get harder in earlier areas after you move on, so that wasn't an option either. I ended up never figuring out a good way to farm. At the end of the game, I didn't even have half of the memories/skills unlocked on any character and had no motivation to go back and figure that part out again.I would have loved to have a list of unlocked skills somewhere on the screen to reference during the fight instead of tucked away in a menu I have to open. Usually I stuck to just a few skills in battle because I couldn't remember or find a use for the rest. The puzzles and riddles were ok. I was able to figure out most without help (and I am bad at puzzles).Overall this a 7/10 experience for me and I will definitely be keeping an eye on this developer to see what they do next.

_childDocuments_.review: While playing Cryptmaster, one word kept drifting to the front: DELIGHTFULThe irony here. is that the game is about four desecrated corpses of fallen heroes having been pulled from their graves to go and destroy the city they fought and died for for while they were alive and it's a delightful experience - all in a gritty black and white cell shading art style. Allow me to justify that a little. In essence, the game is a type (as in tippy-tappy on your keyboard) based RPG that also leans heavy on riddles and wordplay. The characters Joro, Syn, Maz and Nix each have skills you can unlock by figuring out what their recently reanimated brains are trying to remember and this functions like the hangman game, with you adding letters and completing the word. The chests you open do not give armor or swords, but rather, letters you can use to figure out the next word. This is done a little like the 20-Questions game, only, you only get five to guess the object.Sofar, this all sounds like it could go horribly . Yet..., where it goes  is the implementation. The characters do not only remember their skills, but also who they were before dying. Their backstories and the contrast of what they are currently made to do becoming all the more clear. The writing is simply amazing and the voice acting right-on with the back-and-forth with the narrator (the utterly charismatic Cryptmaster) and NPC's standing out because they really put a hell of a lot of effort into doing that right. I will use a slight spoiler as an example:To pass a door right at the start of the game, you are asked simple questions to prove that you are "alive" (even though you are not). Question one: What was the last fruit you ate? You put in your response and off you go. Question two: Describe the sun.On this one, I decided to be right clever and type in "Star" and not only did it work, but the door commented on me being a "clever one".   That moment there was utterly  and it is one of .The game goes so far out of it's way to give you little delightful moments, that yes, that is the word for this game. It's full of little surprises; Little bits of wordplay; Little quips and comments from the Cryptmaster that will keep you delighted. As a last note: If your grasp of the English language is good and you can type relatively fast, then this game is an absolute must and I would even advise getting it on full price. It definitely is on my shortlist of games that every person out there should experience, and that list is very VERY short. Yes, it is THAT good.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly smart game so far.It's basically somewhere between an old school dungeon grinder, one of those real-time typing games like The Typing Of The Dead or Epistory, and a word puzzle.You move through a stylized dungeon in 90° turns and fixed movement. You fight by typing words in realtime (stronger and longer words are costlier, each character has a free attack). If you get attacked, you lose letters from your characters, their names actually shorter (consequently, increasing your max-HP means you get to pick an extra letter to append to their name!). When you win, you get to pick letters from the enemy's name and those will "reveal" letters in the unfinished words under each character.At any time, you can try type in whatever you feel is under a character. If you're correct, you'll get either new skills for them or more of their background story.Also, you can just always... type stuff. And the eponymous Cryptmaster accompanying you will react to just about . It's ridiculous how much they recorded for this character. You can also ask him to just, well, WIN. Hey it's worth a short, right? :P

_childDocuments_.review: I get what the developers are going for and commend them for their hard work and novel idea. However, there is not much meat on this bone. For the 25 USD price point the game has not met my expectations. Combat is lacking, some mechanics are straight up bad and should be removed, and the game can soft lock you repeatedly during random encountersThe setup of the game is simple. You type words to execute an action or attack. You find new actions or attacks by revealing words one at the time per character. The way the game helps you discover the words is through combat, which reveals 1 letter you choose, or through riddles, where the letters in the answer will apply to all of the characters speeding up the discovery proces.The combat is based on the player typing these discovered words. - One of the main gripes I have with combat is the cooldown mechanic. It completely removes the player's typing speed from the combat skill equation: How fast you can type only matters at the initial attacks, after that you just line up the words and hit enter after the character's cooldown expires. - There is also not a lot of variety in attacks between characters- Some words (like  or ) do the same thing on the same character. - The overview of all the unlocked 'words' (i.e. attacks) mixes the important attack words with other useless 'memory' words that have no use throughout the game- Enemies have a shield that can soft lock you (You unlock  early on in the game for . If the shield enemies have  before being able to do damage. An enemy shield that states any of the letters that are used in the word can counter it, making it so you can't progress and just have to wait for your party to die. - The exploring gets old quickly. All areas start to look the same. Rocks, grass, a wooden door and rampart. It never really changes. The black and white visuals do little to redeem this and perhaps even add to the repetitive look of the dungeon. The rooms you will explore can be quite big. As a dungeon crawler it makes sense you want to explore these rooms, but the game does nothing to reward you for it. You can waste a lot of time navigating all the nooks and crannies of the map, expecting perhaps a chest or puzzle, but instead be rewarded with more black and white walls.The riddles are great and are a nice addition to the game. The mental switch from 'Wordle Dungeon Crawler' to solving riddles is fun and feels good. Not all riddles are equal though, some are unoriginal and you've probably heard before many times whereas others are quite clever and new. The one thing they completely messed up is that not all riddles have the correct answer. Early on the game acknowledges this in the . The riddle  can be given multiple answers and the NPC will reply with . You can answer  and all will be true and counted as such.Later in the game this completely goes away. For example the riddle  requires the answer , but a)  and  should also fit. Or . There are many riddles that can be given multiple answers to in this game and I was hoping, due to the core mechanic being trial and error inputting words, the game would accommodate this throughout the game.This makes solving riddles much more frustrating and less fun. It makes it feel abitrary. It highlights the fact that the 'dungeon master' that you interact with has much more limited interactions than you'd expect at first. The game also has a big difficulty spike at  when it comes to riddles. There is one where you straight up need . It makes the pacing feel weird and the new area feel like a brick wall which I am sure will discourage a lot of players. You can have the narrator literally give you the answer after 1 or 2 tries, but for a game about solving riddles, where is the fun in that.You are probably not buying this for the story but rather for the gameplay mechanics described above. If you mainly want a good dungeon crawler story, this is not the game for you. The characters in this story are weak and interchangeable. Your party of heroes consist of mutes. The game tells you to talk to NPCs and interact with them using action keywords like 'talk', 'use' or anything contextual. But 90% of the time you can't talk to the NPCs and the dungeon master gives you the same reply again and again. 'You will talk when I will tell you to' as you roll your eyes and move towards the next door on your map. The fun and interesting parts in the story are few and far between.The game has an insane amount of potential. It just needs a lot more polish and more thought into the design elements of the game. The gameplay loop could use a review. The combat needs a complete overhaul that caters more towards typing fast while remembering the words you unlocked, removing the cooldowns or making them much shorter will be a great start. Currently the game to me is a 4 or 5 out of 10 because of the reasons mentioned above. With some more TLC it can be a 7 or 8.

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliantly original mixture of word games and old-school grid-based dungeon crawling like the Ultima games . The dialogue system where you type in any word and the characters respond accordingly feels magical. The way you level up by simply guessing the name of your next skill (with letter hints unlocked by various methods) is genius. The writing is genuinely funny with great voice acting, and some of the puzzles are fantastic, especially the variation on the old 'two guards' riddle.I am not usually a fan of grid-based exploration, but finding your way around isn't too confusing (apart from one specific puzzle with simple solution) and you won't need to break out the grid paper to draw a map. There is a mini-map that shows the local area, but it would be nice to have an option to see a world map that fills in as you explore (maybe as a New Game+ option).It's not a long game (it took me about 16 hours to finish the story, although you could rush through it a lot quicker), but once you finish the story there is more to do: there's a great card mini-game you can play with a lot of the characters, plus some optional 'crypticisms' to solve. It's a shame that finishing the story ends the game and you have to go back to your last save - it would be really nice if you could watch the ending and then carry on in a world that reflects your choices in the story somewhat, although I appreciate that would be a fair amount of extra work for the devs.If I had to be critical, the need to replenish the reserve of 'souls' that powers your combat abilities can mean you end up doing a bit too much bug collecting and fishing, which get slightly boring. The final couple of areas of the game are also not quite as strong as the rest. Overall I would strongly recommend getting this if you have any interest at all in RPGs or word games and riddles. I hope this sells a million copies so the devs can make a sequel on a grander scale.

_childDocuments_.review: As a word/puzzle game, Cryptmaster does a pretty solid job at creating novel mechanics peppered with fun riddles and language based puzzles.  For that reason, alongside the beautiful art style, engaging soundtrack, solid (if sometimes exhaustive) writing, and top tier voice acting, I wanted to love this game.  The problem is my least favorite aspects of the game are the combat and exploration.  The two things you spend the most time doing: fighting and exploring.Despite having seemingly infinite flexibility with the combat system, most skills feel repetitive and simply unfun.  Combined with long timers in the 'realtime' combat that force you to sit and eat hits, I found myself dreading every encounter.  Especially towards the end where enemies have many letters and I spent maybe 5 seconds playing and 30 seconds waiting and doing nothing PER encounter.  Oh, and you can't flee.When you explore, there are chests and skulls with riddles to supplement finding new skills and to recharge your 'souls.'  These were fairly fun.  But they are sprinkled throughout large monochromatic empty rooms that can get rather disorienting.  The movement system seems designed more for traversal through small rooms and solving escape room-like puzzles, as you move one cell at a time and look in one of the four cardinal directions.  It's serviceable in theory, but not for moving hundreds of cells exploring several rooms usually looking for a single person/object for your quest.  Good thing these giant rooms are loaded with plenty of enemies to fight!... Ah, there's the problem.Truthfully, despite the investment, I grew really tired with the game by the end.  Especially since   Overall, I'd recommend watching someone stream the game. Not to save money, but because to me, it was 10x more enjoyable to watch than play.  It felt like a 4-5hr solid experience that was fluffed into a 8-10hr one.  So much potential, and can be a genuinely good time, but just seemed to try and juggle too much and missed too many marks.

_childDocuments_.review: I love typing games, and this is a glorious specimen.  For those of you who are looking for more Typing of the Dead (because who doesn't want more Typing of the Dead?), this has a lot of that, but keep in mind that it's a little more thinky, especially in realtime combat -- for example, you might meet a monster who is wearing a shield that negates any T, so you can't use attacks with a T in them.  You also have a set of fixed attack-words for each character which you learn slowly as you play, as opposed to having words appear over the monster's heads like in TOTD, so you can't just mindlessly type in combat.  (There are plenty of situations where you can mindlessly type, just combat isn't one of them.)The "crafting" system, such as it is, is also letter-based, .  There's also a silly  which will no doubt consume many hours of game-time for me.  Letters!  EVERYTHING is made of letters.All that aside, the characters/VA are hilarious, the riddles are cheesy but fine, the FOMO from chests is real, and the unique black-and-white level design is fantastic.  This game is a total winner.  I only wish you could strafe, turning 90 degrees over and over gets a bit old.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and refreshing at first, I really wanted to like the game and there are a lot of individually enjoyable elements. Many of the Cryptmaster's responses elicit a laugh, the -very- few that are ideologically driven feel in good jest and easily ignored.Overall though it becomes rather stale and repetitive, you fall into the same actions over and over and that just starts to wear on the whole experience. Unfortunately it ended up feeling like a chore to sit down and play- the mechanics are neat but the game never adds ways to optimize out or simplify your engagement as it goes on in order to keep the inherent repetitive nature of the combat loop fresh.I do appreciate that you can crank up the number of letters you get at the end of combat, but it feels like a token effort that only reduces the grind, not change it in any fundamental way. It's a great premise but I can't help but feel something could be done to further improve it.Give the demo a try, it is representative of the whole experience so if you think you will enjoy it 10 hours in just pick it up.

_childDocuments_.review: Pains me to say that despite my admiration for the spelling concept (typing gameplay), the art direction and the voice acting, I didn't love the game, on the contrary.(For the record I stopped after talking to Ulara and reading her library scrolls)I got my eye on it after playing the demo, but the more I played the full game, the more it delved far away from my good graces, as it grew harder, oddly designed and more frustating than anything.Early on you are shown that you can "play" with words and produce awkward moments. This was a delight and felt very organic ! And the writing in Cryptmaster is top notch really.But after a while you see it was only pretending, and there are more and more limits. After the "prologue", you realize you can't actually make litteral conversations with NPC on topics that would make sense. You are forced to use story-driven vocabulary most of the time to trigger any meaningful dialogs other than "not interested in talking about that" or "I didn't understand what you say".As for the fights, maybe it's my own fault, but I can't memorize the many skills of each character. It feels overwhelming and I ended up using the very first words (I assume being the equivalent of low level abilities) in the game such as "hit", "boot", "jab" etc And hope to be alive in the end, spamming "soothe" to heal up my team before resuming my journey.This lead to a game getting more difficult for me, and not the enjoyable way.Perhaps keeping the basic skills from the start only, and allowing to level them up with additional effects as you progressed could have been an option ? Or better yet, allow players to rename skills by themselves.Also, I'd say I found the environnement pretty empty for their size and number. Some areas are big, and basically all rooms are samish, more or less. Except to pick insects up or find riddle skulls (which are easely spotted by a mere look at the map), there is barely no reason to lurk, and thus no reason to make rooms so large (and so many !).I'm not even mentionning the fact that the map displayed onscreen is rotating as the player turns around, which is very annoying to keep track of things. I'd rather have a key to display a complete map of the whole region too, than a room-by-room map.Now then, the riddles ! The demo didn't expand much on that part other than guessing a few items. It is only with the full release that I got the impression something was brewing. I never liked riddles in general, although I felt pretty proud finding out the answers to the most of them at the beginning ! However the more you go on, and the more vicious, dumb or terrible they are. This eventually got on my nerves.Finally the game isn't clear about the saving state. All I am sure about is that it saves whenever I come across an Altar, which are scarce. But that is a very stupid way to set things in a dungeon crawler. Especially when the exploration takes so much time. I wish there was a manual save system, because if you leave the game inadvenertently, only god knows where and when you'll resume when you launch it next time.So I got a game in which I couldn't talk to people the way I wanted in order to flesh the lore out a little more, in which I can't fight confortably enough to appreciate my encounters, in which I had to look for halve of the answers in the forum or google, in which I got tired of moving through uselessly big and mazy places with an helpless map system, and in which I can't even save whenever I need to.Very disappointed, because I saw potential, but it was all far too unbearable at some point, to call it a good memory in the end. I'm just glad for people enjoying it because I can see how original it stands these days.

_childDocuments_.review: This checks a lot of the right boxes for certain people. As an elder millennial, I grew up on old-school PC dungeon crawlers and text-based RPGs and MUDs. This is an excellent combination of the two genres with far more interesting interactions, at least equal story-telling with voice-acting, very intriguing visuals, and fun riddles/puzzles along the way. There was often a lot of humor and love put into those older games, so I can't say the humor is better, but it is definitely a game with a decent sense of humor - especially when trying some of the more off-the-wall suggestions that are typed.The game doesn't have kid gloves and lets you type stupid ♥♥♥♥ you don't think will work but totally does. SPOILER: The short of it: It's a very unique game for 2024, and I'm glad to see it. Vibes of Inscryption mixed with Might and Magic mixed with King's Quest mixed with a book of riddles. Fully recommend if you want to be entertained, and scratch your brain for a while.QUICK NOTE: There is timed typing-based combat. If you have a good memory and can touch type, you will have an easier time with this game. If you need to hunt and peck, things will get challenging!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This is a fun and unique spin on RPGs with the main mechanic being that your only way to interact with the world is one word at a time. You get to kill enemies with an interesting and dynamic combat system and solve puzzles that are fun and interesting especially if you enjoy word puzzles and riddles. Combat is done in real time with commands that need to typed to make characters take certain actions with cooldowns based on the character and ability used. There is also a turn-based option for those who either wish to have more time to make decisions or are slower at typing out words due to dyslexia or similar issues. There are also some mechanics that require specific actions to deal with them like enemies that have armor thus requiring one of your characters to use their ability to break it and thus causing you to need to think ahead or take more hits from the enemies. I really like this system of combat, but it can feel a bit repetitive especially in the earlier parts of the game before you have a decent variety of actions.The characters and setting are great I love trying different things to see if I can find a new response from them. There is a surprising  amount of viable things that you can say to most of the npcs within reason and get a proper response. The main limitation is that you can only type a single word, thus requiring simple responses. I feel that the game does a decent job of maneuvering the conversation in a way that allows for one word responses while still feeling like you get to play an active role in it.Ability unlocking is probably one of my favorite things in this game. It is done by gaining letters that can be obtained from killing enemies and taking a certain number of letters from their name (number taken depends on settings. I recommend the default) or solving puzzles which can range from riddle solving to guessing the name of an item based on certain hints that you get to ask for. There is also fishing which gives a letter from the name of the fish that you can try to time and get the one you want or just take a random one. You then guess what you think the name of the ability is based on the letters you've acquired. interspersed with ability unlocks is additional background info for the characters in your party.I absolutely love text based rpgs and this scratches that itch and then some.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first Dungeon Crawler I've played in a long while and I loved it! The characters are all super charming and also hilarious! The Cryptmaster himself is the true star of the show though, I love how stereotypically evil he is lol. A lot of the riddles and puzzles were challenging, and most are optional content, but it was nice that there was the option to have the Cryptmaster solve them if you are really stumped. Combat, especially later on, really ramps up, but it's not so difficult that it's impossible and there are ways to avoid enemies or make combat a bit easier. You can tell that everyone involved with this game poured their heart and soul into it (pun intended) to make this game as fun as possible! I highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a charming Dungeon Crawler experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: The game relies heavily in it's premise of typing to battle and explore stuff, witch is a nice premise. Problem here is that it gets old very fast. The gameplay loop is really repetitive, and the story and characters are not good enough to carry that flaw. It's very rare for me to get bored of a game before i even finish it once, but this game did it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: The easiest way to think of Cryptmaster is as follows: take an old-school dungeon crawling blobber like Wizardry or Might and Magic, remove all colour from it, start the adventure by killing the characters, let them rot for a while to make sure their brains are good and fried, resurrect them and replace all their weapons with thesauri. Bam, instant classic!Cryptmaster is a party-based RPG playing in the style of a 'blobber', where the entire party is represented by a big 'blob' occupying a square on a grid and they have to fight similarly-sized opponents in tight quarters. While the genre has been floating around since the beginnings of PC gaming, there have been recent additions to it like Legend of Grimrock. However, the perspective and general idea are where the similarities between the genre and Cryptmaster end, as Cryptmaster is really only HALF RPG. The other half is an English exam. Every significant way for you to interact with the world is achieved by typing.And I mean EVERY way. Your party gets into (real-time) combat with a monster. Attack it by telling the Barbarian to HIT! The Rogue to STAB! The Sea-witch to conjure CRABS! And the Bard to SOOTHE wounds! Well done, you have defeated RATICUS the rat. All of the letters in his name appear beneath your characters as part of their next unlockable skill, allowing you to play 4-way Hangman in order to guess them ahead of time. RATICUS was guarding a BOX, which contains a talking skull who's going to give you a riddle. Answer correctly and you'll get the solution's letters! But there's an important NPC you have to talk to in one-word responses, and much like in another well-known RPG, they're all ready for a card game whenever. So just ask them to play WHATEVER!And throughout all this, the necromancer who raised you from the dead, the titular Cryptmaster, is right at your side. His brain is almost as badly fried as your party's (as he attempts to remember objects that he describes the SMELL and TASTE of to you), but he's far more capable of snark as he reacts to just about every word you throw at him. ESPECIALLY non-words like SHMONGLE. The amount of voice-acting work that went into him must be astounding, it's that impressive. Be careful that you don't say poopy words too much however, eventually he'll institute a swear jar to punish your death-transcending nastiness.Graphically speaking, the game's...serviceable. There's no colour because you're undead, you don't know what they look like anymore. The soundtrack is all over the place on the silly to serious scale, which I don't really mind seeing how silly this game can get. Some of the maps can also get pretty big and somewhat boring to navigate, doubly so if you try to find all the secrets. And the story itself isn't anything to really write home about, though the characters you meet along the way can prove rather colourful (the big-hatted dork who asks you to help him with his diss rhymes comes to mind).Cryptmaster is an innovative little package. I had lots of fun with it and I'm thankful to Mandy for showing it to me. If testing your vocabulary in a humorous, fantasy environment while accompanied by a snarky voice in your head sounds like a good time, you can't go wrong with this. At least as fun as Typing of the Dead while much more innovative.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly fun, relaxing and sometimes a bit of a headscratcher.The dialogue carries the experience with a sense of dry and sometimes dark humor. Exploration was somewhat underwhelming and I missed character costumization or a gear system, but that could be something for a sequel! I highly recommend the game at full price!
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: I think if you watch a couple minutes of gameplay, you should get a clear idea of whether this game is for you. Mavis Beacon Teaches Dungeon Crawling.That's it, that's just about the entire pitch. Movement is Grimrock-like -- strictly grid-based -- which is important, as it keeps your hands on the keyboard. Your  controls other than movement are typing. Since typing is only letters and backspace, and movement can be done with arrow keys instead of WASD, you don't even have to switch modes -- if you start typing something and decide you want to move instead, you can do that. Finally, combat locks you in (JRPG-style), taking movement out of the picture entirely.Typing is done one word at a time. Some of the other reviews mention Scribblenauts, but I think that's overselling it -- this isn't really a puzzle game. There are  but it's far more often about guessing what words the game knows about, rather than actually being creative. You can have a conversation with an NPC, but this is basically a dialog tree where you have to guess what choices you have.The story is... there, but mostly as background. There's enough talking that there has to be a story, but I felt the game was more about the characters and the moment-to-moment gameplay.So it's a narrow focus, and a relatively short runtime, but: The game is surprisingly polished! There are very few NPCs that will actually converse with you, but those are all -voiced and quite memorable. The art style is simple enough, even  but it gives a sense of walking through an illustration in some old book, and the sound design usually sets a pretty strong atmosphere. The JRPG system isn't all that sophisticated, but it can be  intense just having to remember and type abilities very quickly.Is it worth the price? Depends who you are. For me, a typing game with solid gameplay is  and I might go back to 100% it. If that's not you, though, it's probably at least worth your time if you find it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: It is definitely a game that I could describe as: An experience. A unique experience. This is the first time I have played a game of this type. The visuals alone are gorgeous, dark and intriguing. The conversation with the narrator is really wonderful and at times unpredictable. There really are a lot of words working here, some I even thought wouldn't work, and here you go, the narrator is always trying to answer them in some way! The fight itself is an interesting approach. Someone will say, writing, meh, a relic, yet I like it. Admittedly, in the long run, just waiting for the cooldown of our characters' abilities is a bit long, despite the possibility of shortening them with other words, but the combat really is unique. What's also cool is that we run into opponents who, for example, block a letter for us, making it necessary to quickly figure out how to defeat it.Exploration is fun, especially guessing what's in the chests to get more letters for more skills. I'm only writing this review after 1 hour of play, so I probably haven't unlocked most of the content, although at this point the game seems intriguing. If you are open to new and strange titles, I heartily recommend Cryptmaster to you!To the developer's credit, when he heard about regional pricing in my country (Poland), he ensured that he would look into the matter, contact the publisher, and on top of that he handed me a code to the game for free, which I wanted to buy anyway. That's what I love indie games for. For the approach to customers!
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Full Game Walkthrough + All Endings - I’ve never played an RPG quite like Cryptmaster. That’s thirty points (™) right there. Yet, while simple and unique in its execution, I’d venture to say this is a niche title because it definitely leans towards those with a love of language and depth of vocabulary. While I wouldn’t say verbosity and wealth of knowledge are required traits, they certainly help, and not just in terms of skill. To enjoy Cryptmaster, solving riddles, using clues to uncover words, and being able to guess long words based on only knowing a few letters should be preferred activities.Visually, black and white can be a cheap way to establish mood and avoid the work that providing color would offer, but given the undead theme, dark atmosphere of being underground most of the game, and Cthulhian vibe at times, the palette works. Shades aside, the actual drawings are a joy to behold, with an eerie level of detail in some cases. Although I would never call Cryptmaster a scary game, it certainly has an edge to it.Cryptmaster does what it sets out to do capably. Monotony never strikes in this nearly fifteen hour jaunt since the gameplay always changes, though always vocabulary-based. If words are your thing, I cannot think of a single game that does what this game does better. This isn’t a type-as-fast-as-you-can first-person-shooter. Thoughtful, patient play drives success, so sate that frenetic itch you have elsewhere.Rating - 9/10( Insanely Unique and fun game , Go for it )

_childDocuments_.review: This typing-based graphical RPG has been a treat from the first scene. Cleverly written, excellent VO, wonderful sense of humor, distinctive visuals -- I've played for 12 hours and I'm not done, but I'm thoroughly entertained and now want to savor the rest of the journey. _childDocuments_.review: A seriously and severely underrated game, very fun. Great to stream with friends on Discord (for the help), or even publicly if you're one of those.You play as a party of four undead adventurers that were resurrected deep within the crypts by the Cryptmaster, and he wants you to escape (for reasons unspoiled), but you have forgotten everything about your past lives and you must relearn all of your abilities and history during your journey.I also offered sex to a Ratman in exchange for a fishing rod and he actually considered it because there was nobody around.Must buy, try the demo at least.

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely impressed with this lovely little RPG Dungeon crawler. This harkens back to the days of Dungeon Master (Legends of Grimrock for newer players) with the added bonus of everything having to be typed in.  It's Simply a joy to play and experiment with as you progress through the different levels accompanied by the sarcastic and witty Cryptmaster. The monochrome graphics add to the dungeon feel of the game while the Audio is impeccably designed for the noises of a slimy, grubby dungeon. Voice acting gives us some vivid memorable characters with which to have some witty banter.There's enough variation in the gameplay to keep you going until the end; the various guessing games at the chests & idols, fishing for letters to complete memories and the delightful 'Whatever' card game has kept me coming back well past completion. At the price point it's at I whole heartedley recommend it and cannot wait for some form of sequel to be on the cards.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely game, far more of a word puzzle and typing challenge than dungeon crawler though.  Mind you, that isn't a bad thing at all, I merely bring it up so you can set expectations. There are no levels, XP or any of that RPG stuff, just movement and lots and lots of typing.  Riddles aplenty and the combat has enough mechanics added in to keep things interesting.  Things like enemies who will block you from typing certain letters, have armor tiles interspersed in their name (name length is one's health bar), can only be hurt by skills containing a particular letter and so on. Upon victory, you can take choice letters of the fallen foe's name to fill in the new words you're working on, Wheel of Fortune-style.  Complete a word and you progress that character, either by adding lore bits about them in the case of black words or a new skill they can use by typing it in the future in the case of white ones. Each character has a particular theme or two that can make guessing words far easier when you figure them out. You don't have to get all the letters of a word to "solve the puzzle", which is appreciated.The puzzles and riddles are clever and run the gamut of difficulty, which is refreshing.  The writing is charming throughout and the world and its inhabitants interesting enough that you want to learn more about them by talking to them and piecing together those words.  You can type whatever you want as a general comment and you can get some fun reactions depending on what you say to whom. Bear in mind, this is a one-word-at-a-time sort of situation, you don't type sentences. Accordingly, you'll get the most out of this game if you have a sufficient vocabulary and combat in particular will be easier if you're a speedy and accurate typist. It's not without its faults though.  The biggest is that it sort of runs out of steam at the end.  By which I mean, the last two areas are the shortest and most sparsely-populated.  They don't hold up to the promise of the earlier levels at all and given how many words there are left to discover by that point (your word discovery is capped by progress through the ladders between levels), I can't help but suspect the team may have run out of funds or time around that point and rushed them through.  It's not the end of the world other than how jarringly quick that last stretch is after all of the excellence leading up to it. Besides, if the big complaint is "I want there to be more", that's not too bad.  By the same token, the final boss isn't all that tough and you don't need all the skill words or the final health letters to defeat him.  It's just the achievements and lore to hold out for, really. I went back to old areas to grind for them and I sort of regret it.  I wish there was enough game to get to all the words organically instead of the slog I inflicted upon myself for completion's sake.There's  a fun little card game on the side as well, it has no plot significance (kind of, I think you're introduced to it to get a hint to a puzzle but I guessed the correct answer on my own and effectively skipped all that until being totally blindsided later by Steve) but is a good way to get souls (letters usable for most skills) and is genuinely entertaining.  Anyway, the characters and setting are fun, the art is fitting, everything is voice-acted, the puzzles are clever and the gameplay is refreshing if you're the erudite or sesquipedalian sort.  The price is certainly fair and it's a fine addition to the library if mix of genres and themes look interesting to you.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Fun concept and the emphasis on classic riddles is unexpectedly enjoyable. I like the humor, feels very "Droll British Quips" a la Hitchhiker's Guide and similar. Can be tense to remember useful combos while having to remember you can't use certain letters or you'll be blocked. "Whatever" is oddly enjoyable though I wish I could get all the cards that the NPCs have, at least right now that doesn't seem possible.My only real complaint is that by the time I finished the story I only had maybe 1/3 of the words unlocked and it is going to be a slog to get the rest (though the speed you get letters for hints is better after you beat the game). Fun game, novel concept, decent jokes, and I'm sad I beat it and there isn't really much more to do but grind out to 100% complete.

_childDocuments_.review: The developers deserve a lot of credit for trying something completely new. After playing through the game and seeing everything it had to offer, it never really "took off," in my opinion. I was waiting for something to happen where all the different systems came together in an unexpected way, but truthfully the gameplay is mostly a gimmick. The typing mechanic doesn't really allow for much creative problem solving or wordplay. You will typically know exactly what to type and when. Even the conversations did not feel particularly open-ended the way the game wants you to think they are.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Such a remarkable game. It is a perfect blend of creepy, clever, interesting, unique, and yes, even fun. I do not usually review games, but this seems like a true labor of love.Everyone is comparing this to Typing of the Dead (and understandably so), but this felt different to me, gameplay wise. At no point in Cryptmaster are you asked to type more than one word, and you are only ever trying to get one word at a time for riddles, chests, and conversations. If you want to split hairs, the exception to "one word" would be battles, of which there are plenty. In those cases, you have four characters, each of whom can take one action (one word) at a time. What elevates this _way_ beyond Typing of the Dead is that you aren't just spamming or parroting words. Many combat words from each character don't affect the enemy but rather one of the other characters, and you have to plan and time your words strategically in order to win battles. For example, you have your 'wizard' say a word that increases the damage of the thief's special attack, or try to funnel incoming attacks to your fighter (who said a word to avoid damage till his next turn) by having other characters dodge and deflect to him. Later in the game, wrinkles are added, such as "this enemy can only be damaged by words that contain 's.'"The game is fairly forgiving in its base mode while you are getting accustomed to it (i.e. there is no permadeath). I did not use any Accessibility options, but others seem to find them very favorable when necessary.I played the demo and then completed the full game at about 17 hours. I spent maybe a more-than-usual amount of time playing Whatever, the side-card game. I would have loved if this game were ten hours longer. I would love if there were a few more secrets and diversions rather than being relatively linear. I would love some sort of New Game+ mode. I would love more cards and opponents for Whatever. In short, I want more of everything this game has to offer. Unqualified recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting combat system that makes your brain work and wards off the dementia. Great writing, really funny a lot of the time. Great art style. Excellent excellent voice acting (and it seems like they put a massive amount of work into recording a wide variety of voice lines). Maybe 1 or 2 hours too long for its own good, depending on how you play it, but the ending is very very good and totally worth it (I would recommend turning the fingers setting up to 5, I played at the recommended setting of 1 and I only unlocked like 30% of the abilities by end game even with a little farming). Overall, a unique and really well done game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those unforgettable indies. It found a cool mechanic and it ran with it, and it does it well.The writing is truly funny. I love the Cryptmaster and his comments. I wanted to drink every drop of the worldbuilding, if for no other reason that to hear him make some remark or another. Months after beating it, I still try my Cryptmaster impression to say "eugh, no I don't like it" because his delivery is just perfect.The puzzles are fun, the combat is fresh and interesting, and  is the music good. So many of the tracks are memorable. The swamp theme in particular just puts me in a trance.This is a game worth playing, it's a game worth remembering, and it's almost certainly my game of the year.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: This game first popped onto my radar for its artstyle. The black and white 3D environment in a decrepit crypt works well, although admittedly the movement was janky and took some getting used to. Along with the narrative/narrator, there are 2 main gameplay loops in Cryptmaster: combat and riddles that I'd like to discussCombat: You attack by typing words that your 4 undead party members used during their lifetimes. Enemies can have modifiers such as shields that prevent certain letters from being used or taking more damage for each occurrence of a specified letter. The enemies and your party members have cooldowns between attacks so you need to plan your attack and execute before the enemy deals enough damage to kill your party members. The combat is fun enough, as you continue to expand your selection of attacks by restoring memories of your party members. I didn't love it, but it was far from a hinderance.Riddles: This is one of the areas where the game truly shined for me. Throughout your journey you'll enter many riddles and other word based challenges. Some of these can be attempted multiple times which lead to many instances where I was actively puzzling out a riddle in my head while investigating a cave or fighting slimes. There are other riddles where you are given a single attempt to guess an item in a chest within 6 guess. The catch is that you can ask the Cryptmaster for hints as to what the idea is. You can ask him to smell the item, or look at item. I also enjoyed trying to get him to wear some of the raunchy chest items. By completing riddles, you gain souls which allow you to use your attacks and the letters in the correct answers get added to the current memories of your party that you are trying to figure out. Turning unlocking memories/new attacks sorta into a game of hangmanNarrative/Narrator: Speaking of the Cryptmaster, the performance by the voice actor is amazing. The narrative as a whole is relatively simple with a couple slight twists at the end that were enjoyable. But the narrator makes everything in the game feel like you're actually interacting with a whole. From getting chastised for swearing, sarcastically praised for spotting a fishy, or hearing the glee in his cackle as I desecrate another holy alter in an unholy manner
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: As of writing this I've put in 5 hours into the game and have unlocked about 1/6 of the words for each class, meaning either I'm very bad at word games (I am) or this game is a lot longer than I'd expect. I wanted to get an early upvote out for this game even before beating it, because I'm that confident this game is a winner.  It's incredibly unique and charming and offers something completely new that I've never seen before. It's a dungeon crawler meets Wheel of Fortune (for you youngins out there, that's like worldle but with an attractive older couple that tells if you you were right or wrong). The writing is also quirky, but not in an overbearing 'cringe' way. I'm still constantly surprised by the amount of dialog options they put into this game, I even thought it was AI at first because they seem to have recorded a voice line for nearly everything, even 'fart'! And yes, he did mock me for giggling, and yes I WAS giggling.So far the weakest aspect is the combat, so far it boils down to me yelling various fish at enemies and then waiting for cooldowns to do it again. However, as I've said, I've only unlocked 1/6 of the 'words' for characters which I can assume at least 1/2 of those are more skills to use, so hopefully combat will get more indepth and difficult. Another weak point is the story, I have no real idea what I was doing in the second 'area', I met some pigs and then got some crowns and I think I'm married now? It was all very sporradic and maybe that's just me not paying good attention but it all gets thrown at you in no particular order other than the order you find them in which leads me to another issue with the game: there's no real map. It is SO easy to get lost, I gave up trying to mentally map out the areas and just enjoyed the game for what it's worth.You may think with three 'negatives' of the game that it'd be a negative, but honestly the game itself is so good that the negatives don't matter.  I don't care that I get lost a lot, or that combat is me covering enemies in a buffet of sea creatures, because everything else is good enough to carry the game through those luls. Finding new riddle stones is exciting, and trying to open chests and not mess it up is always fun.  They also regularly come up with ways to make the format of 'guess word' interesting and unique, and each one is just as fun as the next. The writing also keeps me interested consistently.  It also makes a good 'play with someone' game because you can both interact with guessing.  It's just a fun, unique game! And honestly it's really nice to see something so original and unique and well done. Oh also there's an entire card game system you can play with anyone and omg I have to complete my deck because it's so fun and has no business being so enjoyable for a minigame within an indie game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great, clever little game.I have the same issues with it that I have with all word games, which is that your enjoyment is directly tied to your language mastery/vocabulary, but there are some good hint systems and accessibility tools to help.I'm also constantly surprised with the amount of things they thought to add reactions to when I'm trying to be smarmy.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just such a creative delight. It uses a very simple core system, typing one word phrases at any time, and finds every possible avenue to use it.Helping to write a rhyming diss track.Solving riddles.Asking questions.Remembering your past.And has all of these systems interact, with stuff like giving single letters for longer phrases as your level up system.All combined with insanely creative writing that knows you better than you know yourself.Just such a joy of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Fell in love with the game during the demo. A game about typing words (sometimes fast) with voice acting that'll allow me to insert all sorts of weird stuff and I get a comment on it? Sign me up.I loved the premises of the old heroes being revived by the BBEG immediately. (At least that was my guess on what's happening here from the start of the demo already!) Using words to battle and solving riddles left and right is great. It's like playing with a gamemaster/dungeonmaster (hence the name, I imagine!) and asking about the environment. Especially when opening chests. What does it look like? What does it feel like? What does it taste like?! Yeah you can make him lick the items, because why wouldn't you!?There's a cardgame in this as well and while it's simple, it gets challenging eventually as well. It's a little slow at times, but the rest of the game certainly isn't. There's really not much more to say about the game. There's apparently fishing, too - haven't figured that out yet, but maybe I just walked past the moment where it's unlockable, too, or haven't encountered the unlock yet. There's combat. This isn't a cozy game, but it certainly is riddled with hilarious puns and characters (see what I did there?)I really can't emphasize enough how much I love this game. I didn't know I needed it, but I did. The language barrier of having English as a second language can sometimes be a challenge, but ultimately you could solve everything without in-depth knowledge, too. Better not make many typos in battle though!If you're unsure whether or not you should get it, get the demo, try it out a bit. See if it clicks. I for one am very happy with my purchase and can only sing this game's praises for a linear gameplay that feels very fresh despite old-school inspirations.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Go ahead, type 'fart.' You'll thank me later.In all seriousness, what a unique and great game. The core gameplay loop is refreshing and the environments are fun to explore. The cryptmaster himself is incredibly charming and the art direction is very distinct!10/10 I love piloting 4 corpses to eat bugs straight off the wall and skulk around in corners.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: This is lovely little game.  I do wish it was just a bit longer as I beat the entire game without even coming close to fully "leveling up" and the final zones consequently felt a little anticlimactic (especially the ending).  However, despite the lackluster final act I thoroughly enjoyed my time leading up to it and would love to see either a sequel or another game take this concept and run with it, especially if they put a bit more focus into the turn based side rather than the real time.  I played on that mode and, while I had a lot of fun with it, the game was definitely not balanced around the mode making the strongest strategies mostly made up of words you get within the first two rows (longer words eat up your turn timer while providing little more utility than just single hit and dodge strategies, something I suspect would be less of a deal in the real time if you are able to type fast enough).  Overall a great game witha fun sense of humor and a unique style that I would recommend highly.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent style, unforced humor, fun riddles and gameplay. Go in blind, as part of the fun is trying to figure out the puzzles. Only complaint is some things are not immediately obvious. The soul mechanic is explained but not immediately used, so it wasn't clear until part way into using it. Bug catching is fun at first but becomes a little tedious. Luckily, you do not have to do much of it to progress easily. Ratty's quest seemed like it would be easy, but I scoured the swamp for nearly an hour, only to be spoiled that it would not give a prompt (most thing give a prompt to interact). The first time using a portal is a bit confusing/disorienting. Also an option to allow certain things like hold backspace to quickly erase (or erase repeatedly) or holding arrows to quickly navigate menus would be appreciated. And "looping" menus, so when I reach the bottom I don't have to spam up 5 times to go to the top again.However, all that is minor, and really enjoying my time with this. Shout out to the RTVS crew for showing it off!
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: You can pee on an altar, throw crabs at enemies, and flirt with cryptdaddy. GOTY contender for sure. Full disclosure, I'm a word nerd. I love wordplay and enjoyed old school text based games. You don't have to love puns or text heavy adventures to enjoy this, but it certainly helps. This weird lil word dungeon crawler is a gem, and I am having to force myself to wait to play more until I can stream it - I just want to keep guessing words! The combat seems like it would be overly simple at first, but when you're flailing about trying to remember attack words to type, it's a dizzying panic that surprises you. The artwork is so striking, and the the music and sound effects are perfect atmosphere as well. Plus the voice acting is superb.  I'll update my review with more detail once I get further in, but I had to go ahead and give a  S H O U T O U T to a game that literally made its way into my dreams last night.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Listen, I only have 7 hours in this game and I feel like I could put 70 hours in. ~It's scratches an old-school 1980s RPG itch mixed with Mavis Beacon mixed with The Riddler mixed with Gwent. That's just the gameplay, then the art style & the music is fantastic. I love the color tint options and ability to completely change the mood of the dungeon yourself.This game deserves attention as it's innovative and really makes you think throughout the game.I recommend getting a group of friends to help you when you play.~Note to the Devs:I would love if this concept could be iterated / expanded to accept up to 2-3 words. I know that drastically increases the complexity, but it would drastically increase the flexibility and make it unique. I think the omnibox approach is really well implemented in Cryptmaster currently. Well done!

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game. Having had this recommended to me via the discovery queue a month or two ago, I knew I'd love this. A buddy got me it as an early birthday present and I've rinsed just about all the content in around 3 days (bar the majority of crypticisms; those are super challenging in an almost unfair way, but more on that later).Most of the time I'm a bit of a wiki gamer but I decided since this is a word puzzle game and I'm a bit of a language-head I'd jump in and force myself to not do anything more "cheaty" than showing my mates a riddle and asking them to help guess, and I'd recommend anyone else thinking of playing to do the same.The Cryptmaster himself immediately drew me in. Lee Williams has a great sense of humour and you can really feel the contempt/arrogance dripping from every word he says, but there's a certain joy and playfulness to the whole performance that really sells the comedy in this game.That is of course not to discredit the rest of the team. The game has a delightful art direction somehow keeping each environment distinct despite an entirely monochrome colour palette. Paul is really putting the Art in Hart. In my opinion the sound design and music helps it along, from Surasshu's jaunty medieval tavern music in the bonehouses to the relaxing piano + leaf rustling combo in the downwoods. Not to mention the incredibly satisfying clacking as you type up a frenzy at every possible moment whether you're looting, fighting, or talking. I guess in a game where all you do is type you'd have to make it feel good to do so and Catton Arthur absolutely nails it on that front.The aforementioned perfect storm of vocals, music, sound design, and gameplay makes for a remarkably compelling game in which it's incredibly fun and satisfying both to succeed and fail. Either way, despite the fact I've mentioned the largest names in the credit screen, everyone who worked on this masterpiece should be patting themselves on the back.Just a few quickfire bullet points about how the gameplay and wordplay work well together:-Abilities and memories being more easily guessable if you've been paying attention to their lore, or trends in previous abilities (the sea witch, nix, being the strongest example of this in my opinion)-Areas in which you can't use certain letters force you to switch up your comfort ability rotations sometimes-Rock paper scissors with the cryptmaster is a brilliant touch-Stepped back from a skull i was struggling with and started spamming expletives and the cryptmaster got sick of it and started up a swear jar-Whatever is a surprisingly competent card game and i had a lot of fun trying to optimise my deck-Enemy abilities were also varied (interestingly, with the slimes I found myself making them large on purpose so i could make sure all my sea creatures hit)-It had me physically writing on paper to complete puzzles (this is a positive) I haven't played a game that has required me to do that in YEARS but that could be a me problem-I picked up on a certain important thing early game, and was overjoyed that the game respected my intelligence and the thing I picked up on ended up being relevant (it's a bit of a Payn to avoid spoilers best I can while reviewing the whole thing)-Enemy names make PERFECT sense. I met a decrepit butler called MRSMYTHE and a rat called WEIRDFELLA I can't explain it well, but they just fit impeccably.While this game was hand-delivered to me, embodying everything I was waiting for in a video game, sadly it is not without fault, so I'll write up some negatives in more detail. Let it be known, if I didn't love it I wouldn't be criticising it and talking about things that could be improved. I would've just thrown the game into the darkest deepest crypt below the city and prayed it never showed up at the surface again.One of the things that stuck out to me is that it breaks out at a sprint, with the Bonehouses absolutely oozing with charm, with lots to do and many different people to chat to.Similarly, Pantry Below Ground has a lot to do, a unique NPC to buy letters from as a late-game soul sink, and plenty of secrets alongside a marketplace.It's when you get to Downwood that the game seems to lose a lot of the charm it previously had. There's Orthos who's a delight (except when he's playing cards then he's a [-1 souls]), then there's the cage guard, who's bit is very funny. Yet, there's a lot less to explore with there only really being the mines, a couple more vendors, and a quest that requires you to hunt for a certain monster type, buy another of the items you need, and ask nicely for the other. It's hard to describe but it loses a lot of the "sauce" that it had in the early game; it feels like it tapered off super hard. Not nearly as much to explore as I would've liked.The temple is when I thought to myself "what happened?". I get that it's The Endgame Boss Zone and so that's why it's a bit of a gauntlet but there are zero NPC interactions, no sidequests, no vendors. None of that care and love that was present in the earlygame remains when you're up there. There's the propaganda reels which I won't deny are cool and create a good atmosphere, but ultimately those are just ambience. Obviously this is just my opinion!! I'm just one guy but yeah, the temple and Downwood really didn't scratch the itch the first couple of zones did and felt vast yet empty. They'd benefit immensely from more content.Crypticisms. The lore snippets were fun and I really enjoyed them, but the overall story was really barebones. I thought that a game about writing and language would be a bit more clever than . But, I understand that's a personal preference thing + I understand it's mainly a comedy game and it  make me laugh so I won't note it as a real criticism since it achieved what it was trying to do.Anyway, my soulstone is running low on letters now so I'll leave off with the reassurance that the fact my two main criticisms of the game were:-There's not enough of it-Wah too hard for my monkey brainI would definitely recommend buying this, even if just for the pleasure of a game of rock paper scissors or "Whatever" with the Cryptmaster.tl;dr - If you don't like reading then why are you even looking at this game or its reviews >:)

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally leave reviews- or play typing games for that matter- but Cryptmaster is so much more than that. The devs have created a really unique world and you can feel the care and passion they have for this game in every area, character, and story beat. The combat and exploration are both fun and engaging, and each new feature introduced is well explained and easy to pick up while still allowing you room to grow and master using it. Skill progression is very free-form and allows you to either focus on a character's skills or work on leveling the group as a whole. Each character has a role to play and you really feel the impact each one has.The riddle/puzzle aspect of the game was what really drew me in and it ends up making this game great for streaming to friends, with everyone chipping in ideas and answers and occasionally sharing in your frustration. The riddles/puzzles range in difficulty and there are a few "well-known" riddles used, but there are more that took me a while to solve while still making me  to solve them. The only issue I've experienced has been with two or three riddles repeating, but only ones I believe may be "radiant" riddles and only within the first hour or so.I could honestly say good things about this game forever (there's a fishing minigame), but I just recommend you give it a try and see why there are so many positive reviews for yourself. Even if you don't think this game is something you'd normally play it will seriously surprise you. 10/10 - Devs  make more games(TL;DR- This game had me staying up until 2AM solving riddles on paper and practicing my typing. I couldn't recommend it more)

_childDocuments_.review: Somewhat slow-paced, thought provoking game.  Definitely not for people only looking for something action packed, but if you want something interesting and unusual in a game, this would be a good pick.  All in all it has a good sense of humor and some interesting gameplay, mixing riddles and word games with dungeon crawling.  All the characterizations in the game - the necromancer's constant needling, the weird vocalizations your characters do, and the NPCs you run into - are entertaining, and manage a level of weirdness that isn't just 'zomg isn't this random hehe'.  The voice acting suits the game very well.  I also find the card minigame pretty enjoyable.I've got a few very minor gripes with it - something about the way the camera moves was very disorienting to me at first, but there are options to change the speed and such, so it's workable.  This is a game that is served well by having a demo available for sure, but overall I think I would be able to recommend this to a lot of people I know.

_childDocuments_.review: A game I should have loved, but didn't. It's a very, very, very strongly presented game with really good voice acting and, while it's usually subtle or not very present, good music design as well. But it has some issues with the actual gameplay.Firstly, the concept of using key words to trigger abilities is fun but very rapidly starts to just be a very annoying way of clicking buttons. Especially once each of your four guys have 6+ abilities and you need to remember what all of them are and what they do and... it just becomes kind of miserable and you start ignoring a lot of them in favour of remembering two or three for each.Secondly, the way you get more letters by completing guessing games out of chests. Conceptually cool! Fun! The problem is that you have only the Crypt Master's five senses to give you clues. Once they've Looked and Touched, that's about it. Taste and smell rarely give anything important, and most objects make no sound. An orb with a tail? It's fuzzy and has a head? I refuse to believe some of these clues are meaningful to most people.What you use them for is to give you hints to "guess" at new keywords for your characters to use. Once again, conceptually neat, and at first I enjoyed it, because the words seemed to be tied to my characters. Like a Bard would be able to YELL or SING. A barbarian would HIT, CRACK and BOOT. But then the Assassin gets... ATLAS? FJORD? Once again, that's kind of the situation where you're mostly stuck brute forcing it because there's just no logical connection.Another annoyance was related to the dialogue. While it's all well-written, I feel like I would've enjoyed it more if it was unvoiced, because as far as I could tell, I couldn't skip it and would have to listen to the end of it every time, even if I'd heard it before and knew what my reply was going to be, and a good deal of it was filled with verbal tics and Dark Souls-esque cackling that I truly could not be bothered to sit through.Ultimately I think what I enjoyed most was the Whatever card game. It was absolutely one of the more creative things about the game.The monochrome presentation also started to grate on me because the "brightness" seems to vary wildly so sometimes I'd just be looking at white on white on white on white on white. And the bug collecting for soul points... considering that bugs respawn every time you enter or leave a room, there's no upper limit to soul points stored(that I found) and no time pressure, it feels like a vestigial mechanic that exists to cause eye strain.But yeah, giving Cryptmaster a bad review makes me really sad because it feels like it was just another iteration or two from being something I'd absolutely love. Sadly, at least for me, the experiment was a bust.
