_childDocuments_.review: This is one of these games that make you wish the authors had twenty more firends to help them make the thing bigger and deeper. The mechanics could easily carrry a lot, and I mean *a lot* more content (not necessarily in the sense of there being more dungeons, but more in the sense of there being more points of interaction, more kinds of interaction, and so on). Likewise, the authors' imagination could easily carry a much broader narrative. Having finished the game in a respectable time of 18 hours, I absolutely don't mean to complain about its size, but still, it does feel like a demo version of something even more magnificent.Things to keep in mind:- if, like me, you're not a native speaker of English, some wordplay may be much harder for you than intended, and typing is very likely to be harder, too- realistically speaking, you're going to unlock about 20 verbs for each character. In my case, trying to remember them all in their context in real time was very difficult. It's not that I don't *know* those words. It's just that I'm not wired to make the kind of instant connections between them that I make in my native language. This kind of gameplay would really shine in a turn-based format (the game has a turn-based mode, but wasn't primarily designed for it)- unlocking the best fun stuff (i.e. the backstories and the advanced verbs) involves grinding, because you run out of places to explore a bit too quicklyOther than that, a really refreshing experience. The combat mechanic isn't just typing, it's actually several layers of word and letter associations. Sometimes you need to pay attention to just the letters, sometimes to the sounds, sometimes to words' meanings. It's fun, and could be even more fun in many ways not (yet?) explored in this game.The story is, of course, a satire, and a somewhat nihilist one at that, but it doesn't cross the line between making characters a little bit ridiculous and / or pathetic, and making them unlikable. The writing is funny, the narrative consistently takes into account the fact that your characters are literally a bunch of zombies, and there's also a healthy dose of "things are not as they seem" done in smart ways.I want more.

_childDocuments_.review: Innovative take on both the dungeon crawling and typing game genres. One of the most satisfying aspects of the game is how often you'll be met with a unique response for what you say in a dialogue with a character. The game rewards you for responding cleverly by awarding you with alternate solutions or even just an entertaining response. The Cryptmaster is certainly the star of the show, but the other characters are all well-voice acted and charming in their own way. Don't let the typing aspect of the game scare you off. It doesn't play like typing of the dead regardless of the obvious comparison. Nothing is time reliant except for the battles which can be paused at any time to view your skills and the game even has a turn-based mode if you'd rather not be rushed. The focus on the game is more on vocabulary, riddles and conversation than purely typing speed, unlike the majority of typing games.I'd highly recommend this game even if you don't end up finishing it. Just experiencing such a charming, innovative game is well-worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: You think you've seen all typing games have to offer just because you've played Typing of the Dead or uh, Mavis Beacon? Well you haven't seen Cryptmaster.The more I play the more I see the genius of the design. Typing isn't just a shallow means of interfacing with the world, and letters themselves are used in ways I've never thought a letter could be used. They are attacks, defenses, vulnerabilities, experience, hit points, rewards - they are the very fabric this world is made from. The expected mechanics of a dungeon crawler RPG within a typing based framework comes together in such an interesting way that it's no wonder the game won the IGF Excellence in Design award.It's delightful to type in the stupidest word you can think of in a situation and get a unique reaction from it. Kind of staggering to think about the amount of these reactions the devs thought to include, I expect there would be thousands of unique voice lines to be found. I spouted some bussin zoomer slang and no cap giggled and clapped my feet together when the Cryptmaster had something to say about it.The art is very distinct and unique, they are going for an old school TTRPG guide book ink illustration style and totally pull it off.Writing of course is great and a core part of the game. A mixture of grandiose high fantasy with plenty of jokes that doesn't take itself too seriously.All in all, I highly recommend this game and guarantee you haven't played anything like it before.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic fun. As a word game enjoyer and a dungeon crawling lover I bought this as soon as I heard of it and have not been disappointed. The gameplay is very engaging and addictive, story is great, voice acting is awesome, and at risk of sounding like a total dork the UI, fonts, and general visual feel brings me so much joy. If this game sounds appealing to you at all, you'll almost certainly love it.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely novel and charming game. The core of running around as single word uttering undead crew with Necromancer Gman getting into "situations" is fantastic. Some things I'm mixed on or would prefer to see changes in further iterations.The Combat is.. ok. The drip feed of new skills is so heavily dependent on getting lucky with letter drops that I had maybe half of the skills by the end of the game, the final encounter is not at all tuned for full skills as I found out while getting additional endings. The encounter density is exhausting compared to the overall complexity of the combat (which compounds into tedium with all of the typing). NPC interaction is fantastic, there are some delightful subversion you can do with your word choice. The squad has a lot of personality buried in their memories and actions on the field.Exploration is confusing due to the uniform art style, the map isn't very helpful. Towns could stand to be a little more coherent and not purely dungeony. Big plus for silly things like fishing and Whatever.I really hope they're able to either iterate or expand on Cryptmaster because overall it is a lovely experience that doesn't overstay its welcome.  Thank you for this unique entry in the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: The charming art direction is obvious from a glance, and so is the voice acting right off the bat, it has a lot of charm. For the past day I have been thinking in the Cryptmaster's voice and making Cryptmaster iMpRrreSsiOnS with friends, and probably will do so for a good while!The mechanic of typing out words to attack and interact is brilliant and the Cryptmaster has a LOT of reactions to what you do, the variety and range of recognised words is staggering. I personally really enjoy the guessing mechanic (under the names of each character is a word you have to guess and you get letters for these from combat and loot), and the riddles, and love that names have a role to play; your characters' names are their HP (4 letters = 4 HP) and enemies can be dealt extra damage to by using skills that deal extra damage to specific letters (for example, you may get a skill that will do +1 extra damage for every letter "A" in the enemy's name).There is a very interesting fishing mechanic, and a card game, both of which make use of typing.All-in this game is very unique and clever, I am excited to see the rest of it. It's a real gem!

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting idea stretched too thin, with many quality of life problems. It feels as if the game didn't value your time.1. Lack of "running" and number of empty rooms is baffling- It feels as if half of the time spent playing the game is spent on awkward semi-turn-based walking2. Then there is talking, which is bugged and slow. It's especially annoying that you can't skip the "Giggle" from the mad rat. That being said, voice acting and some dialogue is fun, but nothing amazing.3. Story, at least as far as I got is not really motivating me to continue playing4. Combat is poorly explained- it seems it's not possible to chain interrupt attacks? Sometimes it works sometimes it doesn't. Sometimes units that are on the ground still attack. Sometimes I take damage for no reason (I assume the other side used guard skill, but it's not indicated in any way makint the situation confusing). No idea how summoning spells work in practice?5. Having to collect bugs to get mana is atrocious, and again feels like a waste of time6. The "whatever" mini game is heavy on double-randomness (card game with random letter pulls)Normally I wouldn't leave any review, as the game is all in all between 2.5 and 3 / 5, so in a "meh" category, but after getting stuck and loosing quite a bit of progress trying to win a whatever match, my opinion went down to not recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version of the review : I want to pay the voice actor of the Cryptmaster to tell me i'm a good boy and everything will be alright.Long version of the reviewI come to you as a happy man.I was on a terrible game streak recently, the last three games i had gotten on steam were just awful and i hated myself for spending my hard earned money on them.And here i was, reading about this strange game filled with riddles and an unique atmosphere. I expected a risky Hangman and riddle type game with a gloomy twist.What i got was an incredible story driven game with amazingly designed NPCs, reponsive commands, unique combat and AMAZING riddles that got me thinking and enjoying myself!I cannot thank the devs enough for their hard work, i was really plesantly surprised by the light hearted jokes, the wholesome and touching moments, and the whole companionship this party has.The only downside is the bit of the abrupt ending. Hopefully we'll eventually get a DLC or expension that will add more of the mini game or a NewGame+. (Please!)
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: NYT Games meets Knightmare. Emphasis on the puzzle and riddle elements rather than stats and resource management, you'll want a notepad over a spreadsheet as your companion. Has some player signposting issues and drags a bit late game as the clues and memory unlock economy don't quite seem to catch up with player progression though devs seem quite aware of these issues. Constantly keeps your brain cells buzzing with typing combat, puzzles, riddles, crossword clues and even a card game. A clever premise with the ever-likeable Cryptmaster himself and a great soundtrack seals the package. One of the most inventive things I've played in years.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: The game's humor is mean-spirited, and while you can "say anything you want" the game often just doesn't respond unless you obey its lines of thought. In order to unlock save points you have to defile the statue of a goddess that is animated and asks you to please not do so, and there aren't even voice lines about refusing.More generally, creativity in word choice is usually punished or absent. You can't even say that the sun is (gloriously) incandescent and the loot guessing game pushes towards useful questions rather than fun ones. I also tried turning on hints for the riddles and the first "hint" I got was flat-out being given the answer.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Despite leaving an outstanding first impression, the game just doesn't have enough, mechanically, to stay entertaining for as long as it lasts. Art direction is stylish, voice acting is great, writing is amusing, but the gameplay just starts feeling like a chore after few hours and it doesn't get any better. Mash the same skills in every encounter, mash the same names of bugs, mash the same names of fish, solve riddles, play extremely RNG card game, over and over and over again. Extremely repetitive and shallow. Even the dungeon crawling and treasure hunting feels like a chore because only reward you ever get from it is few extra letters, same letters that you can get by fishing/fighting. The game would be great if it was, like, 4-6 hours tops, but it just keeps dragging on and on.The idea is great, but as the game is now, you might as well just play the demo and buy the soundtrack. This way you'll get to enjoy the best the game got on offer and support the developer without wasting your time. As of right now, according to achievements only 30% of the players made it to chapter 3. There're reasons for that.I hope this game gets a sequel, but with proper gear, proper dungeon crawling, proper rewards, and combat system that can't be solved just by spamming same skills in every battle.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Fun old school text adventure with a graphical interface from the late 80's-90's dungeon crawlers. A lot of groanable humour, puns and dad jokes being some of the puzzle answers and some quite difficult riddles (mostly optional). The fighting and spellcasting is memorable as you type attacks like jab or cleave to attack your enemy, and you play a sort of hangman game to unlock more memories and special moves for your team of four.Fun in a sort of PG way, kids would love it too but some of the riddles may be too tough to them. Saying that I looked a couple up on Google, so I'm leaving this review to immortalise my shame for taking the easy option rather than ruminating on it for months.Three endings and it took me 19 hours to beat with a decent story, I was put off by the price but feel this was worth it, the time being more important no regrets with this title.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Great game overall.  I have some gripes, but overall it is unique enough for me to keep going. First off, It's got a super cool look. The story, while sparse, is intriguing too. I wanna keep going to figure out who my party is and what's going to become of them. I do NOT trust the cryptmaster. What nefarious purpose does he have with my crew??I like the word puzzle and typing aspects. You guess words for each character kind of wordle style in order to unlock memories and skills. Type those skill words in combat to cast them on monsters. My biggest complaint with combat is I have so many skills and it is hard to remember what the word is and what they do. You can pause to look at them but it's kind of annoying. So I keep spamming the same combos over and over. I wish I could pin some of them to the side of the UI and they'd show up in combat only.10 hours in I'm sick of riddles lol. They're optional in most cases but helpful to solve.

_childDocuments_.review: Part dungeon crawl, part word game. Actually, more word game than anything else really. The way it makes use of those word game principles for everything is very clever. Basically everything except movement is done through essentially a version of hangman: combat, identification of items, discovery of backstory - everything. And it works remarkably well, resulting in a game that feels like something very original. The art and voice acting do a good job supporting the gameplay, too, including a part played by Hugo Myatt of Knightmare (for those of us who were kids in the UK in the early 90s). It's humorous, clever, and well performed. There's some very well realised worldbuilding too. There's even an extra game hidden in here. You know the grand old tradition of having a recurring minigame - something like Triple Triad in Final Fantasy VIII? Here it's a card game called Whatever, and it stands up really well as its own game. I'm very impressed. One of my games of the year, for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely ingenious concept, executed with flair and a welcome dose of silliness. Great for fans of word games, dungeon crawlers, and humour.The gameplay could be described as 'Legend of Grimrock meets Wordle', the striking visuals look like they were pulled straight out of a 70s D&D sourcebook, and the music is both eclectic and memorable.By far the biggest selling point is the Cryptmaster himself - a fully-voiced necromancer who responds to just about everything you do with a combination of dry wit and exasperation. The sheer number of specific words and actions that the game can recognise and react to is mind-boggling and frequently feels a little bit like magic. But it's not quantity over quality either - this is one of those rare games that actually makes me laugh out loud while playing.Sure, the combat is a little shallow and I'd love some more QOL features (like a world map), but this game has something special that keeps me coming back for more: ironically, Cryptmaster has soul.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: My partner and I have been playing Cryptmaster together. While the combat sections don't lend themselves to cooperative play in real-time, otherwise this game is PERFECT to play with people who like word puzzles and riddles. (Giggling childishly at bodily functions is purely optional but a bonus.)Strong recommend.(Only missing QoL feature would be some way of tracking incomplete skulls etc - I realised the answer to a riddle at 3 in the morning, but for the life of me cannot remember where the skull is.)
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: It becomes more difficult to distinguish games made by developers who have a true talent for it and those who are just looking for a quick and simple way to produce content for some quick cash as we move closer to the day where artificial intelligence will be used more heavily and openly to create games left and right, including some that are made almost entirely of AI. With several layers of responses prepared for every possible thought as long as it is a single word the developers of Cryptmaster just had a great deal of passion for creating a more transparent type of interaction with their player base. If you're a little too snarky, you might receive some witty sass in return; if you're inappropriate, the same thing will occur. Although it's unfortunate that it's not even more detailed since it was a short adventure, it was still a wonderful experience that I would love to see more of. It has Wordle components, great narrative & story with a ton of other captivating aspects that all come together in the style of the classic Typing of the Dead to create an extremely entertaining and challenging riddle and puzzle game that will hold your interest. Regarding the reviews, both favorable and unfavorable ones criticizing the game's chest section. There are alternatives in the main menu that provide you more chances and tips to obtain the solution with more options. You're also not always expected to be correct or to be spoon-fed the answer, which is the entire experience of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've said many times that I do not like traditional dungeon crawlers, like Grimrock. While this uses the gameplay of classic dungeon crawlers as a framing device, it has more in common with a text adventure game. It's an absolutely magnificent marrying of genres with witty writing, deep mechanics both in combat and outside of it, and oozing with passion and love for its craft.I adore this game, even if I haven't been able to put as much time into it as I'd like. I also have no doubt that I will never find all of its secrets. In particular, the sheer number of memories to discover is overwhelming, in a good way. Playing what is essentially a Wheel of Fortune-style word guessing game is such a brilliant way to discover more about your characters while creating an in-universe reason for them to learn new skills. It may sound odd, but I can assure you that playing the demo makes it very clear.If I had any complaint, it would be the controls. I fully understand why they are the way they are, but they are not my preference. I find it rather annoying to move about one square at a time, and even as someone who isn't particularly prone to screen-based motion sickness, pivoting left and right while looking for bugs will sometimes make me nauseous. I'd almost prefer an option to disable movement animations and just snap around. Although that would presumably break some puzzles, since they're no doubt tuned for your limited movement speed.Besides that, I give an extremely high recommendation. It is, frankly, ridiculous that this game has fewer than 1,000 reviews. I obviously have no idea what sales look like, but they're not anywhere near high enough. This is a fantastic work of art, and it deserves to be recognized as the modern classic that it is. This is what indie games are all about.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo for this game and was blown away. It seemed like a fun take on a typing game, but when I got the full game the ideas presented to me in the demo just got vary arduous soon after the demo ended. Cryptmaster is a dungeon crawler mixed with text adventure, with a typing game also. There are many puzzles and dialogue things where you can just type whatever you want, so things are very "open ended"(?) kind of? This could be cool, the allure of text adventure games is the freedom you could have from being able to "do anything", but that is the same allure that falls short in this game.There are a lot of mechanics that feed into each other so I kind of just have to start explaining them all. Let's start with the memories of your 4 person party. At all times your party will have a blank word that will gradually fill up as you gain letters. Letters are gained from fighting enemies, doing riddles, or opening chests. The more letters you have, the easier you can guess the word, but you can type in the word anything once its the one on screen. These memories can either be lore, or moves to use in combat. There appears to be like 40-ish for each person, mostly consisting of lore from what I could tell. I beat the game and ended up with like less than 20 on each character.Chests are puzzles in which you ask the Cryptmaster to describe a mystery item (look, touch, remember what it did, taste, etc.). Limited number of guesses, and when you solve it all the letters get put into your memory words. There are skulls that give you riddles to figure out, and similarly if you solve them, the letters get added. The problem with these is purely a chance thing where maybe none of the letters actually help you, or you already had those letters, just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying i think. Fighting enemies gives you 1 letter of your choosing from their name, but I find the combat ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying. The combat is recommenced to be in real time (more in line with most typing games), or you can do a version of turn based combat. In real time, you must type your moves fast while a timer counts when the enemy will attack. However, you have a cooldown after each move (per character), and this feels so ridiculously long compared to enemy attack speed. Also the fact you have to remember every move for 4 characters in a high speed fight, that was just not feasible for me, so I went to turn based. Turn based isn't traditional turnbased, it just makes every letter typed advance time. Enemy attack timer goes down per letter, and when a party member is on cooldown, each letter takes away a segment of cooldown. This slows it down so you can think and you can actually look at your list of attacks, providing more "strategy". Turn based was a band-aid to finish the game because I don't think the combat is good overall. I will say its mainly because the moves all kind of suck too. idk none of them felt really good to use, but maybe there are cooler moves i didnt unlock even though i beat the game! Maybe if I could get memory words faster, combat would be better, but even then combat just woudlnt be fun until "late game" so it seems not very good.Then the other part of this game besides combat is the mystery object and riddles and boy ♥♥♥♥ do I hate word puzzles. I didn't think this game would be so full of them, so ♥♥♥♥ me i guess. Im just not good at them. I can't solve riddles, and I cant remember words when I need to. Then it just pisses me off like *really* bad man. If you like word puzzles you might be happier than I!Also, there is a card game in this, and I also think it sucks. Maybe thats just me not understanding how I should play it, or not understanding how to build a deck, but you dont get a lot of cards to even build one. Most cards you get from beating opponents, but you have to *beat* them with your crap cards.The card game has you draw 4 cards, and a whole row of  random letters (maybe like 20ish?). You pick 2 letters at a time, and if any of the letters are in the name of the cards in your hand, you deal damage. If you get all the letters in a card's name, its effect will happen. You can also skip your turn to mulligan your letters.  This is heavily reliant on you actually getting letters you can ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ use in your hand, which I barely ever had. From what I could piece is that deckbuilding would revolve around either picking cards with a variety of letters so you can have more letters that are useful, or cards with a small variety so letters do more damage per pick. Again, you don't really get a lot of cards to do either of these I feel. Maybe I just fundamentally did not understand this card game, but I dont think its very fun at all.Mainly just every mechanic frustrated me and it just did not gel with me, im sad it didnt, but oh well.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the concept of the game, but after a couple of hours of gameplay I unfortunately discovered that the novelty of typing gets old extremely quickly, and that the whole 'SAY ANYTHING", "words control everything" stuff is just a moot selling point that's neither very well designed, nor very true. The things you can type that make an impact are severely limited, any "out of the box" thought that you type is met with generic responses. It is essentially a pretty bland dungeon crawler where you mostly walk around in uninteresting, black and white landscapes with poor navigation, typing the same few words again and again whenever you come across a chest or an enemy. Moreover, the game has a pretty high price tag for what it offers. I might have kept it and given it some more time if it was cheaper, but at this price I chose to refund it and get another game instead. Then again, it's a nice thing that the game offers a demo version so you can try it out before buying. If you can imagine yourself continuing to enjoy this game for ~13 hours (according to HLTB), then go for it I guess.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot to like. The art style is great, and the sense of humour this game has is amazing. I love a lot of the characters that I've seen so far, and there seems to be a decent scope of words which are picked up in the main gimmick of the game. The word games, riddles and puzzles are all interesting and fun. However, unfortunately there are big issues with some main gameplay elements. This game advertises two input methods, keyboard and controller, and also voice in.put. The voice input option is awful, and does not work the majority of the time, so the idea of playing through with voice and controller is just not actually possible. Keyboard input is fine, and definitely how the game should be playedBut the biggest issue for me, is combat. While you are given seemingly a lot of scope of potential attacks and abilities to use, combat itself ends up being spamming the same four short words over and over again, as the alternative looks like memorising an ever growing list of words, which is just not fun. And one more note, it's "turn based" combat isn't turn based, it's still a rush to write in those words. Ultimately, I really want to like this game. I could forgive the issue with the control methods and inputs, and a few other miscellaneous issues I had. But the combat is boring, annoying, though not challenging, and that's, to me, the worst of both worlds, and damages for me what had the potential to be one of my favourite games so far this year. If you can get over that, then the rest of the game has a hell of a lot for you to enjoy. Unfortunately, I couldn't, which is why I wouldn't personally recommend it.

This game is filled with pointless hallways/areas of the map that seem to be there only to waste your time. The soul system has no impact on game play outside of the first area. Once you unlock WHATEVER then souls become a non-issue. Currently stuck in the Tower where I can't access the Library. Even after playing the record and getting the rust bombs, which you would think are used to blow up the gates... but no. Can't figure out the next step and not invested enough to keep looking.

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like a mostly enjoyable first three or four levels of a much bigger game, but not a fully realized game. The main conceit - typing words to attack - is fun and unique. and the visual style is a great choice. But a lot of the later half of the game feels empty, and the fights are tough enough that exploring can get frightening, and isn't rewarding enough. Maybe the worst bit of the game is the map system. There's no overworld map, and it's hard even in friendly areas to keep track of where you are in relation to where you've been. I finished the game in two sessions, and despite it being fresh in my mind, was still constantly getting lost. It's sad, because the game has some great moments. But much of what comes in between is frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: You know how people talk about the replay value of a game? This game doesn't even have full play value. I sincerely doubt that most people will finish the game, because it becomes repetitive and boring very, very quickly. You'll spend most time unlocking a huge array of redundant and useless skills to be used in the clunky and tiresome battle system, and the rest of the time playing minigames that don't serve any purpose other than to give you more souls (mana, basically) to engage in the battles you don't want to fight. zzzZZzZZZzzZzzz...I love word games and puzzles, wanted to love this, but it's badly executed and needed far more work. The game was a lot of fun for about 5 hours, but not at all worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: The typing mechanic and voice acting is super awesome. The game is overall very immersive and reminds me of old dungeon crawlers I used to play on my Gameboy Colour. The puzzles are all interesting, and I love the characters and their eccentricities.My main problem with this game, and why I can't recommend it is the combat. It's overly repetitive, the healing is annoying, and if you lose your one healer, you go all the way back to the last save point, which can often be entire rooms before. Mashing keys to attack enemies by remembering words seems like a cool concept, but in practice I find it overly tedious and the enemies get far too many attacks in before I can even do much to them.I suspect that making enemies attack slower would improve the combat, or even making turn based combat more like an RPG and less like a Mavis Beacon Typing program. Keep the typing to the parts where you don't need twitch reflexes and the memory of a god.On top of that I really hate the Soulstone mechanic and how it acts as a mana meter. It doesn't really add much to the game. I'd much rather have a potion crafting minigame where I can make healing/mana potions or something. As it is, you just pick up bugs and solve puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Cryptmaster has a great mechanical premise, terrific art, fantastic voice acting, decent low-key music, and wonderful style overall.  Unfortunately, it's just not fun to play.The main hook is that you have to type in words to guess and unlock your new abilities.  You can also find answers to riddles and guessing games by typing.  Those things are fun.  Unfortunately, they are a relative minority of the game.  Once you've guessed that you have to type, say, "attack" to attack... that's how you attack.  By typing "attack" again.That means that you're going to have to hit somewhere between three and who knows how many keys to attack.  After three or four times, it's not fun, it's annoying.  At best, it's extra stress and difficulty.  At worst, it's busy work.  It also means that you're going to have to remember an ever-growing library of words for each of your four characters.  God help you if you step away for a long weekend or get pulled away for awhile by life.  You're going to have to spend 15 minutes re-memorizing the buttons to attack.On top of that, the exploration is also pretty dull.  Most of the rooms are largely empty, and interactable objects and enemies are highlighted.  While that's nice, it also turns a lot of rooms into big, wide hallways that you have no reason to bother with or look at as you walk forward until you hit the next door.Cryptmaster has a lot going for it, but the core gameplay is just not there.  This is a classic case of a game working way better on paper than in reality.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Awesome concept and writing, not a good game, and sometimes feels actively hostile. Needs a few polishing passes.It almost hurts to give this a negative review. My first hour or two of gameplay were fantastic. The writing is great, the sound design is fantastic, and you're constantly amazed by the amount of audio responses there are to what you can type, but as you progress the newness wears off and the frustrations pile on.Some examples:1.  This is toggleable with an option, see developer response below.2. There's no objective tracking. You basically have to complete this game within a few days. At a 15-20 hour game that's not a tall order depending on your schedule, but if you were to take a break and come back to it you will have no idea where you are, what you're supposed to be doing, or how to do it. You do have sort of list of objectives, but they're in a random(?) order and unmarked which ones you've completed already, so that's quite unhelpful.3. The riddles and puzzles are all over the place. There were a few where I thought "wow that's genuinely clever, I had a lot of fun figuring that out" but for every one of those there were two which were blatantly obvious and two more which even after looking up the answer require some point-and-click adventure levels of abstract thinking.4. The card minigame which you unlock fairly early on is just not worth playing. I remember some comment by the developer that it's supposed to be reworked in an upcoming patch, but at the time of writing it's so heavily RNG based I can look at my starting hand and tell with a high level of confidence whether I've won or lost.5. Combat becomes quite samey early on. You quickly discover a combo which you can repeat over and over to nuke many enemies before they even get an attack. Later on you get enemies with armor or that block certain letters, but it was quite rare that these caused any problem. Most of the unlocks in the second half of the game seem useless, and if the length of the unlock track is anything to go by that means you won't need a full 80% of the skills in the game. Plus you end every fight by spamming the same heal spell which is again just annoying rather than interesting in any way.6. The beetles. There are a TON of them, the game implies they'll be a big deal for keeping your "mana pool" up, and they make a very distinct sound so you're encouraged to hunt them down. In reality it's a complete waste of time. They give a pitiful amount of mana and they're only needed for making potions, which is thing you have to do once for one mission. Might be cool if they were 5x as rare but gave 5x the mana but they're hardly worth the trouble at the moment.Could probably think of some more if I put my mind to it, but yeah overall it's a game with a fantastic concept and some really unique gameplay, but it feels actively hostile to play and I was thankful when I was done. At $25 and 15 hours for one playthrough I would give this one a pass though, unless it hits a dramatic sale.

_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one to write because a lot of love clearly went into this game, but it just doesn't quite hit the mark.The whole novelty of the game is that you can type any word you want to say and the Cryptmaster or other NPCs will respond to you. For the first few hours of gameplay this is fun and, well, novel. Unfortunately you'll quickly start to realize that any time you think you're saying something clever or you deviate from the paved path in what the NPC expects you to say, you're frequently met with dialogue placeholders that effectively say "invalid input, please try again." As much as it pains me to admit this, if this game had come out several years earlier it probably wouldn't have felt so jarring, but in the age of natural-language AI chat tools, this ends up feeling frustrating and cagey.Another issue the game has is its lack of new novelties being introduced. This the the sort of game that thrives when it's treating the player to small new novelties either as a reward for exploring off the beaten path or as they progress through the narrative. Each time a novelty is wearing thin, something new should be introduced to keep the game feeling fresh throughout. Instead, with this game, you can more or less expect the entire experience to basically just be riddles. Find a chest? Basically just a riddle as the Cryptmaster describes some object to you. Talk to an NPC/door blocking your path? Riddle. Find a talking skull? Riddle. I really love riddles, but even for me this just became rote. There are so many fun things you can do with words and this over-reliance on riddles is a shame.I really wanted to like this one and I do think there's something here, but this just falls a little flat for me. The folks who worked on it did a nice job, but I just can't recommend it.TLDR: I love typing games, I really wanted to like this one, but its novel mechanic of typing any word you want is too limited and the game relies too heavily on riddles to progress everything.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Thought I would like this as I'm very into Typing of the Dead but this is a very different game and it's one that isn't for me. Most characters don't really follow conversations so the typing doesn't factor in much there, either; even going slightly off the path will get you an "Ummm I don't know what you mean..." response. Why type if there's no real freedom? It's got very good presentation and it's a light-hearted gimmick but the game controls are sluggish and every minigame is annoying aside from opening chests. It's just not that fun.If this wasn't overwhelmingly positive I probably wouldn't have bothered posting this but I think people should know that there is a chance you won't like this, even if you saw a glowing review that made you sure that you would.

_childDocuments_.review: When I got this game, I was hoping for a game similar to Legend of Grimrock.  Cryptmaster is not that.  Cryptmaster is basically a never ending game of Wheel of Fortune, the old TV show where you guess words with missing letters.  That's an interesting gimmick, I thought, but I didn't realize that it was the entire game.  The rest of the game is background noise.  It's an adventure, a fantasy medieval setting (mostly caves and dungeons), and it is monochrome all throughout.  None of this is a problem, I think the game is well made.  I just want to stress that this is not a dungeon crawler or RPG, it is a word game.

_childDocuments_.review: one of those games where you can answer the answer correctly, but not in the correct way. one chest puzzle seemed to give me random hints that didn't seem to logically make sense, and spelling errors/mistypes count as attempts in the chests. the skulls also have illogical pun jokes as the answer in a game about trying to figure out riddles with logic. all of these are nitpicks compared to the combat which is pretty horrific, can't imagine even attempting to remember the insane amount of skills for each situation you may need them in.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially bought this game to try out my brand new keyboard. Although I think I enjoyed the tactile pleasure of pressing fresh keys more than this game's main gimmick. The whole "type whatever you want to solve puzzles your way" thing wears off pretty damn fast. Sure, you can say whatever you want at any time, but the most you'll get is the Cryptkeepe- Sorry, the CryptMASTER- remarking vaguely on your chosen word, and by vaguely, I mean "What? Why did you say that?" And thats all you get. Unless you say something specific yet thematically obvious like bones, water, bugs, dead, etc, then you'll get some more fluff in the responses. Keep in mind, however, that this is just typing out the random words while you walk around.Interacting with any character is much more narrower than you think. Take for instance, the rat guard before entering the "Bonehouse". No matter what you say, you'll mostly get the same responses and results anyway.Answering his question about business or pleasure with anything OTHER than those two words will result in him just picking one for you anyway. Trying to tell him my weapons were "moderetly" sharp just resulted in him telling me to give him a yes or no response. It seems to mostly follow this trend throughout the game so far as I've gone. Oh and, as for the riddles you can solve, well, riddles only generally have ONE solution, there's not a lot of flexibility there. Does this game's advertising lie to you? Not in the sense that you can take them to court for it.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: If you're looking for story, riddles, or just a curious piece of art - this game is great. If you're looking for replayable dungeon crawler with captivating mechanics i'd rather pass this one.I really struggle to decide shall it be the positive or negative review. Demo was charming, so i decided to try out more. "Okay, that's... Not a job. Or it's not a job i've ever heard of, anyway. Try again." like ten times in a row kinda irritating. Yeah, probably "undead" sounds more like a job than "assasin" or "undertaker", but y'know, stumbling just after i leave the demo zone, with absolutely insignificant question? _childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game so bad but it wasreally disappointing to me. I thought it might have been because I was playing on the Steamdeck but I played it briefly on the PC and didn't find it much better. There's a good bit to love about this game, such as the art, the novelty of the combat system, the card game you can play vs NPCs, and the riddles, but that is all drowned out by extremely tedious gameplayThe soundtrack was mostly fine but in the 1st (I think?) chapter where there are frog babies, the music was insanely irritating to me. Every time that bass line repeated I got frustrated. The loop was too short and the music just sucked to begin with in that sectionNone of what you do in this game seems super relevant to its story. You are given quests to accomplish to make your way up to the surface from the underworld, and the info you get about the actual storyline is heavily backloaded. An altar infodumps on you in the 3rd or 4th chapter, and the final boss fills in the remaining story through what is essentially a monologue. You get nothing else that furthers the story in each chapter - only tasks to complete for NPCs that help you progress upwardsThe combat seemed so cool at first but never ended up being enjoyable. I still hadn't unlocked half my abilities by the time I beat the game, so every encounter went very similarly. I didn't get many opportunities to use new abilities because I just didn't have them. The enemy abilities seemed to want to remedy this by doing something like disabling half your abilities so you'd have to use ones that you didn't usually use, but I found that these just made combat more annoying. In the final leg of the game I ended up avoiding enemies whenever I could just to skip tedious combat. Every encounter ended with your characters wounded, which you could fix by either using healing abilities which ate away at your "souls" you spent to use them, or teleporting back to an altar which would then require you to travel back to where you were to resume your journeyThe potion system was so bad. I would be curious to know if anyone used this more than once or twice. It seemed so weak and, once again, tedious to use, since crafting them had you scrolling through like 40 bug names looking for letters you neededThe menus were horrible to use as well. Organizing notes and map locations alphabetically made it hard to identify the relevant items. It would have been much nicer if the more recent items were at the topI'm kind of just rambling so I'll stop here but I would avoid this game. The art is incredible but the gameplay is too rough around the edges to be enjoyable

_childDocuments_.review: A very clever and engaging typing game.The jokes almost always landed with me and I was constantly surprised by new ideas and nuances that were being introduced.There are many mechanics created around the concept of "language", from wordplay and using literal and metaphorical meanings of words to riddles, "20 questions" puzzles, and some light cryptography.Only problem I had with the game was the low difficulty of combat or lack of meaningful word upgrades (You fight using words in this game. _childDocuments_.review: Cryptmaster is a game that is kind of difficult to quickly describe to your friends. The presentation is quirky, endearing and darkly humerous, the music is excellent, the voice cast is really well rounded and I never get tired of listening to the Cryptmaster berate me for typing the same words over and over in an attempt to discover a new ability. It's also worth mentioning the card game, "whatever", which makes innovative use of the overall concept of letter mechanics that the game revolves around.If you've played enough farming sims, hack and slash rpg's, deck builders and roguelikes and want something off center for a change of pace, give it a shot. If English is not your native language or you type slowly you are either going to learn fast or you will hate this game.The Four Heroes of the CIty have been resurrected as zombies and are climbing up out of the catacombs to the light of day and the City itself. What could go wrong?  The eponymous (you'd better know that word if you want to win) Cryptmaster is hilarious. A combination of every horror movie narrator ever, he puts up with your childish and feculent inputs, and has voiced responses for a surprising number of unique words. This is also the only game ever (I think?) where you can save your game by JIZZing on an altar.I would *highly* suggest you write down the words you discover and what they do in a Joplin or Notepad++ document, because you aren't going to remember them and what they do otherwise.

_childDocuments_.review: is an incredibly creative wordy spin on the classic dungeon crawler RPG. Its amusing world and charming (dry) wit is what especially kept me intrigued, especially in an atypical fantasy adventure that delves into the depths below ground and its residents. Not an epic quest, a grand adventure, nor a world-saving odyssey, instead you're simply trying to reach the surface and bumbling through all the silly (yet occasionally unclear) obstacles and hijinxes that comes with it. All the more enjoyable is how freely they allow you to interact with the world in certain moments, letting you freely type your action of choice and almost always having a corresponding response.This typing theme continues to its combat system where your (theoretical) pen becomes your sword! While engaged in battle, you'll type out each spell / skill you'll want to use from a party member's list of abilities but each battle can vary so much as the enemies often will have passives that prevent or hinders you from using abilities keeping you constantly pausing to pull out the lists to re-strategize. Furthermore new abilities are acquired via a Wordle-like system where new letters are acquired from solving riddles, opening chests, or defeating enemies.Overall, Crypstmaster is great but especially great if you're enjoyer of the written word.

We were having a weird problem after a new update and when we brought it to the devs, they responded quickly despite being such a small team with limited time and made a rolled back version available for us. Definitely worth giving your money too, you won't regret it!

_childDocuments_.review: Cryptmaster was my most anticipated indie game of 2024 and for the most part I think it lives up. I say mostly because even though this is a game I recommend I do so lightly. It's innovative and there's not many other games out there that manage to combine spelling, guessing, and vocabulary skills with dungeon crawling gameplay. It's more like the execution of this mish-mash. First of all, I am an avid enjoyer of spelling games. I write a lot and like to keep my mind in check with my terminology. Learn new words and keep important ones in mind. I like games that test my skills in this category, but Cryptmaster does exactly that. Every attack and action you perform during combat is a word you must type, and to learn new skills you must guess the words correctly. You gain letters from combat and they help fill in the blanks for words you may be trying to guess. Meaning there's an incentive to grind out encounters and gain further hints. With more powerful skills usually being longer words or one you may be less familiar with.Exploration is fun as you traverse maze-like labyrinths and try to get to where you need to me. The story is not much to be honest, but it's the writing that makes up for it. Funny characters, jokes, and moments that will make you laugh your head off for how stupid it is. You're playing a game where actions are typed out, so of course it's gonna look at it and say "how more ridiculous can we make this?" I like Cryptmaster a lot. When it comes to the caveats though oh boy there's a lot of them. As much as I like guessing words I think there's too many skills in the game. Once I hit the final chapter I had only 1/5 of skills/memories for each character. The memories honestly take up unnecessary room, because it's the skills that actually matter. Trying to remember what skills you have is tricky, so 90% of the time you rely on basic ones unless you run into an armored or shielded bloke who can block certain lettered attacks. By the combat feels less about strategy and more on what typing combo will kill the dude in under ten seconds. There's a crafting system, but that's pretty useless outside one story quest. You can't heal outside of combat so sometimes you run back to altars to fully heal. Chest tests are fun as you interact with the object in the chest, and the different ways you interact reveals a different letter. Skull riddles not so much because you have to guess whatever absurd thing the lost soul is trying to describe. Sometimes it makes sense and other times it doesn't. I could go on and on, but again I do really like Cryptmaster. It's innovative and original. These are the risks that come when taking on experimental projects, and I'm fine with that. Not every game is perfect and who knows if someone will look at Cryptmaster, take influence, and try to make a better game like it. That's why innovation is so incredible. Play this game. It's worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: This is a unique take on the whole dungeon delving mechanic, where you essentially play hangman with a cast of beautifully voiced villains. The wordplay is fun and the mechanics really work well with its clever take on combat, but you'll probably mostly spend your time trying to spell out a variety of dumb words in the hopes that the narrator has a witty retort to them. Writing has great humor and definitely gives off Monty Python farce vibes for sure. Looking forward to seeing more games from this developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: I am a little bit into this game and am absolutely in love. The concept is really fresh, the art is really neat, and the writing keeps making me laugh out loud. The game involves guessing words, solving riddles, and identifying objects based on a brief, twenty questions-style inquest. I love crosswords and riddles so I feel like this game was tailored for me. There's even a fishing mechanic and a card mini game! What more do you need?Definitely recommend checking this game out.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so weird, from the cryptmaster, to the words. but it's wonderfully compelling. As I continue to play, there are so many wonderful little minigames and tools to try and get your characters powers and skills, their stories and memories. All the while the cryptmaster lurks and mumbles as you adventure once more.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: A truly unique typing-combat-puzzle-exploration game.I've been trying for a while to properly describe this, but I fail to.If there is anything in the videos and screens that speaks to you, chances are you will like what you will get.Easily my visual style of the year, for daring something this reduced and unique (and pulling it off).
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliantly written, with great, innovative gameplay. An  much creativity packed in to it. Also a pretty lengthy game (although I might just be illiterate.) Was honestly sad to see it end. I think that there was a little bit of missed potential to build a bit further on the combat, and wish that there were more proper boss battles. For the most part, they really did manage to push its gimmick to its absolute limits in terms of depth and design, and the love and passion put into the game shines through in every corner.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most unique takes on an RPG I've seen in a long while! Fantastic voice acting and a nice, straightforward plot but with surprisingly rich world building; the history of the world and relationships of characters to one another being steadily revealed via a combination of unlocked memories and snippets of texts felt very satisfying and gave a real reason to want to find/unlock everything.The sheer number of accessibility options/difficulty tweaks was also fantastic, particularly the option to play on turn-based mode, rather than real-time. The riddles in the game also span a really decent breadth, so no matter whether you're better at literal or more abstract riddles, there will be some that you get immediately and others that present a (pleasant!) challenge. I also very much appreciate that kissing is considered altar desecration, because I panicked and it was the only thing I could think of typing. 10/10, cannot recommend the game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: I love Cryptmaster. At first I thought it might be a bit too crosswordy for me, that it'd leave me in the dust so to speak. But no... it eases you into it, to such a degree that I could start plucking out the eyeballs of the hardier words with surgical ease. Well, except from those where I bruteforced the last letter because I'll be taffed up a lightpost if I know the word mellif-somethingsomething. But that comes much, much later. Cryptmaster doesn't really care to be scrabbler than thou. Most words you'll encounter are really mundane; the entire point is teasing out "what" mundane word the parser is looking for. And that is where the magic lies. Its like re-teaching yourself all the basics, and Cryptmaster is spelndid at doing that, without feeling like you're wearing a duncehat in a corner.Its unique all the way through in regards to gameplay: get letters to spell out words, then guess the words to progress your duuds. Then you spell out words in order to wallop smegheads, or remember something from one of your characters' backstories. I played most of the game in turnbased mode, and while I appreciate that that is a massive downscaling in difficulty and not the recommended mode, I felt it suited how I interacted with the game in a ponderous, rather than action oriented fashion. Don't be afraid to play in turnbased mode. What you've got to prove anyway?The visuals are astonishing. How each area of the game can feel distinct from one another in a black white subterranean setting speak to how unified the game's aesthetic vision is. It feels like a high-end goth webcomic thats taken some cues from old D&D artwork. The same goes for the music; a combination of cold dream-pop and darkwave synthersizer landscapes having intercorse with shoegaze guitars and heavy rock rhythmns. They even feature a little regal harpsicorde ditty. Very catchy stuff. Together with the visuals you get a very atmospheric and off-kilter experience that feels like what you'd get out of a bunch late teenage graveyard folks on a bit too much wine and video game enthusiasm.So easy recommend. This game is great and I'm not even finished teasing out all the secrets yet. Which I of course will do in due course, just know you gotta comb the areas, as well as your own grey matter in order to accomplish some of the later game puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Not terribly deep but definitely something different. Love the voices, enjoyed the humor, and feel challenged by most of the riddles. Do have trouble remembering all the combos during the heat of battle, so I've never felt very good at that.  But I have adjusted the options to make it less frustrating and a little easier too (because you don't get second chances on some of these, and I don't see myself replaying it).  Gameplay is not very complex but makes it good to return to in small pieces, and I imagine I'll keep it installed and eventually play my way through it like that.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly charming dungeon crawler with a lot of dry humor, riddles, and word guessing. I don't want to go into too much detail for this review because I would hate to spoil anything. But wandering around and fighting stuff by typing out skills your party members recall from guessing words while exploring is really fun. I have to say I'm surprised about how enjoyable Cryptmaster's optional card game is, again it's one of those things I don't want to go into too much detail, but it's surprisingly addictive.The Cryptmaster himself is your narrator/DM for the entire adventure, and he makes for great company. I've spent a lot of time just interacting with the world and seeing what he has to say about it. On the subject of enjoyable audio, the game's mostly laidback guitar soundtrack really helps establish the mood and is also a great companion while you delve into the dungeons.Honestly the only minor complaint I have is the little arrow representing your party on the minimap can be a little hard to read at times if you play with a non-rotating map.If you're a fan of dungeon crawling, wordplay, and riddle solving, I'd highly recommend picking this one up.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Cryptmaster is a game developed by Paul Hart, Lee Williams and Akupara Games and published by Akupara GamesThe game offers some nice graphics and a really cool aesthetic, although some ugly glitches here and there, it is pleasant all the sameThe game does suffer with some repetitiveness at certain areas of the game but a fun game nonethelessCryptmaster overall, however, is a fun game to play, yet sometimes repetitive and it does get boring and tedious if being played for a long time, but is a very good and really funny and unique dungeon crawler typing game to play in short bursts!
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun, hilarious, challenging and full of interesting characters. Love the art and the sound design. Highly recommended if you like word puzzles at all, it's definitely worth it.My only two criticisms are: The voice acting is all over the place, which is easy to ignore and it's too short! I wanted more.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: This game's an absolute blast to play! Personally I'd recommend the turnbased mode, as the real time one can be quite hectic...But if you need a game that you can stream to a small crowd of friends... This!Is!It!I swear, there's genuinely nothing more fun than trying to puzzle out the chests and 'character words' together.it's co-operative hangman if you will, but honestly it's so much more.The Cryptmasters (and honestly all of the other characters') narration, and all of the funny tidbits you can do (try pissing when you're prompted to 'corrupt' something :V), just make for an *amazing* experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't played for long, but let me say this: this is probably one of the most charming games i have played in a long time. The story setup, the atmosphere, and the gameplay. The gameplay together with the superb writing and voice acting really makes this a gem!It's just fun to "guess" words and to use words for everything in the world, it makes up for a very unique and special experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a 10/10. Unlocking the characters' abilities by spelling them out is a really unique and fun dynamic. Some of the puzzles are a little hard but all the really hard ones are optional. The voice acting is also amazing in this, I don't know how they managed to get so many different lines of dialogue at that quality. The story is really interesting and fun too. Like I said 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Such an amazing game for the literary-minded!The combat is engaging and incredibly well paced, as well as the leveling and skill-progression. Every enemy you fight brings you just *that* much closer to learning a new combat skill, or even the past of the party.The world-building and story are also incredibly well laid out, I *know* there'll be more to find on second or even third playthroughs.Overall an amazing, artistic, dungeon-crawler-itch-scratching game, well worth the $30!Hope to see more from these creators!
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: A really charming and stylish game. You play as a party of 4 on a grid-based RPG adventure. Instead of levelling up, you play hangman as you discover clues to the next word, which unlocks the next attack or lore-item for each character, earned from combat or riddles. Honestly, the riddles, puzzles, etc. where stronger than the combat loop, which for me got a little old.The star of the show is clearly the writing and the titular Cryptmaster, who just is so drily funny. The voice acting for him too is top notch, as is the case for the main cast. The voices for the little riddles littered over the dungeon are a mixed bag, I get the feelings friends and children contributed voices, but if anything, that adds to the charm and the narrative that these are lost-souls being forced to speak by the Cryptmaster.The art style is really really cool too, pure black and white, which looked great on my OLED monitor. The character designs too were really fun and varied. Accompanying this strong art-direction is some amazing music, like surprisingly so. It made trudging around, or 'skulking' as the Cryptmaster would have it, that much more fun.Overall, a tight little game. It took me about 11 hours and I enjoyed it the whole time. Definitely something I'd recommend if you're searching for something different.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed pooping on altars. This is a very fun word game where the riddles are neither too hard nor too easy. It has a very nice black and white aesthetic which I don't know of any other game that has it.Cryptmaster is funny with some funny lines from some interesting characters. It also allows me to let out an immature side as if I'm ten years old again typing rude words into it to see what happens, and Cryptmaster has some interesting responses to certain words.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: A genuinely fun (and funny) dungeon-crawler/typing adventure/word puzzler, Cryptmaster's one of the most pleasant surprises I've come across on steam. It's a great time on it's own, has a unique visual flair and charming atmosphere that masterfully-balances being amusing without being outright wacky. It's also a surprisingly-enjoyable party game, too! Try it on a Discord stream with friends or on a couch with some guests, it's something that a group can definitely get some mileage out of, even as much as a single player. Overall, an easy recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: An unholy blend of old school dungeon crawler, , and Hangman. All narrated by the titular Cryptmaster, a sarcastic and somewhat childish necromancer with a Vincent Price-esque voice - and an  number of voiceover lines for your potential inputs.It's unique, stylish, and charming, with some nice riddles to boot, and just about the perfect length to not wear out its welcome (unless you're going for 100% completion).The main weakness is its combat, which is, in a word, shallow. The enemies just aren't challenging enough for there to be any point in using something like 2/3 of your skills - for each party member, just use whatever does the most damage, throw in some cooldown resets and soul-stealing skill as appropriate, then heal afterwards.Oh, and turn up the loot sliders - the game isn't nearly long enough to fill out your skill trees.
