There were 2-3 times I had no clue what I was doing/looking for and had to go online to look up what to even do.  This could be solved like a quest log/journal that you can always tab to to see what/where you need to go or what you need to do.   I would have liked the heroes to have slightly shorter of CDs and the mobs to have more health.  This would lead to more type battles rather than me blast 4 words in 3 seconds and then wait for 7 seconds to type something else.The puzzle/riddle difficultly was perfect - starts easy, gets harder and harder.  The comedy/voice lines/ art are all top tier.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Charming, silly, subversive. Full of clever wordplay and puzzles and a colorful cast of characters in a greyscale world. Surprisingly in depth combat. It's a joy to explore with your guide, the Cryptmaster, as he oozes personality from his dead skull face, and every time you think you've outsmarted the game but it has anticipated you is its own little triumph. The music is also surprisingly well done and the game is full of thoughtful incedential experiences on every level. If you like riddles, dungeons, rats, jumbles, or having a good time, pick this one up!
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, and im not even a big fan of word games, i suck at those actually!Basically, its a dungeon crawler mixed with a word game, to unlock new skills and memories you have to guess words. Throughout the game, there will be chances to earn letters to help you guess these words, such as looting them from enemies, solving riddles, fishing, or guessing items inside chests.Besides that, the writing is hilarious. And the music is really good, good vibes all around despite being dead, yknow. And some of the puzzles in this game are really good, more specifically the 4 puzzles about halfway through the game, no spoilers but it was really fun to figure out! Albeit it was really tricky to understand at first.There is also accessibility options, Ranging from extra loot fingers (Which tell you how many letters you can loot from enemies) to extra guesses when guessing chest items, to making the game turn based instead of realtime! You can even make the cryptmaster solve riddles for you if you cant figure any of them out (The riddles in question are optional and are not required to beat the game)So personally, i would recommend this game, especially if you love word games!
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful game. I was drawn in by the graphics and the typing interface. What I didn't expect was to be so invested in learning more about our heroes and our guide, the Cryptmaster. He's a perfect mix of dry, peevish, sinister, and dotty. Talking to him was a delight, even as our one-word responses frustrated him to no end. (I always asked him to remember his past when peeking at the chests.)I was also pleasantly surprised to learn there was worldbuilding and backstory to the places I stumbled through. The game is genuinely funny, with the loose, anarchic vibe of the classic point and click adventures of the 90s, transported into an oldschool 80s RPG. The sound design deserves a shout out too. Every satisfying crunch of a bug or meaty smack as I landed a hit in the card minigame never got old. Obviously a recommend. Try out the demo, that's what sucked me in, and see if you don't end up attached to the Cryptmaster too.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best typing games in a while. I absolutely love the artstyle and character design. The puzzles are challenging, but not unbeatable and the story is as charming as can be. I like the humor and almost all of the soundtrack. It took me about 12 hours for the first playthrough and all the endings and another 4 hours for 100% achievements. None of them are dull or lead to long backtracking, which is always a bonus. I experienced 2 bugs specifically, one of which softlocked me and I had to load a previous save. The other one has to do with fishing and the fishes getting stuck on terrain. Altogether an amazing experience for 16 hours and a must play for people who like quizzes. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Cryptmaster creates an excellent first impression with its novel wordplay features, but the execution suffers, especially later into the game.GOOD:- Being able to type almost anything and get a relevant response is very appealing and provides a ton of immersion- Excellent voice acting, particularly by the necromancer- The dialog and most other language-centric themes are implemented really well; for example, guessing words to gain skills and level up- The graphical style is very appealing -- bold move to go completely grayscale, but it works wellBAD:- Combat is way too easy. FLIP + PINCH until enemy is dead, SOOTHE when needed. You will literally *gain* souls every fight.- The mini card game called "Whatever" is wildly imbalanced, allows for almost no counterplay against the opponent, and each match takes far too long to complete. It also feels terrible to skip your turn to refresh the letters. One simple suggestion for a fix is to spawn vowels more often, considering how important they are.- Some of the riddles are practically impossible to solve, even after finding the hints. For example, what's a 6-letter word for a closed, metal receptacle with a long, wooden handle? It is weighty, and you can lift the lid to see something inside it. Spoiler: the answer is a bedpan. You ever see a bedpan with a lid and a wooden handle? Yeah, me neither.I want to emphasize this point, because the riddles and wordplay are the core mechanics in this game. Far too often, I would find myself staring at the hints on the screen for many minutes at a time, absolutely certain that there was no reasonable solution to be found. Eventually I would give up, google the answer, and then feel even more frustrated when my original frustration was validated because I was right -- the riddle itself was just poorly-written.In other types of games, this would be forgivable. Here, however, the integrity of the wordplay is critical to the player experience. Ultimately, I quit the game because I ran into far too many unfair, unsolvable riddles.For a game that prides itself on dynamically responding to the player's input, the riddles are far too brittle.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: A great game if you love crossword puzzles, I mean this in a 100% positive wayLike, do you enjoy puns? do you enjoy vague, possibly misleading, clues? do you enjoy words that nobody ever actually uses? do you enjoy things that are black and white?Then this is the game for youAlso it runs great on Proton, which is always a huge plus, even if it's becoming common
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting concept for a game and unique enough that I enjoyed it. I loved all the riddles from the skulls. Overall, despite my nagging issues below, the pros of this game definitely outweighed the cons. Combat felt like an old flash game I played in middle school called TyperShark. I had a hard time remembering all the different word commands (there's like fifteen each eventually), so really up until right near the end (when I unlocked some stronger moves), I basically used the same combos for every encounter.Enjoyed the puzzles for the most part. Some of the chest objects were a little too abstract to guess correctly, although i think I got the majority of them. The crypticisms were a bit too obtuse for my liking, needed quite a bit of hints/nudging. Memory / combat unlocks were usually okay but some were words I would have never guessed (or even heard of for some). By the time I got to the end game the first time I still had 1.5 to 3 rows of memories to unlock for each character. These definitely did not progress as quickly as the progression of the story, I really can't imagine anyone would have a full unlock at the end without brute forcing.On some of the bigger levels (swamps at first, sunken seas, etc), navigation can be annoying. Stopping the minimap rotation helped a bit but trying to remember where you have or haven't been is a bit hard when all the areas look so similar. Overall, enjoyed the game quite a bit. Wordplay, puzzles and riddles were the highlights for me, combat was fine but wasn't my favorite, more of a means to get more unlocks / answers.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: It's mostly pretty great, can't say I've played anything quite like it except the typing games we'd play in school when I was a kid combined with an old-school dungeon crawl.It's got:- Good writing and voicework - the Cryptmaster is particularly good, which is good since he's front and center. It's often fairly funny. - A sort of 20-questions-ish game to identify objects, though you really get like 5/6 words. It's a fun diversion that helps you "level up"- A mostly solid set of riddles.- Some light puzzles which are mostly good, although one is a simple substitution cipher and ain't nobody got time for those.- An in-universe card game, which I thought was... not good at all. Thankfully optional.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first gather-and-craft mechanic that I've loved. It's immediately intuitive, and you instantly know which ingredients will be perfect for which potions as soon as you look at them. That they've made gather-and-craft legitimately fun is a small miracle in my book. That miracle happens to be couched in a 10/10 word-based dungeon crawler with genuinely entertaining writing. This game is actively generating joy for me and I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: If you get the following reference you'll fall head over heels in love with this game. "You are standing in the cavern of the evil wizard. All around you are the carcasses of slain ice dwarfs."And if you don't; It's likely you'll not have any idea why you would want a game such as this, but believe me you DO.Deliciously simple; surprisingly quick to reveal it's depth. British TV show 'Knightmare' with a dash of Sesame Street whipped up by a Pagan Mavis Beacon.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game because of a youtube video I watched. Only saw a few minutes of the beginning of the game and instantly thought "this looks cool"! (And it is!)Its kind of a mix of an old school adventure game, and a typing game. Weird concept but works really well. Camera takes a second getting used to, but you start to not mind it after a short while.TLDR: If a typing RPG Adventure game sounds interesting to you, try it. Its great.Voice acting is tight as well, no complains. Great work, good delivery, kudos to the voice actors!The art is wonderful, and I really like they have systems in place to make the game easier for idiots like me.The humour feels very british to me. I like it. The main voice of the game (the cryptmaster) has never become boring or annoying and was fun to be around until the end.The puzzles are fun to solve, the combat is engagingly different, and the world seems really interesting.The negatives:tbh there arent much.Sometimes the character you talk to becomes louder than the rest which is probably just a bug. Noticed this at , whos voice was much louder than anyone elses.The levelling(?) is kind of off. In my first play through I beat it with only levelling up once. If you use all the words they give you its also kind of easy with the right strategy.I barely unlocked half of all characters memories / attacks at the end. Could also be my fault though ^^There is no map :( -> please add a world map! (and the ability to mark places on it)Steven (why is he alive, also I love him)These are all fairly minor issues. They haven't impacted my fun my much if any. Because this game seems to be in active development, I am sure some of these will be tweaked in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Two hours in and I am in loveA dungeoncrawler word game with lots of charm. Can't think of any other game that is like this, worth it alone for the unique gaming experience. You seek letters to discover words for your characters. Figuring out the words is fun, very much the Wordle vibe. At any point you can type a word and shout it into the void, unlocking new fun things!The combat consists of typing your abilities, with a (so far, seemingly) robust combo/synergy system as you unlock abilities. I'm a giant nerd with a blank-keycapped keyboard and take typing tests for fun, so the heat of timed combat in which ya gotta quickly type the various words to fire off your combos is totally my jam. So far, combats have been short and juuuust often enough to be fun rather than tedious, with a steady stream of new abilities and words to type to keep em fresh. The devs were also kind enough to add a turn-based mode for the non-masochists who don't want to spell under duress, but I'm soooo thankful for them turning duress spelling into a game mechanic. The yapping feels purposeful and my responses feel meaningful, as I typed them in myself rather than selecting from a list. A few times I gave what I thought would be a cheeky answer and the (all voiced) NPC responded in a way that actually made me laugh out loud. And of course, an in-world card game. Love a good in-world card game. I think each match does go a liiiiittle too long for what it is, hopefully the future update condenses it a bit. A few things that bug me - playing on ultrawide, turning the camera makes me a tiny bit motion sick. Turned off blur and that helps a little. With the 20 questions chests, I wish the game made it more clear what happens if I get the answer wrong. My gamer brain does not like the idea of a chest completely vanishing with no recourse, but it turns out there's no harm at all in getting such things wrong, you only miss a chance for more letters (which are beyond plentiful). A hint system for some riddles would be nice, rather than the Cryptmaster just giving the answer if you're stuck. Very polite to allow infinite tries rather than missing out on anything though. Looking forward to obsessing over this for the next week or two
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Short game, very glad I played it. A lovely little world that gives you an exceptional degree of freedom to poke and prod it, with stellar voice acting from main and side characters. A simple adventure story, but told in a way that leaves you invested anyways. The only major complaint I have is the in-game card battles. They are completely optional, and I did enjoy them, but it feels strange that a game so short feels the need to throw in mini-games when there isn't even a challenging boss for the primary gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't expect this game to test my typing skills I gained from middle school XD The amount of responses and Easter eggs I got just from typing single words is surprising, and I had so much fun pissing off the Cryptmaster from time to time. The variety in gameplay such as the chest puzzles and skull riddles tie compliment the typing mechanics well, and having those be tied to unlocking each character's skills is clever. The combat was something I had to gradually get used to, but including the turn-based option helped out a lot. Throwing in mechanics like the word-specific shields adds some nice variety to the combat too.What got me hooked into this game even further are the characters and world building. From unlocking each party members' memories and finding out that one of them's responsible for the extinction of a bird species, to writing a diss track with a piper, to discovering a crab dimension, there's a lot of love and care put into this game, and some parts ended up surprising me the more I played. I really hope to see more of this funky fantasy world if there are more plans for it in the future!If I have to give some critique, I do feel like a NG+ would be nice after completing the game instead of just opening back to our save points. I also hoped that the last two chapters would be longer, and I'm glad to see that there's going to be an update that will do just that.Overall, Cryptmaster's such a delight to play through, and I hope it gets more recognition! It's not afraid to experiment with its gameplay, the art style gives off these beautiful 80s fantasy vibes, the writing and dialogue are witty, the voice acting is superb, and the music suit the game quite well!9.5/10 Came for the typing mechanic, DNDesque visuals and the hot skeleton necromancer, stayed for the characters and worldbuilding. Also Syn deserves better ;-;SooOOOothe

_childDocuments_.review: Cryptmaster is a unique spin on your classic puzzle game that combines it with a dungeoncrawler has a lot of neat ideas that ended up falling a bit flat for me. I've refrained from including any major spoilers and included a summary at the bottom.The Good:* The game knows its gameplay loop well. The core gameplay loop involves exploring around the dungeon, engaging in combat by typing various words you learn and unlock by earning letters that help you guess the word Wheel of Fortune style, giving you various puzzles in the form of either 20 questions or riddles. This results in a nice contrast between tense moments of frantic typing and contemplative moments of trying to think of the perfect answer to a brain teaser.* The enemies are varied enough that they do genuinely force you to rework what attacks/words you might use on them. As an example, some are immune to particular debuffs, while others are punish or reward using certain letters or require specific kinds of attacks. There were definitely times when I caught myself and went "crap, I can't use words A, B, or C that I normally do, so I need to remember the other words or pull up the word list to see which ones I actually can use." The actual typing combat itself typically lasted somewhere between 10-90 seconds depending on the enemy's health and how disruptive its abilities were. There is an option to turn on a turn-based combat system, but it's clear from the game's design that completing combat in real time is how things were meant to be played.* The game has a great sense of charm and whimsy without being distracting or pulling you out of things. Probably the most memorable part of this game is the characters and how they interact with your party and each other. I had quite a few moments where I couldn't help but crack a smile.* The hint system is relatively well done. Oftentimes if you get stuck on a puzzle, you'll have resources to either get little hints over time or the game will offer to point you close to the answer if you fail enough times. This fail forward system is paced well enough that I felt like I never had clues forced on me when I didn't want them, but was generally given enough help that when I was about to feel truly stuck I could continue playing rather than the game grinding to a halt.* There's a trading card/word game hybrid that is pretty cleverly done as a minigame. It's never mandatory to play, but provides a nice relief and way to grind the game's currency if you feel the need to do so.* The dictionary of words considered and used by the game is genuinely impressive considering no AI was used. There's at least one point in the game that comes to mind that reflects a labor of love in taking the open ended responses the player might give and turning them into a charming moment.The Bad:* While the ideas in the gameplay loop are solid, after a while you'll likely fall into a predictable combat pattern within that loop. Many of the words you can use to attack enemies, buff yourself or allies, or debuff your enemies are either situational due to a cooldown timer. Although I think the timer is an incredibly important restriction (it prevents you from repeatedly typing the same word 20 times in a row to kill an an enemy, while also forgiving players who are slower typers), it also severely limits the strategies you might realistically use. After a while, many of the words you unlock are simply worse versions of words you've already unlocked or are so situational that you probably won't bother learning them. After a few hours, I was solidly in a rhythm of typing out the same half a dozen words (swapping them out as I got upgrades) to combo together since the time pressure to type fast (for reference, I type at around 90 words per minute) means that, unless an enemy really punished my default approach, I wasn't going to sit there and think of the optimal words for the specific situation. * Similarly, the 20 questions minigame sounds great in theory, but has a fatal flaw. Since it takes away one of your questions whenever it doesn't understand what you're trying to ask (you provide a single word that it tries to interpret), you're encouraged to play it safe and use the same half dozen questions. Every time I wanted to get clever I had to ask myself "Is it worth burning a question that I might not get *any* information out of when I can ask one of the safe questions I know and know it will understand what I'm asking?" The answer was rarely yes.* The map is a nightmare to navigate. While the game provides you a nice minimap of the grid for each room, there is no map for the general area of the dungeon you are in. This means that sometimes the game will be asking you to find a Macguffin or you'll be searching around an area (trying to make sure you explored everything if you're like me) and not be sure if you've missed anything. On one hand, this is certainly solvable by creating your own map and there's something to be said for encouraging players to engage in old school mapping, but it can be incrediby frustrating in the moment.* The Macguffin system can be incredibly frustrating at times, in part due to the map. Particularly, the last set of macguffins in the game was something I spent multiple hours (literally) lurking around the map trying to find it without cheating, but ultimately had to look up online and found it in a location that only made sense to me in retrospect.The Uncertain:* The play length according to the developer is between 8-15 hours. That means you're paying somewhere between $1-3 per hour of gameplay outside of a sale. My playthrough ended up taking just over 15 hours since I tried to do all the sidequests I encountered and got stuck a few times (due to the map and mandatory Macguffins).* Little replayability. While I don't think every game needs to be replayable, I wish the game had a little more to do in it after completion. There's technical multiple endings to explore and a few secrets to uncover, but overall once you're done you're done. The main thing is the attack unlock system has far more words than I think most individuals would get through in a single playthrough (I got through about half of the list in mine), so you could grind away at that if you'd like.Conclusion:Cryptmaster is an innovative game I had quite a bit of fun playing, but it had some roughness around the edges that soured the experience a bit for me. At times it feels like a collection of good ideas that could have used a bit more refinement and tied together with a bit more cohesion. It's definitely a game I enjoyed playing, but not one I'd recommend to the average gamer at it's retail price unless you're a big typing/puzzle games person. That said, if it was expanded to have a bit more content/replayability or was discounted more steeply than the $21 USD I paid for it, I think it's an experience you won't regret. Overall, I'd give it a 3.5/5 stars.

_childDocuments_.review: If you had told me last year that one of the coolest games I would play in 2024 was all about typing words I would never have believed you. Yet Cryptmaster, a game about typing words, is here and it is without a doubt one of the coolest games I've played this year. It does a phenomenal job making word guessing games, riddles, and even just speed typing challenges into game mechanics. All of this bundled in an excellent looking black and white dungeon and filled with a lot of weird characters with fun voice acting. At its core, Cryptmaster is a game about guessing words related to your four characters' memories so you can unlock new abilities and character lore. There are various activities spread throughout the map that allow you to obtain letters that will fill out spots in the words you're trying to guess. As an example of this: chests will contain an item that the titular Cryptmaster will describe for you, at your prompting him to look, touch, taste, or whatever you can think of to have him try, and if you can correctly guess the item, all letters in that item's name will be added to the character words you are trying to guess. Writing that out now makes it sound kind of confusing, but I promise it's very intuitive. Combat consists of typing out the name of an ability of one of your characters to have them attack an enemy, buff an ally, or try to avoid damage. Once you've used an ability for a character, that character goes on a brief cooldown before you can use another ability of theirs. Once you've defeated an enemy, you can choose one letter of its name to see if that letter is in any of the character words you are currently trying to guess. I don't want to get too much into it for now, this game is definitely better to experience yourself than to read about, but if any of that sounds at all intriguing to you I highly recommend checking this game out!

_childDocuments_.review: If what you want is a mashup of _Mavis Beacon Teaches Typing_ and _Wizardry IV_, have I got excellent news for you.Formally, it's a cardinal-directions blobber upwards dungeon crawl.  In fact, exactly _Wizardry IV_ except you're playing a minion carrying Werdna's phylactery rather than Werdna himself.  If you are not a nerd of a certain age, that probably doesn't help you.Also, old-school riddles and a cool blind-men-describing-the-elephant mechanic.It's also got surprisingly good fishing and collectible-card minigames.  Seriously, "Whatever" would work as an actual standalone game.This game is not going to be to everyone's tastes.  I suspect it's not actually to very many people's tastes.  But if you, like I, are one of those people, you're going to love this.  There are whole optional questlines I haven't even cracked yet, and one of the cipher puzzles literally made me snort when I found one of the things-to-be-deciphered, because...of course it was.  You'll know it when you get there.There are plenty of Let's Play videos of this out there.  Watch 20 minutes of one to decide whether this is your thing.For me, this is one of the best games of 2024.  Balatro is the other one.  They are nothing at all alike.

_childDocuments_.review: A game about soulless entities that should pride itself on the amount of soul it has. From the writing, to the visuals, to the sound design, this game is dripping with character and the passion and love for the project is always on full display. With a dev team of just two people this game is massively impressive, but you won't be thinking of that when you're playing the game. Instead you'll be wracking your brain trying to figure out tons of clever and fun literary puzzles, like riddles, wordles, or playing 20 questions with the amazingly voiced "Cryptmaster," who always gets a laugh out of me. While I'm trying to sum up my thoughts on this game and why I like it so much, my mind keeps wandering to another game I love - Monkey Island. While tonally and visually distinct from one another, theyre both games with this great sense of humor that's absurdist, clever, and just straight up silly at times, and this wonderful sense of humor pushes you to explore the game in way that I find so much more gratifying than a simple item pickup that pads your stats. If you're someone who loves literature, brain teasers, funny jokes, independent art, or you're just looking for a breathe of fresh air, "Cryptmaster" delivers.

A handful of characters are definitely more uncomfortable looking than others, but there's never anything really disgusting or scary that happens.Cryptmaster is a game where you interact with the world by typing in one word at a time (with the exception of movement). _childDocuments_.review: Slightly pricey at forty bucks for a ten twelve hour game, but as it is, excellently crafted from just about every angle. Thorough accessibility options, an eclectic though interesting list of music, and some great voice acting. You can get more out of it if you put more into it, take your time, etc.For downsides, I would say I can't see any world that you complete the skill tree without truly excessive grinding or changing the default options to be several times more generous, and a couple of examples of weird and kind of grating voice acting that- for example- feel like the dev's four year old niece or something. The sound mixing can be a little weird, and the currency mechanic can be extremely strict depending on your playstyle, but overall- these are pretty minor notes, especially because the game can be completed without said grinding.Highly recommended puzzle game-- at ten or twenty bucks this'd be a steal. Great fun on a voice call with friends if they're into word games. Go without spoilers.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like wordplay, typing, and cheeky dungeon crawlers, PLAY CRYPTMASTER! Lead your party of four undead amnesiac adventurers out of the crypts and through areas populated by just as delightfully bizarre people and monsters to get to the surface... Where you can solve the riddle of who you are – and who the Cryptmaster is, really – as you decide the fate of the underworld. Not to mention the built-in card game and fishing! The music, art, and voice-over performances combine to create a world wholly weird and endearing.I will say that Cryptmaster isn't perfect – I experienced two buggy chests, the ways that puzzles are presented in the later game without much context can feel daunting, and more than once I found myself walking in circles because I was unclear about how to find something that was needed to continue. The voice acting is spectacular (especially in regards to Lee Williams as the titular Cryptmaster, whom I just love to egg on), and there's a plethora of more NPCs full of personality in this notably monochrome world. Before you buy the game, you can play the demo moments before your party leaves the crypt. It's a great way to gauge if the rest of the adventure will be your cup of tea, so I recommend giving it a shot if you're having doubts. But I honestly can't praise this game enough.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally leave reviews for games, but I genuinely had such an interesting and refreshing time with Cryptmaster I feel like I have to. Think I completed all riddles, chests and crypticisms as well as many secrets, 21 hours of gameplay total which feels very fair for the price.The artstyle, music and gameplay are fantastic. I've always wanted a a "Typing of the Dead" style game with some more mechanics and Cryptmaster pulls it off essentially flawlessly. The voice acting and character design are both rich and full of humour. And 'Whatever' is a great card game that could definitely be it's own game .My only small complaint is I didn't get to learn all the character's stories/skills by the end of the game, and despite the fishing mechanic being enjoyable I don't think I'd grind it for hours on end to try and guess the remaining rows of words. Think I got to the third/fourth rows for each character by the end of the game, and thats with having done every possible riddle, chest and fighting every enemy I encountered. An end-game mechanic to help get letters without too much of a grind would be a really welcomed addition. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a real diamond in the rough. Surpassed expectations in every regard. Overall very big recommend, the game deserves much more attention than it's getting. I still have some feedback, but I'll save that for the end. If there is a just one thing I want people on-the-fence to read, it'd be to  It encapsulates the gist of the game very effectively, and sold me on buying the full game almost immediately. It might be the same for you too. At the same time, if it doesn't tickle your fancy then you won't have spent money on it. (More games should have demos! They're great!)I'm not gonna lie, when first getting into the game, I was worried that the gimmick would get old quickly and the game wouldn't expand on the concept, and instead only continue to engage with it on a surface level. Either that, or the game would just be very short. Such is the fate of many Gimmick Games(TM) that revolve around a singular gimmick. The game is surprisingly long, goes surprisingly in-depth, and does indeed expand a lot on the initial gimmick of the game, and utilising it in ways I wasn't expecting (the brewing, card game, fishing, and combat modifiers are big examples of this). There is a lot of "Game" here, which I think justifies its ~$20 price tag, which initially put me off because I wasn't sure if the game was just going to be a total of 4 hours long. There is also a very significant amount of exploring and secret hunting. You go out of your way and find a cryptic clue about something or other, wonder "hm I wonder what that's about", go to a specific spot or say a specific thing (or both), and you unlock a neat little thing. The game is full of that. Outside of the optional one-off riddle puzzles/chests, this is also the first time in a very long time where I make IRL notes about stuff in a game as I try to work out a puzzle or cipher. That was a very cool experience. Figuring puzzles out feels very organic, which is important. There is an air of mysticism and intrigue at times, which is a feeling I wasn't expecting the game to capture.Additionally, the soundtrack goes unreasonably hard, which is a big bonus. The tone is just right for me, as well. It doesn't take itself too seriously, but isn't even nearly "haha random haha nothing matters haha satire" that it becomes hard to be invested in literally anything in the game's world. It feels like a 90s text adventure game, but the devs are in on the joke and recognise the primal urge to type stupid ♥♥♥♥ into the game. The voicework is fantastic, too, which definitely helps a lot! Again, overall, big recommend! That is all. Remember to  on your altars, fellow undead horrors!

_childDocuments_.review: An innovative game with enough meat on its bones to support its central gimmick admirably. It's got the gameplay of Typing of the Dead, the world of a Soulsborne, the wit of one of the sassier British humorists, and a narrator straight from one of those VHS board games that were apparently popular in the 80s. The combat is engrossing and occasionally challenging, with enough variety to keep you interested. I'm not quite sure how I feel about metering players' attacks with the same currency you buy cards with, but it only really got frustrating once. The riddle and 20-Questions-styled challenges the game throws are pretty enjoyable, albeit rather annoying if you have a tendency of getting stuck on certain bits of wordplay. Hints do exist, but in my experience the ratio of "get it immediately" to "a hint actually helped" to "screw it, I'm getting the answer from Google" is about 70-10-20. The writing is good-to-stellar, although there are some points that, while not exactly weak, do kinda throw one for a loop. I would say that the tone of the game is "Soulslike meets Shrek," which is a noble target to shoot for if you can hit it. They do. Most of the time. That being said, it sometimes leans a bit too far one way or the other to be pitch-perfect in its consistency; the Piper, for instance, leans much further towards the Shrek end of the scale than basically anyone else in the game (although he does set up a great bit about the Cryptmaster being a crotchety old man a bit later). That being said, the world could use more comedic takes on dark fantasy, and even if it didn't, the writing is a 9/10 in my book, and honestly would have justified buying a game somewhat inferior to this.It's a skosh short, but I think it's just long enough to fully explore its central conceit and its (actually pretty fun) world without overstaying its welcome; if you include exploring every nook and cranny I suspect it would be far longer.If you have motion sensitivity issues, PLAY THE DEMO FIRST. It took a bit of tweaking with the options to get to the point where it didn't immediately give my wife motion sickness or me a little bit of a headache. Tragically, as much as I adore grayscale 3d graphics, it can be a bit migraine-inducing to the elderly, decrepit members of the late-20s-and-up club. (for the record, the options I found useful were to turn off screenshake, turn the turn speed down, and select a dark blue color tint. It had the added benefit of making things look Very Cool)Finally, I know that asking for a world map in a Soulsborne tale of the undead is somewhat heretical, but it would be appreciated. I'm complaining a lot here, but this is one of the best things I've played during a year that has had a surplus of great games. At the very least, check out the demo. You _we y_ursel_ that much.

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserves a lot of praise. But first, some first impressions that I had that were wrong: This game is not horror at all, the style is just... a bit creepy, but the contents is just comedy and puns. To me, this game has been a wonderful DnD campaign where you interpret four stupid undead. It has a good story, tons of riddles, tons of puns, a lot of mechanography and I learned a lot of English along the way (not my native tongue). Good accessibility options as well to customise the difficulty of it all.It has a lot of symbolism as well. "Words control everything" is an understatement of the general description. Words don't only control everything, words are everything here. Your memories. Your actions. Your solutions to problems. Your way of transportation. Single words are the main mechanic of this game, and I sincerely praise the devs because it feels very natural, and I was surprised every time I went to say something uncommon and there was a wonderful programmed response to it. And I want to note, does not have any AI to it, they basically programmed a ton of specific things you could say and crafted proper responses manually, which manages to make them feel very human and real.This game has some flaws, but honestly I don't care about them. I had fun, I laughed a lot, the style is extremely unique, the experience was great. For people considering buying it or not, if you like either of these three: DnD, riddles, puns, then you're going to like this. If you don't like neither, then sure, check a gameplay first.

_childDocuments_.review: I really love seeing unique games taking big swings on a distinct vision and having it totally pay off! Great voice acting, funny writing, and unique game play that really becomes rounded out the more words you learn for your party. There was something about the combat that didn't click with me at first but once I got more words and discovered a few solid combos to loop between, it came together in a much more satisfying way. And the concept of "looting" a letter from a defeated enemy's name to reveal a letter in your party's next skill is a great idea. Even just the core action of figuring out your party's skills is such a fun part of the experience sometimes I found myself sitting there guessing words for a few minutes trying to brute force a couple and it's still fun. I really get a kick out of the 20-questions style guessing game for opening chests because of all of the different verbs you can use to elicit a description from the Cryptmaster. Maybe a little disappointing how quickly you see these items repeat though. There are skulls you can find that give riddles which are fun enough, if not a little generic. And navigating some the dungeon spaces can be a little tedious or samey. But the interactions between characters and the Cryptmaster's running commentary are consistent in quality and charm. I love when he pokes fun at the different members of the party too. Conversations really shine when you can experiment with words and see what kinds of reactions you get. It's like Scribblenauts in that way where you just want to try everything and see what they've accounted for. I was pleasantly surprised at how often my weird off-kilter words actually had scripted responses. It's always fun when you think of a non-obvious word to use in a conversation that actually has a special response and reaction from the character you're speaking with. Also, Whatever is a top tier game-within-a-game. I would buy a standalone Whatever mobile port. I really love seeing unique games taking big swings on a distinct vision and having it totally pay off!

_childDocuments_.review: This game was outstanding, sort of a typing dungeon crawler.  Your characters don't have equipment, they have words that you gradually unlock by getting letters in each one until you can guess it correctly.  You're navigating, fighting, playing four separate games of Hangman (minus the 'lose' part), exploring, riddling, and puzzling.  You'll have a better time in Realtime mode if you're a good typist.  I mostly played it in 'turn based' mode (where each letter you type in combat, including typos, advances the enemy's clock), and you should be fine there as long you can be accurate in your typing.  I can type fast, but I can't *think* that fast anymore at my advanced age, so turn-based was excellent.  I've never seen a game quite like this, and I mean that in the good way.  It's super creative.  It was a lot of fun in turn-based mode, and if you have a good memory and can type quickly, real-time might be even better.  I finished with maybe half the words unlocked.  If you want to get all the words for all the achievements, looks like it will take quite a lot of grinding. Oh, and a hint: don't stress out if you don't guess the contents of a chest or box.  All you're getting is letters for your current unknown word for each character.   Some items have a lot of letters and will substitute for many fights (you get one letter per fight), but it's not a crippling blow to lose out on some.  Don't worry about perfection with this game, just have fun.  It'll work out.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game, but there are plenty of caveats to go with that. I strongly recommend playing through the demo as it is basically the start of the game, and I knew as soon as I played through that I would be buying. Cryptmaster has a really strong start, and is engaging for a good amount of time, however, I feel like it loses its momentum at about the halfway point or so, and kind of just fizzles to the end. I can't quite put my finger on why this is. I think, for one, the text commands become somewhat cumbersome, both from a memory standpoint and a catalog standpoint. Pulling up the word list is kind of tedious, especially mid-combat, but also memorizing every combination and ability would require playing for much longer. I only spent 8 hours from start to finish, which is pretty short for an RPG and definitely not enough time to really ingrain all the commands. I basically just used a few of them for the entire thing, even if I knew that it wasn't the optimal way to get through. Should it have been longer? No. There wouldn't be much to do. The puzzles are fine, though very rote after a while. Exploring is not really a thing as there isn't anything novel to find other than more riddles that are kind of the same riddles you've been seeing in every room. I was actively trying to avoid combat towards the end as there doesn't seem to be much point. You lose your soul currency with every action and then more of it to heal after the fight, and it's honestly easier to guess the words than to fight and hope for more letters. The soul currency seems too rare at certain points, especially if you feel like buying cards for the card minigame at any point (I didn't because that got to be too frustrating to even bother playing).  So why am I recommending, despite all this negative sentiment?  The first few hours are incredibly engaging, and it feels very novel to use typing to fight (I personally have never played any other typing game). The presentation is top-notch, as is the voice acting. The story is intriguing, to a point, and was really the thing that kept me playing to the end. I was genuinely curious to see what climbing up these many levels was going to expose. Overall, this is a game worth your time. It's clever, mostly fun, and looks great.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going against my rule of rating things before I finish them just so I can tell you how good and fun Cryptmaster is. This game is absolutely overflowing with passion and love. There is so much fun to be had in this game, you just have to be sure not to blow through it all. Look around the world, settle in, you're here to stay anyway. The amount of chests to find, skulls to commune with, lore to read, words to type to every character imaginable with full voice-acted responses will keep you busy for a long while. Not to mention the combat, complete with a leveling system based on how good you can spell words, keeps things fresh and interesting while moving you through the world and story. The soundtrack is actually a f--kin banger and Rats! (the track, not the animal) has got to be one of the best songs in gaming. Actually feels like it could go up against something like Outset Island from Wind Waker and compete and idk man that's really high praise from someone like me I don't know how else to explain that the tracks are just good and really "get it". Awesome stuff.AND THE VAs?! Nice. Weird. Loved it. Not sure how much directing went into the voice work but the direction of all the voices was the best part so whoever's idea that all was? Nice. Good job VAs, you brought the whole world together!I really just can't give this game enough praise. It is truly something unique, something I've never played before. I haven't laughed this hard AND been this frustrated at a game all at once (seriously some of those riddles would make even a father roll his eyes!) and I donno, I think that's the desired effect. Without the silliness the riddles would begin to drag and without the puzzles the humor wouldn't hit near the same; it's honestly a match made in...uh...wait.ALSO (omg how did I almost forget?!!) there's an entire card game in this game and it's SO fun. Kinda hoping there's a way to play this with the community at some point? Maybe a DLC? I would buy it in an instant! The world NEEDS more fun and interesting card games that don't take 50 pages of wiki knowledge to play. Truly blessed.So uh.. Yeah, play the game. This one was kind of all over the place but the game is much more articulate than me anyway so whatever. I suggest it BUY THE GAME!!!!! thanks. (:

_childDocuments_.review: Games like this that are a highly underappreciated hit only come once in a while. Cryptmaster is definitely one of those.At its core it's a dungeon crawler, and they've built a very interesting world to explore. I think I've barely scratched the surface at 3 hours in.Instead of an XP system, progression is done by basically you actually learning about the characters in your party, and typing in a word related to them that unlocks either a skill or a memory for that character. It's a very fun way to drip feed lore, and then you have to actually remember and type the skills as you need them. The artystyle is very distinct and I like it. There are lots of funny little interactions like how the Cryptmaster hides his mouth when he "licks" an object (ostensibly because animating licking is a lot of work for little reward, but this way is better anyway because it implies he's a shy little guy.)The humor and everything is pretty spot on so far, I've had a good couple chuckles. Haha, Joro, you look stupid!I wish after you failed chests that it gave you a hint as to what it was anyway, as there have been times I felt like I was really close but couldn't glean anything else and failed a guess, which feels kind of bad. But I think I have plenty of souls and skills so far, so not really a problem.All that said, this is one of my favorite 2024 game releases so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Gamers often complain that games these days aren't as innovative or creative as they were in the past, but Cryptmaster is yet another proof that innovation and creativity is still alive and well in game dev, you just have to search more in the indie space. Cryptmaster's idiosyncratic melding of word games and dungeon crawlers might be a bit too niche to really become a big hit, but I'm sure everyone can still appreciate both the nostalgia and novelty this game evokes. Also if you end up loving the goofy characters, fun riddles, clever typing-game-turned-combat systems, and the gorgeously illustrated B&W universe, then you will be utterly, completely HOOKED. I can't stop thinking about this game since I started playing it.

Upon first look, the artwork appears creepy and dark, but it is such a funny and clever game. It contains no horror, gore, or jump scares. I guess there might technically be one or two but it's definitely more like "That was not supposed to happen like that!"   The art and creativity of this game makes it so unique. The default graphics are gray-scale, but you can change it to a different single color-scale. I went default then red-scale then blue-scale (which was beautiful with purple hues) and back to red. The voice acting is awesome and also hilarious.I had an  time playing this game, but there are a few things I would point out that may be an issue for a would-be player: I haven't checked yet, but I hope they will make more games like this. _childDocuments_.review: Fun game, enjoying both solo and streaming to friends. First run took 13 hours but I know I missed some side content (and A LOT of words). _childDocuments_.review: Cryptmaster is to traditional dungeon crawlers what typing of the dead is to light gun games. It's what you'd expect from a dungeon crawler, navigating grid based environments, fighting battles that can be real time or turn based, solving puzzles, and talking to NPCs, except all of it involves typing out words.The way characters level up is very clever; your 4 party members are recently raised undead who don't recall anything other than their names. To make them stronger they need to remember details and skills from their past, which involves figuring out the right word to jog their memory. You get hints in the form of letters which fill in the blanks, until you either fill out the entire word or can guess what it is.It starts out very simple but some of the puzzles get more involved later on, and there are some optional 'endgame' puzzles that are quite challenging to solve. Overall it does a great job of mixing various word based puzzles/challenges into a narrative driven game, with a nice art style, excellent voice acting, and solid and amusing writing.

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzles and riddles galore. The perfect game if you love solve word based conundrum.  In Cryptmaster, you are long dead warriors trying to escape from a crypt, aided by a mysterious necromancer called the Cryptmaster. You generally do this by exploring, playing card games, rapping with a bard at one point, and killing various creatures that roam the undergrounds dark depths. Visually and auditorily, the game is an utter treat. Everything is beautiful black and white and look like an inky drawing out of an old fantasy novel. The writing, as expected of a game based around words, is excellent. The major gripe I have of the game is the combat, it isn't very interesting, and doesn't get much better as the game progresses. It takes until the last fourth for enemies to become any danger. Despite that I give a high recommend. The game is 8 hours long if you're just doing the mainquest, but can last much longer if you want to do side content.

Moreso how much of it reacts back to what I thought were very specific words. In addition, the puzzles are genuinely difficult but not to the point they're unsolvable. It does require you to know basic words and type pretty fast in battles. Still, an amazing game. Congrats to the team behind it.

Riddles make you strain your brain and there are puns abound. However, this is not a game for everyone. The typing / speaking gimmick is unique, but it limits how you interact with the world, for better and worse. The weak points of the typing interface become most obvious during combat. While you gain a literal list of skills for each character, only a few are useful. For anyone else, I would advise they look elsewhere for a dungeon crawler style game.

_childDocuments_.review: Articulating how much kid-me would have lost their mind over knowing  would one day exist seems like a futile endeavor, so I’ll just leave it at this: I adore fishing minigames in RPGs. I adore card minigames in RPGs. I pored over strategy guides and gaming magazine articles seeking secrets in titles I loved, and even those I had yet to play. I grew up writing letters and school notes in Tengwar. My sense of humor is steeped in dad jokes and utterly atrocious puns, and my teachers were sporadically concerned by how much I liked doodling the Horned King from .  has all of these elements and more. It’s a game that’s been stunningly compatible with a much broader pool of people than I expected—but it scratches a multitude of my long-standing gaming and storytelling itches at a level that’s stunningly rare for me to find in any piece of media.I highly suspect  will be my personal Game of the Year for 2024. That would hold completely true even if I had no professional involvement with the title whatsoever—I might be even more annoying about my love for it in that instance—but, as the universe has a sense of humor, I had the immense privilege of ending up in the game’s English voice cast. (I got a copy of the game for free; my enthusiastic yelling about it is entirely of my own volition.)Much as I would love to continue gushing about  in concept and sing the praises of its devs and production staff ad nauseam, I understand that this is meant as a review. So, let me take the opportunity to break things down with as few spoilers as possible:- Fantastic visual style- Mechanically interesting- Frankly mind-boggling player/Cryptmaster responsivity (thanks for recording all that, Lee!)- Deceptively robust lore and worldbuilding (I’d really love out-of-universe documentation)- Unabashedly silly, steeped in dad humor and awful puns, but also very smartly written-  is phenomenal- The soundtrack is consistently amazing- Region diversity, despite the monochrome!- Absurdly complex, old-school secret-hunting- Significant characters have extensive voiceover - Party characters are quirky and endearing (Joro’s “Joh-rohh” and Maz’s singing are highlights for me personally)- Controller support feels very functional for a game that utilizes typing so heavily!- Potion-brewing is interesting and could be situationally useful, but feels underutilized- Although the game suggests Realtime combat, I personally preferred turn-based- Very sporadic bugs (hangups when exiting dialogue screens; one literary secret didn’t trigger properly and locked me out of movement, requiring a restart)- Basic combat loop may feel repetitive to some players- Occasional navigation issues (particularly in the )I may have finished my first venture through the story, but I'm not nearly done with —I've still got secrets to find, lore to uncover, and an entirely new run of the story en español to complete!

Have fun sleeping after playing!

_childDocuments_.review: No game before it has had special interactions for typing words such as "fart", any swear word, or a card game you can just play at any time with the cool guy stuck in your head. One of the main mechanics involves the option to jork your penits in front of a goddess's avatar. It doesn't get better than this. I'm not finished with the game yet and may revise this review later, but safe to say I recommend it completely. An insane amount of style and substance put into a fun, unique package. The voice acting alone is worth the price of admission, I can't begin to imagine how long it took to record so many lines, so many words and interactions, and have them all sound THIS GOOD.Bonus points for the  Cryptmaster being cool and checking out my stream, love that guy.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond just being a good typing game, this game also has very good real-time/turn-based combat mechanics. The puzzle aspects are simple, yet brilliant.The humor in this game is fairly good too, and the fact that you can only communicate one word at a time is honestly brilliant.The experience system is downright genius. I won't say much since I'm already teetering on a line with spoilers.Highly, highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked the game!  I felt like there was a lot of character backstory and moves that I just didn't get close to unlocking by the end of play, so I ended up using a guide to figure out the rest.  I wish there was a more involved way to get letters so I can guess the characters' story more, but it feels like that would've made me OP in combat if I did it sooner.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Fun blend of word games, riddles, and other word puzzles with a traditional RPG form. Combat is a really fun puzzle in and of itself, figuring out good combos, remembering the words, typing them in sequence under pressure. Good sense of humor throughout the game. Definitely recomend if you ever enjoyed Wordle or word games in general.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Currently having a very good time with the game. The art and sound design is fantastic, the voice acting is great, the typing gimmick doesn't get old 'cause I like typing. The story's pretty engaging too. The puzzles are a little meh at times but are usually pretty fun and well-made. Expect a couple of little bugs but I haven't encountered anything game-breaking. Worth the price for a unique experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very impressive game for the amount of detail that was put into dialogue and puzzles. I went into the game expecting a typical dungeon crawler experience, but it plays much more like a casual adventure game. Whether or not someone will enjoy the game will depend heavily on whether or not you like the "Cryptmaster", who I found incredibly charming.---The combat started off interesting and began to build on itself naturally, which I was looking forward to how it would scale. Unfortunately, the combat did not develop fast enough and the game ended before I even unlocked a third of the skills. Even with all the skills, there is not enough of a challenge to utilize the depth of skill choices.Even with my criticisms of the combat and difficulty curve, the game was ultimately is driven by dialogue, puzzles and riddles.....so I can't complain that much.---The puzzles and riddles were overall very fun, and made for a good experience streaming the game for friends on Discord. The Wheel of Fortunesque guessing for the characters abilities was a highlight. There are a few moments that I feel are expected in all puzzle games, where the puzzle seems like it was not clear enough and left a sour taste. Overall, these moments were few and far between, which is all that can be expected.---I would recommend this game, because it is a unique experience that was well written and executed. I'm hoping that there is more of this in the future as either DLC, sequels or new games developing on the base system.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most interesting concepts for a game and its been pulled of here perfectly. It feels like a fun text adventure game but with parts like Typing of the Dead, lots of riddles/puzzles, and mad libs. Even more, a lot of times where there are answers to things that arent the expected answers but still work. Also a fantastically unique leveling system I cant talk about too much without spoiling what some of the levels are. Since its all about remembering words for your party members. Pick this game up.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Dude, love this game, it's not incredibly fast paced but you still definitely feel a sense of urgency when somebody is slapping the shiz out of you and you've mispelt "murder" like 6 times. definitely recommend. also, why does the cryptmaster not want to dance for me? give me a lil bit of the "Rattle Dazzle" as it were. hah, anyway, seriously, good game, defo worth picking up.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: A unique game that plays kind of like a crossword puzzle RPG.  You're trying to figure out the next skill for each of your characters and are given letters as rewards for winning combat and solving riddles.  The game starts pretty rough and doesn't hold your hand.  It took me a while to figure out the first move for my party but once I did the game flow made a lot more sense.  Big fan of this game even after finding out it wasn't ai but actually hand crafted respones.Also it has a card minigame.  Very good.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game wholeheartedly with a few caveatsThough the game is text based and has a few fun interactions it is nowhere near as deep as you may believe going into it through the tagline and other reviews, the game is comfortably finishable in about 5-6 hours, likely more if you go for the achievements, though there isn't much of a reason to do soIt is a very fun game with a lot of potential, though some of that is a little squandered through not utilising its tools to its full abilityGood puzzle game
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: What a blast! I played for 6 hours straight my first session. I need to go to bed and rest my lil brain to think of more neat words. Like "hit" or... "stanky"..."friend"....or "lonely".....wish my kids would call.....Anyways! I have never played a game like this - I can't imagine the amount of work that went into it.So good I bought it for a friend!
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game unlike any other I have played.  It is quite like an RPG - a dungeon crawl.  Yet the weapons to attack enemies, open chests, and interact with NPCs are words discovered throughout the game by finding letters and solving for the words like a crossword puzzle.  Words discovered grant you skills described by those words that you can use to fight enemies and get stronger.  The concept is very novel, the graphics are a stylized throwback to 1980s RPGs like Wizardry and Bard's Tale, the soundtrack music is reasonably moody, and the gameplay is addictive.  This is a really FUN game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredible and charming game where you are tasked to solve riddles and fight by typing your attacks to defeat your enemies.I'm vaguely familiar with the Knightmare show, and know it was a big inspiration. This game captures all the fun of it with a creepy atmosphere, a devilishly humorous narrator, and many tricky puzzles to solve.I was hooked instantly by the voice acting and the many words that the Cryptmaster will respond to...even the naughty words. Please Cryptmaster, may I play some more?
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most unique games i have ever played. It's like wordle mixed with a dungeon crawler, but calling it only that feels like a disservice to the game. The voice acting is great, combat is fun + satisfying when you start to combo stuff, and the sense of humor in the game is great as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: HEAVILY UNDERRATED!!! One of the most unique and fun games I've played in awhile!Don't let the pricepoint deter you from getting this game!*** EDIT!!! JUST BEAT THE GAME!!- So, it was a fun venture all around, BUT the soul/bug system is horrid imo.You won't notice it at first but as the game progresses it forces you to eat the same bugs/words over and over to collect souls to fight. It very easily becomes a chore and will quite often ruin your runs. Tying souls to the word combat shouldn't be a thing imo. Once you unlock every word it becomes pointless to even use the newer/better words because they cost too much soul and you should just stick to the simpler words to maximize soul usage. This could've been alleviated if you get extra souls as from bugs as you progress but that doesn't happen. Also having merchants deal in souls is another weird decision. You'll never have enough currency to buy merchant goods because you're either.1.) Saving it for combat2.) Don't have enough because you just got done fightingThis soul/bug system is the only thing that really bogged the game down. The enemies get stronger as the game goes on, but your character doesn't because you're constantly being tied down to soulbugs.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: About 8 hours in and I've never quite seen a game like this. The CryptMaster helps you out a bit in the beginning, but you'll find yourself getting the hang of it pretty quick.The black & white aesthetic adds a lot to the game. It's got a nice haunting vibe without being "scary" and I'm really digging the combat. I haven't tried the turn-based combat yet, but the real time is super neat.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the strangest games I've played in a while and i mean that in a good way. In terms of vibe it's a mix of dungeons and dragons, one of those typing games and animal crossing (that last one makes sense at the bonehouses)Overall if you're into INTERESTING experience i would definitely recommend. it's slow paced and puzzling. like...word puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly creative puzzle dungeon crawler that uses typing for interactions and combat. The humor is fantastic and the voice actor for the cryptmaster knocked it out of the park for the dorky DM doing an impression you would find at any dnd session. The music is very calming and easily some of my favorite ost for 2024 so far. The song between area 1 and 2 after getting past the tutorial is especially chill. The riddles and puzzles are genuinely challenging as well. Something I wish I got to do much more is the card game called "Whatever". It's essentially scrabble with a health bar. Each of your cards has a name and every turn you'll pull two new tiles to replace the ones you picked. The tiles you use do one point of damage for every letter they share with your cards name. When you've used every letter of a cards name at least once it has a special effect and a new card is drawn from your deck. First person to lose 40 health is defeated and gives you a unique card gwent style. Absolutely addicting feeling for card game fanatics.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: this is a very cool throwback style game where block by block movement and solving riddles is the appeal. it has moments where it's frustrating people you don't know the right thing to type, but walking away and trying something else while the back of your brain comes up with other options is a much better way to play that just looking up the answers. The challenge IS the fun (unless you can't make any more progress and you've slept on but you're truly stumped).
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Delightful ... that sorta game where you're like "how has no one thought of this before!?" and what a treat it is. A typing of the dead dungeon crawler with puzzles that will quickly humble you (if you're a dullard like me anyway). Funny, great art, great music. Get on this train now instead of waiting for some youtuber to brandish this a hidden gem in a year or two
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: A novel game that's primarily a hangman-style word game combined with dungeon crawler RPG. There's also a dash of riddles, puns, and in one case, a substitution cipher-- but most of those can get a LOT of optional help to skip them if you don't feel that it's worthwhile to the main game. If you play real-time mode, it's also a speed-typing game-- but this, too, is optionally reduced in difficulty if you pause frequently, or just play the turn-based mode instead.Unexpectedly, the game isn't really dependent on story and dialogue. You can ignore almost all lore except in the VERY few cases where progress depends on you mentioning something to NPCs, which seemed a little bit like an opportunity gone unused; I expected some of the many, many lore given to you to be more useful. But in the end, you'll be mostly saying random mundane nouns for guess-an-object game, or random dictionary words for the skill-unlock hangman puzzles.Ultimately the gameplay isn't particularly special if you take away the infusion of word games-- it's a fairly barebones dungeon crawler RPG with some collection elements, so your enjoyment hinges on whether or not you like word guessing games. I sure do.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: An insanely original dungeon crawler, i really can't understand how the developers could reach such a creative idea. Great humour, awesome artstyle, and all around a really good experience that is difficult to forget. I'm really loving it.The only thing i could think of if i had to criticize it, is that some riddles or words puzzles may be a tad more difficult to solve if you're not a native english (or spanish) speaker, but so far (chapter 2) i still haven't found a riddle that i wasn't capable of solving alone as a non-native english speaker.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: I've had a jolly good time with this one.It doesn't bombard you with dictionary words ala typing of the dead. Instead it tests your own vocabulary with riddles and guessing games to aquire letter clues to new abilities and lore to your 4 characters, as well as progression of the story.It also has a cheeky dark sense of humor and well voice acted by all the speaking characters I've encountered so far.I would like to see more of this type (😏) of game genre in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: I think I have a lot of game left to go but this game is incredible and I highly recommend it. Art style - awesome Sound track - amazing Voice work - great Puzzles - fun, and sometimes pretty challenging If you like wordplay, writing and adventuring, this game is for you. In Cryptmaster you'll dungeon crawl and interact with the world through typing. Your feats in the world such as guessing puzzles and defeating enemies will earn you letters you can use to unlock your characters' past memories and new powers. Along the way you'll encounter other challenges for your brain such as chests which give you a certain number of hints to discern the name of the item within or talking skulls which will challenge you with riddles and reward successful answers with souls. It's got a fun, addicting gameplay loop that keeps you playing, great atmosphere, and even a fishing mini-game! Standout indie game for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly unique, fun, hilarious Typing Dungeon Crawler with a great assortment of riddles! The voice acting is way better than the VA in most games! Awesome soundtrack! Great visual style!Hot recommend if you like riddles! Fun to try and solve them with friends!Oh yeah P.S. IT HAS AN ADDICTING CARD GAME!
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a ton of fun with having to write out what you want to do. There's a good amount of unexpected dialogue from my experiences, it definitely rewards you for information hunting. Would also recommend playing on reallywide fov because it makes the camera shaking and blurring more manageable along with seeing bugs, etc on the walls more clearly.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly fun and creative game. The responsiveness and depth is really impressive. The writing and dialogue is one of the most important aspects of the game, and thankfully it does really well in that regard. It can be very funny, and the unexpected reactions to your inputs sometimes make for a pleasant surprise.The combat isn't incredibly deep, and the waiting can get a bit annoying, but it is fun to try out the synergies and also have your typing speed have a direct impact on your combat effectiveness. I think there are a few negatives; I think the environment and lack of a full map can make it a bit easy to get lost at times, there are a few bugs here and there that cause minor annoyances, but I'd expect those to be ironed out in time. Finally, and perhaps most importantly, there's a pretty fun card minigame.Overall, it was a great experience and the game executes very well on its core concepts.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Played the demo, bought the game, I regret nothing.Edit:  Still amazing.  In my 40 yrs of gaming, I have never played anything quite like this.  I have one negative thing to say; this game seems to ask a lot of the player's capability for memorization.  If there were some way to access past text or already known info, I would be so grateful.  Tooltips are a great option and I praise whoever first invented the concept, honestly.  To those who will inevitably bring this up; even if part of the challenge is a test of memory, the game has so many other enjoyable qualities that I think even people with poor memory but fast typing skills and a love of logic should also be able to excel in real time combat.  :)As it stands, I need to keep notes, but there is no way to have them all available to view when needed.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Personally enjoying the game, and the riddles accompanied throughout the game give nostalgia from older dungeon crawler games. I am playing with the keyboard input with hints disabled at the moment - and haven't tried voice or controller as an input yet. The writing is so witty, and the music is charming - and the voice acting is superb!I think the only addition I would suggest is to provide a small log of previously used words during the riddle sequence when coming upon treasure chests or talking to skulls - that way you can see what words didn't work. It could appear on the side and set as a toggle if a player wants to see what was used before on each click. That's just my own personal skill issue, since short-term memory retention is not my best asset.Overall though, I love this game and would recommend it to anyone who's looking for a fun little dungeon crawler!
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like rouge-lites? Do you like puzzles? Do you like furiously typing to fight/figure out how your characters gets more moves? If you said yes to all or any of these, I'd give Cryptmaster a chance. This game has pretty great voice acting, a familiar game play loop, and some frustrating bits all while simultaneously giving you something brand new! I played the demo and was immediately hooked. So give it a try and see if you like it, because it's right up my alley. 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: So far, my personal GOTY.This game has so much character, and has such an ingenious gameplay loop. Bought this and "another game" that came out on the same day. This game is so much better, and more refreshing, than the "other game", for some reason the other game has been getting all of the attention, which is unfortunate. I've never played an old school dungeon crawler in depth, but this game is making me want to go back and check some out. This game absolutely NEEEEEDS a sequel, and I want the same developers on it, don't bother adding or subtracting anything from the development of this, hopefully, series. The vision is on point, and none of the formula should change.Bravo to the developers, a fantastic job. Thank you for this experience!

_childDocuments_.review: I like that if you ask the Cryptmaster about a certain other crypt themed undead, he'll state he cannot comment for copyright reasons.The mild comedy that doesn't break the drab, dark vibe of the environments is great.  What's the point of being raised from the dead and sent on an adventure if you can't get a few laughs out?The gameplay mechanic of typing out a single word and how everything gets responded to is amazing.  Can't wait to see what's next in this.  You can do combat realtime or turn-based to your preference.
_childDocuments_.name: Cryptmaster

_childDocuments_.review: This game was so unique! It hurts my brain thinking of how much work was put into the vast number of possible responses. I found a lot of them, but there are still quite a few puzzles that I haven't been able to figure out.There's also a card game included called Whatever. It's really addictive for something that was kinda just included as a joke! Hopefully there are some updates giving more opponents.All in all, HIGHLY recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: 4/5 A very weird dungeon type-em-up puzzler.If you like puzzles and riddles check this game out. The whole feel of the game is very good mix of goofy and creepy. You are four undead heroes bumbling around trying to remember anything you can while trying to reach the surface. I love games where as I am learning and solving things I can find clues to puzzles I haven't found yet and I am very excited to see how deep it goes! It also has a trading card mini game From what I understand this game was made by a small group and there is and impressive amount writing and dialogue as well as great voice acting and music. You guys did an awesome job! my only feedback is 1 the floor spike traps are crazy loud even with all the sound sliders at 10%-30% and also it would be nice to have an accessibility option to select abilities from the list during combat.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic work breaking the mold and creating a super fun, novel new game experience. Love the art style uniqueness and simplicity. The diversity of mini-games. Variability of what to do. The killer music soundtrack, alternately laid back/chill, electric guitar wailing during combat, and mood music in between -- just perfect for this type of game. Without that music, it would feel a lot more empty. Great work!Suggestion for creators: Allow option to turn on subtitles for riddles/chests, but off for 'walking-about' cryptmaster speech.  It's more enjoyable to not know how he might respond before hearing it, so I'd prefer to turn off subtitles, but then I find I forget or miss key info I need to solve puzzles, and sometimes there's no way to repeat it without failing entirely.
