_childDocuments_.review: I honestly don't understand how this game has an overwhelmingly positive review on steam. If souls games are your thing, that's one thing. But this game is an absolute buggy mess. The Mantis Shrimp battle is actually laughable. One time, i was punched up out of the ocean and into the sky. Another, (this happened MULTIPLE times) I was booted into the bushes which are supposed to be inaccessible. After all of this, and having this character literally spit on your dead body over and over again, when you finally defeat him, you aren't allowed to kill him. He's supposed to be available to "teach" you things. This game is a 5/10 at best. And that's if you ignore the bugs and graphics that look like they're from a 2000's game. But hey, the dialogue is cool.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really write reviews for games but this game unfortunately has had some really frustrating elements to me that eventually became game breaking.Issues I Encountered:- Enemy hit boxes can be so large that they encompass an entire platform that you would be required to stand on to be able to fight in melee range, but the enemies actual body size only takes up about 75% of the platform. This will force you to slide over and off platforms and fall to wherever you fall.- Targeting for your grapple seems to always prioritize targeting shells over targeting enemies. This can leave you exposed and vulnerable when trying to force the auto aim to shift off of a shell and onto an enemy. This really sucks when it's a boss as a lot of bosses have fast motion gap closers.- Looting your corpse can glitch and reset all your dropped currency to zero. Normally your corpse will contain all your currency you were carrying at time of death and is only lost if you die again before looting. Unfortunately there is a glitch where the currency on the corpse just resets to zero.- You can be stun locked to death. When enemies attack you there is an animation for being knocked back and another animation for you recovering from the hit. During these both of these you are animation locked, which means if anything else hits you the animations restart. You cannot block, dodge, move, cast spells, or attack during this. So you can just get animation locked to your death.- You can be knocked through walls that are not designed for traversing which leaves you permanently stuck in place. In addition, if there's no coded surface area for standing then you will be stuck in a falling animation which prevents any kind of attacking. So if an enemy can get to you, like a ranged enemy, you're a fish in a barrel.Some of these felt tolerable at first as they were not frequently encountered but after getting further into the game, I'm now in a zone where I seem to encounter a new glitch every 4 or 5 minutes.I would not recommend this game in its current state till some of these issues are fixed. Without these issues, it's a cute and fun game overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Another Crab's Treasure

_childDocuments_.review: Damn this is a good one.I started it for the action adventure combat, but the game's writing after the treasure map is done was genuinely compelling, and did strike an emotional chord. No wasted space there, every character and line of dialogue is important to the script. Game does a wonderful job of allegory. Yes, the devs construct an intentionally similar mirror to RL junk, but they trust the player to look through it as much as they choose to. I certainly did not expect such a powerful "where is your rage" moment, that's for sure. My tip for maximizing your fun is to avoid some of those Souls habits of being overly-fastidious and cleaning every corner.  Don't worry about it. You will have plenty of upgrade crystals to max your skill tree, which is all you really need anyways. If a miniboss if giving you a hard time, slap on those revive trinkets and don't waste your own time.

_childDocuments_.review: Baby's first soulslike. Don't get me wrong, it's good, but it's only as hard as you make it.As a souls veteran, the early parts of the game were the hardest. Everything after spearfishing and the mantis punch was trivial. I realize I could've not used them, but to set arbitrary challenges like that for oneself on the first playthrough isn't really experiencing the game as intended. I was disappointed that none of the assist features could make the game harder. I was similarly disappointed to find there was no NG+.All of that said, it's a pretty, well-made platformer. It's like if Battle for Bikini Bottom was trying to be Dark Souls (and mostly succeeding). The writing is okay, the little jokes are fun, and the voice acting is neat. Check it out to support the studio if nothing else, but you should be able to squeeze two dozen hours of fun or so out of this game.Give this to your kids if you want them to grow up to be good at video games

The establishment, with its rustic charm and inviting ambiance, promised an authentic experience of coastal cuisine. Little did I know that this visit would inspire me to write a review that encapsulated not only the meal but also the essence of community support.The moment I stepped inside, the aroma of freshly prepared seafood enveloped me, awakening my senses. The menu featured an array of dishes highlighting crabs in various forms—steamed, fried, and even in rich bisques. After much deliberation, I settled on their signature crab cakes, which were touted as a local favorite. As I savored each bite, it became clear why this dish garnered such acclaim; the delicate balance of flavors was complemented by a tangy remoulade that elevated the entire experience.As I reflected on my meal while jotting down notes for my review, it became evident that writing about Another's Crabs Treasure transcended mere culinary critique. It was about celebrating local entrepreneurship and fostering connections within our community. My review aimed to highlight not just the quality of food but also the warmth exuded by staff who treated patrons like family. In sharing my experience online, I hoped to encourage others to explore this hidden gem and support small businesses like it—an endeavor essential for preserving our local culture. - the good ai

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best soulslikes I've ever played. This game clearly takes inspirations from it's predecessors but it really carves out it's own identity. The setting and art direction is amazing. It's both beautiful and hilarious from start to finish. Everthing from the environments, to the enemy and boss design, to the various shells you'll find to wear or the abilities you unlock. It's all inspired and you can tell the devs put love and soul into it. Music was really great too but I wished it was a bit louder than the ingame setting allowed. The story isn't really anything crazy but what's there is entertaining and gets you invested just enough.The platforming in this game is really fun. Krill is responsive and has a lot of movement options that chain together. It also gives the level design a lot of verticality and makes exploration enjoyable beyond just finding hidden secrets. The level design felt a bit linear in the beginning but it really comes into it's own later on. The combat is really similar in that sense. In the beginning you feel like there isn't much you can do and it feels a bit basic but as you start unlocking more of the skill tree (get parry ASAP), it quickly becomes fast paced and super satisfying.Anyway, highly recommend this to anyone that loves soulslikes, old-school 3d platforming games, the ocean, and SpongeBob.

_childDocuments_.review: I like Crab's Treasure, but I'm not sure if I *love* it.The Good: The game's writing is its strongest feature, it does not pull its punches on capitalism and its pollution. It's loaded with easter eggs and references to other games. The character designs are cute, everyone has a cartoony charm, which is contrasted by how dark the game's tone becomes in the later half. The main character "Kril" is a scruffy little dork trying his best and you want to see his mission through.The Combat is crunchy and satisfying, and a great introduction for someone who's never played a Souls game before. Crab's Treasure isn't terribly difficult, and dumps exp and upgrade materials into your lap. By the first half of the game you're very powerful and can build Kril however you like. Despite only having 4 stats to choose from (HP, Attack, Shell Defense, Special Attack), there are "builds" in Crab's Treasure. If you invest heavily in a certain stats, there are pieces of equipment that only work with high investment in that stat and will change the play-style of your Kril. I went with a traditional tank build, high Hp high attack and ignored the other 2 stats. The game rewards it. The "shark tooth" increases the strength of charge attacks but only works if you have 45 attack investment (very difficult to reach without deliberate focus on attack stat). Unique equipment like this adds replay value and variety.It's a game that clearly had a lot of passion put into it and it shows.Which is why it bums me out when I have to bring up The Bad:Crab's Treasure stage layouts are rather bland and same-y. Normally I wouldn't mind getting lost, but this ends up working against it in larger areas because everything looks the same and you end up running in circles. There aren't very many landmarks or distinguishing features to differentiate other parts of a stage and this can make navigating areas like the Sand Between annoying/a chore.The game balance is wonky. Crab's Treasure is mostly very easy, but it has strange spikes in difficulty especially in the last section of the game. I'm not a fan of "large hoards of strong dudes attacking on top of each other in cramped spaces" but the final area of the game is very guilty of this. I ended up skipping most of the stage and just running through it. It's just didn't feel very polished and needed more time in the oven.While the game's low difficulty is likely intentional. getting overpowered feels inevitable. You're given so many materials and exp, most fights become trivialized. I casually reached lvl 50 with no farming. I never really had to apply the Sekiro "shell deflect" technique all that much. Especially once I got the Valve shell which has an absurd amount of shell HP, I combined that with my already high HP to make myself effectively invincible and casually smashed everything. I never got stuck on a fight longer than 15mins (depending who you ask this is a good thing?).The Game's Narrative is clearly important to it, but also kills pacing. There are a lot of cut-scenes in Crab's Treasure. This can really break game-flow and makes me lose interest in repeat playthroughs.Despite everything said, I still recommend Crab's Treasure. It's a game experience worth having, whether you get it now or wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought it for the promise of crab sekiro, got a nice game that was far longer than I had expected with enough variety through shell swapping and stowaways to stand well enough on its own. One of the better games I've played within the souls like genre even if you can get shoved through walls by some enemies and angles on occasion.The story starts out simple enough but there's enough weight behind it and shifting subplots to make it interesting enough to follow, while not as cryptic as a lot of souls and souls-likes. Not the most complex by the end of it, either, but the setup is fantastic and the use of light and color throughout the game set it apart from the standard dim soulslike experience.10/10 would, and shall, crab again. I'll report back after having done a no shell run because the parrying bare-clawed is incredibly fun for the risk of it.

_childDocuments_.review: allow me to list just a couple of gripes I have with this game:• poor optimization - the game with cartoonish graphics runs worse than elden ring on my not very high-end laptop.• dodges - the main character runs frantically around the arena, however the dodges are like 0.5 inches forward. I get it it's because of the shell, but that should not be the case when I am not wearing one.• parries - imagine playing a rhythm game where every action comes out not when you press but when you release a key. that's how parries are designed in this game, and I'm sorry, I am not willing to play in this weird ska punk rhythm.• fighting multiple enemies - every early game area that's littered with lvl1 crabs and fish is a nightmare to go through. because once the enemy sees you, it's going to fight you no matter how many other guys you're fighting. I mean, in other souls games, if you position the enemies one behind the other, they will take turns fighting you, to make it more manageable.• left handed grip on the weapon - I am not opposed to it too much, I am just curious - why? having the weapon equipped in my right hand is just so baked into my perception of every game. well, most of the games have an ability to put one weapon into each hand. that would've worked ig.• corny soulsborne references - first time it's fun and silly, all the other times it's just annoying how not subtle and in the face it is.this would've been much better if it were a knock-off of a mario game, not a souls-like

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR It's a fun game with sometimes janky but mostly solid platforming, and combat that feels a bit too over tuned, but that's not an issue. It's cute and fun, with some good world building and gameplay that feels pretty good. The platforming will make up a solid chunk of your playtime, and it can be hit or miss. The issue comes down to readability with intended platforms blending in a bit too well with what is intended to be scenery. After a while you'll start to get an eye for it, but it can be a bit frustrating at first. Second, the combat is definitely over tuned. Everything in the game can one or two shot you. I get it, you're a squishy hermit crab and you should be blocking more often than not, but you'll get locked into attack animations fairly often and find yourself dead again and again. Once I turned the damage down in the assist settings it felt fine, and the combat was fun again. Personally, I feel that the low damage setting should be the default, and regular damage should be part of a challenge mode or something. But then again, it's not my game, and it's not my vision. Overall I'd definitely be happy to recommend this game to anyone who likes soulslikes with a lot of personality, and simplistic-but-hard-to-master combat. Oh and the music sometimes feels just a little off. Maybe that's just me, but it can be kinda distracting sometimes.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to enjoy this game, and I think for the most part I do, but there are a lot of things that make it hard to enjoy the game. My biggest frustration is that despite being able to run elden ring perfectly on my computer, Another Crab's Treasure constantly, and I mean constantly drops frames. It makes it hard to play the game in anything other than short bursts because everything takes twice as long to do and it gets frustrating. There is a bit of other jank that I have encountered already, like getting stuck on map geometry and dying, or getting thrown into a wall and stuck in the wall in midair during a bossfight and dying, or falling off the map but all my souls/microplastics were unrecoverable because they were below the death plane somehow. I love the character design, I like the story and I think the world is fun to explore but damn do I really wish the game didnt freeze from dropping frames every time I rotate the camera.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game and can't wait to start my second playthrough. Overall, it was a pretty positive experience. Environment/Boss Arenas: Some boss arenas were definitely interesting, they each have little issues but the mini bosses could use some help. Bosses would occasionally get stuck and become unreachable, and sometimes I’d get stuck on objects scattered around the arena that didn’t seem to serve much purpose. Another issue was how the camera behaved, frequently blocking my view completely.2. Enemies: I had two issues here. One was with enemies appearing during boss fights. For example, when fighting Pagurus, (I wasn’t using a shell and was close to level 1 for more difficulty) but I would almost never die to the boss itself, as the environment or the enemies would be what killed me. A few other fights had this same issue. As for regular enemies in the wild, I found it difficult to fight just one because of how they are grouped. _childDocuments_.review: This game surprised me, in a good way. I thought it will just be a good souls-like, but turns out its very clearly that the developers put in a lot of thoughts and details into this. The gameplay is amazing, the combat is smooth and crisp, I like that the attacks actually feels like they have weight behind them. I think the bosses and enemies are fair as well in terms of difficulty. The level design is solid, though I would prefer a little bit more environmental puzzle, but thats just my personal taste. I think two aspect that really stand out is the story and art direction. The story is surprisingly profound, I was expecting a souls-like story about despair and hopelessness, but I got a story about determination and finding hope. The characters also have good character development as well, especially the MC Kril. As for art direction, the beauty of the different maps and world is unparalleled. I has a mix of colorfulness, from the colorful trashes left in the bottom of the ocean, and a hint of sadness, which also comes from the plastic trashes left in the ocean. I like how the game turns these trashes left behind by humans into the worlds architecture, into our weapons, shells and what the enemies wear. The way they integrate into the world and the gameplay is really creative and impressive. The humor (sometimes dark humor) is just the icing on this delicious cake. Overall I can highly recommend this game, the gameplay is amazing and the story is deeper than I initially thought. In the end I was really invested in the story and quite attached to some of the characters as well.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a joy to play from start to finish. This concept of a Souls-like game taking place in the ocean, the real, polluted ocean, is one that demanded a crazy level of attention to detail. From the extremely spot-on dark humor littering every aspect of the game, to the tasteful references to other games, it's an unforgettable time to roll around this vast expanse. Funny and depressing at the same time, it probably does a better job at raising awareness to the damage our human trash causes to the planet without causing damage to itself in the process by mere lecturing.I couldn't think of any missed opportunities in the concepts being thrown at you in terms of character designs or story beats. The game covers all that one could ask for it. It's a perfectly good package for its price and I can't stress enough that I did not expect it to go that far without getting crushed under its ambition. The whole team has done an incredible job on whichever individual part you focus on, music, gameplay, graphics, dialogue... and becomes more than the sum of its parts when carried by the story.As a veteran of every game in the Souls franchise and also having played a lot of Aggro Crab's first game Going Under, I'll also add that if you care to use the tools at your disposal, ACT is surprisingly easy. Much easier than Dark Souls, Elden Ring or Going Under. I beat a lot of the bosses on my first or second try without even going for 100%. It also adds an impressively good platforming element to the mix, which I did not expect to be so enjoyable in the Souls-like formula. I can't test this idea, but I have a feeling this could make for a great introduction to the Souls-like subgenre if you're new to it.My only criticism would be, as of writing this, there is no way to discard a hammer until it breaks, one boss is a bit frustrating (let's just say it kind of "short-circuits" the fun) and some levels are slightly too long for my taste.I loved this game and I will gladly bother my friends about it. I look forward to anything new Aggro Crab has planned to make.

The number of times I've died to the bosses solely because I tried to swap shells is astounding.Shell-swapping is the core mechanic of the game, and it is implemented poorly.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR --> Don't let the eye-candy, cartoonish look deceive you; this is a very solid souls-like, with a mix of different ideas that blended greatly with a good balance between humour and a serious tone. Combat was very cool and I ended up using all resources the game gave me. Currently my indie of the year 🦀-------------------------------(POTENTIAL MINOR SPOILERS ABOUT GAME'S MECHANICS) I'm another one of those annoying souls fan who can't stop talking about them and I'm up to play any souls-like you throw at me, so obviously this game caught my attention. And still, I did not expect it to be this good and this fun to play.Another Crab's Treasure (Crab Souls), despite its cartoonish look, is a souls-like by all rights: roll to dodge, posture bar, methodic combat, big bosses, bonfires' system, and so on. At the same time, it has a mix of things we've seen on other titles and genres that works surprisingly well: a skill tree, upgrade system similar to hollow knight, grappling hook which together with the posture system resembled Sekiro, etc. Even some Breath of the Wilds elements are present. All blended in a 3D platformer environment featuring many sorts of obstacles aside from enemies.Storymode was surprisingly engaging to me too. I expected something just functional to have an excuse for the game going but I ended up pretty invested into it. Just another welcomed surprise. Combat is very entertaining, and original as well. While only having one weapon, your build will strongly depend on shells you equip, and none of them are permament. They all have different resistance levels, weight and skills attached to them, and some enemy patterns WILL force you to block (and therefore lose shell HP) instead of constantly rolling like in traditional souls. There's plenty of shells on the floor wherever you go so you will see yourself constantly switching shells and adapting to their nature, and I found that very very cool. Further into the game you will have more combat options and I ended up using all of them. It honestly surprises me how well all these combat mechanics from different games mixed so well here, so much testing have been done here probably.The game is far from perfect, though. Being a 3D platformer (a genre that is a bit janky already by itself), I found many situations with silly deaths and falls that I felt more a buggy issue rather than my own mistake; some enemy placements are weird too, in platforming areas that feel a bit too troll;  some areas felt unnecessarily long and tedious, with the same platforming concept aaaall the way through. And then some other minor bugs that will likely be patched in the following weeks. Lastly, the game has many difficulty-related accessibility options, in case the experience is too heavy for you.Overall, I couldn't stop playing the game until the end. I have so many positive things to say about the game and very few negative as you can see. As of now this is my current indie of the year, you can tell they've put a lot of (dark) soul and passion into it and they made it right. I truly hope they succeed with this game because it deserves it

_childDocuments_.review: I'd give it an 8/10 after completion, definitely worth the price and a playthroughGOOD:I'd easily recommend this as a starter soulslike to anyone new to the genre, it's digestible and very accessible, I'd even recommend it for someone not good at games. The story is surprisingly good, with fleshed out characters, a strong anti capitalist and conservation of nature theme, and an impactful emotional arc for the main character. I say this as someone who usually is bored with game stories: this one was really engaging to me. The world is endlessly creative and funny. There's tons of references, puns, hidden little jokes, and so much detail in the worldbuilding, I was thoroughly impressed.The combat and build systems are fluid and have good variety, you can be a heavy attack parry god or a ranged magic user, it all works as well as a mainline souls and has its own unique flavors.Good music and voice acting.NEUTRAL:It's a little on the shorter side, which is fine the quality is good throughout but it's worth mentioning.It's definitely the easiest soulslike I've ever played even without using accessibility options, not a bad thing though.BAD:There are a LOT of bugs. I had several gamebreaking bugs or softlocks and I was not doing it on purpose. Luckily there's an option to die in the menu. Although it sucks it didn't sour my experience that much, however.Enemy variety is a little lacking, you'll see about 2-3 unique enemies per area but there aren't many areas, and they'll frequently reuse enemy types. The repetition got a bit stale for me near the end of the game.The map is unfortunately REALLY bad. You can't move it at all, and I would also love the ability to set stamps on the map so I could keep track of important locations to come back to, as the game requires a lot of backtracking if you want to 100% it.

Really the same length as their health bar?!?! For smaller regular enemies is fine but for a boss that's way to much?!?! I have played other souls like games but I'd say this is my least favorite in my list, again still great game but there needs to be a big balance change to combat both for the player and enemies specifically. I know souls games are supposed to be hard but they need to be fair, and this feels unfair. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly I picked up this game purely because the videos they made on YouTube treated it as a joke of an experience that I expected to refund almost immediately. What I wasn't expecting was for this to be the first souls-like to retain my attention and adoration for long enough to not only complete the game but get every achievement. It's got the difficult challenges that your average souls-like such as Elden Ring or Dark Souls might have, with a simple yet satisfying combat flow. Mastery of the mechanics doesn't feel like some immense task or mundane chore but comes naturally and easily. It doesn't punish players for not being the best version of themselves and better yet, it allows you to customise your experience, slowing time, increasing dodge and parry windows, decreasing the damage of enemies and even preventing the loss of your currency upon death. By far the funniest part of the game is the gun, an assist mode item that instantaneously eliminates every enemy in one hit which allowed me to skip a segment of the game I haven't liked since I first picked up a controller. If it weren't for the gun, I still would have persevered despite not being one for souls-likes because this game has a charm like no other, vibrant colours that are pleasing to the eyes and soft on them and lovable characters voiced by some talented people. If you take one look at their YouTube, it's clear to see a lot of love was put into this game and it definitely shows from the jokes on popular products such as "Duracell" and "I can't believe it's not butter" to flavourful curse words that fit the game world beautifully.Overall, would I recommend the game? Yeah. It's vibrant, funny, challenging and lovingly crafted. This game just oozes with its creators' love and you'll see if you play it.

_childDocuments_.review: The TLDR is that ACT is basically Dark Souls but in a Spongebob/Little Mermaid package. It's a game about a cartoon crab trying to get his shell back from a greedy banker-type character who repossesses it. The gameplay is just like Dark Souls but with a bit more emphasis on 3D platforming. The combat is very much dodge/roll/parry just like Dark Souls, but you can get a lot of upgrades for yourself, your stats, with tons of perks to keep it fresh and interesting. The difficulty curve is higher than expected, but there's still options to tone it down so kids shouldn't have a problem here. It isn't like DS where the difficulty can be masochistic; Another Crab's Treasure is more approachable if you want it to be. There are also ample opportunities to grind for currency so you can upgrade your character. Simply go into a shop, upgrade, come back out, and the enemies you just killed will have respawned. Kill them again to get more currency, lather/rinse/repeat until you have enough currency to upgrade again. Some might consider this bad design, but it didn't bother me too much. I wasn't that reliant on it as a tactic, but it's there if you want to play the game like that. The game never forces you into that strategy, so it's on you if that's how you play. Overall I had a good time with the game but there are a few problems. Firstly, the game is obviously made on a low budget. Many scenes play out eerily quiet, where you'd expect there to be music or sound effects there simply aren't any. There are also some instances of getting caught in the world geometry, forcing you to restart the game. There's the occasional camera hiccup too, where it gets caught in a wall or something and doesn't show you what you want to be looking at. But these problems are not that common overall. What is a common problem is the terrible, God-awful dialog. It is the worst example of millennial writing I've seen in a long time. Every single line has to have some sort of quippy pun to it. EVERY. SINGLE. DAMN. LINE. It's endearing at first but after the first couple hours it's just annoying. Making matters worse was the heavy handed way it just shoves the themes into your face. Yes yes, capitalism is bad, the rich are subhuman and need to die, got it. You're not special or original for thinking that. But it never, EVER shuts up about it. Muh eeeeevil capitalism is a tired trope at this point, so to have it featured so prominently, and in such a pun-filled way just gets on your nerves by the end. At least they let you skip cut scenes and you can mash A to get through the dialog pretty easily. And at the very least they didn't follow the millennial trope of "nihilism is cool and edgy" because if they did it would truly be insufferable. Overall I think it's a nice change of pace for the genre. Not all Souls-likes have to be drab rust colored games in a dark fantasy setting. You can have bright colorful cartoon worlds too. It feels like a N64/PS1 era platformer but modernized with Souls like mechanics. I really like and respect it for that. I'd give it 7.5/10, and if they could tone down the cringe dialog and fix a few bugs it could easily be a 9. I think a sequel that polishes things up, with a bigger budget for graphics, animation, and play testing could make this into a really nice franchise.
_childDocuments_.name: Another Crab's Treasure

_childDocuments_.review: Everyone's already mentioned what's good about this game; the humour, the simple mechanics, the freedom in exploration, a challenging but doable Souls-type game, the soundtrack, the characters and story, the Easter Eggs, you can read the other reviews for the positives But man, this game has plenty of bugs, and isn't very well optimised. In no particular ranking or severity, Sometimes the bounces are meant to make you go a certain direction, but it doesn't guarantee where you're gonna end up, and your input will skew this as well. Be prepared to fall into the abyss unintentionally many many many times.  You can focus on enemies during fights, but certain interactions can make this quite the headache, especially with enemies who move around a lot or have the ability to "disappear", or when there's more than 1 enemy. At one point you can unlock a power move on downed or "capsized" enemies, but if you've multiple enemies around, your head's gonna spin trying to figure out what happened and where the camera decided to focus on.  Sometimes you get stuck in a certain place because you were walking along and then suddenly you slid into a gap and now you can't get out. There's no clear distinction between which terrain is real terrain or just slide-to-the-abyss terrain. I liked the exploring and freedom, but my interest slowly dwindled when I realised I would climb something real high and then slide off the entire thing without realising whether it was an actual exploration point.  Melee attacks go thru the wall, and enemies can just fall off the map for no reason. Might be a good thing, but I doubt that is meant to be the experience. At one point, some mechanic screwed itself up, and I could double jump, but the 2nd jump was a random jump in a random direction. And climbing the fishing nets, sometimes Krill would grab the net and then immediately jump off, especially when climbing the rounded nets, or worse, just not grab the net at all.  I know Souls-type games are meant to be difficult and players are supposed to discover things for themselves and just deal with it sometimes, but that can't be the excuse for everything. Pause/equipment menu; Gotta manually cycle thru your stowaway pages by going to the end of each page, and 0 info about your fork and how many Stainless Relics you're holding. Selling/buying things; Either sell one at a time, or all of it, and after you sell something, it always brings you back to the top of the page. MSG usage; HUD doesn't show how much MSG your shell spell / adaptation will consume, gotta memorise all of them. Item pickup; I've picked up this item 20 times, I don't need another pop-up describing what this item is. Map; Might as well not have a map. It can't move, it doesn't show you explored landmarks, you can't see the other areas you're not in. Many small things like these slowly build up enough to irritate and frustrate.   I've been reading the reviews for this game, and was honestly surprised how little comment there was about the unpolished state of the game. It's still a decent game, but I'm giving it the thumbs down for now.Would've given it a 8.5/10, but if the above are intended game mechanics in view of the "nature" of a Souls-type game, 6/10Or disagree with me cos I've never played a Souls-type game. It's the internet, do what you want.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent Souls-Like!A little poorly marketed by game journalists, this is not a "light-hearted" game. I'd call it more of a super-satire, kind of like Helldivers. You are hit over the head over and over with human trash hurting the ocean. And yeah, ♥♥♥♥ is sad, it ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ SUCKS. And much like any proper Souls inspired game, the game is unambiguously bleak at times.But these are themes very much worth making art of and ACT is an excellent representative of the niche of this art form!I will say, it's a great argument for the Dark Souls version of difficulty scaling! When I got frustrated I gave some of those "accessibility options" a try, and other than the gun just being really amusing, I don't think any of them were especially helpful? It could just be the fact that I've played so dang many of these games, but I genuinely got better scaling down of the difficulty for my playstyle by switching to a different archetype. I started using a Resilience build and the difficulty dropped by half without making any animations jank or dropping the framerate to a hard 20. So your sorceries in Dark Souls/bleed in Elden Ring etc. easy mode rather than just cutting hp by a certain percent.That all is really just the nitty gritty, though. I really liked the game! And I think if you like any Soulsish game, Subnautica, Terra Nil, or anything of the like, you should give it a try!

_childDocuments_.review: This is an awesome and fun game! While it features combat inspired by FromSoftware titles, it's not punishingly difficult. Not every game in this genre needs to be brutally challenging.The only downside I found was the platforming. It can feel clunky at times, especially when climbing to the top of certain surfaces. Additionally, the double jump mechanic seems inconsistent, not always triggering if you don't jump off certain platforms.However, the game excels in many areas. The humor and references to its inspirations are clear indicators of the love poured into its development. The diverse levels are packed with secrets to discover, and cleverly designed shortcuts connecting you back to earlier areas. The combat system, while simple, is very good. The classic dodge roll and parry mechanics combine to create thrilling encounters that rival fights from FromSoftware titles.Overall, I highly recommend this game to both experienced and newcomers to the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and addictive game! I'm about halfway through and I've loved it so far. The game is heavily inspired from the "Souls" genre which is most obvious in combat. There is a lot of dark humor regarding the ongoing oceanic crisis, pollution and economics which I thoroughly enjoy (especially the puns and satire within "New Carcinia")Major positive points in my opinion include:Very accessible difficulty (you can customize the difficulty to your liking but the default is "Hard" which is what I've played)No game breaking bugs I've experienced so farFresh and interesting mix of 3rd person Souls like combat and platformingRewarding learning curve based around combatDying against a boss resets you and your XP right before the boss (compared to the Souls genre, where you would have to travel from a reset point and pick up your lost experience during combat) This is a very nice change in my opinionNegatives:Obviously not multiplayer or PvP (although I don't miss the janky ganky Souls-esque PVP) but not being able to summon my heartkelp munching minion of a friend is a bummerNot all dialog has voicelines which makes it difficult for people with dyslexia (my spouse) to understand the story but for now I just read all the unvoiced dialog out loud so she doesn't have to miss out on the humor and informationSo far 10/10 game but will update if anything changes!

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game to anyone interested. The humor is just right for me, and I found myself laughing at quite a bit of dialogue. The parry system with the shells is also extremely satisfying, and the story is really neat and pretty decent.BUT, there are a few cons. While I love the combat in this game, quite often the combat was over shadowed by wacky bugs, poorly designed environments, and terrible enemy placement. These are minor issues compared to my big 3 gripes with this game.1. Some bosses were simply awful (specifically near the end for whatever reason)2. This game has a ton of parkour, yet I feel like my character wasn't made to do the designed jumps at all. Like some of the parkour in this game was simply infuriating for a game where it should feel satisfying. (This is also probably mainly due to level design)3. And my biggest gripe. THE PROJECTILES. Like ALMOST EVERY projectile has a homing effect, and half of the projectiles explode in a big AOE. Put those projectiles into poor level design and some simply awful boss fights, and I quickly went from enjoying the came to really wanting it to just be over.This game has really high high points, and really low low points. I recommend it, but just be aware of what you are getting into.

_childDocuments_.review: Crab-based Dark Souls simulator.If you're the type of person that has been interested in a "Souls-like", but only understand them to have unforgiving masochistic difficulty, this is a great introduction to the genre without having to die repeatedly on a particular boss fight for hours on end. There are plenty of accessibility features to customize your experience and adjust the challenge to your liking. Left to defaults, If you're a seasoned veteran, you will be humbled throughout many of the battles ahead in a great way.The plot and characters are charming; while the game is on the shorter side, I was pleasantly surprised how far and deep it goes. Plenty to explore, lots of combat variety, and meaningful progression at every step. Worth the price of admission!

_childDocuments_.review: Another Crab's Treasure has quickly risen to be one of my favorite souls-like games. The environments are incredibly detailed and effectively make me feel terrible about pollution. The dark comedy is on point and I frequently stopped to send pictures to my friends. The main character customization, shell selection, is very interesting in that it ties different character builds to the shells you find around the levels rather than traditional armor. The game utilizes a combination of other game systems (stat growth, upgrade trees, "trinket" slots with different effects) that make for a lot of good customization. The controls are well tuned and platforming is very fun. The game also respects my time, eliminating unnecessary friction that is common in the souls-like genre. Most bosses will respawn you right at the arena entrance to allow for quick retries. There is a very clever system of "insuring" your shells so you respawn with specific ones to prevent you from backtracking after a death. Overall, I picked this up because of the silly premise and have been incredibly pleased to find how much more it has to offer than that initial hook. I legitimately have not been able to put it down and I am wrapping this up so I can hop back in to my run.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games in this genre I've ever played. In fact, I'd say this is far and above the most competent Soulslike ever made thus far outside of Fromsoft. Absolutely no ill will to any of those games, but Another Crab's Treasure is on another level, and It's an incredibly refreshing experience.I don't have much if anything to really complain about. I was a little put off by the parrying and other minor things at first, but once I learned to stop playing it like a Fromsoft game, everything started becoming very clear and intuitive. This game wears its inspiration on its sleeve, I've noticed dozens of direct influences from every mainline Fromsoft title (Dark Souls, Elden Ring, Sekiro, Bloodborne) In so many different places throughout the game, and It's so charming and made me smile whenever I realized. It really feels like a love letter to Fromsoft, while keeping its own identity.Highly recommend, much love to the dev team for this incredible experience. Can't wait to see what they do next.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, I was skeptical at first. I had never played any Dark Souls games and honestly suck at most soulslikes in general. However, the addition of assist options and the pretty forgiving respawn mechanics made it not only possible to play, but fun. No doubt helped by the most important part of any soulslike- the bosses. Between the incredible voice talent, the amazing artistic design, and the extensive audio and haptics work, everything about each of the bosses perfectly captures their scale, speed, and power. Not to mention the characters, every character really feels fleshed out, with their own aspirations and motivations for doing everything they do. Nothing ever feels like plot device, it all seems like natural reactions the characters would have. One thing that caught me off guard, however, was how scary the game would be. Don't let its lighthearted demeanor fool you, there's some genuinely terrifying things in this game. Plenty of people probably saw some of the brutal deaths you can get online, but it gets so much worse the further you go. Finally, the games message is really well done. It would have been easy to just shove the whole "protect the earth" message down your throat at every turn, and it is present, but the game always comes first. There's very few points where the game directly talks about it's message, and even when it does it's not the plain "just stop polluting" platitudes, it recognizes that it's not something you can just fix and it delves into the whole progress vs sustainability argument without guilt-tripping or acting like it's not a hard decision for humanity to make.All in all: solid experience, and definitely a good soulslike for newcomers and long time fans alike.

_childDocuments_.review: ***SPOILER ALERT!***Okay, so after pretty much finishing the game (I don't want to waste time on the final boss, because holy hell is the ending not worth it) I can conclude that I wouldn't recommend this game to pretty much anyone.The gameplay controls like a platformer, and the combat feels painfully slow. A good portion of it seems to just be hiding in your shell every time the enemy makes a flurry of attacks- parrying is so inconsistent it isn't worth it. The story starts off sort of strong. You get your shell stolen, realize the whole ocean is getting polluted, and go through a journey slowly making friends (If you could call it that) and pretty much spend the entire game trying to get your shell back. Only towards the very end does your character even give a damn about saving the ocean. . .which, doesn't end up getting saved in the end, because who the hell cares about rewarding your journey?The characters you meet are charming...unfortunately there's literally no character development to be seen anywhere (If you don't count the overly stupid twist final boss) INCLUDING YOUR CHARACTER! No matter how much the game tries to make you think he's changed, his mindset is pretty much the exact same from start to finish. The MOMENT he gets his shell back, it's just "Hur-dur, screw the ocean." Hey, remember the "shark" that stole your shell? Yeah, after area one, he ((SPOILERS)) sells it to some dude and never comes back. Then for the rest of the game, the shell just. . .stays in the hands of that dude. Nothing more interesting comes out of it. I expected funny circumstances to come up and constantly keep you from your shell, not for it to stay in purgatory for the remainder of the game. Speaking of, the game really, really needed to be longer. You're pretty much just slapped with the final few areas out of nowhere. The treasure hunt that becomes relevant to the plot? IT'S PRETTY MUCH THE ENTIRE GAME! After it's finished, you're placed in the final few areas. Yes, the game expects you to explore. But when there's enemies that aren't fun to fight scattered everywhere (I should also mention their AI isn't intelligent enough to stop you from running past them and just grabbing what they've been positioned to "protect") traversing areas just isn't fun. I might have enjoyed the first half of the game, but the second half was just me trying to avoid every enemy because I had the main currency of the game out the wazoo, and get to the next boss.The shell mechanic is also painfully misused. Every shell has a special ability. Unfortunately shell abilities aren't unique, and many are out of nowhere, having nothing to do with what the shell actually is. A tin can has a motion detecting-homing missile special ability- why? Cause magic! There's so many shells you'll never use because their abilities are just so worthless compared to other shells. Some shells have high defense but make you slower, some break faster (not that it matters, shells are everywhere and there's abilities you can get later on to make the shell-breaking mechanic worthless) but apart from that, you'll just be using one or two shells the entire game because there's no reason to use anything else.Most of the bosses were just frustrating, not fun. Poorly telegraphed attacks, attacks that literally are useless to parry because they're spammed on on top of the other, and attacks that could very well OHKO you. Most of the positive reviews seem to literally just be positive because there's a cute little crab in it and the story is "darker than expected."------What absolutely pains me is that this COULD have been a great game. It has good concepts for characters (At least the ones that have a personality, unlike most of the NPCS) good voice acting, a good premise, and good combat concepts. Unfortunately, it feels so poorly managed and so rushed that it all falls flat on it's face to become an UNSATISFYINGLY BLAND experience.

_childDocuments_.review: As a biologist, I can appreciate the humor in the bosses' names being either their generic or specific epithet  and also a pun on their common name (Pagurus,  being an EDIBLE crab among other such brilliant contextual and visual puns). As a general enjoyer of video games, I can appreciate the hard work that went into making this meme-packed (but not intolerably or obnoxiously so) soulslike experience just that. An experience. The dark, heavy moments are dark and heavy as the situation calls for, there's an appropriate amount of impact, and an appropriate sprinkling of comic relief to keep the game from getting too depressing, despite its very loud environmental wake-up-call Aesop, which is about as subtle as a brick. For a game about ocean trash, the apocalypse, that no one you love is safe, and that you can't live in blissful ignorance forever, it's surprisingly hopeful, and very delightfully captures the spirit of Soulsborne games in a crossroads between affectionate parody and love letter to the pioneer of the genre. A bevy of accessibility features that don't shame you for using them is a welcome change, and something I hope to see more of, not just from the Crab Crew (Crusty Crew?), but from other indie, AA, and AAA studios. I bought this game and promptly devoured it in the span of a weekend. Even though it's not exactly bursting at the seams with content (a good chunk of my "play time" is just me having the game on but paused and out of focus while I was doing something else, my actual play time was probably closer to about half or even a third of my logged hours), I still see myself playing it start to finish over and over just because of the various ways one can optimize their playthroughs. The soundtrack is, while not flawless, something I would happily bump while doing some writing, my other hobby, the way that Feasley introduces the areas of the game with tracks that are desolate at first, then call in the rest of the composition to kick off the zone name is pure art, the boss themes are appropriately high-octane and panic-inducing, and the penultimate area's theme...well, I'll let you either peep the OST or play the game and figure it out for yourself.Tl;dr, it's a great, quirky, fun, emotional little game with a small handful of bugs that, while funny, don't really make the game unplayable, though I did have a bit of an issue with the  where I ended up OOB and unable to do damage to or be damaged by the boss.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is charming. It's compelling. It's fun. But it's not a good game.The whole premise of the game involves the main character's shell being stolen with the subplot that life is unfair, but I don't feel like this is an excuse for the unfair, or rather, poorly implemented combat mechanics. Don't get me wrong, engaging in combat in this game feels good. The thing you are using/wearing have a real impact on combat in a way that makes it worth considering. However, it is also littered with random attack delays, inconsistent attack patterns (to the point where some ranged enemies will fire instantly), and a targeting system that will target enemies far off in the distance leaving you open to the enemies around you. When you have spent 40+ hours in a game like Breath of the Wild, having a harder difficulty where enemies become a little unfair is a fun challenge. But when it's the only way the game can be played, and it's clearly a case of poorly managed states, it's a nightmare.Let me get into some good though, because there are some reasons you might want to play this game. Like I said before the game is very charming. It has a nice story flow, and feels rather open despite it's story-driven gameplay. When you have good luck with a fight, it feels very rewarding to kill a boss that has completely stomped you 100 times.However, when the reason said boss has completely decimated you 100 times is because the attack delays are random to the point where sometimes they attack instantly without a tell, it becomes more frustrating than fun. Which, again, if you've beaten the game and seen everything there is, I do believe this kind of feature can be a fun addition to make a game you've learned inside-out much harder. But if during the process of learning how an enemy works you can't rely on attack delays to time the horribly implemented dodge that has no i-frames, even though sometimes attack that clearly hit you will just go right through you while you're standing completely still... It's not a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Another Crab's Treasure is truly a gem in that it perfectly encapsulates everything that made early 3D platformers great, while adding a soulslike twist.I'm genuinely, GENUINELY bad at Souls games. I've never completed one entirely on my own, but I had completed DS3 with friends. It has always felt like my timing is incredibly bad in that genre, parries always felt lucky and with how accurate the hitboxes are, I had no one to blame but myself for my poor performance. It was and always has been a skill issue.This lil' ~20 hour indie game finally made a Soulslike game possible for me. While not the most difficult game in the world, the Al/parrying for each boss just clicked with me within a few attempts each. While some may prefer climbing up grander hills of memorization, I simply just don't have the time or the patience, and that is where Another Crab's Treasure excels.The platforming was genuinely smooth in between each fights, to the point where I am not sure whether bosses or traversal were my favorite part of the game. I had a few bugs (falling through the ground after hit, launching super far in the sky, camera sometimes getting stuck in the grapple view), but they were... charming bugs? I'd compare it to Skyrim overall - sure it sucks that you've died and it's a bit annoying, but never did I ever feel annoyed by the back-traveling to get what I needed.One thing I will say against the game is that its barely playable on the Deck. I wanted to complete this game while sitting out with my family, but it couldn't keep 60FPS on lowest settings for mine personally. I didn't want to stream from my PC due to precise timing/platforming, so I was kinda stuck at my desk.Mechanics, characters, story, humor... This is a game I very much looking forward to revisiting down the line!9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Combining crabs and souls games... This game was made for me. I can highly recommend it if you're a fan of soulslikes or if you're looking to get into souls. Thanks to the assist mode, the difficulty is adjustable. While I'm pretty good at souls, I am absolutely terrible at platforming, but turning off pit fall damage has made the experience better overall for me personally.The combat is fun and the shell system is incredibly clever and allows for various different playstyles (magic/umami, dodge rolls, parry, turtling). And my favourite Soulslike (Sekiro) is also repped thanks to the parry, posture bar and grappling hook. Also similar to Sekiro, you are stuck with one type of weapon (a fork), but unlike Sekiro you can (temporarily) turn it into a heavy hammer-type weapon if you choose a certain skill in the skill tree.The writing is incredible as well - I have played Aggro Crab's "Going Under" as well, the humour is still fantastic. I expected this much going in and wasn't disappointed, but in addition to that, the overall story and themes exceeded my expectations. The environment and character design is also really clever in the ways that trash is utilised. One of my favourite parts in playing this was reading the labels and brands of the discarded trash; there are some gems in there ;)The only negative point I have about this game is that the geometry is sometimes really janky (e.g. uneven flooring just makes walking unnecessarily annoying, or you get stuck in a piece of geometry during a boss fight, etc.). This is made worse due to my personal dislike and inability regarding platforming, which was rage-inducing sometimes (but your experience may be better if you're really good at 3D platforming). Despite that, I had so much fun with the game that my overall enjoyment of the whole product wasn't impacted at all. I'd give this a wholehearted recommend! Thanks for making this game! So far it's my personal GOTY of 2024 <3

_childDocuments_.review: 5.5/10. Decent gateway drug into the soulslike genre that is almost too easy if you're already a souls veteran. You can expect probably about 70% 3D-platforming and 30% combat in your entire playthrough. This game is a one-and-done with very little replay value, and boss fights are not particularly memorable or challenging at all.Game controls are pretty horrendous, but somehow serviceable since there aren't any complex mechanics. The devs actually put a heavy/charge attack on the same button as your light attack. Worse still, there's either too much input delay, or the recovery frames are too long. During faster-paced combat, sometimes your character doesn't swing when you press R1 (light attack). Other times, holding down R1 for a heavy/charged attack results in a light attack.In-game map is borderline useless. Overall UI is poorly designed and becomes apparent when you start playing the game. A giant 'Junk Recovered' text obscures your vision and stays on for too long whenever you pick up your souls. Imagine an elite or boss rushing towards you while giant text covers your screen. Whenever you walk near a shell, a giant popover obscures your vision as well. In arenas where there are shells littered all over, you literally can't see the boss most of the time.I'm a huge fan of DS1/2/3 and ER, but can't recommend this in good conscience. Even Lords of the Fallen is better than this. However, if you're looking for a fresh concept with some soulslike combat that isn't Dark Fantasy, I suggest that you pick this up on a 50% or more discount just for novelty's sake alone.

_childDocuments_.review: Charming and quick soulslike that relies a bit more on blocking and parrying than dodging. Great for beginners in the genre and veterans.The first little bit of the game can feel a bit rough, as the game fairly slowly introduces the major mechanics of your moveset. Buildcrafting is a bit limited compared to other soulslikes, as there are less overall options to change, but for a 20 hour full playthrough taking time to explore a large portion of the game, you can't expect the same potential depth as a 100 hour Elden Ring playthrough. That's not to say there isn't buildcrafting at all, as the various shells you find throughout the game come with their own weights, defenses, shell spells, and stat bonuses that can make the choice of shell very meaningful to your overall build, and there are plenty of stowaways (trinkets) to further augment what your playstyle leans into.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game, I really do.  Between the humor and the heart and effort we can see, this is an easy game to love.  Except I cannot stand the execution. Starting with the combat - it feels so underwhelming and in some cases, unfun. It tried to merge the Zelda BoTW duration system with Sekiro's parrying, except now we have a junky parry system that is difficult to chain parry, and if we mistime the parry we get heavily punished, even more than Sekiro, and I Platinum'd Sekiro, this is saying something.  Then the map/level design - the pacing feels awful. The maps are littered with tiny "come back later when you get this power" things. But there are three problems: 1. There's no marker, so while the game tries to copy Elden RIng, it didn't learn one of the best things of ER, making returning to those points difficult and confusing; 2. when we first encounter the "come back later" objects, the game doesn't tell us. So we may spend a lot of time wondering if there are mechanics nearby or some powers we can use to trigger the objects. This waste a lot of time; 3. many of the secrets are underwhelming. Like, cool we got a minor upgrade/stowaway, yay! But the upgrades themselves don't change how we play the game, at least most of them don't. So we are just getting minor power increases.Next, there are the NPCs. Most dialogues in this game is meaningless. And many of them are not likable. And yet, we see those dialogue boxes encouraging us to go talk to them. It's not like talking to them would unlock some secrets or give us useful hints... well the Yellow dialogues do but those are rare. This shows the world building is really just there for show without depth.  Last but not least, the platforming or the jump system. It's. So. Forking. Clunky! Like, what the shell. You jump too close to a ledge? You are going to bound back. You started holding x too early? You miss the long distance jump. Like crabs can swim and we are under water FFS, So why can't we swim up?  IDK, this game seems so likable on the surface, but the more I play it, the worse I feel. And why is it so damn long? The game is meant to be a simple and quick adventure, the mechanics aren't even sophisticated enough to warrant such a long gameplay. Anyway, if you got nothing better to do, this can be a way to pass your time.

_childDocuments_.review: I just started this game, and I already know I'm going to love it. How can that be?Because Aggro Crab's other game, Going Under, is one of my all-time favorites, and it became apparent very quickly that this game shares everything I loved about the studio's first title: zany physics, deep combat and customization, and surprisingly powerful social commentary beneath its irreverent humor and vibrant colors.Plus, it's the ocean. I love the ocean. There are too few games that really explore it, and even fewer that seem to envision any better relationship between humans and the ocean than (at best) a passively destructive and (at worst) an actively exploitative one.Buy this game! Buy Going Under! Support environmental policies that will reduce our systemic overreliance on single-use plastics, so we can maintain such beautiful crustacean diversity in our world! And all the other good things.*Dismounts soapbox*Knocking it out of the park again, Aggro Crab--thanks for your years of hard work to make sure we all have a shell of a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: This will be my go to recommendation for anyone looking for a starting point in the soulslike genre. The game not only gives you assist settings to make the combat more forgiving (or bypass it entirely), it actively encourages you to use them if you find that the difficulty is detracting from your enjoyment.For those of us who aren't new to the genre there's still plenty to enjoy. The hack n slash combat built off of well timed blocks and doges, methodically clearing out enemies as you explore the level, and of course the currency/xp that's lost upon death. The game also finds its own twists as well, such as a grapple hook and the shells you'll be using throughout the game. I will say that even without the assist settings it's not the hardest soulslike you'll ever play (a couple stowaways felt like assist settings in and of themselves), nor is it the most fluid. Despite that I still had a really fun time with the combat.On top of all that dodge rolling and slashing your fork is a fun story about a little hermit crab out to get his shell back. There's a memorable cast of characters for you to meet, some that you'll learn to hate, and others you'll fall in love with. Not to mention a hefty dose of commentary about pollution destroying our oceans and the consequences of unrestricted crabitalism. At the end of it all is a very satisfying conclusion that made me glad I saw Krill's journey through to the end.The game may mostly take place underwater, but it's a breath of fresh air for those of us looking for something new and more forgiving in the soulslike genre.

_childDocuments_.review: For anyone interested in a Soulslike experience, but who's bounced off of the FromSoft games for difficulty, complexity, or narrative noncohesion - This is absolutely the game for you.This is a clever, charming, beautiful game with hopeful themes. It is a very well crafted Soulslike experience, with a diffferent taste in difficulty than the FromSoft titles, but can still provide a challenge to anyone going out of their way to look for one.The one place this game is weak is the fact that it has more of a platforming focus than most of the FromSoft titles, and in a few key places it can be challenging and frustrating to get around, and intuit how certain platforming mechanics work and what the path forward is meant to look like. The game is forgiving enough that this isn't the end of the world, but the platforming feels like the least tuned aspect of the game.For anyone willing to put up with that, and a few other minor bugs here and there, I still highly recommend this game. I will just say, it is still a challenging experience, and I wouldn't recommend it to players still getting into video games in general, but it serves as a great potential entry point into an otherwise very difficult genre.

Overall, this game is great fun and an easy recommendation.

It's a shame the combat, the thing the majority of the game revolves around, was designed by a 3 year old. Hit boxes are worse than the cs2 launch hit boxes, it's slow, it's not fun, the enemies have strange delays on attacks and then the same attacks will have no delays so i'll go ♥♥♥♥ myself then and there is nothing intuitive apart from the different "shells" you can pick up. Wow they did one thing different from regular souls likes, i guess, if you don't count armour, weapon or shield abilities as being the same thing but better and more variety so it doesn't even have that going for it.Went in with high expectations, rightly so due to all the praise I've seen this below average game get and yeah it's fair to say the game doesn't even nearly live up to the expectations in any aspect aside from the simple graphics which are very nice on the eyes, and the setting, which is just a breath of fresh air. Nothing else comes close to anything that can be described as adequate. Don't even get me started on the useless platforming. It's bad. You set the game underwater and somehow platforming is one of the worst parts of it. Why after the "swim" stamina bar depletes does my tiny little hermit crab dude turn into a brick? It's a really bad implementation because a mud crab doesn't weigh 400kg so why does a tiny hermit crab? Why does dodging just straight up no work sometimes? Sometimes the button doesn't work at all, i'll press it 3 times at least for it to dodge on the last press. Sometimes i'll dodge out of the way of an attack, clearly out of the way of the attack, but still take the hit. Is this a hitbox error or an error with the dodging? either way, it's not good enough.Enjoy the game, don't enjoy the game, buy or don't buy it. I just needed a little rant about the most disappointing gaming purchase I've made since anthem, and i even enjoyed that more than this crap.I love soulslikes, I've played a ton of them, good and bad and played through every fromsoft soulsbourne game, some multiple times and some 100% achievement runs, I love these types of games and am very very familiar with them. This is a terrible game, dressed up in a popular genre it would've done better to stay out of, with a pretty coat of paint on it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolutely amazing game that feels very refreshing for the souls-like genre. while it was challenging at times, it is by far the easiest souls-like game that I have played so far, even on the hardest difficulty, which is not necessarily a bad thing. My only complaint is that the player cannot move the map around which was quite a big annoyance.

_childDocuments_.review: A really cool souls like. Though not without its flaws, it's a fun adventure so far. The team has brought back the same wit and comedy that was present in Going Under. This game is more or less their take on the souls like genre. The game has cute look but it's challenging experience nonetheless. You venture in the Sands Between (XD) on a journey to get back your shell. It feels really good to go from one area to another. You see the state of ocean and the various troubles citizens have. You have one weapon, but they give you several mechanics to make your build, including your shell and a skill tree of sorts.That being said, the game has it issues. The biggest issue the camera in cramped spaces can betray you. It's not so bad that you're helpless, but it's an issue nonetheless. The accessibility is a neat way to tailor the experience if you want to play this game, but don't like certain elements.Standing ovation for Aggro Crab making a legit souls like.
_childDocuments_.name: Another Crab's Treasure

_childDocuments_.review: What looks like Baby's-first-Soulslike from the outside is a fun and engaging romp that does not overstay it's welcome. Especially the "environmental storytelling" (yes this is a pun) this game is based around is just wonderful.The combat loop in the later half can be a bit repetitive and boss encounters do not scale well with how overpowered you are in the last quarter of the game.Still easy 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Another Crab's Treasure

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game. Despite the funny bits and the cutesy looks, it proved to be quite a challenge. Initially, that is. Like more of it's kind (like Elden Ring but Baldurs gate 3 too), the later game content didn't go up in difficulty enough. The first few bosses proved to be quite a challenge, when I didn't really know what I was doing, fought them in the wrong order and lacked the tools to build, depending on the situation at hand. However, around the half way point, I got so strong I just ended up speedrunning, ignoring most stuff, because the bosses became push overs. Most went down on the second or first try, including the final boss, because at that point I had so many of these resurrection shells I could go on forever. Still, it was fun enough I wanted to finish it so that's good.
_childDocuments_.name: Another Crab's Treasure

_childDocuments_.review: Very competent souls-like. Not very challenging but also not completely brainless. You still need to learn and master the moves and mechanics the game gives you. There are enough of tools to choose your preferred playstyle. The level design is mostly linear with shortcuts and some secrets along the way, though some areas are more open.The main downside is the lack of polish. Sometimes you can get stuck, but the game has "Die instantly" option so it's not a softlock (but can still be a frustrating setback).More importantly, the game often ignores some inputs in the middle of battle, specifically healing. You need to press the button multiple times or stop completely which is not ideal in the heat of the battle when you most likely need to heal. This can cost you some lost battles which can also be frustrating.All in all, it's a good souls-like. I can recommend it to people who are not familiar with the genre or to someone who wants more relaxed experience compared to other souls-likes.
_childDocuments_.name: Another Crab's Treasure

_childDocuments_.review: Another Crab's Treasure is a great soul-like game for those who are interested in getting into soul-like games like me. It's heavily inspired be Dark Souls, but isn't as difficult as Dark Souls, giving the player an assist mode in case the player finds the game difficult. The player may choose to play easy which doesn't fully remove the souls-like aspect of it, or there's story which is fully helping the player. The story is also very nice, not vague like Dark Souls in which you'll eventually start connecting things together.The story, the music. the art, and everything in the game is beautiful and perfect! There maybe some bugs that aren't resolved yet, I haven't encounter any and this is also an indie company that's doing their best into making this game perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: Another Crab's Treasure

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really fun game and Sekiro/Souls-like that i'd happily recommend. My first impressions so far are good,*BUT* there is are two pressing issues that makes me write this review so early in my playtime, and why I'm down voting this game until a patch comes out adressing these two points:1. The most pressing issue: PerformancePerformance takes a hit no matter what setting I chose in graphics, I can barely maintain 30fps (my laptop can handle Atomic Heart at 60fps and Helldivers at a consistent 30 with higher than medium settings). I just barely finished Nephros and part of the reason why I've died was because after a big hit or a wind up, the screen would freeze and hitch, and when it comes back, I'd be splattered across the ocean floor. This hitching and random performance drops at even medium or low settings, is unacceptable for a game that relies on quick reactions like this.I've died on bosses like Nephros because the game would hitch, especially whenever i've been hit, letting the boss close the distance again and land another hit on me. While Shellsplitter was more functional, I noticed that the issue was still present whenever I did dodges or movements, with this constant feeling of sluggishness that wasn't present whenever I was moving around the overworld (for reasons I genuinely don't know or understand). Turning graphics down didn't help much in boss-fights, especially Nephros where the game visibly froze whenever I was hit for a good 1-2 seconds, or I would be stunlocked visually from framerate dips.2. Sound de-syncingThis is most prevalent during the opening, and seems tied to performance dips, though I'm not too sure on that front. Randomly, dialogue will occur a full 5 to 6 seconds after the text comes on screen, music would randomly, yet regularly, hitch and repeat like a broken tape recorder. Voice/melee sound effects, as well as UI sound effects would occur a full second after they appear sometimes. This last bit, with the melee/voice sounds is partially fixed with reducing game quality BUT it doesn't fully remedy it. At best it lowers the time difference to a half-second to second of delay.The reason why its a disservice, at least to me, is that it interrupts and damages the voice acting + music which I was really enjoying so far when I *could* hear it. I like this game so far, but if I'm gonna keep playing, I wanna be able to enjoy the game without worrying whether the game's teetering on crashing, hitching, or having the game effectively handicap my enjoyment of the combat and story/voice-acting/music.
_childDocuments_.name: Another Crab's Treasure

_childDocuments_.review: While I only have slightly less than an hour of time in this game, I do have a few things to say. (TL/DR: 6/10 so far)The Good:The storytelling and humor is glorious. Love the satire and social commentary.The Bad:It's a souls-like. If you don't like intentionally difficult RPG games, (like me. I usually despise this sort of game) this is NOT for you. It does have a difficulty selector and several assist modes for people like me, so I enjoy that, as long as the game doesn't punish me for using them.The Ugly:There are several UI elements broken, showing the UI tags like "<!interact>" instead of showing the button icon. It also never properly detected my XBox One controller (or any other controller for that matter) and the controller section for button rebinds was perpetually blank no matter what I did.So far, I give it a 6/10. This review may change later if the UI and controller stuff get fixed later. I'll definitely be using the assist options because I suck at these kinds of games.
