_childDocuments_.review: if you've played every other from software game and you are itching for more gameplay of that style, you will enjoy this game. BUT......you need to acknowledge that this game is NOT made by from software. this is the second game from a completely different studio that wanted to make a game for this audience. and they did what they wanted to do perfectly. what this game lacks in difficulty it makes up for in environment, art style, and fun combat. the story is hard to take seriously sometimes, but the whole game is not meant to be taken completely seriously. the whole game is riddled with puns and references to other media, even including an outfit of a certain dark souls character. the gameplay itself does lack some difficulty, with certain adaptation and stowaway combos being quite unbalanced. however, the combat is still very fun. the parry system is highly satisfying and the balance/capsize meter is a fun take on dark souls stance breaks. overall, this game is meant for those looking for more from software gameplay, but are willing to branch out in terms of art and story direction.
_childDocuments_.name: Another Crab's Treasure

_childDocuments_.review: Once upon a time under the sea of AAA filth, an indie studio had a story to tell through a souls-like. Seeing as their game could never compete with the big boys of the genre, they did the only reasonable thing and put in Gen-Z humor.If you're a souls-like veteran, Another Crabs Treasure will feel less like the formula you're used to and more like a parody of the games that inspired it, whether that be intentional or not. It wears it's influence on it's sleeves, often times to hilarious results. But despite all the jokes, it thankfully never takes away from the unknowingly thoughtful and emotional story beats. The story is portrayed drastically more linear for a souls-like, but that just makes it clear that the devs thought this story was important to tell and wanted every player to experience it. This is more evident from options to flat-out make the game easier (including the option to give Kril a gun and one-shot everything, which on it's own is pretty funny). Even without them, the games is just much more forgiving that the genre standard, allowing me to recommend it to anyone who is even moderately interested in souls-likes, story-driven games or indie games, as Another Crab's Treasure is simply a fantastic experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Another Crab's Treasure

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great introduction into the souls-like genre.I found this game to be easier than most games in this genre on default settings, but I still appreciate that there are a multitude of accessibility options to make the game easier for those who still want to enjoy the story and gameplay, but may not want the stresses of challenging gameplay. The story and world are so unique that it would be a shame to not finish the game on account of it being too difficult, so I think the availability of these options is awesome.I loved all the crab puns and the overall message of the story is very powerful. It pokes fun at our economic structures, but slowly gets darker and more serious as the game goes on.The skill trees left some to be desired. I maxed out all skill trees pretty early in the game, but I did really enjoy that the magic system is tied to your shells, so the game still has some interesting progression mechanics.Very compelling game. Give it a go!100% Achievement Completion Perspective:I got all achievements in one playthrough. On top of that, adjusting the difficulty settings doesn’t lock you out of any achievements. In fact, you need to tweak a setting in order to get one of the achievements. I appreciate this as a 100%er that doesn’t like feeling locked into a certain difficulty to 100% the game.

_childDocuments_.review: better than elden ringnot even a hyperbolic joke, I like it better than elden ringreasonably challenging (until you get a solid build, then it can be fairly easy), I never felt like the game was sadistically difficult and I never stepped away feeling frustratedthe game tells a compelling story without having to hide it in flowery monologues and obscure item descriptions and it's good, great even. huge shoutout to the voice actorsso many fun little decisions (like dropping your heartkelp after having the animation interrupted, or the entirety of the environment and shell design) that show there was a real team of people with a lot of heart making itthis is one of my favorite games of all time

_childDocuments_.review: I have never written a review for a game before, but oh my. _childDocuments_.review: I had such a fun time with this game even from someone who gets very annoyed at themselves while playing soulslike games. I loved basically everything this game had to offer, from its self aware world it places you in to its music and even the gameplay itself. I really felt how much this game eases you into how soulslikes function and makes sure you get a grip on the combat before throwing more "complex" things at you. The areas you explore are fairly basic in design but my god are they gorgeous, and utilising gimmicks like returning to certain areas after you get an ability didn't phase me as much cause I just like walking (or rolling) through the world. The big make-or-break was the combat and I think they pulled it off, taking aspects from Dark Souls and Sekiro and combining the more player dependent and fun parts to make a responsive and rewarding combat loop. Even the story i loved, starts off like it may take a backseat to everything else but slowly picks up into a passionate, self aware and very personal message that I feel reached out to the people that needed to hear it. Now the game had some jank to it, but i'm certainly not letting that take over my overall enjoyment but its worth mentioning the movement, while really good, had a few instances of not being a bit annoying in some platforming areas and of course the camera, where you are fighting it more than the enemy when you get backed into a wall. Last thing to mention is defsharp does the credits song and that artist is goated to its an honorary 10/10 just for that
_childDocuments_.name: Another Crab's Treasure

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game. I never had played a souls-like game before, and I liked the overall concept of it. Part of this game is also a platformer, though these sections really aren't difficult since it mostly revolves around fish-hooking around. The humor is also interesting. most scenes were elevated by the various ocean puns, and much of the story seems to be a metaphor for the issues with capitalism, monarchy, and the greed and pride that corrupts both. There isn't much else to say, this is a fun game to play for 15-20 hours, and I might replay it to try other builds, though there is no need since you can switch builds at any time in this game. There are some issues- Some areas of the game are laggier than others. In the beginning of the game, the lag wasn't bad, but by the end, it was unbearable. I was able to reduce the impact of this by using a ranged build.Another issue is that it is just an indie game- the world isn't fully polished and you can easily go out of bounds in regular exploration, which is fine, except when you get stuck between a crevice and have to reset to a checkpoint.These issues don't take away from the charm/novelty of this game, so I would give it a try if you are on the edge.

_childDocuments_.review: Another Crab's Treasure really is an extraordinarily charming game bringing together charming 3D platforming reminiscent of games like Banjo-Kazooie or Konker's Bad Fur day, and the challenging combat in souls-like games. Now, being reminiscent of those golden era games from the N64 also means that Another Crab's Treasure does have a similar bit of jankiness that those games had; this hardly took away from the experience though. From the fish puns to the world design and all the different shells you can get with different effects. It was extremely satisfying going through the game, getting new skills, finding new shells, and beating more bosses. Another Crab's Treasure offers a charming, original, albeit somewhat easy (which is not necessarily a bad thing) entry into the soulslike genre.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone new to playing any sort of souls-like game, like many others before me have said, this is quite a good and unique introduction to such a category, but looking past that, I personally find some moments to be clever, especially with all the references to various things you find.I do like the assist feature too, even the game encourages it if you are struggling, so no shame in tweaking some modifiers here and there. The only true gripe I have with this game is the somewhat inconsistent camera combat system when you are focusing of multiple enemies, as it may focus on some far away crab rather than the one in front of you.It'd be super cool to see something like a boss rush where you fight all the bosses back to back in the future, it would be a nice post-game addition as a test of endurance and game knowledge, and as a way to rematch them, too. That's my one wish other than DLC or a sequel.Overall, it's a silly crab game with a lot of environmental messages beneath its exterior. I do think it's one of a kind nowadays, and a non 2000-2010s game that really got me hooked often for the duration of my playtime.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot of soul put into this soulslike(heh) and a suprisingly good story!The fishes are using our trash to build their empire unknowing of the dangers it will bring. You will meet many interesting, funny and some annoying characters on your journey when all you want is to sleep in your (stolen) shell.Combat is very good and and there is a varity of viable playstyles, at the end game you will probably feel very strong.Only downside is there are a couple sections where it is not so clear what to do to progress, but it's really not bad.Very good game, definitely try it if you love soulslikes and wanna play one with a lot of personality.Krill them all!
_childDocuments_.name: Another Crab's Treasure

_childDocuments_.review: Have ever wondered what a game would look like if the creators of Dark Souls, Disney, and Rick and Morty collaborated? Wait no further, Another Crabs Treasure is a masterclass of difficult boss battles, undersea visuals, great humor, and storytelling wrapped up in one. Though don't be fooled by the adorable characters, this is by far no cake walk. Everything from ancient king crabs to cute minnows will try and kill you, its every crustacean for themselves in the deep. Between the crude humor and hours of exciting game play its a steal being about the same price as a 8 piece meal at KFC. Only downsides to this game is if its run on highest settings it will drain your steam deck of juice and some may be turned away by the difficulty. All in all i would give this 5 stars, round of applause to the developers. Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game in good faith. It feels unpolished in all aspects. From bosses and enemies getting constantly stuck on terrain to Kril (yourself) also getting stuck and sliding off the environment and interact-ables. I do not make games so I do not know how much longer they should have kept developing this game but it definitely needs more time in the oven so to speak. Next for the combat once again unfinished and unpolished. It feels like every enemy and boss is vastly overpowered because of the range of their attacks and speed as well. I recognise this game is souls-adjacent but it constantly feels like you are lvl 1 with a stick poking at enemy health sponges.  It feels over punishing even in a souls-like genre. For the art style, I would say it is this game most refined part but even so I found objects and structure in environment that were clipping into each other which in my opinion just feels like finding a rotten strawberry hidden in the middle of the box and kind of sours the whole pleasent-ness of the art-style.So, if this game is aiming to feel be an unpolished fan-made homage to soulsborne game. It has accomplished that but nothing more.  Hopefully, the devs and everyone there keep working on this game because I can truly see this being an easy nominee in their category for an award if so.

_childDocuments_.review: Another Crab's Treasure is a lot of fun, and really made for folks who like soulslikes but want a change of pace.  It has a good story and thematic gameplay.  If you are fishing for nautical nonsense with satisfying bosses this is your game.  As for length, I completed the game and all achievements in 26 hours.  I think I arrived at the final boss at around 22 hours.As for things you can sink your claws into, the game really captures being a crab underwater well.  You are underwater and a hermit crab in a mostly open world game.  You don't swim well, but you can flail about a bit to fall a little slower.  There is a deflect and parry mechanic in the game that is tied to using your crab's shell.  If you hide in your shell, it will absorb and negate some damage (deflect).  If you exit your shell just as the attack lands you will perfect parry, taking no damage and giving the opponent posture damage (and allowing for a riposte when you get that upgrade).  The parry mechanic takes a little getting used to as you have to be in your shell first and exit at the right time.  Many games do the opposite, where you have to time your deflect just as the attack hits.  By the end of the game I was parrying swimmingly.With respect to difficulty, if you don't learn the game mechanics you are going to have a bad time.  I found the platforming bits in the game much more difficult than the combat; but I tend to not like parkour in games so that may just be me.  All that said, if you flow with the game its a decent challenge and a lot of fun.  If you find yourself getting frustrated they added in an "Assist Mode" with a bunch of options.  Normally I ignore that completely, but there is an achievement for using one of the Assist features.  That one involves giving your crab an actual handgun that just one shots anything.  I have heard you can use that on bosses if you want to just surge past them.The story is actually pretty good.  We start off with some light tax evasion and end up less of a hermit.  There's a lot of "obvious subtlety" in the art and mechanics about ocean pollution.  Microplastics are the main currency and trash is something you interact with all the time as your shell is made of it.  The way the ocean dwellers interact with it is best described as aggressive capitalism, which keeps the story light.  The music and level art are great too, and fit with the theme well.As for issues, I did encounter a few small glitches here and there.  There were several times that I exited the scenery and had to find a way back into the level.  I also had the game go into "slideshow mode" when my controller disconnected.  Overall nothing to be too crabby about.  Mechanically, it is a little less "snappy" than games a lot like it.  What I mean is, sometimes I would press an input for an action and nothing would happen as it was finishing up a previous frame of something else.  That was a little frustrating.The achievements are not miss-able in this game, so its a good one to 100% if you are into that.  Like this review to Acknowledge Knowledge!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this game for what seems to be since the dawn of time. I loved the Dark Souls trilogy and have a weird obsession with crabs and thought "haha soulslike crab game". So I followed the publisher and fell in love with Aggro Crab as their posts were amazing and even now finding things in the game I remember from those posts. I thought it'd be a fun game, a little difficult, but a silly little game. I was wrong. It's really good, the combat feels deep and rewarding. It feels unique enough to differentiate from the Souls series with an odd familiar feel. The exploration feels rewarding, and even the platforming feels fun to do. I'm constantly looking around for hidden areas, both high and low. This game has turned into a thing I was looking forward to for the goofs, to a fully fledged game that I'm not ashamed to say I love. Easily 9/10 for me so far.The only thing holding back that I've noticed is the following 2 items. Umami feels introduced a little too late, where I was leveling and collecting these powers thinking I was missing something. Granted, I don't know when the right time to introduce it would be, but I'm 6 hours in without a clue of what to do with my crystals. The only minor thing that holds me back is sometimes the camera and geometry don't mix well, true to a Souls experience. I've gotten frustrated at where the camera gets to, especially with faster enemy lock-ons, and sometimes the platforming feels cheap because there will be random gaps that look good, but when you fall into them, you question your own sanity.That does not take away from the game too much though. If you enjoy a Soulslike experience, or want a fun little game about ocean pollution, this is a really fun one. Don't let the difficulty scare you away either, because the Devs have added many options for those looking for a fun game to play without the hair pulling that a Soulslike can give you.

_childDocuments_.review: Soulslike is a genre that plenty of devs have tried to imitate, improve, subvert, etc. They often either change too little of the formula, resulting in me feeling like "well, why not just play DS3 again instead of this?". Or they change too much, or change the wrong thing, destroying the harmony of how the various mechanics come together to form the experience.Another Crab's Treasure gets it. The combat is GOOD. What it lacks in weapon variety it makes up for in the unique shell mechanic. The Sekiro-like (or really, more Lies of P-like) stance bar gives you multiple ways to wear down an opponent. The way that fundamental combat mechanics that you'd expect of the genre (parry, plunging attack, etc) are locked away behind a skill tree serves as a second-layer tutorial to ease you into advanced mechanics (this might sound annoying but you unlock skills very fast. I had about 80% of the skill tree unlocked in the first 3 hours).The story, the voice acting, the whimsical and comedic but slightly unsettling tone, it's all good. If you like souls games, play this. If you have never played a souls game, I would say this is a great entry point.

_childDocuments_.review: Another Crabs Treasure is anywhere from 40 to 60 hours of challenging fish-themed fun; witty, crabby dialogue and not-so-thinly-veiled anti-capitalist sentiment -  which isn't for everyone, but is surely for some. The game is clear in its message - we need to address how our consumption is affecting the world around us - but there's no time at which the point detracts from the game's enjoyability. The platforming is fun; the combat and shield (shell) system is well thought out and the skills progression system lets you customise Krill's build to your own, tailored style of play. The bosses form a perfect balancing act. They're challenging and frustrating in measures that you'd expect from any soulslike - leaving you shaking the monitor one second, telling the screen: 'one more time', and having you proudly announcing your victory the next. Furthermore, there are options to make the experience easier, so you aren't locked into a game that you feel that you can't win. If anything, the game sometimes lags but not to the extent that it ruins the experience - at least for me, personally. It's definitely worth purchasing if you're new to soulslikes or if you just want a short, sweet stint in the ocean that'll leave you with a poignant message and a hankering for further challenges.

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, this game is fantastic. Based on the "souls-like" game varlety, It can be challenging for gamers of different skill-levels but also made easier so one doesn't get too frustrated with fighting in particular  (changed via the menu options). That being said, it is a far-cry from traditional souls-like game in the traditional fighting and combat style-- different but very well executed. It has a wonderful score and soundtrack that's pleasant to listen too and a wonderful one-of-a-kind story that has the added benefit of raising awareness of trash and plastic in our oceans, which is a huge concern for anyone that knows about it and humanity as a whole.I haven't beaten it, having played quite a few hours on "hard difficulty" and takes re-learning the controls if you break from it for too long.For me, this game gets high marks all-around and the game of the year nomination.

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me want to write my first ever review, partly because Aggro Crab is a small studio that delivered such an excellent game.The first obvious thing, this is a Soulslike game, but in a simpler scale, which I found works perfectly well and does not feel empty or leaving more desired. The stats, shells you use, and magic attacks have enough variety to keep you finding new ways to play the game, and its so seamlessly easy to do so, that you don't ever feel stuck in one style.The story on the other hand, take the "world in decline" of Souls game and uses it to deliver a strong message about the pollution of our oceans while also putting strong critics on the capitalist system and drawing parallels from the crabs to human and how we adapt to the ecological and ethical disasters all around us.The characters are few but distinct and interesting. Dialog lines are both very humorous and sometimes very serious as well, which I really consider one of the game's biggest strengths.In the  end, it left me satisfied that I played it, with a huge smile on my face and a recommendation for everyone to try it. The difficulty settings allow even  casual players to play it and enjoy it. Overall 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game may un-ironically be my 2024 Game of the Year, and probably the best non-From Souls-like I have played.Combat is phenomenal. It is very smooth Souls-like combat that revolves around picking up different pieces of trash as your hermit crab shell, such as a tin can or a shot glass. The shells act more or less like a shield in a Souls game, except they have their own health bar and can break. Each one also has its own special ability. For example, your tin can shell might give you lightning damage, or a Yakult bottle's health bar can be consumed to restore some of your own. There are many different ability and shell combos that allow you to modify your playstyle. Think light, med, heavy rolling in a Souls game.The music is perfect for the setting. It ranges from fun and upbeat, sometimes techno-y, to the very emotional and epic and symphonic. The visuals are great. It has a cute style that belies its nature in some ways, but it makes for an excellent contrast. The sound effects add a lot for impact and personality.The narrative of the game is far more effectual motivating than you might expect from a game that looks like this one. It basically starts with your character Kril, a small hermit crab, getting his shell taken by someone claiming to be a tax collector. Kril has no idea who could even be ruling over him to impose this tax, and chases down the collector and tries to get his shell back. This is the basic premise, but it has an extremely cohesive theme that runs through the whole game, and marvelously drives home it's message. The characters are also funny and charming, and many of them had definitely grown on me by the end of the game.The humor is on point. This game had me laugh out loud multiple times, whether it was a piece of dialouge or satirical fictional branding on a piece of garbage. This game's universe is like Spongebob if Bikini Bottom was made of garbage that fell down to the sea floor. The game even makes a few clever references to things like Spongebob here and there, I don't think it would be unfair to say it was inspired in some way by it.I adore this game. Can't recommend it enough. Will probably update this review if I think of anything else to add.

_childDocuments_.review: Fresh look and vibe for a souls-like while not being as tediously punishing as something like elden ring. Also the only chill and semi-happy looking souls-like game I've played - really nice to not have a dull, depressing, monotone-esque world surrounding me all the time (and provides a nice contrast when things are not happy). World mechanics are par for the course with some nice thematic flavoring. Actual combat mechanics feel (movement, attack, responsiveness, etc...) a bit on the loose side, overall pretty mid. But the game is balanced around it well enough that it's not an issue even if it is kind of frustrating at first (pro-tip: don't use the camera lock mechanic, messes up movement and dodging). It feels like a fair trade-off for the fresh story and art of the game, especially considering the size of the team. While it may be the weakest part of the game, it is only in contrast to the rest of the game - overall solidly mid souls-like combat (definitely a lot worse out there). The game is still really well balanced overall, taking into account its own flaws and playing to its strengths, resulting in a challenging but fair & fun souls-like experience. 5/7 would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Finished it, loved it. Great game. Gets better as you go. Best Souls-like I've played. Looking forward to what this developer does next.Went on a genocidal rampage with a fork because I was told to pay taxes. Surprisingly good Shoals-like, my personal favorite out of the top contenders because they finally did something original with the format. I haven't finished it yet but I can't put it down, I'd recommend this to basically anyone who likes Souls games.The creativity on display here in the narrative, levels, and enemy design is really special. The humor really lands for me on this one, which is very unusual for games in general in my case. The fish (lol) you meet have a ton of personality and variety, but don't overstay their welcome by bombarding you with cutscenes or party chats, similar to a Souls game. They say their lines and you're back to playing a video game instead of skipping through a movie. Their society adapting to  is a really unique narrative device , really great take on it.The level design is tight, and doesn't hold your hand. Plays a bit like a Metroidvania with backtracking made possible by unlocked abilities. Navigating the levels faster once you have some skills unlocked and get a good feel for the platforming is super fun, and separates it alot from a more grounded Souls game.The combat is really fun; it's different enough from Souls to be interesting. Your block sustain is determined by your shell durability, and the shells have different special abilities with some shells being obviously better than others, giving it an interesting "economy" where blocking and parry attempts have trade offs. It also doesn't allow (or require) i-frame abuse as much as the typical FromSoft game, meaning that blocking is a requirement rather than a crutch for bad players. You'll end up maxing out your skill tree if you are any good at games at all, but the skills themselves give you enough options that your playstyle can vary, along with your shell loadout (). The whole thing ends up being surprisingly nuanced for a game about a crab.An incredible achievement for apparently a core team of 11 developers, and well worth your $30.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, chums, this game made me leave a review, which is 'nuff said. I’ve completed the game 100%, and as an avid Soulsborne player, I can confidently say this is a game done right. The atmosphere is captivating, the characters are vibrant, and the gameplay is hella cool. Each shell gives you an umami power (spells) and provide a different array of stats (mostly weight, defence and durability) so you can find tour favorite tool for the job (if lucky, or crazy enough). How cool is that??? Despite I mostly played a melee stagger build, I can definitvely say that all builds are available. I will totally try an umami one next time I will play! And last but not least, the metaphor behind Kril's adventure is incredibly endearing and progressing through the game feels both like a physical and spiritual journey. This feels like a Sekiro meets Dark Souls meets Hollow Knight in a flavorful colorful soup where love and passion are the main ingredients.It’s true that there are a few frustrating issues (e.g., dying on a ledge means you respawn on it and if you have no way out... death is your only solace — looking at you), but the pros far outweigh the cons. It’s not the hardest Soulsborne you’ll ever play; in fact, I would say it is a 5-6 (but keep in mind I have been playing the genre since 2011), but definitively a memorable one that will have you coming back for more down the line (I am looking at you Hollow Knight!!!) Nevertheless, it’s still as enjoyable and arduous as a game of this kind should be.I would love to see a New Game+ mode, FASTER bosses and enemies, and secret endings, but considering this game was made by a team of just 20?... 22 people, that’s pretty impressive. Do yourself a coddamn favor and grab this game—you won’t regret it. And if soulsborne games aren’t your cup of tea, you can always turn on story mode and enjoy the platforming and great story. Great job Aggro Crab, this is easily the best game of 2024 for me.. Krill 4 life!P.s: Poise damage babyyyyyyyy!

_childDocuments_.review: Like many souls-like games enjoyers, I have recently been experiencing souls-like fatigue. This being the case, I wasn't sure about this one. It looked fun, I saw a few reviews, but wasn't certain I would enjoy it. In the end, I went ahead and got it on sale, figuring I would give it a try.I was very impressed by this game. Combat was fun and varied, with different shells having different abilities, and earning new attacks and abilities through the collection of Umami crystals. The rate at which these are earned is perfect, keeping things interesting, and once everything is unlocked you have a small arsenal of tools at your disposal to turn the tides of battle (pun not intended).This is elevated further by the writing, which is excellent, and the atmosphere. Things are relatively cheerful and bright at the beginning of the game, but get darker as things go on. By the end, it feels much more in line with other souls games, but has what I think is a nice happy ending, and a somewhat subtle environmental message. Trash is a continuous theme of the game, but is never really directly addressed by the characters as a proper issue, or really the source of the gunk plague until the end of the game.Finally, the difficulty was on point here. I feel like there's been a difficulty arms race in souls-like games which (at least for me) is causing the aforementioned fatigue, and having the right balance of challenging gameplay is pretty important. This game hit the sweet spot. It's difficult, but not oppressively so, which is perfect, at least in my opinion.I highly recommend this one, it was a great experience, and I'll happily revisit it in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I just want to preface that I have never enjoyed a souls game enough to complete it, or even particularly want to play it. This review is most certainly for others that feel the way I did, should they see it.I wanted to play a cute little game I kept seeing on youtube about a cute little crab, knowing full well that my history of enjoying souls games was pretty poor, but I thought "hey, I'll still think its worth it just to have the cute little crab game."Almost 27 hours later I've gone further in this game than I ever thought I possibly would, and I had a blast the entire time. Even when I was beaten down by challenging enemies I wasn't annoyed or frustrated, I just wanted to get back up and see if I can go even further than I just had. It helped that the game had a lighthearted tone that just encouraged me more!This is the best game I've played all year and it very likely will remain the best game I've played all year. For the first time in my life I would wake up in the morning and *want* to play a souls-like. The combat was challenging and enjoyable. The mechanics were very well thought out and I never experienced an unfair moment in the game. My failures were my own and I learned how to adapt to whatever obstacle I was against. The npc's were so endearing and fun, the story enraptured me as it blew out of proportion from its starting premise, the bosses were smartly designed and so entertaining to fight especially when the strategy to defeat them finally clicked.If you're on the fence about this game, I encourage you to take that leap of faith. Take it from someone who thought they'd never like a souls game, if you're the same way this is the one that just might do it for you. Genuinely, I'm happy that I was able to enjoy the full extent of this game first hand. I hope whoever reads this review will feel the same way if they take a chance on it.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot to like about this game, but I think I only wholeheartedly recommend it to try first, borrow or buy on sale. Don't get me wrong, with the team they had this game is a massive achievement -- one of the first games that captured some of the beautiful balance that the genre is known for.  It does not, however, capture it all and does not stick the landing.Many of the achievements are hidden, but at the time of this writing only 18% of players actually defeated the final boss. To me, this reflects how the game gets old over time without new and fresh ideas invigorating it. The thing that stops me from saying, PLAY THIS GAME full stop is that I'm just not sure how many people who pick it up will stick with it to the end.I feel I am starting to sound overly negative, so let's talk about the positives because there are quite a few.Dodging and attacking are well animated and for the most part attacks are well choreographed earning the "tough but fair" idea of difficulty.The game does a great job with collectables. They are quite bountiful and generous but it still generally feels worth it whenever you go out of your way for a shiny or a clam shell. There are Zelda-style pieces of the heart to grab, your fork can be upgraded a la Hollow Knight and you can get more MP, upgrade your spells, get new abilities which leads to a rich experience for those who can't say no to treasure.Likewise, the shell mechanic is elegant. There are a ton of shells to try on, several of which are so freaking neat that I won't spoil them here. The game uses a similar idea to Sekiro in that you only have the one weapon, but instead of prosthetic tools which are more limited in their use, the shell powers always feel cool and I like that you can build around them and even insure the shell to make sure you get a new one every time you die.After the first fight there's generally no tedious running back through the enemies to get to the boss if you die. The mechanic they use for this is even quite cute.While I personally never messed with any of the difficulty settings and kept it on the default Hard setting, I do like that it has difficulty options for people to play with. If you just wanna explore this crabby world and not ever get frustrated you don't have to mod the game! AND, it did not detract from my experience whatsoever.There is tons of creativity on display with the world design that are clever and adorable. One of the main characters has an orange peel for hair. The stairs in the main city are made of dominoes. The idea of trash being the main economy of the world is unique and poignant, although that leads me into...You take the good with the bad.The puns are all fun and I generally love the lightheartedness of the game. It even tries to fit in a character arc for the central character which, while not at all complicated, makes narrative sense. Yet, that same jokey nature of the game makes it harder to swallow the more serious concepts they try to throw in especially towards the end of the game. When the satire works, it works but when you get to a certain point it starts to feel too serious.Some bosses are great, others are tedious. For the most part, the bosses that are on the same level as you but slightly bigger work, but the ones with gimmicks and overlong standby phases slow down the game's pace. While I loved the final boss, the two right before it are doing clever things (including one I had not actually experienced in a Souls-like before), but it is not measured and feels like wasted time.You have a jump button. You can even Yoshi float! There's a grappling hook, which you can even use offensively! Jumping is even essential to dodging some attacks, which is cool. However, this felt like an active hindrance to appealing level design in the later levels. Puzzles are all well and good, but function best when they get to make the player feel smart. Here, they are not the central element of the game and the platforming feels like a huge waste of time when not used sparingly. I love the platforming sections that ask you to balance your jumping with managing the enemies but especially later in the game it feels like it makes for these vacuous, confusing levels that get in the way of, you know, fightin' stuff.The design team is small here. The number of names in the credits were easily countable and it makes me wonder how much a Souls-like depends on a AAA budget. The designs here were often creative, but often also felt just like some Unity assets someone bought and stuffed into the world. I also felt the game was a bit too long and could have benefiting from making things smaller and tighter but with that comes the lack of build diversity and a sameness that infects many off-brand Dark Souls. I'm glad to say that I still think this game is a peer of those games rather than an off-brand version but sometimes it sadly can feel that way.While I was quite pleased with the total number of shells you could inhabit, I was a bit disappointed by how many of them had the same powers as others. Part of me feels this is an unfair criticism as that often comes with the territory in Souls-likes and especially given the size of the design team. However, it would make it feel more exciting to get a new shell and wonder if it has a unique ability and how you can use it.Then there's some jank.I got stuck in the level geometry a few times and had to use the merciful "die instantly" feature. No game is without glitches and at least they made sure you can't hard-lock yourself out of your save. The throw attacks of certain enemies also can lead to some wonky physics and clipping.The jump can feel inconsistent, especially when you are grappled to a wall.The map is well designed, but not being able to move it, while clearly intentional, is more of a hassle than any real benefit, but others could disagree on that.Sometimes chaining attacks feels clunky and it feels like nothing comes out particularly when you are trying to begin the startup of the heavy attack.There are too many NPCs that you can talk to that do not really add anything meaningful to the game and just feel like they exist to make the world feel populated and it feels artificial and forced. You learn pretty quickly who you can ignore, but it still felt bad to leave all of these people not talked to when, for whatever reason, you can technically talk to them.Very small gripe, but when you sell an item and then pick up another one a new abrasive textbox comes back up telling you what the item is as if you hadn't gotten one before. The inconsistency of the press A versus hold A to acknowledge you read something can also be confusing particularly early on. When fighting the first optional boss, myself and two other players felt we got attempts ruined by one of these hold A to acknowledge boxes and while it did hold important information it only actually appears in that fight when you are doing well and completely ruins the flow of the combat.I do recommend this game if you have been made insane enough to enjoy these masochistic titles. I cannot speak to whether it is a good entry point to the genre, but I can say I am glad I played it even if I'm not all that glad I beat it.

_childDocuments_.review: This absolutely blew me away.  was an excellent freshman showing for Aggro Crab, but damn they seriously knocked it out of the park with this one. I went in expecting a cute, not especially difficult Soulslike; what I got was a cute, not especially difficult Soulslike with some really innovative ideas of its own, paired with excellent storytelling.Very few Soulsborne games from studios other than FromSoft manage to get the "game feel" right, but Aggo Crab nailed it here. Mechanically sound, with a ton of creative and fun boss encounters. No, it isn't particularly difficult, but it's just so damn fun. I played this right after , and maybe a hot take here: Aggro Crab made bosses more fun to fight than FromSoft!The writing is funny and witty, as you might expect from the studio that brought us . The story is cute and engaging throughout, but it really comes into full swing in the third act. This is a story about late-stage capitalism, pollution, mental health, and a classic coming of age story—it's a lot, but  juggles it all exceptionally well.One last comparison to , since it's still fresh on mind after playing these two back-to-back. When I finished SotE, I felt annoyed, disappointed, and relieved that I could play a different game. When I finished , I had a tear in my eye, a smile on my face, and I felt so lucky to be able to have experienced this phenomenal work of art.Bravo, Aggro Crab, bravo.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a simple fun story and is a great game to pick up for souls lovers looking to pick up a quick gameoverall rating 7.8/10Gameplay 8/10 - a game for souls lovers, despite only being given 1 upgradable weapon through the game it finds creative ways to enhance the gameplay. bits of platforming and puzzle solving help keep you on your toes. There are not too many cons to the combat, bosses just become super easy once you get your hands on the pistol shrimp adaptation and grappling hook upgrades, you can chain stagger the bosses to victory. Story - 8/10 Krill the protagonist has a simple goal and you feel him grow as you continue to progress through the game. Krill who starts out shy and scared becomes aware of his strength and is what you want out of a protag toward the end.exploration - 7/10 the game looks overall great. especially toward the end game areas. plenty of references included. the sands between (The one area of the game that connects all the other areas together) is very barren and can be very difficult to navigate considering that you have a map that you cannot interact with it becomes a challenge to figure out where to go as you have to rely on landmarks to even know where you are.  100% difficulty 6/10. I was able to complete the game in about 15 hours in my first playthrough. Majority of the achievements are story progression with the collectables being something you consistently find through the game and about half of them can be purchased from the shell merchant. luckily there are no achievements tied to finding all the purple crystals in each area.

_childDocuments_.review: Another Crab's Treasure is an extremely well-made soulslike with the usual primary gameplay loop (Bonfires, dodge rolling, estus flasks - you know the trappings) broken up by platforming sections that give the player room to breathe while still keeping them engaged. The graphics have all the animation and color of a Saturday morning cartoon, and the writing offers laughs galore along the way while still ultimately having a world that follows all the dour, sad beats and environment of a Souls game with an overarching plot not only with obvious environmental commentary but also a heartwarming story about the importance of mutual aid. The sole complaint I have against this game is that I encountered bugs throughout my playthrough, from the graphical (lighting errors) to the gameplay (phytoplankton+ seems to not trigger randomly?) to level design (frequent clipping issues). The difficulty is perfectly tuned but if you disagree there are accessibility and difficulty settings all the way up to giving our pro-crab-onist a gun. While I think the $/hour metric is overrated and leads to bloated games, this is an excellently paced yet decently lengthy experience that clocked around 20 hours according to my Steam playtime; I could probably get all the achievements if I were a completionist in another 4-6. I wholeheartedly recommend Another Crab's Treasure.

The world, the characters, and the story are fin-tastic, having a lot of silly moments and at times lines of dialogue I wouldn't expect out of a game surrounding a cartoon crab. While the game isn't as difficult as some souls-likes I've played, it still has some challenging moments. If you aren't the type of person who wants the game to be very challenging and you just want to experience the story, they have a handful of assist options that will make the game as easy as you want it to be. All in all they have a bit of something for everyone and I highly recommend at least trying the game out.TL;DR:fun game, interesting characters and a good story. highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say? I LOVE indie games. I have beaten so many indie games over the past 3 years its not even funny-Transistor-Guacamelee 1 and 2(AMAZING GAMES)-Trek to Yomi-Gato Roboto-Enter the Gungeon-Dead Cells(Very hard)-Bastion-Hollow Knight-Death's Door-Carrionand much moreNow I added Another Crab's Treasure to the mix and I am TOTALLY sold. I just beaten the game a few weeks ago on xbox game pass. Now I have it on steam full price after A good 30 hrs in the game(trying to 100% the game) and got almost all the achievements except 3. Its 32 achievements in Total. If you are a PATIENTGAMER you will be spending days playing this game. Anyway I want to talk about my experience. The pros and the Cons to be exactPro-The voice acting is VERY GOOD-The cast of characters in the game are diverse and fantastic-The aesthetic of the game is gorgeous. The notion that almost the entirety of the game is inside the ocean gave me Dark souls in bikini bottom vibes haha-The game is challenging-The inclusion of adaptations that diversifies the gameplay-Every single game mechanic is utilized very well in the environment where the game is located AKA the ocean. Spearfishing to pull enemies towards you, adaptations of the shap of a crab or tentable to do additional damage, You can float in the water while platforming, but if you are ABOVE water you obviously can't,etc-Tons of easter eggs that are references from So many different franchises in video games and TV shows. Spongebob squarepants, elden ring, etc.-The utilization of trash as a shell that gives you abilities and protection is just utterly amazing and quite innovative. Using the ability of a banana can give you raw health, while a probiotic can heal health overtime, or a coconut or tennis ball can roll to stagger enemies. -The soundtrack, sound design, and ambiences are absolute TOTAL fire. Every single area, boss, Scuttleport was fire, fort slacktide was fire, new carcina lower or upper was fire, parrying sound effect is fire, heck even simply healing yourself with kelp had a nice ring to it. -Utilizing trash as an offensive weapon which can be swapped is AWESOME! but beware some trash can be broken. Also you have to learn this UMAMI ability. Cons-Platforming can feel a bid weird.-You can get stuck in some places and have to spam the jump button to get out. But at least I never been in a situation where I had to restart or let myself die. Only place O** O**** trying to get a secret item-Stats dont seem to be very effective in combat unless you devote a lot of time. It seems you can easily lvl 1 your character through the entirety of the game but I havent tested this yet.-Costumes dont affect character stats. That REALLY sucks! -Parrying and riposte have to be learned before you can use it. Good news is, it doesnt take very long so its not a big problem. 8.75/10I am replaying this game right now as we speak. The devs also heavily communicate with the fans! NG+ is coming and bugs are getting fixed! As well as good merchandise! Now that is KRILL :)

_childDocuments_.review: I really wasn't expecting to enjoy this game as much as a I did, but it was genuinely very fun. I got every achievement in the game and in only 20 or so hours. The game is very difficult by like Dark Souls or Elden Ring standards but I think it's accessible enough with or without accessibility settings that a lot of people can enjoy this game.In my own run through the game I only ever put levels into Umami or Resilience when a stowaway I wanted to use required it. I basically went pure damage and went through most of the game using the same stowaways with little variation. I often use heavy weapons like giant hammers or swords in the FromSoft games, so the ability to use a heavy hammer weapon was a blessing for me until it felt like a hindrance in the last stretch of the game.The messaging of the game regarding capitalism and ocean pollution was really great to see, since it actually came off as genuine. I felt disgusted and sad because of the locations in the game and how pollution effects the characters, locations and history of the game's lore. Spoilers: Overall, I recommend this game to souls players and those wanting to get into the souls-like genre especially, since the game can be played through quite casually and as casually as you want it to be.

_childDocuments_.review: I couldn't recommend this game hard enough if I tried. A polished, challenging, wonderful game with its fair share of tongue-in-cheek humor and poignant moments. There's a wide, *wide* set of options for playing, from build style to upgrades to accessibility options, and in my experience ACT handled all of them gracefully. I think the game's weakest point, especially near the end, was the finicky platforming (paired with a grapple with some oddly aggressive target snapping), but sections like those are optional and still rewarding. The fact that the game also allows for re-configuring your build at a minor cost also helps if you're struggling with certain bosses, as well.Another Crab's Treasure doesn't just imitate the popular and (in)famous patterns in its predecessors- it follows its own current and nails (forks?) them in a way that satisfies time and time and time again. There wasn't a single session I played where I didn't have a good chuckle over the humor or have an "a-ha" moment over a new shell or upgrade perfectly-suited to my playstyle. I can't wait to play it again to see every single detail and secret I missed on my first go through it- of which there are *many*- and really take in everything it's got to offer. And once it sinks its claws into you, I imagine you will too.

_childDocuments_.review: A really compelling soulslike game. It plays very similar to the Dark Souls series, but in a more bite sized manner. I didn't find this game as hard as Dark Souls, but it still had an engaging level of challenge. The combat especially felt very good, blocking and riposting feels great to pull off.I loved the shell mechanic -- the fact that part of my equipment loadout could break pushed me to try different shells, and try different play styles. I also loved the world, the writing, and the story, the ending felt like it many satisfying payoffs, and the characters were compelling.I would highly recommend this game to any fan of action/adventure, and I look forward to the next game from this studio.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my Cod, where to even start??The humor is riveting, the game play is fresh and uniquely delightful. The art is crisp and goofy as it is stunning. The soundtrack and sfx are captivating! The game is challenging but rewarding. And the premise/story is both exciting and meaningful, told in a uniquely immersive way. There aren't many cut-scenes, the but the few that there are were fully utilized and the game lets the immersive game play ring in the rest of the story. There are so many funny trash/pollution props to notice and other little Easter eggs (I'm looking at you-- a certain musical composition near the end of the game!) The combat is also fresh and innovative-- the shells are an interesting take a resource system similar to Zelda, but executed in a non-tedious way. Now that I've beaten the game, I've LOVED watched speed runs-- this games funny glitchyness has offered some incredibly fresh and creative WOW moments in speedruns and I am hoping that keeps the game alive for years to come. Also-- If this game sells for $30 how can you ever justify buying a loveless game for the new standard AAA $70 price?I could go on all day-- I couldn't be more proud of what a small indie studio of 11 was able to pull off. This game is a masterpiece and deserves indie game of the year. You all are seriously so creative and witty over there at Aggro Crab. Thanks for creating a truly memorable and fun experience with an even stronger story and message.

_childDocuments_.review: You play as Kril, a small hermit crab in the big unforgiving ocean. While on his adventure, Krill will learn of the affects of the industrial revolution. He will learn all of the fundamentals of society as we know it, such as: taxation, classism, corporate greed, the plight of the working class individual and most importantly, the feeling of dying over and over again.Another crab's treasure has great visuals, simple yet fun feeling combat and is easy enough to pick up and play for the experienced souls-like gamer. But don't worry, this game also offers an assist mode, where you can customise the gameplay to suit your needs. Want to steamroll your way though this mankind created hellhole with a gun? You can do that, or just simply turn off the fact that you lose your microplastics upon death. You can set the tone.If you are a fan of souls-like games, or just want to dismantle a monarchy who tax the poor and give to the rich, or fight your way through a corrupt CEO's factory, where all the works have gone crazy because of poor working conditions, then this is absolutely the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Crab Souls was a fun experience, providing me overall with exactly the kind of pains that a traditional Souls game does but wrapped up in a silly, cartoony, genre-savvy shell.The narrative! It's lighthearted and entertaining, and they did a great job with the writing right off the bat. You're just a guy who had his day interrupted and wants nothing more than to get his shell back so he can go back to relaxing alone. Eventually, as one might expect, it takes a darker turn, especially nearing the end, as the topic of the ocean being polluted so heavily is more directly tackled.It was interesting, though, that I never felt like the game specifically told me "we should stop polluting the ocean," rather it instead showed the ramifications of the ocean's pollution and allowed me to derive the message for myself. Not that it's a hard message to grasp, but that presentation certainly means something.The gameplay? Honestly, if you've played one soulslike, you know what you're getting into. This game is far easier than any others in the genre, so I would consider it a great point of entry if you're concerned about the difficulty. The shell mechanic is by far the most unique thing about the game, as it makes you feel like you're finding and deciding to switch to a new shield every so often, which has its own innate ability. There's a high degree of personality your playthrough can have based on what shell(s) you prefer to use.The studio has released one game prior to this, which I've played and 100%ed as well, and let me tell you, the physics jank is something you'll just be living with. There's a not-insignificant amount of moments where I know I got screwed by hitboxes or some collision with the environment or enemies that didn't make much sense. That being said, fighting remained enjoyable enough that these moments didn't deter me from wanting to engage with it.The music was kind of hit-or-miss, I think, which is a shame because of just how much a good OST can contribute to the quality of a game. A couple tracks I can think of are memorable and will stick with me for a bit, but most of them are just part of the background and don't particularly hit you with any impressive vibes.I may be in the minority for this part, but the voice acting felt about equal to the music for me. A few of the characters had very good voice acting that accurately matched what you see, and for such a small team you could say that having a diverse set of voices to work with is still very good in and of itself, which I agree with, but I found that probably half of the voiced lines had me wondering more when they'd stop talking.Overall though, very fun game. The downsides definitely detracted from how wonderful the experience might have been, but for such a small dev team to put out what we did get is still fantastic. I can't wait to see what they'll be able to do next, especially if they decide to increase their team size and budget for more depth in the future. Maybe they'll even add Anor Londo to the game for real this time!

_childDocuments_.review: You need to play this game. I repeat: you NEED TO PLAY THIS GAME. Take it from me, who was apprehensive about playing a soulslike games until now: if the base game is too hard for you, then that's what the assist mode is for!That said, I was able to get by just fine with the base mechanics & maintaining a balanced level of stats. The game pits you against some challenging enemies/bosses but rewards you with valuable tools like unlockable special moves, systems that allow you to keep using your favorite shells, and stowaways that give you enhanced effects. The base mechanics alone allowed me to breeze through the final boss, but I will admit it can be difficult to gauge how much/how little you want to challenge yourself once you reach the endgame.Aggro Crab even continues several traditions that they started with Going Under which includes but is not limited to: enemies based on memes, characters that are total JERKS, tongue-in-cheek humor, and—most importantly—a soul-crushing ending that alludes to the deafening reality of capitalism.The narrative has its surprises and twists, and I loved how deep it gets...both literally & figuratively. I thought that Going Under was an important critique on our crappy society, but Another Crab's Treasure takes it a step further through a crabitalist trash economy. It left me feeling devastated by the end, but it's important. REALLY really important.I cannot stress this enough. You need to play this game, even if you dont play soulslikes. Even while the devs are currently (as of writing) wrestling with post-launch bugfixes. _childDocuments_.review: I had been following this game's development for a while, and it was absolutely worth it. The moment-to-moment gameplay is fun and leaves a high skill ceiling with lot of room for mastery. It's certainly not the hardest souls-like (I beat it and still can't get past the Abyss Watchers in DS3), but it is substantially hard enough for beating the bosses to feel rewarding. There are a couple of bad bosses (Ceviche Sisters I'm looking at you), but most are fun, and some have genuine surprises to offer.Despite the game's colorful and happy appearance, the narrative goes deep and dark into themes of decay, corruption, and loss, and the ending refuses to pull its punches.

However, this game has it's own mechanics, such as using different kinds of shells for different situations and Unami abilities. It also has a skill tree, but it is not big and can be easily completed and there is no need to miss out from any of the skills to upgrade other branches, which I like better than having to choose one or the other and then not get the other path. Each boss has something unique for them, which I appreciated. The game is well made overall. One of the best souls like games I have played. _childDocuments_.review: Very fun game!  I love that the devs were able to make a souls-like that's suitable for kids as well. I don't have any young'uns currently, but the souls genre is my #1 favorite and I used to play souls games with my kiddo back when she was in her early teen years. I often wished that there were options like this back then (i.e. with a less violent take on the genre), and I think she would have loved this particular game when she was younger.  Not that it's any less fun for those of us who have seen a few more years!!  I would also like to give a huge thank you to the devs for the way that the game addresses the ongoing destruction of our underwater ecosystems.  I feel like this is something that is grossly under-represented in games today, and love the way that this game weaves these issues into the story and gameplay.   In addition to being a souls-like, this game is just a ton of fun. It's definitely more accessible than some of the other souls games, while still giving the player a challenge. _childDocuments_.review: One of the truly great indie games of our time. If you are a Souls fan, an action RPG fan, a narrative fan, there is something very special here for you. Incredibly polished, a compelling and very inventive narrative (that occasionally gets a bit heavy-handed with the point it tries to make, but steers its way back), very immersive across the board from the abilities and shell mechanics to the detailed areas themselves.My only real complaint is that there's not more of it. Only 11-ish hours to finish when removing some AFK times, but a very enjoyable 11 hours. It won't soak up huge swathes of time the way Elden Ring might, but it will be a time you don't regret taking once you're finished. Huge kudos to the dev team for making such a gem in a genre that has become more saturated in recent years.

_childDocuments_.review: Another Crab's Treasure is a fantastic 3D Platformer / "Soulslike" game that has a lot of charm and is very good value for money.It's not as complex as something like Dark Souls or Bloodborne, but it still stands beside them as a great game that tells a deep and interesting story.The entire premise of the game is just genius! - It just really works and presents a good message without feeling like that's the entire point of the game.The combat is very fun, responsive and challenging at times.The boss fights are very creative and funny. The difficulty settings are a really great idea - more games need this! (You can one-shot every boss with a gun if you want).Graphics are very stylised and fun - certainly has a cartoony / "childish" style.Quite a good amount of enemy variety, even towards the end of the game.Exploration is always rewarded with something useful or funny (No "lore notes" here).Quite a decent amount of build variety (runs deeper than you'd think, even though it's still quite simple).The Systems / mechanics aren't too overwhelming.LOTS of easter eggs / references to other games / media that doesn't feel forced.Runs very well (which is a miracle seeing as that's not been a thing with recent games).Would be nice if you could pan / zoom  the map as sometimes things you want to see are just out of view - [They added this in an update!]Some platforming sections are very tight and unforgiving, when the rest of the game is completely fine. There are a few bugs that let it down a bit:- Getting stuck in walls or on objects, resulting is having to force kill Kril from the options menu (glad they added this option).- The camera can be very awkward at times (which is a common problem with 3D Platformer games).

_childDocuments_.review: GIFTED FROM A FRIENDAnother Crab's Treasure is a very compelling Soulslike with a solid story. You're a little crab named Krill who is essentially on this quest to get his shell back, which was stolen at the start of the game. When it comes to the gameplay I really love one of the core mechanics: you can use different shells that have different weight, armor rating and spells; this gives Krill a certain versatility and makes the game a fresh/different Soulslike. Along with the shell you can also spec different charms which gives boost in attributes/certain buffs. Can't do a proper review without mentioning the bosses. All of the fights are fun and fair. However, during mid-late game things are not that difficult since you end up being quite OP in my opinion. The environmental design and layout are nice, except for some areas, which honestly are too big imo, and makes exploring a bit tedious. All in all, a solid game, and I recommend it to fans who enjoys quirky sea puns, Soulslike and a good time :-). The final boss and ending is really satisfying.8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: A combination of two of my favourite genres: collectathon platformer and dark souls/sekiro and it works fantastically. The platforming breaks up the combat and has a good balance of finding worthwhile items, something which the souls games even struggle with. The lore is fun and rewarding and the story as whole while starting off silly and an excuse for (terrible) puns evolves into a story that seethes about how we treat our planet and as you might imagine it's oceans in particular.The combat gameplay is tight and has a counter system that feels visceral and rewarding although it may take a while to get into the frame of mind to release a shoulder button for a counter if your coming off another souls like.The aesthetics while graphically relatively simple are very creative and it was fantastic seeing how trash was incorporated into character/enemy designs and moves and never failed to raise a smile.Only minor quibbles I had was outside of when silence is used for mood, I wouldn't mind more area music, the first main area has a wonderful chilled song (for some reason i find the count in very charming) but then music either fades or is used very sporadically, I would love to hear it more.Had some interesting bugs that seemed to do with standing or jumping on certain material slopes, every so often my double jumps would rocket me or i'd randomly move in a rapid figure of 8 when defending, was quite surreal but easily fixed with a quit out to the menu (though interested to see speedruns possibly do this stuff intentionally)The other issue I found was the maps are useful but have no detail nor the ability to add anything, in a game with large areas it would be nice to be able to tag things that can be unlocked later on or have at least a totals page like banjo kazooie (a game i have a sneaking suspicion that the devs have played) so you know what area that you may find new stuff in.All in all a fantastic game and in all honesty I enjoyed this game much more than Elden ring, think the bosses were challenging but not as ridiculously punishing as ER. Looking forward to hopefully a sequel or whatever else Aggro Crab have up their sleeves!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great homage/parody of the Souls-Like genre.I found the first hour or two to be the most difficult by far. The game really starts to open up once you start leveling up and gaining additional talents. The game has a Breath-of-the-Wild-like durability system, but instead of weapons, it's shells for your crab. Each shell has different defense values, durability, and a special attack. I tried rolling through almost every attack just like a Souls title, but you're intended to block ninety percent of the time. You can level up RES to increase their durability, and there are certain skills that allow you to rally shell health, and to even restore a broken shell once per life.Highly recommend if you're a fan of the Souls games.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could recommend this game, i truly do. The voice acting is cute, cut scenes are fun, and the world is interesting. Only problem is it just feels janky. Combat is frustrating and does not work as intended. Even if you make everything super easy in the assist menu, blocking only works 60% of the time as either the blocking animation itself takes too long or it just flat out decides to not block at all. The heavy attack also bugged out, forcing me to either stare passionately into my enemies eyes or it just starts light attacking multiple times. With heavy attack being a major mechanic in this game it often leads to you dying in the most frustrating ways. Enemies are also placed intentionally around edges, so if you get hit by one you will just get knocked off into an abyss and instantly die, normally this wouldn't be an issue but again because the block doesn't work and the dodge itself isn't consistent with how far it goes, you're basically just destined to die in un-fun ways. _childDocuments_.review: If you have any interest in tough-but-fair combat and these aesthetics, you should pick up Another Crab's adventure. The graphics are cute and colorful: think Finding Nemo, with a combination of cutesy and still grounded in some reality. The combat is challenging and every bit as difficult as Dark Souls. Yes, you can tone down some difficulty in the options (which is nice), but make no mistake--you will die a lot. Pretty much every "souls" mechanic is represented here, albeit in simplified form. There's bonfires, rings, i-frames, parries/ripostes, huge enemy health bars, estus/blood vials, eventual fast travel, magic and all the rest. Anyone who has played Dark Souls will be right at home. I've found the story so far to be a clever take on environmentalism and ocean life, although it's also a small part of your time. Also, it runs perfectly on the Steam Deck and doesn't take up much space. Critiques? Some of the open areas are same-y and I got lost sometimes. There's a lot of verticality and sometimes I found it hard to know when an enemy could hit me on a slightly different plane. There's really just one weapon and moveset. Voice acting quality ran the gamut from hilarious/frightening to whomever-is-in-the-office-today-amateur. Apart from some gripes, this is an insta-buy for anyone with interest in the genre. Kudos to the devs for successfully making their own take on the formula, when others have completely failed. My hope is that the cute graphics draw new players to the genre--to show that it's rewarding and fun to face tough challenges. Buy yourself some Crab Souls.

_childDocuments_.review: A genuinely excellent soulslike in all aspects, I give it a 9/10. Completely caught me off-guard. If you like soulslikes, just get this game. It's got great combat, great level design, and a very satisfying story. The humor is consistently on-point with jokes basically everywhere, from the actual character dialogue to the item descriptions. The story was also surprisingly compelling. Without spoiling too much, this is much more than just a "funny crab game".The combat strikes that perfect old-school "Dark Souls 1" balance of simple but satisfying. Enemies aren't flying around doing 20 hit combos like in Elden Ring. The enemy does a couple attacks, you do a couple attacks, and it repeats.This game makes blocking a first-class-citizen, however, and as a result the combat has quite a lot of depth when it comes to defense. You can block, parry, or dodge basically any attack which gives the player a ton of choice for optimizing each encounter. The 'shell' variety (basically your shield) is also really fun to play around with.The difficulty curve is a little all-over-the-place. Early game was perfect, midgame was very easy, endgame alternated between punishingly difficult and pretty easy. Despite that, it's still a satisfying experience.The skill tree is super fun, with tons of really fun, consistently useful abilities. There's also a surprising amount of 'build customization' despite the fact that there's only one main weapon.The levels are consistently interesting to navigate. The ideal soulslike often involves exploring and navigating a big level with branching paths and shortcuts, so pairing this with the 3D platforming genre just feels natural.I didn't personally run into any gamebreaking bugs, but I do recommend you back-up your save file periodically as a decent number of folks on the steam forums have mentioned some save file-related issues.There were a few enemies that felt more annoying than fun to fight, but outside of that I think this game is amazing.It's the perfect length too; Took about 13 hours to finish, and I explored probably half of the optional areas. There's probably at least 3-5 more hours of content left that I missed.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished “Another Crab’s Treasure”. 16 hours. All achievements. Here’s my review. The Good:- ACT is an indie game full of passion and love. The developers clearly put a lot of love into this game. The environments are fun. The characters are hilarious. Overall, it’s exactly what you’d expect as an indie-souls-like game.- The story itself is hilarious and quite whimsical. I found myself smiling often at reactions or certain story beats. The ending was not at all what I expected and exceeded expectations.- This game is a souls-like experience and the combat shows. There’s your typical parries, dodges, blocks, melee attacks and more. If you get hit, it hurts. When you beat bosses, it feels amazing. The combat versus a singular enemy is top notch. Against multiple enemies…? More on that later.- This games unique mechanic are shells. You find shells scattered across the world and each shell has a unique ability. This is a rafter neat mechanic  and I enjoyed using multiple shells. My favorite is a Coffee Mug that, when used, increases your attack and movement speed until it wears off.- For a souls-like game, I wasn’t expecting the load of accessibility options. You can make the game much easier or simply tweak one or two settings for a better experience. I turned off fall damage (more on this later).The Ugly:- Combat versus multiple enemies really just turns into a chore. Most enemies will swoop in, hit you, then run away. It’s annoying to face multiples as you’re often chasing after one (due to your pitiful melee range) only to be smacked by another.- The game seriously lacks direction. There’s one section where the map is grayed out and the zone is dark. This area took me two hours to navigate, what really should have been 30 minutes. The map itself is beautifully drawn and I just wished I could have set waypoints. If the game put markers on your map showing a general direction, it would have been a huge quality of life improvement.- The lack of direction really shines with platforming sections. Often times you could fall and drop 2-4 stories requiring repeating sections multiple times. Other times, you’d barely miss a jump and fall to your death. I’m certain most of my deaths were from falling.. which is why I turned off fall damage.- The combat-to-leveling curve was unreal. I was stuck at one boss and when I looked up how to beat him, the suggested level was 40 and I was 12. This was the second major boss in the game. Thus, I began to grind. That’s when I realized there’s no solid way to farm levels in this game. I spent 4 (out of my 16 hours) grinding levels. Eventually I just stopped. By the end of the game I was level 51 and would still get 2-shot by some enemies. I killed every enemy along my path. The curve just didn’t keep up with the pace and diffuclty of enemies.Overall, I enjoyed the game a lot. For an indie title, I’d give it a solid 8.5 out of 10. Comparing it to similar AAA titles, it would sit at around a 6 out of 10. I also didn't realize this game was on GamePass. I paid full price for it and do not regret my purchase. However, it's definitely worth playing if you have GamePass or catch it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was decent. It wasn't anything spectacular, but it was still good. I enjoyed the combat system (besides a few specific parts that I'll mention), the story was actually really good, and I think this has some of the best humor I've seen in a majority of games.One issue I do have with it though is level design. A lot of the time it feels like areas have enemies just spammed everywhere with no rhyme or reason, which means you get overwhelmed very often!-----Minor Spoilers-----One thing I don't like about the combat however, is that a lot of it is based off of parrying your opponent's attacks (or at least that's what it seemed like from my playthrough). For a majority of bosses, they have at least one attack that can't be blocked or parried, and you need to dodge away from. This alone is fine. But when it's not fine is when there's a boss or two that have a majority of their attacks be completely unblockable! And I'm not talking about any hardcore endgame boss, the boss that gave me the most trouble with this issue specifically was a miniboss in one of the first areas of the game. It was legitimately harder than every other boss in the game for me.-----Major Spoilers-----Another criticism I have is for the game's ending. It's just kind of... underwhelming. There's not really any resolve, and most of the usual "happy ending" stuff happens off-screen. Not to mention there's not really any post-game content, which is a bit of a shame.Overall, I give it a 6/10. Nothing groundbreaking, but it could've been worse.
