_childDocuments_.review: Another Crab's Treasure is an amazing addition to the souls-like genre, and is never afraid to break the mold (or in this case, shell) of so many of its predecessors.The world is alive, colorful, and extremely humorous. The level design is more traditional, in the sense that each zone is its own separated by loading screens. The levels have a seamless flow between combat and platforming, with bite-size branching paths that always provide meaningful rewards and satisfying secrets (or even enemies). The character and enemy designs, paired with extremely committed performances from voice actors, show how much this title is a product of passion and creativity. This is all backed up by extremely satisfying movement, combat, and encounters that fit well together, albeit a little clunky at times. I do believe Aggro Crab were a little too afraid to let the player sequence break, and thus I was left a little wanting with some movement options (mainly the aerial attack and aerial dodge).Aggro Crab use their resources well, many unimportant characters are given a gray silhouettes during dialogue interactions, while characters with influence and pull over the world have amazing portrait art with a variety of emotes and text flairs that make them truly stand out in your mind. I have pretty bad ADHD, and getting me to read text box after text box is a huge stretch goal for games like these, but you bet your ass I'm taking my time and reading through all the dialogue of the characters that have won over my heart. Each zone feels unique and its own, and even if there are some reused assets or move sets, you never notice it. Each boss and miniboss has its own scavenged and forged weapons they use that fit perfectly in the world, and each grapple that one shots me (I get hit by these a lot :P) has a unique animation and personality to it.Finally the mechanics. Aggro Crab follow a game design philosophy I heavily agree with, and that's focus on ONE unique mechanic, and make it as fleshed out as possible. Another Crab's Treasure takes the traditional souls combat and turns it on its head by bringing your "off hand weapon" in as the focus of most creative builds in the form of your shell. While so many games focus on a variety of unique weapons, ACT focuses on you shield, your defensive options, and turning that on your enemy in pivotal moments of gaining the upper hand. Each shell has a defensive stat, its own health pool, and a unique ability (spell) that goes along with this. Kril (the character you play as) is even able to retreat into his shell while sprinting in order to roll at high speeds for moments of insanely fun traversal. There are only 4 base stats to focus on while leveling, making committing to a build extremely simple and straightforward, while perfecting a build become a fun dance of stats, shells, and stowaways (additional items that boost stats or given unique affects, such as stagger damage or life steal).I had just replayed Hallow Knight before this, and I have no problem comparing Aggro Crab with Team Cherry. There is a lot that goes into indie game design, and I'm so glad they were able to get this game out there and talked about enough to see it succeeding as it is. I remember originally seeing this games demo on Iron Pineapples channel, and whatever Aggro Crab is doing, they should keep it up! There is so much to say about this game and what it does right, and if I had more time, I would have said less. I hope this review was helpful, and I hope Aggro Crab sees this just so they know how much people can appreciate a game like this.I give Another Crab's Treasure: All The Microplastics In My Bloodstream / 10

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I beat the game on the hardest difficulty (default mode) and beat every boss in less than 2-10 tries.. Game is INCREDIBLY easy if you know how to parry, so if you want it to be hard then don't parry LOL. Also, I didn't even find out there was a gun or easy mode until after the final boss. I also got 95% of the achievements without any guides, so there's not much hidden, which is good btw, thank god they don't make you beat the game no death cause i would've definitely done that lmao. Anyways, time for an actual review...I love this game, incredibly unique take on a "soulslike", coupled with its equally unique take on trash and the ocean. I thought this was a satirical game, it was funny all the way through, especially near the ending when i can finally beat up that stupid prawn. I was NOT expecting the story to be so deep and introspective. It had a whole overarching lesson of leaving your comfort zone and learning your place in a vast world. You're not useless, you find your own purpose, I LOVE that. The combat itself is also very simple, but very effective. You can have cool timed dodge counters and parries, and doing them makes you feel badass af, but they also make the game a bit easy (assuming you have the reaction time of a rhythm gamer lmao)I think this game can be more compared to sekiro. It had a somewhat similar world-design, same weapon, and a mechanic that is somewhat similar to the prosthetic (adaptations and shells), and PARRYING. Honestly, some of the attacks felt too fast for the roll dodge. I only parried cause it was fun af though. This is still a soulslike, it has all the level design aspects, enemy and item placement, and even the worldbuilding lore of an inectionThese are just my minor critiques and these aren't gamebreaking. I just encountered these and would like to point them out.- I love the combat, but it is inherently very simple. This is through my personal playthrough, so take it with a grain of salt. The shell abilities were generally underwhelming, which just led me to using the first adaptation in the game, which delt EXCEPTIONAL damage. On max level, you can just destroy bosses after stunlock parrying them. - A lot of the bosses only had 3-5 attacks. Just an observation.- First off, although i like the level design, there is A LOT of walking. There's not that much travel time though and there's plenty of checkpoints, but there's a lot of cases where i just don't feel like walking back to the moon shells and just pressing "die instantly."- There are actually quite a few collision bugs. Frequently, Kril and the bosses fling around. I fall through floors and walls after getting hit or doing abilities. This only happened a few times though. There's also some cases where simply touching some environment will get you stuck or killed. You can fall in one of those deathfall areas and just keep spawning in it over and over. _childDocuments_.review: So I've got a confession to make.  I don't like soulsbournes.  Locking a game into a specific difficulty and then making that difficulty obnoxiously, unfairly hard is stupid.  I see your oncoming GIT GUD and preemptively counter with no u.Then along comes Another Crab's Treasure, the most accessible and customizable soulsbourne I've ever seen.  As an added bonus: you play as the cutest little hermit crab on the verge of snapping that you'll ever see in a videogame!One part Battle For Bikini Bottom and one part Elden Ring, the game is a brightly-colored environmental disaster that is fun to navigate and play.  Combat is smooth, as is platforming.  The story knows its Fromsoftware roots well; it can be silly, it can be freaky, it can be sweet, it can be frightening.  As mentioned before, you can make the game as tough or as easy as you want.  There's other little options that show the devs just wanted to make a game that was fun for players to discover.  You can equip a one-hit KO gun and its the funniest thing.  You can pat a lil fish buddy and its the cutest thing.  You can swap out all sorts of memey shells and its the greatest thing.  And I mentioned the story but I want to repeat: the story is very well-crafted with some great twists and turns carried along by very nice voice acting.I've been following the development of this game for awhile, and I am so glad to see how the final result turned out.  This is the best aquatic game to release this year, as well as the best soulsbourne game and the best conservation-minded game.  Kind of a weird set of bases to cover, but the game was designed for a weird set of people so it all works out.

_childDocuments_.review: A great, wholesome souls-like with a story that poses compelling commentary on modern society and ecological activism. I highly recommend this to everyone.It's not perfect by any means, but it's got a lot to love! It's somewhat early since 1.0 now so some complaints of mine may get fixed later on. Here's my suggestions on things to improve:1. Map - Currently you can only view a small area of the region map around your current location. I'd suggest letting you see the entire map of whatever region you're in, perhaps including other regions you've already visited. Other souls-likes and open world RPGs implement fast-travel in the map, but I think the requirement to use the moon snail shells (campfires) is better because it adds difficulty to get to them despite enemies/environment, while the rest of this game makes general gameplay easy enough for the average gamer. I also don't think it'd be good for this game to require the map to be collected from a location like other RPGs do. This game's excels at being an accessible souls-like so no need to make it more complex than it needs to be. There's also a big chunk of the story that is collecting pieces of a map, so being able to collect one completely and collect another in pieces would be jarring.2. Stats - Currently the only way to view what stats your entire build has (level points, stowaways, and fork level) is to manually tally them up. The fork level isn't even shown, merely how the fork looks indicates it's level. The only stats shown easily are only the points you use after each level up, but these points also don't match the character stats (x dmg level points = x% dmg = ? dmg value). While further clarity on all build stats is useful, I'd also like a toggle to see real-time stats on HP and shell armor in battle. More info means more informed decisions, which means less player frustration and more enjoyment from optimization (but not too much bc that can ruin a game).3. Stowaways - I don't think there's any need to change the existing systems for stowaways (enemy drops, selling for microplastics, capped stowaway capacity, etc). However, I would love to see an ability to combine multiple stowaways of the same kind into a higher tier of the same stowaway. This would help players have access to more higher tier stowaways and not require repetitive enemy grinding or exhaustive game wikis for item locations.4. _childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of souslikes, but why do they all have to take place in a dreary and depressing fantasy world? Why not a dreary and depressing  world instead? A... shoals-like.Enter: Another Crab's Treasure. You play as a hermit crab whose shell was "repossessed". Without a shell, you're squishy and pathetic. You live in a vast ocean littered with human trash, so you grab whatever is around you for protection. Unlike armor in other games, "shells" are very disposable and have unique abilities-- your shell is expected to break in the middle of a battle, forcing you to constantly adapt; switching from a sturdy coconut shell with the ability to roll into enemies at high speeds until it finally breaks, forcing you to make do with a flimsy banana peel that you can munch on to heal a little.  Another thing that separates Crab Souls from other soulslikes is the platforming. In this game, you can jump, "float", use a grappling hook, and roll down hills to gain a speed boost. You can use these to retreat or reposition in fights, but also to find secret shells and other collectibles. That said, my favorite thing about this game is just looking around. The devs had tons of fun with the trash, using it almost like a Lego set. A receipt used as a bridge, a maze from the back of a cereal box being confused for a "treasure map", makeshift bows made out of rubber bands + toothpicks, etc. It's constantly creative.Overall, this game makes itself impossible not to love. It's got good story, humor, platforming, combat, worldbuilding, and tons of charm.

After overcoming these difficult skill checks, there should be more of a celebration than the boss slowly fading away to give you a better sense of achievement. _childDocuments_.review: Another heavy hitter from Aggro Crab. The world they've built here is something to be proud of.In a society constructed from the trash and microplastics we leave behind, these creatures watch pollution slowly consuming the only world they've ever known. There's so much of Aggro Crab's trademark heart and humor layered into the story, that sometimes it's easy to lose sight of the darker themes bubbling beneath the surface. The story executes on this perfectly.The combat iterates on the soulslike framework more than enough to stand on its own. The more technical hallmarks of the genre like complex stat builds and magic systems have been streamlined to make them more approachable, while still offering the challenging action fans of the genre enjoy. The shell mechanic starts out seeming to be a simple shield system, but the rate at which you are swapping them out, and how parrying is tied to the timing make it feel like a central mechanic - and not just a way to prevent damage.I really enjoyed this game, and think the ending hit home pretty hard. _childDocuments_.review: Someone took crab jokes too far and made a game - unfortunately.You play the role of a hermit crab who got his shell stolen and is going on an adventure to get it back. It doesn’t take him long to realise that the ocean is much different than he remembered - trash is all over the place and other habitants embraced it as technological advancement. This setting and exploration are the only things that did not make me flush this abomination of a game. It’s aesthetically pleasing to look at and the locations themselves are interesting enough to make you want to explore them as much as you want.But the game tried its best to make this as good as the Borderlands movie. Constant jank is making you either skip platforms or barely reach them even if you do parkourking correctly. Movement is so inconsistent you never know when movement gamba clicks to drain your sanity.With movement comes combat with weird camera. Why is it weird? It’s placed so behind your character it looks more like only fans showcase rather than fighting scene. Enemies you fight are quickly becoming repetitive; it feels more like a chore than a challenge.But let me tell you about the core of combat - parrying. Couple of games did that very well, but Another Crap’s Treasure devs decided they need to be original and you have to release the block button rather than pressing it. This absolutely counter-intuitive design makes the core of this joke of a trash-fencing your least optimal option. I found that your best bet is just brute forcing your way with massive damage to avoid game mechanics completely.But let's say you want to parry. Like you can expect - enemies have their bar you need to fill by either parrying or damaging to knock them off. So what is your reward? Free combo lmao. Yes, only a few free hits or one “special” hit that is making this effort barely worth it. Of course you need to unlock it first by reaching the end of a skill tree.And lore? Plot? Characters? Game is trying to send out a very mature message about polluting our planet, about mindless consumptionism. However, that is constantly demolished by low quality zoomer dad jokes that are vastly exceeding the highway speed limit. Every serious situation is destroyed by a joke that gets old after 69th time and characters are either with a very toxic or very childish mentality (with a few decent exceptions). This also includes our protagonist. Every harem anime shounen protagonist is a top-notch character compared to our crab, who keeps being just dumber and dumber with every cutscene. Even the final boss is some random-ass npc.I don’t even know if this game tries to be a satire, serious or just a product of some very bad acid trip. If there is any message this game tries to deliver, there is definitely one - sometimes it’s just not worth it. In this game, it was not worth it playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: A really good game that maybe doesn't quite stick the landing.  I think it's the perfect game for somebody interested in Souls games but maybe turned off by the amount of time you need to waste to learn some Souls bosses.I was nervous coming off of (the superior, imo) Nine Sols that I was getting sucked into another grind but the game wound up being about just right for me.  I got stuck on a few bosses for a bit but it was nothing I couldn't handle.  Like another reviewer, I went all in on my Attack stat at the expense of everything else and it paid off.  I had a lot of fun being a glass cannon who could blaze through bosses if I pulled off my parries correctly.The story is fairly quirky and goes places you wouldn't expect.  There's basically three major arcs, with the middle one being the largest portion of the game, but you wouldn't anticipate there being so much to do from the start of the game.  It's kind of like Okami in that regard.  You go up against the Big Bad, asking yourself "was that it?" and then it turns out that was only the beginning!  This game is much shorter than Okami though; nearly finishing 100% of it (did not get every Shell but did all the things to do) I clocked in at 20 hours.The story starts off with some heavy libertarian themes as Big Government comes for your character's home and he can't pay the necessary taxes to get it back.  But much of the game feels more like a critique of libertarianism.  Your character's desire to just live alone and not worry about other people really comes into question, and the direction they go with it is pretty dark.  I would read it as sort of a cautionary tale about libertarianism (or maybe materialism).  The main character made me think a little of Shinji from Neon Genesis Evangelion, in that he clearly does not want to be a part of anything and the game shows the toll that takes on him.But, the ending (after you lose control of the character) is IMO completely at odds with the entire rest of the game.  Almost like you completed the bad ending but got the good ending cutscene.  And that really sours what could have been a very thought-provoking tale.Another fault I had with the game was its soundtrack.  It does its job, but it's no Ecco the Dolphin: Defenders of Time (to reference a game with a similar setting).  The title theme takes on new meaning later in the game, which I thought was very cool.  But otherwise, the songs are pleasant but unremarkable.I played it months after release and did have to suffer some unfortunate bugs that cost me some Souls.  On occasion, I would die and go back to where my Souls should be (they are called "Microplastics" in this game, which is great) only to find nothing there.  The map marker still said they should be there, but they weren't.  Also, while the map itself is fine, the markers for the fast travel points changed location every time I opened the map.  I had to just memorize in my head where they actually were located in the game.  I played on PC, for reference.I'd give it a low 8/10, I think the gameplay is probably my favorite take on a Souls game and the story is much deeper than expected but it all leads to nothing and the audio experience doesn't meet its potential.  I can see why some people really love the game and I think it deserves much of the praise.

_childDocuments_.review: Another Crab's Treasure ♥♥♥♥♥♥ rocks. It understands its inpirations but knows when to deviate and do its own thing. I cannot wait for the next Aggro Crab game, and will be playing this one happily in the years to come.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This is a cute mix of the style of Spongebob Battle For Bikini Bottom with the gameplay of Fromsoft's souls games. It's a fun game with flaws, but it's worth your time if you're a soulslike fan or if you are interested in the quaint art style.You journey as a small hermit crab through a trash-ridden ocean and fight against sea creatures that have succumbed to pollution by attacking with a fork and using the powers of makeshift trash shells. Though there are some interesting twists on traditional soulslike mechanics such as the shells, the game is a pretty traditional reskin of soulslike gameplay: You play through sections of platforming and fighting smaller enemies, you'll fight large, creative bosses and collect microplastics (souls/currency) to level up and purchase other upgrades.  Despite the cutesy look of the game, it can be very challenging, but it is still quite accessible with a substantial set of difficulty adjustment settings so that newer players can play at a level that is just right for them.What I did like:The strongest parts of the game for me were definitely the art-style, world design, and gameplay. The developers chose an art style that is going to age very well. It's cute, cartoony, and the cast of characters is very huggable. It reminds me heavily of 2000's platformer games like Battle for Bikini Bottom, Psychonauts, and Ratchet and Clank. Those games may be dated, but the look of them is so endearing and they capture my imagination. I can picture myself saying the same thing in 20 some years about Another Crab's Treasure.The world design isn't immaculate like some of the souls games, but I love the way that the world looks. You are in an ocean with a city made of trash. The buildings are made of cereal boxes. The benches are made of playing cards. The roads are made with those insanely long receipts you get from CVS. It's so creative and I couldn't help myself but smile seeing all of the choices the developers made to create the environment. While the hub area is a bit big and disjointed for the limited amount of things you can do in it, it's still fun to just lost for a bit.The gameplay is solid. It doesn't quite feel as weighty as Fromsoft's souls games, but everything feels right.Okay, now for what I didn't like:My main complaint about Another Crab's Treasure is the writing. It can be a bit funny at times, but you can tell the game is written by self-indulgent, bleeding heart environmentalist millenials/gen Zs. I don't have a problem if you want your game to make people ask interesting questions and ponder humanity's pollution of the ocean. In fact, please do. That's an interesting subject. However, the game forces its serious points through realizing its villains (the destroyers of the ocean) as comically straw-manned evil businessmen/confederate plantation owners, and cyptobros. The game flat-out says that revolutionary violence and anger towards people you can classify this way is justified, which is definitely giving "I'm a member of antifa". It's embarrassingly lacking nuance and disappointing when everything else in this game is so great and inspires so much awe. If you want someone to consider your viewpoint and messaging, insulting the people who need to hear your message the most is the worst thing you can do.Other than the annoyingly blunt messaging and poorly realized villains, I wish there was more voice acting. We really only get voice acting for major cutscenes and no other part of the game, so it starts to feel weird when we do get it. I forgot what characters sounded like due to how infrequently I actually heard them speak. I understand if this is just for budget reasons, but I can't help but mention it.All of that being said, Aggrocrab set out to make an absolutely huge game for their second project and they did a great job. Even if I don't like how they implement their writing, what they have done here is not an easy thing and they should be praised and paid for it. I have played Going Under as well and enjoyed that too! I'm looking forward to hearing more from them.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid fundamentals, a fun aesthetic, endearing characters and an actually effecting story (wasn't expecting that) make this a more then worthwhile experience. It's not particularly difficult and has options for decreasing difficulty so is truly accessible to any and all levels of skill. Some negatives are bugs that are semi-consistent (items and attacks clipping through geometry, a bizarre bug where you go flying up into the air seemingly at random, and some enemies pathing breaking). In terms of a souls-like the enemy variety is low and difficult, complex fights only really come around in some of the later game bosses (and a few early game bosses if you attempt them early). On the whole though I would definitely recommend this as a fun game that is easy to pick up and not a huge investment (particularly if you don't spend a few hours searching for the 2 stainless steal forks you're missing like I did). Oh also I'd like to see the map improved, like actually being able to move around it or leave markers for some of the stuff you need to come back to.

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal 'souls-like', though 'Hollowknight-like' might be a better descriptor.While the player only has a single weapon to use, with a simple attack pattern, the flexibility that comes from the Shell Spells, Adaptations, and Stowaways means that there are multiple fun and end-game viable builds, including pure attack focused, and pure Adaptation focused, and anything in between.  While the platforming has some rough edges, with inputs sometimes seemingly not received, or a few jumps(steps really) being a little too high to comfortably reach, it does add a lot of joy to the game, especially chaining together grappling hook shots.  This also aides in the fun of exploration, as there are a good number of optional paths to take that lead to useful treasures.I also love the art style, with both the environments and characters being charming, and their use of trash to create the world looks fantastic.  I adored the storytelling and narrative itself in the game, the combination of a tale about the downfalls of capitalism and the damage we do to the Earth was done in a non-preachy way, and the laughs along the way were great.  Of course, the faux products add to this joy, with 'unfathomable meat' being my personal favorite.My only real complaint with the game, outside of some platforming gripes, were the limited enemy types, but I definitely understand the pain of adding new enemies, and even FromSoft re-uses enemies a ton, so it's really a nitpick!All in all, a great, 9/10 game for me personally, definitely worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: the lovechild of the classic 3d platformers of the gamecube/PS2 era with a soulslike combat system. And the two compliment eachother better than you'd expect, especially when Aggrocrab is doing the mixing. At it's best the combat feels almost like a rhythm game, action and reaction. Winning runs against bosses felt almost like performances--the earlier attempts was learning the choreo, now it was time to put on the show. This is effect is helped by the relatively small attack set. Because there's a relatively small pool of attack animations, enemy attack patterns can be tightened in a way that makes every encounter feel like an edge of your seat dance along the edge of death. Which is when soulslike combat is at its peak, in my humble opinion.The platforming is also masterfully done, the world design has a sprawling feel to it that begs you to explore its every nook and cranny, and the exploration moveset makes traversing these environments a joy in me that allows this game to stand tall among the other giants of this genre. Aside from just being fun, Aggrocrab managed to reward my exploration in a way that made had every corner piquing my curiosity. Just when I'd come to expect the umami crystals and various bits of trash, I weaved my way around several brute-type enemies to scoop up another bread-claw, only to find that my received an upgrade to a much more precious resource than trash. Every fight is made worth it.I wholeheartedly recommend Another Crab's Treasure to anyone who loves exploration, and doesn't mind dying a few dozen times while learning the choreography.
_childDocuments_.name: Another Crab's Treasure

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very linear soulslike game. It's not as difficult as the average soulslike, but it's still pretty challenging if you're not into this subgenre. Nice variety of enemies.Combat is very simple but feels ok, skill tree is meaningful, and I like the build variety.Great game if you just wanna chill but still have somewhat of a challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: No I-frames while riposting.Successful parrying requires you to parry about eight frames before the attack connects.Every enemy has poise. You do not.Most minbosses and bosses prefer to keep distance between you and them when you have very few, if any, ways to close the distance.Dodges are very short and don't provide enough I-frames.Enemy damage seems completely random at times. Sometimes you get killed in two shots, sometimes it's in five. Doesn't matter what shell you're wearing.The devs added a whole 'accessibility' page in the settings to let you tweak the game so you can 'have fun your way', like giving you a gun to one shot every enemy if you're a games journalist. It's not a bad idea, but here's a better one for you Aggro Crab; if you're gonna make a game in a very oversaturated genre, based on one of the most flawed gems in gaming history, you should learn the lessons the original had to do the hard way.Overall: 4/10. Decent humor and colorful world weighed down by clunky, Dark Souls 1-esque combat and controls.

_childDocuments_.review: If I had a nickel for every indie crab game that I enjoyed, I'd have 2 nickels, which is strange but it's exactly what happened.1. Combat is decent, but parrying takes the limelight. Whoever thought of hermit crabs "peekabooing" out of their shells needs a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ raise!3. Exploration is well done. It's not open world (thank god) but big enough for an abundance of upgrade materials. However, those hooks are getting really annoying ngl 4. The dialogue is pretty funny ngl, really breaks the trope of dark souls NPC dialogue "oh (insert another obscure NPC name), forgive me"However, there are several criticisms of the game:1. Whonky combat. The final hit on your light attack combo has a longer animation than expected, which means I can't dodge attacks even tho I pressed the dodge button after executing the final hit. That inconvenience has costed me many boss attempts...2. Terrible platforming. I died to the cardboard way more than any boss I've defeated mainly because I somehow glitch through the cardboard itself, even enemies did that ♥♥♥♥...Although I had 2 main criticisms, the game's still solid and I am still enjoying it at the time of writing. _childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - Decent game, but a lot of people are forgiving how immensely rough around the edges it is because it's charming and cute and a Soulslike that isn't just a bunch of corpses and rock and dirt. Gave it a 3/5 on Backloggd I've been way too busy to do a deep write-up on this game. The short version is this was one of the more deeply flawed games I've stuck out until the end credits. It has a good heart, and the spirit of what it's trying to do is all in the right place, but honestly, I only finished it because I'm considering doing some analysis of Soulslike combat design at some point in the future, and this is a marked example of something that misunderstands some core principles of what makes those games work in spite of their frustrations and difficulty. Don't let the fact that this game is cute trick you, this is as mean and rude, if not more so, as any Fromsoft game.There is just so much obnoxious behavior in this game, particularly concerning how many enemy hits turn your character into a flying physics object to be thrown off of ledges or across the arena. The only thing that offsets the awful difficulty design is the fact that the player is, in turn, granted some incredibly overpowered abilities without a hint of balance behind them, making it so you can easily spam and tank your way through everything. The best elements of combat have "the juice," as it were, though the roll-out shell spell was so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good compared to everything else that I never used any other shells after I got it! The worst elements irritated me through at least a third of the game's run time.Their economy balance is also pretty weird; you can max out all the upgrades in the game with like ~60% of the limited crystals available. Maybe that's good, I don't know. It certainly fully disincentivizes finding all of that currency -- even as a completionist, and even given the fact that they show you exactly how much is in each zone on the fast-travel page -- but there's just too much of it.People hype up the story a lot. It's fine. It has a lot of character, but it didn't make me feel anything or get invested. A lot of the dialog is just too by-the-numbers smarmy indie-game-core without enough substance for me to really care. The way it progresses is pretty straightforward and obvious, they foreshadow everything about it well enough, but it's also kind of incoherent in terms of themes. I mean, the themes are clear, there are just several that have not a lot to do with each other and rely on a kind of cartoon logic while also trying to feel super sad and serious at the same time. Then again, I'm also on record feeling literally nothing about anything Fromsoft has ever done with story or worldbuilding, so anything inspired by that foundation, even if written more clearly, I probably find boring by association. "Ah, the world is in decay, and everyone's sad." OK. Lastly, the fact that the player can't scroll around the map UI is garbage. Just...absolutely trash. Do not give a player a map that is so zoomed in they can't actually see anything other than what they could already see without a map. Absolutely flabbergasting decision. Conclusion: I wouldn't say DON'T play this game if it looks cool to you. It has good elements, and people less nitpicky than me seem to love it, but don't go in expecting a polished experience in any regard. It's rougher around the edges than any game I've finished in the last 15 years (including tons of indie and AA games).Combat Design: 6/10Level Design: 6/10Music: 8/10Story: 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game, and I thoroughly enjoyed. It's more reminiscent of Sekiro than Dark Souls, which is fine. The game is very funny and comedic, while still having a plucky, compelling protagonist. The graphics are a little generic and flat some of the time, though there are also some genuinely awesome ideas, especially the character designs. The crabs with phones and laser eyes are a particular favorite of mine. I also really enjoy the shell variety, lots of creativity on display. I also appreciate some of the messaging about environmentalism, crabitalism and liberalism. I also like the references, very fun. The combat is a bit mind-numbing sometimes. You can get really intentional with parrying and dodges, but you can also just whack most enemies to deaths mindlessly. The music is really good. No tracks stand out in particular, but it definitely modulates tones and establishes atmosphere very effectively. Overall, I'd highly recommend it to soulslike fans and casual gamers alike. 9/10P.S. I'm coming because after the updates fixed a lot of balances issues and jank, I think it earned another point. 10/10 for developer commitment.

_childDocuments_.review: Another Crab's Treasure is a game that baits you with its cute graphics, adorable world design with funny references and puns galore. Shortly afterwards, it becomes apparent that there's a clear message here about climate change and the forces that drive it. It's so on the nose that by the time you're hooked on the fun gameplay you don't really stop to consider it. You get what the game is trying to say and it starts to flow over you. However, by the time you reach one of the last areas of the game, a major plot twist is revealed. For me, this is where I realised that the devs have done something ingenious. They've been spoonfeeding these little tidbits of commentary in a digestible form and then at the end it asks you what you've learnt - and there's so much to take away. It's shockingly impressive how the writers have managed to seamlessly transition the story from "they took muh shell away" to making you consider how one can live a normal life with a looming threat of apocalypse.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game because I had seen some of accessibility stuff like giving Kril, the main character, a gun that just one shots everything. Seemed like a cool studio. The game was really, really good. Lots of funny references and light humor, while still allowing itself to be serious at times. Plenty of references and inspirations from the Dark Souls games, which were fun to see in action. This game gives you options, like in your choice of shell, but doesn't overwhelm you. It keeps things simple where it counts. Unlike Souls games, the way to progress is very clear, and the story is easy to follow without pulling up a Wiki on a second monitor. Great game, 10/10, strongly recommend to anyone looking to try a Souls-like game
_childDocuments_.name: Another Crab's Treasure

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible. Absolutely in the category of must-play Soulslikes along with Lies of P. It is NOT super easy like I was scared it might be, and it has some really interesting innovations that set it apart from the Souls games, Elden Ring, and Sekiro. Highly entertaining writing as well. It's so much more than just crab punsI don't listen to soundtracks in my free time, but I'm considering buying it just to support the devs more. These guys are great and deserve every penny of full price. The hours have just been flying by in this gameEdit: I have now 100%'d the game. Definitely could have taken another couple hours exploring if I wanted to, but I think my ~20 hours is a decent baseline if you're wondering how long the game is. My opinion of it has not changed at all. This is an amazing game. One of the most fun soulslike classics of all time.The end of the game does get fairly easy, however. It turns into a bit of a boss rush like the ends of Souls games, but it took no more than two tries for each boss. My final level allocations were 20-20-20-0 at level 60 and I really didn't do any grinding.

_childDocuments_.review: This game proves something that I have been preaching for years: A souls-like doesn't NEED a story but it can be IMPROVED with a story!But even outside of that, this is a great game. I love all the character and enemy-designs, combat and bossfigths feel satisfying(and this will come across as herresy, but I honestly prefer bossfigths in this game over Fromsofts stuff. Am I in the minority with that? Maybe. But it's the truth for me).It even gives u a good reason to kill a lot of the minor enemys at least once, because there is a certain upgrade-currency u can only get from enemys with glowing eyes(they no longer glow after u have killed them once), which is a simple yet ingenious solution to ye age old "why am I not just running past things?" question. Sure, if I have to retread my steps I will probably still try to avoid a lotta enemys, but it's nice that there is a good reason to actually figth most things the first time u go through an area.And lastly, the meat of the game, the combat. This game really mixes up the base-souls-combat with a lot of it's mechanics, like the shells, the magic(or rather "umami")-system and so on. I havent quite finished it yet, but so far I am having a great time and I doubt thats gonna change in the last area anymore.2024 has been a great year for indiegames and Another Crabs Treasure is one of the contributers to that!
_childDocuments_.name: Another Crab's Treasure

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that doesn't do any one thing particularly well, but the whole package adds up to something greater and more memorable than the sum of its parts. The combat, while true to the Souls template, leaves something to be desired, though the platforming is admittedly pretty good. The music and general atmosphere are put together well, and the NPC dialogue is definitely a highlight. Everything put together produces a truly fun and memorable experience; it's only when you look any single element in a vacuum that you notice the faults. As a souls vet and comedy connoisseur, this game has made me laugh and smile a lot so far, and I will likely update this after I finish the game.

name: Paper Trail
detailed_description: Paper Trail is a top-down puzzle adventure about leaving home, set in a foldable, paper world. You play as Paige, a budding academic, leaving home for the first time to pursue her studies. On the journey, you learn to fold the world, merging two sides to solve puzzles, explore new areas and uncover long-lost secrets. Fold the world, one page at a time What feels simple at first, folding and joining paths together to explore and progress, quickly becomes devilishly tricky! Alter the fabric of your world, contorting, spinning, rotating, twisting around - as you try to untangle the puzzle of the Paper Trail . Engaging puzzles, intriguing people Solve puzzles that challenge your wits and bring you through the world of Paper Trail. Travelling through the folds will introduce Paige to a unique cast of characters, who tell their stories and enlighten Paige about the wider world. Handcrafted beautiful environments From deep dark caves that have been untouched for years to the tallest treetops buffeted by rain. Explore a variety of handcrafted environments as Paige makes her journey to University, taking in the sights and wonders as she goes. You play as Paige, a budding academic, leaving home for the first time to pursue her studies. Fold the world, one page at a time What feels simple at first, folding and joining paths together to explore and progress, quickly becomes devilishly tricky! Alter the fabric of your world, contorting, spinning, rotating, twisting around - as you try to untangle the puzzle of the Paper Trail . _childDocuments_.review: Puzzle game, nature, successful atmosphere, exploration, full of color.PLOT The young Paige, an aspiring astrophysicist, lives in Papirea, a small village overlooking the sea; The age has now come for her to decide what to do with her life, her choice falls on attending university.But her parents do not agree with her sudden departure, fearing that it is dangerous to face this journey alone; so Paige is forced to escape secretly and undertake a long journey to the city, to chase her dream.This adventure of hers will take her to see wonderful places and meet many characters: some will involve her in their stories while others will enrich her with their wisdom.All this will lead Paige to reflect and beautiful moments spent with her little brother Oscar will resurface in her, but also the bitterness of having lost him due to an accident in the river.PLAYABILITYSet in a paper world where the scenarios are made by hand, the path must be created by folding in the right way and matching the front and back to overcome the puzzles.As we progress through the chapters the difficulty increases a little, we will find obstacles to move and platforms to operate.Between one level and another we can see Paige's story, learn about her emotions and thoughts, which will be collected in the Diary section.Beyond the house there are 7 worlds to visit, each one characterized by a colour:Green - The swampOrange- The forestYellow - The ruinsGray -The cityAzure-The caveViola-The TempleBlue-OceanThe dialogues that we can understand by reading them are original, the characters use a bizarre and funny language and way of speaking that livens up the game.The soundtrack is very beautiful and engaging, suitable and evocative, it reflects well and highlights the feelings of the protagonist.There is no shortage of collectibles to collect, in each level there are hidden "Origami" to get them you have to follow the path to reach them.The graphics are wonderful, full of details, although it is 2D you don't feel the lack of 3D.I recommend it, it is a true masterpiece of art, it is pleasant to hear the rustle of the paper as we fold it, the plot is engaging and the colors enliven our senses.

_childDocuments_.review: Our heroine is 18 yr old Paige who lives with her parents in a remote village.  She has a brilliant mind and wants to be a astrophysicist, but that requires going to university.  Her overprotective parents won't let her go, so she runs away to fulfil her dreams.  As Paige journeys on her way, the reason for her parents fears are revealed.Paige travels through caves, swamp, forest, ruins, Temple, Ocean and finally reaches the city.  Along the way, she meets people on each level including an archaeologist, a lost man and some rebellious kids.  The dialogues are short but entertaining.  So there are 7 levels plus a prologue and an epilogue.  Be sure to continue to watch the credits.The graphics are simple and bright but delightful.  This is a top down puzzle game which requires you to make a path for Paige.  Each scene is double sided and the RM flips the page.  So you have to fold over the page to use the backing as a path.  To my surprise, I found this very difficult and a friend of my vintage was the same.  It was like a part of my brain had to be woken up!  I initially used a walk through to get me moving, but eventually I had my light bulb moment - and was able to continue on my own.This game is a very clever concept and was executed well.  It is very fiddly and requires patience to play, but oh, it is so rewarding when you finally work something out!!  The folding of the page even has the rustling sound of the paper. You also have to find origami collectables in each level....usually 3 to 5 of them.  You use boulders or statues to sit on pressure pads, there are portals to skip difficult bits, laser lights to light lighthouses which trigger platforms.  I found it fun and quite innovative.  Some people found the game play boring and repetitive but you still need your wits about you.The sound design was good and a bit spooky at times but wasn't too loud or overbearing.  This is a cute and charming game which is non violent.  It is exclusively a mouse based game, so no WASD required for those less dexterous of us.  There are no timed events but there are coloured puzzles towards the end.  There is a hint system, but you will lose an achievement if you use it.  Depending on your puzzling ability, it is medium difficulty level....nothing like Chants of Sennar which I flunked!  You can do a speed run under 4 hours, unless you get a brain fade like me!!  Buy on sale if you're an Einstein!!I do applaud the devs for such a creative and unique game.  It is very charming and reminds you of the importance of family but also to be brave enough to follow your dreams.  Highly recommend - 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: "Paper Trail" is a puzzle game. Ok, it's not a  puzzle game! You like origami? You like folding papers? You like coming up with clever solutions and to think outside of the box? Then this puzzle is for you!Unlike other puzzle games, this one is actually cute and clever! You need to reach your destination and in the process solve the puzzles that are blocking your way. Find keys, origami (collectables), secrets and more in this heartwarming adventure!So, what do you actually do? You manipulate the world around you as it was made out of paper; you fold, flip and twist it in more than 1 way. But that's not all! The game uses various mechanics such as different moving platforms (they have different abilities), "portals", locking mechanisms, more than 1 area to simultaneously manipulate and then some!The different backgrounds, characters and movement, due to interacting with the world, make it feel alive and breathing! It's actually breathtaking and magical! Immerse yourself in it and help out the heroine reach where she needs to be.The artstyle is cute and heartwarming, while the dialogues are full of humor, coziness and silliness! The music is perfect for this game and it will never distract you or bore you; on the contrary, it will help you feel closer to it, as if you are indeed a part of its vast atmospheric world.While the story isn't particularly complicated, the gameplay itself is! It's becoming trickier and trickier by each passing frame yet it remains fresh, fun and addictive! You  to see what else the developers have come up with and explore it! It's lengthy for the complexity it offers and you will love it! Really smart puzzles but never tiresome. There is always something to keep you entertained on this journey.No puzzle is unsolvable or difficult to the point of frustration; and what I love about it, while it's challenging, it's never a chore or needlessly excruciating. Plus, the artstyle and how unique it is as a game.Just buy it, play it and love it! Highly recommended!!!For more reviews, follow my curator

_childDocuments_.review: AVOID | LACKING | MAYBE | WORTHWHILE |  | UNMISSABLEPaper Trail is primarily a puzzle game that relies on you folding the world around you to create new paths. In general, the art/overall look of the game is beautiful. The music is very serene and relaxing in effect. The puzzles range in difficulty from straightforward to requiring a lot of thought, as the game often introduces a new concept for a particular segment of the game and it becomes progressively more difficult throughout that segment. Don't be fooled by the cute art design though; this game is high-key kind of difficult at its toughest points particularly if you are going for all collectibles (which I was). There is a hint system, but I avoided using it, so I can't speak to how well it's implemented. That said, making a mistake is low stakes here; you aren't punished in any way for being wrong while solving the puzzles.The only real criticism I have of the game is the storytelling. On the one hand, the game clearly makes an effort to tell a story here, but on the other, it's not fleshed out enough to really seem worth it. You could have plopped me in this world and said, "This character just wants to solve puzzles" and I'd be like, "Ok, dope, let's go" and I would have got an equal amount of satisfaction out of the story.  That said, it's inoffensive enough, so meh?The game took me 3 hours and 57 minutes for a complete run, which is lucky because there is an achievement for completing the game under 4 hours lol. It's almost certainly easier the second time around though, if you need to redo it. Yet, I imagine the replayability in terms of the puzzles is actually on the higher side of things because you'll likely have a sense for how you previously solved a puzzle, but you probably haven't memorized the solution (the game doesn't really lend itself to that).If you enjoy relaxing (mostly...) puzzle games with beautiful art and atmosphere, and incredible music, and don't mind a game that is weaker on the storytelling side of things, this game is a great pick. The game also reminds me quite a bit of Carto and Monument Valley, so if you enjoyed those titles, this is probably a safe bet.

_childDocuments_.review: Paper Trail is a charming puzzle adventure that unfolds a unique and engaging experience. The game’s innovative mechanic of folding the environment to solve puzzles is both refreshing and challenging. Players will find themselves immersed in a visually captivating world where every corner holds a potential solution.While the core gameplay is undeniably strong, the narrative could have been more substantial. Additionally, the pacing of the puzzles can be inconsistent, with some sections feeling overly simplistic. Nonetheless, Paper Trail is a delightful journey for puzzle enthusiasts and those seeking a fresh perspective on the genre.The game’s artistic style is a standout, with its watercolor-like visuals creating a serene atmosphere. The audio design complements the visuals perfectly, enhancing the overall immersive experience.Overall, Paper Trail is a commendable effort that showcases the potential of innovative gameplay mechanics. While it may not redefine the puzzle genre, it certainly leaves a lasting impression.

_childDocuments_.review: 7 hours without a guide, 2 hours with a guide 3/10 1, but I would suggest 2 I wrote , which also contains links to a youtube playthrough to get all the collectibles No Yes, there are 3 missable achievements (speedrun + complete the game without hints +  one at the beginning of the game) No No Yes, complete the game in under 4 hours. I highly suggest doing this on a second playthrough so you can just take your time and enjoy the game the first time around No No No difficulty setting, but it has an achievement to complete the game without hints NoWow, I'm blown away but how beautiful and creative Paper Trail is. The gameplay is so unique and done in such a wonderful way while it will also ask you to think deeply about how to solve the later puzzles. I love how you play through different theme levels and how they all add a new mechanic to the already creative gameplay. What makes this game extra good is how it saves automatically at the start of each new puzzle, so you can just quit the game and come back later to a puzzle when you feel stuck or had enough for that moment. It allows in such an elegant way to play this game in short bursts. furthermore, it is also impressive how the game had no bugs for me. I'm quite good at breaking games and it is quite normal for me to contact developers about breaking X or Y so it can be fixed soon. However, I didn't encounter any bugs at all in Paper Trail!Paper Trail has a few missable achievements. _childDocuments_.review: Most people that can enjoy puzzle games will have a nice little time with this game. It is amazingly well polished, art and music shine wonderfully. If you think the trailer gameplay looks fun I bet you will have a great time. I mainly purchased the game because I enjoy puzzles and the paper theme. It is worth noting there are many longer and more complex puzzle games for half this price, but I consider those underpriced, not that this game overpriced, the art and music are worth it.I finished the game and had a mostly good time, exceptions below aside, with an especially well done final chapter and ending.Devs if you can put this much polish on a game with a REALLY solid core gameplay loop, I imagine you will have a big hit.Unfortunately for me, the core puzzle mechanic really felt limited, the puzzle/gameplay possibility space of a 2 dimensional sheet that can't fold more than once got old fairly quickly, especially when combined with not being able to see the puzzle pieces you were working with clearly. By the time you understood the pieces of the puzzle at your disposal it often would have been easier to have simply done trial and error or nearly every possible fold and stumbled upon the answer in less time. In the puzzles where I had successfully understood the final goal and all the folds needed, the process of implementing them and moving things around became a chore waiting for the animations to finish.Many puzzles do not having a strong "Ahaa!" moment of both understanding the needed solution with the given elements and getting to that solution quickly. This left a number puzzles and elements overstaying their welcome, causing the length of the chapters to feel like a chore more quickly than they would have otherwise.

_childDocuments_.review: really love the idea, but the execution was too tedious tbh. you see, this is a "paper folding game", where you have to fold the paper . however, you cannot fold it over your character (at least to visualize the pathway, which allow you, the player, planning on which is the final fold you need, then actually make such fold later). instead, you have to use right-click to see the other side of the paper and imagine the fold you need in your mind. otherwise, if you aren't great at visual thinking, then you have to  move your character around the screen (to avoid folding the paper onto yourself) a lot in order to try which fold do you need. not to mention that you can't try out some fold entirely since you can never reach some tile on the paper. this is a fatal issue that hold back the game.and that issue fold out in another way (no pun intended): the folding in this game is too simple! you can only (1) fold from edges (2) fold from corners. in both methods you cannot fold the paper over the previous fold. in other words, you only have 1-folding level. so, while folding from top-edge and bottom-edge at the same time is possible (when the result fold is not overlapping), you cannot fold more from left or right edge... i guess that if it allow free-folding in the first place (not restricted by player's character), it can also enjoy the more big brain puzzle theme of multi-level folding.all in all, i think this is a  game if it were a physical game, where you can touch and flip and fold the actual piece of paper as freely as you wish (and have a better visualization on how your fold gonna actually affect the paper). but as a computer game, it is too half-baked.

_childDocuments_.review: is an adventure puzzle game developed and published by Newfangled Games.  You take on the role of Paige, a young teenage girl who has been accepted into university.  However, there is one problem.  Her parents refuse to let her leave, so Paige decides to run away to university, leaving a letter behind for her parents.  As Paige goes on her journey, she meets various characters, each of whom has their individual stories, and you get to learn about Paige's backstory, particularly .  That's the basic story premise, so I'll stop my synopsis here. ^^As for the gameplay, it has point-and-click elements although the main one is folding paper (yup, as in origami style XD), as the story is set in a foldable, paper world and Paige has the ability to fold paper and open up  and connect paths that may be inaccessible, otherwise.  Paige can push boulders, which can either be obstacles that need to be moved to the side or paperweights that can keep buttons pressed down in order to make bridges and such appear.  There are statues as well that serve the same purposes as boulders.  Later in the game, there are lights that need to be activated and having them reflect in particular symbols or lighthouses can pave the way for Paige to access areas.  In addition to the brief prologue, there are a total of 9 chapters.  Also, there are plenty of Steam achievements although no Steam trading cards at the time of this review.Now that I've gone over the story and gameplay, I'll move onto my thoughts.  Being a fan of cozy, cute and puzzle games,  caught my interest very early on, so I was very happy and surprised that I was offered a review key for the game.  (I apologize that it took me a while to get around to it due to work and other real life things keeping me busy. ^^)  Thus, I wanted to get around to it as soon as I could.  Without further delay, I'll first touch on the story.  At first, it feels like your typical runaway story in which Paige wants to pursue her goals of studying at university, but her parents are being overprotective, so they don't want her to go.  Of course, Paige isn't going to let that stop her.  As she goes on her journey, she meets a cast of characters, like the archaeologist searching for lost artifacts.  Paige has brief interactions with them, but what caught my attention most was   Anyway, the story is more on the light-hearted side, and the dialogue between characters can easily be skipped although I wouldn't recommend doing this on a first playthrough since some characters give subtle hints about how to progress through areas.  As for the ending, .However, the main focus here is the gameplay, so I'll talk about that.  It has been a while since I last played a puzzle game, so I admit that my skills were probably a bit rusty.  I will say that it's a good idea to follow the tutorial and the instructions, and definitely don't be afraid to use hints if you have trouble figuring out how to fold particular paper pieces to access certain paths and whatnot.  The world of  has two sides, and if you check out the reverse side (clicking the right mouse button will access it), it'll give you a hint on how to progress through areas. (By the way, you can use the mouse or keyboard for controls, and I also believe it has controller support.)  It would have helped if I had known about this reverse side feature from the start since it's not stated until Paige leaves home and enters chapter two.  (Also, there's a particular Steam achievement that can be missed if you're not aware of this feature although you can access Paige's journal, where she narrates her story, whenever by simply pressing the Escape button and clicking on the Journal feature.)  Oh, I shouldn't forget, but in each chapter, you can find anywhere from two to five origami figures.  They aren't necessary to progress through the story although if you're an achievement completionist (like myself), then you should keep an eye out for them, and they can be a bit tricky to find and access (although doable).  The puzzles can be challenging at times, especially if they're not your strong point, but thankfully, there are guides out there and video playthroughs especially help.  XD  As for Steam achievements, I was able to obtain them all although it took me two playthroughs to do so.  Heck, it's even possible to earn the speedrun achievement, where you have to complete the game in under four hours. ^^As for the art, it is absolutely gorgeous.  I love the art style and the use of colors in this game.  You really feel like you're in a paper world and following Paige on her adventure.  I only wish there was some sort of gallery or such available since I love taking screenshots (but I suppose you can look at the Steam store page screenshots and video playthroughs to see the art for yourself).  Also, the animations that pop up are done well, like .  In regards to the music, the tracks are very lovely to listen to.  They feel soothing and relaxing, and they fit perfectly with the chapters they're placed in.  I have to admit that I especially enjoyed listening to that ending song in the credits scene.  The singer's voice is beautiful as well as the lyrics.  Also, there's voice acting from Paige.  I played the English version, so I listened to Paige's English voice actress.  She fits really well with the character, and I liked listening to her narrate her adventures in between chapters and such.  As for the other characters, they aren't really voiced although they do have sound effects.Overall, would I recommend ?  If you like cozy, cute games with a light-hearted story and don't mind the challenging puzzles, then this is a game definitely worth checking out.  I had such a delight playing it, and Paige is a lovely main character.  The puzzles did prove somewhat frustrating for me on occasion, but the developers have a discord server where you can ask questions, report bugs, etc.  For the asking price, mileage may vary.  If you're good at puzzles, then this might be a bit on the pricey side.  However, it's obvious that with the art, the music, etc., a lot of love and care was taken into creating this delightful game.  At the time of this review, the game is having a launch sale and it's a limited time bundle, so if this interests you, you may want to check it out.Finally, I want to give a major thank you to Newfangled Games for the review key.  I'm happy to have gotten the chance to play and review , and it deserves lots of praise and love.  I can't wait to see what future games there will be although I know it's too early for speculation. ^^

_childDocuments_.review: Paper Trail is a decent puzzle, particularly for those who enjoy cozy/semi-casual games.The story is somewhat good, which reminds me of picture books and short graphic novels I read as a kid. The usage of folding paper is rather creative, notably during various kinds of scene transitions. Neither the story nor the characters are rememberable, although it's fine since it's a puzzle game.Paper Trail boasts a gorgeous and eye-catching art style. It uses folding paper(s) for all aspects of the game, including the credit. The sound effects are okay, while addition of audio tracks that mimic conversation helped me enjoy the story.The puzzle mechanics and design are exceptional. The game introduces new mechanics as you progress into new areas and serves puzzles that combine multiple mechanics, where I never feel overwhelmed. Figuring out possible puzzle solutions wasn't difficult, although sometimes I forget to fold in specific ways (horizontal, vertical and diagonal) or not fold too much.The difficulty is just right for those who are looking for cozy/semi-casual games. If it's too hard for you, the game provides hints by showing step-by-step folding the paper(s). Although even if you see whole steps, usually you still need to figure out other mechanics by yourself. For obvious reason, please hold back from using hint too frequently or see many steps at once. And if it's too easy for you, you can try collecting all origami/collectibles which is quite a bit more challenging.The game runs well on my Linux device with minimal issues. It's also available on Android and iOS, but limited for those who subscribe to Netflix.I had a great time with Paper Trail, where I bothered to collect all collectibles. The base price is a bit pricey though, considering you could beat this game under 4 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: First off I wanna say a huge thanks to Newfangled Games for giving me the chance to beta test and receive the game early. Since I had played Hue I've been waiting for a new puzzle game to come out and as soon as the creators announced Paper Trail I've been super excited to play. We follow the story of a girl named Paige wanting to leave her home to go and attend university as her dream. I really enjoyed experiencing this as it's not over the top, it's not complicated, it's short and sweet which I really enjoy. The way they execute telling the story is so unique and clever like you're not just watching a cutscene you're actually interacting with it yourself. The visuals in this game are lovely. The hand drawn artstyle really fits so well. Each puzzle involves of course folding paper to reveal new pathways and get to your goal. Throughout each section you get introduced to many new elements such as blocks that have to be together so you can walk across them, moving platforms and statues getting in your way. There's a load more to it but I won't go fully into it as I want you to experience it for yourself. A lot of the puzzles you get a grip of quite quickly but then as you get onto a bigger one you end up forgetting so many things. Like in one of them I was stuck for ages only to realise that I haven't tried folding it in a specific way. It's really relieving when you finally get it. But this game messes with your brain a lot because even just folding the paper diagonally can change so much. It wouldn't be a review without me mentioning the soundtrack. It is made by Claudie Mackula and goodness paired with the gameplay it is just so relaxing and beautiful to listen to. They did an incredible job coming up with these tracks and you know i'm definitely getting the soundtrack when I can. I am so happy with how this game has turned out. It has the right amount of difficulty, it's so visually pleasing and that music all paired together makes for a fantastic experience which I urge you all to try. Definitely Recommend 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Every "world" had its own tricks and series of folds needed to complete levels, it kept the game fresh and intriguing- As with any good strategy game, some levels were easier/more straight-forward than others. Although, nothing quite beats the feeling of finally figuring out a level and immediately thinking "duh, I can't believe that took me so long" lol- Collecting the "hidden" origami along the way was fun, the taglines were cute and I liked that they matched the theme of the game- The art style and background music both definitely added to my enjoyment of the gameCons- When a level involves interacting with multiple sheets of paper, it can sometimes be hard to "grab" the corner/side you want without accidentally grabbing a corner/side that is right next to it. I was playing on a laptop so I'm not sure if using another method helps to avoid this issue but maybe color-coding the line that pops up when you hover over a corner/side might make this easier.- I agree with others that the actual story could use some work.  so the ending left me a bit unsatisfied.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Trail

_childDocuments_.review: Paper Trail is one of those games where it was exactly what I had hoped it would be from the trailers. The art is lovely, the characters are cute and charming, the story is sweet, and each area feels unique and distinct with its own identity. This extends to the puzzles as well, with each area's new puzzle element feeling interesting and fresh without feeling forced. The puzzles overall are just the right level of challenging while remaining approachable and make you think outside the box in a way that tickled my brain. Each solve is satisfying and brainstorming the steps you'll need to take is fun. I like that there is no timer or pressure and you can take each level at your own pace. I didn't find myself needing it but I LOVE that there is a built-in hint system. I especially like that you control how much of a hint you get, so that if you just need a gentle nudge you can get that without the entire answer being spoiled for you. I loved seeing accessibility options in the settings menu (low motion camera, reduced flashing, a grid display to name a few). My only critique is that I wish the collectible origami showed instructions for how to make them in real life, though I imagine that would become quite complicated quite quickly! Overall I highly recommend Paper Trail if you're looking for a new puzzle game with a concept that feels fresh and unique, with satisfying solves and a beautiful art style.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Trail

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I’ve finally gotten my hands on Paper Trail I have to say it’s exceeded ALL my expectations! 10/10!  It has the most beautiful and captivating art style I have ever seen, with an emotive narrative and the most compelling soundtrack. The puzzles elegantly sit between being challenging enough to keep you engaged but at the same time being achievable (even to a non puzzle expert like me) But it’s the tactile experience of folding over the paper world which cannot be overstated. It’s such a unique game mechanic which has blown me away and changed my view of what a puzzle game can be! an honestly mesmerising and quite magical experience.Paper Trail is truly a work of art and you really need to try it for yourself!
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Trail

_childDocuments_.review: Paper Trail is a clever puzzle game with beautiful scenery and music.  It feels satisfying when you find a solution to a puzzle, the hint system is designed so you don't accidentally spoil yourself, and there's origami hidden around each level to collect as an extra challenge.  Paper Trail takes its core concept of folding paper, takes it as far as it can, and combines it with other puzzle mechanics for a novel experience.  I will say that the characters in the story are a bit flat (no pun intended), but that doesn't take away from the game's style and the puzzles.  Also, there are many block-pushing puzzles in this game, so if those make your blood boil, maybe don't play this game to relax.  That being said, I am definitely going back to Paper Trail to collect all the origami.

_childDocuments_.review: Check out my full review here!  Challenging puzzles, a charming art style, incredible soundtrack, and a memorable one of a kind gameplay experience. Paper Trail is a top down puzzle adventure game that follows The story of Paige. Players will take control of Paige through her journey through a variety of different terrains as she leaves home travelling to the university. The gameplay starts out quite simple, in order to navigate through blocked paths or gaps in the terrain. Paige can essentially bend the fabric of space and time by altering the environment around her. The way this is implemented through gameplay and art design is quite clever. Each room, so to speak, is made up of paper panels which can be folded over to create new paths. You can fold the edges corners or even multiple sections of the paper at the same time to create new paths for page to traverse. The first chapter, Home, acts as a tutorial showcasing how these folds can be applied, and it seems almost trivial to begin with. But in the same way that 2016 the witness took one mechanic and added elements. Paper trail slowly but surely complicates the puzzles with a variety of added mechanics in fun and creative ways.I also strongly recommend getting every collectable for an added but more satisfying challenge. In each chapter, you can collect hidden origami, which requires an additional level of folding and problem solving. And most of the time you need to go out of your way to put together the correct folds to obtain origami.Of course it wasn't just the puzzles that were driving me, but the other elements of the game that added to the experience. Cutscenes at the end of each chapter, involve the player folding the panels over to continue the cutscene. The themes of family and a coming of age story act as a beautiful backdrop and in tandem with stunning art design, help keep the player motivated and driven to discover what lies in the next chapter. Every time I started to get bored of one area, the game changed it up just at the right time, and a new colour palette not only made the game look more appealing, but also helped me visualize and understand the progression I was making as I travelled closer towards the university.The pacing of these levels were on point. Also, not to mention the soundtrack was incredible. I read the team brought in a Canadian multi-instrumentalist composer and vocalist, Claudie Mackula, and just like the level and art design. You can really feel the passion for the project in the music.I cannot stress the impact good music has in a video game. And while there is some ambience and sound effects, the player is going to be listening to the music the whole time while solving complex problems. So a super effort was done here to achieve this high production level.For me, paper Trail was an extremely memorable and satisfying experience that left a lasting impression. I played on PC and it took me roughly 10 hours to complete the game and get every collectable. Now I did get stuck a couple times but I would say most people could get the main game completed in 8 hours.Paper trail was ultimately an absolute pleasure and a rewarding title to play, and because of that it has absolutely earned my strong recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most creative, inventive and brilliantly designed puzzle games i've played, even though there's some real brain twisters involved. Paper trail takes the idea of folding paper to the next level by adding tons of extra elements into the formula, making it both more challenging and keeping it fresh. There's never once a puzzle that gets stale because each of the 9 chapters has its own gimmick that changes the way you think about it. What makes the game so brilliant though is the simple fact that you can fold not only horizontally and vertically but also diagonally as well. Not every page is square or rectangular either so that alone creates a ton of variety especially in later stages with side pages and ledges that get thrown into the mix.There's also another brilliant mechanic at play where you cannot fold a piece over or underneath yourself so you have to think ahead most of the time. Other objects like heavy statues or boulders also have this property further challenging your options, which makes for some real head scratchers. While things like portals, moving platforms and elevations further complicate matters. Paper trail however never goes too far, always having an approachable design to each of its puzzles, of which there are plenty to solve. I was actually very suprised at the amount of different puzzles the devs were able to come up with, and it really speaks volumes about their creative genius. As it is much harder to design a puzzle that is both hard and solvable. The game is bug & lag free, had no possible softlocks and didn't crash once during my playtime, so it's safe to say that the game is incredibly polished. Not only technically but also visually as all the pages look utterly beautiful with clear and well defined lines never cluttering the screen. There's also an amazing soundtrack to soothe your ears, one that reminded me of Ori's luma pools at times which is in my opinion still the greatest OST of all time! Finally we arrive at story and while it had a subplot that had me really invested it didn't go anywhere in the end. I had hoped to find some closure of this subplot in some way, good or bad. But the main plot is still enough to give some meaning to it all. The cutscenes being told with folding as well was refreshing and thematically consistent! All in all paper trail is a super solid game to challenge your grey matter :)
