_childDocuments_.review: Full Walkthrough  -  ( almost won the first game , I got second though ) Rating - 8/10  ( PC BUILD ) Solium Infernum is one of those games that really make you hate your friends. It makes even a non-believer like me hope that there is a hell so they can be sent there after all’s said and done, just to atone for ruining my carefully laid plans. Or, to put it another way; it’s the perfect thing for a board game night.How the Game Starts , well here we go - So Every player chooses one Archfiend with special abilities and can equip them with an item that remains hidden until it’s used, giving them a secret trump card to be played at a critical moment. Each of these demonic entities who strive to be hell’s next shepherd comes with their own play style, and all of them are equally viable.Variety is one of the best parts of Solium Infernum, because winning the election requires you to collect a resource called Prestige. Prestige is awarded for many activities: Conquering and holding important landmarks, successfully threatening other Archfiends to do your bidding, generating and fulfilling quests, and so on. Overall, each Archfiend’s playstyle gives them a defined way of gaining Prestige without feeling constricting – the economy-focused Mammon, for example, can funnel his great wealth into military or diplomatic ventures, depending on which opportunities present themselves.Solium Infernum has tons of subsystems to offer: Magic rituals, event cards, a combat system, auctions for troops, leaders, and items, diplomacy, a dueling system – it’s a lot to learn and keep track of during a game. This has the advantage of always giving you something to do, even if you just suffered a big setback. There is always some scheme to plot, some adjustment to be made, some enemy to be sabotaged. On the other hand, this immense depth doesn’t make the game very approachable. It includes a solid tutorial, but the sheer amount of systems to be used can still feel overwhelming.That said, once you’ve wrapped your head around how the game works, all of these mechanics feel very satisfying to use. When you’re testing how to synergize the effects of different systems and putting together rough plans in your head, Solium Infernum really slaps. It’s a constant mix between feeling like a diabolic genius outsmarting everyone and a drunken idiot who couldn’t see the most obvious foil to their plan coming.It’s not surprising, then, that the multiplayer mode is this game’s core. Be it with strangers or with friends, as long as everyone’s roughly on the same skill level you’ll have a blast. Playing by yourself is possible thanks to the AI filling up the rest of the player spots, but it’s definitely not a comparable experience – half the fun is in subtly manipulating your friends to do what you want them to do or laughing in their faces after they’ve realized who thwarted their last scheme.It’s a relaxed, non-intrusive way of playing out a match over days, weeks, and even months. You can also set a time limit people can take to give their next orders to keep the game going in case someone has to drop out. Should everyone find themselves online at the same time, you can simply play as if you were in a regular session. It sounds very old-fashioned, and if I were still in university I probably wouldn’t care about it at all, but for anyone with less time than that, this system offers a great way of enjoying a game with friends on a time constraint.Having just two orders per turn really makes you think carefully about each move, especially as the order in which they’re resolved matters, too. Having that time without any extra pressure can be helpful in navigating the complex game, mitigating the difficulty factor a little.Though the visual style of Solium Infernum’s characters may not be to everyone’s liking, the title is chock-full of brilliant artwork that decorates the cards of events, items, and units. Overall, the graphics and the soundtrack create a good atmosphere and background for the backstabbing. Another strong point is the character writing – every Archfiend has a strong personality and the diplomatic dialog is quite witty at times.Despite saying mostly positive things about it, I find Solium Infernum difficult to score, because no number will be able to properly describe everyone’s experience. Solo players will not enjoy this game a whole lot and strategy newcomers diving into multiplayer alone may have a hard time until they get the hang of it. Jump into a game with people you know, however, and Solium Infernum is a magical experience that will provide an unending stream of funny anecdotes and memories to recount later.

_childDocuments_.review: In short, Solium Infernum is an infernal success, rewarding intellect, patience, and observation over brute force and brawn.Dominating Hell never looked so good. SI is a 4X political strategy game that puts player interaction to the forefront, forcing the players to react and read their devilish opponents to successfully ascend to the throne. By competing for Places of Power, and claiming neutral territory by a Legion walking upon it, you will need to befriend, backstab and intimidate to complete your objectives. Solium Infernum has a decent package of content: a serviceable tutorial which goes through the basics of Hellish ascension, a comprehensive encyclopedia of game mechanics, a scenario for each of the Archfiends that serves as a basic primer and a nice little challenge complete with secondary objectives and rankings. The real meat of the game is through the eponymous Solium Infernum mode, which supports asynchronous gameplay - allowing you and your friends to continue a game on their own time and acting like a regular session when the crew is all present. The core gameplay loop is intuitive and deep. Many of the game mechanics are divided into four categories: Sanctum (upgrades, objectives, events), Diplomacy (player interaction), Bazaar (bidding on army units), and Rituals (casting spells) and each of those actions uses an order slot. Each of these categories are a viable way to gain prestige, of which the Archfiend with the most at the end of the game takes the crown, provided nobody has forcibly taken the capital city of Pandemonium, or excommunicated all the Archfiends, or worse. The game provides plenty of alternate wincons for the power hungry or those who wish to inflict chaos.Most of the actions you take will interact with other players, or aid you in the future power play against another. This is where the game absolutely shines brightest. Just obtained a powerful Praetor in the bazaar? Demand resources from everyone or threaten to meet them in a Praetor Duel. Just upgraded your Destruction tree? Extort your friends into giving up an artifact or have their best Legion sniped across the map. Want to start a war between two players or secretly backstab your ally? Ritual Framing has you covered. The game's art direction, sound, and music are fantastic. The aesthetics of grey, black and red wash over the barren landscape to immerse you in the depths of calm Hell. The 2D art for the Legions, Rituals, Praetors, Artifacts and Event cards are a particular standout. The combat and ritual animations are meaty, with leagues of soldiers flying hundreds of feet away with devilish satisfaction.The only gripe is the 3D models for the archfiends can look amateurish at times and sometimes clashes with the aesthetics of the rest of the game. Other issues are that the tutorial is not comprehensive, and you may need a couple games under your belt if you're a hands-on learner to truly feel like you know what you're doing. However, I recommend reading the excellently written in-game Encyclopaedia Infernum; it can and will speed up this process considerably. The last issue is that this is a game about exploiting human nature and petty vendettas. This game is best played with human players. While the AI is okay, the single player is best used to test strategies and try new Archfiends in a controlled environment.Despite this, Solium Infernum is one of the best 4X strategy games on the market. If you are looking for an excellent outlet for your Machiavellian machinations and to backstab and racketeer your friends, then look no further.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR;The game is super fun. Performance issues have gone for me. I changed a couple of things. GPU is now a GTX 1080 TI with 11 GB VRAM and 1800Mhz Clock. Also new SSD and reinstalled all fresh Windows. This seemed to have done the trick. All Ultra settings now runs at 60fps without any drops. Maybe the performance team has done some work as well? Can't tell.What I love most about this game is, that it just doesn't play like your normal type of 4X or grand strategy board game. There is more depth here, and way more turn of events. You can amass a lot of wealth just to lose it in the blink of an eye. Likewise the other way around, or you could simply do the same to one of your opponents. If you like scheming and baiting your oponents or tricking them otherwise to basically beat themselves, then this is the kind of game for you.Also the artworks are super nice. If you're an art enjoyer, like I am, you'll love what you see here.

_childDocuments_.review: This gem quickly went from "Oh, my friend told me I should take a look. I've never heard of this before, but maybe I'll watch a video. . ." to "This is one of the best strategy titles I have ever played."I play tactics and strategy games as the vast majority of my gaming, and Solium Infernum is a really solid investment for those like me. The only caveat is that the AI is still undergoing some work, which is really needed before it can pose a problem to a human player. Even on my first game, as I was still feeling out the systems, it didn't feel like I was under any threat of losing to the AI. Thankfully, the devs said this is the top of their list to work on going forward!That being said, the multiplayer is really, really strong here. If you join the Discord or have friends to play with, this game will offer lots and lots of joyous scheming.Lastly, I will praise the fact that the game is not very long per match. Many of its competitors are very time prohibitive (especially in multiplayer) due to taking often multiple days and play sessions to complete. Solium Infernum, at least for me so far, is a 2-3 hour commitment for a full game on the normal game length, and that has been without a turn timer or anything like that.So overall, if you like strategy games, especially in multiplayer, I can't really think of a better value proposition right now than Solium Infernum for the monetary and time investment.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: I love 4x games, but, frankly, after the peak of Endless Legend/Endless Space 2, this is the first truly original (I didn't play the original at the time) enjoyable 4x I've played in years.It's much easier to learn than it may initially seem, and the tutorial is great in this regard.There are several different path to victory and each Archfiend feels different (some just a bit, others a lot).The graphics are good, while the art style and the little bits of lore are excellent.Definitely worth the price, and hoping for DLCs to enrich the content for the long run!
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: A clever game of outmaneuvering your opponents. The early game is setting up your strategy, the midgame is a constant battle of remaining one step ahead of your opponents while they are trying to do the same to you, and the endgame is where you either try to hold off your opponent's last gasp attempts to overthrow your lead or finding a weakness in your opponent's strategy and exploiting it. The mindgames are fantastic and the opportunities to outplay your opponents are numerous.There are some minor balance issues, but overall is a very fun game if you play multiplayer (which supports asynchronous play). Single player is lacking and I would not recommend outside of learning the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Grade A. There are Digital versions of board games where they recreate the experience of playing Monopoly or Small World or some other real life game. and then there are Digital Board games that provide you a unique Tabletop inspired gaming experience but with so many moving parts and unique pieces that the idea of setting it up and playing it in real life would be difficult and tedious if not impossible. This is a really great digital board game, With well thought out and balanced rules. With devs that are actively working on and tweaking the game to make it better, and they've done a good job, it really is something great. THE PRICE MIGHT SEEM A LITTLE BIT HIGH AT FIRST BUT ITS A COMPLETE WELL MADE PACKAGE. WITH NO MICROTRANSACTIONS. something it does not need but that less scrupulous developers have managed to shove into a game any way often breaking the game to do it.    Solium Infernum is a 4x Strategy game Set in hell where you pay as an archfiend with its own specific powers and special units and you compete to be elected ruler of hell by the council or to get strong enough to overthrow pandemonium and declare yourself ruler. It is a tabletop war game, but it focuses more on intrigue and diplomacy (or what passes for diplomacy in hell) there is combat but its heavily regulated, like everything in hell, so that the games main focus is on things like extortion, secret plots, magic rituals and tactical maneuvering over the brute force build up of most table top wargames. At first it feels like there is a lot of things going on and lots of options for you to take. and thats because there is. Your limited by a certain number of orders per turn and you can use these to do things like gather resources or bid on units or equipment or other artifacts. you can threaten or extort your opponents, cast magical rituals or maneuver your game pieces, and really alot more. and after about 50 turns whoever has the most prestige is the winner. Its a very deep and engaging game. My only real complaint would be the game length (50+ turns at 3-5 minutes each) there is an asynchronous play mode thats basically a play by mail sort of thing where you take a turn and then wait. and a live mode that wants you to sit and play all 3+ hours of the game in one sitting with no ability to pause or save or do anything else. This seems like a design flaw that makes it hard to sit and have a 1-2 hour game session with my friends that we pick up later and finish. The lack of the ability to save or pause a casual game though seems like an easy thing to fix and the Developers are pretty good about updating the game so i wouldn't be surprised to see that addressed soon.  But this game is really a gem and well worth your time and money to play if this sort of thing looks at all interesting to you. I certainly recommend it, since i am enjoying it myself.

_childDocuments_.review: That game is super addictive mostly thanks to the atmosphere - the hellish setting is just perfect and I doubt I can find any other game where I will feel that dark, evil and gothic vibe. For turn based strategy it is quite easy to learn and I was not overwhelmed by walls of text like in Civilisation or other games from that genre. The pictures (of everything - ranging from units, artefacts, events, etc.) are extremely beautiful and I am really glad that I have paid for this game so I could support these amazing artists! I love admiring how their imagination pictures hell. The only thing I miss in this is more graphics for other legions - when titans come to play it is like a *whoah!* wake up from  a stagnating pace of watching the same models of standard legions (not titans) occupying the cantons and the same patterns of combat... Titans are gorgeously animated - from their entrance, combat and their death. I understand the other legions would require a lot of work, but honestly, with this that game would be on my top favourites! We already have beautifully animated models of titans decimating other legions in the most satisfying way one can imagine, the archfiends are just a bliss to watch, especially when they get annoyed! But other poor legions are just coloured pawns with the most basic movements possible... Pretors - exist only as stunning images and extra (the same) model unit when added to the legion.The Pretor arena gives so many possibilities! I wish I could see the entire combat instead of just getting a message which one has won... A bit sad though. Maybe, just maybe - the dlc will bring some changes or perhaps Solium Infernum 2 could implement more stuff like that. Nevertheless, I really enjoy this game. I am just worried I might get bored quickly as I just love seeing more variety in such games!

_childDocuments_.review: I was an avid player of League of Geeks other virtual board game Armello for several years and I'm really enjoying this much spicier revisit to its basic game design with far more dynamic and rude gameplay.My biggest gripe with Armello was how the most reliable path to victory tended to lean towards crafting an "unblockable" combo in the endgame, which meant if you wanted to avoid that you had to expend a lot of energy just suppressing the player most set up to do that. This meant that end-to-end play strategies were often pretty obvious from turn one just based on what character you were playing.In Solium, the whole game is built around the notion that people can play baddies vs police one minute to all baddies another, layering on different chess games where you have to make a guess at which chess games are for show and which ones are intended to result in a win or a specific advantage. By making doubt and deception a major part of the game design from turn one, it makes for a more dynamic nail biter. I expect players will find a lot of tactical exploits in these early days, active devs will help keep gameplay styles balanced. So far my only two major gripes are: 1) AI players are too easy. Find at least one other player you know who won't disown you just for trying to win.2) The Praetor Duels, a way to resolve conflicts between players, is extremely boring. It's hard to express just how boring the duel structure is. Yes, it's more complicated than rock paper scissors. No, it's not fun. I wish I could offer a more nuanced critique here but I am completely unmotivated by the entire mini game.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, this game is incredible--the writing reminds me of something like Sunless Sea, and everything about this game oozes theme. The gameplay is very nuanced with a lot of very deep mechanics that you  read about in the Encycaelopedia Infernum, but are just as fun to figure out when your orders go horribly wrong because you had no idea how Praetor duels actually worked until you had to do one.That said, I think the reviews likening this to a 4X game are a bit misleading. It has elements of 4X, sure, but it is  a "video-game-style" 4X. This is a board game that would be too complex to actually put on a table. If you go in expecting Civ: Hell, I think you'll be a bit disappointed. However, going in expecting something closer to Twilight Imperium--particularly the social and political elements of that game--or Diplomacy, you'll be delighted.As someone once said of another game, this game is very much a bunch of Dark Crystal Skeksis plotting, scheming, and backstabbing, and is a hell of a lot of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: A faithful re-imagining of 2009 cult classic, if you even remotely enjoyed the first SI, get this.Obligatory shout out to Rock Paper Shotgun's legendary write-up of a SI session - look it up.For the completely new and everyone else, it's a board game inspired backstabbing scheming hex-based strategy that still plays snappily due to the order system and frequently produces delightfully unexpected results. Your mileage may vary overall and I would heartily recommend embracing chaos and messing up people's plans instead of always going for an optimal win yourself.The paths to victory are as myriad as the ways your friends can mess them up.In terms of new things and technical aspects:Async multiplayer is great (up to 10 games at a time and no more shuffling save files around by e-mail or Dropbox), the UI and visual refresh are genuinely quite good with some excellent art for the unit/event/ritual cards.Game is generally great visually, runs fine, have had no stability issues.The AI is unfortunately a bit naff, but the devs are already working on it and the recent patch improved a few of it's weakest points. Overall however this is a Multiplayer experience first and foremost.Really hoping this gets long term support and thrives for another decade (or more) just like the original.Best of luck to League of Geeks and their hellish endeavors!

_childDocuments_.review: Chief issue I have are miserable random events and votes that can completely ruin your game through no fault of your own. These happen on a consistent basis, too, which makes the game extra not fun at all.Additionally, the excommunication mechanic kills the game since it can be (easily) deliberately induced and essentially boots someone from the lobby. Naturally, it can also trigger via a random event, so sometimes RNG will simply dictate that you need to walk away from the PC and do something else.AI is also totally worthless so this game has little value outside of multiplayer.The art and theme are fantastic, but the 3D models are very hit and miss.Overall there's some very fun and neat ideas, but it's dragged down by boneheaded RNG that's completely unacceptable in such a slow-paced and methodical game. Excommunication is supposedly getting fixed but the game has other problems. Might be worth it if you later acquire the game without buying like I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Solium Infernum at heart is a game that seems like a lot, if you're someone new to this style. There's a lot to keep track of and a lot to learn but this game has been absolutely incredible during my time playing it. Now, the game does come with a few small glitches, as does any new game. But they are very minor and I'm sure will be handled by the team as soon as possible.It is a lot of fun and gives you the opportunity (and misfortune) of ruining friendships and stabbing people in the back. Magic and Monsters run rampant as you attempt to take the Infernal Throne for yourself. It's an opportunity you won't wanna miss if you enjoy Grand Strategy games. The Async and Live options make game time relatively convenient too. I have enjoyed the game thus far and eagerly await its future.

_childDocuments_.review: A Magnum Opus to Hell-Genre and Political Game deserving to be the indie game of the year;Of all the games with thematics based on Hell or Christian hell from Heretic's Fork (a roguelike tower-defense deck-building based on Dante's Divine Comedy) to Inferno (an indie sokoban also based on Dante's Divine Comedy), Solium Infernum is really the cherry on the top of the cake. For the basics, Solium Infernum is a hex-based turn-based tactics political simulation based on Hell with inspiration and easter eggs in-game from world famous literature Paradise Lost By John Milton considered to be the greatest English author, Divine Comedy by Dante Alighieri considered to be the Supreme Poet and God's Demon by Wayne Barlowe.The game has everything you wish for an armchair Machiavellian, an aspiring Mastermind and an All-For-One villain with edifice complex hungering for a political simulation. All warlocks, demonologists and cultists gathered forth on February 22, 2024 with the advent of this wonderful remake of a 2009 masterpiece indie game with the same name. Kudos to Victor J. Davis for creating that indie game which in turned inspired Anthony and Trent of League of Geeks studio to transform it with a modern take and make it available for everyone. The game might be dark but there is no darkest sin if not to play this game at all.Abandon all simple IQ gaming and impatience when you buy this game. First definitely you must buy the game. Yes it costs $33.9 USD but fret not for this game has infinite replayability as the deepest abyss itself. This game is easy to learn the few fundamentals but to master and conquer it will take you to the ninth level of hell where you wish one day to meet the Dark Majesty himself. It took me 55 turns to win in the tutorial taking more than a few hours to complete it. Astaroth is the first archfiend I won with by using brute force now I plan to win with rest.The feeling of any victory in this game is like the salvation of the damned. Yes there are multiple victory conditions in this game in fact If I recall correctly there are 4 ways but it is up to you to learn it by yourself. One I'll give is to be the Power Behind the Throne; ever heard of the tragedy of Tywin Lannister? Yea be that guy in this game, the crownless king just like how he was when all his family was in King's Landing. Though try not to die while playing the game in a toilet bowl.Needless to say this game has artworks comparable to a gallery in Italian Renaissance, the oil painting done by Dominik Mayer is breathtaking and I would gladly even buy an artbook of this game. Take note devs >:D I don't know about the other artists but for sure they also did excellent works such as the UI/UX designer. Of all the games I bought since 2020 no other UI has better accent than Solium Infernum. You can see the thematic colors of red, gold and black that accentuates the feeling of being an archfiend of hell. With all the beauty of visual aesthetics, the sense of hearing is not forgotten. The music is epic and an upcoming soundtrack will provide delight to all music fiends. The game music also helps you relax while you fine-tune your strategies. Eternal Nights by Sarah is fitting theme for you play this game in endless nights.Then for the loremasters, the game has a built-in encyclopedia known as Encyclopedia Infernum a fitting repository of hellish knowledge. The only caveat I have with this codex is that there should be multiple colors for quality of life searching and colorblind. One thing to excite the loremasters is the section of the Praetors, where most of the demons found in the lesser key of Solomon are found. Yes I mentioned those 72 demons; one of them is in the Conjuring movie part 2 and the other is in League of Legends inside the hands/body of a man named Jericho Swain, a champion that would play Solium Infernum before League above all else.The game despite fully launch has lots of potential to grow even further. The maps are just still 3 imagine if they added new map realms from Heaven itself to other type of hells maybe those inspired from Asian Hell such as Buddhist Hells (Naraka) or the underworld of Shintoism (Yomi). Of course the current 8 archfiends are based on the eight evil thoughts but in hell there are more archfiends than you can imagine. There can be also more game modes and more campaign/scenarios. The only drawback I have for the game is that it is not a laptop friendly game especially to those who own budget laptops. I'm using an Asus TUF 15 gaming laptop model year 2020 to write this review and play Solium Infernum with all the settings in low and all other effects disabled with a resolution of 1600x400@144 HZ, the game still has optimization issues and memory leak especially in the later parts of the game. Otherwise if you have an above average laptop, my goodness don't miss out on this masterpiece. I would also love to let you all know on how friendly and hospitable the League of Geeks developers and staff are. Kudos to Trent for helping me in many ways playing the beta and for Chan in reading all my suggestions both in the Steam forums and Discord channel. One of the few developers in Steam that takes community feedback and implement as they can the changes you sought to better the game.I might have received the game for free but I'm not biased in my review for I also bought my girlfriend this game so we can now enjoy co-op skirmish vs AI or are we even going co-op? Oh yea it is a free for all guess who will win this time? If I have the money like Mammon I would have bought this game 666th time so to all who read my review and to all my dear friends who love decision making, this game is a worthy collection to be played in your game library.For Steam collectors of community items, I already suggested to Chan and LoG Devs what you may want for as Solium Infernum's point shop items in the discussion thread. Avatars of the archfiends, a game profile, animated backgrounds and emoticons hopefully they will come later. I leave this review with a cryptic message;What is Hell? But other people.What is Solium Infernum? A masterpiece waiting to be in your Steam Library. Just play it.The Dark Majesty might be coming for you if you won't.

_childDocuments_.review: This is bringing back to life a work of genius by Vic Davis of the now defunct Cryptic Comet. The original game was released in 2009 and had a charm of its own, but League of Geeks has breathed beautiful new life into it. The few actions you can take a turn, the many different avenues of advancement (conquest, schemes, rituals, etc), the unpredictability of what happens, and the scheming of players make for often epic narratives. For example, people are hating on excommunication as an unfair gameover. I was excommunicated and then proceeded to conquer the remaining archfiends strongholds (as I was no longer barred by diplomacy rules). When I removed the last archfiend, the city of Pandemonium started to fail, losing half of its combat strength and hit points each turn. If it reached zero, all hell would fall into the void and everyone--including me--would lose. Pandemonium at full strength was much too powerful for me to attack, but I was able to reach it just in time (with my very slow legion) and take it over to win the game. Had I been one hex farther away, it would have been defeat. This was a pretty epic feeling, and it's the kind of narratives that stick with you (whether you get the better of the story or it got the better of you). Highly recommend this gem of a game, and I hope it is wildly popular to make multiplayer wonderful for years.

No matter how much advantage you get early no matter how fast you scale you cannot overcome the action economy of multiple player a.i. all targeting you every turn with their actions. _childDocuments_.review: Great game, the combination of limited actions (Orders)  per turn and limited economy works in the game favor by avoiding the late game tedium of most 4x games, while the sheer variety of options keeps everything fresh and interesting. Simultaneously the tutorial and encyclopedia keeps everything comprehensible. As an added bonus the default low turn limit on prestige victory helps preventing the game from dragging on to long as in most 4x games.My only critique is that I wish the bazaar changed up it's offering without player action from time to time and  that some of the special abilities of the demon lords seem questionably useful while others are very good. A solid 9/10 game in my book, depending upon how the multiplayer community develops could go to a 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: What a brilliant implementation of the 4x principle with a strong focus on diplomacy and backstabbing. It plays like the old Dune board game in a much more complex way. It's a psycholgical exchange of blows. The computer opponent is not (yet) a challenge, but the developers are working on it. The game is fantastic in multiplayer and the best part is the asynchronous mode. In addition to live games, you can play over several days with fixed moves every 24 hours or over a longer period of time. You can easily find players via the discord. An absolute highlight in the strategy sector and definitely unique if, like me, you haven't played the predecessor.

_childDocuments_.review: So many of the other negative reviews well sum up my experience, but I want to make sure to emphasis that this isn't a bad game per se. The graphics are great, setting is neat, general premise is nice. Some systems are cool, but yeah... The best way I can put it is that I played it back when they had the demo live during... Next Fest I think? I had played it, and it had stuck with me, but for some reason I hadn't wishlisted it. I got it, played a full 50 turn game, and remembered why I hadn't. To me, and I'm going to emphasise that this is my subjective view, there isn't enough difference between games. There are multiple options for what you do per turn, but you're limited in how many actions you can take. This means that, unfortunately, you can technically rank your actions, and there's very little that will modify those rankings. It makes it very repetitive, but not in a good way. Also, the fact that like EVERYTHING costs tokens just... kills me at times. It's another area that, like the limit on how many things you can do per tern, makes it so you can personally rank all actions, and anything too low you just ignore. It makes it so you can ignore whole systems in the game if you want to because they cost more than they're worth to you. I mean in all my play throughs (3, 2 in demo, 1 in live), I never used rituals. Manuscripts? Barely touched. Powers? Never really saw the benefit. Diplomacy? The AI targets you enough you can just bunker up. I had an overwhelming victory with 2x the prestige of the next guy down and being a Demon Prince, while having only spend tokens on legions, praetors, and then any duel that was put against me bribing the hell out of the judge. Like the fact that that braindead strategy worked that well just pains me, because I actually love a lot about this game. Because the games are all set with a fixed number of turns you really only need to take 2 places of power, and then just bunker up. Going after Pandemonium? Not worth it. Taking out competitors? Too many restrictions and again, just generally not worth it. All your need is that delicious prestige. Honestly, if you're in doubt and reading this, get it, and try it. I realise after my rant above that may sound weird, but there are a lot of things in this game I like, but the base systems just prevented me from loving it. This may not be the case for you, so give it a go.(Editing for an obvious spelling mistake I missed)

_childDocuments_.review: I'll give a brief review as I don't have the time to make one as long as I would like to. 1) The art direction: Every card/illustration is perfectly done. Whoever is responsible for the art needs a bonus and well deserved vacation. ( from artist to artist, really good job ).... however whoever is responsible for the map and the archfiend models clearly didn't look at the mood board for the game. Hell ( lol ), it might as well have been done by an outsourced fiverr artist for a few hundred dollars. None of the models look fitting at all with the serious tone of the game. I don't know how this happened, but mind you. It is jarring to the point of immersion breaking.2) Pacing. listen I understand games  are supposed to go on for weeks and weeks, but damn does that destroy the audience you're trying to appeal to. There's gotta be available modes for this game like any other 4x game so i'm not having to speed click 1,000 times a game to get to my next turn vs AI. If it's multiplayer and y'all are sitting down for a few hours to play this game, you'll be sitting waiting for half of that time. 3) AI in all these games are trash. I'm not even mad, but i needed to point it out.4) This is veryyy specific of a critique, but the Excommunication council vote ends your run and ends your fun. This is the most stupid mechanic I've seen in a 4x. Everyone just randomly gets to vote someone off the island??? WHICH LOCKS THEM OUT OF THE BAZAAR in turn means you can't do anything interactive in the game anymore. no diplomacy. no bazaar for units or items or whatever. You're forced to go the tyrannical route and pray you don't get smashed or you'll have a shorten run.I like the illustrations, I like the card mechanics, I like the progression of your archfiend and legions.I hate the pacing, character and building models, and excommunication. The game in it's current state is a 3/10 for me. If the models and map are redone to fit the illustrations and tone better it would go up to a 6/10 easily. Excommunication being removed from the council vote would then land the game at a 7. The rest of the things holding this game back are too minor and numerous for me to list out and they are things i see being fixed in the future. The art is so concerning to me as I can't imagine they would through the effort to fix it. None of my friends will even touch this game because it looks visually that bad.I will continue to play the game because I do enjoy it, but I wish it just looked better so it would catch more people's eyes especially my friends.

_childDocuments_.review: The best thing about Solium is the asynchronous multiplayer mode, which is implemented well and generally worked as intended for me. Unfortunately, half the game design is bad: duels, high-level powers, generally obtuse mechanics (presumably a "feature"  given the setting, but makes for a very dissatisfying game play experience), massive balance issues across the board. Not for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an excellent premise with a lovely aesthetic. It's got a lot of room for different strategies and the vibe is pristine.It just doesn't work. Simultaneous games and asynchronous games both have this charming habit of suddenly not letting turns advance. My friends and I tried leaving and rejoining but eventually even that stopped kicking it back to life. I fear this game is more limbo than hell. We have a game that's locked on the final turn and will NOT kick over to conclude. This has happened in two of our last 3 games. I really want to love this product, it's so close to being something amazing. But certain things JUST NOT WORKING makes it literally impossible to play.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: terrible. At least the price tag matches the theme, because it is a blasphemy to charge so much for this mess.---I picked this one up after reading reviews, saying it is basically is a Civ V in hellish setting, amazing concept and idea, I was hyped about it, but oh boy that was a lie. The game is an empty board game simulator and offers literally nothing. No diplomacy except demanding resources, no conquering (because the game will end long before it is possible), no territory expansion, no city building (???????), no alliances, no nothing. In single player you can do 2-3 actions per turn (and for the first twenty turns you are forced to do nothing except gathering resources anyway), meanwhile the AI does 5-10 (they will move 3 legions, send a demand, play a event card, perform a ritual and bid on a new legion in one turn). In multiplayer the player who is lucky enough with tributes to max out their talent tree (deceit usually, cuz its broken) wins, that is it.Probably the most disappointing and misadvertised of all video games I have ever tried.

_childDocuments_.review: The game can be a lot of fun. It's made by the creators of Armello, but if you've come from that game looking for a similar experience like myself, just be aware of two things:1) The game is far more complex. The map is far larger and there's far more things you'll be interested in doing on your turns. Rituals, buying units/praetors/artifacts/manuscripts, move units, attack, insult, rank up, plot schemes, cast rituals, upgrade your abilities, demand tribute, dueling, attaching praetors/artifacts etc. That's just the shortlist, there's far more. This complexity can easily be a positive or a negative for you depending on who you are.The problem with this is that for a large portion of the game, you can only perform two of these actions per turn. EVERYTHING you do takes an action point. Even consolidating your money (which is basically grouping coins into bags) takes an action PER consolidation. Just taking the time to do it so you can buy better units can feel like such a waste of time because that's half your turn gone playing accountant. A lot of the time you feel like you've accomplished absolutely nothing in your turn. And to be honest you probably haven't. Anything you want to get done will likely take a lot of waiting through many turns before you can actually achieve it. And that's just assuming no other player interferes and delays it further. Later in the game, you can gain access to more actions per turn, but it does take a long while. It's a real shame because it does leave you in a game with so many options but so little agency to exploit any but a few.2) Games are long. Quite long. I played a "Very Short Game", a 30-turn game and it took me 3 hours to complete. It's not exactly Civ sort of length games, but as a game that plays very differently, you might not expect it. Not to mention, it can also FEEL longer as well due to my earlier point and also because the game doesn't actually end on turn 30. You then enter the endgame phase where the winner gets to be decided. Except it's really not clear how long the endgame lasts. The endgame is supposed to last 5 phases. But how many turns a phase is seems random. It didn't move from 3/5 for a while. And then it jumped from 4/5 to 5/5 in 1 turn. Then it stayed on 5/5 for ages. My game for instance didn't actually end until turn 41. I felt myself just sitting there after my turn repetitively thinking "yep this is it, the game is finally going to let me win now". I see what they're going for but it causes a lot of issues because you can't really plan ahead to win by the end of endgame because you have absolutely no clue when it's finally going to end.Everything I have mentioned above you can find as positives, or negatives. More just notes to be aware of. Perhaps you enjoy the slow-paced, limited-action strategy this game offers. Perhaps you don't, I find myself sitting on the fence. I reckon you'll have a lot more of a blast playing with friends. The art-style is great and I'm sure there's a lot more fun to be had once we all get some more hours in.

_childDocuments_.review: You do not need to work around anybody’s schedule and playing with randoms is easy. You do your turn before the timer runs out (from 24h to a week per turn). Other players submit theirs on time - it doesn’t matter if someone’s turn was done in the 1st hour or 23:59th minute. If you want -  Steam shoots  you notifications when the next turn is ready to play. You have a limited number of action slots ( 2 initially but you can get as many as 6 over the course of a match ) per turn, and you make strategic decisions with every move - No adjusting a tax slider from 14.5% to 14.76%. Limited number of actions also helps to speed up the turns - you cannot queue a long line of orders that you then keep readjusting as the situation changes. You are scheming your way to the throne of Hell. Each match has a set turn timer and the victory conditions are clearly defined (There is 1 main victory condition and 3 alternative ways to steal victory) - You are not building an empire or managing a logistic network - There is no chance for someone to be so far ahead that they could be as well be playing SimCity.- If anything, being clearly in the lead paints a huge target on your back , and you can get disqualified from the main victory condition, or just outright eliminated by other players. You have to be the most sneaky crab in the  bucket - Hell is other people after all. The visual side of the game is well above what you usually get in the genre. Not only does the game have actual graphics unlike many turn-based strategy games, but also the art direction is solid and the style is consistent with the theme and across all elements - the clear and stylish visuals make it not only more pleasant to play, but help you remember the events of the match as you log back in.  Regular match AI doesn’t seem to pose any challenge, but there are single player scenarios with more specific victory requirements that should provide some variety. The main focus of the game is Multiplayer, and the asynchronous mode should make it easier to get started, even if you have never managed to play strategy games online. If you are not touching MP out of principle - first of all, asynchronous is a game changer give it a go, secondly  wait for the patches to either improve the AI or add either more scenarios, or perhaps add a scenario editor so that the community can do its thing and provide the game with more longevity. As far as I can see the game doesn’t seem to have a way to penalise quitters, so joining some sort of discord or other group might be necessary long term to ensure commitment until the end.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't going to write a review until I saw they bumped the price to 58 AUD from about 39 which I'd purchased it at. I think this is a ridiculous price to ask for it.At this stands, it is a beautiful adaptation of a board game to a computer setting but it's like paying 60$ per person for a boardgame in order to play it. You could get the same experience with a 40$ actual boardgame with the same premise. There's cool art for all the unit cards but the combat animations are dull and the same for each unit, the map is really interesting and the flavour text is good but those are all things that a good board game kinda does anyway. There's a wide variety of ways to play but they fundamentally boil down to character choice so there's no thinking on the fly or change of strategies. if you choose the war Archfiend, regardless of any change in circumstance you will be recruiting troops and invading, you're locked out of schemes/rituals to an extent that you feel like why bother unless you're playing the Scheme Archfiend. The main reason for this is you have a limit of two actions in a turn when simply moving a unit or raising tribute counts as one action. So if all you want to do is move a unit, raise some gold and insult someone it's too many things, you can only do two, which feels really restricting.It's not so much it isn't enjoyable to do these things, just all of them feel quite 2D and like part of a whole which never comes together. None of the options available for victory are attractive enough by themselves, I kinda hoped it would be a mixture of all of them but when you can only take two actions per turn (including raising money and moving troops) it just bogs down your turn and you feel restricted in what you can do. In short, this is a 40$ boardgame they've remade digitally to basically produce an inferior product. Is it fun? sure, but not when to get four people playing you'd need to spend 240$ to experience it.

_childDocuments_.review: Solium Infernum is a great example of taking popular board game elements and blending it into a great strategy game you can play with other people. A lot of classic Eurogame elements are present here like auctions, leveling up, collecting tokens, and plenty of event cards. You're an Archdevil and you want to rule hell, since Satan's mysteriously gone. Using the might of your armies, magic, and the infernal bureaucracy against your enemies you all are trying to get established as the new lord of darkness. Every devil has a special ability, a personal legion and stronghold. There's impressive balance and forethought in these abilities, making them tools to use rather than central to their entire strategy. The focus is on capturing points of power to generate more prestige and empower your magics; spend prestige to increase your rank so that you gather better tribute. Tribute in turn lets you strengthen your magics and commit more orders per turn. Direct conquest is rarely necessary, but remains an option. A lot of the mid-game relies on identifying weak players and bullying them every few turns for their resources. if they decline then you embarass them in the arena or in warfare. Winning three wars against a player lets you declare blood feud and destroy their base. Alternatively, you can just storm the palace and seize the throne for yourself; though this kicks you out of the conclave and revokes your prestige. Gameplay is really tight. you can do 2-6 things every turn, based on how many level four stats you have. This makes turn times short and it's generally pretty easy to identify what you want to do. Unlocking your order slots early is the most important part of winning, because that is the clearest indicator of power. This makes a non-aggressive strategy just as viable as an aggressive one, since you can just sit in the shadows and accumulate strength. Oh, did I mention that there's items you can take before games that let you declare other players as false winners? You can wear a crown that lets you declare that if somebody else wins, you win. There's a mix of good and bad design here. Hell looks like Mordor, and Satan's palace just looks like the tower of Sauron. All of the legions just look like orcs. On the lava map you even get Mt. Doom, all we need is a few hobbits and we've got an off brand Mordor strategy game. This isn't a bad thing, but it's kind of weird that they could of went with some amazing visuals but the 3d modeller just went for LOTR Orcs. The other thing is that Lilith is incorrectly portrayed as a harpy because she is entitled "leader of the harpies" in Hell, despite the furry harpies being completely different folklore, all depictions of Lilith are of a fair skinned woman with red eyes. Beelzebub is a literal fly because they are lord of the flies... yeah the character design sucks. The AI is bad. Really bad. On the lava map, your enemies will just sit in lava the whole time and die. Most of the time they just patrol around their land and try to prevent other from taking points yet never really try to take points themselves. They buy titans and then don't pay upkeep, they summon zombies and then waste magic to heal them every turn, they launch suicidal wars, they all gang up on the weakest player, near the end of the game their prestige values implode and plummet. To say the game is easy in singleplayer is an understatment. Another major negative is the developers themselves, who clearly have good intentions but comes off as... let's say "very controlling"; and I don't think it's helped market the game to buyers. For one they want to segregate out people that didn't buy the game from being allowed to post or get attention from the devs, they actually posted that this is their intention on the forum itself claiming that by not regarding people that didn't buy the game as people, the community is much healthier. Now, this obviously makes no sense because at the end of the day there will always be trolls and simply ignoring literally everybody else because of a few trolls is just fascism; which makes sense for the guys that exclusively make games about monarchy and slavery. Kinda clear where their heads at.SI is a fantastic game to play with others, though the game's focus on the constant bullying of your neighbors may grow tiring to some of your friends who dislike the "Republican Workplace Simulator" tone of the game. Those that like aggressive games will enjoy the short format, in your face nature of the game, and the fact that it's generally difficult to eliminate other players.

_childDocuments_.review: Quickly becomes boring and tedious.  I would refund if I didn't have 2.9 hours on the game.First, let's talk about how complicated it is to engage in warfare.  No, you don't get to just move onto enemy tiles or attack an army.  No, you don't just have to declare war first.  What you have to do is the following:1. Go to diplomacy tab. 2. Insult enemy or demand tribute from them.3. Wait one turn.4. If enemy refuses tribute or does not accept insult, you get to declare a vendetta.  You then have to set a rather underwhelming sounding goal such as "kill one troop" or "take a couple hexes" and decide how long you have to accomplish your goal.The implication, of course, is that a subpar power can just keep taking insults and giving up tribute to forestall their annihilation, which is exactly what happened with me and Lilith.  The whole system is annoying and doesn't make sense: I'm playing a violent sociopath in hell.  Why is it so hard to declare war on an archfiend?Oh, and vendettas don't even let you take over an enemy stronghold.  No, you need more justification to actually eliminate a player.Then there's the currency system.  Why are there like 10 different currencies?  Why can I only have so many of a certain type of currency?  What am I actually doing when I consolidate currency? Because as far as I can tell, I'm not seeing any new coin pop up in my treasury, like I just exchanged pennies for a dollar.  Am I really throwing money away and calling it consolidating?  And again, why is this consolidation thing a mechanic?  Did someone on the design team just really not like big numbers?Perhaps the worst part of the game is the two-action economy. Would you like to move your armies? Moving one army is an action.  Moving two is two actions.  Like to do some diplomacy? Every interaction with a foreign leader is an action.  Like to level up your archfiend? Action.  Appoint a general? Action!  Bid on troops? Another action.  Learn a spell or scheme? Action. It turns every turn into a nightmare of tedium where you barely accomplish anything.Ah yes, I did say bid on troops.  Like an auction.  You'll also bid on generals.  Meaning, in theory, at least, you can throw your money away on something you will never use.  You'll also only have 3 options available any turn for troops, generals, artifacts, and so on.  Most will be unaffordable.  Just to add one more headache.Great game idea, terrible execution.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: I do not leave many reviews but this game and League of Geeks deserve it.Simply put, this game is one of the most amazing backstabbing strategy games I have ever played. I has compelling characters, factions, and well-thought of innovative mechanics.It received quite a lot of undeserved backlash at the beginning from casual 4X singleplayers... Because that is not what the game is about... thankfully!This game is all about political intrigue in the underworld. It requires cunning, planning, and a plethora of dark intrusive thoughts!Think of games such as Dominions, Diplomacy, even a bit of Scythe thrown into the mix, a lot of "Gotcha!" moments, evil plans that take turns to come into fruition... Speaking of Dominions, turns are resolved simultaneously (witha clever initiative system) and this is one of the only games that has a well-implemented turn registration and notification system. If you wish to play a month long campaign with your friends on and off because you have a time-demanding job (random example, I don't know what you are talking about), you can configure the game in such a way that everyday you can set up your turn (it takes 10-20 minutes) and then wait for the next day or until everyone has validated their actions for the turn, and bis repetitam until one of you is crowned ruler of Hell :)The developpers have a let's play with insight into each of the players' strategies and it is really fun to watch!I can't recommend this game enough and the studio needs all the support it can get to continue supporting this game!PS: Even though I've personally had a lot of fun in SP with it, the true fun lies with your friends and even with a bit of RP thrown into the mix ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: What a game! Hellish strategy, very unique and very innovative. The graphics and the gameplay create fantastic atmosphere of hell, machinations, lies and deception. I loved especially the diplomacy mechanics which gives you just the right options to humiliate the enemy or to take the revenge in different ways. It takes couple of games and hours to learn all the mechanics and tricks (tutorial will give you solid foundation, but by far not everything), but all of those hours were very enjoyable. Finally, after some 25 hours I was able to defeat all AIs on hellish and it was brutal from the beginning to the very end. I was often angry, felt deceived and was cursing my opponents for their unfairness, i.e. truly a hell (exactly what the game promises), but in a way a strategical heaven :-) I loved my 25 hours and although it is time to move on to another game, I already know I will return to this brilliant strategy game soon. My respect to the devs!

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favourite strategy games of all time; a truly unique and complex game that 100% deserves more attention than it gets.While this game does share the same basic makeup to games like Civilisation, the focus is entirely different, with scheming and diplomacy being at the forefront of the game. You win the game by manipulating your opponent into wars they can't win and completing 'schemes', rather than conquering territory.This makes multiplayer especially enjoyable when up to 6 of you are playing off against each other in a bid to take over hell. One of the game's greatest features is the Asynchronous multiplayer, where you can set up a game with turn times of 1 day - 5 days, meaning everyone can submit their turns in their own time.I have 5 of these on the go currently and it is great fun to do in between work.combine all this with a beautiful looking game with stunning art, and you can see why this is one of my favourite strategy games of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Prob the best strategy game of the year. Instead of long buildinglists and micromanaging your workers this game instead focuses on a few things, while still providing a lot of depth. This is due, to making 3 to max 6 decisions per turn (plus diplomacy).The main aspects are:1. War with your legions: Their strengths can be adjusted by rituals, artificats, gladiators and strategems. Later you summon titans, which are a small army in itself.2. Rituals: Destroy or steal enemy legions, give yourself more prestige, steal artificats or ressources from the enemy. 3. Gladiatorfights: You either win a war on the battlefield or in the arena. It is a valid strategy to focus solely on one guy and win every battle for prestige for example, while not having a real army to back it up.You either win via prestige or by capturing the main city, pandemonium. There are rules which kinda protect you, such as it is mostly prohibited to capture a main city and eleminate an enemy. If you attack pandemonium, there are no rules binding you anymore, but you have to capture it now to win the game ultimately.What happened to me last game:The vassal of Lilith (Liltih is winning the game atm) attacks pandemonium, so she isnt the vassal anymore. Now she is able to capture liliths main city and eleminates her, bc her troops are too far away to protect it. Secondly she also overwhelms my city and eleminates me, while I was fighting another guy.At that moment I had 400 prestige and she had 0 (attacked pandemonium) and I was about to win the game in 3 rounds, bc Lilith was no more. I did savescum to see if I could prevent it and it was possible, but holy moly. This ♥♥♥♥ is awesome

That's probably the biggest disappointment in this game for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Forget what they want you to believe and consider the facts: The heavens have one and only ruler, who exiles dissidents to a barren, lightless abyss of suffering. That sounds like a full-fledged dictatorship. Meanwhile, these powerful dissidents establish a Conclave which, though dark and corrupt, functions as a Parliament. Thus, Hell is a democracy.Ask yourselves some questions and consider the answers.Solium Infernum is a gem. It's immersive—its OST is a masterpiece, and the sounds, colors, and ambiance capture your senses, drawing you into the Abyss. It's strategically deep, unpredictable, and often frustrating.You play as a mighty and powerful Archfiend, one of Lucifer's lieutenants. The dark ruler of Hell has disappeared for unknown reasons, and the Conclave must elect his successor. The game unfolds as a digital tabletop experience, with a procedural map full of points of interest and varied terrain. Each player starts in their citadel, with a limited number of actions per turn—moving a legion, casting a spell, harvesting tributes (currency), engaging in diplomacy, and more. These actions can be increased by reaching the fourth level of each skill. Skills shape your playstyle: do you want more legions? More powerful rituals? Greater influence within the Conclave? The choice is yours. Legions, commanders, spells, artifacts, and more are represented as beautifully designed cards. Once you've selected your action, you end your turn and watch what the other players have done. Keep in mind that all actions are resolved at the end of the turn, starting with the first player's first action, then the second player's, and so on. This makes it crucial to choose the order of your actions wisely. The first player changes every turn, usually in a cyclical manner, though this can be altered by specific voting events.Hell is a paradise (pun intended) for bureaucracy, where troop movements, battles, and aggressive rituals cannot be executed without Conclave approval. Battles, for instance, can only occur if you manage to declare—or provoke your enemy into declaring—a feud. Similarly, you cannot move into another Archfiend's territory without the proper authorization, which is why diplomacy is so important. However, before calling it "diplomacy," remember that the game is set in Hell—so there are no alliances or peace. You can only insult, extort your "f(r)iends," or kneel before them as a weak blood vassal or tributary, knowing that you're likely to lose the game (unless you're extremely cunning).The strategic depth of Solium Infernum is astounding. The game offers a wide range of possible actions, from espionage—especially in multiplayer, where human players are more unpredictable than AI—to research, and so on, culminating in combat, which adds another layer of strategy. Every legion has three stats: ranged, melee, and magic. These are resolved in the order listed, but captains, heroes, stratagems, rituals, terrain, neighboring legions, and artifacts can all provide bonuses or penalties, or even change the resolution order.And this is just scratching the surface! Of course, a review shouldn't be overly detailed, but it also shouldn't be too vague. It's important to help readers make an informed purchase—a purchase which, in my opinion, is well worth your time.--- EDIT ---Of course I have voted Solium Infernum as Game of the Year, thus granting some juicy souls to my coffers

Especially since the bland meta is to build up your forces, do a small, non-consequential raid pandemonium to excommunicate yourself, kill everyone else, win. Solid game, would love to see some future updates to it soon.Edit: totally was hooked on this because a friend recommended the demo to me so great job with including a solid demo that not even warhammer 3 is daring to try especially with the heafty overpriced DLC.EX Edit: I forgot to mention how it would be nice to see more Points of Power so that the many option doesn't feel like the all option. _childDocuments_.review: With a discount, I really recommend if you like strategy boardgames.I played the solo scenarios first. They were all fun as they push you to learn the different mechanics bit by bit.I didnt like the DLC character though. Took me 7-8 tries before catching how to make it work.It killed the fun out of the game for me :)There is a lack of polish, and lack of basic information about the game that makes it a bit cringe sometimes.No research bar in the codex (over 100 entries). No level of your elites in the codex (which count for half the damage during duels). Some power (like Belial's) over-riding diplomatic orders with no explanations. Etc...I think a simple manual (wether in-game or wiki) should be put out. That s what this game needs to really be up there: a way for players to learn the rules without having to test and memorize everything that is not explained.The AI difficult rises with uncertain bonus too. Nothing is explained there also.Rituals are based on a dice roll depending on your power versus their defense: your never know what kind of percent chance it is, and you dont know how raising your power or lowering their defense impact the percent chance. That s a super vital info to plan ahead.So a lot is missing.But it is still good, with a discount.Best,

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, I have grown quite fond of it in just a few days, but it could achieve greatness (IMO), if they changed/included these points:- No election game mode, prestige would be made expendable for additional legion experience or resources (games tend to get interesting just when the council is about to vote).- Give each non-titan legion their own campaign map model.- More flavour in neutral enemies, the barbarian camp mechanic from Civilization could fit pretty well.- Make more elavorate maps (make continents and separated landmasses with lava oceans in between for example) and for the love of satan, make an interface map so you can move your camera directly to the point you want and be able to have a strategic view of what is going on.- Some rituals are downright op, being able to bribe praetors and steal artifacts is unhealthy for the game, and is too easy nonetheless, I would make those rituals destroy the item instead and make them cost more tokens. The level 6 destruction ritual which restricts an archfiend's order slots to 1 is also pretty stupid, since you have no way of countering it unless you manage to sabotage the culprit's resources (ongoing rituals should have a limit of turns and then enter cooldown and/or introduce a way of stopping them for the victim, spending tokens for example, wich could not only put those rituals in cooldown but also give you immunity for some turns).I could think of more but those are the main issues wich could propel the game to the hall of fame, I highly recommend this game to anyone who loves 4x games and the aesthetic of hell!!
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: If you love strategy games, you owe yourself to play this one. The gameplay is awesome, the systems are beautifully designed, the UI is sleek, and the visuals and theming are a dollup of hellish cream on top. The AI could be a bit better, but this is a game that was made to be played online first-and-foremost. Quick word of warning however: I'm a single-player kind of person, and while I found a lot to love with the single-player mode (the Chronicles, which are challenge scenarios), they are quite challenging, and the learning-curve is steep. If you're here for the same reason, be ready to bump your head against the same Chronicles a few times before your succeed.

T_T

_childDocuments_.review: The game does its thing well, well flavoured towards the "evil" Hellish beauraucracy of myth.Combat, intrigues and politics are all done simply enough to be approachable for a beginner, but with enough fine points to wrangle a little satisfaction from getting just right.Not a game of building so much as endless machiavellian intrigues, it isn't exactly a competitor for Civilisation, but fun in its own way and priced appropriately.Would be interesting to see a few opportunities to mimic a "holy" side also, playing out the lore of devils as rebel angels seeking to cling to their vestiges of sanctity while actually trying to build their own heaven (as they allude to in the introduction), but hey, what's there works just fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun political strategy game that allows for multiple strategies to assume the throne. My favorite thing about this game is that theres no traditional tech or economy so it makes people who do nothing but metagame econ booms actually have to think about the game and develop new strategies. 10/10 in my book.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Admittedly I don't play a lot of asynchroneous strategy games, or strategy games in general (the only one that I enjoy that comes even remotely close is HoMM3), but this game has almost everything that I would want out of this kind of game - There're unique characters, you can level up yourself, you can level up your troops, there's a lot of diplomacy and different spells and a whole bunch of strategic options but it's all packaged relatively tightly to not feel *too* overwhelming and has a really cool theme and art around it. Some parts do feel rather clunky but not anywhere near enough to worsen the experience.Really cool game, never played anything quite like it!

LoGs remake delivers on every aspect, streamlining some fiddly parts, providing a graphical overhaul with quality of life improvements to UI, making setting up multiplayer games a breeze, and with beautiful artwork to boot. _childDocuments_.review: I bought it purely for it's art design and 2D illustrations. _childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: It took me some time, but I can say confidently I love this game. The triumph when you win is worth the challenge. The artwork is gorgeous. I have some very favourite praetors and legions. The mechanics can be brutal but there is a counter for everything. I especially love playing the chronicles- having the extra win conditions is a fun extra thing to strive for.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: I first played the demo of the game before the full release and I enjoyed it, wanting more. The art work for the cards was something I found amazing, feeling really demonic. It does take a little bit a time to understand the game and moves, but where's the fun in that if it's easy. Better to rule than to serve.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Solium Infernum has been described as "Civilisation in Hell", which in fact I think, does the game injustice: it is one of the more unusual and refreshing strategy games out there with some quite original mechanics and approaches to issues which other strategy games generally solve the same way. The learning curve is a bit rough but not prohibitively so. The game gives you multiple vectors and tools for reaching victory and lend itself to multiple playstyles.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Some minor details could be included in the tooltips, like that you can not move through your own units or at what skillrank specific spells get unlocked and the cost of diplomatic actions and spells. So one could plan their first few turns outside of a game or just try to scheme more efficiently. Some relics feel quite a lot more useful than others, not necessarily more powerful. Maybe could have used voice chat but there is a discord from LoG where you can also find lobbies. That said, this is the only criticism i could come up with at this point. This game has multiple interlocking progression systems that interlock and support as well as detract from one another, depending on the situation. Adding to that, there are potentials for mindgames. It can feel like you do not have a lot of agency, but that very much depends on your playstyle, only relying on one strategy to win with no plan to fall back on or almost perfect defenses, meaning potentially having to build them in your loadout before the game, will result in a loss. Your opponents simply are not AI and you are never invulnerable. Honestly, I wish I knew of a game this style that is more complex with as good gamedesign. Play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like Async mode in any game. I don't like overused combination of red and black in any form of art. I don't like extremely slow and tedious games. I don't like waiting. I don't like lack of QoL features, messy UI / UX anywhere.. Except, this game somehow manages to make me like all of them at once.Almost like all of it is on purpose to make it all more immersive and meaningful. The game is great. Highly recommend it in Async mode after you get used to its mechanics in live games.Gorgeous art. Epic titans. Cool maneuvers you can do. Every move matters. Lots of cool tricks and things to learn. Feels satisfying when it all goes according to your plan. When a trick you try pull off works out. Some things will seem broken at first, but it all makes sense afterwards.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun especially if you convince friends to play with you. It's a lot like Civ, but in hell! Being able to find games to play with other people has been fun as well. Although, there normally aren't a lot of games open at any given time. If you can't find any games, it's easier to go onto their discord to find people. I'm hoping it ends up gaining more popularity making it easier to find games.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant game what can I say! It has all the right elements, works perfectly in async which was unexpected. You can plan a game night with your friends, play for 2 hours go to bed and then play some slow turns to later on plan another night to finish the game. It's all possible because of how smart the game works.If you like boardgames and like strategic games like CIV then this game is a perfect one to play. 10/10 for me so far!
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: A game of uneasy neighbours and hellish betrayal, this game truly shines for multiplayer. You need to be a little competitive for it, but you're looking at board-game video games on Steam, you probably are. Play Asessional if you've a few hours to sink into a faster paced game, play Asynchronous to slow burn a campaign over 30+ days.Your fellow (im)mortals contend best for the throne. Will one max wrath to rule them all? Will the charismatic line their coffers and dominate through duels? With prophetic insight, you can stave off the destructive and deceitful rituals intent on sapping the life from your prized legions or stealing your souls and silver.There's a lot to this game to explore because the information is limited. A definite tier to the items, the necessity of economy, the dangers any foe can pose to that expensive new artifact you just bought. Once you get the precarious balance between plans, power and potential, you'll be a match for any lesser contender to the throne.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Not a very difficult game to pick up mechanics-wise. However, having to balance various resources (including how many orders you can give per turn!) means you'll constantly be trying to find the best choice among a list of bad ones. The game also rewards backstabbing and being an overall "little ♥♥♥♥" to the other players. Asynchronous turns allow you to also play PvP games at your pace instead of having to spend hours in a single game that may not be returned to (looking at you Stellaris).I also can't keep from mentioning the amazing artwork (most of which seems to have been made by Dominik Mayer). It definitely captures the atmosphere and lore where you not only are battling with your fellow arch demons, but incursions by holy saints and angels in service of "the Tyrant". I get hints of Wayne Barlowe's work with the glowing sigils and "native" inhabitants of hell.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: The game is alright. It has a lot of good things going for it but the core needs work. i.e.: 1. When making a game with a friend, the turn order can't be changed (the host always goes 1st and the 2nd human player goes second, meaning the host plays before their friend for 5 of the 6 turns)2. The AI is very bad. It's almost impossible to lose to AI so you need to play with people (which is fine and good, but always playing either right before or right after your friend is an issue).3. This may be a steam issue, but the game always tells me that I have a turn waiting. 9/10 times there isn't actually a turn waiting. I end up booting the game just to close it right back.The cherry on top that deserved the negative review is that before polishing the game, they're releasing paid DLC instead.Not a bad game overall, but it's not even close to being worth the cost in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: I EFFING LOVE THIS GAME. I CANNOT STOP HITTING THE NEXT TURN BUTTON. OH MY GOD PLEASE HELP ME. IT HAS MY SOOUUUUULLLLLL.Can't wait to see what kind of love the devs show this game because if they keep adding content (artifacts, legions, maps, PoPs); just to add the feel of a larger game and add some more randomness to different playthroughs, this game will be near perfection!
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: A refreshing take on hex-grid turn based strategy. It's not a civilization builder; instead, it's more of a game of intrigue and politics, maneuvers and counterplay. I'm looking forward to exploring all of the nuance.Also, the art is brilliant. I just wish each of the legions were a bit more uniquely modeled (the Titans are huge and easily recognizeable!).
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: The game concept is definitely something special, and I think it's a pity that you dropped Jumplight Odyssey, but you've released a little project close to your heart here. You can see it in the animation of the Archfiends, in the layout of the menu, in the descriptive texts, the entries from the Libri Inferni and - I'm glad to finally get to this point - in the soundtrack.The whole soundscape is an all-encompassing experience.The notification sound when a certain event occurs, and the songs of the OST in general. I would definitely have many more hours in this game if you add in the time I spent listening to the OST and working on my own interpretations.Thank you from the bottom of my heart for allowing me to experience this.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: This's a fascinating game, with intricacies inside intricacies. It rarely feels unfair, but perhaps you lost track of an essential detail along the way that could turn into what the entire match hinges upon. (or you kept track, and are pressing the advantage to victory)It lends itself well to games with people you know, and the revival of async gameplay is delightful. I've already gotten my value's worth, and I can only hope the studio continues hammering on it and refining it for years to come

_childDocuments_.review: The look and feel of the the game is really cool. The artwork is fantastic with a cool soundtrack to go with it.There is a lot going on gameplay wise, so much to take in all at once but after playing a few games you get a handle on the basics and start to find cool ways to use all these options together. Soon you'll plotting your way to the top of hell over the bodies off your fellow fiends.The asynchronous multiplayer is really good addition when you find a good group to play with.
