_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: The game is extremely well done. You get a very limited number of actions each turn (2 at the beginning of the game) which makes every move feel super consequential. The theme is obviously a big draw and they do a good job of differentiating each 'faction'. Combat is easy to understand, engaging and very consequential. The biggest problem with the game is frankly the price. It's trying to compete with far bigger titles at this price and it should have had a four pack to encourage multiplayer since that's really where the game shines.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: The cool thing about this game is that there is more than one strategy to get to the throne. Playing the game thus far, there are several delightful and rewarding ways to win the game. Here are a few fun examples in my time playing.1: Ruling over an empty hell as Andromalius by framing everyone by launching false flag destruction spells on Pandemonium posing as the other players. Everyone was excommunicated. I hunted down everyone and put them to the sword, leaving me winner by default. 2: Usurper Victory is hard, but I was able to do it once as Lilith. Got a pair of units so strong they sacked Pandemonium in a single turn. Proceeded to once again rule over an empty hell by killing all the other archfiends. 3: Tried to go for kingmaker once as Belial. My puppet was Mammon. The dude was a complete muppet and threw the match. Had to transition to election victory by going ham on the praetor duels. Murmur completely obliterated my armies with destruction spells and I barely squeaked by. Shows that you don't have to commit to one strategy. You can definitely transition to something else. Overall, this variety in the available strategies is definitely one of the most fascinating aspects of this game. It adds a layer of unpredictablilty to this game, making you wonder what the other guy is going for. Don't really have any friends to do this multiplayer, but this game is honestly just as fun with the AI. They are competent enough to punish you if you play sloppy. League of Geeks outdid themselves with this one. Would absolutely recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. It's been enormously satisfying learning the gameplay and digging into the strategy. At the same time, the flavor of hell and the archfiends is so good. Nothing feels better than sending a catty but dignified letter to gloat about a victory on the battlefield. Can't wait to see how the game continues to develop after release.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: It's the kind of game that unless you know literally every mechanic (there are a LOT of them and they don't make them easy to know), you're basically ineffective and will have a very bad time playing it.Half of this game is really baked and beautiful and wants to be something really deliberate and precise. And the other half of the game hasn't even been put in the oven yet. There's just a lot of mechanics and things that happen and nobody knows why and the game doesn't bother allowing you a way to actually figure out what's going on until after it occurs. You're just constantly surprised by things and it's frustrating.For something that really wants to be based on a board game, they completely wiffed.  It's a board game for rules lawyers in all the worst kinds of ways.(Also the price is bonkers, lol wtf were they thinking)

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic strategy/board game. If you have a group of friends, playing this game in an asynchronous way is almost certainly going to be memorable. It may look daunting, but the restricted number of possible moves (orders) each turn keeps things manageable and there are so many ways of  promoting your strategy, the decisions are always interesting.It has been receiving good post-launch support from the devs, and I look forward to seeing what they intend to do with the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Such a good & clever strategy game ! I want to start by commenting on what several people said, that this is more of a boardgame than a strategy game. Well that actually motivated me even more to get the game even if in the end I don't quite agree wit this comment. the "Actions" mechanic can seem a bit boardgamey but (to me) this is a 4X (albeit light on the eXplore) with a good focus long term agenda. _childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: I have just fallen in love with this game, the intrigue, the backstabbing, how every play MUST be bold, decisive and confident. I just adore this game and with the asynchronous multiplayer you can play every day even if you only have 10-30 minutes of available time. _childDocuments_.review: An awesome refresh of an old somewhat slept on strategy classic- the devs has preserved most of what made the original game great, while reworking some core mechanics entirely. Some of these changes are (in my opinion) direct improvements, like re-balancing the stats and what they do, while others are wholesale replacement systems that are different, but also good. As noted in some other reviews, the AI is not super good at the game, but it's good enough to learn the basic ins and outs. The real fun is playing against other humans though!For newcomers, the biggest draws for this game compared to other strategy games are (In my opinion)- The odd formalized diplomacy & war systems: Instead of games like Civ where you can just declare war whenever you want, here you are bound by the rules of the infernal court, and you must manufacture a casus belli with demands and insults. Once it comes time for war, whoever is the official Aggressor must pick an objective and a turn limit to achieve it, and wager victory points on achieving it.-The sheer variety of ways to torment your opponents: harass them in court, force them into wars and arena duels, try to steal their stuff with magic, misdirect their troops, blow things up, or a wide array of event cards. There is a huge amount of build variety, play & counter play options here when you get into it.- Seamless asynchronous play: Tired of never actually finishing longform multiplayer strategy games because the sessions go for hours? Solium Infernum will let you set a timer for up to a week on a game- each player can log in and submit their orders for the turn at any time, and as soon as all players have entered their orders the turn will run. That means you can plow through 20 turns in a row if you're all sitting at the computer,  and then if someone needs to go offline for a few days things will pick up as soon as they come back & put in an order. It's awesome!For returning players, here's what I think are the most important changes- The full pointbuy archfiend customization is gone, replaced by a set of unique archfiends with preset starting stats, army, fort, and special unique move (generally unique rituals or diplomacy actions). You can still tinker with them though, thanks to the relic system which is basically a slimmed down 3 point pointbuy system for adding extra perks to your fiend.- Tribute changes! Rather than being more or less mandatory to level charisma to get decent tribute, tribute quality is now based on whatever your highest stat is (though charisma still gets some tribute and manuscript related perks). The amount of tokens you get to select from/keep is determined by your rank (see below). Making charisma non mandatory for econ opens things up a lot IMO, though I only dabbled in the original- Infernal ranks have been changed as well. Now instead of being part of the pointbuy for designing your fiend & permanently locked in, you can upgrade your rank over the course of the game by using an order & paying victory points. By default everyone starts at Baron/ess/ex, and you can pay 30 -> 60 -> 90 points to promote through the stages up to Prince/ess/ex. Each stage improves tribute as noted above, but also unlocks new diplomacy options, allowing you to "Extort" (demand a praetor or artefact) or "humiliate" (Insult, but you get to preset whether they have to declare war or declare a duel if they refuse the insult)Also the new graphics and animations are pretty nice & make it much more approachable - I doubt I would have been able to sell my friends on the game without it, so great job artists!

The political dynamics in player interactions allow for a plethora of strategic viability. The characters, style, and soundtrack are immersive. "To reign is worth ambition."
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a commitment but a rewarding one at that. It is slow. It is a giant confusing info-dump of a game. Once you make sense of a path to victory, experimentation opens up. Once you start to adjust to its pacing and get a small grasp on this games mechanics it rewards you as much as possible. It has a steep learning curve at first but the smallest grasp snowballs into common sense.Its a pure strategy game and an amazing one at that. I highly recommend this game to all skill levels of strategy players. Just take your time with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. Many seem to pitch this as "Civ in hell", but I think its more than that. Despite the hex grid and similar look, this game feels much more like chess or a board game than civ to me. Every turn you have a very limited amount of actions and need to think deeply about each of them and how they will interact with your opponents' actions. From what I've played so far, this game shines the most in multiplayer, both synchronously and asynchronously. Now I just need to get my friends playing!
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing. Finally turn based strategy with a whole bunch of new gameplay mechanics. So many ways of achieving success with magic, military strength, diplomatic mischief etc. It is also really fun playing it asynchronous with friends over days with bursts of activity. _childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: I don't leave many reviews, but I really want more people to buy and play this game so they can continue to make it even better. Played the OG with my friends and family back in the day, and this was such a refreshing way to capture that nostalgia with modern day UI/UX. _childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: positives:highly enjoyable strategy, exceptional in-game art and animations, critically underrated, 4D chess, intricately developed AI, comprehensible multiplayer techniquessome 'game journalists'  describe it as 'Civilization in hell' just because they're both TBS games yet that's like describing Dark Souls games as 'Fable in hell' just because they're both RPG games lol, imo Civ 6 is bloated with too many leaders, AI, mediocre art, exploitable strategies, etc. while SI has good versions of all the concerns I had with Civ which is commendablenegatives:when it released it was fun but had bugs/balance issues which were ironed out (likely due to a lack of beta testing meta availability), for example on discord I complained about the meta of prophecy locking rituals and within 3 days the issue was balanced, they also actively responded to players concerned about an AI bug early onseveral currently visible negative reviews describe it as abandoned because the studio is in hibernation yet this is not the case with multiplayer servers planning to remain up and if there is a game-breaking balance issue devs said they'd patch it, seems some people can't read well, it is just at basically a development stall for DLCadditional:this project is clearly made from talent and understanding of what makes TBS games fun, with ongoing prevalent issues of major publishers (looking right at u activision-blizzard) it is a breath of fresh air with fun modes, yet not being made by a AAA developer means that content for it is stalled because they don't have normies to drain microtransactions from, despite that it is a complete game with the money I purchased it for and would recommend it

I found myself always wanting more actions than I had available, and with how important order can be, it's hard to choose which action should be first. Great tension. _childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. Small scale 4X which feels more like a board game but don't let the smaller scale fool you into thinking it's simplistic or easy. The systems within this game are very well designed and intriguing. There's plenty of depth to it.The only potential downside I can mention is that some things aren't made as clear as they should be (like artifacts that you use as rituals instead of attaching them to a unit/place of power, unlike other types of artifacts) but most of the things can be deduced or figured out with a bit of effort.

_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: It's basically the original game with updated graphics.  If you liked the first Solium Infernum then this is more of the same.  If you've never played the original then you'll like this if you enjoy board games like Game of Thrones or Twilight Imperium.  It's pretty slow, requires a lot of thought and has several paths you can take to victory.  I haven't played online yet but I assume it's fine.  This game is best played with friends like a traditional board game.  I can't say I like the 3D portraits of the demon lords but the art for the cards is great.  It's worth a buy if you're a fan of complex, back stabby board games.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: This game revels in backstabbing and intrigue, and there's not a turn that doesn't feel pivotal to your fiendish plans. Even if you fall behind everyone else, there's always opportunities to snatch victory from the jaws of defeat.While the singleplayer experience is okay (the AI tends to make questionable decisions), I'd highly recommend this if you're looking for a strategy game that really shines in multiplayer.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Solium Infernum really is one of the best strategy games yet, and perhaps one of the best 4X strategy games ever. It feels like a really well made board game. _childDocuments_.review: While the usual 4X features a familiar "Explore, Expand, Exploit, Exterminate" formula, Solium Infernum provides players with an openly revealed and relatively small map. There is no place to "Explore" the randomly generated realm of hell.  - 3 to 5 opposing Archdevil players seeking the very same throne as you.Solium Infernum does not suffer from a "lengthy turn" fatigue as  (a limit which can be sensibly increased as the match goes on). A plethora of complex and intriguing game mechanics shine in the multiplayer. And if you cannot afford a few hours for a single game session you may find an asynchronous mode more accessible - , before you stand up to take a shower and think how could you snatch an extra inch of advantage in this merciless tug-of-war.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time Armello fan, I picked this up mostly out of respect for the studio even if the theme isn't normally my cup of tea. That said, it's really fun. It takes the 4x civ like strategy to a level I didn't expect. The game is simple on its face, but incredibly nuanced in its deeper complexity. There are a lot of ways to play, customize your approach, strategize, and win. I also think no other game quite captures the political conniving of the court quite like this. TLDR, I enjoy it and think its worth your time, especially if you're willing to get the time to know it, and play with live people. (Note the Async play is fantastic)

_childDocuments_.review: like civ but in hellsome notable changes are the limited actions per turn which i like cos it speeds up turns and instead of being overwhelmed with stuff to do you are overwhelmed with what to do. also the ways to win are way more varied and interesting allowing for different play styles and ways of adapting. overall cool game great theme, fun strategy game that leads to interesting stories.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking forward to Solium Infernum for months after I had found out about it. Needless to say it delivered tremendously. The vibes of this game are on point and have nailed everything I could have wanted. The music and art direction are beautifully done. As of right now I can say it is a fun and unique experience in a few ways that I really appreciate, like the map having no edge and just scrolls in on itself if that makes sense. It is like you are playing on a small globe but it is a flat map. It's a trippy experience. You have no safe direction, and any archfiend can become a problem at a moments notice.Game mechanics are fun and every turn is like a puzzle to figure out how to keep yourself in contention. Turns are locked in simultaneously, but the order of everyone's actions is one at a time starting with the "Regent" (1st player that rotates every turn). So everyone's first action happens, and then each persons second action happens. It is a really neat system that I have personally never seen before. You have to decide what to do based on concerns of other player actions as well as the benefits of doing certain things first, like getting better tribute (currency) if you choose to do that first out of your up to six actions in a turn.Anyway, I can fully recommend this game, especially after seeing a update today with the developers going into detail about ways they are going to improve aspects in the future to make it even more fun and challenging. I am so glad this turned out the way it did, the wait was worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Relic balance issues(looking at you crown of extra orders).Stat balance issues among archfiends(mammon, belial and andro are by far the most useful).The game need more relics on the powerlevel as the crown for variation and balance.It also needs more archfiends for variation and balance.The manuscript order needs rebalancing. It is totally useless right now since it only gives dueling manuals.Map generation with PoP placement could use a balance patch.We also need more different legions, prators and arifact with unique abilities instead of just stat bonuses.Some event card are bugged. Angelattack being one.The game itself is relaxing and good fun. Im pretty sure that the devs will only make this better as time passes.If you like turnbased strategy with a focus on diplomacy its an easy reccomend.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to give a shoutout to the devs who really brought back an old masterpiece from the dead. The original Solium Infernum was awesome, strategic, intricate, complex, nail-biting and also quite ugly (except the artworks). This one is exactly the same except it's pretty! I'm having a blast, it feels exactly like it should and it is one of the best grand strategy games I've played in a while. I can't recommend it enough to someone looking for a fresh yet complex startegic experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: So this is a thumbs up with some qualifiers. I think SI is a great game, but whether or not you will like it comes down to two factors:- Do you see yourself playing it in Multiplayer? Then buy it, minus a few nitpicks you'll see below the game is fantastic when played against human opponents.- Are you considering the purchase based on the SP experience? Then I recommend you check in another time once a few patches have come out. The AI is frankly speaking terrible, although this is on top of the Devs priority list so might see improvement in the future. There is also just not much SP content to go around, the currently implemented scenarios can be beaten in a lazy afternoon and afterward there is really only skirmish to play by yourself.To talk more about the game generally, SI could be described as Game of Thrones in hell. The gameplay consists in very large part of bluffing, schemeing, murdering or thieving your way into being crowned the ruler. While most strategy games have a smoke & mirrors element to it, SI was built from the ground up to encourage it in all aspects of the game. Be it diplomatic intimidation or just tricking an opponent into unprofitable trades, SI is probably the best game of its kind if you ever felt like the interplayer interaction in other examples was lacking.There are def. some areas that can still be improved upon. The ingame Encyclopedia is not nearly complete enough for how much the game wants you to check it for information. Little to no information on a lot of tiebreaker scenarios, for example. Certain Events wording makes it seem like they obey rules, but the actual execution is ultimately arbitrary (The Angelic Host card makes it sound like it will only kill 1 Legion per Player, but will often arbitrarily go out of its way to kill twice that number). Ultimately, the game can still use polish, but as stated earlier, it mostly comes down to your preference between MP and SP.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

It's wickedly fun game to play! I say to anyone that wants to try this game, do so. Buy it right now, you'll LOVE it. See you all in Hell (muti-player) lol.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: This game finds the beautiful balance between board game and computer game.  It's rooted in board game mechanics with its limited orders per turn and simple math for determining outcomes but it takes advantage of a computer's ability to track and manage many things to provide a wealth of choices every turn plus an arbiter of hidden information.  Full recommendation to any lover of strategy games.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic recreation of the classic game. Performance issues from the beta have been fixed for the release. There's a fun flavorful selection of single player scenarios that really function to prepare you for the wonderful multiplayer gameplay.Some game elements are a little unclear for new players, the visual display for things like "tribute quality = highest rank", "ritual resistance = your rank in that power" etc are in tiny corners of the screen, but the community discord is friendly and great at answering questions.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Hellishly Good Times: Conquering the Infernal Board in Solium InfernumSolium Infernum is like hosting a board game night in hell, and I can't get enough of it! The theme alone is worth the demonic price of admission – commanding legions of hellspawn, engaging in infernal diplomacy, and battling for supremacy in the fiery depths. It's as if Satan decided to organize a grand strategy game night, and I'm all in for the devilish fun.The depth and strategy in Solium Infernum are hotter than the seventh circle itself. Every decision feels like a demonic chess move, and plotting against my infernal rivals is as satisfying as striking a Faustian bargain. The game's resemblance to a board game adds a unique charm, making me feel like I'm physically moving demonic miniatures across a tabletop covered in brimstone. From demonic politics to strategic warfare, Solium Infernum is a captivating journey through the underworld, proving that even in hell, there's room for strategic merriment. It's the kind of game that makes me say, "Who needs a soul when you can conquer hell in style?"
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game, been waiting for it for 15 years since the original was out of reach for young me.Addictive, and seems very complex in some aspects, not really the rules themselves but they way in which they interact. Very boardgamey, which I like.Would definitely benefit for a real manual in addition to the in-game encyclopedia, which is basic in some aspects.Waiting to play some more SP before plunging in MP, which might be hard for me due to business travels which would make me lose some turns in async play.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent and unique turn-based strategy game.The main attraction is the excellent multiplayer implementation.  While you can play in a single sitting, the asynchronous multiplayer allows you to plot to your hearts content and think about your next move.The theme is great and even though it’s a bit dark, it does not take itself as seriously as the original.  There’s lots of ways to interact with other players and it’s not all about building the best economy.There’s likely a need for some balancing but overall a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: The best graphic design I've seen for years! The sound, scripts, ui and details are so charming and attractive that I will highly recommend this game with the following exceptions.A.I. is very weak and lack of strategic thinking. Whoever would like to play with A.I. - do not expect anything. It is bad. If your game focused on solo playing - it is kind of boring. Sometimes the A.I. makes some nice things like redirecting your war target to the other Archfiend, or summon Angelic Creature near you, but that is all.Bugs in the interface. I and my friend observed bugs in the ui, menus that cannot be closed and quite annoying. Hopefully that is fixable relatively easy with time.Map generation - the map concept is really cool. You have infinite map that is like sphere projection on the flat surface. The generator will create some places of power and mountains. I think that part is also could be improved. Because it impacts your plans a lot and sometimes you are in a bad spot where it is difficult to start.Now why you should buy this game and how to play. You must play async multiplayer! If you have at least 1 friend - buy this game and play together! At first you can play as a team, later with experience play all against others. As I remember 6 gamers are valid. You all play simultaneously, so the time to think is reduced. It is kind of like board game.Graphic, animation, history and culture details, sound, scripts - all of those are very impressive. I would pay those designers double compensation for their work!The gameplay and variations of the game - You choose Archfiend that has kind of special ability and game style. But that is not really true! There is very small differences between them and there will be not a lot of impact in your gameplay style. You can try to win by rituals or places of power, but in reality you should focus to something in between, that makes those unique features too weak. That is good to start, but I found no real unique ways to win the game. I hope in the future the developer will create the second version with the mechanics that allow to win the game with some more different ways of gameplay.The possible actions in the game are nice. The only problem are imbalanced artefacts. In combination with places of power that could be a win ticket. I believe the artefacts should be craftable and only few of them unique. But that is not the case in the game. You have some unique artefacts that once bought can only be obtain by force.Anyway. I had 14 hours of fun with my friend and few hours in demo. Highly recommend for multiplayer. Only recommend for solo if you really would like to enjoy the visual and audio part of the game. And I wish the developers bright future, because they showed that they can create something really unique and beautiful!
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing with my friends and it's absolutely delectable. Whilst we're still acclimatising to the nuances of the game, I've had a wonderful time focusing on short term objectives - akin to tying their shoelaces together and patiently waiting for the result of my labours.The amount of meta-gaming between friends forging temporary alliances and faux-diplomacy is staggering. The game goes into Discord with private messages and calls between each other as you scheme, scheme, scheme. I would say the biggest benefit is asynchronous gaming. With more responsibilities throughout the day, it's difficult to find time to schedule a session together - and perhaps you want to spend what bigger blocks of time you have playing a different game that isn't multiplayer. Solium Infernum offers the opportunity and convenience; a 1 Day to 1 Week countdown timer option to submit your turn. You can take 5 minutes to submit your turn and then do other things in your life. But think about the game you will. While you're out there, touching grass, you lay under a sun dappled tree ruminating with great anticipation how silly Guthrie, currently playing Beelzebub, is going to look after he falls into your trap. Egg on his face. IF he falls into your trap...I believe the singleplayer aspect of this game, with currently limited AI difficulty, is merely a tutorial for what it truly is; the best strategy game to play with friends. Social Chess in Hell. Wonderful stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Fun.  Priced right.Probably best played as a board game with friends once you get used to it.  I like how the AI will play differently with different demons.  However, once you figure out the mechanics it is just flavor when you play; the difference is trivial after the first few rounds as it is easy to make the Wrath demon play as a Charisma or the Greed play as a Deceit.No major bugs.  Couple times it runs slow or stutters on my machine but never crashed or stopped play and this isn't a FPS so the occasional stutter is acceptable.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Cool digital politics/dudes-on-a-map board game.  The game runs great, the presentation is pretty slick, and the UI is decent but for a few instances of where-is-the-close-window-button.  And the single player is definitely not worth the price of entry.Reminds me quite a bit of Oath.  Your turns contain a small number of heavy decisions, with lots of political wheeling and dealing.  And of course the option to clobber your opponent when diplomacy (inevitably/intentionally) fails.I really like the red-tape around Vendettas.  That makes for some interesting decisions on when to time things, and keeps the game from just being Risk.Overall, the game's been fun, and is a good follow-up to Armello (which is still near and dear to my heart).  And so far it's scratching the Oath itch.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: It's a perfect update, all the scheming and backstabbing from the original packaged up with modern conveniences. There's nothing like getting a notification on your phone that it's time for your next turn, and you start cackling because you remember the orders you placed last night, and everyone on the subway is staring at you but it doesn't matter because you know that idiot Astaroth just walked right into your trap.It also runs well on the steam deck, which is nice for quickly submitting your turn in an async game. I'm looking forward to the UI scaling update though, since the text & button size is rough on such a small screen.Edit: They added UI scaling back, but a lot of the game's windows (sometimes including important bits of text or even buttons) go off the edge of the screen if you go over 100%, so for now I'm sticking to tiny text + a magnifying glass when I use the steam deck
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely adore this game!It's oozing with style, exciting and addictive. Multiplayer is the big draw here. As many have pointed out, the AI players leave a lot to be desired. Single player is more of a testing ground, at least for now. That's really the only downside.Solium Infernum is one of the most unique experiences in gaming. The fact that it is now more accessible with much needed quality of life and visual upgrades is a dream. Not to mention the possibilities in the games future for expanded content. I'm frothing at the mouth for it!
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game that I really hope does well because there's so much love and care put into it.The character designs and overall art style are fantastic, and the characters even speak the real life occult language Enochian. The game's focus on politics and subterfuge are a treat, my first game I was playing on every side, being friendly and carefully pitting everyone against each other while I completed hidden schemes, up until the end where all my schemes were revealed, I gained a ton of prestige and stole the strongest unit on the board from another player to protect myself until I was elected. The character designs and playstyle, and the messaging system, also really motivate the player to get into character which is a lot more fun than you may think.The main complaint I see is that the AI is bad which I think is probably true, but as somebody bad and somewhat new to 4X games I haven't noticed it much yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Armello was my favorite tabletop game and was really excited to pick this up. I think the creative pivot to new game set in hell was a bold choice! The amount of detail and artwork is amazing to gawk at and you can tell a lot of time and effort was put into it. Performance: I'm currently running an AMD 6900XT with a Ryzen 9 5950X CPU. The optimization blog showcased Nvidia as their main benchmark leaving AMD users like myself unsure how optimized it would be. Happy to report performance at max settings without anti-aliasing is 100FPS+ and i'm sure this will only get better in time with future updates Gameplay: Have to give props to how well the tutorial was done to help make it entertaining and informative. Once I was left on my own I had fun learning how to take the lessons learned and apply them. I have to agree with many other reviews pointing out the AI. Unless you're playing multi-player the AI isn't smart enough and does moves that make no sense or doesn't challenge me. This needs to be improved on a major scale. I'm sure it will... but it's one of the major issues with the game. Multi-player is where this game shines and is a blast to play. Artstyle: I really like the look/feel of the game. Whats strange is the beautiful artwork on the cards doesn't match up to the "look" of hell which is very grey. I'd like to see more pop of color or some of the artwork showcased on the field you play on. The one thought I had was "Wow... Hell doesn't seem all that bad" but the artwork you see in the Bazaar, event cards, ect... should be present on the field of play.  Overall I look forward to the content this game receives over time.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Faithful to the original and plays smoothly. No other strategy game I've played makes me thrilled to have my ass kicked when the Angelic Host shows up just to smite me. Every turn counts, even when you've been beaten down.Enacting blood feuds is hard though, so make sure to be demanding early and often if you want the chance to wipe an opponent off the map without needing to become persona non grata.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Straight remake of the original flash game, with a decent amount of art and modern 3D graphics. They did a real good job - my only criticism was the AI was terrible (never came close to losing across multiple games, never really needed much strategy). Best played multiplayer I suspect (I don't know - I have no friends).
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: The diplomacy aspect is where the game shines most! Throwing around demands never expecting to get the tribute but instead instigating conflicts, be they military or gladiatorial, so that I can steal prestige from my fellows while earning some too is a great time. A game of, sometimes quite literally, stabbing each other in the back!
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Fun enough game, needs a few more months to cook. A lot of things aren't explained clearly and, as this is a turn-based game, discovering that you "should have done that thing" 25 turns prior (56 turns being a full game) that was neither mentioned nor fully explained can be a real letdown. Eg: each archfiend has specific scenarios that more or less introduces their gameplay mechanics (for multiplayer, you see). I'd just beaten the Lilith scenario which had a "bonus objective" (necessary for earning a gold medal) of destroying a Place of Power. Nowhere nor at any time prior was it mentioned just HOW to destroy a PoP. I thought "given that Lilith's unique objective is to destroy this thing...perhaps I simply capture it then have an option to destroy it? Because Lilith is petty, I guess? This wasn't the case. The only way (that I know of so far) to destroy a PoP is through either an artifact called "Orb of Oblivion" (requiring that your legion loses the battle and destroys the defender along with it) or "The Devourer Statuettes." Utilizing The Devourer Statuettes requires placing them in a ritual slot. This then provides a ritual to summon the Devourer, though it can only be summoned on a controlled tile next to a controlled PoP/ your Stronghold. The Devourer itself requires a flat 2 upkeep of every resource and moves 1 tile/ turn (if no movement bonuses/ teleport is equipped). I discovered this at turn 46 some 13 spaces away from my target. Winning was an impossibility. I pored through my saves to see if I could save-scum and start working toward making this happen and saw that I'd have to jump back some two hours. All for the lack of a properly-explained mechanic. That's not fun. If you work or only have a couple of hours to play per night well...it's simply not a good feeling to have "wasted your time" doing the wrong thing when you didn't even know what you were doing is wrong. I recommend coming back to this in half a year or so. Let all the kinks get worked out.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Heard about the original but never played it. Finished tutorial as a full game and had a lot of fun! So many different options and decisions to make each turn. _childDocuments_.review: This game is just wow!The community is wow!You will download the game, you will do the tutorial and you will be captivated by the mechanics and how from a winning position you can lose everything and vice-versa.If you're into strategy and manipulation, this game is just what you need.It provides a unique gaming experience.10/10 (apart from the AI, they're not very smart, but you won't be playing with the AI ​​much)Have fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Slow paced grand strategy with some of the best political gameplay. Incredible art and music. 9/10. Best thing is that you can complete an entire match in one setting. _childDocuments_.review: Always good to find a game that embraces and does Asynchronous turns properly - especially with an expectation of maybe only a turn or so a day. As someone who loves strategy PC games as well as Board Games, this is/was a key purchase and I don't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you consider yourself a Machiavellian character?Do the concepts of honor and fairness bore you more than usual?Do you seek other avenues, however unconventional, to power and glory?Do the ends justify the means in your estimation?THEN THIS IS THE GAME FOR YOU!Engage in political maneuvering, scheming, plotting, backstabbing and all-out underhanded tactics to secure your place as the new Monarch of the Hellish Realm!Just beware, in your mind you are always the victor.When you are thrust into the unforgiving political arena of Hell, there will always be a bigger, more sinister hellfish out to get you.Tread lightly, here be demons......

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game, with a lot of possible diplomacy effects and combinations.It's like a digital board-game.The only downsides so far that I have found is the AI which needs a bit more work and that in multiplayer, 3-5 minutes for a turn is too little in the end-game, where you need to maintain your spells, tribute for titans, etc.Mainly, it is a great game, which I recommend playing with friends(then you can play asynchronous and not have the 3-5 mins time limit per turn and also not wait 20 hours for a random player to make his turn).Keep up the good work!
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Aesthetic notes only thus far:The sheer quality in the presentation of this game is absolutely fantastic. You have hellish orchestral music blaring all the way through, the grey and red tones of a hellish barren landscape with dust clouds flying around the map, lava spurting at the seams and the creature animations a joy to behold. Looking through the cards and event art is a treat, as anyone who has played LoG's previous game Armello may know, their team is quite talented when it comes to creating artworks for cards and events, and in Solium Infernum, their talents shine once again to great effect. I had a lot of fun just exploring the artworks in the encyclopedia before even playing the game!A lot of work and care has been put into this game, and if you're one to find joy in the infernal depths of hell, you'll enjoy your time with this game. I've only had one match thus far, may update this review in the future. --But for what it's worth, if you want to support a struggling developer down under, and are looking for a neat game to pass some time with, you've got far worse choices than Solium Infernum--

If you like turned based strategy, a must buy. A classic.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR Solid and unique Strategy game where you really feel like your in hell and worth getting.I never played or had heard of the original before a few days before this game launched and saw some gameplay videos and decided to get it and give it a go. I have to honestly say I was not disappointed. It's not like anything I have played before and honestly its unlike any strategy game I have seen or played, it is great to play.Pros:- Visually the game is just stunning, the art and vibe is just spot on. You truly feel like you are in hell.- The game play is unique and really engaging, there is nothing like it and its great to play with.- It's in many regards a true strategy game that requires you to think and plan thoroughly, all for your carefully laid plans to fall apart almost immediately and so you have to react and adapt.- There are many styles and ways to achieve victory even from the jaws of defeat.- The map forces you from the get go to be proactive and engage with other players, you can't camp it out.- The way the turn system works is unique and really does force you to prioritise and think hard about what you will be doing.- There are a lot of different mechanics and systems at play that you need to understand, though the learning curve is not as steep as you would think. It's easy to grasp but takes time to master and become cunning about them.- It's fantastic to play with friends and a multiplayer experience like no other.Cons:- It is not an easy game, you will be challenged when you try to win.- The AI is not able to make the games full potential come out, it doesn't take the opportunity to stab people in the back or make the complex plots and political plays needed to win. You really need to play this against people for it to be at its best. However, to my mind that's the case with any game with multiplayer.- There are some balance issues, there is the potential to meta the game with certain combos, rituals that shouldn't affect titans seem to work whilst others don't etc.- The amount of content is solid and diverse. However, you can quickly go through it all in a normal game and it feels like there should be more. It's not bad but feels like it could do with 1/3 more legions, artefacts, Preators etc. Though it feels almost certain that more content will be added and add more to the game but as is it is still good.Key Points:- It is a game that does encourage you to be the bad guy, there are no rules and no sympathy. You will be kicked whilst you are down, you will be bullied, you will have stuff stolen form you and much more. You have to do the same to get ahead, it's a game where you can't be the nice guy. So be prepared for that and to do that.- You can easily put yourself into a corner from which it is very hard to get out of, you do have to be proactive and think out thoroughly what to do or you will get stuck and then become the target of everyone else.- However in that same breath it can be manageable. For example if your being ganged up on by 2 players and they seem to be focusing on you, then another player can take notice and stab one of them in the back forcing one of them to have to shift their focus, so now your dealing with one instead of 2 players. All in all a solid game and worth the price, needs a bit more stuff and some balancing but so long as the game does well and gets the support, which I hope it does, then it will just get better.8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: As a solo player, I 100% recommend you try the multiplayer, even if you usually play solo. It's incredibly fun to pull off tricks and backstab one another. As a typically solo player, multiplayer was really stress-free and fun to get into once I'd played the tutorial, and gotten the hang of things in an AI game. Think of it more like a party game than a serious competitive game. It's a ton of fun tricking and backstabbing other players, and then having the whole board turned on its head with a massive game-changing event.Even if you don't have hours every day to devote to the game, you can play an asynchronous game, where you play one turn per day, which really takes the stress and time investment down compared to other similar games.This game is absolutely fantastic fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely phenomenal game. First, the aesthetics would have sold me alone; extremely well designed, from character profiles, through UI assets, and all the way to the music. But then you also have a really deep strategy game WHERE POLITICS, INTRIGUE, AND DECEIT ACTUALLY WORK. For anyone who is a massive Total War fan but has always wished that diplomacy actually mattered - this game is for you.So far, the PvE scenarios have been great so even if you're not into the idea of async multiplayer, this game has plenty for you. I just finished my first "moderate" challenge one and it was engaging enough to be fun. Next I'll try the really hard ones and see what's what and then maybe dip my toes into multiplayer.Bottom line - if you liked R.U.S.E, tabletop games like Twilight Imperium or Veiled Fate, you must play this game. If you prefer your Grand Strategy to focus on manipulation and deceit (with a share of personal and unit based combat thrown in) you must play this game. Do it! It rules.

_childDocuments_.review: Solium Infernum provides quite possibly the most intricate, expansive grand strategy experience. If you have enjoyed games like Civilization in the past, this game will surely sate your strategic appetites. Resource management in this game is superb, where even something as simple as moving a unit costs a valuable order. The sheer number of options for gameplay are mind-blowing, and I could not recommend this game more.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: This is a recreation of the original Solium Infernum from 2009. The core gameplay elements of Solium (the old and the new one) are absolutely unique. The strict limit on the number of orders per turn makes sure that every decision matters and that long games don’t degrade into micromanagement.  The map has no borders but instead “wraps around”, which means there are neither central nor edge positions. The diplomacy system makes sure that “steamroll everyone by getting the strongest military” isn’t a universally winning strategy.For context: I have played the original Solium Infernum back in the days. For me, just being able to run the same game on a modern system with readable fonts is sufficient justification for a positive review. The core gameplay (which has been faithfully preserved) was amazing even with the horrible UI of the original game, and anything that improves on that is just “icing on the cake”. So with that said, let’s discuss the quality of the icing!The main changes compared to the original SI are: graphics and UI have been completely redesigned, some concepts have been simplified (archfiend creation and Praetor duels), and there is proper support for multiplayer.The asynchronous multiplayer support (you have 24 hours to submit your turn, and games can span over weeks) is a fantastic addition. The simplification of archfiend creation is also a welcome improvement.The Praetor duels, in my opinion, have been reduced to a single round of rock-paper-scissors while, at the same time, making them harder to understand(!). I very much hope this will see some significant post-release changes.I guess since this is 2024, the graphics are mostly 3D (even 2D drawings get a depth effect), even though there is zero need from a gameplay perspective. The quality is, unfortunately a little worse than Endless Legends (released 2016 IIRC) while for some reason requiring a much higher end system. The map textures are mostly a featureless gray. Many 3D objects look like someone forgot to put textures on it at all. The character models are between okay to cringe-worthy (looking at Lillith here). The combat animations are always the same and get tiring after the first 10 rounds. They can be skipped, but unfortunately that's also the only way to see how combat plays out - I'd much rather have a summary table that I can call up after the fact.Don’t get me wrong, most of this is irrelevant for the gameplay and orders of magnitude better than what the original game had. However, I can’t help but think that if the developers hadn’t gone for 3D, the graphics would be more beautiful, the system requirements lower, and the game would have been finished more quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend picking this up if you're a fan of hex based strategy games, It does several innovative things with diplomacy and action economy that make the actions feel a little more meaningful and intentional. I think these changes help set it apart from Civ and other similar games with a very flavorful infernal backdrop. In the future it would be nice to have a little more map and 3D model variety between legions to match the amazing card art. However the core game play loop is solid enough to pick up at the full price if you are a fan of the genre and have friends who are down to play multiplayer with.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the first game, and this is a fantastic, and faithful, remake.  For anyone that played the first one, play this one.  For anyone who hasn't played the first one here are some things to know. This is a very complicated game, it can feel overwhelming as you try to figure things out.  Play the tutorial for sure. HIghly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: At first glance it may seem like a Civ clone, but it very quickly becomes one hell of a mental gymnastics simulator. The world, even at its largest, isn't very large. But that's not an issue. It's as large as it needs to be, and all the edges loop back on each other, so there are no corners to hide in. Also, it's merely a canvas for border disputes, and so it could be a 10 by 10 square and it would still get the job done. Besides, the real depth of the game comes from all the schemes, rituals, diplomacy, and any other kind of strategic mind game you can think of. Every archfiend even has a "dark art", a kind of superpower specific to them, and Belial's lets you frame someone else for an insult. If you upgrade a specific power path enough, you can even frame someone else for any rituals you perform as well. It's fantastic, and by far the best way to stab all your friends in the back to date.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: I think the optimization needs work. Maybe I just need to update GeForce, but the gameplay feels laggy even on the lowest settings when I don't have this issue with other new titles. This'll probably be fixed either on my end or through an update, so it's not a dealbreaker.The aesthetic is awesome, and the execution is perfect. There's some weird sense of mask-off honesty when all of the players are explicitly evil and you're simply fighting over who wins, like pure distillation of Machiavellian gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Solium Infernum

_childDocuments_.review: This is a FFA turn-based strategy about becoming the new Prince of Hell. You compete with other archfiends in an asymmetric strategy game with twists and turns. It offers twists and turns and expects the player to keep thinking and looking for solutions out of tight spots. It's accessible, but very deep in terms of possibilities and tactics. It can be played singleplayer, in a standard multiplayer way - or with long simultaneous turns that can last very long.This is a great game for you if you:- Love 4X FFA strategies.- Appreciate "easy to learn - difficult to master" game design, or League of Geeks games.- Love bizarre and/or stories about villains.- Appreciate strategies/board games with a strong intelligence theme to them.- Love e-board games.- Played the original Solium Infernum.- Insist on having enough time to think about your actions in a turn-based strategy game.- Like the idea of turns lasting up to a week. They end upon everyone playing - but the time limit can be as long.The depth of the game is extremely rewarding. The theme... I'm not a fan of morbid, bizarre or evil - but the game's mechanics drew me in all the same.Cons:- AI seems to be stumbling with the basics so much that it fails to provide a challenge.- No meta-progression features like the ones in Armello.- One can stumble into bugs without trying.- The variation of rituals.... upon figuring them out - you just wish for more of them.- The duels don't offer much feedback.- No familiar single-player campaigns or any attempts - The game's neat. But not fancy. Well made - but not fancy.I loved it.I certainly do recommend it.Most of what irks me about it is that there isn't much more. That's always a compliment, I think.

_childDocuments_.review: I forged the ultimate Praetor as Andromalius, from my fort of pride i demanded the lesser for tribute, confident that anyone who would defy my right would fail misserably and spectacularly in the arena and so it was for a time, until the Council called for the excolmulgation of a single ArchfiendOf course they choosed me, how else would i be tested.But Andromalius is no stranger to betrayal, for The Father Above casted him down to hell a long, long time ago. Curious how history repeats itself time and time again.Freed from the biding laws of the Council and surrounded by all the hate Hell can conjure, Andromalius called upon his forgone kin to raze hell once again, giving him enough time to bless with forbidden knowledge his Chosen and, with newfound strenght, he set his sole legion to behead every single Archfiend in this behement circle of hell.This game told me a story i was surprised to play as the protagonist. _childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game as long as you know what you're getting into.Solium Infernum isn't a traditional 4X title, not really. It plays more like a digital board game on hellish steroids. It has a lot of warring, money management, area control, drafting units and upgrades and strictly mechanical approach to the diplomacy. _childDocuments_.review: I first played Solium Infernum years ago, back when it was a niche indie game only playable in Adobe Framemaker. It was a tremendous concept, so I was thrilled to see it get a remake, and I'm even happier to say that the remake is excellent.The mechanics of the game remain the same: you are an aspiring Archfiend of Hell vying to claim the throne of Pandaemonium after Lucifer disappears. Claiming the throne is simply a matter of having the most Prestige (points) at the end of the game, but there are a dizzying number of actions available to help you achieve that goal. The trick of the game is that, while you may have a dozen or more options per turn, you can only perform, by default, two actions. Every move matters enormously, and with games lasting as little as 30 turns, there's little room for error.As for those mechanics, I could spend this entire review struggling to list them all. You'll wage war, bid for new armies and attachments for those armies, cast spells, and more. Much of the game is built around secrecy, with the exact choices that players make often obscured from everyone else. This is a big part of why the AI is bad: it can't really account for so much information that is hidden from it. The developers have done an admirable job with the tutorial, and a full in-game encyclopedia further rounds things out, but it is quite a complex game in terms of the number of plates you need to keep spinning. The AI is not particularly impressive, and in some ways is more of a practice dummy to let you get to grips with the many gameplay systems than a real opponent. A single-player challenge mode is available that functions as a sort of advanced tutorial for each playable Archfiend, but as a single-player game, Solium Infernum is unfortunately lacking. Hopefully the game receives enough support that this changes, or even gets some mods to that effect, but it really is intended more as a multiplayer experience. As a multiplayer game, it's quite fun. Not only are the mechanics well suited for it, the game is actually designed well to accommodate both standard multiplayer and asynchronous multiplayer. The asynchronous option allows players to take their turns within big spans of time (such as a whole day or more). The game has a complex simultaneous turn system, so absolutely nothing is lost by using this method. Creating games is easy, and you can even create a public asynchronous game, so even with random opponents you don't necessarily have to give more than a few minutes a day to the game.In terms of production values, I'm surprised at how lavish this game is. You can tell that it's not a AAA production, but the art direction is very strong. Despite plenty of relatively low-resolution textures, the game always looks gorgeous. Character models brim with personality, the landscape is appropriately bleak, and the UI oozes with gorgeous artwork. The soundtrack is also quite nice, all moody organ music and light choral singing. Even (Especially?)  when you're losing, you're getting an appropriately Hellish experience. I don't think Solium Infernum is for everyone. You need a high tolerance for complexity and a willingness to play against others. But if you like the concept and don't mind the learning curve, then I think it's an easy recommendation. There's just nothing else like it out there.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good strategy game filled with very interesting choices and great production quality.  Against the AI the game is fun but the AI is not much of a challenge. _childDocuments_.review: C.S Lewis said Hell is a bureaucracy, and by god, this game is a bureaucratic nightmare. With a delightfully devilish aesthetic that is miserably oppressive and claustrophobic, Solium Infernum is an extremely flavorful game that incentivizes you to be as despicable and vile and two-faced as possible.  because even at the larger sizes the maps don't give you much room to stretch in, and you'll be forced to become very intimate with your neighbors within the first ten turns or so. This game also has one of the coolest gimmicks I've seen in a strategy game, where the map loops in on itself from every angle. in addition to being very disorientating, it forces you to always be mindful of your borders, and it feeds into the paranoia that there is no respite or safety to be found in this world where the walls are slowly but surely enveloping and constricting you. Even the currencies of this game are a nightmare to work with. There are four resources that you will earn as tribute, Souls, Ichor, Hellfire, and Darkness. These tributes are dolled out as tokens that are worth 1-3 each, and you cannot stack them, and this becomes problematic when you consider that trades are limited to eight tokens. You can get around this by compressing these tributes into a single token, but this costs an action slot, a turn that may let the item you want be snatched up by a rival, and it puts a great deal of resources at risk if you consolidate everything you own, because these tokens can (AND WILL) be stolen by your rivals. Every decision in this game must be weighed against the unknowable intentions of the other archfiends, and i hope this brief synopsis of one of the game's mechanics conveys the weight and depth of everything this game has going on.I only have two complaints for this game. The first is that the animations are way, waaaaay too slow. This is fine for their asynchronous mode where you're only going to play this game for a single turn, and you may need the slow reminder of everything that happened over the past day, but for when you're sitting down to commit yourself to a single session, which is possible because you can clear a 50 turn scenario in 2.5 hours, it becomes really frustrating to see every unit move so ploddingly slow. Second, the A.I isn't anywhere near aggressive enough. The AI in this game feels like something to be exploited for your own gain, rather than a conniving, conspiring archfiend that is working against you to its own ends. This is an excellent 4X game, masterfully blending flavor and mechanics to create an enthralling experience. I look forward to my next scenario, and hope to get a lobby full of friends to fully explore this game's potential with.

_childDocuments_.review: Solium Infernum is the depraved edgelord love child of Diplomacy and Mario Party.Like in Diplomacy you can spend five hours looking at a game state and trying to psychoanalyse every player and how they feel about every other player and the likelihood that there are alliances and deals you don't know about and how likely those potential deals are to be betrayed and so on, all culminating in the most powerful set of moves ever devised. And you can do that in Solium Infernum too, but then someone might play a card that randomly murders your best army and lynchpin of your entire strategy. Weirdly, I think this actually softens the absolutely cutthroat, friendship-ending experience of Diplomacy. The pure chaos of everyone throwing game-changing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around every five minutes makes the feeling of getting absolutely brutalised a lot easier to deal with. And in addition, the action limit and limits on fully eliminating a player make comebacks pretty plausible. Bottom line, the core gameplay is great, as it was historically.The art and accompanying lore snippets are great, and give a bit of extra life to the standard graphics on the game map, which are good but lean towards the grey.The only two problems with the game in its current state are a very weak AI opponent, and a tendency to favour a clean UI in situations where that can obscure vital information, particularly as a new player. The AI is just not aggressive enough, and tends to get too embroiled in side conflicts when you the player are forging ahead with a near insurmountable lead, but realistically you'll have the most fun on multiplayer anyway, even with complete randos. The UI has a slight tendency to obscure important information, such as terrain effects. Once you fall victim to a terrain effect or something similar once, you'll probably remember them going forward, but learning through mistakes is probably not ideal in a game where single turns can be massively impactful on the outcome of the game overall.The price point is also a little on the high side for what's presented, I'd like a little more content, perhaps some alternate game modes to really split this version of SI off from its predecessor. Perhaps a game mode with two rival Pandemoniums, for example. I'd say it's currently a solid deal at £25/$30 or so, and with a bit of expansion on the launch state, the asking price could be a lot fairer.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, this is a great game, first and foremost!  BUT......you have to take the time to understand it, if you do not put in the time you will be selling yourself short.  It is deep and has many different strategies and I know that at this point I do not fully understand the complex interplay fully; however, that is part of the fun.  It is a slower pace, but do not let that deter you either, it is a game you need to play several steps ahead or you will find yourself literally and figuratively mired in hell.  I do not know what the road map is for this game as far as DLC but I think the sky is the limit for these guys.  If you like strategy, but hate micromanagement, this is really pure strategy, then you need to buy this game.  I personally enjoy 4x games like CIV and others but I will get turned off on grand strategy games (EU4/CK2/STI/etc) at times because you have too much micromanagement; this game really gives you great strategic value without the bloat of micromanaging.  If you are on the fence after reading what I wrote and are thinking, "this review really speaks to me", then buy, download and ENJOY!

_childDocuments_.review: The game perfectly encapsulates the fantasy it is trying to portray.Fiendish machinations and opportunism are the name of the game. Follow the rules of hell, but only as long as they suit you. This is a fantastic game, but not for everyone. It is a long and convoluted game; this is not a game you can just pick up and play a couple of minutes of. But if you like the idea of spending an afternoon in a chess-like cutthroat battle against cunning, deceitful, disloyal archfiend bullies like yourself, this is definitely the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is Fantastic! From the little time I played so far, the tutorial kept it easy to understand and the art is just so beautiful. A fantastic computer based board game. Two suggestions though, there is no hotseat for some reason and the max players should be seven for the seven deadly sins to quarrel with each other, but six is still fine.UPDATE: After beating a large map 80 turn game (Very long setting), I loved it so much. The AI are competent enough to know who's winning and who to target to make their chances of winning better. Late game I steam rolled all 5 AI as Beelzebub, I was at 400+ victory points while 2nd place was at 200+. Movement speed is broken early game because you can block a majority of the victory point generators simply by being faster by going one more space then everyone else (Crown of Alacrity). Astaroth was the only AI that was able to compete against me purely by his special ability alone that allows him to violate the Geneva convention. I barely used diplomacy because if you have enough money every turn, you just throw a chunk of tribute (cash) in their face, then they are no longer aggresive for a few turns besides Astaroth. Overall I had a great experience, cannot wait for updates and maybe expansions.

_childDocuments_.review:
Take the Infernal Throne in this hellish turn-based grand strategy game. 

The Prince of Darkness has vanished, leaving Archfiends to conspire: muster your legions while intoning dark sorceries, devilish schemes, and machiavellian plots. Who will be the new ruler of Hell and ascend the Throne?

Play as one of eight all-powerful and menacing Archfiends and indulge your Machiavellian dark side. Command legions, enlist champions, cast sinister rituals, and trick, rob, and insult your rivals to be crowned Hell's new Dark Majesty.

Experience Solium Infernum's legendary devilish political machinations. Requiring nerves of steel and a true heart of darkness, every order you give will have lasting consequences. Get into the minds of your rivals, second-guessing their every move both on the map and on the floor of Hell's parliament as you sling insults and demands in the only truly political strategy game.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's get this out of the way:All of the negative reviews you've read about the game thus far are accurate in their depiction of its gameplay experience. Now, I'll say the people expecting it to be like the mainline Dragon Quest games feel like purchasers that didn't look into what the game was before buying it; this was always marketed as being part of the action RPG spinoff subset of the series.You'd be forgiven for thinking that. No, it's actually more akin to the typical reskinned anime arena fighters that we get for most franchises.Now, from jump with the way they marketed the game I had my concerns; they seemed to place a really heavy emphasis on showing off boss fights and special moves. My suspicions were confirmed once I actually started playing the game...or...tried to anyways.Valve,  This game absolutely  deserve to be listed as SD Verified.Does it run well? Sure; you can play on medium settings at 6 TDP with 40hz refresh rate making 40FPS stable and get great battery life...except for the fact that .Yes, you read that correct. You have to be online to load your game in a single player game...with no online components to it whatsoever. Because reasons.On desktop this won't be a problem, but in that this is Steam Deck verified one expects to be able to use their portable system as a portable system...I know, right?At this price point? Absolutely. Here are the reasons why you might not feel you got your $60 - $70 dollars worth:Ah, I see you are also a person of culture. I'll raise a glass to your health.Here's the thing: I'm giving this game a negative review, but that **** don't feel good! Those of you that only got into Dragon Quest becaues of DQ11, you don't understand how hard we've had to fight to make Japan understand we love this series. Statistically speaking, we buy A LOT of copies of each game that makes it here, but we've had to fight tooth and nail for years to make Enix and later Square Enix believe that we truly do adore this franchise.There are  so many Dragon Quest games that have never and probably will never make their way to the West, and us diehards of the series are terrified of giving any title bad press because Square Enix is literally always one bomb away from going "See, I told you Westerners don't care about Dragon Quest!"I'm shocked that we got Adventure of Dai in the West. I'm shocked we got Dragon Quest Treasure in the West. I'm shocked we're getting Dragon Quest Monsters: The Dark Prince in the West. Hop on Wikipedia and take a look at how many of these games we never get. And like a lot of die hards who remember the struggle, who remember all the times Square Enix said things like "DQ7 isn't worth bringing to the West for the 3DS; it's not worth spending money localizing a game none of you are going to play" and how hard we had to fight to prove that we would, I hate to leave a negative review on a Dragon Quest game already listed as "mostly negative" because I've been at this long enough to know how Square Enix will choose to take that.Like most major companies, I sincerely doubt they'll go "Oof, maybe we just made a bad game and charged too much for it, and maybe our choice in how we implemented Denuvo was way too severe..."Nine times out of ten they go "Well obviously they just don't like insert franchise here, so, let's either just stop bringing spinoffs to the West, stop porting them to other platforms, or (worst case scenario) maybe we just stop bringing these over for a while."And, I wouldn't be surprised if they were using Adventure of Dai sales as a metric for future spin-offs, like the  offline port of DQ10. What's that you say? They're completely different styles of games and unrelated? Lest you forget Namco Bandai once said they weren't willing to bring Tales Of games over unless we bought enough copies of Majin and the Forsaken Kingdom to prove we were into Japanese games.But y'know what? If I left anything but an honest review of this game, I'd be betraying my sense of integrity.So, do I recommend this game? No, no I do not. Not at this price point, and not until they let you load your saved games when you're offline (if you don't want to change that, Square Enix, then I encourage you to tell Valve to remove your Steam Deck Verified badge).

_childDocuments_.review: I am of course a very big fan of the dragon quest franchise, and the Adventure of Dai story is one I unabashedly love. After seeing that the characters from the series may be brought to life in game form, I was ecstatic. Dai, Maam, Pop, and Hyunckel all in particular.As a forewarning, this *is* a game based on an anime first and foremost. As a result, it suffers as bit from similar issues that other anime-based games do. You'll specifically be reliving the anime's story and fighting at core moments within it. A fair bit of the game revolves around cinematics and recounting the story, as is expected for a game like this. But if you'd like complete control over your game from start to finish in the gameplay, this may not be the game for you. Which is totally understandable, so it's important to know what youe're getting into so you don't end up disappointed.The main cast here feel just as loveable as the real things, but what is most important to me is that I get to continue interacting with and experiencing these characters that I've come to be attached to and love. This offers that for me. So at its core, regardless of gameplay (which I'll still get into, this game has an inherent connection with me and is something I enjoy wholeheartedly.As for the actual game, it seems a lot of people didn't know what to expect. Which is totally valid, but at the same time I'd discourage leaving negative reviews based on misconceptions or misunderstandings about what the game is. Infinity Strash isn't a traditional JRPG, and you won't find a grandiose retelling of the main story here. The game revolves mostly around fighting, so some have come to refer to it as an arena fighter. Though fighting isn't necessarily *all* the game is, it really is the main focus. You can think of games like dynasty warriors for a reference in terms of the balance of fighting and story. Which is a fitting comparison, since Dragon Quest already has some collaborations with the dynasty franchise. If you're skipping through the story as you may already be familiar with it, then that's the experience you'll get — instance-based fighting against enemies.The combat is fun. Nothing particualrly unique, but a very safe solution for action-based combat. With that in mind, though, there are some parts of the combat experience I do still find super refreshing. Due to the AI and aggression system, I'm able to play wahtever character I'm most fond of exclusively. In my case, that's Maam. Since most of her damage is from the backline with her gun, it's important that one of the forwards on my team (usually Dai) is drawing aggression from enemies. The AI makes this possible, and allows for the team to really flex and meld to what YOU want to play. This is the essential part of the combat experience in Infinity Strash that I think makes things feel good to me. The game really revolves around your ability to enjoy the characters you may have come to love, and the developers seemed to recognize that and build the game around it well. You may, however, want to increase the difficulty for a real challenge. Despite being action combat, you benefit a lot from taking your time in the fights and not spamming attacks. Increasing the difficulty will help punish you for when you don't take your time, and assuming you have a grip on the combat system, the normal difficult is pretty easy.The beginning intro of the game is directed very well, and I was pretty surprised by the production value of it despite what this game is. Easily an experience that will be heightened immensely by having experienced the original story, but doing so is not necessary to enjoy this gem. Just bare in mind that there WILL be spoilers, and it isn't very good as a retelling of the story. This is simply supplemental material TO that story. The artstyle is fantastic, a perfect reflection of the core series it's based on both in anime and manga form. I think the strongest part of this game from a functional standpoint is definitely its art and effects. Although I don't own the devices my self, I've also seen it praised for performance on Steam Deck and Switch. Living in an age where so many games perform poorly on the switch or eventually drop support for it, I can add my bit of praise for GameStudio tending to the console properly.I also inevitably need to dedicate a line to this game's music composition, because I can at the very least share unabashed praise for its soundtracks, even if just by inclusion.Infinity Strash has been such a refreshing experience to me, and is a reminder about the point of games in the first place. Sometimes you don't need a serious story or hundreds of hours of content in order to enjoy a game. Sometimes... a game is just meant to be fun. Infinity Strash is exactly that — fun for people that have come to love the story of Dai and its characters. A game that allows you to continue to explore, enjoy, and immerse yourself in the world of Dai's adventure. It could have been more, for sure. But what we got? It's something I still wholeheartedly love and enjoy.Just as one bonus note... entirely based on my own experiences and opinion. But it seems like a lot of the gaming audience these days has developed a bit of a bizarre/twisted view on games as a product. Have we forgotten what this medium of entertainment is all about? Is this why people make the claim that gaming is no longer 'fun' for them? That's really unfortunate, and is an ideology I hope many can pull themselves out of in favor of experiencing these unimportant parts of life in a much more positive light. Sad to see so many feel that they've grown out of video games because of it, since there's a lot of magical experiences that games have to offer; if this isn't a magical experience for you, that's okay. It's such a vast industry that there is bound to be something out there that fills that hole for you.I think despite the beginnings being fairly limited in terms of mechanics and gameplay, I recommend holding out until the ~1 hour mark, or when you first reach the temple of recollection. From this point on the game's little twist on the series add a certain layer of uniqueness that might be able to refresh your attention and enjoyment of it even if it wasn't what you may have expected or wanted. It's effectively like a roguelike, and offers so much playability that I can't wait to explore into the future as I continue to play Infinity Strash out of love for the characters.
