_childDocuments_.review: If you're expecting an RPG/JRPG like the mainline Dragon Quest games, DO NOT BUY THIS. I truly can understand why fans of the series are upset and what their issues with the game are, but from my personal experience it reminds me of more of playing a beat 'em up than an RPG/JRPG. The entire game is as follows: (long) Cutscenes that are either stills for the anime or (to me) somewhat decent animated cutscenes, then timed/numbered horde mode fight or a boss. Timed/numbered horde fight then cutscene/boss. Rinse and repeat. And for whatever reason I have no complaints with that system for this game. The combat is basic but I still had fun with it. Its just a short 3 hit combo that changes slightly if you delay the final attack, and 3 spells/abilities that you continue to unlock as you level up. You can swap between characters mid battle and use all of their spells and attacks, too. This adds the slightest layer of depth to the combat. The majority of people will say that the general feel, layout, and presentation of this game is like that of a mobile game, but to me it feels more like an older game with basic combat that relies more on parrying/dodging.  And for whatever reason I still have no complaints with that system for this game. I still haven't beaten it yet, but when I get home from work I'm always ready to complete my chapter for the night. I don't know anything about The Adventure of Dai anime or manga, but it reminded me of playing Budokai 1 for the first time before I ever finished watching the Android/Cell saga. It was just a fun way to experience the story for the first, so far. But, since I don't know much about the story I don't know how much is skipped or simply not in the game, and that makes me want to watch the anime. Idk. Its fun for me but that might not be your thing. I paid $23 for this game and I think I've at least gotten that much enjoyment/fun out of it. Go in knowing that it'll be a very simplistic and I think you'll like it.UPDATE: Just beat the game. I would still recommend it on sale only because now I wish the story was finished. _childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr, an attempt was made to make something nice. A sincere attempt I'd argue. Not good for a first introduction to the series, but good for a Dai fan (like myself) or someone who's okay with bypassing the story for gameplay.Let's start with the good; gameplay wise, it's serviceable. Play's like an arena fighter, which if you enjoy that kind of gameplay, this game does it with flying colors. The movement is fluid, the characters are fun to play, and being able to build up the playable cast with upgrades is rewarding. The game gives a very fair challenge, and you'll find even the early game has a little bite to it, but can be overcome if you build properly.Graphically, it's beautiful. The game is nice to look at and easy on the eyes. Effects are bright and colorful, and characters look brilliant, and the cutscenes are lovely recreations of the anime... This leads me into one of my biggest gripes with the game; The Story's presentation. If it's not a cutscene, the story is presented as a slideshow of screenshots from the anime. And there is A LOT of this. As someone who already watched the anime, I can skip these no problem, but for someone who is using this to experience Dai's story for the first time, DON'T. It glosses over so many important characters, and arcs that the characters go through feels ham-fisted via this presentation, which is a shame because this is where Dai's story excels.If I had to improve this, I'd argue that an abridged version of the story would've sufficed nicely. Less of the slideshows, and more storytelling during gameplay, even if it was just voiceovers during combat. Maybe even lightly done cutscenes where the characters stand around talking.I'm recommending this out of my wholehearted love for the series, and out of the enjoyment i've gotten from this game so far despite it's evident flaws. I hope this will encourage people to watch the anime before playing this game. I know this team restarted development of this game in hopes of providing the best way to experience Dai's story, and they had to compromise somewhere. Start with the anime, then play this if you enjoy arena fighters.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is purely my opinion after finishing the game (40-50h) but please consider reading the full review on reddit link below if you want to get a better idea what's good or badI don’t use to write something like this because usually a game is either really bad and I stop playing it or just good and I don’t have anyhing to say. Review bombing with 20min playtime is crazy..Short answer I recommend this game. But only if you met these criteria :- Dragon Quest Dai's Fan (especially the 2020 remake anime, being just the old manga fan or a simple anime fan will not be enough I think)- Like Yuki Hayashi’s OST and the Japanese voice cast (absolutely amazing to see these voices back just for a game) Idk about the enligsh sorry- Like Boss Rush & Rogue Like- Like simple gameplay and system but with cool tech (combo cancel, perfect dodge, perfect guard)- Like Challenging Boss (post game)- Being aware of this game's scope (anime low budget, development issues, small game not mainline DQ and not a real "spin" off)And even after that you may not enjoy it, depending on your personal preferenceLong review (full review with challenge mode section and my conclusion. I'm sorry more free space to write on reddit unfortunately) : Introduction context, this game was planned to be release alongside the anime remake (so in 2021) that's why it didn't cover the whole story, but after releasing the first trailer, they decided to reboot the entire development (at this point they lost between 1 and 2 years of development for a game that already has low budget and small scope) Now considering this game is an ANIME adaptation and not a DQ game, you start to get what went wrong. Anime game budget is really low because it is calculated based on the Production Committee of an anime (they only share a part of the overall budget to produce game, merch etc) so it will never be as big as a real "game" (DQ builders, Monsters or Heroes have far more budget than Infinity Strash) This game is not developed by Square Enix. This is Kai graphics and Game Studio Inc first new console games (the credit has more marketing and voice actors than developpers) So keep that introduction in mind it doesn’t totally justify the game quality but it helps you to understand how anime adaptation works.- Gameplay :If I had to hardly disagree with most of the people, is the gameplay system. This game seems to be oriented for kid/ young teenager because the gameplay is really simple, no combos or crazy thing here. However, Infinity Strash is not a MUSOU no thousand of enemies and map strategy, and if I need to compare the way it plays, bosses in post game seems to be closer to a simplified Dark Souls than One Piece Pirate Warriors (I'm not saying it is nearly as good as a Souls) The way you should play is not button mashing or farming 50 levels, you have to learn the boss pattern, try 5, 10, 20 times or even more if you are not good. You can be 2 shot. Then you have "hidden" tech, and I didn't see any review mentioning that. The game has combo cancel, by pressing quickly guard just after a hit, you can reset your character animation and decide after to either dodge, combo again or guard. This allows you to react quickly. Popp and Martial Artist Maam can perform this move with meditation if you want. You have also 2 different dodges. Neutral dodge is when you press the dash button without pressing a direction, this dodge has less recovery time so you can quickly guard or do something after that. Then you have the classical dodge/dash, by pressing a direction you can dash in that direction, it has more recovery times depending on the character because YES all 6 characters are not the same (Popp has more invincibility frame, maam and hyunckel can dodge faster than dai). People complaining that the gameplay is simple and can't even understand how it works (as simple as it is) are the real crybaby (sorry). If it is simple it is accessible, not for you taste maybe but for other people, casual players or even kids.- GraphicsGame made with unreal engine 4, simple environnement, basic lighting but some part of the game like the Temple of Recollection has cool environnement artistic direction. Cel shading anime style, amazing 3D model, facial expression and animation are on point. 2D FX (skills effects etc…) are good and even better than the anime (3D VFX look in the anime), they did a great job. Some anime games doesn’t even have this “simple” standard and it is quite alarming. The HUD/UI looks good, respect the anime artistic direction, simple to understand, really easy to access and navigate it might be stupid but I’ve played One Piece odyssey this year and the interface and menu are horrible, comparing to DBZ Kakarot for exemple. But graphics is not really important for some people so let’s talk about the content.Game content : - Story mode (4.5/10)This is the worst part of the game, the game has mission/stage based structure with no level design (nowadays mobile game like to do that because it allows short play session) that doesn’t mean it is completely trash. You can enjoy that (some people prefer small ambition game compare to empty open world) but my main problem is it has too much cutscenes and not enough gameplay. 3D CGI cutscenes are amazing but it cost a lot, this game is not a Dragon Ball Z game and will never be one (no ones care about Dai especially outside japan) I don’t get why they decided to tell the entire story (even the small details) because for the pacing of a game it is really bad. Maybe Shueisha (the Shonen Jump magazine) or the Author (Riku Sanjo) asked Square to tell the entire anime without forgetting element (weird decision lol) I understand that it is impossible realistically to tell 41 episodes in full CGI, games like DBZ kakarot has most of the time no voice actors, no animation A poses 3D model watching each other and a lot of missing part of DBZ story. They should (imo) skip some part and tell only the essential part of Dai’s story to have a great pacing and better story mode. The anime and manga are amazing and enough if you want to discover the story. My only positives thing is, if you like Dai 2020 anime, you will appreciate the effort of the voice actors (they’ve recorded everything again just for this game), the OST by Yuki Hayashi are rearranged (Haikyuu, My Hero Academia…), the 3D cutscenes are great, and some missions has cool details in it (Popp’s Megante sacrifice, Dai casting Raidein spell against Hyunckel with Popp in the background, the final boss is cool, similar to Oz from One Piece Unlimited Cruise 2)  If you are expecting a big ARPG open world you are wrong, Square Enix never mentionned that, just inform yourself before buying. I will put this game mode arround 4.5-5/10 max- Temple of Recollection & RPG system (7.5/10)One of the positive part of the game, an infinite rogue like dungeon or survival mode (that’s why the game name is Infinity Strash) where you can collect bond memories (accessories with manga art/animation voices and stat boost) this is easy to understand even for casual players or kid and fortunately without gatcha economic system (because I hate that). You have over a hundred random rooms to defeat with Vearn as a final boss (amazing boss pattern and animation) and Medoroa Spell to unlock for Popp. Lot of enemies and bosses, trap, chest, shop, you need to manage your party members, your item and your buff efficiently (you have to choose a stat boost/buff after beating each room)......Challenge mode (8.5/10).......Conclusion (6.8 - 7/10 max)........

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is not terrible, but everything else is.When it comes to the action part, it's stage-based. I don't mind that, there are many stage based game that I enjoy, like Nights of Azure and Musou, but they feel like they have some more objectives. I cannot speak about variety yet, but from what I read from others, this game doesn't provide much variety anyway. The combat looks a bit repetitive, but, as a fan of the anime and DQ in general, I really like the art style, the skills, spells and the enemies. I'm particularly liking to play as Popp.What bothers me the most is the story. As others have pointed out, it's basically a powerpoint presentation. If they were going to use images from the anime, why not use anime scenes then? Or even better, the whole episode could be available to watch, that would be awesome.The other issue I have, still related to the story, is the pacing. The powerpoint presentations are too long! You watch a 5~10 minutes one, then you watch another 5~10 minutes one, then you finally can play a mission with combat (which has also another 1~5 minutes intro).  I've been playing it for around an hour and have fought only three battles, that were quite short (2~3 minutes long). Overall, it feels more like a visual novel with some gameplay (like Utawarerumono games) than a full fledged action game. If at least the story scenes were actual anime scenes it wouldn't be that bad.Now one thing that I really liked is that some of the story cutscenes before some important battle are actually rendered in game and they look AMAZING, but short. If only the whole game was presented that way, this would be a super recommended from me, regardless of everything else.I don't know if I will beat this game, but even if I do, my opinion is already set. It's a bad game (specially for its super expensive price).

_childDocuments_.review: So Infinity Strash isn't a bad game but it's likely badly marketed and maybe a bit mismanaged - it could have been a great Rogue-lite Dragon Quest, it partially is. Now it's mostly an average fun action game, for a small niche audience that misses even their target audience due to most of the fun content being barred behind late/endgame.After I've read a lot of them, unfortunately I think reviews do no justice for the game and most of them seem very lazy - that make the situation even worse.I for one think the game is actually pretty good, a fantastic love-letter and an above-average action hack and slash that has a poorly executed beginning and scares players away before it gets really fun.The Campaign and the Story is just unfortunately mediocre no matter if you are an old-time fan of the Anime/Manga or a complete newcomer - the bulk of the story ( 90% ) is told in still images and vignettes, skipping important fights and context, so story if anything is mostly nostalgia for those who love it but even then...you're better off watching the anime if you have the option for that.The small amounts of in-engine cutscenes though are absolutely gorgeous and amazing and you should definitely NOT skip those - I loved them all and they capture the story perfectly, which is why it's a shame the majority are vignettes.The beginning is going to be very easy and gives terrible first impressions but Boss Fights and Combat gets fairly challenging after a few chapters and you really have to use your Perfect Dodges, Blocks and Abilities perfectly to win fights, so I would say the combat gets quite fun and I haven't seen the post-game Challenge Mode yet that sounds like a NG+.Sadly this beginning is a typical JRPG that is handholding too much and scares away players with overly basic early game.Nevertheless, I think one of the best parts of Infinity Strash is the amount of love that went into the Monster Design and the general Character design of it as if you are a DQ fan and listen and look for the details - each character and monster has excellent sound and visual design that I'd say is on par with any Main Dragon Quest Title and while the rest of the game is low budget - you can see a lot of love that went into making this!The Campaign is roughly a 10 hours experience if you decide to skip all the vignette recaps and only watch cutscenes and play the game - roughly twice as much, 20 hours if you watch everything!BUT, I would say the campaign and the story is just the tutorial to the game and the LARGE majority of the content is the challenge mode AND the Temple of Recollection ROGUE-LITE mode - especially after completing the Main Story once, that unlocks even more extra content and layers in the Temple.Yes I think Infinity Strash was likely designed to be a Rogue-lite Dragon Quest but a campaign was attached to it for whatever reason, maybe to increase price...or to have a story-based nostalgic factor, I don't know but I think that part is mostly wasted, but that's just me.Even the game's story is all about collecting Dai's Memory I think it was pointless to make it a story-based action game and should have just focused 100% on the Temple of Recollection and make this game a proper fun Rogue-lite experience, since it already can be one - but misses the mark due to lots of filler content in Story / Challenge Mode that's just not as enjoyable.- Randomized Battles- Party Builds / Combos / Synergies- Rogue-lite progression for skills / abilities- Character Builds- Basic Roguelike Ability / Stat Boosting each Floor- Fast paced mindless-fun action combat- Post-game extra abilities and skills- Solo/Duo Challenges- Super BossesInfinity Strash is a wonderful nostalgic experience to return to the Adventures of Dai, but the storytelling isn't good for veterans nor for newcomers due to rushed pacing, but the in-game cutscenes show how much love went into creating it and what it could have been with a higher bugdet.Because the Temple of Recollection is actually fun, I would recommend the game but I can't agree with the $60 Price on it - but if you'd like a simple Action Hack and Slash with Rogue-lite experience in Dragon Quest coating - I think you can get it here, just get past the story and enjoy the rest of the content!Thank you for reading all this ^^

_childDocuments_.review: I am a fan of both Dragon Quest and the Dai anime. I was excited to see what a game based off the anime would be like and unfortunately, this game is the biggest disappointment I've had in a while. This game is basically a retelling of the story from the anime, which isn't a bad thing, but when the game is LITERALLY a retelling of the anime, it makes the game feel more like a visual novel rather than an action RPG. When you do get to the gameplay, you are put in a small area where you fight the enemies. This is not a bad thing, but it results in a lack of exploration I've come to expect in other Dragon Quest games.The few things I liked about the game were the graphics, the music, and the combat, but those things alone aren't enough to make up for the issues with this game. The majority of the time I spent playing was watching cutscenes, which were mostly screenshots directly from the anime. The pacing of the story was also way too quick and barely gives any time to develop the world and the characters. I've also had some weird screen resolution issue and the frame rate felt a bit choppy at times for some reason. I wanted to like this game, but sadly this isn't the game for me. This is not a terrible game by any means, but I wouldn't recommend this game unless it was on sale, you enjoy games of this genre, or if you are a die-hard fan of the Adventure of Dai. Otherwise, just go watch the anime instead.

Below are the main cons and pros that I can say about this game, having completed the main game (and the side dungeon along the way):1)  The story of this game (and majority of its "gameplay") is just a  that is told through multiple narrated "still-images" that have been ripped off straight from the 2020 anime remake and that's basically how most main points of the story are told for the entirety of the game. Needless to say, having already watched the whole 2020 anime remake before playing this game, it was a "grueling experience" to sit through all those cutscenes and whether I skipped them or not, the fact is that majority of this game is just these anime-ripped cutscenes that neither serve anime fans (because of how poorly the story is told through them) nor the video game fans who just want to play the game rather than sitting around, doing nothing while being bombarded with all those anime cutscenes for most of the game.2)  It is even sadder that, when you FINALLY get to the "gameplay" part, most of playable locations are either  with boring/bland backgrounds and barely anything to do besides killing a few monsters before reaching the end of the level OR  where you are immediately get thrown into a boss battle, which simply RUINS the "build-up" to the boss battle that you would normal get from other games where you actually ADVENTURE through a long level, leading into the boss room/area.3)  As for the combat itself, it's very basic and to me is RUINED by the inclusion of annoying  for skills (which are especially frustrating when enemies interrupt you and then you have to WAIT AGAIN until the cooldown is over to be able to attack again), while the dodge/guard feel very "unresponsive/sluggish" that led me to take A LOT OF DAMAGE for absolutely no reason even when I pressed the buttons at the correct time. The only exception is maybe the "World Map Music" which actually sounds "decent/catchy" so I didn't mind that one in particular, but the rest of the music would have been better off being  that should have been made specifically for the video game adaptation IMO.5)  I saw other reviewers claim that this was the "highlight" of this game, but to me, it had its own set of issues that made it another "tedious" aspect of this game such as being:-  for both regular monsters and main bosses.-  to be able to resume at a later point.-  during the entirety of the run, so if a character dies, you either have to continue at a MAJOR DISADVANTAGE (i.e. by making all subsequent battles longer/more tedious) OR quit the dungeon run at the earliest point possible and start over again with a full party (oh, and if your entire party dies or you quit mid-way through the floor, you LOSE all the rewards you gained to that point).-  ESPECIALLY those stupid "exploding rocks" that self-destruct and OHKO one of your characters, forcing you more than likely to quit and start over because of the disadvantage that you have to deal with afterwards. This is even extra frustrating when those self-destructing rocks kill one of the "AI-controlled" party members (so even when it is not your fault, the game STILL punishes you for things that are out of your hands).1) Character 3D Models look actually nice in-game.2) Elemental aspects like "Fire, Water, Lightning, etc..." look gorgeous.3) As such, combining points 1+2, "Ultimate Attacks" for both good and evil characters look badass.4) Also, the few  (using the game's engine) that generally play after defeating major bosses look AMAZING and really made me wish that THIS was how the overall story was told (along with properly constructed "adventuring levels") for a better story experience.Overall, "Infinity Strash: Dragon Quest The Adventure of Dai" video game didn't get the treatment (and budget) it deserved. _childDocuments_.review: I started getting into Dragon Quest a few months ago (maybe 5 or 6) with the first four games and Monsters: The Dark Prince. I got curious after I saw Infinity Strash in my Steam Queue and bought it at the beginning of 2024 when it was on sale. I really liked the story that I got into the manga and watched both animes (1991 and 2020). I already had some experience with some similar games, so I just needed to get used to the game's mechanics. Now about the game:-Dai's Zap paralyzing bosses at unexpected times (like one second before  Coup de Grâce is launched).-Using Popp (good spells, awesome Coup de Grâce).-Maam (Martial Artist) becoming a damage sponge with the use of some Bond Memories.-Hyunckel (Dark Armour Spear) is better than the Dark Armour Blade version (my opinion).-The DLC outfits for Maam (Warrior Priest) and Hyunckel (Dark Armour Spear) look good on them.-Certain Coup de Grâce aren't only dealing damages, they can also buff the user.-Some gimmicks during boss fights.-Being able to control the cutscenes (even if it is weird).-Having a challenge mode.-Bond Memories can compensate for being under level. (Note: I was around twenty levels under the recommendation for the final challenge when I did it.)-My favorite battles are the chapters 2, 5 and 7's final challenges.-The final battle in challenge mode.-The prophecies -Sections having unique gimmicks (except for the first two sections (layer 1 to 6)).-Being able to add some challenge  .-Some characters have skills/spells with a rather long cooldown and some others taking a little long before being sent (many enemies and bosses have time to move away or attack).-Perfect dodge and taking damage at same time (funny, weird and almost got me killed in my solo run of the Temple of Recollection).-The ally AI's tendency to attack and come back to me instead of killing their target.-The AI trying to kill a Rockbomb about to explode.-There are not many side quest/battles.-I don't like how the story ends, a lack of follow-up after the final battle.-Not being able to easily know the playable characters and foes' elemental resistances.-It looks like Dai and Maam receive more unique bonuses from Bond Memories than the others.-Getting interruped in the middle of a boss fight because of a cutscene.-Grinding for challenge mode becomes difficult.- -It is not possible to use both Maam (Warrior Priest and Martial Artist) or Hyunckel (Dark Armour Blade and Spear) in the party.-It is not possible to choose the second door after opening one.-The Bond Memories are limited to the section that correspond the chapters where they are found.-Shrooms are (almost) homing missiles.-The bonus mission timer for boss battles against two or more bosses.-I feel like  doesn't appear often while Hadlar appears a lot.-Same thing with  (even if he appeared more often). -  often using his bullet hell attack. (I'm not bad at touhou but it is hard to attack when there's no gap large enough to fit in.)-Adding Crocodine as a playable character (Not just because he's my most favorite character, he has a great potential and his size doesn't matter after having played as the Great Fairies, who are giants, in both Hyrule Warriors).-Adding Leona as a playable character (She also has some potential).-Some skills/spells Charge Time could be reduced by a little amount (  are among those that could be modified).-Maam (Martial Artist) and Hyunckel are kinda limited in term of attacks (one Coup de Grâce, three skills for Maam and Hyunckel has four).-Maybe improve the dodge frames.-More side quests (maybe even more if Crocodine and Leona were playable).-A character gallery/bestiary that describes every character, both playable and enemy, their battle abilities and shows their elemental resistances.-Giving the possibility to choose another door after opening one.-Maybe show the amount of enemies in a room. I would have liked to play as Crocodine, but at least I can see him in action as a boss. Even after having unlocking all the achievements, I try to max out every Bond Memories and skills/spells for a true 100% completion. _childDocuments_.review: The 2020 revival of the Adventure of Dai series has been fraught with its fair share of setbacks, from the Toei hack delaying the airing of a climactic episode to the lack of success and discontinuation of the mobile game A Hero's Bonds. Perhaps most intriguing among those is the tale of a little game called Infinity Strash, first announced way back in 2020 with a targeted release date of sometime in 2021.The Infinity Strash that released in 2023 does not resemble the glimpses we were given in 2020 and 2021. The graphical style was different in the original trailers, gameplay appeared to proceed through more open maps, and perhaps more notably a trailer shows a playable Leona and a screenshot shows a playable Avan.With that in mind, compounded with the obvious flaws of the game, it's easy to conclude this is a product compromised by some sort of developmental turmoil. Whatever form that turmoil took will likely remain a secret, but... is the final product still worth playing?I believe it is, with some caveats. The story mode is quite a mess, its presentation held back by the relative lack of action stages in comparison to the static, slideshow-esque cutscenes. This flaw is especially inherent during the game's first chapter, in which critical early bits of the story are skipped over with blazing speed. It's an awful first impression. The story itself is very linear, with no exploration of towns or dungeons, no side-quests apart from extra stages meant to help level up your characters, and no character banter during the stages themselves. The first half of the story of Dai is presented here in a very condensed form, with no additions and no embellishments aside from a framing device that is promptly forgotten about.However, as the game progresses and more features unlock, fans of the Dai series can find a lot to love here. The model work and animations are full of detail and personality, bursting to life in the scattered 3d cutscenes as well as on the character menu. Yuki Hayashi's score does an excellent job at hyping you up for the combat, which at first appears dead simple but shows a decent amount of depth as your party gathers and you unlock the true star of the game, the Temple of Recollection. Traversing the temple and collecting Bond Memories is quite addictive, and the combat truly shines here.Finishing the story will net you a go at the Challenge Mode, which I cannot comment on yet.If you're a gamer who primarily plays games for the story mode, there probably isn't much on offer here. But if you're a Daihard Dai fan with a little patience who's willing to overlook some admittedly big flaws, you may find a lot to love. I can't really recommend it as a first intro to the world of Dai, though. Check out the excellent 2020 anime adaptation for that.Though I do recommend waiting for a sale, a lower price of entry may make the flaws sting less.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty simple hack and slash that has everything you'd expect, regular and special attacks with the gameplay being a mix of that and a perfect dodge and perfect block system. I will say though this is the strongest I've ever seen blocking be, it actually does make a significant difference even if you're not going for a perfectly timed one. But since what you really want to know is why the community is so divided on this, I'll just get to the pros and cons.Very addictive gameplay, as to be expected from a hack and slash.Just about every party member plays uniquely and is fun.Surprisingly in depth "Bond" system (essentially your equips that do anything from stat increases to bonuses on fulfilling special conditions. Perfect dodging, below and HP threshold, ect.Tons of Dragon Quest love here, if you're a fan of the series there are a bunch of points you'll get giddy about.Voice acting is surprisingly good with only one minor stinker I can think of (Sorry Crocodine, you're just trying too hard lol).Popp is best character.The Price is just...too high. I'm sorry, even as a hardcore DQ fan this should've been $39.99 max.I'm not sure if this is just an English dubbed issue, but in a Lot of cutscenes the voicelines just end prematurely. That kinda sucks when everything is building up to a climax. Was it really too much trouble to shorten the translation into something more workable in order to fit?The final bosses were waaay too easy. I'm over here expecting some big showdown and I end up facing 1 boss who just stands there doing a straight line AoE attack that you KNOW will come out, so the only reason you could possibly get hit is if you were spamming moves. Not to mention, his attacks are somehow WEAKER than I think any other proper boss in the game.On the other hand, the "real" final boss just summons a bunch of trash mobs you can easily wipe out before doing very predictable AoE. After which he leans down, you shatter his paper-thin break guage, and chip away at his hilariously small HP pool. Just disappointing.The game feels incomplete. I know the game was advertised as only going through the first 41 episodes, but it just feels like we missed the best parts.Depending on your taste, both the non-animated cutscenes and roguelike mode might not be something you enjoy, which could be a real buzzkill since they make up in my opinion the most important parts of this game.Overall I love this game and I'll be going through challenge mode plus through the entirety of the temple of trials, but mixed is absolutely where this game should stand in review score.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun playing this game and i'm here to give a full honest non-bias review.I recommend this game if you're a huge fan of Adventure of Dai and love hack n slash games.  For everyone else I recommend waiting to get this game when it's on sale. I can't justify the $60 price for something that you're not guaranteed to enjoy.Infinity Strash is a retelling of the 2020 anime of Dai's Adventure, although they did a pretty good job, it definitely would've been better if they did the entire game in CGI or the in-game models(not sure if they couldn't do it cause of budget or everything was rushed) I can see why many fans were upset with the still images, they don't do the show or this game justice. This game would've been fantastic if it was open world and had the option for multiplayer instead of just being single player, this is unfortunately a huge opportunity they missed out on big time, the experience for Infinity Strash would be more impactful with those implemented.The Temple Of Recollection is a good rouge-like challenge and was a blast to stream for my viewers, it can get very grindy and repetitive but it is a necessary requirement for challenge mode and clearing all the floors in the TOR.The combat system is pretty straightforward but solid. It has parries, perfect dodge,etc. you really notice it in the post-game challenges. In order to complete all of the post-game events and the rest of the TOR, you need to have mastered the mechanics or have a really good understanding on how things work to further proceed. They really turn up the difficulty on stuff in challenge mode so you want to have mastered the mechanics before attempting those fights or else you'll have a miserable experience and it'll probably make you quit.The overall experience for me ended on a positive note and hopefully this helps give some insight to give Infinity Strash a chance for those that were skeptical in purchasing this game, I spent 70+ hours playing this game and don't regret it at all. I just recently did a no damage run vs all the bosses on challenge mode on my yt channel, if you're interested it that and would like some insight on gameplay when you have mastered mechanics go ahead and check it out, you won't be disappointed.I just started playing Infinity Strash again last week and cleared TOR(Temple Of Recollection)with Maam (Martial Arts) solo and ran into King Vern twice in the run.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: I finished the game just to see how the story unfolded. It's not worth it, honestly. The ending had me feeling nothing. The motivations for certain characters are flimsy at best and not enough gets resolved. Charging $60 for this feels insane. I hope no one loses their job for how poorly this performs. I'm actually worried about the developers and we all know how Square Enix loves to say games under-perform even for ones that seem to be pretty good.This is not a good video game. This is a moderately interesting VN game with some combat sprinkled in. I might go as far as saying that anyone that would actively recommend this to other people shouldn't be taken seriously for their other reviews. It's fine to enjoy it, but to think that this is a good video game for other people and for $60 would be the opinion of someone who really has no idea what they're talking about and they don't consider the time or money of other people when sharing their recommendations.Listen, I watch isekai anime. I know what trash is and I know better than to recommend a lot of it to most people. I can enjoy a thing and also realize that it's *not good* and shouldn't be recommended to others.Positives- The art- The music- The voice acting- Parts of the story (some parts are kind of stupid, like  motivation and maybe that's how DQ story lines go. I don't know.)Negatives - The lack of depth of the gameplay- The number of hours you can get out of this- The price. It should be $25 at most- The way they tell the story in what amounts to a several slideshows per every 6 minutes of combat.I'm not even done with it yet, but I believe I'm over halfway done at around 6-7 hours. When I wrote this I've also already left my game running for hours in the background while I was talking to people so it's a bit inflated.I'm thinking the DQ franchise isn't for me. They certainly can't do an action game. At least I didn't play full price, but I also can't get a refund since I got it from GMG. That's the risk you take when you get a steep discount.

Pros: Follows the anime directlyMusic of course is awesomeGraphics are pretty detailedCons:There's no open world at all.While I don't mind action combat, the combat is really stale.The fights are way too easy. It's pretty much click this town, scenario, back to main screen, click this town to fight a boss, click this town, scenario. The value you get out of the game isn't worth the 60$ price tagThe game crashed for me mid fight quite a few times.All in all, it's a casual game with no risk/reward. _childDocuments_.review: Infinity Strash: Dragon Quest - The Adventure of Dai is a brand new spin-off from the popular Dragon Quest series that adapts the anime (which is based on the manga) into a videogame. I haven’t watched the anime yet, so I could be considered a newcomer in this case, though I love the Dragon Quest series and I have played most of the classic RPG titles in the past. For some weird and unknown reason, the story of Infinity Strash only covers around 50% of the anime series, so you won’t get to the end of Dai’s story by playing this game. Maybe a sequel is already in the works, but personally I don’t like to play a game that features an incomplete storyline, especially when it’s based on finished material such as the anime. Essentially, the story is about a young hero named Dai who must save the world from the Dark King Vearn. After a tough fight against Dragon Master general Baran, Dai loses his memory, so the game slowly starts introducing the beginning of his journey, how he met his friends and how he got up to this battle. The story is narrated through multiple chapters, with each one divided into story cutscenes and combat sequences. The first are basically narrated as a visual novel, with still-images and text appearing on-screen.  These images are captured directly from the anime, but they are not animated, which is really disappointing to see and makes the whole narrative boring and uninteresting. I honestly don’t understand this choice, if you are going to use the original material from the anime, at least use it in a good way. I think that they could have made all the sequences in-engine (like  and  games do), instead they only took a bunch of images from the anime to make these visual novel slideshows. So yes, the narrative is bad and didn’t get me invested in Dai’s story as I thought at the beginning. I have watched the anime trailer and I know that it is worth watching, but I don’t think that anyone (fan or newcomer) would really enjoy how the story is narrated in this game. At least the combat sequences include some in-engine cutscenes that look pretty cool, but most of the story is told through still-images.Despite being an action RPG, there is no exploration at all. The whole combat sequences take place in decently sized arenas in which you can move freely. Fighting seems like a mix of mousou and soulslike mechanics, but it’s pretty much bare-bones and probably oriented to a young player base. Commands are basic; you can dodge, block and combo-attack. Usually you play as Dai, but you can swap characters freely and the rest of them are controlled by the AI. Each character has a specific set of skills and spells that go in a cooldown state after use. There is also a powerful ultimate attack that needs to be charged before use and is really cool to watch. Overall, the combat is acceptable, though more adapted to casual players because of its simplicity and ease. What I didn’t like is that, except for the bosses, there isn’t enough variety of standard enemies, so you fight the same ones over and over. The Temple of Recollection is a really fun addition; it’s basically a roguelike dungeon that you can explore whenever you want, but each time you enter, your characters downgrade to level one. The Temple allows you to fight enemies through multiple rooms, with the difficulty increasing after each battle as well the possibility of collecting special rewards such as new memories and amber (used to upgrade your characters).The artistic aspect is where the game really shines. The 3D models are gorgeous and faithful to the anime representation, while the special effects (such as fire and lightning) are beautiful to see, especially during spells and ultimate attacks sequences. The in-game cutscenes during combat look really nice too, but it’s a pity they decided to mix still images from the anime with these ones to build an inconsistent narrative. Technically speaking, the game is very well optimized and I didn’t experience any bugs or glitches. Infinity Strash: Dragon Quest The Adventure of Dai is really hard to recommend. After playing for many hours, I still can’t figure out who the target is in this game. Despite being a fan of the series and loving this crazy good art style, the story didn’t arouse my interest because of the way it was narrated (through many still images in a visual novel style), while the combat was generally okay, though not really engaging for someone used to playing challenging action and soulslike games. Newcomers should definitely watch the anime or read the manga first (to avoid ruining their first experience), though even fans of the original material will find the game tedious and pointless (considering it doesn’t even cover the whole anime story). The price is also insanely high in my opinion, as this is nowhere near any AAA game I have played recently in terms of content and quality. If you are desperate to try a game based on the anime, then I really suggest getting Infinity Strash with a pretty decent discount. It’s an acceptable game, but an underwhelming Dragon Quest one.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a long time Dragon Quest fan. I even enjoyed both Heroes and their Mincraft spinoff. I love the cartoon graphics and art style. I hope their future real games adopt this. Now I fully understand this was taken from the pages of Manga comics. But I suffered through an hour of barely animated still pictures just to finally get to the "game". Which turned out to be shallow and boring arena battles in small enclosed areas. This is a game I'd expect for the less than $30 pricepoint. It will be one of the first in over 500 game purchases that I actually request a refund on.

_childDocuments_.review: The presentation of the story is not the best. Whenever there was a cutscene using the in-game models it was pretty decent.The gameplay is fairly simple in terms of mechanics, but is surprisingly fun. This game has the foundation to be a great game, but it's too short campaign-wise and doesn't have any depth in the mechanics to make up for the short length. The Temple of Recollection is neat, but not really enough to make up for the lack of content. This game is definitely not a $60 game for what you get, maybe $40 at most.That being said, I really enjoyed this game and I hope a second game is made to finish the rest of the anime story and to refine what this game started.
_childDocuments_.name: Infinity Strash: DRAGON QUEST The Adventure of Dai

_childDocuments_.review: While this game could be better I am having fun playing it. It doesn't have that exploration and sense of adventure that most dragon quest games have. But I am having fun with the combat and feel very nostalgic when playing it. If you're someone who enjoys the anime then you will probably enjoy this game. I would give it a solid 7/10. If $60 is a lot of money for you then I would wait for a sale ($40 seems worth it).

_childDocuments_.review: The story of the game is a masterpiece which fills the negative gaps of the game.If you enjoy story games. This is the game for you!Game play is not bad and it is fun.The game story is too long and this is why they added chapters and made it as a slide show. Still, I see it as the best suitable for such a storytelling of a masterpiece adventure.Watching the anime is fun and interacting with some chilling gameplay against monsters is fun. Fighting some big characters like crocodine, Hyuneckel etc. This is just awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: Infinity Strash: DRAGON QUEST The Adventure of Dai

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't your normal "Dragon Quest" rpg. It's a beautiful, well-crafted tribute to the incredible Manga, and Anime series: "Dragon Quest: The Adventure of Dai." This game tells the story of the Anime Series up to chapter 41. I thought it was totally epic, as a fan of the original Manga, and the original Anime Series, it was a trip down memory lane. I geeked out on the classic, fantastic Dragon Quest art throughout the entire game! Fighting all those Dragon Quest Monsters in real time combat was a blast. The cell shaded graphics look great, and match the anime style of the game perfectly. I ended up getting hooked on the action rpg combat too, leveling my characters up to level 60+ and feeling much more powerful as I equipped, and maxed out "Bond Memories" in the "Temple of Revelation." I really enjoyed the grind. Thank you Square-Enix for allowing such an amazing tribute to the original Manga and Anime Series to happen. What a work of art to be proud of! This is a dream come true for the fans of the original anime like me.  It was such a great joy. Also, please add some more paid skins or playable Crocodine to the game, my credit card is ready for more! "Beast King Anguish Blast!"

_childDocuments_.review: Format for the story mode is a lot of still cutscenes to explain the story, the combat does not feel very fun and slightly clunky i havent gotten past 2nd fight but i think ive seen enough to know that this is a cashgrab on dragon quest lovers, it for sure does not feel worth the 60$ maybe 20$ at best.

Square Enix is too scared to invest in games that aren't Final Fantasy, so we end up with games like this where the cutscenes are just screenshots displayed in sequence. Dragon Quest was always one of my favorite series at least back when Enix was the in charge. _childDocuments_.review: It's not a terrible game. It's just meh. The game is split into 2 sections. The story mode which consists of very short stages/boss fights (3-5 minutes unless you're severely underleveled) with a retelling of the anime and an uninspired roguelike mode. The story is actually kinda interesting but it's told in such an awful way that I started to skip the cutscenes. The combat is serviceable but not good enough to carry the game given how it's 99% of what you'll be doing. It's slow, shallow, methodical combat, except the enemies attack quickly. The only reason the game isn't a complete write off is the progression system. If you want a game to just shut off your brain and grind resources to get stronger than this is your game... Well there are still plenty of better games for that. Ultimately that feels like every part of this game. There are just games that do it far better than this one.There are some weird bugs and performance issues you might run into. It's the 2nd game that I own that has problems with Windows Game Mode. I also had to do some other tweaking in Windows App settings to fix some other stutters. Now I'm just left with shader cache stuttering but that's mostly gone away. Also, the first time I started the game I was locked at 1280x720p 60 hz (default VGA display settings for my monitor). After closing the game and opening again it randomly fixed itself but apparently someone in the Steam discussion board is stuck with the game like that.
_childDocuments_.name: Infinity Strash: DRAGON QUEST The Adventure of Dai

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend to get this game on full price only if you are a hardcore fan of Adventure of Dai, the game is the 2020 anime, so If you have already finished the anime, it will be as watching it again.It would be great if the game had some exploration, equipment buying or some other features than fighting, the Memory and Spell system upgrades feel like they where taken from a gatcha, obtian hundreds of the same item, hundreds of forging materials and thousands of money.  The temple of recollection is a good rouge-like challenge but it can become repetitive, in-game visuals are incredible but somehow the game feels incomplete, just like the 90's anime, the 2020 adaptation of it may have ended the story, but the game does not portrait the full story, hopefully some DLC will complete it, but honestly I doubt it.The combat system is somewhat simple but entertaining I had a good time figuring out bosses paterns and switching between spells and abilites to learn better strategies, overall it is a decent game, but as I said in the beginning of all of this, wait until a sale to play this.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game but it's not worth the price.It's a pleasure to farm cards on temple of recollection and the more you advanced on levels the more difficult it becomes (level 4 with poisonous mushrooms for example)I suggest not to start the temple before baran fight to get some challenge on story against some bosses.

_childDocuments_.review: I think I kinda got this game at the right time for me. I'm recommending it simply on my own experiences.I'd think you get this game based on a few different factors1: You have no knowledge of The Adventures of Dai BUT you've played and/or are interested in Dragon Quest in some way. Simply because it does an alright Job giving you the gist of whats going on within the universe but it does just jump over a lot of scenes from the anime and and they ain't great looking.2: You want something brain dead to play. I simply say this because the Game play is Brain dead, like other then some boss-fights which require mild thought process. But all in all, if you need something to just turn your brain off for 20 hours this isn't that bad a run through.3: You are REALLY into Anime mainly because it plays like an anime game, a more action-ish linear level one with big flashy moves.This game does have problems however, like some of the one on one fights. This game is not made for one on one fighting, Their is this weird input lag with the parry system and enemies have this real weird no-frame like attack pattern where they start an attack and then before the animation has even moved they have already done the attack. It's odd to get through and it's only been noticeable in one on one fights, when you're fighting in a group against a big boss you won't even realise its happening. And that's my biggest real gripe with the game, some of the animations are just oddly timed and don't really come out as they should.I do however like the character interactions and it's kinda got me into maybe watching the anime. Its been great to really play through the game get concepts, races and monsters that jump from game to game.Now other then the animation issues, the game has a real good Base level Dynasty Warriors kind of fighting. Minor RPG Progression with levelling and bond memories work as stat boosts and special effects, it's pretty basic and it does the Job I think it's trying to convey.I will say this ain't worth full price simple for it's length and how simple the game is as a whole. But I'd recommend it in a year when it's discounted and heavily dropped, their ain't enough here for the price it's going for now. But it's an overall good experience, and a good pallete clenser for me because it's good to play something sometimes where you can just mash and switch your brain off.

_childDocuments_.review: Not the game fans wanted, but still fun if you like the manga. So please, read the manga, fall in love with it and then buy this game. You won't like it otherwise. I love to play Poppu and the other heroes, and the sanctuary mode is challenging if you don"t greed at first tries. This game can be liked, give it a chance :)
_childDocuments_.name: Infinity Strash: DRAGON QUEST The Adventure of Dai

_childDocuments_.review: I Enjoyed this game, l kind of liked the storytelling in this game, basically the presentation of the story are bunch of slideshows from the anime itself, and probably the voices are too, still better than forcing me to read a script to understand the story, it feels a bit scummy but I think that they were on a budget and maybe they didn't want to risk it by going all out on a game that might not get the recognition that it deserve, personally not really mad about it and it's still better than making me go from A to Z I guess, but the in game cut scenes look amazing, they are really really cool, wish there was some quick time action to make me feel more immerse, and the music is as the same as the one from the Anime, Which Totally not a bad thing, a lot of it's music are badass and really hype, Imagine if the whole campaign used more of the in-game cutscenes, this game would've been 9/10 at least.if you like a challenge then I recommend this game for you, the toughest Bosses I played against are Crocodine, Hyunckel and Baran, they are stupid strong in challenge mode, Mystvearn pissed me off the most.And we got the temple, the deeper you go, the harder it gets, it is the heart and soul of the game, enjoyed it alot and beat it, wasn't an easy task until I got a certain ultimate, Don't want to spoil but let me say that it's so funny and busted, you will know what I mean when you get it, I really hope that Square Enix don't nerf it, but in general I wouldn't recommend this game to someone who is new to the Anime, I'd rather if you watch it first.combat is mid, and Ironically it plays like a RPG Game, I can only mash square and activate 3 of my abilities, wish I can equip all of my abilities (there are more than 3 to choose from) don't know why I'm restricted to just 3, but they gave a reason to switch characters mid fight to use these other abilities that are equipped on Popp, yeah and I can't lock on to monsters, kept missing every ability, like Why can I only lock on Bosses? make 0 sense, but I have to say it's rewarding when you get the timing right with your attacks, blocks and dodges, Special Moves and Awakenings are really impactful.if I'd rate it out of 10, to me this game is 6.5/10, or maybe 7 just because this game have 0 bugs, now if you're reading this don't rush buying this game, just wait for Black Friday or any other special sale this game gets.The price alone is bugging me, this game should've been 45-50$ Max, like Square Enix, do you really think that this game on the same bar as GOW and RDR2?!

_childDocuments_.review: Glorified slideshow with intermittent combat. It isn't remotely similar to any other game in the franchise, be it spin-off or main line. I love this series so much and this was a major letdown. Watch the anime instead if you're interested in Dai's story, and wait until this game is nearly free on a sale if you want to try it out of morbid curiosity. Otherwise just avoid it entirely.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR-Mid game Wish I could give this game a neutral review since with what the screenshots show isn't what the game really is, mostly just consists of level to level dungeons and "big" arena boss fights which are very easy granted I only played very little, if you were expecting a open-world Dragon Quest this isn't that at all sadly. For the story its just a recap of what the previous stories was in the early chapters and maybe until the end of the game, in which you can just look up a manga recap on Youtube if you're curious enough for Dai's story.

_childDocuments_.review: So imagine going to a vending machine and you spend 1.50 on a small bag of Funyuns. You hit the numbers and get the bag but once you open it.. it's filled with 90% air and almost no Funyuns. Pretty much that's how bad this game is.Story is fine, gameplay is uninspired and bland, presentation is top notch but everything else is horrible. A complete waste of my time.
_childDocuments_.name: Infinity Strash: DRAGON QUEST The Adventure of Dai

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Runs Great. Simple but fun gameplay loop. I.e. Attack Attack Attack, Special. Repeat, but some bosses have to fun mechanics to learn and dodge. There's a decent amount of customization for characters. Id say this is only really for die hard dai fans/DQ fans.Cons: Lots of cutscenes. No Actual Armor/Equipment other than "Bonds" Which are cool. Short. Im 6 hours in and almost done with chapter 4 out of 7, so unless 5, 6, and 7 are much longer its about 10-12 hours. but there is Challenge mode for another probably 10 hours. and some Grinding for upgrades. all in all fun game. I'd give it a solid 7.5/10

name: Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart
detailed_description: Steam Exclusive Offer Link your Steam account with your account for PlayStation™Network and unlock 25 Raritanium* while your accounts are linked. * In-game upgrade materials. About the Game The intergalactic adventurers are back with a bang in Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart! Go dimension-hopping with Ratchet and Clank as they venture onto a PC near you for the very first time. Help them take on an evil emperor from another reality as you jump between action-packed worlds and beyond. With their own universe next in the firing line, dust off the dynamic pair’s outrageous weaponry and stop a dimensional collapse in its tracks! Unite the double team supreme with a cast of familiar allies and new faces, including newcomer Rivet. She’s a Lombax resistance fighter from another dimension, who is just as determined to take out the robotic scourge. DualSense™ wireless controller integration Enjoy a dazzling interdimensional adventure. Developed by acclaimed studio Insomniac Games and brought to PC by Nixxes Software, you’ll go beyond what you see with in-game actions coming to life in your hands via the DualSense™ wireless controller.* Haptic feedback and adaptive trigger technology create lifelike sensations: feel the hum of a spacecraft vibrate across the surface of the controller, or the kick of pulling your trusty Enforcer’s trigger. PC features Blast your way through an interdimensional adventure as Ratchet and Clank make their way to PC for the very first time! Wrap your eyes around delightful, diverse dimensions, with ultra-wide support for 21:9, 32:9, and 48:9 (triple monitor support) resolutions!* See the omniverse brought to life with the option of unlocked frame rates! You can also enjoy ray-traced reflections, as well as newly added, ray-traced shadows for exteriors.** Witness the latest upscaling technologies, including NVIDIA DLSS 3, AMD FSR 2, Intel XeSS and Insomniac Games’ Temporal Injection. NVIDIA Reflex and image quality-enhancing NVIDIA DLAA are also supported. Tailor a variety of graphics quality options to a range of devices, from high-end PCs to portable PC gaming devices. Play with the DualSense™ controller to experience haptic feedback and dynamic trigger effects.*** Or choose mouse and keyboard – with a wide range of control customization options. Includes support for achievements and cloud saves on PC game launchers. Join the heroes Employ an epic arsenal of explosive weapons, including the Burst Pistol, Topiary Sprinkler and the Shatterbomb. Zip above cityscapes, boost into combat and slip through dimensions with physics-defying new gadgets. Connect with the sounds of combat and explore in wonder as worlds come to life, enveloping you with high fidelity sound. Sense the impact of in-game rumbles and explosions through the DualSense™ wireless controller’s haptic feedback. Travel in style Planet-hop with abandon as this adventure sends you hurtling across the galaxy at hyper-speed. Experience the intergalactic shuffle of dimensional rifts as they combine new worlds and gameplay. Warp across battlefields to rapidly gain your combat advantage and repair planetary rifts with dimension-spanning puzzles. Explore never-before-seen planets and see alternate dimension versions of old favorites, now more alive than ever with exotic flora and fauna. An epic journey awaits Play as Ratchet and as newcomer Rivet – a Lombax resistance fighter from another dimension. Discover Clank’s all-new interdimensional mechanics. * Compatible PC and display device required.  ** Compatible PC and graphics card required for enhanced graphics. *** Wired connection required to experience the full range of in-game controller features.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first played the game, back when it came out, I played it on this system where I'm writing the review:Ryzen 5600xRTX 307016gb ramSSDNow I made an upgrade to Windows 11 and bought a gaming laptop, the game presented problems in said laptop up until I upgraded its RAM, from 8gb to 32gb. Prior to that it was a game that would crash randomly, reporting issues with the graphics card, but in my testing, I found out the game didn't have problems with the card, it was maxing out the RAM instead.Now I try the game here and it makes the whole system crash on anything above the "medium" preset; it has a BSOD that reports a failure with the graphics driver; ran DDU, reinstalled the most recent NVIDIA driver, and it still happenned.End up rebooting the pc, lowering the preset to "medium" and now the game is running perfectly fine; this my friends, is the demonstration of a bad pc port; any pc port that can't run at certain settings would drop the framerate or even crash, before actually affecting the PC in a negative way.My recommendation for this game is as follows: play it if you have a top of the line pc, or if you're confortable dropping the preset to "medium" -it doesn't help the game defaults to the "high" preset either-, independently of your configuration.Other than that, just expect a nice game, that's more flash vs substance, and you'll be okay; it's a very graphically intensive game, and a fairly badly optimized one at that.I didn't got the BSOD with any other game, which is to say, this is the game that makes the driver crash... maybe it's a problem with Windows 11, but either way. It's a pain.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time Ratchet and Clank fan, I was delighted to hear this game is coming to pc and having finished it, I can confidently say that it might be one of the best games in the series and a great experience for both new-comers and veteran fans.Throughout the years Ratchet and Clank series transitioned from a platformer-shooter to more of a shooter game with exploration and platforming as its second focus. But this installment feels like a perfect mixture of both. I really felt like playing the original trilogy with this - There's a lot of platforming and it feels great. I especially liked the Phantom Dash, it makes the moveset feel complete and also fresh. There's a lot of platforming challenges to do and collectibles to find. As for the combat, it feels polished and has more depth. The weapon roster is really good with a lot of variety and the enemies and bosses are fun and fair. It's also worth mentioning that their attacks are telegraphed well. Overall I have no complaints for the gameplay aspect.This game continues the plotline with Dimensionator and Lombaxes, previously explored in the Future saga, but you can still enjoy the story without playing the previous games. The plot of this game was great and more serious that I expected. It drives the main focus to its characters and their developments, touching on subjects such as self-worth and trust.I really enjoyed seeing these characters grow and change throughout the course of the game.The new characters : Rivet and Kit - are especially interesting and I find their stories engaging. It's also worth mentioning that the game was pretty funny.Due to my hardware I played on medium settings, but this game still looked gorgeous. Planets are distinct from each other, with unique, beautiful designs and a lot of details and thecharacter models are also of high quality. Overall the game is pretty, not much to add here. In recent years, as Ratchet and Clank switched to more story-driven format, the soundtrack began to less funky and more cinematic, but honestly? This game has fairly good music. There's few tracks that genuinely have this og feel to them.The dialogue and audio-design in general was also good, no complaints here. I was plesantly surprised that my computer ran this game fairly well. There were some minor performance issues with the dimensions switching, where it would take some time to load in, but despite that, it all run pretty good. I did encounter some bugs though and the game crashed few times, but it wasn't game breaking. The only bug that really got me confused, was when the music stopped playing in the levels - upon further researchI found out that this bug also existed in the ps5 version, not sure whether or not it was fixed.So yeah, that's pretty much it, I enjoyed this game a lot, buy it!!

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this on PS5 and PC at launch so you know where I stand in terms of voting with your wallet. Insomniac earned this as one of my favorite studios. I've played all of the R&C's and this is one of my favorites. Let's get the huge negative out of the way: it's a crying shame how they lobotomized the humor, dumbed down the story for three year olds, and shoved the most generic obvious morality so far down your throat you can't breath anything else. If you need a good narrative or count on the humor it's hard to recommend actually. Luckily you can pause then skip the cutscenes, which is so sad for a R&C, especially one with such high production quality. However they're really that bad: eye-rolling, vomit inducing, not funny-at-all dialog. Shame on letting this happen to such a wonderful series. With that out of the way it's still an absolutely thrilling experience from start to finish because of the amazing visuals and phenomenal gameplay. R&C nails the formula of tickling your pleasure centers; visual, audial, sensory, muscle-memory, & rewards. I literally feel great while playing with a huge smile plastered across my face. In most games it's stupid to be smashing boxes everywhere but Ratchet trains you to crave that satisfying sound as you smash a huge pile of crates & ammo as they swirl around you like a tornado tingling against each other. You can't wait to see what each new environment will look like and what craziness lives there. Each enemy is so fun and creative. All the weapons are so unique, yours and theirs. The projectiles look so cool as they're whizzing towards you in funny patterns- always slowly to give you time to dodge. Also appreciate the upgrade system that encourages you to utilize all your weapons. The PSP versions didn't do R&C justice so playing the first half on the Steam Deck was a mini-dream come true. It plays really well around 45fps and enabling customized gyro for aiming makes it feel fresh.Played the second half on my bigrig PC and OLED tv and holy moly what a time to be a gamer! Never dreamed gaming could be so good. Do yourself a favor and play with a DualSense controller (works wirelessly now). Completely elevates this game. It somehow connects to your inner caveman: vibrations good, mmm! The guns all pop and it's hard to describe but it just feels so damned satisfying feeling the haptics react to your gameplay. It's even useful like when you run out of ammo.This version also adds a wonderful dash ability and traversing is super fast with mad acceleration. It will be hard to go back to older R&Cs without these features now. Highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: Ratchet and Clank: Rift Apart is a chicken pot pie barium extravaganza that left me speechless and craving seconds from start to finish. Insomniac Games has cooked up a gaming masterpiece that combines the perfect blend of action, adventure, and a heaping serving of chicken pot pie barium goodness. Prepare your taste buds for a delectable feast of interdimensional proportions!Let's start with the chicken pot pie barium storytelling. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Get it on sale. Don't get hype.The writers clearly didn't know anything about the previous games(The trilogy especially), and the plot is rushed. Ratchet and clank both act overly nervous about doing most anything and it just doesn't feel like the same duo we've come to know over the passed decade or so. Ratchet went from being a hothead to military trained to death defying gauntlet king and he's scared or amoeboids now?Characters make pivotal decisions in seconds that make it very clear that there were plans to stretch certain character developments across a longer game, but we ended up with a handful of planets with too many scripted or uninteresting sections that drag down the game to a decent C grade or 6-7/10. Ratchet's effectively a boring nerd(Stronger words can describe this but I'll keep that to my friend circle), Kit's ok, and her being nervous actually made sense to me as a brand new character, but as another reviewer mentioned, she wouldn't hold up to scrutiny Rivet is unnecessarily a jerk at random, despite the very obvious things that happen around her that should convince her to not be a jackass to the people who aren't outright trying to hurt her. Dr Nefarious is ok but is effectively put in time-out. Emperor Nefarious has a striking attitude(That I love) and has moments where it's clear that he doesn't mess around, but he still ends up messing around(Which becomes very disappointing in the end), and in general they clearly wanted to focus on Rivet's universe of characters, but not enough to commit any meaningful amount of time to exploring them except for their Skidd(Who also only has a short screen time).Kit sits at the top in terms of characters I like, and both Ratchet and Clank sit firmly at the bottom. Which is insane to me. Kit, Emperor Nefarious, Rivet, Dr Nefarious, Ratchet, Clank from most to least liked.Personally, the biggest draw in any game for me is the gameplay. I prefer to spend most of my time  something rather than watching cutscenes or sitting through scripted sequences. Thankfully, you're allowed to skip the vast majority of cutscenes, and a lot of the miscellaneous stuff is very easy to find(I found all the bolts and lorbs and spy bots on my first run, before starting the first loop, make of that what you will, lack of challenge or easy to 100%), so I don't have any complaints about the cutscenes specifically(We'll get to this in a moment). While the devs clearly had fun and were very creative about a select number of weapons that are very satisfying to use, there are still a number of weapons that definitely overlap and become redundant through the game. Several of the mini ally weapons could have been combined or tossed, in all honesty. Or like, why couldn't the Blackhole Storm just be the Burst pistol's ultimate form, like how the N60 Storm becomes the Hurricane? Yeah the explosion trait would be odd but it's effectively two different rapid fire weapons that could have just been one minigun in the end. My personal favorites are probably the Void Reactor(The shield gun that, while I see what they were going for, it's just not quite so good while leveling it up), and the Cold Front(It rivals the Ryno is how effectively it just clears the entire screen. It feels like a second, better Ryno because of how it functions in comparison(You'll want to find out for yourself because I was surprised when I found out, compared to it). What I do have complaints about are these E3 Presentation style moments that suck any interactivity out of the game and bore me to death. One of the planets is halved by a long grinding section followed by a cutscene(Which has a large problem solved by a garbage single sentence that drains any sense of tension or danger from the entire section, and makes the planet feel very weak) The flight sections aren't very interesting, and the big moments that are often punctuated by rift tethering generally put me to sleep. I'm sorry, but the rift gimmick doesn't really become all that interesting over time. It's a neat idea, but they don't really do anything truly innovative with it outside of giving you another place to move to. Could have had something like allowing your weapons to interact with the rifts, or anything really. The rift mechanic really only sees the use of moving from point A to point B and that's really all they do with it, outside of some hidden items.Doing the mini puzzles is ok the first time, and to be fair, there's never been anything to really write home about when playing clank's sections in the original trilogy, but again, thankfully you can choose to just outright skip them. For the longest time, I was interested in Glitch right up until I did her puzzles. She won't shut up.  Clanks are more interesting because they actually make you think about how to solve the puzzles, whereas Glitch's "puzzles" are more just stepping on buttons and mindlessly shooting the turrets and then the missiles and that's about it. I can give credit for the navigation, I liked moving around in her environments, but that's about it.You'll never see people talking about this. The original trilogy clears it by a country mile. David Bergeaud cannot be topped because his music was extremely unique and experimental across every single planet. a good 90% of the songs will be more memorable than anything in this game, and it's mainly because the sound mixing is bad. The rift tethering sound is boosted, so it's loud, as well as the fighting, and very cluttered, so it tends to be drowned out. What the music actually is, is the kind of music you'd find in movies, the orchestral type. A lot of "Epic inspiring orchestral" pieces that mush together and beg to be noticed by your ears when the games default audio settings won't even give you the time of day on any of it, unless you're out of combat, or in the character menu(Which is one of the only decent pieces I liked and could hear). We had two different musicians on this game, and neither of them took any notes from the previous games to make anything unique, only to have a Nefarious theme and then everything else is just "Epic movie soundtrack" the album. David's music is constantly remembered to this day because there was a general theme of weird, zany, and ear worm like moods across the board, with the occasional intense track that the game's audio respected enough to allow you to really take it in and get it stuck in your head. Rift Apart's music just sounds like any other song you'd hear if you watched a Marvel movie.The credits song is alright though. I can't complain about that. Both Nefarious' singing was a big surprise.Just go back. Get it on discount, or go back to the older games. This is kind of a let-down for anyone who's been a fan of the series for such a long time like myself, but an ok pick for someone who doesn't tend to think too hard about what's happening on the screen. Nobody feels like anyone you've known before, and you'll find yourself frustrated at the decisions people make, the music is unnoticeable, it's very easy to find everything if you're the type that enjoyed really going out of your way to find the secret collectibles, leaving good gameplay as the only stand out part. Only good, though.

_childDocuments_.review: [Disclaimer: This is my first Ratchet & Clank game, and thus this review will be made without regards to previous games in the series]Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart is a 3D platformer / shoot-‘em-up where the player is given a growing arsenal of weapons to mow down hordes of enemies in extremely expressive combat. The game follows the titular Ratchet and Clank as they are tossed to an alternate dimension, meeting their dimensional counterparts, Rivet and Kit, and try to foil the schemes of Dr. and Emperor Nefarious and fix crumbling reality.As implied, the combat in this game is very fun. The player is given new weapons to buy at a rapid pace, which are easy to buy if the player is fully interacting with the game’s levels (at least until the late game). Using a weapon gives it experience to level up, at which point the player can spend collectible currency to upgrade the weapon substantially. This makes it feel like combat is constantly evolving and giving you new options, while still allowing you to focus on improving the weapons you like once you’ve found them. The platforming also feels dynamic and seems like it’d be great to speedrun, with several level mechanics and player options letting the player go faster and faster as the game progresses. I enjoyed the game’s story, though it’s nothing revolutionary. It also features a heavier emphasis on the dimensional counterpart characters, especially Rivet and Kit, rather than the titular ones, which as a newcomer I didn’t mind, but veterans might be a bit disappointed. I had a great time with this game, so my main complaint was that it was rather short, only taking me 14 hours to 100% my first save file. It’s a pretty tight experience, but I still would’ve liked to see at least a couple more levels. Additionally, while mowing down regular enemies never got old, there was a disappointing lack of variety in boss enemies. There were three repeating bosses that interchangeably were mini-bosses and level bosses, and only four unique bosses across the game’s twelve-ish levels. The game compensates with a few thrilling platforming sequences, but I still would have appreciated more, which can really sum up my issues with this game. Finally, at least on the PC version I played on (v1.922.0.0), there were a handful of bugs, mostly a problem I encountered frequently in the late game where my weapon would switch randomly but the weapon wheel still thought I was using my intended weapon, and a hard crash I got when platforming to an area in the early game I maybe wasn’t supposed to get to.Overall, while I wanted more, what is there in the game is excellent and very fun.
