_childDocuments_.review: As a disclaimer do NOT buy this game if you are running an RTX 2060 and an i5-8400 processor. This game will run absolutely terribly with those internal parts. An RTX 4070 and an i5 12th gen will run the game buttery smooth though.Ratchet and Clank Rift Apart is yet another PS5 game that has made it's way to PC and I couldn't be happier. Even two years out from the original release it still holds up remarkably well in most every regard. Although I do have my issues with the game, the biggest being that it feels like a glorified tech demo for the PS5 which means the game doesn't have nearly the breadth of content that it could have.Moving on to specifics about the game I'll start off with the most notable part; Graphics and performance. As far as the visuals of the game they're absolutely stunning. The level of detail on nearly every single texture, model, and background is a visual treat which is all the sweeter when it's backed up by a rock solid frame rate. The game visually and performance wise is one of the best examples of what "next gen" can look like. Additionally the load times are fantastic, even though I don't have the most powerful PC possible loading entirely new areas only took mere second or two and that's so damn impressive.Talking about the gameplay I think it's really fun. The majority of the weapons in the game feel good to use and all have a great impact when firing them as well as hitting enemies. The controls are buttery smooth, platforming feels precise and rarely ever has any issues on it's own. And the pace of the game is great in that it rarely ever takes a second to stop as you're pretty much on a roller coaster the entire way through. That being said while the gameplay is fantastic the variety in enemies isn't. You'll pretty be fighting the majority of the same enemies throughout the entire game. Not only from the perspective of archetypes (small enemies, big enemies, flying enemies etc.) but literally the exact same models. It's somewhat masked by the dimension aspect of the game but I wish there was more enemy variety throughout.Now when it comes to dimension hopping it's honestly super fun ♥♥♥♥. It's great to go into pocket dimensions for fun side challenges as well as use dimensional tears to move from one side of the arena to the other.As for the narrative and the story I have mixed feelings no them. Although while I like Rivet and Kit as dimensional counterparts of Ratchet and Clank as well as the arc they go through I can't say I was heavily invested into the overall narrative or the stories of each individual planet. They're not bad but they don't stand out as anything more than locations for the plot to take place, they just have little personality. And the writing is probably the weakest aspect of the game for me. When it comes to the main cast they're usually alright, but it's when side characters start talking is when I have a problem. Most of the time they have a "Disney/Marvel" issue where every serious situation has to be undercut with a joke afterwards. Or sometimes they're just straight up not funny like the Morts. The only joke about them is that they're all named Mort and they act Canadian.All that said I would still recommend this game quite a bit even with my grievances about it

_childDocuments_.review: With this review I want to address this game and also Steam and their review system. 1) The steam review system is really anything but accurate. Only "yes" or "no" is not really helpful especially with games like this one. A 1-10 system or grades would be much more helpful. I'm a huge fan of the franchise and as the reviews and the voices of players and professionals were both overwhlmingly positive, I was kind of hyped that I can finally play it. And yes, I had fun with the game.2) The positive aspects of the game are the following: a really good graphic and graphic design with a really atmospheric soundtrack. The voice actors make a really good job and the the new added characters fit the universe pretty good. The highligt of this game is the gameplay. A fast paced jump & gun with focus on gunfights and cinematic jump passages. Frustrating jumps/ blind jumps do not exist. It is for both Jump & run veterans and newcomers. Although newcomer will have more fun with the game, cause it is not really difficult. I played directly on the highest difficulty and for someone who played one R&C game before this should not be much of a challenge. The planets are well crafted and they differ enough so everyone of them has something unique. Now why I say, that I don't recommend the game? 1) The story: 2) The weapons: 3) Dr. Nefarious: 4) Copy and Paste: The last point of criticism for me is, that the collectibles are so easy to find, some of them are so lazily hidden, that you find them without the map that reveals all treasures. _childDocuments_.review: I grew up on the old Ratchet and Clank games from as early as the PS2, and have fond memories of playing entire nights away listening to the jazzy, spy movie-ish music tracks and smashing crates with fewer pixels on their textures than I had cares in the world. I can confidently say that while this game doesn't completely copy those older titles, it knows it's roots and brings back some of those old memories while still introducing new and interesting mechanics.I never thought I'd see the classic band of characters in such high-definition and with such animated models, but it really brings their eccentric flips and punchy hits to life. Plus a backdrop of simply gorgeous environments, with mixes of the old dull, brutalist designs and new vibrant vistas throughout the game's several levels. Wrap all of that up with flashy, explosive effects and some very theme-centric character designs and you've got one of the best looking games I've played in a while.The controls can admittedly be a bit frustrating at times, between the odd momentum (or sometimes lack thereof) and indecisive gravity it can be a real pain to do some of the platforming sections, especially while under attack. Speaking of combat, it can get a bit repetitive at times, and although I personally liked it I can see where some might get annoyed with the rather boring difficulty scaling. Especially towards the end where the fights actually get pretty challenging, both because they just keep throwing enemies at you, and because there isn't much of a checkpoint system for battles. Overall, as a long-time fan of the series I definitely enjoyed this game and think it's worth a try for both veterans and newcomers alike.

The spaceship dogfights were pretty good in the first games, and while I was excited to see where they took it in this game, I wasn't too disappointed to see it wasn't there. The annihilation nation challenges were much more sorely missed. I used to get so much fun out of managing my ammo well enough to beat the bosses at the end of the "endless" challenges in earlier entries, and you will not find that here. What you will find is much more engaging gameplay than earlier games, with a dodge that elevates it completely. It is now possible to survive on good timing which means positioning becomes more strategic and less "just get out of the danger zones". Weapons are solid and the leveling and raritanium systems are a nice improvement on earlier games. New game+ is excluding the harder annihilation nation challenges about what earlier entries have done with omega versions of weapons now for purchase. All in all, if you've been in the same situation as me: playing the earlier game remakes on ps3 etc. wondering if this would play as well on pc?GET THIS GAME. You will not be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I had PS2 back in day, but for some reason I never got in contact with Ratchet & Clank series. First time that I heard of this was with the 2016 soft reboot which frankly I can agree that it felt something was missing and was genuinely bad overall. When this came out first on PS5, I couldn’t care enough even though was intrigued with rift mechanics and overall visual. During my life I genuinely loved playing platformer games like Rayman, Ori, Spyro, etc. and revisited couple of ps2 era games, at the end decided to give R&C chance when I heard of PC port. Even though I never had the gameplay feeling of this franchise, I still decided to watch main recaps/scenes of previous games to familiarise with it and review this as a bridge to continuation in the future story.It’s the latest entry and the 9th main installment in the nearly 2 decades old action-adventure-platformer linear franchise, which is to this day, one of the main mascots of Playstation. Rift Apart continues the storyline from Into the Nexus, focusing on the Dimensionator and the ongoing discussions about it. Despite Clank's efforts to repair it and hand it over to Ratchet to assist in his quest to locate his species, Dr. Nefarious manages to steal it right in their presence. Subsequently, Ratchet recklessly fires at the weapon, leading to a disturbance in the space-time continuum. This results in the emergence of dimensional rifts to diverse worlds and alternate realities, where will the player be introduced with other new main and side characters, vast planets and distinct ecosystems.There are two main playable characters which are basically the same, gameplay wise. As of weapons, you unlock array of varied from shotgun, automatic rifles, bombs, laser railgun. While I liked all of these weapons, even the ones which were more similar to the other ones, I must say that outside of 5 weapons that I used most of the time, others were needless through whole game. Other than arena specific levels, the game lacked a form of challenge in the hope of you needing to mix all of them, to progress further. Only in certain situations, I had to employ clever tactics to avoid running out of ammo quickly. Along with lack of needing a bunch of weapons, bosses were repeatable with same techniques. Although neither of these aspects pose a major distraction rather a specific critique, the game still manages to provide enjoyment and a sense some kind of challenge when the difficulty is set higher. The primary highlight of this game is inclusion of rifts and the seamless transition between different areas when traversing them. Devs have executed in truly fascinating manner, and I found to be highly enjoyable despite at first thinking 'twas gimmick that would overstay it’s welcome. Conversely, there were periods through game where it felt like 'twas less utilized. Emphasizing the shooter aspect is good, on the flip side, devs seemed to neglect platforming, that used to define it. At times, the game resists your attempts to discourage and prevent you from climbing objects that are evidently meant to be climbed. It might restrict your exploration of these worlds in creative manner beyond the predetermined path you've established. In my view, the level design suits the nature of this game quite well. I love more smaller, intricately levels that offer variety of layers, which contrasts with the larger areas that can sometimes feel lacking in activity, as seen on the planet Savali. I think there's room for an open-ended world design, and would welcome a future game that strikes a balance between maintaining the expansiveness of these while infusing them with vitality and diversity.Despite not experiencing the whole writing from previous games, I think this game really hooked me up within a minut. The main highlight is the introduction of Rivet, who serves as direct counterpart to Ratchet. Liked her from the moment the game started and can be seen how the writers were heavily focusing on her story with later introduction Kit. Both of their narratives evoke a similar dynamic to the first game in franchise where R&C frequently engage in arguments and struggle to find common ground in various situation. I could genuinely envision her as potential successor to the main character, possibly leading to Ratchet's retirement. His character comes across as rather one-dimensional and unexciting throughout entire game. Truly sympathize with the writers because, after 8 main games, seems incredibly challenging to introduce anything novel for him, especially since they've explored nearly every emotion and characteristic. Aside of that, I struggle to accept that conflicts in this game couldn’t have lasted a little bit longer or have been deeper than they were. Two instances that come to mind are the conversation with the Fixer, where Clank at the end with just single statement somehow instantly convinces Fixer he can live better. The other instance, is the conflict between Rivet and Kit. Leading up to these moments, all the acts were well executed. Loved Rivet and Kit moment, as well as Ratchet and Rivet, which could have provided an opportunity to develop Ratchet's character further and perhaps offer some wisdom and advice. But, in a larger perspective, the emotions didn't come across entirely, and it didn't leave significant impact on me, especially since the characters merely exchanged apologies and expressed desire for forgiveness.From the beginning to the end was astounded by graphics and visual style. Ray tracing elements like ambient occlusion, reflections were really bringing life to this game. While the emotions didn't completely captivate me, the animation of every character I encountered was truly remarkable. None of them ever appeared dull or lacking in life; instead, their body language vividly conveyed their personalities. No complaints about the voice acting. I particularly enjoyed how, new lines of dialogue when revisiting a planet after completion.I can only applause, what kind of remarkable job have Nixxes done. They delivered a great port, which likely presented challenges due to its heavy reliance on SSD and other technologies for seamless transitions. While not an exact 1:1 match with the PS5 version, it comes remarkably close. I did encounter crashes through whole game, but the detailed saves prevented any loss of progress. No encountered bugs.An awesome game with great graphical presentation. Gameplay remains consistently engaging and avoids becoming tedious, repetitive, or bothersome. It combines excellent gunplay, challenging enemies, and some platforming elements seamlessly. Coupled with the outstanding visuals, audio, level design and character design, music, lighting, animation, art, VFX, it delivers a comprehensive and immersive gaming experience. While the story doesn't consistently hit the mark, there are instances where the humor, light-hearted dialogue, and shallow apologies can detract from genuinely emotional and serious moments. Today there seems to be a reluctance to be sincere, often masking it under layers of irony and humor, when a more straightforward approach would have been far more compelling. In spite of a few drawbacks, I thoroughly enjoyed from beginning to end, and I eagerly anticipate an upcoming sequel.Rating: 9.5 / 10I wholeheartedly recommend this game to newcomers who haven't experienced the previous titles in this franchise. Don't be misled by its cartoonish appearance; it's not exclusively for children but rather suitable for others. To core fans from the PS2 era, I encourage you to give it a chance and not to dismiss it simply because it incorporates some updated design, gameplay and new character compared to 16 years ago version.

_childDocuments_.review: Partway through newgame+ now and can more accurately review the state of the game:First of all the game itself is great, loads of mostly polished fun with impressive visuals (if your PC runs it smoothly) It's not long but not exactly short, took me around 25~ hours to finish my first playthrough but that includes a few hours of graphics troubleshooting as well as replaying several hours worth of the game after getting stuck on a mission that glitched.My biggest complaint is while it's visually stunning it feels really poorly optimized at parts. A few examples, some of the planets ran smoother than others on my laptop with a 1050ti. Parts actually ran pretty well while others lagged and bugged out both visually and even the audio at times became unintelligible, some planets I noticed lag spikes when looking in certain directions as it seems like many of the visual FX are constantly running even when not visible. A few maps have waterfalls and for whatever reason walking under them caused massive lag spikes. There's a lot of graphics options at least but no render distance, this laptop runs some games surprisingly well like Borderlands 3 and Doom Eternal at high settings in 4k while this game ran pretty rough even at the lowest settings which feels like a console optimization issue.The crashing was annoying on release but sounds like it was at least partially a windows 11 issue and IME it got better within a few days though I still had occasional crashes. The autosave works well at least but towards the end of the game the save became stuck on a glitched mission and after reloading a ton I gave up and went back to my last manual save which was 2~ planets back and had to rush back through several hours worth of the game. Which is weird as it sounds like the console version has multiple autosaves instead of overwriting the same one all game. It's worth manually saving occasionally just in case as otherwise you might have to restart from the beginning.While the gameplay feels very polished overall a few things stick out as missing compared to the older games. There are little to no gadgets, the hover boots and phantom dash are fun but unlock early and don't change much, the puzzles are all pretty basic though with some fun parts and can be skipped at least. There's no racetrack despite having slugs you race around several maps, the arena only has 3 tiers and feels very basic compared to previous games. The armor system is interesting and the rifts are fun to complete but a few more armor/melee upgrades would have been nice. And while there are a solid amount of weapons they have a lot of overlap IMO and lack some of the more unique weapons from older games, though newgame+ does add at least 2 more weapons and more upgrades it would be nice to see more customization in future games.Overall it's just nice to see Ratchet And Clank on PC after 21~ years of being console exclusive, it would be amazing to see the older games ported or even remastered and I hope if they release the next one on PC it gets more optimization and is made more with computers in mind from the start as this definitely feels like a "next gen" console game that they decided to release on PC's later.

_childDocuments_.review: Rat Chit and Clank as always been kind of underwhelming. Many of the PS2 games were made in a year and it shows, the PS3 games were either too short or absolute trash and the PS4 game was a decent shooter whose story suffered from being a movie tie in. Rift Appart has none of these issues. It's a lenghty, well developped, well written and honestly kind of charming video game.It might be the best entry in the franchise. It's the first one I played long enough to see trough the end, at the very least, and it wasn't because of making a review. I just casually played it. Like a person.My fursona is a spermophile. Big parade in metro city otropolis. You are being awarded the biggest most important ever person award for being so awesome when suddenly, da lil robot goes, heres a magic interdimensional space gun I built in my spare time. Use it to go get laid, you useless virgin.But then some character from a previous entry in the franchise comes out of nowhere  and snatches himself away to a universe where he aint a little ♥♥♥♥♥♥.So you go after him, you fight stuff, shoot stuff, buy guns, have sexual desires towards a cartoon. The usual stuff. My biggest issue is how droning the gameplay can get. You're not very vulnerable and many weapons can single hit enemies. So, outside of bosses, it lacks a bit of challenge, and given that 95% of the gameplay consists of combat, it can make the game feel a bit more boring than it could be.Variety is kind of an issue. I'm fine with a game being mostly combat, but there's no juggling or strategy to it. You can just point shoot and dodge every thing with every gun. They do try to bring in different ennemies and constant upgrades to weapons and stuff. And certain weapons are better for certain situations. So, it's technically competent. But, I dont know, something about the pacing of this game felt like swimming trough gruel. I dont know how else to explain it.Visually, the game is pretty stunning, it's true pixar level stuff. From the beautiful fur drenched with sweat from her delicious armpit to the amazing level of detail put into every inch of the environment. The levels are varied and while some of them do boil down to a swamp with some platforms, there is enough beautiful vistas to stare at to overlook some of the less stellar work.So, yeah, overall I give Rift appart a solid 92 out of 114. It's a game for kids of all ages. Nothing special, but a solid experience that left me satisfied.

_childDocuments_.review: As a die hard fan of the original games on PS2 and PS3, I went into this game with nostalgia glasses on expecting to be disappointed. However to my surprise, this game blew me away. Rift Apart is hands down one of the best RaC games ever made. A prime example of how a modern day sequel to a long running franchise should be. First of all, the game is absolutely gorgeous to look at. Especially with max ray tracing and HDR, this is easily one of the best looking games I've ever seen in my life. The gameplay is as smooth as ever and easy to pick up as all RaC games should be. Combat feels good, and there is some new in-game mechanics added to the game to give the player more movement and ability to dodge attacks. Another thing Insomniac absolutely nailed was the cutscenes. They are all visually stunning and the characters feel very real with the help of phenomenal voice acting. Lots of humor in the game as well which was very nice to see as it felt like a tribute to the originals. Lastly, the guns are the best they have ever been in RaC, Rift Aparts weapons are so much fun to use and make you feel godly. Especially on NG+ when you get the Omega versions of each. I also just wanted to comment on the direct storage thing. I did notice a small difference on my SATA then on my NVMe, but not too much. But this game for sure could not be ran on a hard drive.List of negatives:-Game is a little short-Quite a few reused bosses and re-skins of enemies-Battle arena (which is usually the best part of any RaC game) was very disappointing. It isn't very challenging at all and the boss fights were reused from the main story missions.-Game is pretty demanding, I didn't have any issues personally but for someone with a mid range-low range PC I can see how this game could give you troubles.Overall a 9/10, I highly recommend to anyone who has never played a RaC to pick it up.Also can we get all the games ported over now? Thanks.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best Ratchet and Clank games in my opinion  I played almost all of them since the first one on the ps2.  Its not a perfect game, but it has lots of fun guns, good replay-ability, and a good story that respects other games in the series.    The PC version is not as good as the PS5 version, but its still a fantastic way to play if you dont have a PS5.  Everything is basically just as smooth and optimized really well, despite my PC not having a solid state drive.  The only real issues I faced were 3 occasional bugs.   Audio would sometimes cut out/ become distorted, but restarting the game fixes it.  Sometimes my weapons would not aim/ fire properly when using the hover boots and going back.   Switching weapons fixes this, but its the most common bug.  Lastly, when upgrading a weapon, sometimes my mouse would not be able to select a few nodes, but you can use the arrow keys and the enter button to make it work.Despite those issues, this game was a lot of fun to replay.  Other than the fun ps5 features and the bugs from the port, it almost feels like the game was made for the PC.  9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished my second run on new game plus, and I originally played this on the PS5. So I'm gonna talk as if I have some sort of authorityTL;DR: Good gameplay, little enemy/boss variety, story is alright if a bit bare bones, Overall a good experience.I'd recommend getting this on a saleThis is a port, and there are are some problems with it. I've heard the horror stories, but the most I've personally experienced was a freeze or crash at most once every play session.I'd recommend using a controller, and if you have access to one, use a PS5 controller. Half of the interactivity with the weapons is a part of the controller and its reactive triggers.Beyond all of the port stuff, here's some criticism of the actual game I've had since playing it originally:The entire point of the dimentionator being destroyed in Into The Nexus (The previous game) was to stop it being used because it was unstable and dangerous. Clank fixing it for Ratchet to find the lombax dimension is stupid.I feel like they could have given Clank some dialogue to fix this, something like "I'm sorry ratchet, I was overcome with Curious selfishness to explore the dimensions." Just some sort of Justification of his stupidity would've been nice.Also, when a piece of media explores something like dimensional counterparts, you'd expect some sort of interaction between some counterparts, maybe explore the characters by making them different in some way but still having the same sort of motivation.The only real example we got of that was with Captains Qwark and Quantum, Captain Quantum lacks confidence and is pretty cowardly, he interacts with Qwark off screen and apparently rehearses a speech, and Qwark acts as a good friend and is supportive of him.There was no interaction between Clank and Kit, supposed dimensional counterparts and main characters, the most they get is laughing together at a no dialogue interaction.Also, there is very little enemy variety, there is around 6 unique boss fights with the difference being either setting, visual design, or the amount of enemies you have to face around them.One thing I have to say that is good about the game; The gameplay is good, I don't think there are many strafe shooters out there nowadays and I'd say it's genuinely pretty fun, especially the mechanic of different weapons having levels, It gives you a good reason to try new gameplay styles and I enjoy that.

_childDocuments_.review: A long time ago, in another lifetime (I'm old), I worked on (tested) a game called Ratchet & Clank: Up Your Arsenal (ho ho ho). It was one of the few games I had to test (play) every day that I went back to and played after release.  It was fun and genuinely funny, with a engaging story, likeable characters, interesting level design and a compelling game-play loop of using weapons repeatedly in order to level them up.And that is pretty much my review of Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart.  Fundamentally not much has changed in twenty (yikes!) years, though understandably the voice actors now sound older.  Graphically, its totally stunning, with beautiful and detailed environments, especially with ray tracing ramped all the way up.  At times its like watching a big budget animated feature.  The dimension hopping mechanic is very cool but perhaps slightly underused.  And despite the semi-open world there feels like very little grind and busywork meaning you can beat the game in under twenty hours.

_childDocuments_.review: At last the 15th installment of Ratchet & Clank. I played the game to completion and PC port does have some Bugs (Please Insomniac give update to fix) The game is a new fun advancement of the Series as the 9th installment of the R&C Future line of games. The new worlds Update designs of old enemies and more Inter-dimensional Hijinks.I do notice some of that Polish The R&C normally have with the games writing is missing some oomph in there dedication to the jokes. The game with weapons is still fun and with addition of Running mechanic even if we have Hover Boot is still good. and the Phantom step is great addition to the gameplay. The story is pretty solid with minor holes that bothered me. There also was possibility expand Rivet the new character universe more but that is why we will have see what the 16th game will unfold. The music and voice acting great yes even if Armin Shimerman pulls back on his voice work as Dr. Nefarious. I fine with him not over working his voice. I cant Imaging how rough it is on his Voice. There a bunch good easter eggs to the past games as well as to other nods to Sony's other First part game franchises. the only disappointment i feel is This is the first Ratchet & Clank to leave out the Insomniac Museum from the mainline. I always felt joy exploring looking around the Museum and all the work that was put into the game from weapon concepts, character designs to world designs. I know the prior Ratchet & Clank (reboot) did kinda down tone the Museum as a Garage which did work but had a minor bitter taste how it was design, yet i still enjoyed it. This is a great game for the fans of the Franchise to enjoy that still has Strong quality control in place and for new players of the franchise you will enjoy a fun destructive playthrough coming at a planet and so ya start BLASTIN'!Have Fun Space Cadets!and don't forget to bring a spare charger for your Crotchitizer! You'll need it.

_childDocuments_.review: Great entertaining story driven game. Story wise it is a very linear story with optional exploration. This game is not super long or bogged down with a ton of side quests (Being a parent gamer, this is a definite bonus for me, as I do not have a lot of free time to get to game as much as I would like so being able to finish the game & experience the whole story without extended breaks and forgetting what was happening in the story was a huge plus for me.). There are some collectibles (approximately 6-10 per map) but most will be acquired without any additional exploration as you proceed through the maps. This game is graphically beautiful, even more so when HDR is enabled (which I typically don't do for games).

_childDocuments_.review: Makes it's much welcome debut to PC, choosing an excellent title to start with.  is easily the best entry in the franchise since  in 2009, and while it's newer extra family-friendly is unfortunately here to stay since it's redirection in 2007, that doesn't hinder the amazing and fun franchise that it is. Featuring absolutely insane graphical fidelity, fluid and fast gameplay that's been perfected over the years, and a wide arsenal of new but familiar weaponry with incredibly creative twists and features; it's no wonder Sony chose this title to show off what the PS5 was capable of, and how that could be elevated with PCs. Making this a great title for fans new and old to jump in to.Definitely a title I can recommend to anyone interested in a faster paced 3rd person shooter/platformer with hints of exploration and nothing but sheer fun-factor on offer. With genius concepts of creativity utilizing a whole alternate dimension that you can swap to seamlessly, though I will say they definitely could've leaned into the potential of such a prospect a bit more, nonetheless not taking away from how cool the concept is. Great gameplay, visuals, soundtrack, characters and voice acting (albeit you can tell the voice actors are, well, getting to be seasoned veterans). Nothing but great things on offer here.A franchise I hold dearly for getting me into the world of gaming back in 2005.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite a few hiccups in the port to PC resulting in some stability and performance issues at launch, I had a truly wonderful time revisiting the universe of Ratchet & Clank. This is a brand of gameplay I can easily slip into and always find it immensely enjoyable.The series' trademark sense of humor is on full display here and never feels like it's overstaying its welcome, and yet Rift Apart also has a way of tugging at the heart in a way the previous games were never able to really accomplish. Credit has to be given to Debra Wilson (voice of Kit) and Jennifer Hale (voice of Rivet) for their outstanding work here.The weapon variety (another series staple) is outstanding... in previous games, there was always one or two weapons I'd completely ignore (looking at you, Tools of Destruction Tornado Launcher), but that didn't happen here. While some of them were effectively overlaps in terms of their mechanics (such as the Pixelizer being functionally another shotgun) I enjoyed leveling all of them up to max.This also has to be one of the best looking games I've ever played... benefitted greatly by its cartoony artstyle. The Pixar comparisons have been made with this series since its PS3 days, but this is getting incredibly close to cinematic quality. There are a few visual flaws apparent in the PC version (some really bad looking water reflections, for instance, with some graphical settings), once you get the settings dialed in the game is stunningly beautiful and well animated.I was also pleased to see the return of the series' battle arenas (one of my favorite parts of previous games), however I do wish these were a bit more fleshed out. I could spend hours on end making my way through progressively more difficult challenges in the arenas of previous R&C entries, but they seemed to be over in the blink of an eye here... with the only reason to revisit them being to level up weapons. Zurkon Jr's announcement lines during these do make them quite entertaining however.As someone who has not (and probably will not) bought a PS5, the wait for this game to come to PC was well worth it. Some kinks to be ironed out, for sure, but I for one am just glad to have Ratchet back! Now if we could only get the rest of the series ported over...

_childDocuments_.review: Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart is one of the best games I've had the pleasure to experience.In this game you play as Ratchet, a member of a fictional species called the lombax, and are tasked with retrieving a portal gun-like device called The Dimensionator from Dr. Nefarious, aswell as with rescuing your partner-in-uncrime, Clank, who you lost due to dimensional mishaps.Along the way you meet another lombax named Rivet, and she becomes the second playable character and helps you on your adventure. You may have seen her online a ton, internetians went crazy when she was first revealed, and for good reason! She's adorable! >ᴗ<The game sees you traverse multiple planets collecting various items ranging from small bolts and raritium (used as a currency in the weapon shop) to more important collectibles such as golden bolts and spybots. There is also a variety of collectible costumes that you can dress Ratchet and Rivet up in, and a plethora of weapons that you can equip that all have their own mechanics, advantages, and drawbacks.Mechanically, this game nails it. Running around feels great, swinging feels great, zooming around with your rocket shoes is amazing. Defeating enemies is very satisfying, and the bosses are really fun.Visually, this is among the best looking games I've ever played, if not *the* best looking one. Turn those settings up and you'll feel just like you're there. A very handy "frame generation" option allows for your FPS to skyrocket even on older hardware (I played on a computer with an RTX 2080 card on high graphics and stayed around 100 FPS, dipped into the 70 FPS range when there was a lot going on). It's clear they put a lot of work and love into the world building and design, as well as the writing. The story of this game is very enjoyable and genuinely had me extend my sessions just so I could see what was next.The only thing I wish this game had more of was some more difficult platforming challenges. It doesn't even get "medium" difficulty by the very end, with the movement being as nice as it is, I really wish it was utilized to its fullest.My run, which was going for 100% completion, took around 17 hours over the course of three days. Yeah, I was hooked. I say "was" going for 100%, as I encountered a bug which is apparently extremely easy to run into. One of the spybots I collected (there are only 10 in the whole game) disappeared from the total count. This left me unable to purchase the last weapon and has prevented my save file from truly reaching 100%. Oh well, a small bump in the road that won't make me love the game any less, all the more reason to play it again and get all the achievements!Overall, Rift Apart has been immensely enjoyable, and if you like 3D platformers, collectathons, or casual shooters, I definitely recommend giving this game a look. And if you like it, wishlist it. You never know when someone might surprise you!

Port - We still have to remember that this Game is a Port of a Console which if you look back in Time and at Games such as Saints Row 2 (as an example) which has been ported from the Xbox to PC (and PS3) with poor FPS and Stutters to the follow if your Hardware is not to specifically emulate an Xbox.Crashing - Crashes only did happen at Game close with Alt+F4 or me tabbing out due to Dual Screen Setup.FPS/Stutters - The Games FPS for my overall experience seemed to be alright and about 75FPS (my which suited my Monitors RefreshRate), however i´ve noticed a pattern with specific Worlds in the Game which use more Decals, Visual Effects and Rain/Light effects which pulled the FPS down to around 40/45 but never into the Unplayable.The overall Gameplay was fluid and didnt have any stutters for me.Hardware/Setup - I´ve been Playing the Game using a PlayStation 4 Controller with an Sony Wireless Adapter.Running it of my Current PC which is an AMD Ryzen 5600G (6C12T 3.9-4.4GHz) CPU + AMD RX 6600 XT (8GB VRAM) GPU + 32GB DDR4 3200MHz RAM + My current System Drive which is a Samsung 980 Evo Plus 250GB SSD and Windows 10 Installed.The Systems GPU isn't ideal for the Games High Settings Preset so i had to tweak it to be a hybrid between High and Recommended for best Performance.However whenever i've been looking at some of those Negative Reviews most of these Players are not Sharing their Hardware Specs which might did help determin if maybe the hardware is off the charts for even being able to play this Game.I did wish Steam would use the System Information under Help (when they do the next suvery for that) for being able to Display at least MoBo, CPU, GPU, RAM and Maybe SSD/HDD Info on Reviews automatically in like a Drop down or Player uses this Hardware Configuration.EDIT: AMD RayTracing - I´ve seen some Negativ Reviews regarding AMD and RayTracing not working, however if those People would have actually taken a look at the release Notes they did notice that it was stated that its being worked on and not available at Launch for AMD Users.Final Thoughts - I think the Port was done Quiet well, i like the Ratchet & Clank Games and think that porting this Game over was a Good idea since Nixxies (even if i think that some people might have something against them or Sony with their Reviews) did a really good Job for what it is, after all in the End this is a Port to a whole nother System and that we should be thanking them for.After all this could be way worse... if any of you even do remember the Deadlock/Gladiator Port at all to the PS3 with screwed up Facial Animations and Poor FPS in Combat.(or the other ones which only bad Facial Animations)Rating: Graphics -  9/10 Looks as it Should (since its different for everyone and i´ve spotted a few things here and there.)Controls -  9/10 Feels good (sadly i felt like the Cam on the PS4 Control did rotate a good tad slow)Gameplay -  9/10 Quiet Alright FPS      -  7/10 Room to Improve on it ( Due to the Few Dips on Specific Worlds with Power consuming effecs)Story    - 10/10 Loved itCrashes  -  8/10 Little to Non at All

_childDocuments_.review: Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart" is a stunning game with breathtaking graphics and engaging gameplay. It is a genuine technological achievement, especially considering the implementation of ray tracing and the level of detail.However, it's worth mentioning that the game is quite demanding in terms of hardware. Based on recent benchmarks, older NVIDIA graphics cards such as the GTX 1080 may struggle with high settings, particularly given they don't support ray tracing. Furthermore, graphics cards with 8GB of VRAM, like the RTX 3070 or even the new RTX 4060, might be insufficient for this game. In this context, the NVIDIA RTX 3060 with 12GB of VRAM might be a more preferable option.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best recent games I've played. Combat manages to feel like you're absolutely destroying everything with ease while actually providing a challenge. The multiverse aspect is integrated into the plot well, with counterpart characters and locations appearing frequently and the ability to swap between realities in some situations.My one big gripe with this game is that, despite being "Verified" for the Steam Deck, the Deck struggles with it even at low settings. Most of the game comes in at 25-30 FPS, but there are frequent drops and audio stuttering during combat, and one of the worlds even tanks it to barely 15 FPS whenever you're there. Lowering the resolution alongside the graphics settings doesn't help much and just makes on-screen text hard to read. That said, I still enjoyed it on the Deck because it's still a very good game and is still at least playable.Makes me want to give the rest of the R&C series a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: First time playing this franchise as this is the first official available game outside of PlayStation ecosystem. I loved it. _childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of Ratchet & Clank since childhood, having played the series 1-4 back on the PS2. I haven't had a chance to play since then and figured I would never be able to play again unless I acquire a PlayStation. I was very excited to see that the latest game of Ratchet & Clank was being ported to PC and was keen on playing it. A couple of hours into it and I'm enjoying it a lot. This is not to say that I had a couple of issues. The first hour was stuttering a bit, with FPS fluctuating up and down. I figured this is due to shaders compiling because it started to stabilize the more I played. I only had 2-3 crashes,  which is to be expected as I read some reviews about it. I'm fortunate enough to be able to launch and play it, unlike some folks who are having issues. My specs are Ryzen 5950X + RX 7900 XTX. I play @ 3440  x 1440p (widescreen). Max settings with FSR 2.1 @ quality, ray-tracing cannot be enabled on AMD card, so it looks like Nvidia wins this time.  I've noticed that the game hangs and freezes sometimes, which left me dumbfounded as I have 2 Sabrent Rocket 4 Plus in Raid 0 (double the speed/ combined capacity), pushing a satisfactory 11.5 GigaBYTES per second. More than enough as this game is expecting Gen 4 M.2 NVME which maxes out around 7 gigabytes per second. This is in line with what PS5 has as their storage unit. Turns out this game uses Microsoft's DirectStorage, which incorporates GPU compression to load textures on the fly, requiring fast storage. Again this is only possible with Nvidia GPU's, so another win for them. This explains why cut scenes hang for me sometime. Overall the game is quite playable and a lot of fun, it is rather a demanding title that chokes your PC, especially in the VRAM department as I saw 14 GB being used of my available 24.

_childDocuments_.review: Out of the box performance is impressive for the fidelity/ performance you get (considering previous launches). At this point you should know the game and what to expect. The game hitches a fair amount, but I suspect it to be more of a cpu bottle neck i9- 10850k. Smoothing the microstutters out would give it a 10/10. Still very playable and enjoyable. As far as ports go, this is very good for a day 1 launch! good ♥♥♥♥! (SSD - Samsung SSD 970 EVO plus 1TB) m.2 so, im no problems with loading worlds or dimension stutter, something to consider in this game)

_childDocuments_.review: Short but sweet is the simplest way to describe this game. It’s got an above average story, paired with pretty fun combat and amazing graphics. Unfortunately, it’s pretty quick to play through, a full completion coming to around 15 hours, and not really much longer in challenge mode to grind bolts for Omega weapons if you want to do that (because of bolt multipliers combined with gold bolt no. 23). - : The true highlight of the game. While it’s not anything on the level of hyper-realism, the effects used are so incredibly thought out. The character models are highly detailed and every world has their own thematic architecture, and not to mention all the rifts. The use of them is perfectly seamless and so stunning.- : While it’s not the best story, arguably the short length of it allows for it to still be pretty decent. All plot points don’t take longer than they need to and each have their own clear objectives to keep things moving. While on the other side, the short length doesn’t give each individual character besides the main four their time to shine. - : While on the surface the combat is all the same - endlessly shooting guns, when you actually play it you see the differences in each type and weapon and how they affect how you play around the enemies. Even besides some of the more basic guns you’ve got minions, bombs, lasers, even a shield, and that’s not to mention the upgrade every weapon gets once you level it to 5. - : As mentioned several times before, the game to completion is pretty short, which on its own is one thing, but what makes this so interesting is how to get 100% achievements, you can very easily spend only 10 hours. Almost none of the collectibles need to be all found, most of them only need around a third of their total amounts. Besides that, the majority of the achievements are achieved from the story or will likely be obtained during it. - : Pretty standard difficulty settings of PlayStation games, increasing aggressiveness, damage, and health, as well as having the no death mode. - : While the collectibles are few in number, except for one planet, the majority of the maps are largely linear, with most of the collectibles being found on ‘that one small offshoot from the path’. While it’s definitely nice to see something so casual, I wish there was a bit more substance to them.- : Now as the big one, there is no way they are asking for a reasonable price for this game. While the quality is good, there’s no real reason that the base price should be 4-6x the expected time you’ll get from the game. Even when it goes on sale, it hasn’t even dipped to half off yet, which is a bit ridiculous for a year-old PC port of a game that’s already three years old total.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, to clarify: the last games I played, let alone finished, from this series were during the transition from the PS2 to the PS3, so needless to say, I'm pretty rusty, so imagine my surprise when I learned of a game being ported to Steam.Originally I had hoped that Insomniac and Sony would've started PC porting by way of starting with the earlier games, relieving computer gamers who loved the classics of the need to find ROM's for Playstation emulators. Having finished the main story last night, however, I'm content with this alternative, given its deep story relative to the PS2 era. While I won't give spoilers for this review, I will say even some older enemies that debuted from those days turn out to have some depth to them.Now that several patches have been applied since launch day, my only criticism of any significance has mainly to do with compatibility and performance: as primarily a Mac user, I had no choice for now but to cloud game due to DirectX12 requirements, and even there, performance sometimes did falter with enough action and AI going around, which will happen a lot toward the end of the game.Still, figured I'd contribute my two cents and say that overall, this is a good PC port of what once was a PS5 exclusive, and hopefully it's just the beginning of that much.

_childDocuments_.review: I gotta say as much as I enjoyed this game, it still has problems, although most of them don't have a ton to do with gameplay. Gameplay wise this is one of the better Ratchet and Clank games. If you just want to have the best third person shooter experience of your life, buy this. Otherwise, I have several gripes that I will detail in later paragraphs. There will probably be spoilers, so read at your own risk. Also, my ideas are not organized, I'm just writing them down as I think of them. A lot of it will be negative, but I do have some pretty positive things to say as well towards the end, they mostly have to do with gameplay lol. But still, don't anything I say as me hating the game. I just love it and want it to be better.My problem with the game mostly has to do with the characters and story. It has a great idea, with Dr Nefarious transporting everyone to a universe where he always wins, but it's wasted on the writing and character design of modern RaC games. For whatever reason Ratchet is no longer the hot headed renegade he was in the original games, even though he mellowed out as time went on, it's still nothing compared to the bland garbage that he is now. And Clank is somehow even worse; he never opens his mouth unless if it's to say he loves ratchet, apologize to someone, state the most obvious fact known to the player at any given moment, or ask a question about said fact with an answer so obvious you want to stab a fork in your eye to relieve the pain. Honestly, I don't know how you can mess up this badly. If it ain't broke, don't fix it. But I guess they thought that instead of a badass hero we wanted a ♥♥♥♥♥ and instead of an intellectual genius we wanted a dumbass.A big problem with the way ratchet and clank currently are now that I think of it comes from the fact that this is a rebooted series. I remember first playing and during the intro, clank told ratchet he's his closest friend and wanted to give him the dimensionator as a gift to find his family as a token of his appreciation, i was nearly in tears. When I saw it again in NG+ I felt absolutely nothing, because I had realized that this just isn't the same series I grew up playing. Ratchet and clank don't grow together and form an inseparable bond like they do in the original trilogy, in the 2016 reboot, they're practically best friends as soon as they meet each other, whereas in the original games, they actually hated each other for most of the first game, insulting each other and fighting and bickering after nearly every mission. By the end they had learned to put their differences aside and were able to work together to achieve the impossible, forming an unbreakable bond that would last a lifetime. They had actual real character development. It's not just "lol i love you bro because both of our names are in the title of the game"As for Rivet and Kit, they're kinda just boring. Rivet is kinda cool, but at the end of the day doesn't really have any personality traits that truly stand out or make her meaningfully different than ratchet, and as for Kit, I really liked her initially, and she has an adorable design, but the more I saw of her the more bored and disappointed I became. I just think both of these characters had potential that got wasted. To be honest, it's mostly a symptom of the rebooted series just being a neutered version of the old PS2 games, back when characters were actually characters.Another big gripe I have is with the main villain, Emperor Nefarious. It's kind of ridiculous how at every possible turn you take the dude is always right there to stop you in your tracks, conveniently after you just finished completing your mission so he can steal everything you just worked for. This happens multiple times and it really gets old. He could easily just kill ratchet and rivet where they stand at any given moment but instead he spares them every single time, and eventually just gets his ass kicked. It's like this guy actually seemed like an intimidating enemy until he actually showed up in the game, and from then on it became impossible to see him as anything more spooky than Dr Nefarious himself, just a big old tom cat for jerry mouse to clobber the ♥♥♥♥ out of. And it's funny when it happens to Dr Nefarious, he's just a clown getting hit by the proverbial slapstick, but for Emperor Nefarious to be set up as this unbeatable competent villain who always stomps out Rivet's resistance, he does not deliver at all.Now I don't want everything I say about the game to be negative, after all I do recommend it, So I'm going to end it on positive feedback.First of all, I love all the side content. Outside of the arena challenges, the side quests on every planet you visit feel a lot like helping those random people who need it in spyro 2 and 3. W side quests, no complaints here, they absolutely nailed it.Whoever designed the new charge boots needs a raise. By far my favorite mobility option in any Ratchet and Clank game.I think overall, they nailed the weapons. Other than the bombadier and pixelizer, every single weapon is either fun to use, has absolutely stunning visuals, makes me happier every time I use it, or any combination of those. Probably the most balanced weapons of any Ratchet and Clank game too, there are a few outliers but most of them feel very fair and reasonable or the super powerful ones have a small enough amount of ammo to keep them from being a one trick solution to every fight, you have to actually swap to different weapons and use everything you buy.One thing that I also find interesting is the attention to detail and visual design of this game, but don't take my word for it. I think dunkey's video on it does a good job of explaining how wonderfully crafted the details and environments are.Overall, 8/10; the good gameplay really does come through. It could honestly be as high as a 9/10 if you never played the ps2 games.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of the series since the beginning, this latest entry carries the same charm and fun as the rest of them.Your arsenal of weapons in this game are plentiful and very well rounded, I didn't find myself disliking one weapon over the other once I upgraded them all. Of course there is a bit of a grind to get the resources to fully upgrade everything but by no means is it a requirement if you don't mind a bit of an added challenge.The platforming & puzzles carry that classic Ratchet & Clank feel while not being stale, I did find one or two puzzles that racked my brain a little more than the others, but for the most part its friendly for both beginners and veterans like myself. Exploration is, again, on par with the previous titles, offering a bit more freedom out of mapped perimeters. I am one who enjoys testing the boundaries of maps and as I expected, there were very few ways to get yourself stuck in polygons/environment requiring a checkpoint restart. The enemies and boss fights do get a bit recycled towards the end but with a few visual changes that (in my opinion) still keep the game fun and relatively fresh.This title played great on my Deck, with only a few frame drops in some of the busier cinematics and playable areas. Aside from very rare and very brief character t-poses when skipping cinematics, there were no game breaking issues I ran into.Overall, I was just as pleased with this game as I have been with all the others after a solid 26 hours to get all the achievements. I absolutely plan on replaying this one just as I have with the other entries in the series.Throw this one on your wishlist or grab it now, either way it's a fantastic addition to your library!

_childDocuments_.review: Ratchet and Clank: Rift Apart is a really beautiful third person shooter created by Insomniac. Originally created as an exclusive for the PS5, it has now been brought to PC.The premise of the game is that the titular Clank has built a weapon/item called the Dimensionator, by which Ratchet, the last Lombax – the other titular protagonist – can go and find the other Lombaxes, who fled from his dimension to other dimensions.Dr. Nefarious – Ratchet and Clank’s perennial foe – shows up to steal the Dimensionator, resulting in the duo (plus Nefarious himself) being catapulted into an alternate universe, ruled by EMPEROR Nefarious, a more competent and charismatic alternate universe version of Dr. Nefarious who has conquered the galaxy and who wins every time (unlike Dr. Nefarious, who loses every time).Cue the entrance of Rivet, a female Lombax and this universe’s version of Ratchet, a plucky freedom fighter who always loses. She has a mechanical arm because she lost hers in a previous battle that she lost, and she has no robot buddy.Ratchet and Clank get separated, and Clank ends up with Rivet while Ratchet ends up running into a robot buddy of his own from this dimension – Kit – who he quickly has adapt Clank’s role (and position on his back).The game, thus, alternates between playing as Ratchet and Kit and Rivet and Clank as they try to save this dimension – and every dimension – from Emperor Nefarious, who is causing reality to break down by abusing the power of the Dimensionator.The game itself is a third person shooter. The central appeal of its third person shooter gameplay is the huge variety of weapons – there’s 18 different weapons in the game, plus two new game plus exclusive weapons. These allow you to prosecute combat in a wide variety of ways, from shooting people with a simple pistol, to stunning enemies by turning them into living topiary, to opening up portals to dump huge objects on the heads of enemies. Some of these weapons are pretty standard, but most of them are at least a little wacky, and many are more than a little bit offbeat.As you go through the game and use the weapons, you level them up, allowing you to unlock more upgrade slots on them, which give the weapons permanent upgrades. Ratchet and Rivet share experience, and indeed, everything else – despite the alternate universe shenanigans, the two of them are EXACTLY the same gameplay wise, which is a missed opportunity. The guns are upgraded via drops you find in the environment and by beating bosses, and you can get other sorts of upgrades by finding collectibles.Unfortunately, while the game is full of a good variety of nice to look at environments, the core gameplay itself gets kind of stale as it goes on.Ratchet and Clank alternates between third person platforming sections, and third person shooting sections.The problem is that the core shooting gameplay is kind of bad – the good weapons are so overpowered that once you get a few of the better ones, the combat becomes increasingly trivialized. No enemies – not even bosses – can seriously threaten you, and indeed, it is possible to stun-lock bosses to death using the stun abilities and alternating between those and shooting them.While it is nice that you can use all the cool toys on the bosses – it would be rather lame if you couldn’t – the game doesn’t really figure out a solution to this, and as you approach the end of the game, the game relies more and more heavily on throwing swarms of enemies in you, turning the levels into little more than a series of third person shooter arenas where you just slaughter waves of enemies with your powerful weapons and mass stun effects.But even the third person platforming stuff often isn’t really very good. It’s certainly no Super Mario Odyssey – most of the third person platforming in the game is very easy, with only a very small amount of challenging platforming content. And as the game goes on, there is less and less of it, with an ever increasing focus on the third person shooter arenas.There are some other random sort of “minigames”, like riding around on the back of a flying dragon who shoots fireballs and riding around on a fast bug (oddly, both on the same level), but they don’t last very long and it would be bad if they were longer because they basically do everything that those mechanics can do in the time you spend with them.The end result of it is that, while the game is very short, if it was any longer, it would outstay its welcome, and honestly, the end of the game ends up having you go back to previous planets to fight a bunch of arena combats, which feels like they ran out of time to make planets but still wanted to keep up the Ratchet/Rivet alternation.One other oddity – while the game’s trailer loves to feature you falling through rifts, you actually only visit three dimensions throughout the game, and 90% of the game happens in just one dimension.The core plot is very simplistic. The voice acting is good, and Rivet, Kit, and Clank were okay characters, but the NPCs are pretty one-note and the main cast is pretty much like two or three notes at best. Ratchet himself is a pretty bland character, sadly, and his central conflict over whether or not to find the other Lombaxes is not executed in a very interesting way (and is pretty much resolved without much feeling of accomplishment in resolving it). I was a little surprised there’s no romance, even though the alternate universe versions are gender-swapped. All in all, the game feels like it had its edges sanded off, and while the game is inoffensive, for all the zaniness that the plot would seem to indicate, it honestly never grabbed me all that much – it was entirely too predictable what Kit’s relationship with Rivet was going to be, and the game never really sold me on any sort of feeling of tension.This might all sound down on the game, but honestly, I liked it overall. It is short and well paced – my 34+ hour time is due to me leaving the game open at times; the actual play time is probably closer to 15-20 hours to 100% it, assuming you explore everything and go everywhere and grind all your weapons up to the maximum level. There’s less than a dozen levels in the game, and they take an hour or two to beat each, so you’re not looking at an inordinate amount of playtime. This makes the game pretty snappy, and you’re always getting thrust into new situations without lingering anywhere too long, a lesson some other games need to learn.That being said, this is not Sony’s answer to Super Mario Odyssey – this is an okay game, but in the end, it’s not anything near a must-play, and it is very much a “kid’s game” in many ways.

_childDocuments_.review: This title is bittersweet and ill explain why. I love it because it's a Ratchet and Clank title and I've wanted one for ages. It's not often i pay full price for a title but for this i did because i was so excited for it. Ratchet and Clank is one of my favorite titles. one that brings back the good ole day's. I hold these close to my heart but i cannot fully stand behind this title. first i will start with what i liked and then move on to what i didn't.-Overall fun gameplay some levels more than other's.-Challenge mode after story.-Selectable difficulties.-Cameo's of the old characters.-Good mechanics.-Great gun play-Varied enough to not feel super repetitive. There was only a couple point's in the game where i felt as though it was starting to feel a little repetitious. But it did not last.-Customization though more limited than i like is an awesome feature for your weapon's and armor.-Enemy dialogue is downright funny in spots.  Some things i did not like and could not stand-Still pretty buggy in spots. Menu's often times will have left over artifacts from another screen that glitch through my character. This is particularly annoying in the armor menu. I've been stuck in wall's. Had the game crash only once at the end. My weapons will switch on their own or sometimes it will say i'm using the weapon i want to be using in the weapon wheel but a different one entirely is out and can get stuck like this for a minute breaking the fun you're having in combat.-Certain things like the speetles get very repetitive. IMO this is something that should have been used in one world and more creative thought should have been put into other worlds for unique transportation.-Some weapons feel useless especially on harder difficulties and i feel as though there should have been a bigger and better weapon selection.-A big gripe i had with this game is that instead of Ratchet and Clank sometimes it felt more like Rivet and Kitt. I don't mind playing as them once in a while but i'm here for Ratchet and Clank. -Another thing i hated and this is a bit of a spoiler so you were warned. It felt to me that i fought the boss got the gun (or accomplished and objective) and had it taken from me way to many times. This was so repetitive i questioned if i should keep playing. Literally over and over i thought it would never end. -Story was ok nothing to write home about. certain part's were cool but few and far between. -My last gripe is this game is too short and not varied enough. I beat it and 100% the game and all achievements in a little over 17 hrs. For $60 this should not be the case so ha got me i guess. Final thoughts:I really wish this game had the originality of the first one. Lot's of different enemies and scenario's it's 2023. I love this title but time to step your game up. It feels lack luster to have gone so long without a RnC game and then this is what is delivered. Why can't we have all this game had to offer plus the originality of the first game plus all the gun's from the past with new additions the ability to fly in space and customize your ship as in the old titles But even better and on a larger scale. Hell make it open world and open space. We have the technology so step up your game. I hope that this has shown you we have interest in these titles and to continue making them. Man id love to have all the original games remastered with all the Jack and Daxter's remastered and a new entry for Jack and Daxter. If you have read this far down it is worth a buy probably wait for it to go on sale though.

_childDocuments_.review: Ratchet & Clank Rift Apart is everything you expect out of a Ratchet & Clank game and nothing more. That's not a bad thing, though, as it has all the wonderful, well-written dialog, colorful characters, excellent platforming and level design, and top-notch wacky weapon design and gun play as the originals. The new Phantom Dash mechanic helps to speed up the gameplay a bit over prior entries, but doesn't change the formula all that much if you're used to the prior games in the series. As a port, it's excellent - as is tradition with Nixxes PC ports. There are a few kinks to work out, like some RT AO issues on water and the like, but it's overall well optimized and loads quickly. I haven't experienced any crashes. Running on my rig, I can max the game out completely (including all RT at max) with no upscale techniques (like DLSS) and hit a solid 4K/60. I understand that my PC is not a typical usage case, so the recommendation would be to start the game on medium settings with with a frame-rate target you have in mind, then adjust your settings and DLSS options accordingly to hit your desired performance. There are a litany of options, and the typical Nixxes start up screen helps to detail your settings before jumping into the game proper - which is always nice. Worth $60 bucks? If you have the game on PS5, I can't recommend at full price. If you haven't played it, though, and your PC is more powerful than a PS5, you'll for sure get your money's worth. If your PC is marginally better or on par (ish) with a PS5, you can pick up the game used at at a shop for much cheaper and get an great experience. The graphical bells and whistles, added RT options, etc. all make this a compelling purchase for PC users who don't have access to a PS5 or for PS5 owners with a decent rig to see this game all but surpass or be on par with just about any fluffy CG animated film of the last decade. It's all very impressive visually, and the game is an absolute blast. Basically, play it any way you can if you're looking for some fun gun-play without all the seriousness in most modern AAA titles.

_childDocuments_.review: very charming game, imagine your hamster going on a sci-fi adventure.looks great, runs great, no complaints. highly recommended.some people have reported crashing issues persisting after the patches, but I had no such issues. game ran fine for me on windows and linux, with a ryzen 3600x and radeon 6800xt. no crashes in 5.5 hours of gameplay. (Also, game just takes 38GB storage, not 75 as indicated by steam)slight complaints: 1) no option to cap fps! there are options to enable/disable vsync and change the refresh rate in exclusive fullscreen, but neither option locks the framerate. not a big issue though. 2) the game maintains fps very well, no matter the settings, which is weird. with my setup at very high settings (no RT) at 2560x1440, the fps barely deviates from 60, at either very low or very high settings (so perfectly playable either way). upscaling methods do wonders though, i recommend insomniacs custom AA instead of FSR, it gives slightly better performance. at high quality, this mode improves fps from 60 to 70-90 range. 3) I am running the game off of a SATA ssd, and my setup does not support direct storage even though the game does. during the dimensional transitions, you do notice that the game is waiting for data to be transferred for a second or two (literally 1-2 seconds). not a major issue, but noticeable.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of the Ratchet & Clank series since the original trilogy on PS2, which I consider some of the solid platformers out there. Rift Apart, a PS5 launch title, is my first next-gen experience and even without 4K, its still a stunning looking game. The story is a mixed bag. It felt slow mid-game but picked up towards the ened. The focus on the duo characters over our classic duo was clear. Rivet, the female Ratchet from an alternate universe is a great addition, but her gameplay feels too similar to Ratchet. She is wielding a hammer, while heavier and slower than Ratchet's wrench, doesn't significantly change the overall experience. Combat is where Rift Apart excels, maintaining the signature shooting-platforming style while updating and improving it. I loved the Topiary Sprinkler and Lightning Rod among other weapons which also adds a punch depending on your playstyle. The new hover boots add a fast paced element, letting you skip minor enemies quickly. While Rift Apart is a solid game, it doesn't quite match the storytelling and platforming magic of the original trilogy. It took me about 16 hours to complete the main story and 95% of the side quests and challenges. Overall, it is a good game that shines in combat but falls short in story and bits of innovation compared to its predecessors. Buy it on sale and if you're a fan of platformers and the series.

_childDocuments_.review: RAC is BACK! RAC fans rejoice, this is the port you've been looking for. Flawlessly executed!This is the most worthwhile $60 I might have ever spent. This game is positively majestic, smooth, story-rich and so much fun to play. I started playing RAC in 2002 with the original and it's been my favorite series since. I've owned all of the games up until the 2016 PS4 release (minus the mobile games), and I was beyond excited to see this released on PC. If you're a nostalgic or super familiar with the franchise, you're going to love this. It's an ode to the classics with many many references to previous games throughout (like... all of the games), but with modernized mechanics and probably the best graphics I've seen to date.If you're new or less familiar with the franchise, I recommend watching The Golden Bolt's spoiler-free review on YT if you want a deep dive. But I think those new to the franchise will probably find this approachable. There's a lot of new characters and a lot of new story here. You're going to miss a lot of references, but if you enjoy things like exploration, alien worlds, blends of combat and platforming, and brilliant mechanics to blend it all together, you're going to have a really good time playing this.Oh, and you're going to want to use a controller.

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up playing the Ratchet and Clank games on PS2. I really enjoyed the PS3 future series as a departure from the classic PS2 era of Ratchet and Clank; they're both good in their own way.The PS4 reboot had me scared a little, as it was the first Ratchet and Clank game I did not fully enjoy.However, this game is an affectionate love letter to every moment from the past games; many of the maps are cleverly redesigned stages from previous games, with little nods and winks in nooks and crannies previous games held collectables or secrets. Don't get it twisted, though, this game is innovative and well-made and can absolutely stand on its own right without an appeal to nostalgia - if this was a players first introduction to Ratchet and Clank, I'm sure they'd enjoy it all the same, even if some of the story beats fell a bit flat, due to a lack of perspective on the previous games.The core gameplay is satisfying; gunplay, melee, smashing loads of crates and the platforming roots of the series are still here. Many new interesting minigames and elements have been added as well. None hog too much of the run-time which keeps every new element novel and interesting, and if you truly hate a new addition, the pause menu has a helpful "skip puzzle" option. Personally, even when a puzzle didn't feel particularly engaging for me, I never skipped because the character dialogue is interesting enough for me to want to stick it out, and most of the puzzles are strong enough to motivate you to complete them without any reward in mind.The story is actually very heartwarming and intriguing. Although the dialogue can feel a little hammy for the first half, this stops feeling the case towards the midpoint. Stellar performances from all of the voice talent. Insomniac really gives enough time for the new characters to be developed and feel naturally involved, and the new motivations and development for longstanding characters from the series feel seamless.Visually, this game is beautiful; I've not been sold on the character design of Ratchet since the future series began (because he looked so different, imo) but this game finally made the design pop for me. Every level is rich and beautiful, with a scenic shot of the planet before you land, and a nice panning angle of the opening area of each new planet showcasing the stunningly gorgeous landscape of where ever you've just found yourself.Additionally, the animations are phenomenal. Certain scenes would fall flat were it not for the amazing facial animations and body language of the characters portraying complex emotions.Ultimately, I'm extremely surprised. This feels very identical to my childhood experiences of buying a new ratchet game, and excitedly playing through it for the first time. I'm at the midway point and I'm truly in love with everything I've experienced so far!I hope the entire series gets a re-release on the PC.

_childDocuments_.review: It's another ratchet and clank game except on PC (yaay) so if you aver played on the playstation you know what to expect.If the game does not have acceptable performance in the first 40 minutes of gameplay, the entire thing is going to run poorly. In other words, if you can't tweak the game to run nicely by the time the title card comes up, it is going to run poorly the entire time. I have a 5600x and a RTX 3060 Ti with 8gb vram and it was around 30 fps in intense areas. In extreme cases it went down to 20 (such as on Torren IV looking into the entire junk city). Someone else with a similar setup was sitting at 60 most the time. So your mileage will vary. Oh also I originally tried playing this with a 1070 Ti and it failed miserably. In fact most modern games I have been playing can't seem to be handled by the 1070 Ti anymore. Just a heads up.The story its self is good. Not a mind twister but it's fun and the humor is pretty slapstick. Buying and upgrading is fun, the combat was fairly satisfying, and the game looked great even on Low settings which I had to use. 60 dollars for 13+ hours I think is pretty alright. I didn't even bother to do collectathon gameplay, just the story plus a couple side quests.

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointing Experience with Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart on PCI'm afraid I have to give Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart a thumbs down for several compelling reasons, with the most significant one being the presence of memory leaks. It's baffling to witness a game of this magnitude from Sony suffering from such a fundamental issue. One might attribute this unfortunate flaw to the game being made for the PlayStation 5, which undoubtedly placed limitations on its PC adaptation. Initially, the game appears to run smoothly, but the longer you play, the more it unravels into a nightmare of lag, frame drops, and various other problems. To make matters worse, the game feels like a relic from a decade ago.While it gives the illusion of open-world segments, it's deceiving, as invisible walls plague the experience. These barriers consistently obstruct your exploration, and even when it seems like you could land safely below, invisible death drops await. As someone who has played every Ratchet and Clank title to date, I had high hopes that this game would push boundaries like God of War did. However, those hopes were quickly dashed. This game could easily pass for a PS2 title, offering little more than a fresh coat of paint.There's nothing truly special about this game, and its PC optimization is, to put it mildly, awful. It's not just poorly optimized; it's a technical disaster. The voices frequently cut out, and you'll miss essential dialogues if you venture a step too far. It's frustrating because the game often encourages you to stand still and listen to engaging conversations. Why can't we move and listen at the same time?The combat is enjoyable, but only for the first hour, as it quickly succumbs to lag. To make matters worse, the memory leak persists even after you close the game, sometimes necessitating a full computer restart. This is far from the smooth and polished PC experience players expect.Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart on PC falls short of its potential at every turn. It has moments of promise, but it ultimately falters and disappoints. It's as if the developers deliberately tease you, hoping you'll invest in their subpar PS5 just to enjoy the game properly. This sort of behavior from Sony is frustrating, to say the least.
