_childDocuments_.review: 6 hours in as of writing and I can recommend the game so far. Tech side: very little stuttering (only a few traversal stutters), no crashes, a HUGE amount of settings to tweak (which you can set before the game starts!), and 60+ FPS with a mix of ~high settings and DLSS quality, with some dips during heavy combat. My aging 9700K and 2070S system can even pull off raytraced reflections on high, although generally sub-60 when they pop up, and very high if I were cool with low 40s (1440p). Sacrificing quality DLSS for performance or targeted framerates could probably fix that, but even without raytracing the game is quite beautiful. It'll definitely be a nice benchmark to return to when you build that next future-proof system and want something to crank all the settings on. Nixxes gets credit again for a high quality port, as far as I'm concerned.Gameplay wise it's good 'ol R&C, just how I liked it. Honestly it would be incredible to someday get remakes/remasters for Going Commando and Up Your Arsenal in the vein of the first game's reimagining, with releases on Steam for the first trio at least.Edit - Temporarily dropping this review down to not recommended due to the broken direct storage implementation that's causing massive FPS drops in 8-10 gig VRAM cards and high-very high textures. I'm confident Nixxes will fix it, and I will adjust my review accordingly if they do.

_childDocuments_.review: Having a blast playing this game. The portal jumping is very good and the range of weapons and upgrades is quite good. Combat dynamics is very enjoyable and there is a skill level to choose for everyone. The storytelling is very good too.There are a few glitches, some a little distracting (and it was crashing until I disabled NVIDIA reflex), but overall for me performance is very good - I play on "very high" preset with very high RT reflections and other RT settings on medium, and use DRS + DLSS at 90 fps, and the graphics quality is excellent - really does feel properly next gen. Apart from a couple of cut scenes where performance tanked, it has stuck almost perfectly to 90 fps. FG + RT and unlocked framerate got very high fps, but I found it a little less stable that way.Played on 13700K + DDR5-6000 + very fast gen4 SSD (7,000 MB/s read) + 4070 ti at 1440p. Obviously for 1440p, this is perfect and can brute force its way through most performance issues.To max out 1440p you will likely need a 12 GB+ GPU to avoid excessive stuttering. _childDocuments_.review: Definitely a solid Ratchet and Clank game.  But in my opinion, not one of the best.  Perhaps I'm over this series now, or maybe this series is getting stale, but this wasn't quite as fun as it used to be.  I was a huge fan of the series on the PS2, and Going Commando is still my favorite entry in the entire series.  Maybe it's unfair, but I compare every single Ratchet and Clank game to Going Commando.  That was the most perfect game in the series in my opinion.  Plenty of different and varying worlds, lots of puzzles! and very interesting weapon selection.  Not to mention, way more activities to keep the game fresh.  Rift Apart was great, I just felt like it focused more on being a beautiful game than a good one. It felt very repetitive at some point, and there wasn't enough to really mix up the activities you do throughout the story. Also, I kind of miss how imaginative the weapons used to be. A lot of the weapons now just feel like a copy + paste of something from an old one.  I know there's only so much you can do to make new weapons, but part of what I liked about the older entries in the series is that the game didn't seem to take itself too seriously.  Almost as if they had way more fun coming up with implementations for the game. Another thing I miss is the old humor of the old games.  The games had humor that tried to go for an older audience, and now, Ratchet and Clank games seem to be more kid-friendly.  Again, this is still a solid game, but if there's a sequel, I hope they try to go back to the old days of the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Ratchet & Clank is always fun. The older games are clearly better, as it feels like the more modern they get, the shallower and simpler they become. They now feel almost like a demo of a game - you just get to dip your toe into each of the systems, never really fully engaging with any of them. New abilities are just thrown at you with no fanfare, and then you only need them 3 times, and it never asks you to combine them in new ways. Everything feels underwhelming and tossed aside shortly after being introduced. That's almost the theme of the game - they even have Ratchet meeting a fellow Lombax for the first time ever, the thing he has been focused on since game 1, and it's pretty much just "hi, let's go do the next thing." The series has been casualized, just as neutered as their formerly innuendo-laden titles. But it's still fun to play, it's just lacking the magic it used to have.

_childDocuments_.review: For reference, I've endlessly replayed the original trilogy, endless-ish-ly replayed Gladiator/Deadlocked, and had one or two playthroughs of A Crack In Time and the PS4 reimagining (the former because I borrowed a PS4, so no replays, and the former for a reason I'll establish later on in this review). I also like to write, so bear with me.In short, not only is Rift Apart incredibly heartening to behold on Steam, for technical performance and the Halo/God of War-esque unprecedented tearing down of the Forbidden Wall that prevents many games from being multi-platform, but it is damn spectacular, in every sense of the word. You should absolutely play this game (as long as you respect the minimum recommended specs, I couldn't play the game without upgrading from my less than a decade-old computer), if for no other reason than I  you to, so we get Sony to release their necrotic, senseless grip on the rest of the series to loosen and for the ports to flow.The core gameplay seems as refined as Insomniac seems capable of, in a good way; the guns are as ridiculous and powerful as always, and the changed takes on (what I believe to be) standard categories of weapon are interesting, like the visually and functionally distinct version of the Groovitron. I have some personal gripes about platforming in the more recent Ratchet and Clank entries, mainly how reined in the gliding, double-jump and more specific movement tech has become, but Rift Apart manages to provide a surprising amount of variety to movement that I'm less disappointed at the continued trend of Stunted Movement this time around.The tech for this game is phenomenal, in that way that makes you double-take and want to stare at it to try and unravel the net of mesmerising knots in front of you. The rifts are the obvious first point, especially in more dynamic circumstances or structured sequences; I haven't tried it on my hard drive, but I don't care to, because this is witchcraft and I'm going to tie a rock to my computer to test if the sorcery makes it float regardless.I've poked and prodded at what the portals will and won't allow, but so far I've only found one or two restrictions that make sense. Otherwise, you might as well consider them Portal(tm) portals, and I have nothing but respect for the devs responsible for this stuff in particular, as well as an immense curiosity to see a CD PROJEKT RED-esque presentation on how it all works.Please make one of those. Please.More subtle is... everything else. Take the introductory grind rail segment; the destruction going on around you, the movement, the seamlessness of going from moment to moment, not including the framing that is more standard with seamless transitions in games nowadays, all of what goes on demonstrates a lot of care and detail that is arguably not present in previous games (perhaps in Into The Nexus, I haven't played that one yet but I desperately want to now). It's gorgeously handled, and performance doesn't seem fazed by Insomniac's efforts. Again, sorcery, get in the medieval contraption.It's no surprise that in terms of style, and rendering quality, that this game is a looker. There's some amount of critique I could probably make about clarity, but I think that's in nitpick territory, and is potentially a bonus if you think about it as exploration challenge (like, the glowing Gold Bolts don't stand out as an omniscient marker by being the only glowing thing on there? This is a stretch, but stretching is good for you, so there). Otherwise, environment and world design, character designs, props, weapons, effects and all those good bits of basil leaves on this tasty pizza are incredibly solid, with a tender chew and aromatic compliment to the saucy gameplay base.I'm writing about the rifts again; sometimes, you go through several rifts in sequence, and by extension go through several  in sequence. With a different game, you could observe and assume that a sequence like this is limited by smaller set pieces, such as a familiar looking room where you conveniently can't see out of the windows because nothing is out there, for performance reasons.If they're doing this, they put so much detail into these "smaller" set pieces as to reach the point of absurdity, and are basically John Silver flexing at everyone for how technologically jacked they are. If they're , and they're loading in other planets whilst you're not looking, and activating unique props or environments as they load in, and it's just working without being incredibly obvious and performance-harassing, once more, they've been Granted Eyes and can see traces on the motherboard that uncorrupted beings do not comprehend and use them to make this happen, at the behest of creatures that will ultimately subsume us all.The story and characterisation is a little bit more than alright.This sounds like this is the weak point of the game, but it's only the weak link because it's an iron chain link on a chain made primarily of synthesised super-materials. I don't dislike the milder, less joke-dense style of the more recent entries, but it does mean that the amount memorable quotes and non-gameplay events is rather sparse. I think they've done a reasonable job, however, of providing other appeal points; I do like how the recurring Collectable Hunt for Fun and Profit is justified as helping an animal that's a bit hungry, for example. It's also not like the game is devoid of humour, that would just be misinformation on my part, and Insomniac have competent writers at worst, so don't think that the story is like pulling teeth or something like that.The keyboard and mouse integration is as you would hope for, meaning "like any other shooter" and not "like an emulator's best efforts of simulating the right amount of analogue stick inputs to roughly approximate mouse movement". This is incredibly positive for this modern iteration of Ratchet Gunplay, as you're able to fully utilise your movement options without compromising your accuracy beyond having a pre-existing skill issue. The presence of accessibility options is also pleasant, even though I won't use them myself.The one issue I've had with this game as an unintended problem rather than a design difference I >:| at, is that wall jumping will be triggered regardless of movement. This makes being a bit more careful about wall jumping trickier, because you can't stand against the wall without losing height on your initial wall jump position, and it makes complex movement limited, because it will stick you to a surface that wouldn't have been an issue with earlier entries. That's a super nitpicky nitpick, but I'm noting it because I initially thought it might have been a form of platforming assist accessibility option, which would have made more sense to me than "it just works like that now". Even the witches of Insomniac misjudge the height of a step and have a stomach lurch from time to time, I suppose.I can't tell if this is a bit 'memberberries on my part, but the repeated use of old designs and tools is a lot of fun. It's nice to see certain enemies with simplistic designs in their original games, but rendered with ray-traced detail. Shot in 4K, perhaps. I also like the shared detailing present in the customisation options, which are both comprehensive and amusing in fairly strong measure. Stuff like palette swaps for your wrench and hammer, the ability to give Ratchet a fish instead of a wrench, the legally distinct versions of items like a keysword, and hexagonal gemstone money.Overall, this is an immensely enjoyable game, and more than worth at least one try to see if it clicks with you. If not for specific, self-imposed context, I'd be either in or well on my way to a NG+ playthrough of Rift Apart, a game that genuinely does stand apart in a stacked games industry.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR for fans of the series, this game is not worth the time nor the high price tag; working but semi-questionable port for a game that feels like a Ratchet game for people who have never actually played Ratchet gamesWith all the talk about Rift Apart's PC port, I figured I would give it a go and ramble about it as a long-time Ratchet fan (PS2 through PS3 barring Into the Nexus). So might as well start with the technical quality of the port.Running a 3070TI, Ryzen 9 5950X, 32 GB ram, and a Crucial MX500 SATA SSD (560 Mbps), I ran the game easily enough at 1080p with a mix of high and medium settings (leaving bloom, etc. on, no raytracing) for 60 FPS throughout. The only times I ever encountered frame drops was when using the Burst/Blast Pistol and the Enforcer/Executor, which seems to be really common amongst users (some pointing it out to be a Windows issue, but I'm unsure on that). There were two total times I crashed: once crashing to desktop when quitting to the main menu, and another time as a hard lock crash when spamming a mix of Cold Front and RYNO rounds, on a later visit to Sargasso. Ultimately to me the port runs fine from an "it works" perspective. There were numerous smaller bugs I encountered playing the game (mostly audio, the audio triggers in this game SUCK), which I don't know if are related to the port or the actual final product, but it mostly works. I can't speak for higher end users who are trying to crank this game up to 4k with all the bells and whistles, as it seems like those features can cause issues (between crashing and not looking ideal). Nixxes is still patching things up as we speak, so things may continue to improve with more time. Buyer beware in this regard, and do your research on hardware specs for this game (there are several videos on Youtube to compare for this).However, even if you do get this game running with optimal settings, is it really worth the time investment?I'm going to say no. While the game still looks incredible even when on lower settings, stuff like the gameplay, writing, and the pacing of it all don't add up for a good experience.Gameplay itself is a wash. Playing on Renegade Legend (hardest) for basically all of my game time, the "challenge" presented feels not so much challenging as it is cheap. This game has a LOT of weaponry designed to distract or weaken + freeze up enemies, which in turn usually makes them not even a threat. And when you're not using those weapons, you will eventually get hit by a stray bullet or melee enemy from behind you because of two things: Phantom Dash and the camera. The combat is mostly balanced around you having the Phantom Dash, which is an i-frame dash new to the series. So enemies will now lead shots as you're strafing, which more or less demands you change strafe direction and/or to use Phantom Dash as liberally as possible. And to top that off, the camera is now zoomed in behind your character at all times in combat for this game. Most combat encounters are wide open spaces where enemies have a lot of room to hide and shoot you. So while you're focused in on a small part of the fight, something off screen is liable to hit you for free and it ends being incredibly frustrating. Which is where you use stuff like the Topiary Sprinkler and Cold Snap stop enemies completely and shoot with everything else you have on hand. Not very fun either way.As for the writing, I understand that the game was rewritten at some point in development, but it still doesn't feel cohesive enough for a 20+ year old series. For one, it's like Ratchet and Clank have both forgotten most of what's happened prior to this game, e.g. Ratchet acting like Rivet is the first other Lombax he's ever met (she's not). Anything that pertains to previous games is basically treated like a memberberry with no actual consequence (Ratchet 1 enemies reused all over, characters from old games returning for just brief moments during the intro just so they can have alternate dimension counterparts, etc.). I didn't mind Rivet and Kit, though even their own development doesn't seem complete with how the game flies by. Dr. Nefarious is back but only as mostly a coward for the sake of Emperor Nefarious existing now. I could probably go on, but all these small things just add up and it's quite annoying.Probably the best part of the game are the graphics and the setpieces out of context. If you don't pay attention to anything else but those things, you will probably love this game, which is why I feel this game is designed for people who have never played Ratchet. It somehow hasn't refined its gameplay enough for the better, and continues to double down on modern Sony-isms of characters talking too much and having graphical setpieces that do nothing for meaningful gameplay. So for anyone that actually cared about the series at any point, ignore this game. Otherwise wait for a sale if you're deathly curious.

_childDocuments_.review: Exceptional game.Has the Playstation 2 era fun & difficulty mixed together with ultra HD graphics. Plus the technical feat of traversing through different worlds instantaneously (via rifts) makes this game extremely satisfying.I only have two issues. First the worlds you travel to have minor design flaws (floating grass & square terrain) but this is quite rare/not that annoying and will hopefully be fixed. My second issue is the boundaries, which prevent the player from going to areas (only encountered on the swamp planet as of writing this). The walls preventing me from exploring areas are intensely frustrating as I don't want to miss any collectables, but also do not exist for areas which I should definitely not be in, which causes soft locks that are difficult to escape from but not impossible (if you die you re spawn in that same area you're trapped in).I know my complaints seem longer than the good things I've said about the game, but honestly the whole experience is flawless, which makes the minor issues stand out a lot more.Edit: nominated for Sit Back and Relax award 2023

Strongly recommend.EDIT #3: Near the end of them game now, constant crashing.EDIT #2: Weapons are getting better, having your own army of bots is pretty fun.CPU: Ryzen 5800x, Intel 12700kGPU: Radeon 6800XT 16GB, Radeon 7900XTX 24GBRunning the game on 2 computers.On my main gaming desktop with the 12700k and 7900XTX, game ran flawlessly.However, on my 6800XT computer, I would get constant crashes at game start.On startup, game tells me to update my drivers to the latest, running 7.2 which came out yesterday.There's nothing newer.Game crashes on startup, with message that game uses more memory than available.GPU-Z shows only 8GB of GPU and system ram being used.The Devs responded to a thread on the discussion forum, that this is caused by Windows' Page File being manually set too low.I found this strange as I had never changed this setting but sure enough, it was manually set to 8GB.Set it to Auto, and restarted the computer. _childDocuments_.review: I've seen some really bad ports this year (Jedi Survivor!!), this game is not one of them. Played it over 6 hours today without a break. No crashes, no shader compilation shuttering, no bugs so far. I read other reviews and people complained that the game would crash every 5 minutes or that they can't get high fps on a 4090. That's not the case in my experience. I also played on a 4090, everything maxed out with rt and output res is 4k on a display with vrr, dlss setting: quality and like i said no problems. The fps is always above 60, sometimes 120, often around 80. I'm sure i could get locked 120fps if i'd lower the dlss2 setiings or turn on the dlss3 framegenerator. The game itself is great. The only complaint i have is that i think it would have made more sense to release the Ratchet and Clank 2016 game first because it was a reboot of the franchise and Rift Apart is the sequel. The 2016 game is also very good in my opinion and gameplay is nearly identical. Edit: locked 120fps with no frame drops is possible when framegenerator is turned on (all other settings still same as before). Noticed a bug with shadow reflections on the lakes which appear when the camera stands still but not when the camera is moving

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous game, running well as expected, albeit on top-end hardware (13900k, 4090, 64GB DDR5, SSD). _childDocuments_.review: 3 hrs in and i can say this game is just phenomenal! as a 20 year fan of the R&C franchise, i have to say this may well be one their best of the newer games yet.i don't want to spoil too much, but lets just say that a lot of old faces come to greet us fresh with face-lifts, the platforming feels fluid and dynamic, the gun-play is fun and honestly i feel like a lot of choices the developers made in this port was really well done! my first game sequence i got to explore my cosmetic armour options and was excited to see one of my favourite games of the series had an armour in this one, (you can play in deadlocked armour) alongside other old and new stuff. that's a nice touch all on its own!i wasn't sure at first about some of the control choices, even the sensitivity seemed a lil high at first, but then i found myself instantly immersed, and the controls and mouse movement just made sense and felt very natural to me.some of the mechanics are so fluid platforming wise that it literally felt like i was watching a cut scene on occasion while moving (i checked and died just to make sure i wasn't experiencing one of those play along moments), but i was pleasantly surprised that in fact no, wall jumping and bolt cranks really just do feel that clean and fluid!moving between combat and platforming and utilising everything you have in dodging enemy fire is very rewarding, i uped the difficulty to give myself a challenge and while a little tricky (died a few times to bosses) it felt amazing to learn and counter/dodge and weave through enemies as i destroy them with one of the many and still more to unlock weapons in my arsenal!they seem to have leaned heavily on past good things, such as Raritanium upgrades, levelling up weapons isn't completely clear at first what it does, but seems to enable you to add more Raritanium upgrades. there's secret collectables to find (gold bolts, potential secret weapon, cosmetics etc), and i have to say, controls wise; on mouse and keyboard this game plays really well, like the controls are insanely intuitive, which was something i wasn't sure about before purchase tbh!i am hooked and as a long time fan this game is everything I've wanted in a Ratchet and Clank title for the longest time.personally i feel their last greatest title beyond deadlocked was a crack in time, and i have to say, the first few levels feel just as wonderful and then some.there seems to be parts of tool of destruction here with level design, weapons from both TOD and crack in time, the weapon previews aren't really anything to write home about, not quite the same amount of sass as other games in the series previously, but i can live with it!my only gripe is that you cant seem to fire weapons while gliding/using some of the in combat platforming abilities which i find a little annoying, but nothing major.I'm running higher end hardware admittedly but this game runs exceptionally well on high on my 3090i locked frames to 60 ofc cut-scenes are 30 which was a little jarring at first, i noticed no dips in frames but i did notice maybe some tearing, even with v-sync.i have owned every Sony console except for the PS5 and i have to say i think if anything it looks better on pc (ive not played this title on PS5 so don't take my word for it)this game looks and feels fantastic, i did get one crash 3 hours in just after defeating a boss, but it auto-saved and was easy enough to get back in again.this game feels amazing so far and honestly was well worth the wait. i never thought i would be able to play my fave series again but for my first PlayStation on PC title this was a fantastic show of what i can hopefully expect with their other titles too!

_childDocuments_.review: I played through and finished Ratched and Clank: Rift Apart on PC. I enjoyed it quite a lot, being a long-time fan of the series. The gunplay and movement are awesome as expected, the variety of weapons and silly gadgets is great and the whole game flows nicely from setpiece to setpiece. The side-quests aren't overbearing and quite fun as well, so even causally, I finished the game with 98% completion rate. The voice acting and cut scenes also were really great!On a technical level, the port is solid. There is Ray-Tracing in the game, but even with rasterized lighting, the game looks super good, so the biggest difference is the screen-space reflections - and even then, with my RTX 3060Ti, I eventually turned them off in favour of solid frame rates. Generally, the game looks great and plays very nicely. I also played it a bit on the Steam Deck, where it can hit around 40 fps with medium details, which is great if you limit the Steam Deck's screen refresh to 40Hz as well. On the slight negatives, the game really is quite linear in it's design and approach. Coming from the incredible freedom of Tears of the Kingdom, the levels feel very restricted and like the game goes out of it's way to not allow you to explore in some parts. And while the story was great, the humor definitely wasn't the strongest in the series and took a backseat to the galaxy-threatening bad guy plot. Having two playable characters in Ratched and Rivet was fun, but unfortunately the two play exactly the same on a gameplay perspective, even sharing a pool for unlocked gadgets and weapons, so it feels a bit gimmicky to even have this option. It works for the story, just not that much for the gameplay.Would overall recommend it however - it's a solid bit of fun that doesn't overstay it's welcome and instead delivers very nice non-stop action.

name: Wylde Flowers
detailed_description: Play as Tara (she/her), who has just moved to a cute rural island to help out her grandma and the family farm. Get to know a memorable cast of fully voiced characters with intriguing backstories — find friendship or even romance! Relax into your rural lifestyle as you tend crops, care for animals, fish, craft, and more throughout the day. By night, nurture your inner witch as you learn to fly your broomstick, brew potions, control the weather and seasons or even transform into a cat! Fairhaven awaits you. 🌸 A WITCHY TALE Savor an earnest and emotional story that blends farming with magic and personal discovery as Tara finds herself, and brings a town together. 🌸 FULLY VOICE ACTED DIALOGUE IN ENGLISH The characters in Wylde Flowers are brought to life with a cast including BAFTA award winning voice actors in over 18 hours of voice acting. ㅤ ㅤ 🌸 30 DIVERSE CHARACTERS From Natalia (she/her) the local Blacksmith, to Sophia (she/her) who runs the diner, each character in Fairhaven has an intricate backstory waiting for you to love and fall in love with. 🌸 SWEET ROMANCE Seven folks of Fairhaven are eligible to be wooed and romanced. From the local butcher Kim (they/them), to Amira (she/her), a flirty doctor. 🌸 FARMING & MAGIC Develop both domestic and magical crafts through cooking, fishing, farming, animal care, magical spells and potions. 🌸 LOTS TO ENJOY Explore and relax through 35-60+ hours of immersive gameplay. 🌸 BESPOKE SOUNDTRACK The music is closely entwined with the narrative and features a music score created with the help of a real orchestra, that responds to your choices. ㅤ

_childDocuments_.review: I can't praise this game enough! The characters are all so diverse and well written, the dialogue never feels stale or forced to me, and it's easy to immerse yourself in the game. Sure, there are alot of farming games out there, but the witchy aspect really stands out and truly makes the game feel different from the rest. There's always something to do, and it's so easy to lose yourself in the game, even if you're like me and can't focus for too long. If you like games like Stardew, but want something that's a little more story heavy, definitely give Wylde Flowers a try!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the absolute ideal of a cozy game. Let me just start with saying: everything that annoys you in other cozy games has been solved in this one. You don’t have to stress over small inventory, run to the chests all the time, worrying about endless grind or skipping the boring dialogues. This game hits the spot, it is challenging enough for you to get invested but it just isn’t annoying. The storyline is very well thought through. It is WAY different from other popular farm games, it will get you engaged and shock you just when you’ll start thinking you’re getting a hang of it. I really appreciate that the storyline doesn’t have any loopholes or stupid explanations.It’s also just extremely fun! Only one game, but it will give you a new fun mechanics every time you might be getting bored. You start out just exploring the town and renovating the farm. Then you’re about to play with magic and discover the features it unlocks (don’t get discouraged by your slow walking speed, trust me). And avoiding the spoilers, when you’re nearing the end game and have it pretty well figured out, you’ll have the option to make your own outfits, which kept me occupied for when I didn’t have any ongoing quests.This game is . I cannot stress that enough, since I am so over developers releasing games that are “in progress” which makes you feel like there is no clear direction. This game has amazing lore, which when you finish it, will leave you with the feeling of sentiment you get after finishing a good book.  But don’t worry, the game doesn’t end after the base storyline! You still have some quests to do and mysteries to solve.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: Wylde Flowers is a delightful witchy farming sim that makes you wish you could live on this idyllic island too. There's a surprising amount of care that went into this game, from the colorful cast of characters to the cutesy aesthetics to the magic and world-building, and it made for an immersive experience. I especially loved the diversity in this game; seeing so many cultures and identities represented made me feel like this really was a wholesome place, and I feel I got to learn things from the characters about real-world traditions. The voice acting was also superb. It was a bit disappointing, or anxiety-inducing, that this game, while advertised as cozy, had so many missable achievements. At a one hundred hour playthrough, I would have resented having to replay the whole thing for a single missed recipe. I did really love this game, but I'd be wary of tackling it without a guide if you're an achievement hunter like me.

Then, once the world opened up to me a little more, I actually ended up having a ton of fun with resource management and crafting for about 20 hours.  Unfortunately, I swung back around to being bored in the last quarter of the game, which really overstayed its welcome and dragged on forever.  The plot was interesting and the characters are okay, but there just isn't enough interesting gameplay to sustain its 30-45 hour runtime.  Overall, it's not a bad farming game and I did have some fun with it, but there are better on the market.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game originally on Apple Arcade, not expecting much. But after being introduced to Tara and the other characters of Fairhaven, it was the first time since  that a game narrative and gameplay progression gripped my attention like this; ultimately putting 54 hours into the mobile version before jumping to the PC Version. As more developers push to create more Wholesome/Cozy games,  has now become my platonic ideal of what I would want to see out of this fledgling genre of video games, not because it has the most in depth systems or the most polished experience, but because it narrative and gameplay so effectively communicates the struggles that occur when living in the communities that so many of these Wholesome/Cozy games strive to depict. Without going into story specifics, if you go into this game expecting this to be a piece of digestible wish fulfillment, you are going to be surprised by the depth and nuance that can be found in each character and their stuggles. Hats off to the narrative designers Desiree Cifre, Elizabeth Ballou, Jhenne Tyler, Nyasha Bryant; because you have made something pretty special that I hope more developers take inspiration from.Link to the full analysis of the game:

_childDocuments_.review: Tara discovers that she and her grandmother are witches and she’s quickly initiated into the coven of Fairhaven. She simultaneously learns farming and witchcraft, as mysterious things happen and the normie townspeople begin to grow suspicious.     • The game autosaves throughout gameplay. No manual save.    • When Tara runs out of energy, nothing bad happens, she just can’t take any more actions until she rests or consumes food or a potion to restore energy.    • The player has until 2 AM to get Tara to bed. If not, at 2 AM, Tara is teleported to bed, the next day progresses, and she wakes up with half of her energy restored at 11:30 AM.     • Seasons change when the player chooses for them to (via story explanation).     • Gameplay entails: farming, animal caretaking, fishing, foraging, woodcutting, mining, cooking, several types of crafting, NPC affection increasing, and fulfilling requests. No combat.    • There are seven romance/marriage candidates: 2 women, 4 men, and 1 non-binary character. Divorce is possible. No children.     • No character customization. However, Tara’s clothes can be changed later in the game.    • Fast travel via magic broom is unlocked about half way through the game’s story. The map isn’t really that big though, so it’s more for convenience than a necessary game mechanic.     • No product quality tiers, but there are variations of products. For example, after obtaining magic animals, they produce magical variations of milk, eggs, and wool.     • Controller worked perfectly for the entire game. Mouse/keyboard was never needed.    • There are 14 different languages available for the game, which is a lot for an indie game.     • Tara adopts the stray cat that wanders around town once her affection is raised by one heart.     • There’s a story quest involving possessing one’s familiar, which is the cat, so Tara gets to run around as the cute kitty, then gets the spell to do so for her own needs, so the player can do it again later for funsies. It’s so f*cking cute to run around as a cat!  cute.     • Farm animals are absolutely adorable! I love their animations too. So f*cking cute! The chickens and ducks move so accurately to real life. The ducks also get to swim in the pond.    • One of type of crafting is clothing and there are a lot of designs to unlock. Tara looks cute in most anything, but there were a lot of outfits that were my favorites.     • Once Tara is married, she and her spouse can go on dates, and there are cute, little animations of affection that can be done anytime.     • I like the cinematic character and camera positioning while talking to NPCs. It’s great for screenshots.     • Good diversity. Some NPC heritages: Native American, Persian, Japanese, South African (black), Indian, Hawaiian (native), Latinx, and Romani. Several queer characters and one non-binary character. A few thicc characters.     • A lot of farming sims involve the protagonist inheriting the farm after the grandparent has died or moved away, but in this story, Tara is actually moving to the farm to . I absolutely love that. I wish more stories depicted elderly caregiving. (As someone who has worked in a caregiver role, it really saddens me just how many people abandon their parents and grandparents at nursing homes and act like they’re burdens to be forgotten about.)     • Encourages the acceptance of diversity and to reject the fear of the unknown. A bit cliché, but still a good message.     • A couple of mysteries in the story keeps the player interested, both for year 1 and year 2.    • Lots of side romances between NPCs.    • Violet isn’t a romanceable character. My pupils probably dilated upon seeing this character, because dat a$$ and dem thighs can barely fit in those jeans she wears and I practically fell in lust right there! Then, the cute face and purple hair is nice too … like, this is so f*cking unfair. Why put someone so “booty-licious” in the game if you didn’t want the players going after her? She’s single and age appropriate for Tara. I just don’t understand. WHY?!!?!     • There are achievements for marrying  marriage candidate, meaning the player either has to have Tara divorce each one and remarry again and again or replay the game more than once. Either way, that makes 100%-ing the game annoying.    • I wish the game helped the player keep track of all the sidequests that have to do with Angus and Francis’s wedding. For example, I went a long time not talking to Juliet because she’s a 13-year-old girl and I’d already maxed out her friendship so I had no reason to talk to her and logically didn’t think she’d be involved in the wedding planning, but it turns out she had a sidequest involving playing music for their wedding. I would’ve never thought to go find and talk to her. I just happened to walk by her at some point and notice the quest icon show up next to her. There are  other people that have sidequests related to their wedding, but the quest log doesn’t tell the player who to talk to at all, so they have to be happened upon. It was just a lot of wasted time because of the lack of direction.     • The only way to get the ingredient “animal fat” is to murder a farm animal. I mean, I get that in real life animals are slaughtered for our food, but like, the devs made them look super f*cking cute with expressive eyes and sh*t in this game. Not cool. It’s not cool to  the player to kill the animals to get this ingredient that is needed for several things that are needed to get achievements.     • [(Maybe) Bug Report] Mistletoe doesn’t show up until the second year, despite getting an incantation recipe that calls for it during the first year. I swept the forest (where Shelby lives) nearly everyday during winter during the first year to find some. Also, checked Peri’s shop, when it was open, but it didn’t show up for sale until first year’s winter ended and second year started. I have no idea if this is intentional or a bug.    • [(Probably) Bug Report] It seems like rainbow and golden egg spawns are significantly reduced if the player isn’t using the feeding robot. Before the robot: a rainbow or golden egg once every week or so. (And yes, I was feeding the 2 magic chickens and 2 magic ducks daily, along with their favorite food.) After the robot: 2 rainbow eggs, 2 golden eggs every single day. Seems like there’s definitely something off in the coding there. I really liked how story-driven the game was. A lot of farming sims are disappointingly weak on that aspect. While NPCs often have stock dialogue, there are lots of times when they have new, unique dialogue after certain events happen, which is fairly often. It didn’t feel like I was just chasing after milestones (like a lot of farming sims have you do), but actually following a story and the gameplay aspects were just a part of it.

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★★ - 5 out of 5 StarsIf you love farming sims like Stardew Valley, this will make you very happy. Great story, super fun and amazing artwork. The fact that it's fully voice-acted is amazing, too. As far as I know, the game isn't completely finished yet - it seems there's a least another update coming with more to the story. As of right now, the main story finishes at the end of the first year and secondary story quests are through the end of the 2nd year. I just went into the 3rd year and I'm pretty sure there are no story quests from here on out at this time.Nitpicks; you can marry some of the villagers, but it's VERY unsatisfying because no one else in town acknowledges your relationship. My Tara married Westley, and you would never have known if it weren't for the few cut-scenes. The entire town seemed oblivious to the fact that we were dating, and when I proposed, no one said ANYTHING leading up to the wedding. It was very weird. I've heard from other players that if you date Kim, the villagers even tell you all the time how cute Kim would be with Amira if they worked up the confidence to ask them out. ??? That would drive me NUTS. The other nitpick I have concerned the farm animals. Kim is a butcher in town and you can sell your animals to them for meat/money. I was super against that, was never planning to do that, but THEN I realized, if you want the achievement for cooking all the recipes, you HAVE to sell some animals to Kim to get animal fat. There's no other way to get animal fat, apparently, and you need it for two recipes. Rest in peace, Marshmallow and Annabelle. I was not thrilled about that aspect.But other than that, I LOVE, LOVE, LOVED the inclusivity, the LGBTQ+ acceptance, learning the recipes and I had so much fun playing this game. I'm hoping for another update soon so I can play some more. Let's fix the lighthouse!

Maybe it's all the money I made selling fish sticks, turning myself into a millionaire and destroying the game's economy within the first couple of hours of play. Who can say?But what I *can* say is what I especially loved was that once the main story campaign and its mysteries were all wrapped up (and credits rolled!): the game keeps going? Because the devs knew you'd be invested in this world and its characters? And that there's all new story events and shenanigans and it's all still fully voiced? That's such a wonderful epilogue.In fact there's just a lot of care and after-care put into this game that's honestly very sweet and endearing! Like, you've got your typical gameplay loop of farming and harvesting which COMPELS of course; but that time investment also comes with a rewarding world and characters that grow alongside your crops. METAPHORalso you can get married to erika ishii and go out dates with them and also do an affectionate nose boop and say "boop" and 1 out of every 10 of those boops is that throaty muppet "BOOP!" and I get a little rush of dopamine every time I get that particular boop. you understand.

_childDocuments_.review: So for now on, I'm rating cozy games on serotonin levels. For Wylde Flowers, I give it a 9/10 on serotonin quality. This game is premium happy brain juice. Edit: Now that I'm well over 30-40 hours in. I think this may be the best cozy game I've played out of the countless I've played so far. One of of my biggest pet-peeves in farming/cozy game is the lack of story and character development which seems to be an issue for decent amount in the genre. _childDocuments_.review: God, I have so much to say about this game I don't even know where to start and it's gonna be a long one, but if you're not gonna read the entire review then just please take my word for it and buy this game. I sincerely doubt you will regret it. If you're even remotely interested in farming sims with magical elements at all, I guarantee you will enjoy this game.So I had no idea this game was a port of a pre-existing iOS game. I came across it while idly looking through upcoming titles wanting to wishlist things I found interesting, and this one stood out to me as something that seemed like it was tailored just for me. A cozy farming sim set in an idyllic, diverse small town where you also happen to be a witch? Casting spells and brewing potions? Multiple romance options? It felt like the developers made a checklist based on things I wanted in a game. So I wishlisted and thought nothing of it.I didn't expect to get so obsessed with it so quickly. Immediately I was so, SO impressed by the fact that this game is fully voice acted. And not only fully voice acted, but WELL voice acted also. Throughout my entire 50+ hour playthrough, I made sure to talk to every single character every single day, and coming across repeated voice lines was so rare. The townspeople always had something new to say and they were always reacting to the events of the story, the changing of the seasons. When they're sad about something that's occurred, their idle animations actually convey that sadness for a certain time period to show you how they're dealing with things. It makes you want to check on them every day, to see how they're doing. This game just feels so alive in that sense. I was so invested in all of them.The story, while it had some predictable parts to it, always had things that kept me guessing and left me eager to get to the next point where a major event would happen. The game is a slow burn and delivers the story to you bit by bit, and the best part is that if you make sure to talk to everyone every day, you'll notice plenty of little hints and breadcrumbs the villagers drop here and there that will make sense to you later. One of my favorite moments in the game is when you have to uncover who the members of the coven are one by one. You essentially have to guess which villager is which coven member, because they're cloaked and masked and their voices are altered, but if you've been paying attention then chances are you'll be able to guess--or at the very least narrow down--who's who. I won't spoil any specifics, but one of them absolutely had me fooled because I was expecting someone else entirely.Gameplay-wise, to me the game feels very much like a warm hug. It has the usual farming sim staples; planting crops, tending livestock, fishing, etc, but underneath that is the highlight; witchcraft. You'll spend a lot of your time down in your sanctum, AKA a basement area that houses your cauldrons, a distillery to create essences, a desk to write your incantations, and other lovely witchy things. The magical aspects of this game are utilized so well that it truly does make farm life much easier until later on your farm can pretty much run on autopilot to leave you room to focus on the story or getting ingredients for things tied to quests. A lot of quest items you need to craft will have a deadline later on in the game, but honestly they give you plenty of time to finish any errand and also you'll have many magical tools at your disposal to speed up the process. The items you'll need are often fairly easy to get, or you'll already have a decent supply of them if you've been stocking up. It's pretty stress-free. The most annoying thing to farm was soil.There are seasons in the game, but season changes are actually manually done by the coven, so theoretically you could keep a season going for as long as you'd like. However the game does give you incentive to go ahead and change the season when it's time, because trust me, you will feel it when a season has stretched on for too long and you will be eager to see what the next one brings. Because yes, a new season often introduces new features and mechanics as well as advances the story. I think it's great that the game gives you adequate time to prepare for the changing of the seasons, so you'll be ready when you decide to go through with it. I personally like that you don't have to adhere to a strict calendar and the seasons can change on your own terms.My favorite part of the gameplay is the difficulty options that are based on how fast the time of day moves. I was really happy that these options existed because when I was playing Stardew, I got so overwhelmed by how fast the time moved and I didn't like that I needed mods to make it slow down. This game's "relaxed" mode however felt very comforting because time moved the perfect pace to let you do most things in the day, such as talk to everyone. And the cherry on top is that you can change the difficulty any time you want, so you're not stuck with just one setting. My recommendation is to play this game mostly in "relaxed" mode, but occasionally switching to a faster one if the day is moving a little too slowly for you and you want to speed things along, before switching back. But that's just my recommendation, because the beauty of this game is that you can quite LITERALLY set your own pace.I also appreciated the lack of inventory management. Now I know there's a lot of you out there that like having to manage your inventory, having limited stacks of items, keeping them in storage chests etc, but me personally? I find that annoying nine times out of ten. Every item in this game is just magically in your infinity bag, and the stacks can go up all the way to the thousands, and I personally love that. It takes the stress out not having to worry about an item reaching a stack of 99 and then clogging up your very limited inventory that you need to buy more slots for, and to have to make like 15 million chests cluttering your house in order to store everything you need. (Disney Dreamlight Valley, I'm lookin' at you) For me, the fact that there was no inventory management in this game is a plus and a blessing.Do I have critiques for this game? Honestly very minor nitpicks. For example, I'm not really a fan of the fact that you clip through every single townsperson. I wish they were actually, you know, solid. But this was so minor that I never got annoyed by it. Another thing that would've been great is if Tara, the main character, was customizable in some way. Even if you couldn't change her hair or skin color or whatever else, at the very least I would've loved if you could change her outfit.  And/or being able to customize her house would've been great too. It would've also been fun to see the townspeople change outfits every season, or at least for the winter. I was a little disappointed when none of them had winterwear versions of their default clothes, but I didn't mind that much. And I guess I got a little disappointed when characters would repeat dialogue during parts where they SHOULD have something new to say, but like I said, it was very rare. Also though I've only romanced one person, I wish there were more intimate moments you could've had with your romantic partner. You can marry them, and the wedding was adorable, but I feel like I wanted a bit more depth to the romances.I can't think of any other negative things to say honestly, I absolutely loved this game. I just finished the story and there's still some endgame-y things I wanna do, but I know I'll be doing another playthrough sometime in the future. It's not often I can feel when a developer has put so much love and care into a game, but I felt it with this one from start to finish. This game was without a doubt a labor of love. Thanks for reading the whole review if you've reached this point. If you decide to pick the game up, I hope you'll enjoy it just as much as I did.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adore this game!As someone who has been playing the Harvest Moon/Story of Seasons games for about as long as they've existed, I can confidently say that this game maintains the charm of the best of those games while layering in real depth to the characters and the plot. The addition of magic creates a fun, captivating aspect to gameplay that really made this game for me.I will say that if you are looking for a really in-depth farming sim, you might consider the farming/ranching side of the game to be a bit too easy. For me, though, it came across as nicely streamlined. There is a lot going on in this game, and some simplification to the farming duties raised the quality of life aspect. There are still plenty of things to keep a player challenged.Pros:An engaging main character.A fully voiced cast that really brings your neighborhood to life.An intriguing magic system that effects everything from the length of the seasons to the way you interact with friends/love interests. NPCs that really feel like people.A plot that kept me up playing for much longer than I really should.Beautiful graphics and fluid motion (Example: I LOVE the way my character just hops over fences! It cuts down on routing frustration and is just plain fun. I'd hope over my fences rather than go through gates more often than not, just for the fun of it.)cons:Fully animated interactions with animals made ranching frustrating at first. Having to feed chicken by hand, and then pet each one was really time consuming and pushed my patience. Fortunately, there are ways to make this much simpler as time goes on.The buying process for animals was also clunky and inconvenient. I ended up not bothering to fill my chicken coop or my barn, since a handful of animals was all I really needed to obtain abundant products anyway. All in all, the cons were pretty minor for me, far out weighed by the rest of the gameplay and narrative. I highly recommend this game for people who love cozy life sims, farming elements, and witchy magic!
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: Wylde Flowers is one of the best farming and life sim games I have played. In the game, you play as Tara who moves to Fairhaven to help on her grandma’s farm. In doing so, she learns about the coven of witches and joins them. The game is fully voice-acted, which I appreciate as many farming and life sims do not have voice acting. I also enjoy expanding the farm, completing quests, and befriending the villagers. If you are looking for a witchy farming life sim, I highly recommend Wylde Flowers!
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: I was fortunate enough to have been given a key as a streamer to help publicize the release of Wylde Flowers. I tuned in on day one, and streamed it alongside my long-time streaming friend. We were actually graced by the presence of one of the developers for the game, and it was SOOOOO amazing. Enough about the community outreach of Studio Drydock, you're here for the review.The basic mechanics resemble that of every game in the genre. What sets Wylde Flowers apart is the combination of your spells and potions to aid you in taking your farming game to the next level. The game perfectly balances the transition form manual to automated, helping to decrease the grind for the player. That said, this game can get very grindy at times, much like My Time at Portia. The graphics are fun, and lend themselves to the upbeat nature of the game. The diversity of the characters in the game leave players, especially of minority groups, feeling a sense of belonging and understanding towards characters... without going too far into politics. Overall a great game, and my first 100% on steam. I can't think of a game more deserving of that title. I hope you enjoy playing it as much as I did!Edit: I did want to mention that if you're playing this game, looking for a Stardew Valley-esque game, I will mention that Wylde Flowers is a narrative driven game. It's not really an RPG, and the developers didn't advertise it as such. Some of my friends were disappointed that there weren't, but I think that's what makes it so unique in the genre. In so many games, like Harvest Moon, the narrative is highly lacking, leaving us with pretty much only farming. Wylde Flowers delivers an amazing story, and that's why you should be playing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly one of my favorite games to date.So, this game is a farming sim.... but it's also so much more. The best feature of this game is definitely the story. This game, for the most part, takes place for the duration of a year. For experienced farming sim players, you may be thinking, "is this really enough time?" And in a way, there do feel like there are many more mysteries to be solved and adventures to be had in Fairhaven. Alas.You begin to understand the brevity of the game when you consider this very important aspect of the game - the characters. The characters are so well developed, you will find yourself falling in love with EVERYONE. Even the characters we should dislike in the game become likable because of the fully rounded characters. And, the VOICE ACTORS. OH MY GOD. I found out about this game originally from Erika Ishii publicizing this on their social media, but it is so hard to find farming sims with voiced characters. It adds a lot more work for the developers. In this game, it was worth it. Personally, I am going to stop playing this game now that the main story line is done, but I am excited to call Fairhaven my home whenever I need to get back to this cozy escape. Play it. It's worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of the Harvest Moon series, this game filled the void the lack of good Harvest Moon games has created. Wylde Flowers is lovely! The game mechanics are simple to understand, it's not clunky, bugs are very few and far between, and it feels like a completed game! The story was riveting and engaging, like a good book you don't want to put down. I laughed, I cried, and the characters really touched my heart with their well written personalities. I could not have asked for a better farming game. It took me just shy of 67 hours to complete the story, but there's more achievements to be earned! I can see myself coming back to play this one again and again. Some of the features I really enjoyed are:The ability to speed up/slow down the passing of timeBeing able to craft items from the resources you find/grow/mineCooking! Flying on a broom is pretty awesomeThe GloamingThe graphics - overall stunning and charmingI really hope we might see a season 2 come out in the future so the story continues.

_childDocuments_.review: This game pleasantly surprised me. I admit, from its art style, lack of combat, and premise, I judged it as a little “twee” for my taste. The way some cozy games minimize conflict and try to feel cute and pleasant and unchallenging. But I was willing to give it a shot as a relaxing after-work game with progression that hits my dopamine receptors just right. It exceeded my expectations in its characters’ dialogue and emotional depth, in its willingness to confront death and loss and othering, and the way it optionally tackled the butchering side of animal husbandry (no other farming sim I’ve played has—only leaving the fate of sold animals to your imagination!). Like, a character mentioning their child’s would have SHOCKED me coming from Harvest Moon, Stardew Valley, My Time in Portia, or Sun Haven! Conversations here feel more genuine than in many games where characters feel like smiling cutouts. These people feel more properly alive and often frustrating! Plus, yep, progression did give me that dopamine fix.I’m not saying it was super dark or had incredible mechanical depth. But I judged it harshly on first sight, and if you feel that impulse, maybe give it a chance like I did and be pleasantly surprised by its maturity like I was. I’m eyeing my next cozy game and wondering if this one has set my expectations for NPC dialogue too high to enjoy it!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, the game is just okay, which is really unfortunate because the character dialogue and voice acting is pretty great. I do wish there were more dialogue choices so that what you say to another character feels like it matters more. The ability to choose dialogue is very few and far between in general. The game is definitely lacking. You can't customize your character in any way, or your farm. You can't change clothes, you can't decorate or buy furniture. Mining and farming and fishing are overly simplified and you just don't feel engaged while doing any of them. For fishing, you just hit a button once to catch it with no haptic feedback on the controller, and there's no bar to mimic reeling the fish in. It's just one hit and done. Mining is the same regarding haptic feedback - nothing happens besides a single button press. Because of this, things don't feel as immersive as they could.Energy costs are an issue because of how quickly you run out of stamina. Although you can cook recipes to bring it back up, in the beginning of the game especially it's harder to obtain ingredients, and you'll be spending all of your money to be able to craft recipes to get small amounts of energy again. It's not sustainable long-term because of how fast energy depletes. You have the option of then going to bed, but the day won't be over and it ends up feeling like a complete waste.One of the very positive aspects of the game is how inclusive it is. There's a wide variety of people (race, gender, sexuality, etc.). But overall, the play-style feels more geared toward really little kids because of how simplified all of it is. Which is unfortunate, because sometimes adults just wanna feel like a witch, too. I hope at some point they update the game with some added features, because it could be really great.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best (farming) life sims out there.The characters are all well written and multidimensional. No one feels like a stereotype or one note, and I've been enjoying getting to know all of them. This is made better with everything being fully voice acted, I can hear the tone and understand the emotions being conveyed, instead of having to interpret from text alone (this is not a knock against games without voice acting, just stating this more for those who struggle understanding tone from text without indicators). So far I've had very little repeated dialogue, nearly every interaction I'm learning something new about my neighbors. The cooking and crafting are fun, and I love the collectathon feel to getting all the recipes. I ADORE that there's vegan/vegetarian options too, it's a nice touch for those of us who want that representation and nearly never have it, being able to swap out meat ingredients for veggies or other proteins is such a nice detail. Although, some recipes that are naturally vegetarian aren't always listed as such for some reason. I'm very much enjoying the story, and it's enthralling enough that even my daughter likes to watch to see what happens next. Without spoiling, it's been really helpful to explain more serious topics in a more light-hearted manner.It is truly unfortunate that Violet is straight and I can't romance her :( I can't escape being attracted to straight girls even in video games, fmlJokes aside, this game kicks ass and I love the representation. Looking forward to the next big update.runs well on steam deck~

_childDocuments_.review: Updating with the Fabulous Farming update.Updating again with Violets boutique.Updating my review since the Endless Seasons and Romance update.The devs are listening to their players, fixing things, adding things and they seem to actually care and work with their community. There's been 3 content updates and they seem to care and keep adding things for the players to do.I will add- the broken down lighthouse you still can't do anything with that and it still bugs me. Honestly I'm still mixed on this, but the devs are making an effort for their work.The story is actually really great and I loved it, but this is where I wish steam had a mixed review option. I played one hour of the demo and instantly got sucked into the world of Wylde Flowers, instantly bought it and put 56 hours into it in less than a week. Unlike most games like this, this is the first one I've played where it has voice acting, and honestly the VA is fantastic.This game was made for the story, so it's heavily story driven above all else.I'm not saying don't play it, but if you're looking for something to fill the SDV itch, I don't really think this is it. I'm only bringing up SDV because people are comparing this game to SDV, and that's not really the case here. This plays more like a interactive visual novel farming sim, and once the main story is done I just felt no need to keep going because it was boring, like attempting to drag on a story that's done and over with. The way this game plays, you can't exactly compare it to SDV. SDV you could continue after main story is complete and still have a ton of stuff to do because there's much more content. SDV has SO much more to it for 15$ compared to this for 25$.Pros:The story and voice acting are really well done.The world and the story are just beautiful.The story itself sucked me in, the story telling I personally think the story telling is really good and the way the characters genuinely show emotions, is absolutely fantastic.This is more of a game to just play, sit back, listen to the story and just relax.It's a bit grindy but not too grindy. Further on in the game you get help with this which is amazing.You are able to get some help for your farm, wood cutting, mining, fishing,and watering plants.I like the fact that fishing isn't a huge mini game, it's click and move on to next spot. The mines are also simplistic, can go at my own pace and I don't have to worry about a bunch of enemies.It's really easy to get on friendly terms with the characters and make best friends.I love the characters and how they're done.As for the ES&R update- You can interact with your spouse more and go on dates once you fill up the gauge.Your spouse will now ask if you need help on your farm on your days off, at least that's what Westley did, though I wish they would automatically help instead of asking.Also spouses will sometimes give you gifts.They added a spring festival. Fabulous farming update- The green house has more plots, the shed is bigger, they added more stuff even animals. Violet's boutique update- You can now change clothes whenever you want, and put jewelry on Tara.Cons:This is a VERY grindy and time consuming game, which I think is the biggest downfall for me. Most games like this are grindy but this game was more obnoxiously grindy. Some people like the grind which is fine, grinding can be ok but maybe I just had bad luck especially with fishing.When you fish you need to keep constantly changing spots since every spot you can only catch one fish then you have to move to next spot. I spent a lot of time moving to next area and coming back since I was trying to catch every fish for the achievement. Honestly I got tired of fishing and not sure if it's just me but I wasn't very lucky and it literally took me between 1.5-2 hours (real time not game time) to catch the last ocean fish I needed which was extremely ridiculous. Plus you can only get some recipes from fishing so just spending a lot of time sitting and waiting to grab a bottle instead of a fish.I wound up having to look up a guide for which bait to use to catch what fish and fishing was still a pain.I try to 100% games and fishing just got to be a very irritating and a not fun task. Also for another achievement you need to cook every recipe.... Grinding for the recipes is also kind of ridiculous, especially since you get a lot from fishing, digging, in the caves, and some of the characters and at least 2 recipes can be really easy to miss which kind of sucks.So it's VERY easy to miss recipes and if you're going for achievements it requires a second playthrough if you missed any on the first playthrough.I had a bug after one of the updates where walnuts were bugged for me and none spawned for me anywhere.You can't customize your farm, when you go to build stuff, there's already a place where everything goes, so you have no choice in the matter. Though it sucks that the 'dirt' maker has to sit on the plots instead of being able to place it elsewhere.When it comes to the barn and coop, you get a wheat/hay field for your cows and sheep, it's an automatic feeder, yet the chickens don't get anything so you have to feed them everyday until you get further and get something to help you. Don't know why I can't let my chickens out in the same field as my other animals, or why they don't have their own feeder.The festivals, your marriage, and the other marriage you go to. That's it, there's nothing to do at the festivals other than eat food and talk to people. During Spring festival I collected 12 eggs and that's it. The little they do have is not interesting at all, the marriages are cute but that's about it. The festivals are boring.You can't customize your house, at all, can't buy anything for it either. You get a pet, and the pet doesn't wander around much or even go into the house, just basically follows one path between two points and stands in two different spots and I know this is petty but it bugs me.After the ES&R update- Pistachios, almonds, and walnuts, you can only get them from the forest north of the farm. I did a complete restart after the update and I got maybe 6 pistachios, 3 almonds, and absolutely no walnut drops by the time I started year 2. I checked both mountain overpass and the woods for walnuts and absolutely none spawned in either place. So I got screwed with some stuff.Final thoughts:The devs are listening to their players, fixing things, adding things and they seem to actually care and work with their community. I'm just mixed on this game. It's not bad but unlike most other games like this there's no need to keep playing after main story is done which I completely understand that's the point of this game. I will replay this game a few times or so, but since I have all achievements I don't need to grind as much so I can afford to miss out on stuff but it sucks I have to just skip stuff.I will add, the devs did an amazing job with what they have with the game, they made an amazing world and brought the characters to life.

_childDocuments_.review: so far its a nice cozy farming game with a nice story-line. sometimes i lose track of time playing this game and end up playing for hours. if you think its a game that you'll finish in 20 hours you will not there's a lot of things and quests to do in the game story-line wise and side quest for townsfolk. so far I've only found a few things that could use improvement in the game: 1: Weeds. You'll need a lot of dirt  in the game for some upgrades and potions but the game doesn't really give you a whole lot of weeds to collect and there is no townsfolk who sells the either.2: Coven secrecy. this isn't a game issue just a thing that might bug you if you're die hard on the story-line. All the coven members where robes and masks for a good portion of the early game until you hit a certain quest. the reason for the robes and masks is cause they don't show themselves to just anyone and to keep identity from the townsfolks a secret, but later on in the game during another quest-line they just show themselves to a  after the coven's first interaction with them. i think it would be cool if that character has to go through the same initiation Tara had to  and Tara could offer hints to help them, i think it would help keep in line with the whole coven secrecy thing.3: Ore Distribution. this is probably my biggest problem with the game. the ore distribution system sucks you would think that the lower you go into the mines the chance for finding the ores that appear on the upper levels  (copper and iron) would be lower or you wouldn't find them at all, but that doesn't seem to be the case. It's annoying when you're trying to find gold for quests and upgrades but you're just being plagued by copper and iron on the lowest levels and only walking away with like 7 gold ores from one level but like 15 copper ores from the same level.Anyways the game is lovely and fun so far and is great for anyone who likes cozy farming sims like Stardew Valley but also has a magical element to the game. There's always a quest-line you can be working on and its very rare that you'll find yourself idling in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall Impression: 91 A- Wylde Flowers is a charming farming and life sim game that has solid mechanics and a good story that gives you incentive to interact and learn about the people in your community instead of focusing exclusively on working.Review: Wylde Flowers is a pretty well put together farm and life sim. While not breaking new ground in the farming, fishing, mining, crafting department, Wylde Flowers does a great job of mixing in story elements that make you want to learn about your neighbors and interact with them. While the story is a bit cliche, it is well written and the people of the town actually feel like real people, There are a couple of less interesting characters, but overall I enjoyed finding out more about the citizens of the town.There are a couple of weaknesses to the game I have to point out. You have to depend on luck to get all the recipes you need to get a full cookbook. There are a couple of ingredients in crafting and cooking you can only get through one method, which is really strange.  Many of the items you need to craft to move the story along are of the one-and-done variety that have no further use in the game. While not flawless, I would recommend Wylde Flowers to anyone who like farming and life sims without hesitation.

_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: The coziest of cozy games.Farming, fishing, foraging, building, crafting, livestock, relationships, quests, errands, cooking, and magic. It is one bug net short of every familiar cozy game mechanic.I wish there was a way to "un-transform," but after nearly 100 hours of gameplay that is my only complaint. I also really appreciate the thoughtful menu options to "embargo fish sticks" and the different time speed settings. It feels like this game is built to carry you through the dev's story, but all of the grinding and the day-to-day depends almost entirely on player preference.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: This game is everything you could ask for. It’s a beautiful blend of Harvest Moon and Stardew Valley with diverse, interesting NPCs and an engaging plot. They simplified the farming mechanics and the game is easy enough for a newbie-but can be challenging for an experienced player. I would 100% buy DLC for this game to expand on the story, crafting, and world.  One thing I really appreciate is that the characters are diverse-but it’s not a plot device. The nonbinary character, Kim, is a butcher with a rich storyline that does not revolve around their gender identity-it’s mentioned, but it’s not the entire point of their story.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly charming game where you play as Tara, a young woman who's come to the town of Fairhaven to help out her grandmother, coming from the city Tara has to adjust the farm life not to mention she just found out she can become a witch! In this delightful cozy farming/life sim you will get to know the townspeople of Fairhaven, who are all fully voice acted, farm, complete quests, fish, cook and cast spells as you learn more about your new home.  Check out my curator page for more cozy recs!

_childDocuments_.review: It's definitely a slow, cozy game. If you are more aggressive with resource collection/storage, you end up waiting for in-game days to pass fairly often, but the game is cute, the story is fun, and I've really enjoyed the mix of magic and farming. Once you get a bit farther, everything gets a lot easier (which can lead to the waiting I mentioned), but it's still challenging and enjoyable. 9/10 recommend (unless you have no patience, then this is not for you.)
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: This is, without a doubt, my favorite cozy game to date. It's going to be incredibly difficult to top. I wish I could take a pill to forget it and experience it all over again. ♥It features all the busywork we love in these types of games: farming, cooking, mining, fishing, animals, romance, and oceans. However, it has a unique charm unlike any other game I've played.Every character is brought to life by an incredible voice actor, making it easy to become attached to so many of them. In some games, talking to everyone can feel like a chore. In this game, you don’t HAVE to talk to everyone, but you absolutely WANT to. Each character has a story that draws you in and makes you want to learn more.The story itself is heartwarming and exceptionally well-written, blending themes of family love, friendship, betrayal, good, and evil (in a completely non-scary way), along with humor.It’s wonderfully inclusive, representing various backgrounds, races, and LGBTQ+ identities, which I absolutely love.One of the most random features that I loved is the game's intuitive tool system. If you want to hit a rock, the game automatically equips your pickaxe. If you want to chop a tree, it equips the axe. Why don't other games have this?I'm definitely keeping an eye on these developers for future games. Wylde Flowers 2? Yes, please! ♥
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: I got hooked on this game. The farming system is super simple and easy to do, and the farm animals are so cute. _childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: Great immersive farm game with a town of characters you will love by the time you reach the credits. _childDocuments_.review: I suppose I should review this game since I have spent many hours playing it. For this to be a first game for this developer, I must say that I am impressed. _childDocuments_.review: I wasn't sure how I would feel about this game.  I ended up getting it after watching a youtuber say its one of the best cozy games shes played in a while.
