_childDocuments_.review: Here is my honest feedback:For the first 10-15 hours of the game, it's very grind-y and very slow to make progress. However, after about the 15-20 hour mark, I started making better progress and the story really started moving on. There are days in the game where the only thing you may be able to do is talk to the town folk for a good chunk of the beginning hours you play the game.I finally turned the season to summer in game and after all the grinding I did for a long extended spring, I'm making good progress now.If games that start a bit slow and super grind-y are not your forte, you may not be the target audience for this game. If you have patience (or have the my level of determination and stubbornness), you may just find yourself enjoying the game after getting through the slow start of the game. The pros for me for this game: - You can adjust the speed of time: Relaxed (slow the day down), Normal (day goes by a bit quickly), and Challenge (very quick days). This helped with the slow times for me in the game or areas I wanted to extend the time longer to get a bit more done- The options to gain stamina as far as cooking is concerned, even in the early stages is a decent variety - especially as you unlock more recipes- The story lines for all the characters are well written and you get invested very quickly.- The art style is beautiful and unique- Animals in the game are adorable (who doesn't want to pet a kitty?!)- The ability to change spring to summer (not sure about other seasons yet as I have just gotten to summer in the game)- Unlimited storage for people who like to hoard materialsThe cons for me for this game:- The game starts very slow and grind-y (if this is an issue for you, you may not be the target audience as stated above)- The quickness of the stamina bar can be an issue especially if you do not have the resources to cook to replenish the stamina early on in the game- The availability of some of the resources can be pretty scarce so while people may grind or want to stock pile, the resources go quickly and can take an extended period of time to replenish- Progress on some areas of the game take a long while to open up more content within the game (ties into the slowness of the game as well)I plan to continue to play the game and explore more of what it has to offer!
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not good with words, so forgive me in advance.I've been playing Wylde Flowers since it was released on Apple Arcade, and I have gotten to play it (as often as I was able - work and life and all) on Steam for the past couple weeks, and I love it as much now as when I first started it.It's such a cute, cozy, and chill game. But even more importantly, it's one of the best representations of inclusivity and respect for others' orientations that I've come across in a game.The voice acting is outstanding (aside from some occasional, early scratchiness), and there are witches!If nothing else, definitely give the demo a whirl, and if you enjoy it, I can't highly recommend it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has charmed my socks right off. I have played scores of farming simulations, but this one struck a nerve with the thoughtful story lines and design choices. I recently went back to also playing Stardew Valley multiplayer with my spouse and found myself wishing it has some of the mechanics present in this game (lookin' at you, Freeze Time spell!)The thing I would rate absolutely highest is the voice acting.  The entire game is voiced by very skillful voice actors, and that brings this place to life. Every single character is believable and rich and layered and realistic in lots and lots of ways.  The characters are diverse expressive.I have had a few moments of lull related to grinding needed materials, but I powered through it because I am hooked on the core story and will absolutely see it through.  The nod to LGBTQ+ people is ever-present, respectful, and honest. Thank you for bringing these stories to life in a very chill game that has brought me more joy than then cost of the download put me out. Keep up the good work, devs.

_childDocuments_.review: Very impressed with this game. A friend of mine who knows I enjoyed My Time at Portia said to try this. This game took all of what Portia did right and built on it. The character development, the time it takes to allow you to enjoy the story and complete chores is a testament. My biggest compliment is how it does not overwhelm you with tasks from the get go. _childDocuments_.review: NICE BUT GRINDY, NEEDS PATIENCEThis game is a bittersweet experience. The repetitiveness of the daily routine can feel like a grind, as you find yourself visiting every area of the small map for foraging and shopping every day. Unfortunately, this aspect didn't resonate well with my lack of patience, and I quickly grew weary of the monotonous tasks. I yearned for animation cancelling desperately, as it would have alleviated the frustration.Mining, in particular, left me unimpressed. Extracting one random ore at a time felt tedious and unsatisfying. However, my utmost disdain was reserved for collecting weeds. It was an absolutely exasperating endeavor that I detested. Additionally, the need for copious amounts of soil added to my frustration. I gathered 50 units to expand my farming space, only to realize that I required even more soil to create garden plots. I found it perplexing why the ground needed to be soil if the garden plots would be placed on top of it. The process of arranging those plots turned into a mini-game of Tetris, further adding to the tedium. Moreover, the demand for 40 soil units to automate animal feeding in the barn felt excessive. Soil, soil, soil—my hard work on the farm seemed consumed by this constant need.My breaking point came when despite my efforts to farm happily, everyone rushed me to turn the season, when I had just sown seven-day plants. In essence, farming is merely an element of this game, and it doesn't serve as the main focus. Instead, the game centers around unraveling the story, following a predetermined path. It may be the perfect game to play before bed, as it exudes a relaxed and cozy atmosphere. The final straw was the unnecessary time wasting imposed by the game. Completing missions and purchasing seeds required multiple visits to stores, which only opened four to five days a week. I often found myself waiting extra 3-4 days to visit the stores, even when I had everything I needed from the start. During these days , I was forced to endure the same tedious chores, further exacerbating my frustration. The game compels me to rush when I wanted to take my time and impedes my progress when I wanted to be productive.Regardless of who the player is, the impact on the game's outcome remains minimal. Perhaps I'll resort to watching playthrough videos to uncover the stories I have yet to experience. This game is well-suited for those with patience, who prefer playing only a few in-game days at a time and who are less inclined towards farming aspects.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't getting the attention it deserves. It's a love project through and through.10/10 - Worth the Price - Great Representation - Good Accessibility - Beautiful Graphics - Runs Smooth - Can Pet the CatIt's not about the grind, or min-maxing your way through. It's about the experience of life, the happy and sad and the happy again. Representation is amazing, from young to old. The ability to really slow down time (or speed it way up) let's you play at your own pace, and the caption opens are fantastic as well to go with the FULLY VOICE ACTED dialogue. You play as Tara, her story and her life but making your own decisions too like who you marry and what friends you make. Every character feels right at home and the voice acting choices are immaculate. You are not limited on your inventory, and the management of said inventory is easy to use and categorical. The hours of game play within this glorious world make it worth every penny, did I mention the soundtrack is recorded from a LIVE ORCHESTRA??If you enjoy Stardew Valley, Animal Crossing, and other games from the genre you'll be happy you discovered the world within Wylde Flowers.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game. I'm big into games like Stardew Valley and grew up on Harvest Moon games. I was a bit hesitant at first to play it; my partner had to literally beg me. BUT I'm very glad I gave it a try. I really appreciate the storyline and how it keeps the game structured and moving along, while allowing you to move at your own pace to focus on tasks you would like to. I like that it's more mature; I feel like in the "cozy game" genre that is sometimes hard to come by. I appreciate the inclusivity and diversity as well. I've put 52 hours in so far and I still have more to go. There is a lot to discover and that keeps it interesting and fun too.

_childDocuments_.review: I am thoroughly enjoying Wylde Flowers, although I'm still experiencing the story for the first time. My only dislike thus far is the time element; time either moves too fast or too slow, no matter what setting I'm on.- The controls mostly make sense.- The UI is mostly logical and helpful.- The story progresses as you progress.- They include cut scenes with voice acting throughout the game, which is often overlooked but adds the finishing polish to the experience.The dev team did an amazing job with this game!

_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

Lots to do each day, I love the witchy magical element to it and the story line is also not bad so far. _childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute, surprisingly well-polished, gem. This has long been my favorite genre, all the way back to Harvest Moon on the GameCube, and after the nostalgic depth of Stardew Valley (and Everything in between) I really thought that was it for me, for this genre. Then along comes Wylde Flowers. Excellent voice acting: check (I even actually listened to some of the non-essential dialog, it was that good). Enjoyable Character Diversity: check. Progressive underlying philosophies: check. Quality of Life improvements: big check (**** you inventory management! Auto tool select for the task at hand, awesome). Interesting and progressively evolving mechanics: check. Alleviation of grind just as it's becoming tedious: check. My only complaint of course is that there wasn't more, though at 60 hours - the main story recently completed - I still have a number of things that remain locked. Well done... just... well done. Hopefully the beginning of a beautiful, bountiful new franchise. Well worth it at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't expecting a whole lot and ended up finding this game more than a little addicting. I'll have to set a timer for myself. The characters dialogue is surprisingly realistic and heartfelt, and the voice acting is generally good. The concept is fun, and it's well paced. You won't run out of new things to do, but you don't feel rushed. There's enough mystery to keep you hooked. Highly recommend for those looking for a cozy game with a witchy atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like an evolution of Stardew Valley that probably wouldn't have existed without its success, but I wouldn't call it a clone.  The characters have a surprising level of depth to their stories and there are many variations to the dialogue interactions that unravel their backstories.  It feels like an advancement of what was started with Stardew.  Plus, it is voice acted by a talented team.  The world really feels alive due to the characters and the way you interact with them.  I have found myself really caring about them  and having real emotional reactions to what is going on.  The story is great and I can tell it still has a lot more in store from here.   I also feel the pacing of events is very well put together.  I have played for 22 hours and have never felt I was on a dull grind.  There is just enough engagement to keep the task interesting.  This is definitely the best of the "cozy games" I've ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of good in here, but once again a game is sunk by the utter lack of systems design. it is CRAZY how terribly balanced the economy is. Any fish + flour = fish sticks, which restores tons of energy and can be sold for a tidy profit. Fish+3-4 hard to obtain ingredients sells for LESS and gives you hardly any energy. This is BASIC game design errors. Big kudos for the interesting setting and characters, but you simply can't have a stupid broken economy in a farming/econ game. If you can't be bothered to make a basic spreadsheet to check your values, don't try to make a game that involves econ. Make a visual novel.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: My perfect cozy comfort game! I love that you can play on relaxed speed which gives plenty of time to get tasks done. You can also change the seasons when you're ready which gives you, again, plenty of time. I love the storyline as well... oh and you can marry a werewolf! Tara is lovable which makes up for the lack of character customization. Overall, I love this game and fully get behind the hype.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: Wylde flowers is unique to a lot of farming games due to the personal story it's attempting to tell- and I love that aspect of it! The game is giving you the ability to help that story flow, and while you control the main character, you are NOT that character. From the details hidden in the backgrounds, to the fun dynamics that grow alongside budding friendships and relationships, as well as the fun mechanics of witchcraft mixed with farming, Wylde Flowers is a wonderful experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played many farming games. But this one is definitely a favorite of mine. The gameplay is simple but addicting. But what really won me over was the story and characters. I'm still in the middle of it, and sometimes tasks can be quite stressful, but I keep coming back to it to see what happens next.It's also cool how there is more to do than farming. The player character is a witch and you can brew potions and write spells and do all sorts of cool things that I haven't really seen in other farming games.Plus, the game is voice-acted! When I heard that I didn't realize how many lines there were in the game. There is a crazy amount of work put into this game, and it shows. I definitely recommend this to anyone who likes farming sims games with a sprinkle of magic.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: The game is not as challenging as other games in its genre, but provides a nice casual gaming experience. I love that a bit of Tara's story is left up to the player to be made up by selecting from choices prompted during certain NPC interactions. This game is LGBT friendly. So far, my only con would be that my energy/stamina level is very low, but I'm hoping as I progress I will learn spells to at least temporarily boost my energy, if not permanently upgrade it. At this time, I do recommend the game to players who enjoy casual games, and or are new to gaming and enjoy a topic of witches, and building relationships. I tried to avoid comparing it other popular games in the genre because while I could say it reminds me of Stardew Valley because it contains elements of farming, fishing, mining, and building relationships with the villagers, the game play being less challenging keeps me from wanting to compare the two side by side. To further elaborate, by less challenging, I mean that at the point I have reached in this game, it is a peaceful game. Though it has mining, there does not appear to be any enemies in mines, or even a health bar. The fishing element is very simplified with no strategy necessary.8/10 at the time of review.

_childDocuments_.review: This is game is amazing! I stumbled across it on TikTok and decided to give it a try. As of now, I've played almost 100 hours. 😅 It is so easy to get lost in. The game play is fun without being too much of a grind, like some farming sims. What really stands out about this game are the story and the characters. The story is deep and heart-felt. _childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: *I did get my copy of the game for free, but I did purchase a copy for a friend because this game is worth it*I know I haven't played a lot and I know that I haven't finished the main portion of the story, however, this game deserves all the kind words it has been getting.You have a game that is incredibly story rich, that you get invested in the town and what happens to the main character. All the characters feel real. They are all complex and interesting and different. The voice-acting helps really bring them to life, but even if it didn't have that, they are all meaningful parts of the story and their stories are interwoven. Getting to know them is worth-while just to know who they are and their experiences. You have your farming, fishing, and mining tasks to do, but there is no real grind to get the best crops just to make money. That is not the focus. The focus is on the main character reconnecting with her grandmother and becoming a part of this new town. Also witchcraft.I haven't experienced a lot of the witchy side of things yet, but I cannot wait to.One of the best things is that, you just need to move and click 1 button. No complicated controls, no difficult mini-games. My review is a mess, but I hope it helps you understand that this is a very special game because it does so many things right. _childDocuments_.review: I had the privilege to playtest this game, and I have to say, I don't think I've played another farming sim quite like Wylde Flowers. _childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is the best Harvest Moon style game I've ever played. If you like that type of game, you should try the demo and grab the full version if it hooks you.The thing that separates this from most games in the genre is that there's a pretty clear narrative. You're not a voiceless self-insert protagonist, you're playing a specific role with a personality and a back story, and your character has as much a part in the narrative as all of the NPCs. Speaking of NPCs, the characters are competently voiced and will occasionally comment on recent events, which gives them a greater feeling of depth/development/community than you'd usually see in these types of games.All of the other elements of farming/life sim style games are there, there's stuff to grow, build, craft, upgrade, etc, and it's all implemented well with good quality of life features that make for a fun puzzle of figuring out how to manage your resources and plan your day. But it's the character and story driven narrative that really makes this game feel unique.

_childDocuments_.review: I was very fortunate to receive a copy of this game from the developers, having checked out the details for this game I was expecting to enjoy it, but honestly WOW! _childDocuments_.review: Wylde Flowers is a ~cottage cozy~ farming and life sim, where you play as a young witch named Tara. After her fiance dumps her, and she loses her job as a journalist, she decides to ditch the city life for Fairhaven. By day, Fairhaven is a charming coastal town. By night, well, that’s when the *magic* happens!After about 50 hours of gameplay, and almost through the coven questline, I realized that Wylde Flowers was the best example of how sometimes a game can really surprise you! This is a game I often glanced at, but had never purchased. When I finally got my hands on it, I was so glad I did. I’ve been playing this off and on for almost a week, while fighting off a nasty bug. As someone who does not manage being sick very well, this game offered me the calm and relaxation when I really needed it.I’d also like to note that it was the Uplifting Adventures Game Bundle by Humble Bundle, curated by Wholesome Games, that finally gave me a chance to experience such a great game. The bundle is still on sale for 10 more days! (ends 12/20/23) And the minimum price for the entire 8-item bundle is $20. Pay more to support Save the Children.Pros:    It’s beautiful. It is truly a magical, delightful escape, and I can see myself putting in many more hours to escape to the magical world of Fairhaven and Ravenwood Hollow. The art style is very charming, very cottage-core, or perhaps ~cottage cozy~ !    Fairies, goblins, and werewolves (and yes, you can even romance the werewolf…!) Potions, incantations, and a crystal ball! It’s all the witchy magical stuff that makes this game so special.    The magic and spell casting is so charming, but all of the crafting in this game is very well done. There are tons of crafting stations, magical included, but it doesn’t feel overwhelming or confusing at all. It does not feel like a grind, either. Taking the time to craft, including magical items, really does pay off. Think incantation that lets you shape shift into a cat for a day, or casting a spell that allows you to auto-loot all harvestables!    Fishing is simple, but unique. Not only is there a ton of fish to discover, but fishing can also provide cooking recipes as well. Fish is a staple in a lot of recipes and it’s a great way to make money in the game.    There is no tool wheel. No-need for swapping tools. The upgraded tool doesn’t break. Amazing.    Fantastic writing. Diverse and interesting characters with well-developed backgrounds. So much representation! There is a lot of story to be enjoyed here.    Did I mention you can marry a werewolf, from Alaska, who owns a bookshop? Because I feel like that’s a very important piece of information…Cons:    You might forget what sleep is and stay up until 6 am living your best cottage-cozy life (while gazing lovingly at your werewolf bookworm husband…)    That’s it.In a nutshell, I hope you consider giving Wylde Flowers a chance – I think you’ll be pleasantly surprised and perhaps even smitten. For more cozy game reviews! ^o^

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the main story on this game and found it a fun distraction with great inclusivity. Then I went on a sort of collecting spree and was trying to make all the recipes when I found out that some require animal fat and the only way to get that is to sell your own animals you’ve raised to a butcher to be killed. And not only that, but apparently to increase the amount of fat you get beyond a tiny amount you have to love/ cuddle them more. I was loving how inclusive this game was, but as an animal loving vegetarian it makes me sad that they refuse to implement any work around for this (for some things you can substitute olive oil, just let us do that? Or let us buy animal fat?) In a magical game where you can levitate and have this super inclusive community, why do I have to kill my own well-loved livestock to complete all of the recipes?

_childDocuments_.review: Wyldeflowers is fun for what it is, but manage your expectations going in. If you go into Wyldeflowers expecting a mobile game with some cool characters, then you'll be pleased. Unfortunately, I believed this game would be one of the best farming sims of all time thanks to recommendations from r/cozygaming, and I was pretty disappointed at the uninspired, mobile game-esque, bobblehead art style, incredibly simple farm mechanics, and overall generic feeling of the narrative.I'm 20 hours in and I will just say...This game did not meet the hype. It is fun and enjoyable, but I wish I had known more about exactly what it is before I went in expecting it to be something it just isn't. I went into this playing on PC, expecting interesting character development and plot while also a cozy farming game. I got character dialogue that felt too good, too perfect, too happy to feel genuine, and the farming in this game is kind of a joke. Farming, mining, gathering are all as simple as pointing and clicking and it doesn't seem to be able to optimize at all. This...is a mobile game. The interface and UI is incredibly simple, the graphics and art style is not aesthetically pleasing. I've played Stardew Valley and I love complex characters and relationships (Shane in SDV; Gale in BG3) weaved into my story's narrative. The story is very linear and Tara is just not a compelling protagonist; her uncertainty doesn't make her relatable, it just makes her seem...empty, without talent or traits except for being "of Hazel's bloodline." I could go on and on to how flat the story feels, but I'll leave this review with this:TLDR - Don't believe the hype surrounding this; the game mechanics and UI are so simple that I almost believe this game was intended for children. The art style is...a choice. I don't think I'll continue playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Wylde Flowers is a farming/crafting/social sim that is closer to My Time at Sandrock or the Rune Factory series than Stardew Valley or it's imitators (such as Coral Island or Fae Farms). Farming sim enthusiasts may be disappointed by how simple it's farming system is (you just plant crops and water them rather than tilling soil), but there is a ton of stuff in this game that will appeal to people who find the Stardew formula overwhelming.Wylde Flowers is heavily plot driven. Instead of creating your own avatar, you step into the fashionable ankle boots of Tara Wylde, a pre-established character with a set history and motivations, who has come to the rural community of Fairhaven to care for her ailing grandmother's farm. While she's learning the ropes of how to cultivate carrots and raise chickens, she will befriend the villagers of the charming country town: the butcher, the baker, the smarmy mayor, the local cult leader. Ya know. Standard farm sim stuff. It's farming game business as usual. At least until Tara's grandmother has her inducted into a secret society of witches that works to balance the forces of nature in Fairhaven. Then Tara is learning sorcery in addition to fishing and mining to prepare for battle against dark entities from beyond the veil that will threaten the peace of the community.If you always found the process of talking and gifting random junk to villagers in other farm sims a drag because you so often end up click through the same rotating five lines of dialogue a billion times, rejoice! The villagers of Fairhaven have a ton of different things to say and most of it interesting as you learn about the characters' lives. The social sim aspect actually feels like you are talking with real people and really gives Fairhaven a sense of place and history. I always looked forward to talking with everyone as moving the plot line forward would always give everyone a bunch of new things to say when their dialogue got exhausted.And every single line of dialogue is fully voice acted. As stated, Wylde Flowers has a plot that goes far beyond gather up a bunch of specific items to magic the community center back together. The game has a generous amount of quest lines ranging from those mandatory to move the plot forward to optional quests and errands to boost affection with other villagers. Depending on your preferences, this is either going to make the game feel too restrictive and linear or it will give you some much needed structure if other farm sims feel like they have just too much going on at once. This might actually be it's greatest innovation. Stardew is great, but I usually feel like I'm under the gun when playing it because you have to plan around the 28 day season cycle. There is nothing worse than not getting that one fish that only appears on rainy days in autumn to complete a community center bundle and realizing you will have to play another full year to complete the game. Or miscalculating growing times and have a patch of vegetables turn into weeds when the season changes.Wylde Flowers does away with time restrictions except for some optional quests. The witches of Fairhaven manually change seasons with their spells so each season lasts as long as you want it too. If you want to finish the storyline as fast as possible, you can charge full steam ahead. If you want to do nothing but muck about in town, grow a thousand strawberries, and romance and wed a villager before the first season change, you can do that too. I love how chill removing the time limits makes the game. Like I can play completely at my own pace. Here are a few more things I really like:The fishing system is very simple. You bait your hook, cast your line, and wait for a big fish to bite. No frustrating mini game that you just endure for forty hours because you have to.There are mines, but no combat. There are only 20 levels, so if you really hate mining, you don't have to deal with too much of it.This is a 3D game, and I have to complement how well optimized it is. It am so used to 3D farm sims that are glitchy, have tons of slowdown and pop in. Even my beloved My Time at Sandrock feels like it's code was duct taped together. But Wylde Flowers runs smooth as butter. In my nearly 30 hours, I haven't seen so much as a single frame rate drop. I love this game, and I think you will too if you want a more guided experience that doesn't turn into a full fledged RPG like many of the other plot heavy farm sims do.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are after a chill and relaxing experience this is the game for you. The professional voice acting makes this game a joy to play, and the relaxing background music sets the mood.You'll be lead into the game gently by the story in a clever way - the game introduces new concepts carefully and explains how to use them as you unlock new things to do.The characters are very diverse and well designed. You can't customise your main character (Tara) but this is because the game focuses very heavily on the storyline of Tara and the residents - it wouldn't have been possible to put in such a rich story otherwise.I play using an Xbox controller and the controls work well. A tip - when you are farming and presented with multiple plots of land to tend to you can use the dpad to select the one you want to interact with. This is easier than trying to align yourself perfectly using the analog stick.I've barely scratched the surface so far but I can already recommend this game, and I will continue to stream this game!

_childDocuments_.review: What do you get when you combine diverse tokenism, witchcraft, cutesy graphics, and the LGBT+ agenda of "love applies to minds, not bodies"? This game, and it's a worthy effort. It's been well-scripted, you fall into it, there's plenty to do but you don't feel beat down by it, and you can automate in a lot of ways to free yourself up later in the game to just pal around and do what you want instead of what you feel you -have to- the way a lot of farming sims make you feel. You can change your outfit all of the time, and are encouraged to do so. There's also depth here, from loss to growth to joy, but I get the feeling that this game was lined out by humans and then given over to an AI to complete for one reason: Gaming companies these days spin out weak glitchy proto-games (example: "Spellforce: Conquest of Eo," which is still a mess months after launch), flip them up on the market, and let gamers play-test them and comment before bothering to go back and fix the problems they should have debugged out before trying to get paid for it. There are no bugs in this game; I'm extremely critical of them, and I haven't found a single one. Either this team is pro and exacting and did everything just right...or it came from a program. And given how focused the team was on the message (where in the world is there a community with exactly one member of almost every demographic in existence, no more, no less, and there exists exactly zero racism, bigotry, or even social coldness based upon it? But then again, when you're making the game, why not create your fantasy?), it feels like they probably just let AI fill in all the gaps to complete their vision, because while these aspects are present, they're somehow lacking in impact, like a translation from Google which has the right vocabulary but the text feels weaker than intended.Then again, they might just be amazing and wanted it to be soft for comfort's sake. It's a possibility. One final thought: you're locked into one character because of the text-heavy scenes with voice acting for every word, which is detailed and immersing, but not flexible to multiple characters, and the entire first year is closely mapped out, however; for a game with farming and changing seasons, the story is exactly one year long to the day, so don't stock up on springtime seeds in preparation for a second year. By then it's just sandbox time. They've got me curious, and I'll certainly be watching for future games. It's worth full price, unequivocally . I'm giving a solid 4.1 out of 5.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not regret buying this game. It was made with love and I will always support developers who offer this type of genre. But for everything holy, I just had to put the game away completely. I believe I gave it a fair shot and I took the negative reviews with a grain of salt but they are all mostly right in their critique. A lot of similar types of games do what is needed to hook the player in from the start but not Wylde Flowers. I was bored out of my mind for the first half of my playtime. In the beginning, the stamina bar is so small you get to do few things before you run out and then I was just waiting for the day to be over (you can not end the game whenever you want, you have to wait for the night) while scrolling on my phone, completely disengaged and bored to tears. Your character, Tara, moves really slowly before u get a chance to craft incantations to actually run, and without relaxed mode on it's damn tough and nerve-wracking to bother with the witch quests. I wanted to push them to the background until I had more resources but was reprimanded by the coven (the game) to not do that. Honestly, if I hadn't, by a complete accident, found out a "cheaty" way how to make money, I would drop the game right here. You get absolutely no indicator of very important things (how much is something worth, how much energy something gives you etc.) and a crucial lack of any information on how stuff works. Cooking seems pointless, fishing is quite boring, and stores are closed two days per week which can frick your quests n gameplay up marvelously unless you plan everything ahead (and even then I got rolled over by an in-game event more than once, losing on interesting game events). You have either not much to do or you are in a death spiral of trying to manage stuff. There are almost no fun things to do to take you out of the routine.The game lacks any RPG aspects which usually makes this type of genre the unique signature of the developer and makes you feel like you are moving up, getting better and all the empty stamina bars are worth it. When you gather/mine/log you get stuck in an animation which makes everything tedious. The magical aspects are, except for a few things, kinda bummer. I read a message that "this is predominantly a story game set in a life/farming sim, with relaxing simple gameplay" - fair enough, but it just wasn't fun. It was tedious and at some points didn't make much of a sense. And for a predominantly story-oriented game player should not get fricked over by things that are out of their control, romance shouldn't fall so flat, and trying to achieve stuff so mind-numbing. And this is coming from someone who almost finished Stardew Valley with all unlocked achievements, I live by the pain, grind, and waiting. I mean even here I got to the achievements that only a third or less players obtained to give it a fair shot. Because I desperately wanted to love it. The graphics are very cute, the animals adorable, the voice acting is great and all of the characters are lovely/fun. The add-on of the boutique was amazing decision by the devs. I genuinely believe that Studio Drydock Pty Ltd poured its heart into this game. And let me repeat - I do not regret supporting them. And if there will be another game in their repertoire, I will give it a go. But this game was rough because it got stuck somewhere between a story game and life/farming sim, while it should have leaned more into one or the other direction, so that direction gets more polished.

The character dialogue is so in depth, the voice acting is phenomenal, too. The story really takes a turn from it just being a work load of a "farming sim" and makes it lively and vibrant. After reading into the developer's vision for this game by accommodating for those who are minorities or women, I immediately fell in love more with this game. This game includes all types of personalities, identities, and secrets! For everyone wondering, this is NOT a farming Sim. You plant things, sure, but you can also fish, forage, craft, upgrade, cook, date / marry, and the story-line is WORTH IT but I will not spoil anything. _childDocuments_.review: What a delightful and cozy game. If you're a fan of Stardew Valley and magic/witches as a theme you will no doubt enjoy this. I really loved all the characters (Tara, the main character you play as, was a big plus for me), the writing and the superb voice acting. The story is well paced with some good twists and emotional moments that made me tear up a little. I also enjoyed the game progression - unlocking spells, potions, buildings and the like. The art direction (the character designs are soooo cute) and music are lovely.A big, thankful praise to the developers for the positive and organic way they portrayed diversity. Representation matters. Other developers take note, this is how you do it!As for criticism, my main one is that Tara's starting stamina and movement speed could both be higher.Despite loving this game, I feel there's a lot that could be added to it to flesh it out even more and I hope they keep releasing content/DLC. Personally, I would love to see some kind of professions/skill system as well as a town museum for your collectibles. New characters and interactions/dialogue is always a plus (even though the game has a crazy amount of stellar voiced dialogue already), as well as buildings and areas to explore.Although I finished the main story, I still fell that I've got things to explore and do, which is great.The town of Fairhaven, with its characters and stories, will stay with you.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a year late to this game, but it's easily the best cozy game I've played, ever. The characters always have something NEW to say on a daily basis, and they have a lot of depth. The animal interactions are incredible, so much detail from the animations of feeding and petting them to the actual sounds of your characters hand stroking their fur. All of the animations and sounds are great, the voice acting cast did an amazing job with each neighbor. And the story is really well done. My favorite feature is the time system. I've seen a comment or two that it takes too long to traverse the map or do tasks compared to the time system speed. However! In settings you can choose your game speed between Relaxed, Normal and Challenging. This is a life changer! On days you have a lot to do, go to relaxed, enjoy the breathing room. Not much to do or just want to get to the next day quicker? Go to Challenging, or Normal. Also, being a magic themed game, there are some items that help with movement speed and time of day. The only disappointment I found was the same as any other game with a great story...I didn't want it to end. But alas, all great things must. Yet even after the ending, there are things that pop up to do every couple of days. An epilogue of sorts to keep playing a bit longer.

_childDocuments_.review: This game combines elements that I enjoy the most in games. Farming, sim and storyline makes this my perfect cozy game for relaxing. _childDocuments_.review: This game is truly unique. The voice acting is wonderful and adds SO much when building relationships or uncovering the stories behind the characters' lives. It is 100% the most relaxing game I've played. You can switch to a "relaxing mode" which slows the clock significantly and really allows you to fully enjoy the game and, well, relax. Freely switching between normal and relax mode tailors the game to whatever my mood is and truly made the game perfect for me. In my opinion, the farming element is not as expansive compared to others that exist. There is more of a finite area for farming and there are many other ways to make money that you don't particularly need to farm that much anyways. It became a bit of an afterthought for me. Getting animals later in the game is wonderful and they're cute as hell, so that's something.I think the lack of addictive farming element was more than compensated for by the engaging storyline. Delving deeper into magic, building relationships, the dynamic shift in the town as the year continues... For how leisurely I was taking everything at the beginning, I found myself trying to plow through the late game just to see what would happen next. I'm definitely in the more grind-heavy portion of the game, but I'm still enjoying it. The demo is pretty lengthy and gives you a great feel for whether or not you'll enjoy it. Plus, it carries your save over into the full game. No reason not to give it a shot!

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game.  I like pretty much everything about it, UI, the look of it, and especially that the NPC's are well developed characters and not jut sprites with two or three lines repeated over and over.One thing I found disproportionately pleasing is that you can just hurdle over fences in your farm, instead of going around.  Not sure why, just makes me happy.Three very minor complaints/issues - in the gifting system, a comment from an NPC that one could reasonably see as a hint to a favorite... isn't.  It's annoying, because figuring out what they like is part of the game and in similar games a hint is legit.Like some of it's spiritual ancestors, there are characters that seem like they might get together, then it goes nowhere.  So you have to watch them pine for another.  Sniff.Also I was really happy there were alternatives to selling your animal for slaughter for most recipes requiring meats, but there is one ingredient (so far) that doesn't seem to provide that option.  No alternative, and can't buy it.  So you can't complete every recipe without selling your animals. _childDocuments_.review: Hours of cozy fun! Build your fish stick empire, drink more coffee than you do in real life,  and romance a super charming doctor or handsome werewolf. Wylde flowers has me coming back for more despite other games that I've played longer not being complete. The gameplay is easy to learn and intuitive, the spells you can cast make sense and actually make a difference in gameplay, and the voice acting is really good! I've enjoyed the quests, they all have a real purpose in the game and aren't just busy work. They are right on the nose with people being sold into a cult/MLM/religion that promises everything, and I love that there are characters you can bond with against that. The crafting is fair, not easy but not insanely hard. The only downside if that I think some of the characters are a bit TOO hard to get to know, and I've had trouble finding characters when I need to interact with them for a specific thing. Besides that - BUY IT, YOU WON'T REGRET IT.

_childDocuments_.review: Tara is a wonderful character, her grandmother is a woman I now see as life goals. You play as this wonderful young woman whose life has lead her here to these moments you control in her life and while you don't get to choose everything that make her so special, you do get input on (not so subtle) choices on her sexuality by choosing the gender of her ex in conversations as well as many hetero-romantic or LGBTQIA+ choices for her life should you find new romance for her. You get to navigate her learning about the magic of the world but also gaining confidence in the magic in being the more-capable-than-she-ever-knew young woman she truly is inside. You make friends, maybe some enemies, lovers, and life-long connections hopefully for her as she settles into this lovely new life!This game is fairly accessible with the ability to change how fast time moves in any given moment. Find yourself bored waiting for something in the evening and out of things to do to kill time in that game day? Set time to move faster and then set it back to the pace you find more comfortable when you're done waiting. Alternatively, find yourself with too much you want to do and too many people you want to talk to without running out of daylight too quickly? Slow time down to a leisurely pace. Fishing too hard and/or just not your vibe? Change the setting for the fishing mechanic. Change individual types of sound volumes rather than just master volume controls to best enjoy the  voice acting or the subtle echoes of pickaxe and heavy breathing in the stone caverns of the mines.The stamina is the biggest potential negative I want to mention. You will run out of stuff to do sometimes during the day, perfect time to go to bed early if there's nothing later in the day you want/need to do. But if you need more stamina in that moment, eating is a really important mechanic to keep you going - especially before the I truly adore the magic mechanics as you unlock them and all the little things that Tara gets to do over time. The hardest choice I made in this whole game is who I marry this play-through haha.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good, and it is worth the price because there is enough content to warrant the cost. It has a nice art style and the music and ambiance is also good. It's definitely a cozy game, which is nice for unwinding and relaxing. It's got a really nice atmosphere and doesn't have the feeling of pressure to get a lot of things done as quickly as possible, which is very nice.Pros:- Ability to change daytime speeds, allowing for a more relaxed style depending on what you like- Involved story, which is pretty good- Mining mechanics are enjoyable. The different nodes are really neat- Art is really cute- Very customizable in how you use your time, even with the passing of seasons- Good number of interesting achievements- Addition of magical elements was pretty fun- Help board quests are goodCons:- Outfits not unlocked until later. The dress/boots combo is distracting while doing farm work and mining- Early game energy use is extremely punishing. This can be mitigated by the "fish sticks hack"- Farm customization is pretty disappointing. Limited space, limited areas to place things.- Dating options are lackluster, but this is a huge matter of opinion!- Accessing heart events isn't very intuitive- Some upgrades are weirdly expensive resource-wiseMehs:- Farming is just okay. The use of the planter boxes is clunky and space is limited.- Fishing is fine, but the limited nodes (1 fish per node, then reset) and need to move around constantly isn't super appealing- Shop schedules can be a little frustratingOverall I do like the game, but it doesn't carry a lot of replay value for me outside of completing all of the achievements. It is a good addition to the genre for the most part, but there are some clunky aspects to farming that made me want to largely avoid it, especially in the beginning. This game seems to rely mostly on the magic element and the story, which is fine for what it is. The story is good. The voice acting is what I would expect for a game with this level of polish. The characters are interesting for the most part, but not always likable (dependent on personal taste, of course). The art style is extremely appealing, though, and it's a really pretty game. I haven't encountered any major bugs, either, which has been nice. It's clear that the developers care about the work they put into this game, and they seem very active when engaging with fans and answering questions, which is definitely refreshing to see given the current climate of game development!Also, the things that I consider cons or even "meh" are definitely subjective and might be things that another player enjoys about the game. Overall, it's a good buy and it keeps me engaged enough to put the time into it. The achievements are also pretty intuitive, and you get a lot of them just by playing the game normally.

_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: Ah yes, Freemason simulator 2022Life sim, farming, magic and gay marriage… Hell yeah!This game is the perfect mixture of everything I love. Magic, farming, quests, mysteries, relationships, gays and quirky graphics!! The game is really one of a kind, it’s kind of like playing a game and watching a movie at the same time.I truly was on the fence about this game at first, mainly because of the character designs, and also the lack of ability to customize the player character. It also struck me as a little kiddy-ish, and I'm in my mid 30s and was looking for something with more depth. After seeing tons of glowing reviews, I finally caved and made the purchase and... Holy crap... This is one of the best games I've played in quite some time!! The character writing is phenomenal, the farming mechanics are excellent. I love the representation. I love the dialogue. I love the storyline and pacing. I wanted depth and I GOT depth.I don’t know where to even begin. The storyline, the town, the visuals, the magical elements, the inclusiveness, just enough farming/mining… it’s everything I could possibly want in a game. I finished the game about two months ago and I still just feel empty without the game in my life (I’m still playing here and there but I’m sad the main storyline is over). Few other games have hit the same. The writing is just something else. There’s fully realized and fleshed out characters with a talented voice cast. By the end of the main storyline, I felt like I knew everyone on the island personally… and loved all of them.I highly recommend this game to everyone who likes story driven farming games. The story is great, the diversity in characters is outstanding and I really like how dynamic the events, the music and the story feels. The characters' back stories are nuanced and elaborate, there's a lot of mechanics - and without wanting to spoil anything the game tackles some very serious life topics and handles them maturely and with tact. I really appreciate how well-made it feels and it’s clear that a lot of love and care went into making it. I think what makes it so special is that the characters grow with the story. There’s always new dialogue from everyone and they feel so alive instead of just saying canned phrases until a specific cut scene. It’s excellent and very unique in that aspect, such an enjoyable experience. It’s not common to find a game of this level that’s fully voice-acted! Every line is voiced beautifully, and it’s refreshing to have so much fresh dialogue and the NPCs rarely repeat the same lines over and over.It’s more simple than other farming sims, less customizable, less farming focused. Mining isn’t as exciting, and there’s no combat whatsoever. The map isn’t huge and can be a bit slow at first. But again the voice acting and character development is some of the best I’ve experienced. All the characters are interesting and unique, the storylines are really good, and again EVERY dialogue is voiced. They clearly did a stellar job in that regard. I liked making and casting spells, it mixes things up and makes it different than a regular farming sim. I also really like farming sims that allow you to slow down time. I'm not fast at these games. Being able to slow the game speed was literally the best thing! I love to take my time in games. But then at times, I could speed it up if I didn't want to wait for something to be done.It's also great that you don't have to switch tools. I tend to get tools mixed up easily. And endless inventory! No organizing or chests to worry about. So awesome. And how you change the seasons! So perfect. The game being so inclusive and diverse was so nice to see! I loved that the game is filled with so many wonderful surprises and stories, the town is filled with amazing people. I only wish there were other games out there that were just as well developed. Thumbs up to the developers, for making a great game for us to play. Now, it’s is a quality game, without a doubt, but whether or not you like it depends on what you're looking to get out of your life sims/farming games. Are you a min/max-ing grinder that likes to have deep gameplay systems that grow over time? Do you need to be able to customize every aspect of your farm and character to be satisfied? Are you looking for a challenge? If you said yes to any of these, then you probably won't like Wylde Flowers. It is not that kind of game.However, it has the best and most natural dialogue and character building that I've seen in any of these types of games. It feels on a different level than Stardew or Portia or Animal Crossing, and I love it for that. The closest comparison I can draw to its storytelling is Spiritfarer, but lighter. And like Spiritfarer, if Wylde Flowers is going to grab you, it won't be with its gameplay but its humanity.If you've been considering this game and haven't played it yet, I VERY much encourage you to give it a go. Don’t be discouraged by the “Dora the explorer” vibes from the graphics. It's a breath of fresh air and SO immersive.Honestly, Wylde Flowers goes to answer that NO, we’re not tired of farming games (and that's why I haven't been clicking with many recently). On the contrary, it's that companies have gotten lazy and are making boring farming games. Wylde Flowers shows you how to do this genre right!10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I am loving this game so much! I love sassy Tara and her interactions with the town. The art style is gorgeous. My only thoughts for the game so far: - I love the diversity with the characters. You really get a small town/family vibe in this game and I love that so much! Some of the dialogue while sometimes sweet, but is also sometimes wacky gets a nice chuckle. It gives the characters more LIFE to them, rather than just a hi/bye situation and that's it. - I'm hoping with later updates we can get a good solid map, with titles of the character's homes/shops so it's easier for a newer player like myself to navigate. I'm slightly getting better remembering where I am, but a map with names of the locations would be perfect.- The nonexistent time limit to turn in a fetch quest is BEAUTIFUL. I've had this quest from the town square for Parker to turn in wood for days and he hasn't complained/quest hasn't timed out and I love that. _childDocuments_.review: I won't lie, I didn't think I'd like Wylde Flowers at first due to the art style and premise. The crafting becomes extensive (in a good way), giving the player a ton of options in attire, items to sell, plants to grow, dishes to cook (truly awesome), and magic to discover. _childDocuments_.review: A nice game if you're looking for something that is a lot more relaxed and slow paced with a little bit of everything plus suddenly being a witch and making spells and other stuff. Like that's pretty neat as a different aspect to what otherwise is another farm sim. I wouldn't say there's a ton of different options and things to do necessarily, but I feel like there's also just enough of each category of interest that it will keep your attention well enough. I like that you don't have to always go and talk to an NPC in order to get all the new things built at your home. I enjoy the variety of things that can be built without choices becoming overwhelming. I appreciate the slow unlocks to help with that process. I like that some stuff is tied to the story, itself, and can't be unlocked until a certain point. As far as mechanics go, they're really simple and easy to grasp. It's a point and click game essentially. You go do the thing and you do it until you run out of energy for the day. The energy bar at the beginning isn't very big, so you can't do a whole lot to start. You also have to upgrade tools in order for them to consume less energy and that can take some time to do. You can have Tara consume food in order to regain energy, but I've found it often times not worth it to collect much food in the beginning because of the sheer cost of ingredients or the food itself from stores. I ended up just making a lot of that moonflower tea. That's one thing I did find a little annoying in this game, too. There's such a big variety of recipes you can make- but they all require a lot of ingredients that are much easier to get in late game. But I  feel like by the time I get to that point, I'm probably going to lose interest in the game and stop playing it. So, it feels a little silly to even have that as an option. I guess it's to help bribe the villagers into liking you more, but honestly, it's only the fall and I've already become best friends with half  of the villagers without even having to gift them things. It's just a lot easier to talk to them and do odd jobs for them.You know. Except for Cameron cause **** Cameron. lolThis also isn't by far a game with any kind of means to money farm like crazy in some streamlined way, so if you're looking for something like what you would be able to build in Stardew Valley, you aren't gonna get that. Which is fine for me. I'm not here for that, so it's whatever. But something to consider if that's your jam.Lastly but I feel like it's most important? The voice acting really took me by surprise in the best way possible. I wasn't sure if I would be muting it or not as I've done with some titles, but the whole cast does a solid job and I'm really impressed! The game's themes can be a bit too on the nose as far as some of its inclusive dialogue goes- as in please don't bang me over the head with things. Like I already picked up what you were putting down, it's fine. I believe you. But outside of that, like. I genuinely enjoy the characters and I didn't expect that. And it's pretty much what's kept me along for the ride. I love that Hazel is such a takes no crap kind of person. And I just generally enjoy how everyone just has a distinct part and personality and it's pretty cool. Bonus points that the kids all act their ages, too. Probably won't bug most people, but I work with kids, so it's really noticeable when people guess work how to write kids. Also, some nice LGBT+ rep including a non-binary character. I do wish there were more options for datable ladies. Listen, Violet would be hella cute to date. Alas.Music's nothing I absolutely love but it's nice. Graphics are alright enough. I'm not a fan of the style, but the game functions and there's no notable bugs that I've run into, so I'll take it.Overall, a fun, easy-going game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: A unique take on farming sims.What I like:This might just be the most diverse game I've ever played. Not just in terms of it being LGBT+. There are characters from all over the world, with their own cultures that, while they don't bring them up OFTEN, are mentioned and are part of these character's personalities.Your player isn't the only one to find love. Four NPCs get married throughout the course of the game (if memory serves, you need to play through at least a decent bit of year 2 for two of these characters), and four other NPCs start romantic relationships. Two of those four in the latter category are some of the single people if you choose not to date them.What I don't like:The foraging system. It's a fairly key part of the game's mechanics, yet the items you need can take forever to spawn. For example, I need 12 pistachios in my main save. I have spent literal in-game weeks looking for these pistachios, and have found a grand total of 3. There needs to be a better way of getting foragables, even just an NPC selling them on occasion.A minor quibble, and one I don't know if it's changeable, but it would be nice if NPCs, the bachelors and bachelorettes at least, had dialogue that took into account relationship status (if such a thing is possible). For example, a recent update brought in a new bachelorette, and the NPC I married said 'It's been a long time since I've had a new crush'. Ouch.Overall, however, this is a great game, with an enjoyable story, and a unique spin on farming sims.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy farming games and building games, and I love female protagonists, so I thought going in that I would enjoy this game. It's a plot-driven game with interlocking events, where plot progress is activated by completing certain tasks. Mostly, the quest goals and dialogue events activate as expected, creating a plot with more cohesion than flexibility, although there are a few hiccups. The game does allow you to get ahead of certain plot developments by building or planting things ahead of when they're strictly necessary. Sometimes this works well, and sometimes less so. The characters are well-drawn and the conflicts are compelling. Character-driven conflict is probably this game's #1 selling point, to be honest. All of the NPCs feel like multi-layered characters with unique motivations that stem from their life experiences. Being fully voice-acted definitely adds dimensions to the characters, making them deeper and more affecting. I ended up finding some liking for every character, even the ones I initially thought I would hate. Some aspects of the plot resolution are predictable, but not in a bad way. If you pay attention to every character's dialogue, you learn their motivation, and that helps you predict some of the turns of the plot. That's just good foreshadowing. And, well, secret identities can't be kept well when there are only 25 or so characters. The game's balance could use a few tweaks, with some items being difficult to get and the difficulty levels being a bit too much of a jump. That didn't ruin my enjoyment of the game, though. I could see myself happily replaying it, although probably not back-to-back.

_childDocuments_.review: This Is another one of those games that Is hard to recommend against because It definitely feels charming and full of heart, with a lot of characters radiating personality, and such a cute style and a nice story to tell. Please, don't let me knocking the game on the things I don't personally like stop you from buying and playing It, because I might just lack the patience needed to enjoy this game to Its fullest.With that said, there are plenty of positive reviews, so I thought I'd share my experience with the game. TLDR Is that It's just WAYYYY too slow and boring for me. All progress In this game feels like a crawl, and that's EVEN with the tips on how to make a lot of money fast. You have the worlds smallest stamina bar which runs out before you can make almost any progress In any way,  A lot of quests reward you for way less than the effort that went into them, everything Is accommodated by a long and slow unskippable animation you have to watch every time you do It, you walk very slowly and shops are closed half of the days. You get a small plot of land but require a LOT of resources, and need so many resources to upgrade.For example. You need weeds to create dirt (they spawn maybe 1-5 per day). You need to create a compost bin with wood, 2 weeds to create soil, and wait over a day in-game time. After that, you have 1 soil, which you then can make one farming bed with. There, you can plant one crop. To create a bigger field to plant more crops, you need 40 soil, and another field costs 50. But no, you don't save up all these expensive and slow to obtain resources in order to just PLANT more things, you spend them to unlock the space to create MORE farming beds to place there. Why?You cannot buy soil or weeds (that I'm aware of), stuff you CREATE with your OWN resources at the farm COSTS MONEY? Why? It feels slow and drawn out just for the sake of It, that Is not a user-friendly or fun experience In my opinion.There are tasks you must do at night time, across the city from your house, when you have a curfew and walk as slow as possible. Things that benefit you such as speed buffs cost so many resources and have a time limit, and It just feels like so much "why?". It's like they made the game very inconvenient for the player but I can't understand the reason behind It.If you are coming to relax and don't mind the slow pacing of the game, that Is more than fine, I think you'll love the wonderful little world that Wylde Flowers has created, but for me, I'm quite the ADHD gamer and my patience can't take this game any more than I have. I love farming games, I do! They are cosy and I love achieving all the goals and progression there Is, but lord, If I have a slow and relaxed play style OR a fast and efficient play style, let me play the way I want, rather than forcing one of them on me.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game a lot more than I thought I would!I'm a huge Stardew Valley-fan, and was looking -as always- for something remotely like it, but most of all: quality. _childDocuments_.review: Did you play games like Stardew Valley or My Time At Portia and think "This is great, but what it really needs is more diversity, more witchcraft, and no annoying minigames."  Well if so, this is the game for you! The game is way more story and character focused, the protagonist already has her own backstory and personality (rather than being a blank slate for the player to create). There are several obvious nods to other popular games in the genre (like the 'Meet everyone!' starter quest from the mayor, and the strangely convenient jobs of the towns people "Yes we're a town of about 22 people, but we have our own blacksmith and carpenter!"), but after that the game takes it's own path and explores its own story.The characters feel way more human and 'real' than I'm used to for NPCs. While they all have their own quirky personalities, they have very relatable backstories and motivations. There's a non-binary character, who feels like a fully fleshed out person rather than a caricature. There are gay, straight and bi characters who's identities exist outside the protagonist (they're not just 'player sexual'). While dialogue will eventually repeat, there's a stunning amount of dialogue to get through before that happens (mostly, the 'coven' seems to have way fewer casual conversation lines). Since the whole Witchcraft plot is rather central to both gameplay and the game's USP, it's obviously no surprise when it starts, which can make it harder to share Tara's (protagonist) surprise. But it's fun and creative, and you're free to largely ignore it for as long as you want, while focusing on fishing, farming, foraging, mining, and of course rebuilding Granny's farm. Or dive right in at the first opportunity.  The story and gameplay unfold naturally, so if you can't figure out how to progress, just do something else for a bit and it'll all become clear. I like the diversity in terms of race, sexuality and gender identity. I like that there are a variety of love interests and your character has plenty of options in terms of the gender of her potential partner.  The romances are a little minimal at the moment but the devs have been very involved and taken that feedback onboard. At time of writing they are planning more content that will hopefully expand on the feedback players have given them. Also, there is an adorable kitty. You can pet the kitty. Pet the kitty!

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to take a moment here to thank the friend who gave me this game. It was truly the breather I needed! So thanks a lot!Hair customization for Tara will now be possible thanks to the upcoming update in which the game will welcome Eury's Salon! Adding a new way for players to personalize our lovely Tara and... Meaning a new romanceable character for us to add to the list of already available suitors! Something I need to warn you about is the way time runs so fast in this game. If you already played Stardew Valley, you may have an idea of how that works, but here, time goes on even faster. When you progress a bit within the game, some of the perks you can obtain through items and such, will help you with that... But even so, it was frustrating in the early stages of the adventure, since, personally, I was running like crazy trying to do all I wanted before calling it a day!I kept repeating myself mentally so hard : Maximum Effort! So many times… That even Deadpool would love to sue me claiming author rights on that quote given my excessive use of it! Welcome to Fair Haven, an island surrounded by mysteries to unravel and with plenty of people to chat with, either to make a new friendship or to “find the love you've never thought you would be able to find”.7 romances available suitable for all tastes! (1 of them will not appear until progressing to a certain point of the story!)Play as Tara, the granddaughter of the most beloved citizen of the island, grandma Hazel. Help her to reconnect with her grandma and make up for the time lost being apart. You will be in charge of her piece of land, trying to get a hold of all the daily tasks and chores a farm usually involves: growing crops, chopping wood, mining resources and even fishing.Cook food, following Hazel's wise advice of luring the stomachs of your neighbors with their favorite dishes, to win their hearts over. Until night comes you will have plenty to do, explore and pass the time the way you choose!But remember, once the sun goes down, all your responsibilities will involve tons of magic!Learn how to master your new acquired powers with the guidance of grandma Hazel, by brewing potions and casting spells! There's a fair number of items to unlock while progressing with the story and the seasons. Some of them are upgrades to help with the daily tasks that follow due to becoming a farmer, other ones could be considered temporary perks or boosts for our lovely Tara and, lastly, some could be categorized as utilities.And once you learn how to sew, a lot of cute outfits will be at your disposal to customize Tara's appearance to your liking!Maybe a farming simulator involving witches and magic may sound a little odd and not appealing. But honestly, it’s one of the latest games I've played featuring the farming sim genre that kept me glued to the screen for hours, and helped me destress.The way they added magic into the world and the plot of the story makes the player get interested in discovering more and keep advancing through the game!Also, the autosave feature of this game is quite amazing and works wonders, with little transitions acting as a “loading screen” while moving from one zone of the map to another one that will only last seconds!I’ve discovered a little trick: If you go into the blacksmith's building at the same time as Natalia goes home (a bit before 12 at night) and you go in just while she is crossing the doors, you can click on her and commerce as if she was on business hours! It works even on Thursdays when the blacksmith is not open!Also, a reminder: If you don’t remember at which day or hour some stores will be open to the public, quickly check in your book below the picture of the character in charge of the said business. They have all the schedules written there!May the broom be with you!
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: Very rarely will I leave a review for a game, but this charming life/farm sim was well worth the price of admission. With dozens of little touches varying from full voice acting throughout the adventure, to quality of life features that Should be genre staples, Wylde Flowers is borderline a no-brainer for fans of cozy games. If you can look past the somewhat bland art style/character models, I can state that you will almost absolutely have a fun time.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: It has the fun and farming element of Stardew, but with a cool witchy vibe. I wish there were more things to do after the main story ends. Like there could be a task for fixing the lighthouse or the bramble gate, or even bringing someone new to Ravenwood. There is a lot of room for more tasks to complete and I hope this story gets expanded.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: Wylde Flowers is an extremely cute, cozy, and absolutely addicting game. If you love Stardew Valley or Coral Island, you will adore this game. The art style is adorable, and the  blew me out of the water. I have yet to see a farming game similar to this that is fully voice-acted.Start off playing as Tara, a beautiful young city girl who arrives in Fairhaven to assist with her grandma Hazel's daily living, only to discover that she is a witch and always has been since the day she was born. You will be able to farm, sell your produce, and complete jobs for people around the town to earn an income. Make friends with the people of Fairhaven, and maybe even find someone special to romance (Amira all the way!). Don't forget to bond with your witch coven as well!There are 30 characters that each have their own unique personalities and quirks. I found myself really enjoying talking to each person every day and even falling in love with one of them. I absolutely loved the diversity and representation of all genders, sexual orientations, and cultures in Wylde Flowers. The gameplay is just so charming. Tara can farm, bake, go fishing, make her own candles, manage a bee hive, brew potions, forage, and eventually even learn to fly and ride her own broomstick! There are so many cool features to unlock as you play through the game, it is just absolutely fantastic.Wylde Flowers has a lot of gameplay for you to enjoy, with up to 40+ hours of fun to be had! This game is so cute, and it's not difficult to pick up if you're a variety gamer who can't seem to stick to one game at a time.The controls are fairly simple and work great on mouse & keyboard, and controller as well! All in all, this is an amazing game, and I highly recommend you try it out!My only gripe is that I wish I could customize my character! I think it would be so cute to see Violet work her way up to owning her own boutique (since that's her dream) and buying different clothes from her.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend giving it a go!Wylde Flowers has been so addicting, it’s like a cross between Stardew Valley and Animal Crossing with a touch of magic!Pro’s:1. The storyline so far has been very captivating, and it gets me hooked. 2. The character development of the NPC’s and the deep relationships you can build with them. 3. The game is very inclusive, all the characters have different backgrounds and stories you get to experience.4. The game mechanics were very easy to learn and navigate.5. A very cozy game, I don’t feel pressured and has been very relaxing.Con’s:1. I wish there was more customisation, but this is also refreshing because it’s one less thing to focus on.

_childDocuments_.review: This had such potential to be a great cozy game, but after finishing the main story line I have to not recommend. Diversity is a great thing to want to include but it shouldn't feel forced. SDV did a fantastic job of letting the player make those decisions, not having it forced on you 24/7 like this game does. When there are some events that cannot be skipped in the main story line that make the person playing uncomfortable you lose the coziness. This is sad to say, but it's a DEI game and may have similar mechanics to SDV, it is nothing like it, more of a RPG. People play games to get away from reality and this just shoves "the message" in your face every chance it gets. If I had known that this game was like this then I wouldn't have bought it, thank goodness I waited for a good sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok.. So...   I DID get a refund BUT it's not because the game is bad... So many I know enjoy this game.. I have been looking forward to it.. _childDocuments_.review: Kitty. You can pet, feed and befriend it. _childDocuments_.review: A fantastic game. Only two things that made me sigh occasionally is how tedious the mining gets (as it's the quickest way to make money), and whenever I missed closing time of a shop by a few seconds and had to wait to get my things done there for several in-game days. But the game provides solutions for both of those at some point. The story is super interesting and sucked me right in. After finishing it, I felt like I had finished a really good, intense detective fantasy novel. The voice acting is phenomenal and the characters are very well fleshed out and multi-layered. I also like how diverse the game is. The soundtrack is amazing. This is not your typical farming simulator, the witchcraft and multi-layered story made it much more interesting. There is some clipping of feet into the ground here and there, but that does not take away from the experience at all. Really really well done!

_childDocuments_.review: While I ran into some major bugs later in the game with the newest update (unlocking the Corgi happened after getting the final final cutscene and the letter saying the game was beaten), as well as missing one recipe on a save due to an event not triggering which messed the save up and caused a restart. The recipe could easily be fixed by having a feature in late game where you could buy any recipes you didn't unlock. Same with crafting. That said, a full from zero to 100% completion save was around 90ish hours. You are getting a grand bang for your buck, especially if you replay this game. I played this primarily on my SteamDeck and it worked flawlessly!I REALLY recommend this game. I cannot scream from the top of a mountain enough that this game is underrated and needs more exposure. The focus on making a more inclusive story, using voice acting, and lots of accessibility features creates a fantastic experience. I would definitely love to see more disability representation in the characters as well. Really looking forward to all future projects by this studio. 10/10 recommend.
