_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game.  I think of it as Stardew Valley that's a little more approachable and with modern graphics and voice acting.  The best part is the story and the characters.  The writing is just fantastic.  There is humor, grief, mystery, and drama--in proportions that work just right.  The humor is often cheesy (and will definitely resonate with Millenials and older Gen Zs) but in an endearing way.  Impressively, the game is entirely voice acted, and almost all of it is top notch. Each character has a unique personality and I wanted to get to know most of them.There is plenty to do: farming (of course), magic, crafting, cooking, fishing, mining, raising animals, building relationships, customizing your outfits/hair, and more.  You will not get bored, trust me.  Some of the side quests are a bit basic, but the main campaign will keep you invested for many hours.  The only thing I wish they had included was the ability to customize and expand your house.  Sadly that remains unchanged.  But you can customize your tool shed, farm (to a limited degree), and basement.  Highly recommend this game for anyone who likes cozy farm simulators.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: I really love the balance between the story and just doing your own thing in this game. I enjoy that I can just follow the narrative when I want to and bounce from quest to quest, or I can just linger on a part of the game if I'm enjoying the season or other things that are happening. Being able to set the game pace as well is SUCH a great feature. This game has all of my favorite activities: puzzles, farming, crafting, and foraging. The crafting system is quite large and there are tons of different kinds of things to craft so I found there was a lot of fun stuff to try to make.The  are probably my favorite thing of the game, and it felt really rewarding to finally unlock them. I love my little ! I was worried that there wouldn't be things to do after finishing the main story, but there is so much new and fun stuff to try.I think an honorable mention for favorite things should also go to that fact that you can go back to a previous save file (on PC) if you maybe made a relationship mistake (sorry Westley).

_childDocuments_.review: Witches and farming sim together? Sign me the heck up. I was insanely excited about this game when I stumbled across it and yet playing through it, it somehow ended up being so much more than I could have hoped for. This game literally became my life while I was playing through it. I’m a huge fan of farming sims, and this game did not disappoint in that respect. In fact it had so many extra little things in addition to your typical farming sim that made it even better (such as making your own clothes, dye, and others besides). Then there is the witchy aspect. Getting to learn your witchy heritage and interact with your very own coven is just incredible. It’s the witch game I’ve always wanted. And the characters just had my heart entirely. All this to say play it! Not only is the story amazing and heartwarming, but there’s also fantastic voice acting and beautiful yet adorable graphics besides. The only downside is finishing the main storyline. I had such a crisis on finishing it and the hugest game hangover. I just wanted it to go on forever. I can only hope a similar game comes along at some point.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm cautiously recommending this game.  The art style is right up my alley.  I love cute and cozy games.  However, there are so many things that I found highly frustrating in this game.  Primarily what I'm calling the time system (for lack of a better word at the moment).  Time goes by super fast and yet the character travels very slowly.  It takes hours to go from one end of the board to the other.   That wouldn't be as much of an issue if there wasn't a hard stop in the game.  I've never encountered that before (side note:  I've never played Stardew Valley and I think it has this?).  Regardless if the energy bar is high or not, the game shuts your character down at the stroke of midnight like she's Cinderella or something (close to midnight).  The first time it happened shocked me.  Her energy bar was full!  The second time, she wakes up in the hospital.  So, not only does it take hours to traverse the map but now you have this hard stop at midnight.  It barely gives you enough time to accomplish anything!  Once you get a broom, it gets better thankfully.The spawn rate of some of the foraging items is ridiculous.  Weeds?  Pearls?  Good luck finding them.  The quest with the malasada?  Felt hard just for the sake of being hard, it didn't have to be so difficult.  It annoyed me so much that I just gave up on it.  I'm not here for something that takes days...DAYS...to find.  Finally, the story line is short.  It's over and done.  Is this an abandoned game?  The last update was over a year ago?  That's a shame because it has potential.  There are so many things left open ended that the game feels unfinished.  Why can't we use the ferry?  Why is the lighthouse in ruins?  What happened to it?  So many questions.The good parts of this game are really good!  The short story line kept me interested, especially there at the very end.  I found myself staying up till 2 am just to see how it all works out.  Was kind of sad to see the ending credits.  I am not a fan of games with an ending.  I didn't realize this game had one or I probably wouldn't have played it.Also, the graphics were just stunning.  Loved the way the world looked in the snow, so pretty.My apologies for the rambling review....TL:DRCute game, great graphics, adorable characters, enjoyed many aspects of it.  Cautiously recommend because of the time system, the slow spawn rate, and the way the game just ends, over and done.  Leaving you with the feeling of what now?
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: This game has quickly become one of my absolute favorite farming games. It keeps some elements of the trope perfectly and turn many of the more annoying ones around. This game is very story-driven, so if you like the vague, open-endedness of Stardew Valley, this isn't quite that. It's telling a story, and you're not forging your own throughout. Which isn't to say your choices don't matter - they really do - but there are events and forces and stories happening and you are part of them, not creating them. One of the things I love most about this game is that the small community isn't tight-knit and all buddy-buddy. In every other game of this type I've played, everyone is good friends, or at least always friendly, with a real community spirit. Escapism at its finest, absolutely, but very unbelievable!Wylde Flowers has actual character conflicts, where people just plain don't like each other. There are secrets, friendships, animosities, pretty much what you'd expect with a bunch of people. Also, people seem to interact with each other without your character being there to facilitate everything. I also like that you don't just give random things to people to increase friendship. No, you give FOOD, which makes PERFECT sense to me. You don't get to choose your character in this one - you are Tara Wylde - and I do wish there was a bit of character customization. I would love to be able to change my clothes and hair! But back to things I like - not every young, single person in this game is dateable. Some of them play for the other team or are plain not interested, and you can be best friends with them. I really like that feature.Speaking of identity, this game intended to and succeeded at being very LGBTQ+. In addition to straight, gay, and bi characters, there are also non-standard genders. Despite the realism of the game, the entire community is very positive about the LGBTQ+ characters, with any homophobia or transphobia being off screen and mentioned as historical issues with family. I like that magic is an important part of the game while keeping the farming/crafting element. As the High Priestess tells us, "Magic is important, but so is life. It's a balance," and the game commits to that hard.The game is also gorgeous. The graphics are delightful, everyone is voice acted and well, and the music is stellar. I have honestly opened my inventory to stop time but to have the music still playing. This game is absolutely fantastic. The story is logical, fantastical, and delightful, and even better, sometimes out of order! Sometimes, I found I stumbled across a story that didn't make sense - YET - much like in life. The characters are not all delightful - some are extremely aggravating - but that adds to the joy of the game. And even the "conflicting group" have many kind, wonderful, helpful people who have been hurt in the past and are just trying to make the best of their life. I cannot recommend this game enough. It might actually replace Stardew Valley as my favorite farming game, except that I'm not sure how replayable it is, given the story rich aspect. And (right now, anyway), this game has a demo! Download it and try it!

_childDocuments_.review: Wylde Flowers let me life out my fantasies of being a bisexual cottagecore witch in small-town America in *this* economy and I am living for it.Wylde Flowers paints a pastel, yet colorful haze of cheeriness and understanding on everything in life. It's not Stepford Wives fake but it's not completely 100% out of Uncanny Valley when everyone's problems are solved with few consequences wrapped up with a neat bow at the end of every day. This is not a game that only children will play, as there are jokes and concepts for adults too, but overall the tone is kept pretty light.Speaking of understanding, this game is notable for being a family friendly farming game with LGBTQ+ relationships. It features several lesbian relationships as well as a nonbinary AFAB character. Wylde Flowers may make some roll their eyes, but frankly I don't feel it's too much and it's refreshingly presented as Not A Big Deal. The characters are just people who are being themselves without fear of judgment. The Mayor's office may have a Pride flag flying at its front gates for some never-specified reason, but at the same time the characters make tongue-in-cheek jokes about things real-world small-town gays would like how small their Pride parade is.The characters may be a little stereotypical at times - there's characters of various nationalities and yes, the half-Japanese person *does* like gifts of sake and ramen as their favorite foods and yes, the Native American likes corn bread and succotash, why do you ask? - but there's reasons for that (you have to guess their favorite foods based on dialogue and background mostly) and overall it's okay to me. The characters pretty well written and enjoyable, engaging enough to keep me wanting to dip back in to check in with them. They're not too stereotypical overall. I learned a few things about other cultures and authentic dishes thanks to this game.As mentioned, the game does have some jokes for older players but I wish at times that it challenged me a little more in terms of difficulty. It's meant to be either universally accessible or a relaxing time for older gamers. I didn't feel pandered to or dumbed down though, so I think they successfully set out in what they attempted to do. If you don't feel like messing around with certain stuff such as the fishing minigame, there's a few toggles to make things even more relaxed.There's a lot of things you can do in Wylde Flowers and you unlock more by playing through the story. I'm currently in Fall, about to go to Winter and I have a fully decked out barn with chickens, cows, and sheep. One of my favorite details is that you can name the chickens colorful things like Chimken, Nugget, Fowlplay, or just Annabelle. You can similarly name the other livestock such as cows and sheep Peta, Cocoa, Pancho, Gus.. I could go on. It's pretty funny and the reaction you get from the guy who sells you the livestock had me amused.This is a farming game of course and there's a ton of things to grow per season. You can then refine some of those crops and make butter in your butter churn, cheese in a barrel, wine out of grapes, soy milk out of soy beans, oh and you can grow your own silk worm farm and sell the products for profit. I just wish the economy was more robust as the biggest profits you'll be pulling will be either from infamously cooking fish sticks (which now humorously has a toggle to turn on a 'fish stick embargo' added in a patch if you prefer more of a challenge) or later on, selling your livestock. It's up to you how you make your profit though and you can roleplay a vegan witch to make things more challenging, I guess. You'll just miss out on some achievements to craft all food items.Oh yeah, and you find out during the course of the story that you're a witch, so you can craft magic scrolls at your desk and brew potions in your cauldron. I wish the magic were a little more useful but I found myself using it especially when I was forgetful and let a plant wither. The added detail of being able to cast magic puts a fun spin on things but also adds more stuff you can craft for profit. There are many shops and items and you'd do well to get to know all of the shop owners.The story of Wylde Flowers is pretty decent and actually had me invested in the lives of these people at times. To my surprise, the game even gets pretty serious at times when it touches on themes such as illness and life and death. It made this world feel alive when characters changed and didn't stay entirely stagnant. This game's story sets it apart from many other farming games whose story is way more bare bones. You may find it cheesy at times to be fair but it's apparent that real effort was put into this game.I got the opportunity to playtest the game before it was released on Steam and the developers were really communicative when it came to finding bugs and other errors so I've spent a lot of time with this game. It's been a really nice, bug-free experience for the most part and anything we did find was addressed by the team.Overall I'd recommend Wylde Flowers a lot if you're a fan of farming games or story-rich games and like the themes presented here. I easily lost myself in "just one more night" of mining or farming or fishing many times and am really enjoying the time and effort put into it. I'd say it was released with a fair price.Check out my Curator  for more recommendations of casual indie games like this!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely, cozy game where you farm, fish, craft, do magic, find romance and more. It's about 40 hours for the main story and then another 20 hours of additional (but fewer) quests and achievement-chasing, if you're into that.I especially like that this game has some genre-defying elements, such as not using the 28-day-season calendar and not having a shipping box for selling items. It's also much more story driven than others in this genre. It's a lot of fun for fans of Stardew Valley, Coral Island, or witchy aesthetics.

_childDocuments_.review: So - after about half an hour of play time, the game crashed for me. BUT it also just released on steam today, so I will give that a pass. First impression? I like the game. It's definitely something I'd like to play through, but I am typically very slow with these kinds of games. The game is beautiful, in my honest opinion. There are a lot of bright colors - not hyper realistic, but beautiful. It's cozy, and cute, and I love the jokes in it. It's also very inclusive, which you don't see enough of in a lot of games. If you are a fan of things like Animal Crossing, Harvest Moon,  Story of Seasons, or My Life at Portia, I'm fairly certain you'd enjoy this game. On the more critical side, there are definitely some quality of life improvements that could be made. I wish I could rotate the camera/view, and I feel like that would make a lot of the movements feel more natural and easier to do. That is probably my biggest complaints, after 30 minutes of playing. I also don't know what caused the game to crash, but it was very suddenly, so I'm sure there's some things that need to be ironed out for a smoother gameplay experience. I also think further details with how certain gameplay mechanics function would be very beneficial, as some parts I felt like I was kind of wandering until I figured out what to do next. I look forward to seeing how this game develops, and seeing what other content may be coming. I truly hope that this game gets the love and attention it deserves, because I think it could be a big hit if it is given the right attention. As for now, I will continue to play this to relax, and follow any developments. I would also recommend it to my friends that enjoy games like this, even if it hasn't gotten a lot of attention yet. ~~Hayley AKA Roxanne
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: This game has me torn. On the one hand, the art style, animation, characters, story are all really great for this type of game.On the other hand, I can't help but feel that the quest line and general gathering/building/simulation aspects of the game could use work.As an example, you start out with a tiny plot of land to do your farming (which you need for cooking, gifts, quests, etc). The amount of materials you need to open up the larger lot is insane. Additionally, you need to build "garden boxes" with the same materials you need for the large garden plot. You'd think that maybe... just maybe after working hours to be able to unlock the large garden plot you would simply be able to garden, right? No. You still need to build garden boxes. I feel like it kind of says something when only 49% of players have the "achievement" of getting the bigger garden plot... I suspect most people give up before ever reaching it.My main takeaway is that it feels very grindy. With a lot of bottlenecks that lead to frustration.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! You get to learn your witchy heritage, cast spells, brew potions, run a farm, and hang out with great folks in Fairhaven. Easy to play and the graphics are lovely! I really like it as Fairhaven has a mix of ethnicities, inter-racial marriages, same sex couples and LGBTQ+ aspects to the game. With Fairhaven being small it really is a community oriented game that you don't have on games like this. I like how different people and lifestyles are represented. Some helpful tips for folks new to the game:1. Fish, fish, fish for money when starting out. After talking with Bruno and getting fishing rod fish everywhere as much as possible. You can sell the fish to Bruno and he pays very good. It also uses up much less energy than mining in the beginning. 2. Once you are able upgrade your rusty pickaxe mining becomes less taxing on your energy. You can have Natalia smelt the ore you mine down which you can then sell to her. Another good way to save up money.3. Plant, harvest and plant some more. Whatever season you are in plant and harvest as many of those crops as possible. Also be sure to harvest some of the wildflowers that grow specifically in that season. They most likely will not be available when it changes and there are some things you will not be able to cook or make. If I had ONE critique it would be to have a small wardrobe option. As in when I want to run around town or get my hands dirty on the farm I would not mind having a set of farming clothes to change into. And save my red dress outfit for bar nights at Damon's place.  Or have corresponding outfits to wear for each season.I am doing a full play through of this game on my YouTube gaming channel Mad Ferret Studios. Big shout out to Studio Drydock and all the creators who worked on this game! It is a delight to play and so well done! Especially since I grew up as a farm girl. :)

_childDocuments_.review: The storyline, the voice characters, the composed music - what is there not to love about Wylde Flowers! _childDocuments_.review: This might be my favorite game of 2022. It definitely isn't for everyone, but people who love cozy games NEED to at least play the free demo.The game is incredibly easy. Some people might not like how simple it is, but the beginner inclusiveness in this game is absolutely amazing. Even though there aren't any groundbreaking mechanics, I never found myself bored. I fully played through most every day of the year (except towards the very end when I had cheesed the game and made myself rich and I didn't need to worry about farming/mining), and I loved how the farming aspect didn't feel forced or rushed (You can farm/raise animals at the bare minimum if you find it boring).I only encountered a few minor bugs here and there, and the load times/transitions in this game worked really well. All-in-all it was a stellar performance.The real showstoppers in this game are the story and characters. The voice acting is superb, and really brought the town to life. I felt myself really feeling like I was friends with the villagers. They rarely repeated dialogue (except for some exceptions - looking at you Statue Ladies!) and I often found that I would spend all in-game day talking to different NPCs just to see what their thoughts were on any of the recent town events or gossip (I really loved the fact that they reacted differently to things that happened in the town - they didn't just repeat the same dialogue over and over)Did I mention the representation? Almost all of the villagers are either POC, queer, or both! I loved how diverse the game was, and to me, it handled this perfectly. I love seeing queer media that's not centered on queer trauma!In short, PLEASE play this game and support these developers. If you're on the fence, pick up the free demo and see if you like it (you will). I will be shouting its praises for a long, long time.

_childDocuments_.review: So, what is this game? It's about Tara, a young woman who comes to stay with her grandmother. Tara soon learns that she, like her grandmother, is a witch. The game-play revolves around Tara helping her grandmother around the farm. She also is asked to help others on the island, all of this in the form of quests, some of which advance the main story plot. Most of the quests involve Tara collecting things. That's where the sim part of the game comes in. You grow flowers and crops like corn, rice, etc. based on the season. You can mine ore, fish and gather/pick things growing around the island. There are hobbies you can do and things related to witchery for you to fuss with. All of these things are neatly woven into the plot. The nice part about that is that about the time you grow tired of something, the game introduces a way to make it less painful.The real charm of this game is in the voice acting. It's 100% voiced with a text overlay as well. You wander around meeting and interacting with people on the island. The more you talk to them, the more they like you and open up to you. You can even get married, divorced and remarried - back to the same person if you want. The game has all of that, but it's really a game about forming relationships more so than a dating sim. It's not a dating sim. There are no alternate endings.The story isn't epic but it appeals and it's well told. It's charming. The game art is colorful, playful. I did find myself rooting for certain characters and shaking my head at some others. It does check ALL of the boxes for diversity: cultural and sexuality.I'm happy that I bought this. For me it was 75+ hours of poking around the island. Like a good book, it was hard to put down and that is as good of an endorsement as I can give.

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking for a cozy game that wasn't monotonous, and I found that in Wylde Flowers. Just when you feel like you've done all there is to do, a new cut scene happens and you're off on a new set of objectives. Even after the game is technically 'over' and the credits roll, you can still play and there are still new things happening. This game really sucked me in, and I have really enjoyed playing it. I find myself repeatedly saying "Okay, I'll play just one more day (in game time) and then call it quits for today." before I actually stop playing hahaWylde Flowers is an adorable cozy sim game. I highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: Poor Sophia's diner must be built out of fishfingers I've sold her that many...I am a sucker for stardew/harvest moon/animal crossing type games, as well as a sucker for well written stories.Wylde flowers feels like a fusion of all of them PLUS MAGIC, and in the best way. It is positively a warm, wholesome, comforting hug in a game and I couldn't wait to get home and play it after a stressful day.If you expect this game to be just like Stardew and are expecting to be min-maxing your profits, you will be disappointed. Farming is definitely important in WF but it comes secondary to the story, you could just grow the crops you need for quests then ignore the rest, for me this is a massive plus as it gives way more freedom, but I know for others it may be a turn off.Now to talk about the best part of this game. The writing. All of the characters are different, but believably written, with their own quirks and interests. There are some heavy topics brought up in a tasteful  manner such as grief, loss, family estrangement, religion, gender dysphoria, sexuality, loneliness, bullying and so much more. The cast is inclusive, diverse and fully voice acted.The story and characters have been written in a way that I actually care about them, even the less likeable ones, all of them make mistakes or have flaws and I was always really excited to find out the next piece in their story. The overall main storyline is really well written and very sweet. It got me emotional with full on sobbing on more than one occasion, something that games haven't managed to do that often. I was proper sad when I realised I'd finished the main story!!The daily loop can get a bit repetitive, but I honestly didn't mind that much as the whole game just made me feel relaxed and happy.I would LOVE to see a DLC or a sequel to Wylde flowers, I want to learn even more about the beautiful island of fairhaven and it's witches that Studio Dryrock have built.Oh and you can adopt a cat called Cleocatra, instant 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so art style of this game is great, the story really draws you in and the voice acting is great. Now a word of advice for the devs the folks that play these types of games have a hard time leaving their save game and characters after they complete the main quest...so with that being said you may want to address the leaving the character in one season for the end of time if you choose to keep playing after the main quest.  Other than that this game gives so much of what you want in a game of this type and the fishing was the easiest ever.  I was so relieved to fish and not swear the whole time.  All in all this is a solid game.

_childDocuments_.review: Was hesitant to purchase as I've never played a narrative story driven game before. On a whim I bought it. So glad I did! All the positive reviews I read prior to playing are correct. The voice acting is amazing and brings so much life to the game. The music is calming and appropriate for each event and scene. The conversations with the npc's are not repetitive which is refreshing. The graphics are colorful, clean and well done. I love the way the camera zooms in during conversations, the cut scenes, and the way it pans across areas that are new to the player. This game is expertly created. It's like being part of a movie. Gathering, cooking, farming, mining it's all here too. There's diversity here represented by different races, cultures and orientation. Not something I personally look for in a game but it is very tastefully done. Each character has a complex life story that is revealed slowly to you as you interact with them. I'm enjoying the townsfolk very much. I also don't have a sense of humor whatsoever and don't laugh easily but this game broke that wall and had me laughing at some of the humorous things the townsfolk would say. Well done! Have a feeling I'm going to be sad when then main story is over. It's a game I'll wish I could keep playing with new content. Perhaps the devs may expand on the game in the future. I sure hope so. Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: Very cozy with very easy controls for players who need a break from more complex or fast paced games.  The story lines with each of the characters are incredibly sweet and adorable and have a surprising amount of depth to them.  All the characters are the shinning star of this cute game.   It addresses complex issues in an easily digestible and understandable format but doesn't shy away from rawness of emotions like the pain of grief, longing, betrayal, and even the growing pain of taking accountability for one's actions.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard for me to like a game, I'm extremely picky for some reason. Decided to give this a try during the summer sale and I am not disappointed. I am seven hours in and I really enjoy this game! I like the gameplay, I like that you can play using your mouse. The characters in the game are cute, so are the story lines. They have strangely satisfying voices. There's not too much grind, there's a hint of magic, which I usually don't like, but I can totally cope with it in this game. The game is not difficult to play, there's not a lot you need to figure out on your own. My boyfriend sometimes watches me play (we are in to parallel play) and so far we've laughed, we've cried, and we've really enjoyed Wylde Flowers!If I'd have to voice one thing that could have maybe been better, it's that you play a set character. It would've been nice if you could create your own. Though it doesn't bother me too much that you can't.Overall, I definitely recommend this game!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very nice and cute farming witchy game. Farming, crafting and even moving with spells and magic potions are the main activities in Wylde Flowers.You are an apprentice witch who must take care of the small town and even of several magic beings. The story is also very well written and somewhat exciting. Otherwise it's the usual fare of growing plants, mining, breeding animals and crafting. But, as I said, all the activities are very well integrated, almost like a puzzle, with the story.Pros:- beautiful graphics- magic spells and potion- magical creatures which are funny and interesting, also the town people have interesting personalities- infinite inventory- a way to minimize micro-management early in the game- a lot of content- cute- very good story, probably the best for a farming game- addictive- may modify the length of the dayCons:- hardly any; a little too slow in the beginning
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who loves farm-sim games, this was a no-brainer. But Wylde Flowers offers so much more. I found myself caring so much about the characters, in part because it's wonderfully voice-acted, more story-driven, and VERY inclusive. I was pleasantly surprised at how diverse the residents of Fairhaven were. Some of them even brought up festivities and other unique things of their culture. But also the characters feel so genuine. Without giving away any spoilers, the beginning of summer was so touching. Everyone reacted in a way that felt so honest to each of their previous experiences and personalities. As someone who has gone through what Tara went through, I felt so understood.Besides the great story-telling, this game is also aware that many farming-sim games can become overwhelming. So Wylde Flowers finds a way to make the gameplay more laid-back. For example, the fact that you can decide when summer begins was a huge game-changer for me. No more stressing about what crops can make it on time during a season. Plus the spells let you do more on a given day if you still care about efficiency.This is definitely my favorite game of the year. I play it a lot on my Steam Deck (and it works perfectly there, by the way). I cannot recommend it enough. Here's my first impressions:

_childDocuments_.review: Wylde Flowers is a unique story-driven game with farming and witchy elements. _childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: What an incredible surprise, this is the definition of a cozy game in my book. Such cute design, diverse characters, adorable story, it's amazing how much love and care was put into this game, It lacks several "stresses" from other similar farming games and improves on some annoying or repetitive parts from the genre, and it does this in a very innovative way. I am still struck by how much I liked it, I certainly did not expect to fall in love with it the way I did. Hope to play a lot more and will look forward to future projects from these developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: A witchy romp with a heavy story focus. I enjoyed my time with Wylde Flowers, but it's not quite the farming sim I expected it to be. The story was what kept me engaged, and the farming and crafting systems primary function seemed to gatekeep objectives that advanced the story. Spells, potions, and incantations felt limited in their use, again, primarily to gatekeep story interactions, however there were a few that I found myself regularly using. I was blown away at the voice acting in this game -- every line is voiced, and it works well with the diverse cast of characters. There were times that they continued to repeat the same few lines each day, but every time the story advanced, there was so much interesting dialogue and interactions to be found. "No wonder we're friends! We're both vindictive trash!"Overall, I'd recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: Such an amazing game! I've played 140 hours so far and still play almost every day.Pros: The quests keep me interested and engaged. There are a lot of different ways to play and replay the game. I also love how diverse and inclusive the characters are - so many different stories and backgrounds which is amazing for a story- and character-driven game. Cons: Can't stop playing!
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game a week ago and then clocked into it like it was my full-time job - now at 50hrs+ and counting. I am a big fan of crafting/social sims and this one might become my personal favourite. I'm not finished, but I have to give it praises for what I've experienced so far. Here are my highlights:Every character is fully voice acted and they each have an incredible amount of novel dialogue. Whether it's commenting on a recent event or telling you a story about their family, their culture, or their neighbour's favourite food, you'll usually hear something new and interesting. One of my main complaints with "social sim" or "dating sim" games is that you often have to skip through the same dialogue to gain "hearts" that get you to the cut scenes. In Wylde Flowers, I talk to people every single day... for enjoyment. I could have them at full hearts and I still talk to everyone every day.  Of course there is some repetition, the since events occur so often and usually there is new dialogue after each event. If you want to explore the entirety of the map every day, pick up every item, talk to every character, craft clothes, explore the mine, get a drink at the bar and then go chill with your coven you can. In one day! I love the timing options, relaxed is my favourite but normal and challenging are there to save you if the day becomes slow. I love finding new recipes, crafting them and then giving them away only to hear an unexpected story when I learn it's one of their favourite meals! I love the whole process of making clothes, and just how cute a lot of Tara's outfits are. I realized I had become one of those rich homesteading wives on tiktok when I walked outside my toolshed in a newly completed homespun "vanilla chai" wool sweatsuit with a silver diamond necklace and matching ring. I'm not even a material girl in real life but holeee, Tara was looking like she ran the whole island that day. I appreciate that money is almost an optional part of this game. Once you understand what your main source of easy income is, money is no longer a barrier. I was afraid that it would break the fun, but truly, the compost situation, not realizing the true value of cotton your first spring (smh) and the rarity of some materials keep it from maxing out too much too early.  I'd say once you figure out the mechanics, the upgrading is very well paced. I haven't even touched on how dense the story feels. In comparison to other games of this genre, it feels jam packed with events every season so far (I just made it to first winter). I think the voice acting adds this vibrancy and robustness to the story that is non-existent in other farming/crafting games. The story itself clearly has me fully invested in the lives of these characters. I realized just how invested I had gotten when after a certain event went down in summer I stopped talking to people on the island I had been speaking to every single day since day one! I was actually upset at them, I was cussing out my screen! No more free fruit punch and pumpkin spice lattes, I'll tell ya what!!!It should go without saying but games are a thousand times better when gay and trans people can exist as complex people. Francis and Angus don't have to be hypersexualized to be gay, they can just love each other. I love it when they don't agree, or don't seem to like each other in certain moments. Kim sometimes does make their non-binary identity a large portion of their personality - but honestly, that's most non-binary people I know so it feels very accurate (im trans relax yall). I love that Amira flirts with you even though she is your doctor and it's wholly inappropriate (lol I forgive you Amira there is literally 3 viable people to date I get it). I love that there's even a lesbian who isn't witchy at all, and actually talks down to you about science! I wish there was a trans fem, but of course, I just pretend Tara is a trans fem duh. <3 Lastly, as a strange older gay man who one day dreams of living alone in the woods because the time for love has passed and now there is only [redacted to keep spoiler free]... thank you for representing my future self in this game. I wish I still had the hair for such an exquisite pony, but maybe I'll just have to get a wig. Anyway, I love this game. I'm already planning my villain arc for when the new animals drop end of April. I love Fairhaven and all the little people they created to live in this world.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: Wylde Flowers is a cute and idyllic game filled with beautiful locations, fun and interesting people, and a plot reminiscent of a Hallmark television show. You play as Tara who moves from the big city to a small island town to take care of your grandmother, and to push the restart button on your own life. While you are on the island of Fairhaven you will uncover plots, secrets, new locations, and you'll engage with a fully voiced cast that helps immerse you into a magical and carefree world. Sit back, relax, and let the simple splendor of Fairhaven take you away on a journey that could only happen to a young and beautiful white woman.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: While there are plenty of redeeming qualities about this game, the way time progresses is absolutely infuriating and wildly unbalanced.  It feels like they took one of the worst aspects of Stardew Valley and found a way to make it even worse.   Day/night and energy works similar to Stardew, in that you can either eat food or go to sleep until the next day to replenish it.  You can even choose to make your day move slower or faster.  But each store on map has different hours and randomly open and closed on different days of the week.  If you set your clock too slow, you have to wait around for stores to open and you might not have that much to do if you already used up all your energy.  To make matters worse, you can only sell items to specific merchants.  So fish has to be sold to the fish guy, gems have to be sold to the jeweler, etc.  Just looking to sell stuff?  You've got to run door to door, hope the right merchants are open at that moment and just run around trying to figure out what you can sell to who, if they're even open today at all. But wait, it gets worse.  So you've done all you want to for the day, you can go to bed, right?  Nope.  All of the coven stuff (this is a witch game, after all) takes place at night.  So now you have to wait around until night time for that.  And naturally the coven meets on the farthest away location from your house...so after you're done meeting with the coven, you've got to run alllllll the way back home.  You might enjoy the game if you really like running back and forth for absolutely no reason because you can't quick travel home.  I'm not sure how many days I made it, but I got absolutely sick of the constant running back to my house, waiting around for nighttime, not being able to sell stuff because its Sunday and most of the stores are closed.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: The game is cute with some of the farming sim type elements you would expect, but I feel it is lacking certain ones that keep it engaging. I found it frustrating that there was no visible calendar to tell you the length of seasons, even which season you were in, only the day of the week is shown but it is easy to lose track of how far into the season you are.There is no option to change the main mc's outfit from as far as I played and while her outfit is cute, the city look while farming can ruin the immersive elements. Gifts for townspeople seems to just be meals. which limits options for gifting and also makes gifting rather time heavy. Overall the game is definitely cute and while I was looking forward to it, the lacking features lowered my interest in playing a couple of hours in.

_childDocuments_.review: I saw this game by happenstance as part of Wholesome Games Direct some months ago. Honestly, I wasn't sure what to expect- But the more I played it the more I loved it. The characters are compelling and lovable, though you might not like every single one, they're all written with care and well developed. The motivations they have for things are real and tangible, their fears and hopes are relatable. You get to know them, you get to see them struggle, you get to help them thru their struggles...The farming mechanics are as solid as you expect them to be and the story and feature reveal is paced very well, a lot of times I was wishing for an easier or faster way to accomplish a task mere days before the game would introduce exactly what I'd been hoping for. Small spoilers, but some examples: in the beginning you feel pressed for time, like you simply arent fast enough to get everything done. One of the first abilities you will get speeds your walking pace to a faster running pace, allowing you to do SO MUCH more and instantly alleviating the pressure you were beginning to get fatigued by. Towards the later game, you start to understand how tedious watering dozens of plots every day in perpetuity will get, and like magic you are introduced to your automation features and how to use them... The pacing is so good, it feels like every time I wanted something from the game it gave it to me. The only exception would be when certain wild forage wont spawn! There are tons of recipes to cook, a whole catalog of outfits to collect and craft, a leveling system for both friendship and the shops in town to reward you for selling things to each various shopkeeper, characters have REAL backstories and concerns so you actually care to check in with them, plus super cute animals and tons of secrets to find! As a farming game fan since harvest moon 64, I cried multiple times during this game, mostly due to story reasons- I cried the longest during the credits, cuz I knew I could never experience it for the first time again... Do yourself a favor. Get this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: This reminds me of Stardew Valley in the best of all possible ways. You're tasked (like in Stardew) with managing a farm for your elderly grandma, befriending the townsfolk, and helping them with...whatever.What makes it maybe even more appealing to me are the updated graphics and fairly strong main plot line. (Stardew had one...but  Wylde Flowers is far more plot focused.) I also like that the seasons only change when you choose to make them, thus saving many harvests.  The graphics are also more modern and there's full voice acting (which is really well done and adds a lot!)I think there's somewhat less to do (20 vs. some unfathomable number of levels to the mine...), but personally I'd prefer less to do and a better story.Also, IMO charmingly (although probably in other's less so), the island is incredibly welcoming to people of all gender identities and sexual orientations. (As well as, possibly, religion. When I found one of the characters was Jewish, I nearly screamed "BINGO!" because the creators seemed almost at pains to make sure that they'd covered every possible racial, sexual and religious identity.) I think most players will see themselves in at least one of the characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not that far into the game yet but I can already tell that it was made with a lot of love. This farming sim is more story driven than any in it's genre I've played and it does an outstanding job at that. The characters are fully voice acted, which often can be a hit or miss. Wylde Flowers does this so well that it truly gives depth and personality to the characters. This makes me feel that talking to the townsfolk is a treat, not a chore.Apart from fun and gossip the people in town will also share their worries and fears. The devs don't shy away from topics like dealing with loss, coming out, loneliness, etc. This is beautifully done and I found myself to really come to care about the people that live in this town.Now for the farming... it's very slow, especially in the beginning. Resources are also scarce. That said, after a few days I found this to be more relaxing than constantly having to run around on the farm. It gives you time for foraging, fishing and of course, talking to the towns people.Fishing is easy and relaxing. You don't have to play a mini game. You just get a fish on your hook, click on it and you're done. Just like your other basic tools, your fishing rod will be given to you by someone in the town.One of the best features regarding farming and collecting is that you never have to worry about inventory. You don't need to craft 100 chests to keep your stuff in. It all fits and stays in your endless backpack, neatly organized, thus saving you much hassle.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this because it is so unique and all the dialogue is voiced which is kind of bananas??? it is hella relaxing and made for a great game to play before bed. super comfy, hanging out in a small town living your best witch life and eventually being able to sleep with a werewolf man. also was impressed with the lgbtq representationhowever it did not satisfy my need for farming. the farming is way too slow. it is not a farming game, but rather the illusion of a farming game. too many moments were spent foraging for resources only to come up short and be unable to continue my farming progress. I am aware that there was an update focused on farming just recently, but I was unable to interact with these elements within the first five hours.EVERYTHING is slow. but the slow pace is very much deliberate. the game is meant to be taken at a relaxed pace.I will recommend with the caveat not to expect farming. expect a young woman living her best witch life as she rediscovers herself and potentially finds love.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so unique out of all the farming games out there! There's incredible voice acting for every character and you never get the same dialogue twice, also because everyone always has something new to say it was very easy to befriend the townsfolk. The farming was very simple which was a nice break from other farming sims where farming gets a bit extreme, but the main interests were the spells and potions and crafting you could do. Being a witch is a lot of fun, especially since you can explore further into the magical world. But finally, the best part of the game was the story which was absolutely phenomenal. There were so many cinematics throughout the game but some long ones at the end and the ending itself left you satisfied and smiling. This is definitely not your typical farming game and I highly recommend it for the witch experience and for the story alone.

Even though it touches on some sensitive topics, I haven’t felt this immersed and cozy in a game since Stardew Valley. _childDocuments_.review: Great game, lovely story, cosy atmosphere. If you like rune factory, or want a Stardew-esque game with more story, then this is perfect.Positives:- Cosy vibes- Cute, witchy story- Loveable farm animals- Nice music- NPCs who actually feel very fleshed out as people (not just carbon copies of each other)- Diverse options of marriage candidates- Good accessibility optionsCould be improved:- No disability representation amongst NPCs- The game almost forces you to slow down in some quests while you wait for things to grow (mulberry trees and bees come to mind), which could be good but just verges on annoying in some placesI would definitely recommend this game as one to play if you are a cosy gamer and like farming sims with a twist.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really solid cozy farming sim with all the bells and whistles that you’d expect to be present.A huge standout to me is the fact that the entire game is voice acted! Very unique and hard to pull off in these types of game but I think it works great here.The witch elements and story are really fun, they provide you with another avenue to focus on if the normal farming gameplay gets a little old. The potions and spells really help give the player some agency over their direction.I would’ve liked a few more romanceable characters. The layout of the town is a little frustrating, sometimes I felt that the distance was unnecessary between each end of the map. I think if the town was more circular and had more depth, it would’ve solved this problem.Overall, the asking price is fair and if you like stardew-likes, you’ll feel right at home.

_childDocuments_.review: Great. Not one dud out of the cast, and the main character, Tara, especially is performed with a nice mix of charm and awkwardness that really lends to likability. I also really enjoyed the voice performances for Sophia, Shelby, and Otto. But truly, I like them all. There were one or two lines I heard so far in my ten-hour playthrough that sounded tinny and low-quality, but I'm surprised I haven't heard more considering a lot of the voice lines were probably recorded during COVID lockdown. Each of the characters you meet in Fairhaven have their own rich backstories and complex relationships with the other inhabitants of the island. At first, I thought the only characters with real "work" done for them would be the datable people of the island. But as I talked to everyone throughout the game days, I realized that EVERY character has their own worries, dreams, or drama going on in their inner lives. Just like -- GASP -- real people! I've grown to like every character in Fairhaven, and I especially like the dynamic between Tara and Thomas. The story is a bit predictable, but it's made engaging by the stellar cast and subplots that really rope you in. There are some story beats that got to me emotionally and made me actually cry once or twice. Not a dramatic, epic, world-threatening saga by any means, but if that's what you were expecting, then go play a JRPG. Wylde Flower's story fits right in with the cozy-yet-emotional-and-secretly-not-so-secretly-involving-magic plots we see in other life sims. This is one of the few games that I actually noticed and appreciated the cleverness of the sound effects. Like the game itself, every little bloop and blop is quirky and oozing with charm. It almost reminds me of 60s classic sitcoms like I Dream of Jeannie or Bewitched! The music is great as well. Nothing I would play on loop for weeks on end, but enjoyable to listen to in the moment and, again, fits right in with that magical charm. The farming mechanics in Wylde Flowers aren't too demanding. You get to choose when the seasons change, so you can take as much time as you'd like growing your seasonal crops, and you don't have to worry about soil quality or preparing for storms or other strategic mechanics that more involved farming games have. You also won't be growing endless fields of cash crops any time soon, as you're required to build each plot separately. This is never really frustrating, however, as the game's pace matches the simple, relaxing cycle of farming. With a bit of patience and planning, you won't run into stressful farm management.The implementation of magic is a unique twist to what would be an otherwise vanilla farming sim. The magic system is, in the beginning, just a helpful way to boost growing speeds or crop yield. But as you progress, you'll also be able to perform more powerful spells such as freezing time. I haven't gotten too far in the magic system yet since the game makes sure you're comfortable with its other mechanics first, but I'm excited to see what else magic adds to the experience as it looks like the developers really wanted the player to have fun with it.The progression of the game itself rewards each little step and makes you feel fulfilled no matter what area of the game you choose to focus on. I'd say what shines the most is the amazing, diverse cast of characters that you can tell the developers really poured their heart and souls into. Wylde Flowers is quickly becoming one of my favorite farming sim games, and as a long-time lover of farming/life sims, it's wonderful to see a recent game of this genre that still holds the heart and care that made me fall in love with these games in the first place.

_childDocuments_.review: The game play is familiar, but solid. No mechanics are new(so far that i have experienced), but they work together well. Being able to use magic to expedite certain aspects and interactions feels natural. Where this game shines for me and makes me give it a hard recommend is a mix of the characters and their voice acting. The non-binary character talking about their acclimation to the town, how characters reference your actions with other characters. How (so far anyway) no one is just one dimensional. I can relate to them and their interactions. It really feels like conversations as a non straight person I have had myself. Guarded, but leaving openings to allow others in, but slow to really open that door. Other townsfolk giving insight as to why another character acts the way they do......it all really REALLY works. It isn't a game that let's you play as a Joanne every woman, but it does an amazing job of putting you into the world and caring about it. The complete voice over really sells it as well. The inflections, the hesitations, they all add to it in an amazing way. It is much easier to relate to these people and want to help them because they aren't just asking for you to do a fetch quest....you get to KNOW why the butcher wants to make more Vegan options and why other characters ARE the way they are. It isn't stardew, but that is okay. It is something entirely else and i love it.For the negative I feel like the controls are a bit twitchy on controller sometimes. When you have multiple things close to each other and you want to check the status of like...a beehive, you risk plucking your flowers instead. I haven't had many bugs that i couldn't attribute to my alt tab life(it pauses on tab btw <3). Sometimes when you go to pick up an item instead you perform a chopping action on a nearby tree which can be a problem if you are measuring your energy, but those are really small gripes for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Wylde Flowers is a tough one to pin down, I can't not recommend it because it gets so, so much right, but describing how much it gets right without spoilers or rambling is another thing. I think the easiest way to describe this game is Stardew but more story focused and with magic. Yet, at the same time, I think that'd honestly be doing this game a disservice because it ignores the powerful themes and wonderful character writing at the very core of this game.Because, for a game about farming and witches, the heart of this game has nothing to do with either of those. Instead, players are thrown into a rich world with so many secrets and drama to become invested in without going too dark and ruining the relaxed mood of the game. This game comes off as so simple and cutesy on the outside, but I constantly found myself surprised, conflicted, and thrilled by all the world building and twists this fantastical island had to offer! Fairhaven felt alive to me. Not only did the town itself have many secrets so wonderfully woven into the existing witchery, but so did all of the characters each with their own surprising amount of importance to this tale.The game puts you right in the middle of this, giving you and the other characters plenty of ways to react to the world through dialogue, relationship levels, and spells. Characters will react to current events, remember how you helped them or other characters, give hints and pieces of dialogue about how their businesses or relationships are going, and even come to you for help from time to time. As I became closer to the characters, it really felt like they were confiding in my character and letting me take more of a peek into their piece of the world, and it was hard to not do this for multiple characters, as everyone has stakes in the mysteries of this island. Even when I completed the base game, every day felt full of opportunities because the characters were just so colorful with their own lives, struggles, and biases, and the game/story really lets them explore this. I know this might sound small but, its been a while since I've played a game that was actually able to make me forget I was walking up to an NPC and just hitting the "continue" button. Add a diverse cast to this with an impressive amount of cultures, races, and orientations, and you have a cast I'll be revisiting time and time again in the future. Speaking of the story, I was just absolutely blown away by how this "farming game" used this trope as such a good vehicle for mystery. Although the description may make it seem this way, this isn't just "move into a farm and become a witch" this is "I had no idea I was a witch and now suddenly I'm a part of a coven and every night I keep learning more and more about this magical part of the island", and I can't say more without spoiling it, but if that doesn't hook you, I don't know what will. The story is oddly relevant, using the conflicting forces of the witches and a religious order to discuss themes of discrimination, and prejudice, and through the town's history, even sometimes goes into themes such as death and loss. Only a few of the characters are completely hate-able, and even then there's so much nuance  to their situations and why everyone has the views that they do that its difficult not to hear them out. Every twist made me see the characters and the world in an entirely new way, and I was all in for it. Of course, it doesn't hurt that this all works so smoothly within the gameplay. Leveling up my relationships with characters was genuinely fun because I was rewarded with special dialogue and cut scenes (all the voice acting is amazing, but they really put in the emotion for these scenes), giving gifts isn't necessary but it can be so satisfying to discover the character's favorites and see all the little bits of dialogue they have for each item. Your tools can be upgraded and, unlike some games, it doesn't feel like its just for show and genuinely makes salvaging for materials a lot easier. There are so many options for getting money that, unlike when playing Stardew Valley, it didn't feel like I was being pigeon holed into one method or constantly being strangled out of my money as I was able to earn it back soon after and kept more as my resources increased. There's of course your crops, but also raising animals, fishing, creating products such as food, drinks, potions/spells, candles, and many more, and so on and so forth. But, through all of this, it feels as if the game actually values your time, giving you spells and potions to speed up certain processes, help you get certain resources, etc. The game wants you to play it in the way you find fun and relaxing, and it is so, so refreshing to be able to play a game, especially a modern, cozy farming sim and collector game where I didn't feel as if I was having its version of "calm" dictated over me.That being said, this game did not just throw "cottogecore" into the description for the sake of sales. All the things I said above are true, the game can cover some heavy topic matters, and all the characters certainly have their flaws, along with the typical fantasy mayhem one would expect. But at the end of the day, this game is . It wants to make you say "aw" at the characters, and give an even bigger "AW" at your cute little farm animals and even cuter romantic partner. It seeks to give you both the sensation of curling up in your cabin home with a warm cup of tea while also letting you do and see cool magic stuff that is thrilling but with a safety within the overall feeling of the game. This absolutely shows in the adorable art style, the dialogue, character relationships and romance, and the story line. Yes the story has great twists and turns that I think a lot of audiences can enjoy, but if you're the type to gag at overly sentimental pieces or get beyond annoyed when games encourage you to slow down and smell the roses, you're probably going to find this game more pretentious than cool. This review probably didn't scratch the surface of all the unique gameplay elements, magic, and story this game has to offer, but let me sum it all up with this. If you played Stardew Valley but really wished there was more focus and development as far as the characters go, you'll love this game. If you really want a witch story that is cool but keeps the cute elements of a farming sim, you'll adore this game. If you want a farming sim or witch sim with a deep story and good world building, and don't mind the former elements, you'll really, really love this game. Overall I'd recommend it to those who want a relaxing little world to escape to, but also have an interest in stories, relationship sims, and quirky magical elements. This game is just super charming, and I plan to revisit it even when I finish all the current after game content.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my gosh, I am just absolutely obsessed with this game! The story is so creative and beautiful, and honestly, after being tired of the usual farming sims, this one has completely blown me away. The adorable aesthetics, fun gameplay, and lovable characters are all fantastic! The best part? The interactions are super user-friendly—you can play the whole game using just the mouse! This is a game-changer for my mom, who usually shies away from gaming because she finds it a bit confusing. But she absolutely loves this game! She still can't figure out how to leave a review, so just think of this as a double thumbs up from both of us! _childDocuments_.review: You can feel all the love that was put in the making of this game, so many positive things about it. _childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game, but there's too much that rubs me the wrong way. The voice acting is annoying (there should be an option for text only), the graphics feel juvenile, and the gameplay itself feels very basic, like I'm checking things off a To Do list to progress a visual novel. Except in a visual novel, choices matter, whereas after four hours, I'm still on a linear story line. It seems like this game has taken elements of Stardew Valley and My Time in Portia, and given it a witchy twist, but not it a way that feels compelling or fun, at least to me. _childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best farm sim/life sim games I ever played, and it's strongest points can be summarized in three paragraphs:- The characters are amazingly written, unique and it feels good to interact with them daily, in quests or on the overall plot! The game being fully voice acted makes it even better, and even the character animations, things like the way they walk and move, are very perky and unique to each one of them <3- The magic side of the game is very well integrated in the farming mechanics and it feels very fun to be a farming witch. Fantasy life simulators aren't the most common thing, and even though this game doesn't have combat, it was nice seeing how the non-mundane aspects of the game helped with common goals and objectives.- Back to characters, but now something that deserves it's own spot on the list, there's a HUGE diversity in the cast, main and support. Ethinic diversity, sexual orientation diversity, the game was flavorful even in the cooking aspect, there were recipes for brazilian food, even CAIPIRINHA! It feels like the developers did a lot of research and had a lot of consultancy from people from lots of different countries!This game is a masterpiece for anyone who loves cozy, narrative oriented life/farm sims, and I can't wait to check the next game from Studio Drydock!!
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: This really just is a wonderful game. The farming mechanics run smooth, the game has such a vibrant and likeable cast and a wonderful storyline, and is it's just all around a lovely and relaxing experience. It's hard to say that Wylde Flowers does anything different for the genre, but it does everything you want from a farming game extremely well.It initially took me so long to play because the art style wasn't my style (a friend of mine said it looks like one of those free-to-play mobile games at a first glance), but it's so easy to lose yourself to the world once you settle in. A high recommend for all the cosy, farming sim lovers out there!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is exceptional. The writing is some of the best I've seen in any video game. The characters feel so realistic and well-developed, and they react to events that happen in the game and your actions in a way that makes them feel alive. It is a joy to get to know Fairhaven and the people in it (including Tara!). The narrative is definitely the standout feature of this game for me, but the mechanics are also quite cute and fun. It feels great to use magic to get quality of life improvements or solve puzzles, and I love how the quests are always accessible with one button press. Additionally, the fact that you control the turning of the seasons and can change the game speed clock means that you never have to feel stressed out about making the most of your time. Just hang out and do your best!PS: This has the cutest petting animal animations I've ever seen. My favorite is the baby cows. <3

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent Life/Farm Sim Game-------------------------------While perhaps not as re-playable as Stardew Valley (once the main story quest line is done, the game is pretty much over save for a few post-credits quests), Wylde Flowers should definitely be in the library of every life/farm sim game fan.The actual farming portion of Wylde Flowers is a bit anemic, with limited options for planting location as well as number of available seeds; however, this game shines in personality.It shines like a supernova.In terms of story, character types and especially the voice acting, Wylde Flowers deserves to be in the same best-of lists as Grim Fandango, BioShock and the Monkey Island games.Did I mention the voice acting? While none of the cast seem to be immediately recognizable names, each one of them submits a stellar performance, breathing so much life, humor and even pathos in the 3D rendered computer characters, that they deserve to be cast in non-gaming animation roles. Even the child NPCs are believable and sound like children, not child actors or adults speaking in a squeaky voice to invoke prepubescence.It was actually player character Tara's vocal performance that convinced me to stop playing the demo and purchase the game.Any criticisms I have are greatly, greatly outweighed by the overall quality and obvious love and care everyone involved in this game brought to it, and even though I began my review lamenting how Wylde Flowers is pretty much over once you get to the credits (when compared to games like Stardew Valley that offers a near-infinite amount of playtime via farm layout experimentation), I still put close to 90 hours into it, making this game very cost-effective.My wife watched me play for a couple of hours and bought her own copy. She even reached the end before me and immediately started a new game, while I sent a gift copy to my daughter who also enjoys games like this.I cannot recommend this game enough. It has been one of the best games I've played in years.If anyone doesn't like this game, that's entirely their problem. Not Wylde Flowers.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy so much about this game. It's my current hyperfixation. In particular I really enjoy: racial and cultural diversity of characters; inclusion of social issues in a really smooth, sweet way; the voice acting is phenomenal; little details and accuracy in the animations (look at how the chickens walk! also the onions actually grow blossoms like real life)I wanted to share that I do think a bit of a weak spot in the game is the audio environment, in a few ways. In contrast to the visuals and the animation, the soundtrack overall misses the mark for me. Some areas like the Gloaming and Ravenwood, I would say are a success. Otherwise, I find the soundtrack in most other places annoying, or unnoticeable.Other cozy farming type games like Animal Crossing or Harvest Moon, the soundtracks really hit that sweet spot of subtle but catchy - they blend in enough to not be a distraction, but I'll still find myself humming them after I've played. In Wyldeflowers, some of the transitions between soundtracks are sudden and jarring enough that I notice while playing. Other times, I'm playing only to realize I can't hear any music at all. Or, I realize that I CAN hear it but it just doesn't "fit". So far none of the soundtrack has been enjoyable enough that I find it reaches that "earworm" status where I'm whistling it afterwards.With some tweaking to the way the soundtrack "flows" as you play and move through spaces, it could be enough to elevate it. For me this doesn't apply for the sound effects and notification sounds; I think they did a great job there. Appropriately satisfies the dopamine craving. :) Other point of note; the volume on some characters dialogue is a bit off. When I'm speaking with Natalia I feel like I need to turn the PC volume down - you're playing and everything is chill then you talk to her, and suddenly it's like when you hit an ad on Youtube. On the opposite end, when I talk to Parker I find I need to turn the volume up to hear him! Something about his audio just doesn't have the same clarity as the others. This is all small beans for an overall excellent game bound to become one of my favourite titles. On most games it wouldn't be worth mentioning. But with the standard Wyldeflowers has set in so many other areas, with the awards it has won and the recognition it has, I'd really love to see this 98% awesome game tweak a few little things with the soundscape to really hit 100%.I waited to purchase on sale which happens often, but honestly it is more than worth the full price!

_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: For the first time in ages I'm not having to look up game guides or tips and tricks to figure out how something works or what I need to do next.There is a clear cut story to follow, both with the town, the witches and each NPC, but it's not in your face nor do you have to do "THIS RIGHT NOW" type of gaming. The story line is linear but the game play is not. Yes you have to do certain things to complete tasks/farming/crafting/potions/spells, but unlike some games, you are able to do those in any way or order that strikes your fancy. You can talk to each NPC as much or as little as you want to. Just realize that you very well might be leaving part of the story line on the floor if you shy away from any single NPC , for whatever reason.I'm not thrilled that the game devs decided to add Woke to the mix, however, as much as I personally am not enamored of that choice, it was done in a way that you get the point but it's not in every single aspect of the game. I'm all for people making their own choices, and in this game you can. The above being said I will say this about dialog choices ... The devs have given players a wide range of replies to every single interaction. That is the #1 reason I continued to play the game.  If you want to be mean spirited in your replies, that choice is there, but so are generosity, kindness, thoughtfulness and even little quips of wisdom.Do not be afraid to try something.  Yes your choices have an impact on your game play, but I have yet to find myself boxed into a corner like many story lines or quest adventures out there.I bought this at full price literally hours before the summer sale ( I know, I'm so impatient sometimes).I'm glad that I did, especially if it means helping the devs with future content.Given the limitations of the game, there are 2 things I would love to see changed or added onto.  1. Altering your house, especially around 30 hours in.  And having unique quest rewards to decorate with. Or being able to change the outside look of your house/barn/chicken coop.2. Having more items to pick up/find or discover. They did a brilliant job of ways to find recipes. For everything.The random items that you pick up seem seriously sparse. I'm afraid to sell much since a number of times I've just sold something and the very next quest calls for that exact item. Which then you might have to wait for the correct season to find it, or the shop that sells it randomly to have it.The immersive voice acting is great. Click through the dialog if you don't want to read each and every line. But don't just rush through everything. You might miss that little extra thing that makes you go "AHA!" or even miss a favorite food of someone's being mentioned. Highly recommended for fans of  Stardew Valley, Dinkum, My Time at Portia or the like.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, witchy farming sim where you play as Tara, who has moved onto her Grandmother's farm. Very easy and straightforward to play and the game gives plenty of hints and holds your hand quite a lot. But even if you prefer a more challenging game, this game is worth it for its story. Lots of twists and interesting storylines. The characters are great and also fully voice acted, and the island feels very lively. The game includes romance, but no character customisation since you play as Tara (). You have an unlimited inventory which is a bonus, and tools automatically switch. You start off with stamina which hinders what you can get through in early game but you will soon build this up. The day speed is easy to toggle in the main menu, and I frequently switch between normal and relaxed. Very fun, easy going game with a great story.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers
