_childDocuments_.review: I have a love-hate relationship with this game. It does a lot of things amazingly well and let me enjoy myself over longer stretches of time, but there's also a bunch of things that really ruined my mood. Most people won't have a problem with the stuff that bothered me most though. - The well-written and believable characters that you can get to know in daily snippets and occasional cut scenes- The absolutely fantastic voice acting that really brings them to life- The sense of humour, some of the characters (including the main) often cracked me up- The way the game deals with serious issues like loss, and with queerness and being different in general- The engaging fantasy story that goes way deeper than I would have expected. It creates a sense of urgency and danger sometimes, but you can still take your time without negative consequences and your character can't be harmed. - The pleasant visuals, especially of the places you'll discover later on ( one of the prettiest places I've seen in a game)- The atmospheric music and sound design- Oh yeah, the actual farming sim and crafting aspects were quite satisfying too (apart from some resource spawns being too scarce/random for about the first half of the game and farming becoming irrelevant during the last quarter)- The , and especially the way it's portrayed as a hierarchy from friendship to marriage that makes friendship look inferior and marriage as the ultimate goal in life- That weird American-style dating stuff where if one of my supposed best friends asks me to have dinner together and I say anything other than "absolutely not" then apparently I'm in love and agreed to a date. And while it's great that the game tries to be so inclusive, a lot of queer people have non-traditional views on relationships. -  being portrayed as cool and helpful (gives a boost to magic...), and the characters who don't drink as boring and literal antagonists. The bar doesn't even offer a single soft drink or alcohol-free beer as an alternative. This is such a bizarre choice especially considering this game would be awesome for kids and teens otherwise. On top of that, a lot of queer people have addiction problems (because mental health suffers from being treated worse than "normal" people etc.) and this game is full of stuff that might give cravings to recovering alcoholics. ...There actually turned out to be a recovering alcoholic later in the game, and another character is shown to possibly quit drinking. Which is great, but it was surprisingly half-baked compared to the game's usual quality. And the rest of the content makes it seem like it's just a storyline  and not  someone struggling with alcoholism. Plus according to achievements so far most people don't even get to this point in the game. - For an otherwise cozy game, there's an awful lot of , and for an otherwise so inclusive game there's little consideration for people who are sensitive to that. Here in Europe a LOT of younger and especially queer people are vegetarians/vegans, and in parts of Asia it's a common tradition. In this game you can avoid having your farm animals slaughtered and you may not be required to keep animals at all. But you have to catch and obviously (though off-screen) kill a squid and several fish for the main story, you're supposed to prepare a meal with fish, the "date" I stumbled into was a forced non-vegetarian dinner, you get raw slabs of meat as gifts... Every time something like that came up it ruined my mood. Not to mention that if you don't want to catch and sell lots of fish then you'll have a much harder time making money. Even if it's "not real" it reminds me of real life and for me killing animals is just not a nice and cozy activity that I want to deal with. I guess I'm spoilt by other games (, , ...) where fishing and animal ingredients are fully optional. - At least the way I played it, the pacing was sometimes off, there were continuity errors (at least one major one and a lot of small ones) and there was a stretch towards the end when the game just dragged on without any incentive to continue the regular gameplay loop while waiting for the story to progress. It did have a pretty exciting climax, but then there were a few in-game days when I was confused about whether the story was over now or what I was supposed to do to trigger the final scene and credits. (You can continue playing indefinitely, apparently with a few new things happening too.) If I'd known about the animal stuff in particular, I probably wouldn't have bought the game. Do I regret playing it? I'm not sure really. I did have many hours of good fun with it, but then again if I'd spent that time and money on another game then I might have had about as much fun without all the stuff that was disappointing and off-putting for me in this game. Then again, the good stuff is SO good... Knowing what I know now, maybe I should have left it unfinished when I started to get fed up and watched a stream of the dramatic happenings towards the end. All in all I'm left with the impression that Wylde Flowers caters to fairly conventional straight women who want to feel open minded (the female main character isn't supposed to be a self insert but it kind of IS imo). Not that there's anything wrong with that necessarily, and this game truly does a great job at it. * * * If you like chill and story-driven games, check out my curator . You're also welcome to join the .

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is a lovely and very well-done little game. There's much more story than one might expect from this type of farming/life sim. And all characters are voice-acted, with well-defined personalities. I've barely scratched the surface but I am looking forward to playing more, unlocking the various upgrades, and seeing where the story goes. Some nice features are the fact that inventory appears to be unlimited, and you don't have to use hotkeys to switch between items like axe, watering can, etc. You get context-sensitive popups when you are near something like a tree, then you just click to harvest. I love that feature.I do think the game can stand some tweaking. I am playing on "relaxed" mode, but harvesting and fishing still cost too much energy. You have to constantly be cooking food and eating; chopping down two small trees is enough to totally drain Tara's energy. And the various vendors' store hours are rather annoying. If you run out of fishing bait, you can't buy more until that store is open, you can't sell items unless certain stores are open, and they are all closed a couple of days out of each week. The effect this has, for me, is that relaxed mode causes the days to pass more slowly (good) but I find myself out of things to do until the next day since I can't access vendors I need (bad). The rewards for town board missions could be better too; in most cases they are not worth doing because you'll need whatever items the quest requires for OTHER purposes, like cooking or crafting. Turning in 5 fish for one request might get you 38 coins, but you're better off selling the fish or cooking with them. I hope to see some of these things adjusted, but I still really like this game and hope to play it for many hours to come.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 Absolutely buy this game!! I have been waiting for a game like this without even realising it. I think the studio has done an amazing job with this game, and if this is their first game, I am super excited to see where their journey takes them in the future! The seasons are different to your usual farming game, you as a witch choose when to change the seasons, so it's taking some time to get used to the laid-back feeling of farming without any real worry about crops dying and running out of time before a crop grows, but I can see good and bad for that, I am starting to get used to it though and enjoy it, and it does not take away from the games beauty at all.The only downside is.... *SPOILERS*That poor gran was taken from us far too soon!! _childDocuments_.review: I was so sad when this game ended! The blend between the familiar Harvest Moon-esque type of games and magic is an interesting choice that ends up working out very well. Like many games within the farming RPG subgenre, you are able to make friends and romance characters. However, this game seems to especially focus on this social aspect, which I particularly enjoyed. Every NPC has a beautifully handcrafted backstory that the devs clearly invested a lot of time on. These scenes all have voice acting and custom animations -- a TON of work was put into making sure the player was immersed. By the end of the game, you feel like you know some of these characters as your own friends / family.I don't usually leave reviews but I have been looking for a game with this kind of immersive social dynamic for a very long time, so if you are also someone who enjoys cultivating digital relationships, GET THIS GAME! As someone who has been into this specific niche of simulators since the early Harvest Moon games of the 90's, I am constantly trying to find a game with attention on forging friendships and finding love on your little farm that's on par with HM 64, HM: A Wonderful Life, Stardew Valley, etc. Having been disappointed with the somewhat lackluster focus on this within the latest Story of Seasons game and (ESPECIALLY) the latest Harvest Moon game, Wylde Flowers is a breath of fresh air.Hoping the devs come out with something new soon and spend as much time on character development as they did on this game! Highly recommend! Thank you devs for such a wonderfully unique game in what is now an oversaturated genre of uninspired farming RPGs that do not build upon the characters. Beautiful job!

_childDocuments_.review: Hour 1: Wow, this is fun! Great art style, love how unique the characters are and how they have so many voice lines. So much stuff to do! Unlocking stuff slowly but surely. The only negative so far is that Tara's stamina bar is horribly low, you can barely do any work on the farm at all. Hour 3: Yay! Unlocked the mine and on the first day already got to level 3! I'm joining the coven, that should be interesting. I also basically filled out my entire beginning farm area with composters and garden boxes. How much does it cost to make another farm area? Oh… that will take a while.Hour 5: Hmmm.. To unlock the next part of the main story, I need copper? Where do I get that? I guess in a lower level in the mine? Still stuck on level 3 though. Also, what's with wood being so hard to get? The kids have started to repeat their lines, uh oh.Hour 7: Still stuck on level 3, what's up with that? I guess I might need a shovel so I can dig up those mud patches. Also, I noticed that Francis sells gold bars, so if you have the money you can upgrade directly to gold tools. Why even bother having Copper and Silver tools then? My goal is to get the Gold Pickaxe first to help with mining. A lot more lines are starting to be repeats now. Hour 9: Still stuck on level 3, shovel didn't help. Hour 11: Still stuck on level 3, just grind, grind, grind with no reward in sight.Hour 13: Almost all lines are repeats now. It's been like a month+ since people had their "it's almost summer" line and I haven't gotten much closer. This feels like a chore now and I'm losing interest.Hour 14:  I'm only about half way saved up for a Gold Pickaxe. This is ridiculous. Weeks upon weeks mining on level 3 and still haven't found the key yet. There's no way I'm going to spend another 10+ hours in this game just so I can progress a single step further. Time to look up a guide on the best way to earn money. I'm guessing  considering there is an option on the menu to embargo them. If there's not a fast way to earn money, I quit.Hour 15: Got lots of money quickly, then in a single day went from level 3 to level 13. The progression in this game is ridiculously bad. I love the characters, story, setting, and dialogue in this game. I just don't think I can deal with how bad the progression feels. Not sure if I will continue playing.

_childDocuments_.review: My newfound cozy game obsession! I can easily see myself pouring hundreds of hours into this. That's how much grip this game has on me. _childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: I would describe this game as a 'befriending sim' with a very shallow veneer of farming/resource gathering/'witchy' activities. The farming/mining/fishing is nowhere near as fun or sophisticated as other games e.g. Stardew Valley. And there are no customisation options - even very shallow ones - to make the game experience your own, e.g. the layout of your farm and buildings can't be changed or decorated, there's no home decoration, no character customisation or clothing options. So the game feels very linear and daily tasks are repetitive and grind-y. There's also a dearth of special/seasonal occasions which adds to the repetition.And even though this game majors on the social/befriending angle, which is largely ok, it still doesn't feel quite right. You can get to be 'good friends' with a character and they still repeat dialogue asking if you've met their family members (of course you have) and/or your character asks them really basic getting-to-know-you type questions that previous cutscenes have already answered. The voice acting is great though.I think this game would have been a lot better had it been done as an all-out graphic novel/choices matter game, and dropped the farming etc. As it is, it's a jack of all trades and master of none.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: A very nice story-driven game about being a witch and having little understanding of what that means or of all the magical stuff around you. It does get a bit cult-y midgame with that creepy Scientology-ish, health supplement-y "church", but if anything, making me actively despise several characters for their wilful ignorance of the harm they cause society is impressive. Cameron and Otto make me livid, and if that's not a compliment to their personality writing and story presence idk what is.My favourite feature is the time controls which can slow down or speed up your day from relaxing to challenging, because sometimes I just need some extra daylight to get all this mining done before the quest deadline. It's not necessarily what I'd call cozy purely because there are time-based quests you can fail if you don't work smart to gather resources in time, but it is still highly enjoyable and the story is great.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: Hmmm. Just kind of...boring? Which is very unfortunate.The opening was good, very heartfelt, very nicely written and voiced. The characters in town are unique, the story is original, but the gameplay...woof. I've tried to play through twice and each time, by the end of the first summer, I'm bored out of my mind. The pacing just feels very erratic. Stretches of nothing, then almost frantic assignment for quests, a massive amount of new dialogue, that then just abruptly drops off, with characters constantly reiterating "It feels like it should be (next season) already"...even though it's barely been long enough for a bit of cotton to grow.It feels like a really, really nice story game that decided it need a "gameplay challenge" and dropped a wholesale Harvest Moon game on top of it. There's almost too much to do if you want to relax and be neighborly....but not enough to do if you want to really "play" a farming game or feel like you're having an impact. I like that you can adjust the speed setting, but I didn't jive with any of them. One was ridiculously slow, one slightly too fast, the last one was way too fast.The magic element seems almost superfluous. The inputs for spells are high, but the outputs are vague, barely helpful, or not worth the inputs if you're "playing"...if you're just chilling your way through though, you don't need them at all, outside of a couple story quests.I wouldn't recommend this game, but I would look forward to trying another game by the same studio. Their storytelling skills are very good. I would just urge them to either go full no-stress all story or full "challenge/management play" in their next game.(I'd also like to be able to play as a male or even non-binary character. I spent my teenage years picking the "girl" characters in games because I wanted the pursue the male love interests (and had no other choice), so ironically, this felt like forced heteronormativity despite their focus on inclusivity. :P)

_childDocuments_.review: Such potions, very crafty.  You really gotta grind hard to level up in this game.  The inventory system is really simplistic and easy and I'm glad I'm not having to worry about where to find which item in some chest located in what could be a dozen places. Very smart, thank you!Mining has become an absolute bore since I reached Level 14 and find I'm just continuously clearing out that level until I can figure out how to go beyond it ... some nice handy UX hints would be great at this point as I dont know how to open the chests or progress into Level 15 of the Mines.  So far have managed to finance all of my building projects, however. I'm not complaining but it gets tedious doing the same thing over and over again, day in, day out with no indication of how to actually get beyond that door ... omg i'm having flash backs to MY job LULMy only real gripe is that there needs to be more instances of Weed, Mandrake & Conch Shells spawning at regular intervals as I am CONSTANTLY waiting on those to appear on my morning harvest runs. In the prompts to uncover the masked identities of your coven mates, could you maybe give a small hint?  Some of these people were really hard to figure out.This game is great!  I've really enjoyed playing it! I'd really like it if you could enrich the story further within the main quest arc so it would tie the whole game together.  However, I have played a number of farm sim titles over the last year and I gotta say this was in my Top 3!  Thank you for building such a delightful game.A+

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to give both the good and the bad about this game. Mostly positive, but there are a couple of big issues. Spoiler warning, and also trigger warning. First, the good. I'm extremely impressed with the quality of this game. The voice-acting is far beyond what most other games of its genre have: exceptional quality, a huge range of original content (I'm 15 hours into the game, and I have yet to hear an NPC repeat the same line!), each NPC voice is very distinct and unique, and it's very believable... many developers don't do scripting well, but Wylde Flowers does it well. It's polished, mostly bug-free, and runs about as beautifully as you could hope for. The art style is well done, somewhat cartoonish (not that there's anything wrong with that), but the detail work is excellent. The NPCs feel like unique individuals with their own unique lives, like I could meet any one of them on the street. The farming is about typical of the genre... instead of fertilizer, you use magic; instead of farming rows, you get boxed farm plots, the crops you grow are dependent on the season and will die if you switch seasons, watering with a watering can... the usual. Also typical is the mining and crafting and processing of raw materials into manufactured goods. I'd like to clarify this typical-ness by saying that... this kind of typical works, and I'm glad it doesn't stray too far from the usual formula.Now... the bad. The seasons change when the player wants them to... EXACTLY when the player wants them to. While this does give the player a lot of control over how they play, and it prevents the standard dying of crops when the seasons change (unless you just want them to), this also takes away a big part of the urgency and planning and challenge of farming games. There's no real need to plan anything out, like standard farming does, and there's zero risk of accidentally destroying crops. In fact, there's really very little risk to your crops at all other than just not watering them. It makes this aspect of the game too easy, at least for me.SPOILER WARNING IN THIS PARAGRAPH!!! The pacing of the plotline is pretty rough. I think the developers pull the trigger on Gramma way too soon. She dies after the first season, before we have any real chance to invest ourselves in the characters, and they play up the sorrow extremely hard. My viewers on both YouTube and Twitch comment quite a bit on how sad the game feels, and I can't disagree with them... rather than building up the character development and giving the player time to come to love and respect Gramma, we're artificially shoved into "Oh no, Gramma is sick! Oh no, Gramma is dying! Oh, no, Gramma is dead! Everyone... BE SAD!!!" We're not given enough time to invest any emotion into Gramma before she's killed off, which is a huge opportunity missed. The character of Gramma is really well made, and this would have been much more powerful had we been allowed a year or so to invest our emotions into her. As it was, I recognized the sadness of the scene, but I wasn't really moved by her death at all, other than "Aw.. I liked her character, that's too bad. Oh well, moving on..." And I see this pattern developing with the other characters as well. We're not allowed to develop opinions of each NPC; rather, each NPC is very upfront and obvious about who they are, how they feel, what side of the conflict they fall under, who each of the "secret" coven members are, how we're supposed to feel about each NPC, and how "good" and "evil" each person is. There's very little subtlety about them and their viewpoints, and it's kind of shoved into our faces rather than giving us the opportunity to learn about each one and letting us form our own opinions... we're supposed to feel a certain way about each one, and that's that. It's very manipulative in that respect.And I think that's what really bothers me about this game: the obvious political agenda of this game. I like that the game gives both binary and nonbinary options for romance, and I like the representation of every race and gender, but it feels a little like the game is shoving it into your face rather than just representing. Traditional marriage is only practiced by church members, everyone else is nonbinary and/or nontraditional, and it's very in-your-face about which side the game considers the "correct" one. The game feels like it's desperately trying to represent EVERY possible aspect of a nontraditional lifestyle, and the community ends up feeling more like a social experiment or a commune than a typical small town. It doesn't feel representative of the standard societal norm, and feels more like someone's own viewpoint of how the world SHOULD be rather than reality. It's a video game, so an alternative world is fine, but it feels too much like I'm being force-fed an agenda rather than experiencing a unique world of its own.It also feels like the drama between church and witches is kind of over-the-top as well: the church is represented as a bunch of bigoted, uncompromising people who are friendly on the outside while hostile to anyone who isn't the church on the inside; the witches are represented as nothing but good and harmless people (with one obvious exception) with no agenda but peace and harmony to all. I haven't gotten that far into the story yet, so maybe that will change as the story progresses, but it's representing organized religion as some sort of evil force and witches as a kind of hippie peace cult who only want balance and prosperity for all. Both are extreme views of each of these communities, and the reality tends to fall somewhere in the middle. As such, the game paints a very one-sided picture of these groups... again, the political agenda of this game shows its face, and the game ends up feeling manipulative rather than fun. And before anyone starts complaining, I'd say the same thing if it were the church being represented as all-good and the witches as all-bad... I'd like to see less politicking for one side, and more of a balanced view for the player to decide what's right and wrong. There are two sides to every belief system, and I'd prefer to see both sides being represented equally rather than being force-fed that one side is better or worse... remember, this is a game, and a game should be about player choices, not developer choices.Overall, TL:DR version would be that this is an extremely well-made game mechanically, but I think it's too preachy and the pacing is wrong. It's basically Fern Gully with witches instead of fairies and society instead of nature. Do I recommend it? Yes, because it's a pretty good game overall. But it's also manipulative and has an obvious political agenda that's going to appeal to some and repel others, which is not a good aspect to have in any game. Don't drive off a large portion of your audience with your opinions, developers... rather, present both sides and let the players decide. It's a much more effective way to make your point.

_childDocuments_.review: (Played this game on Switch, but bought here to support the devs and write a positive review, hence the short play time)This game is absolutely lovely. It has all the aspects of a farming sim, but also an intriguing storyline and loads of surprises. The NPCs really feel like unique and engaging characters that you can grow attached to, and the voice acting in particular brings them to life. The farming aspect itself is well balanced. The amount of help you can give yourself with spells and potions increases proportionally to the amount of work needing done around the farm and island, so there is always a certain degree of time and resource management involved. People tend to complain about the short day cycle, but I believe that having to prioritise and not being able to do every single thing every day makes for less repetitive and more engaging gameplay. The characters, as mentioned before, are great. The diversity feels genuine and loving. Food is indeed the only thing you can give as gift, but I don't see that as a downside - in fact, having to figure out their favourite meals, and collecting the ingredients and recipes is an engaging system that reflects well the real work one would do for their friends. This, I think, works well with the spirit of the game, and it makes you actually think about the characters' cultures of origin, making the diversity feel less tokenistic. I do wish there was perhaps an extra special gift, even if just for the romantic interest, but that's just me wishing I could give Amira a new necklace...If there is anything I would hope would get expanded upon, it is the outfits. Even a couple to choose from for the main character, as watching her mine iron in H&M boots breaks the immersion somewhat. Ideally clothes that change with the season...but that is only a cosmetic critique. The more technical aspects of the game I have no complaint with!Overall, definitely recommend this game! And lastly, this is a spoiler, but I have to say, this is the only game where  The drama of it all...

_childDocuments_.review: Wylde Flowers is a delightful farming/witching sim set in a small town, where our protagonist Tara moves to in order to take care of her ailing grandma. While the gameplay is of course fun, the game truly comes to life with its fully voice-acted cast of wonderful and diverse residents who are a pleasure to get to know! (Especially Amira, who has my whole heart.) I highly recommend this game for anybody who enjoys wholesome games especially, but the cute and engaging narrative and characters make this game great for many!
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: Truly love this game, it's so rare to experience full voice acting and lush soundtracks in this genre! Feels really refreshing and different, it's hard to choose who to romance (in the best way). Tara makes me feel fabulous and seen as a bi gal as well. :) Great accessibility and difficulty/challenge settings too! Love seeing so many of my fave cozy creators loving Wylde Flowers.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: This game has (for me), the perfect balance of relaxation and "always something to do." There's always a potion to craft, a meal to get ingredients for, an outfit to sew, etc., but you never feel rushed (even if the task at hand *seems* time-sensitive). If you think you just can't get something done in time because you don't have a required element, the resource you need "magically" appears in a mostly-believable or coincidental way.I also love the writing and the characters: They are all clearly individuals, with varied and believable personalities, accents, dialects, and body types. There were ones I genuinely liked (), and ones I didn't, though none were so awful that I couldn't stand talking to them, even if it was just to further the story-line.It felt like there were no heavy negative repercussions for any "mistakes" or dialogue choices, though I did not let myself pass out from exhaustion, so I don't know what the consequences of that might be.Overall, this was the perfect game for my casual play style. It kept me interested for hours at a time (the sh*t hits the fan a couple times!), and never frustrated me.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: This is honestly my all time fave life sim. Every single cutscene and interaction with an NPC is voiced and it's done well. The music in the game is beautiful. The characters are charming and you get attached to them. You'll laugh, you'll cry, and nothing else will compare again. If you enjoy life sims, this is the game for you, hands down.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: I was a bit burned out on farming sims and really didn't think I needed another one in my life... until I tried out the demo. I was completely hooked in only a few minutes and, by the time the demo came to an end, I just knew I had to buy this game and play the rest of it. I was a bit unsure if it would be worth the investment, especially since I'm a bit tight on money right now, but I have no regrets. I was invested in this story and eager to know what would happen next like I haven't been in years - once I started playing this game, I could not put it down. Wylde Flowers has quickly became one of my favorite games ever!The main star of this game, by far, has to be the story. The dialogues, the voice acting, and the story archs, are all beyond well executed. In similar games, I really struggle to talk to each NPC over and over and be genuinely interested in getting to know them but, in Wylde Flowers, each day I would go around talking to all the NPC, because I couldn't wait to learn more about them. It was a lot of fun to theorize who each of the coven members were but, even after I knew, I was still interested in all the dialogues, in the main quest, and in all the side quests. The side quests, much like the daily dialogues, help you learn more about each character and their personality, and they always make sense in the story. I never felt like there was a quest that had been put in the game for no reason. All the elements come together perfectly, like pieces of a puzzle. Elements of traditional farming games, such as farming, fishing, and mining, are also really well integrated into the main story, and you will be farming, fishing, and mining to gather the necessary materials for quests, your magic, or to upgrade stuff around your farm - this means that I always knew what I was supposed to do, and never felt lost or bored.While at first Wylde Flowers might feel a bit claustrophobic, over time you unlock more and more areas, like the mine, the mountain pass, , and . As the story unfolds, the map keeps expanding with it, giving you more areas to explore and providing more ways for you to keep busy and entertained. The town also changes over time and you end up unlocking | and a |. And you'll get to know new characters over time as well. Plus, you can pet the cat!Each character is unique and, because several of the characters are native to different countries, you get to learn a tiny bit about the culture of other places, like specific expressions they use in their dialogues, and also, local dishes. I was quite impressed by the variety of foods,, and spells the game had to offer.I wasn't going to marry one of the romanceable characters but I did end up settling down and I am really glad I did. You have adorable interactions you can do with your spouse, they can occasionally  or offer to help on the farm and you slowly unlock more and more  over time. They can also comment on what Tara is wearing. This makes the partners in Wylde Flowers feel more realistic than in other similar games.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: I played Wylde Flowers on my Ipad long before I got it on desktop, and honestly it has become one of my all-time favorite games. Relaxing and story rich game play with a cozy and adorable atmosphere, I really couldn't ask for anything more. Its one of those games you can play over and over again and still enjoy it every time.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed playing this game! Perfect mix of magic and farm. I love the intricate social details put into all the NPCs. Having the characters voiced over makes the game more personal and immersive. _childDocuments_.review: If you want to recreate your experience with Stardew or AC, give up. My God, give up. Portia is a fair bit better but still terrible. I haven't experienced games this badly made until SV and AC got me into this genre, they very much do stand alone. You're going from meticulous masterpieces to games that are barely functional, made by capitalists (who don't play games or get them) that have noticed a demand from a new audience and have whipped up utter discharge like this to take advantage. _childDocuments_.review: If you have played Harvest Moon, My Time at Portia, Stardew Valley and the likes of that, you're going to love this! Story-wise, it is very unique. Magic plays such a crucial part, not only will it make your time grinding for money and other stuff easier, but it will also help in your story's progress which for me is a very different take on the usual farming games. I love that it doesn't limit you in relationships and you have options from both genders but personally, I will always go for *COUGH* Westley. The barn and coop animals are also such a delight to witness, the animation style of everything just makes me warm and fuzzy inside. You can also just chill and fish, honestly everything in the game is pretty chill.The game is literally just so cozy and aesthetic looking. I really recommend that you guys try this out! _childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: It breaks my heart to not be able to recommend this game because there are so many aspects of it that are wonderful and it seems like it was made with love. But I agree with another reviewer that this should have been a visual novel or some other story-driven genre, and not a sim, or should've spent more time and attention making sure the simulation part was better realized. I was enchanted with the demo and bought the game straightaway and continued to enjoy it for a few hours before the widely unbalanced features became more apparent. For one example, you are expected to do witchy stuff in the woods all the way across town AT NIGHT, but there is a curfew for when your character must be in bed. If she isn't, she passes out and gets sick, which can only be cured with medicine from a pharmacy that has limited hours and is closed two days a week. Until you cure her, her stamina, which is already excruciatingly limited, is capped at about 1/4 or a 1/3. Did I mention how slowly she walks? I thought surely the first witchy thing we'd learn is a teleportation spell of some kind, maybe a portal from the farm to the woods, but no. I'm over 10 hours in and still having to run back from the woods to the farm, panicking each time about passing out. My favorite part? If you stop going to the woods because you learn to hate them, like I did, they send you a letter scolding you for not doing your witchy duties -_-It's very hard to get resources due to the tiniest stamina bar I've ever seen, and everything costs not only a ton of resources, but also money. Even stuff you build on your own farm with resources you've collected costs money. Smelting ore costs money. Upgrading equipment costs money. Money is very hard to come by. This is not helped by baffling choices for fish prices (as fishing is a common money maker in these games). I can sell a flounder for 40 gold, but rarer fish are priced the same as other common fish (ex: sturgeon sells for only 20 and tuna for only 10!?). The money issue could be easily alleviated by adjusting these prices to make sense. If I could sell a tuna for, say, 200, maybe I can actually get somewhere. The recipes I've encountered so far are not better. I understand we can sell fish sticks for a premium, but fish sticks are the only way I get anything done in the game and I didn't grow enough wheat in the spring so here we are, poor and tired.The fishing is horrible (not the mechanics overall but the constant need to get specific fish is horrid). All fishing quests are sadistic imo and I did not consent to that, lol. ALL of the quest rewards are pittances, not worth your time at all. Every time you unlock something big you think, oh yeah, now finally maybe things will get easier and open up a bit, only to realize that things are harder and cost even more. I don't mind grindy, in fact I like it, but my problem here is there's no flow to what you do in a day. The stores are closed a lot of the time and the map doesn't give you their hours so unless you write them all down, you're constantly going to places that are closed for things you need and having to wait. You don't have autonomy over your farming space so you have to be INCREDIBLY careful about what you plant in the beginning and if you mess up, you're just screwed. I often find myself out of energy at like, I'm not kidding, 9 am, and not having proper resources to make food that's worth a damn and so I just walk around foraging and talking to people waiting until I justify going to bed for the next day. I have a similar issue in Dinkum, where energy goes faster than I'd like as well, but in that game you can make a TON from fishing alone, and it's very easy to cook. You can fish for money and keep some fish to cook, just grill it plain, and you're set.There's a huge lack of information in the game. For instance, certain fish only like certain kinds of bait, but when you look up fish you've caught in your 'pedia, it doesn't tell you what bait they like/avoid. But you get so many quests for specific fish, so you have to remember what they respond to or you won't catch them to fulfill the quests. For another example, when you go to cook a recipe, it doesn't tell you how much energy it restores or how much it sells for. So you don't know which recipes are worth it, because MANY of them are absolutely not worth it and ingredients are hard enough to come by that you don't want to waste it. I could go on but that's enough there. I read a review a lot like mine before I bought the game and still bought it, and now wish I had trusted my gut reaction to that review instead of letting all the positive ones change my mind. I am genuinely glad this game is popular and has such a loving, happy community around it. I don't want to harm this game in any way and I would not leave a review like this if there weren't so many rave reviews to counterbalance it. I'm just putting this out for the folks like me who have played enough farming sims to read a description like this and know this wouldn't be a good fit before it's too late. I hate having to say this because I was SO HERE for a farming sim with witchy vibes and inclusive dating but, unfortunately, my queermance with Violet will likely never come to pass because I don't know how I will ever amass enough soil to farm anything so I can cook things so I can hit rocks and trees enough to build a beautiful life for the two of us. Developer, if you are reading this, please know I mean you no harm. I'm happy you're getting tons of praise and I hope you make more games, Just please keep these things in mind if you make another farming sim!
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: Does away with some of the worse aspects of most games like this, unlimited storage that is always on you, no more tired inventory management! The right tool presenting itself depending on the activity, traversing the mines without danger and anything you have to wait for in the game is a much shorter time period than any other game of this type. It encompasses so many gameplay aspects of other games of this type but does it better and more to the point, the grind is still the grind but not in such a way that you get tired of it. The ability to have time run normal or relaxed is a great feature for when you want a bit more time to plant seeds on the first of the season. Overall a really positive gameplay experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: YES!!!! Finally a game with FULL voice over!!! That's one of the things I love about Wizard 101! Wylde Flowers is exactly the type of game I truly enjoy! It's not just the gardening and fishing but the coven, witches, potions and spells add such an exciting twist to the game. It was recommended as a "cozy" game but it's much more than that. It's soothing, relaxing, sweet, complex, and the game doesn't rush you. (It takes several days for crops to grow.) Your relationship with every village member is unique and evolves as far as you choose it to go. It's an interesting balance between normalcy and wonder. _childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: I like the witch aspect of it, makes it a bit feel different from other farm sims. and the people in town have back stories, life aspirations, problems and relationship that sounds like it can happen in real life. theres extensive voice work also, you character actually talk and you can hear her voice. At the 20 hour mark i started to get bored. the farming is very limited that it makes it feel like "gardening sim" instead. theres no customization options - you plant crops, milk cows, feed chicken and do mining in a red dress and ankle high boots. the game makes a big deal about the secrecy of witches but once you get access to a flying broom you can fly/teleport anywhere even on daylight and land in front of non witches and they dont even notice.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: The amount of time and care that was very obviously put into Wylde Flowers is astounding. The NPCs are stunning and so diverse in every way which is so amazing to see, especially when so many farming sims seem to be lacking in the BIPOC representation, LGBTQIA+ representation, and gender diversity department. _childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: i have to admit, i wasn't sure if id actually play this game, there are so many similar games.after playing the demo i was completely hooked! this game has a charm that just pulls you in, not only is the main story line well rounded and thought out, but the amount of little side missions are plentyful, to keep you playing long after the credits roll.It is such a cosy game being able to play fully with only the mouse means chilling and eating snacks while you fully emerge yourself into the world. the mechanics of the game are simple and effective, making it the perfect game for what ever system you decide to play on.the characters are charming, inclusive and well rounded, with lots of dialog which means talking to them isn't repetitive like some games.whether your most interested in the farming side of the game growing crops and raising animals, or you enjoying all things magic and whimsical, this game has something for everyone. Overall im very impressed with this game the amount of content surprised me straight of the bat.i have recommended to a few of my friends who are now enjoying the game to!
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: I was really surprised by the diversity of this game. Of course, it's a cozy game, but not too cozy  to get bored. Actually, I was expecting more of an ordinary farming game, but it's so much more. It's about becoming a part of the village, and the way you get in to it, is just damn interesting! Each character has their own story, and most of them are really cool  to get to know. I really enjoyed the dialogue, it was just fun to read. Also, the whole story fascinated me and even the magical parts. Every time I thought I had seen it all, something new and unexpected happens. I love the graphics, the sound and don't noticed any bugs so far.This is my first review on Steam, but I'm really convinced that this game deserves it :)
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: Wylde Flowers has my whole heart! _childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: This is a truly cozy game. It wraps you up in a magical, romantic, and inclusive story, allowing you to explore a quaint town and partake in the classic farming sim that we all know and love. I love the chibi-esque art style and that there is a real narrative to play through, adding more depth to a genre that has seen a huge resurgence these past few years. _childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: i've mostly played this on the switch, but just a quick review here: this is such a heartfelt and wonderful game. every time i think i must have hit the endgame, there's another five or six hours of story line content to follow. all of the characters are detailed and have complex stories and motivations. the mechanics are fun. the art style is adorable. i have so much fun running around, making spells, and figuring out new machines to make new fun products to sell. 10/10, give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: Where do I even start! This game is so, so incredible! The story is intriguing, the characters are so fun and wonderful, and the design is absolutely gorgeous! The game cuts to the chase of being a witch and starting the process fairly quickly compared to many other games, and it doesn't feel rushed at all! I was a tad concerned at first about the 24 hour wait time on the composter because some games will make you wait irl hours to do things, but it's in-game time, which means that you only have to play through one day! Already a massive bonus!The representation in this game is amazing beyond words, as well. It's nice that the options are diverse in many ways. From characters of different races and ethnicities, to even a nonbinary character (who talks about it) that you can romance! It's so incredible!It's so worth the money that you spend on it. I can't recommend this game enough!
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really great so far. Though I was initially put off by the lack of customization features and the choice of outfit for the MC (in the mines in a dress and heels??) I've come to accept those as quirks of a farm sim with literally the highest production values in the genre. From the writing, VA, and detail in the animations, you can really see how much effort was put into this title. This is one of the few farm sims that leans heavily into the social sim components of the game and I love it for that.On the gameplay side, things aren't as strong. But that doesn't mean it is bad. Farming, mining, fishing, and crafting is fairly basic. But honestly, it probably needs to be to allow the player to get deep into the storyline and social sim components of the game.UPDATE: Unlocked fast travel and that basically fixed my issues with quests having too many steps. I have finished my first playthrough and I adore this game. The story is genuinely probably the best in the farm sim genre currently, the voice acting stayed very excellent and overall, the game left me wanting more. Always a good thing.A couple of new gripes. Dating folks is a bit weird in this game. Their dialogue doesn't really change that much and that feels weird when you have romance cutscenes that have nicknames and established dynamics that you don't see in actual gameplay. I wish there was just a bit more characterization for these romances at all stages of the process.On the gameplay side, on a first playthrough it felt really bad to sometimes have timed quests I couldn't finish because of rotating stock issues with some of the stores or just simply not having the right crop in an off season. I feel fairly confident that this may have been a decision to encourage additional playthroughs but this is a linear narrative game. Running through the same story for a couple of side quests isn't going to appeal to everyone. I had a very complete gaming experience even though my first run around was very much not "optimal" but I do wish that there was some sort of signposting for new players that they need to stockpile ingredients they can only get in certain seasons. Because you only get to play each season (except Spring) ONCE. But overall I am super excited about this game and I hope the devs will update this game with more content one day. I'd buy another year in Fairhaven in a heartbeat.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game and have been addicted to it for the past couple weeks. It is very story driven, and I like how unique and thorough each character's story is. It is a very cozy game. Some SPOILERS:PROS:-Unlimited inventory (I hated in SDV running out of space!)-Fish stick hack. I like unlocking things relatively quickly, so it is an easy way to make money and enjoy the game without it being too grindy for me.-Westley, my Alaskan king :D-Being able to play as a cat!-Fishing game is simple-Feels like there is always something to doCONS:-Walking speed and having to keep crafting to increase speed. I know eventually the broom is unlocked but its still been a lot hours of needing to craft.-Wish there was a teleport feature-Some shop hours are annoying (Looking at you Marty)-Cameron and Otto LOL
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly rich in different types of people, more so than you usually see from games in this genre. I also appreciate how they don't shy away from actually discussing topics like sexuality instead of simply glossing over it with a hand wave like so many other games. There's definitely a place for those games, but there are so few like Wylde Flowers that it makes it a breath of fresh air. It runs surprisingly well on my aging laptop too. The game does take a while to get you to the point that most others start off at, but there's so much to do and the people are so enjoyable to talk to that it doesn't feel like it's tedious.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: This is a less stressful version of Stardew Valley that is incredibly diverse, amazingly magical, and unapologetically queer. It's genuinely so relaxing, and while there is a very entertaining storyline, you can veer off from it to do whatever you please whether it be fishing, gardening, cooking, building, crafting, mining, item collecting, relationship building, and more. 11 hours in and I can tell there's so much left for me to unlock storyline wise, and some villagers haven't even come into the game. The design is beautiful, the mystery of the Fairhaven Coven is a nice added touch to keep me on my toes, and I am all around so impressed and happy with this game. I cannot wait to play more.EDIT upon game completion: Thank you, kind stranger, for my first ever steam award! At this point, I have 100%ed this game and I can happily share that this is my favorite game of the year and will be a forever recommendation to friends. I've convinced 5+ friends to pick it up, with more to come. I broke my ankle this summer and was basically trapped inside my family home, away from my apartment, most of my friends, and with no independence. This game was such a happymaking distraction from an at times bleak and painful reality. It brought me so much joy when I really needed it, and I think it would do the same for anyone else who picks it up. And I want to shout out the in-game dev support as I thought I had a buggest quest for a storyline I really wanted to see the end of and they helped me navigate it with no problem at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: Great story patiently told like a season of a TV drama series.Some activities feel like a boring grind with a lot of walking, e.g., daily Gloaming farming. Otherwise not bad and you can adjust the time scaling if you want.Crafting is not very satisfying and a lot of things are useless to make.Play it primarily for the story. As a farming sim it's okay and has some neat updates (e.g., rainbow magical animals) but otherwise between mediocre and unsatisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: Wylde Flowers

_childDocuments_.review: I can't get enough of Wylde Flowers! LOVE this game so much, (I bought the Switch version of the game to travel with as well!) This has now become my Go-To game whenever I have time to play it. All the other games in my Steam library are now on hold.The storyline is great. Wylde Flowers is a cozy life and farming sim with a witchy twist! Escape to a cute world of diverse folks, and magical spells, as you and the coven unravel a mystery!

Play as Tara, as she arrives at a cozy rural island to help out her grandma and the family farm.

Explore a wholesome world of magical realms, beautiful beaches, secretive forests and the friendly town of Fairhaven.

Meet a charming cast of fully voice acted characters, with intriguing back stories to reveal. Find friendship or maybe even romance?

Reveal the hidden darkness which is affecting the town and discover how to bring everyone together.

name: Worldless
detailed_description: Worldless is set in a newborn universe based on entities trapped in an eternal conflict by the polarising nature of their attractions. These interactions can result in an exchange of their polarities, but this process is very unstable, and who knows what new results can come from it… In this 2D active, turn-based, platformer, players will explore intricate and interconnected areas full of secrets and mysteries to uncover with a plethora of abilities like dashing and wall-jumps. Along the way you will encounter different beings that aim to stop you as you seek to find your place in this universe. Using turn-based rules, fights combine traditional combat with active time actions for a thrilling and strategic combat where your knowledge of game mechanics and skills will be put to the test. Establish Yourself Uncover unimaginable possibilities - Jump and dash your way through abstract areas in pursuit of transcendence. Grow to Survive Upgrade your abilities through an intricate and rewarding talent tree Ready yourself - Engage in active time, turn-based battles, and time your attacks and defences perfectly to shatter your enemies. Immerse yourself Indulgent Melodies - Connect to the areas of Worldless on a deeper level with a haunting yet beautiful score. Cherish the moment - Define the world and challenge its secrets in a mysterious and enchanting narrative.

Grow to Survive Upgrade your abilities through an intricate and rewarding talent tree Ready yourself - Engage in active time, turn-based battles, and time your attacks and defences perfectly to shatter your enemies. Immerse yourself Indulgent Melodies - Connect to the areas of Worldless on a deeper level with a haunting yet beautiful score. Cherish the moment - Define the world and challenge its secrets in a mysterious and enchanting narrative.
short_description: Worldless is a stylised 2D platformer with a unique, active, turn-based combat system, and a mind-bending interpretative narrative. Players embark on a journey of self-growth and understanding, pushing the limits of their nature in a newly born and abstract universe.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really glad this game has a demo, it's really hard to tell what you're actually looking at in the screenshots and trailers, and it would've been unfortunate to pass on something this unique.  The closest thing to this I can think of is Valkyrie Profile, with a combat system that, while turn based, involves using your turn to string together combos like an action game, but even then, Worldless is structured much more like a metroidvania than an RPG, with platforming and regular unlocks that give you new options for moving around the map.  It has wonderful music as well.I can't fully endorse it without a key warning, though.  Metroidvanias live and die by their maps, and the map in Worldless may well be the worst I've ever seen in this sort of game.  I get what the devs were going for, it fits the minimalist vibe, but considering the game contains multiple objectives that explicitly need you to leave and then come back, sometimes a considerable amount of time later, the game really needs something that gives you a sense of where to look.  IMO it needs a complete redesign, or at absolute minimum an indicator that tells you how many pickups you're missing in each sector, and what kind.That said, the individual areas aren't huge.  They're just big enough that a bad map is annoying, but not so massive that it seriously stunts progression.  I would like to see it get a redesign or at minimum some quality of life improvements, but there's so much good in the other aspects of the game that I have to recommend it, because it really is an experience worth having.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often review, but I'm surprised this game hasn't received more marketing. It scratches the itch left by Ori and Hollow Knight in the sense of being locked off from areas until you unlock the movement required for it. Uniquely comparative to Ori or HK though is that it's undeniably relaxing to venture through the world because you don't have enemies always in your face. It also has a decent range in difficulty from start to finish.Power up menu was easy to navigate and learn. Though you can learn everything it would be nice if you could refund something if you still had another slot elsewhere on the tree to spend that same soul, but it wasn't a huge deal in the end I think.There are quite a few reviews complaining about the map and honestly... it's not as bad as they make it out to be. Just hit R3 often to confirm where you are -- voila. My only complaint is that the Endurance upgrades aren't put on the map. The blue, orange, and neutral souls are shown so it feels a little annoying the Endurance ones aren't. Finding a missed one is rough, but that's a part of exploring I suppose, do it thoroughly. The visuals of this game are absolutely gorgeous, the combat art, the movement, everything. I didn't see a single area with visual issues and it was all incredibly pretty. Only drawback would be some colors blended into the colors behind it, particularly in combat attacks, could be easy to miss an occasional horizontal or vertical flash because the light blended with the enemy or background.- half pt for no Endurance markers- half pt for attack indicatorsHonestly there's not much there storywise, but I think that's also to be expected given the game's premise. What is there though is intriguing enough. Though fair note is that I'm 2, maybe 3 bosses away from 100% I believe (so far). Movement on the map itself feels responsive and quick, though nothing too overly difficult excepting one spoiler area that is absolutely awful, terrible, makes you hate your life for at least 3 hours until you 'git gud' enough at it, only to find out there's more fokkery later on in the map... ugh. The rest of the zones are good though, with no real feeling like you've gotta stay in one spot and bang your head against an enemy until you win. It was simply a matter of turning around and getting more powerups if you came across a particularly tough enemy, and the map allowed for it in every scenario I can think of. - half pt for  parkour zone. The combat actually shines pretty well. It has quite a bit of depth and difficulty to it. The timing aspect of defense feels rewarding when you pull it off, and the same for some of the attacks as well (mostly charged attacks). The enemies are varied and require different strategies to tackle them for absorption. Just because there's a health bar doesn't mean you have to be perfection before killing them -- some of them absorb your attacks to regain health, and failing to absorb them gives them health back too so you can prolong the fights at times. The difficulty definitely is noticeable in some fights versus others, but not so incredibly challenging that you can't overcome it I think (note as above I still have at least 2 fights left). My only gripe is that there isn't more done to indicate when you're Perfect Guard or Perfect Combo'ing. There's one blue boss that was awful for me when I tried to do it by parrying its attacks perfectly... it just felt too inconsistent and I couldn't get enough feedback as to how to improve. Getting hints somehow whether you were late or early would be helpful I think, but perfection certainly isn't necessary to progress.- half pt for not being able to pause on enemy's turn- half pt for underwhelming timing indicators

_childDocuments_.review: My first Steam reviewI really like Wordless. VisualsThe art direction and execution is fantastic. Each area feels different yet cohesive with the rest of the world, full of life yet empty. I'm left with a feeling of awe and melancholy and a desire to keep playing just to see more of this comfortingly stark world. I also really like abstract art so this is definitely a bonus, but its beautiful regardlessGameplayA metroidvania with a unique turn-based take on combat. There is platforming, exploration, unique environments, skill trees, combos and an atmospheric story. There is a stunning amount of diversity in this game without making me feel like its just bloat. There is little to no guidance and even less HUD, but that's part of the fun and immersion. It's not hard to figure out by playing around, and you can enjoy the game without figuring much out anyway. There is a unique capture mechanic where you have to fill up an alternate bar for enemies before their health runs out in order to get more skills. This is more a reward for skillful gameplay and you can get more skills through pure exploration.DifficultyThis is the quality that I think is going to polarise players.It's not easy, but not Dark Souls in its difficulty. The platforming is the easier part, though it still requires precise inputs at times. The combat can be really challenging. You need to develop a strong sense of timing to master it, however its possible to finish the game without getting the timing right through exploration and prioritising the extra block layers in the skill tree (and the guard counter). It's worth putting in the effort to get really good at the game because it really feels amazing when it all comes together. It flows in a way that feels really powerful and looks pretty epic. Luckily its really easy and fast to redo fights so a relaxed and patient approach was what ended up being most fun for me.Sound designAmazing. Brings the world to life and makes platforming and combat feel juicy.StoryDepends on how much you like vague atmospheric storytelling. The story itself is nothing groundbreaking, but I loved the way it is delivered, especially with some optional lore and one really cathartic moment. The end of the story can be polarising, but don't let it spoil your journey.In summary, come to be immersed in a beautiful abstract world, stay to make angels cry at how ineffectual their strongest attacks are

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really know how to even review this game without devolving into gushing and incoherent rambling, but here it goes:This game was incredible. If you like the active turn-based combat in games like the Paper Mario series or the Mario & Luigi RPG series (Superstar Saga, Bowser's Inside Story, etc) Then I think you will really like this game. The combat system is really unique and interesting, there are combos, elemental resistances, shields, shield breaks, and a big skill tree for you to work through. I found most moves had their uses, and combat is extremely satisfying. It just feels good to string together hits, get a string going, and finish it off with a huge hit of some kind. The main mechanic in this game is absorption. You need to absorb your foes to get the equivalent of skill points. Killing an enemy by reducing their health bar usually results in what is effectively a loss because you have to absorb them to get the enemy off the playfield. It's quite difficult to explain the combat system, but just know it works really well and is really fun.If you are good enough, just like the Mario & Luigi series, you can avoid almost all damage as the white character. That character has a perfect block to negate all damage if you time it within the perfect window. The combat in my opinion does not overstay its welcome, and is always kept interesting in some way.It's not all combat, there is some great exploration, and some fun platforming challenges. I had a lot of fun just exploring the world, finding enemies to fight, getting skill points, getting a couple upgrades, and trying them out on some fights. There is some light backtracking, but the game is mostly linear in my opinion. The world design seemed to me to be really good, areas are very distinct from one another, and often visually striking with setpieces.Special mention has to be given to the presentation, both in graphics and music. This is a very pretty game in my opinion. The art style for the characters and enemies is very minimalistic, but in contrast they go all-out with the animation, the environment design, and the combat effects. The flashes, the explosions, the hit effects, the lasers, lighting, it's all very juicy, sharp, tasteful, and extremely well done. The environments are very pretty, mostly simple shapes, but with a lot of detail. The music takes a bit of a back seat as it's mostly atmospheric, but it's still excellent and pops off when it needs to. There are some pretty intense battle themes, and some dramatic music during pivotal story moments.Story... I will say, I didn't really understand the story, but I think I got the gist of it. There is very little text, most of it is just from NPCs you meet in the hub world, and the rest is world-building and implied context. The ending wraps things up pretty clearly, but it's arguable what the outcome of that is.Overall I really enjoyed this game, and if it sounds interesting, try the demo. Just know that the demo is pretty limited, and the combat gets a lot more interesting about 1/3 of the way through the game. It's about a 9 hour game, I got stuck on 1 or 2 fights for an extra hour or 2 which brought my tally up to 10. I got it for about $16CDN, and it's 100% worth that. It was on sale, and it's probably still worth full price, but it was a bit short. Thank you to the devs for making this game, it was a very memorable experience, and I was really craving a game like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Snippet: I know a lot of people were initially turned off by the idea of the combat being turn-based, but the way NoName Studios tackles the pacing makes it feel incredibly dynamic and constantly keeps you on guard, more so that an active combat system would. I absolutely love this game, allow me to gush over this.TLDR:+ One of the most creative and dynamic takes on turn-based combat, never feels slow, always tactical.+ Stunning aesthetic vibes and art direction + Beautiful soundtrack+ No enemy is the same, they all have their own flavor and level of challenge.+ Fun collect-a-thon element for lore/worldbuilding+ Secrets Challenges!!- All biomes are connected, but I would've liked to fast travel to nodes if already unlocked. Mini-map showing your location is very minimal.OVERALL------------------An absolutely beautiful aesthetic paired with a dynamic turn-based combat system that never slows down and keeps you on your toes. I have nowhere near mastered the game yet for the secret challenges, but I enjoyed every minute of Worldless. Whether I was fighting and figuring out enemy attack patterns, or running and swinging around the map, I was in awe with how polished the game was at launch.GRAPHICS------------------The art direction for this game is absolutely gorgeous. Discovering how the character's actual form was hidden in the ability/combat animation VFX was a delight, and always made me look forward to be actively use the skills to see her. In a way, the game presents itself as minimalistic, but there is so much depth in the shape language presented to the player.GAMEPLAY------------------Controls are intuitive and skills come at a natural and logical pace as you discover more biomes. It was very easy to pick up, and gradually teaches you to incorporate more abilities to be more effective. By the end of the game, you'll definitely have some mastery of the gameplay. Because there's a purpose to each skill, and the way the turn-based combat activates different mindsets per phase, everything gets compartmentalized and sooner than later, it becomes clear when you should use a certain task.The Absorption mechanic adds a layer of challenge in the sense that while yes, you can just beat certain enemies into submission and continue exploring, but some enemies do not allow for that and force the player to understand the importance of the mechanic. I sometimes found it hard to effectively fill the gauge fully and more often than not just hoped to randomly guess the button-inputs correct rather than maxing out the gauge on purpose.COMBAT------------------I know a lot of people were initially turned off by the idea of the combat being turn-based, but the way NoName Studios tackles the pacing makes it feel incredibly dynamic and constantly keeps you on guard, more so that an active combat system would. It's instinctive and clearly defines the mindset you need to be in, and the more you do it the more fluid the whole thing comes together. There is a beauty and satisfaction in mastering the combat system in both the attack and enemy phases. Parrying is a delight and learning the patterns of the enemies is no slouch either. CHALLENGE-------------------As mentioned in the combat, mastering the combat system is and getting the space to retry as often as you want at no major penalty makes it very accessibly for people new to the genre to really learn and become more dexterous and reactive. This kind of intrinsic training will carry over to other games for sure. The build up in difficulty never plateaus; once you overcome enemies you were struggling with before, you are rewarded with new tools to approach encounters with, but it is completely up to you whether you utilize the tools or not, allowing you to set up your own level of challenge. All encounters are carefully designed to teach and test you.EXPLORATION-----------------The contrast in exploration and combat is a very welcome one. As there are no roaming enemies in the map, it can feel empty but that is exactly the point. As you unlock more exploration abilities, zooming through the different biomes is almost meditative and calming. I had some minor gripes with the way the the minimap was very minimal (only showing the "room" nodes and not really indicating how big or small the areas were, or where my relative position was, leading to some minor frustrating backtracking. In early-game with fewer exploration options this sometimes felt very time-consuming and counter productive.SOUNDTRACK----------------------B A N G E R S. The contrast in exploration and combat is enhanced by the intensity of each activity in the game, Sometimes maybe overwhelmingly so, but it only lets you know you're at a very big encounter, vs a regular enemy. I would've loved to have heard a medium-intense track for the non-boss enemies during exploration, simply to enhance the activity mindset. The sound design is beautiful, no effects were jarring at all. CONCLUSION-----------------Worldless is expertly crafted, with fun mechanics and the most fun I've had in a metroidvania. It was a beautiful journey in the genre where the emphasis feels more about learning everything (both gameplay and the narrative) at a steady and controlled pace, while maintaining the freedom of exploration. All of the devs in each discipline should consider this a crowning achievement and a beautiful highlight in their career. I HIGHLY recommend Worldless.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite what Steam says, as of writing this I have played Wordless for 13/14 hours (played with Steam offline), finished the main game and trying to finish the post-game challenges, and wow! This is one of the best games I've played in a long time.-The presentation of everything is beautiful, from the map, to the menus. I especially like the charachter design, most charachters are abstract creatures made of shapes, but they reveal glimpses of their full appreance only when attacking, which elevates the visual impact of the battles, and in the case of the main charachter also when using overworld abilities. -On that note, moving around in the world feels so good. There aren't that many abilities, but the ones that are there are sufficient and incredibly satisfying to use. At the end of the game you can also unlock a movement challenge, similar to the Path of Pain of Hollow Knight, but shorter.-My favourite part of the game is undoubtedly the combat. Battles in Wordless are divided in two phases: The attack phase is a combo game, you have to try dealing the most damage you can in the time you have, by chaining different the different types of attacks at you disposal, without (usually) worrying about the enemt striking back.In the defense phase it's the enemy's turn to attack, you have two shields, and based on the enemy telegraphing, you have to use the right one for every hit.Both phases reward timing, and when you get how a certain enemy attacks, or how a combo works and how you can optimize damage, it feels incredible.Of course there's a lot I'm leaving out, there are many combat abilities that you continously unlock via skill tree that can change how you fight someone, at the end of the game basically every button on the controller does something, plus a bunch of hold button or two button combos. It's satysfing gradually learining to use everything.The only little complaint I have is maybe the map, it's very minimalist, too minimalist in my opinion, so it gives you a general idea of where you are and not much more, so sometimes I felt a bit lost, but never for too much.Other than that fantastic game! Whished where was more of it, I don't know if the devs have any intention of making updates or makeing new similar stuff but I hope they do!

_childDocuments_.review: Showed this to one of my friends while I was playing it and they immediately went "Dude that looks like a flash game."Honestly, it's the most beautiful flash game I've ever played.Combat feels like a lite fighting game. You're still capable of complex combos / strings but much simpler than a traditional fighting game.Exploration has no tricks to it, nothing hidden behind walls. Anything worth doing is both within your sight and reach.Worldless is right on the precipice between telling the player too little and being a masterwork of subtlety and Show, Don't Tell. For 95% of the game I just wandered around and found most of the collectibles, intuitively. Only thing is I wish there was a little bit more info given directly. There were a couple of times where the map failed me for a few minutes, but the bigger one is combat.A more comprehensive guide maybe? A lab with infinite time to practice? When I watched videos of people playing I'd see the true depth of the combat system. But I couldn't ever quite dive into it myself and by the endgame I still felt like I hadn't truly explored it. It's perhaps my only real ding against Worldless, but plenty fixable.I was able to 100% the game in 22 hours with some looking stuff up to wrap up the final few collectibles I'd missed and achievements. Overall, pretty comfy game. Endgame is definitely difficult but try the demo, it's worth your time and should tell you if it's worth your money.

_childDocuments_.review: 100%ed the game, but I haven't gone and done all achievements () Excellent and unique combat system, mediocre platforming and metroidvania. This game had a really good start, with a lot of mystery, and extremely good environments. I fell in love with the fighting system immediately, very unique, somewhat fighting game-reminiscent. The art is just, amazingly unique, and the environments really look great. Extremely well polished gameHowever, by the mid-game, the game slows down, you get barely any fights, you keep unlocking new combat moves, but you don't get to try them out because the game simply does not throw any fights at you, instead opting to give you more upgrades where a fight could have been. Eventually, yeah, there's moves you completely forget even exist because it's been too long since you've had a proper fight that didn't finish in seconds.The late game though? Gosh. Okay. The late game fights are all extremely rewarding, they're fights that ask for actual execution and thinking about the attacks you use. I really wish there would have been more of those fights, but I'm still very satisfied with how tough and how rewarding it was to finally beat the optional superbossOutside of combat, platforming is pretty standard, nothing really jumps out or makes the game feel unique, which is somewhat of a shame. However, the game has a very natural way of teaching you new movement mechanics, where it sets up situations that you end up accidentally using said movement mechanics. There's something really nice about these moments when you finally realise that you've always been able to do something, you just hadn't done it yet.Puzzles are alright. You need to pay attention to the environment to solve them, and some of them were pretty satisfying to solve, but most of the time, they're really easy to solve, or even accidentally solve.Honestly? I think the game is worth it for its combat system alone, but if you think that having to do parries and dodges as well as timed inputs to do optimal damage is not for you, or the only part that brought you here is the metroidvania tag, I'd recommend looking elsewhere. Otherwise, it was a very unique and wonderful experience, if somewhat short due to the lack of fights.
