_childDocuments_.review: I first got into Ib way back when, when I was just a 11 year old running around the internet. I came across a bunch of RPGMaker-based horror games, and while I loved many, Ib is the one that stuck out in my mind for a long, long time. The characters stand out very strongly despite the shortness of the game, and all manage to shine in their own ways, and the aesthetics stuck with me as well-- it was my first exposure to a horror game, leading me further and further into the genre. I said many times it was my favorite game of all time. So of course I had high expectations for the remake, and kouri absolutely, 200% delivered. Even just opening the title screen and hearing the music made me feel like I was home. The visuals are amazing-- they're a direct upgrade to the original game's graphics (including fixing text readability issues), without sacrificing aesthetic or the heart of a classic RPGMaker game. In a gaming climate where a lot of games will clamor to have the new best, most glimmering, most advanced never-before-seen graphics advancements in the world, that classic RPGMaker vibe that doesn't fight to add every pore to its graphics imaginable is a breath of fresh air. It's pretty, charming, and the pixel art is absolutely gorgeous-- I found myself often using the zoom function just to take in the quality of some of the work.The only thing I can possibly criticize here is that I feel the game can hold your hand a little too much with its puzzles sometimes. It may just be the brain of someone who's been obsessed with this game for years, but I do feel sometimes the game did a little too much wink-wink nudge-nudge. Even so, that's preferable to no direction at all, and it's really just a minor gripe.I know it's easy to be blinded by nostalgia because of my fondness for this game. But doing my absolute best to be objective, Ib is still a haunting game with a story that has stood the test of time, and I think even if this is your absolute first time even learning it exists, you'll have a terribly great time in Guertena's gallery.I'm gonna talk about spoilers past this, but let it be known that even if you can only read this far-- Ib is 100% worth your time and money. It's a great, atmospheric little game perfect for even those new to the horror genre, while still being deeply unsettling. Great characters, great environment, great story, 10/10 any story with haunted art still makes me go crazy in a good way.[Story spoilers below this point.]The story is just how I remember it, seeming pretty directly lifted. Which is no problem at all, because Ib has always had a great story and it maintains here. A chilling atmosphere without needing to be over-the-top, the sense of deep, permeating unease drags you in, the idea that anything in the gallery could reach out for you at any time. The fact that there's only very occasional chases adds to this, making you just high-strung enough without letting you get too used to it. Chases are generally simple but still stressful-- the escape from the Toy Box will always make my heart pound. Garry is an incredibly charming, sweet character, reliable as the only adult but obviously still stressed and nervous. Ib is a silent protagonist, but it's made clear that she is still a young girl cracking under the pressure. Their reactions to the gallery seem very real, adding further to the uncanny valley of just how unsettling this place really would be for someone. And of course, Mary remains one of my favorite antagonists in any game -- a young child who you can't fully blame for her actions, likely not understanding human morality from being raised in the fabricated world, that just wants to be real, but the only option is to do something terrible. It makes her as scary as she is sympathetic, and I think that's a strength of Ib. The tragedy of how the gallery works, of this inherent imbalance where someone must be trapped forever or even die, makes it all the sadder. I want Mary to be happy, wanting to escape isn't a bad wish and the circumstances aren't her fault, but I don't want Ib or Garry to die in the fabricated world either. It's just people at the whims of the gallery, and that's what makes it so compelling. Not to mention how charming Mary is, just as much as the other two -- yes Mary you DO look so cute in your scarf.The new puzzles are very fun, and I think the ones that were replaced from the original game make sense -- for example, replacing the equation in the yellow area with the tree windup keys feels a lot more artsy and true to the gallery than doing math. The teacup puzzle was fun and made me remember I'm bad at sliding puzzles, and I'm obsessed with that cat thing in the gray area. Also, oh my god the last chase in the grey area is so much more stressful!! I say that positively!! The changes to the puzzles in that area as well as the insanely stressful chase are top-tier, and I love that the nightmare sequence is so much more horrifying and now has control. Paradoxically, being able to move in that only makes me feel even less in control-- it's amazing!I could go on forever, really, I could, about the new graphics, new puzzles, how charming all of the new Garry and Mary dialogue is (and the time it must have taken to add all of it!), the cute new talksprites and how painful the one of Mary starting to burn is... and all of the music, god I could genuinely just gush forever. Also, did the doll room get its timer shortened or is it just me? Scared the ♥♥♥♥ out of me. All in all, Ib remains my favorite game of all time. Play it now.

_childDocuments_.review: Every little detail matters. Ib is a game with multiple endings, requiring multiple playthroughs. Through each playthrough you’ll have to play differently, and for 100% completion almost every interaction matters. This makes Ib a memorable experience, with every area, puzzle, painting, character, and dialogue sequence being ingrained in your brain. This level of careful attention to detail, and overall quality of that detail, makes Ib one of the best RPG Maker games to date. The story itself is unique, and multi-layered, with repeated playthroughs containing details you’d miss on first glance. The game is also rather short, not feeling like a burden to repeat. The endings and extra interactions/dialogue sequences you’ll experience enhance your overall connection to the games characters and story. As someone who came into this with no expectations or prior knowledge, I’m ecstatic. Goosebumps covered me upon experiencing the true ending, overwhelmed with joy due to the trials needed to unlock it. While the gameplay is simple, given it’s a RPG Maker game, Ib manages to explore various different puzzles, each unique, culminating to the completion of each area. These get progressively more challenging, with some even requiring the use of multiple characters to finish.The games True Guertena Exhibit is the icing on top, as you explore an exhibit featuring all the games art work, music, and endings, requiring 100% completion to finish. Also the bonus content you unlock on second playthrough feels like a sizeable expansion to the games content/story, so you have more to look forward to outside of whatever ending you’re going for. Ib is one of those games that feels “perfect”, with no real issues outside of personal taste or nitpicks. An indie classic that needs to be experienced.

_childDocuments_.review: Ib is a very short and cute little game. one of the staples of the RPGhorror genre.you play as little 9-year old Ib (pronounced "Ebe" (probably meant to be Eve?? but Japan doesn't have the letter 'V' to it turned to "Ebe")) exploring a spooky little art gallery filled with not very friendly paintings and artworks. The puzzles you have to go through are fairly simple yet still fun to solve. soem can be pretty head-scratching too.the background music is eerie and sets-up the game's atmosphere nicely.the pixel art and character portraits are well-made and unique in it's own right. Though the game has "horror" as one the tags, it's really not that scary. But i don't really see that as a negative. it just means it's more accesible to folks who may not be all too fond of jumpscares (speaking of which, there're like, 2 jumpscares at best in this game. The horror mostly comes from the unsettling imagery depicted through it's simple pixel graphics.The story itself is very simple and cute. it has it's moments, some twists and turns, but overall i'd consider it pretty average amongst other 2D story-based pixel RPGs with hints of depression™. I'd put the story to be on par with Mad Father, but sliiiiiiiightly lower. by a veeeeery small margin.idk how this game is priced in other countries but i'd definitely recommend picking it up when it's on sale.7.9/10 game very cute and simple.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adore this game. The soundtrack is iconic and I still listen to it to this day, Mary's Theme in particular has sat with me for years. It feels obvious to say the game feels interactive and lively when the main premise is about works of art trying to attack you, but I don't know how else to describe. I love the little details when you interact with the different pieces, the world of Ib definitely feels immersive. We only get to really know three characters, one of them being Ib who is the player character, but the personality both Garry and Mary have never get bored. Especially now that I am already I have a greater appreciation for Garry, who has always been a favorite character of mine. Mary is a character I could talk about forever, but I am glad people sympathize with her more. I still have no clue how people despised this nine year old lol. The dialogue that comes from these two characters never gets old and, even though it might not be a lot dialogue, fleshes out them out a ton.Phenomenal game with phenomenal art, music, and characters. I can not recommend this game enough.

_childDocuments_.review: While there is a numerous amount of horror themed adventure games made on RPG Maker, I’ve never been fond of them usually. There have been some good examples here and there, but more often than not these games leaned too hard either in pure tasteless jumpscare territory or were simply too poorly written, relying on shock value or extreme themes. Due to that, I had no knowledge of Ib when it became an extremely popular free game back in the early 2010s and would have not paid attention to this 2022 updated (and no longer free) remake, if not for catching a few streams and videos on it. I am glad, however, that other people promoted this little gem and that I got to experience it for myself.Ib is a short horror themed adventure about a little girl who finds herself in a strange world where paintings come to life. And as it often happens with these RPG Maker based titles, it avoids the combat completely, instead focusing on avoiding enemies and traps and solving problems and puzzles. There are no special mechanics like stealth here, nor are the puzzles usually hard, so the game focuses mostly on just delivering a good story driven experience with lots of small and huge variations depending on how you play. Nicely enough, despite having quite a few different endings, the game isn’t really focused on this aspect as well and as far as “unlocks” go, you only need to get a few of them, with the rest of endings only existing to provide an interesting reaction to your choices through the game and occasionally learn some little additional thing about the characters.Despite being a horror story and having some genuinely creepy ideas, the overall atmosphere of the game is more reminiscent of a darker folk tale or something one might expect from Through the Looking-Glass, and What Alice Found There. Which works really well and completely avoids the typical for these games issue of going for the gore or overdone tropes. Most of the puzzles in the game, I’d even say all of the ones in the main playthrough, are really fun too. While the extended playthrough, that is available upon replays, has some weaker moments, it’s still really fun. The visuals and the music are also really nice and the simplicity of style works really well for the game.I really enjoyed playing the game and my only real complaint is that due to the engine choice and overall style, the game runs in a rather small resolution by today’s standards and can become less comfortable to run in the future as resolutions increase. But it’s a rather minor thing and I could easily recommend anyone who likes horror themed adventure games to check Ib remake from 2022 out.

They invite you to read and explore without getting lost anywhere. There is also a lot to discover and find in-game, and there are several endings. The downside is that for most of them you will need to play through the whole game several times. Also choices do matter here, more than you will expect!
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Very charming and interesting little rpgmaker game. Story-wise, you are trapped in an odd art museum. The main focus of the gameplay is puzzles, often related to the artwork featured in the exhibitions you'll see. By completing puzzles, you hope to break out of the museum. Ib has a bit of a horror feel to it, but I wouldn't call is a horror game. It's more puzzle, narrative, and choices matter. If you are a completionist this may be a good game for you, because you are encouraged to collect all the artwork featured throughout the game. There are also a good number of different endings. Personally I got the few that were easy for me to get without replaying the whole game and called it, but if going back and seeing how every option affects the outcome of the story is your thing, you can do that. I was a bit confused as to why the puzzles and overall environment existed at all, but the game was fun and charming enough I can overlook that small qualm. It's a good game!
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Although I have only played a few hours, this game has already claimed a petal of the roses of my heart.Truly brilliant and thought-after puzzles and a unique ambiance that curtains every moment of game play. If you liked Yume Nikki, Omori, Mad father, or classic rpg maker games; then this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: very classic game. i never had gotten the chance to play it, but i remember watching many people play it.the story is still intriguing even though i already knew what was going to happen, and i still love garry as much as i did several, several years ago.it is pretty short but there is the exhibition if you want to complete that. the updated graphics and small features are also quite nice.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: This is incredibly nostalgic for me. While I never got to play the original, I watched multiple people play this game when I was in my early teens. I was obsessed with the story and the characters stole my heart. This remake is incredibly faithful to it's predecessor and has a nice polish to it without taking from the original experience. I love this game so much, made it a personal goal to achieve the best ending, and felt as though I was reuniting with an old friend for a moment. Highly recommend even if you're not big into horror. This is definitely a great first step into the territory and I speak from experience saying that. Play this game at least once all the way through, I promise it's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: It's not just a porting version, it's a remake of the original.The main story and all endings have not changed, but the details have changed.It was as scary as Resident Evil2 (1998), at least to me.Every single playthrough will take less than 3 hours.It's an old game, but still one of the best pixel graphic RPG.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: I don't mean to be a downer on the way the game is right now because it's great. It would, however, be nice if the original version of the game was available. I would imagine that some people (like me) would like to play the original version for nostalgia reasons. Thank you. Sorry if this seems rude, it was not intended to be.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Being someone who went into this game blind, this is probably one of my favorite RPGMaker horror games of all time.It's chilling atmosphere and unique puzzles really sold me, but my favorite part about this game is its characters! Even though you know little about them, they leave a lasting impact. The game focuses less on the lore behind the museum and more on the characters, which is pretty refreshing. (I actually got the true ending first time around because I liked talking to Garry so much!)The gameplay itself was really fun. Ib really kept me on my toes! Of course the puzzles were a delight, but I enjoyed collecting all of the art pieces too! Plus, I love how your choices throughout the game contradict what ending you get, especially the doom counter. In most games your choices don't mean much until the end. I ended up replaying the game a LOT of times..I definitely recommend it!!
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since it's original release in 2012, I loved this game from beginning to end. From the puzzles, the story, and of course the characters that come to life in the work of the artist. Being able to play a remake of this game gave me nostalgia feels, while there are differences compared to the original. I'm glad to play this version of the game, so whether you go for the classic or the remake, I hope you enjoy the beauty and horror inside the gallery.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Not much has changed story-wise from the original. The visuals have been improved, some puzzles replaced with simpler ones, there is a bunch of new dialogue for the characters, but the horror aspect has been toned down in favour of a more 'atmospheric puzzle game' feeling.Overall, not an extreme "remake" like The Witch's House MV or YUMENIKKI -DREAM DIARY-, but a welcome improvement anyway, if only because it evokes nostalgia.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: This was a cute, yet creepy adventure.  There is no combat.  Occasionally, you'll need to avoid enemies.  Lots of puzzle solving, lots of collecting.The story is pretty interesting and actually gives the game a lot of replay value.  You cannot 100% the game without playing it a few times.  Luckily, you can skip any dialogue, but not scripted animations.  Lots of secrets that contribute to the player's understanding of what's happening.  Still, even if you complete and collect everything, it's up to you to mentally figure out what the deal is.Certain decisions affect the outcome of the game, while others merely affect what others say or how things behave or look.  There is a certain character whose fate depends on your decisions, as well as how good your relationship is with them.  The progress of these items is not shown, but is otherwise hinted at with different actions or dialogue.  It's a little complex, but nothing a guide wouldn't help with, should you wish to use one.Ultimately, this is a great game for completionists and those who are fans of creepy retro visuals and art-based themes.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: A horror game disguised as an artbook... or maybe the other way around?The remake mostly changed the room layouts along with some puzzles (mostly making them way easier and less scary), but not without their additions. Personally I find the addition of the chat button to be cute; it's not just a hint button but with it you can kind of learn more about their personalities. Wished it was longer and at least a tad bit harder, but I cherished every second of it, and some of their artworks themselves I find them worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: the remake is so much better than the original! the visuals improved so much and there was a lot of content added. classic rpgmaker horror every fan of this genre should play. the horror element is good and characters are really likeable. 10/10 ost. i love the chat option that they added here in the remake as it not only helps with puzzles but also gives more insight into characters. the only thing i could complain about is that there is only one achievment to get but that's just my personal preference that i would want more. one of the best rpgmaker horrors, definitely. garry's the best boi i luv him <33
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Ib has always been my favorite RPG so I was so excited to hear it was coming to Steam. Playing it, however, is bittersweet. In many ways it's still the same game I know and love, but many things have also changed. I feel the original art style for sprites, roses, pause menu, etc was much more unique and pretty than its newer, rounder, and more modern art style. I enjoy the new puzzles it has to offer as well as the same beautiful soundtrack. I mostly just miss the old hand drawn looking aspect of the game. I still love this game though ❤️ 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: 12/10Timeless Classic RPG maker horror game. Ib was one of my first experiences with RPG maker horror, and it left a great impression on me. The game is typical maker fashion, with added horror elements. Ib has a lot of puzzles that are easy to solve if u just pay attention. It has multiple endings, with only 3 being "main" endings? The characters are Ib, Gary and Mary. These 3 have been around for like 10 years now. This remake adds a bunch of new things which I didn't expect, new sprites, new levels, redesigneed rooms etc. Kouri even added a button to speak with your party members, which is even more dialogue + lore. The "horror" aspect of Ib remains as it was 10 years ago, it's not scary for me, this is true even now. But what drew me in was the story itself. Emotional and unique. Overall very good remake, hopefully more people are exposed to Ib.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Ib is the first real horror game I've had growing up and my favorite of all time. The original game held a special place in my heart and when it came to recommending new people into horror, I would always recommend this game first. Everything in it was brilliant at the time and breathtaking as a child, the puzzles, the horror, being on edge, the hints, characters, atmosphere, everything was so unique compared to other horror games. It was more of a puzzle game to be fair and dived into it's story and character development more than it's horror element but that's what also made the moments where there where horror hit and hit hard. I'll never forget the moment where I was alone as Gary and meet that stupid doll, the moment where I was alone with Mary but still felt mistrust against her before I knew of her true nature, and lastly when being thrown into that toy box and trying to escape for the first time. All these moments are deep in my memory and will stay there. Though the one thing that really made me stay in this game other than the horror aspects and the puzzles, was Gary and Ib. I've never before cared much for a pixel that much, Each interaction, each moment together, and finally the end where Gary remembers Ib broke me to where I cried tears of joy to see that he remembers everything they went to. i could never forget all the times I was scared but I could never forget the times where his beautiful Guitar calmed me in these moments, to give me strength to carry on.Now, does this extent into the remake? Yes but also no. I enjoyed the Remake and I spent 12+ hours getting all 150 artworks without looking online(or trying to). I loved more interactions with Gary, I loved the new visuals, and New Puzzles. Though I wish there was more. Once I was done with the game I felt accomplished yet still not whole... like there needed to be more added to call this a remake. It also didn't help that some of the puzzles where removed to make the game easier, which I thought was taking away from the original. Overall, the only complaint I have is that I wish that there was more in this game. Then again, I had that same complaint in the original but this is a remake... it desires more. Perhaps a sequel? Though I doubt there will be one. Perhaps do the same with Mad father or Witches house and have a harder difficulty in the game which adds a secret ending or a new room, that would honestly help but that is up to the creator. P.S.If you're the creator of this beautiful Remake. Thank you for bringing me back to my childhood, back to simpler times, and making it overall feel like a brand new experience. Even though I wish there was more as stated before, this is still a damn fantastic remake that I'd recommend anyone. This will always be apart of my Memories.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: AaaaaaaaaaThis game will always hold a special place in my heart. I played the original and I'm glad for this remake.A small but very memorable cast of characters especially as you observe how their behaviours and interactions are moulded by the circumstances of the gallery that makes you sorrowful when you realise after getting all the endings that that will all you'll see of them. Very sad.While the graphic upgrades are not as drastic as I initially expected, they are still a considerable improvement over the original. As for the gameplay itself, I do enjoy most of the changes and additons of some of the room layouts and puzzles, adding a little bit more depth to some of the areas (as well as new artworks) and simplifying some welcome aspects though for one I feel like the sketchbook part, while I do enjoy some of the changed bits has overall become too simplified and less challenging but maybe that was the intention. Another part is the doll room which in the original I could consistently find the key but in this version I feel like I fail more often than  any case, overall I still highly enjoy and will fondly remember the game and I'd recommend it to anyone regardless of their genre preference. Alas, I again still wish to see more of the characters but I'm still grateful for a loving remake after ten years.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: I've been in love with most of the immersion aspects of the game since the original release back in 2012. Although I've noticed some significant changes in this remake, it felt as if I was replaying my Ib experience only that Ib was a completely new and refined game. Overall the story is short, but has different endings and the experience is phenomenal.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: One of, if not the BEST RPG Maker series remakes. I've loved Ib since the og came out when I was a kid. When I learned that there was going to be a remake, I was ecstatic! The remake has better graphics, smoother gameplay and more lore added on compared to the OG. ALSO, YOU CAN TALK TO GARRY AND MARY NOW! I LOVE THAT!!!!!! I'm so happy they added more to Ib and gave it tons of love. This game is WORTH THE MONEY! Garry is Bae. Don't trust Mary. PLAY THIS GAME IT'S WORTH YOUR TIME AND MONEY!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is mostly walking around and solving puzzles. The puzzles are not very difficult. The only time I got stuck was when I forgot to pick up an item.The story is very good and the characters are compelling.I would recommend playing it 2 or 3 times. Anything beyond that gets kind of repetitive since very little changes in most of your choices until the end, you're better off watching a video of the endings you didn't get.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: A classic, and for good reason! It remains spooky and charming even all these years later, and the puzzles are a good time too! The only problem is that I beat it pretty dang quickly, so it's a bit of a hard sell for 12 dollars if you're focused on a time:money ratio. That being said, I've watched playthroughs of the game in the past, meaning the puzzles were quicker than average, and there does seem to be a degree of replay value here. I know there are variations to the endings, and it seems like there's some extra content after beating the game. I'm gonna leave it for another time, though. Overall, I'd highly recommend it if you're wanting for an experience that sticks with you despite a short runtime. If it's on sale, definitely go for it. As I said initially, it's highly regarded for a reason, and it's still worth your time if you haven't been spoiled on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: This is my all time favorite game. I love the characters, music art and as someone that adores the original i love the parts that they changed because it gives more of a challenge than it would've had if it was exactly the same. It's so easy to fall in love with the characters personality and designs. Overall a 10/10 game
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Ib is such a masterpiece. The horror aspects, the atmosphere of the game. It really pulls your heartstrings as you feel for the characters involved who are scared and terrified of the situation they have to endure. You really don't need ultra graphics to make a quality game, and that's how RPG like games get right every time. The quality of the story, they way you can interact with the other characters that you've been stuck in this hellish like art gallery makes for an authentic experience that I personally love. I recommend the game. Nice work :D
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to recommend yes in the first 10 minutes of game play.  Very enjoyable romp through an art museum with multiple endings (I will admit I'm not a completionist so I only played till I got through my first ending) for those who like playing in new game+ there are multiple opportunities to discover new things.  In my opinion $13 is a bit steep for the 3 hours it will take to play through the first time so I would wait for a sale.  Overall this game had me interested from start to finish and had some really great moments.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: I usually only buy games when they're on sale, but Ib is a very special case. I'm buying this full-price as payment for all of the original free versions of this game I've enjoyed playing over the years! I love Ib so much, and I love this remake version! It's familiar, but also fresh in a lot of ways. Well worth the time getting every ending and unlocking the full gallery.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: I have come to play this game over and over again. First when I was maybe 12 and had downloaded it off some sketchy site, then again when I had gotten a new laptop, then again when I had gotten a new computer. Finally, I played it again when it was released on Steam. Throughout all these playthroughs, I have never been bored. While most of the puzzles and story have been the same, I was never tired of it. This is seriously one of my favorite horror rpg maker games. This game has a special place in my heart. 10/10 everyone should play.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: This was an amazing game when it first came out, and this remake is even better.The new art looks amazing and the new puzzles are more creative and interesting.The story is mostly the same, but the original story was pretty much perfect.Overall, this game provides great value for new and old fans alike.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Originally played this game back in Winter 2012 and it still remains to be one of, if not, my favorite RPG Maker game 10 years later.The features like the updated sprites are really nice and the the ability to talk with Garry (And Mary) is a really nice quality of life feature for those who are playing through for the first time.I think my only real gripe about this new version is the replacing of Mary's theme with a new track only because it was ingrained into my memory for so long that it threw me off when I heard the new track instead of the original midi song that was used in the original version. Despite that, it's still a good song nonetheless.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: The moment I mentioned I was gonna play this game, I had all sorts of friends pop out of the woodwork going "Ib?!?! OMG IB!!!!" and recalling stories of the olden days when they would skip class just to play Ib as a group. Wish I could have been there because this is a game worth being nostalgic for. As a horror game, it gets the atmosphere just right and the guitar music they chose for this game is perfect for that melancholy art gallery. Highly recommend if you're in the mood for a classic RPGmaker game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: A game I loved when it first came out. I got lost in the world this game crafted, and adored finding all the endings. When I saw it was getting remade I was both excited and nervous. Thankfully, I can now say this new version is just as enjoyable and engrossing as the original, even with some changes that make me miss the older game if only a bit. If you like whimsical and eerie pixel horror games, this one is worth every cent.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. It will hit you with a bunch of nostalgia if you already played the first version, it is also refreshing and entertaining. Several details have been changed and more things have been added which makes me wanna get this game complete at 100%, enjoyable and recommended even if you haven't played the first version.Also, must protec Gary!<3
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Ib is a masterpiece talking about Horror RPGs; an incredible story mixed with well-descripted characters with strong emotional impact; a great bunch of awesome and engaging OSTs and a highly pleasureful art style! I've been playing Ib since the first release in 2014, and i've always loved Kouri's work and effort, the 2021 remake, has been a great pleasure.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: i was so excited when i saw this that i bought it before it had an english translationjoining the trend of remaking/remastering rpgmaker games, ib joins the steam store with a new coat of paint, and a really nice overhaul of the game. the small changes, like new puzzles, were really nice. not very long, but i think it's a necessary experience if you're trying to recreate late 2000s-2010s nostalgia
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original and Im a big fan of Ib. When I randomly tipped "Ib remake" in google, I couldnt believe my eyes when it really got announced. So Im really happy that it got released this year. The new Graphics are amazing, many things are waaay better, like the font, but also some puzzles got reworked and are better now. Only thing I dont really like, is the artwork you get, when finally read (the full Title) of every Artwork with Ib. Was a bit disappointing. But Im sill really happy that this game got a remake
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best rpg maker games, is up there with the likes of "The Witch's House", "Yume Nikki", "Mad Father", "Misao", etc.The thing that separates this game from the rest is, that it actually has a good story that poses a very simple philosophical tesis, wich is "the world is a percieved world". Each character has their own interpretation of the world, and they percive it through their own posibilities, their own background and knowledge of the world.For example, Ib doesn't know many words, so her perception and knowledge of this world is very limited, and so will be yours looking it throug her eyes. It also has a commentary in Barthe's Death of the author, the "main villain" of the story being a painting and all, invites us to think the art as more than what an author can concive. This also connects with the world as a perception on the self, one then learns more about themself by the way they percieve things, and every character even the villain is in a journey of selfknowldege.The puzzles are also quite fun, even more so the new ones, the new area is fine if a little short, and the special room is one of the greatest additions to this game. It improves significantly upon the original, but it also censores some aspects, like the imagery of death and suicide in the final area, wich is a minor complain. I recommend this version to old fans of the original and newcomers, it is a great and thought provoking experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: One of the classic Indie Horrors of the past.While the remaster is effectively the exact same game there are some small changes to some areas/puzzles and the ending routes have been slightly tweaked around a new "mechanic" while still retaining the previous "checks" for endings.I will say however, the additional interactions between the characters with the new talking "mechanic" is quite nice, nothing too major, but it's sweet to see more dialogue between the leads.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Truly one of the most iconic RPG horror games out there. I'm so glad the remake is just as amazing as the original with little extra bits and pieces to make it somewhat different. Amazing story, love the scary atmosphere and the characters are still dear to my heart almost 10 years later since I first played the original game. Forever recommend <3
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so happy I finally got around to playing this! I practically grew up with Ib and I have played it so many times in my lifetime. I was excited to play it again, and enjoyed the new puzzles and the new sprites and artwork, which are so much more expressive than the old ones. Plus there's an actual button to talk to Garry! Everything I've ever dreamed of. I was very glad to be able to play it with my controller, too.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: If I had to recommend an RPG maker game that's not Omori to someone I would recommend Ib :DWith this I'm not downgrading or comparing either games with one another, Omori is my favorite and Ib is a close second.The game goes in much deeper detail than most RPGM games, what with simple yet captivating graphics and with puzzles that are simple but straight to the point and don't take away from the story line.Only recently did I actually play the entirety of the game (by which I mean I got each possible obtainable ending and unlockable for the achievement) and I have to say I've fallen in love with it even more.The characters are likable and understandable, Garry being a perfect depiction of a devoted stranger turned friend in a tight situation, where his actions clearly show how caring he is of Ib (who knows knows).With as little spoilers as I can, I highly recommend this game to anyone that loves the RPG maker category, and especially to those that played them a while back when they were at it's peak. If you played Ib before (the free version) this Steam version is a subtle but appropriate and beautiful remake, with better graphics and certain gameplay values. ALSO, it serves as a 'thank you' and support to the maker, which I think is very well deserved.This game awoke a lot of pleasant emotions in me and I think everyone should experience them as well :D
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: I've known about Ib since it released back in 2012 and, ho boy, this remake does not disappoint. Ib's wonderful plot can't be described without spoilers, and I urge you to play game for yourself. The game's use of dramatic irony cannot be understated, and the plot twists are twisty.I don't often cry to games/movies/whatever. In real life? I'm a crying little ♥♥♥♥♥. But games have to try hard to get me to cry. Ib succeeded, which I consider a major win for it's immersion. Little details, like Ib not knowing certain words because she's a young girl, make this game all the better.The remake itself is a major glowup. I've wanted to buy this ever since I found out about the remake before it released, but by the time it was localized to english, I didn't have the time (or the $13.00 to spend). This was worth every penny of tax Steam took from me though. It's such a short, simple game, but the puzzles are fun, and the story is genuinely incredible. (There is one gripe I have with the pacing, but I can't go into it without spoilers, so just know I acknowledge it.)Ib is wonderful, and you should by it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: The game is excellent, I played it a long time ago in its first versions and now it's something completely new, 10/10.But it can get even betterthere are small fps hitches in the game menu and in some scenarios it still gives small fps hitches.It would also be a good option to add the option to play in full screen.but they should definitely add the translation to Spanish so that many more people can play it.excellent game congratulations, I was waiting for this remake.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Really good horror/adventure/puzzle game with emphasis on solving creepy puzzles. This game was worth my time and it's worth yours. There are multiple possible endings. If you enjoyed the Team Silent  games, you will probably enjoy this. It's not nearly as gross or depressing or even scary by comparison but you will get the creeps and you will have to run for your life more than a few times.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: I remember playing this back in 2012 when it was initially released and it's still just as incredible now as it was back then. Despite the existence of the free version, this new addition is worth every penny. If you never had a chance to try it out then I absolutely recommend you do so. Especially if you are a fan of pixel horror or RPG Maker horror games.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: I had originally played the 2012 version so seeing this amazing little game get a remake was heart warming. Some of the puzzles have been replaced or taken out (They were a pain in the original) I love how the only achievement for this game is finding all the art pieces. there are 150 in the whole game which sounds like a lot but its nothing if you have been looking at the paintings on the walls throughout your play through. Its a collectable trophy I didn't want to die getting. Of course the graphs look a lot better then the originals- which is nice because the text was kinda hard to read in the 2012 version but that problem is fixed in the remake ( CG's also look cleaner) The only problem I had was getting the "Promise of Reunion" I think this was because you have to talk to Garry a LOT you will be spamming E every where you go. You also have to make the right choices of course- Other then this my play through's were fun and nostalgic.In all I was super happy with this remake and seeing one of my childhood favourite games getting some love made me really happy.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Literally a remaster of my favorite JRPG. 1000/10 Seriously though the original game was always held dear to my heart so this new version was a treat to play. The graphic had an upgrade, new content was added and overall the game gotten a new breath of life into it. What I appreciated the most was the simplification of communication with Gary and Mary making the achieving all endings simpler than the original. I ADORED that we were able to get to interact and know Gary more because he had always been a favorite of mine.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who absolutely adored the original to death, this was one of the best things I ever heard when I saw the steam remake announcement. Truly outstanding, I love the visual upgrades, the puzzle changes are fun even if a little less difficult in places (I don't mind at all!).You have a talk to Garry button, what more could you want?Played through it all to get all the endings and paintings, loved every step of the way again, 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Okay. I know only 0.5 hours on record BUT I played it when it was still an rpg maker free game. I am so happy I can see Garry again and love him like I always didWe STAN Garry and will do everything for him. This game may have founded a cult but I am truly happy to be a part of this cult that worships Garry
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: This remake was alot better than i expected!After finishing absolutely everything i think i can give this review.I recommend this to even the people who have already played the original as this changes quite a bit of stuff, which in turn made me more engaged to want to know what changed.An amazing remake to an already amazing game, 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Still my favorite horror game! I played this when I was a kid, like a lot, and now I will still play this gem for more years to come. And I still have a crush on Garry, he's still wholesome and kind in my memory and the fact that this remake added a lot of his dialogue makes it even better! I also love the post-game extra content that is newly added in the remake, that area is just dang cool! and also collecting all the paintings makes it rewarding because of the achievement. Thank you for this amazing game, Kouri!
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not as scary people say it is, apart from a sudden sounds, and some nightmarish imagery, but anyway, a lot of the paintings in the game are really good works of pixel art, which is the game itself, which I recommend if you would like a game that is simplistic, but story-driven with dark themes than Yume Nikki which is still very dark but more focused on exploration
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: A nice remake of the original, I'd always go back and replay the original just for fun since it was a personal favorite of the RPG horror genre for me. Now that there's this remake, it's a lot nicer to have a slightly more updated and newer version of Ib to mess around in. It sticks to its roots, and nicely adds some more stuff to it. Thanks for the nostalgia hit.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: I played Ib as a kid on rpgmaker, so seeing it come back alongside Mad Father and Misao is incredible. I loved playing Ib when I was younger, and I love the remake now! It's still got that soft, slow creeping horror that I adore, and the world is so vast and leaves you wanting for more. _childDocuments_.review: If I had to summarize my feelings for this game, Ib could be described as a horror rpg that is unique and is personally one of my favorite indie games to play. You take on the role of a girl named Ib, whom visits an art exhibition by the artist Guertena with her parents. It's not long after wandering into the gallery alone that Ib enters into another world and must pass multiple puzzles and countless killer artworks to escape. From the beginning, Ib's graphics are absolutely stunning, with the game feeling very artsy yet having a touch of horror as the game's theme and genre suggests. Being a remake of the original game released in 2012, all of the graphics have been updated, including a major revamp of the character busts, the option to zoom into the game, and some of the obstacles/layout having been changed. Despite this, the game retains the aesthetic of the original in contrast to other remakes such as The Witch's House and Mad Father, which helps it give off the same feel as it's predecessor.There's not much to say about Ib's ost other than it is the same from the original. That being said, each song fits well with where you are in the game and it's cutscenes.One of the best thing about Ib are the choices you can make throughout the game that can lead to different endings. What makes Ib unique in this regard is rather than solely making choices to a certain ending, interaction with characters and the environment is also a big factor in what ending you get. This not only helps you get invested in getting to know the characters more and analyze your surroundings, but it is also something that helps Ib stand out as most games with multiple endings I feel only focus on doing a certain action or choice rather than taking advantage of the game itself. It really shows the potential of what doing or not doing can really have on a game.In conclusion, playing Ib was a fun experience that while lasting only a few hours, it really shows how much a single developer is capable of doing and how enjoyable a game can be despite it's length. Would definitely recommend to horror game fans and for people looking for something in the horror genre yet not too scary to make you jump out of your boots!
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Ib is a short journey, but its brief playtime means it doesn't overstay its welcome (for reference, at time of review, I have completed one of the endings. There is replay value here). It's sufficiently creepy as opposed to being scary. The updated menus and sprites are a treat to look at, and it's nice to see Ib's Parents this time around. Aside from the addition of a master gallery to track which endings you've acquired, however, not much seems to have changed. If you loved it then, you'll love it all the more now (which is why I'm excusing the high price tag on it-- I downloaded the original version for free years ago and fell in love with the game, and I want to see the developer hopefully make more. Thank you very much, kouri, for the experience long ago and the decision to remake it and make it available on Steam).If you've never played Ib before, I wholeheartedly recommend it. (3/5)

_childDocuments_.review: Ib is yet more evidence that video games are a fantastic medium for storytelling. If you are looking for a horror game, you can find far scarier games, and admittedly, if you're looking for a good story-focused game, you could find better. But what makes this game good is the big picture. This game is a unique combination of things. It's eerie yet adorable. It's deep in it's own way, yet doesn't come off as pretentious. It's creepy, but not lonely. It has a small, yet lovable and memorable cast. For these reasons, I say that this is a fantastic "gateway horror game", for someone who is too scared to play things like Resident Evil or Silent Hill. The whole "RPG Maker Horror" genre can be considered great gateway horror games, but Ib in particular has something special about it. Unlike many horror games, RPG or otherwise, this game never kills you unfairly, and is really easy to boot. This was the very first horror game I ever finished, several years ago. This remake doesn't change a whole lot (although area layouts are different) but it gave me a reason to play through this great game again.

_childDocuments_.review: The original Ib released in 2012 was my first introduction to the RPG horror genre. This is the game that inspired me to learn more about (and eventually dabble in) game making, and Kouri's blog gave me some of my first resources to start that progress. I think it goes without saying at this point, but I was more than excited to see that a remake was on the way!If I'm being honest, I was a little worried that the major hype I had going in would make my expectations a little high- but *wow* was I wrong! The remake is a perfect blend of old and new, containing not only a polished new look but refreshing puzzles to keep it interesting for returning players. Oh, and I can't forget to mention my favorite non-spoiler part of the remake, the loads of new dialogue added to every single area of the game- really makes the whole game feel so much more personal and special.Whether you're new to Ib or a returning player, you're in for a treat. _childDocuments_.review: The Ib Remake still offers that same endearing narrative experience to new players as the original and also makes a good number of changes to surprise older, more familiar fans.The art is as charming as ever, still maintaining the RPG Maker 2003 style while also adding details to sprites from the original. Kouri's new drawings for the game still keep with his iconic style from the original game. All of the art pieces featured in the game are now detailed enough to discern the subjects instead of merely representing a few pixels.The music still uses the iconic YASUPOCHI Guitar Diary arrangements from the original game. Despite the quality of the recordings, they still manage to fit the story beats well emotionally. A lot of the original music has been replaced and don't feel as iconic as their originals, but new additions also seem more appropriate for the narrative than the original's smaller soundtrack.Kouri's writing is still solid. The world of Ib definitely feels like fleshed out with moving parts, characters aren't flat and a lot can be discerned about them and the world they live in from dialogue and environmental objects. A new gameplay feature  allows players to experience even more of this world building, with it being responsive to real time interactions with the environment or story events.The English translation was solid with minimal typos every now and then. The only arguable negative for this game is its relatively short length. This is, however, made up for in replayability: multiple endings and an optional collectathon on top of Kouri's writing makes paced and slower playthroughs more enjoyable.As a fan of Ib since its rise to cult internet status in the early 2010s, I played the original executable file from a thumb drive in elementary school. With its 2022 remake, I'm happy that Kouri can finally make a consistent profit from their most popular work.

_childDocuments_.review: Ib is a legendary game that everyone should experience at least once. A few things are changed, the art looks better overall (if a bit less stylised) some puzzles are different and some new stuff was added. The big new feature is the talk button which adds a ton of new dialogue to the game and gives Garry and Mary things to say in each room, and even give hints for certain puzzles. Adds a lot to overall character development.Only complaint is that a handful of puzzles and areas were removed, which is unfortunate as it made the remake a bit shorter and easier. Also they removed the games most iconic song (Puppet) for some reason.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very different kind of remaster than most of the other RPGmaker horror remasters that have been done.  Rather than just porting the original to the new engine with a few updates and changes while they're at it, this instead takes all of the stuff that made the original memorable and rebuilt the entire game focusing on moments like those.  While a lot of the scares and complex puzzles have either been simplified or removed, all of the art pieces, character interactions, and weird humor are still there with more added to them.  If you mainly liked the horror from the original then you might want to stick with that version but if you liked the story and environments then this is very much worth picking up.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to try my best to be brutally honest here, only because I believe all new players and RPG horror veterans alike should understand what they are getting into when considering this version of the game.If, as of reading this sentence, you haven't played the original Ib, go do it. Now.The original Ib is one of the most, if not THE most, titular game of the horror RPG genre. It is compelling, scary, the soundtrack and characters are iconic and lovable in every sense of the word, and most impressively, IT'S FREE. You can go out and  and get the same experience that this $13 Steam copy would give you, minus the redundant GUI changes and saddening puzzle removals.So, why am I recommending this game?Well, because I personally don't think this Steam version of the game is bad, but I also don't think it's anything new. My love for Ib and it's developers practically require that I throw my money at them, especially because the original is free and untouched from any new changes.Let's look at a game like The Witch's House compared to The Witch's House MV.The Witch's House was freeware which utilized default RPG Maker VX graphics, and, while dated, the storytelling and simple execution was done as perfectly as it was in it's newer counterpart. So why would I urge you to buy and play The Witch's House MV over it's original? The Witch's House MV not only completely overhauls the outdated graphics, replacing them with beautifully hand-drawn sprites, but rewards the player with a brand new difficulty setting as well, (in the same vain as Mad Father's remake) which expands upon the lore, what made these games so satisfying in the first place.What is different about the original Ib and it's Steam counterpart?(Spoilers ahead, by the way.)The UI for displaying your health is different (personally harder to differentiate). Some of the puzzles have been changed arbitrarily. One of the most iconic songs of the original soundtrack has been completely replaced, assumedly due to licensing issues. There is pop out sprites for dialogue now. A lot of the original sounds have been changed, more often than not to its own detriment (such as the roar when a painting or statue comes to life). The game looks almost completely identical visually. The way the game is now designed has, consequently, become less horror and more drama. The best thing I can give this version is the rework of the talking mechanic, along with a mass of new Garry dialogue.TL;DR Play the free version of Ib , if you haven't. If, afterwards, you want to support the developers, as I did, buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly faithful remake! Successfully preserves everything that made the original game so good while overhauling the jankier aspects of certain puzzles- or introducing completely new ones in their place.After playing the game for a while and watching other people play the game, I had gotten so used to the new UI and text boxes that I was surprised to see just how different the game looks compared to the original, even though I barely even thought about it while playing!Overall, I'm very happy with this remake. This is the definitive way to play Ib. Worth the price tag.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: The same good ol' rpg maker horror game from 10 years ago. Some puzzles have been tweaked or changed outright, but those changes are mostly welcome. There are some new additions, too, and they're pretty fun. It's also a short game (I completed all the endings and the gallery in under 7 hours), but I think that's to the game's benefit. It's a classic, so if you haven't played it and have any interest in it then you should give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: If you've never played the original, the game is worth buying not only by the fact that it supports the creator. But there is also a couple new endings, the presentation is generally better, and there is more characterization to characters having you enjoy them more. With the puzzles being better than the original.Ok, so if you've played the original Ib. Then yes, I can tell you that the game is worth buying. It's got all the extra content from the original Ib with an added "Press E for Banter" button, that way you can hear what Gary or Mary has to say. The endings also are a lot easier to get than in the original, but it still has a similar style which has the game checking if you've done certain acts in certain amount of times.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: an old favorite game of mine, finally on steam (remade, too!). shorter than i remembered, but that's not a bad thing. "short but sweet", i'd say.if you are worried about jumpscares, the ones in here, if you can even call them that, are very, very mild. trust me, i'm a super weenie baby when it comes to jumpscares and i didn't get startled once. no screamers or anything like that, which i appreciate.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: I've never been this happy for a remake. Playing Ib as a kid, the game was a big part in my life growing up. Being able to relive the story and meet the characters once again, but at the same time getting positively suprised at all the new puzzles and add-ons really made this a wonderful and refreshing experience. Thank you Kouri! I'll never forget Ib!
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Ib is a simple but compelling experience that embodies some of the more subtle aspects of what I love about games. I played the original years ago as a free, RPG maker game. This version features the unique aspects that made the original so iconic as well as new details that are sure to be enjoyed as well.This experience is defined by completely original, pixel-based artwork. Each one is different and manages to leave a lasting impression on the viewer. From insect specimens, to abstract sculptures, and very many paintings, you will get the unique chance to see all of these pieces while exploring the mysterious, living gallery of the fictional artist Guertena. Meanwhile music serves to communicate the mood of the gallery very delicately while still keeping you entertained. You will be relaxed, amused, and very intrigued by what you see in this very special game!A small note for players who played the original, this game will feature new puzzles and artwork from the original. Most of the experience has been preserved, but some minor elements have been replaced. All of the endings have been kept in this version, so see if you can still figure out how to find them!There are few games as humble as this one that manage to keep your attention, so I highly suggest you purchase it and find out for yourself!
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing and thinking about the original Ib for AGES! Ever since I discovered it, it's inspired me. And the remake is taking me right back to those days. It's an improvement on what was already basically perfection, with new puzzles and new dialogue and more time spent with everybody's favorite purple-haired guy. I love this game more than I can ever say. It's one of my all-time favorites that I'll come back to again and again and again. Really, I couldn't recommend it enough. Thank you for this masterpiece, kouri.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: The original held a special place in my heart and mind, I actually went back and re-played the original when I first heard the news of the remake release approaching to have a good comparison and familiarize myself with the world in depth again!The remake takes that original and enhances it wonderfully! The additional features (conversations with your traveling companions especially was my favorite) the rework of existing puzzles, the addition of new, the ability to view the true gallery from the title screen once you beat the game, all fantastic!!!This is a wonderful update and re-release of a beloved classic.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: If you love sprite based rpg horror games I don't have any I can recommend with higher praise than IB. Its a concise story that unless you've played through a few times and know how to do it perfectly you'll have your heart strings pulled on. Noting my username is Guertana a play on the in game artist Guertena I've loved Ib since its original RPG Maker release and this release is just that and more.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: The original Ib is one of my favorite games. I have so many great memories playing it 10 years ago and this remake made me so happy. Some things are a little switched around and different, but I loved all the new puzzles and the new dungeon area! The new art is gorgeous and the music made me nostalgic. Can't wait to replay this one just as much as the original :)
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: The first RPG Maker game I ever played, now remastered. A puzzle/exploration experience in a surreal art gallery. Playing through the story doesn't take very long but there's tons of hidden secrets throughout all the endings. And exploring each little moment can give you a lot of insight into the characters and what they've been through.The art-style is charming and the overall art gallery theme works really well, both with the horror and puzzle elements. Anyway, the game was great in 2012 and its still great.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: No loud conversation.    No photography.    No food or drink.    No touching the displays.    No fountain pens.    No leaving ever.Ib is an absolute classic of its genre and one of my personal all-time favorite games. It's clever, has a great atmosphere and is incredibly memorable. It is a short horror game in which a girl tries to escape a creepy gallery full of living artwork. The variety in concepts used in this gallery and the particular ways in which they spring to life is one of the main appeals I found in it, from creepy to funny to sweet to just, well, clever. It's cast is tiny but interesting and likable, the deadpan, brave little Ib, the soft, gentle and protective Garry and the cheerful but lonely Mary. These characters have stuck with me for years despite the little time the game gives itself to show you what they're about, and the origin of some of them remaining a mystery people still theorize about.  In terms of the remake's changes to the original, the new art is wonderful, showing even more of the characters' personality and detail in the gallery's artwork. The new and replaced puzzles are friendlier than the original, which required to keep pen and paper on hand occasionally. Whether you prefer this simpler kind of puzzle is a matter of taste, I personally enjoyed the note-taking, but the redesigned areas make up for that loss by being full of the particular flavor I loved in the original.The absolute best addition in my eyes though is the dedicated "talk" button to hear your companion's thoughts on any room you're in and the events that occur in them, not only does it work as a subtle hint system to keep you on track if you get lost, but it has a shocking amount of new lines for areas you wouldn't normally visit with a companion at all. The amount of love and care shown here makes the remake even more of an absolute steal.I would recommend this game in a heartbeat to anyone who enjoys horror, and especially to those who liked the era of RPG Maker Horror games, if they somehow managed to miss out on this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: To put it very simply: Ib is a game that means a lot to me. I've played the original over and over again, and this remake definitely improves on the original game that I already loved so much. It's largely the same, the OST remains untouched which I'm happy about because it's great and very nostalgic, there are a few new puzzles that were a new sort of challenge to me, I've played the original so much that I can basically clear it with my eyes closed, so the new puzzles were a great addition to make the game feel fresh. Plus, the puzzles that got replaced were the most annoying ones, so that's great! The art also has upgraded significantly, which is especially noticable in the CG's you get during the gameplay. All in all, great remake of an already great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! I'm so glad this game got a remake, this is what im waiting for! only 1 problem with this game is, i already unlocked the dungeon guertena but sadly i got error when i entered the blue room and when u rest with garry there. i dont know this bug or this is just me. but i want this to be fixed soon as possible.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Although my opinion may be swayed by nostalgia, I can't help but absolutely adore this game.The updated visuals are enchanting without losing the appeal of the original and the new zoom in feature is greatly appreciated to take it all in.Ib's story in my mind is a masterpiece, so now that its out officially in English why not give it a try?
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Very well developed atmosphere that mixes cute and creepy perfectly, with everything feeling handmade. It's somewhat short and the puzzles are relatively easy, but the game's multiple endings does offer a good deal of replayability. If you enjoyed the original or are only finding this now, please give it a try. TL:DR The game is like a lemon candy, short, simple, and sweet.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: used to speedrun the original, i loved it so much. this remaster is every bit as wonderful as the original. i imagine i may even speedrun it again, haha.i can hardly believe it's been ten years since the original. can't wait to get all the endings again.much love to kouri, i'm glad to be able to pay for the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: I adored this game years ago, it's an amazing little game. Almost 10 years later and the remake still does just as well, and I'm delighted that I can in some way support the creator of one of my favourite gamesThe art is wonderfully updated with Kouyi's signature style unchanged, the newly added art and puzzles is in keeping with the original and just as uniquely wonderful as the original. The talk feature was relentlessly spammed by me for dialogueA lot of the base game was left untouched for the most part, plot and character remains the same, majority of the changes were aestheticA good update to a classic and highly recommended for anyone who loves a rpgmaker horror
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully done remake. The pixel art is truly marvelous, they spiced up a few puzzle segments and it makes a lot more sense now, but, overall, the gameplay is almost the same, there are no new endings or something like this. Different from 'The Witch's House MV', which offered a brand new game+ with different puzzles, Ib's remake is not that interesting if you already played the original after all the latest updates (the ehxibition patch), but it's still a good way to support the devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Ib was a huge part of my childhood and played it so many times (I was around the same age as Ib when it came out in 2012). Now, it has once again came to bring that childhood joy I got out of it. It is a very short game and fairly easy, but I don't mind that at all. It is a fun experience and I feel the new puzzles that were implemented helps streamline the game more than the original. I'll be sure to play this one over and over again like I did back then. I adore it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up watching this game, knowing that someday I will buy it. But before the remake, I couldn't find this anywhere. Now that it's here. I'm playing it to my hearts content. Another reason why I love this game, and would recommend, is because her name is my middle name. Never in my life would I ever find a character or whole entire game at that, be my name. My name is very unique and since Ib came out 10 years ago, my 12 year old self is dancing with joy. Love this!
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for a remake of this game for 10 YEARS!!!!!!!!! And it did not disappoint! Ib is an exploration game with horror-esque elements where you play Ib, a nine year old girl trying to escape an art gallery come to life. The game is very charming and fun! The story is simple but the writing is so good that it really gets you feeling for the characters! I love seeing everything revamped and revisiting my faves trying to escape the gallery. I love the multiple endings and how the difference between talking to a character or not at a certain point can help determine if they survive or not. Some endings can really make you feel things if for example you got an ending with a character you liked no longer with you and another character that escaped with you did something that made you go "WOAH, HEY!!" It's a great experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Jesus, this game takes me back. Back to those years in high school with my high school sweetheart and my online friends.It is a bittersweet feeling, because those were good times, but you realize that long after they become memories.Sorry I drenched this review with tears. Game is amazing, has some new content, music is crystal clear and while I'm not too big on some stuff (like characters portraits or the flowers having a more modern looking, gamey like UI instead of a painting picturing how damaged the flower is), it is still the exact same wonderful game from back then.You should buy it NOW
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: A great horrific adventure game. I never played Ib before this remake but I'm glad I finally did it.There's nothing really scary about it but the art gallery in which you lose yourself is varied, full of creativity and is always giving off a creepy feeling.The characters you meet along the way are surprisingly fleshed out and endearing for a game so short (~4-5h)Gameplay-wise, there's a lot of walking around, some not-so-hard puzzles and just enough dialogues to make it interesting.I can only recommend it to people who like this kind of game!
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game when it first came out - the RPGMaker horror game scene was big and Ib really was just a gem that me and my friends enjoyed. Upon playing the remake it was not only nostalgic but fresh with great updated artwork and some new puzzles thrown into the mix! On my first playthrough I didn't get the ending I thought I was heading for, and upon seeing the other new features I might just head back into the gallery for another go.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: I have never written a game review before but I just have to for this game, genuinely one of the most memorable games to ever cross my path about ten years ago and I was so ready to play it again here on Steam. The story, the character, the music, and art and just overall atmosphere of the game is all a 11/10! I first got it and played it on my own in Japanese, and now that the English patch is out I wholeheartedly recommend everyone and anyone interested in Horror RPGs to give this game a chance. There are new puzzles compared to the original version and way more new dialogue this time around! Kouri is an amazing game creator and you feel like the love put into the game. If you want to play or look more into games of this genre, honestly look into Horror RPG Maker Games, there are some that have remakes on Steam and others that are for free out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Nostalgia/10 I was waiting impatiently the remaster of this beautiful piece of art <3 I played at the first version when I was in middle school and it was my introduction to horror RPG. It's truly a pleasure to play again at this masterpieceThe adding of the True Guertena exhibit is so cool, I love to try new endings while searching for missing art pieces!

_childDocuments_.review: my absolute favorite game ever for years now. if youre considering buying it please do, you wont regret it. ib is a masterpieceadditionally, if youve played the older version, the steam release is 100% worth getting to enjoy the story again with new puzzles and more content, not to mention supporting kouri! so mwahhaha get it get it i dare you double dog dare
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love that Ib has been added to Steam! I was a huge fan of the original and enjoyed playing it over and over. While that version was obviously good, Kouri has surpassed it and gone to excellent. I was expecting the same exact game (just better graphics maybe). But no, this game has new elements that make the gameplay so much better than the original. On top of that, it's definitely worth way more than the 13 USD price tag, just with the quality and care put into this game. I was astonished and blown away by the game I played, and am looking forward to many hours of play!
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Ib is my favorite and most treasured game and has been since it came out back in 2012. It still holds some of my favorite characters after so long. The remake was beautifully done with many additions and changes that were great! The puzzles are always fun and I love the music even though Mary's theme was changed (the new theme is nice!). The new art is lovely and I adore the gallery for when you beat the game! Would recommend this classic rpg horror game to anyone! This exact game brought me into loving so many similar games such as The Witch's House, Mad Father, Misao, Corpse Party, Forest of Drizzling Rain, etc. Ib is definitely my most favorite though with the most unique story and creative, colorful, and interesting world! Thank you for letting me replay the game I have loved so much with this wonderful remake!
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: Well, despite not being able to read the dialogue yet, very happy with this remake of Ib. They've streamlined certain areas, changed a few puzzles (for the better, unless you're gonna miss that hidden-button-maze room in the grey area), and overall it clearly pays homage to the original game's intent.Very excited for the incoming english version, but even just playing through with phone-translation and memory I'm a very satisfied fan! Thanks so much for taking the effort to make this, Kouri!
_childDocuments_.name: Ib

_childDocuments_.review: The original version was my first of the genre, and it's basically how I discovered more and more indie RPGs that honestly changed my life. This remake is something I was really excited about - and I can safely say I wasn't disappointed! It's still only in Japanese, but with how I know the original + some Ggl translate I managed to go through the game easily enough. Some puzzles changed, some paintings were added, some music as well.I feel that for the people who already know the game, it's a good remake and it adds something valuable, and for those who don't know it, well they might have to wait for the English translation but it's really good!! Play it to your heart's content! Hoping to unlock everything soon eheh

_childDocuments_.review:
A young girl named Ib visits an art gallery with her parents. While perusing the various works of art, Ib suddenly realizes that she is alone. As she searches for someone - anyone - else, the museum begins to change... A 2D exploration adventure game set in a creepy, mysterious art gallery.

Inspect the area around you, discovering items and disarming traps to find your way out of the strange gallery.
